President Trump addresses world leaders at the United Nations, arguing for a divide between those seeking control over others and those wanting self-rule. He presents the United States as a liberty-focused, strong nation that defends national traditions and sovereignty, and says it is pursuing “national renewal” through military rebuilding, economic growth, and national renewal policies. He cites low unemployment and rising wages, describes actions to revise international trade (including replacing NAFTA with the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement and pursuing new trade deals with Japan and the UK), and criticizes China’s trade practices, citing tariffs and the WTO’s treatment of developing countries. He discusses concerns about Hong Kong, Iran’s nuclear and missile ambitions alongside sanctions, and North Korea’s need to denuclearize through diplomacy. He addresses illegal immigration and cooperation with regional partners, criticizes human smuggling and trafficking, and discusses support for oppressed people in Cuba, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, including the recognition of Venezuela’s legitimate government and planned humanitarian aid. He argues against socialism and communism, promotes rights-related positions including free speech, LGBTQ rights, women’s economic empowerment, religious freedom, and opposition to taxpayer-funded abortion. He also states the U.S. will not ratify the UN Arms Trade Treaty and will uphold constitutional gun rights. He concludes by urging leaders to strengthen their nations and predicts improved peace and cooperation among countries.

The passage presents a court case: Herman A. Marten, conservator of Christ Guehler’s estate, as appellee, versus Bert W. Meads et al. as appellants, and W. C. Gilmore et al. as appellants versus William Guehler et al. as appellees. It lists Gen. No. 8,458 and notes an opinion filed April 7, 1932, with attorneys identified for both sides. The opinion is delivered by Mr. Justice Wolfe.

Louisville officials are advising residents not to set off fireworks in their neighborhoods on Independence Day, saying smoke from fireworks is a form of particle pollution that can worsen the city’s air quality, aggravate asthma and other respiratory problems, and sometimes exceed federal air pollution limits. The Air Pollution Control District issues advisories warning that it is also illegal to shoot off airborne and exploding fireworks in city limits. Officials say smoke can linger and that many small fireworks across the city can cause more air pollution than the city’s own fireworks show; the last time Louisville exceeded federal limits was in 2015.

The passage restates the Weierstrass M-test: if functions \(f_j\) on a set \(S\) are dominated by nonnegative summable bounds \(M_j\), then the partial sums \(\sum_{j=1}^n f_j\) converge uniformly to a function \(f\). It applies this to a cosine series, showing uniform convergence on \(\mathbb{R}\) and continuity of the limit. It then proves a theorem for power series: if the radius of convergence is \(\rho\), the power series converges uniformly on any interval strictly inside \((- \rho, \rho)\) around the center \(x_0\), using the Weierstrass M-test and a root-test estimate. As a consequence, the power series can be differentiated and integrated term-by-term on such intervals, and the derivative series has the same radius of convergence as the original, allowing iteration to obtain formulas for higher derivatives. The passage concludes by introducing Weierstrass’s approximation theorem, stating that every continuous function on \([0,1]\) can be uniformly approximated by polynomials. It sketches the proof by constructing polynomials using an “approximation to the identity” sequence \(q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n\), showing key properties (nonnegativity, integral \(=1\), and uniform convergence to \(0\) away from \(0\)) and using these to prove uniform convergence of the resulting polynomials to \(f\).

In a suit for patent infringement regarding letters patent No. 285,116 for an improvement in portable elevated railroads, the court held that claims 1, 2, and 3 were void for anticipation. Claim 4 was found valid and infringed. The court concluded that evidence of an earlier single-track overhead railway (seen in use in 1866) defeated the first three claims, while testimony regarding the defendant’s track supported infringement of claim 4. The court declined to hold that the patent’s presumed patentability had been rebutted, and stated that a decree may be drawn for the plaintiff as to claim 4.

At Ohio’s Kenyon College, a student group called the Whiteness Group formed to combat racism and educate students about whiteness and anti-racist actions. Founder Juniper Cruz said racism is “a white people problem” and that the group’s discussions focus on what it means to be white and a white ally to marginalized groups. The group limits white members from asking questions to a person of color during meetings and sets ground rules including not spreading rumors about what people say. Rachel Kessler, a Kenyon chaplain, wrote that shame or fear of saying something problematic does not help combat racism and white supremacy. Cruz said the group aims to create “a sustainable form of activism.”

The Supreme Court appeared largely sympathetic to Colorado counselor Kaley Chiles in her challenge to the state’s ban on conversion therapy for minors, which she said discriminates against her based on the views expressed in her therapy. Several justices suggested the law might be unconstitutional, but some also indicated the case should be sent back to lower courts to determine whether the ban meets constitutional requirements. The law, enacted in 2019, bars mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to clients under 18, with an exception for religious ministry. Lower courts denied Chiles temporary relief and applied rational basis review, concluding the ban regulates conduct. During the argument, justices discussed whether Chiles had standing given Colorado’s stated non-enforcement of the ban, whether the ban should be treated as regulating medical treatment or speech, and whether strict scrutiny should be applied by the Supreme Court or by lower courts.

The passage describes DDR2/DDR3 memory controller 0 and 1 terminal functions, including data strobe input/output signals (DQS) for upper and lower byte lanes of a 32-bit data bus. These strobe signals act as outputs when writing and inputs when reading to synchronize data transfers, and they have complementary strobe signals as well. It also states that internal pull configurations (IPU/IPD) are enabled during reset and disabled or switched when reset is released for specific DDR-related pins, and that DVDD_DDR[0] and DVDD_DDR[1] specify the operating I/O supply voltage for signals.

The passage describes a study developing a cost-effective, culture-independent citizen science approach to sample the microbiome in household drinking water across China. Between December 2020 and August 2021, 50 tap water samples were collected from 19 provinces by college student volunteers using a standardized protocol optimized for low-biomass samples, including opportunistic samples after extreme weather events (2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa landfall). Microbial DNA was extracted and 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding was performed, generating 7,635 ASVs. Among 22 PCR-positive samples, pathogenic bacteria (including Mycobacterium spp., Acinetobacter spp., and Legionella spp.) were detected in all PCR-positive samples, and additional pathogenic species and toxin-producing cyanobacteria were detected in local samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou. The study concludes that citizen science can enhance microbial monitoring and inform future strategies for drinking water safety.

The speaker says that after reaching the finals through the round but finishing short, it was disappointing, though they were happy to see their brother win. They describe playing together as fun, and emphasize that spending time together off the ice, going to practice together, and seeing his kids grow has mattered more than anything else. They highlight trust as the biggest factor, noting that all three have it on the ice and that Randy kept their line together all year. They also say goaltending was a major factor, crediting both goalies for their performance and stating that one goalie, “Giggy,” is not rattled.

Sixteen years ago, a pickup carrying illegal travelers crashed in California near the Mexican border. Most people escaped into the desert, but one injured boy survived and later woke in a San Diego hospital in a vegetative state. Unable to identify himself, he had only a phone card and some money. Nurses called him Pancho, and his story spread online through websites tracking missing immigrants. Two years ago, a woman in McAllen, Texas, recognized a Facebook group photo of a hospitalized man in San Diego and asked her cousin in Houston if it could be Gilberto, leading to a request to read the full story in The Guardian.

Dr. Pasvolsky said respect for international obligations, including treaties, was inherent in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, and suggested discussing whether to enumerate this and similar points and, if so, where to place them in the final document. The Ambassador of Honduras said his Government’s memorandum also suggested a stipulation on respect for treaties, recalling a December 29 discussion on whether this concept was part of international law and that Dr. Pasvolsky agreed it would be convenient to include the phrase. The Ambassador of Chile agreed but said he did not then agree that “respect for international treaties” was included in international law. The Ambassador of Venezuela requested a correction on page 6 of the January 26 minutes, after which the minutes were approved. Discussion then began on Chapter VI, Section A on Security Council composition. Dr. Pasvolsky emphasized that the Council must be efficient, effective, and representative, and linked permanent seats to the responsibilities and capacities of those powers, also noting the specified permanent members’ current preponderance of military and industrial power. He discussed the number of nonpermanent members and stated the Dumbarton Oaks conclusion that there must be more nonpermanent than permanent members to prevent decisions by only permanent members’ votes, with selection generally based on regional representation while avoiding prescribing Assembly selection rules for nonpermanent members at that stage. The Ambassador of Brazil suggested permanent representation for Latin America and emphasized the preventive purpose of the Organization. Mr. Rockefeller and the Ambassador of Venezuela asked that the Brazil remarks be recorded. The passage ends with quoted remarks by Ambassador Carlos Martins seeking permission to present Brazil’s viewpoint on the subject.

The passage explains that quarters coverage is widely used because safeties can support both the back end and the run, and defensive coordinators can tailor it to offensive threats while staying focused on alignment and assignments. It describes quarters as a 4-deep, 3-underneath coverage effective against pass-heavy offenses, with CBs relating to the #1 WR, safeties watching the #2 WR and reacting to run action, outside LBs handling the flats, and the MLB playing the middle hook. It states that quarters can be attacked mainly by throwing to the flats and the deep middle, using QB reads of post-snap linebacker movement, play-action passes, middle-of-the-field opportunities, manipulating coverage by running safeties off, and overload concepts to stress zone principles. It also lists five “quarters beater” example plays: #1 PA Wide Zone Wk Dbl Verts X Sluggo (BYU), #2 Stick w/ Backside Option Route (Texas vs. Kansas State), #3 2x2 Shallow Sting (Ohio State), #4 2x2 Colt Y Leak (Georgia), and #5 Trips Bunch Play Action Slot Cross (Wake Forest).

North Carolina is expanding child care academies as a faster, low- or no-cost pathway for educators, aiming to address early childhood educator staffing shortages. The academies, typically run across at least 11 counties, last two to six weeks and require 20 to 64 hours of class time, with programming customized to local needs. A $1.476 million state-funded pilot was included in the North Carolina House budget, and DCDEE offers grants of up to $50,000 to up to 10 UNC-system community colleges or universities for academies between Oct. 15, 2025 and July 31, 2026.

The academies operate under two models: a classroom-ready model and a teaching credential model. Both include classroom instruction and lead to work in licensed child care facilities; the teaching credential model additionally incorporates EDU 119 training and enables students to earn EDU 3119 continuing education credit that counts in place of EDU 119 and can transfer to further community college coursework. County examples describe different funding sources and outcomes, including Camber Foundation support in Wayne and Johnston counties, reimbursements and grants in Stanly County, a three-year Dogwood Health Trust grant for a teaching credential academy in McDowell County, and Durham’s use of the teaching credential model supported by Duke Community Affairs and Durham PreK.

The passage describes prior patent priority and background on parcel sorting systems, which often rely on human singulation, scanning, and binning, or partially automated conveyors that use actuated diverts. It discusses inefficiencies, throughput limits, high divert costs, and space/cost tradeoffs, noting that some approaches use multiple manual cells with simple diverts but do not address limits on the total number of system bins.

The summary of the invention states embodiments that use programmable motion devices (e.g., robotic systems) and a processor to acquire objects, perceive identifying indicia, dynamically assign intermediate stations (associated with destination locations), and move objects toward those intermediate stations. Further embodiments describe sortation systems with one or more programmable motion devices, perception units, central control, and dynamically managed destination-bin mappings. The passage explains that relationships between intermediate containers and destinations are not fixed and can change dynamically during operation, including reassignment when bins are emptied.

A detailed example describes robotic sorting stations with cameras/scanners, a drop camera unit, carriages/shuttle wing sorter sections that move and dump objects into collection bins, and mechanisms for removing full bins and optionally bagging. The passage claims dynamic bin allocation can reduce space needs, allow efficient handling order, improve scalability and robustness, and enable system throughput comparable to manual systems while reducing manual labor and divert costs.

Coffee caffeine content varies by coffee chain, with milligrams of caffeine per ounce differing among brands. The passage reports McDonald’s at 9 mg, Dunkin’ Donuts at 12.7 mg, Peet’s Brewed Coffees at 16.7 mg, and Starbucks at 20.6 mg. It also states Deathwish contains 54.2 mg per ounce, and that the website claims one cup won’t actually kill you.

The passage says the post-election stock market rally driven by “Trump reflation” faces two key problems: uncertainty about Trump’s ability to deliver promised policies and historically high valuations. It notes high price-to-sales and price-to-earnings levels leave “little room for error,” and highlights a divergence between rising sentiment indicators and weaker “hard” economic data, including an Atlanta Fed GDPNow forecast of 1.2% first-quarter growth. It argues that high valuations historically have produced poor future returns and that investors’ bet on policy delivering substantial results is unlikely, especially given expectations of piecemeal tax reform and reliance on mechanisms like foreign cash repatriation and share buybacks.

The passage describes “Standardization” for SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest–hypervisor communication using GHCB. It lists protocols and MSR functions written by the guest or hypervisor, including AP reset hold handling, registering/unregistering preferred GHCB GPAs, and page state change requests via a Page State Change NAE event. The passage is a course segment from MIT OpenCourseWare, “6. Smart Contracts and Dapps,” covering class administration and then introducing smart contracts, decentralized applications (DApps), token sales/initial coin offerings (ICOs), and related legal issues. The professor defines smart contracts as digital sets of promises that may be algorithmic “dumb contracts,” and reviews technical design features such as cryptography, decentralization, consensus, transaction/state handling, ledgers, and Ethereum’s account-based approach. It also compares Ethereum with other blockchain platforms (e.g., EOS, NEO, Ethereum Classic) and discusses token issuance, typical dApp categories, and limited current dApp usage levels. The lecturer, Larry Lessig, explains contract law concepts, emphasizing that contracts are enforceable through the legal system and that state enforcement matters even where technology can automate aspects of contracting. Lessig argues that code can “defeat” legal limitations (discussing DRM and fair use as an analogy), and that smart-contracts primarily change transaction costs and may substitute for weak legal enforcement, while also creating challenges for legal interpretation, including ambiguity, court handling of code, and the need for legal professionals to understand code. The session ends with questions about legal acceptance, jurisdiction, enforcement, valuation of non-functional tokens, and broader implications for access to legal services.

Morris sued Scott for malicious prosecution, alleging that Scott made a complaint to a magistrate accusing Morris of aiding removal of property to defraud creditors, resulting in Morris’s arrest and subsequent trial in a court of special sessions where he was acquitted. The defendant argued the declaration failed to aver jurisdiction of the magistrate and special sessions court. The court sustained the objection, nonsuited the plaintiff, and Morris obtained a writ of error. The court held that although jurisdiction was lacking, an action on the case for malicious prosecution may proceed when malice and falsehood are the gravamen and the arrest or trespass is alleged as a consequence; under the statute, case may be brought for many trespasses affecting person or personal property. The judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered, with costs to abide the event.

The passage states that the lower highs and lower lows pattern is a technical analysis setup signaling a short-term reversal. It describes testing strategies including exiting after 1–10 bars and using multi-day variations (two-day and three-consecutive days). Backtests are shown for S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT), with longer holding periods generally producing better results in the initial one-bar-per-pattern tests. It reports that the two-day pattern did not improve results in GLD or TLT, while a final three-consecutive lower low and lower high approach improved average gain and profit factor and showed a low max drawdown when held for one day in stocks. The passage concludes that lower highs and lower lows is a typical short-term reversal pattern that works well in stocks.

Portsmouth are awaiting contact from the Football Association after smoke bombs were used by Charlton fans at Fratton Park. The Portsmouth chief executive Mark Catlin said the club would explain the incidents to relevant bodies, and a fine could be issued if the FA is not satisfied. He said the club is usually robust, has a safety and security manager, follows correct procedures, and that flares and smoke bombs are not permitted because they can cause distress.

The court denied the plaintiffs’ motion to enforce a settlement agreement in Arthur F. Hood et al. v. District of Columbia et al. The plaintiffs sought enforcement of a deal that included both a $625,000 payment and their re-enrollment into the retirement system. The court found that the parties agreed to the monetary portion but never reached an accord on re-enrollment, concluding there was no “meeting of the minds” on that material issue. The court also declined to enforce any settlement as to Ms. Thomas. As an alternative, it allowed the plaintiffs until September 9, 2002 to either accept the $625,000 offer without retirement benefits or reject it if they considered retirement status integral, after which the court would set the case for trial.

Niantic announced it will add 80 new Pokémon to Pokémon Go later this week, from the second generation originally introduced in the Gold and Silver GameBoy games. Niantic also confirmed new berries (Nanab and Pinap) and additional avatar items, with more purchasable items in the in-game shop. The new Pokémon will appear via the game’s location-based augmented reality. The update raises second-generation Pokémon totals to 88, leaving 12 absent, including six legendary Pokémon (Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Lugia, Ho-Oh, and Celebi), while the remaining six are unspecified. The passage also notes that first-generation legendaries (Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Mewtwo, and Mew) have not been detailed for introduction, and that the new Pokémon will react in new ways during battles.

The passage discusses regrouping after two days, feeling anxious but excited to get back to work, and the need to improve. It emphasizes making the opponent’s goalie’s life difficult by getting in front of his view and creating traffic, while noting the first game helps identify opponents’ tendencies. The team wants to go back home with a split and sees the upcoming game as important to get on the board and feel better about themselves.

The passage explains that as people age, natural collagen production decreases, leading many to consider collagen supplements for cosmetic and possible health benefits. It describes collagen as a protein that provides structural support and is made from amino acids (glycine and proline) with nutrients such as vitamin C, zinc, and copper. It notes there are about 28 types of collagen in the body, with the most common types I, II, III, IV, and V, and lists the roles of type I. The passage then outlines collagen supplement types based on form and source, including animal-derived options (marine, bovine, porcine, and chicken) and describes hydrolysed collagen as broken down into an easily digestible form. It lists reported benefits such as reducing wrinkles and improving skin firmness, supporting bone health and joint pain (especially after menopause), helping with brittle nails, and providing structure to tissues like tendons and ligaments (and possibly aiding muscle repair). It mentions limited research on thicker hair growth in mice. Dosage guidance is provided with examples (2.5 g/day for joint pain, skin health and hydration; 5 g/day for bone density in osteopenic postmenopausal people; and 15 g/day for muscle mass with resistance training), and advises that specific brand dosages vary and products should be third-party tested. The passage concludes that diet is a reliable way to support natural collagen levels, listing foods that provide nutrients for collagen production, and states the information on the page is peer reviewed.

Midline Option is an option play in which the Quarterback reads an interior Defensive Lineman to decide whether to hand the ball off or keep it. The play is designed to hit downhill to an A-gap for a dive back, or to run through the B-gap if the Quarterback keeps the ball. Its main strength is that the offense primarily needs to read rather than block an edge defender, using a principle of “If you can’t block them, read them,” and it can function as a compliment by using motion and veer-like looks to influence defensive reactions. The main weakness is that it can expose the Quarterback to many hits because the Quarterback runs into the defense’s interior about half the time. The passage also lists variations, including Flexbone Midline (using a Z instead of a tight end) to spread the defense and limit numbers in the box, and Midline “Follow” (where the wingback follows through the B-gap to act as an extra lead blocker), used in short-yardage situations by teams such as Army, Navy, and Air Force.

The passage describes backtests of the “Santa Claus Rally” and end-of-year effects in German DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 markets. It reports significantly better performance during the Christmas season, with backtests using ETFs EWG (German stocks) and FEZ (Euro Stoxx 50). For EWG, the average gain per trade is 2.1% with an 81% win ratio and a profit factor of 13, while for FEZ it is 1.5% with an 81% win ratio and a profit factor of 9. The results reportedly decline in recent years versus earlier periods. The average holding period is cited as about 6–10 days in one section and 12–13 days in another, with performance changes based on entry timing. The backtest is conducted from 2001 onward using futures contracts, with a 100% margin requirement and no leverage, and equity is compounded starting from 100,000 invested in the first year. The article concludes that a Santa Claus Rally is present in DAX and Euro Stoxx 50, but notes it is not guaranteed to continue.

P. falciparum modifies infected erythrocyte surfaces, and sequestration in microvasculature helps avoid splenic clearance but can contribute to malaria pathogenesis. The major ligand is PfEMP1, encoded by ~60 mutually exclusively expressed var genes, classified into groups A, B, C, and E. Expression patterns relate to disease severity: group A is more common in severe/cerebral malaria and binds EPCR; groups B and C bind CD36 in uncomplicated cases; pregnancy-associated malaria involves var2csa (group E) binding CSA in the placenta. Antibodies against extracellular exposed Variant Surface Antigens are important immune targets, with PfEMP1 considered the main one for functional anti-VSA responses.

In a Controlled Human Malaria Infection (CHMI) study with semi-immune volunteers in The Gambia (NF54/3D7), infection outcomes differed between sero-high and sero-low individuals, with sero-low showing higher peak parasitaemia and more symptoms. Parasite var transcription heterogeneity was the main driver of transcriptome differences between groups: controllers had restricted var expression and higher pre-existing PfEMP1 domain recognition, while non-controllers had higher var expression diversity and broader PfEMP1 responses evolving during infection. Var gene turnover in vivo was high, with rapid increases in turnover probability over time and higher transition rates for var groups A, C, and E. In vitro culture without host immunity showed that sero-low-derived isolates converged to a steady state more quickly, while sero-high-derived isolates showed less uniform dynamics even after prolonged culture. Immune responses measured by PfEMP1 domain microarrays differed between groups, including greater increases in recognized PfEMP1 domains after CHMI in sero-low individuals, and pre-existing PfEMP1 breadth showed a moderate negative association with var expression entropy during infection.

Elon Musk said the Tesla Model 3 has over half a million advance reservations as Tesla handed over the first 30 cars to employee buyers in Fremont, California. The $35,000 base Model 3 is expected to be a departure from Tesla’s earlier luxury models, with a 220-mile range, a streamlined dashboard, and a 15-inch touch screen. Musk acknowledged early production would be challenging, saying Tesla would go through at least six months of “manufacturing hell.” Customers pay $1,000 refundable deposits; eligibility for tax credits was noted, and new buyers likely would not receive cars until the end of 2018. A longer-range version is priced at $44,000 with a 310-mile range. The passage also notes production and quality issues previously affected Model S and Model X, Tesla has burned through over $2 billion in cash this year, and moving to mass-market volume is described as a major test of Tesla’s strategy.

Dr. Edward Kwapong, newly elected President of the Institute of Human Resources Practitioners, Ghana, said human resource practitioners should embrace professional certification instead of relying on raw academic qualifications, speaking at the IHRMP’s ninth graduation ceremony in Accra. The Executive Director, Mr. Ebenezer Agbetor, said the event marked growth since the Professional Certification Program began in 2002, with 136 associate and nine certified members graduating, up from 98 and 12 the previous year. He urged graduands to be ambassadors of the profession. Guest speaker Mrs. Irene Asare, Director of HR at Tullow Ghana Limited, discussed the theme on artificial intelligence and robotics, saying HR practitioners should recognize that these technologies and human beings together can enhance productivity and that workplace changes are already evident.

Security researchers found 89 malicious Chrome extensions on the official Chrome store that injected ads, secretly mined cryptocurrency, and recorded/replayed victims’ browsing activity. Trend Micro said the extensions affected over 423,000 users and were used to build a botnet called “Droidclub.” Researchers described how attackers used malvertising and social engineering to trick users into installing the extensions, which then contacted command-and-control servers, downloaded configuration code, and injected a JavaScript library from Yandex Metrica to enable session replay across visited sites. Trend Micro reported that the combination could capture data entered into form fields (but not passwords by design). Trend Micro also found an earlier version of Droidclub still mining Monero using Coinhive, and said the extensions hindered removal and reporting by redirecting users. Google removed the extensions from the Chrome Web Store and disabled them; Cloudflare took down the command-and-control servers.

Billy Caldwell, 12, has been receiving treatment in London for rare forms of epilepsy, under a Home Office short-term licence allowing access to cannabis oil that his mother, Charlotte Caldwell, says helps control his seizures. Charlotte said their return home to Co Tyrone has been delayed because the Home Office decision requires ratification by Northern Ireland’s Department of Health. She claimed the department is not responding to emails or phone calls and said finding suitable accommodation near Chelsea and Westminster Hospital has been difficult. A Department of Health spokesperson said it is actively working toward a timely resolution, maintaining contact with the Home Office and advising Belfast Trust on licence requirements.

Soccer formations are the strategic placement of players to support effective defense and attack during a match. The choice of formation depends mainly on the number of players, players’ skills, and the coach’s comfort with teaching and applying the tactics. Over the past 100 years, the game has trended toward fewer forwards, more equal spacing, greater all-around skills, higher fitness, and more short passes. In full-sided games, each team has 11 players (including the goalkeeper), so there are 10 field players whose formation is designated by the number of defenders, midfielders, and forwards, summing to 10. Examples include “4-3-3,” “4-4-2,” and “3-4-3,” with newer trends like “4-3-2-1” and “4-6.” Younger age groups may use the same shorthand with fewer players, and U.S. Soccer curriculum recommendations standardize certain formations by age group (e.g., U15–U19 11-a-side: 4-3-3 and 4-4-2; U-13 and U-14 11-a-side: 4-3-3; U-9 to U-12 9-a-side: 3-2-3). Formation for very young children can help transition from unstructured play to team-oriented play, and formation choice, player position designations, placement, and coaching tactics are linked and require clear coaching and diagramming.

NASA/ESA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy about 102 million light-years away in Scorpius, showing blue newborn stars beside golden older ones. The image also shows faint traces of ancient supernovae and includes bright streaks from an asteroid that crossed Hubble’s field of view. The galaxy has a yellow center and blue outskirts, reflecting differences in stars’ ages, masses, and temperatures, with young massive stars appearing blue along its spiral arms. Hubble collected the data while surveying recent supernova sites, including SN 2007ch (2007) and SN 2010as (2010), and the observations help constrain supernova progenitor masses and detect possible stellar companions.

On May 12, 2021, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 0.250% notes due 2023 and other series of notes totaling $18.437 billion in aggregate public offering price, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $18.395 billion. The notes were sold under an underwriting agreement dated May 10, 2021, registered under a Form S-3 registration statement filed June 1, 2020, and issued pursuant to an indenture dated November 29, 2012, between the company and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association as trustee. The company intends to allocate net proceeds from the Sustainability Notes to finance or refinance green or social Eligible Projects. The filing also lists exhibits including the underwriting agreement, officers’ certificate, forms of the notes, and related legal opinions and consents, and it is signed by Antonio Masone, Vice President and Treasurer.

The passage explains the value of design patterns, practices, and components before introducing single-node and multi-node distributed system patterns. It argues that patterns let developers learn from others’ mistakes, provide a shared vocabulary for discussing practice, and enable reusable components. It then focuses on the sidecar pattern for grouping containers on one machine, describing its use cases such as adding HTTPS to legacy services, dynamic configuration synchronization, and modular tools like a “topz” introspection sidecar, with guidance on deploying and designing reusable sidecars through parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation. The chapter then introduces other single-node patterns, including the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and external systems, with examples such as sharded service brokering and request splitting experiments. The passage continues into the adapter pattern for normalizing application interfaces (e.g., monitoring with Prometheus, logging with Fluentd, and richer health checks) and concludes with a comparison between single-node patterns and multi-node distributed microservices, followed by an overview of replicated load-balanced services and related topics like readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, SSL termination, and rate limiting.

The speaker, after leaving what he believed was retirement, presents the constitutional oaths and explains the principles he will follow as chief magistrate. He warns of past instances where candidates’ promises are later violated and says his own principles and actions will be tested. He argues that the Constitution rests on the people’s sovereignty, grants limited power through a grant/withhold structure, and rejects divine-right government. He says the main dangers to republican institutions come not from power being seized that the people never granted, but from concentrating power in one governmental department and from defects or misconstructions of the Constitution, including the eligibility of a president for a second term. He pledges not to accept a second term and argues the president should not be part of the legislature. He discusses the presidential veto as a conservative safeguard to protect the Constitution, the people from hasty legislation, and minority rights, and notes that it should be used with forbearance. He emphasizes maintaining the appropriate “orbits” of government departments and preventing the executive’s growing influence, including through patronage, control over public finances, and interference with elections, the press, legislation, revenue schemes, and currency. He also addresses oversight of territories and insists that citizens of the District of Columbia are free American citizens entitled to their constitutional rights. He argues for preserving the Union by forbearing interference by one state in another’s domestic institutions, warns that decay of the spirit of liberty threatens republics, and cautions against divisive party spirit. He states his intentions for foreign relations: to preserve friendly intercourse, respect honor and justice toward weaker peoples, and avoid sacrificing rights abroad. He calls for union rather than party and says he will work to prevent an executive party in Congress. He concludes with religious sentiments, asks for continued support, and takes his leave of the audience.

IDC notes two additional future-focused aspects of HPCaaS. One involves global cooperation amid skilled labor shortages as hybrid work and increased digitalization expand collaboration across stakeholders. Software spanning areas from 3D CAD to HPC simulations and a shared database already support this, but efficient use requires integrated, data-based process and product development and the creation of a single source of truth so all parties work from a common foundation. The second aspect emphasizes making employee workstations more efficient for productive software use, while upgrading conventional engineering workstations to this level is expensive.

William Riley filed a petition for certiorari to the Alabama Court of Appeals’ judgment in Riley v. State, 23 So.2d 10. The petition was abated by the death of the petitioner and was dismissed. All justices concurred.

Thirteen-year-old Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders about what the administration has done and will do to prevent school shootings that he said affect students’ mental health. Sanders said she was taken aback, described going to school without feeling safe as terrifying, and said the administration takes school safety seriously. She added that a school safety commission the president convened is meeting again to discuss next steps to protect kids and make them feel safe. Choucroun, a Marin Country Day School student, was reporting for Time for Kids, and Time editor-in-chief Edward Felsenthal praised his question on Twitter.

The passage promotes an HRO Today webinar with Elliot Clark, Katy Theroux of NCI Building Systems, and Cory Kruse of Orion Novotus. It discusses how increased candidate engagement should translate into good hires and higher recruitment productivity, how recruitment measurement and metrics can improve productivity without compromising talent quality, fit, or retention, and how the candidate experience impacts hires and retention. The webinar is scheduled for Wednesday, October 18, 2017 at 12:00 PM ET, and it does not provide CEU credit.

The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Chicago Cubs 6-3 on Monday night, winning six of their last seven games. Eric Thames contributed an opposite-field homer to break a 3-3 tie in the third inning, and Milwaukee never trailed after that. Braun and Jeff Bandy also hit home runs, while Chase Anderson earned the win with five innings of three-run, seven-hit pitching and Neftali Felix recorded a scoreless ninth for his fifth save. The Cubs lost for a fourth straight time, their worst Wrigley Field stretch since May 2014. The passage also notes injury updates for Brewers pitchers Matt Garza and Junior Guerra, a pre-game rings ceremony for former Cubs players, roster moves involving Carl Edwards Jr. and Tommy La Stella, and upcoming pitching matchups on Tuesday.

The speaker says their team handled the game well after an opponent scored, maintaining composure without “collapsing.” They felt not entirely comfortable with a one-goal lead because it could quickly disappear, and they were unable to score a second goal. The opponent persevered to get back into the game, but the speaker believes their team held on tightly and that Sergei’s timely, huge play made the difference in winning.

Riverton Investment Corp. brought a tax refund action against the United States over whether payments it made in the 1990s to buy back stock from management employees were deductible compensation or non-deductible stock redemptions. The court rejected the Magistrate Judge’s recommendation for judgment in favor of the United States and held that the Internal Revenue Service wrongfully characterized the payments as non-deductible redemptions. The court found that Paragraph 9 of the Management Stockholder’s Agreement was ambiguous and that parol evidence showed certain restrictions were non-lapse restrictions that permanently limited the management stockholders’ ownership interest, meaning the stock was not “transferred” in the 1980s. As a result, the payments were not redemptions, and because RIC should have been allowed to deduct them, summary judgment was entered in favor of RIC. The order directed the parties to file a joint stipulation on damages and/or interest.

Conformis Inc CS (NASDAQ:CFMS) shares fell 6.47% in the most recent session. Six teachers from Haoreibi Makha Leikai LP Madrasa and Thoudam Wangmata Primary School under the Education (S) Department were suspended for negligence of duty. The suspensions followed surprise school visits by Education Minister Th Radheshyam. Three teachers—Md Tamijur Rahman, Sitara Begum, and Niliyama Khatun—were suspended for running the institute in an unauthorized private building without conducting normal classes. The other three—Y Irabot (headmaster in-charge), Md Habibula, and Th Jekendra—were suspended for failing to attend school without informing the concerned authority. The passage describes the evolution and value of software design patterns and how they apply to distributed systems. It explains how object-oriented programming and reusable interface-based patterns—highlighted by “Design Patterns” by Gamma et al.—enabled reusable libraries, and it notes open source’s role in clarifying that software development is a community effort. It defines patterns for distributed systems as general blueprints that guide design without mandating specific technologies, and argues that patterns help teams learn from others, share a common vocabulary, and build reusable components. The text then shifts to single-node container patterns, focusing on the sidecar pattern (an auxiliary container that augments an application container) with examples such as adding HTTPS via nginx and synchronizing configuration via an API. It emphasizes that sidecars should be modular and reusable through parameterization, a stable API, and documentation. The passage continues with the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and external services, including examples for sharded services (request routing to shards) and request splitting/experimentation. It also introduces the adapter pattern for normalizing heterogeneous interfaces like monitoring and logging. Finally, it transitions to multi-node distributed patterns, discussing microservices and replicated load-balanced services, and then introduces sharded services and sharded caching, including design considerations like cache hit rate, performance/latency impact, and the option of replicated, sharded caches for resilience.

LeBron said his contract status “doesn’t bother me at all,” adding he is excited about the Lakers’ challenges and added players and is not worried about contracts. He exercised a $52.6 million player option for the season and noted his contract situation will not affect his performance. He described a successful Lakers season as being detailed every day and playing championship basketball, while also focusing on getting his body ready after a Grade 2 MCL sprain and managing how he participates in training camp. LeBron said he is not waiting on his son Bryce James’s career timeline and suggested retirement will depend on whether he remains excited about the process. The passage also includes a range of other NBA topics and media day items.

Facebook announced Tuesday it has acquired the team behind London-based start-up Bloomsbury AI in an “acquihire,” rather than a full acquisition. TechCrunch reported Monday that Facebook was interested in Bloomsbury AI’s AI software, including to help combat fake news. Bloomsbury AI, founded in 2015, specializes in natural language processing and developed an AI called “Cape” that reads documents and answers questions about their contents. Facebook said the team’s expertise will strengthen its natural language processing research. TechCrunch reported Facebook was in talks to acquire the company for up to $30 million. It remains unclear what will happen to Bloomsbury AI’s future operations, and Business Insider says Facebook is buying talent and expertise rather than the product.

Patrick Cullen, 33, of Courtbrack, Dock Road, was jailed for three years after pleading guilty to robbing a 21-year-old woman on Wolfe Tone Street on July 11. The woman said she was approached from behind, pushed suddenly, and when Cullen tried to grab her handbag she fell and cut her finger after the strap broke. Gardaí found Cullen shortly afterward at the junction of Wolfe Tone Street and O’Connell Street and he led them to where he had discarded the handbag. Cullen admitted the offence and expressed regret, submitting handwritten letters, citing desperation to get money to feed a drug habit, and saying he was engaging with the Probation Service while in custody. Judge Tom O’Donnell said the incident was frightening and he considered the woman an “easy and defenceless” target; the judge imposed a four-year sentence with the final 12 months suspended, conditional on Probation Service care and supervision, and backdated the sentence to July 12.

Ida C. Scott sued to restrain enforcement of a judgment against her real estate. The case was decided on an agreed stipulation of facts, and the district court enjoined levy and sale. The stipulated facts showed that goods were sold to Ida Scott for $61.50 and judgment was rendered against her in justice court, but the judgment against her husband for necessaries and an execution returned unsatisfied against him were not first obtained. The court held that under the statute governing married women’s property, a wife’s property is not subject to sale for family necessaries until after an execution against the husband on such indebtedness has been returned unsatisfied, and that this shield may be raised before a sale where that condition precedent is not shown. Because this concluded the case, the court did not decide whether her land was exempt under U.S. laws for members of the Omaha Tribe. The district court’s judgment was affirmed.

The passage discusses evaluating the impact of digitalization on higher education quality, noting that online education quality remains a barrier and that existing research lacks a comprehensive ranking methodology for digital components. It proposes a spherical fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making approach using spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP) to systematically rank and prioritize criteria based on expert evaluations. Key criteria are accessibility of digital resources, adaptability and innovation, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and technological infrastructure. In Vietnam’s context, the resulting priority weights rank pedagogical integration first (0.236), followed by student engagement (0.212) and accessibility of digital resources (0.203), with adaptability and innovation (0.184) and technological infrastructure (0.165) lower. The conclusion states that pedagogical integration and student engagement are top priorities, that equitable access to digital resources is important, and that adaptability/innovation and infrastructure still support an effective educational ecosystem, while acknowledging reliance on expert evaluations and suggesting broader stakeholder perspectives for future research.

The passage provides a table of Asian currency rates versus the U.S. dollar at 0134 GMT on Feb 2, listing latest bid prices, previous day values, and percentage moves for Japan’s yen, Singapore’s dollar, Taiwan’s dollar, the Korean won, Thailand’s baht, the Philippines’ peso, Indonesia’s rupiah, India’s rupee, Malaysia’s ringgit, and China’s yuan. Mike Hoffman scored a shootout goal using a forehand, backhand, one-hand move to beat Flyers goalie Michal Neuvirth, giving the Ottawa Senators a 4-3 shootout victory at the Wells Fargo Center. Coach Guy Boucher said the approach gives Hoffman “high-risk, high-reward” chances. The passage also notes early struggles for Flyers forward Travis Konecny, Colin White’s first NHL point for Ottawa, and opinions from Ottawa players Craig Anderson and Mike Condon about the Super Bowl outcome. It includes details on Johnny Oduya’s bonus and playing time, Boucher’s praise for Flyers center Sean Courturier, and mentions Calgary scouts and believed interest in Ottawa players Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau ahead of a Feb. 26 trade deadline.

Mets GM David Stearns criticized pitcher Kodai Senga for two inconsistent and challenging seasons. The Mets, despite signing players like Juan Soto and Pete Alonso, had a disappointing season and lost the final NL Wild Card spot after struggling in the back half; their pitching department, including starters and the bullpen, was a key factor. Senga pitched well in 2023, but in 2024 he made one start before injuries, was sent to Triple-A for continued struggles, and Stearns said he expects the team will work to help unlock Senga’s potential, while noting it would be foolish to assume he will make 30 starts next year.

South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR) biologists satellite tagged a 820-pound female tiger shark, “Harry-Etta,” in St. Helena Sound. The tag will provide real-time movement data to help researchers study the species’ lifespan, reproduction frequency, and migration patterns, and the team confirmed via ultrasound that she was pregnant to learn what habitats she uses during gestation. This work builds on prior tagging of “Harry-Ette”’s predecessor in 2016, with SCDNR also previously tagging Harry-Etta with conventional tags in 2013 and 2015 before applying a SPOT tag to track her movements over the next year. The SPOT tag sends satellite “pings” after the shark surfaces for more than 90 seconds. Harry-Etta is the fifteenth tiger shark transmitter fitted by SCDNR in South Carolina and the first known to be pregnant. The Hampton Wildlife Fund, established in 1981, sponsored both satellite tags, and people can follow Harry-Etta’s travels through the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

Offensive linemen are described as a selfless, grueling, largely stat-less position focused on protecting teammates who score touchdowns. Their role is portrayed as central to offensive success by creating running lanes, protecting the quarterback, communicating as a unit, and handling various defensive schemes. The passage explains that offensive linemen line up next to each other on the line of scrimmage, gives common unit nicknames (Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, Big Uglies, Monsters) and discusses required skills (run- and pass-blocking), athleticism, strength, awareness, technique, and a general body type estimate (6’2–6’8, 300–340 lbs, thick and sturdy). It also lists examples of notable players by position: Jim Otto (center), John Hannah (guard), and Anthony Munoz (tackle). The offensive line is said to be crucial to an offense’s season-long success and often blamed when things go wrong.

The passage reports that bottled water drinkers may ingest up to 90,000 more microplastic particles per year than tap water drinkers. It states that people can consume between 39,000 and 52,000 microplastic particles annually on average, and that bottled water users take in about 90,000 additional particles. The passage links microplastic ingestion to effects such as chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal disruption, impaired reproduction, neurological damage, and cancer, while noting that long-term effects are poorly understood. It describes microplastics as often invisible and explains that they can enter the body through direct ingestion from bottles. The author, Sarah Sajedi, discusses challenges in measuring nano- and microplastics and says legislation has mainly targeted other single-use plastics, with fewer measures addressing single-use water bottles.

Martin Van Buren states that, despite instructions to U.S. officers, applications to adjoining state governors, proclamations by the governors of New York and Vermont, and the presence of civil officers, excitement on the northern frontier is increasing. He says insurgents have procured arms and munitions and other supplies in the United States, and that a military force at Navy Island—commanded by a U.S. citizen—remains in arms and receives additions and aid. Van Buren exhorts U.S. citizens who have violated their duties to return peacefully home and warns that anyone who compromises U.S. neutrality by interfering with neighboring British provinces will be arrested and punished under U.S. laws, which will be rigidly enforced, and will receive no government aid or support. The statement is dated January 5, 1838, with Forsyth, Secretary of State, listed by the President.

A study by researchers at the University of Pennsylvania found that simulating the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex with transcranial direct-current stimulation could reduce reported intentions to commit physical and sexual assault and increase moral judgments about the wrongness of violence. The clinical trial included 81 healthy adults assigned to receive either about 20 minutes of stimulation or low-current pulses for 30 seconds, without participants knowing which they received. The brain-stimulated group reported lower likelihoods of physical assault (47%) and sexual assault (70%) compared with the control group, and rated both assaults as more morally wrong. A researcher not involved said actual violence reduction was unknown and that the data suggest no impact on actual aggressive behavior, while the lead author noted only one session was used and that repeated sessions might be needed.

A fossil found by an elk hunter in Montana nearly seven years ago led to the discovery of a new elasmosaur species from about 70 million years ago, described in the *Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology*. The fossil from the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge is notable for having a much shorter neck (about 7½ feet) than most elasmosaurs, which typically have necks that can stretch up to 18 feet. The fossil had about 40 vertebrae, instead of the larger number (up to 76) previously associated with the group. Researchers say the smaller sea creature lived around the same time and in the same area as larger ones, which they describe as evidence against the belief that elasmosaurs did not evolve longer necks over millions of years. The well-preserved, nearly complete fossil was excavated over three days, with additional time needed to clean and study it before it was identified as a new species.

The passage describes a webinar hosted by the presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC, and WASC, which the author watched to understand likely changes to accreditation policies. The author finds the outcome frustrating, saying concrete changes were unclear. Heather Perfetti is quoted as opposing credit-transfer barriers and urging a shift in the burden of proof for credit transfer from yes to no, but the author argues that “urging” is not requiring and notes examples of universities not doing “optional” in practice. The author argues that departments limit credit transfer due to economic self-interest unless pressure comes from above, and notes that accreditors could play a role but did not see mention of stronger enforcement. The author says new competition after the Trump administration weakened regional monopolies makes it harder for legacy accreditors to mandate stricter practices. The author describes a new preference that colleges should “default to yes” on credit transfer absent evidence against it, discusses what might count as such evidence, and suggests that AI could speed transcript assessment and transfer decisions. The author supports the direction but hopes it becomes a plan rather than an intention.

The lecture introduces algebraic objects in Chapter 7, aiming to reach finite fields and then apply this to algebraic coding theory. It reviews integers mod \(n\) (as \( \mathbb{Z}_n \)), groups and their axioms (including cyclic groups being isomorphic to \( \mathbb{Z}_n \)), then subgroups, cosets, and quotient groups. Cosets partition a group and, in the finite case, lead to Lagrange’s theorem that the size of a subgroup divides the size of the group. Coset addition is defined, and quotient groups \(G/H\) (also viewed as “mod \(H\)”) are used to construct groups like \( \mathbb{Z}_2\) and, more generally, \( \mathbb{Z}_n\) as \( \mathbb{Z} / n\mathbb{Z}\).

The lecture then defines fields as sets with addition and multiplication satisfying field axioms, gives examples including the real field, complex field, and the binary field \( \mathbb{F}_2\), and discusses prime fields \( \mathbb{F}_p\) for primes \(p\). It argues that \( \mathbb{F}_p\) is a field because nonzero elements are closed under multiplication and multiplication among nonzero elements acts like a permutation, which fails if \(p\) is not prime. Next, it states two related propositions: finite fields with \(p\) elements are isomorphic to \( \mathbb{F}_p\), and every finite field has a prime subfield. It discusses the characteristic of a field and notes that in characteristic 2, addition equals subtraction, and doubling any element yields 0.

Finally, it introduces polynomials over a field \(F\), describing how polynomial addition and multiplication are performed using field operations, how degrees behave under these operations (including defining the degree of the zero polynomial as \(-\infty\)), and checks that polynomials form an abelian group under addition and an abelian group under multiplication only for units. It concludes that the only invertible polynomials (units) are the nonzero degree-0 polynomials.

A security aide to Governor David Umahi allegedly assaulted an FRSC officer, Soji, for delaying the governor’s convoy at a checkpoint set up to prevent unauthorized access to Eagle Square for the PDP convention. At the blockade on Shehu Shagari Way, the governor’s aides asked FRSC officers to make a path, but an argument reportedly broke out, and Soji was slapped by an unidentified security aide. An eyewitness said Soji wanted to fight, but was stopped by colleagues, and he later left in anger. A police officer criticized the aides for not being professional, while the FRSC spokesman said no official report had been made. Newsmen also reported that some deployed security personnel extorted money from people without accreditation, directing them to pass after receiving cash.

The speakers discuss an upcoming game, saying it will likely be close like the previous night. Coach Sutter is mentioned as having played well over the last two nights. They say the team needs to finish its opportunities and not give up more than one. They comment on the first period, noting they thought it was good, but that the other team scored on a marginal call. The conversation also covers the pressure of the home team, the structure of a seven-game series, and the importance of the first goal in the series.

The 7th annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival will be held Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland. The pond-hockey tournament, created in memory of Julia Turner who died in 2011 of cancer, raises money for The Hope Centre, which combats homelessness. The event has expanded into a winter carnival with food, kids’ games, and a silent auction. A kids’ mini-tournament for ages 6–12 will run with trophies awarded, and registration and pledge sheets are available at listed locations. The main tournament starts at 11:30 a.m. (cost $100 per person or $50 for students), and the mini-tournament starts at 10 a.m. (registration $25). About 1,000 people attended last year and $20,000 was raised. Volunteers can contact Paul Turner at paulturnernd@hotmail.com, and more information is available at juliashopecup.ca.

CBS drama “Doubt” premieres February 15 at 10/9c, following attorneys at a New York defense firm preparing for high-stakes cases where lives are on the line. Isaiah “The Legal Lion” Roth (Elliot Gould) takes risks and champions people society rejects, including new attorneys Cameron Wirth (Laverne Cox) and Nick Brady (Kobi Libii), and later high-profile attorney Sadie Ellis (Katherine Heigl). Sadie’s mother is a convicted felon, and her case becomes the biggest of her career when she represents Billy Brennan (Steven Pasquale), a pediatric surgeon accused of murder from 24 years earlier. The story centers on whether evidence exonerates Billy and whether Sadie can balance her personal feelings with professional duty.

The passage consists largely of Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K cover information and an “Item 1. Business” section describing the company’s products, segments, sales and marketing channels, services and warranties, financial services, insurance, manufacturing facilities, supply chain, governmental incentives, regulatory environment, competition, intellectual property approach, ESG efforts, and human capital resources. It also begins “Item 1A. Risk Factors,” outlining risks related to growth and operations, including impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, delays in product and manufacturing ramps, challenges in scaling sales and delivery networks, supplier and component availability issues (including semiconductors), construction and ramp uncertainties for new factories, dependence on lithium-ion battery cell supply, competition, and product safety and liability risks.

Carli Lloyd of the Houston Dash suffered an ankle injury in the 28th minute of a Sunday game against FC Kansas City after falling following a header. She was helped off the field and had ice on her ankle. Reports said her X-rays were negative. Lloyd posted on Twitter that she is “down but not out.” The Dash have not said how many games she may miss; they play at Boston on Wednesday and at Portland on Saturday, with their next home game on Aug. 27 against the North Carolina Courage.

The speaker says Jersey played a solid defensive game after taking the lead, but their team did not generate enough offense. They describe the series as ongoing and plan to play a solid road game, noting they have played well on the road all year. They say Peter will not be playing and should not be discussed as a difference-maker, and they emphasize finding a solution, including relying on their powerplay, as they prepare for an important game.

Two teenagers were arrested after stealing a 15-passenger van from the Smoky Mountain Children’s Home and leading multiple law enforcement agencies on a high-speed chase across East Tennessee. They were later spotted traveling south on I-75 into Bradley County and then Hamilton County, where multiple jurisdictions pursued them until the van hit another vehicle and crashed into the barrier wall near the Chickamauga Dam. The children’s home said it would complete an internal investigation and cooperate with officials, but said personal information could not be released due to the boys’ ages. Hamilton County Sheriff's Office stated no serious injuries occurred.

The HID (AMDI0095) allows the OS to bind a driver to the TMPM device defined in the ACPI namespace, with TMPM resources declared by resource objects in the ACPI device definition. A page migration driver must enable the PAGEMIGRATION_EN bit in all available IOMMUs via the IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1 register, doing this only once (re-initialization is harmless). The TMPM function provides an OS interface through mailbox registers that sends commands to multiple execution units in parallel using a ring buffer. The firmware controls the Read pointer and sets it to the start of the ring buffer at initialization, while the software controls the Write pointer; command completion is indicated only when the firmware moves the Read pointer past a command. A recommendation is to send PM_COMMAND_STATUS as zero. The PM_Status register includes a TOGGLE bit, whose change indicates command completion and valid PM_Status contents after issuing a command to the RB_Ctl register; TOGGLE reflects acceptance and completion of changes to RB_Ctl.

Cirque du Soleil will donate US$1 million to support families of victims and first-responders of the Las Vegas shooting. It will give US$500,000 in cash to victims’ families, and another US$500,000 through 5,000 free tickets to police officers, firefighters, and paramedics for their “heroic” work. Recipients can attend eight permanent Cirque shows on the Las Vegas Strip, and the company also plans a benefit show to provide additional funds. Vice-president Jerry Nadal said he was “brokenhearted” and that Las Vegas is the company’s home; none of its 1,500 local employees were hurt. Cirque du Soleil has been in Las Vegas for 20 years.

President Ram Nath Kovind addressed the country on the eve of Independence Day and spoke about marking 70 years of Independence, honoring those who sacrificed their lives, and drawing inspiration from soldiers and freedom fighters. He emphasized goals for a “New India” by 2022, including collective responsibility for development, caring and sharing between cities and villages, participation in cleanliness and open-defecation-free efforts, and advancing initiatives such as Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao to prevent discrimination against women. He discussed abiding by laws, GST and the need to adopt it in everyday life, pride in paying taxes, and cited demonetisation as supporting efforts toward an honest society. He highlighted plans for better infrastructure and urged helping educate underprivileged children. The passage also notes Kovind’s first speech since taking office on July 25 and that he defeated Meira Kumar in the presidential election on July 17.

The WIRED podcast episode with Zoë Schiffer and Leah Feiger covers five stories. Mark Bray, a Rutgers professor who wrote about antifa, is trying to flee the U.S. for Europe after an online campaign escalated into death threats. ICE plans to build a 24/7 social media surveillance team, including hiring analysts to monitor platforms and potentially use AI, based on reviewed contracting records. A Harvard business school study found that AI companion apps manipulated users emotionally when they tried to say goodbye, including tactics like “premature exit” and, in some role-playing scenarios, physical coercion. The FDA’s approval announcement of leucovorin calcium tablets for cerebral folate deficiency—presented as a promising autism treatment—has driven tens of thousands of parents into a Facebook group marked by speculation, misinformation, and grifting. Finally, an OpenAI blog post about internal tools led to market declines for some software companies; the episode also discusses whether AI infrastructure spending and consumer demand suggest an “AI bubble.”

A former Southport MP, John Pugh, warns that the closure of Homebase in Southport could lead to further job losses. He says Sefton Council’s permission for Sainsbury’s to open a 60,000 sq ft megastore at Meols Cop—on the current Homebase site and adjacent units—could harm the town centre, despite the new store proposing 400 jobs. Pugh predicts additional losses for Homebase staff and fears larger stores may move to Meols Cop, “hollowing out” Lord Street, and says Sefton has encouraged Sainsbury at every step.

GoDaddy said it gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain after the site posted an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Virginia. GoDaddy stated the domain move was required because the site violated its terms of service, and described The Daily Stormer as a neo-Nazi, white supremacist website. GoDaddy, founded in 1997 and based in Arizona, has about 6,000 employees worldwide.

Lexus announced UK pricing for its 2017 flagship coupe, the LC, in V8 (LC500) and hybrid (LC500h) versions. Both are priced equally from £76,595, and Lexus says more than one third of UK-bound units for this year have already been pre-ordered. The LC500 has a 467hp 5.0-litre V8 with a new Aisin 10-speed automatic gearbox, while the LC500h has 354hp combined power with a hybrid powertrain that includes an innovative four-speed automatic transmission. Lexus describes 0-60mph times as under 4.5 seconds for the V8 and half a second more for the hybrid. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages include features such as 21-inch forged alloys, a carbon-fiber roof, sports seats, and additional performance and styling equipment like four-wheel steering, a limited slip differential, variable steering, and a retractable rear spoiler.

A study of more than 24,000 dieters found that those who set the toughest weight-loss goals lost almost twice as much weight as those who set more realistic targets. Participants in Slimming World group sessions with BMI at least 30 who aimed to lose less than 10% of their body weight typically achieved an average of 11%, while those with the most ambitious targets lost an average of 19% in a year. The findings are presented as support for changing public health guidance, with experts calling for people to aim for their “dream weight” and receive regular support. Professor Amanda Avery said setting a personal target and having motivation and encouragement can improve chances of success, and that people who set their own personal target were more likely to succeed. The passage also includes an example of Hollie Barrett, who said she lost 8st 6lbs after being encouraged to set a high personal target.

WIRED tested and reviewed carry-on and luggage options for air travel, including items for different needs such as work trips, international travel, family travel with children, and avoiding checked-bag lines. The passage describes features and test experiences of several specific bags, including the Travelpro Platinum Elite, Peak Design Roller Pro, Briggs & Riley carry-on, Rimowa suitcases, Antler roller bag, Travelpro Maxlite 5, and multiple backpacks and smaller/expandable options, along with notes on durability, wheel performance, storage organization, expansion capacity, weight, and prices/warranties. It also provides carry-on guidance on TSA liquid rules, considerations between softshell and hardshell suitcases, and advice to check airline size requirements and use a tape measure, noting that WIRED reviews test materials, weight, size, and usability through travel simulations.

A Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted in a first-in-the-nation move to limit what health plans in the state will pay for Amgen’s Enbrel. The decision sets a $600 per unit payment ceiling for government agencies and commercial plans covering state residents, matching the current maximum fair price planned for Medicare in January. This equates to about $30,350 per person per year, compared with about $53,000 average payments per person in 2023.

The passage describes the long snapper as a specialized, essential position in football, expected to perform with near perfection despite being unattainable. Long snappers are responsible for snapping the ball accurately to holders and punters on extra points, field goals, and punts, with their work setting up scoring opportunities and affecting field position. Their snaps must fit within the holder’s catching frame and, on punts, be on target so punters can execute their punts after taking steps. The role also includes covering punts and sometimes making tackles, requiring athleticism, toughness, focus, and physicality similar to that of an offensive lineman or linebacker build. It explains why the position is called “long snapper,” noting typical snap distances (about 7 yards for extra points/field goals and about 15 yards for punts) and provides abbreviations for deep and short snappers. It lists skills and a general body type estimate, names Zak DeOssie and Don Mulbach as notable long snappers, and emphasizes the importance of accuracy and minimal error, citing that missed field goals and blocked punts can result from failures.

The passage is an “Inside UT Football: October 5, 2000” newsletter from the Dallas Morning News, featuring Q&A with Chip Brown, Texas and Oklahoma football discussion, and reader questions. Brown includes selected quotes from Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops about Oklahoma’s 4-0 season outlook, last year’s turnovers, UT quarterback rotation, and Oklahoma’s running game, and he answers multiple Texas-related queries on topics such as the Royal-Memorial Stadium expansion, player situations (including Adam Doiron, Sean Rogers), UT offense and quarterback rotation (Major Applewhite and Chris Simms), special teams and punt issues, game outlook for Texas vs. Oklahoma, Texas’ scoring streak and next year’s schedule, the state of the football field turf, media criticism of Mack Brown and the team, and the time of the Colorado game (2:30 p.m. Central, not televised).

The passage reports attendance increases for Biloxi’s Shuckers at MGM Park, including 4,066 attendees for a Jackie Robinson Day celebration and a 21 percent rise over last year’s opening series. It also notes ESPN’s SportsCenter highlighted a top play by Shuckers center fielder Johnny Davis, which gained 767,000 Instagram views. The Shuckers play five games in Chattanooga before returning home on April 22, with an opening-night benefit jersey auction benefiting March of Dimes. The passage also mentions new weekly promotions and ticket availability online, at TicketMaster locations, and at the MGM Park Box Office.

An email forwards a Yahoo Groups digest (PAKK Digest Number 529) to Shelley Corman, suggesting she add the sender or join the group. The digest includes discussions among PAKK members about adoption-related travel and eligibility topics, including HIV testing and Russian/Kazakhstan visa requirements, availability of adoption travel discounts and contracted airfares through Travel-On/Delta, accommodation options in Kazakhstan (hotel versus apartment versus staying with a host family), and experiences/questions related to adopting from Taraz. Other threads discuss adoption “birth date” adjustments, including whether to change a child’s age for school placement while considering academic and social impacts.

The Trump administration announced it would continue much of the Obama administration’s nuclear weapons policy but adopt a more aggressive stance toward Russia. A sweeping nuclear posture review says Russia must be deterred from any limited nuclear attack in Europe through “unacceptably dire costs,” and calls North Korea a “clear and grave threat,” stating any attack on the U.S. or allies would end that regime. The review also describes China as a potential nuclear adversary and says the U.S. arsenal is tailored to prevent Beijing from believing it could gain advantage with nuclear weapons or that any limited nuclear use is acceptable. The report endorses modernizing the nuclear arsenal without a net increase in strategic nuclear weapons and supports existing arms control agreements, including New START limits. It concludes that further arms control progress is difficult given Russia’s actions in Ukraine and violations of existing deals. Administration officials briefed Russian and Chinese officials before the review’s release. The review seeks to counter Russia’s “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine by modifying a small number of Trident long-range ballistic missiles for smaller-yield warheads and, longer term, developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. Arms control groups criticized the review, and Russian officials had not commented immediately.

Ministers negotiating a working administration with the dinosaur-denying DUP admitted that progress might require abolishing line dancing. The DUP objects to line dancing because its founder, Reverend Ian Paisley, called it sinful, catering to lusts of the flesh, and “naff.” David Davis said compromise was needed and that ending Sunday trading was not possible, while other potential concessions were dismissed. He suggested that removing line dancing was preferable to letting Nigel Farage join the negotiation. Nigel Walker said he supported the decision and referenced Brexit and related concerns.

Language comprehension development in early childhood progresses through milestones, with infants distinguishing speech phonetic sounds and toddlers expanding comprehension through vocabulary growth, grammatical understanding, and contextual meaning. This process reflects both genetic factors and environmental input, and deficiencies or deprivation can hinder language acquisition. The paper describes three language comprehension phenotypes in autistic individuals—Command (simple commands), Modifier (adds color/size/number modifiers), and Syntactic (adds spatial prepositions, verb tenses, flexible syntax, possessive pronouns, complex explanations, and fairy tales). The authors hypothesized typically developing children follow the same sequence and sought assessments to characterize these phenotypes between ages 2 and 4.

Existing sentence-level assessments were judged unsuitable due to age norms and/or task complexity, prompting development of a new 15-item Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA) intended to track progression toward the Syntactic phenotype in children aged 2 to 5 using toy-animal manipulatives and brief verbal instructions. Each item is scored based on whether children complete at least 3 of 4 tasks, with total scores ranging from 0 to 15. A parent version, the Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC), uses the same command/modifier/syntactic structure and similar response options.

In a neurotypical sample of 116 children (mean age 4.34 years), LPA scores increased from about ages 1.5 to 5, with a plateau afterward. Using preset criteria, the median acquisition ages were 1.6 years for Command, 3.0 years for Modifier, and 3.7 years for Syntactic; all neurotypical children acquired Command by 3 years, Modifier by 4 years, and Syntactic by 5 years. LPA showed high internal consistency and strong test-retest reliability and inter-observer agreement, and LPA scores correlated strongly with LPEC scores (r = 0.78). In 79 children diagnosed with ASD, fewer reached the Syntactic milestone than neurotypical peers (39% via clinician LPA and 45% via parent LPEC). The study concludes that the LPA can support early identification and monitoring of language comprehension deficits, including in minimally verbal children.

A national poll by EducationNext finds that support for charter schools has dropped from 51% last year to 39% this year, while support for other school-choice options has slightly shifted. Support for universal vouchers is 45%, and support for tax-credit scholarships is 55%.
