The charter drop was consistent across Democrats and Republicans and across racial and ethnic groups, and the article suggests the wording about “formation” may explain part of the change. The poll also shows a partisan reversal on universal vouchers: Republicans increased support to 62% while Democrats decreased to 50%. The poll measures a “Trump effect,” finding Republicans respond more favorably to issues when told Trump supports them, Democrats the opposite, with Trump’s overall net influence described as nearly nil. Despite differences, approval of local public schools is similar among Republicans (55%) and Democrats (54%).

The passage describes robotic systems for selectively gripping and transporting objects using robotic multi-gripper assemblies with addressable vacuum regions. It outlines how target objects are identified using captured image data, how selected vacuum regions draw in air to independently grip the identified objects, and how the robot transports and releases the objects, either simultaneously or sequentially. The robotic setup is described in the context of warehouse/shipping operations, including use of imaging systems, controllers, vacuum grippers with manifold assemblies, sensors for tracking and force/contact measurements, and transport plans. It also describes method flows for operating the system, including generating base motion plans, verifying pickup with vision and grip measurements, performing regripping actions when grip thresholds fail with an iteration counter, and continuing or stopping the plan based on whether thresholds are met.

On Feb. 16, the Fraser Institute will release a study on carbon pricing titled “Examining the Revenue Neutrality of British Columbia's Carbon Tax.” The study examines whether B.C. carbon tax revenues are offset by tax reductions elsewhere and how much the B.C. government collects through higher taxes. Revenue neutrality was a promise when the tax was introduced in 2008, and policymakers are looking at B.C.’s carbon tax as a possible model. A news release will be issued on Feb. 16 at 5:00 a.m. Eastern.

The passage describes the De'Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker, which is $200 off and priced at $1,300 even at the discount. It features a built-in touchscreen to select milk-based drinks and handles the process automatically after configuring the grinder and settings. The machine has a swappable hopper for different beans and includes a “bean adapt” function that fine-tunes settings per bean type and brews a test cup. It uses its own milk frother to produce micro-foam and is easier than manual options, though it may not match the quality of a classic portafilter machine.

The passage explains pointwise versus uniform convergence for sequences of functions. It states that uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but gives examples where pointwise convergence does not imply uniform convergence (using \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\)). It then introduces the issue of interchanging limits and frames three related questions for sequences of functions: whether the limit preserves continuity, differentiability (including whether derivatives commute with the limit), and integration (whether the limit of integrals equals the integral of the limit). The answers are presented as “yes” under uniform convergence and “no” under only pointwise convergence, illustrated by examples. The passage proceeds to prove the theorems corresponding to the “yes” statements: the uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous; the integral commutes with uniform limits; and if \(f_n\) and \(f_n'\) converge uniformly, then \(f\) is differentiable with \(f'=g\). Finally, it presents Weierstrass’s M-test: if \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) with \(\sum M_j\) convergent, then \(\sum f_j(x)\) converges absolutely for each \(x\) and uniformly, providing a method to establish uniform convergence of series of functions.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya from Myanmar, was officially declared a refugee by UNHCR. He describes spending four birthdays in Manus prison, arriving in Papua New Guinea on October 29, 2013 at age 19. He recounts being placed in Delta compound with about 300 men in a narrow shipping-container room, where daily life involved long queues and shortages for necessities like toilets, showers, washing, razors, and washing powder. He describes praying in D block because there was no dedicated place to pray, feeling distressed and crying often, and later moving to Mike compound at the end of 2013, where he says conditions remained harsh despite a larger, newly constructed area. He notes limited space for recreation, discomfort from heat in metal shipping containers, and restrictions on activities and communication, including limited phone access earlier on. He says he coped through learning and writing with help from teachers and a psychologist who gave him the motto “the pen is mightier than the sword.” He concludes by saying his detention has involved ongoing obstacles, pain, anguish, and in some cases death, and expresses hope for freedom and survival elsewhere.

The passage describes how total solar eclipses have historically been interpreted with fear or religious significance. It cites beliefs from the ancient Greeks, Vikings, and ancient Chinese, and an 1878 total eclipse in which many Americans were terrified, believing it meant Jesus’s return and Judgment Day, leading to a tragic suicide and murder. It also notes that some Christians and Catholics today may worry the upcoming Aug. 21 eclipse signals the end of days, while Sister Mary Elizabeth says the Passionist Nuns’ Monastery will watch the eclipse confidently and not view it as a bad omen. The passage further mentions an Islamic explanation that eclipses are signs of God, not evidence tied to human death. It concludes that even nonreligious observers may find eclipses awe-inspiring, with David Baron comparing the experience to standing on the rim of the Grand Canyon and describing it as making people feel small in the universe.

A funnel-web spider, described as the world’s most venomous, was spotted in a house in Springwood in the Blue Mountains near Sydney. Bec Sheedy noticed a black, fang-bearing spider on a wall and quickly identified it as a funnel-web. The passage says funnel-web venom can rapidly shut down the nervous system and has been linked to human deaths; it also notes 13 deaths recorded in Australia and advises going to hospital immediately if bitten. Funnel-webs are common around east-coast households but rarely seen, living from Queensland to New South Wales, with a new species found in northern Tasmania. They are attracted to cool, damp environments and are often found in bathrooms, laundry areas, or pool filter contexts, and can survive submerged for days. They are described as defensive rather than aggressive and as unlikely to be fatal today due to antivenene introduced in 1981, though caution is urged (e.g., don’t pick them up, wear gloves when gardening, and avoid putting hands into areas they may be in). The passage adds that they play a role in the ecosystem by killing insects such as cockroaches, flies, and mosquitoes.

The passage describes a “Triangle (1-3-1) Offense” strategy to attack the Diamond & One defense by placing the “Star” player in the middle and running triangle action to isolate the Star 1-on-1 against the “Chaser,” who is primarily responsible for pass denial but may be unprepared for post defense. It outlines role assignments and sequences, including high post entry, drive right/left options, kick out passes, post flashes, and lob exchanges when the high post pass is overplayed. It also emphasizes execution and coordination for success, requiring preparation for high post isolations, back cuts, interior passing, and spot-up shots, along with defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. The passage recommends scouting opponents to anticipate defensive reads and counters, watching for changes after substitutions and timeouts, using varied alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. It concludes with a description of the Diamond & One defense as a box-and-one derivative where four players zone and the fifth defender maintains strong pass denial against the opponents’ scoring ace, typically best against one-guard (odd or one guard front) offenses.

KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo said this year’s Apple Watch model will keep the same design as previous iterations, meaning three generations will share the same form factor. The passage notes that between the original Apple Watch (unveiled in 2014) and last year’s refresh, the only design change was a slight increase in thickness. Kuo also predicted no obvious change in form factor and said LTE connectivity is the key, with LTE and non-LTE versions in 38mm and 42mm sizes. The passage discusses uncertainty about what a form factor overhaul would change and suggests thickness could be easier to adjust than form factor. It ends with a question asking whether the Apple Watch is due for a form factor change.

The speaker binds himself to faithfully perform the duties of his office, vowing to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution. He states that the Constitution defines the Executive’s powers and purposes of government, and he describes the past progress under it, including expanded population and territory, laws and executive and judicial operations, peace and commerce treaties, and improved economic and social conditions. He acknowledges remaining hardships from disease, foreign wrongs and war, and internal dissensions linked to disagreements about republican government, foreign policy, and sectional interests. He argues that political party conflicts have largely been resolved and outlines shared principles: popular will, limited sovereignty, election accountability, economy in spending, subordination of the military to civil power, freedom of press and religious opinion, and a peace-focused policy and union. He reviews the relationship between federal and state governments, emphasizing respect for state rights and national authority where federative or foreign interests are involved. He then summarizes his immediate predecessor’s policy priorities—peace with defense, justice toward other nations, support for freedom and equal rights, debt reduction, limited military force, army organization, internal improvements, and Indian and internal development—along with specific actions taken. He proposes to continue and complete those improvements, especially internal improvements, while calling for legislative deliberation on constitutional authority. Finally, he explains his confidence in legislative and executive departments, cooperation of states, and public support, and concludes with reliance on divine providence.

A recent college graduate living at home says she has no savings and will earn about $1,600 per month from a three-month 9-to-5 minimum-wage job starting next week. She must pay tuition ($1,700), certification exams (~$600), and save for a car and an apartment. She claims her mother demands $100 weekly rent and $80 monthly for a phone, totaling $480 per month, and says her mother has previously made her pay rent (including $3,000 over four months while student teaching). She describes a recent conflict where, due to her hearing problems, she did not realize her mother was speaking to her, after which her mother yelled that she would have to pay to continue living at home. She asks whether she can handle the situation without ruining their relationship. The response suggests four steps: manage money, possibly get a second or third job, take time for perspective and consider trying other experiences while waiting for her teaching career, and be honest, adding that the writer finds parts of her account concerning and suggests her mother may need professional help if her description is accurate.

The passage is a proclamation by President James Madison (September 1, 1814) responding to British actions during the war. It describes the British invading the U.S. capital, destroying public buildings and archives, and placing Alexandria in range of a naval force that plundered private property. It states that the British commander avowed a purpose to destroy and lay waste assailable coastal towns and districts, claiming retaliation for alleged U.S. destruction in Upper Canada that the passage says did not occur. The proclamation characterizes these actions as disregard for humanity and civilized warfare, and calls for Americans to unite to chastise and expel the invader. Madison instructs all officers, civil and military, to execute their duties, especially requiring military district commanders to prepare defenses and authorize use of convenient militia portions for threatened places. The document is signed by Madison and countersigned by James Monroe, Secretary of State.

The passage describes a tough loss and says the team needs to rebound throughout the playoffs. It states the team played well but gave up too many chances in the third period, possibly due to not executing well in the last ten minutes. It notes the team lost two goal leads, gave Detroit credit for battling hard, and calls the outcome frustrating, though it also says the team will continue.

The passage describes a tight hockey game with several scoring chances and key moments involving puck bounces off sticks and boards. The speaker says multiple shots were blocked, and a bounce led to the puck hitting Flower’s leg and eventually resulting in a goal by the other team. They also discuss that their team expected a tight contest, made some mistakes, and had opportunities that “didn’t go in,” which may have made the difference. Another moment includes a puck rolling and resting on Osgood’s back after a shot, with the goalie covering it and questions raised about the rules, but no goal. The speaker concludes that, despite the loss and giving up goals in the first and last minutes, there was still time left in the game, and they plan to prepare for the next game.

The passage contains multiple news items from May 9, 2001, including: Questia laying off about half its workforce as it slows book additions to its online college library; Wall Street indexes ending mixed ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting, with bond yields rising and stock movements discussed; and several Enron-related reports. These include Enron saying Japan’s deregulated power market lacks competition and needs an independent regulator; Williams preparing to expand into Europe’s deregulating gas and power markets; and multiple reports about Dabhol Power Company in India, including executive families being moved to Singapore, disputes involving the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) and arbitration plans, claims and denials about capacity use and government pressure, and coverage of lenders and other companies’ plans related to the Dabhol power purchase agreement and Enron’s equity stake.

The passage describes an optimization-phase study using the MOST framework to develop a mobile health platform (Way to Health) for promoting sleep in children aged 9–12 with insufficient sleep. Participants completed a 2-week run-in period, then were randomized to a 7-week intervention plus a 2-week follow-up. The core intervention included sleep tracking and weekly performance feedback, with candidate components varied in a 25 factorial design: guideline-based vs personalized sleep goals, child-directed vs caregiver-directed loss-framed financial incentives, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging. Sleep duration was measured at home using a Fitbit sleep tracker. No study week-by-component interactions were detected and no single component met the ≥30-minute optimization criterion. However, component combinations met the criterion: two top-ranked combinations (both including sleep tracking, performance feedback, a sleep goal setting, a caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and/or daily routine messaging) increased average weeknight sleep duration by ≥30 minutes during intervention and follow-up. The passage concludes that optimal component settings for the platform increased sleep duration by at least 30 minutes and may be implementable in pediatric primary care, while noting limitations including single-site sampling and a short follow-up period.

The passage reports that at least 30 children died at Gorakhpur BRD Hospital. It says a central team visiting the facility found the hospital had accommodated patients at 10 times its admission capacity. The team reportedly raised concerns about Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs), stating that each infant warmer was shared by multiple infants. It notes that SNCUs are typically 12–20 bed units and that monitoring quality is a problem, with sick babies still being referred to tertiary care despite SNCUs. It adds that SNCUs in nearby districts like Basti and Ballia are either non-existent or non-functional, and that babies are still referred to BRD Hospital. The report also says there is a problem with oxygen supply, with standby cylinders being used, and that overcrowding is the real issue. It further mentions that Union Health Minister J P Nadda, Minister of State Anupriya Patel, and health secretary C K Mishra announced a regional medical centre in Gorakhpur costing Rs 85 crore for research on children’s diseases.

The passage introduces deontic argumentation as reasoning about whether actions or states are obligatory, permitted, or deontically qualified, especially in legal and dialogical settings. It argues that weak permission—where permission follows from not deriving the obligation to the contrary—poses specific challenges for existing argumentation semantics. The authors note that grounded and stable semantics fail to support weak permission when there is a conflict between two applicable obligations, formalizing this with a “conflictual” theory definition and proving that weakly facultative conclusions cannot be derived in those cases.  

To address this, the passage defines a Deontic Argumentation Theory, formalizes attack relations, and develops a new “wp-semantics” (wp-acceptable/wp-rejected) extending defeasible-logic argumentation to handle weak permission using imaginary arguments. It proves that the wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, and does not allow any argument to be both justified and rejected. It further shows that wp-justified conclusions include weak permission in “wp-conflictual” theories, and that wp-semantics extends grounded semantics. The discussion contrasts the approach with other frameworks and summarizes that the proposed semantics resolves limitations of grounded semantics regarding weak permission under unresolved obligation conflicts.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow rapidly over the forecast period due to innovations in packaging, sustainable and smart product designs, and increasing demand from emerging economies. Aluminum packaging provides a resistant, hygienic barrier for beverages, food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics, and is corrosion-resistant and non-toxic. Market growth is influenced by the pharmaceutical industry and demand from cosmetic and personal care sectors, while barriers include inadequate recycling processes in some countries. The market is also seeing trends in manufacturer research and development focused on cost reduction. Changes in packaging forms, technological innovation, and competitive dynamics, along with evolving consumer expectations, support growth, especially in Asia Pacific, expected to be the fastest-growing region with rising per capita income and purchasing power. The market is projected to grow at about 4.5% CAGR.

MyWorld is a new gaming platform that lets users build their own games and choose elements such as objects, genre, scenes, rules, and who can play (single-player, PvP, or Co-Op). Game building occurs in design mode (quickly placing/removing objects) and constructor mode (designing placed objects in a model editor). Players can create functional designs like turrets, sensors, and robots, and can level up by building and playing to unlock pre-built materials. MyWorld creators can also customize their avatars, and created games can be stored locally or uploaded to share and improve through the community. The platform has been demonstrated on livestream but is not ready for release; the team has launched a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign, with early backers receiving exclusive materials.

The passage says naïve Forex traders often believe success requires super talent and quick, easy profits, which the market can mislead them into. It advises avoiding external influences, waiting for profitable trade setups, making independent decisions, and developing mental stability to handle losses and avoid taking excessive risks without understanding market probabilities. It states that becoming profitable requires mastering technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis, and that traders should rely on their own judgment rather than copying others. The passage also recommends taking experts’ advice carefully, starting with small “baby steps,” and thinking twice before following guidance due to limited experience and differing opinions.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that at its 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on October 7, 2021, stockholders voted on nine proposals. Proposal 1 elected James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk as Class II directors. Proposals 2, 3, and 7 through 9 were not approved. Proposals 4, 5, and 6 were approved, including ratifying PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2021 and approving non-binding advisory proposals on one-year director terms and additional reporting on diversity and inclusion. The report is signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, dated October 13, 2021.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 5, 2019. It reported that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President, Retail, would depart effective April 15, 2019, and that Deirdre O’Brien assumed the role of Senior Vice President, Retail + People effective February 5, 2019. The report was signed on February 6, 2019 by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The NTSC and Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) plan to partner to improve vendor cybersecurity by promoting adoption of cloud security best practices. They aim to standardize and improve cloud security vendor reviews by strengthening CSA’s Security, Trust & Assurance Registry (STAR) and related tools, seeking to streamline vendor security review processes, reduce effort for vendors, and create a STAR-based questionnaire mapping to common compliance frameworks. They will collaborate on research, participate in each other’s events, discuss issues in working groups, and publish a joint whitepaper on the program. The passage also describes the roles of the NTSC and CSA in advocacy, best-practice promotion, and cloud security education and activities.

An electrical appliances maker said it submitted a bid on September 20, 2017 as an expression of interest for the business and brand of Consumer Electricals Ltd (CGCEL), a subsidiary of Kenstar within the Videocon group. The company said the bid was made in response to an invitation from Videocon Industries and affiliates dated September 6, 2017, but did not disclose the bid price. It stated results of the bid process have not been announced and no binding transaction documents or negotiations have occurred so far. The Videocon group, facing debt of over Rs 40,000 crore, has considered selling parts of its businesses, including earlier asset sales and a plan to merge its direct-to-home business.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to offer modest women more attractive swimwear. They found demand from women with medical procedures or skin conditions, including those who had mastectomies or bariatric surgeries who wanted garments for support and concealment, and those with skin cancer or psoriasis who needed all-over skin protection. The company now designs athletic wear such as swim tops with built-in mastectomy bras, compression workout gear, and skin-protecting suits with sleeves and longer legs. Teutsch says customers report feeling newly empowered to be active after finding HydroChic. Before starting the company, the two were educators and met while working as sales representatives at a women’s hat business; they became inspired by a beach trip in 2006 due to their shared love of swimming and dislike of revealing suits.

Legal experts expect the Supreme Court’s new term to frequently address higher education, though only two main-docket cases—both about transgender rights—are currently listed. A secondary “shadow docket” allows the Court to issue interim decisions quickly, sometimes in days or weeks, using an emergency-style process that can bypass traditional steps and create uncertainty. Higher education institutions have seen effects from shadow-docket decisions, including reversals of lower-court rulings on issues such as staffing cuts at the Department of Education and stays on actions affecting immigration policies. Experts say likely future areas include visa policies, First Amendment rights, academic freedom, and federal funding. The two sports-related cases are West Virginia v. B.P.J and Little v. Hecox, involving barred participation in track and cross-country under state law after presidential directives on “gender ideology” and transgender women’s sports. Even if some cases are dismissed, other cases may proceed, especially those involving Title IX’s equal protection clause, with potential impacts beyond sports. The shadow docket also includes Trump v. Orr, which concerns whether a passport can match gender identity and could affect other identification practices used by universities. Experts add that shadow-docket outcomes may leave little time to prevent policy effects before final rulings, making temporary remedies crucial.

Riley Oil Company is a family business in Paoli, Indiana that has operated for decades and aims to continue. It is one of the last full service gas stations in the area, where employees pump gas, wash windshields, and check oil for free. Daniel McCabe started working there in August as a gas pump assistant, and customers say staying in their cars while staff handle services is a treat. Owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley say the service began in 1971 with Jeff’s father and that family involvement remains central, including the growing number of family members working there and their choice not to charge extra for the service.

Employees of an Oklahoma City Taco Bell called police early Tuesday after a woman they believed had a crowbar chased and threatened them, destroyed cash registers, and demanded money. Police said 52-year-old Zette Madden smashed glass at the entrance doors and drive-thru window and damaged the drive-thru menu, causing thousands of dollars in damage. Officer Phillip Paz captured her standing on the other side of the smashed glass and said he told her seven times to drop the weapon, which he identified as a tire iron. After she ignored his commands, he used his taser, and she was taken to a local hospital for cuts on her hands. Taco Bell employees said she previously trespassed and allegedly tried to steal soda. Madden remains in the Oklahoma County Jail on charges including malicious injury and destruction of property, robbery in the first degree, and robbery with a dangerous weapon.

Titanium and its alloys have properties such as high strength, low density, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility, and they are used in applications ranging from medical implants to aerospace. Their behavior depends on alloy composition, thermo-mechanical treatments, crystallography, and temperature. The study focuses on deformation mechanisms in single-crystalline α-titanium (hcp α-phase stable up to ~882 °C, with β-phase stable above), using atomistic molecular dynamics nanoindentation at 10 K, 300 K, and 600 K for three orientations ([0001], [10̅10], [2̅110]). The work couples nanoindentation simulations with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping to relate slip system activation to temperature-dependent stress, dislocation activity, and surface morphology. Load–displacement curves show an elastic Hertzian response followed by pop-in for [0001], while prismatic orientations show smoother nucleation. Dislocation analysis identifies dominant basal a-type dislocations, with pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ slip becoming more active at higher temperatures. Surface features and shear strain maps indicate localized deformation at low temperature and more diffuse behavior at 600 K, with distinct pile-up and slip-trace morphologies by orientation. Dislocation density calculations show the highest density in [0001] across temperatures, with lower densities in prismatic orientations at elevated temperatures. The study concludes that both temperature and crystallographic orientation strongly determine nanoscale plasticity under nanoindentation and reproduces surface features consistent with AFM experiments.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 2, 2022. The report states that Microsoft updated its guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022 due to unfavorable foreign exchange rate movement through May, and that a slide deck with revised guidance is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes forward-looking statement cautions and notes that the information is not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. Exhibit 99.1 is listed, along with an Interactive Data File, and the report is signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Alexander (Sasha) Arkhipkin said that where no regional fisheries management organisation exists, high-seas fishing is often unregulated with limited information on fishing vessels, catch, species composition, and sizes. He noted that in the Southwest Atlantic, more than 250 jiggers and trawlers take hundreds of thousands of tons of resources each year, constraining stock assessments of straddling stocks and increasing overfishing risk. Arkhipkin also described concerns in the Eastern Pacific, where foreign vessels fishing for jumbo squid increased to almost 300, prompting fisheries management institutions in Mexico, Peru, and Chile to raise concerns. In September 2017, IMARPE organized an international workshop in Lima where Arkhipkin spoke on squid life cycles; recommendations were developed on acoustic survey designs, stock structure analysis, and stock assessment techniques to be implemented by IMARPE to improve knowledge and assess the impact of high-seas fisheries on squid stocks within their EEZ.

The passage describes wireless communication systems and techniques for physical layer preambles and signaling, particularly for WLAN transmissions. It discusses WLANs composed of access points (APs) and stations (STAs) using packet structures (PPDUs) with preamble portions that include legacy and non-legacy signaling. It introduces a universal signal field (U-SIG) followed by version-specific signal fields such as Extremely High Throughput (EHT) signal fields (EHT-SIG), where the U-SIG includes version-related and frequency-occupation information (including PPDU bandwidth and puncturing information) and where packet formats determine the content of subsequent fields. The EHT-SIG can provide signaling for STA scheduling and data interpretation, including resource unit (RU) allocation and spatial stream configuration, and may vary across subchannels and content channels. The disclosure also covers signaling parallelization across subchannels/content channels, puncturing support, flexible RU allocations for OFDMA and MU-MIMO, and optimization goals such as minimizing preamble length and accommodating different signal-field types and future protocol versions.

Nintendo’s Labo line of cardboard accessories will include, as part of the Toy Con Garage, a kit for building cardboard gizmos. Nintendo confirmed this at an event in New York, showing a brief look in a promo video and describing the Toy Con Garage workshop as a basic set of inputs, actions, and if-then statements. Nintendo demonstrated potential creations including a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis. The passage says it is unclear whether a Labo set is required for access to the app.

Darren Till defeated Stephen Thompson by unanimous decision in the main event of UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool, England on Sunday, May 27, 2018. The decision was described as close and controversial, with some arguing it could have gone the other way if not fought in Liverpool. Till said he is willing to rematch “Wonderboy” in America as soon as possible, stating Thompson is not injured and that experts attributed concerns to the location. The fight featured little action aside from Till’s knockdown in the final round, and some disagreed with claims that Till won four of five rounds.

Brian Sandoval, former Republican governor of Nevada and president of the University of Nevada at Reno, is defending UNR’s UndocuPack program for undocumented students after the Department of Justice directed the university to be investigated. The DOJ letter said it received reports that UNR helped “illegal immigrants” through referrals, student aid, and academic and career support, including help finding jobs that do not require a Social Security Number. Sandoval said UndocuPack provides support to all students regardless of citizenship status and uses no federal funds, adding that UNR remains compliant with federal and state law and plans to respond through legal channels. Advocates said the DOJ action is part of broader federal efforts to limit higher-education benefits for undocumented students and could lead campuses to scale back or close support programs, with some schools and scholarship providers weighing how to respond.

The passage describes a mobile payment invention for processing offline transactions when disconnected from payment servers. User devices in an e-wallet can be set to an “offline payment mode,” enabling offline payments without external network connectivity; offline mode is enabled for only one device per e-wallet at a time to prevent overdrawing. When offline, a merchant payment system and a user device communicate via a local communications connection to exchange an offline payment request and a payment approval message, which the merchant stores and later provides to a payment server once connectivity is restored. The payment server processes offline transactions using offline transaction information and avoids duplicate processing by using transaction identifiers, including checking whether an offline transaction ID was previously received. The passage also describes transferring the offline mode between user devices using local communications when both devices are offline, including temporarily suspending and then disabling/enabling the offline mode, and provides example system components and flowcharts for enabling offline mode, transferring it, and conducting and processing offline transactions.

The passage describes the “High Post Split Offense,” an offense built on quick high-post splits, down screens, and back cuts. It emphasizes that execution—not complexity—makes the offense effective, using a 2-3 high alignment to free the baseline for cuts, create scoring opportunities for all five players, reduce weakside help, and generate strong offensive rebounding and second efforts. It outlines phases including: Phase 1 (high post split reads/counters), Phase 2 (down screens and options like down-screen feeds, double splits, and back screens, plus various defensive-read counters such as curl, fade, back cut, screen and roll, and slip), Phase 3 (high post isolation after the split with “triple threat” options and counters to overplay such as over-the-top lobs), and Phase 4 (strong post ups when defenders focus on shooters). It also lists variations (e.g., flop/back cut entry, wing pass entry, wing double away entry, post single/double) and discusses offensive rebounding principles, required spacing/execution/coordination, and the importance of individual skill development and preparing to defend the offense.

The passage describes a tonneau cover for pickup truck beds that provides a covering for the truck bed when used with the truck’s side walls and tailgate, helping create a secure storage compartment. It outlines various cover features, including latch and pinch handle systems, panel sections that are selectively movable for bed access, and other components such as support assemblies, sealing elements, connector systems, and side rails. 

An illustrative embodiment includes a pickup truck with opposing upward-extending side walls and a tonneau cover with a fixed base panel over the bed, plus multiple pivotable panel sections secured by first and second latching assemblies. Each latching assembly includes pinch latch assemblies with latch handles, spring pockets, guides, guide tabs, springs, inner pinch handle portions with slots, and mechanisms that move latches between latched and unlatched conditions. The passage further explains embodiments where activating one pinch latch can unlatch latches on both sides of a panel section via a longitudinally extending connector, and mentions integrated lights positioned near latching locations. 

The passage also describes hinge assemblies for folding panel sections, side bed rails with rail clips and clamps, sealing approaches to reduce water ingress, gusset support structures for holding panels upright when the cover is open, and a securement system using buckles to keep panels in an upright stowed configuration. It includes an overview of the drawings and a general description of figure contents related to these components.

A Bank of England regulator, Vicky Saporta, said British banks should not expect major further changes to capital or liquidity requirements because most Basel III reforms have been implemented. She said the Bank’s future focus would be on new risks and unintended consequences of existing regulation, including resilience to cyber-attacks and research suggesting post-crisis leverage rules may have discouraged central clearing and settlement of over-the-counter derivative trades. She also reiterated that the BoE does not want regulatory standards to slip after Brexit in March 2019.

Aaron Judge suffered an elbow injury in late July, missed 10 days after an IL stint, returned as a DH for nearly a month, and then went back to the outfield in early September. His arm strength appeared reduced, with him making shorter throws. Despite the injury, he hit .331/.457/.688 with 53 home runs and 114 RBIs in the regular season and .500/.581/.692 with one home run and seven RBIs in the playoffs. In offseason remarks about the elbow, Judge said he will “do some work on it and get it right,” but said he does not know whether surgery is needed.

The passage is largely an excerpt of Microsoft’s Form 10-K materials for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, including exhibit-like data tags, the cover page information (including registered securities and filer status), the table of contents, and narrative sections under Part I Item 1 (“Note About Forward-Looking Statements” and “Business”). It describes Microsoft’s mission and product and service offerings across cloud, AI, productivity, devices, gaming, and search advertising; outlines its R&D groups, distribution and licensing programs, operating segments, competition and risk factors; and includes sections on corporate social responsibility, human capital resources (employment levels, culture, diversity and inclusion, total rewards, wellness and safety, and learning and development), and company information about executive officers and investor resources.

The passage describes a semiconductor packaging approach in which semiconductor dies and interconnect structures are fabricated and tested before being assembled into a multi-chip module and wafer-level package. It explains that solder bump connections can be affected by thermal expansion mismatch among layered materials, which can lead to stress and delamination, and then outlines embodiments using reconstructed wafers, interconnect structures with through-substrate vias (TSVs), integrated fan-out (InFO) layers, underfill options, and encapsulation processes. The process includes bonding semiconductor components to redistribution layers (via direct Cu-to-Cu bonding or solder reflow), applying underfill (capillary underfill or moldable underfill), encapsulating in a molding device, thinning to expose contacts, and de-bonding the carrier substrate using thermal or UV-based methods to form external connections. It also discusses embodiments using a single universal interconnect structure shared by multiple dies, along with fabrication of dielectric layers, redistribution layers, passivation, under bump metallizations, and bump formation. The passage further states that these embodiments are intended to support super large package sizes for high-performance computing applications and to improve component and board-level reliability through testing and controlled bonding conditions.

The passage compiles multiple news items from Nov. 26, 2001 about Enron and related market and legal developments. It reports that Enron shares and bonds fell sharply and that investors showed increased doubt about Dynegy’s proposed takeover, citing concerns including financing needs, possible bankruptcy risk, and Enron’s deteriorating financial disclosures. It also describes a formal extension of Enron’s $690 million loan to Dec. 14, litigation alleging Enron mishandled its 401(k) plan (with plaintiffs seeking $850 million), and reporting on how Citigroup used credit default swaps and synthetic notes to manage Enron exposure. Other items mention energy-trading market concerns, a denial by India’s AV Birla group of interest in buying an Enron stake in Dabhol Power, and additional coverage of credit-rating implications for Dynegy if it acquires Enron.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, was jailed for 18 weeks after slashing his ex-lover and her daughter with a knife during an attack in January. The court heard Hodder had been drinking vodka and, after initially placing the knife to his own throat, attacked the two women. Magistrates described it as a sustained domestic attack while he was in drink, and Hodder admitted two assault charges. The older victim criticized the sentence, saying she cannot sleep or eat and that Hodder will be out soon, while the prosecution said he continued living with his ex. The defense said he had not been in trouble for six years.

The passage is a series of comments from Coach Julien and others about an ongoing injury evaluation, team performance in a recent game, and preparations for the next game. It says there is “no panic” and no further information beyond that he is being evaluated due to injury, with a possible return depending on updates. Julien discusses a replacement player’s performance, the team’s need for better starts and awareness near the net, and that game outcomes are influenced by momentum swings, penalties, and goaltending. He also addresses line pairings, depth and secondary scoring, adjustments between games, and the difficulty of predicting whether games will be high-scoring or penalty-filled. Additional remarks cover player roles and confidence in specific players, including David’s and Zdeno’s contributions and off-ice leadership, along with decisions about bench usage, matchups, and winning the next game.

Enerfax Daily (No. 937, Feb. 20, 2002) provides natural gas physical prices by region and a list of Henry Hub natural gas futures highs, lows, closes, and changes. It also includes an “Open Season” notice for SG Resources Mississippi, L.L.C. seeking firm storage services at the Southern Pines Energy Center (Feb. 4 to Mar. 4, 2002), along with commentary that March NYMEX natural gas rose on fund buying. Additional sections list natural gas futures volume, power bulletins, power and gas price tables, and reports such as a suit against JP Morgan Chase over Enron exposure, plans by El Paso Energy Partners to buy Texas natural gas assets, and AES to sell $1.0–$1.5 billion of assets. The email ends with a financial summary of several market indexes.

The passage describes TI’s Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS), including LFSS_B, which combines peripherals clocked by the 32 kHz LFCLK for long-term timekeeping and low-power operation. It lists LFSS_B components: RTC_B (real-time clock with prescaler extension and timestamp captures) and an asynchronous independent watchdog timer (IWDT). The RTC_B section explains its 32 kHz input clock operation and summarizes its counters, alarm and periodic interrupt options, calibration and drift compensation features, and device support table. It also describes IWDT_B as a supervisor with its own clock source that issues a POR reset if not reset in time, and outlines additional watchdog functionality (WWDT). The passage further includes overview information on timer peripherals (TIMGx and TIMAx) and brief notes on device analog connections, I/O muxing, serial wire debug (SWD), boot strap loader (BSL) requirements and invocation methods, factory constants, and other sections related to applications, documentation, and revision/support information.

The passage consists of multiple remarks about a hockey team’s performance in a playoff series, emphasizing that outcomes and momentum depend on team play and preparation rather than luck or individual factors. The speaker discusses having quality scoring chances, winning faceoffs, playing better in the second period, skating and involvement as positive changes, managing the puck and staying under control, and responding to mistakes. They also highlight the importance of winning faceoffs for ice time, leadership and poise in settling teammates, and the idea that the best team will win the Stanley Cup.

The speaker says they have been feeling better, noting that the past couple of days helped and that they improved each day. They discuss starting as a goalie in the NHL, explaining that sometimes it does not work out with the organization that drafts you, but in their case they had supportive general managers in Ottawa and were traded to Tampa, which gave them a chance to play. They say it took longer than expected and that additional time in the minors taught them how to be a pro, helping them be ready when they got their chance in Tampa. They also describe their approach to games as consistent across preseason, regular season, and playoffs, saying they prepare the same way and do not change anything even in do-or-die situations. They mention bouncing back after losses, feeling it will not change how the team responds tonight, and reflect that a past situation was enjoyable with a great group of guys.

Researchers at the University of Michigan say they have developed an “everything-repellent” or “omniphobic” clear, durable coating that can repel nearly every known liquid and prevent grime buildup. The coating can be applied to surfaces such as tables, floors, walls, and phone screens, and is made by mixing fluorinated polyurethane with F-POSS, which forms a surface layer. The work was inspired by an associate professor’s desire to make cleaning up after his child easier, and the next phase is to ensure the material is not toxic.

The court granted Defendant Waste Away Group, Inc.’s Motion for Summary Judgment in Paula Norrell’s Title VII lawsuit alleging (1) disparate treatment based on sex for refusing to promote her to district sales manager for a combined Montgomery and Opelika district, and (2) disparate impact employment practices. Norrell sought compensatory and punitive damages and attorneys’ fees.

For the failure-to-promote disparate treatment claim, the court found Norrell established a prima facie case. Waste Away articulated a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for promoting a male candidate, John White, citing White’s prior experience as district sales manager for the combined district and other qualifications, while noting Norrell lacked certain relevant outside sales and market knowledge. The court concluded Norrell’s evidence regarding alleged discriminatory statements and claims that she should have trained White did not demonstrate pretext or a genuine issue of material fact. The court also determined Johnson’s remark about pregnancy was an isolated, unrelated comment insufficient to show pretext.

For the disparate impact claim, Norrell stated she did not contend after discovery that she had a disparate impact claim, so summary judgment was granted on that claim as well. The court ordered final judgment for Waste Away, with costs taxed against Norrell.

The passage describes the Triangle Post Offense, created, developed, and refined over the years by Tex Winter. It is described as a system of defensive recognition and execution rather than set plays, using precise court spacing (players spaced 15–20 feet) and fundamental execution to spread defenses, prevent help/double-teaming, and enable passing. The offense involves three components—Entry, sideline triangle, and a weakside two game—where offensive options depend on what the defense is doing. It includes many sideline triangle entry methods and post split actions, aims to isolate and attack the post one-on-one, and provides weakside two game options initiated by pass or dribble, including drives, jumpers, rolls, cuts, lobs, and continuity actions. The passage also outlines automatic counter moves based on defensive overplays (e.g., fronting the post, sagging off, double-teaming, denying reversal passes, or denying backdoor entries). It concludes with guidance on teaching (whole-part-whole method, breakdown drills), practice structure for individual skill work, and game strategy/scouting, plus a “case for defense” noting the offense’s frequent use and the importance of learning how to disrupt it.

The passage explains Bollinger Bands as a widely used technical indicator for visualizing an asset’s volatility and potential trend changes. Developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, the bands consist of a central moving average with upper and lower bands calculated by adding and subtracting a multiple of standard deviation from the moving average. It notes that while Bollinger Bands can be useful, they can produce false signals, may be less effective in range-bound markets, can have signal delays, and are sensitive to time period and settings; they also require backtesting and well-defined trading rules to form a profitable system. The passage describes how to set up Bollinger Bands in TradingView using Pine Script functions (ta.sma and ta.stdev) with configurable moving average length, standard deviation multiplier, and source. It also mentions that Bollinger Bands can be used in breakout, mean reversion, or squeeze strategies, and that parameter optimization and risk definition are important; an example strategy on the H4 timeframe is cited as producing a considerable return but with uncomfortable drawdown.

Jane Goodall, who died on October 1 at age 91, had studied chimpanzees in Tanzania’s Gombe National Park for nearly 30 years and helped reveal the complexity of chimp social lives. The passage describes her collection of chimp skeletons: her team retrieved chimp bodies soon after death, cleaned them after insect removal, and preserved each skeleton with known details such as sex, age, body weight, and life experiences. This information enabled researchers to study how individual development affects skeletal features. Goodall also said that when working in the field, researchers “shouldn’t waste anything,” explaining her interest in preserving the bones of dead chimps alongside observing living ones. The passage uses Flo, a dominant Gombe matriarch who died in 1972, as an example of how her skeleton provided findings about body weight estimation from bones, bone loss patterns, and evidence related to menopause in female chimps living past 50.

The passage describes difficult early weeks of motherhood, focusing on the author’s experience during the second week after bringing babies home from the hospital. A follow-through day is a key concept in William J. O’Neil’s market-timing system, used to identify a change from a downtrend or market correction to a new uptrend. It occurs during a correction when a major index closes significantly higher than the previous day with greater volume, typically on Day 4 or later of an attempted rally. An attempted rally begins with Day 1, when a major equity index gains versus the prior day; Days 2 and 3 must not make a new low below Day 1’s low. A follow-through day confirms a new market uptrend, though the signal is not perfect and should be studied alongside leading stock behavior and sentiment. The passage also describes failure conditions, including the index making an entirely new low below the level used to start looking for Rally Day 1. The article includes a backtest on the S&P 500 using SPY, noting results were not good short term and improved slightly with an RSI filter, and it provides trading/backtesting rule details.

The double top chart pattern is a bearish reversal formation with two swing highs at roughly the same level and a swing low between them. The shared level acts as resistance, while a neckline is formed by connecting the swing low to the preceding swing low; breaking below the neckline suggests a potential downward reversal and possible end of an uptrend. Traders may close long positions or open short positions after a neckline break, and profit targets can be estimated by measuring the pattern height and projecting downward from the neckline. The passage also summarizes research referenced from Thomas Bulkowski’s work, noting that only 39% of double top formations reach their target. Identification and trading rules mentioned include finding an existing uptrend, having swing highs within 3% of each other, and waiting for a significant volume break below the neckline.

On Oct. 29, 2001, multiple reports described deterioration in corporate credit conditions and Enron’s declining stock and credit status. Reuters reported that corporate credit quality was expected to worsen, with about $100 billion of corporate debt likely to default this year, alongside extensive downgrades by Moody’s and defaults forecasts by Standard & Poor’s. A retired Metro Police homicide detective, Phil Ramos, reviewed newly released 1 October police body camera videos. A heat wave is expected to move west after the Fourth of July, bringing dangerous temperatures to areas including southern California. The passage discusses how education policy in the U.S. has shifted amid the 2024 political cycle, pandemic learning loss, and post-2020 racial and political tensions. It describes how COVID-19 increased scrutiny of schools, eroded trust, and made curricular and extracurricular decisions focal points for activism, with social media and partisan divides contributing to education becoming a central election issue.  

It then argues that cross-partisan education policy progress is still possible despite polarization and legislative gridlock, contrasting outcomes in many states with stagnation at the federal level. The passage identifies five recurring factors in successful cross-partisan initiatives: clear and easy-to-communicate policy proposals; responsiveness to local context; political cover for stakeholders; allowing both sides to claim a win; and using media to accelerate policy adoption. The conclusion emphasizes optimism that substantive cross-party education reforms are occurring in states and can meaningfully improve outcomes for students and communities.

The passage is largely a structured excerpt from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2021. The passage discusses the Indianapolis Colts’ upcoming 2018 NFL Draft and how general manager Chris Ballard’s rebuild makes it crucial. The passage discusses distributed system patterns and the book’s resources and permissions. It explains that distributed systems require reliability, scalability, and agility, and that while they are difficult to build, containers and container orchestrators help by enabling reusable patterns and components. It provides a history of software pattern development (algorithms, object-oriented patterns, open source) and defines what a pattern is in this context: general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without mandating specific technologies. It also describes single-node container grouping patterns—especially the sidecar pattern—covering how sidecars augment an application container (e.g., adding HTTPS, dynamic configuration synchronization, debugging tools, and building a simple PaaS), and how to design sidecars for modularity via parameterization, a stable API, and documentation. The passage then introduces multi-node concepts like microservices and contrasts monolithic systems with microservices, including benefits and downsides. Finally, it describes replicated load-balanced services and outlines related Kubernetes deployment examples, session tracking, caching and SSL termination layers, and then begins a discussion of sharded services and sharded caching, including the need to shard when state is too large for one machine.

Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral disease caused by Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), leading to millions of documented cases worldwide and often persisting joint and musculoskeletal pain. In Ethiopia, it has been detected since June 2016 and has since spread to multiple districts, with no approved vaccine or antiviral therapies; control relies on symptom relief and mosquito/vector elimination, supported by public education and improved diagnosis.

A systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD42023271579). It searched multiple databases and included observational studies in Ethiopia published in English from 2016 to November 2023 that reported lab-confirmed seroprevalence using serologic or virologic antibody detection methods (ELISA IgG, ELISA IgG+IgM) or RT-qPCR. Case reports and reviews were excluded, and specificity/sensitivity of tests were not considered. Two experts screened and extracted data, with quality assessment using PRISMA checklists and publication bias assessment using Begg’s test and Egger’s test.

From 40 identified articles (2016–2023), five eligible studies (cross-sectional: 4/5; case-control: 1/5) were included, covering regional states including SNNPR, Amhara, Tigray, Gambella, South Eastern Ethiopia, and Dire Dawa. Across included studies, ELISA was used in 4/5 studies and RT-qPCR in 1/5. The pooled seroprevalence of chikungunya in Ethiopia was reported as 12.35% (95% CI: -0.57, 0.81), with the highest prevalence in SNNPR (43.6%) and the lowest in Dire Dawa (approximately 12%). Within districts, Bebub Ari had the highest prevalence (51.58%) and Lare the lowest (6.25%).

The review found variation in seroprevalence by factors including occupation, education, age, and sex, though results for gender were inconsistent across studies. Subgroup analyses indicated significant heterogeneity overall, and differences between ELISA and RT-qPCR results. The authors concluded that chikungunya remains a public health concern in Ethiopia and recommended considering multiple factors and test types for virus detection, along with proactive preparedness, Ministry of Health collaboration, and public awareness campaigns.

The passage describes the Piotroski F-Score as a stock selection method developed by Joseph Piotroski that uses financial analysis to identify undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals. The F-Score is based on 9 criteria—profitability, liquidity, and efficiency—scored 1 or 0, with scores of 8 or 9 indicating strong fundamentals and 0 to 4 indicating poor financials. It is presented as a systematic approach used for selecting value and also potentially growth stocks, but it is not guaranteed to succeed and should be used alongside other research. The passage summarizes steps for applying, analyzing, and backtesting the strategy, including evaluating risk-return and implementing it in a portfolio. It also reports backtest results from Alpha Architect (NYSE stocks 1974 to Dec 2014) showing annual returns of 13.3% for Alpha Architect’s F-Score version, 12.6% for the original Piotroski score, and 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviations across portfolios. Additional tests include Alpha Architect’s results on cheap stocks (15.9% vs. 15.2% vs. 11.2%) and mentions ValueSignals testing on European stocks (June 1999 to 2011) and a thesis study on Norwegian and Swedish stocks (1997 to end of 2011).

Patrick McCaffery committed to Iowa on Thursday night, saying the decision came out of the blue despite expectations, after his father, Fran McCaffery, discussed a house Connor McCaffery would live in as an Iowa sophomore and that Patrick would live there as a Hawkeye. At oral argument, some Supreme Court justices appeared open to allowing trial judges to restrict what defense attorneys can discuss with clients overnight while the client remains on the stand. In David Villarreal’s case, the trial judge told his lawyer not to discuss Villarreal’s testimony overnight, though the lawyer could discuss trial strategy and client options; Villarreal was convicted and the Texas courts upheld the restriction. Stuart Banner argued the distinction between “trial strategy” and “about testimony” is unclear and could chill broader legal advice. Other justices questioned that, including Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, Justice Elena Kagan, and Justice Neil Gorsuch, leading to disagreement over how lawyer “coaching” or “management” differs from permissible guidance. During questioning, a prosecutor said advising a client about factors like mumbling or eye contact during an overnight recess would be coaching testimony, while Chief Justice John Roberts challenged that view and Justice Amy Coney Barrett discussed a potential rule. The debate also contrasted Texas’s proposed line between disallowed management of testimony and allowed matters indirectly touching testimony with the United States’ proposed bright-line rule prohibiting any discussion of the client’s testimony.

The passage explains motivations for breaking applications into containers, including resource isolation, separation of concerns, and enabling modular reuse and easier testing and deployment. It then focuses on the single-node sidecar pattern, describing how a sidecar augments an application container (e.g., adding HTTPS to a legacy service or managing dynamic configuration) by sharing resources like networking and filesystem. It discusses other benefits of sidecars such as modularity and reuse, and outlines how to design sidecars for modularity and reusability by parameterizing containers, defining a stable API, and documenting container usage. Later sections introduce other single-node patterns, including the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions (e.g., sharded Redis via a proxy) and the adapter pattern for converting heterogeneous interfaces into consistent ones for monitoring and logging (e.g., using Prometheus exporters or Fluentd). The excerpt concludes by contrasting single-node patterns with multi-node distributed systems, introducing microservices and distributed design patterns such as replicated load-balanced services and sharded services, including considerations for cache sharding, routing via sharding functions, and the use of consistent hashing.

The report and appendix cover events up to January 17, 1893, after which the narrative continues in the report accompanying the President’s message of February 15, 1893, sending to the Senate the treaty signed at Washington on February 14, 1893, by the U.S. Secretary of State and representatives of the Hawaiian Provisional Government. The passage also describes a chronological list of papers followed by a subject index, plus a bibliography and references to various congressional reports and printed documents. It includes document listings spanning 1826–1853 and then presents “Document 3,” the Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation between the United States and the Sandwich Islands, signed at Honolulu on December 23, 1826, with its articles of agreement and signatories, followed by dated notes from 1826 and 1829 regarding arrangements and instructions for cultivating friendly relations and gathering information.

The lecturer summarizes lower bounds for the predecessor problem, aiming to show that previously known upper bounds are essentially optimal. The focus is on proving an almost matching lower bound of \(\min\{\log_w n,\ \log n/\log\log w\}\) (with an unavoidable \(\log\log\) factor under polynomial-space assumptions, for static—no update—predecessor data structures). The discussion frames lower bounds using communication complexity and the cell-probe model, leading to a proof technique called round elimination. A historical survey reviews earlier predecessor lower bounds (Atjai 1988; Miltersen; Beame and Fich; and a round-elimination approach by Sen in 2003), and it notes later tight trade-offs by Patrascu and Thorup (2006–2007) that relate space and time.

To prove the bound, the lecture introduces the colored predecessor problem, where each stored element is colored red or blue and queries ask only for the color of the predecessor. Round elimination is used to show that if a protocol uses too few communication rounds (equivalently, cell probes), then iteratively removing messages would yield an overall success probability that contradicts the limits of best possible guessing. The proof proceeds by relating each message-elimination step to shrinking effective word size and problem size, producing a lower bound that matches the desired trade-off up to the \(\log\log\) factor.

Rudy Gestede said Middlesbrough must believe they can end their slump to avoid relegation risk ahead of their Premier League match against Arsenal on Monday. Middlesbrough have 22 goals, have not won since mid-December, and are 19th, six points from safety with seven games remaining. Gestede, who joined from Aston Villa in January and has made 10 appearances, hopes a change in luck can help the promoted side survive. He added Arsenal are a strong team, despite having won once in their last five league games and suffering a 3-0 defeat to Crystal Palace earlier in the week, and said Middlesbrough need to stay focused and play their way.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere architecture GA10x GPUs (GA102 and GA104) and their advancements over Turing, including faster performance (up to 1.7x in raster and up to 2x in ray tracing), improved power efficiency (up to 1.9x vs Turing), and new hardware features. It references figures, tables, and appendices that provide additional specifications and performance data.

Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara plans to launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October. The rollout will begin in Jakarta with four to five sites, then expand to other cities across Java and Bali, eventually covering 33 municipalities. Each plant is designed to process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily to generate an estimated 15 megawatts of electricity, with projected capital costs of 2 trillion to 3 trillion rupiah (around $180 million) per facility. Danantara will finance and oversee the projects with technology partners, while state utility PLN will purchase the electricity and integrate it into the national grid. The government has removed tipping fees for municipalities and local governments will provide land. The initiative aligns with Indonesia’s 2025–2034 electricity plan targeting 453 MW from waste-to-energy facilities and requires $2.72 billion in investment, aiming to reduce landfill reliance, cut emissions, and support renewable energy goals.

MTN and four banks plan multiple capital-raising exercises on the Ghana Stock Exchange between April and September to raise a combined GH¢4.67 billion, including MTN’s offer to raise GH¢3.48 billion by offloading 35% of the firm. The banks—Access Bank (GH¢450 million), Agricultural Development Bank (GH¢310 million), Republic Bank (GH¢255 million) and Societe Generale (GH¢170 million)—seek GH¢1.19 billion in total through rights issues to meet the Bank of Ghana’s new capital demand. A financial economist, Dr Sam Mensah, said the market has limited capacity and that the banks’ timing is risky, requiring a “plan ‘B” should targets fail. The passage also discusses potential currency (cedi) impacts depending on inflows, notes a larger pool of pension and other institutional funds following the National Pensions Act, and suggests foreign participation may be needed for success. Retail investor uptake is expected to depend on the offered value and, for rights issues, reduced share prices to encourage participation.

The passage describes how the COVID-19 pandemic has caused over 6 million deaths and significant economic and social disruption. It states that SARS-CoV-2 spike-targeting vaccines are effective overall, but vaccination can be less effective in immunocompromised patients, including those with autoimmune disease receiving immunosuppressive therapies, and that viral variants may partially evade antibody-mediated protection. The study focuses on rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab and compares their SARS-CoV-2 vaccine responses with healthy controls. Serum analyses after the second dose of Pfizer BNT162b2 or Moderna mRNA-1273 show that rituximab-treated individuals have almost no detectable anti-spike antibodies, while abatacept-treated individuals have significantly reduced spike-specific antibodies and decreased pseudovirus neutralization activity; MTX showed no significant decrease overall. Cellular analyses indicate that abatacept does not reduce the number of RBD-specific B cells in peripheral blood but reduces their activation and class switching toward IgG, alters memory B cell differentiation, decreases the proportion of S-specific CD4+ T cells in MTX and abatacept groups, and reduces production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 by S-specific CD4+ T cells in abatacept-treated subjects. The passage concludes that abatacept limits vaccine efficacy by impairing T cell help for B cell responses, and provides support for temporarily stopping abatacept before vaccination when clinically manageable.

The Supreme Court will consider on Oct. 14 whether the Constitution’s ex post facto clause applies to restitution imposed under 1996’s federal Mandatory Victims Restitution Act as part of a defendant’s criminal sentence. If it applies, Holsey Ellingburg would not have to pay more restitution than the law required when he robbed a bank; if it does not, later revisions to the restitution statute would increase his obligations. The passage says courts traditionally limit the clause to criminal punishments, not civil remedies, and it describes arguments that MVRA restitution is effectively criminal, including that it is set by the trial judge as part of a criminal sentence, uses criminal procedures, gives victims limited control, and involves incarceration for nonpayment. It also notes that restitution under the MVRA is described as serving “punitive purposes.” The passage suggests the outcome may be largely foreordained because the government will not defend the view that restitution is criminal, and that the Court’s majority may accept the government’s concession.

Delta Air Lines Inc announced its intention to acquire additional shares of Grupo Aeroméxico. Delta plans to start a tender offer after obtaining required regulatory approvals in Mexico and the United States. Delta currently owns about 4.1% of Grupo Aeroméxico’s outstanding shares and has an option to acquire an additional 8.1%. The deal is to acquire up to an additional 32% of outstanding capital stock, with an offer price of MXP$43.59 per share. After completion, Delta’s pension trust would own or have options to buy up to 49% of Grupo Aeroméxico’s outstanding shares.

Orthognathic treatment corrects dentofacial deformities and malocclusion using combined orthodontic and surgical management, with treatment taking months to years and potentially affecting patients’ quality of life (QoL) and willingness to undergo treatment. Because existing QoL questionnaires may be too general or lack construct validity for orthognathic surgery, the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) is used; however, translated versions have not undergone formal psychometric evaluation.  

The study aimed to assess reliability, validity, and responsiveness of an Arabic version of the OQLQ in Saudi Arabian adults seeking orthognathic treatment. The OQLQ contains 22 items across four domains, with higher scores indicating lower QoL. Translation followed a forward-backward process with expert review and pilot testing.  

In 74 participants, internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Test-retest reliability in 15 participants was generally excellent overall and for three domains, with “awareness of dentofacial deformity” showing good reliability. Validity was supported by correlations between OQLQ scores and satisfaction/appearance effects after surgery. Responsiveness was supported by significant decreases in overall OQLQ scores after surgery, and in paired analysis the facial aesthetics domain improved significantly. The study concludes that the Arabic OQLQ version is reliable, valid, and responsive, and recommends its use in future Arabic-speaking QoL research.
The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals dismissed the appeal after it was docketed, on motion of the appellant and with consent of the appellee, without costs to either party in that court.

Tradeshift, a supply chain payments and marketplaces startup, raised $250 million in a Series E round led by Goldman Sachs and PSP Investments, with additional participation from HSBC, H14, GP Bullhound, and Gray Swan. The funding brings Tradeshift’s total funding to more than $400 million, and the company claims its valuation has passed $1.1 billion. New investors join existing backers including HSBC, American Express Ventures, CreditEase Fintech Investment Fund, Notion Capital, Santander InnoVentures, and others. Mikkel Hippe Brun will join Tradeshift’s board.

Steve Pearse, an angel investor and former executive/entrepreneur, discusses starting and pitching startups. He emphasizes that only a small fraction of startups succeed, and that investors seek returns such as 10x (and sometimes more), with expectations around the fund’s timeline. He explains that startups generally need an “exit” through going public or being acquired, and that founders should plan accordingly.

He focuses heavily on how to raise money and make an effective pitch: cut through “noise” with a strong hook, keep the pitch simple for the audience, tailor messaging to different people in the room, use pictures, limit pitch length (about 20 minutes), and manage questions so the pitch can conclude with a clear offer. He also recommends practicing, being confident, showing passion, explaining customer pain points in terms of dollars, and demonstrating credible business details including financials, status, timeline, and the specific investment ask.

Pearse also covers startup practices such as raising money before you need it, orchestrating investor outreach in parallel, maintaining cash flow (CFIMITY), being flexible and willing to pivot based on customer feedback, prioritizing speed to market over relying on patents, clarifying the mission, and assembling a team with strong chemistry and complementary skills. He concludes that leadership—shown through passion, confidence, engagement, and a clear call to action—drives startup success.

The passage discusses being confident and excited for the next game in a series, emphasizing that success depends on bringing their game into the rink. It states the team was not fully playing in the early games but believes that bringing their legs and game in later games gave them a chance to be successful. The speaker highlights the team’s strength on the road, its depth in lines and defense, and good goaltending, as well as additions made around the trading deadline that helped fill roles. The passage also credits the owner’s commitment to the team and praises a player who has faced injuries but has worked hard and performed as one of the league’s best. It concludes that tomorrow’s game is the focus and that there is no easy game.

The passage discusses how online learning in higher education is expanding and how student personality traits are linked to satisfaction and success. It notes that traits such as conscientiousness, openness, and agreeableness are positively associated with engagement and achievement, while neuroticism can relate to lower satisfaction and success. The passage also describes the increasing adoption of hybrid and fully online education formats, including in occupational therapy programs, and highlights a gap: no systematic review had consolidated evidence on personality traits’ impact on online learning outcomes in higher education.  

A systematic review using Cochrane and PRISMA methods investigated peer-reviewed studies from January 2000 to June 2024, focusing on students in higher education with online learning experiences and recognized personality assessments (Big Five or Myers-Briggs). The review identified 23 studies after screening, all rated as level IV evidence. Studies were synthesized into three themes: (1) personality interactions with online education (including relationships with GPA, satisfaction, engagement, and assignment preferences), (2) comparisons across different class formats (online, blended, face-to-face), and (3) personality interactions with students’ choice of class format. The review reports that evidence is generally low strength and that no included studies specifically examined occupational therapy education. It concludes that students high in openness, agreeableness, conscientiousness, and emotional stability may be more likely to succeed online, and emphasizes tailoring online education using approaches such as Universal Design for Learning and supporting self-regulated learning skills.

In November 1977, Leeds hosted the UK’s first Reclaim the Night march, prompted by women’s fears of harassment and vulnerability at night amid the Yorkshire Ripper attacks. Women organized two marches from Hyde Park and Chapeltown and encouraged feminists’ groups across the country to march on the same night, gathering in 12 towns and cities and chanting “Reclaim the Night” or carrying banners. The marches continued for more than a decade, ended in the early 1990s, and were revived in 2004. The event also inspired The Darkest Corners, a new RashDash performance mixing cabaret, physical theatre, and live music, to be staged in a car park on the outskirts of Leeds city centre in Holbeck. The creators say the issues from 40 years ago persist and that the show celebrates women who stood together, drawing on global female activists as well.

The passage describes how Turing GPUs address VR and ray tracing performance challenges.
