It explains that current VR setups require multiple headset connections (display, power, and USB data) that can limit user movement and complicate headset design. Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an industry standard that uses a single USB-C connector to deliver power, display, and tracking data to VR headsets, aiming to simplify setup and enable VR on small-form devices.  

It also outlines “NVLink improves SLI,” noting that earlier SLI relied on MIO/PCIe, while Turing TU102/TU104 GPUs use NVLink links for GPU-to-GPU transfers, with specified bandwidth. The passage then covers Turing ray tracing: limitations of prior real-time ray tracing, the use of RT Cores and RTX software technology, and a hybrid rendering approach combining rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, and shadows. It describes denoising and BVH acceleration, compares shadowing/AO/reflections from ray tracing versus traditional methods, and summarizes how these technologies enable real-time ray tracing on a single GPU.

The passage introduces Eye on AI, featuring AI reporter Sharon Goldman, and highlights several developments in AI. It profiles Demi Guo, the 26-year-old founder of AI video company Pika, which creates TikTok-like short videos from simple prompts. Pika has raised about $135 million at a $470 million valuation and has 16.4 million users; it launched “Predictive Video,” which lets users upload a selfie and receive a full video with inferred intent, including script, music, dance moves, and visual effects. Guo says the app is designed for Gen Z and Gen Alpha and emphasizes self-expression rather than “Slop,” contrasting Pika with competitors focused on cinematic generation or broader platform video feeds. The passage also covers San Francisco housing pressures from AI boom-linked startups, TSMC’s 39.1% profit increase tied to AI chip demand, Spotify’s partnerships to develop “responsible” AI music products, and public skepticism toward AI mental health tools.

Adjuncts of Southwestern College organized a rally for better wages and equal protections for full-time instructors, but only a few people attended. The passage describes that adjunct instructors teach nearly 75% of the college’s classes and do not have the same benefits as full-time professors. Several adjuncts shared accounts of long work hours and travel across multiple schools, higher risks of losing or not being rehired, and difficulties accessing medical benefits. Speakers also said the broader concern is the quality of education. President Dr. Kindred Murillo and Trustee Roberto Alcantar supported adjuncts, and Dolnick and Johnson urged students and faculty to get involved to help adjuncts receive better pay for office hours and disability leave.

The passage describes emergency remote education (ERE) as a temporary shift adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic to keep higher education activities running online. It contrasts ERE with online learning (OL) defined as a technology-mediated process that is flexible in time, space, and learning styles. The study aims to identify students’ perceptions and preferences about and between OL and ERE using Colombia context and an add-on preferential groups (APG) methodological framework. Conducted as a case study at a medium-sized private university in Colombia with 88 undergraduate participants, it used a survey with Likert-scale items across dimensions such as content, interaction, assessment, feedback, resources, technical support, and time requirements, plus open-ended questions. Results indicate students generally prefer OL over ERE across most assessed factors, with most respondents showing positive perceptions of both modalities and statistically significant differences favoring OL in several dimensions. Content analysis reports that students viewed ERE advantages as enabling continuity during crisis, flexibility, comfort, and ICT use, while disadvantages included organization/structure and instructor preparation; for OL, advantages included convenience/flexibility, learning effectiveness, and course structure, while disadvantages included needing improved interaction, increased activity dynamism, and occasional concerns about the amount of content. The study concludes that both modalities have positive perceptions, but emphasizes ongoing instructor training, improved interaction and assessment practices, and designing better learning experiences post-COVID-19.

Billionaire Mark Cuban said President Donald Trump’s plan to launch TrumpRx.gov, a federal website selling discounted prescription drugs directly to consumers, could succeed if it forces pharmaceutical benefit managers (PBMs) to change. Cuban’s own direct-to-consumer discounted drug company, founded in 2022, sells hundreds of discounted generic drugs by bypassing PBMs that negotiate rebates with drug manufacturers but often keep the cash from those rebates. TrumpRx.gov is expected to launch in early 2026 and, under the White House partnership, offers a three-year reprieve from Trump’s pharmaceutical tariffs while aligning with the “most-favored-nation” pricing approach. Cuban graded the effort a “B” and said stock prices of PBM firms rose after the announcement, suggesting limited near-term impact; he added it could still work if PBMs’ power is reduced. Public-health experts, including Drew Altman of KFF, said DTC platforms may mainly help the uninsured because TrumpRx.gov currently applies to Pfizer and DTC platforms generally cannot accept insurance plans.

The passage describes the Russell 2000 Index, which measures about 2,000 U.S. small-cap stocks, and explains that it is rebalanced once per year in June to reflect the small-cap universe according to predetermined criteria. Rebalancing involves adding new qualifying companies, removing those that no longer qualify, and adjusting weights of existing constituents so the index continues to mirror the performance of small-cap stocks. The process typically includes preliminary portfolio communications from June 9, with updates on June 16 and 23, and the newly reconstituted indexes taking effect after the close on June 23 (or the fourth Friday of June). The passage also states that rebalancing can create temporary trading imbalances as managers must buy stocks that have grown and sell those that have declined. It presents a trading strategy aimed at the “end of June rally/effect,” where traders buy the Russell 2000 cash index (^RUT) on the close of the first trading day after June 23 and sell on the close of the first trading day of July, based on a backtest from 1988 that reports an average gain of 1.34% over an average holding time of 6 trading days. For comparison, the S&P 500 (^gspc) gained an average of 0.85% during the same period, and a hedged long Russell 2000/short S&P 500 position is described as underperforming in the backtest.

The passage advises Galaxy Fold users to unfold their phones or view them in full screen. It explains that offers on the site may be influenced by compensation paid to The Motley Fool, but that product ratings are not influenced by compensation. It then describes credit card offers, including the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 welcome bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, a 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, then variable APRs, a $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible, with approval most likely for good credit (670+). The passage also includes details for the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card, featuring unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases, potential 5% cash back on certain travel booked through Capital One Travel, a limited-time $300 welcome offer including a $100 travel credit and a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases in 3 months, a $0 annual fee and no foreign transaction fees, and a 0% intro APR for 15 months (with variable APR afterward) plus balance transfer terms. It adds general approval and credit-score disclaimers and includes disclosures about advertising partners and ownership.

The passage describes how digital leaders align teams using transparent, data-driven objectives that connect employee goals to the organization’s strategy, creating a shared “North Star” vision. It says organizations should use a combined top-down and bottom-up approach rather than simply mandating OKRs, and it notes some companies struggle when excessive analysis slows decisions and undermines human intuition. It also explains that adopting a data culture aligns organizations vertically (leadership-to-front line goal understanding) and horizontally (shared data models and transparent access for cross-team collaboration). The passage contrasts digital leaders—who emphasize a data culture through consistent learning, transparency, measurement, and reinforcing values and behaviors—with digital laggards, who show weaker connections between priorities and strategy and misalignment between stated values and day-to-day behavior. It argues digital laggards are not doomed, citing examples of ongoing cultural transformation among digital leaders. Finally, it categorizes organizations’ data transformation patterns as data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, based on which capabilities and cultural elements they have, and suggests each can target actions to build a stronger data culture.

The passage is a veto message to the House of Representatives regarding a bill appropriating $1,378,450 for more than forty harbor and river improvements. The author argues the Constitution does not grant the Federal Government power to make internal improvements within states or appropriate Treasury money for that purpose, and contends that the bill revives a settled denial of such authority. They also criticize the difficulty of defining limits for federal spending, noting that some proposed projects are local and not connected to foreign commerce or naval/marine protection, and that restrictions based on ports of entry could be evaded. The author warns the bill would consolidate federal power, divert funds for local benefits at the expense of the common Treasury, fuel sectional conflict, encourage wasteful competition for money, and be unjust to states that oppose the power. They further cite practical concerns: the appropriations are not pressing necessity, proposed during a foreign war, and could lead to increased future spending, larger debt or higher taxes. For these constitutional and practical reasons, they withhold approval.

Coach Deboer says the team made some bad decisions but is playing to win, and feels they made mistakes after the other team capitalized. He believes the team must “find another level” after starting tentative in a Stanley Cup final and playing better as the game progressed, though he says they did not generate enough success despite pushing in spurts. He says the group self-analyzes and has two days to improve for Saturday night. He adds they did not believe they deserved to win the game and mentions excitement in the community. Deboer also discusses handling strong opponents and the need for traffic, bodies, and shots, referencing past experience against Lundqvist, and says they will keep their preparation routine and not change everything. He mentions that preparation and organizational experience, from management to coaches and the locker room, are advantages.

The speaker says they will not analyze the game, noting disappointment despite their players giving their best effort. They credit Boston with strong goaltending and tough goals scored around their net, and say Boston deserved to win. They state injuries will not be used as an excuse and mention their inability to score on grade-a chances, while Boston handled rebounds and collapsed in front. They also discuss Game 7 and preparations, saying the team will be focused on process and playing hard, with nerves expected but managed. The speaker expresses excitement about coaching in the NHL and the opportunity to play for the Stanley Cup in the seventh game.

The passage describes a statistical analysis plan for Zealand Pharma A/S protocol ZP4207-17086, including study objectives, design, sample size rationale, general reporting and testing rules, analysis populations (safety analysis set, full analysis set, per protocol set), and detailed methods for efficacy (primary time to plasma glucose recovery and secondary recovery/change timepoints with hierarchical testing), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic handling and summaries, and safety analyses (extent of exposure, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory/vital sign/ECG/immunogenicity summaries). It also specifies data handling rules (e.g., missing data without imputation, LLOQ handling), statistical models and stratification variables, software/tools used (SAS, Phoenix WinNonlin), and quality control/documentation requirements for SAS programming.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x (Ampere) platform and related technologies. It says GA10x uses high-speed GDDR6X memory developed with DRAM industry partners and Micron, claiming up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth using PAM4 signaling. It explains PAM4’s multilevel approach and mentions MTA (Maximum Transition Avoidance) plus new training, adaptation, and equalization to address SNR challenges. The passage also describes RTX IO, which works with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable rapid GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game and creative assets, aiming to improve I/O performance, reduce CPU usage, and reduce loading/stutter while enabling high-rate streaming textures. It further covers NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 GPUs for data center and workstation use, including performance comparisons, virtualization support, and NVLink-based memory scaling. Additional sections discuss display capabilities for Ampere GPUs (e.g., DP 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 features), fifth-generation NVDEC hardware video decoding (including AV1 hardware decode on GA10x), and seventh-generation NVENC hardware video encoding. Finally, it includes information about GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for memory overclock error handling and ends with specification/disclaimer language.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 1, 2018 reporting results of operations and financial condition for its second fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018. Apple issued a press release and a related data sheet that were attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The filing also includes a signature by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Reports quoted a Royal Household source saying Queen Elizabeth, 91, plans to abdicate when she turns 95 and may consider passing the reign to Prince Charles if she is still alive then. The Regency Act would come into force to grant Charles full power while the Queen is still living, and preparations for a Charles-led regency are described as moving ahead. Clarence House made no comment. The passage also states that Queen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952, that her father George VI died in February 1952, and that if she abdicated the throne would pass to Charles, with William and Prince George next in line.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 12, 2021. Under Item 7.01, Microsoft announced via press release that it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc. for $56.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $19.7 billion, inclusive of Nuance’s net debt. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, and an investor presentation is attached as Exhibit 99.2. Item 9.01(d) lists Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, and the report is signed by Keith R. Dolliver (Assistant Secretary) on April 12, 2021.

Punith Kumar, a 19-year-old resident of Choolai, achieved first place in India and third internationally in the ACCA Chartered Accountant final P2 exam. He completed the course in two years and three months after attending coaching classes at the School of Excellence, despite juggling a paid internship and ACCA studies, and credits his mentor and boss, Niranjan Sir, for support. He interned with IRIS Techsolve in Chennai, studied from about 4 am to 9 pm, and scored 83% in corporate reporting. He plans to start his own company but aims to clear three to four remaining papers and finish his course by September this year.

The passage discusses international cases applying a rule about damages for the arrest and detention of vessels, stating that loss of use is the proper measure and includes the loss of probable catch during enforced absence from fishing grounds. It references awards before arbitration commissions, including the Hope On (damages for arrest and detention) and details several Bering Sea Commission cases to show that awards consistently used estimated earnings from catch, often adjusting claimed amounts by excluding certain ownership or duplicate items. It further asserts that it is not disputed that a government agent may not, on mere suspicion, enter a peaceably engaged ship under a friendly nation’s flag, and force citizens or subjects into public service without their consent, citing Hall and Bluntcheli.

The Office of Management and Budget identified over 4,100 federal workers for layoffs as the government shutdown continues, with Russell Vought posting that “RIFs have begun.” Business Insider reviewed an OMB filing estimating 4,132 to 4,232 workers expected to be affected across the Department of Commerce, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Homeland Security, and the Treasury. Several agencies confirmed roles being cut and said the layoffs stem from the shutdown; other officials described specific impacts, including within Homeland Security’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Labor unions have challenged the planned layoffs in court. Federal employees interviewed by Business Insider reported furloughs, pay concerns, and anxiety about financial effects and broader economic ripple impacts.

The passage explains that momentum investing suggests assets that have been rising are likely to keep rising, but it presents a short-term pattern in the SPY where it tends to be higher after a red day and lower after a green day. It attributes this behavior to mean reversion, which holds that prices and historical returns revert toward the long-run average. The article outlines simple trading rules—buy after a red day and sell after a green day—and reports that a backtest on the SPY (with data adjusted for dividends and splits) produced stronger returns after red days than the opposite strategy, with less time in the market and less than half the drawdown. It concludes that mean reversion appears effective in the short term, while momentum or trend following still works over longer timeframes.

The passage contains an “Option Investor Newsletter” email with market updates and stock option trading recommendations dated January 23, 1999 (forwarded from Option Investor). It provides “PICK NEWS” for multiple call and put candidates (e.g., PRIA, NOKA, DELL, CSCO, AOL, WCOM, T, MSFT, TLAB, MYG, SUNW, LXK, XIRC, COF, ETH, and several put plays such as AVT, BAC, BDX, CPB, DD, EK, ERTS, HSY, LLY, MCHP, MRK, PKN, RMBS, WLA), along with “NEW CALL PLAYS” (VOD, QWST) and “COMBO PLAYS”/“NEW PLAYS” describing diagonal spread and example trade setups for CTXS, RDRT, LVLT, and SEPR. It also includes market wrap data and commentary on stock/index performance, sentiment indicators, expectations around earnings, and several “dropped picks” and play updates, plus subscription and disclaimer notes.

Ofcom has proposed a statutory scheme requiring landline and broadband providers to automatically compensate customers for certain service failures, such as not fixing outages quickly, not activating new services by the promised day, or missing scheduled appointments. Compensation would be set by Ofcom and provided as cash or a bill credit without requiring customers to file claims. The scheme would apply only to fixed broadband and landline telephone services. Ofcom estimates it could add up to 2.6 million customers receiving up to £185m in compensation per year. The passage cites a customer’s experience of long-term broadband problems and says the proposal is intended to align broadband with other essential services. A consultation is open until 5 June, with a decision expected around the end of the year.

The passage reports that Sonora High School’s 2017 Athletic Hall of Fame class includes a dozen former Wildcats who graduated between 1950 and 2008. It describes honorees’ athletic achievements in sports such as football, basketball, baseball, wrestling, tennis, swimming, track, volleyball, softball, golf, water polo, and soccer, and includes a coach honoree. The awards will be presented at an open-to-the-public dinner and ceremony at Sonora Elks Lodge on Saturday, Nov. 4, with dinner at 6 p.m. and the awards ceremony at 7 p.m., and includes ticket prices and contact information.

The passage reports that a PEN America report found 22,810 instances of book banning in U.S. public schools from 2021 to 2025, amid a growing climate of fear that affects librarians and promotion of banned books. It describes book banning efforts across colleges, including an example at Franciscan University of Steubenville where a seminar policy was revised after controversy over a book, and actions reported by Gov. Ron DeSantis’s press secretary toward the Gender and Diversity Center at New College of Florida. It also cites censorship at military academies, including the U.S. Naval Academy where 381 books by Ibram X. Kendi were initially removed and then reduced to 20 after public outcry. The passage further states that censorship targets curricula through “divisive concepts” bans, course audits, and legislative proposals requiring public syllabi. It describes actions involving Texas A&M University’s course auditing and dismissals related to permitted ideas about gender identity, and mentions a Trump administration “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education” that would require transforming or abolishing institutional units that belittle conservative ideas. The passage concludes with claims that most Americans oppose book banning and calls for education stakeholders to unite to defend against censorship.

A federal judge in Brooklyn ruled that FACEA’s provisions barring harassment at abortion clinics also apply to Falun Gong practitioners, rejecting the alliance’s constitutional challenge to the “religion” section of the 1994 law. The ruling says religion rooted in interstate commerce and that “a place of religious worship” in FACEA must be construed broadly to avoid First Amendment issues. The judge certified the opinion for appeal ahead of a two-month trial, noting the case would be difficult to try due to interpreters and many issues for a jury.

The passage describes how the Carter administration used presidential findings (MONs) for higher-risk, higher-cost, or geographically specific covert operations within broader objectives, requiring coordination between the CIA and the Department of State and additional interagency coordination. It notes that significant changes could use MONs while entirely new covert actions required new presidential findings, and that the CIA typically notified Congress within 48 hours. The Intelligence Oversight Act of 1980 later changed congressional oversight by limiting briefings to the two intelligence committees, clarifying that being “fully and currently informed” did not require congressional approval, and creating the “Gang of Eight” arrangement if prior notice was limited for extraordinary circumstances. The passage then shifts to document excerpts from January 1983 related to U.S.-Soviet discussions, including memoranda to President Reagan and references to a four-part agenda covering human rights, arms control, regional issues, and bilateral relations.

Fannie M. Conarty, as administratrix of her deceased husband W. Gr. Conarty, sued the St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Company under the Federal Employers’ Liability Act as amended April 5, 1910, based on alleged violation of the Safety Appliance Act. The jury awarded $10,000 for death-related damages including loss of contributions and the decedent’s pain and suffering. The railroad sought removal to federal court on diversity grounds, but the court denied removal based on Kansas City Southern Railway Co. v. Cook, holding the act’s removal prohibition valid.  

The court held that the amended 1910 Act allows only one recovery for the same injury in a single action prosecuted after the injured employee’s death for the benefit of the widow and next of kin, and that no election between causes of action was required. It also found that a defective coal car—taken to Fort Smith for heavy repairs, stored until the repair track was available, then moved and left on the main track while switching—was still in use for interstate commerce within the Safety Appliance Act. The railroad was held liable under the Safety Appliance Act for injuries caused by missing or defective couplers even though the decedent was not attempting to use or handle the coupler.  

Finally, the court affirmed admission of testimony by the decedent’s widow about the amount of his contributions, concluding it did not fall within the constitutional bar on testimony about transactions with the deceased when liability is established by other evidence. The circuit court’s judgment was affirmed.

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said the official US dollar to bond note exchange rate remains 1:1 and that the public should use licensed financial agencies for currency exchanges. RBZ Governor Dr John Mangudya said exchange rate distortions on the black market could be avoided by transacting through registered institutions and noted that 45 financial institutions are licensed. He advised that the permissible exchange is 1 bond note for 1 US dollar, with other currency exchanges allowed only with a fee spread not exceeding 10% of the nominal value. He also said illegal money changers have been arrested under new exchange control regulations and that RBZ, with the police, would target retailers refusing non-cash payment modes. Mangudya urged the public to report traders who insist on cash payments only. The passage also states that a new law was promulgated to address money changers inflating US dollar and bond note cross rates, which allegedly led to panic and artificial shortages of basic commodities.

The U.S. dollar rose early in the week as a Fed official said the central bank could avoid raising rates at the same time it begins shrinking its bond portfolio, supporting U.S. yields. Markets also watched Syria-related geopolitical tensions, while the euro fell slightly due to uncertainty around the French presidential election. U.S. jobs data missed forecasts but showed labor market strength, and speculators reduced bullish dollar positions to a five-week low.

The passage discusses continuous-wave optical interferometry, where an external signal imprints a phase shift δϕ on an optical field. It states that, for a time-independent case, the variance of an unbiased phase estimator is bounded by the quantum Cramér-Rao bound (QCRB), Var[δϕ̃] ≥ 1/FQ. Heisenberg scaling (precision scaling ~1/n) can be achieved using a pair of squeezed states with mean total photon number n, while for unentangled input states FQ ≤ n(n+2). It highlights that practical squeezing has finite bandwidth modeled by a power spectral density with squeezing and antisqueezing factors V± and a bandwidth ΔΩ around frequency Ω0. With pure squeezed inputs and no losses, the precision for estimating a time-dependent phase is bounded by a spectral QCRB: \( \bar{S}_{\delta\tilde{\phi}\delta\tilde{\phi}}[\Omega] \ge \frac{1}{\Delta\Omega}\frac{\pi n(n+2)}{} \), which shows Heisenberg scaling for n ≫ 2. The passage then claims this bound can be attained using a nonlinear estimator applied to homodyne detector records, with an intuitive explanation based on rectifying (squaring) Gaussian homodyne processes oscillating out of phase with the signal. It further describes that, with finite-bandwidth squeezing, filtered homodyne records are used and presents an unbiased linearized maximum likelihood estimator and a resulting PSD expression (partially shown).

Chronic hepatitis C (CHC) is an inflammatory liver disease caused by hepatitis C virus (HCV), leading to liver cirrhosis and potentially hepatocellular carcinoma. Complications of chronic hepatitis and gradual extrahepatic manifestations—including autoimmune disorders, cryoglobulinemia, Sjogren’s syndrome, and endocrinological diseases such as autoimmune thyroid disorders and type 2 diabetes (T2DM)—affect quality of life and prognosis. HCV infection is described as a significant risk factor for developing T2DM, and HCV clearance may reduce the risk. The prevalence of T2DM is generally higher in individuals with clinically infected HCV, and systemic inflammation indicators such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), along with prognostic nutrition index (PNI), have prognostic uses in cancers. The study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of PNI, NLR, and PLR in patients with chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis complicated by T2DM. From January 2018 to December 2021, 56 patients in group A (CHC-associated cirrhosis with T2DM), 85 in group B (CHC-associated cirrhosis), and 85 in group C (T2DM) were included, with 23 in a poor-prognosis group and 33 in a good-prognosis group after 6 months of treatment. Laboratory parameters included serum albumin (ALB), AST, ALT, platelet and blood cell counts, with NLR, PNI, and PLR calculated from admission laboratory tests.

The passage describes the Rubber Band trading strategy as a contrarian/mean-reversion approach for trading stocks. It aims to detect points where the market is overbought or oversold and likely to snap back toward the mean. Traders may use indicators such as Keltner Channels or Bollinger Bands (or momentum oscillators), with Keltner Channels commonly set to 20 periods and a 10-period ATR. The strategy’s buy setup occurs when the price opens and closes below the lower Keltner Channel band, with targets at the middle band or just before the upper band; sell setups occur when the price opens and closes above the upper band, with targets at the middle band or just before the lower band. It emphasizes contrarian timing based on sentiment, referencing Warren Buffett’s idea of being fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful. The passage also mentions a backtested example strategy using XLP data, reporting 328 trades, average gain per trade of 0.45%, CAGR of 6.1%, 20% time in the market, profit factor of 2, and max drawdown of 16%.

The passage describes a study on predicting Alzheimer’s disease–related cognitive decline using plasma biomarkers combined with other non-invasive measures. It notes that early detection is important for interventions and that current AD diagnostics often rely on costly, invasive or resource-intensive methods targeting amyloid-β, tau, and neurodegeneration. Plasma biomarkers—Aβ42/40, p-tau181, and neurofilament light (NfL)—are presented as a promising, non-invasive alternative but may be limited when used alone, so the study integrates plasma biomarkers with MRI data, demographics, APOE4, and baseline cognitive assessments. The study uses ADNI data and machine learning with a two-stage framework: MRI features are summarized using ridge linear regression to create an MRI score, then random forest regression predicts the rate of cognitive decline from combined predictors. Four models are compared (basic, plasma, MRI, combined), tested in two cohorts that differ by whether Aβ42/40 is available. Results report that adding plasma biomarkers and MRI generally improves prediction, with the combined model often performing best. Memory decline (ADNI-MEM) shows the strongest predictive performance across analyses, while other cognitive domains—especially visuospatial—show weaker or less consistent results. The passage also reports separate analyses for cognitively unimpaired versus mild cognitive impairment groups, showing prediction is generally more challenging in cognitively unimpaired individuals. Finally, estimated cognitive decline rates are evaluated for predicting progression to MCI or dementia using survival analysis, with significant differences across predicted-rate tertiles and the combined model showing the highest predictive accuracy in the reported dementia progression outcomes.

UK university staff are entering the fourth week of strikes over the defined benefit aspect of pension schemes, and the disputes may affect exam periods for some universities. Talks to resolve the dispute have been unsuccessful, leading the union’s higher education committee to issue an additional 14 days of strikes likely between April and June. UCU general secretary Sally Hunt said the action is a precaution if talks fail and that UCU prefers dialogue with negotiations via Acas. Whether the strikes proceed depends on talks between Universities UK and UCU. The University of Edinburgh has been criticised for trying to break the pensions strike by providing out-of-date recorded lectures to law students who will miss classes. UCU Scotland official Mary Senior said students deserve lecturers’ full attention and criticized the use of recordings if the university does not stop.

A new report from the National Academies of Sciences and Medicine says scientists should be allowed to alter germline DNA passed to future generations only to prevent serious, strongly heritable diseases, not to enhance traits like strength, intelligence, or beauty. Germline editing is illegal in the United States and has been largely considered ethically off-limits, but CRISPR-Cas9 research is advancing for editing adult cells to treat genetic mutations causing diseases. The report says clinical trials involving germline editing should be pursued only when no reasonable alternatives exist, when targeting genes that cause or strongly predispose to serious disease, with demonstrated risk-benefit consideration. Such trials should be under public scrutiny and include long-term follow-up on effects to subsequent generations, with ongoing public debate. The report emphasizes that genome editing is an international endeavor requiring oversight reflecting societal values, and was produced by a panel with members from multiple countries, supported partly by the U.S. Department of Defense’s ARPA and the FDA.

Eight women and 15 men aged 27 to 41 were arrested during a week-long joint enforcement operation by the Singapore Police Force from May 21 to May 27, supported by the Central Narcotics Bureau. About 700 people at more than 70 residential and commercial units in Yishun, Ang Mo Kio, and Sengkang were checked. The eight women, arrested under the Women’s Charter, were believed to be advertising sexual services online and operating within residential areas; S$730 cash and 10 handphones were seized. Four men were arrested for operating a gambling den and 10 for participating under the Common Gaming House Act. A 44-year-old man was also arrested at a roadblock for drink-driving, and investigations are ongoing.

Aiden Markram says he is honoured to be named South Africa’s new cricket captain after Faf du Plessis was forced out with a finger injury. Markram acknowledges the added pressure and the responsibilities of the role, and says senior players and the team’s culture will help him. He adds that du Plessis has advised him since he joined the environment. South Africa trails India 1-0 in a six-match series after losing the first ODI by six wickets in Durban, and Markram says the team must bounce back with an improved performance in the second ODI on Sunday.

Google announced it is expanding speech recognition to support 30 new languages and locales, bringing the total supported to 119. The update adds 8 Indian languages, plus Swahili and Amharic, and will initially be available in Gboard for Android and Voice Search, with the new languages also supported in the Cloud Speech API. U.S. English speakers can use voice dictation with emojis. Google says it trained the new language models using speech samples collected from native speakers, and it plans to add the new languages to other products like Google Translate. The passage ends by stating a full list of new languages follows.

Saints begin their Anglo-Welsh Cup campaign on November 4 with an away game against Aviva Premiership champions Exeter Chiefs, the same opponents who beat them 15-8 in the 2014 final at Sandy Park. They play the Dragons at home on November 11 after defeating them 71-21 in a pre-season friendly. Their next away pool game is against Sale Sharks on the weekend of January 26, and they conclude their bid for semi-final qualification with a home match against Harlequins in the first weekend of February. The competition has four pools of four, with teams playing clubs from another pool; the top team from each pool advances to the semi-finals. Saints are grouped with Saracens, Scarlets, and Worcester Warriors.

Agent-based modeling is described as a bottom-up simulation method where researchers define what an agent represents, its behaviors, and initial simulation conditions. Such models are characterized by local interactions and emergent behavior, and are used across many domains with systems that may contain very large numbers of agents, including human cortex estimates. The passage argues that existing simulation platforms do not provide sufficient scalability: BioDynaMo is limited to about 1.7 billion agents per single server and is restricted by memory limits, poor integration with MPI-based third-party tools, and limited hardware flexibility. To address these issues, the paper introduces TeraAgent, a distributed simulation engine that executes simulations across multiple servers via scale-out domain decomposition, supported by optimized agent serialization and delta encoding to reduce data-transfer overheads. It also describes modifications to BioDynaMo to support distributed execution and interoperability, outlines the distributed execution steps (aura updates, agent migration, load balancing), and reports evaluation results including large performance and scalability improvements (e.g., up to 501.51 billion agents and scaling to 84,096 CPU cores), along with improved serialization performance, reduced message sizes, and faster visualization in situ.

CoreLogic’s Home Price Index report says home prices rose 7.1% nationally from May 2017 to May 2018 and increased 1.1% from the prior month. The report attributes higher prices to lean home supply and notes May mortgage rates averaged 4.6%, a seven-year high. In the 100 largest metropolitan areas, 40% were overvalued as of May 2018, while 26% were undervalued and 34% were at value; for the top 50 markets, 52% were overvalued. States with double-digit 12-month price growth included Utah (12.9%), Washington (12.8%), Nevada (12.4%) and Idaho (11.2%). CoreLogic projects the national home-price index will increase 5.1% from May 2018 to May 2019, and says demand for homeownership remains strong despite financial obstacles.

Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infections are widespread neglected tropical diseases, affecting over one billion people worldwide, primarily in low- and middle-income countries. The WHO recommends integrated morbidity control using sanitation, hygiene education, and preventive chemotherapy (PC). PC coverage has increased to about 60% of children in need by 2019, reducing prevalence and intensity, and countries conduct STH Impact Assessment Surveys (IAS) after about 5 years of PC to determine whether and how frequently PC should continue; WHO suspension is based on local prevalence below 2%.

The passage describes a cost-challenging IAS and proposes extending model-based geostatistical methods to design and analyze IAS more efficiently. The proposed approach uses baseline prevalence survey data, PC treatment coverage history, environmental risk factors, and a model to project prevalence forward to the impact survey time. Baseline prevalence is estimated with a geostatistical model (generalized linear mixed model), then changes after intervention are projected using multi-state Markov models (with endemicity classes defined by prevalence ranges) and local thinning of the baseline prevalence surface. Different sampling designs are created and evaluated using performance measures related to sample size reduction and accuracy of treatment decisions (endemicity class assignment). The methodology is applied to Kenya, Sierra Leone, and Zimbabwe, showing similar accuracy to classical methods but with substantially smaller samples and average survey cost decreases of 80% (91% for Zimbabwe, 86% for Kenya, 62% for Sierra Leone). The authors conclude the MBG approach can provide higher-accuracy, lower-cost IAS and support more detailed prevalence mapping, and they are developing a manual and web application to implement the method.

Alere said it concluded that financial statements and other financial data as of December 31, 2015 and 2014, and for years ended December 31, 2015, 2014, and 2013, should not be relied upon due to misstatements. It preliminarily expects restatements to relate mainly to revenue recognition at its South Korean location and also identified a revenue recognition error tied to one transaction at its Japanese location that affects 2013 and 2012. Alere expects the misstatements will not change total revenue reported for any transaction, and that its review will lead to a revenue adjustment for the Japanese transaction that recognized about $1 million in 2013 instead of 2012. It expects material weaknesses relating to revenue recognition as of December 31, 2015 to remain unremediated and identified an additional material weakness related to the control environment at SD. The company is working to complete its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31 but may need additional time beyond the May 15, 2017 deadline.

The passage describes a vehicle vision and driver monitoring system that uses one or more cameras to capture images exterior and interior of the vehicle. It estimates driver distraction workload and driving workload, and determines an amount of driver attention by comparing the weighted sum of these workloads to a maximum driver workload. The system estimates driver physical and mental state using camera and vehicle sensor inputs, including possible driver identification, driving behavior, posture, emotions, health biometrics, focus, drowsiness, environmental and media inputs, and may monitor passengers. It includes modules that process inputs with confidence and availability and uses calibration elements that may be adjusted during testing or operation, including via machine learning. The system can process captured image data to detect objects and display images/alerts, and in certain conditions may autonomously take control to avoid hazards based on risk level and whether the driver is aware of the detected object. The passage also describes example camera placements, an ECU, optional sensor suites for autonomous vehicles, and communications with other vehicles or infrastructure.

Shonda Rhimes signed a deal with Netflix to create new shows through her Shondaland production company. Netflix said “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal,” and “How to Get Away With Murder” will continue airing on ABC. Rhimes said she is grateful to ABC but is looking to expand her audience and creative identity with Netflix, with a plan developed with Netflix Chief Content Officer Ted Sarandos. No financial terms or the length of the Netflix production deal were disclosed. Rhimes, 47, has three Emmy nominations for “Grey’s Anatomy,” which begins its 14th season next month.

A letter from an anonymous woman describes conditions in an immigration detention facility, calling the chain-link cages a “la perrera” (kennel/dog pound). She says she did not bathe or brush her teeth for eight days, slept on the floor under “aluminum paper” blankets, and wrote that she and others were treated “as though we were animals.” She also describes 21 days of not knowing her children’s fate after they were taken.  

The account was posted online by Grassroots Leadership, which is circulating a petition to reunite separated families, and the group’s volunteers helped women write letters to publicly describe their experience and request release and reunification. ICE said it could not address specific claims because letter writers’ identities and facility details were redacted.  

The passage includes additional letters from women describing separation from children, messages to their sons, and accounts of where some family members were sent. It also describes one woman spending eight days in “la perrera” after capture near Hidalgo, Texas, with her children later moved to other locations, and she was released from custody June 26.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says that five medical tests often ordered for children who are short, overweight, or showing early puberty may not always be necessary, especially if they are otherwise healthy. The tests listed include hormone tests, other endocrine tests, vitamin D screening, thyroid or insulin tests for overweight children, and thyroid ultrasounds for children with an enlarged thyroid or autoimmune thyroid disease. The AAP advises weighing risks and benefits and using evidence-based strategies. It notes that hormone and endocrine screening are unlikely to help in certain cases, such as when puberty signs are limited or growth rate is normal, and that even in children shorter than average these tests find an underlying health issue in about 1% of cases. Vitamin D testing is appropriate mainly for disorders linked to low bone mass, thyroid testing in obese children should be considered only with abnormally low growth or other thyroid signs, and thyroid ultrasounds should be limited to specific findings to avoid unnecessary worry and expense.

The passage explains pairs trading and how it works, presenting it as a market-neutral strategy that trades the spread between two highly correlated assets rather than overall market direction. It describes how pairs can be identified using historical co-movement, and how trades may involve shorting the stronger asset and buying the weaker one when the price difference widens, expecting convergence later. Examples mentioned include KO/PEP, MS/GS, and SPY/TLT, including a brief description of a KO/PEP chart showing divergence followed by convergence. The passage discusses research claims of average annualized excess returns (reported up to about 11% for self-financing portfolios) and states that pairs trading is a subset of statistical arbitrage. It lists advantages such as market neutrality and potential gains in sideways, up, or down markets, while also describing disadvantages and risks including leverage, slippage and commissions, shorting costs and hard-to-borrow stocks, pair “wandering” and reduced out-of-sample cointegration, and issues from leverage and hedging not being equal to low risk. It includes comparisons between correlation and cointegration, describes cointegration tests (e.g., Johansen and Engle-Granger), and outlines some sample KO/PEP strategy criteria using end-of-day data and exits based on RSI, reporting varying backtest returns. The passage also notes that profitability may be diminishing and emphasizes understanding stock fundamentals.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for a method and apparatus for displaying marker elements in a virtual scene. It provides a system in which, when a user marks a target virtual item, marker indication information is obtained, marker graphic data is determined, rendering produces the marker element, and the marker element is displayed at a designated location around the target item in the virtual scene. The marker is intended to be viewable by user accounts in the same team, including across terminals via server synchronization, and may be shown only when the target is within a visible distance, with optional distance information displayed near the marker. The passage also outlines steps and modules for implementing the method, example behaviors for team synchronization and marker cancellation after a preset duration, and describes possible terminal/server roles, virtual scene components, and device architecture.

A district court judge ordered Thomas Alter, a recently tenured history associate professor at Texas State University, to be reinstated after he was terminated for allegedly inciting violence during a virtual socialism conference speech. The judge found the university violated his free speech and due process rights and breached his employment contract. Alter will be reinstated without pay but will not be allowed to teach classes, while the university reviews his case through its standard faculty investigative processes as the lawsuit continues. The passage also notes that other public university faculty were recently terminated for online speech, including Michael Hook at the University of South Dakota, who was ordered to be reinstated.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2016 with the U.S. SEC. As of October 25, 2016, it reported 149,891,190 shares of common stock outstanding. The filing includes unaudited consolidated financial statements and notes, including consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), and cash flows. Key areas covered include forward-looking statements, revenue recognition and performance obligations (including automotive leasing and resale value guarantees), warranties, inventory valuation, credit and supply risk, stock-based compensation, derivative financial instruments, and fair value measurements. The notes also describe recent accounting pronouncements, legal proceedings (including an appealed securities class action), commitments and contingencies, and debt and equity incentive plan details.

The passage contains post-game comments from Henrik Lundqvist and others about a series where their team is behind and needs to turn things around. After a last-second goal and difficulty preventing chances, they emphasize confidence, belief, and focusing on tomorrow’s game. Lundqvist says he has been feeling good but that conceding three or more goals makes it tough to win, and he analyzed specific plays involving deflections and a two-on-one. He discusses maintaining process-focused mindset, relying on hard work and possible luck, improving aspects like first-period play and creating traffic in front of the opponent’s goalie, and moving on emotionally while preparing for the next game.

Researchers report that people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) show stronger autoimmune T cell responses to C9orf72, while responses to other ALS-linked proteins were not preferentially targeted. In the study of blood samples from 40 ALS patients and 28 controls, patients with anti-inflammatory immune cell signals and IL-10 production in response to C9orf72 were predicted to have longer survival. The findings suggest a possible immune contribution to ALS and raise the prospect of new treatments or disease monitoring based on targeting or tracking immune responses, though the authors and experts caution the results do not prove ALS is an autoimmune disease.

The passage reports several market headlines, including AMD shares rising after an AI chip deal with OpenAI, a view from Evercore that a bubble scenario could take the S&P 500 to 9,000 in 2026, and gold rallying above $3,900 per ounce amid a yen slump and U.S. rate cut bets. It also describes July results for the S&P 500 as up 2.2% for the month and 7.8% year-to-date, while noting that August began poorly with losses erasing part of July’s gains. The passage says volatility and credit spreads are seasonally turning up, investors are increasing exposure to tech stocks, and U.S. electricity demand has reached a new all-time high. It includes promotional information about Investing.com’s AI-picked strategies and a risk disclosure stating trading involves high risk and that data on the website may not be real-time or accurate.

Crime involving cryptocurrencies is increasing in Japan as overall reported crime falls. The theft of 523 million NEM coins from Coincheck on Jan. 26, which the company says involved losses of ¥58 billion, has raised concerns about security; the Financial Services Agency (FSA) had warned Coincheck to address customer-asset security beforehand. The passage notes Japan’s role in developing crypto exchanges, including Bitcoin’s creation by Satoshi Nakamoto and the failure of Mt. Gox in 2014, and that the government recognized bitcoin as legal tender in April 2017. It also describes other risks, including a reported defrauding case involving a Ripple firm and ransomware scams targeting crypto searches. It further discusses initial coin offerings (ICOs), which the FSA warned about in an Oct. 27 advisory, citing risks such as rapid token price fluctuations, potential fraud, and possible registration requirements depending on the ICO structure. ICOs are described as largely unclear to regulate in Japan. The passage also reports that Facebook will no longer allow ads for ICOs, and that the U.S. SEC has halted a reportedly fraudulent ICO after it raised nearly $600 million, suggesting a broader crackdown.

The Ontario Liberals are poised to scrap EQAO provincewide tests for Grade 3 and Grade 9 students, eliminate the requirement for high school students to pass a literacy test to graduate, and water down provincewide tests for Grade 6 and Grade 9, according to an Ontario: A Learning Province report commissioned by Premier Kathleen Wynne and released by Education Minister Indira Naidoo-Harris. The government postponed implementing the report’s 18 recommendations until after the June 7 election and said it would do “further consulation,” while keeping the independent school testing agency (EQAO) uninformed. The report proposes shifting substantial student assessment responsibility to teachers. The EQAO criticized the proposals, saying eliminating EQAO’s primary-division assessment would remove half of independent data and expressing disappointment in the report’s view of large-scale assessments. Under the proposal, students would not be tested across the province until Grade 6, and the report also discourages using EQAO results to rank schools.

Auswide Bank grew from Queensland building society mergers, expanded to Sydney and Melbourne, listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1994, and converted to a bank in 2015. Its mission emphasizes “the power of small” and rebalancing Australian banking dominated by the “Big 4.” For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, it reported AUD 3,789 million in total assets, net interest revenue of AUD 70.5 million, net profit after tax of AUD 18.5 million, and dividends of AUD 13.6 million. The passage then lists 15 representative transactions assumed for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, including issuing shares, borrowing from the Reserve Bank of Australia, purchasing supplies and furniture, recording deposit and loan activity, receiving and paying interest, expenses, selling a loan, paying dividends, depreciation, and loan impairment. It also provides suggested questions to record these transactions, prepare a June 30, 2021 balance sheet, and calculate net income and cash flow for fiscal 2021.

The passage discusses special education teacher shortages in the U.S., noting that shortages are prevalent in high-poverty urban and small rural districts and that Washington state has a high share of special education teachers licensed via conditional certification. It describes concerns about emergency substitute waivers and references U.S. Department of Education guidance that special education teachers should obtain certification through sustained, intensive, classroom-focused teacher certification programs. 

The article presents an exploratory case study of the Washington Education Association (WEA) Teacher Residency Program, piloted in 2023–24. The program is union-led and not affiliated with an in-state higher education institution, and it emphasizes evidence-based training components, inclusive curriculum design using Universal Design for Learning, alignment with Washington state teaching standards, and the incorporation of emerging technologies. The program uses Mursion software for virtual student interactions and includes technology across coursework and seminars, with technology goals linked to state and ISTE standards. 

The study collected data through needs assessment, coursework and field experience analysis, semi-structured interviews, observations, and document review across eight participating school districts. Sixteen teacher residents participated in an 18-month training program, and mentors and coaches provided structured support. Incentives include a living wage, health insurance, funded placements, and requirements for residents to work in the district where the residency occurred for three years after licensure. The passage concludes that the WEA program offers a robust approach to addressing special education teacher shortages while promoting diversity and evidence-based preparation, with limitations including scalability, sustainability, and the study’s small size and time frame.

Motivate rolled out 250 new Ford GoBikes with electric pedal assist at dozens of stations across western San Francisco. After a group ride in Hayes Valley, riders said the assist made climbing Page Street easier, and Jay Walder, Motivate’s CEO, said the bikes were added to attract more users by smoothing San Francisco’s terrain and encouraging longer rides. The e-bikes are part of the Ford GoBike program overseen by regional transportation agencies and sponsored by Ford, with GoBike operating 287 stations and 3,600 bikes across five Bay Area cities; for now, e-bikes are only in San Francisco. The program is intended to help people make short trips without cars and address first-and-last-mile connections to bus or rail stops. Walder said Motivate works with cities on station placement and bike counts, contrasting this approach with the scooter controversy.

The speaker says their first goal is to prevent the other team from scoring, and that scoring is a bonus. They emphasize pride in playing simply, avoiding turnovers, and not giving the other team free chances, focusing on winning rather than personal records. They note that prior experience helps because it is not new to them, and that media attention can be enjoyable but sometimes is too much.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Secretary Abid Majeed directed the formation of provincial, district, and union council committees headed by paediatricians to oversee technical and communication aspects of the upcoming measles campaign. He emphasized effective communication and social mobilization to raise parents’ awareness and create demand for vaccination, along with staff training, logistics, vaccines, and referral systems for children in case of AEFI. The campaign, to run from October, will vaccinate children aged nine to 59 months, targeting 4.3 million children, with planning based on increased measles cases across the province and a focus on staff training and quality vaccine provision.

The passage states that industrial enterprises face disruptive changes and that IDC views IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers for greater agility and innovation under international competitive pressure. It says virtual process steps can streamline and speed up product development and manufacturing, support analysis of alternative materials and processes, and help optimize supply chains, energy consumption, and sustainability, as well as enable new digital products, services, and business models. IDC also says HPC technologies are increasingly required for modern simulations and modeling, and that public cloud and HPCaaS can expand agility and scalability or remove the need for in-house HPC infrastructure. The passage further emphasizes creating and integrating data to provide a single source of truth across the product life cycle and using data analysis in the cycle’s final stage to drive innovation in digital offerings. It recommends setting up virtual product and manufacturing development, creating transparency and a holistic data strategy, selecting an appropriate HPC operating model considering factors like cost, performance, security, and skills, and prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency while leveraging external expertise and ecosystem partners. It notes the findings come from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers in industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Sarah and Laura Ayoub, classical musicians aged 22 and 24, say their music education in Scotland was crucial to their careers. They describe “fully funded” tuition there, including one-to-one lessons, orchestra experience, choir singing, chamber music, and weekly coaching. The passage also reports that some Scottish local authorities charge for music tuition or have increased costs, which campaigners argue creates barriers for children. Examples include Highland Council transferring tuition responsibilities to a charity and Renfrewshire pledging funding to widen access, while other areas face cuts or higher fees. Concerns are raised about potential cuts ending music education services and a decline in the number of music teachers. Scotland’s Culture Secretary Fiona Hyslop says the Youth Music Initiative aims to ensure every child receives music tuition by Primary 6, and she says there should not be charging but acknowledges local budget decisions. Campaigners argue additional tuition funding is insufficient, and Sarah Ayoub says musical education benefits people even if they do not become musicians.

The court considered defendants Aluminum Workers International Union and Local 480’s motion for summary judgment in Toy Lykins’s case seeking declaratory and injunctive relief. Lykins alleged that union security dues compelled from him are being spent for purposes other than collective bargaining, contract administration, or grievance adjustment, in violation of his first amendment rights. The court denied summary judgment, finding a justiciable controversy exists and that the action is not barred by failure to exhaust remedies under 29 U.S.C. § 431(c). The court also concluded that union shop agreements under the NLRA involve sufficient governmental action and that the NLRA does not authorize spending a dissenter’s dues money for ideological or political purposes, though it would not decide the specific expenditures requiring refund until further factual development. The order denied summary judgment, directed the plaintiff to amend his complaint to correct jurisdictional allegations, and set deadlines and a pretrial conference.

A new Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than 1 in 4 U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support, which significantly affects workplace satisfaction. Over 60% reported shortages including teaching assistants and mental health resources or special educators, with two-thirds citing not enough teaching assistants, aides, or paraprofessionals. Teachers also reported issues with classroom furniture, laptops/computers, and printing supplies, and that ordering materials is difficult for some. The survey of thousands of teachers across the 2024–2025 school year found that 77% of teachers with adequate resources were satisfied at work versus 44% without adequate resources, and that many teachers said professional development is not grounded in students’ needs and that opportunities for collaborative or observational learning are limited.

The speaker says joining the group is a wonderful feeling and expresses appreciation for key figures, including Chris Chelios, who contacted him and said Ken Holland thought he would be a great addition. The speaker talks about enjoying his time in Detroit, being part of a winning team and winning the Stanley Cup, and hopes to do it again next year. He also comments that the coach (Steve Yzerman is mentioned) does a wonderful job, that there is a lot of respect for him, and that ending a long career must happen sometime. The speaker notes that things feel different now, with more awareness of what happens and more ability to enjoy it, and that time tends to fly by.

The lecture explains how linear shift-invariant systems described by linear constant coefficient difference equations can be implemented using digital networks. It states that such difference equations relate the output sequence to linear combinations of past outputs and delayed inputs, and assumes causal systems with boundary conditions that the output is zero when the input is zero for earlier times. Implementation is described as requiring three operations: delay, multiplication by coefficients, and addition (accumulation). The lecture then introduces block diagram notation for representing delays (e.g., using \(z^{-1}\)), coefficient multiplications, and additions, and uses an example first-order equation to illustrate the representation. It presents an alternative representation using signal flow graphs, defining their nodes, source and sink nodes, directed branches, and algebraic rules: node variables equal the sum of outputs of entering branches, and branch outputs are functions of branch inputs. For linear constant coefficient difference equations, the lecture shows how these flow graphs correspond to a matrix form of linear equations involving transmittance coefficients and delay terms. It further discusses separating coefficient and delay matrices, interpreting the resulting equations as a coupled set of first-order difference equations, and demonstrates an example of how node numbering affects computability. It concludes that a network is computable when a suitable node ordering makes the coefficient matrix have no non-zero elements on or above the main diagonal, and that delay-free loops lead to non-computable networks (though equations can still be solvable). The next lectures will focus on common digital network structures for infinite and finite impulse response filters.

Ron Washington said the Angels will not pick up his contract option and that he will not return as manager in 2026. Interim manager Ray Montgomery will also not get the full-time role in 2026, as the Angels will search for their sixth manager in nine years. Washington said the decision was based on the Angels’ performance rather than his health, though he noted his quadruple bypass heart surgery affected his ability to manage. The Angels finished 72-90 and had their 10th straight losing season and one playoff appearance since 2009. The general manager, Perry Minasian, is under contract through 2026, and Albert Pujols and Torii Hunter are considered candidates to become the next manager.

Mr. Fox informed Mr. Upshur in a June 25, 1843 note that the Earl of Aberdeen said the occupation of the Sandwich (Hawaiian) Islands was unauthorized by Her Majesty’s Government, and that inquiry would be made into the proceedings. The passage describes how American influence in Hawaii predominated, shaping the rivalry between England and France. It says French and British policies pushed Americans into defense alongside natives threatened by punishment for perceived wrongs. It also recounts that Hawaii’s first embassy, led by William Richards and Timoteo Haalilio, sought recognition of independence from the United States and then proceeded to England and France. In December 1842, the embassy communicated with Mr. Webster, who in December 1842/1843, on behalf of the President, recognized the independence of the Hawaiian Government and said foreign interference should not be countenanced, noting that formal treaties and diplomatic relations were not yet necessary. The President’s correspondence was sent to Congress on December 30. The passage then states that the recognition was later confirmed by Mr. Calhoun, and that in London on November 28, 1843, Hawaii’s ambassadors secured a convention between France and Great Britain to consider the Sandwich Islands independent and to refrain from taking possession or establishing protectorates over any part of their territory.

Manchester United lost 2-0 to Spurs at Wembley, dropping 15 points behind leaders Man City and allowing Spurs to move within five points in fifth place. Mourinho wants an immediate bounce-back as Alexis Sanchez makes his home debut against Huddersfield Town. Ahead of the match, Mourinho will address fitness updates on Marouane Fellaini and likely discuss touchline issues with Paul Pogba. He will hold his pre-match press conference at Carrington.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU as an Ampere (GA100) data center accelerator built for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It highlights features such as Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) virtualization for secure partitioning, third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (including TF32, BF16, and IEEE-compliant FP64), and a new sparsity feature intended to double Tensor Core throughput. It also covers architecture and system scaling elements including HBM2 memory, L2 cache enhancements, third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch for multi-GPU performance, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and CUDA improvements for programmability and task graph acceleration. The “A100 Introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity” section explains fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 sparse matrix pattern.

Elliott Management Corp said NXP Semiconductors NV is worth US$135 per share on an intrinsic standalone basis, above Qualcomm Inc’s US$110 offer. Elliott, which holds about a 6 percent stake, said Qualcomm’s October 2016 offer has acted as a ceiling on NXP’s valuation and has taken advantage of NXP’s depressed stock price. Elliott also said NXP’s prospects are bright, with about half of its revenue exposed to automotive and industrial growth, and it retained UBS Investment Bank to analyze NXP’s finances. NXP shares have traded above Qualcomm’s offer, though the gap has narrowed. The passage also notes Broadcom’s rejected US$103 billion acquisition approach to Qualcomm and gives premarket share prices for NXP and Qualcomm.

The passage describes a study and project by the Japan Society of Technology Education (JSTE) to develop a new framework for technology and engineering education in Japan. It explains that STEM/STEAM education worldwide has increasingly emphasized design and technology/engineering roles, but these roles are sometimes misunderstood or narrowly defined. In Japan, MEXT has promoted STEAM education as transdisciplinary learning and defined the scope of “Arts” broadly, and the next national curriculum is expected to incorporate STEAM. Because directly applying ITEEA’s STEL to Japan may be difficult, JSTE initiated a project to revise its “Technology Education in the 21st Century” work, including organizing activities such as an Ideathon, holding symposiums (2019–2022), and publishing the New Framework of Technology and Engineering Education (NGTE) in 2021.  

The passage reports Japan’s current technology education status (junior high school “Technology” subject within “Technology and Home Economics”), including lesson allocation and stated objectives and content areas. It then presents a survey of 1,656 students (Hyogo Prefecture) on technology learning and problem-solving, finding positive perceptions of “Technology” classes but limited exploratory activities (inquiry, experimentation, observation) and weak contribution of certain activities to abilities for technological innovation and governance. Based on these findings and societal changes described through Society 5.0, the NGTE aims to strengthen exploratory and engineering-related problem-solving, define technology/engineering education literacy goals, outline a scope connecting physical and cyber technologies, and introduce a Triple-Loop Model of engineering design and a STEAM learning model centered on engineering design. The NGTE draft was evaluated via a symposium and survey, with most proposals receiving mean agreement values of 3.00 or higher, while the concept of “engineering” received lower agreement and was revised in the final version.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated March 8, 2019. On March 6, 2019, its Compensation Committee approved a new form of global performance-based restricted stock unit notice and agreement under the company’s Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan. On March 8, 2019, the Compensation Committee adopted a Variable Compensation Plan for fiscal year 2020, which allows eligible executive officers to earn variable cash payments based on achievement of specified corporate performance goals. The plan’s performance goals are based on fiscal year 2020 revenue with threshold, base operating plan, and stretch operating plan levels. The filing includes target award opportunities for named executive officers under the base operating plan and states that eligibility requires remaining an employee through the payment date unless the Compensation Committee determines otherwise. Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2 are included, and the report is signed by Rebecca Peters.

Robert Cyrus Garrison was charged with first degree rape in Tulsa County District Court, first resulting in a hung jury and then a conviction with a thirty-year penitentiary sentence. The case used a two-stage proceeding: the jury found him guilty in stage one, and stage two involved court instructions on punishment under 57 O.S. Supp. 1969, § 138, which was the only complained-of error. The court referenced Williams v. State, which held § 138 unconstitutional for mandating jury instructions and allowing commentary on its provisions. Although the court found the instruction did not warrant reversal, it said the instruction prejudiced the sentence because it led the jury to believe he could serve 30 years in about 15 years; it noted good time credits depend on institutional rules and can be removed, and should not be considered by the jury in assessing punishment. The judgment and sentence were modified from thirty years to fifteen years and otherwise affirmed.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 13, 2019. The report states that, pursuant to a prior announcement, Tesla appointed Zachary Kirkhorn as Chief Financial Officer to succeed Deepak Ahuja, and appointed Vaibhav Taneja as Chief Accounting Officer. It also describes each appointee’s prior roles at Tesla and other employers, and notes stock option and restricted stock unit grants that will be granted and vest over four years under Tesla’s standard equity policies.

The Port Hardy Secondary School (PHSS) Seniors Girls soccer team won the Island Championships and will advance to provincials. At a tournament in Duncan, they beat Duncan Christian School 6-1, lost to Glenlyon Norfolk 5-4, and drew St. Andrews 1-1 before winning 3-1 in extra time. They qualified for provincials by winning the semi-final, but then lost 4-3 to Glenlyon Norfolk for first place. PHSS will compete in the BC Single A High School Provincials in Penticton from May 31 to June 3rd. Players Leanne Wilson and Hailey Ranger said they are most looking forward to traveling and facing tough competition. Coach Jim Buchan said he wants the team to represent the school well.

An audit by state Auditor General Eugene DePasquale found that former Duquesne School District superintendent Barbara McDonnell and four employees used district funds for personal loans. The audit said McDonnell authorized about $41,000 in personal, no-interest loans to herself and others, with about $22,000 going to her, and board of education approval was not provided. DePasquale also criticized questionable accounting, including missing documentation for $1.3 million in state transportation reimbursements and concluded the state overpaid at least $180,000. Although the employees repaid the loans through payroll deductions over time, DePasquale referred McDonnell, the employees, and the matter to the State Ethics Commission.

The passage is a political address in which the speaker emphasizes responsibility in interpreting the Republican Party’s covenant and believes in party sponsorship and party government as a constitutional, representative system rather than personal rule. He argues that the Constitution and party-led popular government have preserved liberty and stability, and he calls for restoring representative popular government after wartime shifts toward executive autocracy. He outlines foreign policy priorities for maintaining American independence while engaging in international peace through international law and a co-operative association of nations, while opposing surrender of rights to a world council or military alliance such as the League Covenant. Domestically, he stresses constitutional order, protection of civil liberties with limits against sedition, and urges economic policies focused on full production, reduced cost of living through efficiency, opposition to profiteering, and thrift. He highlights labor-management-capital understanding, economic and social justice, and calls for government to avoid class-based political appeals. The speaker also discusses transportation needs (especially opposing government ownership and advocating infrastructure support), monetary stabilization through deflation and restoring the dollar, agricultural support through cooperation for farmers, and various governance positions including business-like federal administration, protective tariffs, strong maritime and defense capabilities, and immigration standards. He addresses postwar adjustments, law enforcement, honoring World War I veterans, women’s suffrage, anti-lynching action, housing aid, bond value, revised war tax burdens, civil rights for Black citizens, and improved relations with Mexico. The address concludes with pledges of service and acceptance of the Republican Party’s nomination for President.

Warren Buffett is reportedly eyeing Berkshire Hathaway’s biggest deal in three years: acquiring petrochemical unit OxyChem for roughly $10 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal. The Journal says the potential deal could be finalized within days and would be Berkshire’s largest since its 2022 purchase of insurer Alleghany for $11.6 billion. Berkshire has a record cash hoard of $344 billion. Buffett, 95, plans to step down as CEO at the end of 2025 but remain chairman, and Greg Abel is expected to succeed him. Shares of Occidental, Houston-based where Berkshire holds a 28.2% stake worth over $11 billion, fell 1.8% Tuesday despite the report; Buffett previously said he would not take full control of Occidental.

The passage describes “Lobster 207,” formally the Maine Lobstering Union (MLU), a cooperative and local lodge of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM).
