Only eight of 32 councils expect to meet the government’s October deadline; Perth and Kinross is the only council to have completed a list, and seven more plan to do so this year. Eighteen councils have no plans or are unsure, which activist research says leaves passengers in areas such as Aberdeen and Stirling facing higher prices and difficulty booking trips. The law fines taxi drivers up to £1,000 for refusing to take wheelchair users or charging extra, but only applies to drivers registered on council Section 167 lists. The research also found many councils have low wheelchair-accessible taxi registration and that only 30% require disability awareness training; it reports that in 2016, Muscular Dystrophy UK found a quarter of disabled people had been refused taxi service due to disability. Activists and Muscular Dystrophy UK are calling for the government to require councils to set deadlines and promote list creation.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 21, 2018 reporting that at a special meeting of stockholders held on March 21, 2018, Tesla’s stockholders approved the CEO Performance Award previously granted to Elon Musk on January 21, 2018. The award’s material terms were incorporated by reference from Tesla’s February 8, 2018 proxy statement (Exhibit 99.1). Approval required affirmative votes under NASDAQ, amended and restated bylaws, and disinterested stockholder standards. The vote results were: under the NASDAQ standard, 96,795,092 for and 23,407,632 against; under the bylaws standard, 96,795,092 for, 23,407,632 against, and 173,167 abstained; and under the disinterested standard, 63,014,339 for and 23,407,632 against, with broker non-votes reported as 0.

Point-of-care lung ultrasound (LUS) may help evaluate cardiopulmonary conditions in emergency and critical care, offering portability, rapid results, lower cost, and no ionizing radiation. It has been proposed for COVID-19 pneumonia to help prevent nosocomial spread and potentially identify patients at risk for decompensation in resource-limited settings. However, standardized evidence-based use has not been fully established.  

This prospective study aimed to assess whether baseline LUS findings were associated with subsequent oxygen support needs or death in adults hospitalized with RT-PCR–confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. LUS was standardized using 6-second clips from 12 lung zones, and a mean lung ultrasound score (mLUSS) was calculated to allow inclusion of missing zones. The primary outcome was subsequent ICU-level care (high-flow oxygen, noninvasive, or invasive ventilation); secondary outcomes included 28-day mortality and 28-day progression to mechanical ventilation or death.  

Among 264 participants, mLUSS and several individual LUS characteristics were associated with increased risk of disease progression. Each point increase in mLUSS was associated with ICU-level care progression and 28-day mortality, and results were unchanged in several sensitivity analyses. In subgroup findings, A lines were associated with decreased risk, while pleural abnormalities were associated with increased risk of mechanical ventilation plus death and death. The study concluded that individual LUS findings and the mLUSS across available lung zones are associated with ultimate oxygen requirement or death in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, independent of duration of illness.

Todd Kimberlain forwarded an email from Jack Beven, who reported that Jim Gross provided a file of watch/warning areas from 1963 to 1998, constructed by Mark Demaria and assumed complete for the continental US. Gross listed a key with fields (mn, dy, year, hr, storm name, # of warnings, strmid) and codes mapping 6=hurricane warning, 5=hurricane watch, 4=storm warning, 3=gale warning, 2=tropical storm warning, and 1=tropical storm watch; the from/to or to/from portions were described as arbitrary. The remainder of the message shows watch/warning entries by date/time, storm name, code number, and location pairs for multiple storms across the years 1963–1998.

An international team led by scientists from Senckenberg and the University of Vienna, including UCL researchers, found that the number of newly established alien species has increased continuously worldwide over the past 200 years, with more than a third of first introductions recorded between 1970 and 2014. Trends differed among taxonomic groups, with increases in vascular plants, birds, and mammals in the 19th century linked to horticulture and beneficial introductions during European colonial expansion, and steep increases for algae, molluscs, and insects after 1950 linked to globalisation of trade. Using a database of first detection dates for 16,000 alien species from over 45,000 records, the researchers found 37% were introduced between 1970–2014, with a 1996 peak of 585 new alien species worldwide. The study suggests there is no sign of saturation for most groups and that current laws have not been effective enough, indicating a need for more effective prevention policies.

The passage says that on an NPR program, a researcher from People’s Pharmacy discussed how losing weight may require a calorie reduction: losing 5% of body weight would require 10% fewer calories to maintain weight. The author suggests this could explain why patients often regain weight after losing it. The passage then promotes dMeetings as a new way to educate diabetes patients so they can learn independently from certified educators, and directs readers to a New Product item to get started.

The passage describes a study assessing the impact of implementing pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) for all advanced solid tumor patients at Providence between September 2019 and November 2021 using a standardized 523-gene DNA/RNA assay. The study reports that 49% of CGP-tested cases had at least one guideline-based actionable biomarker and that CGP increased trial matching and actionable mutation detection compared with an in silico 50-gene panel. In an analyzed cohort of 1,482 patients with follow-up, utilization of precision and immunotherapy was high, and patients treated with biomarker-guided targeted therapy or immunotherapy had improved overall survival versus chemotherapy alone, with median overall survival of 25 vs. 17 months overall (and 26 vs. 16 months for NSCLC). The study also notes remaining gaps, including that many CGP results are non-actionable for some tumor types and barriers to treatment access and adoption.

The passage describes Lenovo’s Legion Go S handheld with SteamOS, presented as a $120-off upgraded version intended as an entry into gaming handhelds. The author prefers the SteamOS model over the Windows version, citing a setup process involving turning on the device and scanning a QR code to download games and saves from the cloud. The device is described as bulky but comfortable, with built-in controller grips, a spacious button layout, and well-placed triggers and bumpers. It features a bright 120-Hz IPS screen, 1 TB storage, 32 GB memory, and a MicroSD card slot. The author notes that newer non-Nintendo handheld games may require some settings or resolution tweaks, but the Legion Go S ran games well with minimal tweaking, aided by SteamOS support. The author compares it to a larger, more expensive Legion 2 that runs Windows and says the deal is solid for users planning to use SteamOS.

Mercedes introduced a limited-edition “Grand Edition” version of the seven-seater GLS 500 4MATIC to keep its flagship SUV competitive. The Grand Edition includes unique exterior details such as 20-inch lightweight alloy wheels with a high-sheen finish, black contrasts, and “Grand Edition” badges on the front wings. Inside, it features an all-nappa leather dashboard, model-unique wood trim, specific leather color combinations, diamond quilted seats with porcelain and espresso brown leather, mid-brown seams, Budapest-design piping, and velour floor mats in espresso brown. The Grand Edition package is offered as an €8,250 upgrade on all non-AMG GLS-Class variations, from the 350d 4Matic to the GLS 500 4Matic, with order books opened and deliveries starting in March 2018.

George Washington states that initial measures to call out the militia rather than embody them were taken, but that overtures of forgiveness and conciliation in Western Pennsylvania were only partially accepted and did not stop violence or treasonable opposition. He declares that, in obedience to the Constitution to execute the laws, he will reduce the refractory to subordination to law and announces that a sufficient force is already moving to the scene of disaffection, with full support for those who rely on the government. He says those who qualify for indemnity will be treated with liberal good faith if they do not forfeit their claim, and that instructions have been given accordingly. He exhorts individuals and officers to oppose the measures leading to these crimes, uphold truthful and stable government, and maintain the Constitution and laws, and he warns against aiding insurgents while requiring officers and citizens to bring offenders under the law.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on April 26, 2022. The report states that Microsoft issued a press release on April 26, 2022 announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2022, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes information about securities registered, an item regarding results of operations and financial condition, and an exhibit list showing Exhibit 99.1 as the press release dated April 26, 2022. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko appeared at a news conference in Kyiv less than 24 hours after Ukrainian police reported he had been shot and killed. Ukrainian security services said his death was faked to foil a plot against his life, and that authorities had solved the slaying. Security service head Vasyl Gritsak invited Babchenko into the room, where he apologized to mourners and said he was still alive. Investigators identified a Ukrainian citizen allegedly recruited and paid $40,000 by Russian security services to organize the killing, who then hired an acquaintance to act as the gunman. Babchenko had fled Russia in February 2017 after receiving death threats, and after moving to Kyiv in late 2017 continued to face threats, according to Ilya Ponomarev.

Czech central bank board member Toms Nidetzky said the central bank will likely deliver one more interest rate hike this year after three increases since last August, but no immediate action is needed. He said inflation does not require signaling another rate rise now, and he expects a more thorough debate toward the end of the year, adding that one more hike is likely based on current economic development. The bank’s forecast predicts an increase in the repo rate from 0.75 percent around end-2018 or start-2019. Czech inflation has slowed, and at its March 29 meeting the bank assessed risks to its forecast as slightly anti-inflationary, while another board member, Vojtech Benda, said he saw risks tilted higher but no need to raise rates in the short term.

The passage describes FoLix, a first FDA-cleared fractional laser hair-loss treatment that aims to be surgery-free. It is administered in-office, takes about 20 to 30 minutes per session, requires no anesthesia, and has little to no downtime, with minimal aftercare needs. FoLix works by stimulating hair growth through existing hair follicles by creating microscopic channels in the scalp. It is intended for people with early to moderate hair loss who have intact but underperforming follicles, and is not meant for complete baldness or extensive scarring. Sessions are required regularly—three to six times in the first year and up to twice yearly for maintenance—with costs ranging from $750 to $1,250 per session. Potential mild temporary side effects include redness, tightness, scalp sensitivity, and temporary shedding. The passage advises consulting a doctor because hair loss can have multiple causes.

During the infant plaintiff’s delivery, shoulder dystocia occurred and the infant was found to have sustained Erb’s palsy. A jury found the municipal hospital and a staff member negligent and awarded damages for past pain and suffering ($50,000), future physiotherapy ($200,000), future psychological counseling ($600,000), and future pain and suffering ($2,000,000). After a post-trial motion, the plaintiff consented to reduce the award to $50,000 for past pain and suffering, $116,000 for future psychological counseling, $180,000 for future physiotherapy, and $1,500,000 for future pain and suffering. The reviewing court rejected the defendants’ argument that the reduced award deviated materially from reasonable compensation under CPLR 5501(c) and found no basis to disturb the trial court’s determination that the portion of the verdict for future pain and suffering was excessive.

Protesters against hatred and racism said they gathered to counter a white supremacist rally in Virginia that led to deadly violence. On Sunday, anti-fascist protests occurred in San Francisco, and there was a march to President Donald Trump’s home in New York. In Seattle, police arrested three men as Trump supporters and counter-protesters converged downtown. In Denver, several hundred demonstrators marched from Martin Luther King Jr.’s statue in City Park to the state Capitol. In New York, protesters marched to Trump Tower demanding Trump denounce white nationalist groups. In Charlottesville, protesters held a vigil at the site where a day earlier a car attack killed one person in a peaceful anti-white-nationalist crowd.

The speaker says the team feels comfortable playing in front of anyone because their goaltenders have been put in tough situations and responded well. They describe a goaltender as smart and mention that last night they had good looks but didn’t score, emphasizing persistence and not getting discouraged by bad bounces. The speaker adds that the team focuses on playing rather than what is said in papers or on TV, and that they believe they can play with the opposing team but need to execute and play better. They also discuss rallying around a player who has battled for them, noting concerns about him being pulled, and say they were tentative at times but mainly avoided penalties, with most penalties being stick infractions. They conclude the team can be more physical while staying within positioning against a team that moves the puck well.

Birel ART and PSL reported double victory at Palm Beach Round 2 of the Florida Winter Tour, ROK Edition, with 191 drivers. Ryan Norberg won the ROK Senior final, earning fast lap and regaining the championship after qualifying P2 and setbacks in heats. Scott Davidson won the ROK Shifter Master final for his first win of the season. Igor Pushkin finished P5, Ryan MacDermid ended P10 after heat incidents, and Justin Aresneu finished P12. The team credited Allison Race Engines and Legree Engines and noted the Rotax edition of the championship begins Feb 16.

The passage describes distance education’s growth and implementation, especially during COVID-19, and frames it as a sustainable education option that can be disrupted by events like wars, disasters, and pandemics. It outlines how distance education developed in Turkey through different technological periods and discusses distance education in music education, noting limited suitable offerings for digital music education. The study aims to determine visually impaired students’ views on distance education in vocational music education, including the model used (synchronous/asynchronous), technologies used, adequacy of materials, assessment methods, perceived strengths and weaknesses, and suggestions for improvement.

Methodologically, it uses a qualitative case study design with semi-structured interviews. The study group includes seven visually impaired students with undergraduate or graduate education in music departments in Turkey, reached via a “barrier-free music score” initiative network. Data were analyzed using content analysis.

Findings report that most courses were taught synchronously, with some exceptions and variations in how students followed lessons (including asynchronous listening due to circumstances such as health problems). Students primarily used computers, with some using phones or tablets. Many reported that course materials did not consider their special needs; some required parental support, and slides or PDFs were not always usable. Assessment and evaluation sometimes involved individual arrangements, but limitations remained for theoretical courses and exam participation. Students cited time and place flexibility as strengths, while weaknesses included technical inadequacies (especially sound synchronization and inability to sing/play simultaneously) and issues related to instructors’ technological competence. Students suggested longer lesson duration, regular support, accessible audio/document tools (including screen-reader-related solutions), improved infrastructure, faster problem resolution, and accessible interfaces compatible with assistive technologies. The conclusion states that distance education during COVID-19 was difficult for visually impaired professional music education students and emphasizes the need for accessible environments, tailored materials, and appropriate technological and support measures throughout the process.

The speaker says they had chances to score but did not, and mentions a missed attempt when the puck rolled and went wide. They emphasize staying positive and preparing for the third game, taking it one game at a time and “putting things in perspective.” They note the opponent is a great hockey team that capitalizes on turnovers, so they must prevent breakouts or lapses, keep the puck on the outside, and avoid chipping it into the middle. They say the loss is difficult but the team will go out with the will to win, give their all, and be ready for the third game.

The United States brought an action under the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to enforce rights under the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments against Hale County, Alabama, and related defendants. The court found that Hale County is covered by Section 5 and that legislative enactments changing the method of electing Hale County Commissioners from district to at-large basis in 1965, 1971, and 1973 were not given required preclearance, making those acts of no force or effect and elections conducted under them unlawful. The court ordered that the November 2, 1976 election be held as scheduled, with the elected commissioners serving provisionally pending further orders, and directed submissions to the Attorney General and possible proceedings in the District of Columbia. If no timely action is filed or if an action does not reverse the Attorney General or uphold the 1973 act’s constitutionality, a prompt district-based election is to be held. In the supplemental opinion, the court concluded that Alabama’s designation subjects all its political subdivisions, and therefore Section 5 applies to Hale County.

The passage strongly criticizes Hillary Clinton, asserting that her truth depends on whether it supports a myth about her ambition and “greatness.” It claims she used police-state tactics, vulgar libels, and failed on health care and national security. It alleges she played a role in events in Libya and references WikiLeaks and adviser Sidney Blumenthal. It further claims the media helped the Clintons for decades and cites reports about an FBI investigation into her use of a personal email server, interactions involving Loretta Lynch, and alleged failures by Rod Rosenstein in an FBI informant matter. The passage also lists numerous alleged scandals and characterizes Clinton as a liar and arrogant, concluding by questioning whether America is “done.”

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x (GA102) GPU architecture features, focusing on 2x FP32 processing, second-generation RT Cores for ray tracing and motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity support and new data types like TF32 and BF16. It also covers memory and interconnect technologies including GDDR6X (with up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth), third-generation NVLink (scaling memory to 96 GB with two GPUs), and PCIe Gen4. The text provides examples of performance and feature benefits for products such as GeForce RTX 3090, RTX A6000, and A40, including applications in graphics workloads, compute acceleration, data center use, and professional visualization. It further discusses display features (DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1), video decoding (fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode), video encoding (seventh-generation NVENC), and NVIDIA RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression to improve I/O performance.

Anna Gasser won gold in women’s Big Air snowboarding at the Olympic debut, edging Jamie Anderson in a final at Pyeongchang. Gasser, the reigning world champion, scored 96 on her last jump—a double cork 1080—for a total of 185.00 after Anderson led initially but sat down while trying to land her final jump. Zoi Sadowski Synnott won bronze with 157.50, giving New Zealand its first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years. The results followed concerns about windy conditions at Phoenix Snow Park, leading officials to move Big Air finals earlier and complete the competition at Alpensia Ski Jump Centre.

The passage describes a patent continuation for connecting electrical circuitry in quantum computing systems, incorporating prior related applications by reference. It provides background that quantum computers may use superconducting Josephson junction structures and require many interconnected components such as wire bonds, connectors, cables, filters, attenuators, and feedthroughs. The passage outlines example drawings and technologies involving flexible stripline cables connected to rigid boards within cryogenic dilution refrigerator assemblies, including configurations that fan out flex cables for mechanical integrity and thermally anchor them to isothermal plates. It discusses integrating components like filters and attenuators into rigid boards or flex cables using absorptive materials near windows in grounding planes, and routing RF/DC signals through overlapping flex cables and rigid boards to a quantum processing unit (QPU). It also describes flex cable constructions with parallel insulating surfaces, internal stripline conductors, grounding planes, vias for electromagnetic shielding, optional stiffeners, and materials/composition details for conductors, dielectrics, and absorptive polymers. Further, it explains cryogenic electrical connections using compliant joints between flex cables, interposers, PCBs, and the QPU, including examples of signal conditioning modules and compliant-joint contact structures. The passage concludes with enumerated claim clauses defining flexible cable and cryogenic system components, including configurations with superconducting/non-superconducting metals, integrated shielding, thermal/Mechanical connections to isothermal plates, and QPUs with at least specified quantum bit counts.

A Teagasc survey found that 20% of the 314 Irish male farmers interviewed had never consulted a doctor about their health, and 57% had visited a doctor in the past 12 months (below the national average of 65%). The research reported higher mortality rates from cardiovascular disease and cancers among Irish farmers than other occupational groups, noting that the causes of these health inequalities are not fully understood. Over the past 12 months, 39% reported ill health, mainly lower back pain, arthritis (rheumatoid and/or osteoarthritis), and/or anxiety. The study also reported that 20% of farmers were current smokers (vs 24% nationally), 88% consumed alcohol regularly, 22% drank weekly, and 22% reported weekly binge drinking. Farmers under 45 were more likely to smoke and drink weekly, while those over 45 were more likely to report arthritis, with rheumatoid arthritis reported by 13%—three times the national average.

A former New York judge, Louis L. Nock, joined Anderson Kill last month and said he did so due to family considerations and mandatory retirement looming when he turns 70. However, Law360 reports he did not mention that New York ethics regulators agreed to drop ethics charges after he agreed to resign from the bench and never accept judicial office again; he had resigned effective Sept. 2. The complaints alleged Nock acted rudely and demeaning toward court staff and threatened retaliation against commission staff and witnesses unless the charges were dismissed; Nock denied misconduct. Anderson Kill said it was satisfied there was no finding of wrongdoing and that the allegations did not call his character or conduct into question. Nock’s lawyer said there were no findings and no further charges, and said Nock had planned to leave the bench.

The passage summarizes evidence that GM-CSF and CRP are involved in the hyperinflammatory immune response in COVID-19, with CRP increasing due to IL-6 and correlating with disease progression. In the phase 3 LIVE-AIR trial, GM-CSF neutralization with lenzilumab improved survival without invasive mechanical ventilation (SWOV) versus placebo, with no treatment-emergent serious adverse events attributable to lenzilumab reported to date. A comprehensive analysis of LIVE-AIR CRP data found baseline CRP to be the strongest predictor of SWOV, with participants with baseline CRP <150 mg/L (78% of the evaluable population) showing the greatest benefit from lenzilumab, including improved SWOV through day 28 and improvements in several secondary endpoints such as reduced incidence of IMV/ECMO/death and ventilator-free days. Participants with baseline CRP ≥150 mg/L were described as experiencing hyperinflammation and having higher risk of imminent respiratory escalation or death. The passage also describes that CRP levels were reduced more rapidly with lenzilumab than with placebo and presents study methods, outcomes, safety findings, and limitations related to post-hoc and exploratory analyses.

The speaker says the upcoming match is the biggest game they can play, comparing it to events like Olympic finals and world championships, and noting the long playoffs run. They say the team is calm but expects nerves, is excited, and wants to enjoy the moment. They add that an injured player has still been involved with the team—giving advice, being in the locker room, and being present—and that his playing and being in the locker room would mean a lot. They also mention strong fan support and that the playoffs, especially the last days before the finals, have been unbelievable.

Donna Adelson, 75, convicted in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, told a judge before sentencing that she is “an innocent woman” convicted “without evidence.” She said Markel would be “appalled” by the lack of justice at her trial, claimed there was no evidence of her participation in the murder-for-hire plot, and said she would have stopped it if she had known beforehand. Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said the motive was the Adelson family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife Wendi Adelson to South Florida with their children.

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw Kathleen Hartnett White’s nomination to chair the Council on Environmental Quality and serve as President Donald Trump’s top environmental adviser. White was announced in October and had been part of a Texas commission for six years under Rick Perry, now the energy secretary. Her nomination was delayed in the Senate and was resubmitted in January after being sent back in late 2017. The passage describes her as not a scientist and cites her past comments that mainstream climate scientists’ work is like “dogmatic” claims, that particulate pollution isn’t harmful unless one were to suck on a car’s tailpipe, and that carbon dioxide is not a pollutant but a “necessary nutrient for plant life.” Critics cited her praise of fossil fuels and her opposition to stricter air and water pollution limits, and she is described as a senior fellow at the Texas Public Policy Foundation, which received funding from fossil-fuel companies. Senator Tom Carper said withdrawing the nomination was the right decision and urged a different nominee.

The author describes an initial belief that institutional investing would be more predictable than retail, but finds that pension boards and investment committees are often imperfect and influenced by unengaged or untrained members. This leads to a five-year PhD research project on asset owner governance (pensions, foundations, endowments), including creating a research protocol because governance data were scarce. The study examines 35 public pension plans (2008–2012) and finds substantial performance variability: the best plan averaged 15% annually while the worst averaged -4.2%. Differences in governance-related behavior help explain performance gaps. The study identifies factors such as organizational institutional knowledge and stability (including member turnover), professionalism (including meeting frequency and board composition), engagement, staff involvement, and diligence. It reports that investment expenses were not statistically significant in its model, and that governance measured by Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ) scores is linked to investment outcomes: the top 20% by FEQ outperformed the bottom fifth by nearly 2 to 1, and each FEQ unit improvement corresponded to a 0.36% increase in five-year investment performance.

Ray tracing is a computationally intensive rendering technology that realistically simulates lighting. Turing GPU-based ray tracing can render physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting in real time. Previously, GPU architectures could not perform real-time ray tracing for games or graphical applications with a single GPU, so games relied on fast rasterization techniques instead. Real-time ray tracing required about 10 years of collaboration and is enabled by multiple new hardware ray tracing acceleration engines called RT Cores.

The study assessed knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) of contraception and their predictors among female TV studies students in Nigeria. It was a cross-sectional study at NTA TV College, Nigeria, using a semi-structured self-administered questionnaire; multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify predictors. Among 217 participants (mean age 22), levels of good knowledge, good attitude, and good practice were 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7% respectively. About 74% reported ever having sex; friends and the internet were the main sources of contraceptive information, and condoms and oral contraceptive pills were the most commonly used methods. The main reason for non-use was fear of side effects or health risks. Being a young adult (>19) predicted good knowledge, while being a diploma student, living off-campus, and having good knowledge predicted good attitude. Being from the state’s indigenous population and ever engaging in sex predicted good contraceptive practice. The study concludes that KAP levels were relatively low and calls for urgent improvements in advocacy, policies, and young people-friendly sexual and reproductive health services.

Fiscal year 2017 financial statements were restated for 2016. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2017, total revenues increased 88.4% to $46.50 million from $24.68 million in 2016. Loan origination service fees were $26.70 million, loan repayment management fees were $18.21 million, and financing income from entrusted loans was $1.58 million in 2017 (with nil entrusted-loan income in 2016). Operating income rose 301.6% to $17.95 million, and net income increased 343.9% to $15.27 million. Diluted EPS was $0.21 in 2017 versus $0.05 in 2016. Loans facilitated through the platform increased 59.9% to $1,308.7 million in 2017 from $818.5 million in 2016. The company reported 8,047 borrowers, 69,232 investors, and 23,263 loans in 2017, compared with 1,067 borrowers, 39,999 investors, and 8,739 loans in 2016. As of December 31, 2017, cash and cash equivalents were $12.68 million, with total current assets of $55.27 million and total current liabilities of $17.47 million. Net cash provided by operating activities was $24.07 million in 2017 versus $4.83 million in 2016, and net cash used in investing activities was $34.02 million in 2017 versus $9.16 million in 2016.

Chrissy Teigen, due to give birth to her second child in June, shared in an interview that she has had stretch marks for years, mostly on her inner thighs, and uses various products and nightly routines to help prevent stretch marks during pregnancy. She said her belly is the only place she doesn’t get marks, and emphasized prevention over reacting after skin changes. Her routine includes Aquaphor, coconut oil, and Lumière de Vie products, and she spends 10–15 minutes per night applying layers of product to her belly, with help from her husband John Legend and daughter Luna. She also said she gets Lumière products because she worked with the brand and believes stretch marks are common among women, including supermodels.

New research found that girls who start using social media younger tend to be unhappier as they progress through their teens. Scientists at the University of Essex and University College London reported that girls used social media more than boys and showed a larger decline in well-being during adolescence. In a survey of 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10 to 15, girls who used social media for an hour or more by age 10 had lower well-being by age 15. The study, published in BMC Public Health, based happiness scores on multiple life aspects and used a questionnaire for negative emotional and behavioural problems. Researchers said early monitoring of social media interactions, particularly for girls, may be important, and they noted the link may be underestimated due to self-reported data and tracking only school-day interactions.

The passage is a collection of dated Enron-related news and editorials from multiple publications. It includes commentary on California’s 2001 power crisis, reporting on Wall Street market moves and earnings focus, and pieces on political and social reactions, including an op-ed about the author’s four-month fellowship absence. It also contains analysis of energy deregulation issues, a report on wind power’s growing role in addressing blackouts, and an item about Enron employees’ “rank and yank” performance-review system. Another section reports that India’s Maharashtra State Electricity Board may miss a payment to Enron’s Dabhol Power, and another editorial discusses potential U.S. mediation with Maharashtra regarding Enron contractual obligations.

The passage consists of a coach’s remarks about managing lineup losses during the playoffs and preparing for upcoming games. It discusses how removing key players like Chris Pronger and others forced the team to distribute minutes differently, rely on specialty teams (power play and penalty killing), and have other players step up. It covers decisions related to suspensions and game-time health checks for players such as Chris Kunitz, including concerns about not risking players’ health and using personnel based on what gives the best chance to win. The coach also comments on discipline and penalties, arguing that undisciplined penalties should be reduced and that the team must play its best game to match opponents’ intensity. The passage then describes a previous game’s emotional start, a sequence of penalties and special-teams time, the importance of penalty killing, and standout contributions from players such as Teemu Selanne, Dustin Penner, and Huskins, emphasizing execution, team play, and leadership. It concludes with the idea that after a win, preparation must immediately shift to the next, toughest game.

The President returned House bill No. 6242 without his signature and with objections. He said the bill’s appropriations include some for purposes beyond constitutional limits, benefiting only particular localities rather than the common defense or general welfare, and not promoting commerce among the States. He argued that such local appropriations increase over time as states seek similar benefits and that the bill’s river and harbor appropriations have grown rapidly. He also objected that the bill appropriates an amount he considers greatly exceeding the country’s needs for the present fiscal year and would force expenditures too large and fast to be economical. He suggested Congress could enact the bill with only half the aggregate amount appropriated for the fiscal year and that spending be limited to objects the Secretary of War, under the President’s direction, determines, with no purpose exceeding the bill’s stated amounts.

A domestic violence support group led by Rebecca Hunter, MSW, in partnership with Helping Hands Against Violence meets Tuesdays at noon, is free, open to women survivors, and is held for healing and empowerment; call 541-400-0186 for location and details. AARP Tax Aide sessions are available at no charge for personal federal and Oregon tax returns, but not for Sch C losses or Sch E rental properties; sites include Hood River Library (Mondays, 2–6 p.m.) and Hood River Adult Center (Thursdays, 2–6 p.m.), plus Mid-Columbia Senior Center in The Dalles (Fridays, 2–6 p.m., and Saturdays, 9 a.m.–1 p.m.), with walk-in service and Spanish-speaking assistance; bring photo ID, proof of social security numbers or ITINs, last year’s return, 2017 tax documents, and proof of health insurance. Chess for Success Region 20 Tournament registration is open for students in grades K–12 for a Feb. 24 event at The Dalles Middle School. Girls Up is collecting cleaned used bras and sports bras for homeless Hood River Valley High School Girl Up members and shelters, with local distribution through Helping Hands Against Violence Women’s Shelter, and donations accepted throughout February at Melika and Foundation 45 or HRVHS.

Pakistan Volleyball Federation Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob said the federal government should build a well-facilitated sports complex in Abbottabad so national athletes can hold summer camps there instead of training in Islamabad during heat waves. He said Pakistan has only one mega sports facility, the Pakistan Sports Complex in Islamabad, and that similar facilities at Abbottabad would allow camps from May to September and enable international events in summer. He criticized the Narowal Sports Complex for being far from the sports fraternity and noted Liaquat Gymnasium in Islamabad is not air-conditioned, causing problems for volleyballers. Yaqoob also suggested improving boarding facilities at Islamabad, requested an early Asian Games volleyball camp for lack of time, and said Pakistan’s youth and junior camps were shifted from Islamabad to Peshawar. He added that PSB will meet federations and the Pakistan Olympic Association on June 6 and that the Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi will arrive to handle all three camps.

The passage describes slope compensation for TPS7H500x-SP peak current mode controllers to prevent subharmonic oscillation when duty cycle exceeds 50%. It explains that adding a voltage-ramp slope compensation, with a minimum stable value of 0.5 times the inductor falling current slope (m) and a recommended value of 1×m, can maintain stability. It then provides formulas and component-setting guidance for determining slope compensation, compensation frequency components (Type 2A/2B), and notes differences for various converter topologies and transformer turns ratios. Additional sections cover thermal shutdown behavior, fixed-frequency peak current mode operation, and a push-pull converter design example including selected values for resistors, capacitors, dead time, blanking time, output/filter components, clamp and inductor settings, current limiting, and frequency compensation parts. Layout guidelines for noise reduction and routing are also provided.

The Johnson Publishing Company headquarters in Chicago, previously home to Ebony and Jet magazines, was granted landmark status and sold for $10 million. It was acquired by 3L Real Estate, which plans to invest $20 million to convert it into a luxury residential complex with 150 apartments and amenities including a fitness center, laundry room, and underground parking garage. Rents are expected to range from $1,200 to $2,700. The project is set to begin in 2018 and be completed the following year, with some parts of the structure preserved, including the Ebony and Jet signs. The building’s ownership has changed over the years, including sales involving Linda Johnson Rice and Columbia College.

The Federal Government unveiled plans for multiple developmental projects in Nigeria’s South-East region, including a foundation-laying ceremony for the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Minister of Science and Technology Ogbonnaya Onu said the Buhari administration is committed to implementing international universities and youth cooperation with Africa through informal science learning for sustainable development. He said the ministry entered a Memorandum of Understanding with the Pontifical Council for Culture of the Vatican City and urged state and local governments and stakeholders to ensure project sustainability, arguing that science and technology are needed for national development and economic growth. Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha, represented by Chris Nwike, pledged support for speedy completion and urged the community to treat the project as an opportunity for both present and future generations.

The passage is a beginner guide to CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) in 2022, describing it as an online advertising company and one of the oldest affiliate networks, operating since 1998. It explains how CJ works as a middleman between advertisers and publishers by tracking sales or leads and paying commissions, and lists features such as tracking, management, payment options, account manager support, promotional tools (banners and product feeds), and granular reporting. It outlines how to start: create a free account with a website or social media profile targeting audiences from the US or Canada, complete the application and profile, wait for approval, set up payment/tax information as needed, apply to advertisers/programs, and share affiliate links while using the dashboard to view performance (clicks, sales, commissions). The passage notes that CJ offers thousands of programs across niches, includes a review claiming it is easy to use but may have a learning curve and strict approval, and provides FAQs on legitimacy, earnings potential, fees, commission rate (5–10%), payment methods (direct deposit/check/Payoneer), payout timing, and accepted payment thresholds.

Duane Boning welcomes students to MIT 2.830J in Singapore and Cambridge and explains class logistics. Most lectures are live video-linked; on holidays, Singapore may use the recorded lecture posted on the website. Students are directed to the Stellar website because class materials (lecture notes, readings, assignments, problem sets) are deployed there, and direct handouts are rare. Slides are typically loaded in advance, and students may print them for note-taking, but copies are not provided in class.

Boning discusses course expectations and prerequisites: students should have substantial manufacturing process experience (examples given include 2.810 and 6.152J, plus industrial experience) and basic probability/statistics (examples include 6.041 or 15.064). The course is interactive, with emphasis on sharing experiences and doubts, and on students providing individual write-ups that articulate reasoning rather than only final answers. Grading is described as weekly problem sets (~40%), two quizzes (~40%), and a team project in the last third of the class; there is no final exam. Teams are typically three students and produce both a world presentation and a project report.

The required textbooks are identified as a semiconductor process control book by Gary May and Costas Spanos (readings start soon) and Montgomery’s *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control* (available via MIT library reserve). The teaching assistant, Hayden Taylor, is introduced, along with administrative contact details and office hours plans.

Boning and David Hardt outline the course focus: manufacturing process control centered on quality and manufacturing variation. Early lectures include process physics background, statistical models, and techniques such as statistical process control, design of experiments, process optimization/robustness, and active/feedback control. They discuss manufacturing goals such as minimizing cost drivers (labor, overhead, time, setup), maintaining equipment and quality, and addressing flexibility and energy/resource considerations. Examples of process control challenges include small semiconductor feature sizes, microfluidic channel geometry issues for DNA diagnostics, assembly tolerance accumulation, and high-density connector variability, illustrating the growing importance of process control as dimensions shrink. The class ends with guidance to watch the Thursday videotape, obtain assigned readings, and check for related seminars (including 2.888).

The Eagles practiced Monday morning at the NovaCare Complex ahead of Thursday night’s preseason game against the Buffalo Bills. Jordan Matthews was traded to the Bills on Friday, and cornerback Ronald Darby, 23, practiced for the first time Sunday and took snaps with the first-team defense. Defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz said they worked to get Darby out with the starters immediately despite limited time to get up to speed. The passage also notes questions about Alshon Jeffery’s preseason debut and how long quarterback Carson Wentz and the starters will play, and it mentions live coverage from beat reporters at practice.

The passage describes Texas Instruments device terminal functions and configuration behavior across multiple tables and sections. It specifies analog video output (composite/S-video luminance and chrominance) amplifier output pins, feedback pins, and the use of external resistors in normal versus TVOUT bypass modes, including when pins should be left unconnected. It also covers supply voltage and operating/reset behavior: required supply connections, how boot mode is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset de-assertion, how pin multiplexing is controlled by PINCNTL registers, and guidance on pullup/pulldown usage for unused and boot configuration pins. Additional sections describe system architecture elements (switch fabric and connectivity), power/reset/clock management including PRCM roles, SmartReflex DVFS/AVS concepts, SRAM shutdown behavior, power supply sequencing requirements, and multiple reset types (POR, warm reset, watchdog, software resets, test reset) and their effects on pin states. It further outlines clocking sources and requirements (DEV/AUX oscillators, external LVCMOS clocks, SERDES differential clock AC coupling), timing/test guidance for AC timing measurements, and general descriptions of peripherals such as DCAN, EDMA, tracing/JTAG, and the Ethernet MAC switch subsystem, including related register listings.

The passage describes laterality and footedness as behavioural predictors of cerebral functional laterality, noting that footedness, handedness, earedness, and eyedness are interrelated, with footedness and handedness showing the strongest association. It reviews findings that gait and postural control show left-right asymmetries and that footedness is relevant for rehabilitation, including stroke-related severity effects. It argues footedness should be assessed with multi-item inventories and presents the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised (WFQ-R) as a commonly used tool. The study’s purpose is to translate the WFQ-R into Arabic, adapt it for Saudi culture, and evaluate validity and reliability. A longitudinal cross-cultural adaptation process follows Beaton et al.’s five stages, including translation, synthesis, back-translation, expert review, and pre-testing, followed by testing measurement properties in 290 adult Arabic speakers. Results report that the WFQ-Ar is clear and appropriate based on face and content validity, shows one-factor construct validity, has excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha 0.93), excellent test-retest reliability (ICC 0.94), a standard error of measurement of 4.5 points, and acceptable agreement on Bland-Altman analysis. The authors conclude the WFQ-Ar is a valid and reliable measure for determining footedness for clinical and research use.

The passage says the IRS furloughed nearly half of its workforce due to a government shutdown. It also reports that CoreWeave’s stock rose as the company introduced new tools for developers to build AI agents, including a serverless reinforcement learning service that automatically manages computing power. Tests cited in the passage indicate developers can train models faster with 40% lower costs compared with running Nvidia H100 GPUs locally, with no impact on model quality. The passage adds that CoreWeave’s new product complements its business of renting Nvidia GPUs to OpenAI and other clients, and notes CoreWeave’s acquisition of Weights and Biases for $1 billion five months earlier.

Peace founded on equality must be an equality of rights, with guarantees not reflecting differences between big and small nations, or powerful and weak ones. Rights should be based on the common strength of nations, and no full equality of territory or resources is expected beyond what results from normal development. Peace must also recognize that governments derive just powers from consent of the governed and that peoples cannot be treated as property transferred between sovereignties. An example given is an independent, autonomous Poland whose security and development should be guaranteed. The passage argues that stable peace requires freedom, justice, and a sense of right. It further states that nations should have direct, free access to the sea and that freedom of the seas is necessary for peace, equality, and cooperation, requiring changes to international rules and cooperation to keep seas free and safe. It links these goals to limiting naval armaments and, more broadly, military preparation, emphasizing that peace cannot be achieved without concession and sacrifice.

The passage explains seasonal trading and applies it to silver by investing only in the best-performing months. Seasonality is described as regular price patterns tied to times of the year and can be influenced by business cycles, news, or holidays. It states that silver typically rises rapidly at the beginning of the year, with January and July noted as the best months, and June and September as the worst months. It attributes silver seasonality to industrial silver users placing orders at the beginning of the new year and notes traders can exploit this by going long during favorable months. A backtest from 2001 finds the strategy holds silver 5 of 12 months and outperforms buy and hold by about 3.9% per year, with higher risk-adjusted return and reduced maximum drawdown.

President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo is expected to deliver his State of the Nation Address in Parliament on Thursday, February 8, 2018. Parliament will adjourn early on Wednesday, February 7 to allow the State of the Nation Address planning committee to prepare the chamber. The Majority Leader Osei Kyei Mensah Bonsu urged members to be punctual and asked them not to bring guests into the House on the specified date. Majority chief whip Kwesi Ameyaw-Cheremeh said members should be in the Chamber by 9:15am and noted the House is expected to adjourn early on February 7 for preparation before the February 8 address.

The passage is a compilation of articles and related items about California’s 2001 energy crisis. It covers Gov. Gray Davis requesting additional state funding for power purchases, utilities repaying the state for earlier electricity costs, and debates over rate hikes and disclosure of long-term power contracts. It also describes efforts to speed approval and relax environmental review for new peaking power plants, proposals for conservation incentives and energy-saving legislation, and actions to improve emergency blackout notifications to cities. Additional coverage includes related natural gas price investigations, disputes over greenhouse-gas policy and the Kyoto Protocol involving President Bush, and commentary on attracting or siting generation and distributed power solutions.

The passage describes the device’s reference options, alarm features, and multiSPI-based operation. It explains how to select and use an internal 4.096 V reference or an external 4.096 V reference with the internal buffer, including required decoupling capacitors and guidance to filter reference noise and avoid driving external loads directly from the reference pins. It also discusses internal reference accuracy, potential degradation from mechanical/thermal stress (including reflow effects), and temperature-compensated drift over –40°C to +125°C. Next, it covers alarm functionality on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin, including input and AVDD alarms, threshold/hysteresis behavior, default enabling and selective disabling, and how alarm flags are set, cleared, and read. The later sections outline device functional modes (RESET, ACQ, CONV), data transfer frame behavior, command/register write rules, output data word formation with optional appended flags, and supported data transfer protocols (legacy SPI-compatible modes, dual SDO-x option, and source-synchronous SRC modes).

The passage discusses India’s likely squad for an England tour in January 2017, noting that injuries and resting of key players may lead to a different T20I team than in 2016. It says India will play three ODIs (starting 15 January) and three T20Is (beginning on Republic Day) before the ICC Champions Trophy in June, and that the limited-overs series is their final one before the tournament. It outlines likely selections by role: Rohit Sharma’s fitness may keep KL Rahul in the opening role; Shikhar Dhawan and options including Mandeep Singh and Rishabh Pant are considered; Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni are presented as sure picks; Ajinkya Rahane’s fitness may shift selection toward Manish Pandey; Karun Nair and a possible recall for Suresh Raina are mentioned; and Deepak Hooda is considered for an all-rounder slot. For bowling, it notes likely rest of Ashwin and Jadeja, injuries to Jayant Yadav and Axar Patel, and that Kuldeep Yadav and Shahbaz Nadeem could debut, while Mohammed Shami and Umesh Yadav may be rested and Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar are expected to complete the squad.

The passage describes video encoding/decoding techniques for using a single bitstream for both SDR and HDR systems. It outlines a method where an encoder receives an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and target SDR display properties, finds a color volume transform to convert HDR values into SDR values that closely match the reference SDR values after SDR display operations, generates metadata identifying the transform, and encodes the SDR values into a bitstream. It further explains how an SDR decoder can decode the bitstream to present SDR video, while an HDR decoder can use metadata to reverse the encoding steps via an inverse color volume transform and reconstruct HDR video for display. The passage also includes a process for selecting the color volume transform by trying candidate transforms, emulating target SDR display operations, comparing results to the reference SDR master, and choosing the smallest-difference option, along with discussion of metadata types (e.g., tone mapping parameters, scaling factors, and LUTs) and possible alternate embodiments where HDR values are encoded and metadata guides SDR conversion.

The passage describes a city contract between the city and LIHI for the first four months of operating Camp Second Chance at 9701 Myers Way S. in southeast West Seattle. It states the contract was obtained from the city Human Services Department, is worth $75,000 to cover LIHI costs through the end of last year, and that a new contract for this year is not finalized yet but expected to be finalized this month. It also summarizes terms of the 2017 contract signed on November 21, including LIHI operating and providing case-management services, expectations about the duration of stay, that the camp is self-managed but campers cannot veto LIHI decisions, security requirements with at least one person on duty at the gate, and a rule that no one under 18 may stay. The passage further mentions an issue raised at Community Advisory Committee meetings about renewing the camp for a second year at the Myers Way parcels site, and ends with an incomplete quote from HSD spokesperson Meg Olberding.

A judge temporarily halted the Trump administration’s federal worker layoffs tied to the government shutdown, responding to a lawsuit claiming the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to cut staff. The case was filed by AFSCME and AFGE in Northern California, and Judge Susan Illston issued a temporary restraining order after a Wednesday hearing, blocking layoff notices. AFSCME and AFGE officials said the decision likely makes the threatened firings illegal and stops terminations. An Office of Management and Budget filing reviewed by Business Insider indicated between 4,132 and 4,232 federal workers were marked for layoffs, affecting multiple departments. Administration sources said additional reductions-in-force are expected, and OMB head Russell Vought said layoffs would total about 10,000.

Ella Ravenscroft, a 20-year-old model from Salford, warned about the dangers of sunbeds after undergoing surgery to remove moles that had changed shape and colour. She had used sunbeds once or twice a week for two years and first noticed the moles had grown when her mother pointed it out. She had two moles cut out, then returned to hospital for two more weeks later, leaving scars. Ella shared her experience to urge others to check moles for itching, growth, or changes, and said she will use fake tan instead. The passage also states that using a sunbed can increase melanoma risk by 16 to 20 per cent and notes that almost 500 people in Greater Manchester are diagnosed with melanoma each year, with around a fifth dying. It provides general guidance that most moles are benign but changes in colour, shape, texture, or symptoms like bleeding, oozing, crusting, or inflammation can be early warning signs, and advises people to show unusual skin changes to a doctor.

Sprint announced that, as part of its 1Million Project, it will connect 180,000 low-income high school students during the 2026 school year. The 5-year program aims to connect 1 million high schoolers who lack internet access at home. Sprint will provide selected students with a free smartphone, tablet, or hotspot device and 3GB of high-speed LTE data per month for up to four years, starting Aug. 15. The program will operate in more than 1,300 schools across 32 states, including districts such as New York City, Miami-Dade, Los Angeles Unified, Chicago Public Schools, and others. Sprint says teachers assign homework requiring online connectivity and that more than 5 million families lack internet at home. The company previously piloted the program in January with 3,750 students, reporting 86% said it improved their attitude toward learning and helped them do their homework. Sprint plans to donate about $2.16 billion in wireless service, tech support, and staffing over five years.

Hexane is a hydrocarbon solvent found in the volatile fractions of plants such as guava and orange, where it exists as n-hexane. It is made from crude oil and is a blend of hydrocarbons with six carbon atoms. Hexanes are used in gasoline and are available as pure hexane (used in laboratories) and solvent-based hexane. Solvent-based hexane is used to extract vegetable oils from crops including soybeans, cottonseed, rape seed, mustard seed, and safflower seed, and solvent-chemical hexane is also used as a cleaning agent and in consumer products such as glues, gasoline, rubber, and cement. Hexane can pose health hazards if inhaled, and OSHA has set a permissible exposure limit of 500 ppm. It is also used to remove unwanted taste and odor in edible oil production. The passage states that Asia Pacific, especially China, dominates the global hexane market, and companies in Europe and North America are shifting production to Asia Pacific due to skilled labor availability.

Gulf stock markets mostly fell on Wednesday in modest volumes, led by Qatar, where QNB and other blue-chips dropped due to profit-taking after a mid-May MSCI weighting increase. Qatar’s index fell 2.3% with QIB down 4.7% in heavy trade, and QNB down 2.1%. Dubai’s index slipped 0.5%, including DAMAC down 2.5%, and fell back below the level after the UAE’s long-term visa and foreign ownership ceiling announcements, though details remain unclear. DXB Entertainments rose 4.1%. Abu Dhabi’s index ended 0.4% lower, while Saudi’s index edged up 0.1% as Al Tayyar rose after repaying a 307 million riyal loan early. Outside the Gulf, Egypt’s index dropped 1.4%, with Talat Mostafa and EFG Hermes also falling.

Josie Goodenow will speak to the Laguna Beach Garden Club on Oct. 13 about “All About Bees.” The meeting includes a social get-together at 9:30 a.m. and a general meeting at 10 a.m.; the public is welcome and first-time guests are free. Her program will address differences between native bees (including the Blue Orchard Mason Bee) and the European honeybee, and ways to increase bee populations and improve yard health. Goodenow has served as bee chairman for the California Garden Clubs Inc. since 2014 and has given bee programs statewide. The club meets the second Friday from September through May at Laguna Presbyterian Church, and attendees can also browse the “Garden Boutique” and buy donated garden items. Parking is free in the Laguna Canyon Rd lot (spaces 300–422) or $3 all day in spaces 185–228.

Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were arraigned in Dunmore, Pennsylvania, and charged with endangering the welfare of their two children after investigators said they knowingly left the children home alone for three days. Police responded March 7 to a report of children left alone, found a 10-year-old and an 11-year-old unsupervised, and said the home was in deplorable condition with food, boxes, pills, and trash on the floor and a thermostat reading 58 degrees. Court papers say Sciortino initially said she was nearby but later admitted she was in Florida and said the children’s father was watching them; she also said she did not realize leaving them unsupervised for an extended period was against the law. Police said Licciardello dropped the children off early March 5 at Sciortino’s mother’s home and occasionally stopped by to drop off food while she was in Florida. Investigators said one child missed 16 days of school and the other missed 26 days. Both were charged and given $10,000 unsecured bail and walked free; the children were staying with family friends.

The passage describes a study evaluating cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis for leptomeningeal disease (LMD) in patients with advanced lung cancer. The authors used CAPP-Seq with a lung cancer–specific sequencing panel on 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients undergoing lumbar puncture for suspected LMD. CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA levels, and CSF and plasma tumor DNA levels were positively correlated. For diagnosing definitive LMD, cytology sensitivity was 81.8% and CSF-tDNA sensitivity was 91.7%, with CSF-tDNA also associated with worse overall survival. The study also found that resistance mutations detected in plasma were often rare in time-matched CSF, suggesting compartment-specific resistance mechanisms. In a prospective subset of 12 patients treated with osimertinib for refractory LMD, increased CSF-tDNA after three weeks was associated with CNS progression, and post-osimertinib CSF-tDNA strongly predicted CNS progression. The authors conclude that CSF-tDNA detection is feasible and may improve LMD diagnosis sensitivity, prognostication, and therapeutic decision-making.

The passage says Jon Klemm is an underrated defenseman and highlights Greg De Vries’ strong performance, including playing many games, doing well this year, and establishing himself as a solid NHL defenseman known for physical play, skating, and puck movement. It also describes Skoula as an up-and-coming defenseman with good skating, poise, a strong shot, speed, strength, and size. It further states that Skoula has had a successful season in goals, assists, and points and has been one of the best forwards in the league in recent years.

Hundreds of people were admitted to hospitals in the South West with eating disorders in 2016-17, including two children under 10, 13 children aged 10-12, 91 young people aged 13-15, and 117 people aged 16-18, as provided by NHS Digital to Devon Live. Across all ages, 21 people aged 61-80 and people over 81 were also hospitalised. Anorexia was the most common type (45%), followed by bulimia (24%), with other forms making up the rest. Women and girls accounted for 94% of cases. The number of hospital admissions has risen to the highest recorded level, with more than twice as many admissions as in 2010-11, but experts said admissions may reflect factors like awareness, bed availability, or service provision rather than the true number of people suffering.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 8-K filed June 16, 2021 reports that on June 14, 2021 it entered into an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to issue and sell $5.0 billion of unsecured notes. The notes consist of $1.25 billion each of 0.309% notes due 2023, 0.584% notes due 2024, 1.550% notes due 2028, and 2.000% notes due 2031. Net proceeds were approximately $4.98 billion, intended for general corporate purposes, including possible repayment of indebtedness. The notes are governed by an indenture dated September 16, 2016, as supplemented by an Officers’ Certificate dated June 16, 2021, and include maturity and interest payment dates, redemption provisions, covenants limiting certain actions, and customary events of default, including a change-of-control-related offer to repurchase at 101% of principal plus accrued interest. The report incorporates Item 1.01 into Item 2.03 and lists related exhibits.

Poor medication adherence is reported among hemodialysis patients, who often take 10 to 20 tablets daily. Studies report non-adherence rates above 50%, with some estimates up to 98.6%, and non-adherence is linked to inadequate management of CKD complications and higher mortality. A multidimensional strategy to improve adherence includes simplifying regimens, improving health literacy, and strengthening physician-patient communication through person-centered care (PCC), although empirical evidence for PCC is limited. PCC is proposed to improve adherence by addressing individual preferences, goals, and values, with qualitative findings suggesting elements such as care continuity, needs-driven practice, and coordination may help, though prior evidence is largely hypothesis-generating. Limited research has examined how PCC affects doctor-patient interactions and, in turn, medication adherence; trust in physicians may mediate this relationship. This multicenter cross-sectional study in Japanese hemodialysis patients aimed to explore relationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and to test whether trust mediates the relationship between PCC and adherence using mediation analysis. The study enrolled adults attending six outpatient hemodialysis facilities, collected data from April 2022 to February 2023, and measured medication adherence using the Japanese ASK-12 scale.

The passage describes preparations by Supreme Court justices for the 2025-26 term and notes that Victor Tony Jones, scheduled for execution Tuesday at 6 p.m. EDT, has asked the court to block his execution. It says the Supreme Court has not granted any requests to postpone executions so far this year; if that continues, Jones would be the 34th person executed in 2025, likely increasing debate about the rise in executions and the Court’s role. It summarizes that executions had generally declined in the U.S. over the prior decade, including a Biden administration moratorium on federal executions and related extensions by Attorney General Merrick Garland. It then says that after President Donald Trump returned to office, he ended the federal moratorium through an executive order and that 2025 has seen the highest number of executions in about a decade, with Florida playing a major role. The passage also explains that the Court’s death-penalty emergency docket typically involves brief stay applications, which the justices have rarely granted, and contrasts this with prior decisions during the 2024-25 term that favored death-row inmates. It further notes that the Court will consider issues related to intellectual disability and execution eligibility in a future case.

Archive360 announced it was named a finalist in two categories of the 2017 DBTA Readers' Choice Awards. Archive2Azure™, its managed compliance storage solution for Microsoft Azure, was named a finalist for “Best Cloud Storage Solution,” and FastCollect for PSTs™ was named a finalist for “Best Data Storage Solution.” The passage describes Archive2Azure as enabling migration and management of data within Microsoft Azure with regulatory compliance and eDiscovery readiness, and FastCollect for PSTs as a fully automated solution for PST discovery and migration with compliant location, rehydration, deletion, storage, and auditing. It also states that Archive360 has migrated tens of petabytes into the Microsoft Cloud since 2012 and is a Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider.

In March 2016, Elon Musk unveiled the Tesla Model 3 to an audience of Tesla owners and said earlier Tesla EVs would enable an affordable “for the masses” car. The baseline Model 3 was priced at $35,000, offered 220 miles of range (310 with a long-range option), and was set for deliveries at the end of 2017, with pre-orders reported at 115,000 (rising to 500,000 by 2018). By August 2018, production delays and highly automated factory bottlenecks led Musk to describe Tesla as being in “production hell,” including pauses in production and concerns about cash needs after the company posted a $743 million net loss on $4 billion revenue in Q2 2018. The case then outlines the wider U.S. auto industry—market size, major automakers and their returns, entry barriers, supplier structure, customer behavior and dealership dynamics—and discusses industry changes such as electrification, autonomous driving, and connected services, along with related trends in mobility-as-a-service. It also details Tesla’s background, Master Plans, past vehicle programs, Model 3’s manufacturing approach and production challenges, and how Tesla sells cars, builds charging infrastructure, and provides service, concluding with the question of whether Tesla can thrive in the industry.

The passage is a collection of news items mentioning Enron and related topics, including an Enron-related Fortune Global 500 reference (Enron No. 16), a BusinessWeek analysis of declining corporate profits with emphasis on Enron’s revenue gains, and multiple energy-market stories. The passage is a coach’s discussion of upcoming playoff games, emphasizing that both teams are skilled, hard-working, and closely matched. The passage describes DLSS transitioning from CNN-based neural networks to transformer-based AI models in DLSS 4, aiming to improve image quality and rendering smoothness. It explains how CNNs and transformer models differ, noting transformers use self-attention to identify longer-range patterns, scale effectively, and improve temporal stability, lighting detail, and detail in motion. It also details transformer-based improvements to DLSS Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, emphasizing better temporal stability, reduced ghosting, improved anti-aliasing, and fewer denoiser artifacts. The passage then outlines NVIDIA’s “neural shaders” direction with the Blackwell architecture, reviews shader evolution milestones, and describes neural shader-related features such as RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Finally, it provides hardware specification details for Blackwell GPU variants (GB202, GB203, and GB205) and mentions RTX 50 series products (e.g., GeForce RTX 5090, RTX 5080, and RTX 5070 Ti), followed by standard NVIDIA legal and trademark notices.

The passage describes an electric fat tire bike design shown in seven figures: front and right perspective view (FIG. 1), front elevation (FIG. 2), rear elevation (FIG. 3), right side elevation (FIG. 4), left side elevation (FIG. 5), top plan view (FIG. 6), and bottom plan view (FIG. 7). The Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s dismissal with prejudice of Lewis Williamson’s appeal challenging the Town of Surf City’s closing of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 160A-299. The court held that the town obtained a vested interest in part of the street as a result of the closing and that § 160A-299 does not limit the town’s authority to close a street based on the town’s intent, as long as the town complies with the statute’s procedural requirements. The opinion also stated that the statute permits closing all or part of a street upon compliance with required procedure.

The passage identifies Sid Sivakumar as a puzzle constructor and M.D./Ph.D. student in biomedical engineering who edited the puzzle. MKM Partners raised its price target for Tutor Perini Corporation (NYSE:TPC) from $31.00 to $34.00 and has a buy rating on the stock. Other analysts issued mixed ratings and targets, and the stock’s consensus rating is Buy with a consensus price target of $27.29. TPC opened at $28.00 on Wednesday. The passage also notes an insider sale by COO James A. Frost and describes the company’s business and segments.

The passage describes a rotating shaft mechanism and a foldable mobile terminal for flexible foldable display devices. The mechanism is fixedly connected to two housings and folds when the housings rotate around a main shaft assembly using swing arm assemblies, support assemblies, and connecting rod groups. The swing arm assembly includes connecting rod groups (with two rotatable connecting rods on opposite sides of the main shaft assembly) and swing arm groups (with swing arms rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly and fixedly connected to the housings). Support plates located on opposite sides rotate to enclose folding space for the flexible display; their surfaces support the display when unfolded and form concave space when folded. The design aims to improve folded thickness alignment with the stacked housings and enhance the bending/support effect of the flexible display. Synchronization between opposite housings during folding is provided by gears on the connecting rods, and a limiting mechanism using cams (with protrusions/notches and an elastic part such as a compression spring) limits relative rotation positions for unfolded/folded states and provides damping. The mechanism may include a flexible blocking layer of elastic material to block exposed notches and improve appearance. A mobile terminal embodiment includes a flexible display fixed to the housings and/or support plates using adhesive, with optional non-adhesive regions shaped as droplet or semi-arc forms when folded, and optional use of the flexible blocking layer to shield the notches.

The passage is a collection of Investing.com headlines and market commentary, including claims about NVIDIA stock, AI stock picks, bitcoin staying below record highs, and several investment products/funds. The passage introduces the need for COVID-19 forecasting models for both confirmed and death cases in five heavily affected countries (USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and UK). It describes the pandemic’s global impact and reports worldwide figures of confirmed infections and deaths, with WHO declaring COVID-19 a global pandemic. Because COVID-19 data are described as dynamic and exhibiting both linear and nonlinear patterns, the passage argues that single models (e.g., ARIMA, ANN/ARNN, SVM) are insufficient. It motivates hybrid modeling approaches to produce short-term and long-term (STM and LTM) out-of-sample forecasts and proposes hybrid ARNNS and SVMAR models, claiming experimental results show strong performance for both confirmed and death cases. The paper’s structure is outlined, including data analysis (Section 2), model formulation (Section 3), experimental evaluations (Section 4), and further discussion and conclusions (Sections 5–6). It states that daily confirmed and death datasets are collected from the Global Change Data Lab for a shared terminal date of January 15, 2021.

The passage describes the U.S. position on not using armed forces to collect ordinary contract debts, arguing such force would injure relations among nations and risk oppression and unjustifiable warfare. It notes that at the Rio conference a resolution recommended asking the Second Peace Conference at The Hague to examine compulsory collection of public debts and ways to reduce conflicts of financial origin. The U.S. supported the resolution, saying an international examination should distinguish cases involving fraud or treaty violations from simple nonpayment, and that Rio should instead request Hague consideration because it could appear politically lopsided. Royalty North Partners Ltd. announced on October 6, 2017 that it granted 35,000 incentive stock options under its Stock Option Plan to certain directors, officers, employees, and consultants. A court in Kuwait sentenced a couple to death for torturing their three-year-old daughter until she died, and for keeping her body in a freezer for a week. The father and mother, both Kuwaiti, were arrested in May and accused of beating and torturing the child; interior ministry said burn marks were found and they were drug addicts. The verdict is not final and must be reviewed by appeals and supreme courts. Executions in Kuwait are carried out by hanging.

The passage describes “The Clean 20,” a clean-eating guide by Dr. Ian K. Smith. It explains the benefits of clean eating and how to reduce unhealthy processed foods, linking these to weight loss, disease prevention, and overall health. The book centers on twenty clean foods (including avocado, whole wheat pasta, and others) that are easy to find and prepare, and includes a clean eating program with a daily meal plan, 60 recipes and substitutions, and 20-minute workouts.
