It emphasizes choosing foods wisely within each food group rather than eliminating groups, and states that incorporating all relevant categories (vegetables, grains, fruit, fats, meats, and fish) helps weight loss “stick.”

Lincolnshire railway history is linked to the rivalry between Lincoln City FC and Grimsby Town FC. The Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway opened the Lincoln-to-Grimsby line in 1848 to transport goods, especially fish, to and from Grimsby’s port. A railway bridge over the River Witham at Stamp End was designed by chief engineer John Fowler, using box-shaped iron girders as described at the time, and the line opened in December 1848. Network Rail’s report says the River Witham Bridge may be the oldest surviving wrought iron box girder bridge in Britain and possibly the world, and describes it as the oldest such bridge in Britain still carrying trains. After the initial double-track bridge construction, reinforcement and repairs were carried out in 1903 and 1948 due to heavier trains, including replacing timber spans with metal decks and reinforcing girder elements, and in 1968 a new steel deck was added to the central span.

The passage describes a multicenter cross-sectional seroprevalence study conducted in emergency departments in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany (August–September 2022) to assess SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity and factors predicting antibody levels and neutralization. Population immunity and immune evasion are highlighted as major issues, with Omicron variants driving worldwide infection surges; BA.5 was predominant globally in June 2022, and BQ.1 and BQ.1.1 later increased in prevalence. In 1,411 treated patients, SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG (S-IgG) was detected in 95.6% and Nucleocapsid IgG (NC-IgG) in 24.0%. S-IgG levels correlated with neutralizing activity against Wu01 and BA.4/5, which was present in 94.4% and 84.9% of participants, respectively, with lower neutralization against BA.4/5 than Wu01. Neutralization was impaired against BQ.1.1: 73.8% showed detectable activity, and geometric mean ID50 was reduced compared with Wu01 and BA.4/5. Multivariable regression and Bayesian network analyses identified S-IgG detection and the number of prior S-antigen contacts (vaccinations and/or infections) as major predictors of antibody responses and neutralization, including for BQ.1.1. The authors conclude that while S-IgG detection can assess immunity, immune-evasive variants reduce the accuracy of predicting neutralization, especially at low S-IgG titers. The methods and assay details for measuring IgG and pseudovirus neutralization are also provided.

Scientists used Japanese kirigami (paper cutting) to make parachutes that open automatically when dropped. Perforated Mylar disks with concentric slits expand into a latticework shape, and the resulting drag slows the payload’s fall while the parachutes fall straight down regardless of their initial orientation. In lab tests, the kirigami parachutes fell closer to an intended target than traditional parachutes or uncut disks. The researchers also demonstrated a drop test using a 1 kilogram water bottle from a drone, where the parachute reduced the fall speed compared with no parachute. The parachutes are suggested for humanitarian aid drops and drone package deliveries, and the team is considering biodegradable materials and design changes, including cutting the disks for programmable reconfiguration that could aid space missions.

The passage explains what intraday trading is and describes common intraday strategies, including scalping and day trading. It discusses aims and risks, noting that intraday trading is often considered speculation and that many traders lose money. It outlines US pattern day trading rules set by FINRA, including the $25,000 minimum equity requirement and limits on buying power/leverage, and it advises developing a personal intraday trading plan that is backtested and proven to have a statistical edge. The passage lists intraday trading rules such as learning the market, setting realistic goals, avoiding herd mentality, choosing a regulated broker, trading only liquid stocks, studying company fundamentals, using quantified/automated systems, and periodically reviewing results. It provides guidance on profitability and backtesting difficulty, includes an example backtest using hourly data on WTI crude oil futures, and concludes with FAQ-style recommendations on best time to trade (first two hours after market opens), capital considerations, strategy types, markets to focus on (high liquidity/volatility markets like forex, stocks, futures, options), and commonly referenced indicators (moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, RSI), while warning that expecting these indicators to work for intraday strategies may be naive.

The State appealed the trial court’s dismissal of charges against Ryan Jeffery Adams for controlled substances violations on double jeopardy grounds. After Adams was arrested and cocaine and marijuana were seized, the North Carolina Department of Revenue docketed a certificate of tax liability totaling $456,574.26 and Adams paid part of the amount before trial. Adams moved to dismiss based on double jeopardy, and the trial court granted the motion. The Court of Appeals reversed, finding the trial court’s ruling conflicted with North Carolina appellate decisions upholding the Drug Tax. The court held that, except for United States Supreme Court decisions, lower federal court decisions are not binding on North Carolina courts, and that reexamining state holdings in light of a Fourth Circuit decision or modifying the statute is not within its province.

The Ohio Supreme Court reversed the judgment of the court of appeals in State v. Montecalvo, citing State v. Szefcyk, decided the same day. Judges Moyer, Douglas, Resnick, F.E. Sweeney, Pfeifer, and Stratton concur, and Cook, J., did not participate.

Netflix is down 0.68% in premarket trading Monday despite adding content partners. Shonda Rhimes, behind “Grey’s Anatomy,” “How to Get Away With Murder,” and “Scandal,” has agreed to move future shows to Netflix; existing ABC US shows will continue, and Rhimes will continue working on them. The move is described as part of a plan developed with Netflix Chief Content Officer Ted Sarandos. The article notes other recent Netflix content-related news, including Disney pulling movies from Netflix and Netflix’s acquisition of Millarworld. The selling is not expected to be linked to the Rhimes deal, but may relate to a Barron’s story calling for shares to fall amid content producers leaving Netflix and rising Netflix debt. Netflix is up 32.95% for the year.

The passage discusses documenting containers using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE (including port explanations), ENV (default values and usage), and LABEL (metadata using Label Schema project names). It then summarizes container patterns: the sidecar pattern, the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions with the outside world, and uses of the ambassador pattern for sharded services via a localhost “sharding ambassador proxy.” It provides hands-on examples for sharded Redis (using Kubernetes StatefulSets, Services, and twemproxy) and request splitting experiments with nginx. Next, it introduces the adapter pattern, which modifies an application container’s interface to match a common expected interface, with examples including monitoring via Prometheus exporters and logging normalization via fluentd. It also describes health monitoring adapters and then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node systems, introducing microservices and replicated load-balanced services (including readiness probes) plus session tracking and caching layers with SSL termination. The passage further covers sharding concepts and design, including sharded caches, hit-rate impacts, shard replication, sharding functions and shard keys, consistent hashing, and hot sharding. Finally, it introduces the scatter/gather pattern for parallel request processing (including straggler/99th-percentile considerations), scaling it for reliability via replicated shards, and concludes with an overview of event-driven/function-as-a-service (FaaS), noting benefits (simplified deployment, auto scaling) and challenges (strong decoupling, network-only communication, external state storage).

The Buck Sweep, credited to Tubby Raymond and the University of Delaware, is the Wing-T signature play and a versatile misdirection off-tackle run that uses two pullers as lead blockers. Although it involves “sweep” misdirection, it is not limited to perimeter runs; it aims to exploit defensive indecision and can hit off-tackle or the edge depending on reactions. When run in the traditional Wing-T as part of the Buck Series, it is difficult for defenses to identify the ball early due to layered actions involving the fullback, tailback, and quarterback, and it can create creases if defensive fit is incorrect. Blocking uses angles that horizontally displace defenders, and it does not require a “mauler” guard, though success depends on timing, spacing, and guards (sometimes a tackle) pulling and blocking in space. The play is described as intricate and requires practice for layered hand-offs, pull paths, and tailback reads. The passage also lists blocking rules versus 3-4 odd and 4-3 even defensive fronts, and describes two variations: Shotgun Wing-T (with simplified QB action and possible QB keeper read) and I-Wing (with a tailback counter step before the hand-off).

The passage discusses user concerns that Google could discontinue apps and services, raising questions about the future of Inbox, an alternative Gmail interface. It notes signs that Gmail may be redesigned to include features like Inbox’s native email snoozing, Inbox-specific updates have slowed, and the iOS Inbox app had not been updated for the iPhone X notch. However, a Google spokesperson says there are no changes to Inbox by Gmail. The passage also cites new AI-powered Inbox features, such as Highlights and suggestions for unsubscribing or follow-up emails, and argues Inbox’s interface and features still differ from Gmail, including automatically organized bundles and reminder integration. It recounts earlier statements from Inbox leadership about launching Inbox as a separate product and possibly having users switch in the long run, and it references indicators suggesting Inbox has a non-trivial and growing user base.

A freelance writer, Oobah Butler, created a fake TripAdvisor listing called “The Shed at Dulwich,” using his home—a shed in South London—as a prank after writing fake reviews in the past. The listing was approved, gained mostly five-star reviews, and generated increasing reservation inquiries, calls, and external attention as its TripAdvisor popularity ranking climbed from last place to No. 1 in London. After Butler exposed the ruse in a Vice piece, TripAdvisor declined to comment on specifics and said it had already applied a penalty before the article. The story is presented as an example of how online platforms can be gamed, and it is compared to other misinformation-driven incidents; TripAdvisor later said its review checks are focused on catching fake reviews for real businesses. Butler later described opening the “restaurant” for one night with actors and food provided with instant items.

The shiitake mushroom market is projected to reach USD 26.7 billion by 2022 and grow at a CAGR of 15.31% during the forecast period, with global growth projected to reach USD 35.4 billion by 2023 at the same growth rate. Asia Pacific holds 82.54% market share in 2017, with China accounting for 97% of the region’s market. The report attributes growth to increased use of shiitake for nutritional and medicinal benefits. Key players include Bonduelle SA, Mitoku Company, Agro Dutch Industries, The Mushroom Company, Modern Mushroom Farms, Hirano Mushroom LLC, and Banken Champignons. Findings include highest growth for dried shiitake (CAGR 14% for 2017–2023) and fresh shiitake growth in Asia Pacific (CAGR 15.59%), with pharmaceutical application projected to grow fastest, followed by cosmetics. The report covers country-level analysis across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific and targets manufacturers, food and pharmaceutical industry participants, personal care manufacturers, and retailers and traders.

Voluntary movement depends on interactions among the motor cortex, spinal cord, and skeletal muscles, and these relationships are altered after stroke, impairing neural pathways and reducing upper-extremity muscle coordination and strength. Stroke survivors commonly struggle with activities of daily living such as manipulating doors, utensils, and clothing, and the variety of functional motor deficits creates challenges for assessing treatment efficacy and motivates the need for more sensitive motor measures. Surface EMG offers a non-invasive way to measure post-stroke changes in muscle activation; co-contraction, muscle synergies, and excessive antagonist co-contraction are described as measurable and linked to motor impairment and spasticity. 

The passage describes a study using an easy-to-use high-density EMG wearable sleeve spanning the forearm to characterize movement coordination in able-bodied and chronic stroke groups across functional hand and wrist movements. Seven individuals with stroke and hemiparesis and seven able-bodied individuals were included, with EMG recorded using a NeuroLife EMG sleeve during 12 specified movements for all participants; able-bodied participants additionally performed 25 other movements and fine grasps. Clinical assessments for stroke participants included UEFM (gross arm movements and hand coordination), Box and Blocks, and the Modified Ashworth Scale, with possible grouping by hand coordination score. The experimental setup used visual cues for movements at 25–50% maximal effort, and EMG was recorded at 3000 Hz with filtering and artifact correction using a blind source separation approach. The passage further outlines processing steps including RMS binning and mapping sleeve channels across sizes and arms, mapping HD-EMG channels to muscle groups, and decomposing EMG features through co-contraction index and muscle coupling metrics and muscle synergy analysis.

Port Gregory residents were without power for four days, leaving elderly people unable to use medical equipment and causing frozen food to spoil. Betty Sawers, 78, said power failed at 5.45pm last Thursday and was restored briefly several times, with outages lasting from Thursday to Saturday, again from 9.15pm Saturday to 3pm Sunday, and again from 11.45pm Sunday to 9.30am Monday, before going off again at 11.30am Monday. She reported losing about $500 in food and her neighbour being unable to use a CPAP machine, and said outages were expected when it rained. A Western Power spokesman said storm fronts stretched resources, crews checked for visible damage but could not inspect in detail during the storm because they had to make other hazards safe. He said customers without power for 12 or more consecutive hours were eligible for an Extended Outages Payment capped at $80, and that claims could be made if Western Power was responsible for negligence. He also said the network is susceptible to salt and dust, with maintenance including washing and insulator siliconing, and that Port Gregory’s location limits backfeeding during outages.

The passage argues that coalition divergences and nationalist absolutism lead to uncoordinated strategy, reducing attention to an enduring peace program. It describes how nationalist emphasis caused conflicts among Allies, misunderstandings between Russia and the West, and political isolation leading to military disasters for Italy and Romania. It says unity of strategy requires simplifying and pooling purposes, shifting political power toward middle parties and placating the moderate left, with this movement affecting both coalitions. For the Allies’ success, it emphasizes exhausting Germany’s reserves on the Western Front through morale and resource economy, maintaining political power via popular consent, and countering deceptive German liberalism. It anticipates Germany will seek a winter peace discussion to weaken Allied morale, while the Allies plan to resist in winter and pursue operations in summer, leading to a military decision involving destroying submarine bases, recapturing northern France, and preparing a potential invasion of German territory, with the deeper factor being relative manpower reserves.

Sonali Bendre said in an official statement that she has been diagnosed with high-grade cancer that has metastised. She said a niggling pain led to tests and an unexpected diagnosis, and that she is undergoing treatment in New York as advised by her doctors. She expressed optimism and determination to fight, and thanked her family and friends for their support, adding that she is grateful for the outpouring of love she has received.

The S&P 500 fell on Friday, ending a six-day streak of record highs after a monthly decline in U.S. nonfarm jobs and concerns that Amazon may sell prescription drugs. The Nasdaq rose for a ninth straight day, reaching a sixth consecutive record high close. Walgreens and CVS shares each fell about 4.9%, while Amazon shares rose 0.9%. The jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls down 33,000 in September, with average wages rising more than expected. The Dow slipped slightly, and the S&P 500 lost 0.11% while the Nasdaq gained 0.07%. The week’s gains were 1.2% for the S&P 500, 1.6% for the Dow, and 1.5% for the Nasdaq, as volatility rebounded and other factors included North Korea missile test preparations and lower oil prices.

Apple says tax reform gives it greater access to foreign reserves previously held to avoid repatriation taxes, allowing a more optimal capital structure. On an earnings call, CFO Luca Maestri set a goal to bring Apple’s net cash position to approximately zero over time; Apple’s current net cash position is $163 billion. CEO Tim Cook clarified this would mean an equal amount of cash and debt balancing to zero. The passage notes Apple could reach this by reducing gross cash, increasing debt, or both, potentially through actions such as higher capital returns (special one-time dividend or increased share repurchases) and that existing callable debt could be handled by extinguishing, rolling over, or paying off naturally as it matures. Apple plans to update its specific capital allocation plans when it reports second fiscal quarter results.

The passage describes cryogenic imaging of polar behavior in bulk SrTiO3 using 4D-STEM. SrTiO3 undergoes an antiferrodistortive transition below ~105 K that produces a non-polar tetragonal phase, followed by increased dielectric response indicating proximity to a polar ferroelectric transition; however, pure SrTiO3 remains a quantum paraelectric where long-range polar order does not set in. The study uses polarization-sensitive asymmetries in Kikuchi bands (Friedel pairs at ±k) to extract local polarization from the center-of-mass shift of diffraction patterns, mapped as Δk(r). Dynamical scattering simulations confirm that intensity differences between Friedel pairs appear only when polarization is present and that the asymmetry direction follows the polarization direction. At 69 K (well below the AFD transition), SrTiO3 shows nanoscale domains with opposite polarization directions and a characteristic polar nanodomain size of ~20 ± 0.6 nm from an exponential decay of an autocorrelation function. At ~25 nm, an additional correlation peak indicates periodic spatial correlations between nanodomains below the typical domain size. Below ~40 K, SrTiO3 enters the quantum paraelectric regime where polar nanodomains become smaller (~14 ± 0.4 nm), more fragmented, and periodic ordering is substantially reduced, described as a re-entrant disordering. The passage also outlines cryogenic STEM methods and simulation/analysis procedures, including extracting polarization direction and amplitude from Δk measurements and quantifying domain size and periodicity via autocorrelation functions and superlattice peaks.

The dollar rose to more than two-month highs versus the yen and seven-week highs versus the euro on Friday after the September U.S. jobs report showed rising wages. Average hourly earnings increased 0.5 percent in September after 0.2 percent in August, while nonfarm payrolls fell 33,000 jobs due to disruptions from Hurricanes Harvey and Irma. Win Thin said the surprise was wage growth and that it is a missing piece for the Fed, predicting the dollar rally would continue. The dollar reached 113.41 yen, the highest since July 14, and the euro fell to $1.167, the lowest since Aug. 17. Improving U.S. data, prospects for U.S. tax cuts, and expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December supported the currency, with CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showing a 93 percent likelihood of a December rate hike.

Fior Markets published a “Cooking Oil Market 2017 Global Analysis and Forecast to 2022” report. It covers industry trends, statistics, segmentation, growth, market share, revenue, leading players, regions, types, and applications, based on primary and secondary research. The report provides market forecasts and analysis, including market size and share estimates, industry drivers, restraints, challenges, opportunities, investment potential, leading technologies, a future roadmap, player profiles, regulatory ecosystem, strategies, and charts. It is divided into product, application, and regional segment analysis and includes research on regions such as the USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and South East Asia. It also includes definitions, supply chain analysis, company profiles, globalization and trade aspects, supply channels, marketing strategy and barriers to entry, and import, export, and consumption metrics by major countries for 2017 to 2022.

Protests by employees under the All Employees’ Movement for Restoration of PIMS continued for a fifth day in Islamabad, with protestors forcibly sealing the VC’s office at SZABMU and demanding separation of PIMS from the medical university. Prof. Dr. Javed Akram offered to resign and said patient services should not be halted, citing up to 20,000 patients treated daily at PIMS. The ministries of Capital Administration and Development Division and Law assured that the PIMS amendment bill summary has been finalized for Prime Minister approval, after rectifying legal observations and delays. The Prime Minister has agreed in principle to the separation, with completion expected soon. Protestors decided late in the evening to continue the strike until their demand is met, and political figures including JI leader Mian Muhammad Aslam and CDA representative Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin joined them in support.

After three early high-scoring wins, Dinbych were defeated by well-drilled Wrexham, 12-10 at halftime and finished as a tight Division Two (North) contest where Dinbych had territory and possession but were frustrated by Wrexham’s defense. Wrexham led after a ninth-minute try by James Price, and later went ahead again, scoring an unconverted try from a driving maul by James Weston. Dinbych reduced the deficit with a Dan O’Sullivan penalty and took their first lead eight minutes into the second half with an unconverted try by Aidyn Jones. Dinbych then scored under the posts through Owain Davies with a conversion by O’Sullivan, but Wrexham counter-attacked near the end for a converted try by Jack Ratcliff. Dinbych held on to secure the win; Wrexham only earned a losing bonus point. In Division Three (North), Dinbych 2nds gained a losing bonus point from a 16-10 loss at Flint.

The passage discusses a hockey team’s experience with loud arenas and media, noting that they are used to starting series on the road and want to focus on the game rather than media. It describes the Western Conference’s competitiveness and the importance of every shift. The team reflects on a disappointing previous game where they were too passive and didn’t make it difficult for the opponent’s defense, leading to an “easy game” for them. They plan to play harder and better next game, improve their effort, skate/work more, stick with their plan, and respond to adversity by remaining patient and level headed.

Singapore Airlines will restart non-stop flights between Singapore and Newark in fall, with service beginning Oct. 12. The airline previously flew the route until 2013 and said it planned to resume after taking delivery of new long-range aircraft. Tickets are expected to go on sale by Thursday. Singapore’s Newark route will be about 9,000 nautical miles and is expected to become the world’s longest flight by distance, replacing Qatar Airways’ Doha-Auckland route. Singapore says the non-stop flight will reduce travel time by four hours or more versus connecting options, with scheduled flight times of 18 hours 45 minutes outbound and 18 hours 25 minutes back. The flights will use the Airbus A350-900ULR, configured with 161 seats (67 business and 94 premium economy) and no standard coach seats, initially flying three times a week from Newark. The carrier expects to increase to daily service a week after launch when an additional A350-900ULR enters service.

Peruvian interior ministry said police are evaluating expulsion of U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian citizen Jennifer Moore for allegedly inciting rural communities to protest Hudbay Minerals’ Constancia copper mine. The authorities requested documents, saying they have information the pair did not comply with their tourist status and focused on inciting townspeople against Canadian mining activity. The ministry added that their actions are causing a change in public order and expulsion may be appropriate. Hudbay temporarily suspended operations at the mine in November amid rural protests over development projects. Neither the two foreigners nor the Canadian embassy were available for comment.

The passage describes entry-level occupational therapy education in the United States as consisting of didactic education and fieldwork education, with fieldwork transforming students from classroom learners to competent entry-level generalist practitioners. It reports that the American Occupational Therapy Association convened an Academic Fieldwork Coordinators group and a Research Promotion committee to evaluate fieldwork-related literature and recommend future scholarship, with the manuscript presenting the committee’s findings.

An international systematic mapping review (Roberts et al., 2015) previously characterized the fieldwork literature, but the current work updates it for the past 30 years and maps it to the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda—Revised (2018) across levels of education (OT, OTA) and fieldwork (Level I, Level II). The authors conducted a mapping review using searches of four databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education, applying inclusion criteria for U.S.-based, English-language articles from 1989–2019 (expanded to October 22, 2020). After screening, 67 articles met final eligibility.

Results indicate the literature focuses more heavily on Level II occupational therapy fieldwork than on Level I and is also disproportionately concentrated in the agenda categories “Instructional Methods” and “Learner Characteristics and Competencies.” The review found no articles mapped to “Theory building,” “Signature pedagogies,” or “Promotion of diversity, inclusion, and equity,” and it reports gaps including OTA fieldwork experiences, Level I fieldwork experiences, and research for multiple other agenda categories. The authors discuss limitations of mapping reviews and difficulties mapping fieldwork to agenda categories, then outline implications calling for collaborative stakeholder efforts and potential inclusion of fieldwork in future revisions to the AOTA Education Research Agenda.

Archaeologists in Egypt announced the discovery of a 4,400-year-old tomb near the pyramids outside Cairo. Egypt’s Antiquities Ministry said the tomb likely belonged to Hetpet, a high-ranking official during the 5th Dynasty, and that it contains wall paintings showing Hetpet observing hunting and fishing scenes, including a monkey reaping fruit and another dancing. Mostafa Al-Waziri said excavation is underway for another tomb believed to belong to Hetpet, who is thought to be close to ancient Egyptian royals.

The lecture discusses how the collective Thomson scattering spectrum depends on electron and ion dynamics, starting from the scattered power into a solid angle and frequency and introducing the spectral density function, which involves the Fourier transform of electron density and plasma spectral-response (susceptibilities). Using a test-particle formalism, the speaker derives formulas for the electron and ion components of the spectral density, assuming Maxwellian distributions with possibly different temperatures and defining parameters such as the collective scattering parameter \(\alpha=1/(k\lambda_{Debye})\) and the plasma \(w\)-function. The lecture explains the roles of limiting cases of \(\alpha\) (incoherent scattering when \(\alpha^2\to0\); coherent regimes for larger \(\alpha\)) and identifies high-frequency electron plasma (Langmuir) waves and low-frequency ion-acoustic (anacoustic) waves as resonant features of the spectrum under appropriate conditions. It further covers how total scattered cross-sections depend on \(\alpha\), practical implications for detecting electron vs ion features, and how magnetic-field effects and electron-ion drift can modify the spectrum (including asymmetric anacoustic peaks), enabling inference of plasma parameters like temperatures, ion flow, and electron-ion drift/current under certain assumptions. The lecture also notes how collisions and finite spatial/temporal measurement effects (finite collection volume and angle, velocity gradients, and turbulence) can broaden or distort spectral features, and briefly mentions current research directions such as non-Maxwellian distributions and multi-angle Thomson scattering.

The passage describes Turkey’s highly centralized and unitary educational administration structure, where policies and key decisions are made centrally by top authorities and applied top-down to subunits. It argues that this system generally does not consider components such as accountability, transparency, democracy, participation in decision-making, scientificity, efficiency, and flexibility, and claims that administrators are often assigned based on political views rather than competencies. The study proposes changing the centralized National Education System toward a contemporary model based on local education boards to improve governance and education standards.  

Methodologically, it reports a mixed-method exploratory sequential design using literature and OECD reports for qualitative data and a questionnaire for quantitative data administered to teachers and administrators in Seyhan district (Adana) during 2016–2017. Qualitative findings list various local education board structures used in OECD countries and identify board-member compositions. Quantitative findings report teachers’ and administrators’ preferences for local and participatory administration models using elected boards/commissions, including roles for a wide range of education stakeholders and preferences for inspection and evaluation commissions. The passage also outlines a proposed “Local Education Board Model,” including central and local organizational structures such as a National Education Supreme Council and provincial/district boards, and provides recommendations for piloting and further research.

A federal judge declined the US government’s request to pause an order allowing transgender individuals to join the military starting January 1, 2018. The judge ruled the government had not shown it would be irreparably injured. The Pentagon said it is already following a prior court ruling and is preparing to enlist transgender individuals as of January 1. The White House said the Department of Justice is reviewing legal options regarding the ruling.

Texas education experts, parents, and administrators say a new Texas law replacing STAAR with three shorter tests could increase student stress and testing time instead of reducing them. Critics say banning practice tests may not lower pressure because schools may still need to prepare students for three exams. The law requires the Texas Education Agency (TEA) to study how to reduce the weight of testing in school accountability ratings, but findings won’t be due until 2029-30 and TEA is not required to implement them, leading some to worry accountability will still rely heavily on end-of-year results while students take more tests. Schools can choose assessments for the first two exams from a TEA-approved menu, while TEA will create the third; the new tests will release scores about two days after exams so teachers can tailor instruction. Administrators also worry about whether the new exams will face the same strict testing protocols as STAAR. Some educators and parents argue for educator input in designing and selecting assessments, and describe MAP testing as less stressful than STAAR.

The passage describes how NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to reduce I/O overhead for NVMe SSD-equipped gaming PCs by enabling GPU-based lossless decompression and offloading work from the CPU to the GPU, improving I/O performance by a factor of two. It also outlines NVIDIA A40 data center GPU capabilities, including performance improvements over Turing, benefits from PCIe Gen4 and NVLink, virtualization features, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform. The passage then discusses NVIDIA Ampere display support (including DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC), the fifth-generation NVDEC video decoder and the NVDECODE API with supported codecs, and AV1 hardware decode support with low CPU usage. It further describes NVIDIA’s seventh-generation NVENC encoder for accelerated video encoding and streaming, and highlights GA10x Ampere architectural features for ray tracing, AI processing, and GDDR6X memory.

A bug in widely used Atlassian software like Jira and Confluence can let attackers abuse a vulnerable proxy to perform XSS and SSRF attacks, potentially extracting AWS secret access keys from the AWS instance where the software is hosted. With those keys, an attacker could take over the instance and steal or destroy data. NIST rated the bug severity 6.1 out of 10, and Atlassian products have since been fixed, though many companies may still run legacy versions. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen major companies with outdated exposed deployments. Some organizations, including EE (UK), Insider, Easy Metrics, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, IEEE, and Ronin, reported fixing or securing their vulnerable deployments after being contacted; others did not respond and remained vulnerable, so the affected companies are not named. The passage concludes that updating Atlassian software is the best solution.

The passage argues that England may face group-stage humiliation at the 2018 World Cup unless manager Gareth Southgate changes his tactics. It says England qualified for the World Cup finals in Russia but performed poorly in a 1-0 Group F win over Slovenia, lacking pace, verve, invention, and risk. The author criticizes Southgate’s 4-2-3-1 formation as outdated and claims England played cautiously like Slovenia, despite keeping the ball. Dele Alli is presented as England’s best option for the No. 10 role, while Raheem Sterling is said to belong on the wing rather than as a No. 10. The passage also recommends England take chances in friendlies against Brazil and Germany next month by switching to three centre backs, using wing-backs, keeping Henderson and Dier as protection, and attacking with Alli, Rashford, and Kane.

The passage is part of NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2015. It includes general filing information, a table of contents, and unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements (income statement, comprehensive income, balance sheet, cash flow statement) and related notes. Key disclosed items include revenue of $1,305 million for the three months ended October 25, 2015 and $3,609 million for the nine months ended October 25, 2015; net income of $246 million and $406 million for the same periods; and cash flows with $664 million of net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended October 25, 2015. Notes describe significant accounting policies, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities (classified as available-for-sale with temporary unrealized losses assessed), fair value measurement, intangible assets, balance sheet components, an interest rate swap, product warranty and a SHIELD tablet recall, long-term debt (1.00% Convertible Senior Notes Due 2018), commitments and contingencies including a headquarters build-to-suit operating lease, litigation involving Qualcomm and Samsung (including ITC proceedings and related patent actions), shareholders’ equity and share repurchase activity, segment reporting (GPU, Tegra Processor, and “All Other”), restructuring and other charges related to wind-down of Icera modem operations, and a subsequent-event ASR entered into in November 2015. It also contains management’s discussion and analysis covering forward-looking statements, business overview, recent developments, litigation, restructuring, capital return, and results of operations.

The passage is from *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1902* (Appendix I), concerning whaling and sealing claims against Russia over the arrest and seizure of the American vessels “Cape Horn Pigeon,” “James Hamilton Lewis,” “C. H. White,” and “Kate and Anna.” It includes an introduction to an electronic edition by the Office of the Historian, followed by document listings and communications from John Hay and Herbert H. D. Peirce. The documents transmit English translations of a memorandum presenting U.S. claims to an arbitrator at the Hague, in support of indemnity for the owners, officers, and crews of the vessels.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle have announced co-CEOs in the past eight days, as more companies adopt a model that had been uncommon. While co-leadership can work, the passage says it can create risks such as unclear authority, power struggles, and employee confusion if roles and governance are not clearly defined. Equilar found the share of companies led by co-CEOs remains around 1.2% of the Russell 3000 index, though more firms could adopt it as leadership change accelerates. Harvard Business Review data cited in the passage reports higher average annual shareholder returns for companies with two CEOs (9.5% from 1996 to 2020) than single-leader companies (6.9%). Examples discussed include Spotify’s planned succession, Comcast’s promotion of Mike Cavanagh to co-CEO with Brian Roberts, Oracle’s leadership change with Larry Ellison still central to strategy, and earlier dual-CEO arrangements at Sony Interactive Entertainment, Salesforce, Chipotle, and Netflix. Experts cited say the structure’s success depends on well-designed roles, alignment between leaders, and their ability to collaborate, and some argue co-CEOs should be used sparingly due to governance complexity and costs like two compensation packages.

Berenice M. Brubaker sued the State of New York to recover damages for appropriations of real property for improvements to the International Rapids Section of the St. Lawrence River under the Highway Law and the Public Authorities Law. The claimant originally owned about 365 acres near the Village of Massena. The land included two easements for drainage/sight and had no improvements; it was zoned agricultural north of Middle Road and industrial south of Middle Road.  

The court addressed multiple appropriations: May 19, 1955 (about 183 acres north of Middle Road), June 12, 1956 (a 0.15-acre flooding easement within an existing drainage easement), April 1, 1957 (an additional 25.34 acres with reservations for farm use and access), and May 1, 1957 (an easement for electrical transmission lines over 55.38 acres). The claimant claimed damages of $309,000, while the State claimed $28,000 to $40,000.  

Applying the “Miller” rule as discussed in related case law, the court ruled that no project-related value increment could be included for the May 19, 1955 taking due to insufficient proof of likely condemnation. For the later appropriations, the court found the lands fell outside the category of probable original project takings, requiring payment based on market value as enhanced by proximity.  

The court awarded: $32,000 for Parcels 185 and 148; $100 for Parcel 2202; $39,750 for Parcel 2159; and $27,700 for Parcel 2169, with specified interest periods for each award. The written findings and conclusions were submitted by the parties and signed as part of the court’s decision.

The passage describes a display device, including a substrate; a pixel electrode and opposing electrode; an encapsulation portion on the opposing electrode made by alternately depositing organic and inorganic layers; and a planarization layer on the encapsulation portion that covers the edge portion while creating a larger angle between its edge side surface and the substrate surface (≥ about 70 degrees). The planarization layer may include organic material and may be flat on its upper surface, potentially covering and exposing portions of the encapsulation portion depending on the embodiment. The device may include patterns such as touch sensors on the planarization layer, with touch electrodes and wiring positioned in display and peripheral areas. The planarization layer is presented as improving flatness for forming patterns, reducing dead space, and reducing parasitic capacitance that could otherwise affect touch sensor performance. The document also provides detailed examples of display panel structure, encapsulation layer materials, and capacitive touch sensor electrode arrangements.

The passage outlines defensive fundamentals and strategies to counter the UCLA offense, focusing on defending high post rub cuts and down-screen actions. It describes three phases for defending the high post rub: (1) show to force the cutter inside and wide off the screen, (2) recover into pass-denial positions while weakside defenders pack in, and (3) complete final matchups with show-and-recover coverage, ball pressure, and a post defensive position while the defense packs in. It also presents an “All Out SOS” approach to disrupt the offense by trapping the wing on the first pass, with vulnerabilities tied to the point guard’s cut to the low post and the difficulty of wing ball reversal against a double team. The SOS method is detailed in three phases: setting the first-pass trap, rotating pass out of the trap using near player concepts, and then performing final matchups with helpside and post-front positioning.

The passage describes a Supreme Court discussion about whether candidate Michael Bost has “standing” to challenge an Illinois mail-in ballot law. It says many justices appear inclined to overturn a lower court ruling that Bost lacked standing to sue over a rule allowing ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they arrive up to 14 days later. The justices debate what standing test should apply in election-law cases, including Justice Elena Kagan’s view that candidates should show the new rule likely puts them at an electoral disadvantage relative to the old rule, and other justices’ concerns about whether that would be enough, how it relates to proving election outcome or reputational harm, and the potential remedy and consequences if such standing is denied and litigation is forced into a post-election context.

The passage describes an SEM-based microscale study of electrical resistivity in Al-Mg-Si alloys that couples in-situ four-point probe electrical measurements with microstructure characterization. Grain interior resistivity (Al solid solution including nano-precipitates) was found to depend on heat treatment rather than composition, with similar values for different Al contents under the same anneal. Resistivity across individual Si and Mg2Si precipitates showed that both precipitate types contribute equally to resistivity, and that the alloy’s bulk resistivity increases linearly with solute content (Si and Mg) for a given heat treatment, with coefficients dependent on the annealing condition. Other microstructural defects were neglected due to low densities, leaving Al matrix grains and secondary-phase precipitates as the main contributors to resistivity.

Y-Cross is a drop-back passing concept used in the Air Raid offense and widely across football. It is described as a weak-side flood concept that gets skill players moving to create deep shots downfield, with the core routes being a post, crosser, and an RB stretching the flat to the boundary. Offenses tailor the concept to personnel, including using either the TE or the slot receiver as the tagged crossing runner. The QB progression in the base read is Post, Deep Crosser, then RB check-down or dig, with high-low reads against a 2-high defense. The concept is coached differently versus man and zone coverage, with specific route and landmark guidance for the TE, FB, TB, X, and Z receivers. It is noted to work well against man coverage and Cover 4, but 1-high defenses in Cover 3 can limit the post by using a “post safety.” Variations include a post-wheel read and a curl-flat tag to adjust the progression versus 1-high defenses.

Bitcoin rose to a six-week high on Tuesday, gaining 4.4% to $9,340.88 on Bitstamp amid positive headlines about major financial institutions entering the cryptocurrency space. The rise followed a 50% loss in the first quarter after a nearly 1,400% surge in 2017, and bitcoin climbed in six of the last seven sessions. Gains lifted demand for other cryptocurrencies like ripple and ethereum, increasing total digital-currency market capitalization to $427 billion, the largest since early March. The article cites comments from ZenCash co-founder Rob Viglione and ULedger CEO Josh McIver, and reports that Goldman Sachs enlisted Justin Schmidt to lead digital asset markets and that Barclays PLC is gauging client interest in launching a crypto trading desk. A Thomson Reuters survey found one in five financial institutions is considering trading cryptocurrencies within 12 months, with 70% of those respondents planning to start trading in three to six months. Analysts said $28 billion changed hands over the prior 24 hours, the largest trading volume since Feb. 10, while noting regulatory challenges remain.

DWI arrests are down in Wichita Falls, with only 5 arrests over St. Patrick’s Day weekend. From January 1 to March 19, DWI arrests were 39 in 2016, 38 in 2017, and 25 this year. Sgt. Harold McClure suggests the decrease may be due to people understanding the importance of not driving after drinking and to ridesharing. Uber and Lyft have recently come to the area, and Uber reported that 4 of the top 10 St. Patrick’s Day destinations were bars and restaurants. A student, Kari Bell, said rideshare apps could be an alternative to a designated driver to avoid danger, and an Uber 2016 study found 90% of riders felt Uber reduces drunk driving and 80% felt it personally helps them avoid drinking and driving. Sgt. McClure also said having sober drivers and increased police presence encourages smart decisions.

The passage provides guidance on trading EUR/USD, emphasizing the pair’s high liquidity and global importance. It outlines topics such as building a comprehensive trading plan (including identifying support/resistance, using technical and fundamental analysis, setting risk limits, and backtesting), developing entry and exit strategies (e.g., breakouts/breakdowns, narrow range patterns, and Fibonacci levels), and using leverage cautiously. It explains how interest rates, inflation, economic data, central bank policies, news releases, and geopolitical events can affect EUR/USD, and discusses timing based on European and U.S. session overlap. The passage also covers different trading styles (position, swing, day trading, scalping), hedging and diversification approaches, broker selection and security/regulation, and transitioning from demo to live trading with continuous strategy refinement. It lists common mistakes to avoid, including lack of discipline, inadequate risk management, excessive leverage, and not backtesting or using a demo account.

The passage describes opportunities and challenges of using artificial intelligence (AI) in education, and specifically in STEM education, including benefits such as personalized learning, real-time feedback, improved assessment, and administrative support. It also introduces a study that conducts a bibliometric analysis of AI in STEM education from 2020 to 2024 using citation analysis and data from the Dimensions database, including 35 articles. Results show no publications with citations in 2021–2023, while 2024 had 15 cited publications with 234 total citations (15.62 citations per publication). The United States leads in document count and citations, and the most cited authors are Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson (55 citations each). The most cited journals and articles are identified, along with leading institutions such as Carnegie Mellon University (55 citations). The study highlights ethical concerns, the need for increased AI literacy, and potential effects on student engagement, and concludes that AI’s importance in STEM education is growing while requiring ongoing evaluation and balanced implementation.

The passage says Trump officials argue the H-1B program is being abused and that the Trump administration’s proposal to require employers to pay a $100,000 fee to secure H-1B visas could imperil thousands of jobs at colleges. As of June 30, U.S. colleges and universities employed more than 16,000 workers on approved H-1B visas. It explains that the H-1B program is used to hire foreign workers for “speciality occupations” requiring highly specialized knowledge and related bachelor’s degrees, and that the professional, scientific and technical services sector has the most H-1B visas. Data cited show at least 930 colleges and universities had at least one H-1B employee as of June 30, with many visas concentrated among a small number of institutions. The passage notes the president’s fee proposal does not apply to current H-1B holders, and that how it will be applied to universities is unclear. It also states that agencies may exempt certain people or industries from the fee if the secretary of homeland security determines hiring foreign talent is in the national interest, and quotes experts and organizations arguing the policy would be a barrier to hiring international researchers and postdocs.

The passage argues that disaster preparedness should follow the idea of “prevention,” noting health hazards from hurricanes Maria, Harvey, and Irma, including lack of power and resources, contaminated floodwaters, toxic chemical releases, mold, mosquito-borne disease risks, unsafe structures, downed power lines, and deaths linked to heat and other conditions. It says health risks and damage to health systems can persist after storms and could be reduced through more prevention measures and planning, including public education, infrastructure hardening, securing hazardous industrial sites, strengthening seawalls, and improving electrical grid storm resistance. It also describes Florida’s efforts before Irma and the impact of Irma on power, with lights restored in habitable structures after ten days for Florida Power and Light.

Two Democratic candidates in targeted Southern California GOP House districts won state party endorsements on Feb. 25, following contentious convention fights. Dave Min, after a rare floor battle in a field of five Democrats, won the endorsement to challenge Rep. Mimi Walters with 60 percent from 50 convention delegates; however, opponents later gathered 300 delegate signatures to push for more speeches and a voice vote from over 2,000 delegates, where support for ratifying the endorsement prevailed and Party Chairman Eric Bauman ruled it would stand. Hans Keirstead was endorsed despite five opponents attempting to block it, and the endorsements will appear on sample ballots for voters. In other targeted Southern California districts, preferred candidates fell short of the 60 percent threshold; Mike Levin and Bryan Caforio each received 53 percent, while Jay Chen led at 47 percent. For statewide offices, no governor or U.S. Senate candidate reached the 60 percent consensus, including Lt. Gov. Gavin Newsom at 37 percent, while convention delegates backed Sen. Dianne Feinstein’s preferred rival, Kevin de Leon, 54 percent to 37 percent.

The passage discusses several market headlines, including AMD shares rising after an AI chip deal with OpenAI, projections by Evercore that a “bubble scenario” could take the S&P 500 to 9,000 in 2026, and gold rallying above $3,900/oz amid a yen slump and U.S. rate-cut bets. It also notes seasonal weakness over the past 35 years, diminished liquidity, and institutional rebalancing and tax loss selling adding pressure to markets, with earnings momentum and optimism potentially tapering off in August. A technical discussion focuses on TLT, yields, the dollar, gold, and related levels, and includes references to divergence between growth and value and several specific price points. The passage includes promotional content about Investing.com’s AI-picked strategies and concludes with extensive trading risk and legal disclaimers.

The passage describes coccolithophores, microscopic ocean algae that regulate Earth’s climate by removing carbon from seawater, producing oxygen, and forming calcium plates that sink to create chalk and limestone layers recording climate history. It states that European scientists and five named research institutions are collaborating to establish October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day, led by the Ruđer Bošković Institute, to raise awareness of their role in carbon regulation, oxygen production, and marine ecosystem health. It also summarizes related research by teams at the Lyell Centre, NORCE, MARE, and the International Nannoplankton Association, including studies of CO2 uptake, ecological interactions, effects of warmer or more acidic oceans, and links between living coccolithophores and their fossil record.

A Tennessee woman, Kimberly Jones, shared a Facebook video in which her son Keaton described being bullied at middle school, including being mocked and having food poured on him. The video drew over 18 million views and a crowdsourcing page for his education raised more than $29,000. Athletes and entertainers responded, including invitations to attend games or visit, and messages from figures such as Delanie Walker, Tyler Byrd, Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr., and Snoop Dogg.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 farmers from three villages in Darz Ab district of Afghanistan’s Jowzjan province while they were working on their land. Most were members of the minority Uzbek community. Regional officials said the motive was unclear; provincial police blamed Taliban fighters who control most of the district, with police spokesman Mohammad Riza Ghori stating elders were trying to secure the release and an operation would follow if talks failed. A Taliban spokesman, Zabihullah Mujahid, said he was aware of the report but could not confirm it. The passage also notes that last week gunmen killed six International Committee of the Red Cross employees in Jowzjan and kidnapped two workers, leading the ICRC to suspend operations; officials blamed Islamic State fighters, while the Taliban denied involvement, and police said there was no Islamic State presence in Darz Ab, only Taliban.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 28, 2021, reporting that it completed a simplification of its corporate structure by repatriating economic rights of certain non-U.S. intellectual property to the United States through domestication of a foreign subsidiary. In connection with this domestication, the company updated its tax rate outlook for the second quarter of fiscal 2022, expecting GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates of 13% (plus or minus 1%), excluding discrete items, and expecting a discrete tax benefit of approximately $250 million to $300 million. The filing states the information is furnished under Item 7.01 and not deemed “filed,” and notes the domestication aligns the corporate structure more closely with the operating structure under OECD BEPS conclusions and changes to U.S. and European tax laws.

The passage describes a cross-disorder study of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) using primary care data from the Health Improvement Network (THIN) and replication in the UK Biobank (UKB). It focuses on prodromal symptoms and drug prescriptions before neurodegenerative diagnosis, with THIN data spanning January 1996 to April 2020 and UKB providing reported cases of AD, PD, and dementia. The study compares odds of 12 health conditions and medication classes in time windows up to 15 years before diagnosis, using logistic regression and Bonferroni correction. In THIN, symptom and treatment patterns differed between AD, PD, and DLB, including higher frequencies of certain motor or non-motor features compared with controls. DLB showed stronger associations with several health conditions, and additional analysis in PD assessed drug prescriptions associated with later dementia within five years after PD diagnosis. UKB replication compared AD versus PD medication differences and other comparisons involving dementia. The passage concludes that neurodegenerative diseases have long prodromal phases and reports a differential role of lipid-lowering therapies in the prodromal period.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2015. As of July 30, 2015, 127,142,147 shares of common stock were outstanding. The report includes condensed consolidated financial statements (unaudited), including balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive loss, and cash flows. For the three months ended June 30, 2015, Tesla reported total revenues of $954.976 million and a net loss of $184.227 million; for the six months ended June 30, 2015, total revenues were $1,894.856 million and net loss was $338.408 million. The report also describes accounting policies, including revenue recognition and resale value guarantees, leasing programs, warranties, inventory valuation, and stock-based compensation, and discusses recent accounting pronouncements. It outlines liquidity and capital resources, including cash and cash equivalents of $1.150 billion at June 30, 2015, and notes credit arrangements such as the Warehouse Facility and an asset-based revolving credit agreement.

The passage explains that gold trading is speculating on gold market prices to make a profit, typically using cash-settled instruments such as futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs like GLD, with physical gold bars or coins usually not involved. It describes gold as a precious metal used for jewelry, ornaments, exchange, and as a store of value, and notes that its price can fluctuate due to supply and demand changes and political, social, and economic unrest. Gold trading may also be used to hedge other positions because gold is often viewed as a “safe haven” with limited sensitivity to certain political and inflation factors. The passage then presents a gold weekend swing trading strategy using GLD, tested from late 2004 to September 2021, where trading from Thursday close to Friday close and Thursday close to Monday open produced average gains of 0.14% and 0.19% per trade with profit factors of 1.4 and 1.3 respectively. It reports that adding a simple parameter improved results, suggesting the strategy may be acceptable for a small position.

Jerry Jones, owner and general manager of the Dallas Cowboys, was fined $250,000 by the NFL for an “inadvertent” obscene gesture toward fans at MetLife Stadium during the Cowboys’ 37-22 win over the Jets. Jones said the gesture was unfortunate and inadvertent, adding he intended to give a thumbs-up and point at Cowboys fans. The Cowboys are expected to appeal and have until Friday to decide. The passage also references other NFL owner fines for fan interactions, including Panthers owner David Tepper being fined $300,000 for a drink toss.

The passage describes the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and how countries submit Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) to report progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It focuses on SDG3 (health) in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR), noting that health-related progress has been slow and that by 2023 progress is nearly at a standstill with setbacks across indicators. It argues that achieving health-related SDGs depends on access to quality data, which requires well-functioning national health information systems; however, limited data availability, including lack of trends and disaggregated data, is a major monitoring challenge. The study reviewed the latest VNRs from 18 EMR countries (submitted 2016–2021) and assessed reporting comprehensiveness and data availability for health-related SDG targets and indicators. Results show that all VNRs reported mechanisms to monitor SDG progress, but comprehensiveness varied by country income level and only some VNRs explicitly set 2030 targets for indicators. Data availability for SDG3 was reported by nine countries, and fourteen VNRs cited limited data availability as a monitoring challenge, including issues such as limited human resource capacity, low data quality, and lack of data disaggregation. The most commonly reported health indicators included maternal and child mortality measures, while trends were rarely reported, with only one country providing trend data across all SDG3 indicators. The authors conclude that EMR countries’ VNRs reflect commitment but also reveal weaknesses in health information systems, limited data availability, and limited analytical capacity; they recommend strengthening regulatory frameworks and health information system capacities, including civil registration and vital statistics and population-based surveys.

A rare white moose was filmed in Sweden and drew global attention. The BBC said there are about 100 white moose in the country and that they are not albino; they grow white fur from a genetic mutation. People compared the moose to characters and stories online. It is not known whether twin white calves are albino or piebald moose, which have a few small brown specks.

The speaker says tomorrow night’s game is important and that the team is regrouping today and will face the opponent tomorrow. They are concerned it may disrupt their rhythm, noting they need to score more on the power play. They mention controlling the play in the first two periods, letting up in the third, and that the opponent tends to “hang around” before responding when least expected. The speaker emphasizes the need to avoid any let-ups, citing good energy and chances, and saying they would have been better with a second goal.

The passage describes requirements and options for an ADC system, including the need for a high-bandwidth low-noise amplifier buffer to charge ADC input sample-and-hold capacitors at maximum sampling rate, and the use of internal (nominal 4.096V) or external voltage references selected via programming INTREF_DIS. It details internal reference decoupling, limits on using REFIO/REFCAP for external loads, potential reference shifts caused by mechanical/thermal stress (especially during solder reflow), and temperature-compensated reference behavior over –40°C to +125°C. It also explains alarm features (input and AVDD alarms), ADC transfer characteristics (straight-binary output and LSB sizing), and multiSPI device functional modes and data transfer/reading protocols, including single/daisy-chain topologies and RESET/ACQ/CONV states.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators developed an AI tool called Diag2Diag that uses sensor input to generate synthetic, highly detailed plasma data for diagnostics that cannot capture certain readings, especially in the plasma edge region. The system aligns synthetic data with real-world measurements, is intended to improve control robustness while reducing hardware complexity and cost, and could help recover data from failing sensors in other applications. Research used sensor data from experiments at the DIII-D National Fusion Facility. The AI is positioned to support plasma monitoring and control in future commercial fusion by enabling fewer, more compact diagnostics, lowering maintenance costs, and providing new evidence supporting a magnetic island theory for ELM suppression.

The passage is a 2022 list of 10 AI content generator and writer tools aimed at creating engaging, efficient content. It describes features, supported content types or formats, language or template options, originality/plagiarism claims, SEO-related capabilities, and pricing or trial details for several tools, including Jasper (with search-optimized blog posts and original-content claims), Copy.ai (templates and multi-language output), Frase (SEO optimization, briefs, and competitor data), Article Forge (keyword-based article generation and integrations), Rytr (multi-language, tone options, plagiarism checker, and image generation), and other tools such as ones focused on grammar/plagiarism checking, e-commerce/product descriptions, beginner-friendly video/article/infographic creation, niche-specific content (with free trial and tiered article generation plans), and lightweight blogging support. It concludes that AI writing tools are presented as cheaper and high-performing, suggests Jasper as a top option by the author, and notes affiliate links.

Origin PC announced a new Eon15-S gaming laptop starting at $999 in the US, using Nvidia GeForce 1050Ti graphics. The $999 model pairs the 1050Ti with an Intel Core i3 processor and a 120GB SSD, while adding $100 can upgrade to a Core i5 and double storage. Compared with Dell’s Inspiron 15 7000, it costs more but offers an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support (with a one-year warranty term). CNET plans to test it soon and publish a full review.

The Supreme Court announced it will not hear Ghislaine Maxwell’s appeal, leaving her 20-year prison sentence in place. Maxwell argued that a 2007 non-prosecution agreement clause covering “potential co-conspirators” should have prevented the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York from pursuing charges because the agreement used “the United States.” The 2nd Circuit had ruled that such an agreement is generally binding only in the region that made the deal unless it clearly shows it was intended to bind multiple districts. Maxwell also said the ruling deepened a circuit split over how to determine the scope of non-prosecution agreements. U.S. Solicitor General D. John Sauer said the clause was “highly unusual” and that the case-specific interpretation did not warrant Supreme Court review. The Court’s denial was announced as part of its order list dated Sept. 29.

The passage describes the “5-Day Low of The Range Strategy,” a simple long trading approach using two criteria: IBS lower than 0.25 and a close lower than the lowest low of the previous 5 days. From January 1993 to today, it produced 517 trades with 309 winners and an average return of 0.46% per trade, outperforming the average return for any 5-day period (0.11%). Profitability is highest over 3–7 days, and exiting after five days yields a 10.76% annualized return, outperforming buy-and-hold despite buy-and-hold being held much longer. The win ratio is 60%, with average winners larger than average losers, though performance has not been as strong lately. The strategy may be adapted for short selling using criteria based on today’s range (e.g., 0.75, needing 0.9 for similar fill counts), producing almost 10% over the same period, though short strategies are described as less profitable.

The passage discusses stock and commodity-market movements, stating that gold held up relatively well and stayed below a rising resistance line, while silver and mining stocks did not move noticeably higher. It says the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF failed to rally meaningfully and closed below the April high for three consecutive trading days, implying a bearish setup and a likely early part of a bigger decline, with the USD Index preparing to rally. It also describes stocks taking a breather after declining below rising support and combining bearish signals, and it compares the overall situation to 2008. The text includes various Investing.com headlines and standard trading risk and website-disclaimer language.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) is a neural shader that caches and approximates radiance to produce high-quality global illumination and dynamic lighting in real-time rendering. It uses path-traced rays after one bounce as input and infers lighting values for many bounces by training small neural networks on live game data. NRC increases performance by avoiding ray tracing beyond the initial bounces, improves indirect lighting quality by inferring multiple bounces on a limited ray budget, and preserves image quality in challenging scenarios due to its adaptability and in-game contextual awareness.

The State of Washington appealed a judgment from the Superior Court for Spokane County in case No. 12-1-00619-0, entered June 10, 2013. The appellate court reversed the judgment and remanded the case in an unpublished opinion by Korsmo, J., with Siddoway, C.J., and Fearing, J., concurring separately.

The passage discusses the Supreme Court’s two-step test for Second Amendment challenges under *New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen*: courts first determine whether the Second Amendment’s plain text covers the challenged conduct, and if so, the government must show its regulation is consistent with the Nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation. Critics argue this test is burdensome for judges, citing Justice Stephen Breyer’s view that courts are staffed by lawyers, not historians, and Judge Carlton Reeves’s complaints about judges lacking historians’ knowledge and differing methods for evaluating evidence and sources. The author argues the relevant question is not whether judges are good historians, because judges decide cases and must answer historical questions as part of legal decision-making. The passage explains that, in Second Amendment cases, step one may often be straightforward using the text’s meanings, while step two may require historical work at the margins, though the tradition inquiry may be limited by the difficulty of proving credible historical traditions. It also notes that courts, unlike historians, must decide cases even amid uncertainty, using legal tools such as burden-shifting to resolve it.

The passage describes a voice-directed inspection system that supports multiple inspectors performing inspections of business assets. It explains that inspections can be labor intensive and that voice and mobile devices enable hands-free receipt of inspection-plan commands and voice entry of inspection data. For large inspection plans (e.g., jet engines), the system splits an inspection plan into multiple sections and assigns different unfinished sections to different inspectors to work in parallel without overlapping. A first and a second inspection assistance device request assignments and receive audible commands for their respective plan sections, then send audible updates on completion back to a site computer, which forwards combined updates to a host computer. The system includes a host computer, multiple site computers, and inspection assistance devices with portable computers and headsets. The passage also outlines methods for receiving/creating inspection plans, determining multiple unfinished sections, sending sections to requesting devices, receiving updates, and submitting updates to the host computer. It includes details about an inspection plan editor and voice processing (e.g., text-to-speech and speech recognition), plus supporting hardware and network communications.

The speaker says they are thrilled the series is over and that Buffalo played a great series, with a good young team likely to return. They describe their own experience of tough playoffs, including missing last year and being excited to compete this year, and they reflect on how hard it is to win the Stanley Cup due to adversity and injuries. They praise their teammates, highlight the importance of Hull even with limited shifts due to wrist injury, and say the team has veteran experience and know how to win.

COVID-19 spread rapidly in late 2019–March 2020, and RT-PCR was identified as the gold standard for diagnosis and tracking, though it was initially limited by long turnaround times, reliance on central laboratories, and the need for nasopharyngeal swabs that can cause discomfort and inconsistent results. Point-of-care RT-PCR was proposed to reduce wait times, but early non-laboratory-operated RT-PCR platforms were limited and required additional sample handling that could introduce cross-contamination risks and operator exposure. The passage notes that SARS-CoV-2 can be detected in saliva reliably, with reports that saliva-based testing may be acceptable for diagnostic testing, especially for repeat testing or challenging patients.  

The MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test is described as an emergency-use-authorized saliva-based RT-PCR POC device that uses patient self-collected saliva directly into a sealed processing cartridge to protect operators and reduce sample mix-up. A study evaluated clinical performance and usability of Sal6830™ when operated by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers at two centers, using comparisons to a Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV POC platform and a tiebreaker assay for discordant results. Blinded-sample results were concordant with expected outcomes, and in the prospective trial overall percent agreement was reported as 93.3% with high positive and negative agreement. Usability questionnaire responses indicated the device was easy to use, well integrated, and could be operated without additional technical support. The report concludes that Sal6830™ can be used accurately and easily by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers in point-of-care settings without additional sample handling or nurse-collected swabs, while using gold-standard RT-PCR detection technology.

The lecture discusses how to analyze poker using a “decision mentality,” focusing on expected results rather than actual outcomes. It illustrates this with “credit card roulette” and with examples showing that good or bad results can occur despite correct or incorrect decisions, so players should evaluate the best possible decision and consider long-run averaging (law of large numbers). The professor then explains three levels of poker reasoning: (1) hand vs. opponent’s specific hand (“soul read”), (2) hand vs. opponent’s range/probabilities (exploitative play), and (3) optimal play using ranges vs. ranges and frequencies to prevent exploitation. The class also covers concepts and rules relevant to playing poker: blinds/antes, stack size vs. effective stack size, position, equity (as probability of winning or fraction of the pot), pot odds to equity conversion, raising vs. going all-in thresholds, and basic strategy distinctions like bluffing vs. value betting. Near the end, the professor provides recommended pre-flop opening ranges by position for beginners and runs a class exercise based on game theory (“Who’s Taller?”) and later a Nash-equilibrium-based all-in scenario, awarding gift certificates based on card selection and equity results.

The passage says many women in the UK are diagnosed with ovarian cancer only after emergency care, with just one in three identified at the earliest stages when treatment is most effective. It attributes late diagnosis to factors such as difficulty getting timely doctor’s appointments and being dismissed by healthcare providers, and emphasizes that there is currently no screening test. It highlights that 90% of women are unaware of the four main symptoms and that ovarian cancer symptoms are often mistaken for other issues, leading to delays. The four main symptoms described are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary urgency with little urine, and persistent pain in the tummy/pelvic area. It advises making an appointment with a doctor if concerned, and mentions a free online symptom checker and a downloadable symptoms diary to help people seek earlier medical advice. The passage states that early-stage diagnosis gives a higher survival rate and that less than a third of cases are diagnosed at stage 1 or 2. It concludes that awareness should extend beyond people with ovaries and stresses the importance of encouraging others to seek medical help.

On September 20, 2017, Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico with sustained winds of 155 mph and gusts up to 190 mph, along with torrential rains of up to 40 inches, causing large floods. The hurricane destroyed the island’s electricity grid, leaving 3.4 million people without electricity, and damaged or left without fuel many infrastructure elements including aqueducts and sewers, roads, bridges, ports, airports, cell phone towers, and gas stations. Estimated damages exceeded US$82 billion, and Maria destroyed about 80% of the value of the island’s crops, resulting in a $780 million agricultural yield loss. The passage also discusses indirect deaths during emergencies and notes that varying guideline interpretations and personnel training can hinder mortality counts. Several studies examined excess deaths after Maria, but one study assessed indirect causes only through the end of October 2017, limited causes, and did not account for population displacement, potentially underestimating excess deaths. The research described builds a semi-parametric Poisson regression model to estimate deaths related to a state of emergency, incorporating intra-annual variability, population displacement, and causes of death, and modeling the duration of mortality effects by cause. The model assumes death counts follow a Poisson distribution and uses period and cause indicators, interaction terms, a smooth function for within-year variation, and year trend terms, with coefficients estimated via penalized likelihood and smoothing penalties determined by REML.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran, and Garry Cullum were the main winners in the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at KartSport Hamilton’s Agrisea Raceway. Cullum won the Wifiplus KZ2 Masters class title for a record fourth time, while Drysdale secured the Wifiplus KZ2 class title and Loughran won the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters title. Taylor Harte took pole position, but Mat Kinsman won the heats and Pre-Final before contact ended his Final.
