The Final results affected point margins, including penalties for kerb hopping that impacted several drivers, such as Madeline Stewart. In the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters, Enrico van der Griend crashed early in the third heat and Tim Loughran ultimately won the round and class title. In the KZ2 Restricted class, Cullum won all heats plus the Pre-Final and Final to take the series class win by 20 points, followed by Aaron Wooley and Gerhard Benadie, with Jamie Pollock and Shaun Anderson finishing fourth and fifth in points.

DryShips (NASDAQ:DRYS) reported after the April 17 market close that it had been issuing common stock through a continuous offering plan under a prospectus supplement. As of April 17 close, DRYS still had $173.4 million remaining to be issued, with an equity market capitalization of $106 million at that close. From April 10 to April 17 (post 1:4 reverse split), DRYS raised $14.5 million by issuing 7,912,449 shares at an average price of $1.79, diluting existing shares by 16.8%. Kalani Investors did not fully satisfy DRYS’s fixed amount requests: $5 million requested for April 10 and $25 million requested for April 11–17, but Kalani issued only 48% of the requested amounts, with weak market demand for the equity (equity issuance as a percent of volume traded: 8.86%). The passage also states that completing the remaining issuance could require issuing about 105.7 million additional shares, which would result in massive dilution, and notes that the stock price had declined sharply after the reverse split before some later announcements.

NASA has a plan to address a potential future impact from asteroid Bennu, a near-Earth object orbiting the sun 54 million miles from Earth. Bennu is “potentially hazardous,” with a 1 in 2,700 chance of crashing into Earth on September 21, 2135. NASA’s HAMMER spacecraft would use an impactor for smaller rocks, but for an asteroid like Bennu it would deploy a nuclear device to destroy it before it reaches Earth. NASA has monitored Bennu since its 1999 discovery and sent a probe to collect samples.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study examined returns of about 26,000 public shares listed between 1926 and 2015 and found that most stocks did not outperform one-month Treasury Bills. Between 1926 and 2015, only 43% of equities had returns higher than Treasury Bills, and only 86 of 26,000 stocks achieved half the return. The study also reports that while the average stock market performance can be strong, the median stock performed poorly, contributing to the difficulty of selecting winning stocks. The passage suggests passive funds as the easiest option and emphasizes that diversification is essential for investors choosing individual stocks. A similar survey for Norway’s Oslo Stock Exchange (1985–2017) is presented as showing the same pattern.

The passage describes soccer sportsmanship when a player is injured but the referee allows play to continue, possibly due to the advantage rule or not seeing the injury. It suggests players may stop play by kicking the ball out over the sideline or touchline so assistance can be given. After the injured player is attended to, the referee restarts with a throw-in taken by the team that did not kick the ball out, and the thrower demonstrates courtesy by throwing to the team that previously kicked it out, effectively returning possession. The throw-in should generally be sent mostly backward down the sideline to the opponent’s back defender, and neither team should take advantage of the courtesy. The receiving team should wait for the thrower to get back into position before resuming; if a midfielder receives, they should pass back to a defender, and the ball should not be challenged until the defender has clear possession. A similar approach is described when the referee stops play for an injury while the ball is live, in which case play resumes with a dropped ball; if the team had clear possession at the whistle, the receiver may pass backward to an opponent, and the receiving team should again send the ball backward before attacking.

The passage describes predictive e-maintenance systems as part of the e-Manufacturing and e-Business concepts, using real-time and smart monitoring to assess performance and support near-zero downtime. It explains how web-enabled functions and agents can integrate maintenance decisions with business tools such as CRM, ERP, and e-commerce, requiring technologies like sensing devices, reasoning agents, wireless communication, and integration platforms. It also outlines research needs including predictive intelligence, data processing tools, scalable informatics platforms, security, distributed computing for dynamic decision making, and technician education. Further sections present reconfigurable maintenance concepts for aligning production configuration with changing demand and customer requirements, enabling enterprise-wide failure prediction and intercompany maintenance cooperation. The modular reconfigurable maintenance system is described as using system-wide communication with a control center for remote maintenance, sensor-based monitoring with radio signal transmission, and data analysis for detecting adverse conditions and informing preventive and remedial measures. The conclusion states that production environments face mass customization pressures, so integrated reconfigurable maintenance systems are needed to respond with minimal cost, improve quality, and ensure overall reliability.

The passage says the authors previously gave up on the US equity market too early and suggests reconsidering a bearish stance in light of potential upside (“What if equities melt up instead?”). It discusses low VIX attention being linked to complacency and recommends caution. It states that an attached presentation includes 21 charts covering various equity and VIX-related tickers, aiming to prompt doom-and-gloom predictors to reconsider. The authors say the market’s breadth, which initially made them bearish, now shows underlying strength, and they invite comments. A disclaimer notes the views are discretionary ideas limited to discretionary portfolios, and includes an investment-related disclosure that the author is long US equities and VIX.

John MacGabhann, general secretary of the Teachers’ Union of Ireland, warned teachers against becoming Facebook friends with students, saying it narrows professional distance and that virtual friendships or photos can lose context and professionally damage teachers. He also cautioned teachers about social media comments, arguing that words sent electronically cannot be recalled and that employers’ use of technology can lead to unreasonable expectations and harassment-like behavior. He advised teachers to be slow and circumspect before posting, not to send risky messages, avoid getting drawn into online feuds, and, if contacted unreasonably, not to respond and to turn off their devices.

The passage is a VentureWire newsletter dated May 17, 2001, sent to Jeff Dasovich. It lists top stories, including Tahoe Networks’ $38M first round, Startups.com changing its model and cutting 30% of staff, Hermes Pensions Management allocating $965M for private investments, and OffRoad Capital reorganizing and laying off 50%. It also reports “new money,” “bad news,” “new products,” and M&A updates, followed by announcements of new directors and new executive appointments, VC fund and personnel news, and a correction regarding MolecularWare.

The passage is a formal address in which the speaker thanks the people for their confidence and states their accountability in carrying out federal duties. These duties include executing U.S. laws, managing foreign and confederate relations, handling revenue, commanding forces, and communicating with the legislature to promote national interests. The speaker says they will respect limits on executive power, preserve peace and friendship with foreign nations, and address issues involving separate states with respect for their reserved powers. They emphasize faithful, economical management of public revenue to help extinguish the national debt and reduce waste. They discuss choosing import subjects to support agriculture, commerce, and manufactures, with possible exceptions for products essential to national independence, and they support internal improvement and spreading knowledge where the federal government can. The speaker argues against enlarging standing armies, supports civilian control of the military, describes plans for strengthening naval forces and maintaining military infrastructure, and identifies the national militia as the primary defense. They also commit to a just policy toward Indian tribes and to “reform” by correcting abuses tied to federal patronage and election freedom and by improving appointment practices. The speaker says they will select diligent and talented collaborators, look to predecessors for example and guidance from other government branches and citizens, and end with religious supplications for the country’s protection and blessing.

The passage explains that TRNC education policies have changed over time under the influence of political leaders’ discourses, especially statements by TRNC Presidents. Education is described as more than academic instruction, serving to strengthen social belonging and preserve Turkish Cypriot identity. After the 1974 Cyprus Peace Operation, the education system in Northern Cyprus was restructured with close relations to Turkey, and Presidents then helped determine education’s fundamental directions, with a Turkish model emphasizing national identity. The text also outlines earlier education phases under Ottoman rule, British colonial administration, and the 1960 Republic of Cyprus, and describes how the Turkish Cypriot community sought an independent education system after 1974. It highlights the role of Turkish Cypriot Education Council decisions in reforms, particularly through language, history, and culture courses, and notes that history textbooks have often presented Turkish identity-centered narratives that can be polarizing, while later reform efforts aimed at more reconcilatory and multi-perspective approaches sometimes faced setbacks. The passage summarizes differences across presidential tenures, such as emphases on national identity and Turkey integration, harmonization with Europe, technical education investments, peace and intercommunal dialogue, and multiculturalism. It concludes that political discourse and council decisions together have shaped major education reforms and recommends history curricula adopt multi-perspective, scientifically grounded approaches, with education policies guided by long-term strategic and scientifically neutral principles while considering local needs and autonomy alongside cooperation with Turkey.

Sergey Lavrov said India’s accession to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has increased the group’s political profile and its capacity to stabilise Central and South Asia, including helping resolve the crisis in and around Afghanistan. He said India’s foreign policy contributes to security and stability, and that trade between Russia and India should rise to $30 billion by 2025. Lavrov also discussed deepening defence cooperation and technology transfer, said a US strategy of using force in Afghanistan is unlikely to work, and argued drug production and terrorism are linked. He denied alleged Russian support for the Taliban, saying Russia’s contacts aimed to extract citizens and encourage negotiations under UN Security Council criteria. Lavrov regretted the US declined the “Moscow Process,” mentioned the “Six Plus One” framework, and said Afghanistan’s political resolution requires broad participation, with a smaller group including Central Asian countries rather than the Kabul Process.

A letter taped to the door of Michael Ben’Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney abruptly fired last week, said he was terminated after a false social media post while he was working on a terrorism prosecution. The letter warns that DOJ leadership is making America less safe by removing career officials and argues Ben’Ary’s firing shows a focus on punishing the president’s perceived enemies rather than protecting national security. It also mentions his firing followed pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly’s social media claim that Ben’Ary was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco, and cites alleged internal resistance to an indictment involving former FBI director James Comey.

The speaker says they will prepare for tomorrow’s game as the opposing team plays “for its life,” and emphasizes that getting off to a strong start is crucial. They believe the other team has been successful at home during the playoff run and will try to continue, so the focus must be on being prepared and competing from the beginning, or it could be a difficult night.

Malcolm Mitchell, a New England Patriots wide receiver, will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance during its 20th Anniversary Summit and Gala in New York. After realizing in college that he struggled with reading, Mitchell taught himself to read by starting over with children’s books and practicing. He later launched the youth literacy initiative “Read with Malcolm” to promote book access and literacy in underserved communities, aiming to introduce book ownership where reading is not a priority and improve school literacy where grade-level skills are below average. The passage cites America’s Promise Alliance research linking multiple adversities and low reading access to poorer school outcomes, and includes Mitchell’s account of overcoming literacy challenges through persistent practice, outreach to schools, and ongoing advocacy, along with details about his book, “The Magician’s Hat,” and his goals for encouraging children to read.

Yandex announced it will report its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2018, on July 26, 2018. Management will hold a conference call and webcast that day at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time to review and discuss the company’s second quarter results. The release includes call and webcast details, as well as background information about Yandex and its investor and media relations contacts.

Digital accessibility is presented as an inclusive practice of designing and developing digital technologies, platforms, and content so they are usable by people with disabilities, aiming to remove barriers and enable equal participation. The passage notes that accessibility is guided by the W3C’s Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), which use four principles (POUR) and three conformance levels (A, AA, AAA), and states that it is mandated by law in multiple countries, including the U.S., EU, Canada, and India under the RPwD Act, 2016. Despite this, compliance is reported as low, and digital inaccessibility is described as having economic consequences and being linked to developer skill and awareness gaps, partly attributed to limited inclusion of accessibility in CS curricula.  

To address this, the authors designed and delivered a one-day informal accessibility workshop in India for software professionals and CS educators, with a focus on fundamentals, technical and social dimensions, and hands-on learning using assistive technology simulations, accessibility tools, and case studies. Evaluation used pre- and post-workshop surveys. The workshop had 73 participants (software engineers, educators, and UX designers, including some participants who self-identified as having disabilities) and received positive feedback across engagement, confidence, effectiveness, and intention to apply learning. Post-survey results and thematic analysis indicated interest in advanced inclusive design, AI and emerging technologies, accessibility for diverse user contexts, organizational and policy strategies, and more practice-based learning with real-world examples.

The passage discusses the Supreme Court case “Is Humphrey’s Executor headed for Slaughter?” analyzing the Court’s approach to administrative law, agencies, and lower courts. It focuses on whether presidents have constitutional power to fire Federal Trade Commission (FTC) heads without cause, centered on the Court’s 1936 decision in *Humphrey’s Executor*. The passage says the Court seems likely to uphold President Donald Trump’s firing of FTC commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter, without necessarily overturning *Humphrey’s Executor*, though it suggests the Court’s prior signals could threaten FTC independence. It recounts how in 1933 President Franklin Delano Roosevelt fired FTC commissioner William Humphrey despite a statute requiring cause. The passage then contrasts the FTC with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) in *Seila Law LLC v. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau*, where the Court emphasized evaluating an agency’s actual powers and rejected CFPB independence based on the CFPB Director’s structure and authority. It argues that the modern FTC differs from the 1935 version, describing expanded rulemaking and enforcement and citing scholarship that the FTC now acts primarily as an executive law enforcement agency. The passage also notes a separate brief order where the Court stayed lower court orders regarding removals of NLRB and Merit Systems Protection Board members, and it compares the Federal Reserve’s different structure and powers. Finally, it describes how the Court framed the question in Slaughter’s case as whether FTC statutory removal protections violate separation of powers and suggests the Court may “mend it, don’t end it” regarding *Humphrey’s Executor*.

DA leader Mmusi Maimane MP says President Zuma’s “Radical Economic Transformation” is a cover for elite self-enrichment and criticizes the ANC for corruption and for actions such as the Esidimeni 94 deaths, which he says the ANC refused to mark with a minute’s silence. He argues the ANC protects power rather than vulnerable South Africans and describes the President’s SONA as involving heavy security and violence toward Members of Parliament. He also outlines the DA’s “Rescue Plan” for the “Lost Generation,” including reforms in education, youth employment and training, labour and business support for entrepreneurs, stopping the nuclear deal and opening the electricity grid, changes to mining and empowerment policy, land and agricultural ownership measures, and additional policing and health improvements. He concludes by calling for change and says the DA will build an “honest, capable” state and move the country forward.

The passage describes ways to use an Echo with Alexa to make cleaning easier: using the Cleaning Buddy skill to set cleaning tasks on a schedule, setting up voice purchasing through Amazon to automatically order cleaning supplies (with a four-digit code and One-Click payment), automating vacuuming with robot vacuums via Alexa voice commands (including example commands for Neato and Roomba), using the Laundrapp laundry service by booking pickups and having clothes delivered back (available in about 100 US cities), and installing the Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone skill for advice on removing tough stains.

MIT scientists developed a refined prime editing approach that makes gene edits more precise and safer by reducing unwanted DNA mistakes. The team altered key proteins driving prime editing, lowering error rates from about one in seven edits to about one in 101 for the most common editing type, and in another mode from one in 122 to one in 543. By incorporating additional RNA template-stabilizing components, they created a final editor (vPE) with an error rate about 1/60th of the original, ranging from one in 101 to one in 543 in different modes, tested in mouse and human cells. The researchers are working to further improve editing efficiency and address delivery to specific tissues, and they hope other labs will adopt the editors in research.

The passage describes how superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavity performance depends on the quality of the inner surface, particularly regarding electropolishing (EP) and buffered chemical polishing (BCP). It reports that EP can produce smoother surfaces and cites XFEL processing statistics showing EP can achieve high gradients and quality factors, but also notes that some low-performing cavities may result from defects in the cavity inner surface that can be improved using combinations of mechanical polishing with EP or BCP.  

Focusing on the question of what limits peak magnetic fields in Nb SRF cavities, the study explains that the metastable Meissner state can break down at the superheating field due to vortex nucleation, driven by factors such as surface roughness. Surface roughness can reduce the superheating field by introducing magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression, potentially leading to cavity quench.  

Using white light interferometry (WLI) and atomic force microscopy (AFM), the authors characterize electropolishing-induced defects on bulk Nb samples, specifically identifying sharp intergranular sloped steps and measuring their slope angles and step heights. They model these geometry-induced defects with London theory to calculate associated magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression factors, and use diffusion modeling (Fick’s second law) to study how impurity migration near these defects can alter impurity profiles and uniformity relevant to shallow impurity treatments.  

The results conclude that electropolishing produces grain boundary defects with substantial slope angles and steps that compromise high-field stability, with estimated enhancement and suppression effects causing a larger degradation of achievable peak magnetic field than previously expected. The passage emphasizes the need for smoother surfaces and states that step heights comparable to relevant diffusion and penetration lengths can strongly affect impurity dose near vortex penetration positions.

British police said counterterrorism officers are working with local detectives after a man and a woman in their 40s were found unconscious at a residential building in Amesbury and left in critical condition after exposure to an unknown substance. The incident is about eight miles from Salisbury, where former Russian spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter were poisoned on March 4. Police cordoned off places the two visited, with health officials saying there was no believed wider risk. The pair were hospitalized at Salisbury District Hospital, where initial thoughts included a contaminated batch of heroin or crack cocaine, but further testing is ongoing and police say it is not yet clear whether a crime was committed.

The court held a final evidentiary hearing in an adversary proceeding where D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny debtor Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak’s Chapter 7 discharge. The plaintiff alleged denial under 11 U.S.C. §§ 727(a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), and (a)(5) based on alleged fraudulent transfers or concealment, failure to keep records, false oaths, and unexplained loss of assets. 

After reviewing evidence, the court found the plaintiff did not prove that the debtor acted with actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud under § 727(a)(2); did not identify specific missing records under § 727(a)(3); did not show that the debtor’s inaccuracies and alleged false statements were made with fraudulent intent under § 727(a)(4); and did not establish a predicate showing specific owned assets in 2002 with unexplained disposition under § 727(a)(5). The court ordered final judgment for the debtor and against the plaintiff on all counts and directed entry of the debtor’s discharge in the Chapter 7 case.

The passage describes the history and spread of polo, saying it originated in Persia more than 20 centuries ago and later developed into the version known today from India. Polo reached the U.S. via England, and there are about 250 polo clubs in 43 U.S. states. It introduces the Milwaukee Polo Club (in Hartland, about 26 miles west of Milwaukee), founded as an extension of a 1923 formation in the Milwaukee area, and discusses efforts to make the sport more accessible. It explains that matches typically last about two hours with six seven-minute chukkers, and that play depends on fair-weather safety conditions for riders and horses. The passage also emphasizes horse care and limits, stating that much of polo performance depends on the horse, and describes balancing a horse’s physical and mental work. It provides the club’s address, phone numbers, notes that the summer opener was June 18, and directs readers to its website.

The passage is a series of remarks emphasizing preparation, focus, and executing rather than relying on momentum or carryover. It argues that opportunities are limited in a cap world and that depth is important for sustaining playoff success. The speaker also stresses controlling the game, avoiding puck turnovers, and improving forechecking by executing properly. Additional comments focus on team unity, supporting teammates, wanting to win for each other, and continuing to perform despite prior setbacks, while enjoying the current opportunity because it may not return.

After ICE arrests in the Austin area, Austin ISD lawyers directed campus principals and staff not to share with students resources or fliers not vetted by the superintendent’s office or general counsel. A memorandum sent to campus leaders Monday also instructs employees not to speak about political affiliation, views, protests, advocacy, or other controversial issues on district property, warning of possible scrutiny from state lawmakers due to the district’s heightened oversight. The memo followed at least 51 people detained by ICE agents last Thursday and Friday in the Austin and San Antonio area, which schools said caused student anxiety and confusion. Austin School Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo, saying the board was not briefed and that he was surprised by its tone. Austin Superintendent Paul Cruz posted a general list of district resources for immigrant and refugee students, while Education Austin distributed thousands of documents about what to do if ICE shows up and shared names of trusted immigration lawyers, holding Know Your Rights seminars. Education Austin said it is providing informational guidance relevant to families’ security. A news conference is planned for Wednesday at Lanier High School, and Saldana said board members will discuss the memo at Wednesday’s board operations meeting.

A 13-year-old girl is in serious but stable condition in hospital after being shot in the thigh in Guildford, Sydney’s west, on Tuesday night. Police said she was sitting with a group in an open garage when several shots were fired at about 9.45pm. Emergency services found her shot and paramedics treated her before she was taken to the Children’s Hospital at Westmead. A neighbour reported hearing five or six “pops” she believed were gunshots and later hearing police and screaming. Police believe the shooting was not random and plan to speak with the girl once she is well enough.

Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said he believes Republicans are making an “unprecedented” attempt to undermine special counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation and the FBI’s integrity. He said the release of the Nunes memo was part of a campaign to weaken the Mueller investigation, and he told David Axelrod that he and Sen. Richard Burr were denied access to the memo before it was released. Warner said they were blocked because a legitimate review would question its methodology and use of classified information. He also said House Intelligence Committee actions reconfirmed the memo’s partisan nature, while Paul Ryan said it provides “greater transparency” and supports Democrats releasing their own memo. Warner added that the Senate Russia investigation is ongoing and is important for defending against future cyberwarfare threats.

The passage argues that penny stocks are bad and should be avoided because many involve unproven or failing business models, are illiquid, are highly volatile, and have limited financial disclosure due to less regulation. It describes penny stocks as often traded over-the-counter (OTC) or in Pink Sheets, where companies typically do not meet formal exchange requirements like those of NYSE or Nasdaq. The passage also warns that penny stocks can attract scammers, citing types such as “pump and dump,” “know-it-all” formula scams, share dilution schemes, and inverse stock splits. It concludes that while some people may trade them with small allocations, starting without understanding risks and pitfalls is not acceptable.

The passage contrasts “digital leaders” with “digital laggards” in areas such as learning mindset, data transparency, and measurement. Digital laggards often focus on short-term efforts, discourage risk-taking, keep data access restricted, hoard data, and rely on business judgment or process adherence rather than data-driven metrics. They also struggle to ground objectives in realistic, well-understood data, leading to avoidance of measurement and “best effort” approaches. Digital leaders, by contrast, promote experimentation in safe contexts, emphasize transparent data sharing with appropriate governance, and use detailed metrics to learn and set structured goals aligned to strategy, while retaining flexibility in execution. The passage includes case studies of a pharmaceutical company fostering localized experimentation and a retail company operationalizing real-time sales reporting, illustrating outcomes like improved efficiency, morale, autonomy, and real-time decision-making.

The passage discusses two-sided many-to-one matching and fairness notions based on justified envy. Gale and Shapley’s stability is linked to justified envy-freeness for participants, but this can be unfair to teams; analogous team fairness criteria include envy-freeness, envy-freeness up to one participant (EF1), and versions that account for participant preferences (team-justified EF1). It explains that while team-EF1 and participant-justified EF allocations can exist in one-to-one matching, they may be incompatible in many-to-one settings, motivating a new criterion (team-justified EF1) that reduces to team-EF1 when participants are indifferent.

The paper defines formal preliminaries, including SD-based fairness notions, balancedness, swap stability, and Pareto optimality. It presents two warm-up algorithms that achieve some fairness and balance properties but not swap stability. The main algorithm (Algorithm 3) constructs team-slots, maintains eligibility sets for each participant, iteratively computes lexicographically optimized matchings under eligibility constraints, and guarantees an allocation satisfying team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, and Pareto optimality. The algorithm runs in polynomial time, unifies round-robin and Gale–Shapley in special cases, and is proven group-strategyproof for participants (with augmented tie-breaking). The passage also outlines extensions to settings with team quotas and the possibility of being unassigned, showing how to maintain stability, extended team-justified SD-EF1, Pareto optimality, and group-strategyproofness.

The passage reflects on the United States’ first century, beginning with the adoption of the Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union about 100 years earlier and the subsequent move to a National Union based on the will of the people. It describes the Constitution’s expansion of freedom and strengthening of order, the growth of the nation through added states, the larger jurisdiction and population covered by the Constitution, and the Constitution’s “supreme trial” in the civil war, after which the Union emerged “purified and made stronger.” It argues that the nation should preserve the gains of liberty and good government, end controversies settled by the Constitution and laws, and affirm the permanent supremacy of the Union. It highlights emancipation as a major political change and addresses ongoing disputes about equal suffrage, warning that violations of ballot freedom and the dangers of ignorance and corruption could undermine the Republic. The passage calls for universal education and civic cooperation to secure the future, then shifts to topics including prosperity, monetary policy, currency and debt refunding, support for agriculture and manufacturing, transportation and possible interoceanic canal/rail options, religious freedom, governance of territories, regulation of criminal practices, civil service reform, and commitment to enforce laws, practice economy, and require honest public service. It concludes with an appeal for public support as the author assumes office and invokes divine blessing.

The passage describes the ATR (Average True Range) trailing stop, a technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder to help traders set stop-loss levels based on price volatility. It uses ATR to calculate dynamic stop-loss levels, which can protect profits, minimize losses, and adjust to changing market conditions. ATR trailing stop values are calculated by multiplying ATR (typically 3.5) by a multiplier and then subtracting it from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions. It can be used for exit points and also for entry signals based on breakouts or reversals, and it can be applied to stocks. The indicator may signal potential trend reversals when price consistently breaches trailing stop levels, and ATR bands derived from ATR are used to gauge volatility and possible breakouts. Risks and limitations noted include that it does not account for past performance and price movements and that trading involves uncertainty and potential losses. The “cross point” is defined as the intersection of price with trailing stop levels, indicating potential changes in market dynamics.

Drew Faust, Harvard University’s first female president, announced she will step down at the end of the upcoming school year, ending her 11th year and the Harvard Campaign launched in 2013. She said the transition will be led by a new president and plans to take a sabbatical and return to her scholarship. Faust became president in 2007 after serving as dean of the Radcliffe Institute. Harvard leaders said she restored trust after a period of campus controversy and credited her with fostering collaboration, expanding financial aid, and supporting the arts and sciences. Her tenure also included backlash over crackdowns on all-male social clubs, demands from Black students for greater diversity, suspension of the men’s soccer team over a lewd scouting report, and a 2% investment loss for the university’s endowment. In her final year, she will focus on federal funding threats for research, attracting top students and staff, and advancing inclusion and belonging. A search committee will be formed to find a replacement.

Texas A&M has had at least one first-round NFL pick in every draft since 2011, and receiver Christian Kirk is described as the Aggies’ best hope of keeping the streak alive after bypassing his senior season. The draft begins Thursday at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, where Kirk is not planning to attend in person. Kirk is projected as a fringe first-round pick, with USA Today listing him fourth-best among receivers in the draft. A&M safety Armani Watts is forecast as a mid-round pick, and Damion Ratley as a late-round selection. The passage also discusses A&M’s recent draft history, the youth of the team last season, recruitment issues from earlier classes, and an arrest in December involving defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson that affected his draft outlook. The article notes which A&M players were first-round selections from 2011 through 2017 and outlines the draft’s schedule by day.

Alphabet, which owns YouTube, will pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump’s case related to his post–January 6, 2021 ban on YouTube. Of that amount, $22 million will go to Trump, with $2.5 million split among co-plaintiffs. YouTube had suspended Trump’s account for at least one week in 2021 due to concerns about potential violence, and restrictions were not lifted until March 2023. The passage also says Trump directed the $22 million to the Trust for the National Mall for construction of a White House ballroom, and that Alphabet admitted no liability or fault under the settlement terms.

Michigan’s State Superintendent Michael Rice, the state’s top education leader since 2019, is retiring Friday after decades as an educator. Until Rice is replaced, Glenn Maleyko will begin serving as interim state superintendent, with Sue Carnell serving as interim state superintendent before then. Rice said Michigan lawmakers should stop allowing schools to count up to seven professional development days and up to 15 online-instruction days as instructional days, noting that pandemic experience showed many students struggle with virtual learning and that children “shouldn’t have to pay for professional development…with lost instructional days.” He also said Michigan’s academic recovery from the pandemic has been slow, with chronic absenteeism up, mental health concerns increasing, and third graders posting their worst reading scores in the 11-year history of the Michigan Student Test of Educational Progress. Rice highlighted progress under the Michigan Department of Education’s Top 10 Strategic Education Plan, including expanded funding for vulnerable students, increased preschool enrollment, and a 82% high school graduation rate, but said no goals have been fully achieved. He cited Mississippi’s earlier, required LETRS literacy training and hiring of literacy coaches as factors in big fourth-grade reading gains on the NAEP, and he contrasted Mississippi’s approach with Michigan’s allowance for incursions into instructional time. Rice also said teacher shortages have improved as Michigan invested in stipends, scholarships, “grow your own” programs, and workforce-strengthening efforts, with the number preparing for teaching rising from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually, though he said challenges remain.

The passage describes Peter Lynch’s background and investment approach. It states that Lynch was a retired money manager who managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, earning average annual returns of 29.2% and increasing the fund’s value from $20 million to $14 billion; he retired in May 1990 at age 43. It says he was a value investing proponent and is known for the slogans “invest in what you know” and “ten baggers.” The passage explains that he did not try to predict markets or focus on short-term price changes, instead emphasizing company fundamental indicators and clear business models. It outlines Lynch’s company-categorization approach into groups such as slow growth, moderately growing, fast growing, cyclical, and companies coming out of a crisis, and it describes portfolio construction with different percentages by category, ongoing monitoring every three months, and selling or adding based on changes in fundamentals relative to price movements. The text also notes that the fund held around 40 companies at the start under his leadership and 1,200 companies when he retired.

The passage reports that the Vice President of the Ghana Football Association, George Afriyie, was relieved of his duties after an Executive Committee meeting on Tuesday. It links the decision to a rumoured rift between Afriyie and Kwesi Nyantakyi, which had reportedly started months earlier over financial disagreements and suspicions about Afriyie’s ties to critic Nii Lante Vanderpuije. It says Afriyie’s removal has emboldened his campaign to contest the 2019 GFA polls, potentially strengthening his bid against Nyantakyi. The text also describes internal divisions within the Executive Committee and notes that Afriyie was removed as head of the Black Stars Management Committee, with Winfred Osei taking his place. Finally, it discusses concerns about Nyantakyi’s continued leadership and suggests people may press him to seek re-election, ending with “We wait and see.”

Lenders and consultants are assessing the Dabhol Power project after Enron-promoted DPC’s phase II became uncertain amid disputes with Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over the power purchase agreement and escrow. Foreign and Indian lenders in Singapore directed US-based Stone & Webster to estimate the cost and implications of suspending the 1,444 MW phase II for about a year, including potential losses and restarting needs, and a temporary suspension was proposed by Enron India’s managing director K. Wade Cline. Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee said he was optimistic that Dabhol Power and MSEB would resolve their problems, while lenders also formed a panel to negotiate with MSEB. DPC also appealed to the Bombay High Court to stay orders restraining reactivation of the escrow account and arbitration proceedings, arguing the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission lacks jurisdiction. Related reporting discussed possible tariff and return adjustments, including reducing projected returns and keeping DPC’s return on equity within specified limits.

The passage reports that scientists, including those supported by the National Geographic Society, have conducted assessments of cheetah populations in southern Africa and urged that cheetahs be listed as “Endangered.” It states that a year ago scientists reported cheetahs had disappeared from 91% of their historic range, and that evidence from low population estimates supports the call for an IUCN “Endangered” listing.

The passage describes increasing global mosquito-borne disease concerns, noting that dengue cases have risen in the Americas and spread to temperate regions such as Europe. It discusses factors including climate change, human mobility, and the roles of Aedes mosquito species. It then outlines the study’s aim in the Basque Country (northern Spain), where autochthonous Aedes-transmitted diseases have not been recorded, to estimate invasive Aedes mosquito abundance using ovitrap egg count data and environmental variables (temperature, humidity, precipitation) with machine learning models. Data from Basque provinces (2013–2023 for egg counts, 2016–2023 for meteorological data) are processed (biweekly intervals, smoothing, handling missing values, and selection of highest egg counts), and models including GLM, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Trees are evaluated using MAE, RMSE, and R². Results indicate that model performance varies between provinces, with Random Forest generally performing best on training data and Generalized Linear Models sometimes performing better on test data, while SARIMAX performs strongly in some cases. The study uses best-performing models to forecast mosquito abundance for 2024 and concludes that continuous localized surveillance and appropriate modeling are important for controlling spread in non-endemic regions.

The speaker describes a playoff series with momentum shifts between teams and says both teams played hard, with the playoffs being a major battle for their team despite injuries. They emphasize the excitement and meaning of winning and competing for the Stanley Cup, describing it as the greatest prize in hockey and a unique opportunity for players to share with family and friends. The speaker discusses comfort and performance on home ice in the playoffs, notes confidence gained since the last time in this situation, and suggests that focusing on execution and details helps avoid being “paralyzed” after an opponent scores. They also reference coaching privileges and team preparation habits, highlight learning “steals” from great players, and mention specific battles between star goaltenders. The speaker concludes with comments about their opponent’s defensive strength and states that who scores is less important than doing one’s part to let the team win.

The passage describes a photo taken on a trip back to visit campus years after graduation. The author says they have few photos due to having a flip phone in college and reflects on how nearly a decade later, what they did right and wrong has become clearer. They note they didn’t take advantage of available opportunities and didn’t realize how much time they had for adventure. The author says they loved college but feel like a “tedious adult” telling younger people to enjoy it. They include a disclaimer that people do college differently, then mention they met exceptional people, took fascinating classes, and enjoyed returning to campus after breaks, before stating they will list things they did wrong.

HPBOSE declared the Himachal Pradesh Board Class 12 Result 2018 on April 24 at 14:07 pm on its official website, hpbose.org. The Class 12 examinations were held between March 6 and March 29. Students can check results on other websites such as examresults.net and indiaresults.com, and via SMS. The passage also outlines steps to access the result by visiting hpbose.org, clicking the Class 12 results link, entering required details including roll number, then downloading and printing the result.

Seven more candidates qualified Feb. 14 to join the race to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price in Georgia’s 6th Congressional District seat, bringing the field to 15 candidates with one day of qualifying left. The new qualifiers include Bruce Levell, David Abroms, Ragin Edwards, Bob Gray, Richard Keatley, Rebecca Quigg, and Kurt Wilson. Previously qualified candidates include Mohammad Ali Bhuiyan, Keith Grawert, Alexander Hernandez, Judson Hill, William Llop, Dan Moody, Jon Ossoff, and Ron Slotin. Price won nomination as President Trump’s new U.S. secretary of Health and Human Services. A special election is set for April 18 and a runoff, likely, is scheduled for June 20.

Liverpool’s 2017/18 Premier League fixtures were announced. Liverpool begin the season with an away match at Watford on August 12, host Everton at Anfield on December 9, and play Everton away at Goodison Park on April 7. They face Manchester United at Anfield on October 14 and travel to Old Trafford on March 10. Liverpool play Swansea City at home on Boxing Day, host newly promoted Brighton and Hove Albion at Anfield on May 13, and play champions Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on May 6. All dates may change for broadcast coverage.

The passage argues that smoking can worsen health outcomes, including exacerbating diabetes, causing nearly half of liver cancers, and reducing cardiovascular disease risk by 50% after quitting. It summarizes a Cardiff University-led study in *Thorax* showing that lung cancer screening with CT scans may increase quitting rates among smokers who are “motivated and receptive.” Researchers sent information packs to nearly 2.5 million British residents aged 50 to 75, identified high-risk respondents, and invited eligible participants to CT screening or not. Quitting rates were higher for screened participants (10% at two weeks, 15% at two years) than for those not invited (5%). The passage also notes that screening did not falsely reassure smokers and that quitting was associated with a marginal tendency toward distress about smoking. It concludes that CT screening can provide a “teachable moment” for smoking cessation and suggests combining screening with other anti-smoking interventions.

The Geminid meteor shower will peak Wednesday night, with the best viewing time between midnight and 4 a.m. Thursday. Up to 50 meteors may be seen at its height, and viewing could be better from rural areas with limited city lights and without needing a telescope. To watch, head south toward the constellation Gemini, where the meteors last longer and are slightly brighter. Viewing this December is expected to be better due to a smaller crescent moon, and clouds late Wednesday night may be present but overall are not expected to be widespread. The meteors are named for the Gemini constellation and occur yearly when Earth passes through debris from an asteroid named Phaethon that lights up in the atmosphere.

Caltech and six other institutions received a total of $4.9 million from the U.S. Geological Survey to develop an earthquake-warning system for the West Coast, and the USGS also plans to buy about $1 million in sensor equipment for the ShakeAlert system. ShakeAlert is intended to provide residents several seconds of advance warning so they can seek shelter or take steps to reduce damage. Caltech was funded along with Central Washington University, UC Berkeley, the universities of Oregon, Washington, and Nevada-Reno, and UNAVCO. Rep. Adam Schiff praised the funding, and the passage notes that the program previously faced possible loss of federal budget support, leading to $10.2 million being provided after legislative outcry. The USGS estimated in 2014 that completion would require about $38.3 million in capital investment and $16.1 million per year for operation and maintenance.

Northwestern’s first NCAA bid is seen as within reach after a 66-59 upset over Wisconsin, but the team may face challenges from increasing media attention as March approaches. Coach Chris Collins said managing attention and expectations is part of the process and could otherwise distract players. Players Bryant McIntosh and Vic Law emphasized that each Big Ten win matters and that losing later games could leave the team without the NCAA ticket. The Wildcats’ next test is against Maryland, and Scottie Lindsey is expected to miss his fourth straight game due to mono.

Valmet Oyj announced on December 11, 2017 that its Board of Directors decided on a new long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees. The plan aims to align shareholders and employees to increase the company’s long-term value, commit key employees to Valmet, and provide a competitive reward based on holding Valmet shares. It covers three discretionary periods (2018–2020), with performance criteria set at the start of each period. For 2018, rewards are based on Valmet’s Comparable EBITA margin and orders received growth in the Services and Automation business lines, and are paid partly in shares and partly in cash in 2019. Cash is intended to cover taxes and tax-related costs. The Executive Team is recommended to own and hold company shares equal to 100% of gross annual base salary. Rewarded shares cannot be transferred during a restriction period ending two years after the end of the discretionary period, and as a rule no reward is paid if employment ends before payment; shares must be returned if employment ends during the restriction period. The plan targets about 120 participants (80 management positions, including the Executive Team, and 40 management talents). The total combined reward is capped at approximately 586,000 shares before deduction of taxes and tax-related costs.

An American Airlines email titled “American Airlines Net SAAver Fares” was sent to Theresa Staab (Nov 19, 2001) offering Net SAAver Weekend Getaway Fares valid for travel the next weekend. It lists domestic departure dates of November 30–December 1, 2001 and return dates of December 3–4, 2001, with tickets required to be purchased by Friday, November 23, 2001 (11:59pm CT). Domestic and international fare tables provide routes and prices. The email also includes “Thanksgiving SAAle” information with a purchase deadline of Wednesday, November 21, 2001, and describes how to book on AA.com using an AAdvantage number and PIN. Additional rules and restrictions state taxes and fees may not be included, tickets are nonrefundable, seats are limited, and fares may change. It further mentions AAdvantage Net SAAver Awards for travel departing November 30–December 1, 2001, plus other vacation package advertisements.

A U.S. study surveyed 202 Head Start and other daycare center administrators, managers, and teachers in Illinois in July and found that priorities for teaching toddlers and preschoolers focused mainly on healthy food choices, exercise, and brushing teeth, while fewer than one in five listed bike helmets, vaccinations, or sun protection as top priorities. The researchers reported that about half of programs provided sunscreen, but 77% did not allow children to apply it themselves; state regulations for elementary school students may influence daycare decisions. About half used spray sunscreen, but many sprayed directly on children’s faces. Most programs reported no sunburns and generally followed guidelines for keeping children out of the sun when the heat index is high. The authors said the study’s limitation was that it only examined Illinois centers, and they called for increased early childhood awareness about sun protection, with suggestions that teachers be educated and that parents apply sunscreen and provide hats and protective clothing.

A federal jury in Denver found that radio host David Mueller groped Taylor Swift during a 2013 preconcert photo session and ruled his actions amounted to assault and battery. The verdict came in a civil trial that began Aug. 7, awarding Swift $1 in compensation. The judge cleared Swift, but her mother Andrea and a radio liaison were still facing allegations related to efforts to have Mueller fired; the jury also found they did not interfere with his contract. Swift had countersued after Mueller filed a 2015 suit denying her accusation and claiming it led to his firing by KYGO. The case resumed Monday with jurors not informed of earlier changes in the defendant lineup, and they also considered an assault allegation made by Swift.

The author describes being pregnant while working as a lawyer and recounts how her appearance drew attention and how opposing counsel and others repeatedly touched her pregnant belly without consent, which she views as sanctioned assault. She says she did not lose hearings while visibly pregnant and attributes any advantage to spectacle rather than merit, with the cost being loss of autonomy. She argues that euphemisms like “Stroke” and “Rub” conceal the reality of harassment and that the practice is improper in legal settings. She notes that federal law prohibits pregnancy discrimination and that the EEOC recognizes harassment based on pregnancy, including unwelcome physical conduct, but says this “belly stroke” is rarely addressed. She calls for explicit consent-based policies and training—“Do not touch”—and urges people to stop touching pregnant women without consent, including when other women do so.

The passage is a hockey player’s remarks about improving performance and preparing for a crucial Thursday night game. The speaker says they scored fewer goals but played better by handling the puck more effectively and putting it in better spots, while aiming to keep it away from Brodeur and get into the opponent’s zone. They describe being confident after winning two in a row, focusing on the one most important game, and preparing despite travel fatigue. The speaker also comments on home-ice factors, matchup considerations, and the impact of goalie performance and team confidence, including recent overtime success and the expectation that both teams will stay competitive even if they concede or score first.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth summoned hundreds of generals and admirals from across the globe and made his case for shaking up a military force he said had gone soft and “woke.” The speech is discussed by Greg Jaffe of The New York Times.

The passage describes Commander Chris Hadfield playing Santa on Christmas Eve 2012, when he floated weightlessly through the International Space Station about 400 kilometers above Earth. It notes the challenges of observing holidays in orbit, including frequent sunrises and the timing of “morning” in space, and explains that Hadfield asked crew families for cards to hide for the other astronauts to find on Christmas morning. The text also outlines how holiday traditions continued for the crew, including discussions of turkey and a dense fruitcake made by Trappist Monks, chosen to avoid crumbs that could clog ventilation filters. It highlights the crew’s prepared meals, a two-foot-tall artificial tree velcroed to a wall, personalized stockings, and the importance of traditions for psychological health. The passage concludes by mentioning Hadfield’s upcoming science-based variety show and a WE-related reference.

Setting write blocks to be pre-erased using ACMD23 can make a following Multiple Block Write operation faster. ACMD23 defines the number of write blocks to be sent next; if transmission stops early, remaining blocks’ content is undefined, and if more blocks are sent, the card erases block-by-block as new data arrives, with the count reset to the default after the operation. ACMD23 should be sent just before the WRITE command to use the pre-erased feature, and may be cleared automatically by other commands. The card responds to ACMD22 with the number of well written blocks, and pipeline buffering may prevent determining the last well-written block if an error occurs.

The passage then describes Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 erase-related operations, including erase range identification using ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32) and ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33) followed by ERASE (CMD38). It outlines sequence error handling, behavior with write-protected sectors, DAT0 low during erase, erase data contents after erase depending on DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE, and long erase times. DISCARD (CMD38 with 00000001h) and FULE (CMD38 with 00000002h) are described as alternatives to ERASE, with support limits, required sequences, error behavior, busy/timeouts, and that these operations are not supported through SPI. The passage also covers write protection methods, password-based card lock and unlock via CMD42 (including Force Erase password registers and COP feature behavior), and notes about accepted commands for locked cards and CMD55 behavior for application-specific commands (APP_CMD).

The NVIDIA A100 GPU’s L1 cache and shared memory unit offers 1.5x more aggregate capacity per SM than V100 (192 KB vs 128 KB) for additional acceleration. It includes new SM features to improve programmability and reduce software complexity. The GPU has 40 GB of high-speed HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (73% higher than V100) and a larger 40 MB Level 2 (L2) cache (nearly 7x V100), with 2.3x higher L2 read bandwidth due to a partitioned crossbar structure. It also provides L2 cache residency controls and Compute Data Compression for up to 4x additional improvement in DRAM bandwidth and L2.

Polling began in Uttarakhand for 69 of 70 assembly seats amid tight security, with voters queueing outside polling booths since early morning. The election office said over 74 lakh voters will vote for 628 candidates in EVM machines from 8 AM to 5 PM, and arrangements include nearly 30,000 security personnel, 60,000 polling officials, and polling across 10,685 booths, including 460 snowbound areas. The polling schedule for the Karnaprayag seat was revised to March 9 after the death of BSP candidate Kuldeep Singh Kanwasi in a road accident.

An action of tort was brought by Sylvester Michael McGillivray against Harry Eramian for personal injuries from a splinter in a bowling alley “sliding floor.” The jury returned a $750 verdict for the plaintiff after the defendant’s motion for a directed verdict and requested jury instructions were denied. Evidence showed the floor was uneven, wavy, and had rotten boards and missing splinters; the splinter entered the plaintiff’s finger as he delivered a ball with his hand close to the floor, and the flooring had been reused and was several years old. The court held there was no error in denying the directed verdict, that the proprietor owed a duty of reasonable care, that contributory negligence could not be ruled properly on the evidence, and that the refused instructions were appropriately withheld. Judgment was ordered for the plaintiff in accordance with the jury’s verdict.

Samsung announced cheaper, water- and dust-resistant versions of its Galaxy A smartphones, first unveiled since the Galaxy Note 7. Later this month, it will launch Galaxy A3, A5, and A7 models in Russia before expanding to other markets. The phones feature water/dust resistance for the first time, a new 16-megapixel camera with a “selfie mode,” screen sizes of 4.7, 5.2, and 5.7 inches, and design elements including a fingerprint sensor, metal frame, and 3D glass backing. They have less processing power than Galaxy S phones and max at 32GB internal storage without an external SD card. Pricing has not been announced, though Galaxy A models typically start under $400. Samsung is also moving past the Note 7 recall and will show new technology at CES 2017.

The passage outlines rules for obtaining U.S. passports. Passports may be granted and issued only by the Secretary of State. Applicants should apply through U.S. diplomatic representatives abroad, or consular officers if no representative is present; applicants in U.S. insular possessions apply to the chief executive of the possession. Passports cannot be granted to those who do not owe allegiance to the United States, and those who have only declared intent to become citizens are ineligible. Applications must be written affidavits containing birth date and place, occupation, permanent residence, temporary overseas travel with intent to return and perform citizenship duties, and an oath of allegiance. Applications require personal description details and a credible witness certificate verifying the applicant’s identity and the truth of affidavit facts. Additional requirements are specified for native citizens, those born abroad with native-citizen fathers, naturalized citizens (including submission of naturalization certificates or certified records), women (including marital status and related naturalization documentation when applicable), children of naturalized citizens, and residents of insular possessions who owe allegiance to the United States (including affidavits from at least two witnesses).

Matthew and Wendie Childress, whose 18-year-old daughter Chloe was a counselor who died in the July 4 Kerr County Camp Mystic floods, joined other Camp Mystic parents to push for tighter camp safety regulations. Their advocacy led to bills signed by Gov. Greg Abbott requiring camps to move overnight cabins out of floodplains, use weather warnings with radios and alert systems, and train staff on emergency plans. The parents said these steps could have prevented their children’s deaths. After gathering in Austin, meeting with Abbott, House Speaker Dustin Burrows, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, and testifying at legislative hearings, the House and Senate passed camp-focused bills (House Bill 1 and Senate Bill 1). Abbott signed the bills on Sept. 5, but the parents’ grief remained, as their daughters were not coming back.

The passage provides references and descriptions related to memory maps and pin configuration for the TMS320DM814x device. It notes that L4 Fast and L4 Slow peripheral memory map regions are broken into Tables 3-5 and 3-6, and that some regions are decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 subsystem and reserved for non-Cortex-A8 masters. It describes the DDR DMM TILER extended addressing map, which adds a 4-Gbyte range via a 33rd address bit to access frame buffer rotated and mirrored views, with full access limited to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems while other masters can access views through the 512-MB TILER region. It also explains that terminal function tables list external signal names, pin multiplexing, pin numbers, pin types, pullup/pulldown status, supply source, peripheral function details, de-selected input state, and Multi-Muxed options. Finally, it includes part of Table 4-1 for boot configuration terminal functions, describing GPMC CS0 default pins and their reset behavior, along with a note about RSTOUT behavior based on BTMODE sampling.

China launched its first talent visa program to attract young professionals and people with science and technology degrees from top universities to study and do business in the country. The launch came as the US increased restrictions on H-1B visas with a $100,000 fee and prompted xenophobic backlash.

The passage discusses how AI, particularly modern AI techniques and LLMs, could transform social science research by improving access to large-scale data and potentially automating parts of data analysis through reasoning capabilities. It identifies methodology challenges such as limited access to high-quality datasets, high costs of training and deployment, and the need to address biases, ethical risks, and responsible use. It also highlights possible roles of LLMs in synthesizing research data, exploring novel social theories, and enabling human–AI collaboration to maintain rigor and integrity. The passage further addresses AI governance, describing risks from generative AI (e.g., misinformation, deepfakes, and amplification of biases) and the difficulties of regulating rapidly evolving technologies under existing legal frameworks. It calls for human-centered, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI governance, emphasizing cooperation among industry, academia, and policymakers, combining top-down and bottom-up mechanisms, and using transparent reporting and monitoring to update regulations.

The passage describes diagnostic testing for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), including nasal nitric oxide (nNO), high-speed video microscopy analysis (HSVA), electron microscopy (EM) and immunofluorescence (IF), and genetic testing. It notes that while multiple tests are usually needed, some individuals can be confirmed with genetic testing or EM alone, but combinations are important to relate symptoms, ciliary defects, and genotypes. The study reports limited knowledge about how diagnostic tests are used across countries and aims to assess which tests and combinations are performed worldwide, how well participants recall tests, and what factors relate to more comprehensive testing.  

Using COVID-PCD cross-sectional data from 747 people with PCD across 49 countries, most participants (92%) reported undergoing diagnostic testing. nNO was reported in 49% of participants older than age 5, biopsy in 75%, and genetic testing in 58%; HSVA and EM were reported among many biopsy users. Diagnostic test use and recall varied by country, with recall generally lowest for biopsy and highest for nNO, and poorest recall reported in Switzerland. Among participants older than age 5, only 36% reported all three tests (nNO, biopsy, genetics), while others reported subsets or did not recall. Year of diagnosis after 2010 and situs abnormalities were strongly associated with reported testing, and country-related differences were observed in specific tests. The authors conclude that PCD diagnostics vary markedly worldwide and that many people have incomplete diagnostic work-up, emphasizing the need for clinicians to review tests and plan further testing to improve diagnostic characterization for personalized medicine.

A federal judge, Judge Reed O’Connor of the Northern District of Texas, rejected an effort to overturn the Biden administration’s gainful-employment rule and sided with the Education Department on every point. The rule required for-profit and certain nondegree programs to show that graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than a high school graduate, with programs failing tests for two consecutive years risking loss of federal financial aid, and it added new reporting requirements under a financial value transparency framework. The lawsuit began under Biden, and Trump officials had previously sought to scrap the regulations, while lawmakers passed new legislation requiring most college programs to be held accountable for student career outcomes, with how the Education Department carries out the test set to be handled through a rule-making process later this year.

Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share, compared with a year-ago loss. Adjusted earnings were 41 cents per share, meeting Wall Street expectations. Revenue was $5.74 billion, which missed forecasts. Halliburton shares were up more than 6 percent year-to-date and 10 percent over the past 12 months, while the S&P 500 has stayed nearly flat.

The passage reports that arrivals in the U.S. showed 19% fewer international students in the same month as 2024, which experts said aligns with enrollment predictions and reflects visa interview freezes. It notes limitations of the arrivals data, including it not counting students already in the U.S. who stayed over the summer or those entering in September. While another dataset (SEVIS) showed an unexpected 0.8% increase from September 2024 to September 2025, NAFSA criticized the figure as likely inaccurate. Experts warn the declines—estimated at least 19% and possibly higher—could have major effects on universities and local and national economies, with additional insights expected in mid-November from the Institute of International Education’s Fall Snapshot report.

The Third Circuit reviewed a district court’s second denial of Prava Chatterjee’s petition to vacate and set aside a settlement and release of an admiralty claim stemming from the January 31, 1975 S.S. Edgar M. Queeny–S.S. Corinthos collision. Chatterjee, the mother of the deceased seaman Pratik Kumar Chatterjee, argued the settlement and release were invalid because the special power of attorney authorizing her son-in-law, Anil Ranjan Ghosal, was forged or obtained fraudulently, and that evidentiary and procedural rulings denied her due process and a fair trial.

The court held that federal maritime law governs the validity of the release, but that the validity of the special power of attorney should be determined under Indian law. It also held that the “Garrett” careful scrutiny and the shipowner’s burden of proof apply to land-based family members seeking protection under the maritime “wardship” doctrine, shifting the burden to the shipowners to prove the release was executed freely, without deception or coercion, and with full understanding of rights.

Regarding procedure, the court found no due process violation in the denial of the former Calcutta Commission transcript (given hearsay/unavailability and lack of adequate cross-examination opportunity), but concluded the district court’s failure to authorize a new commission in India was a gross abuse of discretion that prevented Chatterjee from substantiating her allegations of forgery and fraud. The court vacated the district court’s order and remanded with directions to invoke a commission in India under Rule 28(b) to take testimony.

NAFTA is described as an unqualified success for Canada and its partners, supporting robust economic growth and transforming manufacturing by enabling regional production rationalization. The passage argues that Canada should prioritize modernizing NAFTA and address vulnerabilities shown by renegotiations: Canada exports too little outside North America and needs a stronger, more globally competitive manufacturing sector. It notes Canada has 14 FTAs, but exports to most markets have not expanded since signing. The passage says signing new deals alone will not ensure prosperity and calls for a five-part plan: improve Canada’s domestic business competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; ensure FTAs level the playing field by addressing non-tariff barriers; choose trade partners based on business fit rather than politics; leverage integrated supply chains (with most value-added exports described as production parts); and support the global expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises by consolidating export-support programs and improving access.

A New Delhi court deferred to July 6 the hearing on Enforcement Directorate (ED) charges against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in a money laundering case related to the Aircel-Maxis deal. The ED had filed its chargesheet on June 13 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ED said the CBI and ED are investigating Karti’s alleged role in getting FIPB clearance in 2006, when his father was Union Finance Minister, and alleged that CMSPL was promoted by Karti and ASCPL was set up on his directions. The ED claimed that Maxis invested Rs 3,565.91 crore while approvals were limited to Rs 600 crore at the time, and said CMSPL and ASCPL received specific amounts from Maxis and Aircel Televenture. The passage also mentions an earlier CBI chargesheet involving the Aircel takeover and that a special court dropped charges against Dayanidhi Maran and others due to lack of concrete evidence.

The speaker discusses a player’s likely status for tomorrow, saying they are not willing to provide details and that they don’t think fatigue is a factor. They comment on pride in their players, note that review of replays can be deemed inconclusive, and describe the team’s performance, stating they have won two series and two big home games plus a road game. They say distractions at home may have affected top players in the first period of last night, but express confidence. They add that the upcoming game follows two overtime games and that the team’s situation could have changed depending on overtime outcomes.

The speaker, returning from the Crimea Conference after a long trip, says it has been a fruitful start toward international peace and reports on military and political agreements. He argues that lasting results depend on the American Congress and people supporting the conclusions reached at Yalta. He describes continued Allied coordination, including daily exchange of information among Allied forces, to hasten Germany’s collapse and to maintain unconditional surrender as a condition that does not aim to destroy or enslave the German people. He outlines Yalta and Crimea outcomes for Germany’s occupation and control, the end of Nazism and militarism, and reparations in kind. He discusses international organization efforts for lasting peace, including a forthcoming United Nations conference in San Francisco on April 25, 1945, and proposes that voting procedures in the Security Council be settled in a fair solution. He also summarizes plans for liberated areas, joint responsibility of major powers, and specific settlements including Poland and the invitation for France to participate in postwar governance and international bodies. He notes that the conference focused on Europe but that plans for the fight against Japan continue, including preparations for Japan’s unconditional surrender. He concludes that the Crimea Conference should mark a shift toward universal international cooperation rather than unilateral action or spheres of influence.

Pokémon GO’s fire and ice-themed Solstice Event has been live for a little over a day, with spawn changes and reward tweaks ahead of the big anniversary event. For the next week, the game offers 3x XP for catching Pokémon, 3x XP for nice/great/excellent throws and curveballs/first throws, and a discounted Lucky Egg, resulting in 6x XP for catch-related actions. The event bonuses apply to catching and throwing but not evolving. The passage says the bonuses make catching feel satisfying and comparable to evolving for XP, while evolving does not benefit from special XP.

Theresa May has been warned that failing to deliver Brexit would be “catastrophic” for the Conservative Party ahead of a meeting of top ministers at Chequers. Conservative MPs Andrea Jenkyns and Jacob Rees-Mogg urged May to keep her promises, warning that compromising on Brexit “red lines” could lead to unrest and a “Brexit in name only.” Jenkyns said a “soft Brexit” would be a disaster, while Remain-supporting MPs argue a pragmatic approach is needed to avoid disruption at ports and issues around the Northern Ireland–Republic of Ireland border. Environment Secretary Michael Gove played down concerns that May would smudge her red lines and said cabinet would agree a united position on Brexit.

The passage describes a decade of strong U.S. stock market performance followed by signs that conditions are worsening in 2018. It notes the S&P 500 has quadrupled from crisis lows and reached all-time highs recently, but that new highs have been absent for over 60 trading days. It attributes part of the change to shifting monetary policy: the Federal Reserve has raised interest rates, is expected to raise further, and is shrinking its balance sheet, unlike earlier periods of volatility when central banks provided reassurance. The passage also highlights sustained increases in stock volatility, with the VIX remaining elevated after spiking in early February and higher volatility resembling past periods before major downturns. It further contrasts 2017’s low market movement with 2018’s higher frequency of large daily moves, arguing that markets may be entering a more challenging, potentially prolonged bear-market phase. The author concludes that markets managed to rise by policy makers are unhealthy, expects volatility to persist into 2019, and advises investors to look for risks not widely recognized.

The passage describes Jack Bogle–inspired Bogleheads 3 and 4 fund portfolio strategies, both built with low-cost index funds and intended for diversified, long-term “buy and hold” investing. The Bogleheads 3 portfolio uses three funds (U.S. total stock, international stock, and U.S. total bond) and is allocated 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, and 20% bonds in the article. The Bogleheads 4 portfolio adds an international bond fund to those three assets, allocated 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, 10% U.S. bonds, and 10% international bonds. It explains that market conditions can affect stock and bond performance, and includes backtest results using the article’s ticker allocations: the Bogleheads 3 portfolio had an annual return of 7.6% (with dividends reinvested) and a max drawdown of 28%, while the Bogleheads 4 portfolio had an annual return of 7.8% and a max drawdown of 31%.

The Caribbean Water and Wastewater Association (CWWA) is to hold its 26th Annual Conference and Exhibition in Guyana from October 16 to 20, following Cabinet approval. The event, themed “Promoting Innovation and Creativity in Water, Wastewater and Waste,” will feature technical papers on water, wastewater, and waste management, and include two high-level documents presented by a Caribbean minister. It will focus on water resource, quality, supply, management, and wastewater management, and is expected to attract over 250 delegates and more than 40 exhibitors. Minister of State Joseph Harmon said the forum will review a regional waste management action plan to be presented to the United Nations general assembly in December in Nairobi, Kenya. Minister of Communities Ronald Bulkan will lead Guyana’s delegation, and the conference will be held at the Guyana Marriott Hotel. Development partners include the Inter-American Development Bank, United Nations Environment, the Caribbean Development Bank, and PAHO.

The broadcast announces the beginning of a nationwide mobilization to provide security for citizens facing unemployment and privation during the coming winter.
