The speaker says success depends on the sympathetic and generous action of individuals and outlines a new national organization under Mr. Walter Gifford to coordinate with governors, state and local agencies, and national organizations in business, labor, welfare, churches, and fraternal and patriotic societies. The plan is to support existing local unemployment relief efforts through nationwide fundraising, including work programs, direct relief, and health and character-building measures. The Federal Government will expand public works to provide jobs and take additional measures affecting immigration and employment; states and localities will also expand public works and tax-supported relief. The speaker emphasizes that voluntary action must fill remaining needs to ensure no hunger or cold, calls on communities to rely on mutual self-help, and frames the effort as a test of human relations and individual responsibility. The speech also appeals for Thanksgiving Day on November 26 to reflect that communities have given assurance against hunger and cold. The speaker ends by referencing Yorktown and earlier sacrifices.

LG has introduced the LG V35 ThinQ, a premium smartphone and successor to the LG V30S ThinQ. It features a Qualcomm Snapdragon 845 processor, 6GB RAM, a 6-inch 2880 x 1440 pixel OLED display with Corning Gorilla Glass 5, no notch, and a headphone jack, with IP68 dust and water resistance and MIL-STD 810G testing. The phone includes a dual 16MP rear camera setup (one wide-angle lens) and an 8MP front camera, with ThinQ AI features in the camera app for scene selection, portrait mode, and low-light photography. It supports Google Lens and “Super Far Field Voice Recognition” for Google Assistant interaction up to 16 feet away, and includes a 32-bit Hi-Fi Quad DAC (7.1 channel audio), a 3,300 mAh battery, Bluetooth 5.0, NFC, 802.11ac WiFi, and a USB 2.0 Type-C port. It offers face recognition and fingerprint support, Qualcomm Quick Charge 3.0, and storage models of 64GB or 128GB with microSD expansion up to 2TB. LG says it will be available alongside the LG G7 ThinQ, but pricing and release date have not been announced.

The lecture previews upcoming course deadlines, including a problem set due today, a short next problem set, a first quiz on statistical basics through statistical process control and control charting, and a separate lecture on yield modeling. The main focus is a brief review connecting control charting to hypothesis testing, explaining false alarm rate (alpha), missed alarm probability (beta), and average run length (ARL). It describes how control limits are set using alpha, how beta and ARL depend on the sample size and shift size, and how changing sample size tightens distributions and affects beta while keeping alpha fixed. The discussion also emphasizes that an out-of-control signal alone cannot distinguish false alarms from true alarms and that alarms require investigation. The lecture then shifts to process capability, contrasting control limits with specification limits, introducing tolerances and quality loss functions, and defining CP and CPK based on how process spread and mean location relate to spec limits. It concludes by discussing limitations of X-bar charts and introducing alternative control chart approaches for faster detection and continuous/near-continuous sampling, including moving average, exponentially weighted moving average, and cumulative sum charts, which will be covered next time.

Drug repurposing (repositioning/reprofiling) identifies new therapeutic uses for existing drugs developed for different indications, reducing time and cost of development; it accounts for about one-third of drug approvals and nearly 25% of pharmaceutical sector revenue. In rare diseases, it is emphasized as significant due to limited treatment options, small patient populations, delays in accessing therapies, and the established safety profiles of known drugs; the passage also states that drug repurposing should have high success probability because known rare diseases outnumber druggable targets.

The passage describes knowledge graphs as graph representations of biomedical entities (e.g., drugs, genes, diseases) and their relationships, integrating associations such as protein-protein interactions, drug indications/toxicities/targets, disease symptoms, biomarkers, and protein-disease associations. Elsevier’s Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG) is built from open access and controlled access literature using proprietary AI/NLP methods that extract and annotate relationships with supporting sentences and reference identifiers. EBKG supports a disease-centric repurposing workflow by scoring proteins important to disease mechanisms and then ranking drugs that modulate those proteins.

Results presented compare open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) contributions to EBKG relevant to drug repurposing for rare diseases, showing roughly equal contributions at the level of knowledge graph relations, with OA relations exceeding 50% for rare-disease repurposing. The passage further reports that most relations in both OA and CA are supported by a single reference, that CA-only facts increase over time but at a slower rate than OA, and that citation rates and first-citation timing for relations do not differ substantially between OA and CA. It argues that the accumulation of single-reference (often uncited) relations is mainly due to lack of follow-up rather than discovery of fraudulent research, and concludes that additional confidence scores beyond the number of supporting references are needed.

Managed by Q (“Q”) is a 15-month-old on-demand office cleaning and maintenance company led by Dan Teran, which aims to provide customers with clean floors and windows as well as whatever they need to manage their physical office space. After launching in New York in April 2014 and later expanding to Chicago and San Francisco following a Series A raise, Q used a technology platform (including a wall-mounted iPad and cleaner app) to offer transparent, trackable cleaning and maintenance services, with office managers able to request tasks, monitor work, and communicate feedback. The company hired and trained “operators” rather than relying on subcontractors, and it implemented compensation, benefits, hiring, and training processes designed to maintain quality and reduce turnover. Q also emphasizes culture, transparency, ongoing customer feedback, and community, while Teran is deciding how best to grow—either by entering new markets or by expanding services in existing ones without compromising its business model.

President Donald Trump will deliver his first State of the Union address Tuesday night, with lawmakers using the event to make political points. Many Democratic women plan to wear black in solidarity with the #MeToo movement amid sexual harassment allegations and related Capitol Hill investigations, and some invited sexual assault victims as guests. Dozens of young immigrants, including people protected under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, will sit in the gallery to highlight immigration policy, while other lawmakers have invited guests connected to border wall development. At least eight Democratic lawmakers announced they are boycotting the address. Bill Nye is also listed as a guest, invited by Republican Rep. Jim Bridenstine, and Democratic lawmakers have criticized Bridenstine’s nomination to lead NASA. Rep. Joe Kennedy will deliver the Democratic response, with Democratic leaders presenting him as a champion of policies for the middle class.

Iraq has begun an aerial bombardment of Tal Afar, a town under Islamic State control west of Mosul, according to al-Sumariya TV and an Iraqi Defence Ministry spokesman. A ground attack to take the city is to start after the air campaign ends. Tal Afar is described as the next target in the war against Islamic State, whose self-proclaimed “caliphate” effectively collapsed last month after U.S.-backed Iraqi forces recaptured Mosul. The passage also notes that Tal Afar had about 200,000 residents before falling to Islamic State, has seen sectarian violence between Sunnis and Shi’ites since 2003, and has produced senior Islamic State commanders.

The Sarahah app has quickly gained popularity on social media over the past week, though it is a few months old and has already been a hit in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, according to a BBC report. The app lets users create profiles that can receive anonymous messages, which appear in an inbox where they can be flagged, deleted, replied to, or favorited. Messages are anonymous by default, though users can choose to tag their identity. Reviews on Google Play show a near 50-50 split, and some reviews warn about hurtful or hateful comments. The developers are adding privacy options such as removing profiles from search results and limiting commenting to logged-in users, and users can block senders. Sarahah is barebones, focused on anonymous messaging rather than social interaction, and is available free on Android and iOS.

The passage lists multiple telegram entries dated from January 8, 1942 to September 3, 1942, with locations including Washington, Helsinki, Kuibyshev (Moscow), Ankara, Stockholm, and London. Each entry includes a time of sending (e.g., noon, 3 p.m., 7 p.m.) and, in many cases, a received time (e.g., “Received 5:51 p.m.”). The entries are labeled with different document or reference numbers and frequently include “European War 1939” classifications.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output. It uses a high-speed current-feedback input stage with an internally matched gain resistor network and a four-resistor differential amplifier output stage. The device offers eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V via three digital gain-selection pins (A0, A1, A2), and is intended for applications including factory automation and control, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test.  

Its linear operating input voltage range extends to within 3V (maximum) of either power supply, with common-mode rejection maintained across this range at all temperatures. Linear operating input common-mode range limits depend on input common-mode voltage, input differential voltage, gain, and reference input voltage.  

One described typical application drives a single-ended-input SAR ADC (ADS8860) using independent input and output power supplies, with REF6250 as the ADC voltage reference and OPA192 buffering the PGA848 reference. The input includes multiple filters to reduce interference/noise, support ADC settling and distortion performance, and maintain stability, resulting in a nominal f–3dB bandwidth of 318 kHz (277 kHz at the high side of feedback resistor tolerance).  

Power supply recommendations specify nominal performance with ±15V supplies for the input and output stages, and operation within specified limits without compromising performance. Supply voltages higher than 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. The layout section provides guidelines to ensure matched inputs, use local supply bypassing, reduce parasitic coupling/leakage (especially at DA_IN+ and DA_IN–), minimize thermal junctions, and consider thermal placement.

A police detective in eastern Missouri’s Washington was exposed to fentanyl while trying to save an overdose victim. He gave Narcan and began rescue breaths, during which he inhaled drugs the man had snorted, described as heroin mixed with fentanyl. Afterward, he reported a headache, lightheadedness, and tingling in his hands. Both the patient and the detective were taken to the hospital and are okay. Police say heroin mixed with powerful fentanyl is increasingly seen and can be very dangerous to first responders.

The passage describes why tungsten is considered a preferred plasma-facing material for fusion devices, but notes that it oxidizes readily in air, causing material loss and dispersion of tungsten oxide as sublimated species or dust spalled from oxide scales. Oxidation is expected to be a concern when tungsten is above 500°C and exposed to air during accident, maintenance, waste handling, or detritiation scenarios. The study aims to understand long-duration oxidation and the microstructure of the resulting oxide scale, using long-duration dry-air oxidation experiments, TGA/DSC (including tungsten trioxide sublimation), and characterization methods including microscopy, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and EBSD. The results report a transition from parabolic to linear oxidation kinetics across tested temperatures, preferential oxidation at specimen edges, oxide spalling and crack/void formation at higher temperatures, and a three-layer oxide microstructure identified by Raman spectroscopy: an inner ~30–50 nm WO2 layer, a middle 10–20 µm WO2.72 layer, and an outer WO2.9/WO3 layer. The presence of the WO2 layer is discussed as a possible contributor to low detritiation efficiency observed for JET tungsten components.

A court in Barrie heard from the parents of 16-year-old Joey Tanner, who was stabbed to death by Joseph Nicholson on Father’s Day in 2007. Nicholson was originally sentenced to life in prison for first-degree murder with no parole for 25 years, but the Ontario Court of Appeal ordered a new sentence for second-degree murder because the jury instruction was inadequate; second-degree murder carries no parole for 10 to 25 years. The Crown asked to set Nicholson’s parole eligibility at 16 years, citing his violent criminal record and behavior in prison. Nicholson apologized and asked for a chance to rehabilitate. The family said the decision has caused them to rehash their pain, and Justice Guy Di Tomaso will impose sentence Aug. 11.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo High School graduate and full-time psychology student with a minor in studio art, describes her fourth installment of a six-part study abroad series in Florence, Italy. She reports that her Italian classes are advancing, her art work continues with multiple on-site painting and drawing projects using various mediums, and she participates in university cultural activities such as cooking classes and day trips to Siena, Pisa, and Lucca. She also recounts traveling to seven countries in 10 days during spring break, visiting multiple museums and cities, including stops in Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Germany, and Switzerland, with a notable trip to Becherbach tied to her ancestry. After returning to Florence, she notes the start of the tourist season, her return to classes, and a later trip to Split, Croatia, including rafting, cliff diving, and stops at Braĉ and Krka National Park. She marks reaching 20 countries by age 20 and describes the remaining time in Florence before final exams and departure.

About 1.2 million Australian families are eligible for childcare subsidies, but from July 2 489,000 will miss out unless they switch to a new system. The Turnbull Government is replacing the current Child Care Rebate and Child Care Benefit with a single means- and activity-tested payment. Families must update Centrelink details through myGov, including estimated income for 2018/19 and each parent’s approximate work or activity hours, and both parents must meet at least eight hours per fortnight of approved activity. The annual cap for rebates will be removed for households earning under $186,958 and will increase for higher incomes. The passage also outlines subsidy payment percentages based on income tiers, required activity hours for subsidised care hours, what counts as an activity, hourly rate caps by childcare type, exemptions, additional subsidies, and a $1.2 billion safety net. It warns that children must be immunised or have an exemption to receive subsidies and lists steps to take before July 2.

Jeffing is a fitness method created in the 1970s by Olympian Jeff Galloway. Also called the run-walk-run method, it alternates running with short planned walking breaks during a single workout or race to make exercise more manageable. Dr John Gallucci Jr says its main benefits include improved aerobic endurance with reduced exhaustion, built-in muscle recovery between running intervals, and feeling less intimidating to help people maintain consistency and avoid burnout. Beginners are advised to start by running 1–2 minutes and walking 1–2 minutes, then gradually extend running intervals while keeping breaks as needed. Gallucci notes Jeffing can reduce physical stress and lower overuse injury vulnerability, can help experienced runners maintain pace on long runs and during recovery weeks, and may be less suitable for athletes requiring sustained high-intensity effort without breaks. He cautions that improper progression or poor running mechanics can still lead to injuries, and recommends starting with a comfortable, sustainable pace and interval.

The passage surveys how matroid theory connects combinatorics with algebraic, geometric, and topological methods. It describes matroids via their ground set, independent sets, bases, circuits, rank function, and lattice of flats, and it introduces multinets as partitions of a matroid’s ground set equipped with multiplicities and connectivity conditions. The survey outlines related structures such as nets, reduced multinets, and connections to Latin squares and finite groups, including questions about when 3-nets are algebraic.

It then introduces algebraic invariants associated to matroids and (when relevant) to hyperplane arrangements: the Orlik–Solomon algebra, holonomy Lie algebra, holonomy Chen Lie algebra, resonance varieties, and Koszul modules, including how these invariants reflect matroid dependencies and relate to the topology of arrangement complements. The paper’s organization is given: Section 2 covers matroids and multinets, Section 3 defines Orlik–Solomon and holonomy Lie algebras, Section 4 studies resonance varieties and links to Koszul modules and Chen ranks, and Section 5 connects these invariants to hyperplane arrangement topology.

The passage describes the last trading day of the month as a weak and negative seasonality period for stocks, noting it is the last trading day rather than the last calendar day. Using S&P 500 (SPY) results from 1993 onward, it reports an average loss of about 0.06% per trade with a negative annual CAGR of about 0.8% when investing on the close of the second last trading day and selling at the close of the last trading day. It also states that exiting on the open of the last trading day produces an average gain of about 0.04% and that the open-to-close performance on the last trading day is poor, with an average gain of about -0.11% and a low win ratio of 42%. The passage adds there is no end-of-month effect on the last trading day because it performs significantly worse than any random day, and it suggests profit-taking as a possible reason while highlighting that a strategy based on the last trading day has been developed.

Sharon Haliwell, a 48-year-old wife of a Wigan millionaire businessman, died by suicide at her home last April after being addicted to sleeping pills, according to a coroner. An inquest heard that her husband Darren had abused her and that concerns existed about communication between teams within North West Boroughs NHS Foundation trust. Prof Jennifer Leeming said Haliwell had mentioned suicidal tendencies to two services within two weeks but was not considered “high risk.” The trust’s chief executive, Simon Barber, said efforts were made to improve “connectivity” between teams, including training for IAPT staff and work to flag when patients receive help from multiple teams. He also said standard operating procedures would be amended by March 2018 to ensure clinicians act on “red flag” alerts and share clinical information. The inquest also heard she had triage and a second mental health assessment in February, but an error meant she was not referred for counselling by an advanced nurse practitioner. The coroner issued a prevention of death notice, expressing ongoing concern despite improvements.

The passage discusses the intensity of playing for the Stanley Cup, describing how deterioration and fatigue are overcome by adrenaline once game time starts. It says the team has not yet won a game but has rebounded and performed strongly, citing experienced key players and noting that lines that have played together are working well due to familiarity. It also argues that Joe is playing well despite not scoring in the first games, pointing to his line’s time in the offensive zone and his overall contributions to generating scoring chances.

Anna Ryder Richardson says the stresses and expense of running Manor House Wildlife Park have destroyed her 16-year marriage to Colin MacDougall. She is divorcing him and preparing to leave the zoo and animals for good, moving to a dilapidated farmhouse in France with her daughters, Bibi and Dixie. Richardson previously enjoyed her work with exotic animals—including rare Sumatran tigers—described as “the best therapy,” and the zoo’s renovation and life there were followed on Channel 4’s *Chaos At The Zoo* and other TV appearances. She later says the park became overwhelming, with constant financial and operational pressure, loss of privacy due to filming and public attention, and costs following an August 2010 incident in which a tree fell and injured a young visitor and his mother. She says she is rebuilding her life, learning French, and returning to television to co-present *60 Minute Makeover* while Colin continues to manage the wildlife park.

The passage describes Tiffany Gholston’s support for the American Heart Association’s Go Red For Women campaign. Born with a heart murmur, which caused a slow heart rate and low energy, she did not outgrow it and received her first pacemaker at age 20. She highlights that the surgery was minimally intrusive and mentions managing her health through staying active, eating well, and meditating each morning. Tiffany is also involved with the American Heart Association’s Circle of Red, working to spread awareness and raise money for ongoing research that she says helped save her life.

Hackers who broke into HBO’s computer network have released additional unaired episodes of several popular HBO shows, including “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers,” and “The Deuce,” but the latest leak did not include “Game of Thrones.” HBO said it was not communicating with the hacker and would not comment on each new release, adding that the hacker may continue posting stolen information to gain media attention. Earlier this summer, HBO acknowledged the hack and said thieves were leaking stolen materials and seeking a multi-million-dollar ransom. The incident occurred as Time Warner awaited regulatory approval for its proposed $85.4 billion sale to AT&T.

The passage is a list of headlines and brief descriptions related to education news and commentary. It references topics including reopening an all-girls camp after west Texas floods, teens responding to the L.A. fires, an American Idol winner named Jamal Roberts, lawsuits involving youth vaping, school supply debt, COVID vaccine support, school integration and related documentaries, and multiple items about education policy, state accountability under the Every Student Succeeds Act, and school innovations.

The passage advises users of Galaxy Fold phones to unfold or view in full screen for the best experience. It describes compensation and that product ratings are not influenced by compensation. It then promotes credit card offers, focusing on the Wells Fargo Active Cash card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 spend in the first 3 months, a 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, a $0 annual fee, and cell phone protection up to $600 with a $25 deductible, with approval most likely for applicants with good credit (670+). The passage also lists features for the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards card, including unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% cash back on certain travel booked through Capital One Travel, welcome bonuses, a $0 annual fee, and a 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers, followed by a variable APR. It further includes general disclaimers that falling within the recommended credit range does not guarantee approval.

Researchers in a PLOS Biology paper report that temperature changes during intense exercise signal appetite suppression through TRPV1-like receptors in arcuate nucleus (ARC) proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons. In mouse hypothalamus tissue, capsaicin and heat activated POMC neurons via receptors present in about two-thirds of these neurons. In mice, infusing capsaicin into the ARC reduced food intake over 12 hours, and blocking or silencing the TRPV1-like receptors prevented this effect. After treadmill exercise, mice reduced food intake by about 50%; this reduction did not occur in mice whose ARC POMC neurons lacked TRPV1 receptors. The study suggests body temperature can regulate feeding behavior and may inform new approaches to appetite suppression or weight loss.

The Texas Department of Labor and Standards sued under the Health Spa Act to enforce obligations secured by a letter of credit for which American Savings Bank was the surety on Anna Black. The trial court ruled for the Department, and the court of appeals affirmed. On appeal, Black argued the trial court erred by allowing documentary evidence not timely identified in response to an interrogatory. The appellate court held there was no abuse of discretion in finding good cause under Tex. R. Civ. P. 215.5 and distinguished Sharp v. Broadway Nat’l Bank as applying only to witnesses. The Supreme Court denied the application for writ of error, stating it should not be construed as approving the distinction and that its action should not relieve a party of the duty to show good cause in the record under Tex. R. Civ. P. 215.5.

Researchers propose using a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs) from within the Milky Way. They say participating phones would continuously listen and record candidate FRBs, periodically upload data to a central processing site to correlate signals and identify a globe-encompassing event. GPS-based pulse arrival times would provide the FRB sky position, and pulse timing across frequencies would yield dispersion measure to estimate the source distance within the Galaxy. The researchers note that FRBs have been detected at mobile and Wi‑Fi frequencies and estimate the Milky Way could host an FRB every 30 to 1,500 years, or more frequently if bursts repeat.

McLaren says the reliability problems that affected its pre-season testing in Barcelona have been addressed, and the team is heading into the Formula 1 season opener in Australia confident of a step forward. Testing issues included a wheel nut failure, battery problems, a loose exhaust, and overheating bodywork. Racing director Eric Boullier says the team has worked on these issues at its Woking base, while Fernando Alonso says the new Renault-powered MCL33 showed promise but needs more development. Both Alonso and Boullier acknowledge that performance at the first race cannot be predicted and that the midfield battle is close.

The speaker describes winning his first Stanley Cup after eight years in the league, saying it was a long, difficult journey with many hockey games and minutes. He praises teammates and leaders in the dressing room, and specifically mentions Larry Murphy as an exceptional player. He credits support from Scotty, his family, and his six-year-old daughter Dasha, and says he feels healthy and motivated to play another series. He also discusses the Stanley Cup final’s international interest, particularly in Russia, and proposes bringing the Cup to Moscow to help generate interest and investment in Russian hockey.

Early National Weather Service forecasts suggest the weather in the Philadelphia area next Monday for a partial solar eclipse is uncertain. Lance Frank said seven days out is at the edge of forecast time, with unsettled weather likely to affect areas farther south, and forecasts from Friday should be more reliable. Philadelphia is not in the path of totality; the nearest state is South Carolina. The eclipse is expected to first become visible in Oregon, and NASA reports totality in Charleston at 2:48 p.m. ET. The last total eclipse visible in the United States was in 1979.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2017. It reported that Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017, and furnished the press release as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also states that the information in the report, including Exhibit 99.1, is not deemed filed for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except as expressly set forth. Exhibit 99.1 and the signature of Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer, are included.

The passage describes systems and methods for adaptive radiotherapy that update radiotherapy treatment plans and/or radiation delivery during or based on real-time imaging data. It explains that imaging acquired during treatment can be used to extract biological/physiological/anatomical data (including PET, MRI, SPECT, CT, ultrasound, and others) and to evaluate whether to proceed with a prescribed plan using parameters such as geometrical changes, tracer uptake (e.g., SUVs), plan quality index (PQI), and dose-volume histogram (DVH) metrics against clinician-defined acceptable ranges. The passage further details examples of plan adaptations based on biological activity data (e.g., hypoxia or HER2 tracer uptake thresholds, altering dosimetric objectives, target geometry, fractionation, and session duration/number), and methods for generating bounded DVH curves (min/max DVH) for plan evaluation and notifications. It also outlines adaptive workflow categories: adaptive radiotherapy based on real-time data, online adaptive radiotherapy (adaptation between or at the start of sessions using current imaging), real-time adaptive radiotherapy (multiple updates during a session), and offline adaptive planning (using data from prior sessions). Finally, it describes system components such as an imaging system, radiation treatment system, a controller, and a clinician interface with tiered notifications (e.g., GO/NO GO, PASS/FAIL, and recommendations).

Huddersfield opened their Super League season with a 28-16 win over Widnes Vikings, following a 12-0 pre-season victory at Warrington Wolves. The team is entering their next match against Salford Red Devils at the John Smith’s Stadium with early momentum, and head coach Rick Stone said the players must build on their positive start and remember it is only the beginning.

The passage lists English versions of reports and materials related to the 1945 San Francisco Conference and the United Nations Charter. It describes a compilation designed as a bridge between the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the Charter, focusing on the role of the United States in establishing the UN’s legal framework and presenting the American Delegation’s positions on issues and informal decision-making among major powers. The documentation is organized chronologically from early 1945 through signing on June 26 and covers four phases—policy development, negotiation, debates, and drafting—drawing on minutes from U.S. delegation meetings and informal coordination among the “Big Four” and “Big Five.” The compilation also notes that many records are informal notes, includes various forms of selected documentation from U.S. sources, makes occasional deletions to save space, and states that documents were gathered from multiple archives and collections.

On March 22, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC. NVIDIA will pay $500 million and receive 12,108,715 shares of NVIDIA common stock. Additional shares may be delivered to NVIDIA by Barclays at settlement, or NVIDIA may be required to deliver shares or elect to make a cash payment, depending on the average daily volume-weighted average price during the agreement term. The repurchase is part of NVIDIA’s intention to return $1 billion to shareholders through quarterly cash dividends and share repurchases in the current fiscal year.

The speakers discuss team strategy and player availability during a playoff series. They say their approach in the third period is to shorten play and keep players from coming to the bench tired, so they can perform better when shifts roll. They describe line and matchup focus, including rotating shutdown coverage based on who is producing against certain opponents, and emphasize that players must know who they will face. They discuss injury disclosure practices, saying they do not share specific injury areas to protect the player and team, and that they aim to provide clear status on whether players are in or out; they state that one player (brett) is believed not to be a player tomorrow. They also describe managing minutes for keane and giving options to skate. The speakers discuss working with brett hull’s style by allowing creativity with the puck while requiring physical, team-oriented play without full possession. They emphasize mental and physical sacrifices after a prior loss, the importance of blocking shots, and the need to maintain composure in intense goal situations. They conclude with expectations about hogue’s progress and whether benny can play, and they note peca as a dangerous offensive player whom they want to keep away from their net.

Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips for AMD in Intel’s foundry business, according to a Semafor report. Intel shares rose 7% and AMD shares were up over 1% after the news. The report says an AMD customer would be a significant win for Intel Foundry and could signal to other chip companies that Intel can handle their business, while also indicating AMD’s confidence in manufacturing with its biggest competitor. It is unclear how much manufacturing AMD would do with Intel, and Intel declined to comment while AMD said it does not comment on rumor or speculation.

The passage compiles Enron-related references and several news reports dated May 18, 2001. One Dow Jones column argues that California’s long-term power contracts may lose value because state Republicans did not back a $12.5 billion bond deal; it describes falling forward power prices and notes California may still buy summer power at lower prices while avoiding blackouts. A separate options report says volatility is near recent lows, yet many investors continue selling options for income, citing examples involving Ericsson and Microsoft. Multiple reports describe Saudi Arabia selecting international oil companies for three major natural gas “core ventures,” totaling about $25 billion, with Exxon Mobil and Shell receiving major roles; Shell says it is pleased to participate in core ventures 1 and 3, and the U.S. Energy Department says it welcomed the selection of American firms and said it aligns with the administration’s energy plan. Additional detail notes that Saudi Arabia would announce leaders for core ventures 1 and 3 by June 5 and that memoranda of understanding are expected in early June.

Steven J. Kean tells James Hughes that Enron believes it may be playing a smaller role than indicated by a Wall Street Journal article, and describes budget cuts for 2001 after discussions about OPIC, ExIm, and other funding organizations. He says John will continue project finance work related to existing projects, pursued projects, and transfer issues from asset sales, and asks if Hughes agrees. In a reply, John Hardy says this is not a fight to pursue against OMB, but that Enron needs to show support for agencies and their budgets, and notes negotiations with EXIM and OPIC on Electrobolt and Rebecca McDonald’s role on EXIM’s private sector advisory committee.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 18, 2019, reporting the issuance of a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing states that the information in the Current Report, including Exhibit 99.1, is not deemed “filed” and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except as specifically referenced. The report includes Exhibit 99.1 and is signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage describes the “Stack Offense,” which compacts players into two stack alignments just outside the free throw line to keep possession with three ball handlers while two posts act as stationary screeners. It outlines rotation and continuity after an initial dribble penetration to a wing: if the dribbler cannot beat the defender, the ball is passed to another handler who pops off a post screen, with options to penetrate either wing and trigger the next pop via stationary screens. It also covers basket roll and back cut options when defenders overplay or deny passes, including quick rolls to the basket, post rolls for layups or drop passes, and back cuts to the basket with post step-outs. It concludes with resetting stack alignment at the free throw line and giving O1 options to dribble penetrate to either wing.

The passage describes a study in the United States showing STIs remain a major public health problem, disproportionately affecting marginalized groups, and causing substantial health and economic burdens. It focuses on Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT), a CDC-endorsed strategy to facilitate treatment for sexual partners of STI patients, noting inconsistent implementation due to pharmacist awareness and misconceptions, and limited knowledge about whether electronically prescribed EPT medications are fillable.

The study’s objective was to assess accessibility of electronically prescribed “nameless” EPT in New York City pharmacies using a secret shopper methodology and to examine whether EPT acceptance varies with neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability (CDC Social Vulnerability Index socioeconomic subcomponent). A cross-sectional observational audit surveyed 335 pharmacies within the Mount Sinai Health System catchment area, recording whether pharmacists dispensed EPT, payment method, counseling, interaction time, and reasons for refusal. Pharmacies were sampled randomly, with categorization by chain type, and neighborhood vulnerability was linked by census tract.

Results reported that 40% of pharmacists were aware of EPT and willingness to dispense nameless EPT prescriptions was 30%. Awareness was higher in national chain pharmacies than non-chain pharmacies, and EPT awareness increased with higher socioeconomic vulnerability quartiles; however, socioeconomic vulnerability was not associated with willingness to dispense. Common reasons for refusal included unfamiliarity with EPT and belief that a patient name was legally required. Only 46% of dispensed prescriptions met New York State guideline-concordant practices. The passage concludes that pharmacy-level barriers to EPT implementation include limited awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor adherence to guidelines, emphasizing the need for targeted education, policy interventions, and electronic prescribing integration.

First Lady Melania Trump said combating bullying among children was a top priority at the UN General Assembly last month. In Union County, Horace Maynard Middle School principal Greg Clay said he was not aware of repeated bullying of sixth-grader Keaton Jones and that the incident shown in a viral video had been resolved weeks earlier, with action taken involving other children. The video was posted by Jones’ mother, Kimberly Jones, who said she picked her son up early because he was afraid to go to lunch. The school planned an assembly to address bullying and an anti-bullying talk in January, and media would not be allowed to attend. Other parents said bullying can occur but did not believe it was more prevalent in their district than elsewhere.

The passage describes hardware-aware AI/ML model searching and swapping techniques to reduce resource consumption and improve model performance under changing hardware and environmental conditions. It introduces an ML model scaling (MLMS) system with an MLMS engine and a performance auditor that monitor inference quality and context information (such as hardware modes, system state, physical environment, and networking conditions). When monitored metrics indicate a status change, the system triggers a subnet search and selects a replacement subnet from a subnet pool. Efficiency is achieved using similarity-based subnet selection that picks a replacement subnet with the most overlap in pre-trained parameters to minimize memory write overhead and data transfer energy. The system is agnostic to the specific model search/NAS approach and can use weight-sharing and elastic supernet/subnet structures. The passage also outlines example performance metrics, context information types, a two-stage search and swap algorithm, and several potential use cases including edge/IoT deployments, drones, and federated/distributed learning scenarios.

The passage discusses globalization as a widely used but often ill-defined concept, describing it as increasingly interconnected social life in a “global village.” It argues that globalization affects education policies and English curricula, and that English can serve as an international language for communication and global engagement. The text provides examples of how globalization education is addressed through international organizations and country-specific policies (including Switzerland, Japan, and China), and it suggests incorporating global issues into English teaching materials.

A study involving 372 adult university students in Taiwan used surveys and interviews, group discussions, films, online resources, and social media to explore globalization education through topics such as global warming, global health issues (HIV/AIDS), and diverse perspectives on war. Survey results report that students view global issues as important, sometimes urgent, and feel increased confidence communicating about global topics in English, while learning about diverse cultures. Students also supported including global subjects in formal curricula and proposed additional topics ranging from environmental protection to human rights and economic impacts of globalization. The conclusion emphasizes that English teachers should help students become prepared for international intercultural situations and suggests using students’ fields of expertise to design syllabi connected to global issues.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend focused on simplifying a facial routine to a few high-quality, well-chosen products. Expert Dr Hazel Parkinson says it encourages using targeted, multitasking products that support the skin barrier and avoids layering many active ingredients that can compete or clash. She recommends barrier-friendly routines and mentions ingredients such as niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, peptides, and targeted actives like azelaic acid, salicylic acid, or retinoids depending on concerns. While many people can benefit from a balanced, barrier-friendly approach, she notes it may need adjustment for conditions like acne, pigmentation, sensitive skin, hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and menopausal skin changes. She advises introducing actives cautiously, easing into changes by removing one or two products at a time, and consulting a professional if needed. The passage also claims skinimalism can reduce irritation, sensitivity, waste, packaging, and budget strain.

In August 2014, Rosie Hagopian and other Market Basket employees arrived at work unpaid after the company’s board fired CEO Arthur T. Demoulas and reinstated him with full operational authority only hours earlier. The firing followed a long family dispute over ownership and governance between Arthur T. and his rival cousin Arthur S. Demoulas. Employees, joined by some vendors and customers, had protested and walked out for six weeks demanding Arthur T.’s reinstatement, which shut down store support and halted deliveries. The conflict included board actions, executive resignations, and widespread effects on sales, customers, suppliers, and nearby businesses. In late August 2014, the board and shareholders agreed to a buyout that restored Arthur T. and his management team; the company resumed operations, though observers questioned whether it could sustain low prices and high employee benefits while carrying significant debt.

Neurobehavioural comorbidities in epilepsy reduce quality of life, but their fluctuating burden is difficult to monitor outside hospital-based snapshots. Smartphones may objectively track day-to-day neurobehavioural patterns. The authors report a single late-20s man studied in a six-month prospective cohort (NCT04617418), using the TapCounter app to record touchscreen interaction timestamps and a seizure diary, with data transferred to a cloud server. During May–November 2021, 718,357 touchscreen interactions were recorded over 185 days while his anti-seizure medications (lamotrigine and perampanel) were reduced before admission and withdrawn during admission; he also had video-EEG-confirmed seizures during a five-day EMU evaluation. Using touchscreen inter-touch interval distributions and cluster-based permutation tests, they found significant changes in interaction dynamics during ASM tapering versus pre- and post-tapering periods, with fast dynamics increasing during tapering and reversing after medication restart. They also found touchscreen dynamics differed on the day of a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion compared with the three preceding days, with slow dynamics increasing on the convulsion day. The discussion suggests touchscreen tracking could help monitor medication and seizure-related behavioural changes that questionnaires and self-reports may miss, and notes that the study did not evaluate effects of focal seizures.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018. The report includes unaudited financial statements: income statement results for three months ended September 30, 2018 and 2017, comprehensive income, balance sheets as of September 30, 2018 and June 30, 2018, cash flows for the three months ended September 30, 2018 and 2017, and stockholders’ equity statements. For the quarter, Microsoft reported total revenue of $29.084 billion (up from $24.538 billion), operating income of $9.955 billion (up from $7.708 billion), and net income of $8.824 billion (up from $6.576 billion), with diluted earnings per share of $1.14. Notes describe accounting policies (including recast items), earnings per share, other income/expense, investments and fair value measurements, derivatives, inventories, the GitHub acquisition agreement, goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes (including effects of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and uncertain tax positions), unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, share repurchases, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment and geographic information. The report also contains an independent registered public accounting firm’s review of the interim financial information and a management discussion and analysis section with forward-looking statements and discussion of results of operations.

The passage says the 2022 NFL draft included a record 6 wide receivers taken in the first 20 picks, arguing that wide receivers are increasingly valuable because offenses are more pass-focused. It describes wide receivers as key to the passing game by running routes, getting open, and securing catches, while also requiring mental and physical toughness for limited touches and physical plays. It notes wide receivers also perform run blocking, including holding perimeter blocks. It explains the name “wide receiver” as coming from their wide split near the sideline and their role in receiving QB passes, and lists related terms (WR, wideout, split-end, flanker). It provides skills (route-running, run-blocking, body control, speed, strong hands, coordination, agility) and an estimated body type range (height 5’10–6’4, weight 180–220, lean build). It highlights Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent as top historical players. Finally, it argues elite wide receivers disrupt defenses by drawing attention across the field and forcing defensive alignment decisions that help offensive game planning.

Perovskite solar cells have improved rapidly to over 27% power conversion efficiency, but their performance and stability depend on the microscopic morphology of perovskite thin films. Because film morphology is polycrystalline and includes features such as grain size, grain boundaries, defects, and residual lead(II) iodide, accurate SEM-based characterization is needed; however, manual SEM interpretation is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. The passage introduces PerovSegNet, a lightweight deep-learning segmentation framework for SEM images of perovskite and lead iodide, built on YOLOv8-seg and enhanced with two modules: ASDCB for multi-scale feature fusion and boundary localization, and SAD for downsampling that preserves fine textures and large-scale structures. The authors construct the PerovData dataset with 10,994 augmented, manually labeled SEM images and use UMAP to verify feature separability among perovskite, lead iodide, and defect classes. Experiments on this dataset report improved segmentation performance over baseline models and show that the two modules jointly improve accuracy, especially for defect regions, while maintaining computational efficiency. PerovSegNet outputs per-image masks and quantitative descriptors (e.g., area and counts) that are used to relate microstructural descriptors to photovoltaic performance, and the paper concludes with prospects for process optimization and higher-throughput or real-time quality control in perovskite manufacturing.

The passage describes a University of Connecticut study suggesting that vaping nicotine-based e-cigarette liquid may cause DNA damage comparable to smoking unfiltered tobacco cigarettes. Using a 3D-printed “organ on a chip” electro-optical screening device, researchers measured DNA damage after exposure to vaping, with damage increasing from 20 to 100 puffs. The findings are presented as evidence that DNA damage could contribute to cancer and that toxicity may vary with inhaled vapor and other additives. The work is published in ACS Sensors, and the researchers plan additional 3D-printed bio-analytical platforms for toxicity screening and cancer diagnostics.

The passage explains how to backtest a momentum trading strategy in Python. It defines momentum as an asset’s trend, where rising assets have positive momentum and declining assets have negative momentum. The strategy downloads historical adjusted close prices for select sectors SPDR ETFs using yfinance, resamples them monthly, and computes monthly percentage changes. Momentum is calculated as each ETF’s rolling past 9-month performance. Trading rules are implemented by selecting the top 3 ETFs by 9-month performance for each month and forming an equally weighted portfolio from them; portfolio returns are calculated for each date from 2005 onward. The resulting returns are plotted and compared to SPY, and the strategy is reported to compound at a 9.89% CAGR versus SPY’s 9.46% CAGR, indicating little alpha.

Authorities said a 92-year-old woman, Anna Mae Blessing, was charged with first degree murder, aggravated assault, and kidnapping after her 72-year-old son was found dead Monday at their Fountain Hills home. Authorities said she hid two pistols in her robe, shot her son several times in his bedroom, and that his girlfriend was in the room and heard Blessing tell her son she was tired of how he treated her. The girlfriend said she struggled with Blessing when she was pointed at with a gun; court documents stated the girlfriend knocked the second pistol out of her hand when Blessing tried to use it. After being disarmed, Blessing sat until deputies arrived and arrested her. Court documents also said she made a statement during escort. Authorities said the dispute involved her son wanting to send her to an assisted living facility, and that Blessing had moved in with him and his girlfriend about six months earlier. Her attorney was not immediately available.

The passage describes the Evening Star as a bearish reversal candlestick pattern used to identify potential bearish price reversals and profit from them. The pattern consists of three candles: a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above the first, and a third bearish candle that closes below the midpoint of the first. Traders may confirm the pattern using tools such as trendlines, resistance levels, and momentum oscillators before entering short positions, with exit methods that can include profit targets and stop-loss orders. It notes the pattern is more reliable when the gap between the first and second candles is significant and when the third candle is longer than the first, and it suggests considering support and resistance levels and trendlines when spotting it. The passage also mentions that backtesting requires defined rules and settings, and it claims that all 75 candlestick patterns have been backtested with testable rules, statistics, probabilities, and performance metrics. It lists potential risks including false signals, market volatility, over-reliance on technical analysis, lack of diversification, and losses without proper risk management, and it states that indicators such as RSI, stochastic oscillator, and Bollinger Bands can be used for additional confirmation.

The passage describes how U.S. public education adopted business-based practices, initially to improve economic opportunities and later through increased bureaucratic categorization of students. It discusses reports such as *A Nation at Risk* and subsequent moves toward teacher professionalism, arguing that these changes did not make teachers financially secure or improve student test scores. It then outlines the No Child Left Behind Act’s business-like approach using competition, incentives, accountability, standardized testing, and sanctions, and summarizes critiques of charter schools and related claims that wide academic gains have not occurred.  

The passage contrasts this with a “medical model” mentality that attributes learning to diagnosed biological differences, linking it to stigma and fixed mindsets that can hinder learning. It proposes reframing education as problem-solving and emphasizes learning processes centered on inquiry, prediction, explanation, and error correction. It argues that education should use a problem-solving structure at the student, teacher, and institutional levels, supported by mentoring, feedback, metacognitive reflection, and collaboration, with assessment focused on progress toward goals rather than norm comparisons.

Minister Richard Bruton said that during the 2018/19 school term a number of Autism Units are expected to be built in Leitrim. He stated that 12 Autism Units will be built within Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal this year, and that since 2011 ASD special classes in Co. Leitrim have increased from two to five, with new Primary and Post-Primary ASD classes planned. He listed existing special units in Leitrim and responded to Fianna Fáil Deputy Marc MacSharry’s questions about applications for September 2018 and plans to accommodate them. Bruton outlined increases since 2011 in SNA support, resource teachers, and special classes, and said that a professional report is needed before a child is placed in a special class; where demand exceeds places, a non-discriminatory selection process may be required. He also said parents should apply in writing to schools early, and that details are available at www.ncse.ie.

The passage discusses damages for unjustifiable detention and collision. It states that international law admits the loss of catch as part of estimating damage to a whaling vessel due to detention. It then quotes U.S. Supreme Court opinions saying owners of an injured vessel may recover for loss of use while the vessel is laid up for repairs, based on market price when available or evidence of profits if no market price exists. It also describes the general collision-damages rule of indemnifying the injured party for loss sustained, including repair and raising expenses and compensation for loss of service during repairs. A referenced English case held that adequate compensation is owed for detention during the period needed to complete repairs, using gross freight less ordinary expenses; the passage notes this may be inadequate if repairs take longer than a typical voyage. Finally, it says a rule based on what the vessel would earn on hire was applied to whaling ships captured by the Confederate cruiser Shenandoah and forced to abandon their whaling voyages in the Alabama Claims decision.

Semiconductor crystals of Cd1-xZnxTe1-ySey (CZTS) are being studied as promising X-ray and gamma-ray detector materials, but processing methods such as cutting and polishing create a damaged near-surface layer (tens to ~100 µm) that blocks charge collection and increases surface leakage currents unless it is removed. The paper focuses on chemical etching/polishing using a 5% bromine–methanol solution, noting that CZTS differs from the more studied ternary Cd1-xZnxTe (CZT): adding selenium changes thermodynamic properties and hardens the CZTS lattice, which decreases extended defects and leads to a reduced etching rate. Experiments examined bromine–methanol etching for CZTS samples with selenium contents y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.1 at controlled temperature and staged etching times, measuring etching trajectories and average etching rates. Results show that increasing selenium concentration significantly lowers the average etching rate (from 24 µm/min for CZT to 13 µm/min for y = 0.1), with a reported sharp ~20% decrease already at y ≈ 0.02 compared to CZT, and convergence of etching rates at higher selenium contents. The observed selenium-dependent etching behavior is compared with a thermodynamic model based on excess Gibbs energy and is found to agree with experimental trends. The effects of etching dynamics are also shown to depend on initial surface roughness, damaged-layer characteristics, etching temperature, and solution mixing, and conclusions are provided for selecting processing methods for detector fabrication.

The passage discusses INF deployment, noting that Europeans, particularly Chancellor Schmidt, originally pushed it to address regional imbalances and reassure Europeans by reducing fears of “decoupling.” Ambassador Hartman argues that deployment has become divisive and that, given current European attitudes, deployment is unlikely; he recommends trading in the option for an arms control agreement with the Soviets to improve relations and strengthen deterrence, and moving soon to prevent Soviet propaganda from causing European rejection. The author rejects Hartman’s argument, saying the INF decision’s origin is irrelevant because it is a “litmus test” of NATO’s viability, and disputing Hartman’s assessment of European mood by citing supportive statements and continued commitments. The author recommends holding firm on the “zero-zero option” and intensifying efforts to demonstrate U.S. sincerity, then deploying first INF units as scheduled if the Soviets do not change their position, and only considering adjustments if the Soviets restructure their INF position. The passage also includes a memorandum of conversation in which Dobrynin and the Secretary discuss U.S.-Soviet relations, agreeing to regular meetings and reviewing ongoing talks, suggesting a potential Foreign Ministers’ meeting before the next UNGA, and emphasizing a need for an arms control process that includes resolving major issues through Foreign Ministers when necessary.

Vanuatu’s Reserve Bank may investigate APMA Financial Investment Centre (AFIC), a savings and loan cooperative managed by Barnabas Tabi. AFIC is said to have 25,000 fully vested and 30,000 partially vested depositors, but there are no deposits with any Vanuatu commercial banks, and three of four banks deny having any business with AFIC. The passage also reports that Ambae volcano’s rating was lowered from level 4 to level 3, with monitoring continuing, and that the Ambae Port Vila Disaster Committee collected essentials for evacuees. It adds that new teacher salary scales will take effect from the start of 2018, and 21 retired teachers were recognized for 35 years of service with medals presented by President Moses Tallis.

Crystal Palace host Newcastle United at Selhurst Park, with both Rafael Benítez and Roy Hodgson potentially dissatisfied with their transfer business. Hodgson has lost Bakary Sako to a broken ankle and has several other long-term absentees, while Newcastle are hoping to repeat a 4-0 win at Crystal Palace from a year ago. Islam Slimani is listed as doubtful with a thigh issue, and both teams have noted fitness, injured, and suspended players. The match is at 2.15pm with Andre Marriner as referee, and odds are listed for home, draw, and away.

The second edition of *The New Zealand Land and Food Annual* was launched at the National Field Days in Mystery Creek. Edited by Massey University Director of AgriFood Professor Claire Massey, the book—published by Massey University Press—features thoughts from 31 expert contributors on how New Zealand can address issues and lead the world’s green revolution, focusing on sustainable food production and the environmental impacts of food grown and transported. The land and food sector is described as worth $33 billion to New Zealand’s economy, with an intention to treble this by 2025, requiring nutrition-driven agriculture operating within planetary boundaries. The passage also cites recent reports by the OECD and the Ministry for the Environment and notes contributor Professor Ralph Sims’s view that current farming and food-processing practices are not sustainable.

The passage explains that small-body populations in planetary systems exist in discrete dynamical groups (“reservoirs”) formed from material orbiting after gas-disc dispersal, and that understanding these reservoirs is needed to infer the possible origin, composition, and thermal history of exocomets. It summarizes the Solar System’s reservoirs across semi-major axis ranges, including near-Earth asteroids sourced from the main belt, outer resonant populations such as Hildas and Trojans, and trans-Neptunian populations including cold classical Kuiper belt objects, excited populations, and the Oort cloud. It describes how stellar and disc environment affect planetesimal and exocomet reservoirs, covering star formation in dense cores, disc evolution from protoplanetary to debris discs, thermal processes and snowlines, disc dust and gas conditions, and early planetesimal growth mechanisms leading to pebble-based gravitational collapse and streaming instability. The passage also discusses observational evidence from Solar System small bodies and debris discs, including compositional studies enabled by missions and telescopes, and highlights open questions and conclusions about reservoir formation, evolution, and detectability across different stellar masses and environments.

The passage describes planned summary statistics, tables, figures, and listings for plasma concentration (PK) and plasma glucose (PD) by treatment group and time point. It specifies that mean and individual concentration curves will be shown on original and log scales, and that placebo samples will not be analyzed for dasiglucagon and GlucaGen®. Plasma glucose is measured at specified pre-dose and post-dose times with allowable sampling deviations from nominal times, and pre-dose is defined within 2 minutes prior to dosing. The PD endpoint is the plasma glucose response as area under the effect curve above baseline from time 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min), calculated using SAS.  

It also outlines safety analyses, including exposure, local tolerability, adverse event summaries (TEAEs definition, MedDRA mapping, causal relationship and severity categorization), listings of safety data, and tabulations for laboratory parameters. Additional sections cover vital signs, ECG summaries (including QTcF thresholds and change-from-baseline categories), and immunogenicity (ADA incidence calculation without planned statistical tests). Appendix sections specify data presentation/programming rules, QC requirements for SAS programs, and a list of tables/figures/listings included in the SAP.

The passage contains U.S. State Department circular instructions from David J. Hill and John Hay. It addresses (1) passport eligibility, stating the Department does not bar passports solely for applicants who cannot or will not state they intend to return to the United States within two years, while noting passports are valid for two years and a new one may be issued upon a satisfactory application; (2) how missions should be charged in the absence of the head, interpreting article 19 to mean the first secretary acts ad interim as chargé d’affaires without special letters in ordinary cases, and that in emergencies the Department should be consulted before leaving the mission to the second or third secretary; and (3) an executive order prohibiting diplomatic and consular officers from preferring charges against or publicly criticizing other officers except confidentially to the Department of State.

Seminary graduation exercises were held May 20 at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Huber Heights for 16 Miami Valley seniors. More than 100 students and their families attended as students received certificates for completing the Book of Mormon course. Named graduates came from several cities, and speakers included Mark Skouson, who addressed the students, as well as several seniors who discussed how seminary study affected them. The program lets high school students study the Old Testament, New Testament, Book of Mormon, and Church History over four years, and this year classes were taught by 11 volunteer instructors. Seminary is open to all interested high school students, and Peter Stoddard can be contacted for more information.

The passage describes design and layout considerations for a push-pull converter using TPS7H500x-SP controllers. It covers selecting leading-edge blank time (initially ~50 ns; RLEB set to 49.9 kΩ), choosing a soft-start capacitor (33 nF, yielding ~7.5 ms), and transformer parameter selection including a turns ratio of 2.5 and primary inductance (calculated 33 µH but 40 µH used). It specifies GaN FET voltage ratings for the main switching and synchronous rectifier stages, discusses using an RCD clamp and an output inductor with 0.47 µH (targeting 40% ripple), and outlines output capacitance requirements (at least 1.3 mF; ~2.3 mF used for SET mitigation). It also includes guidance for adding an output filter, setting overcurrent sensing components (RCS selected as 7.5 Ω), selecting a hiccup capacitor (3.3 nF), and choosing frequency compensation and slope compensation values. Finally, it provides power supply bypass recommendations and detailed PCB layout guidelines to reduce noise and EMI, including grounding, trace routing, capacitor placement, and compensation component placement.

The passage is largely a dataset-like section listing financial statement line items and dates, followed by portions of Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019. It includes company and investor information, incorporation details, executive officer and director listings as of January 22, 2020, and an extensive discussion of risk factors in Item 1A. The risk factors cover topics such as competition, expansion and growth strains, international risks, fulfillment network and data center optimization, seasonality, commercial agreements and acquisitions, foreign exchange risk, management and personnel retention, security and system interruptions, inventory risk, intellectual property, stock price volatility, government regulation, litigation and investigations, taxes, supplier relationships, government contracts, product liability, and payment-related risks. The document also includes sections on unresolved staff comments (none), properties as of December 31, 2019, and selected consolidated financial data for 2015–2019, along with discussion of liquidity and capital resources.

Anthology Inc. lost nearly $80 million over the past two years and has more than $1 billion in debt, according to court filings. The company is restructuring to become debt-free by early next year, with Oaktree Capital Management and Nexus Capital Management providing $50 million, focusing resources on Blackboard, and selling multiple business lines, with Encoura and Ellucian identified as stalking horse bidders for different segments. Analysts attribute Anthology’s downfall to failed assumptions about institutions buying its full software suite and to operational challenges from rapid expansion through acquisitions, including integration difficulties and inflated costs. The passage also links its bankruptcy to higher interest rates and slowing revenue growth, and it describes a broader shift in the education-technology market toward sustainability, interoperability, and modular platforms.

Fed Chairwoman Janet Yellen questioned the logic of President Donald Trump’s economic policies and refused to support efforts to roll back the Dodd-Frank Act. She said the Fed has seen healthy growth in actual lending, with bank commercial and industrial lending exceeding the 2008 pre-crisis peak, and she cited well-capitalized, safe, and strong banks. Yellen disputed Trump officials’ claims that banks are not lending and that Dodd-Frank makes banks less competitive, noting banks nearly doubled Tier 1 capital and that the financial system is more resilient than before. She acknowledged regulatory burdens on community banks and said lawmakers should exempt them from the Volcker Rule. At the hearing, she declined to comment on Trump’s spending and taxation plans, instead urging policies aimed at improving productivity and keeping fiscal accounts on a sustainable trajectory, and said interest rates should rise sooner than expected.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label phase 2 multicenter trial assessing the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It compares standard of care (mostly supportive) versus standard of care plus convalescent plasma, with standard of care reflecting (inter)national guideline updates during the trial. The trial’s clinical outcomes are based on a WHO master template to support data pooling with other studies. Randomization uses a 2:1 allocation to standard of care plus convalescent plasma. Protocol amendments and investigator/operational coordinating personnel information are described in specified appendices.

The passage describes Germany’s education system and its special education and inclusion developments, shaped by historical events and laws. It outlines Germany’s general school structure (e.g., Hauptschule, Realschule, Gymnasium; plus Gesamtsschule), differences across federal states, and the history of special schools (Hilfsschulen) established in the 1920s. It explains that special education is organized through various specialized school categories and services, with a push since the early 1990s to include more students in general education settings. The passage provides enrollment and inclusion figures for students with disabilities and discusses how teachers are trained under KMK guidance, including special education teacher training emphasizing pedagogy and behavior management. It also summarizes related legal and policy frameworks, current challenges (such as inclusion practices, funding, teacher perceptions, and school quality), and concludes that Germany is shifting toward greater inclusion while redefining the role of special educators.

A Department of Education spokesperson said Friday that ED employees will be impacted by reduction-in-force (RIF) layoffs taking place across the federal government, though the number of affected employees and which offices would be unclear as of Friday afternoon. Other sources said no one in the Office of Federal Student Aid would be laid off. A senior ED leader said the layoffs were directed by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and came as a surprise to ED, and that ED had edited a list from OMB. Rachel Gittleman, president of the union representing Education Department employees, said the administration is dismantling the department against congressional intent and promised to fight the layoffs. Meanwhile, Democrats argued that firing federal workers during a shutdown is unconstitutional.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel said she would be pleased if Poland’s talks with the European Union produced a solution to the standoff over Poland’s rule-of-law record, related to changes to Poland’s judiciary that could lead to EU sanctions. Merkel and Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki also emphasized European unity, discussed economic cooperation and support for countries most affected by migration, and discussed the EU’s response to the poisoning of Sergei Skripal and his daughter in Britain. Merkel said she expects strong conclusions at an upcoming EU summit and stated that evidence points to Russia’s responsibility, which Russia denies.

The passage describes a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications related to “Metal Gates of Transistors Having Reduced Resistivity.” It explains that MOS devices may use polysilicon gate electrodes, which suffer from a poly depletion effect that increases effective gate dielectric thickness. It discusses using metal gates, including tungsten, where tungsten adhesion issues are addressed with a tungsten nucleation layer; however, the nucleation layer’s higher resistivity can degrade transistor performance as gate dimensions shrink. The passage then outlines embodiments for forming FinFETs, including forming substrate and STI regions with recessed fins, creating dummy gate stacks, forming gate spacers, forming source/drain epitaxy regions, creating ILD and replacement gate stacks with gate dielectrics and work-function layers, and depositing metal-containing gate materials. It further describes forming metal nitride barrier layers and depositing cobalt or metal silicide layers, including specific layer compositions and deposition approaches, followed by planarization and etch-back steps. The passage also covers forming source/drain and gate contact plugs and vias using barrier layers and metal-containing layers, and provides device and method summaries emphasizing metal nitride barrier layers with cobalt or metal silicide to improve adhesion and reduce resistivity compared to tungsten nucleation layers.

The passage describes the Spinlock module, which provides hardware assistance for synchronizing processes using 128 spinlocks (hardware semaphores), enabling efficient lock operations without requiring a read-modify-write bus transfer. It also explains the Mailbox module’s inter-processor communication features between ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and other processors, including message FIFO queues, interrupt signaling for message queuing and overflow, and flexible mailbox-to-processor assignment. The device overview section discusses unified memory mapping and provides references to L3 and L4 memory maps, including details about L3 access for the C674x DSP and notes about reserved regions for masters other than Cortex-A8. It further outlines additional addressing via the TILER extended map, with extra addressing range accessible to specific subsystems. The passage then includes extensive information on device pin multiplexing and terminal functions, covering boot configuration pins (BTMODE sampling and boot mode execution order), descriptions and requirements for various interfaces (e.g., GPMC, EMAC, I2C, UART, SPI, USB, video interfaces), general-purpose I/O behavior, and supply voltage connection requirements.

OpenAI’s new Sora app generates a personal digital avatar and lets users scroll a TikTok-like feed of user-generated AI videos featuring their likeness and friends’ likenesses. Sora 2 powers the app, which is available on iOS only and requires an invite code. An advisory during sign-up warns that some videos may depict recognizable people but the actions and events are not real. Users can record their avatar during setup and control who can use their digital likeness, with options ranging from everyone to approvals or mutual connections; clip access is available from the user’s account page. The app can add people as “cameos” and produce nine-second clips with generated scripts, sound, and visuals; safety guardrails block some content, including certain sexual or “racy” requests, self-harm-related content, and requests involving similarity to third-party public figures. WIRED testing found some outputs contain errors but often look and sound convincingly real, and some requests—like marijuana depictions—were not restricted.

A study in the *Journal of Consumer Psychology* reported that parents may favor children based on gender, despite claiming equal love. Across four experiments in the US and India, mothers chose daughters more often and fathers chose sons more often when asked to give a $25 treasury bond to only one child and when deciding between entering a raffle for a boy’s or girl’s school backpack. The study said the bias appeared in both cultures and may be driven by stronger identification with same-sex children, linked to spending aligned with identity. In interviews, more than 90 percent of participants said they did not prefer one child over another, even though their choices indicated favoritism.

The passage describes off-highway recreational side-by-side utility vehicles and related embodiments. It claims priority to a U.S. provisional application and incorporates material from co-filed applications. The background discusses ROVs’ ability to carry multiple occupants and the factors affecting access to harsh terrain, including vehicle width, suspension, turning radius, under-carriage clearance, wheelbase, center of gravity, and power.  

A summary embodiment describes an off-highway recreational vehicle with a longitudinal centerline and a frame, where the rear suspension includes a left A-arm whose pivot axis is on the right-hand side of the longitudinal centerline. The detailed description then outlines vehicle construction elements such as frame members, drivetrain and axle/differential configurations, seating arrangements and adjustability, fuel filling port and fuel tank packaging, lighting, doors and hinges, ROPS structure and its connection members for mating and accessory attachment, and a brake pedal assembly including reservoirs, master cylinder arrangement, switch outputs, and pedal ratio.
