The passage describes multiple container design patterns and their uses, focusing first on the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and external services, and then on sharding-related routing trade-offs and request handling. It explains how ambassador containers can proxy requests to shards, enabling a separation of concerns between the application (connecting to a localhost “single backend”) and the sharding proxy. The passage also gives examples of using the ambassador pattern for service brokering (e.g., selecting a MySQL connection) and for experimentation/request splitting (e.g., routing a fraction of traffic to a test version).  

Later sections introduce the adapter pattern, which modifies an application container’s interface to match a consistent interface expected by other tools, with examples for monitoring (e.g., adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus), logging normalization (e.g., using fluentd), and richer health monitoring (e.g., adding query-based health checks for MySQL without modifying the original container). The passage then shifts to multi-node patterns and microservices, discussing replicated load-balanced services, stateless service readiness probes, session tracked services, caching layers, rate limiting/SSL termination in web serving, and ends by comparing replicated services with sharded services. It outlines sharded cache design considerations, the impact of cache hit rate and latency, replicated sharded caches, routing via sharding functions (including consistent hashing), and how scatter/gather and sharded scatter/gather systems operate and scale, including issues like overhead and the “straggler” problem. Finally, it introduces event-driven function-as-a-service (FaaS), listing key benefits and challenges and noting that FaaS is often unsuitable for long-running background processing or workloads requiring large in-memory data.

AT&T announced that by the end of June it will turn on LTE-M, a nationwide technology for connecting Internet of Things devices. LTE-M is a version of cellular technology used by smartphones, tuned for everyday objects, using less energy and able to last up to 10 years on a single charge. It can penetrate walls up to 8 inches thicker than standard signals, and transmits a low data rate (about 386 kilobits per second), which AT&T says is sufficient for small IoT data. AT&T representatives said concerns about LTE-M affecting calls or streaming are unlikely because IoT devices use little data and are mostly not connected. Examples shown included Pepsi’s LTE-M-enabled soda fountain radios for tracking drink preferences and smaller radios embedded in the machines, and RM2 pallets with built-in LTE-M radios to track pallets and goods during transport. The passage also describes smart water meters using LTE-M to detect toilet flapper issues, potential hand-washing behavior, and near real-time alerts for leaks. AT&T has not set pricing yet, but is considering charging per bit or per device.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended a 7-day win streak. Tesla debuted more affordable versions of its Model Y SUV and Model 3 sedan. The Model Y standard is priced just under $40,000 and does not include features like a panoramic glass roof, leather seats, or light bars found on higher-end versions; it costs about $5,000 less than the previous entry-level Model Y. The new Model Y standard has an estimated 321-mile range versus 357 miles for a Long Range rear-wheel-drive version. Tesla also released a new version of its driver assistance system. Tesla’s shares climbed 5% on Monday after investors anticipated updates, then fell about 3% on Tuesday. The lower prices were noted as potentially helping Tesla after the loss of $7,500 federal EV tax credits, which ended with a spending bill, alongside competition from other EV makers.

Speakers discuss the Detroit Red Wings ahead of a series, saying they will prepare better and capitalize on limited chances, including focusing on the power play. They comment that a great offensive player also works hard on defense and is playing at his best, with increased confidence from experience. They describe recovering from an injury using a day-to-day approach, and say being sidelined during a team losing stretch was difficult. After returning, they made changes that improved how the team started and approached games, leading them to believe they had a chance to make the playoffs. They also note facing the same team as last year, calling the series highly competitive.

The Rock Springs City Council will hold a public hearing on May 1 to consider amendments allowing downtown restaurants to offer outdoor dining areas (“Dining Decks”). The Planning & Zoning Commission unanimously approved a petition on April 11 to amend Section 13-809 and add Section 13-819 with regulations. If approved, outdoor dining decks would be allowed seasonally from May 1 to October 31, with off-season storage of equipment, at least six-foot sidewalk clearance, and restrictions on structures, umbrellas, and alcohol service. Restaurants would manage maintenance (including snow removal), and building and fire inspections would apply, with outdoor heaters identified as a primary fire concern. The hearing will be at Rock Springs City Hall on May 1 at 7 pm.

Detroit manager A.J. Hinch said Tigers ace Tarik Skubal will not be available to pitch in Game 4 of the ALDS versus the Mariners, even though Detroit is facing elimination. Skubal pitched Game 2, throwing seven innings of two-run baseball with nine strikeouts, and was initially set to pitch a potential Game 5 on normal rest, but Hinch is keeping him on his schedule and available for a potential Game 5. The Tigers will have their high-leverage relievers available for Game 4.

Lego DC Super Villains was officially announced with a full trailer. The game lets players create their own super villain and team up with classic DC bad guys, set in a parallel universe where DC Super Heroes are not around. It releases October 16, 2018, for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, and will be available in multiple editions including special editions with bonus characters. The passage also notes that more information is available on the official game website and asks readers for their thoughts.

The “Boston” Zone Offense was developed and refined by Tom Davis and gained national exposure while he coached Boston College. It is described as a unique zone offense because players stay in one position, only flipping sides, allowing them to be more efficient at single roles. The offense emphasizes a strong low-post attack and uses a dribble entry to start, making it suitable for up-tempo teams. It combines overloading and spreading to attack zone defenses. The basic alignment includes a point guard O1, swing guard O2, low post O5, baseline runner or corner O3, and weakside rebounder or power forward O4. Key concepts include moving the ball sideline to sideline with sharp passing, using skip passes, post feeds, and pump fakes, avoiding difficult passes, minimizing dribbling, and using multiple ball-reversal and cut actions (including corner give-and-go cuts and baseline runner options). The passage also outlines post-read situations based on defender positioning, and counters such as skip passes when passes are overplayed or denied, plus options created by zone pressure like dribble penetration, isolation mismatches, and kick-out or drop-pass opportunities.

The passage discusses several hockey players and team performance. It praises a top right winger as a quality veteran whose minutes change based on matchups and line rotations, and describes him as an underrated, disciplined player who plays against top opponents and in tough areas without taking penalties. It also compares another defenseman’s role to a younger but experienced presence, notes adjustments involving older defensemen, and highlights Jarome’s leadership and leadership shift from being the team’s face to becoming captain, which is presented as a reason for his improved play. The speakers address the team’s need to focus on self-improvement rather than opponents, argue that ice conditions and heavy playoff schedules have not been excuses, and include comments about officiating and playoff roles for officials and linesmen.

Pakistan’s federal government has stopped work on three CPEC road projects after China stopped funding them, according to Dawn. Planning and Development minister Ahsan Iqbal told a parliamentary committee that the projects were halted, and the committee later said they had not been abandoned because China was reviewing the financial mechanism and would start the work after Chinese approval. The passage also notes that China stopped funding on December 9 and that prior refusal by Pakistan to accept Chinese funding terms and to allow yuan trade at Gwadar were cited as factors in China’s actions. It adds that experts have warned CPEC could become a debt trap, referencing Sri Lanka’s handing over the Hambantota Port to China due to loan repayment inability.

The passage argues that national legislators should enact a law imposing a graduated inheritance tax with increasing duty rates on gifts, bequests, or devises. It suggests making the tax heavier for recipients more remote from kin and increasing the pro rata tax sharply as amounts left exceed a certain point, keeping taxes small for moderate amounts to encourage thrift and ambition. It states that such government regulation of gifts and inheritances is ethically proper and that progress should be gradual, beginning with a permanent inheritance tax that may be smaller and less graduated at first. The passage cites earlier temporary national inheritance taxes from 1797, 1862, and 1898, describing their graduated and kin-remoteness features. It also references Supreme Court rulings upholding inheritance-tax features as constitutional, while contrasting inheritance taxes with income taxes and discussing past constitutional difficulties with federal income tax laws, concluding that if constitutional amendment becomes necessary, it may ultimately be required.

The passage describes coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) for ischemic heart disease and outlines different surgical versions (on-pump vs off-pump) and approaches (endoscopic or thoracotomy), including newer use of the Da-Venice robot. It notes that post-CABG complications are common and lists complications such as postoperative arrhythmia, psychosis, stroke, myocardial infarction, hydrothorax, re-sternotomy, dyspnea, and sternal wound infection, along with reported risk factors (e.g., diabetes mellitus, hypertension, advanced age, CPB and aortic cross-clamp time, and hospitalization duration). The study retrospectively analyzed 290 patients treated 2017–2021, collected preoperative characteristics and operative details (including number of shunts and internal thoracic arteries used), and assessed postoperative complications and correlations. The results report frequent hydrothorax and associations between complications and factors such as age, CPB/aortic cross-clamp time, ICU/total hospitalization days, and certain preoperative conditions (progressive angina and post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis). The conclusions state that elderly CABG patients are at higher risk for psychosis, arrhythmia, longer ICU and total hospitalization, and stroke, and that hydrothorax is associated with low BMI and longer aortic cross-clamp time.

The passage is a series of remarks attributed to Coach Sutter about team strategy and players, emphasizing matchups, two-way play, competitiveness, tenacity, leadership, preparation, and the team’s maturity. It discusses specific players’ roles and performance, including mentions of nominations for the Selke, playoff play-making, increased minutes in crucial situations, strong leadership with young players, and goalie performance. It also notes adjustments for players in the Stanley Cup Final, the team’s speed, and the importance of addressing upcoming elimination games through ongoing play.

The passage discusses a team’s playoff success, attributing it to handling adversity, confidence at home, and a focus on being tough to play in their own building. It highlights specific players’ contributions, including John’s defensive role and leadership when others were injured, and mentions overcoming injuries and travel fatigue during a deep postseason run. The speakers also reflect on roster changes after losing Bobby Holik and other leaders, describing growth together and later paying off. They express satisfaction with winning the Stanley Cup, while also emphasizing that the team is not finished and aims to build for the future rather than call itself a “dynasty” yet.

Lewis Roberts (respondent) sued the attorneys David B. Prosser and Charles R. King (appellants) for false imprisonment after Roberts was arrested and imprisoned based on an execution issued on a judgment obtained in a creditor’s action for an accounting and distribution of funds from insolvent debtor Robert Mills’s assignees. The court held that such a creditor’s action against an assignee for an accounting and distribution is not an “action for money received” in a fiduciary capacity under subdivision 2 of section 179 of the Code, where arrest may occur. The action was described as requiring a judicial determination of net amounts chargeable to the assignees, and the distribution among creditors contributing to suit expenses, not a simple recovery of money received. The court found the execution against Roberts unauthorized and affirmed the circuit judgment for $100 damages with costs.

Two out of every five U.S. households report good or excellent progress in meeting their savings needs. America Saves Week, an annual event since 2007 coordinated by America Saves and the American Savings Education Council, brings together financial institutions, government agencies, employers, bloggers, and organizations to promote savings behavior and help individuals assess their saving status. Thousands of groups typically participate, reaching millions. America Saves Week 2017 runs from February 27 to March 4, with daily focuses such as family savings and saving at tax time, and includes engagement opportunities like a photo contest, tweet chats, and free products and resources. Participants can sign up to be recognized and receive information, a toolkit, a participation badge, and tips for planning activities. The passage also notes Military Saves Week 2017 for organizations supporting servicemembers and their families.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite President Trump’s new $100,000 fee for new H-1B applicants. A calculation based on U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services data estimates Nvidia could have to pay about $147.3 million for the H-1B visa holders it got approved in 2025, though the fee does not apply to renewals or current visa-holders. In an internal memo, Huang wrote that “legal immigration remains essential,” and he said the fee may set the bar too high while still eliminating abuse. Nvidia’s spokesperson declined to comment.

The speaker expresses gratitude for his reelection and for public approval of his prior term, viewing his role as an instrument of union rather than a cause. He outlines how an elected leader should review past events, correct errors, and support sound policy, emphasizing thorough knowledge for judging past and guiding future administration. He recounts that the United States had recently ended a war, describing its effects on commerce, defenses, casualties, and public debt, and explains subsequent defense measures: reducing the land force and expanding coastal fortifications and naval forces, supported by laws passed in 1815 and 1816. He argues that these measures are economical and aimed at preventing war and defending the country’s coast and interior. He states the government maintains peace with other powers, and describes U.S. neutrality regarding the conflict between Spain and South American colonies, including equal treatment of public vessels and trade, and his view that neutrality should continue. He discusses actions taken against piracy and buccaneering, execution and pardoning practices, and describes diplomatic developments such as the ratified treaty with Spain, the Florida acquisition, and renewed or adjusted agreements with Great Britain, France negotiations, and relations with the Barbary Powers. He then addresses national finances, noting debt payments, defense progress, and revenue shortfalls due to depressed prices, and discusses possible responses such as loans, repealing internal taxes, and using internal duties and excises. He proposes reforms for dealing with Indian tribes and concludes by describing the U.S. political system’s structure and progress, including territorial expansion and population growth, and by pledging to begin his duties with help from officials and reliance on God.

In autumn 2011, St. Olaf student Erik Brust pursued an idea he developed with his cousin Jonathan Jeffrey at Duke University to create a simple, fruity-and-creamy frozen treat with natural ingredients. After Jeffrey died, Brust named the company JonnyPops in his honor and recruited classmates, including Connor Wray, to test recipes. The final formula used fruit, real cream, cane sugar, and a pinch of salt, with additive- and filler-free pops. JonnyPops expanded in 2012 through farmers markets and other local venues, then grew in 2013 to representation in several states after moving into its own manufacturing space and pursuing broader distribution. Brust and Wray were named to Forbes’ 30 Under 30 and launched in spring 2014 with about 50 Minnesota store partners. After graduating, they worked full-time at the company, which later reached 10,000 unique distribution points nationwide. JonnyPops is also pursuing a social mission, Better Pop for a Better World, featuring messages on pop sticks and partnering with retailers to raise money for addiction treatment organizations. In March, it launched a new Delights line with five creative flavors made from real cream and natural ingredients, listed as gluten-free and under 200 calories each.

The passage lists analysts’ Friday, October 6th price target changes and ratings for multiple stocks, including Covestro AG (BNP Paribas €64.00, sell), AdvanSix (Cowen raised $40.00 to $46.00, outperform), Ascena Retail Group (RBC cut $5.00 to $2.50, sector perform), Basf Se (BNP Paribas €96.00, buy), Costco (Oppenheimer $185.00, buy), Deckers Outdoor (Stifel Nicolaus raised $74.00 to $80.00, buy), New Oriental Education & Technology Group (Benchmark raised $94.00 to $100.00, buy), Evonik Industries (BNP Paribas €29.00, neutral), Inovio Pharmaceuticals (HC Wainwright $13.00, buy), Linde AG (BNP Paribas €175.00, neutral), Eli Lilly (Morgan Stanley $86.00, hold), Lanxess (BNP Paribas €65.00, neutral), Mallinckrodt (UBS $70.00, buy), Netflix (Oppenheimer raised $200.00 to $215.00, outperform), Plug Power (Craig Hallum raised $3.00 to $4.00, buy), Rite Aid (Mizuho cut $2.95 to $2.25, neutral), Constellation Brands (Stifel Nicolaus raised $216.00 to $235.00; RBC raised $222.00 to $226.00, both buy/outperform respectively), 2U (Needham raised $62.00 to $66.00, buy), Wacker Chemie (BNP Paribas €110.00, neutral), and Yum China (Oppenheimer raised $43.00 to $45.00, outperform).

The passage says that, for the fourth time in the Republic’s history, the Chief Magistrate has been removed by death. The elected constitutional successor is called to assume the executive chair to ensure the government is not imperiled by the uncertainty of human life. The new executive states that the late President’s aspirations, measures to correct abuses, enforce economy, advance prosperity, and promote general welfare will be carried forward. It also claims that prosperity exists, fiscal policy is fixed by law and well grounded, foreign relations are not threatened, and no unusual session of Congress is needed. The successor concludes by saying he assumes the Constitution’s trust with reliance on divine guidance and the virtue and intelligence of the American people.

The passage describes a planned systematic review within a series focused on determining how viral culture results relate to surrogate measures of viral burden (such as serial rt-PCR cycle threshold values) for assessing infectivity of SARS-CoV-2 in transplant recipients who are immunosuppressed. It notes that infectious virus presence may be prolonged in immunosuppressed patients, so decisions about isolation removal should be based on forward transmission risk assessed by viral culture or, if not possible, surrogate markers like rt-PCR Ct values. The review aims to collate and evaluate studies using viral cell culture to estimate the relationship between viral culture and repeat rt-PCR Ct or other measures of viral burden, specifically in solid organ and hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. The research questions address the relationship between serial PCR Ct (or other viral burden measures) and the likelihood/duration of infectious virus presence from viral culture, and how factors such as age, sex, underlying conditions, degree of immunosuppression, vaccination status, symptoms, and disease course influence viral burden and infectious virus likelihood. Methods include searching LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO COVID-19 database (Nov 2019 to Dec 31, 2021), screening by four researchers, including studies with serial respiratory sample viral burden measures alongside viral culture data, and excluding studies without viral cultures or using only post-mortem or non-respiratory samples. Quality assessment uses five criteria related to case diagnosis, population reporting, follow-up sufficiency, PCR replicability/generalizability, and viral culture replicability/appropriateness. Data will be reported using PRISMA flow and tabular summaries, with narrative synthesis planned rather than pooling for a cutoff due to assay/laboratory differences.

Lincolnshire County Council approved a new care leavers strategy, with the corporate parenting manager saying the council has a legal responsibility to support young care leavers as any parent would. The passage notes that research found care leavers may struggle to pay bills after leaving care, and it describes measures such as council tax discounts up to 100% for care leavers aged 18–21 and extending advice and guidance from authorities to age 25. Support mentioned includes assistance beyond age 18, help with university costs and driving licences, and guidance for care leavers held in custody. The leaving care services budget is about £1.2 million, and the council has more than 600 people in care and about 300 in leaving care services, expected to rise with the age extension. Support can be accessed through the council or Barnardos.

A fossil from southwestern China shows a pregnant long-necked marine reptile, Dinocephalosaurus, dated to about 245 million years ago in the Triassic Period, with a developing embryo. Scientists said the fossil indicates Dinocephalosaurus gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs, changing understanding of vertebrate reproductive evolution. They noted Dinocephalosaurus was the first known archosauromorph (a group including birds, crocodilians, dinosaurs, and pterosaurs) known to be viviparous. Measuring about 13 feet long with a long neck and paddle-like flippers, it was fish-eating. The researchers said live birth likely helped it avoid leaving the ocean, and they found evidence the embryo was the mother’s baby. They also said Dinocephalosaurus determined offspring sex genetically rather than through nest temperature.

Farmers State Bank of Craig sued Samuel J. Lydick on a $3,000 promissory note dated March 17, 1920, payable six months later. Lydick alleged the note was part payment for prior $5,000 notes and that he received no consideration because he was fraudulently induced to purchase stock in the Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company; he alleged cashier/president Everett J. Martin conspired and made deceptive representations. The bank and Martin filed separate defenses. The court directed a verdict for the bank against Lydick on his cross-petition seeking affirmative recovery, submitted to the jury whether the bank was a good-faith purchaser for value without notice of defects before maturity, and submitted whether Martin made the alleged representations; the jury found for the bank on the first issue and for Martin on the representation issue. The court withdrew a second cross-petition stock-purchase issue for lack of competent evidence. The appellate court held the evidence supported the verdict, found no error in jury instructions and refused instructions, rejected the defense’s holder-in-due-course theory by citing Bank of Commerce & Savings v. Bandell, and affirmed the judgment.

James Schenck accepted an award on behalf of the PenFed team, crediting a “People Helping People” philosophy and describing driven people as making a difference. The annual Business Philanthropy Summit in Alexandria promotes cooperation among businesses, nonprofits, and government entities to increase community wellbeing. PenFed supports citizens in the Washington metro area through the credit union and the PenFed Foundation, and the passage lists recent donations including funding for wounded warriors, military families’ concerts, veterans’ affordable homeownership, veteran financial literacy training, and educational programming for veteran entrepreneurs. It also notes PenFed donations to the Gary Sinise Foundation for accessible homes and the launch of the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program. Marcy Anderson praised Schenck’s volunteerism and expanded foundation efforts. The passage adds background on the PenFed Foundation’s mission since 2001, Schenck’s volunteer leadership roles without compensation, his board service, and his honors and education. It concludes with general information about PenFed Credit Union.

Amazon Prime Day is returning on October 7–8 (“Prime Day 2”), with early deals already available. WIRED says it features products independently selected by editors and focuses on items its editors have hand-tested, with coverage including a liveblog and updates. The passage lists several early deal highlights and, in an update dated September 30, 2025, adds 10 new deals and notes accuracy checks. Mentioned deals include discounted Apple iPad (2025, A16), an Anker MagGo power bank (10K), an Apple MacBook Air (M4, 2025), an Arlo Pro 5S security camera, an Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024), and a Ring Air fitness tracker/wearable, among other items.

For about 20 years, China has worked to modernise and upgrade its armed forces, aiming to gain “hard” military power alongside its growing “soft” power. Beijing increasingly uses military force or the threat of force to defend regional interests, such as South China Sea territorial claims and protecting SLOCs, and China’s expanding global economic activities also depend on coastal infrastructure and access to strategic pathways of the Indian Ocean. The PLA’s modernisation has led to significant progress since the late 1990s, making it a much more assertive force in recent years, though the future end result and further use of China’s growing military power remain unclear.

A Reuters report says North Korea’s rarely traded defaulted debt may become even harder for investors to access after new sanctions imposed on Pyongyang this week. The debt, originally issued as syndicated loans tied to defaults from the 1980s and later repackaged in 1997 into transferable securities by BNP, has been frozen by longstanding sanctions and has seen little to no trading for the past three to four years. Prices rose briefly after Kim Jong-il’s death in 2011 but hopes for progress with the international community faded, with trading effectively freezing in early 2013 after UN and other sanctions. The new sanctions, following Pyongyang’s ICBM tests, ban exports including coal, iron/ore, lead, and seafood and could cut North Korea’s annual export revenue by about a third. The report also notes that some investors, such as the Franklin Emerging Markets fund, have held NK Debt Corporation bonds and previously valued the holdings at much lower amounts than their original purchase costs. Debt restructuring expert Charles Blitzer said there may be no progress on North Korean issues for a long time.

Latin American stocks rebounded on Monday after last week’s selloff, as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased and officials played down the prospect of imminent war. Key U.S. comments and strategists’ notes said geopolitical risks had fallen somewhat, though risks remained if North Korea renewed missile testing. Emerging markets had dropped sharply, losing nearly $1 trillion globally. In Latin America, Mexico’s S&P/BVM IPC rose 1.1%, Brazil’s Bovespa reached its highest level since May, and power utility Cia Paranaense de Energia SA led gains. Currency moves were more subdued: the Mexican peso rose 0.3% ahead of NAFTA-related negotiations, while the Brazilian real fluctuated ahead of a revision to the government’s fiscal goal. Key index and currency figures were reported at 1620 GMT.

Let’s Grow Kids, founded in 2015 by Rick Davis, aimed to create Vermont’s near-universal child care infrastructure over a time-limited decade and to sunset in 2025. Davis brought Aly Richards on board, and with help from former Govs. Peter Shumlin and Howard Dean, the organization built a team to push Vermont to become the first state with a near-universal child care system. Over 10 years, it raised over $70 million, grew to 40 staffers, and supported the implementation of Act 76, signed into law in 2023. The organization sunset its operations on Oct. 3, as planned, with its transition managed through partnerships with permanent organizations covering financing, workforce, data, and advocacy, while remaining staff moved into related groups such as the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network to protect funding for Act 76.

Materials characterization is important for discovering new materials and understanding structure–property relationships, especially for compositionally complex and heterogeneous systems like high entropy alloys, high entropy oxides, and energy-storage materials. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) are described as complementary bulk techniques: XRD probes long-range periodic structure while XAFS measures short-range local structure in an element-specific way. Multi-modal measurements are often done at large user facilities such as synchrotron light sources, including spatially resolved studies for devices like battery cells and combinatorial materials libraries.

The passage notes limitations of conventional homogeneous mapping strategies due to limited beamtime and the mismatch between uniform sampling approaches and inherently inhomogeneous samples. It describes the development of data-driven AI/ML approaches—especially machine-learning-based active learning using Bayesian optimization—to improve measurement efficiency and scientific outcomes, including rapid phase mapping and detection of subtle phenomena.

A modular, multi-beamline AI-driven framework is presented, featuring an ensemble of AI agents for data processing, analysis, and decision-making, moderated by human adjudicators and executed through secure queue servers. The framework orchestrates synchronized XRD and XAFS experiments on identical combinatorial ternary alloy libraries (Al-Ni-Pt) using multiple beamlines at NSLS-II, with examples of automated data processing and decision-making workflows. Post-experiment analysis includes mapping composition and phases using XAFS modeling and diffraction fitting, and the work also includes a “digital twin” for simulating diffraction measurements and benchmarking AI-driven mapping strategies. The authors conclude that the framework enables autonomous yet collaborative multi-modal synchrotron experiments while preserving safety considerations and improving mapping of phase boundaries and minor localized components compared with conventional strategies.

In Portsmouth, Virginia, court documents describe how a social media post led to the March 14 shooting death of Jennifer Bartell. Joshua Bowen is accused of shooting Bartell multiple times; the documents say he is Albany Pierce’s boyfriend. Pierce, her mother Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson are charged with accessory after the fact, along with another person. The documents say Pierce argued with Bartell’s daughter and the daughter’s friend on Facebook, which escalated to a planned meeting at a nearby church that the daughter and friend did not attend. The group then allegedly went to Bartell’s home, where a fight broke out and Bowen began shooting. Bowen told documents that Bartell appeared to be armed. Investigators say a gun was taken from Bartell’s home after the shooting, but none were taken from the scene. Neighbors said they were shocked and relieved to learn the shooting was not random. Four people have been arrested.

A federal judge ruled that a 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill is not pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who said the photo—taken when he was 4 months old—should qualify for civil remedies under a law covering certain crimes against minors. Olguin found factors such as lack of focus on genitalia, no sexually suggestive setting, and no intent to elicit a sexual response. He said the image was most analogous to a nude child bathing and was insufficient to support a finding of lasciviousness, noting the only factor close to the child pornography standard was that Elden was shown nude.

A Florida Museum of Natural History study examined lice and their vitamin-producing bacterial symbionts that enable lice to parasitize mammals, including primates and humans. The bacteria live in specialized cells in lice, are passed from female to offspring, and lice depend on them for vitamins because lice feed only on blood. Researchers Bret Boyd and David Reed found that lice parasitizing primates and humans have hosted these endosymbionts continuously for at least 20–25 million years, with bacterial evolution staying closely matched to primate and louse evolution. The researchers sequenced symbiont genomes from several primate/monkey lice and found very small bacterial genomes (530,000–570,000 base pairs) and evidence of extensive genome remodeling over the last 25 million years that clustered genes critical for symbiosis. They also reported that much of the symbiont genome is devoted to vitamin synthesis, including B-vitamins, and noted that changes in symbiont genome size and retained genes are important for understanding long-lasting mutualistic relationships.

A new study using deep learning on thousands of European satellite images finds that Martian winds can reach speeds up to 160 km/h (44 m/s), much stronger than previously assumed. These high-speed winds lift large amounts of dust into the atmosphere, forming visible dust devils that act as markers for studying wind behavior. The researchers identified dust devils in over 50,000 images and used stereo images of about 300 to measure their movement and speed. The study, published in collaboration across multiple institutions, provides global-scale findings on wind strength over roughly two decades and is described as important for future mission planning, atmospheric modeling, and understanding features such as dunes, slope streaks, and weather and climate models.

The passage describes a study of adults diagnosed with ADHD in adulthood, focusing on whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) involving the nucleus accumbens (NAc) predicts changes in ADHD symptom severity over about three years. ADHD is presented as a common neurodevelopmental condition with childhood-onset symptoms that can persist into adulthood, and it is associated with higher rates of comorbidities and poorer outcomes. The researchers recruited 54 physically healthy adults (age 18–50) diagnosed using the Wender-Reimherr Interview (WRI) at baseline (t1) and followed them at t2 after a mean of 3 years, measuring symptom change as ΔWRI (WRI t2 − WRI t1). About 30% stopped stimulant medication before follow-up; at t2, 34 were still taking stimulants and 20 were not. Using fMRI preprocessing and seed-based connectivity analyses with the NAc as the seed, the study reports that lower FC between the NAc and specific brain regions (right paracingulate gyrus and right insular cortex) related to higher symptom severity and/or symptom change over time, with the direction of associations differing by medication status at t2. The authors conclude that FC patterns between the brain’s reward system, default mode network, and salience network correlate with ADHD symptom course and response to stimulant medication, and suggest potential use as a biological marker, while noting limitations and the need for further research.

A state audit found Utah’s Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control overcharged customers nearly $1,200 after entering incorrect prices for seven items in its computer system during a required markup change. Auditors said the incorrect markup caused customers, mainly businesses, to be overcharged $1,161 across 28 sales, while the department lost $186 in nine sales. The department plans to refund the overpayments and has added a program to flag incorrect markup percentages and apply the correct pricing formula. The audit also found the department failed to transfer $4.6 million in revenue to state school lunch and public safety programs in November 2017, and said the department corrected the error after auditors discovered it.

The passage recounts the 1793 yellow fever outbreak in Philadelphia, driven by hot, dry conditions that lowered water levels and created breeding grounds for mosquitoes, alongside refugees from the Caribbean who brought the disease. Symptoms included head, back, and limb pain and high fever, with temporary improvement before the disease returned with severe symptoms, yellow skin, and death. More than 10% of Philadelphia’s population died before the epidemic ended in November. Medical efforts initially failed due to limited understanding of infectious disease transmission. Later, physicians discovered yellow fever was spread by mosquitoes biting an infected person and then a healthy one, leading officials to improve water and sanitation, drainage, and public education. The most recent North American outbreak was in 1905 in New Orleans. The passage then describes Brazil’s major yellow fever resurgence beginning in December 2016 and the risk of spread toward major cities, noting climate and environmental factors. It states that a yellow fever vaccine is available, highly effective (99%), and usually needs one dose, and WHO recommends it for people in endemic areas and those traveling to Brazil. It concludes by discussing ongoing Zika vaccine development at Penn, including DNA and mRNA candidates, and mentions WHO’s current recommendation for yellow fever vaccination for travelers.

Rachael Caplan, 29, has CRPS (Complex Regional Pain Syndrome), which causes excruciating, constant pain and has left her essentially bedridden and confined to the top floor of her parents’ home since August 2016. She was once athletic and working toward a law career, but after CRPS spread throughout her body, she began experiencing symptoms seven years ago and took about a year and a half to receive a diagnosis in June 2013. CRPS is described by doctors and advocates as beginning like an autoimmune disease and later becoming a neurological disease, with symptoms that can include intense pain starting in a hand or foot and spreading, along with swelling, color changes, sweating, temperature changes, and other physical effects. Treatment early in the disease is described as having a high success rate, but after about six months reversal is described as unlikely, and many patients become disabled. Caplan’s coping is supported by family and friends, who created a social media awareness campaign using the hashtag #AceThisFire, and she has tried many therapies without success; physiotherapy and opioids aggravated her pain. She recently began green light therapy, which she says has improved her head pain and helped her sleep up to nine hours per night. Caplan hopes sharing her story will lead to quicker diagnoses, more treatment options, and a cure or remission.

Gulf Island Fabrication (GIFI) trades at a significant discount to book value, and the author says there is a significant chance book value is not inflated. The company’s shares fell after a fourth-quarter report that included technical problems with two multi-purpose support vessels for Hornbeck Offshore, resulting in a $23.9 million loss and a $24.3 million quarterly loss on $37.3 million revenue. The offshore markets are described as under severe pressure, with oversupply of offshore support vessels and muted near-term prospects for new offshore platform building. 

The author highlights positive factors: GIFI has “no debt” and a backlog concentrated in shipyards and related services, including construction and engineering work tied to multiple vessel projects and selection as prime contractor for a SeaOne Carribean fuels supply project. The author notes possible future equity raising if additional contracts and earnings visibility improve. 

The main thesis is valuation. GIFI’s market capitalization is around $120 million, and the company is selling non-core Texas facilities, including a purchase option for the Texas South Yard for $55 million. The author argues this could make the remaining business close to $30 million, and expects that realizing asset values and confirming book value could support a return toward earlier-year share levels.

The passage describes Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) as a tool for real-time insight into glucose fluctuations in type 1 and type 2 diabetes, enabling clinical and research applications such as glycemic control, improved prediction of hypoglycemic and hyperglycemic events, and analysis of glucose dynamics. It introduces QoCGM, an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive CGM data analysis that automates preprocessing and derives multiple CGM metrics. QoCGM processes preprocessed CSV inputs with timestamp and glucose value columns, handles duplicate timestamps, and manages missing data either by interpolation using PCHIP or by removing missing periods. Metrics are organized into categories including basic descriptive statistics, time-in-range metrics (whole day and separate night/day), glycemic risk indicators, glycemic variability metrics, glycemic control indicators, and entropy/complexity measures. In an example study using CGM data from 331 insulin-treated T2DM participants (initial seven days), QoCGM produced metrics whose relationships were assessed using coefficient of determination (R²); results indicated substantial overlap among many metrics and some metrics with low R² values capturing distinct information. The authors conclude that QoCGM can support efficient use of CGM in research and help identify metrics with clinical relevance, while noting further research is needed for clinical implications.

European statesmen will likely focus on obtaining the means for recuperation after demobilization, with political and economic pressures driving intense negotiations. Access to sea-borne materials in a disputed belt from the Baltic to the Persian Gulf is presented as crucial, especially if outer-world communications can be controlled. Germany’s supremacy in the Near East is described as tied to its victory so far, but a major obstacle is the blockade and the need to organize reconstruction resources from the outer world and regain lost foreign markets. The passage describes two German imperialist schools: one led by Kühlmann-Helfferich favoring “accommodation” with Western nations and relying on overseas supplies, and the other led by the Fatherland Party favoring access through military and naval power supported by threats of force. Belgium is identified as a key pivot in German policy, with control of Belgium seen as enabling Germany to prevent England from landing an army in France and to leave France vulnerable.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch its fall-inspired lineup of foods and beverages on Aug. 28, bringing back pumpkin spice and adding maple and pecan flavors, including a maple-scented response expected for a new maple flavor. The menu additions include pumpkin cream cheese for bagels, pumpkin-flavored coffees, donuts and muffins, and limited-time maple pecan coffees and lattes plus a maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. The passage notes competitors Starbucks and McDonald's released spiced drinks last year but have not announced this year’s plans. Dunkin' has reported better-than-expected earnings for seven straight quarters, with strong sales attributed to limited-time menu items and product launches.

Sarasota County petitioned for writ of certiorari to seek judicial review of a declaratory statement issued by the Florida Department of Administration. The statement concluded that the definition of a development of regional impact (DRI) under Section 380.06(1) was limited by and applicable only to projects described by Fla. Admin. Code Rule 22F-2. The court denied the petition, finding the County lacked the requisite standing to invoke Chapter 380 procedures.

The passage discusses giving someone a day off and having a day-to-day approach. It notes two games in Boston where the first two periods were played well but the second period caused the game to get away. The speaker says the team needs to make every shift in every period count and plans to focus on one game at a time, with a plan for tomorrow. It mentions two demanding players, improved play beyond what their point total indicates, and credit for the opposing goaltender’s saves and the team’s defensive shutdown efforts. The speaker expresses confidence that things will improve soon and that they were ready for the challenge of winning, describing it as physically taxing due to travel and other demands.

ICICI Bank said its mortgage loan portfolio has crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player in the segment. The bank targets Rs 2 trillion by FY20, with the mortgage book half of its overall retail loan portfolio of about Rs 3 trillion and 52% of its total assets of USD 172.5 billion. Executive director Anup Bagchi said growth is expected to come mainly from tier II and III towns under PM’s Awas Yojna, where the average ticket size is just above Rs 30 lakh, and that the mortgage portfolio has low credit cost, including the LAP segment. To reach the target, ICICI Bank is pushing digitisation in mortgages, including online approvals for projects, an online repository of 30,000 approved projects across 40 cities, and adding 50% more loan processing centres from 1,050.

The passage describes how SARS-CoV-2 vaccine rollout initially reduced COVID-19 cases, hospitalisations, and deaths, but variant emergence—especially Omicron—reduced vaccine effectiveness against infection and transmission while effects against severe outcomes remained more durable. Omicron replaced prior variants globally and became dominant for over a year; repeated infections occurred due to waning immunity and reduced effectiveness of vaccine- and infection-induced immunity. Two Omicron-specific bivalent vaccines are available and showed higher immunogenicity against Omicron subvariants than original vaccines.

It proposes a modelling approach that estimates vaccine efficacy from immunogenicity, using neutralizing antibody titres (NAT) as a correlate of protection. The authors fit a Bayesian mechanistic model to England national vaccine effectiveness estimates for three vaccines (AZD1222, BNT162b2, mRNA-1273) against three endpoints (symptomatic mild disease, hospitalisation, death) for Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2, and incorporate booster effects and a variant fold reduction parameter for immune escape. Results estimate a 6.5-fold reduction in immune level against Omicron versus Delta and project waning over time, with more sustained hospitalisation protection than protection against infection or mild disease. The model predicts that switching to the bivalent vaccine provides additional protection after a fourth booster compared with continuing the original vaccine, though estimates depend on model assumptions.

The discussion highlights challenges and limitations, including difficulty separating infection- versus vaccine-induced immunity, lack of direct immunological measurements, assumptions about immune markers, and challenges distinguishing COVID-19-related hospitalisations or deaths from other causes. The authors conclude that validated models using immunogenicity data alone will be important for evaluating future booster strategies as SARS-CoV-2 evolves.

The passage reports new research that the average Brit wakes up three times during the night, with 1 in 10 waking 7 to 10 times. It lists 10 reasons people say they cannot get a good night’s sleep, including needing the toilet (47%); discomfort or aches (19%); snoring (41%); waking up on the bed edge (25%); tossing and turning (10.5%); partner talk or noises (10%); partner phone light (10%); partner watching TV or reading (4.6%); bad dreams (11%); and anxiety (6%). The survey involved 2,000 British adults, and psychologist Robert Stewart says sleep depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles, noting that REM is the lightest stage and that surrounding factors like noise or discomfort can affect whether people return to sleep smoothly.

The passage describes Larry Connors’ R3 (RSI 2) strategy from his 2009 book *High Probability ETF Trading*, which is a mean-reversion approach. It outlines the trading rules, including requiring the close to be above the 200-day moving average, entering based on specific conditions involving a 2-day RSI dropping three consecutive days (with the first day’s drop from a reading below 60) and entering when the 2-day RSI is below 10, with exit when the 2-day RSI is above 70. The passage reports backtest results: on an all-ETFs portfolio using 25 ETFs from 2000 to December 2020, the strategy had 992 trades, a 75% win ratio, an average gain per trade of 0.68%, a profit factor of 2.08, a maximum drawdown of -16% in August 2011, and a CAGR of 6.47%. It also reports results for QQQ and SPY allocation scenarios, noting a high profit factor (3.37) but a lower CAGR (2.69%) due to low time in the market.

Treasury bills maturities of N62.4 billion (91-day and 182-day) are expected this week, likely offset by a rollover, while an OMO maturity of N168.1 billion is also expected. Financial system liquidity remained negative last week due to increased primary market issuances and a CBN Retail SMIS foreign exchange auction. CBN OMO sales totalled N28.6 billion and kept open buy back (OBB) and overnight rates in double digits, which later fell after an OMO maturity inflow of N113.05 billion; rates then closed higher week-on-week. The treasury bills market closed bearish with benchmark yields rising to 18.5% due to tight liquidity, though average yields fell earlier in the week before trending up. In the forex market, the CBN continued weekly interventions and auctioned US$100 million SMIS to clear matured obligations; the naira rate stayed flat at N305.55/$1 and appreciated week-on-week to N365.91/$1 on FMDQ NAFEX, with similar activity on other segments. Analysts said stability would likely continue short-to-medium term and expected rates to remain around current levels. The domestic bond market was bearish with investors cautious ahead of an August bond auction. The Federal Executive Council approved dollar-backed treasury instruments to reduce Nigeria’s debt profile and extend treasury bill tenors, alongside approval of the 2018–2020 Medium Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper. The I&E forex window had attracted $4 billion from foreign investors between April and now, and the Bankers’ Committee said the economy was on the recovery path with FX rates nearing convergence.

Conservative Texas politicians ordered curriculum, syllabus, and course description reviews across six Texas public university systems after criticism over lessons on gender identity, including actions that followed a Texas A&M audit. Other systems, including University of North Texas and the University of Texas, issued expedited or comprehensive reviews to ensure compliance with state and federal guidance and board priorities. University leaders said there are no current laws banning professors from teaching transgender identity, but several institutions cited policies limiting what faculty can teach. The passage also describes increased public access to faculty syllabi through the Simple Syllabus platform, which can be searched by keywords, and recounts a case involving a lecturer whose syllabi were used for targeting; privacy features and advice to reduce detail in public syllabi are also mentioned.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit denied the petition for rehearing en banc and the petition for rehearing by the panel in the case of Earl Ringo v. Donald Roper. Judge Bye would have granted en banc rehearing. Judge Benton did not participate in the consideration or decision.

The Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs website is described as offbeat but educational and focused on dinosaurs. It includes factual reports from scientists and paleontologists, with links to scientific papers and magazine articles, as well as paleoart in many artistic styles. The site’s book reviews are highlighted as snarky and entertaining, sometimes discussing zoological inaccuracies in a sharp but not nasty way, and it also reviews toys, films, and TV shows. It features museum visit reports with photos from dinosaur exhibits worldwide. The site has been active since 2009, posts nearly every week, and provides a monthly dinosaur news roundup; its name is a play on *Love in the Time of Cholera*, and it uses a mascot on the homepage.

Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder marked by high blood glucose due to insufficient insulin production (type 1) or insulin resistance (type 2), affecting about 10% of the global population and predisposing people to complications such as cardiovascular disease, diabetic neuropathy, and nephropathy. People with diabetes are at increased risk for more severe COVID-19 outcomes, including intensive care, mechanical ventilation, and death. COVID-19 vaccination has been reported to reduce symptomatic infection, hospitalization, and mortality, and vaccination is described as a critical defense for individuals with diabetes.

In a longitudinal clinical trial (1 June 2023 to 31 October 2023), COVID-19 mRNA booster vaccination increased SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, spike IgG, and neutralizing abilities in healthy controls and diabetic patients without significant differences in immune response indices among groups. However, in pre-diabetic and diabetic subjects, boosters were associated with increased glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, shown by elevated HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglyceride, and TyG, with no significant changes in fasting blood glucose or insulin levels. In mice given repeated mRNA vaccine doses, the study reports impaired glucose tolerance, increased serum triglycerides, reduced insulin sensitivity response, and reduced insulin-induced Akt phosphorylation, suggesting impaired insulin sensitivity rather than insulin secretion. The study reports that metformin alleviated vaccine-induced insulin resistance in mice without affecting vaccine-related immune markers. The discussion concludes that booster doses weaken insulin sensitivity in pre-diabetic and diabetic patients and that long-term monitoring is needed.

Olivia Munn said she had clear mammograms and no breast cancer symptoms, but a two-minute online lifetime risk assessment led to her stage 1 breast cancer diagnosis at 43. She later sought an MRI, after learning she had a 37% risk. Her mother, Kim Munn, also completed the assessment and was diagnosed with more aggressive stage 1 breast cancer in July 2025. The passage says the assessment asks eight questions about factors such as age, race, and family history, and encourages earlier screening for those scoring 20% or higher, with Munn saying it should be standard care.

Hugh Jackman said he is being treated again for basal cell carcinoma, sharing photos with a bandage over his nose on Twitter and Instagram. He noted that it is the latest basal cell carcinoma and thanked frequent body checks and doctors. He has previously been treated for basal cell carcinoma at least four times, with his first treatment in November 2013. The passage describes Doug Ford kicking off his election campaign with a highly enthusiastic, concert-like event at the Toronto Congress Centre. Stan Lee, 95, was recently rushed to the hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat at home. Valeant Pharmaceuticals International Inc reported that it, along with J. Michael Pearson and Pershing Square Capital Management and William Ackman, entered into a litigation management agreement. The passage discusses players focusing on preparation and good habits that pay off in high-stakes games, maintaining the same approach despite different circumstances. Severe storms with tornadoes moved across the Southeast on Monday night, damaging homes and downing trees. Forecasters warned they could threaten more than 29 million people, with risks including powerful tornadoes, damaging winds up to 70 mph, and hail up to 3 inches. Northern Alabama reported power outages and at least three confirmed tornadoes in Huntsville, and Limestone County officials posted photos of significant property damage; no injuries were reported. Parts of northern Alabama and southern Tennessee were under tornado warnings, and a tornado watch was issued for much of northern Georgia. In addition, Jacksonville State University reported major roof damage at Pete Mathews Coliseum, school systems released students early, and the University of Alabama suspended operations from 6:30 p.m. to midnight, closing libraries and opening shelters. Alabama officials increased emergency staffing, and Gov. Kay Ivey urged residents to follow safety plans.

The passage describes evidence that inflammatory processes influence the pathogenesis and development of congestive heart failure (CHF), contributing to myocardial dysfunction, endothelial dysfunction, and cardiac cachexia. It reports that heart failure and progressing mitral valve disease are associated with higher inflammatory markers (including CRP, cytokines, and WBC) and that oxidative stress is linked to myocardium hypertrophy and heart failure. The study hypothesized that oxidative and “seditious” stress markers are linked to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) or other cardiomyopathies and measured selected inflammatory and oxidative stress markers.  

In a prospective study of 101 cardiomyopathy patients (43 DCM and 58 other cardiomyopathies) and 101 healthy controls, cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP and TNF-α than controls. TNF-α correlated positively with GPX and MDA, while IL-6 did not significantly correlate with GPX. NT-proBNP was associated with MDA and positively correlated with GPX activity across cardiomyopathy patients. The discussion concludes that inflammatory and oxidative stress interact in cardiomyopathy and that these relationships relate to disease severity. The authors state no conflict of interest.

Premier Li Keqiang said China will further open its economy and allow foreign and domestic firms to compete on equal terms. He said China will increase access to its services and manufacturing sectors and lower import tariffs, aiming for fair competition in China’s market for companies of all ownership types. Li said China’s integration with the world means closing its door would block development, and he stated there will be no forced technology transfers and that China will better protect intellectual property rights. The remarks come amid global trade war concerns, including US tariffs on steel and aluminium and expected new tariffs on Chinese technology and consumer goods, and debates over forced technology transfer claims.

Amadeus FiRe AG issued a voting rights announcement under Article 26, Section 1 of the WpHG, correcting a prior release from 10.02.2017 (17:36 CET/CEST) with the objective of Europe-wide distribution. The passage describes how patients undergoing cardiac surgery often need blood transfusions after the heart is opened for repair, but transfusions are linked to lower survival rates after AVR or CABG. In the U.S., about 48.9% of patients require transfusions, while at Huntington University Hospital (HUH) the rate was about 71% for AVR/CABG from 2011–2013. Dr. Frank Young led a blood conservation project beginning after he joined HUH in 2011, with a goal to cut blood product utilization during and after cardiac surgery by two-thirds within one year (by end of 2014), reduce transfusion rates to the national average, and save $2.5 million annually, with an estimated additional 125 lives saved per year over 10 years. The project faced challenges due to HUH’s complex organizational structure and limited direct control over nursing and other team members, as well as skepticism from veteran surgeons who preferred routine. The passage also outlines HUH’s staffing and reporting setup, the committee and value-based purchasing environment driving cost and quality pressure, relevant transfusion/bleeding statistics, and two blood conservation techniques Young planned to use: autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming.

Sheikh Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi issued a decree reducing the tourism tax paid by hotels and tourism companies in Ajman from 10% to 7%, effective immediately and running until December 31. The reduction is intended to promote tourism and improve the emirate’s investment environment. It follows a June recommendation by Sheikh Ammar bin Humaid Al Nuaimi to reduce the tax, and is expected to help realize Ajman Vision 2021, which aims to attract over 700,000 visitors to local hotels.

Meb Faber’s Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model strategy invests in stocks, bonds, and gold using a momentum rule: initiate or maintain positions if the monthly 3-bar moving average is above the 10-bar moving average. The strategy returned 13% annually from 1971 to 2015 and has been updated with backtests showing results after 2015. A described implementation invests equally among assets with positive momentum, with capital allocation varying by how many positions are held. Backtests using GLD, SPY, and TLT (starting from 2006) produced a CAGR of 8.9%, a win rate of 57%, a profit factor of 1.6, and a maximum drawdown of 18%, with notably low drawdowns even in poor years like 2022. The passage also discusses momentum investing generally and reports a study where a momentum-based approach outperformed the S&P 500, while noting the need to filter survivorship bias.

The passage outlines statistical methods for determining sample size and for general, efficacy, PK/PD, and safety analysis considerations. It compares dasiglucagon 0.6 mg with placebo using an exponential time-to-recovery assumption and a stratified 2-sided log-rank test, planning 20 patients in the dasiglucagon arm and 10 in the placebo arm with 90% power at a 5% significance level (45-minute follow-up). It specifies analysis population definitions (safety set, full analysis set, per protocol set), 2-sided testing at 0.05, summary/statistical presentation rules, handling of missing data (no imputation), covariate adjustments, and hierarchical testing for confirmatory primary and secondary efficacy endpoints. It describes methods for time to plasma glucose recovery (Kaplan-Meier, stratified log-rank, sensitivity/supportive analyses including censoring rules), secondary recovery rates (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel or ANOVA if needed), and PK/PD data presentation rules (including LLOQ handling and interpolation supportive analyses). It also specifies safety analysis set usage, adverse event definitions and coding (MedDRA), and planned tabulations/listings for safety endpoints such as local tolerability, AEs/SAEs, ECG, laboratory parameters, immunogenicity (descriptive ADA incidence), and extent of exposure details.

The passage defines soccer passing directions terminology as the line or path a ball is expected to take from the passer to a potential receiver, using general terms applied when a player faces the attacking goal. It outlines directional categories such as forward (angled right/left, straight), clockwise directions around the player, and back-related terms (e.g., back, behind, straight back, back and right/left angled, diagonal, reverse). It also provides definitions for other common terms including passes on the ground or in the air (e.g., long beyond about 30 yards, short up to about 15 yards, deep/upfield), positional areas (e.g., corner, post, near post, far post, left/right center), and pass types based on relation to the touchline (e.g., parallel, down the line, flat, lateral, square, diagonal). Additional terms include center, back heel, outlet, interface (between two defenders to an attacker in front of goal), passing angle (degree from straight ahead to avoid interception), possession, reverse field, straight lines, switch fields, and horizontal/vertical axes of the field.

Samsung Galaxy J5 Prime was unveiled in India at Rs 14,900, featuring a 5-inch HD TFT display, a 13MP rear camera, and a 5MP front camera. It has started receiving the Android 7.0 Nougat OTA update in the UAE, with SamMobile noting imported India models may receive it while a full rollout could take longer. The update, originally launched with Android 6.0 Marshmallow, is a little over 1GB and includes features such as improved multi-window usability, notifications, quick settings, dual messenger, stricter app permissions, a new emoji set, better battery optimisation, bug fixes, stability improvements, and speed optimisations. U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping by more than 650 points and falling below 26,000 for the first time since breaking that level two-and-a-half weeks earlier. The Dow declined 2.5%, while the S&P 500 fell 2.2% and the Nasdaq Composite declined 2%. The drop capped the Dow’s worst week in two years. Analysts attributed the selloff to fears that a stronger-than-expected jobs report would lead the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates more than expected, which could move investors from stocks into bonds. Fidelity’s Jurrien Timmer said the market had underestimated rate increases, and noted that recognizing interest-rate changes now was healthier than having a larger crash. The Labor Department reported January job growth of 200,000 versus 190,000 expected, and wage growth of 2.9%, which analysts said increased expectations for tighter monetary policy. Beginning with GA10x (Ampere) GPUs, ROPs are moved into the GPC rather than being tied to the memory controller and L2 cache, increasing raster performance by boosting ROP count and reducing throughput mismatches. GA102 combines seven GPCs with 16 ROP units each for 112 ROPs, improving multisample anti-aliasing, pixel fillrate, and blending.

GA10x SMs are partitioned into four processing blocks sharing a combined L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem. Compared with Turing, GA10x increases L1/shared capacity, adds FP32 processing on both datapaths in each partition to double FP32 peak throughput, changes Tensor Core count and generation (third-generation Tensor Cores), and supports sparse matrix acceleration via the Sparsity feature for up to 2x throughput on matrix operations. GA10x also includes second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing and adds a motion-blur-related Interpolate Triangle Position unit, enabling faster ray-traced motion blur.

The GA10x platform supports concurrent RT and graphics/compute work within SMs, unified shared memory/L1 reconfigurable allocations for workloads, faster shared memory bandwidth, and GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling for up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. It also introduces RTX IO for GPU-based loading and lossless decompression using DirectStorage, offloading work from CPU to GPU to improve I/O performance. The passage further describes data-center GPUs (A40, A6000) and display/video features including HDMI 2.1, fifth-generation NVDEC for hardware video decoding (including AV1), and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding.

Peloton launched new AI-powered fitness equipment, including a $6,695 AI treadmill and updates to its Bike+, Tread+, and Row+ with Peloton IQ, an AI coaching system that provides real-time feedback, counts reps, and suggests weight adjustments and training plans. The company is also overhauling its Cross Training Series with personalization features and a movement tracking camera. Peloton raised prices across its lineup, with the original Bike up to $1,695, Bike+ to $2,695, the base treadmill to $3,295, and Tread+ to $6,695, while monthly membership fees increased by $5 to $49.99. RaySearch and Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG signed a partnership agreement to integrate the RayStation treatment planning system and the RayCare oncology information system with Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG’s brachytherapy systems. The integration is intended to provide Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG with a complete brachytherapy solution, including treatment devices, planning, and oncology information management. The passage says the 48-inch LG C4 OLED is priced at $800 on Amazon for Prime Day, which the author calls the lowest price they have ever seen. The passage discusses evaluating the success of green or health-related real estate decisions through different stakeholder perspectives, using examples from the Winthrop Center and a separate project at 425 Park Avenue. The project also faced financing disruption when COVID hit, pausing construction, though later financing was arranged and occupancy certification was expected. The lecture then describes how “Passive House” and similar ideas spread from pilots in risk-tolerant segments to broader adoption, supported by studies of cost premiums and subsequent regulation influence in Massachusetts, leading to additional large Passive House projects.  

The discussion transitions to 425 Park Avenue, an office project aimed at “health and wellness.” It outlines project size and challenges (ground lease, cash flow strain, financing uncertainty, and zoning requiring retention of 25% of the structure), then compares market conditions among locations and the demand shift toward health. The project’s health approach considers indoor air quality measures and WELL-style certification, with participants debating whether the projected rent premium justifies added capital and operating costs amid uncertainty about technology and operating assumptions. The case concludes that success depends not only on “science and performer” metrics but also on how tenants and the market are engaged, and it notes that 425 Park Avenue experienced distress tied to structural and project risk rather than the health strategy itself.

The speaker says the team was not good enough offensively, physically, quickly, or defensively, and that specialty teams were also not strong, while noting they can improve in many areas. Lecture 16 discusses how beliefs can affect utility, including anticipatory utility and information acquisition. It explains that when people cannot change future outcomes (e.g., Huntington’s disease), overoptimistic beliefs may still increase utility by improving how people feel, though overoptimism can distort decisions when actions depend on the true state (e.g., seeking treatment). The lecture also describes disappointment as another reason people might limit overoptimism, and presents evidence of overoptimism from studies such as Weinstein’s, including overestimating positive outcomes and underestimating negative ones, as well as overconfidence in abilities. It contrasts this with survey results for MIT students and discusses possible reasons for underconfidence among female students, including motivation and feedback.

The lecture then introduces “ego utility” as another motivation for inflated self-beliefs and summarizes research arguing that positive illusions can support mental health, contrasting this with “depressive realism.” It outlines factors that affect positive biases, such as personal importance of outcomes, availability of objective information, feedback ambiguity, and perceived control.

Next, it reviews evidence that biased self-beliefs translate into behavior, including lab experiments (e.g., Eil and Rao) showing asymmetric processing of positive versus negative self-related information, and real-world evidence where overconfidence can lead to worse outcomes (e.g., trading losses and managerial hubris and value-destroying mergers). The lecture concludes by shifting to heuristics and biases, arguing that Bayesian learning is hard; people use shortcuts that speed decisions but can produce systematic errors. It highlights three well-known deviations from Bayesian updating—gambler’s fallacy, hot-hand fallacy, and base-rate neglect—along with heuristic explanations such as the representativeness and availability heuristics, and discusses implications for policy and information design depending on whether people miss information, have wrong theories, or have motivated beliefs.

The speaker praises Oskar and Barbie as underrated for intelligence, noting Oskar’s timing, hard work, and good chemistry with his line. The passage explains why lasers are difficult to maintain, describing how defects and increased power can cause unwanted colors, instability, and distorted beam profiles. It then outlines how topological insulators work: electrons form two energy bands with a gap in the bulk, while surface states can conduct in a way protected from scattering because reversing direction requires difficult spin-flip processes. It connects this to lasers by describing topological insulator lasers that use protected states to produce light with a specific energy, momentum, and well-defined wavelength and spatial profile. The passage describes a model using a 2D crystal of coupled optical waveguide rings that can be excited so that only edge light travels, with protection controlled by phase-shifting between rings; unprotected states scatter out. Researchers modeled the design, fabricated tightly controlled structures, and built crystals with both protected and unprotected edge states. They report that the protected-state laser is more efficient, continues functioning after knocking out rings, and does not generate new colors as power increases, unlike the unprotected-edge laser. The passage concludes that such lasers are important for 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

The passage describes phlogopite (KMg3(AlSi3O10)(OH)2) as a monoclinic, layered mineral with low resistance to ionizing radiation under conventional low-dose-rate conditions, with applications including insulation, reinforcement, construction materials, coatings, and radiation-related uses. Its radiation susceptibility underlies a geological dating method based on recoil tracks from natural U and Th decay, and its layered structure motivates radiation-damage studies for radionuclide waste storage and dielectric uses in 2D optoelectronics. It also outlines a unified simulation approach using the XTANT-3 code to model nonequilibrium electronic excitation and coupled atomic dynamics, employing transport Monte Carlo, Boltzmann collision integrals, and tight-binding molecular dynamics. Results for irradiation by 92 eV, 10 fs laser pulses show distinct dose-dependent damage mechanisms: at ~0.17 eV/atom, hydrogen detach/migrate; at ~0.4 eV/atom, Mg begins liquid-like diffusion; at ~0.5 eV/atom, the atomic lattice disorders; at ~0.9 eV/atom, the electronic bandgap collapses and the material becomes metallic; and at higher doses (~2 eV/atom), nonthermal atomic heating accelerates elements such as oxygen and potassium. The passage concludes that irradiated phlogopite can exhibit varied transient states that may be tailored by adjusting the deposited dose, and notes agreement between the computed hydrogen-migration threshold (~0.17 eV/atom) and experiments (~1000 kGy = 0.2 eV/atom).

The Philadelphia Eagles and New England Patriots have been preparing Super Bowl game plans for two weeks, while law enforcement has planned security for two years for Super Bowl LII in Minneapolis at U.S. Bank Stadium. Minneapolis Police, led by about 840 officers, will coordinate with dozens of federal, state, and local agencies because it is not large enough to handle the operation alone. The NFL will limit and inspect spectator items and begin stadium screening more than four hours before the game; attendees will also be prescreened at indoor locations like the Mall of America to avoid waiting outside. Additional regional concerns include previous incidents and fears related to Al-Shabaab, while Homeland Security Investigations will monitor illegal counterfeit goods. The National Guard has been called up, with more than 400 guardsmen providing security support. The overall goal is safe and enjoyable event participation.
