The passage describes Resource Generation (RG), a 20-year-old nonprofit that helps wealthy millennials discuss their “money stories” and use their money to fight social, economic, and racial injustice. RG works with about 500 members (ages 18–35) across 17 U.S. chapters, offering education on budgeting and accountability and campaign work for “structural change” on issues like health care, taxes, and workers’ rights. The organization says public silence around money and class normalizes inequality and that, unlike traditional philanthropy, it teaches principles rather than pooling funds, emphasizing that people most affected by injustice should decide how money is spent. It highlights members’ experiences and motivations, including shifts in how they view identity and wealth, and argues that wealth inequality is tied to institutionalized racism and is reinforced by inheritance. The passage also includes example member profiles and reported giving before and after joining RG.

Since Israel’s establishment in 1948, Druze education was part of the Arab school system. In the late 1960s and early 1970s, Druze leaders sought greater ethnic consciousness and demanded that Druze education be separated from Arab education. The Israeli Ministry of Education and Culture implemented this decision by establishing a unit for Druze education and culture, developing independent curricula, textbooks, and unique contents. Within five years, the unit created an independent education system regarding pedagogy, curriculum, and educational resources, and the Druze school system aimed to build Druze youth identity while also fostering loyalty to the state.  

The study investigates how separating Druze education from Arab education affected eligibility rates for the matriculation certificate and the number of Druze students in higher education, examining perspectives from Druze high school principals, supervisors, and trainee principals, and also considers students’ preparation for academia. Interviews with nine educators generated eight main themes. Interviewees reported rising Druze education achievements, especially in matriculation exam eligibility, and expressed satisfaction and pride. They highlighted continuing investment in development and improvements, described the Druze study program as sharing many universal subjects while emphasizing “Druze heritage,” and cited factors such as the quality of teaching staff, sociocultural liberal-modern trends, identity-related motivation, and ongoing academic advocacy by schools. Some principals viewed the separation as accelerating development of Druze education, while others argued that high achievements were not directly caused by separation and pointed instead to internal Druze actions, including educational leadership and sociocultural or family factors. The study also notes a perceived gap between high matriculation/secondary achievements and preparedness for academic studies, calling for interventions and better alignment between matriculation preparation and academic requirements.

On March 7, 2018, NVIDIA Corporation’s Compensation Committee adopted the Variable Compensation Plan for Fiscal Year 2019. The plan allows eligible executive officers to earn a variable cash payment based on achievement of specified corporate performance goals, with performance goals set based on fiscal year 2019 revenue and levels including threshold, base operating plan, and stretch operating plan. Participants must remain employees through the payment date unless otherwise determined. Target award opportunities for base operating plan achievement were $1,100,000 (110%) for Jen-Hsun Huang, $300,000 (33%) for Colette M. Kress, $650,000 (68%) for Ajay K. Puri, $250,000 (29%) for Debora Shoquist, and $250,000 (29%) for Timothy S. Teter. The plan is filed as Exhibit 10.1 and is incorporated by reference.

Alex Caruso said he wasn’t sure what to expect from the Lakers’ two-way player system when he became the inaugural two-way player. After 42 days with the Lakers by Wednesday’s game against the Magic, he has three days left before a cut-off and then would spend the rest of the season with the South Bay Lakers. Caruso has appeared in 25 games for the Lakers and has averaged 2.6 points and 1.9 assists, with a standout performance on Jan. 21 against the Knicks. Lakers coach Luke Walton said the system helps players get familiar with the team and allows more continuity than repeatedly signing new 10-day contract players. Caruso’s two-way deal runs through next season, and he will earn nearly $300,000 this year compared with a G-League contract max of $26,000 for six months. In South Bay, Caruso has averaged 19 points and 7.4 assists in 25 games.

Williams Jones & Associates LLC reduced its stake in Star Bulk Carriers Corp. by 52.6% in the 2nd quarter, leaving it with 31,600 shares after selling 35,000 shares; its holdings were worth $311,000 at the end of the reporting period. Other institutional investors also reported changes in their stakes, including GLG Partners LP, Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Citadel Advisors LLC, Impala Asset Management LLC, and Capital Fund Management S.A. The passage urges the public to “trust the government” regarding a bird flu outbreak in Pampanga, saying the situation will be controlled within a few days. It describes government restrictions limited to a 7-kilometer radius around San Luis as ground zero, including controlling poultry and poultry products and culling chicken Monday and Tuesday to isolate infected birds. It states that the detected virus strain H5 in birds is not transmissible to humans, though additional samples were sent to an Australian laboratory to check for H5N6, with results expected within 12 days. The Department of Health says virus transfer to humans is difficult or remote, there is no sustained human-to-human transmission so far, and it advises proper precautions, notes safety measures and epidemiologists deployed in farms, and testing of ill workers.

Alcoa reported a large loss in fourth-quarter earnings but investors are focusing on its adjusted earnings outlook. Two contributors discuss why Alcoa may be a buy or still uncertain. Rich Duprey says Alcoa has defied expectations since the Arconic spinoff and expects improved results, highlighting a significant increase in bauxite production and new bauxite supply contracts worth nearly $600 million over 2016 and 2017; he notes potential for earnings growth if guidance holds but mentions risks from higher prices. Jason Hall argues Alcoa’s stock may appear cheap versus asset value, but warns that book value fell due to rightsizing actions and impairments, with possible further write-downs. He also cites risks tied to trade policy, raw material dependence, and aluminum price levels, concluding that it remains hard to value and he is staying on the sidelines.

The World Health Organization recommends European countries prepare strategically for potential winter surges of COVID-19 cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, adapting response strategies to a largely immunized population. Contact tracing and quarantine have been eased, but case isolation remains central to reducing SARS-CoV-2 spread; isolation lengths have varied by country, and fall 2022 booster vaccination uptake is uncertain due to declining booster coverage.

This study assessed testing and isolation strategies used in France, Belgium, and Italy during winter 2022/2023. Using vaccination data adjusted for waning immunity, a multi-country survey of 4,594 participants, and a mathematical model parameterized to Omicron subvariants, the study evaluated how differing protocol rules and adherence would affect infection dynamics.

Survey results showed high testing adherence when symptomatic and lower adherence when asymptomatic, with near-universal declared compliance to rapid isolation when symptomatic. Protocol effectiveness varied: under a scenario with an effective reproductive number R=1.6 without interventions, testing and isolation using the French protocol reduced R by 18.4%, the Belgian protocol by 17.2%, and the Italian protocol by 24.4%. None of the protocols alone reduced R below 1. The analysis also found reduced effectiveness if testing required payment (up to 20 euros) and differences in isolation duration and exit testing that affected onward transmission after isolation. The discussion concluded that simpler isolation/testing guidelines could maintain performance while reducing testing resources, and that booster uptake remains important to control the winter wave. The study noted limitations including a non–age-stratified model and not modeling healthcare impacts such as hospital admissions.

The passage is a collection of news excerpts about California’s 2001 energy crisis. It describes local air pollution and price refund proceedings, federal and state actions involving potential overbilling and price justification by power suppliers, the role of state agencies purchasing electricity, and related financial and customer impacts such as rolling blackout “Block 50” changes, possible utility bankruptcy threats, and business disruptions due to billing and service problems. It also includes perspectives on efforts to address energy supply and conservation, reactions to OPEC oil production cuts, and commentary criticizing political arguments focused on whether electricity generators are based in out of state.

Vienna topped Mercer’s annual quality of living survey for the ninth straight year, with Zurich second and Auckland and Munich tied for third; Vancouver ranked fifth in North America. Singapore led Asia and Montevideo led Latin America, while Durban was the top African city. London fell to 41. The survey evaluates 231 cities on factors including political stability, healthcare, education, crime, recreation and transport. The report said living standards rose most over 20 years in some eastern European cities, and that eastern cities increasingly attract multinational businesses. Baghdad remained last for the past decade, affected by sectarian violence since 2003, with Sanaa and Damascus ranking above it.

The passage compares playoffs and Olympics formats, noting that playoffs allow teams to recover even after going down, while Olympics end after quarterfinals, leaving no further chance. It also says the Olympics format is more draining and longer, making it hard to relax until it ends. The passage further describes a coach’s behavior: he is relaxed during preparation and games if the person is doing their job and focused, but after stepping off the ice he tries to help the person regain attention or mental sharpness. It concludes that there has been mutual understanding without many words.

The passage is an Enron- and markets-focused set of news clippings dated Nov. 11, 2001, covering Enron’s decline and related financial and political issues. It describes Enron’s agreement to be acquired by Dynegy for about $9 billion, following an SEC probe, investor flight, accounting errors, and losses tied to off-balance-sheet partnerships. Coverage also discusses broader market themes, including a weekly stock market rise linked to Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts, Wall Street scrutiny of pro forma accounting and restructuring charges, and debate over a Senate stimulus bill criticized as a set of special-interest provisions. Other excerpts address the impact of Enron’s collapse on Houston’s business image and the status of electricity deregulation amid the California energy crisis and shifting energy-company performance.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Quarterly Report on Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2017. The report includes unaudited consolidated financial statements showing total assets of $25,053,726 (in thousands) and total liabilities of $18,885,353 as of March 31, 2017. For the three months ended March 31, 2017, total revenues were $2,696,270, gross profit was $667,946, and net loss was $397,181 (with net loss attributable to common stockholders of $330,277). The report also presents statements of comprehensive loss and cash flows, and includes notes covering topics such as overview of the company and segments (automotive; energy generation and storage), significant accounting policies (including resale value guarantees), business combinations (including Grohmann acquisition and SolarCity acquisition-related updates), goodwill and intangible assets, fair value of financial instruments, inventory, solar energy systems, property and equipment, other long-term liabilities, customer deposits, convertible and other debt, equity and stock-based compensation, commitments and contingencies (including legal proceedings), and related party transactions.

The passage describes a class session focused on sustainability strategy, reflecting on an article by Porter and discussing how companies should (and should not) approach corporate social responsibility (CSR). The professor outlines administrative plans for future discussions with a company (EMC) and then reviews the article’s main ideas, including criticism of relying on CSR alone and avoiding “index traps” where companies target rankings rather than meaningful internal improvement. The discussion covers Porter’s critique of common motivations for CSR—moral arguments, license to operate, reputation, and sustainability—arguing they are incomplete or problematic due to issues such as measurability and unclear tradeoffs. The professor then explains Porter’s framework for prioritizing social issues using concepts like generic social impacts, value chain social impacts, and social dimensions of competitive context, distinguishing between avoiding/mitigating issues and pursuing “strategic CSR” that aligns sustainability with competitiveness and core capabilities, with examples including Whole Foods, Siemens, GE, Toyota, Nestlé, and UPS/FedEx. The later portion addresses implementing strategy through life cycle thinking and measurement (e.g., life cycle assessment), determining responsibility boundaries across supply chains, and setting goals and targets tied to credible metrics and operational data rather than relying only on end-of-year reporting. The professor emphasizes that measurement enables actionable decision-making, notes challenges in supply chain depth and supplier compliance, and concludes with guidance for a team project comparing companies using CDP-related performance and course concepts.

Sugar output in Tamil Nadu is expected to fall by more than a third in the season beginning October due to the worst drought in more than a century. Sakthi Sugars’ executive chairman M. Manickam said Tamil Nadu is likely to produce 600,000 tonnes of sugar in 2017/18, down from around 1 million tonnes in the current season to September 2017. He described the situation as very grim, noting that drought has also affected other parts of southern India and forced hundreds of farmers to protest in New Delhi for government help after crop losses and increased loan-taking. India is forecast to produce 20.3 million tonnes of sugar by September 2017, 5% lower than a previous forecast. The monsoon is critical for India’s rain-fed farmland, though the government meteorological department said India could be unscathed from the El Nino pattern. Tamil Nadu’s cotton production in 2016/17 is also expected to drop 21% to 550,000 bales.

The passage is an overview of an MIT class on the mathematics and algorithms behind folding and unfolding geometric objects. The instructor, Erik Demaine, explains that the class covers geometry, folding, and related algorithmic problems, with lectures covering the full field in a “bleeding edge” way. He describes key application areas such as robotics, computer graphics, manufacturing, optics, medical uses, space deployment, biology (especially protein folding), sculpture, and interactive architecture, and notes that the field has both old problems and many developments in recent years.

He outlines main structures studied: linkages, paper (origami), and polyhedra, including foldability and design questions. He categorizes results by universality (constructing folding for many goals), decision/recognition algorithms (determining foldability), and hardness limits (no efficient algorithms). He then summarizes class structure (mandatory lecture attendance for credit, limited problem sets, and a required project and presentation for credit) and describes potential projects and an optional weekly open problem session.

Finally, he previews content for the lecture’s main topics: linkage folding (including motivation from mechanisms like Watt and Peaucellier linkages), rigidity and intersection-free folding (often very difficult), paper folding (e.g., flat-foldability, roadmap refolding problems, and design methods like Origamizer and TreeMaker), and polyhedron unfolding and reverse folding (edge unfolding, general unfolding, and related open problems). He ends by introducing hinged dissections, including a theorem about folding polygons of equal area using a single chain of hinged pieces, and mentions related practical transformer-like and interactive sculpture applications.

The passage describes a Metrocosm animation now on YouTube showing the growth of the world’s cities, starting with Eridu achieving city status by about 3000 BC. For each city, the map presents the date of the earliest recorded population figure, with dot size indicating population at that time. It states that 54% of the world lives in cities today and that 75% is expected by 2030, noting that 34% lived in cities in 1960. It says urbanization’s history was difficult to track beyond 1960 because the UN World Urbanization Prospects dataset goes back only to 1950. A Yale-led research team released a report enabling analysis back to 3700 BC by digitizing, geocoding, and standardizing data from past studies, producing a dataset of cities, locations, and populations over time. The passage notes the dataset has limitations and is “far from comprehensive,” with uneven regional representation and some cities appearing centuries after founding, but calls the amount of data assembled impressive.

The passage introduces the convection-diffusion equation as a core transport model and focuses on steady convection-dominated regimes, where solutions develop narrow layers that are difficult for mesh-based methods. It discusses stabilization needs for classical finite element approaches due to oscillations, and reviews strengths and weaknesses of cell-centered finite volume (CCFV) and discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations. It proposes a bound-preserving coupling of CCFV and DG for steady convection-diffusion problems using an adaptive procedure: if DG cell averages violate bounds beyond a tolerance, the approximation is reverted to CCFV in a small neighborhood, then conservative slope limiters are applied. The passage also surveys related techniques for suppressing spurious oscillations and presents the mathematical model problem, domain decomposition into FV and DG regions, mesh assumptions for TPFA admissibility in the FV region, and the construction of the coupled CCFV/DG discretization, including function spaces and jump definitions across interfaces.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2018 with the SEC. The filing includes unaudited consolidated financial statements showing total assets of $27.91 billion and total liabilities and equity of $27.91 billion as of June 30, 2018, and net losses of $742.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2018 and $1.527 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2018. The passage outlines MIT OpenCourseWare’s course plan for building secure systems. It explains that the semester will use lecture discussions of assigned research papers and lab assignments focused on exploiting and defending security vulnerabilities, starting with buffer overflow attacks in a provided web server and using different programming languages across labs. It emphasizes that security involves policies, threat models, and mechanisms, and that security is hard because attacks can violate assumptions and because systems are often compromised due to bugs or incorrect assumptions. The lecture discusses how policies, threat models, and mechanisms can fail, giving examples such as weakened security from password recovery questions, multi-system vulnerabilities illustrated by a Gmail reset incident involving Apple and Amazon, changing or unrealistic threat models (e.g., Kerberos key length and certificate authorities), and mechanism failures from issues like inconsistent authentication rate-limiting in iCloud interfaces, missing access checks in a Citibank URL workflow, poor randomness seeding in Android’s Bitcoin key generation, encoding/name-handling discrepancies in SSL certificates, and buffer overflow exploitation in a simplified C program. It concludes by noting that reducing the number of mechanisms needed to enforce security (minimizing the trusted computing base) can mitigate mechanism bugs and that defenses against buffer overflows will be covered in later lectures.

The passage introduces vdW heterostructure materials as integrated, tunable building blocks for nanoscale quantum circuitry, emphasizing proximity-induced quantum phenomena. It discusses excitons in TMD/hBN systems and how magnetic vdW materials (vdW magnets) can split otherwise nonmagnetic excitonic states via a proximity field, motivating an ab initio approach that can treat proximity effects beyond the single-particle picture. It describes the use of higher-order quasiparticle self-consistent GW methods (QSGW and QSGŴ, with vertex ladder diagrams) and, in general, possible augmentation with DMFT, to model the WSe2/CrI3 interface and determine emergent excitons and magnetic-field-induced effects on WSe2 excitons. Results include optimized bilayer/trilayer structures, band alignment changes from type II (LDA) to type I (QSGW/QSGŴ), preservation of WSe2 A and B excitons, identification of magnetic CrX3 Frenkel-like excitons, and discovery of new interlayer excitons appearing between A and B excitons with enhanced brightness. The passage also reports magnetic splittings of A and B excitons that depend on AFM vs FM trilayer configurations, and concludes that these heterostructures provide platforms for in-situ generation and control of interlayer excitonic states, with robustness of the interlayer excitons emphasized despite sensitivity of splittings to band alignments. Methods and data availability details are provided, including computational parameters and exciton wavefunction analysis.

The passage describes how polar topological quasiparticles (polar skyrmions and antiskyrmions) were studied in barium titanate (BaTiO₃, BT) and then extended to Zr-substituted BT (Ba(ZrxTi1−x)O3, BZT). It focuses on BZT with a 12.5% Zr ordered superlattice and on randomly substituted compositions. In the ordered 12.5% superlattice, finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations at 1 K show stable nanodomains whose plane-resolved topological charge alternates along the nanodomain axis: one chemically defined half hosts a −2 antiskyrmion decomposed into six −1/3 “topological quarks,” while the other hosts a +4 skyrmion decomposed into six +2/3 quarks. The two halves share a similar vortex geometry, but differ by an integer offset of +1 per vortex due to chemical unit-cell doubling and a resulting change in local anisotropy. For randomly distributed Zr, nontrivial topological textures remain stable at 1 K across 0–12.5% Zr, but disorder pins and distorts vortex lines, causing irregular fractional-charge conversions and “skyrmion-glass”-like behavior with fluctuations of the plane-resolved charge along the axis. Thermal stability tests show that critical temperatures depend non-monotonically on Zr concentration and domain size: stability decreases with initial Zr substitution (minimum near 6–8%) and partially recovers toward 12.5%, with larger domains generally more robust. Finally, near room temperature (293 K), the 12.5% ordered superlattice can sustain field-written nontrivial textures under a local electric field aligned with [111], yielding Q = +4 on each (111) projection, while the random 12.5% composition does not retain a single domain under the same bias and instead forms multidomain states.

The passage presents Michael Liersch’s top five tips for investors, arguing that most people can succeed with a plan, good perspective, and staying the course. It recommends making a budget to see where money goes, reframing investment decisions by focusing on longer-term goals and potential opportunities during market declines, staying patient because returns are a long game, not relying on only oneself by seeking second opinions from people or advisers, and starting with small steps such as paying down credit cards, contributing small amounts to retirement accounts, or automating transfers to build momentum.

The passage explains that the reproduction number (R) is widely used to measure pathogen spread, but it does not account for time-varying testing/diagnostics, which affects case counts. It argues that because testing levels change and because observed transmissions depend on who is tested, R can be biased when tests vary over time. The authors introduce an acceleration index (ε), defined as an elasticity measuring how cases respond proportionally to changes in tests, and describe ε as a unit-free, test-controlled measure of viral acceleration. They derive a theoretical relationship showing that ε corrects R by accounting for test intensity, and that R overestimates or underestimates viral acceleration relative to ε depending on whether test intensity is higher or lower than infectivity intensity. Empirically, they apply the comparison to France (May 13, 2020–October 26, 2022, including vaccination and lockdown periods) and report substantial discrepancies, especially during the Omicron wave in 2022, which they attribute to bias from not correcting for changing test volumes. They extend similar comparisons to five other countries, finding that R’s bias can vary by country and time period. The passage concludes that if authorities aim to measure viral acceleration accurately, they should use ε or use R together with test and infectivity intensities, and it recommends including ε-type test-controlled measures in epidemic dashboards for public health decisions.

A Poland Local Board of Education dissolved the contract of Poland Seminary High School teacher Cassandra Kibler after an allegation she had an inappropriate relationship with a student. Simone Askew became the first Black woman to lead the Long Grey Line at the U.S. Military Academy, assuming duties Monday as the first captain of West Point’s 4,400-member Corps of Cadets. After a 12-mile march Monday morning with 1,200 new cadets in basic training, she described the role as humbling but exciting. She advised aspiring young women to seek mentorship and be “vessels to be poured into.” Pat Locke and Simone’s mother, Pam Askew, said she is a role model and a natural leader.

Syrian rebels in southern provinces Daraa and Quneitra faced a deadline in negotiations with Russia to either accept tough surrender terms or face renewed military attacks by President Bashar al-Assad’s forces. Russia is backing a two-week offensive while brokering talks with rebel towns; more than 30 towns have already agreed to return to regime control. Rebels were to meet a Russian delegation to decide on a proposal for a regime takeover of the rest of the south. Russia rejected rebel terms earlier and countered with conditions including no population transfers in the south, army return to pre-2011 positions, and local police taking over towns in coordination with Russian military police, warning the Wednesday meeting would be the last day to negotiate. The offensive has expanded regime control of Daraa province to about 60% and displaced 270,000 to 330,000 people, with Human Rights Watch urging Jordan and Israel to allow asylum-seekers. Reports cited civilian deaths, including a land mine blast killing 11 family members returning to a town that had reconciled with the government. The UN Security Council will hold an emergency meeting, and Jordan’s foreign minister met Russia’s Sergei Lavrov, while Lavrov said Moscow hopes rebels will lay down their weapons and reconcile.

The study examined Ethiopian national education policy documents and how secondary school principals and teachers conceptualize curriculum differentiation (CD). It analyzed documents such as the 2012 Guidelines for CD and IEP, the 2020 General Education Curriculum Framework (GECF), and the 2023 Education and Training Policy (ETP), and collected interview data from two school principals and 17 subject teachers across one regular and one special day secondary school. The national documents conceptualize CD differently: the guidelines emphasize differentiating curriculum components (contents, instructional processes, assessment strategies, and learning environments) in inclusive classrooms, while other documents conceptualize differentiation through tracks/streams/fields of study and different school types. Principals’ and teachers’ conceptualizations varied across levels including lack of awareness, divergent views, and alignment with policy intentions. Factors such as the absence of coherent policy guidance and limited commitment to reform contributed to these differences. The study concludes that there is a lack of alignment and awareness, and calls for clearer operationalization of CD in curriculum frameworks so practitioners can implement policy intentions consistently.

The Central Bureau of Investigation told the Supreme Court it has initiated a probe into the SSC question paper leak case. The CBI said a preliminary inquiry was launched after complaints about the leak. The court granted petitioners liberty to approach it if they were not satisfied and said a court-monitored probe was not necessary. The Centre had ordered a CBI probe into the alleged leak in a Staff Selection Commission test after the SSC requested it over allegations that CGL Tier II Exam-2017 questions were leaked. SSC candidates have been protesting outside the SSC office since February 27 demanding a CBI probe.

Traps catching more than 500 mosquitoes are being set in central Illinois by the Macon Mosquito Abatement District at 19 locations to enable rapid West Nile virus testing after the virus appeared unusually early. Jason Probus said using a Decatur lab allows mosquito capture, testing, and treatment in less than 24 hours, with testing results available by Tuesday afternoon and potential action by Tuesday night. Probus and director Sam Force said the process previously took about a week but now allows quicker monitoring of potential trouble areas. The Illinois Department of Public Health reported the state’s first human case in mid-May, two months earlier than last year, and the CDC agreed to investigate. No human cases have been reported in Macon County this year, though a positive mosquito test occurred in June. The passage also notes that West Nile virus is spread by infected mosquito bites and that older people are more likely to die or develop severe illness.

The passage states that the bark Cape Horn Pigeon sailed on the whaling voyage on December 7, 1891. It also notes that the arresting officer claimed the Okhotsk Sea was a closed sea, while a Russian foreign affairs note dated June 12/24, 1893 is said not to support any claim of exclusive Russian jurisdiction. After arrival at Vladivostok, the captain telegraphed the U.S. legation at St. Petersburg, and the U.S. chargé d’affaires later received a reply from the Russian ministry informing him that the bark had been released.

On Jan. 2, 2017, an Islamic State car bomb in a busy square in Baghdad’s Sadr City killed 24 people and wounded 67, targeting a Shi’ite Muslim gathering. The militants also cut a key road north from Baghdad to Mosul, where U.S.-backed Iraqi forces are fighting Islamic State amid fierce resistance. The passage describes additional bomb and attack fatalities across Baghdad, including deaths among women in a minibus, a separate blast near a hospital, and other incidents in and around Mosul, Baiji, Shirqat, and a village near Udhaim. Canyon Barry scored a season-high 30 points as No. 15 Florida beat Auburn 114-95 on Tuesday night. Florida (21-5, 11-2 SEC) won its seventh straight game, broke its previous scoring high of 106, and surged from a 50-50 halftime tie with a 13-3 run to end 56% shooting, 11-of-19 from three, and 37-of-42 from the free-throw line. KeVaughn Allen scored all 17 of his points in the second half, while Devin Robinson had 14 and Kasey Hill had 11 points and 12 assists. Anfernee McLemore led Auburn with 19; T.J. Dunans had 13 and Ronnie Johnson 12. Center John Egnubu left with a knee injury midway through the first half and did not return. The game marked the first time in nearly two years Auburn allowed 100 points, and it ended Barry’s school-record made free-throw streak at 42.

Using data from the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS) for students in grades seven and nine, this study examines the relationship between parental education level and child cognitive ability. It uses a multiple linear regression model with parental years of education (maximum, average, father, and mother) as key explanatory variables, and child cognitive ability measured by standardized scores from the 3PL test. Control variables include child personal characteristics, family characteristics, and school characteristics, while educational expectations and parent-child interaction are included as mediating variables. Findings report a significant positive correlation between parental education level and child cognitive ability, effects mediated by educational expectations and investment, and differences by child gender and urban-rural parental location, with the impact declining as children’s cognitive ability increases.

The passage describes native assembler, “stackless” procedures that use a register passing model. One procedure initializes the processor and cache system, allocates a pre-memory stack region by dividing available space among processor cores, maps it to global address space, and sets MTRRs. It must run on all cores, conditionally leaves SS unchanged when protected mode is enabled (with host requirements), sets ESP/SS:ESP appropriately, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance in the stack frame area. AARCH64 APUs with PSP initialize DRAM without using the stack and very early macros. It reports status codes (AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING for stack reentry, AGESA_FATAL for unknown processor family) and notes registers destroyed and EBX fully preserved.

Another procedure removes the pre-memory stack by returning the processor and cache to a non-stack-enabled state, expected to run only once when main memory becomes available on the BSP, flushing all cache lines and disabling CAR mode without modifying MTRR settings. It provides expected exit state details for BSP, notes AARCH64 PSP behavior, lists destroyed registers, and returns AGESA_SUCCESS when stack space is disabled.

The passage also introduces AmdCreateStruct, which creates storage for a parameter block by allocating structure storage space using a specified method, including PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, and ByHost options with cautions about host-allocated space.

The lecture explains how to finance sustainable real estate at the portfolio level, building on prior discussions of asset and building levels, and notes that a later session will cover the global market. It focuses on public-market financing channels, particularly equity through REITs and debt through green bonds, along with benchmarking and disclosure tools needed to measure sustainability.

The instructor describes REITs as publicly traded companies that primarily invest in income-generating real estate, such as commercial properties, and distribute income to investors. REITs are said to receive tax benefits in the United States under rules requiring most income to come from real estate (75%) and requiring a large share of income to be distributed (90%). The lecture also compares investing directly in real estate versus investing via REIT stocks, citing diversification, liquidity, and lower required capital for REITs, while noting reduced control.

Examples are provided of REIT-like concepts in other countries (e.g., Colombia’s PEY and Mexico’s REIT adoption, plus discussion of how China developed infrastructure-focused REITs during periods of financial stress). The lecture then shifts to green bonds, defining bonds as fixed-income contracts issued by governments or companies, and explaining that green bonds fund projects such as renewable energy or climate resilience. Green bond issuance is linked to the potential for lower cost of capital, and the lecture gives examples including REIT-issued green bonds and mortgage-backed green bonds via Fannie Mae. It also highlights the importance of standards and verification to avoid “greenwashing.”

Finally, the lecture covers the need for measurement, benchmarking, and third-party assurance (including carbon reporting and tools such as Portfolio Manager, GRESB, and assurance providers). GRESB is described as a portfolio-level sustainability benchmarking system analogous to building-level LEED, used to score and compare ESG performance across portfolios. The lecture also notes research suggesting that higher GRESB scores are associated (on average) with better performance and cheaper financing. It concludes by mentioning an “ESG Confusion” project studying inconsistencies across ESG ratings and methods for deriving reliable ESG measures.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere-based GA10x (“GA10x”) GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104. It highlights improvements over Turing GPUs, including up to 2x faster ray tracing, up to 1.7x faster traditional raster graphics, expanded concurrency between RT cores and graphics/compute, and second-generation RT cores that add acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. Motion blur is supported via an “Interpolate Triangle Position” unit and a doubled ray/triangle intersection testing rate, enabling up to 8x faster motion blur rendering than Turing; examples include Blender, Chaos V-Ray, Autodesk Arnold, and Redshift with NVIDIA OptiX 7.0. The passage also covers third-generation Tensor cores with new data types (TF32, BF16), Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x throughput, performance examples for RTX 3080 vs RTX 2080 Super, and DLSS enhancements for 8K. Additional sections outline memory and I/O features such as GDDR6X (including PAM4 signaling), third-generation NVLink scaling to 96GB configurations, PCIe Gen4, and NVIDIA RTX IO for faster GPU-based loading/decompression using DirectStorage. It further discusses data center features via the NVIDIA A40 and workstation/data center GPUs like RTX A6000, along with NVDEC hardware video decoding and NVENC hardware video encoding support. Appendices mention GA10x specifications and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for GDDR6X overclocking-related errors.

Tristan Walker struggled to find shaving products that worked for his hair and skin, leading him to launch Walker & Co., a beauty line designed with people of color in mind. He hopes to make the mainstream beauty industry more inclusive and eliminate segregated “ethnic” beauty aisles at drugstores. In 2015, Walker was a sleep-deprived father and his two-year-old company, Bevel, sold men’s shaving products via a subscription service; Walker & Co. later launched Form for women. Before founding the company, Walker was an entrepreneur-in-residence at Andreessen Horowitz and previously worked at Foursquare on brand partnerships. He also founded Code2040 in 2012 to increase access and opportunities for young people of color in tech. Walker discussed challenges in fulfilling his company’s long-term vision, his inspiration from not having efficacious products, and advice drawn from Tyler Perry: lessons from trials are blessings. He emphasized faith, family, and work, named influential figures he would like to meet, and said he is building a library for his son and wants his legacy to show people of color deserve “first-class” treatment as consumers and producers.

The passage is an introduction to a general relativity course, focusing on course texts, structure, and the geometric viewpoint. The passage also covers units where the speed of light is set to 1, the definition of displacement vectors between events as components that transform between inertial frames, Lorentz transformations (including matrix notation and summation conventions), and concludes with a definition of a spacetime vector as a quartet of components that transforms between inertial reference frames according to the Lorentz transformation law.

The passage describes how ultra-processed foods (UPF) have increased productivity and shelf-life but may harm health and sustainability, with evidence linking UPF consumption to unhealthy diets, non-communicable diseases, and exposures to industrialized preservatives and pesticides. The passage describes a study on using deep learning to estimate mammographic breast density from low-dose mammograms (about 10% of standard radiation dose) in younger women. High mammographic density is linked to higher breast cancer risk, and early screening and risk-reducing interventions may benefit younger women, who are not routinely screened partly due to radiation dose concerns.

The study investigates variability between density predictions from standard-dose and low-dose images, assesses confidence in low-dose predictions, and evaluates methods to reduce uncertainty. It uses the ALDRAM dataset for low-dose and standard-dose paired mammograms (patients aged 30–45) and trains models on the PROCAS dataset with standard-dose density labels from two readers, then simulates low-dose images from standard-dose images for training a low-dose model.

Preprocessing standardizes image sizes and intensity normalization. Models based on ResNet-18 are trained with mean squared error loss. Results on PROCAS show high predictive consistency between standard and simulated low-dose models, with especially high similarity when comparing standard vs low-dose predictions and when averaging across multiple trained models.

Further analyses consider sources of variation including differences between CC and MLO views, model variability, image size, breast area, and breast density level. The passage reports that combining CC and MLO predictions and averaging across multiple models increases similarity between standard and low-dose predictions. It also finds no significant relationship with age or exposure ratio, while larger prediction differences occur at higher densities and smaller breast areas, with poorer performance on smaller image sizes likely linked to breast area compression effects. The authors conclude that low-dose predictions can be highly similar to standard-dose predictions overall, but with systematic differences (low-dose predictions generally lower) and uncertainty that increases with breast density and smaller breast area.

Tecomaria capensis, a deciduous scrambling shrub or small tree in the Bignoniaceae family, grows up to 6 m and has opposite compound leaves and orange-red to pale orange trumpet-shaped flowers that occur throughout the year. Its fruit is slender and flattened. It is known as Cape Honeysuckle and is a popular garden and hedging plant, with lighter orange and pale yellow forms including a slower-growing variety. The SANBI Red List status is Least Concern. The species occurs in thicket and on forest margins in southern eastern and eastern South Africa and tropical Africa, including provinces Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and Western Cape. Ecology notes browsing by game and stock, visits by sunbirds and butterflies, and leaf-eating by the death’s head hawkmoth and fulvous hawkmoth larvae. Uses include traditional medicine for several ailments and cultural use of its wood in making the protective necklet isixhoxho, with recorded earliest use in 1929. Cultivation guidance includes planting in well-drained compost- and fertiliser-mixed soil, regular watering until established, winter pruning, and managing shoots for a self-standing form.

From November 1961 to October 1962, a Special Group (Augmented), chaired by General Taylor and including Attorney General Robert Kennedy, oversaw Operation Mongoose, a covert program aimed at overthrowing Cuba’s Castro regime. President Kennedy authorized the program in November and designated Brigadier General Edward G. Lansdale as chief of operations, coordinating activities among the CIA and the Departments of State and Defense. CIA units in Washington and Miami primarily implemented Mongoose, including military, sabotage, and political propaganda efforts. Kennedy also established a Special Group (Counter-Insurgency) on January 18, 1962, to set broad policies against subversive insurgency and indirect aggression. Later memoranda renamed and reorganized the approval group for covert actions, with the “Special Group 5412” becoming the “303 Committee” while retaining composition, functions, and responsibility, chaired by Bundy. The Special Group and 303 Committee approved 163 covert actions under Kennedy and 142 under Johnson through February 1967, though a 1976 Church Committee report estimated that only 14 percent of CIA projects were considered case-by-case by the 303 Committee and its successors, and it described disputes over CIA recommendations. In 1969, the Nixon administration required annual 303 Committee reviews and termination of unreviewed operations, and in 1970 NSDM 40 renamed the group as the 40 Committee, added the Attorney General, reaffirmed the DCI’s role, and required annual 40 Committee reviews of approved operations. The 1976 report stated the 40 Committee considered about 25 percent of CIA covert action projects and that Congress received briefings on only a few. The passage also notes that in 1970 Nixon directed the DCI to promote a coup against Chilean President Salvador Allende without committee coordination or approval. After the Hughes-Ryan amendment in 1974, covert actions required explicit presidential approval for each action and expanded congressional oversight, with CIA spending limited until a presidential finding was signed and Congress informed.

The passage discusses the economics of spam and security, contrasting technical threat models with why attackers act and how financial incentives shape attacks. For realization, it describes payment flows through merchants, payment processors, banks, and credit-card networks, and argues that spammers often classify transactions to reduce penalties and ship goods to avoid chargeback fines. The passage also mentions “hackbacks” by companies like Microsoft that took control of botnet command-and-control systems under legal rationales involving trademark or similar claims, reflecting an ongoing shift of some defensive/offensive responsibilities toward private organizations.

After remand from the Third Circuit, the court scheduled a new trial and denied Defendant Willie Tyler’s motions to dismiss the indictment. The motions argued that retrial is barred by the Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause, the Fifth Amendment Double Jeopardy Clause, and the Due Process Clause. 

Tyler had previously been convicted for obstructing justice involving the murder of Doreen Proctor and appealed successfully on legal-error grounds related to two statutory theories under 18 U.S.C. § 1512. The government conceded it could no longer prove one of the theories, and the court later ordered retrial based on the other theory (investigation-related communications). 

On the Confrontation Clause claim, the court held that admission of a statement through narcotics detective David Fones would not violate the Confrontation Clause because it would be offered to show Proctor would have made a communication to a federal law-enforcement officer, not for the truth of the matter asserted. 

On the Double Jeopardy claim, the court rejected Tyler’s arguments that retrial was barred after vacatur, distinguishing Burks and Sanabria and concluding the convictions were vacated due to legal errors rather than insufficient evidence. 

On the Due Process claim based on allegedly outrageous government conduct, the court rejected allegations that the government fabricated Diller’s status as a DEA adviser/consultant and also rejected a Brady-based claim about nondisclosure of a witness statement, finding no established Brady violation or prejudice, and concluding the conduct did not warrant barring retrial.

In Watauga County (YCS), Valle Crucis School was flooded to about 70% of the building after water entered on Sept. 27, 2024. The passage introduces regression—especially linear regression and its extensions such as ridge, lasso, ℓp, and Huber regression—and notes uncertainty about whether quantum computing can provide speedups for broader regression tasks beyond linear regression. It proposes a quantum algorithmic framework based on generalized linear model (GLM) sparsification, which replaces a large dataset with a smaller weighted subset that approximately preserves the objective for all candidate solutions. The framework formalizes GLM optimization as minimizing a sum of loss functions applied to inner products and develops a quantum method that constructs ε-approximate sparsifiers for a broad class of “(L, θ, c)-proper” loss functions. The main result (Theorem 10) claims quantum algorithms that generate sparse ε-approximate sparsifiers with high probability, achieving quadratic speedups in the number of samples over the fastest classical methods under certain regimes. The approach uses quantum computation of multiscale leverage score overestimates (MLSO), quantum leverage score approximation, and quantum importance sampling with state preparation and sum estimation. Applications include quantum algorithms for ℓp regression, γp (generalized Huber-type) regression, and extensions to multiple regression, ridge regression, and lasso regression by embedding them into the GLM sparsification framework.

Digital Foundry reports that while Monster Hunter World plays well, its console visuals and performance have notable technical problems. Both PS4 and Xbox One have strengths such as strong monster character and environment modeling, but issues include reduced visual contrast, barely noticeable HDR effects, and problems like clipping, collision detection gaps, and poorly implemented motion blur. On base consoles, PS4 runs at 1080p while Xbox One X is lower at 864p, with sharper motionless images and more blur during movement on the One X. Frame rates are uncapped on both, with uneven frame times and frequent dips. For PS4 Pro and Xbox One X, resolution mode uses checkerboard rendering on the Pro (1800p) but not on the One X (1728p), yet the Pro and One X still differ in missing distant assets on the One X. Digital Foundry also finds inconsistent performance between the One X and Pro, suggesting limited optimization for the Xbox One X. In frame-rate mode, both target 1080p but still omit certain distant visual assets on the One X; the One X generally achieves higher frame rates. In graphics mode, both remain at 1080p but LODs extend further, with missing assets appearing; the Pro runs slower than the One X. Overall, Digital Foundry concludes the game is a technical disappointment, with disappointing performance and visuals across consoles and especially problematic results on the Xbox One X.

As external feedback and internal support issues arose, including difficulties obtaining help from practice-group specialists, Chris reorganized team work to finalize the product for beta testing within about 10 days. In her Friday meeting, Chris presented progress and emphasized team cohesion and effectiveness. On Monday, Meg decided to cancel the scheduling and budgeting project, citing limited capacity for new products and lack of reported district interest in other regions, and asked whether Chris would lead a new direction focused on marketing rather than product development or return to IT as a functional specialist.

Donald Trump told “the young people of TikTok” and Gen Z in the Oval Office that he “saved TikTok” by not carrying out a 2020 executive order to ban it, saying they “owe [him] big.” The passage says TikTok’s ban evolved into a 2024 law signed by Joe Biden requiring TikTok to sell its U.S. operations or face a ban. Cynthia Nixon, a Sex and the City actress, announced her gubernatorial run for governor on Twitter on March 19, 2018, saying she was born and raised in New York City and believes the government should change. The District Court of Appeal of Florida granted Denny Jenkins’ petition for a belated appeal from the October 5, 2015 judgment and sentence in Suwannee County Circuit Court case number 14-532-CF. After issuance of the mandate, a copy of the opinion will be provided to the circuit court clerk for treatment as the notice of appeal under Fla. R. App. P. 9.141(c)(6)(D). It highlights the spin-off of Weiss, Peck & Greer’s venture arm into Lightspeed Venture Partners with a $1 billion first fund, the formation of MobileAria by Mayfield, Palm, and Delphi to develop an in-car wireless Internet service, and other funding rounds and deals across technology sectors. The passage describes the United States as making significant progress after a “great conflict,” leading the world in general readjustment. It says domestic confidence and business have revived and prosperity is spreading, while America has helped European nations through resources and counsel. It argues these successes come from continuous effort over generations and stresses the need to learn from past experiences and keep enduring principles in view. The passage outlines a history of U.S. expanding freedom and independence, including actions tied to the Monroe doctrine and entry into the Great War, followed by withdrawal after victory. It emphasizes an American approach to peace and security through law, arbitration, conferences, limitation of sea power, and support for the Permanent Court of International Justice, while stating the U.S. should maintain a military force that is balanced and not menacing. Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 23, 2019. The report states that on October 23, 2019, Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2019, and that the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer.

Canada’s main stock index fell from a record high and closed lower Thursday as trade fears pushed down North American markets. Kash Pashootan said the TSX’s drop reflected both a “hangover” from the prior day’s near-high performance and rising volatility tied to escalating trade-war tensions. Energy stocks declined amid expectations that OPEC would agree to increased production, which investors expect to depress prices; the S&P/TSX capped energy index fell 2.11%. The S&P/TSX composite index closed down 85.80 points at 16,335.15. Mining stocks also fell, while cannabis stocks lifted the health-care index after Prime Minister Justin Trudeau announced Oct. 17 marijuana legalization. In the U.S., the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed lower. The Canadian dollar averaged 75.13 cents US, and commodities also ended mostly lower, including crude oil at US$65.54 per barrel and gold at US$1,270.50 an ounce.

Soft-tissue sarcomas (STS) are rare, heterogeneous malignant tumors arising in connective and other mesenchymal tissues. The passage describes a study using the SEER database (2000–2018) to analyze 24,849 STS patients in the United States, including heart cancer patients, to estimate mortality and overall survival by sarcoma type and treatment. STS patients were, on average, 59 years old, and 56% were male; most were white (82%). Survival differed by sarcoma type, with Myxofibrosarcoma (MyS) showing higher overall survival (75%) and Synovial Cell Sarcoma (ScS) lower survival (37%). Increasing age, male sex, non-white race, higher cancer stage, and higher tumor grade were associated with worse survival, while radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and surgery were associated with improved overall survival, though primary systemic therapy showed conflicting results. The study developed an all-cause mortality nomogram to predict overall survival probability and reported close calibration between predicted and observed event probabilities. Limitations included missing clinicopathological details in SEER, lack of histological subtypes, no recurrence data, limited radiotherapy technique details, potential unmeasured confounding, and the need for external validation. The passage concludes with the main negative prognostic factors and that an all-cause mortality nomogram was developed for STS patients.

BART said it will add more members to its rapid response team and launch a mobile option for passengers to file bio-hazard complaints due to increasing reports of hypodermic needles littering the transit system, including a media report of a woman being pricked on a train. The rapid response team will respond to urgent cleaning needs at the MacArthur and Lake Merritt stations and BART will also allow complaints through train conductors who notify the control center. BART reported receiving 10 cleanliness-related rider complaints in the past two weeks, and it currently has 14 rapid response team members with plans to add five more. The passage also notes that San Francisco distributes hundreds of thousands of needles monthly, with many estimated to be unaccounted for, and says San Francisco has no known cases of disease spread from accidental needle pricks.

The case, State ex rel. Stern v. Mascio, originated when a complaint for a writ of mandamus was filed in this court. Respondent filed an answer on March 20, 1998, though it was due March 19, 1998. The court, sua sponte, ordered that the untimely answer be stricken because Rule XIV(1)(C) prohibits untimely filings.

Queensland’s cyclone season remains active with possible wild weather leading up to Easter. Some models suggested two deep low pressure systems could develop off the Queensland coast by next Tuesday. A tropical low north of Thursday Island was expected to intensify and move west across the northern Gulf of Carpentaria, while another system in the Solomon Sea was forecast to shift into the north-eastern Coral Sea on Wednesday and Thursday. The Bureau of Meteorology rated the likelihood of a tropical low developing or moving into Queensland waters over the next three days, with an updated forecast expected at about 2.40pm for the Northern Territory, and said a low or tropical cyclone could move into the Gulf of Carpentaria next week but with significant uncertainty. Forecast mapping indicates multiple low pressure systems by Monday afternoon, with models differing on increased cyclone potential in the Gulf of Carpentaria or Arafura Sea. Sea temperatures are above the minimum needed to support cyclonic development in several areas. The Sunshine Coast is expected to see increasing showers from sea-tracking troughs, with predicted rainfall probabilities of 90% on Wednesday (up to 20mm) and 80% on Thursday and Friday (up to 10mm), alongside south-easterly winds reaching 30km/h on Wednesday.

The lecture introduces MIT’s 14.271 industrial organization course, explaining that it covers industrial organization theory and empirical thinking, with Wednesdays focused on theory and Mondays on empirical work. It argues that industrial organization is inherently theoretical, using examples of monopoly decisions that cannot be resolved by natural experiments. The lecture begins with a single-product monopoly pricing model, deriving the condition that markup (Lerner index) depends on the demand elasticity and explains deadweight loss and other potential harms of market power.

It then extends monopoly pricing to multiple products, introducing diversion ratios and emphasizing that pricing must be treated as a system because changing one product’s price affects sales of others. The lecture discusses product quality choice, showing how a monopolist’s optimal quality can differ from a social planner’s due to focusing on the marginal versus average consumer, with special results under consumer homogeneity. It covers durable goods pricing and the idea that “walking down” demand may fail with forward-looking consumers and commitment power, leading to strategies like keeping prices constant (or not selling in later periods). It also describes reasons real-world prices may still fall, including changing preferences, changing costs, and firms’ commitment problems, and reviews the Coase conjecture as an extreme commitment problem and reasons it may not occur.

Finally, the lecture outlines information design in monopoly pricing, contrasting situations where consumers get much versus little information (e.g., laptops vs. mattresses; auctions for used cars). It presents examples where withholding or structuring information can affect prices, consumer surplus, social surplus, and profits, and closes by noting upcoming empirical papers and guidance for reading them.

A senior House Republican, Rep. Trey Gowdy, said there is no evidence the FBI planted a “spy” on President Trump’s 2016 campaign, contradicting Trump’s claims that the FBI inserted a “spy” for political reasons. Gowdy said he was briefed by the Justice Department and FBI and that he has not seen evidence supporting the “spy” claim, noting he had never heard the term used.

The lecture discusses natural sandwich structures—lightweight engineering-like designs found in monocot leaves such as iris (with schlerchyma fibers on the top and bottom and parenchyma cells in the middle), and in bull rush/cat tail leaves (with webbed cores resembling I-beams and honeycomb cores). The instructor describes how these leaves behave mechanically like sandwich beams, including an analysis using measured geometric parameters and estimated face modulus and core shear modulus, and compares calculated versus measured beam stiffness. Additional sandwich examples include honeycomb-like kelp, bird skulls with foam-like cores between two plates, horseshoe crab shells, and cuttlefish bone. The lecture then shifts to palm stems, which resist bending despite relatively constant diameter as they grow by depositing additional cell-wall layers, creating a radial density gradient with denser tissue on the outside. Based on studies and mechanical testing, the instructor relates density gradients to increased flexural rigidity and strength matching the stress distribution. The talk concludes with mention of related bamboo work and plans to discuss biomimicking and review for an upcoming test.

The passage describes the use of Temperature Scaling (TS), a simple post-hoc calibration method, to improve the calibration of convolutional neural networks for classifying brain tumor MRI images under different noise conditions. It notes that deep learning models can be highly accurate but miscalibrated, leading to overconfident or wrong probability estimates in healthcare settings. The study trains a lightweight CNN on a composite dataset of T1-weighted MRI images and applies TS to the model’s logits using an independent validation set to minimize Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL). Synthetic noise types added to test data include Gaussian, Poisson, Salt & Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform. Results across noise scenarios show TS consistently reduces NLL and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) while preserving accuracy-related metrics such as precision, recall, and F1-score. The work also includes further testing on ResNet50, reporting similar improvements in false positive/negative behavior and reductions in NLL and ECE without changing overall accuracy. The conclusion states TS improves reliability across noise types without sacrificing prediction quality and suggests future comparisons with other calibration methods and evaluation on larger datasets.

The passage explains Cantor’s theorem: for any set \(A\), the cardinality of \(A\) is strictly smaller than the cardinality of its power set. It shows first that there is an injective map from \(A\) into the power set by sending each \(x\in A\) to the subset \(\{x\}\), and then proves by contradiction that no bijection from \(A\) to the power set can exist, using a constructed subset \(B\subseteq A\) and surjectivity to derive \(b\in g(b)\) iff \(b\notin g(b)\). The discussion then transitions to defining real numbers as the unique ordered field containing \(\mathbb{Q}\) with the least upper bound property. It defines ordered sets, examples and non-examples of orders, and the least upper bound (supremum) and greatest lower bound (infimum). The passage states that \(\mathbb{Q}\) does not have the least upper bound property, and begins an argument using the set of rationals \(E\) with \(q^2<2\), proving that if \(\sup E\) were rational \(x\), then \(x\ge 1\) and \(x^2=2\), before ending mid-proof.

The passage argues that many schools operate under monolingual norms that limit multilingual learners, and that educators may struggle to understand and apply translanguaging without additional training. It states that translanguaging is a distinct approach from code switching and can support multilingual students’ learning, identity, and sense of belonging, particularly in middle grades where students are often in English-dominant spaces.  

The study described focuses on teacher candidates (TCs) and cooperating teachers (CTs) in middle school settings during a year-long Professional Development School (PDS) experience. Research questions examine how TCs view, experience, and use translanguaging and how ESL-focused coursework prepares them for it. The study uses interviews, course-based field notes, and classroom supervision notes, analyzed through a case study approach with coding and theme development.  

Findings emphasize a theory–practice gap: although the two TCs expressed positive, asset-based views of translanguaging and believed they had learned strategies, they struggled to fully implement it in their classroom practices. The passage attributes this to factors including discomfort working with multilingual learners, difficulties applying learned strategies, and cooperating teachers’ limited use of students’ native languages. It concludes that teacher education programs need to add training for cooperating teachers to create linguistically inclusive classrooms so TCs gain real classroom experiences with translanguaging.

Posted Australia’s business investment grew 0.4% over the first three months of the year, below expectations for higher capital expenditure growth. The buildings and structures sector fell 1.3% for the quarter, driven by a 16% drop in new factories being built, while equipment, plant and machinery investment rose 2.5%. Expectations for capex next year were softer, with second-estimate capex for the next financial year at $87.7 billion, above the first estimate but below forecasts. Capital Economics’ Paul Dales said risks are emerging for the outlook because non-mining investment was particularly disappointing and firms’ investment plans were only modestly revised.

George Herbert and two friends in Bristol saw a suspicious man running with a bike and chased him. The thief abandoned the bike and fled, leaving Herbert with it. Herbert is seeking the bike’s original rightful owner because he does not know where it was taken from or whose it is, and the police are trying to match the bike’s description to theft reports. On February 6, 2024, CFO John Lawler prepared for an investor call presenting Ford’s first full-year results under a new segment reporting structure that separately tracked the company’s electric vehicle business, Ford Model e. Ford Model e’s 2023 performance showed a loss before interest and taxes of $4.7 billion, increasing from $0.9 billion in 2021 and $2.1 billion in 2022, contrasting with profits from conventional vehicle sales.  

The passage recounts Ford’s history of EV efforts, including early experimentation, later restarts such as the Focus Electric in 2009, and eventual large EV investment commitments (rising from $4.5 billion through 2020 to $50 billion through 2026, with a goal of 50% EV share by 2030). It also describes early EV successes in 2021–2022, including customer orders/reservations and milestones for models like the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning. Finally, the passage explains differences in accounting for R&D under U.S. GAAP versus IFRS, noting that development costs may be capitalized under IFRS if conditions are met. It states Lawler was aware that international competitors capitalized some development costs and that, during review of Ford’s 2023 results, he noted Ford’s $8.2 billion R&D expense.

The passage explains that using AMD’s RDRAND and RDSEED instructions requires MMIO reads from a cryptographic co-processor, which is slower than software PRNGs. It notes that this may be acceptable for non-latency-sensitive cryptography, and suggests a hybrid approach for latency-sensitive cases by seeding a PRNG with hardware-generated values to improve performance and security. It also describes AMD Zen processors as including hardware random number generation, and states that the AMD Secure RNG library abstracts low-level MMIO and x86 instruction calls into an easier API for applications like cryptographic key generation.

HCPEA represents major private equity firms focused on privately held healthcare businesses across multiple segments. North American cannabis stocks fell sharply this week. The North American Marijuana Index dropped 27.2%, driven largely by poor Canadian stock performance after more than $1.2 billion in deal offerings from publicly traded LPs in 2018 and concerns tied to Aphria’s purchase of Nuuvera. The United States Marijuana Index, tracking 15 large U.S. marijuana stocks, fell 18.1%, with more speculative names hit hardest.
