Jeff Greene, a billionaire real estate mogul, said higher interest rates and fiscal policy could upend the stock market rally entering its ninth year. He argued that Washington’s inaction left the Federal Reserve as the main driver, leading to near-zero interest rates and a $4.5 trillion balance sheet over seven to eight years, which he described as boosting “animal spirits.” Greene said GOP fiscal-policy promises and higher rates could threaten the market’s bullish advance, arguing low rates have been more stimulative than tax cuts. He noted 10-year Treasury yields fell from about 5.027% a decade ago to around 2.230%, helping support low-yield gains in major indexes, which have roughly tripled over eight years. He added that pro-growth legislative changes may be delayed and that he sees growth as lackluster, expecting rates to rise slowly.

The passage explains divergence trading and how to identify bullish and bearish divergence using price action versus oscillator indicators (such as RSI, MACD, and Stochastic Oscillator). It defines divergence as when price swings and indicator movements are not in phase, and describes classical (regular) divergence and hidden divergence, including how each can imply potential reversals or continuation of trends depending on market structure. It lists commonly used indicators, discusses the role of momentum and volume as confirmation, and outlines advantages, including potential early detection of momentum shifts and clearer entry/exit signals, while also warning against common mistakes like misinterpreting signals, relying on divergence alone, overtrading, poor risk management, and emotional trading. The passage also provides example scenarios involving Nasdaq 100, S&P 500, and TSLA during the Covid-19 period, describing specific divergence signals and candlestick triggers.

The UAE said its first nuclear reactor at the Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant would come online in late 2019 or early 2020, further delaying the start of the Arab world’s first atomic power station. ENEC said construction of the first of four reactors is complete, with the second, third, and fourth reactors 93 percent, 83 percent, and 72 percent finished, respectively. The plant is west of Abu Dhabi, built by a consortium led by Korea Electric Power Corporation. When fully operational, the four reactors are expected to produce 5,600 megawatts, about 25 percent of the UAE’s needs.

Power traces on a standard PCB should be kept as short, direct, and thick as possible, with a minimum of 15 mils (0.381 mm) per Ampere. The inductor, output capacitors, and output diode should be placed close together to reduce EMI, noise spikes, ringing, and resistive losses. Grounds for the IC, input capacitors, output capacitors, and output diode should connect close together to a ground plane, ideally on both PCB sides; multilayer boards can separate power and signal planes. Vias are needed to connect planes, using one standard via per 200 mA when significant current must pass between planes. Components should be arranged so switching current loops curl in the same direction to prevent magnetic field reversal and reduce radiated EMI.

The passage sets out a proclamation by President Andrew Johnson dated May 29, 1865, stating that the U.S. must guarantee North Carolina a republican form of government and protect it against invasion and domestic violence after rebellion deprived it of civil government. It appoints William W. Holden as provisional governor to convene a convention of loyal delegates to alter or amend North Carolina’s constitution, with authority to restore the state to constitutional relations with the federal government. It requires delegate election eligibility to include prior amnesty oaths and voter qualifications under North Carolina law before May 20, 1861. Johnson directs military officers to assist the provisional government and not hinder loyal organization of a state government, and instructs federal officials to implement relevant U.S. laws in North Carolina: the Secretary of State, Secretary of the Treasury (including tax assessors, customs collectors, and revenue officers), Postmaster-General (post offices and routes), district judge (holding courts under an act of Congress), Attorney-General actions regarding confiscation and enforcement of justice, Secretary of the Navy (naval public property and acts of Congress), and Secretary of the Interior (Interior Department laws). The proclamation is signed by Andrew Johnson, with William H. Seward as Secretary of State.

The Tenth Circuit unanimously decided that oral argument was unnecessary and affirmed the district court’s dismissal of Charles A. Meeker’s civil rights complaint filed under 42 U.S.C. § 1983. The case stemmed from a child abuse investigation involving Meeker that led to custody of his four minor daughters being transferred to the New Mexico Human Services Department; Meeker alleged violations of family rights in the state proceedings. The district court found improper service of process as to four defendants and that res judicata barred claims against the other defendants except guardian ad litem Grout. The court also dismissed the claim against Grout on alternative grounds, holding Grout was not acting under color of state law. On appeal, the court held that Meeker could not represent his daughters because a minor cannot sue through a parent acting as next friend if the parent is not represented by an attorney, and it adopted the district court’s reasoning. The appellate court further elaborated that a guardian ad litem is not acting under color of state law for purposes of § 1983, citing the analogous reasoning in Polk County v. Dodson.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court’s grant of summary judgment in favor of the Bank of St. Louis and two bank employee defendants in a malicious prosecution claim by Harvey F. Euge. Euge sought $100,000 actual and $300,000 punitive damages after his indictment and conviction for obtaining money by means of a bogus check; his conviction was later reversed and he was discharged by the Missouri Supreme Court in State v. Euge (1966). The appellate court concluded that, for malicious prosecution, absence of probable cause is required and that—based on the undisputed facts underlying the prosecution—probable cause existed as a matter of law. The court rejected Euge’s arguments that his discharge established no probable cause, that the indictment was improperly procured, and that probable cause was necessarily a jury question. The appellate court stated it was unrealistic to suggest defendants could have foreseen the narrow statutory construction leading to reversal, and held the trial court did not err. The judgment was affirmed.

Britain’s FTSE 100 rose 0.6% to 7,353.89 points on Monday, recovering from a three-month low and its worst week since April. Gains in financials and miners helped, with the banking index up 0.8% and miners up 1.7%, while risk sentiment improved after tensions between the U.S. and North Korea eased somewhat. Energy shares lagged, with Royal Dutch Shell flat and BP down 0.4% as oil prices fell. Broker upgrades and downgrades drove individual stock moves, including TUI up 4.8% to an all-time high after a Credit Suisse upgrade, and Experian down 1.5% and G4S down 1.1% after Morgan Stanley downgraded both to “equal-weight.” Mid caps rose 0.8% as financials and industrials gained.

A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards are ready to implement a policy preventing regional oil exports if the United States bans Iranian oil sales. President Hassan Rouhani had threatened to disrupt oil shipments from neighboring countries, and Major-General Qassem Soleimani praised Rouhani and said he was ready to carry out such a policy. The U.S. has demanded that countries halt all imports of Iranian oil from Nov. 4 or face U.S. financial measures. Iranian officials said U.S. pressure would raise oil prices and harm the U.S. economy. The European Union pledged to keep the 2015 nuclear deal alive without the United States but acknowledged U.S. sanctions would make guarantees difficult. Rouhani said Iran would stay in the deal if remaining signatories can guarantee Iran’s benefits, and foreign ministers from China, France, Germany, Britain, and Russia will meet in Vienna to discuss keeping the accord.

Multimodal audio generation can synthesize audio from conditional video or text, and artificial Foley models aim to produce soundtracks for videos with high user controllability and strong semantic and temporal accuracy. Diffusion and conditional flow matching have improved audio quality, but existing methods still lack precise guidance; in complex scenes, text-based object specification can become unfeasible. The paper proposes a new task, video object segmentation-aware audio generation, which generates audio for a specific object region in a video rather than the full scene, and presents Segmentation-Aware Generative Audio Network (SAGANet) built on MMAudio. SAGANet adds a segmentation-aware control module that uses visual segmentation masks with global and localized visual feature streams fused via gated cross-attention, conditioning the DiT-based audio generator; the method can use single-source training samples to generalize to multi-source scenes by targeting the segmented object. The authors also introduce a benchmark dataset, Segmented Music Solos, with sounding object segmentation maps and high audio-video correspondence (5,395 train, 665 validation, 745 test samples) across 25 instruments. Experiments on this dataset report that SAGANet outperforms the base MMAudio model across quality, semantic alignment, and temporal alignment metrics, with the largest improvements in temporal synchronization; LoRA fine-tuning of segmentation-related DiT layers further improves results. The paper concludes that conditioning audio synthesis on visual segmentation masks enables more precise, user-friendly Foley models, especially for complex multi-source scenes.

Tom Petty’s cause of death has been deferred. The 66-year-old musician died last week after being rushed to hospital following a cardiac arrest, and after an autopsy was completed, further tests were needed. His agent said Petty passed away after his family agreed to switch off life support when he had no brain activity. Petty died at UCLA hospital in Santa Monica, surrounded by friends, family, and bandmates. Tributes followed his death, including from Nathan Followill, and the passage notes Petty’s rise in 1976 and his time with The Traveling Wilburys in the 1980s.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis’s succession, sued David Lewis to recover $505.58 withdrawn from Priscilla Lewis’s bank account after her death, and also claimed rent for occupying a succession house. David Lewis denied liability but admitted withdrawing the funds, asserting he was entitled to them because he had loaned his mother money and she said the funds belonged to him, and he denied owing rent. Priscilla Lewis died on August 4, 1929, and David Lewis was originally named executor but was removed for failing to take an inventory and to deposit collected estate funds; Willie Lewis was appointed and later discharged, and the bank was then appointed executor. The court found the funds were deposited to Priscilla Lewis’s credit and were withdrawn after her death, concluding David Lewis was only a creditor and could not satisfy his claim by taking succession assets. The court held the withdrawal illegal and ordered judgment for the bank for $505.58 plus legal interest and costs. The court did not uphold the rent claim due to insufficient proof. The prior judgment dismissing the suit was reversed.

The passage describes a research work on building explainable robots that can compare competing action plans, infer which plan is better based on modeled plan properties, and narrate the comparison to users. It formulates ontological support for plan comparison by extending OCRA with a new OWL 2 DL model, defining plan qualities (e.g., cost, expected makespan, number of tasks) and relations for comparing qualities and plans, then uses logical rules to infer better/worse/equivalent relations. To generate contrastive explanatory narratives, it introduces ACXON, an algorithm that retrieves divergent knowledge from a time-indexed knowledge graph and constructs textual contrastive narratives with controllable specificity. The approach is validated by instantiating plans in a robotic scenario and answering competency questions, and evaluated against a baseline (AXON) using objective metrics (number of attributes, construction time, communication time, and readability) across multiple temporal planning domains. Results indicate ACXON generally reduces the knowledge used and communication time compared to the baseline, and a later modification is proposed to further restrict knowledge retrieval for shorter, more selective narratives.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, about eight percent fewer than 2016 (3,157), averaging eight reports per day. The charity cited cases including two four-month-old kittens beaten to death by their owner, for which Aaron Barker was jailed for 20 weeks, and a home where 40 animals were kept in stacked cages without essentials; five dogs were put down and a puppy died. Most complaints involved dogs (1,702), then cats (737) and horses (281). The RSPCA said cruelty complaints nationwide totaled 141,760 in 2017 and urged the public to report concerns via its 24-hour cruelty helpline.

The report examines the relationship between Treasury liquidity and the stock market in relation to the saying “Sell in May and come back in November.” It uses US Treasury cash balances from 2006–2017 and describes recurring peak patterns: a peak in January, a major peak in May, and another major peak around November. The report links January to Fed reverse repurchase agreement operations, May to government tax refund payouts that increase investable funds—especially for wealthy taxpayers—leading to an expected stock market rise, and November to Fed Treasury buybacks that may cause another stock-market “pop.” It concludes that outcomes depend on the size of fiscal cash flows entering the market and suggests more research is needed to distinguish strong years from flat years, with January/February and November patterns tied to Fed operations aimed at managing government money creation.

A Karolinska Institutet study using MRI scans and machine learning found that people who report poor sleep have brains that appear older than their chronological age. In 27,500 middle-aged and older participants from the UK Biobank, sleep quality was assessed using five self-reported factors and grouped into healthy, intermediate, or poor sleep. The gap between brain age and chronological age increased by about six months for every 1-point decrease in healthy sleep score, and people with poor sleep had brains about one year older on average. The study also found that low-grade systemic inflammation could explain just over 10% of the link between poor sleep and older brain age, and suggests other possible mechanisms including effects on brain waste clearance and cardiovascular health. Limitations include the self-reported nature of sleep measures and that UK Biobank participants may be healthier than the general population.

The passage says banks are likely to challenge a Goods and Services Tax Intelligence demand that could exceed Rs 6,000 crore for taxes on free or bundled services provided to account-holders who meet minimum balance norms. It explains the taxman’s calculation based on charges applied to those who do not maintain minimum balance, arguing the services are treated as free for minimum-balance customers. It characterizes the demand as retrospective (for over five years) and argues it is effectively a deterrent against zero balance rather than a charge for services. It adds that if the demand is upheld, customers will suffer because banks will pass on the charges, and it criticizes the demand as “ham-fisted,” saying such demands perpetuate “tax terror” the government had promised to tackle.

The passage is largely excerpted from Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2019. It includes consolidated financial statements (unaudited) with amounts for the consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), redeemable noncontrolling interests and equity, and cash flows, along with detailed notes describing revenue recognition (including automotive sales with and without resale value guarantees), leasing (ASC 842 adoption on January 1, 2019 and related impacts), income tax and other topics, earnings per share, restricted cash, risk concentrations, warranties, recent and newly adopted accounting pronouncements, and business combination details such as the May 16, 2019 acquisition of Maxwell Technologies, Inc. The document also contains additional note disclosures on fair value measurements, inventory, solar energy systems, property, plant and equipment, other long-term liabilities, and customer deposits.

The passage introduces weak gravitational lensing as a competitive cosmology probe, enabled by cosmic shear measurements from surveys such as Kilo Degree Survey, Dark Energy Survey, and Hyper Suprime Camera Survey, which have achieved percent-level constraints on the structure growth parameter \(S_8\). It notes that lensing alone leaves \(\Omega_m\) and \(\sigma_8\) strongly degenerate and that additional data are needed to break this degeneracy. Current cosmic shear precision is mainly limited by uncertainties in intrinsic galaxy alignments (IA) and baryonic feedback; the paper focuses on IA because unaccounted-for IA can bias inferred cosmological parameters and inaccurate IA models can impair inference. It describes several IA modeling approaches (e.g., NLA, extended-NLA, TT, TATT) and the difficulty of generalizing observational IA constraints across surveys due to selection effects. The paper presents a numerical pipeline that infuses IA models into a shared large N-body simulation to produce distinct cosmic shear catalogues, including an extended-TT model and realistic non-linear galaxy bias via halo occupation distributions, and discusses the need for such simulations for non-Gaussian lensing studies beyond two-point statistics. The passage then outlines cosmic shear statistics, starting with two-point shear correlation functions predicted using tomographic power spectra in the Limber approximation and measured from simulated galaxy ellipticities, followed by a discussion of non-Gaussian lensing statistics and how these can be measured on galaxy, convergence (\(\kappa\)), or aperture mass (\(M_{\rm ap}\)) maps using mass reconstruction (e.g., Kaiser–Squires inversion).

The passage is a statement welcoming the signing of a declaration of principles on interim Palestinian self-government by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization. It describes the Middle East peace process, credits leaders including Prime Minister Rabin, Foreign Minister Peres, Chairman Arafat, and U.S. Presidents and other figures, and recalls Camp David accords and earlier negotiations. It argues that the agreement should reconcile Israeli security with Palestinian hopes, place old antagonisms behind both peoples, and advance the peace process through continued mutual recognition. The speaker pledges active U.S. support for implementing the agreement and emphasizes the importance of protecting and supporting Israeli and Arab children so they can experience peace and not be affected by extremism, despair, and the violence of the past.

A 14-year-old girl was arrested by Kingston Police after a violent outburst when a phone at her grandmother’s home was not working. She threw a tantrum, slammed doors, hit walls, and smashed dishes, then grabbed a baseball bat, smashed a rear window, and fled. After returning and being apprehended following a foot chase, she was belligerent and continued swearing and screaming at officers. She was charged with mischief and later released to her mother with conditions and a future court date.

Oil prices fell further below US$56 as a U.S. inventory report indicated ample crude supply. The American Petroleum Institute said U.S. inventories rose by 9.9 million barrels last week, with analysts expecting the Energy Information Administration to show a 3.5 million-barrel rise, which could set a fresh record high. Despite OPEC’s record compliance with its supply-cut accord and output cuts by OPEC and other producers, rising U.S. stocks and increased U.S. oil output limited price gains. Oil was also pressured by a strong U.S. dollar after Fed Chair Janet Yellen signaled faster interest rate rises. OPEC compliance is mixed, with Saudi Arabia exceeding its target, Iraq’s low compliance potentially problematic, and Russia and other non-OPEC producers making smaller cutbacks. Oman’s oil minister expected compliance to improve.

Rich Piltch, founder of ARS, was influenced by The Go-Giver philosophy and helped form Restoration Affiliates (RA) in 2011 with three other restoration company leaders—Damon Gersh, Ras Fenger, and Andy Goldberg. RA aimed to help smaller regional restoration firms compete with national providers by offering national coverage for clients, especially large insurance companies and property management firms. By fall 2013, RA had 21 member organizations totaling about $300 million in revenue.

The passage describes the restoration industry’s fragmentation and the roles of national providers (e.g., Belfor and franchise models), preferred-vendor programs, and third-party administrators. It also explains ARS’s approach to building relationships, using priority service agreements, providing 24/7 live phone coverage, delivering frequent project updates, and emphasizing communication and operational transparency. RA’s structure includes a nine-person board, standing committees, membership eligibility criteria, dues, referral-fee rules, and behavioral/ethical expectations.

As RA expanded, founders and members debated strategic questions, including the administrator’s authority, communication transparency, service standards and pricing consistency, how to handle overlapping service territories, how to resolve the competing disaster-planning software options, and how referral fees affect incentives and cooperation.

The passage honors Henry Clay and recounts his birth amid the early period of American independence, his public career, and his death. It includes a eulogy from a politically opposed journal that describes Clay as a national figure whose eloquence, wisdom, and devotion to liberty influenced both domestic and international events. It then provides a biographical sketch: Clay was born April 12, 1777, in Virginia, was licensed to practice law at age 23, moved to Lexington, Kentucky, and held various offices including Kentucky legislative roles, the U.S. Senate, the U.S. House (as speaker), commissioner for peace negotiations after the War of 1812, Secretary of State under John Quincy Adams, and later roles in the Senate before his death. The text emphasizes his involvement in major issues such as the War of 1812, the Missouri question, Nullification, and slavery-related compromises, portraying him as a decisive figure during crises. It also describes his opposition to slavery in principle and support for gradual emancipation in Kentucky, and discusses his association with the American Colonization Society, including quotations from Clay and his views on colonization. The passage concludes by mourning Clay’s death while asserting that the nation remains prosperous and will need divine support in future emergencies.

The passage introduces a framework for deriving codensity presentations of monads in category theory using a uniform principle: “Codensity Monads = Density + Duality.” It explains Kock’s codensity monad construction (via right Kan extensions) and motivates why existing codensity proofs are often technically difficult. The paper’s main result is Theorem 3.2: in any “codensity setting” where a functor decomposes through a dual equivalence, a dense functor, and a contravariant right adjoint, the monad induced by the adjunction is the pointwise codensity monad of the functor. The authors outline a method to obtain codensity presentations by (1) choosing a dual adjunction inducing the target monad, (2) extending it to a codensity setting, and (3) applying Theorem 3.2. They then demonstrate the framework on many monads, including ultrafilter, filter, neighbourhood/double dualization, Isbell duality, Vietoris and lower Vietoris, sobrification, and several probability monads such as the expectation monad, Giry monad, and Radon/Kantorovich-related monads, providing both known and new codensity presentations. The conclusion summarizes the unifying approach and outlines directions for future work in extending Theorem 3.2 and studying further monads, especially Vietoris-related and probabilistic powerdomain variants.

The passage is a collection of quotes attributing taxation and banking to exploitation through debt, suggesting banks profit by controlling debt, and claiming taxation involves legalized theft. It also includes views that patriotism is used to justify wrongdoing, that large-scale stealing leads to power, and that corporations allegedly steal through tax breaks without national allegiance, focusing only on profit.

On January 30, 2017, Microsoft Corporation entered into an Underwriting Agreement with several underwriters for the issuance and sale of $1.5 billion of 1.850% Notes due 2020, $1.75 billion of 2.400% Notes due 2022, $2.25 billion of 2.875% Notes due 2024, $4.0 billion of 3.300% Notes due 2027, $2.5 billion of 4.100% Notes due 2037, $3.0 billion of 4.250% Notes due 2047, and $2.0 billion of 4.500% Notes due 2057. The Notes will be issued under an indenture dated May 18, 2009 and an expected Twelfth Supplemental Indenture dated February 6, 2017, with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. Interest will be payable semi-annually in arrears on February 6 and August 6 starting August 6, 2017, and the Notes will mature on their respective February 6 dates from 2020 to 2057. The Company may redeem the Notes in certain circumstances. The report also lists relevant exhibits, including the Underwriting Agreement and forms related to the supplemental indenture, global notes, and legal opinions.

A visiting law professor at Harvard Law School, Carlos Portugal Gouvêa, was arrested Oct. 1 after firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during a Yom Kippur service, according to police. He told police he was hunting rats. He was charged with illegally discharging a pellet gun, disturbing the peace, disorderly conduct, and damage to personal property, with the damage charge tied to allegedly shattering a car window. The temple was placed on lockdown after shots were heard. Police reported that he admitted using the pellet rifle to hunt rats, and officers advised him it was unsafe and to be aware of the alarm he caused. Police and synagogue officials said antisemitism was not a factor. Gouvêa was placed on administrative leave while the school seeks more information, and his lawyer said the incident was a misunderstanding.

A pet owner, Jacob Hackin, became the first person in Cambridge prosecuted for failing to clear up dog mess in a park. He was spotted at Midsummer Common, given a fixed penalty notice, and after not paying appeared in court and pleaded guilty. He was ordered to pay a £75 fine, £125 toward council costs, and a £30 victim surcharge. The council issued 15 fixed penalty notices for dog fouling between April 2015 and March 2016, with 93% paid within 14 days; collected money is used for upkeep of streets and public spaces. Cllr Anna Smith said dog owners are responsible for cleaning up and that the prosecution sends a message that noncompliance will not be tolerated.

Prosecutors allege that former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory betrayed the U.S. by giving a Chinese spy information about human assets and other top-secret information in exchange for $25,000. Defense lawyers say Mallory is loyal and tried to string along the Chinese to learn about their intelligence operation and feed phony documents. The trial in the Eastern District of Virginia began with opening statements. Prosecutors said Mallory was found with $16,500 in undeclared cash after secondary screening at O’Hare Airport in April 2017 and later reached out to old CIA contacts to create a cover story; they said a Samsung phone used by the Chinese recruiter revealed text conversations with Mallory and that computer discs found at his home contained secret and top-secret documents sent to the recruiter. A CIA analyst and contractor testified that Mallory contacted them in February 2017. Mallory faces up to life in prison under a statute with stiffer penalties than those used in prior cases cited.

Kelly Keefe will become president of ERC, a Highland Heights-based HR resources, training, and consulting provider, on Jan. 1. She will be the first woman to lead ERC in its 97-year history in Northeast Ohio, succeeding Pat Perry, who has served as president for nearly 20 years. Perry will continue as chairman, supporting the leadership transition and focusing on NorthCoast 99, the ERChealth insurance program, and client relations. Keefe, currently ERC’s vice president of training, consulting, and coaching services and with ERC for nearly 13 years, has also previously worked at Deloitte for eight years.

The passage describes a virtual object machine learning approach for classifying highly dynamic subjects. It explains that training data for dynamic subjects is difficult to generate and label manually, and therefore uses synthetic, labeled training images created from 3D models (e.g., hands, dogs). The system constructs 3D models using rigging structures for key-point tracking, varies poses, applies different textures to simulate subject types, and controls environment backgrounds and lighting. A trained machine learning scheme (e.g., supervised or non-supervised methods) is then used to classify objects and their gestures/poses from received images or video. The disclosure also describes how the virtual object machine learning system can be integrated into a messaging system, including messaging client/server components, server-side image processing and databases, and an ephemeral timer system that time-limits access to content and content collections (e.g., ephemeral stories).

Upgrade is a near-future sci-fi horror action film starring Logan Marshall-Green as Grey Trace, whose idyllic life is destroyed by a savage attack that leaves him paralyzed. He later receives a top-secret healing process called STEM, which bridges his mind and body and gives him mechanical control, but also enables horrific potential. Using STEM to seek the truth and pursue revenge, Grey faces upgraded villains while the film explores the consequences of unchecked artificial intelligence and human loss of control. The film features highly violent, well-shot action scenes and automation-filled technology, while critics note the mystery could be more refined and the story may need more exposition.

Sen. John McCain criticized President Donald Trump for approving the release of the GOP-Nunes memo, saying it undermines the rule of law and helps Vladimir Putin. McCain urged officials to avoid viewing special counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation through politics, arguing Russia interfered in the 2016 election and that the efforts fueled political discord. He said the memo amounts to “partisan attacks” on the FBI and Department of Justice that serve no American interests. The memo, spearheaded by Devin Nunes, alleges the FBI abused surveillance authority during an investigation into Carter Page. After its release, congressional Democrats urged the House Intelligence Committee to publish a Democratic memo produced by Adam Schiff.

The passage communicates to the U.S. Congress copies of correspondence between government agents of the Hawaiian (Sandwich) Islands and the Secretary of State. It describes the islands as strategically located in the Pacific, used by American and European vessels for refitment and provisioning, and notes that the U.S. has substantial commercial involvement there. It characterizes the islands’ government as emerging from “barbarism,” seeking to improve conditions through education and civilized institutions, and argues that U.S. interests require respect for the islands’ independence and rights while also warning against possible moves by other powers to take possession or subvert the native government. The President recommends a moderate Treasury allowance for the consul to have authority to seek redress for American citizens and to enable communication with the local government regarding acts by Americans.

It then shifts to China, stating that English military operations against the Chinese Empire ended by a treaty opening ports Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, and Chinghai to British merchants. It questions whether these ports will remain closed to U.S. commerce, noting that the treaty does not address admission or exclusion of ships of other nations, implying other nations must negotiate with the Chinese government. The passage provides data on U.S. imports from China and on U.S. exports to China, discusses China’s prior policy of excluding foreigners and suggests treaties may soften this stance, and argues that western nations’ goods have found a market in China. It also says correspondent embassies and resident diplomatic missions are not necessarily contemplated between England and China. Finally, it recommends that Congress appropriate funds to compensate a commissioner to reside in China to protect American persons and property, hold intercourse with local authorities, and communicate with Chinese officials or the Emperor if instructed.

The case involves a real estate broker’s claim for commission against a purchaser. The broker solicited houses and later attempted to negotiate a purchase contract, but the sale was not consummated under his efforts. While he was working, another broker procured and got acceptance of an offer by the purchaser. The court found no proof of a special contract making the purchaser liable for commissions and found positive proof that the plaintiff never brought about the sale. The judgment for the plaintiff was reversed, and a new trial was ordered.

A 24-year-old man, Thabane Sigadla from KwaDabeka, was sentenced by the Pinetown Regional Court on 25 June 2018 to an effective 38 years’ imprisonment for carjacking, possession of an unlicensed firearm, and possession of ammunition. He was accused of hijacking vehicles in KwaDabeka in October 2016 and in New Germany in 2017, and was arrested in June 2017 after hijacking a vehicle in New Germany. The passage alleges that on 13 June 2017, a man and his family were accosted by three balaclava-wearing gunmen who demanded the victim’s Mercedes Benz and took his wallet. Police searched for the vehicle, arrested the suspect on Claremont Road, and linked him to the 2016 KwaDabeka hijacking. He was found guilty on all counts and sentenced.

Azerbaijani Health Ministry spokesperson Safaya Ahmadova said the US Department of State’s recommendation to its citizens not to undergo surgery in Azerbaijan and to bring prescription medicines in original packaging has nothing to do with Azerbaijan’s healthcare. She added that foreign states have accepted Azerbaijan’s medical institutions and professionalism, citing that many foreigners come to Azerbaijan for high-level treatment and surgery. Ahmadova also criticized a US report on tuberculosis in Azerbaijan as not reflecting the truth, stating that tuberculosis figures in Azerbaijan have been dropping year by year and that Global Fund data confirmed this.

The passage introduces AI-Noether, an AI system for abductive reasoning in scientific discovery. It addresses the problem that machine-learned formulas may not generalize, may be hard to interpret, and may not be consistent with or derivable from existing background theory, which can be incomplete or incorrect. AI-Noether takes polynomial background axioms and a hypothesized polynomial formula Q and generates candidate additional polynomial axioms (or reports failure) that make Q derivable from the augmented axiom system. The method uses an Encode–Decompose–Reason pipeline based on real algebraic geometry: encode axioms and Q as a solution set (variety), decompose it into irreducible components via primary decomposition, and reason by extracting generators from components and testing which candidates allow Q to be implied using ideal membership and projection/elimination. The approach is demonstrated on recovering missing axioms for multiple benchmark scientific laws, including Kepler’s Third Law, and performance is reported for cases where one or multiple axioms are missing, along with runtimes and recoverability criteria.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists led by Dr Henry Leung developed a method to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. The process involves adding water and bacteria to “Nanyang coffee,” letting it sit for seven to 10 days so bacteria consume the waste and produce PHA, which is extracted using environment-friendly solvents. The team used Cupriavidus necator for easier handling at room temperature and genetically modified the bacteria to improve yield, achieving more than 50% purity. From 100g of coffee waste, they can now obtain about 1g to 3g of pure PHA. Dr Leung said PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than PVC. Laboratory experiments began in 2013, and the team is now seeking industrial partners and aims to commercialise in three to five years.

The passage is a morning rundown of science, politics, and money driving biotech, mentioning multiple stories, including a planned furlough of more than 32,000 at HHS and disruptions to CDC and CMS communication due to a government shutdown, U.K. antitrust regulator action requested over alleged coordinated drugmaker efforts to raise medicine prices, and the Trump administration backing off 100% pharma tariffs threatened to start. It also lists several other biotech-related headlines.

The Iowa Supreme Court held that the district court had jurisdiction to review the Department of Job Service’s decision, but erred by reversing the Department. The court found Kehde was correctly disqualified from unemployment benefits for misconduct under section 96.5(2). Kehde was discharged after a night supervisor found him holding a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises, and the hearing officer and appeal board concluded this violated a known company rule and constituted misconduct. The court also held that Dubuque Pack’s withdrawal of its protest did not require reversing the misconduct decision because withdrawal did not affect the facts relevant to eligibility, making any error harmless. The case was reversed and remanded with instructions to enter an order consistent with the opinion.

A regulation American football field measures 120 yards long and 53.3 yards wide (360 feet by 160 feet), covering about 1.32 acres. Most play occurs between the end zones, where the open field is exactly 100 yards long and 53.3 yards wide. End zones are 10 yards deep and 53.3 yards wide, and a ball carrier must break the plane of the end zone to score; catching a pass requires demonstrating control and having at least one foot down in bounds (two in the NFL).  

Key markings include goal lines (10 yards from the end line, spanning sideline to sideline, with two goal lines 100 yards apart), yard lines marked every yard with solid lines every five yards and numbers generally appearing every ten yards, and hash marks that determine ball placement and vary by level (18 feet 6 inches in the NFL, 40 feet in college, 53 feet 4 inches in high school). Field numbers along the sidelines differ by level (bottom edge 12 yards from the sideline in the NFL, typically 9 in college, usually 6 in high school). Sidelines are 6 feet wide along the perimeter, and coaches are commonly restricted to between the 25-yard lines.

The IMF says Ghana’s “Ghana beyond Aid” vision and the economy’s first-year performance under President Akufo-Addo are an inspiration to African countries. At the maiden “Governor Speaks” series, IMF Deputy Director Abebe Selasie told Ghana to “keep on track.” Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta, speaking on a new IMF platform for learning from economic management success stories, explained the “Ghana beyond Aid” agenda and plans to achieve it within a generation. He cited revenue measures to boost domestic resource mobilisation, using those resources for job-creating growth in the real sector, improving incomes, and maintaining recent high growth levels.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials are described as increasingly complex, with more data collection and regulator review contributing to longer Phase II and III durations. Trial burden on participants and staff is increasing, especially for lower socioeconomic and minority groups, and this can reduce recruitment, retention, and site attractiveness. The ICH E19 guideline encourages reducing irrelevant or nonessential data, but progress has been limited due to complex protocol design, often driven by copy-and-paste approaches and template-based schedules of assessment (SoAs). The passage reports that costs of trial inefficiencies from protocol design have not been measured well, motivating Merck’s “Lean Design” project and Faro Health’s tools to quantify impacts of SoA design choices. Lean Design workshops rebuild SoAs starting from a minimal “Ground Zero” and evaluate proposed additions using simplification principles, including relevance to plausible biological effects, appropriate timing/frequency, and whether assessments can be done in subsamples; routine clinical care data may be handled as adverse events rather than included in the SoA. In workshops across six Merck protocols, major SoA changes were often identified that could reduce participant and staff time, costs, and complexity; recommended reductions varied, including examples of large cost savings in a cardiovascular trial. Changes were not always adopted because many protocols were already late in development, teams anticipated regulatory concerns, and some groups asserted that certain assessments could not be changed. The passage concludes that rebuilding protocols from Ground Zero with quantitative feedback can substantially reduce inessential SoA elements and reduce burdens and costs, though estimated impacts were limited to items listed in the SoA and did not include broader downstream costs.

The passage says that WebRTC VPN bugs can leak a user’s real IP even when using a VPN service, and that VPN providers have worked to address this. It reports that on March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers, finding 20 that leaked users’ IPs via WebRTC (16.13%) and 101 that hid users’ IPs. It lists providers that leak IPs and suggests testing with several websites. If a VPN leaks IP, the passage recommends disabling WebRTC or installing an add-on. It also claims to list and rank VPN services that protect privacy with WebRTC, including ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, and others.

The passage says MoviePass has provided solid value for frequent moviegoers despite customer service problems and scare tactics. It reports that MoviePass ticket purchases made up 13.21% of the opening weekend domestic box office for *Roman J. Israel, Esq.* and 10.00% for *Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri*, with percentages reportedly increasing from the first to second weeks for titles like *Justice League*, *Coco*, and *The Snowman*. The passage also states MoviePass signed a marketing and performance-based revenue deal with an independent movie distribution company, under which MoviePass will promote a particular film and earn revenue based on incremental ticket price increases; it suggests ads for certain movies may appear. The CEO of Helios and Matheson Analytics previously said the company aimed to attract customers to collect viewing data for targeted ads. MoviePass reportedly did not disclose the distribution company’s identity when contacted.

Last Friday, MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges council members reassured residents that recyclable materials collected locally are valued despite ongoing reports of a global recycling crisis. The passage says China previously bought about two thirds of North America’s recyclables, but new stringent Chinese rules now deem some previously accepted materials, including “contaminated” plastics and paper, to have little to no value, potentially leaving municipalities unable to sell or distribute rejected recyclables. Since 2017, the MRC has been a member of Tricentris, which manages nearly 33% of Quebec’s recyclable materials. Council members and municipal employees visited the Lachute sorting centre, where Hans Gruenwald stated that Tricentris is doing well due to a pension fund and investments in research and development, and urged citizens to keep recycling and improve material quality. The passage also mentions an online sorting tool (tricycle-mrcvs.ca) and the Tricentris Express newsletter (www.tricentris.com/tricentris-express/).

The passage describes an improved non-occluding intravascular axial blood pump intended to reduce or minimize hemolysis. It explains that blood pumps can create stresses that lead to hemolysis and blood clotting, and presents design approaches to reduce shear forces, including a cylindrical shroud with an inlet and outlet, a centrally disposed shroud and impeller on a shared central axis, a centrally disposed motor, and pillars that couple the motor to the shroud and keep the shroud close to the impeller. Additional geometric features discussed for reducing hemolysis include a trumpeted shroud inlet, raked-back impeller blade leading edges, an appropriately long shroud inlet length, a bare hub length, designed shroud-to-impeller clearance, matching stator and impeller flare angles, and pillar geometry/angle selection including possible mismatching between pillars and impeller blades. The passage also outlines analysis and testing methods, including transient CFD with hotspot evaluation, Lagrangian particle tracking with a power-law damage model for estimating hemolysis, and in vitro hemolysis testing and flow loop performance validation. It reports improvements from an initial reference design to prototypes including P_ref and P_31, with reductions in shear stress (e.g., a reported reduction of maximum shear exposure by 150–200 Pa and average impeller shear reduced below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm) and a reported 78% improvement in Normalized Index of Hemolysis at a desired operating speed of 20 krpm compared to a reference pump BP80, while maintaining flow rate and pressure generation after design changes.

Asteroid 2025 TF passed extremely close to Earth over Antarctica on October 1, flying about 428 km (±7 km) above the surface at 00:47:26 UTC. Measuring about 1 to 3 meters in diameter, it was detected only a few hours after the flyby by the Catalina Sky Survey and was later observed by ESA astronomers to confirm its trajectory with high precision. The asteroid was small enough to pose no real threat, though objects of this size can create bright fireballs and sometimes leave small meteorites if they enter the atmosphere.

Mason Brothers & Tarlin v. United States (No. 5961) concerns the proper dutiable value of Christmas tree ornaments exported from Germany and imported at Boston, Massachusetts. The parties stipulated that the ornaments were exported in August 1938, were similar to those in F. W. Woolworth Co. v. United States, and were subject to similar foreign market conditions; the Woolworth record was incorporated. The judge found that the ornaments were freely offered for sale in Germany’s Sonneberg-Lauscha district in wholesale quantities during the export period. He held that, as a matter of law, the proper dutiable foreign and export values for ornaments exported after January 1, 1938 are the per se unit invoice prices plus 3% social assessments, and—if not included—costs of cases, packing, containers, and other charges to place the goods packed and ready for shipment to the United States. The appeal was dismissed insofar as it related to other merchandise, and judgment would be rendered accordingly.

The passage describes molecular dynamics simulations of radiation damage in pure niobium at 300 K over primary knock-on atom (PKA) energies from 1 to 75 keV, using four interatomic potentials: SNAP, EAM, FS-1, and FS-2. It summarizes prior experimental and computational work and notes that MD studies focused on niobium at higher energies and detailed defect morphologies are limited. The simulations analyze Frenkel pair evolution, defect counts, subcascade formation, clustering fractions, cluster sizes, and defect morphology. Results show that defect production occurs rapidly after the ballistic phase and then partially recombines to a stabilized residual population; the peak time and surviving defects increase with PKA energy, and a two-regime behavior emerges around ~20 keV linked to subcascade formation. Vacancy clustering is high across energies and potentials, while interstitial clustering is lower and more sensitive to energy and potential choice. Cluster morphology is highly potential-dependent: FS-2 primarily produces 1/2⟨111⟩ loops (over 70% of its defects), FS-1 and SNAP produce larger fractions of C15-like rings and hybrid/disordered structures, EAM yields a more balanced mix of ring-like and loop-like clusters and occasional ⟨100⟩ clusters at high energies, and SNAP produces compact cascades with relatively high C15-like ring fractions (up to nine atoms) that may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ and ⟨100⟩ dislocation loops. The study concludes that interatomic potential choice strongly influences defect types, sizes, and growth behavior, providing insights into niobium’s irradiation response.

The speaker says a major win boosts confidence and shows the team can play against another team without needing many changes, putting pressure on the opponent to adjust. They prefer playing games over practicing and believe having four or five days would be good, but they see the current schedule as not a disadvantage. They note that after a big win in San Jose they have time to enjoy it, which they say is harder in playoffs. Live Nation is offering $20 “all-in” tickets for over 2,000 summer concert tour dates to celebrate National Concert Week. The promotion runs April 30 through May 8 on Live Nation’s website and includes over 1.5 million tickets for live performances across genres such as Comedy, Country, Hip-Hop, Latin, Metal, Rock, Pop, and more. The ticket offer features artists including Alan Jackson, Bon Jovi, Kevin Hart, Keith Urban, and Shakira, and a full list of shows is available at livenation.com.

Horsell Lodge near Woking, Surrey offers specialised residential and dementia care, including short-term respite and tailored long-term care. Staff work with residents and their families, friends, and advocates to understand each person’s history and plan bespoke care, support, and daily activities. Residents are encouraged to bring personal possessions to furnish their rooms. The passage advises checking that a care home fits the individual’s circumstances and notes that service and facility descriptions come from the care home, with no responsibility for errors; readers should email the site if information is missing or incorrect.

The passage compares the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and the Pixel Watch 4 as adventure/outdoor watches. It argues that Apple’s watch has superior adventure features, including satellite communications for regular texting, stronger water performance (automatic water lock under 10 cm), and suitability for diving and underwater use. In the author’s weekend off-grid testing, the Ultra 3’s battery lasted from Friday morning to Sunday morning (up to 42 hours in the Apple Watch Ultra 3), and the Pixel Watch 4’s larger model lasted a full weekend as well (up to 30 or 40 hours), charging from 16% to 100% in 45 minutes. The Pixel Watch 4 is described as better for health and sleep tracking due to Fitbit, including more accurate sleep measurement and hypertension-related notifications. The Pixel Watch 4 offers emergency satellite services but not regular texts over satellite, requires an active carrier plan and clear sky for satellite access, and its water lock requires deeper submersion than the Ultra 3. The author concludes the Ultra 3 is the better adventure watch overall, but the Pixel Watch 4 is more compelling due to its lower price ($399 for 45-mm, $349 for 41-mm) and stronger health features.

A Federal High Court in Katsina ordered former Governor Ibrahim Shema to be remanded in EFCC custody until April 27 for alleged money laundering. Shema is on trial over alleged misappropriation of about N5.7 billion SURE-P funds and faces a 26-count charge bordering on fraud. He pleaded not guilty. His defence counsel filed for bail on April 18 and said Shema is a senior lawyer, former governor, and has his international passport with the Federal Government. The prosecution objected, arguing the bail application was premature and that double bail applications should be disregarded, urging the court to remand him. Justice Babagana Ashigar remanded Shema until April 27, when the court would hear the written bail application.

The passage describes how algebraic generalizations in computer science have led to increased interest in semirings, which provide modular modelling and analysis tools in areas such as algorithms, automata theory, optimization, and machine learning. It outlines logical and computational frameworks over semirings, including weighted automata and weighted Turing machines, semiring semantics for propositional, first-order, and existential second-order logic, and satisfiability notions. The text defines semirings and gives examples, then introduces logics over semirings (PL\(_K\), FO\(_K\), ESO\(_K\)) with semantics based on assigning semiring values and treating “truth” as any non-zero value. It defines BSSK machines as real computation models extended to semirings, establishes a semiring analogue of NP as the class NPK via nondeterministic polynomial-time BSSK machines, and discusses reductions and NPK-completeness. Finally, it presents a semiring version of Fagin’s theorem by proving that ESO\(_K\) equals NPK, using encodings of semiring interpretations and simulations between logical formulas and BSSK computations.

Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) can be limited by missing or costly phenotype data, and ML-assisted GWAS methods that impute missing phenotypes before running GWAS are becoming popular. The passage argues that existing ML-assisted GWAS strategies may yield pervasive false-positive associations because they typically treat imputed phenotypes as observed and rely on heuristic checks. Using a T2D example in UK Biobank, the authors report high replication failure rates (e.g., 81% at P < 5e-8) for GWAS performed on imputed phenotypes, including failures driven by variants associated with imputation predictors such as HbA1c through non-T2D-relevant pathways.  

To address this, the paper introduces Post-prediction GWAS (POP-GWAS), a framework for valid and more powerful inference using summary statistics. POP-GWAS imputes phenotypes in both labeled and unlabeled samples, runs three GWAS (observed and imputed phenotypes in labeled data, plus imputed phenotypes in unlabeled data), and combines summary statistics to debias SNP-level effects. The authors claim POP-GWAS provides unbiased estimates and calibrated type-I error without assumptions about phenotype missingness degree, imputation quality, or the ML algorithm, and it only requires GWAS summary statistics. In simulations and reanalysis of the T2D benchmark, POP-GWAS is reported to control type-I error and improve power while restoring replication.  

The method is applied to bone mineral density (BMD) across 14 skeletal sites in UK Biobank using DXA-BMD imputation, reporting increased effective sample size and more genome-wide significant loci than conventional approaches, including novel loci and site-specific genetic architecture insights. The discussion concludes that POP-GWAS can improve the reliability of ML-assisted GWAS and supports future study designs using phenotype imputation alongside formal statistical safeguards.

The passage discusses limitations in predicting polymeric materials’ mechanical and rheological properties before fabrication, noting that varying design parameters (e.g., polymer molecular weight or concentration) changes both viscoelastic properties (such as shear modulus \(G_0\) and relaxation time \(\tau\)) and other factors like viscosity and normal stresses, making it difficult to separate mechanical from chemical origins of flow differences. It motivates investigating how design parameters—polymer concentration \(c\), molecular weight \(M\), and solvent viscosity \(\eta_s\)—affect viscoelastic properties, particularly \(G_0\), \(\tau\), and the first normal stress difference coefficient \(\psi_1\).  

The authors develop and experimentally verify a framework to design dilute Boger-like polymer solutions with controlled viscoelastic properties using a Zimm-model-based fitting approach. They describe material preparation for polyisobutylene (PIB) dissolved in a polybutene (PB)/light mineral oil solvent system, including gel permeation chromatography for molecular weight and polydispersity, and rheological measurements using small-amplitude oscillatory shear and rotational shear. They present scaling relationships for how \(G_0\), \(\tau\), \(\psi_1\), and a correction factor \(\delta\chi\) depend on \(c\), \(M\), and \(\eta_s\), and then use a design matrix to map target properties \(G_0\), \(\tau\), and \(\psi_1\) to fluid compositions.  

Finally, the framework is tested by fabricating multiple fluids with targeted and systematically varied \(G_0\) and \(\tau\), and separate fluids with targeted constant \(\psi_1\) while varying viscosity, with results reported as close to target values. The passage concludes that the method enables practical design of dilute viscoelastic fluids and can support interpretation of viscoelastic flow experiments.

Jason Day will play a rematch against Louis Oosthuizen from his 2016 final win in the group stage of this week’s World Golf Championships-Match Play event in Texas. Day, the eighth seed, will also face Jason Dufner and James Hahn at Austin Country Club. Marc Leishman, a top-16 seed, drawn against Branden Grace, Bubba Watson, and Julian Suri. Cameron Smith, seeded 46th, will play Hideki Matsuyama, Patrick Cantlay, and Yusaku Miyazato; he needs a strong finish for a Masters invitation at Augusta. An all-Australian final is possible, and Smith could face Day in the semi-finals. The passage lists the groups for the event.

Week 7 Idaho high school football rankings were highlighted by largely unchanged top 15 teams, including Bishop Kelly and No. 4 Eagle staying undefeated despite late scares. Several changes reshaped the bottom rankings, with new teams Minico (4-1) and Ririe (6-0) entering, while other teams fell out after losses. The passage lists numerous game results and top performers, including Bishop Kelly’s 22-20 win over Columbia, Eagle’s 21-14 win over Mountain View, Timberline’s 50-19 win over Capital, and multiple other shutouts and high-scoring victories across classes.

The passage describes the Supreme Court’s return after a three-month summer break, including plans for an annual gathering and the release of order lists. It notes commentary from Justices Clarence Thomas, former Justice Anthony Kennedy, and a column by George F. Will on legal precedent, court discourse, and originalism. It also covers several recent Supreme Court actions and filings, including emergency docket orders related to Trump administration policies on foreign-aid funding and birthright citizenship, and a due response brief concerning protected status for Venezuelan citizens. The passage explains what Supreme Court order lists are, how they are typically released, and how emergency relief timelines can vary, citing analysis that conservative and liberal outcomes correlated with different decision speeds.

The passage describes Enron’s rise and decline, focusing on its culture and leadership under Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay. It portrays early Enron as energetic and innovative, transforming from a pipeline company into a trading and marketing firm that grew rapidly in stock value and revenues. Skilling helped develop the “Gas Bank” concept, build a market-dominating trading operation, and create a knowledge-based, aggressive company culture that emphasized profit and constant performance. Enron later expanded into other commodities, online trading, broadband, and communications, while using practices such as mark-to-market accounting. As Enron’s success continued, the culture became increasingly harsh, competitive, and paranoid, contributing to high staff turnover and strained relationships.

The passage then links Enron’s troubles to external pressures and internal factors, including the California energy crisis, declining stock price, scrutiny of accounting practices, and problems with the telecommunications business when the tech bubble burst. It notes Skilling’s resignation as CEO in February 2001 and recounts his personal sacrifices and dissatisfaction. Ken Lay responds by promising changes to Enron’s approach and culture, stating that innovations would occur closer to Enron’s core and that the Performance Review Committee had created morale problems.

Euro zone stocks opened 2017 higher after euro-area factory PMI data showed the fastest manufacturing activity growth in more than five years. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.5% to its highest since December 2015, while the euro fell 0.4% back below US$1.05 as the dollar resumed an uptrend. European indexes and bank shares rose, and yields on lower-rated euro zone government bonds fell to multi-week lows. A gun attack in Istanbul and another attack in Baghdad were seen as having little market impact, though the Turkish lira slipped. China’s manufacturing expanded for a fifth month but growth slowed, and bitcoin rose above US$1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

The NBA released the full national TV schedule for the 2017-18 season on Monday, four days after the Christmas Day schedule and the first-week national TV schedule were released. The passage lists game matchups with dates, times (Eastern), and networks (including TNT, ESPN, NBA TV, and ABC) from October 17 through April 11.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2015 includes company and filing information, forward-looking statement disclosures, and a description of its business. Apple designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. It discusses its business strategy, geographic operating segments (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific), major products (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, iPod, Apple TV), operating systems and applications, and services such as Internet Services, iCloud, AppleCare, and Apple Pay. The document also outlines competition, supply and manufacturing considerations, research and development, legal and regulatory risks, warranty and backlog policies, employee count, available public information, and begins its risk factor discussion, plus information on stock exchange listing, dividends, and share repurchase activity.

The passage lists mappings from digits and certain special symbols to typed characters and Bengali-related symbols (e.g., ্, ়, ʼ, ঽ, ৺, ৹, ৲, ৳, danda forms, ₹).
