It explains that ligatures are rendered, with ZWJ and ZWNJ used to produce alternate ligature rendering: a consonant followed by ZWJ gives a half-formed consonant, and a consonant followed by ZWNJ gives a dead consonant (examples: প্রশ্ন, প্রশ্‍ন, প্রশ্‌ন). It also says ZWJ separates English characters that form one Bengali vowel (ai, au) into two vowels without adding ZWJ as a character.

Oil prices fell as Israel and Hamas struck a rare truce, which helped calm markets after months of unrest. In early trading, Wall Street was modestly higher near record levels, with the S&P 500 up 0.1% and gold holding near its latest record. U.S. benchmark crude fell to $62.34 per barrel and Brent to $66.07 per barrel. European stocks were mixed and most Asian markets rose, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 up 1.8%. Company highlights included PepsiCo’s net income falling 11% and Delta projecting full-year profit within the upper half of its prior guidance.

Callinex Mines Inc. announced it filed an independent technical report for a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) on SEDAR for its 100% owned Nash Creek and Superjack Projects in New Brunswick. The 2018 maiden PEA for the Nash Creek Project outlines a 10-year, 3,900 tpd open-pit operation with a Dense Media Separation plant and a 1,950 tpd conventional flotation facility, reporting a pre-tax internal rate of return of 34.1% (25.2% post-tax) and a pre-tax NPV at an 8% discount rate of C$230 million (C$128 million post-tax), based on C$168 million pre-production capital costs and a zinc price of US$1.25/lb. The company plans to start a drill program within 10 days to look for potential satellite deposits and says additional exploration could improve economics. The PEA is preliminary, includes Inferred Mineral Resources considered too speculative for economic evaluation into Mineral Reserves, and there is no certainty it will be realized.

The passage attributes an aphorism about buying when “there’s blood in the streets,” even if the blood is one’s own, to Baron Rothschild after the Battle of Waterloo. It argues that the retail apparel industry is “bleeding,” citing about a 20% decline in the retail apparel sector over the last 52 weeks, driven by e-commerce, store chain overexpansion, and mall overcapacity, and it highlights uncertainty in the product supply chain from changing trade policy. The passage focuses on Francesca’s Holdings Corp. (FRAN), describing it as financially strong with $48 million cash, no debt, and about $57.6 million in free cash flow, and operating 670+ stores with plans to reach 900. For 1Q17, it reports sales up 1% year/year to $107.7 million, comparable store sales down 5%, and diluted EPS of $0.12, along with reduced gross margin and lower net income versus the prior year. It provides FY18 guidance for net sales, comparable sales, EPS, and store openings/closures, and notes analyst FY18 estimates. The passage discusses valuation and accruals, referencing measures related to earnings quality and describing FRAN as profitable on earnings and cash bases, using cash for share buybacks, and concluding that FRAN could see share price growth over 1–3 years and 3–5 years. It ends with a disclosure stating the author has no positions and no plans to initiate positions.

Pay for private college presidents continued to rise, with the number earning over $1 million spiking in 2015 and average compensation increasing 9% to $570,000. The New York Times, citing an executive-compensation survey by The Chronicle of Higher Education covering more than 1,200 chief executives at over 600 private colleges from 2008–15, reported that 58 presidents earned more than $1 million in 2015 (up from 39 in 2014). The passage also notes that two Ohio presidents ranked in the top 50 and two more in spots 51–100; Daniel Curran was the highest-paid at over $2.4 million total pay (No. 8), and Barbara Snyder ranked No. 41 with total compensation of $1,152,836. Other top-100 Ohio-related entries included Grant H. Cornwell with $911,651 and Marvin Krislov with $829,913.

The Department of Trade and Industry of the African Union Commission organized the First African Union Start Up Fest symposium themed around unleashing the potential of start-ups through start-up development. The meeting aimed to assess the capacity needs of start-ups and tech-hubs, enable interaction between policy makers and the private sector, lay foundations for an African Association of Start-ups, and provide political support for start-up development. Participants included tech-hub managers, youth entrepreneurs, senior officials, regional economic communities, business leaders, development partners, academia, and civil society. Speakers highlighted the role of SMEs in improving competitiveness, the need to address Africa’s unemployment through youth entrepreneurship supported by digital economy opportunities, and the importance of including inclusion and improving youth access to education, skills, employment, technology, and economic opportunities. Major outcomes included hosting a follow-up side event at the 2018 Transform Africa Summit in Kigali focused on setting up an African Association of Community Innovation Hub, with the African Union Commission working with i4Policy and other participants to draft the side event agenda.

Many offsites focus on alignment, communication, coordination, or celebration, but when breakthroughs are sought, the passage recommends using an environment that disrupts routines and enables connections. It emphasizes centering on a meaningful, rewarding shared purpose, organizing people and program flow around it, actively driving deeper connections, and ensuring actions are both impactful and practical with follow-through and measured success. Yarrow Kraner and partners apply these ideas in their HATCH experiences; the passage says these principles can be used to “HATCH a better world.” It outlines “five BRAVE questions” across behaviors, relationships, attitudes, values, and the environment, including “Where to play?” through unfamiliar places and communal living (e.g., no cell phone, limited Internet, tents, shared meals), and “What matters & why?” through an inclusive, supportive group at the intersection of creativity, technology, and design thinking. It also describes organizing “People” via curated cross-pollination of diverse participants, and designing “Program” with a mix of pre-work, talks, exercises, activities, prototype sessions, music, meals/drinks, and free time.

Adult-onset dementia involves gradual neuron degeneration and loss of brain function, leading to cognitive decline and impaired daily activities. In the United States, Alzheimer’s disease (AD) affects 6.8 million adults age 65+; vascular dementia (VaD) is the second most common form and often co-occurs with AD and is difficult to distinguish. AD is associated with amyloid-beta aggregation and neurofibrillary tangles, while VaD may result from reduced brain blood flow due to small vessel disease or stroke. Differences in aging versus dementia pathology and limited understanding of molecular mechanisms across ancestries motivate a multi-ancestry study to identify gene-trait associations.

The study uses METRO, a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association method, integrating genotype and gene expression data from 1,032 African American and 801 European American participants from GENOA with GWAS summary statistics for general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), and AD. Fine-mapping is performed with FOCUS, and functional enrichment and gene overlap analyses are conducted. Results reported significant METRO-associated genes at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold: 602 genes for general cognitive function, 45 for WMH (EA AD input), 231 for AD (EA GWAS), and 9 for AD (AA GWAS). After fine-mapping, overlapping genes included ICA1L between WMH and AD, and TOMM40 as the overlapping gene between AD TWAS results from EA and AA. The study concludes that transcriptomic mechanisms involving innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, and neuroinflammation are implicated, and that downregulation of ICA1L may contribute to overlapping AD and VaD neuropathology.

The passage compiles multiple news items and editorials dated June 7, 2001, centered on Enron and related issues. It reports on Enron and Exelon’s Commonwealth Edison deal to supply power to Chicago and 47 suburbs, ongoing disputes involving Enron’s Dabhol Power project in India and related lender meetings in Singapore, and India’s prime minister expressing confidence that the dispute will be resolved. Other items cover Enron-related office space in London, Enron’s plan to challenge a power regulator’s order in India, California regulators considering ending direct access for large electricity users, a U.S. debate in which automakers and suppliers criticize a Bush move to investigate foreign steel imports, Pacific Hydro’s wind and hydro expansion, and a Chicago Tribune report on city council redistricting and Enron’s proposed electricity supply contract for municipal buildings.

Since SARS-CoV-2 emerged in late 2019, COVID-19 has remained an ongoing global public health threat, with official cases approaching 600 million by August 2022 and estimates of prior infection reaching about 3.4 billion. The passage reports that first-generation lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines (Comirnaty and Spikevax) provide temporary protection against infection and longer-term protection against severe disease and death, but vaccine challenges include antibody waning and variants of concern (VOCs). Additional boosters and hybrid immunity (vaccination plus natural infection) are described as improving immune responses, and the role of exposure timing—especially the interval between vaccination and natural infection—is a focus of the study.

The study analyzes two cohorts and uses ELISA and live-virus neutralization assays against SARS-CoV-2 WA1 and VOCs (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, Omicron BA.2). Hybrid immunity shows higher neutralizing titers than vaccination alone across all tested strains, with variant cross-neutralization and antibody quality also improved. Neutralizing titers and full-length spike antibody levels correlate with the exposure interval, and neutralizing titers increase up to at least 400 days after first exposure, with the largest fold increases against more resistant variants such as Beta and Omicron. The authors conclude that longer delays between vaccination and infection are associated with stronger neutralizing antibody responses and improved breadth of neutralization.

Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones addressed why he did not pursue or tackle Trevor Lawrence on Lawrence’s game-winning touchdown in the Chiefs’ loss to the Jaguars. Jones said it was a “teaching point,” admitting he thought the play was over when Lawrence went down. He also said he will do better going forward and that it “won’t happen again.” Jones said he deactivated his X and Instagram accounts before the game, contrary to what fans believed after the loss. The Chiefs next play a prime-time game Sunday night against the Lions, and Jones said he has been focused on stopping the NFL’s top-scoring offense.

A company in Leicester and Leicestershire, DPI (UK), which makes aluminium frames and lightboxes, has received a grant of more than £12,200 from the Collaborate project to support growth. The funding will help it buy a new automated saw to cut larger aluminium panels, produce bigger structures in the UK instead of importing, reduce contract completion times, and eventually create more jobs. DPI’s directors said the current saw needed more maintenance, causing delays, and that the new saw increases capacity, competitiveness, and output. Collaborate grants of £5,000 to £25,000 are available to eligible businesses to cover a third of capital project costs, and the scheme provides workshops and one-to-one advice.

Andrew W. Lo welcomes first-year MBA students to MIT 15.401 Finance Theory and says the course will satisfy curiosity about finance over 13 weeks. He argues finance is practical “lifeblood” of business because it applies to practical management problems and is indispensable for financial management. He shares his background (20 years at MIT, prior Wharton teaching, PhD in economics from Harvard, Yale economics degree) and uses an analogy of tasting finance to explain why students may become excited by it. He outlines course structure: motivation, key course characters, financial analysis challenges, and frameworks involving time and risk. He states two fundamental challenges of finance are (1) valuing assets and (2) managing assets, where managing means choosing among options based on value and objectives. He explains valuation is difficult because the concept of “value” can vary, and he demonstrates price discovery via an auction where a sealed packaged item is auctioned with limited information; the market establishes a bid, illustrating how markets help establish value. He then presents a framework for financial analysis based on accounting (stock and flow), using balance sheets and income statements, and discusses corporate financial decisions in terms of cash and timing, extending the framework to personal household decisions. He describes that time and risk make finance challenging and that modern finance comes from combining them. He lists six fundamental principles of finance, covering preferences and self-interest, and notes approximations that will be questioned later in the course. Finally, he reviews course requirements and grading: participation (10%), one case write-up (10%), midterm (25%), and final (55%), along with readings, recitations, optional problem banks, and advice on how to engage with lectures and questions.

The passage contains excerpts from Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2022, including portions of the consolidated financial statements, notes, and forward-looking statements. It provides figures for the consolidated balance sheet, statements of operations, comprehensive income, changes in equity, and cash flows, along with accounting policy notes covering items such as revenue recognition, estimates, income taxes, net income per share, restricted cash, accounts receivable, warranties, fair value measurements, debt and finance leases, digital assets, intangible assets, inventory, property and equipment, and other long-term liabilities. It also describes commitments and contingencies, including operating leases and multiple legal proceedings, regulatory matters, and variable interest entity arrangements.

President Trump’s description of a House-passed health care bill as “mean” is aggravating some conservatives he had pushed to support it, while Senate efforts to reshape the bill increasingly threaten to extend discussions into July. Rep. Dave Brat said Trump’s comment left him and other Republicans “scratching their heads,” noting Trump previously praised the bill after the House passed it May 4. Congressional sources said Trump made the “mean” comment at a closed-door White House lunch with 15 Republican senators. Senate leaders’ attempts to write their own bill have been slowed by disagreements between conservatives and moderates over issues including Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements, and subsidies. John Cornyn urged patience, saying a July 4 recess passage was a “good goal” and that the chamber should finish “by the end of July.”

ARDD issued a report on Jordan’s legal response to the Syrian refugee crisis at an international conference held at Yarmouk University, praising several government agencies’ “rapid” support in partnership with UNHCR. The study said the legal sections at Jordanian refugee camps are “internationally recognised” and provide specialised services such as juvenile courts and family protection, with legal services aimed at preventing human-rights violations. It also noted safety and quality measures through legal awareness programmes and improved capacities for lawyers and legal service providers. ARDD CEO Samar Muhareb said challenges remain, including new daily needs seven years into the crisis and difficulties related to accessing the formal labour market outside camps, as well as pressure on resources and limited evaluation of the legal aid sector. She cited a campaign started last month to encourage UNHCR registration, which has led to 25,000 newly registered refugees so far.

A Moody’s Investor Service report said the government faces risks in achieving its 3.3% fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019, but it may still meet it by cutting planned capital spending to offset slippage. A Moody’s and ICRA poll in Singapore and Mumbai identified rising crude oil prices as a major risk, and most attendees expected India to miss the fiscal deficit target. Only 23.3% of respondents in Singapore and 13.6% in Mumbai thought the target would be achieved. The report also said the government’s PSB recapitalisation package is not sufficient because banks have not raised capital as planned. Moody’s cited higher oil prices as a growth risk, noted risks to sovereign credit dynamics have diminished since subsidy reforms, and said elevated oil prices are a downside risk; the Indian crude oil basket rose from $66 per barrel in April to around $75.

The passage says that mic’d bats and high-tech sensors reveal how greater noctule bats attack and snatch songbirds out of the sky. It also describes a greater noctule bat caught in a mist net with a passerine feather and blood in its mouth.

The passage describes a database privacy system that receives analytical queries from a client and returns differentially private (DP) responses. A hardware database privacy device is coupled to a private database system and identifies a differential privacy level for each request, including a privacy parameter indicating the degree of information released. It selects relevant data and modifies the operations for the requested query so the resulting output set is differentially private, which is then provided to the client for display.

The system includes modules for user interface, query/library support, account management, query handling, data integration, and a privacy system. The privacy system contains engines for common DP query types such as count, median, mean, variance, interquartile range, batch gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, random forest, histogram, model testing, synthetic database generation, and validation of (ε,δ)-differential privacy. It defines differential privacy using neighboring databases and parameters ε and δ, and discusses concepts including global sensitivity, local sensitivity, and smooth sensitivity. The engines produce DP outputs by perturbing query outputs or intermediate computations with noise, and the passage also describes generating DP visualizations, testing classifier performance with perturbed confusion matrices, and creating a DP synthetic database via projection while retaining approximate spatial relationships.

The passage warns that the integrated circuit can be damaged by electrostatic discharge (ESD) and advises using appropriate handling precautions, noting ESD damage can range from subtle performance degradation to complete device failure. It also describes that mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 is the most current, may change without notice, and includes notes such as soldering the package thermal pad to the printed circuit board and that via and solder coverage details depend on application and board design. The revision history lists multiple updates from July 30, 2025 to September 30, 2025, and the document includes technical/disclaimer information about data sources, lack of warranties, and limitation of liability.

TyreWatch predictive tyre management was launched on 16 May at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus in Oxfordshire. The system aims to improve fleet productivity and efficiency by continuously monitoring tyre pressure and temperature via wheel-rim sensors, sending data to a central server for real-time analysis and secure delivery through a web portal and push notifications. It issues maintenance alerts based on trends against vehicle baselines, provides driver warning lights, and continues monitoring after vehicles return with reduced frequency to detect debris punctures. TyreWatch supports multi-brand tyre policies, works with existing tyres, and can integrate with manufacturer-installed technology through open system architecture. The company says testing prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns and includes impacts on fuel consumption, tyre wear, and road safety. TyreWatch is part of the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium and received £1.2 million funding from Innovate UK to develop intelligent tyre telematics for autonomous and platooned commercial vehicles.

When the star player is a ballhandler, the “horns” or double mid screen alignment can isolate and free the star player by allowing them to go either right or left, making it difficult for chasers to defend. After passing the mid screen, the star can drive hard to the basket to create an outnumbered situation. If they can’t drive, they can feed the rolling screener or make a kick-out pass to corner shooters for outside shots. Variations include dropping to a cutter for a layup when a ballside post helps, or screen-and-pop options where one screener pops while the other rolls. Single/double continuity can be initiated with a reversal pass to the top, forming single and double screens using baseline players and the roller. Success depends on proper execution and coordination, including defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. The passage also discusses scouting opponents for defensive reads and counters, watching for defensive adjustments after substitutions or timeouts, and deploying different alignments to prevent defenders from focusing on one set. It further describes the “Box & One” defense as four players playing a box zone while one “chaser” denies passes and rebounds.

Japanese government bonds firmed on Friday after a two-year auction saw strong demand, with investors awaiting details of the Bank of Japan’s regular bond purchases for May. The benchmark 10-year JGB yield stayed at 0.015%, and 10-year JGB futures ended at 151.02. At the Ministry of Finance’s 2.2 trillion yen two-year JGB sale, 97.2833% of bids were accepted at the lowest price of 100.585, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 5.51 times. Yields generally fell across two-, five-, and superlong-dated maturities. The BOJ planned to release May purchase details later on Friday, and Governor Haruhiko Kuroda said the BOJ’s main policy target is interest rates, not the pace of bond buying, and that it can achieve yield targets with less bond buying. The BOJ also kept monetary policy unchanged while offering its most optimistic economic assessment in nine years.

The passage is an address to the Senate and House of Representatives expressing gratitude for Providence’s mercies, reviewing foreign relations, and describing domestic policy and administration. It notes peace and growing harmony in some federal relations since the prior session, discusses issues and negotiations involving Russia and the Ottoman Porte, France and unresolved indemnity claims, and Great Britain regarding the northeastern boundary and commercial disputes. It outlines a general U.S. policy favoring liberal commercial treaties, free trade principles, and reciprocity, and recounts earlier treaty history and the decline of colonial exclusion, while criticizing revived exclusion by Great Britain. It summarizes progress on indemnity claims involving Denmark, stability and unsettled conditions in parts of Central and South America, and recent peace between Buenos Aires and Brazil. The passage reports favorable treasury revenue and planned debt reduction, discusses tariff effects on revenue and sectional burdens, and addresses federal and state sovereignty principles. It then reviews reports from the War, Engineer, Navy, Post Office, and other government departments, including Army discipline and Indian-tribe relations, fortifications and public works, naval improvements, postal growth, and public building and land office matters. It concludes by requesting attention to preparations for the next U.S. census and suggests improvements to future enumeration methods.

Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh said the government is considering introducing skill development courses in educational institutions to provide students with knowhow and technical knowledge of various vocations. He interacted with students at Government College for Women in Gandhi Nagar and Nawakadal, Srinagar, and praised students’ efforts in activities such as mushroom cultivation, florist shops, making fresh chocolates, and producing paper mache items. He said colleges should continuously upgrade students’ technical skills and improve product quality, and that an optional skill development paper in the curriculum would be explored.

An employee fired from a Washington State Walmart for allegedly trying to steal a safe returned days later to retrieve it, according to the Pierce County Sheriff’s Department. The man called the store saying he forgot the safe and was coming in to pick it up. Loss prevention opened the safe and found a yellow container with heroin and Xanax. When the employee arrived, customer service asked what was inside, and employees called 911. Deputies arrived as the man began crying and said the safe, container, and narcotics were his and that he paid $350. He was booked into the Pierce County Jail for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

Donna Adelson, 75, convicted for the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, told a judge Monday that she is “an innocent woman” convicted “without evidence.” She said she would have stopped the murder plan if she had known about it, and called Markel “a fine and decent man,” while claiming there was a “total lack of justice” and insufficient evidence of her role in the murder-for-hire plot. Before sentencing, Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Adelson was sentenced to life in prison for the murder and an additional 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation. Prosecutors said the motive was the Adelson family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to South Florida with their children. Her husband Harvey Adelson testified in her support.

The passage describes the structure of the human adrenal central vein, noting it has unique age-related asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles and lacks a circular smooth muscle bundle. It discusses fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) as vascular wall abnormalities with overlapping clinical and morphologic features, and suggests genetic susceptibility for FMD. The authors retrospectively examined adrenalectomy specimens (2018 to Sep 2022) including normal adrenal tissue and neoplasms (adrenal cortical adenomas and pheochromocytomas) and compared adrenal vessel morphology with FMD/SAM. They report that normal adrenal tissues show asymmetrical smooth muscle bundles in adrenal veins, while tumor tissues show less frequent asymmetrical bundles but commonly show SAM features. They also found hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis as common complications and no FMD or FMD-like lesions in arteries outside the adrenal gland, with normal findings in 9 fetal autopsy cases. The authors propose that similar morphologic features across adrenal veins, FMD, and SAM may involve adrenal hormone actions and/or hormone receptor signaling, and conclude this may guide further investigation into FMD in other anatomical sites. The study received no funding and declared no conflicts of interest.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2021. The report states that Microsoft issued a press release that day announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes an Item 9.01 exhibit listing for Exhibit 99.1 and a signature by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage discusses how cloud-based architectures and HPCaaS are changing high-performance computing (HPC). It says cloud architecture and program-based control have broadened possible HPC designs, with public cloud expected to be most important for manufacturing enterprises and hybrid cloud as a way to handle peak loads without outsourcing all data or workloads. IDC recommends choosing between “make or buy” (in-house infrastructure vs buying HPC services), noting that public-cloud HPC can reduce CAPEX through OPEX and that in-house clusters have limits requiring hardware renewal or expansion. It also highlights that on-premises HPC is typically less flexible for changing usage scenarios, which can hinder agility and the development of new data-based products, services, and business models. The passage reports survey results indicating that performance, flexibility, cost optimization, security, and resilience are important, and describes benefits of HPCaaS over in-house infrastructure, including faster access to advanced methods and modern hardware. It concludes that HPC supports digital transformation through simulations, modeling, and data analytics, and recommends actions such as virtual development, a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating the best operating model (on-premises, HPCaaS, or hybrid), considering scalability/security/energy efficiency, and using external expertise. The methodology section states the findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers in industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Two pieces of ammunition were found in the bathroom of Litchfield High School in Illinois at 8:40 a.m. on Wednesday, prompting a lockdown and activation of the school’s safety protocol. The high school and middle school were placed on a “soft lockdown,” and students were being dismissed to their parents around 10:00. Police officers were seen around the school, and classes were to end before noon that day.

The passage argues that the Yankees, like much of baseball, have shifted emphasis away from starting pitching toward the use of relievers and closers. It points to Aroldis Chapman being signed as a closer for the team’s next five years and to the Yankees’ long reliance on bullpen closers, including during the Joe Torre era. It questions whether expensive starting pitchers are “earning their keep” given common managerial decisions to remove starters after pitching only about five innings. The passage cites that major league starters averaged 87 pitches per start in 2015 and notes that “quality starts” decline beyond top pitchers. It also quotes John Smoltz’s view that pitchers should pitch more, while stating that overuse of bullpens contributes to longer game times. The Commissioner is described as considering limits on reliever use to reduce game “dead time,” with input from the Players’ Association required.

The passage describes a new study on the risks of catching germs such as the cold or flu during airplane travel, noting that there has been little prior research. The study’s lead researcher recommends passengers take a window seat and not move during the flight, and the study found that on average only one person on a roughly 150-passenger flight would be infected from a hypothetical infectious aisle-seat passenger. The study involved testing cabin surfaces and air and observing passenger contact patterns across 10 flights, but it observed only one coughing person and found none of 18 cold and flu viruses tested. Researchers concluded how often passengers left their seats and reported that aisle-seat passengers moved more than those in window or middle seats, with the highest risk for the 11 people closest to an infectious person. Outside experts said the small study makes general conclusions difficult. The study was initiated and funded by Boeing, with input in writing, and published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The passage describes the SuperTrend indicator, a trend-following tool created by Oliver Seban that signals trend direction, continuation, or changes. It is shown as a line overlaid on a price chart, reversing direction when the candle close crosses the previous period’s SuperTrend value. The indicator uses median price and the Average True Range (ATR) to build upper and lower bands, with the SuperTrend line taking values from these bands under specific conditions. A backtest on the S&P 500 over 60 years using a weekly timeframe and parameters (ATR period 10, multiplier 3) reports a probability of entering a winning trade of 65.79%, risk-adjusted returns with a max drawdown of 24.6% versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold, and an accuracy around 67%. The passage also outlines formulae and trading rules, notes the indicator is lagging, and discusses use in intraday and ranging markets, adjustment to volatility, and potential enhancements with Bollinger Bands, RSI, and moving averages, alongside stated limitations such as false signals.

A small AI policy nonprofit, Encode, and its general counsel Nathan Calvin publicly accused OpenAI of intimidation tactics related to California’s AI safety law SB 53 while it was still being debated. Calvin said OpenAI used a lawsuit involving Elon Musk as a pretext to intimidate critics, including Encode, and alleged OpenAI had sought Calvin’s private communications about SB 53 through a subpoena served to him at home, along with a subpoena served to Encode. Calvin said Encode is not funded by Musk. The accusation drew responses from inside OpenAI, former employees, and researchers, with some expressing concern about the alleged tactics. Calvin also alleged OpenAI tried to weaken SB 53 requirements through pressure on California to treat companies as compliant based on federal safety agreements or international frameworks. Encode said it would not turn over documents in response to the subpoena, and Calvin described the episode as highly stressful while saying OpenAI still conducts and publishes AI safety research he values.

The passage is a presidential message to Congress describing the state of the Union and recommending measures. It states the country is at peace, government departments were run with public devotion, industrial conflict freedom increased, education and science advanced, public health is at its highest level, and the national election’s calm acceptance shows institutional strength. It also describes widespread hardship relief efforts involving private agencies, local authorities, states, and Reconstruction Finance Corporation loans, aiming to prevent hunger and cold. Public health data is provided with mortality rates for infants and general rates from representative states, showing declining trends.  

The message reports that an unprecedented global economic depression continued, with European collapse contributing to acute crises, and it credits emergency measures for preventing disaster and aiding recovery beginning in July. It presents tables of monthly business indicators and outlines federal unemployment, agricultural, and financial relief expenditures. It argues that continued constructive recovery policies are needed, emphasizing restored confidence, continued budget economy and balancing, banking system reorganization, and international economic cooperation, including efforts through world conferences and disarmament initiatives.  

It recommends further actions including reductions in appropriations, limiting federal public works to commitments and work in progress, continued furlough systems with additional salary reductions, eliminating certain veterans’ service payments deemed beyond original congressional intent, and pursuing revenue changes. The message also reiterates the need for major banking reforms, describes bank failures and their effects, and discusses international cooperation and additional proposed legislation. It concludes with general principles about aligning laws with national purposes, maintaining ordered liberty, limiting government participation in economic and social life except in emergencies, and promoting voluntary cooperative action.

Researchers at Case Western Reserve University reported that the U.S. spends an estimated $55 billion annually addressing effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. A study published in The Journal of Family Violence found that such exposure is associated with higher health-care costs, higher lifetime crime rates, and lower productivity as children age. The research states that by age 64, the average lifetime cost to the national economy for one exposed child is nearly $50,000, including at least $11,042 in increased medical costs, $13,922 from violent crimes, and $25,531 in productivity losses. The study also estimated that Ohio’s young adults face cumulative lifetime costs of nearly $2.18 billion for the portion exposed as children, and that applied to the entire nation the burden is over $55 billion. The authors said the study is the first to attach a price tag to this public health problem and that understanding the costs can help policymakers support preventive and therapeutic interventions.

D.L. Cromwell Investments, Inc. and four individual plaintiffs sought an injunction against NASD Regulation, Inc. to prevent it from compelling testimony under Rule 8210, initiating punishment for invoking the self-incrimination privilege, and allegedly misusing federal grand jury materials. The plaintiffs argued Regulation acted as an agent of federal prosecutors and violated Rule 6(e) grand jury secrecy.  

The court found that plaintiffs did not provide direct evidence of government involvement and declined to infer that DOE/CPAG was acting as a government cat’s paw. The court concluded the Rule 8210 demands were the result of independent action by DOE staff conducting Regulation’s private investigation and that Regulation was not a government instrumentality for this purpose.  

On the grand jury secrecy claim, the court found no credible proof that Rule 6(e)-protected materials were disclosed to or used by unauthorized Regulation personnel. It held plaintiffs failed to show that the materials at issue were grand jury matters protected by Rule 6(e). The court ordered that the injunction was not warranted.

The passage criticizes We Energies for high utility rates and well-paid executives, arguing that as a regulated monopoly it faces little competition and has rates set by the Public Service Commission (PSC) for an allowable return of more than 10%. It claims municipal power companies can be accountable to customers and often provide lower-cost energy. It says Milwaukee distribution area electric rates were low decades ago under CEO Charlie McNeer, but later governance changes led the PSC to approve most utility requests, contributing to the highest electric rates in the Midwest. The passage attributes rate increases over 15 years to the utility seeking rate hikes for overbuilding and high shareholder returns. It argues that citizens and large energy consumers, including the Citizens Utility Board (CUB) and a new group of businesses forming the Initiative for Competitive Energy (ICE), are pushing for changes; ICE and CUB argue that rate rollback may be needed rather than a proposed We Energies rate freeze through 2019.

Canadian Blood Services is opening the largest blood donation clinic in Canada at Eau Claire Market on July 10, with 20 donation beds, replacing an 18-bed clinic on 13th Avenue S.W. Susan Matsumoto said the average clinic has about eight beds and that the added capacity is hoped to help address Canada’s blood shortage. Canadian Blood Services aims for 150,000 donations by July 1 for Canada’s 150th birthday, but Matsumoto said they are not on track and need 50,000 more donations by the end of June; the O negative blood supply is very low, with less than three days of supply. Matsumoto urged Canadians to book appointments to donate, noting Calgary donors have been responding to needs. The current clinic is expected to close July 7, and Canadian Blood Services is also building a new operations facility in Calgary off Barlow Trail set to open in 2020, housing administrative staff, blood production, and donor testing.

F2 Logistics, the reigning titlist, will play Generika-Ayala at 7 p.m. in the resumption of the 2018 Chooks to Go-Philippine Superliga Grand Prix at The Arena in San Juan City, aiming to extend its winning streak to four and claim the No. 2 seed. Generika-Ayala, having broken its losing streak against Smart over the weekend, will try to build on that momentum despite F2 Logistics coach Arnold Laniog urging his team to focus on “one game at a time.” Earlier at 4:15 p.m., Sta. Lucia faces winless Smart, with Sta. Lucia seeking to rebound from a four-set loss to F2 Logistics and improve its position in the standings. Other teams are still competing for spots from Nos. 3 to 7, making the matches crucial.

The passage describes licensing requirements and disclaimers related to adopting SD Specifications versions 1.0 or 1.01, including requirements to obtain appropriate licenses from SD-3C, LLC for specific implementations (e.g., host devices and SD cards with memory). The passage describes reactions to Prince’s music becoming available on Spotify after his death. It notes that Prince had been opposed to his work on the platform, and some fans view the release as a betrayal. It also lists other artists refusing or criticizing Spotify, including Taylor Swift (pulling her 2014 album and arguing music has value), Garth Brooks (not available on Spotify or iTunes, planning his next album on his own website), Thom Yorke (criticizing Spotify while noting Radiohead’s music is on it), Beyoncé (citing Tidal as the reason her album “Lemonade” is not on Spotify), and Joanna Newsom (calling Spotify a villainous cabal).

Market Research Future published a report on the global Blowout Preventer market, forecasting growth through 2021. The market is driven by increased oil and gas exploration, especially unconventional sources and offshore activities, along with rising safety standards. The report outlines objectives including segment and sub-segment forecasts for five years, factors affecting growth, analyses such as price and supply chain and Porters five forces, historical and forecast revenues across six regions, country-level analysis by market segment and region, and strategic profiling of key players and competitive developments. Lake Lugano, about 40 kilometers west of Lake Como, is described as a quieter, lesser-known Swiss destination in Ticino, an Italian-speaking canton. Positioned on a glacial lake with a mild, sunny climate, it offers art, hiking, local cuisine, scenic villages, parks, and views from mountains such as Monte San Salvatore and Monte Generoso. Experts say Lugano is less crowded than nearby Lake Como and is suited to couples, families, and older travelers, with activities including local ferries, funicular rides, village walks, wine tastings, and specific restaurants and hotels. They emphasize slowing down and enjoying small moments like lakeside coffee, hill walks, and chats with locals.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau made an early statement after a deadly Toronto van attack, saying there is no apparent link to terrorism and that all Canadians are with Toronto. He extended condolences to victims and praised first responders for their professionalism and courage. Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale said the attack has led to a large homicide investigation led by city police with all levels of government involved, and he also saw no reason to draw links to a national security risk or organized attack. The attack allegedly began Monday afternoon when a man drove a van along a busy sidewalk on Yonge Street, and Toronto police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian, who was scheduled to appear in court later that day.

European stock markets rose slightly at the start of trading on Tuesday. London’s FTSE 100 gained 0.2% to 7,467.24 points, while Paris’s CAC 40 and Frankfurt’s DAX 30 each added 0.1%. The energy sector rose as Brent crude hit a more than two-year high after the Forties pipeline in the North Sea was shut down for a few weeks due to a leak. The passage also notes upcoming central bank interest rate decisions in the US, Britain, and the eurozone.

The majority dismisses the exceptions and confirms the account absolutely, holding that the word “grandchildren” in the will clearly means all grandchildren and is not ambiguous. It reasons that heirs cannot be disinherited except by express words or necessary implication, and that the per stirpes provision in the gift to grandchildren sets the shares without indicating discrimination among ancestors. The dissent argues that the court should seek the testator’s intent and that at the will’s execution he intended only the grandchildren who were issue of his four named children. The dissent contends that afterborn children caused a pro tanto revocation by law, leading to an intestacy for those afterborn children, and that the majority’s reading improperly gives afterborn-line grandchildren shares meant for issue of the named children, resulting in an unjust distribution.

The passage lists several finance and business headlines, including EU climate reform for development banks, Dunas Capital’s approach to asset management, and other global updates. It describes Dunas Capital as a Spanish asset management firm founded in 2016 with about €4.5 billion in assets under management as of July 2025, offering traditional and alternative investment strategies for capital preservation, risk management, and value-driven investing. The firm’s investment philosophy focuses on limiting market risk via portfolio volatility (“risk budget”), using a multi-asset approach and active risk/return management, including options and futures to mitigate tail risk. Dunas Capital manages four mutual funds under the same team and non-indexed conviction-driven process, differing by return target and risk profile, with volatility targets ranging from 3% to 15% across its funds. It also mentions alternative investments in areas such as infrastructure, renewable energies, transportation assets, and agriculture.

The passage contains the legal specification agreement and an overview of AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) standardization document. It states that the GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted memory area for guest-hypervisor communication, supports Automatic Exits (AE) and Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), and standardizes GHCB memory layout and required protocol behaviors for interoperability across hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. It also describes GHCB mapping and alignment requirements, the need for hypervisors to not intercept access to a specific GHCB MSR, hypervisor feature advertisement and versioning, and negotiation/CPUID information exchange. The document further outlines changes across GHCB version 2 revisions (including initial SEV-SNP support), mechanisms for guest-triggered VMGEXIT processing via #VC for NAE events, and structures and protocols related to secrets pages and an EFI configuration table for the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob.

The passage states that the tax department will likely use the net asset value (NAV) method to calculate the fair market value (FMV) of unlisted shares for capital gains tax. It says the budget proposal is to compute capital gains based on the higher of the selling price or FMV and to specify the FMV calculation method. Some tax experts believe the main goal of the provision is to address sales at undervalued prices by using NAV rather than the discounted cash flow (DCF) method, which they say is subjective and could lead to litigation. It also quotes the budget announcement that if the consideration is less than the prescribed FMV, the prescribed FMV will be deemed the full value of consideration for computing capital gains. The passage notes this was seen as a major dampener for unlisted companies, particularly start-ups, where stake sales are common.

The passage describes the Dogs of the Dow (DOD) strategy as a stock-picking approach that selects the 10 highest dividend-yielding Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) component stocks and rebalances the portfolio at the beginning of each calendar year. It notes that the strategy became popular in 1991 through Michael B. O’Higgins’ book “Beating the Dow,” while earlier related ideas appeared in 1951 and the early 1980s. The passage reports backtest results showing the DOD strategy underperformed the S&P 500 over the last couple of decades, and that several related ETFs tracking the strategy also underperformed the broader market. It also mentions options for investing via individual stocks, ETFs, or a mutual fund.

Ibrahim Shehu Shema, former Katsina State governor, was remanded in EFCC custody by Justice Babagana Ashigar at a Federal High Court in Katsina over alleged money laundering of N5.7bn SURE-P Funds. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 counts. The court ordered him detained until 27 April 2018 to hear his written bail application; his oral bail application was overruled. EFCC counsel Sam Ologunorisa objected to bail, arguing the offence carries at least 7 years’ imprisonment without option of fines.

FULE (CMD38) logically erases the entire user area and is similar to default ERASE. The full user area is identified using ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32) with argument 0 and ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33) with the argument equal to the end of the user area; the host command sequence is CMD32, CMD33, then FULE with CMD38 and its arguments set to 00000002h. Hosts supporting FULE must check the FULE_SUPPORT bit (b312) in the SD_STATUS register; if unsupported, the host must not issue FULE and the card shall execute ERASE. If CMD38 or CMD32/33 address setting is received out of sequence, the card sets ERASE_SEQ_ERROR and resets the sequence; for other out-of-sequence commands (except SEND_STATUS), it sets ERASE_RESET, resets the FULE sequence, and executes the last command. If the host does not provide the full user area via CMD32 and CMD33, the card executes ERASE with busy timeout as specified. FULE is supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards and not through the SPI interface; during FULE, the card holds DAT0 low to indicate progress.

The June 26, 2001 emails and included news articles describe California’s electricity crisis refund negotiations and related policy issues. State officials and energy regulators held federally ordered, confidential settlement talks in Washington, D.C., seeking repayment of about $8.9 billion (and other issues such as creditworthiness, long-term contract needs, and generator payment), while power generators disputed the figures and said they are owed money by California utilities. At the same time, two new Federal Energy Regulatory Commission commissioners met with Gov. Gray Davis in Sacramento, and Davis discussed natural gas, possible refunds, and allegations involving Duke Energy operations during Stage 3 alerts. Separate coverage discusses state debate over utility direct-access choices and outlines solar housing developments in California, including how photovoltaic systems and subsidies can affect energy costs and building interest.

The passage describes the “COVIDFast” assay, including SwabFAST (anterior nares/oropharyngeal swab) and SalivaFAST (saliva), for rapid, high-throughput, RNA extraction-free qPCR detection of SARS-CoV-2. It addresses limitations of conventional PCR methods that require nucleic acid extraction, which is laborious and expensive and can be affected by contamination risk and extraction supply shortages. COVIDFast uses proprietary buffers, an extraction-free RT-qPCR approach based on proteinase K digestion, and sample collection kits designed to enable automated processing. The paper reports analytical validation results showing equivalence to RT-qPCR with RNA extraction, a limit of detection of 4 copies/µL (over 95% positive replicates), and clinical validation with high percent agreement versus both standard extraction-based RT-qPCR and SalivaDirect. Real-world testing experience includes 409,883 tests by December 23, 2021, with differing proportions of SwabFAST and SalivaFAST use.

In February, the S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index showed a 6.3% annual gain, up from 6.1% in January. The 10-City Composite rose 6.5% year-over-year (up from 6.0%), and the 20-City Composite rose 6.8% (up from 6.4%). Seattle, Las Vegas, and San Francisco had the highest year-over-year gains among the 20 cities, with February increases of 12.7%, 11.6%, and 10.1% respectively. Month-over-month, the National Index increased 0.4% before seasonal adjustment (0.5% after), while both the 10- and 20-City Composites rose 0.7% before seasonal adjustment (0.8% after). The analysis cited continuous national price increases for 70 months through February 2018 and noted employment-related differences across cities, including larger-than-expected price gains in San Francisco and Los Angeles and smaller increases in Miami.

The passage contains Coach Qinneville’s remarks about the team’s approach to upcoming and past playoff games. He says the team is focusing on proper preparation, staying excited without getting ahead of themselves, and concentrating on each shift against their opponent. He describes the process as challenging but valuable, highlights the team’s resilience and depth, and credits top players for consistent production and raising teammates’ performance. He also emphasizes keeping the same mindset and practice routines, maintaining accountability as a group, and preparing for different series and situations. He notes that the team must improve aspects such as quickness and pace, and discusses handling players missing games without health-related issues as part of relying on organizational depth.

In an action on an accident insurance policy, the court held that letters from the insurer and its agents were admissible to show waiver of proof of death and cause within the policy’s 60-day period, but that the insurer’s denial of liability excused the beneficiary from making such proof. The court also found that after a formal denial of the death benefits, the insurer was not estopped from invoking the policy’s time limit for bringing suit for death benefits, and that encouraging the claimant to seek proofs did not waive the time limitation or estop the insurer. However, the insurer had waived requirements and recognized the beneficiary’s right to weekly indemnity for disability if disability was caused by an accident, so the weekly indemnity claim was treated differently. The judgment for the beneficiary on the death benefit was reversed because the suit was not brought within the contract time limit, and a new trial was ordered limited to the weekly disability indemnity claim.

Austria’s Financial Market Authority (FMA) increased its forecast for earnings from the sale of assets in the wind-down of “bad bank” Heta Asset Resolution to 8.6 billion euros, raising the estimate by 2.6 billion euros from a previous 6.0 billion euros. The FMA attributed the revision to better-than-expected proceeds so far from Heta’s asset sales and said it confirmed Heta’s recent optimistic comments. The update is seen as beneficial to the Austrian state and Carinthia, which had received loans to buy back Heta bonds after Carinthia said it could not honor 11 billion euros in guarantees. The FMA also said an initial payment of around 4 billion euros to Heta creditors should soon be made, and that roughly half of what is on the account could be paid out over the summer.

The preliminary inquiry into the murder of Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser continued before Principal Magistrate Judy Latchman, with three police ranks called to testify. Imran Khan called Christopher Khan, Steven Andrews, and Phillip Suffrien are charged with killing the elderly women between October 2 and 3, 2017 during a robbery. Witnesses included Detective Lance Corporal Desmond Johnny, Inspector Mohan Khan, Constable LeAndre Gillis, and former Police Corporal Derwin Eastman, who is on remand facing a murder charge. After testimony, the witnesses were questioned by Khan and Andrews, who are unrepresented, while Attorney-at-Law Saphier Hussein represented Suffrien. The PI is set to continue on Monday, following reports that the women’s bound and gagged bodies were found in their South Road home by members of the South Road Full Gospel Assembly after they failed to attend a church service; Caesar was the caretaker and had the alarm code and nearby school keys.

The passage describes SD Physical Layer behaviors and command-related timing, including tuning of sampling points using CMD19 and a data tuning block, and CMD19 execution constraints (40 times within 150 ms, with rules on transfer state and illegal command handling). It outlines data transfer modes and how reads/writes can be aborted with CMD12, buffering behavior for block writes, restrictions during programming (no parameter set or read commands), and erase-related command sequences (CMD32, CMD33, CMD38) including DISCARD (CMD38 with specific arguments) and FULE (CMD38 with specific arguments), their support limits, busy indications, and error handling. It also covers SD lock/unlock mechanisms via CMD42, including password protection (PWD/PWD_LEN), optional Force Erase Password (FEP/FEP_LEN) and Card Ownership Protection (COP), state behavior across compatible/COP modes, required command sequences (CMD7 selection, CMD16 block length rules), and error conditions. Additional sections describe CMD55 APP_CMD behavior, general command CMD56 as a placeholder/blank, and CMD6 switch-function command handling (function groups, mode 0/1 operations, busy status, status data structure, and power/current limit considerations). It concludes with CRC usage for commands and data blocks, illegal command behavior, and read/write timeout condition guidelines.

The passage describes a hybrid deep-learning framework, DNN–Transformer–Autoencoder (DNN-Transformer-AE), for corporate tax risk supervision and risk-level assessment. It addresses limitations of traditional rule-based monitoring by modeling multimodal enterprise data: static features via a DNN, temporal financial data via a Transformer with self-attention, and anomaly signals via an autoencoder for feature reconstruction. Outputs from these components are fused and mapped to a risk score, which is categorized into high-, medium-, or low-risk classes. Experiments use a real dataset of about 12,000 enterprises from corporate tax declarations and financial records, with 70%/15%/15% temporal splits and labels assigned by domain experts. The proposed model outperforms baselines, achieving 0.91 accuracy and 0.88 macro-averaged F1 on the test set, with training/validation loss curves indicating stable convergence and generalization. The study concludes that the hybrid approach improves identification of high-risk firms and provides a tool for more reliable risk grading, while noting limitations including missing macroeconomic and inter-firm relationship data and potential computational complexity.

The passage discusses how quantum materials exhibit emergent phenomena from interactions between particles and quasiparticles, focusing on orbital degrees of freedom (ODF) in electrons and magnons and the related effects in electronic, magnetic, and phononic systems. It highlights that ODF definitions vary across quasiparticles and that, particularly in hybrid magnon–phonon systems, conventional orbital/pseudo-orbital notions are not well understood. The letter addresses this gap by studying orbital angular momentum (OAM) in magnon–polaron systems and showing that, in bosonic quasiparticles, ODF originates from two mechanisms: global rotation and the quantum geometry of magnon-polaron wavefunctions. In a model two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order, magnetoelastic coupling breaks required symmetries and enables conversion of orbital degrees of freedom between magnons and phonons, producing finite intra-band and inter-band OAM contributions even when lattice orbital terms vanish. It also proposes that this orbital activity can be probed experimentally through electric polarization and a transverse voltage generated when temperature or strain gradients excite magnon-polarons, decomposed into contributions from spin Berry curvature and orbital moment. The passage concludes that magnon–phonon coupling enhances the electrical activity of orbital degrees of freedom and enables experimental detection of OAM, with results described as universal and extendable to other phonon modes and orbital phenomena.

The IMF advised Saudi Arabia not to rush reforms and price hikes while overhauling its economy to cope with low crude prices. Although it praised the reform programme aimed at boosting non-oil revenues and curbing government spending, it recommended pacing implementation to avoid harming growth, warning that rapid fiscal consolidation could lead to large fuel and power price increases. The report cited budget deficits totalling $200 billion over the past three years and forecasts a $53-billion shortfall this year, with the IMF expecting the deficit to be nine percent of GDP. Saudi Arabia’s economy has contracted due to lower crude prices and production, and the IMF expects growth of 0.1 percent this year while other forecasts differ. Saudi reforms include austerity measures such as higher excise taxes, increased energy and water prices, and higher expatriate labour fees, with further price hikes expected in 2017 and an IMF-estimated $67.7 billion revenue gain from fuel and electricity price increases by 2020. Saudi Arabia also plans a five-percent VAT next year, which the IMF said could be challenging, though Callen said progress had been substantial enough to allow implementation.

Janet Yellen, outgoing chair of the Federal Reserve, said in a PBS interview that she did not believe recent Wall Street gains qualified as a “bubble,” but warned that asset valuations are elevated and advised investors to diversify and remain cautious. She also said the US economy is looking strong, citing job growth, rising wages, and an unemployment rate of 4.1 percent. Asked about not being renewed for a second term, Yellen said she was “disappointed.” She leaves her post on Saturday and will be replaced by Jerome Powell on Monday.

The passage explains the value area trading strategy, which uses the volume profile (market profile) to identify the price range where most trading activity occurred during a given time period. It defines the value area as the range of prices containing 70% of total trading volume, used to pinpoint potential support and resistance levels and areas for buying and selling. The text notes the strategy is commonly used in futures but can also apply to stocks and forex, and it describes ways to generate signals using breakouts, reversals, and pullbacks around value area highs and lows, supported by price action patterns and momentum oscillator divergences. It also covers potential benefits and risks, including false signals, changing value areas, and the need to consider other factors and use risk management such as stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, and discipline. The passage also states the strategy is not as easy to backtest as it sounds and includes questions it plans to answer about value area trading.

Defects such as vacancies govern microstructural evolution and properties in multicomponent alloys, and diffusion depends on equilibrium vacancy concentration. Predicting equilibrium vacancy compositions is important but difficult because multicomponent alloys have complex defect energy landscapes influenced by short-range order, and correlations in alloys with three or more elements are not well established. The study investigates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy (from periodic table groups 4, 5, and 6) using first-principles calculations to parameterize an embedded cluster expansion (eCE) model and a canonical coarse-graining method, with equilibrium vacancy concentrations computed via Monte Carlo simulations. Results show that adding group 4 elements significantly increases vacancy concentrations (by about 10–100 compared to alloys without group 4 elements) and that equilibrium vacancy concentrations depend strongly on short-range order and bonding energies. The formalism is validated by comparing predicted vacancy concentrations with semi-grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and by testing agreement of the eCE model with DFT formation energies and solute-vacancy binding trends. The study also discusses limitations of the dilute-vacancy approximation and effects of possible phase transformations, and notes that vibrational contributions and vacancy cluster effects are not included.

Astronomers plan extensive observations of a total solar eclipse next Monday across the U.S., from Oregon to South Carolina, using ground telescopes, an International Space Station, 11 satellites, three planes, and more than 70 high-altitude balloons. Funded by about $7.7 million from NASA and the National Science Foundation, the effort aims to study the sun and also its effects on Earth’s weather, space weather, and animals and plants during totality. The passage also describes public participation, including the “Citizen CATE” project training volunteers to capture images for a movie of the sun’s edge, plus guidance through apps like iNaturalist and contributions such as wildlife tracking and the “Eclipse Megamovie 2017.” It notes that eclipses help scientists study the sun’s corona, outer atmosphere, and related plasma loops and temperature questions, and highlights historical eclipse contributions such as helium’s discovery in 1868 and the 1919 eclipse confirmation of general relativity.

The passage lists several education-related headlines and links, including that the superintendent of Iowa’s largest school district was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, along with other stories about schools, education policy, student experiences, and related news.

The court held that there is no difference in construction rules between a conveyance by extent and one by deed, and that an extent executed on the debtor’s land conveys to the creditor the debtor’s buildings standing on the land, even if their foundations are not sunk below the surface. Parol evidence was not admissible to show that buildings were excluded from the appraisement or reserved for removal when the execution returns and sheriff’s returns stated no such exception. The defendants’ evidence was therefore properly rejected, the plaintiff’s verdict was upheld, and judgment was to be entered on that verdict.

A study analyzing long-term Danish birth data found that children born to mothers diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis before pregnancy had higher risks of developing rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease, and epilepsy. The research included over 2,100 such children and 1.3 million children born to women without the disease, with results indicating nearly threefold higher likelihood for rheumatoid arthritis, 2.2 times greater risk for thyroid disease, and 1.6 higher risk for epilepsy. The findings were published online Dec. 11 in Arthritis Care & Research, and the researchers said they should increase doctor awareness and prompt special attention to child development for these conditions.

The passage is largely excerpted from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2020, including sections on the cover page, consolidated financial statements (income statements, comprehensive income, balance sheets, cash flows, and stockholders’ equity), and notes. It provides unaudited results for the three and nine months ended March 31, 2020 and 2019, including revenue, costs, net income, earnings per share, comprehensive income, cash flow items, and equity changes. The notes describe accounting policies, earnings per share, other income (expense), investments and fair value measurements, derivatives and hedging, inventories, goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, stock repurchase programs, dividends, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment and geographic information. The passage also includes an independent registered public accounting firm’s review report and a management discussion covering forward-looking statements, company overview, financial conditions, COVID-19 impacts, and seasonality.

A University of Maryland study suggests that consuming energy drinks may be linked to later use of cocaine or prescription stimulants for non-medical purposes. Researchers followed 1,099 participants from ages 18 to 21–24 and found that over half had a persistent pattern of energy drink consumption, and they were significantly more likely to use stimulant drugs. The increased risk also applied to those who consumed energy drinks occasionally, while participants who did not consume energy drinks as they got older were less likely to develop substance-abuse issues. The study does not explain the link, and researchers say it should be investigated further.

The passage describes video coding/decoding technology, including incorporation by reference of multiple prior patent applications and a general focus on video coding. It explains inter-picture prediction with motion compensation and intra coding, particularly intra prediction methods that use directional modes with neighboring reference samples at signaled angles, as well as non-directional smooth modes, recursive-filtering modes, chroma-from-luma (CfL), and multi-line intra prediction. It also discusses non-separable transforms used for intra coding, including primary and secondary (e.g., low-frequency) non-separable transforms and reduced secondary transforms, with restrictions on when the secondary transform is applied. The summary section then outlines apparatus and methods in which coding information for a block can include intra directional information with a nominal mode and angular offset, and can indicate a transform set mode and non-separable transform index to select and apply a non-separable (secondary) transform for reconstructing the block. The remainder includes descriptions of encoder/decoder communication system architectures, streaming scenarios, and additional details about intra prediction modes and transform coding processes.

The passage describes the annual Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards, which recognise accountants’ work in private and public sector organisations. It outlines the event programme, including a champagne reception, welcome, a 3-course dinner with wine and coffee, an awards ceremony, and carriages. Awards are presented by TV presenter Sarah Heaney, with entertainment by DNA, a mind-reading act. It lists categories such as large and small accountancy firm of the year, finance director and emerging finance director of the year, young accountant of the year, and several team awards. It explains how to attend via ticket purchases for 2018, provides ticket prices, and states what is included in the ticket price.

The study examines the characteristics and employment patterns of Hungarian higher education lecturers, focusing on how changes in Hungarian higher education and related regulations have affected academic staff employment, student participation, and lecturer earnings. It reviews post-1990 higher education development, including policy shifts that increased non-state institutions, changed admission and tuition funding policies, and later tightened and then relaxed admissions requirements. The paper reports trends in student and lecturer numbers, noting that after 2005 lecturer numbers did not follow student population changes, and it provides data on student-teacher ratios, lecturer age and gender composition, and the structure of academic staff categories. It also describes employment rules for lecturers based on Hungarian legislation (1993, 2000/2003 amendments, 2005, and the 2011 act and related changes), including qualification requirements, appointment procedures, working hours, and governance changes that reduced institutional autonomy and altered employment conditions for some state universities. The paper analyzes earnings, reporting that monthly and lifetime earnings for doctoral graduates entering academic teaching and research are lower than those in the business sector, and it compares salary ratios internationally. It further examines doctoral student numbers internationally using UNESCO data and finds Hungary ranks poorly in both total share and per-capita measures. The summary concludes that policy and funding changes have shaped the “force field” for lecturer work and that Hungary does not perform well in international comparisons of doctoral student numbers.

The passage describes a speaker’s memories and feelings about their first team, the Detroit Red Wings, including playing in the semi-finals for two consecutive years and enjoying Detroit as a city. After being traded to Washington, the trade did not work out and the team was described as having gotten it going too late, leading to summer changes. The speaker says they have always believed in the current team’s players and is excited to be here, noting they have played well on the road. They also mention being shocked by the trade and finding it difficult at the time, while later being able to move on.

Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov said Azerbaijan aims to increase exports of honey and beekeeping products. He noted that global honey production is about 1.5 million tonnes and is expected to face rising demand in 2020–2022 for 2–2.5 million tonnes. Asadov said Azerbaijani honey is organic, with last year’s sales totaling 6 tonnes at 8–8.5 thousand USD per tonne, and that organic honey accounts for 15–20% of world demand, with interest from countries such as China and Japan. He added that the ministry has developed programs and plans to submit proposals to the Azerbaijani President and the government to increase state support for beekeeping, following discussions with the Association of Beekeepers.

Marc Ó Sé said that an injury-free James O’Donoghue could be a huge boost for Kerry this summer. Ó Sé noted that O’Donoghue returned to the Kingdom jersey with nine points in Kerry’s win over Clare and expects him to improve with each game if he stays injury-free. He said the last performance gave O’Donoghue confidence, adding that Kerry would have another strong option beyond Paul Geaney. Ó Sé also stated that because O’Donoghue had a non-existent league campaign, the key is getting more games, and that could be “huge” for Kerry.

Legal experts and public education advocates criticized a Texas Education Agency investigation into hundreds of teachers’ social media posts about conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s killing, saying it violates teachers’ free speech rights. Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath said the comments were “reprehensible and inappropriate” and sent a letter to superintendents to refer such posts for investigation, recommending license suspension. The experts described the actions as a “witch hunt” and said public employees retain First Amendment rights when speaking in a personal capacity, arguing the state would need to show a significant workplace disruption to discipline teachers for such speech. The passage also outlines processes for district and state disciplinary actions, including possible license revocation, and notes differing views among teachers statewide.

The passage discusses bond trading strategies, including what bonds are, how strategies work, and how they differ by time horizon, risk tolerance, and market conditions. It explains that bonds carry risks, especially interest rate risk, where rising rates lower bond prices. It notes common mistakes such as poor understanding of market dynamics, overreliance on historical data, chasing yield without assessing credit/liquidity risk, misjudging interest rate moves, lack of diversification, and emotional bias. It argues bond strategies can be complementary with stocks due to low correlation, presenting backtested examples involving Treasury bond ETF TLT (including seasonal and monthly strategies) and showing improved combined results with an S&P 500 strategy bundle. The passage also covers how interest rates affect strategies, mentions day trading and automation of bond trading via algorithmic systems, and suggests a beginner approach of dollar-cost averaging.

Enron is reported to be in advanced discussions to sell its Portland General Electric utility unit to Northwest Natural Gas for about $1.8 billion in cash and stock, in a highly leveraged transaction that would eventually give Enron a minority stake in Northwest. The deal is described as delicate, with key points needing finalization, potential financing difficulties, and board approval not certain; Enron and Northwest Natural declined to comment. The transaction would also involve Northwest Natural assuming roughly $1 billion in debt and would occur after Enron’s earlier Portland sale agreement to Sierra Pacific Resources collapsed amid the California energy crisis. Separate reports also note Northwest Natural increased its quarterly common dividend and that Enron planned job cuts in Europe.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 1, 2020. The report states that Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer, announced his retirement; he would step down as Chief Accounting Officer on July 31, 2020 and remain with the company through September 30, 2020 to assist in the transition. It also states that Alice L. Jolla, age 54, will become Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31, 2020, having served as Corporate Controller since 2014 and in other roles at Microsoft and previously at FASB, Dow Chemical, and Union Carbide. Upon appointment, Ms. Jolla will receive a $1.5 million stock award under the Microsoft Corporation 2017 Stock Plan, vesting quarterly at 6.25% each quarter, subject to continuous employment.

Bitcoin fell below US$8,000 for the first time since November, then recovered much of the losses, as 2018 brought ongoing concerns for cryptocurrencies. After reaching US$19,511 on December 18, bitcoin wiped out more than half its value amid negative developments including regulatory threats from India, South Korea, China, and the US, the US$500 million Coincheck heist, fears of price manipulation, and Facebook’s ban on ads for bitcoin, cryptocurrencies, and ICOs. Japanese authorities raided Coincheck’s offices to gather evidence and assess user security. Bitcoin dropped as much as 16% to US$7,643 and was down 21% for the week, while Ripple, Ether, and Litecoin fell at least 18%. Nouriel Roubini said bitcoin’s bubble is bursting and that many G20 countries are discussing crackdowns.
