The Asus Zenfone 5Z was launched in India in Delhi, announced earlier at MWC 2018. It features a notch display with a 90% screen-to-body ratio and comes with Android Oreo, dual rear cameras, Face Unlock, and AI charging. It is offered in Meteor Silver and Midnight Blue, with three variants priced at Rs. 29,999 (6GB/64GB), Rs. 32,999 (6GB/128GB), and Rs. 36,999 (8GB/256GB). The phone is exclusive to Flipkart and goes on sale July 15. Specifications include a 6.2-inch FHD+ Super IPS display, Snapdragon 845 SoC, hybrid dual SIM support up to 2TB, dual rear cameras (12MP+8MP), and an 8MP front camera, along with features such as a rear fingerprint sensor, 3.5mm audio jack, FM radio, DTS headphone, dual speakers, dual 4G VoLTE, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5, GPS, and a 3300mAh battery with Asus BoostMaster/AI charging. Launch offers include a Rs. 3,000 discount with ICICI cards, Flipkart Complete Mobile Protection for Rs. 499, no-cost EMI from Rs. 3,333, and for Jio users Rs. 2,200 cashback plus 100GB additional data.

Richard L. Helzer was convicted in Alpena Circuit Court of two counts of committing acts of gross indecency and of being a sexually delinquent person at the time of the offenses. The trial court allowed only five peremptory challenges to select the initial jury on the gross indecency charges and later refused Helzer’s request for 20 peremptory challenges related to the sexually delinquent-person charge, which carries a possible life sentence. The Court of Appeals reversed and remanded for a new trial, holding Helzer was entitled to 20 peremptory challenges.

The Supreme Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing matter, not merely a penalty enhancement tied to proof of the principal charge, and that its hearing requires a separate jury when the defendant does not waive a jury trial. It concluded the decision to empanel a separate jury must not be left to the trial judge’s discretion; a second jury must be provided in every such case and should be empaneled immediately after conviction on the principal charge. The Court further held Helzer is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges for the second jury, while at the time the first jury is empaneled he should be allowed only the number appropriate to the principal charge. It also held the sexual delinquency charge must be brought before trial begins and that no reference to it should be made to the jury deciding the principal charge. The Court affirmed the principal gross indecency proceeding as having no error, but reversed the Court of Appeals’ order for a new trial and remanded for a separate hearing before a separately empaneled jury if the prosecutor pursues the sexual delinquency charge; otherwise, sentencing would be only on the principal charge. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, arguing the sexual delinquency statute is unconstitutional as void for vagueness.

On March 27, 2017, Tesla, Inc. was notified by the underwriters that they exercised in full their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million aggregate principal amount of Tesla’s 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022. The option notes were sold under a Registration Statement on Form S-3 and related prospectus, and issued on March 30, 2017 pursuant to a supplemental indenture. A legal opinion regarding the option notes is filed as Exhibit 5.1. Tesla also entered into additional note hedge transactions and additional warrant confirmations with hedge counterparties in connection with the option notes; the company paid approximately $26.6 million for the hedge transactions and received approximately $6.9 million in proceeds from the sale of the additional warrants.

The American Cancer Society updated its colorectal cancer screening guideline to begin at age 45 for people at average risk, citing increasing CRC rates in young and middle-aged adults and modeling that shows a favorable benefit-to-burden balance for starting at 45 versus 50. The update is published in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians and recommends regular screening for adults ages 45+ using either a high-sensitivity stool-based test or a structural (visual) exam, based on patient preference and test availability. Starting screening at ages 45–49 is a “qualified recommendation,” while screening at age 50 and older is a “strong recommendation.” Positive non-colonoscopy screening tests should be followed by timely colonoscopy. Screening should continue through age 75 for average-risk adults in good health with life expectancy over 10 years; decisions for ages 76–85 should be individualized, and screening should be discouraged after age 85. Approved screening options include FIT annually, HSgFOBT annually, mt-sDNA every 3 years, colonoscopy every 10 years, CT colonography every 5 years, and flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years, with no test prioritized. The guideline development committee emphasized endorsing all test options to improve screening uptake and includes new materials to support clinician-patient discussions.

GPU performance is increasingly limited by memory bandwidth and size, prompting NVIDIA to work with the DRAM industry to develop GPUs using HBM2 and GDDR5X, and introducing Turing as the first architecture to use GDDR6. Turing redesigns the GDDR6 memory interface for speed, power efficiency, and noise reduction, adds clock gating, and pairs the memory subsystem with end-to-end optimizations such as reduced signal crosstalk and expanded L2 cache (TU102: 6 MB). Turing also uses lossless memory compression to reduce bandwidth demands and improve effective bandwidth (reported as 50% higher on Turing vs Pascal in the TU102/RTX 2080 Ti example). 

The passage further describes a Turing display engine supporting higher resolutions, faster refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K at 60 Hz, and DSC 1.2, along with enhanced NVENC/NVDEC support for HEVC and 8K. It explains VirtualLink/USB Type-C support for VR headsets, NVLink-based SLI data transfers for TU102/TU104 with stated bandwidth, and introduces real-time ray tracing enabled by RT Cores and a hybrid rendering model combining ray tracing and rasterization. It outlines related ray tracing concepts (BVH traversal, denoising) and discusses additional Turing features for rendering and performance, including NGX AI technologies (e.g., DLSS, inpainting, slow-mo, super-resolution) and rendering techniques such as Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering.

The University of Manchester’s Students’ Union launched Earth Week with a panel featuring Asad Rehman of Friends of the Earth and Martin Empson of Campaign Against Climate Change. Rehman discussed how climate change affects developing countries, including estimates of deaths and displacement, and argued that richer countries are responsible for a disproportionate share of carbon emissions. He compared climate change to the Titanic and said people affected deserve legal protection rather than being labeled “economic migrants,” calling for rebuilding justice and supporting efforts like Friends of the Earth and Campaign Against Climate Change. Empson said people can help by getting involved—through protests, petitions, contacting local MPs, or donating—and emphasized coordinating environmental and migration movements to create a positive agenda.

Higher wind supply and easing demand on Tuesday reduced prompt power prices in Europe’s wholesale market, while forward contracts tracked lower coal prices. Traders described the outlook as bearish due to improved French nuclear supply and demand declines next week. Germany’s Wednesday baseload contract fell 16% to 28.75 euros/MWh, and the French same-day price dropped 20% to 27.75 euros. Demand was forecast to ease day-on-day to 61.2 GW in Germany and 47.1 GW in France, with wind output in Germany rising to 15.8 GW on Wednesday. On the forward curve, Germany’s Cal’19 contract fell 0.4% to 37.7 euros and France’s 2019 contract fell 0.4% to 42.75 euros. European carbon emissions rights for December 2018 held at 12.91 euros/t, while Cif Europe coal for 2019 fell to $82.75/t. Gas and oil prices rose, and Czech contracts also fell. Innogy reported unresolved questions at its annual general meeting about a planned asset swap between RWE and E.ON.

American Girl is releasing its first male 18-inch doll, Logan Everett, part of a new series of contemporary characters. Logan plays drums for Tenney Grant, a girl pursuing a music career in Nashville, and is available for sale starting Thursday. American Girl spokesperson Julie Parks said male characters have been a long-time request, based on research showing demand for more contemporary characters and stories with more diversity and interests. Thursday also brings back classic doll Felicity Merriman. Later in 2017, American Girl will release two new dolls: Z Yang, a contemporary filmmaker, in spring, and Nanea, a historical doll living in Hawaii during World War II, in fall. Each 18-inch figure costs $115, or about $140 including accessories and the book.

The country’s Privacy Commissioner is launching a formal investigation into a 2016 Uber breach that exposed personal information of tens of millions of users. Similar investigations are underway in the U.S., U.K., and Australia and multiple U.S. states, and a class-action lawsuit has been filed in Alberta. Uber said last month that more than 57 million riders and drivers had information stolen in 2016, but it said it has no evidence the data was misused; it did not disclose how many Canadian users were affected. The U.K. government said 2.7 million users were affected. The breach was kept secret for over a year by Uber’s former chief security officer Joe Sullivan until last month, when Uber revealed it paid thieves $100,000 to destroy the information, allegedly disguised as a bug bounty payout. Uber Canada said it will work with the Privacy Commissioner, and another spokesperson said more details would be provided after work with authorities. The Privacy Commissioner said his office plans to be more proactive, and noted that while it cannot issue binding orders or fines under current law, it can take non-compliant companies to Federal Court. A spokesperson for the privacy office declined further details citing confidentiality provisions.

The passage describes quantum spin relaxation in chemical systems as important for optimizing quantum computing, spintronics, and quantum biophysics, and focuses on radical pair spin relaxation dynamics. Radical pairs consist of two unpaired electrons interacting with surrounding nuclear spins under external magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation and strength. It outlines existing modeling approaches, the main computational difficulties (ensemble averaging due to randomly oriented nuclear spins at room temperature, exponential growth of Hilbert/Liouville-space dimensionality with hyperfine-coupled nuclei, and numerically stable long-time propagation on the 1 ns to 1 µs timescale), and ways these challenges are addressed (Monte Carlo sampling, classical-vector nuclear treatments, Markovian decaying terms, and tensor-network methods). It then motivates the work as introducing tensor-network methods to spin chemistry and presenting the radical-pair problem for physics and quantum biophysics, specifically avian magnetoreception. The passage further defines the radical pair Hilbert space, provides the Hamiltonian terms, discusses observables as electronic-state populations expressed through traces over the propagator, and introduces tensor-network formalisms including matrix product states (MPS) for stochastic sampling and a matrix product density operator (MPDO) framework with vectorization approaches (vMPDO).

A cave expert describes the challenges of the Thai rescue of 12 boys and their soccer coach trapped in a flooded cave for nine days. He says cave flooding rescue is guided by “WAIT,” monitoring conditions and determining whether trapped people are alive, since unnecessary risk endangers rescuers. He explains cave flooding behavior, typical waiting periods, and how temperature and water level changes can affect survival. In this case, the team was found about 1.2 miles inside, the cave temperature was in the mid-70s, and the waiting period was longer than usual; they have water but no food, leaving them weak and unable to stand for rigorous activity. He outlines three options: attempting to teach them diving skills (most dangerous), drilling or finding new entrances (difficult), or waiting for the monsoon-season water to drop (may take weeks or longer). He notes that if the location remains safe and divers can supply care, they may live in the cave until rescue is possible, but otherwise diving them out may be the only riskiest option.

Terry Rozier delivered a career-high 31 points and seven rebounds in his second NBA start as the short-handed Boston Celtics beat the Atlanta Hawks 119-110 on Friday. Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 points. Rozier started for the injured Kyrie Irving, who missed his second straight game with a right quad contusion. Boston outscored Atlanta 41-20 in the third quarter to build a large lead after trailing 55-53 at halftime. Taruean Prince led the Hawks with a career-high 31 points and eight rebounds; Dennis Schroder scored 25. The game featured multiple Boston injuries, and Prince was named to the Rising Stars game as an injury replacement for Malcolm Brogdon. The Celtics had not announced a reported signing of C Greg Monroe, and the teams’ next games were against the Knicks and Portland, respectively.

The passage describes President-elect Donald Trump’s reaction to photos used of him, focusing on a CNN book cover. On January 2, 2017, Trump tweeted that he hoped CNN’s book *Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything* would do well but called the cover photo of himself “the worst photo of me.” It notes that CNN also posted a different 2017 edition cover photo. The article says the tweet adds to attention on Trump’s Twitter account, including prior buzz about a briefly followed “Emergency Kittens” account and other widely viewed tweets. It also reports that people responded to Trump’s complaint with comments calling him vain and joking about his focus on images.

Sources say Japan’s central bank is unlikely to rush exiting ultra-loose monetary policy despite solid economic growth, largely because a sharp yen appreciation would be risky and inflation remains stubbornly low. The Bank of Japan’s policy has contributed to yen depreciation, and officials prioritize preventing abrupt yen spikes that could choke the export-reliant recovery. The passage also notes global peers are moving toward tightening, and that maintaining an ultra-easy stance could leave the BOJ with limited tools if a recession occurs. Some easing could occur next year via modest, one-off yield target adjustments rather than a full rate-hike cycle, amid uncertain inflation and political pressures. The BOJ faces added complexity from Governor Haruhiko Kuroda’s term ending in April and the possibility that successors may favor aggressive easing.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars a defendant in a noncapital case from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that contemplated restitution and capped the amount. The court reasoned that such restitution orders are part of the defendant’s “sentence,” so the defendant’s only route for appellate review is through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. The court affirmed dismissal of Frank Hoffman’s appeal from a restitution order entered after he pleaded no contest to DUI under a plea agreement requiring restitution up to a specified cap.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 25, 2021. The filing includes condensed consolidated financial statements for three months ended December 25, 2021 and December 26, 2020, reporting total net sales of $123,945 million in 2021 and $111,439 million in 2020, net income of $34,630 million and $28,755 million, and diluted earnings per share of $2.10 and $1.68. The notes cover accounting policies, revenue by product and service category, cash and marketable securities, derivatives and hedging, accounts receivable, debt (including commercial paper and term debt), share repurchase activity, restricted stock units, warranties, legal proceedings (including Epic Games), operating segments, and items related to controls and procedures, risk factors, and exhibits.

The passage describes the need for expeditious, non-invasive diagnosis of primary glial malignancies (GLI-M) in patients with brain imaging lesions, noting that standard care relies on histopathological evaluation from surgical biopsy or excision, which can be challenging and carry risks. It presents a blood-based, non-invasive test that detects circulating glial cells (CGCs) using immunocytochemistry (ICC) profiling of GFAP and OLIG2 from enriched blood samples. The test’s performance is assessed through analytical validation (including stability/recovery, linearity, detection limits, sensitivity/specificity/accuracy, precision, and interference studies) and multiple clinical studies: two blinded case-control studies, two prospective multicenter studies, and orthogonal verification using FISH for EGFR gene amplification in tumor tissue matched with blood results. Reported findings include ≥80% recovery up to 48 hours and analytical sensitivity of 92.5% (GFAP) and 95.0% (OLIG2), with clinical studies reporting high sensitivities and specificities for detecting GLI-M and differentiating it from BBT, and in one study also from EPI-M and NGCM. The test is described as minimally invasive using a venous draw of 5 mL peripheral blood, supporting diagnostic decision-making, while not intended to detect rarer subtypes or to differentiate malignancy subtype/grade.

U.S. stock futures were cautiously higher ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee’s interest-rate decision and Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s statement, with Dow Jones Industrial Average futures up 0.12%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.16%, and S&P 500 futures up 0.06%. Options volume was average on Tuesday, with about 13.8 million calls and 12.2 million puts traded, and the CBOE single-session equity put/call volume ratio at 0.64 (10-day average 0.62). Tim Cook said Apple is focusing on autonomous systems and described the effort as one of the most difficult AI projects, while Tesla options volume increased after reports including a five-star crash rating for the Model X and an investor call for a $1,000 stock price. Micron rebounded following a bullish note from Macquarie Research.

Carleton University in Ottawa is hiring a chair named after Allan Slaight to establish a research and teaching program in “conjuring arts” focused on perception and deception. The role will study why people can both deceive and be deceived, and will cover research on the history of magic and perception, investigation through global magic archives, and building a digital archive linking widely gathered information. The five-year renewable position is funded by a $2 million grant from The Slaight Family Foundation. The passage also describes experiments by researchers at the University of London testing how people explain magic tricks, noting differences in solution rates depending on how the magician’s actions are presented, and quotes researchers about how people may stick to constructed explanations or rationalize when they cannot logically figure out how a trick works.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 31, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet with its financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. The speakers discuss facing a strong, physical, deep team that cycles pucks well, controls play, has defensemen who jump in, and a goalie who can play the puck and make saves. They say they were nervous and tentative in the first period, threw pucks away too much, didn’t move their feet or forecheck as usual, and missed an opportunity to play their best while still staying in the game. They conclude there is room for improvement in execution, forechecking, winning battles, and generating offense through cycles, high-to-low plays, point shots, traffic, and shots on net. They also note adam henrique’s return adds depth and leadership, making the team stronger for big situations, and they expect the series to be more physical as it progresses.

The speaker says their father, Patrick Kane, supported them through the years. They mention being inspired by hockey opportunities in Buffalo and that they enjoy both setting up plays and scoring. They played wing and say they would play center if it benefits the team. They credit various coaches and motivators, including Don Harkins, John Hines, Dale Hunter, and Dave Gagner, and note choosing the OHL route over college, while staying in touch with Gagner. They express hope to bring a first cup to Buffalo, though they say it is special regardless, and they mention liking Briere.

Former U.S. senator and Alaska Democrat Mark Begich’s entry into the Alaska governor’s race has caused concern that he could act as a spoiler and help Republicans. The race is described as shaping up to be a three-way general election contest among Begich, independent Gov. Bill Walker, and the eventual Republican nominee. Some Democrats and independents fear that Begich and Walker could split the vote, opening the door for Republicans, and they have voiced worries in particular about conservative former Sen. Mike Dunleavy, an early GOP favorite. The passage also outlines how Walker and Democrats previously formed a “unity ticket” involving Walker and Byron Mallott, and why Walker’s campaign decided to skip primaries once Begich entered. Begich said he would not have run unless he thought he could win, and he discussed issues including Alaska’s budget deficit, oil-wealth fund earnings, and decision-making. Other candidates and party officials expressed views about the race’s timing and prospects.

After President Donald Trump’s election on Nov. 8, U.S. stocks rallied on hopes for cutting taxes, investing in infrastructure, and reducing regulations, but progress since he took office has been uneven. Four “Trump trades” are described: (1) hospital stocks fell from election to inauguration (-7.1%) and rose modestly since (+4.1%), despite early concerns about immediate Obamacare repeal; (2) infrastructure stocks gained after the election (+13%) but leveled off since (+2.4%) as an infrastructure package has not yet materialized; (3) bank stocks rose sharply after the election (+20.8%) but have increased less since (+3.1%), amid concerns about loan growth and doubts about deregulation; and (4) small-cap stocks rose after the election (+12.6%) and continued higher since (+5.3%), with expectations for tax cuts tempered by legislative setbacks and worries that foreign issues could distract from the domestic agenda.

Howard W. Ellzey, a practicing Memphis physician, was convicted by a jury of conspiracy to illegally distribute controlled substances (21 U.S.C. § 846) and 11 substantive counts of illegally distributing controlled substances (18 U.S.C. § 2 and 21 U.S.C. § 841(a)(1)). He received concurrent three-year imprisonment terms on all counts except count 16, where he received three years’ probation, and he was fined $1,500 per count (total $18,000). The evidence described a practice involving “diet patients” who paid $15 for quick visits including a B-12 injection and amphetamine prescriptions, recruitment of people to obtain prescriptions for resale, separate records across two offices to allow multiple prescriptions per day, and a DEA survey showing most schedule II prescriptions in the period were written by Ellzey and were largely for amphetamines. The Sixth Circuit found substantial evidence supporting the conviction, held there was no error in denying acquittal motions, rejected challenges to admitting suitcases of 29,000 prescriptions and related jury arguments, and rejected an indictment claim about “distributing” versus “dispensing.” The court affirmed the judgment.

The passage is an Energy Central Direct daily edition email dated November 22, 2001, for delivery to paul.d.thomas@enron.com. It also notes that the list is “ever-changing,” may be updated during the week, and encourages readers to check back.

Ebberston, Mulgrave and Ganton won finals at the first triple-header T20 Cayley Cup Finals Day at North Marine Road. Ganton beat Kirkbymoorside by nine wickets in the Division Two final, with Ian Cousins scoring 40 not out and Ganton passing the target for one wicket down in 10 overs. Mulgrave beat Sherburn by 28 runs in the Division One final, scoring 165-5 and restricting Sherburn to 137 all out. Ebberston beat Filey by six wickets in the Premier Division final, with Filey all out for 86 and Ebberston reaching 89-4, helped by an unbeaten 25 from Ben Lealman. Cups were presented to the winning captains, and Scarborough Cricket Club, umpires and other contributors were thanked.

The passage describes the author’s experience with panic attacks and subsequent diagnosis of panic disorder, noting that panic attacks typically last fewer than 30 minutes and often occur without an apparent trigger in panic disorder. It outlines differences between panic attacks and what is loosely called “anxiety attacks,” lists common physical and psychological symptoms, and advises getting a physical exam to rule out other problems. The author and mental health professionals recommend coping strategies such as writing reassuring facts and mantras on an index card or phone, visualizing panic sensations as a wave, using smartphone distractions (games, relaxing music, guided relaxation), and practicing slow, deep breathing daily and during an attack to calm heart rate and body tension.

The study examines different types of Child Care and Early Education (CCEE) searches and whether these search types vary by family and child characteristics. Using data from the 2019 NSECE Household Survey, it analyzes households with a focal child under age 6 who conducted a recent CCEE search (within 24 months) and considered more than one provider. Families could report up to two sources of information used in their most recent search: friends and family with children, providers they already knew, social media, internet search tools, and Child Care Resource & Referral (CCR&R) or other local organizations. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) identified five search types, each defined by the most common combinations of two sources, with about half of families reporting one source and half reporting two sources overall.  

Key findings include: (1) five search types were identified, including types centered on CCR&R/friends-family, internet/social media, known providers/friends-family, social media/friends-family, and friends-family/internet; (2) search types varied by whether families were looking for information about the type of care; (3) search types varied by whether the focal child had a condition affecting how care is provided, with Search Types 1 and 3 more likely to involve such children; and (4) search types varied by geographic region, with differences noted across regions and search types. The analysis finds limited differences by other family and child characteristics relative to differences in information sources. Limitations include an indicator restricted to the first two reported sources and an analytic sample that excludes most households not conducting a recent search considering more than one provider.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 GPU architecture and features, including its 40 GB HBM2 memory (five active HBM2 stacks) with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection for memory and caches, and a 40 MB L2 cache divided into partitions/slices with higher bandwidth and read performance than V100. It also discusses Compute Data Compression in L2 (up to 4x improvements for bandwidth and up to 2x for capacity) and Ampere features for improving Tensor Core performance and data movement, such as data sharing, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, CUDA Task Graphs, async copy APIs, and L2 residency controls for persistent data (disabled in MIG mode). The passage further covers MIG partitioning (up to seven GPU instances) with isolated compute and dedicated memory paths, third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch bandwidth and resiliency, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and fault detection/isolation/containment technologies. It additionally mentions A100 hardware accelerators (NVJPG JPEG decode, optical flow accelerator, atomic improvements, NVDEC), CUDA programming/runtime enhancements, and DGX A100 and MIG-based scaling software stack concepts, followed by a primer on sparse neural networks and pruning.

A.J. Brown said he is frustrated with the Eagles’ lack of production and wants the ball more, especially in critical moments. He noted that in a victory over the Rams he had six receptions for 109 yards and a touchdown, but otherwise has had few targets and little production. The passage also says DeVonta Smith has not recorded more than 60 yards in a game this season. It adds that the Eagles are 4-0 despite disappointing numbers from their top two receivers, and that offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo needs to find ways to involve them to repeat as Super Bowl champions.

The lecture describes several web security vulnerabilities and defenses. It first demonstrates the Shellshock bug, explaining that attackers can craft HTTP requests with custom headers that CGI servers pass into environment variables used by Bash, leading to execution of attacker-controlled commands. It then gives a cross-site scripting (XSS) example where a CGI script prints untrusted input directly into HTML, allowing JavaScript execution, and discusses browser-side defenses like XSS filters and how they rely on heuristics but are incomplete. It surveys additional defenses including HTTP-only cookies (partial against XSS), privilege separation via separate domains for untrusted content, and server-side content sanitization, illustrated with Django templates that encode user input to prevent it from escaping HTML context. It also covers limits of sanitization due to complex and tolerant parsing, and suggests using less expressive languages like Markdown to reduce attack surface. Further, it explains Content Security Policy (CSP) as a way for servers to restrict allowed content sources and to block inline scripts and `eval`, and mentions `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` to prevent MIME sniffing. The lecture then outlines SQL injection risks from untrusted input used in SQL queries, emphasizing rigorous encoding/escaping and the use of framework-provided database interfaces, and briefly notes issues with path traversal when filenames come from untrusted sources. It discusses cookies for session management and stateless alternatives using message authentication codes (MACs), giving an AWS example of signing requests. Finally, it covers protocol parsing problems via ambiguous URL origins, attacks involving crafted files across parsers (e.g., GIFAR), and covert-channel attacks based on time and caching such as visited-link inference from link colors, cache timing, DNS timing, and rendering/access errors to infer visited sites.

Scientists in the United Kingdom studied how bumblebee queens are affected by neonicotinoid pesticides. Neonicotinoids are systemic seed coatings on widely grown crops such as corn, soybeans, and canola, and traces can end up in plant pollen consumed by bees and in pollen of wildflowers near fields and streams. In a laboratory experiment at Royal Holloway University of London, queens fed syrup containing traces of thiamethoxam similar to field exposure were 26% less likely to lay eggs. The researchers warn that reduced reproduction could contribute to declines in wild bumblebee populations and potentially lead to die-out. The findings were published in *Nature Ecology and Evolution* and are expected to support calls for further restrictions, including the European Union’s consideration of making a 2013 moratorium permanent. Pesticide companies and some farmers oppose restrictions, arguing moratoriums reduce canola yields and increase spraying of other pesticides.

Swarthmore students are described as generally ages 18 to 22 but pressured to achieve top grades, internships, and a poised, error-free image. The passage argues that while academic improvement matters, students should remember they are in college and that making mistakes is okay. It says laughing at yourself can help you get through a campus where expectations are high and mistakes are not life or death, since learning often comes from mistakes rather than successes. It also emphasizes taking perspective on Swarthmore’s intense and unique environment, focusing on the funny at times, and giving others the benefit of the doubt when they err—such as by asking for clarification instead of assuming bad intent. Laughter is presented as a way to cope with uncomfortable situations, though it may not solve everything.

The passage discusses MITOCW course content on “codes on graphs,” focusing on Hadamard transform realizations of Reed–Muller codes and an introduction to decoding with the sum product (APP) algorithm. It explains that exercises may be difficult without sufficient background, notes homework strategy and mentions potential coverage of the BCJR algorithm. It then outlines how allowing cycles in graphical realizations can simplify representations, while requiring cycle-free graphs can make realizations more complex. The instructor describes building Hadamard transform realizations over \(F_2\), properties of the generator matrices \(u_m\) (constructed via tensor products), and how Reed–Muller codes are generated using fixed and free coefficients. A graphical realization for the \(8,4,4\) Reed–Muller code is constructed using Hadamard transform graphs, reduced via simplifications, and compared across different styles: a cyclic reduced realization, an agglomerated cycle-free realization, a trellis realization, and a tail-biting realization, with trade-offs in state complexity, branch complexity, and decoding performance. The latter part introduces APP (a posteriori probability) decoding and explains the motivation for the sum product algorithm, initially on cycle-free graphs where it yields exact APP in finite time, and then on graphs with cycles where it becomes iterative and approximate. It defines APP decoding as computing probabilities for internal and external variables given the received sequence, relates this to sums of likelihood products, and begins describing the sum product algorithm via past/future decomposition using cut properties in cycle-free graphs.

The County Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) confirmed a woman from Spring Valley tested positive for West Nile Virus on Friday, the first confirmed case in San Diego County this year. The county said she developed rash and headache four days after traveling outside the country, though symptoms can occur 2 to 14 days after a mosquito bite. The virus mainly affects birds and can be transmitted to humans by mosquitos; symptoms may include headache, fever, nausea, rashes, fatigue, or swollen glands, and rare cases can be deadly. In California this year, 231 people have been reported ill and 12 have died; in San Diego County, 32 dead birds, eight batches of mosquitos, and one horse tested positive. Residents are encouraged to use insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants, and remove standing water sources; dead birds and mosquito breeding sources can be reported to the Vector Control Program at (858) 694-2888 or vector@sdcounty.ca.gov.

Asian equities turned cautious after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the second time this year by 25 basis points and provided details on unwinding its balance sheet. Despite inflation below the Fed’s target, the Fed’s guidance was seen as dovish, with regional markets mostly declining: Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.6%, South Korea’s Kospi declined 0.75%, and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 dropped 1.13% as materials and energy weakened. China’s Hang Seng fell 0.91% while the Shanghai and Shenzhen composites edged higher. Markets also questioned whether the Fed will follow through on three rate hikes this year. In Japan, Toshiba shares fell 2.68% amid Western Digital’s legal action and the company’s likely missed annual filing deadline. Oil prices dropped to a seven-month low, the dollar index stayed below 97, and currency moves followed better-than-expected Australian jobs and mixed New Zealand GDP data. Central bank events listed include the Bank of Japan’s two-day meeting and the Bank of England’s rate decision. On Wall Street, stocks closed mixed after the Fed announcement, with the Dow gaining 0.22%.

The passage describes author affiliations and correspondence details for a medRxiv preprint posted January 3, 2024, about modeling brain ageing and multiple sclerosis (MS)-specific neurodegeneration using MRI. It introduces the brain-age paradigm and the brain-age gap (BAG) metric, then proposes a quantitative neuroimaging measure of structural brain damage referenced to disease duration (DD), called the brain-predicted DD gap. It also explores an alternative MS-age modeling strategy and the corresponding brain-predicted MS-age gap. The study is a retrospective multicenter design collecting T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI and clinical data, using deep learning for age and DD prediction, and applying interpretability and statistical analyses to validate gap metrics against disability measured by EDSS. Results reported include associations between BAG, DD gap, and MS-age gap with EDSS, and findings that DD gap adds incremental explanatory value beyond BAG for EDSS variance and worsening. The discussion states that the DD gap is a clinically meaningful measure of MS-specific brain damage, while the MS-age gap appears less disease-specific and does not add significantly beyond the classical brain-age paradigm. The passage also lists funding, competing interests, and members of the MAGNIMS network.

Archaeologists confirmed five years ago that a skeleton found beneath a Leicester car park was that of Richard III. The discovery became life-changing for several people, including Dominic Smee, whose spine condition matched Richard III’s and who trained in knightly activities for a Channel 4 documentary. Dominic later said he gained confidence and respect, including recognition by Benedict Cumberbatch. Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard III’s sister, provided DNA for the identification process and said he experienced media attention and public recognition after the remains were confirmed and reburied. Mike Mistry, a car park attendant, helped unknowingly by painting an “R” on the reserved bay and later hosted visitors from around the world, though he was made redundant in 2016. Musician Ian Churchward said the discovery reshaped his career by inspiring Richard III-themed songs and multiple albums, including a concept album.

The passage describes the use of the Situation Calculus in artificial intelligence to specify and reason about dynamical systems, where action effects are represented using fluents and the frame problem concerns stating which fluents remain unchanged. It summarizes Reiter’s successor state axioms for the Markov property, and extensions to non-Markovian properties (allowing action preconditions and effects to depend on past situations), citing applications such as database transactions and integrity constraints. It also discusses extending the framework to knowledge-producing actions (Scherl and Levesque) and the need for non-Markovian theories in emerging domains like smart contracts, which require formal accounts of obligations. The paper then outlines its structure and introduces sequential and temporal Situation Calculus, including its logic sorts, action and fluent representations, time functions, foundational axioms, and the general form of action precondition axioms, successor state axioms, and basic action theories. It defines non-Markovian control via bounded formulas and boundedness conditions, and provides a running example about opening a door with specified primitive actions, fluents, precondition axioms, and successor state axioms. Finally, it introduces obligations in the Situation Calculus by summarizing an embedding that combines deontic accessibility with time, using a fluent O(s′, s) and defining an obligation modality Oblg(ϕ, s) to express that an agent is obliged to make ϕ true in a given situation.

The passage describes configurable duty-cycle programmability for TPS7H5001-SP, TPS75002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP using the DCL pin, while TPS7H5004-SP only supports a 50% maximum duty cycle with DCL connected to AVSS. For applications needing 100% duty cycle, a compatible device should be selected and DCL connected to VLDO. For other applications, DCL can be connected to AVSS for a 50% limit or left floating for a 75% maximum, with noted differences in which devices support the 50% limit and when OUTB/SRB are active. It also explains current sense and PWM generation via CS_ILIM and COMP, including an offset in the PWM comparator, use of CS_ILIM for current-limit configuration, and how a sense resistor is selected with topology-dependent calculations. Hiccup mode operation is described: when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, the device performs cycle-by-cycle limiting and then enters delayed shutdown and restart sequences controlled by CHICC (and related thresholds), with recommended CHICC minimum value. External fault protection via the FAULT pin, thermal shutdown behavior, slope compensation requirements for stability (including how to set it with RSC), and an overview of device functional modes (fixed-frequency peak current mode control with comparator turn-off based on COMP) are also covered, alongside additional application and layout-related guidance.

The passage is a daily FOX News “Halftime Report” that covers political commentary and multiple news items. It argues that “weak parties” and reduced partisan incentives may increase “more partisanship,” discussing California’s decline in registered independents and the elimination of partisan primaries, and suggests that unaffiliated voter growth and additional minor parties could make politics more fragmented. It also lists approval and control-of-House polling averages for Donald Trump and Democrats vs. Republicans, reports discussion topics, and summarizes a Quinnipiac poll showing Ted Cruz ahead of Beto O’Rourke in Texas, plus campaign ad strategies by Republicans and Democrats. Additional segments include reports on Trump’s outreach to big donors, Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton resigning to run for Congress, Trump continuing spy-related claims despite Trey Gowdy’s assessment, and coverage of Trump pushing Jeff Sessions to reverse recusal. The remainder includes brief sports, entertainment, and reader commentary sections.

Junior County committed to UConn as part of the 2026 recruiting class. The 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy (Utah) chose the Huskies over other finalists after a final visit last weekend, citing practice, conversations with coach Dan Hurley, and campus life. County described Hurley’s intensity and said he expects to develop and make winning plays on both ends. He is ranked No. 43 overall and No. 4 shooting guard in the SC Next 100, and averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 3.4 assists for Utah Prospects on the Nike EYBL circuit, including games with 20 points and multiple 3-pointers. This commitment is Hurley’s first in the 2026 class; UConn previously secured a top-five 2025 class and has ranked in the top 10 in consecutive years, winning back-to-back national championships between 2023 and 2024.

VentureWire’s Tuesday, November 14, 2000 issue compiles private company business news. Top stories include Apax merging units and pledging $600 million for Israeli telecom, IT, and healthcare investments; New Edge Networks laying off 135 employees; KSolutions receiving $50 million; and Cisco acquiring Radiata for $295 million. The issue also lists multiple funding rounds (“New Money”), layoffs and closures (“Bad News”), product launches and name changes (“New Products”), mergers and acquisitions, board appointments (“New Directors”), executive changes (“New People”), venture capital fund and personnel updates, and two corrections (an omitted partner name and a misspelled TenantDirect URL).

Beijing ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising, and content on feng shui by Wednesday as part of efforts to cool the housing market. The portals must not promise rising returns, assist buyers with local hukou permits or school enrollment, spread rumors or disseminate misleading claims about price gains, or provide feng shui or financing advice. The move follows earlier restrictions, including higher down payments on second and larger homes and suspension of individual mortgage loans longer than 25 years, with third property purchases already banned.

Researchers combined fossil evidence with rare gene transfers (horizontal gene transfer) to reconstruct fungal evolution and find that fungi diversified close to a billion years ago, hundreds of millions of years before land plants. Because fungi rarely fossilize and likely evolved complex multicellularity multiple times, the study used a molecular clock calibrated with 17 gene-transfer events to establish older/younger relationships between fungal lineages. The analysis suggests a common ancestor of living fungi dated to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, supporting prolonged fungi–algae interactions that may have helped create primitive soils and make Earth’s continents habitable by breaking down rock and cycling nutrients. The work involved researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology and collaborators across Europe.

The passage argues that after the 1962 Cuban missile crisis, U.S. peace prevailed because of strategic superiority, but later defense policy ignored evidence of Soviet aggression and accepted Soviet inferiority as a permanent position. It claims that U.S. Soviet leadership gains occurred over time, with administrations described as weak and inconsistent. Examples cited include Soviet actions in Cuba and Afghanistan during the Carter Administration, followed by warnings and admissions of lacking force, which the author says damaged U.S. credibility and unity among allies. The passage concludes that a more effective alternative is restoring “the margin of safety” through prudent, measured defense rebuilding, firm action against terrorism, maintaining strategic deterrence, and consulting allies to restore confidence and alliance cohesion, asserting this is necessary for world peace.

The passage is an email forwarding multiple news items from October 2001, largely involving Enron and related business and political coverage. It includes a Wall Street Journal report that Enron CFO Andrew Fastow’s limited partnership LJM2 made millions in profits from transactions with Enron, including management fees and capital increases, and discusses controversy over potential conflicts with Fastow’s fiduciary role. A Business Wire item says The New Power Company revised its netting agreement with Enron subsidiaries to expand acceptable collateral through January 4, 2002 and reduce required cash collateral. Additional excerpts cover topics such as lobbying firm rankings in Washington, an award ceremony for Houston business leaders, expectations for LME Week amid recession concerns, and a court case in India where Dhabol Power Company challenges the jurisdiction of Maharashtra’s electricity regulator.

United Airlines described its “premium” initiatives, including uncrowded lounges and seatback entertainment, as a response to rivals’ perceived shortcomings. The airline pointed to Delta’s long lines at Sky Clubs and to American’s lack of seatback screens on most domestic planes, highlighting that it has seatback entertainment across more than 146,000 seats on 765 airplanes. United’s premium cabin revenue rose about 6% year-over-year in the third quarter, compared with Delta’s 9%, and the article notes Delta has raised lounge pass prices and restricted access at times while introducing a new exclusivity tier. American said most customers use their own devices and that it is focusing on fast connections and free entertainment on those devices. The passage also compares recent stock performance among United, Delta, and American.

China warned Hong Kong it would not tolerate anyone using the city to damage mainland stability, according to Zhang Xiaoming, head of China’s liaison office in Hong Kong. He said controlling the independence movement requires “bottom-line awareness,” emphasizing limits on activities that harm national sovereignty and security, challenge central authority or the Basic Law, or use Hong Kong to undermine mainland social and political stability. The warnings follow tensions after two pro-independence lawmakers were ousted, and concerns that Beijing is tightening controls in a territory that retains autonomy for 50 years. The passage also cites worries about freedoms and a rules-based identity, including the disappearance and later detention of five booksellers last year. Hong Kong leader Leung Chun-ying said he would not run again, and Regina Ip announced she will run for his position, which opponents fear signals further tightening by Beijing.

The passage describes Spotify and Amazon Music as music streaming platforms and says users can transfer playlists from Spotify to Amazon Music using MusConv, an online software program available at MusConv.com. It outlines three MusConv subscriptions—Basic, Professional, and Ultimate—with features such as unlimited songs and playlists per session, CSV export, batch importing (Professional), and additional options like Apple Music support, priority support, lifetime updates, and duplicate track deletion (Ultimate). It also provides a brief description of MusConv and includes contact information for MusConv.

The speaker discusses preparing for games based on past experience, staying focused using headphones, and learning from both good and bad outcomes. They mention looking for “seawalls” in Boston, and describe how staying in position and taking advantage of rebounds matters. They say motivation comes from wanting to win the Stanley Cup for themselves, teammates, family, and friends. They also emphasize the importance of strong first-period penalty kills, blocking shots, avoiding second and third chances, and focusing on a Monday night opportunity.

A watchdog said some care homes may bill unscrupulous fees to vulnerable elderly people and their families, potentially breaking consumer law. It cited practices including charging for residents who died months earlier, charging people before a resident entered a home, threatening eviction, and failing to advertise prices. The report said homes make it difficult for residents and families to complain, and that the abuses targeted self-funding residents who often pay fees exceeding £600 a week and may be forced to sell houses. The watchdog is considering new legislation and is bringing a test case to court to assess residents’ protection under current law, while Citizens’ Advice said older people and their families are experiencing distress and financial pressure due to gaps in consumer protection.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 23, 2015. The report states that on July 23, 2015 Amazon announced its second quarter 2015 financial results, with the press release included as Exhibit 99.1 and additional information regarding non-GAAP financial measures included as Exhibit 99.2. The report lists items 2.02 and 9.01 and is signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Caring Health Center in Springfield is participating in National Health Center Week, joining more than 50 health centers in Massachusetts and over 1,200 community health centers nationally. The center provides care to more than 20,000 people in Springfield, and President and CEO Tania Barber said many people still do not know community health centers like Caring Health Center exist. On Monday, the center held Elected Officials Day with local and state representatives and community leaders, along with healthcare community honors. National Health Center Week ends on August 19.

Education regulators in Ohio are reviewing a whistleblower’s claim that the online charter school Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT) inflated attendance figures tied to state funding. A former ECOT technology employee said school officials ordered staff to manipulate student data using software called ActivTrak, which the employee said was obtained after the state demanded ECOT repay $60 million for the 2015–2016 school year. The state challenged ECOT’s use of ActivTrak after finding duplicated learning hours, according to the Education Department. The Education Department said the ActivTrak issues were considered in an attendance review and that it questioned how ECOT claimed learning time, not intent. ECOT’s lobbyist and attorney disputed or said they were unaware of the allegations. The AP reported the employee’s concerns were shared with state officials, including Auditor Dave Yost, and that the department delayed meeting with him until December, with a subsequent review planned for summer. Some politicians and critics called for a criminal investigation, while the Franklin County Prosecutor said he has received no criminal referral.

The passage is a final Oval Office address from the President, thanking citizens, Vice President Gore, Cabinet members, and others for their service. It describes the past eight years as a period of transformation and credits the American people with stronger families and communities, economic gains, improved schools, expanded health insurance, reduced poverty, and environmental improvements. The President outlines three future priorities: maintain fiscal responsibility by paying down national debt and providing tax relief; continue leading globally to address security threats and global poverty while ensuring trade benefits all; and unite a more diverse America by upholding common values and treating all people with fairness and dignity. The President also congratulates George W. Bush and ends by emphasizing continued public service and wishing blessings on America.

The passage describes the role of blockchain technology across industries and highlights a knowledge gap in enterprises regarding blockchain competences and scaling beyond proof-of-concepts. It presents a study of blockchain education in AACSB-accredited US universities: in March 2024, 533 universities were identified, and 151 (about 28%) offered at least one blockchain course (361 courses in total). Course data were collected from university catalogs and websites and analyzed by classifying course topics into categories, determining scientific fields and intersections with emerging technologies (e.g., AI, IoT, cybersecurity), and using peer review for consistency. Findings show blockchain courses are mainly offered at the undergraduate level (72%), most often by Computer Science and Information Systems departments, and mostly focus on fundamentals/overview and digital assets/cryptocurrencies, with additional emphasis on technical development and business and legal topics. The passage concludes that blockchain education is increasingly connected with other emerging technologies and that social, methodological, and personal competences, not only technical skills, are addressed. It also calls for future research on how disciplines align competencies with industry needs and for replication to assess changes over time.

Joseph Nyberg, a seven-year-old who likes singing and writing stories, created “Heart Cents” after his grandfather died from heart disease. He placed collection buckets in Savannah and Richmond Hill for a month to collect pennies and dollars for St. Joseph’s heart patients, raising more than $200. St. Joseph’s Foundations agreed to match the amount, bringing the total to $422, and the money will help cover transportation and co-pays. After presenting a check, another family made an anonymous $250 donation, bringing Joseph’s total to $672 and 14 Heart Cents. Joseph plans to keep the buckets up year-round to honor his grandfather and raise more money.

The passage describes protocols for reading data from the device, grouped into three categories: legacy SPI-compatible protocols with a single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible protocols with dual SDO-x, and an ADC controller clock or SRC protocol. For single SDO-x legacy protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S), the device supports SPI-00-S after power-up or reset. To switch protocols for both read and write, SDI_MODE[1:0] is programmed in SDI_CTL_REG (first write uses SPI-00-S, subsequent frames use the new protocol) and SDO_MODE[1:0] is set to 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. When SPI-compatible protocols are used, the RVS output stays low throughout the data transfer frame. The passage also explains that using a short frame reads only required MSB bits, while a long frame with SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0]=00h enables daisy-chain operation. For dual SDO-x operation, the device uses two-bit output by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0]=11b, and in this mode the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin acts as SDO-1. In dual SDO mode, two data bits are launched on SDO-0 and SDO-1 at every SCLK launch edge. It notes that the timing specifications are the same for single and dual SDO modes, with the device requiring half as many SCLK cycles in single SDO mode for the same number of bits.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring using optical sensors at multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single measurement of a physiological parameter. It incorporates prior applications by reference and relates to combining minimally processed sensor data from different sites into one algorithm to calculate parameters such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, and glucose. The system can use multiple light emitters and multiple photodetectors, including spatially configured three-dimensional detector arrangements that conform to patient anatomy to improve measurement robustness and provide topology information to help confirm sensor placement. Examples include monitors with sensors attached to cephalic (e.g., nose, earlobe) and peripheral (e.g., finger, arm, palm, foot) sites, with sensor interfaces providing raw or minimally processed data to a signal processor that combines signals to produce the single measurement and may also generate independent site measurements.

The passage describes surgical robotic arms and wrists, focusing on a wrist design for torque sensing and accurate instrument positioning. It summarizes prior applications and explains that surgical robots must balance flexibility, accuracy, size/weight constraints, and force measurability for tactile replacement. A torque-sensing wrist is described using articulated segments and articulations with torque sensors that sense torque about specified axes. The passage details an example robotic arm with revolute joints and shaft sections, and a wrist that can move the instrument within a hemispherical region while avoiding high-speed joint requirements. It explains how forces applied to the instrument can be measured via multiple torque sensors and used in a control unit to generate force feedback (e.g., via haptic input devices). It also describes embodiments where the wrist is located at the distal end of the robot arm or at the end of the surgical instrument, along with torque sensor technologies, potential wireless or wired data transmission, sterilization considerations, and operational steps for aligning, inserting, and moving instruments at an operation site.
Biochemist Katalin Karikó was one of the few women to win a Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine in 2023, and she initially thought the call about the prize was a joke.

House prices rose in Southern California counties over the 12 months ending in May, according to the CoreLogic Home Price Index released July 3. Los Angeles County increased 8.3% year over year, Riverside and San Bernardino rose 8.2%, and Orange County rose 6.2%. CoreLogic said this was the third straight month that appreciation topped 8% in Los Angeles and inland areas and 6% in Orange County. The report attributed higher prices to a lean supply of homes for sale, with the shortage more acute for entry-level homes, and noted many homeowners are staying put because about half have mortgage rates of 3.75% or less. A CoreLogic and RTi Research sentiment study found 15% of homeowners hope to buy in the next year and 11% want to sell, while 28% of renters hope to buy. CoreLogic CEO Frank Martell said prices will continue to rise until more supply becomes available. Nationally, prices increased 7.1% and California prices increased 8.9% over the same period.

The passage says that distributed systems require reliability, agility, and scale, and that patterns and practices can regularize and improve how distributed system algorithms and object-oriented programming are developed. It explains that the book first covers patterns on a single node because containers are foundational, and co-located container groups form the atomic elements of distributed system patterns. It provides motivations for splitting a single-machine application into multiple containers: resource isolation (e.g., separating a user-facing server from a best-effort background loader), scaling team organization by ownership of small focused and reusable modules (e.g., a reusable Git synchronization container), and separation of concerns to make applications easier to understand, test, update, and deploy independently. It then notes that the following chapters describe patterns for modular groups of containers, assuming tight dependencies where containers can be reliably co-scheduled on a single machine and may share volumes and other resources; in Kubernetes this tight grouping is called a pod.

Kesha tweeted support for Taylor Swift after former DJ David Mueller filed a lawsuit accusing Swift of fabricating a story that he groped her during a 2014 Denver meet-and-greet. A judge dismissed Mueller’s lawsuit against Swift on Friday, but Swift’s countersuit for $1 in assault and battery remains and will be deliberated Monday. Kesha wrote that she supports Swift and that “Truth is always the answer.” The passage also notes that Swift previously donated $250,000 to Kesha during Kesha’s legal case against Dr. Luke and that Kesha released her album *Rainbow*, which recently reached No. 1 on iTunes.

The passage describes a “Combo” defensive approach using a mix of person-to-person and zone defense against North Carolina’s Four Corner style offense and other spread offenses that rely on dribble penetration. In the basic alignment, outside defenders apply aggressive pass denial while inside defenders provide backside zoning support. United Distributors, Inc. sued Henry R. Burke, Alfred R. Willis, and Air-eo Appliance & Hardware, Inc. to recover the amount of a $3,107.82 note, alleging Willis and Burke had guaranteed the corporation’s credit. The court found Willis’s motive for signing the guarantee failed when he was not to become associated with the corporation and the plaintiff was apprised of this, and it affirmed the dismissal.

The passage describes a study aimed at understanding nanoscale, depth-resolved degradation of LiNiCoMnO2 (NCM111) cathodes by tracking how structure, chemical composition, and transition-metal valence states evolve in three dimensions during electrochemical cycling. It notes that conventional 2D or single-modality methods struggle to resolve heterogeneous, depth-dependent changes in beam-sensitive materials. To address this, the authors developed a simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography method that captures 3D maps of structure, chemical composition, and valence states in a single, low-dose acquisition with reduced cumulative electron exposure and precise channel alignment.

NCM111 half-cells were cycled for 50, 100, and 200 cycles at 1C (2.7–4.3 V). Capacity degraded progressively, losing ~34.3% after 50 cycles, ~52.2% after 100 cycles (still functional), and fully losing capacity after 200 cycles. Atomic-resolution ADF-STEM showed structural phase transitions from a layered structure (pristine) to a spinel-like structure after 100 cycles and to a rock-salt structure after 200 cycles. The 3D chemical composition mapping showed oxygen and transition metals were largely uniform up to 100 cycles but changed sharply by 200 cycles, including increased transition-metal-rich regions associated with structural transformation. Chemical composition was largely uniform through particle depth, whereas transition-metal segregation and valence-state changes were surface-localized and depth-dependent.

The 3D EELS valence-state maps indicated that Mn4+ and Co3+ dominate in the pristine state, with fractions remaining relatively stable up to 100 cycles but changing substantially by 200 cycles: Mn4+ and Co3+ decreased while Mn2+ and Co2+ increased. Mn and Co valence states showed strong depth dependence even in the pristine state, attributed to surface-localized transition-metal clustering rather than depth gradients in oxygen, excess lithium, or secondary phase formation. Finally, the authors link degradation to a combination of structural phase transitions, transition-metal migration (which can reduce inhomogeneity), and dissolution-driven segregation (which increases inhomogeneity), with degradation pathways differing between uniform compositional changes in the bulk and stronger gradients near the surface.

Brayan Rocchio hit a home run in the bottom of the eighth to give the Guardians a lead and force a decisive Game 3 in the AL Wild Card Series against the Tigers. The game had been low-scoring and tied 1-1 entering the eighth, with Cleveland managing only two hits through seven innings and Detroit leaving 15 baserunners. Rocchio’s 99.9 mph homer came off Tigers reliever Troy Melton, and the win was described as part of the Guardians’ ability to play without pressure, even in elimination settings.

Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. sought a refund of sales/use taxes paid on purchases of drilling equipment used in installing pumps and plumbing for extracting water. The case was previously partly resolved by holding some claims barred by the statute of limitations and reversing others for a factual determination of whether the Taxpayer qualified for an exemption. On remand, the trial court found the taxes properly paid. The appellate court determined the Taxpayer is a contractor under Ind. Code 6-2-1-38(k), making transactions subject to sales or use tax, but only exempt if the ultimate purchaser would qualify under Ind. Code 6-2-1-39(b)(6). The Taxpayer relied on the exemption for sales of manufacturing machinery, tools, and equipment directly used in extracting tangible personal property. The court concluded the exemption did not apply because evidence showed ultimate users used the extracted water for personal or farm/business use and there was no evidence of resale, so the Taxpayer made an insufficient showing of exemption. The judgment was affirmed.

Ralph Nelson Elliott discovered the Elliott Wave theory by studying 75 years of stock market data and proposed that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. The theory classifies waves into impulse (motive) waves, which move in the trend direction, and correction (retracement) waves, which move opposite the trend. Impulse waves have five sub-waves (waves 1–5) with specific rules, including that wave 2 should not retrace more than 100% of wave 1 and wave 3 should not be the shortest. Correction waves have three sub-waves (A, B, and C) that make net movement opposite the trend, and sub-waves in pullbacks do not fully retrace the previous sub-wave. The theory is used mainly by technical traders across stock, forex, and commodity markets, often alongside other indicators like trend lines, moving averages, and momentum oscillators. The passage states there is no best timeframe, interpretation is highly subjective and hard to backtest, and the theory lacks clearly defined entry and exit signals, which can enable curve fitting. It concludes with examples of common questions about wave types, rules for impulse waves, and how Elliott discovered the theory.

Justices debated whether restitution imposed under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act (MVRA) is criminal, civil, or both under the Constitution’s ex post facto clause. They discussed that the MVRA was adopted after Ellingburg’s offense, so applying it to increase his punishment would allegedly violate the clause if restitution is “criminal.” The government agreed the MVRA cannot be used to increase Ellingburg’s punishment. Justices questioned counsel arguments, with Justice Alito emphasizing features that seemed more civil than criminal, including victims enforcing restitution as a judgment lien under state law and congressional language about helping victims. Other justices, including Kagan and Jackson, leaned toward the view that placing restitution in the criminal sentencing system brings the ex post facto clause into play. The passage also predicts the justices will reject applying the new statute to Ellingburg and likely do so without lengthy separate opinions.

The passage describes mechanisms and computational methods related to microtubule (MT) dynamics in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), focusing on therapy resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxanes (docetaxel, cabazitaxel). It notes that resistance to systemic therapy is universal, with about one-third of tumors primarily refractory, and that mCRPC refractory to tubulin inhibitors is uniformly fatal within 12–18 months. The text explains how androgen receptor (AR) splice variants can remain constitutively active and how differential MT dynamics associate with taxane sensitivity versus resistance. It presents a computational pipeline for tracking EB1/EB3 “comets” in microscopy sequences to infer MT polymerization behavior, including spatiotemporal clustering to analyze growth, pauses, and shortening. Experiments in isogenic prostate cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids evaluate how AR variants alter MT growth speeds and spatial MT organization, and how paclitaxel changes MT dynamics. The passage also discusses patient-derived organoid culture challenges and optimization, androgen-independent circulating tumor cell (CTC) detection issues, roles of pVHL/GSK3β in MT regulation, and MT-associated pathways connected to drug resistance. Finally, it outlines approaches to anticipate and validate drug resistance using MT dynamics signatures, drug-response assays, xenografts, and gene-expression correlations, concluding that there is an unmet need for molecular markers and methods to match tumors to effective tubulin inhibitors.

It introduces NVIDIA RTX IO, which uses GPU-based lossless loading and decompression in combination with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to offload work from CPU cores to the GPU, aiming to accelerate I/O performance by up to 100x and enable near-instantaneous game loading, improved frame rates, reduced stutter and object pop-in, and faster streaming of high-quality textures. Alexis Perez pled guilty, pursuant to a plea agreement, to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and was sentenced to 51 months’ imprisonment. He appealed, arguing the district court (1) erred in not reducing his base offense level by three levels under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy and (2) erred in not awarding a minor-role reduction under U.S.S.G. § 3B1.2. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed, concluding the court properly declined the three-level reduction because Perez and his co-conspirators had taken “crucial steps” and were on the verge of executing the mail fraud offense when law enforcement intervened. The court also found no clear error in denying a minor-role reduction, noting the record supported the finding that Perez played an important role in planning and preparation, knew how the scheme would be implemented, and was paid, and Perez failed to show he was less culpable than most other conspirators.

The passage explains day trading price action strategies as approaches that use patterns of an asset’s price movement to determine trade entry and exit points. It defines price action trading as a technical analysis method focused on past price movements—such as price swing highs and lows, price bars, chart patterns, and candlestick patterns—often with little or no reliance on indicators. It also describes how traders may assess broader market structure using tools like trend lines, moving averages, support/resistance, and pivot levels, and lists different pattern types including reversal, continuation, harmonic (advanced) patterns, and candlestick patterns. The passage emphasizes that there are no general rules for strategy success, and that strategies should be backtested, noting that coding and backtesting price action strategies can be challenging but is necessary to establish definitive trading rules. It includes an example of a WTI crude oil futures strategy converted from daily backtesting to day trading and discusses out-of-sample results. The passage also includes FAQs summarizing what price action trading is, how it can be used for day trading, and how to backtest such strategies.

In 2016, credit card debt and auto loans increased household bills for millions of people. The passage advises paying off debt fast by reducing credit card use, creating a spending plan and emergency fund, making the largest monthly payments possible, directing extra money toward debt, using overtime income, and cutting nonessential spending such as daily trips to coffee shops. It recommends paying off debts with the highest interest rates first, doubling payments after one card is paid, and reallocating freed funds to the next debt. It also suggests making gradual lifestyle changes so the process is not overwhelming.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network that exploited transsexuals recruited in fake “Miss Trans” competitions in Venezuela. Police said they freed over 20 victims forced to live in inhumane conditions in overcrowded apartments in Barcelona and Palma de Mallorca, where they had to work through prostitution and drug dealing to repay debts. The network paid for travel, accommodation, and breast implants, and promised “great prosperity,” but confiscated travel documents on arrival and imposed a 15,000-euro debt for return. Victims were required to be available 24 hours a day to clients, and 14 people were arrested. The network earned up to 1 million euros over five years.

The passage describes Google’s 2017 Doodle honoring Max Born’s 135th birthday and summarizes his contributions to quantum mechanics, including the “Born Rule.” It notes Born’s birth details in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland), his professorship at the University of Göttingen, his work and relationships with scientists such as Werner Heisenberg and Albert Einstein, his forced emigration to England after Hitler rose to power, and later recognition including the Nobel Prize in 1954 for the Born Rule. The passage also states that Born died on Jan. 5, 1970, with his death attributed to a heart ailment complicated by arterial thrombosis.

The passage outlines the “Regulatory Sandbox in Education” bill, which allows districts or charter schools to create an innovation plan and apply to the State Board of Education for waivers of state board rules. It also permits LEAs supporting an innovative education program to expend certain state restricted funding under specified circumstances and accept private grants, loans, gifts, endowments, devises, or bequests. Charter school authorizers must amend charters to incorporate approved innovation plans and remove them when no longer in effect. The Utah State Board of Education must submit reports to the Education Interim Committee, including annual reporting by November 30 on approved plans, waivers granted or declined, terminated plans, related statutory provisions, and legislative recommendations. The State Board must also annually report on innovation plans, report on the use of state restricted funding upon request, and may terminate innovation plans. The passage further notes there are no known applications or approved plans reported, and recommends the State Board create awareness, provide website information, develop optional application forms, and promote the program through existing communication channels.

The passage says the UK faces growing economic worries as pay growth slows while inflation rises, squeezing households through falling real pay and increasing business uncertainty after the election. Schoenfeld questioned the feasibility and defense implications of such control and argued for security based on political foundations, which led to discussion of comparisons between German and British actions toward small nations and of “realism” in Finnish policy.
