Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated December 22, 2015, reporting that on December 21, 2015 its Board of Directors adopted amendments to Apple’s Amended and Restated Bylaws to implement proxy access. The amendments add Section 5.15, allowing shareholders (or groups of up to twenty) holding at least three percent of outstanding common stock continuously for at least three years to nominate director candidates and have them included in annual meeting proxy materials, up to twenty percent of the Board, subject to Bylaw requirements. The amendments also revise Section 5.14 and make ministerial, clarifying, and conforming changes to Sections 2.4, 5.4, and 10.6. The report states the description is qualified by the full text of the Bylaws attached as Exhibit 3.2.

Mr Walson Ibarakumo, coordinator of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) South East Zonal office, warned of impending floods in parts of Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi States. He said the warning was based on forecasts by the National Hydrological Services Agency (NIHSA) and the Nigeria Meteorological Agency (NiMET), attributing the heavy rainfall, storm and wind to climate change. He advised residents to change their attitude, especially regarding energy use, and to begin preparations early. He listed highly probable and probable flood-risk areas in each state, including Enugu South and East, Oji River, Udi and Uzo Uwani in Enugu; Aguata, Idemili North and Ogbaru in Anambra; and Afikpo South, Abakaliki, Ezza South, Ikwo, Ohaukwu and Afikpo in Ebonyi.

DBS Banking Group said the outlook for Indian government bonds remains challenging amid supply pressure into fiscal year 2019 and expectations that developed market yields will rise with monetary normalisation. It expects upward pressure on INgov yields but says much of the sell-off may be behind them, with more modest yield increases. DBS is tactical about shorter-term bonds, neutral-to-negative on longer-term bonds, and expects yields to head higher. It noted India’s CPI easing, reducing urgency to hike rates, and suggested better entry points may emerge as the market digests increased issuance. DBS also said the rupee has depreciated alongside Indian equities since late January, citing capital inflow needs driven by a widening current account deficit and forecasting rupee depreciation toward 67 this year.

Al-Qaida-linked militants in Syria downed a Russian Su-25 fighter jet in the Idlib province on Saturday, killing the pilot after he ejected and resisted capture, according to the Russian Defense Ministry and Syrian monitors. The ministry said the pilot died fighting “terrorists,” and preliminary reports indicated a portable ground-to-air missile was used in an al-Qaida-controlled area near the rebel-held town of Sarqeb. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported intense airstrikes and residents fleeing, and Syria’s state news agency said troops captured villages and a hill, cutting links between Sarqeb and Maarest al-Numan. The U.N. said more than 270,000 people have been displaced in Idlib since Dec. 15. Fighting also continued Saturday between Turkish forces and allied Syrian opposition fighters and a Syrian Kurdish militia in Afrin; Turkey reported deaths connected to its “Olive Branch” operation and said it wants the YPG to move east of the Euphrates and leave Manbij.

The passage describes how strong mentoring relationships help young people thrive academically and overcome school-related challenges. It notes that the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted student engagement and progress, with greater impacts on low-income students, students of color, students with learning disabilities, and marginalized youth, and reports low levels of student connection to adults and concerns about depression and anxiety during virtual learning.  

The passage summarizes research findings that mentoring programs and mentoring relationships support multiple educational outcomes, citing meta-analyses and syntheses showing positive impacts on academic achievement and related behaviors, attendance, and school engagement. The passage concludes that mentoring is an evidence-based practice with broad benefits but is inequitably distributed, with fewer mentoring relationships reported among youth of color and low-income youth, and calls for investment and policy changes to expand mentoring access and quality.

Xiaomi Redmi 5 goes on sale in India today at 12 pm on Amazon India, Mi.com, and Mi Home stores, starting at Rs 7,999. It is Xiaomi’s budget-friendly smartphone with the highest variant priced at Rs 10,999, and it is launched in three versions: 2GB+16GB (Rs 7,999), 3GB+32GB (Rs 8,999), and 4GB+64GB (Rs 10,999). The phone supports a microSD slot with up to 128GB expandable storage, uses a metal unibody design, and has a 5.7-inch 18:9 HD+ display (1440 x 720 pixels). Redmi 5 runs Android Nougat 7.1.2 with MIUI 9, offers 4G dual SIM and Bluetooth 4.2, and includes sensors such as proximity, gyroscope, accelerometer, vibration motor, and ambient light sensor. Xiaomi claims over 4 lakh units will be on sale, and users can use “Notify Me” and Mi account login to shorten checkout.

The passage is a message to the U.S. Senate transmitting the Secretary of State’s report and documents related to a proposed 1853 convention between the United States and Mexico for a transit way across the Isthmus of Tehuantepec. The author explains that multiple objections have deterred him from requesting Senate ratification. Key reasons cited include that the convention would bind the U.S. to a foreign government, guarantee a private company’s contract and the security of its invested capital for long periods, and require one year’s notice to withdraw protection even if traffic regulations conflict with the convention’s intent. The author also states that agreeing to this convention would disregard obligations in an 1850 convention with Great Britain that covers any interoceanic communication by the same route. He concludes that, after careful consideration, he will not ask the Senate to ratify the convention.

The passage describes the Colts’ game in which Indianapolis blew six leads, including a late play negated by a flag after a pass from Jacoby Brissett to Jack Doyle appeared to give them an 8-7 lead with 1:16 left. Adam Vinatieri tied the score with a 43-yard extra point in blizzard conditions, but the Colts lost 13-7 in overtime. The loss had lingering effects the next day, with Marlon Mack saying he still felt cold and concern about recovery time due to weather and “dead legs.” Coach Pagano said the conditions likely took more out of players, and running back Frank Gore planned to rest. The Colts were on a four-game losing streak, eliminated from playoff contention, and facing questions about Pagano’s future. The passage also includes injury updates: Kelly and Rashaan Melvin practiced Monday, with Kelly not yet cleared; Melvin worked with a cast, and Donte Moncrief is listed week to week with an injured ankle.

The passage describes a longitudinal evaluation of SARS-CoV-2–specific immune responses in residents of a 149-bed nursing home that began experiencing an outbreak in October 2020. As of December 5, 2021, nursing home COVID-19 outbreaks had caused 740,034 cases and 141,084 deaths among residents, and residents often mount immune responses within 15–30 days of diagnosis, though antibody kinetics beyond the early phase were unknown. The evaluation collected questionnaire data, nasal specimens for BinaxNOW and RT-PCR, and blood specimens for serology from October 25, 2020 through April 1, 2021, with additional monthly follow-up after the first four visits. During the evaluation period, willing participants received Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccination (considered fully vaccinated two weeks after the second dose).  

Among 11 participants (median age 74), most had detectable anti–SARS-CoV-2 antibodies after infection: 90% had Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA; 80% had IgM; and 1 participant did not mount binding antibodies. Pan-Ig and IgG titers rose and remained elevated after infection, while IgM and IgA declined around 31–60 days with some seroreversion. After vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, and 60% had detectable IgM. Antibody titers generally decreased after vaccination by 61–90 days, and previously infected participants showed higher Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers post-vaccination than pre-first dose. The study reports that no culturable virus was identified in respiratory specimens following antibody detection, and it highlights augmented antibody responses after vaccination, along with stated limitations including small sample size, incomplete timing of seroconversion assessment, and evaluation limited to Pfizer-BioNTech vaccination.

The passage discusses optimism about Oclaro (OCLR) despite some industry headwinds. It says Oclaro’s shares are reasonably priced, the company has less legacy business, and it is positioned in high-growth areas. Oclaro reported a 47% revenue increase, with margins rising and earnings per share growing 460%. Analysts reportedly do not expect further EPS expansion in fiscal 2018, with average estimates of $0.74 per share in 2018 and $0.82 in 2019. Demand is described as strong in 100G, with 100G making up 81% of Oclaro revenue and QSFP28 sales doubling sequentially, while legacy products declined sequentially. The passage states China demand is down 11% sequentially and may not recover soon, though management expects China’s fundamental demand drivers to remain intact and anticipates future demand shift to QSFP28 and growth tied to 25G and 100G for 5G front-haul. It also cites longer-term drivers like network capacity needs and discusses expectations for 100G growth into the next decade and modest 400G revenue generation. The passage provides valuation and financial details, including no debt, $258M in cash and short-term investments, and reported cash flow figures, and concludes that it expects Oclaro to avoid further decline absent broad market issues.

The appeal concerns whether Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners, Inc.’s proposed service mark “Thrift-D-Lux” for dry cleaning and pressing services is likely to cause confusion with Lever Brothers Company’s “Lux” trademark used since 1900 for soaps and related products. The Commissioner, through the Assistant Commissioner, affirmed an examiner’s decision dismissing Lever’s opposition. The court found that “Thrift-D-Lux” conveys “thrift” combined with “de luxe,” where “de luxe” is commonly used, and that restricting use of a public-domain term would not support Lever’s position. The court also found cited prior cases distinguishable and concluded that Lever did not provide sufficient evidence of likely confusion or damage, especially given the tenuous relationship between goods and the services at issue. The Commissioner’s decision was affirmed.

The passage describes the “outside day” (outside bar) as a two-bar price action pattern where the current day’s high is higher and low is lower than the previous day, and the second day’s open and/or close fall outside the first day’s open and/or close. It notes that outside bars can be hard to interpret because they rely on context, and that strategies using them should be backtested. An outside day indicates rising volatility, and if the second bar falls or rises, it may suggest further downward or upward movement. Outside days have four configurations, but only cases where the first and second bars move in opposite directions are called outside reversal patterns. The passage also says outside days can act as continuation or reversal signals depending on alignment with the prevailing trend. It concludes with backtesting results on SPY and other ETFs, reporting that average post-outside-day performance is near zero (~0.04% random baseline), that conditioning on the next day’s close produces a negative average (~-0.07%), and that another rule yields a positive average (~0.06%) but is “not tradable.” It states that the author found little use of outside days for day trading, while inviting suggestions for other opportunities.

The passage is a presidential inauguration address. The speaker thanks President Reagan, repeats George Washington’s oath, and prays that power be used to serve people. He describes a “new breeze” toward democracy, freedom, free markets, free speech, free elections, and free will, and says future progress depends on unity, diversity, and generosity. He urges Americans to value moral purpose over possessions and to focus on children, work, and compassion. The address outlines plans to address social problems such as homelessness, child hardship, addiction, and crime, while reducing a deficit through hard choices and prudent safety. It calls for new community engagement (“Thousand Points of Light”), cooperation between the Executive and Congress, budget balance, unity with other nations, and renewed bipartisanship after Vietnam. The speaker also emphasizes protecting peace, honoring commitments, strengthening alliances, and fighting drugs. He closes by expressing confidence in the future and framing the day as the start of a new chapter of unity, diversity, and generosity.

The passage summarizes a legal dispute in “Noble et al. versus The Thompson Oil Co.” concerning a $54,000 recognisance and whether a judgment obtained in New York foreign attachment proceedings barred recovery on that recognisance. The Thompson Oil Company assigned portions of a Pennsylvania judgment to Brown et al. in good faith for value, after which the assignors had no attachable interest. Garnishment in New York was issued against the garnishees before they had notice of the assignments, and the New York court entered judgment against the garnishees, which they later paid to the attaching creditors. The court held that the assignments were valid and valid everywhere, that attaching creditors could not set aside the assignment through foreign attachment, and that the New York court lacked jurisdiction over the assignees and their property. It also held that the assignees were not parties or privies to the New York suit and were not bound by it. The trial court’s judgment for the defendants in error was affirmed.

Aziz Ansari says he uses a flip phone, has no email, and avoids ChatGPT, which he criticizes for “outsourcing critical thinking” and making opinions more similar. He describes relying on human conversation when needed, such as calling his wife when lost, and hailing taxis instead of using an Uber app. Ansari says a low-tech lifestyle helps him keep a clear head for writing, while acknowledging that living offline is a privilege. The passage also mentions that other celebrities, including Chris Nolan, Dolly Parton, and Christopher Walken, have spoken about preferring analog or limited technology use.

The appeal challenges an order granting summary judgment dismissing a complaint brought by a plastic surgeon alleging a human rights violation under Executive Law § 296 after the New York State Department of Health revoked his medical license due to disability from adult ADD. The defendant argued the claim effectively sought judicial review of the license revocation, which had to be pursued via a CPLR article 78 proceeding under Public Health Law § 230-c (5) and was time barred. Supreme Court agreed, finding the essence of the action was review of the Administrative Review Board’s determination and was time barred. The appellate court affirmed, holding that the complaint’s allegations and requested relief necessarily depended on reversing the ARB’s decision, and that article 78 review is required in this context. The court rejected the surgeon’s argument that “may” in Public Health Law § 230-c (5) allows an independent action, noting it could circumvent the body of law governing judicial review of administrative proceedings. The court did not address res judicata and collateral estoppel because Supreme Court addressed them only in dicta.

The passage describes Northern Ireland’s health service as the only UK region not led by a minister, and notes it faces challenges such as an ageing population, complex care needs, staffing problems for GP practices, and rising drug costs. It says hospital waiting lists are longer than targets and that an additional £30m was allocated in March to ease pressure. It reports that 83,392 people were waiting over a year for a first hospital appointment, and that GPs warned in an open letter that practices were struggling to recruit and retain family doctors and needed urgent extra funding. It also cites crises including the recall of over 3,200 neurology patients and findings of horrific treatment at Dunmurry Manor care home, with registration conditions placed by the Regulation and Quality Improvement Authority (RQIA). The passage further mentions criticism of the RQIA by Commissioner Eddie Lynch, RQIA’s denial of failing its duty, and recommendations by international expert Rafael Bengoa in 2016 to transform the service, with no health minister in post to lead reforms since the collapse of Stormont in January 2017.

Nassau County Court jurors acquitted 18-year-old Jasmine Copeland of all charges in the Nov. 1, 2014 killing of 17-year-old Abbigale Thomas. Jurors deliberated for about three hours and found her not guilty of manslaughter and other charges, including gang assault. Copeland’s attorney said Copeland had no contact with Thomas and argued that the knife was carried but not used. Prosecutors said they respect the verdict and had argued in trial that Copeland stabbed Thomas in the back with a steak knife during a brawl that began with taunts on social media and escalated to a confrontation at Copeland’s home.

The lecture is a wrap-up on stochastic methods, focusing on evaluating multidimensional integrals using weighting factors in Bayesian analysis and Monte Carlo. Green explains that Metropolis Monte Carlo requires choosing a step size, with too-large steps causing many rejected transitions and repeated states, and too-small steps causing poor space coverage; adaptive methods aim for an appropriate acceptance probability. He emphasizes the need for sufficient sampling across the whole physically accessible region and performing reasonableness checks using approximate known answers. He then discusses Monte Carlo accuracy scaling (about \(1/\sqrt{n}\)) and the benefit of reducing problem dimensionality by removing degrees of freedom.  

He describes kinetic Monte Carlo for non-stationary probability distributions defined by differential equations, using a catalyst-surface model with many possible site configurations (e.g., \(4^{100}\) states) where storing or enumerating the full state space is infeasible. Instead, trajectories are generated (e.g., via Gillespie), requiring random numbers and careful computation of averages on the fly, including sampling initial conditions (e.g., Poisson-distributed counts). He outlines strategies to speed up kinetic Monte Carlo, such as simplifying fast processes, using approximations like infinitely fast diffusion or accelerated reaction times, and removing processes that occur on timescales beyond practical simulation.  

Finally, he contrasts stochastic methods with molecular dynamics, which solves Newton’s equations (often with thermostats) to model time-dependent behavior on physical timescales, but is limited by small time steps and challenges with long-timescale equilibrations. He concludes by stressing that different methods fit different problems and warns against using an incorrect tool.

The speakers discuss the difficulty of having two-goal deficits in the last three games and the need to correct many aspects of their game to get better starts. Dwight King describes taking time off for physical recovery and focusing on preparation, while also emphasizing the importance of getting traffic in front of the net and playing within goalie-protection rules. Marian Gaborik says it will be special to return to the Garden after being traded, noting the fans and the team’s energy, and that coaching changes and team balance have helped the opponent. Both mention that home ice and momentum are important in playoff hockey, and they aim to avoid having to come back from two-goal deficits again.

Zeta Global, a marketing tech company led by David Steinberg, is making its biggest-ever acquisition by agreeing to buy Marigold’s enterprise software business for $325 million. The deal includes Marigold’s Loyalty brand, Cheetah Digital and Sailthru email platforms, and the Selligent marketing automation platform, while Marigold’s small and midsize-focused business will continue operating with products including Campaign Monitor, Emma, and Vuture. Zeta says the acquisition will expand its Fortune 500 customer base and broaden its footprint in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Zeta expects Marigold will bolster its bottom line in the first year after the deal closes, and says it will pay $100 million in cash and $100 million in shares up front, with the remainder paid via a seller note after closing.

The passage describes technology for detecting neoplasia, particularly premalignant and malignant gastric neoplasms such as gastric cancer, using DNA methylation markers. It explains background on gastric cancer incidence and difficulty of cure, and discusses DNA methylation at CpG island sites as a potential stable biomarker mechanism. The passage outlines methods for identifying and validating differentially methylated regions (DMRs) using approaches such as Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS), and reports discovery and optimization of marker sets, including 10 optimal stomach cancer markers, 30 optimal stomach cancer markers, and 12 optimal gastric cancer markers for plasma. It further describes methods for screening by assaying methylation state in samples (e.g., gastric tissue, stool, plasma), comparing to controls, optionally calculating sensitivity/specificity and statistical measures, and identifying subjects with neoplasia when methylation differs. The passage also covers related compositions and kit components, and systems/software for analyzing methylation data and generating outputs such as cancer-associated alerts or risk values, using computer-based operations and databases.

The passage says that 26 hazardous rocket bodies have been left in low-Earth orbit over the last 21 months, adding to collision risks with growing satellite constellations. A paper by Darren McKnight and coauthors identifies 50 particularly concerning debris objects, mostly dead rockets deposited before 2000, and notes that collisions at orbital speeds can create cascading debris (Kessler Syndrome). The paper estimates that removing all 50 would cut overall debris-generating potential in low-Earth orbit by 50%, while removing the top 10 would cut it by 30%. It also states that since January 1, 2024, 26 abandoned rocket bodies will remain in orbit for more than 25 years, and discusses policies and trends involving different countries’ rocket-stage disposal. The passage further highlights that China’s focus on megaconstellations may lead to more long-lived rocket bodies if upper stages are left in orbit, and it mentions research and debate over active debris removal, including example initiatives by ESA, Japan, and Astroscale.

In re Buchanan concerns a petitioner tried in New York City for the murder of his wife by poison. After a guilty verdict and denial of a new trial motion, petitioner was sentenced to death and appealed, but the Court of Appeals affirmed his conviction. Petitioner then sought a writ of error to the U.S. Supreme Court, alleging violations of due process and that he was not tried by an impartial jury in the proper district. His principal federal-based claim involved juror Paradise becoming mentally and physically incapacitated during deliberations, allegedly causing an improper verdict. The Court of Appeals found no warrant to refuse the verdict based on the incident, and held that issues regarding juror separation and the juror’s capacity were properly discretionary and based on conflicting expert testimony. The U.S. Supreme Court concluded that the juror’s physical and mental condition and competency to return a verdict were questions of fact that it could not review on writ of error from a state court. The application was denied.

Industrial relations between East Dunbartonshire Council and unions show no signs of improving, with three unions warning that refuse collections will be affected this month. The GMB, Unison, and Unite plan strike action at specified sites from Thursday, July 12, through Sunday, July 15, alongside ongoing “action short of strike” including working to rule and no overtime. Council leaders said the further strike notice is disappointing and raises concerns about unions’ commitment to resolving the dispute through discussion, while the council continues assessing service impacts and advising residents of disruption. Meetings with unions are planned in coming weeks, and the council reports that four days of industrial action last month caused widespread disruption. UNISON’s Simon Macfarlane said the council’s failure to change employees’ terms and conditions could lead to further action.

Cerebras said on Friday it is withdrawing its plans for an IPO, according to an SEC filing stating it does not intend to conduct the proposed offering “at this time.” The company said it still hopes to go public as soon as possible and provided no reason for the withdrawal. The announcement follows the company’s report earlier this week that it raised $1.1 billion in new funding at an $8.1 billion valuation, and it comes just over a year after it filed its IPO prospectus. Cerebras also said the original prospectus was out of date, and that the government shutdown did not factor into the decision.

A UN World Water Development Report 2018 highlights the importance of nature-based solutions to address global water challenges, citing five billion people at risk of poor water access by 2050. The report provides examples such as China’s rainwater recycling, India’s forest regeneration, and Ukraine’s artificial wetlands, and includes a case study of Tarun Bharat Sangh in Rajasthan that supported landscape-scale restoration and led to increased forest cover, higher groundwater levels, and improved cropland productivity. It also describes community-led efforts involving small-scale water harvesting and regeneration in upper catchments, including estimated groundwater gains and increases in productive farmland and forest cover. The report notes rising global water demand, the goals of SDG 6, projected increases in potentially water-scarce populations, and that instruments beyond reservoirs and irrigation infrastructure are needed, including China’s Sponge City project aiming to recycle 70% of rainwater.

The passage is a WIRED guide to choosing among Google Pixel phones and highlights software features, Pixel-exclusive tips, and recommended accessories and cases. It compares the Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro/Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, and guidance on buying previous-generation Pixels, including pricing and update/support timelines. It details key hardware differences such as display brightness, chipsets, camera systems (including Pixel 10’s 5X zoom and Pixel 10 Pro models’ Pro Res Zoom and Video Boost), battery life, storage technologies, and charging (Qi2 and Pixelsnap with magnets). It also covers US-specific differences like eSIM-only Pixel 10 models and Pro subscription features, plus services like Pixel Care+ and Pixel Care+. The latter part lists Pixel-exclusive software features for calls, photos, translation, accessibility, security, and device safety, and recommends official and third-party cases and other accessories certified for Pixelsnap/Qi2.

The passage describes Ryan ToysReview, a YouTube channel run by a six-year-old named Ryan who opens and plays with toys for millions of children worldwide. It says Ryan’s parents began recording videos when he was three, and his channel became highly profitable, with Forbes ranking him eighth among highest-paid YouTube entrepreneurs and reporting $11 million in revenue between June 1, 2016, and June 1, 2017. The channel grew from a simple 15-minute Lego Duplo train video and expanded rapidly after a viral video reviewing “hundred toys at once.” Ryan’s videos are described as unbranded in most cases, with his family paying for many toys and donating most toys to charity after reviews. The passage also notes high view counts, frequent “SURPRISE” themed titles, regular daily posting, and comments from parents and children about Ryan’s impact on their children’s interests and behavior.

The passage describes AGESA™ interface rules, error reporting behavior, key status code meanings, and the host/AGESA call mechanisms. It explains that AGESA interface calls return control to the host, with actions indicated by error class while the host implements them, and it defines returned status codes such as success/no issue and various warning/error/critical/fatal conditions. It outlines concepts like CallOuts (host BIOS callbacks), the Bridge as the call entry point from system BIOS into AGESA software, and the Dispatcher as the AGESA entry point that invokes published functions, plus the Router as the call-out re-entry point to the host. The passage also covers UEFI execution staging, binary module versus source integration build approaches, and host environment requirements for stack setup and standard header handling, along with high-level descriptions of PEI/DXE drivers, memory initialization steps, and various platform configuration options.

Michael Cohen removed “personal attorney to President Donald J. Trump” from his Twitter biography but kept the same description on his LinkedIn page and still linked to it. The change came days after he spoke to ABC News about his legal situation, including his admission that he facilitated a hush payment to Stormy Daniels and claims that Trump reimbursed him. CNN reports that after Trump’s election victory, Cohen pitched himself to major companies as an access point to Trump. In the ABC interview, Cohen said he prioritizes his family and country over loyalty to Trump and said he respects the FBI, describing interactions with agents during searches of his home and hotel room.

The court addressed plaintiffs’ motion for class certification in *Lewis v. Bayer AG* arising from ingestion of Baycol (Cerivastatin). Plaintiffs proposed four classes (two medical monitoring classes, and two personal injury/unjust enrichment classes), but the court found the prerequisites for certification under Pa.R.C.P. 1702 were not satisfied for Classes II, III, and IV because individual questions predominated and, for nationwide classes, differing state laws created conflicts.  

The court concluded only Class I satisfied commonality, typicality, adequacy of representation, and the fair and efficient adjudication requirements for a statewide medical monitoring class. Class I was certified for Pennsylvania persons who were prescribed and ingested Baycol and who have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart disease. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed as class representatives, and plaintiffs’ counsel were appointed as class counsel. Certification was denied for all other classes, and the parties were ordered to submit proposals for notice within 30 days.

The speaker discusses Peter’s aggressive system, saying it took about one to two months to figure out but became effective once players learned it. They say the team is now in better shape and playing a successful, pressure-focused system that requires being in great condition. They describe Peter as competitive, tenacious with the puck, and a “jack of all trades” who does many things well, while also working hard and making linemates better. The speaker notes limited time off due to scheduling and travel, and expects the finals to be exciting without team “letdowns,” emphasizing the need for consistent play. They stress defending well without engaging in a “track meet,” creating chances through getting pucks to the net, using bigger bodies in front to distract opponents, and relying on gritty goals rather than “pretty” plays. They describe strong respect for Peter’s approach and leadership and say he is among the best players in the world.

The passage describes wireless communication methods and apparatuses for downlink assignments for downlink control channels. It states the application is a continuation of earlier U.S. patent applications and relates to downlink control channel assignments in networks where downlink data is received on a downlink channel. The disclosed embodiments include monitoring first and second downlink control channel candidates associated with different control resource sets, receiving downlink assignments, determining downlink data channel allocations, identifying demodulation reference signal symbol locations based on the assignments and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing symbols, and decoding the downlink data channels. It also describes receiving indications of associated search spaces and determining corresponding downlink control channel monitoring occasions, including using subsets of monitoring occasions based on different control resource sets and quasi-collocation relationships. The passage further provides general apparatus descriptions for remote units and network units, and includes additional detailed discussion of related signaling, monitoring occasion determination, and decoding/acknowledgment behavior, culminating in flow chart descriptions of the methods.

The speaker says they are not frustrated because the series is not over and they are playing better with chances. They note they expected the series to be difficult against a great team, and say they will keep doing the same things. They praise Marc as a strong goalie who has proven himself and believe he will do well tomorrow. The speaker also says both goalies are dedicated and emotionally invested in winning, acknowledging some frustration may arise from wanting to get the first win and avoid being in a “big hole.” They believe playing at home with different matchups and lineups will make things easier and help carry momentum forward.

The passage explains how and when to perform a soccer “defensive switch.” If the first defender is beaten, the second defender (support/cover) calls for the switch, moves to take on the ball carrier, and the first defender sprints to cover the opponent the second defender was marking, effectively exchanging positions. The support defender should start behind and to the inside of the field, be goalside and properly goalside/stance to react, block the direct path to goal, influence the dribbler to go toward the sideline, and maintain appropriate distance without overrunning. Because the second defender is facing away from the first, the second defender must announce arrival (e.g., “support,” “you have help”). The passage further describes how the support defender communicates defensive instructions to manage the attacker by jockeying/delaying/containing, or by calling to challenge/tackle, and notes that switches often follow a crossing pattern initiated by the second defender. It provides coaching instructions and practice progressions for demonstrating positioning, oral communication, switching scenarios (down the sideline, outside, inside from the sideline, and alternative midfield switches), and “switch back/return” after play ends so defenders return to original responsibilities. It also notes defensive switches can occur without a dribbler, such as when an opponent sprints past and needs to be picked up, emphasizing correct “angle of recovery” by the first defender.

The passage says the Air Force’s advancement in cyber depends on rapid continuous change and openness to new ideas in organization, procurement, and operations. It describes Air Force cross-training between active-duty cyber defense and offensive specialists and suggests that the structure and flexibility of Air National Guard (ANG) cyber units may inform the evolution of all cyber forces. It profiles Tech. Sgt. Kyle Hanslovan of the Maryland ANG’s 175th Cyberspace Operations Group (175th COG), noting his military and civilian cyber background and his view that diverse civilian experience improves readiness for offensive operations. It outlines that the 175th COG grew from a 35-Airmen detachment to more than 200 Airmen across four squadrons and mentions a range of cyber missions and support activities. It also highlights the ANG’s role in providing continuously updated tools and tactics, emphasizing transparency on operations floors (including real-time attack information displayed on a Norse attack map) and the value of combining private-sector experience with Air Force training. Leaders discuss challenges in training and retaining cyber talent, the need to attract and keep full-time cyber expertise, and the importance of innovative approaches such as the National Guard’s Innovations Program.

The passage describes how IDEA provides services for students with disabilities and how families can contest alleged IDEA violations through special education due process hearings facilitated by Pennsylvania’s Office for Dispute Resolution (ODR). It explains that hearing officers review evidence and issue written decisions with remedies that must be followed. ODR also notes limits in its annual reporting, including how it categorizes ruling outcomes based on the hearing officer’s judgment. The passage outlines COVID-19–related IDEA compliance issues, including pandemic shutdowns, requirements for LEAs to continue providing FAPE with adjustments, and continuing procedural notice obligations. It states Pennsylvania was among the most litigious states in IDEA compliance disputes before and during the pandemic, and highlights that city LEAs—particularly Philadelphia—had frequent hearing activity. The study aims to examine whether city Pennsylvania LEAs were involved in more hearings after COVID-19, whether there is a significant relationship between ruling outcomes and the pandemic, and what remedies city LEAs were required to provide after the pandemic. It uses an ex-post facto design analyzing 323 ODR-published hearing officer decisions (March 16, 2018–March 15, 2022) involving city LEAs, dividing decisions into pre- and post-COVID groups using March 16, 2020 as the cutoff. It plans to use frequency distributions for hearing counts, a chi-square test for ruling outcome relationships, and review remedy types (IEEs, compensatory education, and financial reimbursements) in the post-COVID sample.

The passage reports that Apple may debut a “blush gold” iPhone 8 at its September keynote. It describes this as a new name for a previously rumored copper gold iPhone 8, and says the phone is reported to have an edge-to-edge screen, no home button, and wireless charging. A leak from Twitter user Benjamin Geskin also claims storage options of 64GB and 128GB, and notes that the internal Foxconn name is “Blush Gold,” leaving open the possibility of other names. The passage says the details will be confirmed at Apple’s fall keynote in September.

The report values the global Pyridine market at USD XX million in 2016 and projects it to reach USD XX million by the end of 2022, growing at a CAGR of XX% from 2016 to 2022. It segments the market by regions (United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India), by product type (Chemical Synthesized Pyridine and Coal Tar Extracted Pyridine), and by applications/end users (Agrochemicals, Pharmaceuticals, and “Chemical Synthesis”). It also covers global competition among listed top manufacturers, including BASF, Bayer, Dow Chemical Company, DuPont, Mitsubishi Chemical, Lonza, Vertellus, Royal DSM, Sanonda, Jubiliant Life Sciences, Koei Chemical, Nippon Steel & Sumikin Chemical, Sinopec Qilu Petrochemical, Shandong Luba Chemical, and Xinxiang Hengji Chemical, with details such as sales volume, price, revenue, and market share.

The lecture discusses culminating results in model-free optimal control, comparing policy gradient methods and value-function-based methods. Policy gradient methods can scale well to high-dimensional systems but are local searches with typically high variance, requiring many trials to converge. Convergence for policy gradient is described as virtually guaranteed due to stochastic gradient descent in the policy parameters, motivating their use over value methods, which can diverge or oscillate when the policy changes with function approximation.

Value methods are described as efficient and often faster when they work, but they provide weaker guarantees because small changes in the value function can cause large, destabilizing changes in the policy. To combine strengths, the lecture introduces actor-critic methods, which represent both a policy (actor) and a value estimate (critic). It emphasizes a two-timescale approach where the policy changes more slowly than the value function-derived greedy policy. The lecture explains how critic estimates can reduce variance in policy-gradient updates while preserving convergence properties, provided the value estimate subtraction is uncorrelated with the added noise.

A case study from the speaker’s thesis describes applying actor-critic learning to a walking robot (“Toddler”), using return maps and an online stochastic gradient descent approach updated about once per footstep. The robot learns to walk and recover from disturbances quickly (minutes), using a simplified value function to speed convergence and improve robustness. The lecture concludes by suggesting actor-critic algorithms as a practical choice for model-free optimization and references related research papers.

The passage describes global air pollution rankings based on WHO PM 2.5 measurements in urban locations. It states that Delhi has an average PM 2.5 concentration of 150 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with London’s 16. WHO tracks air quality at 1,622 locations across 92 countries, but only in urban areas, so country rankings reflect city pollution rather than rural regions. Data from aqicn.org (using 2014 WHO data) weights PM 2.5 averages by each city’s population and provides additional figures such as PM10. Pakistan is listed as having the most polluted urban areas on average (115.7), followed by Qatar (92.4) and Afghanistan (86); the UK ranks 21st out of 92. Australia has the least polluted urban areas, followed by Brunei and New Zealand.

Kathrine Clark appeals pro se from a Chatham County Superior Court order granting Ricky G. Rau’s petition to modify custody and child support. The record contains no transcript of the relevant hearing, and Clark’s appellate brief does not comply with required briefing rules, offering no statement of facts, record citations, or numbered enumerations of error with supporting argument and authority. The appellate court therefore presumes the regularity of the trial proceedings, assumes sufficient evidence supported the trial court’s findings in the absence of a transcript, and affirms the judgment. The court also rejects the dissent’s view that the custody order is facially deficient for not verbatim reciting the “best interest of the child” standard.

Under a May trade deal, China began exporting cooked poultry meat to the United States, while the United States agreed to accept U.S. beef and liquefied natural gas in exchange. The passage says imports are likely limited to cooked poultry due to concerns about avian influenza risks from raw poultry, including the possibility of spread to U.S. birds and humans. It states that properly cooked poultry poses no food safety risk from viruses or bacteria, but risks arise if poultry is undercooked or cross-contaminates other foods, such as with salmonella and campylobacter. It also raises concerns about contaminants, including antibiotic residues from inappropriate antibiotic use and heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic), and notes that U.S. rules and testing programs are more robust than China’s, with China lacking publicly available data and facing limited transparency. U.S. inspectors would rely on USDA-equivalence testing and ongoing foreign government certification and regular on-site audits, including annual plant audits. The passage says cooked poultry is excluded from country-of-origin labeling for consumers and restaurants, so it may not be clear to U.S. buyers where the meat was grown and processed.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture features, including support for FLUX.dev image generation at different precisions, and enhancements to ray tracing through upgraded RT Cores and Mega Geometry. It explains how Mega Geometry improves level-of-detail ray tracing using cluster-based BVH construction (CLAS) and PTLAS to reduce TLAS rebuild costs. It also covers Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for faster ray intersection with strand-like primitives, Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 for improved GPU thread utilization, and the AI Management Processor (AMP) for scheduling GPU contexts to reduce CPU bottlenecks and improve responsiveness. The passage further outlines Blackwell video/display updates (hardware 4:2:2 encode/decode, NVENC/NVDEC improvements, and DisplayPort 2.1b), power-efficiency features for Max-Q (advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep), and DLSS 4 updates using Multi Frame Generation and transformer-based models for super resolution, ray reconstruction, and anti-aliasing. It concludes with an overview of neural shaders (e.g., Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces) and provides hardware and product spec information for Blackwell GPU variants such as GB202 (RTX 5090) and GB203 (RTX 5080, 5070 Ti).

The passage discusses how traders and investors may make money in a bear market. It states that a bear market is when the market is below its 200-day moving average, occurs about twice a year on average, and lasts about 25 trading days, with the stock market spending about 30% of its time in such conditions. It advises being prepared and sticking to a backtested trading plan, including trading both long and short directions. It highlights cognitive mistakes such as buying high and selling low, using an example where investor returns lagged fund performance due to buying after strong runs and selling near bottoms. The passage claims short strategies often start working in bear markets and that long trades can also improve, supported by backtests described for strategies trading S&P 500 (SPY) and QQQ. For long-term investors, it recommends continuing to invest, noting that stocks have historically served as an inflation hedge with positive real returns. It concludes that bear markets should be treated as an opportunity, with emphasis on discipline and avoiding fear-driven deviations from the plan.

The passage describes design considerations for a UC1825B-SP push-pull converter, including calculating diode voltage stress and selecting a 60 V-rated UC1825-SP diode, choosing main switching MOSFET voltage ratings about 2.5–3× the input voltage due to stress when switches are off, and determining output capacitance (about 1145 µF) and additional filtering to reduce voltage ripple using an output inductor (500 nH) and damping resistor (0.5 Ω). It also outlines sense resistor use for ripple current sensing and shutdown when peak current exceeds a current limit, and provides layout guidance to reduce EMI and improve operation, such as keeping traces short, placing key components close, using ground planes, and bypassing VCC and VREF.

The passage explains that strength training (weight, resistance, or muscle training) offers fitness benefits but injury can occur if correct technique is not used and if warming up and cooling down are not done properly. It describes common strength-training injuries and prevention and management steps, including rotator cuff injuries (often linked to repetitive overhead motions), hamstring injuries (often caused by sudden powerful movements), herniated discs (from sudden extreme or repetitive poor movement during weightlifting), tendonitis (from minor stress and repetitive motions or sudden impact), and tennis elbow/golfer’s elbow (from repetitive wrist and arm movements). Tips include using good form, warming up and cooling down, working within limitations, gradually increasing workout intensity, maintaining good posture, adjusting workouts for shoulder discomfort, stretching and warming up properly, not ignoring pain, resting, and seeking medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen. The passage notes that warming up increases heart rate and blood flow to prepare muscles and help prevent injury, and includes additional suggestions such as light jogging and dynamic full-range movements for warm-ups, and gentle exercise afterward for certain injuries. It also mentions general recovery support like eating a good diet, staying hydrated, and using ice, compression, and elevation for initial treatment of many sport-related injuries.

The passage argues that it is disrespectful for celebrities to refuse to perform at Donald Trump’s presidential inauguration. It mentions a list from The Daily Caller of eight celebrities who “shot Trump down,” and states that performers such as Jackie Evancho, the Radio City Rockettes, and the Mormon Tabernacle Choir will attend, along with military, police, first responders, and supporters. It also reports that Bristol Palin called boycotting celebrities “sissies” and criticizes “elitist snobs” who avoided Trump after he became a Republican president.

Human Rights Watch reports that desperate Syrian refugees fleeing violence in north-west Syria are being shot at and beaten at the Turkish border, with some accounts of Turkish border guards shooting refugees, detaining asylum seekers, and denying medical assistance. HRW also cites a case where a woman gave birth while trying to cross but was sent back to Syria with her child without medical help. The Turkish border is closed to Syrian refugees except for critical medical cases. The reports come amid increased violence in north-west Syria, including Syrian government advances and warplane attacks in multiple provinces, with civilian deaths reported by monitoring groups and rescue agencies. International concern is rising over 400,000 people in besieged eastern Ghouta due to acute food and medicine shortages and the UN’s description of the worst malnutrition of the war.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 13, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing the final offer consideration for its offer to exchange all outstanding shares of Maxwell Technologies, Inc. common stock for Tesla common stock. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes opinions regarding material U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Offer and subsequent merger as Exhibits 8.1 and 8.2.

Princeton, NJ, April 17, 2017—Value in Health (ISPOR) published research stating that testing for variants in 7 cancer-associated genes instead of the usual BRCA1/2 testing, followed by risk-reduction management, could cost-effectively improve life expectancy for women at risk of hereditary breast cancer. Using hypothetical cohorts and a decision-analytic model, the study compared a next-generation 7-gene strategy (BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, PTEN, CDH1, STK11, PALB2) with the BRCA1/2 strategy. In base-case scenarios, ICERs for the 7-gene strategy versus BRCA1/2 were $42,067 and $23,734 per life-year gained (and $69,920 and $48,328 per quality-adjusted life-year gained) for 50- and 40-year-olds, respectively. The study said these ICER levels would be considered cost effective under World Health Organization guidelines.

Crime scene investigators are examining a murder at a Plantation duplex. Police say Eric Robinson, 46, was arrested and charged with murdering his roommate and attempting to hide the body in a garbage dumpster. Neighbors expressed disbelief, saying Robinson was a “nice guy,” and described frequent conflicts involving a woman who lived there. Police said Robinson had recently been arrested for domestic violence and strangulation in June, for cocaine possession in August, and was released from jail on October 3; neighbors said he returned, beat the woman, and then killed his roommate. Police say Robinson took the body and dumped it behind a busy shopping center near Nob Hill Road and Cleary Blvd. The victim’s name is being withheld until his family is notified.

The passage describes “SOS Switching” as an integral part of the SOS Pressure Defense system, using “Screen-Over-Switch” terms for switching action. It says automatic switching and contact switching reduce hesitation, limit quick catches and jump shots off screens, disrupt offensive screening flow, and can reduce fouls while forcing turnovers and rushed or bad shots. It outlines off-ball switching techniques (contact switching and snuggle pass denial) for down screens, back screens, and a “Hi-Lo Switch Rule” on base screens, and it notes on-ball switching approaches above the free-throw line (aggressive contact switching) and below it (aggressive trapping near base or corner checkpoints). It also provides step-by-step actions for on-ball scenarios above and below the free-throw line extended.

The device includes SmartReflex modules to reduce power consumption in each Core Logic Voltage Domain by having the host processor adjust domain supply voltages using external variable-voltage regulators based on process, temperature, and desired performance. SmartReflex uses two main techniques: Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling (DVFS), which changes Operating Performance Points (OPPs) in real time without a reset, and Adaptive Voltage Scaling (AVS), which continuously adjusts supply voltages within each OPP’s voltage range. Each Core Logic Voltage Domain can operate independently at selected OPPs defined by maximum module frequencies and associated supply voltage ranges, with power-performance tradeoffs. The passage also describes SRAM power-down behavior, power supply sequencing requirements across multiple supply groups, and system reset types and their effects, including Power-on Reset (POR) and warm reset sequences. It further covers clocking inputs and PLL/clocking architecture, supported reset isolation features, and general reset/pin behaviors during reset.

The passage describes a continuation patent and several example figures for storage systems, big data analytics pipelines, and artificial intelligence/machine learning infrastructure. It details a clustered, peer-to-peer storage architecture using multiple storage nodes and non-volatile solid-state storage units, with erasure coding, redundant metadata, and distributed control via “authorities” that manage data placement and consistency. It explains how data is sharded into stripes, mapped through authority identifiers and segment/indirection mechanisms, and reconstructed when nodes become unavailable via proactive rebuilds. Hardware and software layers are outlined, including storage nodes within chassis, interconnects and power buses, controllers, fast-write NVRAM backed by flash using energy reserves, and elasticity where stateless authorities migrate across blades to balance load and maintain concurrency. The passage also outlines example storage service communication with clients and possible integration with cloud services providers.

The South Shore neighborhood is closer to getting a grocery store in a former Dominick’s location after Shop & Save Market signed a letter of intent to open a new store at Jeffery Plaza, 2101 E. 71st St. The owner confirmed the letter but said the deal is not finalized, with a possible opening in 18 to 24 months if it progresses. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said details are still being finalized and that more than $10 million in city tax increment financing would be used, and the store may not match Dominick’s original footprint. The site is the last vacant former Dominick’s within city limits, and South Shore has been classified as a food desert since Dominick’s closed in 2014. The city had issued a request for proposals for the plaza, emphasizing the goal of a grocery store to anchor it and noting eminent domain could be used if necessary. Shop & Save hopes to buy the entire plaza, keep existing tenants, and attract others, and the owner said the former store building requires major construction.

Whitworth University, a private Christian institution in Spokane, Wash., says it will reduce its annual tuition starting next fall from $54,000 to $26,900 and base merit discounts solely on GPA using a publicly available scale. The change is intended to provide clearer information about college costs earlier in the application process, not to address enrollment declines, which began reversing in 2023. The passage describes how most students do not pay the full “sticker price” due to grants and scholarships, but families may not be aware of discounts. It also notes that tuition “resets” have shown mixed research results, potentially increasing the number of Pell-eligible students, while economists say some colleges may avoid resets because lower prices can signal inferior quality and because institutions’ incentives resemble a “prisoner’s dilemma.” Whitworth reports overwhelmingly positive feedback from parents since the announcement.

A study by Nigel Raine of the University of Guelph reports that the widely used pesticide thiamethoxam increases the risk of bumblebee colony extinction. Raine found that queens exposed to the pesticide were 26% less likely to lay eggs to start a colony, reducing new colony formation by more than a quarter. The results were published in *Nature Ecology & Evolution*, and modelling suggested the pesticide could significantly affect population persistence and increase extinction risk. The passage also notes that bee populations are declining worldwide and that neonicotinoids are among factors linked to these declines, with Ontario restricting their use and Europe imposing a moratorium.

Mediclinic International’s share price rose ahead of the Easter long weekend after the market responded well to slightly improved prospects for its Middle East operations. CEO Danie Meintjes said the company’s Switzerland and southern Africa platforms and its Dubai-based businesses met expectations for the year to March, while Abu Dhabi faced ongoing difficulties due to regulatory change and other challenges. Mediclinic aimed to resolve issues in Abu Dhabi, stabilise Middle East performance, and expected improvement in the year ahead, with Middle East revenue down 8%, Dubai performing well and Abu Dhabi lagging.

A court heard that Tyler Denton was stabbed to death by her housemate Redvers Bickley after he became angry when she slighted him at her birthday party. The night began with a girls’ night in, but after the girls decided to go out, Bickley accessed them on Tyler’s iPad. When they returned, they found blood and Bickley attacked Cody and then Shannen, with Shannen seeking help and Bickley allegedly stabbing her again while she pretended to be dead. Their father, Paul Denton, rushed to the scene and was also attacked. Tyler died from a cut to an artery in the neck, while Paul and the sisters later recovered from serious injuries. Bickley admitted killing Tyler but denied murder and attempting to murder the others; the trial continues and is expected to last six days.

The five English clubs—Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham, and Chelsea—qualified for the Champions League knockout stages and will learn their last-16 opponents in a draw in Nyon, Switzerland. Chelsea, drawn against only PSG, Barcelona, or Besiktas, finished second behind Roma and cannot face Premier League rivals. Bayern Munich and Juventus are major threats for the remaining English clubs, while Real Madrid could face United, City, or Liverpool; Tottenham have avoided Real for now. PSG are bookmakers’ favourites, and the Europa League last-32 draw follows an hour later, where Arsenal could face Celtic.

The passage is a collection of biotech news items and headlines. It mentions European officials working to finalize a major overhaul of EU pharmaceutical policies to improve access to medicines and keep the continent attractive to drugmakers. It also references multiple regulatory and research updates, including studies tied to FDA discussions for an antibody treatment related to Covid-19 prevention with results expected mid-2026, and other drug or study mentions including telehealth’s impact on the drug market and various U.S. policy and drug development updates.

The passage describes Enron’s rise and fall, focusing on how its culture and business practices contributed to both its success and its later problems. It recounts Enron’s transformation into a trading company under Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay, including rapid growth, aggressive market-building, and the use of strategies such as “Gas Bank,” heavy trading, and mark-to-market accounting. It also details how Enron’s internal culture became more ruthless over time, including forced ranking, high turnover, paranoia, and restricted communication. The narrative then shifts to Enron’s decline after Skilling became CEO in February 2001, including stock drops, negative media coverage related to California energy deregulation, setbacks in telecommunications, and questions about accounting and business prospects. The passage concludes with leadership changes, Lay’s statements about a need for a kinder, gentler Enron with innovation closer to its core, and Skilling’s resignation and later optimism about a “second wave” of technology.

Tony Robinson has agreed to be patron of the John Cracknell Youth Enterprise Bank in Yorkshire. The bank serves young people in Hull, the East Riding and Malton, Norton on Derwent, Pickering, and Scarborough, and offers grants of up to £1,000 for individuals or groups needing finance for their ideas. Managed by trustees and linked to the Hull Youth Enterprise Partnership, it has helped more than 400 young people purchase items such as computers, business stationery, chocolate making equipment, and dance costumes. Robinson, born in Hull, has championed small businesses for over 30 years and founded Enterprise Rockers CIC in 2012 to promote and support micro-businesses.

The passage contains a hockey-related discussion where Coach Deboer and others talk about improved defensive awareness in the D zone, earlier issues giving opponents too much room, and how games have been close with several one-goal outcomes. They express belief in the team, noting the players’ experience of how quickly momentum can change, and mention past reminders from other coaches and humorous moments. They also discuss key responsibility expected from “Pav,” optimism about road performance, and the need to be ready for a difficult series.

An engineering graduate, Ankit from Dhakoli village, killed Sheelu, 23, and her cousin Shivani at their residence in Bahpur village in Bulandshahr district after Sheelu rejected his marriage proposal. The SSP said Ankit proposed on Thursday, strangulated Sheelu to death, killed Shivani using a motorcycle clutch wire after she witnessed the incident, then set the bodies on fire after taking petrol from his motorbike. Police said the case was solved in under 24 hours, they put Ankit’s and other suspects’ mobile phones under surveillance, and the investigation showed Ankit was at the residence on the day of the killings; he later admitted to the killings.

The passage explains that lithium-ion batteries face persistent safety issues and limited capacity, motivating the search for solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). It describes why oxide-based SSEs are promising due to higher chemical and thermal stability, but notes their ionic conductivities are generally lower than sulfides, requiring discovery of novel oxide SSEs. Computational methods can accelerate SSE discovery, but template-based data-driven approaches cannot find new structural prototypes; instead, crystal structure prediction is needed. However, predicting oxide SSE structures is challenging because they often involve complex, large unit cells and multicomponent compositions, making conventional methods costly. The passage introduces TOPIC (TOpology-constrained Prediction of Inorganic Crystals), a crystal structure prediction algorithm that generates candidate oxide SSE structures under corner-sharing (CS) bond topology constraints. TOPIC is validated by reproducing known oxide structures and previously unreported polymorphs, including identifying a new LiTa2PO8 polymorph and correctly reproducing LLZO with algorithm modifications. Using TOPIC with a pretrained machine-learning interatomic potential (SevenNet-0) and DFT validation, the authors screen quaternary oxide compositions using a “Li ratio” descriptor and identify 92 candidate materials, then validate 15 with room-temperature ionic conductivity above 0.1 mS cm−1. The screening finds several high-conductivity candidates, including a NASICON-type material (Li4Hf2Si3O12) with predicted ionic conductivity of 14.09 mS cm−1, and analyzes how Li content relates to stability and conduction pathways.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU performance and architecture, focusing on Tensor Core throughput, support for multiple data formats (including FP16, TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8/INT4, and sparsity), and comparisons to the Tesla V100. It explains that A100 Tensor Cores support structured sparsity (2:4) and include Sparse MMA instructions that skip zero values to double Tensor Core compute throughput. The text also covers A100 memory and cache features (combined L1/shared memory, larger 40MB L2 cache, ECC protection, higher HBM2 bandwidth), simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) for partitioning a single A100 into multiple isolated GPU instances. Additional sections discuss third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch connectivity, fault detection/isolation features, and CUDA updates such as CUDA Task Graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls.

The passage describes the David Swensen Portfolio (Yale Model), an investment strategy developed by David Swensen, Yale’s chief investment officer from the mid-1980s until his death in May 2021, who helped invent the model with Dean Takahashi. The portfolio is diversified across asset classes with a focus on alternative investments such as private equity, real estate, natural resources, and hedge funds, alongside low-cost index funds and passive strategies. It emphasizes risk management, including identifying undervalued assets and managing risk through diversification rather than guarantees of future performance. The passage also outlines how to backtest the Yale Model using historical data and portfolio simulation, and it reports a backtest based on specified ETFs and weightings showing annual returns of 6.23%, underperformance versus the S&P 500, and lower drawdowns than the S&P 500.

This prospective study enrolled 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and used bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) at admission and discharge to measure overhydration (OH) and the OH-to-extracellular water ratio (OH/ECW). Patients were stratified by chronic kidney disease (CKD) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). During follow-up (10.7 ± 7.1 months), 51 patients (32.5%) experienced major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and 45 (28.7%) had heart failure hospitalization (HHF). CKD patients had higher OH and OH/ECW ratios at admission but no association with MACE or HHF. Greater reductions in OH/ECW were observed in HFrEF patients, indicating better diuresis response, but OH, OH/ECW, and changes in these BIS parameters were not significant predictors of MACE or HHF in any subgroup. The study concludes that BIS can effectively monitor fluid status in ADHF patients, particularly in HFrEF, but its prognostic utility in CKD and HFpEF-related subgroups is limited.

The passage discusses why wireless communication is more complex than wired communication, focusing on fading mechanisms. It first models free-space propagation using Maxwell’s laws for a cosine input, describing far-field behavior, antenna patterns, and propagation delay. It then considers a moving receiver, deriving a Doppler shift and showing that a single Doppler shift does not necessarily cause rapid problems if the receiver can track the frequency. It explains that multipath fading arises when multiple reflected paths experience different Doppler shifts, producing fast, periodically varying fading.

Several examples are used to illustrate multipath effects, including reflection from a wall leading to fast fading, and a base-station-to-vehicle scenario where reflections from a road can produce cancellation and stronger-distance-dependent attenuation. The passage argues that directly solving the detailed electromagnetic field for real cellular phones is impractical, so it uses a ray-tracing-based approximation that represents the channel as a sum of attenuation factors and time-varying delays across multiple paths. It then frames this as a linear time-varying system with convolution using a time-varying impulse response, and discusses baseband modeling and Doppler spread as a key factor in how long the channel appears time-invariant, affecting measurement update rates in wireless systems.

Chester Gibson, a Mohawk hunter, previously hunted deer stealthily outside the Six Nations Reserve, but in 2017 government parks officers and police met him warmly when he arrived at Short Hills Provincial Park for a six-day hunt and he shot two white-tailed deer. Ministry biologists helped retrieve and examine the deer and load them onto his truck, a change linked to the 2013 government recognition of an 18th-century treaty outlining Haudenosaunee hunting rights. Protesters gathered at the park entrance each night to oppose the hunt, which some supporters view as tied to Indigenous culture, reconciliation, nutrition, and food security. The community describes the activity as a harvest, notes no limit on deer numbers during the six-day access period (sunrise to sunset, bows only), and emphasizes traditions and ecosystem role, while critics cite concerns about the deer population and impacts on plants and ground cover. Reports of vandalism and an investigation by police were also mentioned. The hunt’s meat was distributed across Haudenosaunee longhouses and to elders and hunters’ families, and supporters argue it helps people pass on skills and access traditional food.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 30, 2017. The document includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for the three and six months ended July 30, 2017 and July 31, 2016, including statements of income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, and cash flows, and related notes. Key items include revenue of $2,230 million for the three months ended July 30, 2017 (up from $1,428 million in 2016) and net income of $583 million (up from $261 million). The notes describe accounting policies, adoption and upcoming accounting standards, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities and fair value disclosures, intangible assets, balance sheet components, derivatives and hedging, guarantees and product warranty liabilities, convertible debt and related hedges and warrants, commitments and contingencies (including litigation involving Polaris Innovations Limited and lease financing for a headquarters building), share repurchases and dividends, and segment and geographic information. Management’s discussion covers forward-looking statements, an overview of the company’s businesses, second quarter fiscal 2018 results by segment and market, operating expenses, gross margin drivers, liquidity and capital resources, capital return plans, and off-balance sheet financing for the headquarters building.

A new therapy called BrainWorking Recursive Therapy (BWRT) has arrived in Dunstable to help Bedfordshire residents with anxiety and related conditions such as social anxiety disorder, irrational fear, depression, and stress. The treatment is intended to retrain the brain by stopping reactions to triggers in a 0.5-second gap before conscious awareness, with clients choosing a preferred feeling to replace the “bad” feeling. BWRT was created by Terence Watts in 2011 after he read about Benjamin Libet’s experiments. Keith Tunstall, an advanced BWRT practitioner, offers an initial free consultation, keeps appointments confidential (including via Skype or FaceTime), and is based on High Street South. He can be reached at 01582 475459 or via www.bwrtuk.co.uk.

Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-Q presents financial information for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2020. The consolidated statements include cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets, along with notes describing accounting policies, use of estimates, inventories, accounts receivable, digital content costs, unearned revenue, financial instruments and fair value hierarchy, leases, commitments and contingencies, debt, stockholders’ equity, income taxes, and segment information (North America, International, and AWS). The document also includes liquidity and capital resources discussion, COVID-19 effects on operations and expected impacts through at least Q2 2020, and non-GAAP measures such as free cash flow.

Sterling Bank Plc reported improved performance for the year ended December 31, 2017, increasing loans and advances by 27% to N598.1 billion and gross earnings by 19.8% to N133.5 billion. Net operating income rose 7.9%, profit before tax increased to N8.606 billion, and profit after tax improved to N8.521 billion. Customers’ deposits grew 17.1% to N684.8 billion, shareholders’ funds increased to N102.9 billion, and key indicators including non-performing loan ratio (to 6.2%) improved. The bank’s loan distribution showed the oil and gas sector as the largest at N251.59 billion, followed by real estate and agriculture. Managing Director/CEO Abubakar Suleiman attributed the results to disciplined loan growth, improved asset quality, a diversified funding base, sound liquidity and capital adequacy ratios, and efficiency efforts including the launch of “Specta,” an online lending platform. He outlined 2018 plans to pursue efficiency through agility, digitisation, and business specialisation, with focus on sectors such as health, education, agriculture, renewable energy, and transport.

The speaker says the team’s game was more defensive than the previous one, which was “wide open.” They note they won at home previously and must return home to win home games, and that they have been playing well at home. They describe a goal involving a turnover at the blue line and the use of defense as a screen. They say giving up two goals quickly was difficult, but they played well in the first period and, more positively, played their best in the third period and dominated it. Despite confidence and continuing to look forward to going back home, they express frustration that they did not win and that they could not get a goal. They also mention a “big name” goalie coach they learned from in pro hockey.

The passage describes an investment thesis for Neo Performance Materials based on growing EV demand for rare earths used in permanent magnet motors. It argues that permanent magnet motors use neodymium and that Neo Performance Materials’ main business, Magnequench, is a key supplier of rare earth magnetic powders, contributing most of the company’s 2017 revenues and EBITDA. The author says valuation and the EV/rare-earth thesis looked attractive (6.1x EV/EBITDA), but due diligence revealed a major risk: two specific patents tied to Magnequench’s products (US 6,183,572 and US 6,478,890) expired in December 2017, potentially enabling competitors to make products using the covered knowledge without paying Magnequench. The author notes that Magnequench works with users to avoid patent infringement, but concludes the risk is significant and decides not to take a position.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on December 1, 2022 to report the closing of the sale of $1.25 billion of 4.700% notes due 2024, $1.25 billion of 4.600% notes due 2025, $2.0 billion of 4.550% notes due 2027, $1.5 billion of 4.650% notes due 2029, and $2.25 billion of 4.700% notes due 2032, totaling $8.246 billion in aggregate public offering price. The notes were sold under an Underwriting Agreement dated November 29, 2022, registered under a Form S-3 filed June 1, 2020. The notes were issued pursuant to an indenture dated November 29, 2012, as amended and supplemented, and the terms were established by an officers’ certificate dated December 1, 2022. The filing lists related exhibits and is signed by Antonio Masone, Vice President and Treasurer.

European spot electricity prices for Monday delivery rose in the wholesale market on Friday, driven by forecasts for slow wind speeds that would reduce renewable generation, while demand was broadly flat in major markets. French and German baseload prices for Monday were both at 36 euros/MWh, up from Friday levels. Likely German wind output was expected to be 2.2–4 GW on Monday versus 6.1–6.6 GW on Friday, with demand around 112.5 GW in both countries. Temperatures were forecast to ease, French nuclear availability was stable at 76% of capacity, and generators in Germany and Austria were set to curb capacity availability by 0.5% over the next seven days. Forward prices were mixed, with Germany’s year-ahead flat and France higher; oil, gas, and carbon prices weakened while coal rose. RWE shares increased following a buy recommendation.

NASA employees working on Artemis missions with contractors SpaceX and Blue Origin were told they must continue working through the government shutdown. Their work would be unpaid during the shutdown furlough, but they should record their time, and NASA expects them to be paid after the government reopens. In related guidance, NASA said it would support planned International Space Station operations and satellite missions in the operations phase, and it would continue Artemis operations during any funding lapse. NASA also said it would furlough about 15,000 people and require about 3,000 to keep working part time or full time.

Staff at a Prestwick supermarket face uncertainty after Budgens’ parent company, Owners Food Retail Operations Ltd (FROL), went into administration, leaving almost 900 employees across the country in limbo. The Prestwick store, which became Budgens after being sold from Co-op, employs about 27 staff who were promised continued employment in June. Joint administrator Mike Denny said FROL faces pricing pressures, intense competition, and structural change, and that all 34 stores are continuing to trade while administrators engage with interested parties. Co-op may offer a lifeline if no buyer is found. The passage also notes related ownership changes and that Booker could not comment on whether the Prestwick store’s situation is due to Tesco’s purchase of Booker earlier this year, and a further statement is awaited.
