Consumer gasoline demand is the highest on record for March at 9.6 million b/d, supported by high U.S. exports. Stronger demand reduced gasoline inventories and increased the national average gas price by two cents to $2.55. The price is up two cents from a month ago and 26 cents higher than last year. Multiple states saw monthly price changes, and the most expensive markets include Hawaii and California, while the South and Southeast saw notable weekly increases such as Georgia, Texas, and Florida. Despite inventory declines, inventories remain above 85 million bbl, and Motiva’s Port Arthur refinery is restarting processing units that may boost inventories in coming weeks.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2015 reports revenue of $23,796 million for the three months ended December 31, 2015 and $44,175 million for the six months ended December 31, 2015. Net income was $4,998 million for the three months and $9,618 million for the six months. Diluted earnings per share were $0.62 for the quarter and $1.20 for the six months. The balance sheet at December 31, 2015 shows total assets of $180,098 million and total liabilities of $103,318 million, with stockholders’ equity of $76,780 million. The cash flows report net cash from operations of $5,598 million for the quarter and $14,192 million for the six months. The filing includes unaudited interim financial statements, notes on accounting policies, earnings per share, investments, derivatives, fair value measurements, business combinations, goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, restructuring, unearned revenue, contingencies, and stockholders’ equity, as well as a segment description and management’s discussion and analysis.

The speaker praises a player’s skating ability, size, and the force he brings this year, calling him “unbelievable.” They say last year’s games against him were challenging and that this year they are looking forward to it. The speaker describes him as skilled, hardworking, and a leader who scores goals and makes plays, with more goals than the previous year. They also compare him to Crosby in terms of skill and physical presence and say opponents must stay alert and play physically and on the right side when he is on the ice.

The passage describes civil unrest in Nicaragua beginning on college campuses and says students there are demanding civil liberties and are being shot in response. It contrasts this with Canada, where the organized left on campuses is portrayed as resisting civil liberties through “safe zones,” “trigger warnings,” identity politics, and suppression of conservative views. It discusses Lindsay Shepherd’s lawsuit at Wilfrid Laurier University after she showed a public video of Jordan Peterson, saying she was criticized by university officials and compared to Adolf Hitler, and that an apology occurred but mistreatment continued. The passage argues that “political correctness” has spread to workplaces and HR, leading to expanded harassment-investigation practices beyond legal requirements, and it states that not all complaints must be investigated and that performance management and appropriate discipline are not harassment. It also says stress is not automatically a disability and that stress leave is only required when a medically disabling condition exists.

The speaker says their team ran out of gas, and that playing to win hurt them more than it helped because injuries sustained during the series became harder as it went on. They believed they used all available energy, but the other team had more strength late in the series. The speaker mentions injuries to Donovan (sprained MCL) and Robyn (ankle injury) and expresses uncertainty about the exact nature of the injury. They praise the officiating crew, naming Carey Fraser and Bill McCreary, and say they are disappointed for “them” while congratulating the Tampa organization, noting Jay did a “hell of a job,” and that he probably won’t play. The speaker concludes by saying they are proud of their players for making it to the third game.

A Kashmiri student, Aftab, said he and a friend were followed after leaving a mosque and were then beaten by a group of 15–20 people, with no one helping until police arrived. He said they received medical checkups, informed university faculty, and filed a complaint. Jammu and Kashmir Police said it took cognizance, that an FIR under IPC sections 148/149/341/323 was lodged in Mahenderhgarh, and that an officer is in touch with the students. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti urged the Haryana government to take stringent action and demanded a probe after reports of the assault surfaced.

The passage explains folding polygons into convex polyhedra by gluing a polygon’s boundary to itself, represented using gluing trees. It gives a cube example, describes Alexandroff gluings (no crossings, topologically a sphere, and limited total material at each point), and motivates gluing trees as useful for algorithms and bounds.

It outlines combinatorial results for the number of gluings and the complexity of decision, enumeration, and counting: in the general and edge-to-edge settings the number of gluings can be exponential (with upper and lower bounds of the form \(2^{\theta n}\)), while for polygons with “bounded sharpness” the number of combinatorial gluings and the listing problem become polynomial. It defines “combinatorial type” of gluing via an abstract gluing tree, junction labeling, and assignment of polygon vertices/edges to junctions to make the problem finite.

It then proves an exponential upper bound by bounding the number of leaves in a gluing tree (at most \(n+4\), since fold points can occur at most four times) and discusses a matching exponential lower bound using a “spiky star” construction, including an edge-to-edge variant. For bounded sharpness, it argues that each leaf has curvature at least a constant \(\gamma\), so the number of leaves is constant (bounded by \(720/\gamma\)), yielding polynomial bounds on combinatorially distinct gluings.

Finally, it sketches algorithms: a dynamic-programming method for edge-to-edge gluings that can decide in polynomial time (by storing a minimal-angle solution per subproblem) and enumerate in exponential time; it notes generalization to arbitrary gluings is more complex due to intervals along edges and rolling belts. The passage concludes with experimental implementations and examples (e.g., the “Latin cross” polygon), reporting counts of gluings and distinct resulting polyhedra, and mentioning the “half-length theorem” for certain non-edge-to-edge cases.

The passage discusses a loss in which the team struggled in several areas, including when skilled opponents made plays and when they capitalized on power plays. Early in the third, the team had scoring chances but did not score; then they conceded a power-play goal after Sammy was pushed into the goalie, which led to the team “running around.” The goalie, described as recently returning after three or four months, is said to have made good stops early and played well, with little fault in the goals. The speaker concludes the team must rectify areas for improvement and acknowledges they did not give the goalie their best.

The Nigerian Immigration Service told a Federal High Court in Abuja that suspended Supreme Court justice Sylvester Ngwuta used two similar standard international passports interchangeably. The claim came during cross-examination by counsel for the defendant, Kanu Agabi, by a senior staff member, Tanko Kutana. Ngwuta was arrested in October 2016 after SSS raided judges’ homes. The Immigration Service said it issued Ngwuta a new passport after he declared his original missing, but later discovered he was using the two passports with visas simultaneously, which Kutana said violated immigration law. A forensic analysis found no evidence of forgery on four diplomatic and two standard passports, and the trial was adjourned to October 20.

The Tri State Psychology Conference, founded by Marshall University students and faculty in 1993, will celebrate its 25th anniversary with a 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. conference on Friday, April 20, at West Liberty University in Wheeling. It was created to give students experience with professional conference processes, including preparing and submitting materials for review, having work accepted, and presenting in oral or poster formats. The conference began as a local event with 25 participants and six undergraduate poster presentations, and Psi Chi members later conducted annual fundraising to expand it into a regional conference with speakers from higher education, research, policy, and health care. Up to 25 schools have attended, and other schools have added elements such as West Virginia University’s annual Jeopardy competition. The Psi Chi National Office provides grant funding, and there is no registration fee. Contact Pamela Mulder at 304-696-2770 or mulder@marshall.edu for more information.

The passage explains interrupt handling in SEV-ES, focusing on “interrupt shadows” and the special treatment of #HV, which is delivered without regard to interrupt shadows. It sets a convention for guests entering HLT: they should execute HLT with interrupts disabled without checking pending interrupt state, and the host should re-enter the guest if HLT is intercepted while interrupts or non-maskable events are pending. After resuming from HLT, the guest should examine interrupt state as if it had just received #HV. It then describes how #HV doorbell page configuration is performed via VMGEXIT requests using the GHCB, including SET and QUERY operations and guidance on RMPUPDATE/PVALIDATE and guest PTE access requirements. Host behavior includes emulating APIC interrupt semantics and presenting ready interrupts by writing PendingEvent.Vector in the doorbell page while using #HV injection logic controlled by PendingEvent.NoFurtherSignal and NoEoiRequired. The host must track internal state for presented vectors and handle acknowledgment and EOI cycles. Guest behavior requires atomically exchanging doorbell state: when acknowledging an interrupt, the guest must atomically exchange PendingEvent contents with zero before acting on the vector, and when completing EOI it must atomically clear NoEoiRequired or perform an explicit APIC EOI write depending on its previous value. The guest must validate observed vectors because a non-cooperative host could write arbitrary values, and it notes that unexpected #HV receipt under certain conditions should be treated as grounds for a system panic.

NES Global Talent is seeking a Performance Specialist for a six-month onshore contract in Aberdeen for a global operator, responsible for PSCM functional performance management and risk & assurance for the region. The role includes functional planning, developing a performance framework with financial and non-financial measurement and reporting, leading compliance and risk management, and providing early-intervention insights to PSCM and FPM leadership. It requires knowledge of finance, accounting, and procurement processes, strong team working, organizational and time management skills, analytical problem solving and interpersonal communication, expertise in MS Excel, and experience with SAP and Backbone (desired). An accounting degree or a professional relevant qualification is required. The passage also describes NES Global Talent as a recruitment provider established in 1978 with offices in multiple countries.

The March 19, 2018 edition of BCHL Today recaps playoff action across BCHL series. In Vernon, the Vipers lead Wenatchee 2-0 after a 3-1 game-two win; Wenatchee’s offence scored two goals in two games, and goaltender Ty Taylor lowered his GAA to 1.65 with a .942 save percentage. The article notes game three is Tuesday at the Town Toyota Center. In Penticton vs. Trail, Penticton leads 2-0 after a 7-2 win, highlighted by power plays and a hat-trick from Owen Sillinger; Trail’s Ethan Martini receives a suspension for a blow to the head after the whistle. The Rangers are focused on finding a new manager and their lead internal candidate is Skip Schumaker, a former National League Manager of the Year who has worked with the organization for about a year. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said a formal interview process has begun internally and there are no external candidates yet. Young also said he is not overly concerned about Schumaker in relation to other manager openings. Schumaker previously served as a special adviser for the Rangers and was hired in November as a potential successor to Bruce Bochy, whose three-year contract ended after Texas finished 81-81. Bochy, a four-time World Series champion and the winningest active manager, has agreed to an advisory role instead of managing.

The passage discusses Martin Braithwaite leaving Middlesbrough FC in January to increase his chances of making the Denmark squad for the World Cup, which he likely has only one or two opportunities to attend. It argues that staying at Boro could have helped him secure a place and potentially contribute to the team’s promotion run, while leaving is portrayed as possibly taking the “easy way out.” The main rival in Denmark is described as Viktor Fischer. The passage notes Tony Pulis’ disappointment at Braithwaite leaving so soon after signing a four-year deal and reflects on how other players might have benefited from perseverance. It concludes that Boro’s results between now and May could still earn a play-off place and that it remains uncertain whether Braithwaite’s decision will be vindicated.

Russia’s foreign ministry said that U.S. deployment of ballistic missile defense systems in Romania and plans to add more in Poland violate the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty (INFT). The ministry said the U.S. activated an $800 million missile shield in Romania about a year earlier and planned another site in Poland. It added that the treaty violation is a “gross violation of the INFT obligations.”

The passage discusses using LLMs in social science and the need for human-AI collaboration. It notes that some researchers believe LLMs can generate innovative hypotheses, while concerns remain about their originality and validity, especially because social science theories may be hard to falsify. It then shifts to regulatory issues for rapidly advancing generative AI, citing risks such as misinformation, deepfakes, and societal bias, and challenges in fitting regulation within existing legal frameworks. The passage says timely, forward-looking AI policies should align with ethical values and highlights efforts by the European Union, the United States, and China, as well as company initiatives like Microsoft’s AI Principles. It identifies gaps between industry and government and lack of international regulatory consensus, plus micro-level issues where risks may only be noticed by users. To address these challenges, it calls for top-down and bottom-up governance, partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, transparent handling of reported issues, timely updates to regulations, and use of social computing techniques to monitor regulation needs and discussions in communities.

The passage introduces ASTROCO, a conformer-style self-supervised learning model for astronomical time series. It addresses limitations of transformer encoders that treat time steps equally and lack explicit regulation of noisy or distant measurements, which can reduce reconstruction fidelity and downstream generalization. ASTROCO uses encoder blocks combining multi-head self-attention for long-range dependencies, depthwise convolution with gated linear units for local feature extraction, and a gated feed-forward network for adaptive global information control, along with residual connections and layer normalization. Inputs concatenate magnitudes and uncertainties with time embeddings, fuse them via learned projection, and use BERT-style masked reconstruction with 50% probed positions and specific masking/replacement rules; masked/padded tokens use zero placeholders to prevent input leakage. On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S and ASTROCO-L achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 classification than Astromer v1/v2, with the smaller model outperforming prior work using fewer resources and the larger variant setting the strongest benchmark.

The passage consists of sports commentary criticizing the team’s performance in the Stanley Cup finals, citing turnovers, poor puck movement, and defensive coverage problems. It attributes Anaheim’s success to aggressive forechecking and physical play, especially on dump-ins and in front of the net, and discusses specific game moments involving Wade Reddens and coverage breakdowns that led to a winning goal. The speakers say the loss was a winnable game earlier on, that they expect to play and handle the puck better in upcoming games, and that they must adjust their style, including holding up forecheckers and encouraging officials to clarify rules. The passage also includes discussion of players’ roles and matchups, lineup decisions, and general assessment of how the team and specific opponents play physically. It ends with a comparison to Buffalo’s style, noting Buffalo’s forechecking and wall play but less physical finishing than Anaheim.

Las Vegas Valley residents filing last-minute 2016 tax returns have until 10 p.m. Tuesday to get returns postmarked. The IRS considers returns postmarked by April 18, 2017, or October 16, 2017 (extension), as filed on time. The Postal Service will close at 10 p.m., unlike last year when headquarters were open until midnight, and this year will have a drive-up drop-off area. The Postal Service advises using sufficient postage, writing destination and return addresses clearly, sealing the envelope, and saving receipts showing mailing and/or delivery, and provides contact information for Lawren Linehan and a Twitter account.

Winners of the 2017/18 Carlsberg UK Northamptonshire Food and Drink Awards were announced at an awards dinner at Northampton’s Royal & Derngate on November 15. Workbridge Coffee Shop won Independent Café/Tea Room of the Year, while The Hopping Hare in Northampton won both Booker Food Pub of the Year and had runner-up Arturs Dzerins in the Booker Young Chef of the Year category. The event also highlighted Eat Out Eat Well and celebrated top gold venues from five borough/district councils. The passage lists winners and runner-ups across categories, including local drinks, savoury and sweet products, food and workplace awards, restaurant and chef awards, and community pub and food hero honors.

The speaker describes a second-game situation where the team had a few breakdowns, went to sleep briefly, and conceded quick goals they couldn’t recover from. They say they played a solid hockey game, created good chances, but couldn’t get the puck through and the goalie made saves. After a first loss to Buffalo at home, the team came back to win the next game and is not too worried, emphasizing the need to play hard and work for goals by getting the puck deep and to the net against a strong defensive team that scores on chances.

The passage discusses defensive problems created by the Triangle Offense and presents HoopTactics’ defensive options, including traditional methods and SOS (show-and-recover and aggressive disruptive) pressure concepts. It outlines defensive fundamentals and techniques to deny inside play, congest the three-second area, and force perimeter shots, using sequences labeled as Phase 1 through Phase 4 for show, post feed, corner screen and roll, and weakside two-man actions. It then describes SOS disruptions that can be extended full court to lengthen passing lanes and move the offense away from normal areas, detailing wing pass entry, post split action, and ball reversal weakside two-man game. Finally, it explains “All Out SOS Disruption” via a first-pass trap that triggers rotations like “Triangle I” positions, pass-out-of-trap closeouts, corner pass-out sequences, and an optional trap on a corner pass.

Liberal High School students’ prom is Saturday, April 22, and Girlfriends’ Kenna McNeil said the shop and employees are preparing flowers and prom accessories. She said shop staff guide students in selecting corsage flowers, ribbons, stones, and related items, and they have worked with multiple school proms. McNeil estimated the shop has received close to 100 prom accessory orders, including corsages and clothing. She said staff began preparing around March 1 to allow time to order flowers from Arkansas and match ribbons, stones, and silk flowers. She described the order stream as steady, with many students waiting until about two weeks before Prom, and noted about 20 to 30 tux and corsage orders in the past few days. Her favorite part is seeing completed corsage and accessory photos online. She added that the shop is still working to ensure items are unique and students need to get in and place orders.

Shared tasks are community-driven challenges that compare computational methods on specific problems using shared datasets and metrics, advancing research through innovation, collaboration, state-of-the-art progress, and benefits such as transparency, reproducibility, fair comparisons, and publicly available resources. The NFDI4DS consortium focuses on supporting the research data lifecycle in Data Science and AI and emphasizes FAIR principles, transparency, and reproducibility. Within this context, the paper overviews twelve shared tasks: seven completed, one ongoing, and four under development. Completed tasks include SOMD 2025 (software mention detection), SciVQA (scientific visual question answering), ClimateCheck (fact-checking social media climate claims), FoRC2025 (field of research classification), LLMs4Subjects@SemEval-2025 (subject tagging for an open-access catalog), LLMs4OL-2024 (ontology learning), and Scholarly QALD (question answering over scholarly linked data). The ongoing task is CheckThat!Lab Task 4 (scientific web discourse) with subtasks for discourse detection and claim-source retrieval. Under development are tasks for ML model and dataset mention detection (GSAP-NER), GitHub README to knowledge graph (ReadMe2KG), clinical uncertainty for decision-making (CURED), and algorithm generalisability and domain adaptation benchmarking (Algorithm2Domain).

Scores of Vietnamese fishermen clashed with police in central Vietnam as they tried to file lawsuits seeking compensation after toxic waste dumped by a Taiwanese firm killed tonnes of fish last year. Activists said the deaths destroyed coastal livelihoods, and the Formosa company has paid $500 million to the Vietnamese government, some of which authorities dispersed last year, but the fishermen said they have not received compensation and are demanding payouts from Formosa. Witnesses said police stopped the fishermen in Nghe An province, beat some people, and briefly detained several. Local authorities agreed to receive the lawsuits, but did not respond to an AFP request for comment. In September, a separate group’s compensation lawsuit was dismissed.

Hollywood’s 2018 summer season is expected to start strongly with “Avengers: Infinity War,” amid a year box office that is down nearly three percent and a previous summer that had its worst performance in more than a decade. The season, typically from early May to Labor Day, could help boost results, with major releases including “Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom,” plus many sequels and familiar franchises. Ben Fritz cautions that even with more franchise tent-poles, audience oversaturation and competition for the same box office dollars can lead to more flops, noting ticket sales in 2017 were at a 25-year low and attention competition is intensifying. Studios are also emphasizing variety beyond superheroes and blockbusters, with examples from Universal, Warner Bros., and others, alongside Netflix releases and a range of “hidden gem” and Sundance-style projects such as “Uncle Drew,” “Hereditary,” and “Eighth Grade.” Drew Pearce describes “Hotel Artemis” as an original action-thriller not tied to existing IP, saying audiences want movies with real personality and something less “cookie-cutter.”

Digital leaders encourage employees to collect and examine relevant data to inform objectives and measure progress. Success is defined using detailed metrics, and goals are realistic but ambitious and grounded in measurable data. Employees in leading organizations are expected to continuously track progress toward project and individual performance goals, using data-driven evaluations supported by 360-degree reviews to foster adaptation based on objective input rather than only top-down feedback. While measurement may seem rigid, it is described as providing flexibility and autonomy, with clear data-driven goals increasing structure that supports innovation, experimentation, and risk-taking.

Volunteers from the Colchester-Milton Rotary Club, Dealer.com, and Vermont Gas planted saplings at Pine Island Farm near the Winooski River on Thursday, May 17. The project, organized by Burlington’s Intervale Center, built on a 2014 planting and included help from U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service agents. Intervale conservation nursery manager Mike Ingalls instructed volunteers on steps for planting saplings, which Rotarians quickly carried out. The project is part of a challenge from Rotary International president Ian H.S. Riseley to plant a tree for every club member during the Rotary year. Local Rotarians previously planted five larger trees at Porters Point School in 2018 and plan similar projects in Milton next year. Riseley said the goal is for the effort to produce a Rotary that recognizes responsibility toward both people and the planet.

The passage provides guidance for Galaxy Fold users to unfold or view in full screen for the best experience. It also describes compensation disclosures for offers shown on the site and states that product ratings are not influenced by that compensation. The passage includes details for credit card offers, including the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card (unlimited 2% cash rewards, $200 welcome offer after $500 spend in 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, no annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible) and mentions other cards and their reward/intro APR terms. Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 19, 2016 to report that it issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2016. A copy of the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing states that the information is not deemed filed for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except as expressly set forth. The report includes an exhibit listing for Exhibit 99.1 and is signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU features for accelerating HPC and AI workloads. It states that A100 supports accelerated IEEE-compliant FP64 computations, replacing multiple DFMA instructions and delivering up to 2.5× FP64 performance of Tesla V100, with TF64 throughput of 19.5 TFLOPS. It also discusses mixed-precision iterative refinement via cuSOLVER’s TCAIRS solver, reports that TF32 gives the fastest and most robust convergence among Tensor Core modes, and notes speedups of up to 4× for large complex matrices.

The passage further covers A100 fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern, including sparse MMA instructions that skip zero values to double compute throughput, and compression benefits. It explains A100’s combined L1 cache and shared memory, simultaneous execution of FP32 and INT32 operations, and detailed memory architecture improvements including HBM2 bandwidth, ECC protection, and a larger L2 cache with higher bandwidth. It also introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) to partition an A100 into multiple isolated GPU instances for QoS and fault isolation, and outlines third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch for multi-GPU scaling.

Finally, it summarizes CUDA 11 features related to A100, including CUDA graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls for persistent data, along with additional hardware accelerators such as NVJPG decode and an optical flow accelerator, and ends with information about DGX A100 as a scalable system built on A100 and MIG.

Wall Street stocks fell back from early gains on Thursday as bond yields rose and technology stocks retreated ahead of major earnings. The week has been volatile, with mostly strong earnings offset by higher bond yields amid central banks moving away from easy monetary policy. The Fed held its rate steady but signaled concern about rising inflation, with supporting data including below-expected unemployment claims and high factory prices. The Dow gained slightly, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined. Banks led S&P 500 financials higher as yields rose, while companies such as eBay rose sharply and PayPal fell, and UPS dropped after profit hurt by higher shipping costs. After-hours moves included gains for Amazon and declines for Alphabet and Apple. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners on the Nasdaq, while NYSE had more decliners, and trading volume was 7.80 billion shares.

The passage reviews literature on how global higher education rankings affect the visibility and policy actions of higher education institutions (HEIs), noting that although Asian HEIs have initiatives to improve global rankings, they are generally less competitive than American counterparts. It also highlights limited research on the regional and longitudinal ranking positions of Asian HEIs across different ranking indexes, and describes a study using Times Higher Education World University Rankings data from 2015–2025 to analyze global ranking trends of top HEIs from selected Asian countries using a multiple case study approach. Results presented for countries including China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, the Russian Federation, Japan, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand show country- and institution-specific trends, with China, Japan, and Russia described as the most successful in the overall discussion. The study concludes that most Asian HEIs lag behind other continents and often lack stable, positively trending rankings, and it offers policy recommendations aimed at improving research networks, marketing, funding, and international visibility.

Odell Beckham Jr. has accepted a six-game suspension for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing drugs policy, with the suspension appearing on the NFL’s transactions wire and starting a six-week clock. Beckham said he did not knowingly take banned substances and that the league told him his testosterone levels were too high. He stated he wants to return this season and named four teams he would be interested in joining, but he will not be eligible to play until Week 12.

The paper examines whether increasing school physical education (PE) hours and using cognitively engaging activities improves attentional function in middle school students. Seventy-five participants from two classes were assigned to experimental (41) or control (34) groups, with Class 6 receiving 4 PE hours per week and Class 7 receiving 2 hours; randomization occurred at the class level, with exclusions only for medical conditions preventing activity. Attention was measured using the Bells Test administered in October (pre) and December (post), with scores for bells correctly identified in the first 30 seconds (processing speed), total bells identified over 120 seconds (sustained attention), and error rate. Results showed significant improvements in attention speed for the experimental group in both Class 6 and Class 7, while control groups showed no significant changes. For sustained attention (120 seconds), significant improvement occurred only in Class 6, with no notable change in Class 7, suggesting greater effects on short-term attention than long-term attention. The authors conclude that increasing PE hours with strategically designed activities can improve short-term attention and recommend further research on long-term effects and activity-specific impacts.

The lecture discusses renormalization in soft-collinear effective theory (SCET), focusing on how Sudakov logarithms arise in matching and renormalization-group (RG) evolution. After accounting for contributions in the effective theory, divergences are separated into parts matching infrared (IR) QCD behavior and ultraviolet (UV) divergences that are canceled by counterterms; the remaining difference yields matching. The Wilson coefficient counterterm is specified, including a double-pole \(1/\epsilon^2\) structure and logarithms, with the label \(\omega\) fixed by kinematics (e.g., \(\omega = m_b\) in the example).

The anomalous dimension is computed via RG equations, leading to a structure with a “regular” anomalous dimension term and an additional “cusp anomalous dimension” term multiplying a logarithm. This cusp term drives leading Sudakov double logarithms, producing a Sudakov exponential for the Wilson coefficient. The origin of the cusp is explained using Wilson lines with a kink (cusp), and the cusp anomalous dimension’s general role at all orders is described.

The lecture then explains when SCET momentum labels in Wilson coefficients are fixed by external kinematics (leading to product-form RG evolution) and when they are not (leading to integral-form evolution and DGLAP-type equations). As an example, deep inelastic scattering (DIS) is set up using SCET factorization: in the Breit frame and inclusive operator product expansion region, hard fluctuations are integrated out, leaving collinear operators that match onto quark and gluon parton distribution functions (PDFs). The quark PDF operator definition is given as a forward proton matrix element with a Wilson line, leading to a delta-function constraint from forward kinematics and an operator interpretation tied to quark momentum. The lecture concludes by indicating that combining these operators with hard coefficients yields a DIS factorization theorem involving PDFs and a perturbative hard part, followed by discussion of their renormalization.

Open source software increased dramatically in the late 1990s and 2000s, and container technology used in this book was developed and released as open source. The passage defines software patterns as general blueprints that guide design without mandating specific technologies, and argues that patterns help developers learn from others, share a common vocabulary, and build reusable components.

It then focuses on single-node container patterns, especially the sidecar pattern, which groups an application container with a sidecar container that augments the application using shared resources and scheduling. Examples include adding HTTPS via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration via a configuration manager sidecar, and providing reusable introspection tools (“topz”) as a sidecar. The passage also describes how to design sidecars for modularity and reuse by parameterizing containers, defining a stable API surface, and documenting usage.

Later sections introduce the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and external services, and provide examples such as implementing a sharded Redis using an ambassador proxy, service brokering for environment-specific discovery, and request-splitting experimentation. The adapter pattern is presented as modifying an application’s interface to match a consistent expected interface, with examples including monitoring adapters (e.g., Prometheus exporters), logging normalization (e.g., fluentd), and rich health checks via adapter containers. Finally, it contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns, introduces microservices, and explains replicated load-balanced services and sharded services, including considerations for readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, and sharded cache performance and resiliency.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status (SMS) as part of new UK regulation, following a 10-month investigation. The decision gives the regulator more power and is the first time these powers have been used to target a major tech company. Possible interventions described include requiring Google to let users choose rival search engines, applying “fair ranking principles,” increasing data portability, and potentially requiring consent to use publishers’ content in AI Overviews. The CMA says Google Search accounts for over 90% of general search queries in the UK and that UK firms spent over £10 billion on Google search advertising in 2024. Google criticized the proposals as potentially inhibiting innovation and harming businesses, while a lawyer said the CMA could expand beyond EU rules and that implementing changes could take months. The new measures would affect Google Search’s “News” tab, “Top Stories” carousel, and Google Discover, but Google News and Gemini are not affected.

The passage describes Rockwood School District in Missouri using whole-class instruction for all students, regardless of reading ability, and then providing flexible small-group support or enrichment based on real-time data within the same grade level. It includes daily phonics and comprehension lessons, independent and partner reading, targeted interventions by reading specialists, and whole-class shared reading. The district argues against grouping students across ability levels, citing research suggesting low-track kindergarten readers rarely catch up and may face reduced exposure to complex vocabulary and comprehension strategies. Rockwood reports that its kindergarten, first, and second graders outperformed national proficiency averages in multiple skills and domains during the 2024–25 school year, and concludes that strong, universally applied Tier I instruction with strategic support helps students build literacy and confidence.

A study reported by Science Friday found that about 75% of honey samples from nearly 200 sites worldwide contained at least one of five neonicotinoid pesticides. Researchers tested 198 samples from every continent except Antarctica, finding 45% contained two or more neonicotinoid compounds and 10% contained four or five. The study said the results confirm worldwide exposure of bees to neonicotinoids through food and that coexisting pesticides may increase harm to pollinators. It also reported that North America had the highest proportion of samples with neonicotinoids (86%), followed by Asia (80%) and Europe (79%).

The passage says China announced it will shut down its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017, following continued elephant poaching for tusks despite a 1989 ban. It states that the international ban did not cover older ivory taken before 1989, allowing illegal ivory to be sold as legal. Wildlife experts say addressing demand is essential, and that China has been the biggest source of demand for ivory used for carving. The Chinese government plans to end legal trade, provide work for ivory carvers on existing museum pieces or other projects, and educate the public on the impact of ivory trading. The passage also notes that the U.S. has largely shut down ivory trade and that other countries may be encouraged to follow.

The passage describes methods and systems for configuring hardware to implement deep neural networks (DNNs), focusing on an activation module that uses a programmable lookup table (LUT). It explains range calibration by providing calibration data to a hardware representation, monitoring inputs to determine an expected input range, generating LUT lookup data for an activation function over that range, and loading the lookup data into the hardware LUT. It also discusses processing input streams using the configured LUT, repeating calibration/loading for multiple activation functions, and supporting features such as concurrent LUT updates, handling inputs outside the determined range via clamping to range extremes (or extrapolating), offset subtraction to center the input range, and interpolation between LUT entries (linear or quadratic). The passage further outlines hardware/data-processing system aspects, including activation module architecture (e.g., separate stores for even/odd entries), a possible “simple path” using ReLU to bypass or clamp outside-range values to reduce power, and how configuration logic can generate LUT data independently for multiple activation modules. Additional sections cover implementation in configurable hardware/integrated circuits, manufacturing using layout and circuit-generation systems based on an integrated circuit definition dataset, and computer program code/storage media capable of performing the disclosed methods.

The passage summarizes a collection of studies and reviews on quality in higher education, with emphasis on online learning, quality assurance, leadership, and related frameworks. Key topics include evaluating online teaching service quality during COVID-19 using service-quality dimensions and mixed methods; the role of leadership spirituality in improving higher education quality in Indonesia; how resistance to change affects quality in higher education institutions; factors influencing e-learning quality from students’ perspectives; and research approaches to quality assurance and management in higher education. It also includes studies on perceived service quality and student loyalty, e-learning acceptance using theoretical models, stakeholder alignment in defining quality, and the relationship and limitations of university rankings. Additional items address post-COVID transitions, equity and inclusion metrics, interoperability models for e-learning, and various broader discussions on quality, innovation, governance, and technology in education.

The passage explains what a platinum trading strategy is and how platinum futures work. It describes platinum as a rare, valuable metal used in jewelry and industrial applications such as catalytic converters, and it notes that platinum futures are standardized, exchange-traded contracts on CME Globex settled by physical delivery. The strategy discussion emphasizes using technical and fundamental analyses, setting precise entry/exit signals, and backtesting with quantified rules for position sizing and risk management. It also provides example backtests of platinum futures strategies (including long/short and a seasonal approach) with reported trade counts and performance metrics, and it outlines factors affecting platinum prices (supply/demand, political and economic conditions, and industrial demand). The article covers trading hours, contract specifications (50 troy ounces per contract, tick size), settlement timing, and ways to trade via futures or CFDs/ETFs. It lists risks mainly tied to leverage and physical delivery, and it states historical all-time high and low levels for platinum futures.

The passage argues that high-dosage tutoring can improve academic outcomes and also help cultivate belonging, confidence, and interest in teaching. It says Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship has expanded to over 40 communities, partnered with hundreds of schools, trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors, and delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning. The passage cites academic gains, including faster test-score growth for middle school math and elementary readers. It presents three lessons: tutoring needs non-negotiable training and support; technology should expand relationships rather than replace them; and tutoring can function as a teacher pipeline, with research suggesting increased likelihood of applying to teaching programs and reported examples of tutors later joining the teaching corps. It concludes that tutoring should be part of the future of schooling rather than only an emergency remediation response.

The passage returns without approval House Bill No. 7864, which proposes amending U.S. immigration law to exclude immigrants physically able and over 16 who cannot read and write in English or another language, with limited exceptions for certain relatives of qualified immigrants. The author argues the bill is a radical departure from past immigration policy and contends that proposed literacy requirements and a short reading-and-writing test are not reliable measures of undesirable immigration. The author also criticizes the bill’s family-related exceptions as indefinite and inadequate, questions assumptions about supported relatives becoming public charges, and raises concerns about additional provisions making certain alien employment and repeated cross-border labor unlawful, including criminalizing employment by others. The author further objects to potential retaliation involving the northern frontier and states that ambiguous language about habitual entry and returning abroad would make the statute hard to enforce, concluding the bill is unnecessarily harsh, oppressive, and harmful to citizens.

The passage describes informal discussions at Dumbarton Oaks on October 7, 1944 about dissolving the League of Nations and transitioning to the United Nations, including plans to exchange papers, though none were received from the U.S. It also reports action by the League’s Supervisory Committee in December 1944 to appoint a three-member Conciliation Committee to work with a designated United Nations group on issues from the League’s dissolution. It states a recommended procedure that the U.S. should not take initiative and that the matter should be left for consideration at the United Nations Conference unless the United Kingdom and/or China initiates a different approach. The passage concludes with remarks from an Acting Secretary at a January 31, 1945 meeting and a Chilean request to correct meeting minutes regarding a phrase about assuring respect for international treaties.

The passage describes GeoSQL-Eval, an end-to-end automated evaluation framework for assessing large language models’ ability to generate PostGIS (GeoSQL) queries from natural language. It motivates the work by noting limitations of traditional relational databases for spatiotemporal data and the complexity of using PostGIS, including syntactic, semantic, and execution-related error types. GeoSQL-Eval is paired with GeoSQL-Bench, a benchmark dataset with 14,178 tasks across three categories: multiple-choice/true-false function understanding questions, syntax-level SQL generation questions (with explicit and underspecified prompts), and table schema retrieval questions (using databases themed from UN-GGIM and ISO 19115-1). The evaluation is organized into four cognitive dimensions and five capability levels and measures performance using metrics such as execution pass rate, syntax accuracy, table/field/function hit rates, argument matching accuracy, and result accuracy for numerical/text/boolean and geometric outputs. It also evaluates robustness via multiple generations (pass@n, coefficient of variation, and stability-adjusted accuracy) and ranks models using an entropy-weighted scoring method, while logging resource consumption and categorized error types. The framework was used to evaluate 24 LLMs/strategies as of August 2025 across six model categories, and the results highlight differences by task type, capability level, error distribution, and efficiency; the study also reports a publicly released leaderboard platform for ongoing submissions.

Kyle Busch of Joe Gibbs Racing said he hopes he is not peaking too early in the 2018 NASCAR Cup regular season. After winning at Richmond, he became the second driver to win three races in a row. Busch noted that a win guarantees a playoff spot, with remaining playoff slots determined by regular season points, and drivers are eliminated each round until four remain at Homestead. He said his momentum is special but that the season is still early, adding that running Kyle Busch Motorsports in lower-tier stock racing helped give him an edge, especially on short tracks. He said the start of the season was rough at Daytona but that the last three weeks have been strong, and a fourth consecutive win would be harder due to restrictor-plate racing’s randomness at Talladega. He said the next race at Talladega is “in fate’s hands” and they will “take what we can get.”

The passage reports that new patches to biosecurity screening software can improve detection of AI-altered toxic proteins. The software monitors DNA manufacturing orders to prevent production of hazardous proteins, since AI can tweak known toxins or viral proteins to bypass safeguards. Researchers simulated screening models by generating about 76,000 blueprints for 72 harmful proteins; while original forms were flagged, many AI-adjusted variants sometimes passed, and software patches reduced missed detections to about 3 percent. The work was entirely computational, without making physical proteins, and it was unclear whether AI-generated variants retained their function. The passage also notes that screening for concerning proteins is described as very rare in practice.

Otis Tucker, who lives in New Orleans’ Lower Ninth Ward, describes how Hurricane Katrina and failed levees devastated his neighborhood and how many residents struggled to return amid lack of funds, developer activity, and gentrification. Since Katrina, the city has adapted to extreme weather, including evacuation centers, raising homes, solar panels, rain gardens to capture rainwater, and growing plants in troughs due to contaminated soil. New Orleans-based architects also helped develop the Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan, addressing flooding and land subsidence, and promoting learning to “live with water” through green and blue infrastructure. Louisiana is also responding to wetland loss and increased flood risk through a Coastal Master Plan with $50 billion in priority projects such as restoring wetlands, building levees and flood gates, raising houses, and relocating some homeowners. The passage also notes that Louisiana’s coastal land is sinking partly due to oil and gas extraction, while rising sea levels are expected to further increase disruption, and Tucker says communities across social and economic groups are all affected.

The passage describes the cup and handle pattern as a bullish continuation chart formation that resembles a cup with a handle. It consists of a rounded “U” shaped cup that forms after a price rally and a handle that develops as a trading range on the right side, typically with a slight downward drift and lower volume. The pattern completes when price breaks out above the handle’s trading range, signaling continuation of the prior rally, and traders may use stop buy orders or stop-loss placements related to the handle and cup levels. The passage discusses inverted cup and handle in downtrends, volume and price-action expectations during cup, handle, and breakout phases, common trading mistakes (such as trading before confirmation or ignoring volume), and how the pattern can be used within broader trading strategies. It also summarizes backtest results referenced from Ali Akhtari and Thomas Bulkowski, noting underperformance versus the S&P 500 and a failure rate of 26% (dropping to 10% when waiting for upside breakout). Market volatility and market psychology are presented as factors affecting formation clarity and reliability, with high volatility potentially disrupting the pattern and lowering predictive accuracy.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on May 10, 2018 reporting results for the quarter ended April 29, 2018. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, is attached as Exhibit 99.2 and will be posted online immediately after filing. The lecture revisits Szemerédi’s regularity lemma and discusses an application requiring new techniques: the induced graph removal lemma. It contrasts the usual removal lemma (removing edges to eliminate copies of a graph \(H\)) with the induced version, where \(H\) must be eliminated as an induced subgraph (obtained by deleting vertices only). The induced case is discussed as being related to edge edits (adding and removing edges) and expressed in a more general “colorful” removal lemma where edges can be recolored.

The main obstacle in adapting the usual proof is that, for induced subgraphs, cleaning steps based on irregular pairs in the regularity partition no longer work because embeddings may require both edges and non-edges, and irregular pairs undermine the counting argument. Since one cannot generally partition a graph to eliminate all irregular pairs (illustrated by the half graph), the lecture introduces a “strong regularity lemma,” which refines partitions to yield an extremely regular partition with controlled energy increase.

Using the strong regularity lemma, the lecture derives a corollary (star) that produces an equitable partition along with subsets \(W_i \subseteq V_i\) such that between most pairs \(W_i, W_j\) the pairs are regular, with similar edge densities as between the original \(V_i, V_j\), and with no irregularity among the \(W_i\) pairs. This corollary is then used in a three-step proof of the induced graph removal lemma: (1) partition using the corollary, (2) clean by adding or deleting all edges between part pairs depending on whether densities are too low or too high, and (3) use a counting lemma to show that if the cleaned graph still contains an induced copy of \(H\), then the original graph must have had many induced copies—contradicting the assumption. The lecture concludes with remarks on how the strong regularity framework extends to an “infinite removal lemma” and connects removal lemmas to property testing, including that every hereditary graph property is testable using an oblivious tester with one-sided error.

The passage discusses how higher-order Feynman diagrams with self-energy corrections to a propagator can produce divergent integrals at large momentum, leading to infinite results that would make physical predictions like cross-sections and lifetimes problematic. To address this, a cutoff is introduced to limit the integration up to a scale, with additional contributions still yielding infinite terms. These infinities can be absorbed through re-scaling or re-normalization, resulting in corrected bare masses and couplings. The passage then describes that physical masses and couplings depend on the energy scale, with electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings “running” logarithmically; at very high scales they do not converge, but introducing new particles could change the running behavior and potentially unify the couplings at a specific scale. It concludes that observed masses and couplings are evaluated at specific experimental scales and run with energy, and notes that the running of these three interactions and related mass evaluations will be examined further.

The passage says Boston has been the world’s top life sciences hub for more than a decade, with more lab space in Boston and Cambridge than anywhere else, large amounts of venture capital, and billions in federal funding for research. It also states that federal funding cuts and threats to higher education are undermining Boston’s competitive advantage.

Roma are reportedly interested in signing Manchester United winger Adnan Januzaj, who is out of favor at Old Trafford. After a disappointing year at Sunderland where he failed to score in 25 Premier League appearances, Januzaj has attracted interest amid expectations he may be sold as Jose Mourinho makes new additions. The report says Roma are negotiating Mohamed Salah’s transfer to Liverpool, and Januzaj could be considered a low-cost replacement. Januzaj has scored five times in 63 matches for United, with his last appearance as a late substitute in a 3-2 defeat to West Ham on May 10, 2016.

The passage contains publication and legal information for the book “Patterns and Paradigms for Scalable, Reliable Services” by Brendan Burns, including copyright, publisher details, where to purchase or access online editions, an errata link for release details, trademark notices, and a disclaimer stating that the publisher and author are not responsible for errors, omissions, or damages resulting from use of the work.

The passage compares lump sum investing and dollar-cost averaging. Dollar-cost averaging invests a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of price, buying more shares when prices are lower and less when higher, and is presented as reducing concern about short-term volatility and frustration from immediate drops. Lump sum investing invests a large amount at once, aiming to take advantage of markets rising over time and to give money more time to grow. The article states it backtests a lump sum buy-and-hold strategy using five equally weighted, well-diversified ETFs and includes results such as equity curves, drawdowns, monthly and annual returns, and performance statistics. It also concludes that starting earlier and staying invested long-term (preferably at least ten years) increases the likelihood of success, noting that the before-crisis lump sum backtest produced higher total profit than the after-crisis backtest.

The passage compiles multiple news items from June 4–5, 2001 about California’s energy crisis and related business and international developments. It describes natural gas shortages and limited pipeline capacity contributing to high energy prices, regulatory and industry disputes over alleged price manipulation and trading practices, and a federal and state response including potential pipeline and electricity market rule changes, investigations, and subpoenas to out-of-state power generators and possible state agencies. It also discusses PBS’s “Frontline” documentary “Blackout” covering deregulation, profits by major energy traders, and ongoing concerns about manipulation and national implications. Additional sections report on Enron-related developments in India involving the Dabhol power project, Enron’s withdrawal and Marathon’s acquisition of Enron’s stake in a Saudi gas venture, and other unrelated business and commodities items.

The passage describes NeoWorld, a framework inspired by the idea of on-demand worldbuilding from *Simulacron-3*. NeoWorld constructs an infinite, interactive virtual world from a single image by progressively unfolding content from object-centric 2.5D representations into full 3D as users explore or issue prompts. It uses object-centric Gaussian layers with compact instance semantics from panoptic segmentation, cross-scene label alignment for continuity across viewpoints, and a selection of foreground objects (top-N by proximity or specified by prompts) for image-to-3D reconstruction, alignment, and physics-capable interaction. A user–scene interaction module uses an LLM to interpret instructions into object selection and manipulation attributes, enabling object manipulation and text-guided dynamics. The passage reports experiments and evaluations showing NeoWorld improves 3D rendering quality, object-centric accuracy (IoU), user prompt-driven motion alignment, and balances realism with computational efficiency; it also outlines limitations such as alignment failures, prompt misinterpretation, image-to-3D errors under occlusion, and segmentation errors.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address delays in delivering performance-based bonuses to public school teachers, calling the long delay “unacceptable.” He noted the issue has persisted since school year 2012–2013 and that teachers have yet to receive bonuses for school year 2016–2017, with the delay now extending into the following fiscal year. DepEd Undersecretary Jesus Mateo previously cited failed biddings and delayed clearance processing. Gatchalian urged DepEd to streamline clearance processing to prevent further delays, while teachers and the Teachers’ Dignity Coalition said funding had already been allocated as early as fiscal year 2016.

Former president Robert Mugabe returned home amid allegations linked to a bomb explosion in Bulawayo on June 24 that killed two people. Mugabe, 94, was receiving medical attention in Singapore and is viewed with suspicion by former allies in Zanu PF, who accuse him of opposing President Emmerson Mnangagwa. Government officials said the White City Stadium attack injured over 40 people and was meant to assassinate Mnangagwa, while Mnangagwa said he has a hunch that Mugabe’s allies associated with G40 were behind it. In response to a BBC interview question about Grace Mugabe, Mnangagwa said he could not trust someone who had attacked him. A source said the Mugabe family was unperturbed and expected home, and quoted presidential spokesperson George Charamba as unavailable for comment. Mugabe has called the “new dispensation” illegitimate and urged constitutionalism, and the passage also cites comments by Mugabe’s nephew Patrick Zhuwao and G40 functionary Jonathan Moyo warning that Mnangagwa may use the blast and related statements to target perceived enemies.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 2, 2015 (signed February 9, 2015) stating it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. to issue and sell $500,000,000 of Floating Rate Notes due 2020, and fixed-rate notes totaling $4,000,000,000 due 2020, 2022, 2025, and 2045. The notes will be issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013, and terms for each series are set out in an officer’s certificate dated February 9, 2015. Interest payment schedules and maturity dates are specified, and the notes are described as Apple’s senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Exhibits include the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of global notes, and related legal opinion and consent.

The ADS9803 includes several features and operating/configuration options: an internal input clamp protection circuit on each analog input channel that limits input voltage to ±18V and requires input current above the clamp threshold to stay within ±10mA, which can be helped by a series resistor (also providing an antialiasing low-pass filter and enabling offset cancellation via matched source impedance). Each channel has a PGA supporting single-ended and differential bipolar signals with independently configurable input ranges, programmable PGA output LPF options, and selectable analog bandwidth per channel. The device also includes wide-common-mode rejection supporting CM voltages up to ±12V, common-mode calculations for differential inputs, and optimized configurations for differential and single-ended use; SNR varies with input common-mode range. Conversion output is 20-bit data in straight-binary or two’s-complement formats, with LSB size dependent on the selected analog input range. Operation requires a free-running sampling clock; output data, data clock, and frame clock become invalid when sampling stops. Multiple devices can be synchronized using SMPL_SYNC, and a precision internal reference (or an external one with internal reference disabled) can be used. The ADS9803 supports 2-lane and 4-lane SDR or DDR interfaces, with conversion results transmitted MSB first in a 24-bit packet, and includes a data randomizer using XOR with either the conversion LSB or an XOR_PRBS bit. It supports data averaging (simple or moving), test patterns (fixed, digital ramp, alternating) and associated register settings, and speed-boost mode that increases sampling for a selected channel pair while idling other channels. The passage also describes SPI register read/write behavior, including daisy-chain configuration for multiple ADCs, and provides details for register fields and various configuration controls.

The passage is from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017. It includes quarterly financial statements and notes, such as income statements showing total revenue of $24,538 million and net income of $6,576 million for three months ended September 30, 2017; comprehensive income of $6,475 million; and balance sheet figures with total assets of $249,097 million and total liabilities of $159,450 million as of September 30, 2017. It also covers cash flows, stockholders’ equity, accounting policies and revenue recognition, adoption of new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases with effects on previously reported results, and details on earnings per share, other income and investments, derivatives and fair value measurements, inventories, business combinations (LinkedIn acquisition), goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, restructuring charges, unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, share repurchases, dividends, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment/geographic information.

The passage describes tuberculosis (TB) as an infectious disease caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, spread via inhaled aerosol droplets. In 2019, WHO estimated about 10 million people fell ill and 1.4 million died from TB, with deaths increasing to an estimated 1.6 million in 2021. Progress in reducing TB burden was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, including fewer newly diagnosed cases and reduced access to TB diagnosis and treatment, as well as reactivation of latent TB due to corticosteroid use in COVID-19 patients. Pulmonary TB is the most common form, but TB can also be extrapulmonary (EPTB), affecting sites such as lymphatic, gastrointestinal, central nervous system, and others; about 16% of reported cases in 2019 were classified as EPTB. Treatment for most EPTB forms is stated to be similar to pulmonary TB, but EPTB therapy is less studied.

The passage then outlines development of a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for the four first-line anti-TB drugs—rifampicin, ethambutol, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide—specifically including pleura and lymph nodes. The model is calibrated and validated using plasma and limited lung tissue concentration data, estimating pharmacokinetic parameters and tissue:plasma partition coefficients. Results described include simulations predicting drug concentrations relative to WHO critical concentrations at pleural and extrapulmonary sites, with reported over-prediction for rifampicin in pleural fluid and findings that ethambutol does not exceed its critical concentration in several compartments, while isoniazid exceeds critical concentrations in all compartments. The authors discuss model assumptions and limitations, note that synergistic drug action and immune effects are not included, and conclude that further in vivo data are needed to better validate and optimize EPTB dosing regimens.

The U.S. Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate for the second time in half a year, increasing the upper benchmark by 0.25 points to a 1 to 1.25 percent target area after a two-day policy meeting ended. The benchmark was previously raised in March by 0.25 points to 0.75 to 1 percent, and this was the third hike since Janet Yellen ended the post-crisis flat interest rate policy. After the 2007 crisis, the federal funds rate fell from 5.25 percent in August 2007 to 0.25 percent in December 2008, where it remained for seven years. In December 2015, the Fed began tightening, proposing a 0.25 percentage point margin (such as 1 to 1.25) for the effective funds rate to fluctuate day to day.

Timely recanalization is important in acute ischemic stroke, and evidence from randomized trials supports endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO). The passage notes that East Asian patients (Korea, Taiwan, China, Japan) are underrepresented in high-quality EVT trials and have higher LVO incidence related to intracranial atherosclerosis, greater procedure complexity, and higher post-reperfusion hemorrhagic complications, prompting the need for registry data focusing on this subpopulation.

Researchers created the K-T collaborative EVT registry by harmonizing two prospective stroke registries: CRCS-K (South Korea) and TREAT-AIS (Taiwan). The unified dataset included 9,941 EVT-treated patients (7,835 from Korea; 2,106 from Taiwan) with about 200 common data fields. Outcomes included symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), successful recanalization (mTICI 2b–3), 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and 90-day mortality. Variables collected included demographics, pre-stroke function, vascular risk factors, stroke severity (NIHSS), LVO location, and key time metrics.

Compared with Taiwan, Korea had younger patients and different risk profiles and treatment timelines. Functional independence at 90 days was lower in Taiwan, while 90-day mortality was higher in Korea; successful recanalization and symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation rates were similar between cohorts. Multivariable analysis found age, pre-stroke functional independence, baseline NIHSS, diabetes, and several laboratory and clinical factors associated with functional recovery and mortality, and age and other factors associated with successful recanalization. Age showed a nonlinear relationship with functional recovery and mortality, most pronounced between 75 and 85 years, while symptomatic ICH did not significantly differ across age groups. The authors conclude that advanced age is associated with worse EVT outcomes but selected elderly patients can still benefit, and they emphasize the value of harmonized multinational registries and future work to refine techniques, integrate imaging and follow-up data, and address regional care differences.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2022. It includes an index of financial statement sections and provides consolidated financial statements and notes, including cash flows, operations, comprehensive income (loss), and balance sheets. The financial statements present results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2021 and 2022. Dr. Maria Pane became a neonatologist after falling in love with the field during her last medical school rotation. At GBMC, she treats and cares for the hospital’s sickest and tiniest patients and uses a cohesive approach to pediatric care by inviting parents to join her on rounds so they are included and informed. She says she tries to put herself in parents’ shoes to understand what new mothers and fathers experience and to care for both patients and parents. She also looks forward to the Father’s Day 5K fundraiser, which benefits the neonatal intensive care unit, and she is proud of her team for working together and valuing everyone’s input.

The lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs), built from the GKR protocol. A PCP converts a classical proof into a (possibly longer) proof that can be verified by reading only a few randomly chosen bits of the proof, using a randomized verifier. The verifier may need to read all of the instance \(x\) (unlike PCPs of proximity, which relax this). The class \(PCP_{c,s}[r,q]\) is defined via probabilistic polynomial-time verifiers with completeness \(c\), soundness \(s\), randomness complexity \(r\), and query complexity \(q\); completeness means correct instances are accepted with probability at least \(c\), while soundness bounds acceptance probability for incorrect instances by \(s\). The lecture then presents a theorem for all languages in \(NP\): constructing a PCP with completeness \(1\), soundness \(1/2\), and polylogarithmic randomness and query complexities. The construction is described as “opening up” (unrolling) GKR: it builds low-degree extensions and uses \(2d\) sumcheck protocols across circuit layers, packing the prover’s potential sumcheck transcripts into the PCP. Soundness is analyzed by bounding the probability of successfully cheating in at least one sumcheck (using a union bound), and efficiency is discussed in terms of parameter choices ensuring the PCP remains polynomial-sized. The lecture closes by motivating the need for a low-degree test (since the prover supplies the low-degree information) before proceeding to cryptography.

A Stephens County jury convicted Robert Pearl Bryson of two counts of aggravated sodomy, four counts of aggravated child molestation, one count of child molestation, and two counts of failure to register as a sex offender. On appeal, he challenged the sufficiency of the evidence for the aggravated sodomy, child molestation, and failure-to-register convictions, and argued the trial court erred in denying motions to quash the indictment, denying his trial counsel’s motion to withdraw, denying his motion to sever the failure-to-register counts, admitting evidence related to a no-contest plea, and denying ineffective assistance of counsel. The appellate court found no error, held the evidence supported each challenged conviction, ruled the motions were properly denied (including timeliness/waiver issues), determined severance was not required, found no reversible error regarding admission and jury use of the no-contest plea, and concluded Bryson waived his ineffective assistance claim. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage describes a study assessing how pupil dilation (mydriasis vs non-mydriasis) affects retinal image gradability and the performance of an AI model for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening using a portable smartphone-based retinal camera. It notes that mydriasis can improve retinal image clarity but requires pharmacological agents and trained personnel, while non-mydriatic imaging is more convenient yet may reduce image quality.  

Methods include imaging patients before and after Tropicamide 0.5% eyedrops with two images per eye, labeling by masked ophthalmologists using ICDR-based lesion assessment, and grading images based on visibility criteria. The AI used a ResNet-200d convolutional neural network for binary classification (normal vs DR), evaluated with metrics including accuracy, F1 score, and AUC.  

Results include 1,056 gradable mydriatic images (82.1%) versus 699 gradable non-mydriatic images (55.6%), with systemic hypertension, age, duration of diabetes, male gender, and Indigenous race associated with decreased gradability. For DR detection, the model had higher performance in the mydriatic group (accuracy 82.91% vs 79.23%; F1 0.83 vs 0.79; AUC 0.94 vs 0.93) and fewer false positives (83 vs 106), though false negatives were slightly higher in the mydriatic group (19 vs 18). The study concludes that mydriasis may enhance AI screening reliability and reduce overdiagnosis, while noting limitations including a learning curve, selection bias, and limited generalizability due to use of one dataset and one camera model. Funding was not provided.

Image registration, or image alignment, is posed as a non-linear inverse problem where a coordinate transform φ deforms a moving image M to match a fixed image F by minimizing an objective L(φ)=C(F, M∘φ)+R(φ). The passage describes common choices for transforms (affine and deformable with a displacement field), similarity losses (e.g., MSE, LNCC, Mattes mutual information), and regularizers (e.g., gradient/warp Sobolev norms, total variation, inverse-consistency), and discusses optimization methods including iterative gradient-based methods and deep learning approaches.

It then focuses on scaling registration to high-resolution biomedical images, noting that existing methods face memory and computational limits. The paper’s contributions are twofold: (1) identifying compute and memory bottlenecks and proposing fused components that fit problems up to 64× larger on a single GPU, and (2) proposing Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP) to scale registration to arbitrary numbers of GPUs. The passage reports an example aligning a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo FLASH brain volume (over 11.8B transform parameters) using 8 A6000 GPUs in about one minute, with claimed speedups and memory reductions.

The passage further describes fused kernels for operations such as a composite implicit grid sampler, memory-efficient mutual information via implicit Parzen windowing, and efficient fused cross-correlation via implicit fused LNCC. For multi-GPU scaling, it introduces Grid Parallel (GP) for boundary-synchronized sharding and a distributed ring sampler for correct interpolation without an allgather of the moving image, along with distributed formulations for MSE, LNCC, and MI. Experiments are described as evaluating acceleration of existing registration pipelines, ablations on key operations, weak-scaling behavior, and comparative performance on a simulated dataset. The conclusion states that the framework enables arbitrarily large image registration problems using fused and distributed implementations, improving existing pipelines and enabling previously infeasible large-scale multimodal registration.

The passage describes digital transformation as an emerging, industry-wide phenomenon enabled by digital technologies, where firms need roles for digital innovation and a new approach to data and analytics to gain competitive advantages. It outlines the growth of Big Data and its need for processing to support enhanced decision-making, insight discovery, and process optimization, often combined with AI and advanced analytics. Digital innovation is defined as creating market offerings, business processes, or models using digital technology, and the paper examines the relationship and potential value of AI, Big Data, and advanced analytics (AI/BD/AA) with digital business platforms. It develops a multidimensional, data-driven AI innovation taxonomy and related value-chain and enterprise maturity framework, based on literature review and semi-structured expert interviews. The framework includes an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain (acquisition, curation, storage/reporting, and usage/decision-making) and five levels of AI maturity tied to different extents of the value chain. The paper concludes that organizations can use the framework to evaluate human-machine relationships and automation scope for AI initiatives, identify industry and functional use cases, and support planning and investment decisions for AI-based enterprise transformation.

The passage lists multiple specification update items for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device, describing issues and their implications and resolutions.
