Key topics include: SSMI signaling may not be reliable when SSMI and an interrupt request occur simultaneously; IDE UDMA fails if the bus master is enabled before sending a PIO command packet; certain GPIO inputs (GPIO[27:24]) do not wake the system from ACPI S3, with PWRBTN# suggested instead; RTC CMOS RAM reads may be incorrect under a specific write/read sequence; block and demand mode legacy DMA to LPC can return invalid data, so single-transfer mode DMA is recommended; USB controller clock gating can cause register read failures; ATAPI packet command handling after bus master enable may fail for a specific CD-ROM firmware revision; an AuxOutputfull bit clearing behavior may mis-emulate PS/2 keyboard/mouse, so interrupts should manage USB keyboard/mouse in PS/2 emulation; ATAC can hang if PRD addresses are not DWORD aligned; LPC may abort transactions when sync patterns are observed too late, with a PLD workaround suggested; SMBus NEGACK bit clearing can behave inconsistently, requiring two writes to clear; and additional items cover GPIO register write behavior after suspend, SMBus hold time being too short, LOWBAT_FLAG missing after abnormal standby, sleep signal de-assertion issues when delays exceed PM_SED, and a recommendation to program delay counters accordingly.

Ulysses S. Gandy appealed his second manslaughter conviction in Mississippi after his first conviction was reversed and remanded for a new trial. The second trial again resulted in a guilty verdict and a ten-year state penitentiary sentence. Gandy assigned errors including: denial of peremptory instruction and motion for new trial based on the verdict being contrary to the overwhelming weight of the evidence; refusal of Instruction D-13; admission of State Exhibits 1, 5, and 7; and failure to provide the jury a recess for food or refreshments.  

The court described a June 26, 1976 two-car collision where Gandy was alleged to be extremely intoxicated and to have driven in the wrong lane on a straight road. Testimony on vehicle positions and alcohol intoxication conflicted, with some witnesses stating Gandy smelled strongly of alcohol and appeared drunk, and other witnesses and a physician testifying they perceived no alcohol or that Gandy was alert and oriented. The court held there was competent evidence supporting the verdict and that the conflict was for the jury to resolve.  

On the instruction issue, the court held that refusing Instruction D-13 was not reversible error because other instructions properly presented intoxication. On evidentiary grounds, the court affirmed admission of State Exhibits 1, 5, and 7 as sketches used to illustrate witnesses’ observations shortly after the accident, without attempting reconstruction of positions at the time of impact. Finally, the court found no merit in the jury-recess claim because jurors could have requested a recess and no supporting authority was cited. The trial court’s judgment was affirmed.

The passage describes a study that models how social activity and contact settings relate to SARS-CoV-2 transmission during the pandemic, using Google community mobility reports (GCMR) as publicly available indicators of activity in six settings. It explains that effective disease transmission depends on contacts between infectious and susceptible people and infection probability per contact, and that measuring relevant contacts is difficult in practice. The authors develop a region-specific extended SIR meta-population model with daily time steps, linking transmissibility to GCMR activity levels in four categories (grocery and pharmacy, retail and recreation, transit stations, and workplaces) via an additive contribution to contacts, while seasonality (temperature) and virus variants (Alpha and Delta) are modeled multiplicatively. The model is fitted to weekly hospitalization data for Norway and Sweden (Feb 2020–July 2021) and also applied to Bavaria and Berlin in Germany (Feb–Dec 2020). Results presented include that aggregated over the full period the model attributes 60.0% of infections in Sweden and 38.7% in Norway to settings captured by the GCMRs, with remaining infections attributed to other contact settings represented by region- and week-specific random effects. It also estimates that transit stations and workplaces are the most important settings at baseline activity levels in Norway and Sweden, while in the German regions retail and recreation plays the largest role. The discussion highlights assumptions and limitations of the modeling approach, including linearity between mobility and contacts, multiplicative effects across settings, and potential measurement errors of GCMR indicators.

The speaker thanks delegates and supporters in Texas and Dallas and accepts a nomination for President, saying the campaign offers a clear choice between two visions: an administration based on “pessimism, fear, and limits” versus one of “hope, confidence, and growth.” They contrast past economic and social conditions under opponents’ leadership with improvements they attribute to their own policies, including changes in taxes, spending, inflation, job creation, and poverty. The speech also discusses foreign policy and military readiness, efforts to strengthen alliances, and opposition to nuclear war through reducing nuclear arms with the Soviet Union. The speaker argues for continued government service focused on necessity, individual dignity, and protection of liberties. They reference their political record and a shift of some Democrats toward their platform, and they describe the Olympic torch relay and themes of American unity and opportunity leading into “the ’80s.”

EUR/USD is rising toward daily highs around 1.1840, supported near 1.1810, marking a fourth consecutive session of gains and extending the move up from last week’s lows in the 1.1690/85 range. The rise is attributed to a strong pullback in the greenback after Friday’s US inflation figures. Upcoming ECB and FOMC minutes are expected to clarify prospects for QE tapering and balance sheet reduction. Key levels include resistance at 1.1846, 1.1894, and 1.1911, with support levels to watch including 1.1722, then 1.1687 and 1.1611.

Texas Instruments warns that the integrated circuit can be damaged by electrostatic discharge (ESD), and that proper handling and installation procedures are required. ESD damage may range from subtle performance degradation to complete device failure, and precision integrated circuits may be more susceptible. The passage also includes a revision history noting changes from June 2024 to May 2025, information about mechanical, packaging, and orderable data for designated devices, and multiple TI disclaimers stating that related information and resources are provided “as is,” with limits on TI’s liability and warranties.

The passage compiles news items about California’s electricity crisis and Enron-related developments in 2001. It says California’s energy meltdown involved a wider range of wholesale merchants than Governor Gray Davis suggested, with state records showing several entities charged prices higher than some Texas firms. It also reports that a Senate committee chair accused Duke Energy of not allowing release of certain pricing information needed for a price-gouging probe. Another item describes a mediator’s refund plan for power sold from October 2000 through May, following unsuccessful negotiations, and notes California’s continued demand for $8.9 billion and possible further legal action. Separately, multiple reports cover disputes involving Enron’s Dabhol Power Project in India, including the resignation of Dabhol’s CEO after contract expiry, Enron chairman Kenneth Lay’s efforts to resolve the payments dispute with India’s government entities, and ongoing uncertainty about restarting or withdrawing from the project.

The passage explains that grief is a unique, highly personal emotional response to loss, with effects and duration varying by person and circumstances. It describes grief after different types of losses, including changes in roles or living arrangements, caregiving burdens, and moving after a partner’s or carer’s death. It also discusses anticipatory grief before an impending loss and notes that grief can occur across generations. The grieving process is described as complex and variable, involving possible reactions such as numbness, denial, acceptance or relief, yearning and searching, repeating events, restlessness and disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. It states there is no simple answer to how long grief lasts, that support may be needed, and that additional help such as a GP or bereavement organizations may be contacted.

The ADS9803 supports two data-averaging modes to improve SNR: simple averaging and moving average. Simple averaging reduces the output data rate by a factor of 2, while moving average does not affect the output data rate; register operations for enabling and disabling each are referenced. The device also includes test patterns for debugging, which replace ADC output data with predefined digital data, configurable via registers 0x13 through 0x1B in bank 1 for two channel groups (CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]). Test pattern options include fixed patterns, digital ramps with increments based on configured ramp increment registers, and alternating test patterns. The passage further describes powering down and initialization sequences, a speed-boost mode that enables up to 8 MSPS sampling for a user-selected channel pair while leaving other channels idle, and SPI register bank read/write access procedures. It also explains daisy-chain configuration for multiple devices over SPI, including register writes and read steps, and provides additional register field descriptions related to averaging, test patterns, power-down, and speed-boost mode.

The New England Patriots had one of their worst offensive performances under Tom Brady against the Miami Dolphins on Monday night but remained in the game until the final minute after a field goal. They trailed by seven and needed to recover an onside kick to reach overtime. Stephen Gostkowski’s onside kick attempt was widely criticized as bizarre and effectively failed; Jon Gruden described it as the most bizarre onside kick he has ever seen. The Dolphins recovered the kick and won the game.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell reported in *Nature Materials* that improved hyperlensing using hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) could enable imaging of features as small as 30 nanometers on living cells. The team improved crystal quality by making hBN with isotopically purified boron, reducing optical losses and increasing the lifetime of surface phonon polaritons, which increased polariton travel distance and improved imaging resolution by about a factor of ten over prior results. The work aims to use low-energy infrared light to image living biological samples without damaging them and notes potential applications in communications and nanoscale optical components.

The passage explains how to beat the offside trap in soccer by staying onside when the ball is passed, recognizing when defenders move up to change space behind them and call offside, and adjusting play accordingly during run-of-play and free kicks. It lists strategies such as dribbling through if no pass is made, using onside through passes, horizontal/lateral runs followed by a near-90-degree break toward goal, checking runs back toward the ball, short passes, vertical runs, bending runs to stay onside, back passes for time, delayed runs, and using a designated “non-runner” on free kicks. It also notes that if the trap is successfully beaten, the striker often gets one-on-one with the goalkeeper, and the opposing team may use the trap less afterward.

The passage explains that ocean acidification, caused by carbon dioxide emitted into the atmosphere, is making waters more acidic and is linked to deterioration of coral reefs and oyster hatcheries. Scientists studying periwinkles report that the snails can adapt to predicted 2100 ocean conditions by changing their shell-making process: they slow metabolism but speed up shell production by making less-dense inner shells and developing less-soluble shells that are more resistant to harsher future conditions. The researchers suggest this indicates potential adaptability in periwinkles and possibly other calcifying organisms.

The passage reports that People v. Roldán is almost identical to case No. 2037, differing only in the loan amount. It states that the same evidence was examined and the assigned fundamental errors were the same. Based on the reasons in case No. 2037, the judgment is reversed and the defendant is acquitted. The decision was made June 26, 1923, with Chief Justice Del Toro and Justices Aldrey and Hutchison concurring, and Justice Wolf taking no part.

China has blacklisted Canadian technology research firm TechInsights, accusing it of endangering national security after it published detailed analysis of Huawei’s advanced AI chips. The Chinese Ministry of Commerce said TechInsights and nine subsidiaries were added to the country’s “unreliable entity list,” effectively banning them from doing business with Chinese organisations. Chinese authorities also cited TechInsights’ report suggesting Huawei processors used components from international foundries and said the firm exposed sensitive information tied to strategic industries. Under the restrictions, Chinese companies and research institutions are prohibited from collaborating with or supplying data to TechInsights, and its access to Chinese clients is restricted.

Shares of Netflix (NFLX) fell slightly last week, and Jack Hough of Barron’s argues the stock could lose more than half of its value. He cites threats including Disney pulling content from Netflix in 2019, Facebook’s new niche content-video service, competition from Amazon’s Prime, Netflix’s cash-burning, and unconventional accounting. The passage counters these points by arguing that competition fears are overblown, Netflix has raised prices in multiple countries without losing subscribers, and its scale and “moat” make it difficult for rivals to catch up. It also states Netflix has 104 million streaming accounts and is continuing to grow.

A new study reported that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window-blind related injuries. Most injuries were minor and did not require hospitalization, with common injuries involving being struck by a falling or pulled blind. Entanglement accounted for 11.9% of cases but was linked to nearly 80% of hospitalizations and more than 94% of deaths, and almost all entanglements involved window blind cords, mostly occurring at home. The study found most entanglements happened when children were unsupervised for brief periods and that toddlers and preschoolers were at particular risk. The senior author, Dr. Gary Smith, said voluntary standards and recalls have not been sufficient and called for mandatory requirements for blinds with unexposed or inaccessible cords. The passage also describes efforts toward mandatory standards by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and manufacturer proposals to reduce accessible cords in products.

A 26-year-old man, Ryan Kerr of Evercreech, was sent to jail while Judge David Ticehurst considers his sentence. Kerr admitted multiple attacks, including punching a woman in the face and leaving a man unconscious after an assault in pub toilets, and he also punched the man’s mother during an earlier incident. Prosecutor Caroline Bolt said Kerr received bruises and lacerations during one fight and that witnesses described another victim being punched and stamped on. Kerr claimed one attack was revenge and had prior convictions for battery and assault. His defense sought an adjournment for psychiatric reports, describing him as a “viable prospect for rehabilitation,” but the court heard Kerr showed no remorse, telling a probation worker a victim “deserved what was coming to him.” Kerr was remanded in custody until next Friday and is due back in court on Friday, October 13.

The passage describes Peterborough City Council’s efforts to tackle homelessness and empty homes, including a £4 million pledge for new homes and work to bring empty privately owned properties back into use. It outlines Phase Two budget proposals, warns about likely further cuts to core government funding and reduced grants, and argues Peterborough is unfairly funded due to out-of-date population figures. It also reports early success from two Public Space Protection Orders aimed at anti-social behaviour and announces the launch of CHUMS, a service supporting children and young people’s well-being and mental health, including anxiety and depression.

Cookbook author and chef Shannon Bard announced that the Fore Street restaurant Zapoteca, which she and her husband Tom owned in Portland, is permanently closed. She said the closure is due to changing priorities as their children reach high school and college, and that she and her husband want to spend more time with them. Zapoteca opened six years ago, and the Bards still operate two other restaurants, Toroso and Salud, along with a cooking school and catering company named Salud. Bard’s first cookbook, “The Gourmet Mexican Kitchen,” was published in 2015 and reflected the Mexican food she prepared at Zapoteca.

The passage describes elements of a COVID-19 study’s administrative, ethical, and consent procedures, including independent ethics committee review, investigator notification of serious or unexpected adverse events, and conduct in line with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. It also outlines the study’s objectives: a primary goal to assess clinical efficacy and safety of best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and a secondary goal to evaluate clinical efficacy of convalescent plasma versus standard of care based on clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers (NAAIM), measures the average exposure to U.S. equity markets reported by its members. NAAIM surveys members weekly about their firms’ overall equity exposure as of each Wednesday, and the indicator line is a two-week moving average of managers’ responses. The index is published weekly and is often used to estimate investor sentiment, where high readings are generally linked to bullishness and low readings to bearishness. The passage notes backtest results where trading based on NAAIM readings showed poor performance and the index is described as not predictive and of little value for determining future stock market direction.

Lubrizol Corp. will expand production capacity and technology for its TPU engineered polymers business in response to increased demand. The US$80 million expansion will add new capacity at key plants in North America, Europe, and Asia, with additional investments in North America for production capabilities and logistics, in Songjiang, China for compounding and extrusion lines, and in Europe for elastomers, aliphatics, and adhesives. The company says capacity in North America is expected to come onstream later in 2018, with further investment planned in Asia in 2019 and another major expansion in Europe in 2019. The expansions build on Lubrizol’s 2011 acquisition of Merquinsa and R&D lab improvements in 2016. Lubrizol is headquartered in Wickliffe, Ohio, operates facilities in 17 countries, has about 8,300 employees, and reported 2016 revenues of US$6.5 billion.

Jeff Horn defends his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran on Wednesday at the Brisbane Convention Centre, seeking to dispel claims he benefited from a hometown decision against Manny Pacquiao. Top Rank promoter Bob Arum said Horn’s win would lead to “massive fights” next year and referenced Terence Crawford as the mandatory challenger. Horn, unbeaten in 18 bouts, says he will focus only on Corcoran until after the fight, and Arum expects Pacquiao to return. Horn’s upset of Pacquiao last July was initially disputed by Pacquiao’s camp but later confirmed by further World Boxing Organization scrutiny; Pacquiao has a rematch clause but no date or venue has been set. Corcoran is 17-1, ranked 10th by the WBO, and is fighting for his first world title outside Britain and Ireland for the first time. The buildup has included head-butting accusations from Corcoran’s camp and biting threats from Horn, with both sides responding at the news conference. Horn and Corcoran both made weight, and trainers expect an aggressive fight, with Corcoran’s trainer saying he will not be intimidated.

Sanofi was confirmed to be investigated by the European Commission for potentially anticompetitive activity. The passage also describes a deal in which President Trump said Pfizer will offer lower prices to Medicaid and directly to patients, launch new medicines priced “at parity” with other countries, and avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs if it continues investing in U.S. manufacturing. Policy experts cited in the passage say it is unclear how much the deal will increase drug affordability, including whether it will affect Medicaid budgets, since Medicaid already receives the lowest drug prices under the law.

Manchester City plays Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on Jan. 2 (10:00 AM ET) as City look to win and keep their winning run, while Burnley aim to keep gathering points to avoid relegation. Pep Guardiola says City must keep top players fit, go on an unbeaten run in 2017, win the midfield battle, and defend set pieces. Sergio Aguero is expected to return after sitting out a 0-3 win over Hull City, and City will look to get Kevin de Bruyne and David Silva involved to open Burnley’s defense and score early. Burnley are described as solid but struggled this season and are just above the relegation zone, with Andre Gray and Sam Vokes as main goal threats. The passage also notes Burnley have struggled to win away games, and City’s fans expect a win.

Facebook released an expanded “community standards” rule book detailing what posts are permitted on its platform, including topics like drug use, sex work, bullying, hate speech, and inciting violence. Facebook says this longer document is being published to clarify its content boundaries and be more transparent about enforcement decisions, which use automated tools and moderators. The company also introduced new options for users to appeal takedown decisions for individual content and began providing specific reasons for removals in more situations. Facebook says its standards are updated frequently, including through a biweekly “Content Standards Forum,” and plans public forums in May and June to gather feedback. The document covers categories such as what drug-related admissions are not allowed, examples of harassment and bullying restrictions, and rules about content from hacked sources, while also describing how local-law takedown requests and country-specific blocking work.

The passage describes a study on neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS), linking TS to altered brain circuits and proposed increased “neural noise” from striatal disinhibition. Prior EEG work suggested increased 1/f noise in TS, especially in beta and gamma bands, and neural noise was hypothesised to relate to increased trial-by-trial variability after stimulation.  

The authors used EEG with single pulse median nerve electrical stimulation (MNS) in 19 adults with TS and 19 matched neurologically healthy controls. They operationalised neural noise as increased trial-by-trial variability in EEG response magnitude and/or timing. They predicted decreased variability and increased phase coherence in both groups after stimulation, with higher variability and flatter 1/f noise curves in TS, and reduced inter-trial phase coherence in TS.  

Results showed no between-group differences in early/mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) components’ amplitude, timing, and topography (N1 and N2), and no evidence that SEP timing was more variable in TS. However, the P100 (P2) SEP component was significantly increased in TS, and there was a small average timing delay for the P1 component. Trial-by-trial variability in SEP measures was substantially higher in TS than controls, but variability decreased in both groups in response to stimulation. Coefficient of variation (CV) decreased substantially following stimulation with no between-group differences. Power spectral density analyses showed increased high-beta and gamma power in TS and flatter 1/f slopes in those ranges. Inter-trial phase coherence increased after stimulation for both groups, but TS showed generally reduced phase-coherence early in the response for alpha and beta/gamma frequency ranges. Some dependent measures (e.g., SEP P2 amplitude, changes in coherence, and CV) were associated with clinical severity scores in the TS group.  

The conclusion states that TS is associated with increased trial-by-trial neural variability at rest and a larger P100 SEP response, while early/mid SEP components and their timing variability are largely similar between TS and controls; variability normalised during stimulation.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated June 13, 2017. On June 20, 2017, Apple consummated the issuance and sale of $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.000% Notes due 2027 under an underwriting agreement dated June 13, 2017. The Notes were issued pursuant to an indenture dated April 29, 2013 and an officer’s certificate dated June 20, 2017, and rely on Apple’s Registration Statement on Form S-3 filed April 28, 2016. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 20 and December 20 beginning December 20, 2017, and the Notes mature June 20, 2027. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The filing lists related exhibits including the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of global note, legal opinion, and related consent.

A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive-force accusations stemming from a video of Hudson punching Jon “Chris” Erwin seven times in October 2011. The jury deliberated after two days of testimony and unanimously decided the force was reasonable from Hudson’s perspective. Erwin testified he suffered injuries requiring stitches and later physical therapy, and he complained jurors heard he was arrested but not that charges were dismissed for procedural reasons. Hudson testified he punched instead of throwing Erwin down to control him during an attempted arrest under the police department’s use-of-force policy. Attorneys presented competing views of whether the incident involved an intoxicated person and whether Hudson could have de-escalated. After the verdict, Hudson said he felt vindicated, while Erwin said his goal was to remove “bad police officers” and reiterated that he believes the evidence showed excessive force.

The passage describes how U.S. official statements about the war received little attention in Finnish press. It notes increasing Finnish irritation at German troops and Germany’s growing influence, including German control over press tone and Nazi-style censorship. It reports growing war weariness, including a January 3 trade union memorial to the Prime Minister requesting relief from harsh conditions and maldistribution of food, and it suggests widening divisions between Socialists and Conservatives. It also says common people resented holding Soviet Karelia when men were needed at home, and it speculates resistance could be worn down if Russia kept the Finnish front active. The latter part records U.S. diplomatic exchanges, including queries to Vyshinski about Soviet-Finnish government conversations and a conversation where Mr. Toivola agreed that recent Finnish trends carried danger and would send a telegram urging careful consideration, while discussing Finnish press dependence on Germany and attacks on the United States.

The passage discusses Enron’s rise and fall, describing its transformation from a pipeline company to a trading and marketing firm under Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay. It outlines Enron’s rapid growth, its “Gas Bank” concept, its emphasis on aggressive, knowledge-based hiring and performance-based culture, and its expanding ventures including telecommunications, broadband, and EnronOnline. It then describes how Enron’s fortunes declined amid negative media coverage, stock drops, and questions about accounting and new business. After Skilling resigned as CEO in February 2001, Lay and Enron announced changes, including a shift away from rapid trading and aspects of the performance review system, while Enron continued to face reputational and market challenges.

The passage is an Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018, including the cover page, index, and selected financial statements and notes. It presents unaudited consolidated cash flows, statements of operations, statements of comprehensive income, and consolidated balance sheets, with comparative figures for Q1 2017. It describes accounting policies and interim financial statement preparation, revenue recognition, return allowances, unearned revenue, and valuation approaches. Notes cover adopted and not-yet-adopted accounting pronouncements (including revenue, leases, income taxes, and restricted cash), fair value measurement and investment classifications, commitments and contingencies (including pledges, leases, tax contingencies, and legal proceedings), acquisitions (Ring Inc.), long-term debt and credit facilities, stockholders’ equity items, segment information (North America, International, AWS), and liquidity and capital resources. It also includes discussion of management’s discussion and analysis, including results of operations and changes in net sales, operating income, operating expenses, interest, other income/expense, and income taxes, along with forward-looking statements and risks related to those topics.

The passage discusses how two hockey teams’ play has been affected by penalties and adjustments in the playoffs. It says both teams’ situations are similar, with an emphasis on quicker play, faster puck movement through the neutral zone, and better defensive positioning. The speaker notes limited powerplay production and that major changes are not expected to suddenly generate offense, while highlighting strong penalty-killing performance by the opponent’s intelligent, quick players and defensemen. The passage also describes defensive restructuring after player trades, coaching and communication constraints during loud games, the difficulty of assessing series momentum because of power plays and penalty kills, and general coaching philosophy focused on adapting and relying on staff. It concludes with remarks about player deployment on the power play and the timing of when other lines may start scoring.

Process modeling is important in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) because material performance depends on properties determined by material structure, which is shaped by processing routes. Modeling processing steps is necessary to represent dynamic state changes during the material life cycle, and large-scale initiatives aim to formalize materials data and workflows using taxonomies, ontologies, and knowledge graphs. While multiple ontologies for process modeling in MSE exist, interoperability and reuse issues persist, partly due to limited adoption of ontology design patterns (ODPs), which can provide reusable templates if they are explicitly extracted and published.

The work focuses on scientific workflow modeling in MSE and the extraction of ODPs relevant to process representation. It uses expert-derived requirements (process structure, data/resources flow and parameters, and project goals and participant roles) and nine domain experts for evaluation. A baseline automated method is introduced that applies semantic similarity between natural-language requirement sentences and ontology textual metadata (e.g., labels and definitions) to select relevant ontology terms, then extracts modular ontology modules using ROBOT extraction methods. The extracted ODPs are evaluated with precision, recall, and F1-score against manually curated ground truth mappings.

Results summarize how different ontologies support requirement categories, with P-PLAN scoring highest for Process and Resource ODPs and PMDcore supporting all three categories. The paper discusses limitations including bias from annotation quality and requirement wording, independent processing of each ontology, and a focus on modularization as the main reuse strategy. The conclusion states that the approach supports scalable identification of reusable semantic structures for MSE process modeling, and future work will expand to more MSE subdomains, improve cross-ontology pattern identification, and enhance evaluation and publication of extracted patterns for community feedback.

FSU linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital Thursday, nearly six weeks after he was shot in the back of the head while driving his aunt home. Florida State said he is alert, responsive, and able to communicate, and he is being moved to Brooks Rehabilitation in Jacksonville for the next stage of his recovery. Four people were arrested in connection with the Aug. 31 shooting, which authorities described as mistaken identity.

Old Forge High School students organized a Math-a-thon at their school to benefit St. Jude’s Research Hospital, raising $3,864; donations were made for each math problem completed. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary on June 4, with other officers named for vice president, president-elect, treasurer, secretary, and assistant treasurer; the board will serve for two years and plans fundraisers including Attic Treasures (July 14–15) and Best of the Eagles Concert (Sept. 23). Hannah Perry Burgess presented a program on honey bees at a DAR meeting focused on conservationism, and she is described as a fifth-generation beekeeper involved in bee conservation.

GoDaddy said it has given The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain after the site posted an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed in a Charlottesville attack. GoDaddy spokesman Dan Race said the decision was prompted by the post and that it could incite additional violence, violating GoDaddy’s terms of service. The site later claimed it had been hacked and would shut down, but a contributor said this was a prank. Publisher Andrew Anglin said he was trying to regain control of the site, while contributor Andrew Auernheimer said GoDaddy had not contacted the site and that an alternate domain name could be used if needed. Race also said only the domain is with GoDaddy, not the site’s content. The passage also describes the site’s past harassment campaigns, legal issues involving Tanya Gersh, and prior service bans or advertising restrictions.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales was notified of two cases of salmonella gastroenteritis after attendees reported going to an Eid al-Adha barbecue in a public park in Cardiff, UK. Further cases were found among event attendees, and an outbreak investigation was initiated using case finding, interviews, questionnaires, and stool sample testing, alongside cohort and nested case-control analyses. Whole genome sequencing showed Salmonella Typhimurium isolates from cases were genetically indistinguishable, and food and environmental samples indicated contamination linked to meat preparation from local butchers. The outbreak analysis identified consumption of a traditional raw liver dish (“marrara”) as the most likely infection vehicle (aOR 49.99), highlighting the need for culturally sensitive food hygiene advice and that future investigations should consider culturally relevant dishes beyond routine questionnaires.

An appeals court ruled the federal government cannot legally stop trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S., though other legal challenges may still affect owners. The North Carolina-based United States Association of Reptile Keepers sued in 2013 to overturn a nationwide ban on importing certain constrictor species or transporting them across state lines. Wildlife officials had banned several python and anaconda species starting in 2012, with additional species added in 2015, citing risks to native wildlife in places like the Florida Everglades. The ruling does not change bans on importing or “injurious” species, nor Florida’s prohibition on keeping pythons as pets. The D.C. Circuit said the Lacey Act does not authorize restricting interstate trade among the contiguous 49 states, upholding a lower court’s finding and declining to address the scientific data behind the ban. Wildlife service officials said they will work with the Department of Justice to identify impacts and next steps. Attorneys for the reptile keepers said the decision restores owners’ ability to attend trade shows, seek veterinary care, and move with their pets.

The speaker discusses a hockey series, focusing on changes in pace and momentum after a key opportunity by Holik, and how the team improved by slowing the tempo and starting to hang onto the puck, which increased confidence. They say the team has generally lacked “advantages” in multiple areas, while faceoffs and puck control were positives, and that matching up particular lines (including putting five transition players together) helped. They describe coaching emphasis on emotion and consistency, travel and preparation, the importance of winning faceoffs and maintaining leg strength when tired, and the need to “outplay” the opponent in more areas to win upcoming games. They also mention goaltending and that both teams have championship stakes, with the outcome still feeling “up for grabs.”

The passage argues that loosening home responsibilities and “wilful sterility” are harmful to the nation, citing areas where birth rates are below death rates and claiming this sin results in “national death” and “race death.” It then urges Congress to address two issues: developing American shipping, including laws to encourage it and improved fast-mail and steamship communication with South America; and revising U.S. currency laws due to defects in the national bank act, citing fluctuations in call money rates and rising commercial rates that harm commerce. It states that proposed changes are complicated and should not impair the value of 2% U.S. bonds pledged for circulation, and it mentions a feasible plan in which national banks could issue certain taxed notes to drive them back when not needed for legitimate trade, to handle periods of stringency.

The passage argues that fad diets and extreme approaches like juice cleanses or cutting out carbohydrates may cause short-term weight loss but do not help achieve healthy, sustainable results. Dietician Bonnie Taub-Dix says weight loss should focus on reconnecting with food, building a healthy relationship with one’s body, and aiming to look and feel best rather than feeling punished. She also states that non-diet approaches are more sustainable and encourage healthier habits than strict dieting that leads to deprivation and cravings. The passage adds that fat can be an important part of the diet and emphasizes moderation.

The Gold Coast Titans signed veteran fullback Michael Gordon to a two-year NRL deal after he was released by the Sydney Roosters. With coach Garth Brennan lacking an established fullback following Jarryd Hayne’s departure, Gordon is expected to fill the No.1 jersey immediately and may take over goal kicking after this year’s 72-of-92 attempts. Gordon said he was excited about returning home and contributing to the club’s success. Roosters coach Trent Robinson praised Gordon’s experience and impact on and off the field.

The passage argues that Nick Foles, the backup turned Super Bowl starter for the Philadelphia Eagles, could be key to ending the franchise’s first Super Bowl win since 1960. It describes Foles’ postseason performance and notes that Carson Wentz previously led the Eagles to a nine-game winning streak and an 11–2 record before injuring his knee. It then discusses the matchup against the New England Patriots and raises questions about what happens next for Foles, including whether the Eagles would keep him or trade him after a potential Super Bowl LII win. The passage says Wentz is expected to return as a starter in 2018, and it characterizes Eagles management’s likely focus on Wentz while considering Foles’ contract situation and possible trade interest from other teams.

The passage describes the Coppock Curve strategy, a long-term momentum indicator devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 under a mandate from the Episcopal Church to find long-term investment opportunities. The Coppock curve is calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average (WMA) of the sum of two rate-of-change (ROC) indicators using 11- and 14-month periods, and it is used to identify significant market swings. The strategy signals a long entry when the curve crosses above the zero line and an exit when it crosses below. Examples using the S&P 500 index on a monthly chart are provided, including two trades with profits of about 80% and 65%. It reports 12 trades over 63 years, highlights reduced drawdowns and more time out of the market, notes that all trades were winners, and states that risk-adjusted return exceeds buy-and-hold. The passage concludes that the strategy aims to exploit the bullish bias of markets by filtering corrective phases and mentions that related trading rules are compiled into a purchasable package.

The passage is a lightly edited transcript of a “First Opinion Podcast” interview with Morgan McSweeney (“Dr. Noc”), a biotech professional and social media influencer with 4 million followers and a Ph.D. in pharmaceutical sciences and immunology. He discusses his approach to science-based public health communication, including using “edutainment” to make topics engaging and digestible, the origin of the “Dr. Noc” name, and how he became more comfortable over time as his content gained reach. He describes content formats such as reacting to incorrect claims and explaining research with practical takeaways, and he explains that he avoids directly targeting people who vehemently disagree, focusing instead on audiences confused about public health issues. He also outlines how he chooses topics (often based on recent questions, comments, and news) and how he tries to incorporate nuance, especially in response to high-profile stories like acetaminophen and autism. McSweeney addresses audience trust, saying he aims to present credible information while acknowledging he cannot reach everyone and that more science communicators are needed. He describes separating his social media content from his day job to minimize conflicts, his employer relationship, how he handles negative comments, and how sharing personal details—such as mentioning his wife—helped followers see him as a real person and build trust. He also says he sometimes does lighter, personal content to strengthen audience relationships and has given seminars to students and teachers.

The speaker congratulates members of the 100th Congress during the Constitution’s 200th anniversary, arguing the Constitution should be celebrated for its ongoing youthfulness and guiding words and acts. He shares a story about honorifics used in 1787 and declares members should be titled “honorable.” He praises the Speaker of the House and Senate Majority Leader, describes economic improvements since six years earlier, and says America is at peace with freedom advancing, while acknowledging a major regret regarding U.S. actions in Iran and promising accountability. He urges Congress to pass defense and foreign affairs budgets, criticizes Soviet military spending and Soviet support for client states, and calls for support for efforts in Afghanistan and opposition to Communist Nicaragua in Central America. He emphasizes defense measures like the Strategic Defense Initiative, outlines trade goals through the Uruguay round and a U.S.-Canada free trade arrangement, and focuses on domestic reforms including balanced-budget and line-item veto measures, welfare reform, protection for the elderly from catastrophic illness, competitiveness policies, education goals, and workplace retraining and job mobility. He concludes by stressing the Constitution’s principle “We the people,” portraying Americans’ character through that idea, and recounts Franklin’s remark that the Constitution’s future is a rising—not setting—sun.

The passage refers to the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors Technical Reference Manual for system MMU features and notes that L4 Fast and L4 Slow peripheral memory map regions are broken out into Table 3-5 and Table 3-6. It states that some regions are decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 subsystem and are not physically part of the L4 Slow, are included only for Cortex-A8 memory map reference, and are reserved for other masters. It describes the DDR DMM TILER extended addressing map, adding an extra 4 GBytes enabled by a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame buffer access, which is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can access single views via a 512-MB TILER region. The passage also explains how terminal function tables identify external signal names, pin multiplexing details, pin types, pullup/pulldown options, and de-selected input states. Finally, it includes Table 4-1 entries for boot configuration terminal functions, describing several GPMC-related multiplexed pins and how boot mode input bits (BTMODE) are sampled at reset to determine functions and boot configuration.

The passage is a discussion emphasizing the need to work hard, not be outworked, and “play for the guy beside you.” It contrasts losing despite great effort with losing in a way the speaker says is not acceptable “the way things shake down.” The speaker says the team played well in the first period of the last game, won only one game they “came to play,” and believes their power play was effective against Pittsburgh while the team focused on defense to limit Pittsburgh’s scoring. The speaker also says the team is taking the play into Pittsburgh’s zone, getting shots but missing the net, and that players are not in sync—passing when they should shoot and shooting when they should pass—so they need to come out and play for each other.

Dana Harsell, chair of the UND campus senate, said the executive committee will discuss a draft proclamation in good faith at its Wednesday meeting to determine whether the University Senate supports it. The draft, sent last week to representatives of all 11 campuses in the North Dakota University System, cites a “crisis of confidence” tied to budget cuts, consolidation efforts described as misguided, and a lack of consideration for long-term effects. It also alleges insufficient support from the NDUS and the State Board of Higher Education, and calls for improved advocacy through supportive collaborations between campus and state leadership, including a Higher Education Summit with campus stakeholders, Chancellor Mark Hagerott, the SBHE, and Gov. Doug Burgum. The resolution warns that without immediate collaborative action, the system and institutions may be unable to fulfill their missions. Harsell said the UND executive committee will set the agenda and decide whether the resolution may be supported by the wider body, noting that changes could make the document moot. At the time UND received it, NDSU Faculty Senate did not plan to send it beyond the 11 system campuses.

The author describes building many scalable, reliable distributed systems from scratch, noting that reusing components or applying patterns is often difficult and leads to wasted time and less polished systems. They say containers and container orchestrators changed distributed development by providing objects and interfaces for expressing core patterns and building reusable containerized components. The book aims to bring practitioners of distributed systems together by offering a shared language and common standard library, and to capture repeatable, generic patterns to make reliable distributed system development more approachable and efficient.

An Energy Central Research Report Watch email dated February 20, 2002 provides information about a bi-weekly HTML newsletter for professionals in the power industry. It lists recently published research reports, including downloadable and hard copy items such as “Major European Utility Profiles,” “Home Energy Improvement Loans,” “Home Energy Audits,” and various Minsight country utility industry reports, as well as Datamonitor reports, SCIENTECH InfoGrids, and other company profiles. The email also includes ordering contact information (Mark Johnson at 800-459-2233), options to switch to a text format, and instructions to unsubscribe.

National Weather Service Lubbock, Texas zone forecasts effective Sunday, March 18, 2018 through Sunday, March 25, 2018 indicate windy conditions with west winds and blowing dust late Sunday evening, along with a Wind Advisory until 7 AM Monday. Sunday night lows are mostly in the 30s to lower 50s. Monday is windy and sunny with highs from the mid 50s to lower 70s and northwest winds around 20–35 mph with gusts. Monday night is colder and mostly clear with lows from the upper 20s to mid 30s. Conditions turn sunny through Tuesday, with highs generally in the 60s, then mostly sunny and warmer Wednesday and Thursday (upper 70s to upper 80s). Friday through Sunday forecasts remain mostly sunny, with highs ranging from the upper 70s to around 90 degrees. Some zones mention patchy blowing dust and occasional thunderstorm chances on Saturday nights.

The lecture explains the finance “business case” for sustainable real estate, covering how sustainability relates to green, healthy, and climate-resilient buildings. It describes a chain from end users (tenants) valuing sustainability and paying higher rents, which can translate into higher returns for owners, purchase prices for developers, and the need for capital to build, buy, or invest. It then places real estate within the broader concept of sustainable finance, discussing how climate risk is treated as a financial risk and how sustainable finance incorporates externalities and preferences into asset pricing. A “sandwich” and four-quadrant framework is used to connect physical-space decisions with capital-market funding, emphasizing portfolio theory and efficient frontiers. The lecture argues that green buildings can shift capital and improve returns/risk profiles compared with brown buildings, while also noting market frictions and limited supply. The debt section focuses on mortgage default risk, including climate risks such as flooding and wildfire, and discusses subsidized roles of federal programs and mortgage insurers, plus efforts to incorporate climate risk into appraisal models. The lecture also presents a “green mortgage” mechanism, with examples of how energy efficiency can reduce default risk and free up borrower capacity via lower energy bills, leading to larger loan-to-value lending or financing for renovations. It concludes by introducing private equity on the equity side, describing commingled funds with GP and LP roles and how firms incorporate ESG into investment memos, due diligence, and management/disposition actions.

The passage discusses lineup considerations and matchups involving Patrick Kane, including how he views players like Suter’s reach and defensive roles such as back-checking. It reflects on Kane’s experience playing in Vancouver, winning and losing the Stanley Cup as the defending champions, and taking in the moment while facing challenges in a series. The passage also mentions giving up goals against Pittsburgh, the importance of depth and team defense, and Kane’s focus on getting the puck and making plays rather than emphasizing scoring or points.

Treasury market bears on Wednesday recouped some losses from the prior day after anxiety about instability in Italy’s government prompted a safe-haven rush into U.S. government debt. CME data showed open interest in benchmark Treasury and interest rate futures fell by more than 400,000 contracts on Tuesday, with over 266,000 fewer 2-year note futures contracts and about 137,000 fewer 10-year futures contracts; trading volume in the 10-year benchmark hit a record. Analysts said some short positions were closed and that Treasuries may have been oversold, while yields remained below a seven-year high reached earlier. On Wednesday, the 10-year yield rose to 2.855 percent as Italian politicians moved toward forming a government, reducing some safe-haven holdings. A J.P. Morgan survey indicated clients were the least bearish since April 2017. Bearish bets, however, remain exposed to European political developments, including Italy’s government formation and a potential no-confidence vote in Spain.

A council in Hampshire has banned bouncy castles and other inflatables on its land after a three-year-old girl in Norfolk died following an incident where an inflatable trampoline “exploded” at Gorleston Beach on Sunday. Havant Borough Council said it had not had incidents in its area but will keep the ban in place until an inquiry into the cause of the explosion is complete, so the risk can be managed by event organisers. The ban will be reviewed after the inquiry’s outcome is known.

Gold prices surged above $4,000 per ounce on Tuesday as investors sought safety amid rising expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will ease monetary policy in coming months. The rally followed weak U.S. retail and manufacturing data, leading traders to anticipate possible rate cuts by early 2026 and to see gold as more attractive given retreating yields and a softer dollar. Analysts said the move reflects a broader flight to safety, with central banks continuing to accumulate gold, and that geopolitical tensions also supported demand. Analysts caution that stronger Fed signals or better U.S. growth could cause short-term corrections.

Italian and Spanish Wikipedia sites blocked readers from viewing articles in protest of an EU vote supporting a new Copyright Directive. The vote, on a controversial set of proposals affecting Articles 11 and 13, was backed by the European Committee on Legal Affairs and is due to be decided by the European Parliament on 5 July. Critics said the bill would require content filtering systems and include a “link tax,” and warned it could restrict internet openness and put Wikipedia at risk, while some responses argued the wording is vague and could still harm platforms like Wikipedia. English Wikipedia did not go dark, showing a banner instead; Jimmy Wales said site decisions are made separately by each territory.

The speaker recalls an earlier game, noting it was exciting because his daughter was born the day before, and that Jeff Reese later changed his style, which worked out well. He says he has been jittery and anxious while waiting to start a series, and mentions a short break to rest players and settle injuries. He describes facing two skilled, leading opponents and emphasizes trying to shut them down with top lines and best defense. He says he is not focused on the other team’s goalie, but will instead drive the net and put pucks on goal. He also discusses past circumstances, including stomach and groin surgery that left him injured in Norfolk and affected his ability to play, and says his goal over the last few days was to win the Stanley Cup rather than the conference finals. Finally, he expects the upcoming games to be heated and physical.

Twin Rivers Council of the Boy Scouts, serving youths from Columbia County to the Canadian border, is asking families to sign girls up for Cub Scouts. The effort follows the Boy Scouts of America’s announcement that the program will open to girls in fall 2018, and Twin Rivers Council has permission to begin enrolling immediately. The council aims to enroll girls and families by spring to attend Cub Scout day and summer camping programs, and plans to enroll as many interested families and girls as possible through March 31. The goal is up to 125 girls in kindergarten through third grade in Cub Scout packs. Interested parents can use the “Be a Scout” website or call 518-869-6436. Mark Switzer said the program helps young people learn and grow and that the council is modifying Cub Scouting to better fit modern families’ needs for shared activities and parent involvement as volunteer leaders.

Audi has been teasing its upcoming Q8, described as the German automaker’s new flagship SUV. The production Q8’s design is said to closely match the Q8 Concept shown at the 2017 Detroit Auto Show, featuring a prominent hexagonal grille, vertical slats, large air intakes, and headlamps. Audi is expected to hold the Q8’s world premiere soon, with an event in Shanghai in early June. The Q8 will be built on Volkswagen Group’s MLB modular platform, which also underpins the Q7 and high-performance models like the Bentley Bentayga and Lamborghini Urus. A plug-in hybrid powertrain in the Q8 Concept was rated at 443 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque, but the powertrain for the production Q8 is unclear.

Earth Day, held annually on April 22 since 1970, is described as an official holiday for groups called “Big Environment,” which the author says work to prevent supposedly evil corporations from ruining Earth. The author recalls early 1990s cleanups of roadside trash, but argues Earth Day has become more like a spring ritual that humanizes and deifies nature while elevating human responsibility and power. They contend environmental policy has become politicized, with “Big Environment” now driving politics like “Big Oil.” The passage criticizes groups they say prioritize environmental health above other concerns, citing South Portland’s Clear Skies Ordinance as costing city taxpayers millions in court and harming the local oil industry by banning Canadian oil sands within city limits. The author also criticizes wind power, arguing wind projects damage landscapes, are noisy and dangerous to birds, and cannot generate enough electricity, using Maine’s wind capacity as an example. They further accuse “Big Environment” of using fear to raise donations, referencing tar sands controversy. The author concludes that instead of ongoing fear, Earth Day should be spent outdoors doing something fun, asserting nature is for enjoyment rather than political or financial gain.

The passage presents Investing.com headlines and market commentary. It mentions Netflix stock closing lower after Elon Musk urged followers to cancel its service, the US government shutdown continuing after a GOP funding bill failed in the Senate, and the S&P 500 closing above 6,700 on expectations of limited shutdown impact. It also notes AI-picked stocks for October and an ADP report showing the biggest private payroll drop in 2.5 years, fueling Fed cut bets. The commentary states the S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July (+7.8% year-to-date) but later slipped on the first day of August, with volatility and credit spreads described as seeing a seasonal upturn. It says investors are increasing exposure to tech stocks and that US electricity demand reached a new all-time high, while short-term technicals are described as less stable due to concerns around breadth and potential further selling to reach oversold conditions. The passage includes promotional content for an Investing.com stock screener and a risk disclosure.

SpaceX launched an unmanned Falcon 9 from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center to send a Dragon capsule to the International Space Station, scheduled to arrive Wednesday. The 6,400 pounds of cargo mostly includes experiments, including 20 mice, and also includes ice cream. NASA packed cups of vanilla, chocolate, and birthday cake ice cream and ice cream candy bars for the station’s six-person crew, using extra freezer space. U.S. astronaut Peggy Whitson, in orbit since November, is expected to welcome the treats. SpaceX plans to land the leftover booster back at Cape Canaveral.

Legislators met in the Finance Committee on 3 July as the Government sought a supplementary $20 million for the current budget, with half coming from government reserves and half from the Environment Protection Fund (EPF). The Health Ministry requested $8 million to offset rising indigent and Seafarers health costs. Bodden Town West MLA Chris Saunders said options should be considered to manage these costs and discussed moving toward a national health insurance system, while Health Minister Dwayne Seymour agreed that government is reviewing its options and asked for a review of the children’s national health policy regarding free healthcare for children. The funding request was later approved, and Saunders abstained from voting on the EPF withdrawal.

A “blitz” is a defensive play in which five or more defenders rush into the offensive backfield to attack the ball carrier, disrupt the offense, and pressure or sack the quarterback. While teams typically send about four players to rush the quarterback, a blitz is designed to send more (often five to seven, sometimes eight) to reach the quarterback faster, but it carries risk because it leaves fewer defenders to cover receivers and passing options. Coaches use blitzes as part of defensive strategy, led by the defensive coordinator who calls defensive plays to outsmart the offense and get off the field quickly. Types of blitzes include conventional blitzes, zone blitzes, safety blitzes, cornerback blitzes, zero blitzes, and run blitzes aimed at stopping the run. Offenses can beat blitzes by using quick passes, relying on quarterback mobility, and calling max protection blocking schemes to slow the blitz and create opportunities to find open receivers.

The passage lists five romantic scenes in Indian cinema that were made possible by VFX teams, highlighting their role in creating challenging shots and dreamlike romantic sequences. It names Baahubali (“Dheevara”) with VFX by Makuta, Befikre with VFX by yFX Notorious, Shivaay with VFX by NY VFXWAALA, Sanam Re with VFX by Pixel D Love, and Prem Ratan Dhan Payo with VFX by NY VFXWAALA, describing specific VFX elements such as butterflies, waterfall effects, cliff kissing made with ocean views, snow-filled love sequences, and set or double-role effects.

The passage is NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 30, 2016, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It includes financial statements (unaudited) and notes, such as condensed consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, and cash flows; accounting policy disclosures; discussion of recently adopted and not-yet-adopted accounting standards; stock-based compensation; net income per share; income taxes; marketable securities and fair value; amortizable intangible assets; balance sheet components; derivative financial instruments; guarantees and product warranty liability; and details of convertible and long-term debt and related share repurchases and dividends. It also provides segment information for the GPU and Tegra Processor businesses and includes management’s discussion of results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2017, including revenue, margins, operating expenses, and drivers of segment revenue changes.

The passage explains market sentiment and sentiment indicators, including the AAII sentiment index. Market sentiment is described as the aggregate attitude of investors and traders toward the market (bullish, neutral, or bearish), likened to “Mr. Market,” who swings between moods. A sentiment indicator, such as the AAII index (published weekly since the 1980s by the American Association of Individual Investors), measures members’ views on the stock market’s direction over the next six months. The passage summarizes a set of backtests using weekly data, evaluating a strategy based on bullish versus bearish readings of the AAII bull-bear spread and measuring performance over the following four weeks. Results described include higher returns after bearish readings (e.g., thresholds like -20) and mixed or lower returns after very bullish/euphoric readings (e.g., thresholds above 40), with the authors suggesting other indicators may be better for short-term trading.

The passage says Antarctic krill help influence the global carbon cycle through their waste and that they eject compact leftover-food masses to sink to the seafloor. It also states that when krill are contaminated with plastic, they eject more food, but plastic’s overall effects are described as unclear.

Coach Sutter and the speaker discuss playoff offense, lineup flexibility, and the importance of having top-end players up to speed. They note that it’s difficult to remove players, referencing decisions made during a game based on the score. The coach comments that talking about performance is complicated because teams can play better in losses than wins. Preparation varies due to travel and limited practice, but the team’s emotional approach hasn’t changed for about two months; they describe learning to handle situations through prior series breaks. The team emphasizes routine and fundamentals such as nutrition, hydration, and travel adjustments. They highlight a specific physical, goal-scoring player’s importance, describe the role of their captain and team identity, and say they are not concerned about confidence heading into the finals. They conclude that the series has been close with limited gaps between games, and they stress focusing on “little things” during shifts.

The passage argues that rapid technological and social change prevents initial LIS (Library and Information Science) academic programmes in Romania from preparing graduates with enough knowledge and competences for labour-market demands, making lifelong learning essential. It describes Romania’s library system (National Library, public libraries, education-system libraries, specialised libraries) and the involvement of two ministries and two professional associations. Academic LIS education began after 1999 following communist-era neglect, and the passage outlines three training pathways for librarians: a LIS bachelor degree, a bachelor in another field plus LIS post-graduation, and a bachelor in another field plus competences assessed via occupational standards. It also notes limits of formal and non-formal training due to certification difficulties and limited financial support, despite legislation requiring public libraries to allocate at least 5% of personnel expenses to professional training. The passage then presents Romania’s 2012 occupational standard for “Librarian (higher education),” issued after occupational analysis, listing transversal and specific competences and detailing promotion-related activities and responsibilities. It concludes that these standards are important for professional assessment nationally but that higher education institutions and methodological libraries should better reflect new competences, while stereotypes about the LIS profession hinder youth enrollment.

Residents of the Cottage Grove community in Greensboro, North Carolina, report a long-term decline in housing conditions, especially at Avalon Trace Apartments, citing boarded windows, trash on the property, sewage leaks, inadequate heating, roaches, and mold. Mold has been linked to asthma cases, including in children, and Stephen Sills of UNCG’s Center for Housing and Community Studies says there is a statistical correlation between substandard housing and asthma instances. Collaborative Cottage Grove received a $250,000 BUILD Health Challenge grant to address housing and health needs, with Greensboro Housing Coalition, Cone Health, and UNCG collaborating to identify asthma “hot spots” and map findings to direct residents to appropriate services. Cone Health is also matching the grant with an additional $250,000, and the Guilford County Department of Public Health is a partner, offering a mobile farmers market and a diabetes prevention program.

China’s power generation in July rose 8.6% year-on-year to 604.7 billion kWh, the highest monthly record since May 2014, driven by higher thermal power output, which was the highest since December. For January to July, total generation increased 6.8% to 3.57 trillion kWh. The breakdown showed thermal power at 433.4 billion kWh (up 10.5%), hydro at 124.6 billion kWh (up 0.2%), nuclear at 23.1 billion kWh (up 16.5%), wind at 18.0 billion kWh (up 11.6%), and solar at 5.6 billion kWh (up 26.7%).

The Miami Hurricane argues that student newsrooms face threats such as defunding or absorption into school communication curricula, which reduces editorial independence. The passage says student journalists need opportunities to practice outside the classroom and that campus newspapers should be supported without being controlled. It emphasizes that belonging to a student journalism organization provides accountability to a code of ethics and helps counter biases. It also states that attacks on collegiate journalism harm students’ understanding of independent press and the difference between news and public relations. The call is to #SaveStudentNewsrooms, asking other schools for funding and editorial independence, and encouraging readers to support student journalism and watch for programs and budget cuts that endanger it.

The passage describes information design in microeconomics and decision theory, contrasting the Bayesian persuasion model—where only engineered correlations between signals and world states matter—with behavioral findings that show decisions depend on how information is framed. It argues that in real persuasion, elements beyond signal correlations, including tangential information, text phrasing, and non-textual cues, affect effectiveness. To address challenges in modeling and optimizing framing, the work proposes using large language models (LLMs) to simulate human behavior via a framing-to-belief “oracle.” The authors contribute a formal model combining Bayesian persuasion with framing, defining three optimization variants: recommendation-only (fixed framing), framing-only (fixed recommendation), and joint optimization (both framing and recommendation). They report theoretical results that framing-only optimization is computationally hard (NP-hard) and highly sensitive to errors, while joint optimization is more tractable, with continuity properties and a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme. Empirically, they implement a hill-climbing approach using LLMs and analytical methods, test it on two case studies (realtor property pitching and clothing brand advertising), and further validate with human subjects. The passage also outlines broader related work on algorithmic information design and information design with LLMs, and provides model definitions for Bayesian persuasion/signaling and for framing via a mapping from framings to induced beliefs.

The passage describes Germany’s response to allegations about Belgium, asserting that Germany offered to guarantee Belgium’s territory and independence and to compensate for damages, while Belgium refused. It states that responsibility for Belgium’s fate rests with Belgium and the powers that drew it into its stance, and that Germany protested charges as groundless. It also discusses Germany’s view that an opening to peace depended on the adversary’s decision, which the enemy governments declined. The passage further includes a message from Persia’s minister welcoming U.S.-mediated peace terms, noting that Persian territory was disturbed despite neutrality, and hoping the U.S. will assist Persia in maintaining integrity and rights. Finally, it reports from Elkus in Turkey that a German ambassador conveyed concerns about intended Greek deportation, German influence in Turkey being minimal, and a willingness to cooperate to prevent deportation of women and children, with a suggestion that pressure on Germany could be effective.

Jaguars’ Travon Walker underwent left wrist surgery on Monday and will be listed as day-to-day, with a chance he could play against the Chiefs. He injured his wrist during the second quarter of Jacksonville’s 26-21 win over San Francisco on Sunday, walked to the sideline and did not return. Walker, the No. 1 overall pick in 2022, has missed only two games in his career, both during his rookie season, and is second on the team with two sacks, 12 tackles, and one pass breakup.

The passage explains how the adapter container pattern modifies application-container interfaces to meet common predefined interfaces, enabling consistent monitoring and logging across heterogeneous applications. It gives examples using Prometheus exporters for monitoring Redis and Fluentd adapters to normalize log formats, including Redis slow-query logging and Apache Storm logging. It also describes using adapter containers to add richer health checks to database containers without modifying the original images, emphasizing decoupling, reuse, and dedicated resources. The passage then shifts to multi-node distributed patterns, introducing microservices and replicated load-balanced services, including stateless replication with readiness probes, session-tracked services, and application-layer replicated patterns such as caching with Varnish and SSL termination with nginx, along with their deployment in Kubernetes. It continues by contrasting sharded services with replicated services, covering design and performance considerations for sharded caches, shard selection via hashing and modulo, consistent hashing, hot sharding, and the scatter/gather pattern for parallelizing computation across replicas, including examples like distributed document search. Finally, it introduces function-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven processing, discussing benefits, challenges, when FaaS is a poor fit, and patterns such as request/response decoration for FaaS, plus an event-driven example using two-factor authentication via asynchronously triggered functions.
A new study confirms that pasteurization of milk completely inactivates the H5N1 bird flu virus, even though inactive viral proteins may remain.

The speaker says their team missed several scoring chances and failed to score enough goals, including in the second period. They believe the loss was not because they were outplayed but because they “beat themselves,” citing issues like not being sharp enough, not skating as well as they could, and not making the most of good opportunities. Both goalies are described as playing well, and the team emphasizes needing to hit the net, create more chances, and score at least one goal (and more than one) despite strong opponents and a high number of power plays by the other team. They also note they did not take advantage of an opportunity to go one game away from the Stanley Cup and say the next game is an “opportunity” since the series is best of three.

The speaker says the team will play hard and in the same way as early in the season, and believes they have good chances against a veteran, well-balanced opponent that is the defending Stanley Cup champion. They note the opponent has a solid defense and goalie Dominik Hasek, and that any line can score, so they must be ready. The speaker adds that they are a confident veteran team with few young players, that preparation helps for big games, and that they avoid focusing on “long shots.” They describe success in terms of different players stepping up, including Todd Krygier and Brian Bellows, and emphasize having fun, playing as a team, and not taking excessive pressure to score every night. The speaker also mentions personal improvement this year, credits speed and shot as strengths, and says a good center increases scoring opportunities.

Negotiated rule-making committee members met Tuesday at the Department of Education in Washington, D.C., after two days of talks. Department officials said they would not negotiate their proposed student loan regulations for now, including a fixed definition of “professional” programs limited to 10 specific degrees (pharmacy, dentistry, medicine, osteopathy, law, optometry, podiatry, veterinary medicine, chiropractic medicine, and theology). Department director of policy coordination Tamy Abernathy said the list is not exhaustive but is fixed for now, with flexibility to expand it through future rule making. The department’s stance could affect health-care graduate programs not on the list by subjecting them to annual and overall student loan caps, according to the passage. At the end of Tuesday’s meeting, committee members submitted a separate definition that would be discussed Wednesday, and they planned to vote on the regulatory changes after another week in November. Education Under Secretary Nicholas Kent said the department is negotiating in good faith while aiming to curb excessive graduate borrowing. Committee members raised concerns about the proposed list, including omissions such as mental health practitioners, and several members drafted a new proposal to discuss with department officials the next day.

ESA’s JUICE probe will explore Jupiter and three of its largest moons—Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa. The mission recently received NASA approval, moving it from the design phase to implementation, with a reported total cost of $114.4 million. JUICE is scheduled to launch in 2022 and is expected to reach Jupiter by 2030, where it will remain in the planet’s magnetosphere and explore the region for three years. It will use a 10-instrument suite, including NASA-provided components such as the Ultraviolet Spectrograph (UVS) and parts of the Particle Environment Package (PEP) and Radar for Icy Moon Exploration (RIME), to observe the system’s chemistry and study habitability, particularly regarding Europa.

Drake University’s Student Activities Board (SAB) co-chairs for the Drake Relays are Karoline Sandusky and Meghan Mulligan. Sandusky, a junior public relations major with a Spanish minor, and Mulligan, a junior studying accounting with a marketing minor, joined SAB their first year. Sandusky previously co-chaired Blitz Day, where the Painted Street theme, band, and applications are released. Painted Street square selections are based on creativity and how well designs incorporate the 2018 Relays theme announced at Blitz Day, not on a first-come or rotation system. After the theme was announced April 11, organizations had until April 16 at 5 p.m. to submit designs to SAB for the 54-square display. The Disability Action and Awareness Committee (DAAC) reported that paint for small organizations is expensive because organizations must buy their own paint and equipment, though the University provides cans of paint for the paint fight. Anna Jensen, a junior studying news and public relations and president of SAB, described painting over old squares as emotional because she previously helped choose them.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff at BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side law firms found the group shifted further to the left.
