In 2023–2024, 92.45% of contributions went to Democrats, up from a 6-to-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio in 2017–2020. Derek Muller of the University of Notre Dame Law School said attorneys and staff contributed about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups versus about $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Among the nation’s top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton, Fried, Frank, and Mintz Levin had the highest shares of contributions to Democratic campaigns, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree Deakins had the lowest.

The passage alleges that Washington, DC lawmaker Trayon White has blamed Jews for weather conditions, and it claims anti-Semitism is a serious problem within the Democrat Party and is tolerated by national media. It cites Louis Farrakhan’s past remarks about Jews and then lists nine Democrat lawmakers it says have connections to Farrakhan, including Barack Obama, Keith Ellison, Maxine Waters, Barbara Lee, Danny Davis, André Carson, James Clyburn, Al Green, and Gregory Meeks, describing various instances of meetings, appearances, attendance, or refusals to denounce Farrakhan.

A 25-year-old man, Olusola Simeon, was arraigned and convicted by a Magistrate court in Osogbo for assaulting his girlfriend, Fadunsi Alaba. He admitted guilt. The prosecutor, Jafani Muslim, said Simeon assaulted her on July 2, 2018 at about 9:15 pm at Agowande Area, Osogbo, inflicting injuries, and that the offence contravened section 355 of the Criminal Code. The court found him guilty and remanded him in Ilesha prison custody, adjourning the case to August 3 for sentencing.

The lecture reviews different formulations of the wave equation, emphasizing that writing the second-order equation as a first-order symmetric system yields real eigenvalues \(c\) and \(-c\), corresponding to waves traveling in opposite directions. It discusses a typical real-world situation with variable coefficients and high-frequency oscillating forcing, noting that large spatial steps cause poor numerical accuracy. The instructor then analyzes the standard wave equation using exponential test functions and derives solutions traveling along characteristics with speeds \(\pm c\), matching two initial conditions (initial displacement and initial velocity). The discussion moves to discretization: first semidiscretization (space discrete, time continuous), where the discrete spatial second difference introduces a non-linear “dispersion” factor involving \(2-2\cos(k\Delta x)\) and a sine-over-argument (sinc) behavior for small \(k\Delta x\); then full discretization (space and time discrete), where a growth factor \(g\) leads to a stability condition depending on the Courant number \(r\). Stability requires \(r<1\) (with instability when \(r>1\)), and the lecture concludes by noting that the next topic will be a staggered-grid approach.

A 29-year-old man from Grande Prairie, Wally Adams, was located in Calgary on Aug. 3 and arrested for possession of child pornography and making child pornography available. RCMP executed a search warrant in Grande Prairie on Aug. 2 based on information from the National Child Exploitation Coordination Centre in Ottawa. Adams was arrested the day after the search with assistance from the Calgary Police Service. He has been released from custody and is scheduled to appear in provincial court on Sept. 27; the investigation is ongoing. Police are asking the public to contact Grande Prairie RCMP at 780-830-5700 or Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-8477.

A San Juan High School baseball program in Citrus Heights says someone is allegedly posing as the team to solicit sponsorships from local businesses. The assistant coach, PJ Peterson, says this has already cost an auto repair shop about $1,400 and worries other businesses could be deceived. Peterson learned of the scheme after a business owner contacted him about a sign he paid for and then realized the sponsorship request looked fake. The soliciting company is called “Athletic Sports,” has no website, and uses a UPS store postal box. The team has filed a police report, posted the flyer online, and advises businesses to check directly with the school or program before donating.

The passage discusses hockey team performance and leadership decisions, including praise for player George McPhee, described as having elite hockey sense and compete. It recounts an expansion draft period, roster-management choices, and a philosophy of competing hard and improving daily. It also covers emotional circumstances tied to opening night ceremonies and community support after losses, with players and staff volunteering to help. The passage includes reflections on team identity, challenges around the first expansion draft in a salary cap era, and how expectations were approached as “one series at a time,” focusing on preparing to win the next game.

TSX was slightly higher, with Canada National Railway shares boosting industrial stocks and steady gold prices supporting precious metals miners. The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 12.22 points (0.08%) to 15,564.28 by 9:41 a.m. ET. CN Rail gained 1.2%, and Restaurant Brands International rose 3.7% after reporting a better-than-expected profit. Materials stocks including Barrick Gold and Teck Resources rose, with Centerra Gold up 3.7% after Chaarat Gold Holdings offered to buy its Kumtor mine. Barrick Gold said it would use future asset-sale funds for growth or dividends, and its shares rose 3%. Seven of 10 sectors were higher; the index had five new 52-week highs and no new lows. Mitel Networks was the top gainer, rising 10.1% on an agreement to be sold for about $2 billion, while Prairiesky Royal fell 6.5%. TSX index volume was 15.44 million shares, and total Canadian volume was 31.31 million shares.

The passage describes how defect engineering is achieved in CVD-grown monolayer MoS2 by irradiating the samples with a 1 MeV electron beam at a constant flux while varying exposure time (30 s, 60 s, 120 s). It reports that irradiation does not noticeably change optical contrast or surface morphology, but Raman spectra shift in ways attributed to chalcogen vacancies and increased defect density. Photoluminescence (PL) shows blueshifted excitonic peaks and quenching after irradiation, alongside a growing defect-related emission band 200–300 meV below the neutral exciton; temperature- and power-dependent PL supports the bound nature of these defect states. XPS and KPFM indicate that irradiation promotes oxygen incorporation at sulfur vacancy sites, producing Mo–O bonding and p-type doping through changes in surface potential/work function. Circularly polarized PL shows reduced valley polarization with increasing defect intensity. First-principles calculations are used to corroborate that oxygen-related acceptor states created by vacancies and oxygen interactions lead to the defect peak and enhanced valley depolarization. The work concludes that high-energy electron beams provide a controlled method to tune defect states in monolayer MoS2 and can be extended to other TMDs with appropriate parameter optimization.

The passage discusses gold’s history and its role in speculation and as an inflation hedge, then explains factors influencing gold prices, including supply and demand, US dollar value, investor risk appetite, central bank demand, and jewelry demand. It notes that from 1955 to 2022 gold recorded 80 monthly all-time highs (about 1.25 per year, or ~10% of months), but also highlights that gold can go in cycles, including more than 14 years (1981–2005) without a new high. It describes developing and backtesting a “gold new high” trading strategy using monthly closing prices from the World Bank’s Commodities Markets Database. The strategy’s equity curve shows no major drawdowns, and performance is characterized by lower returns, only about a third of time spent in the market, and a maximum drawdown reduced to almost half, concluding that it may help identify bull regimes in gold.

The passage reports that Japan and China are increasing their forces in Korea, with more than 4,000 Japanese troops reportedly in Korea and Chinese troops arriving at Chemulpo. It says Japan holds possession of Seoul, while Chinese troops are encamped 15 miles south. Japan will not withdraw its troops until China provides guarantees that it will not interfere in Korean affairs except as provided by the 1885 Japan–China convention requiring prior written notice and withdrawal after a disturbance is settled. The passage claims China’s action was communicated to Japan after it occurred and describes diplomatic exchanges in late June where suggestions for simultaneous withdrawal were rejected by China. It notes that Japanese troops occupy strategic points around Seoul and control key routes, and that a conflict is expected at any time, with Japan continuing to receive reinforcements and China massing and equipping forces.

Tencent has added Batman to Arena of Valor, including batrang and forearm blades for a stealth-focused Assassin class playstyle. The update also introduces a new Death Match mode with five two-player teams in a colosseum-inspired map, where points are shown above heroes and earned by opponents who defeat them, with matches lasting eight minutes. It includes Valor TV for watching matches live, viewing event schedules, and replaying recordings, plus optimizations to lobby menus, friends lists, and messaging systems.

The Wing-T offense is described as a unique football offense that uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to exploit aggressive or undisciplined defenders by making plays look similar so the defense can’t identify where the ball will go in time. Developed at the University of Delaware by Coach Harold “Tubby” Raymond, it is often called the Delaware Wing-T. To run it, the passage says teams need at least two solid running backs plus a quarterback who can run and take off on waggle passes, and it notes that a smaller, quicker offensive line that can pull and trap may be effective. Key strengths include slowing down more physically talented defenses through misdirection, play action passes, quick motions, and unusual formations, along with coaches having extensive adjustments due to the offense’s long history. The main weakness is a lack of a traditional dropback passing game, though the offense can include other alignments such as shotgun spread formations. The passage lists common formations (Wing/100–900, Wing-Slot/Red or Doubles 100, and Unbalanced formations) and examples of run plays (Buck Sweep, Down/Belly G, and Trap). It also describes common pass plays (Waggle/Buck Sweep Boot, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass). The Wing-T is noted as largely absent from major college football but active at the high school level, with some major college coaches influenced by its principles, including Gus Malzahn.

The passage describes the device ACQ and CONV states: on power-up or after resets/conversions it enters ACQ to acquire an analog input signal, transitions to RESET on RST falling edge, and enters CONV on a rising CONVST/CS edge. In CONV, conversion uses an internal clock and ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until conversion completes, after which the device returns to ACQ. It also discusses NAP mode for reduced power in ACQ.

It then outlines programming and data transfer. The device has nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read operations. A data transfer frame starts at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends when conversions begin at the next rising edge. During the frame, RVS indicates frame start and the device loads output data into a shift register; clocking SCLK captures input bits into an input shift register and shifts output bits on selected SDO-x pins. Frame handling depends on the SCLK counter value (32 for optimal, less than 32 for short/possible NOP behavior, more than 32 for long/daisy-chain-like behavior). The passage also covers input command synchronization to SCLK, input/output command effects, output data word composition using read commands, conversion results, selectable data flags, and multiSPI data transfer protocols (legacy SPI-compatible and source-synchronous modes), including single or dual SDO-x behavior.

Vishay Intertechnology (NYSE:VSH) shares rose 2.08% in the most recent session. Analysts project a 52-week target of $20 based on 4 opinions, with a high target of $22 and a low target of $18; the latest closing price was $19.65. The consensus price target is an average taken from analysts polled by Thomson Reuters’ First Call over a 12-month short-term horizon. The average brokerage recommendation (ABR) is 3.75 (4 recs), with an industry rank of 138 out of 265. Of the recommendations, 1 analyst rates Buy, 0 rates Outperform, 3 rate Hold, 1 rates Underperform, and 1 rates Sell. ATR-14 is 0.55, with weekly volatility of 2.47% and monthly volatility of 2.50%. RSI is 53.51. The company has a market capitalization of $2.83 billion and 144.15 million outstanding shares; 1.23 million shares traded in the previous session versus about 1.5 million on average.

Scale AI cut a team of Dallas contractors focused on “generalist” AI work, according to Business Insider. The team, known internally as the NPO, worked on generalist tasks like improving AI chatbot writing. The company said the layoffs reflect an industry shift toward more expert-driven data labeling and that the changes affect only a small portion of its workforce without impacting customer delivery. Laid-off workers received four weeks of severance and healthcare coverage through October via a staffing agency email, and were invited to join Scale’s gig-work platform, Outlier. Scale AI spokesperson Natalia Montalvo confirmed the cuts and said Scale continues to expand expert-level programs.

ADA occurrence will be analyzed descriptively by treatment group without planned statistical tests. ADA will be derived from the number of patients with ADA-positive samples during the trial by counting treatment-induced ADA patients (baseline ADA-negative becoming ADA-positive after dosing) and treatment-boosted ADA patients (baseline ADA-positive with ≥5-fold increases in titer after dosing). These counts will be summed for the overall ADA incidence numerator, which will be divided by the number of evaluable patients (patients with at least one post-drug administration ADA-appropriate, reportable sample during treatment or follow-up). Baseline-positive patients without any post-dose samples will be excluded. Unscheduled dosing visits for ADA-positive patients will be included with their results respected.

The passage provides guidance for an ADS9803 board layout: avoid crossing digital lines with the analog signal path and keep analog input and reference signals away from noise sources. It recommends placing 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors close to AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD pins, and not placing vias between those power pins and bypass capacitors. It also advises placing the reference decoupling capacitor close to the REFIO and REFM pins, avoiding vias between REFIO and the bypass capacitors, and connecting GND and REFM pins to a ground plane using short connections. The remainder includes Texas Instruments information on documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD cautions, revision/mechanical/orderable information, and various legal disclaimers.

The passage describes Corning Incorporated’s Growth and Strategy Council (GSC) as a forum for challenging and being challenged to avoid groupthink and to manage hard decisions for complex, difficult-to-measure portfolios. It explains Corning’s history of innovation and how innovation is organized through centralized research (Sullivan Park) and governance councils, including the Technology Council (CTC) and the GSC, which oversee different stages of innovation and help maintain a balanced innovation portfolio. It outlines Corning’s business segments (Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences), the company’s innovation “recipe,” and principles such as idea generation, learning from failed ideas, and long-term “patient money.” The passage also provides examples of how the GSC supported major initiatives and discusses challenges for sustaining the GSC as Corning’s pipeline grows, including prioritization and handling new business models.

The passage describes an optimization-based trading strategy for the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), founded in 2016. It presents a long-only Donchian Channels strategy with short-term Donchian settings and an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) filter to reduce false signals. The strategy uses two variables: the EMA length and the Donchian Channels lookback period. Backtests on BOTZ (daily, September 13, 2016 to present) suggest many parameter choices are profitable and that adding the EMA filter improves results across settings. The passage sets Donchian length to 3 and EMA to 200 to view the resulting equity curve, which the authors say beats Buy and Hold with less volatility. It notes the strategy has a relatively low number of trades and encourages out-of-sample backtesting via an incubation period. It also reports similarly smooth results on a 2-hour time frame, but advises caution before concluding it is a viable short-term strategy.

The speaker says they would have liked to win but acknowledge they cannot change the result. They plan to improve areas to try to win the next game, aiming to limit turnovers and be smarter on the bluelines. They note the puck was bouncing and mention that they had good momentum early but the other team gained momentum after the first few minutes. Overall, they believe they gave themselves a chance to win but did not come through in the third, and they suggest making smarter plays with the puck.

Knox County Criminal Court Judge Steven Sword sentenced Christopher Drone Bassett to life plus 35 years, and Richard Gregory Williams III to 143 years and Kipling Deshawn Colbert to 109 years, for their roles in the 2015 death of 15-year-old Zaevion Dobson, a teenage football player who shielded friends from gunfire. A jury convicted Bassett of first-degree murder and found Williams and Colbert guilty of facilitating the murder. The sentences for Williams and Colbert include time for charges not directly related to Dobson’s death, and Colbert received an additional two-year term on an unrelated charge; Williams’ 107-year term was added to a 36-year sentence for attempted murder.

The passage describes the US S&P Financial Services sector, including that it consists of S&P 500 companies classified under GICS Financial Services and that these firms provide financial services to individuals, SMEs, and corporations, including banks, investment houses, insurance firms, and fintech. It says the sector is tracked by capitalization-weighted ETFs such as Vanguard Financials ETF (VFH) and Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF). It lists five major stocks by market capitalization: Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs, with market-cap figures as of July 21, 2022. The passage also discusses the sector’s collapse in 2008/09 and claims that XLF has traded at about the same level since 2007 (not accounting for dividends). It presents a backtested trading strategy using XLF with 198 trades, an average gain of 1.05%, a 73% win rate, 21% max drawdown, and a 2.25 profit factor, and notes that it works for stock indices but not commodities.

Amazon introduced the Kindle and later the Echo, and is now working on another domestic technology push: home robots. The project, codenamed “Vesta” and overseen by Gregg Zehr at Lab126 in Sunnyvale, is described as top-secret and part of a ramp-up in hiring. People familiar with the plans say Amazon hopes to seed robots in employees’ homes by the end of this year and possibly with consumers as early as 2019, though timelines could change. An Amazon spokesperson said the company does not comment on rumors and speculation. The passage notes uncertainty about what tasks the robot would perform, though some speculate it could function like a mobile Alexa. It also compares Amazon’s effort to other consumer robot attempts and cites estimates that the domestic consumer robot market could grow to about $15 billion annually by 2023.

SAN MIGUEL Pure Foods Company (SMPFC) is delaying its planned follow-on offering to the third or fourth quarter rather than the second quarter. The planned P100–150 billion share sale will be timed to let investors absorb current stock rights offerings and amid stock market volatility; SMPFC may use three foreign banks and two local banks. The company is merging Ginebra San Miguel and San Miguel Brewery into SMPFC to form San Miguel Food and Beverage (SMFBI), which will have a 4.3% public float, prompting the FOO to meet the 15% public ownership rule. SMPFC also plans P56–P60 billion in capital expenditures over the next three years and reported 16% consolidated net income growth to P6.9 billion in 2017, after a 5% revenue increase to P117 billion.

The passage describes digital twin simulations and a computer-implemented method for executing simulations while bypassing selected input parameters or components. It explains that digital twins virtually represent physical assets, track changes over time using real-time data from sensors/IoT and other sources, and enable users to predict and optimize future performance. The method includes creating a digital twin model from real-time feeds, generating multiple separate versions reflecting component and performance changes over time, configuring simulation inputs by selecting versions and components to bypass, and outputting simulation results based on the configured inputs. The passage also outlines a system architecture (including data collection, version management, simulation, and reporting engines), the use of digital twin model versions and hybrid models, optional use of AR to build hybrid models, and reporting or archiving simulation results.

The passage describes Fabry–Perot microcavities and a fabrication method for state-of-the-art visible micromirrors and microcavity systems. It explains why conventional super-polished mirrors and low-loss dielectric coatings are limited by large size and radii of curvature, and how microfabrication techniques address these issues. It discusses figures of merit for performance (finesse, waist size, form factor, quality factor, and coupling efficiency), and notes that finesse is tied to resonator loss and is limited by surface roughness and scattering. The authors compare their microcavity data to prior cavity types using plots of quality factor versus normalized cavity length, and summarize trade-offs between traditional macroscopic mirrors, various microfabricated FP cavities, integrated ring resonators, and microdisk/toroid resonators.  

They present a scalable process using standard nano/microfabrication: starting from a polished silicon wafer, improving surface smoothness via repeated wet oxide growth and HF removal, depositing a dielectric stack coating by ion beam sputtering, defining mirror shapes by lithography, and creating freestanding suspended mirrors by backside Bosch etching, where buckling from compressive strain forms the micromirror shape. The resulting mirror geometries are characterized and simulations match measured profiles with high accuracy, and rotational symmetry is confirmed. Finesse and quality factor are measured using a swept-ring-down method with a laser locked to a rubidium resonance at 780.24 nm; the best measured finesse and quality factor are reported. The study also characterizes how finesse and quality factor vary with cavity length, estimates loss components (transmission, scattering, absorption), and extrapolates telecom performance.  

Finally, the passage demonstrates integrable cavity assemblies made from mirror cutouts using glue and manual alignment, reporting measured linewidths and figures of merit for short and long assemblies, and concludes that the devices are suitable for both quantum and classical optics, including uses as optical interfaces, filters, transfer cavities, and compact laser stabilization systems.

Nigeria is seeing a consumer revolution as large shopping malls open in different parts of the country, creating job opportunities and boosting tax revenues, with emphasis on tax payment in Lagos. Analysts cite factors such as one-stop shopping convenience, brand-conscious consumers, and the desire to shop after work. The Lagos City Mall manager says the increase in malls is good for the economy, noting that over five upscale malls have opened and some are expanding outlets. Examples mentioned include Shoprite’s continued outlets since its 2005 Lekki debut and Spar’s expansion since operations began in the 2000s. An executive from Ibukun Efuntayo & Co links the growth to changing lifestyles and says malls provide employment and signal positive investor confidence and economic development.

After boot, the device determines its state by sampling the BTMODE[15:0] pin inputs when reset is de-asserted. The sampled values are latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register in the Control Module. BTMODE[15:11] determine GPMC CS0 Default Data Bus Width, Wait Enable, and Address/Data Multiplexing. BTMODE[4:0] determine the boot mode order, where the first listed mode is primary and subsequent modes are tried if the previous fails. BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and should be pulled down. For EMAC bootmode, BTMODE[9:8] select the Ethernet PHY Mode. For XIP and XIP w/ WAiT bootmodes, BTMODE[10] selects between GPMC pin muxing options.

Paul Tisdale said Exeter City could be proud after their 1-0 defeat to Luton Town on Saturday. With six players missing, City gave 20-year-old Jordan Storey his first league start in defence and produced a battling performance, losing only to Harry Cornick’s deflected strike. Tisdale acknowledged Luton deserved to win but said Exeter were pleased with their play, despite issues in their back four due to selection. He also disputed a late equaliser ruled out for a foul, and praised the work of Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson in preparing Storey. Tisdale added that Exeter can host promotion rivals Wycombe Wanderers with confidence, saying there has been no drop-off in how they perform.

The passage says messaging has remained consistent as apps evolved, but chat platforms are now building broader ecosystems within chat. It notes WhatsApp’s strong presence in India (about 94% reach) and that it has introduced voice and video calls, with payments described as the next step. It discusses content’s role in user engagement, the rise of content consumption in India, and WhatsApp’s attempt to introduce “stories” that are described as having failed. It suggests professionally produced content could be a better approach. The passage contrasts WhatsApp with Hike, which is described as playing catch-up despite starting payments earlier, and mentions potential bundling with Airtel TV and Wynk. It also describes gaming as an engagement strategy, citing Gamepind, a joint venture involving AGTech Holdings and Paytm, and imagines games integrated into messaging services.

The passage describes a network security appliance designed to allow local command and control without requiring network login, including via a touch screen or similar interface. During denial of service attacks, local interface commands receive priority access to processing resources and memory so the appliance can mitigate attacks (e.g., shutting down ports, blacklisting sources, or modifying filter rules) without manual reboot or disconnection. It also discusses packet inspection and filtering using rules (blocking, forwarding, redirection, or packet modification), including how complex rule matching can be accelerated using geoprocessing-based spatial queries and R-tree indexing. The passage further explains splitting rules into mandatory rules for known threats and potential rules for inactive threats, and distributing rule subsets across multiple appliances based on likelihood/weights to reduce memory and bandwidth. Management systems can adjust rule likelihoods based on detected attack attempts. The passage includes descriptions of security devices, management servers, and methods/flow charts for local control via a multi-touch interface, including prioritizing the user interface during attacks and quarantining communications from unrecognized devices until authorized.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 10, 2015 reporting results from its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held that day. Shareholders elected directors: Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner. The shareholders approved proposals to ratify Ernst & Young LLP as independent public accounting firm for 2015, approve advisory executive compensation, and amend the Employee Stock Purchase Plan to increase authorized shares by 50,000,000 (with the amended plan filed as Exhibit 10.1). Two shareholder proposals—“Risk Report” and “Proxy Access for Shareholders”—were not approved. Exhibit 10.1 is the Employee Stock Purchase Plan as amended and restated as of March 10, 2015.

An environmental organization says the federal government missed an opportunity to protect Canadians from phthalates that could affect fertility and behaviour. After a review, Environment and Climate Change Canada said none of more than a dozen phthalates studied posed a risk to human health, and only one needs further study for possible environmental risk. The organization’s Muhannad Malas criticized Canada’s approach, saying European regulators have concluded at least four phthalates pose human health risks and that Canada’s law requires proving a product is unsafe before banning or limiting it. He said the law should be modernized, noting that in June the House of Commons environment committee recommended aligning Canada’s rules with Europe. Environment Minister Catherine McKenna said the government is considering the recommendations and will develop a plan by June 2018.

A synthesis of studies and district research cited in the passage say high-stakes standardized testing leads educators to change curricula, use more test-like problems, and narrow instruction. The passage argues that school choice can still constrain education freedom when states require choice participants to take state-made tests tied to public-school standards, citing Wisconsin (Wisconsin Forward Exam), Texas (possible ESA-related requirement), and Oklahoma (ACT-based measures for public education and scholarships). It also says students in Wisconsin and North Carolina school choice programs must take the ACT in 11th grade and that many states require SAT or ACT testing for graduation, leading schools to teach to these tests. The passage claims these exams are increasingly biased and have lowered rigor, citing changes to SAT and AP Literature and SAT math rigor declines. It argues that instead of banning standardized tests, states should provide diverse testing choices and ensure admissions testing options are usable for public college admissions and scholarships, highlighting Arkansas and Florida reforms and the Classic Learning Test (CLT) as an alternative.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Colorado’s 2019 ban on “conversion therapy” for clients under age 18, which is intended to change sexual orientation or gender identity. Therapist Kaley Chiles, a practicing Christian, argues the ban violates her free speech by effectively imposing a “gag order” because it restricts her talk-based counseling conversations. Colorado says the law regulates unsafe and ineffective treatments, and that the exemption for those engaged in religious ministry means the bar is limited to particular professional conduct.

Chiles sued to block enforcement, but the district court and a divided panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit upheld the law, reasoning it regulates conduct with speech only incidentally involved and therefore should face rational basis review. A dissenting judge argued the majority treated speech as conduct. Chiles contends strict scrutiny should apply because the ban turns on the content of her counseling speech and fails because Colorado lacks evidence of harm and the law is over- and underinclusive.

The U.S. Solicitor General argues the case should be sent back to apply strict scrutiny, suggesting the state lacks persuasive evidence that the ban substantially advances its interests and appears aimed at suppressing a viewpoint. Colorado argues the ban is “exceedingly narrow,” targets only a discredited treatment seeking predetermined identity changes, and that long-established state regulation of substandard healthcare should remain unaffected; it also argues it would survive strict scrutiny.

A new analysis by the Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians (CSPCP) concludes that providing palliative care and hospice services across Canada would improve care for less money. The report is based on studies comparing palliative care with usual care and cites findings such as hospital-based palliative care saving about $7,000 to $8,000 per patient, outpatient palliative care cutting direct health care costs by about 30%, and projections that expanding in-home palliative team care in Ontario could improve quality of life and avoid $191 million to $385 million in costs. The report also says shifting care from acute settings to residential hospices could save about $600 a day. CSPCP recommends that federal, provincial, and territorial governments improve, monitor, and evaluate the quality and access of palliative care services, and says Canada should act now.

Last week, AMP’s new chairman David Murray said he is likely to take a different and controversial approach. In a speech to the Australian Centre for Public Affairs, he argued that ASX corporate governance principles have led to deteriorating governance standards in the financial sector by inhibiting better models, contributing to a “trust deficit.” He suggested institutions reflect on internal breakdowns and use a “root and stem” approach to create new mechanisms to strengthen governance. He argued that broad principles have become detailed, prescriptive “one-size-fits-all” regulations, and that despite an “if not, why not?” opt-out, people conform by choosing the least resistant path.

Gardaí in Louth appealed for information about the murder of teenager Cameron Reilly. His body was found at Rivervale, Dunleer at 8.30am on Saturday, and he had suffered neck injuries. He had been socialising with up to 20 young people on Friday night and was seen visiting a takeaway at 12.30am on Saturday. Officers are searching for his mobile phone, which they believe may contain messages from attackers, and Superintendent Andrew Watters said their primary focus is establishing the truth for Cameron’s family, urging people with information to contact Gardaí, parents, or teachers. Separately, Gardaí prevented a likely gangland attack in west Dublin by seizing a semi-automatic shotgun during a monitored handover, arresting a 31-year-old man and a 53-year-old woman. Drugs valued at about €1m and cash were also seized, including 6kgs of heroin and 2kgs of cocaine, in an operation led by the Special Crime Task Force.

The Johnston Press South Business Awards celebrated local businesses at Brighton’s Grand Hotel, with awards presented by Nick Wallis. Guardian Angel Carers won both Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Olive and Vine received the Place to Eat or Drink award, Go Creative’s Brandon Relph won Young Achiever, and Southsea Bathing Hut’s Sam Worsey won Retailer of the Year. Talks at Six won Outstanding Contribution to the Community. The passage also lists other category winners, including Gardiner and Scardifield, Bespoke You Beauty Retreat and Spar, Ricardo Plc, Pearl Fit Out Ltd, Nature Shop, Tim Sorensen Hospitality, Bunn Leisure, Transalis, Digi Tool Box Ltd, GTMS, Si Protech, Dawn Lawrence, Martin Putman, and Q Hair and Beauty.

The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced FORM X for SMEs to improve foreign exchange liquidity and access, requiring basic documentation. CBN spokesman Isaac Okorafor said the form is meant to ease documentation challenges and must be completed with a supporting application letter, beneficiary invoice, and bank wire transfer. The guideline aims to remove obstacles for SME forex needs of $10,000 or less and reflects the CBN’s commitment to ensure adequate forex supply for genuine transactions.

This case affirms a judgment for the defendants in a dispute over alleged negligent operation of an automobile at a street crossing. The court held there was no error in the jury instructions regarding the plaintiff’s pleaded negligence, including failure to sound a horn or warn of approach, and no error for not charging specific right-of-way, speed, or related duties absent special requests where those issues were not alleged. It also found no error in instructions on negligence based on state law and a city ordinance, upheld comparative negligence instructions despite it not being pleaded where evidence supported both parties’ negligence, and deemed any alleged error on the measure of damages harmless given the defense verdict. The verdict was supported by conflicting evidence, and judgment was affirmed.

The passage describes systems and methods for providing enhanced “trick-play” video streaming modes so viewers can reposition video playback more accurately, especially at higher fast-forward or rewind rates. It contrasts current streaming trick-play approaches that often require selecting exact timestamps with limited or low-quality feedback, and it proposes media guidance/trick-play optimization that plays faster-than-real-time while updating frames frequently and using low latency and high quality. The approach uses metadata such as frame address information and indexes, maintains a normal buffer window of continuous content, and also maintains a trick-play window that buffers only selected frames (often key frames or sampled frames) outside the normal buffer. During trick-play, the system plays using buffered subsets of frames without buffering interspersed ranges, may assemble buffers by requesting missing ranges and individual frames as needed, and can select streams/frames based on streaming performance metrics, desired playback rate, and anticipated trick-play duration. It further outlines components including a streaming server, an optional proxy server to generate required metadata/indexing, a client with a video player and streaming client that manages buffer and adaptive bitrate streaming, and a performance monitor that provides metrics used by the trick-play optimizer. The passage also includes related background on video formats (key vs. delta frames), buffering and playback modes, buffer management concepts, and mentions HLS-based streaming and the generation/use of jump points within content.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with about 56,000 new cases each year. The passage says it is important to know how breasts look and feel normally, and to regularly check for differences or warning signs, including lumps and changes such as swelling, dimpling, nipple changes, skin dryness/redness/rashes, and nipple discharge or newly inverted nipples. It provides self-exam steps and advises checking regularly (every two weeks or up to once a month, around a week after a period) and seeking medical advice for anything unfamiliar or concerning. When seeing a doctor about a lump, they will ask about medical and family history, review medicines and smoking/alcohol habits, and may offer an examination and referral. The passage also describes risk factors, including modifiable factors like hormone replacement therapy duration and breastfeeding, and non-modifiable factors like family genetic mutations (BRCA1/BRCA2), early periods, later menopause, and certain birth-related factors. It notes that men can get breast cancer, usually presenting as a lump or nipple changes. The passage states that breast cancer outcomes have improved over time due to earlier diagnosis and better treatments, but early treatment is crucial.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 17, 2019. On June 16, 2019, its Board appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer effective June 17, 2019. Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months after stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach with a flick knife during an argument in the Newmarket Tavern in Plymouth over a spilled drink. Plymouth Crown Court heard Haydon pushed the knife into Brown’s abdomen, leaving blood pouring from the wound, and that Brown was treated for a two-centimetre puncture wound and kept at Derriford Hospital overnight. The court heard Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing a knife as an offensive weapon in a public place, and possessing small amounts of cannabis, and that he was in breach of an eight-month suspended sentence for affray. Recorder Paul Grumbar said Haydon had an “appalling record” for violence and carrying weapons, and described the offence as serious and aggravated due to drinking and earlier drug taking, and said a more serious charge could have applied.

SPYR, Inc. announced that shareholders of record as of May 19, 2017 will receive a dividend paid in shares of a new, separate publicly traded spin-off company created to divest SPYR’s restaurant division. Each shareholder will receive an equal number of shares on a 1-for-1 basis; for example, 1,000 shares of SPYR would receive 1,000 shares of the spin-off. After the spin-off concludes, the new company will file a registration statement with the SEC to qualify as a separate entity with a separate trading symbol. A newly described Jurassic lizard, Breugnathair elgolensis (“false snake of Elgol”), was found on Scotland’s Isle of Skye. The fossil dates to about 167 million years ago and shows hook-like, python-style teeth and snake-like jaws, along with a short body and fully formed lizard limbs. Researchers studied the nearly complete specimen for almost 10 years using computed tomography and high-powered x-rays, placing it in a new group of extinct predatory squamates called Parviraptoridae. The study says earlier claims that snake-like and gecko-like features belonged to two animals are not supported, because both sets of features occur together in one animal. The researchers did not reach a conclusive answer on whether it relates directly to snake ancestry, noting possibilities including independent evolution of snake-like teeth and jaws in a stem-squamate group.

The A100 Tensor Core GPU includes 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7× larger than Tesla V100’s L2 cache. The larger L2 improves performance for many HPC and AI workloads by caching larger portions of datasets and models at higher speed than HBM2 memory, benefiting DRAM bandwidth-limited workloads such as deep neural networks with small batch sizes. The shared L2 cache is outside the GPCs, divided into two partitions for higher bandwidth and lower latency, delivering a 2.3× L2 bandwidth increase over V100; cache coherence maintains the CUDA programming model. Each partition is divided into 40 L2 cache slices, with eight 512 KB slices associated with each memory controller, and slice groups used in MIG configurations. L2 read bandwidth is 5120 Bytes/clk versus 2048 Bytes/clk for V100. Ampere also provides L2 cache residency controls and adds compute data compression, which can improve DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidths by up to 4×.

The passage describes major security challenges for three large sports events in Chicago, with expected crowds of about 1.7 million for the Chicago Marathon, 45,000 for a Cubs vs. Nationals playoff game, and 60,000-plus for a Bears vs. Vikings Monday Night Football matchup. City emergency management officials say they review risks from below ground to the sky and say a “robust plan” is in place.

The passage describes several low-frequency subsystem components and related device support topics. The passage also mentions device analog connection guidance for DAC_OUT, describes the IOMUX and a superset I/O diagram, outlines SWD access and boot strap loader (BSL) invocation and pin requirements, and notes a memory-mapped FACTORY region with read-only device capability/trim data. Two AI models, Evo 1 and Evo 2, generated multiple bacteriophage genomes from scratch. In lab dishes, some AI-made bacteria-killing viruses outperformed a well-studied strain. The passage says AI-designed bacteriophages could one day be used in phage therapy.

Saudi Aramco plans to change the formula used to price its long-term crude oil sales to Asia starting in October, marking its first benchmark change for official selling prices (OSP) since the mid-1980s. The new OSP formula will use the average monthly prices of Oman crude futures traded on the Dubai Mercantile Exchange (DME) and the average cash price for Dubai assessed by S&P Global Platts, instead of the average of Oman and Dubai prices assessed by Platts. Saudi Aramco’s October OSPs will be based on the DME December Oman contract settlement prices and the December Dubai cash price assessed by Platts, both set in October. The decision is expected to be officially communicated to customers later on Wednesday, and it could improve liquidity for Oman futures trading on the DME and related derivative instruments. It was not immediately clear whether other Middle East producers will change their benchmarks.

WIRED’s Aarian Marshall discusses DoorDash’s newly unveiled autonomous delivery robot, Dot, and broader renewed interest in delivery robots after years of challenges. DoorDash says Dot is intended for a “hybrid” delivery model involving humans and autonomous vehicles, drones, and related systems. Marshall describes Dot’s size, cameras, sensors, and planned operation on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes, and notes questions about how it will function in real-world conditions and how robots can be made more “palatable” and safer around people. The conversation also covers DoorDash’s partnership with Coco Robotics, which uses smaller sidewalk robots that may still involve teleoperation, and debates how advanced autonomy really is. They discuss why delivery-robot enthusiasm peaked around the pandemic, the technical difficulty of operating in varied sidewalk contexts, and the idea that robots may do better in constrained environments like university campuses. The episode further examines regulatory issues around robots in bike lanes and the labor impact, including the possibility of displaced tasks rather than eliminated work, using examples from China and research on sidewalk robots in Pittsburgh. The hosts end with product and app recommendations unrelated to robots.

The speaker welcomes the visitors as friendly people and assures them that the speaker’s nation is their friend. He argues for lasting peace, protection of the visitors’ lands under established lines agreed by mutual consent, and delivery of a law to punish encroachment. He addresses a request to sell land to pay a debt to merchants, offering to purchase land on the Mississippi for settlements and related needs, and says future representatives will negotiate boundaries. He explains that earlier land sales to the English were customary to be paid immediately, and that information indicates payment occurred at the time. He encourages the visitors to farm and raise goods instead of hunting, and clarifies that earlier supplies were gifts and a store was provided at their request without taking their land. He states that the Secretary at War will handle explanations about the store, interpreter, and agent, and promises travel arrangements, care, and safe return home.

Genel Altimeaux challenged an Unemployment Appeals Commission order denying his unemployment benefits, arguing the appeals referee’s decision lacked competent, substantial evidence. The court reversed, finding the record did not support that Altimeaux voluntarily quit. After an earlier hearing held without Altimeaux, the court remanded for a new evidentiary hearing to determine whether he received notice. On remand, only Altimeaux and supervisor William Tranowski testified, and Tranowski acknowledged he did not personally hear Altimeaux quit. The referee nonetheless relied on earlier testimony from Bruce Milliken that Altimeaux quit, but the court found Milliken’s earlier testimony should have been rejected because Altimeaux did not have the opportunity for cross-examination. The court reversed and ordered reinstatement of Altimeaux’s unemployment award.

Parents raised concerns about Township High School District 113’s process for hiring a new principal for Highland Park High School, including why only two parents serve on the stakeholder interview committee and whether the process is transparent. Superintendent Christopher Dignam said he is using Ray and Associates to solicit and screen candidates to replace Principal Tom Koulentes, who will leave June 30. Dignam reported that Ray and Associates will present semi-finalists on April 14 for review and interviews, leading to two or three finalists. He said an 18-member stakeholder committee will interview the final candidates on April 25, with the goal of selecting a principal by that date. Dignam stated the process matches the one used last year for Deerfield High School and that the stakeholder committee slots will be the same; he said the selection process previously led to Kathryn Anderson being chosen. Board member Julie Gordon said some individuals who applied to join the committee did not know why they were not selected or who was selected, prompting calls for more transparency.

High-tech biologgers and microphones were used to track how Europe’s largest bat, the greater noctule, hunts migrating songbirds in flight. Researchers report that the bats ascend to high altitudes, then make a several-minute vertically downward sprint; feeding buzzes followed by a bird distress call occur at the bottom of the dive. Most of the 611 hunting events involved songbirds, including cases where two birds responded at the last moment and one bird escaped near the ground while another produced distress calls followed by a 23-minute in-flight meal. Sensors did not record video, but tracks of bat movement, feeding buzzes, and chewing sounds indicated successful hunts. The study also found evidence from wing wounds and captured netted bats that the bats remove wings as part of their process.

The passage explains the Pin and Pull run play, which uses down blocks to create favorable angles and gets blockers into space on the perimeter as lead blockers for an outside run. Its strengths include generating lead blockers at the point of attack, versatility in how linemen can down block and then pull based on pre-snap alignments, and allowing the tailback to take the ball anywhere from the C-gap to the sideline according to the guards’ blocks. Weaknesses include requiring specific personnel—at least two guards who can pull—and performing best with speed-type tailbacks rather than power backs. It also contrasts Pin and Pull with Buck Sweep, noting that Buck Sweep requires an inside run threat to force defensive choices, while Pin and Pull is described as a true perimeter run. The passage then provides blocking and execution steps for plays versus specific defensive fronts and lists two variations: Pin and Pull Toss and TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss.

The passage reports that Asia stocks were muted after mixed Chinese PMIs and that Australia was cautious ahead of the RBA. Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli was poised to return to power after winning a parliamentary seat and with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies on track for a majority. Counting was still under way after an election that ended a near-decade transition from monarchy and a civil war that left more than 17,000 dead. Oli, 65, said he would form a government lasting a full five-year term and called for extending China’s railway network into Nepal and implementing infrastructure projects to create jobs. Analysts said a stable government could help development and attract foreign investment, while investor concerns and instability had affected growth, corruption, and post-2015 earthquake reconstruction. Election results were expected to be finalized in about a week, and Nepal is described as one of the world’s poorest countries.

Brock University research found that rosemary extract reduces the growth of lung cancer cells. The study, led by Evangelina Tsiani with graduate student Jessy Moore, examined how rosemary polyphenols affect Akt signalling and related proteins in A549 human lung cancer cells. Results showed that the extract stopped cancer cell survival and spread by enhancing apoptosis, blocking the Akt pathway, and preventing activation of certain proteins. The findings were published in *Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy*. Tsiani cautioned against recommending increased rosemary intake yet and said further research is needed to identify the specific rosemary components responsible, focusing on carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid.

Plans for the longest stretch of England’s “smart motorway” on the M4, a 32-mile section between London and Theale in Berkshire, will be displayed ahead of work starting in September. The road will be widened to four lanes in both directions, with eleven M4 bridges demolished and rebuilt and four additional bridges widened. The project is expected to cost up to £862.4m. The smart motorway features electronic signs to vary speed limits, aiming to reduce congestion. Highways England says the work will be completed by March 2022, noting the current road is prone to congestion with 130,000 vehicles a day. It adds that safety areas will be every 1.12 miles on average, with no more than 1.6 miles between them.

The passage is an Enron-related news compilation dated January 16–17, 2002. GDDR6X memory on GA10x GPUs supports up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and delivers up to 936 GB/sec peak memory bandwidth, with a fully optimized memory subsystem. The passage describes COTUTOR, a generative AI educational model that combines knowledge tracing, convex optimization, and signal processing to provide personalized learning and adaptive allocation of instructional resources in real time. It uses multimodal learning signals (submission/grading, participation logs, and queries/feedback) structured as time-series data to estimate students’ knowledge states, continuously updating its model and generating optimized strategies for resources and feedback. COTUTOR’s design emphasizes interpretability and efficiency through a convex optimization formulation, and it is implemented as an interactive AI copilot integrated with programming education platforms, providing reminders, question handling, and resource recommendations. The paper also presents a case study framing educational resource allocation and student sentiment maximization as a convex optimization problem with constraints on session resource proportions and priority ranking, using theory and application resources to generate optimal allocation plans under different influence models.

Jane Goodall died on October 1 at age 91. Gold prices are expected to reach a four-year high of $1,400 an ounce by the end of the year amid tensions between North Korea and the U.S. and rising demand in major consumer countries. Evgeny Ananiev of VTB Capital JSC said bullion could rise to $1,360 within three months, with support suggesting prices would not fall below $1,200. The metal traded at $1,281.86 on Monday and has gained 12 percent this year due to worries about a potential nuclear conflict and subdued U.S. inflation. Ray Dalio recommended allocating 5 to 10 percent of assets to gold, and other conference participants said gold could sustain above $1,300, potentially reaching $1,400 in six to nine months as investors seek a safe haven. Commentary also cited a softening Federal Reserve stance, cooling U.S. price pressures, improving Indian demand, and strong gold demand in China.

The passage describes a one-night stay at Villa Casa Casuarina, formerly the Versace Mansion, in Miami’s South Beach. The passage describes a U.S. continuation patent application for multi-camera imaging systems, including related priority claims and government license rights. Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan Chase’s CEO, said AI is real and transformative and urged businesses to use it, while noting some asset prices may be in “bubble territory.” He cautioned against denying AI’s impact and warned that job loss from technology happens quickly, urging society, government, and business to save jobs through retraining, income changes, or other measures. Dimon compared today’s AI excitement to early internet conditions but said not all AI projects will play out as announced, recommending case-by-case investment evaluation. He described JPMorgan’s AI work as focused on specific uses like risk and fraud and said it has worked, while placing generative AI in a different category due to uncertain efficiency gains and the need to get data properly. He emphasized agility, continuous training, and urged thoughtful regulation and safety nets rather than denial or delay.

Asian shares were mostly lower on Wednesday after U.S. stocks fell in the final minutes of trading, ending a three-day winning streak. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.3%, the Shanghai Composite dropped 0.8%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.2%, South Korea’s Kospi declined 0.2%, and Australia’s S&P ASX/200 decreased 0.5%, while shares rose in parts of Southeast Asia and Taiwan. The Student Finance Board withheld funding for two events due to concerns about high cost per student, while funding several dance-related events. It denied additional funds to the Association of Students for Africa for its Akwaaba Banquet, citing that extra support for an outside host and performers would make the price per student too high and fiscally irresponsible; the banquet is scheduled for April 22 at 8 p.m. It tabled Medicine, Education and Development for Low Income Families Everywhere’s “A Taste of South America” over concerns it violated a policy against funding charitable events and due to food costs. The Asian American Association received $54.06 for Mystique of the East (April 23) for bamboo poles and dance ribbons, and Swing Dance Club received $1,094.84 for Once Upon A Rock Step (April 28) covering a live band, decorations, food, and sound technicians; a separate request for a dance floor rental was tabled due to cost. The board funded SFB’s Summer Training Retreat with $1,139 for housing rental and meals.

Trees can capture and remove pollutants from soil and degrade them through natural processes, but this has mostly been used in small-scale cleanup projects. Researchers from the University of Washington and several small companies conducted a large-scale field experiment on a Superfund site using poplar trees fortified with a probiotic bacteria to clean up groundwater contaminated with trichloroethylene (TCE). The results, published Aug. 11 in *Environmental Science & Technology*, showed that after one year inoculated trees were bigger and healthier, and after three years they remained more robust with greatly reduced TCE levels inside trunks. The study also found lower TCE levels in groundwater downstream, and increased chloride in soil around roots. The authors say this approach could speed and improve cleanup of Superfund and other high-TCE sites, potentially at lower cost than methods like excavating or pumping, and organizations and landowners have expressed interest in using it.

New reports citing anonymous U.S. officials say Russian intelligence officials repeatedly contacted members of President Trump’s campaign staff, with U.S. agencies intercepting the communications while investigating Russian election tampering. The agencies reportedly have not seen proof of collusion, and they are still determining why the contacts occurred. Trump and the Kremlin denied the reports, and Trump called them “conspiracy theories.” The FBI has been investigating related contacts, and Congress is considering public investigations; some Republicans oppose an independent probe and say intelligence and judiciary committees should handle it, citing concerns about leaks and surveillance involving U.S. citizens. The reports come amid recent departures from Trump’s inner circle, including Michael Flynn’s resignation, Paul Manafort’s resignation, and Carter Page’s removal, with Manafort denying wrongdoing.

Moqtada al-Sadr set conditions for his followers to hand over weapons used against Islamic State. After Iraq’s Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi declared final victory and said the state should have a monopoly on arms, Iraqi armed forces held a victory parade in Baghdad. In a televised speech, Sadr demanded jobs or incorporation of his fighters into official armed and security forces, and government support for families of martyrs from the three-year war. His Saraya al-Salam are part of the Popular Mobilisation Forces formed in response to Islamic State’s advance in 2014; Iran has armed and trained many PMF groups, though not his.

The passage describes implementing a sharded Redis setup on Kubernetes by deploying Redis shards with a StatefulSet to create unique DNS names, resulting in three redis containers (sharded-redis-0, sharded-redis-1, sharded-redis-2). The passage describes a patent application that is a continuation of earlier U.S. patent applications and related patent publications. It introduces “ladar” technology (laser radar/lidar) and discusses limitations of conventional ladar systems, including cost, size, weight, power use, and shortcomings of flash ladar. It outlines the inventor’s disclosed approaches to improve scanning ladar transmitters by optimizing gaze on regions of interest, including (1) using an optical field splitter/inverter to split and invert scan areas so that scan speed is slower in the middle and faster at the edges, (2) optionally creating overlapped inverted fields using adjustable mirror pitch angles, and (3) enhancing Lissajous scan patterns with induced periodic phase drift to reduce gaps and improve revisit density near desired regions. The passage also describes an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) reimaging system intended to enable compact cascaded beam scanner assemblies by reimaging a beam onto a second scan mirror, improving scan field and allowing two small, equally sized scanning mirrors.

Zircon (ZrSiO4) undergoes a high-pressure transition to a scheelite-structured reidite phase, with transition pressure strongly dependent on temperature and compression conditions. An intermediate phase has been observed at pressures above 10 GPa, and both martensitic and reconstructive transformation mechanisms have been discussed; analysis suggests reconstructive transformation can also occur in crystalline zircon. Reidite has been found in meteorites, impact metamorphism products, and Precambrian rocks, implying it can persist over geological time and that its presence constrains minimum pressure experienced by rocks.

The paper investigates behavior of trace elements during shock loading of a natural zircon single-crystal monocrystal to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa under laboratory conditions. Shock compression experiments used oriented thin zircon plates in recovery capsules, with calculated pressure profiles based on hydrodynamic modeling. Calculations and temperature estimates were presented, while phase transition effects were ignored above 30 GPa for simplification.

Results show that after shock loading to 13.6 GPa the zircon phase is retained, with possible reidite microdomains not fully excluded. After 51.3 GPa, X-ray diffraction indicates reidite with oriented, textured grains and relict zircon. Scanning electron microscopy shows strong fracturing in both samples, and different fracture patterns at higher pressure. Raman/IR spectroscopy confirms mosaic reidite at 51.3 GPa with localized residual zircon near fractures. Cathodoluminescence intensity decreases with increasing shock pressure and shifts toward shorter wavelengths in reidite, alongside changes in REE3+ emission features, suggesting different local symmetries. In the 51.3 GPa sample, cathodoluminescence images reveal bright yellow speckles (2–10 μm) linked to enhanced REE3+ emission and related to planar defects; photoluminescence spectra differ from cathodoluminescence.

The study concludes that transformation to reidite under laboratory shock conditions leads to segregation of trace cations, including REE, onto planar defects, without prolonged post-shock annealing. It argues that rapid segregation on short time scales may be associated with the reconstructive component of the zircon–reidite transition and defect generation, with subsequent diffusion and expelling of atoms facilitating segregation on extended defects.

The passage is an email forwarding multiple news articles about California’s 2001 electricity and energy crisis. It highlights debates over federal and state price controls and regulation, concerns about market manipulation and enforcement by regulators, discussions of power shortages and plants returning from maintenance, and related issues such as gas and electricity price impacts, utility bankruptcy and executive bonuses, rate hikes, and court and legislative actions.

Two senators urged “immediate action” to release money the White House blocked for a federal office that oversees inspectors general. The White House said it was blocking congressionally approved funding for the coming fiscal year, effectively shutting the office down after midnight on Tuesday. The blocked funds are not tied to a separate funding dispute that could cause a government shutdown. The decision to defund the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency has been condemned by top Senate Republicans, who are pressing to reverse it.

Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Scientists say there is a small chance that asteroid Bennu could hit Earth on Thursday, September 22, 2135, destroying many living things. NASA researchers propose, if Bennu goes off course, using a nearly nine-ton “bulk impactor” or a nuclear device under the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) to push or gently nudge it away from an apocalyptic path; the work is described as theoretical. The odds of Bennu hitting Earth are about 1 in 2700, and it is not large enough to cause a dinosaur-level extinction, but the framework could help prepare for other potentially dangerous space objects. The passage cites past incidents such as the 1908 Tunguska event and the 2013 Ural meteor, and notes NASA’s Planetary Defense Coordination Office detects near-Earth objects and plans for deflection or destruction. Bennu is also presented as a target for testing impact mitigation theories, with NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft en route to map Bennu’s composition and return a sample, with a larger follow-up mission if Bennu becomes a bigger threat.

The passage advises Galaxy Fold users to unfold their phone or use full screen for the best experience. It describes the Citi Simplicity® Card, highlighting a 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and no annual fee, along with 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases. It notes the variable APR after the intro period (17.99%–28.74%), that balance transfers must be completed within 4 months, and an intro balance transfer fee of 3% (minimum $5) during the first 4 months, then 5% (minimum $5). Party-list Rep. Lito Atienza filed House Bill 4758 to create a fully elected Metropolitan Manila government to replace the current MMDA, which is led by a presidential appointee and coordinated with elected mayors. Atienza said the MMDA has not been responsive to residents’ concerns after 44 years and argued that an elected governor would improve accountability and effectiveness, citing elected governors in megacities like New York and Tokyo. He also pointed to ongoing problems such as worsening traffic, flooding, peace and order issues, and unresolved garbage, and said these require a master development plan rather than temporary measures. The proposed government would include an elected governor, vice governor, and Metro Manila Council, with members elected at large within Metro Manila’s 16 cities and one town, and MMC members elected from each congressional district.

Manchester City, reduced to 10 men after Fernandinho was dismissed in the first half, defeated Burnley at the Etihad Stadium. City improved after the break with goals from Gael Clichy and Sergio Aguero, while Ben Mee scored shortly after. Burnley had chances, including a late chance for Andre Gray, but could not equalize. The win moved City to third, within two points of second-place Liverpool, with Chelsea and Tottenham also able to drop points when they play each other. Fernandinho’s red was his second Premier League dismissal of the season, resulting in a four-match ban, and City had received seven red cards in Guardiola’s 30 games. Guardiola left Aguero on the bench at first, with Kelechi Iheanacho starting, before Aguero came on at halftime to score the winner.

Eric Fung, CEO of Colega AI in Tokyo, left California because the cost of living was high and he felt the Bay Area’s appeal had declined. He moved to Japan last year after visiting as a tourist and was starting his AI company in Tokyo as a foreigner. Fung grew up in New York City, studied advertising and public relations at Penn State, worked in advertising, and later pursued startups, including a first company he co-founded in 2019 and a period where he opened multiple restaurants in California. Colega AI is US-registered, with a team based in Tokyo and other parts of Asia, and he says moving has been both exciting and challenging due to cultural and language barriers, which he addresses by partnering with a local. He and his wife Shana are renting near Shibuya, and he describes Tokyo as safer and cheaper than California while noting differences in work culture and the difficulty of making friends.

An industry group, the Consumer Mortgage Coalition, is urging the Treasury Department to let mortgage lenders and servicers use an alternative to the IRS’s income verification system (IVES) to avoid delays in mortgage closings as application volume increases in spring. In a Jan. 31 letter to Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin and acting IRS Commissioner David Kautter, the coalition’s executive director Anne Canfield asked permission for qualified lenders to pull current and past year income information from the National Directory of New Hires (NDNH) database maintained by the Department of Health and Human Services, transmit it encrypted to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac underwriting systems, and use it only to verify income with the consumer’s signed consent. The group also urged the Treasury Department to request Congress fund upgrades to the IRS IVES system, which it described as antiquated.

The passage discusses MLB parks’ creative new food items for the 2025 season, mentions a “Korean corn dog” item, includes information about the Savannah Bananas selection show airing on ESPN2 and a streaming hub on Oct. 9 at 6:30 p.m. ET, and notes Stephen A. Smith’s reaction to the Yankees’ Game 3 comeback win. It also contains ESPN BET legal and responsible gambling information.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture enhancements, focusing on second-generation RT Cores for ray tracing and motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores for AI workloads. During the 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic, researchers found that superspreaders played a major role in transmission: about 3% of patients caused more than 60% of infections, and the study estimated an average of 2.39 people infected per patient. The passage cites how transmission was higher among people staying home rather than reaching hospitals and care centers, and notes that traditional funeral practices contributed to spread because bodily fluids can remain infectious for hours or days and washing and dressing bodies can be part of funerals. It also describes similar superspreading in SARS (2002–2003) and MERS. Ebola was eventually stopped through public health efforts emphasizing safe burial and quick hospitalization, and the passage says more research could help target high-risk behaviors and demographics.

The automated fare collection (AFC) system market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024, with a CAGR of 13.3% from 2017 to 2024. AFC automates public transportation ticketing and is used for integrated ticketing, improving fare-collection efficiency, transaction rates, and reducing waiting time and cash-related searching. It enables travelers to carry one card across transit modes and includes components such as automatic gate machines, ticket vending machines, and ticket checking machines. Growth is driven by benefits of AFC, adoption of new technologies, and investments in AFC projects by governments; restraints include lack of awareness and limited use of smart cards. The market is segmented by component (hardware, software), application (bus, toll, train, car rentals), technology platform (smart card, NFC, OCR, others), and geography (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Rest of World). Major players listed include Advanced Card Systems Ltd., Atos SE, Cubic Transportation Systems, LG CNS, NXP Semiconductors, Omron Corp., Samsung SDS, Scheidt & Bachmann, Thales Group, and LECIP Group.

Bayhorse Silver Inc. announced that, subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval, it will increase the equity portion of a previously announced non-brokered private placement from up to 1,500,000 units at $0.10 per unit to 3,000,000 units for gross proceeds of $300,000. The placement will consist of 3,000,000 units, each unit including one common share and one half of a transferable common share purchase warrant exercisable into one common share at $0.15 for 24 months from issuance. Participation is open to all existing shareholders under the “existing shareholder” exemption of National Instrument 45-106. Funds will be used for equipment acquisition and working capital to operate the Bayhorse Silver Mine, and for general and administrative costs, with finder fees potentially payable on portions not taken by insiders.

Massachusetts’ House and Senate passed a supplemental budget bill providing $15 million for school districts educating students who arrived from Puerto Rico in the week of Hurricane Maria. More than 2,300 students have arrived since September, and districts had not received extra state aid because the aid formula was set before their arrival. The $15 million will be distributed using the existing local education aid formula, with amounts depending on how many additional students districts enroll. Springfield has accepted more such students than any other Massachusetts city. The House approved the bill Wednesday and the Senate approved it Thursday, with differences to be negotiated before it goes to Governor Baker’s desk.

The passage describes the author’s attempt to become a “Jeopardy!” contestant after receiving an email and passing an online test, though they expect it may be a blessing not to be chosen. The author then discusses long-standing scientific questions about how memory is stored, noting that there is no consensus and citing research by Lashley, Penfield, and UCLA scientists suggesting memory transfer by RNA in snails and possible recovery of old memories via RNA injections.
