Finally, it discusses #HV doorbell page interrupt/shadow behavior, and host behavior for emulating APIC interrupt presentation and EOI semantics using PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields.

The passage defines consumer confidence as an indicator that gauges optimism or pessimism about the economy, produced by the Conference Board (Consumer Confidence Index, CCI) and the University of Michigan (Consumer Sentiment Index). It describes how consumer confidence is surveyed, including that the Conference Board polls 5,000 U.S. households monthly with five questions. The passage states that consumer confidence is important for traders and investors because it relates to consumer spending and potential inflation, and it can influence manufacturers, employers, lending, and government revenues. It reports backtest results using consumer confidence data, claiming stocks perform better when the Michigan consumer confidence index is above its 12-month moving average and perform poorly when it is below, including a strategy that switches between being invested in the S&P 500 and in cash.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, set a world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship. She began competing in triathlons at age 60, after learning to swim at 59, having faced limited opportunities for girls in athletics earlier in life. After qualifying at 61, she built up from sprint triathlons to Ironman 70.3, and competed in the Kona Ironman at an 80-to-84 age category, finishing in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds to set the record. She prepares by working out at the gym for about two hours daily and months before races, and says she plans to keep taking part in triathlons as long as she can.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A40 GPU and related GA10x Ampere architecture features for data center workloads, including performance and throughput advantages over Turing-based GPUs, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, scalable GPU memory via NVLink, virtualization support (vGPU, Quadro Sync), compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform, and display capabilities. It also covers Ampere display support (4K/8K refresh rates, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1 with DSC requirements), and GA10x video capabilities including fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decoding for multiple codecs (including AV1) and seventh-generation NVENC hardware encoding. Additional sections discuss generational performance and specification notes for related GPUs (e.g., RTX 3090, RTX 3070, RTX A6000), and an EDR memory error detection and replay feature for GDDR6X overclocking on GA10x GPUs, followed by legal and warranty disclaimers.

Lenovo officially unveiled the ThinkPad 25, a limited edition 25th Anniversary laptop, at an event at Yamato Labs in Yokohama, Japan. It is based on the current T470 model and draws design inspiration from the ThinkPad 700C (released October 5, 1992), featuring a rubberized coating, red TrackPoint, classic seven-row keyboard with a ThinkVantage blue enter button, a dedicated volume button, a colorful logo, and numerous status LEDs. The ThinkPad 25 includes a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Intel Core i7-7500U, GeForce 940MX, 16GB DDR4, 512GB NVMe SSD, Thunderbolt 3 Type-C and other ports, a 720p webcam, a fingerprint scanner for Windows Hello, and a claimed 18-hour battery life. It is available in limited quantities in select countries with prices starting at $1,899.

Doctors say COPD is a leading cause of death in the United States and that the only way to reduce risk is to stop smoking. COPD can cause chronic coughing and shortness of breath, and patients struggle to get air out when breathing. Patients with symptoms can be tested by determining smoking history and taking pulmonary function tests. Treatment depends on severity and may include inhalers, oxygen, or pulmonary rehabilitation. There is no cure, but treatments can help reduce exacerbations, and stopping smoking can prevent the disease from starting or becoming more severe.

Molecular Dynamics simulations study materials’ thermal properties at the nanoscale using two methods: Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD). GK uses the equilibrium autocorrelation function of the instantaneous heat flux to compute thermal conductivity, while NEMD applies a temperature gradient using thermal reservoirs at a temperature difference and determines conductivity using Fourier’s law. In both approaches, heat flux is central; NEMD typically calculates it from thermostat energy exchange rates, while GK calculates a time-dependent heat flux from atomic velocities and forces, and interfacial heat current is used to compute interfacial thermal conductance. Spectral decomposition of the heat current is also described, requiring a definition of mechanical power due to atoms across an interface, which is straightforward for pair potentials but not for many-body interactions.

The passage notes that LAMMPS can perform both GK and NEMD, but its original equilibrium heat-flux formulation based on atomic stress tensor was valid only for pair potentials, potentially leading to incorrect thermal conductivity for many-body potentials. Exact formulas derived by Torii et al. allow correct heat-flux calculations for arbitrary many-body potentials and partitioning. Prior work has demonstrated corrections or implementations for specific systems and potentials. The article extends and implements Torii et al. formulas in LAMMPS to calculate heat flux and its spectral decomposition for arbitrary many-body potentials, and outlines the article’s organization: theoretical background in Section II and comparative tests and results in Section III, with computational details in the Supplementary Material. The passage then begins Section II with the Hardy formula for instantaneous heat flux through a cross-section and introduces notation and a discussion of potential energy partitioning.

The passage describes distance education as a rapidly growing worldwide sector and notes that its effectiveness and efficiency are questioned in research, especially after the COVID-19 outbreak. It provides historical examples of distance education starting with Caleb Phillips’s 1728 shorthand advertisement and later mail-based training in Sweden (around 1833) and England (1840). It explains distance education as a teaching model where teacher and student are physically separated and communication occurs via print or electronic/mechanical tools, often through an institution, and later emphasizes that distance education now mostly refers to online learning that can be synchronous or asynchronous.

The study described in the passage evaluates distance education in sports higher education during the pandemic in Turkey. It uses a descriptive analysis case study with qualitative semi-structured interviews of 14 sports lecturers selected via criterion sampling, conducted between December 2020 and November 2021. The research questions address lecturers’ views during the pandemic, advantages and disadvantages, challenges, and factors affecting distance education.

Findings are organized into four themes: positive aspects (e.g., independence from time and place, access to resources, use of information technologies, economy, reducing pandemic spread), negative aspects (e.g., social and psychological effects, technology and access issues, educational issues such as ineffective applied lessons and communication problems), challenges encountered (primarily infrastructure and lesson-related difficulties, plus assessment and connection issues), and distance education management (emphasizing process management, education platform issues, and the perceived lack of proper crisis/process management). The conclusions state that distance education can be used when formal education is disrupted, but problems in distance education affect course functioning and student participation, and sports applied courses require special consideration. Data security is also highlighted as an important issue, and the passage calls for further research.

The passage introduces magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) and the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect, describing how TMR depends on the relative magnetic moments of two electrodes and arises from spin-dependent tunneling. It contrasts ferromagnet-based TMR models with recent interest in antiferromagnetic electrodes, where noncollinear antiferromagnets and altermagnets can break time-reversal symmetry and generate momentum-dependent spin splitting and spin-polarized currents. The study focuses on first-principles calculations of TMR in Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn MTJs. Using DFT and a scattering-theory approach with Landauer–Büttiker formalism, the authors model bulk Mn3Sn and MgO and compute tunneling conductance, momentum-resolved transmission, spin polarization on Mn3Sn’s Fermi surface, and MgO complex-band filtering. Results indicate that sz-component spin polarization cancels contributions between ±kz, making the x-component (aligned with Mn3Sn’s cluster octupole easy axis) dominant for TMR. The calculated MTJ transport remains tunneling for sufficiently thick MgO, with TMR ratios reaching ≳1000% (at 12 MgO layers), attributed to momentum-dependent spin splitting in Mn3Sn and electron filtering/screening by MgO. The paper concludes by summarizing the realistic, thick-barrier reference for Mn3Sn-based MTJs suitable for electrical readout.

The passage reports that Jeff Bezos suggested future data infrastructure could be built in space using orbital data centres. He argued this could reduce constraints on land, energy, and cooling and improve resilience against terrestrial disruptions. It notes that growing cloud and AI demand is straining existing infrastructure and that data centres consume large amounts of electricity and water for cooling, raising sustainability concerns. The passage also states that key engineering challenges—such as radiation shielding, power storage, vacuum cooling, and low-latency communications—remain unresolved, and that launch and maintenance costs may limit near-term economic viability. It adds that other aerospace and technology firms are exploring orbital or lunar infrastructure, citing falling launch costs and advances in miniaturised hardware.

The passage describes owl eyes as immobile, tubular structures that help owls focus on prey and see in three dimensions. It then summarizes a study in the *Journal of Neuroscience* in which scientists tested barn owls’ ability to find a moving target among shifting backgrounds, a task previously studied only in primates. The study suggests barn owls can group different visual elements moving in the same direction despite having simpler brains than humans and primates. Researchers tested detection using screens of black moving dots on a grey background, tracked the owls’ gaze, and found the owls could spot the target dot and performed better when the contrasting direction was uniform. They also recorded activity from the ocular tectum, which varied with dot movement, indicating it was involved in the task.

London data indicating strong job creation and wage gains in the United States led to expectations of interest rate hikes, with the dollar and US bond yields rising and stocks falling on Friday. The US added 200,000 jobs last month, above forecasts, and wage growth was reported at 2.9%, the largest 12-month increase in over nine years. The greenback rose after the announcement, as did the yield on US government bonds, with the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 2.84%, a four-year high. Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare said wage gains may be good for the economy but can hurt the stock market if they increase rate-hike expectations.

Lifeline Fiji program director Jeremiah Merekula said suicide remains a taboo subject and emphasized its impact on Fijians, citing NSAAC statistics. There were 124 suicide cases and 107 attempted suicide cases in 2015, and 102 suicide cases and 104 attempted suicide cases in 2016. Since 2011 to March this year, 627 suicide cases and 694 attempted suicide cases were recorded, including 56 suicide cases and 97 attempted suicide cases among children. Merekula linked the high numbers to lack of help-seeking behavior, limited awareness of emotional wellbeing and warning signs, and copying mechanisms, and said Lifeline Fiji runs a 24/7 toll-free crisis helpline and is working with preschool and primary students and expanding programs with parents. People can contact Lifeline Fiji at 132454.

Gold edged lower on Friday as the dollar rose against the euro ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls data due at 1330 GMT, expected to show 180,000 jobs added in January. Spot gold fell 0.3% to $1,345.22 and June gold futures were flat at $1,353.10. Stronger payrolls could support expectations for U.S. interest rate hikes, which would likely weigh on gold. The Fed held rates unchanged but signaled further gradual increases. World stocks were set for their biggest weekly drop since late 2016 amid central bank tightening and higher inflation expectations. Silver, platinum, and palladium fell, with palladium up on the day but on track for its biggest weekly drop since early September, down 4.8%.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security’s Chris Young warned that attackers can corrupt data used for decision-making, calling it “data landmines.” He said stolen and manipulated data disrupted the 2016 presidential election and that undermining big-data analysis can lead to faulty outcomes for businesses. Young also said insecure home networks, including internet of things devices, can be compromised and turned into weapons, and that cooperation among security professionals is needed because none can address the problem alone. Microsoft President Brad Smith urged the technology community to act as “a digital Switzerland” using defense-focused principles—no offensive activity, collaboration, protecting all customers, and refusing to attack civilians—while governments should not stockpile vulnerabilities. He called for an international cyber agency to monitor and attribute nation-state attacks and cited cooperation among Microsoft, Google, and Facebook against terrorist propaganda. Smith also referenced a U.S.-China agreement limiting certain cyber espionage and urged government agreements on acceptable conduct in cyber conflict.

The passage describes a location-sharing and social-media system that provides a geographically based “map GUI” to predict a user’s presumed destination. The system receives location information from a user’s client device, determines the user’s current trajectory, correlates it with historical location information, and identifies a presumed destination. It displays an icon for the presumed destination on friends’ client devices and may also provide an estimated time of arrival, updating or removing the display if the likelihood falls below a threshold. It also explains how historical location data can be processed to extract trajectory patterns by extracting historical trajectories, clustering them, and deriving patterns by aligning and averaging trajectories. The server architecture includes an API server, application server, messaging system, social network system, and databases with message, entity/relationship, and location tables, supported by components for location determination, historical consolidation, prediction, and map GUI generation.

Thursday marked the last day for Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky and the end of the school year. Skorkowsky announced plans to retire last fall, and the school board named Dr. Jesus Jara as his replacement this month. Skorkowsky said he is satisfied with his impact, highlighting increases in the graduation rate from 60 percent to 83 percent and expansion of magnet schools by more than 10,000 seats. He noted the district faced a $60 million budget shortfall and said the new superintendent and board must meet with lawmakers ahead of the 2019 legislative session, which he called pivotal for education. He urged state leaders to rethink how marijuana money is distributed and said conversations should include parent groups and teachers’ unions. He also discussed school funding and teacher pay issues, along with school safety steps after the Santa Fe High School shooting, including single point of entry doorways and adding more mental health professionals. Skorkowsky advised Jara to get to know the community and listen to concerns, and said he and Jara will work together for a couple of weeks.

The passage describes hardware subsystems and peripherals of MSPM0G microcontrollers, including the CPU (ARM Cortex-M0+, pre-fetch/cache, SysTick, MPU, NVIC, and interrupt groups), operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with associated power domains and wake sources, and a summary of supported functionality by operating mode. It also covers the PMU and clock module (oscillators and distributed clocks), DMA, event manager behavior, and additional peripherals such as flash, SRAM, GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, DAC, security features, TRNG, AES and related keystore/CRC/math accelerators, and communication interfaces (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD). Lower-frequency subsystems (LFSS_B with RTC_B and IWDT_B) and other timers and watchdogs are also described, followed by sections on device documentation/support, tools, and revision/manufacturing and packaging/orderable information.

Radyr has been without a pub since 2003, and a Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open a micropub called the Radyr Tap in an empty unit on Station Road. The brewery says it wants to provide a local social space and venue to celebrate local beer, with beers and wines available for takeaway and no cooked food, but artisan meats, cheeses, and snacks from the bar. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council decides.

MIT rejected the Trump administration’s proposal to sign the “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education,” which would require sweeping campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding. MIT said the compact’s demands conflict with its values, including protecting freedom of expression and institutional independence, and argued that funding should be based on merit. MIT president Sally Kornbluth announced the decision in a message to the campus community. Other invited universities have generally said they are reviewing the compact, while some officials have threatened financial consequences for signing. MIT’s rejection was met with praise from some academic leaders and lawmakers, though some Trumpworld figures suggested potential retaliation.

Komar Uddin, a 68-year-old described in court as a priest and spiritual healer, denies sexually assaulting and raping a 19-year-old girl in Leicester at her home while promising to drive out an evil spirit. The jury heard that during a private candlelit religious ritual, Uddin allegedly rubbed holy oil on the girl’s stomach, stroked her back and hips, and then sexually touched and twice raped her. The girl said she initially thought the acts were part of the ritual, that Uddin’s voice became harsh, and that he told her afterwards not to tell anyone and that her “treatment” would not work. The family had invited Uddin due to concern about fear of an evil spirit. The court heard that an internal swab contained Uddin’s DNA. After his arrest in early 2015 and release on bail, Uddin left the country and was extradited to the UK from Germany in November. Defense counsel suggested the girl was lying and that she had offered sex, which she denied. The trial was continuing.

The passage consists largely of Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K content for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020, including taxonomies of line items, company information, and sections of the report. It states that the company’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under the symbol “AMZN” and provides corporate and executive officer and board director listings. It outlines business principles, operations in three segments (North America, International, and Amazon Web Services), and describes forward-looking statements and major risk factors, including intense competition, expansion-related risks, international risks, inventory and fulfillment network risks, data loss/security breaches, system interruptions, fraud and unlawful activities by sellers, intellectual property risks, fraud and payments-related risks, regulatory and legal risks, and product liability and tax risks. It also lists properties and selected consolidated financial data (net sales, operating income, net income, cash flows, and balance sheet totals for 2016–2020) and provides liquidity and capital resources information, including cash flows and cash and marketable securities balances at December 31, 2019 and 2020.

Prosecutors released three undated cellphone videos found on suspect Nikolas Cruz’s phone after the Feb. 14 Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland, which killed 17 people and injured 17 others. In the videos, Cruz says he plans to become the next school shooter, targets at least 20 people, and describes arriving at campus and starting firing, which school surveillance footage showed he did with an arrival at 2:19 p.m. He also discusses loneliness, anger, hatred, and references to others. Cruz is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 counts of attempted murder. His lawyers have said he would plead guilty if guaranteed life without parole, but prosecutors refuse to waive the death penalty. The Broward State Attorney’s Office released the videos under Florida public-record rules. Cruz’s defense says it did not request evidence such as inside-building video and autopsy reports to avoid further public harm to victims’ families and the community.

The passage argues that the navy needs about 1,000 additional officers to man ships now provided for and under construction, with enlarged classes at the Naval School in Annapolis and easier retirement for impaired officers. It describes strained workload on lieutenants and junior grades due to officer scarcity, many recruits, and unskilled men, expecting the strain to continue until more officers graduate and recruits become trained. It claims there is currently no expected foreign-power trouble and warns that refusing to maintain a thoroughly efficient navy would invite trouble and disaster. It cites rising Post-Office Department revenues, including rural free-delivery becoming a fixed policy, supported by financial results and practical benefits to rural communities. It also calls for further national irrigation efforts in the far West, along with thorough scientific forest protection, legislation to protect game and wild creatures on forest reserves, and stopping the slaughter of animals such as elk.

The passage argues that Donald Trump is trying not only to dismantle the existing “liberal world order,” but also to build a new one based on fossil-fuel power competing with green-energy states. It claims Trump’s domestic actions aim to weaken alternative energy and preserve a carbon-dominated economy, while his foreign actions seek an alliance of fossil-fuel states led by the United States, Russia, and Saudi Arabia and to isolate renewable-energy powers such as Germany and China. It describes a strategy carried out through steps including strengthening U.S.-Saudi ties (with major arms sales and energy coordination), undermining NATO and the EU, and withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement to expand fossil-fuel use. The passage also presents the creation of a “new trilateral axis” as energy-focused, citing large shares of global oil and natural gas production by the three countries and describing efforts to improve U.S.-Russia ties and energy cooperation between Russia and Saudi Arabia, while noting obstacles due to differing positions on Syria and Iran.

The passage describes the shooting death of 74-year-old Robert Godwin, which was broadcast and posted by suspect Steve Stephens, with Facebook taking more than two hours to remove the footage. It also mentions an immigrant rights activist, Hugo Castro, who went missing in Mexico after asking for help on Facebook Live, and notes attention on Georgia’s 6th Congressional District, where Democrats aim to flip a Republican seat.

Researchers report that blocking a protein called Ant2 can reprogram T cells’ energy use, making them more active, resilient, and better at attacking tumors. The study led by Omri Yosef and Michael Berger and involving other collaborators found that targeting a specific energy pathway in T cells, involving mitochondria, improves their stamina, replication, and targeting of cancer in mice. The team says this metabolic rewiring can be triggered through genetic modification and also with drugs, and could support new cancer immunotherapy approaches.

Global surgery is defined as improving health outcomes and achieving health equity for people who require surgical care, with emphasis on underserved populations and those in crisis. The passage notes that 16.9 million deaths annually are due to conditions requiring surgical care and describes global surgery as a neglected area in global health. It reports major inequalities in access to surgical and anaesthetic care worldwide, including five billion people lacking access to safe and affordable care and many facing catastrophic health expenditures. The Lancet Commission on Global Surgery 2030 highlighted the need for additional surgical workforce and education for future global surgery professionals, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

The study aims to assess Belgian medical students’ knowledge, attitudes, and exposure to global surgery and to identify approaches for global surgery curriculum development. It used an anonymous online survey administered to first-to-final year medical students across seven Belgian universities, with approval from an institutional review board. Data were analyzed with RStudio and excluded schools with fewer than 10 participants.

Among 304 responses, most students found global surgery relevant and wanted more education, but exposure was limited (24.7%). Knowledge was described as poor, with only small proportions correctly identifying key facts about surgical access, needed procedures, and stakeholders. The passage also reports obstacles to pursuing a global surgery career, including personal or family responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and lack of role models/mentorship. The authors conclude that Belgian students’ knowledge and exposure are lacking despite interest, and recommend pre-clinical global surgery seminars and equitable, bilateral international clinical internships in medical education.

The passage marks 50 years since Paul Ehrlich’s 1968 book *The Population Bomb*, which argued that overbreeding in poor countries was harming the planet, using a Delhi taxi ride as an example. It questions whether Ehrlich was seeing a uniquely overpopulated world or simply crowded conditions that could be found elsewhere, noting critic Jack Caldwell’s view that Ehrlich saw “poor non-Europeans.” It says cities are not the cause of rising population numbers; people in cities generally have fewer children than those in rural areas, with examples from Kenya and India. Urban population growth is attributed to rural-to-city migration, followed by smaller family norms. The passage adds that while cities may reduce population pressure, they are linked to higher consumption: although cities house about half of the world’s population, they consume about three-quarters of materials taken from the planet, and they rely on resources from beyond their limits, with London provided as an example of resource use and waste.

The passage states that the listed pages provide mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, described as the most current data for specified Texas Instruments devices, subject to change without notice. It includes notes for status, material type (preproduction prototypes and warranty-free early internal evaluation), RoHS values, lead finish/ball material options, MSL ratings and peak reflow temperatures (with the shipping label indicating the actual reflow temperature), and part marking conventions. It also contains an information disclaimer limiting TI’s liability and broad warranty disclaimers for provided technical resources, which are intended for skilled developers. Finally, it lists quadrant assignments for pin 1 orientation in tape and includes an address and copyright notice.

A gauge of global equity markets fell as U.S. bond yields neared the 3% level, with the 10-year yield reaching 2.998%. Investors cited concerns about rising government debt supply and accelerating inflation, while commodity prices dropped and pressured materials stocks. Commodities fell after the U.S. hinted it might ease sanctions on Russia’s Rusal; aluminum and gold declined. The U.S. dollar rose to a seven-week high, while the euro and yen weakened. Oil prices were volatile, with U.S. crude and Brent ending higher. U.S. stocks were mostly flat ahead of major earnings, with more than 180 S&P 500 companies expected to report and profit gains expected around 20%.

The passage says that WebRTC VPN bugs have leaked users’ real IP addresses since 2015, even when using VPN services. It states that many VPN providers later worked to hide IPs and that on March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers, finding 20 (16.13%) leaked users’ IP via WebRTC while 101 kept IPs hidden. It provides links to a Google Docs spreadsheet and to pages for VPN logging policy information and testing IP leaks. The passage lists providers it says leak users’ IP and suggests disabling WebRTC or using browser add-ons if an IP leak is found, noting that most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer. It also lists several VPN services it claims can protect privacy with WebRTC, including ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, and others.

Caterpillar Inc. voted to keep its quarterly cash dividend flat at $0.77 per share, payable May 20 to stockholders of record April 24, continuing seven straight quarters of flat dividends. The article notes Caterpillar still pays a 3.25% yield and has increased higher dividends for 23 consecutive years, but plans could include a future hike. It cites analysts at Goldman Sachs, who added the stock to a “conviction buy” list, pointing to increased miner capital spending and potential higher-mid-cycle earnings, with a $120 price target. The passage also attributes recent share gains to Donald Trump’s pro-energy and infrastructure policies, an improving U.S. economy, higher oil prices, and less severe concerns about China, while warning that the infrastructure plan’s timing and passage are uncertain. It further states Caterpillar’s 2016 revenue and EBITDA declined and cash flows fell, and that the company expects 2017 revenue and adjusted net profit per share to drop, making dividend growth difficult.

Electrocardiograms (ECGs) are widely used for cardiac assessment, and researchers aim to estimate echocardiogram (ECHO) variables from ECGs to improve early disease detection and access in resource-limited settings. However, this remains challenging due to (1) the complexity and variability of ECG signals and (2) the scarcity of ECG data labeled with ECHO outcomes. The passage proposes EchoingECG, a probabilistic student–teacher framework that uses PCME++ to model uncertainty with mean and variance and enables many-to-many cross-modal mappings between ECG segments and ECHO frames/text. To address limited annotated ECG-ECHO datasets, it uses ECHO-CLIP as a teacher model to distill ECHO-based cardiac information into ECG representations via training on ECHO-ECG pairs. The contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model, a distillation approach that reduces dependence on large-scale labeled datasets, and evidence that probabilistic modeling supports uncertainty-aware evaluation of downstream tasks.

The passage argues that territorial adjustments, including “trusteeships,” should not be brought up for discussion—especially regarding Pacific areas of interest—because doing so would provoke distrust and attention to aims. It concludes that such topics should be avoided until later in the war and after Russian participation in the Pacific war is accomplished, and notes that no satisfactory discussion can occur without full knowledge of the territories involved. It then quotes the Cairo Declaration stating that the Three Great Allies covet no gain and intend Japan to be stripped of Pacific islands seized since 1914, and describes an informal meeting held in Washington on January 26, 1945, where Mr. Grew discussed plans for a Mexico City conference on international organization, the Inter-American system, and the need for comprehensive measures to preserve peace, including the possible use of force.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 20, 2022. It reported releasing its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 by posting its First Quarter 2022 Update on its website, which is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing notes the information is intended to be furnished under Item 2.02 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act, and it includes Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on April 20, 2022.

Chris King, 57, made his first visit to Headingley Carnegie Stadium in Leeds to watch the Rhinos play Widnes Vikings. His visit was notable because he had both hands replaced in a hand transplant operation at Leeds General Infirmary the previous July after losing them in a work accident. He was applauded at half-time after going on the pitch and pulled out the winning ticket for the golden gamble draw. After the Rhinos’ 42-22 victory, King said the experience was exhilarating and better than he imagined, and that the live atmosphere was stronger than at home.

Crocs’ design patent for its molded-clog shoes was rejected by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office after a five-year legal battle, with the agency citing a similar patent filed earlier by another company. Crocs plans to appeal, but the decision is described as a major blow as the company struggles, including closing 160 stores over two years and a 3.3% revenue decline in the most recent quarter.

The passage discusses the rapid development of ICT and the growing importance of digitization, particularly digital infrastructure and digital content. It highlights the need for “digital accessibility” in education and society, defining it as inclusive access to IT services, websites, and digital information across users’ different needs, abilities, devices, and environments. It outlines the study’s aim to conduct a bibliometric analysis of digital accessibility in education literature and examines research trends from 2013 to 2024 using databases (WoS, Scopus, ERIC) and VOSviewer. The findings report a significant increase in publications over time, with the highest numbers in 2024, and show that most results are indexed in Scopus. For digital accessibility in education specifically, the passage reports an upward publication trend, dominant publication types (journal articles), concentration in certain research areas and educational levels (especially higher education), and a language distribution dominated by English. It also summarizes country/region publication patterns (notably the USA, UK, and Spain), and discusses citation relationships, including that citation counts and author/country link strengths are uneven and that further collaboration is needed. Ethics approval details are also provided.

On Monday, September 15, Rob Doyle and others held a DC Chamber Ribbon Cutting to celebrate the grand opening of The Shippers Group’s newest location at 300 Interstate West Parkway in Austell. The new 540,000-square-foot distribution facility offers warehousing, transportation, packaging, and e-commerce fulfillment. The Shippers Group, established in 1901, provides warehousing that began with the cotton industry and later general commodities, and has expanded to eleven locations since 1970. The company changed its name from Shippers Warehouse to The Shippers Group to reflect logistics and supply chain management services. Chamber vice president Sara Ray congratulated Rob, and the facility supports industries including food, consumer goods, automotive, and contract packaging, increasing the company’s Georgia warehouse total to 1.5 million square feet.

The passage describes the need for comprehensive cytogenomic evaluation in hematological malignancies and notes limitations of standard cytogenetic tests, which have lower resolution, subjective interpretation, manual workload, and lack complete assessment of both copy number and balanced structural aberrations. It discusses optical genome mapping (OGM) as an emerging technique that combines optical analysis and high-throughput scalability to detect balanced structural rearrangements and copy number variants with genome-wide resolution, and summarizes considerations for clinical laboratory validation and workflow integration.  

The study extends an International Consortium framework for OGM implementation by presenting a streamlined, laboratory-ready analysis and reporting workflow using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software for myeloid neoplasm datasets. Ten cases (nine AML and one MDS) were processed using Bionano reagents and Saphyr runs, analyzed with Bionano Solve and further processed through VIA with custom configurations and variant classification options. Independent blinded technologist and director reviews were conducted across replicate analyses to assess efficiency, reproducibility, and concordance with standard of care (SOC) results.  

Results report that OGM identified all SOC findings for the cohort, with SOC and OGM both detecting variants in six of 10 cases and both negative in four. SOC-detected sentinel variants were consistently classified as Tier 1A in all OGM reviews for positive cases, while OGM also revealed additional reportable variants in five of six positive cases, including large copy number losses and complex rearrangements. The passage also reports technologist review times, with faster times for negative and simple cases and longer times for complex cases. The conclusion states that OGM analysis using Bionano Access and VIA provides an efficient approach for interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants, potentially supporting more standardized variant interpretation.

A primary school headteacher, Mark Ryan of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School in Thornaby, was backed by the school community after inaccurate reports claimed he took a two-week holiday during term time to attend a wedding abroad. The reports also incorrectly alleged he told a parent their child would face a fine for taking a family holiday. Ryan said he had been granted three days’ term-time leave (June 7–9) for the wedding of a close family friend as an exceptional circumstance under school policy, and that he did not directly speak to the parent who contacted the newspaper. He said the report caused distress and highlighted that his only other absence request in 22 years was granted for his son’s graduation. The chair of governors and the school chaplain also defended Ryan, citing his commitment to the school and support from parents and the local community. Ryan is set to take up a new post as executive headmaster of St. Patrick’s and Christ the King Primary School.

After missing the playoffs despite the most expensive opening-day roster, the Mets began a staff overhaul. Manager Carlos Mendoza will return, but the team is moving on from pitching coach Jeremy Hefner; hitting coaches Jeremy Barnes and Eric Chavez and third base coach Mike Sarbaugh also will not return. Bench coach John Gibbons resigned, and catching coach Glenn Sherlock is retiring. The team said president of baseball operations David Stearns would evaluate the rest of the coaching staff after Mendoza’s return, and assistant pitching coach Desi Druschel and bullpen coach José Rosado were given permission to speak to other teams, while first base coach Antoan Richardson, strategy coach Danny Barnes, and coaching assistant Rafael Fernandez were invited back.

Apple has been the world’s most valuable public company by stock value and is close to reaching $1 trillion market cap, but its share price retreated after getting within $50 billion in early June. The passage notes that Amazon is narrowing the gap, with Apple’s stock market value dropping from 50% higher than Amazon’s to about 10% higher, a spread of about $85 billion as of Friday’s close. It also states that in 2018 Amazon’s shares increased by $260 billion, describing this as rapid stock gains.

Educational disparities—unequal educational opportunities, attainments, and resources shaped by social background—are presented as central to education and equity. Many studies focus on gaps such as academic achievement, regional opportunity disparities, and gender gaps, based on the premise that disparities are unjust and should be corrected. The passage explains that the fairness rationale is tied to luck egalitarianism: disparities from “brute luck” (factors beyond individual control) are unfair and should be eliminated, while disparities from “option luck” relate to individual responsibility.  

It then outlines problems with luck egalitarianism using Elizabeth Anderson’s harshness objection and humiliation objection. The harshness objection argues that severe consequences of option luck may be left unaddressed as the individual’s responsibility, with an education example of Naomi. The humiliation objection argues that compensation can undermine dignity by imposing stigma, including in educational contexts where messages to disadvantaged children may cause harm.  

To respond, the passage discusses adding values beyond fairness: fresh start and sufficiency to address harshness concerns, and respect to address humiliation concerns. It concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should not only examine fairness but also empirically study fresh start, sufficiency, respect, and related questions such as whether children can get to try again, where educational thresholds should be set, and what kinds of humiliation children experience in classrooms.

The case discusses an action by Hardin to enjoin an execution sale of certain real estate in Keokuk, which the court granted. The defendant White appealed. The Supreme Court held that the injunction bond was not required to be for double the judgment amount because the action was only to restrain the sale of specific property under a general execution, not to stay collection of the judgment. The court also held that White, after taking execution under a decree and selling the property to exhaust his remedy under that decree as to this property, could not later sell the debtor’s statutory right of redemption on another execution for the remainder of the judgment. On rehearing, the court clarified that the execution was issued for the balance of the claim embraced in the real estate decree even though it was issued under a different decree, and concluded its original reasoning was substantially correct. The judgment was affirmed.

Sickle cell disease (SCD), also known as sickle cell anemia, is a group of genetic disorders affecting red blood cells. In SCD, the body produces abnormal hemoglobin cells with a sickle or crescent shape, which do not last as long as normal cells, leading to fewer healthy red blood cells and problems throughout the body. The sickle-shaped cells can also stick in blood vessels and block blood flow. Symptoms can include sickle cell crises (sudden severe pain), acute chest syndrome, swollen hands and feet, anemia, jaundice, kidney and spleen problems, gallbladder disease, prolonged painful erections, bone and joint problems, serious infections, leg sores, high blood pressure in the lungs, heart failure, eye disease, and strokes. SCD diagnosis is done with a simple blood test and is often identified at birth through newborn screening in the U.S. Treatment involves education, regular screenings and checkups, vaccination recommendations (including annual flu vaccination for adults), daily antibiotics for children until age 5, monitoring tests, pain management, hospital care for some complications, medications that increase fetal hemoglobin, and sometimes blood transfusions or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for severe cases. Lifestyle recommendations include quitting smoking and limiting tobacco smoke exposure, maintaining a balanced diet, limiting alcohol, getting plenty of rest, and regular exercise to support overall health.

The passage describes a presentation made in Uganda on a three-year study of the sustainability of HIV treatment programmes in health facilities. The study found that lower-level facilities and small private clinics, especially smaller rural and for-profit facilities, face constraints that lead some to discontinue HIV treatment despite free ARVs, equipment, and training. It reports that Uganda’s HIV treatment funding architecture favors larger, established hospitals, which attract multiple donor grants, while smaller facilities struggle to meet performance requirements. Major barriers identified include shortages and attrition of trained personnel, difficulty meeting reporting mandates, and irregular or insufficient ARV supplies. The study also suggests for-profit organizational goals are not aligned with public health mass access goals, and patients often bypass smaller facilities for larger hospitals due to broader services, more staff, shorter waiting times, and fewer ARV stock-outs. The findings propose interventions such as mentoring through hospital twinning, service purchase agreements with for-profit providers, targeted salary support, increased government involvement, and expanded fiscal space to reduce reliance on donors.

The passage is a lecture on nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, focusing on India and Pakistan as potential flash points for nuclear war. The first speaker explains that nuclear exchanges would be catastrophic for people and could cause global cooling for years, with technology and policy issues such as inspection and verification remaining difficult. A plea is made for technically trained people to work in nuclear arms control. The main lecturer, Vipin Narang, outlines nuclear proliferation in South Asia and its consequences, describing an active arms race and the risks of escalation to the nuclear level. He discusses basic deterrence theory, including deterrence by punishment versus denial, and highlights requirements like capability, credibility, and communication. He then describes how India and Pakistan acquired nuclear capabilities: India’s initial nuclear motivation includes the 1962 war and later authorization of a “peaceful nuclear explosion” in 1974 followed by dormancy until renewed weaponization in response to Pakistan’s public nuclear claims; Pakistan’s program is framed as driven largely by the 1971 war and shaped by uranium enrichment efforts and later shifts to plutonium, along with international factors affecting development. Narang argues that India adopts an assured retaliation posture with no first use and recessed readiness, while Pakistan emphasizes deterrence of conventional attacks with an asymmetric escalation doctrine and battlefield nuclear capabilities. He connects these dynamics to episodes such as Kargil (1999), the attack on India’s parliament (2001/2002), and the 2008 Mumbai attacks, describing how nuclear risks contributed to Indian conventional restraint and ongoing crisis instability.

The passage discusses a Supreme Court case on whether Delaware’s “affidavit of merit” statute, which requires a plaintiff in a medical malpractice action to submit an affidavit attesting to negligence, applies in federal court. The main issue for the federal court is whether to follow federal civil procedure or Delaware’s more demanding state procedures under the “Erie” doctrine. The lower courts dismissed the case by treating the statute as “substantive,” while the defense argues there is no direct conflict with the federal rules, pointing to Rule 11’s allowance of affidavit requirements when a statute specifically states otherwise, and to the idea that the affidavit requirement falls outside what the federal rules address. The passage also notes an argument that the real-world purpose of these statutes is to make malpractice claims harder to bring, and it describes opposing views from civil procedure professors about how applying the statutes in federal court could disrupt routine administration.

The passage describes AIRSS (Ab-initio Random Structure Search), which generates random sensible structures using chemically informed parameters. It notes that resulting structures form a distribution near local minima, shown in FIG. 1. The parameters are set using MINSEP (pair-wise minimum atomic separation) and TARGVOL (target volume). A two-stage optimisation enforces constraints: overlapping atoms are pushed apart until no overlaps remain within a tolerance, then lattice and ionic degrees of freedom are optimised using a truncated Lennard-Jones model with fixed volume.

The passage describes an emergency involving opposition to U.S. revenue laws in South Carolina, which the speaker says threatens to obstruct revenue collection and endanger the Union. The governor of South Carolina transmitted to the speaker an ordinance passed by a convention declaring specified federal acts null and void within South Carolina and requiring state legislation and officials to prevent enforcement from February 1 onward. The passage reports that South Carolina officials are organizing military resources and preparing volunteers to resist revenue law enforcement, and that state laws provided for actions such as replevin against seized goods, penalties for disobedience, and measures for governor-led resistance to coercion by the federal government.

The speaker says previous executive recommendations and Congress’s actions have not reduced resistance, and urges Congress to consider measures to ensure the supremacy of federal law. The passage outlines steps already taken by the Treasury to instruct customs collectors and discusses how South Carolina’s ordinance and related state processes would impede U.S. officers’ ability to retain custody of vessels and cargoes. It argues that constitutional remedies were not properly used by South Carolina and concludes that executing the laws by constitutional means is necessary to preserve the Union.

The passage discusses a hockey game where a player was praised for strong puck handling, finding open teammates, and finishing. It notes that the winning goal involved a screen and that the team needs to play better in the lanes, be less deep, and improve positioning to prevent openings. It also highlights momentum swings, with the opponent’s power play generating many chances and scoring, while the team’s special teams were less effective. The passage mentions surprise at a late-game call related to contact in the corner and includes comments about adapting to matchups while on the road and being alert when changing lines and shifting on and off the ice.

Sequencing microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) in plasma is presented as progress combining genomic sequencing and recognizing mcfDNA as a clinically useful blood analyte. PCR-based multiplex panels have limitations in pathogen breadth and require infected tissue or body fluid; next-generation sequencing and plasma mcfDNA sequencing are discussed as potentially offering unbiased, noninvasive, rapid detection, especially for immunocompromised patients. The Karius Test is described as an analytically and clinically validated mcfDNA sequencing assay that identifies and quantifies mcfDNA in plasma from >1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites.  

A hospital-based commercial laboratory cohort is reported: 19,739 samples from 16,172 patients across 39 states (and D.C.), with a median 26-hour turnaround and 96% valid results. Among valid results, 42% were negative and 58% identified at least one microbe, totaling 701 unique taxa and 22,792 detections. Quality metrics for taxa quantification were met in 90% of positive-result samples. The most frequently detected taxa included bacteria (with major groups such as Streptococcus spp., Enterobacterales, and Staphylococcus spp.), viruses (including cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus), and fungi (including Candida spp. and Pneumocystis jirovecii). The study highlights detection of diagnostically challenging uncommon pathogens and includes discussion of test limitations related to missing orthogonal clinical context and data constraints.

The speakers discuss a difficult game in which they felt they did not play their best, citing issues with decision-making, puck movement, and defensive coverage that led to chances such as two-on-ones and giving up goals, including a game-winning goal. They note that despite the average play, they battled back, created overtime, and scored enough to give themselves a chance to win, which they attribute to effort and refocusing on their game plan. Coach Julien says the whole team was average and that they must be better next game while staying focused on the present. The passage also includes praise for Patrice Bergeron, mentions team discussions about momentum and preparation, and comments on specific players’ roles, conditioning, and contributions on offense and defense.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 28, 2019. The report includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements showing revenue of $2,220 million and net income of $394 million for the three months ended April 28, 2019. Total assets were $14,021 million and total liabilities were $4,317 million as of April 28, 2019. The report also describes cash flows, shareholder equity changes, key accounting policies and lease adoption, stock-based compensation, income taxes, marketable securities, derivatives, debt terms, commitments and contingencies, and segment information (GPU and Tegra Processor). In management’s discussion, revenue decreased 31% year over year, gross margin decreased to 58.4%, and operating expenses increased. The report discusses liquidity and capital return plans, the pending Mellanox acquisition agreement, legal proceedings, controls and procedures, and risk factors, and lists exhibits filed with the form.

The passage describes thyroid nodules and their potential to be benign or malignant, noting that thyroid hormone dysfunction can lead to hypothyroidism and untreated thyroid cancer may spread, especially to the lungs. It outlines a diagnosis process that begins with physical examination and may use fine needle aspiration (FNA) and ultrasound. Because ultrasound interpretation often requires expert radiologists, it proposes computer-aided diagnosis using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify thyroid ultrasound images as benign or malignant. 

The pilot study uses the Thyroid Digital Image Database (TDID) with TI-RADS categories, mapping TR2/TR3 to benign and TR4/TR5 to malignant. The methods include normalizing images, dataset splitting, image augmentation (rotation, shifting, flipping, and noise-related handling, excluding blurring and noising), and early stopping to address overfitting. A hybrid model combining VGG-16 and Inception v3 is trained using binary cross-entropy with class weighting to address unbalanced data. 

In results, the hybrid model achieves 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929, using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and ROC-based evaluation metrics. The discussion highlights that using pre-trained models and class weighting helped performance, and suggests that a larger dataset could improve reliability and refinement.

India’s main opposition Congress party elected Rahul Gandhi as its unopposed president, replacing his mother Sonia, who has led the party since 1998. The move is intended to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of the 2019 national polls. Supporters celebrated in New Delhi and Mumbai. Congress had struggled since its heavy defeat in the 2014 election, and Gandhi has faced doubts about his leadership, though senior leader Ghulam Nabi Azad said Gandhi is ready for the next challenge. The announcement coincides with state polls in Gujarat, with Modi facing criticism over economic growth and implementation of a nationwide sales tax; a Pew survey reported Modi’s popularity remains high compared with Gandhi’s.

The passage explains that interest rates and stock prices are often believed to have an inverse relationship, with rising rates typically lowering share prices. It notes that the stock market may react quickly and discount future rate changes, and that while the correlation between interest rates and stocks has been slightly negative, it has become more positive since the 2000s. The article backtests trading strategies using the S&P 500 based on whether a simple moving average (SMA) is above or below the 10-year yield, using unadjusted data for dividends. The strategy that effectively holds stocks when interest rates are rising produces poor compounded returns, while the strategy that holds stocks when interest rates are falling performs much better, with improved CAGR and similar drawdown. The passage concludes that holding stocks when rates are falling is more profitable than when rates are rising.

The passage says technology is making entrepreneurship easier and reports that Hiscox’s 2016 “DNA of Entrepreneur” surveyed 4,000 small businesses (up to 50 employees) in several countries, including the U.S. It highlights that many U.S. respondents want to be their own boss and that primary motivations often center on flexibility and control rather than money, alongside limited vacation use. It also reports U.S. business optimism and growth, identifies sectors showing strong growth, and notes findings on hiring intentions and lack of succession plans. The passage describes U.S. small businesses’ funding challenges and mentions Oregon programs that provide loans, loan guarantees, and related support backed by lottery dollars. It concludes with mixed views on government support, concerns about political instability, and an overall message of cautious optimism despite ongoing risks.

President Barack Obama said in an email statement released Monday that he will deliver a farewell address on Jan. 10 to reflect on his time in office and thank his supporters. He plans to give the speech in his hometown of Chicago and described it as an opportunity to thank people for “this amazing journey,” celebrate changes made over eight years, and offer thoughts on what comes next. The statement also notes that Donald Trump will be sworn into office on Jan. 20 and that Obama sought a smooth transition despite policy differences.

Apple Watch Series 3 has maintained strong manufacturer domination of volume and profits despite launching in only a limited number of LTE-capable markets. LTE connectivity was added as an upgrade in September 2017, initially reaching countries including Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, Japan, Puerto Rico, Switzerland, the UK, and the US, then expanding to Hong Kong and Singapore. Some wireless providers did not certify the LTE device, and Chinese authorities banned it after initially welcoming it. Global expansion remains slow; pre-orders begin May 4 in Denmark, Sweden, and India, with deliveries a week later. In Denmark and Sweden, support is confirmed through Apple’s only mobile operator, while in India Reliance Jio and Airtel are set to support it. Pricing has not been released.

IFC Films promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Boxer oversees theatrical, non-theatrical, and Canadian distribution for IFC Films, including Sundance Selects and IFC Midnight, and previously covered film distribution for Artisan Entertainment. Schwartz creates and executes promotional campaigns, previously serving as publicity director at Oscilloscope Laboratories. IFC co-presidents Jonathan Sehring and Lisa Schwartz said the promotions recognize their work and expertise, and noted their role in IFC Films’ reputation. IFC Films recently released Personal Shopper, Wakefield, and Chuck.

Marquez Charter Elementary is reopening on a nearly nine-month timeline after the Palisades fire, with the campus sparing only three classrooms. The roughly 130 students returning are the first public school students to come back to a campus destroyed by the Palisades and Eaton fires in January; for the 2024-25 academic year, Marquez shares a campus with Nora Sterry Elementary. Temporary campus facilities include 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library, and play areas. The reopening is described as a milestone for fire survivors, amid recalled memories and community statements about recovery. The district estimates the temporary campus and larger rebuild will cost about $202.6 million and be completed by 2028, with all three damaged campuses likely costing around $600 million. Enrollment has declined about 58% since the fires, and the district estimates three-quarters of enrolled students are not currently living in the Palisades. District officials cited a parent survey and town hall meetings in deciding to reopen Marquez instead of other campuses; 45% of responding parents wanted to return as soon as possible and 36.4% by August, while concerns about transportation and timing were common. Pasadena Unified has installed portable structures at several campuses and does not have a rebuild timeline, relying on multiple funding sources.

The passage presents The MMA Manifesto’s Middleweight Rankings, updated with new weight-class rankings on Mondays and Fridays. A voting panel of Jeff Fox, Ryan MacDonald, Ricky Leone, and Daniel Vreeland determines the rankings, excluding fighters who are currently suspended or inactive for at least 12 months without an upcoming fight. The top ten listed middleweights are Michael Bisping (1st), Luke Rockhold (2nd), Yoel Romero (3rd), Chris Weidman and Ronaldo “Jacare” Souza (tied 4th), Gegard Mousasi (6th), Robert Whittaker (7th), Anderson Silva (8th), Vitor Belfort (9th), and Kelvin Gastelum (10th). Each entry includes points, record, last five fights, record vs. top 10, and a “Next Fight” status, with Derek Brunson noted as dropped off and others mentioned as “bubbling under.”

The passage defines open education as a set of practices aimed at democratizing education by improving access to knowledge resources and making them more affordable and accessible, including OER, MOOCs, open textbooks, and open-access journals. It describes rapid global expansion and emphasizes inclusivity, affordability, and collaboration, while noting that comprehensive research remains limited and that adoption of open educational practices varies by region and is affected by digital divides, awareness gaps, and institutional barriers.  

The study described uses a two-pronged bibliometric approach (co-citation and co-word analyses) on Web of Science data to analyze trends, key publications, thematic clusters, and emerging future research areas in open education. From 402 selected English-language, peer-reviewed documents (search conducted in September 2023 using “Open Education” in the TOPIC field), it reports citation metrics and identifies five co-citation clusters (evolving open education; OER’s role in education; adoption of open education; educational paradigms of MOOCs; and implementation of OEP) as well as five co-word clusters (blended learning in open education; openness in the COVID-19 era; challenges of OER adoption; inclusive digital pedagogy; and collaborative online academia). The passage concludes with theoretical and practical implications for integrating open educational resources and practices—especially in higher education—and lists limitations tied to using only Web of Science, potential bias in qualitative interpretation, threshold-setting, and limited coverage of regional/institutional variation, along with suggestions for future research.

The passage describes the OHL trading strategy, an intraday stock approach that uses the open, high, and low price levels in the first few minutes of the trading session to determine trade entries. A buy signal is generated when the open price equals the day’s low price, and a sell signal occurs when the open price equals the day’s high price. The article also notes an optional modification using CPR levels, where long trades are taken only if the OHL buy signal occurs above CPR levels, and short trades only if the OHL sell signal occurs below CPR levels. It states that the strategy is best used on lower timeframes (1-minute or five-minute, up to 15-minute). Backtests are presented for S&P 500/ES futures (0930–1600 NY time) and WTI crude oil, with mixed results depending on variables such as whether today’s open is above or below yesterday’s close and other rule flips. The passage concludes that the direction of the first minutes may set the tone for the rest of the day, though further development is suggested.

The passage describes physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) as a mesh-free alternative for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), where neural networks are trained by minimizing a loss function that incorporates boundary value problems. It notes that PINNs face difficulties on complex, multi-patch computer-aided design (CAD) domains, including enforcing solution continuity across patches, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and handling variations in geometry size and shape that complicate normalization. The work’s contribution is a novel neural solver that combines PINNs with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to address these issues, including using reference-domain computations based on non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS). The proposed method builds neural-network-based ansatz functions defined on each patch’s reference domain, uses pushforward/pullback mappings to obtain solutions on the physical domain, strongly enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions via a modified NN output layer, and ensures continuity across patch interfaces through interface-conforming ansatz terms. Training uses a variational PINN framework with a discretized energy functional. Related work is reviewed, emphasizing that prior combinations of neural networks, PINNs, and IGA often focus on single-patch geometries and typically enforce interface conditions and Dirichlet boundary conditions only weakly. The passage also introduces the variational PINN formulation for elliptic boundary value problems, and summarizes relevant CAD/IGA concepts such as NURBS parametrization, pushforward/pullback operators, and multi-patch geometry assumptions.

Owen Sound Foodland was named one of 87 new stores authorized to sell beer and cider starting in April. Owner Bill Graham said the stores offer a one-stop shopping experience. The stores were selected through a competitive bidding process by the LCBO, bringing Ontario’s total authorized stores to 370. The Foodland in Georgian Bluffs is the first grocery store in the immediate Owen Sound area to sell beer and cider. It is being built on the site of the former Towers/Zellers building beside the current location, with a tentative opening of March 22. The 34,000-square-foot store will expand fresh offerings, catering, home ordering and delivery, health and wellness options (including gluten-free and allergy-sensitive products), and will add a seating area for meals. Traditional departments will also be expanded, and employee numbers are expected to increase from about 100 to about 160.

The passage explains that machine learning force fields (MLFFs), also called machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), provide a computationally efficient alternative to first-principles (DFT) methods by approximating DFT calculations using large datasets. It notes that state-of-the-art MLFFs are often graph-based equivariant neural networks (GNNs) that can work well with scarce training data, including expensive DFT trajectories, and that they have recent developments such as attention mechanisms and higher-order message passing. The passage discusses challenges in applying GNNs to point-defect simulations, which typically use large supercells and can require prohibitive data for complex 3D defect trajectories. It then introduces ADAPT, a coordinate-based Transformer that uses attention over all atom interactions and is trained to predict per-atom forces from raw Cartesian coordinates and atomic features. ADAPT is trained on a DFT database of defects in silicon (primarily complex defects) and is reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance in energy and forces, outperforming universal pretrained MLFFs (including MACE and MatterSim) and MACE retrained on the same data, while having a training cost two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures. The passage further describes that ADAPT uses separate networks for forces and structure energies and tokenizes each atom into a 12-dimensional feature vector (including coordinates and various atomic descriptors) before embedding into a higher-dimensional space for modeling.

Almost 88% of Ireland’s publicly quoted companies reported earnings that met or beat market expectations, despite fears after the Brexit referendum. A review of 33 companies found that Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil, and IFG Group missed expectations, while analyzed companies delivered average 8% earnings per share growth despite sterling’s slump against the euro. Sixteen quoted companies, including CRH and Kerry Group, beat EPS forecasts as full-year results were reported. The Iseq index reached a 15-month high of 6,750.78 points, about 6% above its level before the Brexit referendum. Irish Continental Group led the Iseq 10 index with a 17% rise since late December, followed by Origin Enterprises, Glanbia, Kerry Group, and FBD. Aryzta was the worst performer, with shares down 27.2%, while several other companies lost between 0.9% and 4.3% so far in 2017.

The passage says the Detroit Tigers, in the midst of an ALDS, need a true closer to end games. It suggests that bringing in Edwin Díaz?—specifically mentioning Suarez—as a potential fit if he opts out this offseason, noting his 2.97 ERA, 75 Ks, WHIP of 0.904, and 40 saves in 70 appearances. The passage criticizes the Tigers’ closer-by-committee approach and states that Suarez could be the definite answer.

The passage describes Turkey’s emergency distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic after face-to-face schooling was suspended. It outlines technologies and services used in Turkey (including EBA, ADES, TV broadcasts, and support guides) and provides pandemic-era enrollment and school-closure duration statistics. It also reviews research on parents’ experiences and views of distance education, citing findings such as added parental responsibilities, adaptation difficulties, infrastructure and digital literacy problems, reduced communication, and concerns about distance education replacing face-to-face learning. The study then reports its methodology (a descriptive survey with quota sampling; sample size 2371 parents) and the data collection tool (a questionnaire with demographic questions, yes-no, open-ended items, and scaled criteria). Findings include that 57.7% of parents viewed distance education positively (e.g., continuity and health protection) while 42.3% viewed it negatively (e.g., inefficiency, learning and adaptation difficulties, technical issues, inequality of opportunity, and insufficient content). Parents’ criticisms were categorized as inadequacy, difficulty, time problems, not similar to face-to-face education, and technical problems. Positive opinions emphasized avoiding being left behind, opportunities to repeat learning, and health benefits. Suggestions focused on online testing/exams, continuing support alongside face-to-face education, improving content and materials, and increasing lesson time. The conclusion states that most parents saw distance education as beneficial but inadequate as a replacement for face-to-face education, and recommendations address resolving infrastructure and internet-fee issues, reducing the digital divide, strengthening openness/open-source approaches, and improving digital literacy for learners, teachers, and citizens.

The passage is an alumni job bulletin email from the Haas School of Business offering a weekly announcement for Haas alumni jobs. It invites companies to submit openings to recruitalumni@haas.berkeley.edu with details such as location, title, company, degree, and contact information, and notes support from the Haas School Annual Fund. It lists multiple job postings across various locations and fields, including roles at Plumtree Software, Sanrise, ViroLogic, CJOL.COM (China Job Line), Atomz.com, Kaiser Permanente, Copper Mountain Networks, Loudcloud, Terrace Consulting, Rhapsody Networks, Pacific Gas and Electric Company, McKinsey & Company, Amerix, The Nature Conservancy, PBS, Zhanra Infostructure, and Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, along with specified degree preferences and some application or contact instructions for certain positions. It also includes announcements for Haas events such as the UC Berkeley Business Plan Competition launch and the Women in Leadership Conference, and a Big Game BBQ with contact information.

The Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission is planned to be merged with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by the end of this year, ending the agency after nearly a century. The Executive Yuan has not proposed a budget for the next fiscal year and says six of the commission’s 49 employees will be transferred to the council, while the remaining staff will continue handling Mongolian and Tibetan affairs under the ministry. The commission serves permanent residents in Taiwan, including 472 Mongolians and 648 Tibetans. Founded in 1928, it has faced calls for abolition despite the Constitution recognizing Mongolia and Tibet as traditional territories. A decision was made in October last year to prioritize scrapping the commission, and the Executive Yuan plans to propose abolishing its authorizing act in the next legislative session, though it also has authority to close it earlier. Lawmakers and parties responded with varying views, including concerns about absorbing parts of the commission, calls for de jure independence, and urging swift abolition of multiple agencies.

The passage describes a team with pride in understanding both losing and winning, focusing on positives while acknowledging that they lost. It highlights players who compete ruggedly within the system, do not think they are above others, back check, and do what’s expected, with a sense of responsibility to each other. It also mentions a brief incident where a puck went under the bar and the speaker hit someone in the head, suggesting a small moment could have made a difference, and concludes by saying the outcome came down to “a game of inches.”

Marouane Fellaini has turned down a new deal with Manchester United, and manager Jose Mourinho has urged him to sign as soon as possible, joking about doing so before knowing the extent of an injury. Fellaini will undergo further tests for a knee injury, will miss the next match against Huddersfield, and is at serious risk of missing Manchester United’s Champions League fixtures against Sevilla. The 30-year-old has missed 20 games through injury this season, returning from a knee problem in January.

Renewable energy output fluctuates with natural variability, and because the grid lacks storage, power must be consumed immediately. Surges from wind turbines can overwhelm the grid and cause outages, so operators sometimes pay consumers to increase usage on especially sunny and windy days. As coal phase-out progresses, managing intermittent fluctuations will become more difficult. Prof. Mahesh Bandi used turbulence theory and experimental wind plant data to study the statistical nature of wind power fluctuations, showing that wind power and wind speed follow similar spectrum patterns for different reasons due to how measurements differ. His analysis indicates that turbines within the same large and small turbulence “eddies” can behave like one giant turbine, and that geographically dispersed plants can have correlated low-frequency fluctuations that cannot be averaged out. He found that “geographic smoothing” only works up to a limit, using data from 20 wind plants in Texas and 224 wind farms in Ireland, and that this limit affects reserve requirements and environmental and policy planning, including optimizing combinations of renewable resources.

Merger arbitrage is a trading strategy that seeks to profit from the price difference between a target company’s stock price and the offer price during a merger or acquisition. It works by buying target shares at the current market price, expecting the spread to narrow if the deal closes, while recognizing that deal failure can lead to large losses. The approach requires evaluating deal completion likelihood, regulatory hurdles, and deal terms, along with active risk management and monitoring of factors like financing, market conditions, and liquidity. The passage reports backtest and performance results for merger-arbitrage funds/ETFs, including IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF and The Merger Fund, and describes a Verdad Research study of 835 deals (2000–2020) with an 89% closure rate; successful deals averaged about 2.0% return, canceled deals averaged -2.8%, and the blended average return on long exposure was about 1.5%. It concludes that disciplined merger arbitrage may provide returns with uncorrelated characteristics, but is difficult to execute without deep understanding of each deal.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 26, 2022. The filing states that Tesla released its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2021 by posting its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update on its website. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report includes standard disclosures that the information is intended to be furnished under Item 2.02 and is not deemed “filed” for certain purposes under the Securities Exchange Act. Exhibit 99.1 is listed, and the report is signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, dated January 26, 2022.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO, RE = Y, Gd, Er, Dy, Sm, Sc, Nd) show a color-neutral photochromic effect under ambient conditions and are highly transparent in the visible/near-IR. REHO films are made mainly by magnetron sputtering (e-beam evaporation also used), and deposition conditions affect microstructure, composition, and optical properties. Photochromism is stronger in thicker films and has been observed in different environments. Prior models for the photochromic mechanism and phase composition are disputed: one proposes a single-phase oxyhydride, while evidence suggests multiphase O-rich and H-rich regions and light-driven hydrogen migration, supported by studies indicating hydrogen mobility.
