For YHO, optical transmittance changes during blue-light illumination show two main processes: a fast component in the first 2–3 minutes with about 30% rapid darkening, followed by slower darkening/relaxation, with bleaching slower than photodarkening. Standard kinetic models (zero/first/second order) do not fit the data, so the authors model transmittance as a two-phase exponential decay including non-photoactive volume. Fits improve strongly with this two-process model. The fast process is linked to local/light-driven structural changes or loosely bound hydrogen release, while the slow process is attributed to hydrogen migration/diffusion and associated lattice contraction. Electron energy loss spectroscopy shows a lower plasmon peak energy in photochromic films versus opaque films, suggesting higher free or mobile hydrogen concentration in photochromic samples.

Thin-film fabrication and optical characterization are described, including reactive magnetron sputtering of yttrium hydride films on glass, oxidation in air, and transmittance measurements under controlled illumination with a 405 nm LED. The study concludes that two processes with distinct time constants contribute to the photochromic effect and that the proposed model fits the experimental data well for comparing photochromic film performance.

Congress failed to prevent a government shutdown that began at midnight Wednesday, creating uncertainty for the education system. The U.S. Department of Education said Title I and special education funds expected on Wednesday would be available as planned, but districts relying on other funding sources could face cash-flow issues. A longer shutdown could also create funding problems for Head Start and school nutrition programs, and grant payments could be delayed. The shutdown may stop most federal employees, pause civil rights investigations, halt work on regulations or guidance, and make it harder for states and districts to get help with grants. Separately, the Office of Management and Budget directed agencies on Sept. 24 to consider additional mass layoffs, a plan already challenged by federal employee unions in a lawsuit.

Chicago wheat prices rose Tuesday, recovering some ground after their biggest three-day decline since 2013, as rains brought relief to the U.S. winter wheat crop in the southern Plains. Corn edged up to end a four-session losing streak, while soybeans rose after deep losses on Monday. The passage cites beneficial rain and snow from a winter storm in parts of Kansas, Nebraska, and northern Colorado, alongside lower good-to-excellent ratings for winter wheat in Kansas and Texas. It also mentions Ukraine winter grains in good or satisfactory condition, pressure on corn from rains in Argentina, and Australian wheat offered at the lowest price in an Iraq tender.

Police arrested William Asa Hutchinson III, the son of Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson, on charges including driving while intoxicated, speeding, and violation of implied consent. He was booked early Monday in Washington County jail and released hours later on $1,626 bond. He is scheduled to appear in West Fork District Court on Wednesday and has another hearing set for July 19. The arrest followed a prior DWI case in which a judge dismissed the conviction due to citation errors. Hutchinson previously had been arrested in May 2016 in Alabama on charges related to MDMA and received pretrial diversion. A governor spokesman did not immediately respond to a comment request.

Billionaire U.S. investor Paul Kazarian, who owns Japonica Partners, said Portugal’s corporate sector is ripe for investment after opening his first European office in Lisbon. He praised Socialist governments in Greece and Portugal for policies aimed at recovery after the euro zone debt crisis, noting Portugal exited its bailout in 2014 and returned to strong growth while Greece’s program is expected to expire in 2018. Kazarian became one of Greece’s biggest bond holders in 2013 and says he saw an “anomaly” in Greek bond pricing, making Japonica a long-term holder of Greek debt with some bonds now matured. In Lisbon, he plans to look at investment opportunities including real estate and technology companies, citing growth in Portugal’s property market and technology sector following Web Summit’s move to Lisbon. He said he prefers larger investments and also plans to consider opportunities across Europe.

The passage describes a study on commercial Ni-rich NMC/graphite lithium-ion coin cells cycled at 1C–3C (room temperature) to evaluate how high C-rate cycling accelerates degradation. It reports that capacity declines faster under 3C cycling, with lower capacity retention and rising internal resistance over extended cycles. Structural characterization using XRD, SEM, and EDS shows changes in cathode and anode structure and surface features consistent with degradation, including a contraction of the cathode c-lattice parameter and increased signs of anode surface damage. Depth-resolved lithium quantification using Li Nuclear Reaction Analysis (Li-NRA) is used to measure lithium distribution in pristine versus extended-cycled “dead” electrodes, finding bulk lithium loss in the NMC cathode and lithium gain in the graphite anode, indicating irreversible lithium consumption and severe lithium trapping/plating. The study concludes that Li-NRA provides non-destructive, quantitative lithium depth profiling and links lithium loss and distribution to structural changes and performance decline under high C-rate cycling.

The Education Department announced it will rewrite two Obama-era student loan forgiveness rules, Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment, after complaints that the regulations are overly burdensome and confusing. Betsy DeVos said the process is unfair and costly to taxpayers, and that many colleges say the definitions are too broad and lack due process. The department will hold hearings in July and said it will fulfill nearly 16,000 borrower defense claims already being processed. Eight states and the District of Columbia filed a motion to retain the rules in federal court. The passage also references past enforcement actions against for-profit colleges and quotes critics and industry supporters reacting to the rule changes.

T-bills traded slightly bullishly, with demand favoring the shorter curve amid buoyant system liquidity from N300bn bond maturity inflows. The CBN raised its PMA offering to N49.60bn on Wednesday, May 30, which was moderately over-subscribed to N103.40bn, mostly by non-competitive bidders. The market expects yields to rise slightly tomorrow due to a likely OMO auction after c.N250bn inflows from maturing OMO bills and net PMA repayments. OBB and OVN rates fell further to 1.75% and 2.50%, and the interbank rate stayed at N305.95/$. The I&E FX window closing rate depreciated to N362.02/$, while cash and transfer rates rose to N362.50/$ and N366.00/$ after additional CBN retail interventions. Sovereign bonds declined slightly, led by the 2047s, down about 1.30 points to 99.70.

Kawann Short’s nickname “KK” comes from “Kawann,” with an extra K added because he is big. The Panthers agreed to a five-year, $80 million contract with Short, ending a year-long negotiation and avoiding the franchise tag placed on him in February. The extension is tied to the team’s win-now approach under GM Dave Gettleman and is intended to keep Short’s interior defensive line production strong through 2021. Other offseason moves to support immediate winning include re-signing Julius Peppers on a one-year deal, adding defensive backs (including Mike Adams and bringing back Captain Munnerlyn), and building a relatively older projected base defense. Offensively, the Panthers are focused on Cam Newton’s shoulder recovery after recent surgery, while also adjusting the offense with changes to receivers and tackle plans, including hope that Michael Oher returns from a concussion and that Matt Kalil can be “fixed” after a major left tackle contract. The passage concludes that the next major offseason move is the No. 8 draft pick, likely targeting an offensive playmaker such as Fournette, McCaffrey, or O.J. Howard.

Dozens of chess players will gather at the University of Calgary for the annual Battle of Alberta tournament on Feb. 18–19. The event, held each February at a post-secondary institution in the province, was hosted and won last year by the University of Alberta and hosted by Mount Royal University in 2015. This year’s tournament will be hosted by the U of C Chess Club at That Empty Space, with 30 to 40 players expected, including 6 to 8 from the club. The tournament will follow World Chess Federation standardized rules, including time clocks and the “no touch” rule. The U of C Chess Club was founded in 2015 by Riley Workman and Chinmoy Ayachit, and holds weekly meet-ups welcoming students of all levels. The tournament is open to independent players and non-students, with fees of $10 for university students and $15 for non-students.

The passage describes systems and methods using a cache coherent switch on chip (C/C SoC) with Compute Express Link (CXL) to enable low-latency, cache-coherent resource sharing among accelerators, processors, and memory. It includes embodiments of server systems with multiple accelerators connected via CXL to provide cache coherency, methods for receiving cache coherent data and bias/line-resolved updates, and switch-on-chip designs with upstream/downstream ports, switched fabric, and processing cores. The disclosure explains how C/C SoC can act as a switching layer to reduce CPU bottlenecks, support multi-host access, enable component disaggregation and composable virtual servers, and maintain cache coherency across components with minimal latency. It further describes resource pooling across servers and racks via networked CXL (including tunneling over Ethernet), fabric management for allocating/deallocating resources and managing hot-plug devices, memory expansion and buffering for persistent memory, and prefetching using AI/ML algorithms. Additional examples cover compression/security modules, erasure code acceleration for redundancy in persistent and other memory, legacy device support via SR2MR and SLD2MLD bridges, and supporting software stack/protocol frame formats for CXL over Ethernet with security and transport layers.

The passage explains that sugar futures are derivative contracts traded on commodity exchanges such as CME and ICE. They represent a legally binding agreement to receive or deliver a specified quantity of sugar at a pre-agreed price, with settlement depending on the exchange: ICE involves physical delivery under exchange supervision, while CME’s Globex settles financially at expiry. It outlines trading purposes for sugar futures (speculation, diversification, and hedging) and describes a proposed strategy type (an ATR channel breakout) that was backtested, noting generally positive but randomized equity results and a low win ratio. It also provides trading details such as trading hours, contract symbols (SB on ICE and YO on CME), contract size (112,000 pounds), minimum price fluctuation (0.0001 per pound), and tick size ($11.20 per contract). The passage states that sugar prices are influenced by government subsidies and tariffs, ethanol demand linked to oil prices, Brazil’s currency value, and weather, and it lists all-time high and low prices for sugar futures (66.00 US cents in November 1974 and 2.63 US cents in June 1985). It compares sugar futures with sugar CFDs (futures have expiry dates; CFDs do not) and highlights major risks from adverse price movement and leverage.

The passage discusses Prime Day as a time to buy MacBooks, noting that current discounts can be beneficial but that new models may be coming. It says all current MacBooks are at least $200 off on Amazon, and the 9/10 (WIRED Recommends) is presented as the best Prime Day deal, with a specific $800 configuration for a 13-inch M4 MacBook Air. The passage states the M4 MacBook Air is recommended for most people due to strong performance, battery life, and support for two 4K external monitors at 144 Hz. It also mentions the M1 MacBook Air remains sold for $600 and is recommended for students and those who want a cheaper option. The passage discusses possible future entry-level and Pro model releases, and it says MacBook Pro discounts are generally smaller (around 10–13 percent) while rumors of M5 MacBook Pro models could affect purchasing decisions.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether police need probable cause to enter a home without a warrant during an emergency. The case involves William Case, a Montana man who was shot in the abdomen after police entered his Anaconda home following a call from his former girlfriend about threatened suicide and harm to officers. Police said they entered to help, not to investigate a crime, and the officers had knocked and looked through a window before entering about 40 minutes later, after seeing what they believed was a suicide note and an empty handgun holster. 

Case argued that evidence from the warrantless entry should be excluded and urged a probable cause requirement; Montana’s solicitor general argued the Fourth Amendment protects against unreasonable searches, not all warrantless entries, and warned that a probable cause-of-peril rule could prevent officers from responding in time. Several justices questioned applying “probable cause” outside the criminal context, while others expressed concern that higher standards could hinder suicide prevention. The justices also discussed whether to remand the case for application of the state court’s “objectively reasonable” standard if one was not clear. A decision is expected by the end of June or early July.

The passage is a proclamation by President Jefferson (dated November 27, 1806) warning that certain U.S. citizens or residents are conspiring to launch a military expedition against Spain by fitting out and arming vessels, collecting provisions and arms, and deceiving others to join. It orders participants to withdraw and all involved parties to cease further proceedings, warning them of prosecution. It instructs U.S. and state officers, governors, judges, peace officers, military personnel, and militia to search for, punish, and prevent the enterprise by seizing and detaining relevant vessels and military materials. It also calls on citizens to help discover, apprehend, and report offenders, and includes the signatures of Jefferson and James Madison.

The passage is part of Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019. It includes the income statement, comprehensive income statement, balance sheets, cash flow statement, and stockholders’ equity statements for the three months ended September 30, 2019 and 2018, along with notes covering accounting policies, earnings per share, other income (expense), investments, derivatives, inventories, goodwill, intangible assets, debt, income taxes, unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, stockholders’ equity (including share repurchases and dividends), accumulated other comprehensive income (loss), and segment/geographic information. It also contains management’s discussion and analysis, including forward-looking statements, business and operating expense descriptions, segment results, and financial condition information such as cash, investments, and fair value measurement approaches.

Kano Pillars drew 1-1 with Niger Tornadoes in a week 12 Nigeria Professional Football League match at Sani Abacha Stadium in Kano, watched by many spectators. Niger Tornadoes scored through Andrew Ikefe in the 19th minute, while Pillars equalized in the 81st minute when Junior Lokosa converted a penalty. Pillars handler Ibrahim Musa praised the team’s fighting spirit, thanked the fans, and said the team would work to win their next match against Kwara United in Ilorin.

The passage describes a market structure trading strategy that involves analyzing swing highs and lows, support and resistance levels, and trendlines/channels to interpret price movements and identify trends and entry/exit points. It outlines three market structures—trending (clear directional movement), ranging (oscillation within a range), and consolidating (indecision with narrower ranges)—and explains how traders may act in each. It also discusses candlestick patterns (e.g., doji and engulfing) and volume analysis to validate potential structure shifts, Fibonacci retracements based on Fibonacci ratios to find likely reversal/continuation levels, and entry strategies including breakout trading and pullback trading. Risk management techniques mentioned include stop-loss orders based on key levels and adjusting position size based on pattern strength, with an emphasis on backtesting. The passage also notes that multiple time frame analysis can help confirm structures and that harmonic patterns (e.g., Gartley and Butterfly) rely on Fibonacci ratios but are difficult to backtest.

The letter to Congress transmits dispatches from Mr. Wise, U.S. envoy in Brazil, describing how the slave trade evades existing U.S. laws. It states that American vessels are ostensibly chartered in Brazil but actually sold for delivery to Africa, then re-crewed and navigated back with slave cargo. Documents also describe trade arrangements involving British brokers and merchants, the clearing of vessels through Great Britain for “coast goods” for the African trade, and the final exchange of merchandise for slaves, with vessels’ names and papers obliterated and crews replaced. The passage says penalties fall mainly on crews who may be unaware, while charterers and owners largely escape punishment, and that British subjects are implicated through their agents and factors. It argues that current British policy tends to perpetuate the trade by enabling large commercial interests through exchanges, colonial transfers, apprenticeship arrangements, and bounties to officers and crews. The letter concludes by urging the British Government to adopt more effective measures consistent with restoring captured Africans to their homes.

DS is expanding its UK range with the DS7 Crossback, adding the PureTech 225 petrol engine. The engine is designed in the Paris region, developed in Belchamp, and manufactured in Douvrin, and includes features such as variable valve timing, turbo twinscroll, 200bar fuel injection, Stop&Start, and a Petrol Particle Filter. It produces 225hp and reduces fuel consumption by 6%. Paired with the EAT8 8-speed automatic transmission, fuel consumption is further reduced via optimized efficiency and an ECO mode. The DS7 CROSSBACK launch year includes four Euro 6.2-compliant engines, including PureTech 180 and PureTech 225 paired with EAT8, and two diesel engines (BlueHDi 130 manual and BlueHDi 180 automatic). In the UK, the PureTech 225 petrol engine is available on DS7 Crossback Ultra Prestige, Prestige, and PERFORMANCE Line models starting at £34,990.

The passage presents an optimistic report to the U.S. Congress, saying the country enjoys domestic tranquility, industrial harmony, and strong prosperity, alongside foreign peace and progress based on mutual understanding and friendship. It attributes these conditions mainly to the integrity of the American people and to Federal Government cooperation and administration, emphasizing “constructive economy,” tax reductions, reduced debt, and growing national income.

It discusses government finances, warning that there is no surplus for further immediate tax revision and cautioning against actions that could lead to an unbalanced budget. It also describes domestic programs and expenditures, including veterans’ relief, public works, and agricultural improvements, while addressing issues such as the agriculture surplus problem, state responsibilities, and support for research and cooperative marketing.

On foreign affairs, it notes progress through inter-American conferences, arbitration efforts, and developments involving Nicaragua, Tacna-Arica, Mexico, China, Greek and Austrian debts, and major peace treaties. It also covers national defense, conservation, immigration policy, civil service pay, education initiatives, public buildings, and matters related to territories and government administration, concluding that prosperity and peace require continued effort and public confidence.

The passage argues that many aborigines, Creoles, and naturalized foreigners favor annexing Hawaii to the United States, especially after the likely death of the current sovereign, which would trigger an election by the legislative assembly for a king and a new royal line. It says any annexation would require approval from the U.S. government and links Hawaiian political tendencies to education and influence from American missionaries and New Englanders, with U.S. cultural influences and the Fifteenth Amendment making annexation more popular. It estimates Hawaii’s native population has declined to about 45,000 and that 5,000–6,000 foreigners live there, holding significant government offices and controlling much foreign capital in agriculture, commerce, navigation, and whale fisheries. The passage further claims the U.S. should consider Hawaii’s strategic position in the North Pacific, its value as a naval depot and coaling station, and its commercial importance due to trade with western regions and Pacific nations. It warns that other powers might harm U.S. commerce by taking possession and suggests the U.S. may acquire sovereignty with little cost, while discussing the current monarch’s lack of heir and the constitutional issue of naming a successor.

A mother shared that after her daughter Chloe, who has asthma and is fully vaccinated, played with a cousin who was sick during Christmas dinner, she developed a respiratory syncytial virus infection and was hospitalized in the intensive care unit. She said the cousin’s illness was believed to be a lung infection that wasn’t contagious, and Chloe required antibiotics, a breathing machine, and had an arm bandaged to protect her IV. She urged parents to keep sick children home to prevent others from experiencing similar outcomes, even if a child seems not contagious.

Ed Russo, developing the Annin Flag building in Verona into apartment units, said he wanted to maintain the property’s historic integrity and commemorated the project’s construction start on Flag Day, June 14, 2017. The building had been a flag manufacturing plant from 1919 to 2013, when operations ended, and will be converted into 112 rental units: 52 loft-style units in the main four-story building plus 60 studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom units in a new second building, with an added penthouse floor. The Verona Fire Department Honor Guard raised the American flag as people involved in the project shared stories about its past and future. Annin Flag CEO and president Carter Beard described the change as both sad and exciting, and architect Kurt Vierheilig said the development is expected to be ready in 12 to 14 months. Joe Vallone, a former plant manager, discussed memories from his 32 years at the plant, and Mayor Kevin Ryan said the site is a gateway to the community and part of Verona’s ongoing redevelopment.

The speaker discusses an important game moment where the team came back after scoring two quick goals and took over the game. They describe a goal-scoring sequence involving a bouncy puck and a hard slapper, and mention making a save by getting a glove on a rebound. The speaker contrasts earlier series outcomes, saying they respected and feared the opponents but kept playing well and eventually won. They also comment on Kenny’s emotional impact of scoring a big goal in a Stanley Cup final and say it reflects his hard work. They further describe Modano’s shot sequence and the save made as the puck went toward Brett Hull.

The passage is an Apple Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 26, 2016. It includes corporate information, checkmarks regarding required filings and electronic submission, and the number of shares outstanding. Financial statements for the three and six months ended March 26, 2016 (with prior-year comparisons) present net sales, costs, gross margin, operating expenses, operating income, other income/(expense), income taxes, and net income, along with basic and diluted earnings per share. It also provides condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income, balance sheets, and cash flows, and includes notes describing accounting policies, earnings per share calculations, financial instruments (including marketable securities and derivatives), share-based compensation, contingencies, segment and geographic information, and selected debt, dividends, and leases details. The report further includes management’s discussion of financial condition and results of operations, including forward-looking statement language, business overview and strategy, seasonality and product introduction effects, and second quarter fiscal 2016 highlights such as a 13% decrease in net sales primarily driven by lower iPhone sales and weaker foreign currencies, higher Services and Other Products growth, and shareholder returns and debt issuance.

The Foreign Office has offered to keep the writers informed about talks with Belgium, but these are described as occasional calls to discuss specific issues rather than ongoing negotiations. Matthews later received a memorandum on renewing the Anglo-Belgian economic accord for the Belgian Congo and summarized its main points: new wartime factors have increased the importance of West African raw materials, leading the British Government to press Belgium to boost production of several commodities, though Belgium finds it difficult to exert effective pressure due to competing Allied offers. The memorandum notes that while earlier agreements aimed to ensure Congo producers received not-less-favorable price and customs duty treatment than British colonies, the Belgian Government faces a difficult position due to higher U.S. offers for some items. It also cites obstacles from lack of coordination of Belgian orders and programs for machinery and other goods, and the hope that Belgium will submit a comprehensive 12-month program. The Secretary of State’s message adds that past confusion over UK and US supply and Congo needs stemmed partly from the Congo Government not providing comprehensive information; it reports that the Ministry of Supply in London proposed a broad over-all arrangement covering Congo requirements and UK/US purchases, after securing U.S. willingness to participate, and says meetings in Washington produced unanimous agreement that the procedure would simplify and coordinate exports and imports related to the Belgian Congo.

Nigeria’s Federal Government has started receiving Automatic Exchange of Tax Information (AETI) data from foreign countries, including the United Kingdom, on overseas assets held by Nigerians. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun said the data is being used to support the Voluntary Assets and Income Declaration Scheme (VAIDS) to verify declarations and to generate “nudge” letters to potential tax defaulters, noting Nigeria has also written to other nations for details on offshore trusts and bank accounts. She advised users of offshore structures to regularise taxes before the VAIDS amnesty expires and said the government is working to build a sustainable tax system. Earlier, NTPIC Vice Chairman Taiwo Oyedele said the Committee considered three policy documents and identified seven tax areas for reform, including CIT, VAT, customs and excise, PIT, pension contributions, IDITR, and education trust fund. He said proposed changes aim to increase and diversify revenue, simplify taxes for business, support SMEs, protect vulnerable people, and remove outdated legal provisions, resulting in two executive orders and five amendment bills.

Google says it will develop an ethics policy to guide its involvement in military projects after fallout from Project Maven, which prompted protests and resignations. The New York Times reports the rules will explicitly ban using artificial intelligence in weaponry. Google expects to announce details in the coming weeks and says it will consider employee feedback in drafting principles for defense and AI contracting. Internal emails and discussions described concern about media backlash, debate among employees, and involvement in policy discussions with Project Maven, including a letter opposing machine learning for autonomous weapons. After concerns escalated, Google held a roundtable discussion broadcast to employees worldwide, which did not fully ease worries that Google had betrayed its “Don’t be evil” mantra.

Sienna Senior Living Inc. announced a dividend of $0.075 per common share for February 2017, payable March 15, 2017 to shareholders of record February 28, 2017. The dividend is designated as eligible for Canadian tax purposes. Sienna’s Dividend Reinvestment Plan allows eligible shareholders to reinvest cash dividends into additional common shares issued from treasury at a 3% discount; participation is optional, and those who do not participate will receive cash dividends. Sienna operates 55 residences and serves independent living, independent supportive living, assisted living, memory care, and long-term care/residential care, with 9,000 employees.

Eleven Ursuline High students and six adults are planning a trip to Nicaragua during spring break from April 2 to 8. The students will help locals with basic needs such as food and housing, conduct home visits, and do simple tasks like cooking and playing with children. Parent volunteer Aimee Morrison said students will also help build houses. Ursuline High assistant principal Maggie Mattune said the experience teaches empathy and compassion, and helps students engage with other cultures and understand more global needs.

A pharmacist, Dr. Chukwuma Agubata of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, said that taking “Ogbono” soup made from Irvingia fat can improve the efficacy of the anti-malarial drug Artemether. He stated that Ogbono formulated as lipid microparticles can help the drug pass bodily barriers to reach its destination, and that the research addressed Artemether’s low water solubility by improving drug delivery and efficacy. Agubata reported good results and called for support from government and private organizations to further develop and mass-produce the locally sourced materials to reduce malaria burden.

A Nationwide Home Insurance survey found that pet owners spend nearly £3,500 in the first year, with average costs of about £2,455 for cats, £4,791 for dogs, £12,654 for horses, £769 for fish (including tank and pumps), and £1,802 for rabbits (including a hutch). The insurer cited record pet insurance claims of £706 million paid in 2016 by the Association of British Insurers. Among home insurance claims for pet-caused accidents, 7% involved carpet damage, 5% sofa or chair damage, and 5% a broken TV. Rob Angus said pet ownership can be rewarding but expensive, and people should plan and budget for lifelong costs.

The Palmerston North Rescue Helicopter made multiple dispatches on Saturday 9 December. It first met the Wellington Free Ambulance at the Avalon Landing Pad to transfer a 31-year-old man with a suspected spinal injury after jumping into a swimming pool to Christchurch Hospital. It was later sent to a rural road east of Pahiatua for a 57-year-old man who fractured his lower leg after colliding with a culvert while riding a motorbike; paramedics stabilized him before he was airlifted to Palmerston North Hospital. That evening, it went to Ohakune for an 11-year-old boy with a back injury after falling from a trampoline, who was treated at the scene and transported to Whanganui Hospital. The passage also states that Philips Search and Rescue Trust (PSRT) operates rescue helicopters throughout the Central North Island and relies on principal sponsors and community donations to provide life-saving equipment and trained medics.

The passage argues that education reform cannot succeed through only administrative changes because the teacher—the key human resource—must not be demeaned or disheartened. The study examines how teachers construct and (re)construct their professional identities during initial formation, based on the author’s experience and on theories of teacher identity that emphasize the interaction between personal and professional selves. It highlights “borderland discourse,” defined as integrating or negotiating personal and professional selves, as a way preservice teachers can develop a workable professional identity without sacrificing personal priorities. The author notes concerns about how the concept may be named or oversimplified, while maintaining that it depends on social, cultural, and historical context and involves complex transformations.

The passage also describes challenges faced by preservice teachers, including tensions between university theory and field-school practice, and cites research suggesting that early teaching years remain especially difficult. Using internship-report narratives from preservice teachers Laura and Richard, the passage shows how they negotiate identities at the border between being a student/apprentice and becoming a teacher. Laura describes anxiety and a perceived gap between theoretical training and school demands, later emphasizing flexibility, mixing innovation with tradition, and focusing on students and classroom reality. Richard describes the supervised internship as challenging and evaluates his training as traditional and disconnected from public-school realities, while also showing evolving professional identity through ongoing negotiation. The conclusion presents four inferences, including that both participants’ professional identities were reconstructed through change in the research context, that categorized identities are transient and not strictly chronological, that Supervised Internship II is important for reconstruction and awareness, and that Moodle interactions supported identity construction by sharing emotions and experiences.

The passage says many payday lenders could be forced out of business if Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rules finalized this week take effect, though Republicans in Congress oppose the changes. The new rule would require payday and auto title lenders to assess whether borrowers can repay in full within 30 days and limit how often lenders can debit borrowers’ accounts without reauthorization. The CFPB’s director says the protections prevent lenders from succeeding by setting borrowers up to fail. The passage also cites a CFPB study showing most payday loans are not repaid on time, with many being rolled over or followed by long loan sequences. Consumer advocates argue the rules would curb repeated debt, while the Financial Services Association of America says the rule would devastate an industry serving 30 million to 40 million customers annually and could push borrowers to other, less regulated options. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be cut in half and thousands of lender stores could close; the rules would not take effect until 2019 and could be rolled back by Congress. The passage adds that Congress and the Trump administration have challenged the CFPB, with proposals to weaken it and polls indicating many Americans want more regulation.

Ariel Miranda delivered seven shutout innings as the Mariners beat the Marlins 6-1 at Safeco Field. He allowed four hits, one runner reached second base, struck out five, and walked none, throwing 97 pitches with 66 through the first five innings. Manager Scott Servais said Miranda pitched more aggressively with his fastball, which Miranda used extensively as part of the game plan. The win also featured a strong performance from Robinson Cano, who hit a 441-foot home run in the first inning, followed by a home run from Nelson Cruz for a 6-1 Seattle advantage.

The passage lists multiple financial and business headlines, including warnings from the Bank of England about rising AI bubble risk, a EU push for climate reform for development banks, and transactions such as Fifth Third’s planned acquisition of Comerica for $10.9B and Santander UK’s CEO stepping down ahead of a TSB merger. It also reports that oil prices fell as easing Middle East geopolitical tensions reduced the risk premium, with Brent down about 1.4% to $65.07 and WTI down to $61.55, amid factors including higher U.S. crude inventories and signs of slowing demand. Market sentiment is described as affected by expectations of potential U.S. interest-rate cuts and renewed focus on production and global consumption fundamentals.

The passage describes how marine heatwaves disrupt the ocean’s “biological carbon pump,” which normally transports carbon from the surface to the deep sea. Researchers studying two Gulf of Alaska heatwaves (2013–2015 “The Blob” and 2019–2020) found plankton-driven changes that caused carbon to accumulate near the surface rather than sinking to the deep sea, interfering with carbon storage and potentially intensifying climate feedbacks. It reports that data from robotic GO-BGC Argo floats, ship-based plankton surveys, and related measurements were used, and that the food-web impacts differed between the two heatwaves. The passage concludes that marine heatwaves vary, highlighting the need for long-term, coordinated ocean monitoring to understand their ecological and climate effects.

Yen Bai province plans to develop comprehensive raw material and hi-tech processing facilities to boost its agro-forestry-fishery sector. Its industrial plan to 2020 (with a vision to 2025) focuses on expanding processing industries, developing trademarks, and growing markets for local products. The province has extensive forests and wood/bamboo resources, with 104 wood processing facilities and additional wood peeling and slicing facilities, but most use low-tech lines leading to low-quality products. Yen Bai seeks investment to produce high-quality furniture for export, targeting 300,000 products annually, and aims to earn 850 billion VND by 2020 from wood processing, doubling by 2025. It has zoned industrial tree plantation areas and detailed tea, cinnamon, and cassava production figures, along with processing capacity for tea and cassava and cinnamon oil extraction facilities. Van Yen district is highlighted for processing cinnamon, cassava, and timber. The province also calls for hi-tech investments to raise product quality, including processing camellia fruits and bamboo shoots, and plans cattle meat processing facilities totaling over 3,000 tonnes per year.

In No. 1995 (Equity), the defendants moved to dismiss, arguing that Frank McVey succeeded Bill Vassar as Lincoln County Attorney in January 1939 and was never substituted as plaintiff, and that the action was not continued within six months as required by Rule 25(d) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. The court noted the rule’s purpose and stated that the rule’s language is clear and unambiguous. It was admitted that Vassar ceased holding office in January 1939 and that no effort was made to revive the action in the successor’s name within the six-month period. The court rejected the plaintiff’s contention that Vassar was only a nominal party, citing the petition alleging the action was instituted by Vassar on behalf of the People of Oklahoma to seek escheat. The court held Rule 25(d) applied and dismissed the action without prejudice, and made similar dismissals in related equity and law cases, allowing the plaintiff an exception and requiring a proper form of judgment consistent with the opinion.

The professor discusses coherent states as quantum descriptions of the electromagnetic field, defined as eigenstates of the annihilation operator with complex eigenvalue \(\alpha\). Coherent states relate to classical electric fields, rotate in phase space during time evolution, and exhibit Poissonian photon-number statistics. The talk uses quasi-probability distributions (especially \(Q\), \(P\), and Wigner \(W\)) to describe phase-space behavior, noting differences such as positivity versus possible negative values. Coherent states are shown to be minimum-uncertainty states, saturating the Heisenberg uncertainty limit.

The lecture then shifts to intensity correlations using the second-order coherence function \(g^{(2)}(\tau)\). Classically, \(g^{(2)}\) is expected to be larger than 1, while quantum states can yield \(g^{(2)}<1\), serving as a sign of non-classicality. For single-mode light, \(g^{(2)}\) relates to photon-number fluctuations and can be smaller than 1. The professor compares coherent, thermal, and Fock (number) states: coherent light has \(g^{(2)}=1\), thermal light has \(g^{(2)}=2\), and photon-number states give \(g^{(2)}=(n-1)/n\) (e.g., the single-photon case yields maximal antibunching with \(g^{(2)}=0\)). Attenuating a coherent state does not produce a true single-photon Fock state because it remains Poissonian and can still produce multiple photons.

Finally, the professor outlines ways to generate single photons using single atoms/ions in a cavity or via heralding with multiple atoms, and reviews the Hanbury Brown–Twiss experiment concept for measuring photon correlations using a beam splitter and coincidence detection, including discussion of mode and system assumptions.

The Ambassador in Austria-Hungary reports that the Imperial and Royal Government received the enemy states’ reply to its December 12 note proposing peace negotiations. It states that the enemy governments declined to accede to the proposal on the pretense of lack of sincerity, and that their reply avoids discussion of ways to end the war, instead focusing on prewar facts, military strength, and their motives as they see them. The passage argues that responsibility for the war has already been judged publicly, cites Austria-Hungary’s forbearance before its ultimatum to Serbia, and says discussion of military advantage is “idle.” It contrasts Austria-Hungary and its allies’ aims of defense with the enemy states’ alleged goals of conquest and partition, and rejects claims that the proposal is a “stratagem,” asserting good faith. It further claims peace negotiations depended on the adversaries’ decision, disclaims responsibility for continued war, and states Austria-Hungary and its allies will continue until they secure peace to ensure their peoples’ existence, honor, and development and enable Europe’s cooperation on equal rights.

Mario Batali has surrendered oversight of daily operations at his restaurant empire after reports of sexual misconduct involving at least four women over at least 20 years. The complaints described include groping and grabbing from behind. Batali said the complaints “match up” with his past behavior and apologized, taking full responsibility. A spokesperson for his hospitality group said an employee reported inappropriate behavior in October, that it was the first formal complaint, and that Batali was reprimanded and required to attend training. ABC said Batali will step away from “The Chew” while allegations are reviewed. Food Network also said it is placing plans to relaunch “Molto Mario” on hold.

Starbucks’ stock has been largely flat since late 2015, disappointing many investors. The passage attributes the weak performance mainly to comparable-store sales that have fallen below 5% U.S. results for several quarters, alongside issues related to the Mobile Order & Pay platform. Management says it is rapidly implementing new solutions and comparable sales are already rebounding. It also cites sales drivers including the Unicorn limited-time drink and Starbucks’ Frappuccino Happy Hour, noting that the latter disappointed last year due to loyalty program changes and altered traffic/transaction recording methods. The company began paying a quarterly dividend in 2010, increased dividends from 20 cents to 25 cents in November 2016, and has had a compound annual dividend growth rate of more than 26%. The passage highlights China as a major growth opportunity, with Starbucks opening about 500 stores per year and expecting this pace to continue for decades, reporting 7% comp-store sales growth for the region last quarter.

The passage describes the development of the Grocery Basket Score (GBS), a model intended to automatically score health properties of grocery shopping baskets by linking basket composition to mortality. It addresses limitations of food-level rating systems like Nutri-Score by aiming to evaluate nutrition as a whole, and it complements dietary guidelines such as the Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), which give recommendations in servings per day. The GBS is built using NHANES dietary recall data linked to mortality data, engineering nutrient “density” and “deficiency” signals, and fitting Cox proportional hazards models to select a score based on a combination of eight signals for foods and beverages. Validation compares GBS outputs with Nutri-Score items from Open Food Facts (overall Pearson correlation 0.60) and with AHEI using NHANES 2017–2018 (correlations around -0.62 depending on moderate alcohol assumption). The passage also reports that the GBS has high correlation with AHEI and moderate agreement with Nutri-Score, with differences explained by which nutrients or attributes each system emphasizes. Limitations include reliance on U.S. self-reported data, missing nutritional labels in validation, and the model not capturing negative effects of alcohol beyond calorie density.

Cam Newton apologized for sexist comments he made at a recent press conference. He had told Carolina beat writer Jourdan Rodrigue that it was “funny” a female was asking him about routes. After facing backlash, including losing an Oikos Greek Yogurt sponsorship, Newton posted a video on October 5 in which he said his word choice was degrading and unacceptable, took ownership, and apologized to women worldwide, reporters, and families, adding that he learned a lesson and urged young people not to repeat his mistake.

Liberty Island was evacuated due to a climber at the Statue of Liberty. The climber was on the base after banner-related arrests on July 4, and police tried to persuade the person to descend. Earlier, a National Park Service spokesman said at least six people were taken into custody for hanging a banner on the statue’s pedestal reading “Abolish I.C.E.” Federal regulations prohibit hanging banners from the monument, and Rise and Resist said the climber was not connected to its demonstration.

The passage explains AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, which supports optional extensions to System Encryption (SEV) and SEV Secure Nested Paging (SNP) for page migration operations. It describes how software determines TMPM availability by checking the ENGINE_READY bit in a PM_Status register and notes that TMPM requires IOMMU enablement.

TMPM off-loads page migration by pausing DMA traffic while copying page content and updating IOMMU mappings, and it can migrate guest pages protected by AMD SEV/SNP features. The document outlines two main page migration commands: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for migrating pages that are concurrent DMA targets (requiring coordination with IOMMUs and a provided IOMMU host Page Table Entry location), and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for migrating guest pages in an SNP-enabled system based on specified page states.

It also covers migration of multiple pages (up to 128) using a Page Migration List, per-page status reporting (including PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS handling and retry behavior such as PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE), and requirements such as list placement at a 4KB system physical address. Performance guidelines include using larger commands (16+ pages and best at 128 pages) and pacing interrupts rather than interrupting every command. Several data structures are stated as not supporting migration, and it gives constraints for PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO involving IOMMU host page tables and avoidance of concurrent modifications to referenced hPTEs.

Finally, the passage describes TMPM firmware reloading: operations must be paused and the ring buffer torn down before issuing a reload command via the BIOS to PSP mailbox protocol (referencing publication #57299). It notes conditions for reload errors, firmware version requirements, and that drivers should check ENGINE_READY before communication. It adds that reload varies by EPYC family and that a TMPM driver should use PM_GET_CAPABILITIES to read FW_VER_Major, with EPYC family 19h corresponding to FW_VER_Major = 71 decimal, and use this to select the reload execution path.

Troy Edwin Tate and Elaine Burris Tate appealed an order affirming dismissal of their Chapter 7 bankruptcy case for abuse. The Fifth Circuit addressed whether, under 11 U.S.C. § 707(b), debtors with above-median income may claim a vehicle transportation ownership deduction when they have no loan or lease payment for their cars. The court reviewed the issue as a matter of statutory interpretation and focused on the “applicable monthly expense amounts” language in § 707(b)(2)(A)(ii)(I). After considering competing “plain language” and “IRM” approaches used by other courts, the Fifth Circuit adopted the plain language approach, concluding the deduction should be allowed even without a monthly debt payment. It therefore reversed the district court’s judgment and remanded for further proceedings.

The passage explains the need to link food data to ontology entities to support FAIR principles, interoperability, and EU sustainability and health goals, and notes that this process is difficult to do manually. It describes how biomedical semantic resources have advanced NLP tasks, while the food and nutrition domain lacks comparable resources, leading to the development of FoodSEM, a fine-tuned open-source LLM for food named-entity linking (NEL). FoodSEM is trained with instruction-response (IR) formatted corpora converted from annotated food datasets (CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA) and uses three ontologies (FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy). The fine-tuning dataset is also augmented with artificial IR pairs to balance ontology entity coverage. FoodSEM is instruction-tuned on an Llama 3 8B model using LoRA and is evaluated with five-fold cross-validation on NER+NEL and NEL-only scenarios. Results are reported using macro-weighted precision, recall, and F1; FoodSEM shows high and robust performance, with F1 scores up to 98% on some ontologies, and it outperforms 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot prompting baselines. The passage concludes that FoodSEM achieves state-of-the-art food NEL accuracy and suggests future work using scientific datasets and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for unseen entities.

The passage describes Checkr’s approach to “fair chance” (second chance) hiring, which aims to give qualified candidates with records equal job opportunities without lowering standards. After launching in 2014, Checkr’s founders noticed that candidates with conviction records—disproportionately Black and Hispanic—were being rejected at high rates, which they viewed as unfair and a missed opportunity. Checkr’s mission combines helping employers assess hiring risk with promoting fair hiring access, including safety and compliance commitments under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. The company supports its mission through tools such as Candidate Stories, Assess (filtering by conviction type, age, and other factors), and an Expungement tool, and it also operates CSR efforts and Checkr.org advocacy and fundraising. The passage outlines broader context on justice-impacted unemployment and barriers to work, summarizes fair chance hiring laws and corporate initiatives, and describes Checkr’s own use of automation to speed background checks. It concludes that Checkr sought to align its mission with business performance, arguing that fair chance hiring depends on company success.

The passage reports that no statistically significant differences were found between randomized treatment groups for any secondary endpoints, with estimated treatment effects close to identity values and similar results in the Per Protocol Set. Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events and overall changes in laboratory parameters (D-Dimer, CRP, Ferritin) and vital signs were similar between groups. Overall, 139 patients (28.78%) experienced adverse events, fatal adverse events occurred in 49 patients (10.14%), and serious adverse events occurred in 66 patients (20.63%), with no observed differences between groups. Transfusion-related side effects were reported in 19/320 patients (6.0%), and no TRALI cases were reported. Fourteen adverse events in 12 patients and seven serious adverse events in 7 patients were considered related to the study treatment, reported as occurring only/mostly within the plasma + SOC group.

The passage describes ESD protection and power-on reset behavior for TI TLV321x comparator devices. It states that inputs and outputs include internal ESD protection circuits, input voltages are limited to 0.2V beyond the rails, and TI recommends using a series current-limiting resistor when connecting to low-impedance sources to limit transient currents to 10mA or less if clamps conduct. It also explains that TLV321x devices have an internal POR circuit that activates up to 32µs after the supply crosses VPOR of 1.65V, holds the output low during POR for both Open-Drain and Push-Pull outputs, and after the delay period outputs reflect the differential input state.

The passage is a speech describing the recent Iraqi election as a “landmark” step toward constitutional democracy, while stating that violence will continue. It explains the speaker’s reasons for initiating military operations in Iraq, including the belief that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and involvement in terrorism, and claims Saddam Hussein was removed and jailed. The speech acknowledges difficulties in reconstruction and training, ongoing violence, and losses, then argues that the threat is a global terrorist movement with goals including driving the U.S. out of the Middle East. It outlines a three-part strategy—security with coalition offensives and increasing Iraqi control, establishing democratic institutions, and reconstruction to improve Iraq’s economy and infrastructure—and cites voter participation and optimism among Iraqis. The speaker argues against retreat, emphasizing risks to U.S. allies, troops’ morale, and terrorist capabilities, and says future troop-level decisions will be based on progress. The speech ends with calls for patience and support, plus prayers for troops during Christmas and Hanukkah.

Southeast Asian stock markets rebounded on Wednesday after early losses tied to fears of a Sino-U.S. trade war. Indonesian shares ended 1.8% higher after dropping 1.4% to a 15-month low earlier; Bank Central Asia rose 3% and Unilever Indonesia gained 4%. The Philippines closed over 1% higher, extending gains into a fourth session, with SM Prime Holdings up 2.8% and SM Investments Corp up 1.1%. Investors awaited annual inflation data due Thursday, which could signal further interest-rate actions. Financials and real estate supported several markets, while Singapore rose 0.3%, Vietnam rose 1%, and Thailand rose for a third consecutive session to a one-week high.

Michael Daniels, 40, of Ashford, was jailed for five years and three months for conspiracy to steal high-value motor vehicles from BMW Berry in Chiswick. He gave accomplice Alex Tingle spare keys to newly sold luxury cars and used customer address data to help Tingle carry out thefts, with a total of nine cars stolen over six weeks worth about £210,000. Judge Simon Davis said it was a “horrendous breach of trust,” and Daniels, described as a family man, was also noted to have worked at the dealership for 10 years. Tingle was jailed for two years and was immediately released after serving 13 months, with additional concurrent time for Class A drug possession. Murphy received 16 months earlier after admitting aggravated vehicle taking. The thefts affected victims, including one who missed the birth of their daughter due to the car being stolen on Christmas Eve.

“Baby Driver” has surpassed $100 million at the domestic box office after seven weeks, with $67 million earned overseas. Its remaining release markets include Japan, Russia, China, Italy, and South Korea. The action film, made on a $34 million budget, opened with $39 million in its first seven days after a June 28 release, following an SXSW debut in March. It has a 94% “fresh” rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and its soundtrack reached No. 1 on iTunes. Directed by Edgar Wright from his own script, the film is a TriStar Pictures and MRC presentation shot around Atlanta, starring Ansel Elgort, Kevin Spacey, Lily James, Jamie Foxx, Jon Bernthal, and Jon Hamm. Wright and other producers are credited, with production by Nira Park and executive producers listed.

Jury selection is underway in the Isaiah Hagan murder trial, where Hagan is accused of killing Halee Rathgeber last year. A judge declared a mistrial earlier this month, and the court agreed to keep the motion in limine to address evidence that could affect trial fairness and whether testimony should be excluded. Ten jurors have been picked so far, with 14 jurors selected from about 200 potential jurors, including two alternates; four more jurors will be selected Thursday. Hagan faces four counts, including murder and robbery resulting in serious bodily injury. Opening statements are set to begin Monday.

The passage explains what ETFs are and how they are traded, including that ETFs are baskets of securities traded on stock exchanges like stocks and can be bought and sold throughout the day via brokerage firms. It describes ETF trading strategies such as trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, quantitative trading, options-related tactics, volatility use, statistical arbitrage, pair trading/market-neutral strategies, global macro strategies, equal-weight and smart beta approaches, currency hedging, fixed-income ETFs, and commodity ETFs. It discusses benefits and drawbacks of ETF trading and mentions key risks such as market volatility, liquidity concerns, and tracking error. The passage compares ETFs with mutual funds, noting that ETFs trade intraday while mutual funds are bought/sold at end-of-day net asset value. It also covers topics including liquidity’s effect on bid-ask spreads, how expense ratios affect returns, taxation and capital gains considerations, potential suitability for beginners, and that leveraged/inverse ETFs have amplified or opposite-return goals with additional risk. The history includes early ETF developments culminating in the 1993 launch of SPY, with growth afterward.

The passage describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine and its role in page migration, including how it supports copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings to move data between faster and slower memory tiers. It explains TMPM’s reliance on IOMMU enablement, outlines key commands for migrating pages with concurrent DMA (PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO) and for migrating hypervisor or guest pages in Secure Nested Paging (PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST and PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO in SNP contexts), and defines a Pre-Migration reverse map table state for SNP guest pages. The document also covers multi-page command support (up to 128 pages per command), per-page status handling and retry conditions, performance guidance, and restrictions on which data structures and page types cannot be migrated. It further details TMPM firmware reload procedure, EPYC family-specific capability detection and reload behavior, ring buffer operation and interrupt sources, device initialization/shutdown requirements, SPA encoding considerations, and the general approach to error handling, including command rejection, partial success, and ring buffer error reporting.

The passage describes the Udvadia surname’s origins among Zoroastrians in Udvada and follows a doctor named Dr. Zarir Udvadia in a case involving a girl with drug-resistant tuberculosis diagnosed in 2012. After initial drugs failed, Bedaquiline was identified as a potential treatment, but it was not administered to the girl because her use was restricted by the Union government to select cities. Dr. Udvadia and the girl’s father petitioned the Delhi High Court, which ordered Bedaquiline to be administered. Dr. Udvadia later said he has 30 patients on Bedaquiline with a 70% success rate and that many more need urgent access, which remains difficult. The passage also discusses bureaucracy’s impact, the risks of drug resistance, strict compliance enforcement, and the lack of preventive vaccination for drug-resistant TB.

The passage is a conversation about hockey players and coaching, focusing on observations of Duncan Keith, Rask’s performance and role in success, and the qualities of a coach described as fair and level-headed. It also discusses teammates’ chemistry off the ice, personal changes as they get older, and references to maturation after prior playoff losses, noting growth as a group.

The passage contains information from Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 27, 2020, including filing details, shares outstanding (4,275,634,000 as of July 17, 2020), and a table of contents. It provides condensed consolidated financial statements for the three and nine months ended June 27, 2020 and June 29, 2019: statements of operations (including net sales, operating income, and net income), comprehensive income, balance sheets, shareholders’ equity, and cash flows. It also includes notes describing accounting policies and adoptions (leases and hedging), earnings per share calculations, revenue recognition and disaggregated net sales, financial instruments (cash and marketable securities, derivative instruments, and related disclosures), accounts receivable and vendor non-trade receivables, property and other balance sheet details, income taxes (including uncertain tax positions and European state aid), debt and repurchase activity, comprehensive income components, stock-based compensation, commitments and contingencies (including VirnetX and iOS performance management cases and French competition authority), and segment information by geographic regions (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific), as well as lease note details and some management discussion content.

Document 29 reports a private and confidential message from Austria-Hungary’s Minister President, Count Tisza, dated January 25. He draws attention to Penfield’s reported declaration in the House of Commons about President Wilson’s address, emphasizing that the enemy’s proposed peace terms would involve the mutilation and humiliation of Germany and the dismemberment of Austria-Hungary and Turkey, contradicting Wilson’s views. Tisza also argues that the ideal of free development of nations cannot be realized in countries with mixed populations, and that the dual monarchy’s political system comes closest to this ideal in southeastern Europe.

Document 30 reports a message from the German Ambassador, Bernstorff, to Colonel House. He thanks President Wilson for a communication made through House and states that the German Imperial Government trusts the President and is willing to accept his offered services to help bring about a peace conference, while not publishing peace terms because the enemies have published terms aimed at Germany’s dishonor and destruction. Bernstorff says Germany would enter negotiations under terms offered in December 12 if accepted by the enemy, agrees to a proposed second international conference after the war based on Wilson’s Senate message, and would have postponed the submarine blockade if possible, but could not due to unavoidable preparations. He argues the blockade will end the war quickly and explains that Germany began it because the Entente powers refused Germany’s peace offer and intended to continue the war to deprive Germany of provinces in the West and East, destroy Austria-Hungary, and annihilate Turkey, which he says violates international law and blocks neutral trade.

The passage is an address to the people of the United States explaining that the death of President William Henry Harrison has led to the speaker’s assumption of the presidency. It says the speaker will rely on public intelligence and patriotism, will follow constitutional principles, and will address foreign policy with justice and peace while ensuring no harm to the nation’s honor through effective military defenses. It calls for a separation between “the sword and the purse,” aiming to prevent presidential control over military and financial authority, and proposes limits on patronage and removals from office, allowing freedom of opinion and maintaining suffrage while restricting official partisanship. It advocates strict economy, avoiding a public debt in peacetime, abolishing sinecures, tightening expenditure oversight, and enforcing laws against peculation with severe punishment. It states that any conflict between government and currency should end, supports measures to restore a sound circulating medium, and emphasizes maintaining the constitutional balance between federal and state powers. It concludes by affirming efforts to implement these principles, preserve free institutions, and transmit them to future generations.

The passage discusses how the team played more physically and aggressively in game two than in game one, describing game two as more intense. It emphasizes the importance of not going down 0–2, playing with urgency, maintaining intensity, and initiating rather than sitting back. The speakers expect lower-scoring playoff hockey, mention needing more offensive chances at home, and anticipate strong home crowds. They highlight game three as a major, possibly biggest, game in the series and stress readiness, fighting for every inch, and playing the same style as in recent periods.

GBP/USD is moving within a 30-pip narrow range as bears consolidate losses after hawkish Fed Yellen testimony. Yellen said rate hikes would be appropriate in the coming months and that every meeting is “live,” prompting a rally in the dollar as treasury yields rose and knocking cable down. Upcoming influences include the UK jobs report, followed by US CPI, retail sales, and industrial production, with additional focus on Fedspeaks. The passage argues that detente means relaxing tensions with potential enemies, and that it requires both sides to take positive actions. It claims arms control negotiations cannot be effective if they are one-sided, and that U.S. defenses must be maintained while negotiations with the Soviet Union continue. The speaker says they would negotiate an honest, verifiable reduction in nuclear weapons to ensure neither side threatens the other, but would not agree to treaties like SALT II if they legitimize a one-sided nuclear buildup. The passage cites the Austrian State Treaty as an example of effective negotiation during the Cold War. It also describes Soviet strategy goals, including dividing NATO, expanding influence in the Arabian Gulf and South Asia, encircling China, and supporting subversion in the Caribbean, and warns that Soviet military effort focuses on strategic nuclear programs. The passage concludes that U.S. strength is intended to prevent conquest, not to prepare for war, and criticizes Lenin-Marxist ideology.

Merck said it is halting the late-stage trial of its Alzheimer’s drug verubecestat after an independent study found it had “virtually no chance” of working. The decision follows Eli Lilly’s ending of its solanezumab trial after no improvement versus placebo. Merck said it will continue studying verubecestat in people with less advanced disease, while experts described the results as highly disappointing amid ongoing debate and concern. The passage notes that there is currently no proven treatment to slow Alzheimer’s progression and that amyloid plaque buildup is long suspected to be a main cause, though verubecestat’s failure raises concerns about the beta amyloid theory. It also says other companies are still trialling BACE inhibitors and that Biogen is running a trial of aducanumab. Results for Merck’s verubecestat trial were expected in February 2019, and Merck’s shares fell by nearly 2%.

Edward C. Turner was arrested for driving under the influence and refused a chemical breath or blood test. After receiving the officer’s sworn refusal report, the Oklahoma Commissioner revoked his driving privileges for six months. Turner received an administrative hearing, after which the revocation was sustained, and he appealed to the District Court. The District Court found the revocation justified but reduced the revocation period from six months to three months. The Supreme Court held that the District Court was not authorized to modify the six-month suspension under 47 O.S. 1967, § 6-211 as interpreted in State ex rel. Oklahoma Department of Public Safety v. Kopczynski, and stated it did not distinguish Kopczynski based on hardship. The opinion also discussed a 1975 amendment to § 755 as a limited exception and concluded it did not reflect the intent of the 1967 legislature; it affirmed the suspension with the modification reversed. A dissent argued Kopczynski was distinguishable and that judicial modification remained governed by § 6-211, especially as hardship became a statutory ground after 1975.

The passage describes a case about Vermont City Electric (VCE), a municipal utility formed in 1905 to lower the cost of providing electric power. It outlines VCE’s demand-side management (DSM) approach, the planned structure and units of demand analysis using load duration curves, and VCE’s power supply options, including owned generation (McNeil and a gas turbine), renewable and hydro contracts, and wholesale market purchases, with fuel mix and projected costs. VCE implements nine DSM programs (e.g., new construction and existing facilities for business and residential customers, retail rebates, smart lighting, heating/air conditioning support, outdoor lighting consulting, and a LED streetlight replacement), with 2009 costs and estimated energy savings lasting six years. After the late-2008 economic downturn, VCE restricts total 2009 DSM direct spending to $800,000, and it needs to optimize which DSM programs to keep. Daniela Shazar is tasked with using a mixed-integer optimization model to compute VCE’s least-cost electricity supply plan for 2009–2014 with and without DSM impacts, including carbon impact calculations and a DSM budget constraint, to answer which programs to implement and the total carbon impact of the strategy.

The passage describes system components and device memory and pin configuration for a Texas Instruments processor. It explains that C674x accesses via the MDMA port are remapped through a system MMU to protect ARM Cortex-A8 memory regions, and that EDMA TC0/TC1 accesses may also be routed through the MMU; EDMA MMU use is enabled/disabled via the MMU_CFG register. It also summarizes the roles of the Media Controller and the HDVICP2 video accelerator, lists supported video codec standards and key HDVICP2 elements, and describes the face detection (FD) module’s resolution, memory use, and features. The passage further covers unified memory mapping and outlines L3/L4 memory maps and DDR TILER extended addressing. It then provides extensive detail on terminal functions, including boot configuration pins (BTMODE sampling), mailbox communication, spinlock hardware semaphores, and pin multiplexing controlled by PINCNTL registers, along with examples of specific peripheral and I/O pin function tables and supply voltage requirements.

The instructor introduces an MIT course on effective field theory (EFT), outlining prerequisites (quantum field theory 2, with background lecture notes and readings from QFT 3), grading (five problem sets, a final presentation, no exams), and the course focus (basic EFT ideas first, then soft-collinear effective theory). The instructor explains EFT’s “big picture”: by focusing on a specific scale, one can simplify calculations using the principle of insensitivity to higher-energy physics. EFT requires identifying relevant degrees of freedom, symmetries, and the expansion (power counting), producing an effective Lagrangian whose higher-order terms allow corrections to arbitrary precision (as illustrated with non-relativistic and post-Newtonian expansions). EFT can be used “top down” (integrating out heavy degrees of freedom from a known high-energy theory with matching to low-energy operators and constants) or “bottom up” (constructing the most general low-energy theory from symmetries, power counting, and degrees of freedom, fitting unknown couplings to experiment). The instructor discusses examples and motivations including hydrogen, where neglected particles lead to small corrections but also affect how parameters like the electromagnetic coupling are defined across scales. The passage also covers the role of ultraviolet divergences, logarithms arising with scale separation, and how these can be handled via renormalization within EFT. Finally, it introduces the standard model as an EFT in a bottom-up approach, describing its gauge and matter content, relevant mass scales, the expansion parameter (ratios of Standard Model mass scales over omitted higher scales), the emergence of higher-dimensional operators, and an EFT-based definition of renormalizability order by order in the expansion.

DTE Maharashtra released the MHT CET 2018 exam pattern and syllabus circular on dtemaharashtra.gov.in. The MHT-CET-2018 is scheduled for May 2018 for admission to the first year of full-time degree courses in engineering and technology, pharmacy, and pharma-D for 2018-2019. The syllabus and exam details were set by the Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education. The circular states the exam will have 20% weightage from Class XI and 80% from Class XII, with no negative marking, and indicates the difficulty level will be on par with JEE. Candidates are directed to download and print the circular PDF for details.

The passage describes how the team values fan support as excitement but says success is controlled by broader forces. It emphasizes that players share minutes, build rhythm, and focus on winning rather than individual minutes. The speaker frames the rivalry as a fight for the cup, saying the team is willing to do whatever it takes to win, and describes hockey as an emotional game where high emotions are positive. The team is described as hating to lose, feeding off its captain’s mindset, and requiring everyone to match each other’s intensity and be willing to sacrifice for victory. The passage also discusses a loss, stating the other team scored more goals and had a better power play, and that the team believed it deserved to lose, while the other team turned up its play with improved passing and sharper execution.

The passage describes a wireless local area network (WLAN) context, including infrastructure basic service set (BSS) and independent BSS modes, and discusses limitations of existing IEEE 802.11ac multi-user grouping mechanisms for large numbers of clusters, mixed MU transmission schemes (OFDMA clusters with OFDM MU-MIMO groups), and flexible per-transmission clustering and scheduling, while noting that current MU control frames add overhead and reduce MAC efficiency.  

It then summarizes methods and apparatuses in which a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) receives and decodes an NDP multi-user (MU) MAC physical layer convergence protocol (PLCP) protocol data unit (PPDU), determines whether it meets an NDP condition, processes MU control information carried in an NDP SIG field, generates a response based on the NDP SIG field and MU control information, and transmits that response. The passage further details new MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms, including signaling membership and position information via clustering management frames and updating position bit-fields per transmission (either via the data packet SIG field or via MU control frames).  

A range of MU control frame and NDP MAC PPDU designs are described, including high-efficiency (HE) NDP MAC PPDU formats with legacy preambles and HE NDP SIG fields (including variations with SIG-A and SIG-B), along with specific HE NDP MU control frames such as MU-RTS/MU-CTS for downlink and MU Poll/ULR/MU schedule/MU ACK for uplink. The passage also provides examples of how sub-channels and cluster-related information can be conveyed to synchronize users and support MU transmission scheduling.

The passage is an investor webinar transcript for Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (XENE) focused on its Kv7 and Nav1.7 programs being developed to treat pain. Xiaomi is celebrating its 8th anniversary and launching two new devices at an event in Shenzhen, China starting 11:30 am IST: the Mi 8 SE (a second Mi 8 variant) and the next generation Mi Band 3. A defense attorney for Quinton Tellis alleges that Panola County District Attorney John Champion sought false testimony from an unrelated defendant, in exchange for leniency. The attorney asked that Champion be removed from the case and punished, and that a September retrial be delayed while the state attorney general’s office takes over prosecution. James Patterson increased his annual donations for classroom libraries from $1.75 million to $2 million. Scholastic Inc. said he is distributing 4,000 gifts of $500 each to teachers nationwide as part of the “Patterson Pledge,” launched in 2015 with Scholastic Book Clubs. Patterson and Scholastic officials said the grants support teachers who often buy books with personal funds, and he has also donated to bookstores, literacy programs, and college scholarships for teachers.

The passage describes a 10-day family road trip that included visits to several National Parks, such as Badlands, Glacier, Yellowstone, and Devil’s Tower. The author shares “confessions” about weather and climate topics prompted by these experiences, including the value of communicating uncertainty in forecasts, how weather agencies can convey probabilities, and warnings people sometimes ignore when making risk-related decisions. The author references comments from weather and psychological experts about uncertainty messaging and risk perception. They also discuss glacier loss in Glacier National Park, and an encounter where someone dismissed climate change based on recent cold weather while camping. The author concludes with a humorous note about Devil’s Tower’s connection to *Close Encounters of the Third Kind*.

Football teams have tendencies that opponents can exploit; successful teams adjust by identifying their tendencies, recognizing defenses’ responses, and attacking the adjustment. The passage explains the Draw play as a running play that briefly resembles a pass before handing the ball late to the running back, aiming to take advantage of defenses committed to pass coverage and spread out to defend the middle. Draw is said to be most effective in pass-heavy offenses or obvious passing situations, because defenses expect throwing and align accordingly.
