Its biggest weakness is against blitzing interior pressure, which can leave the tailback in the backfield if additional defenders come unaccounted for; the passage notes many offenses tag an RPO to address this. It then outlines blocking rules for Draw against specific front structures (3-4 odd and 4-3 even) and describes variations: QB Draw for athletic QBs, and Lead Draw from 12-personnel Strong-I with specific alignment and blocking differences.

The passage reports discussions in which Finnish leaders and U.S. officials express concerns about Finland’s war position. It notes that recent Allied reverses have strengthened Finnish confidence in German success, but fears remain about German exhaustion next fall and Finland’s ability to make decisions. It also states that Finland’s expectation of a short, victorious war with Britain ignoring it was miscalculated. Later sections describe a conversation between the Finnish Minister and Assistant Secretary of State Berle about Finnish-U.S. relations, with Berle emphasizing Germany as the enemy of the United States and arguing that a separate Finnish-Russian war view is impossible. Telegrams from Schoenfeld to the Secretary of State report no Finnish press references to Stalin’s declared Soviet war aims, claim the Finnish government is suppressing or distorting statements by President Roosevelt, and describe a short-lived increase in Finnish bread rations due to Baltic ice disrupting maritime grain shipments and requiring emergency requisitioning of wheat and rye seed.

The passage reports a study on how education leaders influence the introduction and sustainability of ICT use in Morocco’s compulsory primary and secondary schools after the COVID-19 pandemic. It describes Morocco’s pandemic shift to distance learning and the Ministry’s related resources and platforms, noting that many teachers were still dissatisfied and that post-pandemic ICT sustainability had not been adequately studied. Using a 2023 survey (130 teachers who reported abandoning technology after resuming face-to-face classes), the study identifies major barriers including limited access to devices, fast internet, and digital content; limited ICT/techno-pedagogical training; lack of institutional support (training, devices, connection, digital resources, and online meetings); and the need for incentives and support for teachers, students, and parents. The findings emphasize that these barriers are linked more to leadership factors than to teachers’ demographics. The passage discusses the results using ISTE technology leadership standards and proposes implications such as unifying digital learning platforms, strengthening stakeholder coordination, developing structured teacher-training programs, improving digital content evaluation and access, and increasing devices and internet connectivity.

Kingwood High School in Kingwood, Texas reopened for the first time since Hurricane Harvey struck last August. After more than six months of closure due to flood damage, the school district said the storm caused millions of dollars in damage and that 2,782 students were sent to another school while repairs were completed. Superintendent Elizabeth Fagen reported that damaged flooring, walls, and doors were replaced, and renovations included security enhancements plus a new gym, theater, and an under-construction pool. The school will host a community open house next weekend, and Fagen said she is proud of how people handled the situation.

The passage introduces CrI₂ as a magnetic van der Waals material whose reduced dimensionality and tunable symmetry enable exchange interactions shaped by lattice geometry. Bulk CrI₂ is ferromagnetic, while monolayer CrI₂ is antiferromagnetic; few-layer CrI₂ is used to study how stacking geometry controls magnetic energy scales in bilayers. Rotations/translations between layers determine allowed anisotropic interactions, while layer separation and orbital orientation modify interlayer exchange; non-centrosymmetric stacking enables Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) and symmetric exchange anisotropy forbidden in the monolayer, and defects can create twisted or inverted bilayers. Using first-principles DFT (with DFT+U, dispersion corrections, and exchange-tensor extraction), the work finds the monolayer ground state is AFx. For bilayers, among direct and indirect stacking families, the indirect BA′ stacking with antiparallel interlayer AF alignment (↑↓/↓↑) is the global energy minimum, with nearby stability for AB′ states and higher energies for direct and high-symmetry stackings. Formation of bilayers reduces the band gap due to interlayer hybridization, and BA′ stacking shows spin splitting tied to broken inversion and AF order, with the magnitude depending strongly on interlayer magnetic alignment. By mapping sliding, the study shows registry-dependent energy minima separated by moderate barriers (≈25–50 meV/f.u.) and that sliding can switch magnetic states without chemical modification. Exchange-parameter analysis indicates intralayer (in-plane) exchange dominates (strengthened by about 6–10% from monolayer), while interlayer exchange is weaker and sensitive to both stacking and interlayer spin texture; DMI appears only in inversion-breaking (indirect) stackings. The passage also reports that inversion-breaking stackings activate magnetoelectric effects, producing in-plane polarization Px (a few µC/cm²) coupled to DMI and anisotropic exchange, enabling electrically identifiable stacking registry and potential device applications such as reconfigurable spintronics and magnetoelectric control.

Ian Murray, 74, of Hathersage, was fined £185 and ordered to pay £85 costs and a £30 victim surcharge after pleading guilty to driving without due care and attention following a collision on Main Road, Hathersage, on May 14. A cyclist was injured and feared he had broken his neck, and later returned to hospital due to new symptoms. The court heard Murray said he was driving uphill with visibility issues and did not see the cyclist until turning right into the Spar garage area. The cyclist suffered bruises, grazes and a laceration, and has pins-and-needle sensations in his hands, with a prognosis of recovery. Murray’s driving licence was endorsed with six points.

The passage describes basketball defensive and offensive strategies focused on denying a super star the ball, influencing the ball handler away from the star, and attacking offensively by forcing the star to play defense and expend energy. It includes instructions such as using pass denial with a “Stop Sign,” providing defensive help, preventing one-on-one isolation, trapping in mismatch situations with “Go Green,” taking offensive charges to put the star in foul trouble, boxing out to prevent offensive rebounds, influencing the ball handler to the opposite side and establishing box pressure by denying return passes, driving and drawing fouls, running the star through hard screens, and using combination defenses (with links for graphic details).

A Hylian Shield version of the New Nintendo 2DS XL for “The Legend of Zelda” will be available exclusively at GameStop stores on July 2 for $159.99. The streamlined New Nintendo 2DS XL, released in 2015, includes features such as a clamshell design, a faster processor, and amiibo support, but it lacks the 3DS’ autostereoscopic display. It is pre-loaded with “The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds” and can play Nintendo 3DS games in 2D and Nintendo DS back-catalog titles. Nintendo president Tatsumi Kimishima said the 3DS family has sold 72 million units worldwide and noted future developments were uncertain alongside the Nintendo Switch. The passage also states the Switch sold nearly 18 million units in the last fiscal year, with Nintendo expecting to sell 20 million more, and says E3 next month will reveal Nintendo’s projects for its consoles.

Marsha Jackson, newly promoted Head of Internal Audit at RiseEngineer Corporation, is tasked with ensuring internal controls over financial reporting and compliance with the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), including for RiseEngineer’s subsidiary in Elysium. After an anonymous whistleblower tip claims a misconduct-related contract win in Elysium, her compliance team investigates and finds details about an Elysium government tender, related dinners and gifts, official tours, large monthly government payments followed by transfers to Boston, a $3 million offshore payment to TGH Consulting, $5 million in cash withdrawals with limited documentation, and sales communications suggesting escalation to General Counsel. The Elysium team’s head prioritizes profitability over paperwork, gives salespeople uncapped commissions and autonomy, defers to sales in conflicts, and the Elysium finance manager allows cash withdrawals and bank transfers with incomplete or no documentation, with limited approvals and estimates for uncertain accounting. The passage also includes an overview of internal control concepts (COSO framework) and summary facts about the FCPA, followed by discussion questions for assessing the whistleblower claim and potential control/process changes.

The passage explains that soccer players must specialize in different positions while also learning how to interact with players in other positions, guided by a formation and system of play. It outlines common soccer position names and the need for coaches to identify their formation, specify and consistently use the position names, and avoid type-casting young players by ensuring they can play all positions. It describes the common full eleven-player setup (11 v 11) and the main position groups: goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards, noting that many positions have synonyms. It then defines roles and requirements for the goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards, and lists more specific names associated with different formation structures (e.g., center/fullbacks, center/halfbaks, attacking/holding midfielders, and various forward/wing striker roles). It concludes by stating that coaches should choose a formation and system of play that fits their comfort level and players’ talents, select position names for that formation, and use them consistently.

The passage describes the need for a single monitoring solution that can automatically discover and monitor any deployed application, requiring each application to implement a common monitoring interface. It notes that standardized interfaces (e.g., syslog, ETW, JMX) differ in protocol and communication style, and that distributed systems may include both custom and off-the-shelf components, leading to many monitoring interfaces to integrate. It says most monitoring solutions use plugins to adapt different formats to a common interface, and suggests using the adapter pattern: an application container is wrapped by an adapter container that transforms the application’s monitoring interface into the interface expected by a general-purpose monitoring system. It claims this decoupling improves maintainability and comprehensibility, allows application updates without updating the monitoring adapter, enables reuse of the monitoring container across different application containers (possibly provided by monitoring maintainers), and isolates CPU and memory resources by deploying the monitoring adapter as a separate container.

The passage explains how to backtest a Bollinger Band trading strategy in Python. It discusses downloading historical stock or ETF data using the yfinance library, importing pandas, numpy, and matplotlib, and calculating Bollinger Bands using a 20-day simple moving average with bands at ±2 standard deviations. Trading rules are provided: a position of 1 is set when the adjusted close falls below the lower band, and a sell signal sets position to -1 when the adjusted close rises above the upper band. The passage then describes calculating daily strategy returns based on position (shifted by 1), computing cumulative returns, and plotting the equity curve. It reports that the strategy compounded at 2.65% per year while being invested 10.6% of the time, and notes the strategy is for informational purposes.

Scientists from Skoltech developed a mathematical model of memory based on “engrams,” which represent concepts characterized by multiple features corresponding to sensory experiences. Their analysis suggests memory capacity is maximized in a seven-dimensional conceptual space, implying an optimal number of senses is seven rather than five. The model indicates engrams evolve over time toward a steady state, and the researchers report that the number seven is robust across model details, with an added caveat that multiple engrams near a center are treated as one concept. They suggest the findings could inform robotics, artificial intelligence, and understanding human memory, while noting speculation for human sensory evolution.

The Williams VixFix indicator, invented in 2007 by Larry Williams, is intended to create a synthetic VIX reading for instruments beyond the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones 30. The original VIX is derived from the implied volatility of stock index options on the CBOE and is meant to represent market “fear” or “complacency,” with high readings tied to increased fear and market lows and a negative correlation to the S&P 500. Williams VixFix is calculated as (Highest(Close,22) − Low) / Highest(Close,22) * 100, measuring price volatility over the last 22 trading days as a lagging indicator. The passage states that Williams VixFix closely resembles the real VIX in levels, swings, magnitude, and timing, and that it can be used in other markets such as the ETF TLT. It reports tested trading strategies using the S&P 500 and QQQ, including long and short variations using PercentRank and specified exit rules, with results including profit factors above 1 and mean revertive behavior; the strategy is described as trading frequently and outperforming buy-and-hold for QQQ while being invested only part of the time. It notes that the indicator is tested on stock indices, with limited testing on other asset classes.

Major technology companies have strict anti-harassment and anti-bullying policies but mostly rely on user reports to remove abuses. Melania Trump is hosting executives from major online and social media companies to discuss cyberbullying and internet safety in an event that is her first public appearance on the topic. Expected attendees include Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google, and Twitter, along with representation from the Internet Association. The passage describes that some platforms have set up reporting and help resources, but abuses have continued, including Twitter’s efforts to crack down on hateful tweets and protect people whose nude images are shared online. It also cites that Yik Yak shut down partly due to bullying and harassment complaints. Common online bullying tactics include embarrassing photos, demeaning remarks, and sharing screenshots of private messages, and it notes that harassment affects adults as well as teenagers. The passage says there is no federal law covering bullying, and discusses calls for schools to receive more tools and money for anti-bullying programs. It also recounts Trump’s earlier statements about fighting cyberbullying and her broader focus on child well-being.

The passage reports that Opera has launched Neon, an AI-powered browser intended to make browsing more proactive and task-oriented. It describes Neon as enabling users to delegate actions like filling in forms, comparing content, and writing code, with navigation and interaction occurring autonomously while operating locally on the user’s device. The privacy-first design is presented as strengthening data control and reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure, supported by workflow-organizing tools and reusable prompts for automating recurring actions. Opera is marketing Neon as a subscription product with immediate early access and broader availability planned. The move is framed as part of an “agentic browsing” trend, and the passage notes that ensuring reliability and compliance while executing tasks independently may be a challenge, alongside concerns about safety, transparency, and regulatory oversight.

Keaton Jones, a Tennessee middle school student, posted a viral video describing bullying he faced at school. Recorded in his mother Kimberly Jones’ car and shared first on Facebook, the video spread via Twitter and across the nation. In it, Keaton asked why people bully and said he hopes things will get better, and that people who are different shouldn’t be criticized. His sister Lakyn Jones represented him and received thousands of offers of support. After the video gained attention, athletes and celebrities—including University of Tennessee quarterback Jarrett Guarantano, ESPN’s Jemele Hill, the Tennessee Titans’ Delanie Walker, and NBA star LeBron James—reached out and invited support. A Go Fund Me campaign for Keaton and his mother raised over $58,000, and its organizer said it was not about Kimberly Jones while urging against bullying through judgment. Reports also emerged about Confederate flag images on Kimberly Jones’ Facebook account, prompting Lakyn Jones to respond on Twitter. Tennessee senators Lamar Alexander and Bob Corker also tweeted support for Keaton and the need to prevent bullying.

Karuna Nundy, a 42-year-old lawyer, is a Supreme Court advocate and one of the drafters of Womanifesto, a bill of rights for women intended to change laws relating to crimes against women. The passage highlights her work on anti-rape and sexual harassment laws, justice efforts for Bhopal gas tragedy victims, court arguments on constitutional law, and representation of rape survivors. It also notes her education at St. Stephen’s College, Cambridge University (Emmeline Pankhurst Prize, Amy Cohen Awards, Becker Studentship), and an LLM at Columbia University (full fellowship). She is described as speaking out against the Blue Whale challenge and using Twitter and Facebook to raise awareness among younger demographics. Devina Bakshi is quoted praising Nundy’s work on marital rape laws and workplace sexual harassment prevention.

The passage states that Warby Parker (WRBY) is expanding retail presence and growing its customer base. It reports upward average selling price trends, new product lines, and a high gross margin profile despite tariff headwinds. The company raised FY25 guidance to project 14%–15% revenue growth and nearly a two-point margin expansion, with continued double-digit growth expected in FY26. It reiterates a “Buy” rating based on WRBY’s brand strength, margin expansion, and growth runway, despite premium valuation, and notes disclosure statements and chart information.

The passage describes a footwear sole structure and outsole that incorporate traction elements, including an annular cleat set and one or more radial cleat sets arranged around a central axis, with at least one traction element forming a peripheral cleat on a peripheral surface. It outlines conventional footwear components (upper, outsole, midsole, insole) and provides detailed example configurations, including major, minor, and peripheral cleats with specified geometric features (heights, tapering widths, reinforcing ribs, and cleat shapes). The disclosure also describes composite/modular construction of outsole plates (including shells, skeletons, and cleat inserts) and a midsole with a casing and core, plus optional shank and cradle components. It further includes clauses specifying the outsole, sole structure, and related article of footwear configurations, and discusses advantages such as traction in lateral and longitudinal directions and composite construction benefits.

The Motz Corporation, founded in 1977, serves the natural and synthetic turf markets and operates multiple business units, including The Motz Group and USGreentech. Now operating as an ESOP, the company says the transition enables employees to share beneficial ownership, aiming to drive engagement, ensure customer satisfaction, and attract talent. Joe Motz states the ESOP reflects the company’s commitment to employees and will not change the management structure; Joe Motz will continue as CEO, with Zach Burns as President of The Motz Group, Valerie Webster as President of USGreentech, and Kevin McDonnell as CFO. The Motz Group focuses on synthetic and natural turf services for sports fields, and USGreentech focuses on synthetic turf infill.

In the playoffs and particularly in the finals, the speakers say the team has performed well but wants to get a little better to finish strongly. Coach Julien responds to players’ comments by saying they don’t want to overreact, noting the team competed in a tougher overtime loss and is striving for improved play throughout games. He also attributes better power-play performance to added personnel, puck movement, confidence, and better decisions. The team is described as calm with no panic, focusing on the next goal, and confident on the road despite tight series games. Additional discussion includes finding ways to score (including through different play types), being oneself as a player, the balance of respect and authority between coach and players, adapting to changes in how players want guidance, evaluating line matchups based on performance rather than “hard matchups,” and praising Dennis Seidenberg for playing hard and fitting the team’s style.

The passage is an email notifying subscribers of the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for Friday, May 18, 2001. It includes instructions for accessing the journal online or receiving a plain text version, lists practice areas covered (including summaries of three Michigan Supreme Court orders and one Michigan Court of Appeals published opinion), and provides links to sections such as cases, editorial, townhall forum, classified listings, fields of practice listings, bar events, and news and moves. It also contains multiple case summaries organized by practice area (e.g., Administrative Law, Criminal Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Negligence & Intentional Tort, Real Property, Tax, Worker’s Compensation) and many classified/advertising listings, along with contact and subscription/unsubscribe information.

The passage explains that the documents in this edition mainly come from the Department of State and the records of the American Commission to Negotiate Peace, with some additional related documents from other sources for completeness. It notes sources including papers held by the Library of Congress and Yale University, and that the series will be arranged in three groups, with publication generally limited to the period of active U.S. participation in the Paris Conference, ending December 9, 1919. It describes selection principles based on an earlier Foreign Relations series order, plans to print major minutes and proceedings while omitting some secondary material, and credits the Department of State staff and editors involved in compiling and directing the project. The passage then lists sections and topics covered, including treaties negotiated at the Paris Conference of 1919, principal persons and papers, termination of hostilities materials, American plans and preparations, representation of countries at the conference, and U.S. and allied policies and proposals such as a League of Nations.

Cleary’s boxer Lewis Williams will fight at the Magna Science Adventure Centre in Rotherham to claim the Three Nations title, needing two wins to become Elite Three Nations champion at 91kg. Stablemate Morgan Ansell previously claimed the youth 48kg title in Scotland. England coach Amanda Coulson said the boxers are preparing to represent England and gain international experience toward being crowned Elite GB Three Nations champions. If successful, Williams could end the season as Great Britain’s number two, positioning him to challenge Cheavon Clarke for Olympic qualification beginning next year. On Friday June 8, 17-year-old Josh Finch will box Cameron Hatton at Cleary’s Gym home show; tickets are available by calling Ady Bush at 07581 506820.

Weybridge Orthodontics states that Invisalign corrects misaligned teeth in Weybridge using transparent, custom-shaped aligners made from precise 3D images taken at consultation. The aligners are worn in pairs for 7–10 days each, with typical transformation after 12–18 months. Invisalign avoids social awkwardness associated with wire-and-bracket braces, is described as suitable for mild-to-moderate misalignments, and can be removed for meals and brushing without cumbersome attachments. The team offers consultations, may show a simulation of expected results, and claims benefits including improved smile appearance, easier cleaning, improved oral hygiene, and reduced risk of jaw strain.

Researchers have generated muons using small laser-driven particle accelerators, producing muon beams without the need for massive accelerator facilities. Muons can penetrate solid materials and may enable portable scanners to detect materials such as plutonium or uranium in shipping containers. The passage describes laser-accelerated electron beams that strike dense targets to produce muons, with reported muon energies ranging from about one billion to several billion electron volts. It also notes experiments testing applications, including a proof-of-principle demonstration using a muon detector and lead object placed in a truck near a laser-powered muon source.

South32 Ltd abandoned a US$200 million deal to buy Peabody Energy’s Metropolitan coal mine in Australia due to competition concerns about coal supply to local steel makers. South32 said it was unwilling to make anticipated concessions that would compromise the transaction’s merits. The decision reflects steel makers’ concerns that Australia’s coking coal reserves are held by a small group of large miners. Peabody said it was surprised by the impasse and stated it would continue operating the mine, keep its 2 million tonnes a year production and its 16.67% stake in the Port Kembla coal terminal, and resume shipments after a planned change to a new coal panel at the end of May.

President Donald Trump met with Jared Isaacman to discuss another nomination to lead NASA. Trump previously pulled Isaacman’s nomination, calling him a “blue blooded Democrat” who had not contributed to a Republican, and said it was inappropriate for a close friend of Elon Musk to run NASA. Isaacman has close ties to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and is a commander of Polaris Dawn. After the nomination was pulled, Isaacman declined to comment, and wrote about the process in a letter. The passage also says tensions between Musk and Trump have cooled since then.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x (Ampere) architecture and related features. It covers GDDR6X memory (up to 19.5 Gbps on GA10x GPUs, with up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth using PAM4), third-generation NVLink for scaling GPU memory to 96 GB using two GPUs, and PCIe Gen4 performance. It outlines GA102 GPU hardware organization (GPCs, TPCs, SMs, memory controllers, and L2 cache) and ROP optimizations where ROPs are moved into the GPC. The GA10x SM is described as improving FP32 throughput, Tensor Cores (including sparsity support and new data types like TF32 and BF16), and second-generation RT cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing and support ray-traced motion blur and concurrent execution. The text also discusses larger L1/shared memory options, performance/power efficiency claims versus Turing, and hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. It explains DLSS improvements enabled by third-generation Tensor Cores, and RTX IO technologies that enable GPU-based lossless decompression and faster asset loading using DirectStorage. The passage further details NVIDIA A40 data center GPU features (48 GB GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB with NVLink, higher throughput claims, virtualization/EGX compatibility) and adds display and video codec support for GA10x GPUs, including fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decoding (including AV1) and seventh-generation NVENC hardware encoding.

The study investigated whether genes involved in vitamin B12 metabolism and B12 levels are associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, age-at-onset, and progression. Although prior studies linked lower B12 levels with PD and functional studies suggested B12 may inhibit LRRK2 kinase activity and interact with alpha-synuclein, the authors stated that no genetic studies had causally linked B12 metabolism to PD. Using European-ancestry PD genome-wide association data, pathway-specific polygenic risk scores, and rare-variant analyses from whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing cohorts, the study found no robust genetic association between B12-metabolism variants (common or rare) and PD risk. Two pathway PRS analyses showed only signals that did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction, and rare-variant findings did not replicate. Mendelian randomization using GWAS of B12 serum levels as exposure likewise found no potentially causal association between B12 levels and PD risk, age-at-onset, or progression, and genetic correlation analyses showed no correlation between PD outcomes and B12 levels. The discussion emphasizes limitations including restriction to European ancestry and underpowered progression GWAS, concluding that B12 levels or metabolism may not play a prominent genetic role in PD, while non-genetic factors may contribute to B12 differences in PD patients.

The passage discusses how to use stress–strain behavior of foams to construct energy-absorption diagrams and how those diagrams guide material and design choices. It explains converting foam compressive stress–strain curves (for different densities, strain rates, and temperatures) into log–log plots of normalized energy absorbed versus normalized peak stress, identifying a “shoulder point” near the plateau stress as the most efficient/optimum condition. It outlines how to experimentally generate these diagrams by testing foams across relative densities and constant conditions, connecting shoulder points into lines, and repeating for different strain rates (and possibly temperatures). It further describes normalization by the solid modulus, noting that for elastomeric foams this can make diagrams broadly representable across elastomeric materials, while yield-point (plastic) foams produce less general diagrams valid for a specific ratio of yield strength to modulus. The passage also presents modeling approaches for open-cell elastomeric foams and for foams with yield points, deriving equations for the lines connecting shoulder points and discussing limits such as the behavior approaching that of a fully dense solid. Finally, it provides case studies showing how to select foam parameters for impact protection (including a packaged object scenario and a bicycle helmet scenario), and it transitions to a related “woodpecker” talk about how woodpeckers avoid brain injury via high decelerations measured by neurologists, attributing this to scaling factors involving brain size, brain orientation, and impact duration.

The passage introduces interest in lead-free organic ferroelectric (FE) and antiferroelectric (AFE) systems and reports that crystals in the 5-Phenyl-1H-tetrazole (PHTZ) family exhibit FE, AFE, or mixed FE/AFE behavior. Two long-range ordered crystals are discussed: APHTZ, described as canted ferroelectric with FE ordering along the a-axis coexisting with AFE ordering along the b-axis, and MPHTZ, described as a simple uniaxial AFE. The stability of these ordered phases extends at least up to 410 K. The structure common to PHTZs is based on hydrogen-bonded pentagonal tetrazole (CN4) groups forming quasi-one-dimensional chains, with dipoles tied to proton positions via proton tautomerism and switchable π-bonds.  

The authors develop pseudospin models to reproduce structural ordering and polarization-switching behavior for APHTZ and MPHTZ using mean-field approximations with minimal fitting parameters. For APHTZ, the model includes two sublattices and predicts a field-driven switching from a FE-I configuration to a higher-energy FE-II configuration, including a tricritical point where the switching changes from first order to second order. The model produces temperature and field dependences of polarization components and dielectric permittivities, along with predicted switching-field behavior below and above the tricritical point.  

For MPHTZ, a four-sublattice model is reduced to an effective two-sublattice AFE Ising model under symmetry assumptions. The model predicts FE/AFE ordering along the a-axis and describes field-induced switching from the AFE phase to the FE phase with a tricritical point, including the resulting temperature dependence of the switching field and related thermodynamic quantities. The concluding remarks emphasize that while qualitative agreement with available experimental data is obtained, limited experimental data leave uncertainty, and further measurements of polarization, permittivity, and phase-transition characteristics are needed to test and refine the models.

Niantic says that “over 80” new Johto Pokémon from Generation II will be added to Pokémon GO “later this week,” though no more precise date was given. The update will make these Pokémon discoverable “as soon as the update goes live” and all of them will be found “in the wild,” not from eggs. Niantic also confirmed new evolution items (from PokéStops), two new berries (Nanab to slow Pokémon and Pinap to double candy on a successful catch), new avatar items (hats, shirts, and pants), and new encounter gameplay without details. The passage notes trailer features such as a new berry shortcut button and a change to UI layout, but it says there was no mention of improvements to tracking, trading, or player-versus-player battling. It also discusses that some Gen II Pokémon are already in the game, with the remaining additions likely including baby evolutions and Legendary Pokémon. Screenshots suggest changes including berry purchasing, Pokémon genders, and an “Evolve” button that indicates what a Pokémon will evolve into.

Charleston city council will again address carriage horse heat regulations Monday, with a proposed change scheduled for a second reading. Currently, tours can continue when two consecutive readings 15 minutes apart are below 95 degrees. Under the proposed change, tours can resume when the temperature is below 95 degrees or the heat index is below 110 degrees after 30 consecutive minutes from the first reading; if the temperature rises above during the first 30 minutes, the process restarts. The passage also notes other potential changes, including a carriage tour company requiring body cameras for drivers to protect from hecklers and abuse.

The passage discusses German peace plans based on “immediate recuperation” and the organization of the Near East, and notes that the President’s Buffalo speech aims to check these plans. It then describes “Inquiry Document No. 886” and an organized research effort as of December 15, 1917, including an Executive Committee of four, Division Chiefs with assistants and collaborators, and processes for filing, digesting, editing, and cataloging materials under Dr. Mezes and others. The inquiry’s administrative structure is in operation, with collaborators drawn from multiple U.S. institutions, and it outlines research plans and investigations now under way, including collecting official declarations from European newspaper sources and examining press and periodical literature of western powers.

Nutritional High International Inc. announced it secured a 12-month extension for an US$800,000 secured note tied to its Pueblo, Colorado property with Veterans Capital Fund, LLC. The extension keeps monthly interest payments at 13% per annum and adds a one-time 1% renewal fee plus a 1% extension fee; subject to regulatory approval, the expiry of 3,333,334 warrants exercisable at CAD $0.06 will be extended to October 18, 2018, and 1,000,000 new warrants at CAD $0.15 will be issued.

The company also entered into a term sheet for a loan against its La Pine, Oregon property. The Oregon Loan principal will be determined after a formal appraisal and will equal the lesser of 85% of the appraised value or US$400,000. The loan will be secured by a first charge over the Oregon property and carry 13% interest per annum for 18 months. Subject to regulatory approval, up to 1,125,515 warrants may be issued with an exercise price of $0.165, and the lender expects due diligence to be completed in May 2017.

An “Inside UT Football: October 5, 2000” newsletter forwarded by Eric Bass includes a Q&A with Chip Brown from The Dallas Morning News. It discusses Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops’ comments after Texas’s early season, UT quarterback rotation between Major Applewhite and Chris Simms, OU vs. UT keys for the upcoming game, and multiple reader questions covering topics such as special teams and punt penalties/blocks, offensive line development and the use of a gap-running scheme, injuries to players like Sean Rogers, UT’s secondary matchup against OU, expectations and criticism of coach Mack Brown, UT’s scoring streak record, next year’s schedule, and UT’s field/turf condition. The newsletter also notes where and when the Colorado game will be played (2:30 p.m. Central on Oct. 14) and that it will not be televised.

Players discussed their expectations and roles in upcoming games, including hoping for power plays and emphasizing physical play and finishing checks without getting out of position. They said their opponent pressed and was efficient, and that they want to spend more time in the opponent’s end and improve puck possession after not doing so in the first game. The passage also describes a shift in game momentum from timely goals, a laid-back goalie’s attitude and preparation, and praise for a particular line’s energy, forechecking, and offensively productive contributions despite limited ice time. The team expects a loud home crowd next game and says they must play their best, returning to what worked on prior road trips.

After the game, the team was frustrated and upset but planned to come back to work, regroup, and practice. They had a good practice and planned to focus on basic elements in their game, including getting the puck deep and executing their forecheck and simple system. The speaker criticized their neutral-zone play from the previous night and referenced issues from earlier series, saying they didn’t help themselves. They noted that the opponent is good and that knowing what a team will do isn’t enough without execution. The team compared their situation to previous rounds, emphasizing that they must win game-to-game. They also discussed specific goals and mistakes from the prior game, credited the opponent for scoring, and said they all need to pick things up together, including improving speed and neutral-zone play.

During a government shutdown, the federal judiciary plans to use funding such as court fee balances to temporarily continue paid operations. Federal courts expect to pay staff through Oct. 17 using funds not tied to a new congressional appropriation, with most proceedings continuing and deadlines unaffected; hearings and filing dates may be rescheduled if executive-branch attorneys are unavailable. The U.S. Supreme Court plans to rely on funds not subject to annual approval to maintain operations during short-term lapses. Some district courts have issued standing orders pushing back deadlines and delaying civil cases involving the federal government, and some judges are refusing to pause certain civil cases involving matters such as IRS access, DOJ litigation, grant restrictions, layoffs, and Medicaid reimbursement bans. If funds run out, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act, potentially requiring some court staff to work without pay and leading to furloughs; staffing resources would be determined by each court and federal defender’s office for constitutional functions.

The passage describes how NVIDIA Tensor Cores improve deep learning matrix multiplication performance and efficiency. It notes that Tensor Cores were introduced in the Volta GPU architecture, providing an 8x peak speedup for mixed-precision matrix multiplication versus standard FP32 operations. It then compares this with the Ampere architecture-based A100 GPU, which has more SMs and third-generation Tensor Cores that deliver peak mixed-precision compute performance 16x higher than standard FP32 FMA operations. The passage also states that Ampere introduced features and optimizations to enhance Tensor Core utilization, improve programmability, reduce software complexity and memory bandwidth usage, and lower latency and overheads. It further explains that deep neural networks use repeated GEMM-like operations, where output matrices are tiled and mapped across multiple SMs, and that Ampere targets strong scaling by keeping the GEMM tile size per SM fixed even though A100 Tensor Cores consume data faster than V100.

The passage discusses Lehman Brothers’ financial situation at the end of 2007 and explains how leverage and changing housing and interest-rate conditions could rapidly reduce capital. It covers examples of mortgage leverage with 20% versus 5% down payments, the role of mark-to-market and adjustable-rate mortgages, and why increased volatility can lead to large losses. It then shifts to inflation and distinguishes nominal versus real returns, using cost-of-living indexes and guidance for matching nominal or real cash flows with corresponding discount rates. The remainder outlines fixed income securities: their fixed payoffs, major market sizes and categories, market participants (issuers, intermediaries, investors), risks such as inflation and credit risk, and introductory valuation of coupon and pure discount (STRIPS) bonds using present value discounting.

The U.S. Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign aid while Congress considers the administration’s request to rescind the appropriation. The Court said the government made a sufficient showing at this early stage that plaintiffs were not entitled to sue under the law or to mandamus relief, and that alleged harms to foreign affairs outweighed potential harms to plaintiffs, while noting it was not a final merits determination. The case arose from two consolidated lawsuits and was decided on the emergency docket; the Impoundment Control Act gives Congress 45 days to act or the funding would expire. Justice Elena Kagan dissented, joined by Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson.

More than 200 schools in North Wales are closed today due to snow and ice, after temperatures fell to -8C overnight. Councils cited health and safety concerns, and staff and pupils are also unable to travel because roads are covered in snow and black ice. A yellow ice weather warning remains in place until 11am, with the Met Office warning of overnight ice formation and potential injuries from slips and falls. The passage then lists affected closed schools by county: Flintshire (78), Wrexham (48), Denbighshire (47), Conwy (11), and multiple in Gwynedd, plus notes that Ysgol Ardudwy in Harlech will only be open for Year 10–11 and that students in Years 7–9 should stay home due to a staff shortage. It states no current closures are listed on Anglesey’s council website for the day.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 3, 2021, reporting that at its 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders on June 3, 2021: stockholders approved an amendment to increase the authorized common stock from 2 billion to 4 billion; elected all 13 directors for one-year terms; approved, on an advisory basis, the compensation of named executive officers as disclosed in its April 23, 2021 proxy statement; ratified the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 30, 2022; and approved the amendment. The results of each vote are provided. The amendment was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on June 4, 2021 as Exhibit 3.1.

Boston University Summer Term is a premier summer study program in the Northeast, offering high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses across many subjects. Its open-enrollment policy is intended to help students enhance professional credentials, broaden career options, meet degree prerequisites, or focus on a topic. The program provides over 700 courses in 75+ subjects through day, evening, or online options in six-week sessions, and includes Pre-College Programs for motivated high school students. The program is located in Boston and highlights BU’s academic legacy over 100 years. Summer Term registration is available at bu.edu/summer, with sessions running May 23–June 30 (Summer 1) and July 3–August 11 (Summer 2).

President Donald Trump welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron to the White House for a pomp-filled ceremony on the South Lawn, beginning a day of talks on the future of the Iran nuclear deal and the crisis in Syria. Trump praised the alliance between the two nations and thanked Macron for his partnership during a recent Syria missile strike. Macron said the U.S. and France would defeat terrorism, curtail weapons of mass destruction in North Korea and Iran, and act for the planet, and he emphasized a shared “appointment with history.” The three-day state visit includes helicopter and Mount Vernon activities, private and public engagements, and a traditional arrival ceremony with a 21-gun salute, with Tuesday capped by a state dinner for about 150 guests featuring planned menu details and Washington National Opera entertainment. The passage also notes Trump and Macron’s disagreement over the Iran nuclear deal, as well as Macron’s prior ties to Trump and Melania Trump’s role in arranging the dinner and decor.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2015. The filing includes regulatory certifications, an index of financial statement items, and forward-looking statements. Financial highlights shown include condensed consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive loss, and cash flows for the three months ended March 31, 2015 and 2014, along with detailed notes on revenue recognition, resale value guarantees, leasing programs, warranties, stock-based compensation, legal proceedings, and fair value of financial instruments. The notes also describe significant accounting policies and risk factors, including foreign currency risk, interest rate risk, and potential delays in launching and ramping Model X and future vehicles.

The passage is a collection of news items and commentary about Enron’s collapse and related investigations in January 2002. It reports that Enron executives offered wealthy investors insider information about partnership LJM2, that Enron’s board and creditors were seeking a restructuring leader after Ken Lay’s resignation, and that former employees alleged Enron’s Energy Services division inflated profits. Multiple articles discuss Congress’s interest in 401(k) rules after employees’ retirement savings were heavily invested in Enron stock, and they describe the Enron-Andersen scandal, including document shredding and a chronology of events involving Arthur Andersen and Enron executives. Additional coverage includes the potential liquidation of Enron Australia, the emergence of book deals based on the Enron story, and how charities planned to continue without expected Enron donations.

The passage describes initializing the ADS9803 ADC with a register-write sequence after power-up or reset, noting that a free-running sampling clock must be connected before initialization and that register defaults are set once initialization completes. It then outlines how to change default settings for user-defined configuration, including analog input range/bandwidth/common-mode range and data interface options that affect output lanes. The passage also explains speed-boost mode, which can enable up to an 8 MSPS sampling rate for a user-selected channel pair while leaving other channels idle, and references register operations for enabling/disabling this mode. Further, it details SPI register access methods, including how to write and read registers using SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE, and how to configure and use daisy-chain operation for multiple ADCs, including required SPI clock counts and register read/write steps in a daisy-chain topology.

The passage describes the OpenChart-SE citizen science project, created to overcome difficulties accessing Swedish electronic health record (EHR) text for clinical natural language processing research. Because publicly available Swedish EHR-derived text corpora are not available, the project uses artificial EHRs written by Swedish physicians and medical students for imagined patients plausibly encountered in Swedish emergency departments. A Swedish mock EHR form was used for data entry, with fields based on emergency department EHRs in the region of Scania. In the pilot phase (November 2021–December 2022), 50 artificial EHRs were collected, reviewed by an emergency medicine resident physician for realistic writing style and content, and released as the OpenChart-SE corpus (version 1) in Zenodo. Data exploration used Jupyter Lab, Python, pandas, and matplotlib, with manual review and harmonization of synonymous main diagnoses. The 50 EHRs ranged from 954 to 2738 characters, included varied adult patient ages, and encompassed a range of emergency scenarios. The authors state the dataset is artificial and released for training and validation of clinical NLP tools, not for deriving clinical insights.

Particle has released an LTE-enabled module for product developers, targeting devices that relied on retiring 2G and 3G networks. The module includes built-in cloud and SIM support and is positioned as more suitable than 4G/5G for many networked devices due to lower cost, better battery life, and longer range for industrial uses. Particle says demand is expected in hard-to-reach or widely dispersed sensor networks and notes that carriers are ending 2G/3G while planning LTE rollouts. The LTE module is part of Particle’s suite, including a device cloud, operating system, and developer toolkit, and is described as a faster, pre-integrated path to market. Particle’s lineup includes two LTE CAT-M1 models and is fully certified and designed for industrial environments, using Qualcomm’s MDM9206 IoT Modem and u-blox’s Sara-R410-02B module. An LTE hardware evaluation kit costs $89, and individual modules cost $69. Particle reports 8,500 customers and more than 140,000 developers, including Engie, Ideo, Grow Labs, and Keurig.

3D imaging is used in biomedical sciences to visualize complex biological structures, but traditional 2D microscopy can lack spatial context. Advances in 3D microscopy methods like confocal, multiphoton, and light-sheet fluorescence provide structural and functional information, though scanning approaches trade off imaging speed against signal-to-noise ratio and can increase photodamage. Light-field imaging addresses this by capturing a complete 3D scene in a single snapshot without scanning, recording not only intensity but the spatial distribution and direction of light rays to enable computational refocusing, synthetic aperture imaging, and high-speed volumetric imaging. The passage outlines theoretical foundations (plenoptic function) and ray and wave optics modeling, describes multiple light-field rendering modes, and focuses on biomedical implementations including light-field microscopy, light-field mesoscopy, and light-field endoscopy. It also discusses speed and data-size limits, approaches to compress light-field data (e.g., event cameras and squeezed light-field microscopy), and tradeoffs among field of view, depth of field, and resolution. The review further covers meta-optics and AI-powered reconstruction methods, including fully deep learning and hybrid approaches, along with remaining challenges such as generalization, artifacts, and model reliability.

In the Panthers’ loss to the Buccaneers, kicker Graham Gano missed three of four field goal attempts and complained that the Buccaneers used the stadium video board behind the goal posts to display live footage of his kicks. He said the board’s red background during Roberto Aguayo’s kick was not coincidental and referenced prior league discussions. A league official confirmed that using a video board to distract an opposing kicker is against the rules. Officials also stopped play due to loud feedback through the stadium PA system, and Gano missed another field goal after play resumed. Panthers coach Ron Rivera criticized the video board operator after replay slow-motion footage of a play involving Thomas Davis and Russell Shepard was shown, which drew boos from fans. The article notes the Panthers went for two late in the fourth quarter instead of tying the game.

The speaker says he wants to be creative with the puck as a forward while keeping his game simple and making room for two key teammates, Mike and Jere. He will skate, move the puck, and work hard, taking a more defensive role when opportunities arise. He notes the opposing team brings a lot of energy, physicalness, and power, and that both clubs are expected to bring their best in a key game. He also mentions shot-blocking efforts by his team, the closeness and depth of the organization, and that players are ready to step in when opportunities occur. Although they are up, he says they must win the next periods and focus one period at a time, with six periods remaining to win.

The passage argues that teacher education should be reformed to prepare educators for 21st-century classrooms amid technological, demographic, and social changes. It highlights key research areas including integrating technology using the TPACK framework, fostering critical thinking through inquiry-based and constructivist methods, preparing teachers for diverse learners via inclusive and culturally responsive practices, promoting collaboration and lifelong learning through professional learning communities and ongoing professional development, and adapting to global challenges by incorporating global education and critical discussion of issues like climate change and social justice. It presents TPACK and constructivism as guiding theoretical frameworks and concludes that optimizing teacher education requires a holistic, continuous process responsive to evolving trends and research.

On March 11, 2015, Michael McCaffery and Persis Drell were appointed to NVIDIA Corporation’s Board of Directors, and McCaffery was appointed to the Audit Committee. In connection with their appointments, both received equity grants under NVIDIA’s 2007 Amended and Restated Equity Incentive Plan and pro-rated annual cash retainers of $15,625 payable on March 11, 2015. NVIDIA also entered into indemnity agreements with both directors.

Sana Bhat, a Kashmiri hotel management student in Haryana, was diagnosed with leukemia in April 2015; after her family sold their land in Srinagar to fund treatment, she died in February. Her story led to a Facebook appeal that went viral and raised about $40,000 in a month. In February, businessmen launched a crowdfunding campaign called #TwentyRupeesMiracle asking for 20 rupees per month for the Lalla Ded Charity, which aimed to reach 100,000 donors; within days, more than 50,000 donors signed up worldwide.

The passage describes rising cancer cases in Kashmir and the financial burden of treatment, noting that SKIMS is a key low-cost option and that many patients cannot afford care. It also says the charity transfers funds to recognized groups and can provide support; it cites an example of Towseef Ahmad Bhat, whose medicines were funded after an online appeal, and who improved with treatment. The family of Sana says her life cannot be saved, but the charity could help save others.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 15, 2021. In Item 8.01 (Other Events), it states that effective March 15, 2021, Elon Musk’s and Zach Kirkhorn’s titles changed to Technoking of Tesla and Master of Coin, respectively, while they will continue as Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer. The report was signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on March 15, 2021.

The passage describes seasonal trading strategies for the Italian stock market, which the author says has struggled to create value and is trading at a level similar to 1998. It explains that the market index IT 40 tracks 40 large, actively traded companies on the Borsa Italiana, listing examples including Monclear, Pirelli, Tenaris, Ferrari, and Campari. Backtests using the dividend-adjusted ETF EWI are presented: Italian stocks perform best on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, Thursdays are slightly positive, Fridays are flat, and Mondays are very poor. An end-of-the-month strategy using the same rules for EWI and Italian stocks is reported to perform better than buy-and-hold, with CAGR of 6.17% versus 4.71%, while investing about one-third of the time. The passage also reports that March and June are the best months, with May the worst.

The passage announces the new Fiat 500 “Spiaggina ‘58,” a limited special series of 1,958 convertible cars released to mark the birthday of the Fiat 500 and the 60th anniversary of the 500 Jolly Spiaggina. Fiat produced a tribute video to “Volare,” while Garage Italia and Pininfarina created a “Spiaggina by Garage Italia” showcar based on the 500C, featuring distinct styling and structural modifications. The passage also describes key design, color, and connectivity features of the “Spiaggina ‘58,” its 1.2-litre 69hp petrol engine compliant with Euro6D, and provides background on the original 1958–1965 Fiat 500 Jolly, including its design and production history. It concludes by placing the “Spiaggina ‘58” within the broader history of Fiat 500 special editions and notes the model’s sales and market leadership.

Tom Lee, chair of BitMine, says the “bubble has burst” in digital asset treasury companies (DATs), which acquire cryptocurrencies and seek publicly traded vehicles for exposure. He warned that DAT projects are ballooning and could be the next crash. Lee, who became a crypto executive after previously working at JPMorgan and founding Fundstrat, said BitMine holds over 3 million Ethereum tokens and aims for 5%, citing staking rewards and inclusion on stock indexes. He described BitMine as a link between Wall Street and Ethereum upgrades, while questioning whether DATs are already in a bubble.

The passage describes: (1) an arrangement for officers to communicate confidentially to the Department of State any charges they prefer against other officers, with the Department deciding disposition in the public interest; (2) a message from John Hay dated May 20, 1902, stating that the U.S. military occupation of Cuba has ceased and an independent republican government led by Tomás Estrada Palma has been inaugurated; (3) instructions from John Hay dated May 24, 1902, to request Argentina to allow U.S. consular officers to represent Cuban interests until Cuban consuls are appointed; and (4) circular and related instructions dated October 22, 1902, amending passport rules so that loyal residents of U.S. insular possessions may be issued passports, including required application wording, fees, and documentation.

The passage describes features and supporting information for MSPM0 G-Series microcontrollers, including the Keystore for secure AES key management (up to 4 keys, support for 128- and 256-bit keys, and protection against partial key modification attacks). It also covers CRC-P (16-bit CRC16-CCITT and 32-bit CRC32-ISO3309), MATHACL (hardware-accelerated 32-bit math functions), UART (UART0-UART1, UART3-UART7 with parity, baud generation, FIFOs for DMA data transfer, loopback, and protocol support), I2C (7- and 10-bit addressing, controller/transmitter/receiver modes, clock stretching, multiple speed modes up to 1 Mbit/s, SMBus 3.0, FIFOs with DMA, wakeup on address match, and glitch filtering), SPI (controller/peripheral configuration with up to 32 Mbits/s, programmable prescaler/bit rate/frame sizes, DMA-capable FIFOs, PACKEN, and TI/Motorola/National Microwire formats), CAN-FD (ISO 11898-1:2015 compliance up to 5 Mbit/s with FIFOs/buffers), and the LFSS sub-system (LFCLK-based peripherals including LFSS_B with RTC_B and an asynchronous IWDT_B). It further describes RTC_B timekeeping options and calibration, watchdog timers (IWDT_B and WWDT), timer peripherals (TIMGx and TIMAx with various counting, PWM, capture/compare, fault handling, synchronization, and trigger features), and additional documentation/support, software tooling, factory constants (DEVICEID/USERID in a FACTORY region), device nomenclature, SWD, and the boot strap loader (BSL) supported via UART or I2C with protection via a 256-bit user-defined password and ways to invoke BSL.

The GST Council set a 0.1% tax rate on goods procured for export and allowed merchant exporters to claim refunds of 0.1% tax paid on exports. The measures aim to prevent cash blockage from upfront GST payments by extending advance authorization (AA), EPCG, and 100% EOU schemes to allow input sourcing from abroad and domestically, exempting AA/EPCG/EOU holders from paying IGST and cess on imports, and treating domestic supplies as deemed exports with refunds to suppliers. The Council also allowed specified banks and public sector units to import gold without IGST for supply to exporters under a scheme similar to AA. FIEO welcomed the move, and said it had proposed an e-wallet facility to provide liquidity from April 1, with DGFT preparing norms.

The speaker says the team played well tonight, especially in the defensive zone and in front of the net, battling through scrambles and limiting rebounds. They acknowledge that some pucks got through and they personally had moments involving rebounds but tried to adjust by positioning to take away the bottom of the net. The speaker also comments on winning elimination games, noting that while goaltenders differ, they admire the playoff goaltender’s competition and how he elevated his game, which they aim to emulate.

AggregateIQ, a Canadian firm linked to allegations over personal data use in online campaigning and possible Brexit spending rule violations, disputed claims of ties to Cambridge Analytica and SCL. Two AggregateIQ executives, Zack Massingham and Jeff Silvester, told a Canadian House committee they were not affiliated with Cambridge Analytica and that they had never accessed or improperly used Facebook data. Silvester and Massingham said AggregateIQ places online ads and builds software for political campaigns, and Silvester denied illegally obtaining data and disputed an allegation about distributing a violent video in Nigeria. Canadian MPs also questioned how AggregateIQ worked with groups campaigning for Britain to leave the EU in 2016. Silvester said AggregateIQ worked with Vote Leave, BeLeave, Veterans for Britain, and the Democratic Unionist Party, including cases where Vote Leave reportedly paid for work performed for other organizations. He said the ad targeting information came from each campaign, that there was no evidence of coordination between Vote Leave and BeLeave, and that AggregateIQ checked an arrangement where Vote Leave was to cover an invoice to BeLeave, after which it was assured the transaction was legal.

The City of Bisbee petitioned for a writ of mandamus against Cochise County, its treasurer Daniel S. Kitchel, and the county board of supervisors, alleging that since 1918 the county treasurer collected city taxes and related interest, penalties, and fees but failed to remit $2,730.86 in penalties and fees, and later refused to remit additional interest. The superior court sustained general and special demurrers, dismissed the action, and Bisbee appealed.

The court held that mandamus could compel the treasurer to pay over funds held in trust for the city, but the demurrer was properly sustained as to Cochise County and the supervisors because the funds, as alleged, were not legally county funds under their jurisdiction. The court also rejected the argument that the treasurer’s non-continuous service period was material.

Addressing whether the collected amounts belonged to the city or the county, the court concluded the additional delinquent “fees”/“costs” collected by the treasurer were city funds held in trust and that Bisbee was entitled to an accounting for amounts collected up to June 13, 1931. It further held that the statute of limitations had not run because the action was filed within a year after the treasurer notified the city he would not pay the collected amounts.

For moneys collected after June 12, 1931, the court held Bisbee was not entitled to an accounting because a 1931 statute required interest, penalties, charges, and fees collected on delinquent taxes to be credited to the county’s general fund.

The judgment was reversed and the case remanded with instructions to overrule the demurrer as to Kitchel and proceed consistent with the opinion.

World stocks rose to near all-time highs, and the dollar rose for the 11th straight day after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen suggested a possible interest rate rise next month. MSCI’s global equity index and several European and Asian benchmarks climbed, with bank stocks leading after Yellen’s remarks. The dollar index logged its longest winning streak since May 2015, while the euro fell to a one-month low and sterling slid after weaker UK wage growth. Treasury yields rose, boosting the dollar but weighing on crude oil prices; U.S. crude and Brent fell, and gold declined slightly.

The passage discusses HSC 2018 success stories in Maharashtra, focusing on students who faced challenges. It highlights differently-abled students at NGO Niwant Andh Mukta Vidyasalaya, including Kshirsagar Kedar Kailas, who topped with 80.15% and plans to appear for the IAS exam. It also covers Vanshika Joshi (70.77%), who was born with a deformity in her left leg and had to manage pain during exams, and whose goal is to become a banker. The passage notes strong results from night school students, with 104 of 120 passing, including top performers Hirve Ashwini (70.6%), Akash Dhindle (79.23%) who works a 10-hour job, and Vitthal Bashweshwar Ishwarkatti (75%) who returned to studies after an 11-year break and plans to pursue commerce.

The passage describes how to use and manage a Sansa Fuze media player, including the Hold Switch to prevent accidental operation, power on/off and reset functions, navigation with a thumbwheel, battery charging and charging restrictions while connected to a computer, connecting/disconnecting to a computer, updating firmware, formatting (which deletes content), and transferring music, playlists, photos, and videos using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, and Sansa Media Converter. It also covers playing music, audiobooks, video features, photo browsing and slideshows, FM radio setup and presets, voice recording with the built-in microphone, deleting content, customizing settings (wallpaper, display art, backlight, power saver, language, date/time, brightness, USB mode, and press-and-hold behavior), and tips/troubleshooting (supported formats, bit rates, troubleshooting playback and metadata, firmware updates, and microSD support). The passage concludes with information on service and support, warranty terms, and an end user license agreement for software.

The passage states that the Software is provided with “RESTRICTED RIGHTS,” with government use subject to specified FAR and DFARS restrictions and acknowledgement of SanDisk’s proprietary rights. It allows termination of the agreement and license if violated, requiring deletion or destruction of all software copies. It warns the Software is not designed for hazardous or fail-safe use, disclaiming warranties and liability for high-risk activities. It also covers general terms: entire understanding, severability, California and U.S. federal law governance, non-application of the CISG, exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County courts, U.S. export compliance, and that specified sections survive termination. Disposal instructions advise against disposing the device with unsorted household waste and to consult local waste authority information.

The passage describes defensive schemes against the Side Screen offense, which uses a “Big” screening for a “Small.” It notes that many NBA teams avoid switching because it can allow the dribbler to create penetration and let the screener post up; “Show & Recover” is presented as the preferred method, with variations by team and player. It outlines “Show” and “Recover” phases, including how defenders step out to force the ballhandler wide, then re-establish positions and close out on pass outs. It also presents “SOS” disruptions with three scenarios: above the free throw line (aggressive contact switch, snuggle pass denial, and smother/fronting positions), below the free throw line (baseline trap and triangle I, then closing out), and an “All-Out SOS Disruption” that seeks to disrupt the offense before the first screen by trapping the point guard. Additional “secondary trap” rules are provided for when the point guard passes to the screener on a base roll, including how defenders trap, close out, and rotate depending on the ballhandler’s actions.

NASA/ESA Hubble captured an image of NGC 2775, a galaxy about 67 million light-years away in the constellation Cancer. Its appearance is difficult to classify: it has an elliptical-like, gas-free center and a dusty ring with patchy star clusters that resembles a spiral. Some researchers classify it as spiral or lenticular (a type with features of both spiral and elliptical galaxies). The passage notes evidence of a past merger, including a faint tail of hydrogen gas extending almost 100,000 light-years around the galaxy. A previous 2020 Hubble image is updated with additional observations of red light from hydrogen clouds around young massive stars.

A line formed before 9 a.m. for the Crossroads of the West Gun Show at the Del Mar Fairgrounds despite heavy rain, while another group protested outside. The protesters wore bright orange shirts and carried signs denouncing the show and gun violence, including names of people killed in the Parkland, Fla. school shooting, reflecting national division over guns. Protest organizer Rose Ann Sharp said student activists are pushing adults to do more and question morality. During a two-hour demonstration, protesters received honks of support; about 80 gathered. Gun show owner Bob Templeton expected 8,000 to 10,000 attendees, citing the debate after Parkland. He said California gun show purchases require a background check and a 10-day waiting period, and he was not bothered by the protest. Inside the show, thousands browsed vendors selling firearms and related items, along with other goods; the show ended Sunday at 5 p.m.

The passage describes skinimalism as a streamlined skincare approach focused on a few well-chosen, high-quality products rather than multi-step routines. Dr Hazel Parkinson says it emphasizes products that serve skin needs, supports the skin barrier, and avoids overwhelming it with competing or harsh actives. She notes potential benefits including less irritation and sensitivity, reduced waste and packaging, and feeling less overwhelmed by skincare marketing. While she says most people can benefit from a barrier-friendly routine, she advises that those with acne, pigmentation, sensitive or flare-prone skin, hyperpigmentation, rosacea, or menopause may still need targeted ingredients, but without unnecessary extra steps. For people starting out, she recommends tailoring actives and hydration to skin type, easing into changes gradually, and seeking professional guidance if unsure.

A July 14, 2011 report by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Services describes a fossil discovery at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge in Montana, where bone fragments in shale included several plesiosaur vertebrae. Co-author Danielle Serratos said the smaller sea creature lived in the same time and area as larger ones, contradicting the belief that elasmosaurs did not evolve longer necks over millions of years. Elasmosaurs are described as carnivorous with small heads and paddle-like limbs that could grow up to 30 feet, and the northeastern Montana fossil was well-preserved and nearly complete. Ranch manager David Bradt found the bones in November 2010 while hunting after mistaking them for petrified wood, photographed the find, and reported it to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Museum of the Rockies. The fossil took three days to excavate and much longer to clean and study before being determined a new species. Druckenmiller said few marine reptile fossils have been excavated due to greater interest in land-dwelling dinosaurs.

Oral communication among soccer players during a game is described as critical across all phases, with short, quickly recognizable “calls” used for fast and accurate information. The passage explains that players without the ball often speak because they have the best view, especially those behind the ball, and that coaches must teach calls in age-appropriate intervals alongside skills and tactics. Calls are categorized by ability level (introductory to advanced) and by roles, including “Defensive Organizer” and goalkeepers, with some calls having the same meaning and with gender-neutral understanding (“he” implies “he” and “she”). The remainder of the passage provides a long list of specific calls and their associated definitions for various in-game situations, including attacking, defending, set pieces, goalkeeper directives, and coaching notes on building a team vocabulary and using “decoy calling” and “fake name” procedures for offsides.

The Centre told the Supreme Court it is ready to extend pension benefits, including revision, to all Major Generals and equivalent ranks in the Army, Navy and Air Force, even if they retired before 2006. A bench led by Chief Justice Dipak Misra directed the Centre to comply within three months, noting the decision means nothing remains in the petition. The case followed a contempt plea filed by retired Major General S P S Vains and others seeking implementation of the One Rank One Pension scheme, alleging the government delayed OROP despite prior reports and a Supreme Court decision.

SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in China in late 2019 and became a pandemic, infecting over 250 million people and causing over 5 million deaths by the time of writing. The virus has a positive-sense single-stranded RNA genome of about 30,000 nucleotides that can accumulate mutations and has been detected in multiple animal species, highlighting the risk of zoonotic outbreaks. Because targeted tests (e.g., antigen/antibody detection and RT-qPCR) can be affected by mutations and symptoms can be similar across pathogens, the passage describes metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) as a hypothesis-free approach that sequences all nucleic acids in a sample, though it can be limited by a low proportion of viral genomes relative to host material. To address this, the study evaluates pretreatment strategies—DNase treatment, filtration, both, or no pretreatment—before nanopore untargeted sequencing for real-time diagnostics. Using clinical SARS-CoV-2 Delta-variant samples, combining DNase I followed by 0.22 µM filtration increased SARS-CoV-2 BLAST hit percentages to 99.9% and improved reference genome coverage and read accumulation speed compared with no treatment or either pretreatment alone. In individual samples, high coverage was achieved more consistently when CT-values were below 30, and SARS-CoV-2 clade and often lineage could be obtained. The protocol aims to be simplified for field deployment, and the conclusions state that a 15-minute DNase I followed by filtration with nanopore sequencing improved detection probability and enabled genome-wide BLAST identification and often clade/lineage assignment for samples with CT-values below 33.

Consumer Reports testing found that more than two-thirds of 23 popular protein powders and ready-to-drink shakes sold in the U.S. contained lead levels in a single serving higher than the amount its food safety experts say is safe per day, with some products containing up to 10 times that amount. CR advised against daily use for most protein powders due to high heavy metal levels and said many are unnecessary to meet protein goals. The report said contamination had increased compared with CR’s earlier testing, and that plant-based powders were the most contaminated, with higher average lead than dairy-based powders. It also described weak federal oversight for supplements, including no federal lead limit for protein powders and limited FDA inspections, while noting that some certifications allow higher daily lead levels than CR’s limit.

The passage argues that financial institution advisors face pressure similar to sales-focused tellers, with allegations against Big Five bank employees and examples of layoffs tied to revenue thresholds. It says institutions claim to put clients first but must demonstrate it through reforms: shifting incentives toward client satisfaction, allowing advisors to do nothing when appropriate and compensating them for advising against products, and requiring a minimum education level to reduce low barriers to entry and improve the profession’s reputation.

The passage is an email titled “IEP News 7/18” dated July 18, 2001, sent by Jean Munoz to many recipients. It compiles multiple news items from late July 18, 2001, about California’s energy situation, including: NPR’s report that California streamlined permitting for new power plants but likely will not reach the governor’s target supply by July 1; a report that Pacific Gas & Electric sued California over reimbursement for seized energy contracts; coverage of PG&E’s “20/20” rebate program results; reports on Duke Energy’s higher profits amid concerns over California power pricing; commentary on political strategy during the energy crisis; and legislative efforts to prevent Edison bankruptcy through competing bailout proposals, with debate over who would pay and the cost to ratepayers.

The speaker says the team has not yet met, but will address the group and discuss respect. They report that an incident discussed with Danny after the game involved burned wood only, with no serious injuries, and that insurance will handle repairs or Danny will pay if needed. The speaker argues that two teams playing last night deserved to be there, noting Calgary played like they reached their position while their own team did not. They say today is recognition day, though they believe they are a day late. They discuss Marty’s performance, saying he made key plays and that it is a matter of time before he scores consistently again. On the idea of a “must win” game, the speaker rejects that framing and says every game is one they aim to win, with Calgary looking to take two games. They state they watched tape, saw limited secrets, and believe Calgary’s ability to decide when to attack affected the game.
