They say their main problem was their mindset and tenaciousness, not X’s and O’s, and that switching mindset is the major adjustment for tomorrow. They emphasize not panicking after losses, responding to what happened, maintaining even keel, and preparing for the next game, with leadership and young players helping. They express confidence that Nikolai Khabibulin will respond well and lead in the next game.

Intermediate attacking runs in soccer build on individual attacking runs by adding awareness of runs that create opportunities for both the initial runner and teammates. Basic elements include recognizing and reacting to an opportunity, choosing an appropriate run, breaking away into open space, timing the run, receiving an optimal pass, and functional oral communication. The passage lists intermediate individual runs (back-door, drifting, doubling back, holding the run, recycled run, and setting up a defender) and describes how a run by one player can trigger another player’s run to space, with examples of decoy runs, drawing opponents away, drop/leaving the ball, and dummy runs. It also explains switches with teammates as exchanges of positions, including called vs. natural switches and types such as basic (horizontal) switch, vertical switch, and cross-over exchange, noting that switches may be acknowledged with oral communication like “switch back.”

The passage discusses a team’s success in a game, praising a player’s performance and “timely goals,” including an “unbelievable play” and strong third-period play led by speed. It also highlights “unbelievable saves” by Pekka, an empty-net goal, and playing a solid third period to close out the win. The speaker says the win was a birthday gift but that the team must get back to work, emphasizing that continued improvement as a team is needed in the series.

U.S. workers’ wages and benefits rose 2.6% last year, the fastest 12-month pace since spring 2015, according to the Labor Department. The growth slowed at the end of last year, with wages and benefits up 0.6% in the fourth quarter versus 0.7% in the third quarter. The 12-month gain improved from 2.2% for the year ending December 2016. President Donald Trump cited the wage increase in his State of the Union address, but private economists said wages should be rising faster given unemployment’s 17-year low of 4.1%. The employment cost index showed wages and salaries up 2.5% for the 12 months ending in December and benefits up 2.5%. Hourly pay rose 2.5% in 2017, down from 2.9% in 2016, and the employment cost index last rose faster than 2.6% over 12 months in September 2008.

The passage describes a 2023 list of “top 10 AI tools” aimed at driving innovation and efficiency by automating repetitive tasks, improving workflows, and increasing productivity. It names tools including ChatGPT and Grammarly for natural language processing, DALL-E and Lumen5 for image and video generation, and other tools (OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI, Surfer SEO) for specific tasks. Brief descriptions explain each tool’s purpose and note limitations such as variable quality, the need to review outputs, and that suggestions or results may be inaccurate or not optimal. The passage also emphasizes researching and evaluating tools to find the best fit for specific needs.

A semi-annual Institute of Supply Management survey says US manufacturing and services firms expect stronger growth and rising revenue into 2018 after 11 months of continuous expansion. Manufacturing revenues are projected to rise 7.8% next year, with 70% of firms expecting higher earnings; services firms project an average business increase of 6%, with 59% expecting improvement. More than 60% of firms in both sectors report difficulty finding workers, leading 44% of manufacturers and 37% of services firms to raise wages. Employment is expected to grow by 1.2% in manufacturing and 1.5% in services, while labor and benefit costs are projected to rise by 2.1% and 2.6%, respectively. Capital expenditures are expected to increase by 2.7% in manufacturing and 3.8% in non-manufacturing, alongside small increases in material costs.

The passage criticizes Jerry Coyne’s post on “Fake Physics” multiverse evidence, saying it relies mainly on a YouTube video claiming multiverse evidence from NASA and ESA satellite data. It argues that the YouTube-based inflation/multiverse reasoning is inadequate for the multiverse with widely different physical laws needed to counter theological fine-tuning. The author states they support Coyne’s side on evolution versus religion but warns scientists to use accurate science to avoid discrediting themselves, and advises against using Facebook or YouTube sources that support one’s argument. The passage also mentions a Nobel Week Dialogue on truth and the scientific method, where David Gross emphasized rigorous experimental testability and expressed confidence in science’s survival, and notes the author’s concern after attending a disturbing related event.

The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three U.S. companies to produce mifepristone. The approval followed the original approval 25 years ago and the first generic approval in 2019, and it prompted pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians. The article says the additional generic approval is unlikely to affect access because mifepristone is typically taken with misoprostol, a combination accounting for about two-thirds of U.S. abortions. The passage also reports that Amgen said its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, which Amgen says met its two primary goals; full results were not provided.

The passage is part of Apple Inc.’s Form 10‑K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2017, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It includes issuer information, securities registered, incorporation details, and incorporation by reference for portions of the 2018 Proxy Statement. It outlines forward-looking statement disclosures and definitions of “Company” and “Apple,” describes Apple’s business activities, products, services, operating systems, distribution channels, business organization by geographic reportable segments, competition, supply of components, research and development, intellectual property, seasonality and product introductions, warranty, backlog, and employee count. It also covers risk factors related to economic conditions, competition, product and supply risks, legal proceedings, regulatory and data security issues, key personnel, disasters and disruptions, financial market risks, credit and tax risks, and includes sections on properties, legal proceedings, and mine safety (not applicable).

The team said the league made a call on a kicking motion and they could not comment further without reviewing replays. They said they were outworked by the Ottawa Senators and did not play near their capabilities, citing frustration, responsibility for penalties, and issues with discipline, compete level, and movement. They said all players were available to play, including Chris Kunitz, though his status would be decided by coaches. The group credited the Senators’ players for stepping up and said they needed to regroup and adjust for the Stanley Cup Final, aiming to play their best game. They also discussed evaluating an injured player based on doctor clearance and conditioning, noting the demanding arena atmosphere and need to decide if he provides the best option. They described additional players’ defensive and checking roles and strengths.

Gatwick Airport recorded its busiest July on record, with 4.7 million passengers, up 2.4% year-on-year for a 53rd consecutive month. Airports Council International Europe recognized Gatwick as a top five airport in Europe for passenger growth, citing +9.4% in the first half of 2017. The increase was linked to rising long-haul traffic, with long-haul passenger numbers up 10.7% versus July 2016 and cargo up 20.4% year-on-year. California routes are among the fastest-growing, with Oakland up 210.6% and Los Angeles up 47.5% versus 2016. Norwegian plans to add direct flights to Denver and Seattle from September and new routes to Austin, Chicago, and Buenos Aires early next year. Gatwick also saw a 6.1% year-on-year increase in passengers traveling to China in July, and further Asia connectivity is planned with flights to Taipei and Singapore launching later this year.

The warden of Rhode Island’s Wyatt Detention Center says inmate James Walker Morales escaped Saturday by climbing a basketball hoop, cutting through a fence, going onto the facility roof, and shimmying down. Correctional officers discovered he was missing three and a half hours after a 10:30 p.m. count, while video shows he escaped at 7 p.m. The prison is on lockdown as staff evaluate security procedures, including detection systems and staffing; two correctional officers were placed on administrative leave. Authorities continued searching for Morales, who is accused of stealing firearms from an Army Reserve armory in 2015. State police say he fled north into Attleboro, where a K-9 followed a partial trail to an I-95 overpass and troopers found bloody clothing; police think he may have gotten into a car. They believe Morales stole a green Chevrolet Lumina from BK Mart and later recovered the car. Officials say he is 6 feet tall, about 175 pounds, with brown skin, black hair, and an eagle tattoo; he is believed to have been hurt by razor wire. Anyone with information is urged to call 911.

A study by Ombudsman Services found that one in five rail passengers in Britain feel resigned to poor service, with long-term issues causing high levels of disillusionment. Rail service complaints rose by 31% to two million last year based on a survey of 2,477 people, with the most common complaints involving punctuality, poor customer service, and overcrowding. The article also cites regulator Office of Rail and Road figures showing the passenger complaint rate per 100,000 journeys was 13% higher between July and September than in 2015, with possible data effects from methodology changes. Campaigners criticized the situation and said regulators must ensure real action after complaints. Passengers are advised to contact train operators first, then Transport Focus or London TravelWatch if dissatisfied. It notes a bill introduced by MP Tim Loughton to establish a rail ombudsman, while the Department for Transport said over £40 billion is being invested and that penalties apply when standards aren’t met. Rail Delivery Group said punctuality has been affected by congestion, industrial disputes, and major upgrade work, and stated that complaints are generally trending down but improvements are needed. The same study reported 55 million complaints to all businesses last year (up 6%), and said consumers often believe complaining is a waste of time.

Rockefeller scientists led by Shai Shaham studied how cells die and how their remains are cleared. In *C. elegans*, they examined the tail-spike cell, which supports tail formation and then dies, and found a compartmentalized death process unlike other cell-death processes: the cell’s core is separated from its long extension, the cell rounds up and disintegrates, and the extension is removed in two steps, with the proximal part broken into bead-like bits and the distal part retracting into a ball that is eliminated by a neighboring cell. They also observed the same process in a neuron. Shaham’s team found that the protein EFF-1 helps phagocytes seal their arm-like extensions around dead cell remnants to quickly engulf them, addressing a prior mystery about how this sealing occurs.

U.S. hedge fund managers were active in the FAANG tech stocks in the second quarter. Third Point increased its stakes in Alphabet and Facebook, while Omega Advisors trimmed stakes in Facebook, Netflix, and Amazon and kept its Alphabet stake unchanged. Jana Partners, which held no FAANG stocks at the end of the quarter, increased its stake in Whole Foods Market by 9 million shares to 23.3 million and later cashed out after Whole Foods agreed to be acquired by Amazon. The passage also notes that Third Point’s Facebook move and both funds’ Alphabet decisions appeared profitable alongside recent stock surges.

The passage says that a government shutdown could furlough about 750,000 federal workers, according to the CBO. It reports that the shutdown was likely to occur at midnight after Republicans and Democrats refused to move on a funding deal. The CBO estimated the daily cost of workers’ compensation would be about $400 million, with the number furloughed possibly varying by how long the shutdown lasts. House Speaker Mike Johnson criticized Democrats for opposing a stopgap funding bill, while Hakeem Jeffries said that if the government shuts down, it is a Republican decision. The dispute centers on whether a continuing resolution should include an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits, which are set to expire at the end of 2025, and the passage includes competing claims about the impact on health care and other policy issues.

The passage describes a configurable computing architecture and related systems for high-performance, energy-efficient compute-intensive kernels (e.g., FFTs and FIR filters) and heterogeneous applications. It outlines a multi-threaded, coarse-grained configurable computing system with embedded synchronous and asynchronous interconnection networks, dynamic self-configuration and self-reconfiguration, ordered and self-scheduled thread execution, conditional branching, and backpressure control using asynchronous signaling. Representative configurable circuit embodiments are described, including configurable computation circuitry, synchronous network inputs/outputs, configuration memory with instruction and spoke instruction/index storage, conditional logic for modifying next instructions, flow control with stop signals, and control circuitry with loop tables, completion tables, queues (e.g., continuation and reenter queues), and thread identifier pools. A system embodiment includes an asynchronous packet network and synchronous network coupled to arrays of configurable circuits, with interconnection-network and cluster configurations (including hierarchical interconnection using folded Clos and mesh connections). The passage also includes representative method embodiments for configuring the configurable circuits and controlling thread execution using instruction memories, conditional branching logic, flow control, completion/loop counts, and queue-based scheduling. It concludes with references to numerous figures and a detailed description of hybrid computing systems, including a “hybrid threading processor,” a “hybrid threading fabric,” tile-level components (computation, control, configuration memories, synchronous mesh and asynchronous packet networking), and the types of messaging and fields used in the synchronous mesh (e.g., data, instruction addresses, thread identifiers, and transfer identifiers).

A Lewisville mother says she earns money as a mystery shopper by going shopping. The passage also describes Contrave, an FDA-approved prescription weight-loss drug combining bupropion and naltrexone, which ads claim reduces hunger and cravings. Contrave is approved for obese people or those with a BMI of 27 or higher with serious conditions such as heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or type 2 diabetes. The passage states that Consumer Reports analysis finds Contrave’s additional weight loss is small but may pose serious health risks, including anxiety, insomnia, headaches, liver damage, seizures, increased blood pressure, and possible heart risks. Consumer Reports says people who took Contrave for up to 56 weeks lost about five to nine pounds more than placebo and advises discussing risks and options with a doctor, including safer, proven weight-loss approaches like eating less and exercising and intensive behavioral programs with at least 12 sessions per year.

The passage describes MSPM0 IOMUX functionality for selecting peripheral functions on digital IO pins and controlling output driver, input path, and wake-up logic from SHUTDOWN mode, noting that not all pins support features such as analog functions, wake-up logic, drive strength control, or pullup/pulldown resistors. The passage discusses Penn State and USC’s history in the Rose Bowl, noting they meet for the 10th time overall and the third time in the Rose Bowl, with USC holding a 5-4 advantage. Facebook publicly released a detailed version of its Community Guidelines after years of requests from activists and users. The document explains what Facebook will remove, based on principles of “safety,” “voice,” and “equity,” and is described as a manual for human moderators to adjudicate individual posts, comments, pictures, and videos. It includes specific provisions such as restrictions on crisis actors in a harassment section and defines certain child-abuse videos, with examples of broad and precise language. The passage says decisions over what to include are made through regular meetings led by Monika Bickert, described as a “mini legislative session,” where company teams agree on the guidelines.

Point72 Europe London LLP purchased 10,000 shares of Hershey Company (The) in the second quarter for about $1,074,000, and hedge funds and other institutional investors made additional position changes. Sun Life Financial INC increased its stake, QCI Asset Management Inc. NY increased its stake, Fiduciary Trust Co. bought a new stake, Invictus RG bought a new stake, and Independent Portfolio Consultants Inc. increased its stake.
