A 92-year-old woman, Anna Mae Blessing, was arrested on suspicion of murder in Arizona after she was accused of fatally shooting her 72-year-old son over his plans to place her in an assisted living facility. She was taken into custody Monday at the Phoenix-area home she shared with her son and held on $500,000 bail. In statements to detectives, Blessing said she hid two handguns, confronted her son in his bedroom, and shot him multiple times; she also said she tried to point the guns at her son’s girlfriend, but the girlfriend wrestled them away. Court records said she refused to leave the house and was sitting in a reclining chair in her bedroom when taken into custody. She told detectives she confronted her son due to his intentions for her care, suggested she should be “put to sleep,” and said she purchased one weapon and received the other from her deceased husband, with neither fired since the 1970s. Police said they had previously visited the residence after a verbal altercation between Blessing and her son.

Anderson predicted in 1973 that the nearest-neighbor spin-1/2 Heisenberg triangular lattice antiferromagnet would have a quantum spin liquid (QSL) ground state with long-range entanglement and no magnetic order. Numerical verification later found that, despite magnetic order at nearest-neighbor coupling, the triangular lattice antiferromagnet forms a QSL with weak second-neighbor exchange, but experimental candidate materials often show controversy due to disorder and defects. The paper discusses “failed QSLs,” where disorder leads to a fluctuating ground state without magnetic order, and focuses on the triangular QSL candidate YbMgGaO4, which has been reinterpreted as a magnetic disordered ground state due to exchange randomness, glassy freezing, and lack of QSL quasiparticles. It then reports low-temperature properties of exchange-disordered triangular magnet YbCu1.14Se2. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction shows a well-ordered triangular lattice of magnetic Yb ions and non-ordered Cu vacancies with Cu occupancy 56.6±0.7% (stoichiometry YbCu1.14Se2). Bulk measurements find no magnetic ordering transition in zero-field specific heat, while the specific heat is sub-linear at low temperatures and the integrated entropy reaches about 85% of R ln(2) between 100 mK and 10 K. Ultra-low-temperature AC susceptibility shows a symmetric frequency-dependent freezing peak near Tf ≈ 0.1 K, characteristic of spin-glass freezing behavior, and the compound lacks a 1/3 magnetization plateau around 3–5 T seen in some ideal triangular-lattice models. The results suggest possible universality of disordered frustrated behavior and quantify that YbCu1.14Se2 departs from the ideal 2D triangular Heisenberg model due to exchange disorder.

The passage describes a ceremony announcing two NHL-related youth and leadership awards supported by Bridgestone. The Bridgestone Youth Leadership Award is presented as being in its fourth year, and Robert “Knobby” Knudsen is cited as a standout winner for empowering himself despite challenging circumstances and advocating for children. His son, Robert Knudsen Jr, accepts the Bridgestone Mark Messier Youth Leadership Award, thanking Mark, Bridgestone, and the NHL, and sharing a quote about how being important in a child’s life matters more than personal possessions.

The passage also names the Mark Messier Youth Leadership Award finalists: Dustin Brown (Los Angeles Kings), Shane Doan (Phoenix Coyotes), and Ryan Callahan (New York Rangers). It then includes discussion by Mark Messier and others about playoff competitiveness, the difficulty of winning, rule changes and parity in hockey, and observations about team depth and performance, concluding with praise for the New York Rangers’ season and a mention of Marian Gaborik’s continued improvement.

The speaker thanks fellow citizens for their support while expressing concern about his own abilities as he begins the first executive office. He reflects on the magnitude of the responsibilities of a growing republic in a troubled world, and looks to other constitutional authorities for guidance. He urges unity under the law after the national decision, emphasizing majority rule tempered by reason and the protection of minority rights. He calls for social harmony, rejects political intolerance, and argues for federal and republican principles, including confidence in a government strengthened by citizens’ commitment to law. He describes key government principles, including equal justice, peace with other nations without entangling alliances, support for state governments, preservation of the general government’s constitutional power, protections for elections and freedoms (religion, press, speech and person via habeas corpus and jury trial), militia readiness, civil supremacy over military authority, economy, debt repayment, encouragement of agriculture and commerce, and public accountability through information and criticism. He asks for indulgence for his mistakes, requests support against others’ errors, and commits to work for the happiness and freedom of all, concluding with a prayer for guidance and favorable outcomes for peace and prosperity.

Christian Bushman says CPR is one of the most important things to learn and that it helped keep her alive after a May 2014 incident when something fell from a closet and hit her in the chest. Her husband could not revive her and ran for help, and her sister-in-law Cathy Carson—an instructor—found her unresponsive and not breathing or having a pulse. Cathy initiated CPR and called 9-1-1, but Christian lost her again before CPR was restarted. Christian was breathing on her own when paramedics arrived. The passage also notes that 70 percent of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests happen in homes and mentions a study finding women are less likely than men to receive bystander CPR and are more likely to die. Christian says people should not stand by and watch and that she wants to “pay it forward” by teaching CPR. The passage provides information on getting CPR certification via We R CPR and includes contact details.

Torsten Sløk, chief economist at UBS, said forecasts of an imminent U.S. slowdown have been wrong, noting economists’ forecast averages have predicted a nine-month slowdown that has not occurred. He argued the economics profession should “look ourselves in the mirror” after repeated misjudgments. Sløk pointed to resilient consumer spending and strengthening business investment in areas tied to artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, and manufacturing reshoring, along with surprising housing stability, and he attributed slowing job growth to reduced immigration rather than economic weakness. He said delayed negative effects from six months earlier—Liberation Day and reciprocal tariffs—are becoming harder to argue. Sløk also warned that upside risks to inflation are growing, particularly if the Fed continues to cut rates. The passage also quotes Morgan Stanley strategist Mike Wilson, who described a “rolling recession” since 2022 and said the economy is transitioning to a “rolling recovery,” though he suggested this recovery is not appearing in the labor market as the ADP report showed job losses and revisions to negative territory.

The passage introduces a multivariate modeling framework for multivariate count data with excess zeros and dependence, focusing on a bivariate zero-inflated Poisson (BZIP) model. It explains why marginal specifications must handle zero inflation and why independence assumptions are often unrealistic. Traditional zero-inflated and hurdle models are reviewed, and multivariate extensions are summarized. The proposed BZIP class generates observed counts using a common Bernoulli inflation factor (controlling excess zeros) applied to latent Poisson counts (controlling dependence). Dependence is characterized through a parameter θ using comonotonic (positive dependence) or counter-monotonic (negative dependence) shock bivariate Poisson constructions, combined with the common inflation parameter ϕ. The passage presents formulas for marginal means and variances, joint distributions, and dependence measures such as covariance and correlation. It then describes estimation approaches (method of moments, maximum likelihood, and an EM algorithm), simulations comparing these methods across multiple parameter settings, and a data illustration using Australian environmental disaster records to fit positive- and negative-dependence versions of the model. Finally, it notes possible extensions to higher dimensions, particularly for positive dependence.

The passage argues that National Literacy Month is a call to action, highlighting the importance of literacy beyond the classroom. It describes how access to culturally responsive books and environments helped Anastacia Nwosu through a free after-school and summer literacy enrichment program, leading her to become “Kid Mayor,” mentor children, graduate in three years, and later serve as a field deputy to a California Assemblymember. The passage cites that children reading on grade level by the end of third grade are less likely to drop out and claims that homes with more than 100 books have higher reading outcomes. It presents solutions such as Read Lead Freedom Schools, which combines reading instruction with civic empowerment, and reports results from a 2023–24 pilot showing increased English Language Arts proficiency, reduced chronic absenteeism, and reported family gains; students also take home books and alumni return as volunteers. It warns that support for such programs is under threat due to funding uncertainties and potential cuts to services, and calls for sustained support so families can make reading a daily practice and help address inequities.

After Congress adjourned in Philadelphia, the speaker gave directions under the laws to remove public offices, records, and property; these actions were completed and officers have since conducted government business at the permanent seat. He congratulates Congress and the public on the stable residence of the Government and hopes accommodations will improve. He urges Congress to seek divine blessing and to consider whether Congress should immediately exercise constitutional local powers over the District of Columbia, describing the territory’s prospects for prosperity and self-government. He notes the discharge of the temporary army under a prior law. He recommends prompt law execution and the judiciary system, reports that a treaty of amity and commerce with the King of Prussia was concluded, ratified, and will be proclaimed, and says negotiations with Great Britain regarding the sixth article are still pending. He describes ongoing negotiations with France and emphasizes the need for self-protection through defense measures, including a defensive navy, fortifying key sea ports (with some sums already spent but incomplete works), and continued encouragement of domestic arms manufacture. He will submit budget estimates and a report on revenue and expenditures, observing that current-year revenue is higher than in any comparable prior period. He concludes by urging perseverance in national institutions and assuring Congress of cooperation in promoting public happiness.

Beatrice Fihn, executive director of ICAN, warned that “a moment of panic” or carelessness could lead to the destruction of cities and deaths of millions through nuclear weapons use. She said the risk is greater than at the end of the Cold War due to more nuclear-armed states, terrorists, and cyber warfare. Fihn’s remarks were linked to escalating war rhetoric and personal insults between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un, which culminated in Trump’s Sept. 19 UN General Assembly threat to obliterate 25.4 million North Koreans.

The passage states that a US$INR January futures contract on the NSE is bearish, recommending selling US$INR in the 68.20–68.30 range, with a market lot of US$1000, target levels of 67.95/67.75, and stop loss at 68.40. It also mentions a large annual fall in government bond yields, the rupee posting its sixth straight year loss against the dollar due to expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase, and dollar index profit booking during Christmas holidays. In NSE currency futures, the most traded dollar-rupee January contract ended at 68.09, with January open interest up 6.46% and February open interest up 1.33%. It concludes with an expectation that the US$ will face supply pressure at higher levels and advises going short using the dollar’s upside.

The ADS7828 can use an internal 2.5V reference or an external reference. A +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full dynamic range for a 0V to +VDD input; this external reference can be as low as 50mV. With a +2.7V supply, the internal +2.5V reference provides full dynamic range. Reducing the reference voltage reduces the analog voltage weight of each output code (LSB size), calculated as reference voltage divided by 4096, which makes inherent offset or gain errors appear larger in LSB terms. Converter noise also appears increased with smaller LSB size: internal noise typically contributes 0.32LSB peak-to-peak with a 2.5V reference, but 16LSBs with an external 50mV reference; the internal noise errors are Gaussian in nature.

The Ministry of Health and Child Care estimates about 44,586 sex workers in Zimbabwe aged 15–49, including nearly 7,000 in Bulawayo; the figure excludes people with transactional sex and male sex workers. HIV prevalence among sex workers averages 55%, compared with a 13% national average, with site-specific rates including 54.4% in Harare and 54.2% in Bulawayo, while Mazowe and Shamva recorded 59.2% and 54.8%, respectively. The Estimates report is intended to help planners understand how funding levels and allocation patterns affect programme impact and reductions in HIV incidence and prevalence. It also notes that about 25,900 people died of AIDS-related causes in 2016 (71 deaths per day), down from 278 per day in 2005, and that 14 out of every 100 people are HIV infected. A parliamentarian warned that Zimbabwe may not end the HIV and Aids epidemic by 2030 if it ignores key populations such as sex workers and prisoners, whose HIV prevalence is above the national average, alongside other groups identified by the World Health Organisation.

Gas prices rose in Montgomery and nationwide, with the national average reaching its highest point since 2015, according to analysts and GasBuddy. GasBuddy Senior Petroleum Analyst Patrick DeHaan cited declining oil inventories and geopolitical tensions, while noting the national average could peak in the next few weeks. AAA predicted increased summer demand could lead to higher prices through September, citing crude oil storage use and possible OPEC production cut extensions. GasBuddy reported only 405 stations nationwide sold gas for $2 or less on Sunday, compared with more than 80,000 stations a year earlier.

GoSun announced its new solar-electric oven, The Fusion, designed to let people steam, bake, or roast without fuel anywhere, including indoors and at night, using solar energy and a 150-watt electric heating element. The Fusion is described as a vacuum insulated oven that cooks through clouds and freezing cold, remains safe to touch, and is five times more efficient than a typical oven, powered by a compact lithium-ion battery. It weighs 10 lbs., feeds up to five people, and is built for outdoor use. GoSun said the Fusion is the result of six years of work and launched a Kickstarter campaign with exclusive deals for early backers; the company reported having sold more than 25,000 solar stoves in over 80 countries.

The lecture reviews policy evaluation using temporal difference (TD) learning and motivates moving beyond discrete Markov chain representations to more general, continuous function approximation. It provides a crash course on least squares function approximation: fitting an unknown function from input/output samples by minimizing squared error over parameters, with examples of neural networks and linear function approximators using chosen basis functions (e.g., radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators, Fourier bases, and polynomials). It argues that linear-in-parameter models enable explicit least-squares solutions and discusses how this scales to reinforcement learning and system identification, where robot dynamics can be rewritten as linear optimization problems in grouped parameters. The lecture then applies these ideas to TD learning with function approximation, describing eligibility traces extended from state-node values to parameter-based updates via gradients. It notes convergence results for TD(λ) with linear function approximation (for λ between 0 and 1) and contrasts standard online TD with more data-efficient least squares temporal difference learning (LSTD), which computes parameter estimates from accumulated matrices rather than relying on incremental learning rates. The lecture ends by linking function approximation to future policy-gradient topics, including actor-critic.

The order grants AAA Nevada Insurance Company’s motion for summary judgment in Case No. 08-cv-00827-GMN-LRL in the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada. The court concludes that AAA’s insurance policy limits liability to $100,000 for the claim arising from Defendant Vinh Chau’s car accident. It further holds that AAA’s failure to settle within the two-week time limit in Interveners’ demand letter does not constitute bad faith under Nevada law. The court denies the Interveners’ request for a continuance under Rule 56(f) and rejects their arguments that the court lacks jurisdiction.

The passage describes provisions of a solemn covenant guaranteeing territorial integrity and political independence under republican forms of government. It requires disputes over boundaries or territory to be settled by amicable agreement or international arbitration, with investigation by a permanent international commission before arbitration in certain cases. It also obligates the parties not to allow hostile military or naval expeditions to depart from their jurisdictions against established governments, and to prevent exportation of arms and munitions for use in insurrection or revolt, subject to conditions regarding recognized belligerency. The treaty is to be ratified, take effect sixty days after ratifications are deposited at the Pan American Union in Washington, be indefinite in duration, and include procedures for denunciation and continuation for similar periods unless terminated by agreement of all parties. The passage further includes correspondence: Dr. S. E. Mezes acknowledges a confidential enclosure and plans to draft general principles without references to specific nations, and the Secretary of War (Baker) thanks Walter Lippmann, expressing concern about achieving a “victorious peace” that leaves Germany with intolerable economic conditions and emphasizes the need for reliable assurances about use of civilization’s resources.

The passage discusses writing essays and preparing academic papers, emphasizing organization, choosing an essay topic based on interest, using reliable resources, and editing to match the essay’s goal. It also mentions selecting an appropriate tone for formal essays, brainstorming ideas when time is limited, and avoiding ending the essay by merely restating the thesis. The passage further describes the option of using expert essay-writing services to complete coursework, with claims about improved quality, error-free writing, and better grades, and suggests tools like Hemingway for readability and mind-mapping applications such as FreeMind and XMind.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets edged lower on Monday amid investor caution ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting starting Tuesday. A 25 basis point rate hike is expected, with attention on whether the Fed’s “dot plot” forecasts four rate hikes this year rather than three. Thai shares fell the most, Singapore declined for a fourth straight session, and Indonesian shares slipped. Philippine shares recovered from early losses to close marginally lower, while Malaysia rose slightly. Vietnam increased for a sixth straight session, reaching its highest close since March 2007.

The passage explains the “Trap” play as a quick-hitting, downhill run scheme that kicks out an interior defensive lineman and is effective against aggressive pass rushers. It describes how the play can work with different back types (Fullback, Quarterback, Tailback) and how its strengths include speed—especially from under center with the defense needing a split-second to read who has the ball—plus compatibility with deception schemes like Wing-T and forgiving offensive line requirements due to angle blocks, including the option to trap an unblocked defensive tackle. A key weakness is that Trap is difficult to run against defenses that squeeze interior gaps, such as Bear fronts or even fronts, limiting the offensive line’s ability to climb to linebackers. The passage also outlines blocking steps for Trap versus 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, and gives variations including a Gun Trey same-side Trap RPO (run from shotgun) and a Wing-T Trap treated as a sister play to Buck Sweep.

Hillview Middle School will host an outdoor family movie night on Friday, April 27 at 7:30 pm at the school field. The event is open to all ages and requires one adult for every eight children, with adults staying with their groups during the movie. “Sing” (PG) will be shown, and families should bring small bills for bake goods plus $2 for popcorn and $1 for water. A Mexican food truck, Los Carnalitos, will be on site at 7:30 pm. Proceeds will benefit the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society (LLS) and the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation (JDRF), and attendees can RSVP for an accurate headcount.

The passage is a presidential address reviewing U.S. foreign relations and outlining domestic and foreign policy priorities. It emphasizes the President’s goals of strengthening mutual trust with Congress, sustaining U.S. leadership since World War II, and dealing with global challenges such as energy, hunger, and the environment. It describes progress and ongoing competition in relations with the Soviet Union, a historic opening with China, and continued strong alliances with Europe, North America, Japan, and others, while calling for steadier progress toward peace efforts, including in the Middle East and with developing nations.

The speech focuses heavily on crises in Vietnam, Cambodia, and U.S. allies’ security. It recounts U.S. involvement in Indochina and the Paris accords, alleges North Vietnamese violations, describes South Vietnam’s retreat and humanitarian catastrophe, and urges Hanoi to cease operations and honor the Paris agreement. It presents options for U.S. action, including congressional requests for $722 million in emergency military assistance and $250 million initially for economic and humanitarian aid, along with changes to restrictions on using U.S. military forces for evacuation and revisions to protect those owed special obligations. For Cambodia, it highlights the ongoing conflict, a letter from the acting Cambodian president requesting food and ammunition, and regrets that it may be too late.

The address also discusses broader foreign policy tools and constraints, including Congress’s role in intelligence oversight, defense readiness and the national security budget, issues in Cyprus involving Turkey, Greece, and an arms embargo, trade policy effects toward Latin America, and negotiations to limit strategic nuclear weapons and improve relations through “detente” as a two-way relationship.

The passage describes how AGESA™ software interfaces with a host BIOS through mechanisms such as callouts, a dispatcher/router, a bridge, and a call-out port, including typical call sequences between host code and a binary module. It also covers host responsibilities for setting up required execution environments (e.g., stacks), creating standard header data, and implementing a call-out router and matching exported interface definitions. Additional sections describe deprecation of 16-bit Real Mode support, AGESA execution across UEFI execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP), build targets and required tools, and UEFI-specific configuration and stack handling. The text further outlines PEI/DXE responsibilities, event log retrieval behavior via AmdReadEventLog, and numerous AGESA service procedures and related data structures used for initialization, buffer allocation, cache-as-RAM/stack enable/disable, reset/memory initialization, ACPI/DMI table generation, and S3 suspend/resume support.

Gary Kleck and Marc Gertz concluded from 1993 surveys that there were more than 2.2 million defensive gun uses (DGU) each year in the United States, with results presented in 1994 and published in 1995. Their findings were attacked by the anti-gun movement because they did not fit the view that guns are used more in crimes than self-defense. The passage says the CDC conducted three additional studies soon after their publication, each reportedly concluding that about 2.5 million Americans use guns to defend themselves or their families annually, but that the CDC never published the results. Kleck later reviewed the recovered studies and wrote that an adjusted DGU prevalence implies about 2.46 million U.S. adults used a gun for self-defense in 1996–1998, and that CDC results suggest defensive gun use occurred about 3.6 times as often as offensive use. The passage further claims the CDC did not report or acknowledge DGU frequency and was hiding information harmful to the anti-gun narrative during the Clinton administration. It argues that verifying government information matters and frames the issue as an educational and political battle over gun ownership.

The passage discusses concerns about the environmental value of biodegradable plastic bags as an alternative to conventional plastics. Andrew Masterson says there is little evidence that heavier “biodegradable” plastic bag replacements are environmentally helpful. It notes that carrier bag bans have led to alternatives such as biodegradable bags, but questions remain about their effectiveness. Citing a study in Royal Society Open Science led by Jesse Harrison from the University of Edinburgh, Masterson reports that research on end-of-life rates of biodegradable bags is inconsistent, with varied and poorly defined protocols, making it of limited use for policy or regulation.

On Tuesday, stocks including Kinder Morgan, Booz Allen Hamilton, American Woodmark, KB Home, and American Water Works rose, while Bank of America and Petrobras fell. Kinder Morgan rose after the Canadian government agreed to buy a pipeline project for $3.4 billion. Bank of America and Petrobras declined amid falling interest rates and rising bond prices. Petrobras fell as the Brazilian government planned diesel price subsidies to address a trucker strike. Other gains followed news such as ZTO Express receiving investment from Alibaba’s Cainiao and Booz Allen posting stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter profit. Investors also bought high-dividend companies as bond yields dropped.

Mitsui & Co reported that its April–December profits rose more than 60% year on year and it raised its full-year net profit forecast to a record 440 billion yen, citing higher iron ore and coking coal prices. April–December net profit grew 64% to a record 376.8 billion yen. Mitsui attributed its performance to strength in metal and energy assets and progress in steel product, machinery, and infrastructure operations. Mitsui’s iron ore price gains were linked to tighter Chinese steel markets. Itochu reported a 19% rise in April–December profit to a record 357.1 billion yen but kept its full-year forecast unchanged. Sojitz raised its net profit forecast for the year to March by 12% to 56 billion yen due to higher-than-expected coal prices.

The passage describes a hospital visit on April 9, when the writer and their wife checked in at 5:15 p.m. at Norfolk General Hospital’s emergency ward and did not see a doctor until 11:45 p.m., with several beds empty during the wait. The writer argues that staff should not be blamed and calls for higher authorities to reduce wait times by allowing additional doctors to be called in, giving doctors authority to request help, and criticizing bureaucrats for not acting. The passage also includes comments about long-term care, medication fees for seniors, and questions about provincial funding for long-term care beds being announced shortly before the June 7 election.

The passage is a set of comments, attributed to Peter DeBoer, about a playoff series. It says the team believes it can win, that building momentum and getting early goals has been difficult in the first three games, and that finally getting a win provides hope to continue responding to playoff challenges. It highlights DeBoer’s character in rising to pressure, mentions strong performance by a rookie, and emphasizes the team’s composure, “fire,” and desire to play for the Stanley Cup. The comments also discuss the need for players to start scoring, credit for the opponent’s goaltender and penalty killing, and the importance of ending a streak to avoid season-ending elimination.

The passage describes systems and methods for dynamically overlaying video streams. A client device identifies a set-top box and selects a corresponding template, then uses video data to generate query fingerprints and queries a database of reference fingerprints to identify the video content. Based on the identified content, the client selects replacement video (e.g., local instead of national commercials) and presents it in a template-defined region using positioning, cropping, alpha blending, and potentially alpha/transparency or image-processing techniques to mimic the set-top box’s presentation. The passage also describes how replacement overlays can account for animated menus, changing masks, playback speed changes (e.g., fast-forward or pause), and when to stop or resume overlaying based on changes in the video content (e.g., channel switching). It further outlines components such as fingerprint generators, a video identification system, a replacement content server (video provision and template provision), and database structures (e.g., PictureinPicture, MenuOverlay, MenuBlend, and Template tables) used to manage templates and overlay behavior.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV reported false information on social media regarding the June 19 North Braddock shooting of Antwon Rose II, including claims that he fired a gun and that gunshot residue was found on his hands. After Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough stated the video did not show Rose firing a gun and that the residue information was false, KDKA later retracted and apologized on June 27, saying its sources were incorrect. WPXI initially defended its reporting without apologizing, later issuing a written statement dated June 28 acknowledging the video did not appear to show Rose firing a gun and apologizing for pain caused. The DA’s office criticized media for refusing to correct the record, and The New Pittsburgh Courier questioned the stations’ sourcing and whether they sought to provide the alleged video.

The passage describes the growth of Costa and coffee in Britain, citing rising sales and expansion to more than 2,000 UK shops. It focuses on Costa’s new roastery in Basildon, Essex, including why the site was chosen, how it quadruples roasting capacity, and details of the roasting, cleaning, quality control, and robot-based packing processes. It also describes sustainability features and Costa’s coffee sourcing and certification. The Master of Coffee is introduced along with Costa’s barista training, and the lab testing and blending approach are explained. The passage concludes with Costa’s long-term plans for further expansion.

The passage describes a class session on multi-stakeholder engagement using palm oil as an example, focusing on how companies like GAR (Golden Aggregate Resources) should collaborate with growers, mills, governments, certifying bodies, NGOs, consumers, and investors to improve sustainability and communicate strategy. It discusses different proposed approaches (Greenpeace-aligned, non-Greenpeace, and market-driven), the role of brand-focused NGO pressure, and challenges such as limited transparency in supply chains, costs and feasibility of certification for small farmers, and uncertainty in certification impacts. The discussion also covers communication strategies (e.g., reports and use of celebrities), incentives versus burdens on farmers, and broader impacts like potential choices between higher versus lower deforestation-related standards and maintaining sustainability commitments. Later, the passage broadens to examples of collaboration types (one-on-one partnerships and industry collaborations like RSPO) and explains how NGOs and certification labels function, including concerns about label rigor and regulation.

YouTube announced that its Original Content team, led by Susan Daniels, will add four new Original series to YouTube Red. The series are made with the YouTube Kids app in mind, debut in spring, and additional shows are planned to premiere throughout 2017. The lineup features DanTDM, Joe and Cody of TheAtlanticCraft, L2M, and Fruit Ninja. The new series include “This,” inspired by a true story; “DanTDM Creates A Big Scene”; “The Kings of Atlantis”; and “Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force.” YouTube Kids is also coming to Smart TVs, with the app available soon for download on LG and Samsung internet-connected Smart TVs.

The passage describes the “Kiss of Death” trading strategy, a strong sell signal for the S&P 500. The signal occurs when the index falls from an all-time high, drops below its monthly 21 exponential moving average (EMA), rebounds above the 21-EMA, and then drops below its recent low. It has triggered only a few times since 1960 (1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, 2008), and in those cases it preceded major crashes and bear markets. The passage also notes that in September 2022 the signal did not lead to a major drop; the S&P 500 rose afterward. A backtest beginning in 1967 used the S&P 500 index (not adjusted for dividends) and applied selling when the signal triggered, with buying back when the S&P 500 closed above a 10-month EMA. The results reportedly improved performance versus buying and holding and reduced the maximum drawdown to almost half.

Fair Isaac (FICO’s creator) announced a new pricing model for mortgage lenders that allows them to bypass credit bureaus for FICO credit scores by licensing the scores directly to mortgage resellers, who then distribute them to borrowers. The company’s stock rose more than 20% on Thursday, while shares of Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax fell. Fair Isaac said lenders can choose between two pricing models and that it will offer both mortgage score pricing models to the three credit bureaus on the same terms.

MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers are ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs in the MSPM0 family based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating up to 32 MHz. They offer high-performance analog integration, extended temperature operation from -40°C to 125°C, and supply voltages from 1.62 V to 3.6 V. The devices include up to 64 KB embedded flash and 8 KB SRAM, a high-speed on-chip oscillator with accuracy from -2.1% to +1.6% (no external crystal needed), and features such as a 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, and analog peripherals including a 12-bit 1.6 Msps ADC (VDD reference), an 8-bit reference DAC comparator, and an on-chip temperature sensor. Digital peripherals include a 16-bit advanced timer with deadband (up to 64 MHz), four 16-bit general purpose timers, a windowed watchdog timer, and communications peripherals supporting three UART, one SPI, two I2C, and protocols including LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus, and PMBus. The MSPM0 family includes devices with different levels of analog and digital integration and uses an ultra-low-power system architecture to improve performance while reducing energy consumption.

Pekkala told the writer two things: most Finns sympathized with the democracies, and conviction was steadily growing that Finland must make a separate peace with the Soviet Union. He said this view was shared by Field Marshal Mannerheim, many in the Finnish Army, Social Democratic leaders and rank and file, and smaller political groups including the Swedish Party and Progressives. Pekkala said the Agrarian Party still believed Russians could be crushed and took little interest in foreign policy. He said he had not discussed matters with Foreign Minister Witting and hinted at lack of confidence in President Ryti, but asserted the two propositions matched facts and were leading to growing movement. The writer expected to see Witting to make representations and reported increasing uneasiness in Finland about relations with the United States and the possibility of Finland withdrawing from the war. Schoenfeld later reported that Witting indicated Finland’s dependence on German goodwill for most imports and suggested Finland’s position regarding German troop use resembled Iceland’s; he also said Finland could not risk starvation if Germans interrupted imports, and described Finland as “like a mouse in a trap.” Johnson reported from Sweden that Finnish military conditions were rapidly deteriorating and that a Russian offensive leading to Finland’s collapse could prompt Swedish calls for assistance, potentially involving collaboration with Germans and risking an internal political crisis affecting Sweden’s democratic cause; he also reported that Soviet Minister Kollontay was concerned about Sweden and believed only hope for peace was a cessation of fighting.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 11, 2016 to correct an immaterial error in its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The error overstated the cost and resulting net book value of the Supercharger network; the net book value should have been $166.6 million as of December 31, 2015. The error was limited to the referenced section of the Form 10-K and did not impact the consolidated financial statements or the notes in Item 8. Management determined the error to be immaterial. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Jason Wheeler.

Scientists developed a molecular sensor that releases a thyme-like flavor (thymol) when it encounters influenza, offering a potential low-tech alternative to nasal swabs. The sensor is built on a neuraminidase (from influenza) substrate with thymol attached; in saliva from flu-diagnosed people, it released free thymol within 30 minutes and did not change the functioning of human and mouse cells in tests. Researchers plan to incorporate the sensor into chewing gum or lozenges for rapid at-home screening before symptoms begin and hope to start human clinical trials in about two years. The work is described as potentially helping prevent pre-symptomatic transmission, and funding and patent registration are acknowledged.

Four Baltimore County executive candidates spoke at a forum for real estate, builders, and mortgage professionals, promising to encourage smart growth and streamline the development approval process. They discussed impact fees but did not support them: Brochin suggested restricting new housing in overcrowded-school areas instead, while Redmer, Olszewski, and Almond said impact fees likely were not the solution or were too late to consider. The candidates also said approval processes are cumbersome and should be made smoother by reducing barriers and improving predictability. On rezoning, Olszewski, Redmer, and others emphasized consistency with the county master plan, clearer guidelines, and appeals or changes to authority and process. Brochin pledged to end “pay-to-play politics,” while other candidates focused on development’s economic and property-tax value. The forum was hosted by real estate and building industry groups, with additional forums scheduled during the week ahead of the June 26 primaries and June 14 early voting.

The nomination phase for the Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards is underway, with entries due by noon on Monday, March 13. The awards ceremony on Thursday, April 27 will be held at the Royal Hall for the first time, a restored Edwardian theatre reopened in 2008 by Prince Charles. The event is a black-tie evening with dinner and entertainment, and the passage describes the Royal Hall’s capacity and restoration details. The awards are intended to recognize businesses across an area of over 500 square miles, and includes perspectives from organizers and a past winner, Zara Jackson. The main sponsor is Verity Frearson of Harrogate and Pateley Bridge estate agent, with each award having its own sponsor. There are 10 categories, and businesses can enter as many categories as they like via www.harrogatebusinessawards.co.uk.

The passage discusses Robert Oscar Lopez, a former tenured professor at California State University, Northridge, who resigned after eight years, saying he wants to be true to God. It describes his shift from supporting academic freedom and free speech to viewing academic freedom as neither a virtue nor a reality, linking this to issues with tenure and campus discipline, including an account that a Title IX–related complaint process was used against him. The passage argues that academic freedom is “a lie” and compares cases of perceived ideological persecution involving Lopez and other professors. It further criticizes higher education as a political and economic system and suggests cutting funding to colleges, expanding trade schools and apprenticeships, and ultimately replacing academic freedom with a principle focused on “Truth” rather than “a lie.”

The passage discusses the “first trading day of the month effect,” a frequently mentioned stock market seasonality. It defines the effect as the first trading day of each month (not the first calendar day), noting that the first trading day can be later if the first calendar day falls on a weekend or holiday. Using the S&P 500 (SPY), the article states that the market performs significantly better on the first trading day than on other days, reporting an average gain of 0.24% from the close of the last trading day of the month to the close of the first trading day (six times better than the average day). It also says a simple “buy at month-end close and sell at the first day close” approach is too unstable to trade, but improved versions using a filter or additional criteria can increase average gain per trade and change performance metrics.

The passage introduces bilateral trade with a broker who aims to maximize profit while ensuring dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. Prior computer science work has largely focused on maximizing efficiency (welfare/gains-from-trade), but this work focuses on profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade using online learning and regret minimization versus the best mechanism in hindsight. It studies both a stochastic i.i.d. setting (possibly correlated unknown distribution) and an adversarial setting (valuations set by an oblivious adversary). In the stochastic case, it presents a polynomial-time algorithm with nearly tight regret \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}), along with a lower bound \Omega(\sqrt{T}) showing optimality up to polylogarithmic terms, including an implication that about 1/\epsilon^2 samples are sufficient and necessary to learn an \epsilon-optimal expected-profit mechanism. In the adversarial case, it shows no learning algorithm can achieve sublinear regret with respect to a 2/3+\epsilon fraction of the optimal profit. The passage also relates bilateral trade to non-excludable mechanism design, reducing regret for the joint ads problem from O(T^{3/4}) to \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}), and outlines challenges due to a non-parametric action space and potentially non-regular profit functions, including the inadequacy of fixed discretization.

The passage describes multiple views (front and top, rear and bottom, front, rear, left, right, top, bottom, and another perspective in an alternative position) of a cooling fan showing a new design. It also states that broken lines indicate portions of the cooling fan that do not form part of the claimed design.

The passage describes mediation analysis in applied psychological research and the role of mediator variables in explaining how interventions affect outcomes. It outlines advantages of identifying valid mediators, the need to validate causal mediation effects, and challenges caused by confounding and measurement error when using self-report data. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is presented as a standard method for modeling latent mediator variables, but its causal use often depends on the sequential ignorability (no unmeasured confounding) assumption, which is rarely fully achievable in practice. The passage then discusses methods robust to omitted variable bias, focusing on rank-preserving models (RPMs) that rely on a no-effect-modifier (no-essential-heterogeneity) assumption rather than no unmeasured confounding. Because RPMs have not been extended to latent variable models, the authors introduce the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), which integrates RPM with factor score regression and interaction corrections to support robust mediation analysis with latent constructs and measurement error. The document defines causal effects within a potential outcomes framework, including the controlled direct effect (CDE) and controlled mediation effect (CME), and begins model formulation by specifying a measurement model where mediator, covariates, and outcome are treated as latent variables measured by observed indicators.

The speaker says the team felt comfortable throughout the game and played well, leading to capitalizing on chances. They express happiness for a goalie’s performance, noting confidence in him and that they need him to stay “hot” for three games to even the series. The passage also highlights leadership from Ryan Smyth, praising his skill, work ethic, practice habits, and ability to score huge goals while playing hurt. It discusses power-play success as a result of smart play, pressure, active sticks, shot blocking, and competitiveness for the puck, with confidence they will eventually score. The team credits solid game planning and playoff adjustments, including more structure on shorthanded situations. The speaker emphasizes handling adversity by refocusing after frustration, believes the team has played below its best so far, and expects they can raise their level to take over the series, while mentioning the tradition of the organization and the desire to honor past players.

The passage says the team has stayed focused and enjoyed hard practices all season, contributing to its current position. It describes a fearless player who blocks shots, gets up repeatedly, and is on the ice every day, helping others learn resilience. It notes that an earlier break with rest and time away from watching hockey was less exciting once the team arrived, especially as media attention and game hype increased. It also praises a nominated top defenseman as a great, smooth, non-flashy player with a strong career.

Visceral leishmaniasis (VL or Kala-azar) is a vector-borne parasitic disease transmitted by blood-sucking sand flies and caused by protozoan parasites of the Leishmania donovani complex. Ethiopia has reported VL cases across multiple regions, including Denan district in south-eastern Ethiopia’s Somali Region, where VL outbreaks were previously reported and large geographic areas are considered high risk.  

A cross-sectional study conducted from April to August 2021 in Denan district assessed VL sero-prevalence, knowledge, attitudes, practices, and sand fly abundance. Human blood samples were tested using the Direct Agglutination Test (DAT). From 187 participants, overall VL sero-prevalence was 9.63% (18/187). In multivariable analysis, increased odds of VL were associated with age 19–36, sleeping outdoors near animal shelter, and living in houses with damp floors. Most participants had heard about VL (53.48%), knew sand flies could transmit VL (42%), and reported knowing at least one clinical sign (89%), but only 36% believed VL is preventable. Preventive practices included bed net use (42%), insecticide spraying (32%), smoking plant parts (14%), and environmental cleaning (8%).  

Entomological investigation in four kebeles collected 823 sand flies and identified 12 species. P. orientalis was the dominant species among Phlebotomus, and no P. orientalis was captured indoors. The study concludes that VL is relatively high among asymptomatic pastoralist communities, highlights key risk factors (damp floors, outdoor sleeping, sleeping near animal shelter), and suggests that P. orientalis may contribute to transmission in this new VL focus, warranting further studies.

The passage studies whether transformer models can learn to infer transitive relations by learning graph connectivity from training examples, rather than relying on in-context examples. Transitivity is linked to connectivity/path-finding in directed graphs, and the connectivity task is defined as predicting whether a directed path exists between two nodes. The work focuses on comparing learnability in grid graphs versus disconnected chain graphs, motivated by the idea that grid graphs are more easily embeddable in a low-dimensional space. Experiments show transformers learn connectivity well on grid graphs but generalize poorly on disconnected chain graphs. Scaling results indicate that increasing model size improves performance more for grid graphs than for disconnected chain graphs; for grid graphs, performance remains consistent as graph size increases, while disconnected chain graphs improve as graph size increases. Additional experiments vary grid dimensionality and the number of disconnected components: lower-dimensional grids are easier, and increasing the number of nodes helps for higher-dimensional grids; for disconnected chain graphs, performance declines as the number of chains increases, and scaling graph size helps more than model size when the number of chains is large. The conclusion summarizes that scaling graph connectivity learning is more beneficial for grid graphs with model scaling, and for disconnected chain graphs with data (graph size) scaling, with further future work proposed on real-world graph data.

Hawkin's Bazaar, a Plymouth gift and gadget shop, will close for the final time on Sunday, February 4. The New George Street store has told customers it is holding a closing down sale with items reduced by at least 50%, and some by up to 75%. An email to customers says the shop is closing on February 4 and urges customers to visit for the clearance sale before the doors shut. The shop has been on New George Street for four years and previously in the West End for six years; no response was received when The Herald contacted the business for comment.

Cincinnati beat No. 14 Iowa State at home, handing the Cyclones their first loss and snapping their perfect record. Cincinnati used a 17-point first quarter, finished with a 4-1 record, and won after Iowa State rallied late within eight points; Cincinnati recovered an onside kick to prevent further comeback. The Bearcats’ offense produced 314 passing yards and two passing touchdowns, and coach Scott Satterfield said the team differed from last year’s roster.

The defendant, charged with assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill, pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor in open court, withdrew that plea, and then requested time to obtain witnesses from West Virginia and Florida. The court denied the request to continue the case and denied a further request to postpone until the following week, and the case proceeded to trial the next day, resulting in a guilty verdict. The appellate court held it was error to force the defendant to trial on the succeeding day because he was not given time to prepare, noting that the jurors would likely remember the withdrawn guilty plea and that counsel was entitled to a reasonable time to investigate and prepare the defense. The case was remanded for a new trial.

MADSEN Cycles offers a designed bucket bike with accessories intended to improve comfort, security, style, and functionality. The bucket bike can carry up to four kids plus some cargo, and its bucket includes two removable bench seats and four seat belts. The company provides accessories such as rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and a middle bucket seat that can be used as a padded surface for transporting pets, changing diapers, or carrying drinks. MADSEN Cycles manufactures customized, brightly colored bucket bikes and promotes the ease of riding with added accessories.

Jerome “Jay” Powell will begin leading US monetary policy on Monday after being tapped by President Donald Trump, succeeding Janet Yellen. The leadership change occurs at a relatively quiet time following past economic turmoil, though Powell may face difficult decisions about how quickly to raise interest rates. Yellen leaves an economy with unemployment at 4.1%, quiet inflation, and nearly four years of uninterrupted growth; she also moved the Fed toward “normalization” by steering it out of bond buying. The Fed raised its key lending rate multiple times during her tenure, and in December indicated likely additional hikes this year, while meeting minutes showed debate about the pace of moves amid differing views on inflation and the impact of tax cuts. Inflation remains below the Fed’s 2% target, but the latest policy statement expects prices to rise near term. A March rate increase is expected, along with Powell’s first press conference. Economists cited concerns about the effects of new fiscal stimulus and the practical need for the Fed to telegraph rate decisions to markets.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in Barrett’s case involving federal firearm offenses and double jeopardy. Barrett was convicted in 2013, including under Section 924(c), for his role in a robbery in which a victim was shot to death by a coconspirator. Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm to advance a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense and is described as creating a “compound crime,” while also allowing enhanced minimum sentences based on firearm-related aggravating factors. Section 924(j), which applies when a defendant violates Section 924(c) and “causes the death of a person through the use of a firearm,” is at the center of the case and adds another layer to Section 924(c). The question before the Court is whether Section 924(j) creates a separate crime with a separate punishment from Section 924(c), guided by a nearly century-old test for when multiple punishments may be imposed for a single criminal event. The passage explains that courts compare the elements of the two offenses to determine whether one requires proof of a fact the other does not, and it describes presumptions and limits under the double jeopardy clause. The passage also notes that a prior case held that Section 924(j) does not import Section 924(c)’s consecutive-sentence and mandatory minimum provisions. The Supreme Court will now address whether Congress intended separate convictions and sentences under Sections 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct, with the government and Barrett agreeing that separate sentences are not permitted, while disputing whether Section 924(c)’s language affects the analysis. An amicus brief was appointed to defend the Second Circuit’s judgment that Barrett could receive separate convictions and sentences under both provisions for the same conduct.

The passage explains that formative assessment in vocational education is a socially oriented, complicated process requiring active participation, immediate feedback, and time for in-lesson conversations. Teachers use professional judgment to decide whether to guide students or let them practice independently, and students should self-assess with teacher review, though some students may not engage. It defines formative assessment methods as identifying difficulties or missed learning, and gives examples such as clear expectations, descriptive feedback, multiple attempts, peer reviews, and self-assessments, as well as socially oriented workplace-like assessment methods.

It then discusses competence-based education (CBE) as an alternative to relying only on curricular outcome lists, focusing on workplace competence tied to industry-standard performance and workplace contexts. Key CBE qualities include performance against final products, meeting workplace quality standards, observed behaviors, standards not dependent on peers, and communicating expectations. It highlights that authentic competence-based assessment should balance authenticity with reliability, since isolated workplace skills or overly controlled testing may reduce transferability, while contextualized assessment can challenge reliability.

Finally, it argues for a comprehensive assessment program in VET that spans school-workplace learning and includes written tests, technical skill assessments, workplace or practicum evaluations, assessment of both processes and products, and both formative and summative methods. The conclusion emphasizes that VET assessment must account for theoretical knowledge and technical skills and move beyond standardized summative approaches toward authentic assessment that supports deeper learning and engagement.

The Second Circuit affirmed a district court’s February 11, 2010 decision. The court granted Reisdorf Brothers, Incorporated summary judgment on the plaintiffs’ federal claims under the Clean Water Act and the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, refusing supplemental jurisdiction over the plaintiffs’ state adverse possession claim and dismissing it without prejudice for renewal in state court. The appeals also challenged evidentiary consideration and attorney fees; the district court declined to award fees under 42 U.S.C. § 6972(e). The Court of Appeals found no abuse of discretion and held the remaining arguments lacked merit.

The passage describes a study on cardiorenal syndrome focusing on how chronic kidney disease (CKD) kidney function status, age, and sex relate to new-onset heart failure (HF). CKD is established as a risk factor for HF, with age modifying this association; age also affects both renal decline and HF development. The study uses longitudinal data from the PREVEND cohort in Groningen, Netherlands, measuring urinary albumin excretion (UAE) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) across multiple clinical examinations. Kidney function was categorized using KDIGO risk stages based on UAE and eGFR, and new-onset HF was adjudicated by an expert committee. 

Multi-state modeling estimated transition rates between consecutive KDIGO stages and their association with new-onset HF and death, allowing for potential misclassification of kidney measures. At baseline, most participants were in low risk stage. Over a median follow-up of 12.6 years, new-onset HF occurred in 373 participants and death before HF in 710. Forward transition rates between KDIGO stages increased with age, were generally higher in men than women, and younger subjects and women more often showed backward transition from intermediate risk to low risk. More advanced KDIGO stages were associated with increased risk of new-onset HF, with relatively attenuated risk ratios in older subjects but increased absolute risk. Sensitivity analyses using cystatin C-based eGFR largely supported the findings, with lower misclassification probabilities. The authors conclude that slowing progression of KDIGO risk stages may reduce the incidence of new-onset HF in middle-aged subjects.

Phil Kessel scored twice with an assist, and Evgeni Malkin added two goals and two assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Washington Capitals 7-4 on Friday night. Bryan Rust, Carl Hagelin, and Patric Hornqvist also scored for Pittsburgh, which won its fourth straight and seventh consecutive home game. Sidney Crosby had two assists to extend his scoring streak to 11 games. Matt Murray made 29 saves, while Alex Ovechkin scored twice and Dmitry Orlov and Evgeny Kuznetzov also scored for Washington. Holtby made 27 saves but was pulled after three goals in the opening 8 minutes of the third period. The Penguins trailed late after Washington erased deficits but never trailed overall, and Kuznetzov tied the game at 3 before Pittsburgh scored again and pulled away. Notes included Pittsburgh’s return of Carter Rowney, several scratches, and a 3-for-4 power play for Pittsburgh versus 0-for-3 for Washington.

The passage describes ways to access and trade Australian financial markets, including ETFs (such as EWA), American Depository Receipts (ADRs), direct stock trading via international brokers, and stock CFDs via Australian CFD brokers. It discusses backtesting trading strategies using EWA as a proxy for the Australian stock market, noting that commodity exposure can make mean reversion and certain classical strategies (e.g., 200-day moving average, Golden Cross) less efficient. It highlights that seasonal “Santa Claus effect” trading rules for Australian stocks have shown strong performance since 1996, with a 92% win rate and an average gain per trade of 2.4%, though based on a small sample. The passage also covers market structure and hours for Australia’s ASX, exchange information, examples of currency trading pairs involving AUD, and the currency ETF FXA for AUD/USD exposure, as well as information about other Australian ETF types for investors in the US.

The passage discusses values education in society and education, outlining five approaches to values education and various teaching methods. It argues that distance education, supported by technology and online tools, can be advantageous for continuously learning values, with studies suggesting values education can be conducted via distance or hybrid learning, though some teachers report it is less effective in online Social Sciences classes. The literature also notes limited research and a lack of existing scales for values education through distance education.  

To address this, the study aims to develop a valid and reliable scale measuring prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. The descriptive survey involved 341 prospective teachers (Gazi University), using steps based on DeVellis (2017): generating an item pool from literature and participant compositions, expert review, a pilot study (n=30), and data analysis (SPSS 22). Exploratory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure (“Necessity and Usefulness” and “Feasibility”) using 36 items (15 negative, 21 positive), with the scale explaining 63.286% of total variance. Reliability was reported as Cronbach’s alpha of .969 and .961 for the two factors, with additional item analysis and factor correlation results. The authors conclude the scale provides valid and reliable measurements and note limitations regarding participant gender distribution and sample scope (Gazi University).

The email forwards Indian press newsclips about the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) and its power purchase agreement (PPA) dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). Multiple reports say DPC’s board authorized its managing director Neil McGregor (and Enron India’s K Wade Cline) to issue a preliminary termination notice to MSEB, following an internal vote where MSEB representatives were not allowed to vote due to being an interested party and IDBI cast the opposition vote. Other reports describe international lenders urging against terminating and instead favoring renegotiation, while some domestic lenders oppose termination and say further funding depends on India assuring payment mechanisms. MSEB is reported to have made “protest payments” of Rs 134 crore toward its March bill despite disputes over amounts, and the Indian and state governments plan or consider appointing committees to renegotiate the PPA terms. Reports also discuss potential liabilities for the government if termination proceeds, including estimates of a termination fee and amounts tied to future electricity bills.

A law enforcement official said Stephen Paddock’s arsenal included tracer rounds that illuminate a bullet’s path in the dark, potentially improving firing accuracy, though it was unclear if he used them in the Las Vegas massacre that killed 58 people and injured nearly 500. The official said Paddock bought 1,000 rounds of .308- and .223-caliber tracer ammunition from a private buyer he met at a Phoenix gun show. The passage also describes Paddock’s preparations, including requesting an upper-floor room, stockpiling 23 guns, modifying some weapons for continuous fire, and setting up cameras. Authorities said he booked rooms overlooking other major festivals earlier in 2017, and investigators have not determined what drove him to violence. Paddock died by suicide as police closed in, and federal officials said they are looking into whether he planned additional attacks, including a possible car bombing.

Defending against tall or wide body post players requires special team defensive adjustments. The passer must be guarded with active hands and maximum pressure, while helpside players sag off to provide strong backside help, including coordinated execution of post traps. Post defense is played before the post receives the ball, forcing the post to adjust and set up outside their normal area. Tactics include pushing off the block and away from the basket, using front or “face guard” coverage to deny and attack the passing lane, and influencing the ball away from the post player’s preferred “go to” side by forcing them to operate from their weakest side. Post disruptions include extending the court and pressing full court, where press breaks against a full court press require the post to move away from the basket. Defenses also include using a two-three zone and making adjustments to create double or triple teams on the low post player, as well as using a diamond-and-one combination with a chaser fronting or facing the post.

The passage is an excerpt from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2017. It includes the document’s index and financial statements: consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income, balance sheets, and cash flows for the three and six months ended June 30, 2017 (and comparable 2016 periods). It also describes accounting policies and estimates, cash and marketable securities fair value hierarchy and pledges, commitments and contingencies (including leases, the Whole Foods acquisition agreement, and legal and tax-related contingencies), acquisitions and goodwill activity, long-term debt and credit facilities, stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation, income tax provisions and contingencies, and segment information (North America, International, and AWS), along with management’s discussion of forward-looking statements, liquidity and capital resources, and results of operations.

Justice Babatunde Quadri of the Federal High Court, Abuja, admitted EFCC documents as evidence against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, who is on trial for allegedly concealing $300,000 while attempting to board a flight to Dubai. The offence relates to Nigeria’s Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act regarding declaration of cash or negotiable instruments over $10,000. At a resumed hearing, EFCC counsel presented PW4 Hassan Mohammed Misau, a detective with the EFCC’s Advance Fraud Unit, who testified that Nigerian Customs Service reported Li’s arrest at Nnamdi Azikwe International Airport on March 15, 2018. Misau said EFCC investigators followed up, received statements and handover notes from customs officers, and collected items including boarding passes, a Chinese passport, a mobile handset, and the $300,000, then brought them to the EFCC. He added that Li was handed over to the EFCC on March 16, 2018.

Aledo leads the Ryan Raiders 2-0 early in a Friday night game in Denton, Texas. The Sporting News notes Aledo is ranked in its Top 25, is No. 16 in the Massey Ratings, and is No. 28 overall. The scoring started when Ryan was called for intentional grounding in its own end zone, resulting in Aledo being awarded a safety. The passage describes key historian sources and published documentation for U.S. foreign relations toward the Soviet Union for January 1983–March 1985, including White House staff and office files at the Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat files, NSC staff files, Department of State Executive Secretariat “Lot” files, and additional Department of State cable records. It also notes that some declassified NSDD texts are available on the Reagan Presidential Library website and that additional documents are increasingly available online via the Office of the Historian. The passage then shifts to a note explaining, using declassified documents, how procedures for planning and approving U.S. covert actions and special intelligence operations developed across Truman through Carter presidencies, beginning with NSC authorization in December 1947 and a 1948 NSC directive (NSC 10/2) that broadened covert action from psychological operations and defined covert activities and their plausible deniability.

Children of obese women have double the chance of being obese by age two compared with children born to women with a recommended BMI, and childhood obesity is also strongly linked with obesity in fathers. The passage says egg and sperm cells carry molecules that respond to parents’ nutritional intake, which can shape offspring characteristics and obesity risk. Mothers’ BMI at conception is most strongly associated with childhood obesity, and fathers’ BMI relates to birthweight and later body fat increases in children. It also discusses that sperm carry non-coding RNAs that differ in obese male mice and can make offspring fatter, and that egg mitochondria are defective in obese females, affecting offspring metabolism and increasing lifelong susceptibility to obesity and diabetes. The passage further states that embryos are “plastic” and can respond to negative and positive inputs, and that diet and exercise interventions in obese mice can improve egg or sperm quality and stop transmission of obesity to offspring. It notes limited human data, including findings after maternal gastric banding, and calls for clearer advice and research on interventions for obese mothers and expanded approaches for fathers, alongside preventing obesity in adolescents and young adults.

VentureWire’s October 19, 2000 issue reports private company business news and venture capital updates. Top stories include St. Paul Venture Capital closing a $1.3 billion sixth fund focused on early-stage investments; idealab! postponing its IPO due to market volatility; Constellation Ventures closing a new $350 million fund for digitally delivered content; and New Edge Networks raising $139.9 million in its third round. Additional sections cover podcast compatibility (MP3 with appropriate bit rate), handling missing ID3 tag information, and provide support and warranty terms, licensing notices related to Microsoft WM-DRM, the SanDisk end user license agreement, and disposal instructions.

The passage explains that football has become offense-first, making accurate passing a key driver of offensive success. It describes cornerbacks as defenders whose main job is to cover opposing wide receivers, especially in one-on-one situations, by mirroring their movements and staying with them throughout plays. The passage lists skills such as speed, agility, backpedaling followed by sprinting, and turning quickly, and says cornerbacks also help as run defenders. It concludes that cornerbacks are important because strong coverage limits offensive advantages, can force quarterback hesitation, supports pass pressure, and enables defensive schemes; it also references “Revis Island” as a nickname for Darrell Revis’s ability to shut down receivers one-on-one.

The passage is a roundup of biotech news items, including Novo Nordisk’s plan to buy Akero Therapeutics for up to $5.2 billion to develop a treatment for MASH (liver disease). The passage provides an injury update on Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb. David Jones has dropped model Jesinta Franklin after two years, saying it has not renewed her contract and is “taking another direction.” The retailer announced Victoria’s Secret model Victoria Lee as its newest ambassador.
