A pharmacist, Zameer Ghumra of Leicester, was jailed for six years for disseminating “terrorist propaganda” to primary school-age children. The court heard he posted pro-ISIS content on social media and showed a graphic Twitter beheading video to a child, telling boys they had a duty to kill people who insulted Islam. Judge Gregory Dickinson said the actions were a determined effort to radicalise children and were particularly serious due to the targeting of children; he also cited an absence of remorse. The court heard one boy had post-traumatic stress disorder and another was having difficulty sleeping and was afraid of snipers. The conviction related to conduct between January 2013 and September 2014.

The passage explains how soccer goal kicks work and how teams can defend them. A goal kick is taken when the ball is kicked over the defenders’ end line after last being touched by an attacking player, from anywhere within the goal area with the ball stationary; the ball becomes live when kicked and moves. The defending team must position players outside the penalty area until the kick is taken, and if opponents inside the penalty area touch or challenge the ball before it is in play, the kick is retaken. It outlines general defensive tactics such as positioning defenders to cover receivers, pressing to win the ball, and transitioning to attack if possession is won. It also describes role positioning for strikers, midfielders, and backs, plus different approaches for “ball won” and “ball not won” situations. For youth play, it discusses smaller field dimensions and the use of “build-out/retreat lines,” including example goal-kick progressions and coaching reminders. For older youth and adults, it describes expanding target and pass options and notes that goal kicks are restart opportunities with direct scoring possible. The passage ends with coaching tips such as reacting quickly, maintaining awareness of the ball, scouting opponents’ tendencies, and drilling against all goal-kick options.

The passage summarizes a backtest of Larry Connors’ 3-day high/low method/strategy, originally revealed in his 2009 book “High Probability ETF Trading” and tested from ETF inception through the end of 2008 using the 20 most popular ETFs by volume. Connors’ strategy is described as buying an ETF when it has made lower highs and lower lows for three consecutive days, following specific criteria including the close being above the 200-day moving average and below the 5-day moving average, and using a dynamic exit based on moving averages. The passage states that 13 of 20 ETFs performed worse since the original test, and that a portfolio approach (using 25 ETFs with a maximum of 5 open positions and 20% equity allocation per position) produced compounded results, with the worst drawdown occurring at the end of July 2011 during the EU debt crisis. It concludes that the strategy appears to have deteriorated somewhat but still shows some promise.

Nippon Express said one of its employees falsified inspection stamps on government-stockpiled rice it stored, a case involving quality check misconduct. Mitsubishi Corp., which entrusted Nippon Express with the storage, said it received a business improvement order from the farm ministry in May and reported preventive steps on Monday. Mitsubishi said 15 bags (30 kilograms each) were shipped to a livestock feed factory with no reports of health damage, and the rest will be incinerated with none sent for human consumption. Nippon Express said the employee falsified stamps in Hiroshima on 15 container bags whose original bags had become wet after rain in June 2014; it also said similar misconduct affected 251 container bags changed after the original bags tore in February 2015 and around September 2016. The statement said the government stockpiles about 1 million tons of rice for emergencies.

The passage discusses NewMarket Corp. (NYSE:NEU), a specialty chemical company with its Afton Chemical business as the main source of revenue and cash flow, making additives for transportation fuels and lubricants. It notes strong EBITDA margins, cash flows, and returns on capital, and shareholder returns, but also a high share price, thin trading volume, and minimal sell-side coverage due to a lack of stock splits. The passage says growth has been weak, including sales down about 12% from 2014 to 2016, driven by improved vehicle efficiency and longer intervals between oil changes, as well as diesel additive mix not being NewMarket’s focus. It describes the acquisition of Aditivos Mexicanos for about $183 million and the construction of a new Singapore plant, and argues these moves may improve growth prospects by increasing exposure to emerging markets and potentially diesel additives. The passage highlights R&D spending and product development efforts, and projects around 3% long-term revenue growth, improved free cash flow after the Singapore plant, and low-double-digit FCF margins. It concludes that valuation methods do not indicate NewMarket is undervalued and suggests the current price already reflects expected cash-flow growth, making it challenging to justify a new position without business diversification.

Expenses incurred during the voyage for specified misdemeanors or disabilities, or for desertion or disobedient mutinous conduct, are charged to the responsible individual(s). If a master finds an officer or seaman incompetent or indisposed after a fair trial, the master may displace them, reduce their lay accordingly, and increase the lay of any promoted successor after final voyage adjustment. If sickness or death prevents performance, legal representatives receive a portion of the stipulated share based on time served. Officers and seamen must account for vessel apparel, furniture, or stores entrusted to them, replacing losses or damages from carelessness or neglect, and those appointed to handle cargo or stores in boats or lighters must ensure safe landing or delivery. Officers and seamen who perform the voyage properly and commit no dishonest or unlawful acts receive payment in San Francisco for their share of the catch on return at stated rates for whale oil, sperm oil, and whalebone, with whale-bone rates depending on whether the fleet totals exceed 200 whales. The parties agree to the duties and obligations, including boarding by a master-ordered time, limiting distilled spirituous liquor to strictly medical use, and not taking certain articles as private stores or for traffic; violation forfeits the violator’s entire share to the owners. The passage also includes certification documents copied from government files, including a deputy collector’s certificate and a Secretary of State certification dated September 1, 1900.

The Bifrost subsea cable system, a 20,000-kilometre link between Singapore and the U.S. West Coast, is set to begin commercial operations. The $760 million project, led by Keppel with Meta and Telin Indonesia, is built by Alcatel Submarine Networks and connects Singapore to Guam and Grover Beach, California, with branches to Jakarta, Manado, Davao and Winema, Oregon. It uses dynamic routing and redundancy, is expected to provide over 260 terabits per second capacity and about 165 milliseconds end-to-end latency, and faced delays due to weather and regulatory challenges in Indonesia before the Jakarta landing station was completed in mid-2024. Once operational, it aims to upgrade regional bandwidth, support growing cloud, AI and content-delivery demand, and provide an alternative and more resilient route for data traffic in Southeast Asia.

After Irrfan Khan revealed he was diagnosed with a rare disease, he told fans he would update them about his condition. He later said he has a neuro-endocrine tumor and that he recently traveled to London for treatment. He shared an inspiring poem on Instagram. During this time, the film fraternity requested privacy for his family. His film *Blackmail* is set to release, and Vishal Bhardwaj’s movie has been announced to be rescheduled until Irrfan returns.

The passage describes how Industry 4.0 and digitalization are changing work and education, leading to the development of “Education 4.0,” which emphasizes updated curricula, digital transformation, personalized and blended learning, and lifelong learning. It reviews research on digital competences and job skills, including the World Economic Forum’s top job skills for 2050 grouped into problem-solving, self-management, working with people, and technology use and development.  

The study reports analyses of survey data from 147 second-year undergraduate students at a Hungarian university (engineering vs. technical management) conducted in 2019–2021. Using SPSS and CHAID decision tree methods, the study tests three hypotheses about differences in students’ soft-skill priorities, expectations of higher education, and perceived career success factors. Results show both faculties prioritize skills such as problem solving and knowledge related to specialization, with significant differences in several specific skill choices. For studying abroad (Erasmus/Stipendium Hungaricum), most students value improved language skills, and preferences vary by faculty. The study also examines students’ perceptions of how higher education contributes to career success and finds generally indecisive but generally positive views overall. The authors report limitations due to non-probabilistic sampling and a limited sample size, and they suggest further research with broader samples and more industry involvement. The conclusion states that Education 4.0 is relevant to students’ learning preferences and that engineering and technical management students emphasize different skill areas, with universities needing to adapt curricula to develop both hard and soft skills.

Plymouth Argyle beat Gillingham 2-1 on Saturday with goals from Joel Grant and Toumani Diagouraga in the 90th minute. The win drew Argyle level on points with Gillingham, lifted them off the bottom of League One, and reduced their gap to safety to three points, though they remain in the bottom four on goal difference. The article highlights three positives and negatives: the return of striker Ryan Taylor, a successful DJM takeover at Home Park that drew about 2,700 young players and coaches, and Argyle’s improving form with four wins and a draw from their last seven games. It also notes key negatives including a goalkeeper crisis that has required seven different goalkeepers and a season of inconsistency from Graham Carey.

Petronas is pitching an estimated $1 billion stake in Malaysia’s SK316 offshore gas block in Sarawak to potential bidders, including Shell, ExxonMobil, PTTEP and Japanese firms. Sources say Petronas has begun providing financial and operational data and expects bids in the next few weeks, aiming to lower operating expenses and manage the low oil price environment. Petronas said it is seeking partners via its subsidiary Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd to bring technology and capabilities to explore, develop and operate fields in SK316. Gas from the SK316 NC3 field feeds Petronas’ LNG export project LNG 9, and funds from a stake sale could be used to develop the Kasawari field, which has high CO2 content. Individual company responses were not known, and ExxonMobil and Shell declined to comment, while PTTEP said it is keen to invest in Southeast Asia.

The passage discusses racial disparities in income and wealth in the U.S. and in Durham, noting that while income gaps exist, wealth disparities are much larger. It cites 2014 median family income nationally as $71,300 for whites versus $43,300 for blacks, and 2015 median family wealth as $171,000 for white families versus $17,600 for black families. The passage links part of the wealth gap to differences in homeownership, stating that 73% of whites owned primary residences compared with 45% of blacks. It argues that monthly mortgage payments and homeownership help people save and build equity, and describes experiences from interviewing very low-income residents who preferred owning even basic housing. The passage criticizes some Durham “affordable housing” approaches as creating units with little or no equity for residents and adds that dilapidated structures are torn down over time. It proposes alternatives, including Habitat for Humanity partnerships for lower-cost units with immediate equity, housing improvement support to help homeowners maintain their equity, Preservation Durham’s program to help owners in historically black neighborhoods, and property tax circuit-breakers to postpone taxes. It concludes that focusing on helping people keep and improve existing housing would improve the housing stock and help reduce racial wealth disparities.

Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, are leaving Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft for Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe. The group specializes in collateralized loan obligations and asset-backed lending and will join Orrick’s offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Bloomberg Law reported that the partner exits included 33 partners leaving since the beginning of the year, and it noted Orrick announcements and additional partner moves described as special counsel on LinkedIn. The article said Cadwalader faces a choice between staying the course or shaking up its business model and possibly considering a merger, citing lagging revenue ranking and sensitivity of its capital markets and finance practices to interest rates and macroeconomic trends, while noting strong profits per equity partner and the desirability of its talent. Bloomberg concluded Cadwalader appears to be pursuing a shake-up, including adding a second managing partner and other hires, but reported the firm has lost nearly a fifth of its partnership this year.

A Year 7 student at Sydney Secondary College in Balmain was suspended after anti-Semitic bullying that included a Nazi salute. The incident on June 25 followed at least a month of bullying, and parents of 18 students were contacted. Two ringleaders were suspended, and three other students were disciplined for racist behavior, with parents informed and students addressed by an anti-racism contact officer. Counselling and support were offered to affected students. The New South Wales Jewish Board of Deputies said the school acted correctly, and noted students demonstrated disregard for Nazi atrocities. The school has a roll of 785, with 41% of students speaking a language other than English at home.

The passage discusses adult illiteracy as an issue that has been widely discussed in the past but is less talked about now, including in the “first world.” It says Idris Elba, who works with Project Literacy, gave a Fox News interview about the crisis. Elba highlights problems with diversity, calls adult illiteracy a worldwide issue that is hard to admit and often undetectable, and describes partnering through Project Literacy with Wanda Steward, an illiterate mother whose stories were adapted into a children’s book. He also talks about teaching his children to read, noting that many young people cannot read or write and that illiteracy is linked with people in jail, and he expresses passion for raising awareness. The author agrees that millions of Americans may struggle with reading and writing and reflects on personal feelings about reading.

The passage compiles May 30, 2001 news about the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) dispute involving the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC), and the Union government. It reports that the Centre sought a 60-day extension of the conciliation period for settling MSEB’s payment of the December 2000 bill. MERC issued injunctions restraining DPC from proceeding with arbitration and from operating MSEB’s escrow account until June 14. MSEB stopped buying power from DPC from noon on Tuesday after rescinding the power purchase agreement (PPA), and subsequent actions affected the commissioning schedule for Dabhol Phase II. The Union government also submitted proposals and said it would facilitate resolution, while stating it would not buy power from the project. DPC offered to hold talks with MSEB on a 10% tariff reduction, and Indian lenders planned meetings to coordinate with offshore lenders and request restraint.

Board trustees of the Newfoundland and Labrador English School District voted Saturday to keep five rural schools open, despite low enrolment and cost-management efforts. The district said closing the schools would save the province $1.7 million annually, but trustees disagreed; board chair Goronwy Price said a motion to close the schools was defeated and that reviews will restart. One closure was approved: H.L. Strong Academy in Little Bay Islands, which has no students and no expected enrolment. Appalachia High School will be consolidated with Our Lady of Mercy Elementary. The four schools remaining open are LeGallish Memorial, Swift Current Academy, James Cook Memorial, and Leading Tickles Primary, with LaGallish having 47 students. Trustees cited concerns about student safety.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 2, 2017, reporting that it released its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2017 by posting its Second Quarter 2017 Shareholder Letter on its website. The shareholder letter is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing states this information is intended to be furnished under Item 2.02 and is not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Deepak Ahuja, Chief Financial Officer, on August 2, 2017.

The passage argues that slavery is often overlooked in discussions of pedagogy and that Foucault’s theory of panopticism can help explain how surveillance links slavery and pedagogy through extraction, capitalist imperatives, and power. It describes Foucault’s view of surveillance as inherent to teaching and education, connects surveillance to racial surveillance and the history of slavery, and notes debates about Foucault’s engagement with race and slavery. The text then develops the concepts of “surveillance textualization” and “surveillance pedagogy,” explaining how examination, writing, record-keeping, and digitalization encode human experiences as texts/data that enable monitoring, management, and behavior conditioning. It further situates these processes within surveillance capitalism, where digital technologies extract and monetize personal data while concentrating control in the hands of platforms and “surveillance capitalists,” potentially shaping education without full oversight. Finally, it claims that these extractive and disciplinary dynamics connect historical slavery to contemporary educational technologies and urges more attention to slavery in pedagogical discourse, especially as digital surveillance expands.

The order appealed from was reversed, awarding the appellant ten dollars in costs and disbursements to be paid by the respondents, as committee, out of the estate they held. The opinion was delivered by Smith, J.

The paper examines “personal attention” ASMR YouTube videos and explains that ASMR is a term for tingling sensations triggered by auditory, visual, or haptic stimuli, often described as pleasurable and relaxing. It discusses how ASMRtists create high-definition videos, frequently using role-play to simulate personalized, intimate encounters. Using affect and performance studies, the essay analyzes these videos with Olivia Kissper as a case study, arguing that media infrastructures produce the “incarnation of sexuality” through mediated intimacy. It proposes a redefinition of sexuality centered on affect, and suggests that consuming ASMR videos can be understood as a sexual practice and as a sexual relation involving the ASMRtist, viewer-listener, and digital technology.

The Superior Court of Pennsylvania reviewed Clay Williams’s appeal from a December 5, 2006 judgment of sentence that imposed life in prison without parole for first-degree murder. The court also denied Williams’s petition for remand to develop the record, affirmed the judgment of sentence, and dismissed his ineffective assistance of counsel claims without prejudice for collateral review. A jury found Williams guilty of first-degree murder, robbery, firearms not to be carried without a license, carrying firearms on a public street or public property, and possessing instruments of crime. The trial court had summarized evidence that Williams confronted a store customer, demanded a cell phone with intent to rob, left, returned, and shot the customer, after which police recovered the shotgun used. On appeal, the court determined several issues were waived due to inadequately specific or developed claims, including a suppression claim and a sufficiency-of-the-evidence challenge. It declined to reach trial counsel effectiveness on the merits because no evidentiary hearing or developed record addressed those claims, and it denied Williams’s remand petition regarding a juror disclosure, finding the matter adequately developed.

Heroin users experience a high and increasing burden of respiratory symptoms and lung function decline, beyond normal age-related decline seen in tobacco smokers with COPD. This burden has been linked to multiple risk factors, including HIV infection, pulmonary tuberculosis, and undernutrition, and heroin users often have a history of polysubstance use. Heroin can be injected or smoked; injection is associated with harmful effects such as bloodborne infections and lung fibrosis, while smoking can lead to airway damage, airflow obstruction, and respiratory depression. Methadone use for heroin use disorder is described as potentially aggravating lung function decline, and heroin users have higher rates of HIV infection, undernutrition, and pulmonary TB than the general population.

In a quantitative cross-sectional study at Muhimbili National Hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (May 2022–July 2023), 310 clients on methadone maintenance were enrolled and 302 completed spirometry. Lung function decline occurred in 28.5% of participants, with restrictive lung disease being the most common pattern (13.2%). The mean age at onset of lung function decline was 44 years. Independent risk factors for lung function decline were underweight (aOR 4.73), HIV infection (aOR 2.61), and history of pulmonary TB (aOR 2.48). The study concludes that routine lung function screening should be included at MAT clinics to address undiagnosed and underdiagnosed lung diseases.

The passage explains the importance of understanding and predicting ocean currents and describes how ocean drifters are used to measure flow. It notes that most existing drifter placement campaigns use either space-filling designs or ad-hoc criteria, and that an active learning placement strategy has not yet been presented. It proposes BALLAST, an active learning methodology for placing Lagrangian observers, using a spatio-temporal vector-output Gaussian process surrogate and an information-theoretic utility for sequential placement, with efficient implementation via an SPDE-based GP approach. The contributions listed are introducing active learning to Lagrangian observer placement, proposing BALLAST, and developing a GP posterior sampling method that combines standard GP regression with SPDE for efficient utility computation. The passage then outlines notation and the framework for sequential experimental design using an expected information gain (EIG) utility based on entropy reduction, and describes modeling the time-dependent vector field with a spatio-temporal Helmholtz-kernel GP with a separable temporal kernel. It further defines an active learning loop that selects observer placement locations to maximize information gain of the full vector field surrogate using noisy velocity observations.

On May 25, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. shareholders approved a 20-for-1 split of the company’s common stock and a proportionate increase in the number of authorized shares. The amendment became effective on May 27, 2022 upon filing with the Delaware Secretary of State, and trading was expected to begin on a split-adjusted basis on June 6, 2022. The report also summarizes results from the company’s Annual Meeting of Shareholders, including director elections, ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2022, approval of an advisory vote on named executive officer compensation, approval of the stock split amendment by shareholders, and multiple shareholder proposals that were not approved.

Ontario’s education funding formula includes a “learning opportunities grant” of about $179 per student for schools in needy areas, while school fundraising brings in an average of $280 per student. A report commissioned by the Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario says school-based fundraising reverses the impact of the grant, with boards receiving less grant money raising more than the $280 average and boards receiving more grant money raising much less. The report also states that since 1997, when the funding formula was introduced, multiple areas of need have been underfunded for two decades, even with additional spending for class size reductions and full-day kindergarten. The union says changes have been inadequate, points to persistent special education funding concerns, and describes a June move of an extra $219 million to hire additional teachers and education workers, while it recommends further funding increases and regular evaluations.

The passage recommends unfolding a Galaxy Fold or viewing it in full screen for the best experience. It discusses the Citi Simplicity® Card, highlighting a 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and no annual fee. It also mentions a 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases, followed by a variable APR of 17.99%–28.74% based on creditworthiness. Balance transfers must be completed within 4 months of account opening, with intro balance transfer fees of 3% (minimum $5) during the first 4 months and 5% (minimum $5) afterward. The passage states there are no late fees and no penalty rate, and notes a recommended credit score range of 670–850, while approval is not guaranteed.

Joe Ezeokeke appeals his 138-month sentence for possession of cocaine with intent to distribute, arguing the district court erred in adjusting his offense level for obstruction of justice under U.S. Sentencing Guidelines § 3C1.1 and that his sentence was substantively unreasonable. The appellate court states that the district court adopted the PSR’s factual findings, which supported the obstruction adjustment based on the record indicating Ezeokeke testified falsely about several matters relevant to the case. The court concludes the district court did not err in making the adjustment and that Ezeokeke failed to rebut the presumption of correctness for his within-range sentence. The sentence is affirmed.

The study examined how long-term visit-to-visit blood pressure (BP) variability relates to cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) in 1,284 participants from the Kailuan cohort (2006–2022), using MRI measures of white matter hyperintensities (WMH), lacunae (LA), cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and visible perivascular spaces (PVS). BP variability of systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and pulse pressure (PP) was categorized into low, middle, or high groups, and cSVD burden was rated as non, mild, moderate, or severe. High SBP variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and PVS; DBP variability was associated with LA; and PP variability was associated with higher risk of moderate/severe cSVD burden, LA, and PVS. Age and hypertension status modified these associations, with PP variability showing notable effects in participants under 60 years old, and BP variability effects being more significant in participants with hypertension. The authors conclude that higher long-term BP variability is an independent risk factor for total cSVD burden, LA, and PVS, especially in people with hypertension, and that PP variability may be particularly important in young adults.

The password protection feature lets a host lock a card by providing a password, which is later used to unlock it. The password and its size are stored in 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, and optionally Force Erase Password can be stored in additional FEP and FEP_LEN registers when Card Ownership Protection is supported; these registers are non-volatile. Locked cards execute commands in basic class (class 0), ACMD41, CMD16, and the lock card command class, allowing reset/initialize/select/status queries but not data access. If a password was previously set (PWD_LEN not 0), the card locks automatically after power on. Lock/unlock commands are available only in transfer state, require the card to be selected first, and use the structure and bus transaction type of a regular single block write; the data block carries all command information including password setting mode and lock/unlock details.

The session discusses “Payments, Part 2,” beginning with the 10th anniversary of bitcoin and several statistics about its price, size, and network activity. The discussion then focuses on payment-system pain points—such as too many intermediaries, high costs, slow settlement (especially for merchants), and issues like chargebacks, privacy, cybersecurity, and financial inclusion—and whether blockchain can address them. Attendees also consider blockchain’s potential drawbacks, including added issues like scalability, interoperability, error resolution trade-offs, governance, regulation (anti–money laundering), and liquidity/latency effects. The class debates finality versus delayed settlement, blockchain suitability for payments (ledgers and verification cost), and smart contracts’ possibilities and limitations relative to existing payment systems. The discussion covers payment use cases and companies (e.g., BitPay, exchanges, and institutional infrastructure), cross-border payments via “bridge” crypto/technology (e.g., Ripple-related concepts), associated liquidity/volatility risks, and practical adoption constraints. It concludes by framing the course’s goal of evaluating when append-only logs with consensus (blockchain) are appropriate, and it announces the next session will cover central bank digital currencies.

The passage includes an ESD caution stating that the integrated circuit can be damaged by electrostatic discharge and that Texas Instruments recommends handling with appropriate precautions; improper handling and installation can cause damage, ranging from subtle performance degradation to complete device failure. It also contains a revision history for a document revised from November 1, 2024 to April 30, 2025, listing multiple updates such as added PSA-L1 certification targeting notes, changes to feature descriptions and device comparison tables, and updates to electrical and timing specifications. The passage further notes that mechanical, packaging, and orderable information follows, is subject to change without notice, and includes disclaimers and instructions for use of Texas Instruments resources.

The passage explains Bollinger Bands and a ChatGPT-created Bollinger Bands trading strategy that was backtested in Python. It describes Bollinger Bands as three lines based on a simple moving average and standard deviations, with customizable periods and deviations, and notes the strategy uses a squeeze condition where Bollinger Bands fall inside Keltner Channels (which use ATR; 2 times ATR). Trading rules are presented: buy and hold when the lower Bollinger Band is above the Keltner lower band and the upper Bollinger Band is under the Keltner upper band, and sell if either condition is not met. The backtest starts from SPY inception in 1993 using unadjusted data (no dividends or splits) and results are described as poorly performing, with low, erratic returns and high drawdown; adjusting returns for time in the market improves results only slightly, and maximum drawdown decreases.

The passage is an article ranking Taylor Swift’s top breakup songs, ordered from 20 in ascending order, and provides brief descriptions of several tracks across her albums. It discusses themes such as heartbreak, regret, anger, resignation, yearning, and relief, and highlights specific songs and details including release timing (e.g., “Should’ve Said No” as a 2008 single; “You're Losing Me” as a 2023 vault track), songwriting context, production or performance background (e.g., “Better Man” offered to Little Big Town; “Better Man” updated version co-produced by Aaron Dessner), lyrical imagery and tone (e.g., “How Did It End?” described as a “lovers' autopsy”; “Forever & Always” as an escalation from sad melody to anger), and chart/award outcomes mentioned for some recordings. The passage also notes that newer songs from “The Tortured Poets Department” are included in the ranking and that other tracks draw on relationship aftermath, missed feelings, and complicated closure.

Sheree Coffman, a Student Assistance Counselor for Northmont High School, spoke to the Northmont Rotary about the Student Assistance Program and her role in supporting Northmont City Schools’ mission. The program aims to identify and help troubled students whose difficulties may stem from issues such as family crises, depression, substance abuse, or relationship problems. The passage describes why early identification and intervention are important and outlines Northmont’s three-part prevention approach: UNIVERSAL prevention (including U.N.I.T.Y. Day), TARGETED support for at-risk students (such as Reality Club), and INDICATED interventions for individuals showing early signs. It also lists programs including an Alternative to Expulsion Program, Peer Facilitation, SADD, and small groups for grief support and coping, and highlights U.N.I.T.Y. Day (“Be the Change”) as a major program designed to build understanding and belonging. The passage notes that U.N.I.T.Y. Day has involved over 400 students, 60 small group leaders, and 60 high school mentors over the past three years, with activities spanning four days.

Ocwen Financial disclosed that it reached a servicing settlement with Connecticut, bringing the total number of settlements to 28 of the 31 states that took regulatory action over alleged escrow and other servicing issues. The Connecticut settlement is similar to earlier agreements that restrict Ocwen from acquiring new residential mortgage servicing rights until April 30, 2018 and require it to move away from its REALServicing platform to Black Knight’s platform. The Connecticut settlement also requires additional communications and review and reporting obligations for Connecticut borrowers, and includes a $500,000 fine for noncompliance. Ocwen said it is continuing to seek resolutions with the remaining regulators and two state attorneys general.

Geologists in western Queensland have found evidence of rare minerals, including platinum, gold, and rare earth elements, linked to geological pipe structures. The Diamantina Minerals Province is described as spanning from Fifield in central New South Wales through north-west Queensland to the Merlin diamond mine in the Northern Territory. The pipes, previously found in countries including South Africa and Brazil, could be up to six kilometres in diameter and may contain minerals such as scandium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements, along with potential for diamonds. The minerals are said to be in global demand for technologies including fuel cells, mobile phones, superconducting magnets, and hybrid vehicle batteries, and rare earth supply is predicted to face critical shortages in the next 10–15 years.

VentureWire People (Friday, May 25, 2001) reports executive changes and staffing moves across multiple companies, including promotions and CEO appointments at GlobalLearningSystems, TeaLeaf Technology, Coremetrics, and hi-flier. It also lists VC personnel updates at Lloyds TSB Development Capital, Insight Capital Partners, and Willis Stein & Partners. Additional entries cover marketing & sales, operations, and technology appointments for several companies. The newsletter further includes an “EXECUTIVE SEARCHES” section with job listings for CMO/EVP Marketing, CFO roles, sales and business development positions, and several other executive-level openings. VentureWire notes it will take a break for Memorial Day, with the next issue on Tuesday, May 29.

Paolo Alli, President of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, said in Tbilisi that territorial integrity and the inviolability of borders are key conditions and a fundamental principle of cooperation with NATO. He discussed reforms in Georgia’s armed forces and said they support Georgia’s integration into NATO, noting NATO’s support based on international law. Alli also stressed increased NATO expenses, including a proposed membership fee of 2% of GDP, and addressed cybercrime, misinformation, food and climate change, and economic security. Georgian officials spoke on Georgia’s Euro-Atlantic integration, and the session is set to adopt a declaration supporting Georgia’s Euro-Atlantic integration.

A newlywed bride, Sarah Illig, said she was almost mauled by a shark during a honeymoon resort attraction in the Caribbean, losing little more than an arm injury. She described feeling water and a clamp on her arm, quickly realizing it hurt when she saw a shark latched on, then pulling away and getting out. Footage was captured by her husband, Evan Carroll, who posted photos of the bloody aftermath on social media. Illig later posted the video on Facebook and Instagram, saying she had flesh wounds but did not need stitches, and reported that her arm was healing. The passage also states shark encounters are rare and typically only occur if provoked, and notes nurse sharks are not considered highly predatory toward humans.

The passage is largely a mix of XBRL/data tags and a large excerpt from NVIDIA’s Form 10-K filing. It includes details such as the fiscal year ended January 26, 2020, NVIDIA’s corporate information (address, incorporation), market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates as of July 26, 2019, and the number of shares outstanding as of February 14, 2020. It also provides the Table of Contents and sections describing NVIDIA’s business, markets, strategies, sales and marketing approach, backlog and seasonality, manufacturing approach (fabless model), working capital management, competition, patents and intellectual property protections, employee counts, and executive officer bios. The excerpt further presents part of the “Risk Factors,” including risks related to market needs and product development, competition, cybersecurity, reliance on third parties for manufacturing, inventory demand forecasting, international operations, executive and employee retention, acquisitions/investments (including Mellanox), legal/IP risks, privacy concerns, and tax liabilities.

Images of the galaxy NGC 4536 show it rapidly turning gas into newborn stars. The photos, captured by the Hubble Space Telescope using its Wide Field Camera 3, depict intense star formation in several regions within the Virgo constellation, about 50 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers say the star formation frenzies are supported by a high concentration of gas, though they are unsure how the galaxy acquired so much. One possibility mentioned is that it obtained the gas during a galactic collision. The passage also notes that starburst-born stars burn quickly and emit ultraviolet light that excites nearby hydrogen atoms and causes nearby gas clouds to appear in blues and yellows.

Kent McFarland will speak on mercury along elevational gradients at Lyndon State College’s Natural Science Weekly Seminar series on February 15 at 4:00 p.m. in Room S-102 of the Thaddeus Fairbanks Science Wing. The free, public Wednesday seminars continue through May 3 and are held at that time and location each week. The release lists additional talks scheduled from February 22 through May 3, and notes the schedule may change.

A copy of the crew list for the bark *Cape Horn Pigeon* (New Bedford), with Thomas Scullan as master, is certified as taken from the original on file by M. Webber, Deputy Collector, dated December 7, 1891. Another certification by John Hay, Secretary of State, states documents annexed are true copies from the Department of State files, dated September 1, 1900. The whalemen’s shipping paper sets terms for the owner, master, officers, seamen, and mariners for a voyage from San Francisco to the North Pacific and Arctic oceans, including service not exceeding twelve months, freight and payment provisions, interest on advances, limits on trade participation, and duties to obey commands, obtain oil cargo, and not leave ship or go ashore without permission. It also requires shipboard regulations recorded daily in the logbook, including breaches such as drunkenness and unauthorized absences, and specifies penalties for officers and seamen relating to women aboard, failure to enforce admission rules, and offenses like drunkenness and intemperance.

The passage discusses arguments and proposals regarding the World Organization’s handling of disputes and the use of military force. It notes that even if some nations do not find the organization’s plans perfect, efforts should continue, with support to prevent future wars enabled by destructive technology. Mr. Grew emphasizes strengthening the inter-American system and asks Mr. Rockefeller to preside in his place. The discussion then begins with paragraph 5 of Chapter II, where Ambassador Mora proposes that states of other continents or regions not be obligated to participate in military operations decided by the Council and Assembly if the disputes do not endanger general world peace and do not affect them directly. Dr. Pasvolsky responds that the proposed charter would require special agreements for armed forces after creation, negotiated among states with Security Council approval, and that the Council must determine whether disputes are local or worldwide. The Ambassador of Mexico argues it is dangerous to leave decisions about dangers to world peace to regional groups, and recommends that any forces used not come from neighboring states to avoid hate and retaliation, citing the League of Nations handling of the Saar plebiscite. He also comments that “continent” is useful geographically but not politically. The Ambassador of Honduras supports extending Inter-American solidarity globally, treating attacks on one republic as attacks on all. Ambassador Mora says the discussion covered his point and leaves the subject open for future consideration; Dr. Pasvolsky suggests later study of new, difficult points. The discussion continues with the Ambassador of Mexico reading relevant articles from the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and noting suggested amendments from memoranda.

Wall Street indexes rose on Monday as technology and energy sectors gained with rising oil prices. Investors weighed an expected U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike later in the week, with markets assigning an 85% probability of a third hike. The market reaction came despite an attempted terrorist attack at a major New York commuter hub that left the suspect and three others wounded. By 2:38 p.m. ET, the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq were all higher. Information technology led S&P sector gains, while financial, consumer staple, and industrial stocks were among the biggest losers. Company moves included CenturyLink rising about 9% after signing a 5-year Pennsylvania contract, and Bluebird Bio up 19% on positive early myeloma study responses. Crypto-related stocks also climbed on the debut of U.S. bitcoin futures, which Reuters said may encourage wider use of cryptocurrency.

Novak Djokovic beat Spanish qualifier Jaume Munar at the French Open in a second-round match, winning 7-6(1) 6-4 6-4 despite frequent wayward shots and a double fault in the opening game. Djokovic said he was not satisfied with his performance and attributed his serving issues to elbow surgery this year, including changing his service motion and racket. After being broken in the ninth game, he continued with air shots instead of taking fluids. Djokovic acknowledged his form is below his desired level and said he is trying not to give up, noting recent struggles in 2018. He will next play Roberto Bautista Agut for a place in the last 16.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 23, 2018 announcing that on January 21, 2018 it granted Elon Musk a 100% performance-based stock option award (the “CEO Performance Award”), subject to stockholder approval by a majority of votes cast, excluding shares owned by Elon Musk or Kimbal Musk. The press release is filed as Exhibit 99.1. Tesla also stated it will file and furnish a proxy statement to stockholders for a special meeting, urging stockholders to read the related materials and noting that copies will be available through the SEC website and from Tesla’s Investor Relations. The filing includes information about solicitation participants and contains forward-looking statement disclaimers, and lists Exhibit 99.1 as the only exhibit.

The Czech crown strengthened against the euro, reversing an early slide to 18-month lows, as the central bank’s commitment to cap the crown value ended on Friday. The CNB said its promise to keep the crown weaker than 27 per euro would expire at the end of the first quarter, and it removed a line indicating the “weak crown regime” would end around mid-year, increasing uncertainty about when the cap could be removed. The crown rebounded from 27.252 to 27.024 by 1338 GMT, while implied forward rates also improved from multi-month lows. Investors expected greater volatility, amid concerns that accumulated crown buying positions could affect demand after the cap is gone. Czech bond yields were mixed after a 10 basis point yield fall, while other Central European bond markets were generally bullish; the forint firmed slightly versus the euro and the zloty eased but stayed near 17-month highs.

The court addresses whether an employee’s sick time and employer-paid wages for personal days and family illness are collateral sources that must be disclosed and credited against an award for lost wages under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97. The plaintiff, injured in an automobile accident, seeks lost-wage compensation, while the defendant argues the sick and paid-day benefits should be treated as collateral sources and deducted. The court explains the statute’s purpose is to prevent duplicate recovery and deduct overlapping benefits, but holds that sick pay and compensation for personal and family illness days are not collateral-source benefits within the statute. The court reasons that the plaintiff earned the sick leave as part of employee compensation and, due to the defendant’s actions, had to exhaust those benefits, leaving them unavailable for future illness or retirement cash-out. Therefore, the benefits cannot be used as a set-off against lost wages compensation.

The passage argues that Ontario’s education model excludes disabled and marginalized students, despite claims of inclusive education. It discusses how “special education” has historically involved segregation (including institutions and special classes) and why current practices remain barrier-producing, affecting students, families, and educators. It outlines definitions and policy concepts related to inclusion and exclusion, describes how Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and school-based disability identification support access to services, and explains types of educational placements in Ontario. The passage emphasizes that lack of planning and shortcomings in teacher preparation, alongside policy and funding constraints, contribute to exclusion. It also critiques the Ontario Policy on Accessible Education for Students with Disabilities (2018) for making claims without translating them into institutional practices, and it provides recommendations focused on improved teacher training, intersectional policy approaches, inclusion of disabled voices in policy development, and stronger funding and implementation.

TI ships “X” developmental devices with a disclaimer that they are for internal evaluation only. MSP devices are described as fully characterized with demonstrated quality and reliability, and TI’s standard warranty applies. Predictions indicate prototype devices (X) have a higher failure rate than standard production devices, and TI recommends they not be used in any production system because their expected end-use failure rate is undefined; only qualified production devices should be used. TI device nomenclature includes a suffix indicating temperature range, package type, and distribution format, and MSP device ordering information is referenced via package option addendum, TI website, or a TI sales representative. The passage also outlines support resources (TI E2E forums), trademarks, ESD handling caution, revision history changes, and packaging/mechanical/orderable information, including guidance that package data is subject to change.

The passage contrasts a proposed president’s approach to the U.S.-Taiwan relationship with Carter’s actions, saying the Taiwan Relations Act should be treated as official and enforced while unnecessary restrictions that demean Taiwanese Chinese friends should be eliminated. It argues foreign interference in enforcing U.S. laws should not be accepted and states that strict adherence to five principles will benefit the United States, the People’s Republic of China, and Taiwan, with implementation awaiting the November election and considering both sides’ views. It also includes George Bush’s address to the Commonwealth Club, recounting a historical anecdote about “denying” a past campaign promise and stating he will focus on Carter’s foreign policy record rather than Vice President Mondale’s presentation. Bush claims the Carter administration’s campaign misrepresents Reagan’s commitment to peace and portrays Reagan as someone who might lead the country into war, which he calls a false and irresponsible distortion.

The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three American companies to produce it. The approval followed the FDA’s original approval 25 years ago and its first generic approval in 2019, and it triggered pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians. The passage says the change is unlikely to affect access because the pill is typically taken with misoprostol, a combination accounting for about two-thirds of U.S. abortions.  

Amgen reported that its cholesterol-lowering drug Repatha prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial. Analysts said the results could help Repatha reach a broader market, and the passage notes that it generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024.

The passage welcomes viewers to the Stanley Cup Final in Nashville, describing the atmosphere since the playoffs and noting the convergence of CMA Fest and the final, with expectations of over people on Broadway and country music fans embracing hockey. It announces a worldwide opening telecast featuring a special rooftop performance from Tootsie’s Orchid Lounge, with sold-out conditions in Pittsburgh’s PPG Arena and the performance and game shown on screens throughout Nashville. It says this is a major night for the NHL and introduces Luke Bryan, described as a major country star, as the performer to kick off the show worldwide.

The passage describes jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs) and the limitations of existing defenses that rely mainly on analyzing or modifying the input prompt. It argues that more robust protection can come from simulating human-like multi-stage reasoning, using hierarchical evaluation from coarse to fine-grained analysis. The proposed defense, SafeBehavior, is a hierarchical jailbreak defense mechanism integrated into the LLM inference process, consisting of three stages: intention inference (quickly screening for malicious intent and terminating generation if harmful), self-introspection (evaluating the model’s own response via structured introspection and a confidence score to decide acceptance, refusal, or revision), and self-revision (rewriting uncertain responses to preserve user intent while mitigating risk and aligning with safety policies). The study evaluates SafeBehavior on five types of jailbreak attacks, compares it against seven state-of-the-art defenses, and outlines related threat modeling and defender goals including robust output integrity, effective threat mitigation, and efficient execution.

The passage describes the development and validation of a two-week, six-hour “Critical Multicultural Education (CME)” learning module for English language teacher education programs. Using a qualitative research design, the study aims to introduce pre-service English teachers to CME and critical language teaching and to encourage them to adopt a critical perspective in their teaching. The module was developed through a four-stage process, including researcher brainstorming, input from a “critical friend,” initial implementation with a small online group (15 participants) and revision based on feedback, and a second implementation with a larger group (86 participants) evaluated via in-depth interviews with 10 participants. Results indicate that participants perceived benefits such as more positive attitudes toward diversity, increased understanding of social issues and critical educational approaches, greater awareness of the political position of teaching and education goals, and improved lesson planning and teaching resources for implementing CME. Challenges reported included limited time, dense content, and insufficient guidance for critical action, leading to more teacher-centered and less participatory experiences during discussions. The study concludes that the module met its objectives of increasing awareness and understanding of CME and related topics, and recommends extending module duration, adding more interactivity and research opportunities, and further research to strengthen criticality in teacher education contexts.

Higher education in Pakistan has been largely neglected since 1947, with enrollment rising from about 2% of university-age students in the early 2000s. In 2002, the Government established the Higher Education Commission (HEC) as a statutory regulator with a mission to support socio-economic development; reforms included new campuses, tuition waivers and scholarships, and quality improvements through research and technology. Enrollment increased from 2% to 12.6% between 2003 and 2021, and some quality enhancements were reported. Despite growth, the passage highlights persistent access and equity challenges tied to demographics and geography, including rural-urban location, gender, and socio-economic factors. It notes that universities are concentrated in big cities, that more than half of Pakistan’s districts lack college campuses, and that growth in private universities has increased enrollment in urban areas while widening disparities. The passage also describes inequality by poverty zones, showing enrollment and numbers of universities/DAIs increasing as poverty decreases, and it reports gender differences that vary by poverty and region. The study uses secondary data from HEC statistics, AEPAM, Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PSLM), and PPAF to analyze enrollment patterns by region, gender, and poverty, concluding that reforms have expanded access but not inclusively benefited historically underprivileged groups, with continued disparities across region, income, gender, and urbanicity.

Digital leader firms adopt a growth mindset, use data to build shared context, empower teams to examine data, and align the organization with common targets. They further encourage risk-taking, experimentation, and long-term development, valuing continuous feedback and measurement, while also prioritizing individual training in skills like problem solving, statistics, and design thinking. They emphasize transparency in data and decision-making, discourage data hoarding, handle data with appropriate governance controls, and expect ongoing tracking of progress using data-driven metrics. Leaders use structured goals tied to strategy while allowing flexibility in how work is done, aiming for both vertical and horizontal alignment through shared data models and transparent access. The passage contrasts this with digital laggards, who prioritize short-term efforts, discourage risks, keep data on a need-to-know basis, rely more on business judgment than data-driven decisions, and often set goals that are insufficiently grounded in data, leading to process-focused adherence. It also notes that digital transformation may be difficult because cultural shifts require deliberate effort, and it proposes four patterns of readiness: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on May 11, 2020 (report date May 4, 2020) describing that, on May 11, 2020, it consummated the issuance and sale of $2.0 billion 0.750% Notes due 2023, $2.25 billion 1.125% Notes due 2025, $1.75 billion 1.650% Notes due 2030, and $2.5 billion 2.650% Notes due 2050 under an underwriting agreement dated May 4, 2020. The article recounts Howie Morenz’s life and career as the start of a hockey family dynasty, beginning with his early years in Ontario and his rise with the Montreal Canadiens in 1923. The passage says the Dengvaxia scandal has remained unresolved for over half a year despite investigations, and it highlights WHO’s announcement in Geneva. The passage describes a non-traditional bucket list created in partnership with INFINITI, featuring five challenging, empowering activities: taking a road trip alone (including a route from Vancouver to Whistler via the Sea to Sky Highway with a detour to Squamish), starting your own business (illustrated by a person who left a high-paying job to open a Caribbean fusion catering business), volunteering abroad (such as building schools or teaching English while challenging yourself to immerse in culture and language), skydiving as a metaphor for facing other fears, and running a marathon or other physical challenge matched to one’s fitness level.

Joe Girardi said he was curious about lefty Jordan Montgomery’s size, mentality, and minor-league success. LimeWire is an AI content publishing platform that helps users create AI content, particularly AI-generated images, and share it on LimeWire Studio. A Sunshine Coast woman said she was sexually abused by her stepbrother for eight years starting when he moved into her home at age 14. The lecture reviews the Einstein field equations and frames them as differential equations for the spacetime metric sourced by mass-energy. It explains how, for a perfect fluid source, the equations involve density, pressure, fluid velocity, and constraints from normalization, making the general problem difficult. The course then outlines three routes to solutions: weak gravity (linearized general relativity), symmetric solutions (e.g., static or stationary), and direct numerical solutions. For weak gravity, it introduces nearly flat coordinates where the metric equals flat space plus a small perturbation \(H_{\alpha\beta}\), neglecting terms beyond linear order. It discusses how Lorentz transformations leave the background unchanged, treating the perturbation as transforming like a tensor in flat space. It derives the linearized inverse metric and then introduces infinitesimal coordinate shifts as gauge transformations, which change the metric perturbation but leave the Riemann curvature unchanged. Using the linearized Einstein tensor, it defines the trace-reversed perturbation \(\bar h_{\alpha\beta}\) and shows that choosing the Lorentz (harmonic) gauge makes the perturbation divergence-free, simplifying the field equations to a wave equation with the same structure as electrodynamics in Lorentz gauge. Finally, it considers a static, non-relativistic perfect fluid source and shows that the resulting metric reproduces the Newtonian limit of general relativity (with \(h_{00}\) related to the Newtonian potential). The lecture mentions gravitational lensing, solar-system post-Newtonian corrections, and an upcoming homework variation involving a rotating body and resulting “gravitomagnetic” effects, and notes that the next lecture will address dynamic sources and gravitational radiation.

The passage compiles multiple 2001 media items and notes about executive pay and energy-sector issues. A Business Week report says CEO compensation in the U.S. remained high in 2000 despite weaker returns, citing an average $13.1 million total pay, while some pay was reduced and pay growth slowed as stock options became less valuable. It describes examples such as Dana’s CEO receiving reduced pay after poor results, and discusses how compensation practices may be shifting toward more performance-linked awards like restricted shares amid market decline. The passage also includes articles on Enron’s Dabhol power dispute in India, where India’s government refuses to pay $22 million claimed under contracts, possible effects on foreign investment, and a Los Angeles Times analysis alleging that government-run power agencies helped inflate California electricity prices during 2000. The passage summarizes a 2025 qualitative study by Merola examining Mexican higher-education stakeholders’ perspectives on whether online learning can improve access and quality. It notes that Mexico has seen rapid growth in distance/online enrollments, but participation is affected by economic resources, digital and infrastructural gaps (including rural access), unequal institutional capacity, and challenges for certain groups such as neurodivergent students. For quality, stakeholders report difficulties related to faculty proficiency with digital platforms, limited teacher training and pedagogical support, lower student engagement, collaboration and communication problems, subject-matter limitations, and higher perceived academic integrity issues. Overall, the study finds that online learning is viewed as valuable primarily as a complement to in-person education, with stakeholder consensus on needing better internet infrastructure, resources for non-traditional students, and ongoing support and training for teachers to address both access and quality concerns.

The passage describes the author’s menstrual-related skin issues and a face mask from Renée Rouleau that helped her. It says Rouleau helped identify the author’s melasma as being triggered by birth control, leading the author to stop it and reduce the condition. It also recounts Rouleau identifying “acne cosmetica” caused by heavy oil-based foundation and desert conditions, with a suggestion to use powder foundation, after which the author reports no desert breakouts. After a facial, the author describes Rouleau’s Rapid Response Detox Masque ($61) for hormonal acne, which is used weekly for about 15 minutes. The mask is described as lightweight, non-drying to the skin, and formulated with ingredients including tea tree leaf oil, lichocalchone (Chinese licorice), Manuka leaf oil, and a salicylic acid complex, and it excludes several common additives. The author claims it helps with clogged pores from travel, hormones, and sleeping with makeup on, including premenstrual acne.

The passage describes soft-start behavior, switching-frequency configuration, and several control and protection features of the TPS7H500x-SP series PWM controllers. Soft start gradually increases output voltage using the SS pin as an error-amplifier reference until SS exceeds VREF, with synchronous rectifier outputs becoming active when SS reaches 1 V; a capacitor on the SS pin sets the soft-start time. Switching frequency can be set by an internal RT resistor, external synchronization via the SYNC pin, or primary-secondary operation to synchronize two controllers without an external clock. It also summarizes available primary and synchronous rectifier outputs (OUTA/OUTB, SRA/SRB), dead time and leading-edge blank time programmability, pulse skipping conditions, duty-cycle limits via DCL, current sensing and PWM generation using COMP and CS_ILIM, hiccup-mode operation via HICC, external fault shutdown via FAULT, slope compensation via RSC, and thermal shutdown thresholds. The latter sections include an example synchronous push-pull converter design and provide general application, layout guidelines, and additional packaging/documentation notices.

The passage lists multiple issues and their descriptions for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, including failures during DMA and I/O (e.g., software DMA memory writes from LPC failing, system hangs with certain I/O addresses, legacy DMA to LPC devices not working), interrupt and PIC/SMB/SSMI problems, register access problems (e.g., byte accesses to ACPI PM1 registers hanging; PMC register writes possibly corrupting other writes), and power/clock and wakeup problems (e.g., thermal alarm recovery behavior, clock gating failures in USB/UART/GLIU domains, wake events not working from ACPI S3). It also provides implications and, for some items, resolution guidance such as avoiding specific configurations, using aligned PRD/DMA settings, not using certain debug features, and adjusting delays or disabling clock gating.

The passage describes a teleoperated surgical instrument force transmission mechanism that converts input rotary motion into translational motion to actuate an end effector via a push/pull rod or other actuation element. Exemplary embodiments include a drive pulley with an operably coupled drive cable, a driven pulley operably coupled with the cable, and an actuation member coupled to the driven pulley; rotational motion of the driven pulley causes translational movement of the actuation member to actuate the end effector. A surgical instrument embodiment includes a shaft with the end effector at a distal portion and the force transmission mechanism at a proximal portion. A method of operation is described involving winding a drive cable portion over a drive pulley, rotating a driven pulley by unwinding the other cable portion, translating an actuation element, and operating the end effector in response. The passage further discusses implementations within a teleoperated surgical system (including a da Vinci system example), mechanical components such as pulleys, cable routing/idler pulleys, potential pre-tensioning of cables, a ball joint connection to the actuation rod, and how pulley geometry can provide mechanical advantage and affect force based on the driven pulley rotational position.

The passage describes a model for integrating interprofessional education (IPE) in higher education at Clarkson College. It explains differences between interdisciplinary and interprofessional approaches, defines IPE as learners from two or more professions learning with and from each other to enable collaboration and improve health outcomes, and outlines shared themes such as multiple perspectives and knowledge integration. Clarkson College formed an interprofessional education committee to develop an IPE framework aligned with the Interprofessional Education Collaborative core competencies and informed by the Quadruple Aim, NCICLE guidance, and consultations with CIPER. The resulting IPE curriculum includes an online IPE 301 course with four theory-based modules followed by a real-time experiential module with IPE events categorized as knowledge, community, and service, supported by flexible participation options. Beginning in Fall 2018, all incoming degree-seeking students must complete the zero-credit course to graduate, with completion documented on transcripts. Student core competencies are measured using ICCAS surveys administered at multiple points and analyzed alongside qualitative reflection journals. Results from Fall 2018 to Summer 2021 (n=428) indicate increased perceived ability to collaborate after completing modules and IPE events, and qualitative findings report that students enjoyed participation and felt it improved teamwork, collaboration, communication, and career awareness. The passage also discusses implementation support (leadership buy-in and faculty participation), sustainability through ongoing assessment and planning, and concludes that the model provides a structure for educating and evaluating students’ knowledge and collaborative growth, contributing to positive experiences and improved collaborative skills.

The passage describes how, as Enron faced credit and credibility problems, U.S. and other energy trading companies restricted or limited their dealings with Enron to reduce exposure. Concerns cited include Enron’s declining share price, downgraded credit ratings, uncertainties about its complex financial structure, and SEC-related investigations into partnerships involving former CFO Andrew Fastow, which led Enron to provide additional information and restate financial statements. It also reports that Enron and Dynegy were in talks for a possible business combination involving a stock deal around $8 billion, with ChevronTexaco involved, and that regulators such as FERC said they were watching Enron’s situation without intervening in the SEC investigation.

The lecture recaps earlier Schwarzschild spacetime results for a vacuum exterior with a mass parameter, noting a tidal singularity at \(r=0\) and a coordinate singularity at \(r=2GM\). It compares infalling motion described using proper time versus coordinate time, then analyzes how light emitted near \(r=2GM\) undergoes infinite redshift, making the Schwarzschild time coordinate break down at that surface. By studying null geodesics and introducing tortoise and null coordinates, the lecture identifies \(r=2GM\) as an event horizon: once crossed, trajectories cannot return. It then presents Kruskal–Szekeres coordinates, which remove most coordinate pathologies at \(r=2GM\) and allow clarification of the causal structure, including that light cannot cross the event horizon outward. The lecture concludes by outlining other black hole solutions (Reissner–Nordström for charge and Kerr for spin) and stating a theorem that the only stationary 3+1-dimensional spacetimes with event horizons are Kerr–Newman, encompassing Schwarzschild (no charge or spin), Kerr (spin only), and Reissner–Nordström (charge only). Finally, it discusses the No-Hair theorem, describing how collapse radiates away non–Kerr–Newman features so the end state is characterized only by mass, spin, and charge, and notes that the next lecture will focus on testing this spacetime using black-hole orbits.

The passage describes the TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media processors as highly integrated platforms with mixed processing cores and flexible software control. It outlines programmability using an ARM Cortex-A8 CPU (with Neon) and a TI C674x VLIW floating-point DSP, plus HD video/imaging coprocessors. It lists key CPU and cache/memory sizes for the ARM and DSP, describes a rich peripheral set (including Ethernet MACs, McASP audio ports, McBSP, memory interfaces, DCAN, and other peripherals), and notes the HDVICP2 video/imaging accelerator for off-loading processing tasks. Additional sections cover device overview elements such as memory maps, mailbox and spinlock modules, and extensive pin/terminal function descriptions, along with a table-of-contents fragment and revision history updates.

The Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development awarded nearly $480,000 in grants and contracts under the Wisconsin Fast Forward – Milwaukee Grant Program to seven projects that will train almost 600 Milwaukee residents for jobs with area companies. The projects include grants for training community health workers, positions in childcare and adult day care, construction industry entry-level skills, installation of permeable pavement, CNC and industrial sewing machine operations, and call center/customer service work.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU and its architectural and software features for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It highlights improved performance for many deep learning data types, including support for TF32, BF16, and FP64, and a fine-grained structured sparsity feature that can double Tensor Core throughput. It also covers A100’s Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability for securely partitioning one GPU into up to seven instances with fault isolation and defined QoS, along with third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and memory architecture upgrades such as 40 GB HBM2 and a larger L2 cache with residency controls and compute data compression. The passage further discusses mechanisms for improved error and fault detection/containment, CUDA advances including task graphs and asynchronous copy/barriers, and the NVIDIA DGX A100 system as an AI infrastructure platform powered by A100 and MIG.

The passage contains multiple diplomatic telegrams and documents. The Ambassador in Italy reports that the Allies’ joint reply to the President’s note was decided in conference and will be sent by Briand once Russia approves the final draft, with a wholly friendly tone despite uncertainty about details on the objects of war, and that an Italian delay in sending its answer was denied. In Greece, the Minister reports a preliminary conciliatory but indefinite Greek reply emphasizing effective assurances against encroachments, mixed commissions of inquiry, and provisions related to reparation, and notes that since a blockade establishment the Provisional Government seized several islands. He further reports that Italian conditions presented to Greece must be accepted in principle within specified timeframes, with the blockade raised only after all conditions are fulfilled, and that the Italian Foreign Minister urges literal acceptance. In France, the Ambassador describes Allied reply handling: Briand receives the reply and addresses the Belgian Foreign Minister’s separate note expressing Belgium’s situation and gratitude to the United States, along with plans to publish on Friday morning. The translation of the French note states the Allied Governments studied the U.S. note, associate themselves with hopes for a league of nations, discuss requirements for sanctions, and argue that a durable peace depends on a satisfactory settlement, which they say is not currently possible to secure reparation, restitution, and guaranties given Central Powers’ responsibility.

The passage describes a conversation in which Mr. Solanko raised questions about the First Secretary of the Finnish Legation, Mr. Mikkola, and the Legation’s efforts to contact him by telephone while he was in New York. Mikkola was scheduled to return to Washington on Monday, and the speaker stated that the Legation could assume their note would be effective only for future visits outside Washington. Solanko also asked about the whereabouts of Mr. Wrede, an Attaché, who was in New York and had been instructed to return to Washington immediately. The discussion then covered whether the United States knew the details of Finnish restrictions on Finnish and American diplomatic movements, communication delays, and the handling of inquiries by the Department, with both parties focusing mostly on facts. A separate account notes that the Finnish Minister reported receiving guidance from his government stating no additional restrictions were placed on American diplomats in Helsinki beyond those applied to other diplomats, with Helsinki described as a special “war area.” The Minister requested relief from restrictions, and the Secretary of State said they would communicate in due course. The passage also summarizes Finnish public opinion from December 21, 1941 to January 4, noting reactions to U.S. military reverses in the Far East and perceived increasing U.S.-Great Britain cooperation with the Soviet Union.

The passage recommends nine personal finance podcasts that offer education on personal and business finances. The passage is a VentureWire newsletter issue dated October 5, 2000, listing “Top Stories” and various “New Money,” “New Products,” “New Deals,” “M&A,” “New Directors,” “New People,” and “VC Fund News.” It reports company and funding announcements, including Broadcom’s acquisition of Element 14 for about $640 million, Sony Broadband’s launch of 550 Digital Media Ventures with contributed funding, and GameChange’s launch with up to $100 million. Stafford Global, based in the UAE and operating since 1993, invites working professionals to open days and webinars about online or distance learning. VentureWire’s December 6, 2000 newsletter lists top stories, including Oxygen Media cutting 65 employees and restructuring its online business, Softbank stopping investments through two European joint ventures, Innovance Networks securing over $75 million, and Merrill Lynch launching an internal venture capital fund for employees. The issue also reports multiple funding rounds (“new money”), a shutdown of Babygear.com (“bad news”), company name changes and launches (“new products”), business deals (“new deals”), acquisitions (“M&A”), board and executive appointments (“new directors” and “new people”), venture capital fund news, and venture personnel updates.
