The passage describes heating oil and heating oil futures as a derivative contract to buy or sell a specified quantity of heating oil on a future date at a pre-agreed price, traded on ICE Futures Europe and CME. It explains that heating oil is used for heating residential and commercial buildings, and its demand rises as winter temperatures drop, making it a seasonal commodity. The contract size is 42,000 gallons (1,000 barrels) on both exchanges, with the minimum price fluctuation on CME of $0.0001 per gallon ($4.20 per contract). Trading hours and settlement differ by exchange: ICE is cash-settled and trades with specified hours including a pre-open market, while CME is physically settled and trading ends on the last business day of the month prior to the contract month. The passage also mentions a Heating Oil ETF (HEAT) and provides all-time high and low prices ($5.2215 in April 2022 and $0.2920 in February 1999). It outlines key trading risks as adverse leveraged price movements and states that major factors affecting prices include weather conditions, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and the cost of alternative heating fuels.

An inside day in trading is defined by two bars where the last bar’s price action is entirely below yesterday’s high and above yesterday’s low, meaning today’s range is completely within yesterday’s range. The passage states that inside days happen frequently across markets and time frames, and that the opposite pattern is an outside day, which has a higher high and a lower low than yesterday. It also reports that research and backtests indicate inside days are a poor trading signal on their own and that inside-day trading strategies may require additional variables or filters to perform better. The passage includes backtesting examples for the S&P 500 using approaches like buying all inside days and adding an RSI filter, and notes that results were modest or not tradeable, with one swing trading approach described as working in equity markets and not in gold.

GMR Infrastructure reported a consolidated net loss of Rs565.94 crore for the quarter ended 31 December 2017, compared with a net profit of Rs643.44 crore in the corresponding quarter of 2016-17. Total income from operations fell to Rs2,295.83 crore from Rs2,587.26 crore, and total expenses declined to Rs2,487.90 crore from Rs2,623.74 crore year over year. The company’s infrastructure interests include airports, energy, transportation, and urban infrastructure, with assets such as Indira Gandhi International Airport and Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, and ongoing projects including a greenfield airport in Heraklion, Crete, and smart cities near Delhi and Hyderabad airports.

The passage discusses damages awarded for unlawful seizure and detention of whaling vessels, arguing that the losses are direct and not speculative profits. It explains that for whaling ships, damages should be measured by the value of the vessel’s use and services during detention, especially because crew are paid by lay and may receive no remuneration if the voyage is missed. It contrasts this with trading vessels, where earnings capacity during detention might be used, and concludes that for whaling ships the key criterion is the average catch. The passage also quotes an arbitrator in the case of the Costa Rica Packet, noting that detention caused Captain Carpenter to miss the best whaling season and that no conclusive proof was provided that he had to leave or sell the ship under the stated conditions.

Google has begun rolling out the first Chrome UI changes in two years, focusing on the shape of tabs and other top-of-window elements. The updates are available in Chrome “Canary” (rawest build) for Windows only and are hidden behind an experimental setting that users enable via chrome://flags. The tabs change from a trapezoidal shape to near-rectangles with slightly rounded upper corners, and the active tab brightens to plain white. Other visible changes include a rounded address bar and updates to add-on icon layout, while additional potential changes mentioned include moving the new-tab “+” button to the left of the address bar. It is unclear when these changes will reach the stable browser, and Canary version 68 is not planned for production until late July.

The passage is a discussion of upcoming playoff/Stanley Cup Finals gameplay, focusing on strategy and factors such as special teams, execution, discipline, and skating. It emphasizes the importance of early-game discipline, leveraging power plays and penalty kills, and how confidence can affect special teams performance. The speaker also downplays line matchup importance, instead highlighting winning by executing game plans, taking the lead, and playing with it. Additional points include effective neutral-zone pressure, preventing opponents’ scoring chances, and the impact of traffic in front of the net and specific players’ performances in key situations and goals.

The passage explains that strength training benefits include building muscle mass, strength, and endurance, but injury risk can be reduced by using correct techniques, warming up, and cooling down. It discusses common injury types: rotator cuff injuries (including tears and tendinopathy, often from repetitive overhead motions), hamstring injuries (often from sudden powerful movements and with multiple grades affecting healing time), herniated discs (caused by sudden extreme or repetitive poor movement, with symptoms such as pain, numbness, tingling, and weakness), tendonitis (from minor stress or repetitive motions, with pain that can persist and worsen), and tennis elbow and golfer’s elbow (from repetitive wrist/arm movements). Prevention advice includes good shoulder posture, adjusting workouts if discomfort occurs, stretching and warming up, maintaining good form and technique, not ignoring pain, resting, and seeking medical advice if symptoms persist. It also recommends warming up to increase heart rate and blood flow, using dynamic full-range movements for warm-up, and cooling down to regulate blood flow; static exercises are suggested at the end of a workout.

Players discuss their roles and approach in the Stanley Cup Final, emphasizing that offense production is a key job and that they don’t care where goals come from as long as they come from their team. They say the series has started with both teams testing each other, with more scoring in the second period, and that they need to smarten up defensively and limit the opponent’s playmaking. They describe comfort with certain line combinations, confidence in mixing lines, and praise for Patrick Kane’s all-around contributions and preparation. They also discuss staying patient and not focusing only on scoring, using good defensive plays to support offense, and building on what went well in the previous game while aiming to improve as the series progresses.

The passage introduces spin diffusion length (ls) as a key parameter for spintronic devices, noting the need for sufficiently long ls in spin transport channels and the value of accurate simulations to predict materials and optimize operating conditions. It describes an ab initio approach for calculating ls (and spin lifetime τs) using a linearized density-matrix master equation with quantum electron scattering, which has matched experiments across various materials. While incorporating an electric field along a non-periodic direction is feasible at the DFT level, handling a field along a periodic direction is challenging yet important because longitudinal electric fields drive charge carriers and spins and can significantly modulate ls via the spin-drift effect. The passage explains that the commonly used drift-diffusion model may produce significant errors in certain systems due to effects like spatial spin precession, motivating extension of the ab initio method to include the drift term for electric fields along periodic directions using covariant derivative formalism. It then outlines the paper’s structure and begins the methods section by deriving the linearized steady-state quantum master equation under finite electric field, including coherent, drift, and scattering terms, and discusses computing the drift contribution LE via a Wannier-representation finite-difference technique.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x (GA102/GA104) GPU architecture and features. It states that GA10x GPUs improve performance and efficiency over Turing, including up to 2x faster ray tracing and up to 1.7x faster raster workloads. The document highlights GA102 hardware details (e.g., compute resources such as CUDA cores, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores), concurrent compute/graphics and ray tracing capabilities, and second-generation RT Core improvements. It explains GA10x FP32 processing on both datapaths, larger L1/shared memory, and ROP optimizations. For ray-traced motion blur, it details GA10x hardware acceleration via an Interpolate Triangle Position unit and claims faster motion blur rendering versus Turing, with support listed for certain tools and benchmarks. For AI, it covers third-generation Tensor Cores, support for new data types (TF32, BF16), and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity. The passage also discusses GDDR6X memory, third-generation NVLink scaling, PCIe Gen 4, and RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression using DirectStorage. Additional sections cover fifth-generation NVDEC hardware video decoding formats (including AV1 decode) and seventh-generation NVENC hardware encoding. It also presents information on data center-focused GPUs such as the NVIDIA A40, plus appendices on specifications and memory Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for overclocking.

The appellant pled guilty to theft by receiving and financial transaction card theft and received a ten-year probation sentence conditioned on restitution. The trial court granted the State’s motion to continue the restitution hearing to secure victims’ presence, which was found to be no abuse of discretion. The appellate court held the trial court was not authorized to order restitution for all items taken in related burglaries because appellant was not charged with those burglaries; restitution could only cover damages resulting from appellant’s theft by receiving and card theft. The case was remanded for resentencing accordingly, the remaining error was moot, and the judgment was reversed and remanded.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated June 4, 2018. The report states that Microsoft entered into a definitive agreement to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion, announced in a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. It also says that, on and after June 4, 2018, representatives of Microsoft and GitHub will present information about the transaction to investors using slides attached as Exhibit 99.2. The filing lists Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and includes a signature by Carolyn Frantz, Secretary.

After protesters disrupted Charles Murray’s planned lecture at Middlebury College, a Public Safety officer accused Addis Fouche-Channer ’17 of being at the protest and pulled her from Bill Burger’s car. The officer’s name is withheld pending an investigation into whether he racially profiled her, and investigators obtained transcripts showing he identified her by name but provided no other evidence that she was there. Fouche-Channer declined multiple interview requests and contested the allegation, presenting Wi-Fi logs, statements from friends and a coworker, and other materials to support that she was not at the protest. On May 13, a judicial dean ruled there was no good reason to proceed with a hearing. After Fouche-Channer graduated, she contacted Public Safety seeking an apology, leading to a formal internal human relations investigation into whether the officer violated the college’s anti-discrimination policy. As of press time, no decision has been made on whether racial profiling occurred, and the investigation’s timeline was delayed.

Chamomile is a plant group used since ancient times as an herbal remedy, with Matricaria recutita (German chamomile) and Chamaemelum nobile (Roman chamomile) widely grown worldwide. Matricaria recutita is hardy and used historically in teas to treat fevers, flu, digestive disorders, and skin ailments. Chamomile oil, the primary extract from chamomile flowers and flower heads, contains compounds including coumarins, sesquiterpenes, polyacetylenes, and flavonoids. Matricaria recutita extracts are listed in pharmacopoeias in many countries and are noted for anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and spasmolytic properties. Extracting oil is typically done by steam distillation, producing low yields of about 0.2–0.4% from flower weight. The oil is used for relaxation, insomnia, mood enhancement, mild anti-depressant effects, calming nervousness or anxiety, easing aching joints and muscles, and is used in products like lotions and creams, and for digestive problems and conjunctivitis symptoms, as well as in commercial products including soaps, beverages, detergents, perfumes, ointments, hair care, food and bakery products, and cosmetics.

The passage describes America’s science education crisis, noting that only 29% of eighth graders are proficient in science (down from 33% in 2019) and that 42% of students say they enjoy science (down 10 points in five years). It says science standards exist in most states but many middle and high school science classes still emphasize memorization rather than inquiry. The passage compares this to the “science of reading” movement, arguing the nation needs a similar “science of science education” strategy that uses research-based teaching practices, high-quality instructional materials, and districtwide curriculum-based professional learning. It claims educators who receive such professional learning shift from delivering content to guiding inquiry, and reports behavioral changes in students, including more peer discussion and meaningful participation by all students. The passage concludes that district and school leaders should adopt high-quality materials, invest in sustained professional learning from certified providers, provide planning time, support principals in allowing teachers to try new approaches, and emphasize science as essential to economic prosperity and civic health.

On May 25, 2016, Microsoft Corporation announced plans to streamline its smartphone hardware business, resulting in the reduction of up to 1,850 positions, including 1,350 at Microsoft Mobile Oy in Finland. In the quarter ending June 30, 2016, Microsoft expects to record an impairment and restructuring charge of approximately $950 million, including about $200 million for severance payments. The actions are expected to be substantially complete by the end of 2016 and fully completed by July 2017. A copy of the company’s press release is included as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes standard forward-looking statements language and identifies Exhibit 99.1 as a press release dated May 25, 2016.

The passage introduces green computing as an approach to reduce energy use and CO2 emissions in distributed communication, driven by low-latency and compute-intensive service demands in edge and vehicular networks. It presents Vehicular Cloud Computing (VCC) as a scalable offloading solution using underutilized resources of connected vehicles, especially in dense urban areas, but notes uncertainties about feasibility under urban mobility and 5G constraints, energy implications, and how to distribute profits to incentivize cooperation. The paper investigates VCC in 5G-enabled urban environments, with contributions including an integrated delay-and-energy-aware task allocation framework using mobility traces and energy models, a stochastic coalitional game for revenue sharing that ensures a non-empty robust core, and an assessment of CO2 savings and long-term economic incentives for vehicle participation. It then describes a centralized 5G architecture with a controller coordinating vehicles and cloud resources, system workflow based on beacon collection and ranking of candidate executors, formal delay and energy models for task execution and transmission, an optimization-based task allocation problem with deadline and capacity constraints, and a coalitional-game revenue-sharing mechanism where coalition value depends on task completion before deadlines under uncertain realized parameters.

The passage describes a protocol for the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual environment that will combine linked survey and administrative data to study how social, economic, and political factors shape income-related health inequalities in urban Canada. It outlines CSDUL’s development from 2011–2017 data, using a hub-and-node structure: a central hub and five nodes covering political/economic context, environmental context, socioeconomic context, material circumstances, and health systems. The project will create and validate area-based indicators, replicate WHO/Europe’s decomposition analysis of income-related inequalities in self-reported health, and estimate the relative impacts of different social determinants. The protocol also includes plans for interaction/effect modification analyses by group characteristics and notes methodological considerations for the decomposition approach and data sources. The study is funded in part by the Urban Public Health Network and the University of Saskatchewan, includes an ethics exemption, and states there are no conflicts of interest.

Exxon Mobil reported earnings of 88 cents per share for its December quarter, matching the average of the previous three quarters but below analyst expectations of $1.04 and the “whisper number” of $1.11. Shares fell about 3% in pre-market trading. For the year, the company reported total earnings of $19.7 billion on revenues of $244.36 billion, with an estimated $5.9 billion earnings gain attributed to the Trump tax cut. CEO Darren Woods said Exxon will invest $50 billion in the U.S. over the next five years; capital expenditures for 2017 were $23 billion. The dividend remained unchanged at 77 cents, and the article notes disappointment related to the earnings miss reduced Exxon’s market cap by $10 billion. It also discusses Exxon’s investments in the Permian Basin, potential effects of oil price expectations and shale production on earnings, and Goldman Sachs’ revised view that oil could rise above $82 per barrel, which the article says could improve Exxon’s outlook.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 7, 2018. The report states that on November 7, 2018, Tesla published a blog post on its website, attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. The exhibit is described as the blog post dated November 7, 2018.

In informal discussions in Italy, the Ambassador reprobated an anti-American press campaign and government action fixing coal prices too high for American shipment. The Italian Minister said fixed prices were necessary to continue the war, claiming England recognized this as a condition for coal, wheat, and steel, and that if prices were not kept down people would rise and war could not continue; he neither denied nor affirmed a rumor that he had given form to the Allies’ answer. He said he supposed the President would request Germany define its aims.  

A separate report says criticism of alleged Allied plans for the partition of Europe continues, including claims about assigning territories to Russia and arguments that a new war against Russia is possible and probably imminent.  

Another dispatch from Greece says British settlement efforts were proceeding satisfactorily with remaining differences on minor points, and it hoped the blockade would be raised in a week.  

A Dutch communication refers to a Minister’s questions about measures to promote peace and includes references to the President’s January 22 Senate address on bases of a durable peace and Germany’s confidential terms of peace.  

An excerpted address by the U.S. President to the Senate describes an identic note sent December 18 requesting more definite statements of terms for peace. It states the Central powers replied only that they were ready for conference, while the Entente powers replied more definitely, and it asserts that the U.S. is closer to definite discussion of peace and the international concert needed to prevent future catastrophe.

Moderate alcohol consumption is associated with lower all-cause mortality than abstaining or heavy drinking, with follow-up periods averaging around eight years. Moderate drinkers were no less likely than abstainers to die of cancer, but were about a quarter less likely to die of heart disease or stroke. Heavy drinkers had slightly higher all-cause mortality than moderate drinkers and abstainers, driven by higher cancer deaths (about 45% higher odds than moderate drinkers). A meta-analysis of 333,247 adults found that, for most people, consuming a little alcohol is better than drinking none, while too much is worse. Moderate drinking is defined as up to 14 servings per week for men and up to seven for women. Binge drinking at least once a week increased odds of dying during study periods by about 16%, largely by raising cancer rates. The passage also notes that people may misreport alcohol intake and that research on alcohol’s health effects varies. The World Health Organization recommends against any alcohol consumption due to alcohol’s link to cancer and its attribution to 5.9% of global deaths in 2012, while other research suggests possible cardiovascular benefits at modest doses. The newest research discussed finds gender, ethnicity, and age differences: heavy drinking increased all-cause and cancer mortality in men but not women; non-Latino whites appeared to benefit from moderation, while non-Latino blacks did not; and effects were more pronounced in people 60 and older than those 40–59, with no death-rate reduction seen among ages 18–39.

IWM is the ticker symbol for the iShares Russell 2000 ETF, which tracks the Russell 2000 index and provides exposure to small-cap U.S. stocks listed on U.S. stock exchanges. The Russell 2000 index measures the performance of the 2,000 smallest companies in the Russell 3000, represents about 10% of its market capitalization, was launched in 1984 by the Frank Russell Company, and is managed by FTSE Russell. The index is rebalanced annually in June, and components may change. The passage describes a “Russell 2000 Rebalancing Trading Strategy,” developed around the annual rebalancing period, and notes it shows solid performance, with the option to hedge against the S&P 500 or use IWM’s tendency to trend slightly differently for diversification in trading.

Marcus Lemonis, CEO of the Good Sam Club and head of Camping World with ownership in about 100 other businesses, purchased the bankrupt Gander Mountain store chain, now called Gander Outdoors, and has started reopening 69 stores in the United States. The passage says his rise began with buying the Good Sam Club, after which he referred to members as “marketing tools.” It also notes that under his leadership, all national rallies were canceled, and that he repurposed the Good Sam Man as the mascot for Gander Outdoors. The passage questions whether members find this interesting or offensive and whether they care.

Apple has reportedly shelved plans to make a lighter, cheaper version of the Vision Pro and instead will focus on lightweight AI smart glasses, similar to Meta’s products. The Vision Pro, introduced in 2024 after a spring 2023 showcase, has not “made much of a splash,” and Apple has allegedly stopped working on the cheaper headset while potentially releasing a near-future Vision Pro with a better chip. Despite this, the passage says the Vision Pro’s main issues—being expensive, bulky, and unclear in purpose—remain, with Apple executives acknowledging shortcomings privately. The article compares this to Meta’s Ray-Ban Display glasses, which may sell more than Vision Pro devices, but it also notes that it has yet to be shown that many people want to wear face computers in general, including in non-work settings.

The passage praises Doug Weight as a key player who made important saves during the playoffs, noting that if he doesn’t play the team would miss him but has other centermen who can fill the role. It says the team needs to improve by getting to the net, attacking more effectively, creating traffic, and pressuring him when he comes out of the net. The speaker looks forward to Saturday, describing the previous game as tough but the team as resilient and refocused, with an extra rest day to prepare. They emphasize competing and battling every night, being physical, and playing better as a team to close out the series and win.

The speaker says winning the Stanley Cup is the biggest accomplishment of their career, but they believe players must continuously prove themselves and must turn their game around after a poor start. They describe returning from playing in Finland as a tough decision that paid off, and say they stayed level emotionally after scoring because showing emotion could affect play. In the finals, they recall becoming nervous early at home after losing track of a puck, then dealing with pressure from Vancouver while faking nerves. They also discuss the Conn Smythe Trophy as an honor, mentioning reading names on it, and conclude that it is not just them and not Bergie.

The passage says Taylor Swift is credited as the sole writer on more than 60 songs across her career, meaning she composed the lyrics and melodies alone. It lists many of these songs in loose chronological order, including “Our Song,” “Love Story,” “Dear John,” “Red,” and “The Black Dog,” along with track details from various releases such as “Taylor Swift,” “Fearless,” “Speak Now,” “Red,” “Lover,” “Folklore,” “Evermore,” “Midnights,” and “The Tortured Poets Department.” It also notes she has co-produced and co-wrote her latest album with Max Martin and Shellback, but is still credited as the lead writer on every song she has released.

The passage introduces MIT OpenCourseWare’s “Nuts and Bolts of New Ventures and Business Plans” course, explaining that it focuses on planning and executing a new venture rather than treating the business plan as a fixed document. The instructor describes the course’s basis in entrepreneurial thinking, emphasizing two core tasks: creating value and capturing value to sustain it. He outlines the course’s goals, content approach across six evenings, and the audience background and interests. The passage also reviews business plan basics: why planning matters (especially given time as a scarce resource), what a plan should include (e.g., executive summary and market/economics topics), how plans function as “selling documents,” and typical reasons plans fail to attract investment, such as an insignificant market, non-credible technology, or poor market understanding. The session concludes with discussion prompts and plans for team formation and a later pitch-focused segment.

Officials at several public Texas universities have instructed faculty to review syllabi and course content to remove material not aligned with current federal and state laws and executive orders, as well as state course manuals. At San Jacinto College, faculty were asked to ensure course outcomes and content align with coordinating board manuals; the college said it does not intend to bar instruction on transgender identity. The article describes directives at Texas Tech and Angelo State that, by Friday, prohibited Texas Tech employees from teaching about or acknowledging transgender identity, citing federal and state laws recognizing only two sexes. It also notes similar compliance actions underway at Texas A&M University after leadership changes related to a gender identity lecture, and that FIRE is encouraging faculty to report censorship. A senior attorney quoted in the passage says the directives are voluntary efforts to censor and are not supported by the executive order, describing them as contradictory to the First Amendment.

The lecture reviews countable-state Markov processes built from an embedded Markov chain and exponential holding times, describing how steady-state behavior depends on quantities involving the embedded chain’s stationary probabilities and the state-dependent leaving rates. It notes that when a key sum is infinite, transition rates go to zero and steady-state probabilities become meaningless, illustrated by an example of a “hyperactive” birth/death process that appears stable via embedded-chain transition probabilities but lacks a meaningful steady-state because transition rates vanish. The lecture then discusses reversibility for Markov processes, relating backward and forward transition rates and giving a condition connecting reversibility of the process to reversibility/positive recurrence of the embedded chain, including a “guessing theorem” for irreducible processes. Applications include Burke’s theorem for M/M/1 queues and extensions to tandem queues, followed by a transition to random walks and their role in threshold-crossing problems, queuing delays, and hypothesis testing that lead to Bayesian formulations and eventually random-walk analysis.

A U.S. soldier, Charles Robert Jenkins, who deserted to North Korea in 1965, died in Japan at age 77. He told a Japanese court martial in 2004 that he deserted to avoid hazardous duty and combat, drank heavily that night, and walked toward North Korea with a rifle. In North Korea, he taught English to soldiers and acted in a propaganda film, and he later met and married Hitomi Soga. Soga returned to Japan in 2002, and Jenkins and their daughters followed in 2004 after a 30-day sentence for desertion. Jenkins later lived in Sado, worked in a gift shop, and wrote a book; a Sado town official confirmed his death without further details.

The passage consists of multiple classified memoranda and related notes from February to March 1983 involving U.S.–Soviet discussions. It describes Reagan’s review of several staff memos (with Reagan initialing them), cover notes from William Clark and others, and marginal comments by individuals such as “JH” and George Shultz. It includes a diary entry stating that George Shultz arranged a two-hour meeting with Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin at the White House, where Reagan said he wanted George to serve as a direct contact channel with Andropov. Other entries note that Shultz’s schedule affected reading time of a memo, that a later memo was forwarded to Reagan, and that meetings took place at the White House residence and in the Secretary’s office at the Pentagon, with documents prepared and cleared by named staff.

The passage explains how to disable the drop shadow automatically added to screenshots in macOS High Sierra. It says to open Terminal and run `defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow true`, then run `killall SystemUIServer` and take a screenshot to test. If it does not work, it may require restarting the Mac. To re-enable shadows, the same command is used with `false`, followed by `killall SystemUIServer`.

Between 2014 and 2015, the use of sanitary protection increased from 50.7% to 54%, but IndiaSpend reported that a government scheme for promoting sanitary napkins among girls aged 10–19 (launched in 2011, covering rural areas in 107 districts across 17 states) has faced multiple problems. These include poor quality and delayed or irregular supply, low or uneven utilization of funds, lack of awareness and inadequate ASHA training/meetings, and unsafe disposal due to napkins being non-biodegradable. Expenditure rose from Rs 24.33 billion (2014–15) to Rs 37.03 billion (2016–17), while utilization rates varied by year and were low nationally. Reports cited that in some places napkins ran out, quality was poor, distribution was irregular or absent, and uptake was hindered by low sales. A separate CAG report highlighted that allocated funds for safe disposal choolas were only partially used.

The passage describes UHS-II interface selection and initialization sequences, including how a UHS-II host enables SD Bus and UHS-II interfaces after power-up, waits for STB.L detection with a 200 µs timeout, and falls back to SD Bus I/F mode if STB.L is not detected. It outlines the UHS-II initialization steps (PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration with unique 4-bit IDs, configuration including UHS-II registers, and SD-TRAN initialization), notes SD-TRAN behavior with CMD0, and gives related UHS-II interface deactivation and VDD2 handling rules. It also provides background on bus speed mode support for UHS-II/UHS-III, host-card command/control roles, card identification vs. data transfer modes, key command sequences such as CMD0/CMD3/CMD8/ACMD41, and requirements for card initialization and timing. Additional sections describe performance class metrics, cache and maintenance features, command queue schemes, SD bus initialization and state transitions, and extend into command system topics like APP_CMD (CMD55) and CMD6 function switching, including power limit behavior and constraints for different UHS modes.

The passage says that brains need regular exercise and daily attention, like muscles, and that managing emotions is a skill. It describes the goal of brain training as accepting that feelings change and will pass, rather than seeking perfect happiness. Jamie suggests that taking time each day can reduce emotional impact, prevent panic from making things worse, and support happiness over perfection. It then outlines a seven-step process to train the mind to release worries, gain perspective, and feel happier: (1) internal check-in by recognizing and labeling emotions, (2) slow belly breathing for stress relief, (3) write and let go by journaling and tearing up the paper, (4) reframe with gratitude, (5) play a mindful mini game or calming activity, (6) do compassion challenges such as forgiving or expressing appreciation, and (7) spread “good vibes” by helping someone else, with studies cited that thinking of others correlates with greater happiness.

The passage addresses accusations that the Government, possibly the Executive, “edited” or “doctored” an electoral reforms Bill. It explains that a Bill is a draft law, generally drawn up by a government department under a minister, approved by Cabinet, then submitted to Parliament. It describes the Law Commission’s role in reviewing and recommending changes, with recommendations passing through the Executive and relevant minister before becoming a Bill. The author argues the accusations are inconsistent with this process and result from misinformation, adding that Parliament debates and shapes bills to align with constitutional and public aspirations.

The passage describes a framework for explaining why macroscopic dynamics of large-scale systems can become asymptotically linear under spatial averaging, even when individual microscopic elements have nonlinear dynamics. It reports that, in empirical and simulation studies of large-scale brain networks, linear models can effectively capture macroscopic behavior across many subjects and modalities, despite theoretical expectations of neuron-level nonlinearity. The work aims to provide a theoretical foundation for stochastic nonlinear systems by extending results from mixing sequences, particularly using tools from probability theory such as the central limit theorem and strong mixing sequences. The authors develop technical contributions including generalizations of ρ-mixing theory, proofs that spatially averaged state dynamics become asymptotically linear (and under additional assumptions linear time-invariant), and an analysis of the convergence rate to linearity depending on subsystem correlations. The later sections establish notation and introduce background on mixing sequences, including definitions and a central limit theorem for ρ-mixing sequences, along with multivariate extensions and the concept of a residual factor.

A Business Insider virtual event, held September 30 and sponsored by Fidelity Investments, brought together experts to discuss IPO strategy and best practices. Speakers said companies preparing for IPOs face shifting investor expectations and new regulatory demands, and that staying private longer provides more time to get ready. Advice included maintaining focus by hiring experts for the IPO process, preparing for regulatory reporting, shareholder and disclosure requirements, and employee compensation, and planning for the time and resources needed to become public. Panelists also emphasized having the right people, tools, technology, and compensation packages, surrounding leaders with appropriate investors, working with the right broker to unlock liquidity, and communicating regularly with employees about IPO performance and expectations.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Current Report on Form 8-K dated July 30, 2020. The filing states that on July 30, 2020, Amazon announced its second quarter 2020 financial results, with related press release and non-GAAP financial measures information included as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, respectively. The report also lists Exhibit 104 as Inline XBRL cover page content and includes signatures showing Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, signed the report on July 30, 2020.

The lecture reviews a master path-integral formula for time-ordered operator products and applies it to interacting theories by splitting the action into a free part and an interaction part (with the interaction Hamiltonian differing by a minus sign under assumptions stated). Treating the interaction term as small, it derives an exact expression for interacting correlation functions in terms of free-theory correlation functions and then expands it perturbatively. For a specific interaction \( \lambda \phi^4 \), it works through the two-point function to first order, using Wick’s theorem to reduce contractions to products of free propagators, and shows cancellations among terms. The discussion then motivates Feynman diagrams and Feynman rules in coordinate and momentum space, including how to assign symmetry (combinatorial) factors and how translation symmetry enforces momentum conservation at vertices. It concludes by presenting momentum-space Feynman rules and giving a sample momentum-space expression for a second-order diagram.

SOS Defensive “Do’s” include pressuring ball to side, corner, or base checkpoints using SET (on dribble) and SMOTHER (when dribble is picked up), and using contact pass denial positions when one pass away. It also calls for contact “fronts” on deep post ups, specific post-trap rules depending on where the post receives the ball, “Box Pressure” in wing areas directing the ball to corners/baseline, denying drives to the middle, and providing backside help with Helpside “I” alignment. The passage describes rotations after passes out of traps, switching with contact on off-ball screens using “Screen/Over/Switch,” and using various contact traps in set situations, mismatches, corner areas, and baseline checkpoint penetrations. On shot attempts, it instructs to box out, get hands on the ball, and “flood the boards” with all five defenders. It defines sideline push checkpoints (corners, free throw line extended, baseline, half court) to keep the ball out of the middle “Red Zone,” outlines wing push/turn/cross-switch actions, and describes Helpside “I” alignments (Low/High/Top) including Double “I,” Triple “I,” and Triangle “I” sideline and baseline traps, with near-player closeouts and rotations when a pass leaves the passer’s hands.

The passage discusses Netflix’s documentary “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish,” about a junior high harassment case in Beal City, Michigan. It follows Lauryn Licari and her boyfriend Owen McKenny receiving threatening, hateful, and sexually graphic messages from an unknown number that escalate over months, including threats against Lauryn’s life. Local investigations fail, leading the sheriff to involve the FBI, which requests a forensic examination of Owen’s phone. The author criticizes the documentary’s limited explanation of cellphone forensics and discusses how phone and provider records can reveal information for law enforcement. The passage then shifts to the author’s view on cellphone use in schools, noting Oklahoma’s “bell to bell” policy for 2025–2026 that restricts phones and similar internet-capable devices, amid backlash. The author concludes that excessive cellphone access can create serious problems and that everyone can become a suspect due to spoofing.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K stating that on June 22, 2016 it consummated the issuance and sale of $1,377,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 4.15% Notes due 2046. The Notes were issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 and an officer’s certificate dated June 22, 2016, pursuant to a subscription agreement dated June 7, 2016. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 22 and December 22 each year, beginning December 22, 2016, and on June 22, 2046 at maturity. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The filing identifies related documents and exhibits, including the subscription agreement, officer’s certificate, and forms of notes.

The passage describes methods for generating valid molecules with large language models (LLMs) and the challenges of invalid outputs. It compares SMILES and SELFIES representations, noting that SMILES requires strict syntax rules while SELFIES guarantees 100% validity even for randomly generated strings. However, experiments show LLMs perform worse with SELFIES than with SMILES, and LLM-based correction of invalid SMILES tends to reduce other evaluation metrics. The paper proposes “Invalid SELFIES Editing,” which generates SELFIES directly with LLMs and filters out non-alphabet symbols to ensure validity. It also proposes “LLMs as post-hoc invalid SMILES correctors” using iterative generation with external verification (RDKit), though this reduces metrics. Finally, it presents SmiSelf, a cross-chemical language framework that converts invalid SMILES into SELFIES via grammatical rules using molecular graphs as intermediaries, then converts back to SMILES, guaranteeing 100% validity while preserving or improving other metrics. Experiments are conducted on text-based and class-specific molecule generation tasks using the ChEBI-20 dataset, and the conclusion states that SmiSelf expands practical LLM applications in biomedicine, though correction may introduce distortion relative to ground truth.

The passage discusses Mike Peca’s consistency and recognition at awards dinners, noting he has won the Selke Trophy and received at least one other nomination. The speaker says their organization’s goal over nine years with the North Stars and Dallas Stars has been to win the Stanley Cup and remain competitive, and expresses anticipation for participating in the finals. The speaker also describes unrestricted free agency as a newer opportunity in the NHL, which their team tried early on without success, and says player contributions have been positive for both the players and the team.

Semiconductor diodes’ unidirectional conductivity motivates the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where forward and reverse critical currents differ and a current applied between them preserves a zero-resistance state in one direction while exiting superconductivity when reversed. The SDE requires inversion symmetry breaking and time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking, typically achieved using non-centrosymmetric superconductors, heterojunctions, and external magnetic fields or proximity effects. The study reports field-free SDE in strained NbSe2. By applying uniaxial stress through a curved substrate to create stressed regions, transport measurements show forward critical current larger than reverse at zero field, while no SDE appears in non-stressed regions. Under magnetic field, different devices show either B-even, B-odd, or mixed symmetry in the difference of critical currents (ΔIc) and diode efficiency (η); the maximum under zero field is ΔIc = 286 μA and η = 6.76%. A theoretical explanation attributes the behavior to two spatially orthogonal non-reciprocal mechanisms activated independently by stress and magnetic field: a stress-activated real-space polarization mechanism producing B-even SDE along the armchair direction, and a field-activated valley-polarization/finite-momentum pairing mechanism producing B-odd SDE along the zigzag direction. Devices are fabricated using Al nanoridges, h-BN spacers, exfoliated NbSe2 flakes, and gold electrodes, with electrical measurements performed using PPMS with standard instrumentation.

Fitch Ratings affirmed Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc.’s Long-Term Issuer Default Rating of 'A-' and short-term rating of 'F2', as well as its existing senior unsecured debt ratings at 'A-' and short-term ratings at 'F2'. Fitch revised the Rating Outlook to Positive from Stable, citing improved operating performance, stronger credit metrics, in-line performance with upgrade triggers, a strong balance sheet and financial flexibility, strong operating performance and cash flow generation, and a top-tier competitive position. It noted contingent reputation, litigation, and regulatory risks, but said they are manageable, and described strong liquidity (reported $1 billion cash and equivalents at Dec. 31, 2016 and a $1.5 billion credit facility expiring November 2020) and expectations for free cash flow growth and continued strength in key operating and leverage metrics. Fitch listed key rating triggers for upgrades and potential return to a Stable Outlook, and provided a full list of affirmed ratings and the Positive Outlook.

The Beerepoot family, owners of Melita Honey Farm in Tasmania, will have their home auctioned in three weeks after failing to pay council rates since 2010 because they believe the land is owned by God. In a letter to the Meander Valley council, the family said they cannot bow to a false god and that they believe the Heavenly Father is sovereign. Meander Valley mayor Craig Perkins said the family had not contacted the council since a real estate agent was appointed and that the property will be auctioned on September 1 at 11am, assuming unpaid monies are not paid first. The council resolved in March to sell three properties after $9,332 in rates was outstanding; two properties were paid in June, but the “Blue Wren Hideaway” was not. When asked about paying before the auction, owner Fanny Beerepoot said there was “not really much to talk about.” The council said the family maintained the belief that the land was not theirs and that the matter was between the family and God. The council’s March agenda noted prior legal action included police seizing and selling an old motor vehicle; proceeds from that action and from the property sale, minus unpaid rates, will be given to the family. Perkins said the decision was difficult and that ratepayers could still pay.

The passage describes OpenAI’s rollout of ChatGPT Instant Checkout, which allows purchases directly within an AI chat using OpenAI–Stripe’s commerce and payments protocol, the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP). ACP launches first with U.S. sellers and is planned to expand to over a million merchants, with examples including Glossier, Skims, Spanx, and Vuori. The protocol is open-source and could be adopted by other AI assistants, potentially spreading conversational shopping widely and shifting how online shopping works and how brands market products. OpenAI’s product lead says the protocol was designed to be easy for merchants and developers to adopt, aiming to reduce integration work and help grow sales, though adopting it may involve ceding some control and paying transaction fees. To be included in ChatGPT’s Instant Checkout results, brands need to provide structured product data such as rich product feeds with up-to-date descriptions, prices, and availability. The passage also raises questions about how recommendations will be determined and whether vendors could pay for better placement, noting that ChatGPT recommendations are fully AI-driven and that more high-quality product information improves the chance of relevant results.

Scientists studying brown recluse spiders observed them using spinnerets to “sew” silk strands into an industrial-strength material composed of multiple micro-loops. The research, published in *Materials Horizons*, suggests that applying the spider’s thin, flat silk and loop-forming technique to synthetic materials could improve space-travel protective webs, lightweight bungee cords, and cords used in parachutes. The scientists have not yet made a man-made version, but they developed mathematical models of the web’s structure and properties and submitted a patent application for a spider-inspired synthetic product, describing the approach as needing no petroleum, toxic substances, high temperatures, and almost no energy.

Engravings at Jebel Misma in the Nefud desert were made more than 12,000 years ago by early nomadic people who entered the region after a period that made it arid. The rock art includes highlighted human and animal figures, with the Jebel Misma site showing a woman superimposed to indicate scale. Additional engravings found at Jebel Arnaan and Jebel Mleiha date between 12,800 and 11,400 years ago and were likely intended to mark territory or nearby water sources. The petroglyphs were carved in four phases: the earliest phase features small stylized women, later phases show larger human figures, naturalistic animals up to 3 meters long, and finally more stylized “cartoonish” animal depictions. Excavations uncovered stone tools and other objects, and researchers say the engravings indicate a new monumental tradition distinct from earlier regional art. The findings suggest prehistoric humans adapted to climate changes, and that the region had lush periods in the past before becoming one of the driest places by about 6,000 years ago.

The third season finale of the Hero ISL 2016 on December 18 in Kochi drew 54,000 attendees and 41 million television viewers, according to BARC. STAR India reported a 41% rise in total viewers versus 2015 and said ISL was the most viewed televised sport event of the year in Kerala, surpassing other major events. In West Bengal, viewership exceeded IPL 9 finals. Total viewership for the season was 216 million versus around 207 million last year, with rural India at 101 million. Metro markets such as Mumbai and Chennai recorded increases of over 50%, and Tamil Nadu saw a 20% viewership spike. The league also saw over 25% growth in overall viewer engagement versus ISL 2015, doubling total watchtime to 2.3 times over the prior year, including on the on and Jio platform.

Rory Barnes of the University of Washington reports that many exoplanets found by high-powered telescopes will likely be tidally locked, with one side permanently facing their host star. In his accepted paper, “Tidal Locking of Habitable Exoplanets,” he questions the assumption that only smaller, dimmer stars can host synchronously orbiting planets, and he explores broader possibilities such as different initial rotation periods, larger planet sizes, and eccentric orbits. He argues that models allowing initial rotations that could be much larger than several hours increase the likelihood of tidal locking, including scenarios where a planet with a four-day initial “day” could already be tidally locked. He also states that tidal locking may be moderated by atmospheric winds, and he found that every potentially habitable planet likely detected by NASA’s TESS will probably be tidally locked. Barnes says that determining whether an exoplanet is tidally locked will be important for future efforts to search for life, and the research was funded by NASA.

Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said the yen is vulnerable to rising political tensions related to North Korea’s missile and nuclear weapons programs, warning against extreme currency instability. He said the yen is often viewed as a safe-haven currency, but that North Korea-related tensions make it “extremely unstable,” and declined to comment on exchange rates, saying currencies should be set by markets. Aso also urged Japan and 10 other nations to move forward with the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) trade deal excluding the United States, saying the remaining countries should proceed and that the U.S. may rejoin later, though it will take time.

The passage describes how industrial simulation, modeling, and data analytics—supported by CAD/CAM/CAE tools and increasingly 3D displays—are used to improve product development and production while meeting goals such as speeding time to market, reducing costs, and supporting decision-making. It reports that respondents view innovation as a major benefit and that deployment is expected to rise across multiple value-creation stages, with growing use of high-performance data analytics and digital twins. It also explains that high-performance computing (HPC) is increasingly important due to the need for complex calculations, and that many enterprises plan to expand or adopt HPC environments, often via external infrastructure or HPC-as-a-Service (HPCaaS), to address time, quality, and scalability needs. Challenges highlighted include data silo issues, security risks, high energy consumption, compute-performance limits, downtime, expertise shortages, and investment and operating costs. The passage concludes that routine use of HPC-enabled simulations and strong data integration strategies are expected to support digital transformation and new digital products, services, and business models.

Oil prices rose about 1.5% after OPEC+ announced a smaller-than-expected production increase. The group agreed to raise output by 137,000 barrels per day starting in November, which eased oversupply fears and supported prices. Brent crude rose to around $65.44 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate to about $61.77, with analysts viewing the decision as a stabilising, cautious approach. OPEC+ internal debate included arguments for a larger hike versus restraint due to subdued demand and rising inventories, and analysts warned gains may be short-lived given uneven demand and slower consumption. The move reinforced OPEC+’s role in balancing global energy markets while avoiding a supply surge.

The lecturer reviews how extending the black hole metric across the horizon gives four spacetime regions and explains that requiring regularity in Euclidean signature makes Euclidean time periodic, turning the \(rt\) plane into a disc where the horizon is the disc region. This periodicity implies the spacetime theory is at finite temperature, with temperature determined by surface gravity; a similar argument applies to the Rindler case where \(\theta\) must be periodic with period \(2\pi\), giving a temperature for local observers.  

The lecture then discusses physical meaning of this temperature in terms of quantum field theory in curved spacetime: vacuum choice is not unique and depends on the time used. For the black hole, compactifying Euclidean time yields the Hartle–Hawking vacuum (thermal equilibrium and regularity at the horizon), while not compactifying yields the Schwarzschild (Boulware) vacuum, which can be singular at the horizon. The lecturer argues Hartle–Hawking is more physical because observables remain regular at the horizon.  

Finally, the lecturer uses the Rindler example to explain the origin of temperature by showing that the Minkowski vacuum, when described in Rindler coordinates, appears as an entangled state between left and right Rindler regions; tracing out the inaccessible left region produces a thermal density matrix for the right region with \(\beta=2\pi\) in Rindler time.

The passage explains the role of research funding agencies in advancing science and national research performance, noting that funded papers often have higher citation impact and that funding allocation efficiency can be assessed through project publication outcomes and acknowledgements. It contrasts block and project-based funding models across countries and describes Ukraine’s science system, publication requirements, and key funding agencies (NASU, MESU, NRFU), including how Russia’s full-scale war shifted resources away from research and reduced research budgets.  

The study analyzes Scopus-indexed articles with Ukrainian author affiliations published from 2020–2023 (before and during the 2022 invasion) to examine how foreign co-funding, authorship patterns, and citation impact relate, using field-normalised citation impact (FNCI). It finds that the share of articles acknowledging funding increased over time, with MESU/NASU/NRFU-funded shares rising and foreign co-funding remaining common, especially in NASU-funded outputs. Foreign funding is associated with higher citation impact, while Ukrainian-only schemes (notably NASU) tend to lag, with MESU showing an increase in citation impact in 2022–2023. The study concludes that international collaboration is closely linked to higher research visibility and impact and argues for reform in Ukraine’s funding system and for better data infrastructure to track grants centrally.

The passage describes how the 2008 collapse of Northern Rock signaled a wider global financial crisis that led many people to see lower living standards, including frozen or cut wages. It then says that, according to the Office for National Statistics, UK median disposable household income has returned to and is slightly higher than levels before the banking crisis. The passage reports that median disposable income was £27,300 in the financial year ending 2017, up 2.3% year-on-year after accounting for inflation, and about £1,600 higher than in 2008. It also states that while incomes increased across society and inequality fell slightly over the decade, the poorest households benefited more than the richest. It provides figures showing average disposable income of £65,542 for the richest fifth and £12,748 for the bottom fifth, and notes that direct taxes and benefits affect these gaps. Finally, it says disposable income growth has been higher for non-retired than retired households since the crisis, indicating retired households are falling further behind.

The passage describes the spike protein of the SARS-CoV-2 ancestral strain as a key vaccine target and notes that mutations in spike have been associated with breakthrough infections, immune escape, and waning vaccine effectiveness, including low effectiveness against Omicron after six months. It states that booster doses are recommended to augment waning immunity and can increase binding and neutralizing antibody responses; heterologous boosting is described as beneficial versus homologous boosting in prior studies.

It then reports a phase III, multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized study in India evaluating a single heterologous CORBEVAX™ (protein sub-unit) booster given at least 6 months after primary vaccination with either COVAXIN (inactivated) or COVISHIELD™ (viral vector). Adults aged 18–80 without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection were randomized to CORBEVAX™ or placebo (n=416 enrolled; CORBEVAX™ n=156 per primary group; placebo n=52 per group). The primary objective was immunogenicity (virus neutralizing antibodies) at 28 days; secondary objectives included safety/tolerability and additional immune response measures, with exploratory assessment of Omicron and cellular responses.

Results reported that CORBEVAX™ as a heterologous booster was safe and well tolerated, with no serious adverse events/grade-3 adverse events/deaths/AESIs and no study discontinuations due to adverse events. Immunogenicity results indicated superior responses in CORBEVAX™ recipients versus placebo in both primary series groups, including higher neutralizing antibody and anti-RBD IgG measures at day 28, and increased Omicron neutralizing antibody GMTs and responder percentages. Cellular analyses in a subset showed increased IFN-gamma secretion after booster, with IL-4 levels comparable at day 0 and day 28.

Research for the insurance industry found British fire safety tests for building materials are inadequate following the June 2017 Grenfell Tower fire that killed at least 71 people. The research said standard test fires use all-wood, while real fires include plastic (about 20% in actual fires), and that a 20% plastic test fire was 100 degrees Celsius hotter than an all-wood fire. It also found cladding is sometimes tested as a sealed unit, but real installations often have gaps, and materials tested under manufacturers’ conditions may be pierced by vents or ducts. The Fire Protection Association said the cladding test standard requires urgent review, and the Association of British Insurers called for only non-combustible materials and reform of testing to reflect real-world conditions, including mandatory sprinklers in certain buildings and a review elsewhere. The ABI said sprinklers can reduce property insurance premiums by up to 50%, and an independent review’s final report is expected in the next few weeks.

The passage explains that at the end of each tax year taxpayers may either receive money from the government or owe money. Filing taxes late can trigger IRS fees, and not filing may result in forfeited returns and, in serious cases, jail time. The IRS provides a deadline of April 17, and taxpayers can file for an extension to avoid penalties. The IRS reports about $1.1 billion in unclaimed federal income tax refunds for roughly 1 million taxpayers who did not file in 2014, and says there is no penalty for filing a late return if a refund is due. It notes that people may be eligible for refunds even if they were not required to file, including through withheld taxes and benefits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit. If a deadline is missed, the IRS may file substitute returns, which may not account for credits and deductions. If taxes are owed, the IRS may assess penalties and interest, send notices, offer installment agreements, and—after repeated disregard—send a representative, levy assets, or seize and sell property to satisfy the debt.

Colorado is being sought by California for guidance on implementing a regulated recreational cannabis system. Colorado Governor John Hickenlooper will testify on February 14 at a California State Governance and Finance Committee oversight hearing titled “California Cannabis in a Turbulent Time” about Colorado’s experience with cannabis taxes, regulatory timelines, and lessons learned during the creation of its system. The passage notes that California’s medical market was largely unregulated for twenty years and that Proposition 64 requires a taxation and regulatory structure by January 1, 2018—within the same timeframe Colorado had. California Senator Mike McGuire expressed concern that not all rules, including the Track and Trace program, will be in place by the deadline, citing challenges in implementing track-and-trace and resolving uneven tax collection. Local politicians and industry and state officials are also expected to speak, and the hearing will be live-streamed.

The passage describes a laser-diode proximity sensor packaged in a single integrated module, addressing shortcomings of prior art proximity sensors that used small plastic parts, glued glass lenses, and a central barrier. It proposes dispensing optical resin in drops to form lenses over a light-emitting diode and light sensing array, then encapsulating the chips and optical paths in a molding compound that blocks optical cross-talk without needing a plastic cap or central barrier. After molding, the array is polished to expose the lens surfaces, and the modules are singulated by dicing. The passage also outlines alternative embodiments involving baffles, optional outer glass lenses with patterned filters, and other package variations. Manufacturing steps are described from building large substrates with arrays of sensor modules, placing chips and laser diodes, applying and curing optical resin, molding and curing encapsulant, polishing, adding protective covers, and final singulation. Additional embodiments describe a proximity sensor construction with alternative packaging and a “sensor stick” device that integrates multiple sensors (including proximity and environmental sensors) on a common substrate for connection to computing devices.

Automation Anywhere’s Bot Store, described as the world’s first and largest online marketplace for plug-n-play bots, grew 100% in two months after launch, with artificial intelligence as the most popular category. Speech-to-text leads downloads, finance and accounting is the most common business process, SAP is the most prevalent application with 31 bots, and “allocate payments against outstanding invoices” is the most visited bot. Initially, partners and developers provided bots automating repetitive processes or offering API integrations via Automation Anywhere Enterprise RPA; with Automation Anywhere IQ Bot, they can offer native computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning, including pre-trained cognitive bots for document-centric processes such as utility bills, bank statements, settlement instructions, and tax forms. The Bot Store runs on the Automation Anywhere Enterprise platform, is available at https://botstore.automationanywhere.com, and the passage includes related company information about Automation Anywhere.

Arsenal visit Tottenham at Wembley on Sunday for the 50th North London derby during Arsene Wenger’s managerial reign. Arsenal have won 18, drawn 21 and lost 10 of the previous 49 derbies and want to undermine Mauricio Pochettino’s hopes of winning the title from leaders Chelsea. Tottenham fans expect the game to be decided in midfield, believe Arsenal may set up like they did against Manchester City in the FA Cup semi final, and predict a tight 2-1 Spurs win. Arsenal fans cite the FA Cup win and recent league wins as boosting confidence, say the match is about reinforcing their quality, returning to the top four and preventing Spurs from winning the title, and expect either a 2-1 Arsenal win or a 1-1 draw. Wenger’s future is still debated among supporters, with many believing a change is needed.

The passage is a morning news roundup for biotech from The Readout and STAT. It includes headlines such as a new billionaire-backed life sciences investment firm launched by Tony James and led by a former Flagship associate, plus updates on topics including pharma dealmaking after White House praise for Pfizer, a Duchenne drug Medicaid coverage pause recommendation, conversion therapy legal discussion, digital health M&A driven by AI and private equity, venture capital firm rankings, multiple clinical and regulatory updates (including an Orca T cell therapy FDA submission and a Skye obesity drug mid-stage study failure), policy and tariff changes, and various other biotech news items.

The passage discusses parents’ concerns about how to handle children’s belief in Santa, including whether to encourage physical belief, the risk of lying, and how children respond when the myth is revealed. It argues that fantastical beliefs are generally not harmful and are linked to positive developmental outcomes, and that most children stop believing by about age eight. It describes how children’s questions change with age and suggests strategies for parents: offering plausible explanations or evidence to extend belief, redirecting questions to let children develop their own explanations, or providing disconfirming evidence if the myth is to be ended. A study cited in the passage says parents often take the transition harder than children, who typically feel positive. The passage concludes that modest “Santa” gifts can help maintain a positive experience and emphasizes that children should feel loved on Christmas morning.

Three researchers from the U.S., U.K., and Switzerland won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing cryo-electron microscopy, a method the Nobel committee said lets scientists create detailed images of molecules that drive life. The approach “freezes biomolecules” mid-movement and, according to the committee, allows visualization of molecular processes, including individual atoms and how molecular complexes function in their natural environment. The prize is shared by Jacques Dubochet, Joachim Frank, and Richard Henderson. The passage also notes that electron microscopes previously were thought to be limited because their beams destroy biological material, but freezing at extremely low temperatures protected samples. Other recent Nobel Prizes mentioned include Medicine for circadian rhythms and Physics for detecting gravitational waves.

Stephen Hawking, with Yuri Milner, hosted a press conference in April 2016 to announce Breakthrough Starshot. Ten days before his death at age 76, he submitted a paper with Thomas Hertog that could lead to discovering parallel universes. Titled “A Smooth Exit from Eternal Inflation?,” the paper was first submitted in July 2017 and is being considered for publication by a leading journal. It proposes a multiverse theory with infinite parallel universes and suggests an alternate model; it also states that the universe will eventually die out as stars lose energy. Hawking had not won a Nobel Prize, and the award is not given posthumously.

The passage describes a continuation U.S. patent application related to a “Pin Trap Mechanism for Surgical Linear Cutter,” outlining background and detailed components of a linear surgical stapler used to clamp tissue, cut through it, and simultaneously drive staples to seal tissue ends. It explains the stapler’s cartridge half, anvil half, pivoting coupling, clamp lever, firing assembly, staple cartridge, and example surgical operation steps. The passage then describes multiple “pin trap” mechanisms that keep stapler halves releasably coupled at their proximal ends in an open (“hang open”) state while enabling separation via linearly translatable or other biased locking elements, including configurations with slides, biased retention pins, camming surfaces, C-clips, and ejector levers or slides. It also provides examples of claim-like combinations defining locking members, pivot projections, biasing, camming/notch features, and button access for applying threshold forces to decouple the halves.

The passage describes the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) and associated behaviors, versioning, and supported Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). It explains that SEV-ES/SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state so the hypervisor cannot directly access it, and that NAE events let the guest choose which register state to expose via the GHCB. The document standardizes GHCB structure (4 KB, mirrored from SEV-ES VMCB save state area), introduces hypervisor feature advertisement and a minimum required feature set, and outlines protocol mechanisms such as GHCB MSR-based negotiation for protocol versions and the SEV page table encryption bit. It also summarizes changes across GHCB versions and revisions, error handling for malformed inputs, and guest/hypervisor handling of VMGEXIT.

Additionally, the passage covers SEV-SNP secrets and an EFI confidential computing blob configuration table, SNP request/extended request mechanisms (including certificate return), page state change requests, APIC ID list retrieval, VMPL switching, and several SEV-SNP/SEV-ES NAE events (e.g., restricted injection support actions, #HV doorbell page and #HV timer). It further details #VC-driven guest NAE flows and guidance for handling interrupts and NMI/EOI semantics using a shared #HV doorbell page, including host behavior for presenting interrupts/events and performing implicit or explicit EOI handling.

The passage is a list of “Popular Categories” and “Latest Posts” covering numerous trading strategies and topics, including backtests and futures examples for commodities such as gold, copper, crude oil, sugar, lumber, cocoa, heating oil, platinum, palladium, orange juice, coffee, cotton, and corn. It also mentions technical indicators and trading approaches, such as trend following, mean reversion, spread trading, fundamental analysis, arbitrage, and options trading, along with articles on gold diversification and specific indicators like True Strength Index (TSI) and Relative Vigor Index (RVI). The end of the passage includes brief descriptions of some commodities and a note that the site is run by Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette.

As the playoffs progress, the speaker says they feel more comfortable and at ease from one round to the next, though they still feel uptight and jittery at the start of games. They attribute improved relaxation to prior experience with playoff hockey, overtime, disappointments, and pressure situations, including returning from series deficits and having new faces while most players have previous experience. The team is described as physically strong but not small, with players generally sized for strength and prepared to be hit while also playing physical. The speaker says they do not see either team having a distinct speed advantage and believes their own skating and overall strength keep them from being overly outsized. They contrast prior finals experience, noting the level of play rises and teams play their best in the finals; being behind early against the Devils taught them something. They conclude that reaching the finals is exciting, but winning—especially beating Colorado—is the main thrill.

The passage describes an “RSI and moving average” trading strategy implemented in Python. It combines the Relative Strength Indicator (RSI) and a Simple Moving Average (SMA) to identify trade entry points by using RSI oversold/overbought levels (below 30/above 70) together with the relationship between the closing price and the SMA. The strategy’s rules are to buy when the 14-day RSI is below 30 and the closing price is above the 5-day SMA, and to sell when the 14-day RSI is above 70 and the closing price is below the 5-day SMA. The passage explains how RSI and moving averages are calculated, provides code-related descriptions including equity-curve construction based on buy/sell signals, and notes backtesting on Walmart (WMT), with examples of applying the same approach to SPY and QQQ. It also lists performance metrics mentioned for evaluation: annual return, average gain per trade, win ratio, time invested, maximum drawdown, and risk-adjusted return.

Sebastian Vettel won the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix after starting from pole and switching to a one-stop strategy. Late in the race, Mercedes’s Valtteri Bottas closed in as Vettel preserved his worn tyres, but Vettel defended to win by 0.699 seconds. Red Bull’s Daniel Ricciardo and Max Verstappen were eliminated early, while Lewis Hamilton moved up to fourth before fighting for victory. Ferrari and Mercedes used different tyre strategies, with Ferrari initially running Vettel and Kimi Raikkonen on two stops before Bottas’s one-stop approach. A late Ferrari attempt to change strategy failed when Raikkonen left the pits before his stop was completed, forcing his retirement and ensuring Bottas’s pressure in the final laps. Hamilton finished third, Pierre Gasly fourth, Kevin Magnussen fifth, Nico Hulkenberg sixth, Fernando Alonso seventh, Stoffel Vandoorne ninth-tenth gap for McLaren, Marcus Ericsson ninth, and Esteban Ocon rounded out the top 10.

KeyBanc Capital Markets said Fortinet’s shares have gained 23% since the start of 2018 and 45% over the past year, suggesting the stock’s valuation is full. In a downgrade, Rob Owens lowered Fortinet’s rating from Overweight to Sector Weight, with no price target. KeyBanc noted Fortinet remains a standout in network security and still has an emerging cloud opportunity, but said the company’s prior long-term margin expansion target has faded into more of a suggestion. The firm warned this could increase volatility and investor disappointment if Fortinet shifts toward “spend mode” to gain market share at the expense of margins. KeyBanc reported valuation metrics including 13.3x EV/2019 FCF and 4.2x EV/2019 sales forecast, and said that while not particularly expensive historically or relatively, the outlook for more gradual margin expansion makes the risk-reward less favorable than in the past.

The passage describes the Stochastic Indicator Strategy, a technical analysis tool based on the Stochastic Oscillator for identifying potential trend reversals and overbought/oversold conditions. The indicator compares a security’s closing price to its high-low range over a typical 14-period lookback to produce two lines: %K (current price position within the range) and %D (a moving average of %K). Overbought is commonly indicated when %K rises above 80 and oversold when it falls below 20; %K/%D crossovers and divergence between price and the indicator are also used to interpret signals. Timeframes vary by trader, and the strategy’s sensitivity can be adjusted by changing smoothing periods and overbought/oversold thresholds. It can be applied across markets such as stocks, forex, commodities, and cryptocurrencies, and it may help in both range-bound and volatile conditions, though it is not foolproof and can produce false signals, lag in strong trends, and issues under extreme volatility or improper settings. The passage also highlights risk management practices including stop-loss orders, diversification, position sizing, and ongoing monitoring, and notes that combining the Stochastic Indicator with other indicators can provide confirmation and reduce false alarms.

Saudi Aramco cut the official selling price for its lighter oil grades for May cargoes to Asia, lowering Arab Light by 30 cents to a 45-cents discount to Oman-Dubai, and cutting Arab Extra Light by 35 cents to a 60-cents premium; Super Light was cut by 20 cents. OSPs for Arab Medium and Heavy were unchanged. The cuts were the second straight month of reductions despite Saudi Arabia’s role as a major player in an OPEC and allied output cut agreement. The passage links this pricing strategy to increased availability and competition for light crude in Asia from U.S. shale and West Africa, noting that Brent-Dubai swap values have moved up since a late-February low. It also cites data showing the Middle East’s share of Asia’s crude imports falling in March, while Western exporters’ share rose, and concludes that producers may be pushing light grades into Asia while reducing heavier shipments to meet output commitments.
