Due to continued icy weather, thousands of schools across the country closed on Monday. Several schools in and around the Warwick District and in the Rugby Borough will remain closed today (Tuesday), with the list provided above of the specific schools that will continue to be closed; it may be updated if more schools announce closures.

Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is increasing, affecting 10–19% of patients receiving conventional cancer therapies. This study investigated whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with CTRCD. Using TriNetX data (patients aged ≥18 with cancer treated with cardiotoxic antineoplastic therapies, excluding those with ischemic confounding conditions), researchers compared outcomes over 1 year between patients prescribed GLP-1 RAs and those not, using propensity-score matching and multivariable models. Among 12,410 identified patients, 1,223 remained in each group after matching. The GLP-1 RA group had a lower primary composite outcome (heart failure exacerbation, death, or hospital/ED admission) and significant survival benefit. Secondary outcomes showed significant reductions in mortality, heart failure, and all-cause hospital admissions, while effects on atrial fibrillation/flutter and ventricular tachycardia were not statistically significant. The study reports limitations including its observational design, reliance on clinical documentation, missing details on therapy combinations, limited demographic diversity, and a 1-year follow-up. The authors conclude that GLP-1 RAs may be a promising option for reducing major cardiovascular adverse outcomes in CTRCD.

The Under Secretary of State (Welles) met with Finland’s Minister, who asked about Finland–United States relations. Welles said he had been away and had not reviewed recent developments, while the Minister repeatedly expressed hope that relations would not deteriorate or be severed. Welles stated that because the United States was at war, it could not maintain normal relations with any country actively assisting the Axis powers, and argued that Finland’s assistance to Germany in fighting Russia would constitute active assistance to the United States’ enemy. Welles said the United States had pursued a patient policy toward Finland, but that major offensive operations by Finland against the Soviet Union would be regrettable. The Minister sought limits on what Finland could do militarily and information about conversations between Stalin and Mr. Eden, which Welles said he could not provide. The Minister provided a copy of Finland’s President’s address to Parliament. A later telegram to the Swedish Minister of State (Johnson) suggested pressing Swedish officials to urge Finland not to participate in further offensives against the Soviet Union, citing concerns about collaboration with German forces. Another telegram reported that a new trade agreement between Germany and Finland was signed, including statements about continued German economic support and Finland’s delivery of products, and an additional agreement on exchanges between Finland and Norway.

Jane Goodall said the urgency of wildlife conservation is greater now than when she began, warning that continuing business as usual will be too late. She cited concerns including poaching and deforestation, and described climate change as the threat most likely to cause long-term damage. She expressed cautious optimism, noting that there is still some time to act before some climate change impacts become irreversible. The comments precede the release of a new documentary, *Jane*, using 50-year-old archival footage about her early work with chimpanzees in Tanzania, and she hopes viewers will better understand chimpanzees and take action.

A Tennessee woman, Kimberly Jones, posted a video on Facebook of her son Keaton describing being bullied at middle school, including insults about his appearance and being doused with milk and ham being put on his clothes. The video drew over 18 million views and a crowdsourcing page raised more than $29,000 for his future education. Athletes and entertainers responded with offers to support Keaton, including invitations to visit games and visit him at school, as well as messages encouraging him and opposing bullying.

The passage describes parachutes made using the Japanese art of kirigami, with perforated disks that can be used for humanitarian aid drops or package delivery. It includes an image showing a water bottle being lowered by a parachute made of a Mylar disk with cuts that let it unfurl as the bottle falls.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew S. Fastow with Jeffrey McMahon amid investor concern and an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow ran. Lay said restoring investor confidence required replacing Fastow, who was placed on leave while McMahon took over as CFO. Reports described Enron’s stock falling sharply following the partnerships controversy, with related charges including a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and other losses tied to ending or unwinding partnership relationships. Multiple outlets and analysts said Enron’s disclosures were unclear and that the move might not fully address uncertainty about Enron’s complex financial arrangements and potential future impacts.

Researchers reported that in metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma patients treated with avelumab, non-progression during anti-PD-L1 therapy correlates with gains in health-related quality of life. Using data from the JAVELIN Merkel 200 Phase II trial, they found that reductions in tumor size were associated with improvements in patients’ health status measured by generic and skin cancer-specific HRQoL instruments. The authors said this supports the idea that immunotherapy may improve quality of life in coordination with lack of disease progression.

The speaker reflects on imagining coaching in the Stanley Cup finals and says winning has not felt like a marathon, describing the Detroit Red Wings as the best team and defending Stanley Cup champions. They emphasize the importance of beating top teams and the value of leadership, character, and experience from players, citing examples such as Brian Bellows and Tikkanen, and highlighting Scotty Bowman’s ability to adjust and be flexible across different player generations. The speaker also discusses support from management and family excitement, their team’s lack of intimidation despite respecting the Red Wings, and how they used an astronaut metaphor to motivate players by dedicating games to special people. They plan to adapt strategies based on individual matchups, note the importance of humor and a team atmosphere, and describe goalie performance and the finals matchup as highly competitive and exciting.

The passage describes a respiratory assistance system and related methods for humidifying respiratory gases. It includes a gas source, humidification apparatus with a humidification chamber and chamber heater, and delivery to a patient via a conduit and patient interface, with the goal of heating and humidifying gases so they mimic unassisted inspiration. The system includes a controller that determines characteristics of the respiratory gases (such as flow rate, breathing pattern, bias flow rate, reverse flow/rebreathing detection, and temperature measurements) to determine a type of gas source (e.g., air entraining versus non-air entraining). Based on this determination, the controller can generate indicators for a user, adjust heater temperature set points (including lowering set point for air entraining sources), and control chamber heater and optionally conduit heater operation using inputs from sensors (inlet/outlet sensors, flow sensors, temperature sensors, and optional humidity sensor). The passage also describes embodiments for automatically detecting connected hardware components (such as an expiratory conduit/heater wire adapter) and for automatically determining configuration components and settings, including user interface workflows and safety modes. Detailed control logic is described for determining bias flow rate and detecting rebreathing using measured flow profiles (including comparing inlet/outlet sensor signals, gradients, phase lengths, and cross-correlation), which can be used to infer the gases source and determine whether set point compensation is required. The passage further outlines example system components, configurations (single- versus dual-limb, presence/absence of expiratory conduit), and associated sensor placement and control strategies.

CeeDee Lamb has missed the last two games with a high-ankle sprain. After being given time to return, he practiced using resistance bands for the second straight day, with Wednesday marking the first time he did that type of work since his injury. ESPN’s Todd Archer said Lamb is making progress and suggested he should not be ruled out for the next week’s game, guessing a Week 7 return rather than Week 6.

Solomon Dalung, Nigeria’s Minister of Youth and Sports Development, said President Muhammadu Buhari’s 2015 election victory showed that candidates can win without money and described a political shift against “god-fatherism.” He said “god-fatherism” is meant to control elected officials and test loyalty, and criticized “urban gorillas” for manipulating Nigeria’s political system and depriving him of victories despite repeated elections. Speaking at the UN Headquarters in New York at the Seventh Economic and Social Council Youth Forum, he discussed youth’s role in building sustainable and resilient communities and said “Not too Young to Run” signals to political leaders to step aside. Dalung also urged youth to understand the political system, said Nigeria is making steady progress in infrastructure, economy, and security, and called for unity, while advocating engagement with neighbors regarding armed herdsmen. He noted ministers often lack houses and live in rented apartments. Earlier, Ambassador Samson Itegboje commended the federal government’s progress and pledged continued expertise to represent Nigeria internationally.

Epidemiological studies cited in the passage report that people with compromised immune systems, such as those with HIV, have higher cancer incidence, and that before HAART AIDS-defining cancers had poor prognosis. While HAART reduced the risk of AIDS-defining cancers, non-AIDS defining malignancies are increasing among people with HIV. The passage states that cancer risk mechanisms in HIV remain poorly understood and may involve factors such as occupational exposure to toxic metals and hazardous chemicals, which could disrupt immunological and non-immune surveillance systems, including p53-dependent pathways.  

The study described is a cross-sectional study in Nigeria including 128 HIV-positive and 120 HIV-negative adults (age mean 38.35 ± 0.72 years), divided into four groups based on HIV status and occupational chemical exposure (HPE n=62, HPU n=66, HNE n=60, HNU n=60). Participants were tested for HIV using a national algorithm and underwent measurements including CD4 counts (CDC categories), serum p53 and bcl2 (ELISA), oxidative/genotoxic markers 8OHdG and MDA (and SOD activity), and BMI.  

Results reported that in the occupationally exposed group, p53 and bcl2 levels were lower in HIV-positive participants than in HIV-negative participants, and MDA levels were higher in HIV-positive exposed participants than in HIV-negative exposed participants. CD4 counts were lower in HIV-positive participants in both exposed and unexposed occupational categories, with no association between occupational exposure and CD4 categories within HIV-positive or HIV-negative groups. The passage also reports positive correlations between p53/bcl2 and 8OHdG and SOD, and a negative correlation between CD4 and MDA. Multiple regression (adjusted for sex, age, BMI, and cigarette smoking) found HIV status and SOD activity associated with p53 and bcl2. The discussion concludes that immune deficiency, antioxidant deficits, oxidative stress, and dysregulation of apoptosis may contribute to genomic instability and elevated cancer risk, and calls for preventive interventions.

The passage describes temperature sensing, calibration, and several device subsystems and peripherals for MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers. It explains that the temperature sensor outputs a voltage that linearly changes with device temperature and is connected internally to an ADC channel for temperature-to-digital conversion, using a factory-provided calibration value in the factory constants memory region to estimate device temperature. It also outlines the Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) including a Real Time Clock and an asynchronous IWDT, and summarizes the VREF module (internal selectable 1.4V/2.5V references and external reference support), comparator (voltage comparison with additional features), and security/CRC features. Further sections briefly cover UART, I2C, SPI, watchdog timers (IWDT/WWDT), RTC_B functions, timer capabilities, analog and I/O connection management, debug interfaces (SWD and DEBUGSS), and factory constants and identification registers. The latter part includes notes on a typical application schematic, TI development/support information, and general packaging/mechanical/disclaimer content.

The passage describes grim Arctic conditions, including near the North Pole temperatures about 20°C warmer than average last year, and states scientists have proposed “refreezing” the Arctic by installing about 10 million wind-powered pumps to spray sea water over the ice. The cited plan estimates the added pumping could increase sea ice thickness by about 1 metre and reduce the risk of summer sea ice disappearing. It predicts effects such as pushing the timeline back by 17 years if implemented early in the 2030s, and discusses pump numbers ranging from roughly 10 million (over 10% of the Arctic Ocean) to about 100 million (over the entire Arctic), along with large steel requirements and costs estimated around US$500 billion. The passage also references earlier Arctic geoengineering proposals, argues that current emissions-reduction efforts may be insufficient, and links Arctic changes to extreme weather patterns via jet stream disruptions.

Germany’s Federal Cartel Office has launched an investigation into online retailer Temu to determine whether the platform influences independent merchants’ pricing in ways that violate competition rules. Authorities, led by Andreas Mundt, will examine whether Temu’s internal policies impose constraints that distort fair market pricing and whether its algorithmic and pricing tools give it excessive control over third-party listings. Temu, operated by Whaleco Technology Limited, says it complies with European competition law and is cooperating, adding that its platform model supports competitive pricing. The investigation is part of increased European scrutiny of major digital marketplaces, and if violations are confirmed, Temu could face penalties or be required to change merchant terms.
The Third Circuit Court of Appeals examined the record in light of the appellants’ brief and oral argument and found no error. The district court’s judgment is affirmed.

Capacities for genomic surveillance increased during the COVID-19 pandemic, enabling close real-time monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOC). In Connecticut (USA), Alpha emerged in late 2020 and was followed by Beta, Gamma, and Delta in 2021; Omicron then rapidly displaced Delta globally in late 2021. In 2022, transmission remained high and Omicron lineages repeatedly replaced one another. Using Yale genomic surveillance samples from January 2022 to January 2023 (with whole-genome sequencing and laboratory/patient metadata), the study aimed to reconstruct epidemiological and evolutionary features underlying Omicron lineage replacement dynamics.

The study estimated timing and growth of emerging lineages using lineage frequency increases, estimated reproduction numbers (Rt) from a covidestim model, and compared transmissibility and immune escape using RT-qPCR viral copy number proxies and vaccine breakthrough infection metrics. Results showed BA.1 had the fastest growth early in its emergence, with replacement rates slowing for later lineages. BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5 exhibited different Rt patterns, and fitness advantages decreased toward the end of 2022 as population immunity increased. Viral copy numbers (via Ct values) varied over time and did not fully explain replacement patterns. Vaccine breakthrough odds indicated immune escape was a significant factor for BA.1’s emergence compared to Delta, while BA.2 showed little evidence of increased breakthrough risk during its emergence; BA.5 and XBB had tendencies that were not statistically significant. The authors also developed a conceptual SIR-based framework describing how intrinsic transmissibility and immune escape interact in a changing immunity landscape, with different antigenic “spaces” affecting which lineages could outcompete others.

Tesla has announced lower-priced Model Y and Model 3 Standard versions, priced at $39,990 and $36,990, respectively, after the electric vehicle tax credit was canceled. These Standard models are about $5,000 cheaper than the Premium variants but still do not fully recoup the canceled $7,500 credit. The passage describes various cost-cutting changes, including smaller wheels and reduced features, along with performance and range differences. It also quotes a consumer analyst saying a 10% price cut may not be a major win for Tesla and suggests the changes resemble moves by legacy automakers. The passage further notes that Musk has reportedly deprioritized making affordable new cars in favor of robotics and autonomous vehicle technology, while Tesla’s sales are down 6% year over year.

Japan has high life expectancy, but ageing and declining natality have led to pension reforms over the past two decades. While subjective survival probabilities (SSP)—or self-rated life expectancy—are associated with mortality and differ from self-rated health in how conditions and behaviors relate to them, few studies examine socio-economic determinants of SSP or how work and employment factors affect SSP, especially in Japan. The passage describes a study using four waves of Japanese Study of Aging and Retirement (JSTAR) panel data from 2007–2013 to assess how employment status, job satisfaction, working time, and employment category relate to SSP among people aged 50 and over, including how these relationships change after adjusting for demographic, socio-economic, and health-related factors. SSP is measured as respondents’ perceived probability (in percentages) of living to specific ages (75–110).

The lecture discusses entry in industrial organization by starting with models where the number of firms is fixed and then analyzing what changes when firms can enter. It presents a two-stage model with homogeneous goods: potential entrants pay a fixed (sunk) entry cost \(K\), then compete in the second stage (e.g., Bertrand or Cournot). Variable profits fall as the number of firms \(N\) rises, and the equilibrium number of entrants is determined in the first stage based on whether profits exceed \(K\). In Cournot, for example, equilibrium entry is described as leading to exactly two firms under certain assumptions. The lecture argues that in homogeneous-good models, entry is socially excessive: social welfare maximization implies restricting entry because additional entrants primarily cause “business stealing,” which can outweigh the welfare benefits from higher output and reduced deadweight loss. It then extends the analysis to heterogeneous goods, where entry can be either too high or too low depending on whether changes in consumer surplus from better product matches outweigh business stealing.

The lecture includes a Hotelling-style example with differentiated locations, concluding that equilibrium entry can be about twice the socially optimal level due to strong business stealing and limited consumer-surplus gains from improved matching. It then discusses vertical differentiation, referencing Shaked and Sutton’s results that markets may exhibit either a “natural oligopoly” outcome (finite entry) or “specialization” (many firms with different quality products being optimal for different consumers), depending on marginal cost and consumers’ valuation of quality. The lecture also shifts to firm dynamics and entry/exit using census data, describing Jovanovic’s learning model where firms have unknown types (productivity/cost), pay entry costs, and exit when updated beliefs imply low profitability. In this framework, small and less profitable firms grow faster and fail more often due to uncertainty. Finally, it introduces a model by Nikhil Vellodi about rating intermediaries (e.g., Amazon/Yelp), motivated by the idea that limited information about new firms can reduce entry and learning; the proposed policy is partially revealing information that selectively withholds reviews for sufficiently high posterior quality to increase incentives for new entrants.

Frank Schilbach introduces MITOCW 14.13 “Psychology and Economics,” also called behavioral economics, and explains his research interests in poverty and how psychological factors affect the behavior of the poor. He outlines the class structure, including topics such as deviations from standard economic assumptions, examples of such deviations, and how models can be made more realistic while remaining simple and testable. 

He reviews key assumptions of the classical economic model—such as stable and well-defined preferences, rational optimization, self-interest, perfect self-control, constant discounting, risk aversion, Bayesian information updating, and the idea that information has no utility value by itself. He then discusses real-world examples where these assumptions may be violated, including motivated beliefs, preference instability or non-well-defined preferences, information-processing constraints, changes in perceived well-being depending on expectations, demand for commitment (e.g., restricting future choices), imperfect belief updating, and social influences. The lecture also uses multiple examples (e.g., organ donation defaults, medication reminders, charity giving, limited attention) to argue that the classical “homo economicus” model is too extreme in certain respects.

Schilbach discusses what behavioral economics aims to do—relaxing specific assumptions that matter for explaining behavior and using empirical and experimental evidence to test which deviations are important—while emphasizing that mainstream economic principles and methods remain relevant. He illustrates these ideas with the class laptop policy: standard economic considerations include externalities and note-taking benefits, while psychological considerations include limited self-control, multitasking overconfidence, and cognitive distraction. He notes evidence suggesting laptops can reduce test scores and describes the class’s planned “opt-in” laptop section as an attempt to address potential externalities. Finally, he previews the rest of the course topics (preferences, beliefs, attention, learning, malleability, mental health, discrimination, policy/paternalism, and poverty) and assigns a Rabin reading for Wednesday.

The passage summarizes GAO-24-105648, a performance audit required by Senate Report 115-289. It examines (1) characteristics of Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI) schools, (2) how CSI plans address selected requirements under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA), and (3) how the U.S. Department of Education (Education) monitors state oversight of CSI requirements.

GAO analyzed 2019-2020 education data to compare CSI schools with other public schools and reviewed a nationally generalizable sample of CSI plans (most recently available as of June 2022). It also interviewed officials from three CSI schools and held discussion groups with district officials from six states, and it reviewed federal laws, Education guidance, and monitoring documents.

GAO reported that CSI schools serve higher proportions of vulnerable students and have much lower student proficiency rates than other public schools. It estimated that about 42% of CSI plans appeared to address all three reviewed required elements: a school-level needs assessment, identification of resource inequities, and evidence-based interventions. GAO also found variability in how plans addressed these elements and that some district and school officials reported challenges developing them, including understanding needs assessments, reviewing resource inequities, and selecting evidence-based interventions.

For monitoring, Education collects and reviews state-reported school improvement data and conducts routine consolidated reviews, identifying compliance issues and requiring corrective actions in some cases. GAO found Education’s monitoring protocols rely on monitored states and districts to select which CSI plans Education staff review, and GAO concluded Education could improve its monitoring by independently selecting CSI plans for review. GAO recommended that Education update its monitoring protocols accordingly; Education agreed and stated it will independently select CSI plans for monitoring beginning in spring 2024.

The passage describes a study investigating sodium homeostasis in structural brain connectivity hubs in patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy (DRFE) using 7T sodium MRI and stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). It reports authors’ affiliations and correspondence details, then introduces focal epilepsy as abnormal rhythmic activity within an epileptogenic zone (EZ) that can propagate to other regions (PZ). The study rationale includes that sodium MRI can detect ionic changes linked to energy failure, and that network hubs may be vulnerable due to high metabolic demands, though the hub–epilepsy relationship is incompletely understood.  

Patients undergoing presurgical evaluation with 7T MRI and SEEG (23 patients and 21 controls after exclusions) had brain regions parcellated using an atlas, with structural connectomes derived from diffusion imaging and hub status defined using graph metrics. SEEG recordings were used to label regions as EZ, PZ, or non-involved zone (NIZ) based on an epileptogenicity index. Results indicate higher total sodium concentration (TSC) in patients than controls, with increased TSC in both EZ and non-EZ parcels; sodium signal fraction (f) was increased in the EZ but lower in other patient regions. Structural hubs showed higher TSC than non-hubs in both controls and patients, without differences in f between hub and non-hub regions. The discussion concludes that hub-related TSC increases likely reflect general microstructural or tissue integrity changes rather than epilepsy-specific effects, while EZ-related f increases may reflect susceptibility to homeostasis failure associated with epileptogenic activity.

The passage describes Coach DeBoer’s reflections on a team’s season, including a catastrophic injury early on that initially raised concerns about missing up to six months, but later helped the coach and team better understand the organization’s depth. The coach discusses how young players were tested in different roles, and how key returning players came back fresh and the team prepared for the deadline with a clear handle on what it needed. He also comments on leadership decisions, special teams performance trends, confidence and offensive opportunities for player Melker, and how the team has handled travel and road conditions without using them as excuses. The passage further addresses criticisms of the team’s character and leadership as being unsupported by what was observed in training camp and during the season.

Telltale Games, known for franchise-based titles like The Walking Dead, Minecraft, Borderlands, and Game of Thrones, said it is working on an original new IP but did not provide timing or details on its genre or story. Stauffer also discussed expanding Telltale games beyond console, mobile, and PC, including potential use of set-top boxes and Netflix-like streaming services, with more details planned for this summer. The studio said it can work on four projects at once, with more Game of Thrones, Minecraft, and Guardians of the Galaxy episodes underway, and it expects to share “a handful of things” this summer.

Periyar University has published the UG and PG examination results for 2017 on its official website (periyaruniversity.ac.in). The exams were held in April. The passage describes an alarm over “anarchy” in the capital, blaming Japanese rebels and foreign thieves for disorder and threatening disaster for Korea’s people and ancestral homes. The passage describes Britain’s first carbon neutral new-build church in Walsingham: the Roman Catholic Church of the Annunciation, built in 2006 in a design by parishioner and architect Anthony Rossi with a large solar array, a deep bore heat exchange system, a round tower using stones from an older church, and limited available information online. Planning permission was granted in 2013, but funding difficulties led to the church replacing the plan after buying a former nightclub across the street, leaving Britain without a PassivHaus church; it notes one exists in the United States and two projects are under construction in Canada and due to open this year.

The passage discusses Canon’s Rebel-free EOS 77D, suggesting the “Rebel” name may have kept US buyers away from the EOS 760D/T6s line. The passage recommends Via Browser for Android as a lightweight, fast, customizable, and stable alternative to defaults like Chrome.
