The passage explains that the Diverse Device’s Local bus clock uses automatic hardware clock gating and turns off when there is no other activity after an interrupt has been generated and serviced. If an edge-configured PIC input interrupt source remains high after the clock goes off, the PIC cannot return to Idle (defined by the interrupt input being low), so further low-to-high edges are not recognized and the clock may never turn back on, potentially hanging the system. Even if unrelated activity turns the clock back on while the interrupt source is low, the PIC may still not recover if the source goes low and then back high while the clock is off; the PIC can only return to Idle if the clock is on or turns on while the source input is low. The implications are that interrupts may be missed, leading to system hangs or other unexpected behavior.

The passage describes a dispute between Google and Epic Games over Google’s Android and Play store rules. Epic argued Google suppressed competition by discouraging new app stores and requiring developers using the Play store to adopt Google’s payment system and pay a service fee. After a three-week trial in 2023, a jury sided with Epic, and a judge ordered Google to change its terms of service for three years by allowing more app stores, permitting developers to use their own payment systems, and basing any related fees on Google’s actual costs. The independent payment-system changes are set to take effect later this month, while changes related to competing app stores are due by July 2026. Google appealed, but the 9th Circuit affirmed. The Supreme Court declined to pause the short-term parts of the injunction while it considers Google’s expected cert petition, meaning Google must allow developers to use their own payment systems for in-app purchases because the justices will not consider the petition until at least November.

The passage describes traditional Russian remedies for sunburn, including applying sour cream, yogurt, and kefir to soften red dry skin; using egg whites, nettle decoction, or watermelon juice to reduce pain by killing microbes; using sea buckthorn oil for peeling and chafing; using fresh potatoes, carrots, and pumpkins (slices or puree) to stop itching; and using sauerkraut in a gauze sack for 15–20 minutes to help with swelling. It also lists three curing methods: a soda-and-water bandage applied six times over three days, an oatmeal-and-warm-water cream used for about two days, and a mask of lemon juice mixed with sour cream left on for 10 minutes, alongside eating fruit such as kiwi, oranges, pineapples, and strawberries.

The passage reports that academic code violations remain high despite efforts to reduce them, with over half occurring in the computer science department. For the 2015–16 academic year, 49 undergraduate students were charged; outcomes included no violations for 13 students, reprimands for two, loss of credit for two, direct No Credit for 21, No Credit with transcript notation for 10, and one suspension. Seven graduate students were charged: one received direct No Credit, three received No Credit with transcript notation, and three were dismissed. The standing committee on the Academic Code is requesting to increase faculty committee membership due to the number of cases. Prevention efforts include an online tutorial required for all students before matriculating, faculty emphasis on integrity standards in syllabi, collaboration policy testing and reminders, and use of MOSS to detect programming plagiarism followed by professor review. The passage also cites partial reasons for higher computer science violations, such as robust access to collaboration, and notes slight overrepresentation of international students and first-years, leading to revisions in international student orientation to include academic integrity and code expectations. The University is also considering an academic integrity panel/week and an honor code with student-based review, while emphasizing that sanctions are taken seriously but intended to support long-term student success.

The passage is from NVIDIA Corporation’s FY2019 Form 10-K filed with the U.S. SEC for the fiscal year ended January 27, 2019. It includes corporate and securities information, incorporation and business overview, descriptions of NVIDIA’s GPU and Tegra Processor segments and their market applications (gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive), and details on business strategies such as advancing GPU computing, AI, visual computing, autonomous vehicles, and leveraging intellectual property. It also outlines sales and marketing approaches, manufacturing (fabless strategy relying on third parties), working capital management, and competition. In addition, it presents risk factors related to market needs and competition, cybersecurity, product defects, reliance on third parties, demand forecasting, international operations, talent retention, acquisitions, intellectual property litigation, privacy/data protection, taxes, legal proceedings, and corporate governance provisions. The passage further lists properties, legal and mine safety disclosures, and includes common stock trading information and share repurchase activity through the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2019.

On April 16, 2020, Mellanox Technologies and NVIDIA International Holdings received approval from China’s Anti-Monopoly Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation for NVIDIA Holdings’ proposed acquisition of Mellanox. The deal has also received antitrust approval from the European Commission and Mexico. The Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired at 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on May 23, 2019. The transaction is expected to close on or about April 27, 2020, subject to customary closing conditions.

The passage describes the federal government’s condition at the start of a presidential term, when its functions were broadly suspended in several seceded states while federal forts, property, and resources were seized and hostile actions prepared, including near Fort Sumter. It outlines the administration’s policy to exhaust peaceful measures, preserve federal property and revenue not yet taken, continue the mails, and avoid disturbances, aiming to keep the government operating using time, discussion, and the ballot box. It then recounts military assessments about reinforcing Fort Sumter, decisions involving Fort Pickens, and the sequence leading to the bombardment and fall of Fort Sumter. The passage argues that the assault was not self-defense but intended to force immediate dissolution of the Union. It frames the conflict as a test of whether a constitutional republic can maintain territorial integrity against domestic foes, leading to the call for the war power, descriptions of troop responses and border-state actions, and discussion of habeas corpus suspension and other wartime measures. It further argues against secession as consistent with the Constitution, discusses state sovereignty and constitutional boundaries, and concludes by urging Congress to provide legal means to fight and preserve the government, with assurances that after suppression the executive will follow the Constitution and laws.

The Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club celebrated 50 years of service to children at a dinner at StoneRidge Country Club. Organized as the Kiwanis Club of Los Rancheros on May 24, 1967, it received its charter from Kiwanis International on Sept. 13, with Franklin Lenfesty helping recruit 30 charter members. Before his death, Lenfesty donated $160,000, used to start a non-profit club foundation. The club’s annual pancake breakfast around Labor Day typically generates about $20,000 in profit. It sponsors Key Clubs and KIWINS groups, supports Boy Scout Troop 861 and Pack 861, and has raised funds including $120,000 in 2016 for a new tot lot and donations to Rady Children’s Hospital. The club also supports transitional homes in Romania, serves meals at Ronald McDonald House, and helps with holiday decorations. John O’Rourke is the current president, and the club meets for breakfast at StoneRidge Country Club in Poway on the first three Wednesdays of each month.

The passage describes a retrospective single-center CMR study of 15 adults with excessive trabeculation (ET/noncompaction) to assess measurement biases in left ventricular (LV) volumes and ejection fraction (EF). It explains how echocardiography/CMR guidelines may include trabeculations in the LV blood pool or may treat intertrabecular recesses differently, potentially biasing EF and related measures. Using threshold-based contouring, the study labels four LV components (compact wall, central cavity, trabeculations, intertrabecular recesses) and compares how EF and volume/area changes differ across methods. Results report that intertrabecular recesses operate at a higher EF than the central cavity, and that contouring trabeculations changes LV EF categories (halving the number of patients with severely reduced EF and doubling those with EF > 50%). The discussion argues that ET may not directly imply worse pump function as commonly assumed, and concludes that contouring improves LV volume and EF assessment, potentially reducing inappropriate diagnosis/treatment and improving prognosis prediction.

Lois Riess, 56, who is accused of killing her husband in Minnesota and later befriending and killing a Florida woman who resembled her, faces charges in both Florida and Minnesota. She is in custody in Texas awaiting transfer for trial, and if Florida upgrades the murder charge to first-degree murder, she could face the death

Arlo is a home security system with smartphone-controlled cameras, motion detection, night vision, and free online video storage for one week. It uses a central hub to control remote cameras, is expandable with different camera types, and works with Android or iPhone, as well as browsers. It provides instant alerts for movement and live camera feeds, with waterproof, battery-powered cameras suitable for indoor or outdoor installation. Arlo also works with Alexa for voice control and can show live feeds on an Echo Show or Fire tablet. The passage states that an Amazon Early Easter Sales deal reduces the three-camera system from £409.99 to £249.99 (saving 39%) for the rest of 19 March.

The president describes the U.S. progress against COVID-19 and the remaining challenges, saying vaccination, masking, expanded testing, and identifying infected people can turn the tide. He cites increases in fully vaccinated Americans, reductions in weekly deaths, and job growth, but warns that the highly contagious Delta variant is spreading and calls COVID-19 “a pandemic of the unvaccinated,” affecting hospitals and overwhelming emergency and intensive care units. He emphasizes that vaccines provide strong protection from severe illness and discusses a new plan with six broad areas: requiring more vaccinations (including employer, healthcare, federal worker, contractor, and school educator requirements), continuing protection for vaccinated people with boosters, keeping children safe and schools open, increasing testing and masking, protecting economic recovery through expanded COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan programs, and improving COVID-19 care through surge response teams, military health teams, and monoclonal antibody treatments. He also calls for equity in the response and describes international efforts to donate COVID-19 vaccines.

The passage explains that current legal, political, and socioeconomic systems rely on contractual obligations and transactional records, but digital-economy challenges to data integrity and veracity make conventional trust-based governance insufficient. It presents blockchain as a distributed ledger regulated by consensus and secured with cryptography, which protects transaction integrity and is described as potentially displacing trust-based intermediaries. Although some view blockchain as potentially disruptive, the passage also notes debate about whether it truly disrupts existing business models or instead serves as a foundational technology.  

To address a knowledge gap about how blockchain companies generate value, the study draws on digital business model theory (value creation logic, value capturing mechanisms, value delivery architecture, and value stakeholder network) while focusing mainly on the first two dimensions. It undertakes an exploratory multiple case study of five blockchain companies that incorporate blockchain into their offerings, using interviews and public archives, and analyzes how value is created and captured. The paper then presents a typology of five blockchain-inspired digital business models—platformer, disintermediator, mediator, transformer, and co-innovator—based on the cases, along with associated challenges and implications for theory and practice.

The National Council on the Humanities advises the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) on grant making and other policies. After the Trump administration fired a majority of the committee members, only four people remained, all appointed by President Trump. The council, made up of 26 people, provides input to the NEH chair on grant-making, policy, and funding decisions, including feedback on proposals for the National Garden of American Heroes program. Karen Stout, who served on the council since 2022 and was among those fired, said she was disappointed by the firings.

Harvey Ulfers, 64, of Cedar Falls, was sentenced in federal court to 2 years and 9 months for wire fraud and money laundering related to scrap metal sales from the John Deere Foundry. Prosecutors said he defrauded Deere & Company of at least $250,000 between about 2004 and January 2013 by using fraudulent internal documents to allow significantly undervalued scrap to leave the facility and by conspiring with others to obtain excess value after sale. He was ordered to pay a $111,602 fine and $259,132 in restitution to his former employer. A co-conspirator, Patrick Williams, pleaded guilty in April 2016 and received a 27-month prison sentence, with restitution of $259,132.97 ordered to Deere & Company. The case was revealed through internal investigations by Deere & Company and Alter Metal Recycling.

The passage describes Halimat Oniru, an entrepreneur behind Nigeria’s Haleem Group, as a source of hope for women. It says the company operates in Lagos, Delta, Bayelsa, and Cross River, is headquartered in Abuja, and has created job opportunities for tens of thousands despite economic challenges. Haleem Group is described as a top dredging company in West Africa and a major player in Nigeria’s road construction, with notable job offerings in Lagos. The passage portrays Halimat as privately minded, courageous, humble, and influential to younger women, also noting her involvement in humanity and fashion.

The passage provides financial and related disclosures for Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021. It includes consolidated statements of cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets, plus notes covering accounting policies, supplemental cash flow information, leases, financial instruments and fair value measurements, commitments and contingencies, debt, stockholders’ equity, income taxes, and segment information. It reports cash flows, net sales and operating results for Q2 and the six months ended June 30, 2021, discusses COVID-19 effects, liquidity sources and capital resources, and lists legal proceedings and tax-related matters.

The study assessed how COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness (VE) waned over 12 consecutive 4-week periods from 2 weeks after the second dose, extending follow-up to the earliest of 50 weeks after the second dose or 31 March 2022 to cover beyond 26 weeks and the omicron era. Using English primary care electronic health records, eligible adults (≥18 years; no care home/housebound status; no evidence of prior SARS-CoV-2 infection; and complete demographic data) were followed with vaccination status tracked through unvaccinated individuals who remained eligible throughout follow-up. VE was estimated in risk-based age and clinically vulnerable subgroups and for BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 where possible. Third-dose eligibility began for highest-risk individuals from later September 2021, expanded to all adults by mid-December 2021 with a shortened interval. By end of follow-up, third-dose uptake reached ≥90% in the 65+, 18-64 clinically vulnerable, and 40-64 subgroups, and effectiveness estimates in these groups beyond six months were considered unlikely to be meaningful due to selection effects and difficulties separating omicron effects from depleted two-dose groups. In the 18-39 subgroup, maximum third-dose uptake was 73%, and there was log-linear waning against COVID-19 hospitalisation with VE negligible by weeks 35–38 and against positive SARS-CoV-2 test with VE negligible by weeks 15–18; waning in this subgroup appeared not to be affected by omicron, though results may be influenced by testing and reporting differences. The study highlights the challenges of estimating long-term effectiveness of two doses when third-dose uptake is high and when testing policies change.

The passage describes patent-related and background material for a weather forecasting technology that uses real-time, high-frequency, and historical sensor data to determine current weather phenomena (including fog) and generate fast precipitation and visibility forecasts such as runway visual range (RVR). It discusses limitations of prior fog detection and forecasting methods, including difficulties distinguishing fog-related effects from other atmospheric phenomena and handling data beyond instrument/observer range.  

The technology’s system architecture includes four servers: information collection and normalization, offline/background processing, modeling and prediction, and information distribution and alerting. It uses cadence-based processing with repeating cadence cycles and logical “cadence instances” that organize collected, processed, generated, and forecast data into tile layers and tile stacks. The system supports near real-time updates with forecast cycles as short as about 1 minute, parallel processing, asynchronous data collection versus forecasting, and blending of precipitation and other weather estimates from multiple data sources (including microwave links, radar, and NWP). It also uses tile comparison and propagation mechanisms to avoid unnecessary full recalculations by updating only changed or affected tiles and dependent forecast layers.

The Two Oceans Restaurant at Cape Point in Table Mountain National Park is a voluntary member of the WWF Southern African Sustainable Seafood Initiative (SASSI). SASSI recently red-listed West Coast Rock Lobster (WCRL) due to an unsustainable population and uses a traffic light system (green, orange, red) to guide sustainable seafood choices. After the red listing, the restaurant depleted its holding stocks of WCRL and will stop selling it until the population recovers. SANParks TMNP supports the initiative, and it was reported that less than 2% of WCRL remains.

The passage describes multiple device features and support information. It explains the independent watchdog timer (IWDT) in the LFSS, which monitors code execution and hang scenarios using its own clock source and issues a POR reset if not reset in time. It also describes the windowed watchdog timer (WWDT), which supervises code execution and can generate a reset or interrupt when the watchdog is not reset within a specified time window, including features such as software-selectable periods and support for sleep mode stopping. The passage then outlines timer peripherals, including general-purpose TIMGx and advanced TIMAx, listing counter types, prescalers, repeat/reload modes, and additional advanced features such as PWM with dead-band insertion and fault handling. It further covers device analog connections guidance for DAC_OUT on PA15, the IOMUX role in selecting peripheral functions and wake-up logic, and the serial wire debug interface (SWD) plus boot strap loader (BSL) operation, including how it can be invoked and its pin requirements. Finally, it discusses device factory constants in a read-only memory-mapped FACTORY region and provides information on development tools, documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, and ESD caution.

Linda Ronstadt discussed living with Parkinson’s disease, saying she must be selective about her activities and describing day-to-day difficulties such as brushing her teeth, talking, and traveling. She said that before her official diagnosis in 2013 she noticed something “systemic,” especially after losing the ability to sing, and noted that doctors found her larynx in perfect condition. She continues to exercise daily. Ronstadt is also presenting “A Conversation With Linda” events featuring an audio-visual look at her career, followed by an audience Q&A, with upcoming dates listed for San Rafael (September 15), Folsom (September 21), and Saratoga (September 29). The passage also reviews her 40th anniversary expanded edition of *Simple Dreams*, describing its chart performance, Grammy recognition, and details about songs and cover photos.

The passage describes blockchain-based digital certificate management intended to address security issues when a certificate authority (CA) is hacked or acts maliciously by randomly changing certificate permissions. It proposes receiving CA transaction requests to write a digital certificate, determine a blockchain consensus result for the certificate, and then accept or reject the request based on that consensus. It also covers handling certificate revocation lists by receiving CA requests to write revocation lists or update information into the blockchain, performing consensus verification, and using the stored revocation list to verify transaction requests between node groups and to decide whether to accept or reject them. The passage further outlines related apparatus, electronic device, system, and computer-readable medium implementations, and states that certificates and revocation lists are validated via consensus before being chained or used, reducing the impact of a faulty CA.

Kyle Busch of Joe Gibbs Racing won the Overton’s 400, with Aric Almirola winning Stage 1 and Kevin Harvick winning Stage 2. Busch started 16th and finished 12th in Stage 1, reporting the car was too tight and needing more grip; the team made chassis and air pressure changes and adjusted tires and fuel. In Stage 2, Busch started 12th and finished 11th, again describing tight handling; he underwent pit adjustments and later adjusted the trackbar to address looseness. In Stage 3, Busch started 10th and won the race after a caution involving teammate Denny Hamlin led to pitting for fresh tires and a fast stop that helped him restart in sixth; he moved into the top five and led off pit road to take the lead on lap 210. Busch held off Kyle Larson to earn his fifth win of the season, his 48th career Cup victory, and his second Chicago win.

Long Covid (post-acute sequelae of COVID-19) is described as a fluctuating, multisystem condition with many symptoms affecting multiple organ systems. The COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale – Modified (C19-YRSm) is presented as a 17-item, condition-specific patient-reported outcome measure with subscales for Symptom Severity (SS), Functional Disability (FD), and Overall Health (OH), plus Other Symptoms (OS). This study used longitudinal data from the UK LOCOMOTION consortium to further validate C19-YRSm. Results reported good item and scale characteristics, good convergent validity with FACIT-Fatigue, and ability to discriminate between symptom severity levels and between patients with and without hospitalisation or ICU admission. The measure showed internal reliability, test-retest reliability, stability over time, and responsiveness to symptom fluctuations, detecting clinically meaningful change more sensitively than EQ-5D-5L. The authors report initial minimally clinically important differences for SS (2) and FD (2) and OH (1), and minimal clinically important differences based on SEM for SS (4) and FD (4). They conclude C19-YRSm is valid, reliable, responsive, and easy to administer for use in clinical and research settings to capture condition trajectory and intervention effects, supporting inform clinical policy and future trials.

Donald Trump said a Monday underground explosion near Manhattan’s Port Authority Bus Terminal highlights the urgent need for Congress to enact immigration legislative reforms. He said the attacker, Akayed Ullah, entered the U.S. through “chain migration” despite not being a U.S. citizen and having permanent residency. Trump called for ending chain migration and increasing immigration security, including more Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, enhanced arrest and detention authorities, and ending fraud and abuse in the immigration system. He also referenced an executive action restricting entry from eight countries and said terror convictions should receive the strongest penalties allowed by law.

The passage describes design and layout considerations for a push-pull converter, including transformer turns ratio, duty cycle limits, and transformer inductance and current calculations. It specifies conservative voltage ratings for primary and synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, an RCD clamp approach, output inductor ripple and selected inductance (0.47 µH), and output capacitance calculations leading to a minimum of 1.3 mF and approximately 2.3 mF used in the design for SET mitigation. It also covers an optional secondary output filter, cycle-by-cycle current limiting and sense resistor selection (7.5 Ω for RCS), hiccup capacitor selection (minimum 3.3 nF), frequency compensation component selection (Type 2A; RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, CHF 47 pF), and slope compensation resistor selection (102 kΩ between RSC and AVSS). Finally, it provides controller power-supply recommendations and multiple PCB layout guidelines to reduce noise and EMI, including separation of grounds and placement of bypass and compensation components near the controller.

The Department of Transport has warned that official salary rates for top-level personnel in some commercial State companies are too low to attract or retain suitable candidates. Briefing material says there is “discontent” over Government policy not to pay performance-related bonuses and that some chief executives are threatening legal action, with High Court proceedings begun in one case. The 2011 pay rules lowered chief executive salaries after the economic crash, and later policy removed benefits such as car allowances for new and renewed chief executives. The briefing notes that CEO contracts previously included performance-related payments, but standard contract templates were revised to remove the bonus clause. It states that some CEOs still have bonus clauses and are threatening action, including referring unpaid bonuses from the Dún Laoghaire Harbour Company to the High Court. It also lists specific 2011 starting salaries for several companies and says senior management pay at Bus Éireann is to be cut by 10% under a Labour Court recommendation.

Edmonton police seized $3.2 million worth of carfentanil after a fire call led to discovery of a large drug stash in a basement suite in the city’s southwest. The department said it was the largest carfentanil seizure ever recorded. Police found 12 one-kilogram bags of white powder, 16 one-kilogram bags of blue powder, and similar pink powder; analysis confirmed the blue and pink contained carfentanil. Police believe the white powder was caffeine used to cut the drug, and said no arrests have been made. The building was condemned by Alberta Health Services, with a notice saying it was used as a clandestine drug production and manufacturing laboratory for suspected fentanyl and/or carfentanil. Police are still seeking to identify and speak with a tenant considered a person of interest; the investigation continues.

Oscar nominee Ruth Negga said she resented how her teachers spoke to her during her school days in Limerick, describing her impatience to have school end. She compared the structure of school to acting, saying it was ironic yet had a “freeing” glamour. Negga attributed her success partly to luck and said luck affects everything. She received her first Oscar nomination for her role in Jeff Nichols-directed *Loving*, which tells the story of Richard and Mildred Loving, whose case reached the US Supreme Court and resulted in 1967 overturning convictions about interracial marriage laws. Negga will compete for Best Actress at the Academy Awards on Sunday, February 26, alongside Isabelle Huppert, Natalie Portman, Emma Stone, and Meryl Streep.

This VentureWire “People, Wednesday, May 30, 2001” issue lists executive changes and personnel updates across multiple companies in areas including top management, VC personnel, business development, marketing and sales, operations, finance, technology, and HR. It details specific appointments such as Solsoft naming Robert de Monts chairman and CEO, Real Media’s co-founder David Morgan leaving on June 30, Gluon Networks appointing Jo Anne Heywood Miller as president and CEO, InfoImage naming Thomas Niccoli as COO and president, and several other leadership additions. The issue also includes executive search job postings with roles and location details, plus a brief “who’s hiring” note about Proteus of Washington seeking its first vice president of sales and marketing.

The passage is from NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2016, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It provides company and filing information, describes NVIDIA’s business as visual computing across four markets (Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive) through the GPU and Tegra Processor segments, and outlines major strategies, sales and marketing approach, and manufacturing and working-capital practices. It also summarizes forward-looking statement cautions, business and regulatory risk factors (including competition, manufacturing yield and defects, security breaches, reliance on third parties, international risks, intellectual property litigation, and financial results volatility), and includes details on executive officers, facilities, market information for common stock, dividend and share repurchase activity, stock performance graphs, and selected financial data.

The passage is a message from Joe Bryant to the cheatsheets mailing list thanking U.S. veterans ahead of Veterans Day and encouraging readers to thank any veteran they know. It then provides “Matchups to Avoid and Exploit” for week 11, listing several quarterback passing matchups and noting which games favor the offense, including player-starting suggestions and injury/probable-status notes. It also includes “Rushing Game Matchups” with locks and prime matchups, and sections for even and downside matchups. The latter part shifts to an essay titled “WHAT IS A VET,” describing different roles veterans have served in and concluding with a call to say “Thank You” and a reminder that November 11 is Veterans Day.

The San Diego County Fair’s “Where the West is Fun” theme exhibit near O’Brien Gate offers attractions and, on Wednesdays at 12:30 p.m., Kumeyaay Nation members perform songs in their native language, drawing crowds that Jack Robertson says are rare for educational exhibits. The exhibit includes a map of where Kumeyaay people live today in San Diego County, color photos, information about the annual yucca festival, and details meant to dispel myths about the Wild West. Vanessa Christman, a Kumeyaay member, says the information helps visitors and addresses beliefs that the Kumeyaay people no longer exist. The exhibit also includes displays on Hollywood’s portrayal of cowboy life and the accuracy of those portrayals, and it offers other live entertainment during the week, including a high-noon “showdown” and The Long Bar Review variety show.

Chairman Martin expresses gratitude for the welcome and for being nominated again for the Presidency, and says he will not deliver a eulogy of Mr. Nixon. He argues that the future should be the dominant topic for the Republican Party’s centennial convention, and states a “single proposition” that the Republican Party is the Party of the Future. He predicts approval by the American people in 1956 if Americans carry the party’s message to others and help ensure voter registration and turnout.

He gives reasons the party is for the future: it follows long-range principle rather than short-term expediency (illustrated through examples like farm policy, labor relations, and decentralizing power from Washington), it focuses on current and future issues, it brings people together rather than driving groups apart, and it enables individuals to address remaining needs. He emphasizes social justice progress through actions and lists areas still needing work, including discrimination and equal opportunity.

He concludes by arguing that a future requires peace, discussing imperatives of peace: maintaining national strength, pursuing collective security, and bridging the divide with communist-ruled peoples through increased contact. He describes a hoped-for future and ends by accepting the nomination.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 26, 2022. The filing reports that Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2022, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The exhibit is not deemed filed for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except as specifically referenced. The document also lists registered securities, includes Item 9.01 exhibits (Exhibit 99.1), and is signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Bell’s theorem implies that any physical theory matching quantum-mechanical predictions and satisfying certain assumptions must violate local causality. This paper focuses on one such assumption, statistical independence (SI). SI is argued to be best understood as requiring that random sampling procedures yield representative samples, and that violating SI means random sampling fails to be representative (especially in Bell experiments). The authors say that superdeterminism can be equated with SI violation and propose that this can occur in three forms: (1) determinism with fine-tuned initial conditions, (2) statistical flukes, or (3) nomic exclusion, where specific combinations of measurement settings and ontic states are nomologically impossible. They also discuss how retrocausal theories and invariant set theory might not necessarily violate SI, beginning with an analysis of retrocausal interpretations. Philosophical consequences of superdeterminism are addressed later, including free will, conspiratorial concerns, and whether it is scientific.

A Regina father, Marshall Pelletier, shared a photo and message after a driver splashed his wife and infant son on a mild day. Pelletier said the driver was in the inside lane and drenched them while his wife pulled the infant in a sled on the sidewalk. He posted an image showing the baby’s toque and blanket speckled with brown slush. Regina Police said Regina and Saskatoon bylaws prohibit splashing pedestrians, requiring offenders to pay fines and attend court, but enforcement can be difficult because police need driver and vehicle descriptions and a licence plate number. Elizabeth Popowich noted details may be hard to record immediately due to shock and cleaning slush from faces or clothing. Pelletier said drivers should be more conscientious, and he was disappointed that the person did not stop or slow down.

The passage is a lecture discussion of ICM (Independent Chip Mode) theory for tournament poker, contrasting it with chip EV approaches used in cash games. The speaker explains that tournament chip value is nonlinear because players try to survive and move up payouts rather than maximize chip counts. He distinguishes minimizing “tournament risk” from minimizing monetary risk, and notes ICM is most relevant near the payout bubble and final table, with examples including extreme late-stage stacks and satellite-style tournaments where only top finishers get seats.

He then demonstrates how to compute ICM equity using a simplified three-player example, showing that chip EV does not equal money EV because stacks are not guaranteed to finish at their chip-proportional place. He outlines how to use ICM calculators for more players and gives corollaries such as big stacks having money EV less than chip EV and small stacks having money EV greater than chip EV.

The latter part tracks hands from a final-table tournament, repeatedly applying ICM ideas to explain folds and shoves, including “bullying” dynamics by larger stacks, differences in decision-making when opponents are short, and occasional references to exploitative adjustments. The speaker also discusses satellites and the “traffic intersection game” concept (in game theory terms), plus brief mentions of controversial or unethical metagame behaviors.

The World Bank upgraded China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast to 4.8%, citing stronger-than-expected resilience supported by government stimulus and a modest export recovery. It attributed the increase to renewed strength in domestic investment, industrial output, infrastructure spending, targeted manufacturing support, and gradual improvement in consumer sentiment, which offset weaknesses in property and subdued private consumption. The World Bank warned that growth momentum is likely to ease in 2026 due to fiscal constraints and global headwinds, and that long-term risks include high local government debt, demographic pressures, and declining productivity. It said China’s growth remains below its pre-pandemic trajectory and expected a gradual shift from state-led investment toward more consumption-based growth supported by green industries and digital innovation.

Archaeologists report that the oldest known olive oil in Italy dates to the Early Bronze Age, earlier than previously believed. A chemical analysis of residue in pottery fragments found in the 1990s at the Sicilian site of Castelluccio, dated from the early 3rd century BC to the start of the 2nd century BC, identified the liquid as olive oil based on oleic and linoleic acids. The study, led by Dr. Davide Tanasi of the University of South Florida, used Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, Gas Chromatography, and Mass Spectrometry, and was described as the first chemical evidence of the oldest olive oil in Italian prehistory, pushing back systematic olive oil production by at least 700 years. Other cooking-related artifacts were also found at the site.

Jim Cramer’s view of Snap has shifted nearly two months after he compared the company to early Facebook following a fourth-quarter earnings report with 72% revenue growth. He previously said Snap had “run room” despite a 47% stock jump, but he now points to the unpopular December redesign and related celebrity reactions as reasons he is not buying. Cramer says advertisers may leave if engagement declines, and he notes that Kylie Jenner said she no longer uses the app after the update, contributing to a 7% share decline. While he says shares still have risk and are “not cheap,” he would consider buying later, stating “at a certain price, it is time to hit the buy button.” Snap is set to report first-quarter results on May 1, with Wall Street expecting an adjusted loss of $0.17 per share on $243.85 million in revenue.

The passage explains that the running back is an important offensive position, often held by an athletic player. Its primary responsibility is to run the football efficiently after taking handoffs from the quarterback, gaining positive yardage while protecting the ball. Running backs may also need to pass block and catch, and the position values versatility. The name “running back” refers to lining up behind the offensive line in the backfield. Other names include tailback and halfback, and sometimes fullback. The passage lists general body estimates (around 5’9–6’2 and 190–235 pounds, athletic build) and skills such as speed, agility, vision, toughness, and pass-catching ability, noting roles like “short-yardage back” and “all-purpose back.” It also highlights examples of notable running backs (Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and Ladanian Tomlinson) and states that running backs can turn negative plays into major gains, contributing to offensive success.

Adults have a well-formed self-concept, but young children and early adolescents are still developing theirs. During this period, peers become more influential, and normal physical and emotional changes can leave children feeling insecure or scared. Children who aren’t included in popular groups may develop feelings like “Nobody likes me” or “I don’t have any friends,” which can negatively affect academics and may lead to significant depression. Parents are advised to respond with patience and understanding, continue positive reassurance, listen without judgment, and seek professional help if there are clear signs of depression, such as falling grades or withdrawal. School counselors can start this process, as they are trained to help children learn how to think and can also advise parents; Counseling Corner is provided by the American Counseling Association.

The passage explains how to sell unwanted holiday gifts and discusses where to do so. It cites a Kijiji report that Canadians earned an average of $1,037 selling second-hand goods last year, and notes that gifts such as unwanted sweaters or unused store gift cards can be sold rather than kept. Collectibles and valuables are suggested for eBay or auction houses, while household items are recommended for garage sales at low prices. For online selling, Kijiji is highlighted as good for items like TVs, gaming consoles, laptops, smartphones, and speakers, while Bunz and Facebook groups are described as popular for trading or offers, including women’s clothing, perfume, makeup, furniture, and home decor, with some users exchanging items for non-monetary payments. Tips include using clear photos, adding condition labels like BNIB/BNWT/EUC, using holiday hashtags, writing funny descriptions, and pricing based on eBay sold listings and the item’s condition. Timing advice is given for when searches and trades are highest, including January on Kijiji and high activity around Boxing Day to early January on Bunz. The passage also covers selling gift cards through services like CardSwap.ca, and discusses regifting etiquette, which is presented as acceptable only for brand-new, original-packaged items that the recipient would love and where the recipient doesn’t know the original giver.

David Luiz is spending his summer holiday in Dubai after a disappointing season at Chelsea, where he fell down the pecking order following knee and ankle issues and a lack of game time. After posting photos of himself in front of the Burj Khalifa and flyboarding above the ocean, the passage notes he last played for Chelsea on February 5 in a 4-1 defeat at Watford. It also recalls that manager Antonio Conte brought him back to the Premier League in August 2016 and that Luiz played an instrumental role in Chelsea’s title win last year, while his second season was difficult and he had fewer opportunities to play.

Antonio Conte says he is being treated more harshly by the media than other Premier League managers. He argues that journalists repeatedly ask about his future and that other coaches are not questioned in the same way after defeats. Conte says he does not read newspapers or go online and that he does not have a relationship with journalists, and he wants to check whether this exists. He also notes Chelsea’s current situation, being 18 points behind Manchester City and fighting for a top-four finish. Conte compares his position to other managers at top-six clubs and says he wants to respect his contract and have another season in England. He takes his side to Watford after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

The passage introduces inverse problems in science and engineering, where unknown physical states are recovered from indirect or incomplete observations, but the tasks are ill-posed and harder on irregular domains. It notes that classical PDE-constrained optimization is computationally prohibitive and that operator learning (e.g., DeepONet, FNO and related methods) can approximate PDE solution maps efficiently, though many approaches mainly target regular domains and inverse problems on irregular geometries remain underexplored. It also describes diffusion-based generative models as a complementary approach, but says diffusion methods in PDE neural surrogates are often limited to regular domains, leaving extension to families of complex geometries an open challenge. The work proposes GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware diffusion framework for inverse problems on complex geometries, including contributions such as a geometric function autoencoder (GeoFAE) for unstructured meshes, coupling GeoFAE with a latent diffusion model for posterior sampling from sparse/noisy sensor data, theoretical guarantees of accurate posterior approximation under well-trained components, and demonstrated state-of-the-art results on benchmarks. The passage then reviews related operator learning and diffusion approaches, outlines preliminaries on operator learning for PDE solution maps and rectified flow for conditional posterior sampling, and formalizes the problem setup for reconstructing PDE-governed fields from noisy pointwise sensor observations over a family of geometries.

In summer 1977, NASA launched Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 to study Jupiter and Saturn. Although Voyager 2 launched two weeks earlier, it reached Jupiter after Voyager 1. Both probes have continued functioning for over 40 years. NASA later planned trajectories so the probes could also study Uranus and Neptune without additional fuel, and between them they collected data on four planets and 48 moons; Voyager 2 is described as the only man-made object to fly by all four gas giant planets. After these studies, both probes were sent on trajectories carrying them outside the solar system, with Voyager 1 passing beyond the heliosphere into interstellar space on August 25, 2012. Both probes carry the Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph record intended to convey information about Earth and humanity, expected to be useable for millions of years. NASA estimates data return to Earth until at least 2020.

Researchers at Karolinska Institutet (Sweden) and colleagues in Finland developed the CORE model, a web-accessible tool that predicts a person’s risk of severe liver disease within 10 years using three routine blood tests (AST, ALT, GGT) plus age and sex. In a study using data from over 480,000 people in Stockholm with follow-up for up to 30 years, the model differentiated between those who did and did not develop severe liver disease in 88% of cases, improving on the FIB-4 method. The model was also tested in two other population groups in Finland and the UK and showed high accuracy, though it still needs further testing in high-risk groups and integration into medical record systems for clinical use. The work aims to support earlier screening in primary care for conditions such as cirrhosis and liver cancer.

The passage is an issue of the “Option Investor Newsletter” (parts 1–3) forwarded in an email dated Jan. 20, 1999, summarizing market activity and options-trading commentary. It reports market wrap data for Jan. 19, 1999, including gains for the Dow, Nasdaq, and S&P 500, and discusses technology/Internet momentum tied to news such as At Home (ATHN) purchasing XCIT for $7 billion and Microsoft’s after-close earnings results (reported as $0.73 vs. $0.59 estimates). It also notes upcoming events (e.g., Alan Greenspan testimony) and includes “Market Posture” and “Market Sentiment” sections with put/call ratios, VIX readings, and index/sector posture alerts. The newsletter provides “Picks” and “Play” updates, including dropped and new put/call plays, stock-specific commentary, and new speculative combination plays for select telecom/Internet-related stocks, along with subscription information and a trading-related disclaimer.

Chicago hotel workers now have “panic buttons” as an ordinance effective this week requires hotels to provide them. The buttons are intended to protect housekeeping staff and others who work alone in guest rooms from sexual harassment and other crimes. A Unite Here Local 1 survey of 500 workers found 58% reported experiencing at least one incident of sexual harassment by guests, most commonly guests answering their door naked, and only about one-third report such harassment to their manager. The buttons send a message to supervisors, managers, and human resources and include the employee’s name and location. Unite Here Local 1 President Karen Kent said this is a “new day” for women working in Chicago hotels, and similar efforts have occurred in Las Vegas.

The passage describes the diamond industry’s challenge from synthetic (“lab-grown”) diamonds and DeBeers’s response. It recounts Lee Mandell’s dilemma about buying a laboratory-grown engagement ring after watching *Blood Diamond*, which raised concerns about “blood diamonds” and violence in African diamond-producing regions. The text explains how lab-grown diamonds are chemically identical to natural diamonds, can be produced in days, and are often cheaper (generally 15% to 40% less, with specific price comparisons). It outlines industry demand and supply factors, DeBeers’s historical dominance and subsequent legal and reputational pressures, and its shift toward demand-driven branding and “conflict-free” assurance. It details DeBeers’s strategies, including the Gem Defensive Programme, consumer education campaigns, and efforts to secure new sources of natural diamonds. It also covers the Kimberley Process aimed at preventing conflict diamonds and notes disagreement about whether synthetic diamonds are inherently more “ethical.” The passage concludes with Lee deciding against synthetic diamonds being emotionally unconvincing, comparing synthetics to buying an orchid grown in a controlled environment.

The President tells fellow leaders it is his last speech as U.S. president and recounts his public service since becoming a senator in 1972. He describes how the United States and the world overcame major crises, including ending nuclear threats through arms control, ending the Cold War, and resolving wars such as Vietnam. He cites actions against apartheid, efforts regarding Milošević, the Violence Against Women Act, justice after 9/11, and ending long U.S. wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. He argues for rebuilding alliances, addressing current conflicts (Ukraine, Gaza/Israel-Hamas and the risk of regional war, Iran, and Sudan), and managing competition with China. He highlights U.S. investments and initiatives on climate, health, and development, including COVID and mpox support, and efforts to reform the United Nations. He emphasizes preparing for artificial intelligence’s benefits and risks and asks how AI should be governed internationally and aligned with human dignity. He concludes by stressing democracy and serving “We the People,” asserting optimism based on global civic efforts for rights and freedom.

The email “IEP News 5/10” (May 10, 2001) from Jean Munoz to a large recipient list shares multiple news items about California’s energy crisis and related policy and market developments. The included articles describe rolling blackouts and rising electricity costs in California, including fears of high bills for residential customers and impacts on agriculture and businesses. They also cover state actions and proposals such as electricity rate increases approved by the Public Utilities Commission, plans for revenue bonds to pay for power purchases, and Gov. Gray Davis urging electricity generators to accept reduced payments (a “70%” request and lawmakers’ “haircut” proposals) to help prevent bankruptcy and keep utilities solvent. Additional items discuss disputes over compensation for generators, legislative and federal involvement, and ongoing grid and supply constraints, including transmission upgrade bottlenecks and the status of small power plants.

The German Ambassador (Bernstorff) reports that House, acting on Wilson’s behalf, conveyed Wilson’s official message: Wilson offers confidential peace mediation based on his Senate message, without interfering with territorial peace conditions. Bernstorff describes the President’s reasoning that the Entente’s publicly announced peace conditions were unacceptable, while Wilson’s program and the moral obligation to disclose German peace terms justify a disclosure so intentions appear genuine. The President believes Wilson wants Germany to state peace conditions that can be publicly known in both the U.S. and Germany to enable both peace conferences, and the President hopes early conferences could prevent unnecessary bloodshed in the spring offensive. Bernstorff also suggests that if the U-boat war begins immediately, the President would view it as a “slap in the face” and war with the U.S. would be unavoidable, whereas delaying could improve diplomatic position, and that peace conferences may yield a better peace than if the U.S. joins the Entente.

In France, the Ambassador (Sharp) reports that Socialist deputies approved Wilson’s address to the Senate, urging the French Government to clearly agree with it and calling for pressure on representatives of belligerent nations to bring about an early end of the war. Sharp notes that accounts and the Socialist group’s stance have been widely published and are expected to influence sentiment in favor of Wilson’s message, with some professional and government-related figures also approving it. Sharp adds that many French press writers endorse Wilson’s principles as representative of the French Republic, though some argue peace should come only after Allied victory.

Amanda Nunes criticized Ronda Rousey’s coach Edmond Tarverdyan after defeating Rousey at UFC 207 to retain her title. Nunes was quoted saying Tarverdyan made Rousey believe in boxing despite her strong judo, and that this contributed to her career decline. The passage notes Tarverdyan has faced prior criticism, including from Rousey’s mother and from some fans and pundits. At UFC 207, Rousey is described as having been overwhelmed by Nunes’s opponent’s performance leading to Rousey’s second consecutive loss. Nunes defended her title, and Dana White said her popularity will grow; a rematch is mentioned as possible if Rousey wins. Rousey said she needs time to reflect and decide what to do next amid calls from other fighters not to retire and to consider switching camps.

The passage discusses Medicare healthcare fraud and overutilization in the United States, noting large annual financial losses and projected increases in Medicare spending. It describes common fraud forms (phantom billing, upcoding, cloned documentation) and states that current detection is largely manual, causing most fraud to go undetected. Machine learning has been studied for detection using CMS public data, but prior approaches face issues such as dependence on the LEIE dataset (class imbalance and labeling noise), and reliance on aggregate billing features that may miss subtle patterns.  

To address these limitations, the study focuses on ophthalmology and creates a labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists using input from experienced physicians and medical billers. Labels are “non-fraudulent” or “overutilizer,” assigned based on physician-biller review and additional validation. The study preprocesses CMS Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data (2013–2021), extracts standardized ophthalmology-related HCPCS-code features and provider-level payment/patient demographics, and then trains and evaluates multiple supervised ML models (KNN, logistic regression, SVM, XGBoost, multilayer perceptron) plus a stacking ensemble using repeated nested cross-validation.  

Results show varying discrimination across models, with the stacking ensemble achieving the highest performance (AUROC 0.907) and best predictive accuracy/confidence among the tested methods. The chosen stacking model is used to estimate ophthalmology overutilization in Medicare in 2021, predicting about 1,457 of 17,013 ophthalmologists as overutilizers (≈8.6% nationwide), with an estimated potential monetary loss of about $437.1 million for ophthalmology in that year. The passage also reports jurisdiction- and state-level variations, discusses probability thresholding for labeling, and presents feature importance findings using SHAP, highlighting payment-per-patient and HCPCS utilization patterns as important indicators. The study concludes that combining domain expertise with ML may improve overutilization detection and outlines limitations including limited labeled data size, reliance on predictive estimates, and the need for subspecialty-specific labeled datasets.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2019. The filing includes unaudited consolidated financial statements, such as consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive loss, changes in redeemable noncontrolling interests and equity, and cash flows. For the three months ended March 31, 2019, Tesla reported total revenues of $4,541,464 (in thousands) and net loss of $667,645 (in thousands), with net loss attributable to common stockholders of $702,135 (in thousands). The passage also describes significant accounting policies and notes, including revenue recognition, leases (ASC 842 adoption on January 1, 2019), cash flow activity, equity incentive plans, fair value measurements, inventory and solar energy system details, and commitments and contingencies, including several securities-related legal proceedings.

The passage describes planned summaries and statistical analyses for demographic and baseline characteristics, concomitant medications and diabetes treatment coding, efficacy endpoints (primary time to plasma glucose recovery and secondary recovery times/changes), and multiple supportive and sensitivity analyses. It specifies baseline definitions, covariates for the primary model, handling of dropouts/missing data (observed data only, no imputation), and hierarchical confirmatory testing comparing dasiglucagon versus placebo. It also outlines additional time-to-recovery analyses using Kaplan-Meier methods, log-rank and Wilcoxon tests, discrete-time Cox models, optional homogeneity checks across factors, and linear interpolation for recovery times as a supportive analysis. Data handling for plasma glucose, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic reporting, safety analyses (extent of exposure, local tolerability, adverse events using MedDRA coding, laboratory tabulations), ECG and immunogenicity (ADA) are also detailed, along with general data presentation and SAS QC/programming requirements.

The Bihar School Education Board (BSEB) declared the BETET/BSITET 2011 results on its official website (biharboard.ac.in). BSEB had organized the BSITET special examinations for classes 1 to 5, 6 to 8, 9 to 10, and 11&12 in 2016, and released Paper-I and Paper-II results. Candidates can check results by visiting biharboard.ac.in, clicking “BETET/BSITET 2011 Result,” entering a 10-digit roll number, and downloading and printing the result. BSEB also released official answer keys for both papers for different subjects.

The passage says violence against women services are concerned about the election outcome because gender equity and sexual violence were not addressed in the first two debates. It cites two incidents in May: the beating and sexual assault of Elisabeth Salm, who died after being hospitalized, and a Timmins car fire that killed four people, which the passage says indicates domestic violence homicide. It states that since January, about 19 women and their families have been murdered, with men charged. The passage adds that during the third debate gender equity and sexual violence were raised, but one candidate responded with memes and made demeaning remarks about women leaders. It argues this is worrisome and calls for a premier committed to keeping women safe and improving communities. It also notes that Ontario Thrive sent a gender equity survey to candidates, with all major parties except the Progressive Conservatives responding, and it links women’s safety to economic security, safe workplaces, affordable child care, safe transit, and a livable minimum wage, alongside school curriculum addressing consent and body autonomy.

Sheffield’s council, through roads maintenance contractor Amey, is in a dispute with communities over plans to fell hundreds of roadside lime trees. The controversy gained national attention in November when tree surgeons arrived at Rustlings Road with police; two pensioners were arrested and the council later apologized for using similar tactics. Residents near other threatened trees remain concerned, including those near Rivelin Valley Road, where 700 lime trees along three-and-a-half miles are said to form the second-longest avenue in the UK. Thirty-one trees are threatened as part of a tree-felling programme, with campaigners arguing the trees are targeted to make road resurfacing easier and cheaper. A report from an independent panel on the trees’ future is awaited, following a 25-year private finance initiative signed in 2009 between the council and Amey for a large road resurfacing programme.

The passage describes North Carolina child care academies meant to place new early childhood educators into classrooms faster than traditional pathways. In at least 11 counties, academies run for two to six weeks with 20 to 64 hours of class time and are designed to operate at little to no cost to participants, amid staffing shortages among licensed providers.

It outlines two models: a classroom-ready model (at least 20 hours of instruction) that qualifies students to work in licensed facilities but not as lead teachers, and a teaching credential model that adds training tied to EDU 119 and results in a continuing education credit (EDU 3119) transferable to community colleges and used in lieu of EDU 119 for lead-teacher qualification. The DCDEE offers grants of up to $50,000 for up to 10 UNC-system community colleges or universities to run academies between Oct. 15, 2025 and July 31, 2026, and a $1.476 million pilot was included in the North Carolina House budget.

Counties named as offering academies include Buncombe, Cabarrus, Catawba, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Johnston, McDowell, Rowan, Stanly, and Wayne. The passage also summarizes examples from Wayne and Johnston (supported by Camber Foundation funding), Stanly (classroom-ready model with some reimbursed costs), McDowell (teaching credential model supported by a Dogwood Health Trust grant), and Durham (teaching credential model supported by Duke Community Affairs and Durham PreK, with bilingual delivery and 140 applicants for 20 slots).

The passage discusses stock market updates, including the S&P 500 ending a winning streak as Oracle slumps weigh on tech, IBM shares rising on an Anthropic AI partnership, and Goldman Sachs raising its gold price target to $4,900 by end-2026. It also describes a market outlook referencing long-term seasonal weakness, diminished liquidity, thin volume, and institutional tax loss selling and rebalancing adding pressure, particularly into August. It includes commentary on yields, the TLT chart, the dollar, gold, and commodities, noting potential impacts on risk sentiment and levels to watch for technical moves. It repeats that the content is for educational purposes only and includes trading risk and data disclaimer statements.

The lecture discusses how SCET organizes the degrees of freedom for back-to-back dijet production in \(e^+e^-\) annihilation, identifying hard modes, collinear modes for each jet, and ultra-soft modes that communicate between jets. It explains relevant momentum scales (hard \(\mu_h\), jet \(\mu_j\), and ultra-soft/soft \(\mu_s\)) and how measurements like hemisphere invariant masses constrain events to the dijet configuration by requiring \(m^2,\bar m^2 \ll q^2\). Using SCET Lagrangian factorization and field redefinitions, the cross section for hemisphere invariant masses is factorized into a hard function (Wilson coefficient squared), two jet functions, and a soft function, with measurements incorporated into the operators via delta functions. The passage distinguishes peak and tail regions based on scale hierarchies and notes that the leading-power factorization involves power corrections from different sources. It further outlines how thrust can be treated as a symmetric projection of the hemisphere masses and briefly describes how perturbative calculations and renormalization group evolution enter through matching (for the hard function) and loop diagrams (for jet and soft functions), including the qualitative structure of anomalous dimensions and convolutions.

Former Infosys CFO V. Balakrishnan said Sebi’s decision to deny Infosys’ consent plea in former CFO Rajiv Bansal’s severance payment case should be based on legality and merits, not a whistleblower’s emotions. He referred to a whistleblower’s letter alleging lapses in the Panaya deal and issues around Bansal’s severance pay, including concerns about settlement and disclosure. The letter renewed corporate governance allegations after Infosys filed a settlement application with Sebi regarding the severance package. Balakrishnan demanded resignation of board members Roopa Kudva and Ravi Venkatesan, and T.V. Mohandas Pai criticized the whistleblower’s demand while saying Infosys’ move to settle disclosure lapses was “perfectly fine.” Infosys had planned to pay Rs17.38 crore severance to Bansal in 2015 but paid Rs5 crore, withholding Rs12 crore.

The passage discusses STAT’s weekly newsletter “Health Care Inc.” and notes that the government remains shut down due to disagreements between Republicans and Democrats over extending Affordable Care Act enhanced premium tax credits. It explains that the credits, established during the Covid-19 pandemic and extended through 2025, both increase financial help for current eligible people and expand eligibility to those with higher incomes. The article is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on February 1, 2017. Effective that date, Tesla Motors, Inc. amended its certificate of incorporation and bylaws solely to reflect a corporate name change to “Tesla, Inc.” The filing lists Exhibits 3.1 and 3.2 for the certificate amendment and amended and restated bylaws, and is signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel.

The passage says the dollar has risen recently after earlier underperformance, driven by increased prospects for a December rate hike and improving US economic activity. It notes the Bloomberg US Dollar Index fell more than 10% year-to-date through early September, then rallied nearly 4% in less than a month, breaking above its 50-day moving average and exiting a downtrend range. Despite the bounce, the index is still down over 7% for the year. The dollar’s rise is also described as helping slow crude oil’s recent rally; crude dropped below $50 after nearing $53 in late September.

The state budget earmarks ₹970 crore for general education and ₹789 crore for higher education. It includes ₹614 crore to upgrade 138 schools into centres of excellence, and ₹50 lakh to ₹1 crore for infrastructure development for schools with over 500 students. The budget allocates ₹33 crore to KITE for completing classroom digitisation and ₹300 crore from KIIFB for computer labs in all primary and upper primary schools. Additional allocations are planned for schools over 150 years old. Within higher education funding, ₹248 crore is for technical education, ₹28 crore for the Additional Skill Acquisition Programme, and ₹13 crore for upgrading libraries, laboratories, and courses.

The passage says the iPod is no more as an established product, noting the discontinuation of the iPod nano and iPod shuffle as a second decline after the iPod classic was retired. It adds that these models lacked compatibility with Apple Music, which the author describes as the final factor. The passage states that, although an “iPod” name remains for Apple devices, it plays music only in name. It also claims the iPod helped bridge Apple’s shift from a PC maker to an ecosystem of hardware, software, and services, with its influence seen in the iPhone and what follows.

The passage describes two Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (IACT) systems—MAGIC and CTAO Large-Sized Telescope LST-1—at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory. It explains that rapid on-site analysis (OSA) pipelines are used to automatically process data into standard analysis products for daily checks, scheduling, and data quality assurance, with OSA operating on MAGIC since 2012 and on LST-1 since 2021. It outlines the overall data flow from raw digitised pulses (Data Level 0) through calibrated and reconstructed charge and timing (DL1), image reconstruction and physical parameter estimation (DL2), to photon candidates and Instrument Response Functions (DL3), and notes that the LST-1 pipeline is an evolution of MAGIC’s but with rewritten code. The passage also compares computing requirements and processing approaches, including parallelisation methods, batch systems, and data transfer to off-site centres after processing. It further describes supervision tools (web pages, notifications), error-checking and recovery mechanisms, and highlights that MAGIC’s OSA produces additional higher-level products such as detection significance estimates, sky maps, spectra, and example plots. The concluding lessons emphasize the need for next-day analysis for fast transient response and problem detection, tight coordination with databases and simulation tools, and built-in human intervention and error recovery.

An informal meeting was held to discuss a draft agreement, with representatives from the British Foreign Office and Belgian Embassy and Ministries, as well as counselors and secretaries of the London mission. Suggestions were made about revising the agreement earlier than December 31, 1943 if Belgian territory were liberated, and discussion of Art. 3 led to the view that existing price arrangements should not be disturbed, detailed pricing might extend beyond the agreement period, and actual prices should be excluded in favor of future subsidiary arrangements. For Art. 4 on payment, concerns were raised about the Belgian Government’s need for dollar exchange for purchases in the United States, and shipping provisions were discussed due to a lack of a specific shipping article. Questions were also raised about overlapping periods between an existing UK–Belgian agreement and a new US–UK–Belgian agreement, with a proposal that the new agreement begin with a clean slate and uncompleted transactions from the old agreement lapse into the new one. The concluding formal agreement text states that from September 1, 1942 to December 31, 1943, the Belgian Government would make available to buyers in the UK or US the quantities of Congo exports listed in the first schedule.

OpenAI announced new parental control features for ChatGPT following a lawsuit after the death of a California teenager, where the chatbot was alleged to have given harmful advice and helped draft a suicide note. Parents and teens must mutually agree to link accounts, after which parents can restrict sensitive content, disable voice and image functions, set “quiet hours,” and control whether conversations are stored. OpenAI will also alert parents when acute risk signals are detected while keeping specific chat transcripts private. OpenAI is additionally developing an age-prediction system to flag under-18 users and apply stricter safety settings by default, amid growing regulatory scrutiny over AI’s potential mental health risks for minors.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Current Report on Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on April 16, 2020. The filing includes Items 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure) and 9.01 (Financial Statements and Exhibits), stating that a Letter to Shareholders accompanying its Annual Report for the year ended December 31, 2019 is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report is signed by David A. Zapolsky, Senior Vice President, dated April 16, 2020.

A £4.2 million Plymouth Studio School in Devon, opened to train students for sports careers, is set to close after Ofsted criticism and being rated “inadequate.” A “decision in principle” was made with the Regional Schools Commissioner’s (RSC) office and the Department for Education to shut the school, likely in September 2018, with a final decision expected from the Minister for Schools in July 2018. Headteacher Mark Cahill said staff and the local authority would work to ensure a smooth transition, noting there are sufficient secondary places to accommodate pupils. Pupils and parents were informed and invited to meetings, and the RSC will hold a listening period for parents. The council said it is not involved in closure decisions for academies but will place pupils and support families. The school opened first for students in November 2016 and earlier welcomed students in a temporary site.

The passage explains the HHLL trading strategy as a price-action reversal approach. It involves buying in a downtrend after the price makes a lower low and a higher high, then returns to the initial low; selling is the opposite in an uptrend after a higher high and a lower low return to the initial high. The strategy relies on identifying trend structure through swing highs and lows, looking for potential reversals when the series of swings breaks. It discusses difficulties in backtesting due to discretion in reading tops and bottoms, noting the ZigZag indicator lags and uses forward-looking elements. A simplified backtest example is described using an outside day criterion, and a backtest on Philip Morris (PM) reports 118 trades, a 9.8% CAGR, 1.26% average gain per trade, and a 2.2 profit factor.

Designs in Mind, a Community Interest Company, has taken a permanent lease on a shop in Cross Street, Oswestry, called Jolt, to help tackle stigma around mental health. After a successful pop-up trial earlier in the year at the former Chrissie’s, they moved into the shop next to their studio and opened it on 25 November. Jolt sells vibrant homeware and prints and offers public workshops in screen printing and lino printing. Jo Watkins said it is their first retail presence and a natural expansion aimed at drawing people into the shop and selling items to generate public interest about mental health. The products are designed by studio members referred through a mental health scheme and include goods from similar companies focused on mental health care. Rebecca Welch of Halls Commercial said Oswestry is changing and expressed support for Designs in Mind taking out a permanent lease.

The passage announces that Texas has agreed to congressional propositions in an act approved September 9, 1850, regarding establishing northern and western boundaries, relinquishing claimed exterior territory and U.S. claims, and creating a Territorial government for New Mexico. It states that Texas met the requirement to accept the propositions by December 1, 1850, and that an authenticated transcript of a Texas law passed November 25, 1850 accepting the propositions has been received. The passage includes the text of the Texas law accepting the terms, requesting copies be sent to the President and Texas members of Congress, and taking effect after passage. It further remarks that unanimity prevailed in Texas and congratulates Congress on the measure’s success, noting that territorial governments have been established and expressing confidence Congress will address further needs to strengthen the Constitution and the Union.

The passage describes how U.S. directives governed CIA covert actions from 1948 through the early 1960s. It lists prohibited or limited categories (e.g., recognized military armed conflict, espionage, and military cover and deception), and notes that the CIA’s Office of Policy Coordination (OPC) was established on September 1, 1948 to organize and manage covert actions. In 1950, guidance was routed through the DCI. During the Korean conflict, DCI Walter Bedell Smith sought clearer limits, leading to Truman’s creation of the Psychological Strategy Board (PSB) in April 1951 and NSC 10/5 in October 1951, which reaffirmed and expanded the CIA’s covert action authority over guerrilla warfare. The Eisenhower administration later narrowed CIA latitude through NSC 5412 in 1954, defining covert actions, assigning the DCI coordination responsibilities, and designating the Operations Coordinating Board for interdepartmental support. Subsequent directives (NSC 5412/1 and NSC 5412/2) established a “Special Group” to review and approve CIA-initiated covert action programs, with membership varying and meetings becoming weekly in 1959. After the Bay of Pigs failure in 1961, the Special Group assumed greater responsibility for planning and reviewing covert operations, and by 1963 developed informal criteria for submitting projects based on factors such as risk, success, exposure, political sensitivity, and cost.

Veteran actor-turned-politician Shatrughan Sinha criticized the BJP after its recent loss in Rajasthan bypolls, saying the “common man has started to speak.” He tweeted that people have been promised something unachievable. Sinha, who recently joined the Rashtra Manch platform, said he felt stifled in the BJP and that he was treated like a stepson. Union Minister Babul Supriyo responded by telling Sinha to give “triple talaq” to BJP and leave the party.

The passage describes the fullback as an offensive-line extension who does physical, “dirty work” to help the offense move the ball. Fullbacks typically line up in two-back sets next to or behind the quarterback and are most often used as blockers in run schemes and the pass game, including sealing blocks at the second level to create success for running plays. They are described as “tweeners,” usually too bulky for tight end but less athletic than running backs, and are common in pro-style offenses. The text notes fullbacks can also be involved in short-yardage plays such as “fullback dive” or short passes from the flat.
