The passage introduces polymer-grafted (“hairy”) nanoparticles and how their self-assembled mesostructures are typically controlled by polymer ligand properties and grafting. Molecular simulations model nanoparticles as rigid spheres with flexible polymer bead-chains, predicting various mesostructures based on polymer density, chain length, and interaction models such as optimal packing or cone and orbifold topological models. It highlights the example polymer PiPrOx, which can crystallize directionally into porous spheroidal clusters that sprout nanofibers, motivating a new coarse-grained model where crystallized bundles are represented as rigid rods.  

The work develops a “rod-sphere” coarse-grained particle: a spherical head tethered to a rigid rod (a bundled crystalline polymer surrogate). Using molecular dynamics, the authors reproduce experimental self-assembly behaviors of PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles, including small aggregates and fibers. They analyze mesostructures by clustering rods into ordered and disordered groups and computing a dimensionality parameter from the rods’ gyration tensor, alongside an order parameter measuring alignment.  

Results show that temperature and geometric frustration controlled by the sphere-to-rod size ratio R/r determine mesostructure classes, spanning zero- to three-dimensional forms (e.g., bulk, monolayers, bilayers, fibers/ribbons/worms, stars, spheres). Structural evolution is described in stages of aggregation, growth, and consolidation. Mesostructure maps are constructed for different rod interaction types (lock-and-key, symmetric, unspecific), and the sphere size generally lowers dimensionality and induces specific structures. The simulations also find spontaneous ribbon twisting into double helices, with helix pitch decreasing as sphere radius increases. The conclusions emphasize geometric frustration as the key driver, propose guidance for designing self-assembling nanobuilding blocks, and note limitations of the coarse-grained model and planned extensions (e.g., multiple rods).

Advancements in HIV treatment have made infection a chronic condition for many people in the Western world. In this study, the authors report a first transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) comparing virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH; N=194) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) to HIV-1 seronegative individuals (N=361) using RNA sequencing of whole blood. They found 566 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) by HIV status, with GO and KEGG overrepresentation of immune system processes and several cancer-related pathways. Whole-blood deconvolution using an immune-cell reference panel showed five immune cell types with significant proportion differences by HIV status. Using DICE expression profiles, the authors also assessed cell-type–specific expression patterns for HIV-associated DEGs.

To evaluate ART effects, they intersected HIV-associated DEGs with previously reported ART-affected genes and classified 234 as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected. ART-affected DEGs showed enrichment for immune- and viral-infection–related processes, nucleic acid/nucleoside metabolism, NK-cell functions, and cancer pathways, while ART-unaffected DEGs were enriched more narrowly for T cell biology. For genetic analyses, the authors tested whether genetic heritability of 30 traits was enriched near HIV-associated DEGs and found significant enrichment for some inflammatory diseases and blood cell traits, but not for cancer traits or HIV acquisition. They also mapped expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) for the DEGs, performed colocalization analyses with GWAS traits, and found limited shared genetics between HIV-associated DEGs and assessed cancers. Finally, they identified 111 HIV-associated DEGs that were targets of compounds in drug target databases, including cases where targets corresponded to approved drugs or trial compounds.

Overall, the study concludes that virally suppressed PLWH on ART exhibit widespread gene dysregulation linked to immune and cancer-related pathways, and that genetic susceptibility overlap with cancers is limited, while many DEGs may represent potential drug targets for comorbid conditions.

When powered with AVDD = 5 V, the internal OVP can withstand up to ±20 V on the analog input pins; Table 6-1 describes other operating conditions and notes that exceeding limits can cause irreversible damage. The passage also states that higher source impedance reduces diode current and increases the OVP voltage range. When AVDD is floating, protection limits change, with the OVP limit set at the input pin beyond ±15 V, as shown by I–V response figures.

The Ordnance Factories Board said it upgraded 130-mm field guns to 155-mm capability at its Nalanda facility in Bihar, and expects an Army order for 300 such guns. OFB Chairman S K Chourasia said the upgrade costs about Rs one crore per gun versus around Rs 15 crore for a new 155-mm gun, and involves changing the barrel, increasing range from about 27 km to 36 km. He added that the 100% indigenous solution succeeded against private competitors using imported equipment, and that R&D is being carried out at OFB’s 13 ordnance development centres with assistance from IITs.

The lecture discusses numerical linear algebra for solving \(Ax=b\) by elimination in the context of large sparse matrices. A key issue is “fill in,” where elimination changes many zero entries into nonzeros, reducing sparsity and affecting computational efficiency. The speaker explains that elimination can be viewed graph-theoretically: elimination removes edges and simultaneously creates new edges between nodes connected to a pivot node, leading to fill in. Because the order of elimination (reordering unknowns and equations via permutations) significantly affects fill in, different ordering strategies are introduced, including red-black ordering, approximate minimum degree (AMD), perfect minimum degree, and graph separators leading to nested dissection. The lecture describes how permutations relate to graph reordering and how fill in can be estimated from the nonzero structure of the resulting factors \(L\) and \(U\) (or from \(nnz(L)\) in MATLAB experiments). It concludes by outlining graph separator concepts: separating a graph into two groups with no direct connections, ordering the separator last, and applying nested dissection recursively.

Contractor’s Sand and Gravel, Inc. (CSG) petitioned for review of a Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission (FMSHRC) decision vacating an Administrative Law Judge’s (ALJ) award of attorneys’ fees and expenses under the Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA). CSG had previously successfully defended against Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) citations and civil penalty assessments. The court agreed the FMSHRC had jurisdiction to review the ALJ’s award, but held that the Department of Labor’s position in the underlying Mine Act proceedings was not “substantially justified.” The opinion states the regulation at issue required electrical grounding but did not prohibit frame grounding or require “fourth wire” grounding, and that the Secretary offered no evidence or testing to show CSG’s grounding method violated the regulation. The court reversed the FMSHRC and ordered the ALJ’s EAJA award restored, remanding for further proceedings to determine additional compensation for costs of the petition for review.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated September 11, 2015. Effective September 11, 2015, Bradford L. Smith was appointed President and Chief Legal Officer. The filing states Smith is 56, previously served as General Counsel & Executive Vice President, Legal and Corporate Affairs, joined Microsoft in 1993, and has served as General Counsel since 2002.

The passage contrasts the establishment survey and the household survey for September jobs. The household survey reports 906,000 more people at work than in August, with total employment reaching 154.3 million, a record. Unemployment fell by 331,000 to its lowest since July 2001, the labor force rose by 575,000 to a record high, and the employment-to-population ratio increased to 60.4%. The labor force participation rate rose to 63.1%, and the unemployment rate declined to 4.2%, the lowest in 16 and a half years. Average hourly earnings increased 2.9% (12 cents), tied with July for the biggest monthly gain since June 2007. Beth Ann Bovino of S&P Global Ratings said the stronger household results suggest a more upbeat labor market than the establishment report’s 33,000 job loss figure, attributing differences to possible effects of hurricanes and reporting ability. She also noted that nearly 1.5 million workers were unable to go to their jobs, the highest since January 1996, and that markets largely discounted negative parts of the report while waiting for more data.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2020. It includes the company’s SEC filing information, an index of items, and consolidated financial statements (unaudited) showing cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheet figures for Q2 2020 and related prior-year periods. It also describes accounting policies and supplemental disclosures, including inventory and receivables valuation, changes in the useful life estimate for servers, fair value measurements of financial instruments, lease information, and commitments and contingencies. Additional sections provide details on debt, stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation activity, income tax considerations, and segment information (North America, International, and AWS). Management’s discussion addresses liquidity and capital resources, results of operations and drivers of net sales and operating income, and the effects of the COVID‑19 pandemic on operations and costs.

The passage argues that people are never too young to start saving and investing, emphasizing that starting early increases wealth accumulation over time. It gives advice such as saving and investing for longer periods, making frequent contributions, separating savings from consumption to prevent overspending, moving money into investments as soon as possible, and using compounding by reinvesting earnings or dividends. It also recommends creating a formal budget based on take-home pay and reviewing variable spending to redirect money toward investing as income increases. The passage includes a disclaimer stating the information is for educational purposes only and not investment or tax/legal advice, and notes Calamatta Cuschieri has not verified the content.

The passage says Malik Nabers’ knee injury has renewed concerns about the turf at MetLife Stadium. An opposing-team executive said players are “petrified” of playing on MetLife’s FieldTurf and that injured players may be less likely to play through injuries there. The NFL Players Association’s interim executive director David White raised the turf issue, including its history of season-ending lower extremity injuries. Nabers suffered a season-ending torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee. The passage also notes that MetLife installed FieldTurf Core in 2023, and the NFL reported lower injury rates last year and fewer ACL injuries on synthetic turf than grass, along with players generally preferring grass over turf. It states the NFL has no plans to change MetLife’s playing surface.

The passage argues that philosophy of education is often treated as peripheral to mainstream educational research because educational scholarship is commonly framed as empirical, with non-empirical philosophical and theoretical work relegated to the margins. Texts on research methods acknowledge ethical and normative considerations but do not present philosophy of education as a way of conducting research, which can lead students to view it as lacking the essence of research. It also describes why students may avoid philosophy of education: academic precarity and job-market pressures, competitive and performative research assessment (including funding and impact factors), and “scientistic” expectations that prioritize randomized and other statistical experimental approaches while downplaying ethical questions and the limits of generalizability and prediction. The passage then discusses responses by philosophers of education, including encouraging critical understanding of evidence and impact, “pushing against the grain,” and defending the field’s value while noting internal debates about its purpose and success. It concludes by urging a move away from “golden years” and “new precarity” imaginaries toward viewing philosophy of education as a site of pluralism, community-based deliberation, and internal contestation, and calls attention to the dominant assumption that educational research must be empirical.

The passage describes a discussion in which a Soviet representative proposed that trusteeship arrangements for detached areas be included in the Charter, noting that the Soviet Union would need to assume responsibilities regarding Italian colonies and territories detached from Japan. The speaker said there was a tentative British arrangement to exchange documents and that they intended to make documents available to the Russians. They agreed that members of the League should take the initiative on liquidating the League of Nations. On initial membership, the Soviet Government wanted Soviet Republics included and associated nations and neutrals excluded, and the speaker said there were no new thoughts on either point. The conversation covered the possible seat of the organization, including the Pays de Gex idea and the idea of placing it in the Caucasus, and discussed Latin American proposals for the preamble and institutional changes, with concerns about altering the character of proposals by strengthening the Assembly and the Court at the expense of the Council. The speaker explained compulsory jurisdiction, and the Soviet representative questioned voting by permanent members; the speaker responded that advocacy of many ideas would be weakened by acceptance of their voting formula. The discussion ended with both sides agreeing it had been useful for the Soviet representative’s report.

The passage describes how cancer cells can transfer mitochondria to neighboring fibroblasts to manipulate them. Mitochondria move from cancer cells through threadlike nanotubes into fibroblasts, where within 24 hours the fibroblasts grow faster and increase activity of cancer-linked genes. The researchers identify a key protein, MIRO2, which shuttles mitochondria to the cell edge where the tubes form; without MIRO2, cancer cells cannot send mitochondria to fibroblasts. When turncoat fibroblasts were injected alongside cancer cells in mouse ears, tumors increased. The work suggests that mitochondrial transfer may be mutual and that cancer manipulation may extend beyond fibroblasts to immune cells.

The speaker says there is little carryover from last year because teams’ battle levels will be similar at this point in the season. They do not expect extra heated rivalries, even if a specific player returns, and say their focus remains on how they are playing in the playoffs. They believe any advantage for another team would come from the crowd and note that they must keep playing the same way as in the series. They mention early games where results were not satisfactory but they thought they played well enough to win at least one, and they say they missed opportunities despite being used to “crazy bounces.” They state that they needed to win at least one game in the series, remain confident, and are in that position.

The passage argues that the presidential oath does not require being taken in public, but that a public induction creates a “mutual covenant” between the President and the people to uphold the Constitution, serve the whole nation, and faithfully execute the laws. It describes the President’s term beginning as the twenty-sixth under the Constitution and looks to national growth and progress over the past century, while noting that not all citizens are yet happy, prosperous, virtuous, or law-abiding. It discusses how political and commercial developments, including tariff protections, domestic manufacturing, and the elimination of slavery’s sectional effects, are linked to unity and community interests. The passage also calls for uniform enforcement of laws by the Executive, careful naturalization laws, peaceful and non-coercive foreign policy consistent with friendly relations, civil-service reform, fiscal prudence to avoid large surpluses, adequate naval and pension provisions, and timely state admissions and election-law safeguards. It concludes by urging moderation of party conflict, respect for justice and mercy in governance, and confidence in the nation’s future.

The White Building at Penn State has been under renovation since summer 2016 and is expected to be completed by the end of March, with additional improvements continuing through the rest of the semester. Communications Manager Shea Bracken said the work includes renovating the main lobby, adding two registration desks, a new stairwell and elevator, and updating the main entrance exterior and pathway. The renovations aim to improve building flow, enable more efficient monitoring of traffic, comply with Penn State policy, improve safety, and track usage trends. The renovations follow an extensive IM Building renovation that is now in its final stages, and detours have not reduced gym membership or usage. Penn State does not plan to renovate the White Building fitness center anytime soon.

The global visceral pain market is expected to reach USD 14.22 billion by 2024, driven by increasing geriatric population, prevalence, and awareness. North America held the majority share in 2016 due to increasing healthcare expenditure, while Asia Pacific is projected to grow fastest with a CAGR of 6.2%. Crohn’s and irritable bowel prevalence is expected to support growth. The analgesic segment dominated with a 60.4% share, attributed to generic drug penetration and increased opioid use for chronic pain. In 2016, Crohn’s disease was the largest indication segment with a 41.4% share, supported by increased occurrences and drug therapies, along with rising awareness. Key players include Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Takeda, Allergan, and AstraZeneca, focusing on R&D for visceral pain therapeutics.

The passage says superannuation tax changes will take effect in July and are expected to increase self-managed super funds (SMSFs), with over two million Australians expected to have SMSFs in the next 15 years. It lists planned changes and their effects, including a $1.6 million transfer balance cap, changes to transition-to-retirement pensions, reductions to concessional and non-concessional contribution caps, rules on catch-up contributions, and several tax and retirement-product adjustments. It also notes that many younger Australians, including women, are setting up SMSFs, while the number of SMSFs among some groups is declining. Chan and Naylor are mentioned as discussing the changes and inviting readers to contact them for more information.

The passage argues that AI system effectiveness depends on high-quality training data and that regulated financial institutions have extensive data resources supported by global and national regulatory frameworks. It notes a sharp increase in AI adoption by top banks from 2019 to 2023, which increases the likelihood of AI incidents that must be reported to regulators but are rarely public. It critiques existing global AI incident databases that rely on crowdsourcing or news scraping for missing financial market incidents, such as algorithmic trade incidents, and proposes a “regulatory-grade” semi-public AI incident database. The proposed database would have regulators share standardized incident data in a secure environment, using percentage-based metrics and deliberately omitting temporal data to protect confidential business information and reduce market instability risks. It defines “significant incidents” as AI-driven trades causing more than 5% price deviation or more than 20% volume anomaly versus a 30-day average, and includes 15 mandatory fields across market context, volume metrics, price impact, and AI-specific information. The paper outlines two database use cases: systemic risk monitoring using synthetic incident records and detecting market manipulation using clustering and pattern analysis. It also describes intended contributions, methodology considerations, and concludes by advocating for intergovernmental cooperation via a global AI incident reporting framework.

The speakers discuss how every team goes through injuries and stresses, requiring competitors to stay in the lineup. They reflect on a previous series and describe the season as a physical grind that takes a toll. They say they remained confident, focused on themselves rather than outside noise, and view a loss as making the next game a must-win. They emphasize getting angry and giving maximum effort, and they want to avoid having bad games back-to-back by rebounding well.

The passage reports that the 7th Pay Commission news includes an order from the Ministry of Finance amending Rule 80 of the Compendium of Rules on Advances to Government Servants, which concerns the amount of advances to families of government servants who die while in service. It states the existing provisions are retained and amended per an annexure, take effect from the date of the office memorandum, and cases already sanctioned need not be reopened. It also notes that orders for the Indian Audit and Accounts Department are issued in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, and that all Ministries/Departments should notify their offices. The advance amount under Rule 80 is not to exceed Rs. 25,000.

Version 2 of the SEV-ES/SEV-SNP specification adds enhancements to SEV-ES support and initial support for SEV-SNP, including hypervisor feature advertisement so a hypervisor can advertise SEV-ES/SEV-SNP capabilities to the guest. It also introduces additional protocol details such as an XSS MSR value (when supported), requirements for the GHCB shared area to reside in the SEV-ES GHCB SW_SCRATCH field, and restricted APIC emulation support. Revision updates include changes to SEV-SNP Secrets Page message sequencing number handling, new/updated NAE error and SW_EXITINFO2 behaviors, and new capabilities like guest APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page state change notifications, SEV-TIO support, Secure AVIC, additional GHCB protocol functions/events, and documentation for hypervisor behavior on unsupported GHCB MSR functions. The passage further describes GHCB/VMGEXIT negotiation and examples, the GHCB protocol’s NAE event handling requirements (including VALID_BITMAP usage and SW_EXITINFO error signaling), and protocols for SEV-SNP secrets and Confidential Computing Blob EFI configuration tables. It also covers SEV-ES guest identification requirements, interrupt handling approaches (including NMI and #HV doorbell/Restricted Injection mechanisms), and related host/guest behaviors for doorbell page fields PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired.

Unemployment in Sweden stayed steady at 7.3% in July 2017, but it was 3.9% for people born in Sweden versus 21.8% for those born abroad. Arbetsförmedlingen reported a record 76,561 foreign job seekers registered in its Introduction Programme in July 2017, up from 59,362 a year earlier. The programme creates individualized plans based on newcomers’ work experience and education to prepare them for education or work. An increase was linked to Migrationsverket processing much of the backlog of asylum applications from 2015. The number of long-term unemployed grew from 142,499 to 145,896 between July 2016 and July 2017, with Introduction Programme participants making up most of the increase. Arbetsförmedlingen also warned it will need 600 million kronor more funding in 2018 and 900 million kronor more in 2019.

Derivatives trading involves buying and selling derivative contracts such as futures and options, whose value is derived from the performance of an underlying asset (e.g., commodity, stock, currency, index, or interest rate). Derivatives can be used to hedge against price movements or to speculate on price movements. Futures are exchange-traded standardized contracts obligating the parties to buy or sell a set quantity at a predetermined price at a future time. Options give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) an asset at an agreed strike price within a specific expiration period. The passage describes an option strategy as a predefined plan using multiple option contracts to create a specific risk-reward profile. It also notes that CFDs represent an agreement to exchange the difference in an underlying asset’s price between opening and closing a trade, and it outlines examples of hedging and speculation. The passage emphasizes that derivatives trading is risky, advises trading only with a hedging purpose or a specific backtested plan, using leverage conservatively, and not trading products one does not fully understand.

The paper addresses the need to accurately standardize messy POS transaction text with merchant IDs and details for risk assessment, user experience, and reduced inquiry costs. Traditional rule-based and Enhanced String Distance (ESD) methods are limited in scalability and coverage, with ESD managing less than 20% of transactions. The study compares pretrained large language models (LLMs) and small proprietary Transformer models, evaluating accuracy and efficiency. It proposes and tests six work streams across encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder architectures, including a Bi-Encoder SBERT approach and proprietary models trained with contrastive or cross-entropy loss. Experiments use synthetic data and evaluate performance using (weighted) accuracy across rulebased, ESD seen/unseen merchants, and manually labeled raw-cleansed transactions. Results show that larger models do not always outperform smaller proprietary models: proprietary models achieve comparable or better accuracy with fewer parameters and faster inference. Deployment uses a proprietary decoder-only model for previously unmanageable raw-cleansed transactions, increasing overall transaction coverage from 80% to 94% (a 14% improvement) and reducing estimated annual costs by about $13.2 million.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 21, 2015. The report states that Microsoft issued a press release on July 21, 2015 announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2015, and that a copy was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also notes that the information in the report and Exhibit 99.1 is not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act and will not be incorporated by reference except as expressly set forth. The report includes Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated July 21, 2015) and is signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage describes an IHE news and analysis podcast in which editor in chief Sara Custer speaks with IHE news editor Katherine Knott about recent developments from the White House and the Hill affecting higher education. It covers cuts to funding for minority-serving institutions, new restrictions on international students, and discussions about student borrowing rulemaking and the administration’s “Compact for Academic Excellence.” It also mentions what federal policy reporters will follow in the coming months and lists upcoming topics, including declines in world university rankings, a Western accreditor dropping DEI standards, student costs, economic uncertainty linked to September cuts, and a need for academic freedom.

Sunderland manager David Moyes named his team to face Liverpool, with Lamine Kone and Victor Anichebe ruled out due to knocks and Donald Love replacing the suspended Billy Jones at right-back. John O’Shea and Papy Djilobodji started in central defense, Jack Rodwell returned to midfield alongside Seb Larsson and Didier Ndong, and Fabio Borini and Adnan Januzaj supported Jermain Defoe in attack. The bench included George Honeyman, Josh Maja, Elliot Embleton, and Michael Ledger, and Sunderland’s bench totalled 34 Premier League appearances, with Wahbi Khazri the most experienced at 24 games. Moyes said he has limited resources for the January transfer window and wants to bolster the squad quickly.

GOG’s 2017 Piñata Madness event uses a loot-box-like approach by letting users buy $3 “piñatas” and “bust” them to receive a random game title from a prize pool. Each piñata is guaranteed to contain a game worth $6–$45, with expansions, soundtracks, and other items excluded, and users are “all but guaranteed” to receive a title they don’t already own unless they already own every game in the pool. Confirmed games in the pool include Heroes of Might and Magic V, Pillars of Eternity, and Shadow Warrior 2, and new games “may appear” as the event goes on, though GOG does not provide a full list or timing. Piñata contents are generated when purchased. The event runs until August 21, with piñatas automatically opened by August 28, and they can be bought and opened via the Piñata hub on GOG’s website.

The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the third time in six months, increasing the short-term rate by a quarter-point to 1%–1.25%. The Fed said it plans to gradually reduce its bond holdings later this year, which could push long-term rates higher. It expects economic growth to be sluggish but temporary, forecasts one additional rate hike this year, and did not indicate when it would occur. The Fed cited solid but slowing employment and inflation that has remained below its 2% target, while officials said inflation should pick up with the economy. It noted that policy uncertainty in Washington and differing expectations for the future of the Fed’s policy committee membership could lead to rates rising more slowly than otherwise. The passage also mentions potential candidates to fill three Fed board vacancies, including Randal Quarles, Marvin Goodfriend, and Robert Jones, and discusses the possibility of a more hawkish or dovish policy depending on who is chosen.

The passage describes chess’s origins in India about 1,500 years ago and its worldwide spread. It presents chess as an educational and cognitive activity associated with intelligence, strategy, logic, tactical skill, decision-making, planning, and critical thinking, and states that playing chess can improve students’ abilities including planning, concentration, memory, logical thinking, creativity, self-confidence, and social skills. It discusses purported benefits for schoolwork, mathematics, and reading, and highlights that chess provides feedback and encourages considering alternatives and probabilities. The passage also compares learning chess for children versus adults, outlines stages of chess expertise, and addresses debates about how directly chess influences education, noting methodological limitations in some studies and suggesting further research using deeper experimental designs and mixed methods.

The Horns offense is designed to use basic mid-screen/roll action more effectively by employing two high post screeners, which give the ball handler the option to drive off a screen in either direction and clears baseline defensive help. If defenders help, it creates open outside shot opportunities for spot-up shooters. The text notes that many teams have increased their use of Horns and that the alignment makes it effective against pressure defenses and difficult to disrupt by influencing the ball handler away from the screen. It outlines a two-phase schematic sequence: Phase 1 focuses on point guard dribble penetration off a high post screen with options such as driving, pull-up jumpers, return passes after switches, and kick-outs to wing shooters; Phase 2 describes ball reversal and post isolation involving posting up in the low post area and further screen and roll actions. The passage lists key reads and counter options for different defensive reactions, including responses to chasers, sagging help, defenders going under or switching screens, post mismatches, show-and-recover, traps, and overplays. It also describes multiple Horns variations (e.g., Loop, Base Split, Picked Fence, Twin Sides, High Post Rub, Hand Back Lob) and provides example action sequences for several. Finally, it emphasizes proper execution and coordination for installing Horns, mentions specific teaching drills and practice fundamentals, and provides game strategy guidance such as scouting opponents for defensive reads and varying alignments to prevent defenses from focusing on one setup, along with a section advocating preparedness to defend against Horns.

Accelerated frequency switching and faster low-power sleep states in Blackwell improve power efficiency by entering sleep quickly, adapting to short CPU idle gaps, and enabling higher GPU burst clocks. In real-life neural rendering inference examples, these features are said to reduce power consumption by up to 50% due to reduced active periods, lower power transitional states via power and voltage gating, and a deepest sleep state entered 10x faster than Ada. DLSS 4 is described as using transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, with claims of improved image quality, reduced artifacts, smoother motion, and better temporal stability. DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation is presented as generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame on Blackwell, using faster AI frame generation, reduced VRAM usage, and enhanced display-engine flip metering for more consistent frame pacing. The passage also describes Blackwell neural shaders and related features such as RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces, and provides hardware specifications for the Blackwell-based GB202 (flagship) and GB203 and GB205 GPUs, along with related GeForce RTX 50 series product lineup and legal/disclaimer information.

California’s 2016 Gun Violence Restraining Order law, used as a model for pending national legislation, led to 190 court orders in 2016-17 allowing police or others to temporarily remove firearms from people deemed dangerous. The process allows law enforcement or a family member/home occupant to ask a judge for an order, with the petitioner required to show alternative steps were tried and ineffective. Orders last 21 days, followed by a hearing to decide whether to extend them up to one year, and the target can present a counter-argument. Statistics cited by California’s Department of Justice show most orders ended after 21 days, with 17 extended to a full year. The law’s author, Sen. Nancy Skinner, said she expects some deaths were prevented and argued that police and family members should have this tool. Rubio introduced a bill to create a similar nationwide process after reports authorities missed “red flags” in the Florida mass shooter.

Taco Cabana is offering free breakfast tacos through a promotion called “Random Acts of Tacos.” In partnership with the delivery app Favor, today from 9–11am, users who log into Favor can click the promotion banner to request two breakfast tacos delivered in the Dallas delivery zone, while supplies last on a first-come, first-served basis. If the promotion is missed, Taco Cabana locations on Friday morning will provide coupons for a breakfast taco for a next visit, also limited in supply.

AMD created Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) to enable secure, non-persistent runtime updates to selected AMD firmware and settings without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS targets “high-benefit/low-risk” issues, can improve system stability and health, and can mitigate some security issues to reduce unplanned maintenance. It does not patch x86 code (e.g., SMM, AGESA, UEFI) or run-once code such as the AGESA boot loader (ABL). 

AMD limits SFS to priority runtime concerns affecting AMD-provided binary firmware components included in an AGESA release, while other microprocessors can receive updates. SFS updates are interim between BIOS releases and do not persist across reboots. Each SFS update package is cryptographically signed by AMD, with an optional customer co-signing feature where the customer provides a public key during early boot; customers are responsible for maintaining co-signing keys. The ASP verifies signatures, validates package applicability based on version levels (including SFS patch level, component security patch levels, and a system patch level for run-once code), and then executes patches. Applying SFS packages must occur at runtime and be reapplied after reboot; the customer deploys an SFS Deployment Agent to initiate and track updates, and SFS commands require specific memory alignment and buffer handling.

Pharmaceutical dosage form testing systems verify the efficacy and bioavailability of drug formulations, especially by evaluating a tablet’s chemical, physical, and bioavailability properties and monitoring product quality. QC tests include weight variation, content uniformity, diameter and thickness, hardness, friability, disintegration, and dissolution, along with testing for formulary stability and potential degradation and verifying physical strength. The systems may include features such as vibration-free tablet separation, auto separation, and auto alignment, and production uses tests at every stage to ensure compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices. Quality checks are described as important for patient safety and for protecting manufacturers. The global market is expected to grow, driven by regulations (e.g., U.S. FDA) requiring quality, efficacy, and safety checks and by advanced technology, though high system prices and a shortage of skilled personnel may restrain growth. The market is segmented into North America, Latin America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, APCEJ, China, Japan, and Middle East & Africa, with North America expected to dominate by revenue and APECJ and China expected to register significant growth. Market participants listed include SOTAX AG, ABC Laboratories, Almac, Dalton Pharma Services, GEA Process Engineering, Micromeritics Instrument Corporation, Quality Chemical Laboratories, and SCYNEXIS, Inc.

Future Market Insights (FMI) published a report on the global surface protection films market, estimating revenue growth at a 5.7% CAGR over 2017–2027. The market is projected to increase from US$ 1,196.2 Mn in 2017 to US$ 2,081.6 Mn by 2027. The report segments the market by thickness (with 50–100 microns at nearly 38% share and 6.2% CAGR), base material (PE above 40% share; PET highest CAGR at 6.3%), and end use (construction & interior leading with over 50% share, forecast around 56% by 2027). By region, Western Europe is estimated to lead in 2017 with a 30.4% share, followed by Asia Pacific Excluding Japan (22.6%); Latin America is forecast to grow at 4.7% CAGR. Key players listed include Chargeurs S.A., Nitto Denko Corp, Tredegar Corporation, Polifilm GmbH, and others, with company strategies and Chinese company profiles included.

The passage describes the U.S. government’s decision to represent itself at a Panama congress of American nations after invitations from Colombia, Mexico, and Central America. It states that, although the executive had constitutional authority to proceed, no action would be taken until the Senate and both Houses agreed through Senate decisions on nominations and legislative approval of appropriations. A report and related correspondence from the Secretary of State are transmitted to the Senate, and the passage lists expected discussion topics, including principles of liberal commercial intercourse, maritime neutrality in war, limiting blockades through general agreement, and guarding against future European colonies. It also mentions the possible moral influence of the United States on advancing religious liberty. The passage concludes by saying the nomination of Richard C. Anderson and John Sergeant as envoys and William B. Rochester as secretary to the mission will be submitted for approval.

The professor introduces standard “social preference” games to demonstrate how they work and what participants experience. In the dictator game, one person (dictator/divider) gets money (or candy/apples/chocolates) and decides how much to share with a randomly selected receiver, who otherwise does nothing. The class compares versions with different stakes, with and without communication, and with varying levels of privacy/publicity of outcomes, including examples of messages exchanged. The professor then presents the ultimatum game: a proposer offers a division of a sum to a responder, who can accept or reject; rejection gives both nothing. Communication is added in later rounds, and roles may be rotated or used for strategic, contingency-based elicitation. Next, the trust game is explained as an investor who sends money to a responder, which is multiplied (by 3 in the classroom example), and the responder can send part of it back; versions without and with communication are played. The session ends by noting that the next class will discuss these games in detail and how careful research approaches differ from the demonstration, including questions about what the games predict for real-world behavior.

Hollywood Bowl Group’s full-year results prompted a near 8% rise in its share price. Revenue increased by almost 9% year over year, while like-for-like sales rose 3.5%. The company reported higher profits, with net cash from operations up more than 16% and adjusted underlying earnings after tax up 30%, though adjusted diluted earnings per share fell 8% due to a higher share count. The directors announced a meaningful first-time full-year dividend yielding a little over 1.9%, plus a special dividend taking the yield to over 3.5%. The company operates 58 bowling centres in the UK, opened three new centres during the period (with a fourth opened after the trading year), and described refurbishments, rebranding, and new sites as performing strongly. The passage contrasts this with UK Oil & Gas Investments’ onshore UK exploration plans and volatile share performance, suggesting Hollywood Bowl’s cash flow is more dependable.

Reuters describes ARSA attacks in Myanmar’s Rakhine state in late August 2017 and accounts from Rohingya fighters interviewed in Bangladesh refugee camps. Mohammed Rashid, a Rohingya shopkeeper who joined ARSA two months earlier, said he and about 150 men attacked a Myanmar Border Guard Police post with swords, homemade explosives and some handguns, and that many attackers lacked training and weapons despite promises of AK-47s. Other fighters reported recruitment through religious teachers and Whatsapp messaging, with homemade explosives delivered in advance. ARSA, emerging in 2016, says it fights for Rohingya rights, while Myanmar calls it a ruthless Islamist extremist movement. Reuters reports that some refugees support continued fighting, while others criticize the insurgents and say violence brings more suffering. A UN-branded ethnic cleansing operation by Myanmar’s army led hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh, where analysts said desperation in camps could help ARSA recruit and radicalize supporters.

The passage reports a systematic evaluation of reasoning in voice-interactive systems and documents a consistent performance drop called the Voice Reasoning Gap (VRG), which is most pronounced on complex, multi-step reasoning. It contrasts voice accuracy with text-model accuracy (e.g., GPT-realtime 6.1% vs. GPT-5 74.8% on math) and argues the problem is not purely acoustic, since voice models can transcribe and analyze audio well. The authors hypothesize an architectural conflict between low-latency streaming and revisable reasoning, and introduce the Voice Evaluation of Reasoning Ability (VERA) benchmark to measure reasoning under real-time constraints. Using VERA, they find a latency–accuracy trade-off, with fast voice models plateauing around ~10% accuracy and reaching higher accuracy requiring sacrificing real-time interaction. They evaluate 2,931 voice-optimized episodes across five tracks (Math, Web, Science, Context, Factual) and measure speech fidelity (WER), task accuracy (LLM judge), and failure modes. Results show an average 40.4-point accuracy drop for voice models versus text, with near-total collapse on math for GPT-realtime (6.1% vs. 74.8% for GPT-5). Diagnostic experiments indicate the gap persists even with more thinking time, improved audio fidelity, and a decoupled cascade baseline (LiveAnswer), suggesting a fundamental architectural constraint. The passage concludes that different voice architectures fail in distinct ways—native streaming models often produce fluent but incorrect responses, while decoupled systems are more prone to logical/grounding inconsistencies—and argues that bridging the VRG likely requires architectures that explicitly decouple thinking from real-time narration.

Seattle beat the San Francisco 49ers 25-23 to close the regular season. Coach Pete Carroll pulled Russell Wilson and other key players to keep them fresh after a first-round bye became unlikely, and Wilson threw for 258 yards and a touchdown before being replaced in the fourth quarter. Seattle rallied from an early 11-point deficit. The Falcons’ 38-32 win over New Orleans sent the Seahawks to the playoffs as the NFC West champion and third seed, and Seattle will host Detroit next week. Hours after the game, the 49ers fired coach Chip Kelly and general manager Trent Baalke.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeffrey McMahon after the Securities and Exchange Commission began looking into partnerships Fastow ran. Enron’s chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the change was necessary to restore investor confidence, and Fastow was put on a leave of absence while the partnerships were dissolved. Enron’s shares fell sharply following the announcements, and analysts cited concerns about complex financial arrangements, lack of disclosure, and potential further liabilities. Multiple news outlets also reported related losses and ongoing scrutiny, including SEC inquiries and investor and legal concerns involving the partnerships.

Ronny Jackson, the president’s nominee for secretary of veterans affairs and current White House physician, faces allegations of professional misconduct, including creating a hostile work environment and improperly dispensing the sleep aid Ambien, as well as accusations of being drunk on duty during travel. His confirmation hearing was put on hold as the Senate reviews the claims. Jackson said he is eager to answer the committee’s questions. The president said he would stand by Jackson and criticized the allegations as partisan, while the White House later said Jackson met with the president late today, has a “clean bill of health,” and has no plans to withdraw the nomination. Some Republicans called for more time to review. Critics said the administration failed to properly vet him.

A grassroots group of community college administrators fighting legislative attacks on diversity, equity and inclusion will see Gavin step down as president of Delta College in January, a role he has held since 2021. Gavin told the Board of Trustees he plans to resign to lead a national coalition focused on defending equity in higher education, with more details about the coalition to be released soon. Delta College trustees said they will begin appointing his successor in the coming weeks.

The passage introduces NVIDIA’s Ampere architecture GPU family, focusing on GA102 and GA104 (the GA10x “GA10x” class), which build on the earlier Turing architecture and add features for faster traditional graphics and ray tracing. It describes specific GPU models (A100, GA102 in GeForce RTX 3090/3080, RTX A6000, and A40) and compares performance and power efficiency versus Turing, including up to 2x gains in ray tracing and improvements such as 2x FP32 processing, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity support and added precision modes. The architecture overview covers fabrication details, core resource types (CUDA, RT, Tensor), memory subsystem features (GDDR6X, NVLink, PCIe Gen 4), and SM and GPC composition. Additional sections explain concurrent execution via async compute, hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur, DLSS and 8K support, RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading/decompression, and data-center oriented capabilities of the NVIDIA A40. It also outlines display and video engine features for GA10x GPUs, including AV1 decode via NVDEC and video encoding via NVENC, and provides related specifications and disclaimers.

The passage describes controversy over President Donald Trump attending the opening of the Mississippi Civil Rights Museum in Jackson. Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba said the museum’s opening recognizes a struggle and should focus on what comes next, while expressing concerns about Trump’s positions, including Trump’s refusal to condemn white supremacists and comments that seemed to justify slavery. It also recounts Trump’s promotion of Roy Moore and Trump’s scripted comments at the visit. Lumumba states his goal is for Jackson to be the “most radical city” by increasing people’s access through people’s assemblies, which are described in the Jackson-Kush Plan as vehicles of Black self-determination and participatory direct democracy without a preordained hierarchy. The movement’s origins are linked to post–Hurricane Katrina organizing and Lumumba’s family history in Jackson politics, including earlier campaigns against the Klan. The passage ends with a correction that Lumumba became mayor in 2017, not 2016.

The passage describes a Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) campus guide, “The Alt-Right on Campus: What Students Need to Know,” released shortly before clashes tied to the “Unite the Right” rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. The guide aims to help students respond to an influx of alt-right speakers on college campuses by providing a 360° overview of the movement and advice to avoid “spectacle” or heated confrontations, including engaging classmates and producing videos or pamphlets. It says students are not adequately prepared, and that administrators struggle to balance free speech with curbing hate speech. It also discusses how white nationalism has spread on campuses since around 2012 and recounts canceled and protested speaker events at Berkeley and Auburn. The guide’s most crucial advice is not to engage directly with the speaker or resort to violence.

The TLV32xx input voltage range is 200 mV below V− to 200 mV above V+, with any differential input voltage within these limits and no comparator output phase inversion when staying within range. The rail-to-rail input includes an ESD clamp to V+ and must not exceed the supply voltages by more than 200 mV; TI does not recommend applying signals when no supply voltage is present. Input current must be limited to 10 mA or less, and TI recommends adding series resistance for transients or faults. Unused inputs should not be tied together; instead, they must be tied to voltages within the specified range providing at least 50 mV differential. The TLV32xx family has 1.8 mV internal hysteresis described by VTH, VOS, and VHYST, and unused comparator outputs should be handled according to whether the device uses push-pull (left floating; never tied to supplies/ground/another output) or open-drain (left floating or tied to V−). The document also covers ESD protection limits, a power-on-reset period that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after VPOR crosses 1.65 V, and design notes for comparator behavior and external hysteresis.

The passage describes a Supreme Court habeas case involving Michael Bowe, a federal prisoner seeking to challenge his firearm conviction through a successive habeas petition. It explains his procedural path to the Supreme Court and two questions raised: whether the Court has jurisdiction given a bar in 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E), and whether the court of appeals erred in dismissing his claim under 28 U.S.C. § 2241(b)(1), which refers to claims under § 2254 that were previously presented. Bowe’s lawyer argued that a dismissal based on § 2241(b)(1) should not be treated as a “grant or denial of authorization” under § 2244(b)(3)(E), citing a Supreme Court case about the effect of recharacterizing prior filings as § 2255 motions. The federal government and another advocate responded by defending the application of § 2244(b)(1) to federal prisoners and addressing how dismissals operate under § 2244(b)(3)(E). The passage notes that the justices appeared to focus heavily on the jurisdictional issue and that there did not appear to be five votes for holding that § 2244(b)(1) applies to federal inmates, assuming the Court reaches that question.

Randall Margraves, a father of three daughters abused by former sports doctor Larry Nassar, tried to attack Nassar in a Michigan courtroom after Judge Janice Cunningham denied his request to confront Nassar “in a locked room.” Margraves was blocked by an attorney, tackled by sheriff’s deputies, and removed from court, later apologizing for losing control. Cunningham said she would not fine or jail him for contempt and stated it is unacceptable to respond to assault with assault. The incident occurred during Nassar’s final sentencing hearing; he admitted sexually assaulting girls under the guise of medical treatment and was sentenced to prison terms for abuse and child pornography. Margraves’ action followed his daughters’ statements in court, and after the rush, an attorney urged families to use “words, not violence,” while Margraves apologized and said he snapped.

The passage explains that Python is an open-source, high-level language used for algorithmic trading and data analysis, including backtesting and executing trading algorithms. It describes trading algorithms as programs that analyze markets, execute trades, and manage them based on predefined instructions (e.g., timing, price, quantity). Backtesting is presented as applying a coded strategy to historical price data under strict buy/exit rules to assess past performance, while noting it does not guarantee future success and may omit fees. The passage lists several Python backtesting frameworks—Zipline, LEAN (Quantconnect), Fastquant, Backtrader, Bt, PyAlgoTrade, and others—and provides general notes on their capabilities and tradeoffs. It also outlines a typical backtesting workflow (import libraries, download OHLCV data, split into in-sample and out-of-sample data, run and optimize, then analyze results) and states that Python is widely used for algorithmic trading because of readability and library support.

The lecture introduces data structures designed for memory hierarchies, contrasting the RAM model with real systems that use multiple cache levels and deeper, slower storage. It presents the external memory (I/O/DAM) model, focusing on minimizing block transfers between an infinitely fast cache and an infinitely large, slow disk, where transfers occur in blocks of size \(B\) and the cache has size \(M\). The passage discusses bounds on memory transfers and provides examples and results in this model: linear-time scanning in \( \lceil N/B \rceil \) block transfers, and B-tree search taking \( \log_{B+1} N \) block transfers, along with information-theoretic reasoning for search lower bounds. It then covers more advanced results such as improved sorting bounds, permutation-related limitations, and buffer trees for dynamic behavior using amortized costs.

The lecture transitions to the cache-oblivious model (introduced in 1999), where algorithms do not know \(B\) or \(M\), but block transfers are assumed to bring or evict entire blocks automatically, with replacement modeled as optimal offline or approximated by strategies like LRU/FIFO. It summarizes cache-oblivious performance results for scans, searches, sorting, permutation (including negative results for optimal min), and priority queues under a “tall cache” assumption. Finally, it explains how cache-oblivious search trees can achieve \( \log_{B} N \) search performance using van Emde Boas layouts for static trees, then outlines how dynamic cache-oblivious B-trees are built using additional techniques including order file maintenance (as a black box) and indirection to improve update costs.

The speakers said they were pleased with their series start after a close victory, noting the next game is crucial. They discussed player evaluations and team approach, emphasizing defensive discipline, staying composed under pressure, and not trying to force plays offensively. They credited solid goaltending and defense for blocking and clearing, and said they regained stability after tying moments. They referenced momentum shifts from penalties and goals, praised Philadelphia as an excellent road team, and stressed starting strong in the third game with proper preparation. They also said their recent playoff experience has helped the team remain comfortable, and they commented on penalties and power-play concerns.

The Kentucky Supreme Court granted discretionary review to address confusion over the test under KRS 342.120(4) for determining workers’ compensation responsibility for prior occupational disability when a subsequent injury occurs. David Eugene Bunch had a 1964 automobile accident causing a back fracture and surgery with one year incapacity. After re-injuring his back in 1976 and undergoing surgery in January 1977, he returned to work and then suffered a work-related April 11, 1977 accident that left him 100% totally and permanently disabled. The Workers’ Compensation Board found that the April 1977 injury alone accounted for 15% occupational disability, while 55% was due to Bunch’s occupational disability existing immediately before the injury and thus excluded that portion from Special Fund payment; the Special Fund was responsible for the remaining 30% involving a previously dormant, non-disabling condition becoming disabling. The Daviess Circuit Court affirmed the Board, but the Court of Appeals reversed and remanded for apportionment of the 55% based on Yocum cases distinguishing “dormant” and “active” disability. The Supreme Court disagreed, cited Griffin v. Booth Memorial Hospital for the proper test focusing on the degree of occupational disability immediately before the second injury (not whether the claimant was working), overruled contrary language, and held that Bunch failed this test because the medical evidence attributed functional and occupational disability to him immediately before the subsequent injury. The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and affirmed the Daviess Circuit Court judgment.

Electronic Arts said it will go private in a $55 billion all-cash deal backed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the largest leveraged buyout in history. CEO Andrew Wilson, who joined EA in 2000 and became chairman in 2021, will remain CEO. The deal ends Wall Street pressure, but analysts and professors quoted by Business Insider said private ownership could still bring demands. Observers noted the offer includes about a 25% premium and that EA had limited other buyers due to antitrust hurdles. The passage also discusses recent stock declines tied to EA Sports FC challenges, expectations for “Battlefield 6,” and concerns about EA’s dependence on older franchises and difficulty in mobile gaming.

The Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the European Central Bank (ECB) are assessing a possible link between their instant payment systems to enable faster cross-border transfers. The proposed linkage would connect Switzerland’s SIC network with the Eurosystem’s TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) platform, moving funds between currency areas in seconds. The exploratory phase runs through 2026 and will assess technical and economic feasibility, including legal/compliance, operational frameworks, and settlement risk. The SNB says the move would reduce friction and correspondent banking reliance, supporting G20 efforts to improve global payments. The ECB describes the project as consistent with its strategy to improve cross-border payment interoperability, while noting challenges such as liquidity management harmonisation, cybersecurity, and regulatory alignment.

The passage is an email dated November 17, 2001 from Commissioner.COM to Paul Lucci containing promotional links and Fantasy Football content. It lists “Luccis Losers” roster players, including 8 active and 7 reserve players, with their next bye weeks and an “NFL Injuries for Luccis Losers” section covering several players’ injuries and expected returns. They describe the Stanley Cup Finals context, with Boston having home ice advantage, and emphasize the importance of top players meeting their standards. The team says it has faced adversity all season and has respect for the Bruins’ play while believing they are also a strong team aiming to prove it tomorrow night. The speaker mentions coaching focus areas related to goaltending success and team execution, and highlights leadership and accountability in the dressing room, with players determined to come ready and seize the opportunity. They address limited offense in the series as a team issue rather than a goaltender issue, and discuss trusting specific players and their power play. The speaker also comments on emotions and physical incidents late in previous games.

Colorado Boy Scout Troop 1532 is composed almost entirely of refugees from places such as Burma, Rwanda, and Nepal. The troop, formed in 2014 by Dr. P.J. Parmar in conjunction with a refugee clinic in the Denver area, has members who have moved to the Denver area and, in some cases, previously lived in refugee camps after their parents fled violence. Leaders say the troop helps refugee kids adjust to American culture while giving them a safe place to be themselves, including during campouts that feature foods like fish head stew, fire-roasted corn, and Chatpate alongside s’mores. Leaders also describe challenges including difficulty keeping leaders and maintaining membership, parents working long hours with limited money, lack of reliable transportation to meetings, and issues with discipline or conduct at some camps. A Boy Scouts of America spokeswoman said

Leeds United lost 1-0 at home to Wolves, slipping out of the play-off places after a poor first half. Despite improving in the second half and dominating at times, Leeds created few chances and were shut out, with only one shot on target. The result leaves Leeds seventh, with Reading, Sheffield Wednesday, and Fulham all winning, and Leeds may need to win their remaining games to reach the play-offs. The only goal came in the 39th minute when Nouha Dicko beat Bartley and Rob Green after a Wolves counterattack. Attendance was 32,351, and the match was refereed by Jeremy Simpson.

The passage explains that ChatGPT, an AI system developed by OpenAI and launched in November 2022, can be used in trading to analyze market data, generate trading ideas, and backtest trading strategies. It describes training/asking ChatGPT for specific trading goals, noting it can produce incorrect or insufficiently detailed answers, which users can prompt it to expand. The article provides an example where it prompts ChatGPT to write a Python backtest program for a Bollinger band mean reversion strategy using pandas, numpy, yfinance, and matplotlib, and then runs the unchanged code. The backtest uses SPY data adjusted for dividends and splits, resulting in an equity curve and calculated metrics including a CAGR of 3.20%, 326 trades, and 45.63% time in the market. It emphasizes that ChatGPT is not a trading platform and does not provide financial advice or make investment decisions, and it is positioned as a tool for brainstorming ideas and generating backtests in Python.

The speaker says their approach will not change and they are in an “exciting spot.” They want to be more effective with rebounds and shooting, noting that pucks seem to be bouncing off their goaltender. They emphasize moving on after last night’s game, building on it, and focusing on the next game in St. Louis, which they say they must win. They also address a fast penalty/mistake they feel went uncalled, but say the team did not dwell on it and was able to score soon after. The speaker concludes that their line chemistry and comfort playing together should not be an issue because they share the same system and game plan.

Gold prices surged beyond $4,000 per ounce as investors sought safety amid growing expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will begin easing monetary policy in coming months. The rally followed disappointing U.S. retail and manufacturing data, weakening yields and the dollar and making non-yielding assets like gold more attractive. Analysts linked the move to a broader flight to safety, supported by central banks’ continued gold purchases and geopolitical tensions, while sentiment toward risk assets weakened. However, analysts cautioned that stronger U.S. growth or hawkish Fed signals could prompt short-term corrections, noting the $4,000 breakthrough reflects confidence that the next policy move will be toward easing.

The passage describes Michael Bowe’s 2008 armored car robbery in Florida and his later federal guilty plea, including a Section 924(c) firearm count that required proof the robbery-related offenses were “crimes of violence.” After Supreme Court decisions between 2019 and 2022 narrowed which robbery conspiracies or attempts qualify as crimes of violence, the passage says Bowe argued his Section 924(c) conviction should be vacated through habeas petitions under the federal habeas statute. It outlines procedural hurdles for “second or successive” petitions under Section 2255, including gatekeeping under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E), constitutional arguments about Congress’s control of Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction, and the 11th Circuit’s interpretation of 18 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1) for dismissing previously presented claims, with discussion of related doctrines and the parties’ positions.

ESPN reports that Shedeur Sanders, after being traded onto the Browns’ roster, described being in a “great mental space” and said he is thankful for whatever his role is. Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said he is not yet ready to name Sanders as QB2 and plans to “let the week play out.” Sanders previously spent the first five games as the inactive emergency quarterback and, through the first month, split scout-team reps with Dillon Gabriel and Zappe. Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees praised Sanders’ preparation and improvement. Sanders also addressed critical comments from ESPN analyst Rex Ryan, saying he wants to stay positive and manage how his personality is interpreted.

Coach Dean Smith’s “Four Corner” offense for the University of North Carolina is described as a recognizable spread offense that requires players with special ballhandling skills and one-on-one capability. Spreading the floor into four corners creates isolation for O1, allowing a single player to control the game while reducing ballhandling errors, turnovers, and opponents’ offensive possessions. The passage outlines basic continuity actions: O1 attacks a defender one-on-one, passes to corner players when penetration is cut off, and uses kick-out and baseline actions with options to pass to stepping-out corner players or execute back cuts. It also describes “Return Pass Denial,” where if X1 denies a return pass to O1, O1 exchanges with O2 or O1 exchanges with O3 to initiate dribble penetration.

The passage describes a continuation patent application related to near-eye displays, focusing on waveguide/scanning MicroLED-array display designs. It explains that a waveguide display for VR/AR/MR includes a frame and display assembly with a source assembly and output waveguide that expands and outputs scanned image light to a user’s eyes. A controller provides scanning instructions to control illumination parameters and scanning components (such as scanning mirrors or rotating/actuating waveguides). The source can use MicroLEDs (or other light sources) arranged in one-dimensional, two-dimensional, sparse, curved, or stacked arrays, with options to mitigate optical interference using optical isolators (e.g., aluminum films) and non-adjacent die layouts. The passage also describes waveguide coupling/decoupling elements (e.g., diffraction gratings) and provides example geometries and an illustrative calculation approach for determining MicroLED array/group counts for target brightness.

Air Canada apologized and offered compensation to a family after the boy was bumped from an oversold flight, Brett Doyle said. Doyle said the family, traveling from Charlottetown to Montreal to connect to Costa Rica, was told at the airport there was no seat for the 10-year-old, then drove to Moncton to find the alternate flight canceled. Doyle said Air Canada contacted him with an apology and a C$2,500 trip voucher only after his family’s story was published. The company said it was investigating what went wrong and had apologized and offered “very generous compensation.” Doyle linked the public reaction to a separate overbooking incident involving United Airlines that led to a passenger being dragged from a seat.

The passage praises constructive statesmanship in the Philippine Islands and notes that the Army has been reduced to the minimum allowed by law while remaining highly efficient. It stresses the need for better training, special attention to marksmanship, continued army maneuvering, and reforms including a general staff, supply department reorganization, and prompt action on reorganizing the militia system and defining National Guard relations. It also urges provisions for replacing worn-out cavalry and artillery horses and calls for increased naval gunnery funding, continued naval expansion, and adequate staffing of ships with sufficient skilled sailormen and mechanics. It argues that naval strength is necessary to support foreign policy and ensure peace, and warns that neither ships nor crews can be improvised once war begins.

The passage explains how youth soccer coaches initially place players into positions by choosing formations based on players’ abilities, skill levels, temperaments, and the coach’s familiarity. It describes basic position groups (goalkeepers, back defenders, midfielders, forwards) and the skills and traits associated with each, and recommends evaluating players informally or formally using methods such as observation, drills, testing interaction, player input, outside review, scrimmages, and tracking success and understanding. After evaluating players, the coach selects a formation, assigns specific position names, draws and distributes the formation with attack/defense directions, and has players memorize and recognize their roles. Coaches place players on the field at practices, move the team together while maintaining relative positioning, quiz players on positions, and demonstrate expectations for each position. The passage emphasizes not type-casting players, exposing all players to all positions, and using skills development and small-sided games, while factoring program objectives like equal playing time and development—such as using a playing-time chart and sometimes rotating or adjusting less-skilled players’ roles. It also notes that coaches may not know who will become a late-bloomer.

Rush Bowls, a Colorado smoothie chain, opened its first St. Louis-area shop last month in the Central West End. Customers order at the counter and wait for their bowls, which are blended fruit bases that can be topped and mixed with options such as fat-free milk, fat-free frozen yogurt, vanilla soy, acai, chai, granola, peanut butter with house-made jelly, or basic smoothies. There are seventeen basic smoothie varieties at $6.50, and bowls in four categories priced at $7.95 each, including “Enlightened Bowls” (e.g., the “Yoga Bowl” and “Oasis Bowl”) and four acai bowl options, with acai added as a topping. Seasonal bowls include one for dogs, and “Comfort Bowls” are described as comfort in the form of toppings rather than foods like mashed potatoes, cheese, nachos, or rice. The shop is noted as very noisy due to blender reverberation, with limited indoor seating, and the chain is positioned as a post-workout or pre-workout place to eat.

The passage describes how quality education under the UN 2030 Agenda requires digital transformation, defined as coordinated culture, workforce, and technology shifts that enable new educational models. While digital transformation offers higher education institutions (HEIs) opportunities to improve access, equity, and quality, least developed countries face barriers, including unequal internet access. Data from the ITU show lower internet use in LDCs than in developed countries, and the passage notes that this unequal access can affect information access and international networks, with implications for competitiveness and economic development. It also reports that COVID-19 increased reliance on internet access and highlighted the need for broadband infrastructure.

The passage focuses on Ethiopia, outlining national plans and policies that support digitalization, including ICT-related strategies and the creation of the Ministry of Science and Higher Education (MoSHE) in 2018, which developed multiple ICT and digital-skills policies for higher education and TVET. It also describes initiatives such as the Ethiopian Education and Research Network (EthERNet) and national digital repositories/libraries (NADRE and NADLE), while noting limited capacity and remaining challenges. In terms of actual digitalization practices, it states that Ethiopia’s HEIs mainly use ICT to support day-to-day services and administrative functions, with digital use in teaching and research described as still in early stages.

Finally, the passage identifies factors that deter digital transformation in Ethiopian higher education, especially poor internet connection and ICT infrastructure, lack of skilled human resources and digital skills, and resistance to change. It concludes that policies and strategies alone are insufficient without enabling conditions in HEIs, including reliable and affordable internet, digital infrastructure, skilled personnel, and effective leadership and governance.

US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures fell 46 cents to $52.72 a barrel after rising 7 cents to $53.18 on Thursday. Both WTI and Brent had risen last week for a third consecutive week, but trading was subdued as attention focused on higher US shale oil output, including additional rigs for a 13th straight week and 11 new oil rigs as of April 13. Increasing US production was said to undermine efforts by Opec and others to curb output in an oversupplied market. The passage also notes lower Libyan output due to faction fighting, plans by Libya’s NOC to reopen fields, market expectations of possible renewed North Korea tensions, China’s first-quarter growth and strong data, and Iran’s role in hopes that Opec and non-Opec producers could extend output cuts beyond the initial six-month agreement.

EUR/USD fell further on Tuesday due to disappointing Eurozone economic data and the start of Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s two-day testimony before Congress. Euro area GDP and German GDP both came in below expectations, the German ZEW sentiment indicator was below forecast, and euro area industrial production declined more than expected. Chart-wise, EUR/USD has been declining since early February, moving back into a longer-term bearish trend, with potential targets at 1.0500 and, if it breaks, around 1.0350.

A jury is deciding whether Tomas Gajowniczek should be found not guilty by reason of insanity for the attempted murder of Alicja Kalinowska on June 16, 2016, and related serious harm charges. The prosecution said he was high on cannabis and not eligible for the insanity verdict, citing evidence that he intended to kill her and expert testimony that he had drug-induced psychosis. The defence argued that he had a mental disorder at the time and could not refrain from his actions, disputing aspects of the prosecution’s cannabis/intoxication claims and describing prior events involving suspicion and alleged psychosis. Justice Patrick McCarthy will complete the jury charge.

In 1850 Prince Alexander and Lott Kamehameha, with Dr. G. P. Judd as informant, visited England as Hawaiian commissioners. Lord Palmerston advised that Britain wanted Hawaiians to maintain proper government and independence; if not, he recommended a U.S. protectorate or becoming part of the United States, citing Hawai‘i’s proximity to California and Oregon, dependence on export/import markets, and the likely extinction and replacement of the native population.

The passage then recounts related events: February 25, 1843, Lord George Paulet obtained cession of the islands to Great Britain, and July 31, 1843, the islands were restored to original sovereignty. November 28, 1843, a joint English-French convention acknowledged Hawaiian independence and promised never to take possession; the United States declined to participate. In August 1849, Admiral Tromelin’s French force took possession of Honolulu’s fort and government buildings and blockaded the harbor, later departing. In January 1851, French forces threatened bombardment; Kamehameha III executed a deed ceding sovereignty forever to the United States, to take effect on the first hostile shot. Afterward, the French departed, and the passage states that French authorities took a conciliatory course thereafter, with an alleged secret U.S.-Hawaii treaty.
