Other reports cover failed and clarified aspects of Dynegy’s attempt to buy Enron, including plans involving the Northern Natural Gas pipeline, and describe Enron’s overseas and regional operations, such as the Teesside power station and the Enron Nordic unit.

Arsène Wenger says his new-look Arsenal squad is set up to be an attacking team, including signings Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Henrikh Mkhitaryan, and Alexandre Lacazette, and a new contract for Mesut Özil. Wenger believes it is possible to fit all players into the starting XI, though he acknowledges Arsenal need to improve their defensive record and find a balance without harming their defensive power. He also explains that keeping Özil was the “cheapest option” compared with buying a comparable replacement and says he avoids “living on credit.” Wenger adds that Lacazette is not guaranteed to start against Everton due to illness earlier in the week and that he will not reassure players because competition for places is part of the job.

Houston’s George R. Brown Convention Center was used as a shelter for people displaced by Hurricane Harvey, and it is compared to the Strategic National Stockpile’s warehouses, which store large quantities of medicines kept secret and sent to affected areas during crises. The stockpile, a $7 billion government repository, includes drugs and supplies for bioterrorism, nuclear attacks, infectious disease outbreaks, and major public health emergencies, such as antibiotics, vaccines, antivirals, and antitoxins. 

The federal government plans to shift oversight of the program from the CDC to a different part of the Department of Health and Human Services, with the ASPR office to choose and purchase products. Supporters say the change will streamline decision-making and improve coordination, while critics and some lawmakers worry it could disrupt delivery to state and local agencies, politicize decisions, and raise concerns about safety and whether the stockpile will focus too heavily on specialized, expensive products. The program was created in 1999, has expanded beyond terrorist threats to natural disasters and outbreaks, and has been used during events such as the swine flu pandemic and hurricanes. Congress has expressed bipartisan unease and urged maintaining a strong, central role for the CDC.

Paula and John Larison appeal a trial court’s grant of summary judgment to Public Water Supply District #1 of Andrew County in their personal injury action. The Larisons argue their claims fall within the “dangerous condition” exception to sovereign immunity and that material fact issues exist regarding negligent acts or omissions by the Water District, including whether the District had actual or constructive knowledge of a dangerous condition. They also appeal dismissal of an alternative res ipsa loquitur claim.

The court reverses summary judgment on the Larisons’ operator-negligence theory, holding that the evidence could support differing conclusions about whether the operator negligently replaced the meter lid. However, the court affirms summary judgment on the claims that the Water District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition, finding the causation theory based on a mower shaking the lid loose to be speculative. The court also affirms summary judgment on the res ipsa loquitur claim, finding the Water District lacked evidence of exclusive control over the meter lid and had no superior knowledge or means of information about the cause of the accident.

The passage describes a population-wide study in Australia investigating whether COVID-19 vaccination is associated with audiovestibular conditions. After COVID-19 vaccine rollout began on 22 February 2021 with multiple vaccine types, researchers used (1) an analysis of spontaneous reports from the SAEFVIC vaccine safety platform and (2) a self-controlled case series (SCCS) analysis using a large general practice dataset from POLAR, focusing on events with onset within 1–42 days after vaccination. Audiovestibular conditions included hearing loss, vertigo, and tinnitus. The study found increased relative incidence of vertigo in the 42 days after mRNA vaccines and increased relative incidence of tinnitus in the 42 days after both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines, while no increased relative incidence of hearing loss was observed after any COVID-19 vaccine. The study concludes that clinicians should be aware of these potential adverse events and counsel people accordingly.

Police charged Edmonton blogger Barry Kent Winters, 62, with wilfully promoting hatred against an identifiable group on June 1, a rare charge under Canada’s Criminal Code. Police say his blogs, the Baconfat Chronicles and the Baconfat News, contained racist and hateful references to many groups and people, including indigenous people, LGBTQ people, feminists, Muslims, fat people, multiple racial groups, and others, as well as rants against public figures. Police also say the blogs repeatedly threatened to post nude pictures of Rehteah Parsons and accused her father of molesting her, and they describe violent fantasies about others’ deaths and forced harm. After years of complaints and a 13-month investigation, police laid the charge with written consent from Alberta’s deputy attorney general Philip Bryden, and courts have already required Winters to take down the blogs as a pre-trial release condition. The passage includes criticism and commentary on whether criminalizing offensive speech is appropriate in a free society.

The lecture explains the Higgs mechanism and how it generates masses for the W and Z gauge bosons and fermions. It starts with the issue that adding a mass term for a spin-one gauge field breaks local gauge invariance. Mass can instead be obtained by breaking symmetry, introduced through spontaneous symmetry breaking using a toy model with a complex scalar field. When the vacuum expectation value moves away from zero, mass terms appear for the gauge field (proportional to the coupling and the vacuum expectation value) and for one real scalar field, while the Goldstone boson becomes massless but can be eliminated by a gauge choice; it is described as “eaten” by the longitudinal polarization of the gauge boson, making the gauge boson massive. The discussion is then generalized to the Standard Model with SU(2)×U(1) gauge groups, where the Higgs field’s vacuum expectation value breaks the symmetry. Coupling the Higgs field to the gauge bosons yields masses for the W and Z bosons (with the photon remaining massless) and relates the W and Z masses via the weak mixing angle. In this framework, three Goldstone bosons are absorbed by the W’s and Z, and an additional physical Higgs scalar remains. The lecture notes that the Higgs boson was discovered in 2012 by the LHC, though the underlying theoretical mechanism was proposed in the mid-1960s.

BCom (Hons) third semester students in Indore were reportedly served Corporate Accounts question papers instead of Corporate Law papers during a Monday exam. Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya authorities changed the papers after complaints, but the exam started about 30 minutes late. The initial paper was scheduled for December 18, and the university said bundles were opened mistakenly and that no leak occurred. Regarding BCom (Hons), the university stated it would remain under the annual system, rejecting colleges’ demands for semester exams, citing no instructions from the DHE and stating the coordination committee’s decision was unchanged.

Gold steadied below $1,250 an ounce on Monday after its biggest weekly drop in more than six months, with prices muted ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting ending Wednesday. Spot gold was $1,247.48 per ounce at 1440 GMT, down 2.5 percent last week, while U.S. gold futures rose to $1,249.70. Analysts said the Fed statement, Yellen’s final press conference, and updates to economic projections would be closely watched for signs about future interest rate hikes. In broader markets, world stocks rose and equity volatility neared a record low, while hedge funds and money managers sharply cut net long positions in COMEX gold and silver; net silver positions fell by 34,915 contracts, the largest amount on record. Silver was down 0.4 percent at $15.77 per ounce, while platinum fell 0.1 percent to $886.40 and palladium fell 0.2 percent to $1,004.10.

Disparities in basic education quality across China are linked to a “siphon” effect, where economically depressed areas lose students and teachers to places with superior educational resources. To counter this and promote balanced development, education groups are formed in major cities, typically centered on a prestigious “core school” working with “ordinary schools” as branch campuses. During cooperation, core schools send administrators and anchor teachers to provide teaching guidance and training, enabling teachers to broaden perspectives and improving access to high-quality resources and overall school quality. Education groups are described as improving resource sharing, management and instructional research coordination, teacher job satisfaction and professional competence, and student development by spreading educational philosophy, encouraging higher-order thinking, enabling broader learning opportunities and extracurricular activities, and strengthening group culture. The text also notes challenges, including potential homogenization of ordinary schools’ culture, difficulties applying core-school philosophy due to differences in teacher and student abilities, and management burdens on core schools. Suggested improvements include establishing equal and democratic relationships through shared decision-making structures, strengthening team building via teacher rotation and training plus technology-supported resource sharing, and securing government policy and financial support to reduce operational pressure. The conclusion frames education groups as contractual deep cooperation intended to support educational equity and requires further study on sustaining motivation and preserving each school’s distinctiveness.

Fire Departments across the state are holding education sessions in October for Fire Prevention month. Buffalo Center Firefighter says the theme is “Every Second counts – know two ways out,” emphasizing awareness of surroundings and finding more than one exit in homes and other buildings. Officials warn that colder weather can lead people to block exits by taping doors, placing rugs in front, or blocking doors with furniture, making escape—possibly from a window—more difficult. During Fire Prevention Week, officials reinforce messages to children about what to do when smoke or fire alarms go off, including going outside, staying outside, and not going back in to look for people or pets. Jim Boehmer encourages a simple step: parents should review safety with their families and rehearse a home fire drill.

Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days is underway, offering Kindle sales that the passage says are the best time to buy a new Kindle without needing to wait for Black Friday. It describes multiple discounted Kindle models, highlighting the Kindle Colorsoft and its Signature edition features (including wireless charging, an auto-adjusting front light, and twice the storage), the Kindle Scribe as an e-reader and digital notebook with long battery life, and the Kindle Paperwhite (noted as an all-around favorite) with options like a warm light, larger screen, ad-free lock screen, wireless charging, and an auto-adjusting front light in the Signature edition. The passage also covers the base Kindle for budget buyers, the Colorsoft Kids version with an included cover and Kids+ content, and the Paperwhite Kids model with a cover and six months of Kids+ content.

John Whitfield, the appellant, applied for a writ of error coram nobis to vacate a March 9, 1992 decision affirming a Kings County Supreme Court judgment. He argued ineffective assistance of appellate counsel. The court denied the application, finding he failed to establish he was denied effective assistance of appellate counsel. Mangano, P. J., Rosenblatt, O’Brien, and Ritter, JJ., concur.

The passage provides an example workflow for negotiating and using the SEV-ES/GHCB and GHCB/VMGEXIT protocols, including how a guest and hypervisor coordinate protocol versioning, GHCB page sharing, and determination of the SEV page-table encryption bit. It also describes handling non-automatic exits (#VC/NAE), required GHCB field validation using VALID_BITMAP, and how the guest invokes VMGEXIT and processes results returned via GHCB. Additional sections cover SEV-SNP-specific mechanisms such as the secrets page, confidential computing blob EFI protocol, guest request/extended guest request for SNP firmware operations, page state change requests, and SNP guest request rate limiting. The passage further outlines Secure AVIC support, termination requests, and what to do for unsupported NAE events, along with guidance for guest identification of SEV-ES support and challenges with SMP/AP booting under SEV. It concludes with a #HV doorbell page mechanism for restricted injection, defining doorbell page fields (PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired) and summarizing host and guest behavior for delivering and acknowledging interrupts via #HV.

Adidas created a limited edition set of UltraBOOST X shoes called “Boost the Nation,” with one custom pair for each of the 50 states. Only one pair of each shoe was made, designed by female artists, and will be auctioned with proceeds benefiting Women Win, an international sports-focused charity for girls. Georgia’s shoe, designed by Lizzie Darden, is peach-themed with a plastic leaf on green shoelaces; other states include symbols such as the Indianapolis 500, cheese, grains of wheat, a fern, and blue topaz. Bids for Georgia’s women’s size 8 pair reached $350, and bidding runs through tomorrow.

The judgment convicting Vu Ngo of three counts of first-degree robbery was unanimously affirmed. The court held that the defendant’s claim of unlawful discrimination in a prosecutor’s peremptory challenge was not preserved for review and declined discretionary review. The court also found the defendant’s detention at the hospital emergency room area was lawful and that related evidence need not be suppressed, concluding the initial police approach and subsequent brief detention did not amount to a forcible detention or seizure. It further found that officers had reasonable suspicion to continue detaining him for a showup identification and questioning.

Britain’s FTSE 100 closed 0.4% higher after a choppy session following the formal triggering of Brexit. The index was supported by sterling’s decline, and it is up more than 16% from pre-Brexit levels and has hit record highs this year. The mid-cap FTMC rose 0.1%. Charles Hanover Investments’ Dafydd Davies said the FTSE 100 is driven by pound weakness and highlighted banks and domestic-focused UK-listed companies as potentially volatile. Shares in 3I Group rose 5.7% after a Morgan Stanley upgrade. EU antitrust regulators blocked a Deutsche Boerse and London Stock Exchange merger, and LSE shares rose 2.7%. Mining firms gained, with copper-related gains from BHP Billiton and Antofagasta; gold-related miners fell. Blue chips aside, AA dropped 3.9% and Acacia Mining fell 3% after a JP Morgan downgrade.

The email is a returned message indicating “User unknown” for <hgovenar@mail.acom2.com>. The delivery system reports permanent fatal errors: “Relaying denied, Momo” and “User unknown.” The original message received from mailman.enron.com contains an email from Jeff Dasovich to multiple recipients about a confidential plan involving Ken Lay’s email to Sen. Brulte, and it includes discussion of proposed California electricity crisis legislative solutions, credit issues related to AB1X and DWR power purchases, and related attachments (including talking points and legislative fix documents).

The passage describes the glymphatic system as the brain’s primary waste clearance system and focuses on perivascular spaces (PVS), which can be visualized on T1-weighted MRI. Prior small studies suggested a link between PVS/glymphatic dysfunction and epilepsy, potentially through reduced clearance of excitotoxic substances. This study investigated enlarged PVS burden across 467 people with epilepsy (temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis, temporal lobe epilepsy without MRI-visible lesions, focal extratemporal epilepsy, and idiopathic generalized epilepsy) and 473 matched healthy controls using 3T MRI and deep-learning segmentation (PINGU). PVS volume fractions in the basal ganglia (BG) were higher in all epilepsy subtypes compared with controls, while no differences were found in white matter (WM). In the temporal lobe, TLE-HS showed asymmetry with larger PVS on the contralateral side. There was no association between PVS volume fractions and duration of illness. The authors conclude that BG PVS volume is enlarged in people with epilepsy and that longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether seizures affect the glymphatic system or whether impaired glymphatic function contributes to epilepsy.

On June 16, 2016, David M. Shannon, NVIDIA’s Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, informed NVIDIA he will retire at the end of the calendar year. NVIDIA stated that Shannon joined in August 2002 and is responsible for NVIDIA’s legal and human resources functions. Upon his retirement, Brian E. Cabrera, NVIDIA’s Senior Vice President and General Counsel, will lead the legal team, and NVIDIA will recruit a leader for the human resources function. The report was signed by Rebecca Peters on June 21, 2016.

The passage describes redundancy management in safety-critical systems and motivates formal verification, then presents a correct-by-construction approach for synthesizing an input selection “voter unit” for synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems in avionics control. The voter selects a prime input unit each cycle, using a noise-resilient voting algorithm that discards transient-error measurements, identifies and isolates permanently faulty units, avoids frequent prime switching, and provides reliability-related output to a controller. It formalizes system input/output formats, defines a fault model with deviation faults and self-identified health status (with transient vs. permanent faults determined by persistence limits), and states hypotheses on simultaneous faults. The work formulates functional requirements for fault identification soundness/completeness (with theoretical limits), isolation rules, output generation (including prime switching, validity status, and output age bounds), and implements and verifies the state-transition design using the Rocq interactive theorem prover. The synthesized code is extracted to OCaml/Haskell/Scheme, with reported verification and execution times. Future directions include extending the approach to hierarchical redundancy management and asynchronous fault-tolerant systems.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolution, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN). He said his decision followed marathon meetings and consultations and that ANN had been adopted by the Nigerian Intervention Movement (NIM) on 29 May 2018. A press statement from Ayobami Ogedengbe said Ikubese joined ANN on 29 May 2018 and would run for president in the 2019 election under the party, urging other young aspirants to join the NIM arrangement. The statement also said Ikubese left the National Conscience Party (NCP) on 14 May after accusing its leadership of over-taxation, described ANN as a new dawn and the third force, and urged supporters to register, pay dues, and be active.

Doctors said most eye cancer cases in the country are detected at late stages, making treatment complex and potentially leading to blindness or death. Ocular oncology expert Bikramjit Pal emphasized spreading awareness of eye cancer types and symptoms to support prevention, early detection, and treatment, noting that cancer from other organs can spread to the eye. He added that specialized facilities and trained ocular oncologists are scarce, with one institute in eastern India and none in western and central India, and only about 10–11 trained ocular oncologists in India. Pal also discussed retinoblastoma in young children, describing symptoms such as a squint or a white appearance in the pupil, and said early detection can save the child and eyesight.

The passage describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide, which explains the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine and how it supports page migration by copying page contents and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. It states TMPM is optional for SEV/SNP extensions, requires IOMMU enablement, and can off-load migration, pause DMA, and migrate Guest pages protected by AMD secure virtualization features. It outlines the purposes and workflows of key commands (including concurrent DMA for PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, SNP hypervisor migration via PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST/PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, and a Pre-Migration state for SNP guests), multi-page command behavior (up to 128 pages per command) with per-page statuses, and performance/testing guidance. The document also lists non-migratable data structures, restrictions on page alignment and acceptable addresses, guidance for ring buffer and driver initialization, mailbox/register interfaces, interrupt sources, firmware reload procedure, SPA encoding for encryption (SMEE/SME-MK), and error handling and statuses for migration operations.

The passage outlines different forms of education—formal, non-formal, and informal/random—and explains how learning processes differ by environment, medium, and methodology. It describes how digitalization and the internet enable online and distance education, including synchronous and asynchronous instruction, supporting personalized, accessible learning through tools such as computers, applications, websites, and artificial intelligence. It focuses on design education, noting that studio-based, teacher-student interaction and digital tools support creativity, rapid iteration, and parametric/computational design skills. The study described analyzes online informal education in design through examples of synchronous online workshop and course programs in computational design, assessing their aims, methods, resources, duration, and participation. Findings discuss learning advantages such as hands-on practice, discussion environments, and accelerated acquisition of software/tools, while also identifying limitations including unequal access, restricted maximum participation, and challenges for integration into formal education. The conclusion states that online informal education increases personalization and access but may also intensify competitiveness and raise inclusiveness issues, partly because informal education certificates are not included in compulsory education transcripts.

The passage discusses Thailand’s “expanded education opportunity” schools and the need to integrate environmental education into teaching and learning, especially in junior high schools serving youth in remote areas. It outlines goals related to inclusive, equitable education under SDG 4 and connects environmental education to developing awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, evaluation ability, and participation. The study develops and evaluates an integrated environmental education model based on the theory of multiple intelligences, using questionnaires, interviews, observation, and SWOT analysis with students, teachers, and school directors in Nakhon Pathom Primary Education Area 2. Findings report community pollution issues linked to agriculture, wastewater, air contamination, and garbage, along with students’ comparatively lowest level in environmental awareness. The integrated model’s effectiveness is reported as meeting set criteria (process/result efficiency 81.51/82.11), with post-learning achievement scores higher than pre-learning and high student satisfaction.

The passage says solar energy has become the cheapest worldwide power source, aided by falling battery prices and advances in solar materials. It cites a University of Surrey study stating solar photovoltaic technology outcompetes fossil fuels and wind, with costs as low as £0.02 per unit in sunniest countries. The research reports lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems as cost-effective as gas plants and more reliable for balancing grid demand. Key challenges include grid congestion and integrating large amounts of solar into existing networks, with the authors emphasizing smart grids, forecasting, regional links, and sustained long-term policy support. It also mentions perovskite solar cells could boost output by up to 50% and cites policy examples including the Inflation Reduction Act, REPowerEU, and India’s Production Linked Incentive scheme.

The passage criticizes “Eastern” religious teachings as corrupt, describing them as rebellion against heaven and mockery, and argues that the true doctrine supports universal good government tied to the ruler. It warns religious followers to abandon their texts and promote proper principles, with threats of burning books and attacking dissenters. It also includes an anonymous notice (dated 1893) accusing religious leaders and church-related activities of hypocrisy, exploitation, and immoral behavior, urging crowds to leave quickly or face violence. Finally, it reports that followers of Confucius in Seoul submitted a memorial to the king accusing the “Tong Hâk” of false doctrines and asking that they be compelled to return to the right path or be exterminated; the king said the government would handle the matter and advised petitioners to study their own professed principles.

A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and a voltage reference (VREF). When VIN is less than VREF, the output is low; it switches from low to high when VIN rises above the VIN1 threshold (calculated using Equation 4). When VIN is greater than VREF, the output is high; it switches back to low when VIN drops below the VIN2 threshold (calculated using Equation 5). The hysteresis equals the difference between VIN1 and VIN2 (Equation 6). Further information is referenced in Application Note SNOA997.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 26, 2015 to report results of operations and financial condition. The report states that on January 26, 2015 Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014, and that a copy of the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes a statement that the information in the report and Exhibit 99.1 is not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act or subject to liability under that section, and is not incorporated by reference into other filings except as expressly set forth. The report lists Exhibit 99.1 as the press release dated January 26, 2015 and is signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage describes a “bull market signal” timing strategy that uses the S&P 500 closing above its 200-day SMA for 18 consecutive days during a bear market. The stated trading rules are to sell the S&P 500 when it falls 20% below its all-time high and trigger a buy when the S&P 500 closes above the 200-day moving average for 18 consecutive days. A backtest on the S&P 500 from 1927 to the present generated 12 signals and, according to the passage, produced a CAGR of 7.24%, standard deviation of 15.26, Sharpe ratio of 0.24, and maximum drawdown of 60%, with 87.38% time spent in the market. The passage compares the strategy to the “golden cross,” noting that the bull signal generated 12 signals versus 49 for the golden cross and claims the bull signal performs better in overall results, while not outperforming on a risk-adjusted basis. It also reports average forward returns after the signal: up 9.54% six months later and 21.84% one year later, with the S&P 500 up 100% of the time 12 months after the signal.

St. George welcomed a delegation from Ibigawa, Japan, as part of an ongoing sister-city cultural exchange. Eleven Japanese visitors arrived three days before the 41st annual St. George Marathon, including four runners competing Saturday. The delegation was received at a reception by Mayor Jon Pike and other local officials, recognized at the St. George City Council meeting, and hosted at an international luncheon at the Dixie Center St. George on Friday where ceremonial gifts were exchanged with Ibigawa Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji. Runners include Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita, plus two additional runners from Ibigawa. Mayor Pike said St. George will send a delegation to Japan next month for the 30th annual Ibigawa Marathon, and the visitors’ five-day itinerary includes local sites and ends with departure from Las Vegas Monday.

Commuters in Delhi-NCR may face difficulty hiring taxis on Tuesday as drivers with two app-based cab aggregators, Ola and Uber, threatened to stop operations for a day over low fares. Ola and Uber previously saw a 13-day strike in February that inconvenienced commuters. On Monday, the Delhi High Court restrained two taxi-driver unions from disrupting Ola and Uber services in the NCR and permanently injuncted the unions and related parties from blocking cabs. The Sarvodaya Drivers’ Association, which claims to represent about 1.25 lakh app-based taxis, says the strike could affect private transport and says it wants fares raised from Rs 6 per km to around Rs 20 per km and seeks abolition of the 25% commission drivers pay to companies. The association plans a protest march against the Delhi government and has called a one-day strike, with an indefinite strike if its demands are not addressed. The Delhi Autorickshaw Sangh and the Delhi Pradesh Taxi Union said they will not support the strike.

Rain Bird’s 9V WPX battery-operated irrigation controller is designed for situations where standard mains-powered controllers cannot be used due to unavailable power or costly cable runs. It is IP68 compliant, fully submersible, and 100% water and dust proof, with a waterproof case suitable for installation in a valve box and use in wet or muddy conditions. The controller is available for 1, 2, 4, or 6 zones, supports multiple run times and common programming functions via an LCD screen, and offers Contractor Rapid Programming™ to copy start times and watering days from the first zone to others. Automatic zone-stacking ensures only one valve irrigates at a time, and it can run for about one year on a single 9V battery or up to two years with two.

The passage describes a hockey goal during a line change near the team’s own blueline. Matt made a strong play to Teemu, who fed the puck to the speaker while the speaker was centered on the ice. The speaker drove the net, received a pass on their tape, and scored into an open net. The goal occurred at the end of the opposing team’s shift, with Getzlaf and Perry on the ice next. The speaker says it followed a set play, that it was not especially emotional, and that the team stayed disciplined in the third period, ultimately winning by scoring to finish the game.

The passage describes several SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication mechanisms and related interrupt and CPU control behaviors. It explains how guests can request VMPL level changes via a hypervisor-run vCPU event using per-VMPL VMSA (and optional GHCB), with errors returned when a requested VMPL lacks a VMSA. It also covers SEV-TIO support, including guest setup steps, how TIO guest requests use encrypted, unencrypted guest-supplied data pages to provide nonces, measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports, and how the hypervisor validates and returns required page counts.

The passage further details Secure AVIC, including backing page requirements in nested paging tables and guest actions to register or unregister per-vCPU APIC backing pages, and then describes a termination request NAE event with termination reason codes and feature masks returned in SW_EXITINFO2. It discusses handling unsupported non-automatic exits, guest identification of SEV-ES via CPUID properties, and challenges in SMP/AP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, including approaches using reset vectors, an AP jump table, and hypervisor requirements; it also introduces an SEV-SNP AP creation feature allowing vCPU state creation/updates via VMGEXIT without requiring the AP Reset Hold NAE event.

Finally, it outlines non-maskable interrupt handling requirements, full virtualization or intercept behavior for debug registers, states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported, and defines a “#HV doorbell page” mechanism for host notifications with fields such as PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired, along with specified host and guest behaviors for interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, and end-of-interrupt handling.

Kuwait plans to finish cleaning up a crude oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, according to Oil Minister Essam al-Marzouq, who said no additional oil patches were found and that cleanup was continuing near the shore. The spill’s cause was not provided, and earlier Kuwait statements said services were investigating without giving the spill’s magnitude. The Khajfi Joint Operations stated its facilities were safe, attributed the spill to reports of an oil tanker, and said it activated an emergency plan and would conduct an aerial survey to confirm the safety of facilities and beaches.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Constitution Bench held that re-promulgation of ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. It ruled that presidential satisfaction under Article 123 and governor satisfaction under Article 213 when issuing ordinances are subject to judicial review, including scrutiny for fraud on power or oblique motives. The Bench also held that whether rights survive after an ordinance ceases must be determined by construction, that placing an ordinance before the legislature is mandatory, and that the ordinance has the same force as a legislative law but must be laid and will cease to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles (or earlier if disapproved). It found failure to lay the ordinance before the legislature to be a serious constitutional infraction and said salaries already paid to teachers should not be recovered.

The passage describes an augmented reality system for image-guided surgery, focusing on tracking a patient’s body and a surgical tool using head-mounted devices and markers. It explains that misalignment between virtual images and the patient must typically be within about 2–3 mm and that tracking is used to maintain alignment, including tracking with a single camera and patient/tool markers without requiring triangulation. It also describes using an additional tracking device or a second head-mounted device when line of sight is blocked or tracking devices lose sight of the markers, including logic for when to rely on first versus additional tracking data. The passage includes methods and apparatus for generating augmented reality images that overlay virtual tool and anatomy on the patient, and discusses example display behaviors when line of sight is blocked.

Investors previously dismissed geopolitical and economic risks and focused on economic strength, helped by high corporate profits and President Trump’s tax and deregulation agenda, which extended the stock boom to its ninth year. Recently, stocks fell by more than 2% and had their worst week in two years, with the jobs report raising concerns about rising wages and potential higher inflation. Investors are also concerned that cheap money from global central banks may end sooner, leading to higher Treasury yields and weaker performance in the market. The passage notes that low global interest rates and central bank actions since 2009 supported the stock rise by encouraging investors to move cash from safe government bonds into stocks and bonds to spur company investment and hiring.

The passage argues that while market corrections can be frightening, most do not escalate into bear markets: fewer than one in five corrections become bear markets, and 80% do not. It suggests that panic and moving to cash during a correction may happen before rebounds. Corrections are described as routine since 1900, occurring about once a year on average, with an average decline of 13.5% lasting 54 days. It contrasts corrections with bear markets, noting bear markets have historically lasted about a year on average, with the S&P 500 averaging a 33% drop during bear markets. The passage emphasizes that bear markets end and that markets have risen over the long run despite major events. It also states that individuals should take responsibility for investment outcomes, citing the idea that the stock market transfers money from impatient to patient.

The TPS7H500x-SP controller series includes either one primary switching output (OUTA) or two primary outputs (OUTA and OUTB), with external gate drive recommended due to ~150 mA peak output capability. OUTA provides main switch gate control for buck and single-ended isolated applications, while OUTA and OUTB provide control signals for push-pull and full-bridge topologies; OUTB is active only when duty cycle limit is set to 50% by connecting DCL to AVSS (valid for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP). The series also offers synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA, and optionally SRB), with SR outputs off during soft-start and switching starting after SS exceeds 1 V; SRB is only present in TPS7H5001-SP and also requires the 50% DCL setting. Dead time and leading edge blank time can be programmed (with TPS7H5003-SP fixed dead time), using external resistors to set timing values, and pulse skipping is used to handle minimum on-time constraints. Duty cycle limiting is configured via DCL (including support for 75% or 50% maximum), and current sensing/PWM generation uses the CS_ILIM and COMP signals, including a current sense threshold and an overcurrent hiccup mode. The FAULT pin supports external fault protection with a pulse-width condition, followed by a frequency-dependent delay and restart behavior. The controller includes slope compensation to mitigate subharmonic oscillation, supports internal fixed-frequency peak current mode control, provides thermal shutdown (stop switching above a typical 175°C and restart below 160°C), and includes layout and application guidance for designing specific converters and selecting components.

The passage argues for coherent legislative reform based on moderate, common-sense action against major evils in the present system. It says reactionaries and violent extremists share claims about issues like government ownership of railroads, but the author’s position is different: the government should supervise rather than run the nation’s business, aiming for equality of opportunity and burden for hard-working men. It contends that prohibiting all combination (capital or labor) is harmful where it is not ineffective, and instead calls for rigorous control and supervision to prevent combinations from injuring the public, giving examples involving railroad agreements and rebates. It criticizes laws that cannot be fully enforced and discusses commentary by the Interstate Commerce Commission. The passage then discusses taxation under a federal system, advocating some local taxes, certain state taxes on franchises, and national taxes such as a tariff and internal/excise taxes, along with a proposal for graduated inheritance and income taxes, emphasizing justice and moderation in distributing the government’s tax burden.

The passage discusses a study by Jonathan Rolland and colleagues published in *Nature Ecology & Evolution*, which found that mammals and birds adapt faster and are better equipped to handle temperature changes than reptiles and amphibians. Using data covering nearly 11,500 species and fossil records over 270 million years, the researchers reconstructed historical temperature fluctuations and environmental habitats. The passage explains that traits such as regulating body temperature and using body heat for offspring support quicker adaptation and higher survival during temperature changes. It notes, however, that climate change is occurring rapidly, and it is unclear whether these evolutionary traits will be sufficient. The passage also states that current extinction pressures include pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species, with species disappearing far faster than normal and many mammals and birds threatened with extinction. Rolland is hopeful the research will help connect long-term evolutionary patterns with present-day evolutionary change to better understand adaptation to climate change.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018. The report includes condensed consolidated financial statements showing net sales of $61,137 million for the three months ended March 31, 2018 and $149,430 million for six months ended March 31, 2018, with net income of $13,822 million and $33,887 million, respectively. It provides unaudited balance sheet information (total assets of $367,502 million as of March 31, 2018) and cash flow information for six months ended March 31, 2018, including $43,423 million of cash generated from operating activities. Notes describe significant accounting policies and items such as share-based compensation (including adoption of ASU 2016-09), financial instruments and derivatives, income taxes (including effects of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act), debt and share repurchase programs, comprehensive income, and segment reporting by Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific, along with forward-looking statement language and discussion of business operations and results.

Two teens were arrested and another remains on the run after a police pursuit in Frankston early this morning. Road workers were forced to move as a car sped through road works around 12.20am and Peninsula Link staff alerted police. Somerville Highway Patrol members spotted a black Subaru with stolen number plates, pursued it, and the car was later dumped in a car park on Elizabeth St, Bayswater, where the three people fled on foot. A 17-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man, both from Mill Park, were arrested shortly after, and the man was taken to hospital after being bitten by a police dog. The third person is still being sought, and both teens are assisting police with inquiries.

The passage contains multiple news items dated May 18, 2001. One Dow Jones column says California risks losing over 40% of power tied to $12.5 billion in long-term bond contracts rejected by state Republicans, while forward power prices in the western U.S. have fallen and some generators may face reduced profits. It notes conservation and slower demand as drivers of lower forward prices and reports that the state bought some summer power at reduced prices, with no blackouts that week.

A Dow Jones options report says options volatility fell further and that many investors continued selling options to generate income upfront, focusing on out-of-the-money calls and puts in stocks including Ericsson and Microsoft, while some investors considered selling options risky due to potential downside moves.

Several pieces report Saudi Arabia’s selection of international oil companies for three major natural gas “Core Ventures” totaling about $25 billion. Shell says it is pleased to participate in Core Venture 1 and Core Venture 3, while the U.S. Energy Department says it welcomed American firms’ roles. Saudi Arabia is expected to announce leaders for Core Ventures 1 and 3 by June 5, with memoranda of understanding to be signed in early June, and the initial selection includes Exxon leading Core Venture 2 on the Red Sea coast.

The passage describes the rise and collapse of FTX and the people involved. Nishad Singh ran a 100-mile charity marathon at age 16 and later worked at Alameda Research, which was founded by Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) and Tara Mac Aulay, and led by Caroline Ellison. Singh later also led engineering at FTX, the crypto exchange founded by SBF and Gary Wang. By early 2022, FTX had grown to be the second-largest crypto exchange globally, with large revenue, trading volume, and millions of customer accounts. In November 2022, FTX filed for bankruptcy; the U.S. Department of Justice charged SBF with multiple fraud, money laundering, and campaign finance offenses, and he was arrested. Singh was later charged and pled guilty to conspiracy-related offenses, admitting actions including writing code that enabled SBF to divert FTX customer funds to Alameda, making illegal political contributions using Alameda money, and inflating FTX’s 2021 revenues. The passage also outlines the structure and business of crypto exchanges (including spot trading, derivatives, leverage, and the role of exchange tokens like FTT), and discusses differing global regulation, with the SEC viewing many crypto assets as securities and the CFTC viewing items like Bitcoin as commodities. It then explains how FTX’s decline accelerated after Alameda’s balance sheet was leaked, showing a large portion of assets tied to FTT and concerns about liquidity and valuation; this coincided with a major FTT price drop, a customer run, and withdrawal pauses. The passage further describes alleged undisclosed connections between FTX and Alameda, including Alameda’s line of credit funded by customer assets and coding changes that allowed Alameda to fall below required margin levels. It concludes with questions posed in the aftermath about who was responsible, including investors, auditors, regulators, and customers, and notes civil charges by the SEC and CFTC alongside criminal charges.

Penn State officials said the Penn State Outing Club, founded in 1920, will be barred from organizing student-led outdoor trips starting next semester because the activities are considered too risky after a two-month risk review. The decision followed findings from Student Affairs and Risk Management that the club’s hiking, camping, and similar trips are high risk due to remote locations, poor cell service, and distance from emergency services. Penn State also directed other outdoor clubs, including the Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Nittany Divers SCUBA Club, to end trip offerings. Club leaders criticized the decision process for not consulting students, while the university said safety is its primary focus and that a university-operated outdoors program will still be offered, with staff meeting student leaders about the transition and support.

Android 8.0 Oreo was released in August and includes under-the-hood refinements such as Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, Notification Dots, Smart Text Selection, Notification Snoozing, and an Autofill Framework. PiP Mode enhances multitasking by allowing video playback in a floating window when users press back or home, implemented at the OS level beyond the YouTube app. The passage notes PiP support must be enabled by app developers, and lists supported apps including Google Chrome, Google Duo, Google Play Movies & TV, Google Play Services, Google Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC. For YouTube, PiP requires a YouTube Red subscription, which is unavailable in some countries. The article explains how to use PiP in Android Oreo by playing YouTube in Google Chrome desktop mode, then using full-screen and the home button to resize the video into a floating window that can be moved and dismissed. It also provides steps to enable PiP in settings if the feature is not working.

The passage summarizes a Texas Supreme Court decision in *Thomas Henderson v. Alex. Beaton et als.* (Case No. 838) involving an action of trespass to try title and partition of an undivided one-half interest in a league of land in Navarro County. The plaintiff, Thomas Henderson, claimed title through a chain starting with a Texas government grant to Mastín Latham and a written instrument from Latham to William F. Henderson. The defendants argued that this instrument was only an executory contract, and raised defenses including stale demand and statutes of limitations (three, five, and ten years), along with allegations of repudiation, abandonment, and failure to perform “clearing out”/location/survey/payment obligations.  

The court held the Latham-to-William F. Henderson instrument was a valid, absolute, unconditional deed rather than an executory contract, and further treated the partition/provision clause as not creating a condition that could defeat the estate. As a result, the court concluded defenses based on stale demand were inapplicable. The court also rejected limitations defenses, citing (among other points) constitutional rules affecting computation for ten years, lack of evidence of tax payments for the five-year plea, and deficiencies in the defendant’s claim of adverse possession “under title or color of title,” including that the defendant’s reliance on possession and later chain of title did not support the three-year and ten-year bars. The decision reversed the district court judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings.

The passage states that gifts to the Annual Fund support efforts to protect the rule of law, strengthen independent courts and legal institutions, uphold fairness, and protect rights at home and abroad. It also says the support helps advance representation in the legal system by eliminating bias and expanding access to justice. Donors are thanked with a sticker and magnet set, and the passage includes a 2015 copyright notice.

The passage is a message to the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives explaining that the suspension of the embargo laws was used to pressure European belligerents to revoke decrees viewed as violating neutral rights. Ministers in London and Paris were instructed to pursue a change that would remove the pretext for aggressions and restore U.S. commercial relations, but the arrangement—especially with Great Britain—was rejected, and no indication of changes was received from France. The speaker states that, since no further events authorized continued suspension, the embargo remains as originally set, but that it has saved mariners and mercantile property and provided time for defensive measures. The message also reports no new material changes in relations with Europe, notes continued harmony with the Barbary powers with a specific issue involving Algiers, and describes maintained peace with Indian neighbors, including legal proceedings and growing integration of some tribes. It further discusses harbor defenses, construction of gun-boats, recruitment under military legislation, militia readiness, efforts to increase arms production internally, impacts of halted foreign commerce on domestic manufacturing, and financial receipts and debt repayment, concluding with remarks on future congressional decisions and the speaker’s gratitude and outlook.

Ukraine has partnered with Bitfury Group to place a broad range of government electronic data on a blockchain platform, a project described by Bitfury CEO Valery Vavilov as likely the largest of its kind. Bitfury will provide the services under a memorandum of understanding signed with Ukraine. Vavilov said the cost cannot be estimated but called it the biggest government blockchain deal to date, starting with a pilot for Ukraine’s digital platform. The pilot will explore state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy, with launch expected late this year, followed by expansion into all areas including cyber security. Ukraine’s eGovernance agency aims to make Ukraine a leading blockchain nation. The passage also notes other countries with smaller blockchain programs, including Sweden, Estonia, and Georgia, and that Bitfury previously helped Georgia pilot a land-titling blockchain registry.

The passage outlines five major themes for investors and traders next week: (1) “Super Thursday” in the UK, with Bank of England interest-rate decision, minutes, and quarterly Inflation Report focused on inflation and growth outlook, alongside recent sterling and bond-yield moves; (2) Australia and New Zealand central bank meetings and upcoming China data, including expected slowing inflation and attention to China–U.S. trade surplus; (3) U.S. trade deficit expectations to widen with record imports despite a weak dollar, plus market focus on U.S. retail sales and potential disruption from a looming government shutdown; (4) a gap in earnings growth expectations between European and U.S. equities amid upcoming company results and recent European weakness; and (5) rate-setting meetings across emerging markets, including possible Russian rate cuts, expected Mexico rate hikes, potential Romania hikes, and expectations for the Reserve Bank of India to hold rates while considering inflation risks.

Joseph McGreal, a police officer for the Village of Orland Park, sued after being fired on June 28, 2010, alleging First Amendment retaliation for speech at a November 2, 2009 community board meeting and a state-law intentional infliction of emotional distress claim. The district court granted summary judgment for the defendants, and McGreal appealed.

The Seventh Circuit affirmed, concluding McGreal failed to provide admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his alleged protected speech or that it motivated his termination. The court also found he provided no admissible evidence that the defendants’ non-retaliatory explanations—such as alleged lying under oath, misconduct, and reckless conduct—were pretextual. The court further held that McGreal offered no evidence that the defendants’ conduct was “extreme and outrageous” or that it caused severe emotional distress.

The passage describes HoopTactics out-of-bounds plays, stating they have been proven over time to produce high-percentage shots with two to three options. If a high-percentage shot isn’t available, the plays flow into predetermined continuities to avoid rushed shots and the need to back the ball out for a set play. It covers baseline, sideline, and full-court out-of-bounds situations, noting that full-court scoring in under four seconds is unlikely but teams must be prepared. It also advises keeping the play simple by using the best player first, then the height and best shooter, and substituting to have the best inbounder and shooters available. Additional guidance includes scouting the defense type and, when possible, advancing to the front court to take a time out, with preference for having the ball at midcourt with three seconds remaining.

Kyle Freeland pitched effectively into the sixth inning and doubled as the Rockies beat the San Francisco Giants 11-4 at Coors Field. Colorado’s three-run fourth and four-run seventh featured hits from David Dahl (including his first career pinch-hit homer), Trevor Story (run-scoring triple), and RBIs from multiple players. Evan Longoria hit two home runs for the Giants, while Kyle Freeland allowed three runs on eight hits. Giants starter Jeff Samardzija left after one inning due to tightness in his pitching shoulder, and rookie Dereck Rodriguez replaced him but was removed after being hit by a line drive. The passage also notes that two Giants players were injured, provides updates on Madison Bumgarner’s rehab schedule and Dahl’s shin injury, and lists upcoming pitching matchups for the next games.

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old high school senior in Georgia, has spent years seeking a kidney match for her sick grandfather, Sam Senseney, who has been on dialysis three days a week for several years. After her family and others were tested and no match was found, Maddie raised awareness for organ donation and donated $7,500 to the American Kidney Fund. The day after her 18th birthday, she learned she was a match, though doctors initially said she was too young. Maddie convinced doctors to let her donate, and she will meet with doctors next week to set a surgery date hoped to be within a month. She expects her grandfather to regain energy and life after losing dialysis, and plans to spend three weeks out of school to complete the process.

The passage describes 5G system embodiments related to 5G core network and network slicing, particularly AMF selection for isolated network slices. It provides a glossary of relevant terms and explains how 5G system functions such as AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NEF, NRF, UDM/UDR, NSSF, AUSF, and N3IWF operate and interact across control and user planes. It outlines registration and connection management states for UE, UE reachability management, PDU session establishment, and a QoS flow model using QFI. It also describes edge computing support and definitions related to NSSAI, S-NSSAI, Allowed/Configured NSSAI, and slice selection policy. The passage further presents mechanisms and call flows for selecting an AMF based on network slice isolation information, including fully isolated slices and partly isolated slices where (R)AN and/or AMF may be shared across slice instances, with NRF/NSSF/UDM involved in selecting appropriate AMFs during registration.

Astronomers using the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope studied the rogue planet SIMP-0136 and found strong auroral activity, storms suggested by temperature-linked chemical changes, and sand-like silicate clouds with constant cloud coverage. The team measured minute brightness changes as the planet rotated to track temperature, cloud cover, and chemistry, recording temperature variations smaller than 5 °C. The research is described as the most precise atmosphere measurements of any extra-solar object to date, including the first direct measurements of changes in atmospheric properties, and it includes analysis that inferred atmospheric temperature, chemical composition, and cloud positions using different light wavelengths. Future observations with the Extremely Large Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory are expected to expand studies of atmospheric dynamics beyond isolated brown dwarfs.

The case concerns an action by an assignee of a subsequent creditor to set aside a deed of gift made by Louis Helbing to his wife, Louise. Helbing executed deeds in May 1893 conveying San Francisco property to his wife, but the deeds were recorded on December 11, 1895. Before recordation, between September and December 1895, Helbing obtained credit from W. W. Montague & Co. for plumbing goods based on his apparent ownership. After the deeds, Helbing exercised acts of ownership, including insuring the Waller street property in his own name and making a proof of loss for a fire. The wife testified she helped pay Helbing’s debts and did not record the deeds because she did not know they had to be recorded until shortly before recordation; she was not shown to know her husband represented the property as his own or that he acted as owner.

The trial court found the B street property was not conveyed to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors, that Helbing was solvent when the deed was made, and that Louise had no connection with any fraudulent intent. It held the plaintiff failed to prove fraudulent intent by Helbing, noting the late recordation (more than two years after execution) was suspicious but not sufficient by itself.

The appellant also challenged exclusion of testimony related to concealment and a sworn claim about goods, but the court found these events occurred nearly four years after the deed and had no connection to its execution; any error was not significant enough to reverse. The judgment and denial of a new trial were affirmed.

Tropical Storm Nate, the 15th Atlantic system this season, is moving toward Mexico’s Yucatan Peninsula and is expected to reach the U.S. Gulf Coast early Sunday, likely as a hurricane. Louisiana officials declared a state of emergency late Thursday, ordered evacuations of coastal areas and barrier islands, mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops, and urged residents to prepare for rainfall, storm surge, and severe winds by Saturday night. Nate has killed 22 people in Latin America and brought 6 to 10 inches of rain over Honduras, with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph by Friday morning and likely strengthening in the northwestern Caribbean. Across Nicaragua and Costa Rica, officials reported deaths, missing people, flooding, and emergency shelters. The article also notes this year’s hurricane season has already produced 15 tropical cyclones and that September was the most active month on record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy, exceeding past records.

The passage discusses a backtest of a pair trading strategy using SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (long-term Treasuries) after major, opposite moves on June 18, 2021. The strategy is described as going long SPY and short TLT on the same day when each ETF moves more than a specified “normal” threshold (including a rule example using 1.25 times a 50-day average of the high-minus-low). Tests including holding the pair overnight and varying holding period and movement criteria are reported to produce erratic and inconsistent results, leading to the conclusion that the strategy is not tradeable. The passage also notes that changing parameters did not meaningfully improve outcomes.

OpenAI is preparing to launch a stand-alone social app for its AI video generation model. The app features a vertical, TikTok-like feed with swipe-to-scroll navigation and a For You–style recommendation page powered by an algorithm. Users can like, comment, or remix videos via a menu bar on the right side. The app is powered by Sora 2.

The passage describes the “Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10),” based on a 2013 Berkshire Hathaway letter. It recommends investing 90% of funds in low-cost, passively managed S&P 500 index ETFs and 10% in government bonds to seek long-term growth with reduced risk and lower fees versus actively managed portfolios. It explains that the S&P 500 tracks 500 large U.S. companies and that the bond portion is meant to cushion market volatility. The strategy emphasizes passive investing, long-term focus, and avoiding high fees and overactive trading. It discusses potential risks and tax implications, notes that past performance is not indicative of future results, and includes backtests comparing 90/10 mixes of SPY with SHY, IEI, and TLT; the results suggest portfolios with longer-duration bonds (e.g., TLT) performed better than other bond choices and sometimes close to SPY, with underperformance attributed to bond market conditions in 2022.

Bank of England research says a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could make monetary policy changes more effective by acting as a close substitute for bank deposits, strengthening transmission to the real economy. The Bank says it is not currently planning to issue a digital currency, but has studied how a CBDC could be designed to avoid vulnerability to bank runs. The research argues that interest-bearing CBDC balances and payment services could give the Bank greater control over monetary policy by increasing the strength and speed of pass-through to other interest rates. It also says a CBDC could improve quantitative easing by allowing the central bank to pay for assets from non-banks directly with CBDC, bypassing the banking sector.

Length of stay (LOS) is described as the time in days between hospital admission and discharge. The passage notes that delayed discharge definitions vary internationally, and that average inpatient LOS increased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic in the context provided. It discusses subacute Complex Discharge Units (CDU) as intermediate care that uses person-centred planning to improve functional outcomes and reduce LOS, and outlines delayed transfers of care (DTOC) as involving delays such as waiting for discharge home, community care, or placement in long-term residential places. The passage states that there is limited data on discharge delays from subacute CDUs for patients with complex ongoing needs, including multimorbidity (MM), frailty, cognitive impairment, and patient-centred needs.

A retrospective, cross-sectional study at St James’s Hospital in Dublin analyzed adult CDU patients with hospital LOS >15 days admitted between March 2020 and February 2021. Data were extracted from electronic patient records, and statistical analyses included Kaplan–Meier and (stratified) Cox regression with delayed discharge as the outcome. Among 390 CDU admissions, the median CDU LOS was 19.4 days, and the most common primary diagnosis was infection or sepsis. The analysis identified five major factors associated with delays in discharge: complications related to primary diagnoses or MM, healthcare-associated infections (HCAI), frailty/falls requiring integrated rehabilitation, patient-centred needs, and community services. Patient-centred needs were described as a significant contributing factor to prolonged LOS >15 days, while community services were not. The conclusion emphasizes that complexities from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs were common factors delaying discharge and suggests the findings may support medical decisions and future contingency planning.

The case involved Lawrence B. Schaub, who was charged with child abandonment after allegedly transferring possession of his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for financial gain. A district court dismissed the charge, finding the prosecution failed to prove the elements of child abandonment, including that the child was exposed without care. The prosecution appealed; the circuit court reversed and reinstated the charge, finding sufficient evidence to bind the case over for trial. The Court of Appeals ultimately agreed with Schaub, reversed the circuit court, and remanded for further proceedings.

In its analysis, the Court of Appeals stated that the elements of child abandonment include exposing the child and the intent to wholly abandon the child. It found sufficient evidence of intent to wholly abandon but concluded the evidence did not establish exposure because the testimony indicated the child was handed over to a person to care for her, leaving no basis to find the child would be left without care or at risk from abandonment as required by the statute’s interpretation. The decision was reversed and remanded. O’Connell, P.J., dissented, arguing the “exposure” element should be treated as a jury question and that delivering an infant to a total stranger with intent to abandon puts the child at risk.

Official reports from U.S. consuls in Cuba state that many American citizens are destitute, especially in rural areas of central and eastern parts, lacking food and medicines. Agricultural workers have been forced from farms into towns with no work or money, and local authorities cannot help. Consul-General Lee estimates 600–800 Americans have no support and the author says provisions will be made. The author recommends Congress appropriate at least $50,000 for immediate relief under the Secretary of State’s direction, and that part of the funds may also be used to transport Americans who want to return to the United States but lack means.

The editor acknowledges assistance from personnel at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and the Library of Congress, special access to the Haig Papers, and support from the Central Intelligence Agency for accessing Reagan Library materials for the Remote Archives Capture project. Additional thanks are given to individuals who recommended documents, coordinated declassification review, and managed copy, technical, and editorial work under specific supervisors, with research and document selection conducted under The Historian Adam M. Howard and reviewed by General Editor Kathleen B. Rasmussen. The volume’s documentation draws largely on public sources such as presidential papers, Department of State Bulletin, and Congressional materials, as well as Reagan Library records, especially White House Office of Speechwriting files and Reagan Transition Papers. It also uses classified sources from Reagan Library White House records and the Department of State, including Presidential Papers, White House staff files, Shultz’s donated papers, and specific State Department lot files and microfilm collections, with these eventually to be incorporated into Record Group 59 at the National Archives in College Park, Maryland.

Walmart says it plans to bring drone deliveries to “most areas that we operate in,” moving beyond small-scale tests. Walmart has been testing drones for more than five years and says the regulatory environment makes drone delivery viable. Drone delivery is currently available at a limited number of U.S. locations through partnerships, including Alphabet’s Wing, which Walmart is expanding. Walmart also says it has surpassed 300,000 drone deliveries and calls drone delivery “a key part” of its last-mile strategy. The passage notes widespread drone delivery is still likely years away due to technical, regulatory, and financial issues.

Richard A. Milan, proceeding pro se, filed a 42 U.S.C. § 1983 complaint on August 18, 1988, alleging constitutional claims related to an attempted prison visit on July 10, 1988, at Indiana State Prison involving Judy Ballard. The defendants moved for summary judgment on July 5, 1989. The order describes the standards for summary judgment under Rule 56, referencing Celotex and Anderson, and states that a non-moving party must go beyond the pleadings by designating specific facts showing a genuine issue for trial.  

The court applies due process and Eighth Amendment principles regarding whether inmates have a liberty interest in visitation, citing Hewitt and Kentucky Department of Corrections v. Thompson. It finds that the relevant administrative procedure allows denial of visitation privileges without specific criteria and that the plaintiff is unlikely to establish a protected liberty interest. The court notes an admitted failure to give the denial in writing but concludes the plaintiff’s focus on that failure does not support a substantive constitutional claim. The plaintiff’s motion for summary judgment is denied, and summary judgment is granted for the defendants.

The passage reports factors associated with non-adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) among HIV patients worldwide and specifically in Rwanda. Reported reasons for not taking ART include social isolation (33.4%), preoccupation with other commitments (25.0%), forgetting (25.0%), toxicity/side effects (8.3%), shame and disclosure problems (8.3%), and insufficient ARV medications due to public holidays/weekends (7.5%). The study in Kibungo Referral Hospital used a cross-sectional quantitative design (data collected March 25 to April 30, 2024) and found an overall ART non-adherence rate of 13% (55 of 424) and adherence rate of 87% (369). Bivariate and multivariate analyses identified significant associations with non-adherence: age (younger than 31), lack of tertiary education, stigma interfering with adherence, perceiving ART as ineffective, and failure to integrate ART into daily activities. The conclusion states that younger age, lack of tertiary education, stigma, perceived ineffectiveness of ART, and failure to integrate ART into daily activities are significant factors linked to ART non-adherence in Kibungo Referral Hospital.

The passage explains the Golden Cross trading strategy, which uses two moving averages—typically the 50-day and 200-day—to generate signals. A Golden Cross occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses above the 200-day average, signaling a bullish breakout and prompting a buy; when it crosses below, it signals a bearish breakout and prompts a sell. The strategy is presented as aiming to exploit the stock market’s long-term uptrend while reducing losses in bear markets by staying invested in bullish periods and exiting during bearish periods. A backtest on the S&P 500 from 1960 using daily bars found 33 trades with an average duration of about 350 days. Results reported include 79% winning trades, an average trade gain of 15.8%, and a 6.8% annual return, with risk-adjusted return cited as 9.6%. The strategy showed lower drawdowns than buy-and-hold (33% vs. 56%) and the passage notes the backtest did not reinvest dividends.

The passage discusses the importance of e-learning for business competitiveness and states that effective e-learning requires guidance to improve processes and governance. E-learning governance, defined via CO BIT, includes providing strategic direction, ensuring objectives are achieved, managing risks, and allocating resources, using control principles that cover direction, cost effectiveness, quality, ethics, and security. The paper outlines e-learning systems and defines e-learning ecosystems as a learning community united by an LMS, with descriptions of digital business and e-learning ecosystem components and benefits such as ROI, productivity, and improved employee performance. It then explains governance’s role in decision-making and coordination, and proposes an e-learning governance framework based on structures, processes, communications and relational mechanisms, and an added element of pedagogies and instructional designs. The passage further details six interrelated characteristics/dimensions for e-learning ecosystem governance and emphasizes information security governance, including securing information, creating policies, implementing and monitoring counter-measures, and incorporating risk management and trust-related concepts. It concludes that further research is needed to better understand business benefits of improving e-learning governance practices in evolving digital business ecosystems.

By early March 2020, COVID-19 cases were confirmed in most regions worldwide, including the Republic of Ireland (RoI). The WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on March 11, 2020, and on March 12 the Irish government closed educational, childcare, and cultural facilities; this response expanded into a full lockdown with a stay-at-home order by March 27, 2020. The passage describes using the Disability-Adjusted-Life-Year (DALY) as an internationally comparable metric to estimate the burden of disease (BoD) from March 1, 2020 to February 28, 2021 in RoI, based on Disability-Adjusted-Life-Year components: Years of Life Lost (YLL) from deaths and remaining life expectancy, and Years Lived with Disability (YLD) from incident cases, duration, and disability weights across health states (asymptomatic, moderate, severe, critical, and post-acute consequences). Data sources are cited as publicly available via data.gov.ie, and the study uses GBD standard life tables for 2019 to calculate remaining life expectancy. Ethical approval was obtained from the Social Research Ethics Committee of University College Cork (UCC).

Explainable AI is a global research focus because it can improve understanding of pre-trained language models, address resource limitations, and support transparency needed to mitigate safety risks such as adversarial attacks, harmful behavior, and ethical breaches. The aim of AI interpretability research is to enhance transparency and trust in LLMs’ decision-making by creating methods and tools that provide clear explanations, help identify performance limitations, and guide improvements. Key challenges include the lack of unified evaluation frameworks, computational inefficiency that does not scale to large language models, and difficulty translating interpretability methods to real-world deployment contexts. The passage proposes a framework for editing concept activation vectors to control model behavior for specific concepts (e.g., reducing toxicity or enhancing honesty) even with limited annotated data. It collects activation vectors during text generation, trains a logistic regression classifier to detect target concepts, derives CAVs that quantify conceptual influence, and dynamically applies CAVs during inference to add or suppress concepts while maintaining fluency and supporting multiple concept adjustments through conflict management.

The passage describes data management and protection strategies for backups, archives, and snapshots, including full, incremental, and differential incremental backups, and explains snapshots as point-in-time usable copies. It focuses on a cloud-integrated storage appliance that caches snapshot data while maintaining snapshot metadata in key-value stores per defined data collection, enabling efficient snapshot and file restoration and snapshot reclamation (deletion) by merging or implicitly transferring ownership of valid metadata and data ranges.

It then introduces methods to reduce “stable data eviction” in a forever incremental snapshot setup by creating synthetic baseline snapshots and refreshing eviction state data. The synthetic baseline is created by manipulating snapshot metadata and updating eviction-related time/use indicators (and fingerprint database associations when deduplication is used) so stable blocks are less likely to be evicted, improving restore performance. Variations are also described, including alternative ways to create synthetic baselines (ownership expansion vs. reverse-incremental synthetic baseline refresh), and different sequencing/parallelization and buffering approaches for restore operations.

Police are investigating a cellphone video showing officers shocking 17-year-old Dailene Rosario with a stun gun inside a New York City apartment building while she screamed in agony. The criminal complaint says Rosario, reportedly 14 weeks pregnant, interfered with police and shoved an officer into a doorframe. The incident occurred around 10 p.m. last Friday when officers responded to an unrelated call in the Bronx and found a fight involving her ex-boyfriend; the scuffle reportedly began over a video game. Rosario was reportedly charged with resisting arrest, second degree harassment, and disorderly conduct. The NYPD said it is under internal review.

The passage is a series of comments about hockey games and team decisions. It discusses how goaltender Martin initially struggled to help the team score more than two goals, then improved when Ray Emery returned healthy, leading to wins, after which Martin was designated for the bench and Emery played. It also addresses respect for opposing teams and describes confidence and preparation for upcoming tests, including playing well early. Additional remarks cover leadership and improvements among players, including a player described as one of the most improved due to becoming effective in all situations and as a two-way player. The passage includes discussion of trades and acquisitions, notably the reasons for trading for Mike Comrie and how he became a solid two-way contributor after initially not fitting well on the right side. It further mentions adjusting routines and matchups in the league and reflects on coaching decisions, player development, and strategies involving line and defensive pair usage, including the importance of shot blocking and adapting to changes in the game and equipment.
