The passage consists of teammates discussing their mindset and focus as they approach a final, “last and final step” to win the Stanley Cup. They say the series is not over and they want to be ready to play “tomorrow night,” keeping the same attitude as earlier in the playoffs. Several players comment on Marian’s impact on and off the ice, noting his old-school, smart approach and that he is motivated rather than dwelling on a loss. They describe the importance of staying energized for the game, handling individual emotions and discipline as a team (including penalties and frustrations), and relying on contributions from multiple players, including those with fewer minutes who step up in pressure situations. They also mention their awareness of the rarity of reaching the cup final, describe this as an ongoing, unusual season, and express enjoyment of the moment regardless of what happens next.

The passage is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Form 8-K current report filed by NVIDIA Corporation on August 15, 2019. It states that on August 15, 2019, NVIDIA issued a press release announcing results for the quarter ended July 28, 2019, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. It also states that financial information and commentary by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, are attached as Exhibit 99.2, and that the CFO commentary will be posted to the company’s investor website immediately after filing. The report includes Item 9.01 for the exhibits and is signed by Colette M. Kress.

The passage discusses a game in which the speaker says one goal was not enough to finish and describes a second-effort goal. The speaker notes that prior to a goal, there were “two or three big saves,” and mentions a power play that resulted in no scoring. They say the opponent made a play they had used before and that their own team should have been better on it. The speaker also comments on the team needing to win on the road, having balanced play with four lines after days off, and believes road performance depends more on style and system than lineup. They conclude that the first period needed to be better and that their team was not as sharp as required, despite the score not reflecting the first-period play.

Vertical farming is described as growing crops in a controlled environment without soil and water, with crops stacked in layers and using mechanisms such as hydroponics and aeroponics. The market is driven by factors including better food quality, population growth, reduced dependence on water and soil, and rising food demand, along with adoption of new technologies, zero pesticide and fertilizer use, and artificial lighting. Growth is hindered by high initial investments in urban locations, higher energy use for artificial lighting, and difficulty producing high value crops. North America held the largest global market share, while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow fastest over 2016–2022, supported by urbanization, limited fertile land, and investments in vertical farming systems. The market is expected to reach about USD 6 billion by end of 2022 with a 21% CAGR; key players listed include Aerofarms, Hort Americas, Indoor Harvest Corporation, Illumitex, Koninklijke Philips, Everlight Electronics, Sky Greens, Agrilution, and Urban Crop Solutions.

Only 18% of America’s workers are very confident they are on track for a secure retirement. The passage says you can check whether your retirement savings will be enough by doing three things: (1) project retirement income by estimating total savings based on your current savings rate, using online calculators and adding expected Social Security benefits; (2) review and minimize investment fees because they can significantly reduce returns; and (3) confirm proper asset allocation based on age and risk tolerance, updating it as you get older. It concludes that monitoring these factors can help build a substantial nest egg and improve confidence in retirement plans.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff members in BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found a shift toward Democratic-affiliated groups. In 2023–2024, 92.45% of contributions went to Democrats, compared with a roughly 12-to-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio that was “significantly up” from a 6-to-1 ratio in a 2021 analysis of 2017–2020. The studied group contributed about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups versus about $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. The analysis covered attorneys and staff at the nation’s 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms, and it identified firms with the highest and lowest percentages of contributions to Democratic campaigns.

The passage describes E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures and an E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures strategy. It explains the futures contract represents a $50 times the Russell 2000 Index value (launched in 1993) and trades on the CME Globex platform for speculation or hedging. It outlines trading hours, quarterly contract cycles, settlement as cash on the day of final settlement (normally the third Friday), and trading termination times. It lists contract specifications such as tick size ($5.00 outright on Globex; $2.50 for BTIC/TACO/calendar spread) and minimum price fluctuation (0.10 index points outright; 0.05 for BTIC/TACO/calendar spread), and notes an example price level of $1841.2 as of November 30, 2022. The passage states the all-time high for the E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures is 2460.8 (November 2021) and references the all-time low of the underlying Russell 2000 index as 106.07 (October 1987). It also mentions risks from adverse price movement due to leverage and identifies factors affecting prices, including movement of highly weighted component stocks, interest rate changes, economic news, and the U.S. dollar.

The passage describes a WiseGuyReports market research report on the US data center UPS market (2016–2020). It forecasts the market will grow at a CAGR of 4.01% during 2016–2020. It explains how UPS systems provide backup power during outages until generators take over, and lists UPS components such as rectifiers, inverters, and batteries or flywheels. The report covers market scenario and growth prospects for 2015–2020, segments the market by UPS type (centralized, zone/floor-level, rackmount) and by topology (standby, line-interactive, double-conversion online). It names key vendors (ABB, Eaton, Emerson Network Power, GE Industrial Solutions, Schneider Electric, Tripp Lite) and other prominent vendors, and cites market drivers (increase in data center power outages), challenges (UPS battery failure), and trends (advances in DCIM). It also lists key questions the report addresses and provides a table of contents outline.

The state Board of Regents voted unanimously to let special-education students who struggle on academic exams earn high-school diplomas through an alternative route based on occupational assessments. Under the plan, adopted on an emergency basis by Education Commissioner MaryEllen Elia, such students would not need minimum scores on the state Regents exams in English and math. The change will likely take effect for students graduating as early as January and is expected to be formally approved later by the full board. Long Island parents applauded the decision, while some analysts and advocates raised concerns about encouraging separate academic tracks and about the speed of the emergency vote.

Turkey secured a €974 million loan from a consortium of international lenders to fund a major highway project in central Anatolia. The highway is intended to link key provincial centers, improve access to trade routes and logistics, and reduce travel times, with expected economic benefits including investment, industrial expansion, and job creation. Financing includes environmental and social performance standards supported by European development institutions and multilateral lenders. The project could face delays from rugged terrain and land acquisition disputes and may be affected by volatility in borrowing costs and the Turkish lira, but the loan is described as a milestone in Turkey’s infrastructure modernization and regional development efforts.

Jawed Zia, former managing director of Novartis India who quit days after taking charge, may be moving to rival Abbott India, according to sources. His resignation last Friday came 15 days after he was appointed, and an email sent by ET to Novartis and Zia was unanswered. Novartis did not name a replacement in its stock exchange statement, while Abbott competes with Novartis in areas like cardiovascular and diabetes and also has tie-ups for certain drugs. Novartis India reported domestic sales of nearly Rs 1,200 crore and has faced anti-competition regulators investigating price collusion over its anti-diabetic drug Galvus with other companies including Abbott, USV, and Emcure Pharma.

In December 2019, the Wuhan Municipal Health Committee identified viral pneumonia cases of unknown cause, and coronavirus RNA was found in some patients. The virus was designated SARS-CoV-2 and the disease COVID-19. The passage states there are currently no approved therapeutics for coronaviruses. It describes the DAWN master study protocol to investigate promising drug compounds or convalescent plasma. Convalescent plasma may help newly diagnosed patients clear infection faster due to antiviral antibodies, but it has not been effective for other viral infections (e.g., Ebola) and carries a risk of antibody-dependent enhancement that could worsen ARDS. Therefore, convalescent plasma should be studied in a randomized controlled setting with eligible adult hospitalized patients who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.

Riverwood Nursing Center, LLC d/b/a Glenwood Nursing Center appeals a Florida agency dismissal of its request for an administrative hearing as untimely. Glenwood argued (1) the filing deadline should be equitably tolled based on representations by AHCA counsel and (2) its later hearing request related back to or amended an earlier April 16, 2010 letter to CMS. The court affirmed AHCA’s dismissal with prejudice, concluding equitable tolling did not apply and that Glenwood’s April 16 letter was legally insufficient to invoke a right to a Chapter 120 hearing with AHCA, and its June 15 filing was not properly filed with the AHCA agency clerk as required. The court therefore upheld revocation of Glenwood’s license and a $25,000 administrative fine.

The passage introduces “10 free swing trading strategies” and discusses whether swing trading can be improved and what realistic returns might be. It argues that many internet swing-trading claims are unproven and that backtesting helps estimate expectations. It defines swing trading as holding positions from a few days to several weeks (longer than day trading, but not more than a couple of months), and contrasts it with buy-and-hold and time diversification. It says the strategies listed are backtested (some published since 2012) and provided in Plain English, with many available mainly in Amibroker and some in Tradestation/Python code. It highlights specific strategies (e.g., turn-of-the-month in S&P 500/Nasdaq, MACD-histogram, mean reversion, rotation among SPY/GLD/TLT, Monday reversal, and moving-average systems using 200-day and 12-month averages). The passage states that realistic swing trading returns are between 5% and 20% and claims most traders have unrealistic expectations. It also says the most successful swing traders quantify strategies and that momentum and other strategies can potentially be improved.

The passage describes wood-type golf club heads, especially driver-type heads, and focuses on designs that use raised sole portions and multi-material components to manage mass, stiffness, sound, and performance. It explains that raised sole regions can stiffen the sole through increased curvature, reduce sole mass, and alter acoustics, potentially requiring fewer ribs and freeing discretionary mass for other uses. The designs may include cantilevered ledges, bi-level (two-tier) or toe/heel raised sole configurations, sole and crown inserts made of less dense materials, sole channels/weight tracks, adjustable shaft connections, and adjustable sliding weights. The passage outlines measurement concepts for center of gravity (CG), projected CG (“zero-torque” point), moment of inertia (MOI) about multiple axes, and provides example target ranges and test data, including sample forgiveness ratios, CG/MOI characteristics, and club-head dimensional/volume guidance under USGA constraints. It also includes references to accompanying figures, brief drawing descriptions, and example manufacturing methods and materials for frames, sole inserts, crown inserts, and weight tracks.

When the CS_ILIM voltage exceeds 1.05 V, the device performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting: the controller output turns on each cycle until CS_ILIM reaches the current sense threshold, then turns off. Each time CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V, CHICC is charged by an 80-µA hiccup delay current, which ends at the end of the clock cycle; as long as overcurrent is detected, cycle-by-cycle limiting continues until CHICC reaches 0.6 V, and this period is the delay mode. After HICC reaches 0.6 V, the SS pin is discharged and switching stops; HICC is pulled up to 1 V (limited to ~1 mA), then discharged by a 1-µA restart current until HICC falls to 0.3 V, when soft-start restarts. The hiccup restart time is the total non-switching period and depends on capacitor CHICC. A minimum CHICC value of 3.3 nF is recommended. The OUTB and corresponding CS_ILIM waveforms apply only to TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP.

The passage describes how to deploy Mattermost, an open source instant messaging platform, on a CentOS 7 server. It covers prerequisites (a domain pointing to the server, Nginx installed with an SSL certificate, and an SSL certificate via Let’s Encrypt), creating a MariaDB database and user, creating a system user, downloading and installing Mattermost version 4.9.0, configuring `/opt/mattermost/config/config.json` for MySQL, testing by starting the server, and creating and starting a `mattermost.service` systemd unit. It then provides an Nginx reverse proxy configuration for the domain `linuxize-test.com` with SSL and redirects from HTTP to HTTPS, and reloads Nginx. Finally, it outlines browser-based initial setup (administrator privileges for the first user, team creation, setting the site URL, enabling email notifications with SMTP settings) and restarting the Mattermost service.

Federal regulators fined Altaba, formerly Yahoo, $35 million for failing to disclose a data breach from four years earlier that exposed personal data for hundreds of millions of accounts. The company informed the public in 2016 with usernames, email addresses, phone numbers, and passwords, two years after learning about the breach, and the details became public during Verizon’s acquisition. The SEC said Yahoo did not properly investigate the breach and that insufficient disclosure left investors uninformed.

U.S. Treasury yields rose on Monday as tensions between the United States and North Korea eased, leading investors to reduce holdings of low-risk government debt. Last week’s fears of a military showdown over Pyongyang’s nuclear plans had driven a rush into Treasuries and other safe assets. After comments from South Korean President Moon Jae-in urging a peaceful solution and U.S. National Security Adviser H.R. McMaster downplaying military conflict, some investors moved back into stocks and other risky assets. At 8:59 a.m. New York time, the 10-year Treasury yield was 2.222%, up more than 3 basis points from late Friday, while the two-year yield rose to 1.314% after hitting an eight-week low on softer July inflation data.

The passage describes a medRxiv preprint (posted January 2, 2025) evaluating six machine-learning models for diagnosing pancreatic cancer using a synthetic, binary dataset (diagnosis: 0 no cancer, 1 cancer). Models compared include Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Networks, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner, assessed with accuracy, sensitivity (recall), precision, F1-score, and balanced accuracy after preprocessing and an 80/20 train-test split. All models achieved similar accuracy (~76%), but sensitivity was very low across the board; Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positives. SuperLearner had the highest precision (66.67%) but very low sensitivity (0.42%), while SVM had the highest sensitivity (1.90%) but still insufficient. The passage attributes poor sensitivity largely to class imbalance and discusses potential improvements such as resampling, threshold tuning, feature engineering using PCA/clustering insights, more real-world validation, interpretability methods (e.g., SHAP, LIME), and clinical collaboration.

A Feb. 9 study by 11Alive reported that while the CDC funded a failed project, it cut hundreds of thousands from HIV prevention programs. Georgia’s Department of Public Health said more than $700,000 was cut in 2016, mostly from HIV prevention funding. Georgia State School of Public Health PhD candidate Jamal Jones said prevention awareness is lacking, noting that PrEP is available but expensive and hard to access in lower-income, underserved, and stigmatized communities in Atlanta. Victoria Novak said limited healthcare access, lack of regular doctor encouragement for testing, and fear of diagnosis contribute to the problem, which could worsen if the Affordable Care Act is repealed without a replacement. Jones also cited Georgia law that criminalizes certain activities if someone has HIV, which he said discourages disclosure and timely testing. Jones said many people get tested too late, often reaching advanced AIDS stages by the time results are received. In partnership with Georgia State School of Public Health, Jones helped launch a campaign to increase student testing, and the passage notes that this year House Bill 65 would expand medical marijuana eligibility to include HIV/AIDS.

RTX Neural Faces addresses the challenge of rendering faces realistically in real time, which is difficult due to humans’ sensitivity to anomalies described by the Uncanny Valley. It uses a real-time generative AI model to infer a more natural-looking face from a simple rasterized face and 3D pose data, instead of brute force rendering. The model is trained using thousands of offline generated images across different angles, lighting, emotions, and occlusion, with training data that can include real photographs or AI-generated images created via a diffusion model. After training, the model is optimized with TensorRT to infer faces in real time.

Salesforce said it will invest more than $2.2 billion in its French business over the next five years. The announcement was made during President Emmanuel Macron’s state visit to Washington, where he met U.S. President Donald Trump. Salesforce cited rapid growth in France and plans to significantly increase its headcount, real estate footprint, and data center capacity.

Churchill is a community of about 900 people that has been shrinking since a rail line washed out in spring 2017. Town officials said 30 families left since last May, with low employment and rising fuel and food costs cited as factors. Residents described increased departures as upsetting, and the Duke of Marlborough school has lost about 40 students since last June. School officials said the drop is linked to job losses from the rail disruption and that lower enrollment may affect teaching jobs. The overall long-term impact is undetermined, and there is no timeline for repairing the rail line.

Faith-based organisations, including more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers, are increasingly supporting the overstretched NHS through health and social care initiatives, according to the Cinnamon Network. Its report, *The Church’s Impact on Health and Care*, highlights 32 church-led projects tackling issues such as mental health, obesity, and social isolation, and suggests they are cost-effective. Parish nursing is one example, with registered nurses recruited by churches to provide patient support either voluntarily or through paid roles. The report and interviews describe parish nurses as offering preventative care, support, monitoring, and time for non task-oriented engagement, while also acting as advocates. Parish nursing, which began with a 2005 UK pilot, has grown to more than 100 nurses working with 85 churches, and another 100 are expected to be established within 18 months, reflecting a growing need.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017 includes unaudited consolidated financial statements and related notes. For the three months ended March 31, 2017, Microsoft reported total revenue of $22,090 million and net income of $4,801 million (basic EPS $0.62; diluted EPS $0.61). For the nine months ended March 31, 2017, total revenue was $66,633 million and net income was $14,691 million (basic EPS $1.89; diluted EPS $1.87). The balance sheet as of March 31, 2017 shows total assets of $225,017 million and total stockholders’ equity of $69,729 million. The cash flows for the nine months ended March 31, 2017 show net cash from operations of $28,502 million, net cash from (used in) financing of $11,109 million, and net cash used in investing of $39,412 million. The notes describe accounting policies, earnings per share, other income (expense), investments, derivatives and fair value measurement, inventories, business combinations (including the LinkedIn acquisition), goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, restructuring and unearned revenue, commitments and contingencies, stockholders’ equity (including share repurchases and dividends), accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment information. The MD&A provides forward-looking statements and summarizes the company’s strategy and third-quarter 2017 highlights.

The passage describes how digitalization and modern IT technologies are changing manufacturing, emphasizing the need for reliable information and data to support innovative product development and manufacturing processes. It states that simulation, modeling, and data analysis help speed product development and time to market, reduce costs, support decision-making, and improve product and service quality while avoiding defects. It reports that many enterprises already use these methods in areas such as product development, production/process planning, and quality management, with plans to increase deployment. The passage highlights challenges such as data silos and outdated or inaccurate simulations, and argues that high-performance computing (HPC) enables complex calculations, improves the quality and speed of simulations, unlocks new usage scenarios, and increases innovation and agility. It also notes that enterprises anticipate growing demand for high-performance calculations and that many already use or plan to pilot professional HPC infrastructures, citing barriers such as high investment costs.

Columbiana and Lisbon played in a rivalry game at Lisbon, Ohio, with the Clippers winning 49-47. Lisbon had a 47-45 lead with 36 seconds remaining after two free throws by Izzy Perez, but Alexis Cross tied the game with a baseline score at 23 seconds left. Kayla Muslovski then made a steal and layup to provide the winning points. The Clippers improved to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in the league, while the Devils fell to 3-2 overall and 2-1 in league play. Muslovski and Cross led the Clippers with 14 points each, while Perez led the Devils with 17 points. The Devils’ Chloe Smith scored a three to make it 40-39 at the end of the third quarter. Lisbon also won a JV game 33-23, with Annaliese Quibley scoring 11 points.

Reddit has surpassed Facebook to become the third most visited platform in the US, according to Alexa. Google remains first, followed by YouTube, Reddit, Facebook, and Amazon. Users spend more time on Reddit than on Facebook, and Reddit has high daily page views per visitor. The Facebook ranking decline is linked to the Cambridge Analytica data scandal, and Facebook has announced platform changes aimed at safety and GDPR compliance. The passage also states that about 1.69 billion users accessed Reddit in the most recent period, Facebook had 2.19 billion monthly active users as of the first quarter of 2018, and the US accounts for over 40% of Reddit’s desktop traffic.

The ICC Board meetings in Kolkata on Wednesday and Thursday (Item No. 6.2) may again discuss a proposal to replace the 2021 Champions Trophy in India with a World T20. BCCI treasurer Anirudh Chaudhry said scrapping the Champions Trophy would cost about $30 million for BCCI and its stakeholders, noting that the BCCI previously rejected a similar idea raised at an ICC conclave in Auckland. He also criticized ICC chairman Shashank Manohar and said the matter could be unacceptable to the BCCI General Body, which had resolved the ICC Member Participation Agreement would not be executed without General Body approval. The 2019-2023 FTP events were agreed in Auckland, with Australia hosting the 2020 World T20 and India hosting the 2021 Champions Trophy and the 2023 World Cup, though a recent ICC strategy and financial sustainability meeting reportedly referred to the proposed 2021 Champions Trophy as a “World T20 tournament.” The ICC Chief Executives Committee meeting also agreed on a revised 2019 World Cup itinerary, with India’s matches on June 5 (vs South Africa) and June 16 (vs Pakistan).

Suspected jihadists attacked a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, overnight, killing at least 18 people and wounding several. Communications Minister Remi Dandjinou called it a terrorist attack and said the death toll was provisional while the security operation continued; security forces shot dead both attackers and freed people trapped inside. The incident involved gunfire as customers fled the Aziz Istanbul restaurant, including a woman who said she ran out while her brother remained inside. The passage also notes prior jihadist attacks in Burkina Faso and the region, the expansion of militant reach after actions in Mali, and a new multinational military force against Islamist militants that will not be operational until later this year due to funding issues.

The passage reports severe weather threats across the southeastern United States on Monday, including hail, damaging winds, and possible tornadoes. A strong thunderstorm in northern Mississippi has dropped hail near Ripley and along a 50-mile path from Holly Springs to Booneville, with hail reports from social media showing several inches of pea-sized hail. The Storm Prediction Center says there is increasing confidence in “several tornadic supercells” in northern Alabama, where several tornadoes are most likely, and that a broader risk also includes parts of Tennessee, Mississippi, and Georgia. Schools in northern Alabama and some areas of Tennessee closed early, and Birmingham city offices closed at noon. Forecasts indicate thunderstorms, tornadoes, damaging winds, and hail as large as tennis balls are possible.

The passage describes physics-informed deep learning for discovering and forecasting unknown PDE dynamics, focusing on improving zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization without test-time adaptation. It notes that existing approaches learn domain-generalizable representations but still lack ideal zero-shot capability because they do not explicitly capture a fundamental invariance principle. The authors propose a two-level PDE invariance principle: (i) operator invariance, where PDE dynamics are governed by a fixed set of spatial operators, and (ii) compositionality invariance, where a fixed composition relationship combines these operators with physical parameters and forcing terms. To learn this invariance from limited training trajectories across multiple domains, they introduce iMOOE, combining a mixture of operator experts architecture aligned to the operator/composition structure and a frequency-enriched invariant learning objective that enforces risk equality across environments and adds a Fourier-domain regularization to address high-frequency spectral bias. Experiments on several simulated PDE systems (and real-world sea surface temperature data) evaluate forecasting using nMSE and fRMSE in both data and frequency domains, reporting improved zero-shot OOD performance for iMOOE versus multiple baselines, along with studies on operator compatibility and sensitivity to the number of experts.

Indian stock markets opened strong with sharp gains, but a correction late in the week erased most intra-week gains versus global indexes. Concerns included possible new U.S. tariffs and trade wars, fears of global interest rate hikes, RBI steps to discontinue LoUs and LCs affecting trade credit, political challenges for the ruling BJP, and disputes involving the RBI and finance ministry. The Nifty fell 0.3% for the week, while mid- and small-cap indexes rose about 1.5% each. The rupee ended at 64.93 per dollar. Oil prices were largely flat after the IEA said demand would rise while supply grows faster. The week ahead would be shaped by the Fed’s March meeting, the Bank of England decision, and G20 meetings. Company news included TCS’s planned stake sale decision, supply agreement proposals by Ambuja Cements and ACC, IndiGo grounding A320neo aircraft, and another fraud detected by Punjab National Bank. Three major IPOs—Bharat Dynamics, Bandhan Bank, and Hindustan Aeronautics—were also mentioned.

The lecture discusses quantum gases, focusing on Bose and Fermi gases with interactions and their superfluid properties. It reviews the Bogoliubov approximation for the interacting Bose gas, explaining how it diagonalizes the Hamiltonian into non-interacting quasiparticles with a linear dispersion at low momenta, and it introduces the small parameter controlling weak interactions, expressed as the gas parameter \(N a^3\), along with the assumption of small condensate depletion. The passage describes how sound and quasiparticle excitations can be observed via density perturbations and photon-based spectroscopy using the dynamic structure factor. It then transitions to trapped, inhomogeneous Bose-Einstein condensates, introducing the Gross-Pitaevskii (nonlinear Schrodinger) equation and the healing length, and relates its predictions to experiments such as condensate expansion and vortex behavior. Finally, it introduces Bose-Einstein condensates in optical lattices, deriving the Bose-Hubbard model from a periodic potential using Wannier functions, discussing the limits \(U \gg j\) (Mott insulator) and \(j \gg U\) (superfluid), and presenting a mean-field approach to analyze the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition. The passage concludes with experimental observation methods, including time-of-flight diffraction patterns and quantum gas microscopy that measures site-resolved atom number across the transition.

The passage advises focusing on winning each shift and period rather than worrying about the end of the game. It states that for about three days the team has been focusing on what they do on the ice and executing well, describing the current period as the best of the year. It also emphasizes taking advantage of the opportunity to win the cup, noting some players may never get it again.

Rapid commercialization of GenAI tools outpaced research methods and regulatory oversight, and health systems often operate in silos that hinder evidence-informed implementation. The authors propose using a Learning Health System (LHS) framework with structured governance and workflow-aligned evaluation to address implementation barriers, noting prior GenAI deployments without human-factor and organizational tailoring led to underutilization and inefficiencies.

They present a pragmatic randomized controlled trial protocol within an LHS to evaluate Ambient AI, a GenAI tool embedded in the EHR to assist with clinical documentation and reduce provider “pajama time.” Prior Ambient AI evaluations were limited by observational designs, inconsistent results, and limited interoperability. The protocol uses governance structures and iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, and embeds the system into the EHR within a pragmatic type 1 hybrid randomized trial. The PTOps playbook includes five components: governance, user experience, technical strategies, documentation sustainment, and outcomes-oriented analytics.

Ambient AI was integrated at UW Health under a SaaS agreement as part of a quality improvement initiative with patient consent for clinical use and provider consent for trial participation. A stepped-wedge design was selected to avoid simultaneous rollout and to enable random concurrent exposure. The alpha phase (June 24, 2024 to October 10, 2024 beta start) evaluated implementation and monitoring: 20 providers and 8,527 encounters across five specialties and 12 locations. Interviews identified barriers and facilitators related to organizational characteristics, provider/patient readiness, and service/task suitability. Provider-averaged daily Ambient AI utilization reached a weighted median of 65.4% (IQR 50.6%–84.0%). The authors also describe documentation sustainment issues involving ICD-10 diagnosis code accuracy, subsequent workflow/template changes, and automated LLM-based coding review validated with Jaccard index measures.

The beta phase protocol described a 24-week, individually randomized stepped-wedge trial, with providers randomized into waves transitioning from usual care to the intervention at 6-week intervals; planned recruitment was completed by October 2024 across eight specialties in Wisconsin and Illinois, beginning the trial on schedule. Results presented for the alpha phase include utilization changes following license release, documentation accuracy changes after note-template adjustments, and monitoring using difference-in-differences analyses and drift detection. The study concludes that aligning operational and research priorities in an LHS framework can accelerate implementation and evaluation of rapidly iterating GenAI technology while supporting scalability and operational efficiency.

Crude sulfate turpentine (sulfate wood turpentine), also known as wood turpentine, is a flammable, water-insoluble derivative product obtained by distilling resin from live trees (especially pines) and as a byproduct of the Kraft process. It contains terpene hydrocarbons and miscellaneous sulfur compounds, mainly alpha-pinene and beta-pinene with smaller amounts of other terpenes. It is used primarily in fragrances and flavors, in cosmetics and food & beverages, as a solvent for thinning oil-based paints and producing varnishes, and as a raw material for organic synthesis in chemical industry, especially aromatic compounds. Market use is restricted due to high distillation investment requirements and limited retrieval of black liquor through the Kraft process. Alpha-pinene is described as an anti-inflammatory agent and part of a broad-spectrum antibiotic; beta-pinene is used in perfumery.

Kari L. Baumann appealed a district court’s summary judgment against her in a healthcare malpractice suit against The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler. Baumann did not timely designate or disclose expert witnesses as required by the parties’ discovery schedule and rule 26, and the district court precluded her from using any undisclosed witnesses or materials in opposition to summary judgment under rule 26(d)(4). The appeals court held that Baumann’s argument regarding an additional expert report applicable to Dr. Tayler was unpreserved and was not considered. As to the Kroger-related expert report, the appeals court concluded rule 26(d)(4), not rule 16(d), controlled and affirmed the district court’s preclusion and grant of summary judgment.

The bill “to facilitate the refunding of the national debt” is returned to the House of Representatives with objections. The passage is regarded as important for reducing the nation’s annual interest payments, and the Secretary of the Treasury has urged Congress to act. The President says it would be unwise to authorize the Treasury Secretary to offer 3 1/2 percent bonds, but the main objection is to the bill’s fifth section, which the President believes seriously impairs and would tend to destroy the national banking system. The fifth section is described as limiting eligible bonds for national-bank security and as requiring banks to use only 3 percent bonds for circulation security, while repealing and reenacting related provisions. The President argues this change would restrict bank organization and capital growth, likely turn the system into a monopoly, and endanger existing banks. The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere architecture “GA10x” GPUs, focusing on the GA102 and GA104 models and their features compared with the Turing architecture. The passage discusses API misuse in data science libraries, where deviations from intended API usage can cause runtime errors, performance issues, or incorrect output. It notes prior research focused largely on statically typed languages and that dynamic typing and data-centric workflows in Python create additional misuse challenges, including data conversion errors in deep learning libraries. To address this, the paper presents DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach that prompts models using API directives from documentation and dynamic data information gathered by executing code. An illustrative example shows SimpleImputer strategy misuse leading to a discarded column and an IndexError, with a suggested fix changing the strategy and adding a fill value.

The paper describes dataset preparation using DSMISUSES (38 vetted Stack Overflow/GitHub misuses across five data science libraries, extended with correct code snippets), and evaluation metrics for misuse detection (precision, recall, F1 with explanation verification) and misuse fixing (applying patches and checking for correct resolution). Experiments (RQ1–RQ5) evaluate which prompt information is most effective, whether few-shot prompting helps, whether the approach generalizes to other libraries using a DL misuse sample, how it compares to an existing LLM-based tool (LLMAPIDET), and whether an agentic variant (DSCHECKERagent) can retrieve information on demand via function calling. Results report that combining API directives and data information improves performance (best detection F1 of 61.18% and fix rate of 51.28% for llama), outperforms LLMAPIDET on the evaluated dataset, and shows promise for real-world information-not-provided scenarios (agent detection F1 48.65%, fix rate 39.47%). The passage also outlines background work on API misuse detection, related LLM approaches, implementation of the agent functions, and stated threats to validity and future directions.

The passage discusses hockey games and playoffs, focusing on goalie performance, the importance of scoring first, and how early leads in the first ten minutes are crucial. A study published in *Psychological Medicine* found that lonely millennials have twice the risk of developing mental health problems such as depression and anxiety compared with those who are connected to others. Researchers from King’s College London analyzed 2,066 millennial twins in England and Wales and found that 7% often felt lonely, while 23–31% felt left out or lacked companionship. Overall, loneliness was linked to double the chance of a mental health problem, a 38% increased risk of unemployment, and more risky behaviors like smoking and not exercising. The passage also notes that loneliness is greatest among teenagers and young adults, that older people are not necessarily at highest risk, and discusses possible causes including social media use, loneliness being “contagious,” and hostile or defensive behaviors that may worsen social ties. It concludes that while feeling lonely is not itself a mental health problem, it is strongly connected to mental well-being and that early intervention may help.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science (HMNS) have collaborated on space science outreach since 1988, including NSF-funded teacher research programs that informed Rice’s Master of Science Teaching program. Their partnership helped develop early educational technologies and produced research findings that learning in a dome supports greater content retention than viewing on a flatscreen.  

For eclipse outreach, they created and distributed NASA-funded solar and lunar eclipse animations for use in classrooms and planetariums, tracked animator requests starting in 2021 (186 educators in 33 countries and 33 U.S. states), and used the planetarium show “Totality!” as a central outreach tool. “Totality!” was distributed free in multiple formats and reported wide viewing and distribution metrics across planetariums and schools, with additional Spanish and Romanian audio/subtitle options.  

They also offered formal and informal teacher education (including semester-long courses and workshops), created eclipse activity materials and safety resources for educators, and distributed large numbers of eclipse glasses and viewing cards, including a Texas-wide card program. Public eclipse events included observations and demonstrations at multiple sites and media engagement.  

In the Citizen CATE 2024 project, led by SwRI with NSF NCAR partnerships and funding from NSF and NASA, 35 community sites used standardized equipment and procedures to observe the April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse and capture continuous high-cadence coronagraphy-style data; training and coordination were provided through regional and state lead teams. The partnership also reported space weather forecasting activities under MMS funding and, in results, cited well over 250,000 documented views in leveraged venues, a total reach well over 1.5 million people, nearly a million eclipse viewers distributed to teachers, 5405 teacher users confirmed, and a teacher survey indicating significant benefit with materials reaching on average 500 students each.

Researchers found that the island flying fox is not damaging durian trees; it is helping by pollinating durian flowers. Camera trap footage from Malaysia showed that island flying foxes feed on nectar without damaging flowers and have a positive impact on durian reproductive success. The study, published in *Ecology and Evolution*, involved infrared camera and video traps set up in a durian orchard on Tioman Island, Peninsular Malaysia. The findings add to research on bat ecosystem services, countering negative perceptions of bats, and highlight the potential importance of nectar-eating bats for crop yield and food security amid pollinator declines.

The passage reports that a new European study suggests higher blood levels of linoleic acid, an omega-6 fatty acid found in vegetable oils, nuts, and seeds, are associated with a reduced risk of premature death. The positive effect of linoleic acid was similar regardless of whether participants had a prior history of major chronic diseases. The findings were published in *The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition*.

The lecture reviews optimization and duality via minimizing squared errors, emphasizing that weak duality becomes equality at an optimality condition connecting the primal and dual problems. It also briefly mentions a life-sciences application (gene importance estimation) as an ill-posed derivative-estimation problem in high dimensions.

On Aug. 21, the sun, moon, and Earth will align for a total solar eclipse that will turn day into night and cross the United States coast to coast for the first time in nearly a century. NASA and other groups plan extensive viewing and study, including live video from student-launched high-altitude balloons, observations by satellites, ground telescopes, the International Space Station, and ships and planes. The eclipse will last about 1½ hours overall, with totality lasting just under two minutes in Oregon and up to two minutes and 44 seconds in southernmost Illinois, then shortening in South Carolina. The path of totality will cover about 8,600 miles across 14 states, including National Park locations and national historic trails, with large crowds expected due to an estimated 200 million people within a day’s drive. The partial eclipse will be visible over additional areas in Canada and much of the Americas, and some schools and offices will cancel or close. Events and festivals, along with scientific and public activities from Oregon to South Carolina, are planned, with people also preparing for April 8, 2024’s eclipse.

Canon’s EOS M6 is a mirrorless camera meant for people wanting DSLR-like photo quality to complement a phone. The lecture discusses additive energy \(E(A,B)\) in an Abelian group, defined as the number of quadruples \((a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2)\) with \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\), and relates it to small doubling and additive structure. Large additive energy is shown to follow from small doubling, while the converse fails: a set can have large additive energy due to a structured subset yet still have large sumset \(A+A\). The Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers (BSG) theorem is then presented as the corrective converse: if a set has large additive energy, one can find large subsets with small doubling. A two-set version of BSG is stated and shown to imply the one-set version using Ruzsa triangle inequality.

The proof is reduced to a graph-theoretic version of BSG. One considers a bipartite graph \(G\) between \(A\) and \(B\), defines a restricted sumset using only edges of \(G\), and shows that if the restricted sumset is small and \(G\) has many edges, then large subsets \(A'\subseteq A\), \(B'\subseteq B\) exist such that the full sumset \(A'+B'\) is small. The lecture outlines how to build \(G\) using “popular sums,” uses path-counting, and then focuses on proving the graph result via lemmas: a dependent random choice proof of a path length 2 lemma and an upgrade to a path length 3 lemma. Finally, these path-counting results are used to derive bounds on \(A'+B'\), completing the graphical BSG and hence the original BSG theorem.

Opioid misuse is a worldwide epidemic linked to high overdose and mortality. The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is targeted by drugs of abuse (fentanyl, heroin) and by opioid agonist medications used for opioid use disorder (methadone, buprenorphine), with respiratory depression as a major risk of MOR agonists. Naloxone is a short-acting opioid antagonist used to reverse opioid effects and, with buprenorphine, to manage opioid use disorder. Although MOR pharmacology has been studied using [11C]carfentanil ([11C]CFN) PET imaging, prior studies were largely limited to the brain in humans and non-human primates due to instrumentation limits. The passage describes the first human whole-body neuroreceptor PET imaging study using [11C]CFN with extra-CNS reference regions (aorta and muscle), enabled by long axial field-of-view PET instrumentation (PennPET Explorer). 

The study included healthy English-speaking individuals aged 18–45, with psychiatric/substance use disorders and other exclusion criteria assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and urine drug testing. Participants received T1-weighted MRI for generating volumes of interest. [11C]CFN was produced from [11C]CO2 via specified synthesis steps, with chemical/radiochemical purity assessed by HPLC. PET data were acquired on the PennPET Explorer with low-dose CT for attenuation correction and a 90-minute dynamic PET scan after venous injection of [11C]CFN, then analyzed using PMOD software with spatial normalization to MNI space and specified brain volumes of interest.

Scientists at The Rockefeller University kept a tiny sliver of the cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time, allowing them to observe hearing mechanics in a controlled setting. Using a custom chamber that maintained nutrient flow and native temperature and voltage, the researchers played sounds to gerbil cochlear tissue and observed ion-channel activity in hair bundles and outer hair cell electromotility. They found that a Hopf bifurcation is key to the active process and sound amplification in mammals, showing similar mechanics across animals. The team says this ex vivo approach may support targeted pharmacological testing and improve mechanistic understanding needed for therapies, noting that no drug has yet been approved to restore hearing in sensorineural loss.

NVIDIA Ampere architecture adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 formats to Tensor Cores. BF16 is an alternative to IEEE FP16 and has an 8-bit exponent, 7-bit mantissa, and 1 sign-bit; FP16 and BF16 have been shown to train neural networks in mixed-precision mode matching FP32 results without hyper-parameter adjustment. FP16 and BF16 Tensor Cores provide 16x more math throughput than FP32 in A100 GPUs. Ampere also adds TF32 support so AI training can use tensor cores by default: non-tensor operations use an FP32 datapath, while TF32 tensor cores read FP32 data with reduced internal precision and output standard IEEE FP32. TF32 has an 8-bit exponent, 10-bit mantissa, and 1 sign-bit, and AMP enables mixed-precision AI training with FP16 via a few lines of code changes.

The President thanks Mike and says Mike’s union work is impressive, then discusses support for unions and the goal of rebuilding the “backbone of America.” He describes the American Rescue Plan as an emergency response to save jobs, businesses, and lives, citing vaccination and economic projections. The plan includes transportation and bridge repairs, rail and transit expansion, upgrades to protect infrastructure from climate-related disasters, charging-station and clean-vehicle incentives, replacing lead pipes to provide clean water, expanding affordable high-speed internet, improving power grids, upgrading housing and buildings, expanding home and community-based care, and increasing public research and development. He argues the plan will create millions of jobs and improve competitiveness, including globally against China, and calls for passing the PRO Act. He outlines how the plan would be paid for without raising federal taxes on people making under $400,000, proposing changes to corporate taxes and enforcement. He says infrastructure should be bipartisan, invites Republicans to negotiate, and calls for action to deliver for the American people.

The passage describes functions available on every pin for each device package. It recommends setting PINCM.PF and PINCM.PC in IOMUX to 0 when using non-IOMUX managed functions (such as analog connections), while non-IOMUX managed signals like analog inputs and WAKE inputs can be enabled simultaneously with an IOMUX-managed digital function if there is no contention, which the designer must verify.

The passage describes an automated storage, retrieval, and processing system that moves storage bins to a processing location, where a programmable motion device with an end effector grasps and transfers selected objects into destination bins. The passage describes a timing issue with the XPIC: after the first interrupt acknowledge pulse, the priority encoder should move the highest-priority bit from the IRR to the ISR and clear the IRR bit, but XPIC delays clearing the IRR bit until one clock after the second interrupt acknowledge pulse. As a result, when auto-end-of-interrupt (AEOI) is used, two interrupts may be sent to the CPU instead of one. It also notes that the AEOI bit is bit 1 of ICW4, can only be enabled on the master PIC, and should be enabled only when no nested multilevel interrupt structure is needed. It states that PCs need a nested multilevel interrupt structure and that DOS uses non-specific EOIs.

The passage discusses bear markets, focusing on their characteristics and trading implications. The Supreme Court of Louisiana found the writ not considered because it was untimely filed under La. S. Ct. R. X § 5. Ultra-wide bandgap semiconductors are important for next-generation power electronics, and β-Ga₂O₃ is highlighted for its wide bandgap (4.8 eV), high breakdown electric field (~8 MV/cm), high Baliga figure of merit, and room-temperature plasticity and flexibility. Its use is limited by intrinsically low thermal conductivity and by strains produced during fabrication and operation, which can create nonuniform strain gradients that strongly affect thermal transport and complicate thermal management.

The passage describes a study combining a first-principles-based machine-learning potential with the phonon Boltzmann transport equation and a strain-gradient model to investigate thermal conductivity in β-Ga₂O₃ thin films (10 nm and 100 nm). It finds that thermal conductivity suppression caused by strain gradients (η) at 300 K is stronger than suppression from equivalent uniform strain (ε) under both uniaxial and biaxial cases, and that η reduces k without substantially changing thermal anisotropy ratios, unlike ε. The mechanisms discussed include symmetry breaking and enhanced phonon coupling, which activate previously forbidden scattering channels and expand phonon scattering phase space, with gradient-induced scattering dominating across 0–10 THz.

The methods include training a neuroevolution machine-learning interatomic potential using DFT and AIMD data across temperatures and strain conditions, and solving thermal transport including three-phonon interactions and boundary scattering via suppression functions. The authors conclude that strain gradients are both a design challenge and an opportunity for thermal engineering in β-Ga₂O₃ devices.

Startup fundraising can be stressful, so understanding what investors look for helps businesses present a coherent and attractive offering. Key areas to focus on include return on investment, including equity expectations and terms such as potential further investment and mentorship opportunities. Presenting the founder effectively and having an experienced, proactive team can build investor confidence, with market traction such as revenue or customer satisfaction as supporting evidence. Investors may also look at market opportunities, including industry specialization, emerging markets, and gaps or disruption in saturated sectors. Finally, securing investment requires a detailed business plan with accurate projections, research into competition and market entry, and an understanding of financial implications, including the consequences of missing forecasts.

UCLA researchers Heather Christofk and William Lowry reported in *Nature Cell Biology* a way to activate hair follicle stem cells to promote hair growth. Hair follicle stem cells are usually inactive but activate during hair cycles; failure to activate can cause hair loss associated with factors such as hormonal imbalance, stress, aging, or chemotherapy. The study found hair follicle stem cell metabolism differs from other skin cells, with glucose processed into pyruvate, which can be converted to lactate or sent into mitochondria. Genetically reducing lactate production prevented stem cell activation, while increasing lactate production accelerated it. The team identified two skin-applied drugs in mice: RCGD423, which activates JAK-Stat signaling to increase lactate and drive faster hair growth, and UK5099, which blocks pyruvate entry into mitochondria to force lactate production and accelerate hair growth. The drugs were tested only in preclinical studies and not tested in humans or approved by the FDA; related provisional patent applications were filed.

The passage says Colgate-Palmolive’s recent decline appears to have paused, with Wall Street responding positively to news about a recall and indicating that profit growth has returned. An Argus upgrade raised Colgate’s stock, setting a $72 price target and noting a forward P/E below 20. Analysts expect revenue and profit growth in the next few fiscal years, and the company is described as a long-time dividend payer with annual dividend increases since 1964. Despite these improvements, the passage warns that Colgate’s “no-moat” status and increased competition—particularly from smaller manufacturers using online “virtual shelf space”—pose ongoing risks to the core business and long-term growth potential, arguing that a valuation around 20 times earnings is too high for a no-moat company.

The passage describes the DEBUGSS debug subsystem, which interfaces the ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) two-wire interface to multiple device debug functions, including processor execution and device state debugging, and provides a mailbox system for SWD communication with software through the boot ROM. It lists DEBUGSS key features such as an SWDIO/SWCLK interface compatible with TI and third-party probes, on-chip pullup/pulldown resistors, the ability to disable SWD functions to use SWD pins as GPIO, software-configurable peripheral behavior during processor debug (including freeing or halting selected peripherals), reset and PMCU mode change requests, a mailbox (DSSM), and security features like SWD lockout and password authenticated debugging. It also introduces the memory-mapped FACTORY region containing read-only device capability data and factory trim information, with DEVICEID and USERID address mappings, and notes that revision and identification information appears on the device package top-side marking.

Officials updated the alert level for the AJC Peachtree Road Race shortly after 9 a.m. to Code Red - Dangerous, advising runners to slow down, observe course changes, follow official instructions, and stop if necessary. The passage also notes 11Alive as the official broadcast partner, forecasts dry weather with temperatures in the upper 80s for July 4, and states the 2018 prize purse is $70,000 awarded to American athletes, with top male and female each earning $10,000 and their names placed on the Peachtree Cup.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker said India’s 5.7% GDP growth should not be called a slowdown, arguing it is better than growth in major European economies. His comments came amid domestic criticism that India’s growth slowed to a three-year low in the first quarter ended June due to demonetisation and the implementation of GST. The World Bank President said the slowdown is an “aberration” from temporary disruptions and will correct in coming months, while BJP leader Yashwant Sinha described the economy as a “mess” unlikely to improve before the 2019 general elections and said his article aimed to prompt government course correction.

The professor reviews digital communication as a system with a binary interface between source and channel coding, emphasizing standardization, layering, and that binary interfaces do not lose performance. The discussion then outlines a layered source-coding process: sampling/expansion of analog sources, quantization into a finite set (introducing unavoidable distortion), discrete symbol coding, and binary transmission through a reliable (error-free) channel assumption. 

The lecture focuses on discrete source coding and the goal of mapping a symbol sequence into a binary sequence with unique decodability. It describes fixed-length coding by mapping each of an alphabet of size \(m\) into \(l\)-bit blocks where \(2^l \ge m\), including examples and the idea that symbol meanings do not matter for communication beyond distinguishing possibilities. It covers synchronization assumptions and extends to generalized fixed-length coding by coding blocks of symbols. 

Next, it motivates variable-length coding, where likely symbols get shorter codewords, and explains the need for unique decodability and initial synchronization. Examples are given showing a working and a non-working variable-length code due to concatenation ambiguity. The lecture defines prefix-free codes (no codeword is a prefix of another), represents them with binary trees, and claims prefix-free codes are uniquely decodable via a decoding argument. 

It introduces the Kraft inequality as a necessary and sufficient condition (for prefix-free codes) on codeword lengths using \(\sum 2^{-l} \le 1\), with full codes corresponding to equality. Finally, it formally defines unique decodability, contrasts it with non-prefix-free codes, and then transitions to discrete memoryless sources, defining an IID source model with independent, identically distributed symbol outputs and noting that this model will be studied first before more complex sources.

The lecture’s focus is the economics and business case for green buildings. It reviews the “triple bottom lines” (planet, people, profit) and argues that profit is essential, especially because most city building stock is supplied by the private sector. The class uses a “sandwich story” in which end users’ willingness to pay and investors’ impact/ESG goals push developers and investors to supply greener buildings. The instructor explains how greener buildings can improve cash flow via higher rent and occupancy, lower operational costs, potentially lower risk (e.g., policy, market, physical), and resulting higher net present value (NPV) for owners, which can translate into higher willingness to pay and higher resale prices for developers. Examples from Millennium Partners illustrate how “green” can be marketed for different rationales over time, including job creation, health and wellness, and finally sustainability in the Winthrop Center. The lecture also outlines market mechanisms through three stakeholder groups (tenant, owner, developer) and emphasizes that outcomes vary across ranges rather than guaranteed “win-win” results, supported by studies reporting rent premiums and mixed effects on operational costs. Finally, it introduces market failures that can prevent profitable adoption, starting with information asymmetry and discussing greenwashing and the role of certification (e.g., LEED) in addressing adverse selection.

The passage promotes information about “Total Eclipse Columbia” and explains that on Aug. 21 the moon will gradually move in front of the sun, casting a shadow that crosses the U.S. from West to East. It notes that a total solar eclipse is complete darkness during the day and occurs in the “path of totality,” while only some locations in North America will experience totality. The special is scheduled to air at 7:30 p.m. on WIS News 10, with a mention that mobile users can watch by clicking a link.

The passage describes the “shallow cross” pass concept as a basic route combined with a shallow drag route run from opposite directions. It is intended to stress linebackers by forcing them to choose between dropping to cover the middle route or honoring the drag, and it can be taught as either a simple triangle read for quarterbacks or as a secondary progression from downfield routes. The concept aims to attack the middle of the defense, get the ball out quickly versus blitz, and create opportunities for a tight end to find voids. It is said to perform well against man coverage (via 1-on-1 matchup options), Tampa 2 (with a void at LB level), and Cover 4 (creating a natural triangle read), but it is said to be less effective against Cover 3 due to defensive numbers in flat/hook areas. The passage lists route coaching points and quarterback progression steps, including reading downfield routes first, then transitioning to the shallow cross, and quickly switching to the drag/basic combination if pressured. It also provides two variations: “Bunch X Shallow Cross” with a high-to-low progression and “Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel” focused on quick answers versus pressure. It concludes by mentioning an installation video by Coach Shawn Liotta.

A Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar is patrolling The Tracks at Brea. It has a top speed of 25 mph, 98 miles of battery life per full charge, and a charge time of 6 to 8 hours. The vehicle is used by the downtown liaison officer to patrol the downtown entertainment district and park trails, providing a quicker patrol method than on foot or by bicycle. Introduced at the Centennial Parade and in use for about three weeks, it cost around $21,000 funded by money received from the Air Quality Management District. Brea Police Department Lt. Darrin Devereux said the city monitors amenities to ensure they’re used as intended and to prevent parks from becoming hangouts for people causing problems. The vehicle’s size and capacity are listed, with maximum capacity of 800 pounds and seating for 2, and it has off-road capabilities.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, expanding BG’s exploration and production portfolio in India. The deal covers Enron’s interests in fields and a Gulf of Cambay exploration license, excluding Enron’s Dabhol Power project. Analysts said the assets were acquired at a relatively low price per barrel of oil equivalent, while Enron’s efforts to exit Dabhol were tied to a payment dispute. Separately, consumer advocates warned that Southern California Edison customers could face further rate hikes under a settlement with California regulators, and reports said Enron’s Dabhol Power unit defaulted on a $24 million interest payment to Indian lenders.

Since the mid-1980s, higher education has emphasized learning assessment for credit-bearing courses and programs, largely due to accreditation needs. The passage says less attention has been given to assessing learning in noncredit continuing education, defined as organized activities that do not lead to a degree or credential. It notes that noncredit offerings often end with credentials like badges or certifications, but the literature provides little evidence that other noncredit courses evaluate learning outcomes/competencies. The paper proposes using learning outcome assessment to guide curriculum and improve student learning outcomes.

It discusses setting clear, measurable learning outcomes that fit course length and learner backgrounds, using strategies such as SMART outcomes and collaboration with instructors. It provides examples of learning outcome statements and describes learning outcome-focused surveys, typically common in noncredit education for satisfaction but not usually for assessing learning. The passage recommends adding survey items where learners self-rate achievement of selected learning outcomes and suggests re-administering surveys to monitor effectiveness; for short courses, it highlights retrospective pre-post surveys as an alternative.

For direct assessment, it describes evaluating learner products or performances through practical methods appropriate for shorter program durations, including adding quiz-type questions to end-of-course surveys and having learners complete activities that generate assessable products in medium-duration programs. It also outlines considerations for validity/credibility (using experts or consulting instructors/learners), fairness (via transparency and reflective checks), and ensuring activities/products benefit learners beyond the course. The conclusion frames learning outcomes assessment as a decision-support process and asserts that the provided survey and direct-assessment approaches are feasible and have been used to improve subsequent noncredit professional development.

The passage describes a continuation patent application in the communication field, concerning millimeter-wave (high-frequency band) systems and maximum power exposure (MPE) constraints. It proposes an information sending method and apparatus where a first communication node sends report information to a second communication node; the report includes at least one of first type power parameter information or uplink channel state information. The second communication node receives the report, determines maximum power reduction, and schedules the first communication node to reduce impact on the human body. The passage also outlines variants of what the reported power parameters and channel state information may include (e.g., maximum power reduction, power backoff, power headroom, reference signal and antenna group information, and related indexing/threshold-based triggering), along with corresponding receiving, scheduling, and module-based apparatus implementations. It further provides structural descriptions of a first communication node (e.g., user equipment), a second communication node (e.g., base station), and a storage medium for storing program instructions to implement the sending and reception methods.

The lecture concludes Markov chains with a review of eigenvalues/eigenvectors and then introduces dynamic programming through Markov reward problems. For a Markov chain with transient states and recurrent states, the determinant of a block upper-diagonal matrix factors into the product of determinants for the transient and recurrent blocks, implying that the eigenvalues of the full transition matrix are obtained by combining the eigenvalues from the transient and recurrent submatrices. Eigenvectors can likewise be constructed from left eigenvectors of the recurrent submatrix by padding with zeros.

The lecture then discusses assigning rewards (or costs) to Markov chain states and computing expected aggregate rewards over time, including long-run behavior under ergodicity where expected gain per step approaches a steady-state value independent of the start state. It presents a first-passage-time example by modifying the chain so that a chosen target state becomes a trapping recurrent state, converting the expected time to reach it into a set of linear equations. Finally, it motivates dynamic programming as a method for choosing actions in a finite time-horizon Markov decision process, where actions determine both rewards and transition probabilities. Using Bellman’s backward recursion, it builds optimal expected rewards for one step, two steps, and generally \(n\) steps by maximizing over available actions at each time while using already-computed optimal “reward-to-go” values from later times.

The passage describes the “Power Play,” a gap run play characterized by a backside guard pulling to block a linebacker, along with kick-out and back blocks to create angles and double teams at the point of attack. It says Power can be run from many personnel groups and formations and helps offenses generate yardage by getting multiple blockers to the running lane, offering flexibility with vertical or horizontal double-team coaching choices. The passage lists weaknesses including vulnerability to backside pursuit and penetration through the open gap, and notes that incorrect “point calls” by the center can leave a free backside rusher. It then outlines common blocking rules for Power against 3-4 odd fronts and 4-3 even fronts, followed by two variations: “Diamond Fullhouse,” where an F player arcs to occupy an overhang and affects the kick-out setup, and “Gun Same-Side Power RPO,” which runs Power from formations involving an RPO where the QB may need to throw based on the box count and defensive reactions.

Bill Purswell appealed his conviction for transporting intoxicating liquor, for which he was sentenced to one year in the penitentiary. Officers hid in a field at McElvain’s property, observed people drinking whiskey, saw Purswell approach carrying a jug, and, upon arresting him, found the jug contained whiskey, which was admitted as evidence. Purswell objected, arguing the arrest and evidence resulted from an illegal search without warrants, but the court held that the right to complain about illegal search and seizure is personal to the owner or possessor of the premises, and that the search (if any) was admissible if made contemporaneously with a lawful arrest based on probable cause. The court also held that the court-charge exception must be specific and that the evidence was properly admitted. On rehearing, the court found no jury misconduct shown by an affidavit alleging the jury considered Purswell’s failure to testify and presumed the trial court’s action was justified because evidence on the motion for new trial was not provided. The judgment was affirmed, and the motion for rehearing was overruled.

The passage describes how Enron, led by Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay, rose rapidly from a pipeline company into a major trading firm, with revenues and stock growth. It attributes Enron’s early success to Skilling’s market-focused ideas (such as the “Gas Bank”), rapid expansion into multiple commodities and markets (including communications, broadband, and weather), and a culture emphasizing aggressive performance, high intellectual capital, and intense competition.  

As Enron expanded, the culture became harsher, including forced ranking, paranoia, and inward competition. The company later faced rising criticism and declining stock amid events such as California deregulation problems and setbacks in telecommunications and other ventures. The passage also notes Skilling’s resignation after becoming CEO in February 2001 and Lay’s decision to pursue a “kinder, gentler” culture with more focus on core activities.

The petitioner sought to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by the New York Attorney-General for production of corporate records for a Grand Jury criminal investigation. The Supreme Court denied the petition, finding the subpoena’s scope unduly burdensome only as limited by a concession from the Attorney-General. The court then considered whether an appeal lay from that order and found the State’s cited authorities unavailing. On the merits, the petitioner argued the Attorney-General lacked authority to issue the subpoena, while the Attorney-General relied on subdivision 3 of section 63 of the Executive Law, requiring a request by enumerated officials. The court agreed with the respondent that a sufficient request had been made by the Commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and Markets. The order was affirmed, without costs.

Firefly Aerospace’s Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a test flight at the company’s Texas facility on Monday. The company said it followed safety protocols and that all personnel were safe, and it is assessing damage to its stage test stand with no other facilities impacted. Shares sank nearly 21%, after Firefly debuted on the Nasdaq last month and shares have since pulled back more than 50%. The explosion occurred during a first-stage test flight in Briggs, Texas, and Firefly said it would learn from the test to improve designs.

The South Dakota Board of Regents is preparing to consider closing the jointly operated Capital University Center (CUC) in Pierre. Without a vote, the regents directed central office staff and officials from the state’s two largest universities to bring a plan for “wind-down” of the CUC to their next board meeting Oct. 3-5 at Dakota State University in Madison. The issue was discussed during a three-day planning meeting in Pierre, where regent John Bastian said the board needs to decide what the wind-down would be, and regent Kevin Schieffer argued for action, telling university presidents and other regents that he is tired of delaying.

The passage argues that Arctic security should be understood as a complex, interconnected system shaped by environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors that interact and can produce cascading effects across domains and scales. It uses the Nome port expansion project to illustrate how actions driven by national and economic security can also lead to environmental disruption, cultural tensions, geopolitical shifts, and operational challenges, highlighting the need for systems thinking. The passage then describes systems thinking as an educational framework centered on identifying system components, understanding interactions over time, and moving beyond traditional linear, reductionist approaches. It proposes integrating systems thinking into Arctic security education through interdisciplinary and integrated curricula, scenario-based and interactive learning (e.g., simulations, wargaming, role-playing, concept mapping, and interactive case studies), and assessment methods that emphasize leverage points, anticipatory governance, reflective analysis, and competency-based evaluation. The Systems Thinking Education Model is presented as consisting of core principles, leverage points for educational intervention, and structured learning and assessment strategies, and it is described as suitable for online graduate education using asynchronous modules, digital simulations, interactive tools, and collaborative discussions.

The passage describes LTE/LTE-Advanced architecture and radio operation, including component carrier structures, carrier aggregation, MAC/RLC/PDCP/RRC/physical-layer roles, uplink transmission, and L1/L2 control signaling. It explains semi-persistent scheduling (SPS) and Device-to-Device/Proximity Services (ProSe), including direct discovery/communication over PC5, identity concepts for sidelink, and two D2D resource allocation modes (eNB-scheduled Mode 1 and UE-autonomous Mode 2). For vehicular V2X sidelink, it discusses sensing and radio resource reservation to support semi-persistent transmissions and autonomous resource selection, focusing on measuring/monitoring resources and energy. The “brief summary” then presents improved UE-autonomous radio resource allocation methods: a transmitting UE continuously performs resource sensing to exclude reserved resources and optionally predict energy; it defines a sensing window before data availability and a transmission window after. During allocation, it distinguishes “primary” subframes (where sensing collected full information) from “secondary” subframes (where sensing was not fully possible due to transmission), and it prefers selecting radio resources from primary subframes. It also outlines similar improvements for scheduling assignment transmissions and describes using candidate ranking based on delay and energy prediction, with optional preemption behavior.

On Oct. 29, 2001, Reuters and other outlets reported that Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt rating to Baa2 (two notches above “junk”) and warned it could cut the rating again, contributing to sharp declines in Enron’s stock. Enron said it was in talks with banks to expand or obtain new credit lines to ease financial concerns, after drawing about $3 billion in credit lines to address commercial paper. Reports also described concerns about Enron’s partnerships and related-party transactions being examined by the SEC, Europe energy firms reducing or restricting dealings due to credit worries, and analysts expecting lenders to demand harsher terms and collateral. Moody’s also reviewed Enron’s commercial paper ratings and noted difficulties in rolling over commercial paper tied to deteriorating financial flexibility.

The passage is an introduction to a course on cellular-structured materials, which are porous and typically have low solid volume fractions (less than 30%). It covers different types of cellular solids—honeycombs, foams, medical materials such as trabecular bone and tissue engineering scaffolds, and cellular structures in nature including wood, cork, plant tissues, and various structural examples like sandwich structures and density gradients.
