The course outlines topics such as processing, microstructure modeling, mechanisms of deformation and failure, and applications including lightweight sandwich panels, energy absorption, thermal insulation, medical modeling (including osteoporosis), cell–scaffold interactions, and natural-material structure-function relationships. The instructor also describes class projects, provides references to two books, discusses examples and uses of honeycombs and foams (including catalytic converter honeycombs and foam properties), and begins a section on processing honeycombs and foams, explaining multiple fabrication methods for honeycombs (expansion, corrugation, extrusion, rapid prototyping, casting, and bio-carbon templating) and polymer foams and metal foams (including several named techniques). It concludes with a brief personal background from the instructor about her education and career.

The passage describes “special 5-minute segments” in soccer matches when goals are more likely to be scored for or against a team. These segments include the first five minutes of the match, the five minutes after a goal (including after a penalty kick), the five minutes after a penalty kick is saved or missed, the five minutes after a bad foul or dangerous play, the five minutes before halftime (including added time), the first five minutes of the second half, the last five minutes of the match (including added time), and the start and near the end of extra time. It says these patterns are linked to team and player psychology, such as excitement, lack of mental readiness, storming ahead after scoring, complacency, upset and poor defending, revenge, and adjustments when time is running out. Coaches are urged to prepare for these effects and remind teams, with the common reminder after a goal being “No letdown!”

The passage discusses Q3 2025 municipal (muni) credit commentary, noting that munis are generally viewed as a safe “flight to quality” asset class. It states that the Fed lowered short-term interest rates in September, citing slowdown in job growth and mixed inflation readings. It also says some municipalities have received upgrades due to better-funded reserves, which may reflect budgeting and/or population or economic activity growth, and suggests this quarter may mark a turn in muni credit quality. The passage then includes biographical information about David Kotok and lists several separate headlines and ETF or stock references.

The passage says job hunting can cause emotional highs and lows, especially when searching in an unfamiliar market after moving to a new country. It quotes Ivy Chiu of RBC recommending that newcomers build their network before starting their job search. Tips include starting the search before arriving in Canada using sites like workopolis.com, finding local workshops offered by newcomer associations (example: ACCES Employment in Toronto) for resume help and interview practice, signing up for internships and volunteer opportunities to gain experience and network, cross-checking and updating credentials for specific Canadian fields, and building English or French proficiency through language courses. It also suggests seeking associations that may offer language or related services free or at a discount and visiting rbc.com/newcomers for more advice.

Treetops is a care home in walking distance of Keynsham town centre. Purpose-built in 1992, it provides accommodation for elderly people with dementia in one of three family-sized units, each with its own lounge and dining room. It offers communal and quiet areas for relatives and friends, and involves residents and families in planning care through a family support group. Each resident has a named carer and receives individual support, with activities organised by an activity therapist and care staff inside and outside the home. The passage advises checking whether a care home fits individual circumstances and notes that service information is provided by the care home, with responsibility for errors not taken by the page.

The passage reports on developments in currency and macro markets, including Trump’s remarks at a joint press conference with Trudeau that trade issues between the US and Canada are “much less severe” than with Mexico and that changes are coming without an overhaul. It notes USD/CAD falling to about 1.3060 after the comments and highlights expectations for upcoming events: Yellen’s semi-annual testimony and China’s January CPI and PPI releases, with forecasts for CPI to rise to 2.4% and PPI to 6.5%. It also mentions a Kuroda speech at 0430 GMT and market speculation that he may shift away from yield curve control.

The passage presents “An American Soccer Player’s Creed” for soccer players to follow a tactical philosophy. It includes rules such as knowing the ball’s location and keeping eyes on it, maintaining communication with teammates and talking to a coach about injuries or possible concussion, avoiding actions like throwing-in errors, putting down teammates, inciting opponents or reacting to trash talk, kicking balls out of bounds on corner kicks, and retaliating after fouls. It also emphasizes proper movement with play, creating passing opportunities, awareness of opponents, giving full effort without committing stupid fouls, learning from mistakes, continuous play until the whistle, following the Laws of the Game, and honoring fair play and sportsmanlike behavior on and off the field.

The passage describes planned measurements, assessment timing, and study conduct for the DAWN-plasma randomized, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It outlines ethical review and informed consent procedures, investigator notification of serious or unexpected adverse events, and compliance with Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice. The study aims to evaluate convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus best supportive care alone, including a primary endpoint of % of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 and multiple secondary endpoints related to clinical status, mechanical ventilation, survival at 30 and 90 days, and additional safety and laboratory measures. Inclusion criteria require consent, age ≥18, confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, and specific clinical or imaging evidence, while exclusion criteria include mechanical ventilation at or before randomization and certain prior treatments or conditions. The protocol specifies convalescent plasma dosing (800–1000 mL in 4 doses) with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and the second dose 24–36 hours after the first infusion, with restrictions on neutralizing antibody titers. Randomization uses a computerized system with a 2:1 allocation, and blinding is maintained for the trial statistician until database lock. The passage also describes study monitoring, data handling via RedCap, use of different central laboratories, and related quality control and training documentation.

Digital technologies have transformed business by enabling global customer reach and new business models, requiring organizations to change their processes to benefit from electronic business. E-commerce includes multiple transaction types (e.g., B2B, B2C, G2G). Online marketplaces rely on search engines, directories, aggregators, affiliates, blogs, and company websites, and success requires more than an online portal, including strategy, infrastructure, digital marketing, e-supply chain management, e-procurement, e-CRM, and effective (re)intermediation decisions. This paper focuses on website usability to foster customer satisfaction, defining usability as effectiveness, efficiency, and user satisfaction.

The study evaluates usability implications for e-business applications in Saudi Arabia, an emerging e-business market with reported online shopping adoption and projected growth. A cross-sectional experiment with two student cohorts (26 and 39 participants) assessed 8 popular Saudi business websites (retailers and booking websites) using a questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content. Findings presented in tables indicate generally positive ratings in many areas, but lower scores for issues such as links/menu problems, orphan pages, sitemap navigation, inconsistent Arabic-English interface language, certain design consistency elements, missing contact information, absence of last update dates, and errors or omissions in content. Validity checks using Cronbach’s alpha showed weaker internal validity for group 1 than group 2, with converging results. The paper concludes that improving internal navigation, language consistency, layout and icon labeling, and providing complete contact and update information could enhance user satisfaction and potentially improve customer acquisition, retention, and revenue, while suggesting further long-term quantitative research.

Voters in the Blair school district narrowly failed to approve a $250,000 transportation bond issue, receiving 111 votes in favor and 80 against (58.76%), below the 60% super-majority required by state law. The bond would have purchased three 72-passenger buses to replace currently leased buses. Results were also listed for municipal races in Altus and Walters and school board races in several districts, including Caddo, Comanche, and Cotton counties.

The passage describes Supreme Court justices debating whether Delaware’s procedural requirements designed to limit medical malpractice litigation should apply in federal court. Justice Elena Kagan argued the Delaware rules conflict with the Federal Rules’ notice-pleading system by effectively forcing plaintiffs to prove their case before it begins. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson and Justice Sonia Sotomayor highlighted specific differences, noting Delaware’s requirement for a separate affidavit to initiate a malpractice lawsuit and delaying the filing of an answer until after the affidavit is filed, unlike federal rules. Frederick Yarger argued federal courts should not ignore a state statute entirely if only some parts conflict, but other justices criticized this approach as requiring courts to “pick and choose” and rewrite state law. The passage concludes that several justices likely will reject Delaware’s procedures, but it is unclear how the full court will rule since several justices said little during argument.

Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins told a parliamentary committee that household debt relative to disposable income should gradually stabilize over the coming years, though it may take time since the buildup took many years. She cited a latest debt ratio of 170.4% (about $1.70 in debt per $1 of disposable income), down slightly from 170.5% in the previous quarter, and said credit growth for mortgages and other household debt is slowing while labour income rises. Wilkins added that the debt buildup included asset purchases such as housing, contributing to higher net worths. She said the central bank has assessed risks of consumer debt to gauge how quickly it can raise interest rates, noting that it has raised rates three times since last July. Bank of Canada governor Stephen Poloz said high household debt likely makes households 50% more sensitive to interest rate changes.

The passage discusses the focus on reaching the net by getting pucks into scoring areas and taking shots, including trying to beat a large goalie. It notes that a two-day break allowed time to think, but practice resumed the day before, helping the team get their legs going after a disappointing loss. The speaker says the team has regrouped and is ready to play tonight, aiming to score the first goal.

The passage includes excerpts from a May 6, 1980 Wall Street Journal interview in which Reagan responds to reporters about concerns that Iran might move toward Soviet influence and says the United States should recognize this would be a serious threat to the Middle East and U.S. security. It also summarizes Reagan’s July 17, 1980 Republican National Convention acceptance speech, where he links peace and security, prioritizes protecting Americans, and states the U.S. is prepared to negotiate but will not allow threats to freedom to dictate the future. The passage further notes that the full acceptance speech was printed on July 18 and includes the beginning of a separate address emphasizing “PEACE” and defense capability.

The passage provides guidelines for breaking basketball presses by spreading the floor, bypassing and eliminating defenders, closing distance before passing, using a slow-to-quick tempo, advancing the ball with sharp short passes, creating leads, and attacking outnumbered situations while maintaining ball care through controlled dribbling and no off-the-dribble passing. It advises analyzing the press type, taking advantage of weaknesses, crashing the boards, maintaining defensive balance, and practicing outlet/inbound passing reads. It includes “don’ts” for press breaks (e.g., don’t receive with back to basket, don’t dribble into trap zones, avoid one-handed and bounce passes, don’t telegraph passes, and don’t hurry), discusses training and coaching objectives, and recommends implementing the whole-part-whole teaching method with progressive breakdown drills up to live practice. It also briefly describes the value of defensive pressure to disrupt fast break and early offense, potentially leading to steals and baskets.

Spin defects in wide band-gap semiconductors are used for nanoscale quantum sensing, with the diamond nitrogen vacancy (NV) center being prominent due to long coherence times and efficient room-temperature optical spin polarization. Integrating sensors with target systems is difficult with NV centers because processing diamond is challenging and NV coherence degrades near surfaces from charge trapping. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) defects remain effective near surfaces and can be heterogeneously integrated using pick-and-place fabrication, including studies where ensembles of boron-vacancy defects (V−B) are integrated with magnetic platforms.

The V−B center in hBN is a radiative spin triplet (S = 1) with ground- and excited-state zero-field splittings of about 3.5 GHz and 2.1 GHz. Optical pumping initializes spins, and room-temperature electron spin relaxation and coherence times are about 20 μs (T1) and 100 ns (T2), with dynamical decoupling extending T2. V−B is studied as an alternative to NV for near-surface sensing because it can enable controlled interactions with adjacent 15N nuclear spins. Strong hyperfine coupling allows polarization and control of three neighboring 15N nuclei via optical pumping and electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR).

In an isotopically enriched h10B15N crystal, the coherent control of 15N nuclear spins adjacent to V−B is demonstrated using ENDOR. Electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling enables selective addressing of the four nuclear spin states formed by three identical 15N nuclei, producing distinct transition energies and enhancing the nuclear g-factor, leading to an increase in nuclear Rabi frequency by roughly a factor of 116 compared with pure nuclear spin states. Nuclear Rabi oscillations show a coherence time exceeding 10 μs. However, the work also observes an unexpected loss of nuclear polarization when the defect is optically pumped, which the authors tentatively attribute to relaxation effects associated with an optical excited electronic state (mainly the 3E′′ state).

Overall, the three nearest-neighbor 15N nuclear spins around V−B are presented as a controllable quantum resource, enabling selective multi-nuclear-state addressing, coherent manipulation, and potentially improved sensing performance via long nuclear coherence times and enhanced driving strength.

Amid concerns about Jake Browning’s inconsistency while he leads the Bengals in place of Joe Burrow, speculation resurfaced that the Bengals could consider signing former Cincinnati starter Andy Dalton. Writer Breech noted Dalton’s Bengals history, including five straight playoff appearances after starting his career in 2011, and his prior connection to head coach Zac Taylor, with Dalton starting 13 games for Taylor in 2019. Breech also referenced Dalton’s more recent performance with the Panthers, including Week 3 of the 2024 season when he threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns. Dalton is under contract through 2026 and has mostly served as a backup, and Browning has thrown for 506 yards with three touchdowns and five interceptions through three games.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018. The filing includes unaudited consolidated financial statements showing total revenues of $3,408,751 (in thousands) and a net loss of $784,627 (in thousands) for the three months ended March 31, 2018, along with consolidated balance sheet information as of March 31, 2018. It also describes revenue recognition policies under ASC 606, including the adoption impact on automotive sales, automotive leasing, and energy generation and storage, and provides detailed discussions of automotive regulatory credits and leasing programs. The notes further cover items such as income taxes, net loss per share, restricted cash, concentration risks, warranties, recent accounting pronouncements (including expectations to adopt the FASB leases standard on January 1, 2019), goodwill and intangible assets, fair value measurements, inventory, solar energy systems, property and equipment, other long-term liabilities, customer deposits, convertible and long-term debt, and equity incentive plans.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2016. The filing includes unaudited consolidated financial statements, including balance sheet, statements of operations, comprehensive loss, and cash flows, and provides notes covering items such as revenue recognition, resale value guarantees, leases, warranties, stock-based compensation, debt and convertible notes, fair value measurements, legal proceedings, and subsequent events. The consolidated balance sheet shows total assets of $11,868,952 (in thousands) as of June 30, 2016. For the three and six months ended June 30, 2016, total revenues were $1,270,017 and $2,417,065, respectively, and net loss was $(293,188) and $(575,455), respectively. The document also contains management’s discussion and analysis describing Tesla’s business, production and delivery targets, capital expenditures, and trends in revenues and costs, including revenue and gross profit figures and explanations for changes.

The passage describes an electronic edition of the *Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS)* series (established in 1861), produced by the U.S. Department of State Office of the Historian. It explains features of the ebook edition, including offline access, full-text search, bookmarking, and note-taking, and notes efforts to preserve fidelity to the printed edition by using persistent document numbers for citations. It also includes a “Message of the President” to the Senate and House of Representatives (dated May 2018) advocating bills to prohibit corporations from contributing to campaign expenses and to grant the government a right of appeal in criminal cases on questions of law, citing examples involving conspiracy and rebates and arguing that lack of appeal blocks resolution of conflicting decisions.

The socket base and cover are made from UL 94 V-0 rated Liquid Crystal Polymer, with a black base and natural or ivory cover. The socket cover thickness (including a 0.30 mm pocket recess) must not exceed 1.17 mm, and cover flatness must remain under 0.25 mm before and after SMT reflow and after environmental and mechanical testing. A removable tape or plastic cover overlays the pin holes to enable pick-and-place with a vacuum nozzle, and it must not outgas during solder reflow or leave residue before package pin insertion. Socket markings molded into the cover include “SOCKET 940,” a locked/unlocked directional designator, and a triangular orientation symbol, plus an approved UL symbol visible after PCB solder mounting; lot traceability must also remain readable after mounting. No lubricants may be present on contact mating areas when shipped.

For PCB attachment, the contact base is a high-strength copper alloy, fully plated with minimum 1.27-µm nickel and gold plating on the mating area (minimum 0.76 µm over nickel). SMT solder balls use tin and lead (63/37 ± 5%) with 0.76 mm diameter and require a solder barrier feature to prevent wicking; the socket 940 solder ball field must meet 0.20 mm co-planarity. A stainless steel actuation lever on the cam box provides mechanical advantage; with the lever open, insertion/extraction forces are conceptually zero and must not exceed 2 kgf, and with the lever closed the package extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin. The actuation/de-actuation force must be less than 3.6 kgf, and pins must displace less than 1.0 mm during actuation. The socket must maintain electrical and mechanical integrity after 50 cycles, with no missing/malformed/damaged/misaligned solder balls or missing/damaged contacts and no cracks or flashing; the lever and latch must not be damaged, malformed, or missing. The contact current rating is 1.5 A per contact with less than 30°C rise. Electrical tests include LLCR (initial and final must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact when mated with Kovar pins), inductance and capacitance limits, differential impedance and propagation delay/skew requirements, dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac, and insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ.

The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Department of Education appealed a Commonwealth Court decision holding that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (“Act 109”) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The Department argued that Act 109 was fully declared unconstitutional in *Lemon v. Kurtzman*, that its provisions were not severable, that later legislation impliedly repealed it, and that it could not be constitutionally administered if enforced only for nonsectarian schools. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court rejected these arguments and held that Act 109 is constitutional and severable, and thus enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court’s order requiring processing of the First School’s application for aid, after the Department had denied it based on *Lemon*. The Court also held that there was no excessive entanglement when the Department determines whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian and concluded that Act 109 had not been repealed by subsequent legislation. EAGEN, J., dissented.

The device uses separate power supplies AVDD and DVDD: internal circuits use AVDD, while DVDD powers the digital interface. AVDD and DVDD should be set independently within the permissible range. For power-supply decoupling, AVDD is decoupled to AGND with at least 10µF and 1µF capacitors per supply pin, with the 1µF placed close to the pins; DVDD uses at least a 10µF decoupling capacitor placed very close to provide high-frequency digital switching current, improving PSRR. Power saving includes two programmable low-power modes: NAP mode, entered at the end of conversion when CONVST/CS is held high and exited by a falling edge, and deep power-down (PD) mode at very low throughput rates, entered by setting the PWRDN bit and powering down all analog blocks while keeping the interface active and register contents retained.

After UNC’s 38–10 blowout loss to Clemson, head coach Bill Belichick said the game was tilted by big plays early and that his team failed to recover. He cited Clemson’s passing for 399 yards and admitted UNC gave up about 200 passing yards on five plays due to not looking for the ball. Belichick also pointed to UNC’s offense struggling, including a 2-of-11 third-down conversion rate, and said problems on earlier downs led to difficult third downs. He took responsibility for three illegal formation penalties and said he would not make evaluations about whether a program rebuild is steeper than expected, adding the team will keep grinding. Despite the loss, he praised the team’s effort and said they need to do what they are doing better.

The passage says Moscow denies responsibility for the poisoning of Sergei Skripal and his daughter, Yulia, and claims the blame is unprovable. It reports that the UK says Russia violated the Chemical Weapons Convention and used nerve agent attacks on British soil, with evidence of Russia producing and stockpiling Novichok, including photos of expansion of a poison-making complex. It also quotes Vladimir Putin rejecting blame as “nonsense” and offering cooperation if the other side wants it. The passage argues the West should increase sanctions and pursue hidden Russian assets, noting a new U.S. law to identify them and the need for additional legal changes in Britain and America to close money-laundering loopholes.

The passage introduces topological quantum matter, highlighting topologically protected boundary states arising from bulk-boundary correspondence and their robustness and unidirectional propagation. It notes that quantum entanglement and interference are important for quantum communication, computation, and metrology, and that topological systems can protect entanglement, including Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference of topological edge states.

To address the largely unexplored case of non-Abelian-topology-mediated entanglement and interference, the authors propose a periodically modulated one-dimensional multi-chain platform based on a time-dependent interchain symmetry and inversion symmetry. They first study a double-coupled SSH chain with two branches of edge states whose eigenvalues swap after one period, demonstrating braiding (Abelian) of two edge-state pairs. Using symmetry-protected adiabatic evolution, they show controllable particle transfer between chains with a tunable 0-to-1 ratio set by accumulated dynamical phase.  

They then extend the scheme to a triple-coupled SSH system with three branches. Here, the edge-state eigenvalues exhibit cyclic swapping, leading to non-Abelian braiding where the final state depends on braiding order. This enables non-Abelian topological transport among three chains with tunable ratios governed by dynamical phases.  

Finally, they demonstrate non-Abelian HOM interference by generating spatially entangled two-particle NOON states. With 50:50 splitting, the HOM process produces a NOON state on one chain or another depending on the braiding operator order, and the resulting target-state fidelity reaches about 0.995. The article concludes by summarizing the observed twisted spectrum, braiding-dependent outcomes, tunable transport, and the extension of these ideas toward experimental feasibility and potentially bulk-state braiding.

Speedy grew over four decades and floated on the stock market in March 1999. Since Russell Down became chief executive in summer 2015, the company has improved profits, reduced net debt, and returned to acquisitions after a profit warning and declining performance. Down describes earlier operational and financial challenges, including unreliable asset information due to an IT upgrade, loss of focus on smaller customers, backfired cost-efficiency changes that created a testing backlog, and poor product availability. He says his strategy has focused on customers, transformed the company culture, tightened operating costs, improved product availability, and increased stakeholder support, including staff engagement surveys and customer surveys. Speedy has made acquisitions in the powered access marketplace (Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited) and expects revenue and cost synergies, while Down states the company is in a financially strong position to deliver profitable growth.

Mastitis is described as the most costly disease in the dairy industry, with each clinical case costing more than $400 and harming future milk output and cow comfort. It is commonly treated with antibiotics, which can kill bacteria but do not regenerate damaged mammary tissue, and concerns include antimicrobial resistance and long-term teat harm. Researchers at Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine, Gerlinde Van de Walle and Daryl Nydam, are studying alternative stem cell–derived therapies. In a March 16 paper in *Scientific Reports*, they examine how secretions from bovine mammary stem cells may encourage healing and regrowth while helping eliminate harmful bacteria. They report that secreted factors support blood vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and include antimicrobial peptides. They also suggest these factors could complement antibiotics by producing antibiotic-like effects and being more effective against toxins from gram-negative bacteria. They plan to test whether the therapy works in cows with mastitis.

Clark County schools are deciding at the school level how to use new state funding aimed at students learning English who also live in poverty. The Nevada Legislature approved a weighted funding formula that provides $1,200 per student for students scoring in the bottom 25 percent on state tests and who are either learning English or living in poverty, and excludes students attending schools already receiving state Zoom or Victory funding. At Garside Junior High School in Las Vegas, about 1,200 students are receiving more than $450,000, with the school planning how to spend the money; teacher Kimberly Ivanick said it could expand after-school tutoring and increase students’ access to technology. Garside is among schools across Nevada receiving a $36 million allocation, with Clark County receiving more than $34 million. Schools will track the spending separately in their budgets and analyze whether the funding improves student achievement.

Hyundai Motor Co. and Kia Motors Corp. said they have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system on a 14-kilometer road stretch with seven intersections in Hwaseong, south of Seoul, to advance autonomous driving technology. The system enables vehicles to exchange real-time information with the road, signal lights, other cars, and pedestrians, using special signal relay stations and closed-circuit TVs. The companies plan detailed research to verify the system’s validity and to gather information by the end of the year to make improvements. They said data and know-how will be used to make the system operational for a state infrastructure project enabling vehicle-to-vehicle highway communication in 2020.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Saturday’s Super Netball grand final is unlike anything she has experienced. The 29-year-old Sunshine Coast Lightning will play Greater Western Sydney at the Brisbane Entertainment Centre after a week of hype, with increased media, fan attention, training intensity, and the chance to win the national league title. Bassett has had a fortnight to wait for the match, leading to sleepless nights but also giving her time to “take it in.” She has not previously played a national grand final. She credits Geva Mentor and Laura Langman for helping prepare. Mentor, the Lightning goalkeeper, is expected to contain a dangerous Giants offence and likely face Kristina Brice, a 196cm goal shooter, while Mentor is 190cm. To prepare for Brice’s height, Lightning trained against Junior Levi, a 215cm player from the Queensland men’s team.

The passage transmits to the Senate, for ratification, a treaty of annexation concluded on February 14, 1893 between the U.S. Secretary of State John W. Foster and commissioners representing the Hawaiian Islands. It states that the provisional treaty does not detail issues arising from annexation and that the Hawaiian commissioners consent to leaving adjustment of such questions to the United States. The sender says the Administration encouraged Hawaiian independence while ensuring protection and stability, and that it did not promote the overthrow of the monarchy, attributing it to Queen Liliuokalani’s reactionary and revolutionary policy, which endangered U.S. and foreign interests and civil administration. The restoration of the Queen is described as undesirable or impossible, and the sender argues the U.S. influence should increase. It presents only two options—U.S. protectorate or full annexation—and supports full annexation as adopted in the treaty. The passage claims no government protests have been heard and that foreign representatives acknowledged the provisional government. It also argues for prompt Senate action, stating peace and good order would be secured until Congress legislates a permanent form of government, which should be just and liberal toward natives and residents.

The passage explains the Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by Welles Wilder and widely used by traders. RSI is an oscillator that measures the magnitude of gains and losses over n days (maximum 100, minimum 0) and is used to identify overbought and oversold conditions: readings above typically indicate overbought and below indicate oversold. The article presents an RSI formula and describes using RSI with backtesting, emphasizing that RSI often works best on mean-reverting securities—especially stocks—and usually requires additional criteria, filters, or a second indicator to improve results. It discusses settings such as short RSI time frames (with a “best setting” claimed between 2–6 days), typical thresholds (e.g., buy below 15 and sell above 85 for short time frames), and notes that daily bars are generally preferred. Examples and backtest results are provided for different strategies, including strategies using RSI(2), longer RSI (e.g., RSI(10) and RSI(30)), and combining long- and short-term RSI. The passage also covers divergence between price and RSI as a commonly cited signal but says it is established after the fact and has limited practical use. It mentions variations such as Connors RSI and Cutler’s RSI and states that RSI can be used on other bar types, but daily bars are reported as best.

The passage explains how soccer play restarts when a defending team touches the ball over its own end line: the attacking team takes a corner kick. It emphasizes the importance of understanding Law 17 and outlines a progression for teaching corner-kick offense to young players, including demonstrating the law’s fundamental requirements, practicing right-footed/right-side kicks, and then introducing a corner-kick set play with designated roles (corner taker, receiver, cover man). Players are rotated through positions, taught left-footed/left-side options, and then coaches may assign specific players for game preparation. The passage also suggests adding defenders (passive then active) and possibly additional passing/offside discussion, and provides game tips about using the correct corner arc and waiting for referee acknowledgment.

The passage discusses Supreme Court plans for October Term 2025 and argues that the term’s religious-freedom docket is unlikely to feature landmark “culture war” controversies. It focuses on *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety*, set for oral argument next month, which centers on technical questions about whether RLUIPA authorizes money damages against government employees. It describes Damon Landor, a Rastafarian prisoner whose dreadlocks were previously accommodated but who was later forcibly shaved by prison officials shortly before his release. It states that this conduct violated RLUIPA, and that lower courts disagreed on whether RLUIPA allows money damages, with the Supreme Court agreeing to hear the case. The passage then critiques narratives that Supreme Court religious-freedom decisions are polarized or that religious-freedom protections primarily benefit majorities, and it argues that religious-freedom claimants are often diverse. It concludes by asserting that religious freedom “means religious freedom for all” and that *Landor* highlights the importance of the right beyond a technical remedy question.

San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights after attempting to pull over a person around 12:30 p.m. Sunday. The suspect fled and the pursuit ended when he crashed into fences at Central Elementary School and a nearby fire station, damaging the school’s main gates. He ran through the fence, then through the fire-rescue facility’s fence, where it became stuck in his car wheel. Armed with a gun, he ran off, but was arrested a block away near 41st Street and University Avenue by Interstate 15. No further information was available.

The passage describes documents and actions taken by President Truman in late 1945, and outlines parts of the implementation of American foreign policy, focusing on the Department of State. It mentions resignation and appointments within the Department of State and related diplomatic roles, including the acceptance of Edward R. Stettinius Jr.’s resignation, the commissioning of James F. Byrnes as Secretary of State, and the appointment of Dean G. Acheson as Under Secretary of State. It also covers Truman’s Executive Order 9608 (Aug. 31, 1945), which terminated the Office of War Information and transferred its international and foreign information functions to the Department of State, along with subsequent statements and broadcasts about international information policy. In addition, it notes Truman’s Executive Order No. 9621, signed Sept. 20, 1945, transferring Research and Intelligence activities from the Office of Strategic Services to the Department of State, abolishing the O.S.S. effective Oct. 1, and directing the Secretary of State to lead development of a coordinated foreign intelligence program for federal agencies.

The passage reports background information and results from a retrospective analytical study of 671 traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients admitted between 07/01/2017 and 17/12/2018. It states that gender is suggested to play an important role in post-TBI outcomes and severity (including severity measured by the Glasgow coma scale in prior studies). TBI is described as including contusion, concussion, penetrating injury, and anoxic injury, with risk influenced by factors such as age, hormonal status, and poor health care practice. Classical causes listed include car accidents, falls, sport-associated injuries, and domestic violence, which is described as a primary cause of TBI and related outcomes.  

In the study sample, 212 patients were female (31.59%) and 459 male (68.40%); mean age was 46.016 years, and mean hospitalization days were reported as ranging from 0.00 to 49.00 (mean with standard error provided). The most frequent reported cause of TBI was domestic accidents (43.81%), followed by alcohol-related brain injury (20.71%) and motor vehicle injury (16.54%). Conservative therapy was required for 668 patients (99.55%). Surgical treatment was observed in 198 patients (39.91%), with multiple types of procedures described. The passage also reports associations with residence (village residents at increased risk), hospitalization duration, and age differences between men and women, and includes a discussion and conclusion that domestic accidents were the most frequent cause for both men and women and that gender plays a crucial role in severity and incidence rate of post-TBI outcomes and complications.

The passage describes Blackwell architecture features focused on power management, faster clock changes, and low-latency sleep. It explains advanced clock gating that rapidly shuts off clock trees, memory power management using GDDR7’s fast-wakeup clocking with the ability to gate the entire memory clock tree, and new separate voltage rails for independently powering GPU cores and the memory system. It also covers accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks to dynamic workloads 1000x faster than previous architectures, enabling performance within a power budget and power savings during short idle gaps, and low power states that enter sleep faster, including the deepest sleep state being 10x faster than Ada. The passage then discusses DLSS 4 technologies (multi-frame generation and transformer-based neural models) and several “neural shaders” for developer-created neural rendering, including neural materials, neural texture compression, neural radiance cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces, along with high-level GPU specification details for Blackwell-based GB202 (GB203 and GB205 also mentioned) and GeForce RTX 50 series products. It concludes with NVIDIA legal/disclaimer text and trademark/copyright information.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a hydrotope compound with hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts like surfactants, and it can dissolve in water in powder or liquid form. It increases solubility of less soluble organic matter, lowers cloud point of aqueous products, promotes compatibility of ingredients in multicomponent systems, and moderates viscosity. It is used as a solubilizer and cloud point depressor in applications including wax cleaners, air mist drilling, laundry washing, drilling and stimulation fluids, anti-caking agents, and coupling agents in powdered detergents, as well as in metal processing, oilfield applications, and hydrogen sulfide scavengers. The market is affected by raw material costs and volatility, and heavy exposure may cause eye and respiratory irritation and other health hazards. Demand is expected to be driven by increasing industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies, while declining R&D and raw material price volatility may hamper the market. The liquid form had a major share in 2015 and is expected to dominate, and household applications had a major share in 2015 and are expected to be dominant, with industrial and institutional also expected to grow moderately.

U.S. stocks fell about 2 percent on Monday, led by a selloff in technology stocks after Facebook shares dropped 7.1% on reports that a political consultancy linked to President Donald Trump’s campaign gained inappropriate access to data on more than 50 million users. The Dow shed nearly 400 points, the Nasdaq slid 2.09%, and the S&P technology index fell 2.5%, with tech stocks set for their worst one-day percentage declines since early February. Trading also reflected broader concerns about data privacy and security, worries about a potential global trade war ahead of a two-day G20 meeting, increased political uncertainty, and expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates Wednesday; all 11 major S&P sectors were lower and volatility rose.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January, creating a law firm called FBT Gibbons with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. Frost Brown Todd will gain new Northeast offices, including in New York and New Jersey. The merger’s first focus will be on integration, and leadership will include Robert Sartin as chairman, with Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo as co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd had more than 650 lawyers in 18 offices and $336.5 million in gross revenue, while Gibbons had $115 million in revenue; both had similar profits per lawyer, with Gibbons having higher revenue per lawyer.

Stephen Hawking has died, according to a family spokesman. His children said he was a great scientist and extraordinary man. Hawking was a leading theoretical physicist whose book “A Brief History of Time” became an international bestseller. Despite being diagnosed with ALS at 21 and later facing pneumonia that left him breathing through a tube, he continued working, appeared on television, and married for a second time. He held the Lucasian Professor role at Cambridge and pursued a unified theory to resolve contradictions between relativity and quantum mechanics, though later suggested it might not exist. Hawking also appeared in popular media, was the subject of the 2014 film “The Theory of Everything” starring Eddie Redmayne, and was credited by some colleagues with increasing public enthusiasm for science, while his achievements and longevity showed that severe disabilities need not prevent people from living.

The passage describes multiple attempts to conclude a U.S.–Hawaiian reciprocity treaty. An earlier treaty with stipulations for annuities and admission of the Kingdom as a State of the Union was objected to by this Government but failed after King Kamehameha III died and his successor opposed the project. A reciprocity treaty was concluded in Washington on July 20, 1855 by Mr. Marcy and Judge Lee, but it failed to be ratified. After civil war delays and occasional annexation references, efforts resumed in 1867: Mr. McCook was instructed to revive the 1855 reciprocity treaty on terms more liberal to the United States, and a new reciprocity treaty was concluded at San Francisco on May 21, 1867 by Mr. McCook and Mr. Harris, with presidential approval but failed Senate ratification. Annexation concerns influenced actions, with Seward advising that if annexation conflicted with reciprocity, annexation was to be preferred. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna contributed to delays in Hawaiian ratification. The treaty was ratified July 30, 1867, but the U.S. Senate later rejected it when it finally acted on June 1, 1870.

The speaker takes the presidential oath and asks God for wisdom to restore harmony and protect free institutions. He says he will not seek reelection and will govern only to serve the country faithfully. He describes the recent presidential contest as having calmed after the people’s constitutional decision, and he supports Congress leaving the question of domestic slavery in U.S. Territories to the people (“popular sovereignty”). He notes disagreement about when residents decide this, but says it is judicial and pending before the Supreme Court, and that the government must protect residents’ right to vote without foreign interference. He argues that agitation over slavery should end, warning it could endanger the safety of those where slavery exists, and he calls for suppressing it. He then warns against calculating the Union only by material value, arguing that trade and prosperity would suffer from disunion and that Providence will preserve the Union. Next, he emphasizes preventing corruption and says the nation’s financial condition is unusual due to a large surplus, which can lead to extravagant spending and speculation; he proposes using the surplus for national purposes such as paying the public debt and increasing Navy and coastal defenses. He states revenue should not exceed needed government expenses, discusses tariff modifications, and argues public lands should be reserved for actual settlers at moderate prices while granting emigrants equality under the Constitution. He states he believes in strict construction of constitutional powers, allows military roads under defense powers, and discusses foreign relations principles: peace, commerce, independence of nations, non-interference except for self-preservation, avoiding entangling alliances, and seeking justice. He concludes by stating the U.S. has acquired territory by fair means and will act similarly in the future, and he takes the oath while invoking Divine Providence.

Synaptics announced plans to mass-produce an optical in-display sensor called “Clear ID,” which embeds a fingerprint scanner under a bezel-less phone screen to make unlocking easier. Synaptics claims Clear ID is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, needs only one touch, and allows unlocking from any angle. The company also said fingerprint placement is shifting to display itself as devices move to bezel-free OLED infinity displays. The passage notes that facial recognition systems have been hacked in past instances and concludes that it remains uncertain when the under-screen fingerprint scanner will appear or whether facial recognition will dominate.

On February 16, 2016, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement for the issuance and sale of $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Floating Rate Notes due 2019, $500,000,000 due 2021, $1,250,000,000 1.300% Notes due 2018, $1,000,000,000 1.700% Notes due 2019, $2,250,000,000 2.250% Notes due 2021, $1,500,000,000 2.850% Notes due 2023, $2,000,000,000 3.250% Notes due 2026, $1,250,000,000 4.500% Notes due 2036, and $2,500,000,000 4.650% Notes due 2046, collectively referred to as the “Notes.” The Notes are issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee, and pursuant to an officer’s certificate dated February 23, 2016. Floating Rate Notes interest is payable quarterly in arrears, and Fixed Rate Notes interest is payable semi-annually in arrears. Maturities range from February 23, 2018 to February 23, 2046. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Apple furnished related agreements and related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, and legal opinion.

The Lumberjacks (14-6) beat Thief River Falls 77-45, led by 18 points from Caden Rolfes and 17 from Linaes Whiting. Bemidji took a 45-25 halftime lead and maintained control. Other scorers included Caleb Carlson with 14 points and Jeremy Beberg with 10, with Beberg and Carlson totaling eight and seven rebounds, respectively. Coach Travis Peterson said the team sustained its effort for 36 minutes and took a step forward toward the section tournament. BHS will play Fergus Falls at 7:30 p.m. on Saturday, Feb. 18.

The passage explains that a container defines an API, including how it is executed and how it calls other services and provides HTTP or other interfaces. It emphasizes designing sidecars and other reusable containers with stable, well-defined APIs to prevent breaking changes, and gives examples of how subtle parameter changes can break users. It also describes documenting container images using Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`, referencing Label Schema labels. The chapter then summarizes single-node patterns, including the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and the outside world, and discusses using ambassadors for sharded services via routing logic (e.g., a sharded Redis example using Kubernetes, services, and a proxy).

Florida State University President John Thrasher named a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs and the university’s chief diversity officer, to review FSU’s policy on campus names and markers, including statues. Thrasher said the panel will be deliberate, seek input from the Florida State community, and provide feedback on criteria for appropriate naming policies and any other recommendations. The review followed nationwide efforts to remove Confederate designations and campus requests to remove the statue of Francis Eppes near the Westcott Building. The committee will meet next week in open meetings, and a website will be launched.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU and its role in accelerating AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads in cloud and enterprise environments. It explains how A100 builds on the V100 with faster performance via the Ampere GA100 architecture, including new Third-Generation Tensor Cores, TF32/BF16/FP64 support, and a Sparsity feature that can double throughput. It also covers key system and software capabilities such as Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) virtualization for partitioning an A100 into up to seven GPU instances, Third-Generation NVLink/NVSwitch scaling, CUDA-based tooling (including CUDA Toolkit, CUDA-X libraries, containers via NGC, and Kubernetes support), and enhancements for memory and programmability (HBM2 and larger L2 cache, error detection/isolation, asynchronous copy and barriers, CUDA task graphs, and L2 residency controls). The passage further details MIG architecture concepts and provides an overview of compute acceleration mechanisms and structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) for deep neural networks.

The passage describes how a US government shutdown is affecting federal aviation safety workers, including air traffic controllers and TSA employees, who are working without pay despite assurances that flying remains safe. It cites an FAA engineer saying the shutdown makes work less efficient and could slow repairs, and workers noting that some projects have stopped and coworkers are absent due to planned furloughs. Workers report anxiety over delayed pay, concerns about further furloughs of contractors, and fears about potential mass firings or actions against unions. FAA spokesperson Hannah Walden says the FAA will slow air traffic at affected airports to maintain safety and that safety-critical positions, including controllers, are exempt from reductions in force, while a TSA spokesperson calls the situation unfortunate and blames political gamesmanship. The passage also reports concerns among workers about long-term consequences for union rights if employees take absences due to lack of pay.

The passage describes the 23rd annual BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna, expecting close to 3,000 participants for marathon, half marathon, 10 km, and 5 km events. Walk-up registration is available at the Sports Expo on Friday (3–7 p.m.) and Saturday (9 a.m.–6 p.m.), with race package pickup at City Park on Friday (3–7 p.m.), Saturday (9 a.m.–6 p.m.), and Sunday (9 a.m.–1 p.m.). The course is described as flat and fast, qualifying for the Boston Marathon, and the 5 km event is newly timed, with a beverage garden added for adults. Events begin Saturday with a 5 km timed run/walk, followed by ABC Kids Activities, and Sunday features the marathon, half marathon, and 10 km. The event supports the Sunshine Foundation of Canada, with additional activities including a Kids Zone, a BMO ABC Kids 1 km Fun Run, and a Running Room Free Friendship Run. Road closure and traffic information is available at www.okanaganmarathon.ca.

The passage describes surgical devices, systems, and methods for robotic- and/or navigation-assisted procedures that include placing an implant (e.g., a screw) within a vertebral pedicle. It discusses challenges of accurate screw placement during minimally invasive surgery and limitations of existing approaches, including flexibility or bending of manually placed guide wires, lack of robot-assisted advancement, tool incompatibility, and navigation error from relative vertebral movement after discectomy and cage placement.

A summarized solution includes multiple method aspects involving a manipulator, an end effector, a screw, and a sleeve coaxially disposed around the screw. Controllers position screws and sleeve on a navigation-defined insertion trajectory, advance them together into soft tissue, and then advance the screw relative to the sleeve to secure the screw and disengage it. Other aspects include a sleeve distal movable feature made of flexible material that is initially closed to prevent tissue ingress and deploys outwardly as the screw advances. Another aspect includes a navigation system with a localizer and a tracking device having markers and a ratcheting mechanism to rotate the markers relative to the screw.

The passage also provides detailed descriptions of a robotic surgical system and tool assembly, including drive couplers, interchangeable working tools (e.g., scalpel, depth probe, bur, drill, dilator probe, tap inserter), and mechanisms for coupling/decoupling tools. It describes navigation and localization components, such as optical localizers and tracking devices secured to vertebrae or other anatomy, and discusses reregistering to account for movement of bony anatomy during surgery. Further, it describes an elongate sleeve used as a working channel and associated features (e.g., retracting/dilating tapers, locking/locating features, distal closure/deployment features, and anti-skid engagement spikes). The passage concludes with an example workflow involving preparing a pilot hole and placing a tap marker in the vertebra, including use of a tracking device with a ratcheting mechanism for unidirectional rotation relative to a working tool.

The passage is an Apple Inc. Form 8-K current report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 27, 2022. It states that Apple issued a press release on January 27, 2022 about Apple’s financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report lists Apple’s registered securities (Common Stock and various notes due 2022 through 2042) and includes standard filing and signature information, with Luca Maestri signing as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

A New York Drug Utilization Review Board voted unanimously to recommend pausing New York Medicaid coverage of Elevidys, a Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment, due to a safety controversy. The board said the state should wait for the FDA to add safety and clinical trial data to the product labeling and should first evaluate a regimen Sarepta is developing to mitigate liver failure risk. New York will still cover some patients through its Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment benefit on a case-by-case basis based on medical necessity.

Anjuna police registered two cases of unnatural deaths of tourists/youth from Tamil Nadu and Kerala. In the first case, 28-year-old Pravin Sundaram collapsed in a parking area after visiting Vagator and was declared brought dead at a private hospital; his body was sent for autopsy at GMC Bambolim, and viscera will be preserved while police record friends’ statements and await the viscera report. In the second case, a youth named Abdul died at a private hospital after an unknown person brought him there; police are trying to trace that person and also sent the body for autopsy with viscera preserved. Water Resource Minister and Siolim MLA expressed concern, calling for outdoor music parties to be stopped, and said he had asked police to halt drug-related activities or be held responsible.

The London Lightning delivered a shoddy, unfocused performance and lost 123-110 to the St. John’s Edge in St. John’s, tying the best-of-seven series 2-2 with Game 5 on Thursday. The Lightning had a double-digit lead early but lost intensity in the second half, were outscored in the paint 50-38, missed 13 free throws, and had an on-court confrontation between Royce White and Ryan Anderson near midcourt. Lightning coach Keith Vassell said his team was not prepared enough and that adjustments should have been made. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap said he adjusted by starting Alex Johnson earlier and increasing his play, and the Edge won led by Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams with 28 points each. The article also discusses an investigation by NBL deputy commissioner Audley Stephenson into a fan’s complaint involving an alleged homophobic slur during Game 3.

The passage discusses preparing for an upcoming game on Wednesday, emphasizing focusing on the next game after previous matches and taking positives from playoff experiences. It highlights confidence in the team’s road performance, strategies such as continuing the forecheck, getting pucks deep, closing gaps in the defensive zone, and being tough on opponents’ forwards. It references a prior game where they played tightly, earned scoring opportunities, and had goalies making key saves. It also mentions relaxing and preparing ahead of game day, staying consistent with their road game approach, and aiming to get pucks and players toward the net.

Pop star Christina Perri and James Corden praised a Carpool Karaoke-style video by mums and their children with Down’s syndrome, featuring the song “A Thousand Years.” The video, inspired by a SingingHands video signed in Makaton, was created for World Down’s Syndrome Day (March 21) and has been watched by more than 600,000 people, bringing tears to Corden. The idea came from Coventry mum Becky Carless, whose four-year-old son Archie has Down’s syndrome, and the mums filmed themselves in their cars while a dad edited the clips. Perri supported the song use within an hour after the group contacted her on Twitter. The mothers are part of a Facebook group called “DesignerGenes,” and Becky urged people to share the video to help it succeed.

The passage discusses how Turkey’s education system coordinated distance education with students, teachers, and parents, aiming to achieve planned target behaviors and achievements, and notes that preparation, continuity, necessary materials, and teacher professional competencies are required. During the COVID-19 pandemic, face-to-face education in Turkey was suspended and distance education began, with differences in implementation across cities and schools due to factors such as teachers, students, parents, and technology. Limitations are described as more evident for practical, student-oriented courses, and studies comparing distance education with face-to-face education are referenced.

The study described in the passage uses a qualitative case study design, interviewing 20 Turkish teachers in Hazro district of Diyarbakır across grades 5–8. Data were collected through semi-structured one-on-one interviews and analyzed with descriptive analysis.

Key findings include that teachers generally thought distance education was not efficient enough, and that target behaviors and achievements were only partially achieved due to attendance and infrastructure/material problems, especially lack of internet and devices. Problems are reported from multiple perspectives: students’ lack of equipment, parents’ difficulty managing multiple school-age children at home, technology/infrastructure issues, and teachers’ time challenges from disconnections and repeated instruction. Teachers reported that students needed reading books and dictionaries, plus technological materials and activities. Communication most often involved phones, with WhatsApp as the most used application, followed by Zoom and EBA. Teacher qualifications during distance education are described as including subject knowledge, lesson planning and materials preparation, communication skills, empathy, activity orientation, attention to individual differences, and effective technology use.

The passage concludes with recommendations including resolving infrastructure and material deficiencies, updating and strengthening EBA content, ensuring equality of opportunity for internet/device access, structuring distance education to support face-to-face education, providing professional development for teachers, continuing reading activities, considering students’ cognitive/physical/affective needs, prioritizing health and safety, and revising post-pandemic target behaviors and achievements.

The passage is a presidential address urging unity and peace. It frames the orderly transfer of power and upcoming anniversaries as moments that set long-term directions, citing converging forces that make peace possible. The speaker argues that America’s youth and past achievements are strengths, but that the nation faces a crisis of the spirit marked by discord, division, and empty lives. The answer, the passage says, is found within, through listening, lowering rhetoric, and emphasizing simple values like goodness and kindness. It calls for government and people working together, broader goals such as employment, housing, education, city and rural rebuilding, and environmental protection, and planning to shift resources from war to domestic needs. Domestically, it emphasizes equality in dignity and going forward “together,” and internationally it calls for open communication, negotiation over confrontation, reducing the burden of arms, aiding the poor and hungry, and remaining strong against threats. The speaker concludes by committing to uphold the Constitution and consecrate efforts to peace, using imagery from Apollo’s view of Earth to stress shared human destiny and “riders on the earth together,” ending with a call to seize opportunity with faith and purpose.

Topshop recalled all display stands at tills after an incident in its Reading store killed 10-year-old Kaden Reddick. Police said he suffered serious head injuries in an incident involving a display, was taken to Royal Berkshire Hospital, and was pronounced dead. A Topshop spokesman said it would remove all relevant till barrier units from stores nationwide with immediate effect, and that the Reading store would remain closed. Police, the boy’s family, and Reading Borough Council said they are supporting the family and investigating the circumstances. The report also notes a previous incident in 2013 when an 18st mirror crushed a four-year-old boy in a Bicester Village changing room.

The FDA announced a nationwide undercover blitz to target illegal Juul sales to minors, including store and online retailers. FDA Commissioner Dr. Scott Gottlieb said compliance checks since early March found 40 violations and resulted in 40 warning letters, and that the FDA will not tolerate sales of tobacco products to youth. The FDA said it contacted eBay about Juul listings, which eBay removed and prevented from being re-listed. The agency also asked Juul’s maker for documents to explain why youth find the products appealing and plans similar requests to other manufacturers; noncompliance would lead to enforcement. The crackdown also includes additional actions against companies the FDA believes are marketing e-cigarettes misleadingly to minors, along with efforts to educate young people and assess ways to make tobacco products less toxic, addictive, and appealing.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger lives in a cabin on 160 acres near Merrickville, surrounded by rare plants and trees. With her husband Christian, she bought the land in the 1970s, built their house, and planted many rare trees herself. Raised with ancient forest laws and Irish teachings, she later studied botany and medical biochemistry at University College, Cork, then pursued further research and training in Canada, including cardiovascular research. After settling in Merrickville, an orchard gift from the Department of Surgery helped inspire her arboretum and organic garden, Carrigliath. She began “expotitions” to classify local rare species and save what could be protected, and she now writes books and works on research full-time. Her latest project is the Canadian-made feature film “Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees,” which addresses deforestation, climate change, and her Bioplan idea encouraging people to plant trees to reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide. The film is based on her book “The Global Forest,” has garnered major documentary audiences, and is nominated for awards in Paris, with theatre and TVO.ca showings, while she prepares for European premieres.

The passage includes statements about a tough but honest coach, strong defense and depth on Ryan’s team, and the challenge of playing in a competitive league that requires hard work. The speaker says they are excited for the opportunity, expects strong fan support in Canada and in Ottawa, and emphasizes the importance of being ready. It also notes that opponents’ goalies are athletic and that limited space requires precise shooting. The speaker highlights their team’s forward depth, younger lines performing well, and other lines that can score key goals. The passage also touches on the goalkeeper goalies and market visibility, with a comment that certain players (like Giguere) would be more widely seen in larger markets.

The author describes being disconnected and at risk of dropping out during the first two years of high school in southern Nevada, where they were identified as “opportunity youth” (NEETs). After getting a first job, they agreed to stay on top of schoolwork and then worked at least 20 hours a week while maintaining a 4.0 GPA. The author says employment helped them connect classroom learning to real life, develop durable skills, and build confidence and purpose. The passage cites research that youth employment and internships/apprenticeships are associated with better outcomes such as reduced delinquency, improved academic performance and social-emotional development, and lower criminal justice interaction. It also notes that internships and apprenticeships are rare, youth unemployment is higher than the national rate, and only a few states provide incentives or tax credits for businesses to hire youth, including examples from Nevada and Indiana. The author concludes that expanding work opportunities would help disconnected youth connect, build confidence, and benefit the broader community.

Ravita Meghwar, a Hindu girl in Pakistan’s Sindh province, is now known as Gulnaz Shah, a Muslim who is married. Her family believes kidnappers drugged and abducted her and that she was forcibly converted, while she says she eloped and married of her own choice. The passage describes a recent pattern of court cases in Sindh involving Hindu girls—often minors—who allegedly are forcibly converted and married to Muslim men, which unsettles Pakistan’s small Hindu population and contributes to some Hindus leaving villages for cities or moving to India. It contrasts accusations of organized forcible conversions by Hindu activists with Muslim religious activists’ defensive stance that conversion earns blessings, often with support from shrines, seminaries, clerics, and local politicians. It also discusses legislation in Sindh in 2016 outlawing forcible conversions and conversions before age 18, opposition from hardline religious groups, and ongoing reliance on laws against underage marriage to challenge individual cases. The passage says it is unclear when conversions became organized, and provides anecdotal accounts of Hindu families migrating within Sindh or to India, including estimates of 5,000 per year leaving for India.

The speaker says the team’s “heart” was hurt not by opponents but by their own critical errors, which led to odd-man rushes and contributed to problems in the third period. Despite believing the mistakes are correctable, the speaker stresses that they must react properly, stay within their game plan, and raise their defensive level to win the next game. The speaker attributes the opponents’ success to defending with speed and size, preventing pucks and responding on loose plays, and says the team must defend with the same passion and avoid trying to “hit the home run” too early. They also discuss the mental aspect of playing at this stage, the importance of leadership and dressing-room emotion, and the need to stay in their “element” to maintain performance.

Saturday nights have long been the main ratings battle between BBC1 and ITV. Even with more channels and streaming services, winning Saturday night for the BBC is portrayed as showing its commitment to “inform, educate and entertain,” and it remains a time when families can watch the same programme together. However, launching a new show in this competitive slot is described as difficult, so Saturday nights are often filled with long-running favourites such as *Casualty*, *Strictly*, and *The X Factor*. The passage argues that ratings are not easy and that few entertainment shows have taken off and stayed; it cites examples spanning decades and notes that in the last decade only *The Voice UK* is mentioned as a moderate hit. It adds that when major entertainment formats and hosts eventually become boring, audiences stop watching, but controllers and producers have not yet found a new format that is not similar to existing ones. The passage concludes that most new shows fail and that controllers rely on instinct, producers’ track records, and hope, while highlighting the BBC’s financial success with *Strictly*.
