Combination defenses can severely harm teams not prepared to attack them. They are used mainly to deny and limit the “touches” of outstanding offensive players and can also be used as a surprise tactic; timing and surprise are critical. Common combination defenses include Box & One, where four players form a box zone and one chaser uses full pass denial on a top offensive player; Diamond & One, which denies and limits outstanding scorers, matches up on a single guard front but gives up the corners; and Triangle & Two, which is effective against two outstanding scorers, can change defenses to catch opponents off guard, and can be used to hold the ball late in games.

The study found that pre-existing depression or anxiety disorders and the use of psychoactive drugs are associated with a higher risk of long-term opioid pain medication use. It reported that psychiatric and behavioral conditions and psychoactive medications were linked to subsequent prescription opioid claims, with a stronger association for long-term use, especially among patients with prior substance use disorders. Harmful outcomes from opioid use, including substance use disorders, depression, suicidal or self-injuring behavior, and motor vehicle accidents, also predicted long-term opioid use. Nearly 1.7% of patients with opioid prescriptions became long-term users (six months or longer), with risk increasing more for those with mental health conditions or psychoactive medication use. The researchers reported increases ranging from 1.5 times for ADHD medication use to about 9 times for previous opioid use disorders. The study analyzed 10.3 million patients with insurance claims for opioid prescriptions from 2004 to 2013 and was published in PAIN.

The far-right AfD is gaining support in Bavaria and helped drive Interior Minister Horst Seehofer to push Angela Merkel toward a harsher immigration stance. Merkel agreed to close asylum “transit camps” along three Austrian borders, with migrants who applied in other EU countries not turned back immediately but instead held at transit centers on the German-Austrian border. Rejected asylum seekers would be sent back to their countries after negotiations or, if no deal is reached, sent back to Austria under an agreement with Vienna. The Social Democrats disputed that transit centers were part of their coalition deal, Austria threatened to reciprocate expulsions, and Italy also refused entry, leaving Germany taking far fewer migrants than in 2015 and highlighting wider divisions within Europe over migration.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU and key features for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It highlights improved performance through a third-generation Tensor Core architecture supporting multiple data types and features such as TF32, BF16, FP64, and fine-grained structured sparsity, which can double Tensor Core throughput. The A100 includes Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology to securely partition a GPU into up to seven isolated GPU instances with quality-of-service guarantees, and it supports scaling using NVLink/NVSwitch with improved error detection and recovery. It also covers compatibility with NVIDIA Magnum IO™ and Mellanox interconnect solutions, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and enhancements for error and fault detection, isolation, and containment. Additional discussed items include asynchronous copy and barriers, CUDA task graphs, L2 cache residency controls, NVJPG decode and optical flow acceleration hardware, and further software features in CUDA 11. The passage also introduces the DGX A100 system as a universal AI infrastructure platform using A100 GPUs and MIG for scaling and efficient workload provisioning.

The NPD Group identified five trends expected to shape Britain’s £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018. These include rapid expansion of smartphone click & collect to cut order and wait times and improve sales, investing in staff training to boost satisfaction, loyalty and profits, shifting loyalty schemes to tiered “VIP” offers with personalized rewards, ensuring consistent delivery of brand promises to avoid negative customer experiences and social media complaints, and using staff expertise and customer data to provide personalized recommendations. Cyril Lavenant said success depends on responding innovatively to these trends and delivering on brand promises.

The professor reviews binary detection in a communication system where a one-dimensional signal (±a) passes through channel encoding, modulation/demodulation, and noise is added, producing an observed sample value v. The receiver makes a one-shot decision (guessing whether 0 or 1 was sent) using statistical hypothesis testing, with MAP (maximum a posteriori) decoding chosen to minimize probability of error. The MAP rule is formulated using a known probability model and posterior probabilities, leading to a likelihood-ratio test: choose 0 if the likelihood ratio is greater than or equal to a threshold (the ratio of prior probabilities), otherwise choose 1. For Gaussian noise and antipodal binary signaling (2PAM with ±a), the likelihood ratio simplifies so that the decision depends on the observation through an exponential expression involving v, a, and noise variance, and equivalently a log-likelihood ratio. The resulting probability of error is related to the Gaussian Q-function and, for equal priors, depends on the ratio of signal energy per bit to noise (Eb). The discussion extends from antipodal scalar detection to non-antipodal two-signal cases and then to real antipodal vectors in white Gaussian noise, where the sufficient statistic becomes the inner product of the received vector with the transmitted vector. Geometrically, optimal decision regions become planes perpendicular to the line connecting ±a, and the error probability can be computed using the same Q-function approach with the inner-product statistic.

The Nobel Committee for Chemistry recognized three chemists for creating metal-organic frameworks. The awardees included a chemist from the University of California, Berkeley, Susumu Kitagawa of Kyoto University, and Richard Robson of the University of Melbourne, for work since the 1990s developing a molecular architecture combining metal ions and carbon-based molecules. The release said the frameworks can harvest water or store toxic gases and may contribute to solving major challenges, and described them as “rooms” with large spaces, compared to Hermione Granger’s magical bag. The passage also states that more than 100,000 metal-organic frameworks have been created since the discoveries.

The passage describes an appeal by John Koedding from a Municipal Court judgment in favor of plaintiffs seeking the value of a horse sold to him. The plaintiffs were horse dealers; the defendant selected a horse from those in their stables. After an initial brief use and return over a price dispute, the defendant requested the horse again, kept it several days, returned it, and it later died. The defendant argued there was an agreement for a 30-day trial, which the plaintiffs disputed; the trial court found for the plaintiffs, and the decision was upheld. The defendant also claimed the contract was void under the statute of frauds, but the court found there was delivery and acceptance, so the defense failed. The court also rejected the defendant’s warranty-breach defense due to the evidence. The judgment was affirmed with costs, and the decision was concurred in by other judges.

The passage describes systems and methods for plasma processing that use shaped-pulse biasing to control the ion energy distribution function (IEDF) at a substrate surface. It explains that, in reactive ion etching (RIE), an RF bias generator creates a self-bias (DC voltage drop) that influences ion energy and etch anisotropy through the IEDF. The disclosure focuses on maintaining a nearly constant sheath voltage using a special shaped-pulse bias scheme, enabling mono-energetic IEDF generation. It further states that arbitrarily shaped IEDF profiles can be created by modulating the amplitude of a shaped-pulse bias waveform (and, in some embodiments, the pulse/burst patterns and duty cycle), where the relative number of pulses at a given negative voltage jump determines the relative ion fraction at the corresponding ion energy. In additional embodiments, the ion compensation phase can use overcompensating or undercompensating voltage ramps to produce wider, non-monoenergetic IEDF profiles with energy spread controlled by the ramp slope. A substrate processing system is described that includes a substrate support assembly with an electrode and ceramic layer, and a bias supply with control hardware to generate and modulate the required pulse waveforms. Flow diagrams outline methods involving positive and negative voltage jumps to neutralize and set wafer voltage, and applying ramp voltages to over- or undercompensate ion current.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2020. It includes itemized financial statements and notes, including consolidated statements of cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets, along with disclosures on accounting policies, estimates, inventories, accounts receivable, unearned revenue, fair value measurements, leases, commitments and contingencies, debt, stockholders’ equity, income taxes, and segment information. It also provides management’s discussion on liquidity, capital resources, effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, and results of operations, including net sales, operating income, operating expenses, and interest and other income/expense.

A fire on Kazakhstan’s steppes caused by debris from a Russian space launch killed a Kazakh man and hospitalized another, emergency services said. The blaze was triggered by parts of a Soyuz 2.1a rocket that fell after launching from Baikonur, near Zhezkazgan, after being reported as a dry grass fire about 40 km away. The fire reached 15 km across and was extinguished by around 2100 GMT on Wednesday. Roscosmos confirmed the death, citing difficult meteorological conditions in the fallout region with extremely high temperatures, and said the truck driven by the deceased man was covered by flames due to a strong gust of wind. The two men were clearing debris for NPO Mashinostroyeniya, which Roscosmos said employed them.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere (GA102/GA10x) GPU architecture, including the GA102 GPU’s manufacturing process, transistor and die size, and its compute resources: CUDA (programmable shading) cores, RT cores for BVH traversal and ray tracing, and tensor cores for AI workloads. It outlines performance improvements such as doubled FP32 datapaths per SM, doubled RT core ray/triangle intersection throughput, and tensor core features including sparsity and TF32/BFloat16 support, with related performance figures for RTX 3080 and comparisons to Turing-era GPUs. It also covers hardware and platform features including GDDR6X memory and bandwidth improvements, third-generation NVLink for scaling memory, PCIe Gen4, and GA10x SM and memory subsystem organization. Additional sections discuss second-generation RT core enhancements for concurrent compute/graphics and ray-traced motion blur acceleration, third-generation tensor core usage for DLSS and other AI applications, the RTX IO technology for faster GPU-based asset loading/decompression, and video codec acceleration via NVDEC and NVENC. The passage further summarizes the NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 positioning for data center and workstation use, and includes appendix material and general disclaimers.

The passage describes the Princeton offense as an unstructured, team-oriented style of play developed and popularized by Pete Carril. It relies on constant motion, counteractions based on defensive reads, and creates open shots—especially through the classic back door cut. Coaches and players must be committed to the “All or None Principle,” with skills including outside shooting, passing and driving, court savvy, patience, ball control, unselfishness, and strong conditioning to sustain constant movement. The offense emphasizes key concepts such as Commitment, Adaptability, Spacing (12–15 feet between players), Continuity, and managing tempo through patience and frequent passing. It is presented as adaptable to different defenses and supported by phases: Phase 1 entries triggered by ballhandler passes or dribble penetration; Phase 2 exchanges and constant ball movement to set up back cuts and “Give & Go” actions; and Phase 3 post action when the high post makes basket cuts, often flowing into low post and kick-out passing. The passage also outlines specific entry options, exchanges, back cut counters, dribble penetrations, post play, quick-hitting set options near the shot clock, press break preparation, and psychological aspects intended to create mental pressure, demoralize defenses, and force opponents into mistakes.

The passage describes a team feeling encouraged by a recent win but acknowledging that there is still a long road ahead and they need a couple more wins. The speaker says the goal is to take games on the road and return to Edmonton, where they are strong at home, aiming to force another game. They credit specific players for confident, big goal scoring, especially in the first period, and say the team played four lines, skated well, and clogged the neutral zone. The speaker also comments that although some people thought the team was outplayed in the third period, they felt they played well, noting they were on the road.

The speaker says the team was outmuscled in the low end and in their end during the early part of the second period, but they adjusted by improving work ethic and performed well in the last five minutes of the second period and in the third. They describe a key player as an important part of the team who plays five-on-five, power play, and penalty killing, and who made strong contributions in key moments. The speaker notes the team was strong in the third period during the regular season and continued that through the playoffs, increasing pace and creating scoring chances; they mention a third-line push that wore down Boston’s defense and helped tie the game, with a goal in overtime. They say they were happy to have “Manny” back in the lineup, praising his faceoffs and on-ice play. They discuss handling injury/player availability as a “game time decision” to prevent opponents from exploiting weaknesses. The passage also includes remarks about difficulty distinguishing “danny” and “henrik” earlier, and character differences between them, as well as plans for easing “him” back into play using his strengths in specific situations, without breaking up an effective line. The speaker concludes by addressing penalty issues, including offensive-zone penalties and an incident involving a stick, and hopes for a more effective power play.

The passage summarizes an Iowa appeal involving a foreign judgment against James E. Siver and Elizabeth Siver and a request for injunction to prevent alleged fraudulent conveyance of property to their sons. The district court dismissed the petition and the judgment was affirmed on appeal. The opinion addresses evidence rules for witness competency, holding that objections must be specific and that, under the statute, parties are not generally incompetent to testify against an administrator except for personal transactions or communications with a deceased person; it concludes enough admissible testimony supported the trial court’s fact finding. It also discusses that objections to incompetent witnesses can fail if they only claim a witness is “incompetent and unqualified.” On the merits of the Siver defendants’ counterclaim for damages based on Secor’s alleged fraudulent misrepresentations, the court found no reason to disturb the district court’s decision. Finally, it holds that costs taxed to an administrator in her official capacity will not be relaxed on appeal to the administrator in her individual capacity. The opinion notes a dissent by Stevens on witness-competency grounds, and that Ladd and Salinger concur in parts of the dissent.

Volunteers in southern New South Wales and the ACT are surveying local waterways in late winter to compile a platypus census and gather baseline data on the near-threatened species. In the Upper Murrumbidgee River near Cooma, Antia Brademann says volunteers face challenges spotting the shy, cryptic animals; over four years, surveys suggest platypus numbers are stable at that site, though no platypus were sighted during one group survey, while a native water rat was observed. The passage also notes that citizen science can help inform conservation, encourages people to report platypus sightings year-round, and provides tips for spotting platypus by watching for ripples or bubbles, particularly in August and September during early morning or late evening.

The passage lists 10 AI tools said to transform content creation in 2025: ChatGPT for writing support and content optimization; Canva Magic Studio for on-brand graphic design; RunwayML for video creation and effects like text-prompt weather changes and object removal; Midjourney V6 for AI image generation with professional photography and artistic styles; Synthesia for AI avatar videos with multilingual presentations; Descript for text-based audio/video editing with transcription and filler word removal; ElevenLabs for natural voice synthesis with voice cloning and multilingual accents; Tribescaler for viral content trend analysis and optimization; Clickable for data-driven automated ad variations; and CopyAI for marketing copy generation across formats and industries. It also notes that features and pricing may change and that the article includes affiliate links.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity for threshold-crossing in a random walk, noting that thresholds at values alpha and beta can be handled using a stopping time and moment-generating functions. It derives an upper bound for the probability of crossing the alpha threshold (independent of the lower threshold) using Markov’s inequality and a key root r* of the moment-generating function. The discussion then connects these ideas to sequential hypothesis testing by expressing decisions in terms of likelihood ratios and defining the log-likelihood ratio as a sum of IID random variables, forming a random walk. It explains how sequential testing trades off error probabilities and the expected number of samples, and shows how differentiating Wald’s identity at r = 0 yields Wald’s equality and related second-moment relationships. The lecture transitions to martingales, defining them via conditional expectations, giving examples (zero-mean random walks, sums under a conditional-mean-zero condition, product-form martingales), introducing submartingales and supermartingales via inequalities, and concluding with Jensen’s inequality for convex functions.

The passage describes socket markings and requirements for a “SOCKET 940” identifier, including molding the identifier, directional designator, pin orientation symbol, supplier UL-approved symbol, and lot traceability marking so they remain visible after solder mounting. It also notes no lubricants may be present on contact mating areas for fully assembled sockets shipped to customers. Subsequent sections specify contact and solder attachment details: high-strength copper alloy base metal, nickel and gold plating thicknesses, SMT solder ball type and dimensions, a solder barrier feature, and a co-planarity requirement. The socket actuation lever is described with force and displacement requirements, along with locking/latch features. Socket durability, inspection conditions, and allowable defects for solder balls, contacts, cover/base, and lever components are listed. Additional electrical specifications include a 1.5 A per contact current rating, temperature rise limits, low level circuit resistance limits measured before and after testing, inductance and capacitance limits with measurement frequencies, differential impedance and propagation delay skew limits, dielectric withstanding voltage, and insulation resistance requirements.

Most smartphone brands are moving toward thin bezels, but accommodating selfie cameras and sensors makes true full-screen displays difficult. Xiaomi uses a bottom placement for the selfie camera and sensors on the Mi Mix 2s, Apple added a notch on the iPhone X, and many other brands followed. Vivo’s Apex concept removes bezels by placing the fingerprint sensor under the screen and using a pop-up selfie camera, but the design relies on a complex, bulky mechanism. The passage suggests transparent OLED panels as a more permanent solution, describing a setup with a transparent OLED layer and a hidden selfie camera, where the screen would stay opaque except when the camera is in use. It also notes that transparent OLED could be limited to smaller areas for mid-range phones, and that transparent OLED technology has been demonstrated previously by multiple companies, with the next step depending on who adapts it for smartphones first.

A study describes a traditional yogurt-making method in parts of Bulgaria and Turkey that uses four live ants added to warmed cow’s milk. The bacteria living on the ants and the ants themselves acidify and thicken the milk, and the ants’ colony heat keeps the jar warm by fermenting the mixture in an ant mound overnight. The process produces tangy, herbaceous yogurt as lactic and acetic acid–producing bacteria, along with milk-digesting enzymes from ants and bacteria, help convert the milk. The study found that microbes from frozen or dehydrated ants ferment less well than those from living ants. It also notes that live ants can carry a parasite that, in rare cases, may cause liver or gastrointestinal disease, and advises against homemade attempts. The passage contrasts traditional practices’ greater variety of bacterial species with modern industrial methods that use a few acid-producing microbes for safety and consistent flavor.

The speaker says they are caught up in everything going on and that it has “just been great.” Two weeks earlier they did not expect such an outcome, but coach Burns put them in the situation and they felt supported and blessed. They describe feeling good before the game, staying calmer than usual, and credit the team’s leadership and veterans for keeping them mentally sharp and laughing up to game time. They explain they are in their third season with the organization, spent two and a half years in Albany, and received a call in January that led to playing NHL games. They say the team trained hard for possible injuries and were ready physically and mentally, and that their goal was to contribute in any way, not necessarily by scoring. They praise the team’s depth throughout the playoffs and name several players who stepped up. They mention specific key moments, including Jeff scoring, and describe stressful instances involving their own play. They also discuss a particular teammate’s leadership and presence in the locker room, saying they tried not to “fill his shoes.” They conclude by describing the Stanley Cup finals game atmosphere as intense and clock-focused, with players reacting strongly on the bench.

The Clark County Board of Trustees voted on May 2, 2018 to name Dr. Jesus Jara as the new superintendent. Jara had been deputy superintendent for Orange County Public Schools since 2012 and previously led Monroe County Public Schools in Florida. During the meeting, some trustees and community members supported Dr. Mike Barton, who was defeated 4 to 3. After additional debate, trustees voted on Jara, who won; the board said it expects negotiations and aims for Jara to start before the end of June to allow time with retiring superintendent Pat Skorkowsky. Six finalists were considered, including internal candidates Barton, Dr. Jesse Welsh, and Dr. Eva White, and external candidates Donald Haddad, Shonda Huery Hardman, and Jara. The board said it received 77 applications for the internal search and interviewed all candidates on April 27.

The passage discusses challenges in contemporary academic education and argues that innovative techniques, including gamification and educational games, are crucial to transfer knowledge and develop students’ motivation and competences. It presents gamification as the purposeful use of game mechanisms to increase dedication, loyalty, and behavioral change, and outlines key benefits linked to motivation, fun, and positive emotions, along with the importance of clear goals, instructions, and feedback. It then describes four projects carried out at the University of Wrocław’s Institute of Pedagogy: a location-based cultural education game (“Kulturalny Wrocław”), a five-day gamified career management seminar (“Grywalizacja w zarządzaniu karierą…”), a location-based entrepreneurship game (“Zostań przedsiębiorcą”), and a LARP game for soft skills (“Spell of the Black Magic Master”). Across these examples, the passage reports participants’ generally positive evaluations—such as socializing, engagement, and knowledge retention—while also noting limitations including varying effectiveness by subject, organizational and environmental constraints, the need for prior preparation, and high instructor effort and resources. The conclusion states that educational games can be integrated into curricula if well-selected with regard to students’ experience, topic, time, and costs, and that overly long or complex games can reduce satisfaction.

The passage describes a command that moves one or more SNP guest pages within the system physical address space, intended as a faster replacement for the SEV/SNP PAGE_MOVE operation. It requires that 2M pages be composed of physically contiguous 4K pages, support only physically contiguous 2M pages, and that 2M pages be 2M aligned. DMA to migrating pages is not supported, and the CPU must not access the pages (generally by making them non-present in the CPU host page table). Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destination pages must be in the Pre-Migration state; after migration, destination pages take the source state and source pages return to Pre-Migration.

It lists firmware steps and validation checks (including RMP_ENFORCE=1, non-default SRC_PADDR/DST_PADDR, valid GCTX_PADDR in Context state, exclusive access to source/destination RMPs, matching page sizes, and correct source/destination page states), followed by TLB invalidation and sync, copying data, and updating source and destination RMPs. The command is intended to mark the end of strings of page migration commands and may be configured to interrupt on completion. It also outlines error handling: format/content errors reject commands, migration entry errors may allow partial success, ring buffer errors are reported in PM_STATUS, hardware errors are reported in command status and/or MCA, and timeouts require logging MCA and determining actions such as saving state or terminating VMs. A command can operate on up to 128 pages per batch, and hardware errors may make the pages unrecoverable; failures are reported via command status codes, but memory state may be unfixable, potentially leading to system cessation while allowing software to save state before reboot.

The passage says the goal is zero tobacco deaths, arguing that reducing tobacco-related carnage must be met with the question of how many preventable deaths are acceptable, with the answer “zero.” It claims smokers are victims rather than perpetrators and places responsibility on the tobacco industry for marketing an engineered product designed to be addictive and deadly. It cites the Danish Institute for Human Rights stating tobacco production and marketing conflict with the right to health. It says the global health community adopted the Cape Town Declaration on Human Rights and a Tobacco-Free World in March, endorsed by over 150 organizations, and that May 31 is a target date to be truly tobacco-free. It also describes Action on Smoking and Health (ASH), founded in 1967, as America’s oldest anti-tobacco organization aiming for a world with ZERO tobacco deaths, with contact information for Megan Arendt.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney maths teacher, gained national and international fame through his YouTube channel “Wootube,” awards, and recognition including being named Australia’s Local Hero for 2018 by Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull and being a finalist for the $US1 million Global Teacher Prize announced by Bill Gates. After filming lessons in 2012 for a seriously ill student, his videos became highly popular, reaching over 200,000 subscribers and more than 12 million views. In his new NSW Department of Education role as a “master teacher” and innovation leader for maths teaching, he travels across the state mentoring students and other teachers while still teaching at Cherrybrook Technology High School. Woo’s tours through regional areas featured large student audiences and praise for making maths engaging. He describes his busy schedule as challenging but says he is focused on sharing topics he loves.

Paul Nagy appeals a district court order denying his Fed.R.Civ.P. 60(b) motion. The Fourth Circuit reviewed the record and found no reversible error, affirming on the district court’s reasoning. The court dispensed with oral argument and affirmed the judgment.

Rodes, Trustee, et al. v. Yates, Trustee, et al. was an appeal from an order sustaining a demurrer to an amended petition but making no disposition of the action. The court held that such an order is not a final order and that no appeal lies from it (citing Harrison v. Stroud). The appeal was dismissed.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted tax brackets and deductions for 2026 to provide modest relief and prevent “bracket creep.” The standard deduction will increase for married couples filing jointly to $32,200, for single filers to $16,100, and for heads of household to $24,150. The 37% top marginal tax rate will apply above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for couples. The estate tax exemption will rise to $15 million from $13.99 million, EITC and child tax credit thresholds will be adjusted, and a new $6,000 federal deduction for taxpayers aged 65 and older will begin with the 2025 tax year. Analysts described the changes as a middle-ground approach offering relief without significantly reducing federal revenues.

The consolidated appeals challenge Chancery Division denials of defendants’ applications for costs and counsel fees under N.J.S. 2A:15-53, a labor-dispute injunction statute. The court recounts two related matters: a “strike case” involving illegal mass picketing that led to temporary and interlocutory restraints, and an “arbitration case” where the company sought a declaration that a discharged striker was not arbitrable under a new collective bargaining agreement.  

In the arbitration case, the court held there was no basis to award counsel fees because the dispute did not fall within the intended scope of the Anti-Injunction Act and was essentially a declaratory-judgment request for an arbitration stay. In the strike case, the court affirmed the trial court’s denial of costs and counsel fees to defendants, reasoning that the injunction reversal was based on procedural violations rather than that the plaintiff lacked substantive merit for injunctive relief. The judgments of the Chancery Division were affirmed, with costs to respondent in the arbitration case only.

The passage describes the SanDisk Sansa Fuze portable MP3 player for home and personal use, including its features such as a 1.9” color screen, built-in microphone, integrated FM radio (if applicable), microSDHC expansion, and support for various audio/video/photo formats. It outlines battery charging and limits, basic power/reset controls, connecting to a computer, firmware updating, formatting (which deletes content), and transferring music, photos, and videos using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, and Sansa Media Converter. It also provides instructions for playing music/audiobooks, configuring music options (repeat, shuffle, MusicEQ, adding/removing songs), video playback options (bookmarks, ratings, brightness, delete), photo viewing/slideshow controls (shuffle, loop, slide duration, slideshow music, go list management), FM radio listening and preset programming (up to 30), and using the built-in microphone for voice recordings.

Central Huron Council heard a presentation from Meighan Wark, Huron County’s Acting CAO, Director of Cultural Services and County Librarian, proposing a renovation project to bring the Clinton Library up to Ontario Public Library Guidelines Monitoring and Accreditation Council accreditation standards and improve services. Wark said the Huron County Library system and its branches (except Clinton) received five-year accreditation in 2015, and that Clinton did not due to accessibility issues and insufficient square footage for full service quality. She explained that the county follows rural, county-specific guideline documents to determine minimum square footage and facility standards, affecting items like shelf height and aisle width. Wark described a partnership model where the county provides staff, materials, furniture, equipment, and library services, while the municipality handles the building, maintenance, and utilities. Next steps include agreeing on required service components and space needs, preparing draft drawings with an architect for council review and community input, and pursuing funding if the project is “shovel-ready.” Council will continue discussions with Wark, with an aim to move toward a more accessible and inclusive library.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture, focusing on the Turing SM design, its memory hierarchy, and major performance and feature improvements. It explains that Turing introduces SM changes including concurrent FP32/INT32 execution, independent thread scheduling, eight mixed-precision Tensor Cores, and an RT Core per SM, along with a partitioned SM layout and a unified L1/shared memory/texture caching approach. It also discusses revamped execution datapaths, increased L1 bandwidth and reconfigurable shared memory, and compression and L2 cache improvements that increase effective bandwidth and delivered performance per CUDA core.  

The passage then covers Turing Tensor Cores with additional INT8/INT4 modes and describes their role in AI inference and deep learning features such as NGX services (e.g., DLSS, InPainting, Super Rez, Slow-Mo). It further details Turing features for data centers (e.g., Tesla T4), display and video engine capabilities, VR-related technologies (VirtualLink/USB-C, multi-view rendering, foveated rendering via VRS), and various graphics pipeline features including Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering.  

Finally, the passage explains Turing ray tracing, including the hybrid rendering approach, denoising, BVH traversal, and how RT Cores accelerate bounding volume hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing. It also provides background on ray tracing mechanics, mentions applications such as ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and summarizes key technologies enabling real-time ray tracing on a single Turing GPU.

The passage reports that Charlie Alliston, 18, was tried at the Old Bailey after hitting and killing Kim Briggs while riding an Olympics-style fixed-wheel track bike on a busy street in east London on February 12. The court heard the bike had no front brake and that Alliston blamed Mrs Briggs, claiming he warned her as she stepped into the road. Mrs Briggs, 44, was taken to hospital but died a week later from catastrophic injuries, including two skull fractures and bleeding on the brain. Prosecutors argued Alliston’s unlawful and dangerous riding caused her death and said reconstructions showed he could have stopped if he had a front brake. The passage also describes posts and tweets Alliston allegedly made after the crash and notes that he denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, as the Lobos defeated Boise State 78-73 on Tuesday night. New Mexico took control late in the first half with an 11-0 run and kept control after Boise State closed to 76-73 with 19.6 seconds left; Brown then went 2-for-2 at the foul line. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14 for New Mexico, and Brown hit 13 of 14 free throws. Chandler Hutchison had a career-high 31 points for Boise State, which never led in the game. The Mountain West standings became more competitive, with Boise State, Colorado State, and Nevada tied at the top with four losses each, and New Mexico one game back. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game for New Mexico with a foot injury. New Mexico next plays at Fresno State, while Boise State plays Wyoming at home.

A Harvard University Institute of Politics poll released Dec. 5 found that 65% of voters aged 18–29 favor Democrats and 33% favor Republicans. Polling director John Della Volpe said political institutions are at a tipping point and that millennials, now the largest generation in the electorate, are becoming more motivated. Key findings include: only 14% of millennials think America is generally headed in the right direction; Trump’s job approval among millennials is 25%; 67% of millennials believe the greatest threats come from forces inside the country; and in an open-ended question, “ourselves” and racism were top responses. The poll also reported that 61% of young Americans want gun laws to be more strict, up from 49% in 2013.

Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is defined as new onset reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (<45%) within the last 3 months of gestation or up to 5 months postpartum, and is a leading cause of maternal death. The study aimed to test the hypothesis that perinatal mood disorders are associated with higher odds of PPCM and other cardiac events during pregnancy and postpartum. Using a retrospective cohort of pregnant and postpartum hospitalizations from 2017–2019 in the HCUP-NIS database, patients with prior mood disorders were compared with those without. Among 2.2 million hospitalizations (168,729 with mood disorder diagnoses), PPCM incidence was higher with mood disorders (0.12% vs 0.05%, p<0.001), as were other cardiac events including a composite adverse cardiac event outcome (0.36% vs 0.14%, p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.80) and the composite adverse cardiac events (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.81), including pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39–1.89). Maternal death was not associated with mood disorders (p=0.253). The study concludes that perinatal mood disorders are associated with increased rates of PPCM and other cardiac events, with implications for mental health care and prevention efforts, while noting limitations related to ICD-10 coding and inpatient-only data.

Preempt announced new technology integrations for its Preempt Behavioral Firewall that provide deeper UEBA context for more accurate internal network threat detection and additional enforcement options to stop threats automatically. The integrations include single sign-on vendors (Okta), cloud directories (Azure Active Directory), VPN gateways, and enforcement integrations with SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator, and HP Aruba ClearPass. The firewall uses user/entity role and behavior and targeted assets to respond in real time to suspicious activity, with enforcement options to redirect, confirm, or block threats. The announcement highlights improved contextual threat detection and the ability to apply granular enterprise-wide policies to block, notify, or challenge users to verify identity.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards in this mode, validates the operation voltage range, identifies cards, and requests each card to publish its Relative Card Address (RCA) using CMD lines only, separately per card. During identification, cards operate at the SD clock frequency. In SD mode, CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE) places each card into Idle State regardless of its current state; cards in Inactive State are unaffected. After power-on or CMD0, all cards have CMD lines in input mode, initialized with RCA=0x0000 and a default driver strength at 400 kHz (with driver strength selection varying by 3.3V or 1.8V signaling). In UHS-II mode, RCA is not cleared by CMD0 and is kept as the device ID.

To handle unknown supported voltages, the host issues CMD0 with a specified voltage and then uses CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND) to verify the SD Memory Card interface operating condition. The card checks the CMD8 argument and the host checks the CMD8 response; VHS in the argument indicates the supplied voltage. The card echoes the supply voltage and check pattern if it can operate; otherwise, it returns no response and stays idle. CMD8 is mandatory before the first ACMD41 to initialize SDHC or SDXC cards, and receipt of CMD8 indicates support for Physical Layer Version 2.00 or later.

The passage contains remarks reflecting on a tough loss in a playoff series, with credit given to teammates for their hard work and to the opposing team for playing well. It discusses home-ice advantage, the loud home crowd, and the importance of preparation and aggressiveness in the playoffs. The speaker also addresses fan reactions in New Jersey, contrasting boos and cheers, and talks about aiming for the “big silver” Stanley Cup. They congratulate a retired player’s successor, discuss approaching the next season one game at a time, and express sadness about not winning the Cup primarily for their mother, then planning to move on after the loss.

U.S. police are expected to announce charges against 12 Turkish security agents in Washington, D.C. related to violence during Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s visit last month; seven face felony charges and five misdemeanors. A separate police statement says two men involved in a violent altercation outside the Turkish ambassador’s residence have been arrested—Sinan Narin in Virginia and Eyup Yildirim in New Jersey—on assault-related charges. The passage also notes U.S. officials criticized Turkey’s government after Erdogan’s security forces pushed past police and broke up a protest on May 16.

The passage explains how to receive weekly notifications of documentation updates on ti.com and to review revision history for change details. It also describes TI E2E support forums as a source for verified answers and design help, and notes that linked content is provided “AS IS.” It lists trademarks (multiSPI™ and TI E2E™), provides an electrostatic discharge (ESD) handling caution, and includes a revision history noting changes from Revision (June 2024) to Revision A (May 2025), including document status changes for ADS8685W and ADS8689W. The passage further discusses mechanical/packaging/orderable information being current but subject to change, includes product information footnotes, and provides extensive legal disclaimers and notices.

Mary Meeker’s annual Internet Trends report includes a China chapter compiled by Hillhouse Capital. Slide 246 notes a sharp increase in time spent watching short-form videos (under five minutes) in China, up 360% in 2017, alongside a shift away from long-form and ahead of live and game streaming. Most Chinese consumers use only one short-video service, with Douyin and Kuaishou cited as major players (about 100 million daily active users each and about 52 minutes per viewer per day), and strong daily return rates among monthly users. The report says advertising budgets for long-form video overtook network TV in China last year, and that short-form is nearing long-form viewing time, suggesting content providers should focus on capturing ad revenue.

Stocks rebounded on Wednesday after plunging the day before, as investors hoped Italy could avoid new elections and said there were “new possibilities” to form a government. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq rose, and smaller, U.S.-focused companies gained more, with the Russell 2000 hitting a record high. Bank stocks recovered as bond yields increased, while energy companies rose with gains in U.S. and Brent crude. The euro and dollar moved higher against the yen, European indexes were mixed, and U.S. Treasury yields rose. Oil-related gains occurred despite recent reports that OPEC and Russia might increase production. Gold, silver, and copper also rose.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated May 16, 2018, reporting actions taken at its 2018 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. Stockholders approved amendments and restatements to the Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan and the Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, increasing available share reserves by 23,000,000 and 13,500,000 shares, respectively. The report also summarizes voting results: election of eleven directors for one-year terms; an advisory approval of named executive officers’ compensation; ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered accounting firm for fiscal year ending January 27, 2019; approval of the 2007 Plan; and approval of the 2012 Plan. Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2 include the amended and restated plan texts. The report was signed May 21, 2018 by Rebecca Peters.

Apple’s HomePod initially received praise for sound quality and setup but was criticized for lacking Android compatibility and for Siri’s shortcomings, and it did not yet support AirPlay 2. With the iOS 11.4 update, Apple rolled out AirPlay 2, enabling iOS devices to stream music to multiple AirPlay devices (previously limited to Macs), adding multi-room support and stereo HomePod pairing, and increasing the network buffer to prevent interruptions during network issues. AirPlay 2 also lets music continue streaming during phone calls or while using other media. Apple also added calendar support to Siri on HomePod, including viewing meetings and events and adding items, but calendar changes can be made by anyone using personal request, and individual voice recognition is not enabled. The iOS 11.4 update also includes Messages in iCloud, which stores messages in iCloud so deletions and message history sync across devices, but it increases iCloud storage usage. AirPlay 2 support has been announced by several third-party companies. The iOS 11.4 update is available for download now.

The appellate court modified and affirmed an order with costs. It found the Supreme Court erred in granting summary judgment dismissing plaintiffs’ bad faith settlement negotiation claims, concluding there was sufficient evidence for a jury to find the defendant, as primary carrier, negotiated in bad faith by not timely offering its policy limits and that plaintiffs could be damaged. The court cited testimony that plaintiffs would have accepted $1,000,000 instead of a $1,350,000 settlement if earlier offers had been made, and testimony that a timely offer would have resulted in a $1,000,000 settlement; it held witness credibility and evidentiary probative value were for the jury, creating a triable issue of fact. The court also affirmed dismissal of plaintiffs’ fourth cause of action alleging violations of Insurance Law § 2601.

A study led by Dr Maiken Nedergaard found that low doses of alcohol can improve brain function by increasing glymphatic system activity, which helps clear metabolic waste and proteins associated with Alzheimer’s disease and dementia. The study in mice given alcohol equivalent to about 2.5 drinks of wine per day showed less brain inflammation and more efficient removal of waste than control “teetotal” mice, with similar cognitive and motor test results. In contrast, intermediate and very high alcohol doses reduced glymphatic function, and high doses over a long period increased inflammation, impairing cognitive abilities and motor skills. The study also reported that moderate alcohol effects on glymphatic function were not permanent after chronic exposure ended, and that acute effects depended on dosage. The research was published in Scientific Reports.

The passage describes external synchronization and primary-secondary operation for TPS7H500x-SP controllers, including how the RT and SYNC pins are used, required external clock characteristics, clock inversion in secondary operation, and resulting phase shifts. It summarizes primary output (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier output (SRA/SRB) behavior, dead time and leading edge blank time programmability, pulse skipping conditions, duty cycle programmability via DCL, and current sense/PWM generation using CS_ILIM and COMP/2 for peak current limiting. It also explains hiccup mode timing controlled by a capacitor on HICC, external fault protection via FAULT pin thresholds and delay behavior, slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation, and guidance for selecting compensation components. Finally, it outlines thermal shutdown behavior, fixed-frequency peak current mode controller functional description, and general application and layout recommendations, including routing and grounding practices.

The passage explains how modern “coach speak” around run fits is necessary because defenses often adapt to concepts like Air Raid and RPOs. It stresses that run fits vary by team philosophy and talent, with no one-size-fits-all approach, and that coaches must translate terms like “front spacing” and “gapped out fits” into executable schemes for players. It outlines key influences on run fits—front spacing (even vs. odd) and the coverage played behind the fit—and describes how “spacing” can also refer to 7-, 8-, or 9-man box/run-fit concepts based on defenders in the box versus the offense. The passage then details common tools and second-level fitting approaches for 7-man (“stack track and fallback” in zone; “spill-overlap” versus power), 8-man (“indicator fitting” versus zone; “lever-spill-lever” versus power), and 9-man spacing (often “maxed out” with cover 0/quarters-related ideas), including how these concepts differ against zone and gap/power schemes. It concludes with examples of run fits in a 3-4 defense across 7-, 8-, and 9-man spacing, noting how front type (odd/even) and overhang responsibilities affect the fit.

Andrew Lo discusses market liquidity and low interest rates during a period of stock and bond market fear, noting that banks and other agencies are waiting before resuming lending and that the Fed is working to maintain liquid markets. He then shifts to the course topic of derivatives and hedging, arguing that fear can impair rational decision-making and proposing that technology could improve transparency and liquidity in complex securities markets (e.g., CDOs/CDSs). 

He explains why mark-to-market accounting is important, critiques proposals to suspend it, and defines forward and futures contracts. Lo describes forward contracts as customized, legally binding agreements made today to transact at a fixed price in the future, with long/short positions and a property that the contract is worth zero at inception. He illustrates counterparty risk and illiquidity in forward contracts using a soybean example, then contrasts futures contracts as standardized and marked to market daily to reduce counterparty risk. Futures are also cleared through an intermediary (a clearing corporation) to improve safety and liquidity. He concludes by describing key features of commodity futures contracts, including standard quantities, margin requirements, margin calls, and that many futures are cash settled while some can involve physical delivery.

Sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel announced he will start his professional career rather than return to Kentucky for his junior season. He said he received positive feedback and believes he is ready to enter the 2018 draft, keeping his name in the draft. Gabriel declared for the draft without hiring an agent, did not receive an invitation to the NBA scouting combine, and averaged 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds while starting seven games, shooting 39.6% from 3-point range and leading Kentucky with 40 blocked shots. Kentucky head coach John Calipari said Gabriel is a position-less big man who can shoot and guard multiple positions and that he has made progress from freshman to sophomore year. The article also notes other roster changes, including PJ Washington returning, potential addition of Reid Travis, and players leaving for the draft or transfers.

North Carolina is expanding child care academies, which are short training programs intended to place new early childhood educators into classrooms faster than traditional routes. In at least 11 counties, early childhood education agencies and community colleges offer academies lasting two to six weeks (about 20–64 hours) at little to no cost, customized to local community needs. The programs are designed around two models: a classroom-ready model (qualifies workers for licensed child care facilities but not as lead teachers) and a teaching credential model (includes additional EDU 119 training and leads to a continuing education credit that counts in place of EDU 119 to qualify for lead teacher status). Interest is increasing due to staffing shortages among licensed providers, and Mary Olvera said additional community colleges plan to offer academies. Funding includes a $1.476 million pilot included in the North Carolina House budget and DCDEE grants up to $50,000 for up to 10 UNC system schools. The passage lists counties offering academies and describes how five specific programs operate and are funded, including outcomes such as students graduating and moving into jobs or continuing education.

The lecture explains how to describe stimulated light forces using the dressed atom picture. It reviews that a laser-driven two-level atom is treated by rediagonalizing the atom–laser Hamiltonian, then allowing spontaneous emission to connect dressed states. In this framework, spontaneous emission couples excited and ground bare states, leading to matrix elements and transition rates that determine populations and coherences. In the strong Rabi frequency (“secular”) limit, the optical Bloch equations decouple into separate rate equations for populations and coherences, yielding different relaxation times and thus different Mollow-triplet feature widths. The lecture then discusses how non-adiabatic “time lag” in population adjustments during motion through a laser beam produces friction and cooling, explaining blue molasses. It contrasts average dipole forces (from steady-state populations) with heating and cooling arising from force fluctuations during radiative cascades between dressed states, and describes heating in terms of momentum diffusion. The discussion extends to Sisyphus cooling in a blue-detuned standing wave, where spontaneous emission preferentially occurs near anti-nodes, causing atoms to climb hills more often than descend them. In a perturbative large-detuning limit, the lecture derives cooling rates and heating to argue that the lowest achievable temperature in a standing wave is set by the lattice depth, implying laser cooling cannot fully localize atoms in a simple two-level optical lattice. The lecture concludes with physical interpretations of dipole potentials and optical trapping, including a classical refraction-based explanation (used in optical tweezers), and provides a course outlook for upcoming topics.

The lecture discusses trajectory optimization as a form of “policy search,” where control systems are parameterized by a vector of parameters and optimized to minimize a cost \(J\). It focuses on open-loop trajectory optimization, using shooting methods and then two gradient-computation approaches: an adjoint method (forward simulation plus backward adjoint integration) and RTRL/BPTT-style forward-only gradient computation (tracking a matrix of \(\partial x/\partial \alpha\)). The lecture then compares this with direct collocation, which explicitly includes state variables in the optimization and enforces dynamics as constraints, enabling efficient cost evaluation and gradient computation. Examples shown include optimizing a pendulum and an acrobot using SNOPT/SQP and direct collocation, along with a geometric path-planning example illustrating local minima. The lecture concludes by noting that these methods are local optimizers but can still work well in practice, and it previews trajectory stabilization (e.g., with LQR) to improve resulting trajectories.

A Warren County family near Norwalk, Iowa says the Iowa Department of Transportation’s I-35 highway expansion affected the only well they had, leaving them without clean water for about two months. The family, including Erin and Mark Paschell, said they were told the well area would not be dug within a certain limit, but the project affected their well, forcing them to bring in gallons of water daily for cooking and limiting bathing and laundry. They say they struggled to get help through DOT communications. DOT communications director Andrea Henry said the department is actively looking into the timing and working to resolve issues causing the lack of water. The family says connecting to rural water may take 30–60 days, so they hired a contractor to lay a water line by digging a trench, and they believe they will not get their well back. Erin said the family recently received an offer from the DOT to stay in a hotel until the issue is solved and was told they would be reimbursed for cleaning supplies.

The passage describes COVID-19 in Kuwait and a retrospective review of 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed in Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital from March 2020 to March 2022. Kuwait’s first SARS‑CoV‑2 case was reported on February 24, 2020, and strict Ministry of Health measures were implemented. The study included critically ill ICU patients who required tracheostomy after intubation and mechanical ventilation, with recorded baseline characteristics, timing variables, and complications categorized as intra-operative, early (≤7 days), or late (>7 days). Tracheostomy timing followed a departmental protocol of performing percutaneous tracheostomy after at least 7 days from intubation (with limited earlier exceptions). Over the study period, the mean time from intubation to tracheostomy was 17.4 days, complications occurred in 23% of cases (most commonly minor bleeding), 63% of patients died from COVID-19 complications, and 37% were discharged, with some decannulated prior to discharge. The authors conclude that percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients and suggest performing it as soon as possible after the 7th day, while acknowledging limitations including no comparison arm with open tracheostomy and lack of PCR testing of staff.

Florida Panthers coach Bob Boughner said injured goaltenders Roberto Luongo and James Reimer could become more active and possibly return to the lineup next week. Luongo has been out since Dec. 4 and missed 23 consecutive games, while Reimer, sidelined with a groin injury since Jan. 23, was scheduled to miss at least two weeks that will be reached on Tuesday. Boughner said both would be hoped to practice Monday, pending goaltending coach Robb Tallas, and noted that both reported feeling great after practice today. With them out, Harri Sateri and Samuel Montembeault have been the goaltending duo, and Boughner said Sateri’s play led Florida to delay Montembeault’s NHL debut and to keep him starting. If Luongo or Reimer returns next week, Montembeault’s opportunity would likely shrink, with a possible AHL assignment. The Panthers also expect Jamie McGinn to return Saturday night after missing two games with an upper-body injury, and their projected lineup and scratches/injured reserve were provided for the game vs. Detroit.

The passage describes backtesting an “end of month” (turn of the month) trading effect in Bitcoin using data from Yahoo! Finance starting in 2014. It notes that the strategy optimizes entry and exit timing by entering at the close x days before a new month and exiting n days after, accounting for Bitcoin’s 24/7 market. Results from 100 simulations indicate an end of month effect that could be used as a viable turn of the month trading strategy, with reported average gain per trade of 3.3%, CAGR of 41.8%, time in the market of 16%, and max drawdown of 25%. The passage says the backtest is curve-fitted to some degree, but that performance around turn-of-the-month entries and exits is higher than random periods of the same length. It also mentions that adjusting entry days and adding variables reduced drawdowns and made the equity curve smoother, though with fewer trades and lower CAGR. The authors state they do not reveal the full strategy and conclude that Bitcoin shows a positive end of month effect that can be used as a turn of the month strategy, while offering free resources for developing trading strategies.

The Auditor General, Daniel Domelevo, surcharged 62 organisations for receiving state payments without available documentation. Ninety-year-old Muriel Diaz was born in Shrewsbury and trained as a nurse and midwife at hospitals in London and Bristol. She felt called to missionary work and went to Peru after dreaming of it, where she met her husband Alberto and married him in 1969. For 32 years, she and Alberto lived on the Peruvian coast; she worked in a jungle clinic for six weeks each year as the only nurse, with no doctor nearby. She later returned to the jungle annually for 18 years until leaving Peru in 32 years due to rising terrorism. In 1995 the couple moved to Penparc near Cardigan, where Diaz volunteered for Barnardo’s charity shop for 20 years, repairing donated clothes every Thursday. Yale-New Haven Hospital brought three collection actions for unpaid medical services rendered on multiple occasions. The defendants, Clifford Mitchell and Laureen Wilczynski (with Vincent Wilczynski not appearing), filed answers, two special defenses, and counterclaims that are functionally identical across the cases. The first special defense alleges the hospital violated the Hill-Burton Act regulations and therefore cannot recover; the second alleges the defendants qualified for free care under hospital bed funds trusts and the hospital failed to provide required notice, also barring recovery. The counterclaims allege these statutory violations constitute unfair or deceptive acts under CUTPA and seek damages and attorney’s fees. The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing there is no genuine issue of material fact and that the defenses and counterclaims fail as a matter of law. The court held the first special defense is legally valid, found the second special defense similarly applicable, and ruled that private causes of action exist under both the Hill-Burton Act and the hospital bed funds statute, allowing CUTPA claims based on alleged violations. However, the court found the counterclaims raise factual issues not suitable for summary judgment. The court also rejected the hospital’s claim that the Hill-Burton Act preempts CUTPA. The hospital’s motions for summary judgment in all three cases were denied.

Hansi Flick said he made mistakes during summer talks with Barcelona goalkeeper Marc-Andre Ter Stegen, acknowledging that communication could have been handled better. Cancer can develop without noticeable symptoms, so the NHS provides cancer screening to detect early signs before cancer becomes more advanced, improving the chance of successful treatment and potentially saving lives. The passage explains how screening works, which programmes are available, and which cancers they can detect. It states that cancer screening has saved around 90,000 lives in the last five years and that screening is free through the NHS with invitations sent based on age and the national schedule.

In the UK, the NHS offers three main screening programmes: cervical screening every five years for people aged 25 to 64 to test for high-risk HPV; breast screening every three years for people aged 50 to 71 using a mammogram; and bowel screening every two years for people aged 50 to 74 using a home FIT kit to detect tiny amounts of blood in stool. The passage also notes that some screening (not part of national programmes) may be available locally and can be discussed with a doctor, and it advises seeking medical advice if concerned about symptoms at any age rather than waiting for a screening kit. It includes information on when screening typically starts, how to arrange rebooking if an invite is missed, and an exception for people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), who are recommended to have yearly mammograms starting at age 40.

Grigor Dimitrov defeated American Jared Donaldson at the French Open after Donaldson, hampered by cramp, used an underarm serve. The lecture begins the discussion of computing the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and introduces the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm as a highly efficient method derived from properties of the DFT. The FFT enables much faster computation than direct DFT calculation, which requires on the order of \(N^2\) complex multiplications and additions. The lecture explains how the inverse DFT is essentially equivalent to the DFT computation. It derives a decimation-in-time FFT for \(N\) expressed as powers of 2 by splitting the input sequence into even- and odd-indexed subsequences, computing two \(N/2\)-point DFTs, and combining them using a factor involving powers of \(W_N\). The explanation uses flow graphs with “butterfly” computations and discusses periodicity that avoids redundant calculations. The lecture then extends the decomposition recursively (e.g., \(N/2\) into \(N/4\), etc.) to show that for \(N\) a power of 2, the computation cost scales proportionally to \(N \log_2 N\) rather than \(N^2\). Finally, it describes a modification to reduce the number of multiplications by rearranging the butterfly computation, and notes that the input order into the FFT flow graph is a bit-reversed order, which will be important in the next lecture.

The lecture introduces Szemerédi’s graph regularity lemma, explaining that a large dense graph can be partitioned into a bounded number of vertex parts so that between most pairs of parts the bipartite graph behaves “random-like.” It defines edge density and the notion of an ε-regular pair of vertex subsets, where subsets of sufficient size have edge density close to the overall density between the larger sets. It then defines an ε-regular partition by requiring that only a small weighted fraction of pairs of parts are not ε-regular, allowing some “blemishes.” The lemma is stated: for every ε there is a constant M(ε) such that every graph has an ε-regular partition into at most M parts, with the number of parts independent of the graph size.

The proof strategy is outlined using an “energy increment argument.” The energy of a partition is defined as a mean square of edge densities between parts, lying between 0 and 1. Refining a partition never decreases energy, and if the partition is not ε-regular then a refinement yields an energy increase by at least an ε^5 amount. Repeated refinement must stop after a bounded number of steps because energy cannot exceed 1, producing an ε-regular partition. The discussion also covers that the resulting M can be extremely large, and notes that better bounds cannot be obtained in general due to a result by Tim Gowers. Finally, an equitable version of the lemma is discussed, where partitions can be made to have parts of almost equal size, but the proof must control energy during “rebalancing”; simply refining after obtaining an ε-regular partition does not preserve ε-regularity.

The passage explains how digital piracy emerged after Napster (June 1, 1999) and describes its persistence despite technical and legal efforts. It argues digital piracy damages licensed revenue streams by offering consumers convenient, low-cost access to content, citing an ICC estimate of $213 billion in 2015 and projections to $384–$856 billion by 2020. The authors frame digital piracy as a business challenge and research question about designing business models to minimize its negative impact, emphasizing technology’s role in both enabling piracy and supporting counter-responses.

The study presents a qualitative, theory-driven multiple case analysis of Netflix and Spotify, using archival documents and nine expert interviews. It analyzes how piracy’s value proposition varies across content categories (audio, film, written works, interactive works) and summarizes that piracy is generally more attractive for audio than for film, and more for both than for written and interactive works due to ease of creating, sharing, and consuming copies.

In the comparison of business models, the passage highlights that Spotify and Netflix respond to piracy mainly through subscription-based, streaming services with free tiers/trials, strong navigation and discovery features (including recommender systems), improved service quality and device accessibility (including offline options), and social/community functionality. It includes a causal loop logic showing how free tiers attract users, licensing agreements expand catalogs, and community and personalization increase willingness to pay. The conclusion states that digital distribution can outperform piracy primarily by improving the consumption experience, and suggests the findings may extend beyond music and film to other content categories.

The passage introduces indexed containers as a generalization of simple containers for representing parameterized datatypes corresponding to strictly positive types and set endofunctors. It gives an example of vectors as a Nat-indexed container and explains that such indexed containers correspond to polynomial-like functors. It discusses monads on endofunctors, particularly polynomial monads, and reviews different notions of morphisms used in related work. The authors’ contribution is to extend Uustalu’s characterization of monoid structures from non-indexed to indexed containers, outlining the monoidal structure corresponding to composition and proving the correspondence with monad structures. They use the characterization to describe products of indexed container monads and indexed variants of state and writer monads, formalized in Cubical Agda, and outline the structure and formalization details of the paper.

C.J. McCollum scored a career-high 43 points to lead the Portland Trail Blazers to a 95-89 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday night, despite Damian Lillard missing his fourth straight game with a sprained left ankle. McCollum made 16 of 25 shots, including a 30-foot 3-pointer late in the fourth to put the game out of reach; Mason Plumlee had 18 points and eight rebounds, and Evan Turner added 11 points. The Blazers had lost seven of their last eight games, and the Wolves fell to 9-11 when they lead by double digits. Walmart-owned Sam’s Club will expand its daily hours to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. starting this weekend, with the first hour reserved for Plus members and curbside pickup available from 7 a.m. Sundays are the biggest change, moving from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Exceptions are Christmas Eve (closing at 6 p.m.) and Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, New Year’s Day, and Easter (closed). The Qnap TVS-x73 NAS series is offered in 4, 6, and 8-bay models with a metal design and gold finish, and is powered by an AMD RX-421BD quad-core APU. It supports dual-channel DDR4 RAM (up to 64GB), four Gigabit LAN ports, two built-in M.2 SSD slots with Qtier Technology, up to 1,172 MB/s throughput, and two PCIe slots (one pre-installed with a dual-port USB 3.1 Type-A card and one for an optional dual-port 10GbE network card).
