Mariano Del Cid-Mendez appeals his conviction and sentence for illegal reentry. His constitutional challenge to 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b)(1), (2) is foreclosed by Almendarez-Torres v. United States, and the court notes it remains binding under circuit precedent. Del Cid also argues that the district court erred by sentencing him under the mandatory Sentencing Guidelines regime held unconstitutional in United States v. Booker. The Government concedes the issue was preserved, and because the record does not show the district court would have imposed the same sentence under an advisory regime, the Government did not meet its burden to show harmless error. The sentence is vacated and the case is remanded for further proceedings.

The passage describes how the Omicron SARS-CoV-2 variant differed from Delta in complication risk and in the age groups contributing to community transmission. It notes that earlier variants were mainly spread by younger adults (18–35) and older adolescents, while Omicron increased the role of children. It presents a method using a relative risk (RR) statistic based on shifts in ICU admissions before versus after epidemic-wave peaks to assess each age group’s per-individual contribution to transmission. Using French ICU admissions data from March 1 to Dec. 29, 2022, the study defines four Omicron epidemic waves and analyzes nine age groups. Across waves, children aged 10–19 played the greatest relative role in the Spring, Summer, and first Autumn waves; the greatest relative role in the Autumn-Winter wave shifted to adults aged 30–39, followed by ages 40–49 and over 80. The discussion links these findings to school-related outbreaks and changes in immunity, and concludes that increasing booster vaccination coverage for all adults (and possibly children) may help mitigate transmission, with additional efforts to limit spread among the elderly, including long-term care facilities.

Ryan Taylor and Jaylon Brown each scored 19 points as the University of Evansville defeated Southern Illinois 73-61 at the Ford Center. Evansville, led by Brown and Taylor’s 12-for-19 shooting and 12-for-13 free throws, got six points each from Dru Smith and David Howard. Southern Illinois had three players in double figures, led by Mike Rodriguez with 20 points, including nine made free throws, plus 14 from Sean Lloyd and 12 from Thik Bowl. Evansville led for much of the first half, which ended with Southern Illinois ahead 33-31 after a late push. The Salukis took further control early in the second half, but Evansville rallied with multiple runs, including a Brown triple to tie and a Smith charge and triple to take the lead. Southern Illinois briefly regained the advantage, but Rodriguez’s third triple gave the first double-digit lead, and the Salukis ultimately led by up to 15 before the final score. The program honored former head coach Jim Crews before the game.

Australia’s prime minister Malcolm Turnbull said China has an obligation to use its “enormous leverage” to bring nuclear-armed North Korea back from the brink, following North Korea’s failed missile test and ahead of US Vice President Mike Pence’s visit to Australia. Turnbull called North Korea a reckless threat and said the heaviest obligation is on China to pull North Korea back from threatening neighbors. He noted Australia’s good relationship with China but said China faces pressure, particularly from the US, to rein in Pyongyang. The passage also says China has previously opposed dramatic action due to concerns about regime collapse and refugees, but US threats have led China to pursue a tougher line, including suspending coal imports. Pence is scheduled to meet Turnbull in Sydney on Saturday.

Indian equity markets rose for the fourth consecutive week ended Friday, boosted by forecasts of normal monsoon rains, healthy IT-sector earnings, supportive global cues, and expectations of solid corporate results. The BSE Sensex gained 222.93 points (0.65%) to close at 34,415.58, while the NSE Nifty50 rose 83.45 points (0.80%) to close at 10,564.05. Gains were partially trimmed by higher crude oil prices, a weakening rupee, and heavy selling in banking stocks tied to expectations of a likely hawkish RBI stance. Weekly WPI inflation eased to 2.47% in March, and the rupee weakened to 66.13 per dollar. Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth Rs 2,821.24 crore, while domestic institutions bought Rs 2,124.16 crore. Sectorally, IT, metal, FMCG and realty led gains, while PSU banks, energy, and bank indices were among the major losers; TCS rose nearly 7% to a new high.

Randall Margraves, father of three alleged Nassar victims, tried to attack disgraced ex-sports doctor Larry Nassar in a Michigan courtroom after a judge denied his request for a few minutes alone with him in a locked room. He was blocked by an attorney and tackled by sheriff’s deputies, and later apologized. Judge Janice Cunningham said she would not punish him, but ruled it was unacceptable to “combat assault with assault.” The incident occurred during Nassar’s third and final sentencing hearing on assault charges related to his work with Twistars, after which the judge resumed the hearing. An assistant attorney general told families to use words rather than violence. More than 30 victims have made statements during this hearing, which began Wednesday and is expected to continue into next week. A previous hearing ended last week with Nassar receiving up to 175 years in prison, and he had already been sentenced to 60 years on child pornography charges.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling used the Hubble Space Telescope to survey massive galaxy clusters and discovered the distant quiescent galaxy eMACSJ1341-QG-1, which is magnified 30 times by gravitational lensing from the cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441. The magnification and distortion are attributed to the cluster’s gravitational effect on space-time. The finding sets a new record for the magnification of a rare quiescent background galaxy and provides an opportunity to study its stellar populations and reconstruct its undistorted shape and properties. Follow-up observations are underway using telescopes in Chile and on Maunakea, and the results were published in *Astrophysical Journal Letters*.

The passage describes Larry Connors’ Multiple Days Up (MDU) and Multiple Days Down (MDD) trading strategy from Chapter 6 of *High Probability Trading*. The strategy focuses on mean reversion in ETFs, buying when an ETF has dropped 4 out of the last 5 trading days under certain conditions, and selling when the ETF closes above its 5-day moving average, with no stop-loss. Tests were originally done through December 31, 2008, with results shown for the original 20 ETFs and additional ETFs through December 2020. Portfolio simulations from 2000–December 2020 used up to five concurrent positions (20% equity each), with the capital compounded and no commissions or slippage; the passage reports the strategy’s comparatively low profit factor versus other mean-reversion strategies and notes it may be improved because some ETFs may not fit mean reversion. When adjusted to trade only SPY and QQQ, the passage reports 287 trades, profit factor 1.82, max drawdown 12%, CAGR 2.4%, and 7.7% time in the market. It also states shorting is more difficult, provides equity curve results for a shorts-only portfolio, and reports that with SPY and QQQ (max two positions) the win ratio was 65% and the average gain was 0.68%.

Around 400 students at a suburban St. Louis school received part of the day off Friday after a 9-foot-long, 70-pound boa constrictor escaped from a biology class enclosure. Officials were alerted around 10 a.m., and students were sent home shortly afterward. The snake was found beneath the floor wrapped around pipes after the ceramic floor was ripped up to retrieve her. A broken hinge on the enclosure was blamed. The snake had been adopted by a biology teacher and later left at the school after the teacher retired.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, where a chestnut orchard yielded a robust harvest in 2017 and drew interest from local bakers, brewers, and distillers. The American chestnut was largely lost to blight in the early 1900s, so consumers shifted to chestnuts from other countries; the Bryants, David and Kim, began planting chestnut trees in 2003, testing 200 trees and later hand-planting more than 1,600 Dunstan trees. After harsh winter conditions and cicadas threatened the orchard between 2009 and 2014, the 2015 harvest improved and demand grew, with shipments reaching Richmond and Washington, DC. The 2017 harvest produced at least 3,000 pounds of chestnuts, and processing and storage occur on-site from mid-September through late October. Chestnuts are graded, washed, sanitized, dried, and kept in cold storage before roasting; buyers can purchase whole, retail, or peeled products. Virginia Chestnuts is also involved in local dining events and is used in breads, Thanksgiving stuffing, beer, desserts, and other dishes, with sales promoted via social media and its website.

A near-complete fossil skull discovered in eastern Utah belongs to a new species, *Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch*, described as half mammal and half reptile, with buck teeth and molars for crushing plants. The findings, published in *Nature* on May 16, suggest the Pangea split occurred about 15 million years later than previously thought and that reptile-like mammals evolved rapidly across several continents, occupying diverse ecological niches. The study also updates understanding of how mammals evolved and dispersed during the age of dinosaurs, noting the animal had hair, suckled its young, and laid eggs like a platypus. The skull was discovered on Bureau of Land Management lands northeast of Arches National Park and later found in the lab under a dinosaur specimen named *Hippodraco*. The fossil is publicly held and displayed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

The study found AMP grazing could offset greenhouse gas emissions and that the finishing phase might act as a net carbon sink, while feedlot emissions were higher mainly due to fertilizer-related nitrogen emissions. Researchers measured finishing phase performance, greenhouse gas sources (including digestion, manure, and feed production), and carbon losses from soil erosion. The passage also discusses potential improvements for feedlots (less fertilizer and cover crops) and for AMP systems (high-density grazing with plant recovery), with Rowntree emphasizing environmental stewardship and the coexistence of cattle operations with healthy waterways.

The Second Circuit affirms the district court’s September 25, 2002 judgment denying Rodney Nicholson’s habeas corpus petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2254. Nicholson, incarcerated on a New York second-degree murder conviction, argued that the state courts violated due process under Chambers v. Mississippi by ruling that hearsay in Darnell Phelps’s confession was inadmissible. The court assumes Chambers may apply to retrial motions but concludes Nicholson fails to show the state courts “mechanistically” rejected reliable hearsay evidence. It finds no abuse of discretion and notes concerns about the confession’s reliability, including inconsistency with an earlier denial of knowledge, inability to test reliability through cross-examination at retrial, and corroboration of the eyewitness testimony. The court therefore holds Nicholson cannot demonstrate a due process violation and affirms the denial of habeas relief.

During a government shutdown after Tuesday, millions of federal workers may miss paychecks, depending on how long the shutdown lasts, but members of Congress will continue to get paid. This is attributed to Article I, Section 6 of the Constitution, which requires senators and representatives to receive compensation, and the 27th Amendment, which delays changes to that compensation until after the next election. Lawmakers’ salaries have been funded through mandatory spending since 1981, which is not affected by shutdowns. Some lawmakers have introduced efforts to dock their pay during shutdowns, but they can still choose to accept pay and donate it or forfeit it to the Treasury.

A pipe bomb strapped to a man exploded in an underground passageway near Times Square on Monday morning, injuring the suspect and three other people during the morning rush hour. Mayor Bill de Blasio and Police Commissioner James P. O’Neill called it an attempted terror attack. The suspect, identified as 27-year-old Akayed Ullah, was treated for injuries described as non-life-threatening. Officials said he was inspired by the Islamic State group but had not had direct contact, and that he lives in Brooklyn and may be of Bangladeshi descent. Authorities described the device as a low-tech explosive attached with Velcro and plastic ties and were investigating how it was made. The explosion caused smoke and triggered a large emergency response, disrupting subway and bus service near the Port Authority terminal; injuries to others included ringing in the ears and headaches. White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders said President Donald Trump was briefed.

Ready to Learn (RTL), a program at Helping Hands Hawaii (HHH), holds its annual school supply drive for students in need from June 1 to July 31, 2017. Low-income and homeless students will receive free basic educational tools, and American Savings Bank (ASB) branches statewide will serve as collection sites from June 14 to July 14, with donations kept on each island. RTL creates school supply kits from donations and bulk-purchased supplies; kits are valued at about $10 and include items such as notebooks, crayons, portfolios, glue, scissors, pens, calculators, composition books, erasers, folder paper, rulers, and backpacks. As of April 2017, RTL had raised over $12,000 and collected enough supplies to form 3,115 kits valued at about $31,000, benefiting more than 6,000 students. Individuals and corporate partners can donate, organize drives, volunteer to pack kits, or apply through the RTL Community Partner Application; online, mail, and in-person donation options are listed for the June 1 to July 31, 2017 period. The passage describes application and design considerations for the UC1825B-SP controller. The oscillator generates a sawtooth waveform controlled by RT (set first based on desired maximum duty cycle) and CT (chosen based on desired frequency and DMAX), with recommended RT values from 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ and DMAX less than 70% not recommended. The device is a dual-output controller with integrated drivers for push-pull, supporting half-bridge and full-bridge via external high-side drivers, and it can support current-mode topologies with added slope compensation components. A switching frequency of 215 kHz was selected as a tradeoff between efficiency and bandwidth, with RT and CT chosen as 10 kΩ and 680 pF. Transformer design parameters include turns ratio, primary inductance (selected using a magnetizing current), auxiliary winding turns ratio (using the required auxiliary positive voltage), and an example design using a primary inductance of 120 µH, a transformer turns ratio of 2.2, and an auxiliary turns ratio of 1.5; an output inductor and capacitor values are also discussed. The passage further covers an RCD clamp approach for switch node overshoot, diode and MOSFET voltage-stress considerations, output filter/capacitance selection and ripple attenuation, compensation component placement (Type IIIB), sense resistor use for current limiting, and various PCB layout guidelines to reduce EMI and ensure proper operation. It also includes notes on input voltage range, receiving documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, and packaging/orderable and disclaimer information.

About 200 people gathered in Nottingham’s market square for a vigil supporting Mariam Moustafa, an 18-year-old who died last week after an attack outside the intu Victoria Centre. Her family, including her sister, a former teacher, an Egyptian Coptic priest, and her father Mohamed Moustafa, spoke at the event, calling for answers and an end to violence. The crowd chanted “justice for Mariam,” stood silent, and held a banner with images of Mariam in her hospital bed. Local attendees expressed grief and support, while the vigil was organised by Yousuf Farooq, a Nottingham College pupil and secretary of Nottingham Stand Up To Racism and the Nottingham People's Assembly, who said the event brought people together across ages, races, and creeds.

Analysts questioned whether demand was pulled forward from the fourth quarter, noting that without the subsidy Tesla would need nearly 390,000 deliveries in the final quarter to meet its full-year goal. The regional picture was mixed, with U.S. sales up but weaker performance in Europe and the UK as market share slipped to about 1.5%. Investor reaction was muted due to concerns about sustainability, with attention turning to whether Tesla will adjust pricing, ramp new model launches, or use its energy division to offset slower automotive growth.

The passage describes the Bollinger Band Squeeze trading strategy as a breakout approach that goes in the same direction as a breakout after a period of low volatility. Bollinger Bands are explained as bands around a moving average whose width reflects volatility; they contract during low volatility (“squeeze”) and expand when volatility increases. The strategy’s assumption is that the breakout sets the tone for subsequent days or weeks (depending on timeframe). A backtest is discussed, where the strategy “doesn’t do particularly well” on most assets (with consumer staples as a possible exception), does not beat buy-and-hold (12.5% vs. 14.8%), and is only invested 61% of the time; multiple versions and assets were also reported as unsuccessful. The FAQ section states it differs from mean reversion strategies, can produce “whipsaws,” and emphasizes the need to backtest for positive expectancy. Common mistakes noted are lacking positive expectancy and not following the strategy due to trading biases, and it suggests mechanical trading to help avoid issues. The passage also says strategies may not work across all asset types, contrasting stocks (prone to mean reversion) with commodities (not). It includes brief biographical information about John A. Bollinger, the creator of Bollinger Bands, and mentions related resources such as backtesting code and a collection of trading rules.

The passage describes PFEIFFER v. COMMISSIONER OF INTERNAL REVENUE, a 1937 decision by the Second Circuit regarding the petitioner’s 1931 income tax deficiency of $89,841.75. The corporation made preferred stock distributions as stock dividends to common shareholders in 1928 and 1931, and in 1931 redeemed some of the preferred shares. The Commissioner determined deficiencies because (1) the fair market value of the 1931 preferred stock dividend was not included in income ($629,125), and (2) the redemption proceeds ($200,000) were not included in income. The Board upheld the Commissioner on the first issue, holding the 1931 stock dividend was not exempt under section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, and upheld the second issue as well, finding no taxable income due to a $100 basis and $100 redemption price. The dispute in the appellate decision focused on whether the 1931 preferred stock dividend paid on common stock is exempt under section 115(f). The opinion discusses related case law including Com’r v. Tillotson Mfg. Co., Koshland v. Helvering, and Gowran v. Commissioner, and concludes with “Determination reversed,” with Judge L. Hand dissenting.

The passage discusses Whitmore v. San Francisco Savings Union and related trustees. It holds that failing to present a creditor’s claim against a deceased person’s estate within the statutory period does not extinguish the debt, but only removes the remedy; the estate may assert a defense against an action to recover the demand. Because the debt remained unpaid and the debtor’s estate was not solvent, the majority concludes that equity cannot compel the creditor to surrender its security without payment, so the court reversed and remanded with directions to sustain the demurrer to the complaint. A dissent argues that creditors holding mortgage or trust deed liens must present claims within the statutory period to preserve the lien, and that failing to do so should require release of the legal title so the estate can be administered through probate.

Google canceled the website-hosting registration for the neo-Nazi site Daily Stormer after GoDaddy told it to find a new host. Google said Daily Stormer violated its policies against inciting violence, though it did not specify which content. The site had posted hateful content and, following the death of Heather Heyer at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, web-service companies moved to sever ties. GoDaddy said it gave Daily Stormer 24 hours and that the site violated its terms by promoting or engaging in violence; it said it typically does not act on complaints involving censorship. YouTube terminated Daily Stormer’s channel for hate-speech violations, and Facebook removed links unless captions clearly condemned the content, saying it relies on user flags to remove posts. Google canceled the registration after Daily Stormer registered it via an automated process, and visitors would appear offline until the site registers with another accredited company. Other providers said they were not hosting the site or said it had used services that block public domain information. The actions were described as part of an ongoing effort by tech companies to handle extremist online activity.

He told the National Assembly Transport Committee that laws to streamline the industry already exist but enforcement is a challenge, and that the ministry is working with county transport committees and engaging the traffic department to speed up implementation. Ruiru MP Simon King’ara called for a dedicated motorbike safety authority instead of NTSA and urged the CS to hold accountable those delaying enforcement. He rejected calls to ban boda boda riders from city centres, saying a benchmark mission like one to Rwanda should be considered. The passage also notes that boda boda riders have disputed with county governments, including Nairobi County Government banning them from the CBD.

Investigators found red-stained sheets and an empty box of Coricidin Cold & Cough medicine at Matthew James Phelps’ North Carolina home after he called 911 early on September 1, saying he took cough medicine, had a dream, and woke up to find his wife Lauren stabbed to death. Lauren was alive when police arrived but was pronounced dead after being taken to the hospital. Phelps was taken into custody and is awaiting trial on first-degree murder charges, held without bail at Wake County Jail. After executing a search warrant, investigators seized red-stained bedding, the empty medicine box, four computers, receipts, a mortgage statement, a knife set, credit cards, and Lauren’s iPhone. The couple had been married for less than a year, and Phelps has no criminal record.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics, focusing on bonded microLED/LED display elements that emit single colors (e.g., red, green, blue) and can be combined to form multi-colored images. It discusses limitations of technologies like LCoS/DLP and challenges in producing fine pixel pitch and multi-color displays, then proposes using direct or hybrid bonding to connect optical emitter elements (e.g., LED wafers or chips) to processor carriers (e.g., silicon/CMOS backplanes) with active circuitry for pixel control. It states that direct bonding without adhesive can enable very small pixel pitches (including less than 5 microns or less than 1 micron) and requires carriers with low coefficient of thermal expansion. The passage also describes manufacturing approaches (D2W, D2D, W2W), optical pathways such as waveguides with input/output couplings, and pixel isolation features (e.g., deep trench isolation) to limit crosstalk and support image quality and yield. It further outlines example optical systems and optical assemblies that superimpose monochromatic light from different color elements to produce a polychromatic output for viewing.

The IRS said it is furloughing nearly half of its workforce due to the ongoing government shutdown. About 34,000 IRS workers are being furloughed, while 39,870 employees (53.6%) will remain on the job. The IRS said most operations are closed due to a lapse in appropriations, and an IRS-wide furlough began October 8, 2025, for everyone except identified excepted and exempt employees.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x (Ampere) SM architecture and related hardware features, including dedicated ray tracing cores, concurrent FP32/INT32 execution via a new FP32-capable datapath design, increased unified L1/shared memory capacity and bandwidth, and third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity support. It also discusses second-generation RT Core improvements for faster ray/triangle intersection and motion blur acceleration via an “Interpolate Triangle Position” unit, plus improved power efficiency compared to Turing. The passage further covers expanded memory bandwidth using GDDR6X, the RTX IO technology for GPU-based asset loading and lossless decompression with DirectStorage, and video hardware acceleration using NVDEC (including AV1 decode) and NVENC (seventh-generation). It concludes with claims about performance improvements for GA10x-based consumer and data center GPUs (e.g., RTX 3080 and NVIDIA A40), and includes legal/usage disclaimers.

The passage describes a study that analytically overviews public financing instruments for innovative cleantech start-ups and SMEs in Europe, many under the Horizon 2020 theme (80 billion in funding capacity from 2014–2020). It notes that funding commonly includes loan-based and equity-based financing, with some grants and guarantees, and highlights thematic areas such as energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. Managing bodies include the EIB and EIF, with others such as EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission. The study benchmarks instruments using metrics including portfolio size, average investment size, success rate, accepted TRL, consortium requirements, maximum project financing percentage, and monitoring frequency, and also reports that many instruments provide additional support beyond financing (e.g., coaching, training, advisory services, IP support, policy support, R&D support, and business acceleration). It outlines key topics covered, includes contact information for Research and Markets, and provides a link to the report.

The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service says the refuge headquarters office and Visitor Center at the Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge will be closed Monday, August 21, for the solar eclipse. Since the area is not in the total eclipse zone, visitors are directed to Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge at 643 Wildlife Road in Dover for viewing support from staff and volunteers. Total eclipse viewing is near the Visitor Center or back patio deck, or visitors can park along the 9-mile wildlife viewing road by the Cumberland River, following instructions not to block roads, gates, or crop fields. The partial eclipse begins at 11:56 am (CDT), with totality at 1:25 am (CDT), lasting about 55 seconds. Special solar glasses will be sold for $3.00 per pair, along with glow-in-the-dark t-shirts and bottled water to benefit Friends of Cross Creeks NWR; lunches are not sold and visitors may bring picnic baskets. Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge is an 8,862-acre refuge established in 1962, providing habitat for migratory birds, and more information is available by calling 731-642-2091.

The speaker addresses a meeting in Washington about the horrors of the Johnstown disaster in Pennsylvania, saying that relief and charity are needed. He reports that a relief association in Jacksonville, Florida has authorized him to draw $2,000 for Johnstown sufferers. He then urges practical actions: collect and send food immediately to Williamsport, Pennsylvania; gather clothing and bedclothing; and raise money from business people for reconstruction needs after the initial emergency. He concludes by expressing satisfaction if Washington responds generously and notes that he personally subscribed to Johnstown on Saturday.

William Brock was convicted on February 19, 1987, of molestation of a juvenile under R.S. 14:81.2 and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. On appeal, Brock argued the evidence was insufficient and the sentence was unconstitutionally excessive. The Court of Appeal affirmed, finding the evidence supported all elements of the offense, including that the victim suffered trauma consistent with manual digital manipulation, that Brock was the perpetrator based on the child’s statements and related testimony, that the act was done with intent to arouse or gratify sexual desires, and that Brock had control and supervision over the child. Regarding sentencing, the court found no excessive punishment, noted that the trial court complied with C.Cr.P. Art. 894.1 considerations, and determined the ten-year sentence was not an abuse of discretion and was five years less than the statutory maximum.

The passage defines research as systematic efforts to find solutions through new discoveries and inventions, requiring data collection, analysis, and evaluation while following scientific processes. It describes the curriculum inclusion of a “Scientific Research Methods” course for teacher candidates, later updated by YÖK (2018) as “Research Methods in Education (RME),” though it still appears under the old name in many institutions. The study aims to determine teacher candidates’ attitudes toward the RME course and whether these attitudes vary by department and class, using mixed quantitative and qualitative methods. Quantitatively, a researcher-developed 21-item Likert attitude scale with three factors (contribution to the profession, confidence, and contribution to daily/professional life) is validated through factor analyses and reliability tests; analyses use Kruskal Wallis H and Mann Whitney U tests due to non-normal attitude score distribution. Qualitatively, focus group interviews with 10 purposively selected pre-service teachers address course necessity, perceived contributions, and teaching process. Findings report no significant attitude difference by department, but a significant difference by grade level, with the difference between fourth and first grades. Most candidates (90%) state the course is necessary, cite its role in understanding and applying scientific research steps, while qualitative results also highlight concerns such as insufficient course duration, time and license issues with tools/materials, and the importance of lecturer teaching approach. The study concludes with recommendations to provide preparatory courses, consider offering RME in later grades based on readiness, and adjust course placement and duration/structure to support positive attitudes.

Centrica’s stock price has fallen 35% over the last year, and it currently offers an 8.6% dividend yield, which the passage says may appeal to income investors because it is nearly three times the inflation rate. It also notes that other income-focused stocks could be worth looking at, including Volution (LSE: FAN), which reported interim results with revenue up 11.6% and boosted adjusted operating profit by 6.7% to £18.3m. Volution expects further progress, including increased adjusted profit of 6% in the current year and 7% next year, and its shareholder payouts are covered 3.3 times by profit. The passage also describes Centrica’s ongoing efforts to change its business model, the impact of regulatory uncertainty on performance, and that it trades at a P/E ratio around 10, with expectations of 7% earnings growth in the current year.

The President thanks the press and discusses his relationship with journalists, stating he respects them professionally. He says he has spoken with President-elect Obama about requesting the remaining $350 billion in bail/TARP funds, but that he will not make the request unless Obama asks him to. He addresses questions about a sustainable cease-fire in Gaza, saying it depends on Hamas stopping rocket fire and stopping arms smuggling, and he states Israel has a right to defend herself while being mindful of innocent people and humanitarian aid. He discusses efforts toward a two-state solution, U.S. security concerns including potential threats from North Korea and Iran, and what he sees as the need for the Republican Party to be more inclusive. He responds to criticism about his presidency by arguing that hard outcomes take time to judge and by citing actions on Iraq and the economy, as well as acknowledging some mistakes (including Mission Accomplished and aspects of responses like Katrina). He rejects claims that America’s moral standing is damaged and discusses financial stabilization efforts, protectionism concerns, and New Orleans reconstruction progress. He concludes by wishing Obama success, emphasizing respectful discourse, and expressing hope for a different tone in Washington.

The article describes a study on culturally sensitive mentorship in occupational therapy education. It notes that mentorship supports students’ academic and professional success but that students from historically underrepresented groups may face racism, discrimination, and limited opportunities. The study aimed to address a lack of occupational therapy research on mentoring needs and experiences for these students, using a cross-sectional electronic survey of 133 entry-level students (59 identified as BIPOC/underrepresented). Findings indicated that current mentorship programming was insufficient for students from historically underrepresented groups. Students reported wanting mentors who understand the transition from academia to clinical practice and who demonstrate cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for handling workplace discrimination and microaggressions. The results also emphasized needs for career guidance (e.g., networking, exam and job preparation) alongside emotional and social validation, with preferences for regular mentor communication. The authors discuss implications for developing hybrid and potentially virtual mentorship programs, including mentor recruitment and training, and note limitations related to sampling from a single urban institution and the cross-sectional design.

In Kellner et al. v. District Court of Denver, the court issued a rule to show cause after plaintiffs sought a writ of prohibition alleging the district court would proceed without or in excess of jurisdiction. The dispute centered on whether process served on defendants in California was valid under Rule 4(f)(1) because defendants were allegedly no longer Colorado residents.

Defendants filed a special appearance motion to quash, supported by affidavits, arguing they were residents of California. The trial court denied the motion to quash, concluding defendants were Colorado residents for purposes of service, and ordered defendants to answer. The supreme court held that the issue depended on defendants’ “residence” under the statutes and that, once defendants made a prima facie showing they were not Colorado residents, the burden was on plaintiffs to prove Colorado residence. The supreme court found the facts uncontroverted that defendants had left Colorado in September 1951, intended not to return, and took acts supporting California residence, including California voting registration and other conduct. It concluded the trial court erred in denying the motion to quash and therefore lacked jurisdiction over defendants. The rule to show cause was made absolute.

European markets reached record highs as steel and banking stocks surged. The STOXX 600 gained about 0.5%, helped by expectations of trade policy changes and monetary easing. Steelmakers rose after the European Commission proposed cutting tariff-free steel import quotas nearly in half, and banks gained on stable bond yields and improving credit margins. Auto stocks declined after BMW trimmed its 2025 profit forecast, and analysts cited factors like trade and inflation concerns while noting continued optimism from expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will ease policy next year.

The Sensex closed marginally lower, falling 12.31 points to 28,339.31, while the Nifty fell 0.14% to 8,792. Five stocks hit new 52-week highs: AIA Engineering reached Rs 1,441, Alkem Laboratories reached Rs 1,874, KEC International rose to Rs 170 (then closed at Rs 162.35), Exide Industries reached Rs 218 (closed at Rs 213.75), and Kalpataru Power Transmission rose to Rs 299.85 (then closed at Rs 290.05).

The passage reports that Royal Rumble 2017 is set to take place at the Alamodome and will feature confirmed appearances by Goldberg, Brock Lesnar, John Cena, and expected appearances by The Undertaker, with Shawn Michaels rumored to appear in a non-wrestling role. It outlines that The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels will appear on Raw on January 9th, likely to announce their Rumble roles, and includes an official match card: AJ Styles (c) vs John Cena for the WWE Championship, and Kevin Owens (c) vs Roman Reigns for the WWE Universal Championship with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage. It also describes the lead-up to the Rumble following Roadblock: End Of The Line and notes that the Royal Rumble match is a 30-man event featuring Goldberg as the first entrant and including Brock Lesnar as well. Other names are mentioned as possible participants, including Braun Strowman, The Undertaker, and Finn Balor.

Bath Rugby fans returning home after watching Bath lose 24-20 to Toulon in the Champions Cup faced major travel disruption due to snow, ice and wind across southern England and northern Europe. Many flights from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam were cancelled or delayed, affecting connections via airports such as Heathrow and leading to alternative routes through places like Munich, Brussels, Madrid and Italian cities, or train travel via Paris. Several groups missed connecting flights and faced further issues, including delays at London’s Waterloo station caused by a fire. Some fans did not have scheduled flights back until later in the day or missed a planned funeral, with others reporting long waits, diversions, and cancellations. Despite the chaos, fans cited continued efforts to get home, extended stays in hotels or apartments, and arrangements for work and pet care.

China tightened controls on rare earth exports ahead of an expected meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, restricting exports of products containing rare earths worth 0.1% or more and requiring export licenses for companies using China’s extraction, refining, or magnet recycling technology. Shares of U.S. rare earth and critical mineral miners surged as markets speculated that the White House will invest more aggressively in building a domestic supply chain, including through equity stakes taken this year. The U.S. industry and the White House have accused China of manipulating the market, and both sides are described as assessing the impact of the new rules.

On October 29, 2018, Lion Air Flight 610, a nearly new Boeing 737 MAX 8, crashed into the Java Sea after an abrupt descent shortly after takeoff, killing all 189 people onboard. Boeing initially responded by pointing to Lion Air’s maintenance procedures and suggesting pilot fault, but later issued a bulletin warning that erroneous angle-of-attack data could cause uncommanded nose-down movement through repetition until deactivated; the FAA followed with an Emergency Airworthiness Directive requiring revisions to 737 MAX operating procedures. The MAX’s MCAS software was designed to push the nose down when high angle-of-attack was detected.  

On March 10, 2019, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed near Bishoftu, killing all 157 onboard. Disputes over root causes included claims about pilot capability, MCAS, Boeing’s design process, and FAA oversight; a U.S. Department of Transportation Inspector General report cited weaknesses in FAA certification and delegation processes. On March 13, 2019, the U.S. President ordered all 737 MAX aircraft grounded, and multiple independent review boards were created. The aircraft remained grounded for 21 months, and the FAA later permitted return to commercial service on November 18, 2020.  

The passage also describes context about aviation safety and industry growth, Boeing’s company culture and organizational changes, the competitive environment between Boeing and Airbus (including the 737 vs. A320 battle), and the development of the 737 MAX project. It outlines how MCAS was designed around angle-of-attack sensor inputs, how redundancy and cockpit alerts were handled, and how aspects of certification, flight training, and communication with regulators and airlines were addressed. After the crashes, Boeing leadership changes and additional FAA training requirements were reported, along with surveys indicating pressure on FAA safety personnel and estimates of Boeing’s financial and reputational damage.

The speaker describes being out of action for about seven months, trying to take things one week and one day at a time during deep negotiations that took longer than expected. They say they wanted to return to play competitive hockey, and after being selected to play for the Russian team during the Olympics, they had three weeks of workouts with junior whalers that helped them get back on track mentally. They then describe interest from other teams and a seven-day period for the Detroit Red Wings to match, after which Detroit matched quickly. The speaker says they were excited, met teammates face to face, and focused on winning fans back amid reports about Sergei Fedorov. They say they returned to play in a Friday night game, were exhausted from the rapid events and time zone differences after coming back from Japan, and felt that staying in Detroit was important. They mention seeing Vlad on the ice and describe speaking to him in Russian to help him feel comfortable, and they express happiness and inspiration from that moment.

The passage describes Constraint Acquisition (CA) as automating the modeling process in constraint programming, which is often hindered by the modeling bottleneck. It focuses on over-fitting in passive CA phases, where learned constraints can match limited examples but be overly specific. The study introduces a three-phase hybrid CA framework called Hybrid CA with Refinement (HCAR). Phase 1 performs passive learning to generate initial candidate global constraints and to prune fixed-arity constraints inconsistent with positive examples. Phase 2, the core Query-Driven Interactive Refinement stage, interacts with an oracle to validate candidate global constraints using machine learning-based confidence scores, Bayesian updates, acceptance/rejection thresholds, specialized subset exploration to recover sub-constraints from rejected globals, and adaptive oracle query budget allocation. Phase 3 then uses active learning initialized with the refined global constraints and remaining fixed-arity candidates. The framework’s contributions include the three-phase architecture, the subset exploration mechanism, and the integration of ML prior estimation with a Bayesian confidence framework, with empirical results reported as achieving high accuracy and target model coverage from limited examples using manageable query complexity.

The passage reviews prior research showing that expectations in higher education vary across institutions, departments, and faculty time devoted to research, and it reports a study of US mathematics education faculty research expectations. It describes how institution type (Carnegie R1, R2, and other), department type (education vs. mathematics), and research commitment (percent time on research) likely affect tenure-and-promotion expectations and perceptions. The authors explain their measurement approach (expected number of papers, valued publication types and scholarly activities) and methods (survey development, participant selection, and multinomial logistic regression). Key findings include an average expectation of about 1.64 papers per year overall, with research journal articles counting as “a lot.” Expectations differ by institution type: R1 faculty are expected to devote about 40% to research and publish about 2.25 papers per year; R2 faculty devote at least 40% to research and publish about 1.5 papers per year; other institutions devote about 20% to research and publish about 1 paper per year. The study also finds that research commitment is positively associated with the expected number of papers and that department type relates to differences in expected publication and valued scholarly activities. The conclusion emphasizes using these results to clarify and potentially document research expectations across faculty, programs, and the broader field.

The passage discusses the spin Hall effect (SHE) and spin Edelstein effect (SEE) and then focuses on the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE), comparing its magnitude to the SEE. It explains that orbital moments can produce related transport effects (OHE and OEE) and motivates studying the OEE in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), especially MoS₂ in the 2H structure. Because the Edelstein effect requires a Fermi surface, it considers electron- and hole-doped systems, which can be realized experimentally. It notes that 2H-TMDs have zero Edelstein effect without broken mirror symmetry (σh), so the study assumes symmetry breaking via a perpendicular electric field or substrate, leading to a nonzero Edelstein effect.  

The work models gated doped TMDs using a minimal 5×5 Hamiltonian in the metal d-orbital subspace with spin-orbit coupling, where the gate field breaks symmetry and introduces additional terms. It derives how orbital and spin chiral textures arise from broken symmetry and SOC, and uses these to compute Edelstein susceptibilities for orbital and spin responses. Results state that for electron doping the OEE is significantly larger than the SEE, while for hole doping the OEE and SEE are similar in magnitude but both can be enhanced by strain. Specifically, compressive strain can shift the Γ valley to become the valence-band top, enabling stronger Edelstein response because the Γ pocket dominates. The passage also reports that spin responses from different subbands can cancel, enhancing OEE relative to SEE in some cases. Finally, it summarizes that OEE strengths in the studied TMDs can be much larger than previously reported values, and that doping type and strain strongly affect the magnitude of the Edelstein response.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated December 12, 2016, stating it entered into a Termination Agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. to terminate certain outstanding warrants issued under two letter agreements dated November 25, 2013 and November 26, 2013. Under the agreement, 63,259,180.62 warrants will be terminated, and NVIDIA will deliver shares of its common stock to Goldman based on the daily volume-weighted average price during an observation period from December 13, 2016 through January 31, 2017. The issuance is described as relying on the Securities Act exemption in Section 4(a)(2). The Termination Agreement is attached as Exhibit 10.1.

The passage describes the Keltner Channel (also called Keltner Bands), a volatility-based technical analysis tool created by Chester Keltner in the 1960s. It consists of three lines: a middle line using a moving average (often a 20-period EMA) and upper/lower bands calculated by adding and subtracting a multiple of the Average True Range (ATR). The channel width expands and contracts with market volatility. Traders use it to assess potential price trends, overbought/oversold conditions, and possible buy/sell signals when price touches or breaks outside the bands, including for swing trading and scalping. The text compares it to Bollinger Bands, stating Bollinger Bands use standard deviation while Keltner Channel uses ATR, and notes that the passage’s backtest results showed about a 77% win rate (with additional metrics) and tested different settings. It states Keltner Channels are typically viewed as leading indicators, can be customized with different parameters, may have variations, and the passage claims the indicator does not repaint. It also mentions adjusting settings for volatility, considerations for position sizing, typical entry/exit logic based on band breakouts and opposite-band targets, and common pitfalls like over-reliance on the indicator alone.

The passage says government shutdowns have historically had little economic impact, but this time could be different. It notes President Donald Trump’s threat to make some furloughs permanent and the possibility that a prolonged shutdown could delay key economic data, including Bureau of Labor Statistics reports and the consumer price index used for Social Security cost-of-living adjustments. It also says the impact could affect Federal Reserve decisions and mentions that some analysts expect effects to be mild while warning of potential harm to the labor market from furloughed federal employees and contractors.

The passage discusses a new Netflix documentary, “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish,” which follows students in Beal City, Michigan, as junior high student Lauryn Licari is harassed by threatening, vulgar, sexually graphic text messages from an unknown number. Lauryn’s boyfriend, Owen McKenny, begins receiving messages that initially threaten to break up with her and later escalate to frequent messages per day, personal knowledge of Lauryn and Owen, and threats against Lauryn’s life. Local investigators investigate students but do not find clarity, and the case is eventually turned over to the FBI, which requests a forensic examination of Owen’s phone after receiving 720 pages of messages. The author reflects on cellphone dangers, cellphone forensics, and the impact of technology, and notes that Oklahoma passed a “bell to bell” no-cellphone policy for the 2025–2026 school year with an initial one-year trial.

The Fabian Market Timing Model is a simple quantitative long-term trend-following strategy developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s. It uses intermarket signals among the S&P 500, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and the utilities sector based on their 39-week moving averages, with the Dow Jones and utilities confirming S&P signals to reduce false signals. The buy and sell rules are executed at the end of each week, and the article discusses backtest performance, noting low volatility and low maximum drawdown and that long-term returns are closer to buy-and-hold. The passage emphasizes that sticking to the mechanical system is more important than the model itself.

The Bank of England allocated £5.085 billion in its six-month indexed long-term repo operation, the highest amount since March 2020 and more than double the £2.352 billion allotted the previous week, indicating increased banks’ demand for central bank liquidity. The facility provides six-month secured funding backed by high-quality collateral, typically without surcharges, and the BoE has been encouraging its use as it unwinds quantitative easing and shifts toward a framework where banks actively borrow rather than rely on abundant reserves. The record allotment suggests banks may increasingly use these operations as market conditions evolve, though demand for six-month repos remains modest versus short-term facilities. Future demand levels and the BoE’s ability to balance liquidity provision with smooth functioning of gilt markets will determine how the post-QE environment develops.

A state House panel advanced a proposal to address South Carolina’s struggling pension system, which has a $24 billion gap. The plan would raise employee contributions from 8.66% to 9% and require employers to increase contributions from 11.56% to 18.56% by 2023; the full House Ways & Means Committee will debate it Thursday. Some mayors and agency heads opposed it, saying it would raise local government retirement costs by 60%. Separately, a bill allowing out-of-state concealed weapons permit holders to carry in South Carolina advanced to the House floor and would require recognition of permits from all 50 states. Also, a Senate-passed measure would authorize special Coastal Carolina University 2016 College World Series championship license plates, costing $70 extra and directing profits to scholarships.

Chelsea will play Barcelona in the Champions League last-16. Antonio Conte’s side finished second in Group C behind Roma. The first leg will be on February 13/14 or February 20/21, and the second leg on March 6/7 or March 13/14. The 2018 final is scheduled for Olimpiyskiy Stadium in Kiev. The passage notes Barcelona topped Group D with 14 points and conceded one goal. Chelsea and Barcelona last met in 2012, when Chelsea drew 2-2 and progressed to the final with a 3-2 aggregate win. The main focus for Barcelona is Lionel Messi, described as having scored 363 goals in 397 appearances since 2004.

The passage is largely composed of Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q materials for the quarter ended September 30, 2021, including financial statements and notes. It lists consolidated balance sheet and income statement figures, comprehensive income, equity movements, and cash flows for three and nine months ended September 30, 2021 and 2020. The notes describe accounting policies and estimates (including impacts from COVID-19), revenue recognition by major source (automotive sales with/without resale value guarantee, automotive regulatory credits, energy generation and storage sales, services and other, and leasing), and topics such as income taxes, net income per share methodology and adoption of ASU 2020-06, restricted cash, marketable securities, accounts receivable, inventory and write-downs, property and equipment, warranty reserves, digital assets (bitcoin purchases, impairments, and gains), fair value measurements, debt and finance leases, equity incentive plans (including the 2018 CEO Performance Award), and commitments and contingencies (including an operating lease and related SUNY Foundation program payment terms).

The passage discusses modeling trabecular bone and osteoporosis using Voronoi honeycomb structures, using finite element analysis to compare elastic moduli and compressive strength and to study failure modes (elastic buckling vs plastic yielding) as relative density changes. It explains that random Voronoi structures have similar modulus to analytical models but lower and more variable strength due to broader strain/stress distributions, and it examines how thinning struts differs from removing struts, including percolation thresholds where stiffness and strength drop to zero. It then describes extending the models to structures more like vertebral trabecular bone (2D perturbed Voronoi arrays and subsequent 3D Voronoi models), and relates these modeling ideas to bone loss from osteoporosis. After the osteoporosis section, it covers interest in metal foams as porous coatings/substitutes for orthopedic implants and reviews multiple fabrication methods (e.g., replica, hydride infiltration, fugitive phase, foaming agent expansion, freeze casting, and selective laser sintering) and their general mechanical-property trends. Finally, it outlines evolutionary study approaches using trabecular bone architecture, including a fossil ilium study of Oreopithecus bambolii that compares bone features to humans and primates to suggest bipedal behavior or partial bipedalism.

The passage presents author information for Hanne Rinholm, Ida Heiberg Solem, and Inger Ulleberg and introduces a study about dialogic pedagogy using two classroom cases: a pre-service teacher education music choir project and an upper-primary mathematics classroom talk. It argues that democratic dialogue requires competencies and that education, under frameworks such as UNESCO, Norway’s Education Act, and the Core Curriculum, should foster critical, participative citizenship, connecting dialogic pedagogy to Bildung. The study aims to connect educational rhetoric with classroom practice by developing theoretical concepts and analytical tools, then presenting and comparing the two cases. Methodologically, it is an interdisciplinary qualitative project using a deductive approach where theoretical concepts function as lenses. The analysis focuses on epistemological and ontological dialogue, as well as subject-related processes of musicking and mathematizing and their relation to Bildung. The discussion highlights common dialogic features across both cases, emphasizes teachers’ roles in facilitating participation, and considers tensions and paradoxes, including risks of monologizing under the guise of empowerment and concerns about how ontological engagement can affect students’ personal spaces. The conclusion states that the chosen theoretical concepts helped interpret dialogic classroom practices and showed how epistemological and ontological dialogic aspects interact in concrete settings.

The speaker addresses the United States about its duty to participate in establishing future peace among nations, including joining a league for peace. They argue that U.S. terms for approval must be stated clearly, that the present war must end with settlement terms creating a peace worth guaranteeing, and that permanency requires a force greater than any existing nation or alliance. They question whether the war aims for a just and secure peace or only a balance of power, arguing instead for a “community of power” and an “organized common peace.” They reference assurances from statesmen that the purpose is not to crush opponents, and interpret these to mean a peace “without victory,” since victory would lead to forced terms, humiliation, resentment, and unstable peace. They conclude that lasting peace requires both just settlements of disputes and the proper mindset between nations, based on equality and common participation.

A 19-year-old woman was sexually assaulted by a man on a train in Weston-super-Mare as it approached Highbridge and Burnham. Police said the train jolted, the man fell into her and touched her inappropriately, and then continued to assault her until members of the public intervened. The group left the train at Bridgewater. British Transport Police are appealing for information about the incident on Saturday, April 8, around 4.45pm, and say the victim is being supported while they investigate; contact details are provided.

The lecture recaps linearizing the Einstein field equations by treating spacetime as a small perturbation of flat space and decomposing the perturbation into gauge-invariant and gauge degrees of freedom. It identifies the radiative part as a transverse, traceless metric perturbation \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) with two independent components corresponding to gravitational-wave polarizations (“plus” and “cross”). The lecture then shows that a single body’s geodesic motion can hide the wave’s physical effects due to coordinates, so it analyzes two nearby freely falling bodies using light-pulse timing and geodesic deviation. The geodesic deviation leads to equations showing tidal stretching and squeezing of a ring of test particles, producing the polarization patterns. It explains how an interferometric detector like LIGO measures these effects by timing light traveling between mirrors with laser metrology. Finally, it outlines how to compute \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) from a source: solve the linearized Einstein equation in Lorentz gauge, approximate the solution with a leading multipole (quadrupole) term, relate the result to the second time derivative of the source quadrupole moment \(I_{ij}\), and project it to the transverse-traceless part using projection tensors, yielding the quadrupole formula for the gravitational-wave field.

Researchers reported in The FASEB Journal that activating two receptors, TRPM8 and TRPP3, can increase metabolism-boosting brown adipose tissue (BAT). The receptors are associated with BAT creation in humans and may be activated by certain foods, suggesting potential drug targets. In experiments using human bone marrow stem cells and subcutaneous belly fat precursor cells, TRPM8 supported browning when activated and was inhibited from doing so by specific inhibitors. Eliminating TRPP3 prevented brown fat formation without affecting white fat. The work is presented as having implications for treating obesity, diabetes, and metabolic disorders, and as related to possible non-adrenergic stimulators and functional foods.

Whangarei District Council advises drivers that winter parking congestion around Kensington Park is expected and that there are currently no plans to increase parking. The council’s enforcement and roading departments say tickets will be issued for vehicles parked in ways that break rules, including blocking driveways or residents’ access, damaging underground services or turf, and obstructing footpath users. The council first uses warning fliers under windscreen wipers, then after a few weeks switches to ticketing. Drivers are advised to plan ahead, consider car pooling, leave earlier, drop players off and walk back, and find parking.

Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission (JKPSC) has kept in abeyance the result of the Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination, 2016 and withdrawn the notification for the main examination after discrepancies were found in question papers and answer keys. The Commission decided to refer all question papers and answer keys of 23 subjects to independent experts for evaluation and has also sent them for re-looking and revisiting. Following earlier representations about inaccuracies, ambiguity, wrong options, mistakes, and printing errors, ambiguities were previously referred to a team of experts under the relevant rules, and the preliminary result was declared on April 23, 2017. After further representations under the Right to Information Act, the Commission issued a notice stating consequential action will be taken after receiving findings, and that the next date for the main examination will be notified after the subject experts’ report. Bluehole has launched a new PUBG community event on Xbox One called Snipe City. The event challenges players to collectively make 400,000 kills using the M24 and Kar98 sniper rifles, with rewards available only if the community completes the task. The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the divorce and custody awards to John Geesbreght, reversing only the trial court’s property division. The court held the trial court had jurisdiction to make an enforceable custody decree, treating the children’s domicile as Texas and concluding Texas had jurisdiction under the Family Code. It found no reversible error in the jury trial on custody, including the supplemental charge defining possessory conservatorship and visitation rights. Finally, the appellate court reversed the property division because the trial court allegedly failed to account for enhanced value (“good will”) of John’s stock in a professional corporation, resulting in an inadequate and clearly erroneous award, and remanded for a new trial on property division.

The passage describes validation of a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer’s disease progression using the Predictors 3 cohort. The L-GoM model, developed from Predictors 2 data, uses measures from 11 key domains at baseline and every six months up to 10 years to generate individual-specific predicted survival probabilities (up to 7.5 years) and prevalence probabilities of needing full-time care (FTC). Predictors 3 recruited community-dwelling, multiethnic older adults from Washington Heights and Inwood, including prevalent or incident AD dementia cases and individuals at risk for conversion diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Model validation involved comparing predicted probabilities to observed group-specific proportions for mortality and FTC across diagnostic and demographic subgroups. Results indicated close fits for overall survival and FTC for AD nonreverters and MCI cases, with poor fit for AD reverters, who were substantially more likely to revert to lower CDR scores. The study concludes that mortality and FTC predictions were accurate for subjects except AD reverters, and that the model can be applied to community-dwelling older adults across different ethnic, linguistic, and SES backgrounds, with extension to MCI.

Surveillance officers and health workers in Lagos and Ogun States have been placed on high alert for Lassa fever. Ogun State confirmed one case: a 20-year-old male isolated at Federal Medical Centre, Idi-Aba in Abeokuta after testing positive following a trip back from Lagos; he is responding to treatment, 66 direct contacts are under surveillance, and the hospital was fumigated and decontaminated. In Lagos University Teaching Hospital, confirmed cases are responding to treatment and those under surveillance are doing well, with an official update to be issued. Last week, Lagos confirmed five Lassa cases, with 2 deaths and 150 placed under surveillance.

The passage explains that Fibonacci trading uses Fibonacci tools—such as retracement, expansion, and fan—to conduct technical analysis by indicating likely support and resistance levels, helping traders plan entries, exits, stops, limits, and profit targets. It describes how Fibonacci retracements draw horizontal lines at specified percentages of a previous price swing to mark potential reversal levels, how the expansion tool projects potential impulse swing size, and how the fan tool plots trendlines at Fibonacci levels. It states there is no best timeframe, depending on trading style, and suggests backtesting to determine suitable timeframes and retracement levels. The passage also discusses backtesting and evidence, saying there is anecdotal evidence and no proof that Fibonacci is a consistently successful strategy, noting a quoted dissertation that found a passive strategy with Fibonacci retracements outperformed an active strategy, while concluding Fibonacci may still be useful for support/resistance and target marking if used cautiously and combined with other indicators. It ends by summarizing common Fibonacci ratios and describing Fibonacci retracement as a tool drawn from a peak to a trough using key ratios.

After ChatGPT’s release in November 2022, headlines predicted broad AI-driven job losses, especially affecting entry-level roles. A Yale-Brookings analysis using Bureau of Labor Statistics data on job losses, unemployment, and occupational composition found “movement” but no broad, economy-wide AI disruption, describing reported impacts as “lightning strikes” rather than a “house fire.” The biggest forces driving labor market shifts were described as a slowing economy, an aging population, and declining immigration, not AI. The study and its authors said exposure to AI does not automatically mean jobs disappear; tasks may change instead, and organizational workflow redesign takes time. They expect any systemic effects to take years and believe displacement would come more from embedded AI in enterprise workflows than from individuals using chatbots.

CBOT May wheat was down 3-1/2 cents to $4.58 per bushel, and CBOT May corn was flat at $3.78-1/2 per bushel; CBOT May soybeans were down 2-1/4 cents to $10.18-1/2. A Ukrainian startup, Dropla, is developing an AI system called Blue Eyes to help Ukrainian forces counter Russia’s ambush quadcopters used as explosive devices along supply roads. Blue Eyes processes real-time video feeds from cheap quadcopters flying over routes, trained to detect more than 170 types of explosive threats, including landmines and ambush drones. When a threat is detected, it sends coordinates to Ukraine’s battle management system for commanders to decide next steps. The system is being tested by frontline units since early summer, and Dropla plans to scale deployments near the “zero line” by fivefold. A researcher at the Center for European Policy Analysis says Ukraine must find cost-effective counters as ambush drones disrupt logistics and require convoys to maintain constant situational awareness over distances near the front line.

The passage describes the Side Screen offense as a two-player screen-and-roll isolation play commonly used in the NBA. It is initiated by having a post step out to set an “ON” ball screen, either by the point guard dribble-clearing the wing or by passing to the wing and making a basket cut to clear to the weak side. Teams often run it on the left for right-handed players and on the right for left-handed players to allow dribble penetration into the middle.

The basic option is for the guard or wing to drive over the top of the ball screen, with read-based options including turning the corner, pull-up jumpers, return passes to the post, kick-out passes, crossovers, pull-up shots, post pops, feeds to rolling/posting screeners, isolations against switches, and counters such as slips, back cuts, and lob passes. The keys to success are execution and coordination, including proper footwork, timing, non-verbal communication, and experience, with attention to eight defensive reads and counters.

The passage also outlines entry variations into the Side Screen (e.g., High Post Rub, Power/Motion, Horns) and continuity options when the initial action breaks down (e.g., Flex, Triangle Game, single/double motion, double screen, baseline screen). It emphasizes teaching and implementing the offense through drills and scouting/strategic adjustments, and notes that defenders should understand how to disrupt Side Screens because it is widely used.

Tributes were paid by MP Nick Gibb and Arun chief executive Nigel Lynn. Maconachie served on Arun for 22 years, became council chairman from 2001 to 2002, and chaired the development control committee and local plan sub-committee. The council said it offered condolences to her husband Dougal, her friends and family, and those she represented.

The passage describes hydraulic fracturing (“fracking”) operations that require delivering highly pressurized fluid, often with proppants, through a wellhead into a cased wellbore. It explains that fluid ends used in these operations operate under extreme pressures and conditions, with failures attributed to factors such as expansion or cracking, proppant erosion, corrosion, and fatigue cracking (including at bore-wall intersections and the flange neck). A typical power end has longer lifespan than a fluid end and can service multiple fluid ends.

It also describes conventional fluid end and power end construction, including the use of stay rods, pony rods, crankshaft-driven reciprocation, plungers, bores, packing seals, manifolds, and valves. Fatigue cracks in conventional fluid ends are linked to stress concentrations and corrosion, leading to leakage and replacement or repair.

The passage then outlines a “fluid end” design that departs from a traditional single-housing approach by using multiple fluid end sections with a single horizontal bore per section, eliminating an internal chamber formed by intersecting bores. The described system routes fluid using a fluid routing plug, which engages suction and discharge valves that move axially between open and closed positions, controlling flow through intake bores, passages, and a discharge bore. It further details features intended to reduce stress and improve serviceability, including shaped bores and manifolds, stuffing boxes with packing and lubrication pathways, retainers and fasteners, and seals/grooves for preventing leakage. The passage concludes with valve and sealing-element geometry considerations, including tapered angles.

A new study says first-time heart attacks, heart failure, and strokes usually occur with existing cardiovascular risk factors. In a prospective cohort study, more than 99% of people who experienced these illnesses had at least one of four risks: suboptimal high blood pressure, cholesterol, or blood glucose, or being a current or former smoker. Over 93% of more than 9.3 million people followed for 20 years had more than one risk factor, and among women under 60, more than 95% had at least one nonoptimal risk factor before heart failure or stroke. The article notes that reported prevalence may differ due to how groups define “optimal” levels versus “clinical” thresholds used for treatment, and it argues that even common nonoptimal levels can be treated to help prevent these events.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) enables the A100 Tensor Core GPU to be securely partitioned into up to seven separate GPU Instances for CUDA applications, allowing multiple users to use separate GPU resources. Each instance has isolated memory-system paths, including crossbar ports, L2 cache banks, memory controllers, and DRAM address buses, to provide predictable throughput and latency with consistent L2 cache allocation and DRAM bandwidth even under other tasks’ contention. MIG improves hardware utilization while offering defined QoS and isolation for clients such as VMs, containers, and processes, particularly benefiting cloud service providers by preventing one client from impacting others’ work or scheduling and enhancing security.

The disclosure relates to wireless communications and specifically to applying scheduling offsets for power saving in next-generation networks. It addresses issues in NR HARQ when a UE enters power saving state, where timing parameters (including K values controlling DL-to-UL ACK/NACK behavior and related RRC parameters) may change, potentially causing incorrect HARQ information and misalignment.

A primary method for a UE receiving a power saving signal includes receiving the signal with a minimum applicable K0min indicating a minimum scheduling offset restriction between PDCCH and PDSCH, determining an application delay based on a predefined value, and applying the minimum scheduling offset restriction after the application delay. During the delay, the UE may apply a different scheduling offset (configurable via RRC signaling or provided through DCI). Implementations also include logic for receiving a second DCI after the delay containing an applicable K, comparing it to K0min, applying the indicated scheduling offset if K is larger, or foregoing the minimum restriction if K is smaller. The disclosure further covers sending HARQ feedback after a specified time offset from receiving the power saving signal, with the feedback timing conveyed via the power saving signal or RRC signaling.

The disclosure also describes approaches for HARQ-ACK/NACK feedback for power saving indicators, including adding a power-saving acknowledgment bit into the HARQ codebook, mechanisms for multiplexing and locating this bit within HARQ feedback, and handling dedicated PUCCH resources and cases where resources overlap. Additionally, it introduces enhancements to default UL beam operation in the power saving state to avoid selecting deactivated antenna panels, including using valid/applicable spatial domain/QCL information for PUCCH selection and alternative handling when default selections would be invalid.

The passage describes the “Triangle & Two” defense as effective against opponents with two outstanding scorers or as a change to catch them off guard. It also explains how to invert the triangle zone when the opponent uses a two-guard front, noting that the inverted setup operates like a 2-3 zone. The passage emphasizes that the chasers’ ability to deny the ball disrupts the opponents’ set plays and continuities.

The passage describes changes in UK marriage and civil partnership law and explains how Andrew & Andrew family solicitors handle divorce or dissolution. The passage introduces fusion trees, a static integer data structure designed for the predecessor/successor problem with goal time complexity \( \log_w n \) on the word RAM model. It explains key techniques: sketching (compressing selected “important” bits), computing sketches in constant time using integer multiplication, and performing parallel comparisons on many sketches at once. Fusion tree nodes are built using a B-tree-like approach with branching factor \(w^{1/5}\) and polynomial preprocessing, where each node stores \(k=\Theta(w^{1/5})\) sorted keys. Because all key bits can’t be read directly in constant time, the method identifies a small set of “important bits” based on branching nodes in a bit-tree representation and uses sketches that preserve order among the stored keys.

For queries, the passage describes “de-sketchifying”: after finding the query’s position in sketch space, it constructs a modified value \(e\) to correct for arbitrary queries that may not align with the sketch definition used for preprocessing. The corrected searches then recover predecessor and successor ranks among the stored keys. The passage further outlines how sketching is made approximate via masking, multiplication with carefully chosen parameters to avoid collisions and maintain ordered placement within a limited bit range, and masking to extract the resulting compressed sketch. It also describes auxiliary subroutines used in the construction, including finding the most significant set bit using clustering plus fusion-like operations.

The longest preserved woolly rhino horn, found in Siberian permafrost and nearly the size of a small adult human, is about 30 centimeters longer than the previous record. A local hunter and fisherman found the horn and complete skull near Russia’s Kolyma River and sent the remains to researchers; nearby frozen lemmings were carbon dated to about 19,600 years old. Researchers say the species’ horns may have helped push aside snow and that worn horn surfaces showed extensive use. By counting alternating light and dark keratin layers in the horn base, they determined the rhino lived at least 40 years, the oldest woolly rhino age yet found, and conclude that woolly rhinos could live as long as modern species in Ice Age conditions. The skull suggests a proportionally small adult, possibly female, with sex-related horn-size differences potentially comparable to modern rhinos.

The Relist Watch column reviews Supreme Court cert petitions that have been “relisted” for an upcoming conference and explains that relists can signal interest from at least one justice, with review odds generally increasing after a relist. The passage describes multiple specific relisted cases, including disputes over public schools hiding children’s gender identity from parents; New York’s (repealed) COVID-19 vaccine mandate challenges by healthcare workers; whether Section 230 immunizes apps from liability related to child exploitation; jury trial and notice issues involving administrative or due process matters; litigation over prison mental-health housing and termination of prospective relief; arbitration under the Federal Arbitration Act; rules governing appeal waivers after guilty pleas; Sixth Amendment confrontation procedures for child witnesses; and public trial rights during jury selection.
