It also lists additional relisted questions and notes that the next installment is expected to be less interesting.

The passage lists multiple business and economic news headlines, including Fifth Third’s plan to acquire Comerica for $10.9B, JPMorgan Chase accelerating AI integration, and the Bank of England allocating its largest six-month repo since 2020. It also describes Tesla’s 7 October teaser, which sparked speculation about either unveiling the long-delayed Roadster or introducing a new mass-market electric vehicle focused on affordability, potentially a simplified Model Y with about a 20% production-cost reduction. The timing is linked to record Q3 deliveries ahead of an expired U.S. EV tax incentive, and investors are divided due to Tesla’s history of delayed launches.

The passage explains life cycle assessment (LCA) as a method for quantifying potential environmental impacts of products across their life cycle (“cradle to grave”). It discusses why LCA is used both internally and externally, outlines its four stages (goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact analysis, and interpretation), and describes how ISO standards and standardization efforts developed to address variability and questionable “hired gun” studies. Using a hand dryer study as an example, it highlights key decisions and assumptions in LCAs, including defining the functional unit (a dry pair of hands), setting system boundaries and cut-off rules, handling data gaps with proxy inputs, and dealing with allocation issues such as open-loop recycling. It also describes how impact categories like global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, and more complex methods (e.g., IMPACT 2002+) are calculated and aggregated, and how uncertainty and sensitivity analyses are performed to test the effects of assumptions, with electricity use and hand drying time identified as major drivers.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 14, 2018. Under Item 7.01, it reported that on August 14, 2018 it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1, which is incorporated by reference and not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference except as expressly set forth. Under Item 9.01(d), the filing lists Exhibit 99.1 as the press release dated August 14, 2018. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel, on August 14, 2018.

Sevilla midfielder Pablo Sarabia said his team was drawn against Manchester United in the Champions League last 16, and that Sevilla only wanted to avoid Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain. Sevilla will host United on 21 February and travel to England for the return on 13 March. Sarabia said Mourinho prepares well for knockout matches but Sevilla has options. Sevilla finished second in their group behind Liverpool and currently sit fifth in La Liga with 28 points from 15 matches. Other last-16 ties include Manchester City vs Basel and PSG vs Real Madrid.

A new report by the Children’s Rights Alliance examines how homelessness and living in emergency accommodation affect children’s education, based on research among teachers, school principals, and homeless parents in greater Dublin. It says basic needs like adequate food and rest are often not met, leaving children unable to meaningfully engage in education. The report describes children attending school hungry, in dirty clothes, rising early for long journeys, and falling asleep in class, with frequent absences linked to poor diet, inadequate rest, and poor living conditions. It also cites parents sacrificing food for travel costs, or vice versa, and says emergency accommodation hampers homework and play. The report further links homelessness-related uncertainty to changes in behaviour and mental health, including refusal to eat and increased agitation. It calls for supports such as free travel, ring-fenced school funding for meals, psychological assessments, and homework clubs, and for families to access suitable accommodation near school or childcare, without staying in emergency or temporary accommodation for more than six months.

The passage describes a market research report on the Global Angelica Seed oil Market, providing analysis of market status, growth rate, trends, and historical, current, and projected revenues by sector, segment, end-user, and region. It covers drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, current factors, PEST and Porter’s Five Forces, applications, regional markets, and competitive landscape, including company coverage and pricing, profit, capacity, production, and demand data. The report includes SWOT, investment feasibility, and investment return analyses, regional segmentation for 2018–2025 (United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World), and product and application segmentations (Therapeutic Grade; Medical, Spa & Relaxation, Others). It outlines key points such as market analyses, production process issues and solutions, industry strategies, future outlook with marketing and price factors, and guidance for new players, stakeholders, marketing teams, authorities, and distributors/manufacturers, using primary and secondary research and expert data forecasts in revenue and volume.

The study in Muheza District, northeastern Tanzania, assessed malnutrition risk factors and the impact of intermittent preventive therapy for malaria (IPTsc) on nutritional status in school-age children (5–15 years). Using secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a randomized controlled open-label trial, children were assigned to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ), or standard care and followed for 20 months. At baseline, malaria prevalence was 27%, with 23% underweight (age ≤10), 21% stunted, and 28% thin or severely thin. Malaria was associated with higher odds of stunting (adjusted OR 1.78, P<0.001), and low socioeconomic status was associated with higher odds of being underweight (adjusted OR 1.50, P=0.006). During the intervention, changes in mean weight, height, and BMI over time were not significantly different between DP or ASAQ and the control group. The authors conclude that the burden of malaria and malnutrition is high and recommend reinforcing nutritional programs alongside malaria control efforts.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing-based Tesla T4 GPU and the Turing architecture’s features for data-center inference and real-time graphics. Tesla T4 is presented as a universal inferencing solution for hyperscale data centers and edge devices, with specified CUDA/Tensor core counts and INT8/INT4 TOPS performance, along with claims of higher inference performance and energy efficiency versus CPU-based inferencing and the Tesla P4. It further outlines Turing’s hardware features, including enhanced video engine, multi-process service, improved memory bandwidth/capacity, and compression, and describes display/video capabilities such as DisplayPort 1.4a support, HDR processing, and NVENC/NVDEC updates. The passage also discusses ray tracing and hybrid rendering enabled by RT Cores and NVIDIA RTX software technology, including BVH traversal, denoising, and the use of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. Additional AI-based image enhancement technologies via NGX are covered, including DLSS modes and examples of inpainting, AI slow-mo, and AI super resolution. Finally, it explains GPU rendering features such as variable rate shading, texture space shading, multi-view rendering, resource binding changes, and several VR-focused capabilities including VirtualLink, foveated rendering, and VRWorks audio acceleration, concluding with broader architecture descriptions and specifications for TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4.

Construction at Elliott Field and Don Beebe Stadium is expected to bring major changes in June while staying on schedule despite late rainy weather. Steel for the Con Marshall Press Box was installed in late March, and April–May work added roofs, insulation, finishing masonry, press box exterior framing, excavation for grandstands, and ongoing utility installations. June plans include bleachers taking shape, field grading and drains, beginning rock filling in mid-June for turf installation, and arrival of the scoreboard in the third week of June. Field lighting is being reintroduced, with groundwork starting in the next couple of weeks and lights expected to be used for the September 1 season opener against Black Hills State University. The construction zone has expanded this summer, with traffic shut down between the Nelson Physical Activity Center and Chicoine Center parking lots, though alternative access routes remain available. The board is scheduled next month to approve the design phase for a track facility expected near “C Hill.” Funding continues to be sought to complete the stadium and track projects and support programs and scholarships.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated August 26, 2022. The U.S. government informed the company that a new license requirement, effective immediately, applies to future exports to China (including Hong Kong) and Russia of NVIDIA’s A100 and forthcoming H100 integrated circuits, including systems incorporating them (such as DGX and A100X). The requirement also covers certain future NVIDIA integrated circuits and systems with specified performance characteristics. A license is required to export technology to support or develop covered products. NVIDIA stated the requirement addresses risk of military end use or end user in China and Russia; the company does not sell products to customers in Russia. NVIDIA said the requirement may affect its ability to complete H100 development, support A100 customers, and may require transitioning operations out of China. The company is engaging with the U.S. government seeking exemptions and engaging with customers in China to meet planned or future purchases with alternative products not subject to the requirement. NVIDIA noted its third fiscal quarter outlook included approximately $400 million in potential sales to China that may be subject to the new license requirement.

Stocks rebounded sharply on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Wednesday, with the Nikkei average gaining 199.00 points (1.03%) to close at 19,437.98. The rise was attributed to the yen’s drop, stronger U.S. equities, expectations of an early Fed rate hike after Janet Yellen’s testimony, and brisk Japanese corporate earnings. The Topix index also rose 14.57 points (0.95%) to 1,553.69. Export-oriented companies and financial issues gained, while firms including Toshiba, Nintendo, Rakuten, and DeNA fell.

In the 2016–17 school year, colleges and universities are expected to award more than a million bachelor’s degrees, but many graduates are working adults who face different challenges than traditional students. The Department of Education reported that students over 24 years old accounted for nearly two-fifths of postsecondary enrollment in 2016. Timothy P. Slottow of University of Phoenix says working adult students need flexibility, structure, and career-relevant programs, along with faculty with field experience. He advises working adults to prepare by building a support system, consulting academic and financial advisers, considering credit for prior learning or military experience, and setting a plan that may include flexible scheduling and online or night classes.

The speaker discusses expectations for the Stanley Cup finals, saying many players’ first time there is exciting and that they can be overexcited and try to do too much, but should calm down and play their regular game. They note the opposing team is likely more intense and physical as the series continues and describe their approach as controlling the puck and forcing opponents to chase, including getting traffic in front of the goalie to create good shot opportunities. They mention factors involving injuries, defensive minutes, and trying to tire a veteran opponent. They also emphasize their team’s preference for a puck-possession, controlling-the-puck style and suggest they may need to do more to earn power plays, since going an entire game without one is not realistic.

The passage describes the “Yankee” offensive concept, a pro-style, shot-play design used to spread defenses and get over the top of safeties for big-play opportunities. It emphasizes a post–dig combination from opposite sides of the formation, with the QB throwing downfield to receivers staying on the move and reading a high-to-low progression. The concept is typically run from pro-style sets with multiple running backs or tight ends to encourage 1-high safety looks, and it is said to work well against Cover 1 and Cover 3. It is described as less successful against 2-high defenses, where the QB should transition quickly to underneath routes. Route and coaching points are provided for one-high and two-high variations (including crossing, arrow, dig, and post routes with specific landmarks), along with quarterback progression and progression under blitz recognition. Two variations are outlined: a 2x2 Yankee concept with shallow crossers and a Yankee concept with whip routes.

The passage describes a “pulse” climate scenario in which abnormally warm water could cause glaciers in Antarctica and Greenland to collapse, leading to extremely rapid sea-level rise worldwide. It says current predictions for Miami are up to 7 or 8 feet higher than in 1900 by the end of this century, but some experts expect South Florida could see 10 to 30 feet by 2100 in a pulse, potentially with superstorms. A recent Science Advances study reports that a feedback process involving warm water pooling beneath glaciers is already underway in at least two Antarctic regions—the Amundsen Sea and the Sabrina Coast—where surface waters are not cooling and sinking as usual. The researchers say melting driven by the warm water could further accelerate ice shelf melt and future sea-level rise, and they note related effects on ocean currents, superstorms, and atmospheric warming.

As of December 14, 2021, inactivated, vectored, and mRNA Covid vaccines made up 43%, 28%, and 26% of 10.6 billion administered doses worldwide, but few studies compare immune responses elicited by these platforms, including in India where CovishieldTM and Covaxinâ constitute 15% of world doses. This study enrolled 691 adults (18–45) across four sites in Bengaluru and Pune between June 30, 2021 and January 28, 2022; participants received either two Covaxinâ doses 28 days apart or two CovishieldTM doses 3 months apart and were classified by baseline serostatus using DiaSorin TrimericS IgG. Vaccination significantly increased anti-spike antibodies in both seronegative and seropositive groups, with CovishieldTM showing higher antibody magnitudes than Covaxinâ at tested timepoints. In seronegative participants, seroconversion after doses was higher for CovishieldTM (93.2% and 98.3%) than for Covaxinâ (36.6% and 74.4%), and in seropositive participants CovishieldTM showed higher rates and titers than Covaxinâ, with a substantial fraction of Covaxinâ recipients not responding. Neutralizing antibody testing showed CovishieldTM elicited significant neutralizing responses, while Covaxinâ did not show statistically significant increases despite rises in GMT. In the earliest cohort (BBH), CovishieldTM induced higher frequencies of spike-specific CD4 and CD8 T cells in seronegative participants; in seropositive participants, neither vaccine increased spike-specific CD4 or CD8 frequencies. Across SARS-CoV-2 variants measured by ACE2 inhibition and neutralization approaches, responses against multiple variants were generally stronger with CovishieldTM than with Covaxinâ, and overall breadth and potency were higher with CovishieldTM and in seropositive than seronegative individuals. The authors conclude that the vectored vaccine elicits stronger and broader anti-spike responses than the inactivated vaccine, Omicron-specific antibody responses from asymptomatic infection wane faster than WT/Delta responses, and vaccine non-responsiveness in seropositive subjects is associated with higher baseline antibody titers.

The speaker says he has been overwhelmed by a recent sad event and feels incompetent for the important duties unexpectedly placed on him. He states that any policy for administering the government must develop as the administration progresses and should be shown by actions, using past experience as assurance for the future. He describes his long public service as based on principles of right and his efforts to establish and perpetuate free government, ameliorate conditions for Americans, and believe that the government will ultimately triumph. He concludes by asking for encouragement and support to carry the government through present perils.

Zebronics, an India supplier of IT peripherals, Audio/Video, and Surveillance products, launched its new “Buddy Speakers” priced at Rs.1699. The lightweight, portable wireless speaker weighs 630g and has an LED display with RGB lighting. It features 5 watts RMS output, is designed to fill a small to medium room and work outdoors, and includes a built-in rechargeable battery for up to 3 hours of music. It offers Bluetooth wireless connection with a 10-meter range, built-in FM for live streaming music, and connectivity options including USB, MicroSD, and AUX. Zebronics Director Pradeep Doshi said the speaker is intended to deliver “BIG Sound” in a small design.

The passage argues that apprenticeships will not become more accessible without stronger pre-apprenticeship pathways into construction careers. It says traditional construction apprenticeships are highly selective, favor students with pre-existing knowledge, require advanced technical coursework, and have cumbersome applications, leaving motivated students needing extra help “locked out.” Pre-apprenticeships are presented as short-term programs that expose participants to careers and employers, build skills, connect them with mentors, and prepare them for entry assessments, sometimes leading to industry-recognized credentials; they are described as more effective when linked to real opportunities like union programs, employers, and registered apprenticeships. The passage states that pre-apprenticeships are not more popular mainly because of lack of funding, which limits program capacity and outcome tracking. It proposes rethinking financing for wraparound supports (such as transportation, childcare, or lost wages) using instruments like zero-percent loans or emergency credit, improving data collection by demonstrating graduation and apprenticeship placement outcomes, and using these results to attract additional funding. It concludes that investing in construction pathways and expanding partnerships across employers, unions, government, and philanthropy can improve talent pipelines and economic mobility.

An experiment showed that an AI tool, called Waldo, can scan social media posts to help public health workers identify harmful side effects, using cannabis use as an example. Waldo reviewed more than 430,000 Reddit posts, flagged about 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects, and researchers verified 86% of 250 flagged posts. The tool aims to capture health experiences that public health agencies may not monitor because they do not track social media. Waldo was trained on a subset of posts and outperformed ChatGPT in marking false positives, though it did not outperform human reviewers. Researchers say further testing is needed to see whether Waldo works for other drugs or products, and they suggest any future use should be done ethically with privacy protections.

The passage describes “Robodoc,” a prototype medical chatbot that integrates conversational AI with specialized machine-learning models. The author uses openAI Large Language Models and function calling to route user text or image inputs to appropriate models and generate human-friendly responses. The system includes two main model types: a diabetes detection model built with TensorFlow.js from a numerical dataset, and image-based models trained with Teachable Machine/transfer learning to detect conditions from X-ray (viral/bacterial pneumonia) and OCT eye images (Drusen, CNV, and DME). The chatbot also includes a stub function for scheduling medical appointments based on condition seriousness. Results are presented as behavior demonstrations (not statistical analyses), reporting mostly correct operation with some noted errors, such as urgency classification issues in retinal cases and occasional pneumonia misclassifications. The author outlines methods, datasets, system implementation details (Angular/TypeScript, browser-based simulations, and openAI API models), related literature context, limitations (unpredictable model outputs), and future improvements such as integrating image- and text-triggered paths and expanding capabilities.

The passage describes NVIDIA Turing GPUs’ enhanced Tensor Cores (from Volta) that add INT8 and INT4 precision modes for quantization-tolerant inference while fully supporting FP16 for higher-precision workloads. It explains how Turing Tensor Cores accelerate matrix-matrix operations central to neural network training and inference, and how they enable real-time deep learning features in GeForce gaming GPUs through NVIDIA NGX Neural Services (e.g., DLSS, InPainting, Super Rez, Slow-Mo). It provides performance and architectural details such as TU102’s number of Tensor Cores and per-clock operation capability, and discusses broader adoption of NVIDIA GPU-based inferencing (including Tesla T4) and data center features like enhanced video/video engine support, multi-process service, and increased memory bandwidth and capacity. The passage further covers Turing architecture improvements including memory subsystem changes (GDDR6, L2 cache, lossless compression), display/video engine capabilities (e.g., DP 1.4a, HDR, NVENC/NVDEC updates), VR-oriented connectivity (USB Type-C and VirtualLink), inter-GPU communication with NVLink, and real-time ray tracing enabled by RT Cores and a hybrid rendering pipeline using BVH traversal, denoising, and RTX-compatible technologies. It also details NGX software architecture and DLSS training approaches, plus additional rendering/shading capabilities such as Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading (VRS), Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR), including how these features optimize performance and reduce shading work.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington told the Wilson County Commission that the upcoming total solar eclipse will draw large crowds and described its effects, including that only areas within the 70-mile-wide total eclipse path will experience totality and darkness. She said half the U.S. population is within a one-day drive of the eclipse path and noted the maximum viewing time is 2 minutes and 40 seconds, with Wilson County’s fairgrounds about 2 seconds off the longest time. Wellington also said an extra 100,000 people are expected in St. Joseph, Missouri. The commission voted to allow officers to keep their service weapons upon retirement, and to equip Springdale Elementary School with a school resource officer when the school opens in August, supported by a $10,000 budget amendment for training and certification. Rezoning moved more than 500 students and 200 students from Stoner Creek and Elzie D. Patton Elementary to Springdale Elementary.

The passage discusses swing trading indicators and how they should be evaluated using risk-adjusted return, comparing gross return to maximum system drawdown. Swing trading is described as holding positions for roughly one day to a few weeks (rarely longer than a month). The recommended time frame for swing trading indicators is typically 1–15 days. The article states that six indicators were tested and that conclusions were based on the indicator with the best risk-adjusted return, not necessarily the highest return. It defines swing trading indicators as often oscillating between upper and lower bands, such as mean-reverting oscillators like RSI, Stochastics, and Williams %R. The passage concludes that Williams %R is the best swing trading indicator, citing stable and solid results across variables and the lowest average maximum drawdown. The indicators mentioned as part of the test set include Williams %R, WilliamsVixFix, Bollinger Bands, Stochastics, the Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator, and RSI, and the backtests were run on SPY as a proxy for the S&P 500.

The passage describes a video encoding/decoding application and invention related to improving intra-prediction and inter-prediction efficiency in video signals. It outlines background on HEVC and inter-prediction, noting that inter-prediction can be less accurate when video correlation drops (e.g., during brightness changes) and that more precise motion information increases transmitted data and overhead.

The invention’s technical solutions include: determining whether a current block is merged with an adjacent neighbor block, obtaining motion information and a weight prediction parameter, selecting a reference block, and generating a prediction block using the weight prediction parameter; adjusting motion vector precision using reconstructed adjacent pixels; decoding and optionally correcting intra-prediction results using intra-prediction mode information and correction decisions; determining intra-prediction modes using candidate modes, neighbor frequency, or differences from a previous block; and dividing blocks into sub-blocks for prediction.

Encoding/decoding procedures for weight prediction are described, including encoding flags for whether motion information and weight prediction parameters are merged, encoding/decoding weight prediction information (either directly or as differences from prediction values, possibly based on regression), and performing inter-prediction by applying multiplication and addition parameters to prediction pixels. Additional described methods include deriving weight prediction parameters from reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block and reference/prediction blocks, possibly using multiple lines or sampled pixel ranges, and selecting among candidate parameter estimation methods via transmitted indices.

The passage also describes correction of intra-prediction results using a “correction coefficient” derived from reconstructed-pixel-area features (e.g., standard deviation) and regression analysis, where encoding and decoding involve flags and information to enable deriving or signaling the correction coefficient. It concludes with intended advantageous effects (improved efficiencies and precision) and a discussion of related video encoder/decoder apparatus components and diagram descriptions.

Organized patriotism, which replaces local pride with loyalty to the whole nation, is presented as crucial to a country’s growth and strength. The passage argues that national success depends on unity across sections and classes, including cooperation between industrial and agricultural workers and between capitalists and wageworkers. It says efficient education is likely next in importance to patriotism, but notes that the federal system limits national leadership in technical industrial education, leaving much to the states. It calls for the National Government to ensure that District of Columbia schools promote commercial and especially industrial training, including foreign trade in commercial training. The passage warns against training boys and girls only in literary accomplishments, which it says can leave them unfit for industrial work, and argues that technical education is needed for industrial development and to compete against educated labor. It also emphasizes supporting wageworkers and urges broad interpretation of constitutional provisions to enable action on industrial training and child labor and factory laws. Finally, it states that the welfare of farmers is vital to national growth, and argues that farming must become technical and scientific, supported by practical training and better organization among farmers.

The passage is from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015. It includes consolidated financial statements (income statements, comprehensive income, balance sheets, cash flows, and stockholders’ equity), key accounting notes, segment information, and an independent registered public accounting firm review. For the three months ended September 30, 2015, Microsoft reported revenue of $20,379 million, operating income of $5,793 million, and net income of $4,620 million (diluted EPS $0.57). The balance sheet shows total assets of $172,896 million and total liabilities of $95,451 million as of September 30, 2015. Notes describe accounting policies, earnings per share, other income (expense), investments, derivatives, fair value measurements, inventories, business combinations (including the Mojang acquisition), goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, unearned revenue (including Windows 10 deferrals), contingencies and legal proceedings, restructuring charges, share repurchases, dividends, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment revenue and operating income for Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.

The leu traded steady as investors awaited a decision from Romania’s central bank on whether to continue raising interest rates. Romanian bonds were flat, and analysts said the decision would mainly affect longer bond tenors. Regional currencies were mixed: the forint and Czech crown rose slightly after investors reduced some emerging-market currency selling following the yuan’s rebound, though the crown had been weak despite rate hikes. The market expected Romania’s fourth rate hike of the year to be a quarter-point to 2.75%, and the central bank had tightened monetary conditions by allowing 3-month ROBOR to rise. In Hungary, short-term rates remained low while longer yields rose amid inflation concerns, and the NBH held discussions on inflation trends with analysts, with minutes of its June 19 meeting due to be published later.

Share prices rose across most major Asian markets after last week’s losses, supported by expectations of a more dovish Federal Reserve linked to weak US inflation data and easing US–North Korea tensions. Singapore’s STI gained 29 points (0.9%) to 3,308.69 with 2.2 billion shares traded; Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 1.4%, South Korea’s Kospi 0.6%, and China’s Shanghai Composite 0.9%. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell nearly 1%. The passage notes that US equities had ended a three-day losing streak but still posted the worst weekly loss since March, while geopolitical nerves were described as having eased after assurances that confrontation with North Korea was not imminent, though investors remained cautious. In Singapore, gainers slightly outnumbered losers (234 up, 230 down), with OCBC Bank and DBS Group leading gains, while UOB declined. Property stocks such as CapitaLand and City Developments also rose, and Olam International increased after reporting higher second-quarter net profit.

U.S. stocks opened higher Monday after the Easter holiday, with technology leading gains and industrial and consumer companies also rising following China’s slightly faster first-quarter economic growth report. Major indexes were up by about 0.5–0.6 percent in early trading. Notable stock moves included Nvidia and Alphabet up, while Netflix rose ahead of its quarterly results after the market closes; Amazon also gained. The passage also reports Alere surged after accepting a lower buyout offer from Abbott, while Eli Lilly and Incyte fell after the FDA refused approval of their rheumatoid arthritis pill. Other company-specific changes included Snyder’s-Lance dropping on a weak forecast, Arconic rising after its CEO agreed to step down, and Straight Path Communications climbing on the possibility of another buyout offer. Oil prices were slightly lower, bond yields eased, the dollar fell against the yen, the euro rose, and several overseas markets were closed for Easter while Japan and South Korea posted small gains.

The passage describes challenges and limitations in current HPC usage, including the need for specialized IT infrastructure and the options of using in-house HPC environments or external HPC infrastructure. It reports that most enterprises prefer outsourcing workloads: 87% of HPC users use or plan to use external HPC infrastructure from cloud providers. Some enterprises operate their own HPC infrastructure while outsourcing datacenter services like power and cooling; 74% plan to use colocation datacenters. Innovation partners like scientific research institutions are used or planned by 43% of industrial enterprises but are only suitable to a certain extent for time-sensitive commercial deployments due to preferences for scientific projects and long waiting times. Only 6% currently have their own on-premises HPC infrastructure, while 28% plan to use it within two years, and among manufacturing enterprises planning future HPC use, only seven intend to set up their own on-premises infrastructure.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can be operated in primary-secondary mode using the SYNC pin. With the primary controller’s RT pin populated, SYNC provides a clock signal at twice the switching frequency; this clock is used by the secondary controller in external synchronization mode, with the secondary RT pin left floating. Primary-secondary mode supports synchronizing two independent converters to the same switching frequency without other connections, and designing a single interleaved parallel-phase converter, where VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC pins are also connected. The secondary controller inverts the received clock, creating a phase shift between the primary and secondary switching outputs of 90° or 270°, depending on synchronization timing.

The passage explains how to backtest a MACD (Moving Average Convergence/Divergence) trading strategy in Python. It describes downloading Apple historical data from Yahoo Finance using yfinance, using pandas to calculate the MACD (12-period EMA minus 26-period EMA), computing the 9-period signal line, and deriving the histogram as the MACD minus the signal line. It then outlines a classic strategy where the regime is set to 1 when the histogram is nonnegative and 0 otherwise, with regime values applied to the next row to account for return timing. The strategy returns are plotted, and results are reported: the MACD strategy achieved 15.04% CAGR versus 19.07% for buy-and-hold, while it was invested 51.13% of the time, and the strategy is stated to be informational purposes.

Jean Chrétien said Canada is divided by mountains, prairies, and rivers, and sometimes by language, skin colour, and religion. The day after the Yonge St. van attack left 10 dead and 14 injured, he said he was heartened by Torontonians’ reaction. At a Liberal nomination meeting in Vaughan-Woodbridge attended by about 1,000 Liberals, Chrétien said people came together in both good and bad times. Economic Development Minister Steven Del Duca urged attendees to reflect on the events and emphasized community unity, including donating blood to Sunnybrook hospital and Canadian Blood Services. Del Duca said political campaigns have ups and downs and praised Premier Kathleen Wynne for initiatives including a subway extension, a new hospital, raising the minimum wage to $14 an hour, and free tuition. Chrétien praised Wynne’s courage. Outside the hall, several hundred members of LiUNA Local 183 protested labour changes from last month’s budget bill that affected work sites, and they demonstrated at Queen’s Park Monday morning.

The passage explains a problem in monocular 3D human pose estimation: predicted skeletons are camera-centered, so physical motion changes its 3D joint trajectories when the person or camera moves, distorting kinematic signals and complicating longitudinal analysis. It introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic rectification module that maps an estimated 3D pose (joint coordinates) into a fixed body-centered canonical frame by predicting a global rotation (from a continuous 6D representation converted to a valid SO(3) matrix) and an optional residual correction for fine-tuning joint positions. The network uses a hybrid encoder with parallel graph convolutional (adaptive adjacency) and transformer branches, fused via cross-attention with adaptive gating, and is trained end-to-end using a composite loss including pose reconstruction (MSE), geodesic rotation loss, cycle consistency, perceptual bone/joint-angle penalties, and regularization terms. Evaluations on MM-Fi show reduced positional error (MPJPE) and substantially reduced global orientation error, with stable performance across cross-subject and cross-environment protocols. On TotalCapture, without training or fine-tuning, canonicalized pose-derived wrist acceleration signals more closely match synchronized IMU signals than a deterministic geometric baseline, particularly under challenging lateral viewpoints. The conclusion states that pose-only canonicalization reduces viewpoint-induced variability and improves the stability and physical fidelity of kinematic trajectories, while noting limitations related to residual non-rigidity, lack of absolute scale, dependence on input pose quality, and pose-space augmentation during training.

The passage discusses how changes in federal tax withholding under the new 2018 tax law may alter the amount of federal income tax taken out of paychecks, with consumers and businesses being advised to watch for tax-related ID fraud. It says the extra take-home pay varies by situation, including filing status, income, children, pay frequency, and W-4 allowances. Examples given include a married couple with one income making $90,000 with two children seeing about $61 more per semi-monthly paycheck, and a single person with no children making $35,000 seeing nearly $32 more. The IRS says employers should use the new 2018 withholding tables as soon as possible, but no later than Feb. 15. The passage also explains how child tax credit changes for children under 17 could increase take-home pay for some families, why different coworkers may see different withholding based on how their W-4 was completed, and when taxpayers may need to revisit their W-4 as deduction rules change. It further notes that bonus checks are withheld at a 22% rate instead of 25%, and provides example withholding amounts.

Bill Norton, a 2019 four-star defensive lineman from Christian Brothers and the nation’s 11th-ranked strong-side defensive end, announced he committed to the University of Georgia. He chose Georgia over offers from multiple schools including Alabama, LSU, Ohio State, Notre Dame, Penn State, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, and Tennessee. Norton made the decision about a day after visiting Tennessee following Jeremy Pruitt’s hiring, and he was described by his coach as an athletic, lean player with a knack for finding the football.

The passage explains how ICT and online education have expanded in African universities since the 1990s, supported by flexible education policies and improved ICT infrastructure following late-1990s ICT/deregulation initiatives. It also describes challenges to online learning in Africa, including limited internet access, weak ICT policies, inadequate digital skills among faculty, poor infrastructure, difficulties with digital materials, and resistance to technology. The text then outlines warfare in Africa, its causes, impacts on civilians and higher education institutions, and how online education can serve as a “lifeline” during wartime by enabling continued, remote learning, though it requires training and funding.

The study uses bibliometric analysis to review published research on “wartime and online education.” It defines bibliometrics and describes a PRISMA-based four-step approach using the Scopus database. The search (2000–2024; earliest identified 2009) initially retrieved 90 documents, with 53 included for bibliometric analysis and further narrowing to related terms. Results report that the highest publication counts by country are from the United States and Ukraine, with additional countries having fewer or none. Publication trends show fluctuations, with an increase in 2023 and a decrease in 2024. The findings also summarize results by journal, document type, subject area, and keyword co-occurrence, including two keyword clusters related to learning and to warfare. The discussion highlights a research gap regarding wartime and education in Africa, noting that none of the countries with the highlighted results are African, and concludes that more research is needed on the intersection of wartime challenges and online learning in African higher education, including links to organisational sustainability. Limitations include reliance on Scopus only and not analyzing authorship, affiliations, citations, or reference connections.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic Party operative known for political pranks and subterfuge aimed at tormenting Richard Nixon, died at 94 on Monday in Tucson, Arizona, according to his longtime friend Lorraine Glicksman. Tuck, who described his approach as not malicious, introduced bogus fortune cookies into campaigns, including one in 1958 for Republican Senator William Knowland. As a student in 1950, he arranged and carried out a Nixon campus visit by booking an auditorium, inviting only a few people, and introducing Nixon with a long speech before asking about the International Monetary Fund. He also posed as a fire marshal at Nixon appearances and gave reporters low crowd estimates, and he staged other incidents such as having an elderly woman tell Nixon after a debate with John F. Kennedy that he would do better next time. In 1962, he infiltrated a Chinatown crowd with a Chinese sign about the “Hughes loan,” which Nixon reportedly responded to by ripping up. Tuck worked on Robert F. Kennedy’s 1968 campaign and ran for California Senate in 1966, receiving 10 percent of the vote in the Democratic primary. He also said in 2014 he wanted Aug. 9, the day Nixon resigned, to be made a national holiday called “Nixmas.”

Mathieu Henderson said he exceeded expectations during his four-year Ontario Hockey League career with the Flint Firebirds, finishing ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring with 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games. He ended the OHL season in late March when Flint was eliminated 4-1 by the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds. Henderson described his early OHL experience as nerve-wracking due to highly drafted players, and noted his improvement after rookie and sophomore seasons. After Flint relocated from Plymouth to Flint for the 2015-16 season, Henderson continued to perform despite a suspension involving Rolf Nilsen. He said coaches helped him focus on defence, improving his plus/minus to minus-seven from minus-45. He played three ECHL games for the South Carolina Stingrays after receiving a call during the OHL playoffs, then returned to deciding his next step, which could be playing pro in North America or Europe or going to school. Henderson credited his parents, Randy and Brenda, for much of his support and success.

The passage is a lecture on online markets and auction mechanisms, beginning with a review of Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) mechanisms and how they implement the utilitarian social optimum in dominant strategies for private-value social choice problems, while generally not being budget balanced and potentially being impractical due to large action spaces. It then focuses on Google’s dominance in search and advertising, describing how Google runs an auction for ads on each search query, generally showing more ads for more commercial queries, and using a system based on per-click bids and “quality scores” to rank ads and determine payments. The lecture argues that Google’s ad auction can be modeled (via an Edelman-Ostrovsky-Schwarz framework) as a type of generalized clock auction with bid shading, and that under equilibrium behavior the resulting payments reproduce VCG payments, implying efficiency and an ex post equilibrium that can reduce the need for continual bid updating. The discussion continues to address why Google’s non-budget-balanced structure and reservation prices matter, and then summarizes related work: a model where reserve prices and welfare can align when search has costs, and additional papers on endogenous pricing and platform information design (including how signal structures can affect competition and outcomes).

The passage describes an approach to managing and querying machine-generated data in computing environments. It explains that indexes can speed search by mapping keys to locations, but index storage can become costly as data and indexing grow. It outlines an event-based data intake and query system (similar to SPLUNK® ENTERPRISE), where raw input is parsed into timestamped events, fields are extracted using a late-binding schema during search time, and searches are handled by a search head and indexers that can use a keyword index and other acceleration techniques (parallel indexer querying, keyword indexing, high performance analytics stores, and accelerated report generation). It also discusses data models for structured, hierarchical search-time mappings, and examples of report and visualization user interfaces. Additional sections cover security and monitoring applications, including storing minimally processed data for later analysis at search time. The passage also includes many references to figures, interfaces, and incorporated prior patent applications.

GST is scheduled for rollout from July 1, with preparations at an advanced stage. The civil aviation ministry has written to the finance ministry seeking a two-month postponement, saying airlines need more time to revamp systems to comply and are not yet ready. Airlines have raised concerns about changes required in global ticket distribution systems, unclear areas affecting their business and potential higher operational costs, and whether movement of “stocks (equipment or aircraft parts)” would be taxed. Minister of State for Civil Aviation Jayant Sinha chaired a meeting on GST preparedness with aviation stakeholders. The finance ministry said GST is on track for July 1 and denied rumours of delay.

The IRS announced higher federal tax brackets for 2026 to adjust for inflation, along with increases to the standard deduction and other related tax provisions. For 2026, the standard deduction will be $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single taxpayers. The IRS also raised thresholds for bracket income and boosted other figures including the long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemption, and eligibility for the earned income tax credit. The top 37% rate applies to taxable income above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for married couples filing jointly. The announcements came a day after the IRS said it would furlough nearly half its workforce due to the government shutdown.

The passage describes SEV/SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest–hypervisor communication using the GHCB and VMGEXIT/VMRUN protocols. It specifies GHCBData bitfields for GHCB guest physical address alignment, supported protocol version ranges, and the SEV page table encryption bit number. The hypervisor supplies protocol version range and required SEV encryption bit position; guests choose a version and may terminate if unsupported. Because CPUID interception can trigger #VC, a CPUID request protocol (with request/return register values) and an SEV information request protocol are described. It also outlines protocols for SEV-related tasks such as terminating the guest, registering/unregistering a preferred or specified GHCB GPA, and requesting CPUID/SEV information before the GHCB is established. Additional sections cover GHCB negotiation and VMGEXIT examples, NAE event handling (including VALID_BITMAP usage, required SW_EXITCODE/exit info fields, and guest/hypervisor responsibilities), and specific NAE events like page state changes, SNP guest requests (including certificate-related extended requests), AP creation/reset hold behavior, doorbell page operations for Restricted Injection, and other #HV-related support (including timer and APIC ID list). The passage further describes SNP secrets/CPUID page provisioning, secrets page reserved-area format for guest message sequencing, and a standardized #HV doorbell page data structure and behavior for interrupt delivery, acknowledgement, and EOI handling.

Egyptian archaeologists unveiled the tomb of Old Kingdom priestess Hetpet on the Giza plateau near Cairo. Antiquities Minister Khaled al-Enany said the tomb, built for Hetpet, a priestess to Hathor, was found during excavation in Giza’s western cemetery, which contains Fifth Dynasty tombs. The ministry reported the tomb has Fifth Dynasty architectural and decorative features, including wall paintings in good condition showing Hetpet in hunting, fishing, receiving offerings, musical and dancing scenes, and two monkey scenes. Waziri said such scenes are unusual and previously appeared in the Saqqara tomb of “Ka-Iber.” The tomb also includes a purification basin engraved with Hetpet’s name and titles; al-Enany said related artifacts were found in 1909 and moved to the Berlin museum. Excavations will continue to seek further discoveries.

SOS full court pressure scenarios are designed to force the offensive team to react to backcourt pressure. Depending on circumstances, they can increase or decrease game tempo, serve as a change of pace, or be used as a surprise tactic, and they aim to wear the offensive team down. Player fatigue is cited as a common cause of ball handling errors and forced shots, leading to turnovers and transition opportunities. The primary full court pressure scenarios are called “shadow” full court actions, where a second defender shadows (plays behind) the ON-ball defender. The three primary scenarios—Back shadow, Up shadow, and Face shadow—differ only in their initial defensive alignments; the secondary scenarios are “Blitz” pressures, described as the most aggressive and involving denial of all first passing lanes with trapping in the deep back court. The passage lists a six-fold purpose for SOS backcourt pressure, including creating turnovers, forcing full-court advancement against pressure, increasing passing lane distance, disrupting offensive movements and tempo, removing the ball from the playmaker’s hands, and changing tempo to disrupt game plan actions. It states effectiveness depends on executing basic SOS defensive fundamentals, including forcing the ball away from the middle and denying middle penetration through aggressive denial of first passing lanes and other SOS ON/OFF-ball fundamentals. All SOS full court pressure scenarios except “hold” actions end in Base Go Red, a second trap scenario, and full court pressure is off if the shadow player cannot reach proper position or if certain outlet passes are made, reverting to basic half court SOS defense.

The UK and Ukraine discussed future trade and investment links after the UK leaves the EU, following Deputy Minister Nataliya Mykolska’s visit to London. They welcomed efforts to avoid disruption to trade and to ensure continuity of the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement and its DCFTA, which supports more than £1.7 billion in trade once the UK leaves the EU. The UK also informed Ukraine that during the EU-UK Implementation Period it will be treated as a member state for international agreements, providing certainty that existing trading arrangements and the preferential DCFTA terms will continue to apply. Both countries agreed to work together to strengthen UK-Ukrainian trade.

The speaker says there was little difference between Anaheim and the game tonight and that they did not play the game they could. They mention that although Danny O’Halloran felt a puck crossing the ice was not a goal, officials reviewed it in Toronto and determined it was not a goal, and the team must move on. The opponent capitalized on a power play, and while the opponent had not done so in a previous game, they played their plan tonight while the speaker’s team did not. The game is now behind them, and they need to focus on the next one.

Substance use disorders (SUD) are psychiatric conditions associated with increased mortality and socioeconomic burden. The passage describes evidence that extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules regulate reward memories and focuses on perineuronal nets (PNNs), which stabilize synapses and restrict synaptic plasticity. Preclinical studies suggest that chronic drug use increases PNN components and that inhibiting matrix metalloproteases can weaken cocaine reward memories. The hippocampus, especially CA1, is highlighted as important for integrating reward signaling with contextual memories, and hippocampal PNNs may affect inhibitory neurons and neurotransmitter systems.

The study described uses human postmortem hippocampal samples from subjects with SUD, SUD with comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD), MDD, and controls, along with rhesus macaque samples with or without chronic alcohol self-administration. Human results report significantly increased PNN numerical densities in sector CA1 in subjects with SUD, with additional increases in other hippocampal subregions. Gene expression findings include increased parvalbumin (Pvb) in SUD and decreased expression of ECM proteolytic genes (Mmp9 and Ctss) in SUD. Synaptic marker results include increased Vamp2 mRNA in SUD, while Syn1 gene expression showed no significant group differences. Increased WFA-labeled glial cells (co-expressing GFAP) were also observed in SUD in specific hippocampal regions.

In contrast, MDD showed generally decreased PNN densities in CA1. Comorbid SUD/MDD showed patterns that sometimes opposed or amplified SUD or MDD findings, including altered expression of ECM-related genes such as Chsy1. In macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration, the study found increased PNN densities and increased WFA-labeled glia.

The passage concludes that increased hippocampal PNNs and associated ECM and synaptic changes in SUD support the idea that PNNs may stabilize reward memories and could be targets for addressing cue-induced relapse, while emphasizing differences from MDD and the importance of considering comorbidities.

The passage describes systems and methods for localizing and classifying abnormalities in medical images, including a prostate-cancer example. It discusses receiving an input image, using trained localization and classification networks (jointly trained in phases) to generate localization maps and output lesion classification, with options for multi-modality fusion and lesion scoring via regression. It also presents an abnormality-detection approach that generates multiple incomplete images by deleting portions, synthesizes healthy replacements with a trained GAN, determines a “normal” image from synthesized results, and detects abnormalities by comparing the input image to the normal image using a detector network that outputs localization maps. Finally, it outlines deep learning model training across multiple clinical sites using a two-stage process (training on multi-site data, then optimizing on a deployment site using small labeled data with uncertainty-based sample reordering).

Trump tweeted about a “phony Russia Collusion Witch Hunt,” questioning who would restore the lives he said were devastated. The passage says fewer young aides left due to the investigation than due to infighting, and describes Trump’s continued frustration with the investigations, which he believes aim to delegitimize him. It also covers whether Trump will sit for questioning by special counsel Robert Mueller, with Rudy Giuliani declining to confirm details and saying he was uncomfortable with an obstruction question as a matter of interpretation. The passage notes Trump repeated claims about the FBI using informants as spying, and that Sen. Marco Rubio said the FBI is investigating suspicious individuals connected to a campaign rather than the campaign itself. It further reports that Trump attacked The New York Times, falsely claiming a quoted source didn’t exist, and says the source was a real senior official briefed under rules not to use his name.

A review of the first year of UVA Health System’s thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program found it helped patients leave the hospital sooner while reducing healthcare costs and opioid use. The program reduced morphine-equivalent use by 74% for one patient group and 59% for another without worsening patients’ pain evaluations, shortened median hospital stay for thoracotomy patients by two days, and saved more than $1.3 million while freeing beds for an estimated 28 additional patients. The review also reported benefits without increasing surgical complication or readmission rates. UVA launched the thoracic ERAS program in early 2016, enrolled 139 patients in its first year, and compared their outcomes with more than 220 prior non-enrolled patients; findings were published in the *Annals of Thoracic Surgery*.

Two militants affiliated with the outlawed Lashkar-e-Jhangvi, Shaikh Muhammad Mumtaz and Muhammad Ahmed Khan alias Muna, escaped from the Central Jail in Karachi late Tuesday night. Following the jailbreak, jail officials suspended at least a dozen employees, including the superintendent of jail, and district police were approached to register cases against them for negligence. A DIG prisons letter requested FIR lodging against the escaped prisoners and suspended officials, citing security differences at the ATCs complex and other details; IG Prisons also said a committee was formed to investigate, teams were dispatched to nab suspects, and there would be zero tolerance. Separately, a robber was killed in an exchange of fire in the Defence Housing Authority area of Gizri police station limits after police intervened when gunmen attempted to snatch a car; the bandit died and Imtiaz was seriously injured, while the accomplice fled. Karachi police also claimed arrests of at least 15 outlaws in raids, along with recovery of weapons and narcotics.

The speaker says winning the Stanley Cup comes down to winning a single game and that it is no different from other playoff overtime situations. They note that teams do not have perfect playoff records and that they have lost games before. The message emphasizes preparing for the next game, not dwelling on losses, and aiming to win.

The passage reports on President Emmanuel Macron’s first formal meeting with Nigeria’s President Muhammadu Buhari since Buhari took office. It says Macron arrived in Abuja and was received by Foreign Minister Geoffrey Onyeama, and that their talks would cover security efforts including France’s proposed G-5 Sahel force against Al-Qaeda in the Maghreb and other armed groups, as well as intelligence sharing and Nigeria’s multinational joint task force against Boko Haram. It also notes a MoU for French energy and environmental companies to launch a reforestation and agricultural project in Ogun State aimed at creating about 150,000 jobs, and mentions Macron’s remarks about terrorism being Nigeria’s responsibility and the need to address why young people join terrorist groups. The passage further describes an investigative report on child trafficking in Gabon, involving 12- and 13-year-old children brought from Benin and Mali and sold in Libreville, with one found chained and freed and now housed in a state-run transit center; it states Gabon is among nine West and Central African countries where the UN has documented long-standing child labour exploitation.

Investing.com highlights several market items, including a surge in AMD shares after an AI chip deal with OpenAI, gold rallying above $3,900/oz amid a yen slump and U.S. rate cut bets, and commentary that a “bubble scenario” could take the S&P 500 to 9,000 in 2026. The passage also discusses technical outlooks for USD/JPY, GBP/USD, and BTC/USD, including potential support and resistance levels and scenarios for continued downside or recovery. It notes upcoming Fed officials’ speeches and the Bank of England policy announcement, along with revised and weaker economic data referenced in relation to market reactions.

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation says families in the UK need £40,000 a year for a decent standard of living, due to rising costs including childcare, transport and energy. It reports that working couples with two children require £20,000 per parent (up from £13,900 in 2008), while single people need £18,400 (up from £13,400 a decade ago). The passage argues redistribution would not solve the issue because only around 30% of households earn more than £40,000, and the remainder cannot be brought up through taxing the excess. It suggests reducing costs by loosening regulation on childcare and housebuilding, then proposes stopping taxation below the required income standard by raising the personal allowance to £18,400 and taxing couples separately. It concludes that redistribution would require the country to be much richer, and calls for less government, lower taxation, and more economic growth.

Courtland’s pitcher Alex Kobersteen and Culpeper’s Micah Leuterio set the tone in Culpeper’s 2-1 win Monday, with routine plays and seven Culpeper-related errors in the final two innings proving decisive. Trailing 1-0 in the sixth, Culpeper tied the game on a single by Brady Richardson and subsequent errors, then took the lead in the seventh when Hunter Bowers reached on an error, stole, advanced, and scored on an RBI grounder that Ethan Critz failed to handle. Kobersteen struck out nine and walked none over a complete game, but both runs were unearned. Courtland’s Jake Dudley also pitched a complete game with nine strikeouts and two hits allowed, and Burrow scored Courtland’s lone run on a steal of home. Coaches Tim Acors and Brandon Mack emphasized the importance of making fewer mistakes and completing a defensive game.

The Department of Education said it will halt two Obama-era rules scheduled to take effect July 1 and will instead create committees to review and improve them. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos said the step is to ensure the rules help harmed students. The halted rules involved the “gainful employment” standard affecting federal aid for certain colleges and the Borrower Defense to Repayment rule for borrowers misled or defrauded by their colleges, including a fast-track forgiveness process for closed schools. The department said it will keep its debt forgiveness promise to 16,000 borrowers with claims being processed. Critics and opponents, including a California association of for-profit schools and a lawsuit by the group, argued the rules are burdensome and threaten institutions, while Democratic attorneys general and senators urged keeping the rules in place. The department also plans hearings in July.

This VentureWire newsletter (Thursday, November 30, 2000) lists top stories and brief updates on venture capital activities. Highlights include 724 Solutions agreeing to acquire Tantau Software for about $375 million; El Dorado Ventures forming a $250 million fund; MaMaMedia reducing staff to 15 and aiming to seek a merger or acquisition; and iVMG appointing Samer Salameh as its first president and CEO. The newsletter also reports multiple “new money” rounds and “new products” launches, several board and leadership appointments, and venture fund news such as Hyperion Partners raising $73 million of a $100 million fund and Crosspoint postponing its $1 billion ninth fund. It concludes with corrections, company and investor index listings, and subscription/contact information.

Etisalat Nigeria has not yet agreed a deal with local banks to restructure a $1.2 billion loan after it missed a payment, Reuters was told by a company source. The source said Etisalat and 13 Nigerian lenders had not agreed on a restructuring proposal. At Etisalat’s annual general meeting in Abu Dhabi, CEO Saleh Al Abdooli declined to comment on the debt talks when asked by Reuters, and Etisalat did not respond to a request for comment. In March, regulators agreed with local banks to pursue a default deal rather than receivership to avoid deterring investors and a wider debt crisis, and sources said Etisalat may consider selling its stake in Nigeria after the debt deal is agreed.

The passage describes the purpose and rules of an offensive soccer goal kick, which is taken after the defending team wins the ball back by kicking the ball over the end line from within the goal area, with opposing players outside the penalty area until the kick is taken. The ball becomes live when kicked and visibly moves, and play follows Law 16. It explains that field dimensions and rules are often modified for younger teams, introducing “build-out lines” for 10 and under to prevent defenders from challenging before retreating past the line and to support goal-kick play development. It outlines progressive goal-kick training steps for youth (generally 10 and under, then 11 and above), including designated kickers, targets, secondary receivers, midfield support, and positioning on both sides of the goal area, with defenders added gradually to emphasize realistic kicking distance and movement toward the ball. For adults, it notes that more goal-kick options are available, often with the goalkeeper taking the kick, including short, deep, and targeted kicks to reduce chances of losing the ball. The passage also emphasizes goal kicks as restarts/direct plays and gives examples of goals or corner kicks caused by wind and field conditions.

Greece’s central bank chief, Yannis Stournaras, urged Athens and its foreign lenders to complete the country’s bailout review by the end of February, warning that further delays would renew uncertainty, make a deal harder, and undermine the expected economic recovery. He said negotiations have stalled over disagreements on reforms, fiscal targets, and the IMF’s role. Euro zone finance ministers are expected to discuss the issue in Brussels next week after Tsakalotos met with key euro zone and EU officials last week. Stournaras added that uncertainty could weaken Greek banks’ capital adequacy and noted that household deposit trends reversed in the first weeks of this year. Greece’s economy has been expanding and is expected to grow 2.7 percent this year.

The Finance Ministry endorsed Project Sashakat, a five-pronged strategy to address practical challenges and speed up resolution of non-performing assets (NPAs). The strategy includes setting up independent asset management companies (AMCs) and steering committees, using an asset management company/AIF-led approach for NPA cases over Rs 500 crore. It proposes handling lender alignment through inter-creditor arrangements and lead-bank-led resolution agreed by 66% of lenders in line with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Analysts said the framework aims to attract foreign capital. Steering committees would formulate and validate resolution schemes for stressed accounts over Rs 50 crore within 90 days using a non-discretionary templated approach. The committee recommended an asset trading platform for performing and non-performing assets, did not recommend a “bad bank” for state-owned banks, and proposed a template approach under SME Resolution Approach for loans up to Rs 50 crore, with resolution to be non-discretionary and completed within 90 days.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement to build a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. The facility will allow pilots from Qatar’s air force to train with American military personnel, and will host a contingent of Qatari F-15s and pilots. Hegseth said the project would enhance combined training, lethality, and interoperability. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

An experiment launched after six years of design will study how lower incomes affect baby and toddler brain development. Researchers will test whether giving new mothers an untaxed supplemental monthly income improves children’s emotional and brain development during the first three years, and the results could influence how poverty’s effects on children are understood.

The passage explains the random walk trading strategy, based on the random walk model that assumes stock prices move unpredictably, with future prices independent of past and current movements. It describes the strategy as relying on diversification and random-like entries and exits, under an assumed 50% chance of prices rising or falling, and emphasizes passive investing in broad market index funds. It compares the random walk theory with the efficient market hypothesis (EMH), noting both imply it is difficult to consistently outperform the market, despite differing assumptions. The passage also reports backtests using Amibroker: one on SPY (stocks), with positive metrics, and one on GLD (gold), with negative results. It further discusses related history, including Malkiel’s popularization of the theory and an experiment by the Wall Street Journal in 1988.

Scorpion stings are described as life-threatening emergencies, with limited accurate global statistics. WHO estimated 1.23 million scorpion stings and about 3,250 deaths per year, with many accidents in villages where victims may not seek care. The study reports scorpion biology, venom effects, and clinical features categorized by Abroug’s classification (class I local signs; class II systemic with autonomic symptoms; class III cardiovascular/respiratory/neurologic involvement). It aims to describe clinical manifestations and outcomes of scorpion sting patients admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea and to determine risk factors for fatal outcomes.  

A prospective descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from 1 June 2019 to 31 May 2020. Among 165 admitted patients, sex distribution was almost equal (male 48.5%, female 51.5%), most cases came from urban areas (57%), and most patients were older than 15 years (61.2%). A case fatality rate of 4.8% was reported (8 deaths). The most common symptoms were localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), and vomiting (33.9%). Children under 15 years and patients with no formal education were noted as possible predisposing factors for more severe symptoms. Most stings occurred at night (62.4%) and on the foot (64.8%). The paper concludes that localized pain, sweating, and vomiting were the main clinical features, severity was higher in children, and preventive education targeting at-risk groups is recommended.

The passage discusses rising regulatory complexity and the challenges compliance leaders face in balancing consistent global oversight with adaptable local rules amid frequent new obligations. It cites increased enforcement and penalties in markets including the U.S. and U.K., and argues that compliance failures can lead to reputational damage, investigations, audits, and long-term remediation costs. The passage says StarCompliance provides technology and an enterprise platform for employee and firm compliance, including tools for conflicts management, incident tracking, accountability and training, broker-dealer registration, and MNPI oversight, and positions compliance technology as a strategic advantage through automation, reporting, and real-time monitoring. It also mentions StarCompliance receiving Pan Finance’s “Most Innovative Employee Technology Platform USA” award and offering a free executive brief about the cost of non-compliance.

The passage states that U.S. policy toward the Kingdom of Hawaii consistently opposed foreign aggression affecting American rights and interests, and repeatedly contemplated annexation as a contingent necessity. It cites multiple instances where annexation was discussed or pursued, including Lord Palmerston’s 1850 recommendation of either a U.S. protectorate or annexation, a 1851 prepared deed of cession to be opened after French aggression, advocacy and a draft treaty in 1854, Seward’s 1867 instructions favoring receiving native overtures for annexation, and statements by Johnson (1868), Grant (1871), and Fish (1873) supporting or seeking views on annexation. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, the passage says administrations defended U.S. exclusive commercial rights and supported the existing Hawaiian government. It also includes an 1881 message from Blaine about benevolent neutrality and an “avowedly American solution” if neutrality became impracticable. Finally, it notes that a report and related documents describe U.S. official relations with the Hawaiian Islands, including the 1820 appointment of John C. Jones as an agent for commerce and seamen and supervision of American interests, with occasional information from Navy officers.

The passage explains why official car fuel-economy figures (“mpg”) are often unreliable and describes how Which? measures “real mpg” more realistically. It says official figures come from the NEDC test protocol, criticized for loopholes such as allowing manufacturers to reduce results by 4%, omitting sustained motorway driving, using eco modes, turning off ancillary loads, permitting tyre pressures above recommended levels, and lacking a system to police testing consistency across labs. It also notes a transition from NEDC to the WLTP cycle beginning with tests from September 2017 and full UK adoption by September 2018. Which? tests are described as being run on a rolling road using WLTP cycles (including cold and hot cycles) plus a motorway cycle, with realistic test conditions (default driver settings, air conditioning and dipped lights for additional cycles, and no weight or tyre tampering). The passage also covers hybrid test methods, additional emissions measurements (NOx, CO, HC, PM), risks of manufacturer “cheating,” and use of PEMS on suspected NOx results. It concludes that Which? provides fuel and other performance information for over 700 reviewed vehicles and tests around 120 new cars each year.

Anthurium is a South American plant with bright red, shiny, heart-shaped blossoms also called “tongues of fire,” and its flowers can be red, pink, or white. The plant can act as a natural filter for ammonia and xylene, but its sap and leaves may cause allergies in sensitive people. It needs a lot of light without direct sunlight, dampness, and is best placed indoors near a window at 18°C–21°C. Since it cannot tolerate dry air, leaves should be sprayed in winter, and it should be repotted each year in a pot with a bottom hole, then every other year as it ages.

The passage describes how COVID-19 containment measures, including partial or full business and school closures, affected health and economic activities, and how many U.S. colleges closed or switched to online in spring and reopened in fall with in-person or mixed plans. It notes that college students are in the 18–29 age cohort with a lower COVID-19 death rate but higher chances of socialization, and that colleges used measures such as symptom screening, contact tracing, cleaning and disinfecting, and mandatory masks, while still posing a risk of spreading the virus to faculty, staff, and surrounding regions. The study addresses whether switching to more remote teaching helps control communicable diseases, using a quasi-experimental approach to compare similar colleges choosing in-person versus online (and other modality pairs). The results indicate that college reopening, especially with in-person teaching, increases COVID-19 cases and deaths over time. The passage also reviews related research on school closures and reopening, and discusses limitations such as endogenous selection of teaching modalities and other factors affecting cases and deaths. It outlines that the study measures effects on county-level new cases and deaths rather than the college level and uses multiple data sources and methods to address differences among colleges.

Harry S. Truman marks a solemn and glorious hour, saying Germany has surrendered to the United Nations and that freedom now flies over Europe. He thanks Providence for guiding them through adversity but emphasizes the terrible cost of defeating Hitler and the sacrifices made by Americans and others. Truman calls for continued hard work to finish the war, bind up a suffering world, and build a peace rooted in justice and law, urging Americans to stick to their posts until Japan’s last division surrenders unconditionally. He reads a proclamation stating Allied armies, with God’s help, secured final unconditional surrender from Germany and freed western peoples, and he notes much remains to be done, including victory in the East. Truman appoints Sunday, May 13, 1945, as a day of prayer, calls on the people to thank God and pray for support and guidance into peace, and dedicates the day to the memory of those who died for the victory.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K current report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission dated October 2, 2022, reporting that on October 2, 2022 it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1.
