The passage describes how viral genome sequencing has moved from retrospective studies to near-real-time analyses and how real-time variant characterization can support public health actions, forecasting, and development of vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics. It notes that spatial and temporal heterogeneity in variant populations and unequal sequencing capacity create challenges for early variant characterization and access to real-time prevalence estimates, especially where data are sparse and geographically concentrated. 

To address these limitations, the authors develop a hierarchical mixed-effects Bayesian multinomial modeling approach that pools sequences across countries to estimate global variant growth trajectories and country-specific variant proportions, growth rates, and global fitness advantages. The method is designed to handle sparse data, account for geographic heterogeneity in fitness, and provide more robust estimates shortly after variant emergence. The passage reports findings from SARS-CoV-2, including global sequencing disparities, patterns in variant-targeted sequencing effort, country-to-country differences in BA.4/BA.5 invasion dynamics, and global fitness comparisons among variants. It also includes retrospective validation comparing the multicountry model to single-country multinomial regression, reporting more stable and more accurate predictions during early emergence for the multicountry model, and discusses assumptions and possible sources of bias.

Amber Enterprises received approval from SEBI to raise an estimated Rs 555 crore through an initial share-sale offering. The company filed a draft prospectus on September 29 and received SEBI observations on December 5 to launch the public offer. Amber Enterprises, based in Gurugram, manufactures air-conditioners and also makes refrigerator components, water purifiers, and washing machines. Its IPO includes a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 450 crore and promoter sales of Rs 105 crore by Jasbir Singh and Daljit Singh. Proceeds will be used for loan repayment and advance payments and for other general corporate purposes. Edelweiss Financial Services, IDFC Bank, SBI Capital Markets, and BNP Paribas will manage the IPO.

The passage is an address to Americans describing a week of “violence and tragedy” and appointing a special Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders. The commission, chaired by Governor Otto Kerner with Vice Chairman Mayor John Lindsay, will investigate the origins of recent city disorders and make recommendations for measures to prevent or contain future events, using facts gathered by the FBI. The speaker states that looting, arson, and violence are not part of civil rights protest and must be handled under law, while also arguing that lasting peace requires attacking conditions such as ignorance, discrimination, slums, poverty, disease, and lack of jobs. The address lists recent and proposed legislation aimed at protecting citizens and improving conditions in cities, criticizes reductions to funding proposals, and calls for action rather than angry reaction. It also warns against hatred and fear, urges unity between races, and calls for a national day of prayer on Sunday, July 30. The speaker concludes by urging public officials and citizens to end violence, provide help to those harmed, and work toward better jobs, housing, education, and reconciliation.

The passage introduces Z[ε] as the ring of dual integers Z[T]/(T^2). It states that the paper studies Gorenstein-projective finitely generated right Z[ε]-modules, focusing on their classification and related categories. It defines the category G-proj Z[ε] of Gorenstein-projective modules and notes it is equivalent to several other categories, including torsionless modules, certain perfect differential structures, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, while lacking the Krull–Remak–Schmidt property. It describes the stable category of G-proj Z[ε] modulo projectives and cites results linking it to derived categories, including a main theorem asserting equivalence among multiple categories (stable G-proj Z[ε] modulo projectives, a stable category of submodules, an orbit category Db(Z)/[1], and categories of perfect differential structures). The passage also outlines a chain of categories linked by dense functors, ending with finite abelian groups, and explains that composing certain functors yields a cube of commutative squares.

Scotiabank’s 1832 Asset Management LP will pay an $800,000 fine and $150,000 in investigation costs under a settlement with the Ontario Securities Commission for improper lavish spending on promotional activities for financial advisers. The settlement says the firm provided excessive non-monetary benefits, including tickets to NHL games, concerts and golf events, and gifts such as Apple iPad minis, keyboards and sunglasses, along with expensive food, drinks and entertainment, failing minimum conduct standards from November 2012 to October 2017. The firm began making internal practice changes last year to improve compliance, and a senior vice-president said it will continue working with regulators and that it was fully cooperative with OSC staff.

WIRED’s podcast discusses five top stories from the week, including: federal workers receiving HR templates telling them to blame Democrats for the government shutdown; Peter Thiel’s lectures and discussions related to the Antichrist; Tesla encouraging drowsy drivers to use its “Full Self-Driving” (FSD) mode despite its driver-assist nature and warnings; scientists making human eggs from skin cells to form embryos, with potential implications for infertility treatment and ethical concerns; and OpenAI launching a standalone social app for AI-generated videos using Sora 2. The OpenAI app features a vertical feed, identity verification to create a digital avatar and voice for a user, guardrails against nude or other disallowed content, and ongoing uncertainties about rules such as copyright. The episode concludes with credits and a mention of a future episode about delivery apps and robots.

The passage describes how Vodafone Ghana staff provided effective customer service after Andrew Kufuor, an incoming customer, was helped by Vodafone employees. Eunice Ampomah-Manu, part of the SME Enterprise team, had called Kufuor on a routine check-up when he suffered an attack, became breathless, and said he was dying. She kept him on the line, obtained his wife’s phone number, and called her, leading his wife to take him to a nearby clinic. Eunice later checked on him at the hospital. Kufuor said she saved his life, and Vodafone CEO Yolanda Cuba stated that providing an unmatched customer experience is central to Vodafone’s values.

Nick Kyrgios was drawn to play John Isner in singles in the second rubber of Australia’s Davis Cup quarter-final against the United States in Brisbane on Friday. The match follows Jack Sock’s meeting with Jordan Thompson, and the doubles on Saturday include Sam Groth and John Peers against Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson, before reverse singles on Sunday. Kyrgios has 218 aces this season and is tied for third with Isner on the ATP leaderboard; Isner has a 2-1 record against Kyrgios. Australia’s captain Lleyton Hewitt said Thompson can cope after previously winning singles matches in the first round tie against the Czech Republic, and Kyrgios expects home support after dealing with a hostile crowd when he lost to Federer in Miami last week.

The passage describes how advances in IT enable new manufacturing usage scenarios through simulations, modeling, virtual prototyping, and digital twins, including digital feedback loops using IoT and sensor data. It highlights IT-based design optimization and digital verification and validation, and notes that data analytics and high-performance calculations are needed for large datasets and complex workloads such as AI/ML. The document discusses high-performance computing (HPC) as a competitive factor that increases simulation capability, quality, and innovation, with many enterprises already using or planning HPC. It also outlines challenges of HPC use, including infrastructure costs, security concerns, energy consumption, scalability, availability, and expertise gaps. The passage discusses cloud-based HPC architectures and HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) as alternatives that can improve flexibility, resilience, and cost structure, and concludes with recommendations focused on virtual development, a holistic data strategy (“single source of truth”), appropriate HPC operating models, scalability/security/energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. The methodology section states the findings are based on a telephone survey in December 2021 of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on January 25, 2022. The report states that on January 25, 2022 Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes an exhibit listing Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated January 25, 2022) and a cover page interactive data file, and it contains signature and certification information by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit. In the 1980s, they showed quantum tunneling and energy quantization in an electric circuit involving billions of electrons on a chip, contrary to the expectation that quantum effects were limited to individual atoms. Their work supported the development of qubits and superconducting quantum computers, with later efforts including Martinis’ work toward showing a quantum computer could perform a calculation beyond reach for traditional computers.

The passage is a collection of dated news items and commentary from late October 2001 about Enron’s financial troubles and related market impacts. It includes an interview with Enron’s new CFO, Jeff McMahon, discussing Enron Industrial Markets’ forest products trading growth, obstacles to quality assurance with publishers, and the use of long-term financial hedging tools to reduce price volatility, alongside references to McMahon replacing Andrew Fastow as CFO amid regulatory scrutiny and losses linked to partnerships. Other excerpts report Enron shares dropping sharply after Moody’s downgraded Enron’s credit ratings and placed commercial paper on review; they describe rising bond default insurance premiums, concerns about Enron’s liabilities from affiliates, and Enron seeking new credit lines. Additional sections cover broader market declines tied to weakened consumer confidence, Enron’s role as a major counter-party in natural gas trading and the NYMEX’s move toward clearing to address credit concerns, and a separate Germany cartel office action against utilities over how they charge for balancing power.

The passage covers design choices and component/layout guidance for a push-pull converter using TPS7H500x-SP controllers. It specifies conservative selection of an 80-V GaN FET for the synchronous rectifier, matching current ratings to maximum secondary current, and using a parallel Schottky diode to reduce current during soft-start and mitigate reverse conduction losses. It describes using an RCD clamp to limit switch-node voltage and an output inductor design targeting 40% ripple (selected value 0.47 µH). For output capacitance, it explains calculations for voltage deviation and ripple, includes derating considerations, and notes additional capacitance may be needed for SET mitigation; the example uses about 2.3 mF total output capacitance and optionally an additional output LC/ceramic filter to reduce noise. It outlines overcurrent cycle-by-cycle limiting starting around 35 A, selecting a 7.5-Ω sense resistor, choosing a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, using Type 2A frequency compensation with RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF, and setting a slope compensation resistor of 102 kΩ between RSC and AVSS. It then provides application recommendations for input power supply bypassing and detailed PCB layout guidelines to reduce noise and EMI, including ground separation and placement rules.

The passage describes the MSPM0G-series microcontroller subsystems and peripherals, including the PMU (core supply generation and VDD supervision with features such as brown-out reset monitoring, core regulators for multiple operating modes, and parity-protected trim), the clock module (multiple internal/external oscillators and clocks distributed to processor and peripherals), the DMA (memory-to-memory transfers without CPU intervention and various channel and trigger features), and the event manager (routing event publishers to subscribers, including static events to IRQ, DMA events, and generic events). It also covers peripheral-related sections such as device memory organization and interrupt vector tables, flash and SRAM characteristics, and summaries of additional peripherals (GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, DAC, security features, TRNG, AES-related modules, CRC, math accelerator, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS/RTC_B/IWDT/WWDT, timers, analog connection guidance, I/O diagrams, SWD debug, boot strap loader/BSL requirements, and factory constants). The text further includes brief application/layout guidance and references to documentation and support resources.

Twenty years ago, the Open Source Definition (OSD) was published, building on Richard Stallman’s advocacy for “free software.” The Open Source Initiative dates the start of open source to February 3, 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed the term “open source” after Netscape released its source code; the term was intended as an alternative because “free software” requires explaining that “free” refers to liberty rather than price. Peterson said other suggestions included “source code available” and “freely distributable,” and the term “open source” won on February 5, 1998; Bruce Perens instead dates it to February 9, 1998. Perens said open source is essentially the same as free software, promoted in language more acceptable to business. The passage says open source became widely adopted and that companies including Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Microsoft rely on open source software, with Microsoft noted for later embracing it after prior criticism. Tim Burke of Red Hat said open source has become the center of innovation, moving beyond cloning alternatives like OpenOffice.

J. Bernstorff writes that the blockade will be terminated if a conference can be arranged on reasonable terms. In a separate message from the Ambassador in Germany (Gerard) to the Secretary of State, Zimmermann delivers a reckless submarine note and memorandum, urging the President to stay quiet for two months while submarine war compels England to ask for terms. Gerard also reports Zimmermann’s view that Lloyd George is the real head of the Entente and that failure to make peace would lead to exhausted Europe and confrontation with Japan and other “yellow races.” Another telegram reports that the Greek Government announces concessions to the Entente to introduce indispensable victuals pending the raising of the blockade, while Entente allege unaccounted rifles. An ambassador in Austria-Hungary (Penfield) conveys thanks and urges the United States to consider Austria-Hungary’s defensive position, stating Austria-Hungary will negotiate honorable peace “without victory” and that peace is impossible while the Entente aims at dismembering Austria-Hungary; it also says a technical modification of submarine war is impossible and argues Wilson should use his influence to bring the Entente to accept the “peace without victory” basis.

The passage discusses energy storage—especially batteries—as a way to add more renewable energy to electricity grids and reduce reliance on fossil fuels. It explains that storage takes power from the grid or local generation and returns it later, but that it involves capital and running costs, including electricity costs for charging and round-trip efficiency losses. It compares multiple storage technologies, noting lithium-ion batteries as lightweight, efficient, and suited to small-scale use but currently expensive per unit, while pumped hydro supports large-scale storage with good efficiency and low cost per unit; other options listed include flywheels, compressed air, cryogenic storage, flow batteries, and hydrogen. The passage then compares lithium-ion batteries with pumped hydro, stating lithium-ion costs are declining along a similar curve to solar PV, from about US$1,200 to US$600 per kWh over five years (excluding installation). It provides break-even cost examples under variable retail rates and argues that if variable rates shrink to reflect smaller wholesale price differences, battery cost needs would drop further; it also notes that storage network benefits depend on whether electricity demand is growing. It concludes that pumped hydro is relatively inexpensive and already exists at about 1,500 MW in the market, but that distributed lithium-ion storage may become more widespread due to factors including human behavior.

The passage describes an Irish Times “Portrait Gallery” photograph featuring Ernest Walton, joint Nobel Prize winner for physics in 1951, shown doing technological work with a biro in a lab at Trinity College Dublin. Walton is described as a quiet, shy man in his early 50s who said he was too fond of Ireland to leave. The article briefly notes his 1930s achievement of smashing the nucleus of the atom at the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge. The accompanying picture is described as downbeat and slightly sinister, with Walton’s expression guarded. The passage also mentions where to buy Irish Times images and a book titled *The Times We Lived In* (more than 100 photographs and commentary by Arminta Wallace).

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 3, 2020, reporting an amendment to its Restated Articles of Incorporation submitted to the California Secretary of State. The amendment increased authorized common stock shares from 12,600,000,000 to 50,400,000,000 and provided for an automatic four-for-one split of each outstanding share of common stock as of 5 p.m. Pacific daylight time on August 28, 2020. The filing includes common stock and multiple note classes registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC and lists Exhibit 3.1 (Restated Articles of Incorporation filed August 3, 2020).

Bitcoin futures were set to begin trading at 6pm EST on Cboe Futures Exchange. The launch adds a regulated way to bet on or hedge bitcoin price moves, with futures being cash-settled based on the Gemini Exchange’s bitcoin auction price. Bitcoin’s price has nearly doubled since early December, with sharp swings recently, and analysts said futures could help dampen volatility over the long run, though effects may not be immediate. Reception from major US banks and brokerages has been mixed: Interactive Brokers planned to offer access but restricted short positions and set at least 50% margin, while Charles Schwab and TD Ameritrade would not allow trading from day one. Some banks were also reported not to clear trades for clients immediately. Concerns remain about investor and clearing risks, including fears of inaccurate pricing, systemic risk, insufficient safeguards, and potential manipulation of the underlying spot market.

The passage describes the Korean diet (K-diet) as being based on traditional Korean eating habits and focuses on whole, unprocessed foods. It includes fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, seasonal/local fruits and vegetables, and fermented foods such as kimchi and doenjang/gochujang, alongside side dishes and smaller portions than in the West. Foods mentioned as commonly eaten include various rice/grains, vegetables (e.g., leafy greens, cabbage, cucumber), seaweed and mushrooms, fermented soybean products, and seasonings like soy sauce and sesame oil. The diet limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Reported benefits include a high-fibre, low-calorie approach that may support wellbeing and contribute to weight loss when combined with regular physical activity; health benefits are attributed to plant-based foods, fermented foods for gut health, and antioxidants. Possible drawbacks noted are high sodium from fermented foods/condiments (which may be unsuitable for people with high blood pressure), low calcium due to lack of dairy, potential irritation from spicy ingredients for some people with digestive issues, and high carbohydrate content requiring portion control for those monitoring blood sugar. The passage also briefly references peer review and additional health topics.

The passage describes “General ‘Rules of the Road’” from CoachingAmericanSoccer.com for new soccer players and new coaches, offering guidance on general team tactics such as positioning, ball work, and team functions. It states the rules list aligns with teaching positions and can be adapted to a coach’s personal preferences and style.

The chapter explains how to transfer music, photos, and videos from a computer to a Sansa player. Music can be transferred by drag-and-drop to the player’s MUSIC folder or using Windows Media Player; Audible files require Audible Manager. It also describes creating and syncing playlists with Windows Media Player, converting photos and videos with Sansa Media Converter (including options like cropping, rotating, resizing, and microSD card transfer), and provides player instructions for playing supported audio, viewing photos and slideshows with options, and using FM radio presets. Additional sections cover voice recording with the built-in microphone, deleting content (from the device or via a computer), and customizing system settings such as wallpaper, display art, backlight, power saver, language, date/time, brightness, reset, and USB mode. The later chapters include tips/troubleshooting, how to contact technical support, warranty/service information, and an end user license agreement.

The passage expresses support for Mr. Horton, hoping he makes a full recovery, and notes it’s difficult for him and Aaron to miss the rest of the playoffs. It says the team must move on, focusing on its next game. It references a tough first-round loss in Chicago where the team was blown out but came out strong the next game, and describes a strong first period followed by opponents scoring from lucky bounces and easy goals. It concludes that the series have been hard fought and things happen.

The ADS9803 has a speed-boost mode that increases sampling to up to 8 MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair. In this mode, only the selected pair is converted on every sampling clock while the other six analog input channels are idle. The sampling rate equals the sampling clock frequency, and the data output interface remains the same as in normal mode. Register operations for enabling or disabling speed-boost mode are described, including SPI register bank selection and the read/write enable steps. The passage also explains SPI configuration for multiple ADCs in a daisy-chain topology, including how to connect CS/SCLK and SDI/SDO through the chain, set daisy-chain length, and perform register read/write sequences using repeated 24-SCLK frames. Additional register field descriptions include those related to speed-boost mode, register bank selection, and configuration options.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K current report dated October 28, 2021. The report states that on October 28, 2021, Apple issued a press release with its financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 25, 2021, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report includes details about Apple’s registered securities and lists its CFO, Luca Maestri, as the authorized signer.

Shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) is a problem in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) that can lead to prolonged hospital and intensive care stays and is linked to poor outcomes. Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt is the usual treatment for aSAH patients needing cerebrospinal fluid diversion, and complications of VP shunts make reducing SDHC risk a clinical concern. The study retrospectively reviewed 118 consecutive patients treated for ruptured aneurysms after aSAH between January 2013 and October 2021; 109 were included after exclusions. All patients had external ventricular drainage (EVD) and underwent an EVD challenge; patients with failed challenge or hydrocephalus after successful EVD removal received VP shunt surgery. Variables analyzed included age, gender, BMI, treatment modality, new neurological deficits, rebleeding or delayed cerebral ischemia, admission eGFR, NLR/PLR/PNR, aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and Hunt and Hess scale (HHS). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified three SDHC predictors: age ≥65 years, clipping (vs coiling), and HHS ≥3. A nomogram was developed using these predictors, with an AUC of 0.753 and non-significant Hosmer–Lemeshow test result (p = 0.963). The study concludes that SDHC risk factors are age >65 years, HHS ≥3, and clipping rather than coiling, and that a nomogram was created to assess the relative risk combinations.

Nike reported quarterly results that beat Wall Street expectations, with fiscal first-quarter revenue rising 1% from the prior year after the company had expected sales to fall mid-single digits. Profits fell 31% and gross margin dropped to 42.2%, reflecting ongoing inventory-clearing efforts. CEO Elliott Hill said the company is making strides in wholesale, running, and North America, while noting other parts of the business are still struggling. Direct sales declined 4% and revenue in China fell 9%. Finance chief Matt Friend warned progress will not be linear, and Hill described efforts including clearing stale inventory and reorganizing teams by sport.

The passage argues that postwar economic exclusion would seriously affect Austria-Hungary and Germany and cannot be solved by trade in transit to Turkey because they must still address demobilized soldiers’ employment, replenishing supplies, and financial burdens. It then lists “assets” for Germany’s position: potential satisfaction of Bulgaria’s claims and the likely political effects in Bulgaria; military successes and postwar financial weakness in Turkey; bargaining material in German colonies and Germany’s exclusion from parts of the Pacific and the Americas; dangers to German domination from the Russian revolution due to anti-capitalist, religious, and nationalist motives; the Vatican’s potential value if handled skilfully; American resources making victory over the Central Powers likely; “intangibles” such as longing for peace, belief that old diplomacy is bankrupt, hope for a league of nations, and fear of social revolution; and finally, claims about a changed direction in German policy eastward in view of the Russian situation.

Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated knee during the Dolphins’ win over the Jets, exiting on a cart in the third quarter after twisting his left leg while being tackled out of bounds. He was placed in an air cast and remained hospitalized overnight for further tests. Despite the injury, the Dolphins won, and Hill said to make sure the team got the win.

An international team studied live specimens of the giant black mud-dwelling shipworm Kuphus polythalamia, which feeds on sulfur and lives in a shell resembling a baseball bat. Although giant shipworms were known for centuries, live specimens had been hard to obtain; the researchers found them in a lagoon on an abandoned log farm in the Philippines and published their findings in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The researchers aim to study microbes in the shipworm’s single gill to look for new antimicrobial substances. Kuphus polythalamia burrows into mud, consumes hydrogen sulfide, and its microbes convert swamp gas into carbon. The passage also notes uncertainty about its life cycle, age, and whether it has a wood-eating ancestor.

The passage describes a seasonal trading strategy for the German stock market. The DAX 40 is Germany’s main index, made up of 40 blue-chip German companies traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, and the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG) is presented as an easier way for U.S. investors to access German large and mid-size companies. The passage states that EWG’s best time to be invested is the year’s final quarter, while the rest of the year is more sideways. Based on this, it outlines a simple strategy that holds only during the last three months (fourth quarter), and it notes that a backtest of the strategy using EWG since inception (with data adjusted for dividends and splits) shows performance that paid off well over recent decades.

Christian Nwosu, a former INEC administrative secretary in Kwara state, told a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into admitting he benefited N30m from former Petroleum Minister Dieziani Alison-Madueke. He said EFCC operative Usman Zakari threatened to keep him in detention unless he wrote what Zakari wanted, escorted him to a bank to make drafts totaling N4m and then requested an additional N1m. Nwosu also testified that EFCC prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo ordered Zakari to detain him and allegedly threatened him with conviction and jail if he did not cooperate, including writing out property worth N30m.

The passage describes how climate change in the northern Rocky Mountains is arriving earlier and is warmer and drier than usual, disrupting cutthroat trout that rely on cold, small streams. It also says rainbow trout are invading cutthroat streams and mating with them, creating hybrids that are less fit and reduce the survival of native fish. Biologists report that hybridization is widespread across hundreds of studied locations, especially where rainbow trout have been introduced by fish and game departments since the 19th century. Some states are trying to remove rainbow trout, and Muhlfeld warns that if native cutthroat genes and traits are lost, extinction is permanent.

A large nationwide study linked long-term outdoor exposure to the industrial solvent trichloroethylene (TCE) with a higher risk of Parkinson’s disease in older adults. Researchers estimated TCE exposure for over 1.1 million people using ZIP+4 codes and air pollution data, and found those in areas with the highest outdoor TCE levels had a 10% greater risk than those in areas with the lowest levels. The study does not prove TCE causes Parkinson’s, and it had limitations including that it focused on Medicare-aged individuals and used outdoor exposure estimates based on 2002 air levels.

State Street Corporation, which commissioned the “Fearless Girl” statue, agreed to pay $5 million to settle claims that it discriminated against 305 top female employees by paying them less than men in the same positions. The U.S. Department of Labor also alleges discrimination against 15 black vice presidents by paying them less than white employees; State Street denies the allegations but agreed to about $4.5 million in back pay and about $500,000 in interest. The company said it is committed to equal pay practices.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit and for bringing quantum effects to a scale once thought impossible.

Big yellow signs at Little Beach in Port Stanley warned of a swimming advisory, but people still went into the water. The advisory was issued on Friday due to high bacteria levels and remained in effect as of Monday. The Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit issues advisories when bacteria reaches a threshold, warning of health risks such as gastrointestinal illness and infection. Cathie Walker said a swimming advisory alerts people to potential health effects from swimming, while the beach would not be closed because the closure threshold had not been reached. Walker said nothing prevents people from swimming except their own choice. The advisory was the first for this summer, and Terrie Vergiris said she did not notice the signs, but believes Little Beach is safer and has visited it previously without issues. Swimming advisories are posted on the health unit website.

Talented musicians and singers from Sir John Deane’s sixth form college entertained a packed audience during the fourth annual “Evening of Jazz and Soul” at the Macdonald Portal Hotel, Golf and Spa in Tarporley. The 35-strong jazz collective, directed by Timothy Murphy, performed 60s soul, classic swing, and included commentary from Alison Richards about the performers’ quick progress and the event’s turnout. Listed vocalists and instrumentalists performed, and the next event will feature 14 students performing classical music at Arley Hall on Thursday, February 9, with tickets costing £8 (£6 concessions).

In 2016, an editor’s note introduced excerpts from top Evening Sun stories. One describes Norwich children Evan and Brynn Meek, who after hearing about homeless people in New York City, traveled to Manhattan and handed out 220 bagged lunches. Another story says Thomas Miller, an eight-year Norwich Police Department veteran, accepted a position with the Syracuse Police Department and was to be sworn in on Aug. 10. A separate excerpt reports that Tracy A. Price, 31, of Norwich, was arrested Aug. 16 on an active arrest warrant for torturing/injuring animals and was charged with torturing, injuring, and neglecting a dog, with $750 bail granted.

A 36-year-old man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao of New York, was arrested in Indio, California, on suspicion of stealing more than 100 cellphones during the Coachella Art and Music Festival. Authorities said concertgoers used “Find my iPhone” to locate missing phones, and some were able to find and follow Henao until security detained him. Officials said he had more than 100 cellphones in his backpack; several were returned to owners and the rest were turned into lost and found. Henao faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges. Indio Police advised concertgoers to keep wallets or phones in a front pocket, secure items with an elastic band, consider using a “dummy wallet,” and spread valuables instead of keeping them together.

Scientists at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden used machine learning and advanced computer simulations to unravel the low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a high-performing halide perovskite solar material. Their study addresses challenges related to understanding and controlling halide perovskites, which are promising for cost-effective, flexible solar cells but can degrade quickly. The researchers identified the structure at low temperatures and observed that formamidinium molecules become stuck in a semi-stable state as the material cools. They validated their models with experiments at the University of Birmingham, cooling the material to −200°C to match the simulations. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on 14 August 2025, and the work used machine-learned simulation methods capable of running much longer simulations with larger atomic models than before.

A Syrian grandmother, Wafa Yahia, arrived in Honolulu Saturday evening after receiving US approval for an immigrant visa several weeks earlier, and she is reunited with her family. Ismail Elshikh, her son-in-law and a plaintiff in Hawaii’s lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump’s travel ban, said the lawsuit is ongoing and argues the ban prevented her from visiting. A federal appeals court in Seattle is set to hear arguments later this month on the government’s appeal of a July ruling that allows grandmothers and other family members of certain people in the US to enter, while the US Supreme Court allowed a scaled-back version of the ban to proceed before it hears the case in October. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin said Yahia’s visa approval would not affect the lawsuit and that Hawaii and its residents are harmed as long as the executive order is not struck down.

Cuba held a military parade in Havana to mark the 58th anniversary of the 1959 revolution led by Fidel Castro, who died on Nov 25 at age 90. Soldiers, militia members, students and workers marched at Revolution Square, with no equipment this year. Castro had requested no cult of personality, and Cuba’s National Assembly passed a law banning monuments in his honor and infrastructure named for him. The passage also notes Cuba’s economic difficulties in 2017, plans for Raul Castro to step aside after his term ends, and concerns that US President-elect Donald Trump may halt rapprochement unless Cuba allows more democratic freedoms and economic reforms.

The passage says that, according to a study in the *Journal of Experimental Psychology*, general distraction is the best way to recover from a breakup. It quotes co-author Sandra Langeslag, stating distraction is a form of avoidance that can reduce recovery from a breakup, so it should be used sparingly to boost mood in the short term. Examples of distractions include new hobbies, going back to school, or working out. The passage also mentions an alternative approach: focusing on negative aspects of the past relationship to move on faster.

During pregnancy, the author says it is difficult to get comfortable due to physical changes and guidance about safe sleep positions. After the fifth month, they note people are not supposed to lie flat on their back because it can reduce circulation and cause low blood pressure, stomach sleeping becomes impossible, and sleeping on the left side is recommended to avoid reduced blood flow to the placenta. The author panicked about how they would sleep once they could no longer lie on their stomach and researched online advice, including buying a pregnancy pillow. They found a Facebook post recommending the Leachco pregnancy pillow (U-shaped rather than J-shaped), bought one, and reported major improvements in comfort, ease of flipping onto their side without readjusting, and even help with congestion when using it with other pillows. They also mention drawbacks: the pillow is very large (can be tight in smaller beds), the provided cover is slightly scratchy (replacement covers are softer), and it can make blankets messy. The author concludes that the pillow is valuable for pregnant people and others who like comfort, snuggling, and relaxing.

The passage describes the emergence and rapid global spread of COVID-19 and its disruption of education worldwide, leading to widespread virtual education. In Turkey, in-person education was suspended to reduce transmission rates and courses were delivered virtually, including via EBA TV in collaboration with TRT and the Ministry of National Education. The text discusses potential advantages and disadvantages of virtual education, especially for students with disabilities, including difficulties with adaptation, motivation, socialization, and meeting individual needs. It summarizes prior literature on inclusive education during the pandemic and notes limited research conducted after returning to in-person education.  

The study used a phenomenology qualitative design to examine problems and solution suggestions from 10 general education primary school teachers in two provinces in Turkey’s Marmara region, selected through purposeful sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews in 2021 and analyzed using content analysis with reliability checks. Results are organized into themes about how teachers conducted virtual instruction, student participation, challenges in involving and tracking students’ education (including homework and activities), teacher-parent cooperation, and solution suggestions. Teachers reported varied levels of student participation, with some students facing barriers such as technology access issues, family literacy limitations, and limited social interaction, while others experienced fewer problems due to strong parental support and use of EBA tools. The teachers proposed solutions including closer family-teacher coordination, device/internet support, hybrid approaches for absences, and ensuring continuity of schooling (including keeping schools open) and coordination with rehabilitation centers. The passage concludes with recommendations for practitioners and future research and includes ethics and consent approval details.

The passage defines “youth” using the Nigerian National Youth Policy (ages 15–29) and the UN statistical definition (ages 15–24), which the paper adopts for cross-country comparisons. It notes that experiential learning/work-integrated learning has no universal definition, and it summarizes May’s definition and lists types it includes, such as co-op internships, apprenticeships, entrepreneurship, and work experiences; co-op is described as fully integrated into the curriculum. The paper presents youth unemployment and employment trends in Nigeria (1991–2021), noting that youth unemployment has risen and is often higher than total unemployment, while the youth employment-to-population ratio is lower than the total ratio. It also highlights labor-market features discussed in the literature, including informality and NEET status, with gender and educational disparities. The passage then outlines the history and key dimensions of cooperative education, major co-op models, stakeholders’ perceived benefits, and associated costs. It summarizes literature on co-op’s benefits and practical program features from examples in Canada and Namibia, including eligibility, study/work sequencing, funding, compensation, quality frameworks, and professional associations. Finally, it reviews Nigerian government responses to youth unemployment (SIWES, SURE-P, and N-SIP) and argues for adopting a federated co-op initiative aligned with existing programs, recommending the alternating co-op model, and concluding that co-op should be part of broader, multipronged policy efforts and further research is needed.

The passage describes the TLV321/2x comparator family, including low power consumption (40 µA per channel) and fast propagation delay (40 ns), and two output options: TLV321x push-pull (sink-source) and TLV322x open-drain (sink only) with pull-up capability up to 5.5 V independent of comparator supply voltage. It details input voltage limits around V− and V+ (200 mV below to 200 mV above), guidance to limit input current to 10 mA or less with series resistance, and instructions for unused inputs and internal hysteresis (1.8 mV). It also covers output behavior requirements (high-speed PCB layout, unused outputs floating), open-drain pull-up resistor recommendations (100 µA to 1 mA), ESD protection and input clamp limits, and power-on reset operation (output held low for up to 32 µs after VPOR crosses 1.65 V). Additional sections discuss comparator output logic based on VIN vs VREF, the role of propagation delay and overdrive, and the use of external hysteresis networks to prevent chatter, followed by notes on a low-side current sensing application and design requirements.

Omicron (SARS-CoV-2 PANGO lineage B.1.1.529, later including BA.1 and BA.2) was first detected in Botswana and South Africa in late November 2021 and designated a Variant of Concern by WHO on 26 November 2021. After a surge in cases in South Africa, studies attributed Omicron’s spread to factors including shorter serial interval, immune evasion, and higher transmissibility than Delta, with hypothesised increased replication in the upper respiratory tract. Despite travel restrictions on international flights from multiple southern African countries, BA.1 was locally transmitted soon after in major travel hubs worldwide, including New York City and London, and in England after the first confirmed case on 27 November 2021. Prevalence rose rapidly across English regions, peaking first in Greater London (~6%) in mid-December and later in other regions, then declining by early January 2022 with a north-to-south gradient.

Using phylodynamic analysis of 115,622 Omicron genomes sampled globally and containing 48,615 England genomes (~1% of confirmed Omicron BA.1 cases in England during the study period), the study inferred at least 6,455 introduction events, most of which were singletons. It found that a small fraction of early introductions (before and during early travel restrictions) accounted for most Omicron BA.1 infections in England through the end of January 2022, while importation intensity continued to increase and shifted away from South Africa toward the US. Phylogeographic reconstruction and a discrete phylogeographic GLM indicated that human mobility patterns—especially a central role for Greater London and directional long-distance movements early in December—shaped the spatial dissemination of BA.1. The analysis also examined how changing human mobility related to local case incidence and found evidence that increases in cases at major “hub” areas corresponded to reduced mobility connectivity, with reductions varying by distance. The authors conclude that targeted travel restrictions implemented after local transmission and applied narrowly were largely ineffective, and they discuss limitations related to sampling bias and possible aggregation of lineages.

The passage discusses election law and constitutional interpretation, focusing on Justice Barrett’s book arguing for originalism. It describes originalism’s premise that the Constitution’s enacted text is binding law and should be interpreted by the meaning the lawmakers used. The author argues there are other plausible interpretations, including “original public meaning” versus “contemporary public meaning,” but then addresses implications for a Supreme Court case involving Louisiana’s creation of a second majority-Black congressional district to avoid a Voting Rights Act violation. The Court ordered reargument after not deciding last term, asking whether intentional creation of a second majority-minority district violates the Fourteenth or Fifteenth Amendments. The author contends that the Equal Protection Clause’s original meaning does not constrain election practices in the way applied in prior cases, and that the Fifteenth Amendment’s text likewise does not support claims about racial districting when it does not deny or abridge an individual’s right to vote. The passage also discusses stare decisis, arguing that even if originalism is accepted, precedents must still be followed unless reconsideration is warranted. It claims that applying the “racial predominance” doctrine is unworkable due to tension with Voting Rights Act Section 2 enforcement, and argues an originalist approach would require reconsidering and jettisoning the doctrine to preserve Congress’s power to make vote dilution claims actionable as amended in 1982, and that only Congress could outlaw certain racially motivated districting.

The passage explains that the Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index (also called Advisor Sentiment) is a contrarian indicator based on a weekly survey of investment advisors and newsletters. The passage argues that the “out-of-school children” (OOSC) indicator is too limited to capture educational exclusion, because it focuses on formal school enrollment and overlooks informal and non-formal learning pathways and broader contextual drivers. Using Afghanistan as an example—including the Taliban’s ban on girls’ secondary education, challenges in collecting accurate school-age population data, and issues like chronic absenteeism and “ghost” schools/students—the passage describes how OOSC can underestimate exclusion and fail to account for alternative education options such as madrasas, community-based education, and technology-based learning. It proposes replacing OOSC with a more inclusive “out-of-education children” (OOEC) indicator that defines education as an activity and can capture formal, informal, and non-formal pathways. The passage also lists barriers affecting children’s access to education in Afghanistan, including geographic disparities, nomadic lifestyles, child labor, and disabilities, and argues that shifting to OOEC would require changes in data systems, credentialing, collaboration among education actors, and more equitable resource allocation.

SFS (Seamless Firmware Servicing) is an AMD firmware feature for developing and distributing fixes for selected high-priority system issues. Datacenter operators can apply SFS patches without rebooting, and AMD packages updates into “Seamless Firmware Servicing Update Package(s)” after identifying included fixes. Deploying an SFS package can change three version levels: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), which monotonically increases and uniquely identifies the running AMD firmware via firmware version plus SFSPL; component firmware Security Patch Levels (SPL) that advance but may be reverted by later patches; and System Patch Level (SYSPL), a monotonically increasing virtual component version tracking run-once code changes executed since the last reboot. SFS uses these levels to ensure updates apply to the correct SOC firmware state, and the host OS can query firmware version levels via an SFS command. For security, SFS packages are cryptographically signed by AMD, with an optional customer co-signing header that enables customer approval of deployed packages by providing a public key to the ASP during early boot. The ASP verifies signatures before applying updates. SFS commands are required at runtime and do not persist over reset; in multi-socket systems the first socket’s ASP receives the patch, and multiple updates must be applied sequentially. Customers can enable SFS and optionally require co-signing through BIOS options that are off by default, and the document describes specific command flows, versioning checks, patchable items, and resiliency/security considerations.

Archaeologists in Mexico, led by underwater archaeologist Guillermo de Anda and the Great Mayan Aquifer Project, plan to excavate a secret tunnel beneath Chichen Itza’s “El Castillo” pyramid to reach a hidden cenote, an underwater cavern central to Mayan spirituality and the Yucatan’s fresh water supply. The Maya sealed the tunnel centuries ago; divers previously explored passages from the “Ossuary” pyramid but found them intentionally blocked by stone. De Anda says the excavation is expected to take about three months and that cenotes were part of a three-layer cosmos (heavens, earth, underworld), with careful balance seen as preventing drought, famine, or sickness. The Maya practiced offerings and human sacrifice in cenotes, including victims found in Chichen Itza’s Sacred Cenote—about 80% were children aged 3 to 11, whose remains showed poor health.

The passage says that lab tests indicate jostling microbubbles of air and methane can create tiny lightning zaps. Will-o’-the-wisps—glowing bluish lights seen above swamps and cemeteries worldwide—are believed to result from burning seeping methane gas, but what ignites the gas has been unclear.

The European Union’s Global Gateway plan aims to expand electricity access in Africa and help move the continent away from fossil fuels. Nearly 600 million Africans lack electricity. In late September, Ursula von der Leyen announced a €545 million ($636 million) investment package for renewable energy and electrification, including a high-voltage transmission line in Côte d’Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydro projects in Lesotho, and mini-grids in Madagascar. The EU estimates the program could create 38 million green jobs by 2030. Global Gateway, launched in 2021, is described as an EU effort to provide an alternative to China’s Belt and Road Initiative, which has invested heavily in infrastructure worldwide, including in clean energy in Africa. The passage also notes that China exported increasing amounts of solar panels to Africa in 2025 and that other Western initiatives in Africa have been aimed at responding to China’s investments.

The passage describes how the COVID-19 pandemic led to distance education as a way to continue schooling, including in Greece’s primary and pre-school education. It notes that teachers were asked to use digital skills, but access issues, inadequate digital infrastructure, and limited teacher training create obstacles to equal access and implementation. The study examines kindergarten teachers’ views on integrating distance education in Epirus, Greece, during the 2020–2021 school year. Using an anonymous web-based quantitative survey of 82 kindergarten teachers (May 5 to June 4, 2021), the findings show that most teachers report low readiness and familiarity with distance education before the pandemic, limited experience with remote training, and reliance on tools such as Webex, e-mail, and online classroom platforms. Teachers’ opinions are mostly negative about distance education for preschool children, citing reduced psychomotor activities, weaker development of social skills, the need for an adult supervisor, limited internet/access to technological means, and difficulties for children in using tools independently. Statistical analysis found a significant difference in familiarity with distance education before the pandemic based on ICT certificate level, while no significant relationship was found between teachers’ years of service and ICT familiarity.

The passage explains that a “take a knee chart” is a football coaching tool for deciding when the offense can take a knee at the end of a game to run time off the clock while preserving a lead. It describes using a “victory formation,” where the quarterback takes the snap and kneels down as a run play that keeps the clock running and resets the play clock; if the opponent has no timeouts, they cannot stop the clock. The chart typically shows offensive player positions and movement order. It also discusses the importance of clock management, noting that teams must manage the play clock and be careful with pass plays because completions keep the clock moving while incomplete passes stop it, potentially leaving extra time for the opponent in close games.

S&P Global Ratings downgraded Bridgeview, Illinois, four notches to BB-minus, placing its credit rating in junk status and on a watch list for a possible further downgrade. Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem said the church will appeal an Israeli court decision approving the sale of church property to companies representing Israeli settlers in East Jerusalem. Machine learning and AutoML workflows are increasingly automated, and large language models (LLMs) can generate ML code, motivating benchmarks such as MLE-bench, DA-Code, and Weco-Kaggle. These benchmarks are limited to English problem statements, despite claims that LLM performance drops in low-resource and non-English languages, especially for ML code generation requiring cross-lingual alignment.

The passage introduces ML²B (Multilingual Machine Learning Benchmark), the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs generating complete ML pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. ML²B expands 30 Kaggle competitions into 13 languages (390 evaluation instances) while preserving real workflow complexity. It includes 24 public and 6 private competitions, structured and human-reviewed task descriptions with standardized metadata to control leakage, and evaluation of five LLMs across two execution frameworks. The benchmark extends Kaggle tasks into 13 languages while keeping data realism, uses restricted submission formats to reduce preprocessing leakage, and evaluates results via percentile rank to handle heterogeneous metrics.

Experiments report systematic failure patterns (e.g., missing code blocks, runtime data loading, preprocessing inconsistency, function signature changes, and global dependencies) and show cross-lingual performance variability by language, domain, and model. English is described as a consistent anchor language, while low-resource languages show higher failure rates, and tabular classification/regression is less stable than image categorization and text classification. Static leakage analysis on modular submissions finds potential leakage in 61 of 554 submissions (11%), with further analysis indicating remaining potential leakage in 33 submissions (5.9%). The conclusion states ML²B surfaces weaknesses in multilingual ML code generation and highlights ongoing needs for secure interfaces and code auditing.
