It also states that growth includes sustainable development, aligned with quality manufacturing, people growth, and environmental safety. GOLDWOOD PLY is presented as a top plywood manufacturer in Yamunanagar, Haryana, offering products such as Block Board, Flush Door, and Plywood, with contact details and an address provided.

The passage argues that the effectiveness of law depends less on highly publicized acts than on less publicly understood ones, where interested parties actively seek to defeat enforcement. It states that the government has shifted toward using criminal law in certain trust and interstate commerce cases, moving from civil proceedings and, despite some failures, achieving many successes with deterrent effects through fines and imprisonment. It cites Judge Holt’s view that an offense involving large, deliberate rebate discrimination was especially serious, premeditated, and difficult to prove, and that penalties should be commensurate with its gravity, with the corporation receiving the principal penalty.

The document is an email chain and legal complaint. Mark Palmer forwards an instruction and says a suit filed against electricity generators “will look the same.” The complaint, filed in the Superior Court of California for the County of San Diego by Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of herself and a proposed class, alleges that during spring and summer 2000 electricity generators and traders unlawfully manipulated the California wholesale electricity market, including by using confidential real-time generator and transmission data and by withholding, parking, and scheduling actions that increased prices. It claims this manipulation led to unjust and unreasonable wholesale prices maintained for the period, overcharges exceeding $4 billion, and damages to electricity purchasers, including retail customers of SDG&E. The complaint asserts claims under California antitrust laws (Cartwright Act), unfair competition/consumer-related statutes, and other theories, and seeks class certification, damages (including treble damages where applicable), disgorgement, injunctive relief, and interest.

The passage describes the 9 EMA (9-period exponential moving average) trading strategy, a technical analysis approach used to identify short-term market trends. It generates buy signals when price moves above the 9 EMA and sell signals when price moves below it, and it can be applied to assets such as stocks, forex, and commodities. The passage also discusses backtesting results, noting that the strategy appears to work better in trending assets like Bitcoin than in mean-reversion markets like stocks, and that adding a 200-day moving average trend filter improves results but may still not make the strategy tradable for S&P 500/SPY. It outlines possible uses with risk management (e.g., stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification) and combining the 9 EMA with other indicators (e.g., RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD) or other strategies as confirmation filters. It concludes that the 9 EMA is mainly suited to assets that trend or show short-term momentum, and that it has popular variations and potential components and implementation steps.

The passage says the Konektadong Pinoy Bill became law on August 24, 2025, aiming to remove barriers to competition in the Philippine telco market. It could change the current business structure by enabling Virtual Network Operators to compete with PLDT. The passage argues that increased competition may coincide with declining PLDT profitability and slowing growth, potentially worsening the situation. It also claims that the law could lead to excess capital investment in a mature, highly penetrated industry, depressing participants’ profitability, and concludes that despite PHI’s valuation, the threat of entrants is a reason to stay on the sidelines.

The Missouri Student Union held an annual Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony Friday afternoon to honor veterans. MU participated in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call, during which veterans read the names of MU student veterans killed. Col. Roderik Cox, an MU alumnus and keynote speaker, shared his definition of a veteran as anyone who swore an oath to support and defend the nation. The event included remarks from MU student leadership and the chair of the MU department of Military Science and Leadership, with support from Robert Ross, director of the MU Veterans Center, which works with over 400 student veterans. Ross said the event honored the past and looked toward future peace, and speakers discussed stereotypes of veterans portrayed by Hollywood, emphasizing that many are regular people. The ceremony was followed by a reception at Bengal’s Lair in Memorial Union.

Passports expire two years from issuance. A new one is issued after a new application; if the applicant is a naturalized citizen, the old passport may be accepted in lieu of a naturalization certificate if the original application contained sufficient information. A passport can cover the applicant’s wife, minor children, and servant under specified conditions, but other persons require separate passports; a woman’s passport may include her minor children and servant. Professional titles are not inserted. A one-dollar fee is required per citizen’s passport application, payable by currency or postal money order to the disbursing clerk of the Department of State; drafts or checks are not accepted. The Department of State does not procure visas from foreign government representatives, provides blank application forms only as needed (not as samples for passport-procuring businesses), and communications must be addressed to the Department of State, Passport Bureau with the recipient’s post-office address. The Secretary of State may refuse passports for unlawful/improper purposes or for failure to comply with rules. Rules are prescribed for issuing passports in the United States and insular possessions, including that applications in insular possessions are made to the chief executive there, and temporarily abroad applications are made to U.S. diplomatic or consular representatives. Passports cannot be granted to persons not owing allegiance to the U.S., and those with only a declaration of intention cannot receive one. Applicants must submit a written affidavit with required attestations and declarations, including birth date and place, occupation, permanent residence, and intent to return to the U.S. or insular possessions to reside and perform citizenship duties.

The passage announces that the International Nurses Association is welcoming Joy Williams, BSN, RN, who works in Louisiana in agency and hospital nursing. It states she has over seven years of experience, became an LPN in 2009 after graduating from Nunez Community College, and became an RN in 2016 after earning a BSN from Dillard University. It also notes her involvement in the National Black Nurses Association and the National Student Nurses Association, and says she credits her success to her daughter Londen.

The passage argues that small group differentiation is a promising strategy for improving learning outcomes and inclusivity in elementary and higher education, especially for diverse students with different learning skills and linguistic barriers. It describes U.S. demographic changes and rising language diversity, noting that English-only use at home has declined and the number of English language learners and non-English home language speakers has increased. The passage explains differentiation as tailoring teaching content, process, products, and learning environments to students’ needs, supported by constructivism and sociocultural theory. It outlines practical elements such as forming heterogeneous small groups, using scaffolding and progressive task complexity, differentiating content and resources, and using ongoing assessment and adjustment. It also discusses engagement benefits of small group work, challenges such as the planning time and support needed for teachers, and limitations including gaps in comparative data across settings and limited evidence on impacts on test scores and benchmarks. The conclusion emphasizes flexibility, clear proficiency expectations, multiple assessment types, and inclusive classroom conditions. Recommendations call for longitudinal studies across education levels and research comparing outcomes across learning-style modes.

The passage describes the “Atlas of Human-AI Interaction,” a framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical findings from 1,888 collected HAI-related papers (over 1,000 analyzed) into structured evidence triplets of the form [cause, relationship, effect]. It builds an AI-enabled knowledge graph (1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges) and presents three visualization modes: a 3D Graph View for exploring research themes and gaps, a Cause-Effect View for tracing directional relationships, and a Paper View for viewing extracted findings per paper. The authors report clustering and network analyses that identify common research themes (including education contexts, explanation and trust, design relationships, decision support, and self-referential effects) and structural “holes” indicating integration opportunities across otherwise disconnected communities, with top concepts including large language models, generative AI, trust dynamics, conversational interfaces, and autonomous agents. A user study with 20 expert researchers found the tool helps with early-stage exploration, relationship discovery, and gap identification, while noting limitations in depth/comprehensiveness, coverage, temporal analysis, and domain applicability. The paper positions the Atlas as an open-source research infrastructure and proposes future work to keep the atlas updated, expand relationship types, refine extraction, and enhance connectivity analysis.

The passage explains the 4-3 defense in football, including its history, structure, personnel, strengths, weaknesses, how offenses attack it, examples of common blitzes, and pass coverages. It describes the 4-3 as four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs, and details traditional “Under front” alignments such as 5 technique defensive ends, a 1 technique nose guard, and a 3 technique defensive tackle. The defense is presented as being generally strong against the run and gap sound, with coverage flexibility from four defensive backs, while weaknesses include difficulty versus modern spread offenses and being personnel-specific for linebackers. It outlines offensive strategies like spreading the field, moving the “Sam” linebacker out of the box, and attacking the edge. The passage also gives two blitz concepts (Will edge blitz and DE drop blitz) and two coverages (Tampa 2 and cover 3). Finally, it lists examples of teams/coaches using the 4-3, including early 2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2006 Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic HS under Mike Bukovsky.

Google launched Gemini Enterprise, an artificial intelligence platform for business customers seeking secure, large-scale AI integration. It provides access to Gemini Ultra models and enterprise tools for data governance, security, and regulatory compliance. The platform allows firms to deploy and customize AI applications on Google Cloud, fine-tune models using proprietary data, and maintain oversight through explainability and access controls. Google positions Gemini Enterprise for the enterprise AI market and highlights transparency features such as traceable outputs, privacy safeguards, and compliance tools, aiming to support scalable deployment across corporate operations.

The passage describes Ray Dalio’s “All-Weather Portfolio,” a diversified strategy intended to perform across different economic environments such as inflation, deflation, and stagflation. It includes stocks, bonds, and commodities, aiming to smooth returns and lower drawdowns through diversification and a risk-parity/balancing approach. The article presents backtests showing that the portfolio historically had smaller drawdowns than stocks and tended to outperform during events like the financial crisis in 2008/09, Covid-19 in 2020, and the bear market of 2022, but had lower long-term returns than stocks. It also discusses constructing the portfolio using ETFs, rebalancing (at least annually, potentially more in tax-deferred accounts), and the effects of leverage and changing asset weightings on return and drawdowns. The portfolio is characterized as defensive and potentially suitable for risk-averse investors, retirees, or FIREs.

The mother appeals a dissolution judgment ordering father to pay $31 per month for each of the parties’ two children, arguing the amount is too low and that the court improperly abated father’s child support during visitation. The trial court’s calculation used the Smith child support formula, treating father’s visitation-related expenses as grounds to reduce his obligation. The appellate court agrees that visitation expenses should be factored in but concludes the $31 per child amount is insufficient. Because father’s future income is difficult to estimate and the Smith and joint custody formulas cannot be applied readily, the court modifies the judgment to require father to pay $65 per month for each child effective the date of the decision. The judgment is affirmed as modified, with no costs to either party.

Hamlet Prince of Denmark is staged as a murder trial in real courtrooms in Melbourne Festival and other countries through the theatre work “Please, Continue (Hamlet)” by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat. The production uses real judges, barristers, and jury systems: after legal teams present arguments in a courtroom, a jury of 12 selected from the audience deliberates for 20 minutes to acquit or not acquit. The show has been performed in 12 countries since its 2011 premiere in Switzerland, adapting to each country’s legal system and laws. Duyvendak and Bernat based the case on a real, unredacted file from 2010 about a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father, integrating its social context with Shakespeare’s scenario. Duyvendak says audience members often change their views of Hamlet’s guilt during the show, and that participation by legal professionals reflects the show’s focus on the complexity of the justice system.

The passage introduces the metaverse as a digitally represented, three-dimensional virtual reality where avatars participate in everyday and economic activities, blending real and virtual space. It describes metaverse education as an interactive digital learning environment that can enhance motivation, immersion, and learning through virtual systems, though adoption requires knowledge and guidance for both students and teachers. It discusses using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to analyze adoption factors, focusing on perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, and notes concerns such as lack of technical training or platform complexity. The study reports that it uses a systematic review with descriptive bibliometric analysis of 270 Scopus-indexed journal articles (2015–July 2024), following PRISMA and analyzing data with VOSviewer. Results show no publications before 2020, growth from 2020–2021, a rise to 36 in 2022, and a peak of 131 in 2023. South Korea and China are leading in publication volume, with South Korea leading in citations. The most cited journals include Sustainability (Switzerland) and IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies, and highly cited articles are listed. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies frequent themes and clusters such as metaverse, virtual reality, augmented reality, education, and artificial intelligence, and highlights research gaps including limited longitudinal studies and concentration in East Asia and the United States, with calls for broader comparative and long-term future research.

Lorena Ridgely Jones sued Carolyn A. Dow. The Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department, affirmed the order with $10 costs and disbursements. THOMAS, J., dissented because the order was entered ex parte and deprived the plaintiff of a statutory right to reply to the answer, and CARR, J., did not vote.

Michigan State Police, Emergency Management and Homeland Security are encouraging residents to participate in a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday. Nearly all Michigan state facilities will participate, though participation is not required. Officials say tornadoes can develop rapidly with little or no warning and urge residents to identify shelter locations, practice drills, ensure household members know what to do, monitor radio or television for weather updates, understand the difference between tornado watches and warnings, watch for signs such as dark greenish skies, hail, low-lying clouds, and loud roars, and prepare 72-hour emergency supply kits with essential items including water, food, a NOAA weather radio, and important documents. If severe weather occurs on April 19, the drill will be rescheduled to 1 p.m. Thursday.

The passage argues that effective defensive transition depends on good offense, including taking care of the ball, good shot selection, strong offensive rebounding, and maintaining defensive balance. It outlines “12 musts” such as sprinting back with ball vision, staying ahead of the ball, setting up defensive numerical advantages, forcing extra passes, boxing out to prevent second chances, and countering opponent turnovers and missed shots. It further details principles and techniques for defending outnumbered situations (including communication, “Level of the Ball,” pressuring the ball, containing dribblers, taking charges, and rebounding) and provides specific guidance for breakaways (1-on-none), 2-on-1, and 3-on-2 scenarios. The passage also covers preventing and disrupting outlet passes after missed shots, free throws, steals, and blocked shots, including jamming rebounders, denying outlet passes, and slowing penetration while matching up. It emphasizes turnover recovery (“erasing bad plays”) through quick transition defense and “Really Big Play” effort, and concludes with game strategy recommendations and teaching objectives for installing transition defense using the whole-part-whole method and various drills.

April is Alcohol Awareness Month, and the Navy’s Pier Pressure mobile app helps Sailors make responsible drinking choices. The free app uses interactive gaming and provides tools to explore how excessive drinking can affect health and careers. It is part of the Navy’s Keep What You’ve Earned campaign and was updated with a calorie counter that estimates calories from selected drinks and shows how many pushups would be needed to work them off. The app also integrates with Uber and Lyft for a safe ride home. Since release, it has been played more than 30,000 times, and it is available on iTunes and Google Play, with more resources at www.nadap.navy.mil.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell more than 400 points on Tuesday, closing down 424.56 points (1.74%) amid fears of rising interest rates and signals from Caterpillar suggesting a slowdown in economic growth. The S&P 500 fell 1.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 1.7%, pressured by declines in major technology stocks. Caterpillar shares rose after earnings beat expectations but later fell 6.2% after its CFO said the first quarter would be the year’s “high-water mark.” 3M stock dropped 7% after lowering its full-year profit forecast, and Alphabet fell 5% despite reporting a net profit increase. Investors sold Treasurys over rising inflation fears, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above 3% for the first time in four years, which could lead the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and increase borrowing costs.

The passage describes SEV-ES guest–hypervisor communication using the GHCB and VMGEXIT/NAE events. It specifies that GHCB VALID_BITMAP must have appropriate bits set for each field, including SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2, and that guests and hypervisors must reset VALID_BITMAP before setting bits for an event and its results. It explains how VALID_BITMAP bit positions are calculated and that SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 should be set to 0 unless specified otherwise. It then outlines handling of standard vs non-automatic NAE events, error reporting via SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] and SW_EXITINFO2, and requirements for interrupt protection around GHCB updates and VMGEXIT handling. The passage further describes multiple specific NAE events, including page state changes (with progress tracking and error reasons), SNP guest/extended guest requests (with page-based request/response and returned certificate/measurement data), AP creation, #HV doorbell page configuration, #HV send IPI, #HV timer, APIC ID list retrieval, SNP run VMPL, and Secure AVIC backing page management. It also covers termination requests, unsupported exits, and guest identification of SEV-ES support via CPUID properties. Finally, it defines the #HV doorbell page data format (PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired) and associated host/guest behaviors for interrupt presentation, acknowledgments, EOI handling, and interrupt/shadow conventions.

Florence O. Summers sued Clennon C. Hemsell and Columbian Fuel Corporation for the wrongful death of her husband, J. W. Summers, alleging negligence by Hemsell while acting as an employee of Columbian Fuel Corporation in an automobile collision that occurred on October 9, 1937. The jury returned a verdict awarding appellees a total of $30,890, and the trial court entered judgment. The court of civil appeals reversed, finding reversible error in the jury charges for multiple special issues. It held that the charges improperly fixed life expectancy and expected contributions using mathematical periods instead of leaving those fact questions to the jury, incorrectly framed recoverable damages by including non-pecuniary elements (such as loss of love, care, and fatherly advice, and emotional impacts), and improperly suggested specific education expenses without a sufficient evidentiary basis. The appellate court also found improper and inflammatory jury argument by appellees’ counsel that the trial court failed to correct. The judgment was reversed and the case remanded.

Chinese police shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five people and injured 10 in Pishan County, southern Xinjiang, according to local authorities. They described the attackers as “thugs,” said “social order” was restored, and launched an investigation, without detailing the attackers’ or victims’ ethnic backgrounds. The passage also notes Beijing’s accusations against exiled Uighur separatist groups, claims of crackdowns by some foreign-based Uighurs, and previous killings by police tied to incidents including attacks in Pishan County in 2015 and Kunming in 2014, for which China blamed “Xinjiang separatists.”

The passage previews four midweek MLS games with early 7:30 ET kickoffs and two late ones. It summarizes two early match takeaways: Philadelphia’s Bořek Dočkal, described as a key Czech import, helped the Union remain unbeaten in four matches and contributed significantly in a 3-goal involvement. It also notes a highlight where Ilsinho scored to give Philadelphia a 1-0 lead versus Chicago, and mentions that New England earned a 1-1 draw after a late Teal Bunbury penalty.

A security researcher, Michael Myng, reported that hundreds of HP notebook and tablet models include a keylogger linked to Synaptics touchpad drivers. He said HP confirmed the issue and released security patches last month, including updates for more than 450 affected products, and that the keylogger is disabled by default and could be enabled after a registry change to monitor keystrokes. HP stated neither it nor Synaptics has access to customer data due to the issue, and noted a similar keylogging problem involving Conexant audio drivers reported in May was caused by debugging code left in shipped software.

Johnny Juzang is making the case for a spot on the Minnesota Timberwolves’ roster after Nickeil Alexander-Walker left in the offseason. Playing in the preseason, Juzang scored 20 points in 14 minutes Tuesday night and has shot 9-of-15 from three this preseason. The passage notes he is on a non-guaranteed contract in training camp, has made over 38% of his 3-pointers over the last two seasons, and is seen as fitting the team’s outside-shooter style. It also says the Timberwolves’ young bench scorers include Rob Dillingham and Terrence Shannon Jr.

Researchers from Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and Mayo Clinic compiled peer-reviewed evidence and developed a guideline to help stop using CK-MB, a widely ordered blood test, for evaluating suspected heart attack. Their Aug. 14 report in JAMA Internal Medicine says prior statements from the American College of Cardiology and five studies conclude CK-MB is no longer an effective biomarker and can be safely eliminated. The report, part of a series of implementation guides co-authored by High Value Practice Academic Alliance (HVPAA) faculty, describes a multi-institutional effort to improve value in care. It also outlines a four-step approach to phase out CK-MB, including hospitalwide education, stakeholder partnerships to remove CK-MB from order sets, adding a computerized order entry alert, and measuring test use and patient outcomes before and after. The passage notes that despite guideline recommendations, a 2013 survey found many U.S. labs still use CK-MB, and it estimates heart-attack diagnostic blood tests add $416 million annually.

Molecular cloud collapse unfolds over million-year timescales, making direct observation of material reaching stellar densities difficult. Redshifted self-absorption in molecular line profiles is widely used as an indirect signature of gravitational collapse, and analytic methods such as Myers et al. (1996) estimate infall velocities and mass infall rates from line shapes, though accuracy is limited in more complex cases where infall velocities vary with radius and different molecules probe different parts of the velocity field.  

The paper uses smoothed-particle hydrodynamic simulations of a collapsing prestellar core combined with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer to generate synthetic molecular line observations. Using established techniques to infer infall velocities from the synthetic line profiles, the authors find that measured infall velocities systematically underestimate the true mass-weighted infall velocity, often by up to an order of magnitude depending on the choice of tracer and aperture size. The paper concludes that commonly used two-slab, constant-velocity-based observational methods likely underestimate prestellar mass accretion rates by as much as an order of magnitude.

An Indian-origin surgeon, Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri, was struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his professional position by writing a love letter to a female patient. The patient reported being distressed and called police after receiving the letter. Amaragiri said he had not taken advantage of the patient and called the letter a “moment of madness,” later apologising. He intends to appeal the tribunal’s decision.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 11, 2021. Effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive, to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. The filing states that Mr. Guillen will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including related charging and servicing networks. The report was signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on March 12, 2021.

Sony launched a U.S. instant rebate and trade-in scheme offering photographers up to $500 on select full-frame Sony cameras, including the Sony A9. From now through September 30, 2017, buyers can save up to $300 on select Sony cameras plus an additional $500 for trading in an interchangeable lens camera, with free shipping in the U.S. The A7 cameras offer up to $200 in instant savings, and select full-frame lenses and accessories offer up to $100 in instant savings. The passage lists discounted prices for several models, including Sony Alpha a7R II, Sony Alpha a7S II, and specific FE lenses.

Compass Minerals International is rated a “Buy” because its shares are attractively valued and recent operations have improved. Revenue and volumes, particularly in salt and plant nutrition, are rising, while cost-cutting initiatives are improving cash flow and EBITDA. Although its net debt and leverage are higher than peers, it trades at lower multiples than industry averages, suggesting upside potential. Management projects further top-line growth for 2025, but leverage risk keeps the rating from being a “Strong Buy.”

The passage describes the CANSLIM stock-picking method developed by William O’Neill and explains its use, components, and reported performance. It says CANSLIM, an acronym for seven variables, is meant to identify “good stocks” based on criteria such as quarterly and annual earnings growth, new products/management, new highs, supply and demand factors, leader/laggard status, institutional sponsorship, and market direction, and also considers stocks in an uptrend. The IBD 50 is described as a computer-generated, mathematically ranked list of 50 stocks that fit the seven criteria, published twice weekly, with an ETF used for updated backtesting. The passage concludes that backtests show CANSLIM has beaten the S&P 500 since 2003 but with higher volatility and larger drawdowns, and it suggests the outperformance may be related to CANSLIM’s exposure to small-cap stocks. It also notes risks such as market volatility and potential loss of capital, states the method is primarily for long-term investing rather than trading, and says backtesting is demanding because both fundamental and technical data are needed.

The speaker says they felt great after a win, crediting players including Rucchin for two big goals and noting that the team played well overall. They mention contributing offensively more, having a good start and strong control of the game, and emphasize preparing each night and doing the same things that worked in past games. The speaker discusses team leadership by example, adjusting plays as needed, and believes earlier games in New Jersey were an aberration due to not playing at the same pace. They expect to regain their legs when returning, aim to tighten up defensively while maintaining offensive success, and describe staying focused on preparing for the next game. They also address recovering from a hard stick hit after a doctor check, and comment that playoff hockey involves increased animosity over longer series.

Peter Crouch made a comedy quip about the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge’s third child shortly after Kate gave birth in Paddington, and the tweet was widely retweeted and liked. Abbey Clancy then replied, leading to further comments. The passage also says Crystal Palace posted a tweet after the birth, noting the baby weighed 8lbs 7oz and that both Kate and the baby were “doing well,” and the account added “Great name!”

The passage discusses whether a basketball team’s habit of overcoming large halftime deficits—described as “Superman syndrome”—should concern its coach. Mark Jackson says the team can’t keep relying on urgency after falling into traps, though Golden State has the ability to adjust, not panic. Examples include leading the NBA in third-quarter scoring and overcoming a 17-point first-quarter deficit in Game 6 versus Houston, plus Game 7 come-from-behind efforts. It also notes losses where the Warriors couldn’t “flip the switch,” citing defensive and performance problems in Games 2, 4, and 5. Jeff Van Gundy and Jackson emphasize concern about repeatedly digging early holes and the need for leadership, coaches, and players to identify underlying issues before the Finals.

Investors seeking value buy closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges because sellers often offer units at discounts to NAVs. Unlike open-ended funds, closed-end schemes have a lock-in of three to five years, with redemption typically only at maturity. The discounts occur because exchange liquidity is modest and units may trade below present value. Examples given include Reliance and HDFC closed-end schemes trading below their NAVs, with discounts varying by scheme and time to maturity. The discount size depends on time remaining and tax considerations, with shorter remaining maturity potentially leading to higher discounts due to short-term capital gains tax at maturity. Spotting opportunities is described as difficult, and guidance suggests focusing on schemes with large assets under management and a corpus above Rs 250 crore.

The passage describes Airbus’s Project Vahana, a planned helicopter-style autonomous flying vehicle that would transport several riders and offer an airborne taxi option to reduce road congestion. Airbus says it is testing a prototype, focusing on autonomous driving, AI, and clean technology to avoid increasing urban pollution, and that it could lower infrastructure costs by reducing the need for road and bridge construction. Airbus aims to have the vehicle available for short-haul trips by 2021, with a fully functional prototype targeted for 2017. The passage also notes other efforts toward flying cars, including Uber’s interest in a VTOL network, Urban Aeronautics’ passenger drone Cormorant, AeroMobil’s land-and-fly AeroMobil 3.0, and investments from Skype’s co-founder and Google co-founder Larry Page.

A letter taped to Michael Ben’Ary’s door, after he was abruptly fired last week, said a false social media post appeared to have led to his termination while he was mid-terrorism prosecution. The letter warned that DOJ leadership removed career officials from U.S. attorney offices and the FBI, making America less safe, and said justice should not depend on what DOJ staff see on social media. It also alleged Ben’Ary was part of “internal resistance” to the indictment involving former FBI director James Comey, whom President Donald Trump had fired, and criticized the DOJ for punishing the president’s perceived enemies rather than protecting national security.

The passage describes aspects of a light emitting diode (LED) device and its manufacturing method, including a reliable electrical connection structure between a luminous body and electrodes. It provides an LED device structure with a thin film transistor substrate, first and second diode electrodes, a first passivation pattern, micro light emitting diodes, and first and second bridge patterns that electrically connect the micro LEDs to the electrodes; each micro LED sidewall and a sidewall of the first passivation pattern form a same plane. The micro LEDs are described as cylindrical with a light emitting material (including p-type, intermediate, and n-type semiconductor layers) and a protective insulating layer, and additional passivation layers and bridge patterns are used. A manufacturing method is outlined, including preparing a thin film transistor substrate, forming electrodes and passivation patterns, placing and aligning micro LEDs using a voltage difference, and forming bridge patterns. The method uses a single mask process including two etching processes for forming the passivation patterns and micro LEDs, with different etching conditions (first more anisotropic/longer and second more isotropic/shorter) to achieve aligned sidewalls. The passage also includes a brief description of a display device and driving circuitry that uses the light emitting units.

The passage previews MLB wild-card round Game 3s, emphasizing that Thursday will be “win-or-go-home” with three winner-takes-all games in one day, a rare event. It discusses the Tigers’ need to convert scoring chances, citing 15 left on base in Game 2 and a combined 3-for-38 with runners in scoring position across recent elimination games. It also notes that the Padres vs. Red Sox matchup may hinge on bullpen performance and starter pitch counts, highlighting Yu Darvish’s 2.56 ERA in six postseason starts and Jameson Taillon’s 1.57 ERA in six starts after returning from the IL. For the Red Sox, it points to Alex Cora’s aggressive bullpen use after pulling Brayan Bello early in Game 2 and the resulting expectation of a challenging bullpen workload against the Yankees.

The passage says the U.S. national debt surpassed $21 trillion for the first time, rising by $73 billion in one day (Thursday to Friday) and by $215 billion in February. It also claims the debt increased by more than $1 trillion in the last six months without a major crisis, while the economy reportedly grew by 2.5% in real terms (or 4.4% including inflation). The author argues that debt growth is outpacing GDP growth, noting debt rose from $9.4 trillion to over $21 trillion in about ten years. The passage contends that although some argue the debt “doesn’t matter” because it is owed to domestic institutions, defaulting would cause a severe financial catastrophe, and it describes three groups of responses to the debt before encouraging readers to download a guide.

Jio announced new offers for the Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo under the Jio Galaxy Club. Both phones come with instant cashback of Rs 2,750 provided through 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each, and Jio SIM users also get extra data on plans worth Rs 198 or Rs 299. The Galaxy J2 2018 includes additional 100GB data via ten 10GB vouchers, while the Galaxy J7 Duo offers double data, providing 4GB per day (Rs 198 plan) or 6GB per day (Rs 299 plan). These offers are valid until September 30, and the phones are available online and offline. The passage also lists specifications for both devices.

Aspen, Colorado, will replace its annual Fourth of July fireworks with a drone show due to wildfire risk in drought conditions. Officials say 50 drones will display patriotic colours during a 15-minute Independence Day show starting at 21:15 local time, organised at Wagner Park by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association. The public has been invited to watch the drones choreographed to patriotic music. Officials cite strict fire restrictions in Colorado and say the drone show is intended as an alternative as fire dangers increase. The organisers may have been influenced by the 2018 Winter Olympics drone display, though that event used pre-recorded effects due to possible freezing weather and strong winds.

The passage says many payday lenders could go out of business if Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rules finalized this week take effect. One rule would require payday and auto title lenders to determine whether borrowers can repay in full within 30 days and would limit the number of times lenders can debit an account without reauthorization. CFPB Director Richard Cordray says the rule provides “ability-to-repay” protections, and the passage cites a CFPB study finding most payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. Consumer advocates argue lenders profit from repeated debt and that curbing unaffordable loans protects borrowers, while a trade group representing the industry says the rule would devastate a large customer base. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be cut in half and that many of the 16,000 stores in 35 states could be forced out of business. The rule would not take effect until 2019 and could be rolled back by Congress; it also notes political opposition to the CFPB, related congressional actions to weaken it, and an April Pew poll finding 70% of surveyed adults want more regulation of payday lenders.

Sarcomas are diverse and have varied genetic causes and clinical behavior; metastatic sarcoma is often treated palliatively with systemic therapies, including immune checkpoint blockade (ICIs). In sarcoma, baseline immune infiltrates and epigenetic features were studied to identify factors linked to ICI response. In a cohort of 67 patients across 3 ICI trials, baseline immune infiltrates separated into two groups (“immune-hot” and “immune-cold”) using RNA-seq immune deconvolution. Immune-hot tumors showed higher overall response rates and longer progression-free survival, and had higher expression of checkpoint-related genes such as PD-L1 and CTLA4. The immune-hot/cold groups corresponded to previously described sarcoma immune classes, and immune-hot tumors had lower tumor purity.

The study further found that increased expression of transposable elements (TEs) and the epigenetic regulator IKZF1 predicted immune-hot immune states. TE and IKZF1 expression correlated with inflammatory and immune pathway signatures, including interferon signaling and antigen presentation, and were associated with prolonged progression-free survival in the ICI-treated cohort. These patterns were validated in a separate dataset of 190 sarcoma samples from TCGA, where immune-hot clusters and higher TE score or IKZF1 expression were associated with improved overall survival. The authors propose that tumor epigenetic states involving TE de-repression and IKZF1 may contribute to enhanced antitumor immunity and ICI outcomes.

Meagan Holt, who is participating in a writing session with coach Sierra Nelson, says her daughter Madeline likely has Zellweger Syndrome and that she wakes up to that reality every day. Through a new writing program at Seattle Children’s, Holt writes essays to express and release bottled-up emotions, describing journaling as a powerful outlet. The Pediatric Advanced Care Team (PACT) encourages parents to journal, with consultant Julie Arguez saying it helps them take time to think what they need to be present and well, bringing calm, relief, and sometimes acceptance. Holt says writing helps her handle others telling her she is strong. The writing program depends on donations to continue.

The managing director of Happy Home Furnishers said the company is closing its Neath store, citing lack of free parking, increased business rates, and anti-social behaviour problems near the shop. The firm has been at The Parade for 33 years and described disruption from street works and a bench placed near a nearby shop, which it says led to years of anti-social incidents involving violence, disturbances, and unsafe conditions. Other retailers reported the behaviour mainly worsens in summer and that needles have been found in public toilets. Neath Council said the street works were completed years ago, benches were provided for mobility needs, and they were removed about a year ago after misuse. The council also said free parking is available after 3pm in its multi-storey car park and it runs initiatives and events to attract visitors. The business rates increase was also discussed, with the Welsh Government stating relief schemes support small businesses after a 2017 revaluation. Happy Home Furnishers said it is continuing at other locations and may look for another site in Neath, while thanking customers and wishing the town and traders success.

The passage introduces a research gap in understanding how science teachers—especially experienced ones—view science education research, noting potential links to a theory-practice gap and to teachers’ assumed skepticism about evidence-based teaching. It explains that science education research often assumes practical value, yet teacher scepticism may reduce willingness to use research findings and instead prioritize personal experience. The study aims to explore physics teachers’ perspectives on science education research, focusing on potential skepticism, and uses a two-step mixed-methods design: interviews with 13 physics teachers (to develop categories) and a survey of 174 physics teachers (to test attitudes quantitatively). Interview results identified seven attitude categories, with most teachers expressing scepticism, especially that research findings play a minor role compared to personal experience and that research findings cannot be implemented into teaching practice. Factor analysis on survey items produced four factors: individual relevance, feasibility for teaching practice, general relevance for teaching practice, and cooperation between research and school practice. Latent profile analysis identified four teacher types: “Sceptical Ones,” “Uncertain Ones,” “Undersupplied Ones,” and “Research Advocates.” Multinomial logistic regression showed that only the frequency of reading instructional journals significantly related to profile membership. The discussion highlights that teachers are not generally sceptical but show notable scepticism, particularly about research-practice cooperation, and presents limitations related to sample size, selection, and measurement assumptions.

The passage reports that the Ravens traded slumping pass rusher Odafe Oweh to the Chargers for Alohi Gilman and a fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft, according to sources. Oweh, 26, had 10 sacks last season but recorded no sacks in his first five games this season, and his playing time dropped to 45% of Ravens defensive snaps. The trade frees about $8 million in cap space for Baltimore and leaves the team needing to bolster its pass rush after struggling defensively. Gilman, 28, was a key part of the Chargers’ top-ranked defense last season; he is expected to help cover deep-safety duties as Baltimore addresses an issue with experienced depth at safety. The passage also notes Baltimore’s defense ranks last in pass defense and has allowed the most points in the NFL.

African countries are being urged to use modern technology to address tax non-compliance as global technology transformation advances. At the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe, Secretary to the Treasury Ben Botolo opened the two-day 18th Forum for Value Added Tax (VAT) Administrators in Africa (VADA), saying that electronic fiscal devices are critical for monitoring tax compliance and improving revenue collection. He noted that many African countries remain cash economies and argued that moving toward non-cash, electronic card transactions would make tax collection easier. Botolo said Malawi has made progress in electronic monitoring and that a Tax Administration Act is planned to harmonize compliance, with further improvement needed. Henry Saka, chairperson of VADA, emphasized formalizing regulatory strategies and designing African solutions to schemes used to evade tax. He stated that VADA provides technical support to at least 12 non-member countries and that the forum brings together 10 member countries to share and analyze tax non-compliance challenges and propose interventions to improve domestic revenue mobilization for economic development.

The lecture discusses interpretations and calculations of free-field Green’s functions. The propagator \(G^+\) can be viewed heuristically as a transition amplitude from \(x'\) to \(x\) or as a correlation function of \(\phi\) between \(x'\) and \(x\). Similar interpretations apply to \(G^-\), while retarded/advanced and Feynman time-ordered functions are distinguished by how singularities in the \(\omega\)-plane are handled in contour integration. A practical “epsilon prescription” is introduced to keep the contour fixed while shifting singularities. The lecturer then summarizes that in free theory, all vacuum \(n\)-point correlation functions factorize into sums of two-point functions, due to pairing of creation and annihilation operators. They also note that composite operators (products of fields at the same point) typically lead to singularities requiring renormalization.  

The discussion shifts to interacting theories as the next topic, focusing on how interactions are studied via the \(S\)-matrix. The \(S\)-matrix is defined using asymptotic initial and final states at \(t=\pm\infty\), where interactions can be neglected, and it encodes transition amplitudes between momentum eigenstates. It is argued to be unitary (not Hermitian), and in the weak-interaction limit it approaches the identity. The lecture concludes by indicating that scattering amplitudes \(M_{\alpha\beta}\) can be obtained from time-ordered vacuum correlation functions, and that the next lecture will discuss the general approach (including the path integral).

The passage discusses expectations and factors affecting a team’s performance in playoff series, emphasizing focus despite distractions and the importance of preparing to play a complete game. It notes that players have prior experience with similar situations and discusses how penalties and power plays can pressure a team. The role and confidence of goalies is highlighted, including how they respond to goals and make aggressive plays, and how experience influences outcomes. The team also reflects on home-ice versus away performance and describes how game momentum can shift with territorial advantage and timely scoring. Additional points cover penalty discipline, goalie and forward defensive coverage, player fit on lines, conditioning and preparation routines, and comparisons to other opponents and prior series experiences.

The passage is a letter to the U.S. Senate stating that certain passages in a prior message and protest may have been misunderstood. The author says the intention was not to deny the legislative department’s power to provide by law for custody, safe-keeping, and disposition of U.S. public money and property. The author admits the Legislature’s constitutional authority to prescribe deposit locations and related regulations, and denies any executive right to possess or dispose of public property except when granted by law. The author also denies any right to supervise or interfere with the person entrusted with such property unless that person’s appointment is constitutionally tied to the President alone or with the Senate. The author requests that this communication be considered part of the earlier message and entered on the Senate journal.

The passage describes sidelink positioning techniques and related apparatuses. It states that terminals can determine relative or absolute position using sidelink positioning signals, improving accuracy and reducing positioning latency because measurement values do not need to be transmitted through a core network. Several method aspects are presented: (1) a first terminal receives sidelink configuration, sends a reference signal to a second terminal, and obtains a measurement value used with the second terminal’s known position to determine the first terminal’s position; measurement values may be exchanged with the network device or between terminals. (2) a second terminal measures a reference signal from a first terminal and sends a first measurement value to the network device or to the first terminal to enable position determination. (3) the network device sends configurations to two terminals, receives measurement values, and determines the first terminal’s position based on the measurements and the second terminal’s position; optionally it may use both first and second measurement values. The configurations include details such as time-frequency resources, sequence information, identification of the second terminal, and measurement reporting methods over Uu (core-assisted) and PC5 (sidelink) interfaces, with measurement values including Rx–Tx time differences and/or angle-of-arrival measurements. The passage also includes apparatus implementations (terminal and network device) with processors, memory, and communication interfaces, plus computer program and storage medium aspects, and a communication system including the network device and terminals.

The passage describes perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views of a first and a second embodiment of an analytical instrument, showing a new design. It also states that portions depicted in broken lines are not part of the claimed design.

The passage describes the author’s decision to declutter by throwing out decades-old McGill University law school textbooks after retiring from practice. While deciding, the author recalls several cases and concepts discussed in the books, including contract-related cases and property law topics like fee simple, fee tail, and life interests in land, and ultimately discards the books. The author says the books were put in a blue recycling bin and handled without further inspection by the garbage truck loader. The author kept one book, using it as a reading stand. The passage ends with brief biographical information about Marcel Strigberger and notes that the column reflects his opinions.

In a June 7–8, 2014 Wall Street Journal article, Hertz Global Holdings was reported to have to restate and correct results from the past three years due to more widespread accounting problems, and its stock had fallen about 9%. The passage provides background on Hertz and the U.S. car rental industry, noting that the car rental market had about $36 billion in 2013 revenue and was dominated by three companies. It outlines Hertz’s history, scale (locations and fleet), operations and financial performance through 2013, and how depreciation is calculated and disclosed under U.S. GAAP. It describes Hertz’s depreciation policies for revenue-earning equipment, details about program versus non-program rental cars, and the data collection approach used by analyst Abby Devins to compare Hertz’s revenue-earning equipment balances and depreciation expense (2006–2013) with Avis Budget Group.

The passage discusses how AI could augment human cognitive abilities, learning, and creativity, while also introducing risks that depend on design, deployment, and usage choices. It outlines two key risks: over-reliance on AI systems, which may weaken learning and critical thinking, and limited internalization of AI-learned capabilities, which could undermine independent knowledge retention. To mitigate these concerns, it emphasizes promoting a critical mindset, reducing passive learning, selectively delegating tasks, and coordinating efforts between AI developers and educators. It also describes how LLMs may change society’s social division of labor by addressing knowledge scarcity and blurring job boundaries, potentially leading to shifts such as a rise in the gig economy and new patterns of global collaboration. The passage further notes challenges in social science research as computational approaches grow, and it proposes uses of LLMs for improved data access and automated analysis, while acknowledging biases and ethical risks. Finally, it argues that AI governance should address harms like misinformation, deepfakes, and bias, and calls for human-centered, forward-looking regulation through top-down and bottom-up cooperation among industry, academia, policymakers, and users.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 25, 2018 to report its third quarter 2018 financial results. The passage describes guidance for unused comparator inputs and device behavior. It states that unused channels should not have their inputs tied together; instead, inputs should be tied to an available voltage within the specified input range with at least a 50 mV differential (e.g., one input grounded and the other connected to a reference voltage or directly to V+ while connected to the V+ pin to avoid transients). It notes the TLV32xx family has 1.8 mV internal hysteresis, defines components of the hysteresis transfer curve (VTH, VOS, VHYST), and recommends treating the output as high-speed digital with proper PCB layout. For TLV321x push-pull outputs, it says outputs must never be connected to another output and unused outputs should be left floating; shorting outputs to the opposite supply rail can cause thermal runaway. For TLV322x open-drain outputs, it describes open-drain behavior, recommends a pull-up resistor current between 100 µA and 1 mA, warns against shorting output to a voltage source, and says unused open-drain outputs can be left floating or tied to V-. It also covers ESD protection and a power-on-reset (POR) feature that holds the output low during an initial delay after V+ crosses 1.65 V.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike said the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) is currently structured as a “fund raising commission” for politicians and promotes corruption rather than Niger Delta development. He cited examples including funding related to re-run elections and alleged failure to act on projects and to honor an agreement on the Mother and Child Hospital, which the Rivers State Government later took over. Wike urged the U.S. government to establish a Visa Office in Port Harcourt for South-South and South-East residents, saying it would create opportunities. He also called for the cleanup of Ogoni land and said his administration wants partnerships with the U.S. in commercial agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization, while urging all tiers of government to focus on governance.

Coach Vigneault says he has not yet talked to him personally but that assistants have, and he believes Dan has great teammates. He describes a bounce in a game that didn’t work out and says they must “turn the page.” He says their team likely won’t beat the opponent unless everyone brings their “a game,” because the opponent is strong and structured, with experience and a game plan they don’t deviate from. He notes parts of a game he has watched, says their third period wasn’t good enough, and credits their goaltender for keeping them in the game; they were “one shot away.” He discusses players including Johnny (a consistent left-handed defenseman who skates with the puck) and Rafa, and says Rick has been playing well—competing, using his size, making defensive plays, and generating scoring chances for and against. He concludes that success depends on compete level, execution, and sticking to the plan, and that they need to play to their strengths, including speed, while making adjustments for the next game.

The professor discusses nuclear war risks compared with climate change, arguing that climate change is nearly certain while nuclear war is harder to avoid but would be catastrophic if it occurs. He outlines arguments about deterrence and nuclear “non-use,” questions whether possessing nuclear weapons makes countries more secure, and emphasizes fear and distrust as key drivers of nuclear escalation, including accident, escalation from conventional wars, and specific risks such as Pakistan’s posture and North Korea’s case. He reviews historical arms control efforts, the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and its tensions—especially Article VI obligations—and the effectiveness and problems of the NPT, including states outside the treaty and ongoing negotiations related to Iran’s nuclear program. He also comments on modernization versus maintenance of nuclear forces, the stability of current arrangements, the role of monitoring systems for nuclear tests, and policy steps such as accelerating aspects of arms control and improving inspections.

The passage argues for creating a secretary of commerce with a Cabinet seat, citing increasing labor and capital issues, expanding corporate organization, and the country’s growth in international business. It urges enactment of a Senate measure into law and proposes giving the new department large supervisory powers over interstate corporations. It states the U.S. plans to submit a reciprocity treaty with Cuba and discusses post-occupation relations, saying Cuba should benefit economically as part of the U.S. international political system. It also supports reciprocal trade with Newfoundland via a Great Britain convention and asserts that arbitration and international tribunals should replace war where possible, praising The Hague tribunal and a recent U.S.-Mexico case. The passage recommends Congress consider Hawaiian fire claims, supports building an isthmian canal (if possible at Panama), reports possible acquisition of title from the French Panama canal company, notes ongoing negotiations with Colombia, and calls for the canal policy to continue regardless of administration changes.

CPRE Bedfordshire challenges Central Bedfordshire Council’s claim that it needs up to 55,000 new homes over the next 20 years, saying a Freedom of Information request shows 60% of that figure would be for people moving into Central Bedfordshire. CPRE also says 23,000 of the homes already have allocations or planning permission, and warns this would lead to loss of countryside and greenspaces and is unsustainable given pressures on local road and rail infrastructure. CBC responds that Central Bedfordshire’s location attracts people and that councils must plan for new homes using government requirements based on migration trends, natural change, and affordability, not a council decision. An assessment published in July 2017 had identified an objectively assessed need of 32,000 dwellings for 2015–2035, with CPRE stating 41% would meet the needs of people currently living there, and CBC has added 7,400 homes for Luton’s residents plus up to 20% contingency.

Andrew Johnson transmits a copy of his February 10, 1868 communication to General U. S. Grant, in which Johnson responds to Grant’s published correspondence and argues that Grant’s actions regarding Stanton’s suspension and Grant’s alleged refusal to follow orders show insubordination and a concealed intent to defeat the President’s purpose. Johnson also includes correspondence and statements from multiple Cabinet members (Gideon Welles, Hugh McCulloch, Alexander W. Randall, O. H. Browning, Hugh McCulloch, William H. Seward) recalling the January 14, 1868 Cabinet meeting conversation between the President and Grant, describing discussions about whether Grant would remain in office, whether judicial proceedings would be pursued, and what was understood to be agreed. Later, Johnson submits to the House of Representatives General Grant’s additional letter (received after Johnson’s February 11 communication), and Grant replies that he did not intend to disobey a legal order of the President but acted on an interpretation of what counted as satisfactory evidence of presidential sanction. The passage ends with related departmental requests for military aid and administrative communications involving the War, Treasury, Post Office, and inspectors-general.

The passage discusses grief during the holidays, noting that Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder from the Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group recommend strategies such as making a plan based on one’s tolerance, limiting events, having an exit plan, and being honest with hosts. They also encourage grieving people to feel their emotions, say their loved one’s name, share memories, be patient with themselves, treat themselves, and create new holiday traditions while keeping some old ones. The passage describes Travnicek’s background and the group’s 20 years of meeting, including meeting details at Smith-Leroy Funeral Home, and provides information on additional local grief support groups and programs, with registration phone numbers and dates.

After five games, Bill Belichick’s hiring at North Carolina has been followed by exasperation after the Tar Heels lost 38-10 to Clemson. UNC trailed 28-3 after the first quarter, fell to 0-3 against Power 4 teams, and gave up 120-33 total points. Belichick said the problems are self-inflicted, citing concentration and execution, and said he will not make personnel changes based on a long-term vision, saying the best players will play. The loss comes days after a publicly released donor letter from GM Mike Lombardi describing a “rebuilding” campaign due to a talent shortage, which Belichick downplayed while also acknowledging a long-term approach. UNC player Shipp said he is focused on winning games rather than rebuilding.

Medicine is described as a demanding field with many potential stressors, contributing to higher risk of stress, anxiety, psychological distress, and burnout among medical students and healthcare trainees. The COVID-19 pandemic is noted to have increased anxiety, depression, and irritability, highlighting the need for resilience skills and self-directed well-being approaches.

The passage presents a qualitative phenomenological study at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences in Dubai, exploring medical students’ perceptions of resilience and an innovative, curriculum-based resilience skills building course. The course includes 6 hours of instruction during Year 4 and aims to build awareness of stress and burnout and to provide tools for developing resilience through concepts such as cognitive behavioral therapy basics, healthy coping strategies, mindfulness and meditation, emotional intelligence, mental toughness, and gratitude, with students reflecting via daily journals and end-session online surveys. Assessment components include attendance, OSCE, and reflective essays. Data were collected from students’ reflective essays from 38 enrolled students, with 37 submissions analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.

Results produced a conceptual framework of “3As of Building Resilience,” comprising Awareness, Application, and Appraisal, with themes and categories including interpretations of resilience, associations with concepts such as mindfulness/meditation and social support, perceived relevance, requirement for conscious practice, practical exercises, challenges to engagement, and the perceived value of the course and learned skills. Students reported benefits including improved management of stress and anxiety, emotional regulation, self-efficacy, and mindful and health-supportive habits, while also identifying barriers such as time constraints, skepticism, and difficulty prioritizing practice. The discussion concludes that integrating a resilience skills building course into medical curricula is likely to be positively appraised, supporting further development of contextualized resilience learning opportunities.

Madison, a first-year undergraduate pursuing a special education credential, enrolls in an undergraduate course on inclusive special education created by Dr. Harper. The course is designed to instill the importance of advocacy and is organized around advocacy as a consistent theme rather than a standalone lesson. It integrates policy content from laws including IDEA, ADA, and Section 504 across the term, and uses learning goals that emphasize dignity, critique, evidence analysis, critical reflection and writing, and exploring students’ roles in educational equity and disability justice. Students complete scaffolded advocacy-focused assignments, including TED Talk–style presentations with corresponding papers, weekly reflection assignments, a special education law and policy jigsaw activity, and an in-class debate on inclusive education with preparation using Perusall annotations. In the final week, students present TED Talks and submit a TED Talk paper in lieu of a final exam. The passage concludes that advocacy is intertwined with special education and should be integrated into teacher preparation coursework through active engagement with skills such as argumentative writing, debate, and policy analysis.

The passage argues that community-based organizations and out-of-school-time programs should be part of the mental health solution for young people. It cites that 40% of young people reported persistent sadness or hopelessness, and more than a third of young adults (18–25) with untreated needs cannot access care. While families and schools have a role, the passage says community organizations already have trusting relationships and can provide basic mental health support embedded in familiar settings, not by turning after-school programs into clinics. It states that with the right tools and staff training, nonprofit staff can recognize early signs of distress and refer youth to professionals when necessary, supported by investments such as strategic plans, protocols, resource directories, warm referral systems, partnerships with mental health providers, and well-being support for frontline workers.

The lecture introduces two topics: the morality of markets and regulating large tech platforms. It reviews issues with both “too much cooperation” (e.g., intellectual property sharing, joint R&D, standard setting, data pools, collective negotiations, common ownership, algorithmic collusion) and “too little cooperation,” focusing today on platform regulation.

The professor describes a two-sided platform with consumers on one side and merchants/apps on the other, noting concerns such as behavioral manipulation, lack of contestability (whether new entrants can replace incumbents), and access/fair compensation for apps and merchants. Current law in Europe and the US is discussed in relation to recommendation/content-curation obligations, and the focus then shifts to contestability and especially access pricing.

The lecture critiques a Chicago School-style argument that gatekeepers won’t need to discriminate against third parties because they can raise consumer prices, explaining that in digital markets prices can be constrained by a “zero lower bound,” since charging negative prices would lead to arbitrage by fake consumers. Three reasons are given for why the Chicago argument fails in this context, including the zero lower bound and theories of how platform discrimination can affect entry.

Regulation “limits” are discussed by comparing platforms to traditional public utilities, emphasizing differences such as multinational scope, fast-changing products, and uncertainty about investment and success probabilities. The European Digital Markets Act (DMA) is summarized as designating platforms and addressing contestability and fairness, with obligations that rely heavily on self-execution, plus possible large fines. The professor then connects contestability policies to tools like multihoming, portability, interoperability, and related measures.

Later, the lecture develops a model of access pricing in two-sided markets with negative marginal costs from ancillary benefits, introduces two “zero lower bounds” (on consumer access and on app prices), and analyzes how access charges affect platform incentives to foreclose rivals. It concludes with policy questions, including the need to identify a parameter \(b\) for optimal access charges, and proposes a “masking game” that could elicit \(b\) from third-party entrants, framed as a potentially Pigouvian regulation that still requires further work for practical implementation. The professor ends by noting more discussion of morality of markets on Wednesday.

Executive Order 11905 (Feb. 18, 1976) replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group (OAG) to develop recommendations and conduct periodic reviews of covert actions; it also banned U.S. Government employees from involvement in political assassinations and prohibited domestic intelligence activities. Approval and oversight for covert action continued under the Hughes-Ryan amendment during the Carter administration. President Carter retained the NSC as the top organization for reviewing foreign intelligence and replaced the OAG with the NSC’s Special Coordination Committee (SCC) under EO 11985 (May 13, 1977), continuing the former OAG’s procedures and membership (with additional observers). The SCC for covert action and sensitive surveillance became known as SCC-Intelligence (SCC–I), and EO 12036 (Jan. 24, 1978) reaffirmed this structure, making the Attorney General and OMB Director full members. The SCC–I formed the Special Activities Working Group (SAWG) to review proposals, which later declined in use. By late 1979, interagency debates and guidance were handled by a group chaired by Aaron under several names. The Carter administration also used “world-wide” or “general” covert operation findings supported by “Perspectives” documents that set themes and guidance; riskier operations required separate presidential findings or Memorandums of Notification, with Perspectives drafted by the CIA and cleared by the Department of State.

Avoyelles Parish is projected to spend about $8,123 per student in 2017-18 state and local revenues, with only Acadia spending less ($8,053) among Louisiana’s 69 public districts. Avoyelles’ local revenues are $2,102 per student (68th of 69), while Washington Parish spends $1,519 in local revenues per child. Bogalusa School District is projected to spend the most per student at $11,546, while the state average is $9,015, up slightly from $8,965 the prior year but below 2015’s $10,888. The Minimum Foundation Program uses a starting minimum allocation of $3,961 per student and applies a formula that considers local property and sales tax capacity, aiming for a 35% local and 65% state split; Avoyelles is approximately 25.85% local and 74.15% state. The formula also includes funds for several student and program categories, plus adjustments for 2016 flood-affected parishes and small districts, and the passage notes that MFP funding has no clear relationship to operating costs. A Senate resolution urged the Board of Elementary & Secondary Education to have its MFP Task Force determine the actual cost of education in Louisiana and report findings by Feb. 1, 2018.

The passage previews Super Bowl LII weekend, with the New England Patriots playing the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday evening in Minneapolis. It encourages Steelers fans to root for the Eagles, announces a Sunday game thread and potential contests, and lists five “Friday night five questions” plus two bonus questions for readers. It also summarizes “Senior Bowl Week Friday Night Questions,” including results for several questions, and describes a leaderboard after Senior Bowl Week with Alan Tman leading at 48.5 points.

The passage lists ten late-breaking news and other stories: continued investigations into Russia after Flynn’s exit; a possible shift in Washington’s policy as Netanyahu visits; an arrest tied to Kim Jong Nam’s death; NATO talks in Brussels on defense issues; cracks found in California’s Oroville Dam spillway; a study on risky driving across all age groups; a Boeing vote related to southern unionization; high-tech produce labeling in Sweden using laser beams; Kate Upton appearing on Sports Illustrated’s cover; and a dog winning Westminster best in show after retirement.

New NASA research using advanced computer modeling and revisiting decades of data suggests Uranus emits about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, indicating the planet has internal heat. This revises earlier conclusions based heavily on a single Voyager 2 measurement that implied Uranus had no internal heat. The new models incorporate atmospheric details, including hazes, clouds, and seasonal changes, to better estimate Uranus’s energy balance. The findings may help explain Uranus’s history and provide clues about similar-size exoplanets, though Uranus is still far less warm than Neptune.
