The lecture introduces the purpose and structure of MIT 18.100A Real Analysis: gaining experience with proofs and proving statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. It defines basic set concepts (sets, empty set, membership, logic notation, subsets, equality, proper subsets) and gives examples of number sets (natural numbers, integers, rationals, real numbers) along with set operations (union, intersection, set difference, complement, disjointness). It then proves DeMorgan’s Laws for sets using subset inclusions. The lecture moves to mathematical induction, stating the well-ordering property and presenting induction as a theorem, then demonstrates proof by contradiction to establish the induction theorem. Finally, it provides two induction examples: a geometric-series identity for \(1+c+\cdots+c^n\) and an inequality \(1+c^n \ge 1+nc\) for \(c \ge -1\).

ERS/ATS guidelines define restriction by a TLC below the lower limit of normal and state that it cannot be established from spirometry alone, but that the absence of restriction can be predicted from a normal FVC. However, cited evidence shows lower negative predictive value (NPV) for the FVC lower limit of normal in diverse cohorts, especially among non-Hispanic Black patients, leading to under-recognition of restriction. To improve accuracy and equity, the authors developed and externally validated three machine learning (ML) models to predict restriction from spirometric, demographic, and anthropometric data and compared them with using the FVC lower limit of normal. In the validation dataset, the random forest model had an NPV of 88.3% versus 72.7% for the FVC lower limit of normal, and higher NPV for non-Hispanic Black versus non-Hispanic White patients (74.6% vs 90.9% for random forest; 49.5% vs 79.6% for FVC lower limit of normal). The study reports that ML models were more accurate and more equitable than the FVC approach for excluding restriction from spirometry.

The passage is a court decision in *G. M. Cox v. George W. Burnham* concerning an application for a liquor permit. It discusses how statutes regulating liquor permits should be construed and interprets Code sections governing permit applications, notice, remonstrances, and when hearings must occur. The court holds that an application is not automatically dismissed if it is not heard at the first term and that an adjournment does not ipso facto deprive the court of jurisdiction. The case facts state that P. H. Bell filed an application and notice in Benton county, a remonstrance was filed, and the hearing was eventually held at a later term; the court ordered that a permit issue. The proceedings are dismissed.

Tesla’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018 describes the company’s business and products, which include fully electric vehicles (Model S, Model X, and Model 3), energy generation and storage systems (Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2), and solar energy systems (including Solar Roof). It outlines the company’s sales and service network, charging infrastructure (Superchargers and Destination Chargers), manufacturing locations and facilities (including Gigafactory 1 and planned Gigafactory Shanghai), and regulatory and incentive matters affecting vehicles, energy storage, and solar. The document also discusses competition, intellectual property, employee count, information availability, and multiple risk factors, including potential delays and complications in vehicle and product ramp, dependence on suppliers, regulatory uncertainty, and risks related to scaling manufacturing and operations globally.

Asian stocks were weak on Wednesday as the Chinese yuan stayed near 11-month lows, with investors concerned about a potential Sino-U.S. trade war before an end-of-week U.S. tariff deadline. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index edged up 0.1% after a nine-month low, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5%. Wall Street fell on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 down 0.49% and the Nasdaq down 0.86%, as technology shares weakened and several major companies dropped. Facebook fell 2.3%, and Tesla fell 7.2% amid questions about Model 3 production; Micron dropped 5.5% after a competitor received a temporary injunction banning chip sales in mainland China, which also pressured other U.S. chipmakers and Japanese chip-related stocks. Many investors fear tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods will proceed on July 6, while Beijing plans to respond with matching tariffs. In currencies, the yuan traded at 6.6715 per dollar after hitting a 11-month low on Tuesday, and other major currencies were largely steady. Oil prices rose as U.S. stockpile data eased supply-shortage worries, while copper reached nine-month lows due to concerns that trade frictions could slow global growth.

The passage describes a monthly process for identifying “best all-around” CCC stocks from David Fish’s January 2017 “All CCC” list (excluding REITs and MLPs). It uses the Dugan Stock Scoring System to score overall stock quality, then applies additional filters valued for SA readers: top-half Dugan score, minimum 2.25% yield, at least $5B market cap, relative Graham number of 70 or less, payout ratio of 70 or less, most recent dividend increase of at least 5%, EPS growth estimates of at least 5% for next year and at least 5%/year for the next five years, debt/equity of 1 or less, and minimum Dugan Score of 50. The Dugan system evaluates CCC stocks using criteria across four categories—Risk, Value, Past Performance, and Future Performance Expectations—and produces a balanced, holistic score based on current condition and expected future performance. After scoring, a small broker-based bonus or penalty is applied based on sector weightings. Using the 2017 system and the stated filters, the author reports 21 companies as the highest scoring, filtered January 2017 CCC companies, followed by a discussion disclaimer and disclosures.

East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust has been told by the CQC Chief Inspector of Hospitals to make improvements after being rated “Requires Improvement” overall. In a March inspection, it was rated “Outstanding” for caring and “Requires Improvement” for safety, effectiveness, well-led and responsive services. The CQC said some progress had been made on safeguarding, staff understanding of the Mental Capacity Act, and incident reporting, but the trust did not meet national ambulance response standards; winter delays contributed to serious incidents. The CQC also reported low staff morale, including frustration, disengagement between front line staff and senior management, and staff not always feeling valued. The trust said it was pleased improvements were recognised in some areas, particularly Patient Transport Services and Emergency Operations Centres handling and triaging 999 calls, and acknowledged further room for improvement, including improving emergency call performance and response times, consistent application of processes, reviewed risk registers, and better staff mentoring and support, with additional funding of £11.5m planned.

Temple Grandin, an internationally known speaker and author, will present “Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior” at a breakfast event from 7–9 a.m. Friday, Feb. 23 in the Tyler Jelly Building at the Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff. The event is sponsored by the Shasta College Ag Leadership Club and the University of California, Agriculture & Natural Resources Cooperative Extension for Shasta, Tehama, Glenn and Colusa counties. Grandin is a professor at Colorado State University known for work on animal behavior and livestock handling and is author of several books, including the New York Times bestseller “Animals in Translation.” Breakfast is $15 and will be prepared by Vic Woolery. For more information, contact Josh Davy at 527-3101 or jdavy@ucdavis.edu.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement in Montreal, replacing the 1997 agreement. The revised deal removes duties for thousands of additional products, including fresh fruit and canned goods, and includes dedicated chapters on labor, the environment, trade and gender, small and medium-sized enterprises, and corporate social responsibility, with changes to make dispute settlement more efficient, effective, and transparent. Canada’s trade ministry said the modernization reflects strong economic, cultural, and social ties. The agreement will take effect after ratification by both countries’ parliaments, with a stated goal to double the scope of trade.

The passage is part of Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 30, 2019, including table-of-contents information, condensed consolidated financial statements (statements of operations, comprehensive income, balance sheets, shareholders’ equity, and cash flows), and accompanying notes. It reports net sales of $58,015 million for the three months ended March 30, 2019 and net income of $11,561 million, with total assets of $341,998 million and total liabilities of $236,138 million as of March 30, 2019. Notes describe significant accounting policies and recent accounting pronouncements, revenue recognition (including performance obligations for iPhone/Mac/iPad and bundled services), financial instruments (marketable securities and derivatives/hedging), deferred revenue, income taxes and uncertain tax positions, debt and commercial paper, share repurchases, comprehensive income components, commitments and contingencies, segment and geographic data, and forward-looking statements and investor information.

The passage says real-time ray tracing is now available in single-GPU systems using NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture. Turing introduces dedicated RT Cores to perform ray tracing efficiently, supported by NVIDIA RTX software technology and filtering algorithms, enabling real-time rendering with photorealistic objects and physically accurate shadows, reflections, and refractions. It also notes that Microsoft announced DirectML for AI and DirectX Raytracing (DXR) APIs in early 2018, enabling game developers to deploy real-time AI and ray tracing. The passage further describes new advanced shading features, CUDA enhancements inherited from Volta (including independent thread scheduling and hardware-accelerated MPS with address space isolation), and that several GeForce and Quadro products will use Turing GPUs. It focuses on the flagship TU102 Turing GPU, shipping in GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000, with additional technical details in appendices.

The passage describes a study that conducts a meta-analysis of research on the effectiveness of AI-related technologies in education. It explains that AI in education includes applications such as intelligent tutoring systems, chatbots, virtual reality, and learning management systems, and that AI use has evolved through three paradigms: AI-directed learning, AI-supported learning, and AI-engaged learning. The study follows PRISMA guidelines and searches English-language peer-reviewed journal articles or conference papers from January 2015 to July 2024 using databases including Google Scholar, ERIC, and Scopus, applying inclusion and exclusion criteria that require empirical data with sufficient statistics.

The meta-analysis includes 13 studies from eight countries and reports a generally positive overall effect of AI technologies on educational outcomes (overall effect size 0.86, p < 0.0001, 95% CI [0.45, 1.27]), along with significant findings for chatbots and generative AI (effect size 1.02, p < 0.0001, 95% CI [0.45, 1.59]). It also reports positive effects for learning management systems and AI platforms (effect size 0.62) and indicates that online learning and virtual reality have certain application effects (effect size 0.79, P < 0.07, 95% CI [-0.04, 1.62]). The passage notes substantial heterogeneity across studies (I² reported as 54.03% to 93.23%) and publication bias. The conclusion emphasizes that AI can positively affect educational outcomes but that effectiveness varies by context, and calls for continued research and careful implementation.

In the UK, cold and flu spread more easily as temperatures fall, and the passage says food choices can help provide nutrients and energy to support recovery and immune function. It emphasizes eating a variety of fruit and vegetables (including eating “the rainbow”) for vitamins, minerals, fibers (prebiotics), and nutrients such as vitamins A and C and minerals like magnesium and zinc. It also highlights sufficient protein for growth, repair, and immune defenses, herbs and spices (such as ginger and turmeric) for anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial compounds, and probiotics from fermented foods to support gut and immune activity. Nuts and seeds are described as nutrient-dense sources of minerals, fatty acids, and vitamin E for cell repair, and the passage lists these food groups as easily incorporated into daily diets to benefit health.

A Danish study of 4,741 mothers found that children of older women had fewer behavioural, social and emotional difficulties at ages seven and 11, but not at age 15. Older mothers worried less during pregnancy, were more positive about becoming parents, had more positive attitudes toward their children, and were more likely to be in stable relationships and to be better educated and better off. The researchers attributed these findings to “psychological maturity,” which they said made mothers more tolerant and emotionally stable and led them to scold and discipline children less. The study also reported that while average pregnancy age in Denmark is 30.9 and mothers over 40 have increased since 1985, later motherhood carries physical risks such as miscarriage, premature birth and birth defects, so both physical and psychosocial pros and cons should be considered.

Fredrik had X-rays and a report was expected by the end of the day. After returning, the speaker said he finished the game despite missing a couple of shifts. The team felt they had a poor start, especially in passing, which led to many turnovers that stopped their offense without much damage. They discussed Carolina’s line chemistry and defensive strength, saying it provided space and time but the team didn’t take good shots, including issues on power plays (using onetimers from angles they didn’t pursue often). The speaker emphasized focusing on even-ing up the series rather than relying on past history. They also attributed the loss partly to referee tendencies to call penalties and to power-play/penalty-kill ice-time imbalance, saying scoring chances and possession were limited to under ten minutes for some key players. Additional adjustments discussed included improving zone entry (getting the puck deeper), changing the forecheck to avoid being over-anxious, and correcting puck placement and neutral-zone play.

Scientists created functional human egg cells by fusing human skin cells with an empty egg and coaxing the resulting cells to expel half their chromosomes through meiosis. The proof-of-concept could one day help infertile people have children by allowing the eggs to form early embryos.

The passage says Niu Technologies’ stock has gained significantly in 2025, helped by strong recent growth, but that growth may not continue. It notes that disruptions could affect the expected growth already priced into the stock and that growth may not arrive quickly enough to justify the rally and valuations. The author therefore gives NIU a neutral outlook with a hold rating.

The passage describes the growing popularity of “Russian math” programs in the United States, including the Russian School of Mathematics, which has about 22,000 students and 15 branches in Massachusetts and 40 nationwide. Parents and students say the classes are more challenging than school math and help develop deeper understanding, reasoning, and early algebra and geometry rather than memorization. The program’s rise is linked to dissatisfaction with American math education and to “keeping up with the Joneses,” which some experts compare to an “arms race” of after-school instruction. The story traces the school’s roots to Russian immigration after the Cold War and to co-founder Inessa Rifkin’s experience finding her son lacked expected math knowledge. It also outlines challenges for American schools, including students already covering topics before class, overconfidence, potential widening of gaps between families who can afford the roughly $2,000-a-year tuition and those who cannot, and added pressure on parents.

The passage describes CAR T cell therapies intended to improve therapeutic efficacy by disrupting methylcytosine dioxygenase genes, specifically Tet1, Tet2, and/or Tet3. It states that reducing or eliminating expression and/or function of these genes (including Tet2) in engineered CAR-expressing immune effector cells decreases 5-hydroxymethylcytosine and is associated, in the described theory, with enhanced CAR T cell proliferation, effector cytokine production, and degranulation. The CARs are described as having an antigen-binding domain, transmembrane domain, and intracellular signaling domain, with examples including CD19-binding CARs. The passage further outlines methods of increasing CAR-expressing cell efficacy by decreasing 5-hydroxymethylcytosine via contacting cells with Tet inhibitors (including gene editing, siRNA/shRNA, proteins such as dominant negative variants, and small molecules), including pre-, concurrent, or post-treatment timing relative to CAR cell therapy. It also includes manufacturing and treatment-use descriptions, potential target diseases and cancers, and extensive experimental and drawing descriptions related to Tet2 disruption and CAR insertion, including analysis of insertion sites, transcript effects, methylation-related measurements, and phenotypic changes such as Tscm expansion.

The passage reports a Mendelian randomization study assessing whether genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) causally affects cardiovascular disease (CVD) risks and whether hypertension mediates these effects. It states that this was the first such study to detect a potential causal relationship between genetically determined PAT and multiple CVD risks and to confirm hypertension’s mediating role. The study found PAT was associated with higher risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism, while evidence for several other CVD outcomes was limited. Sensitivity analyses supported robustness, and a 2-step mediation MR indicated hypertension mediated proportions for several outcomes including heart failure, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, and ischemic stroke. The passage concludes that PAT may serve as a potential therapeutic target, with antihypertensive strategies potentially providing cardiovascular benefits, especially for people with obesity. It also notes limitations, including lack of multivariable MR due to missing PAT GWAS data, European-only participants, possible sample overlap, and smaller case counts for some outcomes.

The passage is a discussion with Coach DeBoer about the team’s situation in the finals. He says the team has been in similar spots before and that success comes from getting the first win and then building momentum with successive wins. He discusses lineup change considerations, emphasizing that changes are not made just because a game was lost, and describes a process of watching tape after games to determine who should go in or out. He credits opponents and their goaltender for making key saves and notes that the team has created quality chances without finishing, including power-play opportunities and several near-goals. Coach DeBoer also comments on travel and schedule disruptions, officiating and disciplined play, and a call that he believes was significant. He maintains confidence, says the team played hard to the final buzzer, and argues that the main issue is scoring more goals.

Indian troops killed three youth—Umar Majid Sheikh, Adil Malik, and Irfan Sheikh—in Shopian district during a siege and search operation in the Awneera area. The operation, which began yesterday, involved blasting a mosque and four residential houses, and led to protests where many civilians were injured by pellet firing. Twelve injured youth were admitted to Zainapora hospital, and two other injured people were taken to Srinagar. Locals said troops ransacked houses in Awneera, Zainapora, and nearby areas. Earlier, two Indian soldiers were killed and several others injured in an attack on forces involved in the Awneera operation. In Bandipora district, three troops were injured when a patrol party was attacked in Hajin area. Trains between Badgam and Srinagar and between Islamabad and Banihal remained suspended for a second day. Joint resistance leaders Syed Ali Gilani, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, and Muhammad Yasin Malik opposed attempts to undermine Jammu and Kashmir’s disputed nature or change its demographic character, saying India was using all means to crush the liberation movement. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said the BJP and RSS were working to end Jammu and Kashmir’s special status by challenging Article 35A in the Indian Supreme Court. A civilian, Imtiyaz Ahmad Mir, injured in an explosion in Dalgate area of Srinagar, died at Soura hospital.

The passage discusses sexual harassment and exploitation in universities and other workplaces as a widespread issue in society. It says that after investigation, professor Richard Akindele was found guilty of illegally soliciting sex from a student and was dismissed by the university council. The passage commends OAU for handling the matter promptly and urges other universities to emulate its response. It argues that justice in sexual abuse cases would deter other lecturers, calls for measures to expose and punish such behavior, and advises female students to avoid luring lecturers into sexual temptations.

The passage is a collection of Enron-related news items and commentary dated June 4, 2001. It includes claims that U.S. adviser Karl Rove owned stock in companies such as Enron and that other officials had financial ties to energy firms. It also reports on Saudi Arabia signing agreements with nine oil companies to develop natural gas fields and related projects worth at least $25 billion. Several entries focus on Enron’s financial and contractual disputes internationally, including efforts by lenders to resolve the Dabhol Power project in India and disputes involving utilities and power purchasing. Other items cover energy market developments in the UK and Japan, as well as Reuters reports about India’s sovereign rating outlook and currency/market reactions.

The passage discusses playoff mindset and preparation for an upcoming game, emphasizing matching the intensity seen on TV and feeding off crowd energy by trying to get on opponents early. It notes motivation at this time of year, expectations of the other team’s best effort, and the advantage of having a day off to practice and adjust details. It also highlights the importance of being aware of factors like playing with more jump early on, executing patiently, winning faceoffs, avoiding mistakes, and making plays when opportunities arise. The passage mentions dealing with injuries for both teams, readiness of replacements, and a focus on staying on one’s own game rather than looking ahead. It references recent play where being “on our toes” and more aggressive led to more chances, and describes a specific player as intense and passionate, willing to take on different roles, doing small non-statistical things, and helping teammates with subtle details.

Alfie Evans’ father, Tom Evans, said outside Alder Hey Children’s Hospital that his 23-month-old son was still breathing unassisted nine hours after life support was supposedly turned off. He claimed doctors had initially refused to provide oxygen, but later re-intervened after he said the situation was becoming “unlawful,” and Alfie was given oxygen and water. Tom said Alfie needed some form of life support within a couple of hours and that doctors and others were “gobsmacked” by his continued breathing. Alfie’s mother, Kate, posted on Facebook that Alfie had been allowed oxygen and water.

The passage describes an unbiased metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow intended for faster, lower-cost infectious disease diagnosis. It contrasts conventional pathogen-specific methods with mNGS, noting that existing approaches face limitations including multi-day processing time and high cost due to deep sequencing needs for human-background samples. To address this, the authors developed HostEL (human background depletion that also enriches viruses) and AmpRE (a single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation). The combined workflow aims to reduce processing time and enable shallow sequencing while maintaining pathogen signal. Analytical validation used human plasma spiked with microbial standards at multiple concentrations, including detection down to 70,000 cells/mL, with high sensitivity and specificity on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq. Clinical validation on 42 patient plasma samples showed 93% agreement with qPCR/clinical molecular results, and both DNA and RNA viruses were detected. The passage also describes data analysis steps, sample collection and ethics approval, qPCR methods, and discussion of portability across sequencing platforms and the potential for next-day turnaround.

Sal Diaz, a Mission Hope Cancer Center patient in Santa Maria, previously lacked reliable family transportation for 4- to 6-hour chemotherapy sessions and had to barter for rides. To address this, Cruzin’ for Life raised money to retrofit a wheelchair-accessible transport van. Now in its second year, the van has transported more than 2,600 cancer patients and logged over 34,000 miles across several nearby communities. Cruzin’ for Life, a Santa Maria nonprofit founded in 2003, continues operating the van through its Valentine’s Day crab feed and related events, which have raised funds including $32,000 last year. The van was funded with a $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy. Mission Hope’s staff report the facility is full all the time and the van is needed so patients do not miss treatment, with patients calling directly or staff recommending it based on need.

A woman in South Africa was declared dead by paramedics after a car crash near Carletonville on June 24, but was later found alive in a mortuary refrigerator. Emergency services said mortuary technicians discovered her several hours after the crash when she had shown no signs of life during initial checks (breathing and pulse). The ambulance service Distress Alert launched an investigation, and officials said procedures were followed and they were devastated by the outcome.

The 2025–26 season is Jim Montgomery’s first full year as head coach of the St. Louis Blues after taking over mid-season and leading the team to the first round of the playoffs. Known for structured systems and strong special teams, Montgomery aims to help the Blues return to playoff contention. The Blues open at home on Oct. 9, with seven of their first 11 games at Enterprise Center, and they face a rivalry game on Oct. 18. The schedule includes Central Division battles in April against Colorado, Winnipeg, Chicago, and Minnesota, and a season finale in Utah on April 16. The season pauses for the Winter Olympics from Feb. 5–25, after which March and April are described as packed with crucial games. The roster includes veteran leadership and young talent, with questions about defensive consistency, young forwards’ development, and how quickly Montgomery’s style translates against Central Division opponents.

San Juan mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called Tuesday’s new death toll estimates after Hurricane Maria “a day of collective mourning,” saying the total death toll was not correct and that the government was not telling the truth. Researchers from Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health estimated 4,645 “excess deaths” between Sept. 20 and Dec. 31, with a margin of error of plus or minus 3,852; they said the likely figure is about 5,000. Puerto Rico’s official government death toll is currently 64. Cruz, who has criticized the Trump administration, said Trump did not apologize for lives lost and warned that Puerto Rico is not equipped to handle another Atlantic hurricane season.

The passage describes a backtest of the end-of-month effect in NIFTY 50, using data from Yahoo!finance (starting in 2007). The results suggest NIFTY 50 has a positive end-of-month effect that is reasonably robust to input variations. The strategy is based on trading days (not calendar days): it goes long at the close of the fifth last trading day of the month and sells at the close of the second trading day of the new month. Based on investing 100,000 at the start and compounding until today, the strategy shows a CAGR of 10.5%, outperforms buy and hold despite 30% market exposure, and has a maximum drawdown of 26%. The passage also states the effect is comparable to the turn-of-the-month effect observed in the US stock market.

Celtic are set to build the biggest points gap over Rangers in 91 years, with a 19-point difference approaching the winter break and Celtic having a game in hand. Brendan Rodgers led Celtic to a 2-1 come-from-behind win at Ibrox. The passage compares this disparity to past seasons, noting that in 1925-26 Celtic won the title ahead of Airdrie by 58 points, while Rangers finished sixth with 44 points. It adds that the record may be surpassed if Celtic wins their game in hand, and it references Rangers’ 1985-86 season where they finished fifth, 15 points behind Celtic, after a late-season collapse.

The passage introduces drama in education as a strategy that helps students explore individual and social problems, express themselves in a safe story context, and develop reflective thinking, reasoning, creativity, and interpersonal skills. It outlines a study that reviews literature on connections between drama and STEAM education and includes a pilot qualitative case study using participant observations and researchers’ reflections. Two research questions address higher education students’ views of dramatic activities in science or history classes and what students can achieve in STEAM when engaging in dramatic activities. The literature review discusses arts-based educational approaches and drama-based pedagogy’s reported effects on achievement and skills, and explains how STEAM aims to connect academic content with real-world practice through authentic, interdisciplinary, and collaborative teaching.  

In the pilot, 19 first-year university students at ELTE University in Budapest (all women) participated in two activities: “The Life Cycle of a Butterfly” (group movement/dance after a presentation) and “Indian Caste System” (group sketches and an improvised or scripted scene based on provided materials). Students reflected on their personal understanding and feelings after the activities. Findings from field notes and reflections highlight increased creativity, collaboration, improvisation/problem-solving, motivation and involvement, and varied performances. The conclusion states that drama in STEAM can make learning enjoyable, increase motivation and confidence, and support concentration and language skills, while also presenting challenges such as time, lack of experience/confidence, and uneven student participation. The authors note limitations including the small sample size and narrow demographics, recommending caution and further research.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle system in which multiple independent control systems provide redundancy and independent bypass or failsafe responses for critical safety situations. Examples include an autonomous control system that normally uses multiple sensors to determine vehicle actions and signal control parameters to vehicle interfaces, and one or more auxiliary/bypass control units that operate independently to detect predefined conditions or events and implement predetermined vehicle responses using preselected vehicle interfaces. Auxiliary control units may also perform trajectory verification by processing current and future planned trajectory data from the primary system, generating a vehicle response output that can be communicated back to the autonomous control system to verify, supersede, or weight planned trajectories. The passage also outlines sensor and vehicle interface components, confidence/threshold-based event determination and remote assistance for low-confidence events, and ways for auxiliary outputs to prioritize over autonomous control commands, including direct emergency control to vehicle mechanisms and operation during primary system malfunctions. It further provides an autonomous vehicle example and a method for operating the system, including continuous monitoring by auxiliary units, generating vehicle response outputs based on sensed events or detected primary-system failures, and either bypassing autonomous commands or providing outputs for trajectory verification.

TrackR has announced updates and new products ahead of CES, including the TrackR pixel, a cheaper, colorful GPS Bluetooth tracker for items like key rings. It uses an iPhone/Android app with a GPS locator and a “crowd GPS network” for rediscovery when out of range. The TrackR wallet has been updated to version 2.0 with a credit-card-like design and similar close-range Bluetooth tracking and long-range crowd-sourced discovery, including replaceable batteries lasting about a year. TrackR also introduced the TrackR atlas, a smart plug that maps a home to pinpoint connected TrackR devices by room and supports Amazon Alexa. Pricing is $24.99 for the pixel, $29.99 for the wallet, and $39.99 for the atlas, with only the atlas available for pre-order and all expected to launch in spring.

The passage explains that lightning can strike regardless of conditions like metal or sunshine and highlights five common myths. It says lightning is not attracted to metal objects, that car tires don’t provide protection while the metal body can conduct lightning to the ground, that lightning can strike up to 10 miles from a thunderstorm even when it’s sunny, that lightning can strike the same place repeatedly—especially tall, isolated objects—and that taking shelter under a tree is dangerous because trees are tall and pointy. It also notes that beliefs about golfers being most affected are myths and that many people killed during leisure activities are on or near water.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 8-K dated May 2, 2016 reports that NVIDIA and Samsung agreed to settle all pending intellectual property litigation. The settlement provides for the immediate dismissal of all pending IP litigation in U.S. district courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent Office between the companies. It also includes licensing a small number of patents by each company to the other, with no broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

The passage contains extensive excerpts from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021, including general descriptions of the company, its business segments (North America, International, and Amazon Web Services), executive officers and directors, and a broad set of risk factors. It describes competitive pressures across retail and services, risks related to international operations, fluctuations in results, fraud involving sellers, intellectual property claims, foreign exchange risk, fulfillment and data center optimization, data security, system interruptions, personnel retention, supplier and commercial agreement risks, acquisition/investment risks, inventory and payments-related risks, stock price volatility, and evolving government and regulatory matters (including litigation and tax risks). It also includes information on properties and liquidity/capital resources, such as cash flows for 2020 and 2021, major sources of liquidity, cash and securities balances, and capital expenditure amounts.

Prostate cancer is a leading cause of non-cutaneous cancer deaths in men worldwide, and risk stratification is needed to identify patients who may benefit from more aggressive treatment. The NCCN risk grouping is widely used but has suboptimal prognostic performance, while tissue-based genomic/pathologic classifiers face limited adoption and biopsy-based information may be affected by sampling error. The study uses deep learning on multiparametric prostate MRI to develop and externally validate two imaging biomarkers—extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI)—to aid risk stratification of localized prostate cancer.

Two deep learning models were trained using 820 biopsy-proven prostate cancer patients treated at Yale (612 training/internal test, 208 internal test). Ground-truth labels for EPE and SVI were based on pathology and radiology reports, with validation by board-certified clinicians. External validation used two held-out datasets: 65 patients from non-academic community settings and 41 patients from the NCI-ISBI Prostate Diagnosis Challenge (Prostate-Dx). BCR was assessed as a secondary outcome. EPE and SVI ground-truth labels were associated with increased biochemical recurrence, and in Cox proportional hazards models EPE and SVI remained significant predictors of BCR.

The EPE model achieved AUCs of 0.719 on the Yale test set and 0.743 and 0.611 on the community hospital and Prostate-Dx datasets, respectively. The SVI model achieved AUCs of 0.724 on the Yale test set and 0.678 and 0.775 on the community hospital and Prostate-Dx datasets, respectively. Patients classified as EPE+ or SVI+ had lower 5-year biochemical recurrence-free survival across training and test sets, and combined EPE/SVI biomarkers showed improved prognostic performance compared with either biomarker alone. The combined biomarker also stratified risk in Gleason 7–10 groups and demonstrated utility even among patients without pathologic EPE or SVI on final pathology.

Interpretability analyses (Grad-CAM, hierarchical clustering, and dimensionality reduction) were used to support that model predictions relate to relevant imaging regions and features. Integrating the imaging biomarkers into NCCN risk groups resulted in reclassification of 26.4% of patients and improved discriminatory ability for predicting BCR compared with NCCN and UCSF-CAPRA alone. The study concludes that externally validated deep learning algorithms can identify EPE and SVI on MRI and improve risk stratification for localized prostate cancer.

The passage is part of Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015. It includes the company’s general business description, vision and strategy for a mobile-first, cloud-first world, key offerings across consumer and commercial segments, operating segments and competition, operations and research and development information, distribution and licensing options, executive officers and employee counts, and risk factors. The risk factors cover competition, platform and ecosystem dynamics, execution and profitability risks related to cloud services and new investments, intellectual property protection, cyber-attacks and security vulnerabilities, regulatory and legal risks, talent retention, litigation and tax risks, quality and supply risks for hardware and software, and broader operational risks including international exposure and catastrophic events.

The passage describes multiple reset sources and reset behaviors, including software-controlled Software Global Warm Reset, test reset via the TRST pin, reset priority rules, and reset isolation for PCI Express and the Ethernet Switch (EMAC Switch) using an ISO_CONTROL bit. It also explains the RSTOUT_WD_OUT pin behavior, reset effects on module resets and pin states (e.g., Hi-Z behavior for most I/O pins except certain pins during specific reset modes), and warm/cold reset behavior during power domain switching. Additionally, it provides detailed clocking and timing requirements for reset-related signals and discusses device clock inputs (DEV/AUX clocks), SERDES clocking for PCIe PHY, and general clock source/output selection.

The passage discusses Michael Flynn’s resignation and how it may affect President Trump and possible impeachment. It says Flynn had talked about U.S. sanctions against Russia with Russia’s ambassador before Trump took office, and that some officials knew about these discussions but kept them from the public until leaks. It describes concerns that Flynn could be vulnerable to blackmail due to the Russians knowing what he did, and mentions that Acting Attorney General Sally Yates informed White House Counsel Donald McGahn while Vice President Pence defended Flynn earlier. It includes Trump’s statements criticizing “illegal leaks” and dismissing “Russian” connections, while pundits suggest Trump may be deflecting attention. The passage also notes that investigations could lead to Senate hearings and that Flynn’s conversations occurred before inauguration, potentially limiting executive privilege, and it suggests White House counsel could still be involved.

The passage describes the NBA “Power” offense, which is used by almost every team to free up outstanding shooters by running them off baseline and down screens. It explains the basic action in phases: shooters cross under the basket to initiate the play, then curl off baseline down screens, with reads and counters for various defensive responses (e.g., chasing, cheating over screens, switching). It also covers post mismatches created when defenses switch, options for offensive rebounding, and automatic counters based on defensive anticipation. The offense can transition into different continuities such as Motion, Side Screen, Drive & Kick, and Triangle Post, and it includes a “Single/Double” variation for shooter options off baseline screens. The passage concludes with teaching and implementing guidance, including coordination of screening and post actions, practice drills, scouting and game strategy, and the need to learn how to defend the Power offense even if it is not used.

The passage reports that in an annual message to Congress the speaker reviewed a boundary controversy between Great Britain and Venezuela and proposed that it be settled by arbitration, asking whether Great Britain would submit. The British Government’s reply, received with its dispatch, included communications from the British prime minister to the British ambassador, Sir Julian Pauncefote, including one addressing the Monroe doctrine. The speaker argues that the Monroe doctrine remains strong and applicable and contends that if a European power extends its boundaries into neighboring republic territory, it effectively extends its system of government to part of the continent. The speaker also addresses the claim that the Monroe doctrine is not a recognized principle of international law, asserting that nations are entitled to rights and that international law can consider enforcement of the Monroe doctrine as part of its code. The speaker notes that the United States proposed arbitration, which Great Britain declined on grounds deemed unsatisfactory, and concludes that the United States must accept the situation and act accordingly. The speaker recommends that Congress appropriate funds for a commission to be appointed by the Executive to investigate and determine the true boundary line between Venezuela and British Guiana with careful, judicial consideration of evidence. After acceptance of the commission’s report, the speaker recommends that the United States resist, by every means possible, any British appropriation of lands or exercise of jurisdiction over territory determined to belong to Venezuela, and acknowledges the responsibility and consequences involved.

On June 3, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc to issue and sell ¥250,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 0.350% Notes due 2020. The Notes will be issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 and an officer’s certificate dated June 10, 2015, and are registered under Apple’s Form S-3 Registration Statement filed April 29, 2013. Interest will be payable semi-annually on June 10 and December 10 each year beginning December 10, 2015, and on June 10, 2020. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The underwriting agreement and officer’s certificate are attached as Exhibits 1.1 and 4.1 through 4.2, respectively, with the indenture filed as Exhibit 4.1 to the registration statement.

The passage is an excerpt from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2015. It includes the company’s SEC filing information, an index of financial statement and reporting items, and consolidated financial statements (cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets) along with accompanying notes covering accounting policies, cash and marketable securities (including fair value hierarchy), commitments and contingencies, acquisitions and goodwill, long-term debt, stockholders’ equity, income taxes, and segment information. It also presents management’s discussion of forward-looking statements, critical accounting judgments, liquidity and capital resources, and results of operations, including net sales, segment operating income, operating expenses, shipping activity, and interest, other income/expense, and income tax discussion.

Ruston, a top Louisiana team, travels to Stephenville, Texas, for a midseason interstate high school football matchup. Stephenville’s Bearcats are 4-0 and ranked No. 2 in the Sporting News Louisiana Top 25 and No. 25 in the Sporting News Texas Top 25. Last year, Ruston defeated Stephenville’s Yellow Jackets 63-17. The passage also notes live updates, including a fumble by Dalen Powell on Ruston’s second drive leading to a 19-yard touchdown pass from Trot Jordan to Jhett Banuelos. Ruston improved to 4-0 with a 49-21 win over Midland Legacy, with Powell totaling 686 rushing yards and eight touchdowns for the season. Stephenville is 5-0 after beating Waco La Vega 64-28, led by quarterback Trot Jordan with 996 passing yards and 13 touchdowns, and Zyler McClendon with 664 rushing yards and nine touchdowns.

The passage describes the start of the U.S. Supreme Court’s October 2025 term and summarizes activity on the Court’s emergency docket during the summer involving actions by President Donald Trump. It notes that the Court allowed several Trump administration actions, largely through 6–3 “shadow docket” rulings that reversed lower courts and included strong dissents from the liberal justices.  

It then outlines major cases for the term, including challenges to Trump’s use of presidential powers. These include whether the International Emergency Economic Powers Act authorizes imposing tariffs, whether Congress may limit the president’s authority to fire agency heads, and whether to overrule older precedent related to removal of FTC commissioners. The passage also discusses the government’s request that the Court decide the constitutionality of an executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which federal courts have declared unconstitutional.  

Another major case addressed involves Louisiana’s redistricting and the constitutionality of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act under the 14th and 15th Amendments, specifically regarding racially disparate impact and consideration of race. The passage also mentions cases involving social issues such as conversion therapy laws and restrictions on transgender athletes, and a criminal case about Fourth Amendment emergency-entry rules and whether probable cause is required. It concludes that the term is expected to produce rulings with “profound effect” on law and American society.

Last week in Northeast Mississippi, highlights included: Karmel Davis, a Parkway Elementary parent, was named Tupelo Public School District’s 2017 Parent of the Year for contributions to the school and district, and she received the award as only the second Parkway parent to be honored. Corey Crayton received keys to a dream home built by Northeast Mississippi Habitat for Humanity and funded by HomeStretch Furniture, where she partnered with Habitat three years ago and will move into the three-bedroom house in coming weeks. Noah Barbieri, a Millsaps College junior and Belden native, was named a Truman Scholar, one of 62 students in the U.S. receiving the scholarship, which provides $30,000 for graduate school and professional development; he plans to pursue a doctorate in economics.

The Department of Homeland Security proposed changing the “duration of status” policy, which currently lets international students stay in the U.S. until their course of study is complete. Commenters—including higher education, hospitals, and private sector leaders—said the rule would unnecessarily restrict students already monitored by government and schools, and could harm the health-care system and employers. The proposal would cap stays at four years, allow extensions from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, and bar major changes or transfers between U.S. institutions. DHS said the goal is to reduce overstay rates, but NAFSA and others argued DHS overestimates overstay and that monitoring already alerts ICE when students overstay. The comment period ended Sept. 29, and DHS must review over 15,700 comments before deciding whether to end duration of status. Commenters cited reasons students may need more than four years, potential effects on graduate research and long-term clinical trials, and costs and staffing needs tied to extension applications.

Enron Corp. disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information as part of an informal inquiry into Enron’s related-party transactions, including partnerships run by its chief financial officer, Andrew Fastow. After the announcement and related disclosures, Enron’s stock fell more than 20% to about $20.65, following a previously announced $1.01 billion write-off and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to terminating certain partnership-related financing arrangements. Enron said it would cooperate fully with the SEC and maintained that its dealings with Fastow-related partnerships were proper and properly disclosed. The SEC request covers transactions involving partnerships such as LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, and investors and analysts raised concerns about asset valuation, potential dilution, and possible credit-rating triggers affecting other related financing vehicles. Multiple news outlets and analysts also discussed broader issues with Enron’s transparency and complex off-balance-sheet structures, alongside legal actions and planned investor communications.

The passage reports a qualitative study in Ankara that examines how bilingual early childhood teachers working in foreign-language private preschools and monolingual teachers working in state preschools view bilingualism and bilingual education. The study included 16 teachers and used phenomenology, semi-structured interviews, and content analysis to identify five themes: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children in monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and the impact of bilingualism on children’s development. Teachers generally agreed that bilingualism is an advantage, highlighting benefits such as self-confidence, communication skills, and career prospects, and they supported expanding bilingual schools in Turkey, despite acknowledging insufficient staffing and resources. They also emphasized the importance of parental support, though they differed on developmental needs and social outcomes for bilingual children. The study concludes that teachers lack sufficient training about how bilingual education programs should be implemented and recommends targeted professional development, better staffing and resources, and stronger support for parents.

The speaker says it was difficult to play hard in both games and then lose, especially when the team is in the finals. They plan to regroup and play better tomorrow night, noting that they have been in similar situations before. They describe a past game against Buffalo as different, and say they remain ready and excited with the opportunity ahead. They also state that both goalies played well, with one goal scored in six periods, and that success requires doing things differently. The speaker adds that the game went to overtime with no goals, that a small play will decide it, and that in any loss there are missed opportunities that they cannot dwell on.

The passage introduces STAT’s AI Prognosis newsletter and discusses how AI may affect intellectual property and drug patent disputes. It notes that the U.S. patent office stopped requiring physical invention models in 1880 and instead required diagrams. It then describes unresolved issues DeAnn Smith, a biotech patent lawyer, is interested in seeing addressed in future litigation, including whether AI can be an inventor and hold patents and what “a person skilled in the art” might know.

Lung cancer has a poor prognosis, partly due to limited early diagnosis, lack of screening, and advanced cases that often lack early symptoms. This review examines lung cancer screening methods worldwide, focusing on biomarker-based approaches and studies from the United States within the past 10 years, with screening observed in clinical settings and patients with primary lung cancer.  

Across 32 included articles, reported biomarker performance included volatile organic compounds (80% sensitivity/specificity), circulating tumor DNA (80% sensitivity/96% specificity), specific miRNAs with high sensitivity but low specificity, methylation markers with varying results in sputum versus serum, and imaging approaches such as Ga-Alfatide II scans (86% sensitivity/85% specificity). The discussion emphasizes preventative measures for modifiable risk factors, and future screening improvements using circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II CT/PET, while noting the need to further analyze diagnostic errors. The review also discusses broader screening and prevention concepts, U.S.-focused search criteria, and limitations related to sample size, biomarkers studied, and potential false positives/negatives.

The passage describes a study comparing three surveys of primary care physicians’ experiences with electronic health record (EHR) interoperability and related documentation practices: the 2021 CDC National Electronic Health Records Survey (NEHRS), the 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. The study notes that NEHRS has provided information on EHR adoption but has not been statistically compared with other sources, and that recent NEHRS response rates have been as low as 25%. In this analysis, the CCQ had a 100% response rate, NEHRS had an 18.2% response rate, and the UCSF survey had a 3.6% response rate. Results reported significant differences across surveys in physician demographics and practice settings, EHR platforms, and measures of EHR satisfaction and interoperability experiences. While the surveys commonly indicated limited interoperability and modest levels of EHR satisfaction, the passage emphasizes that survey composition and response bias likely contribute to differences in findings, and concludes that augmenting NEHRS with recertification-based data from certifying boards could improve reliability. Limitations include differences in survey questions and the CCQ’s focus on one primary care subspecialty (family medicine).

The passage reports a multi-centre, randomized controlled trial of PrAISED, a 12-month dementia-specific exercise and functional activity rehabilitation programme delivered at home and in communities. Based on participants with mild dementia or mild cognitive impairment, the primary outcome was carer-informant-rated disability in activities of daily living (DAD). The intervention was well received and delivered largely as intended, but there were no differences versus control in the primary DAD outcome and most secondary outcomes, including physical activity, quality of life, balance, functional mobility, cognition, falls, and other health status measures. The study found small, statistically uncertain reductions in falls and underpowered analyses suggested potential benefits in specific cognitive domains. The authors conclude that it is unlikely that exercise or functionally orientated rehabilitation can change the rate of functional loss in dementia and that wellbeing after diagnosis may need different definitions.

On August 17, Expedition 52 Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy of Roscosmos will conduct a spacewalk from the ISS Pirs airlock at about 10:45 am EDT. NASA says Ryazanskiy will manually deploy five nanosatellites from a ladder outside the airlock; the satellites will serve various purposes, including testing the effects of low-Earth-orbit conditions on 3-D printed materials, transmitting greetings in 11 languages, and commemorating milestones related to Sputnik 1 and Konstantin Tsiolkovsky. During the walk, the crew will collect residue samples outside the Russian segment and install handrails and struts. Yurchikhin will be EV1 (his ninth spacewalk), and Ryazanskiy will be EV2 (his fourth), both wearing Russian Orlan spacesuits with blue stripes. The spacewalk will be the 202nd for ISS assembly and maintenance support and the seventh this year.

The passage says Stenabolic (SR9009) is a synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand developed by Scripps Research Institute under Thomas Burris, taken orally to bind and activate the Rev-Erb protein. It claims SR9009 influences regulatory mechanisms including circadian rhythms, lipid and glucose metabolism, fat-storing cells, and macrophages, leading to increased fat loss and endurance. It describes effects such as increased mitochondria in muscle, improved metabolism and endurance, removal of defective mitochondria, higher resting energy expenditure (5%), reduced fat storage and liver cholesterol production, and improved burning of fat and glucose. The passage also reports study findings including reductions in plasma triglycerides (12%), total cholesterol (47%), plasma non-esterified fatty acids (23%), plasma glucose (19%), plasma insulin (35%), and proinflammatory cytokine IL-6 (72%).

The court granted Garlock’s motion for summary judgment and dismissed Steven C. Gittens, Sr.’s ADA disability discrimination complaint with prejudice. The court found Gittens failed to respond to the summary judgment motion and ignored court orders, warranting dismissal under Rules 41(b) and 16(f). It also held that Gittens failed to establish a prima facie case of disability under the ADA, concluding his lifting restriction did not substantially limit major life activities and that he remained employed. Even assuming a prima facie case, the court found Garlock articulated legitimate, non-discriminatory reasons for reassignment and that there was no evidence of pretext.

The passage argues for sure, swift justice under the law rather than mob violence, noting that people cannot permanently rise by mistreating others, including through preventing education. It says public schooling is central to political well-being and should be available, citing that lack of education correlates with brutal crimes such as rape, while industrial education like that from Hampton and Tuskegee is presented as producing few criminals and reducing lynch-law-type violence. It also warns that inflammatory speeches and writings that arouse mobs increase the likelihood of repeated crime through “suggestion” and by fueling racial hatred. The passage further criticizes demagogues who preach discontent and hatred toward the wealthy, claiming such agitation loosens moral restraints, leads to corruption, provokes violent reactions, and undermines genuine reform. It concludes that success requires a resolute, fearless, sane approach, rejecting demagogues who inflame passions and exploiting greed.

The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District announced plans to finalize controversial high school boundary changes. It will form three focus groups to provide input to trustees, with each group including student representatives, public officials or designees, business representatives, randomly selected patrons (some from recent public hearings), a facilitator from a boundary committee, and members of a previous boundary committee. The district will post proposed timelines and meeting agendas on its website, and focus group meetings will be open to the public. Trustees had tabled the boundary decision last month to seek more feedback, with an original change date of Jan. 11. The change follows a shift from allowing students to choose between three high schools for two decades, after enrollment and socioeconomic disparities led to an end to that policy.

The memorandum of decision in *In re Jeffery Wayne Smith and Paulette Monee Smith* addresses confirmation of the debtors’ Chapter 13 amended plan and the Standing Chapter 13 Trustee’s objections. The debtors filed a voluntary Chapter 13 petition on October 7, 1997, and later submitted a pre-confirmation amended Chapter 13 plan; the Trustee objected, and the matter was tried on February 25, 1998.

The court held it had jurisdiction as a core proceeding. It found the debtors acted in good faith and that the plan’s different treatment of Chrysler Financial’s secured claim and NBD Bank’s secured claim did not unfairly discriminate under 11 U.S.C. § 1322. The court also concluded the plan met the good faith requirement of 11 U.S.C. § 1325(a)(3), including regarding disclosure issues and Mrs. Smith’s Profit Sharing Plan benefits.

For the disposable income test under 11 U.S.C. § 1325(b)(1)(B), the court required changes to protect creditors’ interests: it reduced the emergency/property maintenance cushion, required increased plan payments if overtime exceeded projections, and held that ERISA-qualified Profit Sharing Plan benefits are excluded from disposable income unless and until Mrs. Smith receives cash distributions—if cash is received, net proceeds must be paid to creditors. The court further required any voluntary retirement/401(k) contributions to cease during the plan term and be devoted to plan payments.

The court granted the Trustee’s objection in part and denied it in part, confirming the amended plan as modified, including setting Chrysler’s interest at 3.9% (instead of 8%) and ordering the additional payment and reporting terms described above.

Jim Zemlin of the Linux Foundation said Linux powers 99.4% of the world’s high performance computing systems, 90% of stock exchanges, and 64% of mobile devices, and claimed foundation projects have created $14.5 billion in value measured by cost per line of code. The passage also notes Hart’s Linux Foundation gold membership for developing HartOS, an API platform for HIPAA-compliant sharing of health data across multiple systems. It mentions a free open source software basics publication sampling from an open source management training course, and that the Cloud Native Computing Foundation announced 11 new members at an annual open source leadership summit.

Thinking Machines Lab, a heavily funded startup led by former OpenAI researchers and cofounder/CEO Mira Murati, has launched its first product, Tinker, a tool that automates the creation of custom frontier AI models. The company says Tinker will make fine-tuning more accessible by handling distributed training details while keeping control over data and algorithms. Tinker lets users fine-tune two open source models—Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen—using supervised learning or reinforcement learning with labeled feedback, and users can download and run the resulting models. The API is planned to be available to applicants starting Wednesday, and it is not yet charging for API use. Beta testers and researchers cited in the passage say Tinker is simpler than fine-tuning from scratch, offers a mix of abstraction and tunability, and enables specialized capability improvements; the company plans to add automated systems to guard against misuse.

The passage includes an oath of allegiance and related passport-application details, followed by a letter dated May 10, 1902, from Mr. Lord to Mr. Hay. It transmits copies of an Argentine presidential message delivered at the opening of Congress sessions on May 8, 1902, and notes public interest in the message’s treatment of international relations and the financial situation. The letter says the message was disappointing in being general on negotiations for limiting armaments between Argentina and Chile. It quotes the President stating that negotiations opened in Santiago through British mediation aim at rational limitation of armaments. The passage describes how both countries increased army and naval forces at heavy cost, causing damage to industrial and commercial activity, increased debt and deficits, and leading both governments to consider fresh taxes, with business conditions becoming dull and employment scarce.

The passage argues that the author does not see value in owning Snap in the short term. It cites competition from Facebook’s Instagram features and similar offerings on other platforms, declining Snapchat app downloads, and low marketer adoption. It also discusses upcoming lock-up expiration that could allow insiders to sell large numbers of Snap shares, potentially diluting earnings per share and pressuring the stock. The passage notes that Snap’s recent revenue and losses did not meet expectations, with daily active users slightly below forecast. It concludes that shorting is risky due to substantial short interest and options pricing, and the author plans to watch without making a trade recommendation.

The passage describes using a “Single/Double” offense to attack the Triangle & Two defense and free up shooters, because chasers in this defense are skilled at pass denial and shooters need screens to get open. It explains that the Single/Double screens depend on communication between shooters: if one shooter initiates the single/double action, the other forms the double screen, creating a burden on defenders. It outlines options and reads/counters including double-screen fakes and reversals, sealing off chasers when defenders overhelp, pop-outs, and rolls to the basket, with examples of base screen and side screen sequences (including lob passes, drop passes, and kick-out passes) triggered by defensive steps up or rotations. It emphasizes execution and coordination, including readiness to perform double screens, base screens, and strong post ups, along with defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. It also suggests scouting opponents to anticipate defensive reads and counters, monitoring changes after substitutions/timeouts, using varied alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. The passage ends by summarizing that in Triangle & Two, three players guard in a triangle zone while two “chasers” aggressively deny passes and focus on preventing opponents from receiving the ball or grabbing rebounds.

Safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar between study groups. Before Week 24, at least one adverse event (AE) was reported by 51.2% in the Primary SOC group and 52.0% in the Additional Educational Program group, with related AEs in 8.9% and 7.3%, and serious AEs in 12.4% and 14.7%, respectively. Study drug discontinuation due to AEs occurred in 5.5% and 3.9%. Bleeding events were reported in 6.5% and 9.0%, with major bleeding in 0.7% and 1.1%, and a fatal bleeding event occurred in 1 subject in the Additional Educational Program group. Between 24 and 48 weeks, at least one AE was reported in 33.8% (Primary SOC), 40.8% (Secondary SOC), and 38.6% (Continued Additional Educational Program), with related AEs in 2.5%, 4.5%, and 3.9%, serious AEs in 11.8%, 13.5%, and 14.0%, and AEs causing study drug discontinuation in 2.3%, 3.6%, and 1.0%. Bleeding events were reported in 4.1%, 4.0%, and 3.2%, with major bleeding in 0.7%, 0.4%, and 0.3%; fatal bleeding occurred in 2 subjects (1 in Primary SOC and 1 in Secondary SOC). Overall, 24 deaths were reported, and no pregnancies were reported. Laboratory review did not indicate any clinically concerning signal for drug-induced hepatic or renal effects. The study concluded that the AEGEAN trial showed high adherence and persistence during the first 24 weeks and sustained up to 48 weeks with apixaban for atrial fibrillation, and that the proactive educational program did not provide additional benefits.

The passage argues that inquiry-based learning is linked to solving real-life problems and developing skills such as critical thinking, collaboration, communication, and digital literacy. It notes that in U.S. K-12 science frameworks, “inquiry” has been replaced by eight “scientific and engineering practices,” including asking questions, planning investigations, using models, analyzing data, using mathematics, constructing explanations, engaging in argument from evidence, and evaluating and communicating information. STEM education is described as an approach intended to connect school learning to everyday life through interdisciplinary study, experiential activities, and critical thinking, and the literature review summarizes students’ and teachers’ views on STEM, including reported benefits and common obstacles such as limited time, insufficient materials, and lack of teacher preparedness.

The study described in the passage explores Greek primary teachers’ views and conditions for implementing STEM in primary education. It uses a sample of 114 voluntary primary teachers from Attica, collects data via a Likert-scale questionnaire with open-ended questions and 27 structured interviews (March–May 2022), and analyzes closed- and open-ended responses qualitatively and comparatively. Results report that teachers consider developing students’ scientific thinking very important, often linking it to everyday life and critical thinking, and they rank key STEM practices (e.g., problem-solving, small-group work, observations and measurements, and sharing results) as important while reporting that opportunities to practice them in classrooms are relatively rare. Teachers also report limited confidence in teaching science and mathematics effectively, cite weaknesses including insufficient training, lack of infrastructure/equipment, and limited time, and express needs for further training, materials, guidance, and time in the curriculum. The conclusion states that teachers view STEM as innovative and interdisciplinary with pedagogical advantages, but that successful implementation requires teacher training, infrastructure, and timetable time, noting a gap between teachers’ willingness and the prerequisites provided for implementation.

The passage explains that newly analyzed microstructures help clarify why dandelion fluffy seeds can be hard to dislodge under certain conditions. It also describes that these microstructures provide a seed lift-off or grip to wait for a better breeze, noting that puffing in one direction is surprisingly difficult to blow all seed tufts away from the stem.

A report said South Korea’s birthrate fell in the mid-1980s as more married women received higher education. The total fertility rate dropped to 1.6 in 1987 from 2.1 three years earlier. The report linked women’s marriage and birth patterns to educational background, noting changes in the proportions of married women with middle school versus high school diplomas, and an increase in married women’s labor force participation from about 39% in 1974 to 53% in 2012. South Korea’s total fertility rate was 1.24 in 2015, below the 2.1 replacement level.

The passage describes planned mapping, listing, and summarization of concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment using WHODrug (ATC codes at level 4; summaries by ATC class level 2 and preferred name, with patient counts/percentages ordered by incidence). It defines prior versus concomitant medications based on start/stop timing relative to first IMP administration and states that unclear incomplete dates are treated as concomitant.  

It then outlines efficacy, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic, and safety analysis methods, including the primary efficacy endpoint “time to plasma glucose recovery” (with specific recovery definition, use of FAS/PPS, Kaplan-Meier plots, stratified log-rank testing, censoring rules, and sensitivity/supportive analyses) and secondary efficacy endpoints assessed at multiple time thresholds. Baseline determination, covariate adjustments (age group, injection site), and handling of missing data (observed data only, no imputation) are also specified.  

For PK/PD, it provides sampling time handling rules, concentration/LLOQ handling, data listing/summary presentation, and PD definitions (AUE0-30min). Safety analysis procedures cover extent of exposure, local tolerability, adverse events (treatment-emergent definitions, MedDRA coding, causal relationship/severity handling), laboratory/vital sign/tabulation rules, ECG categorization, immunogenicity (ADA occurrence descriptively), and QC/presentation guidance for tables, figures, and listings.

During the excavation of two sections of the Amstel riverbed for a new subway line in Amsterdam, city archaeologists uncovered about 700,000 discarded objects spanning thousands of years. The finds, dating before the city’s 1300s founding to Neolithic times, range from stone axes to modern items like cellphones and personal documents, offering clues to everyday life. The “Below the Surface” project involved sifting riverbed mud and silt 12 meters below the surface across two construction sites. When the Rokin station opens later in the month, 10,000 of the objects from that site will be displayed to passengers. The project also includes an interactive website with photographs and data for about 30,000 objects, and a book-catalog called “Stuff” with 13,000 photos distributed to local schools. The project cost 6 million Euros.

The passage describes a goalie’s account of a key breakaway and saves, noting he made an initial save but is unsure what happened afterward. He says he kept the puck out during a decisive moment and that staying even despite ups and downs is important, especially in playoffs and finals. He reflects on two finals games, feels more positive about their personal impact, and comments on differences in opponents’ plays, including wanting he could do something differently in the first game. The goalie also discusses the significance of playing at home in Nashville, the crowd’s reaction, and how timely saves can boost confidence and help his ability to track and anticipate the puck.

The passage describes steps toward proving Freiman’s theorem using additive-combinatorics tools. It explains how Ruzsa’s modeling lemma can represent a set with small doubling by a large fraction of a subset of a small cyclic group via Freiman 8-isomorphism. It then motivates why a large set need not contain large subspaces after one addition (giving a “nivo” set in \( \mathbb{F}_2^n\) as an example), but shows that repeated addition does produce structure. The central result presented is Bogolyubov’s lemma: for \(A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n\) of density \(\alpha\), the set \(2A-2A\) contains a subspace of codimension \(<1/\alpha^2\). The proof idea uses Fourier analysis and views convolution as recording sumsets with multiplicity. The lemma is then reformulated for \( \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) using Bohr sets (the “analog” of subspaces), where \(2A-2A\) contains a Bohr set \( \mathrm{Bohr}_R(1/4)\) with \(|R|<1/\alpha^2\). Finally, the passage outlines using geometry of numbers to show that a large Bohr set contains a large proper generalized arithmetic progression (GAP), invoking Minkowski’s second theorem by constructing a lattice associated to the Bohr set and a convex box. The geometric argument is positioned as a key ingredient for the completion of Freiman’s theorem in the next lecture, along with mention of a polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.

The passage describes NVIDIA Ampere architecture features in the A100 GPU, focusing on improved Tensor Core efficiency, data sharing, and matrix multiply throughput versus V100. It details new data fetch mechanisms including an asynchronous copy instruction, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls, along with increased bandwidth for DRAM and L2. It also covers compression, fault detection/isolation/containment, third-generation NVLink and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and A100 hardware accelerators such as NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and multiple NVDEC units. The text further explains CUDA advances like CUDA Task Graphs, async copy APIs, asynchronous barriers, and L2 persistence for repeated data accesses. It introduces MIG partitioning (up to seven GPU instances per A100) for isolated multi-tenant usage, outlines MIG architecture details (GPU slices, sys pipes, compute instances, memory QoS), and discusses MIG migration. Finally, it describes DGX A100 as a system for AI workloads, and includes an appendix on sparse neural network pruning and benefits, ending with legal and trademark information.

A £95,220 donation from the ScottishPower Foundation will support Sussex Wildlife Trust’s education programmes at Woods Mill in Henfield as part of its 50-year celebrations. It will enable ten specialist wildlife identification courses, train 250 wildlife champions, and establish a young naturalists club, with an overall funding boost of almost £100k allowing an additional 1,300 people to take part in events. The money will also support habitat improvements, including restoration of the reed bed and improved path access for visitors, and has already helped install a camera in a kestrel nesting box for public viewing. Trustees visited the site, met staff, and joined a pond-dipping session with students from Upper Beeding Primary School. Woods Mill opened to the public on 8 June 1968.

The passage contains multiple news items dated July 13–14, 2001. It includes an Enron-related email noting attached stories. The speaker tells Cabinet and White House staff that the event is spontaneous, says “au revoir,” and thanks them for serving the next President with devotion and dedication. He praises the “great heart” of the house, saying it comes from those who serve, and emphasizes that each staff member is indispensable.
