The passage describes how Japanese universities lagged in using ICT for education before the COVID-19 pandemic due to beliefs about university teaching occurring in-person and structural barriers such as limited adult student enrollment and regulations restricting credits for distance learning. During the pandemic, emergency measures led universities to switch to full-time online classes, after which MEXT policies encouraged returning to face-to-face teaching with adjustments to credit limits and exceptions. It outlines government efforts supporting digitalization (including subsidies and policy packages related to “Society 5.0” and “My Number”), while also noting concerns about personal information protection and related system issues.

The passage further reviews pre-pandemic ICT use by faculty, challenges faced during online emergency teaching (including weaker communication and difficulty supporting practical work), and possible ways forward through sharing best practices and combining distance methods with face-to-face education. It also discusses student learning issues connected to “substantiation of the credit system,” including limited study time outside class and the effects of online learning on assignments and learning time. Finally, it summarizes digitalization trends in lifelong learning, noting differing levels of progress between degree programs (mainly through distance learning) and non-degree programs (with low digitalization for Kokaikoza, but greater digitalization for newer vocational certificate-type programs), and concludes that digitalization brings both opportunities and remaining challenges, especially around education culture and data privacy.

Social inclusion is described as an individual’s ability to participate in important societal activities and their sense of community belonging, and social exclusion is presented as a multifaceted continuum often associated with poverty, unemployment, inequality, and/or poor health. People with serious mental illness are described as among the most socially excluded, with smaller social networks, lower income, lower employment, and more criminal and violent victimization than the general population. The passage notes that social exclusion can be both a cause and consequence of mental ill-health, and that greater social inclusion is linked to better quality of life and lower loneliness.  

Mental health supported accommodation services are described as providing care and support to people with severe and complex mental health problems, with three types in England: residential care homes, supported housing (time-limited tenancies), and floating outreach services. Service users in these services are described as often socially isolated and experiencing stigma, with evidence of unmet needs such as employment access and forming intimate relationships; the passage states that more research is needed to identify service users’ precise needs and interventions.  

The SInQUE is introduced as a validated measure of social inclusion for individuals with severe mental illness, previously used only in offline research contexts, with stakeholder feedback suggesting potential usefulness in clinical practice for assessing social inclusion and guiding care planning. The study aimed to develop an online version of SInQUE for use in mental health supported accommodation, assess acceptability and perceived usefulness among staff and service users, and determine take-up with and without an implementation strategy.  

The study included two stages in an inner London borough: lab testing with supported accommodation staff using think-aloud testing and semi-structured interviews, followed by five-month field testing with interviews of staff (n=12) and service users (n=12) who used the online SInQUE. The online SInQUE is described as staff-completed with service users collaboratively, accessible via computer/tablet/mobile, generating a reference number without logging personal identifying service user data. The questionnaire is a refined 46-item SInQUE yielding a score of 0–75, covering nine areas of social inclusion.  

Interviews were analysed using thematic analysis within an ICAMO framework, and a logic model and implementation strategy were developed. Ethics approvals were reported for both phases. Results reported that the online SInQUE was generally perceived as acceptable and potentially useful by staff and service users, and that implementation support (especially leadership endorsement) was important for tool use; however, take-up during the 5-month period was limited (about 10% of service users in the participating borough). The passage concludes with implications for practice and research, including recommendations for further testing in residential care and floating outreach settings and for longer-term studies to assess uptake and outcomes.

Dalhousie University researcher Prof. Nancy McLean says there are enough native bees pollinating blueberry fields on P.E.I. that farmers do not need to bring in honey bees. After two years of Environment Canada–funded research on Wyman’s fields, she found that more than half of the bees on blueberry flowers are native. McLean said native bees are estimated to be seven times more efficient than honey bees and may be doing a large majority of pollination, partly because they have evolved with blueberry plants and can buzz pollinate. She also noted native bees are more suited to the Maritime climate, while honey bees are less likely to fly in cool, damp weather. McLean said convincing farmers they don’t need honey bees is challenging and that they should support native bees and learn how prevalent they are. She is also researching other plants native bees prefer to plant around field edges, and she said bringing in honey bees is expensive and may involve risks such as parasite introduction and a shortage of hives in the province.

Michael Dell said Dell Technologies is benefiting from strong AI demand and that the data-center building peak is not yet here. He noted the company’s stock rose significantly due to the growing importance of infrastructure services, and he said customers are deploying infrastructure quickly but are often limited by the ability to bring enough power into buildings. Dell also reported strong server-networking growth and raised growth expectations for revenue and earnings per share. While some market observers warned that equity valuations appear stretched, Dell said he expects demand to continue, adding that while there may eventually be too many data centers, there are no signs of that yet.

Siddharth Agrawal runs Silkasia, a family-managed garment and home textile export business based in Jaipur, with plants in several parts of India and operations managed from Mumbai, Noida, and Panipat. He has been in the family business for 18 years and has pursued research on Indian cow breeds, working to develop satellite farms for milk and milk products. He is also involved as an investor in an urban rooftop farming company and in start-ups, and mentors new ventures. Along with his wife Vrinda, he started a retail store in Jaipur and created the women’s clothing brand Mayori with Japanese designers and Indian sensibilities. Mayori is expected to expand nationwide in 2018–19 with more than eight physical stores, strong online presence, and collaborations. He is a member of EO Jaipur, YPO Rajasthan, and RAIN, and serves as President of TIE, Rajasthan for a two-year term.

The document standardizes the GHCB memory area so a guest OS can interoperate with any hypervisor that supports SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. It defines the GHCB size (4,096 bytes) and a format that mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, specifies required minimal guest state exposed to the hypervisor during VMGEXIT, and standardizes supported non-automatic exit (NAE) events and guest/hypervisor behaviors. Version 2 adds hypervisor feature advertisement, additional protocol elements, and initial SEV-SNP support; revisions 2.01 through 2.04 add updates such as SEV-SNP secrets page changes, error codes and protocol handling changes, support for APIC ID lists, multi-VMPL execution, page state change notifications, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and additional GHCB MSR functions. It also describes hypervisor feature bitmap negotiation, GHCB MSR protocol request/response fields, CPUID handling for establishing negotiation parameters, and GHCB GPA registration/unregistration via MSR protocol. The document further specifies examples of GHCB negotiation and VMGEXIT handling, SEV-ES and SEV-SNP mechanisms for AP booting (including AP jump table and VMSA-based AP creation), NAE processing rules using VALID_BITMAP and SW_EXITCODE/SW_EXITINFO fields, SEV-SNP request/extended request events for firmware interaction and certificate/data return, and #HV doorbell page behavior and host/guest interrupt handling semantics for Restricted Injection.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has been declared the winner of Sunday’s Russian presidential election, securing a fourth term and set to rule for another six years. Authorities said he received more than three-quarters of the vote, while critics claim the election was pre-determined. In Yekaterinburg, Lucian Kim reported a small rally tied to Crimea’s annexation anniversary, timed to bolster patriotic support. Kim said Putin’s message emphasizes that Russia is not doing as badly as claimed, citing sanctions and portraying the West as hostile, including regarding allegations tied to a poisoning case and claims of international anti-Russian efforts. Opposition figures reported harassment of independent election monitors, pressure on government employees to vote, and ballot stuffing, but the opposition lacked a unified alternative, with Alexei Navalny and Ksenia Sobchak publicly disputing after results. There is speculation about whether Putin could extend beyond the six-year term, but he said he does not have plans to change the constitution yet.

The passage explains the Dark Cloud Cover candlestick pattern as a bearish reversal pattern that appears after an uptrend. It forms when a bearish candlestick opens above the prior bullish candlestick’s close but closes below its midpoint, signaling a potential shift from bullish to bearish sentiment. The pattern involves two candles and can be used as a signal for short selling or for closing long positions, particularly during a rally in a down-trending market. The passage notes that the pattern is not a guarantee of a trend reversal and should be used with other factors such as market news, fundamental analysis, technical indicators (Moving Averages, MACD, RSI), and risk management; confirmation may come from monitoring price action over the next few days. It also mentions that backtesting should be done with specific rules and that the Dark Cloud Cover strategy can be applied across asset markets (stocks, Forex, commodities, cryptocurrencies), is limited in bullish markets, and may be traded on different timeframes depending on trader goals and risk tolerance.

Democrat Doug Jones and Republican Roy Moore face off in a special Alabama Senate election on Tuesday amid national attention over accusations that Moore dating and molested teenage girls. Moore denies the allegations and has led in many polls despite a controversial career as a prosecutor and judge. Jones is campaigning across the state and says Moore cares more about personal agenda than Alabama people. Moore has been mostly absent from the campaign trail for the past week.

Thousands of Armenian-Americans marched in Los Angeles on Tuesday to commemorate the estimated 1.5 million Armenians who died under the Ottoman Empire a century ago, demanding Turkey recognize the deaths as genocide. The protests followed the resignation of Armenian Prime Minister Serzh Sargsyan after 10 days of anti-government protests, and included plans for a separate demonstration outside the Turkish Consulate. Organizers and participants said their ancestors were killed or affected, and Armenian and many historians call it genocide, while Turkey argues the deaths were from civil war and unrest. Kim Kardashian West also praised global peaceful demonstrations calling for recognition.

The passage describes how active galactic nuclei (AGN) are powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole and how the standard Shakura–Sunyaev thin-disc model predicts temperature- and accretion-rate–driven variability on long (thousands of years) time-scales, while observations show significant variability on months to years and even “changing-look” behavior on a few years. It notes that AGN spectral energy distributions (SEDs) are more complex than a multi-colour black-body, showing X-ray emission with a high-energy tail, a UV downturn before the expected disc peak, and a connection between the UV downturn and the soft X-ray excess. The authors then motivate using intensive monitoring to test models of disc–corona connections and report their approach for the Seyfert 1 galaxy Fairall 9. They analyze Swift UVW2 and 0.3–10 keV X-ray data by segmenting the light-curves, constructing time-averaged SEDs, and fitting them with the agnsed model (warm and hot Comptonisation regions plus reflection). They find a clear SED evolution between segment 1a and later segments, interpreted as an increase in global mass-accretion rate and a softening of the hot corona photon index with roughly constant integrated X-ray power. For timing, they use Gaussian Process regression to obtain evenly sampled light-curve realizations, compute power spectra and Fourier-resolved phase lags and coherence, and find that the UV–X-ray relationship is more complex than simple reverberation or propagation scenarios, including a systematic drop in coherence between certain segments. They construct an analytic toy model linking observed UV and X-ray variability to combinations of disc variability, seed-photon modulation, reverberation, and wind/BLR reprocessing, and suggest that changes in system structure over the campaign likely affect the lag and coherence behavior.

The paper examines South Australia’s “World Class” public education policy initiative launched in 2018 by the Department for Education, using Bacchi’s Foucault-inspired “What’s the Problem Represented to be?” (WPR) framework applied to publicly available and FOI-retrieved policy documents. It situates the initiative within the Global Education Reform Movement (GERM) and the influence of McKinsey’s “Universal Scale” and “roadmap,” which aims for schools to reach “World Class” status by 2028. The authors argue that the policy centralises authority through a “single source of truth,” differentiated accountability, and scripted curriculum materials backed by dashboards and increased performance management. They contend this approach reduces complex schooling to measurable indicators, marginalises broader purposes of education, and contributes to widening achievement gaps and disengagement among students from disadvantaged backgrounds. The paper concludes by proposing an alternative “Beyond World Class” approach focused on equity, inclusion, professional trust, democratic partnerships, and embracing complexity and uncertainty in system-wide school improvement.

Non-centrosymmetric crystals can display piezoelectricity, ferroelectricity, and pyroelectricity. Among the 21 non-inversion-symmetric crystal classes, 10 are polar and have a permanent dipole moment. Ferroelectrics undergo a centrosymmetry-reducing transition below the Curie temperature and show switchable spontaneous polarization, while polar metals combine a polar crystal structure with enough mobile charge carriers to maintain robust conductivity; in polar metals, electric fields are screened so geometric polarity cannot be reversed by an applied field. The paper discusses “distortive polar metals” (DPMs), defined by a centrosymmetry-lifting structural transformation and guided by “weak coupling” behavior, where Fermi-surface electronic states are decoupled from polar distortions. 

The study focuses on the metallic DPM Mn5Al8, which undergoes a martensitic (displacive) centrosymmetry-reducing transition (cubic γ-brass to rhombohedral γ2) around ~880°C and forms rank-2 laminate twins with a herringbone morphology containing “charged” head-to-head (H-H) and tail-to-tail (T-T) domain boundaries. Using electron microscopy and 4D-STEM differential phase contrast, the authors visualize polar domain variants and map a qualitative “bound charge” density based on divergence of a displacement-vector field, showing that H-H and T-T boundaries appear with negative and positive divergence, respectively. They then report variable surface effects tied to boundary character: low-voltage SEM contrast, copper deposition, and surface oxidation vary along the repeating “interlocking Y pattern,” indicating surplus and depletion of free carriers at H-H and T-T boundaries, respectively. The authors analyze resistivity and density of states (DFT) to confirm metallic behavior and also outline a broader chemical-space search in the ICSD for metallic compounds in polar crystal classes, identifying numerous metallic polar metals and noting that roughly 20% are DPMs.

The Jonathan Hunt Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution held a tea at Parkwood Assisted Living in Elkin to honor Good Citizens selected from seniors in eight high schools in its district. The Good Citizens scholarship program recognizes qualities of good citizenship, including dependability, service, scholarship, and patriotism. Students submitted applications and essays on “Our American Heritage and Our Responsibility for Preserving it,” addressing “How has America advanced the cause of freedom in the rest of the world?” Five students attended with family members, read their essays, and received a wallet card and lapel pin. The overall winner received a monetary award, and all participants will receive a certificate of achievement at Spring Awards Day.

John Wilkerson is a Washington correspondent for STAT who writes about the politics of health care. The passage also refers to D.C. Diagnosis, STAT’s twice-weekly newsletter about the politics and policy of health and medicine, and lists multiple health-related news topics and headlines.

Jane Goodall, a pioneering primatologist and chimpanzee researcher and conservationist, died at 91 while on tour in California. The Jane Goodall Institute said she died “in her sleep” and of natural causes. Goodall discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools, have personalities, and can engage in war, and she led efforts to protect wild places. She began visiting Kenya in 1957, studied chimpanzees at Gombe from 1960, earned a PhD in 1965 from Cambridge, and later founded the Jane Goodall Institute, including the “Roots & Shoots” youth program.

An Argentine defender, Federico Allende of lower-division Sport Pacifico, admitted in radio interviews that he used a needle to hurt rival strikers from Estudiantes during a cup match on Sunday. Sport Pacifico’s president Hector Moncada said he was devastated and vowed to expel Allende. Although Pacifico won 3-2 and knocked Estudiantes out, the team’s atmosphere turned after Allende later said “you need to play dirty” and described piercing Estudiantes strikers with a needle. Estudiantes’ striker Juan Otero said Allende jabbed him and that he complained to the referee, and Otero described Allende as “as a nasty man” after the interview.

An insurrection in Hawaii on July 30, 1889, led by Robert W. Wilcox and Robert Boyd, was defeated, and about 70 U.S. sailors and marines landed by permission to protect the legation and city. Afterward, a constitutional dispute between the King and cabinet was decided by the supreme court against the King, defining cabinet control of his signature and government operations. In 1890, U.S. Secretary Blaine invited the King to the International American Conference, but Hawaii’s delegate could not join before adjournment; later he announced a belated appointment and probable acceptance of the conference conclusions. King Kalakaua visited the U.S. and died on January 20, 1891; Liliuokalani was proclaimed Queen. Stevens reported fears about her course and ministry, noting potential constitutional support for ministers, and in early spring 1891 the supreme court ruled the late King’s cabinet ended at his death. A new cabinet was appointed, a prince consort died in August 1891, and efforts began to revise the reciprocity treaty with U.S.; Mott Smith became special envoy and a legislature favorable to the treaty was elected in February 1892.

The passage explains that stock trading strategies use defined rules and methods to decide when to buy and sell stocks (including ETFs). It compares trading strategies with long-term investing, emphasizing that trading focuses on shorter-term price movements while investing focuses on holding for years or decades. It describes multiple strategy types, including day trading, swing trading, momentum, scalping, trend following, arbitrage, event-driven trading, pair and market-neutral trading, statistical arbitrage, seasonality, overnight trading, mean reversion, and technical-analysis-based approaches using indicators like moving averages, RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands. The passage discusses risks, noting that many day traders lose money and that trading only a single stock is risky for retail traders due to the possibility of large losses. It highlights the roles of research, discipline, backtesting with historical data, accounting for trading costs and fees, and adapting to market volatility and unexpected news through diversification and volatility-based risk management. It also states that trading strategies can be automated with algorithms and that the 3-5-7 rule describes a pattern of price pushes (three in one direction, five against, then seven to reaffirm).

Depression and burnout among physicians and nurses are described as worsening crises in the U.S., exacerbated by the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. Burnout is characterized by emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment. The passage describes mindfulness and Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) as potential approaches, noting that MBSR has evidence for reducing depression and burnout symptoms. It also discusses psilocybin, reported efficacy for depressive symptoms, and growing interest in potential synergy between mindfulness training and psychedelics.  

A previous individual-format randomized trial of psilocybin-assisted therapy for frontline healthcare providers suggested reduced depressive symptoms at 28 days but lacked an active control and used a format described as limiting scalability and group-intervention aspects. The authors report the first group-format randomized controlled trial comparing MBSR vs. MBSR plus psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (MBSR+PAP) for frontline physicians and nurses with COVID-19–related burnout and depression. The trial investigated safety and preliminary efficacy, using QIDS-SR-16 as the primary endpoint (change at 2 weeks) and additional measures including the Maslach Burnout Inventory, demoralization, and connectedness scales.  

In 25 enrolled participants (12 MBSR-only, 13 MBSR+PAP), all study-related adverse events were grade 1 or 2, and there were no emergent suicidality or self-injurious behaviors. The MBSR+PAP group showed significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms at 2 weeks than MBSR alone, with greater improvements on depersonalization at 2 weeks and emotional exhaustion at 6 months, as well as demoralization and connectedness outcomes. The discussion concludes that combining MBSR with psilocybin appears safe, feasible, and potentially effective, while noting limitations including small sample size, sample homogeneity, lack of blinding, and differences between intervention experiences across groups.

Dean thony Gordley, a senior at Churchill High School in San Antonio, earned his diploma after moving to the city following Hurricane Katrina. He lost his father after he was shot, lived with his biological mother until she died of a heart attack, and spent about seven months sleeping outside without homeless training. A stranger found him a place to stay temporarily, and he did not tell school officials because he did not want to ask for help. NEISD connected him to the McKinney Vento Homeless Project, which provided services that helped him succeed in school, and additional families supported him through the program. Gordley said earning his diploma was a major goal and hopes to inspire others to keep pushing forward, sharing his experiences through songs.

Syracuse’s basketball program received a verbal commitment from Jalen Carey, setting up the Class of 2018 as a potentially strong recruiting group in program history. The class includes Top 50 recruits Jalen Carey and Darius Bazley, with Buddy Boeheim as a complementary piece. The passage introduces a list ranking these classes among Syracuse’s best, based on recruiting rankings (or estimates) at the time they arrived and using recruiting sources such as the Recruiting Services Consensus Index, Scout, Rivals, ESPN, 247 Sports, and OrangeHoops.org, without considering their on-court results.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for their work on metal-organic frameworks. The capacious molecular structures they developed can trap gas, water, and other chemicals, including collecting water from air and capturing greenhouse gases.

Stripe plans to further incorporate stablecoins into its payments business with a new product called Open Issuance, announced about a year after its $1.1 billion acquisition of Bridge. Open Issuance lets businesses launch and manage their own stablecoins, while earning yield on reserves typically made of U.S. Treasury bills and bank deposits to maintain a 1:1 peg to real-world dollars; unlike some existing stablecoins, Stripe says the product enables capturing that yield. Stripe’s move follows a July regulatory framework for stablecoins and aims to make stablecoins easier for mainstream payments. Stripe says the newly issued stablecoins will be interoperable for on- and off-ramping and cross-chain integrations. Gaybrick and Abrams cite potential benefits for merchants and platforms handling consumer balances, while noting early adopters so far include blockchain firms such as Phantom, Hyperliquid, and MetaMask.

The 3-2 zone defense is a variation of the 1-2-2 zone. By dropping the point defender to the free-throw line, it allows wing defenders to play wider, deny wing passing lanes, disrupt zone offenses that start with an entry pass to the wing, and protect against passes into the high post. The defense allows point guards to shoot, but it can be adjusted to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 zone if the point guard is an excellent outside shooter. The point defender and a tall, active wing can interchange, making high-post passes harder and helping the weakside baseline defender stay for rebounding. The 3-2 zone is also described as effective for defending fast breaks because defenders are aligned in fast-break lanes. The passage then outlines basic 3-2 zone shifts for ball positions at center, left wing, left corner, right wing, and right corner, and includes a point-wing interchange option when the wing is tall and athletic.

A New York Times report says University of California and California State University campuses are preparing for possible rolling blackouts during final exams due to California’s energy shortage and ongoing legal disputes involving Enron Energy Services and power suppliers. Other excerpts cover business and policy issues, including commentary on British Telecom’s credit rating and regulatory pressures; a Houston Chronicle outlook discussing nanotechnology’s potential applications for Houston; and a Houston Chronicle piece on the Center for Houston’s Future developing plans to improve education, urban design, and the city’s economic base. Cierra Dillard scored 22 points as 11th-seeded Buffalo upset No. 3 seed Florida State 86-65 to reach the Sweet 16 for the first time in school history. Buffalo shot 47.4% from the field, went 24 of 26 from the foul line, and limited Florida State to 3 of 25 from three-point range and 33.8% shooting. Buffalo led after a 10-2 run late in the first half and extended the lead early in the second half; they faced a regional semifinal against defending champion and second-seeded South Carolina on Saturday in Albany, New York. Stephanie Reid added 18 points and Summer Hemphill 17 for Buffalo, while Shakayla Thomas scored 25 for Florida State.

The passage describes a Market Research Future report on the global organic pigments market, forecasting higher growth of around 4.5% during the forecast years. House prices in the West Midlands rose by 7.1% over the year to December, leaving the typical property value at £181,000, about £12,000 higher than at the start of the year, according to an official report. Across the UK, prices increased by 7.2% over the year to December, with growth strongest in England (+7.7% to £236,000), then Wales (+4.7% to £148,000), Scotland (+3.5% to £142,000), and Northern Ireland (+5.7% to £125,000). The biggest rise was in Shetland (+26.1% to £179,000), while Aberdeen saw the biggest drop (-9.8% to £168,000) due to the offshore oil industry slump. Within the West Midlands, price rises ranged from Wyre Forest and Kidderminster (+10.4% to £175,063) to South Staffordshire (+3.1% to £208,478). Richard Snook (PwC) said house price inflation is expected to slow in 2017, with scenarios of 2% to 6% growth.

The passage describes a continuation of related U.S. and international patent applications and a storage system for densely stacked storage bins arranged in stacks under a grid framework. It includes parallel rails forming grid spaces, uprights and rails defining a framework, storage containers in stacks beneath the rails, and at least one load handling device on the grid that moves laterally above the stacks to lift one or more containers or parts thereof. The framework includes service means for interaction, control, and monitoring, with examples including power, water/fluid supply, lighting, sensing (e.g., fire/smoke/heat/gas), and data communications routed through the uprights. A method of condition monitoring is also described, involving sensor means with data logging, communication to a central logging device, and monitoring of received data. The passage further explains how the system supports robotic movement over the grid, container access to retrieve/replace containers, structural monitoring using sensors and cameras, controlled environmental services to bins (e.g., heating/cooling and nutrient control), and fire management concepts including fluid or gas suppression targeted to individual containers or areas under the grid. It also describes container identification and location using sensors such as barcodes or cameras, potential partitioning of the storage system into sections (e.g., temperature or isolated zones), and mentions compatibility with alternative container and partition configurations referenced by other patent applications.

The April 29 Town Meeting will consider whether to support Fire Chief Michael Feinberg’s request to adopt an Enterprise Fund to cover ambulance operating costs. The Finance Committee is not recommending support, saying the residents’ benefit is questionable and there is no urgency, and noting recent ambulance activity and concerns about funding outside Proposition 2½ protections. Selectman Richard Lombard opposes the article, while Enzo Barile and Chesley Taylor Jr. support it and say fees can be waived for residents with financial hardship. Town Meeting will also address Coast Guard Housing land sale decisions, with the Finance Committee recommending indefinite postponement of that article as well, and will vote on 41 articles starting at 12:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, simultaneous-sampling, 20-bit SAR DAQ system with configurable single-ended or differential analog inputs. Each channel includes input clamp protection (tolerating up to ±18V), a programmable gain amplifier with user-selectable bandwidth options, and an output low-pass filter. The system uses a 4.096V internal reference and includes features such as a fast-settling buffer, programmable digital averaging, and a high-speed data interface, achieving up to 2 MSPS throughput per channel. The device operates from 5V and 1.8V analog supplies, supports true bipolar inputs, and provides constant 1 MΩ resistive input impedance. It also supports simultaneous sampling across multiple devices using SMPL_SYNC, configurable straight-binary or two’s-complement output formats, multiple-lane (2-lane or 4-lane) SDR/DDR interfaces, a data randomizer, test patterns, speed-boost mode, and various power-down/reset and SPI configuration options, including daisy-chain operation.

The passage argues that Saudi Arabia’s alleged efforts to distort Islam’s meaning helped create al-Qaeda and ISIS, and that Western mainstream media allegedly distorts peaceful opposition while using money to spread messages. It describes the June 14, 2017 shooting at a local baseball game by James Hodgkinson, who called Trump a “traitor” and vowed to “destroy” him, and who was killed after police neutralized him. It says House Majority Whip Steve Scalise was the apparent primary target and was badly injured but will recover. It also claims Hodgkinson was a Bernie Sanders supporter and avid viewer of anti-Trump shows, held Russiagate beliefs, and that social media threats preceded the attack. The passage links the shooting to anti-Trump content, including a Kathy Griffin photo mock-up of a beheaded Trump, and calls for mainstream media to be held accountable.

A recent report by the Powder River Basin Resource Council says mineral companies owe more than $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 Wyoming counties, largely due to bankruptcy and counties being treated as unsecured lenders with low repayment priority. The report highlights Campbell County’s unpaid taxes of over $26 million and Sheridan County’s about $7.46 million, including debts from Storm Cat Energy Operating Corporation and Summit Gas Resources. It attributes much of the delinquency to an about 18-month county payment schedule and notes that unpaid taxes affect school districts and other public services. The report recommends four policy changes, including more frequent county tax collection and better mechanisms for addressing county tax debt in bankruptcy.

Nebraska youngsters got free dental care at the UNMC College of Dentistry in Lincoln during Children’s Dental Day. The program serves between 159 and 200 children each year with services such as cleaning, fluoride, sealants, fillings, extractions, and root canals, along with education on proper tooth care. A child advised that eating lots of sugar and soda can ruin teeth. UNMC has run the program since 2001, providing over $3 million in dental work to young Nebraskans.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 8, 2018 reporting results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. The company issued a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and provided CFO Commentary (Exhibit 99.2) by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer; the CFO Commentary was to be posted on the company’s investor website after the filing. The press release and CFO Commentary are furnished and not deemed filed for purposes of specified Securities Exchange Act and Securities Act liabilities. The exhibits listed are the February 8, 2018 press release and the CFO Commentary.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2021. It includes financial statements and notes covering: consolidated cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets; segment information for North America, International, and AWS; accounting policies and supplemental disclosures such as estimates, earnings per share, inventories, receivables, and unearned revenue; fair value measurement and investment classifications; lease information and principal lease liabilities and costs; commitments and contingencies including pledged assets, legal proceedings, and tax-related matters; debt terms and credit facilities; stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation; income taxes; and liquidity/capital resources and free cash flow measures. It also discusses effects and uncertainties related to the COVID-19 pandemic, foreign exchange rate impacts, and provides second-quarter 2021 guidance (net sales, operating income, and COVID-19 cost assumptions).

The passage explains that an offensive rebound during a free throw is a “RBP” and emphasizes the need to be well drilled in boxing out on all free throws. It notes that championships can be lost due to failure to box out and says defensive intensity should increase to secure a stop. It advises defenders to keep both feet together, step up the lane without stepping into it, keep hands up in elbow-high position, and communicate to ensure the shooter is boxed out. It also provides cautions about pushing too far under the basket, maintaining inside position by using both hands high and using the butt to push the offensive player away, and using a pinch/double team against strong rebounders. For multiple-shot situations, it suggests relaxing on the first attempt to prevent line violations, recommends placing as many defensive rebounders on the lane as rules permit, and mentions “early push off” responsibilities for made and missed free throws to create an outnumbered advantage.

A Cherokee County community will gather to honor a local school leader, Maleka Johnson, who was killed in a boat explosion in the Bahamas while on vacation. Her husband, Tiran Johnson, was critically injured, and their 12-year-old son Cameron was in Tennessee with family. Family members described Maleka’s impact and said they are trying to comfort Cameron as they plan tributes and ensure memories and joy remain.

The passage tests the “options expiration week” (OPEX week) and related periods, asking what trading strategies and backtests show about stock performance after options expiration. It defines OPEX as the Friday before the third Saturday of each month (with holiday exceptions shifting to Thursday) and describes “pin risk” and reduced option open interest as drivers. It proposes backtesting strategies using SPY (S&P 500) such as being invested only during specific OPEX-related weeks. Backtests indicate the week after options expiration week generally underperforms a random week on average, with monthly variation: August is comparatively positive (average weekly gain 0.55%), while September is notably negative (average loss -0.94%, low 25% win rate). The passage also provides backtest results for the day before expiration and the day after OPEX day, finding average negative returns for the day after OPEX day in SPY. It concludes that the options expiration week effect does not reliably extend into the following week and may require parameters to be tradable.

The passage is a presidential inaugural address in which the speaker takes the constitutional oath and expresses gratitude while acknowledging the burdens of the office. He says he will rely on the Constitution, judicial decisions, and prior presidential practice, and will appoint executive officials with talents, integrity, and pure character. He outlines key presidential duties: command of the Army and Navy, making treaties and appointing ambassadors and officers with Senate consent, informing Congress on the state of the Union and recommending measures, and ensuring faithful law execution. He reaffirms that his administration will focus on the welfare of the whole country, preserve the government’s original purity, and follow republican doctrines. He states that the Army and Navy will receive attention to maintain efficiency, warns against entangling alliances and emphasizes neutrality and peaceful diplomacy in foreign relations, and says he will require honesty, capacity, and fidelity for appointments. He plans to recommend constitutional measures to encourage and protect agriculture, commerce, and manufactures, improve rivers and harbors, address public debt, enforce accountability, and promote economy, while leaving domestic policy regulation to Congress. He concludes by congratulating fellow citizens on national prosperity and calling for continued prudence, moderation, and liberal principles.

Vote counting for by-elections to four Lok Sabha and 10 Assembly constituencies is taking place on Thursday. Lok Sabha constituencies are Kairana and Nagaland, as well as Bhandara-Gondia and Palghar; Assembly seats are Palus Kadegaon, Noorpur, Jokihat, Gomia, Silli, Chengannur, Ampati, Shahkot, Tharali, and Maheshtala. The bypolls are significant for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and opposition parties, including Congress. Kairana is being closely watched, with BJP facing RLD, backed by BSP, SP, and Congress; BJP had campaigned after defeat in Gorakhpur and Phulpur by-elections. In Maharashtra, BJP, Shiv Sena, NCP, and Congress campaigned for Palghar and Bhandara-Gondia. Elections in Kairana followed the vacancy after BJP leader Hukum Singh’s death in February, and his daughter Mriganka Singh is the BJP candidate. In Maharashtra, Palghar is a reserved seat previously held by BJP, which became vacant after sitting BJP MP Chintaman Wanga’s death in January.

The passage describes an under-sink organizer with a sliding storage basket and references drawings labeled FIGS. 1–9, including multiple perspective, elevational, plan, bottom plan, and exploded perspective views. It also states that broken lines in the drawings indicate parts of the organizer that do not form part of the claimed design.

The lecture outlines how to calculate and interpret a corporate carbon footprint using a WidgetCo case study for chair manufacturing and distribution. It explains that the process is mostly data gathering and emissions-factor application, including electricity and direct facility emissions, and transportation modeled using methods such as ton-miles or fuel consumption. It discusses common calculation issues, such as misusing aggregated shipment data and using appropriate emissions factors and units. The lecture covers emissions “scopes”: scope 1 (direct emissions), scope 2 (indirect emissions from purchased electricity), and scope 3 (other indirect emissions), noting that organizational boundary choices drive what is included and can involve discretion, especially for scope 3. It also discusses why companies disclose or avoid disclosure, how standards like the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and programs like the Carbon Disclosure Project shape reporting expectations, and why comparisons between competitors can be misleading due to different boundary definitions and ownership of activities. The lecture concludes by setting up next classes on life cycle assessment and product-level comparisons.

The speaker discusses how their team played against an opponent in the first period and says things became tougher for the other team as play continued. They expect the opponent to come out angry and hungry in Game 2, and stress the need for early discipline, staying physical, and capitalizing on scoring chances. The speaker says in the previous game every puck they shot went in, which they don’t usually see in playoffs, and notes they must do more than in that game against goalie Belfour. They also mention motivating factors like being in the Stanley Cup final and emphasize that tomorrow’s game starts from zero. The passage includes comments on leadership and player development involving Jason Midway through the season, and reflects on their goalie’s and team’s quality and resilience, as well as the importance of hard skating and going hard to the net.

Noma is a severe, deadly gangrenous disease affecting the mouth and other facial tissues, associated with poverty and currently prevalent in Sub-Saharan Africa, with more cases described in northern Nigeria than elsewhere. This retrospective study used health records from the Noma Children’s Hospital in Sokoto, Nigeria, collecting data on consecutive patients diagnosed with noma from 1999 to 2024 and residing in northern Nigerian states or the Federal Capital Territory at diagnosis. Using a World Health Organization (WHO) method, the study estimated an overall incidence of 114.5 cases per 100,000 population between 1999 and 2024, with an annual average and median incidence of 4.4 and 2.2 cases per 100,000. Incidence varied annually from 0.2 cases per 100,000 (2014) to 21.3 cases per 100,000 (2021), and increased significantly between 2020 and 2024. Among 1,383 patients, most presented with acute noma (67.3%) and, within acute disease (stages 1–3), most had gangrene (stage 3, 59.7%) compared with oedema (stage 2, 7.3%) or ANUG (stage 1, 0.4%). The study concludes that noma incidence was highest in states such as Sokoto, Kebbi, and Zamfara, lowest in Adamawa, incidence was highest among children below 10 years old, and gangrene presentations were significantly more common than oedema or ANUG.

The passage describes how COVID-19 and a February 2023 earthquake led to distance education becoming prominent in Turkey, including in higher education and mathematics courses. It explains e-learning and technology integration, outlines a framework of barriers (first-order/external and second-order/intrinsic, plus design and classroom management), and identifies that shifting teaching online creates challenges requiring new teaching methods. The study uses Q methodology to examine barriers to distance education among 13 Turkish university faculty members in mathematics education who switched to online teaching due to the earthquake, using 50 statements developed from prior research. Factor analysis resulted in three factors: student-related barriers (Factor 1), technology-related barriers (Factor 2), and pedagogical/curriculum-related barriers (Factor 4), with “teacher-related barriers” not emerging as a distinct factor load. The findings indicate the strongest perceived barriers come from curriculum/pedagogy, followed by teachers, then school/technology deficiencies, and lastly student barriers; participants generally viewed distance education as not sufficient on its own for mathematics and preferred blended or mixed models.

Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge visited Tottenham Hotspur’s home at Hotspur Way in London, where he met Tottenham player Victor Wanyama and head coach Mauricio Pochettino, along with Tottenham team members and coach Patrick Sang. Kipchoge thanked them for the “wonderful day” after his third London Marathon title, and Wanyama congratulated him. The passage also notes that Kipchoge was crowned World Marathon majors champion and is expected to attempt Dennis Kimetto’s world record at the September Berlin Marathon.

Noe Martinez Paredes appeals his guilty-plea conviction and 57-month sentence for conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. His counsel filed an Anders brief stating there are no grounds for relief and a motion to withdraw. The court allowed a pro se supplemental brief, but none was filed. After independent review, the court found no arguable grounds for relief, granted counsel’s motion to withdraw, and affirmed the judgment.

The passage describes a patent application that is a continuation of several prior U.S. applications and claims priority to a provisional application titled “SECURE AND ZERO KNOWLEDGE DATA SHARING FOR CLOUD APPLICATIONS.” It provides background on the need to securely share encrypted data, particularly personal health information, while addressing risks of key exposure, burdens from electronic medical record requirements, and limitations of cloud storage where encryption control may rest with the provider.  

The summary of the invention states that some embodiments use layered encryption with multiple entry points, including derived keys from a user password and from a challenge question, and a key hierarchy structure to protect data encryption keys. Encrypted data and keys are handled such that the server/cloud provider does not have access to encrypted content or the keys needed to decrypt it (“zero knowledge”). It further outlines secure sharing approaches between users and groups using asymmetric encryption (public/private keys) and a shared data key hierarchy structure that enables authorized group members to access and update encrypted data while keeping decryption keys client-side. The passage also includes descriptions of system components, client/server interactions over networks (e.g., via TLS), key derivation/encryption steps, login/registration processes, and example “enumerated embodiments” describing methods for decrypting shared encrypted data and for deriving keys based on user-provided credentials.

The Senate approved on third and final reading the unified national identification system bill (Senate Bill No. 1738) with 17 affirmative votes, two negative votes, and no abstentions. The bill would establish a single official identification for all citizens and foreign residents, assigning each person a “PhilSys Number” incorporated into government identification systems, with the Philippine Statistics Authority acting as the “PhilSys Registry.” The sponsor, Senator Panfilo M. Lacson, said the system could help law enforcers deter criminality and terrorism and described authentication against registry information. He said privacy protections are included, with PhilSys number release subject to consent, public health and safety risk, a court order, or when the registered person requests access. If enacted, the system is expected to be rolled out in 2019, supported by P2 billion allotted by the Department of Budget and Management.

Researchers report that bacteria naturally found on grape plant leaves can degrade guaiacol, a volatile phenol linked to smoke taint’s ashy aftertaste in wildfire-tainted wine. The team isolated two guaiacol-degrading strains from chardonnay and cabernet sauvignon plants, showed that guaiacol became barely detectable after 96 hours in guaiacol-only conditions, and identified a gene responsible for guaiacol degradation that was required for the bacteria to consume the compound. The researchers note the strains may be choosy and that other volatile phenols also cause smoke taint, requiring further work on the grape plant microbiome. The passage says microbial approaches could be more specific than current treatments such as activated charcoal filtering, which can also remove desirable wine components like color.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality filed a draft red herring prospectus with SEBI for an IPO. The offer includes a fresh issue worth Rs 200 crore and an offer for sale of 61.79 lakh shares, comprising 14.22% of the company’s post-offer paid-up capital. It includes a reservation of up to 1.5 lakh equity shares for eligible employees, and the company will not receive proceeds from the offer for sale. Net proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to set up new restaurants in India, repay loans, and for general corporate purposes. The company operates Barbeque Nation restaurants in India and Dubai. The IPO will be conducted through book building, with allocation limits for qualified institutional buyers, non-institutional bidders, and retail investors.

Andy Penn must present positive news at Telstra’s investor day as the share price has been falling following a downgrade of earnings forecasts. The situation worsened when S&P Global downgraded Telstra, citing a diminished role in the industry and difficulty shifting from telco to tech. Analysts expect Telstra may significantly cut dividends in the 2019 financial year, adding pressure on Penn to show a path to improved earnings after earnings decline when NBN compensation payments end. However, negative analyst commentary in May has eased, with UBS upgrading to buy and Morgan Stanley offering more optimistic outlook.

Six months after Abby Williams and Libby German were killed near the Monon High Bridge in Delphi, police say there are still no arrests. Indiana State Police say the case is not cold and that investigators continue working with more than 24,000 tips and leads, including over 3,000 tips connected to a sketch released July 17. Investigators are testing and comparing DNA found at the crime scene almost daily to determine whether it belongs to the victims, known family members, or the suspect. First Sgt. Jerry Holeman said detectives are reviewing old evidence and tips to ensure nothing was missed, and he hopes that by the one-year anniversary they will identify a person of interest and be ready for court.

Ajay Bodke of Prabhudas Lilladher says retail investors need not worry about the LTCG tax, arguing equities remain the only asset class with inflation-beating returns on a post-tax basis and that 10% LTCG is fair. He points to grandfathering of gains up to January 31 and relief for LTCG up to Rs 1 lakh per year, and suggests investors use market dips to buy equities. Bodke highlights near-medium term equity upside triggers including a revival in corporate earnings, policy disruptions from GST and demonetization being behind, macroeconomic factors within attractive levels versus other emerging economies, range-bound crude oil prices, and India’s GDP growth estimate of 7.5% for FY18-19. He also discusses expectations that RBI may find it hard to maintain a neutral stance due to global central bank tightening and domestic fiscal slippage concerns, and notes strong voluntary equity inflows via SIPs and DIIs outperforming FIIs. In comparing asset classes, he states Sensex has delivered 4–6x returns every 10 years and that gold returns have been inferior, while longer holding periods reduce the probability of losing money. He identifies the insurance sector and certain retail-focused private BFSI players as promising for attractive returns.

Rocky the Red Hawk celebrated his 16th birthday at Montclair State University by handing out free bagels and candy, dancing around campus, and taking photos with students. The Student Center Ballrooms featured campus organizations with free gifts, GIF and photo booths, cupcakes, and a prize wheel. Students and faculty were also encouraged to donate to a local food pantry, and the event included a speech by President Susan Cole, singing happy birthday, and cake. Near the end, raffles awarded prizes such as t-shirts, a $100 university bookstore gift card, and a parking pass, and Rocky later distributed remaining cupcakes and candy around campus.

The passage lists multiple specification-update issues for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. It describes failures and limitations across interfaces such as GLIU (including unexpected MSR address flag behavior and debug port hangs), UART access during DMA, 8237 software DMA memory write failures, PCI I/O-cycle address behavior that can hang the system, PIC interrupt handling problems with clock gating, PIT timing/operation deviations, PRD alignment and prefetch hazards affecting UDMA behavior, UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination, ACPI PM1 register byte-access hang and PMC register corruption from incorrect byte/word writes, KEL/SI/O emulation issues, SMBus/SMB controller status-bit clearing behavior, wake event inputs not working in ACPI S3, and several sleep/standby-related problems including SLEEP signal deassertion and LOWBAT_FLAG not being set after abnormal standby. For many items, it provides implications and workarounds or resolutions, such as avoiding certain access modes, using specific alignment rules, disabling features like debug port or automatic clock gating in relevant cases, and using external circuits or software workarounds.

Police bodycam footage released by Wildwood Police shows Emily Weinman, a 20-year-old mother, being arrested after refusing to give officers her last name while they checked whether she was drinking underage during Memorial Day weekend in New Jersey. Although breathalysed and passing, she questioned the officers’ continued paperwork because the alcohol was unopened, and the situation escalated as officers said she was obstructing and “causing a scene.” The footage includes claims by an officer arriving later that she tried kicking, and she is heard screaming during the arrest. Wildwood Mayor Ernie Troian said the footage would “vindicate” the police. The officers were reassigned to desk duty pending an investigation. Weinman was charged with multiple offenses, including aggravated assault, disorderly conduct, resisting arrest, obstruction, and minor in possession of alcohol.

The passage describes a study of interdisciplinary research (IDR) in medical PubMed articles using correlation networks of medical concepts (MeSH terms). IDR is defined as integrating information and perspectives from two or more disciplines. The authors compare networks built from articles in highly impactful medical journals (top 10% by SCImago Journal Rank) versus less-/not-impactful journals across years 1999, 2010, and 2022, with an additional NI dataset built from one month (June) to reduce sample-size effects.

Using MeSH C-branch second-level “Disease” terms, the authors construct cosine-normalized co-occurrence networks, filter isolated nodes, and analyze network properties including node strength (coherence), average shortest path length (compactness), betweenness (bridging), modularity (community structure), global clustering coefficient, and strength assortativity. Results reported in the passage indicate that non-impactful journals show higher average node strength and higher network density, while impactful journals have higher modularity. The study also identifies stable “inner cores” across decades in the original networks, with certain concepts appearing in all cores, and finds that cancer-related research is a main driver of interdisciplinarity in medical science. 

To examine differences between impactful and less-impactful networks, the authors subtract NI-June link weights from impactful (I) link weights to form positive and negative difference networks. They find a weak tendency for stronger differences to co-locate, and that differences cluster around topic areas that change substantially over time. They conclude that impactful journals tend to publish relatively more disciplinary-based work, while both journal groups agree on a universal core knowledge structure in medicine that remains stable across decades. The passage further suggests that evaluation, guideline evidence standards, and reporting/compliance infrastructures may structurally disadvantage IDR at elite journals, and proposes accommodating IDR evaluation within existing reporting frameworks as a potential improvement.

A Legislative Analyst’s Office report says Gov. Jerry Brown’s administration has a “weak justification” for a short tentative one-year contract with the California Correctional Peace Officers Association offering a 5 percent raise to about 27,000 employees. The analyst found no evidence of recruitment or retention problems and said compensation levels likely are sufficient to meet staffing needs. The report compares the deal to other state labor agreements with 5 percent base wage increases and notes smaller unions received similar raises for other job classifications. It also cites data suggesting the state can recruit entry-level correctional officers, that mid-career staffing is steady, and that correctional officer wages have exceeded inflation since 2001. The analyst estimates wages would be 67 percent higher than 2001–02, while warning the contract could cost more due to overtime and pension contributions; the administration estimated $338 million over two years. CCPOA members are voting on the contract, and the Legislature must also approve it.

Police in Cleveland said they could not determine what triggered Steve Stephens after he posted Facebook footage of killing Robert Godwin Sr., a 74-year-old former foundry worker. Authorities offered a $50,000 reward and expanded a manhunt nationwide for Stephens, whose last cellphone signal was detected in Erie, Pennsylvania. In the video, Stephens told Godwin that a woman’s name was the reason violence was about to happen; the woman, Joy Lane, said they had been in a relationship for several years. Godwin’s daughter said he was collecting aluminum cans and was not harming anyone. Police received many tips, and nine Philadelphia schools were temporarily locked down for possible sightings. Stephens, 37, worked at Beech Brook assisting vulnerable youth; some people described him as kind and pleasant, while others said he had a gambling problem and filed for bankruptcy. Investigators said Godwin was the only victim linked to Stephens so far, despite his separate Facebook claim that he killed more than a dozen people.

Camp America is a summer program that students across the country, including Coventry and Warwickshire, can apply to in order to work abroad and have time to travel afterward. It offers placements at more than 8,000 camps across the USA, including locations on both the east and west coasts, and applications can be submitted as soon as possible for the best chance of getting a place. Camp America also holds a UK recruitment fair in January and February with over 200 American camps hiring on the spot. A former camper, Mully, describes a typical day at a camp in Pennsylvania and says the job is fast-paced but offers “unbeatable” perks. For £599, Camp America provides an all-inclusive package with application fees, comprehensive medical insurance, a 30-day travel period, and return flights, plus pocket money of $650–$1200. The experience is described as helping participants develop skills and shape their lives.

Archaeologists have found remains of the Great Heathen Army, a Viking force known from Anglo-Saxon sources, in a mass grave beside St. Wystan’s church in Repton, Derbyshire, dated to winter 874. A new Antiquity paper using carbon dating re-evaluates earlier estimates and concludes the bones match the first permanent Norse invasion of Britain, with some earlier results skewed by a high-seafood diet causing a “marine reservoir effect.” The study describes burial practices including a double grave with a sword and a silver Thor’s hammer pendant, evidence of severe injuries, a boar’s tusk interred between legs, and four child burials marked with stone and a sheep’s jawbone. It reports that the mass burial contained members of the Viking Great Army and supports the chronology of Viking use of the church area, while emphasizing the importance of applying marine reservoir corrections to radiocarbon dates from human bone.

The lecture introduces plasma diagnostics through plasma spectroscopy and focuses on simplified equilibria used to model atomic states and emitted photons. It contrasts complete thermodynamic equilibrium (Boltzmann occupation with balanced processes and a single shared temperature), local thermodynamic equilibrium (optically thin, radiative processes neglected, collisional processes dominate, leading to Saha equilibrium for ionization states), and corona equilibrium (collisional excitation balanced by spontaneous radiative de-excitation in optically thin, low-density plasmas, with up and down processes not balanced). It then describes non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (nLTE), where many excitation and de-excitation processes must be solved, with examples such as photo-ionized plasmas where photoionization can dominate over collisions. The workflow for modeling spectra includes choosing an equilibrium, calculating ionization and excited-state populations, computing line strengths, predicting spectra with possible radiation transport and detector response, and fitting model outputs to experimental data; line ratios can provide temperature estimates using Saha equilibrium. The lecture also covers X-ray spectroscopy nomenclature (K-shell lines, Kα strongest, impurity signatures) and X-ray filtering via K and L absorption edges. Finally, it explains X-ray imaging approaches (no lenses for X-rays; pinhole imaging with geometric and diffraction blur; bent-crystal monochromatic imaging) and discusses detector types including film, image plates, time-gated cameras, and streak cameras, along with their timing and practical tradeoffs.

The passage describes a study by Aarhus University researchers on how concentrating milk on farms using reverse osmosis affects milk quality. Reverse osmosis is widely used at dairies to remove water, but the researchers aimed to assess key quality parameters—protein breakdown, free fatty acids (FFA), and total bacterial count—when concentration occurs on-farm. They note that farm concentration leaves milk unpasteurized, making it more delicate. In experiments using both ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis, reverse osmosis did not negatively affect total bacterial count, FFA levels, or protein breakdown, and the concentrated milk could be used for cheese and milk powder. Powder quality and durability from concentrated milk matched that from ordinary milk, while cheese showed a minor difference in enzyme reaction and coagulated about ten minutes later than regular milk. The researchers also discuss interest from farmers, but dairy skepticism about finances and handling; Arla is making calculations balancing energy consumption and investments against cost savings.

Shares in agriculture-related companies rose up to 13 percent on Wednesday after the government increased the minimum support price (MSP) for paddy by a record Rs 200 per quintal. Kohinoor Foods, LT Foods, and Chaman Lal Setia Exports gained on BSE, and fertiliser stocks also rose. Vinod Nair said the market gained momentum due to better auto sales and the MSP increase, which he expected to boost rural income and demand. The cabinet approved MSP for 14 kharif crops for the 2018-19 season.

Nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. Safe isolation between an SNP-protected guest and its host requires restricting the types of exceptions and interrupt dispatch that can be performed in the guest. Isolated guests are expected to run with SNP RestrictInjection active, limiting the host to ringing a doorbell with a #HV exception. The host communicates virtualization-architecture-specific information (such as Virtio or VMBus messages) that is delivered in a form understood by guest drivers; however, message dispatch is typically driven by interrupt delivery by the operating system. The document discusses defining a common format for notifications integral to OS functionality while avoiding a common format for information normally interpreted only by drivers.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while he was off work to observe Rosh Hashanah. Conservatives said past blog posts attributed to Rosenzweig criticized President Donald Trump, including claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” Rosenzweig worked on economic crimes and joined the U.S. attorney’s office in September 2020. The Justice Department also fired three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who previously worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith said he was dismayed by dismissals of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law.

The British Secretary of State sent observations to the British Ambassador, for the notice of the United States Government, alongside a translation of the Allied note. The note says that although the President wants peace soon and lasting, peace’s durability depends on its character and on international relations that are not defective. It attributes recent calamities to great powers seeking domination, weak enforcement mechanisms in international law, and mismatched borders and internal constitutions with peoples’ aspirations. It argues that allied proposed European map changes would mitigate these issues. It also contends that expelling the Turks from Europe is now justified because circumstances have changed, claiming German-supported Turkish rule has become aggressive and involved in massacres. The note states that territorial changes may reduce war occasions but cannot ensure security against recurrence, warning that Germany could still pursue dominance using military systems and resources. It argues that treaties and international laws are insufficient, citing Germany’s rejection of arbitration treaties and its promotion of war and military preparation. It concludes that no state can consider its rights secure with only a solemn treaty if Germany remains the same.

The passage discusses 0% and low-interest credit card offers and how they can benefit consumers, noting that card deals change frequently. It states that CompareCards selects cards based on criteria such as long 0% Intro APR periods (ranging from 12 to 21 months) and that it received compensation without influencing its ratings or reviews. In a thermal alarm event, the system enters a Faulted Standby state. There is no self-recovery mechanism for the PMC because the thermal alarm is in the Work domain, not the Standby domain. While in Faulted Standby, the thermal alarm timer is blocked by the Work/Standby interface, so the alarm state outside the component cannot be detected in Standby because the alarm ball is in the working power domain. After exiting Standby, the thermal alarm (THRM_ALRM#) is considered again; if it is still asserted, its timer starts again. The implications state that the thermal alarm removes power to cool the system; after a delay, the system powers up. If the alarm does not de-assert within a specified delay, the system is forced back into Standby, repeating the process until the thermal alarm de-asserts.

The passage compares dating to choosing a content marketing partner, using personal experience to frame five “dating tips.” It advises finding aligned interests, “dating around” by interviewing multiple candidates, not being misled by polished presentations by requesting references and examples of results, knowing what you want by listing criteria and desired services, and starting with a trial period before committing. Play action in football is a pass play designed to look like a run to deceive the defense. The quarterback drops back as if to hand the ball off, then holds it, bootlegs, and looks for an open wide receiver downfield. It works best when the offense sells the run, including offensive line run protection that quickly switches to pass protection, and it can create space behind linebackers and safeties. Play action is effective when teams have established the run and when defenses overcommit, such as in short-yardage, goal line, and red zone situations; teams often use it about 30–40% of the time. Common concepts include Double Post (two identical deep post routes after a fake) and Bubble Y Over (a spread play with multiple quick and deep passing options). Play action differs from Run Pass Option (RPO), which can become either a run or a pass based on the quarterback’s decision after the snap, while play action always remains a pass.

The passage describes Resolute Marine Energy’s (RME) wave-driven desalination technology, Wave O™, and the company’s plans to enter South Africa’s water market. The passage concludes that RME must choose among these approaches while also considering startup funding, investor appeal, and a potential exit strategy.

The United States appealed a Federal Claims Court judgment awarding Christine H. Roberts’ estate $250,000 in benefits under the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Act after Roberts died a few months following her son, Sheriff Harold Ray Presley’s, death in July 2001. The Bureau had denied the estate’s claim, concluding Roberts had not successfully filed a claim before her death and that her death precluded payment. The trial court reversed, finding Roberts met filing requirements and that eligibility is determined at the time of the public safety officer’s death, so a beneficiary’s later death does not terminate eligibility. On de novo review, the appeals court affirmed, holding that the statute requires payment based on whether the beneficiary was surviving at the officer’s death and does not impose an additional requirement to remain alive until payment is issued. A dissent argued the statute does not specifically address whether estates are eligible recipients and would defer to the agency’s regulations requiring payment only to a living payee.

Apixaban treatment compliance was measured as the percentage of prescribed drug taken. Mean compliance was comparable between the Primary SOC group and the Additional Educational Program group, with >95% at Weeks 4, 12, and 24, and >94% at Week 48 across all three Study Part 2 groups. Primary efficacy results showed similar adherence at 24 weeks between the Primary SOC group (91.64%) and the Additional Educational Program group (91.88%) with no significant difference; adherence was also comparable at Weeks 4 and 12. Adherence decreased from Week 12 to Week 24 and from Week 24 to Week 48 in both groups, with no significant between-group differences from 24 to 48 weeks and no significant differences from first dose to Week 48. Persistence at 24 weeks was similar between groups, and persistence at 48 weeks showed no significant differences. Fully adherent subjects were similarly distributed between groups, with median duration of full adherence reported for each group. Logit analyses identified predictors of non-adherence at 24 and 48 weeks, with effects varying by group and, in some cases, no significant predictors in the Additional Educational Program group at 24 weeks. Subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction for some adherence endpoints, but significant interactions were reported for adherence change from Week 24 to Week 48 by atrial fibrillation type and by sex. Safety outcomes at 24 and 48 weeks were similar between study groups, with comparable rates of AEs, serious AEs, discontinuation due to AEs, and bleeding events. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high through 24 weeks and sustained to 48 weeks, and that a proactive educational program did not add adherence or persistence benefits.

Spontaneous symmetry breaking in condensed matter systems is associated with emergent quantum phenomena such as magnetism, superconductivity, charge/spin density waves, and electronic nematic phases, where rotational symmetry breaks while translational invariance is preserved. This work focuses on CoSn2, a structurally simple, three-dimensional intermetallic, where X-ray diffraction, magnetotransport, and polarization-dependent ARPES reveal symmetry breaking below 25 K. In zero-field resistivity, a slope change occurs below 25 K, while specific heat shows no anomaly and susceptibility remains paramagnetic, indicating no magnetic transition. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction finds extremely weak commensurate satellite reflections at 22 K (persisting to 10 K) and a reduction of symmetry from tetragonal I4/mcm to an acentric monoclinic C2 structure with a doubling of the a and c axes. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance shows four-fold symmetry above 40 K and a clear transition to two-fold symmetry below 20–25 K, consistent with the structural symmetry lowering. Phonon calculations show no imaginary frequencies, while electronic susceptibility calculations suggest an electronically driven instability that can break rotational symmetry, potentially via nematic order. Polarization-dependent ARPES shows fourfold-symmetric Fermi surface intensity under linear horizontal polarization but strong intensity asymmetry under linear vertical polarization, suggesting orbital-selective anisotropy. The study also reports evidence for Dirac-like carriers through large linear magnetoresistance and ARPES observations, and concludes that CoSn2 is a platform for symmetry breaking in an itinerant, nonmagnetic nodal line semimetal.
