Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative condition common in the elderly, marked by amyloid beta and tau plaques and progressive symptoms. AD typically presents at or after age 65 (late-onset), with a smaller subset developing in the 30s–50s (early-onset). The paper describes three phases: preclinical AD, mild cognitive impairment due to AD (AD MCI, maintaining independence), and dementia due to AD (AD dementia, interfering with daily living). AD is the leading cause of dementia, but diagnosis is clinically challenging, with primary care physicians reporting discomfort and studies estimating misdiagnosis rates of 12–23%, partly because symptoms overlap with other dementia causes and reversible conditions.  

The objective is to develop an improved AD diagnostic tool using a causal Bayesian Network (BN) that combines medical knowledge with data. The model distinguishes between having AD (“suspected AD”) and being formally diagnosed, updating prior probabilities as new evidence is observed. It is structured using “medical idioms” and includes variables from validated diagnostic criteria, focusing clinically on AD MCI and AD dementia. Key model components include risk factors (e.g., age, family history, certain mutations, traumatic brain injury), signs/symptoms and medical tests (cognitive and biomarker tests), other dementia and reversible conditions, comorbidities, complications, dementia severity, and treatments.  

Parameters are estimated from multiple sources, including the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set (NACC UDS), plus literature and knowledge-based judgment. Validation includes internal checks that the model’s prior aligns with AD prevalence, and external scenario testing showing how probability estimates change with additional information (e.g., explaining-away effects and increased certainty with positive biomarker tests). The paper concludes that the model can serve as a complementary, interpretable diagnostic aid that supports “what-if” analysis, while noting limitations such as simplified modeling of non-AD causes, reliance on data from already diagnosed individuals, some missing causal relationships, and some parameters set manually.

Const. Ken Lam, the Toronto police officer who apprehended the sole suspect in Monday’s van attack, was identified by police and praised by experts for his handling of the deadly incident. Video described Lam confronting a man by a damaged white van, giving verbal commands and eventually approaching without firing; the man tossed aside an object and was handcuffed. The incident lasted 37 seconds, and police say there is no evidence the man was armed. The death toll reached 10 by late Tuesday, with 15 injured, and Alek Minassian is named as the lone suspect, charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder and 13 counts of attempted murder. The passage also notes prior criticism of Toronto police tactics after other incidents and mentions a motion to issue more Tasers and review use-of-force options.

Police in Colombia report a 92% fall in kidnappings since 2000, saying 188 people were abducted in 2016. Police attributed the decline to a peace deal with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc) and improved security, and said the Farc kidnapped no one in 2016 after signing a peace deal in November that ended 52 years of conflict. Police said 88% of 2016 kidnappings were by “common criminals,” 11% by organized crime gangs, and 1% by the National Liberation Army (ELN). The ELN has resisted releasing its last hostage, and exploratory peace talks scheduled for October were cancelled after it refused to free former Congressman Odin Sanchez ahead of talks. The passage also says Mexico has surpassed Colombia as the Americas’ top abduction country, with the Mexican government estimating about 1,000 kidnappings a year while a survey suggests about 64,500 for 2015.

The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection issued a construction permit Tuesday to the Meadville Area Water Authority to install fluoridation facilities and equipment. The permit authorizes only construction and installation, not operation or fluoridating finished water. After bidding and completing the work, MAWA must apply for and receive an operations permit before adding fluoride, and DEP will inspect the system to ensure it is properly installed and meets safety requirements. Officials said it was too early to estimate a completion timeline, and the MAWA board is expected to address bidding and construction timing at its July 18 monthly meeting.

The passage is an outline and partial content of the “Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide.” It describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine and page migration concept, including requirements such as IOMMU enablement and 4K-aligned system physical addresses for page moves. It explains how TMPM offloads migration by pausing DMA to a page while copying page content and updating IOMMU mappings, and how TMPM can migrate pages owned by guests using AMD SEV/SNP. It outlines page migration commands (page move for I/O targets and guest pages), a pre-migration reverse map table state for SNP guest migration, and multi-page command operation using page migration lists and per-page status handling (PM_SUCCESS, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS, and retry-related codes like PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE). It covers performance guidelines (up to 128 pages per command), ring buffer operation and interrupt behavior, restrictions on migratable data structures (ring buffer and IOMMU-related structures do not support migration), and requirements/behavior for TMPM firmware reload, including differences by EPYC family using PM_GET_CAPABILITIES. The passage also includes various command and status/error-handling details, including PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST operational flow and constraints such as unsupported DMA for PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST and possible DMA aborts on concurrent access.

Susan Ann Vansickle was arrested for obstructing a public highway in a road district in Knox County, where Hugh Brown was road overseer. She waived a preliminary examination and entered a recognizance to appear in circuit court, was later indicted, and after a nolle prosequi she sued Brown for malicious prosecution. The court excluded testimony about the arresting officer’s uncivil and insulting conduct because it was not connected to Brown unless instigated by him, and it excluded a prior trespass judgment between William Vansickle and Brown and certain county court proceedings as irrelevant to issues of probable cause and malice. Evidence of verbal directions from the county court to Brown about opening the road was admitted to show good faith and lack of malice. Brown was permitted to testify he acted in good faith and had no ill-feelings. The opinion addresses jury instructions on probable cause and malice, concluding that malice is required and that probable cause depends on the defendant’s belief based on reasonable grounds. The circuit court’s judgment was affirmed.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 1, 2022 (earliest event reported), covering the August 8, 2022 completion of the issuance and sale of $1,000,000,000 3.250% Notes due 2029, $1,500,000,000 3.350% Notes due 2032, $1,750,000,000 3.950% Notes due 2052, and $1,250,000,000 4.100% Notes due 2062. The Yield Hog Dividend Growth Portfolio is down about 2% after nearly seven months, but its annualized dividend income has grown from $4,094 at inception (Sept. 30) to $4,369 (up about 6.7%) as 17 of 22 stocks increased dividends and dividends were reinvested. The passage discusses sustainable development and education for sustainable development (often used interchangeably with sustainable development) and their global relevance, including Agenda 2030 and UNESCO’s definition. It notes that, although frameworks and policies exist, sustainability education is still under-addressed in many schools, including within South Africa’s Technology curriculum. The study investigates pedagogical approaches for teaching education for sustainable development in South African Technology Education, guided by three research questions about teachers’ knowledge, how Technology content informs teaching, and which pedagogical approaches teachers can use.  

Using a qualitative descriptive case study design, the research interviewed and observed eight Senior Phase Technology teachers from Mpumalanga Province and analyzed data through inductive content analysis with triangulation and member-checking. Results show that teachers understand education for sustainable development, emphasizing resource preservation and environmentally friendly practices, and they identify opportunities for integrating sustainability through technology-driven solutions, design processes, and investigative approaches. However, the classroom practices observed did not always reflect these opportunities, with demonstrations and lectures being more common than collaborative learning. The study concludes that collaborative learning is a promising approach for sustainability education in Technology, and it provides recommendations for curriculum and teaching improvements, including value transformation, responsible resource use, practical topics like processing and recycling, and collaborative, critical problem-solving learning.

Breast cancer patients have lower quality of life, and chemotherapy can worsen symptoms. Cannabinoids from Cannabis sativa are presented as a complementary option for reducing chemotherapy-related pain and tumor-associated symptoms, with a pilot study reporting that CBD and THC were generally well tolerated and improved total symptom distress scores. The passage also describes mouse and experimental evidence for anti-tumor effects of cannabinoids and discusses the microbiota, including intestinal and breast skin microbial changes, as possible contributors to breast cancer and related inflammation. It outlines Thai-produced cannabis oils (Metta Osot and Ganja Oil) and their inclusion in essential medicines, and reports preliminary findings from Thai patients on baseline quality of life and symptoms. The randomized, placebo-controlled trial will recruit 90 adult breast cancer women receiving chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital in Thailand, assigning them to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo once daily for 90 days. The study aims to assess symptoms (ESAS), quality of life, adverse effects, microbiome changes, cytokines, bacterial metabolites, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacogenetics, with multiple visits for baseline and post-treatment sampling and monitoring.

The passage explains how soccer position numbers have evolved. It says number schemes began in England in the 1920s, assigning numbers from back to front and right to left in a 2-3-5 formation, and lists the original numbers and roles on jerseys. It then describes changes with the 1950s “W-M” formation, including shifting inside forwards and moving the center halfback toward defense, along with associated “Number 9” and “Number 10” references for central attackers and set-back scorers/playmakers. In the 1960s, experimentation led to overlapping roles, “Total Football,” and greater freedom for players to choose numbers regardless of position; it also notes halfbacks being called midfielders and further shifts in defense and midfield roles. Beginning in 2012, U.S. Soccer attempted to standardize position names and numbers using a 4-3-3-based system, and it describes expected “position profiles” for each number based on “Technical, Tactical, Physical, and Mental (TTPM)” attributes. It also mentions terms like “False 9” and “Double-9s.”

Jonathan Huberdeau scored 7.7 seconds left in the third period to give the Florida Panthers a 3-2 win over the Detroit Red Wings. Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored for Florida, with Harri Sateri making 26 saves for his third straight NHL win. Keith Yandle had two assists. Detroit’s Danny DeKeyser scored both goals, and Petr Mrazek stopped 30 shots. After a tied 2, Huberdeau slid a rebound under Mrazek’s pad; Detroit challenged for goalie interference, but the call stood. Barkov scored to break a 1-1 tie in the second period, and DeKeyser later tied it. Ekblad scored early in the first period, and DeKeyser tied the game again in the second. Notes included Alex Petrovic’s 200th NHL game, Jamie McGinn’s return, and DeKeyser’s 350th NHL game. The Red Wings host the Boston Bruins Tuesday, and the Panthers host the Vancouver Canucks Tuesday.

The passage explains that punters, though often overlooked by fans, play a critical role in flipping field position after offenses fail to advance, by punting the ball with hang-time, accuracy, and touch to help coverage teams down opponents quickly. It describes punter responsibilities such as punting from deep behind the line of scrimmage, providing leg strength and finesse for distance and placement (including inside the 20), executing different trajectories and spins, and occasionally performing fake punts or acting as holders for extra points and field goals. It also distinguishes punting from kickoffs/field goals/extra points, lists basic skills (accuracy, leg strength, coordination, flexibility, creativity) and a general body estimate, names notable punters Shane Lechler and Ray Guy, and argues the position is important because it influences field position and scoring opportunities through factors like hang time and placement.

The passage describes a microservices architecture for cloud computing. It provides background on cloud data centers and network virtualization, then explains microservices as a way to partition functionality into wrappers that can be discovered and provisioned dynamically without requiring the system designer to know in advance which resources (e.g., CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, resource pools, virtual appliances, or hardware accelerators) will execute a function. The architecture includes host software using a microservices API, a microservices driver, and a service discovery function (SDF) that maintains a catalog of available microservices and mappings/configuration (e.g., FPGA gate configurations). It describes dynamic programming and provisioning of microservices, and “service chaining” where multiple microservices are linked in a single flow so results need not be passed back to host software between steps, reducing latency and request/response overhead. It also outlines registration and discovery flows (including a path ID and endpoints), message forwarding mechanisms, and a load-balancing engine that selects instances or spawns new ones based on catalog attributes and telemetry. The passage further includes example implementations related to microservice registration and discovery, including ontological databases and mapping API calls to native invocations.

Millennials are generally saving for retirement, with 71% saving for retirement and 39% classified as “super savers” saving more than 10% of their salary, according to studies cited in the passage. However, many are hesitant to invest, with 42% investing conservatively and a higher share holding investments in cash and stable options than older generations. The passage also notes that 18–29-year-olds report stock-market investing as scary or intimidating. It argues that avoiding stocks could put retirement security at risk and says the stock market’s risk should be put in perspective, while also suggesting options like building simple retirement portfolios or using robo-advisors.

The passage describes a Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures contract created by CME in 2019. It is 1/10 the size of the E-mini, trades electronically on CME Globex, and is financially settled by cash on expiry based on special opening quotes of the index (typically the 3rd Friday of the contract month). The contract trades Sunday 6:00 p.m. to Friday 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily maintenance break, and is listed in quarterly cycles (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec) for five consecutive quarters. One contract unit equals the index value multiplied by $5, is quoted in USD and cents per index point, and has a minimum price fluctuation of 0.25 index point (equivalent to $1.25) with a tick size of $1.25. The trading symbol is MES. The passage states the all-time high was 4808.25 (January 2022) and the all-time low was 2174.00 (March 2020), and it notes biggest risks come from adverse leveraged price movements. It also mentions the contract can be traded via futures brokers and that some brokers offer CFDs, which can be traded without contract expiry concerns.

The passage summarizes multiple media reports from May 2001 about President George W. Bush’s national energy plan and reactions to it. The Wall Street Journal describes how Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay met with Vice President Dick Cheney and pursued policies aimed at deregulating wholesale electricity, gaining open transmission access, and removing regulatory barriers, while also maintaining close ties to government and lobbying the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). It also outlines Enron’s trading and growth and efforts to influence FERC appointments. The Los Angeles Times report says the energy plan would favor traditional oil, gas, coal, construction, and some labor unions, while critics argue it offers limited incentives for renewables, energy-saving, consumers, and environmental goals; it details proposed infrastructure expansion and mentions concerns about climate change silence. Bloomberg reports include Japanese utility opposition to an Enron proposal to separate electricity generation and transmission, citing fears of California-style failures, and comments from Hiroji Ota supporting nuclear energy and criticizing Enron’s “unbundling” approach. Other items discuss residential and commercial real estate impacts from corporate relocation in Mumbai, U.S. and international praise and criticism of the Bush plan including environmental protests, reports from watchdog groups about energy-sector campaign contributions and cabinet ties, and a report that Enron plans to relinquish its stake in the Dolphin gas project.

The passage describes a PS4 Pro deal at Meijer confirmed as of 6:30 AM Eastern, based on the author’s test. It outlines steps to set up a Meijer mPerks account (including using a Google Voice number), enroll for a new account to get a 5% off coupon, find a $50 off PS4 Pro coupon by browsing the coupons under electronics and toys, and buy the PS4 Pro in-store at the $349.99 Sony price. At checkout, the credit card machine applies the 5% off and the $50 coupon, resulting in a calculated total of $282.50. The author says it is the lowest price seen during the holiday season and notes it is in-store only.

Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, a breakaway faction of the Indian National Congress, announced 11 candidates for next year’s Chhattisgarh assembly elections. Ajit Jogi, the party’s leader and former Chief Minister, said more than 11 names were finalized, with names of six sitting MLAs and 7–8 core committee members to be announced in later phases. He said the early announcement would give candidates time to plan and signal the party’s readiness to contest all 90 seats. The list includes three former MLAs, a retired IAS officer, and a physician; sources cited six sitting MLAs including Amit Jogi, Siyaram Kaushik, and RK Rai. The BJP vice president Sunil Soni criticized the list as a Congress “B team” and said the BJP is targeting 65-plus seats, while political observers said Jogi’s early announcement aims to surprise opponents and divert attention from controversy around his fake caste certificate case.

The passage describes a player’s and team’s performance in playoff overtime situations, emphasizing that the player has extensive playoff experience, has scored big goals, and contributes valuable time. It says the team feels good going into overtime, focuses on playing quickly without overthinking, and aims to win without fear. The passage also discusses the team’s year-long responsiveness and success, criticism of giving too much respect, and a focus on playing their usual game. It concludes that recent games have involved a noticeable difference on the ice, that players enjoyed their game, and that overtime is exciting and helps the player get better.

The passage is an email dated July 17, 2001, from Jean Munoz to numerous recipients. It compiles news clippings about California’s electricity crisis and related government actions, including plans by Gov. Gray Davis to expand state involvement in power purchasing and infrastructure; legislative debate over rescue packages for Southern California Edison and potential limits on direct-access electricity contracts; questions raised by a conflict-of-interest inquiry into energy consultants’ stock purchases; use of churches to sign up low-income customers for electricity discounts; and coverage of federal energy policy discussions led by President Bush and Vice President Cheney.

Google laid off more than 100 employees in design-related roles within its cloud unit, according to CNBC. The affected roles focused on using data, surveys, and other tools to understand user behaviors that inform product development and design. CNBC reports the layoffs targeted teams including “quantitative user experience research” and “platform and service experience,” along with adjacent teams, and that some affected U.S.-based employees were given until early December to find new roles. The layoffs come as Google prioritizes AI investment and is cutting headcount to improve efficiency.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 49.8 in September, indicating a smaller contraction than expected (49.6) and the strongest reading since March. Private surveyor RatingDog’s manufacturing PMI was 51.2, above economists’ forecast for 50.2 and also its highest since May. Despite the improvement, the official PMI remained below 50. The official non-manufacturing PMI edged down to 52.9, while RatingDog’s general services PMI eased to 50. The passage links the developments to Beijing’s efforts to curb industrial overcapacity amid sluggish domestic demand and global trade disruptions, including higher U.S. tariffs.

The passage explains that many DIY stores have different opening times over the Christmas break and provides opening-time information for Wickes, B&Q, Homebase, and Argos. It notes that customers should double-check specific local store times using each store’s online store finder or store locator. Wickes and B&Q operating hours are listed for Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year’s Eve, and New Year’s Day, with regional exceptions mentioned for B&Q (England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland, and Jersey). Homebase’s hours are listed for Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year’s Eve, and New Year’s Day, including that Scotland and Eire stores will be closed. Argos is described as operating during the festive break, with an advisory to check local times using its store locator.

The passage explains the Bond MOVE Index as a measure of U.S. interest rate volatility derived from implied volatility in 1-month OTC options. It notes that the MOVE Index, created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, rose sharply in 2022 amid rapid Federal Reserve rate increases and banking concerns, reaching 199 in March and trading near 118 afterward. It states that high MOVE Index levels generally do not indicate a good time to buy bonds and produce few signals. A backtest starting in 2002 tested a strategy using TLT that holds TLT when the MOVE Index is below its historical mean and sells when it rises above the mean, aiming to avoid periods of high volatility. The results are described as not super profitable overall, with reduced harm in 2022 and a maximum drawdown about half that of a buy-and-hold approach.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on November 15, 2018, reporting its quarter results for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. The company issued a press release that day, attached as Exhibit 99.1, and furnished CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress, attached as Exhibit 99.2, which would be posted on http://investor.nvidia.com after the report filing. The press release and CFO commentary were not deemed “filed” for Section 18 purposes or subject to related liabilities. The report includes Exhibit 99.1 (“NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2019”) and Exhibit 99.2 (CFO Commentary on Third Quarter Fiscal 2019 Results), signed by Colette M. Kress.

Vision on the soccer field supports pinpoint passing and helps defenders and goalkeepers read and respond to opposing attacks by seeing and dissecting positioning and movement. The passage says vision enables players to make split-second decisions and that learning and sports performance rely heavily on sight. It cites Pelé as having peripheral vision 30 percent greater than average and notes he studied geometry and chess. Coaches emphasize four fundamentals: know where everyone is on the field, constantly scan and keep the head up while moving eyes and body to maximize field of vision, recognize opportunities through peripheral vision and “what if” thinking, and scan defensively for threats without tunnel vision. Communication is also described as important, with goalkeepers having the best view. Coaching tips include using the first touch away from the body, receiving passes with the opposite foot, and using drills such as two-touch passing in a colored grid that require scanning before receiving.

NatWest’s digital safety report, in partnership with The Future Laboratory, identified eight emerging financial scams for consumers to watch this year, including malware installed on smartphones and fake websites selling discounted FIFA World Cup tickets. The report says more than £100m in banking fraud occurred in the UK during the first half of 2017 and that financial fraud is the most common crime. Other tactics highlighted include social media-based targeting, Brexit-proof investment offers, money mules, fake wedding websites, catfish dating scams, and hackers impersonating solicitors. The report recommends questioning and directly contacting companies requesting personal information, keeping devices updated with anti-virus and anti-malware software, and not trusting links, files, or outreach from unknown people.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated March 15, 2021. On March 15, 2021, its Compensation Committee adopted the Variable Compensation Plan for fiscal year 2022. The plan provides eligible executive officers an opportunity to earn a variable cash payment based on achievement of specified corporate performance goals during fiscal year 2022 (ending January 30, 2022), including threshold, base operating plan, and stretch operating plan levels tied to fiscal year 2022 revenue. Eligibility requires a participant to remain an employee through the payment date unless otherwise determined. The filing includes target award opportunities for named executive officers, and states the plan is filed as Exhibit 10.1. The report was signed on March 18, 2021 by Rebecca Peters.

An experiment on predatory academic conferences tested fake research submissions and found that the conference organizers (OMICS International) accepted papers for fees and were later exposed as running shady conferences. The results showed that after submitting to such publishers, researchers’ names and contact information can be used by scammers, who then send unsolicited journal invitations using the same misspelled author name and references to even unpublished submissions. The passage concludes that dealing with predatory scammers once can lead to continued targeting over time.

Gianluca Vialli says Juventus must contain the atmosphere at Camp Nou to stop Barcelona, recalling a Chelsea match at the stadium where the atmosphere became “hell” after a late goal. He adds that Juventus has “physical and mental shape,” continuity, stability, European stature, and respect, and that Barcelona’s return includes Sergio Busquets and the Camp Nou atmosphere. Vialli believes Lionel Messi will be angry after the first leg and requires extra attention, and he praises Juventus’s first-leg performance as an “almost perfect start,” highlighting Buffon’s crucial saves. He identifies the key to the game as transitions, focusing on defensive compression, quick recovery, and attacking through players like Pjanic or Khedira.

Pakistan’s Bureau of Statistics has initiated rebasing inflation indices, expected to be completed by June 2018. The country currently uses the 2007-08 base for CPI, WPI, and SPI, which PBS says has become obsolete due to new market products. Rebasing is based on survey data, Industrial Census, and Census of Manufacturing Industries; field work is expected to finish by June 2018, with a new base planned to be operational from the 2018-19 fiscal year. PBS has sent forms nationwide with support from provincial industry and labor departments, and the rebasing process was delayed due to the recently concluded population census. PBS also plans to release separate rural, urban, and total CPI to address reported urban bias.

This passage is a VentureWire newsletter dated June 6, 2001, sent to jdasovic@enron.com. It lists “top stories,” “new money,” “bad news,” “new products,” “M&A,” “new directors,” “new people,” “VC personnel,” and “vw corrections,” and provides detailed articles on multiple companies. Articles include Napster’s licensing deal with MusicNet, CEO James P. Labe’s resignation at Comdisco Ventures, Charter Growth Capital’s name change to Focus Ventures, Movaz’s $62M second-round funding, InsureZone’s $8.2M first-round funding, and additional funding announcements (e.g., Mergermarket, Epicentric, Efficio, Clustra, Screentec, AtriCure, Verimetra, OmniCluster, DataCert). It also reports shutdowns or issues for companies such as WhatsHotNow.com, Hologix, TerraShare, Ditto.com, The Dock, and MetaTV’s CEO arrest, plus news including eToll renaming to FastForward, Workadia’s intranet portal launch, and SetNet’s acquisition of Selfswitch. The newsletter ends with indexes and contact/legal information.

European shares rose on Wednesday as Prime Minister Theresa May began Brexit proceedings. The STOXX 600 gained 0.4% to 378.5 points, and Germany’s DAX rose 0.4% to 12,203. Daimler increased 1% on expected record Mercedes sales, lifting autos. London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Boerse shares rose after the EU blocked their merger deal. Banks overall fell, while Deutsche Bank rose 1.3% amid optimism about its 8 billion euros cash call. Engie climbed after a JP Morgan upgrade, and 3I Group rose after a Morgan Stanley upgrade. Scout24 dropped 8.9% on results and a weak outlook, while Aurelius fell more than 35% on investor skepticism over its response to a short-seller report.

Hucknall and Linby Dolphins competed at the Arc Centre Matlock pool novice gala for nine-, 10- and 11-year-olds, with 55 races testing the Junior squad. Dolphins were third after 10 races but finished fifth in the eight-team event after setbacks from injuries and illness. Runner-up spots included three for Katie Hill (U10 Freestyle, Backstroke, Butterfly) and one each for Joel Gospel (U9 Backstroke), Ellie Norris (U9 Breaststroke), Esme White (U9 Freestyle), and Ben Staniforth (U10 Backstroke). Third places went to multiple swimmers across various events, including Joel (two events), Ben (U10 Freestyle), Alexa Sherratt (U10 Breaststroke), Rhys Harwood (U9 Breaststroke), and Sophie Pritchard (U9 Freestyle). Lewis Kemp helped the boys U10 4x25 medley relay win with Joel, Ben, and Tyler Dennis, and other points were won by Brooke O’Hanlon, Ella Skellington, Jacee Jem Fells, Izzy Coleman, Josh Kemp, and Sam Ellison.

The passage is about confidence and performance in the playoffs. The speaker says the team played two good games but needs to limit mistakes and take good play from their last games, noting they created quality chances but sometimes errors cost goals. They emphasize learning from past series, focusing on the next game, and winning two at home to even the series. Mats Zuccarello is mentioned as having leaders on the team and strong fan support, while the team’s strength is described as everyone stepping up and not relying on only one or two players.

The passage reports market movements and outlooks. The S&P 500 fell in recent sessions, closing Friday at its lowest since early July and retracing after a two-day decline; investor sentiment was slightly improved in the AAII survey. The VIX rose to 21.90, and the text outlines how VIX changes relate to market reversals. S&P 500 futures are described as rebounding toward 6,300 with specified support and resistance. Crude oil declined after stocks and OPEC+ news, which included a September output increase and concerns about supply pressure, tariffs, and weaker demand. The outlook suggests the S&P 500 may start higher Monday, but could represent either a short-term bounce within broader consolidation or a temporary advance in a downtrend, with earnings in focus. It also includes general defensive-positioning advice and a risk disclosure for trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies.

The passage describes the DAWN-PLASMA randomized, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter study evaluating convalescent plasma in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. Ethics committee approvals, informed consent procedures, and compliance with Declaration of Helsinki and ICH-GCP are outlined. The study compares best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone, with a primary endpoint of the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include clinical status at Days 15 and 30, time to sustained clinical improvement, mechanical ventilation/death at Days 30 and 90, safety outcomes, laboratory and vital sign assessments, and PCR/neutralizing antibody measurements. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are provided, along with withdrawal and treatment discontinuation reporting. Randomization uses a computerized system with a 2:1 allocation to convalescent plasma plus SOC versus SOC alone, and the statistician remains blinded until database lock. The passage also summarizes planned monitoring, data handling (including use of RedCap), statistical analysis set definitions (FAS and PPS), protocol deviations leading to PPS exclusion, and study disposition numbers. Exposure/compliance data include median time to first transfusion (5 hours), median plasma volume (884 mL), neutralizing antibody titer characteristics of transfused units, and the number of patients who did not receive convalescent plasma.

The passage argues that XLP (the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund, ticker XLP) is “good for trading,” describing it as underused and “boring.” It says XLP has few sudden moves, is mean-reverting, supports profitable short strategies, and provides diversification because it correlates less than other ETFs like QQQ and SPY. The fund tracks large-cap, low-volatility consumer staples in the S&P 500, aims to provide exposure to retailing, beverage, food, tobacco, and personal products, and is rebalanced quarterly. The passage also summarizes backtest results for three short strategies (418 trades, ~0.4% average gain before costs, 75% win ratio, profit factor 2.35) and notes that the strategies have not produced very big losers. It concludes that XLP is an excellent trading vehicle.

People in Chesterfield have rallied around Craig Burr after he threatened to jump onto the A617 Hasland bypass, was taken to hospital, and later released. Craig spoke to the Derbyshire Times about his struggles with mental illness. The newspaper’s You Are Not Alone campaign says it will keep in contact with him, and many community members left supportive messages on Facebook. The passage also includes NHS advice on seeking help for depression or anxiety, using a mental health helpline list, and contacting Samaritans or someone trusted if there are thoughts of self-harm or suicide.

Diversification is described as spreading investments across different asset types whose returns do not move together, so losses in one area may be cushioned by gains in another, reducing overall portfolio impact. The passage says effective diversification requires selecting assets based on how returns respond to risk factors and how they fit financial goals and investment horizon, but errors can reduce its effectiveness. It lists common mistakes: not counting all investments (e.g., Employees’ Provident Fund or stock options), having too many investments (which can dilute benefits and increase costs), buying what you don’t understand (which can lead to concentrated portfolios), losing sight of goals (mismatch in asset allocation can affect income needs and liquidity), and letting allocation drift by not periodically rebalancing. It also notes diversification within asset classes by mixing segments, sectors, credit profiles, and tenors.

The speaker says Holik was important for the team because he performs well under pressure, and that he helped lead to the team letting go of Brian Rolston. They express excitement about returning to New Jersey and note the team reached the Stanley Cup finals, which they feel has paid off. The speaker acknowledges losing a game and says playoffs will be harder, but they believe the team responded well to adversity in the previous series and hopes to do so again. They discuss relying on speed and expect it to be affected by the situation, while emphasizing the need to respect the opponent and win one game to regain home-ice advantage. They also describe being surprised by the speed of a shot and missing it with their glove.

The passage discusses trading SPY based on intraday highs and lows, focusing on a “boring” strategy of buying on weakness and selling on strength. It describes entering at the next day’s open and exiting at 11:30 the same day (day trades), noting similar results when buying on the close but larger drawdowns. Attempts to improve performance using targets and stop-loss did not help. It provides results from January 2010 to August 2012 and notes that an equity curve based on entering long when the low occurs in the last hour and short when the high occurs in the last hour is shown. The passage states the key takeaway is that the strategy appears to work well, mentions variations involving the last hour’s performance and the next day’s market direction, and says it includes accumulated returns, number of trades, number of winning trades, and average returns for different scenarios.

The passage describes how the Covid-19 pandemic affected higher education by stopping face-to-face training and pushing institutions to use online learning platforms. It notes issues with rapid adaptation, course practical content, exam safety, low instructor innovation before the pandemic, student motivation and digital competence deficiencies, and cheating. It argues that effective online platforms should support communication and interaction via educational technology, including learning management and assessment tools, while also addressing data protection concerns with cloud storage.

The study aims to develop and evaluate a cloud-based learning management system for emergency distance education needs, integrating with existing university software and supporting personal data protection. The resulting system, UZEP, is built using an Education as a Service (EaaS) cloud model and includes modules such as an LMS, virtual classroom integration (BigBlueButton), an online exam module, homework-project assessment, digital material sharing, announcements, surveys, and reporting. UZEP was presented to 12 universities starting in Fall 2020, and usage statistics were collected between 1 October 2020 and 1 February 2021.

UZEP was evaluated using expert, pilot, and user evaluations. Expert evaluation compared UZEP with Moodle, edX, and Google Suite, highlighting UZEP’s ease of use and readiness in emergencies, while suggesting improvements mainly in communication/social and reporting/learning analytics. User evaluations included administrator, lecturer, and student surveys, with overall findings indicating positive but not very high satisfaction, particularly needing stronger social tools and improvements in measurement and evaluation. The discussion concludes that UZEP’s integrated and scalable structure supports quick transition to distance education, while limitations include self-reported questionnaires and comparison only with four platforms.

AOL instant messenger (AIM) will be discontinued effective December 15. The company said AIM helped drive new digital technologies and a cultural shift in communication, and many users shared nostalgic memories on social media using the hashtag #AIMmemories. AIM expressed sorrow for discontinuing while saying it is excited to build new iconic brands and life-changing products.

The disclosure relates to apparatus and methods for measuring tissue viability around burns or other wounds by using electrodes to measure capacitance and derive sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values indicative of tissue fluid accumulation/depletion. Background describes challenges in visually assessing viable vs. non-viable tissue around wounds and limitations of current burn evaluation methods. The disclosure summarizes embodiments including (1) determining burn depth by comparing measured capacitance to a data array of capacitance-depth pairs, and (2) mapping regions of damage by converting measured capacitance to SEM values, then marking boundaries between viable and non-viable tissue based on SEM thresholds and optionally projecting/indicating images or activating embedded visual indicators along those boundaries. SEM sensing apparatus embodiments describe electrode arrangements, optional visual indicators (e.g., LEDs or marking elements), and an example system that combines SEM sensing with an optical camera/projector to project indicating images along a determined boundary. The description also discusses an example burn with zones of necrosis, stasis, hyperaemia, and how SEM values may vary across wound regions for assessing depth and risk.

Wound Care Advantage (WCA), collaborating with podiatric surgeon Dr. David G. Armstrong, the Southwestern Academic Limb Salvage Alliance (SALSA), and Gen1 Research, launched Advanced Discovery, an investigative research alliance focused on improving wound care through evidence-based science. The alliance will provide access to an international network of wound and hyperbaric treatment centers, evaluate diagnostic and treatment modalities in partnership with approved manufacturers, and aim to improve wound healing outcomes while reducing treatment costs. Gen1 will provide administrative support and research infrastructure. Advanced Discovery will use electronic clinical data from more than 42,000 patients and 880,000 wound assessments collected over 16 years, with additional data from SALSA, which has global university affiliations. The passage also cites the growing impact and costs of chronic wounds and diabetic foot ulcers in the U.S., and includes background information on Dr. Armstrong, WCA, and Gen1 Research.

Plaintiffs—various trustees of Plumbers Local Union No. 93 U.A. retirement, pension, health and welfare, apprenticeship, and industry advancement funds—sued defendant Waterworks, Inc. to compel an audit under ERISA § 502. The parties filed cross-motions for summary judgment, which were denied.

The court described a disputed fall 2004 meeting between Waterworks’ president Roger Garbacz and Union representative Lynn Earner about whether Waterworks would become a signatory to the Local 93 collective bargaining agreement (CBA) in connection with apprenticeship opportunities for Garbacz’s son and other employees. The court noted that after the meeting, the apprenticeship program involved Dustin Garbacz and Waterworks employees, and Waterworks submitted pre-printed Contribution Reports referencing the CBA and Trust Agreements. However, Waterworks never signed the “Warranty and Acceptance” clauses in those reports.

The court found genuine issues of material fact regarding what occurred at the fall 2004 meeting, whether any contract was formed, and how that related to Waterworks’ later conduct. It also rejected plaintiffs’ argument that the Labor Management Relations Act compelled an inference of intent to be bound, stating that Waterworks’ defense presented unresolved factual questions. The cross-motions for summary judgment were therefore denied.

The passage describes systems and procedures for low-latency MAC protocol data unit (PDU) assembly in wireless systems, such as 5G flexible radio access technology (5gFLEX). It discusses reducing latency by having a WTRU determine network transmission parameters and signaling before a transmission grant, including preparing modulation and coding scheme (MCS), resource ranges, transport block sizes, segmentation/assembly/multiplexing, and flexible grant sizes for early transport block generation. The passage further describes a WTRU processor that monitors and decodes downlink control information (DCI), determines decoding parameters (e.g., CRC length, aggregation level, robustness level), and selects transmission/reception parameters (including QoS level, spectrum operating mode, and HARQ-related information). It also outlines transmitting HARQ-ACK feedback and receiving network configurations that map decoding parameters to transmission parameters. In addition, it provides general system and network descriptions (e.g., WTRU, RAN, core network, and various radio access technologies) and discusses 5gFLEX capabilities such as spectrum flexibility, multiple timing aspects, support for different duplexing schemes, and waveform options (e.g., OFDM and multicarrier variants), along with example frame structures and scheduling modes.

The passage discusses changing credit card offers and highlights that long 0% Intro APR deals can help consumers save money, especially when carrying a balance or making big purchases. It notes multiple card picks, including options with cash back matches, choice-based cash back rewards, and unlimited travel or travel-related points, along with listed intro APR terms, bonus values, fees, and redemption details. It also describes how low or 0% interest cards work (including variable vs. fixed APR and introductory periods) and states that the site uses a data-driven ranking system evaluating over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers, with compensation not affecting ratings or reviews.

In 2013, Sungi Cho earned a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering and later served as a Black Hawk helicopter pilot, where he noticed deficiencies in standard-issue gear. Because large-scale redesign was difficult due to bureaucratic red tape and major defense contractors, he began experimenting with 3D printing and developed a plastic Warbelt Hanger attachment to improve soldiers’ gear accessibility and storage. After iterations and field testing, he founded a company, sold the Warbelt Hanger at $10.99, and expanded sales beyond the military while personally printing, packaging, and shipping orders.

Cho then developed a second product, the MOLLE Backer, a universal base mount for MOLLE systems designed to attach mounting plates more effectively than using rubber bands, bungee cords, or rope. After feedback and design cycles, it launched at $10.99 for a two-pack and met strong demand, prompting additional printers and support from hired engineering majors during his MIT Sloan MBA.

After reviewing stable monthly demand of about 1,800 units, Cho considered switching from 3D printing to injection molding to increase efficiency. The passage describes injection molding’s process, compared performance versus 3D printing, and the need to outsource manufacturing and invest in a steel mold. Exhibit data provides production capacity and unit costs for both methods, including material, scrap rates, packaging, electricity, labor, and capital costs, plus a third-party per-unit price and a mold cost of $11,487.

The passage is largely an excerpt from NVIDIA’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 30, 2022, including XBRL data and sections of the report such as Business, Sales and Marketing, Manufacturing, Competition, Patents and Proprietary Rights, Government Regulations, Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance, Human Capital Management, Executive Officers, and Item 1A Risk Factors. It describes NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform, its two business segments (Graphics and Compute & Networking), its four market focus areas (Gaming, Data Center, Professional Visualization, and Automotive), and major business strategies. It also discusses company information (address, registered securities, market value of shares held by non-affiliates, shares outstanding), the February 8, 2022 termination of the Arm share purchase agreement and a planned $1.36 billion charge, and extensive risk factors including industry competition, demand/supply/manufacturing challenges, product defects and cybersecurity incidents, global operations risks, climate change risks, acquisitions and investment risks, and system security/data protection threats.

The passage explains that an “unknown artist/album” label is usually caused by missing ID3 tags or WMA metadata, and suggests entering Artist, Album, Song Title, Track Number, Genre, and Year in the song’s Properties Summary tab on a computer. It states that the Sansa Fuze player can read and write to microSD and microSDHC cards, and that a power reset is done by sliding the power button up and holding it for about 10 seconds. The passage also provides service and warranty information for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze player and includes terms from an end user license agreement for related software.

The passage explains that options trading in EEM is popular for gaining market exposure and profiting from both rising and falling markets, but it involves high risk. It outlines risks such as significant losses from adverse price moves, time decay, liquidity issues, and volatility risk. It describes how to calculate potential profits and losses based on the difference between the option buy/sell price and the exercised price, accounting for fees and using the Black-Scholes model. It lists common strategies (long call/put, covered call/put, straddle, strangle, collar, butterfly spread), discusses leverage and associated risk, and provides general guidance on costs, minimum deposits ($500–$2,000), and margin requirements (typically 10%–50%). It covers the use of option delta, analyzing pricing with Black-Scholes and technical analysis, hedging and risk management, expiration dates (generally the third Friday of the contract month), tax reporting as capital gains/losses (depending on country), how to select an option contract and set up an account via a broker, and how to use and interpret the options chain.

The device includes programmable high and low alarms for the analog input signal, with independently programmable thresholds and a common hysteresis setting via ALARM_H_TH_REG and ALARM_L_TH_REG. The high input alarm is set when the digital output exceeds the high threshold and resets when it falls to or below the high threshold minus H minus 1; the low input alarm is set when the digital output drops below the low threshold and resets when it rises to or above the low threshold plus H plus 1. The device also provides high and low alarms for the analog voltage supply (AVDD) using fixed trip points (high alarm if AVDD exceeds 5.3V; low alarm asserted if AVDD drops below 4.7V) monitored by an internal analog comparator. The passage also describes the multiSPI interface and device operational states (RESET, ACQ, CONV), as well as programming concepts such as data transfer frames, input commands, output data word composition, supported data transfer protocols, and register maps for configuration and alarm-related registers.

The passage is an Apple Inc. Form 8-K current report dated December 29, 2020, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It states that on December 29, 2020, Apple’s Board appointed Ms. Monica Lozano to the Board effective January 4, 2021, and she will serve on the Audit and Finance Committee. As a non-employee director, she will receive a $100,000 annual retainer paid quarterly and participate in Apple’s Non-Employee Director Stock Plan. On the appointment effective day, she will receive an automatic initial grant of 281 restricted stock units. The report also notes that Apple and Ms. Lozano will enter into the standard director indemnification agreement, and there are no reportable transactions under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. The report is signed on January 5, 2021 by Katherine Adams.

The Office of Attorney Ethics petitioned the court to temporarily suspend E. Nkem Odinkemere from practicing law under Rule 1:20-11(a). The court ordered that the suspension take effect immediately until further order, restrained any funds held by him in New Jersey financial institutions from disbursement except by application to the court for good cause, enjoined him from practicing law during the suspension, and required compliance with Rule 1:20-20 regarding suspended attorneys.

Meteorologist Kevin Arnone reports more snow is forecast for eastern New England after frequent recent snow. Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont already have over 2 feet of snow, with some areas exceeding 50 inches. A snow depth map shows green areas with over 2 feet of snow pack. Connecticut is expected to get much less, with snow pack ranging from a few inches near parts of the shoreline to near 20 inches in northern CT; two systems are forecast to phase too late to bring more than a dusting over the next 48 hours. As the systems move offshore, they are expected to blanket most of Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont with close to a foot of snow and more in the mountains.

South Korea has restored 46 public services after a major fire at the National Information Resources Service data centre in Daejeon, which disrupted hundreds of government platforms. The fire, believed to have been caused by a suspected battery explosion during maintenance, triggered widespread outages across administrative, postal and public-sector websites, preventing citizens from accessing services ahead of the Chuseok holidays. Authorities contained the blaze and restarted 551 of 647 affected platforms, with key security and network functions largely recovered. Systems still awaiting full restoration include passport issuance, welfare services and several administrative tools. President Lee Jae Myung called for tighter safeguards and backup plans, and regulators and agencies are now focused on improving security, redundancy, and disaster preparedness.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2021. The filing states that Rosalind G. Brewer informed Amazon.com, Inc. on January 26, 2021 that she is resigning from the Board of Directors effective February 16, 2021. The report was signed by David A. Zapolsky, Senior Vice President, and includes Item 5.02 regarding the departure of directors.

High-grade glioma is common in adults, and glioblastoma (GBM) has a poor prognosis. The passage describes the importance of molecular markers, especially pTERT promoter mutations, which are linked to increased telomere expression and are reported as a major biomarker in GBM. It notes that current noninvasive prediction of pTERT mutation status using MRI is challenging, and conventional structural MRI is reported to lack predictive capability for pTERT mutations. The study aims to evaluate whether diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) and its associated ADC map can predict pTERT mutations in GBM using a ResNet deep learning model. Patients were retrospectively collected (primary GBM with pTERT mutation status confirmed and MRI within 1 month before surgery), and images were processed with tumor ROI delineation and data augmentation. Model comparisons were made across MRI modalities (structural MRI vs DWI, including DWI+ADC), different ROIs (entire tumor, tumor core, enhanced tumor), and inclusion of clinical characteristics. Results reported that DWI with the ADC map (DWI*) achieved better performance than conventional structural MRI, with the best accuracy using the entire tumor ROI (85.20% accuracy, AUC 0.934). The study concludes that DWI combined with ADC map has the greatest value for predicting pTERT mutation status in GBM, and that using the whole tumor as ROI may support future clinical application.

Antipsychotics are the primary treatment for severe mental health conditions, but about 40%–80% of people experience metabolic syndrome (MS), involving weight gain, glucose dysregulation, and dyslipidaemia. Antipsychotic-induced MS is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and a five-fold risk of type 2 diabetes. Non-modifiable determinants such as gender, ethnic background, age, and family history are reported, but it is unclear which determinants are most significant and how high-risk individuals are targeted. Behavioural determinants linked to MS are modifiable, yet it is unclear how extensively they have been studied or targeted, and few non-pharmacological interventions show clinically significant attenuation. The passage describes a scoping review protocol to map evidence on determinants of antipsychotic-induced MS in community-dwelling adults, non-pharmacological interventions to prevent and/or treat it, and preferred contexts for delivery. The review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR, search multiple databases and grey literature, include quantitative/qualitative/mixed-method studies and evidence syntheses, extract data using a standard form, summarise findings via narrative synthesis, and consult stakeholders at the end.

Mary L. and Samuel W. Breit appealed a summary judgment in favor of Shelter Mutual Insurance Company, which declared Shelter had no obligation under its insurance policies to make uninsured motorist payments beyond $100,000 due to the policies’ anti-stacking provisions. The Breits demanded $100,000 based on two policies covering their automobiles, but it was undisputed their damages exceeded $200,000. The trial court found the relevant “limits of liabilities” and “other insurance in the company” provisions unambiguous and prohibiting stacking of uninsured motorist benefits for multiple policies issued by the same insurer. On appeal, the court rejected arguments that the provisions were ambiguous or contrary to the doctrine of reasonable expectations, concluding the “Other Insurance” clause was unambiguous and addressed different concepts from the anti-stacking clause. The judgment was affirmed.

The ANC in the Free State has not yet started its postponed provincial congress, which will elect new leadership, with provincial chairperson Ace Magashule expected to run again. Delegates registered at the municipal office in Parys, and Bulwane said an attempt to interdict the conference on Friday failed. A High Court ruling last week required 29 branch general meetings to be re-run before the congress could proceed; Bulwane said 28 were successful and the 29th was underway. Bulwane dismissed threats to challenge the conference’s validity, and noted the provincial executive committee’s mandate expired in May while the committee has been involved in court battles.

The passage discusses a Trump administration change that would give the Labor Department more control over career-technical education (CTE), shifting responsibilities that were under the Education Department. Proponents say the goal is better alignment between education and jobs, reduced administrative burden for states, and increased participation in the labor force, potentially improving accountability and outcomes for young people. Supporters also argue CTE can serve as a long-term “springboard” by enabling pathways like trade school admissions or college credits. Critics, including some CTE advocates and Democrats in Congress, fear the shift may dismantle parts of the Education Department’s role, overwhelm limited federal staffing, and steer students toward short-term credentials with fewer opportunities for advancement. The passage also notes concerns that integrating CTE into the Labor Department could overemphasize industry credentialing tied to jobs that may not lead to higher wages, while others argue the Labor Department could better hold programs accountable and still support activities like career awareness and apprenticeships. Alabama’s workforce leader hopes the federal change leads to improved funding and less “red tape,” but a former CTE official worries reduced staffing could limit personalized guidance.

The passage announces the 2018 awards recipients of the Metallurgy & Materials Society of the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum (MetSoc of CIM). It describes the Recognition of Excellence Program and its award categories, notes sponsorship by Hatch, Rio Tinto, TECK and XPS Expert Process Solutions, and says recipients will be recognized in person at the 57th Annual Conference of Metallurgists (COM 2018) in Columbus, Ohio, on October 15, 2018. The 2018 recipients listed are: Sam Marcuson (Airey Award), Priti Wanjara (Silver Medal), Jun Song (Brimacombe Award), Acousto Ultrasonic-Echo (AU-E) (Innovation Award), Xinjin Cao (Distinguished Materials Scientist Award), Georgios Kolliopoulos (Doctoral Scholarship), and Shauna Litke (Master Scholarship).

Cervical cancer is preventable but remains a major health inequity, with most cases and deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), especially sub-Saharan Africa, where access to prevention and treatment tools is limited. The WHO 90/70/90 strategy targets HPV vaccination, screening coverage, and adequate treatment by 2030, but scalable approaches are needed to close cervical precancer treatment gaps.  

Cervical precancer treatment typically requires trained healthcare professionals and is limited in LMIC settings. Challenges include cost, weak infrastructure, lack of skilled providers, privacy concerns, and high loss-to-follow-up after referral. A 2021 Kenya review reported low treatment uptake among women with cervical precancer, and a 2022 assessment found that although screening was offered in many hospitals, few offered precancer treatment.  

Because no topical therapies are approved for cervical precancer, the passage describes research into self-administered intravaginal 5-fluorouracil (5FU). In high-income settings, trials found self-administered intravaginal 5FU to be safe and effective. An ongoing trial in South Africa is evaluating 5FU as an adjuvant therapy among HIV-positive women. The passage then reports a Phase I pilot clinical trial in Kisumu County, Kenya, among 12 women living with HIV aged 18–49 with biopsy-confirmed CIN2/3 who had undergone ablation or excision. Participants received education and self-administered 5FU intravaginally at home (two grams every other week for eight applications) with clinic visits for safety and adherence assessments.  

Acceptability was assessed using questionnaires and in-depth interviews after treatment. Although some participants reported initial worry or fear, by the end of the 16-week course all participants were confident they used the cream correctly and strongly agreed it was safe. Quantitative results showed high comfort with using applicators and tampons and preference for 5FU over prior ablative or excisional treatments. Qualitative findings highlighted reduced fear, ease of use, privacy and convenience of home administration, and less pain compared to previous procedures, along with challenges related to condom use requirements, side effects, measuring dosage, and finding privacy at home.  

The study concludes that self-administered intravaginal 5FU is highly acceptable as an adjuvant treatment for CIN2/3 among women living with HIV, and ongoing randomized studies are underway to assess whether it reduces recurrence and can expand access to precancer treatment in LMICs.

Iranian President Hassan Rouhani told parliament that Iran could abandon the 2015 nuclear deal within hours if the United States continues imposing new sanctions. In his televised address, Rouhani criticized US President Donald Trump for showing Washington was “not a good partner,” and said the US had repeatedly broken promises under the JCPOA and ignored other global agreements. Rouhani argued that failed sanctions and coercion had previously brought US administrations to negotiations, warning that a return to that approach would leave Iran in a previous situation “much more stronger,” within days rather than months.

The Ministry of Education announced it will fund a $28.5-million replacement for the over 50-year-old Walnut Park Elementary, which is on unstable land. Minister Rob Fleming and Stikine MLA Doug Donaldson visited the school to share the news with students, teachers, and Bulkley Valley School District 54. The plan is to build a new two-storey facility beside the old school, move students into it when complete, and then demolish the old building. The new school will support 440 elementary students, include space for StrongStart and a neighbourhood learning centre, and be designed with 21st-century learning, including collaboration and project-based learning. Construction is hoped to begin next spring with readiness for the 2020–21 school year. The Province will contribute up to $27.6 million and SD54 $900,000.

The passage describes a study on using machine learning models to diagnose pancreatic cancer using a synthetic, imbalanced dataset. It evaluates six models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Networks, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner) using metrics including accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1-score, and balanced accuracy after an 80/20 train-test split with preprocessing (handling missing values, scaling, encoding). All models achieved similar accuracy (~76%), but sensitivity was very low across models; Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positives. SVM had the highest sensitivity (1.90%), while SuperLearner had the highest precision (66.67%) but very low sensitivity (0.42%). The discussion attributes performance issues to class imbalance and notes that interpretability, feature engineering informed by PCA/clustering, resampling, threshold tuning, cost-sensitive learning, and validation on real-world clinical datasets may improve sensitivity. The conclusion states that further research is needed to address low sensitivity and class imbalance for better clinical utility.

The passage discusses how credit card offers change over time and highlights that longer 0% Intro APR periods can help consumers save money when switching cards. It describes multiple featured credit cards and their introductory APR terms, cash back or rewards rates, sign-up/bonus offers, and related conditions such as balance transfer fees and eligibility requirements. It also notes that a fixed APR stays relatively stable while a variable APR can change based on prevailing rates, and that the site uses an editors’ data-driven approach to evaluate many cards from multiple issuers.

The Indiana Supreme Court reviewed a wrongful death dispute involving Laura Shaner’s death after complications from surgery and dialysis treatments. Her husband, David Shaner, sued Dr. Albert Milford, St. Margaret Mercy Healthcare Centers, and TRC-Indiana for “final-expense” damages and “survivor” damages, seeking losses including consortium and related benefits. During the case, David died intestate in 2015, leaving no immediately known heirs and his estate escheated to Indiana. The trial court granted partial summary judgment for defendants on David’s survivor-damages claim, reasoning that without heirs such damages would be punitive, and the Court of Appeals affirmed. The Supreme Court granted transfer, reversed the partial summary judgment, and held that David’s claim for survivor damages could survive his death without requiring an heir. The Court, however, remanded for the trial court to determine whether the proper party exists to continue the survivor-damages claim.

Pupils from Richardson Dees Primary School in Wallsend have been tending a rooftop garden at The Forum, a project proposed by centre manager Nick Lambert to develop a partnership with the school. In a couple of months, eight to 10-year-olds have turned the garden into a small oasis, growing flowers as well as fruit, vegetables, and herbs to harvest and share with pupils and families. Teaching assistant Laura Wilson said the project teaches gardening, encourages healthy eating, builds responsibility, and boosts confidence in a relaxed environment. Nick added that the unused space has been transformed into a greenhouse and raised beds with a “seed to plate” ethos, and that pupils’ knowledge, confidence, and ownership have increased as they make suggestions and decisions about the garden.

After Kim Jong Un crossed into South Korea and persuaded Moon Jae-in to step back across the border, the passage says his approach ahead of a planned meeting with US President Donald Trump in Singapore is shaped by demands that actions be on Kim’s terms. It notes that observers believe Kim wants eased sanctions but will not give up nuclear weapons until he feels secure enough to keep power, and that North Korea’s elite may not fully accept denuclearization linked to economic prosperity. The passage describes Kim’s diplomacy, including meetings with China’s Xi Jinping and Moon, and says Kim has shown humour, humility, and flattery. It also states that US officials raised concerns about denuclearization before sanctions relief, references to Libya contributed to the cancellation of the June 12 summit, and Trump later indicated the meeting might proceed. The passage says “complete denuclearisation” remains undefined, and Kim may require US troop and nuclear asset withdrawals, while it reports Kim shifted from “songun” to “byongjin,” seeking both nuclear development and economic growth.

The passage reports that Trump plans to impose a 100% tariff on China starting November 1, with US stock indexes falling as Trump threatens higher China tariffs and S&P 500 declines amid US-China trade war fears. It states that the S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July (+7.8% year-to-date) but then fell 1.6% on the first day of August, and that volatility and credit spreads are showing a seasonal upturn. It says investors are increasing exposure to tech stocks and notes US electricity demand reached a new all-time high. It also describes market signals as both intact longer-term and weaker short-term, with 50-day breadth rolling over from overbought levels, and mentions risk disclosure and site data accuracy limitations.

The passage compares tournament and cash game poker, outlining key differences: tournaments use fixed chip buy-ins with payouts for finishing positions, elimination when out of chips, increasing blinds over time, less table “metagame,” and a general goal of survival; cash games have fixed stakes, allow re-buying after losing chips, and involve more metagame decisions and player targeting. It also discusses variance, excitement, scenario range, and relative casino rake favoring tournaments.

The speaker then explains preflop strategy and equity matchups, giving examples of “favorite” percentages for common all-in situations (e.g., larger pocket pairs vs smaller pairs, dominating hands, and cases where overcards vs a pair are near 50/50). It emphasizes how suitedness matters more when behind than when ahead and describes “going all-in preflop” as a crucial, mostly routine way to improve expectancy, including guidelines based on effective stack size (e.g., shoving with fewer than about 12 big blinds, and different thresholds when antes are absent).

A sample exploitative all-in calculation is used to illustrate how opponent calling ranges affect profitability, followed by a discussion of Nash equilibrium concepts using iterative best-response reasoning for a specific 15 big blind, ante, small-blind shove vs big-blind call scenario. The passage provides approximate Nash-equilibrium ranges (small blind shoving about 66.8% and big blind calling about 38.5%) and explains how strategies should adjust with position and stack size.

Finally, it covers additional practical preflop situations: learning ranges via memorization plus theory-based interpolation/extrapolation, how to handle calling all-ins and short stack odds, when calling is acceptable versus when raising/calling can be bad, and how sizing should change with limpers (adding a big blind per limper). The passage concludes with recommendations to simplify decisions, often prefer all-ins in certain tournament stack contexts, and notes that a next class will review tournament decision history.

The device provides an active-high alarm output on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured for alarm functionality; enabling it requires setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] in SDO_CTL_REG to 01b. There are two alarm types: an input alarm that compares the ADC input voltage to user-set high/low thresholds, and an AVDD alarm that monitors AVDD against typical thresholds (low 4.7V, high 5.3V) and triggers if AVDD crosses them in either direction. When alarm functionality is on, both alarm types are enabled by default and can be disabled via IN_AL_DIS and VDD_AL_DIS bits in RST_PWRCTL_REG. Each alarm has active and tripped flags read in ALARM_REG; the active flag clears at the end of the current ADC conversion (and resets if the condition persists), while the tripped flag clears only after ALARM_REG is read. Alarm output flags update internally at the end of every conversion and are available via ALARM_REG, the ALARM output pin, or by appending them to the data output bit stream. A high level on the ALARM pin indicates an over- or undervoltage condition on AVDD or the analog input channel and can be wired to interrupt the host.

The passage explains the S&P Midcap 400 index and its E-mini futures contract (E-mini S&P MidCap 400 Futures/EMD). The S&P 400 tracks 400 U.S. mid-sized companies formed in 1991, with market capitalization between $3.6B and $13.1B, and is market-cap weighted with quarterly recalculation. The E-mini futures contract represents buying or selling the index at a pre-agreed price and is traded on CME Globex from Sundays to Fridays with listed quarterly cycles (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec), financially settled with cash based on special opening quotes, and trading terminating on the 3rd Friday of the contract month at 9:30 a.m. ET. The minimum price fluctuation is 0.1 index point ($10) for outright trading on Globex and 0.05 index point for BTIC/calendar spreads; the tick size is also $10 for outright and $5 for BTIC/calendar spreads. The passage lists the all-time high for the futures (2924.2 in November 2021) and the index (2925.93 in November 2021) and the all-time low for the index (119.43 in June 1991). It also mentions ETFs that track the index (including IJH, SPMD, and EWMC), trading charts sources (TradingView, Yahoo Finance), trading symbols (EMD for the mini-contract), and risks from adverse leveraged price movements.

Tyreek Hill returned to the Dolphins’ facility and spoke to the team after undergoing season-ending surgery on a dislocated left knee. Dolphins coach Mike McDaniel said Hill attended Friday’s meeting three days after being hospitalized and offered encouragement to teammates. McDaniel said the team would continue staying motivated, emphasizing complementary football across three phases. Jaylen Waddle was described as stepping into Hill’s lead-receiver role, with Waddle saying the “receiver 1” idea is more of a media creation than a real role. The Dolphins also plan increased passing-game roles for 2024 sixth-round pick and tight end Jonnu Smith, while McDaniel said Waller is unlikely to see a full workload immediately and that the team won’t overcompensate for Hill’s absence.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 9, 2021. The report states that on November 9, 2021, Apple’s Board appointed Mr. Alex Gorsky to the Board, where he will serve on the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and receive a $100,000 annual retainer and an initial grant of 486 restricted stock units under the Non-Employee Director Plan. It also states the Board amended Apple’s Amended and Restated Bylaws effective November 9, 2021, increasing the Board size to nine members from eight. The report lists Exhibit 3.2 as the amended bylaws and is signed by Katherine Adams.

A Russell 2000 “Death Cross” occurs when the Russell 2000 index’s 50-day moving average crosses below its 200-day moving average and is often considered bearish. Rob Hanna’s study of all Russell Death Crosses since 1988 found the S&P 500 rose 84% of the time in the following year (with a biggest gain in 2020 of over 60%), but drawdowns were generally sizable. Hanna concluded the signal is not perfect but may be worth watching for potential downturns. The passage also notes that the Russell 2000 is a small-cap index, and small caps are generally more volatile, so the Death Cross may be less reliable for the S&P 500. The most recent Death Cross was in 2022, and the study says the S&P 500 has fallen since then.

The passage compiles multiple news items from July 17, 2001. It describes leadership changes at Enron Broadband Services, with James Fallon set to head the unit after Kenneth Rice moves to a corporate role, amid reported bandwidth losses of $102 million in the second quarter and planned cost cuts and restructuring. Another article discusses how EnronOnline expects increased trading volume while not seeking mergers or acquisitions, and compares its one-to-one trading model with ICE. Additional items report that Rep. Henry Waxman urged a Justice Department review of White House aide Karl Rove’s dealings with companies in which he owned stock, which the White House disputes. Separate coverage includes Mississippi regulators approving plans for a Calpine power plant in Lowndes County and various developments around the Dabhol power project inquiry and Maharashtra’s efforts to address concerns raised by CITU. A PR Newswire item reports Texans raising nearly $500,000 for American Red Cross flood relief in the Houston area.

John Mellencamp knelt and raised his right fist in support of the Black Lives Matter movement after performing “Easy Target” on “Late Show With Stephen Colbert” on Thursday evening. The song, released in January 2017, addresses racial inequality and references Black Lives Matter in its lyrics. Mellencamp said taking a knee began as a protest of racial and social injustice but was later politicized. The passage also notes that Colin Kaepernick started the movement by taking a knee during the National Anthem, prompting a response from President Donald Trump.

The lecture provides a roadmap for discussing empirical demand and supply models of competition, including BLP (random-coefficient) demand estimation, Nevo’s cereal-market paper, and the common ownership hypothesis.
