On the supply side, it describes how firms’ first-order conditions can be written using an ownership matrix and derivatives from the demand model, allowing marginal costs to be recovered given a conduct (competition) assumption; if marginal costs are unconstrained, the model cannot be tested without further assumptions. It then explains that imposing a functional form for marginal cost enables joint estimation and provides additional supply-side moment conditions that can restrict demand parameters.

The lecturer summarizes BLP’s car-market results using data from 1971–1990 and notes that random coefficients and supply-side restrictions help address biases from simpler logit-based approaches. They highlight how the estimated model matches substitution patterns and diversion to the outside option better than logit, and how heterogeneous tastes rationalize observed market behavior. The lecture then turns to Nevo’s cereal paper, outlining how demand estimation is used to recover markups under different conduct assumptions and how fixed effects and instrumental variables are used to estimate price sensitivity.

Finally, the lecture discusses the common ownership hypothesis, which proposes that diversified investors may cause firms to internalize competitors’ profits, potentially reducing competition. It describes related descriptive evidence and a case study involving cereals that develops a testing procedure; it reports rejecting common-ownership-style conduct in favor of own-profit maximization (and also rejecting perfect competition and full monopoly) based on consistency with a flexible marginal-cost specification.

The passage discusses the impact of the Broncos’ early 2017 season exit and then predicts Super Bowl 52 between the Patriots and the Eagles. It describes local fan hostility toward both teams, suggests the game could be close, and compiles multiple commentators’ betting picks and score predictions, generally favoring the Patriots but with several predictions favoring the Eagles. Reported picks include score outcomes such as 24-14 Patriots, 28-24 Patriots, 31-28 Eagles, 35-13 Patriots, 27-24 Patriots, 38-27 Eagles, and 35-24 Eagles.

The passage describes the Ichimoku trading strategy, a technical analysis system that uses multiple plotted averages to define support and resistance levels, show trend direction, and gauge trend momentum. It explains that the indicator forms an Ichimoku Cloud and discusses its components (Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span) and how crossovers and the cloud’s position relate to bullish or bearish signals and volatility. The passage also emphasizes backtesting (and forward-testing) before using the strategy, noting associated risks from potentially inaccurate signals and stating that backtests presented suggest it is not among the best and may underperform risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns.

The passage discusses the impact of the 2007–09 Great Recession on the U.S. restaurant industry and describes the casual dining sector as being hit hardest, while noting that by summer 2016 some investors reconsidered casual dining stocks based on the expectation that sustained consumer growth would lead to more eating out and willingness to spend more. It defines casual dining and fast casual restaurants and provides background on Bloomin’ Brands, including its Outback Steakhouse origins, its “No Rules, Just Right” approach and signature “bloomin’ onion,” and its scale as of June 2016. It lists 13 potential comparable publicly traded restaurant companies as of June 2016 and presents select financial data for these companies and Bloomin’ Brands in Exhibits 1–3, covering price-earnings multiples, income statement data, and balance sheet data.

The passage explains the 60/40 portfolio as a strategy that allocates 60% of capital to equities and 40% to bonds, forming a diversified mix of stocks and bonds. It discusses how diversification works through non-correlation between stocks and bonds, but notes that in 2022 “safe” Treasuries fell more than stocks. It cites performance figures, including a 16.1% decline in the first half of 2022 and a Portfolios Lab estimate of -17.77% year-to-date as of September 17, 2022, while also stating that historical average annual returns have been about 8.8% since 1926. It covers risk measures such as drawdowns and volatility, describes the idea of a 60/40 fund as an easier implementation, and addresses whether the portfolio is “dead,” concluding it is not. The passage also outlines alternatives or substitutes, including 80/20, the All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following (CTA) strategies with example trading rules, and adding assets such as gold, crypto, international equities, and tail risk strategies.

Andrew A. Bucci appealed his Superior Court conviction for furnishing legal advice to Robert Oliva while Bucci was suspended from practicing law. The complaint alleged Bucci gave legal advice during February 14 to April 14, 1978, in violation of § 11-27-10. The court affirmed the conviction, finding the recorded conversations provided sufficient evidence that Bucci advised Oliva on managing his criminal litigation, including procedure and legal issues, even though another attorney represented Oliva in court.

The court rejected Bucci’s argument that the state had to prove he received a pecuniary benefit, holding § 11-27-10 does not require proof of monetary or other consideration. Bucci’s challenge to the increased penalty after a trial de novo was not considered on direct appeal because he did not first pursue the issue through a Rule 35 motion in the Superior Court. The appeal was denied and dismissed, the conviction affirmed, and the case remitted to the Superior Court. Justice Shea did not participate.

The passage is largely the Form 10-Q for Microsoft Corporation for the quarter ended September 30, 2022, including financial statements and notes. It reports three-month results showing total revenue of $50,122 million (vs. $45,317 million in 2021), operating income of $21,518 million (vs. $20,238 million), and net income of $17,556 million (vs. $20,505 million), with diluted earnings per share of $2.35 (vs. $2.71). The balance sheet as of September 30, 2022 shows total assets of $359,784 million and total liabilities of $186,218 million, with total stockholders’ equity of $173,566 million. The notes describe accounting policies, fair value measurements, investments, derivatives, and other items, including lease expense, business combinations (Nuance Communications acquired March 4, 2022; Activision Blizzard transaction announced), goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, contingencies, and share repurchase and dividend information.

Global Agriculture Innovation & Solutions Ltd. (GAIS), a nonprofit working with 200 farmers in South Sudan’s Gbudue state, says it wants the government to restrict international groups from importing seeds. GAIS Executive Director Mike Gaga questions why the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) imports seeds instead of buying local supplies, saying an inspection team FAO planned did not arrive and that imported seeds arrived through Congo without clear origin. He said his group produced about 150 metric tons of maize seeds. Gbudue’s Ministry of Agriculture director general Mariano Erneo said he was surprised FAO imported seeds into the state and that his ministry would investigate details, noting FAO had lined up a local NGO to administer a program. FAO said it distributes crop seeds and tools as part of emergency response to food insecurity, including by distributing seeds it purchases and by supporting seed fairs that provide cash for beneficiaries to buy locally. FAO also said procurement follows international rules and described past support for GAIS. FAO cited a waiver granted for importing maize seeds for the 2018 season due to low prior seed production and displacement from conflict, and said it plans to distribute 5,000 metric tons of seed this year, up from 2,000 last year.

A University of Liverpool study in Schizophrenia Research examined brain structure in 38 healthy people (ages 18–63) using MRI, along with measures of hallucination proneness and musical aptitude. Participants with higher musical aptitude showed lower hallucination proneness. Musical aptitude was positively associated with corpus callosum integrity, while hallucination proneness was associated with reduced integrity in the fibres connecting the brain’s hemispheres. Statistical analysis suggested that the relationship between hallucination proneness and musical aptitude is mediated by corpus callosum microstructure. Researcher Amy Spray suggested musical training might counteract hallucination predisposition and said future work should test whether musical training-based rehabilitation benefits patients with psychosis.

The Assam Higher Secondary Education Council (AHSEC) will release the Class 12 (HS) result on May 31 at 9:30 am. Students who appeared can check their results on ahsec.nic.in and resultsassam.nic.in, or use other websites like examresults.net if the official sites are unavailable. The minimum passing marks are 20 in each subject, and scoring 70% or above qualifies for distinction. Exams were conducted from February 23 to March 22. The passage also lists steps to check results online, methods to check via SMS for different mobile providers, and mentions app-based result checking with pre-registration of roll numbers.

Asian shares sought a fourth straight gain on Tuesday, supported by optimism on global growth and China’s stronger-than-expected credit growth in November. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose 0.06%, with Australian stocks up 0.2% and Nikkei futures steady after Japan’s highest close in 25 years. U.S. stocks rose, led by technology and energy, with the Dow up 0.23%, the S&P 500 up 0.32%, and the Nasdaq up 0.51%; there was no lasting impact from an explosion at New York’s Port Authority commuter hub. Markets focused on Fed policy decisions, with JPMorgan expecting a higher growth forecast, a lower unemployment outlook, and potential implications for the Fed’s “dot plot,” while the ECB was expected to emphasize a low-for-long stance. In currency trading, the euro was steady at $1.1775 and the dollar at 113.54 yen. Bitcoin hit a record high, while gold remained weak and oil prices were firm on news of a temporary North Sea pipeline shutdown.

Psychosis is described as a neuropsychiatric condition thought to involve dysconnectivity between neuronal populations, often studied with network-based methods modeling brains as nodes (discrete brain regions) connected by edges (structural connectivity or functional coupling). Functional connectivity disruptions in psychosis have been inconsistent across studies, with both increases and decreases reported. The passage attributes some inconsistencies to methodological differences in defining nodes using brain region parcellations, noting that there is no consensus on optimal brain parcellation. Many studies use group-based, one-size-fits-all ROIs that may not capture interindividual variability in functional and anatomical organization, whereas individualized parcellations can account for such variability and improve functional homogeneity and prediction of behavior. Standard clinical atlases are derived from healthy participants, which may not capture patient-specific organization; the passage cites evidence that small seed-region displacements can change disorder-related dysconnectivity, emphasizing the importance of valid node definition. The study uses the GPIP method to generate individualized parcellations and compares it to group-based parcellations to test hypotheses about whether failing to consider individual variability leads to noise that reduces power or whether observed FC differences reflect individual brain organization differences. Results described include that individualized parcellations reassign over 40% of vertices and yield slightly higher functional homogeneity, while group-based parcellations detect larger average edge-level FC differences between patients and controls. Network Based Statistic analyses identify connected components with significant FC differences for both parcellation types, with the group-based approach implicating more dysconnected edges. The choice of parcellation alters which specific edges and some regions show differences, but network-level patterns across seven canonical networks are reported as largely robust. Limitations noted include using fsaverage5 with low vertex count for computational cost and that some participants were medicated. The conclusion states that group-based parcellations may inflate case-control FC differences and that individualized parcellations provide more conservative and refined maps of brain network disruptions.

The passage discusses unpredictability in games, the demanding nature of winning a trophy, and praise for players’ preparation and mutual pushing. Coach Quenneville comments that top players may go through scoring stretches but still contribute in other ways, and that ice time is affected by game situations, with players accustomed to heavy minutes. It also mentions adjustments to defensive pairings and line balance, including opportunities for certain players to play together. The coach highlights discipline, especially avoiding penalties to keep the power play effective, and notes the team’s performance in tight games and series progression. The team is described as rising to big stages, with expectations of improvement in the upcoming game.

The passage discusses whether stress or “broken heart syndrome” might explain why some people are hospitalized or die soon after losing a spouse. It notes that shock and stress can affect the heart, and that some studies find increased death risk after losing a longtime partner, though the timing may be coincidental and narratives can be overstated. Dr. Nieca Goldberg says surviving spouses need support because depression after a loss can lead to behaviors like not eating, ignoring symptoms, and getting insufficient rest, which can contribute to life-threatening conditions. It then describes former President George H.W. Bush’s hospitalization for sepsis after his wife Barbara Bush’s funeral, stating that stress can weaken the immune system and make infections harder to fight, while his prior health issues may magnify risk. The passage also cites examples where “broken heart” speculation followed celebrity deaths but later information pointed to other causes, such as diabetes complications for Johnny Cash and a ruptured blood vessel causing bleeding in the brain for Debbie Reynolds.

Local psychologists said the Japanese mobile game Tabikaeru (Travel Frog) has become very popular in Taiwan because it offers companionship and simplicity. Players care for a traveling pet frog, collect clovers to buy supplies, and receive occasional postcards, without controlling the frog. Psychiatrists said its lack of challenges or levels reflects a desire to live simply and to relax amid information overload. Despite being available only in Japanese, the game’s popularity has grown, with Taiwan online searches related to frogs and clovers reportedly increasing 70 times and sales of frog-shaped toys and related items increasing 60 percent since its November release.

Conservative MP Jacob Rees-Mogg was filmed trying to split up a fight after protesters stormed a university hall at Bristol’s University of West England (UWE) where he was scheduled to speak. Footage showed Rees-Mogg being dragged as he attempted to defuse tensions, and he later said the protesters were not intending to debate. Multiple students described masked protesters shouting accusations such as “fascist” and “racist,” with security arriving about 10 minutes after the scuffles began and protesters being escorted out. After the disruption, UWE Bristol stated police were called, the speech resumed, it supports free speech and peaceful protest, and it condemned the protesters’ conduct while praising Rees-Mogg’s composure.

The passage explains numerical methods used to solve linear and nonlinear systems, estimate computational effort, and apply related ideas to implicit ODEs and numerical integration. It reviews solving linear equations with Matlab’s backslash, noting that ill-conditioning can produce multiple solutions that satisfy the equation to machine accuracy. For nonlinear problems it describes Newton-Raphson, trust-region “dogleg” variants, and Matlab’s fsolve, which converts root-finding into minimizing the norm of a nonlinear function, with costs dominated by repeated nonlinear solves and Jacobian formation. It then connects implicit ODE solving to nonlinear equation solving at each time step, discussing how total cost depends on time steps, nonlinear iterations, and matrix/Jacobian costs, and emphasizes nested function calls and functionals.

The later portion shifts to numerical integration via interpolation with basis functions, showing how rectangle, trapezoid, Simpson’s rule, and Gaussian quadrature arise from fitting sampled values to an integrable approximate function. It explains conditions for interpolation (including invertibility/orthogonality of the basis-function matrix), compares polynomial basis choices (including monomials and Lagrange/Newton constructions), and presents Gaussian quadrature’s exactness for polynomials up to a certain order and improved error behavior versus Simpson’s rule. It also describes extending quadrature to multidimensional integrals through nested application of 1D quadrature, and concludes that computation grows rapidly with dimension due to the “curse of dimensionality,” making high-dimensional integration difficult.

Transformer-based large language models have improved natural language processing and enabled AI automation across domains, including financial report analysis, but practical integration into real-world financial systems remains challenging. The passage describes a study conducted with Getinge AB to investigate software engineering challenges and compare open-source (locally hosted) versus commercial (GPT-4o) LLM systems for generating qualitative financial commentary. Using a Design Science field-study approach, the researchers explored domain workflows, defined use cases for summarizing income statement, order intake, and net sales changes, and addressed constraints such as data sensitivity and heterogeneous data formats. They implemented two prototypes: a local multi-agent workflow using open-source models and a GPT-4o API-based approach with structured prompting and post-processing. Evaluation by two professional users assessed usefulness, accuracy, clarity, trust, and workflow integration; results indicated both systems required manual refinement, with issues including redundancy, occasional ambiguity, missed or incorrect trends, lack of transparency, and structural inconsistencies. The study concludes that LLMs can support or partially automate financial reporting, but significant engineering challenges remain, particularly around task specificity, strict formatting/logical rules, data preparation, and output explainability and reliability.

The passage discusses frequent school shootings and the emotional reactions they cause, including anger that innocent students and teachers are harmed and frustration that tragedies continue. It describes police and school preparation such as lockdown drills and notes that no amount of planning covers every situation, including complications from anxious parents arriving to pick up children and disrupted phone lines and transportation. It then considers disaster scenarios like earthquakes, urging families and schools to plan for communication and reunification when phones and roads fail. The passage says drills beyond lockdowns—including fire drills, unscheduled closure drills, and serious disaster drills—can save lives, and it promotes disaster preparedness via disasterprep.dave@gmail.com, mentioning Dave Robinson and his book.

The passage contains a discussion of Hawking–Page transitions and then an extensive introduction to entanglement entropy. Hong Liu explains that the thermal AdS phase corresponds to AdS coupled to a thermal bath, producing mainly a graviton gas, and that the relevant field-theory sector changes at a first-order transition. The discussion also compares confinement/deconfinement heuristically and addresses how partition-function sums relate to the density of states and scaling.

Liu then defines entanglement entropy by partitioning a quantum system into subsystems A and B, tracing out B to obtain the reduced density matrix ρA, and taking the Von Neumann entropy of ρA. For pure states, entanglement entropy of A equals that of B, while for mixed states it can include classical statistical correlations. The lecture provides examples with a two-spin system and summarizes properties such as subadditivity and strong subadditivity.

Next, the passage links entanglement entropy to many-body physics and locality of Hamiltonians, stating that for local systems the ground-state entanglement entropy typically follows an “area law,” with the leading term proportional to the boundary area divided by a short-distance cutoff. It also mentions that subleading terms can encode additional information, giving examples such as topological order via a constant term and the role of central charge in 1+1-dimensional CFTs.

Finally, it describes the holographic (Ryu–Takayanagi) proposal: the entanglement entropy S(A) in a boundary CFT is given by the area of a minimal bulk surface γA ending on the boundary of region A, divided by 4GNewton. The lecture outlines checks such as satisfying subadditivity and reproducing known behaviors, and it explains how, at finite temperature, the minimal surface can lead to results matching black hole entropy in certain limits.

The passage describes a front-view figure of a display screen portion with a graphical user interface. The outermost broken lines indicate the screen area and are not part of the claimed design, while the other broken lines show parts of the interface that also do not form part of the claimed design.

Syrian government forces seized full control of al-Sukhna, the last major town in Homs province held by Islamic State, according to Syrian state media. The military source said Islamic State militants were killed and their weapons destroyed there. The advance is part of a broader push into eastern areas, while Islamic State has lost territory in separate campaigns led by government forces backed by Russia and Iran and by the U.S.-backed Syrian Democratic Forces, focused on capturing Raqqa. Government forces have also crossed into Deir al-Zor province, where Islamic State controls nearly all, except a pocket in Deir al-Zor city and a nearby military base.

Google announced new features for Google Search and Google Play Newsstand to help people follow NBA and NHL playoffs. In Search, Knowledge Panels will show team information such as highlights, photos, or GIFs for NHL, NBA, and MLB teams. Newsstand will provide top headlines, scores, analysis, and videos, along with real-time posts powered by Google’s “Posts on Google” product, which shows approved organizations’ updates as widgets on Search result pages. The Posts on Google program was originally developed for the 2016 U.S. presidential campaign and was expanded last month to other organizations. The sports updates can be triggered by specific queries, like “Stanley Cup Playoffs” or a team’s name, and will be available in both Search and Newsstand for NHL and NBA, with MLB integrated into Search only. Google Play Newsstand will include special NBA and Stanley Cup Playoffs sections, plus real-time posts linked to Search. The features are rolling out globally in English, with team information appearing in the U.S. and Canada.

The passage describes several New York City real estate developments and business moves: controversy over JPMorgan’s Midtown air-rights deal for 270 Park Ave; Salmagundi Club’s use as a TV set and its membership; an East 94th Street garage company buying air rights for a future project; air rights being “mined” for sale at 42 W. 33rd St; L’Occitane en Provence leasing a flagship store at 555 Fifth Ave; CBAM Partners moving into a penthouse office at 51 Astor Place; Knotel receiving investment from Newmark Knight Frank amid flexible office growth; DDG plotting a boutique project in Williamsburg; and a Staten Island housing site being foreclosed due to a low amount owed.

Pennsylvania State Police are searching for the person who killed a dog by burying it alive in a cage in the woods near Minersville, Pa. Workers at the Ruth Steinert Memorial SPCA said it was the worst animal cruelty case they had seen, and found a partially buried cage holding a pit bull that appears to have starved to death after being left for about two months. The SPCA is offering a reward, has set up a GoFundMe for the reward, and asks people to contact state police in Frackville.

The passage outlines four key challenges for QED of attoscience/quantum optics of strong-field physics, centered on developing theoretical quantum-field treatments of strong-field phenomena. Challenge 1 focuses on generating massively quantum states of light, including large-photon-number entangled and multimode squeezed states, using methods such as HHG, bright squeezed light, and structured light. Challenge 2 addresses generating light–matter entangled states in complex materials by exploring entanglement between quantized light fields and electronic states, using ultrafast processes and approaches such as photoelectron density matrix reconstruction. Challenge 3 calls for ultrafast quantum-optical characterization methods to verify and quantify entanglement for applications in nonlinear optics and quantum information. Challenge 4 proposes quantum simulation of QED of attoscience using cold atoms and ions to study tunable strong-field dynamics. The passage then summarizes advances supporting these efforts, including theoretical progress, experimental techniques for photon quantum-state characterization, new structured and quantum light sources, advances in material platforms, quantum simulators, and measurement tools extending tomography and entanglement diagnostics to the ultrafast domain.

The passage describes the DAWN-PLASMA randomized open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Ethical approval and informed consent procedures are outlined, along with requirements to report serious and/or unexpected adverse events to ethics committees. The primary objective is to assess clinical efficacy and safety; the primary endpoint is the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints include clinical status measures through Day 30, mortality and mechanical ventilation outcomes, immunologic measures (including neutralizing antibody titers), safety endpoints (including severe AEs and SAEs), laboratory data, vital signs, and quality of life. Convalescent plasma was administered as 4 doses totaling 800–1000 mL, with the first dose within 12 hours after randomization, and only plasma with neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/160 was allowed. Between 2 May 2020 and 26 January 2021, 320 patients were randomized to convalescent plasma (4 units) plus standard of care and 163 to control (2:1 allocation). The proportion alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15 was similar between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%), and no statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints. Safety outcomes including AEs and SAEs were also similar between groups, with no reported differences in treatment discontinuation due to AEs between arms beyond small numbers.

Matt Damon said he is dealing with a family emergency and welcomed prayers and well wishes as his 74-year-old father, Kent, battles cancer. Damon gave a health update on his father’s cancer, multiple myeloma, which has been in remission since 2011, and said the situation has been slow and unfolding. He has canceled some appearances to stay with his father, including skipping the 2017 Britannia Awards to return to Boston. Damon previously said his father would fight the incurable cancer, and Kent praised Damon as a husband, father, and son at a Massachusetts General Hospital celebration where Kent received treatments.

The passage discusses a difficult situation for a team in a playoff run, emphasizing that a young player should respond and continue playing hard after penalties and setbacks. It also covers managing heavy ice time and conserving energy by playing smart, positional hockey, with players training all summer for expected minutes. The speakers stress that the team is still fighting for its lives, focusing on winning the next game rather than looking ahead, maintaining physical play while staying out of the penalty box, and following the game plan until they win. It further notes challenges in rotating two goalies and says both handled the situation “with a lot of class.”

Australian shares ended Tuesday slightly lower after seven straight gains as financial stocks fell following Australia and New Zealand banks’ quarterly earnings that missed expectations. The Reserve Bank of Australia held rates steady at 1.5% for a ninth straight month, balancing concerns about a property bubble against subdued inflation and wages growth. The S&P/ASX 200 closed down 0.1% at 5,950.4, with ANZ dropping up to 3% on its profit miss; other Big Four banks also fell. Basic materials and gold stocks declined, while consumer non-cyclicals rose, including Woolworth’s. In New Zealand, the S&P/NZX 50 rose for the seventh straight day, up 0.5% to 7,422.49, with gains in industrials and utilities.

The passage describes STAT’s “D.C. Diagnosis” as a twice-weekly newsletter about the politics and policy of health and medicine, available in the web edition and sent to inboxes on Tuesdays and Thursdays. It references a September horse-related event on Virginia’s Eastern Shore and notes that an October scheduling change in 2013 was due to that year’s government shutdown. It also includes a question about which party will win a shutdown, depending on how “win” is defined. The remainder lists multiple health and medicine news headlines and indicates the full content is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

Syed Mohammad Altaf Bukhari, Minister for Education, Finance, Labour & Employment, urged academicians to build students’ confidence and morale, noting that students in Jammu and Kashmir feel they are deprived of privileges compared to other states. Speaking at a two-day national seminar on “Assessment and Evaluation” organized by Cluster University Srinagar, he said schools and colleges should not discourage students and that educators should change how education systems access students in classrooms. He added that students are overburdened by school and private tuition work, leaving less time to assimilate knowledge, and said the seminar aims to improve evaluation. Bukhari asked academicians to investigate why J&K students’ marks percentages are lower and said low marks can limit admissions elsewhere. He also said teachers should expand students’ mental horizons and channel their potential into creative activities. Prof. Dr Sheikh Javaid said the education system needs to match national and international standards and that institutions should do more than provide degrees.

JPMorgan, citing risks and difficulties in monitoring crypto purchases, has decided to restrict them. The passage also says Capital One and Discover do not allow crypto purchases with their credit cards, and Discover’s chief David Nelms characterized users as “crooks.” Additionally, a Coinbase staff member reported that major credit card networks and providers changed digital currency purchase terms so they are treated as cash advances, with additional charges and higher interest rates.

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) arises in the upper aerodigestive tract, and oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) such as leukoplakias and erytroplakias can progress variably to malignancy. Risk assessment based on tissue biopsies can miss low-risk lesions that later become cancer, and recurrence can occur even after surgery. Liquid biopsies using next-generation sequencing to detect cancer-related DNA in saliva and plasma may help detect premalignant or malignant changes before clinical diagnosis.  

A multi-center, non-interventional prospective longitudinal cohort study included 16 Fanconi anemia (FA) patients from Spain who were lesion/cancer-free at enrollment. Saliva and whole blood (for plasma) were collected repeatedly over about 2 years, and DNA was analyzed using a pan-cancer NGS assay for mutations in cancer genes. No copy-number variants were detected. Non-synonymous mutations were found in 15 samples from 9 patients, with limit of detection values down to about 0.07% in saliva and 0.09% in plasma.  

Among patients with clinical follow-up, those with mutations in saliva or plasma developed oral lesions or squamous cell carcinomas with lead times ranging from 23 to 630 days (median 205), while patients without mutations did not develop lesions/tumors in the samples assessed. A diagnostic performance analysis reported 92% accuracy, 86% sensitivity, and 100% specificity. The study concludes that deep sequencing of saliva and plasma mutations can stratify FA patients into higher and lower risk groups and may support closer surveillance, especially in patients without visible lesions.

Anthony Volpe, the Yankees’ shortstop, played most of the season with a partially torn labrum in his shoulder after suffering it in early May and chose not to go on the injured list. The passage says he had a poor 2025 season and struggled in the postseason, including the ALDS. After the ALDS loss, Volpe was asked about the possibility of shoulder surgery and said nothing had been decided and they would figure it out. The Yankees and Volpe will assess the next steps in his rehab during the offseason.

The passage explains offensive line blocking terminology and the responsibilities involved in various run and pass plays. It defines and describes how different blocks are executed, including Trap, Base (1-on-1) blocks, Reach, Down, Log, Pull, Veer, Combo and Double Team blocks (including post and trail roles), Drive, Scoop, Cut, Crack (crack-back), and Kick Out blocks. It also gives specific example play contexts for several blocks (e.g., Trap and Wham; Reach on Outside Zone; Down blocks in gap schemes; Log in Counter; Pull in Power or Sweep; Veer blocks in under-center triple option; Crack in Buck Sweep; Kick out outside the tackle and turning into a Log block if wrong-arms and dives).

Mental health experts are urging barrier fencing on major Lower Mainland bridges. A Crisis Intervention and Suicide Prevention Centre of B.C. release says that between 1991 and 2007, half of suicide deaths from jumping occurred on the Burrard, Granville, Ironworkers, Lions Gate, and Pattullo bridges. The crisis centre’s executive director, Sandy Biggerstaff, said research indicates suicide barriers provide immediate safety and deter people from using other locations or methods, and that crisis phones are important. After crisis phones were installed at Burrard Bridge in March, the centre reported at least four people intended to jump who used the phone to reach a 24/7 crisis line. The centre also reports about 17 police calls per year for suicide attempts on the Burrard Bridge, and says suicide barriers are in place on the Burrard, Second Narrows, and Golden Ears bridges.

Participants were in the study for up to 26 months, and the entire study took about 33 months to complete. The sponsor agent reviewed collected information during and after the study and produced reports after each review. In Phase 2/3, BNT162b2 was 95% effective versus placebo in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 to the end of monitoring on 03 December 2020, with similar results across participant groups. Researchers measured antibody levels after vaccination and reported immune response results that they judged were not likely due to chance. The passage also describes recorded medical problems, including injection site reactions and systemic events, which were generally short-lasting and mostly mild or moderate; it lists examples of temporary lymphocyte changes, and it summarizes serious medical problems and deaths, stating no deaths in Phase 1 and none in Phase 3 among those who had not previously received BNT162b2 before BNT162b2SA.

The passage describes an electronic edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) 1981–1988, Volume IV: Soviet Union (January 1983–March 1985)* produced by the U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian. It explains that the ebook provides full volume content with ebook device features, can be accessed offline after download, and aims to preserve fidelity to the original printed edition, including guidance for citing document numbers. The passage also outlines the FRUS series’ purpose as an official documentary historical record and summarizes the regulatory and statutory standards governing document selection and editing, including accuracy, historical objectivity, disclosure of deletions, and publication within 30 years. It notes that preparing the volume involved sources largely located at the Department of State in Washington and the National Archives and Records Administration.

The passage describes an atlas on evidence-based periodontal and peri-implant plastic surgery and cosmetic dentistry. It aims to bridge research and practice by covering evidence-based decision making, treatment planning, and surgical treatments for recession defects, soft tissue substitutes, aesthetic crown lengthening, and peri-implant plastic surgery. Illustrated case studies show how procedures are applied in daily practice, with guidance on clinical indications, contraindications, and surgical sequence basics. It also includes critical summaries of systematic review results, multidisciplinary decision-making aspects, and decision trees for soft tissue augmentation procedures proposed by the American Academy of Periodontology. The atlas is presented as a clinical guide for general dentists and specialists.

George Tidmarsh, head of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, used his personal LinkedIn page to raise safety questions about voclosporin, which the FDA approved in 2021 for lupus nephritis. In his post, Tidmarsh said the drug has “significant toxicity” and “has not been shown to provide a direct clinical benefit for patients,” leading biotech investors to speculate about whether he is retaliating against a prominent Wall Street investor linked to the drugmaker’s largest investor.

Scientists report that honeybee-collected pollen contains symbiotic antimicrobial-producing bacteria. Symbiotic Streptomyces bacteria produce compounds that fight pathogens of bees and plants, which bees collect with pollen and store in hives as a natural defense system. Researchers found similar beneficial actinobacteria in both honeybee pollen stores and pollen from nearby plants, with DNA sequencing showing the same or closely related bacterial species. Isolated actinobacteria inhibited pathogens in competition assays, including the mold that causes stonebrood, and showed activity against bacterial pathogens and other bee-associated targets. The bacteria had genomic evidence of being endophytes living inside plant tissues. The findings suggest diverse endophytic actinobacteria may help keep bees healthy and could inspire ecofriendly treatments or future hive interventions using beneficial bacteria.

The passage compares value and growth investing strategies and discusses backtesting them on historical data. Value investing is described as buying undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals, expecting market recognition over time; growth investing is described as buying stocks with strong future growth potential regardless of current valuation, aiming for appreciation. It outlines how backtesting works and how it can help identify an optimal mix of value and growth, including a rotation strategy that switches between factors based on performance. The passage also contrasts risk and returns, stating value is generally considered less risky but with lower returns, while growth has higher potential appreciation but higher risk and volatility. It provides historical examples and performance comparisons for growth versus value, including references to ETFs, and concludes that rotating between factors may yield higher returns with less volatility and drawdown than using value or growth alone.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere “GA10x” GPUs, focusing on the GA102 and GA104 architecture and how they improve over Turing. It summarizes performance gains up to 1.7x in raster graphics and up to 2x in ray tracing, and details GA10x features such as second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores (including sparsity, TF32, and BF16 support), and FP32 processing improvements. It also covers related technologies including second-generation ray-traced motion blur acceleration, fifth-generation NVDEC video decoding, seventh-generation NVENC video encoding, and RTX IO for GPU-based decompression and faster I/O. The passage includes information on memory and interconnects (GDDR6X, third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen4), display support (DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC), and datacenter-focused GA10x GPUs like the NVIDIA A40. Appendices reference additional GA10x specifications and an Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature for GDDR6X overclocking.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Current Report on Form 8-K dated February 2, 2021. It states that on February 2, 2021, the company announced its fourth quarter 2020 and year ended December 31, 2020 financial results, with related press release and non-GAAP financial measures information included as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The filing also announces leadership changes: Jeffrey P. Bezos plans to transition to Executive Chair in the third quarter of 2021 and continue as a director, and Andrew R. Jassy will succeed Bezos as Chief Executive Officer and President in the third quarter of 2021. The report lists Exhibits 99.1, 99.2, and an Inline XBRL cover page and includes a signature by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, dated February 2, 2021.

The rupee recovered after a rout, gaining 43 paise to end at 67.43 against the American dollar as traders unwound bullish dollar positions amid easing political uncertainty in Italy and expectations of robust Indian GDP growth. The recovery was also supported by exporters and corporates unwinding long dollar positions and a sharp USD retracement, even as US treasury yields rose ahead of key US data. Crude prices climbed to around USD 76 a barrel despite expectations of higher OPEC supply. The rupee opened flat at 67.87, hit a low of 67.91, and then bounced to 67.42 before closing at 67.43; it reversed the previous session’s fall. The RBI set reference rates for the dollar at 67.6288 and for the euro at 78.1992. The rupee strengthened versus the pound sterling and Japanese yen, but fell versus the euro.

Sony Pictures Entertainment Chairman Tom Rothman told theater owners that the studio aims to appeal to a wide range of audiences, citing franchises like “Spider-Man” and “The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo” series, along with family films, action, comedies, and Quentin Tarantino’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” Tarantino and Leonardo DiCaprio appeared but had no new footage, with Tarantino describing the film’s setting in 1969. Sony also showed footage from “Venom” and “The Girl in the Spider’s Web,” and announced a “Jumanji” sequel with Dwayne Johnson for December 2019, while advising theaters not to give all screens back to “Star Wars.” At CinemaCon, Sony highlighted film quality and diversity, including Gina Rodriguez’s comments about Latino moviegoers and previews for “Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse” and “White Boy Rick.”

U.S. Navy-trained dolphins and their handlers arrived in Mexico to help a last-ditch effort to catch, enclose, and protect the remaining vaquita porpoises. Mexican authorities and international experts plan to search starting Oct. 12 using small boats, with the dolphins using natural sonar to locate the critically endangered animals and guide scientists and veterinarians to capture them and move them to an almost completed floating sanctuary in a protected bay. The plan is considered risky, as vaquitas have never been bred or held in captivity. The vaquita population is estimated at fewer than 30, and threats include illegal gillnet fishing for totoaba. Mexico has banned gillnet fishing in the northern Gulf of California and also announced a ban on all fishing in territorial seas around the Revillagigedo Islands, creating the largest unfished marine park in North America.

Five days after the mass shooting in Las Vegas, authorities said they have not uncovered a clear motive for the gunman. Undersheriff Kevin McMahill said there is no credible information on motivation and that investigators have not found any known link between Islamic State and Stephen Paddock, despite the group claiming responsibility. He said investigators have not uncovered indicators such as notes, social media posts, calls, or computer data evidence, and pledged continued efforts to determine why the attack occurred.

The opinion addresses a dispute between Manuel and Esther Kitrosser (“the Kays”), who guaranteed and pledged collateral for loans and factoring provided by The CIT Group/Factoring, Inc. (“CIT”) to their corporations (Top Form Mills, Inc. and Top Blush Corporation), and CIT’s later liquidation of the pledged collateral after the corporations’ bankruptcy. The Kays sued in 1993 alleging CIT wrongfully withheld collateral and asserting claims for damages; CIT asserted counterclaims based on the guarantees and for attorney’s fees and costs, and moved for summary judgment.

The court’s analysis focuses on three issues relevant to summary judgment: whether CIT could collect postpetition interest on the Top Form/Top Blush debts; whether CIT’s settlement with the EDA for less than 90% of the term loan reduced the amount Mr. Kay could be held accountable; and whether the Kays’ amended claims relate back to the original filing date. Applying New York law, the court concludes that interest continued to accrue during the bankruptcy proceedings because the corporations’ bankruptcy cases were dismissed without discharge, and therefore CIT acted within its rights in liquidating collateral to cover Top Form’s factoring account debit balance, including postpetition interest and the term loan balance. The court also finds CIT’s EDA settlement did not compromise Mr. Kay’s liability under the guarantees. Finally, the court dismisses two additional causes of action in the amended complaint as time-barred, concluding they do not relate back to the original complaint.

Practical labs are important for computer science education, but many institutions suffer from low student engagement, cheating, and inadequate evaluation, leading to graduates lacking practical industry-relevant skills. The paper proposes an AI-based Computer Science Laboratory management system that generates unique, faculty-keyword-guided lab questions per student, tracks progress, and administers an AI-viva test. The viva evaluates not only coding outcomes but also conceptual understanding and reasoning, with faculty override options for automated scoring. The system includes faculty and student dashboards, secure role-based access, an evaluation engine using a fine-tuned XGBoost regressor, and progress analytics. The work also describes a synthetic dataset of 10,000 ML/AI programming questions with difficulty labels and scores, and reports experiments showing agreement between AI and faculty grading and strong evaluation accuracy using cross-validation.

The speaker apologizes for microphones blocking his view, then accepts a nomination and thanks the convention for nominating Senator Barkley of Kentucky. He says the Democratic Party met to reaffirm its beliefs, settle differences by majority vote, and unite to defeat a “common enemy.” He argues the Democrats have delivered security and prosperity over the last 16 years, citing increases in farm income, wages, and national income, and contrasts this with Republican policies. He describes the Democratic Party’s foreign policy as moving away from isolationism and supporting the United Nations, trade barrier removal, and foreign aid. He then criticizes the “worst 80th Congress” for failing to pass Democratic priorities, including price control, housing, labor measures, a stronger labor department, minimum wage increases, education funding, social security improvements, health programs, civil rights, civil rights cloture, and tax relief targeted to those who need it most. He claims the Republicans’ 1948 platform makes promises that were not fulfilled. He calls Congress back into session on July 26 to pass laws addressing prices, housing, education aid, national health, civil rights, minimum wage, social security coverage and benefits, public power and cheap electricity, and laws for displaced persons. He states the results of the special session will be tested by the American people based on the record, concluding with a call for help to win the election and prevent another Republican Congress.

MP Ben Bradshaw called Plymouth’s Johnny Mercer a “bonehead” after Mercer said Jeremy Corbyn is a bigger threat to the UK than ISIS, Russia, and North Korea. Bradshaw said Mercer’s claims are “patently absurd” and criticized Conservative Brexit policies, saying a Labour government should replace them. The comments followed Mercer’s opposition to proposals to take two Devonport-based warships, HMS Albion and HMS Bulwark, out of service. The BBC said the Ministry of Defence described such a move as “pure speculation,” which would save money and free up crew for new aircraft carriers. Luke Pollard said the move would be a “biggest betrayal” of Devonport, warned about the impact on amphibious capabilities and Royal Marines, and said he would fight the cuts in Westminster. Mercer said he would do “everything I can” to prevent the ships being scrapped, and an MOD spokesman said no decisions have been made and discussions are only speculation.

The passage lists multiple dated and sourced State Department and Reagan Library memoranda and related actions from March 16 to April 2, 1983. The passage describes “Triangle Game,” an inside screening offense run with physically strong, well-schooled players. It provides “basic reads & counters” for multiple defender reactions (lowside/topside switch, fronts, switches, anticipation, and double-teams) with corresponding counter actions such as go over/under screens, screen & pop into post advantage, slips to the basket, post lob passes, ball reversals, and post isolation counters (power lay-up, baby hook, turn and face triple-threat, post lob, trap release). The passage describes a DFT+DMFT study using a tight-binding multi-orbital Hubbard model with an on-site density-density Coulomb interaction and a double-counting term to keep DFT quasiparticle energies unchanged. A local DMFT self-energy is used to compute a lattice Green’s function, while non-local self-energy corrections are obtained from charge and spin fluctuations using renormalized interactions and triangular Hedin vertices. Numerical results compare band structures and spectral densities for iron, CrO₂, bulk CrTe₂, and altermagnet CrSb in paramagnetic phases at specific temperatures and interaction parameters. The study finds that non-local magnetic correlations produce stronger changes near van Hove singularities for fillings not very close to half filling (iron, CrO₂) near Curie temperature, while systems closer to half filling (CrTe₂, CrSb) show strong band splitting already from local spin correlations that persists over a wider temperature range. It concludes that the resulting split bands are dispersive and affect spectral weight near the Fermi level, implying sensitivity to magnetic field and potential relevance for transport and spintronic applications, while noting that the density-density approximation may overestimate magnetic transition temperatures.

The passage explains defensive requirements and team strategies to stop the Zipper offense, especially against strong-side down screens. It also presents an “All Out SOS” approach that aims for total disruption by trapping the ball handler on the wing, with a sideline trap sequence (phases 1–3) including rotations, closeouts, fronts, help positions, and pass denial responsibilities, noting timing of rotations when the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The passage describes cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), which reconstructs a 3D protein density from many noisy 2D projection images, and explains that Fourier-space methods rely on the Fourier slice theorem but can introduce information loss and require repeated Fourier operations. It also notes that real-space neural approaches adapted from NeRF are impractical for cryo-EM because reconstruction requires full 3D volumes, CTF application to entire projections, and gradients over dense samples, leading to prohibitive memory and slow training. To address this, the passage proposes GEM, a framework that uses explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for protein reconstruction. GEM represents protein density as a set of 3D Gaussians instantiated only in nonzero-density regions and uses closed-form projection and localized gradient computation to reduce memory and speed up training, avoiding the cubic overhead of NeRF-based methods. Experiments on four cryo-EM datasets report that GEM achieves faster training and lower memory than CryoNeRF while also improving reconstruction quality and achieving gold-standard Fourier shell correlation (GSFSC) resolutions better than 3 Å consistently across datasets.

The passage describes a computational DFT study of carbon upconversion on gold surfaces, focusing on C–C bond formation via the reaction 2 CH2 → C2H4. It compares adsorption, reaction energetics, and reaction pathways on a gold monolayer versus three gold layers using a 2D periodic gold (111) model and the Turbomole DFT setup (PBE with DFT-D3). Results show that the monolayer has larger adsorption and overall reaction energy magnitudes and that both reactants and products bind more strongly to the monolayer than to the three-layer system; product adsorption is very weak in both cases, suggesting likely desorption. The reaction pathway differs: on the monolayer, translational diffusion leads to association over a shared proton followed by bond formation with essentially no significant activation energy, while on three layers, translation is accompanied by greater rotational motion, the intermediate is less stable at larger separation, and bond formation occurs after rotation dominates, with a steep energy and C–C distance decrease. The authors conclude that gold layer thickness strongly affects adsorption energy, reaction path, and energetics, highlighting the role of surface morphology and suggesting further studies on other surface properties and more layers.

AMD testing found that TMPM performance depends on specific guidelines: system activity from overlapping data fabric, DMA, and IOMMU use can reduce performance. For higher bandwidth, commands should use 16 or more pages, with maximum performance when moving 128 pages per command. The TMPM command ring buffer performs best when commands arrive quickly enough to keep it ahead of engine emptying; interrupts should be requested at the end of a sequence rather than every command, using NOP or “Interrupt on Complete.” TMPM can also interrupt when a ring buffer low-water mark is reached. The passage lists several data structures that do not support migration and states that HV/OS must avoid issuing page migration commands for migrating-related structures. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped using IOMMU host page tables, and only one IOMMU host page table may be used per system physical page being migrated. Host software must avoid concurrent modifications to referenced IOMMU host page table entries during TMPM operations and manage reload behavior by pausing operations and using the BIOS to PSP mailbox protocol; firmware reload errors can occur if operations are in flight, if the ring buffer is still initialized, or if firmware versions are incompatible. It also describes interrupt sources, ring buffer initialization steps, SPA alignment/address encoding rules, TMPM command behavior, and key restrictions such as moving only between 4k-aligned pages and requiring certain page states for specific migration commands.

The passage explains the On-Balance Volume (OBV) indicator, a volume-based technical indicator used to assess buying and selling pressure. OBV is calculated by adding today’s volume to the previous OBV when the market closes higher than the prior close, subtracting today’s volume when it closes lower, and keeping OBV unchanged when the closes are equal. It is described as following price trends in uptrends and downtrends, but it may fail to confirm price movements when price makes new highs or lows while OBV does not break prior highs or lows, which is presented as a sign of potential weakness or a fading trend. The passage also states that OBV was first published in 1963 by Joseph Granville and was created to help spot turning points based on changes in volume, with the idea that “smart money” (institutional investors) influences volume. It then describes a backtest on OBV for the S&P 500 (SPY) using RSI applied to the OBV indicator, reporting results for one selected setup (5-day RSI, buy threshold 30) including 337 trades, 0.55% average gain per trade, 73% win rate, 24% max drawdown, and profit factor 2.09. The author concludes that volume may have limited value overall and that other indicators may be preferable.

The passage discusses solving systems of nonlinear equations and the use of iterative methods. It recaps singular value decomposition and defines a matrix condition number in terms of the ratio of the largest to smallest singular values. Because exact solutions are often hard to obtain, the lecture focuses on convergence criteria for iterations, including function norm (residual) criteria and step norm criteria using absolute and relative tolerances. It emphasizes that numerical results must be validated externally (e.g., against experiments, known limits, or analytical results) because calculations can have error and approximations may be insensitive or misleading. The passage then introduces nonlinear systems as vector equations \(f(x)=0\) and explains roots, local uniqueness, and the role of the Jacobian determinant via the inverse function theorem. Linearization and Taylor expansion are used to motivate Newton-Raphson iteration, generalized to multiple dimensions using the Jacobian (solving linear systems rather than computing the Jacobian inverse explicitly). It describes when Newton-Raphson works reliably (near locally unique roots where the Jacobian determinant is nonzero) and problems that can occur near singular Jacobians or non-locally unique solutions, illustrated with a geometric example of intersecting circles. The lecture concludes by noting Newton-Raphson’s local convergence properties, including quadratic convergence when starting sufficiently close to a locally unique root, and previews next-time methods to address breakdowns and computational issues.

The passage describes the widespread habit of scrolling on phones and social media, arguing that technology and social media temptations are affecting attention and mental well-being. The author, a first-year student, says they deleted social media from their phone to focus on revision and meaningful interaction, but the attempt did not go well. They report spending time flicking between multiple apps and feeling invested in others’ lives, which they describe as creating a temporary sense of not being alone but wearing off. The author cites research suggesting more social media use is linked to higher likelihood of depression and that Instagram is rated worst for mental health by young people aged 14–24. They say social media can blur reality for vulnerable individuals and may worsen feelings of worthlessness. Although they feel social isolation increases when they stop, they also find social media is mentally draining and can become escapism and procrastination without benefits. They discuss struggling to fully stop, later checking Facebook occasionally, and plan to use monitoring apps while focusing on creative habits and revision, hoping social media will seem meaningless after exams.

In Illinois federal elections, mailed votes are counted up to 14 days after polls close if postmarked by election day, a rule that Democrats generally support and Republicans generally oppose. In *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, the issue before the Supreme Court is whether Congressman Michael Bost has standing to challenge the rule in federal court. The district court and a divided 7th Circuit panel dismissed his case for lack of standing, concluding he failed to show a concrete, fairly traceable, non-speculative injury that would be redressed by an injunction. The appeals court rejected his “vote dilution” claim as an impermissible generalized grievance and rejected his claimed added costs and harms as self-imposed and hypothetical or speculative. Before the Supreme Court, Bost abandons the vote-dilution argument and instead argues his extra observer-related expenses are “pocketbook injury” and that the 14-day rule harms his electoral chances, potentially affecting fundraising and future political opposition. He also urges a broader standing rule for candidates, while the U.S. supports standing only for Bost’s specific narrow argument and opposes his proposed blanket approach.

The passage describes a study evaluating “Happy Ring” for sleep continuity and sleep architecture in healthy adults, using generalized and personalized sleep-scoring approaches. Participants (40 recruited; 36 analyzed) wore the Happy Ring during one laboratory night and two at-home nights, with sleep assessed against gold-standard or comparator measures: in-lab polysomnography (PSG) and at-home Dreem headband PSG. The Happy Ring uses finger-worn sensors (EDA, accelerometry, PPG heart rate, skin temperature), with sleep and sleep stages classified using a machine learning algorithm. Participants also wore Actiwatch, Fitbit, Whoop, and Oura (variable participation) for comparison. Analyses compared device estimates of total sleep time and wake after sleep onset, assessed sensitivity/specificity for sleep vs wake and sleep stage classification, and evaluated performance via confusion matrices and statistical comparisons. Results indicated both Happy approaches had good sleep-wake detection performance, with Happy Personalized achieving higher specificity than other devices (reported mean specificity 83% in the discussion) and improved sleep stage classification accuracy (P<.001). The discussion concludes the Happy Ring performs well for sleep vs wake detection with moderate specificity, and that the personalized, dynamic scoring approach showed better overall performance than the generalized approach, with further research recommended in broader and larger populations.
