At the U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday, many justices appeared ready to rule against a Colorado law banning licensed mental health practitioners from engaging in any therapy that tries to change a young person’s sexual or gender identity. The case involves arguments about whether conversion therapy harms young LGBTQ+ people, how much evidence is needed to justify a ban, and whether limiting such practices infringes on free speech. A Christian counselor, Kaley Chiles, and her lawyers argue the law is censorship and that talk therapy is protected speech, while the state and medical experts supporting the ban say conversion therapy is harmful, lacks positive evidence of effectiveness, and can be regulated because of the medical context and the provider-patient fiduciary relationship. Major medical organizations oppose conversion therapy. Depending on how broadly the Court addresses the role of medical consensus in regulation, the ruling could uphold the law, increase scrutiny and likely overturn it, or deem it unconstitutional.

Congress MP Jyotiraditya Scindia will lead a 72-hour satyagrah at Dussehra Maidan, TT Nagar, starting Wednesday. Preparations have been made for about 2,000 farmers and party supporters from across the state, including food arrangements at the ground. Scindia will sit on a cot (khatia) with farmers and their leaders to give a “Desi touch.” MLAs and party office-bearers have arrived in Bhopal to help, and participants will include state Congress president Arun Yadav said farmers and supporters from all over the state will join. Other leaders expected to participate include Digvijay Singh, Kamal Nath, Suresh Pachouri, and public representatives. The satyagrah is organized to protest farmer killings by the state government and to mark a silent protest against the anti-farmer government.

Democratic senator Ron Wyden said a U.S. Senate investigation into Russia’s meddling in the election should include a thorough review of financial ties between Russia and President Donald Trump and his associates. In a written request to Senate Intelligence Committee leaders Richard Burr and Mark Warner, Wyden cited resistance to transparency about finances and said financial opacity has hampered efforts to assess relationships. The letter came amid recent disclosures of meetings and arrangements involving Trump associates and wealthy Russians, including Vnesheconombank executives meeting Jared Kushner in December and Paul Manafort admitting he did business work for Oleg Deripaska. Trump has declined to release his tax returns and has denied any untoward relationship with Russia. The passage also references a Reuters investigation finding Russian elites bought property in Trump-branded towers in Florida.

The passage describes iCVS (inferring Cardio-Vascular States), a translational dynamical mechanistic model for estimating a critically ill patient’s hidden cardiovascular state from partially observed data. It addresses clinical challenges such as rapidly fluctuating physiology, noisy signals, and the need to infer unobservable variables (e.g., cardiac output, systemic vascular resistance, filling pressures). iCVS is designed to use routinely available bedside measurements—arterial and venous blood pressure waveforms (and age/weight)—to estimate 15 hidden parameters in real time. The model incorporates cardiovascular control via two autonomic components (a baroreflex-dependent component and an independent component) and allows non-autonomic modulation of systemic vascular resistance. It is demonstrated on data from 10 pediatric ICU patients, where iCVS is used to identify shock states including ongoing bleeding (negative intravascular volume change), distributive shock (negative non-autonomic vascular resistance modulation), cardiogenic shock (reduced contractility), and combinations. The passage also outlines the estimation pipeline: extracting five observables (mean arterial pressure, mean venous pressure, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure) from slow and fast timescales of the pressure waveforms, then fitting model parameters using constrained nonlinear optimization over 300-second segments. The authors report that reconstructed observables correlate well with measured ones and discuss limitations and future directions, including evaluation on larger prospective cohorts and handling noisy, artifact-ridden recordings.

A former BBC weather team leader, Bill Giles, criticized the BBC’s new weather map graphics as a “severe disappointment,” saying the UK appears smaller on screen and that zooming out makes it harder to see details. He wrote in *Radio Times* that the previous maps were clearer and more fit for purpose, and complained that the new national broadcasts offer limited information. Giles suggested Channel 5 instead. The BBC responded by saying the new design is more realistic.

The European Union is preparing formal action against Italy for frequent use of “golden power” laws to influence or block banking mergers. The EU says Italy’s broad application undermines the single market by allowing excessive government control over private transactions, distorting competition, and discouraging foreign investment through uncertainty over approvals. The draft proposal would tighten limits on when member states can invoke national security, requiring clearer explanations and proportionality. Italian officials argue the framework protects economic sovereignty and strategic assets, while EU critics say it increasingly resembles protectionism.

The passage argues for the Payne Tariff bill as a “downward revision” consistent with Republican platform principles. The speaker describes earlier tariff debates (1906–1907), contending that revision should reduce excessive protective rates while maintaining protection strong enough to prevent injury from foreign competition and avoid monopolies that could raise prices. He says the platform did not mean reducing rates enough to introduce foreign competition to lower prices.

He reports that the Ways and Means Committee investigated tariff rates and evidence, and that differences between the House and Senate versions were less than newspapers suggested. Using item counts, he states that of 2,024 Dingley-law items, the Payne law left 1,150 unchanged, decreased 654, and increased 220. He further presents consumption-value comparisons, arguing that decreased duties applied to necessities consumed at far higher value than the increased duties, which he characterizes largely as luxuries.

The speaker addresses concerns, including cotton schedules (with a Senate change toward more specific duties), crockery, and especially wool, which he calls an “important defect” because he believes the wool schedule was not reduced in line with the platform as he interprets it. He concludes that, overall, the Payne bill is the best tariff bill the Republican party passed, pointing to reductions such as in the iron schedule and arguing that higher living costs were not primarily caused by the tariff.

Finally, he justifies not vetoing or defeating the bill on practical grounds and highlights additional provisions: a “maximum and minimum” clause for discriminatory foreign practices, a corporate excise tax to help address a deficit, and free trade between the Philippines and the United States with limits on certain imports. He also describes plans to use funds to support a tariff board to compile factual data for future tariff administration and possibly revision.

China’s rapidly growing debt is estimated by some to reach as high as 328% of GDP, driven by stimulus after the global financial crisis, prolonged loose credit from state banks, and shadow banking growth, with doubts about the reliability of published data such as non-performing loans. Although the economy is still growing and the debt is largely internal behind a closed capital account, the problems are expected to last longer, cause capital misallocation, and require drastic internal policy intervention that may raise governance concerns. The passage also describes China’s overseas lending through investment tied to infrastructure and government support, including loans to countries such as Venezuela, Argentina, Kenya, Laos, Sri Lanka, and Pakistan, with repayment burdens and questionable loan value. It argues that such debt can become political and lead to governments changing priorities, drawing parallels to the Latin American debt crisis of the 1970s–80s and warning that if Belt and Road loans do not generate sufficient returns, China may end up holding unserviceable debt it cannot enforce.

The ADS9803 uses three separate power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. The digital data and configuration interfaces are powered by IOVDD, and a common 1.8V supply powers VDD_1V8 and IOVDD. The passage advises specific decoupling capacitor placement for each power pin, using 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors near AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD, and avoiding vias between these pins and capacitors. For board layout, it recommends not crossing digital lines with the analog signal path, keeping analog inputs and reference signals away from noise sources, placing the reference decoupling capacitor near REFIO and REFM, avoiding vias between REFIO and its bypass capacitors, and connecting GND and REFM to a ground plane with short connections. It also includes sections on TI development tools, documentation update notifications, E2E support forums, trademarks, an ESD caution, and other informational and legal disclaimers.

Ascension Health and Providence St. Joseph Health are reportedly in talks to merge, which would create the largest U.S. hospital chain. The proposed combination of Ascension (St. Louis) and Providence (Renton, Washington) would have 191 hospitals in 27 states and $44.8 billion in annual revenue, surpassing HCA Healthcare. Providence declined to comment, and Ascension did not respond. The discussions have been ongoing for months without an agreement. The report notes nonprofit hospital mergers typically differ from for-profit deals and says the talks come as the healthcare industry is being reshaped by other deals, Affordable Care Act changes, and rising drug prices.

The passage offers advice for having a healthier Diwali, especially for people managing diabetes, poor heart health, or weight. With input from two dietitians, it recommends planning ahead and setting realistic goals, using smaller plates and eating planning, and reducing high-fat fried and salty foods. It suggests choosing higher-fibre options like lentils and wholegrains, adding vegetables for antioxidants, using lean proteins, and replacing refined carbs and saturated fats (like ghee) with healthier alternatives (like wholegrains, vegetables, and oils in small amounts). For sweets, it advises limiting mithai, making swaps to reduce saturated fats and refined sugars, adding fruit-based options, and monitoring blood sugar for type 2 diabetes. It also emphasizes limiting high-calorie sugary drinks and being cautious with alcohol, staying hydrated, not skipping meals, seeking support from loved ones, and using healthier recipes. The page notes that the information is peer reviewed and not medical advice.

The passage describes a pragmatic two-stage adaptive randomized clinical trial of emergency department acupuncture for acute musculoskeletal pain. Background information notes the scale and challenges of musculoskeletal pain management, especially in emergency settings, and the need for equitable multi-modal approaches. The study compares auricular acupuncture (AA) using the Battlefield Acupuncture protocol and peripheral acupuncture (PA) using accessible head/neck/extremity sites, against an attention control receiving usual care (UC). The trial aims to determine which acupuncture style is feasible, acceptable, and safe in the ED, and to assess pain reduction at 1 hour compared with control. The study enrolled 236 patients and found that both AA+UC and PA+UC produced greater pain reductions at 1 hour than UC, with no significant difference between AA and PA, while satisfaction was high and few adverse events were reported. Limitations include a single urban ED in the southeastern U.S. and restriction to English-speaking patients. The conclusion states that both AA and PA are feasible, acceptable, and effective for acute musculoskeletal pain in the ED and should be further explored.

India’s mobile phone customer base rose 0.51% in June to 1.19 billion, an increase of 6 million, according to the telecoms regulator. A table lists subscriptions by company as of June 30, showing the largest totals for Bharti Airtel (280.6 million), Vodafone India (211.9 million), and Reliance Jio (123.4 million). Active mobile subscribers were 1.19 billion, tele-density was 92.12, with urban tele-density at 167.97 and rural at 57.31. In June, 5.88 million subscribers changed service providers via mobile number portability. Total broadband connections were 300.84 million at end-June, including 282 million via mobile phones and dongles and 18.3 million via wirelines. Fixed-phone subscribers fell to 24 million by end-June, and including fixed lines, India had 1.21 billion phone users with a tele-density of 93.98.

The lecture discusses thermal properties of foams used for thermal insulation, focusing on thermal conductivity and how it relates to foam structure. Closed-cell foams are described as having low thermal conductivity due to high gas volume fraction, small cell size, and reduced heat transfer via convection and radiation. The instructor compares foam conductivity to other materials, notes that aerogels have lower conductivity but are weak and brittle, and outlines Fourier’s law for steady conduction and a diffusivity-based equation for non-steady conduction. A data table of thermal conductivity and diffusivity across materials is presented, and aging of blowing gases is mentioned as a reason foam performance can change over time.

Thermal conductivity of foam is broken into contributions from conduction through solid, conduction through gas, convection within cells, and radiation. It is stated that most conductivity comes from the gas, with an example calculation for an air-blown polystyrene foam. Convection is argued to be negligible for typical cell sizes based on the Rayleigh number, with an example showing convection becomes important only for larger cells. Radiation transfer is described using Stefan’s law and Beer's law, including approximations leading to a relationship in which radiation contribution increases as relative density decreases. Figures are referenced showing thermal conductivity versus relative density (including a minimum due to a tradeoff) and increasing conductivity with cell size. The lecture also briefly covers specific heat, thermal expansion coefficient, and thermal shock resistance, concluding that foams can be more resistant to spalling/cracking than the solid they are made from.

The passage describes concerns and expectations for an upcoming series, emphasizing that the opponent is experienced and has few weaknesses, and that the outcome depends on who wants it more. It highlights focus on preparation, strong team maturity, defensive smart play, scoring opportunities, and handling tight games or overtime as battles. Jonathan Toews discusses confidence despite reduced production, personal responsibility across the rink, avoiding letting outside criticism affect him, and learning to contribute in multiple ways. The team aims to set aside personal agendas to win, respond after whistles appropriately, and maintain positivity and unselfishness during the playoffs.

The passage describes a blockchain-based system and method for offering, purchasing, and reselling tokenized securities for transferable equity. It claims priority through a chain of related U.S. patent applications and includes background on blockchain technology, ICOs, and prior art. The invention provides processes for investor accreditation verification using accreditation agencies and databases, maintaining up-to-date whitelists, and optionally blacklists to block malicious parties. It uses smart contracts deployed on blockchain platforms (including examples on Ethereum) and supports document review, acceptance of terms, escrow-based payment and token exchange, enforcement rules such as rest periods before trading, and possible burning of unused tokens. The passage also discusses token transfer after offerings via a marketplace/token transfer framework, SEC compliance features, and examples of token lifecycle periods (promotion, presale, offering, rest, trading). It further introduces BITE tokens and describes their features (e.g., conversion options, dividend rights, financing-related conversions, and liquidity event options) and includes an extended description of contract architecture, including transferrable tokenized securities contracts, proxy contracts, and escrow contracts that encrypt important data.

Justin Timberlake, appearing at a pre-Super Bowl news conference to promote his halftime show, said a reporter’s question about his 3-year-old son Silas playing football drew a sharp response: “He will never play football,” though he later backtracked. He said his main objective is that Silas becomes a great person and that he would support him if he wanted to pursue arts or sports. Timberlake noted that his family is focused on “manners” rather than sports. He will perform at the Super Bowl Sunday for the second time as halftime headliner. In 2004, he performed with Janet Jackson during an incident involving a “wardrobe malfunction,” which both said was an accident; Timberlake said he has since discussed it with Jackson and made peace.

El texto presenta un estudio sobre la expresión de emociones en cuentas corporativas de Twitter en el contexto organizacional y el marketing emocional. Se explica el marco teórico (lenguaje y emociones, y metáfora) y se plantea un análisis lingüístico de un corpus de 798 tuits publicados entre el 1 de abril y el 30 de junio de 2016 por Acciona e Iberdrola. El análisis clasifica tuits como informativos (neutros) o emocionales, y determina categorías de emociones y metáforas asociadas. Se observa que predominan los tuits emocionales en ambas cuentas y que prevalecen emociones con valencia positiva, especialmente “orgullo” y, según la empresa, “interés” y “alegría”. También se describen metáforas vinculadas con la misión, visión y valores de las empresas, destacando en Iberdrola la “luz” para la alegría-felicidad-optimismo y en Acciona la “sostenibilidad” para evocar “orgullo”. El estudio concluye que los mapas conceptuales sobre emociones se relacionan con la identidad organizacional y propone líneas para la enseñanza del español en ámbitos de negocio.

PDP-Laban secretary-general and House Speaker Pantaleon Alvarez said that top presidential aide Bong Go will be part of the party’s slate for the 2019 senatorial elections. Speaking in Caloocan during the oath-taking of new party members, Alvarez also named Zajid Mangudadatu, Senate President Aquilino Pimentel III, Reynaldo Umali, Francis Tolentino, Harry Roque, Geraldine Roman, and Karlo Nograles. Pimentel later added Albee Benitez and Rodolfo Fariñas to the slate, and several of those listed have accompanied Alvarez on party activities. Pimentel said Go “has a slot,” noting Go was expected to join an oath-taking in Bulacan but did not attend.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 10, 2021. The report states that on November 10, 2021, Thomas O. Ryder informed Amazon of his decision to retire from the Board of Directors effective December 31, 2021. The filing was signed by David A. Zapolsky, Senior Vice President, and dated November 12, 2021.

The passage is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Form 8-K filed by Apple Inc. on January 29, 2019. It reports that Apple issued a press release covering Apple’s financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 29, 2018, and states that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. It also includes a statement about the information not being deemed “filed” for certain Securities Act and Exchange Act purposes, and it is signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

A man with a pipe bomb strapped to him set off a low-tech device in a subway passageway under 42nd Street near Times Square on Dec. 11, 2017, injuring the suspect and three other people during the morning rush hour. Mayor Bill de Blasio and Police Commissioner James P. O’Neill labeled it an attempted terror attack. The suspect was identified as 27-year-old Akayed Ullah, and officials said he was inspired by the Islamic State group but had no apparent direct contact; they said he lives in Brooklyn and may be of Bangladeshi descent. Smoke filled the passageway, and a massive police and firefighter response disrupted subway and bus service near the Port Authority bus terminal. Injured people had non-life-threatening burns, ringing in ears, and headaches, while commuters reported hearing chaos and seeing police respond. President Donald Trump was briefed, according to Sarah Sanders.

Airbus Helicopters is threatening to close its Ghimbav-based manufacturing base in Romania and move production elsewhere, seeking a clear commitment from Bucharest on purchasing Airbus helicopters. Its maintenance base in Ghimbav would not be affected. The company reportedly wants Bucharest to place a direct order of at least 16 H215M helicopters for the assembly line inaugurated in August 2016. The reports follow Bucharest’s ties with Bell in 2017, and Airbus is also reported to be targeting orders for 45 attack helicopters and tactical transport. Poland is suggested as a possible transfer location.

The Australian sharemarket fell after losing most of its previous session’s gains, with the S&P/ASX 200 down 26.8 points (0.4%) to 6183.4. The decline was attributed to losses in major bank stocks and broader investor anxiety tied to rising global trade tensions ahead of a US trade tariff deadline. NAB fell 1.3%, Westpac 0.5%, Commonwealth Bank 0.5%, and Macquarie 1.7%. AMP shares dropped 3% after a note from Shaw and Partners raised concerns about potential regulatory fines, lawsuit funding, possible commission changes affecting profit, and dividend impacts. Platinum Asset Management fell 8.9% and Magellan Financial fell 8.8% following broker notes regarding earnings forecast cuts and risks of a retail flow slowdown.

The passage describes a two-center retrospective study developing an automatic, machine learning-based MRI tool for diffuse midline glioma (DMG) prognostication. It uses deep learning to segment tumor subregions (tumor core and whole tumor) from multisequence MRI, extracts radiomic features, and applies machine learning to predict overall survival. The approach was trained and validated on multi-sequence MRI from Children’s National Hospital and tested for generalizability on an external dataset from Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. Reported segmentation performance included mean Dice scores of 0.88 (WT) and 0.91 (TC) internally and similar WT performance externally. For survival prediction, the reported method achieved 77–85% accuracy. The study’s data-driven findings indicate worse prognosis is associated with homogeneous whole tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and a larger post-therapy tumor core/whole tumor volume ratio. The authors propose the tool could support consistent, objective risk stratification and monitoring in clinical trials and practice.

The passage says most discussion of children online is driven by moral panic and child safety, with UK exceptions including Sonia Livingstone’s Parenting for a Digital Future project, Andy Phippen, and Terri Dowty’s Action on Rights for Children. It contrasts this with two more positive US books: Devorah Heitner’s Screenwise, a largely practical guide urging parents to “don’t panic” and focus on relationships, covering risks like pornography, privacy, data collection, and plagiarism while emphasizing asking children’s permission before posting photos; and Jacqueline Ryan Vickery’s Worried About the Wrong Things, which criticizes limiting online youth discussions to “porn, predators, and peers” and instead highlights unequal access and larger opportunities, based on nine months of fieldwork at a diverse Texas school.

Wafra Investment Advisory Group Inc. NY held 167,141 shares of Marsh & McLennan Companies (NYSE:MMC) at the end of the third quarter, valued at $11,240,000. Other investors reported stake increases in MMC, including Washington Trust Bank, Quadrant Capital Group LLC, Homrich & Berg, Sawtooth Asset Management Inc., and HL Financial Services LLC. The passage also reports that institutional investors and hedge funds own 83.81% of MMC’s stock, and provides recent trading and financial details for MMC, including an EPS figure of $0.69 for the quarter reported on October 25th. It lists several analyst rating changes and price objectives, insider share sales by the chairmen Alexander S. Moczarski and Peter Zaffino, and a company profile describing MMC as a professional services firm in risk, strategy, and people.

AUM Capital benchmark indices fell, with energy stocks like Indian Oil Corp Ltd and Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd declining on reports that refiners may buy stakes in GAIL (India) Ltd. The S&P BSE Sensex ended at 32,923, down 253 points, and the Nifty at 10,094, down 101 points. India’s current account deficit widened to 2% of GDP. Asian markets dropped amid investor caution ahead of likely Federal Reserve rate hikes. The passage also provides technical outlooks for Nifty and Nifty Bank, and lists five stocks with stated ratings, targets, stop losses, and near-term return estimates.

The passage says investors have difficulty finding historical comparisons for stock reactions to rising U.S.-North Korea tension, noting that war impacts would be catastrophic. It argues that stock valuations do not consistently correlate with conflict levels. It references the early 1990s after the Soviet breakup and the first Gulf War, when the market’s price-to-earnings ratio rose and a “peace dividend” was cited, while noting that after Sept. 11 stocks dropped. It also cites mixed relationships during the Korean and Vietnam wars and that recent conflicts have not prevented P/E ratios from rising. It attributes a market drop after President Trump’s tough North Korea remarks to factors related to Trump and the reversal of the “Trump trade,” suggesting investors will focus on his unpredictability rather than imminent war.

The passage consists of remarks about a team’s playoff readiness and mentality, emphasizing earning respect through past performance, being “in it to win it,” and keeping confidence stable regardless of outcomes. It discusses day-to-day injury uncertainty, the importance of staying emotionally focused after a previous series, and the need to learn continuously in coaching. The speakers also consider that a long break may not hurt beyond an initial period, review recent rest and preparation time, mention specific players’ situations and goaltending confidence, and stress that both teams should be ready and to avoid panic if something goes wrong during a game. They plan to review options in meetings and decide later.

Seven Myanmar soldiers attacked a newlywed Rohingya woman identified as F in western Myanmar in June 2016, bound her husband, stole her jewelry, stripped her clothes, and raped her while other men held her down and beat her. The soldiers killed her husband, slit his throat after shooting him, and burned their bamboo house. Two months later she learned she was pregnant. The Associated Press interviewed 29 Rohingya women and girls who fled to Bangladesh; they described systematic group assaults between October 2016 and mid-September, with assailants often wearing military-style uniforms. The women said they feared being killed if identified by name. The U.N. cited the assaults as a calculated tool of terror, while Myanmar’s armed forces did not respond to AP questions and an internal investigation concluded none of the assaults occurred. A Rakhine minister dismissed rape claims in September, and doctors and aid workers said only a fraction of survivors had come forward, with Médecins Sans Frontières treating 113 sexual violence survivors since August. F later described another attack in mid-September in which a boy and a man were killed, the women were assaulted again, and she fled to Bangladesh with a friend. She currently lives in a bamboo shelter and fears for her child, saying everyone around her has died and that she would have nothing left if she gave the baby away.

The passage explains how to attack a Box & One defense using a “Pound Cake” offense by isolating the star player 1-on-1 in the post. It describes options after post isolation, including drop passes when the star is helped on penetration, using base screens where O4 and O5 set screens and the star rolls or breaks away depending on defender position, and various reads (curl, fade, back cut, screen & roll) with corresponding counters. It also covers ball reversal passes (O1 to O2, then to O5 stepping out) leading to a star curl back to the middle, additional options such as screener pop and guard basket cuts, and a “pop 1-on-1 isolation” where posts step out and guards/wing players flare to the wings so the star can attack the defender. A variation using double mid-screens (“Horns”) is noted, with O4/O5 or O1/O2 setting double mid-screens to create outside-shot opportunities and match-up issues for the box zone. Implementation emphasizes execution of mid screens, base screens, and strong post ups with coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience, along with scouting opponents and adjusting alignments to exploit weak defenders. The passage also summarizes the Box & One defense as four players in a box zone and one “Chaser” focused on aggressive full pass denial.

Bayshore Petroleum Corp. announced the resignation of director C.F. Cheng effective immediately. The company said he left to focus on other business interests, thanked him for his support and years of service, and wishes him well. Bayshore anticipates replacing him soon in connection with an anticipated financing. The release also states it is not an offer or solicitation in the United States and that the company’s securities have not been and will not be registered under U.S. securities laws.

Daily net share trading on South Korea’s main stock exchange as of 0724 GMT on April 10 shows foreigners net selling (-54.0 billion won), institutions net selling (-4.5 billion won), and retail net buying (6.5 billion won). The passage notes foreigners have been net sellers for six consecutive sessions, with net sales totaling 353.6 billion won ($309.85 million).

The U.S. Supreme Court will consider whether a trial court may bar a criminal defense lawyer from speaking with a client overnight recess about the client’s ongoing testimony. The case involves David Villarreal, who claimed self-defense after stabbing his boyfriend and was convicted after being the only defense witness during the guilt phase. During an overnight recess after Villarreal testified on direct examination, the trial judge told Villarreal and his attorneys not to confer while Villarreal was effectively treated as still on the stand, while also noting Villarreal had a Sixth Amendment right to talk to his attorney. On appeal, Villarreal argued the restriction violated his right to effective assistance of counsel. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals upheld the order, citing U.S. Supreme Court “bookend” precedents from 1976 and 1989 that address limits on attorney-client conferences during recesses. The passage outlines arguments from Villarreal, Texas, and a U.S. “friend of the court” brief, including disputes over whether limiting discussion of testimony is workable, how such rules relate to Sixth Amendment history, and whether the Court might overrule the 1976 precedent that struck down a broader overnight no-conference rule.

A sharp drop in FAANG technology stocks, alongside rising 10-year U.S. Treasury yields and mixed earnings reports from industrials, pushed the Nasdaq Composite lower on Tuesday. Google-parent Alphabet fell 3.9%, and the other FAANG stocks—Facebook, Amazon, and Netflix—also declined. Apple dropped for a fifth straight session amid fears of slowing iPhone demand, while AMS and Corning warned of weaker demand. The technology sector fell 0.7%, and broader indexes were down, with the Nasdaq down 0.60%. The 10-year yield hit 3% for the first time since 2014, while strategists said the level was mainly technical or psychological. Industrial stocks also slid, including Caterpillar after reversing despite stronger results, Lockheed Martin after a cash-flow outlook setback, and 3M after cutting its forecast. Despite these moves, most reported first-quarter results have topped profit estimates, and market breadth showed advancing issues outnumbered decliners.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded Liberty Global PLC (NASDAQ:LBTYA) from a hold to a buy rating and set a $35.00 price objective, citing expected growth drivers but also noting that the stock has underperformed due to multiple headwinds and concerns about Europe’s economic conditions, competition, foreign exchange risks, and integration risks. Other firms issued mixed ratings, with an overall average rating of Buy and a consensus target price of $43.85. The stock opened at $30.59 on Tuesday; the company has a $27.72 billion market cap and 52-week range of $26.16 to $36.76. The passage also reports insider purchases by EVP Bryan H. Hall and Director Paul A. Gould, states that insiders own 3.93% of the stock, and describes recent institutional stake increases. Liberty Global PLC is described as an international cable company operating in 14 countries, serving about 25 million customers with tripleplay services.

The passage states that the bark *Cape Horn Pigeon* was seized by the Imperial Russian Government and detained at Vladivostok, preventing it from leaving before October 1, 1892, after which the Okhotsk Sea whaling season would close between October 1 and 10. It alleges this seizure and detention caused losses including deprivation of the vessel for the remainder of the season, consumption of provisions by Russian officials, and expenses and hardships such as maintenance costs, telegraphic messages, legal counsel, hired clerical assistance, boats, carriages, detention of the crew, and lack of support. The captain estimated damages at $49,500 and submitted a claim to the Russian government on September 15–27, 1892. A U.S. envoy later requested investigation in a May 3, 1893 note (Exhibit Q). A Russian reply dated June 24, 1893 (Exhibit I) said a commission found no reason for confiscation, attributed the arrest to a misunderstanding, ordered release, and indicated $2,500 would be sufficient for losses, while deeming a $45,000 estimate for whale damages excessive. A further U.S. claim was presented June 2/June 14, 1894 (Exhibit R), and after continued requests, a Russian reply was received October 12/24, 1895 (Exhibit S), which requested vouchers for $3,400 in expenses already included in the U.S. claims.

Defence Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said her ministry will assist whenever necessary to rescue about 1,500 Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims stranded in Nepal due to inclement weather, after two Indian pilgrims died. She said the External Affairs Ministry is working on the rescue. She also noted Tamil Nadu’s plan to set up a control room in New Delhi to provide logistic support to pilgrims when they arrive, and that around 19 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu are among those stranded near Tibet.

The passage marks an NHL centennial year, noting multiple events since January and a fan vote that drew over four million votes and nine million page views. It recounts the narrowing process from past Stanley Cup winners to an announced greatest NHL team, led by six Hall of Famers including Wayne Gretzky. The Edmonton Oilers are described as defending their title: they scored more goals than they allowed in the regular season, swept the Los Angeles Kings and Winnipeg Jets, eliminated the Chicago Blackhawks, and overcame the Philadelphia Flyers after losing the series opener to win the Stanley Cup for a second consecutive year. Gretzky is credited with playoff records and winning the Conn Smythe Trophy, and Paul Coffey is noted for winning the Norris Trophy.

Health experts say frequent wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath may indicate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Teresa Summe of Lee Health says a pulmonary function test is key to diagnosing COPD and that symptoms can be triggered by exercise, walking, or even sleep. She advises people at early stages to learn basic management to prevent worsening, noting that untreated COPD can damage lungs further. Summe also says COPD is not only affecting older people and may occur in younger populations due to premature birth, uncontrolled asthma, environmental exposures, or genetic factors. She adds that smoking does not alone determine COPD and non-smokers can still develop it. If diagnosed, patients can manage symptoms through breathing and conservation exercises to help strengthen lungs and prevent COPD from becoming worse.

The passage is a presidential address describing the return from Europe to report on meetings with Premier Khrushchev and others, focusing on threats to West Berlin and U.S./NATO commitments. The speaker says the immediate threat is in West Berlin but that it is worldwide, and argues that Soviet actions aim to end rights in West Berlin and commitments to its two million free people. The address outlines U.S. positions on legal rights and access to Berlin, NATO coverage, and the need to defend against Communist efforts to change Berlin’s status. It also calls for strengthening Western military capabilities, including speeding up allied military goals, expanding defense readiness, missile and bomber alert measures, increased air and sea lift, manpower increases, and procurement of non-nuclear weapons and equipment. The speaker announces requests to Congress for additional Armed Forces appropriations, expanded military strength, changes to draft and reserve activations, reactivation/retention of certain ships and planes, and increased Civil Defense funding for fallout shelters, warning systems, and related objectives. The passage further discusses budget impacts, plans to balance the next fiscal year budget, possible tax changes, and efforts to avoid both panic and timidity. It states the U.S. will seek peaceful discussions while being ready to resist with force if attacked, and concludes with the claim that freedom must be defended, peace sought, and long-term perseverance is required.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 28, 2015 reports that the company designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, portable digital music players, and related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content. For the three months ended March 28, 2015, Apple reported net sales of $58,010 million and net income of $13,569 million, with basic earnings per share of $2.34 and diluted earnings per share of $2.33. For the six months ended March 28, 2015, net sales were $132,609 million and net income was $31,593 million, with basic earnings per share of $5.43 and diluted earnings per share of $5.39. Condensed consolidated balance sheets as of March 28, 2015 show total assets of $261,194 million and total liabilities and shareholders’ equity of $261,194 million. Early Offense is described as having three phases: an initial early push, a continuous early flow into a set, and a final continuity-style play as the shot clock winds down. The initial push is meant to end of the court before the defense organizes, creating outnumbered situations and mismatches, but if it doesn’t produce a good shot or advantage, the offense should move into flow without letting the defense set up. If flow also doesn’t produce a good shot or advantage, the offense should move into continuity offense.

Key success elements include initiating early offense against defensive pressure, breaking on every possession, moving smoothly from push to flow to continuity, and playing disruptive, tenacious defense that forces bad shots and turnovers. Rebounding and outlet/inbound passing are emphasized, including boxing out, executing outlet passes, using fakes/lobs or breaking out on dribble if the outlet is intercepted, and having the receiver see the floor. The passage also outlines transition/fast break guidance, such as starting from run rather than dribble, using quick outlet passes, leading long pass receivers to scoring areas, filling lanes quickly, running wide, and scoring while going to offensive boards.

Dennis Waldron, as administrator of Eugenia Waldron’s estate, appealed an order granting defendants’ summary judgment dismissing his complaint. The court held the conversion claim was properly dismissed because medical records are not cognizable as an intangible property right for conversion and records belong to the doctor. It also found the fraud claim properly dismissed since the evidence did not show the necessary misrepresentation by Tryon, and any statements about the scope and purpose of the records were made to hospitals, not to plaintiff. The court concluded the intentional infliction of emotional distress claim was properly dismissed, noting Ball provided compassionate support and obtained and used the records to defend a workers’ compensation-related claim, but the conduct was not sufficiently outrageous. Finally, it affirmed dismissal of the privacy claim, stating there is no common-law invasion of privacy action in New York and that the relevant statutory provisions and CPLR 4504 did not support plaintiff’s claim. The order was affirmed.

A memorandum from Secretary of State Shultz to President Reagan says the 1983 NSPG discussion highlighted increased Soviet activism under Andropov, requiring U.S. strength and a strategy that uses intensified dialogue with Moscow to test whether improvements in US-Soviet relations are possible. The memo argues there is no realistic scenario for a breakthrough to amicable relations, but firm U.S. policies could induce changes in Soviet behavior. It describes Soviet foreign policy energy in Europe (including actions related to INF), in Asia (renewed talks with China and hints on Afghanistan), and proposes preempting this with intensified diplomatic and public activism. It lists preconditions for the dialogue—rebuilding U.S. economic and military strength, revitalizing alliances, stabilizing relations with China, regional peacekeeping efforts, and continued competition in ideas—and outlines purposes such as probing for Soviet flexibility, controlling events, and maintaining Allied and domestic support. It states the dialogue should not abandon the established policy framework and should address military buildup, international expansionism, and human rights violations while keeping basic requirements for improved relations.

The study used a single-group posttest experimental design with five beginner guitar students (ages 18–33) who had no prior guitar instruction. An eight-week, activity-based lesson plan was developed and implemented, with lessons delivered online for 50 minutes each (16 total instructional hours). The course covered scales, chords, and arpeggios, including major and minor scale formations and finger/exercise patterns, chord formation and barre technique, and arpeggio patterns on open strings and chords. Data were collected through literature review and expert evaluation: three field experts approved the program outline and evaluated performance using a 5-point Likert scale derived from Albuz’s performance assessment criteria. Theoretical knowledge and performance tests were administered at the end of the chapter, and success levels were classified by weighted averages.

Test results showed theoretical knowledge scores of 90, 80, 100, 90, and 100 (mean 92) and students’ chapter average achievements of 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, with a class average of 93.6. The study concluded that activity-based lesson plans in amateur guitar education were effective during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The passage defines a Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) as the co-evolution of a Business Ecosystem and a Digital Ecosystem. It describes Business and Digital Ecosystems, relevant modeling approaches such as Electronic Institutions and Contractual Agent Societies, and the DBE lifecycle phases: formation, evolution (execution), and dissipation. The formation phase is emphasized as crucial for success or failure of transactions, with negotiation as a key activity. The Contract Net Protocol (CNP) is presented as an accessible negotiation protocol that decomposes negotiation into steps involving task identification, announcement, evaluation, bidding, award, contract processing, and termination. The work focuses on extending CNP via Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), adding quality evaluation steps during negotiation to improve committed contract selection, reduce transaction risk, and boost performance. It discusses trade-offs, mainly that added quality evaluation increases negotiation time and can reduce efficiency, while potentially improving overall interaction performance and reducing uncertainty. Quality is described through reliability, trust, and reputation, with these concepts defined using prior references. The conclusion states that the paper proposes CNQP for quality-based negotiation and notes future work on applying the protocol for negotiation on service-level parameters.

The passage describes using Ambassador and adapter-style container patterns to standardize interfaces for experimentation/request splitting, monitoring, logging, and health checks. It explains how heterogeneous application logging and monitoring can be adapted into consistent interfaces for tools like Prometheus and fluentd, and how adapter containers can add richer health monitoring without modifying existing database containers. It then introduces microservices and multi-node distributed patterns, focusing on replicated load-balanced services with readiness probes and session tracking, followed by application-layer replication using caching (Varnish) and SSL termination (nginx) behind additional replicated layers. The later sections discuss sharded services and sharded caching, including how sharding functions map requests to shards using hashing and modulo, why consistent hashing reduces remapping during shard count changes, and how scatter/gather distributes computation across replicas with considerations like overhead and the straggler problem. Finally, it introduces event-driven/serverless (FaaS) concepts, outlining benefits, challenges, and a decorator pattern using FaaS for request/response transformation, with an example of defaulting missing fields and an example of handling events such as sending two-factor authentication codes.

The passage describes the Gaia hypothesis, first proposed by James Lovelock in the 1970s, which proposes that Earth is a self-regulating living organism where living things interact with inorganic processes to keep the planet healthy despite threats like a brightening sun, volcanoes, and meteorite strikes. The passage argues that the best time frame to trade is daily bars, while recommending being agnostic and open to other time frames based on personal needs and where an edge can be found. During a government shutdown, the federal judiciary plans to use funds such as court fee balances to temporarily continue paid operations. Federal courts expect to keep paying staff through Oct. 17 using funds not tied to a new congressional appropriation; most proceedings and deadlines will continue through that date, though hearings and filing dates may be rescheduled if executive-branch attorneys are unavailable. The U.S. Supreme Court plans to rely on funds not subject to annual approval to maintain operations during short-term lapses. Some district courts have already issued orders delaying certain civil cases and deadlines. If funds run out, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act, which may require some staff to work without pay and lead to furloughs, with each court and federal defender’s office determining staffing needs to support constitutional functions.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine report that brown fat contains a hidden “backup heater” system that produces heat and helps burn calories even when usual energy systems slow down. Mouse studies found that mitochondria normally produce heat via uncoupling protein 1, but mice lacking this protein still burn energy, leading researchers to identify peroxisomes as an alternative heat source. Cold exposure increased peroxisome numbers, and peroxisome heat production depended on the protein acyl-CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). Mice without ACOX2 in brown fat produced less heat, tolerated cold poorly, had lower body temperatures, worse insulin sensitivity, and gained more weight on high-fat diets, while mice engineered to have higher ACOX2 showed increased heat production, better cold tolerance, improved insulin sensitivity, and better weight control. The researchers also suggested that certain fatty acids from the body and from dietary sources could potentially support this pathway, and they are investigating dietary approaches and drug compounds that activate ACOX2. The work was supported by NIH and an FP7 European project, and a provisional patent application was filed for targeting ACOX2 activation for obesity and related metabolic diseases.

The passage explains numerical optimization methods for finding minima. It discusses steepest descent for unconstrained optimization, including how using a quadratic (Taylor) approximation determines an optimal step size and how contour geometry affects steepest descent paths. It then connects optimization to mechanics and potential energy, illustrating that “flat” energy landscapes make minima difficult to locate, which motivates better numerical approaches. Linear systems \(Ax=b\) are reformulated as minimizing a quadratic functional under conditions such as \(A\) being symmetric and positive definite. Because fixed step sizes in steepest descent can cause oscillations, the passage introduces conjugate gradient for efficient minimization in at most \(n\) steps for \(n\) unknowns, requiring only products of \(A\) with vectors and applying to symmetric positive definite systems. It contrasts this with Newton-Raphson, which solves \(\nabla f=0\) by using the Hessian inverse and can converge rapidly near a critical point, but may fail to go downhill if the Hessian has negative eigenvalues or is singular. Finally, it describes trust-region strategies that combine Newton-Raphson and steepest descent by deciding which step to take within a radius where the quadratic approximation is trusted, including heuristics for adjusting the trust-region size and the “dogleg” variant used in MATLAB.

The passage discusses the oyster aphrodisiac myth and reports new Harvard T.H. Chan research on seafood intake and sexual activity. A study of 501 couples trying to get pregnant found that higher seafood intake was associated with more sex and higher fertility (“fecundity”). Specifically, 92% of couples who ate fish and shellfish at least twice a week became pregnant within a year, and those eating the most seafood (8+ times per month) had a 22% higher rate of sexual activity than average. The researchers said they did not measure zinc intake and were uncertain about what drives the association, suggesting possible mechanisms involving zinc or shared meals and time together. The passage also lists other claims linking food and sex, including surveys about millennials, dating messages mentioning food (including guacamole), an apple study on arousal in women, and a psychology study comparing how often people think about sex and food.
