The passage provides an overview of a study investigating the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage measured with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI at 7 Tesla in human subjects. Hypertension was described as potentially causing vascular remodeling that can lead to endothelial dysfunction and BBB breakdown, but the precise pathophysiology was noted as not fully elucidated. The study used a sparsely time-sampled DCE-MRI protocol to assess BBB leakage rates (Ki) and blood plasma volume fraction (vp) in grey matter and white matter regions of interest. Twenty-three patients with essential hypertension and 20 normotensive controls matched on age and sex were included. Results reported that hypertension status showed no significant difference in BBB leakage, while higher measured blood pressure (SBP, DBP, and MAP) was associated with stronger BBB leakage in grey matter but not in white matter. Sex was associated with leakage measures, and the associations remained after adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors and cSVD score. A post-hoc subgroup analysis suggested a trend toward less BBB leakage in medically treated patients compared with those with current hypertension, and no significant differences for vp. The authors conclude that dichotomous hypertension status was not associated with BBB leakage, but continuous blood pressure measures were, with antihypertensive medication showing a potential protective effect.

A valid device write operation requires at least 32 SCLK cycles within a data transfer frame. The document describes three categories of read protocols: legacy SPI-compatible with a single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible with dual SDO-x, and an ADC controller clock/source-synchronous (SRC) protocol. For legacy SPI-compatible reading with a single SDO-x, the host uses SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, or SPI-11-S. After power-up or asynchronous reset, the device supports SPI-00-S for read and write. To select a different SPI-compatible protocol for both operations, the SDI_MODE[1:0] bits are programmed in SDI_CTL_REG (using SPI-00-S for the first frame), and the SDO_MODE[1:0] bits are set to 00b in SDO_CTL_REG. The selected SDI_MODE[1:0] protocol applies to both read and write operations; when reading, configure SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b. When using SPI-compatible protocols, the RVS output remains low throughout the data transfer.

Plans have been submitted to extend the use of the former Bartons County Infant School in Bersted for Chichester Free School. The application seeks to amend a condition requiring the site to be vacated and modular buildings removed by September 1, 2018, so the site could be used for an additional academic year up to September 31, 2019. The application cites an increase in pupil numbers from 390 to 420 and possible delays to highways works. It states it may not be feasible for all pupils to move for the start of the 2018/19 academic year, though earlier completion of the move may be possible depending on travel planning work between the school and local councils. The comment and decision deadline is July 27.

The passage describes Belarus’s education system and focuses on out-of-school education as a significant component and part of lifelong learning. It outlines historical development in three stages: early literacy programs, Soviet-era system-building, and post-Soviet reforms combining Soviet and EU ideas. It cites Belarus’s 2011 Education Code defining out-of-school education and setting provisions for institutions, access, student development goals, and government responsibilities, and lists related decrees and regulations. It summarizes the structure and scale of out-of-school institutions in Belarus by 2021, including comprehensive and specialized types, and highlights common specialized sectors such as regional study tours and ecosystem protection. It then presents main cultivation objectives for out-of-school education as four abilities: mastering information technology knowledge, developing social personality, surviving in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong study, with examples of institutions and activities addressing these goals. The passage concludes that Belarus combines Soviet and EU approaches and emphasizes legislation, targeted abilities, widespread public institutions, and balanced development in out-of-school education.

The lecture explains the mean-variance “bullet-shaped” efficient frontier created from combining weighted averages of securities’ expected returns, variances, and covariances, emphasizing that rational investors prefer the upper branch. Using three example stocks (General Motors, IBM, Motorola), it argues that holding 100% in a single stock is typically not on the curve and that diversification reduces risk. It then introduces mixing any efficient portfolio with a risk-free asset (T-bills), forming a straight line; the investor’s best choice is the tangency portfolio, which yields the highest risk-reward trade-off (described via the Sharpe ratio). The discussion also covers how adding more securities shifts the frontier and tangency point, and why negative correlation is difficult to achieve.

The lecture connects these ideas to equilibrium and benchmarking: if everyone chooses the tangency portfolio plus T-bills, the tangency portfolio must correspond to the market portfolio (all equities weighted by market capitalization). This leads to a relationship for expected return on efficient portfolios using the market risk premium and then extends the framework using beta, defined via covariance with the market relative to market variance. Finally, it states that the expected “fair” rate of return for discount-rate/NPV purposes can be computed as beta times the expected excess return of the market portfolio, while noting that key assumptions will be discussed later.

The President transmits to the U.S. Senate a convention between the United States and Great Britain, negotiated at Washington on the 19th instant, for advice on ratification. The treaty aims to form a commercial alliance with major maritime states to protect a planned ship canal through Nicaragua connecting the Atlantic and Pacific, and to extend similar protection to contemplated railways or canals via Tehuantepec and Panama routes and other interoceanic communications. It does not propose using public Treasury funds, and it provides protection to capitalists undertaking canal or railway construction across the Isthmus without preferring one route over another. The President says the treaty would secure the future liberation of Central America from foreign aggression and that negotiations sought both passage for U.S. citizens and governments and the independence and sovereignty of Central American republics, opposing any U.S. policy to seize or annex their territories. The President states the treaty follows principles from prior Senate resolutions and earlier presidencies, including securing equal navigation rights in exchange for reasonable tolls. The President also submits related correspondence between the U.S. Secretary of State and the British plenipotentiary, and says that if the Senate confirms this treaty, it may be necessary to amend it and a previously submitted Nicaragua treaty so both conform. He adds that he believes France and Russia are ready to accede and that no other major maritime state will refuse.

The passage describes four overnight trading strategies for the S&P 500 that buy at the close and sell at the next day’s open, aiming for short holding periods and minimal drawdowns. For the first strategy, trades require the close to be above the 200-day moving average; without it, the equity curve worsens. The second strategy buys on a new n-day low with additional criteria and reports 12.69% profit, a 14% win rate, and a profit factor of 2.6. Strategy three is summarized as having an upward-sloping equity curve and a profit factor of about 3.8. Strategy four is a variation of strategy three, and it is described as impressive because the market is short-term oversold and can bounce quickly; a twist involving holding until the next close when SPY opens down by more than -0.1% boosts the strategy, with later years paying off to hold even when the market opens up. The passage also explains that overnight strategies limit risk by reducing exposure to market fluctuations, though adverse news during closed hours can cause losses mainly in the single digits.

The passage describes a test drive of the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon at Atco Dragway in New Jersey, where the narrator took the car for a dozen runs. It highlights the Demon’s 6.2-liter supercharged V8 (808 hp stock and 840 hp with the Demon Crate for 100 octane race gas), 770 lb-ft of torque, modified components, and an 8-speed automatic with TransBrake drag-racing technology. The car’s weight reduction efforts, drag-focused suspension settings, and performance results are noted, including sub-10-second quarter-mile times depending on fuel. The passage also discusses launch control versus the TransBrake, traction limits in TransBrake mode, the development manager Jim Wilder’s experience, the warranty claim with high repeated testing, pricing and limited production (3,300 allocated units in the U.S. and Canada), and dealer-markup and resale speculation. It concludes by suggesting the Challenger line may continue beyond the Demon’s one-year model.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana case State ex rel. Joshua W. Curran v. State (No. 2010-KH-0233) concerned a plaintiff’s application for supervisory and/or remedial writs from the Parish of East Baton Rouge, 19th Judicial District Court. The application was denied.

During a February 1, 2018 episode of “Jeopardy!” with the Super Bowl approaching, the contestants struggled with a “Football” category. The category was saved until the board was nearly empty, but none of the five questions were answered or even buzzed in with educated guesses. The questions included topics such as option plays, Tom Landry’s coaching, fair catches, offsetting penalties, and the defensive line that led the Minnesota Vikings to four Super Bowls. Host Alex Trebek commented after they drew a blank and joked about going to commercial, while the audience laughed at the silence.

The passage explains that higher education supports individual development and economic and social transformation, but student dropout tendencies are increasing worldwide and in Türkiye. In Türkiye, the dropout rate among university students rose from 2.7% (2012–2013) to 17% (2023–2024). Dropout in higher education is described as multifaceted, with sociological, organizational, psychological, and economic perspectives, and the study addresses the lack of comprehensive research in the Turkish higher-education context.  

The study aims to determine dropout-tendency levels among higher-education students in Türkiye and examine differences by variables (e.g., gender, year of study, metropolitan area, working while studying, close friends who dropped out) and correlations with attendance frequency, parental education, GPA, family income, and number of siblings. Using a descriptive correlational design grounded in Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model, data were collected in 2023–2024 from 1,061 students at Turkish public universities using the School Dropout Scale in Higher Education. The results indicate a moderate overall dropout tendency (mean 2.67). Dropout tendency did not differ significantly by gender, but it increased for students in third year and above, non-metropolitan students, students who worked while studying, and students with close friends who dropped out. Spearman correlations showed negative associations between dropout tendency and school attendance, parents’ education, GPA, and family income, and a positive association with number of siblings. Pearson correlations found strong positive relationships among the scale subdimensions and overall dropout tendency. The study concludes that retention strategies are needed, particularly in non-metropolitan regions, and notes limitations due to self-reported data, recommending longitudinal and mixed-method future research.

The passage describes the fabrication and characterization of ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires using a ZnSe nanowire core, a DC magnetron sputtered oxide precursor layer (WO3 or MoO3), and selenization. It reports that XRD, XPS, and Raman confirm the formation of WSe2 and MoSe2 shells with no detectable precursor oxide peaks. TEM shows the shell morphology depends on selenization temperature: WSe2 forms a continuous ~2 nm shell at 700 °C but becomes discontinuous at 750 °C with protruding 20–50 nm crystals; MoSe2 forms shells under 2 nm at 600 °C with thicker/crystal-like coverage at 650 °C. PL spectra show features corresponding to ZnSe and the diselenides. The discussion attributes the morphology shift to a temperature-dependent transition from solid-state interfacial reaction at lower temperatures to gas-phase reaction and island growth at higher temperatures.

The passage includes diplomatic correspondence and statements involving Japan, Korea, and Chinese officials about withdrawing troops from Korea. John M. B. Sill describes Japan as wanting to end Chinese suzerainty over Korea and assist reforms to bring peace, prosperity, and enlightenment. K. Otori thanks the recipient for advice to withdraw Japanese and Chinese troops simultaneously, but states Japanese withdrawal depends on Japan’s government and he will convey the note to his government. Yuan Shi-Kai acknowledges related communications and reports that Chinese troops were sent to help exterminate rebels, after which they were to be withdrawn, but Japanese troops remained in Seoul and Chemulpo. Yuan Shi-Kai states that simultaneous withdrawal was required by an 1885 agreement between China and Japan, but Japan did not agree. Another delivered statement discusses the Korean emperor directing an official to return with troops to protect the Japanese legation and Japanese subjects and to help suppress troubles, after which rebels were dispersed and soldiers would be withdrawn. The passage ends by emphasizing Korean internal and external stability and long-standing Japan-Korea relations.

Chromatin remodelers regulate processes such as DNA replication, recombination, and gene transcription and repression. A Princeton University-led Nature study (Aug. 2) reports that the ATP-dependent ISWI remodelers use a nucleosome feature called the “acidic patch” to remodel chromatin. The acidic patch is a negatively charged surface formed by amino acids from histones H2A and H2B, and recognition of it in chromatin remodeling had not been implicated before. Using high-throughput screening, the researchers found that acidic patch use is shared by ISWI and other remodeling enzyme families, suggesting a general requirement for chromatin remodeling. They also found that chemical modifications near the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity, affecting other acidic patch-binding proteins differently depending on their response signatures. The study produced extensive data for future work on how chromatin modifications influence ISWI regulation and their cellular roles, and notes that mutations in the acidic patch occur in some human cancers, pointing to potential therapeutic relevance.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon warned that stock markets are likely to face a “drawdown” in the next 12 to 24 months, saying increased capital deployed during the AI boom may not deliver returns and that people “won’t feel good.” He compared the current AI-driven acceleration to the late 1990s and early 2000s internet period, when the dotcom bubble showed winners and losers. Solomon said investors are focused on potential upside while diminishing “things you should be skeptical about,” but he also expressed optimism about AI’s expanding technology and its potential in enterprises. Other speakers at Italian Tech Week also raised concerns about AI speculation and risks.

Scientists from the University of Oxford found a cloud of hydrogen sulphide surrounding Uranus, detected by analyzing infrared light from Uranus captured by the Gemini North telescope. The study reports hydrogen sulphide in Uranus’ cloud tops and says it is the first proof of the gas on the planet, with improved absorption-line data. It notes that Jupiter and Saturn do not have hydrogen sulphide in their clouds and instead have ammonia, and that differences may help explain planet formation. The researchers also speculated that descending through Uranus’ clouds would cause unpleasant conditions, including suffocation and exposure to about negative 200°C air made mostly of hydrogen, helium, and methane.

Cameroon’s government plans to restore 12 million hectares of deforested land by 2030 to address dwindling forests and climate change. The scheme, launched in March, will be supported by local councils, non-governmental organisations, and businesses, and will include efforts to conserve indigenous forests. The government says it will reinforce protection of existing forests and restore lost areas, with local councils receiving FCFA 500 million annually and certain chiefdoms receiving FCFA 70 million annually. While officials and partners back restoration, environmental experts warn that protecting existing forests is even more critical for limiting climate change and biodiversity loss. The passage also cites significant forest loss in Cameroon from 2001 to 2015 and states that the government has increased forest governance and sanctions, though with limited success.

The passage describes research on interactive learning in web-based instruction and the need for an expert-level question answering system for students using online lecture videos. A motivation survey of 52 STEM students found many wanted to ask content questions while watching videos, but few asked in YouTube comments. The work explores whether Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can answer such questions and whether finetuning with synthetic data helps, focusing on the EduVidQA dataset. EduVidQA includes 5,252 QA pairs from educational lecture videos: 270 manually curated real-world pairs from YouTube and 4,982 synthetically generated pairs created from 197 videos, with expert verification for real-world data and quality assurance for synthetic data. The paper reports a qualitative preference study defining metrics (Clarity, Depth, Encouraging Critical Thinking, Conciseness, and Uses Pedagogical Techniques) and uses qualitative and text-based evaluation metrics to benchmark multiple Video LLMs and LVLMs on real-world and synthetic test sets. Results show improvements after supervised finetuning on synthetic data, with qualitative findings emphasizing Clarity and model performance assessed using metrics including FactQA precision/recall and qualitative Likert-scale measures. The passage concludes that smaller open-source models can achieve comparable or better performance than larger closed models, while noting limitations related to dataset coverage, evaluation dependence on LLM reasoning, constrained demographics in human studies, and potential biases.

The passage describes poison as a historically used murder weapon, citing the killing of Kim Jong Nam at a Malaysian airport and South Korean claims that female agents from North Korea administered a lethal toxin sprayed in his face, with an autopsy underway. It lists several deadly chemicals and their effects or detection signs, including ricin, thallium, arsenic, strychnine, cyanide, and potassium. It also recounts related poisoning myths and real incidents across history, including cases involving arsenic, poison-tipped stories, Georgy Markov (ricin via umbrella), Alexander Litvinenko (polonium-210 in tea), and the Tokyo sarin attack, concluding that North Korea may have added to this history.

The passage is a congressional address calling for “direct, vigorous action” to whip inflation. It thanks cooperation from the 93d Congress and a recent Inflation Conference, describes studies of proposed measures, and sets goals for 1976. It identifies ten areas for joint executive and legislative action: food (produce more, remove acreage limits, assure fuel and fertilizer, review regulations, monitor exports, and seek authority to waive shipment restrictions), energy (reduce foreign oil imports, reorganize energy efforts, require cleaner energy and conversions, set targets, and seek deregulation and related legislation), restrictive practices (enforce antitrust laws and increase penalties), inflationary costs (watchdog role, regulatory reform commission, inflation impact statements, and monitoring by state/local governments), capital (fiscal and tax measures to support investment), helping the jobless (expanded unemployment insurance and a Community Improvement Corps), stimulating housing (expand mortgage purchases), thrift institutions (address credit scarcity), international interdependency (pass trade reform and coordinate with other nations), and federal taxes and spending (a temporary income surcharge, spending target, budget deferrals and rescissions, and fiscal discipline). The speaker also urges citizens to save food and fuel, reduce driving, share burdens, and join a volunteer mobilization marked “WIN,” concluding with warnings that inflation could harm the country unless addressed immediately.

CompositesWorld’s 2017 Carbon Fiber conference (Nov. 28–30, Charleston, SC) at the Belmond Charleston Place has a nearly completed agenda. Registration is open, and attendees are encouraged to secure lodging. The event includes a tour of Boeing’s 787 Dreamliner final assembly line in North Charleston and a half-day tutorial by Chris Red on the 2017 Carbon Fibers Global Outlook. Daniel P. Mooney will deliver the aerospace keynote, “Wheels Up: The Dreamliner Journey in SC,” covering Boeing’s composite-material history and the 787’s characteristics, global supply chain, and South Carolina site evolution. A panel on carbon fiber recycling will discuss recycling technologies and recycled carbon fiber reinforcement applications with listed industry panelists. Additional speakers address topics such as digital tools for CFRP processing, automated ply placement verification, resin infusion, electro-optical imaging system design, 3D printing and additive manufacturing for composites, automation technologies for composites manufacturing, carbon fiber in wind energy, rapid-cure prepreg materials, adaptive molds, pitch-based carbon fiber for automotive, and other research and adoption challenges. The co-chairs are Karin Anderston, Arnt Offringa, and Eric Haiss, and sponsors include The Boeing Co. and several named organizations.

The “Blackmore Report - August” from Peter Blackmore to worldwide sales and services personnel says the company has strong momentum and morale across regions despite supply challenges, with continued progress and many successes. It highlights Latin America travel and sales achievements, including multiple e-business-related alliances and strong direct business in Argentina and Brazil, and notes Canadian Q2 profit growth, eStore launch plans, awards, and product wins. The report announces major supercomputing wins, including Compaq being selected by the U.S. NNSA to build a 30+ TeraOPS “Q” system for Los Alamos, plus other large deals worldwide. It also summarizes market share and IDC findings, consumer and CPCG performance and iPAQ demand, Storage and server group news such as enterprise storage center plans and the Zero Latency Enterprise go-to-market program, and various service, professional services, and regional customer wins. The report ends with thanks, plans for further European travel updates, and an option for employees to opt out of future reports via a Reader’s Choice profile page.

Chicago Mercantile Exchange lean hog futures fell about three percent on Friday due to spreading and abundant supplies pressuring cash markets, traders said. October and most-active December contracts declined the most, with October down 1.75 cents to 59.175 cents/lb and December down 1.875 cents to 60.925 cents/lb, after reaching a roughly three-week high on Thursday. Futures traded at a premium to the lean hog cash index, which last read 55.33 cents/lb. The nearly record-large U.S. hog population has pressured prices. Live cattle rose, with October up 0.875 cent to 111.025 cents/lb and December up 0.875 cent to 116.925 cents, supported by technical and investment fund buying, and feeder cattle were up 0.9 cent to 155.75 cents/lb. CFTC data showed speculative investors increased net long positions in live cattle, feeder cattle, and lean hog futures and options in the latest reporting week.

Over the past decade, low-code/no-code (LCNC) platforms have enabled “citizen developers” to build applications using visual methods rather than code. With large language models and agent systems, the focus shifts from syntax abstraction to intent abstraction, where AI agents translate natural-language goals into executable workflows for long-running business processes.

The passage identifies a key bottleneck for LLM agents: the finite context window, which leads to memory inflation (growing dialogue history and token costs) and contextual degradation (loss of older critical information causing stateless or incoherent behavior). It also notes an “experience following property” that can cause error propagation, misaligned experience replay, and self-degradation over time.

To address these issues, the paper proposes a hybrid memory system for long-running LCNC agents. It uses three interacting components: working memory for the current LLM context, episodic memory stored as a vector database of time-indexed interaction entries, and semantic memory storing distilled summaries/abstract knowledge. A core “Intelligent Decay” mechanism assigns each episodic memory a utility score based on recency, relevance, and user-assigned utility, then prunes low-utility entries and can consolidate them into semantic memory via LLM-generated summaries. The system also includes a user-centric visualization interface that lets non-technical users retain, forget, or consolidate memories through a timeline-based Human-in-the-Loop approach.

In simulated experiments on a 500-turn long-running LCNC task (multi-week project plan generation), the proposed hybrid system outperformed sliding window and a basic RAG baseline across task completion, token cost, latency, consistency, and contradiction rate. The paper concludes that this approach improves long-term contextual consistency and provides a foundational framework for reliable, efficient, and transparent AI agents in LCNC environments.

The passage describes SEV-SNP and SEV-ES guest-hypervisor communication mechanisms using NAE (Non-Architectural Exit) events, including the #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, and #HV Timer, as well as events for APIC ID listing, SNP run VMPL, TIO trusted-device requests, Secure AVIC backing page management, and termination requests. It explains that SEV-SNP guests can use SNP AP Creation features to create/update or destroy VMSA state for APs at specified VMPL levels, requiring RMPADJUST and VMSA page assignment, and that a #HV doorbell page enables hypervisor notification of pending events when Restricted Injection is enabled. The passage also outlines how the #HV doorbell page is structured (PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired), required host behavior to present interrupts/events and manage EOI semantics, and guest behavior to atomically acknowledge interrupts, manage end-of-interrupt signaling, validate observed vectors, and handle non-maskable events. Additional sections discuss guest identification of SEV-ES support, challenges of SMP AP booting under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, limitations such as lack of SMM and no nested virtualization under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, and Secure AVIC for guest-owned APIC state.

The author thanks their family, helpers who taught them, and their parents for an SE/30. They note that modern applications and APIs require high availability, reliability, and rapid scalability due to always-on use and potential viral growth, making most applications distributed systems. The author says building distributed systems is challenging and often involves bespoke solutions, but technological advances—especially containers and container orchestrators—have reduced these challenges by enabling reusable components and patterns for building reliable distributed systems.

At the time of seizure, the vessel’s agents and managing owners were Joseph Wing and William R. Wing of New Bedford, Massachusetts, doing business as J. & W. R. Wing. For the Cape Horn Pigeon, her outfits and cargo were owned as follows on September 10, 1892: J. & W. R. Wing (four sixty-fourths); Thomas M. Hart (two sixty-fourths); John Wing (two sixty-fourths); Edward F. Potter (eleven sixty-fourths); Edward F. Potter, executor of William Potter’s estate (eight sixty-fourths); Michael Baker (four sixty-fourths); George W. Collins (one sixty-fourth); and Charles C. Church (two sixty-fourths). An Alexander H. Seabury estate interest of ten sixty-fourths had been conveyed to Louisa B. Haskell prior to that date. A further timeline describes subsequent conveyances affecting the specified ownership shares. All owners are native American citizens claiming U.S. citizenship when the claims originated, with domiciles as stated. The crew on September 10, 1892 numbered 30 besides the captain; their details are listed in Exhibit C, and their lay shares under shipping papers are provided in Exhibits D and E, with crew compensation based on net proceeds. The bark was built in Dartmouth, Massachusetts, in 1854 for whaling, and has always been engaged in whaling. Joseph and William R. Wing purchased her in the fall of 1887 and continued ownership, and in December 1891 she was fitted out at San Francisco for a year-long whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas, with no intent or equipment for a sealing voyage. Certified clearance and manifest copies are attached as Exhibits F and G.

The passage describes Formula 1’s performance and organizational efforts around the 2019 season and into rule changes planned for 2021. It reports that 2019 had 4.2 million total race attendance (including a partial cancellation of the Japanese Grand Prix), 1.9 billion TV cumulative audience, and a social media following of over 25 million, while F1.com recorded 1.1 billion page views. It explains that Formula 1 was close to consensus on an updated Concorde Agreement with the FIA and teams, which includes how prize money is divided and new rules effective in 2021. The text outlines how F1 works (race format, points, car construction, engines, tires, and key technical systems), highlights the roles of teams, the FIA, and Formula 1 as stakeholders, and describes the sport’s operational and revenue business units (promotion, broadcast, advertising/sponsorship, and other sources like Paddock Club and F1TV Pro). It also details how new leadership under Chase Carey, Sean Bratches, and Ross Brawn aimed to modernize the business, improve fan engagement across digital and traditional platforms, and increase competition on track, including a 2021 budget cap and a major car redesign intended to enable closer racing.

The appellate court affirms the judgment of sentence based on President Judge Griffith’s opinion (36 Pa. D. & C. 2d 101). The appellant is directed to appear in the lower court when called and be committed until he complies with the sentence or any unperformed part that had not been superseded at the time of the appeal.

The passage consists of multiple speakers reflecting on a hockey team’s season and Stanley Cup victory. They describe feeling proud and satisfied about winning again, maintaining desire to win after tasting success the previous year, and growing closer as a team through challenges. Players note significant personal moments, including having a player who was injured “last year” come back to the ice for the Cup. They discuss stamina demands from an ongoing schedule with the Olympics and draining playoffs, and express excitement to rest and return for next season. Several comments focus on team dynamics, unselfish play, strong defense, the ability to use four lines effectively, and the team’s youthful core and expected roster continuity. Others comment on the coach’s leadership style and wish for him to return, and one speaker mentions pride in having his name on a trophy.

Despite last month’s approval of the county budget to move Carroll County Public Schools’ Central Office to the former North Carroll High School building, the school board is asking that the move be reconsidered. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie raised the issue again at the June board meeting, saying the board’s concerns focus on the location not being central. The board previously opposed the move, including sending an email before commissioners approved it in April. Commissioners Doug Howard and Richard Weaver presented a March plan to relocate the Central Office along with other county services to the North Carroll building, and in April commissioners set aside $6 million in FY2018 and $6 million in FY2019 for related moves involving the Winchester Building. Guthrie said staff projected additional driving time and mileage—about 50% more miles and 30% more time—along with increased annual operating costs, which would require cuts or more funding. The board agreed to send commissioners another letter detailing its concerns.

The passage describes Turing GPU capabilities and supporting technologies. It states that Turing improves video encoding quality over prior Pascal GPUs and software encoders, lowering CPU utilization and making typical 4K streaming feasible. For VR connectivity, it adds hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, which uses a single USB-C connector to deliver power, display, and data, including DisplayPort lanes and SuperSpeed USB for motion tracking. It also discusses NVLink replacing prior SLI bridge interfaces for GPU-to-GPU transfers on Turing TU102/TU104, enabling higher-bandwidth display topologies. The passage outlines Turing’s hybrid rendering approach that combines real-time ray tracing with rasterization, enabled by RT Cores for BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection plus RTX software technology and denoising. It explains NGX as an NVIDIA RTX deep-learning stack (not working on pre-Turing GPUs), including DLSS and other AI features like inpainting and slow motion. It further covers graphics pipeline features such as Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading (VRS), Texture Space Shading (TSS), Multi-View Rendering (MVR), and Turing’s resource/binding model extensions. Finally, it provides background on ray tracing and BVH acceleration, and summarizes how RTX-OPS relates to workload time distribution across tensor, FP32, RT, and integer operations.

The passage describes WIRED’s picks of discounted tech gadgets from Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days sale event. It notes editors independently select featured products, though WIRED may receive compensation from retailers or purchases via provided links. The text highlights specific deals and features for various products, including smartphones (Pixel 9a, OnePlus 13R), tablets (iPad Air accessories, a OnePlus tablet), Kindles (Kindle Colorsoft models), chargers, cameras (GoPro Hero 13 lens system), power banks/chargers, wallet accessories, smart displays (Echo Show), TVs (TCL QM8K QLED), smart locks, mesh Wi‑Fi systems (Orbi 770), security cameras (including Arlo models), fitness devices (a smartwatch), power stations (Anker Solix C1000), laptops/tablet devices (including Apple and Windows models), monitors, keyboards, mice, a Stream Deck-style controller, and an external drive. It also includes references to other related WIRED deal articles at the end.

The passage is largely comprised of Apple Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended March 28, 2020, including selected financial statements and notes. It includes condensed consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income, balance sheets, shareholders’ equity, and cash flows, with figures for the three and six months ended March 28, 2020 and March 30, 2019. The notes describe significant accounting policies, including recently adopted standards for leases and derivatives and hedging, revenue recognition and disaggregated revenue by products and services, financial instruments and derivative instruments, cash and marketable securities by category and fair value level, credit concentration and non-trade receivables, income taxes and state aid matters, debt including commercial paper and term debt, share repurchase activity, contingencies, and segment information based on geographic segments (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific). It also includes lease disclosures, commitments and contingencies, and a management discussion describing seasonality, COVID‑19 impacts, and second-quarter 2020 highlights.

Medical oxygen has been used clinically since the late 1800s and was added to the WHO essential medicines list in 2002, with hypoxemia as an added indication in 2017. The COVID-19 pandemic increased global demand and exposed supply gaps, including in Peru. Peru’s centralized but fragmented health system, decentralized governance across regions, and political instability contributed to shortages and inconsistent oxygen access, with particularly severe shortages outside Lima. Regulatory factors included oxygen being treated as an essential medicine only later than other systems, sanitary registration requirements, and a >99% purity standard that interviewees linked to reduced market competition and a “policy trap.” During COVID-19, shortages were worsened by underestimation of demand, slow and ineffective government response, limited data on oxygen supply and distribution, and bureaucratic delays, including issues with centralized procurement and oxygen registry launch and data reliability. Civil society and private actors helped by funding and donating oxygen plants, but many installations lacked authorization, maintenance, training, and replacement planning; after the pandemic, many plants became unused or abandoned. The study concludes that Peru needs a National Oxygen System to coordinate supply, quality control, maintenance funding, infrastructure investment, and trained personnel to improve equitable and sustainable access.

Cash-In-Transit (CIT) heists in South Africa reached an all-time high in 2018, with more than 159 reported so far and losses of R1.1 to R1.4 million in damaged or written off vehicles. On Tuesday, three trucks were hit just hours apart in Mthatha (Eastern Cape) and Bloemfontein. In Mthatha, suspects shot and attempted to bomb an armed truck; they did not retrieve the money and the CIT company faced repair and driver aid costs. Earlier on the N8 between Bloemfontein and Botshabelo, two G4S armed trucks were targeted after robbers blocked them off, shot at their tyres, and detonated explosives that failed to explode; drivers survived with minor injuries, and their guns were stripped. The police have not reported progress in investigating either incident.

Palmer amaranth’s spread in the southeastern U.S. has led some farmers to consider switching from cover crops and conservation tillage to conventional tillage, which may control the weed but increases soil erosion and threatens long-term soil productivity. Agricultural Research Service scientists in Alabama suggest a rotation: conventionally till weed-infested cotton fields for one year and return to conservation tillage for the next two years. ARS economist Leah M. Duzy and colleagues compared costs of three years of conservation tillage versus one year of conventional tillage followed by two years of conservation tillage, finding a financial advantage to conventional tillage in year one but little difference in net returns in years two and three. Duzy estimates switching back to conservation tillage would save about $25.57 per acre per year in years two and three, totaling about $15,342 annually for a typical 600-acre farm. If plowing is needed, Duzy recommends using a high-residue cover crop and returning to conservation tillage rather than plowing every year.

Sean Spicer discussed President Donald Trump’s tax returns during a White House press briefing, including questions about whether Trump would release his 2016 returns. He cited that the president is under audit as the reason the returns cannot be made public, while the IRS has said an audit does not prevent individuals from releasing their tax returns. Protest marches calling for the returns’ release were held across the U.S. Spicer said, when asked if Trump would never release them, “We’ll have to get back to you on that.”

The speaker addresses a council focused on enlarging the Nation’s moral and spiritual life, arguing that political success depends on the religious convictions of the people. They describe modern life as increasingly complex and interdependent, with expanded opportunities for crime and wrongdoing. They note crime and violence following war and stress that liberty involves difficult responsibilities. They argue that government primarily maintains order, security, and administers justice, but cannot provide the moral motives for full societal reform because institutions recognize that the human mind must be free. The speaker says law and education can help, but their effectiveness depends on public sentiment and moral growth, which they identify as coming from religion. They contend that government rests on religion, citing the historical religious roots of ideas like freedom, equality, and self-government, and warning that removing this faith would undermine institutions and lead to force-based governance. They emphasize the need for society to be reformed through religion rather than merely punishing symptoms, and call for continued preaching and public renewal of faith to improve the Nation’s moral and spiritual life.

The passage describes a scoping review on how socio-economic status (SES) is measured in sub-Saharan African health research. It notes that SES is important for understanding health disparities and informing public health policy, but that measurement approaches vary by indicators, populations, and data availability, making studies difficult to compare and creating challenges for standardization across Africa. The review searched multiple databases from January 2012 to June 2024 and included 65 articles after screening. The studies covered 22 countries, most often South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana, and were predominantly research articles with cross-sectional designs. Across the included studies, 41 SES measures were identified and grouped into 11 categories. The most commonly used approach was the asset-based Wealth Index (61.9%), often calculated using principal component analysis (PCA), followed by indices incorporating income, education, and living standards. The passage concludes that PCA is the most used calculation method, the asset-based wealth index is most widely used, and that standardization of SES measurement methods in Africa is recommended while allowing local adjustments.

A research team including Binghamton University archaeologist Carl Lipo has confirmed through 3D modeling and field experiments that Rapa Nui moai statues could be transported by “walking” upright using a rocking motion. The study examined nearly 1,000 moai and found features such as wide D-shaped bases and a forward lean, with rope and a zig-zag movement along carefully designed, concave roads that could help stabilize the statues. The team built a 4.35-ton replica moai and, using 18 people, transported it 100 meters in 40 minutes. Lipo said nothing else currently explains how the moai were moved and that the work puts a theory to the test while honoring the ingenuity of the people of Rapa Nui.

Poway Unified School District is recognizing 28 high school teachers retiring after at least 30 years, with teacher profile details provided for Traci Barker-Ball, Don Jones, Melinda Watson, Patsy Malta, Lori “Brick” Brickley, Keith Koelzer, and Robert Saxton. The profiles note their years in PUSD, roles and coaching or sponsorship activities, awards and education credentials, reflections on changes in teaching (including technology and increased expectations), and retirement plans. The article also lists additional retirees at other high school and district levels with years of service and most recent subjects or roles.

Sudan, described as the world’s last male northern white rhinoceros, died in Kenya Monday at age 45 after his health deteriorated following a severe leg infection. Ol Pejeta Conservancy said he could no longer stand, leading his veterinary team to euthanize him. Captured in Sudan in 1975 and moved to Dvůr Králové Zoo in the Czech Republic, Sudan was later relocated in 2009 to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya with two females, Najin and Fatu. Scientists had undertaken efforts to prevent complete extinction, but the two remaining females cannot gestate; one is sterile and the other cannot carry a calf full term. The veterinarian leading Sudan’s care said natural reproduction and artificial insemination are not possible, and only options like retrieving eggs and using southern white rhinos to carry fertilized eggs remain, which has not been done before.

The passage describes background on low use of essential maternal health services and introduces a study in Oromia, Ethiopia that developed and tested maternal vulnerability segmentation tools. It aims to identify pregnant women living with vulnerabilities to enable targeted interventions and examines how intersecting vulnerability scores affect antenatal care and health facility delivery. The study used a community-based quasi-experiment design with baseline interviews and developed a 20-item Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) covering economic, social, and information/access drivers, reduced to sets of items for different settings. Results reported that women in higher vulnerability groups had lower utilization of antenatal care and were less likely to deliver in health facilities, with evidence that the effect of vulnerability on health facility delivery was mediated through antenatal care visits. The authors conclude the MVST is practical for frontline workers but is a population segmentation tool rather than an intervention strategy, and recommend further research and validation across contexts.

Castle Gardens is a purpose-built home in Invergordon near the A9, providing dementia, nursing, residential, and end-of-life care. It has en suite, wheelchair-friendly bedrooms with TV points and a nurse call system, with a GP service and services such as a mobile hairdresser; small pets are allowed and visitors can make drinks in the kitchenette. Organized activities include arts and crafts, baking, quizzes, animal visits, musical events, church services, and trips out in the home’s minibus. The home has a mature garden with views over nearby woodland, plus greenhouse and potting shed access for maintaining vegetable and herb gardens. The passage advises checking the home’s suitability for individual circumstances and notes that service information comes from the care home, with errors addressed via email.

Changing lifestyles and preferences have increased demand for easy-to-eat snacks, with cheese snacks highlighted as a popular option worldwide. The market is expected to grow at a 5.2% CAGR from 2017 to 2025, according to a Persistence Market Research report. Factors cited include savory snack preferences, convenience of frozen/processed cheese, and consumer attachment to cheese and junk food despite growing health awareness. Baked cheese snack products are gaining prominence as consumers seek healthier options, and scientific research is described as improving awareness of cheese’s nutrient profile. Leading companies mentioned include Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE SA, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC Limited, and General Mills.

Soumya Swaminathan, a pediatrician, will head to Geneva in mid-to-late November to become Deputy Director General (programmes) at the World Health Organisation. She is the first Indian to take up this role and currently serves as Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research. In an interview, she says her goals at WHO will align with WHO Director General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, prioritizing universal health coverage, epidemic handling, non-communicable disease burden, and access to diagnostics and drugs, with a hope to contribute to global health. She identifies a key gap for India in delivering preventive and promotive healthcare through health and wellness centres. She also shares that her father, Dr M S Swaminathan, supported her transition, emphasizing how international exposure provides new perspectives and learnings, and she expects a similar learning experience from WHO to continue contributing in India.

The passage describes general statistical and data presentation procedures for a clinical study, including the use of ICH numbering for tables/listings/figures (TLFs), 2-sided testing at a 0.05 significance level, and rules for summarizing continuous and categorical data (including handling missing percentages). It defines analysis sets (Safety analysis set, Full analysis set, Per protocol set) and states how primary and secondary endpoint analyses are assigned to these sets, with primary analyses conducted on the FAS and safety on the safety set. The document specifies planned statistical methods and models for efficacy (Kaplan-Meier, stratified log-rank, hierarchical testing, Cox models, sensitivity/supportive analyses, and secondary analyses using tests such as Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel or ANOVA), baseline definitions, covariate adjustments, and a no-imputation approach for missing data. It outlines data handling and quality control processes, notation and definitions for treatment groups, approaches for PK/PD data transformations and summaries, and safety analysis conventions based on the safety set, including AE and laboratory/ECG/immunogenicity summaries. It also lists various tables/figures/listings and describes protocol-to-SAP analysis changes, along with SAS and QC documentation requirements.

The passage describes an increase in “disconnected” young Americans—18- to 24-year-olds who are not in school, not working, and not looking for work. Goldman Sachs analysis cited shows labor force participation among 22- to 27-year-olds without college degrees has declined, including a rise in those reporting they are “unable to work” for reasons other than school, disability, illness, retirement, or childcare. Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas data shows the disconnected youth share has trended upward, reaching about 12% in May data, higher than any year from 1989 to 2009.

Workforce experts cited by Business Insider say the causes involve economic, cultural, and psychological factors. One theory is that some young non-graduates are choosing not to seek available jobs, related to perceptions and stigma around roles not requiring degrees, and mental health challenges and social isolation. The passage also notes family support may be keeping some young people from seeking work due to longer times to become financially stable, and that gig work could be undercounted in official labor statistics because freelancers may not report themselves as working or looking for work.

Proposed solutions include embedding practical work experience in education programs (like internships or apprenticeships) and reducing stigma around non-degree jobs through campaigns or early education. The experts express hope for younger people but say helping older ones is likely to be more difficult.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2, no-post, motion offense where all five players participate in continuity and should be skilled at passing and handling. Success depends on reading and countering defensive overplays, with cutters anticipating late passes near the basket. Basic continuity cuts include: O1 passes to O2 and cuts to the basket; O2 either passes on basket cut or replaces O1 in the middle, otherwise clears to a corner; O2 may pass to O3 to break into the middle, with O2 then making a basket cut or clearing if no pass is received; O4 replaces O2 on the wing; O3 in triple threat position can pass to O5 or O4, and if passing to O5, O3 cuts to the basket and clears if no pass is received. Back cut counters instruct players to back cut immediately when overplayed or passing lanes are denied, with subsequent clearing to corners. Dribble penetration guidance says the ball handler assumes triple threat, protects the ball, drives to the basket if the passing lane is overplayed, and kick out to the opposite corner if defenders help. A back door option is available when a wing is overplayed or the shot clock is winding down: on the left side, if X5 overplays from O3, O1 can break to the middle and feed O5 on a back cut to the basket; on the right side, if X4 overplays from O3, O2 can break to the middle and feed O4 on a back cut to the basket.

At least five tenured faculty members were terminated or put on leave after social media comments following the killing of Charlie Kirk, suggesting to Das Acevedo that tenure protections have been eroding. In her response to “the war on tenure,” Das Acevedo says politicians are addressing a problem that “didn’t need fixing in the first place,” and she describes how state legislation and university policies have weakened tenure over the past two decades. She argues that the main justifications for tenure—employment security as in-kind compensation and protection that supports academic freedom—remain consistently valuable. She also disputes claims that tenure reduces productivity, citing limited data and studies showing some productivity ramp-up before tenure that levels off afterward. She argues that tenure contracts do not prevent firing for just cause and that institutions’ leadership largely determines whether “bad actors” are disciplined. She further says that recent fast dismissals tied to social media show universities increasingly disregard the notice and faculty-involved processes tenure is supposed to require.

Research from Ben-Gurion University found that using smiley face emojis in formal work emails decreases perceptions of sender competence and does not increase perceptions of warmth. In experiments with 549 participants across 29 countries, emails with smileys led to weaker competence evaluations compared with emails without smileys, and participants shared more content when no smiley was included. A related experiment found that smiling photographs increased perceived competence and friendliness, but smileys in emails reduced perceived competence while leaving friendliness unchanged. The study also reported that when the writer’s gender was unknown, smileys made people more likely to assume the sender was a woman. The researchers concluded that smileys should be avoided in initial workplace interactions, regardless of age or gender.

The passage describes a quality improvement project in a UK anaesthetic deanery to address Stage 1 regional teaching, prompted by the 2021 anaesthetists curriculum change and low regional teaching scores in GMC surveys. Qualitative interviews were conducted with six trainees and eight trainers (college tutors and school board members) to explore perceptions of Stage 1 regional teaching. Findings highlight uncertainty from the new curriculum, high demands on trainees (including passing the primary FRCA exam), and heterogeneity among trainees’ needs. Significant variability between hospital sites was reported as creating unfairness, “silo” working, and logistical challenges for implementing a regional programme (such as location/transport, room availability, rota complexity, travel funding, and maintaining teaching quality). Despite these concerns, interviewees generally supported developing a regional teaching programme, expecting benefits including more exam-focused teaching, standardisation, improved fairness, better resource sharing, and opportunities for social and cross-hospital networking. The authors note that existing tools like the GMC survey were insufficient and that qualitative methods helped clarify issues and enabled actions for their QIP, including designing a regional teaching survey and engaging relevant stakeholders.

A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Houlton, Larry O’Neal, 44, was indicted on Feb. 15 on a felony charge of possession of child pornography. He pleaded not guilty in U.S. District Court in Bangor on Feb. 22. Homeland Security agents investigated him after tracing a suspected downloaded file to his IP address in Houlton; he was arrested Jan. 19, and a search of his home and Subaru found a computer and external drive with child and adult pornography, including images of girls about 12 to 14. O’Neal told an agent he downloaded the pornography from the internet and used search terms such as “young,” “rape,” and “teen hardcore,” and investigators reported no evidence he stored it on his work computer or used government property. He was released on bail and is set to appear in court June 6; if convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison, a fine up to $250,000, and sex-offender registration.

Neonatal jaundice, caused by bilirubin accumulation, affects 50–90% of births and usually resolves without treatment; about 5–10% require phototherapy. Severe cases can lead to neurotoxicity, long-term cognitive impairment, kernicterus, death, and a global health burden. The study performed the first genome-wide association study (GWAS) of neonatal jaundice using nearly 30,000 parent-offspring trios from Norway and included replication in two Danish cohorts. Two genome-wide significant loci were identified: a UGT1A* region variant rs6755571 (missense affecting UGT1A4) associated with a five-fold lower risk of neonatal jaundice and replicated in Danish cohorts, and a second locus near CHRDL1 on the X chromosome (rs12400785). Parental transmitted allele analyses suggested the UGT1A* effect was neonate-only, while the CHRDL1 effect differed by sex. A maternal GWAS identified an ABO-region locus explained by maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility, with additional analysis showing adjustment for ABO incompatibility moved rs687621 effects toward null. The paternal GWAS found a UGT1A* locus. The UGT1A4-associated protection was not modified by maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility and was stronger in full term and post-term periods. Adult bilirubin genetics differed from neonatal jaundice genetics, with neonatal and adult associations at UGT1A* driven by distinct variants and little association in neonatal GWAS at SLCO1B1. Methods included genotyping, quality control, phasing/imputation, GWAS using logistic regression, replication using Danish patient register ICD codes, and additional analyses including conditional testing, colocalization with eQTLs, and polygenic score comparisons.

The passage describes portable shelters and campers, focusing on hard-sided, collapsible designs. It summarizes a need for shelters that are highly portable while providing protection from weather, animals, theft, and limited space, noting that existing fabric shelters offer limited security and rigid shelters are less portable. It describes embodiments of a collapsible camper with rigid, insulated panels and a weather-tight, lockable enclosure that transitions between expanded and collapsed configurations by folding wall panels and sealing joints with gaskets or weather stripping. The camper can be attached to vehicles (e.g., roof racks, pickup beds, trailers, or bicycle/motorcycle/tow systems) and can be designed to remain compact in transit without permanent vehicle modification. The interior may include a movable bed platform for sleeping and standing space, and optional climate control, electronics, wiring, solar panels, batteries, generators, and plumbing. The shelter may include windows, doors, and features such as kitchenette and bathroom fixtures. It also outlines related method steps for transporting the shelter in the collapsed state and unfolding it for use, and provides a brief description of multiple drawings and example dimensions.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2016 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. In Item 2.02, it states that on January 26, 2016 Apple issued a press release, a related data sheet, and supplemental materials regarding Apple’s financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015, attached as Exhibits 99.1, 99.2, and 99.3. The filing also notes that the information is not deemed filed or incorporated by reference except as expressly set forth. Under Item 9.01(d), the exhibits are listed as press release (99.1), data sheet (99.2), and supplemental materials (99.3). The report is signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage explains that pivot points are calculated from the previous trading day’s high, low, and close to form a central pivot point, with additional support and resistance levels derived above and below it using a formula. It describes several types of pivot point calculations and notes that Lewis Borsellino used pivot points daily but did not provide specific details. The article backtests multiple intraday pivot point strategies (from 2010 to the present) using 1-minute futures data for ES, NQ, RTY, and USD/CHF. It concludes that none of the tested pivot point strategies proved consistently tradeable in the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, or the USD/CHF market. The passage lists pros as being easy to use, objective/quantifiable, versatile, and helpful for confirming support and resistance, while cons include being lagging and having a low win ratio according to the backtests.

RWE Supply & Trading may double or triple its LNG derivatives trades in 2017 from 2016, managing price risk for its physical LNG cargoes, a company executive said. It traded 1.5 million tonnes of LNG derivatives last year and 6 million tonnes of physical LNG annually. The executive cited shifts away from oil-linked pricing, fragmented demand and increased short-term trading driven by new and existing buyers in Asia, as well as uncertainty in power markets. RWE is active in Platts’ Japan-Korea Marker (JKM) derivatives, trading 7 to 10 physical cargoes on the JKM index so far this year. LNG swaps volumes settled against Platts’ JKM price assessments quadrupled in 2017 to 50,266 lots, equivalent to about 170 tankers.

A 22-foot Wolverine mural at Lawton High School’s cafeteria was unveiled Thursday by art teacher and artist Kenneth Hobbs, featuring the front and south side of the school and the “Hanta Yo!” sign. The new 10-foot by three-foot mural, funded by the class of 2014, matches a first mural funded by the class of 2006 and unveiled in May 2010. The first mural shows Lawton High’s three buildings, a timeline of athletic state and national championships, and images of the 1927 National Women’s Basketball Team and the 1993 National Wrestling Champions with coaches.

The passage discusses research findings and policy responses related to whether racial-, ethnic-, and language-minority schoolchildren in the United States are overrepresented in special education. It describes federal and local requirements intended to reduce minority disproportionate representation, including allocating funds for early intervening services when overrepresentation is found. It then reports that the study’s analyses using longitudinal, nationally representative data found no evidence of racial-, ethnic-, or language-minority children being disproportionately overidentified as disabled; instead, minority children were found to be less likely than otherwise similar White, English-speaking children to be identified as having disabilities, with underrepresentation evident across elementary and middle school periods. The passage also notes that factors such as academic achievement and behavioral self-regulation were associated with lower identification as disabled, while externalizing behaviors had mixed associations with specific disability categories.

The speaker disagrees with Curtis’s assessment and says the key to shutting down the opposing team is limiting their time with the puck and keeping it out of their end, including preventing forechecking that works the puck down low. The speaker is unsure of Brett’s status but would view him being out as beneficial. They also comment that Mike is a top player who skates well, handles the puck, and creates chances quickly, making him difficult to stop, and that improving the team’s defense would involve giving Joe Nieuwendyk less room and time with the puck.

Mental health care services are available in more than 80% of Minnesota’s public school districts. While school staff and school-based practitioners provide much support, some nonprofits also operate in schools with services such as peer support for students dealing with addiction and culturally specific groups for students from immigrant and refugee communities.  

Know the Truth, created in 2006 as a prevention program, brings young people who completed addiction treatment into schools to share experiences, and later expanded into peer recovery services through partnerships with districts such as Anoka-Hennepin and District 916. St. Paul-based Restoration for All focuses on mental health support for Minnesota’s African immigrant and refugee community and brought mental health programs into public schools, addressing gaps from a lack of cultural understanding and emphasizing questions like “What happened to you?” It provides supports including screening groups, individual therapy, suicidal monitoring, and African mind-body practices.  

Tiffany White, a youth peer support specialist working with Know the Truth, conducts group and individual sessions in multiple Twin Cities public schools and also offers support outside school hours. She uses harm reduction, discusses her own experience with alcohol dependence and recovery, and notes that some school staff may underreport substance use. Her work is funded through contracts and grants, and she described impacts from federal funding cuts, as well as progress with students at an alternative learning center.

South Korean lawmakers said South Korea’s spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Un’s estranged half-brother, Kim Jong Nam, in Malaysia, after Malaysian authorities sought a cause of death. U.S. sources told Reuters they believed Kim was murdered by North Korean assassins, and South Korean intelligence believed he was poisoned. Lawmakers said the spy agency reported Kim Jong Un issued a “standing order” for the assassination and that there was a failed attempt in 2012. They said Kim Jong Nam had been living with his second wife in Macau under Beijing’s protection, and that he also had a wife and son in Beijing. Malaysian police reported Kim died on Monday while being taken from KLIA to hospital; a post-mortem was underway, and CCTV indicated a woman was involved. South Korean officials said the murder was confirmed, and South Korea’s Unification Ministry urged defectors to be mindful of security.

A woman and her partner left El Salvador for the United States after her children were killed by gangs and she feared the killers would wipe out their family. They traveled more than 1,000 miles, crossed into Texas, and were captured by the Border Patrol, separated, and detained; about 100 people including her were flown back to El Salvador Thursday under the U.S. zero-tolerance policy. The article describes thousands of similar deportations and notes that gang members represent a very small share of border detentions, while many migrants say they are fleeing violence and seek safety in the U.S. It details gang control in El Salvador’s neighborhoods, extortion and killings for those who refuse to pay, and threats to people suspected of gang ties, including cases involving police intimidation and “extermination groups.” It also states that deported people often attempt to immigrate again, and the woman flown back said she did not know whether she would try again, needing first to learn when her partner would return from Texas.

A Thames Centre councillor, Kelly Elliot, is urging the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a defibrillator (AED) policy and install AEDs in every school. She says West Nissouri Public School received funds from a student after a child died in a soccer game, including a $2,000 parent donation for maintenance, which Middlesex County EMS would cover. The board has declined to install the device, citing an upcoming Home and School meeting to discuss acquiring a board-approved AED and training. Elliot says the board is the only one in Ontario without an AED policy or AEDs in every school and points to other boards that have AEDs. The board has declined to comment so far.

Tom Belcher and others appealed a September 18, 1989 judgment from the Superior Court for Kitsap County to the Washington Court of Appeals. The appellate court affirmed the judgment by unpublished opinion, with Worswick, C.J. authoring and Alexander and Morgan, JJ. concurring. The decision is now published at 60 Wn. App. 949.

Senior guard Adrienne Motley surpassed former Miami assistant coach Octavia Blue on the all-time scoring list, passing Blue’s 1,724 points to take sole possession of No. 7 as the No. 16 Hurricanes defeated Clemson 81-57. Miami also celebrated its women’s athletic program and hosted Play4Kay honoring Hall of Fame coach Kay Yow, while other milestones included Jessica Thomas’ 1,200th collegiate point. Miami led much of the game, built a 48-30 halftime advantage, and outscored Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. Motley scored 15 points and Laura Cornelius 14; the Hurricanes also won the bench-scoring battle 28-13. Miami next travels to play No. 14 Duke.

The “Inside UT Football: October 12, 2000” newsletter discusses Texas Longhorns football. It includes a Q&A with Chip Brown about Texas rebounding from an Oklahoma loss and the quarterback situation. Texas is described as facing Colorado at Boulder, with notes on Texas–Colorado history and Buffaloes coach Gary Barnett’s comments, including that Texas is the most talented team he expects to face.

The newsletter states that Major Applewhite is named starter for the Colorado game and that Chris Simms will be used only on a “need-to-win” basis for that week. It also lists promotions and changes to the starting lineup, including B.J. Johnson at flanker and Roy Williams at split end, and mentions possible increased playing time for Brock Edwards and more carries for Kenny Hayter.

Across multiple fan questions, Brown addresses topics such as offensive leadership and leadership shortages on offense, play-calling and creativity, using or not using a quick-strike no-huddle offense, offensive performance against better defenses, and concerns about inconsistent results. The Q&A also covers recruiting questions, Courtnee Garcia and Miguel McKay’s roles, and scheduling details noting that a Missouri game start time on Oct. 21 has not been set yet by ABC.

On Wednesday, stocks rose as investors reversed course hoping Italy could avoid another round of elections. The S&P 500 increased 34.15 points (1.3%) to 2,724.01, the Dow rose 306.33 points (1.3%) to 24,667.78, and the Nasdaq added 65.86 points (0.9%) to 7,462.45. Travis Phippen, whose father John Phippen died from injuries suffered in Sunday’s Las Vegas mass shooting and who was himself shot and wounded, has filed a civil lawsuit against the estate of gunman Stephen Paddock in Clark County, Nevada. The suit seeks to take possession and control of the decedent’s assets, including funds and safe deposit boxes, and to collect and preserve the estate’s assets and manage real property. The passage also states that 59 people were killed and 527 wounded, and that Phippen is recovering after being shot in the arm; other SCV residents wounded were also reported to be recovering in a Las Vegas hospital.

Scale AI billionaire Alexandr Wang says 13-year-olds should focus on “vibe-coding,” using AI coding assistants to experiment and build a deep practice over thousands of hours. He compares this to earlier advantages from personal computers and to founders like Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg, arguing that early hands-on time with AI tools can become a career-defining advantage. The passage also says job security worries are increasing as automation reduces some roles, and notes that Wang became Meta’s first-ever chief AI officer in June 2023, leading Meta’s AI superintelligence team.

A petition to save the Gresford Health Centre has attracted over 600 signatures amid fears that Alyn Family Doctors plan to close the Gresford branch and amalgamate patients onto two other surgeries in Llay and Rossett. The practice says it lacks manpower to run three sites and has written to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board to consider the closure proposal. Patients and residents worry about travel difficulties and increased appointment pressure, especially with proposed housing developments that could overload local services. A BCUHB spokesman said the board is supporting the practice and that patients will be able to give feedback via forms in surgeries, post, or email.

When a penalty kick is awarded in normal play, it is a restart: at the moment the ball is kicked it is live and in play, and defending action immediately resumes if the goalkeeper blocks/saves it or if it rebounds off the goal into the field. Defenders (all players other than the kicker and goalkeeper) must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field of play, and outside the penalty area. They should get into position immediately to box out attackers and react to rebounds, holding their ground if jostled, and positioning beside rather than behind an attacker who gets there first. Players should not move into the penalty area or arc based on the referee’s whistle or motions; they must wait until after the kicker has touched the ball and it clearly moves forward. Defenders must be prepared for saved, blocked, or rebounded kicks, and remember the kicker cannot touch the ball again until it has been touched by another player. If the ball is blocked but not captured, or if it rebounds off the goal, defenders must get to the ball first; if the goalkeeper captures the ball or clears it, defenders must transition directly to attacking mode to potentially create a fast break. The passage also describes the rare “tap” (two-man) penalty kick and notes that penalty kick procedures are different from penalty shoot-outs, where follow-up is not allowed and the kicks are not live after being taken.

The passage describes a gaming machine, control method, and program that synchronize the display timing of game events with the beat of background music (BGM). It addresses a problem in a prior approach where audio used for events is beat-synchronized, but event display timing is not, leading to possible lag and discomfort.  

In the disclosed technique, a controller starts game progression on a display while outputting BGM via a speaker using stored BGM sound data and tempo data containing beat information. The controller determines when events should be displayed based on the BGM tempo data, dynamically configures animation data accordingly, and displays the animation at the determined timing. The passage also outlines embodiments where event timing can be based on player operations, where event content can be random, where event sounds can be output at the determined timing, where multiple events can follow a rhythm pattern, and where reel spins/stops in a slot-like game and illumination can be synchronized with BGM beats using frame counts tied to tempo data.

The passage expresses gratitude for citizens’ confidence in calling the speaker to the chief executive office and describes the speaker’s anxiety about fulfilling the duties of the trust. It says previous chief executives explained governing principles and that past causes explain the United States’ current condition. The passage characterizes the government under the Constitution as self-government that has produced strong institutions, regulated commerce, admission of new states, protection of rights, and flourishing prosperity, including during foreign wars. It argues for preserving the Union and the government, citing favorable geography, abundant resources, and benefits to agriculture, navigation, manufactures, and markets. It warns that dangers may come from abroad and that people’s education and virtue are necessary to prevent corruption and usurpation, recommending fortifying frontiers, maintaining the Army and Navy, and organizing and training the militia. It also calls for internal improvements like roads and canals, supports domestic manufacturing and friendly relations with Indian tribes, emphasizes the competency of national resources and revenue, and outlines oversight responsibilities between the Executive and Legislature regarding public funds. The speaker concludes by emphasizing peace, harmony, and continued support from other government departments and divine protection.

Metagenomics, first published in 1998, involves directly sequencing genes from a sample. Shotgun metagenomics uses a hypothesis-free, unbiased approach to study nucleotide sequences from entire environments, including parasites, fungi, bacteria, and viruses. Sequencing advances have made metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) attractive for infectious disease diagnostics, but current clinical diagnostics for bacterial pathogens are culture-dependent and limited by the need for prior pathogen knowledge and, in some cases, slow cultivation times. The passage describes that mNGS could address these limitations by enabling rapid, culture-independent detection of pathogens and antimicrobial resistance, functional gene profiles, and virulence genes from a single extracted sample, though adoption has been limited and barriers are under-researched.

The study aimed to explore stakeholders’ opinions on the utility of mNGS for future routine genomic diagnostic development. It used an interpretive phenomenological approach with semi-structured interviews conducted via Microsoft Teams with 10 purposively recruited participants. Data were analyzed using interpretive phenomenological analysis, with anonymisation and thematic analysis. Interview themes included diagnostic choice and the need for mNGS as part of a broader diagnostic toolkit; barriers and facilitators related to cost, speed, infrastructure (physical/digital systems, workforce training, accreditation/standardisation, digitisation), open data sharing and patient privacy; and communication across hospital settings, between hospitals, and with academia and commercial partners. COVID-19 was highlighted as a proof-of-concept showing metagenomics utility for public health, and the passage concludes that cost, speed, and infrastructure are key considerations for implementing metagenomics in clinical settings, supported by guidance from stakeholder experiences.
