Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for their work on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), described as large internal molecular structures with gaps that can trap gas, water, and other chemicals. The Nobel Committee compares them to Hermione’s charmed handbag: small outside but very large inside. The passage says MOFs can store gases in vast quantities, capture greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, and extract “forever chemicals” known as PFAS, among other applications. It also describes Robson’s late-1980s discovery of a crystalline structure with useful holes, Kitagawa’s later creation of MOFs capable of taking up gases such as methane, nitrogen, and oxygen, and Yaghi’s 1999 creation of a highly porous material with an enormous surface area.

NHS staff recreated a historic 1927 photograph found inside a broom cupboard to mark the 70th anniversary of the health service. The original image, taken at Sandwell Hospital’s headquarters in West Bromwich (then called Hallam Hospital), showed a matron, her assistant, and nurses in old-fashioned caps. Fourteen members of staff from the Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust recreated the photograph nearly 90 years later. The recovered images will be displayed at Sandwell Hospital from 10am to 2pm tomorrow during a tea party to mark NHS70.

The passage describes a finance lecture segment led by Andrew Lo. He first uses an “iPod vs. book” auction example to illustrate how limited information affects valuation. He then discusses recent events involving the federal government taking over Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, explaining their role in buying mortgages, the resulting market pressures, and the government’s backing of their obligations; he also notes concerns such as potential inflation and taxpayer costs. He discusses shareholders, counter-parties holding related securities, and how the course will analyze these instruments over subsequent lectures.

The lecture then shifts to core valuation concepts. Lo defines cashflows and argues that an asset at time \(t\) is equivalent to a sequence of current and future cashflows, emphasizing that assets depend on the point in time considered. He introduces the idea of a value operator \(V_t\) that maps a sequence of cashflows to a number (its value), and in the “no uncertainty” case he develops present value valuation using exchange rates (discount factors). He explains that exchange rates can be obtained from markets, relates discount factors to an interest rate \(r\), and shows how to compute net present value (NPV) by converting cashflows at different dates into “today’s dollars” using discount factors. He concludes by stating that the next lecture will apply these ideas to annuities and perpetuities, including mortgage-payment calculations.

VentureWire’s Tuesday, November 7, 2000 issue reports private company business news, including top stories such as Broadcom acquiring SiByte for up to $2 billion, Alta Partners raising $275–$325 million for Fund III, Furniture.com shutting down and laying off most staff, and eStellarNet raising $30 million for its first institutional round. The issue also lists “New Money,” “Bad News,” “New Products,” and “M&A” items, along with “New Directors,” “New People,” “VC Fund News,” and “VC Personnel,” and includes notes and corrections.

A port in northern Honduras is described with stacked containers, bananas, trucks, forklifts, and freighters shipping cargo to the United States and Mexico. Sergio Romero, wearing an orange mesh vest and blue hard hat, travels through the port to a blue bay where the schooner Avontuur is docked. Unlike most cargo ships, the Avontuur has two masts and canvas sails and traveled using wind power instead of burning bunker fuel. The 97-year-old schooner was guided by a small crew of sailors from Europe across the Caribbean, carrying and delivering small cargo.

The passage explains the role of Title IX staff in higher education compliance with federal regulations and in supporting safe, inclusive campus environments addressing gender equity and sexual misconduct. It describes how Title IX nondiscrimination law has evolved through Department of Education amendments and guidance, including major regulatory expansions since 2020 that created complex procedures requiring dedicated Title IX experts. Using CUPA-HR survey data, the report outlines where Title IX staff are located (most commonly in Human Resources and Student Affairs/Dean of Students), the types of Title IX positions (heads of institutional compliance, deputy heads, and investigators), and trends from 2019-20 to 2023-24 showing increased presence and growth of Title IX staffing. While the total number of Title IX staff rose 38% over five years, 56% of institutions still lacked a dedicated full-time Title IX position. The passage also reports that Title IX positions are held primarily by women (77%), with higher representation of Black women, and that pay equity exists relative to White men across these roles. The report concludes with recommendations to reassess Title IX officer responsibilities, increase staffing where needed, and prepare for potentially changing regulatory requirements, plus a list of related resources.

The speaker says the team needs to talk about its performance from the last game, because they did not play as a unit and they were not happy with how they played. They emphasize that talk is not enough and the team must look at itself and do what it says it will do. The speaker notes that injuries may have helped others step up during the season and says they would like to have certain players back, but if not, other players can take on more responsibility since they have done so before.

Berkshire Hathaway sold 10.6 million shares of General Electric in the second quarter, after having received most of the stake in 2013 when Warren Buffett lent about $3 billion to GE in October 2008. The investment, including dividends, generated a profit of more than $1 billion, and Berkshire cashed out during the same quarter GE changed leadership, with Jeff Immelt stepping aside and John Flannery taking over as CEO. GE shares fell nearly 20% this year. The article also notes Berkshire previously exited most of its Wal-Mart stake and that Buffett continues to own stakes in Bank of America and Goldman Sachs. Other filings cited include Appaloosa selling its stake in an SPDR S&P 500 ETF, George Soros buying a stake in the PowerShares QQQ Trust, and Viking Global Investors purchasing Wells Fargo shares; it describes Wells Fargo’s ongoing issues and related inquiries.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, of Cottage Hills, was arrested Thursday after approaching children offering them fishing equipment. He was charged with loitering within 500 feet of a park, which Jersey County State’s Attorney Ben Goetten said is a Class 4 felony. Darnell was listed as a sexual predator due to a 2003 or 2004 conviction for sexually assaulting a one-year-old child in Madison County. Goetten said a concerned adult reported Darnell after he was suspected from a social media post, and that Grafton PD responded and arrested him. Goetten said his office plans to seek maximum penalties if convicted.

The passage explains the role of arts, especially visual arts, in early childhood education, stating that creative processes help children express feelings, acquire skills, develop imagination and creativity, and enhance self-esteem, communication, and intellectual and social development. It also describes kindergarten teachers’ views that visual arts should be taught with flexibility according to children’s age and interests, using activities such as painting and construction, and providing appropriate classroom space and materials. The literature review notes that inclusion of visual arts in kindergarten can support emotional development, socialization, and acceptance of differences, but that teachers may face challenges such as limited training, limited time and space, and insufficient resources. 

The study aims to explore kindergarten teachers’ views and experiences regarding the importance and teaching of visual arts, and to examine challenges and opportunities for integrating visual arts into the pre-school curriculum. Using an improvised questionnaire with 65 teachers from kindergartens in the Municipality of Piraeus, results show that most participants view visual arts as crucial, report that toddlers respond well, and strongly agree that visual arts support emotional expression, social interaction, cooperation, creativity, and intellectual development. Teachers also report relatively satisfactory integration of visual arts in the current curriculum, prefer approaches involving experimentation and guided/supportive methods, and emphasize positive feedback and continuous adaptation. The main challenges reported are child management and resource limitations, and the discussion highlights needs for targeted professional development and improved access to materials and dedicated art spaces.

His Majesty states that similar agreements with European officers have not received the sanction of their respective governments, causing embarrassment in managing foreign relations and prompting a desire for his Kingdom to be formally recognized as a sovereign and independent state. He says such recognition has been virtually made through the appointment of consuls and commercial agents and the way commanders of national vessels have conducted business with him. He requests the United States consider changes in his dominions over recent years, including the development of a written language, establishment of schools, a library, organization of a limited representative monarchical government, enactment of civil and criminal codes, annual legislative meetings, and establishment of courts with jury trials. He also claims foreigners have brought suit in these courts and that consuls, commercial agents, and visiting commanders have demanded and received protections for persons and property. He argues that formal recognition would promote his Kingdom’s interests and that maintaining independence benefits major commercial nations by making the islands a major center for whale fishing and a key stop for repairs and supplies between the Americas and Asia.

A Spring ISD middle school teacher is reportedly under investigation for allegedly using a racial slur to describe African American students. District officials said the unnamed teacher is on administrative leave after the incident in a classroom at Dueitt Middle School on Wednesday. A parent, Roshonda Davis, said her daughter reported that the teacher called the students “cotton pickers” and that she reported the incident to the superintendent, who took immediate action. Officials questioned other students, confirmed they heard the slur, removed the teacher from the classroom, and replaced him with a substitute. The investigation is ongoing, and the district said it takes such reports seriously.

The German Ambassador, after returning from Berlin, says Germany is willing to confidentially state its peace terms: relinquish Belgium while keeping certain travel rights on the Meuse; keep Holland, Denmark, and Belgium neutral or as buffer states for England; retain the French coast lands entirely for France so it remains independent; restore Russian territory; treat Serbia and Roumania properly; and indemnify Belgium despite incorrect neutral conduct. He adds that German sources say England hesitated because England’s maximum terms with its allies (e.g., ceding Constantinople, parts of Syria, heavy indemnities to Belgium, and ceding Alsace-Lorraine) were not feasible, while minimum terms would cause allied disagreement; he also says Germany learned that if America pressured England, England would confidentially state its peace terms out of respect for and fear of the President and due to a growing peace party. The passage also includes a note from the Greek Chargé to the Secretary of State, reporting Greece’s positive response to a U.S.-forwarded peace proposal dated January 8 and emphasizing Greece’s suffering while neutral, including blockade and starvation. Greece states it could not communicate with one belligerent and had to wait due to difficulties affecting Greece, but expresses support for the President’s peace effort and readiness to exchange views and join actions aimed at consolidating stable peace that secures rights, sovereignty, and independence.

The passage describes “Side Screen Screen/Roll Disruptions SOS” and how on-ball switching and “All Out” SOS aim to disrupt side screen offenses. It outlines scenarios above vs. below the free throw line, including hard contact switches and aggressive trapping near base/corner checkpoints. For the “Below Free Throw Line” sequence, it specifies phases such as a hard double team/trap, pass-out-of-trap rotations, skip-pass handling, and final matchups, noting that rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands. For “Above Free Throw Line,” it specifies a contact switch to deny quick jump shots and middle penetration, followed by pass-denial snuggle positioning and smothering to disrupt passing vision, with other defenders assuming weakside “I” positions and using basic SOS rules. It also details “All Out SOS Disruption” where the defense starts before the first screen option, forcing offensive players into a “free lance” situation, including a double-team trap phase and pass-out-of-trap rotations. Finally, it describes a “Secondary Trap (Pass to O5 on Base Roll)” with post trap and pass-out-of-trap phases, including coverage/fronting in the low post and conditional “Base Go I/Red” scenarios.

Produce Investments Ltd had its target price raised by Whitman Howard from GBX 210 ($2.79) to GBX 240 ($3.18) with a buy rating. Other analysts also restated buy ratings, including Shore Capital and Numis Securities, which set a GBX 286 ($3.79) price objective. The stock rose 0.54% to GBX 187.00 on Thursday with 10,000 shares traded. The company’s 12-month low is GBX 143.00 and high is GBX 220.00, with a market capitalization of GBX 50.52 million. A dividend of GBX 5.03 ($0.07) is scheduled to be paid on Tuesday, December 5th, with shareholders of record on Thursday, November 2nd.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated November 18, 2022. The filing reports that on November 18, 2022 the company entered into a 364-day unsecured revolving credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and other lenders. The credit facility provides up to $10.0 billion in borrowing capacity, has an initial term of 364 days with an option to extend by an additional 364 days, and the interest rate is the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts. Borrowings are intended for general corporate purposes, including backstopping commercial paper notes. The agreement includes customary representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default (with no financial covenants). An event of default not cured or waived could result in unpaid amounts becoming immediately due and payable and commitments being terminated. Exhibit 10.1 is the 364-Day Revolving Credit Agreement.

Marines with Task-Force-Southwest practiced using the Instant-Eye small-unmanned-aerial-system at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, where the drones can record surveillance and perform reconnaissance in small, confined areas. Task-Force-Southwest is scheduled to deploy to Afghanistan in spring to train, advise, and assist the Afghan National Army 215th Corps and the 505th Zone National Police. Separately, Marines with the 2nd Law Enforcement Battalion completed grenade-assault training at Camp Lejeune on February 9, preparing them to use the M67-fragmentation-hand-grenade for an upcoming Integrated-Training-Exercise at Marine Air-Ground Combat Center in Twenty-Nine Palms, California. The Marine Corps also presented the Purple Heart medal to 91-year-old Lee Anderson on February 9, recognizing his World War II injury during the Battle of Iwa Jima.

Three female University of Dayton students reported incidents early Wednesday morning in which a naked man entered their bedrooms, leaving after they confronted him. The first student on Woodland Ave. said the man entered through a window and left when she confronted him around 3:15 a.m. The second student on Frericks Way reported the man entered around 4 a.m., tried to restrain her, and was gone when police arrived. The third student on College Park said he entered through an unsecured door and left after she yelled. In all cases, the suspect was described as a white male in his mid-20s, about 5’10” with a medium build and brown curly hair. University police are collecting evidence and continuing to investigate, and a request for comment was deferred to a university advisory.

The lecture recaps announcements delaying the next problem set and reviews covariant conservation of particle number using a number four-vector whose spacetime divergence equals zero. It then introduces the stress-energy tensor by analyzing a dust cloud: energy density and momentum density arise from combining number density with particle energy, leading to a tensor defined as the tensor product of the number vector and four-momentum. The components of the stress-energy tensor are interpreted as fluxes of energy and momentum, and for dust it is symmetric with equal energy flux and momentum density in appropriate units. The lecture motivates why the stress-energy tensor must be spatially symmetric and presents the covariant conservation law that its spacetime divergence vanishes, yielding conservation of energy and momentum in any chosen frame and integral forms over volumes. Examples follow: a point particle stress-energy tensor using a Dirac delta function, and the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor expressed with the Faraday tensor, including how electric fields create pressures (e.g., between capacitor plates). The lecture concludes by shifting toward the mathematical tools needed for relativistic gravity, starting with flat spacetime in curvilinear coordinates (polar coordinates), emphasizing non-constant basis vectors, resulting changes to the metric, and introducing transformation notation between coordinate systems.

The passage presents a formal address expressing confidence that the new session will produce measures supporting stability and national prosperity. It credits growth in agriculture, manufactures, commerce, and navigation to the U.S. Constitution and laws, highlights public confidence shown by rapid Bank of the United States subscriptions, and reports attention to executing last session’s laws, including Western frontier defense through treaties, actions against hostile groups, and continued peace overtures. It outlines plans for Indian affairs based on justice, regulated land alienation, equitable commerce, and humane civilizational efforts, and notes implementation of distilled spirits duties, with general community acceptance and willingness for adjustments if needed. It describes fixing the permanent government seat district (including Alexandria and Georgetown), laying out a city plan for Congress, notifying the census (population near four million), completing loans in Holland, and provisionally concluding treaties with the Cherokees and Six Nations. It discusses upcoming legislative priorities and administrative matters, including militia organization, post office and roads, establishing a mint to address currency problems, standardizing weights and measures, and selling vacant U.S. lands pledged for public debt reimbursement.

The passage discusses Corey Perry, describing his experience at the major junior level and his performance in high-pressure situations, including the Memorial Cup finals and two playoff rounds in Canadian cities. It characterizes his style as effective “down low” with good hands and slipperiness, and notes that a physical practice described as regrouping, shooting drills, and two-on-ones is typical and was used to support lineup development without separating certain “black aces” players. Perry’s hand injury is mentioned as possibly affecting his availability, but a doctor’s clearance is required and he is currently not near game shape. The speaker emphasizes the importance of a strong start, maintaining an even mindset through both success and adversity, limiting distractions, following a game plan, and focusing on the next game. It also highlights team leadership, commitment to playing a team system, willingness to make sacrifices, and preparation that continues after each game, concluding with the need to play the best possible game the next night.

Hampton and Newport News Police worked to apprehend a 15-year-old suspect allegedly involved in the January 31 robbery of a Tinee Giant convenience store. Hampton Police responded around 9 p.m. after a clerk reported a robbery by a young black man wearing a black hoodie, blackish gray pants, and a black mask, who brandished a gun before leaving in a Ford SUV. A witness followed the SUV, saw the suspect toss something from the car and fire gun shots, and later provided information to Hampton Police. Hampton Police then worked with Newport News Police to locate the Ford SUV on Newsome Drive, where officers found the 15-year-old suspect with a handgun and noted he had outstanding juvenile petitions. The teen was charged with possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, underage possession of a firearm, having a concealed weapon, and underage possession of tobacco, and no charges had been filed directly accusing him of robbing the store.

The passage says critics argue colleges lack viewpoint diversity and notes faculty have skewed left for decades, but warns that viewpoint diversity is defined differently and can be used to project observers’ values. It contrasts definitions from Heterodox Academy, Florida, and conservative critics with the Trump administration’s less clear approach. It describes a federal grant agreement offering funding to nine universities if they ban race and sex-based hiring and admissions, freeze tuition for five years, cap undergraduate international enrollment at 15%, require standardized tests, and maintain a “vibrant marketplace of ideas.” The passage also says the administration’s approach could push colleges to align with the president’s political agenda, while students increasingly consider political viewpoint diversity when choosing colleges and may pay more for schools with fewer opposing political beliefs.

A Sarasota couple, Michael Bennett and Trisha Steffes, were arrested after a package believed to contain fentanyl was intercepted and tested and found to contain carfentanil, a synthetic opioid. Detectives watched as the package was delivered to their home on Proctor Road, and a search warrant was executed minutes later, with Bennett and Steffes admitting the package contained carfentanil. During the subsequent search, more than 7 grams of fentanyl were found in a false electrical outlet, along with other drugs and paraphernalia. Both were charged with delivery of carfentanil, possession of fentanyl with intent, and possession of paraphernalia; Bennett was released on a $15,500 bond and Steffes on a $17,000 bond. The passage also notes rising opioid addiction and that President Donald Trump declared a state of emergency.

Alexander Zverev advanced at the French Open after beating Dusan Lajovic 2-6 7-5 4-6 6-1 6-2 in three hours, 24 minutes, moving into the third round and narrowing the gap to a grand slam quarterfinal. The passage notes Zverev’s past success on the tour and that he had not previously reached a grand slam quarterfinal or beaten a top-50 opponent at a major. It also reports other men’s match results, including Grigor Dimitrov overcoming Jared Donaldson and Kei Nishikori beating Benoit Paire, plus Dominic Thiem leading Stefanos Tsitsipas before darkness halted play. In the women’s draw, Simona Halep recovered from a slow start to beat Alison Riske 2-6 6-1 6-1, with the article also mentioning Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina winning in straight sets.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on November 15, 2019, reporting a temporary suspension of trading under its Amazon.com, Inc. 401(k) Plan. The Company said Fidelity Investments was selected as the new recordkeeper, and to account for assets and transfer records, plan participants would not be able to make exchanges or asset allocation changes, take loans, or request withdrawals or distributions during the “Blackout Period.” The blackout period was expected to begin January 2, 2020 and end the week of January 12, 2020, and participants could contact Fidelity at 1-800-835-5095 to confirm whether it had started or ended. The Company also provided written notice on November 19, 2019 to its Section 16 officers and directors that, during the Blackout Period, they would be subject to trading restrictions relating to Company equity securities acquired through their employment or service as Section 16 officers or directors.

The editors of the Foreign Relations series have access to Department of State retired records, including central files, decentralized “lot files,” Executive Secretariat files, and files from overseas diplomatic posts. Department central files for 1981–1989, stored electronically and on microfilm, will be transferred to the National Archives after declassification and processing and then made accessible; decentralized office files deemed worthy of permanent preservation will also be transferred and made available after declassification and processing. Research for the volumes uses special access to restricted documents at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies, and although material printed in the volume is declassified, some content is extracted from still-classified documents that may not be fully available at publication. The passage also describes how documents are researched in Reagan Library collections scanned under the Remote Archive Capture project and notes ambiguity about attachments caused by scanning methods. Editorial methodology presents documents chronologically by Washington, DC time, reproduces originals as exactly as possible with described marginalia, and follows specified style and transcription conventions, including rules for headings, retention of original spelling and punctuation, bracketed corrections and omissions (in specified typographic styles), treatment of underlined text, telegram numbering, and accounting for fully withheld documents. Footnotes identify document sources, original classification and drafting details, background of important documents and policies, and whether relevant presidential advisers read the document.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for a display device. It provides background that cracks in a display panel can worsen over time and lead to defects such as disconnected signal lines, increased resistance, moisture penetration, and reduced reliability.  

The summary describes embodiments that protect crack/defect sensing circuits and elements in the display panel from static electricity and improve defect-detection accuracy during testing. A display device includes a substrate with a display area (pixels), a pad area (input pads), and a circuit area with a crack sensing circuit. It uses a crack sensing line connected to input pads and to data lines through switching elements, and includes static electricity discharge elements (including capacitors) connected to the crack sensing circuit to store or discharge static electricity. The circuit area may place discharge elements at a center area, with switching elements positioned away from the center. The passage further details static discharge element structures (capacitors with terminals and sub-wires/sub-capacitors), possible inclusion of a connection wire parallel to test data lines, and how the device layout may handle a bending area.  

It also explains how testing applies a test voltage via the crack sensing line(s) and switching elements, and how cracks increase wire resistance so voltages to pixels change, creating detectable lines. Static electricity discharge elements are intended to prevent erroneous defect detection by preventing leakage currents and antenna-like behavior of crack sensing lines. The passage includes extensive structural and test-related details and references multiple figures and cross-sections.

The passage describes a system and method for indicating wireless channel status in digital communications, particularly for 5G New Radio where beamforming and beam failure recovery are used. It focuses on a user equipment (UE) that, after beam failure recovery, assumes or receives a quasi-co-located (QCL) relationship between a newly selected beam and a reference signal on a channel (e.g., PDCCH or PDSCH) to decode frames using the spatial domain receive filter associated with the beam. The UE continues using the assumed QCL relationship until an updated QCL configuration or updated quasi-co-located relationship (e.g., via updated TCI states or signaling) is received, after which decoding uses the updated configuration. The disclosure also discusses reducing signaling overhead for updating channel status information and provides example procedures for handling QCL configurations before and after beam failure, including cases where a TCI field is present or absent in DCI scheduling.

The passage discusses how children may give brief or vague responses and hesitate to ask questions, which can affect their curiosity and learning. It recommends five strategies for parents and caregivers to encourage real conversation with children: ask more specific, open-ended questions; engage with children’s questions instead of dismissing “why” answers; model how to handle not knowing by showing how to find answers and how to research multiple perspectives; clarify and reflect what a child says to help articulate confusion; and avoid multitasking by putting away phones, making eye contact, and following up with questions. It concludes that supporting children’s natural curiosity and confidence can help them ask and answer questions about the world.

The passage discusses that physical activity is a normal physiological stressor and that regular exercise can delay chronic diseases and increase life expectancy. It notes that physical activity patterns may not meet the 2025 global target, and introduces self-esteem as a psychological construct associated with life satisfaction and developmental stability, while noting mixed evidence on associations between physical activity and self-esteem across sociocultural contexts.  

A cross-sectional study assessed 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul (target N=278; analyzed n=225) to examine self-esteem (Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale) and physical activity (IPAQ-SF, including MET scores), along with sociodemographic variables and BMI. Results reported higher ROSE scores in males than females, higher ROSE scores among students who reported regular exercise, and a positive correlation between ROSE and both height and MET scores. ROSE did not differ across BMI categories. Physical activity levels were categorized as inactive, minimally active, or HEPA active.  

The conclusion states that higher physical activity correlated with higher self-esteem, that regular exercise and school success were associated with higher self-esteem, and that height also correlated with self-esteem. The authors note limitations related to the study’s specific population and self-reported height/weight and school success, and call for further investigation into causal relationships.

Canadian researchers studied blood samples from nearly 3,000 people in Toronto to estimate celiac disease frequency and assess whether undiagnosed celiac disease leads to poorer nutrition. Celiac disease involves an immune reaction in the small intestine when gluten is eaten, which can cause symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, anemia, and weight loss. The researchers reported that celiac disease occurs in about 1% of the population and that around 90% of people with the disease are undiagnosed. They noted that about 30% of people have a gene version associated with developing celiac disease, though it does not guarantee onset. The study was published in BMJ Open, and gastroenterologists said diagnosis can be difficult because symptoms overlap with other conditions and because blood tests and biopsies should be done while the patient is consuming gluten. The researchers said further studies in other provinces are needed to determine whether the findings apply nationwide, and El-Sohemy raised concern that some people may unnecessarily follow gluten-free diets.

The ADS868xW includes an input alarm and an AVDD alarm. The input alarm’s low and high thresholds and its hysteresis are user programmable; an input outside the specified range activates the alarm. The passage describes using an NTC thermistor in a voltage divider, where Vout increases as temperature rises and decreases as temperature falls, to monitor for temperatures that are too high or too low. It explains that when temperature fluctuates near the thresholds, noise or interference can cause false alarms or missed alarms, and that adjusting hysteresis improves noise immunity. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, and recommends decoupling AVDD and DVDD with specific capacitor values and placement, which improves PSRR. It also describes power-saving modes, including NAP mode (entered by holding CONVST/CS high after conversion) and power-down (PD) mode (entered by setting PWRDN after unlocking the RST_PWRCTL_REG), detailing what powers down and what remains active. Finally, it provides PCB layout and decoupling guidance for analog and digital sections and the REFCAP/REFIO pins, plus general documentation update and support information.

The Federal Reserve raised the fed-funds futures rate by 0.25 points to 1%–1.25% and said it would reduce its $4.5 trillion balance sheet “this year,” though details on timing and pace were not provided. U.S. stocks showed mixed movement: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped about 0.9%, while the Dow briefly hit an intraday record but later traded slightly lower. Oil futures fell 3.7% to $44.73 a barrel, bond yields moved slightly, the dollar fell 0.2%, and gold rose 0.6%. The passage also mentions company-specific stock moves including Tesla, oil-related stocks, UPS, H&R Block, and Alexion, and reports about separate shootings.

The passage describes a device and related processes for tuning open-loop insulin delivery parameters, especially basal insulin, for users of automated insulin delivery (AID) or artificial pancreas (AP) systems. It explains that basal delivery is intended to cover a portion of total daily insulin, but user needs and open-loop settings may become outdated or imbalanced due to lifestyle/physiology changes or differing basal/bolus behavior. The described system determines total insulin delivered over a predetermined time period as the sum of total basal and total bolus insulin, calculates the proportion delivered via basal, and compares this proportion to a threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, it calculates an average basal dosage for a subsequent time period approximately equal to the threshold and generates an instruction to deliver a modified basal dosage via a pump mechanism. The system may omit basal contributions delivered near bolus timing and may use segmentation and clustering algorithms to generate time-dependent basal profiles. It also includes safety considerations that can reduce the maximum recommended basal proportion if glucose control performance shows increased hypoglycemia time, and it describes example system components (wearable drug delivery device, glucose sensor/CGM, personal diabetes management device, and optional smart device) and their communications and execution of the AP/AID application.

Plaintiffs who were “alien enemies” during World War I filed a bill in equity in 1931 to recover property seized under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The District Court dismissed the bill, including on the ground that recovery was barred by Public Resolution No. 53 (June 27, 1934), which postponed deliveries of money or property authorized under the Trading with the Enemy Act and related legislation while Germany was in arrears on specified obligations.

The court held the case was governed by Cummings v. Deutsche Bank und Disconto-Gesellschaft, in which the Supreme Court concluded that Public Resolution No. 53 suspended the alien enemies’ right to recover seized property, and that dismissal should have been for lack of the suspended right rather than for lack of jurisdiction. The court found the present situation essentially the same and rejected appellants’ attempt to distinguish it by alleging illegal seizure. The decision was affirmed.

The passage describes Schneider Electric’s Edge Module for telco edge computing, developed to enable flexible, scalable, and autonomous edge deployments. It is a turnkey, self-contained solution with pre-integrated power, cooling, software, and IT components, designed for remote and distributed edge endpoints. The module supports single or three-phase power, includes N+1 cooling with a free air option, and can be customized to site requirements, including package cooling units mounted on the outside to avoid external condensers or piping. It is suited to cell tower edge use, with a single-phase 208-volt design supporting flexible power trains up to 48 KW with N+1 cooling, and configurable rack setups from two bay racks to custom four bay racks. The module is compatible with Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxture platform for remote monitoring and control, including metering and the ability to run autonomous “lights out” applications, with security features such as key locks, cameras, exterior lights, and a card kit key reader.

The passage defines IPD (Internal Pulldown Active), IPU (Internal Pullup Active), and DIS (Internal Pull Disabled) as states of the internal pull, noting these represent the default after reset and referring to sections on pullup/pulldown resistor details. It also describes that certain boot configuration pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC peripheral functions, and that at reset specific BTMODE bits (e.g., BTMODE[10], BTMODE[9:8], and BTMODE[4:0]) are sampled to select functions or ARM boot configuration, with pin roles changing after reset to GPMC data/address signals.

At OpenAI’s Developer Day, CEO Sam Altman demonstrated embedding third-party apps inside ChatGPT, turning it into a platform. Starting with a preview Apps SDK using open standards, some developers can build apps within ChatGPT; distribution is limited to a few big partners. The demos included Spotify, Canva, and Zillow appearing in chat and responding to commands, such as creating posters in Canva and viewing and refining home listings in Zillow. Altman said OpenAI plans new monetization options for these apps, including an “agentic commerce protocol” for instant checkout in ChatGPT. OpenAI also discussed building AI agents, introducing tools like AgentKit, and expanding Codex availability and related tools. The announcement frames ChatGPT as a chat-driven operating system that keeps users within ChatGPT, while OpenAI competes with other AI providers and faces pressures from open source models.

Investors fled equities on Friday amid worries that a tightening job market could raise inflation and push bond yields higher. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 666 points for its biggest daily percentage loss in 20 months, while all three major U.S. indexes recorded their biggest weekly losses in about two years; the S&P 500 and Dow had their worst weeks since early January 2016 and Nasdaq since early February 2016. Stocks declined further after the Labor Department reported employment growth outpaced expectations and wages rose the most in more than 8-1/2 years, boosting expectations for more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes and driving the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since January 2014. The 10-year yield increase made Treasuries potentially more attractive versus stocks, though some market participants said a pullback from the January rally was overdue. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq fell 2.12%, 2.54%, and 1.96%, respectively. All 11 S&P 500 sectors closed down, the volatility index (VIX) rose to its highest level since November 2016, and market breadth showed more declining issues than advancing ones.

The thesis analyzes web services that support digitized event organization and describes the development of a mobile application to help attendees access event information and immersion while reducing time spent on secondary activities. It discusses electronic business concepts, distinguishing digital business (broader) from e-commerce (online buying and selling), and outlines technologies such as cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, and mobile applications.  

Using web mining, the research analyzed 200 event management websites for data collected between August 1 and September 15, 2017, applying a model with five website forms: content, social/Web 2.0, public relations/user support, multimedia/mobile technologies, and user experience/technical specifications. Results summarize the presence of website elements, social media links, support options, multimedia usage, performance and technical metrics, and platform technologies. The conclusion states that event organizations increasingly require strong online presence, that users interact online to reserve and check information, and that technology is central to event planning. It also reports that Croatian websites ranked lower in the study and suggests improvements, especially in user experience, social media presence, mobile application availability, and multimedia content.

Jordan L. Couch, a partner at Palace Law in Washington, says recent advances in generative and agentic AI are transforming industries, including law. He defines AI as machine simulation of human intelligence and notes earlier uses such as spellcheck, predictive text, and even AI’s role in World War II. Couch describes generative AI as creating new content from existing data (e.g., ChatGPT4) and agentic AI as focusing on decision-making and recommendations by analyzing and breaking down queries. He argues AI is a powerful tool but not a panacea, emphasizing that lawyers should consider whether AI is the best tool for each task. He gives examples of AI for document review, legal research, and client communication, and suggests AI may help with analysis and rough drafting while nuanced judgment or creative problem-solving may still require humans. He lists several AI tools for legal practice, including Vincent AI, Copilot, ChatGPT (with a caution about using the paid version for client information), built-in software AI features, and custom tools, and states Part 2 will cover integrating AI into practice.

The passage explains tail risk (“fat tails”) as increased probabilities of rare events compared with a normal distribution, often associated with left-tail (loss) events. It describes tail risk hedging as strategies intended to reduce exposure to extreme, sudden market declines while still allowing participation in favorable outcomes, noting that hedging is difficult and may reduce returns due to costs. It presents six alternatives: put options, foreign assets, cash, Cambria’s tail risk ETF (TAIL), Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, and trend-following strategies. Examples and backtests mentioned include Meb Faber’s put-and-bond approach, Cambria’s TAIL ETF performance during selloffs, and the trade-off between higher hedging allocations and lower long-term returns. The passage also argues investors may hedge to avoid large losses, survive downturns, reduce behavioral mistakes during meltdowns, and recognizes the need to weigh pros and cons individually.

Real Madrid will play Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16, with Ronaldo seeking another European title. Other draws include Barcelona vs Chelsea, Manchester City vs Basel, Bayern Munich vs Besiktas, Juventus vs Tottenham, Manchester United vs Sevilla and Liverpool vs Porto, and Shakhtar Donetsk vs Roma. First legs are on 13/14 and 20/21 February, and second legs on 6/7 and 13/14 March.

Minnesota announced that Kirill Kaprizov has signed an NHL-record eight-year, $136 million contract extension through the 2033-34 season. The deal is the highest in NHL history for total money and average annual value ($17 million). The contract begins next season, includes large signing bonuses over the first four years, and Kaprizov will play this season on the final year of his prior five-year, $45 million deal. Kaprizov missed 40 games last season due to a lower-body injury surgery but had 25 goals and 31 assists in 41 games, and the passage also notes that NHL salary cap increases have been announced for the next three seasons.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike documented Ricky’s School of Rock’s 10-week RockJam courses in Linthwaite, capturing about 50 gigs and “rockstars in training.” The project ended after his latest RockJam, and he said the courses let pupils learn favourite songs and perform a gig for friends and family. Ricky Comiskey, the founder and guitar tutor, said many pupils later formed bands and that stage confidence grows, including among adult students. Mark’s son Tom was among the guitar class pupils who formed a band, and Ricky praised Mark’s photos, which are available to parents to see children’s progress in 10-week increments.

The passage reports a qualitative study on anticipated challenges and training needs of 18 pre-service physical education and health teachers in Quebec. The study aims to identify general anticipated challenges, challenges related to supporting students’ motivation, and how pre-service teachers can be better prepared to support motivation. Four focus groups found that the main overall challenges were classroom management and students’ lack of motivation. Regarding motivation specifically, participants highlighted five challenges: student heterogeneity, designing learning activities to sustain motivation, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences. Participants said they want initial training on planning strategies to motivate students, learning how to implement these strategies, and having more opportunities for practice. The conclusion presents recommendations for teacher education to better integrate preparation for supporting students’ motivation.

A Tom Thomson sketch, “Sketch for Lake in Algonquin Park,” that was given away as a gag gift fetched $481,250 at Heffel Fine Art Auction House’s semi-annual auction in Toronto. The work had been kept in Glenna Gardiner’s Edmonton basement until Heffel experts verified its pedigree and valued it between $125,000 and $175,000. The auction of 118 works raised $14.1 million, led by Paul-Emile Borduas’ “Figures schematiques” at $3.6 million, an auction record for the artist. Other results included Lawren Harris’ “Morning, Lake Superior” for $1.1 million, A.J. Casson’s “Farmhouse Near Wingle” for $541,250, Jack Bush’s “Strawberry” for $691,250, and Jean Paul Lemieux works “Le Cavalier dans la neige” for $841,250 and “Le temps retrouve - Kent House 1913” for $391,250.

Lindsay Gottlieb, a women’s basketball coach at UC Berkeley, said that during a Southwest Airlines trip over the weekend, an employee asked her to “prove” that her biracial 1-year-old son was hers by requesting his birth certificate, even though she offered his passport. Gottlieb said the employee also asked for a Facebook post and that the request was “demeaning and insensitive,” and she suspected the delay was due to her son’s skin color. Southwest Airlines apologized and said its policy is to verify lap children under two by reviewing a birth certificate or government-issued identification, and that domestic travel does not require matching last names; it also said it will emphasize the coaching moment with the employee and ensure policies are properly followed. The airline did not specify whether the birth certificate request was due to the child’s last name or race. Chrissy Teigen said she has faced similar requests and described them as a precaution against child trafficking.

The passage discusses an operator–field mapping between a field theory operator \(O\) and a gravity-side field \(\phi\), emphasizing that their quantum numbers match. It explains that, in semiclassical gravity, the scaling dimension \(\Delta\) of \(O\) is related to the mass of the corresponding bulk field. For a massive scalar in AdS, near the boundary \(z\to 0\), the field has two asymptotic behaviors with exponents \(\Delta\) and \(d-\Delta\), leading to a relation between \(\Delta\) and \(m^2\). It describes the Breitenlohner–Freedman (BF) bound: the theory is well-defined when the exponents are real, while violating the BF bound leads to exponentially growing (unstable) modes. The passage then covers normalizability using an inner product, boundary conditions needed for energy conservation, and how normalizable vs. non-normalizable modes correspond to states vs. deformations of the boundary theory. In standard quantization, non-normalizable modes act as sources that deform the boundary action by terms involving the dual operator, and \(\Delta\) determines whether the deformation is marginal, relevant, or irrelevant. It concludes with how correlation functions in the boundary theory are computed via a generating functional related to the gravity partition function, evaluated in the semiclassical limit by approximating the gravity path integral with classical solutions satisfying boundary conditions.

The passage explains that the VIX is the Volatility Index, a measure of implied volatility in S&P 500 index options, and it is related to the S&P 500 and SPY. It notes that the VIX often moves inversely to the stock market (negative correlation), and describes it as a mean reversion indicator: when the risk premium increases and the VIX rises, it may be wise to buy stocks, and when the VIX drops, it may be wise to sell. The article then presents several VIX trading strategies, including an example strategy to go long SPY/ES when VIX breaks above the upper Bollinger Band and exit after two up days, with a test period from 2005 to July 2012. It also mentions that many strategies online are complex and that VIX can be traded via ETFs such as VXX, though an ETF cannot replicate VIX completely. The passage concludes by stating that the strategies presented are simple but still appear to work, and recommends doing one’s own backtesting.

UAE Energy Minister Suhail bin Mohammed al-Mazroui said OPEC and non-OPEC oil producers plan to announce in June an exit strategy from global supply cuts, but the deal will not end then. He said it is premature to discuss the shape of the strategy before the June meeting and that the group’s voices must be considered. Kuwait’s oil minister said the possibility of an exit strategy would be studied before June. Russia’s Alexander Novak said it is too early to discuss exit and that withdrawal should be gradual, potentially taking three to six months depending on market conditions. The supply-reduction agreement involves cuts of about 1.8 million barrels per day.

Nigeria’s inflation fell to 16.25% in May from 17.28% in April, below analysts’ forecast of 16.1%. The National Bureau of Statistics reported a month-on-month headline index increase of 1.88% in May, higher than April’s 1.60%, suggesting ongoing price pressure despite the year-on-year decline. Food inflation rose to 19.27% year-on-year in May, down slightly from 19.30% in April. The NBS attributed higher food prices to increases in items including meat, bread and cereals, fish, potatoes, milk cheese and eggs, and vegetables such as tomatoes.

The passage reviews progress and algorithms for computing or approximating Nash equilibrium in various game classes, with focus on multiplayer imperfect-information games. It describes that exact Nash equilibrium computation is PPAD-hard and that iterative methods like counterfactual regret minimization and fictitious play lack convergence guarantees. The authors propose an exact approach that reformulates multiplayer Nash equilibrium computation as a nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) derived from a generalized sequence-form representation, then models it as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program solvable using nonconvex quadratic optimization advances. They apply the method to reduced 3-player Kuhn poker (after removing dominated actions), where they report solving in 2.47 seconds with deviation gains bounded by 1.4×10⁻17. The full (unreduced) game could not be solved within 24 hours. Experiments also compare against Gambit methods: only logit quantal response equilibrium (QRE) was applicable for extensive form, taking over 40 seconds on the reduced game and 10 minutes to hang on the full GUI run, though the command line produced a solution in about 2 minutes 34 seconds. The conclusion states the new bilinear/NCP approach is effective for smaller instances but has limited scalability compared with logit QRE.

Box Inc. shares fell after the company reported first-quarter earnings ahead of Wall Street expectations. Adjusted earnings were a loss of 7 cents per share versus the expected loss of 8 cents. Revenue was about $140.5 million versus an expected $139.7 million, with a 20% improvement year over year. Billings revenue rose to $116.7 million, exceeding the FactSet estimate of $113.1 million. Box added about 3,000 paying customers, bringing the total to 85,000. For the second quarter, the company projected an adjusted loss of 5 to 6 cents per share and revenue of $146 million to $147 million, which exceeded Thomson Reuters’ guidance at the midpoint. The stock rose nearly 2% during regular trading but ended with a 4.6% decline after the bell.

The case holds that a land certificate transfer dating back more than forty years, coming from proper custody, with no suspicious circumstances, is admissible without proof of execution or prior existence for twenty years, even if its genuineness is attacked. The transfer sufficiently identified the certificate later used to issue a patent, and a power of attorney in support of conveyance more than thirty years old from proper custody and found genuine is presumed conclusive. A certified copy of a third party’s Land Office affidavit was ruled inadmissible to disparage another claimant’s title by transfer. Evidence of a witness’s own character for truth is also barred when not otherwise impeached. The jury found the transfer genuine; based on that and other evidence, the trial court admitted the transfer and found for the appellee, and the appellate court affirmed the judgment.

A certified agreement states that Thomas Scullun will sail the bark Cape Horn Pigeon from San Francisco by Dec. 1, 1891, to go east and return, with the Wings paying half the round-trip ticket to Boston and Scullun paying the other half. Compensation is to be one-twelfth of the lay in net proceeds of the voyage. The document includes certifications and clearances for the foreign voyage, including an outward foreign manifest and Scullun’s sworn statement about the accuracy of the cargo manifest and intentions for whaling. It also contains a letter describing an 1892 arrest of the Cape Horn Pigeon in the Sea of Okhotsk by Lieutenant von Cube of the Imperial navy aboard the English schooner Maria for illegal sealing; it compares von Cube’s account with Scullun’s version, notes an investigation found no cause for confiscation, concluded the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding, and that the vessel was returned to its owners without delay.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for an “intelligent automated assistant for media exploration,” focusing on providing an auditory-based interface for media search and playback. It outlines methods where a digital assistant receives natural-language speech requests for media, identifies and refines media selections based on subsequent speech inputs, and provides speech outputs along with media playback. Other examples include suggesting different media items based on consecutive non-affirmative user responses, requesting user input after a threshold is met, and tailoring media using merged preference profiles when multiple users are physically present. The passage also discusses electronic devices, non-transitory computer-readable media, and a system architecture for client-server digital assistant operation, including components for speech input/output and related device hardware.

Carol Moore, the final president of Burlington College, and others say a land deal Jane Sanders championed in 2010 contributed to the college’s closure last year. The college bought a 33-acre waterfront parcel for $10 million to expand, and Moore wrote that enrollment was about 195 and the budget just over $4 million. Federal authorities are examining whether Sanders accurately represented donations used as collateral for the bank loan tied to the deal. A second agreement also drew criticism: Moore said a deal Sanders brokered between the college and Driscoll’s Vermont Woodworking School left the college at a disadvantage, calling it a “sweetheart deal” for Carina Driscoll, who is Bernie Sanders’ stepdaughter.

Dusty Baker said he believes Jeff Kent deserves a bust in the Baseball Hall of Fame. Kent, a former Giants second baseman managed by Baker in San Francisco, has been eligible since 2013 but has hovered around 15 percent on ballots, below the 75-percent threshold. Kent said he does not understand why his vote total is not higher, citing unfamiliar WAR numbers. He hit 377 home runs, reached 100 RBIs eight times, batted .290 over a 17-year career, and was the 2002 National League MVP. Baker said Kent is genuine, played hard, and he values having him on the team. The 2017 Hall of Fame class will be announced Jan. 18.

QuantifiedStrategies.com offers TradingView trading strategies (Pinescript) and states they aim to provide simple, effective strategies to assist traders. Users can sign up to be notified when strategies are available, view a complete list via a green banner, and select strategies to have them translated into Pinescript. The site includes a disclaimer that trading involves risk and that past performance is not indicative of future results, advising responsible trading and consulting a financial advisor if needed.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 GPU capabilities and architectural features, including hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers and CUDA Task Graphs for more efficient GPU work submission and overlapping of data movement with computation. It details the A100’s Ampere-based architecture, fabrication on TSMC 7nm, Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) for partitioning GPUs into isolated instances with dedicated memory and QoS, and third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch for improved multi-GPU scalability. The text also explains A100 SM features such as third-generation Tensor Cores supporting multiple data types (including FP16/FP32, BF16, TF32, and FP64), asynchronous copy and barrier mechanisms, larger combined L1/shared memory, cache residency controls for L2, and performance improvements from structured sparsity. It further covers A100 memory architecture (HBM2, L2 cache size and bandwidth, ECC protection), compute data compression, error/fault handling concepts, and additional accelerators (e.g., NVJPG decode, optical flow accelerator, NVDEC). Finally, it outlines related CUDA 11 features (async copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency control, cooperative groups, and task graphs) and mentions DGX A100 as an integrated system using A100 and MIG for scalable AI infrastructure.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth addressed hundreds of generals and admirals he summoned from across the globe, arguing for changes to a military force he said had gone “soft” and “woke.” Greg Jaffe, a Pentagon reporter for The New York Times, discusses Hegseth’s speech.

The design requirements include configuring the circuit as shown in Figure 7-7 and generating an alert (logic high output) when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Because of fast output edges, low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitors must be placed directly between each device’s (V+) pin and ground pins to prevent supply ringing and false triggers or oscillations. The device may use split supplies ((V+) and (V-)) or single supplies ((V+) and GND), with input signals staying within the recommended input range; with split supplies, the output swings low to (V-) rather than GND. A stable, low-noise power supply is important for comparator use, and the bypass capacitor should be as close as possible to the supply pin and preferably directly between (V+) and GND pins. Output and input trace coupling should be minimized to prevent oscillations, including avoiding parallel routing without a (V+) or GND trace between them, placing input series resistors near the device, and optionally adding a low (<100 Ω) series resistor with the output to damp ringing or reflections.

Qualcomm reportedly leaked information about an upcoming Asus smartphone called the Asus Zenfone AR, which is described as only the second consumer-facing Google Tango-enabled smartphone. The blog post was dated January 4, referenced a phone to be unveiled at CES, and has since been taken down after sites like GSMArena saw it. The Zenfone AR is said to be the first Tango-enabled phone to also support Google’s Daydream View headset and to use the Qualcomm Snapdragon 821. After the leak, Evan Blass posted renders he said were of the Zenfone AR. Pricing and availability were not mentioned, with more information expected at CES. Asus also teased another Zenfone featuring the “world’s best processor,” assumed to be the Snapdragon 835.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2019. It includes the SEC filing details, index of sections, unaudited consolidated financial statements (cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets), and notes describing accounting policies, leases, financial instruments and fair value measurements, stockholders’ equity, commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings, and debt. It also provides segment information for North America, International, and AWS, along with management’s discussion covering forward-looking statements, critical accounting judgments, liquidity and capital resources, and results of operations, including net sales, operating income, operating expenses, interest and other income/expense, income taxes, and non-GAAP free cash flow measures.

The IMF’s mission chief Ron van Rooden told Ukraine that its pension system is unsustainable because it supports about 30% of the population and runs at a loss. He said pension reforms have been delayed too long and that Ukraine needs to limit early retirements and improve pension funding by targeting companies that avoid paying pension tax. The Ukrainian government has resisted raising the pension age, currently 57 for women and 60 for men, due to voter unpopularity and parliamentary opposition. Ukraine is seeking further IMF funding, hoping for $4.5 billion this year, while the IMF warned that Ukraine must do more to recover and build a modern market economy.

The passage explains the 20-day exponential moving average (20 EMA) trading strategy, which uses the 20 EMA to generate buy signals when a security’s price rises above the 20 EMA and sell signals when it falls below. It describes a backtest using SPY (S&P 500 ETF) data not adjusted for dividends and splits, noting low CAGR and a significant drawdown. It then states that adding an additional technical indicator improved the equity curve and performance metrics for the revised strategy, though drawdown remained the same. Finally, it applies the strategy to Bitcoin using rules to go long when price breaks above the 20 EMA and sell on the opposite, stating the results worked much better for Bitcoin.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate (iron(II) sulfate), also known as ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is soluble in water and acids and has octahedral molecular geometry. It is produced during titanium dioxide manufacturing from ilmenite, where it is also a sulfate co-product; crystallization of hot sulfate solutions upon cooling can yield it. The product has free moisture content of at least 4%, can become dusty due to iron crystals sticking together, and may cause container attack as acid liquid leaches out. It contains 18–20 wt% iron and up to 3 wt% free acid (of total weight), and includes an acidic compound such as sulfuric acid. The hydrated form is used medically for iron deficiency and for industrial uses including water purification via flocculation and phosphate removal, preventing eutrophication, reducing Cr6+ in cement, and serving as an iron supplier in agriculture; historically it has also been used as a textile dye fixative, to blacken leather, and as part of ink.

The speaker thanks and welcomes attendees, saluting military and institution members, and addresses the Corps of Cadets. He discusses lessons from sports and emphasizes that losing is difficult but, if necessary, should be met with full effort and learning. As Commander in Chief, he describes a president’s roles and argues that leadership must be demonstrated through setting goals, persuading others, and working with Congress and the public to sustain military commitments. He says the end of the cold war reduces but does not eliminate threats, and he calls for building a new world order based on democracy, tolerance, and peaceful settlement of differences. He argues the United States should engage internationally and lead but not act as the world’s policeman, rejecting rigid rules for using military force and advocating selective use when stakes warrant, with clear missions, plans, and withdrawal criteria. He recounts examples where military force was used and stresses the importance of adequate forces, strong leadership, training, and caring conduct by the armed forces, highlighting the All Volunteer Force as a success supported by meritocracy, education, and discipline. He concludes by urging public service, duty, and higher purpose beyond oneself, then shares his own experience leaving school to enlist and encourages the cadets as they begin their service, ending with a gesture of amnesty to the Corps of Cadets.

The passage is a set of remarks attributed to Coach Quenneville discussing team play, player roles, and the playoffs. It describes how players often know each other’s styles and how matchups and line mixing are used. Quenneville praises several players for aspects beyond scoring, including speed, defense, puck possession awareness, conditioning, and performance without the puck. He notes that some players were given reduced minutes earlier in the season due to schedule, but played more in the playoffs. He also discusses line responsibility, expectations, and the team’s consistency, four-line play, improved defense, and goaltending. Additional points include handling adversity (being down against Detroit), benefiting from an extra day of rest, managing penalties, and preparations for upcoming playoff games. The passage concludes with Quenneville discussing goaltending confidence, player demeanor, and player performance trends as the playoffs progress.

The passage quotes the first article of a treaty between Russia and Great Britain, stating that in any part of the Pacific Ocean, the subjects of both powers would not be disturbed in navigation or fishing, or in approaching unoccupied coasts for trade with indigenous people, subject to later restrictions. It then summarizes a Paris arbitration decision regarding Russia’s 1821 claim of jurisdiction in the Bering Sea and Russia’s later admission (in 1824 and 1825 treaties) that its jurisdiction would be limited to the range of a cannon shot from shore. The tribunal’s interpretation is discussed as meaning that waters included as part of the “great ocean” would cover connected branches like the Okhotsk Sea as well as the Bering Sea. The passage further supports the idea that open seas should remain free to all states, citing views by F. de Martens and Vattel, and argues that sea areas like the Kara Sea are open to navigation and not considered belonging exclusively to Russia.

The passage describes advancements in NVIDIA’s GDDR6X and RTX IO, along with features of the GA10x Ampere architecture. It explains that PAM4 signaling in GDDR6X upgrades data transfer by sending two bits per clock edge using four voltage levels, and introduces MTA Maximum Transition Avoidance plus new training, adaptation, and equalization schemes to improve signal-to-noise ratio. For storage, it outlines NVIDIA RTX IO, which works with Microsoft DirectStorage to offload GPU-based lossless loading and decompression from the CPU, aiming for up to 100x faster I/O performance and near-instant game loading. The passage also covers the NVIDIA A40 data center GPU’s performance and features, including increased throughput, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, scalable memory via NVLink, virtualization support, and compatibility with the EGX platform. Additional sections discuss display support for high-resolution/high-refresh gaming, fifth-generation NVDEC video decoding with hardware-accelerated codec support (including AV1), and seventh-generation NVENC video encoding. It concludes with mentions of ray tracing and AI improvements in GA10x, GDDR6X support, and regulatory/specification disclaimers.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted by a Manhattan grand jury on charges of rape in the first and third degrees and criminal sexual act in the first degree. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr said the indictment brings Weinstein “another step closer to accountability.” The indictment followed a statement that Weinstein would not testify before the grand jury on his lawyers’ advice. Weinstein was charged last Friday on two counts of rape and one count of a criminal sexual act involving two separate women, and the prosecution said he lacked time to prepare and only learned the women’s identities on Friday. The DA said the case would be tried in court rather than in the press.

Damian Lillard scored 32 points and became the fastest player in Portland franchise history to reach 10,000 career points, but the Trail Blazers’ four-game winning streak ended with a 130-105 loss to the Toronto Raptors. Toronto won for the sixth straight time, with DeMar DeRozan scoring 35 points and Jonas Valanciunas adding 18. The Raptors improved to 20-4 at home, led by a season-high 19 made 3-pointers, and led 37-18 after one quarter and 74-52 at halftime. The Blazers had lost five of their past seven road games.

The passage is an overview of how Enron grew rapidly from a pipeline company into a trading and marketing powerhouse, largely shaped by Jeff Skilling and Ken Lay. It describes Enron’s culture of aggressive risk-taking and “intellectual capital,” its market dominance through models like the “Gas Bank,” and its expansion into trading many commodities and new areas such as telecommunications, online commodity trading, broadband, and movies on demand.

The text then outlines Enron’s decline: its stock fell after problems in California’s energy deregulation, increased scrutiny of its accounting practices and profits, and negative media coverage. It attributes worsening conditions to factors including the tech bubble burst and internal culture changes such as forced ranking and increasing paranoia. The passage also discusses Rebecca Mark’s exit from Enron’s asset-heavy ventures and the leadership transition from Lay to Skilling as CEO in February 2001. It concludes with Skilling’s resignation, Lay’s promise of a more “kinder, gentler” Enron, and Skilling’s shift away from Enron as its stock remains under pressure.

Vertex Resource Group Ltd. acquired a private hydro-vac services company serving the Edmonton, Alberta region for $4.3 million, adding 11 hydro-vac units and doubling Vertex’s hydro-vac fleet. The acquisition expands Vertex’s hydro-vac services into the Edmonton market and enables cross-selling to existing Vertex customers, supporting industry diversification. The deal closed June 30, 2018, and the acquired company began operating as Vertex. Based on historical financial information, the acquisition is expected to add about $5 million in annual revenue.

The passage describes quantum learning tasks focused on estimating nonlinear functions of quantum states, particularly quantities of the form \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{k}O)\). It motivates the question of whether efficient estimation requires \(k\)-replica joint measurements. The paper claims affirmative answers: with access to fewer than \(k\) replicas, estimating \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{k+1}O)\) for many observables requires exponentially many samples, while with \(k{+}1\) replicas it becomes efficiently achievable with constant or relatively small sample complexity, establishing a fine-grained hierarchy of replica quantum advantage.  

To prove these separations, the work introduces a general indistinguishability principle for “Haar-assembled ensembles,” showing such ensembles are hard to distinguish from their average using restricted (1-replica) measurements. The principle is applied to lower bounds for estimating \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{k+1}O)\), to spectrum testing (including rank testing), and it is complemented by upper bound results that show partial replica access can match the optimal dependence on the Hilbert space dimension. The passage also outlines related techniques (e.g., Le Cam’s two-point method, permutation operators, and generalized swap tests) and discusses future directions concerning error dependence, identifying thresholds between hard/easy regimes, extending spectrum-testing applications, and related practical considerations like sequential state resetting.

The speaker addresses Americans training to serve abroad, saying their task is peace and asking how to maintain security in the Atlantic community. He describes how, after World War II, Europe rebounded from destruction into a “new Europe” marked by confidence, progress, partnership, and peace, attributing the change to common action, interdependent institutions, and collective security. He presents NATO as an important part of this design, arguing that NATO should adapt through consultation rather than isolation. The speaker says NATO is an alliance to keep peace, that its success is measured by war being deterred, and that deterrence relies on integrated military power and political unity. He warns that erosion of collective effort would shake Atlantic stability and emphasizes U.S. determination to join allies to preserve and strengthen NATO’s deterrent strength. He concludes by urging efforts toward human solidarity and instructing trainees to make this their task.

The passage describes flash memory characteristics, including endurance limits for total erase operations before failure, how the lower 32 kB flash address space supports higher erase/program cycles for EEPROM emulation, and that on devices with 32 kB or less, the entire flash supports NWEC (LOWER) erase/program cycles. It also defines maximum write operations per word line before erasure is required, program time (from program command trigger to completion interrupt flag set), and sector program time (from first word program command trigger to final word completion and interrupt flag set, including software loading time).

A penalty-kick tiebreaker (“shoot-out”) may be used to decide a winner when a soccer match remains tied after regulation time and extra time (if played), according to Law 10 of the IFAB Laws of the Game (“Determining the Outcome of a Match”) and with technical aspects of the penalty kick in Law 14 (“The Penalty Kick”). The procedure starts with each team selecting five eligible players to take alternating kicks from the penalty spot (12 yards from the goal), aiming to score against the opposing goalkeeper; only players on the field at the end of extra time (or regulation time if no extra time) may take part. If one team has scored more after both take five kicks (unless already mathematically decided), it wins; if the score is tied, it continues in sudden death with alternating single kicks until one team scores and the other misses. The referee conducts coin tosses for goal and which team kicks first, ensures kicks follow the rules (including re-kicks under Law 14), and records the results. The shoot-out winner is the team with more goals after the necessary kicks (or an unmatched goal in sudden death), and the shoot-out result is recorded as part of the match result, though those goals do not count for individual statistics. The passage also outlines coach preparation steps, referee and player roles during execution, eligibility and goalkeeper replacement rules, reductions for unequal player counts (“reduce to equate”), and additional notes on the penalty-kick and forfeiture conditions.

The passage discusses using full-screen mode on a Galaxy Fold and includes disclosures that some offers are from companies that compensate the site, though product ratings are not influenced by that compensation. It then reviews the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, describing it as a no-frills credit card with a 0% intro APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by variable APR rates, and notes a balance transfer fee (5%, minimum $5) plus a 3% foreign transaction fee. The review also mentions there is no annual fee, offers up to $600 of cell phone protection (with a $25 deductible), and provides general guidance on applying (submit personal/financial details, review terms, and wait for approval).

The passage is from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019. It includes general information about the filing, registered securities, and incorporated documents, followed by a description of Microsoft’s business, operating segments (Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing), major products and services, competition, operations, research and development, distribution and licensing options, customers, employees, and available investor information. It also contains a section on forward-looking statements and extensive risk factors, including competition, business model and cloud execution risks, security and cyberattacks, data misuse and privacy concerns, harmful content, IoT and AI-related risks, infrastructure and quality/supply issues, intellectual property risks, litigation and regulatory scrutiny, and anti-corruption and competition law compliance risks.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on June 24, 2020, stating that on June 24, 2020 it entered into an Indemnification Agreement with Elon Musk. The agreement provides interim directors’ and officers’ indemnity coverage for 90 days during which Tesla resumes evaluating options for D&O coverage.
