Tesla plans to obtain a binding market quote for a D&O liability insurance policy with $100 million aggregate coverage, and will select a coverage option after the 90-day bridge term. Under the agreement, Musk will fund up to $100 million from personal funds if the coverage is not indemnifiable by Tesla, and Tesla will pay Musk a one-time fee of $972,361. Tesla will use reasonable best efforts to obtain the market quote and may pay an additional amount to reconcile the fee based on the market-based premium prorated for 90 days and discounted by 50% if applicable. The agreement includes customary terms and is signed by Tesla’s Chief Financial Officer on June 30, 2020.

Sony said its Xperia XZ Premium will receive an Android Oreo update later this year, with improved camera features and a new 3D scanning application. The update is expected to arrive around the same time as Android Oreo on the Xperia XZ1 and XZ1 Compact at IFA 2017. The new 3D Creator app will enable 3D scans of faces, heads, food, and objects for upload to social media, use in GIFs, and sending to a 3D printer. Camera updates include a predictive capture mode that detects smiles and takes three snaps before the shutter is pressed, and an improved burst mode using automatic phase detection to track moving objects at 10 photos per second. Sony did not specify the exact update date.

AGNC Investment is described as a top mortgage REIT expected to benefit from Fed rate cuts, which could lower financing costs and increase book value through higher mortgage-backed securities valuations. The passage states AGNC has shown improved spread performance and posted its third consecutive quarter of positive net interest income in Q2’25, and that the stock trades at a premium to book value. The author reports a bullish stance based on the strong net interest income trend and an attractive monthly dividend, and notes a beneficial long position in AGNC.

The passage describes an appeal by Patrick Sutherland from a Supreme Court judgment dismissing his CPLR article 78 petition challenging the New York State Board of Parole’s denial of his parole release. Sutherland, serving a prison term for numerous crimes, first sought parole release in August 2007; the Board denied release and ordered he be held for 24 months. His contention was that the Board relied on erroneous information about his criminal history, specifically that it stated he shot an individual in the arm despite the charges having been dismissed before trial. The record indicated the information came from the presentence investigation report and Sutherland did not refute it when asked; the report did not note dismissal of the charges, and Sutherland did not seek to correct the report. The court found he was precluded from arguing the Board could not rely on the presentence report because he did not timely challenge the information before sentencing. The court concluded the Board considered the statutory factors and that its decision was not irrational or improper, and it affirmed the denial of relief.

The passage is a presidential address in which the speaker says the traditional State of the Union format is being set aside due to major events and the need to reform American programs and institutions. The speaker emphasizes peace as the top foreign policy priority and describes progress toward ending the Vietnam War through achieving a “just peace,” while outlining new foreign policy directions based on changes since World War II. These include sharing responsibility for defense and reducing U.S. involvement abroad, strengthening alliances, and pursuing negotiations with the Soviet Union and discussions with Communist China.

The speaker then argues that the 1970s should bring domestic reform, focusing on welfare system reform, a “New Federalism” to shift power back to states and people, and expanded opportunities through measures such as equal voting rights and equal employment opportunity. The speaker identifies stopping the rise in the cost of living as a key objective, calls for balancing the federal budget, and stresses expanded federal action against crime, especially organized crime and narcotics. The address also highlights environmental concerns as a major issue, proposing comprehensive clean air and clean water efforts, including a $10 billion nationwide clean waters program, and additional measures on pollution control, open spaces, and automobile-related emissions.

Finally, the speaker discusses national growth policy to address urban and rural problems, describes goals for the future of the country by 200th anniversary, and calls for moral and spiritual leadership and inspiration for young Americans, ending with a statement that achieving these challenges will affect future peace and freedom worldwide.

Andrea Conti’s agent said Conti wants to join Milan, that his time with Atalanta is over, and that Atalanta is no longer in his mind. The agent noted Conti scored eight goals and had four assists in 33 Serie A appearances this season, and said the issue was clarified after disputes. He argued Gasperini should not prevent Conti’s transfer and criticized any veto on players who can achieve their dream, saying players should work realistically to improve professionally and economically.

The passage summarizes Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s work and concepts, including randomness, uncertainty, “tail events,” and his portfolio-focused ideas. It describes Taleb’s background, career in trading and founding Empirica Capital with Mark Spitznagel, and his claim that people confuse luck with competence. It explains Taleb’s barbell strategy analogy: a portfolio structured with low-risk assets on one side and high-risk assets on the other, with no middle ground, intended to benefit from tail risks. It also outlines ideas related to thin vs. fat tails (Mediocristan vs. Extremistan), antifragility, and “skin in the game” from Taleb’s 2018 book *Skin In The Game*. The passage includes brief summaries of *Fooled by Randomness* (role of chance and biases), *The Black Swan* (rare unpredictable events), and *Antifragile* (systems that benefit from shocks). It further discusses options strategies, examples of barbell applications to equities/bonds/options, and mentions Universa Investments and Spitznagel’s *Safe Haven Investing*.

A new remote-controlled swimming robot, nicknamed the “mini manbo,” is planned to investigate damage at Japan’s Fukushima Dai-Ichi nuclear plant after the March 2011 earthquake and tsunami. Developers plan to send it into the primary containment vessel of Unit 3 in July to study damage extent and locate melted fuel parts submerged in highly radioactive water. The robot is about bread-loaf size, uses tail propellers and lights, and collects data with two cameras and a radiation dosimeter; it was demonstrated near Tokyo by remote operation. Japan hopes to use findings to locate and remove fuel after the 2020 Olympics. Earlier snake and scorpion-shaped robots became stuck or failed due to radiation exposure. Scientists need melted fuel’s exact location and structural damage information to determine the safest fuel-removal approach.

The passage contains postgame comments from Coach Vigneault and others, expressing disappointment with the outcome but pride in the team’s effort. It notes that all three games went to overtime, with both goaltenders making outstanding saves, and describes the game as hard-fought with every inch contested. The coach says he will take a couple of days to reflect before discussing further, and emphasizes focusing on improving for the next game by having more puck possession and aiming to capitalize on power-play opportunities that have generated good looks and shots.

Malawi Heath Equity Network (MHEN) has asked the government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, saying their absence is affecting how public funds are managed. MHEN Executive Director George Jobe said internal auditors provide guidance on using financial resources, and councils may fail to account for received money without them. MHEN also reported challenges in budget and programme implementation, including councils and partners working separately and councils not involving rural residents in annual budget preparation. A Planning and Economic Analyst, Yohanne Nyanja, said government plans to send auditors are advanced and will improve transparency and financial management, adding that councils should support auditors rather than treat them as “police.” The research, supported by Mamaye, further found a coordination gap between councils and NGOs/CSOs.

The passage is a lecture introducing initial coin offerings (ICOs) as a new form of crypto-based crowdfunding. It discusses what an ICO is, how it evolved from ideas based on Bitcoin’s technology, and provides statistics on ICO growth and decline. The lecturer describes common ICO characteristics, including raising funds before networks become functional, often marketing tokens on an idea, and frequently lacking published or decentralized open-source code at the time of the offering. It also covers token-related features such as supply/monetary policy, token fungibility and transferability, promoter involvement, and the roles of white papers, source code reviews, team background, venture capital participation, community interest, and token distribution. The lecture compares ICOs to Kickstarter, outlines how token use cases affect evaluation, and explains possible accounting approaches for ICO proceeds (such as deferred or current revenue). Finally, it notes that ICOs vary by jurisdiction and that regulatory discussion is planned for a later session, while summarizing overall ICO market patterns and expected failure rates.

Donald Trump said the U.S.-Canada trade relationship would only be “tweaked,” but the passage argues that small changes by the U.S. could strongly affect Canada due to an imbalance in trade flows: 18% of America’s foreign trade goes to Canada, while 76% of Canada’s goes to the U.S. It notes U.S. grievances about Canada’s beef imports and supply management, as well as softwood lumber, and expresses concern that Trump’s deregulation and low-tax policy could make Canada uncompetitive. The passage credits Justin Trudeau’s diplomatic approach with keeping distance without disrespect and compares it favorably to Theresa May’s handling of Trump. It also describes mutual support in a communique covering trade, energy, border security, alliances including NATO and NORAD, and efforts against ISIS, highlighting Trump’s civil greeting of Trudeau and Canada.

The passage is a set of remarks by coach Deboer and others about preparing for playoff games at home. They emphasize building their game, improving play in specific areas (such as support across the ice and limiting distractions), making lineup decisions the day of the game, and staying focused despite distractions from people in town. They discuss the need to play with the puck more, attack and create penalty opportunities, and handle opponents’ speed that can force teams into difficult positions. They identify Crosby as a key player and note that Kessel, Crosby, and Malkin create matchup problems, requiring awareness of the whole group. The speakers also stress that the series is not over until a team wins four games and that momentum may shift between teams, so they must not get frustrated.

The passage transmits a preliminary report by a special committee (James Bronson Reynolds and Commissioner Charles P. Neill) investigating conditions in the Chicago stock yards. The report is presented as showing an urgent need for Congress to enact drastic, thorough Federal inspection of stockyards, packing houses, and their products entering interstate or foreign commerce, because existing law cannot achieve satisfactory results. The passage describes unclean and dangerous handling of meat products, inadequate federal power to enforce inspection for many prepared meat products, and insufficient appropriations that limit inspectors. It calls for legislation to allow inspections “from the hoof to the can,” to supervise preparation methods and prescribe sanitary conditions, and suggests inspection costs be paid via a fee per animal slaughtered. The passage notes the investigation is unfinished and cannot yet address certain alleged abuses involving chemicals and doctoring of meat. It urges immediate enactment of provisions known as Senate amendment No. 29, the “Beveridge amendment.”

The Santa Cruz County Board of Supervisors has selected Carlos Palacios, the county’s assistant county administrative officer, to replace retiring County Administrative Officer Susan Mauriello. Palacios, 55, will assume the top administrative role on Tuesday with a base salary of $263,057. The board conducted a national search to fill the position, with Palacios among the candidates interviewed. Mauriello, 62, will retire July 7 after 27 years in the role, having earned a base salary of $283,150 in 2016. Palacios will oversee about 2,400 staff and an annual budget of about $720 million, and is credited with supporting several county initiatives.

A 26-year-old man was detained by armed police after allegedly threatening two people with a gun at Shackleton Court, a tower block in Newton Heath. Police were called at around 4:30pm on Monday following reports of an armed man at the flats on Croydon Drive. Armed officers arrived, conducted a search, and negotiators were reportedly involved before the man was arrested on suspicion of making threats with a firearm and remains in custody. Witnesses said officers with rifles and multiple police vans surrounded the tower complex and the incident lasted several hours.

The passage introduces the L-separability problem for logics L and L+ and defines separators as L-formulae ψ such that φ entails ψ and ψ entails ¬φ′. It notes that separability generalizes L-definability when L+ is closed under negation, and that both are central problems with computer science applications. The paper studies definability and separability of modal µ-calculus formulae (µML) by formulae in modal logic ML, over different classes of models including all models, words, and trees with bounded or unbounded outdegree (and their finite restrictions). Table 1 summarizes the complexity landscape for ML definability and ML separability across these classes, including exponential-time, PSPACE, double-exponential, and higher results for higher outdegree (d ≥ 3). The passage provides an example showing that certain µML properties can be separated by ML over the given signature only in specific cases, and it outlines model-theoretic and automata-theoretic foundations used later. It defines separability, Craig interpolation, joint consistency, and provides key preliminary results and lemmas relating separability and interpolation to joint consistency and automata constructions.

A Sunday report said Ashley Hollis, an A&O Shearman associate, won the reality show “Big Brother.” Hollis attributed her victory to hiding her true profession by passing herself off as a social media marketing manager and said she took inspiration from Elle Woods from a 2001 movie. She stated she worked for days on her final winning speech and said attorneys must anticipate others’ arguments and prepare strategies and counterarguments. Hollis plans to give part of her $750,000 prize to her parents and is considering buying a home.

The passage discusses using STEAM education and gamification to increase student engagement, motivation, and learning outcomes, while noting that effects may vary and that further methodical studies are needed. It describes a quantitative bibliometric analysis of Scopus documents using the search string “steam” and “gamification” (English language only), focusing on 2017–2023, resulting in a final dataset of 34 articles. The study reports publication trends (growth from 2020–2023), top cited articles and sources, leading authors and countries by publications and citations, subject-area distribution (with computer science at 37.7%), and keyword co-occurrence results (most frequent terms include gamification and steam education). It also presents countries collaboration patterns and factorial analysis identifying three clusters of related research topics, followed by conclusions summarizing key findings (34 documents and 155 citations) and acknowledgments, methods, and publication information.

The passage describes the DAWn-plasma randomized, open-label phase 2 trial evaluating best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. Protocol amendments and informed consent materials were reviewed and approved by independent ethics committees at each investigational center, and serious/unexpected adverse events were to be reported to these committees. The study was conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines, with informed consent required before enrollment (including provisions for verbal consent).  

Eligible participants (≥18 years) provided consent and had confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection; key exclusions included mechanical ventilation before or at randomization, certain safety hazards, a prior grade 3 allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation/intubation, and recent anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody use. Participants were randomized with a 2:1 allocation to standard of care plus convalescent plasma or standard of care alone, and the intervention involved 800–1000 mL total plasma in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and requirements for neutralizing-antibody titers.  

A primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 489 patients were randomized (326 to convalescent plasma and 163 to control). The primary endpoint was not different between groups (83.7% vs 84.1%), and no statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints. Safety outcomes, including treatment-emergent adverse events and serious/severe adverse events, were similar between groups, and no transfusion-related TRALI cases were reported.

The passage is an introduction to the Tharisa plc Investor Presentation, including a poll and remarks by CEO Phoevos Pouroulis. It describes Tharisa’s phased transition from open-cast mining, which has been in place for 15 years, to underground mining as open-pit resources are depleted. The presentation is described as an opportunity to redefine resources, innovate, and empower future prospects, with an overview goal of unlocking multigenerational value through integrated mining. It states that the company has remained profitable over the past 11 years despite volatile commodity markets and other challenges.

The passage describes authors Arthur Santiago and Christiano Mattos and presents a Freirean dialogic educational activity implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic using the Discord platform. It explains that the pandemic caused urgent adaptations and worsened socioeconomic inequality in Brazil, with schools heavily affected. To respond, the authors developed a remote emergency activity in non-formal physics teacher education aimed at using scientific dissemination resources to develop student autonomy and dialogic interaction, analyzing the activity through Cultural Historical Activity Theory (CHAT). The theoretical sections outline CHAT concepts and treat dialogue as a human activity involving coordinated, targeted actions that supports emancipating, critical engagement. Methodologically, the activity was organized in stages around the problem of reopening schools, using Discord features (text and voice channels, group spaces, chat recording, and reduced teacher access management) to support student discussion, research, and collaborative production of a scientific dissemination project (including an infographic shared via WhatsApp). The conclusion argues that Discord enabled self-organization, increased student agency, and supported learners in connecting immediate pandemic-related problems with broader socio-political issues, fostering more complex conscious awareness through dialogic activity.

Libyan forces fighting in Benghazi have lost four men and have seen 10 wounded so far in December, according to a medical source. Three of the dead from the Libyan National Army were killed by snipers and one by a landmine amid daily clashes and occasional air strikes in the Khreibish district, where resistance continues. The fighting follows a broader conflict that developed after the 2011 fall of Muammar Gaddafi, and it is linked to Khalifa Haftar’s earlier declaration of victory in early July after a three-year campaign against Islamist militants.

The passage describes electronic gaming systems and methods, particularly stop-based bonus games that use one or more “bonus wheels” with multiple stop positions. In such bonus games, awards are grouped into higher-value first awards (e.g., jackpot awards) and lower-value second awards (e.g., credit prizes or non-jackpot awards). When a second-award stop position is selected, that stop position is instead associated with a first award for future bonus-game play, increasing opportunities to win first awards. The method includes initiating a bonus game based on a primary game outcome, displaying the bonus wheel and, when applicable, a secondary jackpot wheel with stop positions tied to credit prizes and jackpot awards, selecting stop positions, and replacing a credit prize association with a jackpot award association. It also describes related system components (displays, player input, credit input mechanisms, memory, and processors) and discusses game regulation and bonus-game triggers. The detailed description further explains that jackpot awards can persist over time and that gameplay can involve networked EGMs and servers, with example EGM hardware and configurations.

Fran Horowitz, CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch, says the retailer is not chasing “cool” but aims to be a long-lasting “lifestyle” brand. After her 2017 turnaround efforts, including shifting from a command-and-control style to giving employees more input and raising clothing quality, A&F reached nearly $5 billion in revenue and sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion between 2019 and 2024; combined A&F and Hollister sales are expected to top $5 billion this year. Horowitz said a key challenge is maintaining momentum through partnerships, including Abercrombie Kids selling at Macy’s and a new NFL fashion partnership featuring merchandise for all 32 leagues, offering exposure to millions of fans, including women, and supporting customer acquisition and brand awareness.

A veteran in Muskogee, Oklahoma, Rodney Orton, who has breathing problems, lost his mobility scooter after it malfunctioned. He contacted the VA and was told he needed another evaluation, with the next appointment in six weeks, despite a prior evaluation 15 years earlier. Orton was already admitted to a VA hospital for an unrelated issue, and Problem Solver Travis Guillory helped by contacting the VA to explain the situation. The VA then provided a scooter from its local inventory that fit Orton’s medical needs, delivering it to his room the next morning. Orton said he now has a scooter again.

The passage lists multiple issues and silicon/behavior deviations for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, including DMA, clocking, interrupt, register access, and system hang/failure conditions. Examples include incorrect rotating priority in DMA, UART register access being discarded or returning all ones during certain DMA modes, system hangs from I/O addresses at 10000h or higher, PIC interrupt handling problems with edge-configured interrupts during clock gating, ACPI PM1 register byte-access hang and PMC register write corruption from WORD/BYTE accesses, GLIU debug/error detection not functioning, SSMI event signaling failures, UDMA CRC corruption after IDE device termination, and multiple wake/standby or clock-gating related malfunctions. For many issues, the passage provides implications and suggested resolutions or usage restrictions (e.g., avoid specific access types/modes, change alignment, disable certain features, use alternative procedures or external circuitry).

Generative AI is described as already capable of solving many undergraduate physics problems and supporting student learning, prompting increased attention in physics education on how and where to use these tools. The paper presents a research-validated approach in which students “teach” generative AI by prompting it to produce physics simulations, then validate the simulations’ technical and scientific aspects and iteratively refine the prompts; students use the resulting simulations to explore physics further. The study is an extension of earlier simulation work (e.g., PhET) and investigates whether this AI-guided simulation-development approach affects conceptual understanding and student attitudes compared to using a prebuilt AI simulation or traditional physical laboratory equipment.

The study was conducted in spring 2025 at a large R1 public university in the western United States during the spring 2025 term in an introductory physics for life sciences course (no calculus). Data were collected from three quasi-experimental groups in the lab component: (1) a traditional physical lab using equipment to generate and measure electric potentials and map equipotential lines, (2) a prebuilt digital simulation created with AI tools and provided to students, and (3) an AI-engagement lab where students used Claude AI to generate, validate, and refine their own electric potential simulation. The lab focus was electric potential and equipotential lines. Across all groups, students completed a five-question multiple-choice conceptual assessment and a feedback questionnaire about the lab medium.

Statistical analysis showed that students’ immediate conceptual assessment scores (CQtot) differed significantly across the three lab types: the physical equipment group had lower median scores than both simulation-based groups, while the prebuilt simulation and AI-engaged groups did not significantly differ from each other. No significant differences were found across lab types on midterm and final exam scores. Student attitude results indicated more positive responses for both simulation conditions compared to the traditional physical lab on the set of survey questions, with one reported difference between the two simulation groups on a single attitude question. The discussion concludes that prompting, validating, and refining AI-generated simulations supports conceptual understanding at least as effectively as prebuilt simulations and better than physical equipment, while also engaging students with modeling and evaluation practices.
The passage says that some dogs are strongly attracted to toys, which may resemble human behavioral addictions. It describes dogs at play as possibly parallel to human addictions.

Stanford University researchers studied whether descriptive vegetable labels would increase college students’ vegetable intake. In a campus dining hall, nearly 28,000 students chose the same prepared zucchini and other vegetables under four different labeling styles. The most “great-tasting” label led diners to choose 25% more veggies than the basic-labeled version, with “inviting-sounding” labels resulting in 35% more scoops than positive “healthy” labels and 41% more than restrictive “healthy” labels. Students also piled more produce on their plates. The passage notes that taste influences buying decisions, citing an IFIC survey where 84% of those polled said taste is a key purchase driver versus 63% citing healthfulness. It suggests trying label- and taste-focused vegetable preparation at home and lists several recipes intended to help increase vegetable intake.

The passage describes images from the Hubble Space Telescope of nebulae. It highlights the Tarantula Nebula, also known as 30 Doradus, whose nickname comes from spindly, spidery gas filaments, and notes the Honeycomb Nebula in the lower left corner. The ESA says the Honeycomb Nebula’s bubble-like shape has baffled astronomers since its early 1990s discovery, and that 2010 research attributes its appearance to interactions between an older and a newer supernova and the viewing angle from Earth’s location in the galaxy. It also states that Hubble launched in 1990 and is a joint NASA-ESA project.

The President’s message to Congress states that the Nation has grown in strength and comfort and that problems are those of growth and progress requiring factual determination, common judgment, and conciliatory solutions. It describes efforts to strengthen foreign peace policy, including adherence to the Court of International Justice, naval arms limitation conferences, and diplomatic actions in Mexico, South America, and boundary issues, along with steps toward Latin American diplomatic strengthening. The message discusses national defense, rising costs, limits on war instruments under the Kellogg pact, and recommendations for Congress to consider actions to reduce mounting expenditures. It reports government finances as sound, outlines budget figures, and recommends tax rate reductions based on expected surpluses. The passage also covers foreign debt settlements, returning alien enemy property, economic conditions including a recovery after speculation-led crisis, agriculture and farm marketing initiatives, tariff principles and flexible revision, and public works and infrastructure topics such as buildings, waterways, flood control, highways, postal finances, aviation, rail consolidation, merchant marine policy, banking and power regulation, radio commission reorganization, and conservation. It further addresses social services, public health, federal prisons, immigration quotas, veterans’ benefits administration, civil service expansion, and broad governmental reorganization proposals, alongside prohibition and law enforcement measures, culminating in a conclusion focused on sustaining American ideals.

The passage discusses electroweak unification by combining weak and electromagnetic interactions. It notes two issues: the interaction strengths differ but can be mitigated by heavy gauge bosons, and the coupling structures differ (QED uses vector coupling, while weak interactions use vector–axial coupling via a \(1-\gamma^5\) term). It explains projecting spinors with \(1-\gamma^5\) to isolate left-handed components so the weak current can be written as a vector current, reducing complications such as mixed left–right terms and helicity changes in QED. The passage then rewrites currents using weak isospin duplets (with matrices \(\tau^\pm\) built from \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\)) to form charged weak currents that rotate neutrinos and electrons, and it identifies a neutral-current-like structure using \(\tau_3\). It introduces a hypercharge-related current using a relation analogous to the Gell-Mann–Nishijima equation, noting this produces additional right-handed coupling (relevant to Z boson interactions with right-handed electrons). The discussion further describes how to unify the interactions by treating weak currents as an isospin triplet \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) plus a singlet hypercharge component, then forming \(W^\pm\) from \(W_1,W_2\) and mixing the photon and Z boson from the triplet’s third component and the singlet \(B_\mu\), using relations involving the weak mixing angle \(\theta_W\).

Kevin Stefanski said there is no single thing Shedeur Sanders must do to earn the Browns’ backup quarterback job, emphasizing long-term player and quarterback development and avoiding roles players are not ready for. Rookie Dillon Gabriel remains the starter after his first appearance against London, England, and the backup spot remains open for Sanders and Bailey Zappe. Jerry Jeudy said Sanders has been doing what he needs as a pro and should take advantage of his opportunity when he gets it. The passage says Sanders is likely to stay in the emergency third-string role while awaiting a chance to start.

The passage provides five tips for starting with the board game Abalone on iOS and Android. It advises not to rush offensively, to plan moves ahead by considering where the board is likely to go, and to gain control of the centre for greater mobility and faster reaction. It also recommends shifting from defense to offense, noting that the first player to remove five of the opponent’s counters is likely to win. Finally, it suggests splitting the opponent’s counters into smaller groups and pushing them toward the edge while watching for counterattacks. The passage also mentions a newly released digital version from Asmodee Digital with updated graphics and additional tweaks.

The passage describes cryogenic storage systems that automate sample storage and retrieval in cryogenic environments. It contrasts typical manual rack/tray handling with embodiments that use a sample handling module (SHM) to automatically transfer individual samples between cryogenic storage vaults and removable cryogenic storage devices, while maintaining samples below a cryogenic temperature threshold (e.g., glass transition temperature). Samples may be organized and tracked using barcode scanning. The passage further describes a system architecture with one or more storage vaults, robotic transfer mechanisms, temperature and humidity control (including refrigerant coils and SHM humidity reduction), and components such as storage racks, trays, vertical shuttles, vault lids/covers, grippers, and docking interfaces for portable cryogenic workstations. It also includes detailed examples of sample transfer operations, retrieval processes, refrigeration and drying mechanisms, and a multi-stage disaster recovery method for handling jammed trays, plus discussion of a cryogenic camera module and alternative rack and vault designs.

Alzheimer disease is the leading cause of dementia and is characterized by amyloid beta (Aβ) plaques and tau tangles. While brain and CSF biomarkers can quantify these changes, their cost and invasiveness limit population use; plasma biomarkers may provide a more accessible alternative. The study analyzes plasma biomarkers—especially Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181—in Amish participants from Ohio and Indiana in the Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project (CAAMP). Plasma assays measured Aβ40, Aβ42, total tau (t-tau), and p-tau181, with quality control and statistical analyses including regression, ROC performance evaluation, and k-medoids clustering.

After quality control, cross-sectional data included 1,067 individuals. In univariate analyses, individuals with AD had significantly higher plasma p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181, while Aβ40, Aβ42, and Aβ42/Aβ40 did not differ significantly across diagnostic groups. In multivariate analyses, no overall statistically significant associations between plasma biomarkers and AD were found, but the association between p-tau181 and AD was modulated by APOE ε4 carriers, with stronger association among ε4 carriers. For cognitive preservation, plasma biomarkers showed opposite association patterns to AD, with Aβ42/Aβ40 and decreased p-tau181 and altered Aβ42/p-tau181 related to cognitive preservation.

For classification performance, the best model distinguishing AD from cognitively unimpaired used all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau, while adding individual biomarkers generally improved AD discrimination except for t-tau. Clustering based on Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 separated Amish individuals into two subgroups with distinct biomarker risk profiles, and a secondary analysis suggested three clusters. Overall, plasma biomarkers—particularly p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181—were concluded to be promising non-invasive indicators for distinguishing AD or cognitive impairment from cognitive unimpaired status in the Amish, with clustering potentially identifying different AD risk levels; longitudinal studies are recommended for validation.

The passage describes a patent application for deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carboline compounds, including continuation and related applications, and their pharmaceutical use. The invention concerns compounds containing trideuterated N-methyl and/or di-deuterated methylene adjacent to the N-methyl, intended to antagonize 5-HT2A receptors, inhibit the serotonin reuptake transporter, and modulate dopaminergic protein phosphorylation, with unexpectedly improved metabolic stability. It provides compound formulas (I–IV and variants), salt and deuterium-enrichment requirements, and pharmaceutical compositions including immediate-release and sustained-/delayed-release depot formulations using polymeric matrices, including specific polymers such as PLGA and poly(d,l-lactide-co-glycolide), as well as osmotic-controlled oral delivery system devices. Methods of treatment are provided for central nervous system disorders, including residual symptoms of psychosis (especially schizophrenia), sleep disorders, depression and anxiety, and various dementia- and Parkinson’s-associated conditions, including prophylaxis. The passage also describes combination therapy with other therapeutic agents. Finally, it includes examples and comparative studies in mice, rats, and dogs measuring parent and metabolite levels and pharmacokinetic parameters, reporting reduced metabolism (particularly to demethylated/alpha-oxidized amide metabolites) for the deuterated compounds compared with a non-deuterated reference compound.

Alex Ovechkin says he had a hard year mid-season, especially after moving to the right wing, but he is now “back on track” and happy. He thanks teammates, coaches, and family, and describes calling Alex Ovechkin immediately after the award. He says Adam helped him adjust to right wing and that coaching staff, partners, and everyone contributed. He also discusses playing through injuries, including a broken foot after the World Championship and later an MRI showing the injury, saying he played when he could skate and hold his stick. He reports his foot is okay, is working to get in good shape, and plans to start playing tennis soon. He closes by thanking the team for treating him well.

The passage discusses the team’s strengths and individual players’ performances during the playoffs. It emphasizes the effectiveness of the puck-pursuit style in wearing opponents down, winning faceoffs, creating offensive threats, and forcing opponents to defend. It praises Sidney Crosby as a complete player and inspiration, credits veteran players for leadership and maintaining composure under adversity, and highlights coaching messages focused on playing fast, making good puck decisions, and avoiding the opponent’s transition game. Other players are discussed positively: Evgeni Malkin for generating scoring chances; Phil Kessel for scoring ability and offensive threats; Conor for skating-related workload management; Bryan Rust for proactive play, forechecking, turnovers, and creating problems for opponents; and defense/lineup decisions based on situational strengths like puck-moving and offensive instincts. The passage also mentions defensive work against San Jose, the importance of balance across forward lines, and the idea of continual improvement through coaching and patience with player development.

The passage explains why the AEP (asymptotic equipartition property) and typical sets arise for discrete memoryless sources, starting from a log-probability random variable whose expected value is entropy. It describes how, using the weak law of large numbers, the sample average of the log pmf concentrates near the entropy, so most sequences are “typical” with probability approaching 1 as block length grows. It then summarizes key typical-set consequences: bounds on the number of typical sequences (about \(2^{nH(X)}\)), bounds on probabilities of typical sequences (about \(2^{-nH(X)}\)), and the small probability of atypical sequences. The discussion connects these results to source coding, fixed-length and conditional entropy, and shows that approaching \(H(X)\!-\!\epsilon\) bits per symbol leads to failure (error probability tending to 1).

The lecture then moves to Markov sources, defining ergodic Markov chains (aperiodic and with all states accessible from each other) and using steady-state/ergodicity to avoid dependence on when sequences start. It outlines how coding for Markov sources can be done using conditional entropy and \(n\)-to-variable-length coding.

Finally, it introduces the Lempel–Ziv universal compression ideas (LZ77/LZ78 context) as universal algorithms that do not assume known probabilities. It describes LZ77 in terms of maintaining a sliding window, finding the longest match for the upcoming unencoded string within the window, encoding the match length and position (and using an Elias unary-binary code for integers), and iterating while the window slides. The passage argues that when statistics match a Markov model, Lempel–Ziv can asymptotically achieve the conditional entropy rate, and it discusses practical considerations affecting window size and initialization.

The passage mentions that Peter Marks, former top vaccine regulator at the FDA, joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases after being forced to resign from the agency in March by health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., according to STAT’s Lizzy Lawrence. It also references other health-related headlines and notes that related article content is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

The passage describes the “Triangle Rotation” offense, which attacks the triangle zone using a simple three-player clockwise and counterclockwise rotation. It notes that, against a “Triangle & Two” defense where chasers focus on pass denial, the triangle zone rotations are usually weak. When initial inside rotations don’t produce a good shot, the offense includes actions such as a pop-out to an opposite elbow, a baseline cut feed, and a lob to a weakside cutter. Side screen actions are also outlined, including passes from the high post to a wing and subsequent screens by O4 and O1. The passage emphasizes that successful execution requires coordination, simplicity due to the offense being secondary, and preparation in fundamental principles for attacking zone defenses, including defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. It also advises scouting opponents for defensive reads, counters, and matchups, and adjusting alignments and entries during games.

Two U.S. government studies bombarded rats and mice with cellphone radiation and found a weak link to some heart tumors, including a small increase in an unusual heart tumor in male rats, but no significant problems in female rats or in mice. The studies did not provide hard evidence for concern about brain tumors, and regulators and some scientists said the findings do not change current guidance that cellphones are safe. The FDA said current safety limits are acceptable, and the lead researcher said typical cellphone use is far lower than the doses used; he also warned the animal results do not translate directly to human risk. Other scientists said the evidence is weak but noted some concern about the animals’ varied effects and criticized limits of the studies. Prior human research has generally found little evidence of increased cancer risk, and California issued guidance to reduce exposure if people are worried.

Michael Johnson has been named president of John Carroll University, effective July 1. He is currently provost and a professor of marketing at Babson College. The university’s board approved a five-year contract on Dec. 6, with salary details not released. Johnson, 61, replaces the Rev. Robert Niehoff, who plans to retire, and succeeds interim president Jeanne Colleran. The university highlights its emphasis on business education, including the Boler School of Business. Johnson has degrees from the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, and he previously taught at the University of Michigan and worked at Cornell University, serving as dean and provost at different points. The appointment followed a national search led by John Carroll alumnus Michael Merriman, and Johnson has an endorsement from Very Reverend Brian Paulson, S.J.

ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, has been released in multiple GPT versions and gained widespread attention since late 2022, including use in education. The passage summarizes scholars’ views on ChatGPT in education, noting potential benefits such as improved learning, collaboration, accessibility, personalized feedback, and assessment support, alongside concerns including plagiarism/cheating, lack of deep understanding, bias, inaccuracy, and false information delivered with confidence. It reports a systematic review aimed at assessing the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT responses, using a replicable search strategy across databases, screening studies by eligibility criteria, and reviewing 18 studies with thematic analysis. The included studies found that ChatGPT can produce coherent writing and can pass some undergraduate exams, but it shows limitations in scientific and complex problem-solving, calculation tasks, depth of understanding, higher-order thinking, and consistent correctness. The study concludes that ChatGPT has potential across disciplines but is not fully correct or relevant in scientific contexts, and it suggests validation, redesigned assessment, and development of guidelines/policies for constructive use.

The passage describes a study assessing pregnant women’s awareness and attitudes toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) and factors influencing their decision to consider it in Ethiopia. It notes that although analgesia during labor is approved and epidural analgesia is considered effective, LEA use remains low in many developing regions, including Ethiopia, due to lack of awareness, misconceptions, and fears. The study was an institution-based cross-sectional design conducted from June 3 to August 30, 2024, at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, with 230 third-trimester women included in analysis (out of 267 participants). Results showed 78% had heard of LEA, but healthcare providers were rarely the main information source, and only 34% received explanations during ANC follow-up. While 47% believed LEA was effective for pain relief, only 14.3% were willing to consider it during delivery; main concerns included fear of side effects for the mother and baby, interference with labor, and additional cost. The decision to use LEA was significantly associated with education level, family monthly income, perceptions of potential harm to the fetus, and perceptions of LEA pain-relief effectiveness. The study concludes that despite relatively high basic awareness, many participants remain hesitant, highlighting the need for comprehensive health education and counseling during antenatal care.

A new study by researchers from King’s College London analyzed 49 studies with 266,939 participants and found that people who regularly exercised had lower odds of developing depression than those who did little activity. The protective association applied to youths, adults, and elderly participants across every continent, even after accounting for factors such as body mass index, smoking, and physical health conditions. The researchers call for prioritizing physical activity across the lifespan and plan further studies on how different types and amounts of activity affect future depression risk.

The passage describes the “Four Down” offense, primarily used to take the last shot in a period but also used as a spread offense for teams with a talented ballhandler. It is called quickly by the ballhandler signaling all four fingers downward. In the basic alignment, non-ball handlers line up along the baseline with the best shooters in the corners, creating space for a one-on-one isolation for the ballhandler, similar to Dean Smith’s “Four Corner” offense. Primary reads include driving or pulling up for a jumper, with posts crashing the boards and corners ready for three-point opportunities; drop passes and kick-out passes are used based on defender help. In continuity, if the ballhandler is in trouble or the five-second closely guarded rule applies, the corners pop out to receive pressure release passes and can take over the isolation role. The passage also lists “Crunch Time Specials”: Mid Screen O4 or O5 drives off a mid screen for a layup or jumper and can create passing options; Triple Base Screen sets stagger, baseline screens for O2 with quick actions based on defensive switching; and Misdirection Double uses a baseline double screen to free O4, with options to feed, drive, or pass to a rolling teammate.

The passage describes the 2-3 zone defense as a commonly used alignment that keeps big players inside to protect the basket area and defend against dribble penetration, and that is effective versus teams with poor outside shooting but vulnerable to teams with good outside shooting. It outlines general defensive positioning, basic shifts based on where the ball is (middle, wings, corners), and principles for rebounding and pass denial. It also covers adjustments and variations including wing shift options, defending against ball reversal, a 1-1-3 variation, tandem options, advanced trap options (corner trap, point traps, and automatic wing trap), and specific “footer” adjustments to double or triple-team an outstanding or tall low post player using pass denial, backside support, and triple-teaming triggers when the low post receives the ball.

Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, will invest $2 billion in Polymarket, valuing the prediction market at $9 billion. ICE will also distribute Polymarket’s data and the two companies will work together on tokenization initiatives using blockchain. Polymarket, founded in 2020 and using blockchain technology, previously gained traction during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, and trading volume peaked near $400 million in November.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Caesars Entertainment Corporation (NASDAQ:CZR) shares from a buy to a hold rating. The passage describes Caesars as a gaming company operating casino resorts under brands including Harrah’s, Caesars, and Horseshoe, with facilities such as land-based and managed casinos, racetrack and casino combinations, hotels and convention space, restaurants, and non-gaming entertainment. Other analysts issued varied ratings and price targets, and the stock had an average rating of Buy with a consensus price target of $14.39. On Monday midday it traded down 0.76% to $13.00, with 4,884,465 shares exchanged. The company’s 12-month low was $6.70 and high was $13.60. Caesars reported quarterly EPS of ($0.21) versus a $0.26 consensus estimate, and revenue of $1 billion versus $2.11 billion expected. The passage also notes institutional ownership and describes Caesars’ segments and services.

The sense resistor detects ripple current from a transformer and initiates shutdown of the switching cycle if the converter’s peak current exceeds a set current limit. The CS pin voltage threshold is about 1 V, and the shutdown current should be above the maximum expected current, with the max current limit determined by Equation 52. The document also describes test setups for voltage stress across main switching MOSFETs and measurements of output voltage ripple and transients using a 48-V input and 10-A load/current. It further provides guidance on the UC1825B-SP operating input range (10 V to 30 V) and recommends low-EMI inductors and specific PCB layout practices, including how to route feedback traces, place input/output capacitors and compensation components close to the IC, and design power and ground planes to reduce EMI and noise.

The email forwards multiple news articles and columns about California’s 2001 electricity crisis. The Dow Jones column argues California’s utilities and government have focused on financial solvency while underestimating a large summer electricity shortage, citing factors like lower generator capacity, reduced hydroelectric output, power sold out of state, generator outages, and skepticism about peaker capacity. Other articles describe statewide and regional supply problems across the West, disputes over building small “peaker” plants, and survey results showing small businesses view the crisis as harming California’s business climate. Additional coverage discusses Gov. Gray Davis’s changing role in the crisis, conservation and efficiency measures, spot power prices affected by plant outages and weather, and legislative concerns over Davis’s plan to buy investor-owned utilities’ transmission lines.

The passage describes a legal dispute in which Community Board 7 of Manhattan challenged the denial of its Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) request for certain documents related to a proposed “Trump City” development under the New York City Charter’s Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP). The issue on appeal was whether the community board, as a legislatively created entity, had the capacity to bring a CPLR article 78 proceeding to compel disclosure, not whether it had standing. The Court concluded that the board lacked capacity because neither the Charter nor ULURP provisions expressly authorized community boards to sue for document disclosure, and the legislative terms and history indicated no intent to grant such authority. The Court held that the board’s advisory ULURP responsibilities did not imply the power to compel broad document disclosure through judicial proceedings. Accordingly, it reversed the lower courts’ decisions and dismissed the petition, despite FOIL’s standing provision for persons denied access to records.

Cboe CEO Ed Tilly said bitcoin futures’ generally smooth launch on Cboe could support progress toward other cryptocurrency-related products, such as options and ETFs, though U.S. regulators may take longer to warm to proliferation. He said the most-active contract was volatile, with a 20% surge that triggered a five-minute trading halt, but trading otherwise worked as intended. Cboe had traded nearly 3,700 contracts by early Monday afternoon, with about 20 trading firms participating. Fund managers REX Shares, Van Eck Associates, and First Trust Advisors sought SEC permission for bitcoin ETFs after the launch. Cboe plans to wait for a couple of settlements on one-month futures before pursuing new crypto-derivative products, and it has appealed an SEC ruling that blocked a Cboe-listed bitcoin ETF tied to Gemini for settlement pricing. Tilly also said he expects other cryptocurrencies to follow and noted Cboe’s website briefly went down due to unusually high traffic.

The passage describes how to power down and initialize the ADS9803, including using the PWDN pin or setting PD_CH in register 0xC0, and performing a register-write initialization sequence after connecting a free-running sampling clock. It also outlines configuration changes from defaults, including settings for analog input ranges and bandwidth, data interface lanes, and a speed-boost mode that allows up to 8 MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair while other channels are idle. SPI register access is explained for writing and reading using register bank selection and read-enable/mode bits. It further covers using multiple ADS9803 devices in a daisy-chain SPI configuration for register write and read operations, including configuring DAISY_CHAIN_LEN and the required SPI frame counts. Later sections list additional register field descriptions and provide general application information and development/support/disclaimer text.

The passage describes Premium Subscription features, including the Lex column (a daily guide to corporate and financial stories), EM Squared, Martin Sandbu’s Free Lunch (a succinct daily take on global economics), the FT Newsmine blog (a weekly email abstracting essential macroeconomic data), the daily FT ePaper, and exclusive weekly emails. It also details “Editor’s Choice,” an exclusive weekly newsletter with insights from Lionel Barber.

The device supports using an external 4.096V reference source with an internal buffer by programming the INTREF_DIS bit in RANGE_SEL_REG. In external reference mode, the external reference is applied to the REFIO pin, which functions as an input, and the buffered output appears at REFCAP with specified minimum and decoupling capacitors to REFGND. The buffer output is stated to be stable across –40°C to +125°C, with specified temperature drift values. The passage also describes ADC transfer characteristics (straight-binary output), alarm functionality (input and AVDD alarms with thresholds, hysteresis, flags, and readout behavior), multiSPI device operating modes and connection topologies (single device and daisy-chain), general programming/data frame behavior, output data word construction with selectable flags, and data transfer protocols (legacy single/dual SDO and source-synchronous modes). It further includes register map descriptions for configuration and alarm-related registers and concludes with application, power supply recommendations (decoupling and low-power modes), and various disclaimers and notices.

Investors sold shares of PPL Corporation (NYSE:PPL) on Wednesday, with $16.41 million flowing into the stock on an uptick and $46.29 million flowing out on a downtick, for a net outflow of $29.88 million. The stock rose $0.19 to close at $37.65. Analysts’ actions included Zacks cutting PPL from “buy” to “hold,” ValuEngine upgrading from “hold” to “buy,” BidaskClub upgrading from “sell” to “hold,” and Jefferies restating a “buy” rating with a $43.50 price target; the consensus rating was “Hold” with a $38.94 target. PPL reported Q2 EPS of $0.52 versus a $0.50 consensus and revenue of $1.73 billion versus $1.79 billion, with net margin of 22.08% and return on equity of 15.96%. The company paid a quarterly dividend of $0.395 to shareholders of record on September 8, with a $1.58 annualized dividend and 4.24% yield. The passage also lists insider and institutional ownership activity and describes PPL as a utility holding company serving electricity and natural gas customers in several states and the United Kingdom.

Europe faces challenges from an ageing population that vary across EU member countries and are often addressed with ambitious but insufficiently grounded strategic plans. The passage proposes digital wellness services delivered over omnivore platforms on mobile smartphones to keep “young elderly” (about ages 60–75) healthy, active, and independent into the 75+ group, aiming to reduce health and social care costs. It argues that proactive prevention should focus on 60–75-year-olds and that interventions can be developed and scaled using mobile and smart phone platforms, cloud analytics, and commercial ecosystems that sustain the services.

The program described includes collecting data from daily routines and other sources, producing understandable summaries for users, and supporting the formation of wellness routines through tools designed with users rather than for them. A four-dimension wellness framework is used (intellectual, physical, social, emotional), intended to reflect impairment dimensions and allow compensatory trade-offs among wellness areas. The BeWell research program in Finland (2014–2016) is presented as developing and testing such services, using the Wellmo omnivore platform and a cloud service platform for analytics. Preliminary empirical work with 101 young elderly respondents from the Åland Islands reports that they often use smart mobile phones and apps, consider wellness issues important—especially intellectual challenges—and provides guidelines for selecting user groups.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 26, 2018 to report its first quarter 2018 financial results. The filing states that the announcement was made on April 26, 2018, with the press release included as Exhibit 99.1 and additional information regarding non-GAAP financial measures included as Exhibit 99.2. The report is signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speakers discuss a playoff series they felt went well after getting success earlier and scoring goals. They emphasize playing as a group, sticking to opportunities, and contributions from players including Patrick Kane and Brent Seabrook, as well as Bryan Bickell’s physical play and its effect on momentum. They describe the games as close, including an overtime win that evened the series, and they talk about offensive and defensive execution, backchecking, opening the ice, and creating shots and scoring chances. They also mention confidence and focus regarding specific opponents and teammates, and the importance of staying disciplined in all zones for upcoming games.

FreeNAS released version 11, intended to avoid bugs that affected version 10 (“Corral”) and led many users to roll back to 9.x. Version 11 is based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE and includes the bhyve hypervisor to host virtual machines. Docker support from Corral is paused for now but planned for a future point release, while FreeBSD jails remain available. It adds compatibility with AWS S3 object storage, integration with messaging tools like Slack or HipChat, and the ability for admins to choose which services start at boot. A new Angular-based GUI is included but is still in beta, and forum chatter says testers reported few issues across four release candidates.

SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants were first detected in November 2020 in England and India, respectively, carrying spike mutations associated with more efficient binding to the human ACE2 receptor and/or escape from antibody neutralization. Alpha and Delta were estimated to be more transmissible than the ancestral strain and Alpha, respectively, and both spread globally to become dominant during 2021. Vietnam initially controlled community transmission through early border and travel restrictions, contact tracing with mass testing and quarantine, and intensive public communication, but importations of Alpha followed by Delta in early 2021 led to a nationwide outbreak with over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths by end of 2021. The study used genomic surveillance and phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses to examine spatiotemporal evolution of Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam in 2021, describing two phases of the 2021 epidemic, sequencing results, and findings that Delta AY.57 was dominant and associated with specific regional introduction and spread patterns, alongside observed changes in genetic diversity and selection signals.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. cut its position in DeVry Education Group Inc. by 9.6% in the third quarter, holding 499,104 shares worth $11,509,000 after selling 53,234 shares. Other institutional investors reported changes including UBS Asset Management Americas (up 10.6% to 41,019 shares), M&T Bank Corp (new position around $229,000), PNC Financial Services Group (up 637.7% to 83,277 shares), Retirement Systems of Alabama (up 0.4% to 73,120 shares), and KBC Group NV (up 82.6% to 6,991 shares). DeVry shares traded down 0.16% to $31.20 with 1,126,573 shares exchanged; the firm reported 50-day and 200-day moving averages of $30.31 and $24.01, respectively, and a market cap of $1.95 billion. In its latest earnings release (quarterly data on Nov. 1), DeVry reported EPS of $0.39 (missing $0.41) and revenue of $449.90 million. Analysts predict $2.55 EPS for the current fiscal year. The company also paid a semiannual dividend of $0.18 per share (yield 1.29%). Analysts’ consensus rating is “Hold” with an average target price of $26.11.

Ostersunds were drawn to play Arsenal in the Europa League last 32. Ostersunds, led by Graham Potter, have won three promotions since 2011 and qualified for European football by winning the domestic cup last season. After three qualifying rounds, they finished second in Group J and will face Arsenal, whose first European meeting with a Swedish side since 1999-2000 will aim to keep them unbeaten. Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, Celtic, and Napoli dropped from the Champions League group stage and will play Atalanta, Copenhagen, Zenit, and RB Leipzig respectively.

The passage describes marijuana (Cannabis sativa) and its cannabinoids, including CBD and THC, and notes that cannabis is widely used globally for psychoactive purposes. It summarizes evidence that cannabinoids and the endocannabinoid system may influence inflammation and immune suppression, and links the gut microbiota to host metabolism and gut-brain communication, including roles in anxiety and depression-like behavior. The text reports that cannabis use and endocannabinoid supplements are associated with changes in microbial composition and health outcomes in various conditions, while also noting potential negative effects and adverse events. It outlines a systematic review and attempted meta-analysis registered on PROSPERO, using PRISMA guidelines and searches in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane (through July 20, 2022), with inclusion/exclusion criteria focused on human peer-reviewed studies on cannabinoids and microbiome changes. After screening, 9 studies were included, and the review concludes that MJ use/endocannabinoid supplements and gastrointestinal microbiota may each contribute to the manifestation of pain and other outcomes, though the limited data prevented meta-analysis.

Chinese textile firms in Dandong are increasingly using North Korean factories to make cheaper clothes, which are then labelled “Made in China” and exported worldwide. Traders and businesses say U.N. sanctions punish North Korea for missile and nuclear programmes but do not ban textile exports, and that Chinese suppliers ship fabrics and raw materials to North Korean factories for garment assembly and export. Reports cited include Rip Curl’s apology after some ski gear was found to be made in North Korea and claims that production in North Korea can save up to 75 percent. The passage says North Korea’s textiles were its second-largest export in 2016, and that Chinese exports to North Korea rose nearly 30 percent in the first half of the year, largely driven by textile materials and other labour-intensive goods. It also describes North Korea’s reliance on overseas labour and gives examples of wages and working conditions for North Korean workers employed in factories in China.

Glenner Town Square in Chula Vista is an 8,500-square-foot, miniature 1950s-style downtown built inside a light-industrial building on Main Street, designed for Alzheimer’s and dementia patients. It opened in April 2018 and features 13 storefronts around a faux grass-lined park with benches, with interactive 3-dimensional building experiences such as watching an old movie with popcorn, eating lunch at a diner, visiting a library, shopping, working on a 1959 Ford T-Bird, visiting a pet store, getting checkups from a nurse, and visiting swaddled baby dolls in a hospital. Reservations, fees, and schedules are available at glenner.org. The passage also lists other licensed adult day programs for cognitively impaired adults in San Diego County, including details on services, hours, locations, and contact information.

The passage expresses hope and excitement about being in the finals for the third time with different teams. The speaker wants to win and “touch the trophy,” aiming for a better finish than in recent years. They describe learning from not winning previously, increased enthusiasm for the new series, and a great team. They say the building was sold out, fans were very enthusiastic, and the city is a “true hockey town.” The speaker also notes their free-agent signing in Chicago, a strong season run through hard work, and expects a tight playoff series against the Flyers due to their strong, experienced team.

Ben Rice was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, southeast of Boston, and attended high school in nearby Dedham. He played baseball at Noble and Greenough School after starting with hockey as a child. Rice went on to play college baseball at Dartmouth, where he had limited plate appearances in 2019, a short 2020 season, and an Ivy League cancellation of 2021; he totaled 110 collegiate plate appearances before being drafted by the Yankees in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft. In 2025, Rice earned a more regular role with the Yankees, hitting 26 home runs over 138 games while splitting time among first base, catcher, and designated hitter, and he hit an early two-run home run in Game 2 of the 2025 Wild Card Series.

The passage is a State of the Union speech asserting that America has improved and will continue improving into the 1980s. It says bipartisan cooperation helped stop a decline marked by economic and governmental problems, with renewed energy and optimism. It highlights reductions in inflation, tax changes including across-the-board cuts and indexing, increased real after-tax income, job gains, and economic deregulation. It outlines goals for the decade: steady economic growth through limiting government spending and regulations and reducing deficits; developing space, including a permanently manned space station; strengthening traditional community values and education through measures like a National Commission on Excellence in Education; and pursuing a lasting meaningful peace based on democratic principles and defense. It also discusses budget actions, tax code simplification, environmental initiatives, crime reduction, education proposals such as tuition tax credits, and policies on fair housing, women’s rights, child care, and enterprise zones. The speech includes remarks on peace efforts internationally, especially with the Soviet Union, and honors examples of service and volunteers.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the third consecutive quarter, moving it to a range of 1 percent to 1.25 percent. It cited continued strength in job growth and dismissed renewed weakness in inflation “for now,” saying the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth has been rising moderately this year. The Fed acknowledged inflation has weakened and lowered its forecast for this year’s price increases to 1.6 percent from 1.9 percent in March, while keeping next year’s inflation forecast at 2 percent. The article says the combination of strong job growth and weak inflation prompted the change, and that some officials now predict unemployment could fall below 4 percent, the lowest level in a generation.

The passage discusses how infectious diseases have historically affected human civilization and cites factors linked to epidemics, including agriculture, animal domestication, and population density. It describes mathematical approaches such as SIR and SEIR models, and the importance of interventions like border control, event cancellation, and quarantine, especially when vaccines and medicines are unavailable. The study developed and analyzed a mathematical model to evaluate a screening-isolation strategy in a semi-isolated community, considering assumptions about pathogen influx, screening efficiency, recovery/death capacity, and time lag. Theoretical analysis and computer simulations suggest the strategy can control spread under certain conditions (e.g., with sufficiently high screening efficiency and frequent screening), but it may fail when reproduction is high or screening is infrequent. Results also indicate strict border control is necessary, as cumulative infections increase with larger influx scales. The conclusion states that regular, periodic screening in semi-isolated communities without vaccines and medications can help control transmission, and that screening frequency and efficiency, along with migration rate, influence infection size.

Tom Brady’s agent, Don Yee, said Patriots fans can expect Brady to return in 2018 and play beyond his current contract. Yee stated Brady has two seasons remaining, earning $14 million plus a $1 million roster bonus each season, and that Brady intends to play into his mid-40s or until he feels he can no longer perform at a championship level. Yee added that Brady has been customizing his preparation and evolving his training methods despite not participating in the start of voluntary offseason workouts amid retirement rumors. Patriots owner Robert Kraft said there is no issue with Brady’s current contract and the team is not focused on negotiating a more lucrative deal.

MultiChoice and its DStv service have been affected by Netflix’s popularity in South Africa. DStv Premium subscribers have declined from 1.962m to 1.921m, and the average revenue per customer has fallen from R353 to R344. MultiChoice CEO Calvo Mawela says Premium is not expensive for the full entertainment package and that customers who switch to streaming do not return to broadcast TV. He says a streaming-only DStv package is being considered, but the main obstacle is securing streaming rights for all DStv entertainment content. MultiChoice also appealed to ICASA to avoid over-regulating pay-TV, warning that excessive regulation could lead to job losses to international streaming companies like Netflix and Amazon.

CoreWeave (CRWV) has rebounded over the past month on bullish AI sentiment and announced AI deal wins, including $22.4B OpenAI and $14.2B Meta deals that diversify its customer base, though Microsoft remains a significant revenue concentration risk. The passage also raises concerns about sustainability due to aggressive capex and debt-funded growth, especially with a high forward revenue multiple. Despite strong momentum, it suggests shares may cool off as optimism appears priced in and risks remain elevated.

Parents and extended family members of Joppatowne High School’s 2018 graduate Amya Hill wore bright purple T-shirts with her face as they gathered after the school’s 45th commencement ceremony. Hill’s mother Carolyn Hill and her father Jeremy Hill, both retired from the Army, said family traveled from Colorado and Georgia. More than 130 seniors in white and purple caps and gowns received diplomas at APG Federal Credit Union Arena at Harford Community College. Principal Pamela Zeigler said about 95 percent of the 138-member class plans to go to college, technical school, the military, or law enforcement. Hill said she would study nursing at Albany State University in Georgia and encouraged students to keep pushing. Other graduates shared plans for an electrician’s apprenticeship and reflected on community support from people including Hazel Morgan. Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson delivered remarks and life lessons, and additional officials and speakers urged students to focus on future goals and the examples of people who served others.

The speaker says they will not analyze the previous game and will instead analyze the upcoming game as a team. They describe the Calgary team as having the pressure because Canada is watching and the cup is expected to be won, while they say their team’s pressure is less and their focus is to win one minute at a time and extend the series in an elimination game. They mention staying in the area after the game for rest and breakfast before traveling to the next game. The speaker also notes that a top player on Calgary should be credited for big plays, and that the outcome depends on which team makes more big plays at key times. They say they felt good and are anxious to see how Calgary responds, discussing how teams can mentally struggle when anticipating events around the cup.

A letter taped to the door of assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary, who was abruptly fired last week while involved in a terrorism prosecution in the Eastern District of Virginia, said a false social media post appeared to have led to his termination. The letter warned that DOJ leadership removing career officials from U.S. attorney’s offices and the FBI made America less safe, and said justice for Americans killed and injured by enemies should not depend on what DOJ leadership sees in their social media feed. Ben’Ary’s firing followed pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly’s suggestion that he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco. The letter also said Ben’Ary’s firing showed DOJ leadership was more concerned with punishing perceived enemies than protecting national security.

The passage describes theoretical work on small-angle (~2°) twisted bilayer MoTe2, where strong correlations in flat topological bands can host non-Abelian fractional Chern or fractional spin Hall insulators. The authors identify evidence for an additional intermediate quantum phase between a ferromagnetic Chern insulator and a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator at half-filled second moiré bands (hole filling νh = 3, approximately 2° twist). Using exact diagonalization of a continuum model including both valleys and screened Coulomb interactions, they find that this intermediate phase has a singly degenerate paramagnetic ground state and exhibits a continuous transition to the fractional spin Hall insulator near dc,2. Multiple diagnostics indicate that the intermediate state is superconducting: pairing tendency and intervalley entanglement increase in the intermediate regime, binding energy is negative and maximized there, the pair density matrix shows a dominant eigenvalue, and the superfluid stiffness is finite and peaks near dc,1 before falling to zero near dc,2. The superconducting order parameter is time-reversal symmetric and identified as a nodal extended s-wave (A1 representation), and the transition is formulated in an effective field theory where topology and symmetry change simultaneously. The authors further argue that realistic band geometry (including non-uniform quantum geometry) is important for stabilizing superconductivity, and conclude that higher moiré bands may provide a platform to explore interplay among superconductivity, strong correlations, geometry, and topology.

The passage explains that over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves two parties trading financial instruments directly without a centralized exchange, typically via electronic dealer networks. OTC markets are decentralized, lack physical locations, and often involve less liquid or specialized assets, including small-company stocks, bonds, derivatives, and commodities. OTC trades may have less public price disclosure and less stringent regulation than exchanges, which can increase counterparty risk, liquidity premiums, and the likelihood of fraud or market manipulation, with penny stocks described as especially risky. The passage also discusses that OTC markets can be used for companies that cannot meet exchange listing requirements to raise capital, and that ADRs can be traded via OTC markets. It cites negative performance outcomes for OTC stocks, including studies reporting average losses and high failure rates, and generally advises against OTC stock investment or short-term trading, especially day trading, due to slippage from thin trading and higher costs.

“Brainsaver” classes are part of a 12-week course offered by OptumCare in the Valley to support brain health as people age.
