The classes include physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, educational material, socialization, and guidance on foods for the brain, and are described as a holistic approach that may help reduce chances of Alzheimer’s Disease. Students, aged from the mid-50s to late-80s, report noticing benefits. Classes are offered at Deer Valley, Goodyear, and Chandler at listed times on Mondays/Wednesdays or Tuesdays/Thursdays.

Top Democrats and Republicans met with President Donald Trump at the White House, and Vice President JD Vance said they are headed for a federal government shutdown, citing that Democrats “won’t do the right thing.” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said there are “very large differences” but added he believes Trump heard Democrats’ objections. Both sides continued to blame each other for a potential shutdown starting Wednesday. Republicans want a continuing resolution stopgap to keep funding at current levels until late November, while Democrats want it to include funding and protection for key measures, including an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits due to lapse at year’s end. Earlier Senate efforts to avert a shutdown failed, and Republicans accused Democrats of refusing a “clean” resolution, while Democrats said they were shut out of the process.

Moina Shaiq, a Fremont, California mother and grandmother, created an advertising campaign after friends were afraid to ask her about her religion. Her newspaper ad, “Questions and answers about being Muslim,” led to her “Meet a Muslim” program after about 100 people attended a coffee house event. She has since spoken at dozens of libraries, coffee shops, pizza parlors, churches, service clubs, and private homes, and traveled with the program to Arizona and Atlanta. Shaiq’s talks address misconceptions and stereotypes, including topics like hijab and niqab, Sunni and Shia differences, women’s rights in Islam, and what it is like to be an American Muslim. The passage also describes similar outreach efforts after 9/11 and notes rising anti-Muslim crimes, threats to Shaiq, and far-right concerns. Muslim advocates say local engagement can counter Islamophobia, while some critics argue that time may be better spent on policy change. Shaiq says her goal is to educate Americans that Muslims are “humans just like” they are.

The passage describes a wireless communication disclosure focused on transmitting and receiving a sounding reference signal (SRS). It proposes configuring and/or indicating a guard period for SRS transmission/reception, particularly when SRS is adjacent to other uplink transmissions such as PUCCH or PUSCH. The guard period is used to manage antenna switching, avoid distortion, and address collisions between the guard period and other uplink channels. The guard period configuration may be provided via higher-layer signaling and can include guard timing position, number of symbols, and rules for priority when overlap occurs, including dropping SRS symbols or the other uplink transmission depending on priority. It also discusses how to handle collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets, using priority rules and potentially shifting or retransmitting SRS resource sets to later slots.

Tensor Cores are specialized units for tensor/matrix operations used in deep learning. Turing Tensor Cores provide speed-ups for matrix computations central to neural network training and inferencing. They include an enhanced design for inferencing with new INT8 and INT4 precision modes that tolerate quantization without requiring FP16. Turing Tensor Cores introduce deep learning AI capabilities to GeForce gaming PCs and Quadro workstations, and they power Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS). DLSS uses a deep neural network to extract features from a rendered scene and combine details from multiple frames to produce a final image, using fewer input samples than techniques such as TAA.

A man, Zsolt Lakatos, sentenced in his absence to 13 years in prison for violently shaking his four-month-old baby, was arrested after hiding for eight days. He had breached bail by failing to return to court on a Monday after being sent home for the weekend. Brought before Liverpool Crown Court, he admitted breaching bail and was sentenced to an additional 10 days in prison. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered catastrophic brain injuries, including bleeding on the brain, multiple fractures, and retinal haemorrhaging, with ongoing care and medication needs for life.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission reporting that on January 3, 2016 it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information is intended to be furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01 and is not deemed “filed” for certain purposes under the Securities Exchange Act. The report was signed on January 4, 2016 by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel.

The speaker discusses coaching in Chicago, emphasizing commitment, improving daily, and open, direct communication with a core group. They describe coach Qunenneville’s approach, including balancing matters and challenging players to stay accountable while maintaining consistent lines of communication. The passage focuses on the team’s goaltending situation, stating that Scottie came in and played an amazing game after a goalie change, while Corey returned to the net and was described as rock solid, with competition and support between the goalies. It also covers player roles and trust, including progression and timely goals, a shift toward a stronger shot mentality, and the importance of defensive responsibility, puck handling, and safe positional play. The speaker highlights the need for faster play as a series progresses, noting the team rises to the challenge against strong opponents, and concludes with praise for playoff performances and play recognition, patience, and imagination with the puck.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defensive coverage with 0 safeties over the top, where defenders have clear assignments to cover eligible offensive receivers or apply pressure through stunts and blitzing. Defenses use Cover 0 to bring maximum blitz pressure while keeping receivers covered, often by adding up to 6 players to the line of scrimmage. It is described as strong against the run-pass option because receivers are covered and defenders focus on their assigned targets rather than the quarterback. The passage also lists strengths against short routes (e.g., hitch or slant) and says it can work against long routes due to the pressure sent. However, Cover 0 is characterized as high-risk/high-reward: if a defender is beaten there is no help, and it can be vulnerable to draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays such as crossing routes that can create separation. It is also referred to as “middle of the field open,” with the middle deep post left uncovered. The article outlines general Cover 0 techniques for different defensive roles and mentions variations like “Rat” coverage (rushing 5 and leaving a free player to limit crossing routes and quarterback runs) and dropping defensive linemen into coverage to add wrinkles, including handling screens or flares while still allowing blitz pressure.

Astronomers report that Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object passing through the inner solar system, likely originated from a two-star binary system. Alan Jackson and his team say it was probably ejected as planets formed and has been wandering interstellar space for a long time. The red-tinged object was discovered in October and is estimated to be about 1,300 feet (400 meters) long, traveling away from Earth and the sun at more than 16 miles (26 km) per second. Previous reporting cited that it is tumbling, likely from a collision that kicked it out of its home system. Researchers conclude that close binary star systems may be a source of many interstellar objects.

The passage discusses education’s Latin roots (“educere” to draw out and “educare” to train or mold) and argues for holistic success involving mind, matter, and spirit rather than material or intellectual wealth alone. It describes Indian sages and thinkers—including Tagore, Osho, Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo—who emphasized spiritual growth, self-development, and integrated curricula. The passage links these ideas to contemporary policy directions such as India’s NEP 2020 and UN SDG 4.7, and to efforts like ISEE.  

The study uses two methods: a literature review to identify holistic education dimensions and a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review (using Scopus and Semantic Scholar, limited to English-language original articles before 2021). It validates the LIBRE/EMC² holistic education framework in the Indian higher education context, identifying four core dimensions—empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry—through thematic analysis. The results highlight the need for systematic, culturally grounded assessment and suggest that classroom-level evaluation can inform institutional practice and policy through iterative feedback. The study concludes that identifying these dimensions supports their application in educational practice, standardized curriculum development, and culturally sensitive assessment tools, while noting limitations related to database scope and excluded journals.

Soybean May futures closed higher week-on-week due to diminishing supplies and intact demand for crushing supported by encouraging soy meal exports. Physical market supplies decreased in the first 10 days of April compared to the previous month, with Agmarknet arrivals of 97,040 tonnes from Apr 1–15 versus about 1,64,286 tonnes in March for the same period. The outlook expects soybean prices to trade higher on expected demand from crushers and diminishing supplies, though adequate supplies and cheap imports could pressure prices; strong domestic demand may keep prices supported. The report also notes that Ref Soy oil and CPO may trade higher due to a technical rebound, alongside a disclaimer about the views expressed by external experts.

A study from the University of Maryland found that young adults who regularly consumed highly caffeinated energy drinks over time were significantly more likely to use cocaine and non-medically use prescription stimulants, and to be at risk for alcohol use disorder at age 25. More than half of the 1,099 participants (51.4%) were in a “persistent trajectory” group who sustained energy drink consumption. Compared with a “non-use trajectory” group, those in an “intermediate trajectory” group (17.4%) had increased risk of cocaine and non-medical prescription stimulant use, while those in a “desisting trajectory” group and the non-use group were not at higher risk. The researchers said they controlled for demographics, sensation-seeking, other caffeine intake, and prior substance use. The study was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence.

Consumer advocates reported “glitches” during the final days of Obamacare sign-ups, including an incorrect “no plans available” message in Illinois after some applications for financial assistance through HealthCare.gov. An administration official said the issue was resolved and that HealthCare.gov is reaching out to affected consumers, though advocates reported similar responses earlier. The last day to enroll for subsidized private coverage in 39 states using HealthCare.gov is Friday, with the heaviest enrollment expected Thursday and Friday and potential website slowdowns and long call center hold times. For hurricane-affected areas, people can apply for extensions to Dec. 31 by contacting the call center. The article also notes that enrollment time runs out for most consumers on Dec. 15, that deadline hour is midnight Pacific time, and that some states with their own enrollment websites have later deadlines, such as Jan. 31 in California and New York.

President Woodrow Wilson formally proclaims that a state of war exists between the United States and the Imperial German Government, and directs U.S. officers to exercise vigilance. The proclamation states that “alien enemies” (German males age 14 and up in the United States who are not naturalized) must preserve peace, avoid crimes and hostility, refrain from aiding U.S. enemies, and comply with presidential regulations; citizens must treat law-abiding alien enemies with friendliness compatible with loyalty. Those who fail to comply may be restrained, required to provide security, or ordered to remove from the United States under relevant Revised Statutes provisions.

The proclamation establishes regulations prohibiting alien enemies from possessing weapons or explosives, using aircraft or wireless or signaling devices or cipher codes, and possessing cipher-written or invisible-writing documents; it allows seizure of property found in violation. It also restricts alien enemies from being within one-half mile of certain U.S. military and government facilities, publishing attacks or threats against the U.S. government or persons in service, committing hostile acts or providing information to enemies, residing in designated prohibited areas without a permit, and departing the U.S. without a permit. It restricts entry and landing except as prescribed, requires registration if necessary to prevent violations, and authorizes summary arrest and detention for those suspected of aiding or about to violate regulations or criminal laws. The proclamation and regulations apply to all land and water within U.S. jurisdiction, and it is dated April 6, 1917.

The Nationals added veteran Jeremy Hellickson on a minor league contract to compete for the fifth starter spot, joining A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde. Hellickson’s deal is worth $2 million if added to the 40-man roster and includes performance bonuses up to $4 million. General manager Mike Rizzo said the team wants rotation depth and may delay Hellickson’s promotion past camp to build arm strength, using an opt-out clause and early schedule flexibility. Rizzo noted a similar approach last season with Joe Ross and Jeremy Guthrie, which backfired, and said he learned from it. Cole pitched well Sunday, and Max Scherzer was announced as the opening day starter, with Strasburg, Gonzalez, and Roark next. Hellickson aims to show he can rebound after struggles with Baltimore, and the Nationals cited adjustments to his delivery. Notes: Trea Turner left the clubhouse for an ingrown nail, and Bryce Harper had the same issue earlier this spring.

Tesla announced more affordable versions of its Model 3 and Model Y on Tuesday: the $36,990 Model 3 Standard and the $39,990 Model Y Standard. The Standard models include fewer features than higher-priced variants, including the absence of certain driver-assist features and exterior components, and no FM/AM radio. Tesla said the Model Y Standard availability is November to December and the Model 3 Standard is December to January. After the announcement, Tesla’s stock dipped 3% on Tuesday, and shares closed down 4.45%. The new Standard models were announced after Tesla’s previous timing and amid discussion of US EV tax credit availability.

The passage is a November 14, 2000 edition of VentureWire, a daily private company business news bulletin. It lists “Top Stories” including Apax merging European and Israeli units and investing $600 million; New Edge Networks laying off 135 employees; KSolutions receiving $50 million for first-round funding; and Cisco acquiring Radiata for $295 million. The issue also includes multiple “New Money” funding announcements, “Bad News” items (executives leaving Buzz MSP, eSociety shutting down, and iExplore cutting jobs during restructuring), “New Products” and “M&A” updates, board and leadership changes for various companies, VC fund and personnel news, and “VW Corrections” about omitted and misspelled information.

In an appeal from a San Francisco Superior Court judgment, John Ortiz was convicted of simple assault after being charged with assault with a deadly weapon. The prosecution involved Ortiz cutting Donaso with a pocket-knife during a struggle after Ortiz entered his home where his wife and Donaso were present. The appellate court held it was proper on cross-examination for the district attorney to ask Ortiz to illustrate how he took the pocket-knife from his pocket and opened it, since Ortiz testified he did so in self-defense. The court also found that evidence about whether Ortiz wrote threatening letters was a collateral issue; striking testimony related to that matter did not warrant reversal. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage describes NVIDIA technologies that use AI to improve real-time graphics. RR (Ray Reconstruction) enhances image quality in intensive ray-traced scenes by generating additional pixels with AI, and the transformer model further improves results in challenging lighting while reducing common denoiser artifacts. DLAA provides higher image quality using AI anti-aliasing built on DLSS super resolution, aiming for increased temporal stability and more detail. It also outlines neural shaders and related Blackwell-era features, including neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache for improved indirect lighting and performance, RTX Skin for real-time subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces using a generative AI model for more natural-looking faces. The passage further provides hardware architecture details for Blackwell GPUs (GB202/GB203/GB205), mentions GeForce RTX 50 series products (RTX 5090, RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti, RTX 5070) and includes specification comparisons, followed by legal disclaimers about accuracy, liability, and use of the information.

Police in Pennsylvania said a 6-year-old girl reported witnessing her mother’s death. Devanna Cornitcher, 25, was found stabbed to death in a Chester apartment. Her boyfriend, Alonzo Carter, 25, was found covered in blood nearby, and police said a bloody kitchen knife remained on the floor. Investigators reported Carter told police he stabbed Cornitcher in self-defense, saying she tried to stab him. Both the couple’s 3-year-old son and Cornitcher’s 6-year-old daughter were present, police said. Carter was arrested on suspicion of murder and related charges, is being held at George Hill correctional facility, and was denied bail.

The passage describes an appeal case, Juan Archibeque v. Jose Maria Miera, involving damages to wheat caused by cattle. The justice of the peace awarded Archibeque forty almudes of wheat; Miera appealed to the district court, where the case was tried de novo as an original matter. The district court overruled Miera’s motion to dismiss based on record reasons and allowed Archibeque to file an account. The court explains that under the organic act, only the supreme court has appellate powers, while district courts and other lower courts act as courts of original jurisdiction; on appeal from a justice of the peace, the transcript is used only to confirm origin, judgment, and proper appeal, and the district court does not revise legal errors from the transcript. The jury weighed discrepancies in testimony and returned a verdict for Miera; a motion for a new trial was denied. The appellate court reviews evidence about cattle being in the wheat-field and finds no clear preponderance against the jury’s verdict, so it affirms the judgment.

The passage lists items for “Chapter I: January 1–March 8, 1945,” describing consultations of the United States with the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, China, and France on issues not settled at Dumbarton Oaks, consideration of views on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals submitted by American Republics and others, and extension of Conference invitations to governments of 39 United Nations. It also includes numerous dated circular telegrams and telegram entries between Washington and other locations from January 2 through March 8, 1945, and ends with a reference to a fourth meeting held December 29 to continue discussions on international organization. At that meeting, a compilation of memoranda regarding Dumbarton Oaks proposals submitted by nine governments (Brazil, Chile, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Haiti, Mexico, Panama, Uruguay, and Venezuela) was presented for discussion, and the Secretary stated that progress was being made toward convening a Conference of American Republics to consider major issues and to help ensure effective cooperation in building an enduring international peace structure.

The passage discusses the difficulty of playing early without being warmed up, especially during power plays and penalty kills. It notes the crowd’s energy as a strength for the team and says it needs to rely on that to win more games in a series. It mentions facing a talented opponent with many goal scorers and highlights a strong penalty killer on the team as helpful. The speaker describes the situation as frustrating but says the team expects to turn things around with two home games, and that they need to improve against a strong defensive opponent.

The passage describes a study using machine learning to predict depressive symptom severity (DSS) from sleep quality, anxiety, and brain gray matter volume (GMV) across multiple cohorts. Prior research linking sleep disturbance and anxiety with depression was limited by conventional statistical methods, single-cohort data, and poor generalizability. In this study, poor sleep quality robustly predicted DSS across three independent cohorts, and adding anxiety improved predictive performance; anxiety also mediated the link between sleep quality and DSS. Structural and functional brain measures (GMV, and functional measures ReHo and fALFF) did not meaningfully predict DSS or mediate the association. Longitudinal analyses suggested that sleep quality and anxiety could predict future DSS, but this future prediction was weaker in participants who received neurofeedback therapy between time points. The authors conclude that screening and treating sleep disturbance and anxiety may help reduce depressive symptom burden, and call for larger longitudinal datasets to assess long-term effects on depressive disorders.

The passage describes the Base Cross Offense in basketball as a strategy that exploits size mismatches and is successful at multiple levels. It emphasizes that the offense’s effectiveness depends on precise execution of the baseline screen and proper use by both screener and receiver. The point guard O1 initiates with an entry pass to wing O3, followed by a “Give & Go” cut or, if not open, O1 sets a baseline screen for post O5. O1 then continues to the weakside wing or pops to the free throw line, while the ball can be reversed or advanced to create post opportunities or weakside down-screen flows. The passage outlines various entries and reads/counters against different defensive responses (such as trailing, low/high play, switches, show-and-recover, and fronting), and includes options like screen-and-pop and post lob. It also covers posting up strongly with basic post moves, low-post two-person and split actions, ball-reversal options, down/mid/side screen variations, teaching and implementation considerations (timing, non-verbal communication, defensive recognition), and practice suggestions. It concludes with game strategy advice for scouting and adjusting, and a note that coaches should be prepared to defend against the Base Cross Offense.

The passage argues that in 1979 the United States suffered major setbacks in Iran and Nicaragua during the Carter administration. It states that the administration failed to prevent undesirable outcomes and collaborated in replacing moderate, American-friendly leaders with less friendly extremist rulers. It claims evidence suggests conditions in both countries are more likely to worsen than improve. It also says Carter’s approach lacks realism about differences between traditional and revolutionary autocracies, arguing that revolutionary autocracies are typically more repressive and create social inequities and poverty, while traditional autocrats are generally more compatible with U.S. interests. It concludes that a lack of an appropriate U.S. policy for dealing with threatened non-democratic governments risks similar “disastrous effects” elsewhere.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately, according to lawyers representing him. The resignation follows his detention by U.S. Customs and Immigration Enforcement Friday, when ICE said he was arrested during a “targeted enforcement operation” and allegedly evaded arrest. ICE reported that his vehicle contained a handgun, hunting knife, and $3,000 in cash. ICE said Roberts received a final order of removal from an immigration judge and that he entered the U.S. in 1999 on a student visa.

Roberts’ attorney said Roberts is a citizen of Guyana and served in Guyana’s military, and that his office is seeking more information and filed a request for a stay in federal immigration court in Omaha. Roberts is being held at the Woodbury County Jail in Sioux City. The passage also describes questions about the school district’s hiring vetting process, including claims by a third-party background check consultant that it did not perform basic I-9 verification, and statements from a school board coalition and U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn criticizing Roberts’ leadership while under a final removal order.

The passage summarizes recent market and economic developments, saying last week’s market-moving events were often muted by controversy or doubt. It cites GDP and labor data that were clouded by tariff-related distortions and sharp downward revisions to jobs, and notes the FOMC included two dissenting votes, with Powell emphasizing patience and data dependency amid uncertainty about tariffs and labor-force changes. It also describes stronger-than-expected earnings and upward earnings revisions, while technical analysis says the week ended with a bearish engulfing pattern and a shift to risk-off. The outlook then discusses sector and global equity signals, volatility changes, and overall risk conditions, along with promotional content for Investing.com tools and disclosures about trading risks.

A motorist with four flat tires led police on a two-hour pursuit across Kansas and Missouri before his arrest. The chase started Thursday in northeast Kansas when officers tried to stop a pickup truck on a warrant for several felony violations. The suspect drove into Missouri, passing through St. Joseph toward Savannah, where a spike strip blew out all four tires. The pursuit ended in Savannah when the vehicle veered into a ditch. Police found drugs and three loaded weapons in the vehicle; the suspect was taken to a hospital after officers believed he ingested methamphetamine. He will be jailed after the hospital evaluation.

The passage explains the NHS Patient Charter, which brings together patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges that go beyond legal requirements, and patients’ responsibilities. It outlines promises including free healthcare at point of use (with exceptions), treatment that meets needs and preferences, equal access, waiting time standards with explanations and alternatives if standards aren’t met, and safe, high-quality care. It also covers rights relating to medicines recommended by NICE, fair and explained local decisions, consent and privacy, choice of GP practice and involvement in care decisions, being told openly if something goes wrong, complaints and escalation options, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. The charter emphasizes that it is a partnership requiring patients to help the NHS function by using services fairly, respecting staff and other patients, following treatment plans, and participating in vaccination and screening, especially during strain on the NHS.

A study on the nocebo effect found that people report stronger negative side effects when a treatment appears more expensive. Researchers tested this by giving volunteers fake creams labeled as either an expensive brand or a cheaper generic and exposing their arms to increasing heat. Those given the expensive-looking cream reported more pain than those given the cheaper-looking cream, with pain increases of about 3% for the generic relative to a no-active-ingredients control cream and nearly 30% for the expensive-looking cream. fMRI scans showed differing activity in the prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray depending on the cream. The study suggests that how doctors, nurses, and pharmacists discuss medication prices may help reduce the nocebo effect.

The passage is part of NVIDIA Corporation’s FY2018 Form 10-K. It identifies NVIDIA, its SEC filing details, registered securities, and various check-mark disclosures (including status as a large accelerated filer and not a shell company). It states the aggregate market value of shares held by non-affiliates as of July 28, 2017, and the number of shares outstanding as of February 26, 2018, and notes that portions of the 2018 proxy statement are incorporated by reference for Part III, Items 10–14. It includes a section describing NVIDIA’s business and market strategy, outlining its GPU-based platform approach, major markets (Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, Automotive), segments (GPU and Tegra Processor), and business strategies such as advancing GPU computing, AI, visual computing, autonomous vehicles, and leveraging intellectual property. The passage also lists risks (including market evolution, competition, cybersecurity breaches, product defects, reliance on third parties for manufacturing, international operations, executive retention, acquisitions, intellectual property protection, fluctuations in results, privacy concerns, tax risks, litigation/regulatory proceedings, and takeover-related provisions under Delaware law), and provides information about properties, legal proceedings, and market/stock details such as dividend policy, stock repurchases, and related transactions.

The passage explains that “goal side” is the basic defender position in soccer, with defenders on an imaginary line between the defending goal and the opponents. It says youth should be taught to “get in their way,” properly and legally position to block an opponent’s path to the goal, or keep opponents “in front of them.” It recommends moving defenders out from their own goal toward midfield, instructing them to stop before reaching forwards and recognize their placement relative to the goal, and training defenders behind opponents to run past and turn to establish goal side. It outlines instruction for defenders at right, center, and left positions, adjusting based on opponent movement, and taking quick glances back at the goal, using field markings like the Penalty Area lines. It describes practice steps without a ball using forward movement at half-speed, then adding a ball and increasing movement speed to show the risk of defenders getting too close. It recommends significant one-on-one time for beginning youth, notes sports analogies (basketball guards and football cornerbacks), and emphasizes defenders must not block or put arms out.

The case is an appeal to reappraisement by the United States from appraised values of imported fishing equipment at Seattle. The defendant-importer conceded that outside packing charges totaling 50 yen in one case and 4 yen in the other, treated as nondutiable, were actually dutiable. The government also challenged a 26.557 yen deduction listed on an invoice, but no evidence was offered to show what it covered and the record did not establish the deduction was improper. The judge found the merchandise values on the exportation date to be the appraised values less specified charges and, for consular invoice 3806, the 26.557 yen deduction, with judgment to issue accordingly.

James F. Robertson III, an inmate acting pro se, petitioned for a writ of mandamus ordering the Escambia Circuit Court to enter a default judgment in his divorce case against Cynthia D. Robertson. The trial court had determined the wife was not served because she was not living at the address listed in his complaint. The husband filed an affidavit for service by publication and the clerk instructed him to publish notice in The Atmore Advance for four consecutive weeks and then obtain proof of publication. Although the husband submitted exhibits showing a charge for publication and a notice that appeared to have been published on July 5, 2006, it was unclear whether this proof was filed with the trial court, and there was no evidence showing an affidavit satisfying Rule 4.3(d)(5) was filed. The clerk returned his default-judgment motion for lack of proof of publication, the judge denied the motion for failure to comply with Rule 4.3, and denied reconsideration. The appellate court denied the mandamus petition because the husband failed to establish a legal right to the relief sought, specifically by not showing that the Rule 4.3(d)(5) affidavit was filed with the trial court.

On Tuesday, the Bombay Stock Exchange Sensex ended a two-day losing streak, rising 270 points to 29,683.87, while the National Stock Exchange Nifty gained to 9,214.15, surpassing 9,200. Metal and energy shares saw buying interest, and FMCG shares also performed well. Tata Consultancy Services traded flat due to concerns about its earnings report later in the day. On the BSE, Adani Ports, ICICI Bank, Tata Steel and NTPC were top gainers, while Coal India, Sun Pharma and Bharti Airtel were at the bottom. Banking stocks rose on both indices. Asian markets recovered, but gains were limited by tensions with North Korea, with the MSCI Asia-Pacific Index, Hang Seng and Shanghai Composite ending lower. The Indian rupee opened at 64.51 per dollar and was 64.40 at 11.10 am, up 0.09%.

In 1980, Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. sought in Washington to collect from Conrad Lapp and his marital community the balance of a $34,710.70 promissory note signed by Lapp in Colorado in 1977 for Joslyn Fruit Company’s debt. The trial court held Lapp individually liable but dismissed the claim against the marital community; the Court of Appeals affirmed. The Washington Supreme Court reversed, deciding the issue under Washington contract choice-of-law principles that Colorado has the most significant relationship to the transaction and that Colorado law should apply to determine the property available to satisfy the debt. The court concluded that, under Colorado law, all of the Lapps’ property was subject to Lapp’s debt except Mrs. Lapp’s separate property (including her earnings), and that this means the same property should be available in Washington despite Washington’s characterization of some property as “community.” Justice Horowitz dissented, arguing that Washington law should govern the source of funds for collection because Colorado lacks community property concepts, and that Washington policy protects marital community property from a spouse’s noncommunity debts.

The WMCC vocational class in modern cabinetry and construction recently built the cabinets and countertops for the Kidder United Methodist Church kitchen. The church, the city of Kidder, and Caldwell County Emergency Management partnered to make the church a disaster relief center once the kitchen is upgraded. Pastor Richard Evans said the church planned a remodel and viewed it as a way to benefit the church and community. Dean Sedokna suggested the partnership and worked with prison communications. Martin Montgomery said the project provided real-world experience and long-term community benefit, and noted WMCC offers nine vocational programs and is the largest secondary vocational school in the state. Warden Sherie Korneman and Evans said offenders’ work taught the trade while giving back to the community; the church paid materials costs and the prison provided labor.

The passage provides an overview of cryptocurrency trading and explains 20 trading strategies and related terms, including day trading, trend following, swing trading, arbitrage, grid trading, sentiment analysis, dark pool trading, and trading around blockchain forks, halving events, and PoS, among others. It also discusses factors and risks affecting crypto prices, such as market volatility, scams, regulatory and macroeconomic developments, DeFi impacts, and trading fees. Halving events are described as reducing the rate of new coin creation and potentially increasing scarcity, while hard forks are described as blockchain splits that can create new cryptocurrencies and affect market sentiment. It highlights Tether (USDT) as a stablecoin used to hedge volatility and move funds between exchanges. The passage concludes that success depends on having strategies suited to investment goals and risk tolerance, including recommendations such as backtesting, and notes that day trading can be high-risk but potentially lucrative with disciplined risk management.

In Century Realty Company v. Travelers Insurance Company, the St. Louis Court of Appeals affirmed a lower court judgment. The court said the proposition involved was based on the same facts and principles as in Century Realty Co. v. Frankfort Marine, Accident and Plate Glass Insurance Company, which was followed for the reasons stated there. Reynolds, P. J., delivered the opinion, with Nortoni and Allen, JJ., concurring.

The passage is a panel discussion at MIT OpenCourseWare about financing sources for entrepreneurs. The professor reviews earlier class topics on business plans, pitching, finding customers, business models, and financial projections, emphasizing that funding is needed after planning. The panelists describe multiple ways entrepreneurs can raise money, including venture capital, angel/friends-and-family funding, customers transitioning from services to products, grants such as NSF and SBIR, crowdfunding (e.g., Kickstarter and newer crowd-investing rules under the JOBS Act), credit cards, and competitions, stressing that financing should match the company’s stage and needs.

Axel Bichara shares his background in software entrepreneurship, venture capital, and hardware-focused acceleration (Bolt), and argues that investors and financing sources should be chosen carefully, with attention to dilution, capital efficiency, and whether investors can help build the company long-term. Julianne Zimmerman discusses the idea that every form of capital has benefits and costs, highlights investor–founder alignment and selecting teams/investors carefully, and shares her experience co-founding Greenfuel Technologies and later founding Vodia Ventures. Amir Nashat describes his background in chemical engineering, his role as managing partner at Polaris, and his conservative approach to investing based on experience and mentorship.

During Q&A, the panel discusses evaluating incubators vs. accelerators, convertible notes versus equity deals (including when notes may be useful and key risks like debt and control issues), the importance of structural and strategic alignment, and common problems in fundraising such as raising too much capital for a limited market, or choosing mismatched investor types (including strategic investors or too many early investors requiring unanimous decisions). They also stress due diligence (e.g., reference checks), getting unstuck by addressing major risks early, and prioritizing questions and alignment before committing to investors or partners.

The passage describes Simulation-Based Inference (SBI), where complex stochastic simulators make likelihood-free Bayesian parameter inference possible, but inaccurate simulators can cause model misspecification that degrades neural posterior estimation (NPE) and yields biased or overconfident posteriors. To address this, the paper proposes “Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation” (FMCPE), which uses abundant simulations plus a small set of high-fidelity calibration pairs to correct simulation-based posteriors without requiring an explicit model of the misspecification. FMCPE trains a neural posterior approximator from simulations, then builds a data-driven, simulation-informed source distribution and learns transport via flow matching in two stages to align the source with the true posterior supported by real observations. Experiments on two synthetic and two real-world tasks benchmark against NPE and MFNPE, using metrics including jC2ST, Wasserstein distance, and MSE; results indicate FMCPE is more robust to misspecification, improves calibration and accuracy, and remains computationally efficient as a post-processing step.

The passage cites several news items: state archivists hope to raise $200,000 to restore state constitutions; the State Ports Authority will net $38 million from selling its Cooper River offices to a California-based hotel developer; Charleston is a test market for a new approach to cardiac care as efforts to revamp Medicare continue; Charleston Mayor John Tecklenburg reflects on his first year in office after succeeding Mayor Joe Riley; some new state laws took effect on Jan. 1, 2017, including changes to the North-South Carolina border; and it mentions a headline about South Carolina’s governor’s race set to have an incumbent in 2018 and a campaign event involving Dustin Waters and Mayor John Tecklenburg in 2015.

Apple announced a free battery replacement program for the 13-inch MacBook Pro (without the Touch Bar). Apple said some laptops built between October 2016 and October 2017 include a component that could cause battery swelling, which it said is not a safety issue. Owners can check eligibility on an Apple Support page using the MacBook Pro’s serial number; if eligible, Apple will provide next steps.

Part A1 of the SD memory card specification (added in version 1.10) extends the SD card Physical Layer Specification to define how Mobile Commerce Extension (Mc-EX) command packets are transferred between a Mc-EX host and Mc-EX enabled SD memory cards, with SDIO cards specified based on the Physical Layer Specification and modifications in the Part E1 SDIO Specification. The passage also summarizes Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, including supported SD card capacity classes (SDSC up to 2GB, SDHC up to 32GB, SDXC up to 2TB), voltage ranges, bus speed modes and performance classes, card form factors and registers, and communication over the SD bus (commands, responses, data blocks, CRC, single vs. multiple block operations). It describes card identification and initialization using commands such as CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3, followed by data transfer mode behavior and related state transitions. Additional sections cover ROM and write-protection rules, UHS-I and UHS-II operation modes and initialization sequences, and erase/discard/FULE operations. The passage further outlines password protection and card ownership protection (CMD42), including lock/unlock behavior, command prerequisites, error handling, and conditions for COP and non-COP cards.

The passage says experts claimed that adding a glass of water to the morning meal can lead to “significant loss of body weight and fat over time.” A study by scientists at the Children’s Hospital Oakland Research Institute investigated the long-term effects of drinking water on body weight and composition, involving 173 women aged 25 to 50 who typically drank less than a litre of water daily. The women added half a litre of water to their breakfast, and the study concluded that drinking the water promoted weight loss. The passage also mentions other studies that found half a litre of water burns an extra 23 calories over a year.

The passage argues that Central powers’ brutality was intended not only to defeat enemies but to intimidate neutral nations, using Belgium as an example through conquest, terror, deportation, and oppression. It claims German methods also included submarine imitation of similar barbarous practices, and that victory would rely on such methods. It questions whether any reform or durable peace is possible if international relations are based on a peace achieved through violations of international law and treaty guarantees, asserting that small states should not rely on violators or treaty scraps. It states three conditions for durable peace: removing causes of unrest, discrediting Central powers’ aggressive aims and methods among their peoples, and devising international sanctions to deter aggressors. The passage concludes that the country continues making sacrifices for the Allied cause, believing prospects for peaceful civilization and international reforms depend on Allied success. It then includes unrelated diplomatic document text: a minister in Greece reporting acceptance of an ultimatum and difficulties regarding political prisoner liberation and internal control, and a U.S. Secretary of State note to Persia acknowledging Persia’s endorsement of a U.S. President’s note and expressing intent to assist in maintaining Persia’s integrity and rights for a peace conference.

The passage introduces DS-STAR, a data science agent that uses large language models to generate Python code for answering natural-language queries from heterogeneous data files. It first analyzes all files in a given directory by generating and executing per-file Python “analyzer” scripts to extract a textual description of structure and content. It then iteratively performs planning, coding, and verification: a planner proposes a step, a coder implements it as a script, and an LLM-based judge evaluates whether the current plan is sufficient based on the cumulative plan and execution results. If verification fails, a router decides whether to add a new step or backtrack by truncating an erroneous step, and the agent repeats until a satisfactory plan is verified or a maximum number of iterations is reached. The framework also includes a debugging agent for execution errors and a retrieval mechanism for scalability when many files are present. Experiments on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code report that DS-STAR outperforms existing methods, with reported accuracy gains over baselines on each benchmark.

The passage says the Yankees and Red Sox will play a best-of-three Wild Card series in New York starting Tuesday, Sept. 30, with details available from The Sporting News. It notes Boston reached the postseason as the No. 5 seed after trading Rafael Devers, while New York entered with the American League’s second-best record but fell to the No. 4 seed due to a tiebreaker with the Blue Jays. The series will be available live on ESPN, with Karl Ravech, David Cone, and Eduardo Perez in the booth and Buster Olney reporting. It also states this will be their sixth postseason matchup, with Boston leading the previous series meetings 3-2.

“Sell the rip” is a trading strategy that sells an asset when its price has risen to a level considered overvalued, either by closing an existing long position or by opening a short position. The approach is based on the idea that overvalued/overbought conditions can lead to price correction or even a market crash, and it is often used by short-term traders who believe the market is overstretched. The passage notes it can be applied to any asset, but it suggests short-selling is often better suited to stocks with weak fundamentals that were overpriced due to market sentiment or overreaction, while it is not considered good for long-term investing or for assets with strong fundamentals and growth potential. It also describes indicators that may be used (oscillating and momentum indicators, plus moving averages and Bollinger Bands) and provides a backtest example using RSI on SPY, including performance metrics and an improved exit rule that reduced drawdowns and holding time, with Amibroker and plain-English/Python code available.

For 15 years, Rev. Brian Sietsema sat by Scripps National Spelling Bee pronouncer Jacques Bailly to cover if needed. Bailly took breaks this year because the bee expanded with a new wild-card program, so Sietsema handled Bailly’s duties for two of five spelling groups over three days. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest and former Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, said working with young spellers is fulfilling. More than 500 spellers competed in preliminary rounds, with nearly 200 words missed onstage; 41 semifinalists were selected via a written spelling and vocabulary test, where even top scorer Shruthika Padhy of New Jersey missed some answers. Other speller stories included Rebekah Zeigler balancing many activities, Reagan Remmers being reinstated after spelling “balaklava” (matching a Ukrainian city name), and Daniel Doudna using deliberate pauses and misspelling fewer words after slowing down.

The passage argues that AI’s promise of personalized learning requires significant curriculum and schooling changes, especially to increase student autonomy and self-determination. It reviews how education has historically become more formalized and curriculum-prescribed, leaving students little control over what, how, with whom, and where they learn. Using panarchy and ecological concepts (resilience, adaptability, transformability), it suggests education transformation should start in small subsystems within classrooms or schools rather than attempting whole-system change at once. Innovations are categorized by size and their impact on autonomy, with transformative innovations seeking more student control often being rejected or confined to limited contexts. The passage provides examples, including the ICEE program in a Chinese school and other initiatives in Australia, describing how such subsystems can spread and influence broader layers of the education system over time. It concludes that transformative ideas need opportunities to survive, be tested publicly, and gradually expand so the entire system may eventually shift.

The passage lists major public statements of American foreign policy from January to December 1945, including messages and addresses by U.S. presidents (Roosevelt and Truman) and officials of the Department of State. It cites dates and venues for items such as Roosevelt’s January 6, 1945 State of the Union foreign-affairs portions; reports on the Crimea (Yalta) conference; statements on conferences in Crimea and Mexico City; Stettinius’s address on writing a United Nations charter and on the economic basis for lasting peace; Truman’s addresses before Congress, the United Nations Conference in San Francisco, the Senate, and U.N. related closing sessions; communications on unconditional surrender and the Potsdam conference; messages on winning the war with Japan and atomic energy; and subsequent statements on the Council of Foreign Ministers, foreign policy restatement, cooperation, and policy in China.

The passage discusses how the team’s defense has performed well throughout the year, highlighting that the top four players take on tough minutes and that having the ability to match up against teams with strong center lines has helped in both the regular season and playoffs. It credits players including Matt Irwin and Yannick Weber for their contributions. It also emphasizes learning from experience—both personal and from others—learning from coaches, players, and daily practice, and staying focused between games. The speaker describes the season as hard-earned through good times and tough times, and portrays playoff hockey as both work and business involving coaches, players, and support staff. The passage concludes by saying that both teams at this stage are hungry for the cup and that success requires readiness and preparation to do whatever it takes.

The passage explains the Martingale trading strategy as a method of adding a larger trade size after each losing trade, with the goal of recovering prior losses and ending with a net profit equal to the initial bet. It originated in gambling, is associated with mean reversion and events with a 50% win probability, and is contrasted with the anti-Martingale and the double-down strategy. The strategy is described as risky because it requires sufficient capital to continue after losses, since a long losing streak can lead to running out of money, and stocks can fall to zero. The passage provides examples using coin tossing, stock trading with increasing purchases, and discusses position sizing, win-rate claims, and limits due to needing theoretically unlimited funds. It also reports a benchmark backtest on SPY and a modified Martingale variant based on RSI levels, noting the results were not desirable. The passage states it does not recommend using Martingale for trading, while suggesting caution and risk-spreading.

The passage describes SPI-compatible and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols for configuring and reading from a device. On power-up or after asynchronous reset, the device uses SPI-00-S for both read and write. A host controller can select other SPI-compatible protocols by programming SDI_MODE[1:0] in SDI_CNTL_REG, with the first transfer using SPI-00-S and subsequent frames using the new protocol; the selected SDI_MODE[1:0] applies to both reads and writes. For reading, protocols are grouped into legacy SPI-compatible with single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible with dual SDO-x, and SRC protocols. Dual SDO operation can be enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, and in SRC mode the RVS pin provides an output clock synchronous with device data. The passage also outlines device register maps, including nine configuration registers with field descriptions, such as DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, and alarm threshold and alarm registers. Finally, it provides application and power-supply guidance, including use of AVDD and DVDD, recommended decoupling, low-power NAP and PD modes, and example PCB layout practices.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed this Current Report on Form 8-K dated August 28, 2017, stating that it completed its previously announced acquisition of Whole Foods Market, Inc. on August 28, 2017. The acquisition was completed under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 15, 2017, under which Walnut Merger Sub, Inc. merged into Whole Foods Market, with Whole Foods Market as the surviving corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Amazon. As a result of the merger, Whole Foods Market common shares and various equity awards were converted into rights to receive cash, including $42.00 per share for eligible shares, and cash payments for options, restricted shares, restricted stock units, and stock appreciation rights, with awards canceled for no consideration when their exercise price was at least the merger consideration. The aggregate consideration paid was approximately $13.55 billion, financed with net proceeds from previously disclosed debt financing. The report also states Amazon intends to file required financial statements and pro forma financial information by amendment within specified timeframes, and lists Exhibit 2.1 as the Merger Agreement.

A New York Times survey found that most federal judges responding expressed dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in cases involving President Donald Trump since his second term. Only 12 of 65 said the Supreme Court made appropriate use of the emergency docket, and only 12 said lower courts received sufficient guidance on applying emergency docket orders. Only two of 54 said the emergency docket improved the public’s perception of the judiciary. In interviews, some judges described the orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” “incredibly demoralizing,” and “a slap in the face,” with one saying their district’s relationship with the Supreme Court was a “war zone” and another calling it a “judicial crisis” (all speaking anonymously). One Trump appointee said the emergency orders were “flushing out anti-democratic rulings” but warned against too many snap judgments and emergency orders creating impressions of “secretiveness or arbitrariness.” The survey also reported that, on the effect on public perception, 42 judges said it caused harm, 10 said no effect, and two said improvement. The newspaper sent the survey to more than 400 federal district and appeals judges. The report notes that at least seven of about 20 emergency orders did not include reasonings and that the orders have had broad practical effects, including deporting tens of thousands of people and slashing federal spending. The New York Times said the responding judges may not represent the entire judiciary, but that several dozen judges out of more than 1,000 were highly unusual in their concern.

The passage argues for integrating dance education with social studies education as part of a holistic, inclusive approach. It notes that international and US educational testing often excludes or limits arts education, which encourages subject “silos” and discourages interdisciplinary teaching. It defines social studies as an integrated study meant to promote civic competence, and describes dance education as focused on processes of creating, performing, presenting, producing, responding, and connecting, with only some emphasis beyond the arts discipline.  

The study reported uses a 12-question Qualtrics survey of 91 US dance education graduates. Results show the strongest coverage of social studies concepts as “people, places and environments” (94%) and “individual development and identity” (97%), while “power, authority and governance” and “civic ideals and practices” received less emphasis (44% each). The open-ended responses indicate concepts may be taught both literally and implicitly, with culture discussed most frequently and sometimes conflated with other social studies categories. The discussion concludes that many social studies elements appear in dance settings, but the interpretation of curriculum and pedagogy varies, guidance for integration is limited, and assessment/testing pressures shape the value and implementation of these subjects.

Crowds gathered in Istanbul for a rally marking the end of nightly democracy demonstrations after Turkey’s abortive July 15 coup that killed over 270 people. Officials said Monday that Turkey’s state of emergency will be extended by three months, starting April 19 with parliament approval, to support the struggle against terror threats, primarily the Fetullah Terrorist Organisation (FETO). The extension was advised by the National Security Council and approved by the cabinet after a public vote confirmed a shift from a parliamentarian system to an executive presidency. Turkey declared the state of emergency on July 20, 2016, and it has already been in place for nine consecutive months; under emergency rule, the government can bypass parliament to enact laws and limit or suspend rights and freedoms.

A Colorado panel, the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, voted to limit what health plans in the state pay for Amgen’s Enbrel to contain prescription drug spending. The payment ceiling was set at $600 per unit and applies to government agencies and commercial plans covering state residents. The limit equals the current maximum fair price planned to enter the Medicare program in January and is about $30,350 per person per year, versus about $53,000 per person that average insurance plans paid in 2023.

The Dolphins beat the Jets in Monday Night Football, but the win was overshadowed by Tyreek Hill suffering a feared dislocated left knee in the third quarter and being taken to a local hospital for evaluation. Miami broke a winless streak but now must prepare to play without Hill. Darren Waller had two touchdown catches in the win, and the Dolphins responded with consecutive scoring drives after Hill’s injury. The Jets’ offense struggled, committing three turnovers and 12 penalties, and they trailed 10-3 at halftime. They lost three fumbles and totaled 14 points for Miami from miscues, while quarterback Justin Fields’ main highlight was a 43-yard touchdown scramble.

The passage describes limitations of searching for alien societies via signals that require synchronized transmission and reception. It highlights a proposal by Spanish astronomer Hector Socas-Navarro in The Astrophysical Journal: instead of looking for emissions, astronomers could search for artificial satellite “necklaces” around distant planets. The idea is based on how geostationary satellites stay fixed in the sky and, if present in large numbers, could cause slight dimming of starlight during a planet’s transit. The scheme is presented as avoiding the synchronicity issue and requiring only analysis of existing exoplanet data, though its chances of success may be low.

China has adjusted the weighting of its trade-weighted foreign-exchange currency basket for the first time since December 2015. The share of the US dollar was reduced from 26.4% to 22.4%, and 11 additional currencies were added to total 24 foreign currencies from the start of 2017, replacing the previous 13. This change is intended to reduce excessive focus on the yuan-dollar exchange rate as the yuan weakened by about 7% against the US dollar in 2016. The People’s Bank of China is described as promoting the yuan against a group of currencies rather than the dollar alone, amid US political concerns about currency manipulation. Chinese officials say the yuan is stable, and Ma Jun said the issue is that the dollar is strong rather than the yuan being weak.

IMI plc shares (LON:IMI) have a consensus “Hold” rating from eighteen research firms: two “sell,” twelve “hold,” and four “buy.” The average 12-month target price is GBX 1,027.29 ($12.84). Recent reports include BNP Paribas raising its target to GBX 1,400 ($17.50) with an “outperform” rating; Goldman Sachs reiterating “neutral” with a GBX 1,000 ($12.50) target; Barclays reaffirming “overweight” with a GBX 1,190 ($14.87) target; Credit Suisse reaffirming “neutral” with a GBX 1,020 ($12.75) target; and J P Morgan reaffirming “neutral” with a GBX 990 ($12.37) target. The stock opened at 1216.00, has 50-day and 200-day moving averages of GBX 1,104.16 and GBX 1,051.38, a market cap of GBX 3.29 billion, and a 52-week range of GBX 751.00 to GBX 1,223.00. IMI plc is a UK specialist engineering company involved in designing, manufacturing, and servicing engineered products that control the precise movement of fluids.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on July 28, 2022. The report states that Apple issued a press release that day with its financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2022, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes company and securities registration information and notes that the contents are not deemed filed or incorporated by reference except as expressly stated. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage reviews Krylov subspace methods, starting with Arnoldi, which orthogonalizes a basis (matrix form \(q\) and \(h\)) and is used to derive eigenvalue approximations via a small symmetric tridiagonal submatrix (Ritz values). It then explains conjugate gradients for symmetric positive definite systems, using properties of residuals and “conjugate directions” orthogonal under an \(a\)-based inner product. The algorithm updates \(x_k\) and \(r_k\) using search directions \(d\) with scalar parameters \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), and requires one multiplication by \(A\) per iteration plus inner products and vector updates. It discusses convergence in terms of an estimate involving eigenvalues and the condition number. The passage connects conjugate gradients to minimizing a quadratic “energy” function whose minimum corresponds to solving \(ax=b\), contrasting it with steepest descent. Finally, it notes that if \(A\) is not symmetric positive definite, conjugate gradients may fail and introduces MINRES, which uses Arnoldi and a \(q\) basis to solve a least-squares-type problem, with computational cost largely in Arnoldi rather than the least-squares step.

Police and Crimestoppers warn people to be on guard for counterfeit banknotes during the festive shopping season. They say that in the first half of 2017, over 237,000 fake notes worth more than £4.88 million were removed from UK streets, affecting retailers, businesses, schools, charities, and the elderly. The passage describes scams involving swapping fake £20 notes for genuine £10 notes and notes being linked to serious organised crime. Crimestoppers partnered with the Bank of England in October to launch the Banknote Checking Scheme, offering targeted training for cash-handling businesses to reduce acceptance of counterfeit notes. Crimestoppers urges anyone with information about making, buying, or selling counterfeit notes to report anonymously via phone or an online form.

The passage discusses developments in the pharmaceutical industry. It says GSK will appoint Luke Miels as CEO on Jan. 1, replacing Emma Walmsley, whose tenure included spinning off GSK’s consumer health business into Haleon and focusing on specialty drugs and certain vaccines. It also reports that AstraZeneca plans to list shares on the New York Stock Exchange while keeping its London listing, with implications for U.K. companies amid criticism of the U.K. drug-pricing environment and AstraZeneca’s disputes over pricing and access for its breast cancer drug Enhertu.

The Department of Livestock and Veterinary Services reports challenges vaccinating cattle for Foot and Mouth Disease due to inconsistent vaccine supplies over the past two years, contributing to unchecked virus spread in several provinces and ongoing infections in Chipinge South, Mwenezi, Chivi, and Chiredzi. The department also cites insufficient veterinary staffing, weak logistical and financial support, abuse of police clearance affecting livestock movement, vandalism of veterinary infrastructure, lack of boundaries in communal areas, ineffective animal identification, and lack of cooperation from wildlife conservancy operators. It states FMD control depends on movement controls, rapid detection and outbreak control through quarantine and vaccination, and stakeholder support, which have been compromised by the loss of FMD control zones after boundary fence losses. The passage notes that with zonal control, around two million cattle required periodic vaccination, while without zonal controls the number increases as incursions occur; after an outbreak, vaccination must be repeated every four months for affected and in-contact animals.

VentureWire (Tuesday, September 19, 2000) reports private company business news, including top stories such as Pseudo.com shutting down and Broadbase acquiring Servicesoft for about $645 million, along with funding announcements for numerous firms. It also lists new products, M&A activity, new directors and people, VC fund news and personnel updates, and “VW Corrections” correcting previously published figures and identifiers.

Cheltenham Town may have to retain midfielder Harry Pell, a 26-year-old targeted by rival League Two clubs. Pell nearly joined Blackpool in August 2017 for £200,000 but did not agree personal terms. He missed Cheltenham’s first match of the season due to a proposed move, later returning as a substitute to help knock out Oxford United in the Carabao Cup. Chesterfield also showed interest last summer, and another club has made an approach ahead of 2018/19. Pell signed a two-and-a-half year contract extension in January 2017, and he joined Cheltenham in 2015/16, making over 120 starts. Born in Essex, he developed at Charlton Athletic and has played for several clubs before Cheltenham. He scored three goals in his last five games but missed a 4-3 defeat at Cambridge United after having two wisdom teeth removed.

The passage consists of four local news excerpts. The Omaha World-Herald (Aug. 11, 2017) says the University of Nebraska-Lincoln is investing in agricultural and environmental studies through buildings, research initiatives, and interdisciplinary collaboration, including a new Veterinary Diagnostic Center and a $20 million five-year NSF grant to study root and soil microbes; it also highlights related growth in enrollment and research spending and mentions initiatives such as INFEWS. The Kearney Hub (Aug. 9, 2017) reports the opening of the Family History Center at Trails & Rails Museum, describing its role in preserving records, supporting exhibits, being climate controlled, and advancing a long-term phase plan funded by a $1.2 million campaign and additional fundraising goals. The Lincoln Journal Star (Aug. 9, 2017) argues Lincoln Public Schools should work to keep small class sizes, citing low student-teacher ratios, evidence from prior research on small classes’ effects, and the need for additional resources given a high share of students qualifying for free and reduced lunch, alongside budget controversy. The McCook Daily Gazette (Aug. 10, 2017) describes Alliance’s plans for the Aug. 21 total eclipse and discusses Carhenge, a controversial but well-known junk-car replica of Stonehenge that draws visitors and generated ongoing attention without tax dollars or a tourism grant.

Stone tools found at Attirampakkam in southeast India have been dated to between 385,000 and 172,000 years ago, suggesting earlier human migration from Africa than previously thought. Earlier research placed tool-making technology in India between 140,000 and 90,000 years ago. Archaeologist Shanti Pappu and her team, who publicized the findings in Nature, said the tools help test theories about the origins and evolution of early cultures and their links to modern humans or prehistoric ancestors, though no human remains were found. Pappu noted that it is not yet known who made the tools or how much local influence was involved, and that continued long-term research funding will be needed.

The passage describes a cloud-based industrial data services platform for providing industrial data services using structured data types called basic information data types (BIDTs). It states that an industrial asset is registered with an identity, an asset model, and available data service applications; client users select an application to process industrial data; a gateway collects data from gateway devices based on data tags referenced by the asset model; and an analytic component processes the data according to the selected application. It also outlines methods and non-transitory computer-readable medium instructions implementing similar steps, and explains how industrial controllers, devices, gateways, and application servers work together to discover BIDTs, organize them in hierarchical asset/plant models, and generate contextualized data presentations. The passage further defines BIDTs (State, Rate, Odometer, Event) and their metadata, describes example gateway and application server system components for aggregating models and delivering graphical presentations, and discusses cloud communication, including use of a gateway device registry to manage secure connections to a customer cloud platform.

The passage describes a study on causes of thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs), which result from structural and cellular disruptions in the aortic wall and can vary in risk even when similar in size. The authors created computer simulations that generate aneurysms from different combinations of contributing insults affecting elastic fiber integrity and mechanosensing. Using maps of aneurysm dilatation and distensibility as image-derived inputs, they trained multiple neural operator models to recover the original insult profiles. Predictions using both dilatation and distensibility were significantly better than using dilatation alone, and the UNet architecture performed best overall among tested models. The results suggest that measuring full aortic shape and mechanics could improve personalized diagnosis and treatment planning for TAAs.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is described as a major and worsening global health threat, undermining treatment of infectious diseases. A 2019 report cited in the passage links AMR to about 700,000 deaths annually, projected to rise to 20 million by 2050, with economic costs potentially exceeding $2.9 trillion. In India, the passage attributes alarming AMR conditions to over-the-counter antibiotic access, weak regulation, and low awareness, alongside factors such as antibiotic misuse, misdiagnosis, substandard prescribing, patient self-medication, inadequate healthcare conditions, and excessive agricultural antibiotic use.

The passage reports a cross-sectional study conducted from November 2023 to May 2024 at ACS Medical College and Hospital in Chennai, enrolling 346 participants. Specimens included urine, blood, sputum, and wound/pus (with other samples such as ear and vaginal swabs), with tissue samples and prior antimicrobial therapy recipients excluded. Microbial cultures and preliminary identification were performed, followed by antibiotic sensitivity testing using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion on Muller Hinton agar and interpretation based on CLSI guidelines. Overall, 76.3% of samples showed positive culture growth, and Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 75.4% of positive cultures. E. coli was the most frequently isolated organism (28.8%), followed by Klebsiella species (26.9%) and Staphylococcus species (13.2%). Resistance was notably high to several antibiotics, including cefoperazone/sulbactam, cefotaxime, cefuroxime, and polymyxin B, while Amikacin and Gentamycin showed higher sensitivity rates. Intermediate resistance responses were also reported for multiple drugs.

The discussion emphasizes Gram-negative dominance, frequent isolation patterns by sample type, and concerns about high resistance to key antibiotics, proposing recommendations for antimicrobial stewardship such as multidisciplinary leadership, surveillance, education, guidelines, diagnostic testing, and restricting non-prescription antibiotic sales and self-prescribing. Limitations noted include short study duration, small sample size, rapid AMR changes, and a cross-sectional, context-specific design lacking clinical outcome and co-morbidity data.

The passage is a lecture by Joe Hadzima on legal issues for startups, emphasizing that legal guidance is fact-specific and not legal advice. It covers an IP-focused lifecycle approach (ownership, protection, and relation to business plans) and explains types of IP protection: trademarks (identifying source; requiring use and possible USPTO search), copyright (rights to prevent copying; ownership by the author unless work is made in employment; contractor ownership requires assignment; includes open-source license compliance concerns), trade secrets (secret know-how protected via non-disclosure and indefinite until revealed), and patents (limited-time right to exclude; country-by-country; requires novelty, usefulness, patentable subject matter, non-obviousness, and an enabling disclosure, with timing rules tied to public disclosure and filing). It discusses patent prosecution steps, costs, US publication after 18 months, and provisional applications as lower-cost placeholders that establish filing dates (not published, but potentially limiting if later disclosure differs). It then outlines university licensing under the Bayh-Dole Act, focusing on MIT’s Technology Licensing Office, its goals (tech transfer and revenue), ownership policies, and typical startup licensing structures (options/terms, fees, diligence, royalties, and sometimes equity in lieu of cash). The lecture also addresses legal forms of business (Delaware corporation, limited liability, timing of incorporation, S-corporation election constraints) and Section 83(b) to avoid ordinary income treatment when receiving stock, stressing early stock issuance and stock-vs-investment timing. It covers founder and employee equity issues (stock motivation, equity pools, vesting and cliff structure, accelerated vesting concepts, stock leaving/buyback philosophy, and fiduciary duties among stockholders/board-related considerations), plus basic securities law cautions and the risks of improper offer/sale language. Finally, it summarizes venture financing term sheet concepts (preferred return, liquidation preference, anti-dilution, and examples like straight vs participating liquidation preferences and full ratchet vs weighted average anti-dilution), and encourages using the provided deck and resources for further self-education.

The author communicates to the Senate their approval of an act regulating the counting of electoral votes for President and Vice-President for the term beginning March 4, 1877. They say this measure is needed because, for the first time under the current Constitution, there is a dispute over the election result of the Chief Magistrate, and depends on how electoral disputes are disposed of by one or more States. They express satisfaction that the act provides an orderly constitutional method for deciding disputes: single returns are decided through Congress, and double returns by a tribunal of inquiry whose decisions stand unless both Houses of Congress agree otherwise. They argue that upholding constitutional law is essential to prevent irregular controversy and preserve peace. The author acknowledges the bill may not be perfect or best for all future occasions, but states it is designed to address the present situation. They describe the country as agitated and suffering economic and social effects from uncertainty and want assurance the election result will be accepted without resistance and that the President will not hold office with a questioned title, and they sign the bill believing it will achieve these ends.

The passage describes the SanDisk Sansa Fuze portable digital audio/video player, including its intended home/personal use, key features (1.9" color screen, FM radio, built-in microphone, microSDHC expansion, supported audio/video/photo formats, and rechargeable battery life), and various controls such as a Hold/Lock switch. It provides instructions for charging, powering on/off, resetting, navigating with a thumbwheel, connecting to a computer, updating firmware, formatting (which deletes content), and transferring music, playlists, photos, and videos (including using the Sansa Media Converter). Additional sections cover playing music/audiobooks/videos/photos, managing repeat/shuffle and other options, recording voice, deleting files, customizing settings (e.g., backlight, power saver, language, display), troubleshooting, and accessing support resources. It also includes warranty information and an end user license agreement outlining software licensing restrictions, disclaimers, and limits of liability.

The passage discusses President Kennedy’s Panel on Mental Retardation (PPMR) and a 1963 trip by PPMR members to the Soviet Union to learn about Soviet approaches to intellectual disability. It describes how Soviet policy barred intelligence testing in 1936 and rejected Mendelian genetics, leading diagnosticians to search for non-genetic or acquired causes and use electroencephalograms, while political constraints shaped their methods. The American delegation was surprised by Soviet prevalence estimates, which were lower than U.S. figures Kennedy would announce; the passage presents explanations that differences may reflect diagnostic practices and testing reliance rather than true differences in impairment levels.
