It then connects these historical themes to later autism diagnosis changes, noting that autism criteria and diagnostic substitution over time contributed to increased autism diagnoses, alongside improved access to diagnosis. The author argues that recent Trump administration statements incorrectly frame autism as a modern epidemic tied to vaccination and acetaminophen, and criticizes proposed changes that would eliminate parts of the Developmental Disabilities Act and follow Medicaid cuts.

The passage describes research on how digitalization/digital transformation affects sustainable development and its components, and how a country’s cultural characteristics relate to its digitalization level. It frames technological change through industrial revolutions and Schumpeter’s innovation waves, then defines digital transformation as using digital technologies to change business processes, products, and assets. It presents sustainable development as relying on synergistic pillars of economic growth, social equity, and environmental protection, with culture identified as an additional dimension that can shape how changes are accepted.

The study examines correlations between the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) and multiple indices that measure aspects of sustainability, including the Global Competitiveness Index, Global Innovation Index, GDP, Global Entrepreneurship Index, Good Country Index, Sustainable Development Goals Index, and Sustainable Society Index. Culture is analyzed using Hofstede’s cultural dimensions. Data for EU countries are collected for DESI from 2014–2017 and sustainability measures as available.

The reported results indicate that DESI significantly correlates with multiple sustainability-related measures, particularly economic and social components, while environmental outcomes show weaker or negative relationships. Hofstede results show strong relationships between cultural dimensions and digitalization, including negative correlation with Power Distance and Uncertainty Avoidance, positive correlation with Indulgence, and no detected relationship with Long-term orientation. The paper concludes that digitalization correlates with sustainable development components, but environmental aspects appear neglected, and that cultural factors influence digitalization and the acceptance of digital transformation. Limitations include the focus on 28 EU countries and that sustainability measurement methodologies are still developing.

The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s judgment. The appellate court found no error in the jury instructions pointing out an inconsistency between the answer to interrogatory No. 4 and the general verdict, and it determined there was substantial evidence supporting the jury’s verdict.

The Houston Astros won 7-1 over the Chicago White Sox on Sunday, extending their winning streak to six. They completed a three-game sweep, outscoring Chicago 27-2, and next play a three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels starting Monday. Jose Altuve hit a go-ahead single in a five-run seventh, and Lance McCullers Jr. allowed one run in six innings. Evan Gattis hit his first home run of the season, and the White Sox had lost seven straight games and 12 of 13, falling to 4-14.

The passage describes card ownership protection (COP) and password/FEP (Force Erase Password) behaviors, including how CMD42 processing changes across COP versions and how lock/unlock commands use specified CMD16 block lengths, PWDS_LEN values, and password data. It specifies error handling via the LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED bit and rules for saving/clearing FEP and FEP_LEN registers, including that setting FEP disables Force Erase and CLR_PWD. It also outlines COP locked-state command acceptance, force erase and FEP force erase procedures, and their impact on card lock state and password registers. Beyond COP, the passage covers CMD42 parameter sizing requirements, CMD6 switch function command operation (modes, function groups, busy status, and returned status data), and additional SD command/response and status structures, including CRC protection, command legality, timeouts for read/write/erase, and high-level explanations of CMD55/APP_CMD handling and command system extensions.

India, the defending champions and title contenders, will play Bangladesh in the second semi-final of the Champions Trophy at Edgbaston on Thursday (15 June). Bangladesh beat New Zealand in their last Group A match using a record partnership by Shakib Al Hasan and Mahmadullah, and their bowlers will aim to challenge India with pace and variation. India, led by Virat Kohli, plans to dominate Bangladesh from the start, with strong group-stage batting and a balanced bowling attack including pacers Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Jasprit Bumrah, and Umesh Yadav, plus spinners Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja, with Hardik Pandya looking for breakthroughs in the middle overs. Live coverage will be on Star Sports Network starting 3 PM IST, and the match will be streamed online on Hotstar.

Over 50 patients and their attendants escaped unharmed after a fire broke out at Scope Hospital in Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh. The blaze started around 4 a.m. when a UPS at the reception caught fire, spreading to other areas and causing panic. Fire tenders took more than three hours to douse the flames, and thick smoke made it difficult for staff to remove critically ill patients from wards, including the ICU. Patients from the ICU were transferred to nearby private hospitals, and a probe has been ordered to check whether the hospital had proper fire extinguishing equipment and followed Fire Department procedures.

Sarah Blakely and her husband bought a modest 1 1/2-storey house in a less-desirable Toronto area for over $300,000, then sold seven years later for more than $1 million as housing values tripled in the neighborhood. They plan to buy a larger four-bedroom home in Ottawa and live mortgage-free, saying it makes sense to cash out of a city that was straining their finances and to move closer to family. Blakely’s agent Josie Stern says the market is cooling, buyers are waiting for potential government affordability measures and possible solutions after a scheduled meeting involving Bill Morneau, Charles Sousa, and Toronto Mayor John Tory. Stern reports a pullback from buyers, fewer high bids than a month earlier, and sellers listing old properties quickly. She cites Greater Toronto Area average sales rising to $916,567 in the past month (+33.2% year-over-year) with frequent bidding wars, and estimates about a third of her sales involve sellers downsizing or moving to more affordable markets, contributing to spikes in nearby areas like Hamilton-Burlington. Other buyers are also looking farther afield, including Eastern Canada, after viral attention to a Nova Scotia mansion. In Vancouver, real estate agent Melissa Wu says the introduction of a 15% foreign buyers’ tax reduced interest in high-end west Vancouver homes, while detached homes in east Vancouver remain strong, with sales taking longer than last year. Stern and Wu advise Toronto sellers to act before the market shifts, while Stern also calls for cracking down on speculators and warns that selling may not allow people to rebuy if the market continues rising.

Jean Melchior sued Hilite International, Inc. for infringement of claims from U.S. Patent Nos. 5,645,017, 5,649,506, and 5,507,254 related to hydraulic cam phasers using torque reversals. After a jury found Hilite’s devices infringed and the asserted claims were not invalid, the district court denied Hilite’s renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law. On appeal, the Federal Circuit reversed, holding the asserted patent claims should have been found invalid. 

The court concluded that claim 22 of the ’017 patent was anticipated by a German patent (Danckert) except for a feature (“transferring hydraulic fluid … direct transfer in a closed line”) that the claims did not require. For the remaining asserted claims of the ’506 and ’254 patents, the court treated invalidity as turning on obviousness over Danckert in view of another reference (Shirai), concluding those claims were invalid as obvious because Melchior’s only argument against obviousness was based on the purported lack of anticipation. The court declined to address other issues raised in the appeal, including noninfringement and claim construction. Judge Newman concurred in the judgment of no liability, stating the record supported the jury’s anticipation finding but that infringement was not supported by substantial evidence.

The passage discusses two international documents relevant to the “future of the Global South”: the Baku Declaration from the Non-Aligned Movement’s 18th Mid-Term Ministerial Meeting (3–6 April 2018, Azerbaijan) and the Communiqué from the 2018 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (20 April, London). It compares the constituencies of the NAM and the Commonwealth, notes India’s attendance by Sushma Swaraj (NAM) and Narendra Modi (CHOGM), and raises questions about India’s priorities. The Baku Declaration is presented as emphasizing non-alignment values such as autonomy in policy-making and concern about adverse impacts of global financial and economic crises, including rising protectionism and trade imbalances. It also reiterates support for ending Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory and condemns actions related to Palestine and the occupied Syrian Golan, and calls for tolerance and respect for diversity. The CHOGM Communiqué highlights risks of protectionism, support for WTO issues including the Doha Development Round and the Trade Facilitation Agreement, and the need to address small states’ vulnerabilities such as unsustainable debt and “de-risking.” It also addresses refugees and migrants, including solidarity with Bangladesh over Rohingya refugees, and calls for safe, dignified returns. The passage concludes that, despite some welcome statements, both documents leave “fundamental existential issues” unaddressed for Global South countries and says questions remain about the ability of underprivileged countries to pursue alternative strategies, particularly regarding autonomy in policy-making.

Although Norway has strong digital infrastructure, digital technology use in Norwegian schools’ PE is mostly limited to basic ICT tools. “Digital competence” in PE is defined as using digital resources to explore, create, and solve practical challenges, which requires teacher educators to have ICT pedagogical competence and support teachers’ development beyond basic skills. However, many (pre-service and in-service) teachers feel unprepared to integrate technology without practice and mentoring, and knowledge about digital technology’s use and benefits in PE is limited, even though existing literature reports positive effects on student learning and motivation.

The passage also describes flipped learning (FL) as a framework where students watch videos before class and then use class time for discussion and student-centred activities. FL has increased in higher education and is reported to have positive outcomes in teacher education across multiple aspects, though it is less recognized in PE and PETE, with calls for more research. The study presented aims to investigate PETE students’ perceptions of FL, using qualitative grounded theory with 22 PETE students. In two modules over two semesters in 2016/2017, students prepared for campus sessions by watching teacher-made videos, and course units were designed so that classroom time emphasized active learning. Data were collected through group interviews and analyzed into five empirical themes: expectations, simple input, deep learning, supportive learning environment, and challenges. Students generally reported that FL improved understanding and motivated participation, supported preparation and reduced uncertainty, and offered repeatable video access, but they also reported challenges including missing opportunities to ask questions during preparation and experiencing technical problems and time consumption. The authors conclude that students experience FL as useful and motivating in PETE, with perceived advantages outweighing challenges, and they note limitations and directions for future research.

The passage describes LeBron James’ career achievements and finances, including his net worth reaching $1 billion in 2022 and his NBA earnings under a two-year $97 million Lakers extension. It outlines his major income sources beyond salary, such as endorsements with companies including AT&T, Walmart, Intel, Kia, Beats by Dre, and Nike, plus social media and other business ventures. It also covers his retirement hints in 2023 and a later teaser that led to a Hennessy promotion, discusses his investments and media company “Uninterrupted,” and lists some of his purchases and expenditures, including homes and luxury vehicles. The passage also mentions his family, his children’s careers, and his philanthropic work, including the “I Promise School” in Akron and related initiatives.

St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital scientists identified hidden kinases, Mst1 and Mst2, that influence T cell production by regulating dendritic cell subset functions, findings published online in Nature. Using a systems biology algorithm called NetBID, researchers integrated gene expression, whole proteomics, and phosphorylated proteomics data to show that Mst1/2 and the Hippo signaling pathway regulate dendritic cell function and T cell responses. They found CD8α+ dendritic cells had higher mitochondrial oxygen metabolism than CD8α- cells, and that manipulating metabolism and cytokine signaling affected CD8α+ function and T cell priming. The study reported that Mst1/2 activates NF-κB signaling to trigger IL-12 production, helping drive CD8α+ dendritic cell activity. The work was conducted with interdisciplinary collaboration and supported by NIH grants and ALSAC.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K current report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 27, 2021. The report states that on that date Apple issued a press release about its financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2020, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report includes registered securities details for Apple’s common stock (AAPL) and various notes due 2022 through 2042. It also includes a signature by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Experts say a Roman pottery fragment found on Chapel St Leonards’ beach near Skegness could indicate a lost Roman settlement. The fragment was discovered in late June by a dog walker and is the third Roman artefact found there in a few months, following a Roman coin and part of a Roman brooch found in December. Previously, experts believed the lost settlement was somewhere in Skegness, potentially with a Roman tower or fort, but Dr Adam Daubney said the pottery likely eroded from a Roman site under the sand along the beach. Other recent beach finds at Chapel St Leonards include medieval items, an Iron Age bracelet, and a medieval silver mount depicting Mary holding Christ. The county council urges residents to report such finds to maintain records.

The Alabama Supreme Court answered a certified question from the Eleventh Circuit in the negative: it held that an insurance policy provision defining an “insured” as an employee acting “within the scope of duties” does not conflict with another policy provision covering “violations of constitutional/civil rights” in a way that creates an ambiguity requiring construction against the insurer. The underlying dispute involved § 1983 claims alleging sexual abuse by city police officers and whether the insurer’s linebacker policy covered those claims. The Court concluded that the policy’s coverage limitation did not make the policy illusory or ambiguous and that, absent ambiguity, the policy must be enforced as written. The Court found that prior “Titan” cases did not control the certified question and rejected the plaintiffs’ arguments based on ambiguity and illusory coverage.

The passage describes COVID-19 as a respiratory infection caused by SARS-CoV-2 and notes that dominant variants, including Omicron, drove pandemic waves in 2022. It discusses evidence that meteorological factors may influence respiratory virus spread and seasonality, though the drivers of infection and seasonal epidemics are presented as combined physical, physiological, social, and behavioral effects, and COVID-19 seasonality remains poorly understood.

The study proposes a hypothesis of a “compromised airway epithelium” early in infection that becomes more vulnerable to external triggers, leading to increased symptoms and disease severity. The main study aim is to assess the relationship between outdoor temperature and worsened symptoms and deterioration during the Omicron-associated pandemic wave in 2022 in Tomsk, Russia. Using daily outdoor temperature data and daily COVID-19 hospitalizations (as a proxy for symptom severity), the authors analyze timing effects and find that temperature drops greater than 3 degrees Celsius are associated with bursts of daily hospitalizations with a time lag averaging 1–2 days. They report identifying 14 characteristic temperature-drop points linked to hospitalization bursts and classify some as primary triggers and others as additional factors. The study concludes that short-term drops in outdoor daily temperature may increase COVID-19 symptoms and severity, and that results could support prediction of hospitalization surges and preparation of healthcare systems.

Peter Joseph Saville, a dentist who cared for thousands of patients in Worthing for more than four decades at West Park Lane, died peacefully at his home in Mill Road, Worthing, on June 27 at age 90. Born in Ilford, Essex on May 2, 1928, he studied dentistry at Guy’s Hospital and later served as a national service officer as a dental surgeon in Cyprus and Egypt. He married Josephine in 1954, moved to Worthing the same year, worked in Lancing, and then set up his own practice. He was active in sports and clubs including Worthing Hockey Club (president), cricket, golf, tennis, and squash, founding the squash section of The Manor Sports Club. He also enjoyed music nights and a wide circle of friends who toured across Europe. A devoted Catholic, he was a Eucharistic minister and visited the sick and elderly, attending mass daily in later years and making trips to Lourdes. He supported charities, served on numerous committees, and is survived by Josephine, six children, and eight grandchildren. A funeral mass will be held at Saint Mary of the Angels on Thursday, July 12 at midday, followed by burial at Durrington Cemetery, with family flowers only and possible donations to CAFOD or St Barnabas House.

The passage outlines weekly minor league baseball coverage plans and highlights top performances from the season’s first full week. It focuses on Atlanta Braves prospect Mike Soroka, who debuted for AA with a 2-0 record, 11 2/3 innings, a 0.77 ERA, 0.43 WHIP, and no walks. Other “big moments” include Kyle Tucker’s seven RBI for high-A Buies Creek, Jose Medina’s three home runs for low-A Lake County, exceptional pitching by Dane Dunning and Josh Staumont, team pitching achievements such as perfect innings by Visalia and a combined no-hitter by Kane County, and notable defensive plays. It also lists leaders in home runs, stolen bases, and strikeouts across the minors, and notes that manager Phillip Wellman won his 1,000th game with the AA San Antonio Missions.

The passage discusses how war affects financial markets, focusing on stocks. It argues that, contrary to expectations of poor returns and higher volatility, historical evidence suggests stock markets show less volatility during wars and geopolitical conflicts, with U.S. stocks performing reasonably well during conflicts. Examples include the Dow Jones’ decline of nearly 20% after Pearl Harbor followed by a rise over 60% before WWII ended, and a selloff during Iraq’s 1990 invasion of Kuwait that was later followed by a sharp market rise after U.S. forces expelled Iraq. A study covering 1890–2017 finds war and conflict periods had less volatility than periods with fewer geopolitical problems, which the authors attribute to government spending, particularly defense expenditures, correlating negatively with volatility. The passage also notes that wars not fought on U.S. soil may limit damage or disruption and highlights different impacts for other assets: gold is described as a safe haven and has risen during periods of uncertainty, while commodities such as oil can increase but are difficult to predict and have shown poorer long-term returns than stocks.

Nobel Prize-winning biochemist Peter Agre will give a free public talk on May 9 at the University of Louisville, titled “Bridging Science and Society: Advocating for Human Rights and Diplomacy While Fighting Disease Worldwide.” The talk begins at 12:30 p.m. in Gheens Science Hall and Rauch Planetarium. The annual distinguished lecturer series is sponsored by the UofL Chemistry Graduate Student Association with Clariant. Agre is a professor at Johns Hopkins University and director of its Malaria Research Institute, and he won the 2003 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his discovery of aquaporins. He has also led science visits to countries including Iran, Myanmar, Cuba, and North Korea to foster collaborations aimed at peaceful science and disease eradication.

Gold prices were steady on Tuesday, with spot gold at $1,225.06 per ounce and U.S. gold futures slightly higher. Investors focused on testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen for signals on interest rate strategy, amid expectations of more rate hikes than currently priced. The dollar index was nearly flat, SPDR Gold Trust holdings rose to 840.87 tonnes, U.S. inflation expectations increased in a New York Fed survey, and the European Commission warned of uncertainty from U.S. policies, Brexit, and elections impacting the euro zone economy. Venezuela’s gold holdings fell 23 percent in 2016, according to its central bank.

The passage explains that breaking chiral degeneracy in lattice vibrations produces chiral phonons carrying angular momentum, offering potential chiral spintronic and thermotronic applications beyond CISS, which is limited mainly to conducting materials. Chiral phonons can transport angular momentum and energy in both metallic and insulating materials and enable effects such as chirality-selective heat transfer and a nanoscale chiral thermal switch. The work demonstrates chirality-selective heat transfer in heterostructures of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and chiral α-SiO2, using time-resolved magneto-optic Kerr effect measurements to detect magnetization-dependent thermal conductivity in α-SiO2. The authors report a 7% difference in κ(quartz) when reversing magnetization M, with molecular dynamics and first-principles-based calculations indicating that conservation of angular momentum in chiral phonons influences heat propagation and produces chirality-dependent, spatio-temporal temperature profiles. They further find that the thermal on/off ratio is about 1.07 at room temperature for direct optical excitation and increases to about 1.2 at 50 K, attributed to reduced phonon-phonon scattering. The passage concludes that ultrafast demagnetization in the [Co/Pt] multilayers generates chiral phonons whose angular momentum sign is set by the initial magnetization direction, and that these phonons transfer into chiral α-SiO2 to realize a magnetically controllable, chirality-selective thermal switch.

The passage summarizes student and school achievements, including Molly Frances Noon’s induction into Pi Theta Epsilon, receiving senior leadership and other honors at Immaculata University and King’s College, and Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine’s Match Day for fourth-year M.D. students with listed residency placements. It also notes inductions into honor societies, student government election, completion of an internship, and various professional and academic recognitions. Other highlights include graduate students’ eligibility for Alpha Epsilon Lambda, presentations at a psychology research meeting, leadership roles in sororities, recognition at an OT Pinning Ceremony with future clinical and research plans, and alternative spring break trips to Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic for community service and cultural exchange.

The passage describes common elements of successful school-based mental health programs, drawing on Nancy Lever’s view that effective models rely on partnership between school staff and community members, including family-school-community collaboration. It highlights the importance of existing school employees and classroom teachers in observing student needs and referring for help, as well as teachers’ collaboration with mental health staff and connections with parents. Examples of adaptation are given across districts, including trauma-focused work in Los Angeles Unified, marijuana-tax funding in Colorado, and leadership support in Wisconsin and Massachusetts. Minnesota is presented as a national leader, with Mark Sander helping start and expand programs and creating a funding model that accounts for clinician time in schools beyond one-on-one counseling; the state’s approach is described as integrated into school culture and emulated by other states. In Baltimore, providers emphasize visibility and access through classroom presentations, social media with QR codes, and mental health events, aiming to reduce stigma and address feedback that families and students were unaware of in-school therapy options. The passage also recounts Maryland’s history starting in 1989 and the shift to contracting with community-based providers to deliver care in schools to overcome barriers like transportation and stigma, stressing that providers should “go where” children are. It concludes that Minnesota’s growth was supported over time by public insurance and state funding, including $20 million from the state legislature.

The passage says the Steelers will enter Week 5 of the 2025 NFL season in sole possession of first place in the AFC North after a successful Week 4 in Ireland and because other division teams have struggled. It notes the Steelers are in the best position to win the division, while the Browns are described as poor, the Ravens are banged up, and the Bengals are affected by a turf toe injury and poor play by Jake Browning. The Steelers have a bye in Week 5, while the Bengals play the Detroit Lions and the Browns play the Minnesota Vikings, and it suggests all three teams could lose again.

A federal lawsuit filed in Connecticut alleges the U.S. Army issued less-than-honorable discharges for potentially thousands of service members without adequately considering PTSD and other mental health conditions. The plaintiffs, including two Connecticut Army veterans, say they were wrongly denied honorable discharges. One plaintiff, Steve Kennedy, described developing PTSD and depression after Iraq service, receiving a general discharge after going AWOL, and later being diagnosed with PTSD by the VA, but said his discharge status prevented access to certain benefits. The lawsuit seeks class-action status and targets Army Discharge Review Boards, arguing they inconsistently apply a liberal standard when reviewing veterans’ claims involving PTSD or related conditions. An Army spokeswoman said the Army does not comment on pending litigation.

The Economist’s “Carrie Bradshaw index,” using typical studio rents and the salary needed to spend no more than 30% of gross income, ranks US cities by affordability for single renters. TMPM commands can move multiple pages using PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which is similar to multiple calls to SNP_PAGE_MOVE. Up to 128 pages may be migrated via a Page Migration List containing up to 128 Page Migration Entries. Page entries need not be adjacent, can reference multiple guests, and must have no order dependence within the list or between commands containing multiple lists. Per-page results are provided through Page Migration Status Entries: if PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS is returned, software must check per-page status; if PM_SUCCESS is returned, all pages were migrated; any other return code means no page migrations were executed. A page’s status may indicate it could not be migrated without an error, such as when the associated RMP entry is unavailable due to a concurrent RMPUPDATE, and migration may be retried after resolving the conflict using PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE.

The lecture reviews how tree-level QED diagrams have intermediate momenta fixed by external inputs, so they require no momentum integration, while loop (quantum fluctuation) diagrams introduce free internal momenta that must be integrated over all values, leading to divergences. The divergences are linked to extrapolating QED to arbitrarily high energies where it may not be valid, and the “program of renormalization” was developed in the late 1940s by Feynman, Schwinger, and Tomonaga to obtain physically sensible answers despite divergences, later clarified by Dyson and eventually given physical basis via the renormalization group by Wilson. The lecturer then outlines key effects of loops: vacuum fluctuations are included, physical mass and charge differ from the parameters in the Lagrangian, and fields and coupling constants require renormalization factors (e.g., bare vs physical electron field, photon-strength factor Z3, and charge renormalization). Using a vertex correction and a nonrelativistic limit of the Dirac equation, the electron’s magnetic moment is shown to correspond to a gyromagnetic ratio g = 2, with Schwinger’s one-loop correction producing a small deviation that matches experiment well; higher-order coefficients are also discussed and noted to agree with increasingly precise experimental measurements.

Inflammatory myopathies include dermatomyositis, antisynthetase syndrome, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, and inclusion body myositis, each with distinctive biopsy and transcriptomic features. Granulomatous myositis (GM) is defined histologically by non-caseating granulomas in muscle tissue, but its muscle transcriptomic profile was not previously defined. In this study, bulk RNA sequencing of frozen GM muscle biopsies (38 samples) was analyzed and compared with other inflammatory myopathies, disease controls, and healthy controls. GM showed marked upregulation of IFN-γ and IFN-γ–inducible genes, notably higher IFN-γ receptor and HLA class II expression than other myopathies, elevated T-cell and B/plasma cell markers, increased macrophage markers, and specific increases in interleukins, chemokines, TNF-family molecules and receptors, and TGFβ1/TGFβ3. Spatial transcriptomics localized several of these findings to non-caseating granulomas. A GM-specific gene set was defined, with 1,293 genes upregulated and 256 downregulated in GM, strongly correlating with disease activity markers and localized to granulomas. CHIT1 was the most significantly upregulated gene and showed RNA and protein upregulation in granulomas and giant cells. Machine learning models built from these gene sets, especially an SVM model, distinguished GM with high accuracy (AUC 99.6%, accuracy 98.6%). The study concludes that GM has a distinct transcriptomic signature that can support diagnosis and monitoring of disease activity, with CHIT1 identified as a key marker.

The lecture recap describes controlling a system of the form \( \ddot{q}=u \) using linear feedback and optimal control. With unbounded control, increasing gains makes the system reach the goal arbitrarily fast; with bounded control, minimum-time trajectories use switching surfaces and yield similar behavior with a curved final switching surface.

The lecture then shifts to two analytical optimal control approaches: Pontryagin’s minimum principle (set up using a finite-time cost and Lagrange multipliers) and dynamic programming leading to the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation for continuous time. It presents a sufficiency theorem for optimality based on satisfying the HJB minimization condition.

Using HJB, it derives the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) for systems \( \dot{x}=Ax+Bu \) with quadratic costs, leading to the Riccati equation for a matrix \(S(t)\) and the corresponding feedback control law \(u(t)=-R^{-1}B^T S(t)x\). It notes steady-state solutions for the infinite-horizon case and connects the result to a “brick” example, including the resulting cost-to-go landscape and closed-loop dynamics. The lecture concludes by contrasting when Pontryagin versus the HJB sufficiency theorem is applicable (smoothness issues), and previews that next Thursday the class will use algorithms to solve related optimal control problems for nonlinear systems.

The passage describes research on niobium (Nb) thin films used in superconducting technologies and studies how femtosecond UV laser irradiation creates and evolves laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) that affect superconducting properties. Nb films were deposited by RF magnetron sputtering and then laser cut into square samples and micro-bridges; surfaces were nanopatterned by scanning with controlled laser parameters to generate LIPSS, with variations in pulse energy and orientation relative to current paths. Microstructure and crystal structure were examined using SEM/TEM and XRD, showing gradual surface roughening, LIPSS nucleation and coverage, film thickness decrease, increased grain size near LIPSS peaks, and a reduction of the Nb lattice parameter with increasing pulse energy. Superconducting measurements using AC susceptibility/resistivity, SQUID magnetometry, and magneto-optical imaging showed that with increasing laser energy toward full LIPSS formation, the critical temperature Tc decreased and the equilibrium upper critical field line Hc2(T) shifted downward, with isotropic depression reported. The critical current density and its anisotropy evolved from isotropic to anisotropic behavior as LIPSS formed; transport and magnetization measurements showed direction-dependent flux pinning, with improved critical currents in certain field/temperature ranges and reduced performance near other conditions. Time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau simulations were used to support an interpretation that thickness undulations create effective flux pinning channels, leading to anisotropic critical currents. The work concludes that laser processing enables controlled modification of intrinsic and pinning-related superconducting properties correlated with LIPSS formation and associated microstructural changes, aiming toward fabrication of superconducting circuit elements.
