A vehicle code violation stop in Chino led investigators to seize more than $200,000 in stolen items dating to thefts beginning in 2006. Mark William Ellis, 36, of Chino, was arrested on suspicion of grand theft and vehicle theft on Feb. 4, is being held without bail, and was on probation at the time. Authorities said Ellis stole property over at least 12 years from vehicles, homes, businesses, and schools in multiple cities, including firearms, electronics, cellphones, tools, and gym equipment, which were found stored in six units. Investigators returned about $63,000 to victims and confirmed over 50 vehicle burglaries with 40 identified victims. Ellis has pleaded not guilty, is scheduled to return to court March 21, and investigators are seeking additional victims.

Centana Growth Partners raised $250 million to invest in financial services startups. Since 2015, it has invested in four companies, including One and Jumio. The New York–based limited partnership is seeking additional investment candidates and expects to invest $5 million to $30 million per company. Founding partner Ben Cukier said it wants to invest in “workhorses, not just the unicorns,” aiming to support innovative yet practical financial product companies. Centana has offices in New York and Palo Alto and was founded by Eric Byunn, Steven Swain, and Cukier.

The passage says the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) affects virtually everyone, including Medicare, employer-sponsored insurance, the individual market, and Medicaid. It describes potential effects of fully repealing Obamacare, including higher Medicare premiums and cost-sharing, the return of the Medicare prescription “donut hole,” and changes to employer mandates and coverage rules. It also outlines Obamacare’s provisions for free preventive benefits for Medicare enrollees, closing the Medicare drug coverage gap, and requirements in the individual market and employer insurance, as well as Medicaid expansion. The passage states that under Obamacare most Americans must obtain insurance or pay a penalty, and that this mandate would be lifted by repeal.

The passage describes how NVIDIA A100 Tensor Cores improve neural network and HPC performance. It explains GEMM computation and Tensor Core matrix multiplication sizes, then details Volta and A100 Tensor Core throughput capabilities, including total A100 GPU performance (up to 312 TFLOPS dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32, and up to 19.5 TFLOPS FP64). It lists supported DL data types (including TF32, BF16, FP64) and discusses mixed-precision training options such as default TF32 usage, FP16/BF16 for maximum speed, and automatic mixed precision with AMP. The text also covers A100 support for structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern and Sparse MMA instructions that skip zero values, as well as architecture features like a combined L1 cache/shared memory subsystem, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and memory architecture improvements (HBM2 bandwidth, ECC protection, larger L2 cache, L2 residency controls, and compute data compression). Additional sections describe MIG partitioning (up to seven GPU instances) for isolation and predictable QoS, third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch for multi-GPU scaling, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, error handling and resiliency features, and other hardware blocks such as NVJPG decode and an optical flow accelerator. It concludes with CUDA software features such as CUDA task graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 persistence controls, and cooperative groups, plus a sparse neural network primer explaining pruning and fine-grained structured sparsity.

The lecture discusses course logistics for an advanced class on holographic duality: no textbooks and no recitations, Monday office hours, materials posted on the web, no exams, and grading based on PSETs due every two weeks (five PSETs totaling 75%) plus a final 8–10 page paper on holographic duality (25%). The instructor notes the outline is flexible and that students learn mostly through outside reading and are encouraged to ask questions for clarification.

The lecture then introduces holographic duality as an “equivalence” (from a 1997 proposal) between quantum gravity and quantum field theories on a fixed spacetime, where gravity/spacetime on the gravity side is dynamical while the field theory side has no gravity. It contrasts unresolved problems in quantum gravity (e.g., whether spacetime is continuous, black hole quantum behavior) with better-understood gauge-theory descriptions of other interactions, and explains that Weinberg–Witten theorems constrain attempts to obtain emergent massless spin-2 particles (gravitons) from ordinary QFTs in the same spacetime. The lecture outlines the theorems’ statements about conserved Lorentz-covariant currents and stress tensors and begins a contradiction-style proof using Lorentz symmetry, helicity under rotations, and matrix elements of conserved currents and stress tensors, concluding that charged particles’ spin must be ≤ 1/2 and that stress-tensor constraints rule out massless spin greater than 1.

Non-communicable diseases are the leading cause of premature mortality worldwide, and risk is influenced by both genetic predispositions and environmental exposures. The BioRecall (BioRecall) study protocol describes a biobank-recall pilot (Central Finland Biobank) to collect lifestyle and environmental exposure data and combine it with genotypes, biological samples, and clinical outcomes to support research on disease prevention. Eligible participants are previously genotyped Central Finland Biobank donors with a type 2 diabetes diagnosis who consent to be recontacted (1,386 eligible candidates). Participants complete an electronic questionnaire (about 30–40 minutes) via the MyBiobank portal using Suomi.fi authentication and REDCap-based consent, with immediate automated feedback related to Finnish lifestyle recommendations. The questionnaire covers areas including physical activity (GPAQ plus strength and balance items), diet and alcohol (Healthy Diet Index), anthropometrics and weight loss history, smoking/substance use, medical history and health status, women’s health questions, work characteristics, emotional states, sleep, residential environment, and background characteristics; postal code data enable spatial environmental data linkage from registers and open-source sources. Ethics approvals were obtained, data collected will be returned to the Central Finland Biobank for future consenting-approved research, and the study plans to expand to other donors and Finnish biobanks if successful.

The passage describes the Supreme Court’s “relisted” cert petitions for an upcoming conference and summarizes several cases the Court declined to review. It discusses a “lost causes” concept for cases showing some interest but not serious candidacy for review, including petitions related to FDA cell-removal rules, California’s unclaimed property law, and a Communications Decency Act Section 230 immunity issue that were denied without recorded dissent. The passage then outlines newly relisted cases, including one involving the constitutionality of 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3) under the Second Amendment as applied to certain controlled-substance users, and another involving judicial estoppel and whether a bankruptcy non-disclosure automatically bars later personal injury claims. It also lists additional relisted prisoner petitions and other questions presented in multiple cases, and notes that the next set of cases will be added to the Court’s conference agenda.

Anthony Rizzo hit his seventh home run of the season and added a two-run single in the ninth as the Chicago Cubs beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0 on Monday. In the eighth inning, Rizzo slid hard into catcher Elias Diaz at home, leading to questions over what constitutes a legal slide; the play was ruled legal after a review, and Pirates manager Clint Hurdle was ejected. Diaz stayed in the game after being tended to and said he was in pain but not close to being removed, while Mike Montgomery pitched strongly for the Cubs, retiring the first 13 batters at one point. The article also notes roster moves, a late dugout confrontation involving David Freese and Joey Cora, and updates from the trainer’s rooms before listing upcoming starts for Jon Lester (Cubs) and Nick Kingham (Pirates).

As Sony prepares for the worldwide launch of the PlayStation 3 (PS3) on November 17, 2006, executives consider both competitive pressures and the broader stakes for video and DVD technology. Sony faces competition from Microsoft’s Xbox 360 and Nintendo’s Wii, each launching in close proximity, with the Wii’s lower price posing a particular threat to Sony’s market share. The PS3 is positioned as a Blu-Ray player as well as a game console, tied to a standards battle between Blu-Ray and Toshiba’s HD-DVD backed by various major film and technology companies.

The passage also reviews prior console history, including the rise and collapse of Atari, Nintendo’s growth through quality control and licensing strategies, and Sony’s earlier PlayStation and PlayStation 2 successes. It describes how the industry shifted from consoles being mainly for children toward targeting broader and more mature audiences, how software—not hardware—drives profits, and how game development and publishing evolved through fragmentation and consolidation. It further outlines how internet connectivity became central to “console wars,” comparing approaches by Sega, Sony, Microsoft (Xbox Live), and Nintendo (Wii online and the Virtual Console), along with ongoing public debate over violence in video games and the role of the ESRB and proposed legislation.

The passage describes several hardware modules and features of MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers. It explains the PMU’s roles in generating regulated core supplies, monitoring the external supply, and providing a bandgap reference, including brown-out reset monitoring and power-on reset generation. It outlines the Clock Module (CKM) oscillators and how various clocks are distributed for processor, bus, and peripheral use across different power modes. It describes DMA_B functionality for memory transfers without CPU intervention, including multiple channels and various transfer features. It then covers the event manager’s event routing between peripherals, CPU, DMA, and other peripherals, as well as summaries related to memory maps, flash and SRAM behavior, and protection features. Additional sections describe GPIO, IOMUX, ADC operation, temperature sensing and calibration, LFSS components (RTC and IWDT), VREF and comparator features, security/CRC capabilities, and communication peripherals (UART, I2C, SPI). The passage also includes watchdog timers, RTC_B details, timer features, device analog connection references, SWD/debug subsystem overview, factory constants, and typical application schematic and decoupling recommendations. It ends with developer support/disclaimer text and references to development tools and documentation resources.

DNA origami is described as a method that uses base-pairing between single-stranded DNA to self-assemble complex, predefined three-dimensional nanostructures with nanometer precision. A team led by Ralf Jungmann reports in *Nature Communications* a super-resolution microscopy mode that visualizes each DNA strand individually within these structures, allowing assessment of assembly quality. Using DNA-PAINT, which relies on transient, repetitive binding of dye-linked “imager” strands to accessible complementary sites and produces a blinking signal, the researchers found that assembly quality is robust across many conditions but that strand incorporation efficiency depends on the precise position of each target sequence during growth. They also found that increasing the number of staple strands can raise efficiency, but not all strands were incorporated into all nanoparticles. The authors suggest adding components in large excess and choosing modification positions based on measured incorporation efficiency, and they say the method could support quantitative structural biology by enabling direct measurement of labeling efficiency for antibodies, cellular proteins, and nucleic acids.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Current Report on Form 8-K dated October 29, 2020. The report states that on October 29, 2020, Amazon announced its third quarter 2020 financial results, with a copy of the press release included as Exhibit 99.1 and additional information on non-GAAP financial measures included as Exhibit 99.2. Exhibit 104 is described as the cover page formatted in Inline XBRL. The report includes signatures by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, dated October 29, 2020.

South Carolina women’s golfers Katelyn Dambaugh, Ainhoa Olarra, and Ana Pelaez received All-America honors from Golfweek. Dambaugh was named to the All-America First Team, while Olarra and Pelaez were Honorable Mention All-Americans. The season ended with Carolina ranked No. 12 in the final Golfweek poll and with at least three All-America selections from seven schools. The announcement gave Dambaugh a program-record five All-America honors; she was previously named to the WGCA All-American Second Team earlier this spring. Pelaez became the 10th golfer in school history to earn All-America honors, and Olarra concluded her junior year with national recognitions from the WGCA and Golfweek. The passage also describes each player’s season and career highlights, including Dambaugh’s scoring averages and finishes, Olarra’s top-10 results, and Pelaez’s freshman-record scoring average and postseason performances.

Modeling noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems is challenging when governing laws are unknown or expensive to simulate, but multi-fidelity measurement data and modern hardware enable data-driven models that can also reveal interpretable spatio-temporal patterns. Transfer operator methods such as Koopman and Perron–Frobenius theory and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) are presented as analytically informative and practically useful, and combining them can yield robust, compact, interpretable models for potentially stochastic time-series. The passage discusses dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) as a Galerkin method blending PCA and a discrete-time Fourier transform, based on eigenvalue decomposition from a linear regression model, and notes its ability to model nonlinear and stochastic systems and reduce dimensionality. It then introduces Gaussian process (GP) regression as a non-parametric kernel regression framework that provides probabilistic predictions and model-selection theory. The work’s contributions are described as transferring GP regression ideas to DMD by developing a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, modifying extended DMD to use noisy measurement data and provide uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions, and using variational free energy methods to address high computational costs for large datasets. The approach is framed in terms of a Bayesian model for the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, with isotropic measurement noise on targets and an extension of GP regression to RKHS outputs using operator-valued kernels, leading to a posterior GP for the embedded PFO.

The speaker says the team played well by keeping the system simple, getting pucks to the net, and grinding for wins. They credit strong games from linemates Ron Francis, Sami Kapanen, and good play from Arturs, noting that good goaltending and getting their cycle game going helps them win. The speaker describes passing to Kapanen when he was in front of the net and says they went into the dressing room tied after the second period, then kept momentum and scored in overtime for the win. They also discuss Aaron’s key role and personal motivation due to his past success with his previous organization, and conclude that although the team is excited for their first win, they expect a difficult matchup against a team described as unaffected by anything.

The passage is a segment of an MIT OpenCourseWare lecture recap and a talk by Bob Jones on entrepreneurship and business planning. The professor emphasizes that planning is dynamic and that investors ask “3 Whys” plus “why won’t it work,” noting that time—not money—is the scarcest resource. Jones discusses that businesses often fail because they do not understand who their customers are and do not identify unique, important value. He shares examples from medical product launches, including a failed nutrition bar for dialysis patients (“Regain”) due to misidentifying customers, selling to clinicians instead of the people who would buy and consume the product. He contrasts this with a later successful product (“NiteBite”) aimed at preventing nocturnal hypoglycemia in diabetes, which succeeded by learning customers’ motivations, messaging benefits (peace of mind), building relationships with diabetes educators, and creating distribution without paying typical pharmacy “slotting fees.” He concludes that the non-negotiable requirement for business success is having customers who will pay, and advises focusing on market needs through direct customer conversations, iteration, and clear evidence of willingness to buy.

The passage lists a “To-day’s Planetary Position” with Moon in Aries, Jupiter in Libra, Saturn and Mars in Sagittarius, Ketu in Capricorn, Sun in Aquarius, Mercury and Venus in Pisces, Rahu in Cancer, Pluto and Saturn in Sagittarius, and Neptune in Aquarius and Uranus in Pisces. The passage states that Baidu is incorporating Pascal-based NVIDIA Tesla P40 GPUs and NVIDIA deep learning software into its new cloud for an AI cloud-to-car autonomous driving platform. The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year, $600,000 study funded by Strada Education Network to assess the economic and social return on investment of five tribal colleges and universities in North Dakota. The project will evaluate graduate employment, survey 5,000 College Fund scholars using a Gallup College Values survey, and conduct a pilot study on how TCUs preserve and restore languages and culture and build strong American Indian nations. Results will be published after the project concludes in September 2019. Cheryl Crazy Bull and Bill Hansen said the research will help explain TCU impact on student success and society.

The passage introduces rare-earth barium cuprates (REBCOs), focusing on YBa2Cu3O7−x (YBCO), as challenging materials where superconductivity depends on oxygen stoichiometry and where defects and oxygen vacancies strongly affect superconducting properties and radiation-damage recovery. It describes prior modeling approaches, including classical potentials that fail to reproduce high-temperature transitions, and motivates using machine learning potentials (MLPs). The study develops an ACE-based MLP trained on DFT data including defects, and reports that the potential accurately reproduces energies, forces, equation-of-state behavior, lattice parameters, defect migration and formation energies for oxygen Frenkel pairs, and the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition. Simulations show the transition occurs spontaneously around 800 K in NPT runs (200–1400 K), with disorder driven by oxygen migration from basal-plane chain sites to interstitial O5 sites; the authors attribute the transition to entropic effects, supported by decreasing Frenkel-pair formation energy with thermal expansion. The ACE potential’s transition temperature is discussed relative to experiments, accounting for oxygen degassing, and the passage concludes that the model enables investigation of oxygen diffusion and complex defect physics, with implications for radiation-damage conditions and HTS device design.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is presented as increasingly influential in education, where it can support teaching and learning, instructional design, technological development, and educational research. The passage argues that AI can make learning more personal by providing timely feedback, improving inclusion through accessible and adaptive learning, and offering tools such as assistive technologies, chatbots, virtual assistants, and AI-powered platforms. It also emphasizes that desired educational outcomes do not result from using AI alone and calls for a comprehensive understanding of AI’s effects on current education systems.  

Inclusive education is described as upholding morals and norms, providing equal educational opportunities, embracing all students regardless of disability or background, and requiring curriculum, technological, organizational, and methodological modifications. The passage notes barriers to inclusion such as lack of educator training, inaccessible or poorly organized digital materials, negative attitudes toward special needs, overcrowded classes, inadequate infrastructure, limited resources, and labeling/discrimination.  

The research described is non-empirical, based on a literature review and analysis using PRISMA-guided systematic review procedures. It investigates AI’s impact on inclusive education and highlights benefits (e.g., feedback, engagement, adaptive learning, support for disabilities, continuous evaluation, and potential cost-effectiveness) alongside limitations (e.g., bias from data, reduced human aspects of learning, high implementation costs, privacy and security concerns, over-reliance on technology, potential disruption of critical thinking, and physical harms or resistance to technology).  

Recommendations in the passage include incorporating AI technologies in child-centered teaching, promoting active student participation, embedding inclusive education in curricula and classrooms, providing continuous professional development and inclusive teaching practice training for educators, ensuring safe learning environments, and promoting public and policymaker awareness of inclusion.

The passage discusses ion traps and how ions differ from neutral atoms in confinement and manipulation. It explains that neutral atoms are confined using magnetic and optical forces with trap depths around 1 K, while ions are confined using Coulomb forces that allow confinement up to around 10,000 K using electric fields of 100 V/mm, enabling room-temperature ion confinement. It describes ion cooling methods including Doppler and evaporative cooling, and notes sideband cooling as a feature of ion experiments that is also being applied to neutral atoms. The lecturer compares major motivations for ion and neutral-atom research, including clocks and quantum information, and then focuses on ion trapping methods, contrasting Penning traps with RF (Paul) traps and explaining how rapidly alternating confinement and anti-confinement can produce net trapping. The passage also outlines how micromotion relates to trapping and then describes ion-based quantum computation, emphasizing the Cirac-Zoller controlled-phase gate. It explains gate construction using trapped ions’ internal states and shared center-of-mass motion as a data bus, including swapping information into and out of the phonon mode to implement a two-ion phase gate, and notes disadvantages of the Cirac-Zoller approach such as requiring cooling to the absolute ground state and slow gate operations due to the center-of-mass mode.

Following the arrest of two Black men at a Starbucks in Philadelphia, the passage describes “National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day,” set for Tuesday, May 29, 2018. It says tens of thousands of Starbucks customers will visit Black-owned coffee shops instead, with Black coffee houses, coffee shops, and tea houses under The Black Star Project forming a federation to promote their offerings as as good as or better than Starbucks. The passage claims these businesses expect higher sales and increased market share, noting Starbucks is closing more than 8,000 U.S. units for diversity training. It also encourages evening “Black Economic Empowerment Forums” and frames the effort as a Campaign to “Circulate Black Dollars in the Black Community,” aiming to increase Black consumer spending among Black businesses. More than 400 participating locations are expected, with links and a phone number provided for information.

Cadillac sold 35,020 units globally in September 2017, extending 16 months of consecutive growth, and is on pace to surpass 2016’s total of 308,718 vehicles. Year-to-date sales total 256,613 units, up 44,336 from September 2016. September U.S. sales rose 1.1% year over year, while China increased 37.6% year over year, with gains also reported in Japan, the Middle East, Israel, and South Korea. Cadillac President Johan de Nysschen cited efforts to attract younger buyers and new technologies such as Super Cruise, along with a product offensive starting next year. The XT5 leads 2017 sales with 103,645 units delivered, ATS sales grew 15% for the month, and CT6 rose 6.6% for the month. Region sales for September included United States 15,530 units (+1.1%), China 17,248 units (+37.6%), and ROW 2,242 units (+3.8%).

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated December 1, 2016, reporting that on November 29, 2016 its Board of Directors amended and restated NVIDIA’s bylaws to implement proxy access and revise provisions on advance notice for stockholder proposals and director nominations. The new bylaws add Section 5(h), allowing stockholders owning at least 3% of the voting power for at least three years to include director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials, subject to specified requirements, with nominees limited to the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board. Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, stockholders nominating directors (other than through proxy access) must give written notice to the Secretary between 90 and 120 days before the first anniversary of the prior year’s annual meeting, with timing adjustments if the meeting date changes. The filing notes additional proxy-access-related administrative changes and references the amended and restated bylaws as Exhibit 3.1.

The passage states that hypertension affects about 1.3 billion people worldwide and is a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline, with race-related differences in hypertension prevalence and control potentially contributing to disparities in cognitive abilities. A study using harmonized cohort data from MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core included 2,284 Black and White participants (age ≥55) with at least two cognitive assessments and two blood pressure readings. Blood pressure was categorized as normal, high, or variable based on mean systolic BP and BP variability. Participants completed neuropsychological testing covering episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, visuospatial ability, and global cognition, assessed using composite z-score measures. Linear mixed effects models tested cognitive change over time by BP category and race, adjusting for age, sex, education, and baseline diagnosis, with multiple-comparison correction.

Results indicated that time and age at baseline were associated with cognitive change. For global cognition, White participants with high or variable BP declined faster than Black participants with the corresponding BP categories, while White normal BP did not differ from Black groups. Domain-specific findings showed faster decline for White participants with high BP in perceptual speed, semantic memory, and working memory, and faster decline for White participants with variable BP across all five cognitive domains compared to Black participants with variable BP. The study also reports exploratory analyses suggesting reduced BP–cognition associations in Black participants were not explained by lower baseline cognitive performance. The discussion emphasizes the need for targeted interventions and notes limitations related to BP categorization methods and lack of medication adherence and detailed medication history.

The passage lists multiple financial and business headlines, including Fifth Third’s planned $10.9 billion acquisition of Comerica, Santander UK’s CEO stepping down before a TSB merger, JPMorgan accelerating AI integration, and the Bank of England allocating its largest six-month repo since 2020. It also highlights tech and market items such as AMD stock surging after an AI chip supply agreement with OpenAI, Tesla’s record Q3 deliveries, and OpenAI reaching a $500 billion valuation. In the detailed section, AMD is described as supplying OpenAI with high-performance AI accelerators under a multiyear deal starting with the MI450 series, with OpenAI receiving warrants for up to 10% of AMD equity upon milestones. AMD’s stock reportedly rose more than 20% in premarket trading, though analysts caution about execution and supply-chain risks.

Judges have imposed hefty fines on attorneys for using faulty case citations in legal briefs likely generated by artificial intelligence. Usually, sanctions are paid to law firms that spent time due to the errors, but in a California case the fines were paid to the court because the opposing counsel did not detect the errors. In Puerto Rico, multiple firms are set to share $24,492 after motions cited at least 55 defective citations; the fined lawyers were Ibrahim Reyes and Jose R. Olmo-Rodriguez. In California, the sanctioned lawyer Amir Mostafavi was fined $10,000 for fake quotes and off-topic AI-generated cases, and the case raised questions about a lawyer’s duty to detect fabricated citations in opponents’ filings.

The speaker mourns the recent death of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, saying words are inadequate, but that silence could be misunderstood. He calls on Americans to remain united, carry on Roosevelt’s forward-looking approach, and continue the fight for freedom with unconditional surrender from Germany and Japan. He emphasizes that lasting peace requires punishment of war criminals, justice and law rather than geographic safety, and continued cooperation and unity among nations under obligations not to use force except in defense of law. The speaker urges support for a strong and lasting United Nations Organization to settle international differences, stressing hope, faith, tolerance, and cooperation among both nations and Americans. He also discusses postwar aims including working with other nations for peace and progress, increasing trade and standards of living, and ends with a prayer for an understanding heart and to be a faithful servant of God and people.

The passage says that several manufacturers in South Africa have discontinued manual transmission variants. Audi has removed the entry-level manual A4 1.4T FSI, so all local A4 derivatives now use a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. BMW has dropped manual versions of the 120i and M140i, kept manual options for the 118i and 120d, and removed manual options for the 220i, 230i and M240i while retaining the 220d and the manual-available M2. Volkswagen has ended the manual Polo GTI, the entry-level Scirocco 2.0 TSI Highline manual, and the Jetta 1.6TDI Comfortline manual. Volvo has discontinued the base S60 in T3 Kinetic manual form. The manufacturers are described as responding to market demand for self-shifting cars, with Audi Sport citing a lack of demand, though Porsche claims the manual gearbox will never die and Jaguar SA added manual versions of the F-Type in March.

Ahead of the third season of *Stranger Things*, the cast’s pay is reportedly increasing, with series regulars split into three salary tiers: Winona Ryder and David Harbour at $350,000 per episode; Finn Wolfhard, Gaten Matarazzo, Caleb McLaughlin, and Noah Schnapp at $250,000; and Natalia Dyer, Joe Keery, and Charlie Heaton at $150,000. Some raises are reportedly up to 12 times their seasons 1 and 2 pay. Millie Bobby Brown is not included, as *The Hollywood Reporter* previously reported she is negotiating her deal separately from the rest of the young cast. Netflix declined comment, and actor representatives did not respond to requests.

The passage discusses agreements and communications related to supplying Belgian Congo commodities. It notes that contracting parties may pursue active development work in the Congo, including sending governmental organizations, encouraging private firms in procurement, or supporting forest cultivation projects, with Belgium facilitating such activity without restrictions. It includes a telegram from Day expecting to forward by August 10 a complete list of commodities for negotiations covering Belgian Congo civilian consumption requirements, and reports on additional survey time and expected preliminary automotive requirements reports. Another telegram advises Belgium that the Combined Raw Materials Board in Washington and the Combined Production and Resources Board are expected to allocate Congo supplies and related commodities, and requests that reciprocal supply data be sent simultaneously to the British Foreign Office and the Department of State for transmission to those boards. Further messages address increased export duties in Belgian Congo, suggesting a tripartite agreement provision against increasing duties during the agreement term for listed commodities, and mention a London decision to postpone signing a tripartite Belgian agreement with retroactive effect to the prior Anglo-Belgian agreement. The passage also includes notes indicating that related negotiations continued through 1942–1943 without agreement, later handled by existing machinery, and that an Office of Economic Warfare mission went to the Congo in 1943 with an informal Tripartite Supply Committee established.

A University of Birmingham academic, Dr Chris Bradley, said flooding in Birmingham was not due to drainage problems, agreeing with Birmingham City Council that drains were overwhelmed by the volume of water. The council said grates and street drains are checked periodically and cleaned more in high-risk areas after weather warnings. It added the event was extreme, with a month’s rainfall falling in one hour in some areas, causing flash flooding, but it reported no drain blockage issues as floodwater drained away after rain ended. A yellow weather warning was issued for Birmingham and the West Midlands, with further flooding risk on Thursday, and the Met Office warned of thunderstorms, possible torrential rain, frequent lightning, and large hail.

The passage describes an ETF rotation strategy using monthly rotation among SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20-year Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) based on recent momentum. It explains why these ETFs were chosen and states that a backtest over about two decades beat “buy and hold” with lower drawdowns, although the strategy performed poorly in 2022, when it fell 41% from the peak and max drawdown exceeded earlier levels. The strategy ranks the three ETFs using the previous month’s performance, goes long on the best-performing ETF for one month, and repeats. It notes the strategy involves frequent rotations and may be best used in a tax-deferred account, and that it has performed less well in the last 5–6 years.

A crucial North Sea pipeline, the Forties Pipeline System operated by Ineos, was shut down after a crack was found, with Brent crude prices spiking on Monday. Ineos said the 450,000-bpd pipeline could be shut for “weeks” while repairs are pursued, including a controlled shutdown after the crack appeared to widen. The outage threatens North Sea supply by potentially forcing production cutbacks, and it has global implications because the Forties system carries much of the oil underpinning the Brent benchmark, with reports indicating many offshore platforms may need to shut down. The article also says the disruption could tighten Atlantic Basin supply, affect OECD inventories, widen the Brent–WTI price disparity, and increase demand for U.S. crude as a knock-on effect.

The passage introduces modal semantics based on lattice semantics, explaining how classical Kripke-style modal semantics can be extended to valuations in different lattices (e.g., Łukasiewicz, Belnap, and Boolean algebras). It defines lattice semantics, designated values, valuations, consequence relations, and filter-matrices, then develops modal extensions where the necessity operator is interpreted as the greatest lower bound (meet) of values over accessible worlds. Regularity of modal extensions is characterized: for a complete lattice, a unique regular modal extension exists exactly when the designated set is a filter and its meet lies in the designated set; for finite lattices this reduces to “regular iff designated values form a filter,” while infinite cases give examples where regularity depends on properties like principal vs. non-principal ultrafilters. The paper further studies formulas that characterize lattice properties, including conditions for designated sets to be implicative under a specific implication operation, and links validity of modal axiom K to lattice-theoretic conditions (linearity outside the filter, or properties such as implicativity under certain negation constraints). It provides an example using twist algebras from Boolean algebras, defining designated sets that yield a paraconsistent semantics and relating implicativity in the twist setting to validity of axiom K. The final remarks summarize that lattice order supports interpreting necessity and highlight connections between lattice properties, axiom K, and cross-logical communication, with future interest in conditions for finite-model properties.

Startup founder Charlie Javice was sentenced to seven years in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase by overstating how many customers her fintech firm, Frank, had. A jury found Javice and her chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty on three counts of fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit fraud. Javice said she felt profound remorse, asked for forgiveness, and was sentenced by Judge Alvin Hellerstein to 85 months in prison, plus three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture, and $287 million in restitution. She will remain out on bail while she appeals.

The passage discusses recent market movement and outlook, including declines in the S&P 500 and oil, changes in investor sentiment, and measures of volatility. It notes the AAII survey showing 40.3% bullish and 33.0% bearish investors, reports that the S&P 500 closed at its lowest level since early July with recent weekly losses, and mentions VIX rising to 21.90 as a sign of shifting market sentiment. It also reports crude oil falling due to tariff-related uncertainty and OPEC+ production hikes, outlines OPEC+ output and potential tariff impacts, and states that the S&P 500 may rebound at the start of the week amid uncertainty about whether any correction is longer-lasting. The passage ends with trading risk disclosures and data accuracy disclaimers.

Erin Howard, 13, improved her spelling of the trademarked word “Klydonograph” from misspelling it at last year’s Scripps National Spelling Bee to spelling it in seconds this year. She will compete in Thursday’s final round and is in her third national competition, studying three to four hours on weeknights and six to eight hours on weekends. Other repeat spellers highlighted include Cameron Keith, 12, who studies for several hours daily and returns to the final round after placing 18th in 2016, and Naysa Modi, 12, who studied with reading, typing, and quizzing for hours to qualify for the final round for her fourth time. The passage emphasizes the hours of preparation and perseverance, along with the personal effects of returning to compete.

The passage discusses US economic and market developments amid trade-war concerns. It states that July job growth came in at 73K, with May and June revised lower, and that this pushed the 12-month job average to its lowest levels since the pandemic, with gains mainly in health care. It also says August–October are typically weaker months and highlights the S&P 500’s 9.1% return mark, with analysts citing strong Q2 earnings results for the S&P 500. The passage notes Trump plans to impose a 100% tariff on China starting November 1, contributing to declines in US stock indexes and a rejection of the US dollar after tariff and weak economic data news. It adds that AI has been supporting the market and mentions that earnings growth and sales growth estimates have risen.

Wesley Wiechmann sought divorce and physical custody of the couple’s four minor children from Sylvia Wiechmann. A custody specialist recommended giving defendant custody of all four children. The trial court found it was in each child’s best interests for the parents to share legal custody, with plaintiff having physical custody of the two older children (Stefan and Loren) and defendant having physical custody of the two younger twin boys (Cameron and Chase). Defendant appealed, arguing the trial court abused its discretion by not awarding her custody of all four children and by separating the siblings.

The Court of Appeals held that although keeping siblings together is often in the best interests of each child, when separating siblings is contrary to an individual child’s best interests, the individual child’s best interests control. It found no palpable abuse of discretion or legal error in the trial court’s decision to separate the children and affirmed the judgment.

The passage describes the Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification, including its purpose, audience, background, security/threat model, supported scope, and operational details. It states that AMD created SFS as a secure, non-persistent way to apply runtime patches to selected AMD-provided firmware and settings without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset, improving stability and allowing datacenter operators to apply patches without rebooting. SFS does not patch customer BIOS code running on x86 (such as SMM, AGESA, or UEFI) and is limited to priority runtime concerns affecting AMD-provided binary firmware components within an AGESA release. The document explains patch levels and versioning concepts (SFSPL, component SPL versions, and SYSPL), cryptographic signing of update packages (with optional customer co-signing), and how the ASP verifies signatures and applies updates. It also covers patch applicability checks, resiliency requirements (prevent updates if dependencies can’t be satisfied), non-persistence across reboots and customer options for when to apply patches, command structures and sending SFS commands to the ASP via a TEE extended command buffer, and details such as patch naming and release mechanism constraints tied to specific firmware/system patch level combinations.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets closed lower on Thursday due to fears of capital outflows following minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve’s last meeting that suggested policymakers want to begin trimming its $4.5 trillion stimulus balance sheet later this year, depending on economic data. Investors also remained cautious ahead of a planned U.S.-China meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. MSCI Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell about 0.6%, while Indonesian shares closed at a record high. Other moves included Philippines down 0.3%, Singapore down 0.03%, and Malaysia down 0.29%, with Vietnam and Thailand closed for holidays.

The Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1 on Monday, winning their ninth game in 10 and reaching 13 games above .500 for the first time since late in 2014. Marco Gonzales pitched into the seventh inning without allowing an earned run for a third consecutive start, and his streak of consecutive innings without an earned run reached 19 1/3. The game was decided in one-run fashion: Texas scored its only run in the third inning, and Seattle took the lead in the sixth after a defensive miscue and RBI singles by Nelson Cruz and Kyle Seager. James Pazos recorded the final out of the seventh, Alex Colome and Edwin Diaz combined to pitch the eighth and ninth, and Diaz earned his 19th save. The Mariners noted multiple one-run wins recently, and the passage also includes injury and roster updates for both teams and upcoming pitching matchups.

According to FCA data from its 2017 Financial Lives Survey, up to 70% of adults planning to access defined contribution pensions in the next two years said their providers had not asked how they would access their pensions. Only 2% said some providers asked about options, while 20% said all providers contacted them; 8% did not know. Just over two thirds (67%) said they had not received advice from an adviser at their pension provider about options for when they start to take money, with 16% receiving advice from their provider and 10% from a different provider; 9% did not know. For those without advice, 40% said they could decide themselves and 10% said they couldn’t afford or didn’t want to pay fees. When asked about expected largest income source in retirement, 33% said state pension, 21% said their DC pot, and 15% said final salary. Regarding knowledge of expected annual retirement income, 44% said they have a good idea, 28% had little or no idea, and 17% did not know.

The passage describes how the COVID-19 pandemic led many countries to interrupt formal education and adopt distance education, highlighting the need to improve and differentiate distance education methods. It presents a literature review focused on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted or AI-based training as a type of distance education. The text explains basic AI concepts such as algorithms, machine learning, artificial neural networks, and deep learning, and gives examples including IBM’s Watson, Alphabet’s Alphago, and Google Car. It then discusses AI in education, including potential uses like personalized teaching systems, student support, data management, and Intelligent Education Systems (IES), which use domain, pedagogy, and learner models and can provide feedback and adaptive learning. The passage outlines possible AI education types (AI-supported face-to-face, face-to-face with AI, and simulation with AI), scenarios for AI teaching methods, and learning environments including classroom-based and online/virtual simulation. In the discussion, it notes expected benefits such as efficiency and reduced training costs/risks, alongside potential negatives including control fears, privacy concerns, isolation, unemployment for educators, psychological impacts, and difficulties returning to real life. The conclusions emphasize the increasing relevance of distance education and suggest that AI-based and simulation/augmented reality approaches warrant further research, while also calling for mental and philosophical preparation for possible future changes.

The passage argues that improving school air quality through installing air filters and upgrading ventilation can boost student outcomes. It cites research from the Aliso Canyon, California natural gas leak, where schools within a five-mile radius received commercial air purifiers, and those students showed improved math and English test scores that persisted and grew. The passage compares costs favorably to class-size reduction and suggests air cleaning may outperform other high-impact U.S. interventions for cost. It also summarizes growing evidence that portable air cleaners reduce absenteeism and improve performance on high-stakes exams, and describes potential pathways including cognitive effects, health improvements, and reduced educational inequality. It recommends reconnecting devices, installing new filters, piloting and scaling portable cleaners with target performance goals, monitoring attendance and related metrics, and involving philanthropy, advocates, and researchers to expand programs and trials.

State officials, including Gov. David Ige, attended a Wednesday groundbreaking for the new Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. The project will add gate capacity for larger aircraft and 260,000 square feet of environmentally friendly space, including a connecting walkway to Terminal 1, passenger boarding areas, restrooms, and agricultural screening for domestic departures. Construction is expected to be completed by the end of 2020 at a cost of $220 million. The modernization effort also includes a five-level rental car structure by 2021 and is part of a $1.3 billion airport upgrade.

El neuromarketing surge desde los años noventa con la incorporación de técnicas de las neurociencias al marketing para incrementar la efectividad de las acciones comerciales. Se define como la aplicación de técnicas de neuroimagen para entender la conducta humana en relación con los mercados e intercambios. Aunque se considera una disciplina en etapa inicial, se plantea como metodología complementaria que puede responder a necesidades de la industria audiovisual en evolución para mejorar su competitividad y el ROI. La aparición de plataformas digitales y cambios en el consumo audiovisual impulsan la investigación para mantener la posición de mercado, y diversas empresas mediáticas ya emplean técnicas de neuromarketing, con usos como test de contenidos, evaluación de efectividad promocional y mejora de bloques publicitarios.

En España, el artículo desarrolla una investigación cualitativa para determinar el estado del neuromarketing en el sector audiovisual. El estudio se basa en entrevistas en profundidad a 18 expertos de empresas consultoras de neuromarketing, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos, y en el análisis de empresas para conformar la muestra. Los resultados señalan la factibilidad de estudiar al consumidor audiovisual con técnicas neurocientíficas, pero con limitaciones vinculadas a la ética, la interpretación de los datos y dificultades de muestreo. También se destaca que la investigación requiere equipos multidisciplinares y seguir protocolos del método científico. Se concluye que la introducción de las neurociencias en la medición audiovisual española es incipiente: las principales barreras incluyen desconocimiento, desconfianza y miedo, mala praxis, falta de actitud innovadora, precio y falta de aplicabilidad a la industria. La implantación se concentra en pocos clientes, especialmente en Atresmedia y Mediaset España, donde se describen estudios de contenido de ficción y bloques publicitarios con tecnologías como EEG y registros biométricos, entre otros. Finalmente, se plantea que la evolución futura sería positiva, condicionada por el desarrollo tecnológico, la estandarización, la mejora de interpretación de datos y el abaratamiento, aunque su consolidación depende de demostrar eficacia en términos de retorno de inversión.

The passage says the Great Barrier Reef is suffering climate change impacts and that other Australian ecosystems are also near collapse. It describes Nature Climate Change research finding sudden, catastrophic ecosystem shifts across Australia caused by combined gradual climate change and extreme weather events that overwhelm natural resilience. It notes Australia’s average temperature has risen by about 1°C since the 19th century and reports more intense heatwaves, fire conditions, altered rainfall, and unusual droughts. The passage states that shorter intervals between extreme events reduce recovery and that climate change is expected to increase the magnitude and frequency of extremes. It lists six ecosystem case studies showing major changes after events such as marine heatwaves, wildfire, drought, repeated fires, extreme rainfall, and weak monsoons. It argues that ecosystem collapse can occur when “presses” and “pulses” push systems toward tipping points, sometimes via single extreme events or when declines have already begun. The passage says consequences include loss of key species and functions such as fish supply, forest resources, and carbon storage, and that predicting collapses is essentially impossible. It adds that interventions like assisted recolonisation and protecting ecosystems from destructive bushfires may prevent collapse but at financial cost, with decreasing success likelihood as extreme-event intervals shorten, requiring decisions under uncertainty. It concludes that many ecosystems may already be at tipping points.

The passage describes a retrospective cohort study examining whether social determinants of health (SDOH) can predict “healthy aging.” Healthy aging was defined using composite measures of comorbidities, cognitive conditions, and mobility function. The study used registered tier data from the All of Us Research Program, including participants aged 50 and older who responded to SDOH survey questions with available EHR data. Three machine learning models (logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost) were trained, with performance evaluated using AUROC and fairness assessed using predictive parity across race and sex; feature importance was examined using SHAP values. The best model was XGBoost, which achieved AUROC around 0.793 in the primary analysis and showed similar positive and negative predictive values across race and sex groups. Health insurance type was identified as the most predictive feature, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The authors conclude that the XGBoost model accurately predicts healthy aging and that health insurance plays a significant role in healthy aging.

Index Markets Research provides a report on the Global Plastic Granules Market, describing the industry definition, applications, manufacturing technology, market size estimates, and trends. It includes analysis of key players, business drivers and dynamics, segmentation by commercial, government, and personal, and geographic segmentation with production, consumption, revenue, market share, and growth rate from 2012 to 2022 (forecast) across regions including North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan & India. The report also covers volume (k MT) and revenue (Million USD), product types (PP, HDPE, PPCP, LLDPE, LDPE, Others), end users/applications (Plastic products, Clothing, Others), manufacturing cost structure, production capacity considerations, and includes new project SWOT, investment practicalness and development trend analysis.

The Bengals will start Joe Flacco at quarterback against the Packers, according to Zac Taylor. Cincinnati completed a trade one day before naming Flacco the starter, sending a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Browns in exchange for Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick. Taylor said Flacco will take all reps to prepare for Sunday and noted Flacco has watched Packers game tape after playing them earlier this season. Flacco has also played the Bengals this year, when he threw 31-of-45 passes for 290 yards, 1 touchdown, and 2 interceptions in a 17-16 Bengals loss. Cincinnati made the quarterback change while Joe Burrow is on injured reserve recovering from left-foot surgery, and Browning has started the past three games; Taylor confirmed Browning will return to backup with another former Packer on the practice squad as reserve. Taylor said the team’s focus is winning games and making the playoffs, regardless of quarterback, and Burrow’s return timetable was not provided.
