Stocks rallied Monday as better-than-expected quarterly earnings reports boosted investor sentiment, with major U.S. indexes rising and bonds mixed. The rally was partly tempered by reports of an anthrax scare involving Washington, D.C., postal workers and by concern over weaker corporate profits ahead. American Express shares rose after its earnings beat expectations, while Enron shares fell sharply after Enron said the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Multiple reports and lawsuits described allegations that Enron’s board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to create and run limited partnerships, which were linked to large charges, losses, and reductions in shareholder equity. Separately, UniPrime Capital announced a letter of intent for a wind energy park ground lease involving a subsidiary of Enron Wind Development Corp.

The passage describes a study that uses real-world telematics data from an Italian province (Asti) to simulate replacing internal combustion engine vehicles with battery electric vehicles (BEVs) under different charging behaviors. It focuses on four charging scenarios (two AC workplace/home options and two “charge only when low SoC” options, one with overnight fast availability and one with DC fast charging) and four BEV models with different battery capacities and consumption profiles. Trip replication keeps users’ original itineraries and updates state of charge (SoC) per trip based on road-type consumption; trips are marked infeasible when SoC reaches 0. Metrics include percentage of feasible trips, number of monthly charging sessions, and average SoC after each trip. Results show charging only during working hours (Scenario 1) performs worst, while the best overall feasibility comes from charging with DC fast sessions when SoC is below 25% (Scenario 4). Even with the most favorable policy and the largest battery vehicle, full trip completion for all users is not achieved; the study also notes limitations such as simplified energy-consumption and charging-power assumptions and the omission of costs and charger availability details.

IES Holdings, Inc is described as a diversified infrastructure services provider whose stock has nearly doubled year-to-date and has outperformed other infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks. The company’s residential division is described as facing a challenging period, while data centre projects are helping other major divisions. Its backlog has exceeded $2 billion and is growing 20% year-over-year, with improved cash flow generation and record cash balances supporting its financial profile. Despite this momentum, the passage says the stock is overextended, not supported by a sub-par FCF yield, and has had higher insider sales.

Kevin Deery said his side were frustrated after their third consecutive draw, conceding a share of the spoils to Larne at Drumahoe. He stated that his team created enough chances to win but has lacked “luck” recently, citing missed opportunities and goals conceded from a wide free-kick that dipped over defenders. Deery also said poor decision-making in both boxes is affecting results and noted several near chances by players including Ciaron Harkin, Gareth Brown, and Dean Curry, who hit the bar or post. He added that his team remains in the top six with three fixtures before the split and 13 games left.

The passage discusses the ACC Tournament’s two-year run at Barclays Center, ending with Virginia’s 71–63 championship win over North Carolina, and mentions Virginia coach Tony Bennett quoting Psalm 133 before the game. It also references related ACC Tournament developments and games involving Virginia, North Carolina, and Duke, as well as future expectations and draft prospects.

The passage is a compilation of news items and commentary dated Feb. 6, 2002, about the Enron collapse and related investigations. It includes accounts of congressional hearings and subpoenas involving former Enron executives such as Jeffrey Skilling and Kenneth Lay, testimony by William Powers about Enron’s partnerships and losses, and criticism of Arthur Andersen’s role. Other sections cover Enron’s ongoing bankruptcy-related financing challenges, a dispute over back taxes owed by Enron Broadband Services, and the Houston Astros’ efforts to change the “Enron Field” naming rights. Additional pieces discuss corporate bond market impacts associated with “Enronization,” a Spanish regulator investigation, and opinion/editorial reactions to the scandal.

After speculation about whether a story involving former Maui County Councilmember Mike Victorino hitting two kids in an auto collision was true, The Maui News reported on April 17 that the incident occurred and that everyone was doing fine. The paper said Victorino was the driver, was not under the influence of alcohol and was not speeding, and that the car was traveling no faster than 25 miles per hour. Police said two teens stepped into the roadway at 9:30 p.m. on April 13 and attempted to cross toward Luana Gardens, that Victorino stopped and waited for police and emergency personnel, and that both young men had nonlife-threatening injuries. The initial investigation reportedly found the pedestrians were not in a crosswalk, but the mother of the older male said her son told her the teens had been in a crosswalk at the time.

The passage describes the linebacker position as requiring toughness, athleticism, and intelligence. Linebackers help organize the defense, stop both the run and pass, and play as a second line of defense positioned 3–5 yards behind the defensive line. They relay coach calls, function as a high-IQ “quarterback of the defense,” take on blocks, drop into zones, and sometimes match running backs or slot receivers. The name “linebacker” comes from aligning behind the defensive line and historically supporting the defensive line in run support. It lists linebacker types (Sam, Mike, Will, Jack) and required skills and body type traits. It also names Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor as standout linebackers and discusses the position’s importance despite changing NFL trends.

The passage describes a tug-of-war between the Bank of Canada and the market over the Canadian dollar (“loonie”). The Bank of Canada appears to want a lower dollar to benefit Canadian exporters, while the market, seeing economic strength, has pushed the loonie higher; it was nearly 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, about 2% higher than the previous week. Stephen Poloz’s comments about challenges for exports are presented as a signal that the bank does not want the loonie to get too strong yet. The passage also reviews the loonie’s recent volatility, saying it is influenced mainly by oil prices and the interest-rate gap between Canada and the U.S. It notes that oil prices fell below US$45 and that the U.S. Federal Reserve increased its target range to 1.0 to 1.25%, while Canada’s policy rate has remained at 0.5%. Finally, it says economic data and recent Bank of Canada statements have led CIBC economist Andrew Grantham to expect a rate increase in the fourth quarter, earlier than previously expected.

During a Thursday Board of Governors meeting, Colorado State University student leaders and athletics officials discussed feedback and logistics from the first two on-campus games at the stadium. ASCSU President Josh Silva said students had limited awareness of the tailgating lot and that the lot was often used mainly for parking; ASCSU has rebranded the lot and plans pre-game programming to encourage longer tailgating. Athletics director Joe Parker reported that attendance was 37,000-plus for the opening game and 27,000 for the second, with improved stadium entry and concession congestion in the second game. He said two-and-a-half years of planning helped, including identifying campus parking for gameday patrons; student re-parking was reported as successful with 50 vehicles towed so far. CSU public affairs director Mike Hooker reported that about half of towed cars were not registered with CSU Parking and Transportation Services, and that the City of Fort Collins towed a similar number from nearby neighborhood streets. Hooker also said planned transit usage predictions increased, and Parker said post-game traffic was not overwhelmed, citing use of the MAX system and Park-and-Ride options.

The passage describes a study on social engineering and how demographic and appearance-based cues (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity, attire) can shape trust and risk-taking decisions. It argues that social engineering exploits human behavior using emotional and authoritative cues delivered through channels such as emails, calls, or body language, and that people may rely on heuristics that place trust based on demographic characteristics rather than accurate risk assessment. To reduce these risks, the study proposes role-taking and literacy interventions focused on increasing awareness of unconscious biases and persuasion tactics, and it outlines a 4×2 online experiment (four groups: two role-taking roles, a literacy group, and a control group) with pre- and post-intervention measures taken one week apart using hotspot trust and risk scenarios. Measures include risk-taking and trust ratings, word of mouth, and issue involvement, with repeated measures ANOVAs used for analysis. The results report no significant intervention effects on trust or risk-taking across persona factors and roles, limited effects on word of mouth, and a significant but role-unclear change in issue involvement (participants’ involvement decreased). The discussion emphasizes that biases appeared resistant to short-term intervention, highlights study limitations (imagined scenarios rather than real-life experience), and concludes that longer-term or more immersive strategies may be needed for lasting change.

The Great Southern Storm have announced an initial colts squad of 45 players for the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin next month, under new coach Glynn Verbruggen. The squad will have two training sessions before the final travelling team is selected, and Verbruggen will replace long-time mentor Phil Gilbert, who moved to Perth after coaching the Storm for seven of the past eight years. Verbruggen has previously won the Sean Plaisted Medal in 2008 and has senior coaching experience, and he said he is excited to help talented regional players. The squad includes State 16 members Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, and players from multiple clubs, with North Albany having the most representation. Training is scheduled at Railways on June 4 and 11 from 5.30pm.

The District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai awarded death sentence, imprisonment terms, and fines to four convicts in separate murder cases. Shehzado was sentenced to death and fined Rs. 200,000 under section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code after being found guilty of stabbing a man following harsh words. Ajab Khan and Fateh Khan were sentenced to 25 years’ imprisonment and each ordered to pay Rs. 200,000. Dilbar Khan was given 25 years’ imprisonment and fined Rs. 105,000. Advocate Samad Khan Mandokhail followed the cases for the victims’ families.

Taxify, a ride-sharing company launching in Sydney, will start servicing residents Tuesday morning with half-priced fares for one month. The company says it has more than 4,000 registered drivers in Sydney and is entering Australia for the first time. Taxify claims its commission is 15%, nearly half of what Uber takes from its drivers, and its business model is based on “fairness and transparency.” The app already operates in 20 countries and is financially backed by Didi Chuxing, with surge pricing on public holidays capped at 1.5 times the usual rate. NSW Trade and Industry Minister Niall Blair welcomed the investment.

Allen Iverson discussed sobriety and the lowest point of his life in an ESPN “First Take” interview about his new memoir, “Misunderstood.” He said his lowest point was self-inflicted and tied to his divorce from Tawanna Turner, which finalized in 2013 and coincided with the end of his NBA career. He described hitting that point in a courtroom while the divorce papers were in front of him, and said he later realized alcohol was a major problem. Iverson also confirmed he and Turner are back together and said he had to “beg a lot” to get her back, including help from Keith Sweat.

The passage argues that Germany needs to organize territories under its influence to later complete its scheme and use Middle Europe’s resources and manpower for its foreign policy, posing four critical problems involving the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. It says U.S. interests should focus on preventing a system that allows Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest to exploit the area for selfish foreign policy, distinguishing between regional unification and how control is exercised. It describes Middle Europe’s control as an alliance of interests among ruling powers in Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, Constantinople, and Berlin, tied to subjection of certain peoples, German control over Austria-Hungary’s external affairs and resources, German-Magyar ascendency, Bulgaria’s exploitation linked to the treaty of Bucharest, possible nominal integrity for the Turkish Empire, and debts after the war. It then outlines objectives to make Middle Europe safe and lists U.S. assets and liabilities, emphasizing economic commercial control over the outer world and potential German exclusion as a main weapon, plus assets in Austria-Hungary, including Czech and South Slav nationalistic discontent and Austria-Hungary rulers’ desire to preserve Francis Joseph’s patrimony through no annexations, disarmament, and a league of nations. The proposed policy is to stir up nationalist discontent while refusing its extreme logic, to reduce resistance to changes and accelerate a move away from Berlin in foreign affairs.

Texas public school administrators, parents, and education experts say a new Texas law replacing STAAR with three tests could increase student stress and testing time rather than reduce them. Supporters say the change is meant to ease pressure from a single end-of-year exam by replacing it with shorter early-, mid-, and end-of-year tests and banning practice tests. The law also directs the Texas Education Agency to study how to reduce the role testing plays in school accountability ratings, but findings are not due until 2029-30 and are not required to be implemented, leading some critics to say the overall pressure and accountability weight will remain similar. Schools can choose early and mid-year assessments from a TEA-approved menu, while TEA creates the third test, and scores are to be released about two days after exams so teachers can adjust instruction. Administrators also worry that TEA could require lockdown-style testing protocols, and some educators want more input from teachers on the end-of-year test.

Portability, performance, and productivity are presented as critical dimensions for long-term adoption of programming framework designs. The passage contrasts traditional HPC and computational science frameworks (e.g., C++, Fortran, MPI/OpenMP/OpenACC, and abstractions like Kokkos and related libraries) that emphasize performance and portability but less productivity, with AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow) that emphasize productivity and portability but rely on manual interfacing to optimized libraries and can be difficult to extend to new architectures. It hypothesizes that an extensible compiler framework supporting performance, portability, and productivity would enable better computational science and rapid algorithm development in AI/ML, and describes a first challenge focused on developing such a compiler framework based on lessons learned from Kokkos. The passage then outlines LAPIS, a performance-portable, high-productivity, extensible compiler framework built using MLIR, including a custom Kokkos dialect, mappings for Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations to MLIR, lowering passes to support accelerators, a memory model inspired by Kokkos (DualView), and an emitter to generate Kokkos-based C++ code. It also summarizes related work, background on Kokkos/MLIR/Kokkos Kernels, and details aspects of LAPIS’s lowering pipeline, particularly a pass that maps nested parallel loops to Kokkos constructs with heuristics and synchronization insertion.

The passage outlines a paper on constructing strong pseudorandom unitaries (strong PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM). It defines PRUs and strong PRUs, summarizes prior work on pseudorandom primitives in QHROM and related models (including inverseless QHROM), and motivates studying QHROM for its ability to provide insights into heuristic constructions. The paper’s main result is Theorem 1.1 stating that strong PRUs exist in QHROM, with a construction described as \(G_U(1^\lambda,k)=X_{k_3}U_\lambda X_{k_2}U_\lambda X_{k_1}\), using two queries to the Haar random oracle. The technical overview explains the use of Ma–Huang’s path-recording framework, replacement of Haar random unitaries with path-recording isometries, and an analysis approach based on defining an approximate merge isometry \(S\) and performing query-by-query progress measurements. It also includes a staged hybrid argument (from the real experiment with the PRU and Haar oracle to the ideal experiment with two independent Haar unitaries) and preliminary definitions and notation for later lemmas and the path-recording framework.

Chipotle released a new queso dip on Sept. 12 to increase sales, but customers have complained about its taste and price. A small order of chips and queso costs $3.95 and a large order costs $6.25, which some say is too expensive. On Twitter, some users expressed disappointment and said the queso tastes microwaved. BuzzFeed reported that Chipotle spokesman Chris Arnold said 63% of test-market tasters were more likely to visit more often and that there are no plans to lower the price because it uses only real, whole ingredients that cost more.

The passage is an email notice for the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for Wednesday, May 23, 2001. It directs readers to a link if they cannot access the e-Journal and provides instructions for receiving a plain-text version. It lists practice areas with case summaries, including Bankruptcy and Constitutional Law (noting one U.S. Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals opinion summarized under both). It also references other sections such as Other Editorial, a Townhall Forum, Classified listings (with examples of areas covered), Fields of Practice listings, Bar Events, and archived e-Journals. The passage further includes multiple case summaries across areas including Civil Rights, Employment & Labor Law, Criminal Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Real Property, Negligence & Intentional Tort, and provides extensive advertising/partner listings by practice area.

The email forwards an Energy Central “Deregulation Public Forum” question dated August 25, 2000, asking whether federal policy should encourage natural gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf, given expectations of high winter gas prices due to exploration budget cutbacks and drilling restrictions. It lists a response deadline of September 15, 2000 (5 P.M. MDT) and states that selected short responses will be published. The message also includes a section titled “Previous Question” about whether wholesale market price spikes in San Diego were caused by deliberate generator manipulation and whether price caps should be imposed, followed by multiple submitted responses discussing causes of price spikes, market rules, and views on price caps and deregulation.

The passage describes CEMEX’s approach to globalizing through acquisitions and post-merger integration. It highlights key deals, including the 1992 acquisitions in Spain, the 2005 acquisition of RMC, and the 2007 majority stake in Rinker, while noting financial impacts such as share price declines during the 2008 downturn. Much of CEMEX’s success is attributed to its post-merger integration process known internally as “the CEMEX Way,” which standardized business processes and knowledge while encouraging continuous improvement and innovation through internal benchmarking and specialized standardization teams. The company’s internationalization is presented in stages—laying groundwork, stepping out, growing up, and stepping up—along with major milestones and changes in integration practices. The case also includes an industry overview of heavy building materials and cement’s characteristics, market structure, and consumption patterns.

Bayern Munich has given Paul Clement permission to speak to Swansea, after Swansea parted with Bob Bradley following a 4-1 Boxing Day loss to West Ham. Swansea have chosen Clement to replace Bradley, and aim to finalize his deal at Liberty Stadium until 2019 before handing him a £30 million transfer budget to help the team avoid relegation. Swansea owners Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan have indicated they are willing to invest. Clement previously worked with Carlo Ancelotti at Bayern, after they had worked together at Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and Clement had a brief stint at Derby in 2015-16. Swansea are 19th in the Premier League and have conceded 44 goals in 19 games, with Neil Taylor saying players would support Clement if he is appointed.

Riots occurred in East Berlin in June 1953 and in Poznań, Poland, in June 1956, both suppressed by direct Soviet troop intervention. The Hungarian revolt in 1956 became a nationwide event and its Soviet repression was a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO. After Hungary was overrun by the Soviet army in 1944, communist rule expanded through repression and collectivization. Following Stalin’s death, Mátyás Rákosi was instructed to appoint Imre Nagy as prime minister, but Nagy was replaced after a heart attack in 1955. In early 1956, discontent grew due to perceptions of irresolute leadership, economic failure, and increased repression influenced by Soviet suppression of the Polish revolt, alongside encouragement from Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization and Soviet leadership visits to Yugoslavia. In July 1956 Rákosi was dismissed and replaced by Erno Gero, and in October 1956 unrest in Poland led to Władysław Gomułka’s release and appointment, influencing Hungarian demands. A radio confrontation between Rákosi and the AVH led to revolutionary councils calling for nationalism, neutrality, and withdrawal of Soviet troops, while the Soviet leadership was alarmed. Soviet tanks entered Budapest on 24 October; Mikoyan and Suslov visited on 24–26 October, dismissed the old guard, confirmed Nagy’s appointment, and replaced Gero with János Kádár. External events diverted attention when the Suez crisis began at the end of October, and the Soviet army surrounded Budapest on 1 November using about 250,000 troops and 2,500 armored vehicles. After concessions, the Soviet Union attacked at midnight on 3/4 November, and Budapest became a battlefield. Main fighting ended by 14 November and all resistance collapsed by 30 November, with about 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers killed.

A federal judge in New York, U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas, dismissed rapper Drake’s defamation lawsuit over Kendrick Lamar’s 2024 song “Not Like Us,” in which Lamar called Drake a “certified pedophile.” The judge said Lamar’s lyrics were “nonactionable opinion” made in a heated rap battle with offensive accusations, and she granted Universal Music Group’s motion to dismiss claims including defamation, harassment, and deceptive acts. Drake plans to appeal, according to a spokesperson.

A Massachusetts police officer in Springfield, Conrad Lariviere, faces disciplinary action after posting on Facebook comments about a car striking and killing a counter-protester at a white supremacist rally in Virginia. He later apologized, calling his comment “stupid” and saying he is not a racist. Springfield Police Commissioner John Barbieri said he received a complaint and initiated an internal investigation, and the matter would be reviewed by the Community Police Hearings Board if the post came from an officer. Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the comments. Lariviere is a member of the Springfield Police Academy’s 2014 graduating class, and an Associated Press message was not immediately returned.

The passage describes parts of the DAWN-PLASMA study protocol, including ethics and consent procedures, study conduct in line with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice, and planned measurements, adverse-event grading, and study endpoints. The DAWN-PLASMA study is a randomized, open-label phase 2 multicenter trial in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 evaluating standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone, with a primary endpoint of % alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 and additional clinical, safety, laboratory, and quality-of-life outcomes. It lists key inclusion and exclusion criteria for participants, notes that IEC review and approval of protocol amendments and informed consent documentation occurred before study initiation, and specifies requirements for reporting serious and/or unexpected adverse events. The study enrolled participants and reports that five withdrew consent before intervention and one was a screen failure before intervention; these six were substituted and no participants were lost to follow-up after intervention. Convalescent plasma was administered to hospitalized patients as 800–1000 mL in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and subsequent dosing between 24 and 36 hours after the first infusion, allowing lower-volume release only in exceptional scarcity; plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was not permitted.

Williams & Connolly confirmed that hackers accessed “a small number” of its attorneys’ email accounts via a zero-day attack but said there is no evidence of further access to its information technology system or extraction of confidential client data from any other part of the network, including client-file databases. The firm believes the hackers are affiliated with a nation-state actor tied to recent attacks on law firms and companies, and it has taken steps to block the threat with no evidence of unauthorized traffic. The incident follows a warning that hackers linked to the Chinese government have targeted firms and seek information related to U.S. national security and international trade.

The passage describes video output data signals that represent the 8 most significant bits of different components (G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR). It states how these signals map in various modes: in RGB mode they correspond to green, blue, or red data bits; in YUV444 mode they correspond to Y, Cb, or Cr data bits; in Y/C mode they are multiplexed luma or chroma data bits; and in BT.656 mode the signals are multiplexed for luma/chroma or unused for the B/CB/C case. It also includes brief definitions of I, O, Z, S, GND, A, and MM, and notes that IPD/IPU/DIS relate to internal pulldown/pullup behavior after reset, referring to additional sections for details.

Coppin State, a historically Black university in Maryland, says its Expand Eagle Nation program is boosting enrollment and name recognition, including more than quadrupling out-of-state student enrollment over the past two years. The program offers in-state tuition to students from 41 U.S. states and territories without an HBCU and to the District of Columbia; in 2024, the number of qualifying-state students rose to 195 from 81. This fall, 416 of Coppin’s 1,000-person incoming class came from qualifying states, and overall enrollment is up 26 percent, with growth on the in-state side as well. The university attributes some of this change to increased attention and recruitment efforts, including high school visits and advertisements, and says it is preparing for student growth by adding housing and ensuring enough courses and faculty. It also notes a challenge in convincing prospective students that the tuition offer is real.

The passage describes how to enable a TPS7H500x-SP device via the EN pin, including direct connection to VLDO, external signaling/PGOOD for sequencing, or a two-resistor divider configuration that sets turn-on thresholds and undervoltage lockout (UVLO) thresholds with hysteresis. It provides equations and guidance for selecting RUVLO_TOP and RUVLO_BOT to achieve a UVLO value of about 75% or less of the input voltage to ensure reliable turn-on. It then outlines the device’s internal 1.23-V bandgap reference and voltage reference divider, the error amplifier operation, output voltage programming using a resistor divider to VSENSE, soft-start behavior controlled by a capacitor on SS, and switching frequency modes using RT and SYNC pins (internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary synchronization). The passage further covers primary and synchronous rectifier output behavior, dead time and leading edge blank time programmability, pulse skipping conditions, duty cycle limits via DCL, current sense and PWM generation via CS_ILIM and COMP, hiccup mode operation with HICC, external fault protection via FAULT, slope compensation, frequency compensation options, and thermal shutdown thresholds. It also summarizes device functional modes and includes application/design discussion and layout guidelines.

The passage describes the completion of a government change in which Democrats gained majorities in the House and Senate and assumed the presidency and vice-presidency. It argues that the meaning of the change goes beyond party success, aiming to reinterpret the nation’s plans and to replace old, harmful conditions with renewed insight. It praises the nation’s material and moral achievements, including government and sympathy, but criticizes waste, neglect of human costs, and the misuse of government for private purposes. The passage proposes restoring national processes according to justice, listing areas to change such as tariffs, banking and currency, industrial and agricultural systems, and undeveloped or wasted natural resources. It also emphasizes government duties in safeguarding health and rights through laws, maintaining justice as the motto, and frames the effort as a dedicated, nationwide task requiring honest and patriotic support.

Indianapolis Public Schools is holding a Board of School Commissioners meeting Tuesday at 6 p.m. at Thomas D. Gregg School 15 to let parents and community members comment on a proposal to close three high schools. The Facilities Utilization Taskforce’s months-long report, released last week, recommends closing three high schools by the 2018–2019 school year, citing a long-term decline in the district’s student population. The report says all seven high schools are under capacity, and it estimates the current high school population could be served in three schools, though operating four would provide more flexibility. Public input will continue through April and May, with administration recommendations expected by June and a board vote on closures in September. Additional meetings are scheduled on April 26, May 1, May 11, and May 15.

Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) detects changes in surface objects or environmental conditions using remote sensing images from different time periods. Traditional methods using thresholding, morphological analysis, and image algebra are sensitive to interference such as seasonal changes, lighting changes, and shadows, leading to performance degradation. Deep learning methods improve accuracy but may struggle to capture long-range context; challenges like limited data, high annotation cost, and complex multi-source fusion remain. The passage presents a visual-linguistic multi-modal approach called LG-CD, which uses a pre-trained SAM2 encoder for shared visual feature extraction and CLIP for text feature extraction. It includes a text fusion attention module to align text with visual features and a visual-semantic fusion decoder to generate change detection masks. The method includes multi-level adapters for fine-tuning SAM2 and is described as improving semantic understanding, detection accuracy, and generalization.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet that led to her ABC sitcom’s cancellation, while Trump and Sarah Sanders also argued that they were owed an apology from ABC for airing derogatory comments about the administration. Sanders expanded on what she described as a double standard, citing examples of media figures criticizing Trump. She said the President was calling out media bias and that no one was defending Barr’s comments, though she also noted that Trump was focused on other matters, including a “right to try” bill.

Kyle Shanahan said practice went well, with both sides battling and the defense performing strongly in the red zone while the offense edged it out overall. He discussed his father, who watches tape and shares ideas but is not considered part of his staff; Shanahan said he is not seeking counsel due to limited time, though having an additional set of eyes helps. Shanahan also said he plans to take time to recover and relax before training camp, describing it as the calm before the storm. He called play-action important to his offensive philosophy because it puts defenses in binds, helps the offense take pressure off the offensive line and quarterbacks, and helps generate explosive plays while keeping the defense honest.

The passage is a poker lecture covering post-flop play and hand-selection principles through examples. It explains how checking or betting after the flop depends on ranges, pot size, and stack depth, including advice on bet sizing (often around half the pot on the flop and larger fractions later). It introduces the idea that bets should serve either value (with strong hands) or bluffing (with weak hands), and that middle-strength hands often check. The lecture discusses when to continuation-bet, when to fold most missed flops, and when calling is reasonable, including factors like being out of position and effective stack size. It distinguishes implied odds from reverse implied odds, giving examples such as set-mining and draw-based calls, and warns against weak draws when reverse implied odds are likely. It also covers bluffing with draws, “bluffing epiphanies” about counting outs and considering what hand ranges you represent, and examples where giving up on a bluff is correct. It concludes by summarizing topics covered: continuation betting, range “respect” to the preflop raiser, betting strategy, leading, implied odds/reverse implied odds, set mining, bluffing with draws, and two bluffing epiphanies.

The email message titled “Energy Issues” lists multiple news articles about California’s energy crisis. The included excerpts describe lawmakers debating competing rescue plans to keep Southern California Edison from bankruptcy, including options involving state purchase or partial buyout of transmission lines or a straightforward debt bailout. Other excerpts cover Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E) suing the state for compensation related to seized long-term power contracts, and a consumer advocate criticizing Gov. Gray Davis’ proposed San Diego Gas & Electric rescue plan as too generous. Additional items report changes in consumer inflation tied to moderating energy costs, local conservation upgrades in Contra Costa County, and the sale of surplus state power at losses amid lower demand and prices.

Prof. Cyril Dim explains that cervical cancer is a malignancy of the cervix, which is accessible through the vagina. He says it is caused in almost all cases by human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly high-risk oncogenic types such as HPV 16 and 18, which are covered by HPV vaccines; he states that apart from HPV, nothing else causes it. He describes a pre-cancer stage without symptoms, detectable by Pap smear to prevent progression, and distinguishes early, late, and terminal stages, with symptoms later including bleeding after sex and foul-smelling discharge; late-stage symptoms may include weight loss, weakness, anaemia, pelvic pain, and loss of control of urine or faeces depending on spread. Diagnosis is confirmed by cervical tissue biopsy and histology; he recommends Pap smear screening for women of reproductive age at least every three years and later every five years, and notes evaluation includes history questions and use of a speculum. He states sex with a man poses no risk to him, though men can carry HPV. He reports outcomes are poor when women present late but improved when found early; survival in late stage may increase to five years with appropriate management, while terminal cases are measured in months. He says cervical cancer is a major cancer burden in Nigeria due to lack of structured screening, with estimates of about 15,000 new cases and about 10,000 deaths yearly in Nigeria. He notes pregnancy is possible in early-stage disease with no symptoms but unlikely in late-stage. Treatment depends on stage: early-stage options include radical surgery or radiotherapy, while late-stage aims to prolong life using radiotherapy and often chemotherapy; surgery is not an option for late stage. He also mentions that myths may attribute illness to witchcraft in a religious context.

A federal judge ruled that a 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill is not pornography. The judge dismissed the 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who said he was depicted as a minor; the ruling considered factors including the depiction’s focal point, setting, whether the child is nude, and whether it is intended to elicit a sexual response. The judge said no factor brought the image within the child pornography statute, except that Elden was nude, and wrote the image was insufficient to support a finding of lasciviousness.

The passage describes the precise estimation of polynomial functionals of an m-qubit state ρ, especially purity Tr(ρ^2) and higher-order moments Tr(ρ^k) that determine Rényi entropies of order k. It states that these moments are important in quantum information science, statistical mechanics, and many-body physics, underpin measures of entanglement and coherence, and serve as primitives in randomness certification protocols.

The passage is a hockey-related discussion focused on Ottawa’s performance and adjustments for upcoming games in Ottawa. The speaker says they believe they have a better team than what they have shown in two games and that they need to prove it, noting there are no guarantees. They discuss factors including faceoffs, puck possession, discipline, forechecking, positioning, turnovers, and offensive strategy versus a team that plays defensively like Anaheim. The speaker provides updates on Chris Neil, whose wife is having a baby today, and mentions expectations for goaltending and specific players’ roles and lines, including Pahlsson’s line and Rob Niedermayer. They also express expectations for a strong, emotional home crowd and plan to use the fourth line more in the next game.

The passage argues that Artificial Intelligence is increasingly present in education, boosted partly by the COVID-19 pandemic, and that education cannot be separated from technology. It presents the goal of introducing AI in education as developing human capital for 21st-century citizens, guided by principles of learning, self-correction, and reasoning. It describes how AI can influence higher education by supporting teaching and learning (e.g., personalized learning and intelligent tutoring), aiding research (e.g., literature review and data analysis), and streamlining administration. It also outlines potential AI applications and advantages, and lists challenges including equity, ethics and security, training needs, student-related issues, financial costs, organizational and policy concerns, and limitations related to AI’s nature. The passage concludes that AI’s application will shape higher education in positive and negative ways, and calls for discussion and analysis of AI-related competencies, guided use, and continued research.

The speaker says they were surprised to be put back into the lineup, despite having not played for two weeks, and that they stayed positive and focused on doing their job to help the team win. They describe being told late the previous night by Pat, feeling nervous during their return, dropping their stick, and trying to follow the puck. The passage also discusses the team’s achievement of three Cups in nine years, a difficult season, changes in personnel, and praise for Pat’s coaching style as focused and no-nonsense, keeping the team and players from getting complacent.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff in BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found a shift toward Democrats in 2023–2024: 92.45% of contributions went to Democrats, versus a roughly 12-to-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio that was “significantly up” from a 6-to-1 ratio in a 2021 analysis of 2017–2020. Derek Muller, a University of Notre Dame Law School professor, estimated about $52 million was contributed to Democratic-affiliated groups compared with about $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Among the nation’s top-grossing firms, the highest shares of contributions to Democratic campaigns were Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton (99.7%), Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson (99.4%), and Mintz, Levin, Cohn, Ferris, Glovsky and Popeo (99.1%); the lowest were Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough (66.4%), Lewis Brisbois Bisgaard & Smith (77.3%), and Ogletree, Deakins, Nash, Smoak & Stewart (81.5%).

The lecture reviews discrete symmetries in quantum mechanics and their quantum-field-theory implementation, focusing on parity (P), time reversal (T), and charge conjugation (C). It explains that continuous symmetries act via unitary operators, while time reversal acts via an anti-unitary operator, requiring anti-linearity so that it sends \(i\) to \(-i\). Using the time-reversal invariance of the Schrödinger equation, the lecture derives why the time-reversal operator must be anti-linear and discusses how adjoints for anti-linear operators must be defined accordingly.  

It then applies these symmetry ideas to quantum fields: for a complex scalar field, P, T, and C can be represented by unitary operators acting on the field and creation/annihilation operators, with phases constrained by consistency conditions like \(P^2\). It extends the parity discussion to the Dirac field, where parity requires a matrix acting on spinor space and leads to constraints on the matrix \(D\) relative to gamma matrices. Similar reasoning is briefly outlined for charge conjugation and time reversal in fermions, with conditions relating matrices to gamma-matrix transposes and signs.  

The lecture concludes by introducing path integrals for fermions. It notes that because fermions involve anti-commutators, the path integral requires replacing the fermionic fields with anti-commuting Grassmann variables. Berezin’s prescription is presented: functions of Grassmann variables are handled using power-series truncation, with special rules for left vs. right derivatives. Integration over Grassmann variables is defined by linearity and the vanishing of total derivatives, which leads to a rule where integrating \(f(\theta)=f_0+f_1\theta\) gives \(f_1\).

U.S. stock index futures rose on Thursday as earnings season began strongly and oil prices rebounded after prior steep losses. Investors remained cautious due to North Korea–U.S. tensions and upcoming French presidential elections, alongside concerns about President Donald Trump’s ability to deliver pro-growth promises. Among 57 S&P 500 companies reporting through Wednesday, 75.4% beat expectations, and overall profits are estimated to have risen 10.8% in the quarter. Visa and Mattel were among companies scheduled to report. Oil prices gained some ground as OPEC-led supply cuts were signaled to likely extend, though inventories weighed on prices. Qualcomm rose after beating analysts’ estimates, while eBay fell after forecasting second-quarter profit below expectations. Futures snapshot at 6:19 a.m. ET showed Dow e-minis up 41 points, S&P 500 e-minis up 6.5 points, and Nasdaq 100 e-minis up 17.5 points.

The passage describes sensor fusion using a rotating LIDAR sensor and one or more cameras, including rolling-shutter operation. It explains how active sensors like LIDAR emit pulses and detect reflections to build distance-based point clouds, while cameras detect external light and produce image pixel rows. Example systems use cameras whose sensing element rows align with the LIDAR axis of rotation, and a controller operates the cameras to obtain a sequence of image pixel rows where each row corresponds to a different exposure time period synchronized with LIDAR scanning. The passage also discusses operating cameras in rolling shutter mode so exposure start times are staggered, selecting the order of captured image pixels based on the order/arrangement of LIDAR light beams, and synchronizing exposure timing using LIDAR pointing direction and overlap between LIDAR and camera fields of view. It further provides examples of device components (controller, actuators, rotating platform, camera ring), camera ring configurations around an axis, and a method for rotating LIDAR, obtaining the image pixel sequence, determining timing configurations, associating LIDAR data with image pixels, and generating a combined representation such as a colored 3D model.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its holdings in Zoe’s Kitchen, Inc. (NYSE: ZOES) by 114.5% in the second quarter, owning 17,056 shares after buying an additional 9,106 shares; it reported ownership of about 0.09% worth $203,000. The passage also notes other investors’ changes in holdings, including American International Group Inc., FMR LLC, Teachers Advisors LLC, California Public Employees Retirement System, and Massachusetts Financial Services Co. MA. It mentions a director, Alexander Taylor II, buying 3,100 shares at an average price of $12.87, and provides analyst ratings and price targets, with a consensus “Hold” rating and target price of $17.55. The passage includes stock performance figures, Zoe’s Kitchen’s recent quarterly results (EPS $0.06; revenue $74.30 million), and a brief company profile describing its fast-casual Mediterranean-inspired restaurant concept.

The defendant appealed convictions and sentences from Queens County Supreme Court: murder in the second degree, criminal possession of a weapon in the second degree, reckless endangerment in the first degree, and endangering the welfare of a child (indictment No. 999/05), and murder in the second degree (indictment No. 1000/05). The appellate court found the claims about the detective’s testimony and the jury consciousness-of-guilt charge unpreserved and, in any event, without merit. It also rejected the claim that the prosecutor changed the prosecution theory during summation and held the principal or accomplice status was not relevant to the liability theory. As the defendant raised no independent claim regarding indictment No. 1000/05, that judgment was affirmed as well. Both judgments were affirmed.

Darren Osborne was sentenced to 43 years in prison at Woolwich Crown Court for driving a van into worshippers outside a mosque in Finsbury Park, north London, killing one person and injuring nine others. He was found guilty of murder and attempted murder, with the judge imposing life imprisonment and a minimum term of 43 years. Reporters described him as emotionless, and he was reported to have shouted “I want to kill all Muslims.” The family of Makram Ali, who was killed, said they were pleased with the verdict and described him as peaceful. Prosecutors said Osborne had been “brainwashed” into Islamophobia after watching a BBC drama, and during trial he claimed he wanted to kill London Mayor Sadiq Khan and Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn. Police released a 15-second clip and CCTV stills showing planning in Wales before the attack. A counterterrorism commander said Osborne failed to create divisions and described community unity.

Several major hedge fund investors reduced holdings in healthcare companies in the second quarter as the healthcare sector led the broad U.S. stock market higher. Jana Partners sold all shares in nine healthcare companies, while Third Point cut stakes in Humana and Baxter. Healthcare stocks in the S&P 500 rose 6.7% in the quarter. The article notes that 13F filings with the SEC are a public way to track such trades but may not reflect current positions because they are released 45 days after quarter end. Overall, hedge funds gained 1% in the second quarter. In energy, Third Point and others sold positions in multiple energy companies, and the sector fell 7% as oil prices dropped.

Facebook is introducing a “Trending News” section in the Facebook app on iOS and Android to help users access current, trending news stories. The stories are aggregated from multiple sources and ranked by how many publications share them. Users can find it under the “Explore” tab, then scroll to “Trending News.” Tapping a story shows headlines from various sources, along with videos, photos, and top Facebook posts; “Trending Topics” in the search feed use a similar format. Facebook announced plans to redesign Trending Topics in May to help users see how publications cover a topic and relevant discussions from friends and public figures.

The passage describes a battery-powered electronic smoking device (electronic cigarette) that vaporizes inhalable liquid using a heater. It outlines conventional device components (housing, atomizer, heating element, control electronics, and optionally an airflow sensor or switch) and engineering challenges for improved atomizers. The invention provides an electronic smoking device including a housing, one or more woven fiber tubes, and a liquid supply. At least one woven fiber tube has an electrically conductive heating section and end sections connected to electrical leads or contacts, with ends in contact with the liquid supply. The woven fiber tubes can transport liquid via capillary action through a hollow interior and/or through porous fiber walls, and can be shaped (e.g., U-, C-, or L-shaped), with varying diameters and configurations for liquid delivery. The passage further describes example e-cigarette structures and operation, including airflow paths, puff detection, activation of a heating element to generate aerosol, LED indication, and options for disposable or rechargeable/refillable designs. It explains coil-less atomizers using woven fiber tubes (e.g., carbon fibers and other listed materials/composites) as a single component replacing conventional heating wire and porous wick, including design options for electrical resistance control, mounting on a board with conductive sections and heating sections, and manufacturing steps involving masking and sputtering/coating to form conductive and heating regions.

The memorandum of decision in In re Access Cardiosystems, Inc. addresses a motion to reconsider liability under Massachusetts securities law and the remaining issue of damages under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2). The court previously found that Randall Fincke made a material false statement in an October 2002 business plan that Access had been advised by patent counsel that its product did not infringe patents known to him, and that Fincke did not actually receive such advice. The court denies Fincke’s motion to reconsider, finding the statement false and material under an objective analysis.

For damages, the court concludes that only Zimmel’s October and November 2002 purchases of Access stock were made “by means of” the misstatement in the business plan. The court finds that the April 2003 transaction and later investments were not made by means of the business plan misstatement, and that no further stock purchases occurred after April 2003. Coleman v. Coleman (1972) addresses whether the first sentence of R.C. 3105.03—requiring at least one year of Ohio residency immediately before filing for divorce (except for alimony alone)—is unconstitutional as a penalty on the right to interstate travel. The court notes that Shapiro v. Thompson and Dunn v. Blumstein apply strict equal protection/“compelling governmental interest” analysis to durational residency requirements affecting fundamental personal rights, including the right to travel. The court concludes that Ohio’s one-year divorce residency requirement does not penalize the constitutional right of freedom to travel, and that the state has a compelling interest in regulating the civil status of marriage and ensuring its laws are not applied to nonresidents. The judgment affirms the constitutionality of the requirement.

The passage describes the Simons Observatory’s use of large numbers of TES detectors for CMB observations and explains how microwave frequency multiplexing readout is affected by diurnal temperature changes. More than 67,000 TES detectors are deployed to four telescopes, and the LAT contains nearly 31,000 detectors. An improved multiplexing scheme using SMuRF electronics can introduce systematic phase drift because room-temperature transmission lines connected to the cryostat experience ambient temperature swings; if not mitigated, this could contaminate TES signals. The paper measures these drifts using non-tone-tracked off-resonance “pilot” tones and a thermometer in the receiver cabin, finding correlated phase drift with ambient temperature at the picosecond level over one diurnal swing. Using this measured drift, the authors convert it into an inferred TES noise-equivalent current and compare its amplitude spectral density with on-sky detector noise and an open SQUID channel, concluding the phase drift contribution is within the readout noise budget and should not affect mapping speed.

The passage discusses how electron–photon interactions in optical cavities are commonly described by the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, which modifies molecular electronic structure and leads to phenomena such as polaritonic states and altered chemical reactivity. It notes that standard quantum chemistry methods for isolated molecules are not directly applicable and that dedicated computational tools are limited. A key challenge is the non-local electron–photon coupling term, whose long-range character requires a basis set that can represent both smooth and rapidly varying wavefunction features with high numerical precision. The sinc basis set is presented as a promising option because it is orthonormal, systematically improvable, and converges to the complete basis set limit with refined grid spacing. Molecular orbitals can be written as linear combinations of sinc functions on a uniform real-space grid. While a direct sinc implementation has O(N^4) cost for two-electron integrals, rapid decay of off-diagonal tensor elements with decreasing grid spacing enables sparse or low-rank approximations to reduce scaling. The passage also states that sinc functions arise naturally from the Fourier transform of momentum-space eigenfunctions for a particle in a finite box and represent band-limited functions in coordinate space.

VentureWire’s Tuesday, September 26, 2000 issue reports private company business news, including top stories on Chiaro Networks receiving $100 million in third-round funding, Bertelsmann and iSyndicate forming a joint European venture, Novalux raising $109 million in third-round financing, Miadora shutting down, Sun Microsystems launching a $50 million Asia investment program, and Mayfield Fund naming a marketing partner. The passage describes the ethical conduct and consent procedures for the DAWN-plasma randomized, open-label phase 2 trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Independent ethics committees reviewed and approved protocol amendments and informed consent documentation before study initiation, and investigators were required to report serious and/or unexpected adverse events to their committees. The primary objective was to assess clinical efficacy and safety, with the primary endpoint defined as the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Inclusion criteria included adults (≥18 years) who provided informed consent and had confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection with evidence of illness, while key exclusions included receiving mechanical ventilation before or at randomization and certain prior treatments or conditions. Convalescent plasma was administered as 800–1000 mL in 4 doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization, and only plasma with neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/160 was allowed. Randomization was 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone. The study assessed safety using treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment-related adverse events and SAEs, with similar numbers of adverse events and serious adverse events reported between groups. Between 2 May 2020 and 26 January 2021, 320 patients were randomized to convalescent plasma and 163 to control, and the intervention showed no impact on the primary endpoint or on mortality and other secondary endpoints. Treatment-related adverse events and treatment-related serious adverse events were also reported in both groups without observed differences.

Poor diet contributes to premature death and morbidity in the US, especially from cardiovascular disease (CVD), and nutrition disparities related to socioeconomic vulnerability have not improved over time. The passage describes a study using pooled 2009–2020 NHANES data (adults >20 years; n=32,498) to characterize empirically derived dietary patterns using principal components analysis, identifying four patterns: “American,” “Prudent,” “Legume,” and “Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy.” Dietary patterns were compared by prevalent CVD status, a social determinants of health (SDOH) score, and SNAP participation. In fully adjusted analyses, adults with CVD were more likely to align with the American pattern, while SDOH score and SNAP participation were associated with differences across all four patterns, including lower alignment with healthier patterns (Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy) among those with higher vulnerability or SNAP participation. Associations between SDOH and diet differed by race and ethnicity, and SNAP-related associations also varied by race and ethnicity. Sensitivity analyses showed generally similar results. The study concludes that empirically observed dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and especially socioeconomic vulnerability, and that interventions should consider these patterns to improve nutrition quality and health equity among people at risk for CVD.

The passage describes a study on hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission in Rwanda, focusing on household members living with HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye district. Results showed an HCV prevalence of 10.8% among participants (16 reactive on rapid test confirmed by ELISA; 132 non-reactive). Significant associations were reported between HCV positivity and factors including unprotected sex, HBV history, and HIV history, while blood transfusion was not significant. The authors conclude that unprotected sex was the most common risk factor for transmission and recommend early screening and follow-up for household members, improved patient follow-up and monitoring by the Ministry of Health, and further research to better determine the origin of infections.

Santa Barbara County sheriff’s detectives are investigating a Tuesday morning robbery at the Summerland Antique Collective on the 2100 block of Ortega Hill Road. The passage introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework to analyze computational problems by separating internal construction (intensional) from observable behavior (extensional). CDF uses three connected spaces—syntactic (Ssyn(f)), semantic (Ssem(f)), and logical (Slog(f))—linked by mappings αf, βf, and γf, and classifies problems based on whether these mappings support stable compositional reasoning (ComCDF) or lead to recursive, explosive entanglement (ExpCDF). It distinguishes syntactic reasoning from semantic reasoning and describes semantic “explosion” as arising from how syntax maps into propositional semantic configurations. The framework is applied to compare 2SAT and 3SAT: 2SAT clauses can be converted into binary implications, leading to stable, polynomial-time solvable behavior, while 3SAT clauses cannot be converted similarly, producing non-local dependencies and exponential growth in semantic space, reflected as unstable and computationally intractable γf behavior.

Patents grant inventors a monopoly until expiration, after which the invention can be used for new products without limitation. The passage concludes that industrial knowledge often becomes public when patents expire and recommends the Wohlers Report as a comprehensive annual resource.

European shares rose on Wednesday after Britain’s formal announcement of its intention to leave the European Union and begin a two-year negotiation process. At the UN Climate Summit in New York, President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China’s green commitment and said the international community should maintain “unwavering” confidence, action, and efforts. He stated China aims to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 7% to 10% by 2035, including an agreement to reduce emissions rather than only slow them down, and noted this marks a shift from a developing-country approach. Xi also committed to 3,600 gigawatts of installed wind and solar capacity by 2035, and to an energy mix with more than 30% renewables, while planning to expand China’s national carbon emissions trading to more emission-intensive sectors. The speech included commitments related to electric mobility, access to rare earth minerals for batteries, increased EV mainstreaming, and forest extent reaching 34 billion cubic meters. China is described as having become a global leader in the clean energy transition by investing $625 billion last year (nearly a third of the global total), reshaping green technology markets, and driving renewable adoption as prices fell and renewables replaced coal domestically.

Paulo Dybala said he has been training with Juventus and expects to play 100% against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-final return leg. WHO guidelines recommend a total primaquine dose of 3.5–7.0 mg/kg over 14 days to eliminate Plasmodium vivax hypnozoites and prevent relapses, but evidence suggests that tropical P. vivax isolates from Southeast Asia may require the higher end. An open-label randomized controlled trial in Kampong Speu province, Western Cambodia, evaluated blood schizonticidal artesunate followed by primaquine in G6PD normal patients assigned to either 3.5 mg/kg or 7.0 mg/kg over 14 days, with a no-primaquine comparator; G6PD deficient patients were assigned to no primaquine. Patients were relocated to a malaria transmission-free town for 90 days, monitored through day 180, and the primary outcome was at least one P. vivax recurrence within 90 days. Among 156 allocated patients (37 G6PD deficient in no-primaquine; 119 G6PD normal split between 3.5 mg/kg, 7.0 mg/kg, and no-primaquine), recurrence within 90 days was 81.4% in the no-primaquine arm, 24.4% with 3.5 mg/kg, and 4.7% with 7.0 mg/kg (p=0.0141). Primaquine regimens were reported as well tolerated in G6PD normal individuals, with comparable safety and tolerability. The study concludes that 7.0 mg/kg primaquine over 14 days should be recommended to reduce P. vivax relapses in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries.

Sebi allowed debt issuers to request reviews of credit ratings through CRA rating committees with a majority of independent members. The change is intended to curb “rating shopping” and “pick-and-choose” practices and improve CRA governance and accountability. Sebi defined independent members as having no pecuniary relationship with the CRA or its employees, and required CRAs to disclose non-accepted ratings for 12 months on their websites in a specified format. CRAs must also upload half-yearly rating summary sheets within 15 days of each half-year end, with disclosures prepared separately for securities ratings and other financial instruments. The decision follows stakeholder suggestions from a prior consultation paper on CRA rating processes and disclosure proposals.

A Mississippi woman, Melinda Rosetti-Spence, was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from the Pink Hearts Fund cancer charity. Harrison County Circuit Judge Lisa Dodson ordered her to repay about $181,000, with Rosetti-Spence’s family paying the balance. Rosetti-Spence, who volunteered as treasurer, pleaded guilty after prosecutors said she wrote 132 checks to herself between March and July 2016. She told the court she had a gambling problem and spent the stolen money on bills, did not make repayments since her arrest, and attended rehab but not a gambling-addicts program. Pink Hearts Fund founder JoAn Niceley said Rosetti-Spence betrayed her and tried to discredit her.

The U.S. government has frozen about $18 billion in federal funding for New York City projects, citing concerns that contract awards may have relied on unconstitutional DEI criteria. After a Department of Transportation interim rule limited race- or gender-based preferences, the DOT suspended a $300 million payment pending review, with audits determining whether grant agreements violated federal anti-discrimination rules. City officials criticized the move, saying it will delay jobs and construction and increase costs, while the federal shutdown has already complicated contract management. The effects depend on the outcome of the federal review and could prompt renegotiation or loss of funding if violations are found.

LG plans to release webOS-powered TVs later this month. English local authorities are expected to receive refunds totalling millions of pounds after being overcharged for legal action to recover unpaid council tax. Councils issue millions of summons annually, and the number has increased in recent years. The Ministry of Justice said it found it had “inadvertently” over-charged £2.50 per application and would outline details of a refund scheme soon; it would also cost HM Courts and Tribunal Service £9m in revenue this year. The passage also notes rising council tax arrears administration costs and reported figures on people taken to court, threatened with prison, and imprisoned for council tax offences.

A group of college accreditors represented by CRAC backed using artificial intelligence to reduce credit loss during student transfer, which the passage describes as inconsistent, time-consuming, decentralized, and often tied to delays and negative consequences. The passage describes a cryotherapy wellness trend in which people enter a chamber that can reach 180 degrees below zero. Supporters claim it helps speed muscle recovery, reduce inflammation, relieve joint pain, improve circulation, relieve anxiety and depression, elevate mood, boost the immune system, and burn 500 to 800 calories per session. Cryotherapy was invented in the 1970s by Japanese doctor Toshima Yamauchi for arthritis, later gaining popularity in Europe and then the United States; a facility called Polar Brrr Cryo opened in West Michigan. The FDA has not approved cryotherapy, and warnings include frostbite, burns, and eye injuries. The passage says Polar Brrr is the only facility of its kind in Southwest Michigan, with the next closest options in Detroit and Chicago, and mentions clients ranging from athletes to people with sleep disorders.
