People with heart problems or hypertension are told to consult a doctor, and introductory rates are listed ($25 for the first class, $90 for the first three, otherwise $55 per session).

A 2,100-year-old chalk stone bowl fragment unearthed in Jerusalem contains the Hebrew engraving “Hyrcanus,” a name associated with two Hasmonean kings but also commonly used at the time, according to the Israel Antiquities Authority. The fragment was found under the Givati parking lot in the City of David, beneath the ancient foundations of a mikvah complex. Researchers say the fragment’s context sheds little light on whether its owner was royalty or a commoner, noting few engraved vessels from the period make it hard to determine whether it was routine or special. The fragment was discovered in 2015, and its announcement was delayed for study; it was found near the remains of the fortress Akra, later conquered by the Hasmoneans.

The passage explains Bollinger Bands as a volatility indicator that consists of a middle moving average (typically a 20-day SMA) and upper/lower bands set at standard deviations from the middle. It describes how band widening and contraction relate to volatility changes, including “squeeze” periods that can precede breakouts. It outlines multiple Bollinger Band-based strategies (e.g., Squeeze, Breakouts, Walks, Bounce, %B, and reversals), including typical signals such as price breaking above the upper band or below the lower band, and emphasizes using additional indicators and risk management rather than relying on Bollinger Bands alone. The passage also states that Bollinger Bands were created by John Bollinger in the 1980s, that indicator settings and timeframes may need adjustment for different markets, and that Bollinger Bands may or may not work depending on the asset and strategy, with some tests showing promise in gold but not in stock indices.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 1, 2019. The report states that Apple’s Annual Meeting of Shareholders was held on March 1, 2019, where shareholders voted on five proposals: (1) elected eight directors (James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner); (2) approved the ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for 2019; (3) approved an advisory resolution to approve executive compensation; (4) did not approve a shareholder proposal titled “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments”; and (5) did not approve a shareholder proposal titled “True Diversity Board Policy.” The signature section shows the report signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on March 4, 2019.

The passage discusses the “holiday effect” in stock markets, described as increased returns around certain holidays and treated as a calendar/seasonal trading pattern. It defines a holiday as a non-trading day (not a Saturday or Sunday) and examines periods around several US holidays using S&P 500 data (via SPY and also ^gspc for earlier data) with backtests comparing performance before and around holidays. The text notes that the holiday effect is small and not a get-rich-quick scheme, though it is described as abnormal in some cases and documented in multiple countries. It provides backtest findings for several holidays: Martin Luther King Day and President’s Day are reported as having little or no support in trading results; Memorial Day is described as small or non-existent; Independence Day (4th of July), Thanksgiving (including comparisons with a retail sector fund), and Easter/Christmas-related timing are described as among the better or tradeable ones. The passage also reports a “post-holiday seasonal effect” backtesting approach in which trades are entered around holidays and held for 1–5 days after, including an “overnight” variant; it states that holding over the holiday showed no gains in the first test, while the second day after showed comparatively good returns, and that only some holiday anomalies/seasonalities are suggested as tradeable (Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas).

Scottish local authorities are setting next year’s budgets and deciding whether to raise council tax. Councils can increase the basic rate by up to 3%, ending the government’s council tax freeze, though some may continue it voluntarily. Separately, MSPs voted to raise the multiplier for the top four council tax bands from April, meaning bills for higher-band properties (E to H) will rise regardless of local council decisions; the passage estimates average Band E households will pay about £2 more per week and average Band H households about £10 more per week, on top of any Band D changes set by councils. In total, about 26% of households (around 700,000 of Scotland’s 2.6m homes) are expected to see increases due to the multiplier change, with variation across areas such as East Renfrewshire, Edinburgh, Dundee, Glasgow, and Aberdeen. The passage also notes that council tax bands are based on property values from 1 April 1991, which could leave some properties in bands that may not match current value; one analysis suggested 57% of properties would have changed bands after a 2014 revaluation. Finally, it discusses how councils rely mainly on government grants, and the political disagreement over planned changes to core grants and additional direct funding under the Scottish government’s budget, including assumptions about how much additional council tax might be raised.

The passage reports multiple technology updates involving Amazon’s Alexa and related devices: Amazon is working on an AI chip to make Alexa brighter and faster; an Alexa-themed Super Bowl ad (“Alexa Loses Her Voice”) performed strongly on YouTube; Sony introduced a more sophisticated Aibo robot dog at CES; Jeff Bezos had a win for Alexa ahead of CES; Amazon and Google discounted home speakers during the holidays, likely losing money per unit; Amazon said Echo Dot sales were boosted by Prime members; Apple’s new home speaker is delayed beyond Christmas; a German man was fined after an Alexa device played loud music at 2 a.m. while he was away; and Amazon plans to have Alexa power “Big Mouth Billy Bass.”

The passage contains AMD’s specification agreement governing use, review, and feedback of a “SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block” specification. It states AMD retains rights to the specification, disclaims all warranties, provides limited use permissions, and limits liability. It also describes SEV-ES/SEV-SNP concepts where encrypted guest register state is protected from hypervisor access, and introduces Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) where the guest selects which register state to expose via the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB).

It outlines the document’s purpose (standardizing GHCB memory area and required NAE events/state), GHCB requirements (size, mapping, and protocol/versioning), and how the GHCB/VMGEXIT flow works for guest-hypervisor communication. The passage further discusses version 2 and revisions, including hypervisor feature advertisement, GHCB MSR protocols, CPUID/encryption-bit negotiation, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, and examples of GHCB negotiation and VMGEXIT handling. It also covers supporting mechanisms such as GHCB VALID_BITMAP handling, various NAE event requirements, and additional SEV-SNP/SEV extensions (e.g., secrets page, confidential computing blob EFI protocol, page state change, SNP guest requests/extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell, #HV timer, APIC ID list, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC, termination requests, and notes that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported).

The passage summarizes multiple news items from late October 2001 about worsening corporate credit conditions and Enron in particular. Reuters, Bloomberg, Associated Press, and other outlets report that credit rating agencies, especially Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s, downgraded or placed Enron ratings under review, citing reduced financial flexibility, asset write-downs and charges, and investor reaction. Enron is described as negotiating with banks for new or additional credit lines after drawing down about $3 billion in credit to increase liquidity and repay commercial paper. Some market participants continue trading with Enron but watch its credit status closely; others in Europe reportedly froze or reduced dealings due to credit concerns. Enron’s stock fell to near seven-year lows amid uncertainty about its financial disclosures, and bond prices and yields were reported to have deteriorated after the rating actions.

The passage says India’s income inequality rose rapidly beginning in the 1980s, with the top 1% capturing up to 22% of national income. It states this level is the highest since India’s Income Tax was created in 1922, noting the top 1% captured under 21% in the late 1930s, fell to 6% in the early 1980s, and rose to 22% today. The paper attributes the change around 1983–84 to new economic policies that disengaged the public sector and encouraged entrepreneurship and foreign investments, and links the start to Rajiv Gandhi’s prime minister nomination in 1984. It also reports that inequality increased more sharply than survey-based statistics typically used in public debates, and describes that income shares were reduced in the 1950s–1970s under strong market regulations and high fiscal progressivity. It characterizes “Shining India” as benefiting the top 10% rather than the middle 40%, and says growth since the early 1980s has been uneven within the top 10%, indicating unequal liberalisation and deregulation.

Ukrainian drone pilots have become top targets for Russia, which has increased attacks on suspected operator positions using missiles, bombs, and other weapons. Ukrainian soldiers and drone operators told Business Insider that pilots hinder missions and play a valuable role in combat, and that eliminating them is aimed at disrupting drones’ battlefield influence. An officer in Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps said the death toll for drone pilots has risen in recent years, and that drones—especially those with small explosive payloads—are responsible for around 70% of casualties on both sides, according to recent assessments. The passage also says Russia locates pilots and strikes them, sometimes extensively over areas even if few pilots are present, while Ukrainian forces attempt protective measures such as deeper underground operations and frequent rotation. The passage adds that Ukraine also tries to target Russian drone counterparts and that drone tactics are fast-changing.

The passage discusses daily water intake and related health effects. It notes the NHS recommends about two liters of water per day and suggests this is roughly 6–8 glasses (1.2 liters), with some water also coming from food. It warns against drinking too much, describing water intoxication as rare but potentially causing lethargy and light-headedness and, in extreme cases, fatal outcomes, especially when people rapidly drink 2–3 liters after exercise-related dehydration. It cites a study suggesting people should drink according to thirst, noting swallowing reflex inhibition after sufficient water intake. It also reports that a 2010 12-week study found participants who drank two cups of water before meals lost more weight than those who did not.

The Chamber of Mines of Namibia announced that the Mining Expo & Conference will be held on April 25 and 26 at the Windhoek Show Grounds under the theme “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector.” Nedbank Namibia Corporate and Investment Banking’s Mining and Resources Finance team will participate by sharing insights on how the Namibian mining sector can position itself globally for direct foreign investments and how Nedbank CIB can help achieve this. The team will highlight its role in providing equity and debt capital for mining development and in supporting mining houses’ long-term sustainability, and it will offer complete funding solutions covering sourcing, designing, structuring, and negotiating transactions, along with a networking lounge. Team head Dominic Shikola said Nedbank aims to be a leader in maximising the sector’s multiplier effect, noting mining’s contribution to GDP and other economic benefits, and stated that Nedbank CIB will continue to support entities in the sector.

The passage introduces the problem that, unlike genetics in GWAS, non-genetic “risk factors” in biobank-scale data have not been systematically identified using effects that account for mediation, confounding, and biases such as reverse causation and collider bias. It explains that controlling for mediators shifts attention from total to direct effects and can introduce bias (the “Table 2 fallacy”). It then describes Doublethink, a Bayesian model-averaging method applied to identify direct risk factors for COVID-19 hospitalization in UK Biobank while simultaneously controlling Bayesian FDR and frequentist FWER. Doublethink tests individual variables and groups of correlated variables using a regression framework, MCMC implementation, and adjusted p-values derived from posterior odds. The study analyzes 1,912 variables from UK Biobank for 1,917 COVID-19 hospitalization cases and reports that at specified thresholds nine individual variables and nine pre-defined groups show significant evidence of direct effects, with additional signals revealed through post-hoc grouping. The results are compared with 127 published UK Biobank COVID-19 studies, finding broad support for categories such as age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic status, and smoking, while some commonly studied categories (e.g., diabetes, cardiovascular disease, hypertension) did not show significant direct effects in this analysis. The discussion emphasizes limitations including that only direct effects are assessed, not total effects, and that no evidence of direct effect does not imply no effect overall.

The passage outlines how teams should prepare for three jump ball situations: defensive (opponent advantage, control doubtful), even (equal chance), and offensive (own team advantage, control likely). It emphasizes defensive caution, early rotation, and gaining an edge by watching the jumper’s eyes and hand, since right-handed jumpers typically tip forward to the left and left-handed jumpers to the right. It then describes box, diamond, and “Y” defensive alignments, including specific rotations and responsibilities for defenders and box-out behavior. For even jump balls, it stresses boxing out, coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotation on a predetermined signal, anticipation, and aggressiveness. Finally, it lists proven offensive jump ball plays to the left or right, including ball possession (tipping back), double tap, post split (diamond and box alignments), jumper fly, forward fly, spread, tandem, and loop, with brief role descriptions for players and ball movement after possession.

The passage describes a friendly conversation in which the speaker showed Mr. Toivola an alleged Tokyo radio broadcast intercept quoting a Finnish Legation statement dismissing Soviet-Finnish peace rumors as Anglo-American “machinations,” and the speaker noted he was not convinced the Legation made such a statement. It then includes a January 20, 1942 Finnish Minister’s letter to the U.S. Secretary of State about restrictions on travel for Finnish Legation and consular staff and honorary consuls, stating pending reply the Legation had not informed certain American citizens about the matter. Another section summarizes a British Embassy aide-mémoire stating a Soviet colleague reported via unofficial Swedish channels that she would contact the Finnish Government secretly and hinted Finland might expect more favorable terms. The passage also contains a U.S. memorandum discussing British and American views aimed at making it easier for Finland to make peace with the Soviet Union by signaling non-leniency toward continuation of Finnish policy, and ends with a draft telegram to convey these views to Witting.

The passage discusses how programming patterns and practices have evolved, starting with reusable, architecture-independent algorithms in Donald Knuth’s 1962 work, and later shifting toward object-oriented programming and interface-based reusable libraries such as “Design Patterns” by Gamma et al. It then describes the rise of open source and explains what patterns for distributed systems are—general blueprints that provide advice without prescribing specific technologies. The text argues that patterns improve development by enabling learning from others’ mistakes, providing shared vocabulary, and supporting reusable components. It focuses on single-node container patterns, especially the sidecar pattern, which runs an auxiliary container alongside an application container to add functionality such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, and operational tooling. It continues through other single-node patterns including the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions (e.g., integrating sharded services, service discovery, and request splitting) and the adapter pattern for normalizing heterogeneous monitoring and logging interfaces into consistent ones. Finally, it introduces multi-node distributed patterns for stateless replicated load-balanced services, covering readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination, and contrasts replicated services with sharded services, emphasizing sharded cache design, its performance implications (hit rate, latency, and reliability), and the option of replicated, sharded caches to improve shard resilience.

The passage describes the Wham play in football as a Trap concept where a tight end or fullback pulls and kicks out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. Its main strength is creating favorable, often unexpected running angles quickly, especially since defensive line coaches practice taking Trap blocks. As a complementary play, Wham can serve as a change-up when it is not frequently shown. Its weaknesses are that it is complicated and time-consuming to teach and install, requiring the offense to identify the front and specific assignments, and it depends on having the right kind of player for blocking; teams may use specific formations to produce a predictable front. The passage then outlines Wham play blocking assignments for 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, and provides two variations: a Gun H-Back Wham RPO where the fullback kicks out the nose tackle and the QB can throw slant or bubble, and a Shotgun Influence Wham example where the fullback traps a 3-tech defender after it widens due to a pull.

The speaker describes being excited during a game after the team scored, including going to Fleury to ensure he made saves. They say the team stayed with a desperate, strong opponent and won, with Fleury making great saves and key sacrifices from players like Geno and Miroslav blocking shots. The speaker praises Fleury as a leader, notes he was injured but the team aimed to win for him, and says they plan to follow leaders’ playoff performance. They also discuss team messages before games about being proud and fortunate to play, personal memories of Sidney Crosby, and credit for Mario keeping the Penguins in Pittsburgh before the recent Stanley Cup win.

Survivors and relatives of the 72 victims of the Grenfell Tower inferno gave tributes during the first phase of a public inquiry chaired by retired judge Martin Moore-Bick. Ahmed Elgwahry described calling his sister Mariem and mother Eslah during the fire and hearing their final words. Speakers said the inquiry should focus on the victims’ human voices and faces, while also addressing criticism about fire safety failures by local government, the building manager, government officials, and fire authorities who told people to stay in apartments even as escape became impossible. Other tributes included accounts from Paulos Tekle, whose family was told to remain inside before leaving at 2:15 a.m., and Marcio Gomes, who said his son Logan died shortly after birth. Elgwahry also described the coroner recovering only fragments of his mother and sister.

The passage says Donald Trump initially responded to the Charlottesville, Virginia white supremacist rally with a vague tweet condemning “hate,” which led to backlash. It claims the president stayed silent until Ken Frazier, a Merck CEO and Big Pharma mogul, resigned from the American Manufacturing Council, issuing a statement about taking a stand against intolerance and extremism. Before denouncing the rally, the passage says Trump used Frazier’s resignation to criticize him, posting that it would give Frazier more time to lower “ripoff drug prices.” It also states that Frazier is among executives stepping down from Trump advisory councils, noting Elon Musk and Disney’s Robert Igor resigned from another forum after Trump pulled out of the Paris Climate Accord.

ResearchAndMarkets.com added the “Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018-2022” report, stating the market will generate revenue of more than $1,000 million by 2022. The report includes market landscape and growth prospects, key vendor discussions, and examines drivers such as demand for automated equipment and automated material handling, along with a challenge of stiff competition from servo and conventional stepper motors. It notes trends including increasing focus on miniaturized stepper motors, advances in stepper motor design for robotics, and emergence of IoT-enabled stepper motors. Key vendors listed are AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons, Nidec, and Schneider Electric. The report covers topics including market sizing, five forces analysis, segmentation by application (industrial machinery and robotics), regional analysis (APAC, EMEA, Americas), and a decision framework.

The passage argues that dividend yields above 6% can indicate increased risk of a dividend cut, though this is not always true. It examines two stocks with a forecast yield of 7.1%. For FTSE 100 housebuilder Taylor Wimpey, a May 2016 dividend policy targets £1.3bn of total shareholder return from 2016 to 2018, with expectations to generate surplus cash and a planned total dividend of £450m for 2017, equating to about 13.9p per share (forecast yield 7.1%). The passage states that 2016 free cash flow (£511.6m) suggests the payout is affordable, though it notes the housing market’s cyclicality could eventually affect special dividends. For logistics firm Connect Group, the passage says dividends are supported by strong cash generation, with last year’s 9.5p dividend (trailing yield 6.9%) covered by free cash flow (£49.6m), and an expected increase to 9.8p (forecast yield 7.1%) based on a low forecast P/E (7.6). It also highlights concerns about Connect’s net debt (£141.7m) and negative net tangible asset value (-£151.8m, excluding intangible assets), concluding that risks outweigh potential rewards.

A survey by the Regina Police Service found the public is relatively satisfied with police performance. Conducted between September and October 2017 with 462 participants, it examined perceptions of police visibility, responsiveness, and public information and social media. Key findings included 79% rating overall service quality as very good to excellent and over 80% agreeing the RPS has integrity and honesty. Nearly 25% felt the RPS wasn’t sensitive to their ethnic group, specifically Indigenous people, and Chief Evan Bray said the service plans more reconciliation training from January to May.

The passage explains that baseline out of bounds plays are unique because the defense has a numerical advantage, making successful inbounding difficult and leading teams to lose games. It stresses that defending from out of bounds behind the defense is different from defending out front, and that shooters typically go directly to the basket with limited margin for error. It then presents four effective defensive approaches: (1) Disrupt or “Jam” (sag off and protect the middle, then jam/smother and deny screens without switching), (2) Jump Switch (aggressively switch to deny passing lanes and possibly create turnovers), (3) Trap (smother the inbounder and trap the receiver, then rotate into coverage), and (4) Combination defenses (e.g., box & one, diamond & one, triangle & two) that can force timeouts or steals. Each approach includes phased instructions for defender positioning and actions around the inbound pass.

The passage describes a study of neuropathic pain using Morton’s neuroma as a model of peripheral entrapment neuropathy. It reports that neuropathic pain is associated with higher pain severity, lower quality of life, and higher health care costs, and notes limited access to human peripheral nerve tissue as a challenge. The study recruited 22 adults with Morton’s neuroma undergoing neuroma excision surgery and 11 control participants undergoing surgeries allowing sampling of unaffected neural tissue. Proximal plantar digital nerve samples were used for analyses. Clinical pain phenotyping included NPSI and VAS measures. RNA sequencing and transcriptomic analyses were performed to compare Morton’s neuroma and control nerves, and immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence was used to validate findings. Results reported a large number of differentially expressed genes, with immune and inflammatory responses and nervous system development pathways overrepresented. Deconvolution and immunofluorescence indicated increased immune cell populations in Morton’s neuroma, including macrophage populations associated with paroxysmal pain severity. A gene signature for a specific M(GC) macrophage subset (MARCO, CD163, STAB1; with MARCO correlating with paroxysmal pain) was highlighted. Histological validation reported demyelination, increased intraneural T-cells, and increased densities of CD163+ macrophage subsets in chronic Morton’s neuroma. The authors conclude that intraneural neuroinflammation and associated immune pathways are linked to chronic peripheral neuropathic pain in humans and that the M(GC) MARCO+ macrophage subset may be relevant.

The passage introduces diffusion models and flow matching as scalable generative approaches for images, videos, audio, and text, and frames them within learning stochastic dynamics between two distributions. It then discusses the Schrödinger bridge (SB) problem—inferring an optimal stochastic bridge between two distributions—and describes iterative proportional fitting (IPF) as a computational approach that maintains forward and reverse processes and converges to time reversals that solve the SB problem. The authors note that standard diffusion model training is a degenerate IPF case, but existing IPF variants require samples from both marginals and cannot handle unnormalised densities without samples. They propose extending IPF to “data-to-energy” and “energy-to-energy” settings where one or both marginals are given by unnormalised densities, and claim their algorithm is the first general method for inferring such SBs. They report three contributions: learning low transport cost stochastic bridges between synthetic datasets and densities (matching data-to-data IPF with oracle samples), improving existing data-to-data IPF by learning diffusion coefficients as well as drift, and applying the method to scalable data-free image-to-image translation in latent spaces. The text then begins Section 2 on data-to-data SB background, formulating the SB problem as a KL-minimisation problem subject to marginal constraints and relating it to dynamic optimal transport and entropy-regularised optimal transport, and introduces IPF recursion starting from the reference process.

The passage is an email compiling news items dated May 26–27, 2001, centered on California’s energy crisis and related energy regulation and disputes involving Enron, including Kenneth Lay’s proposal for deregulation and meetings with prominent Californians. It also includes coverage of Enron’s power and gas projects and legal and contractual disputes in India (Dabhol Power and Maharashtra State Electricity Board), Saudi Arabia’s planned gas project deal structure and partner expectations, and reporting on U.S. Senate actions and confirmations affecting the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).

The passage consists of hockey-related remarks about penalties, chances, and game performance, emphasizing a “one goal hockey game” and the importance of capitalizing on opportunities. It discusses winning “two in a row,” relying on team speed, and moving players to match lines when some did not meet the needed standard. It also includes comments about previous series outcomes (Vancouver, San Jose, Detroit), confidence in continuing play, and mentions organizational and coaching relationships between teams. Additional points cover preparation during draft-related periods, a player’s impact and outside criticism, issues with players getting back to the bench in time for periods, refocusing between periods, and collective bargaining system constraints.

The passage explains overnight trading as buying at the market close and selling at the next day’s open or close, typically holding for about 24 hours (or longer over weekends). It discusses the “overnight edge” attributed mainly to the close-to-next-open period and compares exiting on the open, noting the average gain from open to close has been zero over the last 30 years, while emphasizing the existence of infrequent excessive returns under certain conditions. It presents examples of short-term strategies and effects used over 24-hour holds, including Turnaround Tuesday, holiday and end-of-month effects, weekday effects, mean reversion, and options expiration-week effects, along with an example mix of mean reversion, breakout, and gaps. It describes portfolio construction as combining multiple uncorrelated strategies, using different asset classes, varying time frames, managing overlaps, and avoiding drawdowns to support compounding, stating that it’s better to have many sub-optimal strategies than a few “perfect” ones. The passage also addresses realism of backtests, mentions low leverage and full equity invested in examples, and notes the main practical drawback is the need to buy and sell at the close, preferably via automated execution.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch its unmanned Dragon cargo spacecraft to the International Space Station at 12:31 pm ET from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The first stage will return to Earth to land upright and be recovered and refurbished. The mission will be the last time NASA sends a brand new Dragon cargo craft to the ISS, with future missions using only flight-proven hardware. The NASA contract was extended from 12 to 20 resupply flights, and this mission will deliver about 6,400 pounds of supplies, including scientific hardware for experiments and research, as well as ice cream for the astronauts.

The passage discusses teamwork and depth, highlighting players such as Rob, Ray Bourque, John Klemm, Greg de Vries, Skoula, and others. It emphasizes respecting opponents’ strengths, maintaining good positioning and containment instead of risky battles, and learning and adapting roles defensively. It also notes that making it to the finals depends on factors like injuries, emotions, confidence, and getting everything in order, while describing the experience as pressured, special, and motivating for the team and fans, with a focus on starting fresh and playing simply.

The passage explains that soccer “small sided games” (SSGs) involve two teams with fewer than 11 players per team on a smaller field, and can be used in both practice and competition. It states that the main objective is to give individuals more ball touches due to the reduced number of players, and notes that practice SSGs are used to address specific tactical aspects across all youth levels through higher levels. Practice games commonly range from 3v3 to 9v9, are fast-paced in restricted areas to improve ball skills, and typically follow age progressions (U6, U8, U10, U12, U14, U16) with smaller spaces and fewer players at younger ages. It also summarizes that U.S. Soccer issued Player Development Initiatives (PDIs) in August 2017 for small-sided competitive youth games from U6/U12, including rules such as fewer players, smaller fields/goals/balls, shorter times, no offside before U-9, build-out lines starting at U-9, and bans on headers plus goalkeeper punts and drop kicks. The passage further notes additional standards provided for field markings, substitutions, footwear, officials, kickoffs, free kicks, and restart rules for U6 through U12.

Dr. Pasvolsky said the term “peace-loving states” in Chapter III was chosen to emphasize the organization’s “peace” purpose and that membership criteria would determine the initial members. He noted the Dumbarton Oaks proposal that the Assembly admit new states on Security Council recommendation, with joint responsibility to decide admission based on whether a state is peace-loving, and that further discussion would be required. The Ambassador of Mexico said permanent peace should guide the chapter and that admission questions were complicated. Chapter IV was then discussed: it was meant to indicate principal organs, with subsidiary groups provided as needed; the Economic and Social Council and Military Staff Committee were omitted to focus on the Security Council’s peace and security functions, the General Assembly’s role in creating conditions for peace, and the International Court of Justice’s legal responsibilities, though the Economic and Social Council’s authority could change. Chapter V on the General Assembly was discussed, including comments on limiting delegates to three per country versus not limiting numbers. Dr. Pasvolsky addressed criticisms of limited Assembly powers, explaining that functions would not be assigned to two bodies simultaneously and that “primary” regarding the Security Council meant some peace and security functions would rest with the Assembly, while also describing divided responsibility and the need for continuous Security Council responsibility. He concluded that peace and security depend on nations maintaining relations requiring minimal adjustment and willingness to support the world organization’s principles, warning that the Assembly’s failure would leave the Security Council powerless.

The Syrian opposition, represented by Salim al-Muslit of the High Negotiations Committee, wants face-to-face negotiations with the government on a political transition at peace talks in Geneva next week. He said President Bashar al-Assad cannot play a role in the transition and that discussions should begin with the transition and the Geneva 2012 communique’s call for a transitional governing body with full executive powers formed by mutual consent. Muslit said the HNC had not yet received a negotiation agenda, and that consultations would begin Feb 20 and talks would start Feb 23. The HNC has named a 22-member delegation. The passage also notes that diplomacy has repeatedly failed to end the war, including a recent effort supported by Russia and Turkey after rebels were defeated in eastern Aleppo in December.

A Northern California jury convicted 20-year-old Gonzalo Curiel of torturing, starving and beating two children whose bodies were found in a storage unit, and of torturing their older sister in a Salinas apartment. The convictions relate to the 2015 killings of a 7-year-old boy and his 3-year-old sister. Curiel’s former girlfriend and relative, Tami Huntsman, pleaded guilty in February to two counts of murder. Prosecutors said the children were killed on Thanksgiving after the 12-year-old primary witness was caught stealing a bagel, and the girl testified that she and her siblings were stripped, sprayed with cold water, beaten with a shower head, and locked in a tiny bathroom for punishment. Curiel was a minor at the time of the killings and was tried as an adult, but prosecutors could not seek the death penalty under California law; Curiel and Huntsman were scheduled to be sentenced next week.

The passage describes analyte monitoring systems for diabetes management, including sensor applicators, sensor control devices with electronics housing, sensors with proximal and distal portions, and introducers (“sharp” hubs) used to place sensors under a user’s skin. It discusses challenges in sterilizing such systems because radiation sterilization (e.g., electron beam) can harm electronic components, while gaseous chemical sterilization (e.g., ethylene oxide) can damage sensor chemistry. To address this, it proposes sterilization approaches that avoid separating sensor and electronics by using a cap and collimator to define a sterilization zone that receives the sensor and sharp while preventing radiation from damaging electronics. The passage also outlines methods of preparing the system, describes seals to create a sterile region, and presents concepts for internal or external collimators and radiation shields. Finally, it includes a lengthy description of figures illustrating various system components and external sterilization assemblies.

The passage compiles multiple late-2000 news items, including coverage of weather risk management prompted by major storms, proposed changes to California’s wholesale electricity market following recommendations by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, and related Enron and Azurix transactions. It also reports on a Transwestern natural gas pipeline in New Mexico being cut by 25% after a train derailment and on U.S. natural gas cash prices rising amid storage and transportation constraints, with gas deliveries redirected due to damage to Enron’s Transwestern line. Additionally, it includes a profile of C.I. Global (a C.I. Mutual Funds global equity fund) and an arena debate in Houston.

The passage describes metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters using cyclic platinum(II) and palladium(II) complexes with benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues, represented by General Formulas I–III, IV, and V–XIII. It also presents octahedral iridium(III) MADF emitters represented by General Formulas XIV–XVII, and relates the compounds to full color display and lighting applications, including light-emitting diodes and lighting devices. The invention is stated to be supported by the U.S. Department of Energy under DE-EE0007090. The passage further provides detailed parameter definitions for the general formulas, mentions OLED device structures and layers where such emitters may be used, and includes multiple synthetic examples (e.g., Example 1–31) with reagents, conditions, yields, and some emission spectrum references.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on March 6, 2015 reporting actions effective March 3, 2015. The Board adopted an amendment to Tesla’s 2010 Equity Incentive Plan to prohibit certain transactions with the purpose or effect of repricing equity awards, without requiring stockholder approval (Exhibit 10.1). The Board also approved amendments to Tesla’s bylaws implementing a majority vote standard for electing directors in uncontested elections, while contested elections use a plurality standard, also without requiring stockholder approval (Exhibit 3.1).

The lecture concludes by describing how to construct SNARGs (Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments) using two building blocks: BARGs (Batch Argument) and somewhere extractable hash functions (SSB hashes). First, it recalls the structure and soundness notions of BARGs, including semi-adaptive soundness, and answers questions about whether indices other than the cheated one must be in the language and why fully adaptive conversion is non-trivial.  

It then defines somewhere extractable hash families, including algorithms (Gen, Eval, Open, Ver, Extract) and properties such as completeness, index hiding, and somewhere statistical binding. The lecture further explains how repeating the hash construction can yield binding on multiple locations while preserving hidden indices even when some trapdoors are revealed. It also notes properties of BARG verification efficiency for index languages, where verifier runtime depends on a succinct description rather than on the full batch size.  

Finally, it presents the SNARG construction: the prover computes all wires of a verification circuit, hashes the wire values using a somewhere extractable hash, and provides a BARG proof that every gate is satisfied and that the output wire evaluates to 1. The verifier checks the BARG proof; efficiency is maintained because the verifier’s input to the BARG corresponds to an index language that can be described succinctly.

The passage discusses a case reported in The Irish Times in which a suicidal girl was detained under the Mental Health Act after her psychiatrist ruled out the abortion she wanted. She was later released after a court-appointed guardian ad litem arranged a second psychiatrist assessment finding no evidence of a mental health disorder. Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated June 28, 2021. The report states that, effective July 5, 2021, Andrew R. The passage describes how coupling a quantum critical magnetic system to an optical cavity can amplify responses and enable a superradiant phase transition (SRPT) with enhanced optical squeezing and quantum entanglement. It focuses on a ferromagnetic transverse field Ising model (TFIM) where the cavity mode bilinearly couples to the TFIM order parameter; in this case, the critical cavity-spin coupling for the SRPT vanishes at the TFIM quantum critical point, making superradiant states accessible at arbitrarily weak light-matter coupling near the quantum critical regime. The SRPT involves condensation of a polaritonic mode, and the cavity-spin coupling produces intrinsic two-mode squeezing whose scaling and stronger behavior at the quantum critical point reflect underlying quantum criticality. For comparison, when the cavity couples to a non-critical mode (orthogonal to the Ising order parameter), the Dicke and Ising terms compete, yielding a more complex phase diagram with a tricritical point and anomalous scaling. Robustness is supported by comparing large-S results with density matrix renormalization group simulations for a spin-1/2 chain, and the proposal is discussed in terms of possible experimental study in cavity-magnonic systems.

The passage describes ongoing preparation for an Inquiry, including: examining existing Central Powers newspapers to track economic and political policy discussions; preparing a “Who’s Who” for several regions; digesting outstanding treaty obligations; compiling briefs for subject nationalities between the Baltic Sea and the Persian Gulf; creating charts of international organization plans and major international events since 1870; preparing declarations and proposals and actual practice regarding the creation of a new Poland; and ordering historical sketches, indexed volumes, and race-specific government participation and restrictions for five high-urgency areas. Jackson Chourio injured his hamstring during Game 1 of the NL Division Series and exited after being visited by manager Pat Murphy and head athletic trainer Brad Epstein. Brewers said he was getting an MRI, with Murphy describing the situation as “real scary” due to a prior similar hamstring injury. JM Smucker filed a lawsuit in the US District Court of Northern Ohio accusing Trader Joe’s of unfairly copying its Uncrustables crustless peanut butter and jelly sandwiches. Smucker’s alleges Trader Joe’s used protected design elements, including a crimped edge and a specific trademarked shade of blue, and says the brand is nearly $1 billion and widely consumed. Smucker’s spokesperson said the company is protecting the trademarked design and preventing consumer confusion, while Trader Joe’s did not respond to a comment request. Smucker is seeking disposal of Trader Joe’s crustless sandwiches and marketing materials and demands that Trader Joe’s account for and pay over profits from the sales.

The passage describes a “Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS)” intended to extend the range and capabilities of multiple unmanned systems by enabling autonomous swap of “Swap Cartridges (SCs)” for energized cartridges. The RPS detects a UAV’s request for a new SC, uses identifiers such as vehicle type, SC status, and location to determine landing, guides the UAV to a reconfigurable landing zone using sensors and visible or non-visible markers/emitters that generate scalable composite images, and mechanically and electrically connects to the UAV for the exchange. After landing, the RPS deploys a retention and swapping process: it withdraws the depleted SC, sends it to a modular power bay (MPB) for replenishment/storage, retrieves the appropriate replacement SC based on onboard/received data, elevates it to the landing zone, and installs it into the UAV via a universal Swap Cartridge Receptacle (SCR). The MPBs can house multiple types and sizes of SCs (including electric batteries, hydrogen fuel-cells, or fossil fuels), and SCs can include power and/or payload with identifying markers and connectors for power/data transfer. The RPS includes components such as a dynamic terminal landing system (DTL) for autonomous landing, a central processor (RPS-CP) for coordination and environmental monitoring, sensors for tracking the UAV/UIS location, communications via a universal swap cartridge processor (USP), and modular housing/enclosures that can be deployed in various environments. The passage also outlines methods for SC exchange that include permission to land, landing queue management, mission/payload data download, SC removal and replacement, environmental assessment for safe launch, and handling cases where only data transfer is needed.

The passage reviews experimental progress and theoretical understanding in orbitronics, which concerns orbital angular momentum and related effects such as the orbital Hall effect and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect. It explains that orbitronic effects are often studied using orbital torques measured in magnetic heterostructures, where orbital angular momentum must be converted to spin via spin-orbit coupling to directly affect magnetization. The efficiency of this conversion depends strongly on ferromagnetic materials, motivating the use of additional conversion layers (e.g., Pt or 4f transition metals). Quantitative separation of contributing processes is described as challenging. Beyond torque measurements, the passage discusses magnetoresistance-based, orbital pumping/THz emission, and more direct imaging approaches using magneto-optical and electron microscopy methods, as well as orbital Hanle magnetoresistance.

Experimental findings highlight roles of specific materials and interfaces, including CuOx as a strong source of orbital angular momentum that can enhance torques, and long orbital transport lengths inferred from thickness dependence and sign of torques. The text also describes theoretical issues, especially uncertainty about orbital relaxation/transport lengths and the reconciliation of experimental reports of long orbital relaxation with theoretical predictions. For applications, it focuses on MRAM, outlining potential advantages of orbital torque (e.g., not relying on spin-orbit coupling for generating orbital angular momentum and compatibility with low-resistivity light metals) while noting challenges such as achieving sufficiently large torque per current density, compatibility with high tunneling magnetoresistance, and reducing layer thicknesses by shortening orbital diffusion length. The passage concludes that orbitronics remains promising but that key generation, transport, conversion, and dissipation processes are not fully understood, with opportunities to tune effects through materials and interface engineering.

The passage compiles multiple reports and articles about Enron and broader credit and finance issues. The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly saw noisy scenes and opposition walkouts during the zero hour over allegations of assault on two Kashmiri students in Haryana. The state government said it had taken up the matter with Haryana and that three persons had been arrested, after the filing of an FIR and talks between senior officials. Opposition members questioned why an all-party meeting was held for upcoming panchayat elections when they said decisions had already been taken, and the Parliamentary Affairs Minister said the cabinet would discuss the meeting outcome. Ryan Dempster, a former Cubs ace now a special assistant, said it felt “gratifying” to see Kyle Hendricks—the player he was traded for—start Game 1 of the playoffs Friday night against the Nationals. Dempster recalled being traded to Texas in 2012 and later having Hendricks become a rotation fixture, win an ERA title last season, beat Clayton Kershaw in the NLCS clincher, and start the Cubs’ Game 7 World Series victory. He said he didn’t do anything for the trade beyond turning down other options, and described the situation as meaningful and somewhat like a full circle.

On July 25, 1977, the application for a writ of habeas corpus by the People of the State of New York on behalf of Harry H. Boddie against Ronald R. Emery, as Sheriff of Montgomery County, was denied under CPLR 7002 (subd [b], par 2). Sweeney, J. P., Kane, Main, Mikoll, and Herlihy concur.

Jason Ku, an MIT PhD mechanical engineering student and origami designer, discusses origami as an art form and explains design approaches for representational origami. He contrasts traditional crisp, polygon-based styles influenced by Akira Yoshizawa with non-traditional wet-folding and shaping styles by designers such as David Brill, Michael LaFosse, and Eric Joisel, emphasizing texture, emotion, and realism. He then describes “modern realism” and algorithmic origami design, highlighting Robert Lang’s tree theory and TreeMaker, along with examples from designers like Brian Chan and Satoshi Kamiya, including complex one-square-sheet and modular works. The lecture also reviews tree theory concepts for turning a subject into an origami base and model, including uniaxial bases, the role of flaps and “circle/river” space allocations, and how these map to hinge creases. He demonstrates a TreeMaker design workflow for a crab, notes common issues (e.g., crease/valley-mountain assignment problems), and references additional learning resources, including OrigaMIT events and Origami Design Secrets.

An American prisoner, Christian Beasley, escaped from Kerobokan prison in Bali by sawing through a ceiling and jumping over a 6-meter wall. He was arrested in August for carrying a package with 5.7 grams of hashish. Another American inmate, Paul Anthony Hoffam, was recaptured while attempting to escape. An investigation is underway into possible involvement of prison guards, amid reports of guard shortages and severe overcrowding. This was the second prison escape in Bali’s capital Denpasar since June, following a drainage tunnel escape that left two inmates still at large. The passage also notes that jailbreaks are common in Indonesia due to overcrowded prisons and the anti-drugs crackdown.

The passage discusses how a hockey team and its coach are addressing frustration and emotions during the playoffs, emphasizing refocusing and sticking to the game plan between shifts. The coach says playoff success depends on continuing to play, maintaining composure, driving to the net, creating second chances, getting loose pucks, and improving net-front presence on both ends. The coach compares two games, stating that the opposing team was better at the net, winning battles and scoring more “scramble” goals, and that the team must protect the blue paint area for its goalie while also creating offensive chances. The speaker describes scoring an overtime goal to win a game, saying it was driven by teammates’ effort, inspiration, passion, and emotion. HHH defends WWE’s decision to exclude women from The Greatest Royal Rumble. He says women’s inclusion is supported by cultural change, pointing to a women’s match in Abu Dhabi earlier and audience reactions. He argues different cultures must be respected and that change should not be pursued by staying away from it. The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 HBM2 DRAM memory subsystem and related architecture features. It explains that A100 uses fast HBM2 memory organized in five active stacks, delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, and supports SECDED ECC to protect data and other memory structures including caches and registers. It details A100’s 40 MB L2 cache architecture, including shared partitions and increased bandwidth versus V100, and notes Compute Data Compression that improves bandwidth and capacity. It also covers MIG (Multi-Instance GPU), which partitions an A100 GPU into up to seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated memory-system paths to provide predictable throughput, latency, QoS, and fault isolation while keeping the CUDA programming model unchanged. Additional sections summarize technologies such as third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, error detection and fault containment for multi-GPU and MIG environments, and several A100 architecture features (e.g., NVJPG, optical flow accelerator, atomic improvements, NVDEC). The passage further discusses CUDA 11/Amber architecture enhancements including CUDA Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, and L2 cache residency controls, and concludes with an overview of DGX A100 and an appendix on pruning/sparsity in neural networks.

The World Health Organization said Yemen’s cholera outbreak, which began nearly four months ago, has affected more than 500,000 people and caused 1,975 deaths, with 503,484 suspected cases. The WHO reported that spread slowed significantly since early July but still affects an estimated 5,000 people daily. It attributed the outbreak’s scale to the collapse of Yemen’s infrastructure after over two years of war, including deteriorating hygiene and sanitation and lack of clean water. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said health workers face “impossible conditions,” with thousands sick and insufficient hospitals, medicines, and clean water, and many doctors and nurses unpaid for nearly a year. He said more than 99% of people who contract the disease can survive if they access health services, and noted that over 15 million people lack basic healthcare, calling for urgent political solutions.

President Rutherford B. Hayes issued a proclamation warning that certain persons preparing to forcibly possess and settle on lands in the Indian Territory west of Arkansas—recognized as Indian country under U.S. treaties and laws—would be removed. The proclamation states that laws require removal of persons residing or trading there without express permission of the Indian Department and of persons deemed improper by its agents. Hayes admonishes those intending or preparing to remove or settle without permission, warns they will be removed speedily and immediately by the proper agent, and says military assistance may be invoked to enforce U.S. laws. The proclamation is dated April 26, 1879, and signed by Hayes with William M. Evarts as Secretary of State.

The passage describes a rapidly growing cosmetic tooth whitening market with many products available in stores, leading to consumer confusion. FDA approval is not required for these products because they are classified as “cosmetic,” and the FDA has not determined that currently marketed ingredients are unsafe. The American Dental Association’s seal of acceptance is offered for some products after independent dentist review and sometimes additional studies, and while only one over-the-counter product is noted as carrying the seal, others may still work if used as directed. Bleaching can cause temporary tooth sensitivity, may take two to six weeks for store products, and can leak onto gums if not used carefully. Alternatives include dentist-made custom trays (about $400, up to four weeks) or in-office bleaching (often over $1,000), which uses higher hydrogen peroxide concentrations and can produce faster, more dramatic results but is typically not covered by insurance. The passage also notes that some causes of discoloration cannot be bleached, such as trauma or permanent staining from tetracycline or excess fluoride, in which case crowns or veneers may be needed. It concludes that all bleaching is temporary and the ADA says there is no evidence that “natural whitening” remedies like charcoal, baking soda, or lemon juice work.

The Colombian government set a June 30, 2001 deadline for the delayed privatization of state-run power generator ISAGEN after a Council of State ruling struck down an injunction blocking the sale, following a complaint by Empresas Publicas de Medellin (EPM). EPM argued it was unfairly excluded from the bidding process and that its potential ownership would violate antitrust laws. Finance Minister Juan Manuel Santos said legal issues, possible changes in ISAGEN’s price tag, and paperwork updates would postpone the deal, requiring the process to restart with updated valuation and renewed negotiations; earlier timelines had targeted sales by Sept. 30, then Sept. 30 delays followed legal challenges and rebel attacks.

The tug Ocean Prince, push-towing the oil-laden barge New London, struck a charted rock outside the Hudson River’s navigable channel, causing damage and a substantial oil spill. Tug Ocean Prince, Inc. and Red Star Towing & Transportation Co. petitioned for exoneration or limitation of liability under 46 U.S.C. § 183 et seq. Pittston Marine Transport Corp. asserted claims for damage to the barge and loss of cargo. Red Star brought a third-party action against the United States, and the United States sought pollution cleanup costs and also sued them under 33 U.S.C. § 1321. The actions were consolidated for trial.  

The district court denied exoneration but granted limitation to the tug’s value, found Pittston not responsible for the spill, dismissed claims in various actions, and limited Red Star’s pollution cleanup liability to $100 per gross ton under 33 U.S.C. § 1321(g). The appeals followed “and nobody is happy.”  

On appeal, the Second Circuit concluded the district court was clearly erroneous in finding no negligence or unseaworthiness within Red Star’s privity and knowledge, and held Red Star failed to overcome its burden regarding the privity/knowledge issue. The appellate court also found that the failure to post a proper lookout contributed to the casualty and that this alone warranted denial of limitation. The court affirmed dismissal of the claims over against the United States.  

Regarding pollution cleanup costs, because the tug was unseaworthy at the start of the voyage and Red Star was negligent within its privity and knowledge, the court determined Red Star’s actions amounted to willful negligence or willful misconduct within the meaning of the statute, and therefore limitation should be denied. The appellate court vacated the district court’s limitation ruling as to Pittston’s claim and the United States’ cleanup-cost claim, directed judgment in favor of Pittston and the United States for their damages, and affirmed the district court in other respects.

The passage describes the “Single/Double” offense, a set used in most NBA playbooks to free up an outstanding shooter by having them run off double baseline screens and down screens. It attacks both sides of the defense simultaneously from an initial down-the-middle attack, aiming to make help defense difficult and create hard-to-defend options via single or double screen reads. It outlines basic actions, phases, reads and counters for situations such as defenders chasing, cheating, switching, or showing and recovering, plus ways to “break” double screens using actions like screen-and-roll and back-screen options that can produce scoring opportunities. It also covers execution keys for down screens and double screens, strong post-up plays, and offensive rebounding emphasis, noting that the offense can provide offensive rebounding advantages on the weakside. Finally, it discusses continuity options when initial shots aren’t available (motion, side screen, and drive-and-kick), and provides guidance for teaching and implementing the offense, including player readiness, drill use, individual skill work, and scouting opponents’ defensive responses.

CBD is a cannabis derivative, and the FDA’s approval would be limited to treating seizures caused by Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome in patients aged 2 and older. The FDA says studies provide substantial evidence of CBD’s effectiveness and that risks appear acceptable. Epidiolex, made by GW Pharmaceuticals as a purified, THC-free pharmaceutical-grade product, has undergone required testing and would be produced under good manufacturing practices. The passage contrasts Epidiolex with widespread CBD products whose claims are largely unsubstantiated and have prompted FDA warnings. Parents and physicians describe serious, refractory childhood epilepsy cases and report improvements after CBD treatment. The passage also notes that CBD is being considered for other conditions and differs from medical marijuana because it does not contain THC.

The passage criticizes Google’s Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL design consistency and marketing. It claims Google downplays the Pixel 2’s front in event coverage and store images, and argues the two phones are much more physically different in person than in marketing. It contrasts the smaller Pixel 2’s larger bezels and cornered/chamfered edges with the Pixel 2 XL’s curved glass and different speaker sound, build feel, and overall design quality. The writer says the Pixel 2 XL resembles the design Google “wanted,” while the Pixel 2 feels like modified HTC hardware and is a step back from last year’s more coherent “Made by Google” design vision. A birthday sleepover outside Milwaukee involving three 12-year-old girls ended with two girls missing and Payton Leutner crawling out of the woods covered in 19 stab wounds. A major search involving ground and air continued as a phone was checked for clues, leading to “goodbye notes” on Anissa’s cellphone, including a final wish not to grieve. Surgeon John Keleman said one stab wound cut through tissue but not the heart artery, preventing a major heart attack and likely death within minutes. Nearly five hours later, Morgan and Anissa were found walking near Interstate 94 and were questioned by Waukesha city police; a 5-inch-blade knife was found in one girl’s bag. At the police station, investigators questioned both girls separately about a plot to kill Payton, referring to her as “Bella.” Morgan said the plan had been in place since December and that Anissa described it as necessary, while both girls discussed beliefs connected to the fictional “Slender Man,” including an idea that becoming a proxy required killing someone. Payton was then unable to speak at first but asked if the other girls had been found, and she was told they had been found and police had them.

The passage describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensor systems for under-display and under-OLED display applications, including their operation and related challenges with limited space and interference in display devices. It explains how ultrasonic waves are transmitted through a display, reflected from fingerprint ridges and valleys, and processed to form fingerprint images for authentication. Multiple apparatus configurations are presented, including an ultrasonic sensor system underlying a display with an acoustic path through layers such as light-blocking layers, electrical shielding layers, adhesives, and mechanical stress isolation layers, which may be non-porous or substantially non-porous. The disclosure also covers example sensor structures (piezoelectric transceiver layers, pixel circuits, substrates, electrode layers) and manufacturing approaches for bonding/laminating these layers. It additionally details component and integration examples for OLED displays, including using thin and non-porous layers to preserve ultrasonic transmission and avoid degrading display performance, and using bonding/adhesive layers to reduce mechanical stresses and allow reworkability. The passage includes discussion of example mobile device architectures and cross-sectional figures illustrating different sensor orientations and layer arrangements, including receiver up/down configurations and optional foam or air backing layers for acoustic and mechanical protection.

The passage describes the motivation for trapped-ion experiments in atomic and quantum physics, noting that trapped-ion qubits have long coherence times and high gate fidelities, but entangling gate operation times are relatively slow (on the order of 1 µs or longer) due to entanglement being mediated mainly by ion-chain vibrational modes and limited by low quantum speed limits. It reviews proposals to overcome these limitations by inducing entanglement through electrical dipoles from Rydberg excitation and discusses using electrons created by exceeding the ionisation threshold, because electrons can respond more rapidly to electric fields. The text then proposes an “electron trap quantum computer” concept using a two-frequency Paul trap to confine both a laser-cooled Ca+ ion and a detached electron in the same space, enabling laser-accessible transitions for manipulating the electron’s motional and spin states. It explains categories of electron electronic states below and above the ionisation threshold, outlines how a laser-based photoionisation scheme can generate the electron-Ca2+ system, and presents the trapping potentials and Hamiltonian used for modelling. The passage also addresses experimental and technical challenges, including the need for very low temperatures for coupling and signal-to-noise requirements, and concludes with a planar trap design section describing a ring (point Paul) trap geometry aimed at optimizing electron and ion state energies and confining pseudopotential steepness.

AMP is described as coordinating and scheduling work to prevent performance drops, reduce time to first response, and prioritize game-engine work to avoid stuttering, delivering more predictable timing and improving quality of service. Blackwell adds hardware support for 4:2:2 chroma in video, explains YUV chromasampling tradeoffs, and supports 4:2:2 encoding/decoding. The passage further describes DLSS 4, including Multi Frame Generation and transformer-based neural model improvements for super resolution, ray reconstruction, and deep learning anti-aliasing. It outlines neural shader concepts and examples such as RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces, then provides hardware specifications and product positioning for Blackwell-based GPUs including GB202, GB203, and GB205, with associated GeForce RTX 50 series models.

The passage lists several Spanish stocks that may be affected by newspaper reports: OHL Obrascon Huarte Lain plans to pay a gross interim dividend of 0.349 euros per share; Gas Natural has abandoned a long-standing liquefied natural gas facility project in northern Italy and sold its Italian businesses; NH Hoteles says Minor of Thailand is the only bidder for HNA’s 26.3% stake in NH Hotel Group, offering about 6 euros per share or 600 million euros total; Acciona will pay a gross dividend of 3 euros per share on July 2; Dogi says its shareholder Businessgate will propose a company name change to Nueva Expresion Textil; and Parques Reunidos reports an H1 net loss of 58.6 million euros, compared with a loss of 65.4 million euros a year earlier. (NYSE:TWX) from buy to hold, citing past outperformance, positive earnings surprises, and benefits from investments and international presence, but noting risks from declining advertising spending and currency headwinds. The passage is an address by the U.S. President to Congress about a grave crisis in U.S.-Spain relations caused by the ongoing war in Cuba. It describes how Cuban revolutions against Spanish rule over decades have required U.S. neutrality enforcement, harmed American trade, and upset the public, while Spanish warfare is characterized as cruel and involving devastation and reconcentration of civilians that led to widespread starvation and disease. The President recounts efforts to seek mediation and honorable settlement, including proposals for peace talks and revocation of reconcentration, and explains that Spain did not accept the proposed immediate armistice and negotiation arrangement. The passage ends by stating that information has been received that Spain’s Queen Regent has directed a suspension of hostilities, which may affect the justification for U.S. contemplated action.

The ADS9803 outputs 20-bit conversion data in straight-binary or binary two’s-complement formats, with the output code format selected by the DATA_FORMAT register. The passage describes a study aiming to improve the identification of documented goals of care (GOC) discussions in electronic health record (EHR) clinical notes. Although GOC discussions are guideline-recommended and linked to better outcomes, they remain infrequent and are often documented inconsistently or only in the final days of life. The authors note that prior work used NLP methods on datasets enriched for GOC, which may not reflect real-world EHR conditions where such documentation is rare and inconsistently placed. They therefore train an NLP-based system to retrieve utterances documenting GOC conversations anywhere in EHR notes across a general hospital population with serious illness. Using 776 inpatient notes (including 400 Advance Care Planning notes and 376 general notes) from five hospitals, annotators labeled note utterances as part of a GOC conversation or not, with a palliative care specialist adjudicating disagreements. Because the dataset is extremely imbalanced, they compare passive learning with active learning, using active learning (uncertainty sampling) to select informative examples from unlabeled notes and improve classifier performance while reducing annotation effort. The best ensemble (five base classifiers with weighted-average aggregation, trained with active learning) achieved moderate performance: F1 of 0.557 for utterances and 0.629 for notes. On test data for note-level retrieval, it correctly identified 13 of 18 GOC notes while incorrectly identifying 13 non-GOC notes as GOC. The authors conclude the system can be deployed in production for semi-automated, clinician-curated search and report that they can reduce annotation needs by labeling about 30% of utterances from the unlabeled set without compromising performance.

Finally, it derives \(1/M_Q\) power-correction terms in the HQET Lagrangian by integrating out a field in the QCD Lagrangian, identifying kinetic and magnetic-moment operators that break symmetries in different ways. It also introduces reparameterization invariance (RPI) as a hidden symmetry related to the arbitrary split of the heavy-quark momentum into \(M_Q v + k\); RPI constrains subleading operator structure, implying a specific Wilson coefficient remains 1, while another coefficient has an anomalous dimension.

TMPM command processing can encounter errors in command format/content, which lead to command rejection, and errors in migration list entry content, which may cause partial success. These errors are reported within the commands and/or migration list entries across TMPM command types. Ring Buffer management errors are reported in the PM_STATUS register, including memory addressing errors. Hardware operation errors are reported in command status and/or via the Machine Check Architecture (MCA). If TMPM times out, the client should log an MCA, attempt error detection/correction, and decide actions such as saving state, terminating VMs, or not issuing more TMPM commands. A command can process up to 128 pages per batch; hardware errors during processing can make all pages unrecoverable. Failures return command status codes, but the operated memory state may be unfixable, eventually causing the system to stop functioning after software saves current data and state.

The Supreme Court, Bronx County, judgment from April 1, 1976 convicting Frank Dellipizzi, after a jury trial, of first-degree robbery and sexual abuse is unanimously affirmed. The court found no question raised about the sufficiency of evidence for robbery, and determined the evidence for sexual abuse was wholly sufficient, including statements and conduct involving the complainant and an accomplice. The court criticized a supplemental jury charge on acting in concert, cautioning against language that could be misconstrued as shifting the burden of proof on intent. It held that, considering the charge as a whole and the jury’s questions, the burden of proof was not shifted.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 16, 2018. It reports that on August 16, 2018, certain Tesla subsidiaries that are parties to two Deutsche Bank warehouse loan agreements entered amendments. The amendments extended the borrowing availability date from August 17, 2018 to August 16, 2019 and extended the agreements’ maturity date from September 2019 to September 2020, while keeping the shared aggregate lender commitment at $1.1 billion. The report also includes an Item 2.03 reference to the information in Item 1.01 and is signed by Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja on August 21, 2018.

The swinging gate formation is an unconventional special teams play in football where the offense can run a trick play or shift into a field goal/extraf point formation to attempt a kick, typically on two-point conversion attempts after a touchdown. The offense lines up with kicking team personnel so the kicker is on the field as an eligible receiver, and the offensive line detaches from the long snapper while receivers can line up in different ways. The play is designed to give the defense an unusual look with little warning, hoping the offense can snap quickly to run or throw before the defense can react; if the defense does not show the expected look, the offense can shift back late to attempt an extra point. The passage also describes trick plays from the swinging gate, including a side snap to a running back and quick passes, and explains defensive principles for handling it, such as matching personnel, taking away threats to the heavy side, and using athletic players to cover key “alley” areas. Examples and additional notes on NFL usage are included, along with a reference to Coach John Grayson’s presentation.

The passage explains that Commanders rookie running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt saw an increased workload in Week 5 because of his practice, according to head coach Dan Quinn. Croskey-Merritt recorded season-highs with 14 carries and 16 touches, producing 150 scrimmage yards (111 rushing) and two touchdowns, and he played 28 snaps. ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler said fans shouldn’t lose hope, noting that lack of experience was holding Bill back while Croskey-Merritt was expected to become more involved over time.

The passage argues that the proposed interoceanic canal would benefit America industrially and strengthen its military position, while also aiding tropical American countries. It praises American military and civil efforts, notes that war has ceased, and asserts that wrongdoing by troops was limited and addressed, while emphasizing the large amount of beneficent work done there.

The passage describes NYSE traders and stock-market leverage, noting that while various forms of leverage are not tracked, “margin debt” is measured as the borrowing by investors from brokers. Margin debt rose $22.9 billion in January to $665.7 billion, then fell $20.7 billion in February to $645.1 billion, and slightly increased to $645.2 billion in March, remaining below January levels, according to FINRA, which took over margin-debt reporting from the NYSE. FINRA previously warned investors in January that they may underestimate the risks of trading on margin and misunderstand margin calls, including the ability of brokers to liquidate portfolios under unfavorable conditions, causing losses and preventing participation in market rebounds. The passage also states that over the 12 months through March, margin debt rose $67.6 billion, after a much larger increase in the 12 months ended in January, and that margin debt has risen since 2009 with some down periods during prior sell-offs. It cites correlations between margin-debt surges and market crashes historically, but suggests that the current correction may be more orderly and gradual.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on March 4, 2020. The filing states that on March 4, 2020, NVIDIA’s Compensation Committee adopted a Variable Compensation Plan for Fiscal Year 2021. FLIR Systems Inc reported fourth quarter and full year 2016 financial results. Q4 adjusted earnings per share were $0.52 and GAAP earnings per share were $0.45. Q4 revenue was $474.7 million versus an I/B/E/S view of $452.6 million, and Q4 earnings per share view was $0.54. The company increased its quarterly dividend by 25% to $0.15 per share and approved a new share repurchase program authorizing repurchases of up to 15 million shares over the next two years.
