The passage describes planned approaches for safety and other clinical trial analyses. It specifies how investigators assign causal relationship (not related, unlikely, possibly, probably), how missing causal assessments are handled (queries; otherwise set to “related” for analysis), and how AE severity is graded (mild, moderate, severe) while leaving missing severities un-imputed. It outlines preparation of AE summary and frequency tables by MedDRA terms, ordered by incidence, and provides rules for counting patients with multiple events under the same term. It also defines how special search categories for TEAEs are identified. For laboratory data, it specifies tabulation methods (including reference range flagging, categorical results, and change from baseline calculations) and that all AE/laboratory data are listed with rules for using the most recent value at a visit. Additional sections cover tabulations/listings for hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy tests, alcohol breath tests, vital signs, and ECG summaries (including QTcF thresholds and change-from-baseline thresholds). Immunogenicity (ADA) is analyzed descriptively without statistical tests, with incidence calculations based on ADA-positive samples during the trial and exclusions of certain baseline-positive patients without post-dose samples. The passage also lists changes to protocol-specified analyses in the SAP and includes appendices on data presentation/programming QC requirements, missing/incomplete date handling assumptions for AEs and medications, formulas for derived variables, and an index of planned tables/figures/listings.

Secondary efficacy endpoints assess plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes after injection, defined as a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline at the specified times using actual sampling timepoints. If IV glucose is given before recovery, the patient is classified as “not recovered” for the four endpoints, corresponding to censoring in the primary endpoint time-to-recovery analysis. Recovery rates for dasiglucagon versus placebo at each timepoint are compared using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, with responder rates and 95% confidence intervals reported. If this test fails due to small or zero cell counts, plasma glucose changes from baseline at each timepoint are analyzed with an ANOVA including treatment (3 levels), age group (2 levels), and injection site (2 levels); if rescue IV glucose is administered before a timepoint, the change is determined from the value at rescue administration. Nominal sampling time is used to calculate change from baseline, and least-square mean adjusted treatment means with 95% confidence intervals are presented.

In April, mutual funds’ equity exposure to IT/software stocks rose to an all-time high of nearly Rs 71,000 crore amid a depreciating rupee and market volatility. As of April, allocation to software stocks was Rs 70,773 crore, or 7.37% of total equity AUM of Rs 9.6 lakh crore, up from Rs 64,265 crore in March and Rs 42,023 crore in April 2017. The exposure is the highest since August 2009. Since January, fund infusion into software stocks increased from Rs 29,937 crore to Rs 70,773 crore, which industry experts attributed to the declining rupee that boosts exporters’ rupee revenue. The BSE IT index rose over 18% year-to-date, while the Sensex grew 2.5%. Other sector exposures include finance (Rs 96,727 crore) and consumer durables (Rs 64,476 crore).

Hello Wood, a Hungary-based architecture studio, designed the Pebl Grand prefab tiny cabin, built to blend into nature and resemble a spaceship. The Pebl Grand is about 200–220 square feet, includes a king-size bed, kitchenette, dining nook, and bathroom, and can be customized, with an upgraded version adding an infrared sauna and panoramic window. Its asymmetrical, faceted shell uses organic materials like wood and stone with aluminum, and exterior cladding can be mirror, wood, or stone. Hello Wood can manage permits, site preparation, and installation, and the unit is factory-built in Hungary; for overseas clients it ships as flat-packed panels. Options include using it as a pop-up suite or rooftop rest space, and the interior is described as minimalist yet luxurious, with oak-lined walls and features like saunas and large windows.

The U.S. dollar and Treasury yields fell on Thursday after Donald Trump said the dollar is too strong and that he wants U.S. interest rates kept low, alongside rising tensions over North Korea. The dollar index dropped 0.6% and U.S. yields eased to 2.232%. Asian markets were mixed: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan rose about 0.6%, Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.7%, and Australian stocks fell 0.75%. North Korea tensions lifted South Korea CDS to a 9½-month high, while Korean stocks and the won rose after South Korea’s central bank kept its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% and upgraded its growth outlook. Oil prices declined on concerns about increasing U.S. supply, with U.S. crude at $53.05 and Brent at $55.84.

Cam Newton apologized on social media more than 24 hours after making a sexist remark. The passage suggests the apology could help him avoid further questioning by reporters after his next game. The passage lists multiple telegrams between Washington and Helsinki (sometimes via Stockholm) from September to December 1942, and includes two documents dated January 3, 1942: (1) a letter from the U.S. Secretary of State to the Finnish Minister requesting that the Finnish Legation inquire with the Department of State about trips by Finnish Legation and consular personnel outside Washington and their consular districts, providing visit details and transportation methods; each inquiry would be answered in writing. Union Finance Minister Arun Jaitley said India’s growth has been impressive despite subdued global economic growth, citing an average 7.5% growth from 2014-15 to 2016-17 and a reversal of declining growth in the second quarter of 2017-18. He said India is following a fiscal consolidation roadmap, with fiscal deficit at 3.9% of GDP in 2015-16, 3.5% in 2016-17, and a budgeted 3.2% for 2017-18, achieved through expenditure rationalisation, plugging loopholes via Direct Benefit Transfer and PFMS, and innovative revenue efforts. The 5th Pre-Budget Consultation meeting with leading economists included officials from NITI Ayog, the Finance Ministry and others. The economists suggested measures for fiscal consolidation, tax reforms, incentives for infrastructure and SMEs, better pricing for farmers, additional disinvestment, increases in social security pensions and full maternity implementation, corporate tax reduction and other tax changes, incentives for labour-intensive industries, improvements to tax administration, reforms to crop insurance, new bonds for pension and infrastructure, investment promotion, rural non-farm incentives, defence investment, higher NREGA wages, new bodies for economic strategy and skills planning, support for R&D and banking recapitalisation, implementation of insolvency reforms, expansion of DBT and digital payments, and policies to increase jobs and social protection.

The passage explains football offensive formations, noting that generic names may not match a team’s playbook terminology. Rasterization has long been the standard in real-time rendering but has limitations such as artifacts in reflections and shadows, aliasing and light leaks in rasterized shadows, and screen-space reflections only reflecting objects visible on screen. Ray tracing can produce more realistic images but is computationally intensive, so the passage describes hybrid rendering that combines rasterization (for primary visibility) with ray tracing (for reflections, refractions, and shadows) to improve visual quality while maintaining performance.

It also discusses key Turing GPU technologies supporting real-time ray tracing, including RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, denoising to reduce required rays, and co-operative hybrid rendering where rasterization and ray tracing pipelines operate simultaneously. The document explains how ray tracing works (reverse ray casting from the camera, BVH acceleration, and denoising) and highlights that ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections can address shortcomings of shadow maps, SSAO, and screen-space reflections. Finally, it describes related features such as Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering, along with NVIDIA NGX for AI-based image enhancements, and outlines additional Turing architecture and software concepts enabling these capabilities.

The passage describes SEV-TIO guest requests, including how an SNP guest discovers request-type support via TEE-IO PCIe capabilities and how a device is bound after the first SNP TIO guest request. It explains the setup responsibilities for TIO-unenlightened guests, outlines differences in SNP TIO guest request non-optional unencrypted data (such as guest PCI ID, MMIO range state, and TDISP status), and specifies how data pages may be used to return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report. It further discusses Secure AVIC, including guest actions to register or unregister per-vCPU APIC backing pages and required hypervisor behavior. The passage also covers termination request behavior, handling of unsupported non-automatic exits, guest identification of SEV-ES via hypervisor CPUID properties, challenges and methods for SMP AP booting under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, and the SEV-SNP AP creation feature for creating/updating vCPU state via VMGEXIT. Finally, it defines #HV doorbell page structure and interrupt delivery/EOI semantics, and describes guest behavior for acknowledging #HV and processing interrupts, along with general requirements for system components like nested virtualization and debug register virtualization for SEV-ES.

The passage contains discussion from a hockey coach about upcoming and past playoff games. It emphasizes mental toughness and the need to get the puck and players to the net, noting that results may not be “pretty” but improved puck-to-net chances create better opportunities. The coach says everyone in the room wants to win, but preparation and playing well are what matter. The coach also critiques performance factors such as skating, puck management, speed, physical engagement, and executing better than the opponent, citing a game against Ottawa as an example of the team not missing a beat and giving credit to the other team for being hungrier and executing better.

Saudi Arabia’s stock market retreated 0.6% as Dar Al Arkan, a real estate firm, fell sharply after having surged earlier; it ended down 9.9% at 12.60 riyals following a bubble driven by retail investors. Analysts said the stock had risen well above fair value. Saudi cement shares rose on expectations of higher government spending in 2018 after austerity, with Jouf Cement reaching its highest level since early 2016. In Qatar, the index gained 1.2% after rebounding from near six-year lows. In Dubai, the index rose 0.6% as Emaar Development rebounded 2.6%, despite trading below its IPO price. Other regional index movements were listed in the highlights section.

The passage describes a patent application for a continuation of earlier U.S. and international applications, incorporating their disclosures by reference. The invention concerns a novel phase-stable colloidal polysaccharide suspension (gels) based at least partly on never-dried (1→3)-glucan, optionally mixed with other gel-forming polysaccharides such as cellulose gels. The objective is a suspension requiring no chemical or enzymatic pretreatment and offering high energy efficiency. The method uses a press cake of initially moist polysaccharide (solids 4–80% by weight, preferably 15–45%) and adjusts the final polysaccharide concentration (0.01–50% by weight, preferably 1.0–20%) by adding water, then prepares the suspension by mechanical comminution using a dispersing unit (e.g., Ultraturrax or colloid mill), with high pressure homogenizer use optional for improved homogeneity. The suspension is prepared without dissolving/precipitating steps and, when (1→3)-glucan is never dried, forms a 3-dimensional network and provides shear-diluting behavior and film-forming properties. Examples compare suspensions made from initially moist versus dried glucans, showing better stability and water retention for never-dried material, and demonstrate film formation, viscosity behavior at different solids contents, and spray-dried particle characteristics.

Gold prices ended steady at Rs 28,300 per ten grams in New Delhi on the first trading day of 2017, with gains capped due to global markets being closed. At MCX, gold for February delivery rose by Rs 83 to Rs 27,528 per 10 grams. Silver declined by Rs 100 to Rs 39,300 per kg due to reduced offtake by industrial units, while weekly-based delivery increased by Rs 495 to Rs 39,195 per kg.

Asia stocks were muted after mixed Chinese PMIs, while Australia was cautious ahead of the RBA. The S&P 500 closed higher ahead of upcoming jobs data. Duke extended men’s basketball head coach Jon Scheyer through the 2030-31 season, adding two years to his previous contract. The extension follows his success in three seasons, including 89 wins, an Elite Eight appearance in 2024, and a Final Four appearance last season, plus ACC regular-season and conference tournament titles in 2024-25. The article also notes Duke’s recruiting success under Scheyer, including No. 1-ranked classes in three of his four recruiting cycles, and that Duke is expected to begin the new season ranked inside the top 10 after losing all five starters to the NBA.

Virgin Galactic conducted a second rocket-powered test flight of its VSS Unity space tourism spaceship over Southern California. The rocket motor fired for 31 seconds, reaching 114,500 feet before Unity glided and landed at Mojave Air and Space Port, where Richard Branson greeted pilots Dave Mackay and Mark “Forger” Stucky and the crew of the carrier aircraft. Branson said it was the sixth powered test flight of the SpaceShipTwo design and the second since the fatal crash of the Spaceship Enterprise on Oct. 31, 2014. Virgin Galactic said Unity completed extensive engine testing and seven glide tests before this powered flight.

The passage describes dimensional, mechanical, and electrical requirements for a 940-pin ceramic µPGA Socket 940 and its package. It specifies contact materials and plating (high-strength copper alloy; nickel underplating and gold on the mating area) and SMT solder ball details (0.76 mm balls, 63/37 tin/lead ±5%) including solder barrier and a solder ball field co-planarity requirement (0.20 mm). It also lists actuation lever requirements, force limits for actuation/de-actuation and insertion/extraction, pin displacement limits (<1.0 mm), and durability and inspection criteria after 50 actuations. Electrical requirements include a current rating of 1.5 A per contact with limited temperature rise, circuit resistance limits for initial and final LLCR (<25 mΩ per contact when mated with Kovar pins, measured on daisy-chained pairs), inductance and capacitance limits at 500 MHz and 2 GHz, differential impedance requirements, propagation delay skew limits, dielectric withstanding voltage (minimum 650 Vac), and insulation resistance (minimum 1000 MΩ).

Vincent Bollore, Vivendi’s chairman and largest shareholder, told the European Commission he will obtain “sole control” of Vivendi after the shareholders meeting on April 25. He owns a 20.65% stake that would give him 29% of Vivendi’s voting rights. The Commission has until April 24 to approve. Since becoming head in 2014, Bollore has increased his control of Vivendi’s supervisory board by appointing his son Yannick and reducing independent members. The Bollore Group and Vivendi declined to comment.

Newly elected Student Association State Quad senators said residents misunderstand asbestos despite notices in housing documents and dorm signage. Cassandra Jones and Max Sevor reported confusion and concern after Jones dorm-stormed Eastman Tower. Residential Life has posted asbestos warnings for about 20 years, asking tenants to avoid disturbing ceilings; asbestos is described as harmful only through long-term exposure when ceilings are disturbed. Facilities Management and Environmental Health and Safety discussed posting a frequently asked questions section on the university website, noting past asbestos information efforts and that some older buildings may contain traces of asbestos. The passage also includes claims from RAs that housing directors asked staff not to discuss asbestos to avoid panic, which Residential Life director Carol Perrin denied. RAs said they would talk anonymously, and they argued that greater dialogue and earlier, clearer information—rather than just signage—would be more effective.

Mick Schumacher said he is “not ready” to start thinking about moving into Formula One. After turning 18 in March, he said he took note of other drivers who entered F1 early but he is still stepping out of Formula 4, where he did not win a title. He aims to win in European F3 in the next few years and described his first year there as focused on learning and competing for the front in the rookie ranking. He said there is “no plan” for F1 yet, wants to prove himself and improve, and added that early interest in his career, including from Mercedes and Ferrari, is flattering. He also said adjusting to media attention now will be better than later.

The case involves cross appeals from a Family Court order that dismissed the mother’s request to modify a custody arrangement under Family Court Act article 6. In July 2003, the father received sole custody of two daughters and the mother received visitation “subject to the children’s wishes.” After the father moved to Florida with the daughters in 2004 without telling the mother, the mother sought orders for temporary custody and denial of relocation; the court found the father committed multiple intentional violations of the custody order by blocking the mother’s communication and visitation attempts and moving without providing their address, but initially did not change physical custody. 

After a prolonged hearing (June 30, 2004 to February 2005) and in camera proceedings, Family Court in March 2005 denied the mother’s petition for custody of the younger daughter but continued visitation subject to the daughters’ wishes and ordered the father to allow the mother phone, e-mail, and correspondence access. The court concluded the father’s conduct created a change in circumstances but that changing physical custody was not shown to be in the younger daughter’s best interests, while admonishing the father to foster a meaningful relationship with the mother.

On appeal, the court agreed custody should remain with the father but held visitation between the younger daughter and the mother should not have been left to the daughter’s wishes. The appellate court remitted the matter for immediate consideration of court-ordered visitation based on an updated in camera hearing, and it affirmed the order as modified. The court also found support for suspending the mother’s child support payments pending further order.

The passage is an excerpt from Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 26, 2020 (Q1 2021). The passage discusses how educators should address bigotry, racism, and white supremacy after the Charlottesville, Va., attack in which James Alex Fields Jr. drove into a crowd of anti-racist marchers. Denise Ricco said she learned her son’s mild autism spectrum disorder in fourth grade and thinks earlier knowledge could have helped families seek additional support. She is participating with her husband and son in SPARK, described as the largest study seeking genetic markers of autism, which asks 50,000 families to be tested. The study allows participation through home DNA collection via cheek swab and Internet submission, and families receive a $50 gift card. As of early April, 25,328 individuals with ASD and their families were participating, with Rush University Medical Center handling the Chicago-area portion. Researchers also offered optional in-person testing dates in May and June in Evanston and Northbrook. The study aims to clarify how autism may be genetic, including efforts to identify specific markers and study treatments for groups with certain genetic deletions, while stating prevention is not the study’s focus.

The report “Global Geiger-Mueller Counters Industry 2018 Market Research Report” is an in-depth study analyzing the global Geiger-Mueller Counters industry for 2018–2025. He had been battling idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive lung condition that caused scarring and rapidly worsened toward the end of 2025. His wife Maria, daughter Rose, and son Ted were with him. It lists possible causes, including injury-related fibrosis potentially linked to acid reflux, certain viruses, and environmental dust exposure. Symptoms described include shortness of breath, persistent cough, tiredness, and finger/toe clubbing.

In college football, targeting is an important foul where a player “takes aim” at an opponent with forcible contact beyond a legal tackle/block or playing the ball. The rule includes helmet-to-helmet forcible head-to-head contact and applies to hits on defenseless players, defined as especially vulnerable due to position and focus; when in question, a player is considered defenseless. NCAA penalties include a 15-yard penalty plus disqualification: if called in the first half, the player is disqualified for the remainder of the game; if called in the second half, the player is suspended for the first half of the next game (and if in the second half of the season’s final game, during the postseason or the first game of the following season). In the NCAA, targeting is separate from the NFL, where the analogous penalty is unnecessary roughness against a defenseless posture and does not automatically lead to disqualification unless officials deem the action flagrant. The rule was adopted in 2008, amended in 2013 to formalize disqualification and related suspension rules, and in 2019 made video review required to confirm or deny targeting and added punishment for repeat offenders.

Phase separation and coarsening are common in multiphase complex fluids, but some mixtures coarsen without reaching equilibrium, such as out-of-equilibrium passive mixtures under forcing and active mixtures driven by energy-consuming reactions; the cell cytoplasm is cited as an example. Quenching binary liquids can trigger liquid-liquid phase separation, with droplet coarsening driven by mechanisms including Ostwald ripening and collision-driven coalescence (Smoluchowski coagulation), often showing power-law scaling near equilibrium and self-similar growth. Under external shear, coarsening can be suppressed and a dynamical steady state reached. 

The study investigates DNA-rich droplet coarsening in a 3D self-stirring active fluid made of extensile microtubule bundles, PEG, and clustered molecular motors. DNA droplets form upon quenching and exchange material; droplet growth after a steady volume fraction is reached is attributed mainly to Smoluchowski coarsening rather than Ostwald ripening. Experiments and simulations compare active droplets advected by active flows with passive droplets diffusing in a passive fluid. Active and passive droplets show the same mean-radius scaling exponent (βR≈1/3), while the droplet-number exponent differs and active coarsening is not self-similar because the relative size distribution evolves over time. Droplet transport measurements show that effective diffusivity in active fluids is independent of droplet size and is set by active-flow properties rather than Brownian thermal effects. 

Simulations using different motility rules and analyses of collision kernels link the coarsening behavior to droplet motility: the relationship between the coarsening exponents βR and γN becomes nonlinear when the collision kernel favors collisions between large droplets. A collision kernel scaling with exponent k follows k = 3 − (m+2)/α, where m is the Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland scaling exponent and α is the anomalous diffusion exponent. A probabilistic iterative method using the prescribed collision kernel reproduces the observed loss of self-similarity and the nonlinear βR–γN relationship when k>0. The work concludes that the positive scaling exponent of the collision kernel is a key control parameter unifying active and passive coarsening behavior, and it discusses biological implications, particularly for nuclear condensate coarsening, while noting limitations related to system size and droplet sizes relative to active length scales.

President Trump said the American Dream is “on hold” because “big homebuilders” are “sitting on 2 million empty lots,” and he suggested they may be colluding. He cited NAHB data that most single-family builders report a shortage of lots and said persistent lack of permitted land limits construction and worsens price pressures. Caplan also said that differences across regions like Texas and San Francisco reflect local freedom to build rather than financing, and he doubted that entities like Freddie Mac could overcome local approval processes. He concluded that attention to the housing shortage may have symbolic value, but change requires confronting zoning rather than blaming builders.

Rare diseases affect fewer than 1 in 2,000 people but collectively impact about 300 million people globally. The passage describes an approach using RNA-sequencing and transcriptome-wide detection of splicing outliers to improve diagnosis in rare disease cohorts. Less than half of individuals with a rare disease have a definitive genetic diagnosis, and many gene-centric analyses may miss monogenic mechanisms producing transcriptome-wide splicing patterns.

The study analyzed RNA-seq data from 390 individuals with rare diseases using FRASER (two versions) to detect excess outlier splicing events. Enrichment analyses showed that genes identified as splicing outliers were significantly enriched for OMIM genes and genes implicated in developmental delay and intellectual disability (with different patterns between the two FRASER versions). About 10.3% of the cohort had excess outlier status across at least one metric.

Focusing on intron retention outliers in minor intron containing genes (MIGs), the authors identified five individuals (A1, B1, C1-2, D1) with excess intron retention outliers. Four cases (A1, B1, C1-2) had rare, biallelic variants in the minor spliceosome snRNA gene RNU4ATAC consistent with “RNU4atac-opathy.” The remaining case (D1) did not have RNU4ATAC or RNU12 variants but instead had rare, compound heterozygous variants in RNU6ATAC, leading the authors to propose RNU6ATAC as a novel candidate gene-disease association pending additional cases and functional validation. The passage also reports that technical factors like batch effects can influence measured outlier junction counts, while the MIG intron-retention signature in minor spliceopathy cases appeared robust.

Vijay Mallya, the fugitive liquor baron sought by India over unpaid bank loans of nearly Rs 9,000 crore, appeared before Westminster Magistrates’ Court for an extradition case hearing. He denied the allegations, said he had “enough evidence” to plead his case, and taunted authorities about “a billion pounds.” Chief Magistrate Emma Louise Arbuthnot granted him bail until December 4 and set July 6 for the next case management hearing, though she excused him from attending due to his defence team saying he was swarmed by media cameras. The Crown Prosecution Service, representing Indian authorities, sought a December final hearing date, while Mallya’s defence team argued for March or April 2018 and said they are awaiting “final evidence” and expect a second extradition request. The CPS said the current case could be concluded by December, and that India would responsibly handle any future request. The judge also warned Mallya not to breach bail conditions. The passage notes that extradition proceedings could involve appeals and that, under the 1992 Extradition Treaty between India and the UK, the home secretary would need to order extradition within two months if the trial ends in favour of extradition, with only one prior extradition under the arrangement.

For UEFI porting, it describes SEC/PEI/DXE/RTP execution considerations, required stack/cache procedures, and PEIM/DXE driver roles for processor and memory initialization.

Sprint plans to donate about $2.16 billion over five years for wireless service, tech support, and staffing, and says many first-year devices were donated by multiple vendors.

The passage argues that U.S. higher education has a long history of discrimination and that its “ripple effects” remain in current funding inequities. It cites examples such as Ole Miss receiving twice the state funding per student as Jackson State, and Connecticut’s UConn receiving more per-student funding than Southern Connecticut State University, with the gap widening by 2022 despite SCSU serving more Pell Grant recipients and larger numbers of Native, Black, Hispanic, and Pacific Islander students. The passage says inequities persist because funding is often based on prior-year appropriations (“base plus”) rather than formulas that account for institutional and student need, and because equity has not been a goal of funding policy. It also traces these patterns to historical exclusion, including the creation of community colleges, HBCUs, and women’s colleges in contexts of limited access for marginalized groups. The proposed solution is to rebuild higher education funding with equity first, using need-based allocation tied to student and institutional need and accounting for outside revenue sources, while funding education and student supports separately from other missions.

The passage argues that climate education has mainly focused on scientific understanding and remediation strategies, while often ignoring its epistemic foundations. The authors contend that current approaches lack discussion of the historical, interconnected arc behind climate change, including the erasures of Black and Indigenous knowledge systems and historical injustices requiring reparative projects. They propose reorienting climate education through “decolonial educational ecologies,” which center historically marginalized cosmologies and knowledge systems and confront human and more-than-human power imbalances. 

Within Comparative and International Education, the passage notes that climate change is frequently addressed through Education for Sustainable Development, tied to global UN frameworks and SDGs. It challenges this framework by criticizing “climate solutionism,” “greenwashed” or corporate-led initiatives, and the idea that resilience should be placed on the Global South. It develops the concept of “climate coloniality,” describing how colonial power structures shape who bears climate impacts and how climate solutions can continue patterns of extraction and dispossession. The passage also outlines a “contrapuntal reading” approach to examine which voices are amplified or marginalized in climate education discourse, and it concludes by advocating decolonial, context-based educational practices that avoid reproducing colonial dynamics and support alternative ways of knowing and relating to more-than-human worlds.

The passage argues that the brain does not contain information, data, rules, programs, representations, memories, or other components used by computers, and that people have misled themselves by treating the brain as a computer—an idea the author calls the “IP metaphor.” It describes how babies are born with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms but not with stored computational elements. Using a dollar-bill drawing demonstration, it claims people cannot retrieve a stored image from memory to draw accurately. The passage then reviews historical metaphors for intelligence and argues that the computer analogy became dominant after early work in cognitive science, yet is “sticky” and logically flawed. It contrasts the IP view with accounts that explain intelligent behavior without computations, and it disputes predictions about downloading minds and achieving immortality. The author concludes that brain changes are unique and not like stored, copyable computer data, and criticizes large brain-research efforts based on questionable promises, including the European Union’s Human Brain Project. The author, Robert Epstein, is described as a senior research psychologist and author.

Solution-processed semiconductors are described as a promising, inexpensive alternative to epitaxial materials for optoelectronic devices, but organic laser diodes are challenging due to low carrier mobility and losses from triplet excitons, polarons, and singlet-triplet annihilation. Inorganic materials, including metal halide perovskites (MHPs), have shown prerequisites for laser diodes such as optically pumped continuous-wave polariton lasing and electrically assisted amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), but electrically pumped devices face issues at high current density including EL roll-off from charge-carrier imbalance and Joule heating, low thermal conductivity, and ion-driven effects like unwanted doping and electrode corrosion.  

The passage reports an electrically driven polariton laser based on solution-grown CsPbBr3 perovskite microplates integrated into an optical microcavity. Charge injection is achieved using a chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) thin-film electrode, and a two-stage cooling protocol (280 K then 8 K with constant current) is used to convert an MSM Schottky diode into a rectifying p-i-n structure while preventing continuous p-i-n propagation. Under continuous electrical injection at 8 K, polariton lasing is observed with a threshold current of 60 µA (about 2.8 kA cm−2), accompanied by linewidth narrowing, mode-dependent blueshifts attributed to Joule heating, and spatially localized electroluminescence. The authors conclude that the device demonstrates a perovskite polariton laser diode under continuous direct electrical pumping.

The passage describes a divisional patent application about real-time measurement and control in surgical drilling/driving instruments to determine material strength and improve procedure safety. It explains that torque, energy, power, depth, and forces can be sensed in real time during tissue penetration, processed by a controller, and displayed to the user via an instrument display or an external (possibly wireless) GUI. Based on energy and torque signals, the system can determine regional material strength of tissue and provide information related to conditions such as osteoporosis. The instrument architecture includes working tools (e.g., drills or implants), a sensor for torque and/or force, rotational and axial drive motors, a guide harp with rods for depth control, and optionally axial force sensors on the tool and guide harp. Depth control can mitigate inadvertent plunge by using real-time signals (including power plots) and can measure depth using encoders/transducers. The passage also discusses device components such as guide geometry, motor/sensor mounting (including “floating” torque sensor configurations), communications modules, and optional tool identification. It further provides examples of GUI plotting and alerting based on sensor outputs, and references drawings and detailed embodiments of the described systems and methods.

The passage argues that scientific progress depends on how existing ideas are recombined, but not all recombinations are equally generative. It proposes that a key type of recombination occurs when linking concepts creates knowledge gaps—structural “holes” in a concept network—potentially focusing future research on nearby unexplored connections. The authors analyze 34,363,623 journal and conference papers from Microsoft Academic Graph (1900–2020) using dynamic concept networks built from co-occurrence of level-3 fields, and they use persistent homology to detect gap-opening papers that create topological holes. They find gap openers are rare (0.84%) yet significantly outperform other papers: they are more likely to be highly cited, more disruptive, and show greater delayed recognition and long-term citation impact. Gap openers also tend to come from smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically proximate teams, and use language associated with creation and innovation. The study concludes that topological significance of conceptual recombination—not novelty alone—drives greater generative capacity and long-term scientific influence.

A recent study reports that people with asthma who consume relatively high amounts of cured meats (ham, sausage, salami) are more likely to experience worsening symptoms, with the researchers finding higher worsening rates among high consumers (22%) than low consumers (14%). The study also found that body mass index accounted for only 14% of worsening symptoms, suggesting an effect independent of weight. It is observational, so cause-and-effect cannot be determined, and results may be influenced by participant recall and by smoking or COPD.

The passage discusses using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize research data as low-cost, scalable alternatives to collecting data from human subjects. The passage explains how the ambassador pattern can be used to route requests in sharded systems and to separate application logic from sharding and service-brokering logic. It then provides hands-on examples for deploying sharded Redis and request-splitting/experimentation using nginx, as well as an adapter pattern for normalizing monitoring and logging interfaces (e.g., Prometheus exporters and fluentd-based log normalization). It further discusses sharded caching: why sharding improves memory utilization and scalability, how cache hit rate affects capacity and performance, and design options like replicated, sharded caches and hot sharding. It describes how sharding functions map requests to shards (using deterministic and uniform hash properties, modulo reduction, and consistent hashing to reduce remapping during resizing). Finally, it introduces the multi-node scatter/gather pattern for parallel computation, the replicated, sharded variant for reliability and scale, and concludes with an overview of event-driven/function-as-a-service computing, including its benefits, challenges, limitations (background processing, memory needs, and cost model), and the decorator pattern applied to request/response transformation.

The passage describes the Simons Observatory’s pre-deployment laboratory characterization of 25 ultra-high-frequency (UHF) detector modules, involving testing of over 36,000 transition-edge sensor (TES) bolometers intended for installation in Chile. SO is sited in the Atacama Desert (5200 m elevation) and uses three small-aperture telescopes (SATs) and one large-aperture telescope (LAT). It observes across six frequency bands near 30, 40, 90, 150, 220, and 280 GHz using Low-Frequency, Mid-Frequency, and UHF TES detector arrays.  

The shared module design includes 430 feedhorn-coupled orthomode transducers connecting to four TES bolometers each, with TESs read out via microwave SQUID multiplexing (µmux) using resonators and rf-SQUIDs controlled with SMuRF electronics. Testing involved cryogenic measurements of TES I–V curves to determine key parameters including critical temperature (Tc), saturation power (Psat), optical efficiency (ηopt), effective time constants (τeff), and noise-equivalent power (NEP).  

Results report resonator yields and readout noise performance, TES operable yield (average 83%, minimum 71%), distributions of Tc and Psat with module-level accept/reject considerations, stable operation expectations based on observed instability behavior, and NEP and optical-efficiency outcomes. The best-performing 19 UHF modules meet performance requirements and are planned for deployment: thirteen have already been deployed across the LAT and UHF SAT, and six are expected to be installed in an upcoming LAT upgrade.

The lecture presents a cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity. The goal is to insert and delete edges and answer connectivity queries between vertex pairs, and the theorem claims each operation must take at least logarithmic time in the cell-probe model, even when connected components are paths and even for amortized and randomized settings (with the lecturer proving a worst-case logarithmic bound and discussing how amortized bounds follow similarly).

To prove the bound, the lecturer reduces dynamic connectivity to “bulk” operations using a specific graph construction where vertices form an \( \sqrt{n}\times \sqrt{n} \) grid with perfect matchings between columns, yielding paths. The matchings define permutations; updates replace an entire permutation via many edge insertions/deletions, and queries verify whether a composition (prefix composition) of permutations equals a target. The proof analyzes a “bad” access sequence based on a bit-reversal permutation order, and builds a balanced binary tree over time. Using interleaving properties of the bit-reversal sequence, the argument shows that updates in the left subtree must communicate information to queries in the right subtree, leading to many required cell reads.

The proof uses information-theoretic encoding arguments: first a warm-up lower bound for a prefix “sum/composition” problem is derived by bounding the number of cells read in the right subtree that were written in the left subtree. The main verify-sum lower bound is then proved using a simulation/decoding approach and a round-elimination style technique, supported by a separator family argument (based on succinct hash/perfect hashing ideas) to control encoding size. Summing/charging these subtree lower bounds yields the overall \( \Omega(\log n) \) per-operation cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity, which also applies to dynamic trees such as link/cut-related structures and supports additional update/query trade-off results.

Vernon Clausing appeals his convictions for possession with intent to deliver and delivery of legend drugs. He argues that jury instructions misstated the elements of the crimes and the State’s burden of proof, that the charging document was defective, that the trial court improperly admitted evidence from the executive director of the Board of Pharmacy, and that prosecutorial misconduct deprived him of a fair trial. The court finds none of these arguments persuasive and affirms.

The court discusses evidence that Clausing, after his medical license was revoked for unprofessional conduct involving Soma and Nubain, continued to fill and distribute those legend drugs through his clinic and home. A sting operation involving a former patient led to controlled purchases of Soma and Nubain and a later search revealing large quantities.

On appeal, the court holds that jury instructions accurately reflect Washington’s statutory scheme distinguishing “dispensing” from “delivery,” including requirements that legend drugs be dispensed by a licensed practitioner under the order or prescription of a licensed physician or within the scope of a practitioner’s license. It also holds the charging document sufficiently apprised Clausing of the unlawful-delivery theory and that there was no resulting prejudice. The court concludes that instructions regarding valid prescriptions and labeling did not relieve the State of its burden of proof and that a jury instruction defining “dispense” was not misleading. It further finds any error in admitting the Board of Pharmacy executive director’s testimony harmless and concludes there was no prosecutorial misconduct in closing argument.

In Sparkman v. Brown (decided December 12, 1930), the court states that when nothing is said about payment time in a sale of goods, it is understood as a cash sale, and possession without payment does not pass title as between vendor and vendee; trover lies to recover the goods or their value. The evidence showed the defendant bought the property on a cash sale and did not pay or tender any part of the purchase price before the suit or otherwise, requiring a verdict for the plaintiff. The court found no evidence of waiver of the cash condition, and because the defendant had the burden on that issue, the plaintiff’s finding was proper. The trial court properly directed a verdict for the plaintiff, and the judgment was affirmed, with the superior court not erring in dismissing the certiorari.

When PayPal CEO Dan Schulman found in 2019 that many employees were financially insecure, PayPal developed and launched an Employee Financial Wellness initiative to improve the financial health of hourly and entry-level workers. An assessment and employee wellness survey found that many employees ran out of money between paychecks and struggled with unexpected expenses. PayPal leadership responded with a four-point plan implemented in 2019–2020: wage increases where appropriate, a 60% reduction in U.S. health care premium costs plus a company-funded health reimbursement account, one-time equity grants (with additional grants later), and a financial wellness coaching program offering education and resources. The company also provided emergency relief and later added tools such as on-demand pay platforms. After the initiative, results reported for 2020–2021 included improved financial wellness survey responses, lower turnover in customer service centers, higher engagement, and increased participation in employee stock and retirement plans.

Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) of the thalamus is used to manage tremor in essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, and tremor-dominant Parkinson’s disease, but its mechanism is unclear and current tremor DBS systems are open-loop. Closed-loop DBS for tremor would require physiological internal neural biomarkers measured with the same stimulation lead. Microelectrode and macroelectrode recordings indicate theta-band activity from tremor-related cells distributed across thalamic nuclei, yet it is uncertain how low-frequency LFP activity relates to tremor magnitude across many patients and how DBS alters these signals. 

To address these gaps, the study recorded LFPs from the thalamus (including VIM and VOP) using a bipolar pair of a four-contact DBS lead in 34 surgical patients while simultaneously recording tremor with a hand-dorsum accelerometer. The findings reported include a moderate correlation between tremor and low-frequency LFP spectral power in the alpha and theta bands, and a strong correlation between tremor and peak coherence between LFPs and acceleration. Postural tremor decoding from LFP signals achieved an AUC of ~0.7, and high-frequency DBS (~130 Hz) reduced low-frequency spectral power compared to baseline; postural tremor was also decoded during DBS. A computational thalamus model was used to explain recorded LFP signals, showing that simulated low-frequency spectral power depends on factors such as electrode location, tremor cell spatial distribution, and the proportion of tremor vs. non-tremor cells.

The passage studies classical matching markets under ordinal preferences, focusing on three problems: house allocation (bipartite), marriage (bipartite), and roommates (non-bipartite). It compares stability notions such as Pareto and core stability, then introduces **popularity** as an intermediate concept based on plurality votes between matchings. A **popular matching** is at least as popular as any other matching, and to address cases where popular matchings may not exist, the paper defines **popular dimension** as the minimum size of a **popular winning set** of matchings. The main results concern the popular dimension in different variants (strict vs. tied preferences, unweighted vs. weighted agents) and are summarized as follows: **house allocation always has popular dimension exactly 2** (all cases), **marriage has dimension 1** for unweighted strict preferences, and **roommates has dimension 2** for unweighted strict preferences, while for weighted and/or tied cases in marriage and roommates the popular dimension lies between **2 and 3** (exact values left open for some variants). The paper provides polynomial-time algorithms to construct small popular winning sets (size 2 for house allocation and unweighted strict roommates; size 3 for general roommates with weights and ties) and discusses relationships to Condorcet dimension and related electoral concepts.

Industrial simulation and modeling rely on complex computing, but increasing complexity and limited hardware can lengthen calculations and force trade-offs between time and accuracy. Many respondents report outdated or inaccurate simulations, and developers often wait for computing capacity, delaying development. IDC expects rising demand for high-performance computing (HPC), with many enterprises viewing it as a game changer for product and process innovation due to faster, more complex simulations and greater iteration capacity. Enterprises use different HPC deployment approaches, with many preferring external infrastructures, colocation, or partnerships, while security, investment and operating costs, energy use, and technical availability are key challenges. The passage also describes cloud-based HPC and HPC-as-a-Service (HPCaaS) as options to improve scalability, flexibility, security/resilience, and enable HPC-related business models, supported by IDC’s recommendations on data strategy, operating model choice, scalability and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The passage describes how climate change and natural disasters force about 21 million global displacements annually since 2008, creating internally displaced persons (IDPs) who are uprooted due to conflicts or climate crises. It argues that lower- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face limited resources and reduced access to social services, increasing vulnerability to climate impacts and worsening socio-economic challenges, including disruptions to education.

The study aims to examine how climate change affects internally displaced K-12 learners in LMICs before and after relocation, focusing on educational disruptions, adaptations, and gender inequities. The paper uses a conceptual framework combining human rights-based education and Education in Emergencies research, and a literature review method that includes both academic and grey literature, narrowed from over 100 documents to 73 English-language sources.

Findings indicate that climate change restricts educational access and undermines quality through physical destruction of schools, damaged transport, economic hardship, and health and psychological effects, with attendance and learning outcomes varying by disaster type and conditions. Displaced learners also face additional barriers in new destinations, including financial constraints, administrative and registration hurdles, discrimination, and challenges with distance learning and alternative education. The passage also highlights that girls experience heightened barriers due to gender inequalities, including increased household responsibilities and risks of dropout or early marriage.

In the discussion and conclusion, the passage emphasizes the need for scalable financial support, streamlined administrative processes, mental health and academic assistance, and gender-sensitive policies, and identifies gaps in research and policy, including limited focus on climate-induced displacement within emergency education frameworks and insufficient attention to long-term educational outcomes.

President Muhammadu Buhari said Nigerians are reporting improved power supply and reduced reliance on generators, citing Nigeria’s power generation of 5,222.3 megawatts delivered to customers as of December 2017 and a generation capacity exceeding 7,500 MW. However, his hometown Daura in Katsina State was undergoing a 10-day blackout caused by the collapse of a newly erected 132 kVA power tower felled by a wind storm. Workers had been deployed to fix the situation, with 16 KEDCO power poles also felled, and power was expected to be restored within 48 hours. The passage also notes similar long-term electricity disruptions in parts of Lagos and Ondo states.

The passage is a set of news briefings and excerpts dated April 27, 2001 about the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) and Enron’s power project dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). Multiple articles report that DPC’s board authorized Enron India’s managing director Neil McGregor (and/or DPC President Wade Cline) to issue a preliminary termination notice and potentially terminate the power purchase agreement, while also noting that lenders and formal procedures may affect whether termination proceeds. It also describes “protest” payments by MSEB toward disputed bills, the role of international versus domestic lenders, and calls by Indian officials and governments for renegotiation and conciliation rather than termination. Several pieces discuss the potential financial and procedural implications for the Centre and the dispute’s background, including payment delays, penalties, arbitration/conciliation steps, and tariff disagreements.

The widow of John Mock petitioned to have her share of certain real estate set apart. The heirs argued the estate’s debts were large and that the widow’s interest could not be set off until debts were paid. The trial court struck portions of the heirs’ answer and ordered the widow’s interest set apart; the heirs appealed. The court held that the widow’s interest is not subject to the estate’s debts, and that her statutory interest attached upon the concurrence of the husband’s seizin and the wife’s coverture, becoming effective at the husband’s death. It construed Code sections governing sale for debts as referring to the estate’s remaining interest not yet vested in the widow, and interpreted the creditor-related provisions as limiting only the widow receiving more than the statutory one-third and not making her interest subordinate to creditors’ claims. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage introduces two all-optical nanoscale thermometry methods using fluorescent diamonds with silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers as temperature sensors. Because secondary optical thermometers require calibration against reference temperatures—often under off-situ and in-situ conditions—the authors propose machine-learning multi-feature regression approaches to reduce calibration burden. The methods predict the temperature of unseen diamonds from temperature-dependent changes in SiV photoluminescence and diamond Raman spectroscopy, using either (i) standard multi-feature regression (MFR) as a weighted linear combination of multiple temperature-dependent features or (ii) a two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) combining partial least squares (PLS), lasso regression, and a spline-based residual calibration. Experiments used ~1 µm SiV-containing diamonds (eight samples) measured between 25 °C and 85 °C in 10 °C increments, tracking up to nine physical quantities (SiV ZPL/PSB properties and diamond Raman peak properties). Performance was evaluated on generalized accuracy, resolution, and sensitivity using a train-test strategy with independent test data and automated feature selection for MFR. Results report that with only 3–4 calibration diamonds and temperature set points, MFR achieves accuracy of 1.7 K and resolution of 1.2 K·Hz−1/2 (~26% better accuracy than best single-feature models). With larger calibration sets, 2SMFR improves to 0.7 K accuracy and 0.6 K·Hz−1/2 resolution when trained with seven diamonds and seven temperature set points, with higher sensitivity than single-feature benchmarks. The authors conclude that multi-feature regression provides a flexible, data-efficient, instrument-agnostic framework for optical thermometry when at least two temperature-dependent observables are available.

After the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, major energy and oil companies heightened security and largely shut down or reduced operations, including evacuating offices and closing trading floors. Utility control centers were activated and nuclear plants implemented heightened security plans, with some facilities and management offices largely vacated, while companies said essential deliveries or operations continued. In parallel, energy markets were disrupted: trading at the New York Mercantile Exchange was suspended, many energy-trading activities halted, and gasoline and oil prices rose amid fears of supply disruptions and volatility. The passage also notes Enron resuming North American gas and power trading via its online platform and telephone for part of the day, and companies adjusting refinery and facility access controls.

The passage describes the quarterback as the most important position in sports and a football team’s face and leader, noting that quarterbacks are both praised and scrutinized. It explains that the quarterback works closely with the center, touches the football every play, calls or carries out plays (including audibles), communicates with teammates, ensures proper formation, studies playbooks and opponent film, and takes a central role in scoring and winning. The text covers the quarterback’s main responsibilities (taking the snap, throwing, sometimes running, changing plays and identifying coverages at high levels) and the name “quarterback” and its nicknames such as “signal caller,” “field general,” “gunslinger,” and abbreviation “QB.” It discusses how quarterback body types have shifted toward smaller, athletic players, outlines traits of great quarterbacks (football IQ, decision making, accuracy, leadership, footwork, athleticism, and arm strength), and lists several notable quarterbacks with brief career overviews (Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, Tom Brady). It concludes by reiterating the quarterback’s importance because he touches the ball every play and drives much of the offense.

Police say a self-driving Uber vehicle struck and killed pedestrian Elaine Herzberg, 49, while she was walking outside a crosswalk in Tempe, near Phoenix, on Sunday night. The incident was described as the first fatality involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. Uber suspended all road-testing of self-driving cars in the U.S. and Canada, including in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco, and Toronto. Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi expressed condolences and said the company is working with local law enforcement. The passage also notes voluntary federal guidelines for testing autonomous vehicles, state-level regulation, public fears about autonomous vehicles, and that some states require incident reporting, with California’s motor vehicle department receiving 59 reports as of early March.

HDFC Mutual Fund decided to wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 (1), a scheme under HDFC Fixed Maturity Plans-Series 29, after unit holders’ approval. The notice said a resolution would authorize the trustee or an authorized person to take steps for winding up. The scheme, launched in March 2014, had its maturity date extended twice with unit holders’ consent, and after the second rollover on May 17, 2017 (1,105 days) to May 25, 2020, the scheme’s net assets fell below Rs 10 crore, making it unviable. Its corpus is currently invested in cash and cash equivalents, and it will be wound up under SEBI (Mutual Fund) Regulations 1996, section 39(2)(a).

The case concerns a transfer tax on a trust fund in the Estate of Josephine Slosson. Josephine, the decedent and New York resident, exercised a power of appointment given by her father Peter Naylor’s will, bequeathing $5,000 to her husband, $500 to Margaret Gillesse, directing payment of her debts from the trust fund, and directing the balance to her surviving issue per stirpes. Her husband predeceased her, and her three children elected to take their shares under Peter Naylor’s will. The court held that Josephine’s valid exercise of the power prevented the trust principal from passing to those entitled under intestate laws and that the beneficiaries’ interests were subject to a transfer tax. It further held the children could not take under Peter Naylor’s will because the contingency for taking there did not occur, since Josephine made a valid disposition by her will. The court also held that the amount paid to creditors as Josephine’s debts was taxable, but modified the tax by deducting $682.04 from the taxable bequest to Alice Slosson because the decedent was not indebted to her at death. The order fixing the tax was modified in part and affirmed in other respects.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said there is no trade or commerce between Thailand and North Korea, adding that he had prohibited North Korean boats in Thai waters and that Thailand complies with U.N. resolutions. The U.S. special representative Joseph Yun is due in Bangkok to discuss stepping up pressure on North Korea amid ongoing weapons tests. In August, U.S. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson urged Thailand to take more action, and Thailand’s foreign ministry later said trade with North Korea had fallen by up to 94 percent. The passage also notes that North Korea tested a powerful intercontinental ballistic missile and that the U.N. Security Council is set to hold a ministerial meeting on North Korea’s nuclear and missile programs.

Carol Christ, 73, became the new chancellor of UC Berkeley, saying she is not looking for another job as the university faces sexual assault scandal fallout, budget problems, housing and homelessness concerns, and a free speech debate. She will be the oldest chancellor in Berkeley’s history and has previously led Berkeley roles including vice chancellor and provost, and later served as president of Smith College. Faculty interviewed expressed optimism about her tenure. Christ said she will prioritize concerns including low representation of Black students, and campus sexual assault, and plans to address those issues through conversations across groups. She also intends to make the 2017-18 school year a “free speech year” with a point-counterpoint debate series, and to partner with Berkeley and Oakland to address a student housing shortage while addressing homelessness and safety first. She faces a $110 million budget deficit that UC must cut in half, and she outlined plans to increase private philanthropy and make administrative cuts. Christ also discussed rebuilding community, spending time walking around campus and attending student events, and noted personal interests such as music lessons and family time.

The passage explains what a soccer penalty kick is and when it is awarded, including that the ball is placed on the penalty mark 12 yards from the goal and is taken as a one-versus-one shot against the goalkeeper. It outlines Law 14 requirements before the kick (stationary ball, goalkeeper position and restrictions, other players’ distances and positions, and referee signaling), plus rules after the kick such as rebound handling and retakes if offenses occur. It provides coaching guidance on selecting and preparing kickers, developing technique and a repeatable routine, practicing and experimenting with different kick types and target locations, managing mental aspects and distractions, and following correct procedure (whistle, feints allowed only during the run-up, run-up mechanics). It also discusses follow-up actions, practice progression, team involvement, higher-level tactics like scouting/keeping book and having at least two kicks, and scenarios such as changing kickers, a rare “tap” penalty kick, and simulating game conditions. The passage concludes with an overall mindset for kickers and responsibilities of coaches and teammates, including appropriate response if a penalty kick must be retaken.

The passage explains options expiration in trading, stating that an options contract becomes void at the expiration time and can no longer be used. In the US, the expiration date is the third Saturday of the expiration month, with the last trading day typically the preceding Friday (or Thursday if Friday is a public holiday); the expiration time is 11:59 a.m. EST. It describes “options expiration week” and notes the “Options Expiration Week Effect (OPEX)” where large-cap stocks with actively traded options tend to show higher average weekly returns, with “quadruple witching” occurring four times per year. The article references exploring expiry-related trading strategies, discussing backtests on SPY (S&P 500) and XLV (healthcare ETF), including an overnight strategy and a short day trading strategy, and also reports that volatility is higher on expiry days than on random days (especially quad days). It concludes with general guidance on developing and backtesting options strategies, including researching models, backtesting for at least 15 years across market cycles, and forward-testing selected models.

The UC1825B-SP PWM control device is optimized for high-frequency switched mode power supply applications, with minimized propagation delays and increased bandwidth and slew rate of the error amplifier. It supports current-mode or voltage-mode systems and includes input voltage feed-forward capability. Protection features include a current limit comparator with a 1-V threshold, a TTL-compatible shutdown port, and a soft start pin that also serves as a maximum duty-cycle clamp. The logic is fully latched for jitter-free operation and to prevent multiple output pulses, and an undervoltage lockout with 800 mV hysteresis ensures low start-up current. It has totem pole outputs for sourcing and sinking high peak currents from capacitive loads, such as a power MOSFET gate.

Chenai Mathabire, a Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing how to implement a faster tuberculosis (TB) test at health centers in southeast Africa to save HIV-positive patients. After joining Doctors Without Borders in 2008, she worked in Zimbabwe and South Sudan and later conducted research starting in 2015 in Malawi and Mozambique. Her study evaluated how easily clinics could administer a rapid TB test and found it could produce results in less than an hour, could be taught to staff within a few hours, and was easy to interpret. She described cases where delayed or unapproved testing contributed to patient deaths, and said her data supported quicker same-day treatment. The research led some health centers working with Doctors Without Borders to embrace rapid TB testing, with potential for broader adoption in health systems. Mathabire continues working with Doctors Without Borders and considers further research on HIV and TB.

The speaker says the team’s game has been intense, noting they held on through a period with a big goal at the end and that it was their best game to date. They emphasize staying positive, improving performance across periods, keeping shots down, and responding to their opponent despite the opponent having three power plays. The speaker discusses getting into the playoffs, crediting a playoff opportunity and leadership figures who brought them to Detroit, and describes the success as a team effort involving multiple Russian players in critical situations. They also say they did not predict winning four straight but believed they would outplay any opponent and were ultimately the best team as the playoffs progressed.

The passage is a speech accepting a Democratic nomination and expressing gratitude for support and the party platform. The speaker pledges to lead the party back to victory and the nation back to greatness, emphasizing civil and economic rights, the separation of church and state, and that religious affiliation should not determine voting. He contrasts Democrats’ goals with perceived Republican weaknesses, argues the upcoming election will be difficult, and frames the need for change through addressing problems faced by farmers, workers, and older people. He describes major global and domestic challenges, including shifting power abroad, Communist influence, technological and social changes at home, and moral and regulatory decline, and calls for new leadership for the 1960s “New Frontier,” stressing courage and vigorous leadership. He concludes with a call for public support and asks for divine guidance to meet the nation’s test.

The passage reports a study published in The American Journal of Psychiatry that examined exercise and depression in over 33,000 adults. People who reported not exercising at all were reportedly 44% more likely to have depression than those who exercised one to two hours per week. The study also found that 12% of depression cases could have been prevented with small amounts of exercise. The study followed 33,908 Norwegian adults over 11 years while tracking exercise, depression and anxiety symptoms, and factors including socio-economic background, substance use, body mass index, social support, and physical illness. Professor Samuel Harvey is quoted saying even small amounts of exercise (about one hour per week) can significantly protect against depression and could be integrated into mental health plans and public health campaigns.

The passage describes a weekend trip by Republic of Ireland national team and Florida State University soccer player Megan Connolly to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, where she experienced a scary amusement-ride drop. A Twitter video she posted is noted for her FSU teammate Dallas Dorosy laughing during Connolly’s reaction and for the Fray song “How To Save A Life” playing before takeoff. After the clip went viral, Connolly received supportive messages from friends, including fellow Irish footballer Sophie Perry suggesting she may need throat lozenges.

Google Project Fi, a U.S. phone service that uses major carriers and Wi‑Fi, has added three new compatible phones: the $199 moto G6 (now available for preorder), the $740 LG G7 ThinQ, and the $899 LG V35 ThinQ. Project Fi began in April 2015 and has a limited compatible phone lineup, currently including Google Pixel 2 models, the Android One moto x4, and older Google-supported Nexus and Pixel devices. The passage says Fi lacks iPhones and is unlikely to attract many new customers due to limited handset choice, charging $20 per month for unlimited calls and texts plus $10 per gigabyte of data up to 6GB, with unused data not charged. It notes Fi operates as an MVNO using T-Mobile, Sprint, and U.S. Cellular (and a European provider overseas) and that Google has not provided customer numbers, though it claims a “healthy user base” and “high customer satisfaction.”

The provincial Liberal Party leader criticized NDP Premier John Horgan for rising gas prices, saying Horgan should reduce costs for drivers and lower the gas tax. Horgan responded that the nine-cent increase overnight is not a tax issue, but instead relates to supply and company profits, and he said he has raised the issue with the federal government and within government.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a trial court judgment denying Vernon Leroy Wilson and others recovery for damages from a head-on collision on a three-lane highway on May 28, 1955. Two related suits were consolidated for trial. The jury found that King’s car did not operate in the center lane and did not fail to turn right or maintain proper control, and that the collision occurred in the western lane. The jury also found Wilson was negligent by driving into the most western lane and that Wilson’s negligence was the sole proximate cause of the collision, while his failure to keep a proper lookout was not a proximate cause. The court overruled a motion for mistrial and denied a motion for new trial based on claims of improper argument, jury conduct, and issues submitted or not submitted. On appeal, the court held appellants waived complaints about the charge by not objecting or requesting special issues in time under the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, and it found that complaints about counsel’s argument were not preserved because no timely objections were made. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage is an Apple Inc. Form 8-K current report dated October 27, 2022. It states that on October 27, 2022 Apple issued a press release about its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022, and the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. It also lists the securities registered (Common Stock AAPL and various notes due 2022 through 2042), includes notes about the status of the report’s information regarding filings under the Securities Act and Exchange Act, and is signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speaker says coach Bylsma’s philosophy brought new confidence and helped the team turn things around, noting a five-game road trip where they won the first three games and made trades afterward for Billy and Adams. They express hope for a championship ring and say leadership is shown through playing within the team’s system and contributing defensively, citing Sid’s recent on-ice approach. They also describe Jordan as an offensively talented but responsible two-way forward, and they praise the team’s ability to perform even when early play is uncertain. The speaker concludes that the team’s continued success after losing key players from last year’s Cup run is remarkable and that they run their organization dominantly.

The passage is a collection of May 23, 2001 news summaries and excerpts about the Enron-Dabhol Power Company (DPC) renegotiation and related disputes in Maharashtra, India. It reports that Madhav Godbole resigned as chairman of the Godbole committee after Nationalist Congress Party leader Sharad Pawar made remarks suggesting a “negative approach,” and that Maharashtra chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh refused to accept the resignation. It also describes cancellations of a renegotiation meeting, Enron’s statements about seeking damages and attending committee meetings, and the possibility of Maharashtra issuing termination notices to DPC. Other items cover impacts on Indian lenders and potential non-payment risks, positions by Indian power companies that they would not buy Enron’s stake due to high tariffs, and a state advocate general’s view that MSEB’s rebate claim against DPC is justified. The passage further includes commentary on governance failures in the project and the central government adopting a “wait and watch” approach pending conciliation outcomes.

North Tyneside Mayor Norma Redfearn said the councils south of the River Tyne should be able to join the North of Tyne devolution deal, after the North Tyneside council cabinet voted unanimously to move ahead. She said the deal, announced in November 2017, will bring £600m over 30 years and is expected to create 10,000 jobs. Councillor Ray Glindon asked whether the four south-of-the-river councils could join, and Redfearn said it was too late at this stage but they could request to join later. Redfearn also criticized other authorities for not being democratic, referencing Durham’s 2016 referendum on the previous deal. Plans include setting up the new combined authority in summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle City Council leader Nick Forbes rejected claims the authority would be under-powered, saying the deal is worth more per head and includes health, disability support, and housing elements. A crunch vote to split the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed from Tuesday to mid-April, and Northumberland County Council was also set to discuss devolution.

The passage describes DLSS and Blackwell-related technologies in NVIDIA GPUs. It states that inference on small language models can reduce power by up to 50% using reduced active periods, power/voltage gating for transitional states, and faster entry into the deepest sleep state. It also explains DLSS as neural rendering technology that boosts FPS, reduces latency, and improves image quality, with DLSS 4 adding Multi Frame Generation (MFG) and transformer-based improvements for Super Resolution (SR), Ray Reconstruction (RR), and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA). The passage claims DLSS 4 MFG can generate up to three additional frames per rendered frame, improves speed and VRAM use, and uses enhanced frame pacing with hardware Flip Metering. Transformer model sections describe changes from CNNs, emphasizing self-attention, better handling of longer-range patterns, and improved temporal stability, reduced ghosting, and higher detail. It further outlines neural shader concepts and examples including RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The passage concludes with hardware descriptions for the Blackwell architecture (including GB202 and GB203), and lists specs for several GeForce RTX 50 series GPUs (RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070), followed by legal and trademark notices.

Plymouth Studio School is expected to close at the end of the summer term 2018, three years after it opened, because it is only half full and not financially viable. The Tory MP Johnny Mercer said the school operated at about 50% capacity and that its performance had not improved enough. Closure requires Government approval and was announced ahead of an Ofsted report expected to be critical; the school has faced challenges and was rated “inadequate” by Ofsted. Mercer said his focus is on supporting students who need new places to study from September 2018, stressing there should be no interruption in pupils’ education. The passage also includes a timeline of the school’s funding, opening, leadership changes, and the announcement in April 2018 that it would close.

Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes said he has no regrets about supporting California’s cap-and-trade climate program, though he wished he had attended the signing ceremony on San Francisco’s Treasure Island. He said his absence was due to a scheduling conflict. The vote has sparked disputes within the struggling California Republican Party: conservatives criticized Mayes for betraying party principles, helping Democrats, and taking photo opportunities with Gov. Jerry Brown and other top Democratic lawmakers after the vote. The controversy has led top state GOP officials to openly campaign to remove Mayes from his leadership post, with county and donor groups calling on him to step down and the state party board expected to vote. Mayes can only be removed by his 25-member caucus, where he faces an internal challenge from Assemblyman Jay Obernolte. The turmoil also complicates state party fundraising negotiations, and other Republicans who voted for the legislation have faced criticism and protests. The passage notes that the internal conflict could push Republicans back into partisan positions over climate change and describes additional fallout, including Assemblywoman Melissa Melendez being reassigned to a smaller office after protesting Mayes’ handling of cap-and-trade.
