The email from David I. Levine announces mandatory and optional readings for the following week (beginning November 17) for courses e201b-1 and e201b-2. Mandatory work includes reading Mankiw, Chapter 10, completing Homework #4 (covering shifts in IS and LM from monetary and fiscal policy, bringing a recent newspaper example of an IS/LM shift, and questions about recommended IS/LM shifts during the Southeast Asia aggregate demand decline and what the IMF recommended, plus Mankiw page 292 problems 1 and 2). It also notes that the class will discuss IS/LM shifts across Europe, the US, Japan, and Indonesia during the 1997–98 crisis. Optional readings provided by classmates include a New York Times article on France’s 35-hour workweek, a New York Times article on a Latin American stock market rally, and an article analyzing Japan’s economic problems and responses.

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN). The Norwegian Nobel Committee said ICAN was recognized for highlighting the humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapon use and working toward a treaty-based prohibition. The committee cited ongoing tensions over North Korea and uncertainty about the Iran nuclear deal. ICAN, a coalition of non-governmental organizations in 100 countries, said it helped drive the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted July 7 with support from 122 nations. The treaty bans activities including development, testing, production, acquiring, possessing, and stockpiling nuclear weapons, and the UN Security Council’s five permanent nuclear-armed members did not participate in the negotiations. ICAN said some governments’ belief in nuclear weapons as a security source is dangerous because it encourages proliferation and undermines disarmament.

Pragyan expanded beyond four days with technology and social responsibility outreach events throughout the year, and Pragyan ’18 ran from March 1, 2018 with an inauguration at Barn Hall featuring Dr. B N Suresh. The fest included guest lectures, workshops (including deep learning and armoured fighting vehicle workshops), human library sessions, and multiple infotainment shows by various performers such as The Parchai Group, Shawn Chua, Shivraj, Suhani Shah, and Azeem Banatwalla. It also featured exhibits including Hyperloop India, InMoov, KalamSat, ISRO liquid propulsion exhibits, and Ugears, concluding with valediction followed by further infotainment and stand-up comedy.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow, and Fred Ramsdell for discovering regulatory T cells (T-regs), immune cells that calm the immune system after infection or wound healing and prevent it from attacking the body. Failure of T-regs can lead to autoimmune disorders or damaging inflammation, and they are also important for preventing rejection of the fetus during pregnancy. The researchers identified mutations linked to fatal autoimmune disease in male mouse pups, and subsequent findings showed that without such mechanisms there are not enough T-regs to stop harmful immune activity. The Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute announced the prize on October 6, and scientists are working to harness T-regs for conditions where the immune system is overactive or targets the wrong thing.

The passage discusses design considerations for a GaN-based push-pull converter, including dead time (set to ~25 ns), leading edge blank time (initially ~50 ns with RLEB = 49.9 kΩ), soft-start timing (33 nF giving ~7.5 ms), and transformer design (turns ratio 2.5, primary inductance 40 μH used in the final design). It also covers selection and sizing of main switching GaN FETs (conservatively 170 V rating) and synchronous rectifier GaN FETs (80-V rating), options to use a Schottky diode to reduce soft-start current and reverse conduction losses, and use of an RCD clamp circuit to limit switch node voltage. Further sections specify an output inductor value of 0.47 μH (targeting 40% ripple), output capacitance requirements (1.3 mF minimum from calculations; ~2.3 mF used to mitigate single-event transients), and design of a current sense resistor (RCS = 7.5 Ω), hiccup capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF), frequency compensation components (RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF), and a slope compensation resistor (102 kΩ). It concludes with power supply recommendations and layout guidelines for improving noise and reliability, including routing and grounding practices.

The defendant moves to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing his second marriage is void because it was performed by a Justice of the Peace while he was 19 years old. The Grand Jury minutes show the defendant’s first marriage, to Aud Irene Kvamli Heine, was never legally dissolved and was still valid when he married Marie Licciardi on September 4, 1955, by a Justice of the Peace. The court outlines relevant portions of section 11 of the Domestic Relations Law, including subdivision 5, which provides that such a marriage may be solemnized only by specified authorized persons and renders marriage invalid when performed by a Justice of the Peace if either party is under 21. The decision notes differing case law: Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino held noncompliance with subdivision 5 made the marriage void, while Andrews v. Andrews and Graves v. Graves held the prohibition did not affect validity. The court states it is inclined to follow Caplan and De Martino and therefore grants the motion to dismiss the indictment, ordering submission of the order.

The passage discusses “Santa Claus Rally”/end-of-year effects in stock markets and describes backtests and trading rules using holiday timing around Christmas. It states that markets show significantly better performance during Christmas and the days leading up to the new year, and presents backtest results (including metrics like win ratio, profit factor, and max drawdown) for the S&P 500, German stocks via ETF EWG, Euro Stoxx 50 via ETF FEZ, Emerging Markets via Fidelity’s FEMKX, and the NIFTY 50 cash index proxy. It notes that Christmas Day is a federal US holiday and may not be a trading day, while the day before and after can be trading days depending on whether Christmas falls on a weekend; bond markets close early on the trading day preceding Christmas Day. The passage concludes that Santa Claus rallies appear in multiple regions, though it cautions that results may differ and are not guaranteed to continue.

The University of Maine cancelled its annual American Floating Offshore Wind Technical Summit (AFLOAT), which it has hosted since 2020, citing changing federal policies and priorities. This decision comes as federal support for renewable energy wanes, including the suspension of a $12.5 million grant to the university’s floating offshore wind program. The university launched an experimental floating wind turbine a month after the grant suspension and has no plans to revive AFLOAT, though it plans private meetings with relevant parties.

Darfon America Corp. is showcasing upgraded energy storage products at Intersolar North America 2018, including the H200 and H300 hybrid energy storage systems and the H5001 hybrid inverter. The H200 integrates lithium batteries and the H5000 hybrid inverter in a 19" enclosure, offers Panasonic LNMC and Dragonfly LFP battery options, relocates wiring terminals to the back for easier installation, and features a redesigned distribution panel with micro breakers for increased battery bay space up to 30kWh. The H300 is a wall-mounted solution combining the H5001 hybrid inverter with a 5kWh LNMC battery, and it is now available in a 10kWh configuration with two battery packs and a master box. The H5001 has physical changes including a lockable distribution box and lockable external PV disconnect, laser-cut conduit knockouts, and an easier-to-remove access cover for programming AP registers. All three models have upgraded inverter fans for more precise temperature control and improved in-rush overload handling for 120V circuits, with an optional generator start-up kit available. The products are available through authorized distributors.

The passage discusses Drew Doughty and other players reflecting on a series they had to handle adversity in, saying they are not discouraged and that their opponents are executing better within their system. They note the need to make adjustments, crash the nets, and create and convert chances, while mentioning the effects of distractions before a game and emphasizing being prepared. They describe learning from not playing to potential due to nerves and other worries. They also comment on motivating factors like the Stanley Cup being in the building, the aggressive style of an opposing goalie, and their communication and relationship with Rob.

The Federal Reserve raised U.S. short-term interest rates by a quarter point, its third hike since December, raising its forecast for U.S. economic growth and unemployment. The key interest rate will hover between 1% and 1.25%, and mortgage rates are not expected to rise immediately. The Fed also plans to gradually sell assets it bought during and after the financial crisis, starting later this year with $10 billion a month of mortgage-backed securities and Treasuries, depending on the economy. The decision follows signs of economic strength, including unemployment falling to 4.3% in May and continued job growth. Fed officials lowered their inflation projection to 1.6% for this year from 1.9% in March, and most officials expect at least one more rate hike this year.

The speaker says they are excited to play in a hostile environment on the ice rather than in the stands, and they treat the game like any other to keep focus. They say being out on the ice helps them avoid overthinking and overanalyzing, and they feel comfortable and confident. They note that Edmonton will be ready and point to past games where teams performed well at home. They emphasize matching the other team’s effort, keeping focus even in their hometown, and contributing to their hockey team while having fun with teammates.

The passage describes features of the ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem, including its Cortex-A8 processor, debug support, Harvard architecture, caches and interconnect, and a real-time trace interface using an Embedded Trace Module (ETM) and 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer (ETB). It also explains an embedded interrupt controller (AINTC) that prioritizes system peripheral requests and generates IRQ or FIQ, and notes that FIQ generation to the ARM is not supported for general-purpose devices. The text further outlines the C674x DSP subsystem features, including CPU structure, functional units, instruction capabilities, and enhancements, and it describes a system MMU that remaps C674x accesses and optionally routes EDMA traffic through it. Beyond processing subsystems, the passage includes details about the device’s memory maps, TILER extended addressing, and extensive terminal/pin functions for various interfaces such as boot configuration pins, camera interface, mailbox, GPIOs, Ethernet (EMAC), DDR controllers, timers, UARTs, USB, video input/output, SPI/I2C, and supply voltage requirements.

The passage is largely extracted from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2019. It includes condensed financial statements and notes describing cash flows, results of operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheet amounts, along with accounting policies and disclosures. Key items covered include lease and financing obligations, digital video and music content accounting, unearned revenue, fair value measurement of financial instruments, debt outstanding and credit facilities, stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation, income tax contingencies and examinations, segment information (North America, International, and AWS), and principal contractual commitments and contingencies. It also contains management’s discussion of operating results, liquidity and capital resources, and forward-looking statements.

Volkswagen AG’s U.S. unit asked a U.S. judge to delay several excess-emissions court trials, saying “inflammatory” comments by a lawyer for car owners in a recent Netflix documentary could prejudice the jury. A motion to delay the first consumer fraud trial, involving a North Carolina man, cites an interview by Michael Melkersen describing Volkswagen diesel-fume testing on monkeys and referencing Hitler and the Holocaust; Volkswagen argues pretrial publicity could affect verdicts. The filing says the Holocaust is not relevant to the fraud trial. Volkswagen said it is spending more than $25 billion in the U.S., including buyback or fix offers for nearly 500,000 polluting 2.0-liter diesel vehicles, and that monkey tests were approved by an independent review board. Daimler and BMW said they suspended or moved staff linked to the testing.

James Madison returns the bill titled “An act to set apart and pledge certain funds for internal improvements,” stating he cannot reconcile it with the Constitution. He argues that the legislative power Congress may exercise is limited to enumerated powers in Article I, Section 8, and that the bill’s proposed power to construct roads and canals and improve navigation is not among them or properly derived from the necessary and proper clause. He contends that the commerce power does not include constructing such infrastructure, that interpreting the “common defense and general welfare” clause as a general legislative grant would undermine the Constitution’s enumerated powers and affect state laws and judicial boundaries. He further says states’ consent cannot confer powers not specified in the Constitution. Madison acknowledges the importance of roads, canals, and navigation but concludes Congress lacks the authority to do so under the Constitution as proposed, so he withholds his signature.

Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said NATO’s annual report for 2017 shows alliance trends heading up as NATO recrafts deterrence and defense, including increased forward presence in the Black Sea, resilience against hybrid war, and strengthened cyber defenses. He cited 2017 deployment of four multinational battle groups to the Baltic republics and Poland, increased NATO contributions to Afghanistan’s Resolute Support mission, and over 23,000 troops in NATO deployments at end of 2017. Stoltenberg also discussed burden-sharing increases, with three consecutive years of higher defense spending in Europe and Canada totaling $46 billion since 2014, and $18 billion spent on major equipment. Russia was described as a central focus, including the Salisbury poisoning of Sergei Skripal and his daughter, which Stoltenberg said traced to Russia and violated international norms; he also referenced Russian actions in Georgia, Crimea, and Eastern Ukraine, and Russia’s military modernization and nuclear doctrine. He stated NATO does not want a new Cold War or arms race but will defend allies with conventional forces and a nuclear deterrent. The passage also says NATO stepped up efforts in Afghanistan by expanding training support and increased involvement against ISIS through training Iraqi forces and launching a new training mission in Iraq.

The passage argues that scalping trading is a waste of time because most scalpers lose money. It describes scalping as a high-frequency style that targets small price changes over seconds to a few minutes, often using a 1-minute timeframe. The passage states that scalpers face competition from well-equipped traders and institutions, scarcity of truly profitable opportunities, and difficulties with backtesting due to noise and randomness in short-term data. It highlights transaction costs, including commissions and especially slippage, as major obstacles that can quickly erode profits. The passage also notes that scalping typically requires automation, which can introduce errors and requires safeguards, and that the short time horizon increases stress. A real-world example is provided where a person investing heavily in short-term scalping infrastructure lost money after being outcompeted by a faster scalper. The passage concludes that better opportunities may exist in longer time frames and suggests finding edges on those horizons instead.

The passage argues that Becton, Dickinson and Company (BDX) has strong dividend credibility, paying dividends since 1962 and increasing them more than 10% in all years since 2004 except 2012 (raised 9.8%); it cites 12 of the past 13 years of double-digit dividend growth and an average 16.3% dividend growth since 2004. It states Becton typically announces dividend increases in November and estimates dividends around $2.98 in 2017 and $2.92 in 2017 with a projected dividend payout ratio falling to 37% of profits. It describes Becton’s medical technology products, including producing more than 2 billion insulin syringes per year, and summarizes 2017 GAAP earnings guidance (diluted EPS $7.90 to $8.00) and prior EPS growth driven partly by litigation reserve reversal. The passage also claims CareFusion-related merger costs affected profitability in 2015–2016 but that 2017 is expected to return to higher profits and improve net profit margins. Risks mentioned include manufacturing issues, higher interest rates, and competition from more advanced products.

The passage describes DFT-based investigation of three predicted o-MAX phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), focusing on their structural, dynamical, electronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and optical properties. MAX phases are introduced as materials combining metal-like conductivity and ceramic-like durability, and o-MAX phases are characterized by ordered subgroups with specific atomic layer arrangements. The study uses the CASTEP code with GGA-PBEsol (and GGA-PBE) for calculations, including structure relaxation, elastic constants via stress–strain, phonon dispersion/DFPT for dynamical stability, and electronic DOS/band structures to assess metallic behavior. Results report negative formation energies and no negative phonon frequencies, supporting chemical and dynamic stability. Electronic structure analyses indicate metallic character with orbital contributions mainly from Mo-4d states and mixed bonding (ionic/covalent/metallic). Mechanical analysis shows non-negative elastic constants meeting stability criteria, anisotropy in elastic moduli, and brittleness based on υ, G/B, and Cauchy pressure; Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ is identified as having the highest Young’s modulus and Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ as having the lowest Young’s modulus for thermal barrier coating suitability. Thermal properties include Debye temperature, minimum thermal conductivity, lattice thermal conductivity, melting temperature, thermal expansion coefficient, and heat capacities, with low kmin and small thermal conductivity supporting TBC potential. Optical calculations provide dielectric function and reflectivity, showing metallic optical behavior and reflectivity values exceeding 44% across IR/visible/mid-UV, suggesting potential for solar heat-shielding layers. The conclusions state overall stability (dynamic/chemical/mechanical/thermodynamic), metallic and mixed bonding nature, expected brittleness, and promising high-temperature application potential, particularly as thermal barrier coatings.

The passage lists topics and resources related to trading, including risk-adjusted return types and measurement methods, trading psychology traits and bias, money management, position sizing, trading orders, indicators, and numerous strategy types such as backtested trading strategies, seasonality, turnaround and OPEX effects, candlestick patterns, moving average strategies, swing and breakout strategies, and forex strategies. It also describes backtesting concepts like survivorship bias, curve fitting, and provides examples such as Stochastic RSI, Balance of Power, and the Center of Gravity Oscillator. The passage then promotes QuantifiedStrategies.com, stating it offers free trading strategies and backtests with “numbers, facts, and statistics” via articles and videos, and mentions trading courses, testimonials, and guides covering stock market basics to quantified and algorithmic trading.

The passage argues that Celtic’s win at Ibrox showed they are superior to Rangers and that Brendan Rodgers’s team will keep winning these matches. It claims Dave King has sold Mark Warburton “down the river” by not providing the financial backing Warburton was promised, and it criticizes Rangers players and squad age. The author says Celtic are ahead financially due to Champions League money and cite the signing of Moussa Dembele and Scott Sinclair as examples of “incredible” business. It concludes that Rodgers and Celtic should strengthen in the transfer window and use available money, including from Europe, to widen the gap over Rangers and effectively “finish off” Rangers domestically and in Europe next season.

The passage argues that generative AI represents a fundamentally different challenge for education than prior technologies, raising concerns about ethics and unclear classroom direction despite potential opportunities for humanizing teaching. It proposes a critical, philosophical approach to guide ethical AI use, drawing on Anders (technology reshaping humanity and the “Promethean discrepancy”), Foucault (technologies as systems of power shaping “regimes of truth”), and Freire and Arendt (education should promote humanization, conscientization, and action in a shared public world). The authors critique how AI can produce hallucinations, replicate biases, and enable corporate power over what counts as “truth,” which may undermine learners’ agency. They adapt Bloom’s (revised) taxonomy to understand cognitive learning tasks but argue it is insufficient for ethical direction, so they supplement it with Arendt’s focus on action and propose a spectrum framework for assessing student AI use—from consumptive labor to humanizing action. The framework is intended to be applicable across online, blended, and in-person modalities and is illustrated with imagined examples such as community-based political action and Socratic dialogue for personalized research, alongside guiding questions for educators.

The passage describes a market research report on the Global Silyl Modified Polymer Market. It provides historical, current, and projected revenues by sector, segment, end-user, and region, and analyzes market drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, trends, and competitive landscape. It covers key manufacturers including Kaneka, Bostik, Henkel, Wacker, Evonik, 3M, Dow Corning Corporation, H.B. Fuller, Hodgson Sealants, and Risun Polymer, and discusses macroeconomic and microeconomic factors and expected changes in policy and industry developments. The report includes product and application segmentations (Polyurethane Type, Polyamine Ether Type, Other; Construction, Automotive, General Industry, Others), provides regional analysis for the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World with metrics such as revenue, market share, and growth rate (2018–2025), and features analyses including SWOT, investment feasibility, and investment return. It also offers guidance for market players and outlines inquiry/sample report links and company contact information.

The passage describes a continuation patent application and provides background that low-latency cellular applications may be limited by reduced processing time when using configurable transmission time intervals (TTIs) or short TTIs (sTTIs). It presents methods and apparatus for a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) to determine processing capabilities (PCs), report them to an eNodeB (eNB), receive a PC configuration, and limit timing advance (TA) or Rx-Tx time differences to a maximum based on the applicable TTI length. The WTRU may also measure a processing value (PV), determine headroom relative to the PC, report based on a condition (including proximity), and take actions such as suspending or dropping uplink transmissions. Examples include reporting PCs based on TTI configurations, sTTI proximity conditions, and determining available processing time from DCI/UL grants or downlink transmissions to decide whether to transmit. Additional sections describe system diagrams and general communications system components, including WTRU, RAN, and CN structures, and further explain timing concepts such as TTIs, TA, Rx-Tx time differences, and processing time in relation to latency and short TTI operation.

The passage argues that trucking in India in 2027 will look very different from 2017 due to large population growth, urbanisation, and rising demand for goods. It highlights changes already underway, including a nationwide rollout of Bharat IV (BS IV) and a faster move to Bharat VI/BS VI, leapfrogging BS V, with OEMs expected to meet the standards quickly. It also says the long-awaited Goods and Services Tax (GST), if implemented, would enable longer-distance road travel by removing state border delays, increasing the need for more powerful and faster trucks. The passage expects a greater role for global truck manufacturers, notes the need for infrastructure investment to support speed and power, and links manufacturing growth to the Make In India initiative and Automotive Mission Plan AMP II goals. It concludes that while connected and improved trucks are expected, electrification and autonomous driving are expected to remain many decades away.

The passage describes a device that uses a processor and a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA) to implement fundamental computational primitives needed by applications such as speech recognition, industrial control, object detection/recognition, and vision. It explains configuring streaming engines to stream data from memory, configuring the MMA to format data, and executing primitives using a sequence of load/store/execute (LSE) instructions. The MMA includes multiplier, multiplicand (B) and result (C) buffers with buffering modes, configurable data formatting (including fixed-point parameters and optional LUT-based A formatting), a row offset component for loading data into different B-buffer rows, and an optional nonlinearity component (ReLU). A DSP-like processor with caches and streaming engines provides input/output vectors and performs additional formatting. The passage further outlines how the approach can implement various operations (e.g., convolution, matrix multiplications, pointwise multiplication, addition, vector summation, affine transformation, permutations, transposition) and includes examples for batch small/large matrix multiplication and 2D convolution. It also describes implementing FFTs and DCTs via matrix/pointwise multiplication strategies, and additional operations such as 1D convolution/filtering, correlation, matrix assignment, and matrix transpose.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on June 3, 2021. The report states that Jerome Guillen, President of Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed Tesla as of June 3, 2021. Tesla thanked him for his contributions and wished him well. The report was signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on June 7, 2021.

Cowen Group Inc’s shares rose 19% after CEFC China said it agreed to buy about a 20% stake in Cowen for $100 million. The agreement includes appointing three directors to Cowen’s board, $175 million in debt financing from CEFC, and a $18 per Class A share price (a 29.5% premium to Tuesday’s close). The deal is expected to close by the third quarter of 2017, subject to regulatory and government approvals. The announcement follows news that Tencent acquired a 5% stake in Tesla for $1.78 billion.

Apple overtook Samsung Electronics in smartphone sales in the fourth quarter, selling 77 million iPhones (17.9% share) versus Samsung’s 76.8 million smartphones (17.8% share), according to Gartner. The quarter is typically strong for Apple due to holiday sales of new iPhones, while Samsung’s 2016 ended badly after the Galaxy Note7 recall and brand damage, though it has a new flagship planned for late March. Apple is expected to unveil new iPhones in September, potentially leading some consumers to delay upgrades until then. Gartner also reports that Huawei, Oppo, and BBK (part of the same considered conglomerate but treated separately by Gartner) are next in the fourth-quarter rankings, with Oppo and BBK sharing 6.2% and 5.6% market shares, respectively, and Chinese firms expanding beyond South Asia.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture, focusing on features intended to improve performance and efficiency for AI, HPC, and data analytics in cloud and data center environments. It highlights support for many DL data types, third-generation Tensor Cores with TF32 and IEEE-compliant FP64 options, and fine-grained structured sparsity to double Tensor Core throughput. It also covers A100 memory and caching (HBM2, larger L2 cache, L2 residency controls, and compute data compression), Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) virtualization for secure partitioning into up to seven instances with isolation and QoS, and multi-GPU scaling improvements via third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch. Additional capabilities include Magnum IO and Mellanox interconnect compatibility, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error/fault detection and containment, asynchronous copy, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, and CUDA task graph acceleration. The passage also references system-level platforms such as DGX A100 and includes a list of figures and tables related to these technologies and performance comparisons.

An 80-year-old man, Yousuf, was treated on the floor at Gujranwala DHQ Hospital because staff refused to provide a bed due to all beds being occupied. His family said he was shifted to the hospital after stomach pain, and they urged authorities to address the shortage and ensure bed provision. Separately, Yaum-e-Takbeer was celebrated by the PML-N in Gujranwala, where party officials and workers gathered, cut a cake, and speakers paid tribute to Nawaz Sharif for making Pakistan a nuclear power.

Unidentified gunmen attacked the MINUSMA headquarters in Timbuktu, northern Mali, killing seven people and injuring seven others in a “terrorist” attack, according to mission chief Mahamat Saleh Annadif. Earlier Monday, gunmen attacked two neighboring U.N. camps in Douentza, killing a Malian soldier and a U.N. peacekeeper and lightly wounding another peacekeeper; Annadif also called it a terrorist attack. The U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the attacks, saying attacks targeting U.N. peacekeepers may constitute war crimes, and praised efforts by Mali and neighboring countries against terrorism and violent extremism. MINUSMA said five Malian security guards and a Malian contractor were killed in Timbuktu, six U.N. peacekeepers were wounded, and U.N. troops killed six assailants after dispatching quick reaction forces and attack helicopters. In Douentza, attackers fired from an adjacent hill and further exchanges involved a neighboring camp; two attackers were killed, and the U.N. is investigating whether the two attacks were connected. Annadif called for those responsible to be brought to justice.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back parts of Obama-era Wall Street regulations, including repealing a Dodd-Frank requirement that companies disclose the pay gap between CEOs and employees. The report, the second of four ordered by President Trump, also suggests making it easier for companies to go public, including allowing “testing the waters” through private discussions with likely shareholders before filing, and increasing crowdfunding limits so small companies can raise more money without going public. It also recommends “recalibrating” derivatives rules and coordinating oversight between the SEC and the CFTC. Supporters cited economic growth benefits, while critics warned that deregulation could reduce safety and raise risks for taxpayers.

Douglas Haig, an Arizona ammunition dealer, was charged with manufacturing armor-piercing bullets, according to federal court documents. The complaint says unfired armor-piercing bullets found in the Las Vegas hotel room from the Oct. 1 attack had Haig’s fingerprints and that he lacked a license to manufacture such ammunition, though it does not say whether it was used in the attack. Haig previously said he sold 720 rounds of ammunition to Stephen Paddock and noticed nothing suspicious, adding that Paddock told him he would go to the desert to shoot tracer ammunition as a light show. Haig’s lawyer held a news conference after Haig was revealed as a “person of interest,” and Haig said he has received unwanted media attention and death threats. Agencies including the Las Vegas Police Department and ATF declined comment, while the FBI and Nevada U.S. attorney’s office did not immediately respond.

The passage describes NIST’s revised password guidelines, which differ from traditional advice. NIST says passwords should be simple, long, and memorable, using phrases, lowercase letters, and typical English words, and it no longer recommends special characters, mixed case, or regular expiration. NIST says the previous guidance produced passwords easier for attackers and harder for legitimate users. The passage also notes that longer passwords are harder for hackers to break, password manager apps are useful but not necessary, and that frequent password changes often involve only minor character shifts.

The passage discusses using large language models (LLMs) as synthetic agents in social research and argues that interpreting LLM outputs as draws from well-defined population distributions can be misleading. It explains that LLMs generate probabilistic-looking text via learned patterns and sampling (e.g., temperature, top-k/p) rather than Bayesian posterior updating, and that repeated querying can violate exchangeability/martingale properties, leading to issues like order dependence and “introspective hallucination.” Empirical studies are cited showing LLMs can replicate many social-science patterns and predict certain experimental outcomes, but with limitations including reduced variance (“hyper-accuracy distortion”), weaker reliability for interaction effects, and systematic failures in sensitive categories. The passage proposes guidelines: treat LLM agents as high-capacity predictors under explicit conditioning (not calibrated probabilistic reasoners), validate subgroup performance and dispersion against human baselines, avoid in-prompt self-conditioning and order sensitivity, stress-test across prompts and out-of-distribution setups, and ensure reproducibility and full disclosure of simulation pipelines. It concludes that while synthetic agents have significant potential for near-term quasi-interpolation and exploring sensitive scenarios, the future likely requires many domain-specific tools rather than a single universal “LLM for social science,” with limitations clearly recognized.

The passage is a Dec. 14, 2000 email newsletter edition of “WPTF Burrito” discussing California’s electricity situation and related policy, media, and regulatory issues. It argues the public is mainly concerned about how much electric bills will rise, and proposes industry focus on holding down consumer bills through added generation, more customer choice, and a provider of last resort. It also covers claims and commentary about Senator Steve Peace’s stance, SCE’s CEO John Bryson calling for re-regulation and cost-based rates, credit and market mechanics affecting power imports, CPUC rate stabilization applications for PG&E and Edison being reopened, and a U.S. Secretary of Energy order requiring out-of-state generators and marketers to sell into California on demand, including shipments by BPA and PowerEx. The email additionally notes WPTF support for a Power Exchange emergency filing at FERC, includes “Mailbag” responses about public relations and consumer messaging, provides event details for a WPTF general meeting in February 2001 in Scottsdale, Arizona, and contains other sections including holiday-themed verses and a story about a father-son conversation.

The passage discusses the importance of early childhood education and school readiness, citing evidence that brain development and long-term outcomes are influenced by early programs. It describes India’s Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and Anganwadi centers (AWCs) as providers of early childhood care and education, noting that while coverage is large, research indicates quality in rural AWCs needs improvement. The study presented evaluates the status and quality of ECE in 71 AWCs in the Mewat district of Haryana, using qualitative and quantitative methods, including infrastructure assessment and interviews with Anganwadi workers (AWWs). Results report limited infrastructure safety, poor health and hygiene facilities, scarce learning resources, and low awareness among AWWs about curriculum domains and preschool teaching concepts; many AWWs rely on repetition and memorization methods. The discussion and conclusion state that these issues affect ECE quality and equity, and recommendations include improving infrastructure, training AWWs, increasing parental awareness and engagement, and strengthening monitoring and evaluation.

The passage lists multiple issues and their descriptions for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. Problems include incorrect behavior in various DMA/clock gating, interrupt handling, and register/I/O access scenarios (e.g., DMA and UART/IDE/ATAPI/SMB/LPC/USB behaviors, clock domains not waking, hangs from timing or alignment, and corrupted register interactions). It also describes several workarounds or resolutions, such as avoiding certain programming sequences (e.g., PIT read-back timing), not using a GLIU debug port, disabling automatic clock gating under specific interrupt conditions, ensuring PRD tables are correctly defined/aligned and not modified at unsafe times, avoiding access patterns that trigger CRC errors, and not using unsupported diagnostic modes or illegal address ranges. Some items state negligible/no operational impact or that failures primarily affect debug or rare event sequences.

The passage discusses how to evaluate AI systems, such as LLMs, in new and unforeseen tasks and environments, noting concerns about overfitting, data contamination, and the gap between static benchmarks and evolving models—especially for safety and security. It proposes future LLM benchmarking characteristics: dynamically generating evaluation samples, creating tasks with varied difficulty levels, and conducting multi-faceted ability analysis rather than relying only on final scores, with attention to adapting psychometrics for AI models. It also highlights additional challenges, including evaluating general-purpose AI’s cultural sensitivity, values, and adherence to human safety principles. An early effort described is DyVal, a framework that dynamically generates low-duplicate evaluation samples with uncertainty for risk control, supports multiple complexity levels, and uses a DAG structure to generate infinite samples with guaranteed ground truth.

Raja Jackson, son of retired MMA legend Quinton “Rampage” Jackson, faces multiple criminal charges related to an assault at a KnokX event in Los Angeles in August. The Los Angeles County District Attorney’s office says he will face one count of felony battery causing serious bodily injury and one count of misdemeanor battery, with a formal criminal complaint expected this week. Jackson, scheduled for a staged match, allegedly slammed wrestler Stuart Smith (also known as Syko Stu) to the ground and continued striking him after it appeared Smith was unconscious; Smith said he suffered multiple injuries including jaw damage, head injury, a lip laceration, and lost teeth. Jackson was arrested in September, and his father has condemned the actions. He faces up to four years in state prison for the felony charge, and prosecutors are expected to seek a sentencing enhancement.

The passage explains that stack procedures are provided for the host environment to establish a stack environment and are delivered as included macro code that the host must call. The routines do not depend on segment names from the host via include files and are defined without segment declarations. The host environment must create a local file that sets the proper execution environment and use the INCLUDE directive to pull in the stack code source. The routines are native assembly code that establish or destroy the stack and are intended to run in stackless mode, and they can be included in an assembly or, with care, a C host file.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures are electronically traded Nasdaq 100 Index futures on CME Globex, settled in cash at expiry, and sized at one-tenth the price of E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures. The contract trades Sunday to Friday with specified maintenance/reporting times, is listed quarterly (March, June, September, December), and financially settles on the third Friday of the contract month using special opening quotes of the index. The trading symbol is MNQ, with contract value based on the index price multiplied by $2; minimum price variation is 0.25 index points ($0.50) for outright trading and 0.05 index points for calendar spreads. The all-time high is 16,676.50 (Nov 2021) and the all-time low is 6,628.75 (March 2020). Prices are affected by movements of highly weighted component stocks, macroeconomic reports, interest rate policies, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events, and trading involves risks from large price movements due to leverage.

The passage summarizes two related probate and foreclosure matters (Cases No. 12,391 and 12,392) involving Oliver W. Toll, the executrix/guardian Mrs. McKenzie, and George W. Casey. In 12,391, Toll sought to open a long-closed probate proceeding after a demurrer to his reply was sustained and he brought error. In 12,392, Toll sought to enjoin foreclosure of Casey’s trust deed on his home (820) and appealed a judgment entered against him.

The dispute concerns a series of transactions beginning with an unrecorded warranty deed from Owens to McKenzie, followed by Casey’s recorded trust deed to secure a loan. After McKenzie’s death, Casey arranged a new backdated warranty deed to Mrs. McKenzie and recorded it, allegedly eliminating the minors’ interests. Mrs. McKenzie then contracted to sell 820 to Toll, received purchase money, and Toll later learned through conversation that the minors were true owners of an undivided half interest. A contract (“A”) was then executed to probate the will, initiate guardianship, present facts to the court, sell the minors’ interest to Toll if proper, and cover related costs so Toll would not bear expense. Pursuant to “A,” the will was probated and an order for sale in probate was obtained, followed by guardianship proceedings. Toll later filed a disclaimer in probate and, after protesting the proceedings and refusing further payment, sought to stop Casey’s foreclosure in district court.

The court concluded that the dispute involved a constructive fraud/good-faith misunderstanding settled by “A,” that the probate court had the facts while still having discretion, and that a valid probate sale would give Toll good title equivalent to a valid guardianship sale. However, the court modified the judgments to account for cost and payment obligations, ordering Toll to pay his own costs (with other cost allocations to Mrs. McKenzie or Casey depending on the case) and requiring Toll, by June 1, 1931, to pay the remaining encumbrance balance (less obligations assumed under “A”), after which Casey must release the trust deed to Toll.

On rehearing, Case No. 12,392 was remanded to effectuate the modified judgment and allow any necessary extension of time not exceeding thirty days.

The passage is narrated by Mashal Khan’s father, Muhammad Iqbal Khan. He describes Mashal as an exceptional student who loved reading and writing, and recalls his happiness when leaving for college. Four days before Mashal was killed, Mashal spoke to a local news channel, complaining about the absence of a vice chancellor, which prevented students from graduating, and calling for reduced college fees; he also said teachers at Abdul Wali Khan University held multiple designations and took two paychecks. Shortly before the killing, the father received a call about a fight on campus; Mashal was hurt, later large crowds chased him, and someone shot him. The police arrested several young men, though the father says he has not seen them and urges the government to provide justice and for political parties to unite so no one is scared to go to school. He also notes that people in his area are increasingly aware Mashal was innocent, and that Mashal’s memory should live on.

The passage describes hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) as a common household disinfectant with many uses, from whitening and styling to cleaning. It mentions an Instagram user using hydrogen peroxide and baking soda to clean a stovetop, and then lists 13 easy ways to use hydrogen peroxide: gargling to reduce bad breath, gradually lightening hair color, using peroxide drops for ear infections, cleaning fruits and vegetables, whitening teeth (including mixing with baking soda), disinfecting a toilet bowl, removing caked-on food with a paste of baking soda and peroxide, sanitizing cutting boards, cleaning kids’ toys, soaking feet, removing stains (with a test first), soaking plant seeds to mimic rainwater effects, and disinfecting reusable shopping bags to remove odors.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar and veterinary doctors from MAFSU are implanting a prosthetic limb on an eight-year-old male tiger, Sahebrao, at the Gorewada Rescue Centre in Nagpur. The tiger lost its paw after being caught in a steel trap laid by poachers outside the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in 2012. Dr Babhulkar says the procedure has been done for dogs and elephants but not tigers, and plans to procure an artificial limb from AO Foundation in Germany. The plan includes evaluating and treating a painful neuroma through clinical tests, then fitting a silicone prosthesis designed to look natural, be difficult for the animal to remove, and avoid infections, with a portable x-ray to minimize stress.

The newest Instant Pot pressure cooker, the 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra, is on sale for $120 at both Amazon and Sur La Table, down from its typical $150 price. The passage compares the Ultra to the DUO 7-in-1 and DUO Plus 9-in-1, saying the Ultra adds a 10th cooking option with an “Ultra” setting that lets users control temperature, pressure, and time. It also notes additional preset buttons and more cooking information than the DUO models, including pressure status and remaining time, plus a quick release button.

Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann for the Republican nomination in New Jersey’s 5th congressional district, saying McCann supports President Trump’s “America First” agenda and will help “drain the swamp.” McCann is running against former Bogota mayor Steve Lonegan in the GOP primary, with the winner facing Democratic Rep. Josh Gottheimer in November. The passage notes that in 2016 Lonegan criticized Trump and supported actions that could have affected Trump’s nomination, while Lonegan now describes himself as a Trump supporter. The passage discusses how meeting or learning about successful people can be empowering and highlights young, innovative entrepreneurs in India whose fast-growing companies are creating job opportunities. It lists seven “game changer” entrepreneurs and their companies: Flipkart (founded by Sachin and Binny Bansal; valued at USD 15 billion), PAYTM (Vijay Shekhar Sharma; launched in 2011; valued at USD 9.4 billion), Snapdeal (Kunal Behl and Rohit Bansal; started from an offline coupon business; valued at USD 6.5 billion), Ola Cabs (Bhavish Aggarwal; cab rental service; valued at USD 5 billion in 2015), Zomato (Deepinder Goyal and Pankaj Chaddah; restaurant locator and delivery app; valued at USD 1 billion in 2016), OYO Rooms (Ritesh Aggarwal; valued at USD 250 million), and Practo (Shashank ND and Abhinav; healthcare start-up app; valued at USD 650 million). UnitedHealth Group has named Michael Pencina, chief data scientist for Duke Health, as its chief AI scientist, citing a memo from Mary Klotman. The memo says Pencina stepped down from Duke on Wednesday for the role. At Duke, he advocated increased oversight of AI tools in health care, including a system to track AI product use and disclose details about training, development, and performance. He is also a co-founder of the Coalition for Health AI, which seeks to develop standards for testing and oversight of health care AI tools.

The passage explains that a leveraged ETF trading strategy is a short-term approach using leveraged exchange-traded funds that employ financial derivatives and debt to amplify an underlying index’s daily returns. It describes how leveraged ETFs may target ratios such as 2:1 or 3:1 (and may also be inverse), so gains and losses are magnified—losses can increase when the market moves against the position. The text emphasizes that due to high risk, management fees, transaction costs, and effects like volatility decay, leveraged ETFs are generally not suitable for long-term holding, and positions are recommended for only a few days. It outlines risk management ideas including stop-loss orders and diversifying across markets and between directional and inverse ETFs, and notes that leveraged ETF performance can be measured using ratios such as the Sharpe ratio, Jensen’s alpha, and appraisal/Treynor Black ratio. The passage also discusses tax treatment for U.S. citizens/residents based on holding period and indicates that short-term trading profits are taxed at short-term capital gain rates. It provides backtest examples showing that leveraged ETF strategies can yield higher returns but also experience substantial drawdowns, especially during adverse periods, and concludes that the most effective strategy discussed is short-term trading (day trading or swing trading) to target short-term momentum.

Bayern Munich players Robert Lewandowski, Arjen Robben, Arturo Vidal, and Joshua Kimmich were asked to choose a FIFA 18 Ultimate Team Squad Battle squad, and they selected 99-rated versions of themselves. The featured team includes Lionel Messi on the left wing, Ronaldo (named as a mention) with the Brazilian version up top beside an overpowered Lewandowski, a midfield of Patrick Vieira with Vidal replacing Zidane, and center backs of Lothar Matthaus and Paolo Maldini. David Alaba is on the left defense and Manuel Neuer finalizes the XI, with the passage noting the Bayern players’ stats as “ridiculous.”

The TLV322x comparator series includes an open-drain (open collector), sinking-only output stage that can be pulled up by an external voltage from 0 V to 5.5 V independently of the comparator supply (V+). TI recommends pull-up resistor current between 100 µA and 1 mA, noting trade-offs between rise time, VOL, and power dissipation, with rise time affected by total pull-up resistance and load capacitance. Output shorting to a voltage source can cause thermal runaway and device destruction; if shorts are possible, a series current-limiting resistor is recommended. Unused open-drain outputs can be left floating or tied to the V− pin. The device inputs and outputs include internal ESD protection, with input voltages limited to 0.2 V beyond the rails; a series current-limiting resistor is recommended for low-impedance sources, limiting current to 10 mA or less. The devices also include an internal Power-On Reset (POR) circuit that holds the output low during startup for up to 32 µs after V+ crosses VPOR of 1.65 V, after which the output reflects the differential input state.

After vaccination, common injection site reactions included redness, swelling, or pain, which participants recorded in electronic diaries within 7 days; these reactions were well tolerated, mostly mild or moderate, with pain most common. Systemic events recorded within 7 days (fever, tiredness, headache, chills, vomiting, diarrhea, or new muscle/joint pain) were also well tolerated, mostly mild or moderate, with tiredness and headache most common. Across phases, results for Phase 2 participants were similar to overall Phase 2/3 results. In Phase 2/3, few participants left due to medical problems, and most medical problems were mild or moderate. Serious medical problems within 1 to 6 months after Dose 2 or booster doses were infrequent; researchers generally did not believe serious problems were related to the study vaccine, and no participant died during Phase 1. During Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in participants who received BNT162b2 or placebo later received BNT162b2, and researchers did not believe deaths were caused by BNT162b2.

Kanawha County Sheriff’s Office arrested Zachary Steele, 21, after he allegedly punched his father, stole his parents’ vehicle, and fled. Deputies found him near Route 60 where he held a knife to his throat and threatened to harm himself and a police K9. A supervising deputy fired a less-lethal bean bag to incapacitate him, and he was taken into custody. Steele faces charges of domestic battery and fleeing on foot.

Technology Education Corporation (TEC) appealed a judgment awarding plaintiffs $5,225 each for breach of contract to perform educational services. Plaintiffs had contracts with Paraprofessional Institutes of Ohio (PIO), which sold its school assets to Educational Leadership Corporation (ELC). Plaintiffs attended ELC’s classes, graduated, and later sued alleging misrepresentations about course of study and out-placement services. Default judgment was entered against PIO and ELC, and the trial court resolved TEC’s liability after briefing on TEC’s motion to dismiss.

The appellate court addressed whether TEC could be held liable as a successor corporation despite not being in privity. The court noted that successor corporations generally are not liable for prior debts, with exceptions including express/implied assumption, de facto merger, mere continuation, or fraudulent transaction. The trial court had concluded TEC impliedly and expressly assumed liability and was a mere continuation of ELC, based on constructive knowledge, contract language, and continuity.

The appellate court held TEC did not expressly assume liability because the incorporated asset purchase agreement allocated pre-April 1, 1987 liabilities (with limited schedule exceptions that did not include student contracts). It also rejected implied assumption as inconsistent with TEC’s contractual allocation. On the continuation theory, the court found no evidence TEC lacked separate and distinct identity. It further stated the case is contractual, not products liability, and that plaintiffs failed to sustain their proof where the dismissal record lacked merits beyond allegations.

The appellate court sustained TEC’s assignments of error, reversed the trial court’s judgment, and remanded for further proceedings.

The passage is an email compiling multiple news items dated June 4, 2001, largely involving energy and Enron-related issues. It includes a Wall Street Journal report on Karl Rove holding stock in Enron and other major companies, and coverage of Saudi Arabia signing energy agreements with nine oil firms worth at least $25 billion. Several Reuters and Bloomberg items focus on India’s power sector and rating concerns tied to Fitch’s negative outlook change, including disputes involving Enron’s Dabhol Power project and India’s power reform plans. Other excerpts cover a UK “spark spread” trade involving Powergen and Enron, Nigeria’s president criticizing Enron’s performance on a Lagos power project, and commentary about energy pricing and deregulation in Japan.

The defence ministry said it has measures to ensure the country’s security is not compromised despite the economic crisis, adding that “national sovereignty is guaranteed.” It reported that thousands of soldiers were sent home on furlough to save costs. Defence minister Penda ya Ndakolo said budget cuts and limited expected improvements led to temporary measures to target cost savings, including training and transport, with utilities like water, electricity, and feeding identified as savings areas. The minister said compulsory leave mainly affects older members nearing retirement and troops with social problems affecting morale, and that those who had not taken annual leave can spend time with their families. He said 70% of troops remain to provide capacity, and procedures exist to recall those on leave if needed.

JPMorgan CEO and chairman Jamie Dimon, previously a critic of Bitcoin, said blockchain is “real” as his bank experiments with digital asset ledgers. He argued that stablecoins and JPMorgan’s deposit token could have real-world use cases, but that blockchain’s decentralized nature makes it difficult for parties to agree on permissions and rules, so JPMorgan uses a private, permissioned version of blockchain with control over who can use it and how. Dimon said it could replace certain clunky or non–24/7 systems and cited intraday repos, while also saying blockchain will not “replace everything” and is sometimes a solution looking for a problem. When asked about Bitcoin, he declined to comment and joked that discussing it leads to headlines and death threats.

The passage describes a continuation of U.S. patent applications related to preventing ransomware from encrypting files on a target machine. It explains that ransomware often enumerates and encrypts user-relevant files using a private key, and existing protection is difficult. The disclosed techniques involve monitoring file system activities on a computing device and detecting unauthorized activity involving honeypot files or honeypot folders (forged by an endpoint agent), then performing actions based on an anti-ransomware/security policy. Honeypot files and directories can be implemented as virtual entries using a mini filter driver that spoofs directory listings and redirects access to pre-created files, aiming to have ransomware target honeypots before real files. The system can detect ransomware behaviors such as creating handles for deletion, deleting, renaming, and writing to honeypots, and respond by terminating processes, denying access, raising alerts, and/or monitoring/logging. The passage also outlines example flow diagrams for triggering prevention based on file open, setting file information, file writing, and directory enumeration events, and describes components of an endpoint agent including modules for monitoring, virtual honeypot data, policy/configuration, and user interface for rule configuration.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson announced “conditional support” for the Federal Government’s media ownership and regulation reforms. She said her party backs the changes in exchange for greater transparency of ABC staff wages, agreement to investigate the ABC’s balance and commitment to regional areas, and an extra $12 million for community radio initiatives. The reforms would scrap the “reach rule” and the “two out of three” rule. Hanson said the Coalition agreed to have the ABC provide details of staff wages and conditions for those earning more than $200,000.

The passage explains the Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO), a momentum indicator introduced by Tushar Chande in 1994. It measures momentum based on the difference between sums of higher closes and lower closes over a chosen period (often 20), producing values from -100 to +100. Readings above +50 and below -50 are used to signal overbought and oversold conditions, respectively, and the indicator can also generate divergence signals that may suggest price reversals. The passage provides the formula and basic calculation steps, describes how traders may add a moving average signal line, and outlines how CMO can be combined with trend indicators and used in momentum or mean-reversion (sideways) strategies. It also states that CMO cannot identify main trends, may not perform well in volatile markets, and that best timeframes and period settings should be determined through backtesting on different assets and settings.

A blowout March private employment report from ADP said U.S. companies added 263,000 workers, beating economists’ 187,000 estimate, supporting confidence in the U.S. economy. After the report, the Nasdaq hit an all-time high and the Dow was on pace for its best day in more than a month; all 11 S&P 500 sectors rose, led by financials and technology. Markets were also awaiting a meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and the start of first-quarter earnings season. The Federal Reserve will release March meeting minutes at 2:00 p.m. ET, while stocks like Amazon and Panera Bread rose on company-specific news.

Germany, France, Britain, Spain, and Italy warned the Trump administration that its tax plan may violate international trade rules. In a letter to Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin signed by their finance ministers, they said changes to the U.S. tax code could advantage American companies and argued against a new 20% tax on payments from U.S. multinationals to foreign affiliates and a 10% tax on certain cross-border transfers within banks and finance companies. They also opposed a Senate measure that could subsidize U.S. exports. The letter said these provisions could be discriminatory and raise World Trade Organization issues. The House and Senate have passed competing tax bill versions and are reconciling differences as Republicans aim for a final agreement before Christmas, with Trump expected to speak on tax reform.

The passage describes trends in the global corrugated packaging market, linking consumer internet shopping and demand patterns to innovation and growth. It cites a Research Report Insights analysis predicting the market will expand from 2014 to 2020 at a 4% CAGR to reach US$173.6 million in 2020, while noting developments affecting market growth. The market is segmented by application (including liner board, container board, sheets, and boxes) and by flute type (A, B, C, E, and F), with key drivers including lower cost, sustainability, and growth of industries such as medicine, rubber, food, consumer durables, and petroleum, as well as e-commerce. Growth opportunities are highlighted in emerging markets, while restraining factors include low durability and delayed growth in end-user industries. The competitive landscape is described as consolidated through many M&As, with companies aiming to expand in emerging markets. A regional breakdown is provided for North America, APAC, Europe, and the rest of the world, with key manufacturing locations listed as Japan, India, and China, and dominance noted for specific countries.

The passage describes a bibliometric study of primary school science education research. It argues that early science education supports intellectual development and STEM interest, but implementation is hindered by issues such as limited resources, inadequate teacher preparation, and rigid curricula. The study uses bibliographic coupling and co-word analysis of 2,295 Web of Science indexed publications (1997 to Dec 31, 2024), analyzed with VOSviewer, to map intellectual structure, dominant themes, and emerging trends. Five main thematic clusters are identified: (1) augmented/virtual reality and ICT integration, (2) equity and teacher competence, (3) cognitive and metacognitive supports, (4) dialogic and integrative pedagogies, and (5) artificial intelligence, computer science, and computational thinking. Co-word analysis yields four thematic clusters: dialogic argumentation and scientific literacy; teacher beliefs and professional development; achievement, engagement, and conceptual change; and computational thinking and technology integration in STEM. The study reports publication and citation trends, identifies key highly linked references and keywords, and concludes that the field is shifting toward inquiry-based, digitally supported, and equity-oriented approaches, while gaps remain in culturally responsive computational thinking and teacher identity. It proposes the DIG-EDU-QUEST framework to guide theory, practice, and policy, and recommends future research with broader data sources and qualitative methods.

Tickets for “Black Panther” are very hard to obtain, even for star Lupita Nyong’o. After Ron Clark Academy students in Atlanta learned they would see the film, they danced to an instrumental from its soundtrack in a viral Twitter video. The school’s director of curriculum and instruction, Wade King, said he and fellow teacher Susan Barnes combined the movie with curriculum so students would use comic books to learn imperial history and African art, and use “Black Panther” in math, science, and gym. King also described emotional excitement after students opened a weekly meeting with an African-inspired spoken-word performance.

The passage explains that humans host large numbers of bacteria and that microbiota research has expanded in recent decades, recognizing microbes as essential to health through functions like digestion, metabolism, immune responses, and inflammation. It describes evidence that the gut microbiota shows daily (circadian) rhythmicity, and that modern behaviors such as eating late or exposure to electric light at night may disrupt these patterns and contribute to adverse health effects. The passage summarizes animal research showing that microbiota metabolites released over the day alter gene expression in the mouse liver, and that changing feeding times or removing most gut microbiota with antibiotics changes liver physiology. It also reports that liver responses to acetaminophen overdoses vary over the day, with reduced toxicity at dawn and higher toxicity at dusk, leading to the conclusion that microbiota regulate daily detoxification efficiency. The work is presented as enabled by advances in DNA sequencing and microbiome analysis, emphasizing that microbial communities function as wholes rather than reducible single species. The passage concludes that these findings may be relevant to humans, including people taking long-term antibiotics and shift workers.

Sterling traded in a tight range on Tuesday, rising slightly against the dollar and the euro, as investors appeared to focus less on Britain’s impending Article 50 trigger. Prime Minister Theresa May plans to notify the EU on Wednesday to start two years of exit talks, and analysts said the initial step may be mainly symbolic while sterling’s direction depends on the EU’s response and the state of the British economy. The pound has recently benefited from stronger UK inflation and signs that the Bank of England may raise interest rates, but uncertainty about Brexit terms has continued to weigh on it, leaving it nearly 20% lower since the Brexit vote. Concerns remain about a potentially “hard” Brexit, the difficulty of negotiations, and the possibility of another Scottish independence referendum.

Under the GST regime launched on 1 July, e-way bills are required for transporting goods consignments valued above Rs50,000 to help check tax evasion. The GST Council approved exemptions on 5 August for 153 items, including cooking gas/LPG for households and kerosene for the public distribution system, certain food items (such as fruits, vegetables, fresh milk, honey, seeds, cereals and flour), domesticated animals, betel leaves, non-alcoholic toddy, raw silk, khadi, earthen pots and clay lamps, puja samagri, hearing aids, human hair, semen (including frozen semen) and condoms/contraceptives. Exemptions also include postal baggage, currency, jewellery, used personal and household effects, transport by non-motorised conveyances, and goods moved from international to hinterland ports for customs clearance. The need for an e-way bill starts once notified by the central government after software readiness by the National Informatics Centre, likely by October, and the permit must include details of the goods, mode, origin/destination, and the supplier/recipient/transporter. Conveyance details are not needed if transport distance is less than 10 km within a state.

The passage discusses how integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into multi-organ imaging genetics is advancing precision medicine by introducing new “endophenotypes.” It describes three key catalysts: large-scale multi-omics datasets (e.g., UK Biobank and FinnGen), open science efforts providing publicly available GWAS summary statistics and portals, and computational genomics statistical methods using GWAS summary data (e.g., LDSC for heritability and genetic correlations, and Mendelian randomization for potential causal relationships). Despite these advances, the genetic basis of AI endophenotypes in pleiotropic multi-organ disease endpoints is said to be largely uncharted. The authors previously generated 2024 multi-organ AI endophenotypes from UKBB imaging/genetics, made UKBB-derived GWAS summary statistics public, and note FinnGen and PGC also released GWAS summary statistics. The current study uses these public GWAS resources and advanced statistical methods to depict the genetic architecture of the 2024 MAEs and analyze 525 disease endpoints, including additional FinnGen and PGC data, while systematically benchmarking and comparing statistical methodologies.

Center for Diagnostic Imaging Miami (CDI Miami) offers technologically advanced diagnostic imaging and preventive screening services, including x-ray, PET and PET CT, nuclear medicine, CTA, MRI, ultrasound, open MRI, and 3D mammograms. CDI Miami also provides a Full Body Scan package designed by healthcare professionals to screen for common diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and heart disease, featuring high-resolution CT scanning of head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis, cardiac calcium scoring, and follow-up physician consultation within 24–48 hours. The scan is described as detecting a range of conditions across the body, and CDI Miami also provides nuclear medicine options such as thallium stress tests, bone scans, and thyroid scans. The services are implemented using latest technologies under supervision of board-certified radiologists, physicians, and technicians.

An Energy Central “Professional Dispatch” email dated January 29, 2002, for January 30, 2002, compiles selected electric power and gas industry news, advertisements, and sponsor information. The dispatch highlights top stories and most-requested articles, including multiple items related to Enron, energy regulation and oversight, electricity markets and competition, power pricing and outages, and various corporate, legislative, environmental, and international developments.
