Jurors convicted Joseph Percoco on three counts, finding him guilty on two counts of conspiracy and solicitation of bribes. After a not-guilty outcome on the first two counts, the defense said they are considering an appeal and/or further review; Barry Bohrer said a difficult Albany politics case and a closer case led them to options for further review, and Steve Coffey said he plans to move to set aside the verdict. Prosecutors said Percoco sold his influence in government to help executives before the state. Steven Aiello was found not guilty on bribery charges but guilty on one count of conspiracy; his attorney said the verdict is inconsistent with the law. Joseph Gerardi was found not guilty on all charges, while the jury remained deadlocked on CPV Executive Peter Galbraith Kelly Jr., who is accused of disguising bribes through payments to Percoco’s wife. Sentencing is set for June 11 for Percoco and June 14 for Aiello. Governor Cuomo said he respects the verdict, expressed sadness, and stated there is no tolerance for violations of the public trust.

The passage describes the high frequency and clinical risks of postoperative hyperglycemia after cardiac surgery, including higher infection rates, acute kidney injury, cardiac arrhythmias, longer hospital stay, and higher mortality. The Society of Thoracic Surgeons recommends keeping blood glucose levels below 180 mg/dL after surgery, but early postoperative glucose control is challenging, and current protocol-based insulin titration often leads to both hyperglycemic and hypoglycemic episodes. It proposes GLUCOSE, a distributional offline reinforcement learning model that dynamically suggests personalized regular insulin dosing during the first day after cardiac surgery, validated using MIMIC-IV (development cohort) and eICU-CRD (external validation). The study includes 6,148 development patients and 649 external validation patients and reports metrics on hypoglycemic/hyperglycemic event rates, estimated performance improvements over clinician returns, analyses of time-in-range based on dosing agreement, and multi-phased human evaluations assessing insulin dosing alignment, safety, effectiveness, and acceptability. The model’s limitations noted include the need for prospective validation, restriction to the first postoperative day, exclusion of dietary data, and reliance on accurately documented medication dosing records.

The passage introduces Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for graph-structured data and notes a gap in most existing methods that focus on homogeneous graphs, despite many real-world datasets forming heterogeneous graphs with multiple node and edge types. It describes meta-path-based approaches and their reliance on expert-defined meta-paths, along with limitations such as missing meta-paths and increased complexity from longer or more meta-path lengths. It also discusses challenges in heterogeneous GNNs including over-smoothing, capturing long-range information, and avoiding excessive layer stacking that increases time complexity.  

To address these issues, the passage proposes VN-HGCN (Virtual Node-based Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Network), which adds hierarchical virtual nodes (type-level virtual nodes plus a central virtual node) to shorten graph distances and enable long-range message passing with only 4 layers, without predefined meta-paths. VN-HGCN transforms node types into a shared semantic space, performs node-level and type-level aggregation using attention, and updates node embeddings across layers. Experiments on ACM, DBLP, and IMDB for node classification compare VN-HGCN with several state-of-the-art models and a virtual-node variant of ie-HGCN, reporting that VN-HGCN achieves strong performance across most training ratios and is especially effective with smaller training data. The passage also includes a parameter sensitivity analysis showing robustness to changes in hidden dimension, number of layers, and number of type-level virtual nodes, and concludes that adding virtual nodes improves model performance by improving how the original graph is connected.

The passage describes SimulRAG, a simulator-based retrieval-augmented generation framework for long-form scientific question answering. It addresses challenges in grounding LLMs with scientific simulators by introducing a generalized simulator retrieval interface that converts between textual and numerical modalities, and a claim-level generation method that decomposes answers into atomic claims for verification and updating. Verification is made more efficient using uncertainty estimation scores and simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA), which select only uncertain and simulator-verifiable claims for simulator-based checking. The work also introduces a benchmark for long-form scientific QA across climate modeling and epidemiology, using climate emulator and GLEAM-AI with ground-truth answers derived from simulation evidence and human annotators. Experiments across two domains and two LLMs show SimulRAG outperforms traditional RAG baselines in factuality and informativeness, and UE+SBA improves claim-level verification efficiency and quality. A limitation noted is the assumption that all questions relate to available simulators, with future work suggested on automatic question-simulator relevance detection.

The passage argues that after World War I the world is still readjusting socially and economically, and that no permanent readjustment is possible unless all participate. It says the crisis involves both international rehabilitation and, at home, social, financial, and economic problems, including unemployment reduction and restored industrial activity, while criticizing coal and railway strikes for hindering progress. It highlights agriculture’s distress, especially tied to railway strike effects and broader transportation failures affecting farmers and perishable goods, and says Congress should provide financial and production credit for farmers and improve transportation.

It describes railroad freight growth and claims railroad mileage and capacity are inadequate, presenting transportation as a major national problem requiring coordination among transportation facilities, including better rail-sea connections, using inland waterways, and treating motor trucks as feeders rather than competitors. The passage also calls for reducing freight costs essential to national welfare, discusses government regulation of rail rates and labor issues, and proposes changes such as pooling freight cars via a central agency and replacing the Railroad Labor Board’s partisan structure with an impartial labor tribunal with enforceable decisions to prevent public service disruption.

Later sections address a new tariff law’s flexible customs duties, U.S. international cooperation without dictation, handling domestic issues including constitutional prohibition enforcement and alien registration and education/immigration policy, recommending constitutional amendments related to child labor and tax-exempt securities, and suggesting additional studies on topics like high-cost-living, reclamation and forestry, energy and power distribution, and national defense preparedness. It concludes by emphasizing U.S. roles in promoting peace and assisting other nations within constitutional limits.

The Alaska Department of Fish and Game in Dillingham received reports of an oddly behaving fox along Wood River Road, described as aggressive, snarling, snapping its teeth, following a car, trying to bite a fender, and foaming at the mouth. ADF&G biologist Neil Barten said these signs can indicate rabies and urged people to avoid approaching such a fox and stay away. He also warned that rabid foxes pose a risk to pets and advised dog owners to ensure rabies vaccinations are current. Reports can be made to the ADF&G office in Dillingham at 907-842-2334.

Engineering and construction manager Khalil Ewais, a mid-level Cleveland city worker, tried to resign in June 2015, saying he was underpaid and his duties exceeded those listed when he was hired in 2011. His resignation was rescinded after bosses Richard Switalski and Matthew Spronz promised to hire four new construction inspectors and consider restructuring the office, and Spronz said he discussed Ewais’s raise with Mayor Frank Jackson. In April, federal agents from the FBI, IRS, and HUD entered City Hall and seized records related to Ewais’s side business Pioneer Engineering and projects at addresses on Lorain, Carnegie, and Storer avenues, as well as a Geauga County paving company, Burton Scot Contractors. The city said it was evaluating how to handle Ewais’s work assignments. Ewais’s personnel file also includes details about his employment history, a 2017 internal audit questionnaire denying business with the city, and a 2014 warning for excessive sick time. Burton Scot defended its city paving contracts, stating it was glad to answer investigators’ questions.

In 2017, internet and technology stocks, especially the FAANG group (Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and Alphabet), drove the market to repeated records. The five stocks outperformed the market due to investors paying for high growth, though concerns about overvaluation were raised, including Netflix’s reported high price-to-earnings ratio. Morgan Stanley said the group contributed heavily to Wall Street’s gains, with the largest S&P 500 components accounting for 27.5% of market capitalization growth and a high level of concentration compared with other bull markets. While Morgan Stanley rated FAANG stocks “fundamentally” as overweight and pointed to competitive advantages, it noted “yellow flags” from macro factors and history suggesting returns may moderate and growth may not remain as strong as a driver. The bank warned the stocks may be less insulated from cyclical pressures tied to advertising and consumer spending, and portfolio managers reduced exposure in the third quarter. Morgan Stanley expected a wide range of outcomes, with Amazon’s base-case growth near 10% and a bull case of a little over 70%.

The email forwards a piece by Arundhati Roy titled “Brutality smeared in peanut butter,” arguing that the US-led air strikes on Afghanistan should stop. The passage describes the strikes as unmandated and driven by inadequate or disregarded evidence, and states that terrorism cannot be justified whether committed by groups or governments, since civilians are killed in both places. It critiques the International Coalition Against Terror as dominated by wealthy weapons-holding countries, and contrasts the Taliban’s origins in war with its current brutality toward women. The text also discusses difficulties for pilots and the Northern Alliance’s moves toward Kabul, reports of civilian casualties and blocked access to food, and condemnation of US emergency rations as a dangerous public-relations exercise. It further argues that targeting and surveillance will erode freedom, highlights conflicting definitions of “terrorism,” and questions whether the war is connected to arms, media, and oil interests. The piece concludes by urging people to stop the war and expresses concern about losing the ability to dream and reimagine beauty.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff in BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% of contributions went to Democrats in 2023 and 2024, up from a 6-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio in a 2021 analysis of 2017–2020. Derek Muller of the University of Notre Dame Law School found about $52 million in contributions to Democratic-affiliated groups versus about $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Contributions were analyzed across the nation’s 100 top-grossing firms and 50 plaintiffs-side firms, based on donations related to campaigns of Joe Biden, Kamala Harris, and Donald Trump, major party organizations, and aggregators. Among the top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton (99.7%), Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson (99.4%), and Mintz, Levin, Cohn, Ferris, Glovsky and Popeo (99.1%) had the highest shares of contributions to Democratic campaigns, while Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough (66.4%), Lewis Brisbois Bisgaard & Smith (77.3%), and Ogletree, Deakins, Nash, Smoak & Stewart (81.5%) had the lowest.

Annetta Gibson sued Max Hall Gibson for specific performance of a property settlement agreement incorporated into their dissolution decree. The court ordered Max to perform and required him to delete a trust provision allowing him to borrow, pledge, or use the cash value of insurance policies, and also awarded attorney fees and costs. Max appealed, arguing the court altered the agreement, venue was improper, Annetta had an adequate remedy at law, and fees were unwarranted. The court found it enforced the parties’ agreement by ensuring security through life insurance, held that venue was proper in Platte County based on the parties’ waiver in the settlement agreement, rejected the adequacy-of-law remedy argument, and upheld attorney fees because the contract allowed fees to a successful litigant. The judgment was affirmed.

The lecture introduces taint tracking for detecting Android data exfiltration, focusing on the TaintDroid system. Apps may leak sensitive phone data (e.g., contacts, location, IMEI, credentials) by sending it over the network. Traditional Android permissions are insufficient because they do not express restrictions about specific data. A proposal to block apps with both sensitive data access and network access is discussed as problematic due to breaking legitimate apps, missing side channels, and not preventing app collusion.

TaintDroid works by tracking sensitive information as it propagates through the system using sources (e.g., GPS, sensors, contact databases, IMEI) and sinks (notably the network). It represents taint with a 32-bit bitvector for up to 32 taint sources, propagating taint through Dalvik VM instructions, with unions computed via bitwise operations. Special cases include array accesses, native methods (handled via manual/manual-assisted taint policies based on a limited set of VM-exposed functions), IPC messages, files, and Java state (local variables, method arguments, object fields, static fields, and arrays). Taint labels are stored near variables for efficiency. TaintDroid can deny network transmission of tainted data and may either alert users or alter policies on what is sent.

The lecture also discusses why low-level x86/ARM taint tracking can be expensive and error-prone (including “taint explosion”), and explains that TaintDroid cannot fully handle implicit flows (e.g., branch-dependent assignments where tainted data affects control flow rather than direct assignment). It mentions approaches such as PC tainting to address implicit flows, and broader systems that allow richer label semantics.

Finally, it briefly describes TightLip, which uses “doppelganger processes” that read scrubbed file data; TightLip monitors whether system calls diverge from the original process and flags cases where divergence suggests sensitive data influence, such as when a doppelganger makes a network call.

Today’s sole practice session at Suzuka began with warm air (21°C) and a hotter track (28°C), and while it was dry, bright, and almost sunny, there were still damp patches from earlier rain. Fernando Alonso made the big news by serving a 25-place grid penalty after an engine change following a hydraulic leak, joining Carlos Sainz and Mercedes Valtteri Bottas, who also have grid penalties. Sebastian Vettel was expected to try a gearbox after a post-race clash with Lance Stroll.  

FP2/qualifying simulations were affected by several incidents and red flags, including a crash for Raikkonen at Degner and damage to Bottas’s car after running wide in Spoon, which left damage to the right rear requiring repairs. Despite the interruptions, Bottas set the fastest time overall, ahead of Hamilton, Vettel, Verstappen, Ricciardo, Ocon, Hulkenberg, Alonso, Perez, and Palmer.

The passage discusses attacking a “Box & One” defense by keeping the secondary offense simple and practicing related plays. It emphasizes designing attacks to counter the defense’s overplay and to free up the scorer, with an easy approach being to isolate the star player one-on-one in the middle. It outlines multiple “Chase” Box & One offensive sequences, including Shuffle Cut actions (screens and cuts involving the high post, star, and weakside two game), Screen & Roll options, Base Screen plays, Back Screen action, and Give & Go entries leading to weakside two game or base screen setups. If reversal passes fail, the offense can transition into back cuts with double screens and then flow into single/double continuity. Implementation guidance stresses proper execution and coordination of mid screens, base screens, and strong post ups, along with defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. It also advises scouting opponents when possible to anticipate defensive reads and counters, adjusting awareness for changes after substitutions and timeouts, and using varied alignments and entries to prevent defenders from focusing. The passage concludes with a description of the Box & One defense: four players guard in a box zone while the chaser applies aggressive full pass denial and does not allow the opponent to receive a pass or grab a rebound.

The passage describes the 52-week high trading strategy and the concept of 52-week highs and ranges. The 52-week high is the highest stock price over a one-year period, based on daily closing prices, and the 52-week range runs between the 52-week high and 52-week low, with the high acting as resistance and the low as support. The strategy aims to buy stocks trading close to their 52-week highs, contrary to “buy low and sell high,” based on academic findings that stocks near 52-week highs tend to have better subsequent returns than those far away. The article reports that it backtested the approach on individual stocks and the S&P 500 (using SPY as a proxy) and states that the resulting strategies did not appear tradable or worth further time, and suggests it may not replicate particularly good performance.

The passage says that actress Rose McGowan reached a previously undisclosed $100,000 settlement with film mogul Harvey Weinstein in 1997, when she was 23. It reports that a New York Times legal document described the settlement as not an admission of harassment and intended to avoid litigation. The Times also says actress Ashley Judd accused Weinstein of inviting her to his hotel room and offering her a massage. The passage notes Weinstein’s influence in Hollywood, including producing multiple best-picture Academy Award winners, and says McGowan declined to comment while Weinstein said he would take a leave of absence from The Weinstein Company.

The Department of Energy has approved nearly $67 million in grants for 85 nuclear research projects at university and government laboratories to promote safety, efficiency, and US energy independence. The plan includes over $31 million for 32 university-led projects in 23 states and $6 million shared by 19 universities for research on nuclear reactor safety and performance. The release says that since 2009, the Office of Nuclear Energy has awarded about $472 million to 103 US colleges and universities to support research and train future nuclear engineers and scientists.

The passage describes the NHS Patient Charter, which draws together patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges beyond legal requirements, and patients’ responsibilities to use the service fairly and respectfully. It outlines expectations on access to care (including waiting time standards and explanations when standards slip), equal treatment regardless of protected characteristics, quality and safety (including continuous improvement and regulation), access to medicines and treatments based on NICE guidance and local evidence-based decisions, consent, privacy, and information rights. It also covers choice and involvement in decisions, openness when something goes wrong (“duty of candour”), complaints and escalation options, seeking judicial review, and compensation. The charter emphasizes that the NHS is a partnership needing patient cooperation, such as following treatment plans and participating in vaccination and screening. The page states the information is peer reviewed by qualified clinicians.

The passage discusses a dieting trend claiming fruit is less healthy than previously thought, citing examples like Tom Brady avoiding strawberries and referencing past debunked diets. Samantha Rigoli, a registered dietitian, says fruit is “super healthy,” noting it is nutrient-dense with antioxidants, vitamins, and phytonutrients. She explains that although fruit can be higher in carbs and natural sugars, its nutritional value can’t be compared to calorie-dense foods like cookies. She also suggests considering glycemic index when losing weight and emphasizes that calorie quality matters more than quantity, as different foods affect nutrients and bodily functions differently. Overall, she concludes that fruit is amazing and should be eaten daily.

The passage is a lecture review by Lorna Gibson on biomimicking and cellular structures. It discusses examples where biological materials are replicated or inspire engineering designs, including carbon templating of wood to make silicon carbide replicas, 3-D printed honeycombs with fiber-reinforced resin (aligned by rotating the nozzle), foamed metal coatings inspired by trabecular bone, scaffolds mimicking extracellular matrix, lightweight sandwich panels comparable to structures in nature, and density gradients in palm stems matched to stress distributions. It also covers plant and animal quills with solid outer shells and foamy cores (grass stems, porcupine quills, hedgehog spines, toucan beaks, and feathers) and explains that foam cores help reduce wrinkling and reduce weight for a given buckling load. Engineering attempts to mimic horsetail stems and related structures are also mentioned. The latter part reviews exam preparation for a Wednesday test, what students should know for open-celled foam and related mechanical concepts, and then answers questions about an energy-absorption homework problem involving foam graphs and equations, followed by additional logistical course updates.

The passage compiles multiple news items about Enron’s late-2001 crisis. It describes how Enron’s sharp share price decline harmed employees’ 401(k) retirement plans after plan assets were frozen, and it reports legal action alleging Enron breached fiduciary duties by promoting Enron stock while knowing it was overvalued. It also details financing and deal uncertainty around Enron’s proposed acquisition by Dynegy, including loan extensions, investor discussions about possible equity injections, and concerns that renegotiation or bankruptcy could occur if Dynegy steps away. Additional sections cover Enron’s business reviews in Japan, potential sale interest for Enron’s Wessex Water unit, Enron’s bond-market stress and creditor impacts in Japan and globally, and international effects such as the shock waves of the crisis in Japan and a possible sale of Enron’s stake in India’s Dabhol Power.

The passage describes long COVID as a range of health problems lasting four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with an estimated global prevalence of 43% among infected individuals. It notes that while vaccines show high effectiveness against infection and severe outcomes, some people remain susceptible to infection and long COVID, which has been linked to more than 3,500 deaths. The passage reports that long COVID can occur after both mild and severe acute disease, identifies risk factors in non-hospitalized adults (including female sex, socioeconomic deprivation, obesity, and comorbidities), and highlights that healthcare workers may be more vulnerable due to frequent occupational exposure. It then states the study’s aim: analyzing epidemiological data and risk factors for long COVID among healthcare workers in Brazil. The methods section outlines a case-control study of healthcare workers at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein from March 1, 2020 to July 15, 2022, defining cases as laboratory-confirmed RT-PCR infections followed by symptoms lasting more than four weeks without alternative explanation, and controls as those who recovered within four weeks.

The passage describes the Cahokia Creek Watershed Planning project, which will create watershed plans for two Cahokia Creek watersheds in western Madison County to address storm water, flooding, and water quality issues. HeartLands Conservancy, a nonprofit led by community leaders, is gathering community input through public open houses in Edwardsville (Jan. 17) and Glen Carbon (Jan. 19). The watershed includes Indian Creek and Canteen Creek areas, encompassing Glen Carbon and Edwardsville, and channels water to the Mississippi River. Janet Buchanan, HeartLands’ environmental planning and policy lead, says the collected input will help lay groundwork and guide funding efforts and project focus areas such as flooding-prone areas, storm water infrastructure, littering and dumping-related water quality problems, and impacts on boating, swimming, mining-related subsidence, and fish and wildlife. The project is part of Madison County’s storm water management planning, conducted through a partnership with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, with HeartLands as lead consultant.

Panic followed a report by a 10-year-old student of the Government Primary School at PGI that youths in a black car allegedly tried to abduct her near a Vekra Booth inside PGI around 11 am on Tuesday. She informed school management, and local police responded; a DDR was lodged despite no police complaint. SI Elam Rizvi said police interacted with local residents, who reported they had not observed any kidnapping attempt, and noted the incident occurred four days after a Feb 9 kidnapping attempt involving another student near PGI. Since then, the school management has requested regular PCR patrol car coverage near the school in the mornings and afternoons.

The passage provides James Spann’s midweek Alabama weather forecast. It describes a Flash Flood Watch for much of central Alabama until 7 p.m., with chances of showers and thunderstorms continuing due to rich tropical moisture and an upper trough. It notes recent flash flood warnings, saturated ground, and the risk of flooding in flood-prone areas. Tomorrow, storms are expected to be more scattered, with a marginal severe weather risk in parts of north Alabama and possible small hail and gusty winds. Friday through the weekend, weather is expected to be partly sunny with scattered afternoon/evening showers and thunderstorms and highs near 90 degrees. Next week may turn drier early, with fewer showers, and a surface front could increase shower and storm chances late in the week. The Atlantic basin is quiet, with no tropical storm formation expected for seven days. The passage also references a beach forecast link and a weekly weather netcast.

Belgium’s 18-10 upset win over Spain means Romania qualifies for the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan, while Spain will play Portugal and the winner will face Samoa. Belgium’s win arose from penalty kicks, and there was an incident at the end involving angry Spanish players confronting Romanian referee Vlad Iordaschescu, who was escorted off the field; World Rugby is looking into the appointment of a Romanian referee. The remaining World Cup qualifiers will be decided through a November four-team repechage involving teams including Canada, which dropped in after losing to the Americans and Uruguay, and another Africa Cup runner-up and a series winner between Asia 2 and Tahiti.

Bond yields rose again and U.S. stocks stayed near record highs after reports indicated the economy is strengthening. The S&P 500 was near flat at 2,338, while the Dow Jones rose 0.2% and the Nasdaq rose 0.1%. Retail sales were stronger than expected and consumer inflation hit its highest level in years, giving the Federal Reserve more leeway to raise interest rates sooner. Treasury yields jumped after the data, and dividend-related sectors like utilities fell. Global markets were mixed, the dollar strengthened, and commodities were mostly steady with slight moves in oil, natural gas, and metals.

The passage is an email from Jean Munoz titled “IEP News 5/21” dated May 21, 2001, sharing “Today’s IEP news” and a list of related media items about California’s energy crisis. It includes coverage such as: California Controller Kathleen Connell releasing details of long-term power supply contracts and related tax and revenue issues; reports on Governor Gray Davis threatening actions against Reliant Energy to address price and supply problems; news on efforts to speed permitting of new power plants and expectations of shortages; Los Angeles Times reporting on allegations of power generators manipulating prices through unnecessary shutdowns; Associated Press reports on rising electricity bills, the “baseline” rate concept, and proposals for planned blackouts; and additional reporting and commentary on investigations into market conduct, conservation campaigns, and public polling reflecting worsening economic and electricity concerns.

The passage explains that soccer coaches must prepare players for non-ideal playing conditions and inspect fields before matches to identify hazards or determine if a field is unplayable. It covers how different surfaces and conditions affect ball behavior and player safety, including artificial turf heat, field crown effects, infill and crumb rubber issues, natural grass cutting and slippage, slopes and wet “greasy” fields, standing water, hard/soft dirt, clumps of grass, uneven surfaces, rain, snow, ice, wind, lightning, cold, dew, heat and humidity, and significant weather threats that can cause cancellations. It also addresses referee and assistant referee considerations, perimeter hazards (boards, drainage ditches, tracks, nearby people and fans), lighting and glare, equipment safety (secure goals, corner flags, nets, equipment tied to Laws of the Game), ball issues (extra or defective balls, wrong sizes, wet/waterlogged balls), and field markings (missing, multiple, or non-parallel lines). Finally, it provides coaching tips for using practice conditions to teach ball reactions, running pre-game routines including field inspection, discussing local rules and field status, and emphasizing proper clothing, hydration, and safety for both games and practices.

On May 23, 2017, NVIDIA Corporation held its 2017 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. Twelve directors were elected for one-year terms until the 2018 Annual Meeting, with voting results reported for each named director. Stockholders also approved, on an advisory basis, the compensation of named executive officers, and the advisory vote frequency was set to “1 Year” based on voting results. Finally, PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP was ratified as the independent registered accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 28, 2018. The report was signed by Rebecca Peters on May 30, 2017.

The passage describes reactions to a recent loss, including discussion of referee calls and missed or challenging officiating decisions. The speaker says the team did not play well enough to win, despite killing penalties and scoring on a shorthanded goal, and notes the opponent generated more offensively through better puck recovery and second chances. It also discusses concerns about key players being out of the lineup, including the need to adjust strategies in areas like power play effectiveness, goaltending, defensive matchups, boxing out, and forwards supporting puck movement. The speaker emphasizes that players must respond after the loss with the mindset that games can still be won despite injuries, and mentions possible lineup changes and the impact on younger players.

The passage discusses a first-time meeting with a young player, described as promising and great with the puck, with strong offensive instincts. It emphasizes developing young players, feeling ready for tonight’s game, and focusing on simple play despite unpredictable bounces from the previous game. It notes that both teams face similar conditions and advises making strong plays when getting the puck.

China’s first-quarter GDP rose 6.9%, exceeding expectations and the 2017 government target of 6.5%. The passage argues China’s GDP statistics face accuracy concerns, and similar issues are suggested for industrial production, which was unusually stable for much of the prior period. Industrial production rose to 7.6% in March 2017, which the passage links to export growth that turned positive in Q1 2017, and it suggests the uptick may be temporary or artificially supported. Retail sales and fixed-asset investment are described as not showing stronger sustained improvement, with continued growth attributed to state-owned enterprise capital expenditures and private investment still comparatively weaker. The passage concludes that durable, sustainable acceleration is unlikely given the lack of supporting symmetry across statistics.

The Senate rejected dueling Republican and Democratic stopgap funding proposals to end the government shutdown, which entered its second week and had already failed in five previous votes. In a 54-45 vote, the Senate did not advance a GOP-led bill to fund the government through late November; a Democratic-backed alternative failed 47-52. Democrats want health-care protections, including an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies expiring at year’s end. Republicans want a short-term measure to resume funding at current levels through Nov. 21 and say they are refusing to negotiate health-care changes, while Democrats accuse Republicans of holding up the process. The White House warned federal workers could be fired and back pay denied if the shutdown drags on, and House Speaker Mike Johnson said federal law requires back pay upon return.

The study compared REM sleep microstructure between controls, patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), and patients with REM sleep behavior disorder associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD+RBD), using video-polysomnography. Compared with controls, iRBD patients showed an increased phasic REM sleep proportion and higher REM sleep arousal index. Compared with controls and iRBD, PD+RBD patients showed reduced sawtooth wave (STW) density and shorter STW duration, with STW spectral characteristics shifting toward higher frequencies. Both patient groups also showed altered NREM/REM sleep transition duration, with transitions shortest in controls, longer in iRBD, and longest in PD+RBD. The study concludes that REM sleep anomalies in RBD extend beyond REM atonia loss and dream enactments to include broader microstructural changes.

The passage discusses modeling the mechanical behavior of honeycomb materials, including elastic moduli, plateau stresses, and failure mechanisms for both hexagonal and triangular honeycombs. It derives brittle fracture and fracture toughness for brittle (e.g., ceramic) honeycombs under tensile loading, using continuum crack-tip stress fields and equating applied moments to fracture moments. It then extends to out-of-plane elastic properties (Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratios, and shear moduli), and describes out-of-plane compressive strength via elastic buckling and plastic buckling, plus brittle fracture and brittle crushing/compression for out-of-plane loading. The speaker concludes by noting that these honeycomb models form the basis for later foam modeling and briefly previews applying similar ideas to honeycomb-like natural materials such as wood and cork.

The passage describes California’s recreational cannabis market rollout as highly complex and uncertain. BDS Analytics reported that 2018 dispensary sales through February were $339 million, below state expectations, and said initial projections may have been overly optimistic. Experts estimated that 85–90% of the previous industry remains unlicensed, and they attributed licensing delays mainly to municipal failures, noting that 85% of California cities and counties ban recreational marijuana retailers. The passage also says taxes raise prices across the supply chain, with some dispensaries facing effective tax rates near 80%, potentially encouraging reliance on the black market. It notes that earlier-legalization states like Colorado provided examples where tax revenue initially fell below projections before stabilizing.

The passage describes a player’s response to Paul being hit and then returning to score a goal. The speaker says they were concerned about Paul’s well-being, that his return was a lift for the team, and that scoring an overtime winner reflects his desire and leadership. The speaker also mentions recent tough years, expresses happiness about the chance to win the Stanley Cup, and highlights the importance of sharing the opportunity with teammates, including Paul. They conclude that the team feels good, needs to continue playing well, and is ready for another exciting game.

Cheryl Tickles appealed a Superior Court judgment affirming the Industrial Accident Board’s denial of her workers’ compensation claim for total disability benefits after she was injured on February 17, 1994. The Board found the injury was not compensable because it occurred before her workday began and there was no nexus between the employer’s premises and her presence; the Superior Court agreed, stating her fall was during a personal errand without apparent connection to her employment.

The Delaware Supreme Court held that Tickles was injured at her place of employment because, under Delaware’s “going and coming” rule and its employer-premises exception, an employer’s parking lot counts as premises and Tickles’ accident occurred there. The Court further held that the injury was within the course of employment because Tickles used an employee-only ATM on the employer’s premises in preparation for her workday shortly before her scheduled start time, making it an incidental preparatory action.

The Supreme Court reversed the Superior Court’s judgment and remanded the matter for further proceedings consistent with its opinion.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture improvements, including a unified L1 cache and shared-memory design with up to 64 KB L1 cache and increased L2 capacity, which simplifies programming and boosts performance per CUDA core. It details Turing Tensor Cores with added INT8/INT4 precision modes for inferencing and FP16 support, enabling real-time deep learning features via NGX Neural Services (e.g., DLSS, InPainting, AI Super Rez, AI Slow-Mo). It also explains data center features and memory/display enhancements such as higher video decode support, improved MPS, and the shift to GDDR6 with redesigned interfaces, plus increased cache and compression yielding higher effective bandwidth.

For rendering, the passage covers ray tracing through RT Cores, hybrid rendering (ray tracing plus rasterization), denoising, and BVH acceleration, aiming for real-time ray tracing. It further discusses VRS (variable rate shading) and Texture Space Shading (TSS) as mechanisms to control shading rate for improved performance and image quality, plus multi-view rendering and bindless resource access. Moody’s said Saudi Arabia’s fiscal position remains strong, but high oil dependency is a key credit challenge. The case involves a claim against the city of Marquette for personal injuries allegedly caused by poultry crates obstructing a sidewalk. The court directed a verdict for the defendant based on a charter provision (subd. 16, §1, chap. 7, Act No. 409, Local Acts 1895) stating the city is never liable for damages resulting from a person’s neglect to keep sidewalks clear of obstructions. The court held this charter provision exempts the city despite general state statutes, is not repealed by a later local act (Act No. 423, Local Acts 1899), and is not invalid as class legislation. Judgment for the defendant was affirmed.

The passage argues that forex trading should be avoided and lists 12 reasons, including high leverage, difficult prediction due to many influencing factors, extreme volatility, and large effects from small random market movements. It also cites the 24-hour nature of the market leading to overtrading, limited effectiveness of risk management, counterparty risk from forex providers (including possible insolvency), and the presence of scams and fraud in broker markets. Additional reasons include few strategies being properly backtested—especially those that promise large gains—and that only small price moves can wipe out leveraged traders, making survival of the learning curve unlikely.

Lake Havasu City is described as the hottest place in Arizona, reaching 128 degrees on June 29, 1994—the highest temperature ever recorded in the state. The passage also attributes Lake Havasu City’s heat to a lack of nearby irrigation and agricultural activity compared with other places along the river.

The passage discusses preparation and focus for a Stanley Cup Final, with the speaker saying distractions from past games should be set aside and the team should prepare for the first shift and play hard. CNN reports that advisers close to Donald Trump were in constant communication during the campaign with Russians known to U.S. intelligence. U.S. officials say President-elect Trump and President Barack Obama were briefed on details of extensive communications between suspected Russian operatives and people associated with the Trump campaign and Trump business. Officials said the frequency and proximity to Trump “raised a red flag,” and investigators intercepted the communications during routine intelligence collection targeting Russian officials and other known Russian nationals. Investigators have not determined the intent, and there were also intercepted communications in which Russian officials discussed believing they had special access to Trump, which could have been exaggerated. The communications were included in post-election briefings on Russian meddling, and the FBI and intelligence agencies continue to determine motives, including whether Trump associates coordinated with Russian intelligence operatives regarding releases of damaging information about the Hillary Clinton campaign.

The passage describes Brennen v. Collins, a mandamus proceeding regarding a case transferred from chancery to the law side of the court. The circuit court had transferred a suit that began in chancery because of lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, and plaintiffs were allowed to file a declaration on the law side. Defendants then moved to dismiss the action at law, arguing they were not properly served in Livingston County as required for actions at law. The trial court denied the motion, but the appellate court held that the denial was improper because the transfer statute did not confer jurisdiction over defendants not served with process in the county where the law action was commenced. It further held that defendants did not waive their right to object by appearing and answering in the chancery case or by counsel’s remarks during proceedings about filing the declaration. The appellate court granted the writ and required dismissal for lack of personal jurisdiction over the defendants.

The passage discusses transformation photos of a woman identified as Folake, a survivor of HIV/AIDS in Nigeria whose photos were shared by the United States Embassy in Nigeria to mark World AIDS Day and to show that HIV/AIDS is not necessarily a death sentence. It states that Folake received antiretroviral treatment at a CDC/IVHN-supported site in Lagos (NIMR) that saved her life. The lecture introduces an advanced class focused on how proof systems in computer science evolved, from the mid-1980s to today. The instructor explains course logistics (weekly meetings, requirements for scribing and a mid-course problem set) and emphasizes reading material before and after lectures.

The discussion begins with proof systems and contrasts classical proofs with developments in cryptography-related proof ideas, especially zero-knowledge proofs and the resulting shift toward interactive proof systems. The class defines NP as languages whose membership can be verified by polynomial-time verifiers given a witness. It then defines interactive proofs (IP), highlighting two key components: interaction and verifier randomization, which allow soundness to hold with small error probability. A Shamir result is mentioned: interactive proofs can verify any PSPACE computation with a polynomial-time verifier (IP = PSPACE is stated as the takeaway).

The lecture then presents the sum-check protocol as an important interactive proof. The protocol aims to verify that, given a multivariate polynomial of bounded degree, the sum of its values over an m-dimensional grid equals a claimed value β. The verifier checks low-degree conditions for progressively defined polynomials while the protocol reduces the verification problem one variable at a time via random choices. Completeness is straightforward (honest provers are accepted with probability 1). Soundness is argued using the fact that incorrect polynomials can coincide with correct ones on only a limited number of field points, leading to rejection except with small probability controlled by the field size. The lecture concludes by describing the protocol’s communication/runtime characteristics and noting that applications will follow after a break.

Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy (SUDEP) is a non-traumatic, non-drowning death in people with epilepsy and is described as a leading cause of premature death. The highest SUDEP risk is in patients whose generalized tonic-clonic seizures are not controlled by medication, and poor control of generalized tonic-clonic seizures is identified as the strongest risk factor. Convulsive seizures during sleep and prone positioning are major risk factors; a meta-analysis reports that about 70% of SUDEP occurs after nocturnal generalized tonic-clonic seizures, with many cases occurring in the prone position. Central apnea and autonomic instability are cited as key risk factors, and prone position is said to blunt arousal responses and reduce heart rate variability. The passage argues that SUDEP prevention requires rapid, autonomous intervention during a critical time window, and that existing options are insufficient.  

The study aims to develop “Korus,” a night-time seizure management system centered on an autonomous body repositioning mattress after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The mattress is described as a twin XL inflatable, sensor-equipped system using an 8-by-4 array of inflatable cells, pressure-sensing sheets, networking via Power over Ethernet, and a Random Forest model to detect four body positions (prone, supine, left, right). An iOS/Android app visualizes position and controls cell inflation. In 18 normative control subjects (10 tested extensively), cells reached 14” inflation within 7 seconds, prone-to-recovery from prone was achieved with 100% success in manual tests, and prone detection accuracy was reported as 96.8% over 10 patients. Overall position recognition accuracy was 92.4%, with errors mainly involving side position detection. The passage concludes that Korus could potentially monitor and autonomously deliver intervention to help prevent SUDEP.

The PGA848 output-stage difference amplifier uses a 6.67 kΩ feedback resistor between the output and the inverting input, with DA_IN– and DA_IN+ providing external access to the inputs. Designers can add external capacitors in parallel with the internal resistors for noise-filtering/noise-shaping and can implement customized attenuating gains. Internal resistor network accuracy is 0.01% or better (yielding CMRR of 80 dB or better), but mismatched leakage currents can degrade CMRR; internal resistors also have ±15% absolute variation that affects custom gains or noise filters. The DA_IN– and DA_IN+ pins must not be treated as outputs or used to source/sink current due to risk of permanent damage from excessive currents through the feedback resistors. The device has a single functional mode, operating when input-stage supplies exceed ±4.5 V (9 V) and output-stage supplies exceed ±2.25 V (4.5 V).

Harav Aaron Brafman, zt”l, a long-time Menahel of Yeshiva Derech Ayson–Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, died on Erev Shabbos, 19 Av, at age 73. He was remembered for his dedication to his talmidim and to the needs of the klal, and for instilling confidence in his students to live as bnei Torah. Born in 1944 in Williamsburg, he later moved to Crown Heights, studied at Yeshivah Torah Vodaath for over 20 years (including as a Maggid Shiur), and was closely influenced by several prominent rabbis. He married Susie Schwartz in 1964 and served as a Maggid Shiur in Torah Vodaath’s mesivta in his mid-20s. In 1970, he became Menahel of the Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, where he formed close relationships with students, taught regularly, delivered mussar vaadim, and maintained a tzedakah fund for needy community members. His levayah was held at the yeshiva on Friday afternoon, and after Shabbos the mittah was flown to Eretz Yisrael for additional hespeidim and burial in Eretz HaChaim cemetery in Beit Shemesh. He is survived by his wife, siblings, children, and many grandchildren.

The passage describes the European Space Agency’s 2013 Gaia space observatory and its work cataloging over a billion astronomical objects to build a precise 3D map of the Milky Way. Using Gaia’s initial data release, a University of Toronto team led by Jason Hunt combined Gaia data with measurements from the Radial Velocity Experiment (RAVE) to calculate the Sun’s orbit speed around the Milky Way and to refine the Sun’s distance from the galactic center. The team used stars observed by both Gaia and RAVE to study their orbital speeds and identified an apparent distribution linked to stars on “chaotic, halo-type orbits.” They then combined this information with proper motion calculations of Sagittarius A* after correcting for its motion relative to background objects to triangulate the Earth’s distance from the galactic center. They derived a refined distance estimate of 7.6 to 8.2 kiloparsecs (about 24,788 to 26,745 light years), and they anticipate that future Gaia data releases will further improve the precision of these measurements.

The passage describes a rotorcraft (drone) landing device for landing at a destination without requiring the drone to have an image-capturing function. It includes a landing portion, a position recognition portion that recognizes the drone’s position relative to the landing portion, and a remote control portion that remotely controls the drone based on recognition results. The landing device may use an opening/closing mechanism that covers the landing portion when closed and exposes it when open, and may include movable members that change posture during landing to prevent the package from falling and help position it at the center. Position recognition can be performed using multiple infrared cameras on the landing portion, and remote control can be supported by distance measuring for descending speed and by matching drone identification information to permit landing. The embodiment also details a delivery system with warehouse and home control devices and a management system that manages routes and drone assignments, switching from GPS-based autonomous navigation to remote control near the destination, after which the drone releases the package and returns. Various modifications are described, including adaptations for different weather conditions, integration with residential equipment, adding weather observation and emergency landing use, portable and temporary use, fall response, drone approach warning, battery and black-box related features, changes to takeoff procedures, route and beacon infrastructure, and counter-drone measures against terrorism.

Enrique Marquez Jr., 25, of Riverside, California, is accused of purchasing the assault rifles used in the San Bernardino terrorist attack and has agreed to plead guilty to federal charges. In his plea, Marquez admits he was paid by Syed Rizwan Farook for the rifles used to kill 14 people and injure 22 others in December 2015, and that he conspired with Farook in 2011 and 2012 to attack Riverside City College and commuter traffic on a Southern California freeway. Prosecutors say there is no evidence Marquez participated in the attack or had advance knowledge of it, though he acknowledges he was a “straw buyer” when purchasing two rifles. Marquez is expected to enter his guilty pleas Thursday and faces up to 25 years in federal prison.

Bitcoin’s price fell below $8,000 on Friday before recovering slightly after dropping Thursday following new statements from Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley. Jaitley said India would take measures to eliminate crypto use in illegitimate financing or as part of the payment system. Analysts quoted in the passage suggest India’s crypto market could grow despite its current small size, and they describe government steps such as setting up a committee to study cryptocurrencies while awaiting its report.

Venezuelans in the U.S. under the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program asked the Supreme Court to keep in place a federal judge’s order temporarily barring the Trump administration from ending their protected status. Lawyers said UCLA law professor Ahilan Arulanantham argued the order “restored the status quo” and would prevent “massive injuries” affecting challengers and their loved ones, including American children.

The TPS program, created by Congress in 1990, allows the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate countries whose citizens may remain and work in the U.S. when they cannot safely return due to conditions such as natural disasters or armed conflict. Venezuela was designated under TPS in 2021, redesignated in 2023 to allow more applicants, and extended through October 2026. After the Trump administration took office, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended both the 2023 designation and the 2025 extension.

A federal judge (Edward Chen) temporarily barred Noem from ending the protections on March 31. The Supreme Court later put Chen’s March 31 order on hold, with Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissenting. After further proceedings, Chen issued a final ruling on Sept. 5 concluding Noem acted unlawfully in terminating the 2023 designation and its extension. The appeals court and government then sought Supreme Court intervention to pause that Sept. 5 ruling, arguing the Court’s earlier stay order required it. The challengers argued the Supreme Court’s limited stay did not foreclose further litigation to final judgment and that Chen’s final ruling relied on different posture, statutory authority, and a more developed record.

The passage describes how inclusive education for children with disabilities has gained international attention and is supported by global agreements such as the Salamanca Declaration (1994) and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2006), with inclusive education defined as providing quality education that meets every child’s educational needs. It explains Myanmar’s legal focus on equal access to education for persons with disabilities and presents a study aimed at examining actual inclusive education practices in Yangon, particularly for children with visual impairment. In Yangon, children receive primary education in special schools and from secondary education onward are educated with non-disabled students in regular schools, forming what the study calls “limited inclusive education in phase.” Informants reported benefits of special schools, including Braille education, life skills, supplementary study time, practical training (e.g., computer skills), and a sense of security, while regular schools were valued for social and communication skills and empathy-building for students without disabilities. The study also identifies limitations, including weak communication and cooperation between special and regular schools, regular schools’ reliance on special schools’ expertise, limited interaction and close relationships between students with and without disabilities, and a lack of awareness among parents in Myanmar about educational opportunities and special schools. The authors conclude that implementation challenges require improved teacher exchange, inclusion-focused programs for students, and consideration of broader needs beyond educational needs alone, while noting that countries—especially low-income ones—must adapt models to their resources and context.

The passage describes a system and methods for neuromuscular stimulation that decode a user’s neural activity in real time to determine intended desired movements and translate them into electrical stimulation signals delivered to a target. It explains prior limitations of neurostimulation that do not respond to volitional control, and outlines a “neural bridge” approach for restoring movement in damaged neuromuscular pathways or controlling electronic devices. The disclosed methods include measuring neural activity, removing artifacts, extracting features (such as signal amplitude, wavelet-scale amplitude, or firing rate), using decoders to identify desired movements and movement effort, and using outputs with a body state observer and encoding algorithms to generate continuously updated, potentially multiplexed stimulation patterns. The target may include body limbs or devices such as prosthetic limbs, a wheelchair, a computer cursor, an exoskeleton, a remote control device, or an external robotic arm; compound and rhythmic movements can be supported. Drawings and examples are discussed, including an experiment where a paralyzed participant controlled discrete and rhythmic finger movements using cortical activity, trained decoders, and a neuromuscular electrical stimulation sleeve, reporting accuracies and sensitivity/specificity metrics. The disclosure also covers electrode stimulation details, training procedures, and use of various neural recording techniques.

The passage describes how to use the ADS9803’s SMPL_SYNC signal to synchronize multiple ADCs: all devices share SMPL_CLK and SMPL_SYNC with identical external delays, and a positive SMPL_SYNC pulse centered around the falling edge of SMPL_CLK synchronizes the ADCs once after power-up, sampling-clock restart, or device reset. The SYNC signal resets internal analog channel selection logic and aligns FCLKOUT, ensuring that multiple ADCs using the same sampling clock sample the same respective input channel at the same time. It also discusses using the internal reference with a 10µF bypass capacitor on REFIO for best performance, or connecting an external reference and disabling the internal reference via SPI register configuration or the SDI/EXTREF pin. The passage further covers interface modes (2-lane/4-lane, SDR/DDR), data output structure, data clock/frame clock behavior, data randomization via XOR options, data averaging modes, test patterns for debugging, device reset/power-down, initialization sequencing, daisy-chain SPI configuration for multiple devices, and register access and field descriptions, followed by brief application information and other non-spec informational sections.

The passage describes a study that evaluates COVID-19’s mortality impact in India by estimating how many excess deaths are attributable to SARS-CoV-2. It notes that official excess-death estimates in India are contested because deaths are not routinely attributed to SARS-CoV-2 in available data sources, and official COVID death reporting may underestimate SARS-CoV-2 deaths due to low testing and diagnosis. The study uses WHO-compliant verbal autopsy surveys administered to next-of-kin, coding causes with ICD-10 (including SARS-CoV-2-related codes U07 and U08). It draws living and deceased samples from the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey (CPHS) for 2018–2021 and applies statistical adjustments for over- and under-inclusive death reporting, delayed reporting to CPHS, and non-response to verbal autopsies. Methods include estimating death rates and excess death rates by cause, examining timing across India’s COVID waves and lockdown period, and analyzing heterogeneity by age, sex, rural/urban residence, and income. Results report that SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 17.93% of all deaths during the pandemic and 33.15% of excess deaths, with spikes occurring around the lockdown and especially after wave 2, while limitations include potential misclassification from ICD-10 coding (e.g., vaping-related disorders included in U07) and the need for imperfect representativeness corrections.

The passage describes the 3-4 defense and its use in pro and college football. It defines the 3-4 as three down linemen, four linebackers, and four defensive backs, with outside linebackers creating matchups and a “mirror” alignment. It outlines personnel needs, including bigger, stronger defensive linemen using a two-gap approach, hybrid outside linebackers, linebackers commonly named Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack, and a secondary with two corners and two safeties. Strengths include pressure from multiple places, such as blitzing both outside linebackers to create a five-man rush, and coverage options involving two safeties. Weaknesses include issues against modern spread offenses when outside linebackers must cover, leading to a lighter box that favors offenses, plus challenges against trips formations and slot receivers. The passage also lists common 3-4 blitzes (“Weakside Edge Blitz” and “Crossfire” blitz) and coverages (“Cover 4” and “Cover 2 Man”). Finally, it names coaches and teams associated with the 3-4, including Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick (with Lawrence Taylor and two Super Bowls), and the coaching tree leading to Nick Saban and Kirby Smart, with various championships mentioned.

Using shaders alone, rendering a single frame takes 51 ms (~20 FPS). Moving ray tracing to RT Cores concurrently reduces frame time to 20 ms (50 FPS), and using Tensor Cores with DLSS further reduces it to 12 ms (~83 FPS). The RTX 3080 using Ampere architecture is described as rendering a frame in 6.7 ms (150 FPS) via shader cores, RT cores, and tensor cores. The passage also explains ray-traced motion blur, describing how GA10x RT Core hardware accelerates motion blur by improving BVH traversal and adding an Interpolate Triangle Position unit, which enables up to 8x faster motion blur rendering than Turing. GA10x Tensor Cores are described as improving matrix operation throughput, adding support for sparsity, and enabling DL data types like TF32 and BF16. The passage further discusses GA10x memory (GDDR6X), RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression with DirectStorage, NVDEC/NVENC for hardware video decode/encode, and performance claims for GA10x GPUs in rendering, AI, and data center workloads.

The lecture reviews quiz performance, noting it was difficult, and outlines today’s plan for extending full factorial experimental design to general \(k\) factors. It explains how factorial designs produce coded regression terms using contrasts, including main effects and interaction effects, and how interaction columns can be generated by multiplying factor columns (e.g., \(AB\), \(ABC\)). It then contrasts the “contrast approach” with fitting a regression model using an \(x\) matrix that includes interaction product terms.

A key focus is determining whether estimated effects are significant using ANOVA/F-tests based on sums of squared deviations derived from contrasts or regression coefficients. Residuals are discussed as having sources from replication noise and from lack of model adequacy (e.g., missing higher-order curvature). The lecture describes checking residual plots for trends, using center points to test for curvature via an ANOVA lack-of-fit style test, and the need for replicates to estimate error variance. It provides examples including a break-forming 2\(^2\) design and another example where lack of fit is not evidenced, leading to retention of only significant terms.

Finally, it introduces nuisance factors and how experimental design can control or randomize/block against them, using randomization, replication, and blocking (including confounding with interaction terms). This motivates fractional factorial designs, where not all corner points are tested to reduce the number of experiments while accepting certain confounding.

Preterm birth (PTB) complications, including low birth weight (LBW), are a leading cause of neonatal death in the first week, and identifying vulnerable neonates is difficult in resource-limited settings. LBW (<2.50 kg) includes preterm (<37 completed weeks) and small for gestational age, but many babies are not weighed or do not have accurate gestational age assessment due to limitations in equipment and trained staff. Foot length has been proposed as a proxy measure for LBW and PTB; a prior systematic review suggested <7.7 cm had reasonable accuracy for identifying LBW but highlighted heterogeneity and limitations in gestational age reference methods.

The Neofoot study in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea, was a prospective single-arm diagnostic accuracy study to assess whether newborn foot length could identify LBW or PTB in health facilities and community settings and to compare measurements by trained volunteers versus a researcher. Reference standards included birth weight measured twice within 72 hours using an electronic scale and gestational age determined from obstetric due dates using last menstrual period and/or ultrasound at the first antenatal visit. The index test was right foot length measured within 72 hours using a clear plastic ruler and cardboard box setup, with two measurements averaged. Nine volunteers received a half-day training session.

Among 342 newborns enrolled, 21.1% were LBW and 7.3% were preterm. The optimal foot length cut-off for classifying LBW was <7.7 cm (sensitivity 84.7%, specificity 69.6%), and for PTB it was also <7.7 cm (sensitivity 88.0%, specificity 61.8%). For paired researcher–volunteer measurements available for 123 babies, agreement limits were -0.55 to +0.70 cm, with 7.3% of pairs outside these limits. The authors conclude newborn foot length was a simple and feasible method to identify LBW and PTB babies, with implications for research and practice in settings like PNG.

Dubai’s Iran-related parliament gave initial approval to a bill to boost spending on Iran’s missile program and the Revolutionary Guards in retaliation for new U.S. sanctions. The bill was approved by lawmakers and framed as countering U.S. actions, following U.S. legislation signed by President Donald Trump in August. Iran says its missile program does not violate a UN resolution tied to the 2015 nuclear deal, and the bill would require strategies to counter U.S. human-rights violations and to support those affected by sanctions. It would allocate over $260 million each to the ballistic missile program and the Quds Force. The bill requires a second parliamentary vote and then approval by a clerical body to become law.

MSPM0G MCUs provide five power operating modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—with RUN using an active CPU. Peripheral interrupts can wake the device from SLEEP, STOP, or STANDBY to RUN, while SHUTDOWN disables the internal core regulator and wake is only possible via NRST, SWD, or a logic level match on certain IOs. RUN/SLEEP/STOP/STANDBY include configurable policy options (e.g., RUN.x) for performance versus power tradeoffs. The devices use two power domains: PD1 (CPU, memories, high performance peripherals) and PD0 (low speed, low power peripherals), where PD1 is always powered in RUN and SLEEP but disabled in other modes, and PD0 remains powered in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY, with both domains disabled in SHUTDOWN. The passage also describes how functionality may be enabled/disabled or retained across operating modes, and introduces related sections on the PMU, clock module, DMA, events, flash, SRAM, GPIO, IOMUX, and multiple peripherals (e.g., ADC, timers, communication interfaces, watchdogs, RTC, and security/crypto features).

New clock gating enables entire clock trees to be shut off quickly, reducing dynamic power even when only part of a chip is idle or when idleness is very short. For Blackwell, memory power management focuses on GDDR7’s fast-wakeup clocking, and the entire memory clock tree can now be gated. A new voltage rail provides separate power to GPU cores and the memory system, allowing independent voltage control and improved optimization per workload. Separate rails also support shutting down unused chip portions during brief idle periods to reduce leakage power, and rail-gated states can be entered at frame granularity, aiding battery gaming and creation. The GPU cores can be turned off during GPU idling to lower power.

Spouses may draft a Berliner Testament (“Berlin will”) appointing each other as sole heirs and their children as final heirs. This can provide financial security to the surviving spouse because children do not inherit until both parents have died. However, Berliner Testaments have pitfalls, including a strong binding effect that generally prevents unilaterally changing dispositions and can leave a spouse’s new partner empty-handed even after relationship breakdown; provisions also cannot be amended unilaterally, even after one spouse dies. The passage also notes that tax allowances for inheritance tax should be considered, since making one spouse sole heir may exceed allowances, while distributing the estate among several heirs can use allowances more effectively. It advises informing oneself about the legal consequences and consulting experienced succession-law lawyers.

Delta executives said they expect premium revenue from first class and other higher-priced cabins to overtake coach cabin sales next year. In the last quarter, Delta reported premium cabin ticket revenue rose 9% year over year to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin ticket revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. Delta’s CEO, Ed Bastian, said he has seen no sign of premium-travel demand slowing down.

The passage describes an effort to forecast fatal opioid-related overdose events in U.S. locations to support targeted interventions under resource constraints. It notes that the U.S. opioid overdose epidemic has caused over 450,000 deaths in the past eight years, with more than 80,000 fatal opioid-related overdoses in 2022. The authors emphasize that spatiotemporal patterns have shifted over time and vary by geography, motivating short-term, fine-scale forecasting. They argue that population-level prediction using aggregated data may be more feasible for many public health agencies.  

The study focuses on census-tract-level, annual forecasts in Cook County, Illinois (2015–2022; 1328 tracts) and Massachusetts (2001–2021; 1620 tracts). They compare multiple forecasting models, including heuristic baselines, statistical models, and neural networks, using both error-based metrics (RMSE, MAE) and a new intervention-focused metric called “best possible reach” (BPR), expressed as %BPR. BPR evaluates how many observed fatalities occur in the top K tracts recommended for intervention, given a limited budget (K=100).  

Across both locations, results vary by metric, but the authors report that %BPR can lead to different model rankings and intervention recommendations than RMSE/MAE. They also report that (weighted) historical average baselines performed competitively. Limitations include that findings are based on only two jurisdictions and that BPR depends on the chosen intervention budget K and does not directly prioritize rate of change. The passage concludes that intervention-aware metrics like %BPR and inclusion of tuned simple baselines are important for future evaluations, and that the authors provide open-source software and processed data resources.

The passage describes how traders use the Relative Strength Index (RSI) in CFD trading. RSI is a momentum oscillator on a 0–100 scale used to assess whether an asset may be overvalued or undervalued, commonly by identifying overbought (typically above 70) and oversold (typically below 30) conditions, and it can also signal possible trend reversals or corrective pullbacks. It explains CFD trading as profiting from the difference between an underlying asset’s value at contract start and end, without owning the asset, and notes CFD trading is zero-sum. It outlines RSI-based strategy approaches, including mean-reversion using overbought/oversold thresholds, day trading with shorter time frames and more extreme thresholds (e.g., 15 for oversold and 85 for overbought), trend-following using momentum/regime signals, and using RSI divergences (bullish and bearish) as potential signals. The passage emphasizes personalizing RSI thresholds based on asset class, time frame, and market trend, combining RSI with other indicators, and validating strategies through backtesting. It also stresses risk management in CFD trading, including accounting for commissions, slippage, and taxes, and using stop-loss orders to limit losses.

The passage describes efforts to “hack” the human mind and body. It notes that people have long used substances like caffeine (which blocks adenosine) and nicotine (which mimics acetylcholine) to improve mental focus. It also discusses attempts to develop a “memorization pill” led by Tim Tully, who searches for people with strong memorization abilities and plans to sequence their genomes to guide potential drug development; it mentions genetically engineered fruit flies with photographic memories using CREB activators. The passage further describes a controversial project to identify genes involved in intelligence for possible genetic enhancement and mentions research into deep brain stimulation and new devices that both adjust neuron firing and monitor brain activity to detect abnormal states and respond with electrical pulses, though it is still in development.

The chapter explains how the host environment meets requirements to call the AGESA™ software through the host BIOS interface and binary image mechanisms. It describes establishing a valid stack, preparing and filling standard header data, inserting a bridge procedure before AGESA calls, locating the binary image entry point, and using the AMD dispatcher. It also outlines call-out routing, including implementing a call-out router in the host environment that translates function numbers to host call-out procedures, with function definitions found in AMD.H. Dependencies such as the 32-bit protected mode flat addressing model and stack availability are noted.

The passage further discusses UEFI execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) and related build and platform environment setup, including configuration options and required host/environment integrations. It describes PEI phase procedures using two PEIM modules for processor and memory initialization, publication of PPIs/HOBs with associated GUIDs, and reset coordination. It outlines DXE responsibilities for late initialization and table generation, plus examples for host environment wrapper/reference files and build control files. Later sections describe stack initialization macros and stackless native assembly procedures for early and post-cache-as-RAM stack handling, along with several AGESA service call outlines (e.g., AmdCreateStruct, AmdReleaseStruct, and other helper functions) and required/optional host call-outs such as AgesaAllocateBuffer and related buffer deallocation behavior.

Peter Fassbender, former Langley City mayor and former Liberal MLA, said he has been approached about returning to municipal politics but has not made a final decision. He plans to decide by the end of the month or early next month, and would run for mayor only if he believes he can contribute to the community and it is best for him and his wife. The passage also notes his prior service as mayor (elected in 2005, 2008, and 2011), his provincial roles after being elected MLA in 2013, and that two incumbent Langley City councillors have already declared for the mayoralty.

The passage expresses gratitude and solemn commitment to national duties, describing the world’s and the United States’ difficult circumstances. It says the country previously prospered under republican institutions and peace with other nations, while the transition to distress is attributed not to wrongdoing or errors in U.S. councils. It argues the U.S. maintained neutral obligations with impartiality but was still harmed by the injustice and violence of belligerent powers. It outlines principles for preserving peace, neutrality, constitutional government, state rights, religious liberty, civil rights and the freedom of the press, economic public spending, debt repayment, limits on standing military forces, support for militia, and promotion of agriculture, commerce, science, information, and benevolent plans for indigenous conversion. The speaker also draws on predecessors’ examples and places confidence in fellow-citizens, their representatives, and guidance attributed to God.

The Supreme Court agreed to review a Texas man’s criminal case involving his plea agreement waiver of his right to appeal. The man, who pleaded guilty to aiding and abetting wire fraud in 2024, received a 51-month prison sentence, three years of supervised release, and more than $235,000 in restitution. His challenge concerns a sentencing condition requiring him to take mental health medications prescribed by his doctors. After the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal based on the waiver, he argued the dismissal conflicted with other circuits and noted that the outcome could differ if heard in the 9th Circuit. The justices will likely hear arguments early next year, with a decision by summer.

The case involves a real estate commission claim by brokers against their principals, George W. Thuro and Della B. Thuro. The trial court directed a verdict for the brokers, and the defendants appealed.

The principals had employed the brokers to find purchasers for real estate and personal property. A contract was signed by Della B. Thuro and Mrs. Charles Tallman while George W. Thuro was absent from the state and did not give written authority for Della B. Thuro to sign his name. Afterward, the Tallmans took possession, made payments, then abandoned the contract and the principals repossessed the property.

The court held that the principal could not defeat a broker’s right to commission by refusing to be bound by or sign a contract with a purchaser produced by the broker, and that several disputes about authority, ratification, and abandonment were immaterial to commission liability. It also found no prejudicial variance between the brokers’ pleadings and proof regarding which Tallman parties were bound, because the action was for commission rather than enforcement of the contract. Refusal of requested jury instructions on immaterial issues and overruling motions to strike were found to be no error or harmless.

The judgment for the plaintiffs was affirmed.
