A Yankees scout, Matt Hyde, was amazed by rookie Cam Schlittler’s “unbelievable” performance in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card series against the Red Sox. Schlittler shut out Boston through eight innings, struck out 12, and allowed five hits without walking anyone, becoming the first MLB pitcher to pitch eight scoreless innings with no walks and 12 strikeouts. Hyde attended the game and called the performance “surreal,” especially against Boston. Schlittler was drafted by the Yankees in the seventh round of the 2022 draft and debuted in July, and the Yankees will move on after the game.

A small Montecito Union School District in Santa Barbara County settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, ages 65 and 68, who alleged the district’s former principal molested them in the 1970s. The brothers had sought $35 million, and the settlement is about 40% of the district’s 2025–26 budget, though the district did not disclose payment terms or timing. The district admitted no liability, said it had no insurance coverage for the period of the alleged abuse, and cited financial vulnerability from potential trial awards. The case was filed in 2022 and alleged misconduct by Stanford Kerr, who died in 2013 without facing criminal charges. A third plaintiff previously settled for $1 million. The settlement drew attention to state law Assembly Bill 218, which removed the statute of limitations for certain public-agency child sexual abuse claims, as well as legislative efforts to restore limitations timeframes. A final hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19 to confirm payment receipt.

The passage describes plantar pressure mapping’s use in clinical diagnostics, sports science, and rehabilitation, and notes that downstream analyses depend on data quality because plantar pressure datasets can contain outliers caused by participant, procedural, and technical issues. It discusses Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) as a method for detecting statistically significant deviations in aligned pressure images, while explaining that SPM requires spatial alignment to avoid misleading results. It proposes comparing SPM with a novel explainable machine learning approach that uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) with SHAP for interpretability. The study details a workflow using multi-center plantar pressure data, expert labeling of valid and outlier categories, synthetic outlier augmentation, registration and non-parametric cluster-based SPM testing, CNN training with cross-validation, and nested evaluation including human-centered semantic differential surveys. Results show that the ML approach outperformed SPM on classification metrics (F1-score and Matthews Correlation Coefficient) and both approaches’ explanations were rated positively by expert participants, with no statistically significant differences across semantic differential attributes. The conclusion states both approaches are promising for detecting and categorizing technical/procedural plantar pressure anomalies, emphasizing the importance of evaluating not only predictive performance but also user perception of explanations.

The passage says that common bear and bull market definitions based on fixed percentage thresholds (e.g., 20% for bear markets and rallies, 10% for corrections, 5% dips, and 30%+ crashes) lack a rational basis and hard data showing these percentages are significant. It argues that knowing whether broad indexes meet these traditional definitions does not meaningfully help investors manage risk or decide when to deploy capital. The author proposes alternative “secular” definitions: a secular bull market is a typically 10–20 year period driven by broad economic shifts that supports rising corporate revenues and earnings, decreasing volatility, and investors’ increasing willingness to pay for earnings; a secular bear market is the opposite, with increased volatility, more frequent cyclical rallies and retreats, an economically challenging environment, and investors’ decreasing willingness to pay for earnings. The passage also emphasizes earnings multiple expansion or contraction (rising or falling price-to-earnings ratios) as key drivers, providing an example that much of the 1982–2000 bull market gains were attributable to rising price-to-earnings ratios rather than earnings growth alone.

The passage describes STAT’s London “Pharmalittle” headlines, including that 100% branded-drug import tariffs threatened by President Trump were delayed and will not start as previously said. It adds that a White House official said the administration will begin preparing tariffs for companies that do not build in the U.S. or do not make a drug pricing agreement, without a new timeline provided. It also says drug company executives are receiving near-daily calls from White House staff and senior agency figures, as part of efforts to secure deals ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, citing requests involving Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and AstraZeneca. The rest lists other drug-industry and biotech updates.

The passage describes defensive fundamentals for the High Post Split Offense, which consists of a high post split followed by down screens. It emphasizes that defenders must be trained to guard the high post with and without the ball, defend initial guard splits, counter down screens (“pin downs”) and disrupt screens set by a big player against a smaller defender. The defense is outlined in phases: (1) defending the high post split by sagging off in front of the post to force cutters wide and prevent handoffs and drives, then stepping up to jam the high post; (2) defending down screens using show-and-recover to avoid switching and to force shooters wide, with recovery into pass-denial positions; and (3) additional “SOS” disruption strategies that first aggressively pressure the ballhandler toward the near sideline checkpoint, use snuggle and strike denial positions, and include switching, trapping on passes, and trapping actions on down screens. Further matching-up, trapping (including wing trap and pass-out-of-trap rotations), and post-trap scenarios are also described with specific defensive rotations and pass-denial objectives.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8% stake in Dubai-based Abraaj, an embattled private equity firm in dispute with investors over alleged misuse of investor money. The potential sale, considered for some time, has become more urgent amid Deutsche Bank’s restructuring plans to cut at least 7,000 jobs and its closure of its Dubai equities research unit. Deutsche declined to comment, and Abraaj said it could not comment on matters related to shareholders. A source said Deutsche previously sought a valuation about two years ago, and that any sale now would likely be at a large discount. The stake’s valuation is difficult because Abraaj has not disclosed its debt. Abraaj is also facing an investigation by four investors, has denied wrongdoing, and has been reviewing its corporate structure, including job cuts, management changes, suspending new investments, and restructuring capital commitments.

The passage discusses the metaverse as a technology emerging from science fiction and introduced through platforms such as Second Life, Roblox, Pokemon Go, and Fortnite. It highlights educational benefits including interactive, immersive experiences, practical engagement with difficult concepts, personalized learning, and a risk-free environment for simulations and practice. Limitations are also described, including challenges for teacher monitoring, user mental effort for augmented reality, lack of guaranteed learning differences with virtual reality, and requirements such as reliable infrastructure, network connectivity, device access, and educator training. The passage presents a study aiming to determine teachers’ knowledge, perceptions of metaverse advantages and disadvantages, suitable educational domains, and timing for classroom use. The study surveyed 333 teachers in Türkiye using a 28-question questionnaire. Findings report limited but existing metaverse experience, moderate knowledge scores, a generally positive attitude toward metaverse in education, commonly cited advantages (e.g., engaging environments and learning by doing), and concerns (especially technical problems, psychological issues such as addiction, inequality of opportunity, and data security). Teachers indicated that subjects such as information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics are most suitable, and many expected broader implementation within a few years, provided the education system prepares for related pedagogical, infrastructural, and health considerations.

The passage describes how to attack a Box & One defense using a “Flash/Back Door” action, exploiting vulnerability in the middle by flashing a baseline post player to create matchup problems. It outlines post flash and back door cuts, continuity options like High/Low feeds and Single/Double screens, and several variations for initiating post flash action, including baseline screens and ballhandler entry passes. Implementation emphasizes execution and coordination, including mid screens, base screens, strong post ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. It also recommends scouting opponents to anticipate defensive reads and counters and adjusting alignments to attack weaker defenders, then explains the Box & One defense as four players in a box zone and one “Chaser” focused on full pass denial.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 11, 2015 reporting that it issued a press release announcing its results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, and financial information and commentary by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, is attached as Exhibit 99.2 (CFO Commentary). The CFO Commentary was to be posted to NVIDIA’s investor website immediately after the filing. The filing includes statements that the press release and CFO Commentary are furnished and not deemed filed for specified securities law purposes. The report was signed by Colette M. Kress.

The passage describes a hospital experience that the speaker says was amazing, including watching their baby being born, with mention of their wife handling it well. It also discusses a sports game where the team regrouped after a teammate took a blow to the head, played harder for him, and won. The speaker notes a fast, high-tempo game, mentions a hit involving Drury and another elbow to the back of the head from Holmstrom, and says the league will likely review it and call something if warranted.

The speaker says their knee has not buckled, and that they had the MCL checked by a doctor, who said it has healed and is “pretty tight.” The speaker reports the injury is not painful, and they believe a brace will help; they say surgery will be needed after the series to fix it. They discuss returning to work on motion quickly after a previous MCL tear and say they came back quickly, with a therapist in Dallas noting they were doing well. The speaker expresses readiness to play in an upcoming game and mentions talking with Brett about the difficulty of watching games on TV, hoping others heal quickly as well.

H. B. Fuller Company’s VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares on October 2 at an average price of $58.40, for $315,184.80, as disclosed in an SEC filing. The stock opened at $56.81 on Friday, with a 50-day moving average of $53.88 and a 200-day moving average of $52.11. The company has a market capitalization of $2.87 billion, a P/E ratio of 25.96, and a beta of 1.72, with a 52-week range of $41.52 to $58.74. In the quarter ended September 27, it reported EPS of $0.65 versus a $0.67 consensus and revenue of $562.87 million versus $553.66 million. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.15 per share to be paid on November 2, with a dividend yield of 1.06% and a payout ratio of 29.41%. Analysts’ ratings averaged “Hold” with a consensus price target of $57.40. The company is a manufacturer and marketer of adhesives, sealants, and specialty chemical products, operating in segments including Americas Adhesives, EIMEA, Asia Pacific, Construction Products, and Engineering Adhesives.

The Supreme Court said it will hear on August 17 Lt Col Prasad Shrikant Purohit’s bail plea and a plea seeking cancellation of bail granted to co-accused Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur. The bench of Justices R.K. Agrawal and Mohan M. Shantanagoudar noted both matters are based on similar facts and require detailed hearing. Purohit challenged the Bombay High Court’s rejection of his bail, while Nisar Ahmed Haji Sayed Bilal, father of a blast victim, sought cancellation of Pragya Singh Thakur’s bail, alleging she could influence witnesses. The Bombay High Court granted her bail on April 25 and rejected Purohit’s application; the Supreme Court had sought the Maharashtra government’s response on May 5. The passage also describes the September 29, 2008 Malegaon bomb blast, arrests of 11 accused including Thakur and Purohit, and the NIA’s position that charges against Purohit were serious and that it gave a clean chit to Pragya Singh Thakur.

The passage describes LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web tool integrated into the UK Biobank data preparation platform LUKB and built with R Shiny. It identifies disease trajectories from electronic medical record data using four steps: selecting exposed diseases with increased risk via Cox regression, detecting temporal disease pairs with a binomial test, validating pair directionality with conditional logistic regression, and concatenating confirmed pairs into trajectories. The methods require participant IDs, diagnoses, and diagnosis dates, along with user-defined analysis parameters such as exposure, follow-up period, minimum prevalence, and gap between diseases. A case study using UK Biobank ICD-10 data analyzed subsequent diseases after COVID-19 diagnosis, finding trajectories mainly leading to SARS-CoV-2 infection-related diseases and other medical care, while noting limitations in capturing the full spectrum of COVID-19-related conditions. The tool’s runtime is benchmarked for the case study, and the passage outlines limitations related to reliance on processed ICD-10 records and the non-direct nature of trajectory construction.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated May 7, 2015. It reported that on May 7, 2015 the company issued a press release with results for the three months ended April 26, 2015, filed as Exhibit 99.1, and furnished CFO Commentary by Colette M. Kress as Exhibit 99.2. The report states these items are not deemed filed for certain Securities Act and Exchange Act purposes. It also said that on May 5, 2015 NVIDIA announced it would wind down its Icera modem operations in the second quarter of fiscal 2016 and is open to a sale of the technology or operations, approved by its Board on May 4, 2015. The company estimated restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million primarily in fiscal 2016, including severance and other costs if the modem operations are not sold.

Children with language vulnerabilities (e.g., developmental language disorder, autism, or migrant-related second-language learning needs) often require tailored language support. Speech-language therapists (SLTs) work with caregivers and educators, but reinforcing targeted linguistic structures during everyday interactions is challenging. Existing interventions vary along an implicit-explicit continuum, and morphology teaching approaches are not yet clearly optimized.

The passage describes limitations in robot-assisted language learning (RALL), including issues with speech recognition, timing and generation of verbal/non-verbal actions, and turn-taking—challenges that may be amplified for children with language vulnerabilities. To address these, the authors propose using large language models (LLMs) to improve RALL adaptability and interaction naturalness. They present TalBot, a Furhat conversational robot integrated with an LLM (ChatGPT), developed by a multiprofessional research group and iteratively tested with preschool children with language vulnerabilities and educators. Ethical risk assessment measures were used to minimize sharing children’s personal information.

TalBot is described as managing the Alias word retrieval game by handling turn-taking, feedback, additional clues, emotion expressions, and redirecting off-task conversation. The authors plan to expand TalBot toward morphological and grammar learning, proposing that LLMs can generate unlimited linguistic material, provide consistent high-dose linguistic modeling, and serve as a role model for educators. They outline further development through lab and preschool field studies, including recording sessions, comparing robot and educator performance, quantifying target morphology occurrences, and assessing educator experience and user perceptions. The work also notes regulatory, ethical, and practical considerations, including data protection.

David Ellison, whose Paramount Skydance owns CBS News, said he wants to restore trust in media and expressed strong respect for CBS News. His appointment of Bari Weiss as the top editor has prompted questions about CBS News’s future direction, especially as he avoided directly addressing what the network needs to improve and dismissed claims of a plot to align CBS News with Trumpworld. Ellison described The Free Press, which he acquired and installed Weiss to lead, as aiming to return media to the trust and truth business, aligning its values with Paramount and CBS News’s legacy. He said he wants his news operation to appeal to Americans who identify as center-left or center-right, but what that will involve is not clear.

Officials from the Grand Erie District School Board and Brant-Haldimand-Norfolk Catholic District School Board met with coaches and phys. ed teachers in Brantford on Jan. 23 to discuss amalgamating high school sports across Brantford, Haldimand and Norfolk into a single league. Currently, schools mostly play within their own county, with the only noted crossover being McKinnon Park Blue Devils’ football games against Norfolk County teams. The boards’ communications manager said the proposal aims to create an equitable, inclusive system with the same number of games and rules for both Catholic and public schools, though no final decisions or timeline are set and the goal is for changes to take shape the year after next. Travel and associated costs were identified as a potential issue, and Newhouse said travel would be part of later discussions.

The passage describes dependencies and host-environment requirements for calling AGESA procedures, including the need for a stack, protected-mode flat addressing, and the use of a call-out router function with a standardized header. It explains how AGESA interface call-outs are funneled through an interface portal for consistent filtering and dispatching. It outlines build and execution dependencies across UEFI phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP), required build tools for different phases, and configuration options. The text details UEFI-specific stack setup via macros, early platform control, and stack initialization/removal routines, including their register behavior and status codes. It also describes several host environment service routines and their purposes, such as creating/allocating structure storage, obtaining processor addresses (APIC, PCI), execution cache size, and identifying memory devices (DIMM/FRU), along with MMIO mapping and event logging interfaces.

The passage discusses young people applying for college and argues that at 17 it is unreasonable to know what to do for life, because career paths and technology will change over the next 40–50 years. It warns that industries tied to petrol and diesel will become less dominant with electric cars and notes that future developments may surprise people. It emphasizes that employees (and self-employed people) should make their work as valuable as possible, asking what they can offer to earn more than minimum wage. It uses burger seller and throat surgeon examples to illustrate how specialized expertise can increase pay, and advises concentrating on “adding value” to one’s bank balance. The passage also cautions against assuming any job will be enjoyable every day and highlights that life outside work is what matters.

Scotland plans to abolish local authority charges for the burial or cremation of children under 18, agreeing with Cosla to remove all fees. The Scottish government will provide £500,000 funding for the change, which is intended to align Scotland with England. The Church of Scotland welcomed the policy, and Communities Secretary Angela Constance said it should help support bereaved parents and ensure no family has to pay.

Type 2A frequency compensation is used with a target crossover frequency of 10 kHz. The power stage transconductance is calculated as 16.2 A/V, and the external compensation component values selected are RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF. The output uses seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors to meet a required 2.3-mF value; each has an ESR of about 6 mΩ, giving an equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ to determine the ESR zero frequency and calculate CHF, and compensation may be tuned during testing.

Slope compensation is tailored using the RSC pin of the TPS7H5001-SP to match the falling slope of the output inductor for sub-harmonic damping; a 102 kΩ resistor is connected between RSC and AVSS. The TPS7H500x-SP controllers operate with an input supply range of 4 V to 14 V, require at least 0.1 µF input bypass capacitance from VIN to AVSS, and recommend ceramic capacitors placed close to the controller with additional bulk capacitance if the controller is several inches from the input source. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noise coupling by routing feedback and sensitive signals away from power magnetics and high dv/dt nodes, minimizing switching loops, separating AVSS from high-current power ground, placing bypass/filtering capacitors near the controller, placing external compensation near the COMP pin, and keeping resistor dividers close to VSENSE.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 1, 2019, reporting that on March 30, 2019 Stephen C. Neal was appointed to NVIDIA’s Board of Directors. Upon his appointment, he received an initial equity grant of 1,419 restricted stock units vesting over three years starting March 30, 2019, and a pro-rated annual equity grant of 139 restricted stock units vesting on May 15, 2019, under the 2007 Amended and Restated Equity Incentive Plan. He also received a pro-rated annual cash retainer of $10,890 payable on March 30, 2019, and NVIDIA entered into an indemnity agreement with him.

Cover 2 is described as a common zone coverage used to defend short breaking routes while also protecting against deep throws with two deep safeties. In a 4-3 defense, five underneath players (two corners and three linebackers) cover short routes, while the two deep safeties split the field and cover over the top. The coverage allows defenders to read receiver routes while keeping eyes on the quarterback, and it focuses on shorter passes such as hitches and slants, including success against offenses that throw quickly or use wide receiver screens (“smoke screens”). Cover 2 uses “hard” corners that stay closer to the line of scrimmage to help against outside running. Weaknesses include vulnerability to multiple deep routes, especially 4 vertical routes, and to trips formations that can overload one half. It can also struggle against certain runs, such as 2x2 and trips setups that leave fewer defenders and can enable big runs or touchdowns. Listed rules for player responsibilities are also provided, along with two variations: Cover 2 “Switch” (corners bail deep and safeties play the flat) and Cover 2 from a 1 High shell (appearance of 1 high while playing 2 high to confuse offenses).

Emirates Airlines said it will not remove the “Hindu meal” option from its in-flight menu after receiving negative customer feedback, particularly from Hindus. The airline earlier said it would discontinue the option following a review of onboard products and services, but later confirmed it will continue providing the Hindu meal option. It also said Hindu passengers can choose from a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian regionally inspired meals.

Job growth in the US exceeded expectations in January, with non-farm payrolls rising by 200,000 versus economists’ expected 180,000. Average hourly earnings increased 0.3% month-over-month and 2.9% year-on-year, the fastest pace since the recession and the quickest since 2009. The unemployment rate held at 4.1% for the fourth straight month. The stronger data increased expectations of a rate rise in March, though it led to higher Treasury yields, with the 10-year yield rising above 2.8% and the 2-year note reaching its highest level since September 2008. The Federal Reserve had already signalled a March rate rise, and analysts noted that tax cuts and planned infrastructure spending could lead to more wage growth and potentially tighter policy.

The passage discusses how the team expects no significant changes, saying it has learned from playoff situations where it was behind in a series. It highlights confidence in the locker room and identifies issues including careless puck play, turnovers, poor execution, and mistakes that created momentum for the opponent, such as giving up two-on-ones or breakaways. The team says it had chances to win the last game, plans to stay positive, watch video, and learn from the loss. It also notes that sitting back and waiting to learn the opponent was a mistake, and emphasizes the need to keep the puck away from the goaltender, get forechecking going, and play its game. Finally, it mentions hitting as a momentum factor, especially with a home crowd.

The paper conducts a co-occurrence bibliometric analysis of Information Systems Education Journal (ISEDJ) articles from 2003–2024 (1,076 articles) to identify IS education topics over time and anticipate future directions. It uses author-supplied keywords to build co-occurrence networks, then creates term maps in VOSviewer, with clusters assigned by clustering techniques and term importance based on frequency and link strength. Years are grouped into five-year “eras” (2003–2007, 2008–2012, 2013–2017, 2018–2022, and 2023–2024) plus a full-network map. Results describe era-specific topic clusters, including early emphasis on curriculum, assessment, and pedagogy; later expansion to student and pedagogy issues; growth of cybersecurity, big data, and analytics; COVID-19-related student-focused topics; and an AI-centered era in 2023–2024. The discussion notes changes in topic rankings and cluster counts across eras, and the conclusion states it is the first known full-corpus study of ISEDJ at the time. Limitations include reliance solely on author-supplied keywords, possible inflation from special issues, and the suggestion to add titles and abstracts in future work. Future directions include using a data-driven approach to define eras rather than predefined five-year groupings.

FERC issued an order approving an extension of NYISO’s Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP) through April 30, 2002, with the AMP originally expiring on October 31, 2001. NYISO was directed to file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1, 2002, addressing FERC’s concerns about the AMP and how NYISO’s mitigation measures work together, including in-city mitigation measures. FERC acknowledged fixes NYISO committed to, including limiting mitigation to specific zones and hours that fail the impact test and exempting bids under 50 MW unless there is demonstrated market power concern. FERC also directed NYISO to examine whether the AMP could be a barrier to entry for new generation, whether other energy-limited resources should be exempted or accommodated, and to consider must-run mitigation measures consistent with ISO-NE and PJM, while cautioning NYISO to develop one Northeast mitigation plan as part of the RTO process.

Craig Shakespeare said Leicester’s 4-2 defeat at Everton on Sunday, his first loss since replacing Claudio Ranieri, would not affect the squad as they prepare for a Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. He noted Leicester had won all five Premier League games under him and beat Sevilla in the Champions League, but their run ended at Goodison despite leading 2-1 after ten minutes. Shakespeare said the team’s confidence and momentum would not be hampered, and he made five changes at Everton with future fixtures in mind, emphasizing squad rotation. He said Leicester were disappointed by set plays that led to Everton’s decisive goals and that their defending as a team was the issue. He also confirmed captain and central defender Wes Morgan would miss the Madrid match due to a back injury.

Dr. Harris L. Rittenberg and his staff provide personal dental care in a family practice serving children and adults for over 50 years at the same location. Dr. Rittenberg has practiced for over 25 years and is described as treating patients fairly and providing quality treatment. The practice’s mission is to help patients achieve optimum dental health to improve their lives, avoid dental emergencies, and keep their teeth. Dr. Rittenberg continues education to offer advanced dentistry and state-of-the-art techniques, and he was acknowledged by the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry for participating in restoring smiles of domestic violence victims through the “Give Back a Smile” program. The team now includes Dr. Brittany Jones to allow more time with patients while maintaining quality, friendly, gentle care.

Laredo Petroleum Holdings Inc (NYSE:LPI) shares rose 0.72% in the most recent session. Analysts project a 52-week target mean of $13.54 based on 24 opinions, with a broader high target of $17 and a low target of $9.5; the latest closing price was $9.8. The consensus ABR (average brokerage recommendation) is 2.47 across 15 recommendations, with the company’s industry ranking out of 265; 5 analysts recommend Buy, 5 Outperform, 12 Hold, 2 Underperform, and 0 Sell. LPI’s ATR-14 is 0.45, with weekly volatility of 3.91% and monthly volatility of 3.97%. The RSI is 39.08, with typical overbought/oversold levels above 70 and below 30. The company has a market capitalization of $2.35 billion and 240.08 million shares outstanding, and 3.32 million shares traded in the previous session versus an average of about 2.93 million.

Lowe’s will leave NASCAR after 18 seasons, ending its sponsorship of Jimmie Johnson’s No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports team. Johnson said the change creates a “golden opportunity” for a company to sponsor him, and that his Cup career likely will end after a “handful of years,” though he expects to keep racing other events. He described a bucket list that could include the 24 Hours of Le Mans and the Rolex 24 at Daytona, and he suggested he might compete in the Indianapolis 500 if IndyCar adopts Formula One’s cockpit-protecting halos.

The passage describes the “5-day low overnight trading strategy” in the S&P 500 as a mean-reversion approach where traders enter at the close on days when the market opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than it opened, then exit at the next day’s open. It states that overnight trading in the S&P 500 has historically produced an average return of 0.04% from the close to the next day’s open and cites a test period from 2005 onward showing an average profit of 15.93% (average return 0.26% per trade), which drops to 0.17% when excluding the biggest winner of 6% in October 2008. The article also notes that it backtests the strategy using SPY from 1993 to the present.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for an image processing method and apparatus in computer/communication technologies, aimed at improving efficiency and effect of placing an external three-dimensional object (e.g., a displaylink model) into a video. It involves obtaining a video with at least two frames, placing a target three-dimensional model on a target plane in the first frame, determining feature point coordinates in both world and pixel coordinate systems, calculating the camera pose for the first frame, then determining camera poses for subsequent frames relative to the world coordinate system. The method generates a target video by replacing the target model with a target model and projecting it onto each frame based on the calculated camera poses. The apparatus and related implementations, including a computer-readable storage medium and an electronic device, are also described. The passage further discusses tracking the target plane (e.g., via homography) and optionally using a neural network to segment planes in the first frame, before placing and synthesizing the target model across all frames.

The passage describes how New York’s Excelsior Scholarship Program, which offers tuition-free SUNY or CUNY college for eligible students, is affecting the college affordability discussion for families and private colleges. Gianna Ruffle is weighing public and private options, with her parents encouraging her to pursue the Excelsior scholarship if she can attend College at Brockport. The article explains that Excelsior fills the “last-dollar” gap after other aid, covers only tuition (not fees, room and board, or books), and has an income ceiling of $110,000 that will rise. While some counselors encourage students to compare both public and private options, many private institutions say Excelsior changes the value equation and creates challenges for smaller colleges. In response, private schools are launching or expanding initiatives such as tuition reductions, scholarship guarantees, and programs aimed at attracting New York students, including Canisius’s “Excellence Within Reach Initiative,” Roberts Wesleyan’s “Four-Year Promise,” and Le Moyne’s “Promise NY.” The passage also notes concerns about how long Albany can continue underwriting state tuition, and it includes examples of how specific private colleges are positioning themselves through scholarships and marketing.

The passage discusses how text messaging has become a fast and efficient way to transfer information in modern communication, replacing phone calls for many people. It then describes several apps that offer alternative features to traditional texting: Music Messenger, which lets users send songs for sharing sounds and moods; WhatsApp, a free messaging platform available on any smartphone that supports sending video, photos, sound clips, emoticons, and background personalization; and Facebook Messenger, offered within Facebook, which supports media sharing, HD video chats, sound bites, group chat, customization of emojis and text color, and is free with no advertising.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 27, 2017, reporting that it announced its first quarter 2017 financial results on that date. The announcement press release is included as Exhibit 99.1, and additional information regarding non-GAAP financial measures is included as Exhibit 99.2, both incorporated by reference. The report also lists Items 2.02 and 9.01, and is signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on July 26, 2016 reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet with its financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2016. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and the data sheet as Exhibit 99.2. The report states the information is not deemed filed for purposes of certain Securities Exchange Act sections, except as expressly set forth.

The Federal Reserve is proposing changes to the Volcker Rule, which bars banks from making risky trading bets for their own profit using depositors’ money. The Fed says the proposed changes would align the strictest rule applications with banks that do the most trading to reduce uncertainty. The effort is occurring alongside other moves to loosen financial regulations. The passage also notes prior modifications to Dodd-Frank and legislation that eases oversight and capital requirements for some smaller banks, as well as actions by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau under Mick Mulvaney. Supporters and opponents of the Volcker Rule are quoted, and the article describes the Fed’s leadership and recent appointees, including new chair Jerome Powell and board member Randal Quarles.

South Korean Lotte Group plans to list its Malaysian petrochemical unit, Lotte Chemical Titan Holding, on Bursa Malaysia in the third quarter via an initial public offering that could raise up to $1.5 billion. The IPO would offer up to 740.48 million shares, with an over-allotment option for up to 55.54 million shares. Proceeds are intended for building a naphtha cracker in Indonesia, a polypropylene plant in Malaysia, and expanding a cracker facility in Malaysia. The IPO date was originally targeted for last year but was delayed after South Korea’s investigations into alleged fraud at Lotte Group. Maybank Investment Bank, Credit Suisse, and J.P. Morgan are joint global coordinators, while CIMB Investment Bank, HSBC, and Nomura are joint bookrunners; the size and pricing are not yet determined, though sources expect $1–$1.5 billion.

The passage explains the “offside trap” in soccer as a defensive tactic where defensive backs move up in unison just before an attacker passes to a leading striker, placing the striker in an offside position. If the striker gains an advantage by receiving the ball, officials are expected to call the offside violation under Law 11 and award an indirect free kick to the defending team. It outlines how offside rules apply, historical adoption of the tactic, and how recent changes to offside interpretations and offensive styles affect its risk. The passage notes that the trap leaves the goalkeeper alone, can fail if defenders do not step forward simultaneously, and can be avoided if attackers stop interfering or let a teammate play the ball. It covers coaching decisions, requirements for the back defenders to execute the trap (including communication and specific positioning), who may call it (the upfield defensive coordinator or, in some alignments, other designated roles), the need for a unique signal, and the quick execution during run of play or free kicks. It emphasizes practice, cautions against overuse, and recommends scouting opponents and signals.

The passage is a lecture introduction about blockchain technology using Bitcoin as the main example. It outlines that the class will cover technical foundations including cryptography (hash functions and digital signatures), timestamped append-only logs, block structures (block headers and Merkle trees), distributed consensus algorithms, and networking. The lecturer discusses ledgers as central to Bitcoin, explains the double spend problem, and frames money as a social consensus with fiat currency challenges. It describes Bitcoin’s block design (blocks added about every 10 minutes in Bitcoin), security based on cryptographic primitives, and consensus about who can add the next block. The lecture then focuses on hash functions’ properties (deterministic, fixed output size, one-way and collision resistant, efficient to compute) and their use in block headers. It also explains asymmetric cryptography and digital signatures using public/private keys, including the need for secure random number generation for key generation. Additional details cover Merkle roots, difficulty targets, nonces, mining incentives via a native currency (Bitcoin) with a finite supply, and basic ideas about transaction inputs/outputs and Bitcoin addresses. The lecturer concludes by stating that next topics will be Bitcoin consensus protocol and transactions.

In December 2006, SunPower’s CEO Tom Werner considers questions about how quickly solar power will grow, how long SunPower’s advantage in efficient photovoltaic (PV) cells can last, and how the company can compete with larger rivals such as Sharp and Q-Cells as well as smaller technology-focused firms. The case highlights growing interest in solar power driven by energy independence and environmental concerns related to greenhouse-gas emissions, including rising atmospheric CO2 levels and related climate-change risks.

It describes the PV industry’s value chain (silicon production through installation), market growth and investment trends, and differences among producers and consumer demand globally, including roles of Europe, Japan, the United States, and China. It outlines solar power pricing challenges, the impact of installation costs and sunshine hours, and the role of policy support such as subsidies, renewable portfolio standards, and carbon trading. The passage also details SunPower’s history, partnerships, manufacturing approach, and efficiency-based differentiation, along with its cost structure and intended efforts to reduce downstream installation and integration costs. Finally, it presents major competitors and concludes by framing the strategic question of what mix of module pricing and process improvements SunPower should pursue amid evolving competition.

The Pentagon has not said which North Korean missile blew up “almost immediately” after an early Sunday launch near Sinpo, and the White House has described it only as a medium-range device. Weapons expert John Schilling said the failure likely reflected an early development test of a new system, citing common propulsion and guidance problems, and he noted the missile could have been a new design shown in a Pyongyang parade. Anonymous US officials told Fox News it was a new liquid-fueled Scud type called KN-17, but Schilling said the parade-related device was different. Acting Assistant Secretary Susan Thornton said limited information was available due to the quick failure. Some observers speculated US cyber efforts may have contributed, but Schilling said the idea of hacking is exaggerated due to North Korea’s relatively primitive missile technology. Separately, Pentagon chief Jim Mattis ordered a review of America’s nuclear deterrent to ensure it meets required standards, which typically occur about every seven years.

The passage discusses the speaker growing up in Brick, New Jersey, where they heard about Jim Dowd, described as a great and hard-working person. The speaker says joining an opportunity felt like a “no brainer.” They describe the game as exciting, though they would have preferred overtime instead of a shootout. They plan to stay at their current place as long as needed to reach their goal of playing in the NHL. They mention being close between Michigan and New Hampshire, and say they are happy with choosing New Hampshire and are excited to play next year. The speaker also says their dad, Frans Vanriemsdyk, is with them.

The passage describes the device’s analog input behavior and related circuitry, including a resistive analog input impedance of at least 1 MΩ per input that is independent of ADC sampling and signal frequency. It explains input dc accuracy requirements by matching external source impedance on AIN_P with an equivalent resistance on AIN_M to cancel offset error, and it details an internal overvoltage protection (OVP) circuit with input resistors and protection diodes that limit current and withstand up to ±20 V when powered on, and ±15 V when AVDD is floating. It also covers the internal programmable gain amplifier (PGA), an antialiasing second-order low-pass filter, ADC driver requirements for settling of sample-and-hold capacitors, and internal/external voltage reference selection and reference decoupling. Additional sections summarize the ADC transfer function, alarm features for analog input thresholds and AVDD thresholds (including flags, hysteresis, and clearing behavior), and then outline device functional modes and multiSPI-based data transfer and programming, including data transfer frames, command execution, output data word formation, and configurable SPI/SRC read protocols.

The passage describes a planned systematic review of Rapid Response Team (RRT) service implementation and redesign in hospitals. It aims to identify how RRT services are changed (as novel services or redesigns), why they are changed, the time frame for implementation, and what measures are used to assess success. The review will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies with no restrictions on publication status, language, or year, and will extract data on study, team, implementation methods, and outcomes. Searches will be conducted in Medline, CINAHL, Embase, and Cochrane Library, supplemented by Google Scholar (first ten pages), reference list checks, conference abstracts, and expert contact. Two independent authors will screen and extract data in duplicate, and risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI checklist. Results will be mainly narrative with simple statistics using SPSS. Ethical approval is not required because only published studies will be used. The protocol will be registered on medRxiv, with results planned for scientific meetings and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The review acknowledges limitations such as heterogeneity across studies and possible lack of studies on service/change management, and states there is no external funding.

The lecture provides an overview of equities and how they differ from bonds, emphasizing that stock represents ownership in a corporation and produces value through dividends (including cash or stock dividends) and capital gains. It discusses key equity characteristics: equity holders are residual claimants after bondholders, they have uncapped upside, and limited liability restricts losses to what investors put in, which the lecturer argues supports innovation and capital formation. The passage also covers voting rights, access to public markets, and the role of short sales in making market prices more informative. It distinguishes between primary and secondary equity markets and describes how primary IPO activity cycles with the business and credit cycle, while secondary market trading volume has generally increased due to technological innovations such as the internet, electronic communications networks, and electronic trading.

The lecture then introduces the Dividend Discount Model (valuation based on present value of expected future dividends), noting that unlike bonds, future dividends are uncertain and require forecasts. It explains that the appropriate discount rate is risk-adjusted and can change over time, reflecting both risks of the company’s cash flows and overall market conditions, and that the market determines these discount rates. The discussion extends to simpler cases, including constant dividends leading to a perpetuity value and growing dividends leading to the Gordon growth model, used to explain how growth expectations can affect stock prices and how changes in perceived growth can cause large price swings. It also addresses practical issues in applying these models, such as difficulty estimating dividends, discount rates, and growth far into the future, and concludes with remarks on dividend policy changes, exceptions (temporary suspension during cash crunches and extraordinary dividends from windfalls), and how corporate investment decisions depend on cost of capital and borrowing costs.

Asia-Pacific equities extended gains in April as investors’ risk appetite increased, supported by French election first-round results, easing concerns over North Korea, and strong first-quarter earnings from major Asian companies. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan was near a two-year high. India led with gains of over 20% this year, while China rose about 2.5%. Valuation metrics showed New Zealand and India as the most expensive (forward P/E over 18) and South Korea and Hong Kong as the cheapest (around 11 times earnings). The passage also cites strong earnings and related updates from Samsung Electronics, CITIC Securities, and TSMC.

Enron replaced its chief financial officer, Andrew S. Fastow, naming Jeffrey McMahon as his successor after an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow ran. Enron said the change was intended to restore investor confidence; Fastow took a leave of absence. Fastow-related partnership concerns coincided with a sharp decline in Enron’s stock and related worries across energy-trading companies, alongside criticism that Enron’s disclosures about its complex financial dealings were insufficient.

Containerization is described as an intermodal process where goods are transported without unloading or reloading on containers between places, and it can also be carried out by air for fast transport between regions. Civil airlines and military forces use air containerization, with major commercial airlines using custom containers and ground handling equipment; passenger aircraft carry containers on the lower deck, while cargo aircraft use both lower and upper decks. The market is driven by rising global demand for quick transportation, and supported by technological advancements in lightweight containers that can handle varied loads and rough handling. Factors limiting the market include global economic slowdown in regions such as Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East, and increased aviation fuel leading airlines to restrict cargo flying hours. Future opportunities include growth in commercial airlines and defense authorities’ demand to transport goods quickly, including military equipment. The market is segmented by container type (refrigerated and non-refrigerated), end user, aircraft type (narrow body, wide body, very large, military), and geography, and it includes several listed vendors.

The passage discusses the current state of education in China under the one-child policy, arguing that children are often spoiled and that parents focus on academic grades more than character and moral development, leading to problems when they enter society. It compares reported American and Chinese primary education findings, but says both conclusions were wrong after 30 years, claiming American-style education is now admired and Chinese-style education is criticized. The text argues education should focus on liberating individual interests, functioning as an individual in society, and not just knowledge and discipline. It cites a survey suggesting many children struggle with basic household tasks, that some face emotional and behavioral problems, and that examination-oriented education can contribute to suicide among teenagers. The passage then recommends priorities such as sharing and giving to others, equal access to higher education resources, guiding students to find unique interests, getting closer to nature, emphasizing moral behavior education over scientific knowledge, maintaining health through manual labor or sports, strengthening parent-child relationships through joint activities, and learning from traditional moral education and religious values centered on love. It also calls for greater attention to women’s status in family education, noting that parents’ lack of time can affect children, especially how children learn from mothers. It concludes that family education should emphasize morality and humanity education, proper parental guidance, and applying ancestral moral education in modern life.

A geoarchaeological study of Karnak Temple near Luxor used 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments to trace how the temple complex and its river landscape changed over about 3,000 years. Researchers found the site originated as an island formed by ancient Nile channels and that it was regularly flooded before about 2520 BCE, making it likely unsuitable for permanent occupation then. Earliest occupation likely dates to the Old Kingdom (2591–2152 BC), and the landscape evidence suggests Karnak’s placement may have reflected an ancient Egyptian creation myth in which land emerged from primeval waters. The study mapped how surrounding river channels evolved and affected where construction occurred, and it notes that similar patterns to the creation myth led the researchers to consider a religious link to the idea of high ground emerging from surrounding water.

Microsoft introduced Cortana, a voice assistant similar to Apple’s Siri, and says it becomes smarter with Windows 10 updates. The passage states Cortana is compatible with desktops, laptops, and tablets running Windows 10, accessible via the Mic button, and works with the Edge browser by appearing on the address bar. It can search files across hard drive and cloud, and some manufacturers add a dedicated button to activate it. It is described as cross-platform, available on Android and iOS alongside Windows, with personal recognition that learns the user’s vocal range. Cortana can also joke and interact humorously, and it supports location-based voice commands and reminders.

The speakers discuss the need for mental toughness in a difficult rink and say their players generated more offense, won rebounds and screens, and were rewarded for it, including a strong performance in overtime. They emphasize composure and discipline, not getting frustrated despite potential opportunities in the third, and believe they handled game “bends” without letting them become breaks. They also address lineup and injury-related decisions, noting a player missed games but returned after four days of practice, and that he was not emotional. Finally, they downplay special teams and argue success depends on improving five-on-five play, focusing on preparation for the game day.

The passage advises Galaxy Fold users to unfold their phone or view it in full screen for the best experience. It then provides information and commentary about the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, including that it has a $0 annual fee and offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. It notes variable APR afterward, a balance transfer fee of 5% (minimum $5), and a 3% foreign transaction fee. The card is described as useful for avoiding credit card interest during the intro period, and it also offers up to $600 of cell phone protection (with a $25 deductible) when paying the monthly cellphone bill with the card. The passage includes an application outline and discusses how compensation may affect offer placement while product ratings are stated to be unaffected by compensation.

Mark Fields, former Ford CEO, said US automakers “went full bore” into building EV capacity without adequately discussing consumer needs or considering how demand would develop. He said the market did not develop as automakers expected and that bets made on EVs have come undone over the past 18 months. Fields also noted that while some automakers, including GM, promoted having a full EV lineup, EV adoption is likely to be lower in the near to medium term than planned. Ford’s filing cited a $1.6 billion charge tied to realigning EV capacity and manufacturing to consumer demand, and the company expected EV adoption to slow after federal EV incentives were eliminated.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated March 31, 2020, reporting that on March 26, 2020 it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC to issue and sell $5.0 billion of unsecured notes. The notes consist of $1.5 billion of 2.850% notes due 2030, $1.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2040, $2.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2050, and $0.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2060. The net proceeds were approximately $4.97 billion, intended for general corporate purposes, including repayment of indebtedness. The notes’ terms are governed by an indenture dated September 16, 2016, as supplemented by an officers’ certificate dated March 31, 2020, with maturities and semiannual interest payments specified. The filing also describes redemption provisions, certain covenants and events of default, and a change-of-control repurchase requirement, and lists related exhibits.

The passage describes how TPS7H500x-SP controllers program output voltage using a resistor divider to the VSENSE pin, adjust soft-start behavior using a capacitor and charging current, and set switching frequency through internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary modes using the RT and SYNC pins. It also outlines primary output (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) options, dead time and leading edge blank time programmability with resistors, and a pulse-skipping function with specified COMP and duty-cycle conditions. Additional sections cover duty-cycle limits via the DCL pin, current sense and PWM generation using CS_ILIM and COMP thresholds, hiccup mode operation controlled by a capacitor on HICC, external fault protection using the FAULT pin, slope compensation for stability, and thermal shutdown thresholds. It concludes with application and layout guidance, including PCB routing and capacitor placement considerations, and brief application design example details.

The speaker says they had many scoring chances in a recent game but failed to capitalize on key opportunities in the first period. They plan to work hard to create and capitalize on chances again. They discuss playoff hockey as sometimes involving limited space and the need to play effectively without taking too much risk. They comment that the opposing team was fast, surrounded the puck well, and worked hard. They describe their own performance as having ups and downs during the long playoffs, but feel their game is improving. They also praise Dave’s experience, goal-scoring ability, and more defensive, role-focused approach, noting his work and actions. Finally, they explain a strategy of making plays to wear down defensemen by battling below the top of the circle and below the goal line, including chipping the puck in cycles.

The passage discusses trend following and momentum strategies for Bitcoin using backtests with BTC-USD data from 2015 to April 2021 (excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes). It argues that Bitcoin’s large price swings make it suitable for these strategies and reports that simple moving average trend-following can outperform buy-and-hold/HODL and limit worst drawdowns. A short 20-day exponential average is highlighted, with optimization suggesting fewer than 20 days works best; the best result cited uses five days (CAGR 145%). A longer two-moving-average approach (100-day vs 250-day) goes long when the short average is above the long average and sells on the opposite; it yields three trades, with a max drawdown of 65% and CAGR 115%, compared to 94% for buy-and-hold. The momentum strategy tested buys when the close is higher than the close 25 days ago and sells when it is lower; it reportedly beats buy-and-hold while minimizing drawdown despite a low win ratio. The passage concludes that as long as Bitcoin continues its volatility, these strategies may continue to work, but it notes there is no guarantee regarding future performance.

The Minnesota Timberwolves host the NBA-best Houston Rockets Sunday night in the second game of a back-to-back for both teams, a week after Karl-Anthony Towns’ late-game plays helped Minnesota defeat the Golden State Warriors 109-103 at home. Minnesota is sixth in the Western Conference, one-and-a-half games behind Oklahoma City, and has been playing with tight standings changes. Towns has recently scored 23 in a 117-101 loss at San Antonio, 37 against Washington, and has averaged 25.5 points over his last six games; Andrew Wiggins has averaged 20.1 points over his last six games. Minnesota is 4-4 since losing Jimmy Butler to knee surgery on Feb. 24. 

Houston (55-14) has a 2.5-game lead on Golden State for the top seed and hopes to contain Towns after limiting him to 6-of-15 shooting in a 120-102 loss earlier this month. The Rockets enter on a strong stretch following James Harden’s performance in a 107-101 win at New Orleans, and they have won 5 straight meetings with Minnesota and 17 of the last 19, scoring at least 100 points in the last 16 matchups.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated December 13, 2022, reporting results of its 2022 Annual Shareholders Meeting held on December 13, 2022. Of 7,456,502,484 shares entitled to vote, 6,407,164,715 were voted in person or by proxy. Shareholders re-elected twelve directors, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers, and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent auditor for fiscal year 2023. Shareholders did not approve six shareholder proposals regarding diversity and inclusion cost/benefit analysis, hiring of persons with arrest or incarceration records, retirement funds investment in companies contributing to climate change, government use of Microsoft technology, development of products for the military, and tax transparency. The report was signed by Keith R. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary, on December 16, 2022.

Engineers at UC San Diego developed tiny ultrasound-powered nanorobots that swim through blood to remove harmful bacteria and the toxins they produce. The robots are gold nanowires coated with a hybrid of platelet and red blood cell membranes, allowing platelets’ pathogen-binding functions and red blood cells’ toxin absorption and neutralization in a single coating. The ultrasound response lets the robots move rapidly without chemical fuel and mix efficiently with bacteria and toxins to speed detoxification. Researchers report that in tests on blood samples contaminated with MRSA and its toxins, after five minutes there were three times less bacteria and toxins than in untreated samples. The work is described as early-stage, with future plans including tests in live animals and making nanorobots from biodegradable materials instead of gold.

The speaker says the team had a strong game after handling many penalties in the first period, but that they are only halfway to their goal and still have work left. They note they have not won in the building for a long time, but playoffs are different and expect Jersey to play hard tomorrow. They describe practice at this time of year as mainly for loosening up, emphasizing that the game is what matters. The speaker also says shutting down top lines is key in the playoffs, aiming to keep top scorers off the puck. They mention Arnott’s power-play goal and stress taking away space, using strong back pressure and standing up at the blue line, supported by the speed and pressure of players including Tanguay, Hejduk, Drury, Nieminen, and Ryan.

Brett Veach, Kansas City Chiefs general manager, is entering the three-day NFL draft without a first-round pick but with one second-round and two third-round selections. He previously made multiple draft-related moves, including trading picks for players such as Reggie Ragland and Cam Erving, and trading Alex Smith for Kendall Fuller plus a third-round pick. The Chiefs and Veach expect him to trade aggressively if certain players fall, and he said he has prepared extensively for draft decision-making. The team is expected to prioritize fixing defensive holes early, while also supporting a young, unproven quarterback situation after Patrick Mahomes II took over, potentially with more offensive talent. The passage lists possible local prospects, notes past draft successes and failures on defense, and highlights Pro Bowl-caliber bargains like Tyreek Hill and Kareem Hunt.

In Oxley et al. v. Oldden, a reference was made, and referees examined the evidence with both parties present and agreed on a report, which was signed the preceding day. About an hour before it was delivered to court, L. B. McKean for the defendant obtained a rule to show cause why the rule of reference should be struck off. There was no allegation of irregularity or partiality against the referees. After arguments by Lewis for the plaintiffs and Ingersott and J. B. McKean for the defendant, the rule to show cause was discharged. McKean, Chief Justice, stated the motion was too late to annul the reference since the referees had investigated the entire transaction, agreed on their report, and were clear of any misconduct or refusal to hear offered testimony.

Stifel reported that GrubHub (NYSE: GRUB) investors have gained more than 200% over the past year and said the stock’s risk-reward profile is now balanced. Stifel downgraded GrubHub from Buy to Hold and raised its price target from $100 to $110. The analyst cited an encouraging outlook, including a partnership with Yum! Brands (NYSE: YUM) expected to generate “material” incremental delivery revenue by 2019 and GrubHub’s expansion into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Stifel lifted 2019 revenue estimates by 2% to $1.18 billion and raised the EPS estimate from $2.19 to $2.24, while noting that the stock’s strong past performance and elevated valuation multiples (31.5x 2019 EV/EBITDA and 1.7x 2010 EV/GFS) should be considered. Shares were down 1.6% in Monday morning trading.

The passage describes Katalin Karikó receiving a Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine in October 2023 for her work on mRNA, which helped enable rapid development of COVID-19 vaccines. It explains that Nobel Prizes honor only narrow areas of science and can exclude many fields and contributors, partly due to the prize categories and how winners are selected. It outlines the Nobel Prize’s origins from Alfred Nobel’s will and notes that awarding involves evaluating nominated people to determine if they made a discovery. The passage also discusses patterns in who wins, including underrepresentation of women, racial minorities, and winners often coming from wealthy research environments. It highlights that Nobel recognition usually requires major, long-recognized discoveries and that winners are typically lab heads. It concludes that while many important sciences may not qualify, recipients and others view the Nobel as important for celebrating and publicizing science’s impact.

The passage describes the role of football kickers, emphasizing that they are often paid less than other skill players while having pressure-filled responsibilities to help teams score via extra points and field goals. It explains scoring values, typical kick distances, and expected accuracy rates, and notes that kickers also handle kickoffs, situational kicks such as onside kicks, and may sub in for punters if injured. The passage discusses why kickers are called “kickers” and “placekickers,” lists abbreviations, and outlines required skills (accuracy, lower-body power, consistent technique, flexibility) and typical body estimates. It names Justin Tucker, Morten Andersen, and Adam Vinatieri as notable kickers with specific achievements. Finally, it explains why kickers are important to coaching decisions, especially in close games, and how they affect special teams outcomes through touchbacks and accurate directional kicking.

The passage describes a patent continuation and incorporates related applications and documents about deep learning, convolutional neural networks, and atrous (dilated) convolutions. It outlines the technology’s field and background in machine learning, neural networks, and training methods, including backpropagation and optimization. It explains CNN components (convolution layers, non-linear layers, dilated convolutions, sub-sampling/pooling, residual and skip connections, batch normalization, 1D convolution, and global average pooling) and their roles. It then provides genomic-focused implementations using trained atrous CNNs (e.g., “SpliceNet” variants) to score nucleotides as donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, or non-splicing sites, using triplet scoring and classification based on highest scores. Additional implementations use differences in splice-site scores between reference and variant sequences to detect aberrant splicing and classify variants as pathogenic or benign, with thresholding methods.

The passage is an email newsletter from VentureWire dated May 31, 2001 to jdasovic@enron.com. It summarizes venture capital activity and includes articles and listings covering fund closures, investments, product launches, bad news, new deals, M&A, new directors and personnel, and fund news. Featured items include Insight Capital closing Fund IV with $740 million, Whitney & Co. spinning off international offices, Rho Ventures closing Fund IV with $435 million, and Quake raising a $30 million second-round investment. It also reports several individual funding rounds and transactions across biotech, technology, and financial services, such as Arexis raising $4.5 million, Remedyne raising $3.2 million, and multiple acquisitions including Bertelsmann acquiring MyPlay for about $30 million and Metavante acquiring CyberBills.

North Carolina regulators are discussing how to test backyard vegetable gardens near the Chemours Co. plant near Fayetteville after Dutch researchers reported finding GenX and related chemicals in vegetables near a Chemours factory in the Netherlands. The Dutch study found the chemicals in about 40% of food samples within roughly 2.5 miles of the plant, concluded garden crops were safe, but advised people closest to the plant to limit consumption. In North Carolina, inter-agency talks have not yet decided whether or how to test nearby gardens, though fish tests may be available within a couple of months. The passage also notes that GenX has been used since 2009, there are no federal health standards, the EPA classifies it as an emerging contaminant, and residents have reported concerns and detected GenX in well water.

The passage explains that the higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend but typically indicates weak future short-term gains and is not effective as a short trading strategy. It describes a backtest across S&P 500 (SPY), gold (GLD), and long-term Treasuries (TLT), entering at the close after two consecutive daily bars with higher highs and higher lows and exiting after 1–10 bars using different holding periods. Results show tiny or negative short-term returns, with two-week average gains below random comparisons in SPY and GLD, and negative short-term returns in TLT despite falling interest rates. The passage concludes the pattern is a typical short-term reversal pattern but is not powerful enough on its own to serve as a trading signal.

High-κ materials are important for advanced electronic and energy-storage devices, where high dielectric constant improves capacitance while a wide band gap reduces leakage. SiO₂’s low dielectric constant requires thinning, increasing leakage via quantum tunneling, and ultrathin perovskite oxides face challenges including low-leakage/high-permittivity trade-offs and difficulty integrating with CMOS due to high-temperature processing. Attention has shifted to HfO₂, but its smaller band gap and lower conduction band offset with silicon can increase leakage, and its dielectric constant is lower than other high-κ materials, motivating searches for next-generation materials combining high dielectric constant and wide band gap.  

To enable virtual screening, the passage describes a high-accuracy machine learning (ML) framework that predicts the ionic dielectric tensor εion by factorizing it into Born effective charges (BECs) and phonon properties, predicting BEC tensors with an equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) trained on 928 oxides, and predicting phonon-related quantities using pretrained ML potentials, with SevenNet selected for subsequent calculations. The joint model improves εion prediction accuracy (R2 and RMSE) compared with a direct εion model. Using this approach, the authors virtually screened 8,717 oxide candidates and identified 38 previously unknown high-κ oxides after multiple screening stages that included dynamical stability checks, ML-based dielectric/band-gap filtering using a figure of merit, and validation by first-principles calculations. The passage also reports that 10 of the 38 candidates have already been experimentally synthesized, and most identified candidates contain transition metals with empty d-orbitals.

The speaker says they have not closely analyzed the injured player on the other team and do not feel differently than they did in the home game. They describe the group as focused and ready to play the next day, aiming to perform their best in the series after experiencing multiple games, including an elimination game. After a six-hour plane trip, their last practice focused on loosening up rather than changing systems. The speaker also discusses a player, Marc, who is not present due to health that varies, saying his equipment and place are honored and that he wants to play, though doctors will determine what is possible. The speaker emphasizes that the coach sets the tone, promoting relaxation while staying focused, and notes that they have tried to avoid pressure by enjoying the moment. They credit leadership in the team, including Bergeron, and say they create a positive atmosphere in the dressing room. Finally, they say they need to alter their game based on what they did wrong after yesterday’s game and plan to put it into practice tomorrow.

The passage reports that only one athlete remains going into “Dancing with the Stars” Episode 3. Jordan Chiles is still competing after Baron Davis was eliminated in Episode 2 with an 18 out of 30 points. Episode 3 will be “TikTok night,” and the section will be updated with live results. After the first elimination of Season 34, 12 celebrity contestants remain heading into Week 3; on September 23, 2025, a double elimination sent home Corey Feldman and Jenna Johnson, and Baron Davis and Britt Stewart. The passage also explains that scoring comes from judges (up to 30 points from three judges, converted to a Judges’ Score Percentage) and audience votes (converted to a Public Vote Percentage), combined to determine outcomes. It describes how viewers vote during the live simulcast via ABC website, Disney+ app, or text, with up to 10 votes per couple per voting method, and that only votes cast during the live window in ET/CT are counted.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU and its role in next-generation data centers and cloud GPU systems. It highlights features such as the Ampere GA100 architecture, improved Tensor Cores (including TF32, BF16, and FP64 support), fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, increased HBM2 and L2 cache capacity/bandwidth, Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) virtualization for secure partitioning into up to seven GPU Instances, and third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch for scalable multi-GPU performance. It also discusses supporting technologies and software advances, including CUDA 11 features (asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graphs, and L2 cache residency controls), compatibility with NVIDIA Magnum IO and Mellox interconnect solutions, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and hardware components such as NVJPG decode and optical flow/stereo disparity acceleration. The passage further introduces NVIDIA DGX A100 as a universal AI infrastructure system powered by A100 GPUs and MIG, designed to scale AI workloads from single nodes to large clusters.

Researchers at the University of Edinburgh report that male pattern baldness involves 287 independent genetic signals linked to the trait. In a genome-wide association study of DNA from more than 52,000 mostly middle-aged men in the UK Biobank, they found genetic signals linked across the genome and 40 on the X chromosome. The researchers developed a genetic formula to predict a man’s risk, but said it is too soon to forecast whether and when someone will start losing hair with a blood test. They noted that while the genetic pattern is only somewhat predictive, the findings may help identify those at greatest risk and potential genetic targets for intervention.

In January 2015, Medora Brown joined Sanergy, a company that provides sanitation facilities in Kenya’s urban slums and converts human waste into end products such as fertilizers and insect-based animal feed. In April 2015 she became communications manager and began planning how to expand Sanergy’s social media beyond early efforts on Facebook, Twitter, and its blog. She needed to allocate limited resources to the most effective platforms and develop metrics to show social media’s ROI and impact across different audiences, including slum dwellers, farmers, and investors/donors.  

The passage also describes Sanergy’s background and sanitation approach, the sanitation conditions in Nairobi’s slums that led residents to use unsafe options like “flying toilets,” and Sanergy’s value-chain model. It notes that Kenya’s technology and internet use were increasing alongside mobile phone adoption and that social media use existed but was limited by access and smartphone availability. Within this context, the passage outlines how Sanergy’s brands used or tested social media: Fresh Life had separate social media pages but faced trust and behavior-change challenges; Farm Star used Facebook to develop fertilizer leads and tested WhatsApp and SMS support; and Sanergy corporate focused on fundraising and thought leadership through channels such as its blog, while questioning social media’s effectiveness for major donors.

The passage describes how Mercy University’s School of Education has been strengthened by multiple grant-funded initiatives supporting teacher education, mentoring, curricular innovation, and work with diverse learners. It highlights the 2023 U.S. Department of Education GRAD-PRO (a five-year, $2.8 million PPOHA-funded project) to expand graduate opportunities for Hispanic and other underrepresented students, with graduate-level focus areas including health sciences, education (teacher education with faculty mentoring and induction support), a Faculty Mentoring Fellowship, and business education certificates. It also describes BranchED’s three-year grant (awarded in 2023) to transform teacher preparation by improving quality and diversity through district partnerships, curriculum reviews and updates, and updated instructional practices supported by biweekly coaching and other resources. Additional programs include the NSF-supported MISTI initiative (since 2013) to prepare STEM teachers for high-need schools with intensive observations, seminars, student teaching, and ongoing mentoring; the NSF-funded STEM Master Teaching Fellowship (2019–2024) for pre-K through high school teachers to become STEM teacher leaders through graduate coursework and leadership projects; and Mercy University’s 2023–2028 NYSED CR-ITI/ESOL program (award $687,500) to address ESOL teacher shortages in New York City by providing clinically grounded preparation leading to an Advanced Certificate in ESOL and supporting additional certification. The conclusion states these grants support program improvement, professional learning, career readiness, mentoring, collaboration, and innovation to better serve today’s diverse PK-12 student population.

U.S. mortgage application activity decreased for a second week, dipping 0.8% to 403.6 for the week ended March 24, after 418.1 two weeks earlier. Average interest rates on 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgages fell to 4.33% from 4.46%. Benchmark Treasury yields fell amid doubts about planned tax cuts and infrastructure spending and after House Speaker Paul Ryan shelved an Affordable Care Act overhaul bill.
