Digital leaders report that practices such as adopting a learning mindset, providing transparent data access, using clear metrics to track progress, and aligning the organization with those metrics often lead them to emphasize data culture as a centerpiece. Culture coordinates employee efforts by aligning beliefs, espoused values, and day-to-day actions, which must be consistent and reinforcing. Employee behaviors tend to reflect company values in digital leader firms, driven by leadership core beliefs, while digital laggards often show misalignment due to entrenched habits, lack of individual skills, and insufficient top-down focus. Leaders say changing mindsets and behaviors is the most challenging part of transformation, requiring compelling reasons understood by executives and employees. The passage also describes four cultural patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—based on original culture and technical sophistication, and suggests organizations can target actions to build toward a strong data culture.

The passage discusses challenges in designing efficient RF coil arrays for ultrahigh-field (10.5T) whole-body MRI, including difficulties tuning coils at high Larmor frequencies and increased radiation and electromagnetic coupling that complicate multichannel coil arrays. It proposes a high-impedance microstrip transmission line resonator design aimed at achieving high resonant frequency and improved EM decoupling. A prototype 2-channel 8 cm by 8 cm microstrip array using 3 mm copper tape on a ~2 mm Teflon substrate was designed and tested. Measurements showed that the high-frequency mode tuned to about 447 MHz provided robust decoupling (S21 ≈ -21 dB) at a 10 mm gap between elements, while the low-frequency mode (116 MHz) showed stronger coupling (S21 ≈ -7.6 dB) and did not maintain acceptable decoupling at a 2 mm gap, where its resonant peak split. Numerical simulation with Ansys showed well-defined B1 distribution and reasonable calculated B1+ values, indicating excellent decoupling performance for the high-frequency mode. The authors conclude that the technique is a simple and robust way to design high-frequency transceiver arrays for ultrahigh-field MR applications.

Facebook apologized after its search auto-fill function suggested sexual acts, including with minors. The issue was reportedly noticed when users posted images showing suggestions appearing after typing “videos of.” Facebook said it removed the offensive predictions and stated that search suggestions reflect what people may search for and are not necessarily actual content on the platform, and that it does not allow sexually explicit imagery. The passage also mentions that Facebook previously admitted making a “mistake” involving a survey about whether an adult requesting sexual pictures from a 14-year-old should be allowed.

The passage is Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 8-K filed on April 30, 2020 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It reports that Amazon.com announced its first quarter 2020 financial results and states that a copy of the press release is included as Exhibit 99.1 and additional non-GAAP financial measure information is included as Exhibit 99.2. The filing also lists Exhibit 99.1, Exhibit 99.2, and an Inline XBRL cover page as Exhibit 104, and it is signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage argues that using AI for master scheduling can meet student needs and save money. It describes how declining enrollment and ESSER funding gaps forced districts to serve more students with disabilities and multilingual learners with fewer resources, making across-the-board cuts harmful. The authors say master schedules are a key budgeting lever because they determine teacher time, classroom assignment, and spending. They report that AI-optimization helped Lubbock Independent and Edgewood Independent rebalance class sizes and workloads, producing savings of $2.2 million across 14 schools in Lubbock and $1.05 million districtwide in Edgewood. The passage also explains that AI can analyze large numbers of scheduling scenarios more efficiently than manual reconciliation, supporting student-centered scheduling decisions. It concludes that better master scheduling tools, especially AI, are important for districts facing financial uncertainty, and emphasizes that AI is meant to support scheduling teams rather than replace teacher judgment.

The passage describes a Reuters report from June 30, 2016, noting that investors wary of Brexit have placed record bets against the pound. Some analysts warn that sterling may rise in April, which could hurt those who are short. It says sterling has risen in April by an average of about 2% over the past 12 years, though a Reuters analysis finds the consistent April gain versus the dollar mainly appears after 2004. Speculators’ net short positions reached record highs in the week to March 21, then eased slightly. Nomura cites a pattern of sterling-dollar upside in April as a “risk to watch,” and Bank of America Merrill Lynch suggests factors such as the end of the UK tax year and dividend payouts from UK multinationals. Investors remain cautious due to recent pound strength and short positions near record levels.

The passage describes Active Surfaces, a company founded in 2022 by MIT-based research, with a mission to integrate solar energy into everyday spaces using ultra-lightweight, flexible solar panels. It also outlines the company’s manufacturing approach using roll-to-roll printing to achieve high efficiency and low cost, and summarizes the co-founders’ backgrounds in solar R&D, printed electronics, energy policy, and strategy. The passage then lists fictional transactions for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, including issuing common stock, paying for insurance, opening and drawing on a revolving line of credit, purchasing office supplies on credit and paying them later, buying manufacturing equipment, paying a legal retainer (with part refunded), completing and billing a pilot project and receiving payment after a period, paying off the line of credit, receiving a down payment for a future order, procuring raw materials in cash, recognizing insurance expense and depreciation by year-end, and recording related outcomes. Suggested assignment questions ask to record transactions, prepare a year-end balance sheet, and calculate net income and cash flow based only on these fictional transactions.

Audi’s e-tron prototype, a precursor to its series-production battery-electric SUV, has a drag coefficient of 0.28. Audi says this contributes to a WLTP range of more than 400 kilometers and that a 0.01 change in the drag coefficient corresponds to about a five-kilometer range difference. Engineers optimized drag and noise in Audi’s Wind Tunnel Center in Ingolstadt, which used a 2.6 MW fan running up to 300 km/h, with the prototype tested for over 1,000 hours. To reach the 0.28 coefficient, Audi developed aerodynamics measures across the body, including solutions that reduce drag by about 0.07 compared with a comparable conventionally powered vehicle, increasing WLTP range by around 35 kilometers per battery charge under a typical usage profile. Features include optional virtual exterior mirrors with integrated cameras and adaptable views, an adaptive air suspension that lowers the body at speeds above 120 km/h, a fully enclosed and paneled underbody with protective battery elements shaped to improve airflow, a controllable cool-air inlet with adjustable louvers and ducts for cooling, side air inlets directing air around aerodynamically optimized 19-inch wheels, ultralow rolling resistance tires, and negative tire lettering.

Volunteers from Year 6 at Swallowdale Primary School joined members of the PTA group Friends of Swallowdale to clean a bus in preparation for renovating it into a quiet reading space. The school announced in January it would redecorate the bus, with support from the community, and assistant head teacher Gail Edwards said the bus was being prepared for carpeting and painting after its seats were removed and it was made safe. The bus will be painted as a woodland scene featuring book characters chosen by the children, hiding among the trees to match its position by the school garden. The project is expected to take most of the academic year, and the school is looking for someone with upholstery skills to recover the driver and back row seats.

Observing two objects leads to recognizing similarity/distance, but defining or quantifying it is difficult because similarity/distance is multidimensional and cannot be uniquely formalized. Since objects from various domains are often modeled as graphs, graph similarity/distance measures are important and have been used in network analysis, chemoinformatics, and social sciences to quantitatively assess structural resemblance. The paper surveys key measures, starting with exact graph matching approaches such as Sussenguth’s exact matching, Zelinka’s isomorphism-based distance using the largest common induced subgraph, and later generalizations by Sobik and Kaden. It also discusses inexact matching via graph edit distance (GED) and other methods like graph kernels and approaches based on topological indices or feature vectors, noting that prior work often uses a single index or that converting many indices into a binary representation can reduce sensitivity. The paper aims to develop a more sensitive, less computationally demanding method for larger graphs, and outlines applications in network theory and chemistry, including analysis on random graph models and decane isomers. It then defines similarity and distance measures, explains conversions between them, and introduces graph-based measures using scaled topological indices, defining a framework for computing a distance between graphs.

A Jefferies analysis using Morning Consult data found Disney and Disney+ sentiment and brand awareness fell to their lowest levels in at least two years in the two weeks after Disney temporarily halted Jimmy Kimmel’s show and raised Disney+ prices. Sentiment declined among both Democrats and Republicans, with Democrats souring more strongly. The backlash cited Kimmel’s prior comments and Disney’s decision to halt production, with critics arguing Disney was appeasing President Donald Trump’s administration. Jefferies also noted Disney’s overall brand awareness rose in the past two years, while Disney+’s rise was smaller, which the analyst said could limit streaming churn. Disney shares dropped 6% over the last month, but Jefferies reaffirmed a buy rating and a $144 price target.

Functional emulsifier blends are mixtures used for emulsification, commonly in oil- and water-based emulsions. The ice-cream industry buys blends from specialized firms and primary suppliers. North America is expected to dominate the market due to major food production centers and operations of key suppliers like ADM and Cargill, while APAC’s emerging food processing investments are expected to drive the fastest growth. Demand is increased by food safety concerns, rising demand across industries, and benefits such as improved hydrophile-lipophile balance and product feel. The market growth is supported by R&D investments and formulation innovations, though processing challenges, food complexity, and restrictions on GMO-based blends in some countries may limit growth. Key players include Futura Ingredients, BASF, Evonik, Kerry, Cargill, ADM, and others. Growth opportunities are linked to increased adoption in bakery and confectionery, processed foods, and health awareness; expansion is a common strategy among major players. Food and beverages are expected to be major consumers, with bakery as a leading segment, while growth is projected to be higher in personal care products over the forecast period.

The passage argues that early Americans saw no “middle course” between submission to a foreign legislature and complete independence, and that the main dangers were not foreign fleets and armies but disputes over government forms. It describes the Revolutionary period and the need for a Confederation that was later viewed as not durable, citing widespread consequences from negligence and disunity, including declining commerce, loss of faith, and insurrections. It then states that during the crisis measures were pursued to form “a more perfect union” and produce the present Constitution. The author says they first saw the Constitution abroad, approved it, and later supported it in office, attributing peace, order, prosperity, and happiness to its operation. The passage praises a representative government as reflecting the people’s power and majesty, warns that elections can be corrupted by single-vote majorities or foreign influence, and discusses abuses and foreign influence as threats to the system. It concludes by listing the author’s principles and duties for supporting the Constitution and seeking justice, peace, neutrality, education, and goodwill with other nations, and it ends with a call for divine blessing on the nation and government.

The passage is a wartime address to American coal miners during a “serious crisis” in which the United States is in active battle against enemies worldwide. The speaker describes returning from a tour observing training, war production, farming needed for troops and allies, and soldiers being equipped. He argues that coal production must not stop, warning that even a short coal-supply interruption could endanger American soldiers and sailors and affect victory. He states that after assurances of no strikes were given by major labor organizations following Pearl Harbor, disputes were referred to the War Labor Board, which sought facts from miners and operators. He says the national officers of the United Mine Workers declined to participate, and that stoppages began while the Board was proceeding, leading to a general strike. The speaker says the government took over the mines and calls miners to return to work, citing service of miners’ sons overseas and wounded soldiers. He also discusses wartime efforts to control living costs and concludes by asserting miners will not continue a strike against the government, with mining to resume under the American flag.

Her Highness Sheikha Jawaher Al Qasimi made remarks during her visit to the 10th Sharjah Children’s Reading Festival at Expo Centre Sharjah under the theme “Your Future… Just a Book Away.” She said children’s learning shapes future values and that an attitude of learning supports civilization. During the visit, she toured the festival halls, visited publishers’ stands, joined children’s workshops, and attended a reading session. She highlighted SCRF’s importance in inspiring reading, knowledge, innovation, and a culturally aware generation, noting the participation of children from different nationalities and cultures. She also praised books for restoring harmony and described SCRF as evidence of Sharjah’s role in globally recognised cultural events and as a conduit for knowledge, literature, and art. She praised the Sharjah Book Authority for organizing the festival and urged families and institutions to visit, emphasizing SCRF’s aim to foster awareness of books and openness to global creativity and art.

The passage describes Google’s involvement in “Project Maven,” a Pentagon project to develop AI that analyzes drone footage. After public discovery in March, thousands of employees expressed opposition via a petition, and about a dozen employees resigned in May. Google said its work with the Department of Defense would be used for non-offensive purposes and later reported developing ethical guidelines to guide future defense contract decisions, including precluding the use of AI in weaponry, though it remains uncertain whether this will ease concerns.

The passage is a collection of headlines and promotional text related to education news and commentary, including topics such as a teen called the “Barefoot Bandit,” school integration and related documentaries, American Idol winner Jamal Roberts, legal action involving vape distributors, education policy under the Every Student Succeeds Act, and various stories about schools, students, and teachers. It also includes calls to make donations to The 74.

Human rights education (HRE) at the early childhood education and care (ECEC) level has grown in attention, but the passage says research is lacking on educational content and on research-based guidance for ECEC teachers to select such content. It argues this is important because education is not politically neutral, especially amid political instability and authoritarian voices. The study examines the function of four content selection dimensions—children’s ages, progression, human rights knowledge anchored in social studies, and children’s own interests—for discussing HRE content at the ECEC level, using the Norwegian ECEC context and posts from the online resource Idebroen about observing UN Day.

HRE is described as including knowledge, skills, values, attitudes, behaviours, and actions to defend and promote human rights, and the Norwegian framework plan requires staff to give children early insight into human rights, especially the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), though it provides few specific guidelines. The paper outlines a theoretical basis linking HRE in ECEC to social studies didactics and judicial perspectives, and it presents how progression and age should guide adaptation of content.

Methodologically, the study analyzes multimodal Idebroen posts identified through keywords “rights” and “UN Day,” excluding posts with little information, and conducts directed/theoretical content analysis using the four dimensions. Findings report that ideas for observing UN Day are often planned and adapted to children’s groups, include cross-curricular teaching, and commonly approach UN Day through human rights, diversity, and/or fundraising. The results also note that while many posts refer to human rights values, few specify particular human rights articles or children’s entitlements, and links to the CRC are often limited. The discussion concludes that applying the four dimensions can structure subject-didactic thinking and support teacher planning, but highlights challenges such as ensuring age-appropriate and rights-precise content, maintaining progression, and better aligning activities with children’s interests and legal anchoring in human rights instruments. The study calls for further research using additional empirical data.

The passage describes the Nobel Peace Prize being awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN), framed as a signal to encourage negotiations and prevent nuclear escalation involving North Korea and the United States. It notes that the Nobel committee’s language referenced nuclear nations and that Nobel historian Oeivind Stenersen said the prize also functioned as coded support for the Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA). The committee did not award prizes to Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif or former U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and the United States said it does not support or will not sign ICAN-backed the “Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons,” while stressing commitment to conditions for nuclear disarmament. The text adds that ICAN helped win UN backing for the treaty by 122 countries, though none of the nine nuclear powers or suspected nuclear states listed put their names down. It then details rising tensions and aggressive rhetoric between North Korea and the Trump administration, including references to possible missile tests and Trump’s comments about North Korea, contrasting with North Korea’s insults and threats. The passage concludes that the award is intended to put attention on Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump and that the world should look harder at nuclear escalation risks.

The passage describes a presidential message following President Harding’s death, emphasizing reconsecration to public service. It outlines foreign policy principles of peace, justice, American independence, opposition to joining the League of Nations, and support for a World Court. It discusses resuming relations with Russia while refusing relations with regimes that reject international obligations, and it covers international debts and American claims. Domestic topics include the reorganization of the foreign service; fiscal stability through retrenchment and a budget system; tax reductions and reforms; tariff administration; shipping and transportation policies; public improvements; railroad legislation concerns; judicial reforms and prison treatment; enforcement of prohibition; protection of Black citizens’ rights and responses to lynching; civil service expansion; regulatory measures for pollution, aviation, radio, and navigation; strengthening the Army and Navy; and administration in insular possessions. The passage also addresses education and welfare, restricted immigration, veterans’ care, coal pricing and regulation proposals, governmental reorganization, agricultural relief through organization and reduced burdens, sale of Muscle Shoals subject to wartime rights and fertilizer goals, reclamation charge adjustments, support for highways and reforestation, and the continued importance of the Monroe Doctrine with added responsibilities toward global stability and peace.

Toronto’s transit commission said most of its new streetcars must be returned to Bombardier for preventative repairs due to “inferior frame welds.” The first 67 of 89 streetcars will be sent back, with no safety risk, and all will be fixed by 2022. Bombardier will pay for the repairs at its Welding Centre of Excellence in La Pocatiere, Quebec, returning cars three or four at a time. The maintenance program will involve 25 to 30 employees daily and may delay planned layoffs, and Bombardier guarantees the strength of existing welds until preventive maintenance is performed. The issue was identified 18 months ago and relates to work completed in Mexico.

Ohio State University researchers report that exhausted T cells in cancer are overwhelmed by misfolded proteins, which activates a stress response pathway called TexPSR (proteotoxic stress response in T-cell exhaustion). Unlike ordinary stress responses that slow protein production, TexPSR accelerates protein synthesis, causing toxic protein buildup that cripples T cells’ ability to attack tumors. The researchers say blocking key drivers of TexPSR restored T-cell function and improved cancer immunotherapy in preclinical models. They also found that high TexPSR levels in T cells from cancer patients were linked to poor clinical responses to immunotherapy, and that the mechanism was validated across multiple cancer models, including lung, bladder, liver cancer, and leukemia.

The passage transmits the Kansas constitution and related materials to the U.S. Senate after J. Calhoun provides a certified copy, and it argues that Kansas is in “almost open rebellion” because many residents have rejected the territorial government and sought a rival Topeka government backed by force. It cites correspondence from Governor Walker describing attempts to prevent or respond to rebellion, including organizing insurrection under a Topeka legislature and disregarding territorial laws. The passage claims that Topeka leadership defies U.S. law and that opponents refused to vote for delegates to the Lecompton convention and later refused to vote on slavery. It asserts that Congress must decide admission of Kansas under the Lecompton constitution and states the author supports admission to end agitation, localize the slavery issue, and withdraw U.S. troops from Kansas. It also includes a proclamation regarding the rebellion in Utah, stating that Utah settlers resist U.S. authority, threatening federal enforcement. The proclamation orders federal officers and citizens to assist law execution, offers a full pardon to those who submit, warns persistent rebels of punishment, and declares military forces will remain until Utah complies.

The passage explains flexible working for carers, including common options, eligibility rules, how to request it, and employers’ responsibilities. It notes that employees in England, Scotland, and Wales can request flexible working after 26 weeks of employment, with only one application allowed in any 12-month period. Employers must consider requests seriously and respond within three months, though they can refuse for valid business reasons. If a request is refused, the employee can ask for an explanation, use an appeal process if available, or take the matter to an employment tribunal within three months, but only if the decision was handled unreasonably or was unfair. The page also highlights challenges of balancing work and caring responsibilities and lists related guidance and publications dates.

Galesburg resident Robert Stevens receives monthly hydrocodone-acetaminophen deliveries from the Iowa City Veterans Affairs Health Care System, but in May his medicine could not be found at the post office. Stevens said other veterans have also reported missing pills. In Abingdon, veteran Gary Kilpatrick reported pills going missing multiple times after delivery. Abingdon Police Chief Ken Jones said there are two cases but it is hard to track down the cause. Bryan Clark of the Iowa City VA said there have been multiple reports of prescription drug theft in the Galesburg area and that it is under investigation.

The passage is from NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 26, 2020. It includes condensed consolidated financial statements (unaudited) showing three-month results: revenue of $3,080 million for the period ended April 26, 2020 versus $2,220 million for April 28, 2019, net income of $917 million versus $394 million, and net income per share (diluted) of $1.47 versus $0.64. It also provides balance sheet information as of April 26, 2020 and January 26, 2020, and a summary of shareholders’ equity, cash flows, and notes. Key note disclosures cover accounting policies, adoption of a credit-loss standard, the April 27, 2020 Mellanox acquisition, leases, stock-based compensation, income taxes, cash equivalents and marketable securities, fair value measurements, intangible assets, balance sheet components, derivative instruments, debt issuances and terms, commitments and contingencies including legal proceedings, and segment information (changed to “Graphics” and “Compute & Networking”). The management discussion describes the COVID-19 impact, first quarter highlights, liquidity and capital resources, and controls and procedures, with additional legal and risk factor discussion.

The passage describes NVIDIA Turing GPU features and supporting technologies. It explains hardware support for USB Type-C and the VirtualLink standard to connect VR headsets through a single connector, and it outlines Turing GPU architecture details such as TU102’s GPC/TPC/SM structure, CUDA/Tensor/RT cores, memory controllers, and cache. It covers performance-oriented architectural changes, including concurrent FP32/INT32 execution, unified L1/shared memory and improved L2/cache behavior, and revised memory/compression approaches with GDDR6. The text also details Turing Tensor Cores for AI workloads (including DLSS, inpainting, slow-motion, and super-resolution) and summarizes Tesla T4 and other Turing-based GPUs. For ray tracing, it describes RT cores, BVH traversal/intersection acceleration, hybrid rendering with denoising, and how ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections compare to rasterization methods. It further discusses data center/VR enhancements such as NVLink for multi-GPU connectivity, enhanced video encode/decode, Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, resource/binding model changes, and VR audio acceleration. The passage ends with legal/specification disclaimers.

The passage describes Ferrari’s strategy to balance tradition and innovation while pursuing “controlled growth” in 2024 and 2025. It outlines Ferrari’s financial growth, plans to expand into growth markets and add new models (including its first fully electric vehicle slated for 2025), and the need to innovate while preserving brand heritage. It summarizes the luxury performance market and Ferrari’s position within it, including emphasis on exclusive, emotional luxury rather than utility. The text also covers Ferrari’s history and brand identity linked to Enzo Ferrari and Formula 1, the company’s lifestyle and customer “Ferraristi” community approach, its dealer network and services, vehicle categories and personalization programs, and its production and R&D practices. Finally, it reviews the broader context for electrification, Ferrari’s hybrid roadmap, EV-related capabilities and infrastructure challenges, and risks associated with controlled growth.

First lady Melania Trump responded on Twitter after almost three weeks without public appearances. In a tweet on Wednesday, she said she was at the White House with her family, “feeling great” and working on behalf of children and the American people, while criticizing media speculation. Her communications director Stephanie Grisham retweeted the message. Melania’s last public appearance was May 10, and her office said she had a successful minor kidney procedure at Walter Reed on May 14. Concerns about her well-being during her absence included social media theories about plastic surgery or relocating, which her office dismissed.

The European Commission issued final warnings to Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and Britain for repeated breaches of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) pollution limits. The Commission said NO2 pollution, much of it from road traffic, poses a serious health risk and that EU rules require member countries to protect citizens. If the countries do not respond satisfactorily within two months, the Commission may take the case to the Court of Justice of the European Union.

The passage outlines five guiding principles for early childhood education and care (ECEC) for children aged 1–5: prioritize the early years for holistic development (including brain plasticity and social-emotional growth); create a nurturing, safe, inclusive, and stimulating environment with emotional support; focus on quality in ECEC through long-term benefits, positive teacher-child interactions, evidence-based child-centered curriculum, continuous professional development, and inclusivity; engage families as key partners by leveraging the home learning environment, supporting collaboration, understanding cultural contexts, empowering families, and maintaining feedback and communication; and promote continuous professional development for ECEC educators. It concludes that emphasizing these principles supports children’s future academic and life success and benefits society.

Tyrus Capital S.A.M. bought 182,400 shares of Reynolds American, Inc. (NYSE:RAI) in the second quarter, valued at about $11,863,000. Reynolds American is about 0.9% of Tyrus Capital’s portfolio and is its 14th largest holding. The passage also reports additional stake increases by Vanguard Group Inc., BlackRock Inc., State Street Corp, and FMR LLC, along with an earlier increase by American International Group Inc. It states that 46.34% of Reynolds American’s stock is owned by institutional investors. Analyst ratings are listed with a consensus of “Hold” and an average target price of $59.82. The passage includes recent trading information and a description of Reynolds American’s operating segments.

The passage lists 10 Vanguard ETFs, outlines John Bogle’s advocacy for passive “buy and hold,” and describes backtesting of each ETF from inception to the present with dividends reinvested. It also summarizes each ETF’s target index and general investment approach, including S&P 500 (VOO), S&P 500 Value (VOOV), S&P 500 Growth (VOOG), Total World Stock (VT), Total International Stock (VXUS), Real Estate (VNQ via REITs), and long-term bond ETFs (BLV, VGLT, VCLT) plus Total International Bond (BNDX). It further includes brief explanations of the buy-and-hold strategy, differences among the S&P 500 ETFs, and the role of VNQ in a long-term portfolio.

Pakistan’s national flag was flown at 400 feet at the Attari-Wagah border with India to mark the country’s 70th Independence Day. The 120x80 feet flag, described as the highest in South Asia and the largest in Pakistan’s history, was hoisted near the border by Army chief Gen Qamar Javed Bajwa after midnight, starting Independence Day celebrations. In his speech, Gen Bajwa referenced the 27th Ramadan and Pakistan’s foundation, spoke about progress under the law and constitution, and discussed challenges while promising to respond to terrorists and protect Pakistan. Other speakers also paid tributes to those killed during migration to Pakistan.

Ted Hannah addresses the graduates of 2018 from the perspective of the class of 1959, noting they share early years in Summerland but grew up in a different world shaped by the Great Depression, WWII, and wartime displacement. He describes growing up without television or internet, learning through schooling starting in 1947, participating in sports and youth activities, and choosing from six NHL teams via radio. He recalls post-graduation paths such as education and trades, family life, and staying connected through anniversaries and Christmas cards. He encourages the 2018 grads to value relationships, reach out to others, volunteer, and help improve others’ lives, wishing them to live well and happily.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 3, 2019, reporting that on May 7, 2019 it closed underwritten public offerings of (1) 3,549,381 shares of common stock (including 462,962 shares sold under the underwriters’ option exercised May 3, 2019) and (2) $1.84 billion aggregate principal amount of 2.00% Convertible Senior Notes due May 15, 2024 (including $240.0 million of option notes under the underwriters’ option exercised May 3, 2019). The offerings were made under a Registration Statement on Form S-3 and accompanying prospectus materials. In connection with the notes, Tesla entered into a Fifth Supplemental Indenture dated May 7, 2019, and the report describes key terms of the notes, including interest, conversion rate, conversion conditions, settlement upon conversion, restrictions on redemption, ranking, and events of default. Tesla also entered into additional note hedge transactions and additional warrant transactions with specified hedge counterparties, including paying approximately $475.8 million for note hedges and receiving approximately $174.4 million from sale of warrants at closing. The filing lists related exhibits and is signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer.

The passage describes updates and requirements for the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), including non-automatic exits (NAEs), GHCB/VMGEXIT protocol behavior, and versioning and feature advertisement. It explains how SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state so the hypervisor cannot directly access it, and how Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs) let the guest decide what register state to expose via the GHCB. It also standardizes the GHCB memory area (4 KB mapped decrypted by the guest), supported NAE event handling and VALID_BITMAP usage, and several specific NAEs such as #VC-triggered handling, #NPF/MMIO access, page state changes, SNP guest request/extended guest request, APIC ID list retrieval, SNP AP creation, doorbell page (#HV) support, #HV IPI and timer, and Secure AVIC. Additionally, it covers termination requests, guest identification of SEV-ES support via CPUID properties, SMP booting challenges under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP, non-maskable interrupt handling guidance, and states that nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

The chapter discusses finding minimal trellis representations for binary linear block codes, using a state space theorem and trellis-oriented generator matrices. The procedure reduces a generator matrix greedily to minimum-span form so that generator starting and ending times determine the minimal state spaces and the state dimension profile, which in turn gives minimal trellis realizations. The state space dimensions at each cut time can be read from how many generators are active, and branch space dimensions at each symbol time can also be determined by counting active generators, which relates to Viterbi decoding complexity. The passage also explains properties under duality for state space sizes, introduces sectionalization to trade apparent state complexity while noting that branch complexity cannot be reduced, and derives bounds relating trellis dimensions to code parameters such as block length, dimension, and minimum distance (nominal coding gain). It further covers projections and an alternate form of the state space theorem using dimensions of projected and subcode spaces, with examples including Reed–Muller codes and their resulting trellis structures. The instructor concludes by noting upcoming topics (Muder bound and comparisons to convolutional code trellises) and homework instructions.

After the Monday Night Football game between the Miami Dolphins and New England Patriots, the NFL regular season is down to three final gameweeks. The passage provides an early Week 15 slate with odds and predictions for multiple matchups, including the Broncos over the Colts (20-17), the Lions over the Bears (24-13), and the Jaguars over the Texans (38-7). It also projects outcomes for games such as Chargers over Chiefs (21-20), Cardinals over Redskins (24-17), Ravens over Browns (20-10), Vikings over Bengals (34-10), Seahawks over Rams (24-23), Falcons over Buccaneers (27-17), 49ers over Titans (implied 49ers favored by 2), Steelers over Patriots (24-23), Panthers over Packers (31-27, assuming Rodgers plays status-dependent), Saints over Jets (31-7, assuming Petty starts), Eagles over Giants (24-10, assuming Foles starts), and Bills over Dolphins (24-17, assuming Taylor starts). Some games have no lines due to uncertain quarterback status or injury news, including Rodgers, McCown, Wentz, and Taylor.

The passage consists of social media posts reacting to commentary about Mike Pence and LGBT activism. It mentions claims by John Oliver and others that they “owned” Pence with a book about Pence’s pet rabbit, while some commenters call the reactions “pathetic,” “lol owned,” and argue that Pence is not negatively affected and continues to be polite and friendly. Others share images and claims that pride flags appear in photos of Pence during a St. Patrick’s Day event. Chad Felix Greene criticizes LGBT activists for misrepresenting Pence’s positions and argues that religious freedom is not discrimination, while another commenter disputes arguments and mentions Greene wrote an overview with citations. The passage ends with “This is the Left.”

The passage describes zeenews.india.com’s cookie policy, explaining that cookies and other tracking technologies may be stored on and accessed from a user’s device when visiting the site. It defines cookies and similar technologies, states that the site uses them to identify devices, remember preferences, track usage, protect the sites, administer content, and process user requests, including through third-party service providers for statistical usage analysis. It outlines first-party and third-party cookies, the use of persistent and session cookies, user options to refuse or block cookies and delete stored cookies, and the potential impact on site functionality. It categorizes cookies as essential, analytical/performance, functionality, and advertising cookies, including targeted advertising enabled by third parties. It also provides references for information on targeting/advertising cookies and gives a contact email for questions.

The passage is a class discussion reviewing a case about ReCellular and debating its viability, then moving to a Whirlpool case about reverse logistics options. For ReCellular, students describe the business model as repurposing donated cellphones for other markets, with disagreements about whether it will remain viable due to factors like technology evolution, changing phone pricing, standards across countries, and the need to shift from donations to purchasing phones. The discussion then introduces Whirlpool options: an industry-funded organization (IFO), Whirlpool operating a closed-loop system, or opposing regulation. Students argue that much recycling already happens naturally (reported around 95% to 99%), but that regulation may still be needed for specific materials and changing incentives. For IFO vs. closed loop, students discuss costs, economies of scale, network design, operational barriers, and calculations estimating IFO-related collection costs and comparing them to Whirlpool’s forward distribution costs. The professor explains how IFO typically works through retailers/dealers and how closed-loop would require Whirlpool to take back products, emphasizing the operational complexity and need for volume and partnerships. The session concludes by outlining upcoming student project presentations and a future case study with assigned calculations.

An SDXC card initialized with XPC=0 operates up to 0.36W (100mA at 3.6V on VDD1) in Default Speed or SDR12 and indicates Class 0 in SD Status if it does not support Speed Class. With XPC=1, it operates up to 0.54W (150mA at 3.6V on VDD1) in Default Speed or SDR12 and supports Speed Class; re-initialization is required to change XPC. In UHS-I, the host sets S18R=1 in ACMD41 to request a switch to 1.8V signaling, the card responds with S18A=1 (in 3.3V mode), and after a voltage switch the card sets S18A=0; in UHS-II mode, the card always indicates S18A=0. Fast Boot (Bit 29) is reserved for eSD.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended May 1, 2016. The report includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements showing revenue of $1,305 million for the three months ended May 1, 2016 (vs. $1,151 million for the three months ended April 26, 2015), net income of $196 million (vs. $134 million), and net income per diluted share of $0.33 (vs. $0.24). Balance sheets as of May 1, 2016 report total assets of $7,108 million and total liabilities (including convertible debt conversion obligation and shareholders’ equity) of $7,108 million, with cash and cash equivalents of $547 million and marketable securities of $4,207 million. Notes describe accounting policies, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities fair value and impairment reviews, derivatives, guarantees and product warranty liabilities, convertible senior notes due 2018, operating lease financing for a new headquarters building, legal proceedings, and share repurchase activity, including a $500 million accelerated share repurchase agreement and $62 million cash dividends during the quarter. The filing also contains segment information, management’s discussion and analysis covering results of operations, liquidity, capital resources, market risk, and controls and procedures, and indicates that disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of May 1, 2016.

The passage discusses a team’s confidence in a player named Matt and Geno, emphasizing their ability to respond to changing circumstances, make timely plays, and contribute to playoff success. It also outlines coaching beliefs about keeping players active with their instincts while making calculated decisions and playing the “right way.” The passage notes playoff trends of fewer penalties and describes challenges from last night’s game, especially difficulties with clean entries and limited zone time, which reduced power-play opportunities. It concludes by praising players, including Brian Dumoulin, for evolved roles across special teams and strong defensive efforts such as shot blocking and penalty killing.

The passage describes individual defending in soccer in a 1v1 situation against an opposing dribbler or ball carrier. It explains that a defender should get goal side, take a proper stance, and react based on teammate positioning: use “aggressive defending” when the defense is set, or use “attack stalling” when the defense needs time to recover. Aggressive defending includes cutting off the ball, tackling at the moment the opponent receives it or kicking the ball away, interposing between the dribbler and the ball, or preventing the dribbler from turning to face the goal. Attack stalling involves delaying or controlling the dribbler to allow more defenders to arrive. It also outlines one-on-one defensive tactics such as staying goal side, keeping a clean stance, not overreacting to feints, denying passes or shots, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler’s vision, and specific movements like jockeying, shepherding, stealing the ball, standing one’s ground, and tackling. The passage emphasizes the importance of verbal communication from teammates to the 1v1 defender, typically instructing them to “delay” (contain, delay him, jockey, stand him up) or to “tackle” (challenge, tackle, take him). It concludes with instruction and practice guidance for coaches and defenders, including teaching stances, movement changes by location, techniques, communication meanings, and using drills with and without a ball.

The Michigan State Police responded to a suicide threat on I-696 in Detroit, closing all lanes in both directions after a call around 1 a.m. They organized 13 semi truck drivers to remain under a bridge to shorten the distance the man would fall if he jumped. After several hours, the situation ended peacefully when the man walked off the bridge and was taken to Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak for evaluation. The report also includes information about the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline.

The passage describes wireless uplink data transmission control when a device is in an enhanced coverage state, aiming to reduce power consumption. Enhanced coverage uses repeated transmissions to extend a base station’s cell coverage, but can increase device battery use (e.g., LTE coverage enhancement modes A and B). The device can identify enhanced coverage based on parameters such as coverage mode/level/class, repetition indicators, radio signal strength/quality, and other factors. The application can then control transmission by refraining from sending uplink data under specified conditions or by instructing the modem to transmit conditionally. Two main solutions are presented: (1) the application queries the modem for radio coverage condition/status and decides whether to refrain from transmitting, and (2) the application instructs the modem to apply transmission restrictions so the modem decides whether to send data. Conditions and restrictions can include coverage thresholds, repetition thresholds, signal strength/quality thresholds, data type, QoS/priority, timers/counters, device movement/speed, battery level thresholds, and whether the device is plugged into power. The passage also discusses using attention (AT) commands/APIs between the application and modem to obtain coverage information or configure restrictions, as well as network-provided configuration parameters via downlink signaling (e.g., Attach Accept, bearer context messages) and relevant information elements for transmission restriction indications.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 26, 2020. The filing reports that on June 26 Microsoft issued a press release announcing a strategic change in its retail operations, including closing Microsoft Store physical locations, and the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report also lists securities registered under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act and includes a signature by Frank H. Brod, Chief Accounting Officer.

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is described as a chronic progressive autoimmune disease affecting an estimated 0.5–1% of North American adults and primarily impacting synovial joints, causing stiffness, major joint pain, and irreversible deformity if untreated. RA prevalence varies by age, gender, and ethnicity, and it commonly co-occurs with conditions such as depression, obesity, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes. The study investigates whether depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) are related to RA association individually or synergistically, and whether these relationships depend on inflammatory status measured by C-reactive protein (CRP). Using NHANES data (2007–2008 and 2009–2010), RA was defined from survey responses identifying rheumatoid arthritis, depression from PHQ-9 scores, obesity from BMI, and HTG from serum triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL. The analysis compared RA and non-RA groups and found RA associated with stronger presence of multiple comorbidities, including depression, obesity, and HTG, and showed higher CRP levels in RA. RA prevalence increased progressively across CRP categories (low to high). Pairwise comparisons suggested different patterns of coexistence across CRP levels, and RA prevalence differed depending on the combination of depression, obesity, and HTG and the CRP level. The study reports that depression’s association with RA was strongly increased in the presence of obesity or HTG, with the strongest effect at medium CRP levels (1–3 mg/L). Limitations noted include the cross-sectional design (association, not causality), self-reported RA diagnosis, and CRP’s limited ability to probe specific inflammatory pathways.

The passage discusses that players’ age is not a deciding factor in today’s game, which emphasizes being knowledgeable, making the right on-ice decisions, getting into scoring positions, and sacrificing for the team. It notes a past belief that a team with Brett Hull could not win a playoff series, which later proved wrong with a cup win. The speaker says the team looks beyond goals and that winning is the focus in a one-game-to-win-four scenario. It also mentions injuries described as soreness, but states the speaker could still play. Finally, the passage explains the speaker’s uncertainty about re-signing with Dallas, a delayed decision, and a money/budget issue leading to a move to Detroit, which the speaker describes as a fortunate outcome.

The passage describes a player dealing with a leg injury after being hurt by a teammate’s fall, deciding to see how it feels by tomorrow morning and tonight and possibly play the following night. The player mentions feeling better after treatment and notes others are tired and resting. He discusses watching the game from the dressing room, feelings about discipline and momentum changes in the series, and the need to play their best and stay disciplined against Tampa Bay, which is described as strong. He also says the team should control energy, avoid getting too excited, and focus on the next game, including the idea that winning key moments like the first draw matters. He adds that Stanley Cup Finals are exciting and mentions Calgary’s event atmosphere, while also noting he spends most time at home due to having a newborn.

A survey by online investors True Potential found the average person’s debt increased by £560 in the first quarter of 2017. Single parents with young children took on £930 more debt, and lone parents with grown-up children added £940, about £10 per day on average. Experts suggested tuition fees for university-aged children may explain the highest figures. The report said debts were not driven by extravagance, with about 15% taking on more debt to “get by” (rising to 20% for single parents). It also cited reasons including changing career, taking a new job, and funding parental leave. Couples with no dependents took on below-average debt of £350. The average debt overall was £1,797, with North East households owing the most (£2,664) and East of England the least (£411). True Potential’s David Harrison called for greater financial education due to rising individual debts and a growing share of people needing debt to get by.

The passage describes ontology alignment (OA) as identifying correspondences between semantically equivalent entities across different ontologies and notes that modern OA methods often use embedding-based machine learning, including large language model approaches. It argues that knowledge graph embeddings (KGEs)—which represent entities and relations as continuous low-dimensional vectors—are underexplored for OA, though they can simplify large graphs, enable machine learning, support semantic similarity for search and recommendation, and reveal patterns. The authors propose formulating OA as a link prediction task over merged ontologies using a “triple factory,” then training and evaluating a collection of KGE models tailored for alignment. They integrate this approach into OntoAligner, a modular Python library, and outline an OntoAligner framework with three components: a parser, an encoder, and an aligner. The parser extracts RDF-style metadata and class-membership information; the encoder unifies extracted triples; and the aligner trains KGE models (via PyKEEN) with negative sampling, then computes cosine similarity between learned embeddings, ranks candidate alignments, and applies one-to-one and confidence-threshold postprocessing. The passage also surveys related KGE-based OA work and lists 17 KGE models supported in OntoAligner, including ConvE, TransE/TransD/TransH/TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, HolE, RotatE, SimplE, and others, selected to cover diverse modeling approaches.

The passage describes a historical positivist bias in Information Systems (IS) research and a more recent shift in conceptualising IS success from technical factors to human factors. It quotes Ray Paul (2007) defining an IS as what emerges from users’ usage and adaptation of IT and formal and informal processes. The paper argues that IS research has moved from technologically determinist approaches toward focusing on human and social aspects, with mixed methods increasingly used. It focuses on two developments: complexity science as a theoretical basis for studying mixed methods and human usage, and the User Experience (UX) approach increasingly replacing usability practice by emphasising subjective human concerns such as look, feel, satisfaction, motivation, and expectations. It links complexity concepts—including far-from-equilibrium conditions, irreversibility, self-organisation, and emergent order—to IS and UX, and proposes further research building on debates from Special Issues and critiques about how complexity is handled in IS research. The paper concludes by aiming to present a more complex, durational understanding of IS and stresses that IS continually adapts, so flexibility should be built into future designs.

The passage describes the DAWN-PLASMA randomized, open-label phase 2 trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It outlines ethical oversight, informed consent requirements, study objectives and endpoints (including the primary endpoint of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15), participant inclusion/exclusion criteria, study conduct and monitoring, randomization and blinding procedures, dosing and timing of plasma administration, and data analysis sets (Full Analysis Set and Per Protocol Set). It reports that patients were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma (n=326) or control (n=163), with 83.7% alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 in the plasma group versus 84.1% in control (odds ratio 0.99, p=0.976).

The passage describes a “match-up zone” defense that combines person-to-person and zone principles using a set of defensive rules. It states that offensive alignments never split defenders, overloads are easier to defend, and opponents may become confused, with success dependent on smart, knowledgeable players and communication. It also explains how to dictate offensive alignments by showing different zone looks before switching to match-up rules, and provides basic match-up assignments for defenders (X1 through X5), with variations for 2-3, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, and 1-4 offensive alignments. Further sections give procedures for defending cutters and post-related actions (including switching or interchanging roles), and include matchup guidance for 1-2-2 and 2-3 offensive alignments, plus 1-4 offense and defenses around the high post. The passage concludes by noting trapping can be applied when the ball enters trap zones, and lists example trap/press types (quarter court, half court press, full court shadow presses).

The passage discusses market and economic updates, including confirmation of a slowing economy based on July job data and revisions, alongside strong earnings results for 17 large-cap companies and improved S&P 500 earnings and sales growth. It notes seasonal volatility expectations for August–October and technical factors near resistance levels. It also references AI-related stock-picking claims from Investing.com’s ProPicks and includes headlines about Netflix shares, a continuing US government shutdown, and S&P 500 closing above 6,700. Risk disclosures and information about data accuracy and permissions are also included.

DomeShelter Australia offers the Container Mounted DomeShelter™ (CMDS), a robust, weather-resistant shelter system designed for various industries and applications. Its steel frame fits onto existing container shelters by welding, bolting, or Twistlock, and its design is intended to make shipping and logistics easier. The CMDS is engineered to withstand Australian Wind Regions Class A to D and can be used to relocate operations during harsh weather. The passage states that it protects oil and gas goods from heat and moisture with rain and UV protection, supports agriculture by providing light and heat resistance for livestock, and can be used for events and tourism as a temporary or long-term venue solution with a cool, translucent space for natural light. DomeShelter Australia is described as a family-owned business providing industrial shade and shelter solutions worldwide.

The passage explains patterns for distributed systems and focuses on single-node container patterns (such as sidecar, ambassador, and adapter) and then introduces multi-node distributed patterns (microservices and replicated load-balanced services). It describes why grouping containers on one machine can improve reliability, agility, scale, modularity, and separation of concerns. It details the sidecar pattern and provides examples like adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx sidecar proxy and synchronizing configuration via a configuration manager sidecar sharing a filesystem with the application. It then presents the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between an application container and other services, including examples like routing requests to sharded backends and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern is introduced as a way to normalize interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks by using an adapter container to convert heterogeneous outputs into consistent formats, with examples using Prometheus exporters, fluentd, and richer health-check adapters for databases. Finally, the passage contrasts microservices with monoliths, outlines replicated stateless services with readiness probes, and discusses sharded services and sharded caching, including routing via sharding functions (e.g., hash modulo) and the use of consistent hashing when changing the number of shards.

The passage describes a disclosure for systems and methods that provide user interfaces to let users confirm whether to review or take actions associated with untrusted emails, such as untrusted domains or URLs. It explains that, unlike anti-ransomware technologies that act without user decision-making, the system pauses user actions and prompts for confirmation or reversion, supporting real-time training. It also describes allowing administrators to dynamically customize notification content and structure for different user groups via a server-managed set of settings, which are distributed to client devices and validated using client and server settings hashes. The passage further outlines components such as a driver to monitor process creation, injector and monitor libraries to detect user requests to access untrusted domains (including browser navigation), a core for communication, and a user console that resolves URLs, queries the server for trust status, displays prompts based on settings, records user decisions, and resumes or aborts actions accordingly. It includes additional discussion of browser-based implementations, including injected code and browser extensions with supporting intermediary application logic, and describes server-side handling of URL trust responses and updated notification settings.

The passage describes a fluid (water) flow measuring and control device for plumbing, installed at a single location, that includes a main flow channel and a parallel bypass channel with a flowmeter to estimate overall flow. A valve (e.g., a solenoid valve) can stop main flow, with pressure sensors upstream and downstream of the valve, and a transceiver that sends flow data to a computer. The computer analyzes flow data to detect abnormal usage, compare flow patterns to pre-recorded appliance fluid-usage signatures, identify which appliance was used, and instruct the valve to close; it can also send notifications to a remote server for a user mobile device. The flowmeter uses a wheel with rotating blades monitored by movement sensors to determine rotation direction and assess net flow, including backflow. The device and methods are presented as enabling shut-off for leak detection, abnormal use detection, and pattern recognition for per-appliance consumption without pairing a separate device to each appliance. A leak-detection approach is described using temporary valve closure and pressure comparison, including distinguishing leak rates from baseline leakage and notifying users.

The passage argues that elementary and middle schools that perform well in reading also tend to perform well in math, and vice versa. It cites district data showing many “positive outliers” producing outstanding results across subjects and grade levels, and only a small number of districts that were exceptional in one subject but underperformed in the other (most were strong in math but weak in reading). It also reports that in Mississippi, reading and math scores across schools were strongly correlated, and that schools’ reading and math student growth rates were similarly related. The passage notes that while high proficiency and growth can be intertwined by measurement methods and student socioeconomic factors, overall it finds few schools that are extremely strong in one subject but weak in the other.

Crystal morphology strongly affects the sensitivity and performance of energetic-material crystals, with smooth, near-spherical PETN and RDX showing lower shock sensitivity and needle-like crystals showing higher sensitivity. Morphology also influences performance because bulk packing density depends on particle morphology, affecting detonation velocities and pressures; predicting and controlling crystal shapes is therefore important for safety and performance. Crystal morphology is often predicted using the Wulff construction with models such as BFDH, SE, and AE, but these models deviate from experimental morphologies, fail to capture true growth kinetics, and do not account for edge and corner effects. Zepeda-Ruiz et al. used a Monte Carlo simulation of PETN facet evolution that matched experiment, but their method does not capture true growth kinetics. This work introduces a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation technique implemented in the open-source Python package cgkmc, using only intermolecular interaction parameters, and applies it to PETN growth with results in excellent agreement with AE model predictions and experimental observations.

Soccer teams are advised to have a ready, practiced plan for corner kick defense whenever a corner is conceded. All players should understand and immediately implement the plan, with the goalkeeper remaining in charge and defenders clearing a path or following the plan based on whether the goalkeeper calls for the ball. Key defensive behaviors include getting to defensive positions quickly, being first to the ball, winning clearances, and transitioning into attack for fast breaks or quick counters. The passage emphasizes proper defensive techniques, offside-position movement, and clearances upfield, and notes that zone defense is often easiest to introduce to youth, followed by man-to-man marking and then mixed strategies. It describes basic zone setup and drills, man-to-man setup and drills, and a mixed/combo approach where some players stay in zones while others mark man-to-man, aiming to reduce goals conceded. It also recommends scouting opponents’ corner kick plays, modifying the plan game-to-game, and continuing practice until responses become intuitive.

The passage describes the “Mid Screen” offense, stating it is used by every NBA and WNBA team because it takes away helpside support and, when executed, the on-ball screen offers quick options. It can also be used late as the shot or game clock winds down. The basic action involves a point guard driving off a high post screen set by a high post player, with options to drive for a basket, pull up if the defense goes below the screen, make return or kick-out passes, or execute other reads and counters based on defensive actions (e.g., fights over, sags off, steps out, goes under, switches, traps/doubles). The offense can flow into ball reversal and various continuity or passing games. Variations include Post Pop, Horns (double mid screens), 1-4 Low, Post Isolation, Two Game, and Screen and Pop. The passage emphasizes that success depends on coordinated execution, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and preparation, and it outlines teaching/implementation steps and game strategy considerations, including scouting opponents and being prepared to defend against mid screens.

The passage explains NVIDIA’s combined L1 data cache and shared memory architecture introduced in Volta V100, which improves performance, simplifies programming, and reduces tuning. It combines cache and shared memory into a single memory block for best overall performance, with total capacity of 192 KB/SM in A100 versus 128 KB/SM in V100. It states that integrating L1 within the shared memory block provides low latency and high bandwidth, serving as a conduit for streaming data and providing low-latency, high-bandwidth access to frequently reused data, with A100’s larger subsystem boosting performance for applications using L1 when accessing device memory.

The passage describes a player’s performance in a game against the Dallas Stars, including scoring chances from a two-on-one and power-play involvement. It emphasizes the importance of not extending the series, learning from prior teams’ situations, and advancing to the next game on Thursday. The player also discusses personal adjustment and increasing comfort against Dallas as the series progresses, the Stars’ speed and cycling, and the focus required when close to the end of the playoffs. Other points include maintaining discipline on line changes, communication among players, and praise for an opponent’s performance and conditioning leading into and during the playoffs.

The passage explains that fully self-driving cars are still far off, with current self-driving tech spreading gradually using a Society of Automotive Engineers roadmap of five levels. Levels 1 and 2 are already available in production cars, but both require full driver attention. Level 3 is expected by BMW for its iNext electric car in 2021, allowing drivers to let go of the steering wheel in certain situations, though they must be ready to take over within seconds. Many firms may skip Level 3 for Level 4, which gives the driver more time to retake control and allows the vehicle to safely stop if the driver does not. BMW expects regulations and infrastructure for Level 4 to be ready by the middle of the next decade, though some Level 4 cars already exist, including Waymo’s limited-route vehicles planned for a commercial taxi service in Phoenix with an onboard engineer. Level 5 would require no driver, and BMW expects it to arrive by the end of the next decade.

The passage describes a design example for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN power semiconductor devices, including how to select components for the TPS7H5001-SP and the converter power stage. It specifies a 500 kHz switching frequency and gives selected values for programming resistors, dead time (about 25 ns), leading edge blank time (about 50 ns, with RLEB set to 49.9 kΩ), soft-start capacitor (33 nF, giving about 7.5 ms), and transformer parameters (turns ratio 2.5, using 40 μH primary inductance in the final design). It also outlines voltage rating choices for primary and synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, use of an RCD clamp approach, output inductor selection (0.47 μH with 40% ripple current target), and output capacitance selection (1.3 mF minimum from calculations, with about 2.3 mF used for radiation SET mitigation). Additional sections cover an optional secondary output filter, current sensing and overcurrent limiting with RCS set to 7.5 Ω, hiccup capacitor selection (minimum recommended 3.3 nF), frequency compensation components (Type 2A; RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, CHF 47 pF), and slope compensation resistor (102 kΩ). It concludes with application curves, power supply recommendations (controller input range 4 V to 14 V and bypassing guidance), and layout guidelines emphasizing noise reduction and component placement, followed by references to evaluation modules and radiation/SEE reports.

The passage describes systems and methods for cost-effective, accurate long-term detection of abnormal cardiac activity (such as atrial fibrillation) using deep learning with cardiac and motion data. It explains receiving time periods of cardiac data and motion data, splitting them into windows, computing signal quality indices for each window, extracting cardiovascular features using the cardiac and motion data, quality indices, and optionally subject contextual information (e.g., medical history and demographics). The method applies a tensor transform to generate tensors for each window, then uses a trained deep learning architecture (including a convolutional neural network, bidirectional recurrent neural network, and attention network) to classify windows and/or periods into classes such as abnormal or normal cardiac activity (and potentially noise). The attention network assigns scores/weights to windows to identify where abnormal activity occurs. The disclosure also outlines example sensor configurations (e.g., ECG/PPG and accelerometer), report generation from classifications, and a computing system architecture for implementing the methods.

JPMorgan Chase is moving toward becoming a fully AI-connected megabank by deploying AI across its global operations to cut costs, streamline workflows, and enhance client services. The bank has rolled out its proprietary generative AI platform to all 200,000 employees and is investing about $18 billion this year in technology, including AI, machine learning, and cloud infrastructure. Its AI use includes automating customer support, payments, and account management in retail banking; generating research insights in wealth and asset management; and supporting credit assessments, onboarding, fraud detection, and risk management on the institutional side, with reported productivity gains from more than 175 use cases. The bank faces challenges around compliance, transparency, reliability, legacy system integration, and adoption costs, and it says performance under market stress and tighter regulation will be the main test.

The passage says iPhones’ battery life is often frustrating and that iOS 11 drains batteries more than iOS 10. Researchers from Wandera analyzed 50,000 moderately to heavily used iPhones and iPads and reported that a 100% battery lasted 240 minutes on iOS 10 but only 96 minutes on the latest system. Wandera said some users switched back to iOS 10.3.3 but advised against it, adding that newer software offers better protection from hackers and that older iPhone models may experience worse battery drain. Apple released updates since iOS 11’s release; iOS 11.0.1 reportedly reduced battery drain to 159 minutes, while iOS 11.0.2 had not been tested yet. The passage also suggests battery-saving steps such as limiting background app refresh, restricting background location access, and using low power mode.

The passage introduces cardiovascular disease (CVD) as a leading cause of death in women, noting increased CVD mortality among young women, and describes hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) as risk factors for both short- and long-term CVD outcomes. It states that postpartum diagnosis and management of HDP-related hypertension could improve future pregnancy outcomes and reduce long-term CVD morbidity and mortality, though guidelines for postpartum care are described as relatively recent and somewhat inconsistent. It also highlights limited U.S. data on incident hypertension after HDP, especially studies that control for other heart disease risk factors and examine the first year postpartum.

The study is described as a planned secondary analysis of a retrospective cohort from two academic health systems using routinely collected electronic health data. Women aged 13–54 with an HDP diagnosis and a documented blood pressure (BP) measurement at 15–90 days postpartum (2004–2016 identifying data; analysis included 2014–2017 deliveries) were included, with exclusions including pre-existing hypertension and missing or improbable pregnancy data. The primary outcome was time to incident hypertension diagnosis after the 15–90 day BP check, with Cox proportional hazards models estimating hazard ratios for incident hypertension based on systolic and diastolic BP at the comprehensive postpartum visit, alongside other covariates. Multiple imputation was used for missing covariate data.

Results reported that among 2,514 included participants, 13% (315) were diagnosed with incident hypertension after the 15–90 day BP measurement. Only 32% had BP readings in the “normal” range, while most fell into categories corresponding to elevated or Stage 1/2 hypertension. Hazard ratios indicated higher hazard with elevated systolic BP (140 vs 120 mmHg), older maternal age, and more severe HDP (severe preeclampsia/eclampsia vs gestational hypertension), while longer time to the postpartum BP check was associated with lower hazard. Cumulative incidence within 12 months was modeled, with lower risk for an “optimal” BP category (110/65 mmHg) and higher risk for a “Stage 2” category (140/90 mmHg).

On Oct. 29, 2001, Enron’s share price hovered near multi-year lows after Moody’s cut its senior unsecured debt rating to Baa2, two notches above “junk,” and warned it could downgrade further, affecting Enron’s access to funding and trading conditions. The company also said it was in talks with banks to expand or secure additional credit lines (reported at $1 billion to $2 billion) to ease financial concerns and restore investor confidence. Bloomberg and Reuters reports said Enron faced skeptical lenders likely to demand harsher terms and collateral, as it sought cash for daily commodity settlements and after drawing on credit lines to repay commercial paper. Additional reporting described U.S. corporate credit quality being likely to worsen, with Moody’s putting many companies’ ratings on review for downgrade. European energy firms were also reported to reduce or restrict trading with Enron due to credit worries.

Multiple specification issues and resolutions are described. AuxOutputFull’s bit in KEL can be incorrectly cleared on reads from Port 60h, potentially causing incorrect USB PS/2 emulation if read-order is wrong; use interrupts to manage USB keyboard/mouse. tACK does not affect UDMA timing because IDE_DACK setup is fixed at two 66 MHz clocks (30 ns), so no resolution is required. ATAC can hang if PRD start addresses/sizes are only WORD aligned; use DWORD alignment. LPC transactions may abort if SYNC patterns are missing after turn-around; use a PLD workaround. NEGACK in the SMB controller may clear unexpectedly after access to a non-existing device; write twice to SMB_STS when clearing. The retry counter may include other PCI-bus retries; retry behavior can be disabled by setting the Retry Transaction Limit to 0. After suspend, atomic writes to GPIO High Bank feature registers can clear non-selected bits; perform Read-Modify-Write after suspend. SMBus data hold time is mentioned as too short for CS5535 per the SMB v2.0 requirement. LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to be set after abnormal standby; no resolution. Sleep_X is not deasserted when delay exceeds PM_SED delay due to premature counter reset; set delay counters to values less than PM_SED delay.

A world record attempt in Hintonburg featured the elementary school game tunnel ball at Connaught Public School. The school aimed to set the record for most students playing at one time, after researching possible events, and had over 250 students play while a previous record of 120 was set in Australia. Students organized into lines played for about half an hour, followed by applause; the school believes it broke the record, pending verification by Guinness. The event also raised $10,000 for the school yard renewal project, which will support a new kindergarten playground, basketball court, and other yard improvements.

The passage says Seattle’s housing market is one of the hottest in the U.S., with some people worrying it may be another housing bubble like the Great Recession. A ValueInsured online survey found 71% of Washington homeowners were worried, but the survey included only 1,079 people nationwide. It also cites an NWMLS report showing King County median prices rose 18.6% year over year to $658,000 from July 2016 to July 2017, while the number of homes for sale fell and pending/closed sales rose. An executive from Windermere Real Estate said there is no sign of artificially inflated prices, pointing to high credit scores, higher down payments, and high homeowner equity. Experts interviewed over the last two years generally agreed the market is rising but not in a way likely to reverse like 2008; however, NWMLS director George Moorhead said some market correction is likely, with prices and inventory leveling out.

The passage describes billionaire and executive views that challenge the idea of work-life balance, with some leaders saying nonstop work is important for success. Jeff Bezos argues “harmony” rather than balance, and says home happiness improves work and vice versa. Reid Hoffman links seeking balance to not being committed to winning. Andrew Feldman says greatness is not achievable in a 40-hour workweek and requires “every waking minute.” Lucy Guo reports working long hours and adds that she still makes time for friends and family, while saying those who need work-life balance may be in the wrong job.
