Eric Yuan says he has given up hobbies, saying “work is life, life is work,” while putting family first when there is conflict. The passage also mentions China’s “996” culture and Jack Ma’s view that being able to work 996 is a “huge blessing.”

American consumers’ confidence rose in April, with the Conference Board’s confidence index increasing to 128.7 from 127.0 in March. The index measures consumers’ views of current conditions and their outlook for the next six months. The Conference Board said the strength suggests the economy will keep expanding at a solid pace, citing improved ratings of business and labor market conditions. Analysts attributed higher confidence to a strong labor market with unemployment at a 17-year low, earlier impact of $1.5 trillion tax cuts approved in December, less stock market volatility, and reduced worries about a trade war. Some analysts cautioned that confidence may overstate future consumer spending because real income growth has been sluggish even after the tax cuts.

NEC Corp announced it will establish the “NEC Satellite Operation Center,” scheduled to be fully operational in April. The center will begin operations for the ASNARO-2 high-precision compact radar satellite, launched in January, using NEC’s GroundNEXTAR ground operations system and a high-security data center. It can operate multiple satellites simultaneously, with future expansion planned. GroundNEXTAR includes functions for satellite operation visualization (including 3D animation) and image distribution. NEC plans to bring ASNARO-2 images to market in collaboration with Japan EO-Satellite Service Ltd starting in September, and said it will contribute to solving social challenges through space projects including satellite operation and data utilization.

The passage describes frequency compensation options for the TPS7H500x-SP controllers, which use a transconductance error amplifier (OTA). It explains the difference between Type 2A and Type 2B compensation, including an optional additional capacitor CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation, and notes that the compensation components connect between the COMP pin and AVSS. It then outlines a procedure to select compensation components based on desired converter crossover frequency, error amplifier transconductance, power stage transconductance, and other capacitor and resistor placements, with adjustments depending on converter topology. Additional sections cover thermal shutdown behavior, device functional modes (fixed frequency, peak current mode control), and an application example for a synchronous push-pull GaN converter including component choices and calculated values (such as transformer turns ratio, FET ratings, clamp, output inductance/capacitance, and compensation components). The passage also provides power supply recommendations and detailed layout guidelines to improve reliability and reduce noise coupling.

Software must ensure the halt-on command is last in the ring buffer queue for precise halting; for precise error halting, only one command should be queued at a time due to multiple execution units. Software can clear interrupt status bits by writing PM_RBCtl[CLEAR_INTS]=1, which is accepted only when the ring buffer has no more entries to process or when PM_Status[PAUSED] is true, and interrupt generation resumes when processing resumes (PM_RBTail may be incremented while paused).

For SPA encoding with SMEE/SME-MK, encryption information is encoded into SPAs passed to page migration firmware. When SMEE is enabled, software may set the C-bit to 1 to indicate encrypted memory; firmware selects the encryption key id if encryption is selected. SPAs must be well-formed and in appropriate ranges, and reserved/out fields should be set to zero. The passage also describes TMPM/PAGE_MOVE command behavior for SNP and non-SNP systems, including moving page contents, handling encryption, DMA limitations, CPU access prevention, page state requirements, and firmware validation and migration steps (with status reporting via ring buffer/migration lists and various error codes). It further notes that PM_GET_CAPABILITIES queries firmware capabilities/versions and that errors are reported via command status and ring buffer PM_STATUS; hardware or timeout issues may be reported via MCA, and software may need to log MCA and take actions such as saving state, terminating VMs, or stopping further commands.

McEachern Indians are visiting the Harrison Hoyas in a top Georgia high school football game that began at 8 p.m. EST in Kennesaw. Both teams are 5-0 coming off a bye week, and McEachern is third-week atop The Sporting News’ “The NEXT 25” bubble rankings. The game is presented as McEachern’s best chance to make a case for The Sporting News High School Football Top 25, while Harrison is trying to make a statement with a win that would raise its profile.

Astronomers discovered the most distant and powerful “odd radio circle” (ORC) known so far: RAD J131346.9+500320, nearly 10 billion years old and at redshift ~0.94. The double, intersecting ring structure was identified using citizen science via RAD@home and the LOFAR radio telescope. The finding challenges theories that ORCs are caused by black hole mergers, with researchers instead suggesting galactic superwinds may be responsible. The study also reports two other unusual radio-ring galaxies found in galaxy clusters, and proposes that interactions of relativistic magnetized plasma jets with surrounding hot thermal plasma may shape these structures.

Peter Marks, the former top vaccine regulator at the FDA, has joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases. He confirmed the new role to STAT and said his first day was Monday. The move drew criticism over a “revolving door” between the FDA and industry.

The Louisiana state brought an action against the Banking Department of the Citizens’ Bank of Louisiana seeking a license tax for the privilege of carrying on a banking business. The Citizens’ Bank president, who was served with a copy of the petition and citation, excepted, asserting he had no authority to represent the banking department claimed by the state and that no such corporation existed. The court addressed whether the defendant had been properly cited, finding that corporations must have express authority to be sued and that the suit should have been brought against the Citizens’ Bank of Louisiana itself rather than the “Cash or Banking Department.” The court concluded the president sued was not the president of the banking department entity alleged, and therefore limited its decision to the lack of proper citation. The district court’s judgment for the defendant was reversed and the state’s suit dismissed. Monroe, J., dissented.

The passage is a collection of news and email references dated February 22–25, 2002, focused largely on Enron. It notes that Enron’s pipelines and power plants are expected to provide steady income during bankruptcy, including plans to sell certain assets and reliance on retention bonuses for employees. It also reports that the U.S. FERC said it had contact 25 times with Enron officials between August 2000 and June 2001, and that Pat Wood denied undue influence over FERC decisions. Other items mention creditors’ prospects for Enron Japan, government-backed loans to Enron-related power projects, and separate business and policy news including BG Group’s India investments and an upcoming Senate energy legislation debate.

The passage describes the importance of budget pacing in online digital advertising with real-time auctions and proposes a more principled pacing controller. It explains that pacing systems set a desired spending plan, monitor actual spend, and correct deviations to minimize the gap between desired and actual spending velocity, but that controller design is challenging due to auction dynamics, stochastic traffic, noisy signals, and changing market conditions. The authors present three contributions: implementing a bucketized hysteresis controller (BHC) and comparing it to a legacy variable-step system, providing an analytical framework for parameter selection, and validating the approach through real-world auction experiments showing improvements. The system setup uses conversion probability and bid scaling with a pacing parameter λ (discount pacing), where λ is periodically updated to meet a target spend rate. The baseline controller uses variable step size multiplicative updates to λ, while the BHC uses quantized, multi-step nonlinear control based on discretizing normalized rate error into bands and updating λ using the gain associated with the active error band.

The passage explains how to change the mouse pointer’s size and color in Windows 10 via Settings > Ease of Access > Mouse, where pointer size can be set to small, medium, or large, and color can be set to white, black, or inverted. It also notes that changing the pointer shape can be done through the Control Panel Mouse applet on the Pointers tab. The passage then provides a Safari iOS tip for closing all open tabs: press and hold the Tabs link at the bottom right to get options to create a new tab, close a specified number of tabs, or cancel (and similarly press and hold the Done link if already tapped). It adds that quitting and restarting Safari won’t close tabs because Safari remembers the previously open set.

NASA’s Dawn mission has released two close-up photos of Ceres showing “dramatic new views” of Occator Crater, a 50-mile (80-kilometer) impact site with shiny salt deposits. The images are the closest-ever taken of Ceres’ bright surface features, called faculae, including Vinalia Faculae (east of Occator Crater) and Cerealia Facula at the crater’s center. Discovered in 2015, the faculae are described as the largest carbonate deposits ever found outside Earth, and it remains unclear whether they came from shallow mineral-laden water or deeper brines rising through fractures. Dawn’s second extended mission aims to provide data to address this and to study Ceres’ composition using gravity measurements and instruments including a gamma ray and neutron detector and a mapping spectrometer. The second photo, taken June 22 after Dawn descended to about 21 miles (34 kilometers), also shows a mound on the western side of Cerealia Facula. Dawn began a new Ceres orbit in early June, bringing it within 22 miles (35 kilometers), and the mission is expected to end after providing further data, with the spacecraft remaining in its last-known orbit to avoid contaminating Ceres.

The passage says Casey Mittelstadt’s college season is over and questions have arisen about his availability for Rochester (including the playoffs). It notes he could play for the Amerks via an AHL contract or an amateur tryout contract, which would let him join the rest of the regular season and playoffs. It also states his leverage could lead him to seek an NHL entry-level deal, but that depends on whether he wants to leave school. It adds that if the Sabres sign him to an NHL entry-level contract beginning this season, he could not be sent to Rochester. Buffalo’s ideal option is described as an amateur tryout contract for this season and an entry-level deal beginning in 2018-19, which would provide minor-league games. The passage concludes that his future is important to Sabres fans because his remaining NCAA eligibility would be forfeited with a contract.

The passage is an ISDA press report dated May 16, 2001, summarizing multiple news items about derivatives. It covers proposed IRS hedging regulations and witnesses urging IRS to adopt a broader risk management standard; BIS data showing slowed OTC derivatives growth in the second half of 2000; a report on the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York achieving FAS 133 compliance using Principia Partners’ system; commentary that single-stock futures may face drawbacks due to higher regulatory costs and restrictions; CME and CBOE forming a joint venture to introduce single-stock futures traded electronically; FASB’s FAS 133 options accounting changes and an implementation guideline meant to avoid amending the standard; debate about the Basel “w charge” for credit derivatives; UK legislation proposed to allow building societies to use credit derivatives for risk management; a reported default swap “collapse” creating arbitrage opportunities; Lightrade expanding pooling points to shorten bandwidth delivery times; and ISDA finalizing a credit derivatives restructuring supplement limiting deliverable securities maturities under restructuring events.

Canadian Pacific Railway says it is speeding up delivery of imported goods from Vancouver to the U.S. industrial heartland, reducing transit times to Detroit by up to 48 hours versus Canadian National Railway. CP Rail attributes the faster service to changes in Vancouver and North Dakota and describes a “seamless” intermodal operation through Chicago running seven days a week. It says shorter transit times lower costs by enabling shippers to reuse containers more quickly, and Hapag-Lloyd agrees that faster times and smoother border and Chicago movement improve access to U.S. markets. Canadian National has previously claimed that avoiding congestion in Chicago improves its speed, and CP’s CEO says the faster service could pressure CN competitively.

Euro zone stocks rose on the first trading day of 2017, reaching their highest levels in over a year after data showed euro zone factory activity rose at the fastest pace in over five years. The Euro STOXX 50 climbed 0.5% to its highest since December 2015, with the factory PMI at 54.9, while the euro fell 0.3% to below US$1.05. Trading was thin because several major markets were closed for New Year holidays, and analysts expected potential volatility. European stock gains also lowered yields on lower-rated euro zone government bonds. A gun attack in Istanbul that killed 39 people was described as having little market impact, while the Turkish lira slipped after the attack. Other data included slower growth in China’s manufacturing sector and a large annual loss for the yuan in 2016, and bitcoin rose above US$1,000.

The passage describes how to defend against the “Horns” offense, which uses high post screening similar to the “MidScreen” offense. It notes that if defenses are unprepared for mid screens, the offense can get easy layups or wide open shots, and that most teams avoid switching because the dribbler can flare to the wing and the screener can post up against a smaller defender. It outlines defensive fundamentals and several schematic responses: a show-and-recover sequence after the screen (including show to the sideline, recovery, and final matchup), and “All Out SOS” disruption that aims to start action before the first screen option by trapping the point guard. It provides phases for trapping, passing out of the trap with rotations based on the near player concept, and final alignment after the ball is passed, including what defenders do depending on whether the ballhandler drives or passes to the post.

Roger Poole, chairman of Petworth and Bognor Angling Club, says the new coarse-fishing season on Britain’s rivers has begun and that approaches used in March may not work in June, so anglers should reassess baits, tactics, and swims by watching and observing. He notes the legal close season allows fish to spawn, after which anglers should use varied baits to match different fish, with natural foods like bugs, worms, flies, and grubs available near the river. He highlights the club’s efforts to attract youngsters and mentions National Fishing Month (July 27 to September 2), involving over 250 events and supported by the Environment Agency, with free fishing licences for children under 16. He also provides early-season fishing ideas, saying tench are active in early mornings in ponds, while rivers currently see more chub, plus dace, roach, perch, bream, and possibly barbel using tactics such as light float trotting, maggots, and feeder/ledger setups. He ends by encouraging experimentation and good luck.

The passage describes Nashville police and other agencies explaining how Travis Reinking, suspected of a Waffle House mass shooting, was arrested without police firing or killing him. It says Reinking allegedly murdered four people with an assault rifle, and that James Shaw Jr., a Black man, tackled Reinking and wrestled the weapon from him; Reinking then evaded capture for more than 24 hours. A press conference is cited where Lt. Carlos Lara says a citizen spotted Reinking at a construction site near a wooded area and detectives tracked him through the woods until an officer encountered and ordered him to get on the ground. After Reinking complied, officers handcuffed him, searched his backpack, and found a semi-automatic handgun and ammunition. The passage contrasts this restraint with police killings of unarmed Black men and mentions an incident the same day in which white officers allegedly violently arrested an unarmed Black woman at a Waffle House in Saraland, Alabama.

The Office of Climate Change (OCC) opened a three-day Greenhouse Gas Inventory workshop at Herdmanston Lodge, Queenstown, to prepare Guyana for its Third National Communication (TNC) to the UNFCCC. The workshop aims to build technical and institutional capacity, integrate climate priorities into national development strategies, and target the TNC’s Greenhouse Gas–Inventory component, with other components planned for later dates. OCC head Janelle Christian said the goal is to develop trained national experts to institutionalize inventory preparation and support future reporting. She added that trained individuals will improve Guyana’s climate-based reporting and help the OCC select technical trainees consistently. National Project Coordinator Marlon Velloza said the workshop and resulting findings will provide information to support Guyana’s “green” agenda and encouraged public education and involvement. Professor Anit Garg and Dr. Indu Murthy conducted sessions via Skype, and at the end of the workshop Garg hoped to test and certify participants. The TNC is due for submission in 2019.

The passage says Napheesa Collier suffered a Grade 2 tear of three ankle ligaments and a muscle in her shin in a collision with Thomas, an injury with a minimum six-week recovery period. It reports that Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve was ejected in Game 3 and suspended for her reaction, and that the Lynx were eliminated by the Mercury in their best-of-five series.

NEC Display Solutions announced that some of its pro-grade 24/7 digital signage displays in the P-series will ship with five-year warranties instead of three. The company says four models will shift from three to five years, based on their robust design and build, and that warranty extensions from other manufacturers typically cost several hundred dollars. The five-year warranty applies to P404, P484, and P554 from the first shipment, and P703 on purchases made on or after August 1, 2017.

The passage discusses the Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator and IBS-based trading strategies. It states that IBS oscillates from zero to one and measures the closing price’s relative position between the day’s low and high, with low values described as bullish for short-term mean reversion and high values as bearish. The article claims IBS worked remarkably well over multi-decade periods on stocks and stock indices, with less success on other asset classes, noting poor performance for commodity-related stocks and for certain country indices dependent on commodity prices. It also reports that IBS strategies were successful on SPY and QQQ using specific trading rules, including metrics such as win rate and drawdown, and that adding certain filters (e.g., VIX or an overbought condition relative to a 200-day moving average) can improve results but may be sensitive to optimization. The passage says IBS performs best when market conditions are volatile and suggests it may perform particularly well in bear markets, and it highlights a weakness: the need to enter at or near the close. It concludes that IBS works best on stocks in specific industries and broad sector-diversified stock indices, and that the strategy likely needs adaptation to local market conditions.

The passage argues that high cholesterol and hyperlipidemia are often treated without addressing underlying causes, leaving patients to take lifelong statins and experience related side effects. It cites CDC.gov to state that high cholesterol is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including coronary heart disease, and says cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in the U.S. The passage contrasts conventional medicine’s focus on preset acute treatments with a proposed approach that targets the underlying causes of high cholesterol. It claims hyperlipidemia reflects a metabolic state involving digestion and may relate to liver, kidney, and spleen functions, with different types requiring different causes and solutions. It promotes a “Functional Food Therapeutic Lifestyle Change Intervention Program,” described as side-effect free and natural, and a book that allegedly presents 14 types of high cholesterol, their 14 underlying causes, and treatment solutions intended to make the condition curable and reduce or eliminate lifelong statin prescriptions.

The passage describes the author moving to Tarrytown in 1950 to watch barges carrying caissons for building the Tappan Zee Bridge, which was intended to last 50 years. The author later rides across the first span of the new Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge and describes its main towers, cable stays, span dimensions, and design features, calling it breathtaking. The author’s interest is increased by a library presentation by Jamey Barbas, Project Director and a structural engineer, who discusses her background and the project’s large outreach program. The passage also outlines educational outreach numbers, the bridge’s length and durability goals, details of its structural design and loads, and construction methods, including heavy-lift equipment, concrete batching in the river, environmental studies, and planning for unexpected factors like weather. It concludes by noting extensive thinking and a large consortium workforce involved in design and construction.

A University of Alabama student, Kelsey Hall, posted on Twitter that she would wear a Christmas tree costume to all her classes for the rest of the semester if she received 1,000 retweets. She quickly received 30,000 retweets, and she has worn the costume as promised, but says the attention has been stressful, including people tagging her and requesting interviews. After this experience, she says she will likely think carefully before posting more social media challenges.

High School Sports Talk Presented by VirginiaPreps.com airs Saturdays from 10 AM EST to noon on ESPN Radio 94.1, hosted by Matthew Hatfield and Coach Ed Young, with guests joining them at the Boo Williams Sportsplex in Hampton for the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League. The fourth session, the final leg before Peach Jam in July, features segments with Chris Duhon and Jalen Lecque, David Teel, Cam Bacote, Bryan Kersey, Ed Miller, and Keyontae Johnson. Full replays and individual segments are available via Dropbox for streaming or download.

Alpha Theory’s Analytics Department analyzes clients’ historical data to identify investor biases, which show up as deviations between actual and optimal position sizes. Examples include failing to cut exposure after large positive price moves, not sizing positions to the probability-weighted return when initiating, using undisciplined approaches with positions lacking explicit price targets, and over-diversifying into many smaller holdings at lower probability-weighted returns. The research cited suggests concentrated portfolios outperform diversified ones by 2.2% on an alpha basis, and that for 2016 returns clients would have done better by 5.1% if sized using the suggested optimal position size.

Showstoppers Theatre will stage “Foiled Again!” directed by Radu Azdril, featuring funny melodramas linked by songs. The production offers speaking roles for many actors and actresses, with vocal instructors helping children with stage presence and choreography. Showstoppers’ summer program provides musical theater opportunities for young actors, with no experience required, and includes costumes, sets, lighting, and sound. The program serves children of Santa Barbara County, with all children age 12 or younger admitted free and general admission tickets $7 at the door. Performances are at La Colina Junior High School (4025 Foothill Road, Santa Barbara) on this Friday at 7 p.m., Saturday at 10:30 a.m., June 28 at 7 p.m., and June 29 at 10:30 a.m.

The lecture discusses experimentation and robust design in engineering systems, emphasizing adaptive experimentation in parameter spaces to improve robustness. The professor contrasts an earlier view favoring simple experiments (as expressed by Sir Edward John Russell) with R.A. Fisher’s approach that used complex factorial designs, showing that factorial planning can substantially reduce the standard deviation of effect estimates (e.g., a factor-of-2 efficiency improvement for a 2^3 full factorial) but becomes impractical as the number of factors grows. This motivates fractional factorial designs, which reduce experiment size by sacrificing information and can confound main effects with interactions.  

The lecture then defines robust parameter design (reducing performance variation by choosing control-factor settings to reduce sensitivity to noise factors) and describes Taguchi’s use of crossed arrays of control and noise factors, along with later concerns about its effectiveness. The core focus shifts to adaptive “one-factor-at-a-time” experimentation (OFAT), where factors are toggled sequentially based on observed improvement; empirical and theoretical work compares adaptive OFAT to fractional factorial designs. The results reported indicate adaptive OFAT can perform comparably or better, particularly when interactions are not very small and experimental error is not extremely low, and can reach much of the benefit of exhaustive search using far fewer runs.  

Further sections outline comparisons in robustness contexts (e.g., sheet metal spinning simulations, paper airplane experiments), the role of informed starting points, and the use of ensembles of multiple OFAT runs. The professor also discusses practical considerations (sequential vs parallel experimentation, measurement delays, time trends, and the trade-off between achieving improvement and learning causal explanations). The lecture concludes with broader conclusions about when adaptive experimentation is beneficial and suggests that engineers may need more widespread capability to apply robustness-focused experimental methods.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q reports results for the quarterly period ended April 26, 2015. For the three months ended April 26, 2015, NVIDIA reported revenue of $1,151 million and net income of $134 million. The condensed consolidated balance sheets show total assets of $7,291 million and total shareholders’ equity of $4,556 million as of April 26, 2015. The cash flow statement reports net cash provided by operating activities of $246 million, net cash used in investing activities of $235 million, and net cash used in financing activities of $44 million. The notes describe accounting policies, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities and fair value measurements, intangible assets, guarantees and product warranty liabilities, long-term debt (1.00% Convertible Senior Notes Due 2018), commitments and contingencies related to legal proceedings, and share repurchase and dividend activity. The filing also includes segment information for the GPU business and Tegra Processor business, and discusses capital return, liquidity, and controls and procedures.

The passage discusses the team’s approach to winning a game and the desire to move the series back to New Jersey. It mentions creating more scoring chances, getting shots and rebounds, and blocking a goalie’s vision. Zach Parise is highlighted for playing well and possibly being overlooked, while the opposing defense is described as strong at controlling gaps, pressuring in the neutral zone, boxing out, and limiting what the goalie sees. The speaker also suggests shaking things up, improving puck movement, challenging the opposing defense more in their zone, and applying more pressure on the goalie. Parise references past examples where similar outcomes happened, emphasizes that the margin for error is slim, and concludes that the team should focus on winning the next game and then see what happens.

The 2-1-2 zone is described as a compact variation of the 2-3 zone that protects the middle and keeps “Bigs” aligned near the basket for strong rebounding. Because its compact design can be vulnerable to good outside shooting, it is mainly used against teams with poor outside shooting or to match up against high post offenses such as a 1-3-1 alignment. The middle defender is responsible for covering the high post when the ball is out front and fronting the low post when the ball is on the wing or in the corner, and the zone can be played with defenders having at least one foot in the paint at all times. The passage also outlines zone shifts based on ball location (middle, left/right wing, and left/right corner) and notes that outside defenders typically move together sideline to sideline, requiring quick players. It further describes roles for guarding low post areas, cutting off passes out of corners, and collapsing defenders toward high/low post actions.

Investing.com summarizes multiple worldwide financial market updates and a market outlook commentary. It notes Tesla beating Q3 delivery estimates with a record 497,099 vehicles, Citi raising Bitcoin and Ethereum price forecasts, chip stocks rising on OpenAI’s Stargate project and AI memory demand expectations, and Bitcoin reaching a 7-week high near $120k. The commentary highlights last week’s earnings and economic/policy events as being muted by controversy, contradiction, or doubt, and says market action shifted toward risk-off late in the week, supported by a “bearish engulfing” technical pattern and deteriorating market internals. It also describes data suggesting weakening demand and labor-market concerns (including weaker-than-expected nonfarm payrolls and downward revisions), mentions the FOMC having two dissenting votes, and discusses expectations for potential September rate cuts. The text further reports on company earnings and upward revisions, provides sector and asset-class market-readings (e.g., value vs. growth and bond/utility strength), and includes promotional and risk-disclosure content.

The passage says Google Wallet is still available for transferring money between friends, and that an update (v20.0.158862257) will include changes to its security model. It notes that fingerprint-based unlocking is expected soon, replacing fingerprint-less access and reducing reliance on PIN entry. It also describes replacing the Wallet “Payments PIN” with a “Google Account PIN,” which many users may already have through other Google services, with Wallet offering to set one up if needed. Finally, it indicates there may be an option to stop requiring a PIN entirely, using fingerprint for security instead. It cautions that the discussed features may not be live for all users and that app teardowns are speculative.

The passage warns that a fake WhatsApp link has been circulating for weeks, claiming PM Narendra Modi wants to give everyone free Rs. 500 recharge. It says the link is likely a phishing technique that could expose users to attacks if they click it or enter personal information like mobile number, operator, and state, and it may redirect users to pages that request sharing the link with 15 friends. The website’s terms state it is not connected to any telecom company, and similar past fake messages about WhatsApp video calling are mentioned. The passage urges users not to click or share such links and not to download related software.

The passage explains options trading in Amazon (AMZN), describing strategies such as buying call/put options, writing covered/naked calls and puts, and spread trading. It outlines key risks, including leverage, options expiring worthless, liquidity risk, and margin calls. It describes how option prices move with the underlying stock price, influenced by delta and volatility, and lists advantages including speculation, hedging, leverage, and risk-limiting via spreads. It also covers requirements to start trading, including having a margin account, sufficient capital for premiums and fees, and understanding risks; eligible order types (market, limit, stop); the role of strike price in payoff; how profits are made; tax implications depending on trade type and holding period; factors affecting fees, margin requirements, and costs; expiration date timing; methods to analyze options (quantified analysis); order execution speed; and considerations when selecting an options trading platform (fees, execution speed, and research tools).

The passage introduces classical Heisenberg models on geometrically constrained lattices where bilinear-biquadratic exchange interactions produce rich phase diagrams with exotic phases. It reviews prior work on isotropic and anisotropic triangular lattices and notes that a full phase diagram is difficult for models with six interaction parameters. The authors instead study a simpler partially anisotropic triangular lattice made of isosceles triangles, considering two bilinear and two biquadratic interaction parameters, reducing the problem to determining ground states for one triangular plaquette. They define a plaquette Hamiltonian in terms of angles between three classical spins and describe constraints on these angles, which map to a tetrahedron. The passage then derives expressions for the plaquette energy, determines conditions for minima at the tetrahedron vertices, edges, faces, and interior points, and presents a table of ground-state configurations and their energies. It concludes with discussion of ground-state phase diagrams for bilinear-biquadratic Heisenberg and XY models and starts further derivation for face solutions.

Bank of New York Mellon Corp reduced its Greenlight Reinsurance (NASDAQ:GLRE) holdings by 8.7% in the second quarter, selling 18,470 shares and ending with 193,448 shares, worth about $4,043,000 and representing approximately 0.52% of the company. The passage also notes changes by other institutional investors, including Vanguard Group, Dimensional Fund Advisors, Morgan Stanley, Clearbridge Investments, and Geode Capital Management. It reports that institutional investors and hedge funds own 45.43% of the stock, summarizes recent analyst rating changes, and provides stock and financial figures, including the company’s recent earnings results for the quarter ending before July 31. The passage further mentions director Leonard R. Goldberg selling shares and states that insiders have sold 6,468 shares worth $147,928 over the last three months.

Frickley Athletic’s squad for the 2017-18 season is being built through multiple new signings announced in the past week. Manager Spencer Fearn has brought in Jason Yates, Josh Nodder, and Danny Patterson to strengthen the midfield, alongside defender Joe Austin and players Tom Dugdale and Danny Swales. Existing players Tyler Williams will stay, and striker Jacob Hazell is returning after a spell at Scarborough. The passage includes background on each player’s previous clubs and performances, along with Fearn’s comments praising their qualities. It also notes that Hazell could form a partnership with already signed Gavin Allott.

The passage explains that the offensive guard position is crucial in NFL offenses, despite receiving less attention than tackle. It describes guards as needing strength and athleticism to block in both the run and pass game, including handling defensive tackles, blitzing linebackers, maintaining positioning to protect the QB, communicating against modern defensive schemes, winning run matchups, pulling for advanced players, and creating running lanes. It lists abbreviations and nicknames for guards, outlines required skills and general body type, and highlights Larry Allen and John Hannah as notable offensive guards. The passage concludes that guards are essential in setting the tone in the interior and enabling scheme execution for offensive coordinators.

KPMG principal aIQ program lead Nick Lichtenberg reports that, in six months, organizations with deployed AI agents rose from 11% to 42% in a survey of 130 U.S. C-suite and business leaders. She said the shift in the third quarter moved from “fear factor” to “cognitive fatigue,” alongside a drop in employee resistance from 47% to 21% and increased acceptance or active embrace by over half the workforce. KPMG says technology departments lead AI agent usage for productivity gains, and emphasizes the need for a “human in the loop.” Shears described AI as still immature and potentially damaging without close supervision, and said traditional metrics like KPIs and ROI may miss AI’s value, with leaders reporting conventional KPIs miss much of AI’s value. KPMG’s tracked signals include productivity, profitability, and quality improvements, and it expects entry-level recruiting to be reshaped, with higher expectations for skepticism and critical thinking, especially for “digital first” entry-level workers.

The passage describes an “early offense” in three phases. Phase 1 (“Early Push”) focuses on quickly moving the ball into the offensive operating area within 2–4 seconds to create out-numbered situations and mismatches before defenders organize, including specific goals for breakaways and 2-on-1, 3-on-1, 3-on-2, and 3-on-3 situations, along with rules such as scoring on breakaways, passing ahead when possible, avoiding charges, and requiring practice of finishing (with a stated consequence for missed layups). Phase 2 (“Early Flow”) explains moving into flexible flow actions or set offenses if the initial transition push does not create an advantage, preventing the defense from setting up; it also notes flow actions can function as half-court offenses without backing the ball out. Phase 3 (“Continuity”) describes flowing into continuity play to prevent defensive organization, emphasizing shot-clock control, offensive balance, and offensive rebounding/second efforts, with examples including “Flex Continuity,” “Passing Game Continuity,” “Mid Screen Continuity,” “Side Screen” options, and “Inside Triangle Game.”

The passage is SanDisk’s End User License Agreement. It states that users must not install or use the provided software until they agree to the terms. SanDisk grants a limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, transferable, royalty-free license to use the software in executable form for personal use on a single computer, with the software usable on only one device at a time. The agreement restricts modifications, derivative works, reverse engineering, and disclosure, and requires any permitted copies to be unmodified and include proprietary notices and the agreement. It disclaims all warranties, limits SanDisk’s and its licensors’ liability for indirect and other damages, and sets total liability to no more than the amount paid for the software. It includes “restricted rights” for government use, allows termination for violations with required deletion or destruction of copies, and disclaims suitability for high-risk activities. The agreement includes governing law and venue in California, export compliance requirements, and states certain sections survive termination. It also provides disposal instructions: do not dispose of the device with unsorted household waste; improper disposal may harm the environment and human health, and users should consult local waste authorities for return and collection systems.

The passage explains how to buy gold and other precious metals from Costco online or in-store. It says members must have a Costco membership to access precious metals, and that options depend on inventory availability. It notes that items are listed on Costco.com and can sell out quickly when priced near the spot price, with delivery from online orders typically estimated at 3–5 days via UPS or FedEx. For in-store purchases, shoppers fill out forms with item SKU and quantity, then bring a pickup slip to the front office for an employee to retrieve the order and assist with payment. The passage also warns that precious metals are excluded from Costco’s return policy and that Costco will not adjust prices after purchase. It further advises against financing gold purchases with interest-bearing payment options and suggests planning for the long term when selling.

The passage reviews literature on STEM education, project-based learning (PBL), design, and architectural education (design studio), then reports an ethnographic study in the first-year Architectural Design courses at BUU Faculty of Architecture. It describes how STEM and PBL emphasize real-life problems and skills such as collaboration and critical thinking, and it outlines architectural design concepts including non-linear, feedback-driven design, studio critique, and the use of technical drawing and graphic communication. The research uses participant observation, unstructured notes across four weeks, and interviews with eight students to analyze how students learn through design problems and teacher critiques. Findings from observations are organized into themes including confronting open-ended problems, thinking outside the box, deepening understanding of the problem, and meeting the culture of criticism, with additional interview results on perceived difficulties and the course’s purpose. The discussion applies analogical inference to connect architectural education elements to STEM education, concluding with six recommendations for STEM across grade levels, such as giving students sustained opportunities to solve open-ended problems independently, ensuring motivation, using authentic real-life problem contexts, enabling firsthand contact with materials/tools even when no concrete product is the goal, adding technical drawing instruction, and adopting a studio-like assessment approach with jury-based evaluation.

The appellant sought a writ of error coram nobis to vacate a 1996 decision affirming a 1994 judgment, arguing ineffective assistance of appellate counsel. The court denied the application, finding the appellant failed to establish he was denied effective assistance of appellate counsel. Bracken, J. P., Sullivan, Altman, and McGinity concur.

The American Red Cross says its blood supply is still recovering from severe winter storms in March, with more snow expected this week. Winter weather forced more than 270 blood drives to cancel, leaving over 9,500 blood and platelet donations uncollected in the first two weeks of March; in Connecticut, 39 drives were canceled, resulting in 1,287 uncollected donations. The Red Cross urges people to donate blood when it’s safe, noting ongoing needs for cancer patients, those having surgeries, trauma patients, and others, and advises making appointments via the Blood Donor App, RedCrossBlood.org, or 800-733-2767.

Acordis Technology & Solutions, the official IT provider for the Miami Heat, will attend and sponsor the annual “Men’s Nite Out” on May 9, 2018 at The Signature Grand in Davie, Florida. The Jewish Federation of Broward County’s event has featured motivational speakers for 13 years, including Drew Brees, Bobby Bowden, Mike Ditka, Dick Vitale, and Mark Spitz, and this year’s speaker is Reggie Jackson (“Mr. October”). Registration begins at 6:00 PM, and dinner and refreshments will be served. The event is for professionals who want to network. Acordis is a Florida-based organization focused on helping companies increase efficiencies and reduce costs through technological solutions, including listed IT services and partnerships with companies such as Cisco, Xerox, VMWare, Microsoft, and others.

The lecturer discusses how applying the Fiat–Shamir transform to a protocol that is only soundness \(1/2\) can become insecure in the random oracle model, describing an attack where a cheating prover repeatedly guesses the oracle’s challenge bit and reuses transcripts. The talk then explains that even making soundness negligible (e.g., by sequential repetition) does not automatically yield soundness in the random oracle model, because the prover can still exploit the oracle by extending successful transcripts after failed attempts. The lecturer presents a theorem: Fiat–Shamir is sound in the random oracle model for public-coin protocols with constant rounds and negligible soundness, and sketches a proof by showing that an adversary against Fiat–Shamir would enable a cheating strategy against the original interactive protocol using oracle-query simulation and guessing. It is also noted that random oracle results are not a guarantee of soundness with real hash functions: there are cases where protocols are sound in the random oracle model but insecure for any explicit hash function. The lecturer concludes with related discussion of parallel zero-knowledge failing for a specific Hamiltonian graph protocol, linking (for that protocol) Fiat–Shamir soundness to the impossibility of parallel zero knowledge, and stating that this was proved via the protocol’s Fiat–Shamir security.

The passage describes how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education by reshaping teaching, research, and administration. It outlines the paper’s goals to address institutions’ responses to AI, AI’s short- and long-term effects, and opportunities to improve learning outcomes, close educational gaps, and prepare students for an AI-driven workforce. The passage reports growing global adoption and research interest, notes that 86% of students use AI tools for academic purposes, and describes applications such as intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics, and adaptive learning technologies. It also highlights challenges including faculty resistance, ethical concerns (data privacy, fairness, algorithmic bias), academic integrity risks, and infrastructure gaps that widen the digital divide. The passage provides examples from regions including China and the United States, and discusses institutional responses such as faculty training, curricular changes, and policy frameworks. It concludes that AI offers major opportunities but requires ethical governance, equitable access, and collaborative efforts among educators, policymakers, and technologists.

The passage discusses a hockey team maintaining its game plan and staying composed after being down one goal. It says the team played well in the first two periods, took chances despite limited offensive success, and continued taking many shots until the puck went through Belfour. It also mentions “Dr. McMullen” selling the team and expresses the players’ view that they are hockey players rather than business people, hoping he will be part of the situation as well.

The State of North Dakota appeals a district court order suppressing evidence in its case against Denise Hahne for driving under the influence of alcohol. The district court found Hahne was stopped at a temporary sobriety checkpoint after failing to stop, and suppressed the evidence based on its conclusion that Hahne effectively had no safe or legal way to avoid the checkpoint. The Supreme Court reverses, concluding the district court relied on an erroneous legal view that law enforcement must provide motorists an opportunity to avoid temporary checkpoints. The Supreme Court holds that checkpoints need not, as a matter of law, provide motorists a way to avoid them, though avoidability may be considered in evaluating the intrusion on personal liberty. The case is remanded for proceedings to determine whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable.

New Jersey ranks 25th in The Commonwealth Fund’s 2018 state healthcare scorecard, down two places from last year. The report says New Jersey lags behind other Northeast states, including Massachusetts (2) and Vermont (4), but performs well in access to care (14th), covering kids (5th), and the amount paid by employee-based insurance plans (3rd). It ranks 19th for promoting healthy lives overall and seventh for low infant mortality. The passage also notes that while data covers total infant mortality, black babies are more than three times more likely to die than white babies.

The OECD warned that new trade barriers and rising oil prices could harm global economic growth. It said the threat of trade restrictions has begun to adversely affect confidence and that tariffs would negatively influence investment and jobs. The OECD did not name the U.S. president, but its forecast coincides with threats of tariffs or limits on foreign steel and cars, along with other countries’ retaliatory measures. It also said persistently high oil prices could raise inflation and reduce household incomes. The OECD slightly revised down its world growth forecast for this year to 3.8% after a first-quarter slowdown, with 3.9% expected next year.

Alan A. Brister sued for a refund of taxes, challenging the IRS’s 1993 reversal of withholding credits for tax years 1985 and 1986 and the resulting offsets against refunds for 1989 through 1992. The court had jurisdiction under the Tucker Act. Although the Government conceded the IRS adjustments were made more than three years after the 1985 and 1986 returns were filed, it argued the time limitation was waived under 26 U.S.C. § 6501(c)(1) because Brister filed false returns with intent to evade tax.  

After trial, the court found that Brister’s 1985 and 1986 returns, which claimed withholding amounts that were not actually paid into the Treasury, were knowingly false and filed with an intent to evade tax. The court concluded the IRS’s 1993 adjustments were timely and proper, and entered judgment for the defendant.

The 13/48 trading strategy is a technical analysis method that uses the crossover of the 13-period exponential moving average (EMA) and the 48-period EMA to identify bullish or bearish opportunities: a cross above signals a potential price rise (buy) and a cross below signals a potential price fall (sell). It is momentum-based and is described as working best in trending markets, but it can be risky in sideways or choppy markets because EMA crossovers may be unreliable. The article reports backtesting on many markets, stating it works best on stocks, with an annual return of 5.1% versus buy and hold’s 7.2%, and a slightly better risk-adjusted return of 7.8%, while noting moving average strategies can be prone to whipsaws and are lagging indicators.

The passage explains how fast progress in information and communication technologies has enabled and expanded distance education, which is defined as audio-visual interaction between teachers and learners in physically distant environments. It describes distance education as flexible and able to lower education costs, support lifelong learning, and help reduce opportunity inequality, while also presenting drawbacks such as limited socialization and issues for students lacking technology skills. The concept of equality of opportunity in education is defined as providing nondiscriminatory, equal means and conditions so learners can access required educational services and improve their competencies, noting that it has not been fully established in underdeveloped societies. The study uses a qualitative case study design with 21 faculty members and 26 students, collecting data through semi-structured interviews and analyzing it via content analysis. Findings report that faculty members see both equality-related benefits (learning at personal pace and easy access to information) and inequality-related problems (technology access and internet/infrastructure issues, financial limits, unsuitable learning environments, and disregarding learner competencies). Students similarly report equality benefits (freedom from time limits, free education, and access to sources) and inequality causes (financial capabilities and internet problems). Suggestions to improve equality include identifying learner characteristics, ensuring technology access, improving digital literacy, resolving internet infrastructure problems, state budgeting for technology access, and providing teacher consultancy services.

The lecture explains that entanglement arises in nonlinear interferometers where one photon’s phase affects another, producing states that cannot be factorized into separate subsystem wavefunctions. It reviews the definition of entanglement as states that cannot be written as a product of two wavefunctions and contrasts states that have correlated modes or cannot be physically separated with true entangled states usable as a resource. Examples include EPR (Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen) singlet-like states, photon polarization entanglement, and two-qubit Bell states. The lecture describes that entangled states are characterized by non-factorizability, non-local correlations, and fragility to decoherence, and it discusses quantifying entanglement via the von Neumann entropy of a reduced density matrix obtained by partial trace. It then presents entanglement purification: starting from partially entangled copies, performing operations and measurements on two copies to probabilistically produce Bell states with success probability depending on the initial entanglement. The lecture addresses no-cloning in relation to assumptions about producing many copies. Finally, it discusses creating entanglement between atoms probabilistically using light, beam splitters, and Hong–Ou–Mandel interference, where certain photon detection outcomes indicate that atoms are left in a Bell state.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated August 3, 2017 to early adopt new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases effective July 1, 2017. The company used a full retrospective method for revenue recognition, restating prior periods, with the most significant impacts related to software license revenue. For leases, it used a modified retrospective approach with practical expedients, resulting in material impacts on consolidated balance sheets, including recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for operating leases, while capital lease accounting remained substantially unchanged. The company stated that prior financial information is being furnished under Regulation FD consistent with the new standards, will adjust prior periods beginning with the quarter ending September 30, 2017, and will host a conference call webcast on August 3, 2017. Exhibit 99.1 contains the restated financial information for fiscal years 2017 and 2016.

In May 2007, Victor Reinoso had 12 hours to recommend a chancellor for the Washington, DC Public Schools (DCPS) as Mayor Adrian Fenty prepared to assume control following a legislative decree. The passage describes DCPS as underperforming, with many facilities problems, high superintendent turnover, and governance issues marked by patronage and decision-making by committee. Reinoso, Fenty’s deputy mayor for education and an MBA-holder with prior management and education initiatives experience, had earlier run for the school board in 2004 driven by concerns about poor school performance and lack of reform outcomes. After joining the board, he criticized the board’s emphasis on consensus and slow incremental changes, and he later viewed mayoral control as a turnaround opportunity.

After Fenty’s election in November 2006, Reinoso assembled a team, gathered data by commissioning the Parthenon Group, and drafted legislation for mayoral control. The legislation created a mayor-controlled structure with a chancellor appointed by the mayor and confirmed by the council, reduced some non-core responsibilities, and added mechanisms for interagency coordination. A chancellor search began in March, using criteria focused on rethinking public education without “sacred cows,” having a clear vision and willingness to act, and believing that school systems can change. Reinoso considered various reform leaders, including Rudy Crew and Michelle Rhee, while keeping Clifford Janey as a possible candidate but questioning whether Janey’s pace and board constraints would hinder change. In early May, Reinoso’s copy-and-use of parts of an education plan without attribution caused an uproar and a temporary hold on the takeover legislation.

The passage introduces uncertainty quantification as important in precision medicine and particularly in oncology, where noisy and indirectly informative biomedical imaging data create uncertainty in calibrated computational models. The work develops quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods to efficiently estimate expectations of clinically relevant quantities of interest from a non-linear (semi-linear) parabolic reaction-diffusion PDE model of tumor growth. The model accounts for invasion and proliferation, with patient response to systemic chemo-radiation incorporated via a treatment-related linear effect term. Uncertain diffusion and proliferation coefficients are modeled as random fields, and the expectation is computed by truncating an expansion of the formally infinite-dimensional random inputs. The paper discusses QMC as quadrature for high-dimensional integrals with potential dimension-independent error bounds and faster convergence than standard Monte Carlo for smooth integrands, and it presents well-posedness and rigorous error estimates for special random-field cases (with numerical confirmation). It also outlines problem formulation for the PDE, including boundary and initial conditions, and specifies treatment components and assumptions on initial and coefficient bounds.

An email dated Nov. 25, 2001 from Commissioner.COM to Paul Lucci contains NFL player news and fantasy football updates, listing injuries, expected starters, and recommendations for various players ahead of upcoming games. It also includes advertisements, a “Luccis Losers at Team Chick” matchup table showing player positions and points (all listed as 0.0), and a copyright notice for 2001 Commissioner.COM Inc and SportsLine.com Inc.

Mesh is described as a short-to-intermediate passing concept used across many football offenses to create defensive confusion and potential picks. It is said to work against man coverage by letting playmakers stay on the move and find completions, and against zone by helping receivers find voids so the quarterback can complete passes. The passage lists route coaching points for man and zone, quarterback progression steps (flare, shallow drag, deep drag, FB arrow), and notes the progression remains the same across defensive looks. It also covers variations including a “mesh rail” design featuring an RB rail route and a sit route by the Z receiver, and a variation adding a sit route as a response to zone coverage. The passage mentions that Bruce Eien explains how mesh is used as a variation of the smash concept in a single wing offense.

Chris Lattner, the engineer credited with creating Swift, announced on Twitter that he is heading to Google to work on Google Brain. The passage says his career has involved interest and controversy, including leaving Apple for Tesla in January and then leaving Tesla after only about six months. It also states that Google is betting heavily on AI, especially for its cloud computing division, and hopes its AI technology will help it compete with Amazon Web Services.

Culp, Inc.’s Q4 2017 earnings conference call (June 14, 2017) included remarks from CEO Frank Saxon and CFO Ken Bowling, followed by analyst questions. The company said Q4 results met expectations and were achieved despite a more challenging home furnishings retail environment, with its mattress fabrics segment posting record performance, including total annual sales surpassing the prior year. The board approved a special dividend of $0.21 per share, described as the fifth special dividend in six years.

Financial highlights for the quarter included net sales of $77.4 million, pretax income of $7 million, and net income of $6.2 million ($0.49 diluted EPS). For fiscal 2017, net sales were $309.5 million, pretax income was a record $29.7 million, and net income was $22.3 million ($1.78 diluted EPS). Adjusted EBITDA was $40.1 million, return on capital was 32%, and the company reported strong cash flow from operations and free cash flow.

Segment results: mattress fabrics Q4 sales were $48.8 million (flat), with full-year sales of $190.8 million (up 2.4%) and full-year operating income of $29.4 million (up 11%). Upholstery fabrics Q4 sales were $28.5 million (up about 1%), with full-year sales of $118.7 million (down 6%) due to soft residential retail conditions; operating income for the year was $11.1 million, slightly below the prior year.

Management discussed capital expenditures, ongoing production facility investments and consolidations (including projects in North Carolina, Canada, and a mattress cover joint venture in Haiti expected to begin during the second quarter of October), and an outlook for fiscal 2018 first-quarter sales expected to be comparable to the prior year, with mattress fabric sales slightly lower and upholstery fabric sales slightly higher. Analysts also asked about the mattress industry disruption, raw materials stability, consolidation expense timing, tax rate expectations, and potential acquisitions in the hospitality upholstery market. The company stated it was “cautiously optimistic” about acquiring hospitality-focused businesses and described hospitality as a smaller portion of upholstery revenues with higher-margin potential.

The passage describes updates and specification requirements for the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) and related SEV features. It explains how SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state from the hypervisor, how VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE), and how guests selectively share required register state via the GHCB for NAE events. It standardizes the GHCB memory area (4 KB) and versioning, including hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap. It further outlines multiple protocol functions and NAE events, including CPUID requests, page state change, SNP guest request/extended guest request for secrets and certificates, SNP AP creation, #HV doorbell page support with IPI and timer operations, retrieval of an APIC ID list, and termination requests. The passage also provides guidance for handling non-maskable interrupts (NMI) and lists expected guest/hypervisor behaviors for GHCB/VMGEXIT processing, interrupt shadow handling around HLT, and secure AVIC backing page management. It states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported, and describes required behaviors for SEV-ES guest identification and SMP booting under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP.

Scott is expected to decide how much time he wants to devote to hockey and how much to his family after deciding to have enough of coaching. The passage notes that sacrifices in the business include time away from family, and it says Scott’s passion and energy—watching hockey games, working on broadcasts, and talking to people—are seen as second to none and have contributed to his success.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon said it is “unacceptable” that Channel 4 has a 28.6% gender pay gap. She said she is determined to improve it and aims to have a 50:50 split of men and women in the 100 top jobs by 2023. Mahon said the gap is due to the lower half of the organisation being about 66% female, and that in the top 100 most highly paid positions only 34 are held by women. She said Channel 4 does not consider the gap fitting its inclusive, diversity-focused agenda. The passage also notes that Channel 4’s gap is above the national average and compares it with gaps at ITN and the BBC, and mentions related BBC reviews and resignations.

The passage describes technology for sealing fluid flow passages in high-pressure oil and gas devices (notably plug valves and hydraulic fracturing fluid ends) where corrosive/abrasive fluids cause erosion and leakage. It explains that, under harsh conditions, seals can abrade valve body bores or other body surfaces, and that conventional repairs (e.g., weld build-up and machining) are cumbersome and disruptive. The described approach transfers erosion wear from the device body to the mating sealed component (such as an insert, plug, retaining nut, discharge plug, suction plug, or sleeve), making repair easier and reducing downtime and cost.  

The summary of the invention includes fluid end assemblies with housing conduits intersecting internal chambers and having endless grooves or recessed corner sections for mounting seals, as well as methods for manufacturing such assemblies. The detailed description contrasts previously attempted valve designs where seals mounted on mating components caused body bore erosion with embodiments where recesses/grooves in the body intersect bores so seals can extend to seal against the mating component, shifting wear away from the body. It also describes similar erosion-transfer concepts applied to fluid ends, including seal designs and optional erosion-resistant surface treatments on plugs, and discusses managing air pressure during stuffing box sleeve insertion via breather openings.

The passage describes multivariate long-term time series forecasting and the limitations of existing deep learning methods due to time series complexity. It identifies that accurate long-term forecasting depends on inter-channel dependencies and time dependencies, which include trend and periodic components. The paper proposes CTPNet (Channel, Trend and Period-wise representation learning Network) to learn three complementary dependency levels: inter-channel dependencies (I1), intra-subsequence dependencies (I2), and inter-subsequence dependencies (I3). CTPNet uses temporal query-based Multi-Head Attention for I1, an efficient-attention Transformer approach for I2, and a similar mechanism for inter-subsequence modeling. The method includes downsampling based on periodicity and a unified encode-decode structure with recombination via an inverse downsampling process. It also presents a problem statement, a formulation for downsampling, and descriptions of the Channel-wise Representation Learning and Trend-wise Representation Learning components, along with a table of forecasting results on multiple benchmarks.

A pickup truck driver was taken into custody Thursday afternoon after multiple collisions in Maple Ridge. Ridge Meadows RCMP received 911 calls around 3 p.m. about a black pickup driving recklessly in a strip mall parking lot. The driver backed into a vehicle, crashed through barricades, jumped a curb, and smashed into a bus stop, injuring a female pedestrian and her son with non-life-threatening injuries. A 34-year-old man from Mission was arrested at the scene for impaired driving, hit and run, and dangerous driving causing bodily harm, and was released on a promise to appear in court.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 26, 2020. The report states that Microsoft issued a press release updating its revenue guidance for its More Personal Computing segment for the quarter ending March 30, 2020, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes information about the company, its securities, and a signature by Frank H. Brod, Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage describes disappointment at not scoring right away but maintaining a positive attitude while working and believing the speaker was playing well. They say scoring would come with time and that the most important goal was winning. After eventually scoring, they express that being part of a win would make them the happiest despite earlier concerns about not appearing on the score sheets.

Ray Jones, Jr. was indicted for first degree murder of his two and one-half month old son and, after jury trial, was found guilty as charged. At sentencing, the same jury unanimously recommended life imprisonment without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension of sentence, and the trial judge imposed that sentence. On appeal, Jones challenged the admission of three inculpatory statements, arguing they were not freely and voluntarily made after Miranda warnings. The trial judge found the first two hospital statements were voluntary and not the result of custodial interrogation requiring Miranda warnings, and found the police station statement was also freely and voluntarily made. The appellate court agreed that the statements were properly admitted; even if the police station statement had been admitted in error, the court found the error harmless beyond a reasonable doubt. Jones also argued the trial judge improperly restricted his cross-examination of Dr. Bienvenue, but the appellate court held the restriction was within the judge’s discretion. The conviction and sentence were affirmed.

The passage discusses how generative artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) could transform assessment in higher education. It outlines concerns about academic integrity, including the difficulty of distinguishing AI-generated text from student work and challenges for AI detection tools. The passage describes traditional assessment methods (e.g., MCQs, essays) as potentially less authentic and more vulnerable to AI interference, and it considers ways to adapt assessment by raising question complexity, shifting away from non-proctored formats, and integrating AI into formative and summative assessment design. It also summarizes opportunities for using generative AI for feedback (e.g., idea generation, recommendations, rubric generation, practice questions) while noting risks such as inconsistent accuracy and possible bias or misalignment with curriculum. The text then presents a case study from a UK immunology MSc program where a 2000-word essay assessment was redesigned: students received guidance on AI policies, used ChatGPT to draft outlines, and participated in peer evaluation of those drafts, with the final essay written without further ChatGPT assistance. Student survey and discussion results report that 57.9% had used generative AI, confidence was low (5% very confident), and students mainly used AI for planning, drafting, summarizing, and proofreading. Students were generally critical of AI limitations (accuracy and superficiality) but saw value in learning about AI capabilities and limitations, and they showed mixed views on whether AI use counts as plagiarism. The passage concludes that integrating AI into assessment requires training and holistic policy changes to support educator and student AI literacy, maintain academic integrity, and promote more authentic and diverse assessment approaches.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said there is “no contemplation” of moving the 2026 NBA All-Star Game out of Los Angeles despite the league investigating whether the Clippers circumvented salary cap rules related to a $28 million endorsement contract involving Kawhi Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC. Silver said planning for the All-Star Game and related activities will proceed independently of the investigation. The 2026 All-Star Game, expected to feature a new U.S. vs. international team format, will be televised by NBC on Feb. 15, and the league previously announced it would be held at Intuit Dome. The NBA opened the investigation after reporting last month and said penalties could include fines up to $7.5 million, voiding contracts, and forfeiting future draft picks.

Three months after the new year, Scotland will introduce a landmark law under the Abusive Behaviour and Sexual Harm Act making “revenge porn” disclosures a criminal offence. From April 1, convictions for disclosing or threatening to disclose intimate photos or videos will carry a maximum penalty of five years imprisonment. The offence covers sharing filmed and still images of someone in an intimate situation, including private images where the person is nude, in underwear only, or engaged in a sexual act. The law is intended to address increased sharing online enabled by devices like smartphones and social media. Justice Secretary Michael Matheson said the measures aim to prevent cruelty and fear for victims and reflect technological changes, and that broader work beyond legislation is also being pursued to eliminate abusive behaviour and sexual violence in Scotland.

The passage describes controlling mobile agricultural machines by performing active ground terrain mapping. A pose detection sensor generates position and orientation signals along a route, which are used to identify a virtual point cloud estimated to correspond to the ground surface under and around the machine. Elevation values are generated for points in the point cloud, confidence/weight values are assigned based on distance from the pose detection system, and elevation values are aggregated into a georeferenced elevation map with associated layers such as confidence, number of points, and variance. A control system generates control signals based on the map (e.g., for boom or header height control, steering, speed changes, and crop volume estimation) and may update the map using trigger-based pose measurements as the machine continues operating. The passage includes example implementations and describes related machine components, sensor trigger mechanisms, point cloud and map configuration, weighting functions, and map storage and communication options, including cloud computing architectures.

The passage defines micro-credentials as certifications assessing knowledge and skills gained through specific learning experiences, particularly in technology-enabled contexts. It notes that uptake is driven by a skills gap between traditional higher education and digital-world work needs. In Mauritius, the study explores whether education and industry leaders are ready to adopt and whether employers will recognize micro-credentials from diverse learning pathways. A qualitative interview-based methodology is used, with semi-structured interviews of educational leaders and industry leaders in Mauritius. Results describe varied understandings of micro-credentials and related badge concepts, emphasize expected formal assessment for credibility, and suggest preference for a flexible or hybrid integration model with academic credits. Respondents generally view micro-credentials as part of the future of higher education but expect incremental implementation due to limited current commonness and regulatory challenges. Key recommendations include mapping micro-credentials within national qualifications and credit frameworks, using reliable competency-based assessment, and adapting regulatory structures to support recognition of both formal and informal learning.

Rashad Snell Matthew Shashy, 29, of Montgomery, was sentenced to four years of probation for discharging a firearm outside Maxwell Air Force Base. After a 2017 trial, a federal jury found him guilty of impeding, intimidating, and interfering with Air Force personnel. The jury heard that on New Year’s weekend Shashy spray-painted anti-government graffiti at locations including the Day Street entrance of Maxwell, then on January 3, 2017, fired a shotgun three times toward the Day Street entrance during morning rush hour before leaving. He was identified after a civilian observed the shooting and photographed the truck’s license plate, and after Shashy barricaded himself at his residence with additional firearms, ammunition, anti-government literature, and other evidence found there. The Montgomery Police Department and the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force investigated, and Todd A. Brown prosecuted.

Brookfield recently held an investor day where Brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP) presented from a management perspective, and the article provides additional information and the author’s views. BIP is described as the most successful Brookfield partnership, with 20% annualized returns since inception in 2008 and Adjusted AFFO rising from $352M in 2012 to $926M due to investments and favorable conditions. The article states BIP’s distribution yield is 4% and its AFFO yield is 5.84%, implying 1.84% is retained to grow the business. Brookfield aims to increase distributions annually by 6% to 9%, supported by infrastructure growth opportunities and BIP’s current operations; past same-store EBITDA growth averaged 5% on a constant-currency basis. The lower current yield is attributed mainly to stock price increases, which the author says benefits existing unitholders by enabling unit issuances to be invested at higher rates. The article also warns that growth through issuing units depends on unit prices. It concludes that while past performance was strong, future returns may be less favorable at current valuations, though BIP is still described as attractive due to the 4% yield and expected 6% growth, implying about 10% total returns.

A Phase 2 trial found that combining a 16-week course of omalizumab with oral immunotherapy (OIT) improved OIT efficacy for children allergic to multiple foods. After 36 weeks, 83% of 36 children receiving omalizumab and OIT could safely consume two-gram portions of at least two allergenic foods, versus 33% of 12 children receiving placebo and OIT. The omalizumab group also had fewer OIT-related adverse events during weeks 8 to 16. The trial enrolled 48 participants aged 4 to 15 with allergies to foods including milk, egg, wheat, soy, sesame seeds, peanut, or tree nuts, who received omalizumab or placebo injections for 16 weeks and then began daily OIT at week 8. Researchers said the results suggest omalizumab may help safely and rapidly facilitate desensitization to multiple food allergens, and that larger studies are needed.

An archaeological search for a rifle linked to Willie Halpin at Dublin City Hall found no rifle. Archaeologists excavated debris in a narrow gap believed to have held the weapon for about 100 years, removing a drainpipe blocking access and uncovering roof fragments (including one with a bullet hole), 1930s milk bottles, a teapot lid, and pottery. Consultant archaeologist Franc Myles said the likely scenario was the rifle had been thrown into the gap and removed soon after the Rising, possibly during later inspections involving the Black and Tans. He also said rodent activity mixed the debris, citing findings including a 1980s item at the bottom and pottery likely from 1890. Dublin City Council financed the work, and Nial Ring and the Halpin family had promoted the project despite disappointment.

The passage describes how, in 1874, store credit shoppers’ details were recorded in a blue book, marking the start of the Equifax business model. It says the model was intended for businesses that want to lend, with regular people as the product.
