It explains that knowing patrons makes lending safer and easier for “creditworthy” customers, but notes that credit bureaus like Equifax have grown into large corporations that monitor much of individuals’ financial lives without people opting in. It also states that opting out is difficult and mentions that lawmakers have struggled to regulate credit bureaus for about fifty years.

The passage says Victoria Hospital timed a $5.25 million ovarian cancer research announcement with Valentine’s Day because the donation is tied to a love story. John Knight died on Jan. 21, 2016, leaving $5.25 million from his estate to tribute his wife Mary, who died of ovarian cancer in 2008. The funds will support hiring researchers, buying equipment, and enabling international collaborations to expand the Lawson Health Research Institute’s ability to attract cancer specialists. The researchers involved said ovarian cancer is difficult to detect early and that their work focuses on understanding how it metastasizes and how cancer cells grow and move, with partnerships needed to achieve progress. The first floor lobby in Victoria Hospital’s A-block was branded the Mary and John Knight atrium in recognition of Knight’s generosity.

ETF Channel compared each holding’s trading price to its average analyst 12-month forward target and computed a weighted implied analyst target for the Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth ETF (VOT) of $145.80 per unit. With VOT trading near $132.83, this implies 9.77% upside. Notable upside among underlying holdings includes Sensata Technologies Holding (ST) at $51.40 with a $57.24 target (11.37%), Global Payments (GPN) at $109.34 with a $120.65 target (10.34%), and Markel (MKL) at $1111.05 with a $1225.00 target (10.26%). The passage notes that further investor research is needed to determine whether these targets are justified or overly optimistic.

The government launched the Tanzania Business Clinic (TBC) in Dar es Salaam to speed up improvements to Tanzania’s business climate. Industry, Trade and Investment minister Charles Mwijage said TBC will use business experts and public officials to provide long- and short-term solutions, with a head office in Dar es Salaam and branches in all Small Industries Development Organisation (Sido) offices. The initiative follows Cabinet adoption of a blueprint for amendments to laws and regulations to improve the business environment. Finance and Planning minister Philip Mpango said implementation would begin in the 2018/19 financial year and would focus on attracting private sector investment in sectors including textiles, leather and meat, fish and edible oil, medicines and medical equipment, food and animal feeds, and mining, and would target regulatory reform areas such as value added tax, import prices, immigration and labour, social security, and environmental management. The passage notes Tanzania’s lower ranking in the World Bank’s Doing Business 2018 Report and says Mwijage expects the blueprint to help change regulators’ attitudes toward businesses, with emphasis on locally sourced raw material–consuming industries and manufacturing, including cooking oil and pharmaceuticals.

Chamath Palihapitiya, a former Facebook vice president of user growth, said in an interview at Stanford that he feels “tremendous guilt” for helping Facebook become what it is, citing concerns that Facebook’s tools are “ripping apart” social fabric. He attributed this to “short-term, dopamine-driven feedback loops,” leading to outcomes like reduced civil discourse and increased misinformation, describing it as a global problem. Sean Parker, Facebook’s founding president and Napster co-founder, said social media changes relationships in society, may interfere with productivity, and could affect children’s brains. Antonio Garcia-Martinez, a former Facebook product manager, said the company misrepresents its ability to influence users based on data it collects. Palihapitiya said he believes Facebook does positive good but that he plans to use his pay for structural changes he can control.

Julia Banks, who won Chisholm for the Liberal Party in 2016 after it was held by Labor for almost 20 years, faced questions about whether she held dual Greek Australian citizenship. On Friday, many voters in her electorate were largely unaware of the doubts, and some said they would likely vote Liberal again if she were ruled ineligible and a byelection held. A politics lecturer said a byelection would likely favour Labor in the “classic marginal seat,” noting Labor had held the seat by just over 1 per cent and that a byelection could encourage multiple candidates and increase vote volatility. Labor strategists expressed confidence but said it would likely be tight, with campaign issues likely including young people’s housing affordability and mortgage and rental security. The 2016 campaign that helped Banks win was partly supported by a social media strategy targeting voters from Chinese backgrounds, and she defeated Labor candidate Stefanie Perri by 2,154 votes on a two-party-preferred basis.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says GPT-5 critics misunderstood the model and that his attitude toward AGI has changed. He also describes that GPT-5 had problems during a livestream, including glitches and charts with inaccurate numbers. In a Reddit AMA, users said the model was not friendly and asked for the previous version to be restored, and critics felt GPT-5 fell short of OpenAI’s high expectations.

The passage describes on-field non-verbal communication in soccer, mainly through hand signals, to coordinate actions such as starting set pieces and passes, directing runs around defenders, indicating where teammates should move, requesting throw-ins, substitutions, or specific free kicks and corner/throw-in types, and goalkeeper signals for organizing the wall and directing defenders. It also lists other non-verbal cues like head nods, ball-contact gestures to start play, bounce-counting for corner kicks, and a made-up signal for an offside trap. The passage notes that coaches and players may need to develop non-verbal systems when crowd noise prevents players from hearing each other.

The passage describes UHS-I and UHS-II/III behavior and initialization sequences for SD memory cards. It explains how UHS-I bus speed modes are selected using CMD0, ACMD41, CMD11 (voltage switch), CMD6 (driver strength and mode selection), and CMD42 (unlocking when locked), including restrictions such as switching from 1.8V signaling requiring a power cycle and UHS-I supporting only 4-bit mode. It also covers tuning requirements using CMD19 for SDR50/SDR104. For UHS-II, it outlines interface selection and initialization, including PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization, plus deactivation before completing ACMD41. The text lists supported speed modes and notes optional and mandatory requirements, then transitions into SD card host/card command and state concepts for identification and data transfer modes. It further describes the SD card command flow (APP_CMD/CMD55 and CMD56), card initialization with CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41, and UHS-related voltage switching fields.

Ulysses S. Grant, President of the United States, issued a proclamation warning that illegal military enterprises and expeditions are being organized within the U.S. to act against the people and district of the Dominion of Canada, where the United States is at peace with Her Majesty the Queen of the United Kingdom. He admonished citizens and others to not aid or take part in such unlawful proceedings, warned that those committing illegal acts would forfeit government protection, and instructed U.S. officers to prevent and defeat the proceedings and arrest those involved. The proclamation is dated May 24, 1870, in Washington, and signed by Grant with Hamilton Fish as Secretary of State.

An 11-year-old boy, Damian Sunderland, was attacked by a relative’s dog at home on June 20 and underwent months of surgery after being flown to intensive care at Children’s Mercy Hospital and then transferred to the University of Kansas Hospital. He recently had major surgery to graft skin to his cheeks, lower jaw, nose, and recreate his lips, using skin grafts from his arms and legs, with additional plans to tattoo permanent color later. His mother, DeAnn Tieman, said he is excited to get lips again.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell technologies and architecture features. It introduces the AI Management Processor (AMP), a GPU-based scheduler that offloads GPU context scheduling from the system CPU to reduce latency and improve game performance and multitasking. It explains Blackwell additions to video/display features, including hardware 4:2:2 chroma encode/decode support, a discussion of YUV chroma subsampling tradeoffs, the ninth-generation NVENC encoder and improved NVDEC decoder support, and DisplayPort 2.1b bandwidth and refresh-rate capabilities. It also covers Blackwell Max-Q power-efficiency improvements using advanced power gating, clock/power/rail controls, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep states, with example power savings. The passage then outlines DLSS 4 and its Multi Frame Generation, transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, and how AMP helps scheduling and frame pacing. Finally, it describes neural shaders as a direction for future rendering and gives examples of neural techniques such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces, followed by a hardware overview of the Blackwell GPU family and brief specifications for GeForce RTX 5090/5080/5070 Ti/5070 and other GPUs.

The passage is a VentureWire newsletter dated May 22, 2001, addressed to jdasovic@enron.com. It lists “top stories” including Kodiak Venture Partners closing Fund II with $290 million, Mercury Interactive acquiring Freshwater Software for $147 million, Celetron closing a $48 million first round, and TVM announcing the first close of a life science fund at EUR 70 million. It also includes sections on “new money” (multiple companies raising funding rounds), “bad news” (staff cuts and ceased operations at AgWeb.com, Ironmax, and Rx.com), “new products” (AuctioNet.com renaming to Realm Connect; Nextira Federal launching operations), “M&A” (several acquisitions and stock deals), “new directors” and “new people” (board and executive appointments), “vc fund news” and “vc personnel” (fund program and venture firm leadership changes), plus “vw corrections” noting prior newsletter errors.

The passage describes a Phase 2/3 observer-blind randomized controlled study in India evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of SII-NVX-CoV2373 (NVX-CoV2373 made by Serum Institute of India) in children and adolescents aged 2 to 17 years. A prior literature search found no pediatric publications on SII-NVX-CoV2373 (2–17) before 06 Dec 2022, with one adolescent pre-print on NVX-CoV2373.  

The study enrolled 920 participants (460 aged 12–17 and 460 aged 2–11), randomized 3:1 to receive two doses of SII-NVX-CoV2373 or placebo. Primary objectives were to assess non-inferiority of immune responses versus adult participants and to evaluate safety via solicited and unsolicited adverse events. Blood samples were collected for anti-spike IgG, neutralizing antibodies, and variant responses (Delta, Omicron BA.1, Omicron BA.5) using specified assays.  

Results reported strong immune responses after vaccination: anti-S IgG and neutralizing antibodies rose after the second dose, and non-inferiority versus adults was met in both pediatric age groups. Variant-specific assays in a subset showed immune responses against Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.5. Safety outcomes included no AESIs; SAEs in adolescents were reported as viral infection and gastroenteritis and assessed as unrelated to the vaccine, with no SAEs or AESIs in younger children. Overall, the vaccine was concluded to be safe and well tolerated and to generate robust immune responses, including against variants of concern.

The passage describes Mud Bay’s efforts to create “good jobs” and improve its business through employee ownership, open-book management, and a customer-focused “Mud Bay Experience.” It outlines Mud Bay’s history, including the development of its mission and culture, and details its employee practices such as pay and benefits, scheduling, training, transparency, and profit sharing. It then summarizes industry context and Mud Bay’s “Good Jobs Vision,” including five strategies (invest in staff; deliver more by offering less at everyday low prices; standardize processes and enable continuous improvement; improve efficiencies via cross-training and slack; and partner with animal welfare organizations). The passage reports that although Mud Bay implemented many initiatives from 2015–2018, it fell short on areas like standardization and continuous improvement, and profitability declined due to higher wages, benefits, and lower prices. It concludes with the decision process about shortening store hours, including internal disagreement and an analysis of sales by time of day, as well as reported improvements in customer and employee experiences.

The passage explains that document management affects businesses of all sizes and that poor document management can waste time and money and harm customer service. It cites costs such as renting off-site storage space, office space for file cabinets, and expenses for paper and printer supplies. It also notes risks like sensitive documents being left on printers or accounting documents not being collected. A Xerox survey is mentioned, stating that about 40% of business processes are still document driven, and that the biggest benefit of better document management is improved workflow, with small and midsize businesses improving processes to grow and boost productivity. Suggested steps include tracking printing costs, using cloud scanning with Xerox ConnectKey-enabled printers and apps to scan to services like Google Drive and Dropbox, using CapturePoint to securely scan and transform paper into editable information, and enabling mobility with the Xerox Mobile Link App. Additional recommendations include setting printing restrictions with PIN requirements, limiting color printing by department or other criteria, and using printers that notify users when toner is running low.

The passage outlines distance education approaches and defines distance education using learner-centeredness, lifelong learning, flexible learning, and removing barriers to access. It discusses Moore’s Theory of Transactional Distance, which links course structure, dialogue, and learner autonomy to psychological and cognitive distance, and notes policy requirements for support structures in distance education in South Africa. It also reviews studies applying transactional distance and explains the role of work-integrated learning and practical experience in qualifications, specifically relating to Physical Education within Life Orientation. The study uses a qualitative design at North-West University, involving 17 third-year distance learning students and four lecturers, collecting data via open-ended questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. The analysis identifies five themes: student–lecturer interaction, lecturers’ competence and enthusiasm, obstacles in Physical Education distance learning, experiences with practical training, and how the program content influences perceptions. Participants report positive lecturer availability and increased confidence linked to teaching passion and competence, but identify obstacles including limited student foundational knowledge, technological illiteracy and internet access, and assignment administration problems. Practical training through videos is viewed positively but is constrained by delays in feedback. Students generally perceive the program content as interesting and valuable, and recommendations include more face-to-face contact, additional technological training, improved use of videos and media, stronger student interaction features in learning systems, and better university management and administration.

The passage states that a passport is a legal statement that the named person is a U.S. citizen, and U.S. law forbids issuing passports to non-citizens. The Secretary of State and diplomatic and consular officers may grant passports under rules prescribed by the President, and passports are generally issued to law-abiding citizens who apply and comply, though issuance is not automatic for every citizen. A passport requires satisfactory establishment of the applicant’s citizenship, U.S. domicile, and intention to return to reside and perform citizens’ duties; expatriated persons cannot receive passports. Expatriation is described as quitting one’s country with abandoned allegiance and intent to become permanently a resident and citizen elsewhere, but indefinite residence abroad with bona fide intention to revert does not amount to self-expatriation. Whether expatriation exists depends on case circumstances, and even without proof of expatriation, those permanently resident and domiciled outside the United States cannot receive passports. The passage also discusses how various factors—such as severed ties versus maintained family/property connections or legitimate American enterprise abroad—may influence decisions. Finally, it describes the Department’s position toward American citizens in certain foreign jurisdictions, indicating passports may protect them while their pursuits are legitimate and not harmful to friendly relations.

A city court in Thiruvananthapuram reserved its order on Congress leader Shashi Tharoor’s anticipatory bail plea for tomorrow in a case related to his wife Sunanda Pushkar’s death. Tharoor, already summoned as an accused, sought anticipatory bail after a chargesheet was filed and the SIT said the probe was concluded and custodial interrogation was not required. The Delhi Police opposed the plea, arguing Tharoor might flee the country and could influence witnesses, while Tharoor’s advocates said the police’s position differed from earlier statements. Pushkar died in a hotel suite on January 17, 2014, and Tharoor has been charged under IPC sections 498A and 306 but has not been arrested.

Matt Barbet launched his cycling podcast “Home Roads,” inspired by the idea that bike rides are a way to get to know people. The series, launching on iTunes and Acast on June 8, features Barbet riding in various locations and talking with professional cyclists and other figures about cycling and their past and personal lives. Four episodes are available immediately, with guests including Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche, and David Millar, and additional recorded episodes featuring Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram, and Philippa York.

The passage explains the 200-day moving average (200 DMA) as a technical analysis indicator that averages an asset’s closing prices over the past 200 trading days to smooth fluctuations and identify trends. It outlines how moving averages are calculated, notes that the 200 DMA rule is often treated as a trend-following indicator (price above indicates an uptrend; below indicates a downtrend), and discusses different moving-average types (SMA and EMA), with the article using SMA for simplicity.

It describes advantages of the 200 DMA strategy as simplicity, “riding the trend,” and “playing defense,” and provides reasons it can work well, particularly in recessions and bear markets where it may help avoid bear-market declines. It also emphasizes that it is not a “silver bullet,” citing periods when it may underperform due to whipsaws and false signals when there is no significant bear market. Backtests and examples mentioned include the S&P 500 around the 2007–09 period, oil in 2020, and a comparison to a Jeremy Siegel-based variation of a 200-day SMA strategy, with results generally described as similar and sometimes slightly improved. The passage also covers adding filters and using 200 DMA in crossover systems, and includes brief FAQ-style answers about time frames, what it means when price falls below the 200 DMA, and how to plot it.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 GPU improvements over V100 across the compute and memory hierarchy, including higher DRAM and L2 cache bandwidth, a larger 40 MB L2 cache with improved cache management controls, and Compute Data Compression that can save up to 4x DRAM bandwidth. It also explains MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) for partitioning an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated memory paths and quality-of-service controls, and discusses related concepts like fault isolation and vGPU use cases. Additional sections cover third-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, error detection and fault containment, and several A100 architecture features (NVJPG decode, optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and more NVDEC units). The text further outlines CUDA 11 features such as CUDA Task Graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls for persistent data. It concludes with an overview of DGX A100 as an AI infrastructure platform using A100 and MIG, plus an appendix primer on sparse neural networks and pruning, including fine-grained structured sparsity.

Lecture 14 covers hinged dissections and related ideas. The professor says there is no general hinged-dissection animation software yet, and suggests project possibilities including tools for animating hinged dissections, implementing “slender adornments,” and designing more hinged dissections. The lecture discusses Frederickson’s hinged dissection examples and books, outlines universal hinged folding results for 2D shapes such as polyominoes/polyhexes/polyiamonds using induction and hinge-visible-on-edges conditions, and notes similar approaches in 3D (e.g., tetrahedron-based constructions with cyclic hinges). It also describes hardware and related applications, including salt-triggered folding in a Petri dish, DNA origami as a form of controlled folding, and 3D continuous-motion “chain of balls” mechanisms for shape-changing robots. The lecture then returns to theoretical bounds and techniques for hinged dissections, including a pseudopolynomial bound under grid assumptions, and concludes with a brief overview of 3D dissection constraints using volume and the Dehn invariant, including necessary and sufficient conditions for when polyhedra of equal volume can be dissected into each other.

Researchers found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots learn about the usefulness of objects through play, similar to human infants. In a study led by researchers at the Universities of York and St Andrews, the birds solved tasks more successfully when they had explored the relevant object beforehand. The researchers tested the birds with different blocks and ropes, then required them to collapse a platform and retrieve a reward using tools, replacing the original ball and stick with the blocks and ropes to see if earlier exploration helped. The study suggested the birds learned object properties incidentally through exploration, and found no evidence they changed how they interacted with objects after learning they could be used as tools.

The passage contains multiple hockey postgame and commentary remarks. It describes a win and discusses taxing minutes with players sharing workload, strong forward play that supported defense, and the team’s best period being the third when they were down players. It praises fast, north-south play, taking pucks to the net, scoring chances, players’ speed, physical hits, and effective line performance creating turnovers and playing physically. It notes two top goaltenders with different styles and mentions needing clarification about contact. It also includes discussion of a player’s attitude and work ethic, the intensity and physical nature of series, and expectations for a hard playoff series. Later, it shifts to a coach/player’s background in coaching and excitement about an opportunity to play for the Stanley Cup, plus plans to stay focused and execute game plans one game at a time, without discussing lineup possibilities.

NAE events are all exit events that are not AE events. When an NAE occurs with an SEV-ES guest running, the hardware throws Communication Exception (#VC), and the #VC error code equals the VMEXIT code of the event. The guest inspects the #VC error code, prepares GHCB state, and invokes VMGEXIT to generate an AE event, after which the guest resumes after the VMGEXIT instruction and can copy results from the GHCB back to internal state. The guest and hypervisor use a VALID_BITMAP mechanism to indicate which GHCB fields are set, and SW_EXITCODE/SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2 fields are used to carry request and response information, with non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] treated as hypervisor errors.  

The passage also describes specific NAE events and requirements, including handling for IOIO_PROT faults, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change (including reason/error handling and tracking progress in shared structures), SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request (including use of shared pages and possible retry/error signaling), and additional SEV-SNP-related events such as AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, and Secure AVIC backing page registration/unregistration. It further notes that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported, and outlines interrupt delivery and #HV doorbell page behavior and guest/host handling conventions under the Restricted Injection feature.

Joan Jordan, an Irish software engineer diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) in 2010, said she struggled to get hired after her illness, describing repeated rejections as “soul destroying.” She stopped working the year before her diagnosis and later said her ability to work was taken from her, despite studying computer science at Trinity. She is now working 15 hours a week with Eupati, has the relapse-remitting type of MS, and is on medication. She has written the book “huManS Multiple Sclerosis,” and is looking for a sponsor to print more copies. To mark World MS Day, MS Ireland launched a report, developed with Novartis, aiming to improve understanding of MS research and support researchers, including recommendations such as an MS Research Community, better data sharing, greater involvement of people living with MS, and improved dissemination.

Saskatchewan Roughriders receiver Duron Carter has been used as a cornerback, and the team is also considering using standout return man Christion Jones in the defensive backfield. Jones practiced with the defence before, but received his most extensive defensive back reps this week as an “emergency DB” ahead of a game against the Hamilton Tiger-Cats. He said he is ready to play either offence or defence and that he has practised both receiver and defensive back roles in his background, though he noted the CFL’s style differs. Jones has been comparing notes with Carter, and he is listed as a backup receiver and has tailback experience. The team values versatility, and Jones is a major special teams contributor, ranking No. 3 in the CFL in punt-return average (14.5) and kickoff-return average (24.3), while leading the league in combined yards (531) despite not seeing any offensive action. The team’s head coach and GM Chris Jones said the main reason Jones hasn’t played defence or offence is concern about increasing his workload, citing past return-game issues for other players, but said the approach could change if needed.

The passage describes memory devices and techniques for address obfuscation combined with wear-leveling to improve memory lifetime and make it harder to reverse-engineer wear patterns. It explains how logical addresses received in access commands are mapped to physical addresses in memory arrays using configurable mapping functions that can vary per device/die/array and over time based on triggers, random numbers, unique identifiers, schedules, or security keys. Wear-leveling moves data between physical locations according to a wear-leveling function to distribute cell wear, and the passage discusses how wear patterns could otherwise be deduced if reverse-engineered. The disclosure includes example systems, memory architectures (including 2D/3D and multi-die configurations), mapping/select components and logic operations (e.g., pass-through, inversion, XOR/XNOR, address swap), example address mapping tables, and flow diagrams for selecting a mapping function, receiving an access command with a logical address, determining the physical address, and accessing data.

The passage provides safety instructions, hearing safety guidance, and cleaning tips for a SanDisk Sansa Fuze media player, including warnings about headphone use while driving or in hazardous situations, avoiding high volume to prevent noise-induced hearing loss, and keeping the player away from moisture. It also covers disposal guidance and describes the player’s features and controls, such as supported audio/video/photo formats, FM radio (if applicable), voice recording, storage expansion, battery charging, power/reset functions, and the Hold/Lock switch. Additional sections outline basic usage for transferring media, playing music/audiobooks/videos/photos, using repeat/shuffle/equalizer options, recording voice, managing FM presets, deleting content, and customizing system settings. The passage concludes with troubleshooting and service/warranty information, including how to contact technical support and the terms of a one-year limited warranty and an end user license agreement.

Engravings at Jebel Misma show early human presence in the Nefud, indicating the region was lush in the past. The rock art, highlighted in color, includes a superimposed figure of a woman to show scale, and the camels depicted are described as having been frozen in a march for 12,000 years.

The passage argues that K-12 education has shifted from teaching knowledge to emphasizing “21st century skills,” with little focus on acquiring knowledge. It says skills goals are often vague or confused, and that analyzing, communicating, or using digital tools requires background knowledge; “critical thinking” cannot substitute for it. The author provides examples, including understanding complex physics concepts like string theory and reading passages with cultural references, to show that comprehension depends on studied knowledge rather than the ability to “look it up.” The passage also discusses trends such as grade inflation, reduced state testing requirements, and limited mainstream attention to content-rich curricula, while noting that some states have moved toward high-quality instructional materials that must include “building knowledge.” It concludes by arguing that children need knowledge and that without knowledge people lack the foundation for complex thought.

The passage is largely composed of NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q filing information and detailed financial statements for the quarterly period ended May 1, 2022. It includes condensed consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, shareholders’ equity, and cash flows, along with notes describing accounting policies and specific items such as the termination of the Arm acquisition agreement, lease obligations, stock-based compensation, income taxes, cash equivalents and marketable securities, fair value measurements, goodwill and intangible assets, deferred revenue, derivative instruments, debt, commitments and contingencies, and segment information. It also provides management’s discussion of financial condition and results of operations, including revenue and segment trends, gross margin and operating expense changes, liquidity and capital resources, share repurchases and dividends, debt and commercial paper, contractual obligations, climate-related disclosures, market risk and foreign exchange risk discussions, and controls and procedures. The filing further references legal proceedings, risk factors, and where additional information can be found, including use of social media channels for disclosure.

Malaria is described as a major global health burden, with most cases and deaths in sub-Saharan Africa and over three-quarters of deaths occurring in children under 5. In Nigeria, malaria accounts for nearly 27% of global cases, with substantial reported illness, deaths, and economic losses. The passage notes that insecticide-treated nets (ITNs), including long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), are part of WHO-recommended interventions and are presented as a cost-effective strategy that can reduce malaria burden.

The study uses secondary data from the 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) to examine factors associated with ITN ownership and use among children under 5 and pregnant women. Data were collected from 13,727 households and included household and child sociodemographic and economic characteristics. Results show that 56% of Nigerian households possessed at least one ITN, with rural households, certain geopolitical zones (notably North East and North West), and lower wealth quintiles showing higher ITN ownership.

Regarding usage, only 41.4% of children under 5 slept under an ITN the night before the survey. ITN use among children was significantly associated with age, residence, geopolitical zone, and household wealth quintile, with younger children, rural residence, North West/North East regions, and lower wealth quintiles having higher likelihoods of sleeping under an ITN. For pregnant women, about half (49.6%) slept under an ITN. ITN use among pregnant women was significantly associated with geopolitical zone and household wealth quintile, and was less common among women with no or primary education compared with women with more than secondary education, based on multivariate findings.

The authors conclude that progress has been made but ITN utilization remains below the Nigeria National Malaria Strategic Plan targets, emphasizing the need to address regional disparities and socioeconomic factors through improved access to healthcare, expanded distribution, and strengthened health education.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali is taking a leave of absence from his businesses after allegations reported by Eater that he engaged in inappropriate misconduct with a female chef he met at a New Orleans function 10 years ago, and that three women who worked for him over the past two decades accused him of sexual misconduct. Batali said the allegations “match up” with his previous behavior, apologized, and took full responsibility, adding that the behavior was wrong. He is also removed from the cast of ABC’s “The Chew.”

HMD Global, which makes Nokia-branded phones, has released an Android 8.1 beta for the Nokia 8. The passage says that although HMD’s Chief Product Officer Juho Sarvikas tweeted on September 20, 2017 that the Nokia 8 would not have its bootloader unlocked for security reasons, HMD would share its kernel modifications as a work in progress, the kernel modifications have not yet been shared despite a delay of 136 days. It adds that not sharing Android kernel modifications is described as a violation of GPLv2, citing criticism from developer Francisco Franco. The passage concludes that goodwill is being lost and hopes HMD will comply sooner, referencing Xiaomi’s Mi A1 as an example.

Researchers report that 39 seafloor fossils off the coast of Newfoundland, once considered decomposed pseudofossil material, were identified as a newly named spongelike animal from about 560 million years ago. Paleontologist Christopher McKean and colleagues determined the creature likely acted as a filter feeder, based on fingerlike tubes and pores, and it could grow up to nearly 53 centimeters. The animal’s name is linked to punk rocker John Lydon (Johnny Rotten) due to its spiky appearance and also to a spiky wild fruit, jiggamint, known to the Beothuk people. The findings suggest the organism resembles modern sponges and may be an ancestor of some modern sponge species.

A University of Queensland study found that Black Mamba and other mamba species use a dual neurological attack with their venom: first causing limp paralysis through postsynaptic neurotoxicity, then causing painful spastic paralysis through presynaptic toxicity after antivenom treatment begins. The findings explain why some patients initially improve after antivenom and later develop uncontrolled spasms, and they show that venom complexity varies by mamba species and geographic location, potentially reducing antivenom effectiveness across regions. The study suggests specialized antivenoms could be developed to improve efficacy, and notes mamba bites are a significant threat in sub-Saharan Africa.

The passage describes a systematic review focused on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback, examining both efficacy and challenges. It states that AI can improve efficiency, consistency, scalability, and provide personalized or real-time feedback, including support for automated grading and adaptive assessment. The review also highlights concerns such as data privacy, algorithmic transparency, potential bias, and debates about validity and fairness, especially for subjective skills. It outlines review objectives, the use of the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and methods including database searches, inclusion/exclusion criteria, quality assessment, and PRISMA 2020 reporting. Results from 20 studies (2010–2023) are summarized by key themes including efficiency, assessment design, student perceptions, challenges, and ethical considerations. The conclusion emphasizes AI’s transformative potential while noting the need to mitigate bias, address ethical issues, align with pedagogy, and support further research and professional development.

The speaker says the cheering they received was meant to encourage them to go into Detroit ready, with confidence that others support them. They state they are not a defensive specialist, and emphasize that there is both something to gain and something to lose, aiming to gain ground. They say they know the players on the ice and their own team, and that once play begins they will take a realistic approach by reacting to opponents’ tendencies when the puck is involved, while acknowledging players have different abilities such as shooting and passing.

The passage describes a player feeling good about getting involved in an intense physical battle, making a defensive play by catching and deflecting a puck, and then trying to pass it back to a teammate. The player says their focus is on playing good hockey to help the team win in any way, including contributing defensively. They also mention having family present for the Stanley Cup Finals and describe Cory as a player who moves the puck well, finds teammates for plays, and is “underrated,” contributing points and good plays. The team is focused on the next game at home.

The passage lists Birmingham City’s top ten away days from the last ten years, highlighting key matches and outcomes. It includes wins such as Bristol City 1–0 (07/05/17), Wolves 2–1 (24/02/17), Fulham 5–2 (07/11/15), Reading 2–1 (03/05/09), Derby 3–0 (16/01/16), Club Brugge 2–1 (20/10/11), Tottenham 3–2 (02/12/07), Crystal Palace 4–0 (29/03/13), Shamrock Rovers 4–0 (08/07/13), and a dramatic 2–2 draw at Bolton (03/04/14). Each entry describes notable moments involving players, supporters, and circumstances like relegation survival, promotions, and late goals.

Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher, and Randy Moss were elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame on their first try, while Terrell Owens was elected on his third attempt. Brian Dawkins was also voted in as part of an eight-person class, which included contributor Bobby Beathard and senior nominees Jerry Kramer and Robert Brazile. The passage notes that Lewis and Urlacher helped define the middle linebacker role, that Lewis won two AP Defensive Player of the Year awards and a Super Bowl MVP, and that Urlacher won a Defensive Player of the Year award. It also says Moss and Owens were dynamic receivers but were controversial at times, leading each to play for five teams during their careers.

The passage describes the Deepwater Horizon disaster of April 20, 2010, including the rig’s ownership and staffing, the disabling of gas alarms, the explosions and casualties, the 36-hour burn and sinking, and the scale of the spill and its estimates. It outlines BP’s corporate history and organizational strategy, including cost cutting, changes in decision-making, and reported concerns about safety communication and process safety following earlier disasters in Texas City (2005) and Prudhoe Bay (2006). It then details the Macondo well project: the well’s location and drilling context, BP’s acquisition and role, the role of Transocean and other contractors, the exploratory “temporary abandonment” plan, known maintenance/software issues on the rig, and key decisions related to well casing design, centralizers, mud circulation, and not performing a cement bond log. The passage concludes by noting ongoing investigations and public debates about which decisions may have contributed to the blowout, along with broader environmental, economic, and industry impacts, including a U.S. moratorium on deepwater drilling and the creation of BP’s Gulf Coast Claims Facility.

A passage describes an Acer laptop deal from Best Buy’s “Techtober” sales event, discounted by $450 to $800. The laptop is said to include 16 GB RAM, 1 terabyte of storage, a 16-inch OLED display with 2,880 x 1,800 resolution and a 120-Hz refresh rate, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V CPU. WIRED testing is cited as achieving 13 hours of YouTube playback. The article compares the Acer Swift 16 AI as chunkier at 0.79 inches to the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition at $900 and 0.55 inches, noting similar specs including the CPU and OLED display. The Techtober event runs through October 12, aligned with “Big Deal Days,” with additional laptop deals expected during Prime Day.

Edwin F. Uhl reports that the Department regrets Mr. Allen’s action in asking the U.S. consul-general at Shanghai to have a murderer of Kim Ok-kiun given up to Korean justice; Uhl disapproves because the consul-general’s protection and jurisdiction cover only U.S. citizens. John M. B. Sill reports from the palace that government forces from Chon-ju were defeated by rebels at Yung-won, and that rebels then captured Chon-ju after a detour. Sill also discusses Admiral Skerrett’s inability to send a ship to Chemulpo at present, while Sill warns the rebellion may soon pose danger to the Americans in Seoul and notes that other countries’ vessels have been sent to Chemulpo. Denby confirms a telegram that China is sending troops and ordering three men-of-war to Chemulpo in response to an appeal from the King of Korea, with assurances to Japan and Russia that the troops will be withdrawn after hostilities cease.

The lecture discusses limited attention and how it affects economic decision-making. It reviews prior work on preferences and then focuses on three issues: evidence of attention limitations, a paper on inattention to taxes (Chetty et al.), and a theory of “learning by noticing” that explains why people may fail to attend to important information.

The lecture describes multiple psychology experiments showing change blindness and limited attention, including movie perception tests, bank-teller variations, the “gorilla test,” and dichotic listening experiments that illustrate people’s difficulty remembering unattended information. It then argues attention is limited and influenced by factors such as environmental conditions, distractions, worries, sleep, and temptations.

The lecture presents evidence from markets where people appear inattentive even with high stakes. It describes an event involving EntreMed stock and later reporting that failed replication should not have surprised attentive traders, yet stock prices reacted. It also mentions confusion in the “Zoom” stock case due to similar tickers.

To measure inattention, the lecture discusses making relevant information salient and observing behavioral changes. It introduces a simple model where consumers perceive a visible/salient component fully but only partially process an “opaque” component, with inattention parameter θ. It applies this framework to sales taxes, since shoppers may know sales tax rates but still fail to account for them when choosing items before the register.

Chetty et al.’s experimental approach in stores involves making the after-tax price highly salient using price tags and using a triple-difference design across treated and control categories and stores. Results show that making sales taxes salient reduces demand, and the estimated inattention parameter suggests consumers react to sales-tax changes much less than to other price changes. Additional non-experimental evidence from beer and related taxes compares how consumers respond to excise taxes (more salient) versus sales taxes (more opaque), concluding that consumers largely do not pay attention to sales taxes.

The lecture then explains why governments may want some taxes to be salient, especially for “externality” or “internality” reasons, so that consumers change behavior rather than just raising revenue. Finally, it addresses how inattention can cause large welfare losses when learning fails. Using examples like headaches and historic medical beliefs, it argues that if people do not have the right model of relevance, they may never encode the information needed to update their behavior, leading to persistent mislearning. An example from seaweed farming in Indonesia illustrates learning failures: farmers often did not attend to pod size even when experiments varied it, but providing summarized information about pod size and optimal combinations led to larger behavior changes.

The passage contains multiple news items dated January 19, 2001, about the California energy crisis and related business developments. It describes how California’s two largest utilities were unable to cover power costs under a 1996 deregulation law, accumulating more than $11.5 billion in power-related debt, while natural gas prices rose sharply and out-of-state suppliers worried about payment. It lists key companies, financiers, bond insurers, rating agencies, and state and federal agencies involved, including defaults by PG&E and Southern California Edison and steps such as state emergency spending and federal orders for power or natural-gas suppliers to continue selling into California. Additional items include coverage of a Reuters analysis on how deregulation changed utilities’ investment risk profile, a PR Newswire release about EOTT Energy Partners distributing cash, a Dow Jones report on expanding bandwidth price routes, Reuters coverage of an incoming Bush adviser opposing caps on Western power prices, a Pennsylvania PUC statement criticizing GPU for comparing conditions to California, and announcements that Enron subsidiary Enron Energy Services signed a 10-year energy management agreement worth over $2 billion with Owens-Illinois.

President Hoover addresses Americans at his inauguration, urging candor and decisive action to face difficult material conditions, including reduced ability to pay, frozen exchange, industrial hardship, and widespread unemployment. He says the crisis does not come from lack of resources but from failures of those managing exchange, including incompetence and unscrupulous practices. He argues that recovery requires restoring social values beyond monetary profit, putting people to work, stimulating needed projects, addressing population overconcentration through national redistribution, supporting agriculture, preventing foreclosures, reducing government costs, and unifying relief efforts. He calls for strict supervision of banking and credits, adequate but sound currency, and prompt action rather than mere discussion. He prioritizes restoring a sound national economy before international trade readjustment and advocates a “good neighbor” policy. He outlines possible constitutional and executive measures if Congress does not act and concludes by reaffirming national unity, faith in democracy, and asking for God’s blessing.

@ThingsExpo was named the Top 5 Most Influential Internet of Things brand by Onalytica in “The Internet of Things Landscape 2015: Top 100 Individuals and Brands,” based on Twitter conversation analysis of the #IoT debate from 56,224 users using a PageRank-based methodology. The passage also includes multiple other @ThingsExpo-related posts and sessions covering topics such as IoT data and web/cloud platforms, WebRTC identity management, IoT data back-end platforms, blockchain, data monetization, and event information for ThingsExpo in New York (June 6–8, 2017).

The passage describes a trading strategy that uses both MACD (Moving Average Convergence/Divergence) and RSI (Relative Strength Index) to analyze market momentum, trend direction, and potential future movement. It explains that MACD is a momentum oscillator based on the difference between a 12-period and 26-period EMA and is plotted with a signal line (a 9-period EMA of MACD values), oscillating around a zero line. RSI is a momentum oscillator developed by J. Welles Wilder that oscillates between 0 and 100, traditionally marking overbought above 70 and oversold below 30, with additional interpretations including divergences and failure swings.  

The passage outlines ways to combine the indicators, such as using MACD for trend direction and RSI for identifying swings, confirming one with the other, or using MACD momentum with RSI-based mean-reversion trades. It also notes that the combination can be good but requires clear rules and backtesting, since performance depends on the scenario, parameters, and markets. A specific example strategy described in the passage uses MACD and RSI along with a third mean-reversion filter, reporting 235 trades, an average gain per trade of 0.88% (including commission and slippage), and a 73% win rate on SMH from 2001 until today.

President Donald Trump has made major policy reversals, including a recent change regarding a U.S. Treasury report that did not name China as a currency manipulator despite his campaign promises. An analyst suggested he may backtrack on the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), a trade deal Trump withdrew from in January, saying that if Trump can allow China to avoid accusations, he might reconsider reversing himself for Japan. Japan is expected to benefit from TPP, especially its auto sector, and has decided to pursue revival with the remaining 10 participating nations, though doubts remain about its impact without the U.S. The analyst warned Trump could still change his mind because the treaty text remains valid until February 2018, adding that other members could make concessions to bring the U.S. back.

The Indian equity market consolidated as the NSE Nifty50 ended up 29.65 points (0.28%). After a quiet opening and some late-morning correction, short covering lifted the market, largely driven by rollover. Wednesday is the penultimate session of the current derivatives expiry, and a tepid start is expected as rollovers dominate; the market is expected to resist the 10,650 zone, with 10,650 and 10,695 as key resistance and 10,585 and 10,510 as supports. Technical indicators cited include a bullish RSI at 65.4201, bullish daily MACD above its signal line, and no significant candle formations; however, no clear breakout from the broad range is indicated until a convincing move past 10,650. The passage advises caution due to India VIX dropping and the Nifty Put to Call Ratio staying elevated, which may cap upside gains and increase vulnerability to profit taking. It also notes sector and stock-specific performances and recommends protecting profits while maintaining a cautious view.

The passage discusses the flexbone offense, a run-heavy system evolved from the wishbone and known for option plays and misdirection. It describes how the flexbone differs from the original wishbone by moving two extra running backs (“A backs”) closer to the line to add a pass threat, and notes it is sometimes called the triple option. It outlines personnel needs for quarterback, fullback (B back), slotbacks (A backs), wide receivers, and the offensive line, and lists strengths such as uniqueness that can confuse defenses, ball control and long time of possession, and wearing down opponents. Weaknesses include a lack of high-volume passing, difficulty moving quickly late in games, the need for substantial practice time, and struggles in bad weather. It then provides examples of common formations (Double Slot, Trips, Receivers Over) and run plays (Triple Option, Midline Option, Rocket Toss) and pass plays (Play Action Wheel Route, Toss Boot, 4 Verts). The passage also mentions teams and programs that have used the flexbone, including Navy, Army, Air Force, Paul Johnson’s coaching stops, Harding University, and its continued presence in high school football.

Mississippi State (8-0) will face Cincinnati (7-2) at 6 p.m. Tuesday on ESPN2 in Newport, Kentucky, at BB&T Arena due to renovations at Cincinnati’s Fifth Third Arena. Cincinnati recently lost 66-60 to No. 5 Florida and is No. 25 in the AP poll. The article highlights three factors: Mississippi State’s potential to capitalize on Cincinnati’s turnover issues (Cincinnati had 21 turnovers vs. Florida and at least 18 in four games), the impact of rebounding as Cincinnati averages 13.2 offensive rebounds per game, and how depth could matter late, noting Mississippi State expects a deeper rotation and that guard Eli Wright is expected to be available after a two-game suspension.

In Germany, the Protestant church is marking 500 years since Martin Luther’s Reformation and is experimenting with Twitter to reach fewer churchgoers who do not have time for in-person worship. In Magdeburg, parishioners at St. Augustine use smartphones during evening prayers, tweeting about the liturgy while a live, hashtagged feed appears on a screen. Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann says the social media approach helps the Protestant church retain or gain followers by letting Christians communicate with each other. The passage compares this to Luther’s use of the new printing press and pamphlets that spread quickly and were hard for the Catholic Church to censor. In Magdeburg, some posts are encouraging and others share private prayers, while some participants find the experience too hectic or leave early; an 86-year-old without a smartphone says she prefers traditional services and congregational singing.

The passage describes the “Larry Swedroe Portfolio (30/70, small-cap value),” presented in Larry Swedroe’s book “Reducing the Risk of Black Swans.” The portfolio is described as evidence-based and diversified, allocating 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds to aim for long-term growth while minimizing risk. It typically includes domestic and international small-cap value exposure plus emerging markets, using low-cost index funds or ETFs, and follows a “set it and forget it” approach with periodic rebalancing (at least annually or when allocations deviate). Swedroe’s value investing approach emphasizes a bottom-up analysis of undervalued companies with strong fundamentals and avoiding overpaying, along with diversification and a long-term perspective while avoiding market timing. The passage also includes a backtest using VIOV as a proxy for US small-cap value (starting in 2012 due to data limits), reporting an annual return of 3.71% and noting that the strategy may trail stocks over the long term due to its large bond allocation and lower returns compared to historical expectations.

Marty got a quick chance by turning and trying to score, and Jeff Carter described scoring what he said was his first playoff overtime goal, calling it a big moment that gives the team a two-game lead. Drew Doughty said he skated with the puck, used a defenseman as a screen, and his shot went in off Marty’s quick glove. Carter and Doughty discussed playoff hockey as about putting the puck on net, resetting and refocusing for the next games in Los Angeles, and taking the first two at home. They said the series is essentially starting over with home-ice advantage, that they expect the opponent to come out hard in Los Angeles, and that they need to play their best hockey to keep momentum.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture features and performance across deep learning, HPC, and system scalability. It outlines recommended precision modes (default TF32, mixed FP16/BF16), A100’s acceleration of FP64 for HPC via Tensor Core double-precision matrix multiply, and cuSOLVER’s TCAIRS mixed-precision iterative refinement results showing TF32 as fastest and most robust in provided tests. It also explains A100’s Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern and Sparse MMA instructions that skip zeros to double math throughput, plus performance benefits from hardware and software features such as combined L1/shared memory, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, larger HBM2 and L2 cache, ECC protection, and L2 compute data compression. For multi-user and multi-tenant use, it details MIG partitioning into up to seven GPU instances with isolated memory paths, QoS, fault isolation, and support for compute instances and Volta-style MPS, alongside third-generation NVLink/NVSwitch and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV. It further summarizes CUDA 11 capabilities including task graphs, async copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and cooperative groups, and concludes with DGX A100 system scaling and an appendix on sparse neural network pruning and structured sparsity benefits.

Warren Buffett said in 2011 that buying Berkshire shares at prices below their intrinsic worth is a reliable way to benefit continuing shareholders. Berkshire announced in 2011 a repurchase limit of up to 110% of book value, but only $67 million was repurchased; the limit was later raised to 120%, enabling $1.2 billion of repurchases in 2012, for total 2012 purchases of about $1.3 billion. There were no purchases from 2013–2016, though the 120% threshold was nearly reached in 2013, 2014, and 2016. The passage argues that the 120% limit may now be more conservative because the gap between Berkshire’s intrinsic and book value has widened, and that increasing the limit slightly could allow substantial additional repurchases. It concludes that repurchases should be strongly considered if the price/book ratio returns to the low-mid 120% range.

European shares were set for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016 as rising bond yields and a stronger euro weighed on the STOXX 600, which was down about 1.7-1.8% for the week and aimed to extend a five-day losing streak. Deutsche Bank was a key drag after reporting a bigger-than-expected 2017 net loss and dropping about 5%, with Spanish banks Caixabank and Sabadell also falling after results. The DAX reversed sharply earlier in the year and was down more than 5% in eight sessions, pressured by the euro’s rise and rising bond yields affecting defensive sectors. Coverage also highlighted the “Bull & Bear” sell signal from Bank of America Merrill-Lynch and investor focus on upcoming U.S. payrolls data, alongside multiple European company earnings releases and related market reactions.

Danny Langston appeals a Florida appellate decision reversing a final summary judgment for The Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. Langston was injured in a Florida automobile accident as a passenger in a vehicle owned by George Johnson, Jr. and operated by Fred Johnson. Langston sued, alleging Fred Johnson’s negligent operation caused the collision and that Fred Johnson had George Johnson’s permission and consent.

Personal Service sought summary judgment, arguing its surety bond covered only George Johnson’s personal acts and not Fred Johnson’s operation. The appellate court held that under Florida tort law the vehicle owner can be personally liable for injuries caused by a person to whom the owner entrusts the vehicle. The court then addressed whether Personal Service is contractually liable to extend George Johnson’s liability to the surety under Ohio law governing the bond. The bond referenced Ohio’s Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act and included language limiting surety liability, but the court concluded Langston could qualify as a “holder of a final judgment” for damages resulting from ownership, maintenance, or use of the vehicle. The court found a cited Ohio case distinguishable because the accident here occurred in Florida, and it rejected appellees’ reliance on that distinction. It also noted another Ohio case about discharge after payment did not address contractual liability beyond the bond amount.

The court reversed the summary judgment and remanded for further proceedings.

The paper examines arts education and the competencies of pre-service primary teachers in an Australian university teacher education programme. It focuses on a global problem in initial teacher education—limited arts curriculum time—which leaves pre-service teachers unprepared to teach arts. Using a qualitative methodology grounded in Stephen J. Ball’s education policy sociology and critical discourse analysis, the study examines how the university addressed this gap by developing an arts curriculum specialisation called “Arts Specialism.”  

The paper reviews literature on policy and factors shaping primary arts teacher education, highlighting persistent issues such as insufficient curriculum time, limited preparation in arts pedagogy, and challenges aligning policy intentions with implementation. It describes how the Arts Specialism was developed through stakeholder input, including policymakers and arts education organisations, and how its curriculum text and course structure were created and implemented. The Arts Specialism consists of four courses plus an elective, building on a foundation arts education course and covering the five arts subjects (dance, drama, media arts, music, visual arts).  

Findings indicate that the specialisation, introduced in 2019 and implemented alongside COVID-19-related delivery changes, aimed to provide generalist teachers with expert content and pedagogical knowledge through school-based and practice-focused experiences. The paper concludes that, despite challenges such as limited curriculum time and broader pressures on teacher education, integrating an arts specialism offers opportunities to bridge policy and practice, with potential expansion to more institutions and further research on graduates’ journeys and school-based implementation.

Tales of children raised in the wild by animals are described as long-standing and often apocryphal or hoaxes, but some accounts persist. The passage recounts Jean de Liège, mentioned by Sir Kenelm Digby in 1644: Jean allegedly lived hidden in the woods in Belgium for about sixteen years during wartime, became highly sensitive to smells, was found around age twenty-one with hair covering his body and unable to speak, and later learned to talk. The hair claim is described as unlikely and potentially explained by hypertrichosis. It also notes Nicholas Tulp’s 1672 description of an Irish “sheep-boy” said to have been raised among wild sheep. Lastly, it describes a U.S. “Wolf Girl” near Devil’s River in early nineteenth-century legend, whose mother died and whose father was killed, who was allegedly found after a hunt by a ranch in which she escaped when wolves gathered, and who later was reportedly seen again before vanishing for good. The passage ends by suggesting people should keep an open mind and that such cases may still exist.

The passage discusses tradeoffs between iPhone and Android smartphones, stating that iOS security is generally stronger due to Apple’s closed-ended platform. It claims iOS 10.3.1 includes features such as data encryption (password, PIN, thumbprint), prompts to enable two-factor authentication, automatic data erasure after ten failed login attempts, and secure backups on iCloud. It rejects the idea that iPhones are immune to malware, but says iOS has built-in anti-malware layers and benefits from constant updates and an exclusive app store. It also describes “Find My Phone” for locating, locking, or erasing a stolen device via iCloud, and a permissions confirmation process for apps. The passage compares publicly disclosed vulnerabilities in 2015 (iOS: 375; Android: 130) and argues that Android’s fragmentation and patching difficulty reduce security, while Apple maintains hardware and software exclusivity.

A free five-week self-management course for people living with chronic pain is set to start in Montrose in May. Delivered by Pain Association Scotland for the Angus Health and Social Care Partnership, it is for anyone with chronic pain regardless of cause or stage. Participants are invited to an initial two-and-a-half hour session, followed by four sessions held once a week, with weekly discussion topics including understanding pain, stress management, pacing, flare-ups, relaxation, and medication. The course is designed for relaxed, interactive participation and is intended to improve understanding of pain and provide skills to self-manage health. The Primary Care Team will take bookings by phone or email, and eligibility includes being aged 18 or over and living in Angus.

The passage describes mechanisms for non-maskable interrupts and #HV guest-hypervisor communication in SEV-ES. For NMI injection, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, and it uses a guest “NMI Complete” message to determine when another NMI can be injected; intercepting #DB gives the guest flexibility to send “NMI Complete” only when it can safely handle another NMI. An example guest OS flow sets a per-CPU variable before the NMI IRET, uses TF to trigger an appropriate #VC/#DB intercept, verifies the NMI scenario in the #VC handler, clears the per-CPU variable, and issues “NMI Complete” via VMGEXIT.

It then states that SMM is not supported in this specification version, and nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. For #HV doorbells, the document defines a shared “doorbell page” with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, requirements for host mapping and guest access (C=0), and bit definitions for non-maskable events. The hypervisor should present interrupts by writing PendingEvent.Vector, manage NoEoiRequired to indicate whether an explicit EOI is needed, and handle overwriting pending vectors and controlling non-maskable event delivery via PendingEvent.NoFurtherSignal. The guest must acknowledge #HV by atomically exchanging PendingEvent to retrieve and clear the pending vector, validate observed vectors, and handle EOI by atomically exchanging NoEoiRequired or performing an APIC EOI write via VMGEXIT when required.

U.S. homebuilders’ sentiment has dipped slightly, with the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo index falling to 68 in April from 71 in March. Readings above 50 mean more builders see sales conditions as good. The April decline was below analyst expectations, and related measures of builders’ views, including sales conditions, prospective-buyer traffic, and outlook for the next six months, also edged lower. Despite this, sales of new U.S. homes have been robust this year, with February sales rising to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 592,000, nearly 13% higher than a year earlier. Mortgage rates have been edging down recently, and the average 30-year fixed rate fell to 4.08% last week. The survey this month included 307 respondents.

The passage explains that last-shot situations are complex and depend on court location and time remaining, and that teams should be prepared, keep poise, and give the ball to their best player while reading the defense. It emphasizes practicing last-shot scenarios with a game clock, maintaining physical conditioning, and keeping plays simple to reduce breakdown risk; it also notes that many games are won on putbacks. It provides a “why hold” rationale, describing potential score swings tied to last shot of a period plus first possessions of the next period, and gives a basic timing rule: automatically hold for the last shot with under 30 seconds remaining when leading or trailing by less than eight points. It outlines fundamentals (e.g., long passes like skip and baseball/semi-hook passes, half-court shot practice, tipping and redirecting passes, and practicing intentional free-throw misses) and lists last-shot strategies such as saving timeouts, communicating timeout situations, taking a timeout with 1–3 seconds remaining, using inbound-to-half-court when under four seconds, using quick counter-break opportunities after opponent scores, and practicing from both right and left sides. The passage also includes guidelines for different last-shot situations by time window and scenario, covering out-of-bounds plays, rebounds, opponent free throws, and situations involving intentional missed free throws and jump balls.

John Bishop, a Canadian Korean War veteran, says Canada may not be able to play a similarly pivotal role in the Korean Peninsula again as tensions rise. Marius Grinius, a former Canadian ambassador to both North and South Korea, argues Canada has “run hot and cold” on security commitments and that the prior Conservative government’s “controlled engagement” policy cut off diplomatic ties. He also cites North Korea’s recent nuclear and missile tests and says Canada should focus on long-term stability and security. Korean War veteran Doug Finney and Tina Park, co-founder of the Canadian Centre for the Responsibility to Protect, argue Canada must act due to humanitarian conditions in North Korea and Canada’s responsibility to protect obligations.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer behavior for writing, erasing, and command extensions. It explains that block writes use CRC parity (1 or 4 bits) per received data block; write commands are rejected on block length or address errors, and CRC failures cause discarded data. It outlines requirements for block write sizing, handling of partial-block and misalignment errors, aborting writes to write-protected areas, and CRC protection for CSD-related data, as well as write busy behavior and host polling via CMD13. It then covers multiple-block write performance features (ACMD23 pre-erasing), interleaving multiple cards, and erase operations including ERASE_WR_BLK_START/END with CMD38 for DISCARD (CMD38 with 00000001h) and FULE (CMD38 with 00000002h), including support conditions, sequencing errors, write-protected sector handling, and busy signaling. The passage also covers mechanical and protection-related write protection methods, and the CMD42-based password locking and Card Ownership Protection (COP) mechanisms, including state behavior, command acceptance for locked cards, and FORCE ERASE/FEP Force ERASE rules. Finally, it describes CMD55 (APP_CMD) for application-specific command selection, CMD56 as a placeholder, and CMD6 switch function behavior (modes, busy status, status data structure, function groups), plus related high-speed mode, command system command interpretation, CMD8 initialization behavior, capacity-type differences (SDSC vs SDHC/SDXC), CRC usage for commands and data, and read/write/erase timeout conditions.

October 6 will feature a supermoon, when the full moon appears about 30% brighter and up to 14% larger than a typical full moon. International Observe the Moon Night is on October 4. Between October 6 and 10, the Draconid meteor shower may be visible; it originates from debris trailing comet 21P Giacobini-Zinner and can produce up to 10 meteors per hour, peaking around October 8. Later, the Orionid meteor shower peaks on October 21 (full duration Sept. 26–Nov. 22), producing about 20 meteors per hour as Earth passes through debris from Halley’s Comet. The best viewing for Orionids is after midnight until around 2 a.m., when the sky is dark due to the October new moon.

The lecture discusses corrections to a homework typo and emphasizes that course staff aim to resolve issues quickly so assignments support learning. It reviews linear algebra concepts leading to eigenvalue decomposition, including how reordering equations is important for Gaussian elimination and how permutation matrices swap rows or columns. It explains that eigenvectors are directions that are transformed by a matrix only by stretching (by an eigenvalue), and introduces finding eigenvalues via the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A-\lambda I)=0\). The lecture covers properties of eigenvalues (including multiplicities, complex conjugate pairs, and relations to determinant and trace), methods to find eigenvectors using null spaces and Gaussian elimination, and interpretations using examples like diffusion/Plinko and chemical reaction rate matrices. It then explains eigendecomposition: when a complete set of eigenvectors exists, \(A\) can be diagonalized as \(A=W\lambda W^{-1}\), simplifying solving systems and decoupling linear ODEs. The discussion notes computational approaches (e.g., Lanczos) and when diagonalization is not possible, mentioning Jordan form, Schur decomposition, and that singular value decomposition will be covered next.

The passage lists numerous records Taylor Swift has broken in her career, including Spotify streaming milestones for albums and songs (notably “The Life of a Showgirl” and “The Fate of Ophelia”), Grammy achievements (youngest Album of the Year winner for “Fearless,” first woman to win the award twice and three times, and the first artist to win it four times with “Midnights”), and multiple Billboard chart accomplishments such as having all top 10 entries on the Hot 100 in a single week. It also cites her American Music Awards total of 40 wins, her Billboard US Digital Song Sales No. 1 record (29 hits), and her video and tour achievements, including the Eras Tour grossing $2 billion.

The passage describes exponential moving averages (EMAs) as moving-average indicators that give greater weight to recent data, making them follow price more closely than simple moving averages (SMAs) and treating them as lagging indicators. It summarizes four EMA-based trading backtests on the S&P 500 (using SPY), with results presented for different EMA periods. The takeaways are that mean-reversion strategies work better with short EMA periods (buy on closes crossing below and sell on closes crossing above), while trend-following strategies work better with longer EMA periods (buy on closes crossing above and sell on closes crossing below), with profitability increasing as the number of days increases. It also notes a fourth set of strategies where entries follow the crossover rules but exits occur after N days. The passage includes an EMA formula and discusses practical use, drawbacks such as potential false signals from being too responsive, and the idea that EMAs are often best used alongside other indicators.

The passage describes a systematic literature review of papers from 2000 to 2017 in selected Information Systems journals, using combinations of the terms “Digital business strategy,” “Digital transformation,” and “Business digitalization.” Following Bandara’s guidelines, the authors selected articles through two-stage relevance checks, resulting in a final set of 28 articles, which were coded using Wolifswinkel’s guidelines through open coding, axial coding, and comparative/selective coding to identify underlying dimensions. The review found publication activity increasing from 2009 and considerably in 2016, with research focused on several industries and more on US and European countries than on Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa. The authors extracted 12 dimensions of digital transformation, 6 dimensions of digital business strategy, and 10 dimensions of organizational capabilities, and proposed overlaps and inter-relationships among the three concepts, presenting a conceptual framework in Figures 5 and 6. The conclusion states that the study explains how organizational capabilities and digital business strategy dimensions relate to and drive digital transformation, and it is intended to guide CEOs/CIOs and IS researchers.

The editors of the Foreign Relations series have access to retired Department of State records, including central files, decentralized “lot files,” Executive Secretariat files, and overseas diplomatic posts, and central files from 1981–1989 will be transferred to the National Archives for declassified access. Decentralized office files deemed permanently preserved will also be transferred after declassification and processing. Research involves special access to restricted documents at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies; although the volume’s printed material is declassified, some selections are extracted from still-classified documents and may not be fully available at publication. The editorial method presents documents chronologically by Washington DC time, places conversation memoranda by conversation date, reproduces original documents as closely as possible with described marginalia, transcribes and prints under Office style guidelines, supplies editor headings, retains original spelling and punctuation except for silent correction of obvious typographical errors, and uses bracketed insertions to show corrected, added, omitted, or still-classified text.

The passage discusses a multi-period resource allocation problem under stochastic, nonnegative demands, aiming to maximize total revenue subject to a total resource constraint. It introduces a static open-loop formulation solved via a convex program using bisection on a dual variable, but notes this static solution ignores temporal demand correlations and cannot adapt as demands are realized sequentially. To address this, the authors propose a sequential adaptive “shrinking horizon” policy, similar to model predictive control, that re-solves the optimization at each time for the remaining horizon and updates the joint distribution of future demands by conditioning on observed history. The paper formulates the static and sequential problems, discusses special behavior under independent demands (where the sequential solution matches the static one), and evaluates the methods through simulations using jointly log-normal (and potentially mixture) demand models. Results on synthetic data show the sequential policy achieves higher revenue and better performance than the static policy for non-independent demands, and are compared against an oracle allocation upper bound and a roll-forward baseline. Future work is noted on closed-loop learning and studying the importance of demand distribution modeling.

YouTube reported Monday that April the giraffe’s livestream is officially the second-most-watched live channel in company history, behind Riot Games’ League of Legends esports channel. Cameras began broadcasting from her pen at Animal Adventure Park in New York on Feb. 10, and viewership peaked when she delivered her male calf on Saturday.
