The later section outlines event-driven FaaS/serverless distinctions, benefits (simpler code-to-running, automatic scaling/restarts), challenges (decoupling, observability), and limitations (need for in-memory data, background processing fit, and per-request cost model), concluding with the decorator pattern as an ideal use case for FaaS request/response transformations and a hands-on example of request defaulting via Kubeless.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while off work to observe Rosh Hashanah. The firing followed conservatives’ publication of past blog posts attributed to Rosenzweig that criticized President Donald Trump, including claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist,” which Rosenzweig allegedly wrote while an associate at Kobre & Kim. The Miami Herald reported that he is among dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump’s Justice Department. Rosenzweig handled economic crimes cases and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Department of Justice also fired three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who previously worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith said he was dismayed by dismissals of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law after his first public remarks since leaving the DOJ.

Stock indexes fell Friday after giving up some of the week’s gains. The Toronto Stock Exchange’s S&P/TSX composite index dropped 81.78 points to 15,694.52 after 90 minutes, while the Canadian dollar rose to 79.70 cents US from Thursday’s 79.69. The TSX will be closed Monday Oct. 9 for Thanksgiving, while U.S. markets remain open. Wall Street was lower in the morning after Costco and energy shares declined and a U.S. jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls fell 33,000 in September, though average wages rose 0.5%. The Dow fell 35.02 points to 22,740.37, the S&P 500 fell to 2,544.53, and the Nasdaq dropped to 6,570.11. Costco shares hit their lowest level in nearly a month, and energy declined 0.9% as oil prices faced profit taking and oversupply worries. On the NYSE, decliners outnumbered advancers 1,990 to 793; on the Nasdaq, 1,612 issues fell and 1,070 advanced.

The passage discusses the decline of high street bank branches and the rise of mobile-only banking. It notes that 141 more branches were reported to shut in 2017 and describes branchless firms such as Atom Bank, Monzo, and Revolut that require smartphone apps. A Which? online survey of 9,076 members found that more than half of under-40s would be happy to open a mobile-only account, but the figure drops for those aged 40 and over. It outlines potential advantages, such as competitive savings rates, and drawbacks, including a reported smartphone app crash during a savings account launch and the lack of in-branch customer service. The passage also references earlier Which? research showing over 1,000 branch closures between January 2015 and January 2017 and includes commenter views expressing concerns about reduced human support and inconvenience for certain transactions.

The memorandum states that suitable U.S. negotiators for a peace conference may lack full knowledge of complex questions, so experts should be invited to prepare secret, condensed articles and related indexed materials for the representatives’ use. It proposes subject areas under History, Commerce, and International Law, along with additional topics such as disarmament, international guaranties, arbitration, and analysis of countries’ constitutions and political institutions. It outlines selecting qualified historians, political economists, and jurists to write pamphlets of 10,000 to 15,000 words, plus secretly printing these pamphlets and supporting appendices (documents, statistics, quotations). All division of subjects, writer selection, instructions, article review, and printing/indexing should be directed by one man with assistants. The passage also includes undated queries about U.S. roles in European boundaries and colonial redistribution, criteria for territorial settlement, and guarantees for colonial possessions, followed by a letter from Colonel E. M. House praising a memorandum provided to the President and expressing plans to discuss further with the Secretary of State.

A middle schooler from Tennessee, Keaton Jones, went viral after his mother posted a video in which he described bullying he has suffered at school. Celebrities including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo publicly expressed support for Keaton and opposed bullying.

In a New York Criminal Court trial in November 1974, defendants Antonio Vasquez and Hector Perez were charged with possession of burglar’s tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest. Testimony stated that on June 6, 1974, they attempted to take a bicycle by cutting its protective chain with bolt cutters, but they later abandoned the attempt after a discussion with a third person. The jury found them guilty of possession of burglar’s tools and not guilty of attempted petit larceny and resisting arrest. The court refused to instruct the jury that renunciation was a defense to possession of burglar’s tools, though it did instruct on renunciation for attempted petit larceny. Defendants moved to set aside the verdict, arguing that abandoning their intent to steal should also mean they abandoned intent related to the burglar’s tools. The court held that Penal Law § 40.10 does not authorize renunciation as a defense to possession of burglar’s tools, denied the motion, and suggested that if change is needed it is for the Legislature.

Insecticides India plans to invest Rs 200 crore over the next three years to expand its existing plants and set up new units in Gujarat and Rajasthan. The company expects 10–15% revenue growth this fiscal, based on normal monsoon rains and the launch of 7–8 new products. It is launching three insecticides and one fungicide for crops including cotton, paddy, pulses, and vegetables; the four products are based on combinations intended to provide synergistic effects. The expansion includes capacity additions at Dahej (Gujarat) and Chopanki (Rajasthan), along with two new synthesis facilities and an export-oriented unit, for which approvals have been sought. The investment will be funded through internal accruals, debt, and equity. The company reported a 5% increase in Q4 net profit to Rs 7.68 crore, with lower total income, and a 41% rise in full-year 2017–18 net profit to Rs 83.97 crore, with total income increasing to Rs 1,109.63 crore.

The passage describes the device’s multiSPI digital interface, including host-to-device data transfer modes, supported protocols, output configurations, and operational states (RESET, ACQ, CONV). It explains host connection topologies such as single-device operation and multiple-device daisy-chain topology, including timing and frame-length considerations. It outlines device programming concepts, including data transfer frames, command/register write behavior, output data word formation (including optional flags and conversion results), and supported read/write protocol options (legacy SPI variants with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous protocols). It also provides a summary of reset control options, ACQ/CONV transitions, and power-saving modes (NAP and power-down).

The Supreme Court said the CBI-led investigation into the larger conspiracy behind former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination does not appear to have made “much headway” and that the inquiry by the Multi Disciplinary Monitoring Agency could be “endless.” The court also arrayed the Centre as a party in a plea by convict A G Perarivalan seeking suspension of his sentence until the CBI concludes its probe into the conspiracy behind the belt bomb. The matter was fixed for hearing on January 24. The passage also notes details of Perarivalan’s plea, the involvement of the MDMA, and background on the May 21, 1991 assassination.

The passage discusses causal discovery in asynchronous event sequences and notes that existing methods are often computationally intractable in high dimensions and typically require multiple sequences. It introduces OSCAR, a one-shot multi-label causal auto-regressive discovery method that uses two Transformers as density estimators to infer, from a single observed sequence, the Markov boundary for each label. OSCAR uses conditional mutual information to test conditional independence and supports scalable, parallelized causal discovery across thousands of event types, producing interpretable causal indicators between events and labels. Experiments on a real-world vehicular dataset with 29,100 event types and 474 labels evaluate OSCAR against local structure learning baselines; traditional methods failed to compute Markov boundaries within a 3-day timeout, while OSCAR produced results within minutes with robustness at large scale.

The passage discusses South Carolina Republicans Trey Gowdy and Tim Scott, noting they often joke with each other—especially about Gowdy’s haircut—and have co-penned the inspirational book *Unified: How Our Unlikely Friendship Gives Us Hope for a Divided Country*, releasing April 3. It contrasts Gowdy’s earlier role in the Benghazi hearings, where critics said he focused on building a case against Hillary Clinton, with his later public positions. After announcing on Jan. 31, 2018 that he would not seek re-election and saying he hoped to return to law, Gowdy is described as increasingly supportive of Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation and critical of certain Trump actions. The passage also states Gowdy disagreed with GOP claims tied to Devin Nunes’ memo, said the dossier had nothing to do with specific events, co-wrote the memo, criticized firing Andrew McCabe as credibility-undermining, condemned firing Mueller, and urged Trump to “act like it” when innocent while warning against stopping Mueller.

The speaker says they are disappointed about losing but believe they worked hard and maintain a positive, optimistic attitude. They acknowledge mistakes in the last game that allowed the other team to come back after two two-goal leads in the third period, and say they must learn from those errors. They emphasize sticking to their chosen game plan and systems, with the next game being the main focus. The speaker notes that having two two-goal leads is a positive, but losing the game is negative, and stresses that how they respond next game matters most. They also say they feel they can compete and win, but “beat themselves” last game.

The passage contains post-game and post-series comments about a hockey team’s performance in the Stanley Cup finals. The speakers discuss watching or playing for the chance to lift the Stanley Cup, disappointment at losing four straight games and being swept, and pride in the team’s progress despite missing breaks. They describe how the opposing team appeared to beat them in multiple areas, including early scoring chances and power-play success, and they suggest that experience and preparation helped the opponent. Several players are praised, including mentions of goaltending (Ozzie/Kolzig), Stevie as an MVP of the playoffs, and other leadership and consistency. The group reflects on learning from the loss, bouncing back next year, maintaining belief, and the emotional context of an accident referenced as part of their hockey experience.

The passage discusses solving large sparse linear systems \(ax=b\) with iterative methods instead of direct elimination, since such matrices may be too large for feasible time or storage. It explains the role of a preconditioner \(p\) chosen to be similar to \(a\) but simpler, forming an iteration based on \(p^{-1}a\). The lecture reviews iterative schemes and common preconditioners, including Jacobi (diagonal of \(a\)), Gauss-Seidel (lower triangular part), successive overrelaxation (SOR), and incomplete LU (ILU), where fill-in during factorization is controlled to keep the preconditioner sparse.

It derives an error update equation \(e_{k+1} = (I - p^{-1}a)e_k\) and states that convergence depends on the eigenvalues of the iteration matrix, especially the spectral radius. Using a one-dimensional model matrix, it analyzes Jacobi’s convergence via known eigenvalues and finds slow decay due to low-frequency components, leading to an estimate that reducing the error may require about \(n^2\) iterations. It then considers weighted Jacobi, showing that an appropriate weight can better handle high-frequency modes but still leaves low frequencies as a problem, motivating multigrid. Finally, it compares Gauss-Seidel to Jacobi, noting that Gauss-Seidel effectively squares Jacobi’s eigenvalues, improving convergence but still requiring on the order of \(n^2\) iterations, and concludes with a transition to multigrid.

The passage says a Trump administration amendment announced Friday would allow U.S. businesses to deny insurance coverage for women’s contraception by citing religious or moral objections, potentially unpicking a key Obamacare provision. Reproductive rights advocates criticized the change, while conservative Christian activists praised it. Cecile Richards of Planned Parenthood said it would target contraception coverage for 62 million women, though the government claimed only 120,000 women would lose coverage. California’s Democratic attorney general said he would fight to protect the mandate, and the passage notes Trump had criticized the birth control mandate during last year’s election campaign.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K Current Report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 28, 2020. The report states that Apple issued a press release on that date regarding its financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019, and that the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. It also lists securities registered under Section 12(b), including Apple’s common stock (AAPL) and various notes due 2022, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027, 2029, 2031, and 2042. The filing includes a signature by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The study aimed to examine teacher candidates’ views on a special education course delivered via distance education, including what problems they experience related to the course content and what solution suggestions could contribute to the field. Using phenomenology (qualitative research), interviews were conducted with 45 pre-service teachers at a private university in 2022–2023. Data were collected with a semi-structured interview form created by the researcher, with expert reviews for content validity and pilot adjustments.  

Findings showed that more than half of participants were satisfied with the distance education special education course, but many reported difficulties due to internet connection problems. Participants also emphasized the importance of course participation for success and stated that distance education was generally recommended; however, they noted that distance education was not as effective as face-to-face, especially because of issues affecting learning. Additional reported problems included technical/material deficiency, insufficient technical support, inadequate digital materials, and lack of devices or unstable internet access. Participants suggested improving the system, internet infrastructure, and providing free internet access and better technical/material support.

The passage argues that bearish market theses often sound more compelling and action-oriented, but historical data favors patient, “boring” strategies that can outperform. It references Ray Dalio’s framework for diagnosing market bubbles and notes that the author discussed this in a private investing community. The passage also includes promotional and disclosure content about Envision Research/Envision Early Retirement, a long position in certain tickers, and standard disclaimers, plus chart descriptions with specified time and value ranges.

The passage is a collection of dated news items and excerpts mentioning energy and business developments. It reports that Sierra Pacific Resources suspended its quarterly dividend due to high power costs from the Western U.S. energy crisis, while discussing its delayed plan to buy Enron’s Portland General Electric unit and associated debt and regulatory obstacles. Other items cover the U.K.’s issuance of seabed leases for offshore wind projects, changes in how companies handle layoffs amid internet rumor boards and Regulation FD, and a look at the growth and economics of solar and other renewables in California. Additional excerpts discuss tech stock trading ahead of earnings reports, Business Week commentary involving Enron leadership and U.S. defense nominations, and an Indian panel’s recommendations regarding Enron’s Dabhol power project and Maharashtra’s electricity board. The passage also includes coverage of DivX as a possible online video piracy standard, Enron restarting an MTBE plant, and a committee recommending renegotiation and restructuring of Enron’s power supply deal in Maharashtra.

The passage describes features of NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture. It covers native HDR display processing with added tone mapping using ITU-R BT.2100 to avoid color shift, an enhanced NVENC encoder supporting H.265 8K at 30 fps and reporting bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, and an updated NVDEC decoder supporting HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit streams and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. It also discusses improved encoding quality versus prior Pascal GPUs and software x264, making 4K streaming possible on typical CPUs, and addresses VR connectivity by using hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink. The passage further explains NVLink replacing earlier SLI bridge interfaces, enabling two-way SLI with higher bandwidth and new display topologies. It outlines Turing’s real-time ray tracing approach, including RT Cores, hybrid rendering with rasterization, denoising, and related technologies like DLSS/NGX, plus additional rendering and shading capabilities such as hybrid rendering, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering.

The passage defines a “Reversal Day” as a day when a stock or market index changes direction, either upward or downward, sometimes after an extended uptrend or downtrend and often with high trading volume. It describes two main types: a Bullish Reversal Day (after a prolonged downtrend, the day ends bullish and closes above the previous day’s high) and a Bearish Reversal Day (after a prolonged rally, the day ends bearish and closes below the previous day’s low). It lists factors that can cause stock reversals, including changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, and company-specific news, and notes that technical analysis and indicators can be used to identify reversal patterns. The passage provides guidance on spotting reversal days using trend direction, heavy volume, and technical indicators like moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger Bands, along with support/resistance breaks and divergences with RSI or MACD. It then mentions backtesting two reversal-day strategies on gold (GLD): a bullish reversal backtest and a bearish reversal backtest, stating that bullish results have merit while bearish results produced losses due to gold’s overnight drift, and that bearish average gains were lower than the bullish case.

Cocoa futures are standardized exchange-traded contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity of cocoa at a pre-agreed price on a future date. The contract unit is 10 metric tons and it trades on both ICE (physically deliverable) and CME Globex/NYMEX (financially settled). Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December, and trading terminates on the day before the last notice day (ten business days prior to the last business day of the delivery month). Trading hours are specified for ICE Futures US (including pre-open and post-close markets) and CME Globex (with a daily break Monday–Thursday). The minimum price fluctuation is $1.00 per metric ton ($10.00 per contract), with a tick size of $10.00 per tick per contract. Factors affecting cocoa prices are described as supply and demand influences, and cocoa has seasonality, tending to perform better in summer and poorly in spring and fall. Reported all-time high is $5,379.00 (July 1977) and the lowest since 1979 is $707.00 (December 2000). Biggest risks include adverse price movement due to leverage and liquidity risk. An ETF/ETN offering exposure is iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB), which tracks an index of cocoa futures with three expiration dates.

Health savings accounts (HSAs) are personal savings accounts that allow tax-free investing and tax-free withdrawals for certain medical expenses, such as insurance deductibles and copays. HSAs are currently available only to people with high-deductible health plans, and participation is relatively low: about 20 million of 176 million insured people, according to a 2015 report. The passage attributes low saving to both limited ability to contribute upfront and psychological stress and defense mechanisms that hinder financial decision-making. It also notes behavioral research suggesting that framing incentives to avoid loss can increase compliance. Proposed changes include making HSAs more like 401(k)s so people who do not want to participate must actively opt out. The passage adds that studies suggest HSA holders use less health care, but it is unclear whether health improves; one study found prescription drug costs declined while emergency room visits increased for lower-income families. It concludes that saving for health is difficult because medical prices vary and patients lack clear pricing, and that HSAs may only help those with enough cash to cover current expenses and some extra savings.

MLPs, measured by the Alerian MLP Index, fell slightly over the last four days of the year, while the equal-weight version was slightly higher; in both cases, MLPs outperformed the S&P 500. Oil and natural gas prices rose and finished the year with large gains. The AMZE total return was 22.5%, exceeding the adjusted market cap Alerian MLP index by more than 400 basis points, attributed in part to Enterprise Products Partners’ unusually weak performance versus the Alerian MLP Index. The sector’s December return of 4.4% continued streaks, ending two straight negative Decembers, and 2016 overall ended up 18.3%, beating the S&P 500. Global Partners LP led for a second straight week; top and bottom performers were SunCoke Energy Partners (top) and Ferrellgas Partners (biggest loser). General partners and midstream corporations underperformed MLPs, with Tallgrass Energy GP and NuStar GP Holdings the only positive returns that week. News included Plains GP Holdings filing to sell up to $500 million in common units and Shell Midstream Partners announcing Gulf of Mexico pipeline acquisitions.

The passage describes the S&P 500 Information Technology sector, noting it has the highest weighting in the S&P 500 (over a quarter of market cap) and has had strong growth over the last decade. It covers the sector’s scope, including companies developing or distributing technological items or services, and its major ETFs (VGT and XLK), with top stocks listed as Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Adobe. The article presents two mean-reversion-based technology sector trading strategies, including an XLK strategy, and reports backtest statistics such as number of trades, average gain, CAGR, win rate, max drawdown, time in the market, and profit factor. It also states that technology sector volatility and correlation with broader markets can limit diversification benefits, and that code and logic for strategies are available via subscription.

The passage describes burnout as a state of physical and emotional tiredness caused by long-term job-related stress, with three components: emotional weariness, depersonalization, and loss of sense of accomplishment. Burnout is described as a global public health issue expected to worsen with the ongoing COVID-19 crisis. The World Health Organization classified burnout as an “occupational phenomenon” in 2019. The passage provides background on workplace changes contributing to burnout and notes that burnout rates differ by geography and profession, including among prison officers (POs), who are described as an underserved and at-risk workforce.

The study focuses on burnout among prison officers in Ghana, specifically at Nsawam Medium Security Prison. It used a descriptive cross-sectional quantitative design with self-administered questionnaires adapted from validated tools (MBI-HSS, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist). Ethical approvals and consent procedures are described, along with inclusion criteria (general-duty prison officers present for at least six months) and exclusion criteria (annual leave at data collection). A proportionate stratified random sampling approach was used, and data collection occurred from February 5 to May 18, 2023. Of 266 recruited officers, 243 questionnaires were used for analysis.

Results report that emotional exhaustion was mostly high (42.0%), depersonalization was distributed across low (35.4%), moderate (32.1%), and high (32.5%), and most officers had low personal accomplishment (68.7%). Burnout prevalence was 9% based on defined threshold criteria. Irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and lack of training/development opportunities (47.7%) were among the most perceived causes. For work environment, more than half disagreed that a positive and supportive culture and emotional climate existed. Coping strategies most commonly included talking to colleagues (62.5%) and looking forward to off duty (60.1%), while alcohol use was least reported (29.2%). Associations described include significant links between emotional exhaustion and shift allocation, and depersonalization and officer rank, and burnout being significantly associated with sex and education in logistic regression. The conclusion emphasizes attention to irregular shifts, heavy workload, and regular training/development to reduce burnout, noting patterns in emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and coping.

The passage discusses debate over whether MDC-T leader Morgan Tsvangirai is helping the opposition or has become a liability. It says he previously united people around the MDC, helped the opposition case, and forced a run-off in the 2008 presidential polls by defeating Robert Mugabe. After losses in 2013 and a second party split, the passage says he became a “curse” to the opposition. It also states that a cancer attack is inhibiting him from discharging his duties as MDC-T and MDC Alliance leader, which concerns pro-democracy forces. The passage calls on Tsvangirai to allow leadership renewal by stepping aside for a new leader, while he plays a supporting role, arguing this could help the opposition win.

The SD Card Association releases an SD Simplified Specification/Addendum under conditions that it is a subset of the complete SD Specification/Addendum it owns. It is provided non-confidentially on an “AS-IS” basis with disclaimers, including no warranties and no responsibility for damages, patent infringements, or other rights issues. The release does not grant any implied licenses or create any obligation for the SD Card Association to disclose or distribute technical information.

The passage criticizes Stanford’s Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR) as lacking rigor, teaching students to write vague generalizations under broad course themes such as “The Rhetoric of Happiness” and “The Rhetoric of Success.” It argues that professors tell students to simply write with little serious instruction, that PWR does not provide consistent source analysis, and that grading functions more like box-checking than skill development. The passage also describes perceived political bias in PWR course offerings and events, and suggests Stanford should not create a PWR minor but instead improve existing classes or replace PWR with a more standardized, rigorous source-based course designed to teach academic writing. It concludes that PWR “cannot stand” and should change.

In honor of Fire Prevention Week, Montecito Fire Protection District engine companies will teach elementary school children in the Montecito community fire safety from Monday through Oct. 14. The program will cover how to respond to a fire using “Stop Drop and Roll” and “Crawl Low in Smoke” for preschool through second grade, and will use a “Fire Safety Trailer” for third and fourth grades to simulate home fire situations. Children will also learn to spot home fire hazards, the five most important things to say when dialing 9-1-1, and how to exit quickly and safely, and parents are encouraged to discuss and practice an emergency plan as a family. A note states that due to predicted inclement weather, Montecito Fire has canceled fire prevention activities for Oct. 3–6, with those school visits rescheduled to a later date.

The passage describes BMW M8-related details and comparisons, noting that a particular model’s headlights, brakes, and wheel design appear provisional or downgraded. It says BMW M has not revealed specifications, but the project is based on BMW’s CLAR modular platform from the 7 Series and features bodywork previewed by the 8 Series concept at the 2017 Villa d’Este event. It claims the car will use a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 debuting in the F90 M5 and will include standard all-wheel drive capable of sending power to the rear, positioning it as a “supercar fighter.” The passage also mentions the original 8 Series and M8 rumors, references possible competition with S-Class Coupe and Cabriolet and with a Porsche 911 rival, and concludes by comparing the original M8’s V12 legacy powering the McLaren F1.

Ottawa police allege a woman flagged a Good Samaritan near Innes Road and O’Toole Road, claimed her car was broken down and lacked a phone, and led him back to her car about a kilometre away. Police say the victim exited his vehicle to help, was confronted by an accomplice, and the woman demanded his wallet; he resisted and was attacked by the woman and man. A third man allegedly joined, helping steal the wallet. Police say the trio took an undisclosed amount of cash, fled, and the victim was taken to hospital for injuries. Police provided descriptions of the woman and first accomplice and said a dark-coloured older-model four-door sedan was used. Information is requested via Ottawa police or Crime Stoppers.

At a Code Conference panel featuring All Raise and Cowboy Ventures Partner Aileen Lee, shift7 CEO Megan Smith, and Stubhub President Sukhinder Singh Cassidy, they discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee said the label of being a “good guy” often drives opportunities, while questions about women and people of color focus differently on qualifications, and she argued the industry should systematically map processes to remove biases. She cited repeated news stories and said people have not been given a fair shot, calling for business re-engineering, and she rejected solving issues through men claiming they are afraid to meet women. The panel addressed board-level diversity and backlash, including claims that men should not have one-on-one meetings with women. Smith said those most left out are women of color, noting the absence of black men and women despite women of color being on stage.

StockX CEO Josh Luber said streetwear has been a priority since the company’s start, citing growth across sneakers, watches, handbags, and streetwear in two years. The streetwear category launched in October 2017 with an exclusive Supreme collection, and StockX is described as the largest authentic Supreme merchandise marketplace. StockX added BAPE and Palace, with Scotty Newman leading BAPE and Kenny Locklier leading Palace; the company says it will offer more than 4,000 BAPE products dating back to 2010 and more than 3,000 Palace products. The passage includes background on BAPE and Palace and states that StockX, founded in February 2016, is a marketplace using anonymity and standardization, with products physically inspected and authenticated by StockX.

The passage describes the HIV epidemic’s disproportionate impact on minoritized populations and frames structural and social factors (social and structural determinants of health) as contributors to inequities. It identifies key populations affected by HIV and notes that, despite evidence-based interventions, disparities persist in diagnoses and treatment outcomes in the U.S. It highlights PrEP and Treatment as Prevention, describing access and adherence barriers and the role of factors such as stigma and structural racism. The passage argues that achieving goals of the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative requires structural interventions and addresses a gap in translating developed interventions into implementation.

The authors report their plan for a systematic review: searching literature from May–July 2024 across multiple databases, using NLP for initial screening and manual review for eligibility. Included studies must focus on HIV/AIDS in the U.S. (at least 50% sample), involve implementation or hybrid implementation-effectiveness research with original data, report implementation outcomes, and address risks/behavior by changing external factors and/or target social determinants of health. The review will extract implementation determinants, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions and code determinants using CFIR 2.0, strategies using ERIC, and adjunctive intervention components using TDF and COM-B. Results will be analyzed with tabulations and NLP thematic descriptions, disseminated through multiple manuscripts and conferences, and shared via a literature dashboard. The review timeline includes ongoing screening/analysis with dissemination planned for 2025–2026.

Vertigo, an iOS music app, has integrated with both Spotify and Apple Music so users can share music and import playlists regardless of their premium subscription. Previously it required Spotify Premium when launched last month. Vertigo also offers ad-free listening and “live sessions,” which include live-streamed video/photos, real-time chat, and audio commentary, shareable with specific users, a core friend group, or the wider community. The passage says Vertigo pays royalties for each shared song, with royalties increasing as more listeners join with their own paid memberships. It also notes Apple Music and Spotify compete with exclusive content and personalized features, and suggests Vertigo may help fill a social-feature gap for Apple Music users.

Glen Campbell is battling the final stages of Alzheimer’s disease. In a People magazine interview, his family shared that music is comforting to him, and his daughter Ashley Campbell said he often smiles and sings along even though others don’t know what he’s singing. His fans are also listening to his last work, “Adios,” a recording made in 2012 and released June 9, described as reflecting his love for music even after Alzheimer’s.

The reporter traveled around Europe by train in October 2022 using a Eurail pass, preferring it to flying across four European countries. They paid $560 total for an initial weeklong Eurail pass plus upgrade fees, and said trains were more comfortable and convenient to board, offered better scenery, and avoided issues like ear-popping and dehydration from flights. They also described benefits of traveling in business and sleeper classes and noted that train travel can be more sustainable, potentially lowering a trip’s carbon footprint.

Brazilian stocks rose on Thursday, helped by a rally in miner Vale shares after solid first-quarter production results. Vale’s iron ore output fell 6.7% quarter-on-quarter but rose 11.2% year-on-year to a record high for the period, and its shares gained up to 4.9%, adding the most points to the Bovespa. Analysts at Itaú BBA kept an “outperform” recommendation, citing prospects for strong first-quarter operating profit. Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais also rose after reversing a first-quarter loss due to early signs of industrial output recovery. The Brazilian real was volatile alongside other Latin American currencies as investors weighed geopolitical risks and election uncertainties, though polls favoring French centrist Emmanuel Macron helped ease concerns.

The passage describes limitations of current cytogenetic testing in hematological malignancies and presents optical genome mapping (OGM) as a higher-resolution alternative consolidated with existing techniques. It explains how OGM detects balanced structural rearrangements and copy number variants (5 kbp to aneuploidy/ploidy complexity) and discusses validation efforts and the need to streamline variant review and reporting in clinical laboratories. The study extends an International Consortium framework for clinical OGM implementation by using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software for hematologic malignancy datasets, focusing on myeloid neoplasms. Ten retrospective cases (nine AML, one MDS) were processed using Bionano reagents and sequencing on Saphyr chips, followed by analysis through Bionano Access/Solve and VIA with custom configurations and classification options. Independent technologist and director reviews were timed and performed in replicates to assess efficiency and reproducibility. Results report concordance between OGM and standard-of-care (SOC) testing for variant detection (SOC and OGM both positive in 6/10 cases and both negative in 4/10) and show that SOC findings were also identified by OGM. The passage also reports instances where OGM revealed additional, reportable variants not present in SOC, including complex or interstitial events not detectable by karyotype in some cases. It concludes that OGM with Bionano Access and VIA provides a streamlined, efficient approach for interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants and may support standardization of variant interpretation.

The 2018 Colorado 4-H June conference at Colorado State University concluded the Rio Blanco 4-H senior team’s season. Dr. Kevin Pond and Clay Carlson hosted the contest. Macy Collins, Jilly Bumguardner, Marryn Shults, and Tatumn Kennedy marked cards for RBC. Collins finished third high individual overall and Shults seventh high individual overall, with Collins also placing fifth in beef, third overall in swine (white rosette), and fourth in sheep/goat, while Shults placed fourth in beef and fifth in sheep/goat. Collins judged a 48 and Shults scored 48 on market lamb. In individual placings out of 600 points, Shults placed seventh (572) and Collins eighth (570). Collins averaged 46 across six oral reasons sets for 281 points (third overall), and Shults averaged 45 for 270 points (12th). Bumguardner and Kennedy gained experience. Collins made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team and will be recognized at the Colorado State Fair, then attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full ride academic and judging scholarship.

Trump warned Iran not to restart its nuclear program as he and French President Emmanuel Macron sought common ground on saving the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. Trump criticized the accord as “terrible,” “insane,” and “ridiculous,” and said he and Macron could reach an agreement soon, while Macron said both sides share goals of avoiding escalation and proliferation. The passage notes that if the U.S. withdraws, tensions could rise, potentially leading to regional arms buildup and complicating U.S. plans regarding North Korea. Macron also discussed broader regional security and other issues including steel tariff exemptions, the Paris climate accord, and U.S. troop levels in Syria.

The passage describes the role of the holder in football field goals and extra points. It explains that the holder catches the snap, quickly positions and transitions the ball for the kicker, and must act with urgency and stillness to avoid mistakes that could cause a missed kick. The holder is expected to use soft hands, place the football precisely at the kicker’s preferred angle with laces turned away, and rotate the ball to prevent issues with the kicker’s feet. It also notes that holders may have other duties such as punter, receiver, or backup quarterback, and that teams may use the punter or other players as holders. The passage emphasizes the holder’s importance to consistent scoring opportunities, while noting there are no holding stats tracked by the NFL.

The Daily Examiner is changing from a metered digital subscription model to a premium model where some stories will be subscriber-only. Community access will remain for vital public-safety information such as weather warnings, road closures, missing children reports, and some local stories will also be unlocked. The change is intended to help fund the journalism, and subscriber-only content will be marked with a plus symbol. Existing subscribers will not be affected and will have unlimited access to stories on the website and other News Corp sites. Subscribers can get a newspaper, a digital access package, and access to the current app, plus daily email newsletters and breaking news alerts. Subscriptions can be made online at www.dailyexaminer.com.au/subscriptions or by phone at 1300 361 604.

The passage says Thailand’s junta campaign to curb road deaths during the traditional New Year week (Songkran) reduced fatalities by more than 10%. It reports 390 people died on Thailand’s roads over the previous seven days, an 11% decrease from the prior year. The junta has implemented repeated crackdowns on drink driving, including harsher penalties, vehicle seizures, and requiring offenders to visit mortuaries, but earlier campaigns did not reduce deaths. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said work remains because people are still dying. The passage adds that drunk driving caused 28% of Songkran accidents, authorities seized 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars for exceeding limits, and experts cite speeding and low helmet use. It also notes concerns about bribe-taking by traffic police and reports 285 road deaths in Myanmar over the same period.

The European Union plans to push multilateral development banks to prioritize climate action more aggressively, despite opposition from the United States. A draft policy would align financing with the Paris Agreement, redirect lending away from fossil fuels toward low-carbon initiatives, and accelerate investment in green energy and climate resilience. It also calls for improved transparency, local currency financing, de-risking of climate investments, and enhanced data-sharing for emerging economies. The initiative, led by Germany and France, will be highlighted at upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings, where EU representatives aim to embed climate objectives in global development policy, but U.S. officials warn climate targets could distract from core goals of growth and poverty alleviation.

The Supreme Court of Canada ruled 7-0 that records containing information about abuse gathered from former residential school students under an independent assessment process can be destroyed after 15 years. The ruling clarified a dispute between victims’ privacy and the importance of documenting residential schools’ legacy. The Court said the 2006 settlement agreement was intended to keep the assessment process confidential and private, with claimants and alleged perpetrators relying on confidentiality assurances. The process involved disclosure of intimate personal information and narratives, which were used in steps that included submission to the federal government and the operating church, and, if unresolved, private hearings requiring signed confidentiality agreements. The Court noted that the Indian Residential Schools Secretariat and the federal department’s settlement agreement operations branch hold digital and physical records for more than 37,000 claims.

Eric Thames hit a two-run home run in the fifth inning as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Minnesota Twins 2-0 on Tuesday. Thames reached base three times in four at-bats, and the Brewers scored only on his homer. Milwaukee starter Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings and Josh Hader threw three hitless innings in relief, while Corey Knebel struck out the side for his ninth save in the ninth. The Twins were held to two hits, and fell to 1-7 on their nine-game road trip.

The passage is a periodic update on the status of international electric power sector privatization and restructuring, dated December 6, 2000. It states that many governments are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing competition at wholesale and retail levels, with varying progress by region. The update summarizes developments across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, including changes in market-opening timelines, unbundling and deregulation steps, mergers and consolidation, and specific country actions or plans such as creating regulators, conducting IPOs, restructuring generation/transmission/distribution, and expanding transmission interconnections.

The passage reflects on Inauguration Day dedication since 1789, describing changes in the nation’s people’s tasks from creating a nation (Washington) to preserving it from internal disruption (Lincoln) to saving it from external disruption. It argues that nations’ lives depend on the human spirit and claims American democracy revived and grew after crises, maintaining constitutional functions, the Bill of Rights, and free elections. It asserts that democracy cannot die because it is based on individual initiative and a free majority, and because it supports progress and humane society across continents. The passage describes a nation as having body, mind, and spirit, stating that the spirit is greatest and must not be killed. It emphasizes the democratic faith of America as rooted in centuries of people seeking freedom, citing foundational documents. It calls for continued defense of liberty and democracy amid great perils, concluding that Americans will go forward in service to their country.

Prosecutors say Kevin Mallory, 60, a consultant from Leesburg, betrayed the U.S. by giving a Chinese spy information about human assets and other top-secret materials in exchange for $25,000. Defense lawyers argue Mallory was loyal and tried to string the Chinese along by feeding them phony documents to expose details of the Chinese operation. A jury heard opening statements as authorities found more than $16,000 in undeclared cash after Mallory returned from Shanghai, and prosecutors said he later reached out to old CIA contacts and was caught off guard when a phone showed text conversations with the Chinese recruiter. Agents searched his home and found computer discs containing secret and top-secret documents, prosecutors said. The defense presented testimony that Mallory contacted CIA officials in February 2017, before the airport incident, and said he did so because he was concerned about the legitimacy of the think-tank offer. Mallory is charged in the Eastern District of Virginia and faces up to life in prison.

Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant. The program will award $100 million among 10 community projects statewide, and if successful would be one of the largest grants Olean has received, surpassing a prior $6 million North Union Street reconstruction grant. Aiello said the application was prepared in three weeks by Mary George and her staff, and it must be submitted by 4 p.m. today. The proposed grant area spans from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River, and from Franchot Park to about Seventh Street; George said the area is larger than last year and that some project ideas cannot be publicly listed due to confidentiality agreements. Included ideas range from redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building and supporting business incubator projects to improving pedestrian access to Lincoln Park and creating a park across Front Street from Olean General Hospital. Aiello also said Olean could be eligible for additional assistance through the Buffalo Billion initiative. During the public involvement session, John Sayegh of Jamestown Community College Cattaraugus County Campus praised Olean’s efforts and offered to help upgrade the Cutco Theater to help make Olean a destination, and he said local groups want more downtown performances.

Industrial enterprises face geopolitical uncertainty, higher energy prices, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortages, and growing sustainability demands. Digitalization is changing manufacturing value creation, increasing the need for a holistic information and data base to speed product development and create digital products, services, and business models that save resources. IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis—enabled by modern technologies and high-performance computing (HPC)—are presented as key approaches. The passage reports IDC findings from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in discrete and process manufacturing industries in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Simulation and modeling are used to support goals such as innovation, faster product development, reduced costs, and improved quality, with many firms planning further investment. The paper discusses use scenarios like virtual prototyping, digital twins, optimization, and AI/ML-related analysis, and highlights challenges in current HPC usage, including time/quality trade-offs, outdated simulations, data silos, security risks, high energy consumption, infrastructure availability, scalability, and costs. It describes HPC deployment preferences (outsourcing to external or cloud infrastructures, including colocation, and limited on-premises use) and outlines cloud-based architectures and HPC-as-a-Service (HPCaaS) benefits, including agility, scalability, cost optimization, and enabling new business models. The conclusion states that HPC and IT-based analytics are increasingly important for modern simulations and for digital transformation, emphasizing integrated data as a “single source of truth” across the product life cycle and across partners and customers. Recommendations include establishing virtual development, creating a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability/security/energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The passage describes multiple specification update issues for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device silicon revision A3. It explains conditions where an edge-configured PIC interrupt can prevent the Local bus clock from returning to Idle, causing missed interrupts and potential system hangs, and recommends disabling automatic clock gating for that case. It also details issues involving CRC corruption after UDMA device termination, missed or incorrectly signaled SSMI/ASMI behavior, clock gating failures in UART and USB controllers, ACPI register access problems (including hangs from byte accesses), PRD alignment and timing-related behaviors that can cause errors or hangs, and several other DMA, LPC, SMBus, PMC, and power-management related failures with corresponding implications and recommended resolutions.

Uber’s new panic button lets riders dial 911 directly from the Uber home screen, announced in April after allegations of sexual assaults. The app can display a rider’s real-time location in most cities, and in several pilot cities it automatically transmits location and vehicle details (color, make, model, year, and license plate) to emergency dispatchers. Uber CEO Dana Khosrowshahi said the feature is meant to help riders get assistance in emergencies, and Uber’s Director of Safety Products said accurate information can speed help.

Scotty Bowman discusses playing against a team a couple of times this year, noting they are sound defensively and allow few chances. He says his team was not happy because they generated no chances and gave up goals early, though the game was fairly even after the first ten minutes. He adds that the team needs to play better, especially by creating opportunities after the power play underperformed and by improving overall performance in the second and third periods.

The passage describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system and methods for operating it during descent. It is a divisional application of a U.S. patent application and states it was developed with NASA government support. The disclosure relates to a two-spool turbofan with a fan, compressors, combustor, and turbines, where a motor is connected to a shaft to translate rotational energy and enable electric power generation. The engine is described as undersized for takeoff and/or climb due to the motor, while during descent the controller decreases engine temperature to remove thrust—either by reducing fuel flow, limiting operation to a minimum temperature threshold to prevent thermal cycling, or fully depowering the core by limiting air and/or fuel. During descent, aircraft systems can be switched from engine power to electric power from an energy storage system, potentially supplemented by electricity generated via fan windmilling that spins the low speed spool and motor/generator. It also describes powering components such as an electric air compressor to replace insufficient bleed air. A method is outlined with steps to begin descent, decrease engine temperature, switch aircraft systems to electric operation, optionally windmill the fan, generate electricity, and optionally power the spool to produce thrust sufficient to meet descent needs or overcome engine drag.

Digitalization is described as using digital technologies to change business models and create new value opportunities, including faster transactions and impacts on supply chain activities. Supply chain digitalization is linked to e-supply chains and is said to support supply chain activity performance, which in turn affects customer satisfaction and sustainable business outcomes, though implementing digital supply chain arrangements can involve risks and costs.

The study focuses on Indonesian ICT companies and examines how digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth influence sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image. A theoretical framework is presented, along with hypotheses proposing positive effects among digital customer experience, electronic word of mouth, brand image, supply chain image, and sustainable supply chain performance, including mediation effects by brand image and supply chain image.

Data were collected from employees involved in distribution in ICT companies, using a cluster sampling approach across Indonesia, yielding 315 valid responses. The analysis used PLS-SEM. Measurement model assessment reported factor loadings above 0.7, composite reliability above 0.7, and AVE above 0.5. Discriminant validity was supported via cross loadings. Bootstrapping results indicated that all seven hypotheses were supported, with direct effects and mediation effects showing significant t-values. The model explained 82.3% of variance in sustainable supply chain performance, and predictive relevance (Q²) values were above zero. The findings conclude that digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth promote brand image, which improves supply chain image and ultimately enhances sustainable supply chain performance in Indonesian ICT companies.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 1, 2021. On February 8, 2021, Apple consummated the issuance and sale of $2.5 billion 0.700% Notes due 2026, $2.5 billion 1.200% Notes due 2028, $2.75 billion 1.650% Notes due 2031, $1.5 billion 2.375% Notes due 2041, $3.0 billion 2.650% Notes due 2051, and $1.75 billion 2.800% Notes due 2061, under an underwriting agreement dated February 1, 2021. The notes will pay interest semi-annually in arrears on February 8 and August 8 starting August 8, 2021, and will mature on their respective February 8 maturity dates from 2026 through 2061. The notes are Apple’s senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The filing lists related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of global notes, and legal opinion.

The passage describes the “spring of 1953” as a time when the free world focuses on the chance for a just peace, contrasting hopes for lasting peace in 1945 with the subsequent growth of fear and disciplined hope. It presents two different postwar paths: the United States and other free nations follow principles about peace, cooperation, self-determination, non-dictation, and basing peace on just relations rather than armaments; the Soviet Union is described as seeking security through force, power superiority, huge armies, and subversion. The passage argues that Soviet policies intensified arms spending and fear in free nations, while the free nations remain willing to accept genuine peaceful intentions proven by actions. It warns that atomic war is the worst fear and criticizes ongoing arms spending as taking resources from human needs, then calls for governments to speak honestly about whether there is another way to live without war. It notes new Soviet leadership after Joseph Stalin and lists conditions the United States seeks, including an honorable armistice in Korea with cessation of hostilities and political discussions toward elections, ending attacks on Indochina and Malaya, and pursuing broader political issues and disarmament with U.N. control and inspection. It concludes by asking what the Soviet Union is ready to do, emphasizing that the test of peace is deeds rather than words, and proposing that success would enable a “new kind of war” against poverty and need and strengthen the United Nations’ role in guarding peace and security.

The passage describes how cloud-based HPCaaS supports innovation in high-performance computing by providing fast, flexible access to analysis and simulation methods, state-of-the-art hardware, and new data-processing approaches. It notes that virtual process steps can streamline and speed up product development and manufacturing, support analysis of raw materials and processes, optimize supply chains and energy use, and enable new digital products, services, and business models as part of digital transformation. It says HPC technologies are becoming prerequisites for modern simulations and modeling, and that public cloud and HPCaaS can expand agility and scalability or replace in-house HPC infrastructure. Recommendations include setting up virtual product development, creating transparency and a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating HPC operating models based on circumstances, considering scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 30, 2022 includes condensed consolidated financial statements and notes. For the three months ended October 30, 2022, revenue was $5,931 million, net income was $680 million, and diluted net income per share was $0.27. For the nine months ended October 30, 2022, revenue was $20,923 million and net income was $2,954 million. The report also presents cash flows, showing net cash provided by operating activities of $3,393 million for the nine months ended October 30, 2022. The notes describe items including accounting policies, the termination of the Arm share purchase agreement (acquisition termination cost of $1.35 billion), leases, stock-based compensation, income taxes, fair value and debt, and commitments and contingencies, including product warranty liabilities and litigation. Segment information is provided for Compute & Networking and Graphics, and the report discusses liquidity, capital resources, and share repurchases and cash dividends.

Donna Adelson, 75, convicted in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, told a judge before sentencing that she is “an innocent woman” convicted “without evidence.” She said she would have stopped the murder had she known of the plan and called Markel “a fine and decent man.” Judge Stephen Everett interrupted to warn her he can consider her “utter lack of remorse,” which he referenced before she received a life sentence plus 30 additional years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. Prosecutors alleged the motive was the Adelson family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to South Florida; she was not charged. Adelson’s husband Harvey said she did not participate and that sending her to prison was wrong.

A Saskatoon woman, Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, supports the National Inquiry leadership and says she would not agree to a new commission that would “reset” and take her family’s story from the public record. She said families were not consulted before the Assembly of First Nations (AFN) voted 48 to 15 on Dec. 7 to call for chief commissioner Marion Buller’s resignation, and she supports extending the inquiry’s deadline by two years. Other Saskatchewan families, including Lillian Ewenin, said they were concerned about the commission due to issues including late changes to hearing dates, lack of communication, and uncertainty for families, and they criticized the inquiry’s handling of community trauma.

The passage explains that with rising interest rates and average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage costs just below 5%, borrowers can improve mortgage borrowing power using several techniques. It says paying off debt can raise borrowing ability because lenders assess the borrower’s minimum monthly payments rather than the interest paid, and it notes that lenders compare proposed mortgage payment plus recurring expenses against monthly pre-tax income, flagging challenges when this exceeds 50%. It also discusses getting a co-signer, changing loan programs (e.g., Freddie Mac to Fannie Mae or conventional to FHA) to potentially improve approval chances, putting more money down (generally less effective than paying off debt for qualifying), and changing jobs before applying for a mortgage under certain conditions. The passage concludes by encouraging borrowers to research suggestions for their individual situation and provides information about Scott Sheldon as a local mortgage lender.

The passage describes Singapore’s context and outlines the evolution of special education and teacher preparation. It explains that before 2004, students with disabilities were largely served through special schools run by voluntary welfare organizations, while mainstream education focused on integration rather than inclusion and placed responsibility on students. In 2004, political leadership called for better integration of persons with disabilities, leading to developments such as Enabling Masterplans, Singapore’s ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (including Article 24 on inclusive education), and policies requiring students with Special Educational Needs to attend mainstream primary schools or government-funded special schools. It also details how special education preparation for teachers and professionals expanded through roles such as Special Needs Officers/Allied Educators/Special Educational Needs Officers (SENOs), in-service programs like the Certificate in Special Needs Support, online competency roadmaps for mainstream educators, and earlier special education credentials (CISE/DISE/ADISE) culminating in pathways for advanced study. The passage notes ongoing issues including the purview of special schools under social service agencies rather than the Ministry of Education, limitations in the continuum of special education options beyond special schools, and concerns about the breadth of special educator training and the need to review hiring, pay, career progression, and program length. It concludes that Singapore’s education system is shifting toward more holistic student development and greater inclusionary spaces, with special education’s role expected to expand in partnership across special and mainstream schools.

The passage is an email dated July 31, 2001 titled “IEP News 7/31” from Jean Munoz listing many recipients and directing readers to “www.rtumble.com.” It also includes excerpts from multiple news articles about California’s electricity crisis and related political and legal issues. These excerpts discuss long-term power contracts signed by the Davis administration, an SEC preliminary inquiry into whether energy consultants used inside information to trade stock, fired consultants and their financial holdings, refund expectations from federal regulators being reduced, efforts and disputes over a Southern California Edison bailout, and San Francisco ballot measures to create public power systems that would replace PG&E with municipal utilities.

Sony released a firmware update for the A7Riii. The update primarily fixes an issue with the “Set File Name” function and also “improves overall camera stability.” The passage says reported installation problems for Mac users are likely due to Mac OS High Sierra rather than Sony software, noting that macOS 10.13 is not supported under the stated system requirements. It adds that incompatibility issues on High Sierra may be addressed in updates and suggests workarounds: users on earlier Mac OS versions should be able to install, or they can run Windows to install the update.

The passage is a lecture segment beginning with discussion of PDE homework and numerical solution issues for a drug diffusion problem in a flow field, emphasizing the need for very fine meshes due to small characteristic length scales and potential sharp concentration gradients, and warning that computer outputs must be checked for convergence. It then explains finite volume discretization using mass/energy balance concepts, describes how fluxes and boundary conditions are handled (including alternatives like ghost volumes), and notes numerical considerations such as flux evaluation and stability. The lecture covers solver choices for linear systems with sparse matrices and introduces the CFL number as a limit on time step size for time-dependent PDEs. It concludes by transitioning to probability, arguing that real measurements involve noise and variability, that physical models often use averages over fluctuations, and that probability concepts like joint and conditional probabilities, Bayes’ theorem, and probability distributions (including cumulative distributions and units of probability density) are foundational.

The passage describes a 1968 study by Lew Goldberg that tested how consistently doctors could diagnose stomach ulcers from x-rays. Researchers showed doctors the same ulcers twice without revealing they were duplicates; doctors’ diagnoses varied widely, and each doctor contradicted himself or herself at least once. The passage then says the researchers asked how doctors made their diagnoses and created a simple computer algorithm based on their explanations, which performed better than the best doctor in the group. Lewis concludes that a doctor could be beaten by an equation made by people with no medical knowledge who questioned doctors, while the passage notes missing details about how the algorithm was determined and how it accessed the data. The passage ends by questioning how long human experts will be needed to create programs that process diagnostic data.

The passage reports multiple developments following President Donald Trump’s inauguration, including claims by The New York Times that U.S. agencies intercepted calls between Russian officials and Trump’s 2016 campaign associates, with no evidence found that the campaign worked with Russians to hack or influence the election. It also describes Republican Senators waiting to hear Andrew Puzder’s answers at his labor secretary confirmation hearing, after questions about delayed tax payments related to a housekeeper not authorized to work in the U.S. A U.S. official says the FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn about his interactions with a Russian official after Trump took office, and Flynn had been fired after concerns he misled administration officials. The passage further notes the swearing-in of Linda McMahon as Small Business Administration administrator and David Shulkin as Veterans Affairs secretary, and Schumer’s call for a thorough independent investigation of Flynn’s situation, including Jeff Sessions’ recusal.

Which? research says lenders were slow to pass rising base rates to savers but quickly increased mortgage costs. After the base rate rose from 0.25% to 0.5% in November, Which? found evidence of “double standards” in 327 variable instant access savings accounts and ISAs: in the five weeks after the rise, 48% saw no rate change, 21% passed on the full 0.25% increase, and 30% increased rates by less than 0.25%. Across 95 providers, only 10% applied the full rise to all instant access savings accounts and ISAs five weeks later. For mortgages, Which? reported that 53% of providers with standard variable rate mortgages increased rates for existing borrowers by end-2017, and that market averages for two-, three-, and five-year fixed deals rose between October and December. Gareth Shaw said banks and providers should be fair to customers ahead of a possible future rate rise. A UK Finance spokeswoman said banks balance borrowing costs with savings returns, rates depend on multiple factors beyond the base rate, fixed-rate mortgage borrowers would see no immediate change, and switching/comparison improvements help customers find better deals.

The United Way of Northwest Illinois will host an event on March 28, 2018 at 10:00 a.m. at the Mt. Carroll Township Public Library to launch the Imagination Library in Carroll County. The initiative will provide books to children ages 0–5. Dolly Parton created the Imagination Library in 1996, and it has since grown to over 1,300 communities worldwide, providing books from birth to age five. United Way partnered with the Morse Group and other supporters to bring the program to Carroll County, and more information is available at https://www.uwni.org/imaginationlibrary.

The passage explains how D-branes arise from quantizing open strings with fluctuating boundary conditions, making D-branes dynamical. It then defines the D-brane mass as the vacuum energy (ground-state energy) of the open-string fields on the brane, which can be computed via vacuum diagrams summed over worldsheet surfaces with boundaries using the Euclidean path integral. Using Euler characteristic-based weighting, it derives that the D-brane mass scales like \(1/g_s\) at weak coupling.

An alternative perspective is given by computing the interaction between two D-branes: exchange of closed strings between them can be represented equivalently as a one-loop vacuum diagram of open strings stretching between the branes (channel duality). This duality is presented as a geometric fact with deeper physical significance.

The passage further describes how stacking multiple coincident D-branes changes the low-energy theory. With two branes, open strings come in four types, leading to massless fields becoming matrix-valued and enlarging the gauge symmetry. For \(n\) coincident branes, the relevant symmetry is argued to become \(U(n)\), and the low-energy worldvolume theory is identified as Yang–Mills (non-Abelian) rather than Maxwell. When branes are separated, strings stretching between different branes acquire masses, effectively breaking \(U(n)\) into smaller factors (e.g., \(U(1)\times U(1)\) for two branes). The separation is related to a Higgs mechanism, with scalar fields interpreted as describing transverse brane motion; a vanishing potential occurs when the scalar matrices commute, allowing branes to be arranged into stacks with corresponding gauge symmetry breaking.

On Monday morning, people in Bristol shared photos on Twitter of unusual wave-like clouds resembling Asperitas, a newly classified cloud type. Met Office meteorologist Emma Sharples said the clouds match Asperitas, which was added as a supplementary feature to the International Cloud Atlas earlier this year. Wave-like structures form on the underside of the clouds, creating a rough-sea appearance from below, though experts said their formation is not fully understood. The clouds have been seen in calm conditions, and theories include links to post-thunderstorm weather or formation where wind direction changes. They were spotted by the NPAS helicopter near Monmouthshire and also seen in Thornbury and Filton.

The passage describes multiple features and peripherals of MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 microcontrollers. It explains the Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS), which combines peripherals clocked by LFCLK (typically 32 kHz) for long-term timekeeping and low-power operation, and lists LFSS components including a real-time clock and an asynchronous IWDT. It also covers the VREF module (configurable internal voltage references and external reference support), the comparator (voltage comparison output with features such as wakeup and blanking), and security capabilities including flexible firewalls and CRC-16. Additional sections summarize the CRC module, UART, I2C, and SPI key features, and the IWDT and WWDT watchdog timers. It details the RTC_B time base (counters, alarms, periodic wake-up options, calibration, and drift compensation), timers (general-purpose and advanced timer capabilities), and device hardware aspects related to analog connections, IOMUX, and serial wire debug (SWD) via DEBUGSS. The text further includes notes on typical application schematics and development/documentation support, along with revision history and packaging/orderable information disclaimers.

A white, fluffy Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillar with black markings and long hairs can excrete venom if its hairs are touched, causing a rash, burning, swelling and pain, and sometimes headache, nausea or allergic reactions. It is about 4.5 cm long, is most common from July to September on nut trees like hickory, walnut and oak but can eat many plants. Advice is to wash affected areas with water and apply calamine lotion or cortisone for itching, and seek medical attention if symptoms are more severe or an allergic reaction occurs. A natural heritage leader says the caterpillars are not to be feared and encourages people to look but not touch, noting there may have been more of them in recent years.

The passage explains that options trading in META is a derivatives strategy where investors purchase call or put contracts that grant rights to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price on or before a specified date. It states that META options can be traded with different strikes and expirations, including on Facebook/META and other assets. It outlines account setup and placing orders by selecting the underlying asset, call/put type, expiration date, and strike price, and monitoring orders until execution. It gives a minimum deposit of $100 to open an options trading account, a minimum trade size of one contract, and says leverage may range from 1:1 to 1:100 (up to 1:100 mentioned) with broker-dependent variation in margin requirements. It describes risk management tools (stop losses, take profits, trailing stops), available chart types and technical indicators, access to an options chain via the “Options” tab, and setting up a watch list. It lists commissions as not charged by META but possibly by brokers, and mentions other fees such as financing charges, slippage, and inactivity fees. The passage describes potential advantages (exposure, leverage) and risks (high leverage, potential large losses, speculation), and lists possible strategies (calls, puts, covered/naked variants, and spreads like straddles/strangles).

The passage describes a classical mean reversion trading strategy for the S&P 500 (backtested on SPY/S&P 500) based on Internal Bar Strength (IBS) and Relative Strength Index (RSI) criteria. It mentions an equity curve from January 2000 starting with 100,000 equity, allocating 100% to each trade (compounding, with no taxes deducted), along with “stats” summarizing performance. It also discusses the strategy’s performance when parameters are inverted/reversed, including a separate equity line and stats. The passage refers readers to links for Amibroker and Tradestation code and includes FAQs about the strategy, its statistical results, and performance under inverted parameters.

The passage traces how U.S. occupations have been categorized by “skill” from the 19th to the 21st centuries and discusses “unskilled” work as common, low-paid, and often essential. It describes early census-based occupational classifications and defines “unskilled” work as requiring no special training, judgment, or manual dexterity and relying mainly on muscular strength. It reports that many workers were classified as “unskilled” in 1930, with African Americans disproportionately represented in these occupations, and notes that in the 21st century “low-skill” and “unskilled” terms remain widely used, including in a 2020 Social Security Administration definition. It then outlines trends such as automation slowing growth in some middle-paid jobs while low-paid in-person service jobs rise, job polarization, and the continued prevalence of farm, factory, and service work. The passage also provides examples from agriculture, manufacturing, servant and service occupations, and gig work, and describes legal and organizing efforts to improve pay and working conditions, including minimum wage rules, union activity, and regulations affecting tipped workers and independent contractors. It concludes by arguing that jobs historically labeled “unskilled” are essential, especially during the 2020 Covid-19 lockdowns, and highlights concerns about job quality for lower-wage workers.

The passage describes a nuclear medicine market report that includes competitive outlook, market share, and company profiles for major global manufacturers such as GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging, and Bayer. It provides product and technology analysis (including specifications, product type, and production) and evaluates revenue, cost, gross margin, shipment, price, revenue, gross profit, and business distribution, along with regional and segment data. It states the market size grew from 3500 million $ in 2013 to 4200 million $ in 2016 with an average annual growth rate of 6.27%, and projects reaching 5890 million $ by 2021. The report focuses on global regions including Europe, North America, the Middle East, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia, and categorizes the market by manufacturers, regions, type, and application, including product types (Tc-99, I-123/131, In-111, Xe-133, Th-201), industry segments (Diagnostic, Therapeutic), and channels (Direct Sales, Distributor).
