It also covers price, cost, gross analysis by type, company, and region, consumption data by region, and includes SWOT and investment-related analyses.

Atossa Genetics Inc (NASDAQ:ATOS) shares fell 12.06% in the most recent session. Analysts project a $2 stock price within 52 weeks, with a latest closing price of $0.7, and a consensus based on Thomson Reuters’ First Call. The company’s average brokerage recommendation (ABR) is 1, with an industry rank of 162 out of 265. Of the analyst recommendations, 0 recommend Buy, 1 rate Outperform, 0 Hold, 0 Underperform, and 0 Sell. The stock’s ATR-14 is 0.09, with weekly volatility of 37.88% and monthly volatility of 16.66%. The RSI is 73.41. Atossa Genetics has a market capitalization of $17.25 million and 24.52 million shares outstanding; 29.13 million shares traded in the previous trade versus an average of about 3.7 million shares.

Eric Hirsch, EdReports’ founding CEO, will step down at the end of the school year as the board searches for a new chief. Hirsch said he has led EdReports since its 2014 founding, focusing on linking curriculum and standards, and noted the organization’s reviews are considered a leading authority by many states and districts. During his tenure, EdReports revised its scoring process last year, expanded in June to review pre-K materials, and has faced increased criticism as attention to high-quality materials has grown. Critics said the review process was slow to adapt to reading reforms, while EdReports reported it has caught up on criteria and increased focus on phonics, fluency, and phonemic awareness. Alternatives and partners have also entered the field, and EdReports aims to provide information about programs to support district leaders. Looking ahead, EdReports needs a leader who understands the intersection of artificial intelligence and curriculum, and Hirsch said research shows adopting a strong curriculum alone is not enough because of mismatches between curriculum, teacher training, and assessment.

The passage describes the Gann fan as a technical analysis tool invented by W.D. Gann, consisting of several diagonal lines (“Gann angles”) drawn from important highs and lows, with the main angle at 45 degrees (the 1:1 line). It is used to indicate potential support and resistance levels, time-to-price relationships, and possible reversals or breakouts, based on the idea that price movements follow geometric angles. The passage also discusses Gann fan comparisons with Fibonacci fans, notes that the tool is not always accurate and that levels may not reliably indicate support or resistance, and emphasizes the need for backtesting and risk management. It states that a meaningful backtest of the Gann fan strategy was not provided due to subjective pattern rules.

The passage explains how Cover 1 works, describes defensive objectives using man-free coverage, and outlines ways offenses can attack it. Cover 1 covers every receiver in man-to-man while a free safety plays a deep zone (and sometimes a linebacker or strong safety becomes a “low hole” defender). Defenses can shade matchups, funnel routes toward the middle for help, and flex options such as bracketing, run fits, or blitzing within Cover 1. To beat Cover 1, the passage says the best area to attack is the outside away from where the deep safety can help, using perimeter matchups that let skill players win. Suggested tactics include pick plays, double moves (including Sluggo and Stutter), and routes that get receivers the ball moving (like deep crossing routes, wheel routes, and out routes). It also lists five example plays from college offenses showing specific methods against man principles or Cover 1 looks.

S&P Global Platts said it will launch new low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel oil prices at several Asian bunkering ports from June 1, 2017, to reflect rising sales in Singapore and expected global tightening of sulphur limits. Platts noted Singapore’s low-sulphur marine gasoil sales grew nearly six-fold in three years to 1.14 million tonnes in 2016, and that the new assessments will cover fuels with a maximum sulphur content of 0.1%. The new prices will be published alongside existing marine gasoil and marine diesel prices, with gasoil prices in Singapore, Fujairah, Hong Kong, Shanghai and South Korea, and diesel prices in Tokyo Bay and West Japan.

Christine Milligan said she was shocked when asked if she wanted to “revoke” her daughter Cassidey Ouellete’s right to organ donation after Ouellete died last week in a car accident near Peterborough and was pronounced brain dead. Ouellete had signed an organ donation card at age 16, and Milligan felt the decision was already made. The Trillium Gift of Life Network says families can override wishes only if the loved one expressed regret about donation before death, and it reported that family overrides occurred in about 10% of cases in 2016, down from 21% in 2015, typically in exceptional circumstances. Trillium encourages people to discuss their wishes with family and supports leaving hospital to rest and begin funeral arrangements. Milligan’s brother, former MPP Robert Milligan, introduced a private member’s bill in 2012 to update organ donation rules, including limiting revocation to donors and using presumed consent with opt-out. Trillium’s CEO Ronnie Gavsie questioned presumed consent, citing research and a poll showing many Ontarians prefer opt-in. Milligan said she hopes legislation will be reintroduced and named after her daughter.

The passage provides advice for Galaxy Fold users to unfold or view in full screen for a better experience, and includes disclosures that offers may be influenced by compensation while product ratings are not. It describes a “Wells Fargo Active Cash” credit card offer with unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 spend in the first 3 months, a 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (with variable APR afterward), a $0 annual fee, and cell phone protection up to $600 (subject to a $25 deductible). It also presents a “Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards” card offer with unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases, 5% cash back on certain travel booked through Capital One Travel, a limited-time welcome bonus of $300 plus credits/bonuses tied to travel credits and $500 spend in 3 months, and a 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers (with variable APR afterward). The passage includes approval/credit-score disclaimers and additional marketing and ownership/advertiser disclosures.

The passage discusses South American misunderstandings about the United States’ attitude toward other American republics, particularly the belief that the Monroe Doctrine implied superiority and a protectorate over countries to which it applies. It says this impression hindered understanding, friendly relations, and the flow of American capital and trade. Secretary Root’s mission is described as dispelling the impression, and his July 31 address at the Rio conference is quoted to emphasize peace, respect for independence and equal rights, and support for common prosperity without taking rights or privileges beyond what is conceded to every American republic. The passage also notes that the address was received with acclaim across South America, and it cites Argentine minister Doctor Drago praising a U.S. policy that condemns oppression and European control without seeking preponderance. It mentions Argentine and U.S. commemorations of figures linked to South American independence, Brazil naming a conference building “Palacio Monroe,” and the author’s earlier 1905 message warning about foreign forceful collection of contract debts and the risk of permanent occupation.

The passage describes a speaker praising a player’s performance, the city and its family atmosphere, and the growing local support for their team after Christmas. It says the team is winning and that the speaker hopes the public recognizes his face for a long time. The speaker discusses selling hockey in different markets, the game being more enjoyable with more scoring and comebacks, and coaching kids during the lockout while noting improved team involvement in youth hockey. They express a desire to end their career in the city and mention choosing the team based on its depth and upcoming talent.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm near Kirkaldy, won a Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Award, which he says carries extra weight with big clients. He uses digital and social media to promote deals, farming life, and connect with customers, including posting on Facebook after a buffalo calf named Bert ran into the woods. The farm markets the health benefits of buffalo meat and has developed a niche in Scotland’s food and drink industry, winning in the 2016 Meat category. Mitchell says the award and nomination boosted business credibility and opened opportunities with larger customers. The passage also invites entries for the 2018 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Awards.

Yang and his wife witnessed at least 10 people being hit by a white van on Yonge St. Calls to police were made from their car, and after about two minutes a police car blocked the street near Empress Ave. Yang described severe injuries and deaths at the scene near Mel Lastman Square, including a body on the sidewalk and people with major trauma, and said he believes the driver’s actions were deliberate. Other witnesses reported seeing the van drive on the sidewalk, hit people, and that it did not appear to be an accident. Police said both the van and driver were in custody, but they did not know the motive or cause, and they created a hotline and web portal for witness information. The van was reported to have struck pedestrians along the sidewalk heading south, and bodies and personal items were seen at locations including near Tolman Ave. 

North York paramedics sent multiple ambulances and two ambulance buses; Sunnybrook hospital received 10 patients, with two pronounced dead, five in critical condition, and three serious. North York General received four patients. Yonge St. was largely closed to the public, with police advising people to stay away, and TTC service was initially shut down between Finch and Sheppard with partial resumption later.

Arthur Potts warned Edmonton council that it is too early to call the city’s road salting experiment a success. He said Edmonton saved $4.2 million in operating costs, but that private vehicle owners may face costs up to 10 times higher because liquid calcium chloride is more damaging than traditional salt, including increased rust on vehicles and bikes and more damage to concrete and city bridges. City officials said they reduced sand use by 68% last winter and that calcium chloride is less corrosive than traditional salt, but Potts said the chemical and its corrosion inhibitor were not tested in Edmonton and that the tests may be irrelevant. Officials are seeking capital funds for next winter, would apply less salt with specialized equipment, and plan to pre-wet traditional salt with beet juice. They could not provide the environmental impact and said storm sewer runoff monitoring would have results in October, while collision statistics will not be available because the pilot has run for one year.

A recent experiment tested whether an AI tool, called Waldo, can scan social media to help public health workers detect harmful outcomes from cannabis use. Waldo reviewed more than 430,000 past Reddit posts and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects. Researchers checked 250 flagged posts and verified that 86% described problematic experiences. The researchers say this approach can use information from social media that agencies like the CDC do not monitor and that many people may not have access to official ways to report side effects. The team trained Waldo on a subset of posts and reported it performed better than ChatGPT on identifying side effects in their test, though it did not outperform human reviewers. They caution that Waldo’s performance for other products remains uncertain and suggest future ethical use could flag rare side effects and route them to health officials with privacy protections.

The passage says the Trump administration withdrew from United Nations discussions on an international compact on global migration, stating the negotiations would be inconsistent with U.S. law and could undermine U.S. sovereignty. It notes the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops expressed disappointment and urged reconsideration, with Church leaders arguing for international cooperation that respects sovereignty while also protecting human rights for migrants and vulnerable groups. The passage describes U.N. negotiations in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, as steps toward adopting the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration in 2018, and includes support from Pope Francis calling for migrants and refugees to be welcomed, protected, promoted, and integrated. It also presents reactions favoring the U.S. decision on sovereignty grounds, concerns about language being too broad and affecting U.S. immigration laws, and views from U.N. and other officials that the U.N. is necessary for an international response.

A team of four students from King Edward VI Grammar School in Louth—Rowan Roddick, Jack Leeming, Fraser Whittock and Ben Jeffrey—won second place in the national schools University Challenge. They advanced through rounds that included beating St Ivo School and Nottingham High School, and competed in finals at the University of Lincoln. The team was praised by headmaster James Lascelles, and reached the finals among 10 teams. They were narrowly defeated by Southend High School for Boys, scoring 280 compared to 315, after missing four key questions.

Indian Railways adopted a policy requiring trains to display “if no bill, your food is free” to prevent overcharging and protect passengers. Railway Minister Piyush Goyal said the policy would make passengers insist on bills and stop caterers from charging more than the price. By March 31, trains serving food on a payment basis are expected to have the policy in place, with IRCTC publicising it on its ticket-booking website and deploying inspectors to ensure fair prices and bills, including for small items like tea. Ministry officials linked much of the problem to servers refusing to issue bills, and IRCTC planned to increase inspection staff during food service time. Complaints of overcharging were reported, and the policy follows strict action against vendors, including cancelling licences and terminating contracts or fining caterers. A CAG report had recommended a system to stop overcharging and noted issues found during audits and stagnant food tariff enhancements.

The passage says the U.S. air traffic controller shortage worsens during the government shutdown because controllers are expected to work without pay. It reports staffing down 50% in some areas, with major delays and airports crowded with travelers concerned about safety risks. It describes barriers to staffing, including costly and time-consuming training (which can take 16 months to several years), high washout during rigorous onboarding, halted coaching during the pandemic, and retirement requirements that limit career lifespan. It also notes controllers earn about $144,580 to $145,000 annually on average, with eligibility rules for applicants and a projected 3% employment growth from 2023 to 2033.

Hascall Steel Company is described as a trusted U.S. steel service center offering a diverse range of steel products and processing services for various industrial applications. It partners with local and foreign steel producers and suppliers, carries inventory including cold reduced steel, blanked steel, slit steel, and flat-rolled steel coils, and provides solutions based on customer needs. The company evaluates gauge, width, and physical and chemical properties to match customer specifications, processes materials for commercial purposes including hot rolled black, cold rolled aluminized, and coated steel, and aims to shorten lead times and reduce supply chain costs. Hascall emphasizes rigorous quality testing, an in-house laboratory for multipoint testing, and trained technicians to achieve ideal tolerance levels. The company has served customers for over 45 years, offers competitive rates, and provides availability of in-demand products and services.

The passage describes how NVIDIA’s A100 GPU and cuSOLVER support mixed-precision Tensor Core acceleration for HPC, focusing on iterative refinement methods via the TCAIRS solver. It reports performance results showing TF32 delivers the fastest and most robust convergence among tested Tensor Core modes, with up to 4x speedups on A100 for large complex matrices. The passage also explains A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) and Sparse MMA instructions that skip zero values to double Tensor Core throughput, alongside memory and scheduling features such as combined L1 cache/shared memory, simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution, large HBM2 and L2 caches with ECC, L2 residency controls, and compute enhancements like CUDA Graphs, async copy, asynchronous barriers, and task graph optimizations. It further outlines Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) for partitioning A100 into up to seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory paths, and summarizes related technologies including NVLink/NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and fault detection. The later sections include background on sparse neural network pruning and structured sparsity, and discuss the broader A100/DGX A100 platform software stack and use cases.

The passage includes SanDisk’s 1-year limited warranty terms, stating it applies only to the original end user, is not transferable, may require proof of purchase, and does not cover third-party software/content or failures caused by third-party products. The warranty is void for improper use or damage from misuse, improper installation, unauthorized repair, modification, or accidents. Warranty service is obtained by contacting SanDisk or emailing support@SanDisk.com, with the product returned in tamper-resistant, freight-prepaid packaging and with a tracking number. SanDisk may repair or replace the product with new or refurbished items of equal or greater capacity/functionality, or refund the purchase price; replaced products are covered for the remaining time of the original warranty. It disclaims responsibility for lost data and limits liability for damages, with total liability not exceeding the amount paid. It also includes an end user license agreement covering software use, restrictions (no modification, reverse engineering, or re-creation of source), “as is” warranty disclaimers, limits on liability, termination upon violation, and limits on use for high-risk activities, plus disposal instructions advising against unsorted household waste.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 28, 2019. The filing includes Tesla’s disclosure of a February 28, 2019 blog post announcing that the standard Model 3 is available at $35,000 with specified range, top speed, and acceleration, and that a Model 3 Standard Range Plus is available at $37,000. Tesla also stated it will shift sales worldwide to online only, make test drives and returns easier with a 7-day or 1,000-mile full refund window, wind down many stores while leaving some as galleries and information centers, and increase investment in its service system with same-day or same-hour goals and service availability guarantees. The blog post further announces firmware upgrades that would increase range, top speed, and peak power for Model 3 vehicles. Tesla also stated that the changes affect its expected profitability, saying it does not expect to be profitable in the first quarter of 2019 but expects profitability in the second quarter is likely.

Researchers created tiny, resealable synthetic packets similar to Ziploc bags that release contents when exposed to light of a specific wavelength. The packets are hollow and tens to hundreds of nanometers across, with a water-soluble outer polymer layer and a rigid, glassy inner layer. Light triggers a linked, light-responsive molecule to change shape, softening the inner material so contents can escape; when the light turns off, the glass re-solidifies and the packet reseals. The researchers suggest potential uses such as custom-delivering medicine to specific parts of the body and releasing fertilizers or cleanup chemicals in soil. They describe the outer material as polyethylene oxide and the inner lining as polylactic acid, both of which they say are biocompatible and used in medical contexts. The collaboration is exploring additional molecules that respond to different triggers, and the work appears in Nature Chemistry, funded by the US Army Research Office.

A federal judge ruled that a 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill is not pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who said he was a victim pictured as a minor. The judge said factors considered did not bring the image within the child pornography statute, except that the baby was nude, and wrote the image was “plainly insufficient” to support lasciviousness.

The judgment in Sol Schildkraut v. Angelo Paino was reversed on the law and facts, and a new trial was granted with costs to abide the event. The court found there was no decision sustaining the judgment in its current form and that the plaintiff made a prima facie case for an accounting if certain oral testimony was credited with documentary proof. The trial court’s rulings unduly restricted the plaintiff’s proof. A new trial before another Special Term justice was ordered to determine the credit to be given to testimony and make appropriate findings. Lazansky, P. J., Kapper, Hagarty, Carswell, and Tompkins, JJ., concur.

The passage describes cascaded inference for large-scale model serving, where an inference platform adaptively routes queries through a sequence of sub-models to meet SLOs such as accuracy, latency, and cost. It argues that existing sub-model routing policies are largely heuristic and suffer from limited generalizability and lack of provable efficiency. The proposed framework, T-Tamer, formulates routing and stopping as a multi-stage “costly exploration” problem over directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and computes theoretically optimal policies via a data-driven, model-agnostic learner. The work analyzes no-recall strategies and shows they cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to an offline optimum, motivating recall-based approaches. For with-recall settings on canonical DAG topologies (directed line, its transitive closure, and directed trees), it develops a dynamic indexing strategy with provable optimality and polynomial-time computation. Experiments on synthetic and real CV/NLP early-exit workloads evaluate the strategy and report efficient accuracy–latency trade-offs.

The passage says the S&P 500 closed near record highs at about 6,715 on Tuesday after a mild retreat. It notes investors are debating whether the rally is entering bubble territory amid bubble talk, tech weakness limiting upside momentum, and valuations above pre-2000 levels. The market is described as steady above 6,620 support, with Fed policy and government shutdown headlines driving caution.

The passage describes the rationale and implementation of a Training of Trainer (TOT) capacity-building intervention for maternal and newborn health in Palghar District, western Maharashtra. It argues that pre-service training is not enough and that effective in-service training requires appropriate techniques, competent faculty, and updated approaches; it notes that traditional lectures have little impact while case-based learning, simulations, skills practice, and feedback are more effective. A TOT cascade is presented as a way to rapidly and sustainably build workforce capacity, including through trainer mentoring and non-technical attributes such as communication and teamwork.

The intervention was piloted in Pune (2017–2019) and scaled up in Palghar (2019–2022), with on-site and virtual support from UK obstetricians and pediatricians. The Palghar scale-up involved two phases: (1) selecting and preparing eight clinically competent Pune core trainers with refresher and virtual learning sessions and content adaptations for local MNH needs and additional provider cadres; and (2) developing Palghar master trainers through a six-step process including pre-TOT screening, TOT with pre/post assessments, staggered induction, continuous supportive supervision by Pune core trainers, regular virtual quality assessment by UK experts, and virtual refresher training over 10 months using case-based discussions.

The passage reports mixed-methods evaluation. Quantitatively, post-training assessment scores for Palghar trainees were higher than pre-training scores for clinical knowledge and for abdominal palpation, newborn resuscitation, and eclampsia management. The trained Palghar master trainers reported increased clinical competency and leadership for monitoring, improved confidence as trainers through repeated delivery opportunities, and career growth via recognition and motivation. The discussion concludes that the methodical TOT approach, hybrid delivery, and enabling conditions are important, while recommending further research on long-term effects and costing.

The passage describes the growing evidence for dark matter from observations of galaxy velocities and rotation curves, and explains why understanding dark matter’s power spectrum and evolution requires multiple observational and modelling methods. It outlines how Cosmic Microwave Background measurements, X-ray cluster emission, cosmic shear, and gravitational lensing can constrain dark matter, while noting unresolved “small-scale” problems in cold dark matter simulations (core-cusp, missing/too many satellites, and too big to fail). It then presents a local, particle-physics approach: experiments aiming to produce or detect dark matter, alongside multiple candidate types (e.g., WIMPs, axion-like particles, primordial black holes, warm and self-interacting dark matter, and modified gravity).

The passage also focuses on coordination and open science for dark matter research through European and CERN-related collaborations and platforms, and highlights the ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project (Dark Matter TSP) within the EOSC ecosystem. The Dark Matter TSP aims to store, distribute, and enable FAIR access to software and data, combining workflows and tools for direct detection (e.g., DarkSide), indirect detection (e.g., Fermi LAT, KM3NeT, CTA), and collider searches (e.g., ATLAS), including capabilities for producing summary plots interpretably connected to dark matter properties. It further discusses example efforts to connect particle-physics constraints to astrophysical observations, especially gravitational lensing (substructure effects for WDM, SIDM, and CDM) and dwarf spheroidal galaxies using gamma-ray indirect detection models, then lists some tools for translating these constraints (e.g., pyHalo, GAMBIT, AxionLimits).

Finally, it concludes that ESCAPE Dark Matter TSP provides a platform to support reproducible, open, FAIR dark matter research and to expand services toward astronomically interpretable outputs for combining constraints across astronomy and particle physics.

Mark Brantley, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Aviation in St. Kitts and Nevis’ Team Unity administration, told a town hall meeting in Charlestown, Nevis on February 13, 2017 that the Team Unity Movement brought “a coming together” in the country’s federal affairs. He said the three-party Team Unity coalition launched on September 26, 2013 with Timothy Harris as leader, won the February 16, 2015 polls, and that Harris was sworn in as third Prime Minister two days later, with his Cabinet presented on February 22. Brantley argued unity was reflected in election results and urged the audience to assess the government’s record by reviewing spending and budget support, particularly for Nevis. He stated that in 2013 the SIDF spent $95,474,153 with “every copper” spent in St. Kitts and none reaching Nevis, while under Unity from 2015 he cited SIDF allocations totaling $62.2 million for Nevis projects and said the Federal Government provided regular budgetary support to the NIA totaling $51.16 million, making $113.36 million available to Nevis in less than two years. He also compared this with $17.3 million received by Nevis from 2006 to 2015 and said unity is producing tangible progress and ensuring “a fair share for all.”

The passage discusses a hockey player’s qualities and reputation, saying he is smart, quiet, and helps others when needed. It notes that he played on a famous Russian hockey line, helped create it, and was among Russia’s elite, linking defense to offense and performing in major tournaments like the World Championships and the Olympics. It also argues that due to an age gap, the last generation to see him in practice and play with him was born in the specified decade, and that this is why Russian hockey is struggling now.

The United States and Imperial Russia agreed, by exchange of notes dated September 8, 1900, to refer to arbitration their differences over claims for indemnity by U.S. citizens for losses and injuries caused by Russian arrests and seizures of American vessels and related acts by Russian agents and officers. The case facts, evidence, claimed damages, and supporting arguments are annexed for four vessel cases: the “Cape Horn Pigeon,” “James Hamilton Lewis,” “C. H. White,” and “Kate and Anna.” The U.S. argues the arrests and seizures violated international law and U.S. treaty rights and invaded citizens’ personal rights, including holding vessel officers and crews as prisoners. The passage also discusses whether interest should be added to indemnity, citing prior arbitration decisions where interest was generally allowed. It then begins Case No. 1, describing the “Cape Horn Pigeon,” an American whaling bark registered in the U.S., which sailed on December 7, 1891, and was seized by Russian authorities in the Okhotsk Sea on September 10, 1892, taken to Vladivostok, detained until the end of the whaling season, and released without trial.

The passage summarizes multiple financial-market items, including stock and currency and cryptocurrency technical outlooks. It states that analysts are discussing the Fed’s “neutral” rate and that AI-picked stocks are rallying in September. It also provides technical views for USD/JPY, GBP/USD, and BTC/USD, referencing moves tied to employment data and upcoming central bank and economic events. The passage includes details on the Bank of England’s upcoming policy decision, expectations for a potential rate cut, and updated forecasts. It also includes a section promoting Investing.com’s ProPicks AI strategy and several unrelated headlines. Risk and data-disclaimer text notes trading risks and that website data may not be real-time or accurate.

The speaker says their team put pressure on Buffalo, but Buffalo capitalized on scoring chances and their team capitalized only once, coming up a goal short. The speaker notes the game was close, with chances late to tie that did not result in a goal. They also mention the first game was won by Buffalo at home but say to focus on one game at a time.

The Delhi High Court asked the Centre and the Jammu and Kashmir administration to respond to whether judges in Jammu and Kashmir take an oath upholding the Constitution of India. The court, without deciding the merits, directed Chief Justice G Rohini and Justice Sangita Dhingra Sehgal posted the matter for further hearing on February 13. The petition by advocate Surjeet Singh challenges the Constitution Order 1954 that adds a proviso to Article 368, stating that amendments to the Constitution would not apply to Jammu and Kashmir unless applied by Presidential order under Article 370. The petitioner seeks quashing of the Constitution Order 1954 to the extent of this proviso.

Hundreds of progressive advocates gathered at Wells Fargo’s annual shareholders meeting in Des Moines, Iowa to demand changes to the bank’s investments and business practices, organizing under People’s Action. Speakers criticized Wells Fargo for alleged cheating, racism, and investments in violence, and activists called for the CEO and board to resign. The meeting followed a reported “unprecedented” $1 billion fine required by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for predatory mortgage practices. Protesters also cited Wells Fargo’s fossil fuel investments, including the Dakota Access Pipeline, and noted that, from 2015 to 2017, it invested more than $4.6 billion in tar sands oil, Arctic oil, ultra-deepwater oil, LNG, coal mining, and coal-fired power. Sierra Club campaigner Ben Cushing said the effort to hold Wells Fargo accountable would continue.

The passage describes SPI interface timing and configuration for a device, including a single-device standard SPI pin interface and a multi-device daisy-chain topology. It explains device operational states (RESET, ACQ, CONV) and how transitions depend on CONVST/CS and RST signals. It details the structure of data transfer frames, including how RVS and SCLK/SDI/SDO-x signals operate, and how command execution and frame length affect whether frames are treated as valid read/write commands or NOPs. It also outlines input command word/register write behavior, output data word composition based on prior commands and configurable data flags, and supported multiSPI protocols for configuring and reading data (including legacy single/dual SDO-x and source-synchronous modes). Finally, it summarizes nine configuration registers and their purposes, and includes application/power/decoupling and power-saving (NAP/PD) recommendations along with board layout guidance.

The passage explains that knee problems can be debilitating and that many people over 50 eventually need knee or knee replacement surgery due to wear and tear. It says knee injury risk later in life can be reduced through active lifestyles and healthy habits, including maintaining a healthy weight, exercising regularly, and strengthening and improving flexibility of muscles around the knees. If injury occurs, physiotherapy and appropriate exercises can help recovery, restore range of motion, and in many cases reduce the likelihood of needing surgery. It also describes common knee injury factors, and when surgery may be considered if the knee is too worn or damaged for rehabilitation alone, noting surgery involves health hazards such as infection and complications. The passage emphasizes that expert physiotherapy can support recovery before and after surgery, and that choosing low-impact, flexible, and muscle-building exercises can help protect joints.

The passage describes an absorbent hygiene-product technology, focusing on an absorbent core and articles (e.g., disposable diapers/diaper pants, incontinence products, sanitary napkins, and panty liners) designed to improve liquid absorption, distribution, comfort, and reduce leakage. The core includes substantially interconnected channels extending through the crotch portion along the length and across the width, with channel geometries such as U-bends and diverging or funnel-shaped open ends, and channels that remain visible before and after use (preferably more visible after use). A high fluid-distribution structure is arranged to distribute fluid faster than discontinuous fluid absorption structures, and the disclosure also describes creating tri-stage fluid distribution driven by channels, three-dimensional absorbent material, and superabsorbent polymer. It further outlines a process for making the core using a mold with a 3D insert (inverse channel shape), applying nonwoven webs and three-dimensional absorbent material under vacuum to form channels substantially free of three-dimensional absorbent material, optionally using bonding steps and adhesive zoned by strength.

The Government has launched a six-week consultation on proposed revisions to the Package Travel Regulations, aiming to provide more protection for an estimated additional 10 million UK package holidays booked online. The proposals are intended to ensure holidaymakers are not left out of pocket if travel companies go bust, by updating rules to reflect changed booking habits. They include calls for clearer information about refund rights, extending current protections, and making the business assembling the package responsible for the entire holiday even when third parties provide parts. Consumer minister Margot James said regulations need updating, and Which? and a consumer group spokesman said gaps in protection must be addressed so consumers have peace of mind regardless of how they book.

Japan’s GDP grew unexpectedly fast in the second quarter, extending an uninterrupted expansion streak to 18 months. Growth was annualised at 4% from April through June, compared with the 2.5% expected by most economists, and rising household consumption rose 3.7%, supported by near 10% higher purchases of durable goods. The article notes Japan’s data is volatile and often revised, including an avoided recession in 2015 due to upward revisions. It highlights that Japan’s longest growth streak in more than a decade suggests greater resilience under Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s reforms, alongside a stronger global economy and ultra-easy BOJ policies. It also says the pickup in consumption aligns with Abenomics’ goal of a higher-wage, higher-spending cycle, though wage growth has lagged and the BOJ postponed its 2% inflation target for a sixth time.

The passage contains multiple dated news items about Enron in November 2001. Enron warned that credit worries, asset-value declines, and reduced trading activity could hurt its fourth-quarter earnings, and it disclosed it may have to take large losses related to investment partnerships and repay a $690 million note after a credit rating downgrade. Enron also reported revised third-quarter results, widening its loss, and said its auditor Arthur Andersen had not completed its review due to ongoing investigations. The company faced shareholder lawsuits seeking to stop its planned merger with Dynegy, and there were reported concerns that the “material adverse change” clause could allow Dynegy to withdraw. Several items also discuss calls for investigations into Arthur Andersen, alongside information about debt repayment deadlines, potential collateral requirements, and broader impacts on financial markets and service providers.

The passage describes the “Gold Coast” along the Hudson River as desirable real estate for views of the Manhattan skyline and access to New York City. It says the 2008 real estate crash no longer affects the area, with projects from that period fully occupied and continuing demand for new residential space near water and mass transit. Several developers are building or planning luxury rentals and condominiums in Hoboken and Jersey City, including Toll Brothers’ second phase of Provost Square in Jersey City, with studio to three-bedroom units near the Grove Street PATH station; and Bijou Properties’ 700 Jackson Street project in Hoboken, a 424-unit rental building expected to finish in mid-2019. Other developments mentioned include Ironstate’s 235 Grand in Jersey City (549 luxury rentals) and Ironstate’s multi-phase projects near the Grove Street PATH station, plus buildings at 70–90 Columbus and plans at 80–90 Columbus. Bayonne is described as the site of a mixed-use project from JMF Properties, including commercial space, waterfront residential units, and a shopping center anchored by a Costco store.

The passage argues that Americans across political parties offer immigration “solutions,” but calls for honesty and says the debate is mired in lies. It presents a 20-point plan to reform immigration by keeping refugee families together, reforming legal immigration based on labor needs, limiting family reunification, increasing overall legal immigration, applying asylum laws equally, securing the border with modern technology and infrastructure, using the National Guard sparingly, deporting some while preserving discretion, creating paths to legal status for long-term residents and DACA recipients, restricting benefits for legalized immigrants, allowing citizenship only through effort, scrapping unlawful quotas, stopping local police enforcement, creating tamper-proof identification and fixing work eligibility systems, changing employer-related laws and penalties, investing in job creation in Mexican states, and promoting work expectations for children.

Amber Rose said she is relieved to have had breast reduction surgery in January after her 36H bra size caused pain that peaked during her 2016 “Dancing with the Stars” run. She worked with plastic surgeon Dr. Garth Fisher, going from a 36H to a 36DDD, and also received cellulite treatment on her legs and butt. After surgery, she commented on how much smaller her breasts are and has since shared social media posts in revealing, low-cut clothing.

The South Coast Air Quality Management District says smoke and combustion byproducts from July 4 fireworks may worsen air quality in parts of Southern California Wednesday through Thursday, adding to particulates already present from vehicle emissions. The affected area includes Los Angeles, Orange, San Bernardino and Riverside counties, and Coachella Valley. Inland ozone levels may reach the “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups” category, with risks for people such as athletes, young children, teenagers, the elderly, and those with asthma, lung disease, or heart ailments. The public is advised to limit outdoor exercise and avoid heavy exertion for sensitive individuals. SCAQMD said a heat wave arriving Thursday could trigger another advisory depending on weather. Triple-digit temperatures are forecast Thursday and Friday, and an excessive heat watch is expected Friday through Sunday; heat waves can worsen air quality by increasing ozone formation from vehicle emissions.

The letter argues that Ohio’s district boundaries prevent one-person, one-vote democracy by tilting districts toward specific political parties, making it harder for representatives to lose elections and reducing incentives to listen to voters. It states that Ohio redraws district lines every 10 years and says there are two plans: the Fair Districts Fair Elections plan led by the League of Women Voters would use a bipartisan commission to draw lines while keeping communities together, while another plan would still produce oddly shaped, tilted districts and is likely supported by the Ohio Statehouse. The author urges readers to contact their state representatives and support the Fair Districts Fair Elections plan.

The 22nd District Agricultural Association board voted unanimously on May 22 to reject both construction bids and re-evaluate plans to remodel Surfside Race Place into a multipurpose entertainment venue due to a $4 million funding shortfall. The remodel’s cost rose from an $11 million initial estimate (when plans were 60% complete) to about $23.6 million, and a required $10.5 million storm-water runoff water treatment plant project came in with a lowest bid of $14.6 million. The board said increased construction costs contributed to weak financial returns (about 3% ROI). Although the district is approved for an $18.5 million IBank loan and has spent $1.3 million on the remodel, directors said the remaining funding gap and the possibility of further risks make them uncomfortable moving forward. The board’s motion directs Shewmaker and Penniman to re-evaluate and return with a solution in about four to six months, while emphasizing the need to complete the storm-water project. The June 27 deadline to sign loan documents is approaching.

The passage explains sector trading and investing as buying and later selling securities within a specific economy sector, noting it is typically higher risk than investing in the broad stock market. It states that the worst sectors to invest in, based on lowest median returns, are information technology, energy, utilities, and materials. It distinguishes industries from sectors, describing sector as a broader grouping of multiple industries, and says S&P divides the stock market into 11 sectors. Using JP Morgan research (Russell 3000 components from 1980–2015), it describes “catastrophic losses” as declines of 70%+ from a peak with less than 60% recovery, and reports that telecom, information technology, and energy had the most such losses. It also compares sectors by excess returns versus Russell 3000, concluding utilities are worst, followed by energy and materials, and notes utilities are stable but have weaker long-term returns. The passage discusses success and failure rates by stating the median stock has negative lifetime returns while a minority achieves multiple returns, and mentions inverse thinking and barbell strategy as related concepts.

The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures on AMD-owned boot firmware and serves as AMD’s root of trust for detection for AMD-signed firmware. SFS enables runtime updates by requiring the ASP to verify AMD’s signature before applying each SFS update package, and it can be configured so the OEM/ODM can co-sign update packages to maintain a root of trust for update. System designers own the firmware root of trust for update and, unless an AMD Platform Secured Boot (PSB) solution is enabled, for detection of designer-provided firmware. Early OEM/ODM code initially has full ROM read/write access, then locks down ROM access (e.g., via AMD ROM Armor) so only the OEM-controlled SMM handler can write; later, OEM logic verifies updates before applying them. Customers must opt in to enable SFS and configure BIOS options controlling whether SFS requires customer co-signatures, and must provide and maintain any customer co-signing keys; AMD does not countersign customer keys. SFS patch application must occur at runtime and be reapplied after each reboot, and does not persist across reset; in multi-socket systems patches are communicated to and applied per socket. The passage also describes how SFS deployment agents place command buffers and packages for ASP processing, includes requirements for aligned memory regions and interfaces, and outlines ASP steps: protect the DRAM buffer from x86 access, verify signatures, load and execute patches, update patch-level information, and return status. It further covers versioning, patchable item types, SEV/SNP update notes, attestation-related considerations, resiliency requirements, and examples of update package naming.

The passage introduces the inverse problem for complex systems, where unknown parameters cannot be measured directly and experiments provide observations linked to parameters through computer models and a quantity of interest (QoI). It formulates the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP) as the task of determining a parameter distribution that induces the observed output distribution, using a statistical (Bayesian) approach. The paper describes a framework using disintegration of measures and regular conditional probability to construct a nonparametric Bayesian solution, discusses properties such as continuity and maximum entropy for a uniform prior, and presents numerical solution ideas based on importance sampling. Examples include an exponential decay model illustrating generalized contours, synthetic data generation, and posterior distributions, along with additional examples motivating the measure-theoretic formulation and conditional density expressions for the solution.

The Trump administration initially aimed to dismantle the Affordable Care Act, but it survived. The administration faces pressure to ensure a smooth end to sign-up season as the Dec. 15 deadline approaches for eligible consumers in 39 states using HealthCare.gov, with potential website slowdowns and long call-center hold times expected from heavy traffic. A Dec. 31 extension may be available for people in hurricane-affected areas via the call center. About 9 million to 10 million people are estimated to have ACA marketplace coverage, and subsidies may lower premiums for some even if list premiums rise. Early maintenance has not disrupted sign-ups, but HHS officials have offered little detail on contingency plans; CMS says the deadline remains midnight Pacific time (3 a.m. Saturday Eastern). HealthCare.gov sent targeted reminder emails, while it is unclear whether the Trump administration will allow a grace period for applications started before the deadline. Some states running their own systems have later deadlines, such as Jan. 31 in California and New York.

Colorado State beat Wyoming 78-73 in the 226th Border War, its first win in the last five meetings, and took sole possession of first place in the Mountain West after Boise State lost to New Mexico. CSU led 41-33 at halftime and by as much as 10 in the second half, but Wyoming rallied. With 34 seconds left, Prentiss Nixon hit a three-pointer to extend the lead to four, then scored the next four CSU points from the free-throw line. CSU had foul trouble and shot 21-of-34 from the free-throw line after a season-high free-throw percentage of 74 percent entering the game. Role players contributed, including Braden Koelliker, Anthony Bonner, and Nico Carvacho, while Emmanuel Omogbo recorded a 19-point, 16-rebound double-double despite illness affecting Koelliker. Colorado State has won four straight and eight of its last nine, and will play New Mexico next Tuesday at The Pit.

The passage discusses rising Bitcoin media attention and claims by Indian IT pioneer Vijay Mukhi that Bitcoin exchanges, especially in tax haven countries, are being used to conceal “black money” by tax evaders and criminals. Mukhi, who wrote a 900-page book on Bitcoin and Ethereum blockchains, calls Bitcoin a “ponzy scheme,” warns the government and RBI against stopping black money flows into Bitcoins, and says cryptocurrency avoids paper trails compared with gold or property. The passage cites Bitcoin price increases from Rs 7,304 in April 2013 to Rs 6,26,400 in November 2017 and Rs 11,00,000 in December 2017, and provides figures attributed to Zebpay on user growth, market share, and trade volumes. Mukhi links Bitcoin’s price rise to demonetization and exposure from the Panama and Paradise Papers, while Zebpay co-founder Sandip Goenka argues that Zebpay follows KYC norms, Bitcoin is legal under existing laws, and price increases reflect limited supply and rising demand; he also describes concerns that the market is speculative and unregulated.

The passage describes rules, parameters, dependencies, and status codes for AGESA host-environment interfaces used during processor initialization, caching setup, platform configuration, memory initialization, ACPI/DMI/WHEA table generation, and power management/resume/suspend sequences. It includes guidance to use only published entry functions, discourages reliance on internal procedure names, and details cache allocation constraints (up to three execution cache regions), platform feature controls (e.g., SATA/IDE, GPP, XHCI, power states, PCIe options), memory configuration options (e.g., voltage, interleaving, ECC, UMA, training controls), and MTRR/cache behavior across boot phases. It also outlines required and optional host call-outs for buffer allocation/deallocation, stack establishment, AP task execution, SPD reading, system reset control, IDS data retrieval, heap rebasing, and hooks for memory training/test and suspend/resume context saving and restoration.

The passage summarizes multiple NFL-related headlines and includes a detailed account of Monday night’s Broncos vs. Bengals game. The Broncos routed the Bengals 28-3 with an elite defense, while the Bengals struggled offensively, scored only three points through the first three quarters, and were penalized 11 times for 65 yards. Broncos QB Bo Nix had a settled performance with his best passing game of the season and 81 yards receiving, and there were issues for the Broncos including penalties and drops. For Cincinnati, QB Jake Browning had limited success, finishing 14-of-25 for 125 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions, and the offense struggled especially in the middle of the game as the Broncos controlled possession. The passage also notes schedule concerns for Cincinnati ahead, including games against Detroit and Green Bay.

Isaiah Silva, Courtney Love’s former son-in-law and husband of Frances Bean Cobain, is suing Love and others, alleging they conspired to murder him to recover Kurt Cobain’s guitar. Silva claims the group committed crimes including burglary, robbery, sexual battery, kidnapping, attempted murder, and extortion. The legal documents say the alleged conspiracy occurred on June 3, 2016, involving Love’s manager Sam Lutfi, actor Ross Butler, and Yan Yukhtman, who reportedly tried to enter the home. The passage also notes Silva received a 1959 Martin guitar as part of his divorce settlement with Bean Cobain, and Love has not yet filed an answer.

Researchers from Clarkson University studied older adults (average age 75) performing timed walking and computer-based cognitive tasks to assess how self-reported mood relates to gait. Using LED sensors on a five-meter track, they measured gait speed and stride length before and after physical (six-minute walking test) and cognitive (math subtraction and number/sequence identification) components, and collected mood, motivation, and energy reports. They found no gait change related to mental fatigue in the first 30 seconds of follow-up walking, but later walking speed and stride length decreased significantly in participants reporting more cognitive fatigue, not in response to lower physical energy. The study will be presented at Experimental Biology 2018 in San Diego.

The passage says WWE announced five-year linear TV distribution arrangements for its weekly flagship shows, with USA Network continuing “Raw” and Fox distributing “Smackdown Live.” WWE chief brand officer Stephanie McMahon said the company is open to streaming the shows on digital platforms like Amazon and Facebook in the future. BI Intelligence notes WWE is currently focused on linear TV due to its large reach, and argues that digital streaming could help WWE reach younger viewers, citing age and social media usage statistics. It adds that digital distribution could create sponsorship opportunities, increase traffic to WWE’s other digital properties like Instagram and YouTube, and potentially lead some viewers to subscribe to WWE Network, which has 2.1 million subscribers.

The Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) reported that some schools in Northern Ireland exclude certain pupils from public GCSE and A-Level results to improve their standing in media-published league tables. Pupils can be ruled ineligible due to reasons such as illness, welfare issues, or withdrawal from school. In 2015-16, about 2,900 pupils were deemed ineligible, including 1,635 year 12 pupils at GCSE and 1,265 year 14 pupils at A-Level. The ETI said some schools were inappropriately ruling pupils ineligible, noting cases where such pupils sat up to eight GCSE-level examinations, leading to inconsistencies. The ETI added that there were also many examples of good practice in schools to help pupils decide which exams to sit.

The passage describes Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla joining President Trump in the Oval Office to announce the administration’s effort to lower drug prices. Bourla thanked Trump for his leadership and “friendship,” and the piece notes that the Trump administration’s usual posture toward the pharmaceutical industry is not typically associated with friendship. It says Bourla’s relationship with Trump, formed during the COVID pandemic when Pfizer was developing its vaccine, helped ease investor concerns and included a White House moment that highlighted the pharmaceutical industry. The full story is available via STAT+.

The average brokerage recommendation (ABR) is 3, with 1 recommendation in ABR and an industry rank of 208 out of 265.
