CBSE has released the answer keys and recorded responses for IIT JEE main 2017 on the official website. Candidates can view OMR sheets and recorded responses for Paper 1 starting Tuesday, download them along with answer keys to calculate final marks, and challenge the answer keys by following the prescribed procedure. The answer keys for online and offline exams will be available from April 18 to April 22, 2017. Steps to access include using the current events link on jeemain.nic.in, viewing or challenging the answer key and recorded responses, logging in with details, and downloading and printing the sheets for reference.

HF-band RFID enables wireless communication and also wireless power transfer from a mobile RFID reader to a passive transponder. The NFC use case on mobile devices (e.g., smart phones) increases battery drain because the reader consumes additional power during communication, and existing power-management algorithms often focus on individual components. The article describes a target system where a battery-powered reader supplies power via inductive coupling, and the reader controls transferred power by scaling the magnetic field strength; however, maximum power is often used, which can lead to transponder oversupply.

The work aims to reduce energy waste by dynamically scaling magnetic field strength using a power transfer function (PTF). The study divides the challenge into three investigations: (1) determining PTF during the card detection phase, (2) dynamically adapting field strength during communication when distance and transponder power requirements change, and (3) scaling for multiple transponders where their presence and states affect the PTF. The article’s contribution is the PTF-Determinator method, intended to determine PTF at run-time on the reader side to enable proper field strength scaling. Integration details are provided for incorporating this method into the RFID communication flow and exposing the resulting PTF via a reader-side library for power-management control.

A case study on reading digital business cards with a feature to limit maximum transmission distance (xmax) is presented, with simulation and real-hardware measurements. In simulation, improved hardware enabled up to 80% less transmission energy; on real hardware, transmission energy was reduced by 26% compared to simple card detection when x <= xmax, and up to 75% when x > xmax by cutting off transponder power to prevent energy waste. Comparison with a state-of-the-art NFC smart phone indicates that the proposed approach could reduce battery drain by up to 13% (and up to 39% in the x > xmax scenario). Future work is planned to improve physical relation factor approximation and verify other dynamic-scaling and multi-transponder investigations via simulation and measurement.

A federal judge ruled that a 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill is not pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who claimed Nirvana’s depiction made him a victim of certain crimes as a minor. Olguin said factors such as whether the depiction focuses on genitalia, whether the setting is sexually suggestive, whether the child is nude, and whether it is intended to elicit a sexual response did not bring the image within the child pornography statute, noting it was most analogous to a nude child bathing and “plainly insufficient” for “lasciviousness.”

The passage argues that continuous self-abasement and apology toward the Third World are not morally necessary or politically appropriate, and that it is unnecessary to support vocal enemies of the United States or for leaders to unilaterally forswear military force. It also states that liberal idealism does not require masochism and can align with defending freedom and the national interest. It then includes an editorial note describing Ronald Reagan’s 1979 presidential candidacy announcement, where he says the United States should not accept inevitable decline, blames leadership failures for the crisis, and outlines plans to focus on issues including the economy, taxes, government, energy, and foreign policy. In foreign policy, he warns the 1980s will pressure the United States and allies, says commitments should not waver, rejects negotiations not in the national interest, and argues that negotiation with the Soviet Union must not become appeasement.

Singapore’s Smart Nation vision, unveiled in 2014 by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, aims to enable meaningful lives through technology, with smart networks and sensors supporting daily living, community connection, and future opportunities. The vision was later expanded by Vivian Balakrishnan, who said it would shift society by reducing reliance on the Government and helping citizens use information to solve real-life problems. The passage describes various initiatives supporting the vision, including the Smart Nation Sensor Platform for collecting and analyzing data, a reorganisation that places GovTech under the Prime Minister’s Office to lead digital transformation, plans for a national digital identity framework, and the launch of SGInnovate to accelerate start-ups. It also notes efforts to include the elderly through technology-focused events and training. Despite these efforts, the passage says Singapore has a “success” gap for common people and faces “news fatigue” because many initiatives are technical, administrative, or targeted and piecemeal. It cites Estonia’s digital identity and cashless payments in Beijing as examples of successful smart nation use cases, and discusses Singapore’s PayNow and QR code payments while arguing that adoption has been slow due to consumer choice and ingrained alternatives. It suggests making digital payments opt-out for everyone enrolled with a bank account to create momentum and a broader “virtuous cycle.”

The World Bank upgraded China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.5%, citing stronger-than-expected economic resilience supported by government stimulus, improved exports, renewed domestic investment, industrial output, infrastructure spending, targeted manufacturing support, and gradual consumer sentiment gains. It warned that growth momentum is likely to ease in 2026 due to fiscal constraints and global headwinds, despite China remaining ahead of most major economies. The report said China’s growth is still below its pre-pandemic trajectory and faces structural challenges including high local government debt, demographic pressures, and declining productivity, with narrowing fiscal space and trade uncertainties potentially constraining exports.

The speaker says it was a tremendous honor to captain an NHL franchise, and that Edmonton was special because the team was united and had talent and belief in each other. They describe Rod as the face of the franchise whose daily work and conduct inspire everyone in the room. The speaker recalls being surprised by laughter from Cam about his age during the Dallas series, and says it was hard to look ahead at first but they now feel at ease and excited to return to a special place. They emphasize never looking back, not worrying about where they play, and focusing on playing their game. They praise young players and leaders, including Eric, for strong performance in big games. The speaker also agrees that the loud building and physical, fast play will shape the finals and expresses confidence that their team believes it should win.

The speaker says they have sacrificed a lot and have come far, but advises focusing only on the next game one period at a time. They describe trying to take their mind off hockey by thinking about other things, reading a book, and spending time with family after returning home. They say it is tough to stop rehashing games, but that looking at one game at a time makes it easier to accept the situation. They also mention that big leads matter and that they should not get too high or too low, emphasizing playing their best hockey at home.

The U.S. Department of Energy has awarded the University of Wyoming nearly $10 million to study whether 50 million tons of carbon dioxide can be stored underground north of Gillette, Wyoming. The study will examine capturing carbon dioxide from coal-burning plants and storing it underground. The passage notes that carbon dioxide poses a long-term risk, and that Wyoming’s coal industry—significant to the Powder River Basin and U.S. power generation—faces threats from emission regulations and shifting customer preferences toward cleaner energy.

In a January 27, 1942 telegram from Schoenfeld, former Finnish Foreign Minister Erkko said most Finns wanted withdrawal from the war, but the timing depended on external circumstances—especially when it would advantage Russia to see Finland out of the war and when German success elsewhere might make Germany indifferent. Erkko emphasized that Finland needs assurance that Russia stays out of the country and said supplies from overseas would be crucial to prevent starvation if Germany retaliates. He also believed Finland may have missed an opportunity for settlement due to earlier tenuous contact efforts. Schoenfeld reported growing friction between Finnish troops and Germans and increasing dissatisfaction with German capabilities on the Finnish front.  

A second telegram from the U.S. Secretary of State to Schoenfeld noted that, after Japan’s attack and subsequent Axis declarations of war in December 1941, the U.S. was reviewing other nations’ situations, and said German troops were using Finnish territory as bases with Finnish government consent. The U.S. stated it had no evidence the Finnish government had clarified its position regarding German armed forces and requested Schoenfeld bring the issue to the Finnish government orally with a memorandum. An attached note explained the telegram’s purpose was to record German use of Finnish territory in case of future operations through Northern Finland and to warn Finland that prolonged association with Germany could lead to complications. A third telegram reported Finance Minister Pekkala asking about relations between Finland and the United States; he was told there were no new developments, and Schoenfeld said Finland’s position could not be stationary and required clarification given rapid wartime developments.

President Trump announced a deal with Pfizer to lower prescription drug prices for Medicaid and directly for consumers. Pfizer agreed to launch new medicines priced “at parity” with other countries and, if it continues investing in U.S. manufacturing, will avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs for three years. Trump said additional deals with other companies would follow, warning that otherwise he would levy tariffs. The agreement’s details are confidential, including how much prices will change and the impact on Pfizer’s revenues or profits; the White House estimated Medicaid would save “many millions” and Pfizer cited “certainty and stability.” The article also notes uncertainty about the impact on patients and describes related industry initiatives, including a Trump-aligned direct-purchase website planned for January.

The passage explains the 4-2-5 football defense, tracing its roots to the 4-3 and 3-3-5 alignments. It describes the 4-2-5 as using 4 down linemen, 2 linebackers, and 5 defensive backs, designed to keep 6 players in the box for run defense while remaining sound against the pass, including against modern spread formations. It outlines personnel needs, emphasizing a hybrid “Sam”/“Rover” linebacker role and the use of athletic players to apply pressure. Strengths include versatility against run and pass and the ability to play many coverages from the base alignment, with common pressure and blitz options. Weaknesses include being non-mirror (creating an overhang only on the Sam side), requiring strong weak-side safety play, and struggles versus larger offensive personnel. The passage also describes how offenses often attack the side away from the Sam, common 4-2-5 blitzes and coverages (Cover 4 and Cover 3 Sky), and names coaches/teams associated with the defense, including Gary Patterson at TCU and Greg Etter at Concordia and Carthage.

The passage says the Trump administration’s “Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy” aims to increase breastfeeding rates, citing recommendations such as using WIC and other policies to support breastfeeding parents and working to promote a safe supply of donor human milk. Experts interviewed say higher breastfeeding rates are possible but require structural reforms and financial investments, including a federal paid parental leave policy the U.S. currently lacks. The passage notes that while about 84% of parents initiate breastfeeding, fewer than 40% of U.S. infants receive human milk at one year, and 60% of parents who begin breastfeeding stop sooner than planned. It also highlights related recommendations from a National Academies report, including better coordinated postpartum services, breastfeeding training in health professions, and broader insurance coverage. The passage discusses unequal access tied to employment and state-level paid leave, concerns about potential cuts to food and health assistance programs, and support for funding related to nonprofit donor milk banking.

The passage describes a tour in Otago where the author spoke at schools and community events about mental health. Although they have a cancer background and no professional qualifications, they say they are there because they have faced depression and want to encourage people to talk about mental health and reach out for help, especially to address youth suicide statistics in New Zealand. The author argues that speaking up reduces stigma and helps save lives, and cites examples of other public figures discussing mental health. It ends with guidance on where to get help, including contacting a GP or local mental health provider, calling 111 in emergencies, and listing several 24/7 free helplines and contact numbers.

The passage is a discussion praising a player, described as handling the puck well, skating well, being physical, and staying calm to make good plays. The speaker says the player has proved himself as a dependable goalie, delivers under pressure, has a competitive “gamer” demeanor, and has performed strongly in the past and current year. It also focuses on expectations and preparation for a game in Pittsburgh, describing Pittsburgh as a tough, loud home building and emphasizing discipline, patience, puck control, managing the ice, and executing both defensive and offensive work without unnecessary penalties. The speaker mentions repeating championship expectations, team pride and character, and winning through determination and sacrifice rather than individual stats. The passage also comments on handling momentum and the need for strong efforts during key game moments, including defensive plays, hits, and penalty kills, and highlights other defensive and two-way contributions against top players.

Sleep problems are common in the U.S. and are linked to impacts on mood, quality of life, workplace productivity, cognitive functioning, chronic disease risk, and health care use. Older adults, particularly those with chronic medical conditions, often experience sleep disturbances associated with higher rates of insomnia, sleep apnea, and other disturbances, and these problems may relate to anxiety, depression, dementia, and suicidal thoughts. Sleep disparities are discussed as being influenced by factors such as socioeconomic status, racism, discrimination, neighborhood segregation, and access to health care, alongside lower sleep and poorer sleep quality among minoritized and lower-SES groups. Low health literacy is described as contributing to sleep disturbances and difficulties understanding and applying recommendations. Treatment options for sleep disorders include pharmacological and non-pharmacological approaches, with cognitive behavioral therapy noted as effective; digital interventions are proposed to improve access.  

The paper presents results from a study of a multitopic mobile app for chronic disease self-management, including a sleep psychoeducation module tailored for older adults with chronic health conditions and low health literacy. The module’s content development process is described, as well as study procedures, eligibility criteria, assessments, and statistical methods. In results, 195 participants with insomnia severity index scores of 8 or greater completed the sleep module; participants were largely BIPOC and reported low income. Significant decreases in sleep quality (PSQI) were found over the study period, with significant associations of sleep quality over time with SES, health literacy, and number of health conditions, and the intervention showing a statistically significant small-to-medium effect. The discussion concludes that the brief, personalized sleep information intervention may modestly improve sleep and that further development may be warranted.

The professor introduces pleat folding, describing how alternating mountain and valley folds of concentric squares and diagonal creases can transform a square sheet into an X-shape and then into a saddle form approximating a hyperbolic paraboloid (“self-folding origami”). Similar crease patterns can produce other saddle-like forms, including ones from concentric circles with a center hole. The discussion explains elastic memory versus plastic deformation at creases and how equilibrium between creased-bent and uncreased-flat regions yields 3D shapes. The professor reports simulations using simplified spring-like forces, and describes building physical “origami skeletons” using 3D-printed spheres and aluminum rods based on virtual models.

The lecture then shifts to mathematical sculpture work joining many hyperbolic paraboloids into polyhedral “hyperhedra” through algorithmic construction. It next addresses a key folding question: with a specific concentric-square crease pattern, it is claimed impossible to achieve a proper 3D hyperbolic paraboloid without adding additional triangulating diagonals. The professor outlines how triangulated versions can be constructed and verified computationally using radical expressions and interval arithmetic, including collision checks, with results demonstrated for up to 100 rings under certain angles and with precision requirements. The “impossibility” argument is tied to geometric properties of paper folding, including claims that straight creases remain straight, polygonal boundaries lead to flat interiors, and that interior faces must stay rigid for such crease patterns—leading to contradictions for the hyperbolic paraboloid without added diagonals. The lecture concludes with related topics such as the tea bag problem, Mylar balloon inflation, and discussion of curve-crease origami pioneered by David Huffman, including efforts to recreate his models using computational design and precise fabrication.

A new system of showers is moving into the Houston area after strong storms, with severe weather possible on the first Monday of the new year, including tornadoes. ABC13 Meteorologist David Tillman reports a system that could bring large hail, damaging winds, and isolated tornadoes. A Severe Thunderstorm Warning is in effect until 9am for many Texas counties, including northwestern Liberty, San Jacinto, east central Montgomery, and southwestern Polk. The biggest threats are damaging winds, quarter-size hail, and heavy rains, with greatest concern from between Conroe and Wharton, plus Angleton, Beaumont, Galveston, and Lake Jackson. Tillman says storms may develop and the atmosphere may change rapidly, and the worst is expected to move just east of Houston by 9am.

Adoree’ Jackson told reporters after Sunday’s game that the Titans never practiced the play they ran on their final offensive play. Head coach Mike Mularkey clarified that the team had practiced the play but did not do so in the lead-up to that day. The passage also cites an ESPN tweet from Cameron Wolfe stating Jackson had said they hadn’t practiced the play and that the team only told him his route. It discusses that the situation raised concerns, and concludes that Jackson and the coaching staff should align in practice to avoid future confusion.

Max Correa, an Appalachian State freshman and biochemistry major, announced his candidacy for governor of Kansas. He said he has no family ties to Kansas and has never been in the state, and that regulations for governor candidates vary by state, with most requiring minimum ages except Kansas and Vermont. Correa acknowledged his weakness in the election as his youth, but said it gives him fresh perspectives and new policies, and he is campaigning to appeal to younger voters. He also cited Jewish concepts he learned as a child, including tikkun olam and kibbutz-style communal settlements, and said these could help reduce college costs by letting students work part time. If elected, he plans to leave App State, move to Topeka, and enroll part-time at the University of Kansas. Correa said he will focus on the opioid crisis and proposed lowering overdose rates by offering state-owned properties to pharmaceutical companies to reduce Narcan production costs. Professor William Hicks said his involvement is encouraged and that youth participation teaches political process lessons.

Algoma Public Health is celebrating its 50th anniversary with “Get Active Algoma,” partnered with the Healthy Kids Community Challenge Sault Ste. Marie. The program encourages participants to spend time with family/friends and go out in the community away from screen time, with screen time defined as time using screen-based devices. To participate, download the GooseChase app, search for “Get Active Algoma,” join the game, complete missions, earn points, and upload photos/videos. Participants are entered into a draw based on points, and the contest runs from the week of March 19 to May 31, 2018, with prizes including a $600 bike voucher and other secondary and bonus prizes. Prize winners are contacted via the email address registered with GooseChase.

The CME Group launched micro E-mini futures in 2019 to make futures accessible to more retail traders with low capital. They are 1/10 the size of corresponding E-mini contracts, trade on the CME Globex electronic platform, and are mostly financially settled. The contracts originally covered major indexes (S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000) and have since expanded to other products including bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yield, and FX futures. A micro E-mini futures strategy is used to trade these contracts and may involve technical and fundamental analysis, position sizing, and risk management; the article recommends backtesting ideas. Micro E-mini futures are traded Sunday–Friday with specified daily hours, and contract specifications (e.g., quarterly listings, contract unit, settlement time) vary by asset. Price changes depend on the underlying asset; for example, Treasury micro contracts may be affected by interest rates, inflation, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events. The passage also notes risks from adverse price movement due to leverage, outlines cash settlement based on special opening quotes, and states that seasonality depends on the specific asset. It includes examples for micro E-mini S&P 500 futures regarding contract size, tick size, and minimum fluctuation, and mentions that ETFs track underlying assets rather than contract sizes.

The passage describes Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) as a method that adds randomness to texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré artifacts, and notes it can provide higher-order filtering at the cost of a single point sample, running fast on Blackwell GPUs. It then explains Neural Radiance Cache (NRC), which uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance for real-time global illumination and dynamic lighting by inferring final lighting values for many bounces from path-traced rays after one bounce. RTX Skin is presented as ray traced subsurface scattering for rendering translucent skin materials using film-rendering technology adapted for real-time path tracing. RTX Neural Faces is described as a real-time generative AI approach that infers more natural-looking faces from a rasterized face and 3D pose data, using a model trained from many offline images and optimized with TensorRT for real-time inference. The passage also provides details of Blackwell GPU architecture (including GB202 and GB203) and lists specifications for GeForce RTX 5090, RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti, and RTX 5070, along with licensing, warranty, and trademark notices.

Napheesa Collier criticized WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert in an exit interview Tuesday, accusing her of “negligent” leadership and alleging failures to address officiating, player compensation, and the league’s product. Collier said Engelbert told her that Clark and other young players should be “on their knees” in gratitude for the WNBA’s platform and said Engelbert responded to questions about officiating by saying “only the losers complain about the refs.” Engelbert responded expressing respect for Collier but saying she was disheartened by how conversations were characterized, and she reiterated a commitment to players and elevating the game. The league also announced a multiyear media rights deal with USA Network while players are negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement; Collier said she is concerned about the WNBA’s next chapter and said she expects potential fines but is not worried about consequences.

A British expatriate, Daniel Jones, 31, was given a one-year suspended prison sentence in Siem Reap for using “pornographic” photos to promote a pool party. He had been convicted after police raided a private villa in January where prosecutors argued the images encouraged sexual activity, which they said is illegal and against Cambodian culture. Jones said there was no sex or nudity, apologized, and prosecutors said he breached decency laws and received the maximum sentence, though the remaining time was suspended after time on remand. His lawyer said he would consider an appeal, and it was unclear if he would be released immediately.

The passage contains correspondence between the U.S. Secretary of State and the British minister, reported to the U.S. House of Representatives. On December 29, 1840, H. S. Fox acknowledges Forsyth’s letter stating that the President will not order the liberation of Alexander McLeod, imprisoned in New York. Fox expresses regret and surprise at Forsyth’s remarks about the destruction of the steamboat Caroline, arguing it was self-defense against a hostile piratical vessel and protesting against calling the event an outrage or murder. On December 31, 1840, John Forsyth responds that evidence of the Caroline incident has been presented to the British government with a demand for redress, and he notes that Fox’s strongly expressed opinions would not have been made without the collected testimony submitted to Fox’s government.

Kay Frazier, 50, who married American inmate Gary Frazier after exchanging about 12,000 letters, died after developing a blood clot. The inquest heard she was hospitalised in May with serious headaches and had a large thrombosis blocking blood to her brain. A risky thrombectomy was attempted, and radiologist Toby Williams said she would die without it, but she suffered a ruptured artery during surgery and died two days later at Salford Royal Hospital. It is not known why the clot developed. Attempts to contact her children failed. Gary Frazier, 37, received 49 years for shooting two people in 1994 and is eligible for parole in 2024; the coroner has not yet returned a verdict.

A retired lawyer describes decluttering his house and deciding to toss out McGill University law school textbooks after more than 50 years, even though he initially considered each book and remembered specific cases and property law concepts. He discarded several books, used a used-copy price on Amazon as a regretful reminder of their value, and ultimately disposed of the books in a blue recycle bin. He says one book was kept as a reading stand, and he notes his later work writing and speaking humor.

The passage is a presidential inaugural address in which the speaker assumes the duties of President, relying on support from the countrymen and guidance from God. It describes national economic and financial concerns, including industrial disturbances, the need for revision of the financial system and currency arrangements, and calls for careful study of changes to coinage, banking, and currency laws by a commission appointed from prominent citizens of different parties. It emphasizes preserving the credit and integrity of the Government’s currency, addressing international bimetallism, and maintaining government economy through decreased expenditures and restored revenue through tariff taxation rather than increased internal taxes. The address also urges Congress to enact fair and conservative revenue legislation, restore protective tariff legislation, and consider extending reciprocity provisions to stimulate trade. It calls for action to relieve depression affecting labor and agriculture, improve citizenship through immigration and naturalization reforms and education, continue civil service reform, restore the American merchant marine, and pursue a firm foreign policy based on law, peace, and arbitration. The speaker argues for convening Congress in extraordinary session on March 15, 1897, and concludes by highlighting national unity and reiterating the oath to execute the presidential office and defend the Constitution.

The speaker says opposing players were aggressive in front of Eddie and in front of them, including deliberately falling on the speaker, pushing teammates on the ice when the speaker was down, and pushing defensemen, which they call dangerous. They want opponents to be more aggressive in front of Eddie rather than retaliating, and they plan to address the incident in a meeting tonight. The speaker expects similar behavior in upcoming games, says they are ready, and notes that teammates should clear space in front of them and that referees should call penalties immediately if players push on purpose. They also comment on their own play style and comfort at home, and compare ice and puck bounces between Dallas and Buffalo, saying Buffalo’s puck bounces farther and may make it easier to play the puck and go to the corners and behind the net. The speaker reports being tired after the game but feeling good afterward, with a groin injury that is okay.

The passage discusses two closely matched hockey teams with similar styles and an expected emotional game. It emphasizes addressing errors and improving intensity to provide a better effort. A player notes that after time away from the rink with family and friends, it is important to prepare for the game, and that success came by focusing on creating chances, winning battles in the offensive zone, getting the puck to the net, keeping a proactive approach rather than playing defensively, and playing with intensity especially over the last seven minutes.

An international team reports results from Bell’s test across 73 qubits, confirming large quantum systems generate genuine quantum correlations that cannot be explained classically. The researchers used a superconducting quantum processor to create low-energy states and measured energies well below classical possibilities, with a difference of 48 standard deviations. They also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations, preparing low-energy states that passed this test up to 24 qubits. The study concludes this demonstrates certifiable deep quantum behavior in large systems and could support more secure communication, improved quantum communication and cryptography, and stronger quantum algorithms.

The passage describes advanced attacking runs in soccer, building on intermediate concepts and using the same presentation format as an introduction to attacking runs. It outlines individual advanced runs (blind-side runs, drawing defenders out, inverted runs, overlap/underlap runs, third-man/third-attacker runs, late/delayed runs, and deep-lying runs) and planned runs prepared by coaching staff (designed runs, runs to receive specific passes, and fast breaks). It also covers other factors including offside awareness, timing, and unpredictability, and explains supporting runs that help maintain possession (back-pass options, square pass options, and swinging the ball/switching fields). The passage emphasizes that effective attacking runs depend on completed passes, that only one run will receive the ball at a time, and that players should scout defenders’ strengths, weaknesses, and tendencies.

A research paper in *Climate Change* argues that the 10th eruption of Iceland’s Eldgjá volcano, dated to spring 939 CE through at least autumn 940 CE, may have helped encourage Icelanders to adopt Christianity in the late 10th century. The paper links the eruption—described as the largest known lava flood eruption of the Common Era—with passages in the Poetic Edda’s *Völuspá*, which it says allude to dramatic eruptive activity and meteorological effects. It also notes that the eruption was devastating to Iceland’s new settlers due to ash blocking sunlight and hindering agriculture. The paper further suggests later traditions, including *Kristni saga*, associated conversion and political events around the official conversion date of 999/1000 CE with volcanic events like Eldgjá.

Student mistreatment in medical education has persisted since at least the 1980s, with an AAMC survey reporting a 38.12% prevalence among graduating medical students. Surveys across Asia, Europe, and Canada report similar findings, and studies link mistreatment to psychological harms, burnout, reduced empathy, and career regret. A barrier to preventing mistreatment is lack of reporting: in the most recent AAMC Graduation Questionnaire, 26.9% of mistreated respondents reported incidents, with common reasons including the belief the incident was not important enough, the belief nothing would be done, and fear of reprisal. Qualitative interview research with 21 current medical students at a single U.S. institution (April–May 2019) examined decision-making about reporting and found that participants described four factor groups influencing reporting: personal, situational, structural, and climate. Across these factors, students mostly described reasons not to report, including concerns about repercussions, uncertainty about what counts as mistreatment, logistical and process barriers, low expectations that action will occur, and perceptions of a hierarchical institutional culture that normalizes mistreatment. The study concludes that institutional culture is a key target for improving reporting and creating a safer learning environment, and it notes limitations related to the single-institution, volunteer sample and the predominance of clinical-setting incidents.

The passage argues that remaining coal lands should not be alienated. It says the author has withdrawn, pending legislation, lands likely to contain coal, with ownership kept by the United States and mining allowed only by private individuals under a royalty system and with government supervision of mine and transport rates. It compares this approach to withdrawing forest lands for public benefit. The passage also discusses congressional efforts to increase national oversight of interstate corporations, citing railway rate and pure food legislation and beef-packing control, and says early results show reduced rail freights and fares. It argues that further federal power is needed over large corporations, including controls to prevent excessive overcapitalization and require disclosure, and contends that such regulation is an antidote to abuses driving agitation against wealth while still encouraging individual initiative.

The passage is a weekly alumni job email announcement from the Haas School for jobs posted on behalf of Haas alumni. It invites companies and individuals to submit job openings to recruitalumni@haas.berkeley.edu with details including location, title, company, degree, and contact information, and offers assistance via the Haas Alumni Career Advisor (morel@haas.berkeley.edu). It then lists multiple job opportunities with locations, titles, companies, and degree preferences, including roles at Kaiser Permanente, the University of Michigan, the United Nations Foundation (development officers and writer/communications director), Micron Technology, Informatica Corp, PG&E Corporation (multiple finance/accounting/risk positions), Blue Shield of California (health data reporting and managed care systems analyst positions), ePocrates Inc (business development, strategic alliances, marketing manager), a director of strategy position with an online comparison shopping service, iVenturi (business development and director of finance), Extensity, Inc. (product manager, competitive analyst, procurement PM, telesales director), Fremont Group (economist), and Research Dog (market research/business intelligence analyst). The email also includes alumni-related updates, an events registration reference, and instructions for subscribing/unsubscribing to the alumni jobs list.

Delta reported record revenue and earnings that beat consensus forecasts, driven by continued strength in premium and corporate travel demand. For the first time in Delta’s history, it expects premium seat sales to overtake main cabin sales in 2026. On the earnings call, Delta leadership described an inflection in main cabin demand, with high-end seat revenue rising 9% to nearly $5.8 billion while main cabin sales declined 4% to around $6 billion. Delta’s adjusted revenue for the three months ended Sept. 30 was $15.2 billion, and adjusted EPS was $1.71, ahead of Wall Street estimates.

An Energy Central Daily News email dated January 23, 2002 (for Thursday, January 24, 2002) lists selected electric power and gas industry news stories, promotional content, and additional article summaries across categories such as restructuring, legislation/regulation, rates, transmission/reliability, power projects, legal matters, renewables, people, labor, fuel, environmental issues, nuclear, and financial/results. Multiple stories focus on electricity market changes, energy policy and deregulation, and investigations related to Enron, including congressional and regulatory actions.

The article presents research findings from D’harawal Country in south-west Sydney, where Indigenous community members were asked what education could look and feel like when grounded in Indigenous knowledges. It argues that, in so-called Australia, many Indigenous students face bleak futures due to ongoing systemic harm from schooling and colonial education policies, and it positions Indigenous education sovereignty as an urgent imperative. The research includes 35 participants in an anonymous online survey and face-to-face yarning with over 15 people, with exact numbers withheld to protect anonymity. Methodologically, the paper uses Indigenous futurities, envisioning, and a “layering the vision” approach to re-present findings through story, including a primary story titled “Our Education, Our Way,” supported by concepts of relationality, collective visioning, and protecting participant safety. The article also discusses protecting anonymity, using story as an amalgamation practice, and describes the story’s themes of learning based on Aboriginal knowledges, connection to Country, community control and direction of schooling, and future-focused belonging, identity, and pride.

The speaker says Darren acted respectfully and ensured nothing happened when someone was in Nick’s face. They add that whether it’s strange or not, it doesn’t matter where games are played as long as fans are enthusiastic and support the team, and they describe Dallas as a well-supported hockey town. They also discuss being friends with Guy Carbonneau, whom they say was there from the beginning and taught them about the team’s history. Finally, they praise players for being important both on and off the ice, highlighting physical play, strong defense, and the ability to score, saying successful teams likely have effective lines like that and that they are fortunate to have them.

Crystal Palace drew 2-2 with Leicester City after coming back from two goals down. Leicester led 2-0 through Robert Huth and Jamie Vardy, but Palace reduced the deficit with Yohan Cabaye and equalized in the 70th minute when Christian Benteke headed in an Andros Townsend cross. The result left Palace above the relegation zone on 35 points from 32 games, while Leicester were two points behind. Palace manager Sam Allardyce described the comeback as a “tremendous fight back,” and Vardy said Leicester were disappointed ahead of their Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid.

The passage describes Meb Faber’s simple trend-following strategy for the S&P 500 using a 200-day moving average: go long when the price crosses above the average and sell when it crosses below. It states that the strategy relies only on price, ignoring news, earnings, valuations, sentiment, and interest rates, and highlights Paul Tudor Jones’ view that the 200-day moving average helps avoid large drawdowns by getting investors out. The passage reports performance tests from 1960 to the present, including avoidance of much of the 2008/09 Global Financial Crisis and specific results around COVID-19 (max drawdown 19%). It also describes a version using monthly data with a ten-month moving average, reporting a 6.3% CAGR versus 7% for buy-and-hold and a 26% biggest drawdown during October 1987.

The passage argues that Congress has not appropriated funds for better antitrust enforcement as the law stands, though the Department of Justice has done much already. It says a special appropriation should be made under the Attorney-General’s direction, and it opposes reducing the tariff as a way to address trusts, arguing this would be ineffective and could harm weaker competitors. It maintains that trust regulation should be separate from tariff revision and emphasizes stability of economic policy, warning against frequent or radical tariff changes that could disrupt prosperity. The passage supports maintaining the protective-tariff principle while allowing careful, periodic reapplication to changing needs, aiming to keep American business interests on equal terms with foreign interests and to avoid jeopardizing workers’ wage and comfort standards. It suggests achieving reciprocity through treaties or, if needed, direct legislation and notes that tariff adjustments should be made only after thorough investigation by practical experts or a commission.

Elmatica (Printed Circuit Broker) says it has allocated resources to support increased demand and closer technical assistance for customers in South Africa. The company reports a 245% sales increase compared to 2016 and notes that customers value stronger technical support. Elmatica plans to establish a temporary department immediately, followed by a permanent team to provide access to needed technology, processes, and compliance. As of now, Swedish Country Manager Mikael Jansson has been temporarily relocated from Stockholm to South Africa.

The passage describes how AGESA interface call-outs are funneled through a single host interface portal in the binary image build model, using a host-implemented call-out router that translates function numbers into execution addresses. The router exports an interface matching a specified structure, including a function index/identifier and configuration pointer, with function-specific data passed without conversion. It outlines UEFI execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP), library/build targets and toolchains for different phase widths, and configuration option handling for the UEFI environment. It details pre-memory and early boot stack setup/removal macros and procedures, including requirements and status codes for stackless assembly routines, and emphasizes that the host environment must not modify certain registers or cache controls during Cache-As-RAM. It further describes AGESA initialization driver responsibilities across PEI and DXE phases, including PPIs, HOBs, and protocol publication, and provides examples and host environment build/control integration files. Finally, it lists required host environment call-outs for main-memory buffer allocation/deallocation, reset initiation, and other services, along with the expected parameter structures and status behaviors.

The passage argues that language teacher education fields such as English as a Second Language (ESL), World Languages (WL), and Bilingual Education (BE), though often treated as parallel, require a multifaceted historical perspective to understand their distinctions, connections, and possibilities for bridging. Using Valdés’ framework of “language curricularization,” it analyzes how theories, ideologies, policies, contexts, and program elements shape language teacher education across ESL, WL, and BE. The authors describe their own “border-crossing” curricular innovation, developed in Chicago, Illinois, where emergent bilingual and Chinese-language teacher needs are growing. They redesign an ESL methods course to shift toward translanguaging, revise the ESL course into an ESL-WL combined course to support WL candidates (especially for Chinese teaching) with multilingual and culturally responsive approaches, and outline future work to bridge WL and BE through a BE methods course focused on bilingual teacher training and critical curricular analysis. The passage concludes by emphasizing heteroglossic, translanguaging, multilingual, and critical consciousness approaches, and by discussing limitations and implications for other programs seeking similar curriculum redesigns.

Construction crews on the $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium project have exceeded minority hiring goals since work began in November, with 54% of work hours completed by minorities, women, and military veterans versus a 38% goal. At its inaugural meeting Monday, the seven-member Community Benefits Oversight Committee received an update from Mortenson Construction’s Lynn Littlejohn, who said 80,000 work hours were performed between November and March and that $91 million of $509 million in subcontracts went to 32 qualified small-business-enterprise companies, exceeding a 15% goal. Littlejohn said about 225 workers have been hired, expanding to 500 by fall, and concrete work has begun and will continue into next year. Raiders President Marc Badain said the 65,000-seat indoor stadium remains on schedule for a projected summer 2020 completion. The volunteer committee is required under the public financing legislation and will monitor the Raiders’ community benefits plan and philanthropic efforts in Southern Nevada.

The document is Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015, including financial statements, notes, and initial sections of Management’s Discussion and Analysis. It reports revenue of $21,729 million and net income of $4,985 million for the three months ended March 31, 2015, and provides condensed income statement, comprehensive income, balance sheet, and cash flow statement data. The notes cover accounting policies, earnings per share, other income (expense), investments, derivatives and their fair values, fair value measurement hierarchy, business combinations, goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, restructuring, unearned revenue, contingencies (including antitrust and patent-related litigation), share repurchases, dividends, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment information. It also includes a review report from Deloitte & Touche LLP and discusses forward-looking statements and Microsoft’s business overview and key opportunities.

The professor introduces MIT’s 6.451 course, noting it will be offered on an alternate-year basis and will be videotaped for OpenCourseWare, with permission sheets expected. He outlines logistics, including four handouts, problem set schedules, the teaching assistant (Ashish Khisti), office hours, and a midterm date (Wednesday, March 16) and grading breakdown. He enforces prerequisites from 6.450 and explains there is no single textbook covering the full material, but supplementary texts and notes are used.  

He describes the course as focused on coding for the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel, covering major classes of codes and decoding methods, and explains that the first three chapters will be covered quickly to move to later material. The professor frames the design goal as maximizing reliable digital communication rate over a channel, introduces channel modeling (including typical deep space and telephone-line contexts), and presents AWGN channel parameters and the Shannon capacity formula. He discusses coding concepts as introducing constraints to achieve low error rates near capacity and compares uncoded modulation to capacity limits.  

He then transitions to converting the continuous-time AWGN channel model to a discrete-time AWGN model using orthonormal PAM and a matched-filter receiver, emphasizing that SNR is preserved and bandwidth constraints correspond between continuous and discrete time. Finally, he defines spectral efficiency as data rate normalized by bandwidth (and discusses how it translates to discrete dimensions) and relates capacity to spectral efficiency.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) with lump-sum investing and discusses how randomness and “sequence of return risk” can affect outcomes. It defines DCA as investing a fixed amount through many installments over time, while lump-sum investing invests capital at the earliest opportunity. The article cites studies suggesting lump-sum investing usually outperforms DCA, but notes reasons some may prefer DCA, including reducing fear and avoiding timing the market. It also argues that DCA can underperform if the order of returns is unfavorable. Through backtests using the S&P 500 from January 2000 to December 2019, it reports that a lump-sum investment grows to 193,157 USD with CAGR of 6.02%, while DCA results in a CAGR of 5.5%. After reshuffling the return sequence, it states DCA performance drops substantially (CAGR from 5.5% to 1.9%), falling from 173,949 USD to 87,396 USD. The passage concludes that lump-sum investing is generally the best option and that investing spare capital when aiming for the long term may be preferable.

The passage provides guidance for Galaxy Fold users to optimize their experience by unfolding or viewing in full screen. It then describes disclosure and reward details for credit card offers, including the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card (unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 spend in 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible, with approval most likely for credit scores 670–850). It also lists features for other cards, including the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card (unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on certain travel bookings through Capital One Travel, $0 annual fee, and 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers). The passage includes statements about compensation impacts on product placement, that ratings are not influenced by compensation, and disclaimers that meeting credit ranges does not guarantee approval.

The passage discusses passive investing and presents nine Vanguard ETFs for diversification: Vanguard Total World Bond ETF (BNDW), Vanguard Total International Bond ETF (BNDX), Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF (BND), Vanguard Total Corporate Bond ETF (VTC), Vanguard Global ex-U.S. Real Estate ETF (VNQI), Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ), Vanguard Total International Stock ETF (VXUS), Vanguard Total World Stock ETF (VT), and Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI). Weber State University’s 27th annual Unity Conference, themed “Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship,” was scheduled for Oct. 2–3. Associate professor Sarah Herrmann and her student planned to present research on Utah’s impact on higher education, but on Sept. 29 the student received an email directing removal of terms including “DEI,” “diversity,” “equity,” and “inclusion” from the slides. Herrmann said faculty also pulled out, and organizers cancelled the event on Oct. 1, citing inability to deliver the expected experience.

The passage describes the conference’s sponsorship by the Student Access and Success division, which must follow Utah’s HB 261 rules. Vice President Jessica Oyler told presenters that programming could not discuss prohibited discriminatory practice as defined by HB 261, and that presentations should not describe legislation or policies in a way that takes a side. The university said communication could have been clearer, and it was considering restructuring future Unity Conferences into Academic Affairs to exempt them from HB 261 provisions.

The passage is a formal address that thanks God for continued prosperity and reports that laws from the last session have been carried out as circumstances allowed. It describes measures to maintain friendship and peace with Native nations, including new commitments with the Creeks. It discusses delays and actions related to treaty obligations with Great Britain, Spain’s boundary arrangements, and ongoing negotiations connected to Algiers. The address argues that U.S. neutrality needs naval protection, urges gradual creation of a Navy, and supports certain manufacturing exceptions for wartime needs. It emphasizes agriculture’s importance and the success of information boards funded with public assistance. It reiterates the proposals for a National University and a Military Academy, calls for legislative revision of officer compensations, and notes injuries to U.S. trade in the West Indies from the French Republic. It reports improving U.S. revenues, further steps toward paying down the public debt, submits estimates for next year’s appropriations, and urges an efficient militia establishment and protection of harbors.

The passage is a compilation of April 23, 2001 news items and Reuters/Bloomberg-related excerpts. It includes: (1) coverage of PG&E CEO Robert Glynn’s forecast that California electricity prices would fall, which the article says proved wrong and contributed to PG&E steering its Pacific Gas & Electric unit into Chapter 11, alongside details of deregulation, expansions, losses, asset sales, and a dispute over whether creditors can access assets tied to alleged fraudulent transfers; (2) a proposal by Tri-State Generation & Transmission for a 1,200-megawatt coal-fired plant in Bent County, Colorado, with estimated cost and environmental and economic rationale; (3) a Reuters update that Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi will meet U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham in Washington to discuss likely topics including oil prices and OPEC output; and (4) multiple India-related Reuters/other reports involving Enron’s Dabhol Power Company and related entities, including payment talks between Enron’s India unit and lenders, potential termination discussions, a report that power project promoters cut capacity to avoid a “Dabhol-like” situation, and ONGC disputing Enron’s claims about a gas project, plus a Times of India letter seeking clarifications on Karnataka’s power situation and costs. Eilish McCready founded Fearless, an inclusive drama theatre school in Glasgow, after graduating from an acting and performance course. She said classes are for everyone, including shy children and those with additional needs, and use drama to build confidence and social skills without pressure from end-of-year shows. Fearless keeps classes small and includes a “Fearless shake” to help children shake off nerves. Eilish, 25, runs the company with drama teachers and has seen improvements in children’s confidence.  

Lizanne Conway, whose three sons have autism, said Fearless helps her boys with areas such as social skills, personal space, social interaction, and communication, and does not single children out. She reported positive changes in confidence and wellbeing after sessions. Another parent, Lisa Byrne, said her shy daughter Rua gained confidence through drama classes, began performing, and later started her own YouTube channel. Classes are held at Studio 93, and more information is available at fearlesstheatreschool.com.

Evercore will release its second quarter 2018 financial results on July 25, 2018, and host a conference call that day at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Ralph L. Schlosstein, John S. Weinberg, and Robert B. Walsh will review the results, followed by a question-and-answer session expected to last about one hour. Investors can join by phone or via a live audio webcast on Evercore’s website; a telephone replay will be available for one week and the webcast will be archived for 30 days.

The passage compiles multiple news items and a discussion of Enron’s situation in late October 2001. It reports that Enron may need to cover potential shortfalls in investment vehicles, which could involve issuing additional stock to cover amounts due within about the next 20 months. Enron Treasurer Ben Glisan says the company believes it can repay about $3.3 billion in notes without issuing more stock, citing planned asset sales and proceeds, and saying that if necessary the “worst-case” could involve issuing up to $1 billion in stock. Other sections describe investor concerns and SEC inquiries related to partnerships run by Enron’s chief financial officer Andrew Fastow, Enron’s attempts to reassure investors via conference calls, questions about transparency and off-balance-sheet financing, and share-price declines. Additional items mention Enron’s credit and liquidity plans (including commercial paper and a possible Citigroup loan), and related market and broader news items not limited to Enron.

This winter, Captain Weston Russell says offshore fishing will be productive for sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish. He recommends heading south and letting the stream take you north, using about 160’ depth off the Dodge Wall for sails and around 90’ for kings, and using live bait purchased from local bait boats that monitor VHF 68. He also notes kite fishing, flat lining, and deep rods as options, advises using a wire trace for hoo or king, and suggests inshore fishing around the inlet for jack and tarpon along with spawning sheepshead in the channel. Shrimp is recommended for bait, with clams for sheepshead.

A study reports that AI systems can learn age and gender bias from online images and text. When ChatGPT generated resumes using female and male names, it gave female candidates resumes on average younger and less experienced, and then ranked female applicants as less qualified. Coders assessing about 1.4 million images and videos rated women as younger than men, with the strongest bias in prestigious occupations. Text analysis found less prestigious jobs were linked with younger females and more prestigious jobs with older males. In an experiment, people who viewed occupation images estimated average employee ages for women as about two years younger and for men as more than half a year older than a control group. The researchers also found these distorted inputs caused resumes for women to be scored lower, and noted that overlapping biases may be overlooked by single-bias fixes.

The passage describes Michael Gayed’s weekly rotation strategy that switches between SPY (S&P 500) and XLU (utilities) based on each’s past performance. Rotation systems are presented as strategies that buy one asset and sell it for another to benefit from sectors performing differently over time. The strategy is focused on utilities because they are described as risk-averse, low beta, and sensitive to interest rates: utilities tend to outperform when interest rates are falling and underperform when expectations for rising rates increase. The passage notes that XLU had a maximum drawdown of -45.2% in the 2008 crash versus SPY’s -54.61%. It summarizes backtest results showing strong long-run outperformance, but since the paper’s publication the strategy has lagged the market and did not recover from the 2020 crash. It concludes that the strategy has performed well historically but may be too early to say it has stopped working.

Researchers are rebranding grape pomace, a byproduct of wine production, as a renewable resource to produce antioxidants, grape oils, and dietary fibers for health products. The work is being presented at the 255th National Meeting & Exposition of the American Chemical Society. The passage says grape pomace can harm the environment through water pollution from pesticides and fertilizers, increased soil acidity from its low pH, and attracting flies and pests in landfills. It cites that the wine industry produces about 14 million tons of pomace yearly. Researchers aim to identify technologies to extract, separate, and identify nutrients from pomace while removing pesticides, and they are studying potential effects of pomace polyphenols against foodborne pathogens and effects on piglets’ gut health and survival. They also report separating phenolic compounds (after safety testing and pesticide removal) and adding them to foods like mayonnaise and ranch dressing, where they significantly inhibited lipid oxidation and extended shelf life, especially at warm temperatures, and previously reduced acrylamide formation in potato chips by 60%. The team plans to improve inhibition efficiency and make performance comparable to EDTA, while pursuing “clean label” foods with natural ingredients.

Game is selling an Xbox One S (500GB) bundle for £249.99 that includes Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. The passage lists the individual item prices on Amazon UK as £197.99, £31.97, £42.91, £12.33, and £11.90, totaling £297.10, claiming a £47.11 saving. The Xbox One S is rated 4/5 for its small form factor, 4K game upscaling, and value as a UHD Blu-ray player, with additional commentary that its main value is UHD Blu-ray playback. The included games are described with the following scores: Forza Horizon 3 (5/5), Tekken 7 (4/5), Halo 5 (4/5), and Gears of War 4 (4.5/5).

The passage describes aspects of a COVID-19 vaccine study involving BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, and placebo. Early phases were “observer-blinded” (healthcare staff knew assignments, while participants and researchers did not) and later became “open-label” for the first vaccine given; some booster reassignments remained “observer-blinded.” The study ran at 153 locations in 6 countries from 29 April 2020 to 10 February 2023 and included healthy participants aged 12+ without prior COVID-19 infection or prior COVID-19 vaccination. Phase 2/3 results after two doses of BNT162b2 or placebo were reported as 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 through the end of monitoring, with similar results across participant sets. Immune responses were assessed by measuring antibodies about 1 month after specified doses. The passage also summarizes medical problems during the study, including injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days, medical problems within 1 month, and serious medical problems within defined time windows; researchers in several cases did not believe serious problems were related to the study vaccine. No deaths occurred in Phase 1, and researchers did not believe deaths in Phase 2/3 were caused by BNT162b2; no participant died in Phase 3 among those receiving BNT162b2SA.

The Cassini spacecraft has completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn as it nears the end of its 20-year mission, culminating in a one-way trip to Saturn’s surface on September 15. During the August 14 pass, Cassini skimmed above Saturn’s clouds at 1,010–1,060 miles altitude, and based on atmospheric conditions the team may perform a “pop-down” maneuver on the second pass. Instruments on Cassini are intended to gather atmospheric data, temperature data, high-resolution aurora imagery, and observations of Saturn’s vortexes and chemical composition, including hydrogen and helium proportions. The team also plans to determine Saturn’s day length using the offset between its magnetic field and axial tilt. Cassini has spent 13 years at Saturn, including 127 close flybys of Titan; the team said those Titan flybys prepared them for rapid passes through Saturn’s upper atmosphere. With the spacecraft running low on fuel, the mission ends after a final farewell to Titan on September 11, when its final “drop-down” maneuver begins the spacecraft’s fiery descent.

The passage describes an application that claims priority to multiple U.S. and provisional patent applications, with their disclosures incorporated by reference. It includes a summary of methods for an ultrasonic device’s electromechanical system, including measuring ultrasonic transducer impedance, classifying impedance against a reference, characterizing the state and/or function of the end effector, and adjusting the power level applied to the ultrasonic transducer based on that characterization. It also describes characterizing tissue in contact with the end effector using a similar impedance-measurement, classification, characterization, and power-adjustment process. The passage further references figures and provides extensive background and description of a smart/interactive surgical environment and a modular surgical hub and energy-generation architecture, including cloud-based systems, visualization, robotic systems, and modular modules such as energy generators and smoke evacuation and suction/irrigation components.

The lecture introduces plasma diagnostics as indirect ways to gain knowledge about plasma properties (since density, temperature, velocity, etc. cannot be measured directly). Diagnostics rely on physical effects observed in other systems, often requiring mathematics and careful interpretation due to limited measurement capability (e.g., sparse spatial coverage and line-integrated measurements from light). Measurements are filtered by instrument response functions and can be affected by poorly understood physics, such as atomic data used in spectroscopy, so limitations and uncertainty must be understood.

The importance of diagnostics is illustrated through historical fusion examples: early ZETA neutron bursts were misinterpreted due to inadequate diagnostics, leading to development of Thomson scattering to confirm tokamak temperatures. The National Ignition Facility initially focused on whether ignition occurred using limited diagnostics, but lack of diagnostic information meant they did not understand why results failed; later improved diagnostics coincided with achieving ignition. Diagnostics are needed by experimenters to quantify uncertainties, by computational workers to validate and compare with reality, and by theorists to ensure experimental testability and interpret results skeptically.

The instructor then discusses what is ideally measurable (full particle phase-space distributions) versus what is practical (moments like density and average velocity), and notes additional key quantities such as magnetic fields from currents. The class concludes with an interactive exercise placing different machines/plasma regimes on a temperature–density–magnetic-field scale and discussing commonly used diagnostics (e.g., Thomson scattering, Langmuir probes, Mirnov/B-dots, spectroscopy, interferometry, Faraday rotation, bolometry). The instructor also outlines their teaching scope across plasma parameter space and acknowledges that diagnostics education is dynamic and may require incorporating updates from students and additional review literature.

The Rams are seeking permission from the Jaguars to interview Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy. Marrone, who went 1-1 as the Jaguars interim coach, helped the team play spoiler against the Titans with a 38-17 win. He previously coached the Bills as Rex Ryan’s predecessor, and later worked as the Jaguars’ offensive line coach before taking over after Gus Bradley was fired. The Jaguars may consider removing the “interim” tag and making him permanent head coach.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2015, including financial statements and related notes. It presents consolidated cash flows, operations, comprehensive income (loss), and balance sheets, with highlights such as Q1 2015 net loss of $57 million, cash and cash equivalents of $10,237 million at March 31, 2015, and total assets of $50,075 million. It also describes accounting policies, fair value measurement and marketable securities, commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings (including multiple patent and wage-and-hour matters), acquisitions and goodwill activity, long-term debt details, stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation, income tax considerations, and segment information (North America, International, and AWS). The management discussion covers liquidity and capital resources, free cash flow (non-GAAP), and results of operations including net sales, segment operating income (loss), operating expenses, and discussion of foreign exchange and non-operating items.

The passage describes Tesla’s financial pressures during 2017–2018 as it worked to ramp up production of the Model 3. After building a successful history—rising share value, major vehicle releases, and the addition of products such as the Powerwall and SolarCity—Tesla continued to struggle to turn a profit and relied on repeated equity and debt offerings to fund operations and factory expansion. As Model 3 production forecasts were revised downward and cash burn accelerated, analysts questioned whether Tesla would need more external capital, estimating it could require over $10 billion by 2020. Musk stated in an April 2018 production and deliveries report that Tesla would not require an equity or debt raise that year beyond standard credit lines. The document also includes supporting exhibits with Tesla’s shares, debt, balance sheet figures for 2015–2017, and summary income statement data.

Hurricane Harvey disrupted millions along the Texas Gulf Coast and may have damaged or destroyed up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats, including nesting sites and marshes and coastlines used by birds and marine life. Ryan Fikes of the National Wildlife Federation said state and federal agencies are conducting initial assessments and will do more detailed monitoring in the coming weeks and months. Aransas National Wildlife Refuge was damaged in areas where endangered whooping cranes feed, and Attwater Prairie Chicken National Wildlife Refuge received about 50 inches of rain, with an estimated drop from about 60 endangered prairie chickens to as few as 10 survivors. Fikes said increasing storm size and intensity are being considered alongside climate change, which the federation links to increased storm intensity and sea-level temperature increases, and he noted that some marine species may have survived while oyster beds were lost and marine mammals may have been injured by freshwater inflows.

NVIDIA worked with the DRAM industry to develop early GPUs using HBM2 and GDDR5X, and Turing is the first architecture to use GDDR6. The Turing GDDR6 memory interface was redesigned for speed, power efficiency, and noise reduction, including improvements to circuit training and clock gating; it delivers 14 Gbps signaling and about 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X in Pascal-based GPUs. Achieving these speeds required end-to-end package and board optimizations, including a 40% reduction in signal crosstalk. Turing TU102 also doubles L2 cache to 6 MB and improves effective bandwidth through lossless memory compression, resulting in about 50% higher effective bandwidth versus Pascal, which is reflected in RTX 2080 Ti performance versus GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing GPUs include a new display engine supporting higher resolutions, faster refresh rates, and HDR, with DisplayPort 1.4a and Display Stream Compression (DSC) 1.2. They ship with an enhanced NVENC encoder for H.265 (HEVC) 8K encode at 30 fps and improved NVDEC decoding for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit streams and VP9 10/12-bit HDR.

For VR, Turing provides hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, enabling power, display, and data delivery through a single connector. Turing also uses NVLink to support two-way SLI with higher GPU-to-GPU bandwidth than prior SLI bridges.

Turing enables real-time ray tracing through RT Cores in each SM, combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and RTX software technology, supporting effects such as physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. NVIDIA also introduces NGX (part of NVIDIA RTX technology) for deep learning-based image and video enhancements such as DLSS, Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Additional Turing graphics features described include Mesh Shading (with Task and Mesh shaders), Variable Rate Shading (VRS) with multiple algorithms, Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR). The passage also outlines Turing product implementations (TU104, TU106) and discusses hybrid rendering workload modeling via RTX-OPS.

The passage describes a study on public transit mode hierarchies, noting that planners’ designed hierarchies may not match passenger behavior. It proposes a new “ascending-descending” method using smart card data, classifying transfers before and after half the total trip distance into ascending and descending phases and analyzing transfer patterns to quantify hierarchical relationships among modes. The method constructs ascending and descending transfer rate matrices, computes hierarchy distances and rescaled average hierarchical orders for each mode, and can be applied separately to single-zone and multi-zone systems. In a case study using Seoul metropolitan T-money card data from November 12, 2019 (10,264,700 trip chains) and six modes (walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, metro), results show no significant difference between ascending and descending hierarchical orders within Seoul, with a consistent order. Interzonal analysis between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon indicates different hierarchical positions for modes, including regional variation between metro and intercity bus and differences for the urban bus across regions.

The case concerns a fatal car accident on a back road in Morehouse Parish. Bradd Rudolph, a 16-year-old driver, entered a “T” intersection without seeing a stop sign and drove into Bayou Bartholomew, where two teenage passengers drowned, including 15-year-old Michael Hill. Michael’s father, Jerry Wayne Hill, brought survival and wrongful death claims against the Morehouse Parish Police Jury and the vehicle’s liability insurer; the driver’s insurer settled and was dismissed, leaving a bench trial against the police jury.

The trial court found the police jury had notice of the intersection’s danger and failed to provide adequate warnings, setting fault at 20% for the police jury and 80% for Rudolph, and awarding $31,587.53 (20% of $150,000 general damages plus $7,937.64 special damages). On appeal, the police jury argued for no fault, and the plaintiff sought higher fault and damages. The appellate court amended the fault allocation to 35% to the police jury and 65% to Rudolph, and affirmed the damages award, concluding the general damages were not an abuse of discretion. The court ordered all costs to be paid by defendants.

Open Access (OA) provides free online access to scholarly research, but many publications remain paywalled, limiting reach and entrenching inequalities. The passage describes self-archiving (green OA) as one approach to broaden access, enabled by publisher/journal policies, licensing, rights-retention, and certain copyright law clauses. It reports a study assessing how self-archiving could increase discoverability of clinical trial results using Shareyourpaper (to determine self-archiving permissions) and Unpaywall (to determine OA status). In a cohort of 1,897 clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers (published 2010–2020), 54% were openly accessible (gold, hybrid, bronze, or green), and 46% were not openly accessible via a journal or repository. Of the closed-access publications, 85% had sufficient information to derive a self-archiving permission, and 16% of otherwise closed-access publications realized green OA in a repository. The study concludes that although many closed-access publications could be made accessible through institutional repositories, the opportunity for self-archiving is largely not exploited.

Honor subsidiary Honor marked its third anniversary in India by launching the Honor 9i on October 5. The article provides an initial impression of the Honor 9i, described as the world’s first smartphone with a FullView display and four cameras. It is presented as a rebranded version of Huawei Maimang 6 and Nova 2i, featuring a 5.99-inch IPS LCD FullView screen with full HD+ resolution and an 18:9 aspect ratio, a metal unibody design, dual rear cameras with LED flash and fingerprint sensor, and dual front cameras with portrait-mode bokeh. The phone runs HiSilicon Kirin 659 with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage, includes a 3,340mAh battery, and is priced at Rs. 17,999, with the camera performance and processor capabilities requiring further testing.

Natural gas prices closed at $3.27/MMBtu, staying within a descending wedge pattern since March highs. The passage says Europe’s LNG pivot has boosted U.S. exports, but surpluses have weighed on domestic prices, while seasonal softness and Canadian supply shocks have kept volatility elevated.

U.S. markets fell sharply Tuesday, with Canada’s S&P/TSX composite index also closing down 75.06 points at 15,477. The Dow dropped 424.56 points to 24,024.13, the S&P 500 fell 35.73 points to 2,634.56, and the Nasdaq fell 121.25 points to 7,007.35. The decline was attributed to the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reaching three per cent and added concerns about companies such as Alphabet. In Canada, the materials and gold sector helped offset the drop, with Barrick Gold shares up more than three per cent on better-than-expected earnings and an announcement it is no longer selling assets to pay down debt. The Canadian dollar was 77.95 US cents, up from 77.92 cents on Monday, while June gold rose to US$1,333 an ounce and May copper rose to US$3.14 a pound.

The passage criticizes Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne’s remarks at Humber College, where she said that if people don’t vote, then someone like her—an older white person—will vote. The author argues the comments are ageist and racist, claims they amount to identity politics and assumptions about demographic interests, and cites Ali Taghva’s view that Wynne is separating people along racial and age lines. The passage also notes that voter participation increases with age and that visible minorities may vote at lower rates, but says it is wrong to boost turnout in one group by demonizing others.
