The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) helped astronomers identify the progenitor of the Type II supernova SN2025pht in the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 1637. Hidden beneath dust layers, the massive red supergiant appeared in JWST images but not in earlier Hubble images. Comparing pre- and post-explosion observations from Hubble and JWST, the team found the star was extremely red and brilliant but heavily obscured, with dust making it appear over 100 times dimmer in visible light. The dust was also unexpected, appearing carbon-rich rather than oxygen-rich, and the findings may explain why red supergiant progenitors are rarely seen. The study is described as the first direct identification of a supernova progenitor star using JWST, and the team plans to search for similar future events, with help from the upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

The passage explains that ECG signals show the heart’s electrical activity across each heartbeat and are used to identify normal and pathological conditions. Deviations from a “normal pattern” are interpreted as ECG abnormalities. It focuses on ventricular repolarisation as reflected in T-wave morphology, ST-segment changes, and QT interval measures, noting that the mechanisms behind these features are often unclear and that QTc has limitations due to heart-rate correction and differing formulas.

The study introduces the “Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model,” which represents ventricular repolarisation as expanding within an egg-shaped mass of heart muscle around Wilson’s Central Terminal (WCT). ECG leads register net positive or negative signals depending on how repolarisation spreads relative to the WCT and lead direction. In the model, the asymmetrical “T-zone” generates the T-wave, the ST interval corresponds to balanced repolarisation, and the QTp interval (from Q-wave onset to T-wave peak, when repolarisation reaches the T-zone boundary) is presented as more clearly defined than QTc. The model can also simulate ST depression/elevation and various abnormal T-wave shapes by representing damaged or non-electrical regions within the egg.

The discussion argues that the model supports a unified view of repolarisation starting around the Q-wave and continuing through the T-wave, challenges common interpretations of ST changes, and recommends using QTp rather than QTc—especially for assessing arrhythmia risk and QT-prolonging medication effects. The conclusion states that the model could improve ECG interpretation and diagnosis and proposes future work on repolarisation beyond the T-zone (potentially related to the U-wave) and application to atrial repolarisation.

The article examines experiences of leaders of education-related undergraduate programmes delivered in further education (FE) colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours’ four-level “lifelong learning ecology” framework for analysis (macro policy and national structures, exo institutional relations, meso professional practice, and micro learner context). It describes how education studies and related teacher-training provision in FE developed through policy initiatives such as post-1997 expansion, partnerships with higher education institutions, and widening participation measures including foundation degrees. FE programme leaders are characterized as “keystone species” whose close, hands-on roles support learners’ academic development and pastoral needs, drawing on strong staff–student relationships and local context. The study also reports research methods and questionnaire/interview data from programme leaders, then presents findings on how programme leaders are recruited, their qualifications, and the challenges they face, including limited role clarity, heavy administrative and organisational demands, small staff teams, and competing pressures across ecology layers that can limit time for scholarly activity. The article concludes that programme leaders’ effectiveness depends on better “sightlines” outward beyond FE institutions—such as research opportunities and stronger networks—while also noting similar challenges in higher education contexts.

The passage describes methods and an interactive game system for creating virtual game environments from a real-world scene. It outlines selecting physical objects, scanning them with a capturing device to obtain a digital three-dimensional representation (e.g., point cloud or mesh) including physical property information, converting this representation into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual toy construction elements using conversion rules, and defining game-controlling elements based on the physical properties to create a virtual game environment/scene. It also discusses recognizing known physical objects (via scanning or markers such as AR tags, QR codes, RFID, or Bluetooth) and modifying the virtual environment accordingly, including removing recognized objects and optionally replacing them with virtual objects and theme-based game-controlling elements.

Additionally, the passage explains voxelization and an efficient process for mapping surface geometry onto voxels, including assigning voxel attributes (such as color) derived from surface attributes. It further describes methods for converting mesh representations into voxel representations and then into virtual toy construction models, including an example of converting a mesh with per-vertex colors into an LXFML format, as well as a process for mapping mesh colors to a discrete color palette. The system components (capturing device, processor, storage, display) and a cyclic “game play loop” are described, where a virtual environment is created, game segments are played, and new cycles can be initiated based on outcomes, potentially including recognition and use of physical playable characters made from toy construction elements.

The UAE announced the Mars 2117 Project to build the first inhabitable human settlement on Mars by 2117, unveiled by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum at the 5th World Government Summit in Dubai on 14 February. The project will partner with major international research institutions, starting with an Emirati team and expanding to international scientists, focusing on faster travel to and from Mars. Al-Maktoum said the UAE is a leading investor in space science and referenced its 2015 plans for a Mars Probe mission to land a scientific exploration spacecraft in 2021. The passage also mentions Elon Musk’s plans to make Mars habitable and SpaceX’s proposal to colonize Mars while lowering trip costs over time using fully reusable transportation.

A U.S. District Judge Paul W. Grimm sentenced Gbenga Ogundele (aka Benson Ogundele) to 234 months in federal prison for conspiracies to commit wire fraud and money laundering and for aggravated identity theft, and sentenced his wife Moji Popoola (aka Mojisola Oluwakemi Tin Popoola) to 18 months, with three years of supervised release; her supervised release was ordered to be served in home detention. The court ordered Ogundele to forfeit $2,195,103.36 and Popoola to forfeit about $165,000 and pay restitution of $34,100. The scheme involved using an online dating scam to form relationships with victims from 2011 to 2015, using false stories to obtain money, and depositing payments into “drop accounts” or sending checks, with additional use of victims’ personal information and dispersion of funds to conceal their source and control. Other co-conspirators included Babatunde Popoola, sentenced to 12 years and ordered to pay restitution of $465,170.76, Victor Oloyede sentenced to 234 months, and Olusegun Ogunseye, Olufemi Williams, and Adeyinka Awolaja scheduled for sentencing for roles including money laundering. The passage also describes related enforcement efforts by the Maryland Identity Theft Working Group and the President’s Financial Fraud Enforcement Task Force.

The passage describes a divisional U.S. patent application related to a novel compound (Chemical Formula 1) and an organic light emitting device (OLED) including the compound. It explains the organic light emitting phenomenon and typical OLED structures with electrodes and organic material layers. The compound’s structure is defined through various substituent options (Ar, L, S, and other variables) and includes moieties bonded to a triazine group. The OLED is defined as having a first and second electrode facing each other with one or more organic material layers between them, where at least one layer includes the compound. The described advantages include lower driving voltage, improved light efficiency, and enhanced lifetime due to thermal stability. Example preparation methods and OLED fabrication procedures are provided, where Chemical Formula 1 compounds are used as electron transport layers in Examples 1–15 and compared to compounds ET1–ET7 in Comparative Examples 1–7. Driving voltage, light efficiency, color coordinates, and lifetime (LT98 at 20 mA/cm²) are measured and summarized in Table 1, showing lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime for the Example compounds than for the Comparative compounds.

A woman with multiple sclerosis, Maria Saliagas, says Delta Air Lines employees tied her to a regular wheelchair during a flight from Atlanta to Amsterdam on April 1 because the airline did not provide a wheelchair with straps she said she needs. Her son, Nathan Saliagas, said a dirty blanket was used tightly enough to cause bruise marks. Delta issued a statement regretting the perception of its service and said it reached out to resolve concerns and improve the return flight. The family planned to return to Atlanta on April 30 and said Delta offered 20,000 free SkyMiles, which they said was not enough; they want a policy change for how Delta handles people with disabilities.

Martyn Waghorn returns to Sunderland’s Stadium of Light on Saturday with Ipswich Town, his seventh club since leaving his local team. The 28-year-old, who has 87 career goals, says Kevin Ball taught him “what football is about” after he nearly got released from Sunderland at age 15 due to poor form and little progress. Waghorn credits Ball with helping him refocus on the fundamentals, which led to improved performance, and says he owes both Ball and Sunderland for giving him a chance. After leaving Sunderland in 2010, he later scored 44 goals in all competitions for Rangers over two seasons and moved to Portman Road in August, already reaching double figures this season. Kevin Ball now has an ambassadorial role at the Stadium of Light, where Sunderland academy players are expected to feature alongside Josh Maja, Joel Asoro, George Honeyman, Ethan Robson, and Lynden Gooch.

Truck drivers using GPS have increased traffic through Ponca, near the Buffalo National River in Arkansas, where a steep and curvy stretch of Arkansas 43 has led to frequent runaway-truck crashes. Mike Mills and Austin Albers report rising numbers of 18-wheelers passing through Ponca, including repeated wrecks on a 2-mile stretch north of town in the past 2½ years. Albers says GPS does not alert drivers to the area’s steep elevation drop and curves, and that drivers often lose brake control. Injuries have occurred, and Albers warns pedestrians are at risk, with a fatality reported four years earlier involving a diesel-contamination incident. Examples include a Nov. 9 crash involving a heavy beverage load and other wrecks carrying various goods. After additional wrecks, the Arkansas Highway Department plans to post large warning signs on Arkansas 43 near Arkansas 103 indicating “Crooked and steep next 3 miles,” while re-evaluating the situation.

The passage describes a floor-cleaning apparatus with a vacuum source, a supply tank for cleaning fluid, and a distribution nozzle that dispenses fluid onto a surface. It also includes a suction inlet and a recovery tank that stores cleaning fluid drawn from the surface, with the recovery tank featuring various configurations such as a tank body with inlet duct and movable strainer, a cover with baffle(s), suction air outlet and cage, a shutoff float to close the suction outlet when fluid level exceeds a desired level, and a filter removable via a tab. The document further explains a pivotable floor cleaner layout with a base, body pivoting axes for storage and operation, steering via user-controlled handle movement, a rechargeable lithium-ion battery, and component positioning for center-of-gravity and balance. Additional described features include an agitator/brushroll with hydrophobic textile cleaning medium, a removable brushroll cover actuated by sliding latches, lights to illuminate and indicate spray/operation (including possible flow-sensor behavior), and squeegees to push fluid toward the suction inlet and wipe/debris-control around the brushroll, with optional secondary fluid distribution.

The passage describes the Philippines’ loss to Australia in a 2018 basketball game in Bocaue, Bulacan, and argues that the Philippines’ subsequent violent conduct brought dishonor and reflected poor judgment on the global stage. It states that the Philippines trailed 57-32 at halftime and Australia won 89-53, after which the game ended via default. The article also mentions allegations that Australia’s Daniel Kickert “hit” Philippines players during warm-ups, describes temperamental escalation during the game, and says the Philippines’ reactions were inexcusable. It notes that Australia apologized for its role and that the SBP apologized as hosts, quoting that violence has no place in sports. The passage criticizes a comment by player Jayson Castro/Romeo’s tweet response, and says an apology is a start but more actions are needed as FIBA sanctions are expected.

No external funding was received. The study is a descriptive, register-based cohort protocol using the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register to include adult patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty from 1995 to 2022, excluding hemiarthroplasty and simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty. The protocol will examine trends in revision surgery for periprosthetic joint infection after primary THA, categorized as DAIR, one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange, and will assess the risk of a second revision after each approach. Data will be collected from the primary surgery date until death or first revision, with follow-up up to 28 years, and all patients followed at least 90 days for correct timing. Analyses will use R, including Kaplan–Meier plots and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex. Strengths include long follow-up and examination of multiple revision methods; limitations include surgeon-reported PJI diagnoses and incomplete data from some private clinics.

The passage describes a “Give & Go” isolation offense that keeps the ball with two best ball handlers using a 2-1-2 alignment, with the post set on the weakside. It outlines a main continuity sequence involving passes, hard cuts to the basket, dribbling out and repeating actions when passes aren’t available. It also covers options including back cuts when a defender overplays, dribble penetration turns or moves when defenders play on the wings, and post help where the post steps out and returns the ball. Weakside help includes passing to another player (with a variation involving passing between O3 and O4), as well as weakside action options like exchanges, down screens, and back screens, with a caution to avoid moving screen fouls.

Leam Richardson dismissed comparisons between an incident at Wigan Athletic’s match against Fleetwood and Jose Mourinho’s “Milkgate” episode at Old Trafford. He said the tunnel “handbags” involved Ivan Toney and Nathan Pond, lasted about three seconds, and was laughed off in the dressing room. Richardson also said he moved toward the referee during the clash. He discussed Wigan’s FA Cup tie against AFC Fylde, aiming to win and secure a third-round trip to Premier League Bournemouth, while making changes and keeping focus on the tough test ahead.

The passage describes culturally responsive education as an effort to address inequalities in education as societies become more diverse due to globalization, war, and migration. It argues that culturally responsive education differs from multicultural education and can be used to teach more effectively by embedding culturally diverse students’ experiences into classrooms, curricula, and teaching methods. The study examines Turkish teachers’ opinions about culturally responsive educational practices using Q methodology, collecting data from 21 public school teachers in Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa. Analysis found three factors in teachers’ views—“Unification,” “Student Support,” and “Teacher Support”—with main agreements and disagreements reported across specific Q statements. The discussion concludes that teachers generally see cultural inclusion as present but still identify ongoing inequalities, and it notes that participants were hesitant to explain their extreme responses. The conclusion recommends increased culturally responsive professional development and workshops, support for students to express themselves and live their cultures in class, and further research and dissemination of cultural knowledge.

The passage describes an electronic device with touch sensor and display structures integrated under transparent and opaque enclosure wall portions. It discusses walls formed from transparent and opaque materials, with display layers mounted behind transparent portions and touch sensor layers mounted behind both transparent and opaque portions, including overlapping regions that form a touch screen display region. Touch and display layers may be implemented using thin layers on rigid or flexible substrates or as coatings on enclosure walls, with examples of transparent and opaque touch sensors and different display technologies. The passage also outlines possible enclosure shapes (flat or curved sidewalls), configurations where display and touch cover different areas, and foldable devices with flexible transparent wall portions and hinge regions supporting bending along one or more axes. Fabrication approaches include molding transparent materials, depositing and patterning touch/display layers, lamination, and using specialized equipment for coatings, patterning, and assembly, as well as stress-tolerant features to reduce damage during bending.

The passage discusses Progressive (PGR) and estimates its intrinsic value at about $48 per share, with a further range of $50 to $54 based on FY2018 expected book value and EPS, while still concluding the company is overvalued. It notes monthly dashboard reporting and highlights Progressive’s February 2018 results, including an 87.8% combined ratio and net income of $129 million (4% lower than February 2017). The text also describes Progressive’s financing (senior notes and preferred shares), expansion of commercial auto coverage for Uber’s subsidiary in three states, and growth in net earned premiums and year-to-date premiums. It further states that combined ratio improved and property business margins improved, and it provides an estimated FY2018 dividend per share range of $0.76 to $1.85 based on EPS and a gainshare factor. The author concludes the market reacted positively to the February results, but the company remains overvalued while being well-managed and continuing steady growth.

The passage explains Gary Antonacci’s dual momentum trading strategy, which selects only assets that have outperformed peers over a chosen period and have positive returns, using both absolute momentum (an asset’s rate of change) and relative momentum (comparison to other assets). It typically targets buying “the best of the performers” with positive absolute and relative momentum, and—where shorting is possible—selling short “the worst of the weak” with negative absolute and relative momentum. The passage describes how momentum is calculated (based on current price versus a past price), outlines a simplified formula for dual momentum, and gives example applications (S&P 500 vs. gold ETF; crude oil vs. natural gas futures). It also cites the momentum effect research origin (Jagadeesh and Titman, 1993), discusses Antonacci’s GEM model results as hypothetical and simulated, and reports a sample backtest using ETFs (SPY, EFA, AGG) with 6.75% annual return and 30% max drawdown. The strategy is presented as offering better backtested results than buy-and-hold and generally lower volatility, and it can be applied to sector rotation by ranking ETFs by absolute momentum and rotating among the best performers.

The Break, a longtime restaurant and billiards hall in Five Points South downtown Birmingham, is set to be demolished to make way for high-rise apartments, though no closure date has been set. Some nearby residents welcomed the change, saying the area has declined but may improve with new luxury apartments. Others criticized rising rents and said more affordable housing is needed, including Bethany Pottrhez, who said current prices are out of her range. Management was not available to comment.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis’ trash talk, saying he does not care about him. Gracie said he accepted a fight with Danis at Bellator 180, but Danis was denied, and Gracie believes Danis must fight first because he is an amateur and has not fought professionally. Gracie also stated he will fight Dave Marfone at an event on June 24 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, and added that Danis needs to stop talking and actually fight.

US researchers analyzed scores of over 10 million secondary students over 13 years and found that hotter temperatures lead to worse exam grades, with a half-degree rise in average temperature associated with a 1% drop in average exam scores. The researchers also reported that air conditioning can buffer low scores in the UK, where many schools lack it. They note that negative effects begin when average high temperatures pass 21C, around June, the month when most exams take place, raising questions about the timing of the academic year. Changing the system is described as complicated due to its use by schools, firms, universities, and Westminster, as well as UK exam marking that relies on students taking tests at the same time. The passage adds that grade score thresholds adjust each year based on average scores.

The passage explains the advance-decline indicator (advance/decline index or AD line) as a market breadth measure that plots the cumulative difference between the number of advancing and declining stocks in a stock index, typically on a daily basis. Advancing issues are stocks traded above the previous day’s close, while declining issues are traded below it. The indicator is used to confirm the current stock index trend and may signal potential reversals when it diverges from the stock index direction; a rising value suggests buying momentum and a falling value suggests losing momentum. The passage also defines related concepts including advance/decline issues, advance/decline distribution, and advance/decline volume lines. It provides a formula for the advance-decline line and describes a backtest using strict rules on the S&P 500 via SPY, concluding that the strategy did not perform well, with inconsistent results and a low profit factor of 1.55.

Dive tour operators are divided on whether the ex-HMAS Tobruk landing on her side will affect tourism. Dive Hervey Bay owner Glenn Bowman said the unplanned position could reduce projected income by 50% because the starboard side is largely inaccessible to general divers. Hervey Bay Dive Centre owner Ed Gibson said open divers would still have a “really good swim” and that the vessel remains accessible despite being on its side. Both agreed the dive will be spectacular. The Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service said the wreck is in the correct location and that safety inspections are underway, with a report to the Queensland Government and review of options to ensure the best dive opportunity. The Queensland Government is also engaging with commercial tour operators to inform them of developments.

The passage argues that evolving regulatory frameworks for responsible AI must address legal and ethical challenges from rapid generative AI and LLM development. It cites harms including misinformation and disinformation, deepfakes, and bias amplification, as well as difficulties regulating fast-iterating and increasingly complex technologies. It notes existing efforts by the European Union, the United States, and China, and voluntary actions by technology companies such as Microsoft, but says challenges remain: communication gaps between industry and government, lack of international regulatory consensus, and risks that may be missed during testing and only discovered by users later (e.g., LLM jailbreaking). To respond, it calls for partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulations, and governance that combines top-down and bottom-up input, including channels for reporting issues throughout the AI lifecycle and mechanisms to collect and investigate user-identified risks, supported by social computing for targeted community monitoring.

The passage is an email sent July 11, 2001 by Jean Munoz to many recipients with the subject “IEP News 7/11.” It compiles multiple news items about California’s electricity crisis, including settlement talks over refunds for alleged overcharging, Governor Gray Davis’s stance that California will seek up to $8.9 billion and “see you in court,” and reports that a federal judge Curtis Wagner is likely to recommend only a fraction of refunds. The passage also includes separate business and policy articles on topics such as Calpine buying natural gas reserves, Edison’s finances and legislative deadlines, shepherd working conditions in California under federal guest worker rules, Texas and California differences in electricity markets, California’s overloaded power grid and transmission investment concerns, and an interview about the Shaw Group’s power-plant business.

The passage discusses wealthy celebrities who have launched business ventures, noting that money and access can help them pursue new enterprises even without business experience, though some companies later failed or incurred major losses. It profiles Millie Mackintosh, Ella Mills (Deliciously Ella), Trinny Woodall (Trinny London), Petra and Tamara Ecclestone (Stark/Stark/SBD International and Show Beauty), Alexa Chung (Alpha Charlie), Kate Rothschild (Roundtable Records), and Sadie Frost (Frost French), describing their backgrounds, business pitches, financial outcomes such as losses and debts, and in some cases closures or winding up of companies.

The speaker says they do not need to start gambling and should be more aggressive offensively by going to the net. They credit Detroit’s players with taking away shooting lanes, making defensive adjustments, and playing tight team defense, while noting a close chance when Ronnie Francis hit the post in the last period. The speaker describes the battle in front of the net as requiring constant effort to get space for sticks and bodies, says Detroit’s defense has done better due to being offensively stacked, and emphasizes that the loudest NHL building and their enthusiastic fans energize players, including in the playoffs.

Global Ferronickel Holdings, Inc. renewed its supply contract with Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel Industry Co., Ltd. Its operating subsidiary Platinum Group Metals Corp. (PGMC) agreed to supply 1.5 million wet metric tons (WMT) of nickel ore for the 2018 mining season, delivering medium grade nickel ore with higher iron content at prevailing market prices. PGMC has supplied medium grade saprolite ore to the company since 2014 and operates the Cagdianao mine project. Global Ferronickel said it targets shipments of six million WMT for PGMC this year, subject to weather, and that PGMC’s mineral production sharing agreement was renewed for another 25 years in June 2016. The company reported 2017 income rising more than 20 times to P779.7 million, with revenues up 54% to P5.8 billion, and nickel ore shipments up 39% to 5.97 million WMT. Its average realized price increased 5% to $19.29 per WMT, and its shares fell 2.70% to P2.52.

In 2022, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson’s investiture ceremony occurred after she had served on the Supreme Court for three months following her oaths on June 30. As the most junior justice, she takes notes during private conferences. The passage says federal courts could curtail operations quickly if Congress leads to a government shutdown, while the Supreme Court would continue normal operations using permanent funds; lower courts may delay proceedings due to tighter budgets and rising costs. It also discusses the Roberts court’s upcoming focus on major issues, a call by some state attorneys general to challenge a 2008 decision limiting the death penalty in child rape cases where the victim did not die, and a dismissed NIL lawsuit by former Michigan athletes that the athletes’ attorney plans to appeal. Additional sections describe criticism of Chief Justice John Roberts’ leadership, the Supreme Court’s planned actions on cert petitions, a history lesson from the Burger era involving Nixon, and efforts by Venezuelan citizens to keep protected status through a Supreme Court filing asking the Court to leave in place a federal judge’s order.

The passage describes an electronic edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS)* and its features, including full content access without internet connectivity, full-text search, bookmarking, and note-taking. It notes efforts to preserve fidelity to the original printed editions and recommends citing document numbers instead of page numbers for persistence; for older volumes, page numbers include corresponding document numbers in brackets. It also states that the Office of the Historian aims to make the ebook error-free and provides an email address for feedback.

The passage then outlines the principles and scope for compiling and editing FRUS volumes under Department of State Regulation 045, including requirements for historical objectivity, no unauthorized text changes or omissions of major facts, and permissible omissions for clearance reasons. It identifies responsibilities and personnel involved in preparing *Foreign Relations, 1942, Volume II, Europe*, including editors and compilers for specific sections, and notes publishing services roles in copy editing, proofreading, and index preparation.

Salem residents are driving to Woodburn to find bottled water after the city announced that its drinking water supply is contaminated by low levels of cyanotoxins from an algae bloom in Detroit Lake. The Oregon Office of Emergency Management is not coordinating water distribution points, and grocery stores report a growing shortage, telling residents to keep calling retailers. Major retailers expect water shipments but some are out of water. The city advises that children under 6, people with compromised immune systems, those receiving dialysis, people with pre-existing liver conditions, pets, pregnant women and nursing mothers, and other sensitive people should not drink the water, and should use bottled water for drinking, infant formula, ice, and preparing food and beverages. Price-gauging reports appeared on social media, and many local businesses have closed due to the contamination.

Eurozone stock markets fell on Friday as the euro pressured the US dollar and traders waited for key US jobs data. Germany’s DAX dropped 1.7% to 12,785.16, and Deutsche Bank shares fell 6.21% after the lender was pushed into the red. France’s CAC 40 fell 1.6% to 5,364.98, and the pan-European STOXX 600 fell 1.4% to 388.07. Outside the eurozone, London’s FTSE 100 declined 0.6% to 7,443.43. Analysts said the sell-off accelerated, with attention focused on US nonfarm payrolls and expectations that a strong report could support further increases in US borrowing costs.

The passage introduces LTLf learning, where an LTLf formula is learned from positive and negative finite traces by finding a separator of minimal size. It surveys LTLf learning motivations and methods across software engineering, control/robotics, and AI, and discusses state-of-the-art tools and scalability issues. The paper proposes scaling by treating Boolean operators differently from temporal operators using a new framework that combines bounded enumeration of LTLf formulas with a subroutine called Boolean Set Cover, which constructs solutions as Boolean combinations (using ∧ and ∨) of enumerated formulas. The passage defines LTLf syntax/semantics, the LTLf learning problem, the VFB baseline approach (including characteristic tables and observational equivalence), and the Boolean Set Cover problem with related concepts such as domination and a divide-and-conquer meta-algorithm. It describes an algorithm for Boolean Set Cover using beam search, and presents experiments comparing the resulting tool Bolt to the Scarlet CPU approach and a 2024 GPU-based algorithm, reporting improved performance and formula sizes, along with ablation results showing the impact of Boolean Set Cover. The passage concludes with future directions and the release of code and benchmark suites.

On February 9, 2017, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting its results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing states that a press release announcing these results was issued that day and is attached as Exhibit 99.1, and that CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress is attached as Exhibit 99.2 and will be posted to http://investor.nvidia.com after the report. The press release and CFO commentary are furnished and not deemed filed for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act or subject to related liabilities, and the information is not incorporated by reference in other SEC filings.

The passage explains key offensive positions in American football and their roles. The offense’s goal is to advance the ball downfield into the end zone, or kick a field goal if necessary. It describes the quarterback as the leader who handles every play, analyzes defenses, passes or hands off, and can change plays before the snap via audibles. It outlines the running back’s duties in carrying the ball, following blocks, finding gaps, holding onto the ball, and also catching and blocking. It presents the tight end as a versatile player who blocks and runs routes, including “sniffer” and “attached” tight end types. It covers the offensive line as a core blocking unit made up of tackles, guards, and a center, detailing what each group does, including protecting the quarterback and communicating defensive issues. It also describes wide receivers’ responsibilities to catch passes, run routes, create space, block effectively, and the main receiver types: split end (X), flanker (Z), and slot receiver.

The passage advises ending a job interview promptly by standing up, leaving without lingering, and not adding extra stories. It says successful candidates show confidence, focus more on the opportunity than themselves, and ask needed questions without seeming desperate. It recommends leaving with a quick handshake and saying, “Great conversation -- it was wonderful to meet you,” and avoiding questions about when they will respond or make a decision, since such timelines cannot be known in advance and may lead to being told a made-up date.

Research by Adam Anderson at Cornell University, published in *Psychological Science*, examines how eye expressions help people interpret others’ emotions and mental states. The study argues that emotions are read from eye expressions through features such as eye openness, eyebrow shape, and wrinkles, with narrowed eyes linked to discrimination-related emotions like disgust and suspicion, and open eyes linked to sensitivity-related emotions like fear and awe. Participants viewing eyes paired with emotion-related words consistently matched the six basic emotions (sadness, disgust, anger, joy, fear, surprise), and eye features—especially eye openness—were most closely related to reading mental states. Additional studies found the eye region provided more robust emotion indications than other facial areas, supporting Charles Darwin’s theory that expressions originated for sensory function and later became used for communication.

The primary and secondary education department in Bengaluru has not announced summer camps for state government school students this year, originally planned to start on April 10. A senior official said the camps may be canceled due to a shortage of funds, with teachers also busy with SSLC evaluation and assembly election-related work. The official added that summer camps cannot be held after elections because schools will reopen, and an official cancellation announcement will be made soon. The department had run summer camps under the “Swalpa odu, swalpa moju” programme since 2017-18, including last year’s five-week programme at 7,049 government schools for students who completed classes 5 and 6, with instruction in Mathematics and Science, extracurricular activities, and mid-day meals.

A study commissioned by an eastern Alberta town says closing the federal Immigration, Refugee and Citizenship Case Processing Centre in Vegreville would be economically damaging. The report estimates Vegreville could permanently lose up to 420 people (7.3% of its population), with impacts including lower property values, higher unemployment, fewer students in local schools, and a potential 30% decrease in home prices. The federal government plans to relocate the centre—employing 236 people—from Vegreville to Edmonton by the end of 2018 to improve service. Mayor Myron Hayduk criticizes the decision, and union representatives met with Minister Ahmed Hussen, with the union arguing the Vegreville centre does not need to close to expand operations in Edmonton.

Brendon Naidoo, boyfriend of DJ Zinhle, was granted R50,000 bail at the Alexandra Magistrate Court. State prosecutor Jimmy Shongwe confirmed that Naidoo faces multiple counts of fraud after people claimed he conned them out of millions in a foreign-exchange trading scheme. Magistrate Renier Boshoff ordered Naidoo to report to the Sandton Police station twice a week between 6am and 6pm. Naidoo was arrested on April 8 and held at Johannesburg Central Prison, and he was scheduled to return to court on May 5.

The passage describes a study of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in untreated wastewater from the Western Uttar Pradesh (WUP) region of India during 2020–2021 amid the COVID-19 pandemic. It notes that COVID-19-related antibiotic use, lack of wastewater treatment, and poor disposal of antibiotics can increase AMR. Wastewater samples from three zones were collected and used to isolate Enterobacteriaceae, including Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and then test for antibiotic susceptibility, ESBL production, and multidrug resistance (MDR), with attention to colistin resistance. From 150 Enterobacteriaceae isolates, 74% showed resistance to one or more antibiotics and 79.3% of resistant isolates were ESBL producers. MDR was observed in E. coli (57.14%) and K. pneumoniae (28.57%), with zone-wise differences reported in resistance patterns. The study concludes that diverse resistance patterns, including resistance to last-resort antibiotics like colistin, were present in Indian wastewater during COVID-19, with about 80% of isolates being multidrug-resistant, and recommends periodic AMR surveys and molecular studies.

Three academics affiliated with U.S. universities—John Clarke (UC Berkeley), Michel Devoret (Yale and UC Santa Barbara), and John Martinis (UCSB)—have been awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit, sharing nearly $1.2 million. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said they used experiments with an electronic circuit made of superconductors to show quantum mechanical properties on a macroscopic scale. Olle Eriksson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics, said the work highlights ongoing surprises in quantum mechanics and its usefulness as the foundation of digital technology.

The passage says job interviews vary widely, from banal ones to complex multi-stage processes with psychometric testing and unusual trials. It focuses on interviews with self-described “disruptors,” who reject traditional questions and instead ask unconventional prompts like imagining yourself as a tinned vegetable, reaching “peak awesome,” or solving riddles, often with quirky interviewers and even a lemur. It advises that after responding to these “self-indulgent” questions and when they ask if you have questions, you should respond forcefully.

The passage provides technical guidance for power-supply filtering, reset behavior, system clocking, and several peripheral-related interfaces and timing considerations. It recommends using ferrite beads and multiple capacitors placed close to device pins (with specific capacitance sizes/placement guidance) and warns against excessive capacitance that could affect power-sequencing and reset timing. It describes multiple reset types (POR, external warm reset, emulation warm reset, watchdog reset, software cold/warm resets, and test reset), including required assertion/de-assertion sequences, effects on modules and pins, RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior, and pin states at reset. It outlines clock input options (DEV/AUX via crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS, SERDES clock requirements, and external clock inputs/outputs), PLL bring-up in bypass mode, and general PLL/clock-frequency constraints. The passage also summarizes interrupt controller capabilities, AC timing test assumptions, and interface overviews including DCAN, EDMA, AET/trace concepts, GPIO, GPMC/ELM for external memories, HDMI and TMDS/DDR-related layout considerations, HDVPSS features, video DAC routing guidance, and I2C/MDIO/CPSW Ethernet subsystem elements.

Anthony Davis and Eric Simmons appealed their convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine in excess of three grams; Davis also appealed his sentence. The court affirmed, holding there was sufficient evidence of an agreement to deal in more than three grams despite each individual sale to a confidential informant involving less than three grams, and it rejected the claim that the verdicts were fatally inconsistent. The court also affirmed Davis’s enhanced 40-year sentence, finding that any Blakely/Apprendi issue regarding aggravators was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt because the same sentence would have been imposed based on his criminal history alone.

Construction of Fort Buford began in 1866 at the confluence of the Missouri and Yellowstone Rivers near Williston, and it served as a military post until 1881, when Sitting Bull surrendered. Soldiers provided much of their own food, and shortages contributed to scurvy; there were no trained cooks, so cooking duties rotated every 10 days, which led Surgeon J.V.D. Middleton to criticize the meals. Supplies arrived by steamboat but were interrupted when the Missouri froze. The passage also describes boredom, alcohol, self-inflicted wounds, and a 1876 “Notes from Buford” report mentioning insanity cases in the hospital and the library’s holdings. Fort Buford was later abandoned, but in 1963 a museum opened in the old headquarters building and other parts of the post were restored.

Flippy, a burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has started work as a grill cook at Caliburger’s Pasadena restaurant. The CEO of Cali Group notes the job is hot, greasy, and dirty, but Flippy does not face issues such as low wages, meager benefits, or long hours. The robot can reportedly grill 150 burgers per hour and was developed with Caliburger over two years to operate in existing commercial kitchen layouts alongside staff. In its current version, a human coworker places patties on the grill and adds cheese and extras, while Flippy handles other tasks using thermal sensors, 3-D sensors, cameras, ticket orders, a robotic arm, and interchangeable tools. Caliburger has exclusive use rights for six months; afterward other vendors may buy the robot. Flippy costs about $60,000 per unit now, with expansion planned in the U.S. after a trial period.

The passage describes reset isolation features for PCI Express and an Ethernet switch, including how software and hardware should handle resets, bus re-enumeration, and related interrupt behavior. It also covers device reset behaviors for pins, power-domain warm/cold reset triggers, and reset-related timing and clocking considerations, followed by sections on device clocks/PLLs and interrupt controllers. Additional content includes general peripheral information such as DCAN, EDMA, Trace, JTAG, EMAC switch/MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, and brief overviews of HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, image subsystem interfaces, and DDR2/DDR3 memory controller and routing requirements.

John Essey and his family use an Internet of things setup in their home north of Pittsburgh, where sensors detect issues like basement water or sink leaks and allow control of lights and thermostats. Critics worry these devices may be insecure and used for surveillance for profit. Gierad Laput of Carnegie Mellon notes two approaches to making homes smart—buying many expensive connected appliances that may not work well together, or adding many sensors, which can be unwieldy and visually obtrusive. Laput and his team developed a single wall-plugged sensor that uses a small circuit board to detect multiple environmental factors and sends the information wirelessly to a computer that can identify activities like a running blender or a turned-on light. Internet security expert Bruce Schneier argues that surveillance is a business model of the Internet of things and that device makers often do not prioritize security, raising concerns about data collection and potential real-world risks.

Deutsche Telekom, Nokia, and the Hamburg Port Authority announced they will begin testing 5G in an industrial environment in the Port of Hamburg. The trial covers an 8,000-hectare area and will test various 5G functionality, including network slicing, under live conditions for the first time in Germany. Use cases include traffic lights management, real-time data processing from mobile sensors, and virtual reality monitoring of critical infrastructure. An antenna installed on the Hamburg television tower will provide connectivity.

The passage discusses playoff success based on focusing on one game at a time rather than the big picture, with the team needing only two more wins to advance. It highlights a player who plays hard, avoids mistakes, and provides leadership, and notes that ice conditions are poor and can affect play and getting to the puck. The author also describes sharing a Stanley Cup with loved ones and bringing it to a children’s cancer hospital to make the kids happy. It mentions paying attention to a talented opponent from the previous series and contrasts an earlier series approach—prioritizing not getting scored on and playing defensively—with the team having more offensive power this time. The passage concludes that the team is close to advancing, facing the hardest minutes so far, and aims to play a solid, successful game tomorrow night.

The passage is largely a data extract from Apple Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended June 26, 2021, including SEC filing details and financial statement information. It reports third- and nine-month results with net sales totaling $81,434 million (three months ended June 26, 2021) and $282,457 million (nine months ended June 26, 2021), net income of $21,744 million and $74,129 million, and diluted earnings per share of $1.30 and $4.38. It also provides unaudited balance sheet figures as of June 26, 2021 (total assets $329,840 million; total liabilities $265,560 million; total shareholders’ equity $64,280 million), cash flow information for the nine months ended June 26, 2021, and selected notes covering accounting policies (including revenue recognition and deferred revenue), financial instruments and derivatives, income taxes (including uncertain tax positions and the European Commission state aid decision), debt and share repurchases, and segment information by geography.

Prosecutors dismissed the four most serious charges against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer in a Vermont school shooting plot case, citing a state Supreme Court ruling that made the prosecution “untenable.” The state dropped attempted murder and aggravated assault with a weapon and will proceed with two lesser charges: criminal threatening and carrying a dangerous weapon. Sawyer pleaded not guilty, had been held without bail after his Feb. 15 arrest, and had his bail set at $100,000, which the prosecutor is asking to keep. Authorities said Sawyer kept a diary with detailed plans and was alerted by a friend who provided Facebook messages; the defense said he took no concrete steps. The Supreme Court ruled that “preparation alone” was insufficient for an attempt at aggravated murder. After reviewing the affidavit, Gov. Phil Scott signed bills that raised the age for buying firearms, banned high-capacity magazines, and made it easier to remove guns from people posing threats, changes that would not apply retroactively to Sawyer’s case.

The passage says that since 2000 only 12 albums have spent 10 or more weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, a weekly US album chart. It notes that Taylor Swift and Morgan Wallen each have three albums on the list, while Adele has two, and describes the longest-running No. 1 albums in chronological order, including Swift’s “Fearless” (11 weeks) and “The Tortured Poets Department” (later returning to total 17 weeks), Adele’s “21” (24 weeks), and Wallen’s “Dangerous: The Double Album” and “One Thing at a Time,” alongside Bad Bunny’s “Un Verano Sin Ti” and SZA’s “SOS.”

Stocks rallied Monday on better-than-expected quarterly earnings despite an anthrax scare, with major U.S. indexes rising. Bonds were mixed and the dollar strengthened. Enron shares fell about 20% after the company said the SEC requested information about “certain related party transactions,” including partnerships run by its CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC request followed reported losses and charges tied to limited partnerships, and Enron said it would cooperate; related derivative and class action lawsuits were also filed alleging breaches of fiduciary duties and securities fraud. Separate reporting described UniPrime signing a letter of intent for a wind energy park ground lease involving an Enron subsidiary.

Clio founder and CEO Jack Newton discusses Clio’s $1 billion acquisition of vLex and upcoming Clio Cloud Conference. The vLex deal adds near start-to-finish capabilities, covering intake, research, drafting, case management, communications, accounting, motion practice, and billing. The acquisition follows several years of growth, including acquisitions of ShareDo and Lawyaw, and Clio is preparing for the Oct. 16–17 conference in Boston with keynote speakers including Esther Perel and JJ Velazquez.

The Secretary said negotiations in the Shultz-Gromyko channel could be discussed, but the US preferred conducting INF and START negotiations in Geneva, and he wanted to see what developed before deciding how to treat arms control in future meetings. Dobrynin suggested expanding bilateral cooperation and proposed inventorying bilateral agreements that had been cancelled, lapsed, ongoing, or close to agreement; the Secretary agreed and would discuss this at a next meeting, with Dobrynin contacting Eagleburger. Dobrynin also mentioned other bilateral security talks (radiological and chemical weapons, conventional arms transfers, and Indian Ocean naval deployments) and broader issues including the CSCE Madrid meeting, South Africa, the Middle East, nonproliferation, and the Warsaw Pact’s Prague Declaration. The Secretary said exchanges on South Africa had produced little but should continue as warranted, the United States would not go beyond previous Middle East discussions, and Washington bilaterals on nonproliferation were useful and should continue, with openness to hear about the Prague Declaration and its ignored proposals. The Secretary stressed additional regional issues (Poland, Kampuchea, Afghanistan, Central America) and human rights as central and to be handled practically without publicity. Dobrynin characterized arms control as the most important progress area and wanted START and INF on the next discussion list; the Secretary agreed to keep primary negotiations in Geneva but would not object to discussing START and INF, noted confidence-building measures, and reiterated the need to keep human rights and regional issues on the agenda. Eagleburger reminded participants that Bessmertnykh would soon leave for Moscow, and Americans present wished him luck.

Tyreek Hill suffered a leg injury against the Jets on a play with just over 13 minutes left in the third quarter, after his left leg was out of place. He was taken to the locker room and then to a local hospital for imaging and evaluation. The Dolphins officially tagged the injury as a dislocated knee; reports said it may involve multiple ligament tears, and coach Mike McDaniel said Hill would stay overnight and undergo further tests. An exact return timeline is not available yet, and a dislocated knee was described as expected to be season-ending, with Hill not expected to return in 2025.

The passage describes how citizenship education, originally tied to building national identity, is now presented as a process for equipping students with knowledge, skills, and understanding to participate responsibly in democratic life, including globally. It argues that science education is closely connected to citizenship education through scientific literacy, socio-scientific issues, and the roles of science in addressing global challenges such as climate change and pandemics. A European Commission report is cited emphasizing the need for science to inform policy and citizens in trustworthy ways and to support responsible, evidence-based decision-making.

The passage then focuses on Turkey, outlining shifts in citizenship education policy since the 1920s and changes since the 2000s, including offering “citizenship” as a standalone course only at grade 4 and making social studies responsible at secondary level, which is said to weaken links between science and citizenship education. It notes that Turkey’s science curriculum adopted an STSE approach (updated in 2018) and includes goals emphasizing scientific, technological, and environmental literacy, but that the science–citizenship relationship remains “tenuous” and research is sparse.

The study described uses qualitative methods, reviewing the science curriculum and interviewing eight science teachers to examine (1) what citizenship education aspects are included in the science curriculum and (2) how teachers perceive their role in fostering students’ citizenship skills. Thematic analysis identifies major themes—scientific literacy, technology, society, environment, values and skills, and problems—showing that teachers most strongly link science to citizenship through environmental issues and scientific literacy, while also discussing society-related topics through socio-scientific issues. Teachers report challenges in practice, including exam-focused schooling, limited resources, and classroom conditions, which they say hinder science education from fully achieving citizenship-related goals. The passage concludes with implications for policy and teaching, recommending an explicit citizenship-skills emphasis in science curricula, stronger integration of socio-scientific and environmental education, and teacher training to implement citizenship skills in science classes, aligned with SDG 2030 aims.

UFC 216 takes place Saturday in Las Vegas, where the city is still recovering from a mass shooting that killed 58 people and injured nearly 500. Dana White said the UFC pledged $1 million to help victims and their families, and urged people outside Las Vegas not to be afraid to visit. The main event is an interim lightweight title bout: Tony Ferguson (nine-fight win streak) fights Kevin Lee. The winner could potentially face Conor McGregor to unify the belt. The co-main event features Demetrious Johnson, aiming for an 11th title defense, against Ray Borg, who replaced Borg’s withdrawal from a previously scheduled UFC 215 fight due to illness.

The passage discusses AI literacy in education, emphasizing early childhood as a key time for developing digital competencies, engagement, and motivation. It describes how educational robots supported by AI and robotics can enrich learning environments, support various aspects of child development, and promote inclusive education and skills such as computational thinking, social-emotional reciprocity, and inquiry literacies. The text outlines examples of AI-based educational robots used in preschool and notes that teacher competencies, curriculum alignment, and safe, accessible implementation are essential. It then presents a study on how future preschool and primary school teachers perceive robots and their pedagogical implications, using a mixed-method approach based on students’ hand-drawn robot depictions (Draw-A-Robot Test) and open-ended responses. The results report a small number of misconceptions (often portraying robots as conventional electronic devices), the most common robot appearances (animal-shaped “digital toys” and typical/mechanical objects), dominant perceived functions (educational and assistive), and differences in the reasons for robot depictions between future preschool and primary teachers.

The Green Bay Packers agreed to a deal with veteran tackle Byron Bell, who previously played for Carolina, Tennessee, and Dallas. Bell will join a Packers offensive line with questions at starting right tackle, a role Bryan Bulaga has held for much of the past seven seasons but who suffered a torn ACL last year and likely won’t practice until training camp. During the offseason, speculation that Bulaga could be cut did not materialize, and both general manager Brian Gutekunst and coach Mike McCarthy indicated during the draft that Bulaga is part of their plans. Other options mentioned include Jason Spriggs and Kyle Murphy, both dealing with injuries.

Out of bounds situations are important in the game, and teams should be prepared to inbound the ball from the baseline, sideline, and full court while understanding the out of bounds rules. Out of bounds plays should focus first on successfully inbounding the ball and then getting it to the best players for high-percentage shots, with plays kept simple and practiced rather than improvised. Successful out of bounds plays rely on executing cuts, screens, and passes precisely, anticipating defensive positioning, using counters, and maintaining defensive balance and safety outlets. The passage also outlines specific throw-in rules, including a five-second limit, restrictions on when the inbounder can touch the ball, requirements after made shots and timeouts, and prohibitions such as throwing over the backboard or directly into the basket, plus a technical foul condition when a defender touches the ball behind the out of bounds vertical plane. It suggests coaching tips like testing players on rule knowledge.

The passage reviews experimental studies of neutrino oscillations and the main sources of neutrinos: supernovae, Big Bang relic neutrinos (difficult to observe due to low energies), neutrinos from cosmic ray showers, solar neutrinos, accelerator-produced neutrinos, and reactor neutrinos (also used to monitor nuclear activity). It compares experimental parameters such as baseline length, neutrino energy, and sensitivity to mass-squared differences for solar, atmospheric, reactor, and accelerator neutrinos. It describes historical solar-neutrino observations where early experiments saw fewer electron neutrinos than expected, while SNO found the total neutrino rate matched expectations, supporting flavor oscillations. For atmospheric neutrinos, produced from pion/kaon decays followed by muon decay, the expected muon-to-electron neutrino ratio is disrupted by oscillations, leading to disappearance of muon-like neutrinos. Accelerator experiments use near and far detectors to measure flux and oscillation effects, with examples like T2K showing evidence for oscillations. Reactor experiments study anti-electron neutrino disappearance using inverse beta decay, with multiple experiments probing oscillations by measuring survival probability versus distance over energy, particularly from the 2000s onward.

The Medina City School District is asking voters on May 8 for a 5.2-mill permanent substitute levy to replace a current 5.9-mill operating levy that expires in December. Kids First Medina held a rally on Medina’s square to raise awareness, with speakers emphasizing the levy is not a new tax and that a bond issue will fall off tax bills on Dec. 31, resulting in a slight decrease. Superintendent Aaron Sable said the levy would help maintain current programs and add others, including reinstating the high school’s French curriculum and funding an all-day kindergarten program offered free to all families. City Council members also spoke in support, with one stating strong school systems are a major factor in attracting people to a community.

The passage describes how Industrial Revolution 4.0, driven by artificial intelligence and machine learning, is influencing education and supports a shift toward Education 4.0. It discusses the need for new classroom pedagogies, changing assessments from memory-based to skill-based, and using games and gamification in line with India’s National Education Policy (2020). It explains that digital games can promote meaningful, joyful learning, support competency-based teaching, and provide elements such as challenges, rules, feedback, and multiple solutions that align with instructional design. Two approaches for Digital Game Based Learning (DGBL) are noted: using existing commercial games or designing customized games based on learning outcomes. Digital games are also presented as assessment tools that can offer flexible, media-rich assessment and reduce teacher and student load. A central concept is Stealth Assessment (SA), where learners are assessed during gameplay using data from digital traces and AI/ML algorithms to model competencies and provide learners with new challenges and immediate feedback. The passage outlines SA’s key elements, including Evidence Centered Design (ECD), machine learning, and formative feedback, and emphasizes that SA development requires a multidisciplinary approach. Finally, it lists challenges for integrating DGBL, including concerns about efficiency, the need for strong research evidence, potential cognitive load effects, difficulty-level calibration issues, and the early stage of validating reliability and contribution.

The passage describes the speaker’s long journey to a current point and their excitement about it, saying they have not lost their “butterflies,” especially in Colorado. They compare these feelings to when they were a kid winning championships, noting that the feelings do not change as you get older. They say they enjoyed playing and focused on sticking to their normal routine—having a pre-game skate, working on a few things, then working on their sticks—while trying not to overthink to avoid mental fatigue.

On Friday, Feb. 10, APU students attended The GIG, one of the university’s two formal dances, at La Cañada Flintridge Country Club. The dance, themed after “La La Land,” featured semi-formal attire, ticket purchases through Communiversity for $20 each, and check-in with tickets and identification. The event had two dance floors with different ambiances: one with a DJ playing current hits and another with a live jazz combo. Students could also enjoy activities such as free cartoon drawings on an iPad, a designated photo area with a professional photographer, an outdoor deck with views, and an open room with a grand piano for student musicians. Students described the music, locations, and dual ambiances as memorable, and the event is described as one of APU’s best dances yet.

A court in Kochi convicted a migrant labourer from Assam, Muhammed Ameerul Islam, for the rape and murder of a 30-year-old Dalit law student in Kerala. Ernakulam Principal Sessions Court judge N Anil Kumar will pronounce the punishment quantum tomorrow. Islam was found guilty under IPC sections including 302 (murder) and 376 (rape), and related provisions about causing death or leaving the woman in a persistent vegetative state. He was not found guilty under IPC 201 or certain SC/ST (prevention of atrocities) provisions. The trial involved 100 witnesses and the hearing was completed on December 6. Islam was charged for an incident in Perumbavoor on April 28, 2016, and was arrested from Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, 50 days later. Police cited blood-stained footwear found near the victim’s house as key evidence.

The passage argues that increasing AI regulation by governments has made AI policy and compliance important for the AI development life cycle, but these discussions are largely missing from computer science curricula. It proposes a framework to integrate AI policy discussions into CS courses. It synthesizes AI policy developments in the United States and the European Union, noting US efforts are heterogeneous and not yet a comprehensive federal law, with recent policy volatility reflected by the rescission of Biden’s 2023 executive order and Trump’s subsequent executive order. For the EU, it describes the EU AI Act, including risk-based categorization, prohibitions on certain practices, and added transparency requirements for general-purpose models. The passage highlights three themes for AI education: rapidly changing policy landscapes, translating abstract policy goals into technical controls, and cross-border regulatory impacts (e.g., the “Brussels Effect” from GDPR). The proposed framework uses a continuum of socio-political, translational, and technical perspectives, combined with dimensions of scope, power, and agency, organized through guiding questions to help students connect policy demands to technical specifications and consider different stakeholders and their influence.

When a penalty kick is awarded, it is a restart: at the moment the ball is kicked it is live and in play, and play resumes immediately if it is blocked or saved or rebounds back into the field. If the ball is not in the goal or out of bounds, attacking players (other than the kicker and goalkeeper) must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the penalty mark, inside the field of play, and outside the penalty area, positioned in accordance with Law 14. Players must get into position immediately and react once the ball is in play, typically moving toward the goal for any rebound. The referee signals only after all players are properly positioned and conditions are met; players should not move into the penalty area or penalty arc until after the ball is touched and clearly moves forward. Attacking teammates must follow up on saves, blocks, or rebounds, and the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player touches it. Examples describe Alex Morgan freezing after her kick was blocked, leading to the opportunity being lost. If the ball is secured by the goalkeeper, attacking players must switch to defensive mode. The passage also notes that sanctions apply if penalty-kick procedures are not followed, including retaking if the ball enters the goal or restarting with an indirect free kick if it does not.

An Italian man, Luca Traini, opened fire on African migrants in Macerata on Saturday, injuring six people before being captured, according to police, who said it was racially motivated. Traini was seized while carrying an Italian flag; onlookers said he made a fascist salute. Police said he also fired shots at offices of the ruling center-left Democratic Party (PD) but caused no injuries. Political figures including Matteo Salvini, Matteo Renzi, and Paolo Gentiloni responded, calling for security and calm while denouncing violence. The attack followed days after the arrest of a Nigerian migrant in connection with the death of Pamela Mastropietro, whose body was found in suitcases near Macerata, amid rising tensions and debate over immigration and asylum.

Rutgers historian Mark Bray, who wrote a 2017 book about antifa, says he has been targeted by far-right influencers after a weeks-long online campaign and an antifa executive order by President Donald Trump. Bray received dozens of death threats, including messages that listed his home address and said he would be killed in front of his students. He says he decided to move to Europe when their home address became known and told students he would be relocating. At an airport while traveling to Spain, Bray says United Airlines canceled his reservation after security and boarding-pass checks, preventing him from boarding; he was later rebooked and planned to try again. A Rutgers spokesperson said the university is gathering more information, and Bray reported the threats to local and university police. Bray says he plans to stay in Spain until the end of the academic year.

The passage describes features and configuration of a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) and related analog front-end blocks, including an antialiasing second-order low-pass filter and an ADC driver requirement for charging and discharging ADC input sample-and-hold capacitors. It explains reference operation with internal or external 4.096V sources, including decoupling and buffering guidance, plus internal reference accuracy, thermal effects from solder reflow, and temperature drift. It outlines the ADC transfer function (straight-binary output), alarm features (input and AVDD alarms with thresholds, hysteresis, flags, and output options), and multiSPI digital interface behavior including data transfer frames, command handling, and supported read/write protocols (legacy single/dual SDO-x and source-synchronous modes). It also summarizes register map contents for configuration, alarms, and data output control, and briefly mentions application and power/decoupling recommendations and low-power modes (NAP and power-down).

The passage describes a unified multiscale framework for predicting GaN and III-nitride epitaxy growth kinetics from solid–melt interface energetics. It argues that atomistic interactions at the solid–melt interface govern growth rates and morphology in liquid phase epitaxy and VLS growth, where a liquid group-III droplet (e.g., Ga) captures group-V atoms and mediates their incorporation. The authors use MD simulations and well-tempered metadynamics to study ordered liquid Ga at GaN(s)-Ga(l) interfaces, quantify free-energy landscapes for N adsorption and migration at Ga-polar and N-polar interfaces, and identify mechanisms such as “Ga lubrication” that lower N migration barriers compared with a clean surface. They incorporate these barriers into kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to show N-flux-dependent growth modes, and develop a diffusion-controlled continuous model (based on chemical potential gradients) to predict facet-dependent growth rates. Growth experiments using MBE on Ga/GaN particles are analyzed by TEM/HRTEM, and the predicted facet-normal growth rates (0.01–0.04 nm/s) match experimental facet trends. The work concludes that for systems with low solubility of key elements (like N in liquid Ga), the interfacial free-energy profile for adatom adsorption and migration determines growth kinetics, and the parameter-free workflow can be applied to other low-solubility III-V/catalyst systems.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 17, 2016. On May 20, 2016, it entered into a new credit agreement with Bank of America, N.A. and other lenders, replacing a prior 2014 agreement. The credit agreement provides a $3.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility for three years (extendable up to three additional one-year terms), with initial interest at LIBOR plus 0.60% and a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts (potentially higher if credit ratings are downgraded). Borrowings may be used for working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions, and other corporate purposes; there were no borrowings outstanding at the time of filing. The credit agreement includes customary representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default, and has no financial covenants.  

On May 17, 2016, Amazon held its annual shareholders’ meeting. Directors were elected based on the vote totals shown for ten nominees. Ernst & Young LLP’s appointment as independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2016 was ratified. Three shareholder proposals—on sustainability reporting, a human rights report, and a report concerning corporate political contributions—were not approved, based on the vote totals provided.

It also covers effects of economic data and policy expectations, including NFP-related moves, upcoming BoE and Fed events, tariff and growth concerns, and technical levels such as support and resistance zones for USD/JPY, GBP/USD, and BTC/USD. The passage says Nigerians living abroad sent $21.9 billion home in 2017, up 12% from $19.64 billion in 2016, according to the World Bank’s migration and development report. It also states this amount is the highest in Sub-Saharan Africa and the fifth highest overall.

On April 7, 2015, NVIDIA’s Compensation Committee adopted the Fiscal Year 2016 Variable Compensation Plan, which allows eligible executive officers to earn cash bonus awards based on NVIDIA’s achievement of corporate objectives during fiscal year 2016. Fiscal year 2016 is identified as the year the fiscal year ends. Eligibility requires the participant to remain an employee through the payment date unless otherwise determined by the Compensation Committee. Corporate Targets were set based on specified fiscal year 2016 revenue and include threshold and maximum levels. The plan’s target variable cash compensation for named executive officers lists Jen-Hsun Huang at $1,000,000 (100% of base salary), Colette M. Kress at $275,000 (35%), Ajay K. Puri at $475,000 (54%), David M. Shannon at $200,000 (25%), and Debora Shoquist at $150,000 (21%). The plan is filed as Exhibit 10.1 and incorporated by reference. The report was signed on April 9, 2015.

Australia’s Sino Gas & Energy Holdings Ltd agreed to a A$530 million takeover offer from U.S. private equity firm Lone Star, saying risks in China justified putting the bid to a vote. Sino Gas shareholders would receive A$0.25 per share, a 19% premium. Lone Star is backing two large gas projects in China, where Sino Gas recently secured the first approvals needed to develop them. The board unanimously recommended the offer, though some brokers were surprised and small investors were unimpressed, with one saying he would vote against. Sino Gas shares rose before easing, and shareholders are expected to vote in late August or September; the deal requires 75% approval of votes cast.

Xi Jinping told China’s National People’s Congress that China must not be complacent, saying only socialism can save the country. Speaking at the closing session, he urged lawmakers to act in the people’s interest, called the people “the real heroes,” emphasized unity and warned against separatist attempts, including references to Taiwan. The meeting included lifting presidential term limits, confirming Xi for a potentially lifelong presidency, and reconfirmed his second presidential term. The NPC also confirmed “Xi Jinping Thought” in the constitution, set up a new anti-corruption agency, and appointed key positions.
