Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.2% to 7,476.12 points on Friday after disappointing earnings from BT and AstraZeneca contributed to a lacklustre week. BT shares dropped more than 5% to a five-year low over concerns about growth and its pension scheme, while AstraZeneca shares fell 1.7% due to a disappointing profit outlook. Commodities-related stocks rose, with miners gaining on a firmer copper price and oil stocks advancing as oil prices extended gains. On the mid-cap index, Capita rebounded more than 5% after a Morgan Stanley upgrade to “equal-weight,” following a profit warning and dividend suspension.

A Treasury minister, Mel Stride, said Britain’s fish fingers will be “safe in the hands” of the Government during Brexit talks. He made the pledge after Labour’s Mel Onn urged assurances about customs arrangements to prevent delays to the time-sensitive fish trade and processing industry in Great Grimsby. Onn said continuing sensible customs arrangements are essential for Great Grimsby’s processing sector and 5,000 jobs, and asked whether the minister could assure the public that their fish fingers will be safe after leaving the EU.

The passage describes a continuation patent application and provides background on modern data centers generating large volumes of machine-generated data that are difficult to index and search semantically. It outlines an event-based data intake and query system where machine data from many sources is parsed into timestamped events stored in a data store, with flexible “late-binding” schemas applied during search time. It explains how events can be searched by keywords and fields using extraction rules (including regex rules), and how common field names support a common information model across disparate sources. The passage describes how Education 4.0 brought information technology into education, creating challenges for language education in Indonesia due to reliance on face-to-face interaction, but also enabling alternatives to in-person learning such as online platforms, mobile learning, asynchronous learning, blended learning, broadcast media, new assessment methods, parental involvement, and flexible policies. It states that information technology can improve language learning by helping students learn languages more effectively, offering more opportunities to use language learning strategies, and accelerating digital learning during the COVID-19 pandemic, while emphasizing that technology should support teaching methods rather than replace them. The passage outlines research methods using qualitative descriptive analysis and literature review/observation to develop an operable framework for IT and management strategies in Indonesian language education. It summarizes reported challenges in virtual learning (e.g., technological proficiency, student engagement, resource access, assessment difficulties, the digital divide, motivation and self-regulation, and reduced social interaction) and gives examples of responses using professional development, AI tools, VR, gamification, and community support. It also presents various technological innovations relevant to education (e.g., AR, VR, IoT, AI, LMS, gamification, and ASR) and explains how ASR and task- and game-based learning can support vocabulary and pronunciation through real-time feedback and engaging practice. Finally, it discusses management strategies (digital platform integration, teacher training, language support tools, collaboration and virtual exchange, cloud infrastructure, mobile learning, data-driven decision-making, and inclusive IT policies) and concludes that IT integration offers advantages but requires careful management, attention to teaching methods, and addressing unequal access and resistance.

The court granted Defendants’ motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiffs’ motions to strike. The case involves Melissa Jennings, the sole remaining plaintiff, who was on UNC’s women’s soccer team as a goalkeeper from August 1996 until she was dismissed in May 1998. She alleged that Coach Anson Dorrance and assistant coach William Palladino made sexually inappropriate and humiliating comments during team activities, and that Dorrance made direct inquiries about her personal life on two occasions, including a hotel-room meeting where Dorrance allegedly asked, “Who are you fucking?” Jennings also claimed Dorrance dismissed her from the team based on inadequate performance, while Dorrance said he dismissed her for failure to contribute physically, academically, and socially.

The court denied Jennings’ request to strike Defendants’ amended answer and enter default judgment, finding no bad faith or clear factual inconsistency. The court also denied the motion to strike exhibits C through H to Dorrance’s affidavit, concluding they were properly authenticated and qualified as records of regularly conducted activity.

On the merits, the court held there was no genuine issue of material fact and granted summary judgment on Jennings’ Title IX claim against the University, its § 1983 claims (privacy, sexual harassment, and supervisory liability), and her state-law common law invasion of privacy claim against Dorrance. The court concluded the alleged conduct did not meet the severity and pervasiveness required for actionable harassment or constitutional injury, and that the intrusion-based privacy claim lacked the egregious physical or sensory intrusion required under North Carolina law.

The agreement states it contains the entire understanding regarding use of the software. If any part is void or unenforceable, the rest remains valid. It is governed by California and applicable U.S. federal laws, and the U.N. Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply. Any actions related to the agreement must be adjudicated in state or federal courts in Santa Clara County, California, with exclusive jurisdiction and venue agreed by the parties. The software may not be removed or exported from or reexported from the United States except in compliance with U.S. export laws and required licenses and approvals. Waivers or amendments are effective only if made in writing and signed by an authorized representative of each party.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 private colleges and universities of conspiring in a price-fixing scheme to inflate tuition. U.S. District Judge Sara Ellis found that the plaintiffs did not plausibly allege that the defendants entered into an agreement showing collusion on pricing. The lawsuit, filed just shy of a year ago, claimed institutions overcharged divorced or separated parents’ students by considering both custodial and noncustodial parents’ financial information in aid calculations, increasing tuition by an average of $6,200. The judge said there was evidence the practice inflated tuition prices at the named institutions but found no evidence they conspired, including no allegations that universities exchanged internal processes or agreed on the same aid-calculation formula.

At a multidisciplinary training session on human trafficking in Oshakati, Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa said human trafficking is the third largest international crime, generating $32 billion (N$401 billion) annually, and that 20–30 million people live under slavery worldwide. She cited the United States Department, stating 600,000 to 800,000 people are trafficked across international borders each year, with 80 percent being females and some children. Imalwa said Namibia is affected, citing cases such as an 11-year-old Namibian boy found in South Africa and Angolan children under 16 found in Namibia daily without parents, including reports of street selling and being employed under wages below legal requirements. She said her office sought assistance from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime to train local people to help detect, investigate, assist victims, and prosecute trafficking cases effectively. Police Inspector-General Sebastian Ndeitunga said that from 2010 to 2017, 25 human trafficking cases were recorded, with six pending trial, three declined prosecutions, one conviction, one acquittal, no new case awaiting the prosecutor-general’s decision, and 14 under investigation.

The passage describes SA58 Nasal Spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac, and summarizes prior and ongoing research on monoclonal antibodies used for COVID-19 prophylaxis, including trials of AZD7442, bamlanivimab, and REGEN-COV that were discontinued for emergency use due to Omicron escape. It reports a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Beijing construction sites (Nov 26–Dec 9, 2022) of healthy adults exposed to SARS-CoV-2 within 72 hours. Among 1,222 participants in the full analysis set, SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 and SARS-CoV-2 infection during the monitoring period versus placebo, with reported efficacy of 80.82% against symptomatic COVID-19 and 61.83% against SARS-CoV-2 infection. No severe COVID-19 or death occurred, and adverse events were mostly mild (no SAEs/AESIs reported). The authors conclude SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety for post-exposure prophylaxis in healthy adults and should be further evaluated in high-risk populations.

The passage describes medical systems for assisting rescuers during intubation/airway management, especially rapid sequence intubation, by using sensors (e.g., airflow, oxygen, CO2/capnography, pulse oximetry, ECG, acoustic, impedance, and blood pressure) and patient monitoring devices to determine whether an endotracheal tube is properly placed and remains so. The systems may analyze sensor data to detect the presence of airflow, start and use timers to confirm placement within an interval, and present visual feedback indicating placement status, including parameters such as SpO2 and ETCO2. The passage also describes features such as selectable or default timer values (e.g., 5–15 seconds), physiological baseline methods for detecting deviation after tube placement (using ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, or acoustic/spectral patterns), touchscreen and portable device interfaces, and integration with defibrillators and wearable devices for alarms and guidance. Additionally, the passage outlines systems that detect which steps of an airway intubation procedure are being performed using intubation parameters (gas, physiological, and positioning), identify transitions between RSI steps, and provide step-specific feedback and timers.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, a new law requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose how they plan to mitigate potentially catastrophic risks from advanced AI models. The law also establishes mechanisms for reporting critical safety incidents, extends whistleblower protections to AI company employees, and initiates development of CalCompute, a government consortium to create a public computing cluster for safe, ethical, and sustainable AI research. Supporters cite transparency and appropriate oversight, while critics argue the requirements could burden startups and entrench large companies. The law requires incident reporting to California’s Office of Emergency Services, includes civil penalties enforceable by the state attorney general, and is expected to have global impact because many top AI firms are headquartered in California.

The passage describes Tropical Storm Nate’s projected path and potential impacts on the U.S. Gulf Coast, especially Northwest Florida. Nate is expected to move across the northwestern Caribbean Sea, reach the eastern Yucatan peninsula early Friday evening, move into the southern Gulf of Mexico overnight, and approach the northern Gulf coast Saturday evening. The National Hurricane Center forecasts Nate could develop into a hurricane Saturday night into Sunday, moving northwest at 14 mph with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph. By a 5 a.m. update, the forecast track moved east, putting Pensacola back in the warning cone, and heavy rain from Saturday through at least Sunday is expected to possibly require flash flood guidance. Tornadoes are also possible beginning Saturday into Sunday, with sustained tropical storm force winds Sunday morning. Forecast winds include 35–45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph in Escambia County and 15–25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph in Santa Rosa County, along with 3–5 inches of rainfall and a chance of isolated short-track tornadoes. A tropical storm watch was issued for much of Northwest Florida Gulf Coast, including Escambia and Santa Rosa counties. It also reports local closures and cancellations, preparations by Gov. Rick Scott and state agencies (including a declared state of emergency and National Guard readiness), and guidance for residents to prepare supplies and follow local updates.

Kevin Love, recovering from a concussion and possibly missing Game 1, has dealt with months of physical injuries and heavy criticism since arriving in Cleveland in 2014. The passage describes how he has faced slurs and trade rumors while also managing anxiety and panic attacks. On Jan. 22, teammates questioned his absence, and Love explained his panic attacks; he later wrote an essay for the Players’ Tribune about his struggles, including an earlier episode while recovering from a broken left hand. After his disclosure, he received thousands of supportive emails and said it increased empathy and helped him build community. Love said he does not want special treatment and that basketball helps him escape when his mind otherwise takes over. The passage also recounts postseason struggles, a concussion protocol after a collision with Jayson Tatum, and Jeff Green’s role in helping Cleveland win Game 7. Love remains in protocol and his status for the Finals opener is in doubt, as he looks ahead to trying to “hang a banner” in the NBA Finals.

The passage describes the 2017 summer movie season as having strong box office success for three comic book superhero films—Wonder Woman, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, and Spider-Man: Homecoming—but weaker or failed performance for most other genres. It lists relatively successful non-superhero films such as Despicable Me 3, Girls Trip, Annabelle: Creation, Dunkirk, Baby Driver, The Big Sick, and several smaller-budget titles, while noting many other releases that underperformed against expectations or budgets (including Cars 3, Captain Underpants, various comedies, and several major franchises like The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight, and War for the Planet of the Apes). The author argues that superhero films dominated release schedules and that overall results limited diversity at multiplexes, framing the season as “The superhero movies kicked ass!” with “one successful offering from every other category.”

Researchers at the University of California, Irvine and other institutions are developing a satellite-based drought severity index that uses NASA’s Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) data, incorporating terrestrial water storage (groundwater) in addition to precipitation-based assessments. The index is intended to provide accurate, continuous monitoring for climate scientists and government officials, including assessment of drought impacts on vegetation, food production, and water resources. The GRACE dataset covers 2002 to 2014 and will be extended by ongoing GRACE missions and a GRACE follow-on mission planned for early 2018. The index tracks groundwater storage changes affecting soil moisture recharge and drought recovery, and UCI researchers report significant agreement with other indices when evaluated in the continental United States. The work is being presented at an American Geophysical Union fall meeting.

On May 25, Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi took part in a Q&A at BIMM Music Institute in Birmingham, where he announced details of the BIMM Birmingham Scholarship he is sponsoring. Prospective BIMM students were invited to experience the new state-of-the-art college in Digbeth opening that October, and Iommi discussed his career and said he has always felt it was worth it since day one, despite knockbacks and people who don’t like him.

The passage compiles multiple news items dated May 24, 2001, involving energy and politics. It includes commentary alleging California officials’ hostility toward Enron and Texas energy producers, analysis of how a potential Senate shift tied to Sen. James Jeffords could affect industries such as drugs, HMOs, energy, and tobacco, and a report on Brazil asking users to cut energy consumption by 20% to avoid blackouts amid a power shortage. Other items describe California’s investigation into alleged electricity price manipulation through changes in power-plant output, discussions around U.S.-based Enron’s Dabhol project dispute in India and the nomination of a panel representative to negotiate tariff issues, and analysis of Central European gas market changes linked to pipeline decisions and planned sell-offs. It also notes Endesa’s decision to auction coal-powered generation assets, coverage of political criticism surrounding India’s Enron renegotiation panel head, and a Financial Times report stating Dynegy plans to pursue large acquisitions or mergers.

Ryan ToysReview, a family’s toy review channel starring their six-year-old son Ryan, has made him a top-earning YouTube star, reportedly earning $11 million in 2017 and ranking in Forbes’ Top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars. The channel started in 2015, has over 10 million subscribers, and its videos were viewed over eight billion times during Forbes’ tracking period. Ryan’s parents say the boy was inspired by other children and programs on YouTube and began after asking to be on YouTube, then getting his first toy. They keep their last name and location secret for safety and say the show will continue only as long as Ryan enjoys it, stopping if he gets bored.

The passage explains the long-short equity strategy as an investing method where traders take long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline. It is described as a hedging approach intended to minimize risk while potentially maximizing profits from gains in long positions and declines in short positions, and it may also provide diversification. The strategy is noted as commonly used by hedge funds, often with a long bias (e.g., 130/30), and it can be implemented using techniques such as leverage and derivatives. It outlines a process of identifying underpriced and overpriced stocks, going long on undervalued names and shorting overvalued ones, and emphasizes that outcomes are not guaranteed. The passage also provides examples including a scenario involving Merck & Co. and Thor Industries, and a backtest illustration using Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola with RSI-based trading rules and reported performance metrics. It concludes by noting that long-short strategies typically require more coding and resources, and recommends having portfolios with many pairs rather than relying on only a few.

The passage describes a 16-bit, 1MSPS single-ended SAR ADC input circuit using the PGA848 to drive the ADS8860 ADC. It accepts single-ended or differential inputs and uses independent input/output supplies: ±15V for the input stage and a unipolar 5.3V supply for the output stage and ADC supply, with the REF6250 providing a 5V ADC reference. The PGA848 REF pin is set to a 2.5V midscale voltage via a precision voltage divider buffered by an OPA192, configured for stability with bypassing. It outlines design requirements including three filters for EMI/RFI reduction, bandwidth/noise adjustment, and charge kickback reduction to support ADC sample-and-hold settling and THD performance, with expected bandwidth values (318kHz nominal, 277kHz at resistor tolerance) and flatness to 41kHz. It also provides supply voltage guidance, cautions against exceeding 40V (±20V), and gives PCB layout guidelines to maintain symmetry, reduce noise coupling, manage leakage/parasitic capacitance, and support stable operation. The passage further includes notes on simulation tools (PSpice/TINA-TI), related documentation, how to receive updates, support resources (TI E2E), trademarks, and legal/disclaimer text.

A New York Times survey of 65 responding federal judges found widespread dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in cases tied to President Donald Trump since his second term. Only 12 of 65 said the Supreme Court made appropriate use of the emergency docket, and only 12 said lower courts have sufficient guidance on applying emergency docket orders. Only two of 54 said the emergency docket improved the public’s perception of the judiciary. Judges described orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” “incredibly demoralizing,” and “a slap in the face,” with some describing their judicial relationship with the Supreme Court as a “war zone” or “judicial crisis.” A Trump appointee said the orders were “flushing out anti-democratic rulings.” Survey details included that 42 judges said the emergency docket harmed public perception, 10 said it had no effect, and two said it improved it. The survey questionnaire was sent to more than 400 federal district and appeals judges. The New York Times also reported that at least seven of about 20 emergency orders did not include reasonings and that nearly all benefited Trump, with practical effects including deportations, discharge of transgender military service members, firing government workers, and reduced federal spending.

Quarter Circle Games announced The Peterson Case, a first-person horror game set shortly after the 1947 Roswell UFO incident. Made in Unity, it is planned for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC, and a trailer is available that the company says reflects actual gameplay. The official website describes the game as featuring Detective Franklin Reinhardt exploring a deserted house near Roswell to uncover clues about a missing family, while an unearthly presence pursues him. The game is said to balance atmospheric horror, suspenseful narrative, and engaging puzzles, with a release date to be announced.

The passage describes an AI-assisted inverse design workflow for discovering new diammonium organic spacers for Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites with targeted energy level alignment types (Ib, IIa, IIb). It uses an invertible 12-digit fingerprint representation of organic spacer structures, expands the chemical space from 21 reported spacers to millions of hypothetical candidates via molecular morphing, and employs high-throughput DFT to compute energy levels for training. Machine learning models then predict HOMO/LUMO frontier levels from fingerprints, and a two-step synthesis feasibility screening (PubChem availability and a formability score based on topological descriptors) downselects candidates, followed by DFT validation. From generations G0–G6, the workflow validates 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates with DFT and finds no type Ib candidates due to synthesis feasibility limits. An inverse design strategy constrains fingerprints to search later generations, identifying type Ib candidates in G7–G8 and additional IIa and IIb candidates across specified generation ranges. The work reports interpretable structure–property relationships from ML analysis and proposes design rules based on features like conjugated backbone size and tethering ammonium groups, while noting limitations and the need for experimental validation.

Teck Resources Ltd was upgraded by Zacks Investment Research from a “hold” to a “buy” rating, with a $25.00 price objective indicating 8.84% potential upside. The passage also cites other analyst actions, shows an average “Buy” rating with a $31.18 consensus price target, and provides stock performance metrics (opening price $22.97; 52-week range $14.56–$26.60). It reports quarterly results for the quarter ended July 27, including EPS of $0.73 and revenue of $2.82 billion, and notes revenue up 62.0% year over year. Institutional investors are reported to hold 46.80% of the company’s stock, and Teck Resources is described as operating in segments including steelmaking coal, copper, zinc, energy, and corporate.

In August 2002, DEA agents and Butte County Sheriff’s officers disputed the destruction of marijuana plants in Diane Monson’s backyard. Monson’s plants were deemed legal under California’s Compassionate Use Act, but the DEA said marijuana was a Schedule I drug and ordered destruction. After a three-hour standoff, local officers allowed the DEA to destroy the plants.

The dispute between state and federal authority led to a Supreme Court case involving Angel Raich, who used medical cannabis for life-threatening conditions. Both Raich’s and Monson’s activities were legal under California law, but not under the federal Controlled Substances Act. Raich and Monson sued, arguing Congress lacked constitutional authority to regulate their intrastate, non-commercial activity.

The Supreme Court ruled 6–3 for the government. The majority held that Congress could regulate in-state medical cannabis to preserve its ability to ban the interstate cannabis market, even though the regulation “ensnare[d] some purely intrastate activity.” Scalia wrote separately, grounding congressional reach in the Necessary and Proper Clause, while emphasizing remaining limits. Rehnquist dissented without an opinion, and O’Connor and Thomas wrote dissents arguing that broader regulatory schemes remove meaningful limits on federal power. Thomas also argued for an originalist view of “commerce” and contended that Congress had not shown the necessity of regulating local growers or users.

The passage describes several MSPM0 G-Series MCU features and related documentation. It explains how a linear temperature sensor output is internally connected to an ADC channel and how a factory calibration value stored in factory constants memory (TSTRIM, 12-bit mode, 1.4-V internal VREF) can be used to estimate device temperature using a temperature coefficient. It outlines the VREF module (configurable internal 1.4 V/2.5 V references, support for external reference input, and decoupling requirements), comparator and DAC key capabilities, and security features including AES accelerator modes and keystore behavior. It also covers a true random number generator, CRC options, a math accelerator, and serial interfaces including UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD, along with low-frequency subsystem components (LFSS_B with RTC_B and IWDT_B) and watchdog timers. The passage further describes device factory constants and lists guidance and disclaimers for applications, tooling, documentation updates, support resources, and trademarks.

During a Monday White House press briefing, CNN’s Brian Karem asked Sarah Huckabee Sanders whether she has ever experienced sexual harassment and whether she has empathy for people who come forward. Sanders declined to share personal history, saying she has empathy and that it is White House policy, but stated she is there to relay information on behalf of the president.

The passage provides credit card offer information and related disclosures. It states that on a Galaxy Fold, users should unfold the phone or view it in full screen for the best experience. It also explains that offers shown may be influenced by compensation, though product ratings are not. The passage then describes cash back and introductory APR features and terms for multiple cards, including the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card (unlimited 2% cash rewards, $200 welcome bonus after $500 spend in 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, $0 annual fee, and cell phone protection up to $600 with a $25 deductible) and the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card (unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases, potential 5% through Capital One Travel, $300 welcome bonuses plus other conditions, $0 annual fee and no foreign transaction fees, and 0% intro APR for 15 months). It also includes eligibility notes (recommended credit score range of 670–850 for offers) and general approval/disclaimer language.

A building on the University of Minnesota Morris campus remains from when an Indian boarding school was located there; it formerly served as a boys dormitory and now houses the multi-ethnic resource center. The passage describes the boarding schools’ purpose of assimilating Native American children, including learning English and abandoning cultural and spiritual practices. On April 11, 20 to 30 current Native American students gathered on campus for a talking circle and shared stories about higher education, trauma, and how boarding school history affects Native students. The University of Minnesota Morris joined the UMN system in 1960, and earlier it was an agriculture school and an Indian boarding school. State law requires Native American students attending the Morris campus to receive tuition-free enrollment, which the passage says is believed to be one of two such waivers at non-tribal colleges. It notes the Morris campus has about 1,800 students, is the most racially diverse in the UMN system, and has about 20% Native American students.

The passage reports that the flu epidemic is continuing, with 42 states experiencing high activity last week. This season, 53 children have died. A seven-year-old from Indiana, Savanna Jessie, was found unresponsive at home after testing positive for influenza B, strep throat, and scarlet fever, and her death is being investigated by the local coroner. Dr. Anne Schuchat says deaths in children and adults are increasing and that the season is difficult, in part because H3N2 is most common and is associated with more cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, especially among the elderly. A Canada report says the vaccine is 17 percent effective against the H3N2 strain. Doctors and public health officials still recommend vaccination as the best defense, noting it can reduce the severity of symptoms; they also recommend starting antiviral medications as soon as possible and that flu shots be given to everyone 6 months and older.

Bitcoin rose by more than a third to over $9,000 (about $9,300) for the first time since March and analysts expect further gains. The forecast is linked to a large increase in buy orders, which make up over 92% of market activity for the first time since March 2017, with analysts saying a significant price shift is likely. Regulatory uncertainty has affected gains, including an inquiry into exchanges such as Gemini and Coinbase, but analysts expect regulation to become more supportive. Christine Lagarde said Bitcoin and blockchain technology could transform saving and investing, and Marques said regulatory concerns are dissipating. Analysts also said crossing $10,000 could boost momentum and potentially trigger a bull phase, with expectations that Bitcoin could reach $11,500 if $10,000 breaks.

The passage describes “passthrough” for head-mounted displays (HMDs), enabling users to see physical surroundings using front-facing camera imagery re-rendered based on a 3D model to provide proper perspective and parallax. It notes that occlusion artifacts can occur when the 3D model is imprecise, especially near object edges. To improve occlusion, embodiments generate instance segmentation masks for objects in captured images and compute representative depth values for each instance (e.g., using centroids of corresponding 3D model coordinates). For over-occlusion, padded borders around segmented instances are assigned significantly farther depth values to enforce harder edges. During rendering, the system performs visibility tests and uses instance mask–based depth (or padded border depth) to decide whether passthrough or virtual objects should occlude, falling back to 3D-model depth when no instance mask applies. The passage also describes an approach for resource-limited devices that estimates stereo correspondences using a device video encoder’s motion vectors with verification filtering, followed by depth triangulation and creation of a coarse 3D mesh for rendering.

The passage outlines the structure and content of the “Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00” for SD Memory Cards. It describes SD Memory Card system concepts and chapters covering system features, SD/ SPI/ UHS-II bus concepts, card pins and registers, ROM and UHS-I/UHS-II card operation, cache, self-maintenance, command queue, LV interface, and higher bus speed modes. It also covers card functional description including identification and initialization processes (e.g., CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3), data transfer modes (single/multiple block read/write, stop/abort with CMD12), command/response formats and card states, register contents, and electrical and SPI interface details. Additional sections define memory capacity types (SDSC, SDHC, SDXC), read-write vs ROM cards, security-related mechanisms, bus speed modes and performance classes, and card hardware interface and mechanical form factors (including standard thickness variants and UHS-II interface pads).

The speaker says Ryan Smyth should remain an Edmonton Oiler forever, noting he represents what an Oiler and hockey player should be. They describe evaluating a player over his career and argue no trade would bring back equivalent value. The team’s performance is discussed, including winter trades after believing they had a playoff-capable team that could do damage, despite a late-season slip. The speaker also mentions roster additions and the importance of skating and thinking the game in the “new NHL,” while expecting drama and storylines in a series. They share personal stories about Smyth’s dedication and growth, and about Ray Whitney’s passion and background with the Oilers. The passage concludes with discussion of goaltending, including why they acquired Dwayne Roloson, what they expected him to provide, and confidence in the team’s defensive play and goalkeeper contribution.

An assessment by Karnataka’s department of public instruction found that over 10 lakh students in government and aided schools (Classes 4–9) need remedial classes. For the first time, the Students Achievement Survey (SAS) was conducted with a written exam in October 2017, involving over 36 lakh students from 50,000 schools. Teachers have been informed of remedial measures, and about 4.5 lakh of the students needing help require it in Mathematics and Science. The survey tested language and core subjects across Classes 4–5 and 6–9 using multiple question-paper versions, and students will receive marks cards that will be addressed to parents and sent to schools, with grades shown using black stars.

Auckland Airport says it has found the passenger involved in a security breach. Police and Aviation Security located the woman with the weapon of concern, and the international terminal has reopened with a backlog of passengers. After international screening, an X-ray machine identified a knife “on their person,” and the passenger continued into the terminal, triggering a security emergency. The airport restarted screening but said clearing the backlog will take some time. At least four flights were affected, including Air New Zealand and Virgin Australia flights to Christchurch and Gisborne and flights to the Bay of Islands.

Malaria in Africa caused 246 million cases and 560,000 deaths in 2023, accounting for most of the global burden. Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) are threatened by artemisinin partial resistance linked to Kelch13 (PfK13) propeller-domain mutations. PfK13-associated resistance was first detected in Cambodia in 2006 and later identified in Africa starting in 2014 (Rwanda), 2016 (Uganda, Ethiopia, Eritrea), with increasing prevalence across East Africa and the Horn of Africa; Central and Southern Africa had not yet shown PfK13 mutations above the WHO 5% threshold.  

This study examined markers of artemisinin resistance and partner drug resistance in a low-transmission area in southern Zambia (Choma District) using amplicon deep-sequencing on samples collected from 2018 to 2023. The candidate PfK13 marker P441L was present in 6% of all samples (30 of 501) and increased from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023 (9.3% in 2022), occurring at all four health centers and in all years except 2018. In addition to P441L, the PfK13 A578S mutation was detected in 0.6% of samples in 2023. MDR1 Y184F had an overall prevalence of 41% with no change over time. The study reports that P441L prevalence in southern Zambia in 2023 (7.2%) and overall (6%) exceeds the WHO 5% threshold and highlights limitations including incomplete drug-resistance profiles due to missing data and gaps in PfK13 coverage.

U.S. stocks rose Monday, with the S&P 500 posting its biggest one-day gain since April. New York Fed President William Dudley said another rate rise is likely in 2017 and that expectations for starting to cut the balance sheet in September are reasonable. The prior Thursday selloff reflected concerns about market volatility amid tensions with North Korea. The passage also reports eurozone factory output declining at its sharpest pace in 2017 during June, Fed research finding the natural unemployment rate has been stable over the last century, and China showing a July slowdown tied to Beijing’s property-speculation crackdown and rising debt. It adds that Japan’s GDP grew 4.0% annualized in the April-June quarter, Canada proposed a more “progressive” NAFTA with added environmental provisions while keeping its dispute-settlement stance, and that oil fell to a three-week low and gold dropped as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased.

The passage describes a study on factors that attract and retain rural special education teachers amid long-standing rural teacher shortages. It outlines reasons teachers leave, including geographic and social isolation, limited training and resources, lower pay and benefits, insufficient collegial/administrative support, caseload and paperwork burdens, challenges with multiple service settings and supervisors, and feeling overworked or isolated. Prior strategies discussed include increased pay and benefits (though salary alone may not sustain retention), community and administrative support, improved job-related conditions (such as reduced paperwork/caseload and relevant professional development), and rural initiatives like Grow Your Own programs and rural teacher–hosted career fairs.

The study used a survey of special education teachers from three rural remote Midwest U.S. special education cooperatives to examine attraction and retention factors. After excluding incomplete responses, 93 teachers completed the survey. Data analysis identified themes such as provision of support, financial incentives, job-related factors, and rural initiatives. Results showed teachers most often cited support for retention and financial incentives for both attraction and retention, with specific retention-related priorities including administrative/peer support, increased salary, reduced paperwork/caseload, and professional development. The passage also notes limitations related to self-reported survey data and regional sample constraints, and concludes that combining incentives, support, job-related improvements, and rural initiatives may help address recruitment and retention challenges.

NASA’s Suomi NPP spacecraft captured an infrared image of the northern lights over northern Canada just before Christmas, recording aurora borealis across several Canadian provinces and territories on Dec. 22 from 512 miles (824 kilometers) above Earth. The passage explains that solar wind particles interact with Earth’s magnetic field, sending energetic particles into the upper atmosphere, where they trigger aurora glow by releasing energy as photons of different wavelengths that create different colors. It also notes that major solar storms occur roughly every 11 years, with the last cycle peak in 2013 and the solar maximum described as the weakest observed in a century.

The passage says Nintendo has announced that Mario Kart will soon be available on smartphones as an app called Mario Kart Tour, with a planned release during the fiscal year ending March 2019. It notes Nintendo has not provided further details on the app, and that since 2015 Nintendo has released smartphone versions of games including Super Mario Run, Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp, and Fire Emblem Heroes. It also mentions that the Nintendo Switch outsold the Wii within 10 months of launch.

The passage includes multiple NFL-related headlines and rankings and repeats a sign-in request to manage favorites. It also reports that Tyreek Hill’s dislocated left knee injury required major surgery to repair it and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL. Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN that the surgery “went very well,” that Hill will play next season, and that the realistic goal is the start of the season. Coach Mike McDaniel said he has heard “good things” about any potential nerve damage. The passage further discusses how the Dolphins will adapt to Hill’s absence and mentions other injuries and team performance.

The passage discusses preparing for games by playing a tight game, getting bounces and scoring, then returning home with ice advantage. It says hockey involves learning to forget bad games and being outplayed, which is part of life. It also contrasts the teams’ playing styles, stating that each can counter the other, so the better team will ultimately win. It adds that the speaker observed the other team throughout the playoffs, expected them to play hard, and knew what was needed but felt they did not execute it.

Thomas H. Fisher sued Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane and copartner Homer P. Hargrave for an accounting of losses from commodity transactions handled by Fuller, Rodney & Co. in December 1940 and January 1941. Fuller, Rodney & Co. dissolved at April 30, 1941, and plaintiff’s argument was that Merrill Lynch and its predecessors succeeded to Fuller, Rodney & Co.’s business and assumed its liabilities, entitling him to an accounting. Hargrave moved for summary judgment with affidavits and the court denied plaintiff’s motions to strike and for default, then granted summary judgment for Hargrave on costs.

The court found Hargrave’s and Byron G. Webster’s affidavits and the parties’ agreement supported that there was no merger or consolidation, no assumption of Fuller, Rodney & Co.’s liabilities by Merrill Lynch or its predecessors, and plaintiff’s account was not transferred. Plaintiff’s opposing affidavit was treated as largely speculative and based on information and belief, and the court disregarded it. The court also held the record did not show an order denying plaintiff’s requested discovery. It further concluded that summary judgment was proper in this equitable accounting action under the Civil Practice Act. The superior court’s summary judgment was affirmed.

BAE Systems agreed to sell 24 Typhoon fighter planes to Qatar as part of a 6 billion pound ($8 billion) deal with European defense contractors. British Defense Secretary Gavin Williamson announced the contracts were signed in Doha, and the agreement also includes Brimstone and Meteor missiles, and Raytheon Paveway IV guided bombs. BAE Systems valued the Typhoon contract, including training and support, at 5 billion pounds. The deal is Qatar’s ninth purchase of the aircraft, and Williamson said it is the biggest Typhoon export agreement in a decade and will support Qatar’s military efforts in the Middle East.

On 13 Feb 2017, USD/JPY rallied shortly after the New Zealand open following North Korea’s Sunday missile test and related geopolitical unrest. The Nikkei was largely unaffected, while traders broadly sold the yen and pushed the pair above Friday’s 113.86 before Tokyo open; it reached 114.17 after triggering stops above 114.00 and then eased. A pullback from 114.17 was seen as suggesting consolidation, with expectation of demand on dips and preference for long positions. Bids were noted at 113.85–75 and more above with stops below 113.20, while offers were tipped at 114.20/30 with stops above 114.30/40. With no U.S. data scheduled, order flows were expected to strongly influence intra-day price swings.

The passage is from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2016. It describes Microsoft’s business, including its vision and strategy for a mobile-first, cloud-first world, and outlines its product and service offerings, key ambitions, and operating segments (Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing). It also discusses operations, research and development spending, product and intellectual property development, distribution and licensing options, major customer types, executive officers, employee counts and restructuring, investor information availability, and extensive risk factors affecting competition, cloud services execution, investments, security, privacy, regulatory and legal matters, intellectual property, and hardware/software quality and supply.

A study of Tokyo residents found that longer commuting time increases insomnia and daytime sleepiness, and smaller housing size increases insomnia risk. Even among people living in average-sized homes, commuting more than 52 minutes was associated with reaching the insomnia cutoff value. Researchers conclude that considering the trade-off between home location and size could improve sleep health and quality of life.

After getting “goal side,” a defender’s foot placement and one-on-one stance must be established relative to an opponent with the ball. The stance is described as a comfortable, balanced position far enough from the attacker to stay with them as the opponent moves. It typically starts with one foot forward (lead/front foot) and one back (trail foot), with the dominant leg behind, the non-dominant leg forward, feet about 18 inches apart on a roughly 30-degree angle, toes slightly outward, and the defender balanced on the balls of both feet with slightly bent knees and elbows bent. The stance is intended to enable quick reactions, respond with minimal time, slow or force the opponent, avoid being beaten, and prepare for a tackle. The lead foot is modified by field position: left foot lead on the right side of the midline, right foot lead on the left side. Defenders are taught proper stance at right, center, and left locations, how their stance changes with opponent movement, and to practice movement without and with a ball at half-speed or less, while using “goal side” and field markings and “sneak peeks.” They are also instructed not to block the opponent or impede progress with their arms, with coaching tips comparing stance maintenance to basketball guards and football cornerbacks.

The passage describes the Iso play as a downhill running scheme that uses a fullback as a lead blocker on a linebacker, involving base blocks and double teams at the point of attack. It is intended to overpower defenses and get the ball vertical quickly, and it is named because the lead blocker is isolated one-on-one with the linebacker. The strengths highlighted are that it gets the ball downhill fast and is simple to teach, helping players execute successfully. The main weakness is that the play depends heavily on personnel, requiring large, powerful offensive linemen and a rugged fullback; teams with smaller or weaker linemen may struggle. The passage also outlines Iso blocking assignments versus 3-4 and 4-3 fronts and lists variations, including “Shotgun Iso” and “Weakside Iso.”

GBPJPY is the forex quote for the exchange rate between the British pound (GBP) and the Japanese yen (JPY). It is considered a minor pair and is formed as a cross pair of GBPUSD and USDJPY, allowing traders to take net long positions (longing both GBPUSD and USDJPY) or net short positions (shorting both). Among traders, GBPJPY is also known as “Geppy” or “The Beast.” Its price movements can be significantly correlated with USDJPY, and traders are advised to be cautious during periods of high positive correlation. The passage says forex trading is difficult, but that strategies that work may provide diversification, and it emphasizes backtesting to find positive expectancy. It also provides an example of a GBPJPY futures strategy with trading statistics and performance metrics.

Finally, it offers tips and troubleshooting, information on service/support and warranty terms, and a software end user license agreement summary.

Malacañang said President Rodrigo Duterte will investigate allegations against Development Academy of the Philippines (DAP) President Elba Cruz, his appointee, after DAP employees accused her of unauthorized restructuring, violations of Civil Service Commission rules, threats of mass termination, and frequent foreign travel. Presidential Spokesman Harry Roque said Duterte prioritizes pursuing “government junketeers,” noting employees claim Cruz has taken monthly foreign trips during her first eight months. Roque also said a lifestyle check is among the powers of the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission Duterte created in October, but the President had not yet appointed anyone because the Palace was still vetting individuals. Roque further announced Duterte’s plan to fire all top officials of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor over allegations of unnecessary junkets and failure to meet en banc.

The study reviews leadership models used in education and compares their strengths and weaknesses, noting that no single model can meet the changing needs of school settings. It suggests a synthetic, flexible approach that combines strengths from multiple models. It discusses administrative/managerial leadership (hierarchy and structure but potential rigidity), instructional leadership (focus on teaching and learning but potential top-down limits and narrow attention), transformational leadership (vision, motivation, innovation and support, but criticized for possible authoritarian outcomes), distributed leadership (shared leadership roles, improving collaboration and learning outcomes but with implementation challenges), transactional leadership (rewards and authority to shape behavior, but with risks to morale and innovation), ethical leadership (moral values guiding decisions, but potentially causing conflicts), contingent leadership (adapting style to circumstances), and participative leadership (shared decision-making that increases satisfaction and commitment but may slow decisions and create conflicts). The conclusion emphasizes combining elements such as managerial structure and transformational practices, plus collaboration through distributed and participative leadership and ethical integrity, to improve school effectiveness and adaptability.

The passage describes mandatory and recommended behaviors in an SD card physical layer specification, including definitions for “shall/will” (mandatory), “should” (recommended), and “may” (optional feature). It covers an SD Memory Card interface extension for Mc-EX, the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00, and key card characteristics such as capacity classes (SDSC, SDHC, SDXC), voltage ranges, read-only vs read/write cards, bus speed modes and speed classes. It explains SD bus communication basics (commands, responses, data transfer), card initialization and identification sequences (e.g., CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3), UHS-I and UHS-II/UHS-II initialization and mode selection sequences, and data transfer behaviors in single/multiple block read/write operations. The passage also discusses erase-related commands (erase, discard, FULE), write protection via mechanical switch or card features, and password/card ownership protection using CMD42, including non-COP vs COP card behaviors and related command sequences and error handling.

The University of Windsor’s Board of Governors announced that Douglas Kneale, provost and vice-president, academic, will serve as interim president and vice-chancellor starting July 1 until a successor to Alan Wildeman is found. Wildeman’s term ends June 30, and he said he will announce an acting provost and vice-president, academic, in the coming weeks and help Kneale prepare. The board said it wants continuity during the search and requested the presidential search committee resume efforts in the coming year, announcing a successor once identified.

Ahead of the Ipswich mayoral by-election, mayoral hopefuls received almost $60,000 in donations, with most going to Councillor Andrew Antoniolli. The largest single donation came from Plencove (owned by NuGrow operator Roy Wilson), which gave $15,000 to Antoniolli, who has received $46,400 so far. Two large professional billboards along Ipswich Mwy near Dinmore and Inala have not had their funders disclosed by rival Cr Paul Tully, whose largest lodged donation is $3,300 in kind from Falvey Investments Pty Ltd for a billboard supporting his campaign. Donations are reported on the Electoral Commission Queensland website under “real-time donation” disclosure rules requiring reporting within seven business days. Out of 11 candidates, only The Greens endorsed candidate Brett Morrissey has declarable donations so far, totaling $1,330 across nine transactions handled by The Greens. The passage also lists additional donations above $1,000 for several other candidates and notes campaign-manager internal transactions are not listed.

The lecture discusses orthonormal expansions in moving from finite to infinite dimensions, emphasizing that projections onto an orthonormal set converge and that the difference between a vector and its approximation is orthogonal to the basis functions. It defines countably infinite-dimensional inner product spaces via infinite orthonormal sets and explains issues encountered in Fourier series, such as whether a time-limited function reconstructed from a Fourier expansion returns to the original, and how “leftover” components relate to orthogonality and limits.

The lecture then transitions to communication systems, describing a layered encoder structure (discrete encoding and modulation) and focusing on modulation using signal constellations mapped to waveforms. It reviews why sinc-based ideal signaling is impractical due to delay and filter implementation, and motivates pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM) as a way to replace sinc with another pulse shape while keeping detection feasible.

Finally, it introduces Nyquist’s approach to avoiding intersymbol interference using an “ideal Nyquist” composite filter condition. The lecture explains that intersymbol interference is avoided when samples of the received waveform equal the transmitted coefficients, and it derives the Nyquist criterion in terms of bandlimiting/aliasing symmetry. It notes that sinc satisfies this but has poor delay properties, while practical pulse shapes like raised-cosine filters provide better decay and controlled bandwidth.

The passage describes example methods and apparatus for improving user experience in 3D sound localization using electronically generated binaural sounds. It addresses problems when listeners struggle to determine sound origin in near-field conditions (e.g., when sound is convolved to within one meter), when perceived audio origin does not align with visible or expected images, and when near-field HRTF processing is complex or unreliable. Example embodiments process sound during telephone calls and other electronic communications by convolving or processing voices so that listeners perceive the sound as originating from a target source location, often by selecting head-related transfer function (HRTF) pairs with coordinates that are behind, beyond, or offset from the actual physical/virtual source. The passage also discusses techniques such as selecting HRTFs along a line-of-sight or imaginary line, positioning the origination behind the sound source, adjusting volume for perceived distance, and varying or highlighting sound along a line-of-sight. It further describes systems and methods for quickly switching between externalized binaural sound and internal mono/stereo sound based on detected actions and sensor inputs from portable electronic devices (e.g., rotations, shaking, gripping, face detection/gaze/light/darkness, obstructions, battery state changes, and headphone/speaker output changes), including examples using smartphone cameras and sensors.

The passage describes a Bayesian, probabilistic approach to relevance-theoretic pragmatics, focusing on how audiences comprehend conversational implicatures. It introduces explicatures (developed logical forms with truth conditions) and implicatures (implicit premises and conclusions not derived by logical-form development), using an example where Mary declines Peter’s coffee offer. It outlines relevance theory’s view that cognition aims to maximize relevance, explains how ostensive communication raises relevance expectations, and presents a relevance-based processing heuristic that stops once expectations are met. It then motivates probabilistic modeling through Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between prior and posterior probability distributions over communicated assumptions, and proposes representing parallel adjustment of explicit content and implicit import with a Bayesian network. The paper implements an implicature comprehension model in ProbLog using probabilistic knowledge graphs, inference rules linking words to encyclopedic concepts, and multiple manually constructed interpretive hypotheses (Int1–Int5) that are compared using KL divergence and, when KL ties occur, the size of the Herbrand base. The conclusion states that the resulting “as-if-optimization” model captures relevance-theory insights in probabilistic terms and can be used to test the heuristic nature of relevance-guided comprehension, with future work planned on higher-level explicature comprehension and other pragmatic phenomena.

The passage discusses interest in rutile RuO₂ as an altermagnetic candidate, citing reports of sublattice magnetic moments, high band splitting predictions, and potential THz-frequency memory applications. However, it notes ongoing debate: many experiments and calculations have reported a lack of sublattice moment in RuO₂, implying it would not be altermagnetic in its ground state. Discrepancies between patterned thin-film transport effects and bulk/ground-state modeling are rationalized by the possibility that defects, strain, doping, and especially interfacial effects in RuO₂/FM heterostructures stabilize magnetic behavior.

The study investigates the origin of exchange bias (EB) in incoherently grown RuO₂/Fe heterostructures using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron reflectometry/diffraction, atom probe tomography, and cross-sectional TEM/EELS. Neutron diffraction is reported to show no AFM ordering signatures in RuO₂ films and no detectable compensated magnetic moment within an upper limit. In contrast, polarized neutron reflectometry indicates uncompensated canted moments localized at the RuO₂/Fe interface, sensitive to field history. Chemical/structural characterization (APT, HRTEM/FFT, EELS) finds an interlayer dominated by iron oxide and includes magnetite (Fe₃O₄), along with a Fe gradient into RuO₂. EB is reported to be absent in RuO₂/Ni heterostructures and present in TiO₂/Fe/Ru bilayers lacking the RuO₂/Fe interface, attributed to oxidation through the Ru barrier. The authors conclude that the EB in RuO₂/Fe systems arises from a chemically active interfacial reaction layer (including Fe₃O₄), not from intrinsic AFM/altermagnetic ordering in sputtered RuO₂.

Strange Brigade will be released on August 28 for PS4, Xbox One, and PC. BioSafe Systems announced the hiring of Carleton Birk as Operations Manager and Tenaya Becker, Ester Mastronardi, Patrick Clark, and Kyle Pickles as Technical Sales Representatives for regions across the USA and Canada. Birk is based in East Hartford, CT and has operational and quality management experience, with degrees from the University of Connecticut and the University of New Haven. Becker is based in Southern CA with 25 years of horticultural sales experience. Mastronardi is based in Leamington, Ontario, with experience in agricultural, horticultural, and vineyard product sales, export, and import. Clark is based in Eastern PA with experience in agronomic and precision agriculture support and regional sales roles, plus agriculture-related degrees. Pickles is based in Central CA with education from California Polytechnic State University and experience with The Deerpoint Group, providing water treatment sales and technical support. The passage contains comments about a hockey playoff game. The speaker says a five-minute power play did not produce results but did not hurt the team’s momentum, and that the team is still in decent shape and not discouraged. They frame losses and overtime losses as only counting in the loss column and emphasize confidence from scoring goals on Luongo, while expecting a tough next game and a rebound from two prior losses. The speaker criticizes unwanted or unacceptable conduct, saying emotions led to it, and acknowledges it is partly their fault for not addressing it with the team earlier. They discuss a player going to the hospital (Horty) after a blindside hit, expressing concern for his welfare and stating the league should handle any evaluation of the hit. The team discusses adjustments to respond to losing a player and focuses on penalty kill performance and power-play/neutral-zone puck management, including staying away from turnovers. They also describe the team’s mindset as even keel, optimistic about playing at home, and preparing for an important game expected to help turn the series around.

A new ransomware form developed by researchers at Georgia Institute of Technology can take control of a simulated water treatment plant to shut valves, increase chlorine levels, and show false readings. The researchers simulated a hacker holding the facility hostage by threatening to dump large amounts of chlorine unless a ransom is paid, to highlight vulnerabilities in industrial control systems used in facilities like manufacturing plants and water/wastewater treatment sites. They noted ransomware has affected patient data in hospitals and customer data in businesses, and said it encrypts data and demands a ransom for the decryption key. David Formby warned that control systems often assume network access implies authorization and may have weak password and security policies that allow attackers to control components. The paper also states that operators may mistakenly believe systems are air-gapped, while they are often connected. Researchers suggested improving password security, limiting connections, and installing intrusion monitoring systems, warning that attackers may increasingly target industrial control systems as other ransomware targets become harder.

Mary Meeker, a Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers executive, presented her annual Internet trends survey at the Code conference in Rancho Palos Verdes. The global Internet has 3.6 billion users, and Internet usage growth is 7% worldwide, down from 12% the prior year, with growth becoming harder after 50% penetration. Smartphone sales have stalled. She cited improvements in voice computing, Google’s “learning word accuracy” at a 95% rate, and Amazon Echo in over 30 million homes. E-commerce usage rose 16% in 2017 and accounts for 13% of total retail sales, with 49% of shoppers starting on Amazon.com and 36% on search engines; social media referrals to e-commerce purchases rose 6%. Subscription services include Netflix with 117 million subscribers, Amazon Prime with 100 million, and Spotify with 75 million. Ride-hailing Uber has 31 million drivers and Airbnb has 600,000 hosts. The passage also reports unemployment at 3.9% and 7 million job openings.

The passage is an Enron-related news compilation dated late July 2001. It includes Cato Institute commentary claiming California Gov. Gray Davis misrepresented the energy crisis, alongside reports that Reliant Energy and Peoples Energy reported higher profits driven by wholesale-energy unit performance, and that Enron sought India’s government to buy its 65% stake in the Dabhol Power project amid tariff-payment disputes. Reuters and Dow Jones reports say Dabhol rejected Indian state offers as unrealistic and that investigations in California into potential market manipulation included contempt charges and subpoenas for companies including Enron and Reliant. Additional items cover venture capital interest in energy technology, Brazil’s plan to reduce energy demand to avoid blackouts during an energy shortage, a CNNfn “Talking Stocks” segment discussing Tellabs and Enron, and a Bloomberg report that Buenos Aires printed the “patacon” currency to pay bills and workers.

The passage describes research on training deep neural network classifiers to identify medical imaging modality types in a hyper-scale multimodal dataset. A dataset of 4.5 million images was created by combining 102 medical imaging datasets, selecting four target modalities: CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray. ResNet-50, ResNet-18, and VGG16 models were trained to classify images by modality across many body locations and were tested on unseen data. The best-performing model achieved 96% classification accuracy on the test set, with a balanced accuracy of 86%, and strong performance on CT, MRI, and PET. The authors report dataset-level results and note weaker X-ray performance in some datasets. They conclude that hyper-scale modality classification is feasible and suggest future work to extend the approach to 3D scans.

The passage provides instructions and information for the SanDisk Sansa c200. It describes how to record voice using the record button, connect the device to a computer via USB 2.0 (showing as a “Sansa c200” drive), and transfer photos using Sansa Media Converter. It lists supported still image formats, explains how to delete and synchronize files, and gives steps to safely remove the device in MTP or MSC mode.
