It also covers file transfer behavior in MTP/MSC modes, troubleshooting/FAQ topics (supported formats, DRM-related playback rights, and firmware updates), and service and warranty information, plus end-user license terms, disposal instructions, and Microsoft WM-DRM related notices.

The Korean Government asked Chinese aid after rebellion success in the south, leading to 2,000 Chinese troops being dispatched to Asan; however, the Koreans captured the chief rebels and recaptured Chon-ju before the Chinese actively helped. The Korean Government later asked the Chinese to leave when Japanese troops were sent, but the Chinese stayed after Japanese marines and soldiers arrived at Chemulpo and came to Seoul. Mr. Otori stated the Japanese troops were for protecting Japanese subjects and his legation. The Chinese complied with a 1885 Tien-tsin convention requiring notification before landing troops in Korea, while later Japanese landings at Chemulpo occurred without consent from other powers; this prompted an earnest protest by the writer and alarm in Korea. The King begged the Chinese to leave, but both Chinese and Japanese troops refused to withdraw first, raising fears of bloodshed; Chinese subjects were reportedly leaving for China due to fear of a Japanese butchery. Multiple nations’ ships were present at Chemulpo, Admiral Skerrett arrived and met with the American envoy and the King, and he promised to remain. A report suggested Japan might be sending more troops to Fusan and Wensan, and the U.S. instruction was to use every possible effort to preserve peaceful conditions.

The passage argues that mass formal schooling systems cause largely unnoticed systemic educational harm, rooted in their hierarchical and authoritarian nature. It presents a framework for harm based on adversely affecting students’ important interests, then classifies harm as personal (e.g., bullying and verbal violence) and systemic (structural, objective, and symbolic). Systemic harm is described as patterned social control, prioritizing obedience and conformity, transmitting ideologies of control and acquiescence, and using coercive structures like assessments, surveillance, rewards, and punishments, which can undermine motivation, engagement, privacy, critical thinking, and well-being.  

The passage further develops an “educational pacifist” morality: educational practices are justified only if they do not harm innocents, and mass formal schooling is said to fail this condition because it treats students as means through extensive harms. It then compares this view with Montessori’s ideas, stating that Montessori broadly aligned with educational pacifism by critiquing schooling practices that dominate children, repress their drive to learn, and rely on coercion. Montessori is presented as promoting “positive peace” through systemic protection of the child, freedom of harmonious activity, and reform toward nonharmful educational alternatives. The passage concludes that contemporary Montessori education should reject educational harm and avoid pressures that replicate coercive schooling practices.

The passage explains that the DAX (Deutscher Aktienindex) is Germany’s main equity index, consisting of the 40 biggest or most liquid blue-chip stocks listed on Deutsche Börse Xetra (expanded from 30 companies in 2021). It describes why traders use DAX trading strategies, citing high liquidity, low-cost access (especially via DAX futures on Eurex), and diversification from different trading hours and how DAX movements differ from US markets. It outlines three ways to trade DAX 40: DAX futures (standardized, highly liquid, traded on margin with daily profit/loss settlement and possible margin calls), CFDs (popular in the UK), and ETFs (mostly for investing). The passage also notes trading hours for DAX futures (0750 to 2200 CET) and contract details for original, mini, and micro versions, including multipliers, tick size, and quarterly expiration. It presents backtested overnight strategies from November 2021 (enter 17:30 CET, exit 09:00 CET; 209 trades, 65% win rate, profit factor 2, max drawdown 5.1%) and November 2022 (enter at 17:30 CET, exit at 09:00 CET next day; average gain 0.23% per trade; 303 trades). It states that mean reversion, breakout, gap, and momentum strategies can work on DAX, and that futures rules and settings differ from S&P 500 futures.

The lecture introduces MIT 6.832 Underactuated Robotics and discusses why underactuated robotics is important. The instructor contrasts conservative, high-gain robot control (illustrated by Honda’s ASIMO) with more energy-efficient walking that relies on natural dynamics (illustrated by a Cornell passive dynamic walker). He makes similar points using aircraft, explaining that more complex flight regimes can reduce the need for strict control by leveraging aerodynamic dynamics. He argues that underactuated systems use dynamics more cleverly rather than relying on control to override dynamics, requiring smarter control methods.

The lecture then defines underactuated systems using a second-order robot dynamics form that is linear in control inputs. A system is fully actuated when the matrix multiplying the inputs has full rank, allowing arbitrary accelerations, and underactuated when this rank is less than the dimension of the state coordinates. He explains that whether a system is underactuated can depend on the state (e.g., due to torque limits or obstacles). He gives examples using a two-link robotic arm, including feedback linearization for fully actuated cases, and then modifies the system by removing a motor to create an underactuated example (the “Acrobot”). He further argues that many real robotics problems—walking, jumping, flying, and manipulation before full force closure—are underactuated due to limited control authority.

The instructor outlines the course plan: starting with simple pendulum dynamics and control, progressing through model systems (cart-pole, Acrobot, compass gait walking robots), then increasing complexity with impacts, higher degrees of freedom, uncertainty, and unknown models. He describes the course’s computational approach, including optimal control, numerical methods (dynamic programming), reinforcement learning/policy search, motion planning, and machine learning for harder cases.

The Yankees and Blue Jays, who tied for the best American League record with Toronto holding the tiebreaker, will face each other in a best-of-five ALDS. The series begins Saturday, Oct. 4, with Games 1, 2, and 5 in Toronto and Games 3 and 4 in the Bronx. New York reached the ALDS by defeating the Red Sox in Game 3, while Toronto received a bye as the top seed; the teams split the regular season series 8-5. Games 1 and 2 will air live on Fox and FS1, respectively, while broadcasts for Games 3-5 are to be determined.

The passage is a lecture by Tor author Nick Mathewson about Tor and anonymity. It explains motivations for anonymity networks, describes Tor as an anonymity system using volunteer-operated servers and discusses common uses of anonymity (privacy for individuals, research, protection of sensitive corporate data, and needs of law enforcement). It defines anonymity concepts (unobservability, unlinkability, unlinkability, and related attacker-linking notions) and contrasts them with other goals. The lecture outlines how Tor provides “forward anonymity” using onion routing with layered encryption, circuit setup using TLS links and key negotiation (TAP/NTor), and relaying TCP stream contents rather than raw IP or higher-level proxies. It discusses challenges like correlation attacks via timing/volume, probabilistic vs provable anonymity, node discovery through distributed consensus by trusted authorities, and reasons for abuse controls (noting that criminals and abuse exist, and that IP-based blocking often leads to Tor users being banned). It covers hidden services and how responders can remain anonymous using introduction/handshake concepts, and mentions planned improvements such as key blinding to resist enumeration attacks. The lecture also reviews attacks and defenses, including application-layer risks from unencrypted traffic, traffic tagging from integrity-checking weaknesses, denial-of-service considerations, censorship resistance using pluggable transports/bridges, and examples of cryptographic implementation pitfalls (e.g., Diffie-Hellman misuse). The speaker concludes with future work areas and related systems to study.

Seven months after the Trump administration made “deep cuts” at the U.S. Department of Education, some researchers described developments as “cautiously optimistic” for federal education research. The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) planned to reinstate 20 research contracts after lawsuits, and another lawsuit could provide a brief reprieve for 10 federally funded items. The department also sought public guidance on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) and IES staff and activities have continued in some areas, including survey updates. However, researchers and experts said severe staff shortages and other priorities could threaten data quality, research progress, and reporting. They also discussed disruptions to the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), concerns about NAEP operations and reporting changes, and the expected reinstatement of the regional education labs (RELs). Some observers said RELs and related support systems had been weakened by the cuts, while others argued IES should continue even if reconfigured.

The passage explains that saving soccer penalty kicks is highly stressful and challenging, with a general chance of making the save of under 15%, while about 80% of penalty kicks are scored and around 5% are missed. It outlines Law 14, describing when a penalty kick is awarded and the strict procedures for the kicker, goalkeeper, and other players, including how the ball is placed and when it is in play. It also covers consequences of goalkeeper violations, coaching guidance for preparing goalkeepers (including preparation, training, equipment, and positive support), and methods for decision-making such as “read and react” using cues from penalty takers. The passage further gives detailed guidance on goalkeeper psychological and mental preparation (visualization, positive self-talk, routines, controlled breathing, staying present) and physical preparation (fitness, equipment, diving technique), plus actions immediately before and during the kick, and how to respond after various outcomes like goals, misses, deflections, rebounds, and saved shots. It emphasizes teammates’ responsibilities after saves and discusses additional research on opponents, “keeping book,” and potential “rattling the kicker” tactics that must not violate the Law. It concludes with reminders for understanding and applying related laws and studies suggesting goalkeepers may take positions slightly off-center to affect perceived goal size.

Shares of housing-related companies traded up 2%-5% on the BSE after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced incentives to boost rural and urban housing post-demonetization. At 10:13 am, the S&P BSE Sensex was down 0.39% (104 points) at 26,523. The passage also lists several companies’ price changes between 08/11/2016, 26/12/2016, and 30/12/2016, showing both declines from 08/11/2016 to 26/12/2016 and gains by 30/12/2016.

The passage describes a hockey team’s confidence from scoring early goals, especially on a power play and following key moments like Oleg Saprykin blocking a shot. It discusses leadership and team dynamics, including the value of captains and quiet leaders, and mentions practices and traditions such as wearing a green hat. Players and coaches emphasize limiting space for a crafty opponent, using different parts of the ice rather than only the boards, being disciplined, and skating out of the defensive zone more effectively. The team’s goaltending (Kiprusoff) is highlighted for bouncing back after a rough game. The passage also covers how coaching changes increased accountability, prevented long slumps, and built mental toughness and readiness for the playoffs, aided by offseason and end-of-year player acquisitions.

Jeff Davis Parish is preparing for the first full week of the school year after opening school doors last Friday. Educators say preparations included streamlining district processes, campus work by custodians, and implementing “streamlined processes from the top down” at Jennings Elementary, along with teacher commitment to students’ success. During the summer, bus summer classes and behind-the-wheel training were provided for substitute and activity bus drivers seeking Louisiana certification, and orientations and meetings were held with administrators, teachers, and staff. Educators evaluated students’ academic levels to design plans using the same curriculum while meeting state requirements. The parish is ranked fourth in the state for graduation rate, with 92.5% of students graduating on time, which is 3 percentage points higher than last year.

The passage describes metagenomic binning, which clusters fragmented DNA reads so each cluster corresponds to a distinct genome. Binning depends on DNA representations that preserve genomic similarity and dissimilarity, and accurate embeddings are important for downstream analyses. Traditionally, DNA fragments are represented with k-mer profiles and embedded deterministically for clustering; however, deterministic embeddings cannot fully resolve issues such as DNA sequences shared across multiple genomes and the difficulty of separating sequences with highly similar k-mer profiles. To address this, the authors propose a probabilistic embedding framework that maps each fragment to a distribution in embedding space, explicitly modeling ambiguity and uncertainty. They use a contrastive-learning formulation that yields closed-form expressions for expected pairwise likelihood and provides theoretical analysis of sequences that produce large covariance terms. The approach, called UNCERTAINGEN, is presented as a first probabilistic embedding framework for DNA metagenomic binning extending k-mer-based methods, with theoretical guarantees and empirical results showing improvements over deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings. The passage also outlines related work on DNA embedding models and probabilistic embeddings for contrastive learning, and begins to define the proposed model and objective.

The passage describes a scoping review by Tyminski and colleagues on “Belonging in Higher Education: Implications for Occupational Therapy Education.” The review was conducted to identify barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate health professions education and to determine implications for occupational therapy education. The authors identified 202 studies, narrowed to 70 after title/abstract screening and duplicate removal, excluded 61 after full-text review, and included 9 articles that addressed belonging across occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medicine graduate education. Qualitative content analysis found three themes contributing to both barriers and facilitators: (1) environment (including physical space and institutional culture/climate), (2) relationships (faculty-to-student and peer-to-peer), and (3) personal factors (students’ perceptions of belonging and academic ability). The authors argue that as occupational therapy programs diversify, ensuring students experience belonging is essential for educational success and future healthcare career outcomes, and they outline implications such as creating inclusive and accessible spaces, supporting mentorship and peer relationships, and addressing bias and microaggressions.

The Supreme Court rejected several appeals, including Alex Jones’s challenge to a Connecticut case where he was found liable for defamation and emotional distress related to Sandy Hook families, and an appeal by Colorado parents claiming a school district violated their constitutional rights by excluding them from discussions of their children’s gender identity. The court also denied review in other cases, including a lawsuit against Grindr that a lower court dismissed under Section 230, and a death penalty case involving alleged juror misconduct, as well as challenges to cannabis-related fines without a jury trial, and other matters where the court sought the views of the U.S. solicitor general in two cases. The court granted one new case from its Oct. 10 conference but added no additional cases to the 2025–26 oral argument calendar.

The passage describes research on autonomous endovascular navigation for mechanical thrombectomy (MT), aiming to address limited MT access, delayed treatment effects, and operator-related risks. It proposes a world model–based reinforcement learning framework for MT, focusing on phase-one navigation split into five multi-task stages (A1, A2L, A2R, A3L, A3R) across ten patient-specific vascular anatomies in a CT-based in silico simulation (stEVE with SOFA and industry-standard device parameters). Two RL agents are compared: SAC (model-free) and TD-MPC2 (model-based with planning using a learned dynamics model). Single-task training showed SAC achieved 100% success for A1 and A2R, with lower-but-high performance in other tasks. In multi-task, multi-vasculature training, TD-MPC2 significantly improved mean success rate to 65% versus 37% for SAC (p < 0.001) and showed task-specific improvements in success rate and path ratio, though procedure time increased with TD-MPC2 across tasks. The study concludes that world model–based RL can better generalize across diverse anatomies for autonomous MT, while noting remaining limitations and suggesting future work on improving generalization, planning efficiency, simulator fidelity, and comparisons with image-based RL.

Actress Allison Mack, known for “Smallville,” was released from jail on $5 million bail bond and ordered to await trial on charges of recruiting women to serve as sex slaves in a secret society run by Keith Raniere. A U.S. magistrate judge released her after her parents agreed to put their California home up as collateral and Mack, 35, agreed to live with her parents under house arrest. Federal prosecutors charged Mack with sex trafficking and conspiracy related to her involvement in Nxivm’s Albany organization, which they said was presented as a female mentorship group; Mack pleaded not guilty and the two sides are in plea negotiations. Prosecutors allege that Raniere was arrested on sex trafficking charges and is held without bail, and they accuse the group of branding women, imposing restrictive diets, forcing sex, and using blackmail based on information and assets.

The memorandum addresses cross-litigation in Barnhill’s Buffet, Inc.’s bankruptcy and related adversary proceedings. The court considered Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and Dynamic Management Company, LLC’s motions for summary judgment against SCS General Contractors, Inc. The court found no material facts in dispute and ruled as a matter of law that Wells was entitled to judgment: SCS’s asserted equitable lien claims failed as to the leaseholds because the debtor-in-possession/bona fide purchaser status terminated any such lien, and SCS was not a third-party beneficiary of the leases. The court also ruled that no lien could attach to fee interests under Mississippi law because the landlords did not provide written consent. The court granted Dynamic’s motion as well, dismissing SCS’s alter-ego/joint liability claims, finding SCS failed to present sufficient evidence to rebut Dynamic’s affidavit statements. The court denied SCS’s request for a continuance for further discovery. It also dismissed cross-claims against Spirit Finance Corporation as unopposed.

The passage describes the “Household Sewing Machines-Global Market Status and Trend Report 2013-2023,” which provides market analysis, data, and insights from 2013–2017 and forecasts for 2018–2023. It covers global and regional market size, manufacturing and supplier landscape, market status and trends by mechanical vs electronic types and home vs light commercial applications, and cost/profit and marketing status. It also addresses market growth drivers and challenges. The report segments the market by region (North America, Europe, China, Japan, Rest APAC, Latin America), type (Mechanical, Electronic), application (Home, Light Commercial), and major manufacturers (including Brother, Singer, Janome, Necchi, Bernina International, and others), with planned sections on production, demand, imports/exports, competition, and manufacturer sales and financial metrics.

The passage explains that many people in Western countries avoid eating insects due to the everyday presence and unusual movement of bugs, despite insects being similar to shrimp or lobster. It cites a United Nations estimate that around two billion people regularly eat bugs, noting that many insect species are edible and may provide healthy fats, protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals while being more ecologically sustainable than other animal proteins. It says fears include whether insects’ tough exoskeletons are digestible, but recent research in *Molecular Biology and Evolution* found that most primates have genes evolved to break down insect chitin. The passage adds that cooked insects can be easier to chew and digest, and it describes the Seattle Mariners’ 2017 promotion of roasted grasshoppers (chapulines), which sold more in three games than a restaurant typically sells in a year.

The passage discusses the U.S. Department of Education’s effort to revisit the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) and argues for protecting and strengthening federal education research and development. It cites a coalition’s letter recommending: prioritizing research tied to state and local needs; maximizing impact through coordination, scale, and infrastructure; and helping states and districts use knowledge operationally through better communication and support. It proposes creating learning agendas, establishing faster research tracks for high-need topics, streamlining study approvals, and using rapid-cycle tools like the School PULSE survey for real-time data. It also suggests modernizing data submission and reporting through EDPass, restarting Regional Education Laboratories (RELs) and Comprehensive Centers (CCs) programs, addressing the “last mile” problem with technologies and district support structures, requiring practitioner-facing implementation resources in IES studies, and recognizing effective use of research to improve student outcomes. The passage concludes that the goal is an efficient, effective, and accountable federal education research and development system to support scalable improvement for students, educators, and families.

LG last week unveiled the G7 ThinQ smartphone in South Africa. It is positioned as a competitive next-tier flagship, featuring Gorilla Glass 5, slim bezels, a bright screen, and an AI-focused set of functions including “AI Cam” with 19 shooting modes and a dedicated Google Assistant button that also supports Google Lens via a double press. The phone uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon 845 processor with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage (expandable via microSD), and it has a two-lens rear camera (up to 16MP) and an 8MP front camera. LG expects the G7 ThinQ to reach South African shops in early June at a starting cash price of about R13,999.

Tucson News Now reports that a disabled Navy veteran, Gerard Ah-Fook, had his specialized handcycle stolen from his front porch on the northwest side. After seeing the story about the theft, Randy Sooter stepped in to surprise Ah-Fook by giving him a handcycle, and both expressed appreciation and encouragement about continuing paracycling. Police are still searching for the person who stole the bike, described as a recumbent three-wheel bike with a white frame and red lettering reading “Top End Force RX.”

The passage outlines liabilities and then a “diplomatic offensive” targeting Bulgaria, Serbia, Italy, Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, and France. It recommends public support for Bulgaria and Serbia, strong moves toward Italy including assurances about evacuation and economic needs, and an approach to Austria-Hungary emphasizing national subjection while repeatedly assuring no dismemberment and highlighting debts to Germany. For Germany it calls for penalties tied to democratization, assurances not to dictate government forms, and different treatment toward a responsible Germany. For Russia it suggests stating war aims, promoting a league of nations, and showing the diplomatic offensive is underway. It also advises boosting France’s morale regarding Alsace-Lorraine and coordinating the western Allies through economic unity and supportive U.S. statements to Liberals in Great Britain and France. The passage includes a suggested statement of peace terms: Germany must evacuate Belgium and restore Northern France; Luxembourg is to be ignored for now and left to negotiation; and Alsace-Lorraine must be returned, with Germany unable to escape its conduct since 1871.

The passage argues that distraction leads to long-term losses such as productivity decline, falling revenues, and missed opportunities, and presents eight strategies from various entrepreneurs and experts to improve focus. These include adopting urgency to avoid regret, scheduling deep work away from the office, using a “heck-yes” filter for opportunities, removing unnecessary diversions and tackling one top-priority task at a time, finding something to become genuinely obsessed with, following a customized five-step plan (stress management, morning routine, work in 90-minute blocks, recharging rituals, and sleep optimization), avoiding multitasking between competing priorities, and building an organization-wide “fierce focus culture” with clear measurable goals and a focus filter for decisions and ideas.

The passage describes an AI-assisted activity training system and methods. It claims priority to a U.S. provisional application and relates to providing indoor activity training with guidance, monitoring, and feedback. The disclosed method presents activity categories and multimedia guidance steps via a rendering device, receives a voice-based training plan in a source language, uses an NLP model configured with a single intermediate language to extract selected activities and activity attributes, and then initiates multimedia presentation. It detects the start of the user’s activity performance, captures video using one or more distributed cameras, and processes the video in real time with an AI model to extract user performance parameters. The AI model compares these parameters to target performance parameters to generate feedback, which is rendered to the user in aural, visual, or haptic form contemporaneously with the performance. The passage also describes system and computer program product embodiments that perform similar functions, and includes details about example devices (e.g., smart mirror, display devices), GUI elements for selecting activities and attributes, and additional workflows such as creating/saving training circuits and controlling multimedia/feedback based on intermediate voice input.

Shares in sausage skin maker Devro have risen by almost a quarter since the stock was bought in January. Interim results show first-half sales up 11% to just over £125m, supported by demand in Russia, south-east Asia, and China, where the firm has a new plant. The new facility is currently weighing on return capital, though Devro maintained high cash conversion. The company expects profits, cash, and return on capital to improve as plant output increases, with Peter Page expecting full capacity by the end of the year.

Strength training offers benefits such as building muscle mass, strength, and endurance, but using correct techniques and warming up and cooling down properly is important to prevent injuries. Rotator cuff injuries are common and can occur due to repetitive overhead motions; they may include tears or tendinopathy and can require examination, scans, referral, or surgery depending on severity. Prevention tips include good shoulder blade posture and adjusting exercises if they cause discomfort. The passage also describes hamstring injuries (often from sudden powerful movements), herniated discs (caused by sudden extreme or repetitive poor movements), tendon injuries and tendonitis (linked to micro tears and repetitive motions), and tennis elbow and golfer’s elbow (related to repetitive wrist and arm movements). It advises gradually increasing workout intensity, warming up (to raise heart rate and blood flow), cooling down (to help regulate blood flow), not pushing beyond comfort, getting help if needed, and consulting a doctor if pain persists.

Fall 2017 University of North Texas commencement ceremonies are scheduled for Dec. 15 and Dec. 16 (Friday and Saturday) at the UNT Coliseum (600 Avenue D) and the UNT Murchison Performing Arts Center (2100 North Interstate 35 East) in Denton. Bachelor’s degree ceremonies run from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Dec. 15 and from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Dec. 16, and a combined master’s and doctoral ceremony is set for 7 p.m. on Dec. 15. More than 3,400 students are expected to receive degrees, including 2,731 undergraduates, 615 master’s, and 72 doctoral students eligible for fall ceremonies, with additional graduates from summer also attending. Ceremonies will be livestreamed, with separate links for each venue. Graduates attending the New Orleans Bowl are invited to a special Dec. 15 commencement in New Orleans at 6:15 p.m. at the Hilton New Orleans Riverside (Grand Salon A), with a reception following. Full regalia is not required, though mortar boards, tams, and hoods are encouraged; students must RSVP online.

VentureWire’s Tuesday, October 31, 2000 issue summarizes private company business news, including “Top Stories” about Trinity Ventures closing a $540 million fund, Sun Microsystems planning a $100 million investment in wireless firms, BigWords.com ceasing operations, and Concrete laying off 15% of staff. It also lists “New Money” funding rounds for multiple companies across sectors such as networking, optical technology, broadband, colocation, and software, plus “M&A,” “New Directors,” “New People,” “VC Fund News,” “VC Personnel,” and a “VW Corrections” note stating that an item on Candescent Technology understated its overall funding, which is more than $600 million.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s 2017 Form 10-K includes corporate details and a business overview describing its customer-centric principles, segments (North America, International, and AWS), and offerings to consumers, sellers, developers and enterprises, and content creators. It lists risk factors, including intense competition, strains from rapid expansion, fluctuations in operating results, international and regulatory risks, fulfillment network and data center risks, seasonality, commercial agreements and acquisitions, foreign exchange risk, key personnel risk, data security and system interruption risk, inventory and intellectual property risks, stock price volatility, government regulation and tax risks, supplier risks, government contract risks, product liability, and payments-related risks. It also provides information on unresolved staff comments (none), properties and facility square footage, market information for common stock, and selected consolidated financial data for 2013–2017.

The passage describes a difficult game in which the team lost a lead after making soft plays and errors against a high-caliber Detroit team. The team used stick checking instead of body positioning, which the speaker says is ineffective against Detroit’s caliber. The speaker does not address the team after games, but believes they will bounce back, noting positive aspects, strong goaltending by Olie, and that defense appeared tired, allowing perimeter shots. The team plans to respond at home and, if needed, try to win in Detroit over multiple attempts.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated March 17, 2021. The filing states that a revised press release (Exhibit 99.1) announced the expiration of Microsoft’s previously announced exchange offers for certain debt securities, with the aggregate amount of 3.041% Notes due 2062 to be issued corrected to $1,934,966,000. On March 17, 2021, Microsoft issued $6,250,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 2.921% Notes due 2052 and $1,934,966,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.041% Notes due 2062 as the new notes in connection with the exchange offers. The notes will pay interest semi-annually and mature on March 17, 2052 and March 17, 2062, respectively. The report also lists related exhibits, including the Fourteenth Supplemental Indenture and forms of the notes, and includes the signature of Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

The Supreme Court appointed senior counsel Amarendra Sharan as amicus curiae to examine material produced by petitioner Pankaj Kumud Chandra Phadnis regarding whether further inquiry is needed into a larger conspiracy behind Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination. The bench of Justices S.A. Bobde and L.Nageswara Rao said prima facie the material was insufficient to order a fresh inquiry. During the hearing, the court questioned why the petitioner approached it at this stage, noting the conviction was upheld by the High Court and executions occurred in 1949; it was also stated that the Supreme Court did not examine the case on merits. The petitioner challenged the Bombay High Court’s June 6, 2016 order and claimed British Secret Service Force 136 was involved, including an allegation that the Indian Ambassador to USSR was informed in February 1948 about British organization of the murder. Phadnis described the investigation as a cover-up and argued there is no legal or factual basis to blame Marathi people or Veer Savarkar, asserting there is a need for a new Commission of Inquiry to uncover the larger conspiracy.

The passage describes three separate topics from 2000. It reports that three small-bidding entrepreneurs won rights from the U.S. Department of Energy to withdraw oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, but faced deadlines and lack of required financial guarantees; one entrepreneur, Lance Stroud, had his mother die during the financing scramble and later lost the deal, another, Renard D. Euell, partnered with Enron but ultimately missed paperwork deadlines, and a third, Ronald Peek, later transferred his interest to Hess Energy Trading Co. The passage also covers a $26 million funding round for Artesia Technologies, a digital asset management company seeking partnerships with information management firms; and it discusses Houston’s proposed November 7 election for building a new indoor basketball arena, including arguments about who benefits financially, how costs would be covered through public taxes and bonds, and conflicting views from supporters and opponents.

Angel, a five-year-old born in a Pakistani slum, came to Australia 18 months ago suffering from CLOVES syndrome, a rare condition with documented cases worldwide. Her condition caused severe pain, misshapen swelling feet, and malnutrition, and she was bullied and refused entry to school in her community. After being too weak for surgery when she arrived, she is now preparing for a double amputation of both feet, to be performed free of charge in Melbourne by Australian surgeon Professor Tony Pennington, with Moira Kelly’s surgical team involved. Her mother says Pakistani doctors previously said her daughter could not be treated and would have “no more life,” and Angel is reportedly aware she will lose both feet and the bottom parts of both legs but remains hopeful and “over the moon” about the operation.

The passage describes host-environment dependencies and required/optional call-out interfaces for AGESA™ software, including the need for the host to establish stack and call-out routing/port support before invoking procedures inside AGESA. It explains how a call-out router translates function numbers into execution addresses, the expected router function interface, and parameter structures used by call-outs (e.g., configuration data passed without conversion). The text outlines UEFI execution phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP), build tooling for different phases, and UEFI-specific configuration and stack enable/disable procedures (AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and related stackless behavior), including status codes and register/stack requirements. It further describes AGESA build approaches (binary modules vs. source integration), key initialization procedures for PEI/DXE/RTB (including PEIM modules for early processor and post-reset memory initialization, PPIs/HOBs/events, and coordination/reset logic), and DXE drivers that generate tables and provide protocols. Additional sections include platform configuration options and examples of required host environment call-outs for buffer allocation/deallocation, MMIO mapping updates, event log access, and system reset initiation, along with guidance about cache-as-RAM usage rules and parallel core considerations.

The lecture introduces graph limits as an analytic limit concept for discrete graphs and motivates it using an optimization problem where a minimizer becomes a limiting sequence rather than a single value. It describes graphons—symmetric measurable functions \(W:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]\)—as limit objects for graph sequences, and explains how graphs can be converted to graphons via pixelated adjacency matrices. It discusses homomorphism densities (equivalently subgraph densities in the limit) and defines graphon homomorphism densities using integrals. Convergence of graph sequences is defined as convergence of homomorphism densities for every fixed graph \(H\), and it is related to convergence in the cut metric. The cut norm and cut distance between graphons are defined using the infimum over measure-preserving bijections, with measure-preserving transformations used to handle vertex relabeling. The lecture then states three main theorems: equivalence of convergence via homomorphism/subgraph densities and convergence in the cut metric (Theorem 1), existence of a limiting graphon for any convergent sequence (Theorem 2), and compactness of the space of graphons up to distance zero (Theorem 3).

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on May 31, 2016 regarding its 2016 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. Stockholders voted on three proposals: (1) election of Class III directors Brad W. Buss and Ira Ehrenpreis; (2) approval to ratify PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2016; and (3) a stockholder proposal on supermajority stockholder voting provisions, which was not approved. The company’s inspector of election certified the vote tabulations, and the report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel, on June 3, 2016.

The CBEC says verification of GST transitional credit can only be done by the tax authority, which led it to give central CGST officers jurisdiction to verify transitional credit claims even when taxpayers are assigned to the state government. The Centre is concerned that some taxpayers over-claim transitional credits, which total Rs 1.6 lakh crore since GST launch and have reduced cash CGST payments. CBEC instructions provide for detailed verification and note that only 5–7% of claims were preliminarily found invalid. The change could affect centre-state power sharing and may lead to litigation, experts said. The CBEC also directs that the CGST Act should be amended to exclude credit of earlier-regime cesses as valid, and mentions that some taxpayers have claimed Swachch Bharat and education cess credits because the law does not specifically prohibit them; experts said any amendment must address how to deal with such credits. Others said the government’s instructions are within its legal rights.

Attorney General Patrick Morrisey renewed a contract with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission to protect West Virginians from potentially dangerous products. The CPSC Commissioning Program allows his office’s investigators to visit stores statewide to monitor for recalled items and ensure proper recall notices are posted. Investigators look for recalled non-food products such as appliances, clothing, children’s products, exercise equipment, electronic devices, and furniture. Since 2015, state investigators have conducted more than 40 compliance checks and expect 25 additional searches between February and September.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), a six-meter off-axis crossed-Dragone telescope at 5600 m on Cerro Chajnantor, with observations scheduled to begin in 2026. Two instruments are being built for FYST: Mod-Cam (a cryogenic testbed for a 280 GHz broadband camera) and Prime-Cam (the primary science instrument for broadband polarimeteric observations from 280–850 GHz, with additional spectroscopy at 210–420 GHz). The work characterizes Mod-Cam’s flexible stripline circuitry used to connect KID detectors to warm readout electronics by measuring copper RRR and thermal conductivity, estimating thermal loading for Mod-Cam and Prime-Cam stripline configurations, and measuring thermal conductivity in a dilution refrigerator. It also addresses elevated inter-channel crosstalk observed during Mod-Cam readout testing, identifies custom SMP-SMA transition PCBs as the source, and reports that redesigns and HFSS simulations predict improved crosstalk performance meeting project requirements.

The passage presents an options-based trading strategy for participating in an anticipated upward move in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) without immediately buying AMD shares. It describes AMD trading in a range (about $9.30 to $15.13) with support near $10, and suggests a potential catalyst from AMD’s Q1 2018 earnings announcement around 4/25/2018. 

Three options approaches are outlined using a May 04, 2018 expiration: (1) buying a $10 call for about $0.60, where the buyer can profit if AMD rises above the $10 strike (with static defined risk of $60 per contract); (2) a $10/$12 call spread, buying the $10 call and selling the $12 call to reduce net cost (about $0.50), with capped profits above $12 and risk if AMD falls below $10; and (3) selling a cash-covered $10 put for about $0.56, which can reduce effective cost basis to about $9.44 and can be combined with the call spread to reduce total net cost, but adds the risk of being assigned shares if AMD falls below $10. 

The author concludes that AMD may perform well on earnings due to positive catalysts and notes a large AMD short position that could contribute to a squeeze if results and guidance are positive. The author discloses they are long AMD (and INTC, NVDA).

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 2, 2015. The report states that on October 2, 2015 Tesla published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1, incorporated by reference. The information is intended to be furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01 and is not to be deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference in other filings except as specifically referenced. The exhibit listed is Exhibit 99.1, the press release dated October 2, 2015. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel, on October 2, 2015.

Police said a felon armed with a slungshot forced entry into an apartment at Stark Street Villa Apartments in southeast Portland on Thursday at 9:46 p.m. Officers responded after witnesses reported a man trying to break into apartments and threatening to kill people while holding an unidentified object. After knocking produced no response, officers forced entry and found a frightened woman and the suspect, Jason A. Clifford, who was taken into custody. A slungshot was found in the apartment, and investigators believe it was the item Clifford carried. Clifford, 37, was arrested and booked into Multnomah County Jail on charges including first-degree burglary and felon in possession of a restricted weapon. Two other people in the apartment, Dustin L. Baker and Lindsey M. Walker, were also arrested on outstanding warrants but were not believed to be involved in Clifford’s actions.

The passage describes WIRED’s review and selection of white-noise and sound machines aimed at improving sleep by masking other noises. It explains that “white noise” contains all audible frequencies, while “pink” and “brown” noise are lower in the spectrum and may be less grating; these noise “colors” can be available in one device. The passage reviews multiple models, including the LectroFan Classic (fan or colored noise options, timers, and decibel range), the Snooz (fan-generated white noise with simple controls), and the Hatch 3/Rest models (sound libraries with sunrise or night-light features and subscription details), plus portable and baby-oriented options with timers, lights, and connectivity features. It also includes guidance on running machines all night, whether fans can substitute for white noise machines, and how WIRED selects, tests, and handles donated products after testing.

The Inverted Hammer (also called the bullish inverted hammer) is a single-candle bullish reversal pattern that forms at the bottom of downtrends. It has a small body near the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow, suggesting buyers are gaining momentum and a price upswing may follow, though confirmation with other technical tools is recommended. Traders may use it for swing trading or mean reversion by combining it with trendlines, support levels, moving averages, momentum oscillators, and volume, and should manage risk with stop-loss orders and position sizing. The passage states that backtests on S&P 500 indicate profitability (average gain of 0.36% per trade), with a reported win rate of 70% and a 53–65% win ratio when exiting after 1–10 days; it is also described as relatively frequent. The main disadvantage is that the pattern is subjective, may produce false signals, and may not suit every timeframe. It is not the same as the Shooting Star, though it is described as similar.

President Donald Trump will direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to assess whether to investigate Chinese laws, policies, practices, or actions that may be unreasonable or discriminatory and harm American intellectual property, innovation, and technology. Administration officials said this could lead to steep tariffs, while also stating the potential trade probe is unrelated to U.S. diplomacy efforts regarding North Korea. They said any investigation could take up to a year, and that actions against China could be resolved through a negotiated agreement. The announcement follows Trump’s efforts to pressure China to do more on North Korea, and he postponed an earlier expected Section 301 investigation while seeking cooperation from Beijing.

Violet Brown, a Jamaican woman who worked cutting sugarcane, attended church regularly, avoids pork and chicken, and celebrated her 117th birthday last month. She is believed to have become the world’s oldest living person after the death of Emma Morano, and said she is surprised but grateful. Robert Young of the Gerontology Research Group said he has met Brown and examined her birth certificate issued by British authorities, and that she is the oldest person with sufficient documentation. Jamaica’s prime minister congratulated her, while Guinness World Records said it is researching candidates and will not confirm until its processes are complete. Brown has two caregivers, rests most of the day, can sit up and walk short distances, and attributes her long life to hard work and her Christian faith.

A University of California, Davis study in *Annals of Epidemiology* reviewed 50,921 firearm deaths in California from 2000 to 2015 and found gun deaths fell over the 16-year period. Researchers reported 24,922 firearm homicides and 23,682 gun suicides. The firearm homicide rate dropped from 4.19 per 100,000 people in 2000 to 3.13 in 2014, then rose slightly in 2015. Veronica Pear attributed the decline to reduced gang violence, especially in Los Angeles County, and noted decreases in gun homicides of black men (32% from 2005 to 2015) and Hispanic men (38% from 2005 to 2015), while rates for white and Asian men stayed about the same. The passage also describes limited federal funding for gun-violence studies and mentions new funding efforts, including California’s $5 million over five years for UC Davis and Kaiser Permanente’s $2 million study.

The passage contrasts digital laggards and digital leaders in how they set goals and use data. It says laggards set aspirational goals poorly grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement, rely on qualitative “proof of effort,” and focus on process adherence, which can stifle innovation. It explains that leaders use data-driven objectives aligned to strategy through transparent methodology, enabling teams to connect their own goals to a shared “North Star” vision while coordinating across organization levels. It also describes risks for leaders when quantitative analysis overhead becomes too high, potentially slowing even simple decisions. The passage further argues that adopting a data culture aligns organizations vertically and horizontally and emphasizes learning, transparency, measurement, and consistent cultural behaviors, while laggards face misalignment between espoused and actual behavior. It concludes that organizations often fit into four cultural patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can target actions based on their starting point.

The passage describes NVIDIA GPU and software developments from the Tesla V100 (2017) and T4 (2018) to the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU and its architecture features. It highlights Tensor Cores’ speedups for deep learning matrix computations and discusses software ecosystems such as CUDA, CUDA-X libraries, NVIDIA GPU Cloud (NGC), and Kubernetes on NVIDIA GPUs. The NVIDIA A100 (Ampere/GA100) is presented as an elastic, high-throughput data center GPU with Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) virtualization, a third-generation Tensor Core with TF32/BF16/FP64 support and Sparsity for up to doubled throughput, plus features for scaling (NVLink, NVSwitch) and memory performance (40 GB HBM2, larger L2 cache, L2 residency controls, compute data compression, ECC). The passage also covers CUDA 11 features like CUDA Task Graphs, asynchronous copy and asynchronous barriers, and programming features supporting optimized data movement and synchronization. It further explains DGX A100 as an AI system built from eight A100 GPUs and MIG, and includes background on fine-grained structured sparsity and pruning for sparse neural networks.

The passage describes PSA testing as the most used biomarker in prostate cancer (PCa) clinics and labs, noting that abnormal PSA indicates abnormal growth but is not PCa-specific and can produce false positives, leading to unnecessary invasive treatments. It discusses the use of multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) after PSA testing, yet states that clinically significant PCa can remain undetected in a substantial fraction of cases, making biopsies necessary for histological confirmation, despite their invasiveness and risks. The work focuses on developing point-of-care (PoC) detection of circulating nucleic acid biomarkers using an isothermal nucleic acid amplification approach (RT-pHLAMP) integrated into an ISFET Lab-on-Chip system (“Lacewing”). It targets YAP1 nucleic acid and androgen receptor markers (AR-FL and AR-V7) extracted from blood plasma, aiming for rapid results after minimal processing. The results described include optimization of RNA extraction (using TRIzol LS), rapid detection times with benchtop RT-pHLAMP, and ISFET LoC detection of YAP1 and AR-FL in patient samples with reported concordance to benchtop assays. The passage also reports that YAP1 nucleic acid detection on the LoC correlated with more advanced disease staging and higher initial PSA, and that AR-FL and AR-V7 markers were observed in high-risk or metastatic patients in the tested cohort. Methods for RT-pHLAMP, qPCR, blood processing, Lab-on-Chip operation, statistical analysis, and ethical approval are also provided.

Mark Schroeder comments on an EU restructuring summary, saying it has several errors and omits anti-competitive transitional arrangements in the Netherlands, and that Poland is an “interesting omission” from Central and Eastern Europe. The underlying attached material is a periodic update (June–November 2000) on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring, noting broad market openings to foreign investors, unbundling, and introduction of competition, with country-by-country descriptions across Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa.

European shares rose in a relief rally on Monday after geopolitical tension had driven their worst weekly losses of the year. The STOXX 600 gained 0.7%, while euro zone stocks and blue-chips rose 0.9%. The prior week’s losses were attributed to tension between the United States and North Korea. Banking led gains at 1.4%, with major banks up 2.5% to 2.7%. German energy group RWE jumped 3% after raising its 2017 profit forecast, supported by better gas plant performance. Danone rose 2% after speculation it could be a bid target was reported by the New York Post, while Credit Suisse cut Ladbrokes Coral to “underperform,” sending it down 2.7%. Standard Life Aberdeen rose 2.7% on its first day of trading, and Fiat Chrysler gained 3.5% to lead auto stocks.

On December 11, 2003, Compass Minerals International’s CEO Michael Ducey considered investor reactions to the company’s IPO, which began trading on December 12, 2003. The passage describes salt’s major U.S. uses, three dry-salt production methods (mining rock salt, mechanical/vacuum evaporation, and solar evaporation), and how different methods produce salt with varying cost and purity; it also notes that highway deicing drives significant demand and production growth over time. The salt industry’s ownership and market structure became more concentrated, and the passage discusses contracts, end uses, and shipping considerations. It also presents evidence of increasing environmental impacts from road salt, including rising chloride concentrations in waterways and potential future regulation. Finally, it outlines Compass Minerals’ business segments, facilities and employees, workforce and incentive policies, and management background, along with selected financial information and properties/capacity data.

A study by Rand Corporation, Harvard Medical School, and UCLA found that many American workers feel workplace incidents and conditions affect them acutely. One in five Americans report their workplace has a hostile or threatening social environment. In 2015, the study surveyed 3,066 workers through regular online surveys, finding workers report high job demands and unhealthy work environments, including women reporting “unwanted sexual attention” and young men reporting “verbal abuse.” The researchers reported that two-thirds work at high speeds or under tight deadlines, one in four perceives having too little time to do their job, more than half report exposure to unpleasant or potentially hazardous conditions, and four out of five say their job met at least one definition of “meaningful” always or most of the time, with more than half describing their boss as supportive.

The passage is a farewell “State of the Union” address presenting the president’s assessment of the nation’s challenges and opportunities, the commitments made with Congress, and progress on domestic programs. It says many long-standing problems—such as urban unrest, poverty, education, law enforcement, and crises abroad—have continued, while the nation’s assets include its economy, democratic system, exploration, citizens’ judgment, and love of justice. It highlights accomplishments in the previous five years, including Medicare, expanded voting rights, federal education assistance and Head Start, public land set aside for Americans, job training for five million people, and near full employment with unemployment at 3.3%. The president argues that promises require continued action and additional funding, and then proposes measures on model cities and housing, increased social security benefits, improved health care and child protection, efforts to end poverty with emphasis on jobs, civil rights enforcement (Fair Housing Act, Voting Rights Act extension), support for crime reduction through the Safe Streets Act, and other government efficiency steps. The passage also discusses budget surpluses, surtax extension, inflation concerns, treaties related to arms control and nuclear nonproliferation, support for developing nations and regional cooperation, and ongoing quests for peace in Vietnam, the Middle East, and Paris talks. It concludes with personal remarks about representative democracy and gratitude to political colleagues, and a request for understanding for President-elect Nixon.

The passage introduces a Stackelberg-game model of a monopolist seller offering a single indivisible expiring item with zero value at expiration to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically over a finite horizon. The seller commits to a continuous, non-increasing public pricing schedule, while buyers—who are time-unbiased and derive utility at consumption—choose optimal target purchase times based on private valuations and arrival times. The seller’s time pressure comes from the risk of unsold inventory expiring, and buyer delay incentives arise from potential price reductions and stockout risk from competing arrivals. The paper’s contributions are (1) a tractable equilibrium framework using Value-Based Threshold strategies that decouple buyer type dimensions via a threshold time function, with necessary and sufficient conditions for equilibrium existence and verification, and (2) near-optimal closed-form pricing schedules for thin (infrequent arrivals) and thick (frequent arrivals) market regimes, yielding constant pricing in thin markets and linear discounting in thick markets. The related works section summarizes prior dynamic pricing and mechanism design research and positions the paper’s modeling choice of assigning time-dependent disutility only to the seller.

The passage describes the toss play in football, explaining that the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back trying to reach the edge of the defense. It says the toss play (also called toss sweep) is widely used and benefits from fast tailbacks and an athletic offensive line that can block in space. Its strengths include being simple to teach and install, efficiently getting the ball to the perimeter, and being effective with the right personnel. Its main weaknesses are that it depends on having a fast tailback and offensive line capable of running, and it can be stopped early by edge pressure such as overload or corner blitzes. The passage then outlines blocking rules for toss play matchups versus 3-4 odd front and 4-3 even front defenses, and describes two variations: Flexbone toss (with the backside wingback in motion and no lead blocking by the fullback) and Single Back toss (using a pulled playside guard and tight end lead blocker).

The speaker says the team will try something different after being affected by opponents’ “neutral zone” play and strong forward pressure. They note they have scored on the power play in almost every game, but the last game’s power play performance was poor, so they need to correct it. They plan to review footage tonight and expect changes for the next game, while acknowledging frustration after losing and being down in the series. They hope to play better and tie the series.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated December 4, 2019 reporting results of its 2019 Annual Shareholders Meeting. At the meeting, 6,610,123,128 shares were voted out of 7,632,138,696 shares entitled to vote. Shareholders voted to elect 13 director nominees, approved (advisory) named executive officer compensation, ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2020, and rejected proposals on employee representation on the Board and on a gender pay gap report. The report includes vote tabulations certified by the inspector of election and was signed by Keith R. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary, on December 5, 2019.

Diane David appeals the dissolution of her marriage to Joseph David, challenging the trial court’s property division, particularly awarding Joseph the marital residence and declining to equalize the division, and also claiming the court failed to consider tax consequences of liquidating her retirement funds. The appellate court found no error regarding the residence award and most property issues but remanded due to a mathematical error in the trial court’s calculation of Diane’s assets and because the trial court may need to reconsider the overall property division. The court also denied Diane’s argument about not accounting for tax consequences because the issue was raised for the first time on appeal and the trial court cannot be faulted under those circumstances. The judgment was vacated and the case remanded for reconsideration, with the trial court permitted to adjust the property division as it deems appropriate in light of the error.

Tesla, Inc.’s 2016 Form 10-K (for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016) is an annual report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The document describes Tesla’s business as a vertically integrated company that designs, develops, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles (Model S, Model X, and planned Model 3) and energy storage systems, and that installs, operates, and maintains solar and energy storage products through its network. It also outlines forward-looking statements, a business overview, product and technology descriptions (including powertrain, battery packs, charging, software, and autopilot), sales and service channels (including stores and the Supercharger network), manufacturing facilities (Tesla Factory, Gigafactory 1, and solar factories), supply chain and regulatory/incentive frameworks, competitive factors, segment information (automotive and energy generation and storage), employee figures, and available information about filings. The passage includes risk factors related to vehicle and product development delays, scaling and production ramp challenges (including Model 3), reliance on suppliers, dependence on market adoption of electric vehicles, battery and material risks, potential product liability, and competitive pressures.

The passage discusses improving performance through practice, particularly disciplined adherence to rules and the system, and notes that fewer power plays are allowed than earlier in the playoffs. It emphasizes that the playoffs are a battle of attrition where each game aims to wear down opponents. The speaker says the team remains focused on the next game and on maintaining defensive structure, while trying to deny easy access to the front of the net and increase traffic in front of the opposing goalie. Confidence is described as boosted by coming back from a previous series, and players are encouraged to play at a high level without worrying about outside opinions. The passage ends with a brief exchange about whether the winning team is allowed to keep the puck and a reference to an additional game.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana is appealing to the government and the public for support to resource it with ambulances, saying it has personnel to operate them to augment traditional health service providers. National Operations Director Dr. Eric Asamoah Darko says the society currently has one ambulance serving a health post on the Tema Motorway, but its engine developed a fault; he adds that the Chinese Red Cross donated the ambulance and the society is working to get an alternative engine and fix it. He also notes that the World Bank funded first aid posts in accident-prone areas and that it has built eight posts for the Red Cross to assist with ambulance service. The passage adds that Ghana, with 29 million people, has 55 functioning ambulances out of 155, with 100 broken down, while the remaining 55 provide emergency responses and life support. Vice President Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia has promised government will procure more ambulances, including initiating processes to provide 275 ambulances for the National Ambulance Service.

The passage describes the C674x DSP core and related system features. The C674x is a high-performance floating-point DSP core code-compatible with earlier C64x fixed-point and C67x floating-point generations, with specific L1 program/data memory configurations and a 256KB L2 RAM (ECC) that can be SRAM, L2 cache, or both. It notes that L3 and off-chip memory accesses go through an MMU and discusses a large device context including SoC components, revision history updates, system memory management, and various subsystem and CPU overviews. It also includes extensive device overview and device pin/terminal function descriptions, including boot configuration behavior, memory controller terminal descriptions, Ethernet/HDMI/I2C/UART/USB/video/pin multiplexing, and other peripheral interfaces.

The speaker says the Stanley Cup Finals feel like a long time coming and emphasizes that the team must stay disciplined, avoid penalties, and play hard each night. They note the need to improve their power play, discuss travel and limited sleep before arriving a day early, and say everyone is excited to be there. The speaker praises goaltenders and describes the series as requiring focus after any off night to regain momentum. They say the opponent is the best NHL team, with talent and a mix of skills, and that the team must work hard, avoid easy scoring opportunities, play patiently, keep pucks deep, and not turn the puck over. The speaker also highlights linemates Krejci and Lucic as exceptional playmakers.

The passage is a VentureWire newsletter dated May 22, 2001, sent to jdasovic@enron.com. It lists top venture-capital news items including Kodiak Venture Partners closing Fund II with $290M, Mercury acquiring Freshwater Software for $147M, Celetron raising a $48M first round, and TVM announcing the first close of a new life sciences fund at EUR 70M. It also includes sections for “new money,” “bad news,” “new products,” “M&A,” “new directors,” “new people,” “vc fund news,” and “vc personnel,” with multiple company-specific updates such as funding rounds, acquisitions, staffing reductions, leadership changes, and venture fund formations. The issue concludes with a “vw corrections” section noting editorial corrections to previous items and a “company index” stating no companies are indexed for the issue.

The passage is an email thread and a lengthy complaint document. The complaint, filed in San Diego County Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of a proposed class of California electricity customers, alleges that various electricity generator and trading companies unlawfully manipulated California’s wholesale electricity market during spring and summer 2000. It claims the defendants used confidential real-time generator and transmission data to “game” market rules, including allegedly withholding capacity, parking power with affiliates for resale, scheduling outages to coincide with maintenance, and scheduling flows to cause congestion. The complaint states that these actions caused unjust and unreasonable wholesale electricity prices, overcharges totaling more than $4 billion during summer 2000, record wholesale price levels, and substantial customer harm, while defendants allegedly obtained windfall profits. It also alleges violations of California antitrust and unfair competition laws (including the Cartwright Act and Unfair Trade Practices Act), and seeks treble damages, restitution/disgorgement, injunctive and other equitable relief, and interest. The email portion includes messages about obtaining and forwarding the complaint and references to a press conference notice.

George Washington University students condemned a racist Snapchat post involving two Alpha Phi sorority members after a photo circulated on social media. The image showed one member holding up a banana peel with a caption stating “I’m 1/16 black.” The sorority said the picture was posted by one member and included two other members, and it apologized on its Facebook page. The chapter moved to terminate the memberships of the members involved. University administrators began investigating after students called for action, and meetings were planned to discuss diversity and inclusion. The provost said there was dialogue with Alpha Phi’s national headquarters and affected students, and the GW Black Student Union issued a statement about racially charged incidents.

Vladimir Putin has won Russia’s election for a fourth term, which the passage says will further entrench his power and escalate his showdown with the West. It argues that one of his goals is to develop a post-Soviet ideology, citing a 2014 statement that links Putin to Russia. The passage describes a need for Russia to have a distinct mission statement and says Putin’s inner circle has been shaping a nascent national philosophy. It links this ideology-building to Russia’s economic stagnation, corruption, and dependence on natural resource exports, and portrays the government’s effort over the next six years as an attempt to solidify and codify an alternative worldview for domestic and export use. It also says the West should challenge the vision rather than accept it, warning that the West would need to stay firm to a competing set of ideas and ideals.

A new city partnership called Create Sheffield—Adventures in Cultural Education will bring together education, arts, culture, and voluntary organisations to ensure all children and young people in Sheffield up to age 25 experience and participate in arts and culture. The partnership aims to improve school attainment and provide skills for creative jobs, responding to concerns that music and art are being reduced due to SATs pressures and league tables. Create Sheffield plans to build a list of arts and culture experiences, support learning resources and “fun,” and develop an initiative focused on young makers. It will also offer opportunities such as learning about creative careers, helping parents access the arts with their children, and supporting schools to gain Artsmark. Arts Council England and other speakers link reduced creative subjects to performance measures like EBacc and describe arts engagement as supporting empathy and civil society. Partnership membership begins in September, with annual fees ranging from £125 to £5,000 based on organisation or school size and turnover.

Oregon public schools have one of the lowest high school graduation rates in the country, and the state requires fewer days of instruction than most others. About one in four students does not graduate high school within four years. Education advocates cite factors such as class sizes, early start times, absenteeism, poverty, and budget deficits, while parent and Oregon Board of Education member Kim Sordyl argues the main issue is that Oregon students attend school less: Oregon averages about 165 instructional days versus about 180 nationwide. Other lawmakers, including state Rep. Diego Hernandez, say the situation has multiple factors and that it is not settled by studies, also arguing that simply adding days may not fix deeper support and quality issues. Parents disagree, and one parent moved to Washington for smaller class sizes and a longer school year, where students would receive the equivalent of an extra school year of instruction across grades 1–12. In Oregon, some schools emphasize instructional time and work to reduce absenteeism, with Tualatin High School maintaining graduation rates in the mid-90th percentile.

The speaker says their team has not played the style of game that has made it successful in the playoffs, citing issues with puck management and handling, including turning the puck over in the neutral zone. They credit New Jersey as a strong defensive team that keeps shots down, noting their past playoff record and that the speaker’s team has not generated quality scoring chances for prolonged periods. The speaker also discusses that after reflecting and getting sleep, they recognize New Jersey has won two home games and that the team must “take care of business” at home in Anaheim. They say their disappointment is mainly about not generating chances and not eliminating New Jersey’s opportunities. The speaker mentions the goaltender they faced made saves and that at home they can adjust line matchups with last change to create better offensive opportunities. They emphasize focusing on tomorrow’s play rather than looking too far ahead.

A preliminary U.S. Geological Survey study says Tropical Storm Nate could erode about 70 percent of sandy beaches from the Florida Panhandle to southeast Louisiana, potentially wiping out about half of protective sand dunes along that stretch. Estimates are based on the storm’s current track and forecasted intensity. The National Hurricane Center expects Nate to make landfall on the Gulf Coast as a Category 1 hurricane with winds of 74 to 95 mph, with more than 90 percent of Louisiana beaches likely to erode. The study does not indicate how much erosion will occur. The Chandeleur Islands are particularly vulnerable to overwash, and erosion could increase vulnerability to the next storm and potentially block roadways by moving sand. The passage also notes that major hurricanes have historically intensified wetland erosion.

The passage concludes that copper is most likely not a reliable leading indicator for stocks. It describes why copper is commonly considered one—its broad use across industries and the idea that rising or falling copper prices reflect changes in economic activity that stocks may discount—but then presents a backtested “copper vs. stocks” strategy using SPY since 2000: if copper’s last four-week return is positive, buy SPY for the following week; otherwise, hold cash. The strategy showed decent overall performance with positive CAGR and manageable drawdowns, but had a long period of little activity between 2008 and 2016, and the passage reports low correlation between copper returns and subsequent SPY returns, especially during that period. It states there is no concrete evidence of strong copper-stock correlation and suggests the strategy’s results may be due to luck or randomness, while copper may be more useful for predicting economic business cycles than stock returns.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended July 31, 2016. The report presents unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements, including income, comprehensive income, balance sheet, and cash flow data, along with notes covering accounting policies, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities, fair value, intangible assets, balance sheet components, derivative instruments, guarantees and warranty liabilities, convertible debt (1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018), commitments and contingencies (including an operating lease financing arrangement for a headquarters building and patent-related legal matters), share repurchases and dividends, and segment information (GPU, Tegra Processor, and All Other). It also includes management’s discussion and analysis summarizing revenue growth, operating expense changes, gross margin drivers, income tax rate changes, liquidity and capital resources, and forward-looking statement disclosures.

The passage is a transcript introduction to EON Resources, Inc.’s special conference call about $45.5 million funding and a related Farmout Agreement. It lists speakers and includes a forward-looking statements disclaimer explaining that risks and uncertainties could cause actual results to differ from expectations, with details disclosed in company filings on EDGAR and the SEC. It then turns the call over to management, starting with Dante Caravaggio.

The passage reports how many Phase 1, Phase 2/3, and Phase 3 participants experienced serious medical problems after different BNT162b2 doses and booster doses. In Phase 1, 2 of 24 participants had serious problems after Dose 2 (inflamed appendix in the 20-µg group and inflamed nerves in the 30-µg group), and researchers did not believe these were related to the study vaccine. In Phase 2/3 and later booster periods, serious medical problems were generally infrequent (with no single serious problem occurring in at least 1% of participants in certain groups). It also states that for an additional booster of 30 µg BNT162b2 in Phase 2/3, 1 participant had a serious medical problem between Dose 4 or 5 and 1 month after Dose 4 or 5, and researchers did not believe it was related to the study vaccine.

The passage contains remarks attributed to Coach Q, discussing the team’s performance in a hockey game and the upcoming playoff finals. It addresses losing pace and momentum at times, defensive and offensive chances, and specific comments about player performances, including a player described as having strong conditioning and another line’s effectiveness in overtime. The speaker emphasizes readiness, staying hungry, maintaining momentum at home ice, and keeping players focused game to game while accounting for varying game dynamics and minutes allocation. It also notes the playoffs’ emotional highs and lows and the need to remain even-keeled.

The passage describes correspondence and dispatches to Congress regarding trespassers from British provinces who entered disputed territory between the United States and Great Britain along the Aroostook River claimed by Maine, cutting and destroying large quantities of timber. The Maine governor reported the events to the legislature, which authorized actions to arrest the depredations, disperse the trespassers, and secure timber. A land agent sent with an armed force was seized by trespassers and taken prisoner to Frederickton, New Brunswick, along with two Maine citizens. Maine then authorized the sheriff and appointed officer to use an armed posse to disperse or arrest the trespassers and protect public property.

The correspondence with Sir John Harvey, the lieutenant-governor of New Brunswick, includes a request that Maine recall the armed party, and a response that Maine would support its land agent and that this determination was communicated to the federal government. The passage argues that the British assumption of exclusive British possession and jurisdiction before final boundary settlement is unsupported by the U.S. correspondence. It states both sides previously restrained certain actions to avoid collision, and it distinguishes Maine’s effort to preserve property from a military occupation. The federal government says it will pursue amicable settlement through arbitration or a commission with an umpire if needed, and would not bring federal military force in support of Maine’s use of force.
