It also states that if New Brunswick attempts military occupation to enforce its jurisdiction claim, the federal government would consider the constitutional basis for aiding Maine against invasion. The passage concludes with expectations that detained agents be released and militias disbanded, and urges Congress to consider measures to avoid an extra session.

The passage explains that the perception of frequent all-time highs is misleading because all-time highs are uncommon. From 1950 to 2022, the S&P 500 set 1,526 all-time highs, averaging just under 21 times per year and about 8.3% of trading days, meaning it traded below all-time highs 91.7% of the time. It notes that reaching new all-time highs is generally associated with strong business conditions, higher earnings, momentum, and bullish sentiment, including possible FOMO, though inflation-adjusted markets may show drawdowns from peaks. It describes an “All-Time High trading strategy” that buys when the S&P 500 is within 5% of its all-time high and sells when it falls more than 5% from its peak, aiming to capture trend following and momentum; it also discusses a modification involving earning a 3% annual return on cash when the index is more than 5% below its all-time high. Backtesting results for the strategy in the S&P 500 (daily, not adjusted for dividends) include a 3.20% CAGR, 43.2% time in the market, a 7.40% risk-adjusted return, and a maximum drawdown of 33.75%.

The passage describes a respiratory mask system for delivering respiratory therapy to a patient, including background on respiratory masks used for CPAP and NIV therapies. It outlines mask interface components such as a frame with a gas inlet and outlet vent, an attached seal assembly forming an airtight seal, and optional diffuser placement. It also describes headgear components including a yoke/collector that attaches to the frame and supports connection systems, with various attachment features such as channels, clips/latches, snap-fit structures, and magnets. Additional sections detail example seal and nasal seal configurations with specified dimensions and materials, and provide a detailed description framework referencing many figures that illustrate mask, seal, frame, and yoke embodiments.

The passage presents three free mean reversion trading strategies and discusses mean reversion’s rationale and performance. It defines mean reversion as prices gravitating above and below a moving average, with abnormal rises tending to revert downward and vice versa. It states that mean reversion strategies generally perform best in bear markets, citing higher volatility and more explosive bear-market rallies, which make buying weakness and selling strength profitable. It also notes mean reversion is often more effective in stocks than in other markets like commodities. The three strategies are: (1) deviation from a recent high in XLP (consumer staples), (2) an IBS short strategy in FXI (Chinese ETF), and (3) a 5-day low in the S&P 500, with backtested equity curve examples and the caution to consider drawdown and leverage for futures-like use.

N750 billion will be released this week to Nigeria’s Ministries, Departments and Agencies for capital projects in the 2017 Budget, bringing total releases by the Federal Government for capital projects this year to N1.2 trillion (including N450 billion released earlier). Minister of Finance Kemi Adeosun said this week’s release would raise the year’s total to N1.2 trillion by year-end, after noting that N1.3 trillion was released last year. Adeosun also met a delegation of 30 French firms and investors interested in investing in sectors including banking, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture, and youth empowerment. Philippe Labonne said the firms plan strategic partnerships with Nigerian counterparts and were in Nigeria to assess the investment environment following stability in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market.

The passage describes systems for optically switchable (“smart”) windows, including electrochromic devices, and a high-speed building communications network used to power and communicate with window and non-window devices. It outlines networks using serially coupled trunk line segments (e.g., coaxial cables, twisted pair), with passive circuits such as bias T circuits (inductor and capacitor) or directional couplers, to form a daisy-chain trunk topology that delivers signals (including data >1 Gbps) and may also provide power (e.g., CLASS 2, TCP/IP data and power). It also describes control panels, trunk line and drop line architectures, and digital architectural elements/wall interfaces that include sensors, processors, network interfaces, and peripherals, intended for early installation during construction and for integrated sensing, monitoring, and control of building conditions. The systems can support tasks such as communications, wireless services, environmental monitoring (e.g., light, occupancy, air quality), interactive applications, and automated building operation adjustments, including security-related responses based on sensor-detected events.

The passage discusses Witting’s references to Finland’s 1940 efforts to secure common defense agreement with Sweden, which failed due to Swedish reluctance and later Soviet objection. It states Witting viewed Soviet objection as shortsighted, and that increasing Russian strength and the August crisis led Finland to accept a Finnish-German transit agreement in September as relief. It also reports that by November 1940 Germans were aware of extensive Russian preparations, which confirmed Finnish fears of renewed Russian attack. The passage then recounts discussion about Finland’s strategic aims, German influence over the passage of overseas supplies to Russia, and whether Finland had surrendered free will due to dependence on German goodwill; Witting argued Finland’s freedom was constrained by geography. The author concludes Finland is unlikely to take further actions against Axis forces and may expect military necessity to prevent peaceful understanding or cessation arrangements, and doubts Sweden can influence outcomes as desired. A telegram adds that Swedish colleagues believe Finns cannot and do not desire understanding with the USSR for cessation of hostilities, citing lack of effective leadership and concerns that Witting might report such discussions to Germans, as well as Finnish emphasis on dependence on Germany and promotion of claims for extensive acquisitions of Soviet territory.

Google Play Store no longer lists Kimbho, a real-time messaging app launched by Ramdev’s Patanjali on Wednesday, though it remains visible on the iOS App Store and is accessible to users who already downloaded it. The app was promoted as a “swadeshi messaging platform” to compete with WhatsApp, offering direct messages, group chats, broadcast lists, celebrity following, and features such as free phone and video calling, plus sharing of various media and doodling. Reports cited around 5,000 installations and issues with reviews. The launch followed Patanjali’s earlier release of Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards from May 27, which were promoted with a 10% discount on Patanjali products after full launch.

A new study analyzed gases in Uranus’s atmosphere and found hydrogen sulfide, described as foul-smelling, with an example of rotten eggs. The study, published in *Nature Astronomy* and authored by scientists from Caltech, the University of Oxford, and the University of Leicester, says this is the best proof yet for hydrogen sulfide in Uranus’s cloud tops, based on light captured by the Gemini North telescope. The study notes that while hydrogen sulfide is found elsewhere (such as raw sewage and human flatulence), approaching Uranus would involve dangerous conditions including suffocation and exposure in a mostly hydrogen, helium, and methane atmosphere at around negative 200 degrees Celsius. The discovery is also said to help explain how and when Uranus was formed.

The passage describes teammates’ excitement for Manny’s return, noting his leadership and contributions both on the ice and behind the scenes. It also discusses the importance of not getting too high after a win or too low after a loss, emphasizing focus on the next game against Boston. One speaker mentions playing their first NHL game in Boston, achieving first win and first shutout against the Bruins, and being prepared for anything when the puck is near the net.

The passage reports multiple NFL-related items, including the Bengals acquiring quarterback Joe Flacco in a trade with the Browns. It says the trade provides Cincinnati a quarterback after starter Browning struggled, with the team outscored 113-37 during a three-game skid, and with Burrow on injured reserve due to toe surgery. It notes the Bengals received a sixth-round pick and the Browns received a fifth-round pick. The passage includes statements from Bengals coach Zac Taylor about Flacco’s experience and leadership, and it describes Flacco’s performance with the Browns and his earlier time with Indianapolis. It also discusses how the trade could affect Browns quarterbacks Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders, and mentions Browns offensive quarterback changes after Flacco was replaced earlier in the season.

The passage describes a study on long-term effects of unintended pregnancy on children’s psychosocial problems up to adolescence. Unintended pregnancy is described as common, and prior research is said to focus mostly on short-term outcomes, with inconsistent findings and limited investigation of indirect mechanisms. The study aims to examine associations between unintended pregnancy and children’s psychosocial problems over time, including indirect effects via maternal mental health and bonding, using the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) longitudinal birth cohort. Participants were 7,784 pregnant women from Amsterdam; mothers completed self-report questionnaires at four phases (around 16 weeks gestation, preschool age 5–6, early adolescence 11–12, and middle adolescence 15–16). Children’s psychosocial problems were measured using maternal-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) subscales, with child-reported SDQ scores used as a secondary outcome in adolescence. Pregnancy intentions were measured as multidimensional mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness; mediators included maternal bonding problems and maternal psychosocial distress, while analyses controlled for multiple maternal and child risk factors. Results reported correlations between pregnancy unintendedness and children’s internalizing problems in multiple age ranges, and positive correlations with externalizing problems at younger ages, but direct longitudinal associations were found only at preschool age: mistiming predicted more internalizing and externalizing problems, and unwantedness predicted internalizing problems, while unhappiness was not significant. In mediation analyses at preschool age, maternal bonding was a significant mediator between unintended pregnancy dimensions and children’s psychosocial problems; maternal mental health mediated only the association involving mistiming. The study concluded that focusing on maternal mental health and bonding may be more important than unintended pregnancy itself for reducing children’s psychosocial problems.

The passage describes a display device, including an active-type organic light-emitting display device, with a through portion passing through a substrate. Pixels surround the through portion, and scan lines and data lines provide scan and data signals to the pixels. The data lines curve along the perimeter of the through portion and may be arranged in different layers so they can reduce overlap and reduce the required area of a first non-display region around the through portion while improving sealing performance. A thin film encapsulation layer with alternately stacked inorganic and organic layers forms a lateral surface defining the through portion and helps prevent oxygen and moisture penetration. Various embodiments add or modify insulating/passivation layers, dams, and contact structures (including contact portions between inorganic layers) to prevent moisture penetration and protect data lines. The passage also explains that scan drivers can perform dual scanning and that the described display device can be used in electronic apparatuses such as a mobile phone, smart watch, and a vehicle dashboard, with parts located inside the through portion(s).

The passage is a graduation address in which the speaker, President Hatcher, praises coeducational education at the University of Michigan and emphasizes the future of the nation. He argues that national success depends on protecting liberty and pursuing citizens’ happiness, and describes “the Great Society” as a society based on abundance and liberty for all, including an end to poverty and racial injustice, access to knowledge, meaningful leisure, community, beauty, and a renewed connection with nature. He identifies three areas to build the Great Society: cities, where urban growth requires rebuilding and where community and land values are eroding; the countryside, where pollution and environmental degradation threaten America’s beauty; and classrooms, where education access, teacher quality, overcrowding, and outdated curricula need improvement. He says solutions require cooperation between the federal government and local communities, and he announces working groups and White House conferences to address these issues, urging the graduating class to join efforts against inequality, poverty, and for enduring peace while helping build the Great Society.

The speakers discuss a closely played playoff game, saying they played two strong periods but became more conservative in the third period to protect a lead. They believe Buffalo benefited by getting organized and playing competitively, including in overtime, where outcomes were described as unpredictable. They emphasize that key differences involved controlling “critical areas” and contested puck battles, and that Buffalo controlled those areas better after the first two and a half periods, including the boards, slot area, and in front of their net during goals. They also discuss the importance of generating more second- and third-shot opportunities rather than relying on first shots, and the need to create loose-puck possession around the net. They note Buffalo’s skilled players can score from multiple lines and that the upcoming matchup will be challenging and competitive. The discussion includes comments about power plays, potential lineup changes for the next game, and the team’s tight identity and perseverance through adversity, with goaltending described as a major factor on both sides.

The passage is an email from VentureWire People dated May 17, 2001 to Jeffrey Dasovich, introducing a daily publication that alerts recipients to promotions, hirings, departures, and reassignments among top executives at venture-backed firms. It lists executive changes for that date across categories including top management, marketing & sales, business development, finance, technology, operations, and VC personnel, followed by multiple detailed company announcements of leadership appointments and promotions. The email also includes sections for executive searches and “Who’s Hiring,” plus links related to cancellations, classified advertising, and feedback.

The passage describes the “Box and One” defense, where four players play zone coverage in a box while a “Chaser” takes an aggressive, full-out pass denial position with the sole responsibility of denying the opponent the ball. It outlines how baseline defenders X4 and X5 move like a 1-2-2 zone and how outside defenders X1 and X2 shift like a 2-3 zone, with specific positioning for situations such as balls in corners, on wings, and out front. It then compares defensive reactions versus even front and odd front offenses, detailing how defenders shift on passes (including who pushes out, slides over, drops to the free-throw line, or closes out) while the chaser (X3) maintains strong pass denial on O3. The passage concludes that the key element of the Box & One defense is the chaser’s ability to deny the assigned opponent the ball, disrupting the opponent’s set plays and continuities.

The passage explains how to backtest a simple trading strategy in Python. It describes using libraries including pandas for data manipulation and indicator calculations, yfinance to download SPY historical data from Yahoo Finance, and matplotlib to plot results. It outlines computing simple and exponential moving averages with pandas rolling mean and rolling forward-window functions, deleting the first 200 rows due to missing indicator values, then generating trading signals by checking whether the close price is above both moving averages and recording this in a regime column. It calculates daily returns with pct_change(), applies returns only when regime equals 1, and plots accumulated performance. The strategy’s accumulated returns are 804.82% versus buy-and-hold returns of 1505.31%, so it underperforms. The passage concludes that backtesting can be done without a finance or computer science degree.

Dane Gudauskas describes his adrenaline-filled experience riding a ferocious left during last weekend’s XXL Cloudbreak swell in Fiji, followed by increasing soreness at home. He explains that rare large Fiji swells made him feel it was necessary to see conditions firsthand, despite bad wind and rain and reports that winds would make people wait on boats. He details the decision process for paddling versus towing, the stormy conditions, his nerves during the paddle out, catching a wave on the right spot after considering the low odds of making it, and being wiped out and breaking his board. He compares the wave to one he rode in 2016 as having much more energy and speed, mentions he rode Patrick Gudauskas’s 8’6″ quad-fin board and later switched to an 8’10” backup, and says the swell felt uniquely unruly and raw. He credits the water safety crews for making the day as safe as possible and says he plans to keep surfing as his comedown.

Signing SFS requires the customer to provide an RSA public key used for SFS package verification during early boot (during or immediately after setting up SMM, prior to BOOT_DONE), and the customer cannot update the signature after this stage. The x86 passes a pointer to an MBOX_BUFFER_HEADER, followed in memory by a KeySize field and an OemCoSignKey array defined using RSA_TOKEN_FORMAT. For co-signing, the customer generates an RSA key pair (2048 or 4096 bits) and signs the received AMD update package using RSA-PSS with SHA-256 or SHA-384. The RSA token format includes a versioning scheme set to one, and N depends on key/public exponent size and modulus size.

The specification also describes patchable items, SEV/SNP update requirements (including reboot behavior and HV-FIXED pages when SNP is enabled), attestation security considerations, and resiliency rules for update package application. Update packages are non-persistent across warm/cold reboots, with customer options for applying patches during OS boot or during system operation. It outlines alignment and buffer placement requirements for SFS commands, a customer-provided deployment agent process to create the TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and include optional co-signing headers/signatures, and an ASP process that checks access protection, verifies signatures, loads and runs executable patches, updates patch level, and returns status. It further specifies commands for checking firmware versions, describing GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO output fields, SFS update package naming, and release mechanism constraints that updates match specific firmware/system patch level combinations and are designed to have minimal impact on system performance.

The passage contains information from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2022. It includes financial statements (cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets), an index of items, and notes covering accounting policies, a common stock 20‑for‑1 split effective May 27, 2022, principles of consolidation, use of estimates, supplemental cash flow information, fair value measurement and marketable securities, equity warrants and non-marketable equity investments, and lease details. It also provides commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings, debt and related facilities, stockholders’ equity and stock-based compensation, income taxes, and segment information (North America, International, and AWS) with related net sales and operating income figures.

Augustine Heard reports that after his April 20 dispatch the situation in Seoul remained quiet and there was no further word of the Tong Hâk. He arranged for Commander Book and officers of the Alert to visit and later received orders to leave Chemulpo on the morning of April 29. Reports from areas outside Seoul did not show traces of Tong Hâk assemblages, and Roman Catholic priests confirmed this. He notes ongoing disquieting rumors due to official exactions.

In a later dispatch (after May 1), Heard reports that many thousands of the Tong Hâk collected near Po-eun, with daily increasing numbers and much alarm among Koreans. They were said to be drilling regularly, erecting a walled encampment with hostile flags, and claiming soldiers sent against them would join them. Families were sent into the country, and an official sent to remonstrate could not persuade them to disperse. On the 15th, 800 drilled men with three Gatling guns were sent to Suwen to bar the road, with expectations they might push toward Chong-ju. Heard states foreigners fear danger due to the flags but doubts active hostility, adding that any threat would likely be more from city mobs than from the Tong Hâk themselves. He says the U.S.S. Alert is at Chemulpo and that, while the Tong Hâk appear quiet and focused on their founder’s rehabilitation and permission to practice their tenets, they have attracted discontented and poverty-stricken people, possibly under a political party whose identity and strength are unknown.

Biocon India Group grew from an enzyme business founded in 1978 to a pharmaceutical firm with an “earn as you learn” approach, reaching 800 employees and US$75 million annual revenues by early 2003. The group created Syngene, a contract research organization, and developed capabilities in manufacturing and research. As Biocon considered growth limits, Managing Director Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw launched Clinigene in 2000 to provide clinical trial services and fill a gap in the drug development value chain, focusing on BE/BA studies, clinical lab services, and hospital coordination. The passage describes the Indian pharmaceutical industry’s policy-driven growth, outsourcing trends favoring India for clinical and other services, and supportive government efforts for biotech. It also outlines concerns about Clinigene: market positioning in a competitive CRO landscape, risks from cultural disruption and potential outgrowing of the parent, logistical and partner-hospital constraints for staff, and ethical and reputational risks inherent in human clinical trials. The case frames Mazumdar-Shaw’s challenge as choosing how to expand while managing these risks and shareholder expectations.

The passage describes a crude oil “Friday seasonality” strategy based on historical data (from April 2006 to the present) that involves buying on Thursday’s close and expecting a price increase on Friday. It reports a profit and loss (P/L) of 56.96%, with 98 trades executed and 60 winners, and an average profit of 0.58% per trade. The strategy is said to work better when Thursday is a down day in the market, and it notes that buying on any Thursday’s close may not be as effective. It also states the optimal day for applying the strategy is Thursday under the down-day condition.

Virtual machines use interrupt delivery through an architectural APIC, including for synthetic messages from the host. The #HV doorbell data is structured to match APIC behavior so existing guest interrupt dispatch logic can be reused. The #HV doorbell page defines a 16-bit PendingEvent field in bytes 0–1 and a NoEoiRequired field in byte 2, with bytes 3–63 reserved for future functionality; the rest of the page is unspecified for the virtualization stack’s message formats. The doorbell page is shared with the host, so the backing physical page must be host-owned (not set with RMPUPDATE), and guest accesses must use C=0.

The ADS868xW is a family of single-channel, high-speed, easy-to-use integrated data acquisition devices that support true bipolar differential and single-ended input swings up to ±12.288 V on a single 5 V analog supply. It includes a high-precision SAR ADC, a power-optimized analog front-end with features such as high input impedance (≥ 1 MΩ), a programmable gain amplifier with multiple software-programmable bipolar and unipolar ranges, a second-order low-pass antialiasing filter, an ADC driver amplifier, and an input overvoltage protection circuit up to ±20 V. The device has an internal 4.096 V reference and an enhanced SPI interface (multiSPI) supporting daisy-chain and alarm features, plus options for various input ranges, reference configurations (internal or external), alarm thresholds/flags, and ADC transfer function/format. It also describes multiSPI data transfer frames, host-to-device connection topologies (including daisy-chain), device functional modes (RESET, ACQ, CONV), programmable gain amplifier behavior, second-order LPF characteristics, and reference handling details, along with register maps and data/control interfaces.

On Aug. 6, Dylan Kennedy, 19, was pulled over for speeding on Route 107 and Redding Road. The officer saw a clear mason jar with a green leafy substance in the vehicle, which he believed to be marijuana. Kennedy admitted to marijuana in the back seat. Police seized items, and Kennedy was ticketed for traveling unreasonably fast and for possession of less than one half of an ounce of marijuana, and was charged with possession of drug paraphernalia. On Aug. 5, police charged Caton Preston, 18, with possession of alcohol by a minor and forgery in the third degree after determining he produced a fake driver’s license. Police also took 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs from Meadow Ridge Health Center and a collection box for incineration at Wheelabrator. The passage also notes trespassing charges related to three children found at Falls Hole restaurant, and an investigation into a smashed mailbox reported on Aug. 3. It lists stats including 204 total calls and individual categories such as animal control investigations (7) and drug/narcotic violations (1).

The passage reports that the United States has continued rapid national growth and strength, supported by a native population and a favorable distribution of power between national and state governments that draws the union closer together. It states that foreign relations are generally friendly: revenue remains adequate, agriculture, commerce, manufactures, and navigation flourish, fortifications and navy construction progress, and several foreign differences have been terminated, suspended, or are still under negotiation. It discusses specific treaties and negotiations with France, Great Britain (including West Indies colonies and boundaries), and issues regarding the slave trade, including a proposed convention whose conclusion is suspended pending Congress’s view. It describes commercial reciprocity with several European powers, a treaty with Russia regarding the North West coast submitted to the Senate, and information being communicated to Congress about relations with Spain and Brazil. It also addresses concerns about maritime neutrality rights and ongoing efforts through negotiation to settle disputes from past wars, outlines Treasury receipts and public debt with projections for repayment, and details military, naval, infrastructure (roads and canals), Indian affairs, anti-piracy, and post office operations. It concludes with recommendations on court organization, Indian civilization and relocation plans, possible military posts on the Pacific, improvements for Washington, and a call to preserve national institutions and maintain harmonious state and federal governance.

Mali’s gold exports are declining, and new discoveries have not offset production losses at legacy mines, with the future of the Sadiola gold mine now uncertain. Sadiola requires $380 million to stay open for another 10 years by accessing 3.4 million ounces of reserves, but negotiations to extend its operating life have stalled within the government. The Sadiola mine is described as crucial for Mali’s standing as a top gold producer, as well as for jobs and state revenues. A key factor may be political uncertainty ahead of Mali’s elections in 2018, affecting investment conditions and deals. Sadiola is a joint venture involving IAMGOLD and AngloGold Ashanti, with the Government of Mali as a minority partner. Production has dropped as soft-rock reserves near depletion, and expansion to process hard rock would require modifying the plant and building or connecting infrastructure, including potential links to Mali’s power grid.

The passage describes systems and methods for providing ground support to vertical takeoff aerial vehicles using portable mobile ground stations with protective casings, extendable landing pads, and charging functionality. In one example, a ground station includes a protective casing, a charging mechanism with embedded conducting terminals and a selectable power supply (including solar panels, wind turbines, fuel cells, electrochemical cells, piezoelectric units, or combinations), and an extendable landing pad that transitions between a closed configuration inside the casing and an open configuration sized for landing. An optional elevator mechanism raises and lowers a base platform, and optional centering and homing aids guide the vehicle to the pad, using beacons or contrasting visual patterns. The casing may be transparent to radio signals for satellite navigation, may include locking mechanisms, and may use folding top-closing flaps. The landing pad can include retractable side extensions and bridging lobes, with alternative extension mechanisms such as telescoping wings. The passage also describes deploying multiple ground stations over a required range, coordinating operations via a control server and communications, and outlines methods for extending range and for raising, extending, centering, retracting, and charging during landing operations.

Europa’s surface is largely water ice with varying hydrated materials that may reflect Europa’s subsurface ocean composition and affect habitability. Because accurate compositional characterization will be needed for upcoming Europa Clipper (EIS/MISE) and JUICE (MAJIS) spectroscopy, the passage describes laboratory NIR spectral measurements and Hapke-theory-based spectral mixture modeling. The study focuses on water ice, epsomite (MgSO4·7H2O), and halite (NaCl), preparing intimate mixtures of discrete grain particles under cryogenic conditions using the nitrogen-purged CRONOS facility. Grain sizes were sorted into bins and spectra were acquired for pure materials and 50%/50% volume mixtures. Modeling compared linear reflectance mixing and intimate (single-scattering albedo) mixing using optical constants for crystalline water ice and epsomite, while halite mixtures were modeled only for water ice and epsomite. Results indicate water ice spectra are generally well reproduced by both mixing approaches, with discrepancies mainly in either continua or absorption features. Epsomite modeling shows larger mismatches and is considered potentially limited by possibly incorrect “cryogenic” epsomite optical constants labeled as such but appearing similar to ambient. Halite’s NIR behavior includes a near-1.95 µm adsorbed-water feature that is difficult to discern when mixed with water ice. The study concludes that quantitative spectral mixture analysis is necessary for reliable abundance and grain-size interpretation on Europa, and that follow-up work will update epsomite optical constants and further test mixture-model fidelity.

RTX IO is described as a technology that improves game frame rates, enables near-instantaneous loading, reduces object pop-in and stutter, and streams high-quality textures at fast rates. It also uses lossless compression to reduce game download and install sizes, letting gamers store more games on SSDs while improving performance. RTX IO is said to benefit artists and designers working with large datasets and to enable high-resolution, high-framerate VR imagery for professional uses.

The passage explains that production rendering can be bottlenecked by loading large amounts of data from storage to the GPU before rendering begins, and that loading only needed mesh and texture data for a frame requires the ability to quickly retrieve data. RTX IO is described as plugging into Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to reduce IO overhead and maximize NVMe-to-GPU performance. It uses GPU-based lossless decompression so reads remain compressed through DirectStorage and are decompressed on the GPU, removing work from the CPU and improving I/O performance by a factor of two.

The Sri Lankan rupee fell for a third straight session on Wednesday in dull trade, as importers’ dollar demand outpaced inflows from remittances. It ended at 158.60/75 per dollar versus Tuesday’s 158.50/60. Dealers cited broader downward pressure on emerging-market currencies linked to higher U.S. Fed rates, the China-U.S. trade war, and rising oil prices. The rupee previously hit an all-time low of 160.17 on June 20 and is down 3.4% this year. The strengthening dollar has increased credit risk for several emerging markets, including Sri Lanka, and could reduce foreign exchange reserves, Moody’s said. Downward pressure showed signs of easing after Sri Lanka received over $500 million from China Merchants Port Holdings as part of a $1.12 billion deal for the Hambantota port. The IMF said Sri Lanka’s economy remains vulnerable due to public debt and large refinancing needs, and central bank data showed foreign investors sold net 3.5 billion rupees of government securities in the week ended June 27.

A court in Uzbekistan convicted Zokir Aliyev, an Uzbek-born U.S. citizen, of publicly calling for the government’s overthrow and participating in an extremist group linked to militant Islam. The court imposed only a $67 fine for offences dating to December 1999. Aliyev was detained by Uzbekistan’s state security service on June 16, held for six days, and then went on trial. He previously denied involvement with the militant Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan (IMU), saying he only attended some opposition meetings in Turkey in the 1990s. Uzbekistan’s security service said he was wanted since 2005 and suspected of affiliation with the IMU, including alleged training in Afghanistan. The U.S. embassy declined comment citing privacy concerns.

The passage is a communication to the U.S. Senate responding to a resolution requesting information about an alleged forcible resistance to the execution of U.S. laws in Boston. It states that newspapers publicize an affidavit by Patrick Riley, but that no satisfactory official information has yet been received and some implicated persons deny parts of the account. The author says the incident was unexpected and suggests some negligence and unpreparedness, while also asserting it does not reflect the general sentiment of Boston or Massachusetts. The passage then cites several federal resolutions and laws about states using jails for prisoners committed under U.S. authority and about marshals hiring temporary jails when state jails are withdrawn. It describes Massachusetts legislation repealing the use of state jails for certain federal prisoners, and argues that this state action does not diminish Congress’s duty and authority. It notes no official information that the U.S. marshal obtained a place for confinement, and that instructions and related documents were transmitted to relevant officials. The author also discusses constitutional authority for using the Army, Navy, and militia to execute laws, and suggests possible modifications concerning militia calls and the need for proclamation. The communication ends with assurances that forcible opposition will be suppressed. It also includes a separate April 25, 1851 proclamation warning against unlawful military expeditions to invade Cuba, threatening penalties, and urging lawful prevention and arrest of offenders.

The passage discusses the 2018-19 Union Budget delivered by Finance Minister Arun Jaitley before the 2019 elections, noting the low number of women in the Lok Sabha and questioning how women are addressed in the Budget. It says there is no separate women-focused allocation in this year’s Budget, unlike 2017 and 2016, and includes criticisms from economist Dr Jayati Ghosh and others that the Budget relies on regressive assumptions about women’s social roles and lacks adequate budgetary backing for promises. It also presents some positive views, highlighting the National Health Protection Scheme aimed at covering 10 crore vulnerable families with Rs 5 lakh per family per annum, with supporters arguing it could improve women’s access to healthcare. However, others criticize the scheme, including concerns that it may not reduce out-of-pocket costs and that health spending has increased allocations by only 2.7 percent while health ministry spending has declined as a share of the total Budget. The passage further notes related concerns such as reduced maternity entitlements, limited increases in child health services, sanitation and behavior-change uncertainties, and critiques of expanding schemes like Ujjwala without addressing affordability barriers. Overall, it characterizes the Budget’s impact on women as mixed, with some seeing modest improvements and others saying women’s needs are not meaningfully incorporated.

The passage discusses options trading in NVDA as an investment strategy that may allow large profits from small investments through leverage, with limited loss for long options (loss capped at the paid premium). It outlines factors affecting option pricing—such as the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility (including via models like Black-Scholes), market sentiment, and dividends—where rising underlying prices generally increase call prices and decrease put prices, and implied volatility increases option prices while decreases reduce them. It lists common strategies (buying/selling calls and puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, collars) and notes that risk-reward depends on the strategy used. The passage also mentions liquidity, margin requirements varying by option type (lower for buying than writing), hedging (e.g., protective puts), risk factors (price movement, time decay, volatility, liquidity), risk-limiting approaches (stop-loss orders, protective puts, hedging, diversification, position sizing), and return-maximizing approaches (leverage, deep in-the-money options, covered calls, bullish strategies like spreads and straddles, plus diversification/position sizing). It also notes trading costs vary by option type and related factors, market conditions influence option prices, tools/techniques include technical analysis and options pricing models/software, speculation uses calls/puts based on expected short-term moves, and tax implications generally treat options trading as capital gains subject to capital gains tax depending on the situation, with consultation recommended.

The speaker says they have been in Quebec for seven or eight months and feel at home, with family members likely attending the game and creating a different experience. They attribute team success to hard work and preparation, including starting work on the season in the summer, training camp, and staying tough during critical times, noting that luck is also involved but that hockey luck is created through hard work. They expect a tough battle, emphasizing playing one game and one shift at a time, bringing the right energy, and matching the opponent’s intensity and desperation. They believe the team can play the same style at home or on the road, using their size, toughness, and skating ability, and plan to implement their game plan. They expect an exciting atmosphere, with early minutes being crucial, aiming to quiet the opposition and play their game.

The passage explains USB-C vs USB-A, noting that connector shape (not speed) determines which port type fits, and that USB-A has limitations such as fixed 5-volt power delivery. It describes how USB devices follow USB specifications with speed and power determined by specification versions, and that system performance is limited by the slowest link in the connection chain. It covers USB4 (from 2022), USB power delivery (USB-PD), and DisplayPort Alt Mode (DP Alt Mode) for audio/video over USB-C, including how DP Alt Mode capabilities vary by DisplayPort generation. It explains that USB branding for USB 3.x can be confusing, recommending checking actual speed ratings instead of labels, and discusses older standards like USB 2.0. The passage then compares Thunderbolt (Intel/Apple with stricter certification) to USB, focusing on Thunderbolt 4 (built on USB4) and its features, and introduces Thunderbolt 5 (2025 adoption) with higher bandwidth, expanded display support, and increased power delivery up to 240 watts via USB-PD 3.1. Finally, it advises using appropriate cables—preferably the one included with devices—and checking cable speed/watt ratings, since cable capabilities can limit data transfer and charging.

The passage argues that a policy meant to end slavery agitation instead increased it and will not stop until a crisis is reached. The author claims the government cannot endure permanently “half slave and half free,” predicting the Union will become either fully one or the other depending on whether slavery’s opponents or its advocates act to prevent or expand it. It recounts how, in 1854, Congressional prohibition against slavery in territories was repealed through the Nebraska bill and “squatter sovereignty” logic, and it describes the Dred Scott case’s timing alongside that political process. The author presents the Dred Scott decision and remaining elements of Nebraska doctrine as a “machinery” that, they say, prevents Black people from being citizens, restricts Congress and territorial legislatures from excluding slavery, and defers key questions to slave-state courts. The passage further claims these legal actions were supported through political delays and elections to preserve arguments of “perfectly free” status, and it anticipates further Supreme Court decisions that could make slavery lawful across states. Finally, it argues that opposing the “present political dynasty” is necessary and that the author’s “great cause” should be led by its reliable supporters rather than by Senator Douglas.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed Henry J. Adams III’s conviction and 140-month above-guidelines sentence for armed bank robbery. Adams acted as the lookout and helped plan the robbery, recruited Veronica Johnson to drive, and after the robbery he and Johnson fled with the other participants; Adams later confessed. The court held he was not entitled to a minor-participant sentence reduction because his role and knowledge made him not substantially less culpable than the average participant. It also found no abuse of discretion in varying upward from the guideline range, citing Adams’s extensive criminal history and recidivist pattern, and concluding the sentence was substantively reasonable under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a).

Chelsea and Real Madrid are reportedly trying to beat Tottenham to the signing of Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Sanchez, 21, was dropped after saying he was not in the right frame of mind, but Ajax want to keep him and offer a new long-term contract. The Daily Mail says Tottenham will hold talks with Ajax on Monday, initially proposing £28m, and Chelsea and Real Madrid are preparing counter bids. Sanchez wants to leave for the chance to play in the Premier League and Champions League, and Tottenham have not signed anyone yet, with just over two weeks left before the deadline.

The passage is a State of the Union address that says the United States faces decisive days and major tasks ahead, including reforming domestic programs, saving lives abroad from disease, promoting broadly shared prosperity, and responding to dangers and enemies. It cites recent accomplishments such as education reform, creation of the Department of Homeland Security, tax relief to end recession, and business reforms to hold corporate criminals accountable. It proposes making certain income-tax reductions permanent, ending double taxation of dividends, encouraging economic growth while increasing discretionary spending by 4 percent, strengthening Social Security by enabling younger workers to invest retirement accounts, and reforming health care starting with Medicare. The address also calls for energy independence with environmental improvements, including research funding for clean hydrogen-powered automobiles. It emphasizes compassion-focused initiatives for mentoring disadvantaged students and providing drug treatment, urges action on faith-based and citizen service programs, and calls for protecting infants, ending partial-birth abortion, and passing a law against human cloning. It discusses international policy priorities, including efforts related to Afghanistan, the Middle East, global hunger, and confronting HIV/AIDS through an “Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief.” It describes the ongoing war on terror, counterterror arrests and operations, homeland security measures, and proposals such as Project BioShield and improved intelligence coordination. The passage argues that the greatest danger includes outlaw regimes seeking nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons, and it presents the case for action regarding Iraq’s alleged failure to disarm, including a planned UN Security Council meeting and a potential coalition response. It concludes with messages to the armed forces and a call for perseverance, peace defended if necessary, and support for the United States.

The passage explains the “stick” concept, a quick-game passing play used in West Coast Offense/Air Raid-style schemes. It is designed for the quarterback to make fast reads and release the ball quickly, with five downfield eligible receivers providing options to either side. The stick route runner is typically the primary target, with route adjustments based on defensive coverage. The concept is described as effective against man coverage and Cover 3/4, where the QB reads and targets options such as the TE’s stick cut, an X slant, and the flat defender. It is described as less effective against Cover 2, where the cornerback becomes the flat defender and certain throws (like the arrow and “hole shot”) require specific QB traits. The passage also lists route coaching points for multiple positions, QB progression steps based on flat defender movement, and two variations: “2x2 condensed formation stick” and “Trips Flex Sticko” with double moves and additional routes, including delayed slant and backside options.

Shares of Walgreens Boots Alliance, CVS Health, and Rite Aid fell on Friday after reports that Amazon was considering entering online drug sales. Reuters said Amazon is reportedly discussing with mid-market pharmacy benefit managers, hiring to assess the drug retailing market, and could enter the drug distribution value chain within two years. The news follows CNBC reporting that Amazon would decide before Thanksgiving whether to sell prescription drugs online. Amazon does not comment on rumors, and the stocks closed down 5.8% (Walgreens), 4.9% (Rite Aid), and 4.9% (CVS Health).

The passage describes a study analyzing value loads conveyed by words in reading texts from Turkey’s Ministry of National Education Turkish course books for grades 2–4. It defines concepts such as opinion, sentiment polarity, and values, and explains values education in formal and hidden curricula. The study digitizes textbook texts using OCR, cleans and tokenizes them, and uses three applied linguistics PhD experts to classify word value loads as positive, negative, or neutral. The database includes 3,637 unique prose words (excluding grade 1 writing-focused texts and poems). Results show that 4.72% of words had positive value transfer (172 words), 4.37% had negative transfer (159 words), and 91.43% were neutral (3,306 words). By grade, neutral value transfers dominate in all grades, with no observable relationship between grade levels and the values transferred. The conclusion suggests no established standards for value education based on word presentations and recommends using corpus-based methods and digitizing textbooks for further research.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while he was off work to observe Rosh Hashanah. Conservatives published old blog posts attributed to him that criticized President Donald Trump during his first term, including claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist,” which Rosenzweig allegedly wrote while an associate at Kobre & Kim. The article says he joined the U.S. attorney’s office in September 2020 and worked in the economic crimes section, and he did not respond to a request for comment. It also notes three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors were fired after previously working with former special counsel Jack Smith, and it summarizes Smith’s comments about dismissals of public servants and attacks on the rule of law.

The passage explains that weekly trading strategy focuses on weekly price action and can be used for positional trading, broader market structure analysis for daily trend-following systems, weekly rotation systems, or swing trading the weekly bars. It states the weekly chart is commonly used for long-term position trading, with range trading on the weekly chart described as the most common approach, typically identifying range support and resistance and using price action patterns or indicator signals. It also discusses trading weekly highs and lows on lower timeframes such as H4, using breakouts or reversals, and mentions timeframe combinations (weekly with H4, or weekly with daily) for analysis. The passage says charts can’t be judged “better” without backtesting, notes backtesting may be more powerful on daily bars than weekly bars in stocks, and provides a backtested example of a weekly sector rotation strategy with reported performance metrics.

The lecture introduces a course connecting graph theory, extremal graph theory, and additive combinatorics. It begins with Schur’s approach to Fermat’s Last Theorem via reducing equations modulo primes, noting that Schur showed this strategy fails because for any exponent \(n\), non-trivial solutions exist modulo all sufficiently large primes. The proof is linked to Schur’s theorem: any finite coloring of the positive integers yields a monochromatic solution to \(x+y=z\). The lecture discusses the equivalence between an infinitary and a finitary formulation of Schur’s theorem and explains that finitary versions also raise difficult quantitative questions about bounds.

To prove Schur’s theorem, the instructor uses Ramsey’s theorem for monochromatic triangles, first proving the triangle case by induction and pigeonhole principle. A graph is constructed from an integer coloring by coloring edges according to the difference of vertex labels, and Ramsey’s monochromatic triangle is converted into a monochromatic additive equation.

The discussion then expands into a historical tour of additive combinatorics, highlighting major results such as Van der Waerden’s theorem, Roth’s theorem, Szemerédi’s theorem, and alternative proofs using graph theory, Fourier analysis, ergodic theory, and hypergraph regularity. It further describes generalizations in higher dimensions (Furstenberg–Katznelson) and polynomial patterns (polynomial Szemerédi theorem), and ends with the Green–Tao theorem. Finally, it previews graph-theoretic problems related to Roth’s theorem and Mantel’s theorem, and notes that the course will next focus on extremal graph theory and related open problems.

George Morello appealed the district court’s summary judgment in favor of AMCO Insurance Company on claims including breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and violations of the Unruh Act, as well as the denial of his motion for reconsideration. The Ninth Circuit affirmed, concluding that, even when viewing evidence in the light most favorable to Morello, there was no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO breached the implied covenant in handling his insurance claim. The court found no substantial evidence of an unreasonable investigation, determined AMCO’s reliance on an expert opinion was reasonable, and held that other expert conclusions were conclusory and rebutted by the record. The court also found no error in granting summary judgment on the related claims because they were premised on the same grounds as the bad faith claim. It further held that the denial of reconsideration was not an abuse of discretion. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage is largely data from NVIDIA’s Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended May 2, 2021, including condensed consolidated financial statements and related notes. The passage describes page migration operations supported by the PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST commands, including constraints, required preconditions, firmware actions per migration entry, and error handling. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO moves pages in SNP-enabled or non-SNP systems, updates IOMMU host PTEs to new physical locations, requires CPU access prevention and (in some non-SNP cases) specific IOMMU/ATS invalidation and synchronization steps before calling the command, and, for 2M pages, requires smashing into 4K pages because direct 2M migration is not supported. It also notes that in SNP-running systems, source and destination pages in the migration list must all be Hypervisor state and remain so after migration. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves pages for an SNP guest, does not support DMA to migrating pages, prevents CPU access by marking pages non-present, requires specific guest page states (source Guest-Valid/Guest-Invalid, destination Pre-Migration) and GCTX context state, requires RMP_ENFORCE=1, and performs CPU TLB invalidation/sync, copies data, and updates source/destination RMPs. The passage further explains that the command sequence can use a finalizing sub-command with optional interrupt-on-completion behavior, that certain input fields are ignored, and that errors are reported via command/migration-list statuses and PM_STATUS for ring-buffer issues, with hardware errors possibly reported via MCA and potentially making pages unrecoverable within a batch of up to 128 pages.

Under the GST regime starting July 1, e-way bills are required for transporting goods consignments valued over Rs 50,000. A GST Council meeting on August 5 approved an exemption list of 153 items from the e-way bill requirement, including LPG for household supply, kerosene under the PDS, currency, jewellery, postal baggage, and used personal and household effects. The list also includes items such as live bovine animals, swine and fish, fruits and vegetables, fresh milk, honey, seeds, cereals and flour, along with betel leaves, non-alcoholic toddy, raw silk, khadi, earthen pot and clay lamps, puja samagri, hearing aids, human hair, semen including frozen semen, condoms, and contraceptives. E-way bills are not required for goods transported by non-motorised conveyances or for certain movements from international ports to hinterland ports for customs clearance. The electronic permit details goods, mode, origin and destination, and supplier, recipient, and transporter, and will be implemented from a date notified by the central government after software readiness by NIC.

School systems across the U.S. are increasingly equipping yellow buses with technology such as live cameras, GPS tracking, turn-by-turn navigation, and parent-facing apps. In Kansas City Public Schools, a new contract with Zum added features including driver navigation, student check-in/check-out via tablet, live inside/outside cameras, real-time bus location and speed display, and driver ratings. Supporters say the technology improves safety and provides transparency for parents, while other tools help with routing, maintenance monitoring, and addressing behavior issues in real time. Some advocates and parents raise concerns about data security and retention, including whether sensitive student data could be misused. Companies interviewed say they do not sell student data, encrypt device memory, and delete video routinely, and some districts store video on their own servers with retention and privacy policies. Costs vary by district, with payments described as including per-bus upfront and annual subscription expenses.

The Infiniti Q Inspiration concept revealed earlier this year is expected to influence an all-new electrified vehicle platform, leading to up to five new models built over the next five years in China at an unconfirmed location. These likely global models are intended to be among the best-looking EVs. The concept is described as a four-door coupe with “clear and concise lines,” a sculpted, athletic body, and distinctive lights and grilles. The platform may include other body styles besides the four-door coupe, including a crossover version. The design director Karim Habib said the concept evolves traditional sedan architecture with smarter, more compact powertrains and aims to create a more engaging experience.

The passage describes SOS pressure defense fundamentals and off-ball pressure tactics, emphasizing drill practice, coach attitude, and positive reinforcement. It explains that on-ball pressure is based on three defender actions—Set, On, and Smother—where the defender acts first to force dribbling, guide the dribbler toward a checkpoint, and apply maximum pressure to disrupt passing or shooting. Set action involves a specific crouched stance near the ball and footwork to transition to On; On action continues forcing the dribbler toward checkpoints, including “sprint and recover” if beaten; Smother action involves crowding the ballhandler, extending arms overhead, and moving hands laterally to disrupt passing vision.  

For off-ball pressure, it outlines three actions triggered by the keywords SNUGGLE, OFF, and STRIKE: SNUGGLE denies passes when the defender is one pass away, OFF denies cut-to-basket passing lanes by sliding “away from” the opponent while staying between the opponent and ballhandler, and STRIKE is a weakside “snakelike” movement to impede entry into the three-second area and provide help responsibilities. It also describes a closeout that moves the defender from Strike to Set by sprinting two-thirds of the distance to the ball and using mini-slides to reestablish a Set stance near the opponent.

Fiat Chrysler (FCA) is reported to have rejected an offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker, saying “thanks, but no thanks.” FCA had previously pursued mergers or acquisitions, including attempts to merge with General Motors and interest in Volkswagen, and Marchionne said he would focus on the company’s bottom line. According to Automotive News, FCA declined the Chinese proposal because the financial terms were not enough, while sources say FCA attracted interest from several carmakers, including Guangzhou. The report links potential Chinese interest to government pressure to expand into foreign markets (“China Outbound”), FCA’s distribution network and product line, and Chinese automakers’ efforts to enter the U.S. market through decades of branding activities and joint ventures.

An exclusive report from Digit says Xiaomi will not launch the Xiaomi Mi A2 in India. A Xiaomi spokesperson said no phone exists by that name but that the company will make more Android One phones. The Xiaomi Mi A1 was launched in India last year as the first stock Android smartphone from the company, and the article discusses the possibility that a successor could be launched in India under a different name, while Xiaomi is also preparing to launch the Redmi S2/Y2 in India with unclear naming.

North American markets ended a volatile week with sharp losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 666 points (2.5%) to 25,520.96, its biggest decline in two years, and the S&P 500 dropped 2.1% to 2,762.13, with both indexes posting their worst week since January 2016. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2% to 7,240.95, marking its worst week since February 2016. The declines were attributed to strong U.S. jobs data raising expectations for higher inflation and interest rate hikes, a rise in bond yields, and weak earnings from major companies including Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Alphabet; Apple shares also fell 4.3% after selling fewer iPhones than expected. In Canada, the S&P/TSX Composite fell 255 points (1.6%) to 15,606.03, its worst drop in nearly five months, as oil prices fell and the marijuana sector continued to decline. Cannabis-related analysts said continued volatility was likely due to oversupply and falling prices, and Canopy Growth shares fell 12.5% on Friday.

Appellant Maurice M. Davis, a brakeman, sued Missouri-Kansas-Texas R. Co. of Texas after passenger train No. 6 broke down near Hewitt, Texas, on January 31, 1949, in zero weather. Because only he was assigned to flag and protect the rear of the train, he remained about three hours and suffered severe frostbite to his left foot and mild frostbite to his right foot, with injuries extending into his legs. The train’s locomotive driving wheel tires came off and the other driving wheel tires slipped, making it impossible for the train to proceed. A jury found the locomotive breakdown was a proximate cause of his injuries and awarded $12,000, but the district court entered judgment for the defendant after denying his post-verdict motion.

The plaintiff argued the court erred by refusing judgment on the verdict because the Boiler Inspection Act was violated and by failing to charge the jury on the Boiler Inspection Act’s law. The appellate court held that, given undisputed evidence that the locomotive and its driving wheels failed to function while in use, the breakdown established a Boiler Inspection Act violation as a matter of law. It concluded the plaintiff was entitled to recovery if the violation was a sole or contributory proximate cause, which the jury found. The appellate court reversed and remanded with instructions to enter judgment for $12,000 based on the jury verdict.

The passage describes an analysis of AI ethics education in Indian computing curricula. It notes that AI systems are widely used across sectors and that ethical challenges such as privacy intrusion, algorithmic bias, misinformation, and autonomous agency have prompted global governance efforts. Despite this, research suggests gaps between ethical goals and actual implementation, including limited integration of AI ethics into CS education. The study addresses the lack of empirical evidence by analyzing 3,395 computer science–allied course syllabi from the top 100 Indian engineering institutions listed in NIRF, collected from publicly available online materials.  

Results show that only about 2.21% of the courses (75) included substantive AI ethics content, mostly delivered in one session, with few dedicated courses. Most were offered at the undergraduate level. The most common topics covered were privacy/legal/data governance (42%) and accountability/policies (32%), followed by ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%) and human-AI interaction and agency (24%), with lower coverage for areas such as social impact/justice (8%) and generative AI-specific concerns (reported around 10.67% earlier and 11% in the table). Learning objectives were often stated in terms of privacy risk identification, fairness, explainability, ethical dilemmas, and governance, but the syllabi rarely documented AI-ethics-specific assessments. The passage concludes that AI ethics remains marginal and inconsistently represented, with limited visibility of curricula and instructional resources, and calls for coordinated efforts to embed AI ethics more systematically in computing education.

The passage describes how the growth of a sugar industry in Mazabuka, southern Zambia—marked by an influx of male workers and related sex work—contributed to the spread of AIDS. It recounts the epidemic’s severity, including high HIV prevalence along transport routes, lack of treatment at the peak, and widespread deaths shown by crowded hospital and roadside graveyards. It then says Zambia has moved toward managing the aftermath through a military-style information and testing campaign that also provides drugs, with increased testing and knowledge and reduced AIDS deaths. The passage highlights a local NGO, DAPP, which uses door-to-door efforts, rapid mobile testing, condom distribution, and involvement of former sex workers and chieftains to reduce stigma and expand reach.

The FBI arrested 23-year-old Jerry Drake Varnell of Sayre, Oklahoma, for allegedly attempting to detonate what he believed was an explosives-laden van outside an Oklahoma bank. A federal complaint says the FBI learned in December that Varnell wanted to blow up a building and that an undercover agent posed as a helper. Officials say he initially targeted the Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C., with a device similar to one used in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. Varnell is scheduled to appear in federal court Monday on a charge of attempting to use explosives to destroy a building in interstate commerce.

The passage says that in the UK, heart attacks and strokes have fallen by 30% over the past two decades, though they remain a major health hazard. It attributes progress partly to medicines that lower cholesterol and blood pressure, and it recommends lifestyle changes such as maintaining a healthy weight to improve cholesterol levels. It discusses statins, noting they are widely prescribed in England and that many reported side effects may be influenced by the nocebo effect, including findings from a study where side effects increased when people knew they were taking statins. The passage also mentions other cholesterol-lowering medicines for very high-risk people, including Repatha, Praluent, and Leqvio, and emphasizes quitting smoking, exercise, and dietary changes. It covers soluble fibre sources, suggestions for meals and snacks, cooking from scratch to limit hidden sugar and salt, and salt substitutes to reduce sodium and potentially lower early deaths and heart attack or stroke risk. It also describes plant chemicals that can block cholesterol absorption and mentions fortified foods and soya-based foods. The passage ends with prompts about understanding cholesterol results and the TLC diet.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoff notices sent to nearly all remaining employees at Voice of America, calling the administration’s actions a violation of his April order. The judge criticized Kari Lake and other Trump officials for keeping Voice of America’s programming and staffing at bare bones and for laying off 532 full-time journalists and support staff in August. He warned Lake and other officials that they risk contempt for failing to continue Voice of America’s worldwide news broadcasting, which the judge says is required by law.

The passage provides an introductory guide to American football, covering its origins, how it got its name, and its status in the Olympics. It credits Walter Camp with creating early consistent rules and describes key innovations he introduced, including 11-man teams, the line of scrimmage, the quarterback position, and the modern scoring format. It explains that American football is not an Olympic sport, outlines player and field dimensions, and compares U.S. and Canadian team sizes and field lengths. It details game duration, scoring methods (touchdowns, extra points, two-point conversions, field goals, safeties), and several common rules and penalties (such as offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer, and illegal formation). The passage also defines concepts including catches, turnovers (interceptions and fumbles), turnover on downs, the line of scrimmage and neutral zone, special teams, audibles, downs, and the red zone. It concludes by listing notable all-time players and offering further online clinics.

“Doubt” premieres Wednesday, Feb. 15 (10:00–11:00 PM ET/PT) on CBS following the season finale of “CODE BLACK.” The legal drama stars Katherine Heigl as Sadie Ellis, a defense attorney at a New York City firm, who begins to fall for her charismatic client, Billy Brennan, a pediatric surgeon accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years earlier. The series also focuses on other cases handled by the firm and gradually reveals Sadie’s backstory, including her mother being in prison. The cast includes Elliot Gould, Laverne Cox, Dulé Hill, and others, and the show addresses issues “in evenhanded ways,” according to the passage.

Police announced a breakthrough in the investigation into the Ballina murder of Aaron Marks, who was found with fatal injuries on a footpath earlier this month. Police seized a white Holden Commodore over the weekend and forensic officers are examining it for biological material such as fingerprints, DNA, and items linked to the offence. Investigators are calling for people who were passengers in the car to come forward, and said the driver is assisting with enquiries. Chief Insp Cameron Lindsay said he would prefer not to comment on whether Mr Marks gave any details before he died in hospital, and thanked the media and public for their assistance.

Callum Knott, 21, of Sandy Lane, admitted taking his aunt’s car from her address in Ollerton on November 20 without her consent and driving it without a licence or insurance. He was seen driving the car on Walesby Lane, later abandoned it in Ollerton when the battery died, and said he did it because he was “young and stupid” and thought he could get away with it. The court heard he had previously driven the car with permission and acted out of boredom. He was diagnosed with ADHD, expressed deep remorse, and was living with a friend after being kicked out of his mother’s address. He received a 12-month community order with 80 hours of unpaid work, a four-month driving ban, and was ordered to pay £85 costs and a £85 victim surcharge.

Cover 2 is described as a popular, effective defense because it limits quick passes and forces throws into tight downfield windows. It is defined as a 5-under, 2-deep scheme that supports stopping the quick passing game while having players over the top to deter deep throws. The passage explains that both cornerbacks play as flat defenders, often used situationally to stop perimeter quick passes and middle dump downs. Offenses attack Cover 2 by using high-low stretches on the corners, 3-receiver surface concepts involving the middle linebacker, vertical route concepts to challenge the two deep safeties, and middle-field attacks that exploit the open middle of the field, including corner-to-post route ideas. The passage also lists example plays from multiple college offenses, each illustrating specific ways to stress Cover 2.

The East Demerara Football Association held its Annual General meeting, observed by Mr. Stanley Lancaster of the Guyana Football Federation and Returning Officer Mr. Charles Corbin, with six of seven clubs present and Victoria Scorpions absent. After reports and deliberations, the new executive was chosen and Alfred King was returned for another term. The executive includes Alfred King (president), Gregory Wickham (1st VP), Gillian Frank (2nd VP), Mark Pertab (3rd VP), Gidel Austin (Secretary), Tessa Nedd (Treasurer), and Lindon Charles (Asst Sect/Treasurer). Curaleaf Holdings and the cannabis sector rose last August on news that the Trump administration would consider rescheduling cannabis. The rally later faded, then was revived by Trump’s Truth Social post about CBD benefits for elders. Curaleaf also expanded its international operations by entering Turkey and reported in-line financial results in August. The author maintains a “Hold” rating for CURLF stock due to sector uncertainty.

The passage is from Tesla, Inc.’s Quarterly Report on Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2020.
