Andrew Dawes, CEO of Intels Nigeria Limited, previously worked as Managing Director of Lagos-based AP Moller Terminal and has 20 years of experience in terminal operations and logistics across regions including North America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Dawes discussed Intels’ investment plans with the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Mrs. Hadiza Usman, during a visit to Intels’ Onne office, as Intels partners the Federal Government to boost port investment. In response to allegations that Intels operates a monopoly, Dawes said Intels invests billions of dollars on behalf of the NPA through concessioned terminals under government policy and does not issue oil and gas certificates to all terminals. He said Intels pays the government more than other private jetties and described the company’s approach as building long-term infrastructure. Dawes noted the challenges of low oil and gas prices and reduced cargo, and said investment pace would slow during recession while capacity would support future growth. He cited the Phase 4B project as a facility ready to receive a full FPSO, built with 4km of key length infrastructure to take large ships. Dawes also said the Badagry deep seaport project is progressing with APM Terminals and could be the largest port in Africa by draft. The passage additionally outlines Intels Nigeria Limited’s history, integrated logistics “one-stop-shop” services, and its mission and vision for supporting Nigeria’s oil and gas logistics sector.

The passage introduces a digital business ecosystem (DBE) as a closed or semi-closed system where SMEs interact through buyer–seller relationships in cyberspace. It aims to develop methodology to study ecosystem behavior under assumptions of closure and no external influences, specifically to identify which companies are likely to prosper and survive versus be suppressed under competitive co-existence. Because excitatory and inhibitory interactions among units can be asymmetric and oscillatory, the authors propose a neural-inspired model for mutual company interactions, leading to a set of nonlinear coupled differential equations governing each company’s fitness.

The paper then outlines a simulation methodology for constructing a realistic DBE based on statistical observations from a real DBE, including company product sell/want lists, product attributes, and trust/mistrust lists with reputation spreading. Trust categories are converted into numerical weights using the Weber–Fechner psychophysical law. For dynamics, the authors model fitness decay, self-excitation, excitatory signals driven by product demand/supply matches and trust, inhibitory signals driven by product similarity and strength, and optional input terms. They present iterative and threshold-based simulation dynamics, including removal of low-fitness companies and possible introduction of new ones.

Experiments use a simulated DBE (100 companies, 20 products) and report preliminary results showing how survival counts change with iterations and parameters, and that certain parameter settings can produce monopoly. The authors conclude that the approach enables study of DBE dynamics despite limited real data availability, while noting potential model improvements (e.g., inhibitory signals in finite supply settings) and the need to connect model parameters to measurable real quantities.

The passage explains the Camarilla pivot trading strategy, introduced in 1989 by Nick Scott. It is an extension of classical/floor trader pivot points designed for day traders to identify key intraday support and resistance levels, with four support and four resistance levels plus a central pivot, totaling nine levels. The indicator uses the previous day’s closing prices to compute these levels and is described as a versatile tool for recognizing key price levels, entry and exit points, and risk management. The passage compares Camarilla pivot points with Fibonacci pivot points, noting that Fibonacci pivots use Fibonacci studies with common retracement levels (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 100%) and extension levels (127%, 138%, 161.8%). It also states that day traders use pivot points to define important support and resistance and to detect potential trend changes. A referenced backtest of “ordinary” pivot points is said to show no “super profits,” and readers are encouraged to backtest their own ideas.

The passage describes lung cancer outcomes and the need for early detection, noting that lung cancer is often diagnosed at metastatic stage, leading to poor survival. It discusses US recommendations for annual low-dose CT (LDCT) screening and reports that adherence is low and false-positive rates for LDCT are high. The authors propose that a blood-based multi-omics biomarker test could improve screening and access.

Using data from the MOSAIC observational case-control study, they collected three blood samples per subject from 2,513 participants across 77 US sites and measured plasma proteins, RNA via RNA-seq, metabolites, and four targeted immunoassay proteins. After quality control, data were split into a training set (n=1,225) and a validation set (n=398). The study developed a machine learning lung cancer classifier using multi-omics analyte features and reported that models using only untargeted proteomics achieved an AUC of 0.91 for all-stage lung cancer, while the combined multi-omics classifier achieved an AUC of 0.96 for all stages and 0.93 for stage I. In the held-out validation set, the multi-omics classifier showed specificity and sensitivity of 89% across all stages, with stage I sensitivity of 80%.

The passage also reports that the top features in the validated classifier were distributed across proteins, transcripts, and metabolites, that many analyte features were associated with cancer stage, and that the final classifier used a manageable set of features. Limitations include the need for validation in a prospective study of the intended high-risk population aligned with LDCT screening recommendations.

The passage says longstanding academic publishing criticisms are fueling Trump administration attacks on the nation’s scientific enterprise. It cites concerns including research fraud, paper mills, too few qualified peer reviewers, and the high cost of journal subscriptions and open-access fees. It argues these problems are linked to incentive structures that reward scientists for publishing high volumes in widely cited journals. It describes HHS secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH director Jayanta Bhattacharya publicly criticizing the industry, pledging to address bias, misinformation, and access, and focusing on “replicable, reproducible, and generalizable” research. Some experts interviewed agree the grievances are real but doubt proposed solutions will create meaningful reform, warning that the administration could use them to pursue an ideological agenda. The passage also discusses Kennedy’s efforts to block government-funded scientists from publishing in certain journals, concerns about pharmaceutical industry influence on medical journals, and debate over whether creating or expanding government-linked journals and policies like open-access deposits can rebuild public trust. It notes Bhattacharya’s plan to rein in for-profit publishers by capping article processing charges and says some experts doubt that capping alone or NIH actions by themselves can fully change publishing incentives, emphasizing the need for scientists and academic institutions to lead broader evaluation reform.

The passage discusses a hockey team’s playoff performance and strategy, emphasizing that certain players have been rewarded for hard work and for playing tough minutes without much spotlight. It explains that the team operates within a system they have been comfortable with all year, with adjustments made during closely contested games, and highlights the importance of puck possession and directing pucks at the net. It also addresses tactics such as breaking up and countering opponents’ top line, mentions a key goal by Sammy Pahlsson, and comments on league competitiveness being influenced by the salary cap. Additional topics include player routines on game day, coach responses to questions about criticism of Getzlaf, praise for acquired defenseman Chris Pronger, limiting use of the fourth line for health and playoff experience reasons, and the team’s stated commitment to growth after a conference final loss, supported by roster stability and early-season preparation.

Lookout security researchers report that more than a thousand Google Play apps contain a spyware family called SonicSpy. The malware can silently record audio, take photos, make outbound calls, send texts to attacker-specified numbers, and access call logs, contacts, and Wi-Fi access point information. Researchers say it can respond to over 73 remote commands through a command-and-control server, allowing attackers to manipulate a victim’s device while providing messaging functionality and stealing data. A recent example, Soniac, was marketed as a messaging app using a customized Telegram variant, but SonicSpy hides itself by removing its launcher icon, connects to C2 infrastructure, and attempts to install its own Telegram variant. Lookout also found that the account behind Soniac previously posted two other SonicSpy samples that are no longer live, and said it is unclear whether they were removed by Google or by the actor to evade detection.

The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to proceed with stripping hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan nationals of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) under federal immigration law. In a brief unsigned order, the justices paused a ruling by U.S. District Judge Edward Chen that had barred Kristi Noem, Secretary of Homeland Security, from terminating TPS for Venezuelans. The Supreme Court said that although the case’s posture changed, the parties’ legal arguments and relative harms generally had not. The justices’ Democratic appointees indicated they would have denied the request; Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented, describing the order as a misuse of the court’s emergency docket. TPS designations are made by the DHS secretary based on conditions such as natural disasters, armed conflict, or other extraordinary and temporary conditions. The article describes prior TPS actions by former Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas, Noem’s termination of the 2023 designation and its extension, and litigation in federal court that included an earlier Supreme Court decision, Chen’s final ruling on Sept. 5, and a subsequent request by the solicitor general for Supreme Court intervention.

After the 2018 ICC Under-19 World Cup final, Manjot Kalra spoke with former New Zealand cricketer Simon Doull at the post-match presentation. Kalra described the batting conditions as flat and easy, and said the team environment was enjoyable. Doull tried to get Kalra to talk about his match-winning unbeaten century, which included a huge six on a free hit in the fourth over and two major stands with captain Prithvi Shaw and Shubman Gill; later he said he needed to take charge to ensure incoming batsmen could settle. The passage notes Kalra’s move to giving more interviews after returning home with India’s victorious team and discusses media comparisons to established Indian players. It also mentions Kalra was bought by Delhi Daredevils for Rs 20 lakh in the IPL auction and places his achievement in the context of other Under-19 final centurions, noting that none of four others played for senior national teams. The passage concludes with remarks from Rahul Dravid that the win should be a cherished memory without defining the team, and says it marks only the beginning for Kalra, Shaw, and others.

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Massachusetts is offering voluntary buyouts to about 750 employees as it cuts its workforce amid soaring health care costs and steep losses. The severance packages are for workers 55 and older with at least 10 years at the company, who make up about 18% of its 4,200-person workforce. The buyouts are the insurer’s first since the late 1980s.

The passage indicates that a website (Seeking Alpha) prompts users to enable JavaScript and cookies in their browser, and warns that an enabled ad-blocker may prevent proceeding, advising users to disable the ad-blocker and refresh.

The passage describes an invention for dynamic graphics rendering based on detecting saccades. It claims methods, systems, and non-transitory media that render a computer simulated scene, detect the onset of a saccade causing saccadic masking, and reduce computing resources used to render frames during at least part of the saccade duration. Computing resource reduction may include skipping or repeating frames, lowering rendering detail or resolution, and adjusting frame rate, with potential reallocation of saved processing time to low-frequency updates such as complex lighting calculations. The passage explains saccadic masking in the human visual system, provides background for power savings in VR, and discusses detecting and predicting saccade onset and duration using sensors such as cameras/optical sensors or EMG, including calibration of an eye movement model. It also references system components and examples of calibration and HMD implementations, and notes that saved computation can reduce overall power consumption.

Students at Max Hayes High School in Cleveland presented the city with a refurbished police cruiser they repaired after it was damaged during the Cavs championship celebrations in June 2016. The Auto Collision Repair program spent about a year and a half dismantling and rebuilding the vehicle, including sanding, painting, buffing, and replacing its roof, hood, and side panels. Materials were donated by several companies. After teacher Greg Boykin contacted the city, the students’ work changed the city’s plan to scrap the cruiser and saved about $10,000. Division of Motor Vehicle Maintenance Commissioner Jeff Brown said the cruiser will return to service as a zone car.

FX Strategists at UOB Group expect Cable’s pullback to the 1.2900 handle to be unlikely in the near term. They note that GBP could grind higher slowly toward 1.3040/45, with resistance at 1.3060 and support at 1.2975, followed by the 1.2939 low, which they expect to hold intraday pullbacks. They say the bearish phase remains intact but patchy downward momentum and a short-term rebound reduce the odds of an extension to 1.2900, though another push lower is not ruled out unless GBP moves clearly above 1.3060 to indicate the bearish phase has ended.

The passage describes building and backtesting an RSI-based trading strategy in TradingView using Pine Script. It outlines using a 14-period RSI on DOT with 65/35 overbought/oversold levels on a 5-minute timeframe, entering Long when RSI exits oversold, entering Short when RSI exits overbought, and exiting at the RSI mid level (50). It explains how to add the RSI indicator, write a Pine Script strategy using built-in `ta.rsi`, define entry conditions, use `strategy.entry` and `strategy.close`, add user inputs for adjustable RSI period and thresholds, and run the strategy via “Add to chart” to view results such as equity curve, net profit, drawdown, win rate, and performance metrics. It also notes that “deep backtest” is available with Pro or better accounts for more historical data and that exporting data to CSV is not available for free users.

Police arrested 40-year-old Nannette Perkins on April 16, 2017, at her Taylorsville home after Salt Lake City police received a tip about her identity. She is believed to be the pajama-wearing robber in at least six bank robberies in the Salt Lake City area, including five on Saturday morning within less than two hours. Unified police Lt. Brian Lohrke said the suspect reportedly wore pajama bottoms, eyeglasses, and a blue bandanna over dark hair in a ponytail while robbing banks in Cottonwood Heights, Salt Lake City, Sandy, Holladay, and West Valley City. Perkins is being held at the Salt Lake County jail pending an initial court appearance.

The passage argues that student news is important because going to university is compared to living in a small town where people rely on local news to stay informed. It says removing a newsroom would be like taking away local news, which could harm communities, especially as “news deserts” are spreading in America. It cites John Temple, who said locals can be deprived of understanding and making informed decisions about local government issues, noting that the world does not support local news economically. The passage also claims that a small number of powerful corporations control much of the popular news due to “pack journalism” and media consolidation, making news less diverse than assumed. It argues that without student news, students would lack tools to become well-informed and educated, and the country should not fail the current generation of students by not informing the public.

The passage describes the Band of Brothers Men’s Ring, a 24k gold-layered ring available in whole sizes 8 to 14, shipped in a custom jeweler’s box. It is sold exclusively by American Mint and can be ordered online or by phone, offered at $129.90 for a limited time. Kevin Sacher, American Mint’s president, is quoted about honoring those who fought to preserve liberty and independence. The passage also states American Mint provides collectible products, has served over a million customers from its Mechanicsburg facility, and that its parent company operates in nine countries and has served 10 million collectors. Contact and company information for American Mint is included.

The passage describes challenges affecting Thailand’s vocational education due to rapid technological and societal changes, which have led to skill mismatches with labor market needs and problematic educational outcomes. It states that the Office of Vocational Education Commission manages vocational education in response to external pressures (globalization, science, technology) and internal changes (demographic, environmental, economic, social, political), aiming to improve student and graduate quality, align with employer needs, and build public confidence.

The research used a two-phase R&D method to (1) investigate needs for managing vocational education toward excellence and (2) develop a strategic framework for excellence. Phase 1 involved document analysis, expert review of a questionnaire, reliability testing, data collection from vocational education institutions, and analysis using indices and SWOT/strategy formulation, including interviews with personnel from exemplary institutions. Phase 2 synthesized findings and evaluated strategy suitability and feasibility through expert focus groups.

Results indicate the current conditions were high level and desired conditions were at the highest level, with the overall necessity index (PNImodified) reported as 0.179, highest for curriculum development and cooperation networks. The developed excellence strategies include components of vision, mission, objectives, strategies, and indicators, organized into six strategy areas: enhancing professional management, developing competency-based curricula to international standards, improving teaching and learning management, developing teacher and staff expertise, building collaborative networks, and improving graduate quality for the labor market. Suitability and feasibility were rated at the highest level. Recommendations focus on implementing competency-based curriculum development to international standards and adapting strategies to each institution’s context, as well as future research on curriculum design models and digital content production and professional competency standards.

David Dickinson is a freelance science writer, US Air Force veteran, and long-time amateur astronomer. The passage describes widespread U.S. preparations for an upcoming total solar eclipse (Aug. 21), including warnings about traffic, Wi-Fi outages, and shortages. It explains that a small community of long-planning eclipse chasers, called umbraphiles, seeks the moon’s shadow for seconds of totality, describing totality as a rare, difficult-to-recreate experience. The author recounts previous eclipse viewing attempts, including partial and annular eclipses, and plans to watch the Aug. 21 eclipse at the Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in North Carolina for 107 seconds. The passage also advises that looking at the sun during an eclipse can harm eyes and stresses proper eye protection during partial phases. It notes that the moon is gradually moving away from Earth, making total solar eclipses rarer and eventually ending, and mentions a follow-up eclipse on April 8, 2024 with a rain date idea for Aug. 21.

The passage states that cancer cells use mitochondria to reprogram neighboring cells by transferring mitochondria through threadlike tubes to fibroblasts, which are connective tissue cells. It says the mitochondria infiltrate fibroblasts, fueling cancer growth and altering gene activity, and describes this as cancer “brainwashing” neighbors.

The passage presents a mean reversion trading strategy for QQQ, describing rules for exiting trades by waiting for the close to be higher than either yesterday’s high or yesterday’s close. It reports that since January 2000, an equity curve starting at $100,000 with 100% compounding (without deducting taxes) has shown significant returns, including a high profit factor, minimal drawdown compared with buy and hold, and a CAGR of 12.34% versus buy and hold’s 9%. It states that mean reversion has worked for QQQ historically, but the future effectiveness is uncertain.

The passage describes a study of AI-in-healthcare publications’ “maturity” and key characteristics. The authors report limited prior work assessing how mature such publications are, and perform PubMed searches to identify relevant papers. They state they developed and applied a semi-automated evaluation approach using a BERT-based model to classify publication maturity from titles/abstracts, supported by manual annotation of mature articles’ data types, model types, and disease types. Using three years of data (2019–2021), they report non-monotonic maturation patterns, with 6.01% mature publications in 2019, 7.7% in 2020, and 1.81% in 2021; they excluded systematic reviews from further analysis. They find radiology has the most mature models across specialties, and that image data dominate mature publications, while tabular data declined and was absent in 2021. They report deep learning is the most frequent model type among mature publications and provide results on geographic distribution, noting higher frequencies in developed nations and underrepresentation of some regions. They conclude the overall percentage of mature publications is low and suggest opportunities to leverage diverse datasets and models to increase maturity yields.

The passage describes the London breakout (London daybreak) strategy, a forex day trading approach that trades breakouts above or below the pre-London trading range formed during the Asian session. The breakout typically occurs within the first three hours of the London session: traders take long positions for upside breakouts and short positions for downside breakouts. The Asian session range can be defined using either the high-low prices or the open-close candle body prices. A London breakout indicator is also mentioned as a custom tool that helps spot London breakout opportunities and provides entry, stop loss, and take profit levels. The passage includes a backtest discussion for EURUSD and concludes that performance is not good, implying the strategy likely needs more parameters or risk management, with skepticism about results. It also provides typical times for the London, Asian, and New York forex sessions and outlines how the indicator can automate trades.

The passage introduces antiferromagnetic domain walls as a subject of sustained study, highlighting that antiferromagnets can now be observed and manipulated more efficiently, including through optical/electrical control and current-induced switching via domain-wall motion. It describes antiferromagnetic dynamics as extensions of the nonlinear σ-model for the Néel vector, with behavior differing from ferromagnets and potentially offering advantages such as the absence of stray fields. The authors study domain-wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque, finding that precessional dynamics arise spontaneously as a steady state, along with domain-wall propagation at constant velocity and, for certain spin-current polarizations, periodic oscillations between two positions. The paper then presents a spin-chain model with antiferromagnetic exchange, optional Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and perpendicular anisotropy, along with discrete equations of motion including damping and a spin-torque term from polarized electrons. It develops a continuum extension of the nonlinear σ-model (with damping and spin torque) and provides expressions for magnetization in terms of the Néel vector. Finally, it begins a section on precessional dynamics by simulating a domain wall under a spin-current polarization along \( \hat{e}_3 \) and setting \( \lambda=0 \), leading to a steady state where spins precess with a constant angular frequency.

A Nigerian banker shared a social media warning describing an ATM fraud method in which scammers approach customers, claim they need help withdrawing money, and ask for transfers into the customer’s account. The transfers, the post says, are often made from stolen phones or hacked bank accounts, leading banks to freeze accounts, flag BVN records, block ATM transactions, and sometimes issue memos for police apprehension. The passage includes two reported victims: an 18-year-old held at gunpoint who had 40k transferred and withdrawn, and an adult with about 1 million naira whose 50k transfer led to BVN flagging and an order for possible arrest. The banker advises people not to help anyone with transfers for withdrawal at ATMs, even acquaintances.

The passage describes impurity segregation during Bridgman crystal growth and its impact on impurity-sensitive properties, including magnetic behavior from magnetic dopants such as manganese. It focuses on bulk MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method (IVBM), which form magnetically and structurally distinct septuple layers (SLs) of MnBi₂Te₄ within the topological Bi₂Te₃ quintuple-layer (QL) host. The structural organization—QL/SL stacking sequence, spacing, distribution, and Mn content—varies across different ingot sections even when overall composition is the same, leading to different magnetic phases.

Samples taken from different positions show distinct structures and Mn concentrations: Sample A contains mainly pure MnBi₂Te₄ with local MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ inclusions and the highest average Mn concentration; Sample B shows SLs separated by 1–2 QLs with dominant MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃; Sample C has increased SL spacing with a recurring pattern of about (7 ± 2) QLs between SLs and a much lower Mn concentration; Sample D near the ingot end shows increased disorder with SLs spaced by 4–5 QLs and Mn-rich multilayers. Magnetic measurements indicate antiferromagnetic transitions in Samples A and B (TN = 26 K and 13.5 K for dominant phases), while Samples C and D show ferromagnetic-like behavior with Curie temperatures near 10 K (with Tc values varying by sample). Magnetic resonance data show increased anisotropy near phase transitions, consistent with the phase behavior.

The growth mechanism section identifies four growth stages under IVBM: turbulent flow, rapid MnTe precipitation, stationary flow, and cessation of material flow. MnTe precipitation early in growth reduces Mn in the melt (about ~14 at.% to ~7 at.%), enabling mixed MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ growth. A diffusion-driven competition between MnBi₂Te₄ edges governs SL spacing, described as an inverse relationship between SL spacing and MnTe supersaturation. When convection ceases, MnTe incorporation and edge competition intensify, leading to structural degradation such as Mn depletion in SLs and changes in stacking, producing the disordered Sample D. The conclusions emphasize that controlled melt composition and flow dynamics determine stacking order, Mn content, SL spacing, and thereby magnetic and topological behavior.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) is a familial, autosomal dominant cancer syndrome involving two or more endocrine gland tumors. The passage describes MEN1, MEN2 (MEN2A, MEN2B, FMTC), and MEN4, including their causative genes, typical associated tumors, and inheritance or sporadic occurrence. It notes that MEN is under-studied in India and reports use of IndiGen (1029 healthy individuals) to estimate genetic prevalence and MEN-linked variant landscapes, following ACMG/AMP variant classification guidance. The study classifies MEN-linked variants across RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B, compiles them into a database (MEN-Associated Pathogenic Variants, MAPVar) with 3,280 ACMG-classified variants, and compares likely pathogenic RET variants across 18 global population datasets. Genetic epidemiology in India is calculated, including an estimate of carriers for likely pathogenic RET mutations. The passage also outlines methods for variant annotation, database interface design, patient validation using GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort data (7 cases; 5 variants), and development of an NGS multiplex primer panel covering coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B, with successful resolution of 3 cases and further ACMG-based classification for others.

Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s company Habona Ltd in Rwanda employs 25 young people who collect garbage, separate plastic and metal, and convert organic waste into fuel briquettes for cooking, with remaining material used to make organic fertiliser sold to farmers; the company produces 50 tonnes of fuel a month. The waste management process reduces greenhouse gases and supports a “green revolution” for Africa by addressing climate change impacts on food security and water availability. The passage also highlights initiatives led by young Africans and young people in agriculture and technology: Pilirani Khoza’s programme in Malawi trains sponsored female science students as extension workers who teach farmers simple water-saving irrigation methods, reaching 360 farmers; in Kenya, Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo uses a handheld soil sensor and mobile-phone service to help farmers choose inputs and crops, with reported improvements for some farmers and a goal to reach 200,000 farmers. Additional quotes discuss the need for tailored solutions for smallholders, youth leadership in climate mitigation, and the role of agriculture in reducing poverty through productivity and value-chain improvements, including technologies and clean energy.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 13, 2020, reporting that on February 13, 2020 it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to issue and sell 2,650,000 shares of common stock in a public offering. The underwriters were granted an option for up to an additional 397,500 shares, exercised in full on February 18, 2020. The offering closed on February 19, 2020, and net proceeds were approximately $2.31 billion. The company also reported that, in connection with the offering, registration rights were waived, and it stated that a legal opinion and a press release announcing the offering were filed as exhibits.

Enron warned that continuing credit worries, asset value declines, and reduced trading activity could hurt its fourth-quarter earnings. It said it might need to take a large pretax loss tied to a partnership’s investments and may have to come up with more money to honor a “demand obligation” on a $690 million note after its credit rating was lowered. Enron also filed that its third-quarter loss increased after accounting adjustments and that it was restating earnings dating back to 1997. Separately, senior bankers reportedly worried that Dynegy could withdraw from its proposed rescue deal for Enron, possibly triggering a “material adverse change” clause. Several reports also discussed calls for investigations into auditor Arthur Andersen and noted Enron’s financial difficulties, including upcoming debt repayments and potential further obligations if credit ratings drop.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, with earnings consistent with the prior year but including $2.7 million in charges related to the LSBG acquisition and core system conversion expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2017. Total assets increased $175.3 million to $1.8 billion, and total loans rose $139 million (14%). Fourth quarter 2016 diluted earnings per share were 42 cents, net of 19 cents per share in acquisition and system conversion costs. Total non-interest income for 2016 increased $3.4 million (38%), and excluding securities gains, non-interest income remained flat. CEO Curtis C. Simard said the company expanded its core business while improving loan growth and credit quality.

The passage describes football fans at Silverbluff Audubon Center in remote Aiken County, South Carolina, who are rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl. It explains that the center has bald eagles, including a nesting pair since 1994, and shows them at the site. Speakers comment on the eagles as a national symbol and hope the birds “show on Sunday,” while noting that Patriots also like seeing the Eagles score.

R. Thomas Beach, principal consultant for Crossborder Energy, submits rebuttal testimony on behalf of the Indicated Electric Generators in support of the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement. He says the rebuttal responds to direct testimony supporting the Post-Interim Settlement Agreement (PISA) by the Southern California Generation Coalition (SCGC) and The Utility Reform Network (TURN), and that the sponsors do not support SCGC/TURN’s PISA to the extent it fails to unbundle intrastate transmission. Beach argues that the Commission should focus on a statewide, consistent restructuring approach based on prior findings, and that SoCalGas’s backbone and local transmission functions can be unbundled in a manner similar to the PG&E Gas Accord. He contends that the Gas Accord’s city-gate market produced substantial benefits for electric generators and that unbundling benefited end users without requiring them to hold capacity or pay demand charges. Beach also argues that SCGC/TURN’s cost/benefit analysis overstates costs and ignores benefits of transmission unbundling, including modest reductions in transportation rates and reduced risks for electric generators under the Comprehensive Settlement. He further disputes SCGC/TURN’s emphasis on demand charges, arguing that the proposed structure and settlement provisions limit demand-charge impacts and that generators can mitigate risks through options such as city-gate purchases, interruptible service, and trading capacity. He concludes by stating this completes his rebuttal testimony.

The passage lists VOT shortwave broadcast frequencies and times for “Tibet time,” “India time,” and “Nepal time,” noting that frequencies should be re-tuned frequently and that the target area is Tibet. It also describes VOT satellite radio ASIASAT 7 (AS7) in C-band at 105.5° East (“MOMO”), including a downlink frequency of 4146 MHz, horizontal polarization, symbol rate 5317, FEC 5/6, 24-hour availability, and reception details for China; the service is audio 24/7 with alternating 30-minute segments in Mandarin and Tibetan continuously.

Radford University has narrowed its search for the Vice President for Student Affairs to two finalists. The role opened after Dr. Irvin Clark announced his departure at the end of the 2017 Spring Semester, and Susan Trageser has served as interim since then. On September 11, 2017, Dr. Thomas C. Segar, current Vice President for Student Affairs at Shepherd University, spoke to students, faculty, and staff. He described initiatives focused on student learning and success, belonging, social justice, experiential learning, strong student services, and institutional pride. On September 12, 2017, Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, current Dean of Campus Life at the New York Institute of Technology, spoke. She emphasized connecting with students, especially first-generation students, and highlighted the need for universities to be adaptable and flexible to changing student needs. Both finalists presented as experienced student affairs professionals excited about the opportunity at Radford.

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case over whether the U.S. Postal Service and the federal government can be sued for an intentional failure to deliver mail. Landlady Lebene Konan alleged that postal workers intentionally failed to deliver mail as part of alleged racial harassment, after repeated key and delivery problems that led her to file more than 50 administrative complaints. The government argued that sovereign immunity applies due to a “postal exception” covering claims arising from the “loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission” of mail. A lower court dismissed her case, but the 5th Circuit partially revived it, saying intentional nondelivery is not “loss,” “miscarriage,” or “negligent transmission.” Justices debated how those terms should be interpreted, with some expressing concern about opening lawsuits over lost or late mail and others discussing whether a ruling for Konan would expand litigation against the USPS. The decision is expected by early July.

The passage gives three UFC 216 fight predictions, each favoring Dariush in unanimous decision outcomes (one also predicting a submission in round 2). It states that Dariush is the better overall fighter, with particular strength on the ground, and that despite Evan Dunham or Scott Harris having momentum or certain skills, Dariush is expected to prevail.

Jacob Allen sued Richard Knight and Hannah (as executrix of her former husband, Hope Allen) for withholding and not paying him about sixty-four pounds given to him by Hope Allen’s will. The jury found for the plaintiff, and the defendant was ordered to pay and deliver Jacob Allen his proportional part of Hope Allen’s estate according to the will, plus court costs totaling forty-one shillings and five pence.

Nick Kyrgios helped Australia level against Germany in their 2018 Davis Cup tie at the Pat Rafter Arena in Brisbane. On Day 1, he beat German World No. 2 Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the second singles rubber. Earlier, Alexander Zverev was pushed by Alex de Minaur to a fifth-set tiebreaker, with Zverev coming back after trailing two sets to one and then winning the deciding set. After Zverev gave Germany a 1-0 lead, Kyrgios won to make it 1-1. The tie continues Saturday with doubles, and Sunday features reverse singles between Kyrgios and Zverev, with a possible additional singles match between Struff and de Minaur.

Jeffrey Saut, Raymond James’ chief investment strategist, warned that “the damage is done” after US President Donald Trump and North Korea’s Kim Jong-un exchanged nuclear war threats, with experts fearing escalation could lead to nuclear conflict and trigger a global market sell-off. Saut said some “technical damage” has occurred and investors may want to trim positions, though he expects a market pullback without ending a “secular bull market.” He also said war is unlikely and noted that any conflict could send oil prices up to around $150 a barrel, but that is not expected. Gina Sanchez of Chantico Global said markets could see heightened volatility not seen since the crisis.

The passage discusses efforts in higher education to build global competencies, noting that despite widespread institutional emphasis on global citizenship, only about one percent of U.S. students participate in study abroad. It describes challenges to scaling international education programs—especially financial barriers—and presents a structured methodology for designing sustainable education abroad business models. The article emphasizes interdependence among curricular, operational, and financial logistics, detailing considerations such as learning outcomes, program structure and assessment, host-university alignment, risk management, leadership, travel planning, student preparation and wellbeing, and emergency readiness. It also outlines financial logistics, including how to match expenses with program income, plan expenses and income sources, and distribute program budgets. Finally, it provides a typology of twelve travel-abroad program business models, including external party-led, faculty-led, and student-led models, and concludes with principles for alleviating financial burdens, using staff support, and delegating tasks to students to create impactful, sustainable global learning experiences.

Susanne Henning, the UCLA study lead author, said green tea polyphenols are known to be more effective and provide more health benefits than black tea polyphenols because they are absorbed into blood and tissue. She also reported that new findings suggest black tea may contribute to good health and weight loss in humans via a gut microbiome mechanism that changes intestinal bacteria ratios by increasing microbes linked to lean body mass and decreasing those linked to obesity. The study fed four groups of mice different diets, including low-fat/high-sugar, high-fat/high-sugar, and two high-fat/high-sugar groups receiving either green or black tea extract. The passage concludes that black tea may have an advantage because it works in the gut, while green tea works in the liver as well, and suggests combining both drinks might be helpful.

Michael Buskey, 19, was found dead of a gunshot wound in the woods near his Plymouth apartment on May 8, and his death was ruled a suicide. Court documents say Parker Hogan, 19, brought a gun, notebook, and pen to the scene and instructed a friend on holding the gun at the correct angle to his head, and that Hogan helped plan and practice Buskey’s suicide. Police said Hogan left the woods, returned after hearing the gunshot, removed a phone playing a song on repeat, took the gun and a note Buskey wrote to family members, and then called police and Buskey’s father. Hogan was arraigned and entered not guilty pleas, and police said he posted bail. He is scheduled to appear in court in July.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 8, 2021. The company announced it will redeem all outstanding 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021 on September 6, 2021. The redemption price will equal the €1,750,000,000 principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest up to, but excluding, the redemption date. The filing does not constitute a notice of redemption, and holders are directed to the notice delivered by the trustee. The exhibit listed is a Microsoft press release dated July 8, 2021.

The speaker discusses adjustments during a game, including improving visibility of the puck during power plays, managing Zdeno due to his size, and making key saves early. They describe the game as exciting and tight for room on the ice, anticipate overtime, and credit practicing fundamentals to stay sharp after a long layoff. The speaker also notes limitations in looking over an opponent’s shoulder, describes positioning for better shot visibility, and says they are happy to win and will focus on the next game in the series starting Saturday.

The passage discusses how 21st-century technological developments, especially digital transformation, affect open and distance education and the managerial processes of higher education institutions. It reviews how technologies such as artificial intelligence, wearable technologies, metaverse, blockchain, and brain-computer interfaces could be used across distance education activities and management functions, while also emphasizing organizational adaptation, planning, and investment considerations. It presents a case study methodology based on semi-structured interviews with experienced academics and analyzes responses through content analysis. The results describe anticipated impacts of advanced technologies on education (e.g., adaptive learning, meta-assistants, AI-guided support), management (e.g., more efficient planning/supervision/evaluation, potential hierarchy reduction, knowledge-worker needs), and economy and socio-cultural life (e.g., automation anxiety, potential unemployment and new job areas, possible lifestyle and psychological/communication changes, and concerns requiring rights/legal/ethical work). The conclusion highlights key technologies and suggests recommendations such as developing AI assistants and blockchain-based recognition/certification tools, advancing adaptive synthetic content and metaverse teaching systems, and conducting further research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips.

Officials marked the completion of utility-scale solar arrays near Las Vegas built to power commercial data centers in Northern and Southern Nevada. The 179 MW Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects were commissioned Monday at Apex Industrial Park and are designed to meet the needs of 46,000 Nevada homes, with the generated power dedicated to Switch for facilities in Reno and Las Vegas. The event included Harry Reid, federal land managers, local officials, EDF Renewable Energy, and First Solar, and an NV Energy executive said the arrays bring the total number of Nevada solar plants to 16.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch developers’ project plan after certifying a final additional environmental analysis and declaring issues related to greenhouse gas emissions and protection of the endangered unarmored three spine stickleback resolved. The department originally approved the project in December 2010, but in 2015 the California Supreme Court ordered it to reexamine greenhouse gas emissions and related determinations under the California Environmental Quality Act, and to reassess two mitigation measures approved in 2010 as they relate to the species’ “fully protected” status. In response, Newhall Land and Farming Company revised its greenhouse mitigation plan, including changes to bridge timing and construction methods to avoid water contact during construction and to eliminate the need for the two stickleback-protection measures approved in 2010. The California Air Resources Board concluded the revised project has an adequate basis to determine it does not result in net additional greenhouse gas emissions. The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is expected to take up final re-approval on July 19.

The message assesses implications of the Andropov regime for U.S.-Soviet relations, concluding that Andropov’s foreign policy is largely unchanged from Brezhnev, with no relaxation on Afghanistan, Poland, or hard-line positions such as Southern Africa. It argues that Soviet policy priority is relations with the U.S. and recommends returning to first principles centered on U.S. security and reducing the danger of nuclear war. It calls for heightened emphasis on arms control and focuses on INF, stating that the U.S. “zero-zero” negotiating position is no longer useful and should be changed. The Soviet strategy toward INF is described as seeking to prevent U.S. deployment without affecting its own capabilities by using Geneva negotiations and propaganda to influence Western European, especially German, public opinion. The message also recalls the INF debate from 1977–1979, describing the NATO double decision as primarily political to assure Europeans of U.S. defense, and noting that the number 572 was chosen to equalize SS–20 warhead arsenals in a way viewed as “de-coupling” while still establishing U.S. credibility.

Bank analysts are testing whether Apple will offer an LTE-capable modem in the Apple Watch Series 3. Ming-chi Kuo of KGI Securities says Apple will have both cellular and non-cellular models in 38mm and 42mm sizes, with modems supporting only LTE. He notes that Apple Watch sales could reach 17.5 million to 18 million next year, with at least half being Series 3, and 2.8 million to 3.6 million LTE units (about 35–40%). Sales are expected to begin soon after product launches this fall, likely alongside new iPhones.

The passage describes neural modulation medical devices and systems, focusing on delivering a desired linear electric field in neural tissue using electrodes with fractionalized anode and cathode currents based on a “target multipole.” It discusses continuation/prior-application claim information, neuromodulation examples (e.g., SCS, DBS, PNS, FES), and background on spinal cord anatomy and pain therapy. A system is presented that includes leads with electrodes, a neural modulation generator, and a programming system that determines electrode fractionalizations using the target multipole to produce a linear electric field over a tissue volume. Multiple optional configurations are described (e.g., in-line anodes/cathodes with a center point, directional electrodes extending less than 360 degrees, flanking electrodes, and multipole arrangements with different numbers of poles). The passage also outlines programming and user-interface features for adjusting parameters such as angle, focus, and spread, optionally using patient-anatomy inputs to determine the target multipole, and using search heuristics to optimize field properties. It further describes method steps for programming and delivering modulation energy to generate the linear field, and provides extensive detail on spinal cord modulation system architectures, electrode programming concepts, and embodiments aimed at preferentially modulating dorsal horn and/or dorsal root tissue while minimizing activation of dorsal column tissue.

A Senate committee report released Wednesday makes 50 recommendations to speed up criminal trials, arguing that the Canadian criminal justice system needs a complete rethink rather than rigid “drop-dead” timelines. Senators George Baker and Bob Runciman criticized the Supreme Court of Canada’s July “Jordan” ruling, which set 18-month deadlines in provincial courts and 30-month ceilings in superior courts. They said the Supreme Court lacked enough data about the ruling’s potential impact before imposing the timelines, warning that “tens of thousands” of criminal charges could be tossed next year as a result.

John Bryant, an incarcerated pro se plaintiff, filed a complaint under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 alleging that from about December 24, 1999 to January 13, 2000 inmates at Sing Sing were kept in “Code Blue” lockdown conditions based on a false report by Officer Hernandez, and that this led to violations of multiple constitutional rights and inadequate state labor compensation. DOCS moved to dismiss its claims on Eleventh Amendment grounds, and a magistrate judge recommended dismissal. After reviewing the matter, the district court granted the motion to dismiss as to DOCS and Sing Sing, concluding it lacked subject matter jurisdiction under Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity because state agencies are immune from suit under § 1983 absent consent or congressional abrogation. The court directed Bryant to advise the court on the status of service on Officer Hernandez by June 29, 2001.

The Government plans to increase powers for staff and suppliers affected by large-scale insolvencies and to take action against “irresponsible” company directors. Ministers cite recent failures such as Carillion and BHS as raising concerns that some directors could protect themselves or profit from insolvency while workers and small suppliers are harmed. Proposed measures include reversing asset stripping to claw back money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies, and giving the Insolvency Service new powers. Business Secretary Greg Clark said the reforms would strengthen regulators to address abuse. The Insolvency Service disqualifies about 1,200 directors a year. Frank Field said corporate accountability has broken down in parts of British industry, and Rebecca Long-Bailey criticized the Government for not acting earlier after BHS and Carillion.

A $1.8-million project by the Grand River Conservation Authority will use LiDAR laser technology to create digital 3D maps of the floodplains of the Speed and Conestogo rivers and the entire Grand River floodplain over the next five years. The authority expects the maps to support near real-time forecasting of downstream flooding, identify areas at imminent risk, and integrate with new U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flood forecasting software. Existing floodplain maps are mostly older hard-copy sheets, and the new LiDAR models will show land and detailed riverbed features such as deep gullies and shallow banks. The authority says updating is important because the river changes over time, with possible sandbars and moved debris.

A team of engineers reports a novel optical technique that rapidly screens amino acid sequences to reveal structural properties of proteins, including in living bacteria. The approach addresses the need for fast, efficient screening of large numbers of protein sequences with minimal sample volume and avoids heating that alters crystalline structure. Using femto- and pico-second lasers in a flow-cytometry setup and a method called time-domain thermo-transmission, the researchers screen proteins in milliseconds and do not kill living cells. They demonstrated that the method works in proof-of-concept research for both natural and synthetic proteins, including synthetic variants adapted from squid ring teeth proteins. The team received a DURIP grant to develop a machine for larger-scale screening, and the Army Research Office supported the work.

The passage discusses an upcoming “must win” game tomorrow night and emphasizes focusing on what players need to do rather than worrying about consequences or results. It notes that the team wants to win the cup as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, with coaching staff reviewing defensive tapes and making adjustments. The speaker says the team needs to improve its play, particularly along the boards, and mentions that predicting how Detroit will play is difficult due to the strength of its lines and factors like skated minutes.

The passage discusses how, in e-commerce interactions between a trusting agent and a trusted agent, risk analysis is important before initiating a transaction. Risk is described as reflecting the variance of possible outcomes and is linked to probability of failure and consequences of failure; risk identification is presented as central to risk management. The authors also describe digital business ecosystems and argue that a trusting agent should choose trusted agents based on its desired outcomes, analyzing the probability of failure accordingly.  

A methodology is proposed to quantify an interaction’s probable risk by defining “FailureLevel” and “failure scale,” and by determining FailureLevel in two time phases: pre-interaction start time and post-interaction start time. Risk is treated as dynamic, so FailureLevel is determined in regular intervals by dividing a time space into non-overlapping time slots. In the pre-interaction phase, FailureLevel is based on past interaction history or recommendations from other agents, filtered by trustworthiness, timing, and relevant criteria. In the post-interaction phase, Future FailureLevel is predicted using earlier FailureLevels and a Gaussian distribution to compute the probability of each failure level within a defined range. The paper provides an example with two candidate trusted agents to demonstrate calculating probabilities of future FailureLevel and selecting the highest-probability level for each post-interaction time slot. The conclusion reiterates the need for analyzing possible risk before interacting with a probable trusted agent and summarizes the proposed methodology and example.

Iowa State lost 38-30 to Cincinnati in Week 6, ending its unbeaten season and marking its first defeat. Cincinnati took a 31-7 lead at halftime, and Iowa State’s comeback efforts did not exceed 30. The loss is described as reopening the Big 12, which is portrayed as highly unpredictable. The passage also discusses last season’s Big 12 chaos, including underdog teams tied for the regular season title and teams that underperformed in conference play.

A memorial match will be held this Sunday at Stark’s Park for Kirkcaldy footballer Aidan Sutherland, who died from complications from diabetes shortly after his 20th birthday. The event, organized by Ben Graham, aims to raise awareness of diabetes and donations for the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation, with activities including a pipe band, stalls, face painting, and a “sweetie bar,” and a match featuring friends and former teammates alongside Colin Cameron and Darren Dods. The day follows a card display at Raith’s win over Arbroath, after Aidan became ill in July during a trip to Newcastle. Aidan’s family and organizers stressed the need to recognize diabetes symptoms quickly and take action, and Raith chairman Alan Young said the club is helping raise awareness and funds. Kick-off is 1pm, with events starting at noon.

The speaker says that when things do not go well, teams should talk about it, learn from it, and get better, even if the conversations are difficult. They note that reviewing what happened in games helped, including mistakes that could be corrected. The speaker describes specific game situations involving positioning and discipline, and says emotions must be kept in check and players should stay disciplined. They also discuss using all players, different situations, and depth, citing injuries and teammates stepping up, including Fabbs, who played a “fantastic game” after joining the team at this level.

The passage describes Kazakhstan’s state education program (2011–2020) aiming to improve inclusive education in schools, including increasing schools meeting inclusive education conditions to 70% by 2020 and ensuring unhindered access for disabled children at 20%. It outlines inclusive education concepts (system inclusiveness, access inclusiveness, and social inclusion), the need for appropriate teacher and school arrangements, and discusses the rights to education for people with disabilities, including requirements under UN conventions and the Education of All Disabled Children Act. It also explains distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic and presents a case study evaluating disabled education in distance education using special education teachers’ opinions in Kazakhstan. The study uses semi-structured online interviews with 10 teachers and analyzes data via thematic analysis, organizing results into lesson delivery practices, meeting individual learning needs, family participation, and teacher-student/peer interaction. Teachers reported using online lessons, video sharing, homework control, online events, and mobile applications; most preferred formal education over distance education. They generally found distance education insufficient for meeting individual learning needs, reported family anxiety and issues related to technology, communication, and online family education, and identified problems in interaction including weak communication, insufficient time, and unqualified or irregular interaction. The passage concludes with recommendations to diversify technology-based learning methods, create individualized learning content, organize online seminars to support family participation, and plan regular social activities to improve teacher-student/peer interaction.

The passage describes evidence that network dysconnectivity and hyperexcitability are intrinsic features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), with seizures being a common manifestation. It reports bidirectional associations between epilepsy and AD, including increased risk in both directions, and notes that epilepsy coexists with cognitive impairment and worsens clinical outcomes and lifespan. It summarizes analyses of high-throughput transcriptomic data from multiple AD cohorts to investigate whether epilepsy-causing genes show shared dysregulated signatures in a worse cognitive AD subtype (“SPD,” synaptic plasticity dysfunction). The study reports dysregulation of multiple epilepsy-causing genes in the SPD profile, with 16 genes shared across cohorts and mostly downregulated, and it identifies enrichment of epilepsy-related pathways (e.g., glutamatergic, GABAergic, and synaptic transmission; channel activity). It also finds that effect sizes for epilepsy-causing genes are more pronounced in later AD stages, interprets this as potential involvement in AD onset and progression, and concludes that overlapping genetic and molecular mechanisms may contribute to both conditions while the temporal order remains unclear.

The passage argues that uranium prices, reflected by the URA ETF chart, are correcting rather than losing momentum after a February high. It cites the World Nuclear Association, which says 160 nuclear power reactors are planned and over 300 more proposed, alongside existing reactors in multiple countries, implying increased reliance on nuclear power. Analysts quoted in the passage are generally bullish, forecasting continued demand growth through 2020 and price increases by 2019, while noting that uranium has faced negative sentiment, attributed in part to the Fukushima disaster. The passage also discusses seasonal patterns for uranium-related ETFs and provides technical analysis of URA, including potential support levels and conditions under which prices might rebound or face further correction.

The respondent determined gift tax and estate tax deficiencies against the Estate of Elizabeth C. Dillingham for transfers made by checks. The remaining issue is whether a noncharitable gift made by check is complete for federal gift and estate tax purposes upon delivery of the check to the donee. The decedent delivered six $3,000 checks to six individuals on about December 24, 1980; the donees presented them and the checks were paid on about January 28, 1981. Additional $3,000 checks were delivered and paid on about January 28, 1981. The court held that petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery of the checks in 1980, so the “relation back doctrine” does not apply. Relying on Oklahoma law regarding when a check becomes effective and the donor’s ability to stop payment, the court held that the decedent parted with dominion and control over the funds represented by the checks when the checks were paid by her bank during 1981, making the transfers complete at that time.

The passage is a farewell message in which the speaker says he will leave office in three days after decades of service and expresses good wishes to the new President and Congress. He describes generally cooperative relations with Congress over the past eight years and argues that U.S. leadership and prestige depend not only on material and military strength, but on using power for world peace and human betterment. He states that America’s aims in free government are to keep the peace, foster progress in human achievement, and enhance liberty, dignity, and integrity, while warning that a global hostile ideology threatens these goals and requires a prolonged commitment. He emphasizes the need for balance among national programs, and warns that increasing military establishment and a permanent arms industry create a risk of unwarranted influence by a “military-industrial complex,” potentially endangering liberties and democratic processes. He also discusses technological change in research, noting the growing role of the federal government and the danger of either domination of scholars or public policy being captured by a scientific-technological elite. He stresses that the future requires avoiding exploitation of tomorrow’s resources, and calls for a world based on mutual trust and respect, continuing disarmament with honor and confidence, and resolving differences with intellect rather than arms. He concludes by expressing disappointment that lasting peace is not in sight, noting that war has been avoided so far, and offering a prayer for peace, human needs, freedom, charity, and the elimination of poverty, disease, and ignorance.

The passage promotes discounted toys available before Amazon Prime Day ends, suggesting these items as gifts for children or for oneself. It highlights several specific deals and toys, including Squishmallows plushes (such as a 20-inch Diane Peach Bigfoot and other smaller plushes), Magna-Tiles building kits discounted from $50 to $35, a Lego fall-toned set that is now retired and available only via third-party merchants, Play-Doh, a kid-friendly spooky build with a skeleton minifigure, a blind-box toy suggestion, and additional items like a wooden ice cream counter, a Crayola Color Wonder magic light brush station, and a National Geographic rock tumbler kit. It also notes that featured products are independently selected by WIRED editors, which may receive compensation from retailers or purchases through links.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture and related technologies. It explains fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern, which compresses weights and can double Tensor Core math throughput with little to no impact on inferencing accuracy. It also discusses DLSS, which uses Tensor Cores and a deep neural network to construct high-quality images comparable to native resolution with higher performance, and its enhancement on Ampere GPUs for feasible 8K gaming at 60 fps. The text outlines the GA10x GPU memory subsystem using GDDR6X, including PAM4 signaling to achieve high bandwidth, and mentions improvements for ray traversal and overall bandwidth. For I/O bottlenecks, it presents NVIDIA RTX IO, which works with DirectStorage to enable GPU-based lossless decompression and rapid loading/streaming of assets, reducing CPU workload and improving frame rates and load times. It further covers data center GPUs (such as NVIDIA A40) and display capabilities of Ampere GPUs (DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1), plus fifth-generation NVDEC hardware video decoding (including AV1) and seventh-generation NVENC hardware video encoding. The passage concludes with additional specifications for GPUs and legal/qualification statements about information accuracy and warranties.

The passage describes how methane (CH4) gas bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments form from microbial decomposition of organic matter and grow from below the pore scale to larger, isolated disc-shaped cavities. It states that bubble growth and rise in consolidated fine-grained muds are governed by coupled mechanical and biogeochemical processes that can be modeled using Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM), treating consolidated soft clay as a single-phase medium with negligible pore pressure effects. The model uses a two-stage bubble growth process (elastic cavity expansion followed by localized fracturing) driven by high capillary-entry pressure, and characterizes large bubbles as Mode I (tensile) gas-filled cracks that LEFM can predict in shape, size, and orientation. Method details cover a mechanical-reaction-transport FEM model in COMSOL, including solute diffusion of dissolved CH4, Henry’s law equilibrium at the bubble surface, elastic deformation under overburden loading, and LEFM-based fracture propagation using stress intensity factors and a strain energy density criterion. The numerical approach uses refined meshing near the bubble and validated analytical comparisons for mature elliptical bubbles, showing good agreement across varying fracture toughness. The passage notes limitations: the model applies to individual bubbles and lacks a comprehensive theory for upscaling bubble characteristics to effective properties for remote sensing, so it is intended as a foundation for developing upscaling methods.

The passage describes a study on cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM), a vascular malformation diagnosed with MRI, where intracerebral hemorrhage and seizures are major manifestations. It outlines genetic and immune/inflammatory factors potentially linked to CCM aggression, focusing on SNPs in FCGR2A (rs1801274) and PTPN2 and variants in VDR (rs7975232, rs731236, rs11568820). The study used a single-site prospective observational cohort design with blood sampling from October 2017 to March 2023, assessment of symptomatic versus asymptomatic presentations, genotyping by TaqMan assays, and plasma cytokine measurement using a 18-cytokine/chemokine Luminex immunoassay. Results reported that PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC were more frequent in asymptomatic patients, with associated cytokine changes (including IL-10, IL-18, IFN-γ, IL-27, and IL-23). A weighted diagnostic biomarker combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC and GM-CSF was reported to distinguish symptomatic from asymptomatic patients, and FCGR2Ars1801274 GG was reported to predict symptomatic events during follow-up. VDRrs731236 AA and VDRrs11568820 CC were also associated with time to first symptomatic event, and the study concludes these genetic factors may influence CCM development and progression.

The passage reviews how effective teaching involves observing student learning behaviors, diagnosing learning problems, and designing teaching activities accordingly. It describes a teacher education approach using collaborative inquiry and panoramic cameras to collect evidence of young students’ learning performances for observation and post-lesson discussions, followed by reflection and adjustment of instructional plans. A teacher education course (“Professional Teaching Practicum”) was implemented from September 2022 to January 2023 with 22 prospective teachers, including training on collaborative inquiry and panoramic camera use. The study used an observation record form and a questionnaire to assess diagnostic and instructional design capabilities. Results across four observation-report cycles showed an improving trend in diagnostic capabilities, while pre- and post-test questionnaire results indicated statistically significant increases in perceived capabilities related to lesson preparation, linking observations to learning, and adjusting plans after discussions. The study concludes the course framework is feasible and improved prospective teachers’ diagnostic abilities and perceived instructional design capabilities, while noting that further research is needed to determine the effectiveness of the instructional strategies they propose.

Amazon received a patent for “directed fragmentation for unmanned airborne vehicles” to address delivery-drone problems such as unsuitable weather, equipment malfunctions, and other disruptions. The patent describes a fragmentation sequence the drone would update based on flight path, conditions, and terrain topology to choose preferred drop locations, including natural and built features. It would release one or more drone components so the drone’s weight, speed, air drag, momentum, and trajectory change, allowing controlled descent into calculated trajectories toward selected locations (illustrated with a pond and a tree). The patent also mentions possible release methods such as latches, hooks, springs, small explosive charges, or compressed gas, and selecting the order of release based on factors like component cost, drag coefficients, weight, and purpose. The passage notes that patenting does not guarantee use and highlights concern about catastrophic failure of delivery drones.

The passage describes a congressional assembly after sixty years, presenting the United States as having maintained a stable, permanent government and peace with other nations. It reports foreign relations and specific diplomatic actions, including adjustments with Great Britain, the resolution of an interruption with France, and steps taken to preserve neutrality in a German Empire-related matter and suppress a foreign expedition against Cuba. It discusses international relations with multiple countries, efforts to address U.S. claims (including with Portugal and Mexico), and the management of diplomatic missions, including changes regarding German states. It recommends actions on the African slave trade, infrastructure and transit routes (including a proposed canal in Nicaragua and possible routes across Panama and Tehuantepec), and fostering relations with American states. It provides financial figures and estimates a probable budget deficit, recommending borrowing authority, tariff revisions, and an agricultural bureau. It covers plans for California and New Mexico’s admission, revenue and postal policy, census preparation, domestic administrative issues, and constitutional views on the separation of powers and preserving the Union.

The passage describes how social media platforms strengthen policies and use AI to detect hate speech, extremism, fake news, and other community-violating content, often by improving algorithms and adding staff. It notes that AI can recognize offensive language and images but varies in accuracy and can fail, such as Google Photos mislabeling images of dark-skinned people and Twitter’s outdated algorithm missing context for certain terms. The passage also says AI can be biased because it is trained on human-tagged data, and that bias can spread when training data is shared. It emphasizes AI’s inability to determine intent, citing examples where platforms removed or flagged content incorrectly (including swastika-related and historic images). Despite limitations, AI is described as helping humans by flagging and prioritizing posts for review, increasing review staffing (e.g., Facebook) and enabling faster responses. The passage concludes that ethics and laws may lag behind the speed of AI and moderation technology.

Lobbyists for Connecticut towns and cities asked Gov. Dannel P. Malloy to help them cope with the state’s financial crisis by reducing administrative burdens, allowing local cost-control reforms, and making changes to municipal retirement and collective bargaining arbitration. They also requested keeping a higher percentage of land-transfer fees and easing regulations to reduce local expenses. Malloy said the budget stalemate created statewide uncertainty and described the meeting with CCM and COST as productive. CCM and COST leaders cited concerns about reduced state aid, while Senate President Pro Tempore Martin M. Looney said their claim that they were not seeking “held harmless” treatment was misleading. The group also discussed relief from costly mandates such as binding arbitration, adjusting the prevailing wage threshold (unchanged since 1991), and changing municipal retirement system employee contribution requirements (not adjusted since 1947), which they said affect consolidation.

The passage explains how to obtain SanDisk warranty service by contacting SanDisk or emailing support@SanDisk.com, returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging with freight prepaid, and obtaining a tracking confirmation number. SanDisk may repair or replace the product (with new or refurbished equal or greater capacity/functionality) or refund the purchase price; the warranty on replaced product lasts only for the remaining time on the original warranty. It states SanDisk’s liability is limited to the amount paid and excludes direct, indirect, or consequential damages, including lost data. It also disclaims other warranties and limits implied warranties to the express warranty duration. The passage includes an end user license agreement requiring users to read and agree to terms before downloading or using software, outlines software licensing and restrictions (including no reverse engineering and limits on copying/modification), and provides disclaimers of software warranties and limitations of liability. It further includes general contract terms such as California law, venue in Santa Clara County, restrictions on export, and that certain sections survive termination.

The passage describes a continuation patent application related to digitally planning and manufacturing orthodontic appliances. It explains that orthodontic treatment planning and aligner fabrication involve measuring a patient’s tooth positions and receiving tooth movement constraints, then measuring elements of malocclusion and generating multiple treatment plans. Interim final and final tooth positions are computed through stages that may include measuring and correcting malocclusion elements such as bi-protrusion, molar class occlusion, canine class occlusion, overjet, and potential interproximal reduction or extraction scenarios. After selecting a treatment plan, the method generates appliance models for each stage and outputs instructions to fabricate appliances, including embodiments that involve fabricating one or more stages from the instructions. The passage also describes a system performing these steps using a processor and memory, and provides additional detail on orthodontic appliances, including tooth repositioning appliance structures, appliance sets and staging, and various direct and indirect fabrication approaches. It further outlines computer-based treatment planning and appliance design workflows using measured patient data, digital models, movement paths, force system determination, simulation, and fabrication instruction generation.

The passage is part of Tesla, Inc.’s Quarterly Report on Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018. It includes forward-looking statements, an index of sections, and unaudited consolidated financial statements. Key financial data shown include consolidated balance sheets (total assets of $29,262,713 thousand at September 30, 2018), consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income (net income attributable to common stockholders of $311,516 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2018), and consolidated statements of cash flows (net cash provided by operating activities of $863,241 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2018). Notes describe Tesla’s business segments (automotive and energy generation and storage), significant accounting policies, and the adoption of new revenue standards, including impacts on revenues and balance sheet line items. Additional notes cover topics such as fair value measurements, inventory, property and equipment, warranties, restricted cash, customer deposits, and detailed debt and convertible note information.

The passage lists multiple hardware/software issues for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, including failures or hangs during DMA cycles, incorrect I/O behavior at high addresses, interrupt handling problems, UART/USB/IDE/ACPI-related faults, and issues with timing, alignment, CRC corruption, and clock gating. It also includes detailed entries about PIT operation deviations, a debug port that hangs, incorrect PIT count mode behavior, XPIC interrupt acknowledge clearing delays causing extra interrupts, DMA rotating priority not always rotating as expected, and thermal alarm handling in Faulted Standby with limited recovery until exiting Standby. It further describes a Sleep Clock control side effect: Sleep Clock use is optional but if other Sleep Clock-related options are desired, the Sleep Clock option must be enabled; otherwise operation may not be as expected.
