Patients with hematological malignancies and SARS-CoV-2 infection have high COVID-19 mortality, with immunosuppression potentially prolonging viral shedding and limiting vaccine responses, especially in B-cell lymphoid disease. The study describes a France-based monitored access program using early transfusion of high-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP), targeting viral replication and clearance. Although randomized trials showed limited benefit of CCP in the general population, the authors report outcomes from a CCP cohort of 112 patients with hematological malignancies and COVID-19 and a nested propensity score comparison in B-cell neoplasm patients. CCP transfusion was associated with reduced temperature and inflammatory markers (CRP, ferritin, fibrinogen) and increased PCR cycle threshold values, and 90-day overall survival was 64.9% overall and 77.5% in patients with B-lymphoid neoplasms. In multivariable analysis, age, high blood pressure, and COVID-19 severity were associated with lower survival, while prior anti-CD20/CD19 mAbs were associated with better survival. In propensity score-weighted analyses of anti-CD20–pre-exposed B-cell lymphoid patients alive 16 days after hospitalization, CCP exposure was associated with decreased risk of death, with reported estimates showing 63% reduction in the main analysis. The authors conclude CCP may be particularly relevant for patients with B-cell lymphoid malignancies pre-treated with anti-CD20 due to poor vaccine response and possible humoral escape, while noting that randomized prospective confirmation is needed.

Apple Inc. reported that on September 12, 2017 it consummated the issuance and sale of $1.0 billion 1.500% Notes due 2019, $1.0 billion 2.100% Notes due 2022, $2.0 billion 2.900% Notes due 2027, and $1.0 billion 3.750% Notes due 2047, totaling the “Notes,” under an underwriting agreement dated September 5, 2017. The Notes are issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 and an officer’s certificate dated September 12, 2017, and interest will be paid semi-annually in arrears on March 12 and September 12 beginning March 12, 2018. The Notes will mature on September 12 of their respective years, are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured and unsubordinated debt, and are subject to the terms of the underwriting agreement, indenture, and officer’s certificate. The report lists related exhibits, and it was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, on September 12, 2017.

The passage is a collection of dated news items and email header information about business and energy developments. It includes a Wall Street Journal report that Viacom will not split off Blockbuster due to Blockbuster’s turnaround, alongside details on Blockbuster’s financial performance and market share. Other articles cover federal oversight and deregulation of energy markets in the U.S., including Bush’s appointment of commissioners to monitor electricity markets and Enron-related comments on Texas and California power and rate increases. Multiple reports describe Enron’s international activities, including plans with Japanese and Dubai-related gas power initiatives, as well as Enron’s Japan power-plant proposal and a wind power expansion in India. Additional items discuss policy and financial concerns in India, withdrawals and bidding for an Indian thermal power project, and a U.K. electricity trading system expected to affect generators differently.

Diana Containerships Inc. (NASDAQ:DCIX) reported quarterly results, with EPS of ($0.66) versus a consensus ($0.77), and revenue of $5.40 million versus a consensus $7.50 million. The quarter included a 63.8% year-over-year revenue decline, with negative return on equity of 11.99% and a negative net margin of 350.33%. The stock opened at 2.71, with moving averages of $2.84 (50 day) and $3.29 (200 day), and a 52-week range of $2.00 to $26.17; market cap was $24.82 million. Renaissance Technologies LLC increased its stake by 94.4% in the fourth quarter, ending with 231,485 shares and about 2.53% ownership worth $644,000. Zacks Investment Research upgraded the stock from “sell” to “hold.”

The passage describes Tampa Bay Lightning staff and players discussing their approach to building and succeeding as a long-term team. They say there was no timeline for certain drafting/free-agency plans and emphasize patience, keeping draft picks, and developing players through the team’s scouting and player development systems. It highlights the importance of home-grown talent and assets for sustained success, crediting personnel such as amateur scouting and player development staff for finding and nurturing players. Coaches and executives discuss how leadership and team attitude helped them respond to adversity in playoffs, with Steven Stamkos evolving as a leader by accepting different roles and encouraging other players to step up. The passage also covers what makes a successful program for recruiting players and notes that success is tied to a team environment, character, and readiness to perform in playoff situations.

The Bittle tree on Roanoke’s Turbyfill Quad was planted by Dr. David Bittle and stood for over 100 years until it was removed due to lightning strikes and wind damage. Its wood was later used to create the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for Antrim Chapel in time for Roanoke’s 175th anniversary. Reverend Chris Bowen, inspired by a symbolic theme of trees found in biblical literature and the College community, enlisted George Arthur to build a cross 4’8″ wide and 7’6″ tall featuring rooted branches extending upward. Bowen described the symbolism as reflecting deep roots and future growth for the College and its students.

Two women, May Baxter-Thornton from Newport and Emma Lewis from Swansea, have been appointed to the victims and survivors panel of the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (IICSA). Both have experienced child sexual abuse and will advise the inquiry on how to reach and listen to victims and survivors in Wales. IICSA chair Professor Alexis Jay said their Welsh perspective will contribute to the panel’s work. Baxter-Thornton, abused as a child in the late 1970s and early 1980s, has worked with victims and survivors for 16 years, and said Welsh victims’ voices must be heard in the inquiry’s recommendations. Lewis, taken into care at 10 and disclosing abuse at 12, supports young people transitioning from care and said she wants to help ensure children in Wales are better protected in the future. The inquiry opened in Wales in November 2016 and has met with victims, survivors, and experts in several Welsh locations.

The Louisiana Supreme Court granted Robert Daniel Chappuis’s application for a writ of review regarding his case against Sears Roebuck & Co. The court ordered that the writ of review issue, the Court of Appeal send up the case record in duplicate, and that both plaintiff and defendant’s counsel be notified.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) is used for transporting vapor and liquid objects such as petroleum and gas, including pipes for high and low pressure. Welded pipe is described as ordinary submerged arc welded steel pipe, with notation SC for thicker water and gas pipe and T for relatively thin line pipe wire and tube used for threading. ERW tube uses a high-frequency resistance welded steel pipe process that welds from a steel strip base material; it has high production efficiency, low cost, material saving, and easy self-adaptation, and is widely used in industries including aviation, energy, electricity, automobiles, and light industry. The passage also states that ERW steel pipe differs from seamless steel pipe and that ERW steel pipe production focuses on improved seaming, burr removal (controlled around 0.2–0.5 mm), evenly controlled wall thickness (±0.2 mm), and ends trimmed to fit standards such as American API or GB/T9711.1. It notes that ERW steel pipe has been widely used as the main steel pipe for urban gas network engineering.

The passage describes consumer media playback technologies related to identifying audio content during playback. It states the application is a continuation of several prior U.S. patent applications and incorporates their contents by reference. It discusses an overview in which a playback device can use digital audio data to send portions to an identification system, receive audio-related information from the system, forward that information to a control device, and play the audio via wired-connected speakers. It also describes roles of control devices, which can command playback devices to retrieve identification information and then display received information or metadata. The passage further outlines an example media playback environment with rooms, playback devices, control devices, and a network, including concepts like synchronized multi-room playback, bonded/consolidated playback devices, playback zones, and controller user-interface elements. Example methods are provided for receiving digital audio, sending selected portions (potentially based on detected discontinuities, periodic sampling, decoding, sample-rate conversion, dynamic extraction from different audio pipeline positions, or frequency segregation) to the identification system, and displaying retrieved metadata.

The passage criticizes Rep. Ken Buck’s claim that health care is a “commodity,” arguing that treating health care this way undermines the right to life and serves corporate profit rather than health. It advocates “Medicare for all,” saying it aims to provide care instead of making profit and would reduce costs compared to private insurance. The passage also comments on a Tribune headline about Denver paying nearly $1 million to a teen’s family, expressing sympathy while arguing the teen was driving a stolen car and that crime should not be treated as profitable. It concludes by defending police and stating police are not the enemy.

The passage describes technologies for large-area illumination of light modulation devices, particularly directional and imaging directional backlights for 2D, 3D, and autostereoscopic displays. It discusses problems with spatially multiplexed autostereoscopic displays, such as reduced resolution, non-uniform viewing windows due to pixel gaps, and flicker and cross talk that limit observer freedom. 

The disclosure introduces directional illumination apparatuses that use an imaging directional backlight with a waveguide, and a transmissive spatial light modulator with input/output polarizers, optionally including additional polarizers and retarders (including switchable liquid crystal retarders). These configurations aim to reduce visibility to a snooper (privacy) while maintaining luminance for the primary user, controlling viewing angles and privacy luminance regions, and enabling wide-angle and privacy modes. A control system can regulate light sources, timing (including temporally multiplexed images), and applied voltages to switchable retarders to tune privacy characteristics. 

Waveguide-based embodiments include stepped waveguides/optical valves that guide light with first and second guiding surfaces and reflective ends, using light extraction features to direct light into optical viewing windows in dependence on input positions. The passage further contrasts imaging directional backlights (which form viewing windows) with conventional non-imaging backlights (which do not form windows), and describes directional display systems that can support observer tracking, multi-viewer operation, privacy display, and automotive use.

In the U.S., presidential elections occur every four years and are linked to stock market performance through a “4-year presidential election cycle” theory. The theory says historical data show the stock market’s performance in a president’s first two years tends to outperform its performance in the last two years, with midterm election years showing poor performance until the 4th quarter. Yale Hirsch, associated with *Stock Trader’s Almanac*, is credited with quantifying and formulating this presidential cycle idea, describing that results are relatively steady regardless of presidential political leanings. Related findings also note the year before presidential elections tends to be weaker for stocks and bonds, while stocks may do better after midterms than in other years. The passage further says election-related uncertainty can increase volatility, and that policy impacts may be sector-specific (e.g., healthcare and energy) depending on legislative control, and investors should consider rebalancing and the broader policy effects on domestic and global economies.

The passage describes Intel’s Management Engine (ME), a microcontroller in many modern Intel CPUs that is always on and connected to components such as the network interface and storage. It explains that researchers Mark Ermolov and Max Goryachy presented an exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on the Intel ME, but only as a local attack requiring physical access. The passage also says the ME runs Minix and that Intel previously used closed-source implementation, limiting understanding of its security and potential holes. It reports that arbitrary code execution can be achieved with a USB stick and discusses mitigation efforts: some vendors (e.g., System76 and Dell) offer firmware updates or laptop configurations that disable the ME, while individual users can use Intel’s detection tool and vendor-specific methods to disable it. It states there is no universal way to turn off the ME, and that removing valid ME firmware causes the computer to shut off after thirty minutes. It mentions the me_cleaner tool, which tricks the ME into thinking it has valid firmware while preventing it from functioning fully. The passage concludes by framing the most severe potential threat as a future network-based exploit, and emphasizes the importance of security and auditing code.

A Deloitte study says consumers are increasingly confident in autonomous, driverless cars despite safety concerns, with 49% of respondents believing self-driving cars will not be safe versus 73% the prior year. The study attributes growing positivity to trust in the companies developing the technology, with 53% having more confidence due to the brands building the vehicles. Trust differs between manufacturers, as 51% would trust traditional car manufacturers versus 21% trusting technology companies. While respondents generally prefer engine-powered vehicles over electric, they cite concerns about driving range (26%), vehicle price (24%), and charging infrastructure (22%), though 37% say lower ongoing costs would encourage electric purchases. Customer service and dealer experience were also rated important. The passage notes the UK government is still conducting an inquiry into autonomous vehicle safety ahead of a planned rollout.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening legal protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing families’ input in care. The bill was proposed after Stephen Komninos, who died in a Haddonfield group home in 2007, with family members alleging neglect. The measure allows state inspectors to conduct unannounced visits twice a year, authorizes the Department of Human Services to hire additional staff, requires agencies and group home operators to notify parents or guardians within two to eight hours if a patient is injured, and mandates meetings with families at least twice a year. Christie said the law is not meant to indict caregivers and is intended to ensure appropriate care.

The passage discusses Mortimer J. Adler’s influence on education, focusing on perennialism and its emphasis on eternal values, curriculum development, educational management, and the role of learners’ capabilities. It connects Adler’s ideas to Christian education and global education, and contrasts or relates humanism, posthumanist theory, and technology’s impact on human identity and social interaction, including questions about AI, robots, and emotions. The study described uses a qualitative literature review with primary sources from Adler’s books and secondary sources from recent international journals. It summarizes findings on Adler’s perennialism, docility and obedience as postponement of judgment, and education management in global Christian contexts. The conclusion argues for a just society achieved by empowering women and avoiding education goals that push children to become like adults through job-focused outcomes, and it emphasizes skepticism and intellectual enlightenment within obedience while placing perennial values above instant achievement.

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Cleveland Browns will not rule out taking Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield with the No. 1 pick in Thursday’s NFL draft. Browns general manager John Dorsey said he remains open to “all options” with the No. 1 and No. 4 picks and evaluates quarterbacks on whether they win, as well as accuracy, arm strength, red-zone performance, and driving the ball. Head coach Hue Jackson said last Tuesday that Darnold, Allen, Mayfield, and UCLA’s Josh Rosen remain in play. Most have viewed Sam Darnold as the favorite for No. 1, though Josh Allen has gained steam, and Mayfield is described as having at least been in the conversation. Mayfield won the 2017 Heisman Trophy and threw for 4,627 yards and 43 touchdown passes in his senior season, leading Oklahoma to a Big 12 title and a College Football Playoff appearance.

Jefferies Group LLC raised its price target for Ferguson Plc (LON:FERG) from GBX 5,170 ($68.58) to GBX 5,240 ($69.51) and maintained a hold rating. The passage is a VentureWire “People” newsletter dated May 30, 2001, listing high-tech management news and executive changes. Nicola Sturgeon said the Conservatives would use the snap general election on 8 June to move the UK to the right, force through a hard Brexit, and impose deeper cuts. She called the announcement by Theresa May an extraordinary U-turn and a huge political miscalculation, saying May was putting her party’s interests ahead of the country and seeking to capitalize on Labour’s “utter disarray.” Sturgeon argued the election should protect Scotland from a Tory government, said it would allow people to reject the Tories’ agenda, and referenced an existing democratic mandate for Scotland to choose its future. The passage also notes a conflict between May and the SNP over a second independence referendum, with SNP leaders insisting another vote should occur between autumn 2018 and spring 2019 while May said it is “now is not the time.” Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson said her party would promote strong leadership for getting a best Brexit deal and oppose SNP’s plan for another referendum.

The passage describes features and subsystems of MSPM0C1105/MPM0C1106 microcontrollers. It covers the CPU (Arm Cortex-M0+, pre-fetch/cache, SysTick timer, NVIC interrupt controller), five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with decreasing power and wake sources, and power domains (PD1 and PD0) including what is powered in each mode. It also outlines the PMU and clock module (LFOSC, SYSOSC, external oscillators, and various distributed clocks), DMA_B and event manager behavior, and supporting modules such as NVM flash and SRAM behavior, GPIO and IOMUX, ADC and temperature sensor, LFSS with RTC and IWDT, VREF, COMP, security/CRC, UART/I2C/SPI, watchdog timers, timers (TIMx), and aspects of debug support (SWD via DEBUGSS). Additional sections include device factory constants, typical application schematic recommendations, and general documentation/tools and disclaimers.

Lawyers for Venezuelan citizens in the U.S. under the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program asked the Supreme Court not to let the Trump administration end their protected status. They asked the Court to leave in place a San Francisco federal judge’s order temporarily barring the administration from ending their TPS protection. The filing argues the judge’s order restored the status quo and that disturbing it would cause “massive injuries,” including to American children. 

The TPS program, created by Congress in 1990, allows the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate countries whose citizens may remain and work in the U.S. when they cannot return due to extraordinary and temporary conditions. Venezuela was designated in 2021 and redesignated in 2023, with an extension announced to run through October 2026. After the Trump administration took office, the new DHS secretary ended the 2023 designation and the 2025 extension. A federal judge later found the terminations unlawful and, after further appellate activity, the challengers argued the Supreme Court’s prior limited stay did not prevent continued litigation toward final judgment.

Ed Sachse, who began a window-washing business as a teenager in Detroit, later became president of property services for Kennedy Wilson, overseeing brokers and 21 million square feet of properties across the U.S. He learned early that winter window-washing required working quickly to prevent freezing, and he expanded by contacting potential customers. At Michigan State University he studied accounting, worked for Arthur Andersen, then moved to Los Angeles for accounting work with Douglas Emmett Inc. and advanced to chief financial officer at Camden Financial. After wanting to learn the city and do deals, he became a broker at Coldwell Banker (now CBRE Group), helped sell an empty school for Rabbi Marvin Hier’s organization, and then started his own property management and brokerage company in 1993. He was diagnosed in 2001 with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma and continued running his business during treatment, including a bone marrow transplant and two stem cell transplants. During the Great Recession, he focused on contacting potential clients and eventually sold his company to Kennedy Wilson in late 2009. Sachse and his wife Julie live in Pacific Palisades, and he plays rock-and-roll guitar and occasionally performs with friends in a garage band.

President Rutherford B. Hayes issues a proclamation stating that, under the Constitution, the United States protects states against domestic violence upon application. He says domestic violence exists in West Virginia at Martinsburg and other points along the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad that state authorities cannot suppress. He warns that, where insurrection or obstruction requires it, he will command insurgents to disperse. The proclamation admonishes citizens and others against aiding unlawful proceedings and warns persons involved in domestic violence and obstruction to disperse and retire peaceably by 12:00 noon on July 19, 1877. It is signed in Washington on July 18, 1877, and sealed, with F. W. Seward listed as Acting Secretary of State.

Magid Magid, Sheffield’s Lord Mayor, branded US President Donald Trump a “wasteman” and announced he is banned from visiting Sheffield ahead of July 13. On Twitter, Magid said July 13 would be “Mexico Solidarity Day” and posted a photo wearing a sombrero and a shirt stating “Donald Trump is a wasteman.” In an interview, he said he wanted to draw attention to what he described as Trump’s “awful and disrespectful” treatment of Sheffield people and said he spoke with members of the Mexican community in Sheffield who supported the message. Magid cited reasons for calling Trump the “biggest wasteman,” including a “Muslim ban,” withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement, moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, and enforcing child imprisonment at borders, and said Trump defended white supremacist violence.

The lecture reviews major renewal theory theorems and then applies these ideas to discrete renewal processes and countable-state Markov chains. It explains that renewal analysis requires considering age and duration at a time, not only sample averages. It discusses the strong law for renewals, the elementary renewal theorem, and Blackwell’s theorem for long-term behavior of expected renewal counts, emphasizing that in arithmetic cases the expectation can have persistent “fine structure.” The lecture derives joint and marginal limiting distributions for age and duration, leading to results involving expected inter-renewal times and an additional factor related to averaging over integer versus non-integer times. It then turns to countable-state Markov chains, contrasting them with finite-state chains: in the example of a random walk driven by a Bernoulli process, state probabilities spread out and steady-state distributions may not exist. The lecture discusses recurrence versus non-recurrence using first-passage probabilities, defines recurrence in terms of return probability 1, and relates recurrent states to renewal processes with inter-renewal intervals. It further distinguishes recurrent states with finite versus infinite expected return times and connects this to whether steady-state probabilities are positive or zero.

The passage describes an optical waveguide display method and apparatus in which image-bearing light is injected into a waveguide and released for viewing. Prior waveguide displays use Bragg gratings to diffract input light into guided propagation by total internal reflection (TIR), but the acceptable input angles for TIR define a limited total field of view (TFOV). The Bragg grating is tuned for a first wavelength (e.g., green), and for longer or shorter wavelengths (e.g., red or blue) light entering near extreme TFOV angles can be diffracted to angles that do not support TIR, causing light to escape and reducing TFOV for those colors.  

To address these limitations, the invention enhances waveguide display field of view by coating the external surfaces where guided light reflects internally with a material (e.g., meta-material) having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than about 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This reduces the critical angle for TIR, allowing light from outside the previous field of view to be retained and guided. The apparatus includes first and second diffractive parts (which may be Bragg gratings) for input and output, with guided-light internal-reflection surfaces coated with the low-index material. The meta-material is described as a periodic “fish-net” or mesh nano-photonic structure whose unit cells include a magnetic resonator between conductive meshes, with structural parameters that can be optimized to achieve desired refractive index values.  

The passage also explains that conjugated input/output diffractive gratings can reduce geometric distortions and substantially negate chromatic dispersion, beneficial when using broadband sources. Figures and descriptions are provided to show TFOV expansion compared with prior designs, and additional embodiments include multi-layer slab waveguides for multi-color displays, protective coatings of meta-material and optional plastic outer layers, and optional windows or omission of meta-material over operative input/output grating regions to avoid attenuation losses.

In 2015, the author scratched their hand on a nail while repairing a garden gate, became unwell, and 24 hours later was in a coma in University Hospital Hairmyres with sepsis. Their family were told they had almost no chance of surviving the night; they woke after three months and spent another year recovering. The passage states that sepsis affects over 30 million people yearly worldwide and kills an estimated 6 million, including nearly 2 million children, and that survivors may develop post-sepsis syndrome with lasting physical and mental symptoms. It explains that sepsis can follow viral or bacterial infections, sometimes from minor injuries, and results from an uncontrolled body response leading to organ failure. It lists possible symptoms and advises calling emergency services and asking, “Could it be sepsis?” It also notes that there is no specific cure for sepsis, only symptom treatment, while mentioning research on metformin and gene therapy. The passage emphasizes that awareness is currently low globally and highlights efforts to improve recognition and establish protocols such as Sepsis6.

The passage describes how intelligent education systems using AIED collect student learning data and support personalized learning, including scientific experiments via virtual environments (VR/AR) and classroom or online platforms. It focuses on privacy concerns in AIED, where data anonymization/de-identification is used, but face anonymization is a key challenge. In scientific experiment video, faces may be occluded by hands and instruments, requiring a balance between anonymizing facial identity for privacy and keeping instruments and students’ operational techniques clearly visible for assessment. The authors propose a real-time face anonymization system using an improved YOLOv8 architecture (MSFF-YOLOv8) with a contour-based training data preprocessing method called Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR) to reduce mis-blurring of instruments and edge errors. They introduce two evaluation metrics, SOBA (Sensitivity of Blur Accuracy) and OBR/OBR (Over Blur Rate), and create a dataset of 51 annotated experiment videos (1049 frames extracted). Experiments comparing MSFF-YOLOv8 (with and without CAOR) against YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM report that MSFF-YOLOv8 achieves real-time performance (up to 22.67 fps at 1080p) and high accuracy (up to 96.02%), while preserving experimental details. The conclusion states the system achieves face anonymization with preserved apparatus visibility and notes future work to improve precise edge classification during real-time inference.

Sam Altman said intellectual property is more complicated for AI video than for still images because video feels “more real and lifelike,” creating stronger emotional resonance. He said rights holders respond differently to AI video and generally want more restrictions and guardrails, though some are enthusiastic about using their content. Altman also referenced plans to give rights holders more granular control in OpenAI’s Sora app. After Sora launched, videos using the app went viral, including examples featuring SpongeBob and Pikachu, and a Business Insider attempt to generate an authorized-feeling SpongeBob and Pikachu video was blocked for violating guardrails about similarity to third-party content. Altman predicted that companies’ reluctance may shift as demand and rules develop.

The passage compares Stanley Furniture (STLY) and La-Z-Boy (LZB) across dividend strength, risk, valuation, earnings, analyst recommendations, institutional ownership, and profitability. La-Z-Boy has a consensus target price of $30.33 and is rated more favorably by analysts. Institutional ownership is higher for La-Z-Boy (86.8%) than for Stanley Furniture (29.7%), while insider ownership is lower for La-Z-Boy (3.2%) than for Stanley Furniture (28.6%). La-Z-Boy reports higher revenue and earnings than Stanley Furniture, and Stanley Furniture has a lower price-to-earnings ratio. Profitability metrics are better for La-Z-Boy, with positive net margins, higher returns on equity and assets, while Stanley Furniture has negative profitability. La-Z-Boy pays an annual dividend of $0.44 per share (1.6% yield) and distributes 25.9% of its earnings as dividends; Stanley Furniture does not pay a dividend. Both stocks are less volatile than the S&P 500, with beta values of 0.34 for Stanley Furniture and 0.89 for La-Z-Boy. The summary states La-Z-Boy beats Stanley Furniture on 12 of 14 factors.

The passage discusses scientific progress toward understanding and manipulating human memories. It says researchers may be able to pinpoint where memories are stored by combining methods such as “face cells,” CREB protein activity during learning, and activating neuron groups before learning. It also describes memory reconsolidation during recall and refers to MIT studies by Dr. Susumu Tonegawa showing artificial links between harmless and scary situations, reversing negative reactions into positive ones, and the possibility of implanting and erasing memories.

The passage discusses a team’s excitement about earning the chance to play for the Stanley Cup, emphasizing they were not given anything and had to beat three good hockey teams to reach this point. It says the team’s focus is on playing physical hockey, with big forwards who skate well to forecheck and deliver punishing hits, which the speaker attributes to the team’s success. The passage also mentions relaxing during a long layoff, staying focused as the team reaches Dallas and preparing for the game, and using recent adversity and experience to remain calm and avoid being more nervous than in a prior series, with the goal of responding well again.

The passage argues that a trade deficit can reduce demand in the United States by redirecting spending to other countries, potentially lowering demand and increasing unemployment, though it can be offset by increased U.S. demand and supported by large budget deficits and asset bubbles. It also challenges the claim that the dollar’s role as a reserve currency forces large trade deficits, noting that other reserve currencies are held by countries and that reserve holdings are a deliberate policy used by countries like China and South Korea to maintain the dollar’s value against their currency. The passage then criticizes Samuelson’s complaint about China’s development policy, arguing that it is unclear whether U.S. companies are coerced to transfer technology and claiming that firms such as Boeing and Apple chose to invest in China despite technology-transfer conditions. It further states that Samuelson’s account is dubious regarding China producing better and cheaper goods using technology developed by U.S. corporations.

The passage describes an RSI mean-reversion trading strategy for QQQ using RSI(2), which requires a low RSI reading below 30 to enter a position. It tests an RSI(2)-based strategy on QQQ by entering when RSI(2) is below a threshold and exiting when today’s close is higher than yesterday’s high. The RSI 2 strategy outperformed buy and hold (10.01% vs. 6.39%) and performed well in four bear markets (2000–2002, 2008/09, 2018, and March 2020). It also notes that tightening the entry to RSI(2) below 5 reduced time in the market and total return, and that adding a second indicator while keeping RSI(2) below 10 improved results. With the added indicator, reported metrics include CAGR 12.7% (vs. 9% buy and hold), time in market 14%, 232 trades with 75% winners, max drawdown 19.5%, profit factor 3, and Sharpe ratio 2.85.

The passage describes the SD Memory Card as a security-focused memory card for audio and video consumer electronics, offering higher capacity and faster performance. It includes a content protection mechanism compliant with the SDMI standard, using mutual authentication and a “new cipher algorithm” to prevent illegal use, and also provides non-secure access to the user’s content. It may support a second security system based on standards such as ISO-7816 for interfacing with public networks and systems for mobile e-commerce and digital signatures. The passage also covers the SDIO (SD I/O) Card, defined separately by the SD Association, which provides high-speed, low-power I/O for mobile devices and is compatible with SD Memory cards mechanically, electrically, power, signalling, and software-wise, with added detection extensions for SDIO-aware hosts. It notes that SD Memory Card communication uses an advanced 9-pin interface with operation up to 208 MHz in a low-voltage range, and that the protocol is part of the specification.

The Irish Times reports that JD Wetherspoon’s in Dublin city centre will occupy a 1,600 sq metre space made up of two connected buildings on Lower Abbey Street, using the former Trustee Savings Bank at 12B and the former 1839 Baptist Chapel at 12C. A court decision allows the buildings to be linked by a glazed connection, and the Circuit Licensing Court has granted the company a full drinks and restaurant license, subject to planning permission. Wetherspoon’s currently has six gastropubs in Dublin, Dún Laoghaire and Cork, with other locations mentioned, including one set to open on Camden Street in 2019. The passage also describes Wetherspoon’s reputation for cheap drink and food deals and quotes a spokesperson saying prices have increased, including changes to draught ales, beers, spirits, and gin.

The lecture introduces auctions as a way firms and governments set prices, highlighting applications such as government procurement, Treasury bill auctions, and online advertising. It develops auction analysis primarily using the independent private values model and focuses on sealed-bid second-price and first-price auctions. In the second-price auction, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy, and the lecture derives expected seller revenue using order statistics. It then contrasts practical formats like ascending oral auctions and “button” auctions, arguing they yield similar strategic behavior to second-price auctions. For first-price auctions, it explains bid shading and shows how the equilibrium bid depends on the value distribution, including a result for uniform distributions, and discusses revenue equivalence between first- and second-price auctions under stated assumptions. The lecture presents the revenue equivalence theorem in a more general framework and applies it to an all-pay auction. It then discusses limitations of the theorem in practice, including risk aversion, correlated values, independence assumptions, and restrictions on allocation. The lecture covers reserve prices in second-price auctions, concluding that setting the monopoly price as the reserve is optimal. Finally, it shifts to common-value and winner’s-curse ideas and discusses an empirical paper on offshore oil lease auctions (wildcat vs. drainage tracts), explaining how asymmetric information and winner’s curse can produce higher profits for incumbents and different bidding behavior, supported by predictions tested against auction data.

An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 people, including about half teachers, asked for feedback on draft K-12 curriculum documents. The survey summary said some respondents were confused about subject introductions and “scope and sequence” overviews, and that social studies drew more “strongly held views” than other subjects. Social studies feedback included criticisms about political correctness and “civic literacy,” support for more First Nations, Métis, and Inuit topics with concerns about losing global history and current events, and concerns about “fostering a certain world view” or concerns about applying diverse cultural perspectives and social justice across subjects. Most respondents said the draft plans would foster literacy and numeracy, enhance critical thinking, and prepare students for further studies. Alberta Teachers’ Association president Greg Jeffery said working groups were on the right track but stressed teacher preparation and pacing, noting the previous math curriculum implementation was “a disaster” due to being rushed. Education Minister David Eggen had announced a K-12 curriculum overhaul with all subjects revised at once, aiming to have the new K-4 curriculum written by December and rolling out higher grades until 2022.

High Speed (HS) mode allows codes to be read out one at a time. Because there is not enough time for a conversion to finish between a repeated START and the read-addressing byte, the ADS7828 holds SCL LOW after the read-addressing byte until the conversion completes. A typical HS read sequence (including a shift from F/S to HS mode) is referenced in Figure 4. To remain in HS mode after reading, use a repeated START instead of a STOP, since a STOP returns the part to F/S mode. Notes state that repeated START must be used to remain in HS mode, and SCLH is SCL in HS mode.

The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund is designed to let investors access both onshore (A-shares) and offshore (H-shares, Red-chips, P-chips, and ADRs, etc.) Chinese equity markets through one strategy rather than two. It uses a flexible approach to invest across A-shares and offshore equities by market capitalization, sectors, and factors, aiming to benefit from valuation differences, favorable factors across market cycles, and sector opportunities. The fund is long-only, fundamentals-driven, and concentrated, investing in 20 to 50 companies from a universe of over 3,300 onshore and 1,000 offshore stocks. It is managed by Helen Zhu, supported by 10 China-focused research analysts in Hong Kong and Shanghai. The passage also states that the fund can invest across listings in mainland China, Hong Kong, the US, or elsewhere.

The passage describes the Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) series and an electronic edition of a volume covering 1981–1988. It explains that the FRUS series is the official documentary historical record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and significant diplomatic activity, prepared by the Office of the Historian under the Foreign Service Institute. It notes regulations first promulgated by Secretary of State Frank B. Kellogg in 1925 (with later guidance) and a new statutory charter established by Public Law 102–138 in 1991, which requires a thorough, accurate, and reliable record, adherence to editing principles of objectivity and completeness, and publication within 30 years of the events. The passage also describes how the ebook edition is designed for portability, offline access, and fidelity to the printed edition, including recommendations for citing document numbers and handling page-number cross references. It states that sources used for the volume are mostly declassified and available at the National Archives and Records Administration.

The passage explains that a data-driven culture can align organizations both vertically (leadership goals matched by individuals and groups) and horizontally (teams collaborate using common data models and transparent access). It describes digital leaders’ practices, including a learning mindset, transparent data access, clear metrics, and using those metrics to align the organization, with culture coordinating day-to-day beliefs, values, and actions. The passage contrasts digital natives and successfully transformed firms with digital laggards, noting that laggards often struggle due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus, while changing mindsets and behaviors is a key transformation challenge. It states that mature firms differ in their data culture approach and highlights the importance of learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement implemented in daily practices and core beliefs. Organizations are grouped into four culture/technology patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant (over-relying on data), and companies can target actions based on their starting pattern.

The passage describes how the Covid-19 pandemic led Türkiye and many countries to shift education to emergent distance education (EDE), defined as the temporary transfer of face-to-face education to an online environment during a crisis. It explains that Turkish universities implemented EDE during and beyond the pandemic period, sometimes alongside hybrid models, and notes that the rapid transition limited training and systematic methodological planning.

The study focuses on Turkish tourist guiding education (TGE), where requirements can be met through tour guiding education by institutions or through certification programs by the Turkish Tourist Guides Association. The passage argues that EDE created dilemmas in TGE because students who expect practical, face-to-face training do not perceive distance education favorably, though they also experienced some aspects of its efficiency during Covid-19.

The main aim of the study is to examine students’ perceptions and experiences of EDE in face-to-face tour guiding departments. It uses a qualitative phenomenology design with purposive sampling of 81 students from Istanbul universities in 2022–2023 who had at least one semester of EDE experience during Covid-19. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and an online questionnaire, analyzed via thematic content analysis, resulting in eight themes and findings related to sufficiency, advantages, disadvantages, differences from face-to-face education, and perceived understanding of distance courses.

Findings reported in the passage indicate students generally viewed EDE as insufficient for TGE due to insufficient vocational courses, lack of effective communication, and motivation problems. Students identified advantages of EDE such as time management and access-related benefits, but also reported disadvantages including inappropriacy for TGE’s practical and communication-based needs, motivation and communication issues, technical problems, and low attendance. The study concludes that students prefer face-to-face TGE for efficiency, practice opportunities, and interaction, while still recognizing some benefits of distance education, leading to a dilemma in their attitudes toward EDE.

Brad Vis, who narrowly lost the Mission-Matsqui-Fraser Canyon seat to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015, has been chosen by the Conservative Party’s riding association to stand as its candidate in the next federal election. Conservative leader Andrew Scheer congratulated Vis, and the riding president said Vis brings intensity, enthusiasm, expertise, and commitment to the electoral process. The release also says the next year will involve Conservative outreach across the large riding to learn residents’ concerns, and Vis criticized Liberal government spending while expressing sympathy for seniors on fixed incomes and young families trying to buy homes.

The speaker said they felt they played well and could not control outcomes beyond trying to give their team a chance to win. They described the first goal as Friesen making a move after the speaker went down early, and said they did not see a rebound after the first shot. They stated the next game is the biggest of the year and that the team must learn from adversity, play better, use speed more, and create more traffic and shots in front of the net. They said the second period was the other team’s best, coming out “really jumping,” and that the opponent had experience and played harder. They also said they need to match the opponent’s intensity, bounce back immediately, and show up with no excuses with two weeks left in the season.

The passage discusses multilingualism and cultural awareness in Indonesian higher education, highlighting the need for multilingual language instruction in a globalized, multilingual environment. It describes the study’s background and rationale, noting that teaching multilingualism supports cross-cultural awareness and comprehension, and that few studies have examined this relationship in university classroom learning involving local languages, Indonesian, and foreign languages. The study uses an embedded mixed methods design with quantitative (survey of 388 students from multiple Indonesian universities, validity and reliability testing, Pearson correlations, and descriptive statistics) and qualitative (thematic analysis via Google Forms responses analyzed with NVivo) strands. It defines variables including Multilingualism Competency, multilingual learning process, psychological factors, social interaction, cultural knowledge and communication, cultural practices and participation, sociocultural context, and capacity and attitude toward cultural learning. Results report significant positive correlations between multilingual learning variables and cultural awareness variables. The findings emphasize that Indonesian as a dominant mother tongue and students’ learning of local and foreign languages relate to engagement with cultural practices and sociocultural contexts, and they propose strategies such as educator training, inclusive content development, technology support, intercultural collaboration, community engagement, and active participation in cultural activities. The conclusion states that integrating linguistic and cultural experiences can develop multilingual competence and deeper cultural awareness, providing implications for practitioners and policymakers.

The passage is a periodic mailing providing an update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000. It reports that many governments are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing competition in wholesale and retail markets, while some international players shift investment to less risky markets. It summarizes developments across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, including country-specific changes such as market-opening deadlines, unbundling and privatization plans, regulatory measures, mergers and trading arrangements, and ongoing challenges like financial constraints, currency impacts, drought-related power shortages, and issues affecting IPPs and power purchase agreements. The mailing also notes attached exhibits and offers contacts for additional regional information.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. It includes corporate information, securities details, and an index of the report’s sections. In Part I, it describes Amazon’s business, including customer segments (consumers, sellers, developers and enterprises via AWS, and content creators) and products/services such as retail offerings, electronic devices, Amazon Prime, and AWS. It also outlines competition and intellectual property approach, and discusses seasonality and employee information. Item 1A presents extensive risk factors, including intense competition, strains from expansion, risks from new products and international operations (including PRC and India regulatory structures), fulfillment and data center optimization risks, system and data security risks, inventory and seasonality risks, intellectual property risks, stock price volatility, regulatory risks, taxes, supplier and government contract risks, product liability, and payment-related risks. The passage describes how a trusting agent analyzes risk before interacting with a probable trusted agent in a digital business ecosystem. Risk is defined in terms of the variance of possible outcomes and is described as the combination of failure probability and failure consequences. The approach uses a FailureLevel (based on inability to complete desired outcomes) determined in two stages: pre-interaction start and post-interaction start, using prediction methods for the post-interaction phase and splitting time into non-overlapping time slots to handle dynamic risk.  

The methodology also models resources the trusting agent invests over time using an Amount Invested Curve (AIC), which gives the probability distribution of net resources at stake during each time slot under the mutually agreed behavior. Because failure can prevent full achievement of desired outcomes, the passage introduces a Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC), obtained by convolving the AIC with the trusted agent’s FailureLevel, to inflate the probabilities of required investment considering failure. From the FAIC, the passage defines the Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) as the probability of not achieving full benefit in a time slot, stated as LORB = FAIC(w) at the end of AIC. The trusting agent can use these probabilities to make informed decisions about which trusted agent to interact with.

The AEGEAN study assessed adherence to apixaban using an electronic medication device, comparing a Primary standard of care (SOC) with an Additional Education Program. The primary endpoint was the percentage of days with correct execution of the apixaban dosing regimen during 24 weeks. Secondary endpoints included within-group comparisons across 12–24 weeks, adherence over 24–48 weeks across additional groups, risk factors for non-adherence at 24 and 48 weeks, and safety outcomes including adverse events and major bleeding.

A total of 1162 subjects were randomized (583 Primary SOC; 579 Additional Education Program), with 560 and 538 included in the evaluable analysis set, respectively. At 24 weeks, 91.64% adherence was observed in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Education Program group, with no significant difference. Adherence decreased from first dose to week 12 versus week 12 to week 24, and was similar between groups from week 24 to week 48. Persistence at 24 weeks and 48 weeks was also comparable between groups. Predictors of non-adherence were evaluated using logit models, with results described as varying by group and time.

Safety outcomes at 24 and 48 weeks were reported as similar between study groups, with comparable rates of adverse events, related adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations due to adverse events, and major bleeding. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high through 24 weeks and sustained up to 48 weeks, and that the proactive educational program did not provide additional adherence or persistence benefits.

SD memory cards have two independent accessible areas: a user area and a protected area. Protected-area access requires authentication, and card capacity equals the sum of user-area and protected-area capacities. Three card capacity classes are defined: SDSC up to and including 2 GB, SDHC more than 2 GB up to 32 GB, and SDXC more than 32 GB up to 2 TB; hosts supporting capacities above 2 GB must also access 2 GB or less, and hosts supporting above 32 GB must also access 32 GB or less. Speed classes indicate minimum performance for different card classes, ranging from class 0 (no performance specified) to class 10 (at least 10 MB/sec). The passage also describes SD bus communication basics (commands, responses, data blocks with CRC), card addressing via session RCA, operation flow in identification and data transfer modes, and initialization/identification using CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3. It further outlines UHS-I and UHS-II modes, including bus speed options, voltage switching behavior, command sequences for voltage changes (CMD11) and tuning (CMD19), and deactivation/initialization sequences for UHS-II. The text includes details on erase-related operations (DISCARD and FULE) and write/read block behavior, and it explains write protection methods: a mechanical write-protect switch, internal write protection, and password-protection card locking. Card ownership protection (COP) and password/force-erase handling via CMD42 are also described, including command behavior, state effects, and error indications for lock/unlock operations.

The TDSAT issued an interim order granting temporary relief to Bharti Airtel Ltd and Idea Cellular Ltd, stating that no penalty can be imposed until further orders for failure to comply with tariff reporting requirements to Trai. Scientists reported that the black hole in the Phoenix cluster may recycle extremely hot gas into cold gas that fuels star formation. Observations from MIT and the University of Cambridge showed jets of about 10-million-degree gas and bubbles in the surrounding plasma; while such jets usually quench star formation by removing cold gas, the researchers found they could instead produce cold gas that rains back onto the galaxy. The Phoenix cluster, about 5.7 billion light years from Earth and containing roughly 1,000 galaxies, has a massive central galaxy forming stars at about 1,000 per year. Using ALMA observations, the team mapped cold gas by detecting carbon monoxide emissions, finding giant filaments extending 20,000 light years from the black hole beyond the central galaxy. Comparing this with prior Chandra X-ray maps of hot gas showed a spatial match, with cold filaments draped over the hot-gas bubbles. The study was published in the Astrophysical Journal.

The passage describes a study on postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and placental biomarkers measured in the first and second trimesters. PPH is defined by World Health Organization blood-loss thresholds and is a major cause of maternal mortality; however, few cases are predicted by current risk tools and no biomarkers are used to predict PPH risk prior to labor. Because placental angiogenesis biomarkers are established for preeclampsia risk, the study examines whether similar biomarkers relate to postpartum bleeding outcomes. It uses the NuMoM2b prospective cohort dataset (nulliparous singleton pregnancies; 2010–2015) and, due to missing blood-loss quantity and PPH diagnosis, constructs a proxy outcome of “retained placenta” and/or “hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion” (RP/PPH). Among 2,192 participants, 67 (3.1%) experienced RP/PPH, which was more common among those diagnosed with preeclampsia. Median biomarker levels were significantly higher in the second trimester for the RP/PPH group, including sEng, β-hCG, INHA, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1, with higher first-trimester sFlt-1/PlGF ratio also observed. Stratification showed that many second-trimester associations persisted in participants without preeclampsia, while differences among biomarkers were not significant for the preeclampsia group. The discussion concludes that placental angiogenesis–related biomarkers in early pregnancy, particularly in the second trimester and including biomarker changes over time, may help identify risk for severe postpartum bleeding, with limitations including the proxy nature of the outcome and lack of direct blood-loss measures.

The passage explains that learning shared patterns is valuable because it creates a shared vocabulary, helping people understand each other quickly and enabling knowledge sharing and further learning. The passage describes COVID-19 and vaccination efforts in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) during the first year of implementation (April 2021 to March 2022). Vaccines were developed and WHO-approved, including the COVAX initiative, and early Africa vaccination coverage by April 2022 is reported.

In DRC, COVID-19 was first reported in Africa in February 2020 with Egypt’s first case, and the DRC confirmed its first case on March 10, 2020. The DRC experienced multiple waves of COVID-19, and a vaccine deployment plan was developed in January 2021. The DRC launched a vaccination campaign in April 2021, aiming to vaccinate at least 20% of the population by the end of 2021.

The study is a secondary analysis using data from the DRC Ministry of Health and WHO’s Africa vaccination database. Methods include provincial reporting of programmatic indicators and paper-based registers. Results show that only 16 of 26 provinces began immunization activities in the first year. Fully vaccinated coverage varied by province, with highest coverage in Kasai Oriental and lowest in Kwilu, Tshuapa, and Equateur. By March 2022, about 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% were fully vaccinated, with a spike in doses administered in February 2022 followed by a decline. Men were vaccinated at higher counts than women in most provinces. By the end of the period, 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 elderly individuals had completed their primary vaccine series. The vaccines used included AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson (Janssen), Pfizer, and Sinovac, with Janssen being most preferred.

Comparison with neighboring Central African countries indicates that DRC had relatively low vaccination progress, including the lowest percentage of doses administered per the provided table and the lowest proportion of the population receiving at least one dose. The discussion attributes low uptake to challenges such as early halting of AstraZeneca vaccination due to safety concerns, competing health priorities, shortages of healthcare professionals, logistics issues including vaccine expiry and supply constraints, and barriers to reaching high-risk groups. The study notes limitations related to tracking denominators and vaccination histories using aggregated records. The conclusion states that the first year combined progress and challenges, emphasizing continued investment in health systems and lessons for other countries.

The passage explains that “oversold” means a stock market or stock has dropped significantly during a predefined time period, such as a 10% fall over 10 days, and that objective criteria should be used, often via technical indicators like the 3-day RSI. The passage describes the development of the concept of “social capital,” noting that it was studied academically in the late 1980s by sociologist James Coleman and later adopted and advanced by Robert S. The First Circuit dismissed the government’s interlocutory appeal in United States v. Watson and O’Hearn. The appeal followed the district court’s denial of a continuance sought so the government could depose a key witness, Anthony Spera, after he was deported. The court held that the orders denying the continuance and declining the request to depose Spera abroad did not fall within the category of district court orders appealable under the second paragraph of § 3731, which is limited to orders suppressing or excluding evidence in substance. The dismissal was for lack of appellate jurisdiction.

The passage describes augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) systems and their challenges in localizing the position and orientation of real and virtual objects. The summary then presents a need for improved localization systems and describes embodiments of display systems and AR devices, including a head-mounted AR display with sensors and processors that monitor sensor information to trigger access to virtual content, and an AR display device with stacked waveguides and camera-based QR code decoding to request and present virtual content.

In the detailed description, the passage outlines a system architecture combining local processing (e.g., a belt pack) with optional cloud resources for maintaining and distributing a “passable world model.” It further explains an electromagnetic tracking approach for pose detection, including an electromagnetic field emitter and sensors that calculate position and orientation, strategies for mobile components, and methods to integrate electromagnetic tracking with camera/SLAM. Additional design aspects discussed include sensor placement, compact emitter/receiver configurations, IMU stabilization, duty-cycle/power saving, calibration and noise cancellation, and vision-based pose calculation stages using camera feature extraction, key frames, triangulation, and bundle adjustment.

Generative models, particularly Boltzmann Generators (BGs), are presented as a one-shot alternative to MD/MC for generating equilibrium ensembles. Prior BG work has faced scaling limits due to high training costs and low sampling efficiencies, with large systems typically requiring impractical computation and remaining beyond current capabilities. The paper introduces a local, size-transferable augmented coupling-flow architecture that uses locality assumptions, graph neural networks, and auxiliary variables to improve scaling and computational efficiency. The approach trains without target-distribution samples by optimizing a KL-divergence-based loss, and it supports efficient inference through exact likelihood evaluation and transferable models across system sizes. Experiments on crystalline Lennard–Jones and Stillinger–Weber systems (including monatomic water, silicon, and germanium parameterizations) show accurate equilibrium structure and energy distributions without reweighting, improved effective sample sizes compared to global architectures, and accurate absolute Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies for systems with over 1000 particles. The method is further demonstrated for NPT volume fluctuations and for conditioned models that generalize across interaction parameters and thermodynamic variables, including mapping the silicon (T, P)-phase diagram. The paper concludes that the local flow architecture enables scalable equilibrium sampling and efficient free-energy/phase-stability evaluation across thermodynamic conditions.

It then describes Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders for flexible geometry processing), Variable Rate Shading (VRS) with fine-grained per-16x16 tile shading rate control and example algorithms (Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering), and Texture Space Shading (TSS), which decouples visibility sampling from appearance sampling and can reuse shaded texels for temporal stability.
