Publisher/CEO Lisa M. Umina and publishing consultant Cecilia Sotres are quoted, and contact information for Hola Publishing is provided.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that on May 22, 2019 it held its Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Directors were elected to hold office until the next Annual Meeting based on the votes shown for nominees Jeffrey P. Bezos, Rosalind G. Brewer, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Indra K. Nooyi, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer, and Wendell P. Weeks. The appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2019 was ratified. The advisory vote to approve compensation of named executive officers was approved. Multiple shareholder proposals were not approved, including proposals related to food waste management, special meeting ownership thresholds, government use of certain technologies (and related impact reporting), certain products, independent board chair policy, employment policies, climate change topics, board ideology disclosure, changes to gender pay reporting, integrating metrics into executive compensation, and vote-counting practices for shareholder proposals. The report was signed on May 24, 2019 by David A. Zapolsky.

President Anderson addresses a graduation ceremony at American University, discussing the study of history and public affairs and emphasizing the importance of world peace. He rejects “Pax Americana,” the peace of the grave, and the security of the slave, and calls for genuine peace lasting for all time. He argues that total war and nuclear weapons do not make sense, though he says peace also requires prudent deterrence and arms control rather than relying only on stockpiles. He urges graduates and citizens to examine their attitudes toward peace, the Soviet Union, and the cold war, arguing that human problems can be solved and that conflict is not inevitable. He highlights common interests between the U.S. and the Soviet Union, supports strengthening the United Nations, and describes efforts to manage tensions in various regions. He announces plans for high-level discussions in Moscow for an early comprehensive test ban treaty and declares the U.S. will not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests if other states do not. He also links world peace to freedom and human rights at home, calling for protection of citizens’ freedoms and responsibility from government and citizens, concluding with a commitment to pursue peace rather than annihilation.

Just Patios delivers patio, cover, and roofing solutions, including durable, highly customisable carports designed to withstand harsh Australian weather and help protect vehicles from rust or corrosion. The carports use galvanised or colourbond systems and are suitable for cars, boats, caravans, motorbikes, and jet skis, with installation handled by a team of builders. Designs include Flat/Skillion (including a free-standing or attached option, and an affordable zincalume-and-galvanised variant), Raised Flyover (taller, for boats and caravans, free-standing or attached), and Gable Carport (raised gable roof in three styles and modifiable for home designs). Just Patios also assists with council regulations on property boundaries; the company serves Brisbane and the Sunshine Coast, uses quality materials, and provides 15-year warranties.

Mark Mobius told CNBC that a major correction of about 30% in U.S. markets is not unforeseen, citing massive outflows from exchange-traded funds. He warned that ETFs and automated selling could trigger large, fast market corrections due to a “snowball effect” with no safety valve. Mobius also said emerging markets could face downside and contagion risks tied to Turkey, and noted Argentina and Brazil are not doing well. Separately, economist Paul Krugman warned of a potential self-reinforcing emerging market currency crisis similar to 1997–98.

The passage describes time-aware networks (TANs) and time-sensitive applications (TSAs), focusing on techniques to provide low-latency, scalable gate control, allow multiple TSAs to share the same physical network link, and support time-aware energy efficient network communication. It outlines background challenges in IoT, Industry 4.0, and automation requiring precise time synchronization and timely event delivery, and notes a gap between TSN standards and TSN systems.

It explains TAN architecture using Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and IEEE time-sensitive networking (TSN) standards, including generalized PTP domains and PTP instance types (end and relay), timing message roles, and timescales (PTP and ARB). It also describes TSN transmission selection and scheduled traffic concepts such as traffic classes, transmission selection algorithms, priority-based flow control, frame preemption, and gate control lists (GCLs) with gate operations and state changes.

For low latency and scalable gate control, the passage discusses shortcomings of current TSN-capable NICs that use large, precise scheduling memory for gate control (including silicon area, power, and programming complexity issues). It then presents an architecture that moves the GCL to host memory and uses a smaller prefetch buffer with dedicated channel prefetching, aiming to reduce NIC memory/power usage and enable faster, more precise scheduling by directly programming the GCL in host memory and prefetching gate operations and related queue data in time with PTP-based cycle timing.

Finally, it addresses TSA configuration for end stations, emphasizing challenges when multiple talker applications share one network interface. It describes complex end station configurations and how stream reservation protocols and signaling mechanisms (e.g., SRP with MMRP, MVRP, and MSRP concepts) can manage stream reservations, while allowing configuration to be computed and distributed via centralized management and adapted to limit interference among workloads.

Indiana University of Pennsylvania President Dr. Michael Driscoll announced he has stopped, for now, an investigation by the school’s Academic Integrity Board regarding a controversy in a religious studies class. He said senior Lake Ingle will be allowed to return to the class needed to graduate. Ingle was cited for violating the school’s Academic Integrity Code after speaking during a discussion about transgender issues on Feb. 28, and he argued this violated his free speech rights. Dr. Driscoll stated the decision follows a review of governing policies and that a senior faculty member with First Amendment experience will join the class as a monitor and mentor to maintain a positive learning environment, despite acknowledging it could lead to accusations he is not following school policy.

The passage describes a desk lamp design shown in eight figures: perspective views (FIGS. 1 and 2), front view (FIG. 3), rear view (FIG. 4), left and right side views (FIGS. 5 and 6), top plan view (FIG. 7), and bottom plan view (FIG. 8). It also states that dashed or broken lines indicate portions of the lamp where the design is embodied that are not part of the claimed design.

The passage describes TQQQ (ProShares UltraPro QQQ) as an ETF tracking the Nasdaq-100 index and presents a “comprehensive guide” to trading options on it. It explains that option trading differs from stock trading because it involves buying and selling call and put options, with calls giving the right to buy and puts giving the right to sell at set prices. It outlines factors for trading (option terms, underlying security, volatility, time frame, liquidity, and risk tolerance), common strategies (buying calls/puts, writing covered calls, writing put options), and the need for risk management, such as determining maximum risk, using stop loss orders, and backtesting ideas. It states that TQQQ options are European or American style and that option trading is speculative and high-risk due to leverage. The passage also notes that costs depend on the broker and include commissions and contract fees, plus slippage. It mentions taxes are generally capital gains but vary by jurisdiction and individual circumstances. It adds that regulations may include minimum capital requirements, limits on leverage, and rules related to margin calls, stop-loss orders, and hedging, and suggests consulting a broker for specifics. It also says option fair value can be estimated using the Black-Scholes model.

Roberts speaks to officials and Americans on Inauguration Day, calling it “America’s day” and “democracy’s day.” He says democracy prevailed despite recent violence at the Capitol, and he emphasizes a peaceful transfer of power. He thanks predecessors, cites the Constitution and George Washington’s oath, and urges “We the People” to advance unity. He describes major challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic, job and business losses, calls for racial justice, climate crisis concerns, political extremism, and domestic terrorism. He argues that unity is necessary to repair, restore, heal, and build, and he calls for respectful disagreement within the Republic and for citizens and leaders to defend truth over lies. He promises to be a president for all Americans, fight for those who did not support him, and pursue policies including jobs, safe schools, overcoming the virus, health care for all, and racial justice. He addresses foreign audiences about repairing alliances and leading by example, asks Americans to pray silently for those lost to the pandemic, and closes with a vow to defend the Constitution, democracy, and America.

University at Albany chemists synthesized manganese diboride, a boron-rich compound with higher energy density than current solid rocket materials and stable behavior until ignited. The compound releases more energy by weight and volume than aluminum used in solid rocket boosters, and it is described as safe, combusting only when meeting an ignition agent like kerosene. Researchers say using it could reduce required fuel and free space for mission-critical supplies. The team used an arc melter to produce the material and computer models to identify “deformation” in its atomic structure as a feature linked to stored energy. The passage also notes the compound class has potential applications beyond propulsion, including catalytic converters and plastic breakdown.

Referees and players in Europe are facing renewed disciplinary problems early in the season. Cristiano Ronaldo was punished for pushing a referee and for a rule-breaching goal celebration, receiving a five-match domestic ban after the Spanish federation said referee authority and safety must be respected. Cesc Fabregas received a second booking after sarcastic applauding and another lunge, costing Chelsea in a Premier League loss to Burnley. Newcastle lost their opener after Jonjo Shelvey was sent off for treading on Dele Alli’s foot. In France, Lille goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off for throwing a ball at Strasbourg’s Benjamin Corgnet, with Lille further hurt by an inability to make substitutions after using three. The passage also describes ongoing transfer disputes, including Virgil van Dijk seeking a move from Southampton, Liverpool’s interest in Philippe Coutinho, and Tottenham defender Danny Rose criticizing the club’s spending and urging signings of established stars.

Barry “The Hatchet” Vagnoni, a Reading, Pennsylvania father of two and grandfather of six, has been a Philadelphia Eagles fan since 1954. He and his wife Dawn, married for 56 years, host Super Bowl gatherings in his 2,000-square-foot “locker-room-type” man cave, which has a 35-foot bar, 16 televisions, and team memorabilia. Guests, known as “locker-room members,” are mostly friends and family, wear Eagles gear, and follow family-friendly rules (no smoking or foul language). Vagnoni leads cheers from a stage, changes costumes, and beats a drum, while Dawn helps behind the scenes with cooking and photos. For Super Bowl LII, they plan to welcome over 100 people, along with a band, dancers, two smokers, and wings; food and drinks are free, with no expected donations. Vagnoni said the event is his lifelong dream and he will also be thinking of his late father.

The passage explains what trading “gaps” are and how they occur, noting they are areas between a prior close and the next open with little or no trading, often caused by news or imbalances. It states that overnight gaps are the most frequent and labels common gaps as having little significance, while exhaustion and runaway gaps are described as occurring after extended moves or sudden sharp moves. It says gap trading strategies used to be more profitable but are now harder to find and generally less profitable due to increased computer power and more traders, requiring more filters and increasing the risk of curve-fitting. It outlines general approaches such as fading vs. following gaps, and discusses gap-fill likelihood, including S&P 500 results where fill rates vary by gap size and generally decrease for larger gaps. It emphasizes the need for reliable data for backtesting and provides examples of tested strategies, including day trading and overnight swing trading, with the claim that results are not spectacular but can work reasonably well.

A review of 10 trials involving 77,917 participants with prior heart attack or stroke or health problems such as diabetes found that omega-3 fatty acid supplements did not reduce the overall risk of cardiovascular disease or any specific cardiovascular outcome compared with placebo. The researchers reported similar risks for heart-disease death, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, and procedures to reopen clogged arteries, and concluded there was no beneficial effect of omega-3 supplements for cardiovascular disease prevention in any subgroup. The study noted limitations including variation in trial designs and limited individual data on smoking status and cancer history. Commentary in the passage said evidence does not strongly support heart protection, but omega-3 supplements may still be considered due to being inexpensive and generally safe, and people were advised to eat fatty fish regularly or use high-quality omega-3 supplements as part of a balanced diet.

In 2017, Boscov’s reported a record-breaking sales year, including a healthy increase at its Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania location. Shoppers cited the “personal touch,” with long-time salespeople recognizing customers, and said the store’s downtown presence helps other businesses. Although many people shop online, Boscov’s physical stores saw a single-digit increase in sales. The store is described as having a hometown atmosphere, with staff knowing customers’ names. Boscov’s also plans to open a 47th store in Connecticut.

The passage argues that schools need comprehensive renewal because society changes faster and more drastically, especially in pedagogical and didactic fields. It proposes that, while education should remain a “school for life” and critically account for harmful changes, rapid technological possibilities and fundamentally different learners require moving from digital pedagogy to generative pedagogy. It describes shifts linked to the “Net generation” and “Web 4.0,” including a move toward blended and non-formal learning and the growing presence of artificial intelligence and cyber-physical systems in society. The passage also situates these changes within successive “waves” of technological disruption and claims that generative AI will rapidly and significantly affect economies, politics, cultures, and education, raising questions about the teacher’s role, the value of producing content, and the value of assessment. It concludes that teachers’ roles will need to change drastically and that generative AI should be treated as a partner as educators develop relationships and values rather than being the sole authority on knowledge.

Bayard’s City Council reported it received an “unmodified” audit grade from Fierro & Fierro, despite two small findings. One finding involved a federal Community Development Block Grant fund where budgeted revenue was lower than expenditures, creating a $700 deficit; the other involved small per diem and mileage calculation errors totaling $64. The council unanimously voted to support the village of Santa Clara’s efforts to secure management of the historic Fort Bayard property. Santa Clara’s representative, Scott Terry, presented the village’s plan to rejuvenate Fort Bayard, including renting office space to the U.S. Forest Service, while Bayard Councilor Zeke Santa Maria raised concerns about Santa Clara’s capacity. The council also heard an update on restoring the exterior of the Bayard train depot, with Ortiz working with railroad officials to address ground-ownership issues.

Registration is open for Horses4Heroes’ Saturdays at the Ranch Day Camps, Spring Break Camp (March 26–March 30), and 10 weeks of Summer Camp beginning May 29 at the Horses4Heroes Equestrian Center in historic Floyd Lamb at Tule Springs. The camps for children ages 5–13 include horseback riding and related activities; Spring Break Camp also includes a morning at The Texas Station Hotel & Casino and a karate class. Summer Camp runs Monday–Friday, 8 am–5 pm, with a weekly outing to The Texas and a Friday water slide in the corral. Reduced rates are available for veterans, Active Duty Military personnel, National Guard and Reserve, law enforcement officers, school teachers, and nurses, and teen volunteers (ages 14–17) can serve as volunteer student counselors. For all camps, registration is online at http://horses4heroes.myonlinecamp.com/ and proceeds support care of horses and farm animals and scholarships.

Smart beta strategies have grown in the ETF market, attracting hundreds of billions in assets, but many investors and financial advisors still lack familiarity with how they work. A 2018 FTSE Russell Advisor Smart Beta Survey of 256 fee-based advisors found that about 79% of U.S. advisors were aware of smart beta, while only 35% were very familiar. Forty-seven percent said they do not use smart beta because they do not know enough about how it works. The survey noted continued demand for more education, information, and insight; in the U.S. and Canada, advisors seek information before increasing exposure, while U.K. advisors expressed concerns about performance and limited track records.

A representative for pro wrestling legend Ric Flair said he was hospitalized and dealing with “tough medical issues.” Melinda Morris Zanoni confirmed the report, stating Flair, 68, was admitted for routine monitoring, and asked for “prayers & positive energy.” Mick Foley and Eric Bischoff also sent well wishes on Twitter. The passage notes Flair’s “Nature Boy” nickname and that he debuted professionally in 1972 and was inducted into WWE Hall of Fame in 2008.

The author returns House bill No. 1471, which would double the pension of Andrew J. Hill, describing it as special legislation that frequently reverses decisions of the Pension Bureau. The passage argues that Congress and special bills can override the Bureau’s examination, potentially leading to unjustified claims and prejudice against qualified veterans. The author also notes that nearly 240 special pension bills were returned shortly before the constitutional limit after referral to the Pension Bureau, estimates their cost at over $35,000 annually, and states that many would otherwise be disapproved but cannot be fully objected to in time. The specific reason for returning the bill is a name discrepancy: records and a medical certificate indicate the beneficiary should be Alfred J. Hill, not Andrew J. Hill.

The passage provides guidance for using a Galaxy Fold phone and describes how Motley Fool Money’s compensation from advertisers can affect product placement but not its product ratings. The wife of detained human rights lawyer Yu Wensheng, Xu Yan, said she was prevented from leaving her neighbourhood as police followed her and told taxi drivers not to take her. She said the officers could not explain who authorized the restriction or how long it would last. Yu was detained on Jan. 19 and charged with inciting subversion. The passage says his detention is part of a crackdown on independent legal activists begun in July 2015, and mentions Merkel’s private meeting in Beijing with Xu and another detained lawyer’s wife. It also notes China’s practice of detaining or harassing relatives of people accused of crimes against the state, citing Liu Xia.

The passage describes the Xiaomi Mi 8 and Mi 8 SE. Both Mi 8 models use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 845 chipset with 6GB RAM, with storage options up to 256GB for the normal edition and 1238GB for the other. They feature a 6.21-inch 2,248 x 1,080 AMOLED display with 600-nit brightness. The Mi 8 supports dual-frequency GPS (L1 and L5), which Xiaomi claims improves navigation accuracy by three to five times. Both models have dual 12-megapixel main cameras and a 20-megapixel front camera using pixel binning; the cameras also use AI-enabled studio lighting and portrait beautification software. The Mi 8 SE is introduced with Snapdragon 710, a 3,120 mAh battery, AI features, a 12MP/5MP dual rear camera, and a 20-megapixel front camera; it starts at 1,799 yuan (about $280).

The passage describes defensive preparation against the “Mid Screen” offense, which uses a “Big” screen for a “Little” and can lead to dribble penetration if defenders get hung up. It notes that most NBA teams prefer not to switch because switching allows the dribbler to flair to the wing while the screener posts up, so “Show & Recover” is the preferred defense, though tactics vary by team and player. The passage outlines “Show” (pushing the ball to the sideline and having a defender step out hard on the screen, while other defenders set pass denial and help positions), “Recover” (re-establishing point defense, diving or sprinting back to the post, and adjusting pass denial and help spots), and “Final Match Up” (setting pass denial, forcing the next offensive action, and re-aligning post and weakside defenders). It also describes “All Out SOS Disruption,” achieved by initiating defense before the first screen option, using trapping and rotations to force offensive players into “free lance” situations, including “Double Team (trap),” “Pass Out of Trap,” and “Final Alignment,” with specific rotational rules tied to when the ball leaves the passer’s hands and possible subsequent trap rotations.

The passage discusses using ChatGPT for AI trading analysis, including creating and coding trading strategies and backtesting them on historical data to evaluate performance. It describes ChatGPT as an OpenAI AI model based on GPT architecture that generates text from prompts and can be used for sentiment analysis, predictions, and assistance with technical indicators and trading algos. The passage states that generated strategies cannot be assumed to be profitable and must be backtested, then validated for live trading with a small deployment. It also notes risks such as incorrect or overly confident outputs and the need to debug and validate code. A test example is described where ChatGPT produced a mean reversion strategy with few trades and the generated Amibroker code contained many errors. The passage also contrasts ChatGPT’s role as a tool for creating systems with the idea that it cannot fully automate trading by itself.

The passage describes a volume documenting Shultz’s efforts against bureaucratic obstacles with the NSC to implement NSDD 75’s four-part agenda and to gain regular access to President Reagan by June 1983. It notes Shultz’s collaboration with Jack Matlock and others to keep communication open with the Soviet Union despite arguments by figures such as Defense Secretary Caspar Weinberger that negotiations were futile. It highlights Cold War flashpoints of 1983, including the Soviet downing of KAL 007, concerns over Reagan’s SDI, and the Euromissiles crisis involving U.S. INF deployments, as well as selective material on the Soviet “War Scare” and the NATO nuclear exercise Able Archer. After the Soviet walkout of INF talks in Geneva, the administration focused in 1984 on restarting arms control, with ongoing disputes over SDI and how it would be handled in negotiations. It states that when Shultz and Gromyko met in January 1985, they agreed to a new round of umbrella negotiations for NST tracks (START, INF, and Defense and Space), but that Chernenko’s death before the NST meetings would change U.S.-Soviet relations. The passage ends with acknowledgments of assistance and access provided by multiple institutions and individuals for the volume’s compilation and review.

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) measures gene expression at the single-cell level but relies on slow, subjective annotation using marker genes and expert knowledge, which does not scale to large modern datasets. Existing computational annotation methods, including foundation model embeddings, often depend on fixed predefined categories and classification heads, limiting flexibility and generalization.

The paper introduces Cell2Text, a multimodal generative framework that converts scRNA-seq profiles into natural-language descriptions. Cell2Text uses a pretrained Geneformer encoder to produce gene-level contextual embeddings, a lightweight adapter to project these embeddings into an instruction-tuned language model’s semantic space, and an LLM decoder to generate structured descriptions covering cell type, associated disease, tissue origin, donor developmental stage, and active pathways. Geneformer parameters are frozen during training, while the adapter and language model are tuned via full fine-tuning or LoRA.

Experiments using a large CELLxGENE-derived multimodal dataset (1M cells) show that generated text has strong lexical overlap and high biomedical semantic fidelity (BioBERT F1 over 93.9). For prediction tasks derived from generated text, Cell2Text variants outperform baselines on cell type, tissue, and disease classification. A PageRank-based ontology-aware evaluation indicates that errors are biologically close in the Cell Ontology. For pathway activity, Cell2Text performs competitively on identifying top two active pathways from a set of 34 Hallmark pathways. The authors conclude that training for text generation yields richer cellular representations and more interpretable, scalable frameworks for computational biology.

Nintendo Classic Mini has been popular with gamers, but it is unclear why Nintendo has kept production limited. Originally sold for $60, it has been resold on eBay for higher prices. A report by Geek suggests buyers should get one early because Nintendo may end manufacturing soon. According to WWG and a NeoGAF member, Nintendo has confirmed production has ended and a few more shipments will arrive before stock runs out, expected by April or May. A Norwegian retailer’s Facebook page reportedly supports this, but it is not confirmed whether the stock ending applies only to Norway or to worldwide retailers. The passage says Nintendo previously promised to increase production, which now seems invalid.

The passage describes a study on how exogenous oxytocin (OT) affects social touch processing, focusing on intranasal OT versus oral (lingual) OT and comparing touch targeting CT fibers (gentle stroking) with touch targeting non-CT fibers (medium pressure massage). It explains that CT fibers are specialized for the affective/rewarding aspects of touch and are linked to brain regions including the insula, orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS). The study recruited 180 healthy Chinese participants, with final analyzed data from 171. OT concentrations in plasma were measured before and after OT administration and after touch sessions, and neural responses were recorded using fNIRS in OFC and STS regions, alongside behavioral ratings of pleasantness and other measures, plus physiological measures (HRV and SCR). Results reported that intranasal and oral OT both increased pleasantness ratings specifically for gentle stroking touch (not medium pressure massage) and increased oxyhemoglobin activity in bilateral mOFC and pSTS in response to gentle stroking. OT did not significantly affect peripheral physiological responses measured by HRV and SCR. Mediation analyses indicated that OT-related enhancements in pleasantness were significantly mediated by post-treatment increases in plasma OT concentrations. The passage concludes that OT administered intranasally or orally selectively facilitates neural and behavioral responses to CT-fiber stimulation via peripheral-mediated routes, and notes limitations related to fNIRS depth, touch naturalism, and sampling frequency.

The passage is a Haas alumni weekly job email (11/9/00) that welcomes recipients and instructs companies and alumni to submit job openings to recruitalumni@haas.berkeley.edu with details including location, title, company, degree, and contact information. It also includes announcements for the Women in Leadership Conference (11/11/00) and a Big Game Bar-B-Que (11/18/00), along with a link to an alumni network survey.

The passage describes favorable conditions at the start of a congressional session, including abundant harvests, flourishing commerce, revenue exceeding expectations, and preserved peace with foreign nations. It reports that because a commercial convention with Great Britain would expire in early July, negotiations were opened in London to extend to general commerce and other outstanding issues, with the existing convention to continue for at least eight years. It states that U.S.-Spain relations remain unresolved regarding certain claims and boundary issues, while events in Florida—described as marked by weak Spanish authority and lawless adventuring—are presented as justifying U.S. actions, including suppressing Amelia Island and authorizing Major-General Jackson to enter Florida to pursue Seminoles. The passage also discusses continuing civil war in South America, the status of independence in multiple provinces, and anticipated allied mediation without force. It reviews U.S. domestic finances and revenue, ongoing defense measures and fortifications, Indian treaties and pending negotiations involving land cessions, naval operations to protect commerce, and Illinois’s accession to the Union. Bandai Namco announced Super Robot Wars X for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita, releasing March 29, 2018 in Japan and April 26 in Southeast Asia with English subtitles. A Premium Edition launches alongside the standard edition in Japan and includes 35 more songs. Early purchases include two additional scenarios, an original theme, and Cybuster and Masaki unlocked from the start. The passage also provides background on VGChartz author William D'Angelo and gives contact details.

The passage describes a smart gateway platform for industrial automation that applies analytics to industrial data to achieve business objectives. The platform stores executable components and model templates tied to specific objectives, receives selection data to choose a template, receives mapping data that maps template data inputs to data tags of industrial devices, customizes the template, collects data from the mapped tags, normalizes and adds modeling metadata based on template-defined relationships, and sends structured data to an artificial intelligence analytics system. It also outlines a method and a non-transitory computer-readable medium with similar operations. The detailed description discusses how the platform uses domain expertise encoded in model templates to limit and constrain the data sent to analytics, reducing time-to-value and storage compared with conventional big-data approaches, and supports contextualization and structuring of both smart and raw data for AI analysis. The passage further describes components and example industrial architectures, including multi-level analytics across device, system/edge, and enterprise/cloud layers, plus concepts such as smart data tags, AI metadata, enterprise hierarchy modeling, and time-synchronization of related data items.

Hundreds of built and proposed hydroelectric dams could significantly harm life in and around the Amazon by trapping nutrient-rich sediments and altering climate, according to findings published in *Nature*. The study, led by scientists at The University of Texas at Austin and involving researchers from 10 universities, notes that South America has proposed 428 dams in the Amazon basin, with 140 built or under construction. It argues that while dams are promoted for renewable energy and avoiding carbon emissions, they may disrupt Amazon floodplains, rainforests, the northeast coast, and regional climate. The researchers developed the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index (DEVI) to quantify vulnerability to impacts such as land use change, erosion, runoff pollution, trapped sediment, and river system changes. They report high vulnerability in the Andean Cordillera, especially on the Marañon and Ucayali rivers, and estimate that 68–80% of upstream areas on these rivers will remain unprotected from dam influence. For the Madeira River, the study finds DEVI values above 80 and cites dam effects including a 20% decrease in average sediment concentration after construction of Santo Antônio and Jiaru dams, with more upstream dams expected to trap additional nutrient-rich sediment. The Tapajós River is also projected to be impounded if proposed dams proceed and deforestation continues. The researchers warn that cumulative effects could change sediment flow into the Atlantic Ocean and hinder regional climate.

The passage describes an Australian divisional patent application for novel cationic lipids used to form lipid nanoparticles for delivering nucleic acids (e.g., antisense oligonucleotides and mRNA) for intracellular delivery in vitro and in vivo. It addresses challenges of nucleic acid delivery, including nuclease degradation of free RNA in plasma and limited intracellular access, and states that lipid nanoparticles formed with cationic lipids and other lipid components (e.g., neutral lipids, cholesterol, and polymer-conjugated lipids such as PEGylated lipids) can protect nucleic acids and facilitate uptake. The invention provides lipid compounds with structures defined by Formula (I), including stereoisomers, salts, and tautomers, and describes embodiments of related compositions and methods for administering therapeutic agents to patients, including pharmaceutical formulations and systemic or local delivery. It also includes detailed discussion of preparing nucleic acids (notably mRNA via in vitro transcription, purification, capping, polyadenylation, and nucleoside/UTR modifications) and general definitions of terms used throughout the disclosure.

Robots in unstructured, partially observed environments generate world models used by motion planners to avoid hazards, but sensor noise, occlusions, state estimation errors, and incomplete observations can make successive world maps inconsistent. In field tests on a Clearpath Robotics UGV, relying only on the most recent map led to oscillatory, unstable trajectories around obstacles, since deterministic planners produced inconsistent plans when the perceived cost maps changed. The paper presents a KEASL-based motion planning approach using multiple temporally sampled environment map hypotheses to compute edge costs more robustly. Four multi-hypothesis methods are explored: VEH (edge valid in every hypothesis), PEH (valid in any hypothesis with rerouting in invalid hypotheses), GEH (defers multi-hypothesis validity checks until goal expansion), and GEGRH (adds graph revision after GEH rerouting). Experiments on 221 UGV planning problems using ARA* (1-second limit, heuristic inflation 2.0) compare SH, VEH, and GEGRH with two or three successive maps. GEGRH reduced planning time versus VEH (15.4% for two hypotheses; 29.27% for three) and improved path duration (6.64% and 18.72%, respectively). Qualitative case studies show scenarios where GEGRH can outperform VEH and others where VEH can perform better. The work concludes that incorporating perception uncertainty into deterministic graph search via multiple hypotheses can improve robustness while balancing caution and efficiency, and it outlines future directions such as increasing the number of hypotheses and using richer divergence and cost/uncertainty modeling.

The passage is a large excerpt from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2019. It includes company information and financial statements (income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, cash flows, and stockholders’ equity) and presents key figures such as total revenue ($36.9 billion for three months ended December 31, 2019), net income ($11.6 billion), and ending cash and cash equivalents ($8.9 billion). A 29-year-old man from Essex was arrested at the scene after crashing into a gas meter on Ridge Road at 9 p.m. Tuesday. President Donald Trump condemned white supremacists and neo-Nazis in a White House statement Monday, saying racism is evil and that groups including the KKK, neo-Nazis, and white supremacists are “repugnant.” The condemnation came after Democrats and Republicans criticized his earlier silence following violent protests in Charlottesville, Virginia, that left one woman dead. Federal prosecutors say Matthew Lane, a 19-year-old college freshman from Sterling, Massachusetts, confessed in June to a ransomware attack on PowerSchool. Prosecutors allege he collaborated with at least one co-conspirator to steal sensitive records of more than 60 million students and 10 million educators and extort nearly $3 million from PowerSchool. The sentencing report describes his activity as part of a pattern dating back to at least 2021 and says his conduct was “sophisticated,” involving tools and methods to conceal identity and access networks. Prosecutors are seeking a seven-year prison sentence and more than $14 million in restitution. Lane returned about $160,000, but roughly $3 million remains unaccounted for, according to the report. Open-source and threat intelligence research reported by The 74 from Cyble says Lane used flamboyant online personas linked to cybercrime accounts targeting multiple types of organizations since 2021.

Gartner analyst Stephen Kleynhans argues that Windows 10 Pro is becoming a dead end for enterprises as Microsoft reduces support and limits access to enterprise management features for Pro. Kleynhans says Microsoft has increasingly separated Pro from the Enterprise editions, making the gap unbridgeable, and notes that Microsoft’s on-the-fly support extensions apply only to Windows 10 Enterprise (and Windows 10 Education). The extra six months and paid supplemental servicing are available only for Enterprise/Education, while Windows 10 Pro users must upgrade within 18 months to keep receiving security patches. Kleynhans and Michael Silver recommend that customers using Pro monitor Microsoft life cycle announcements and budget for Windows 10 Enterprise as Pro shifts toward a “pro-sumer” and small-business focus.

Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater Associates, said investors should allocate as much as 15% of their portfolios to gold. He compared today’s environment to the early 1970s, citing inflation, high debt, and uncertainty, and said gold is a hedge during monetary debasement and geopolitical uncertainty. Gold prices surged to an all-time high above $4,000 an ounce, with gold futures last trading at $4,005.80 per ounce after rising more than 50% this year. Dalio also contrasted his recommendation with typical 60-40 stock-and-bond guidance and said gold “is the only asset” investors can hold without depending on others to pay.

Two years after South Sudan’s independence, Dr. Inka Weissbecker toured the country’s only mental health facility, which she described as prison-like, with sedated patients, no medication for people with schizophrenia, and an unattended traumatized girl. President Donald Trump announced a deal with AstraZeneca on his TrumpRx.com platform to lower US prescription drug costs through a “most-favored-nation” pricing policy. AstraZeneca said it will offer discounts on its prescription drug catalog, and Trump said Americans would pay the lowest prices available worldwide. The passage describes several SOS (on-ball and off-ball) defensive disruption schemes for handling wing and baseline actions, including “SOS Disruptions” focused on denying middle penetrations and limiting opponent space. Say it with Diamonds, an Instagram jewellery business started in 2016 by Charlotte Donoghue and Steph Porter, has opened its first city-centre store in Liverpool at Cavern Walks. The shop will offer jewellery, including wedding and engagement rings for different budgets, with a wide range available to browse. The founders say online trading and Secret Warehouse sales surpassed expectations and they now want to expand and become Liverpool’s premier jewellery store, building on their following among customers including celebrities.

Shriram Transport Finance said its promoters are in talks with SVL Group to ensure SVL pays the company’s dues on or before the stipulated date. On Wednesday, the company’s shares fell sharply amid concerns about SVL’s ability to repay holders of certain debentures, dropping nearly 12% to Rs 1,144.85 on BSE, after moving down during the day. In June 2015, Shriram Transport provided corporate guarantees of Rs 870 crore for non-convertible debentures issued by SVL, which mature in June 2019. The passage describes an invention for ecologically sustainable, fiber-based container and packaging manufacturing intended to replace plastics using vacuum molded fiber products. Co-operative Group reported a £132 million loss in 2016 after writing off its stake in the struggling Co-operative Bank, valuing its 20% holding at nil due to uncertain prospects. While operating profit rose 32% to £148 million from growth in supermarkets, funeral services, and insurance, the group recorded a pretax loss. The South Dakota Department of Agriculture encourages producers who may have experienced crop damage from dicamba to complete a Dicamba Damage Survey on its website. Philadelphia City Council will meet before its regular Thursday session to act on bills enabling the “Rebuild” facility renovation project, which would fund renovations of up to 200 parks, rec centers, and libraries over seven years. Council had twice declined the plan but says it has added amendments aligned with council goals. Council President Darrell Clarke and mayor spokesperson Lauren Hitt say the changes will support workforce diversity, and the mayor hopes the bills pass so work can begin after legal challenges to the beverage tax are resolved.

James Hodgkinson of Belleville, Illinois is accused of shooting five people Wednesday morning during practice for a charity baseball game, including U.S. Rep. Steve Scalise, who was in critical condition after surgery. Hodgkinson was killed in a shootout with police. The FBI is investigating his social media presence, motives, and potential motivations, and is searching his home and looking into his whereabouts and associates. Capitol Police said one officer was in good condition after an ankle shot and another was treated and released with a minor injury. Congresswoman Claudia Tenney received a threatening email with the subject “One down, 216 to go...,” which her office alerted Capitol Police about.

The passage provides guidance for using the ADS7828, noting that its SAR architecture is sensitive to glitches or sudden changes on power supply, reference, ground connections, and digital inputs near output latching. Henry Grivi petitioned for a writ of mandate to compel the Superior Court of Los Angeles County to strike from its files, especially from the records in McAdoo v. McAdoo, a document titled “Report of Presiding Judge.” The report stemmed from an ex parte investigation conducted after Mrs. McAdoo filed a divorce complaint on July 17, 1934, when Judge Campbell tried the case and granted an interlocutory decree. The defendant moved to strike the report, and the motion was denied on August 6, 1934; the defendant then appealed.

The respondents argued the proceeding was a collateral attack and that the presiding judge had jurisdiction to file the report. The court held that mandamus could not be used to correct errors or avoid the effect of a court order, and therefore limited review to whether the judge had jurisdiction to file the report. The court concluded the report had nothing to do with issues in the divorce case and that, despite possible administrative or disciplinary purposes, the report was the result of an investigation without notice and lacked jurisdiction to be spread upon the divorce records. The peremptory writ was ordered to issue.

The passage describes improvements to packet processing in Software Defined Networking (SDN) using a reconfigurable match table (RMT) architecture. It proposes a packet processing pipeline for hardware switches that includes an ingress pipeline and an egress pipeline, each with a parser, match-action unit (MAU), and deparser. The parser splits packet header data from payload and determines which header fields may be processed by the MAU. It stores fields that may be processed in a primary packet header vector (PPHV) and the remaining fields in a secondary packet header vector (SPHV). The PPHV is delivered to the MAU for matching against match tables and applying actions, while the SPHV bypasses the MAU and is delivered directly to the deparser. The deparser reassembles the packet using processed header data from the MAU, unprocessed header data from the SPHV, and the payload. Configuration is generated in the control plane by a compiler and distributed via a configurator to program the parser and MAU. The passage also explains how separating participating from non-participating fields can improve efficiency by avoiding unnecessary MAU resource use and enabling deeper packet parsing without increasing data sent to the MAU.

The passage describes an assay for cancer detection using cfDNA fragments and targeted capture of genomic regions with cancer-specific DNA methylation patterns. It provides background on why whole-genome bisulfite sequencing is limited for product assays and summarizes methods for designing and making targeted “bait set” panels using oligonucleotide probes that are complementary to sequences containing differentially methylated CpG sites, including rules for probe length, number, off-target limits, and overlap design (e.g., 2× tiling). It also outlines criteria for identifying differentially methylated CpG sites and genomic regions based on counts of anomalously methylated cfDNA fragments and associated statistical measures (e.g., p-value rarity). Additional methods include enriching (with hybridization capture or alternative probe-based approaches), processing cfDNA by converting unmethylated cytosines to uracil, sequencing enriched fragments, and using classifiers to determine cancer presence/absence, cancer stage, or cancer type, with example performance metrics and cancer-type lists. The passage further includes procedures for developing bait sets/panels, training classification models using hypomethylated/hypermethylated fragment feature vectors, and optionally administering an anti-cancer agent.

The lecture reviews properties of Poisson processes, including their characterization by arrival epochs, IID exponentially distributed interarrival times, memorylessness, and the equivalence of viewing the process via interarrival times, arrival epochs, or the counting process \(N(t)\). It discusses stationary and independent increments, derives the Poisson PMF for \(N(t)\), and presents alternate equivalent definitions using small-increment (increment) conditions. The lecture then covers combining independent Poisson processes (the sum of two independent Poisson counting processes is Poisson with summed rates) and splitting a Poisson process using an independent Bernoulli “shuffling” of each arrival into two streams, yielding two independent Poisson processes with appropriate rates. It extends these ideas to non-homogeneous Poisson processes, noting that counting-process formulas still work with the average rate over intervals. Finally, it examines arrival times conditional on \(N(t)\), showing that arrival epochs are uniformly distributed over the interval and deriving conditional joint densities using order-statistics arguments; it ends by discussing a paradox about waiting time for the next arrival versus the mean interarrival time.

Fifth Third Bank announced a $10.9 billion all-stock acquisition of Comerica, one of the largest recent regional bank mergers. The deal, approved by both boards and pending regulatory clearance, will create the ninth-largest U.S. lender with combined assets of about $288 billion. Comerica shareholders will receive just under 1.9 Fifth Third shares per share (about $82.88) with a 20% premium, and three Comerica board members will join Fifth Third’s leadership after completion. The merger is expected to close in early 2026 and is set to expand Fifth Third’s presence across Sunbelt states while strengthening its commercial payments and wealth management businesses. The announcement comes amid anticipated regulatory changes under the Trump administration, and investors reacted positively, with Fifth Third shares rising 1.4%. Critics warn that increased consolidation could raise systemic risks.

The passage describes E-mini S&P 500 futures as CME-listed financial derivatives that represent a contract to buy or sell a specified amount of the S&P 500 index on a future date at a pre-agreed price. The passage discusses hockey goalies and playoff preparation, describing how experienced goalies and their teams expect strong performance. The passage explains the buy-and-hold strategy as a passive long-term investing approach in which investors buy stocks (or ETFs/mutual funds) and hold them for many years or decades, selling only small portions when money is needed. Poland will invest 20 billion zlotys ($5.5 billion) to connect its national fuel pipeline system with NATO’s Central Europe Pipeline System (CEPS). The plan includes extending infrastructure by about 300 kilometres and adding storage facilities for alliance logistics, with NATO committed 60 million zlotys to support planning and design and construction expected to take several years. Once completed, the link will integrate Poland into a transnational pipeline network across Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands to support more flexible and secure European supply chains for NATO forces. The government frames the investment as essential for national defence and alliance security, though officials note risks from cross-country coordination, standards, regulatory compliance, and potential cost increases from delays.

The passage describes malnutrition—especially undernutrition, wasting, and stunting—as resulting from abnormal or inadequate food intake, increasing children’s susceptibility to disease and death. WHO links stunting to low socioeconomic status, poor feeding practices, poor maternal nutrition and health, and early childhood illness. The passage reports global prevalence in 2019 (47.0 million wasted and 144.0 million stunted children under five), notes South Asia’s highest counts, and states that undernutrition-related death rates are higher in low- to middle-income countries.  

It then presents a multicenter cross-sectional study in southern Punjab, Pakistan, at Community Management of Acute Malnutrition centers supervised by Pakistan’s health department. The study enrolled 185 children aged 6–59 months with severe wasting or stunting based on WHO anthropometric indices, collected baseline information via parent interviews using a structured questionnaire, and assessed breastfeeding, complementary feeding, immunization, and medical history. Anthropometric measurements were taken by qualified supervisors, and z-scores were calculated using WHO Child Growth Standards. Dependent variables included wasting, stunting, and undernutrition; independent variables included sociodemographic, medical, and dietary factors. Data were analyzed with SPSS using t-tests and multivariate linear regression.  

Results included associations between wasting and family monthly income and complementary feeding practices, stunting and TB contact history and exclusive breastfeeding practices, and undernutrition and monthly income and exclusive breastfeeding practices. The conclusion states that wasting, stunting, and undernutrition are associated with exclusive breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices, household size, family earning, and history of infections, and recommends coordinated efforts and alertness in child nutrition programs.

The passage describes frequency constraints for PLLs, SYSCLKs, and module clocks, including that the PLL_USB must be fixed at 960 MHz when USB is used. It discusses interrupt controller capabilities for the ARM Cortex-A8 (up to 128 requests, programmable priority) and the C674x DSP interrupt controller (up to 128 device events combined into 12 prioritized interrupts, with optional multiplexing via control registers). The passage also covers DCAN/MDIO/GPIO/GPMC/ELM, HDMI and HDVPSS interface features and PCB/layout guidelines, and extensive DDR2/DDR3 memory controller and PCB routing/termination/bypass-capacitor guidance, including keepout regions and compatible JEDEC device configurations.

The passage discusses a person’s calm demeanor through good and bad situations, noting that he may seem intense initially but also jokes and knows when to be intense or have fun. It mentions possible prior experiences, including playing in or coming from places such as the University of Michigan, North Dakota, or Hershey, and emphasizes learning consistency and the effort required for both players and teams. The passage explains the value of design patterns in distributed systems, emphasizing learning from others’ mistakes, using a shared vocabulary, and building reusable components. It focuses on single-node patterns using containers, especially the sidecar pattern, where a sidecar container augments an application container by sharing resources like filesystem and namespaces. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service using an nginx sidecar, and synchronizing configuration via a sidecar that updates files through an API. It also discusses the modularity and reuse goals for sidecars, and how to design them through parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation. The passage then introduces other single-node patterns such as the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions (e.g., sharded services, service brokering, and request splitting for experiments), and the adapter pattern for normalizing interfaces for monitoring and logging (e.g., Prometheus exporters, fluentd, and health check adapters). Finally, it contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns, introducing microservices and replicated load-balanced services with readiness probes, session tracking, caching via sidecars and additional replicated tiers, SSL termination, and an overview of sharded services and sharded caching, including the role of sharding functions defined via hashing and modulo.

The passage describes the Death Cross in trading as a widely cited phenomenon involving two moving averages, usually the 50-day (short) and 200-day (long). A Death Cross forms when the 50-day moving average crosses below the 200-day moving average, and it is treated as a trading signal that can indicate short-term weakness and attract media attention. The passage reports backtests on the S&P 500 (daily bars, exits 10 to 200 days after the signal) showing lower returns than random in the short term (less than 30 days), but positive returns on average for periods longer than 30 days. It also states that combining Death Cross and Golden Cross signals can reduce time in the market and drawdowns, with a strategy of buying Golden Crosses and exiting at the next Death Cross producing a reported CAGR of about 7% and lower drawdowns. The passage concludes that the Death Cross has value mainly as a defensive, short-run indicator and cautions that it is a lagging indicator that can lead to premature exits and missed opportunities in bull markets.

Northern Oil & Gas refinanced its 8.125% unsecured notes due March 2028 and issued new 2033 notes. Its annual interest costs are roughly unchanged, and its hedges are structured so a rebound to $70s oil in 2027 would be better than a rebound to $70s oil in 2026. The passage also states that weak near-term oil prices improve the odds of $70+ oil in 2027, and includes promotional and author information about Distressed Value Investing and Elephant Analytics.

Millennials and Gen Z are seeking to enter the housing market, but real estate expert Amir Korangy says homeownership may not be right for everyone. He argues that renting can be cheaper and can offer a more comfortable space, noting that hidden costs of ownership—such as insurance, repairs, property taxes, HOA fees, and upkeep—can add to mortgage payments. Korangy also says building home equity may not be what it used to be, citing recent equity losses and describing the current situation as a long-term market correction. He adds that renting provides flexibility, allowing people to leave if circumstances change, and concludes that not everyone should be an owner.

The speaker discusses playing in loud, passionate hockey arenas, especially in Canada during the finals, and says teams should stick to their game, avoid getting down early, and not let the crowd influence the other team. They praise the goalie’s performance in the previous game, noting no goals appeared to be a goaltending issue. They emphasize the stakes for players’ careers and the importance of respecting the opportunity, with both young and older players playing hard. The speaker expects similar intense environments in hockey towns like Montreal and Buffalo and says teams should embrace and enjoy the emotion in the arena.

The passage describes continuation priority for a medical-device application focused on systems, devices, and methods for delivering neural modulation. It outlines implantable neurostimulation systems (e.g., SCS/DBS/PNS/FES) using an implantable pulse generator and electrode leads, with programming controlled by stimulation parameters covering spatial, temporal, and informational aspects of pulse patterns. It proposes using machine learning and closed-loop, search-based methods to evaluate candidate neuromodulation parameter sets—using patient, clinician, and automatic inputs (including subjective scores and sensor data)—to identify optimal parameter sets and program a neuromodulator. Examples list possible patient inputs (e.g., VAS, NRS), clinician inputs (selected parameter sets/dimensions), and automatic inputs (e.g., accelerometer activity, heart rate/variability, implantable pulse generator field potentials), along with search methods such as sorting algorithms, gradient descent, and sensitivity analysis with regression models. The passage also describes spinal cord anatomy and pain-gate concepts, discusses paresthesia versus sub-perception stimulation, and explains device/system architecture and trial-to-permanent therapy workflow. It further describes managing wash-in/wash-out timing, using objective and subjective pain/comfort metrics, and varying stimulation programs over time to address neurological conditioning, alongside additional implementation details and example figure descriptions.

The passage describes timing and performance limits for SD memory card commands and data transfer, including a tuning sequence for CMD19 (40 executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time) and UHS-I/UHS-II physical layer behaviors. It explains host/card state behavior for operations such as block read and write, aborting with CMD12, buffering and BUSY handling (DAT0 low), and restrictions during programming and erase/discard/FULE sequences, including command ordering rules, busy timeouts (e.g., 250 ms per DISCARD and 1 second per FULE), and effects of deselection/reselection (CMD7) and reset (CMD0/CMD15). It further covers card identification and switching functions (CMD55/APP_CMD, CMD6 switch function), command system reservation, CRC mechanisms (CRC7 for commands/responses and CRC16 for data), and command timeouts for read and write operations (e.g., read timeout using TAAC/NSAC-based typical access timing or 100 ms, and write timeout using R2W_FACTOR-based timing or 250 ms). The passage also details lock/unlock features using CMD42, including password-based locking, Force Erase behaviors, and Card Ownership Protection (COP) modes, along with required command sequences and related errors.

In *Jack E. Scordley et al., Doing Business as Don Pallini Dance Studio, Respondents v. Leon Olsher, Appellant* (May 21, 1959), the court found the contract’s five-day written notice requirement was not proven by the plaintiffs. Therefore, the plaintiffs did not establish a prima facie case and were not entitled to recovery. The judgment was reversed, with $30 costs, and judgment was directed for the defendant with costs. Concurred by Hoestadter, J. P., Hecht, and Aurelio.

The passage says the Apple Watch Series 10 in rose gold with GPS and cellular data is priced at its lowest level yet. It describes Series 10 improvements over the previous generation, including a bigger and brighter display with better off-angle viewing, a slimmer and lighter design, new water features such as a temperature sensor and tides app, and faster charging that fully charges the watch in about 20 minutes. It notes battery life is similar to Series 9, and that Series 11 adds features like better battery and the return of a blood oxygen sensor, but cellular shoppers can save money with the Series 10.

Southwest Airlines’ frequent, short flights and frequent takeoffs and landings are described as increasing wear and tear on aircraft parts, including engines, as investigators continue after last week’s deadly engine failure on Flight 1380 that killed 43-year-old Jennifer Riordan. The NTSB said a snapped fan blade showed signs of metal fatigue. Aviation safety experts interviewed say they do not consider Southwest unsafe, noting its long safety record and large 737 fleet. It also states Southwest has paid millions in FAA-related penalties over skipped or improper inspections and repairs, and it describes Southwest actions after the accident, including promised inspections of fan blades and letters offering passengers $5,000 and travel vouchers.

The speaker says they are disappointed and frustrated because the situation is beyond their control and is due to the league’s decision. They wish it could have been deferred to next season, since they wanted to compete on Thursday. The incident involved pushing someone out of the way at the split second, but the person was hit in the mouth; the speaker says it was not intentional injury. The passage summarizes interviews from The Washington Post’s “Of America” series, where reporters across the U.S. ask Americans what patriotism means amid a divided country. Several interviewees link patriotism to citizenship, supporting the military, and participating in public events like Fourth of July parades. Jane Pettinger, a college professor who protests, says patriotism includes serving the country and defending democracy, and she hopes Americans will protest on July 4. Dave Richardson, a retired Navy veteran, defines patriotism through pride in family service, honoring patriotic traditions, and supporting troops, while criticizing kneeling during the national anthem. Naghem Swade, a Denver Public Library employee and organizer for naturalization, connects patriotism to helping others and upholding shared values. Rudy Gomez and Scott Carlton, owners of a Louisiana restaurant that stopped showing NFL games after anthem kneeling protests, describe patriotism as being proud to be American and say they believe Trump restores patriotic feelings, though they later allow local games. Harry Russell, in Vermont, says patriotism is loving one’s country through local community involvement despite national politics. Lytia S. Brock, in Pennsylvania, portrays patriotism as protesting racial injustice and says she struggles to feel proud as Black Americans face ongoing harm and unequal safety.

Republic of Ireland internationals Greg Cunningham and Alan Browne helped Preston keep within three points of the Championship playoff places with a 2-1 win over Hull at Deepdale. Hull scored through Jarrod Bowen, but Cunningham equalised and Browne’s penalty before half-time secured the victory. Derby beat 10-man Brentford 3-0 as Tom Huddlestone scored and set up goals, while Aston Villa moved third after a 3-2 win against Burton, including goals by Scott Hogan and Albert Adomah and a late strike by Jack Grealish. Cardiff won 4-1 at 10-man Leeds, Fulham beat Nottingham Forest 2-0, Sunderland lost 2-0 to Ipswich, and Birmingham beat Sheffield Wednesday 3-1. QPR beat Barnsley 1-0, Norwich beat Middlesbrough 1-0, and Millwall won 2-0 at Reading.

Внедрение RFID в ритейле в 2000-х годах столкнулось с высокими затратами, технической незрелостью стандартов и проблемами интеграции, но цифровая трансформация создала предпосылки для «ренессанса» технологии. Описано, что RFID обеспечивает автоматическую идентификацию и сбор данных о поведении потребителей и движении товаров в реальном времени, включая точную инвентаризацию и автоматизацию процессов на складе. Рассматриваются возможности снижения потерь, улучшения клиентского опыта (например, умные примерочные), а также архитектура RFID-системы с подсистемой идентификации и корпоративной подсистемой для обработки данных. Далее приводятся обзор исследований по применению RFID в ритейле и других сферах, предлагается подход к оценке эффективности через систему сбалансированных показателей (ROI, снижение потерь и затрат, рост продаж и улучшение клиентских метрик). Также описаны архитектуры сбора и обработки данных (ETL, этапы очистки и преобразования, промежуточное и основное хранилища, многомерный куб), логические модели витрин данных для объединения POS- и RFID-информации и концептуальная схема интеграции данных для анализа пути клиента. В заключении отмечается, что разработанный подход позволяет связывать паттерны перемещения по магазину с покупками и повышает операционную эффективность, продажи и лояльность клиентов.

The passage is a transcript header for a Dell Technologies investor relations shareholder/analyst call on October 7, 2025. It lists participants, begins with Vice President of Investor Relations Paul Frantz welcoming attendees to the 2025 Dell Technologies Securities Analyst Meeting, and provides Regulation G and safe harbor disclosures noting that references are to non-GAAP financial measures unless otherwise specified, with reconciliations to GAAP measures available in meeting materials and SEC filings. The passage describes a message by Wm. P. Lord to open a legislative session, expressing sorrow over the unexpected death of Dr. Amancio Alcorta, the minister of foreign affairs. It states that the Republic is at peace with sovereign states, that boundary issues are settled or being handled through established conventions, and that arbitration treaties and participation in an international congress support its foreign policy of friendly settlements. It includes: (1) business and segment information (automotive; energy generation and storage) and discussion of impacts from the COVID-19 pandemic; (2) unaudited consolidated financial statements for the three and six months ended June 30, 2021, including balance sheet, statements of operations, comprehensive income, redeemable noncontrolling interests and equity, and cash flows; (3) selected notes on significant accounting policies, revenue recognition, inventory, property and equipment, accrued and long-term liabilities, equity, debt and finance leases, equity incentive plans, operating lease commitments, and legal proceedings related to the SolarCity acquisition; and (4) additional disclosures such as forward-looking statements, risk-factor references, and adoption/effects of accounting updates including ASU 2020-06 and other recent pronouncements.

Skin redness or ruddy skin in hot weather is described as a common problem, mainly linked to inflammation, with lack of sleep and stress also contributing. The passage says diet plays a major role: inflammatory foods, dehydration, and food allergies can cause redness and rashes. It recommends eating nuts and seeds with anti-inflammatory properties, alkaline vegetables for cooling and hydration, fruits and vegetables rich in enzymes and antioxidants, and whole grains for connective tissue support. It also advises avoiding alcohol and excess coffee, using herbal teas and vegetable juices to stay hydrated, and avoiding refined sugar and flour to reduce inflammation.

The passage provides PCB layout guidance: place the feedback trace as directly as possible and away from inductor EMI and noise sources, ideally on the PCB side opposite the inductor with a ground plane separating them. Place the low-value ceramic input filter capacitor close to the VIN pin, and if a feed-forward capacitor from the output to the feedback pin is used, position it close to the IC; surface-mount capacitors are recommended. External compensation components for stability should also be placed close to the IC and away from the inductor, with surface-mount components recommended. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per Ampere), and the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode should be close to reduce EMI, lead inductance/resistance, noise spikes, ringing, and resistive losses. Connect grounds of the IC, input capacitors, output capacitors, and output diode close together to a ground plane; multilayer boards may separate power and signal planes, using vias as needed, and switching current loops should be arranged to curl in the same direction to reduce radiated EMI. A dedicated power ground section (PGND) is required for high di/dt output currents, with VCC bypassed directly to power ground, MOSFET sources connected to power ground, and the output clamped with a high current Schottky diode to VCC and PGND. VREF should be bypassed to the signal portion of the ground plane, and analog circuitry should be bypassed to signal ground, with ceramics recommended for VCC and VREF.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids across the U.S. have arrested nearly 700 undocumented immigrants, increasing fear of deportation. A Chicago church led by Pastor Emma Lozano serves nearly all undocumented immigrants and refugees and has received calls from congregants asking for sanctuary space if immigration comes. The panic is driven by the case of Guadalupe Garcia de Rayos, an Arizona woman deported after a routine ICE check-in despite having no violent criminal background; Jessica, another deportation-fearing mother, has been required to check in with ICE for more than a decade due to using a fake visa. Jessica’s message to President Trump is that she is not a criminal or terrorist and does not want her family separated. Lozano says thousands have signed up to provide sanctuary, including 800 churches, but she believes more help is needed; her church has been tagged with hate speech multiple times and now has an armed guard. Jessica does not plan to seek refuge in the church, saying she would rather follow the law and check in with ICE even if it leads to deportation.

Harvard researcher Ian Wallace examined thousands of skeletons from academic collections to study the rise of knee osteoarthritis, finding it doubled in prevalence since the mid-20th century. The increase persisted even after adjusting for weight and age. Harvard professor Daniel E. Lieberman and Boston University co-author David Felson suggest arthritis is not simply “wear and tear,” and that physical inactivity may be a major factor, noting exercise may make joints more stress-resistant. While exercise may help even after arthritis begins, they say it depends on the disease stage and does not guarantee prevention. The authors conclude the changes in living today have affected arthritis risk and call for further research to identify contributing factors.

The passage is from a medRxiv preprint posted January 3, 2023, describing research on how contact network structure and population risk-tolerance regimes affect epidemic spread, using COVID-19 as an example. It models disease transmission through layered social interactions (households, classrooms, workplaces, and background community contacts) and examines differences between two hypothetical U.S. states with distinct age and household-size distributions (Florida and Texas). The authors consider scenarios where vulnerable individuals either fully participate, avoid work/school interactions, or where members of vulnerable households avoid co-worker and classmate interactions. Disease spread is simulated using a modified, discrete-time SEIR framework with symptomatic and asymptomatic states, recovery, and disease-induced mortality, with transmission and progression rates based on literature values. The work aims to assess how network layers and population structure influence infection risk and to inform public health intervention targeting.

The passage describes a study using Mendelian randomization to identify genetic evidence for drug targets associated with prostate cancer and to predict and evaluate potential drugs. Prostate cancer burden and treatment challenges are outlined, along with the use of genetic validation to improve drug target discovery. eQTLGen expression data and prostate cancer GWAS summary data from UK Biobank (discovery) and FinnGen (replication) were used in MR analyses with specific quality filters for instrumental variables. The discovery phase identified 151 genes associated with prostate cancer risk using an inverse variance weighted approach, with no evidence of pleiotropy or heterogeneity. Replication validated 12 genes. Enrichment analyses (GO/KEGG) and protein-protein interaction network construction were performed. Drug candidate prediction used DSigDB, yielding top candidates, and molecular docking using AutoDock assessed binding affinities between the top five drugs and target proteins. The study concludes that 12 genes (HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, HLA-A, PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, TRAV21) are associated with prostate cancer and warrant further validation through experimental work and clinical trials, noting limitations such as lack of environmental and lifestyle factors in the analysis.

British people own large property interests in Chile and Argentina, and both countries are described as seeking a peaceful solution to pending difficulties to relieve business depression and improve finances. The purchase of Chilean warships and resulting concern about further naval spending led to a suggestion for mutual limitation of armaments. Chilean officials hinted to British minister Mr. Lowther about disarmament; Lowther communicated this to Sir William Barrington, who proposed disarmament to Argentina, including canceling Argentine ironclad orders, but Argentina refused. British involvement is stated as nonexistent at one stage. Mr. Concha later returned to Buenos Aires and offered a more restricted proposal that no further armaments be made and both restrict to what was already ordered. The passage describes debates influenced by General Mitre’s newspaper article and commentary in Chile, along with Chile’s position that Argentina should not interfere in West coast affairs. It also states that later negotiations were conducted under British mediation by the respective ministers. Negotiations were temporarily interrupted by the death of Dr. Alcorta, and the outcome is awaited. The President’s message is described as optimistic on financial matters, discusses the debt and revenue, boundary settlement, arbitration policy, and references the army and navy and plans for colonization, with little else emphasized.

Amgen said its cholesterol-lowering shot, Repatha, prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial. Analysts said the results could help the drug reach a broader market, noting Repatha has been available since 2015 and had $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024. The article also states existing data show Repatha reduces heart attack and stroke risks in patients who already have heart problems by lowering LDL-C, and discusses analysts’ views on current low patient penetration.

The passage discusses limitations of traditional echocardiographic assessment of coronary heart disease (CHD), noting that left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) may not differ from normal individuals except in acute myocardial infarction or chronic ischemic cardiomyopathy. It describes an echocardiographic index called first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1), defined as the proportion of left ventricular volume change from aortic valve opening to peak aortic flow velocity relative to end-diastolic volume, measurable by transthoracic echocardiography. The study aims to examine the association between LVEF-1 and coronary artery stenosis severity and changes in LVEF-1 before and after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Patients undergoing coronary angiography (June 2021 to June 2023) were grouped by maximal stenosis (<50%, 50–70%, and ≥70%). The results report that LVEF-1 decreases with increasing stenosis severity, is negatively correlated with the Gensini score and BNP, and independently predicts moderate and severe coronary artery stenosis. After PCI, E/e’ decreased while GLS and LVEF-1 increased; multivariate analysis suggested Gensini score and stent diameter independently influenced changes in LVEF-1. The authors conclude that LVEF-1 is useful for assessing cardiac dysfunction due to coronary artery stenosis and for evaluating early improvement after PCI, especially in more severe stenosis.

NXP Semiconductors NV shares fell 5% on Wednesday after China’s latest warning against US trade threats reduced hopes of early approval for Qualcomm’s $44 billion acquisition of NXP. Since May 18, NXP shares had risen about 9% on reports that approval chances were “optimistic” as US-China tensions cooled, alongside a US government deal to restore ZTE Corp. Qualcomm lawyers were expected to meet Beijing antitrust regulators, but as of late Tuesday the lawyers remained at Qualcomm’s San Diego headquarters, and negotiations were described as “on hold.” The acquisition, announced in October 2016, has been approved by eight of nine required regulators, with China still pending; NXP shares fell 1.2% and Qualcomm stock was slightly up in premarket trading.

The passage links Peter Drucker’s ideas—about government being a poor manager and the rise of an “ownership society”—to later uses of related terms by David Howell and, in popular discourse, George W. Bush.
