It argues that 2017 India is not yet an ownership society because state control is large, governments still run many companies with majority control, subsidies are widespread, and the government interferes in business decisions. It then states that since 2014, the Modi government has pursued reforms to reduce the state’s role and promote “ownership” in individuals and businessmen, highlighting banking reforms, insolvency and restructuring law, reducing political interference, consolidating public sector banks, reducing some LPG and kerosene subsidies, the UDAY program for state electricity boards, and the goal of eliminating government handouts and expanding privatisation.

Researchers measured antibodies 1 month after participants received BNT162b2 or BNT162b2SA and found immune responses that were “as good as” specified comparators. In participants who previously received BNT162b2 without prior COVID-19, immune responses to the original strain 1 month after the booster were as good as 1 month after Dose 2. In similar participants, immune responses to the Beta variant 1 month after one booster dose of BNT162b2SA were as good as responses to the original strain 1 month after Dose 2 of BNT162b2. Among participants who had not previously received BNT162b2 and had no prior COVID-19, immune responses to the Beta variant 1 month after Dose 2 of BNT162b2SA were as good as responses to the original strain 1 month after Dose 2 of BNT162b2. The results were not considered likely due to chance, and medical problems were recorded during the study. Some participants had temporary lymphocyte count drops 1–3 days after Dose 1, which returned to normal by 6–8 days, and most injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were mild or moderate and resolved quickly. Serious medical problems were rare; in Phase 1, two serious problems occurred among BNT162b2 groups and researchers did not believe they were related to the vaccine. In Phase 2/3, serious problems were limited, with no serious vaccine-related problems in ages 12–15. Deaths occurred in Phase 2/3 in participants receiving BNT162b2 or placebo, but researchers did not believe deaths were caused by BNT162b2, and no participant died in Phase 3 among those who had not previously received BNT162b2 before BNT162b2SA.

Health officials reported more than 500 flu cases in the Show-Me-State last week, and experts said it is too early to determine whether it will be a bad year or an early spike. Registered Nurse Sandy Gibbons said people who develop flu symptoms such as headache, upper respiratory issues, and aches should see a doctor for medicine rather than wait. She added that antiviral medicine should be started within 72 hours of symptoms, and advised getting plenty of fluids, rest, and healthy food before returning to work, while not rushing back around others to avoid spreading illness.

The passage promotes a made-to-order school assignment writing service, stating it is convenient for receiving and delivering work on time and helps ensure high-quality “word pieces” for good grades. It says services can be accessed through the internet and that customers need to provide task details while the company creates the papers. It advises comparing personalized writing suppliers by treatments, prices, past prospect ratings, and getting quotes and contacting writers. The passage claims the company prioritizes quality, does not accept mediocrity, offers quick shipping and fast delivery so customers can submit on time, has experience in the writing niche, and emphasizes responsiveness and honesty.

The passage explains programmability and timing features of TPS7H500x-SP controllers, including fixed and programmable dead times (with PS and SP resistor settings), programmable leading edge blank time via the LEB pin, and a pulse skipping mode used to prevent minimum on-time related issues. It also describes duty cycle programmability using the DCL pin, current sense and PWM generation using the CS_ILIM and COMP pins, and current-limit behavior including cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup mode controlled by the HICC pin. Additional sections cover external fault protection via the FAULT pin and slope compensation for peak current mode control using the RSC pin, along with notes on frequency compensation component selection. The latter parts include application guidance for a synchronous push-pull converter example, thermal shutdown behavior, layout recommendations, and general device/application information and disclaimers.

The passage describes a backtest of the “Santa Claus Rally” in the NIFTY 50 from 2008 to the present. Using daily bars downloaded from Yahoo Finance, the strategy goes long at the close of the second Friday in December and exits at the close of the first trading day of the new year, aiming to capture the last two to three weeks of the year. The NIFTY 50 is described as a weighted average of the 50 largest Indian companies and as having derivatives contracts (options and futures). The backtest results reported include an average gain per trade of 1.2%, a win ratio of 71%, a profit factor of 6, and a max drawdown of 7%, which the passage concludes suggests the Santa Claus Rally in NIFTY is not a myth.

Juju Smith-Schuster and team president/owner Art Rooney II unveiled Pittsburgh’s 1978 throwback jerseys at Heinz Field. The Steelers will replace their “bumblebee” uniforms as throwbacks for at least the next two seasons to commemorate the 40-year anniversaries of Super Bowl XIII and XIV. Rooney said the uniforms are intended for current players and younger fans to connect with that time period, and noted the 2018 season marks the 10th anniversary of Super Bowl XLIII. The team will wear the throwbacks against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8, with former players Franco Harris and John Banaszak joining in the introduction of the designs.

Digital leaders emphasize transparency in data sharing and decision-making, supported by shared organizational context and cultural norms that discourage data hoarding. They believe good ideas can come from anywhere in the organization, but also recognize the need for governance controls to protect data and build trust. They encourage group-based decision-making using input from multiple parties and often use standardized APIs to enable data flow. Digital leaders also promote measurement through meaningful, data-driven goals and metrics, using structured objectives and dashboards to support real-time decisions while maintaining flexibility in how work is done. In contrast, digital laggards tend to restrict data access on a “need-to-know” basis, hoard data as a source of power, rely more on business judgment than deeper data interrogation, and struggle to ground objectives in realistic, measurable data. The passage describes how misaligned goals and culture can create organizational disconnection, while aligned data culture can improve both vertical and horizontal alignment; it also outlines four patterns organizations may start from during data transformation: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 25, 2019. The company’s Board of Directors elected Indra K. Nooyi as a director and appointed her to the Audit Committee. The filing describes her prior roles at PepsiCo and notes she has served as a director of Schlumberger Limited since April 2015. In connection with her election, she received a restricted stock unit award for 549 shares under the Company’s 1997 Stock Incentive Plan, vesting in three equal annual installments starting May 15, 2020, and entered into the company’s standard indemnification agreement. The report was signed by David A. Zapolsky.

The passage discusses the differences between stock and bond investment strategies and compares their risks and potential returns. It explains that buying stocks means buying a stake in a company, with prices that can rise or fall based on company performance, and that diversification is recommended due to the risk of losing capital. It describes bonds as lending money to an issuer with a maturity date and usually fixed interest payments, noting that bonds are generally less risky than stocks because bondholders are paid before shareholders in bankruptcy, though corporate bonds may carry credit risk in recessions. The passage argues that stocks have historically performed better, but there is no definite answer since outcomes depend on factors like time horizon, with bonds potentially mitigating losses during stock market crashes. It also covers a mixed portfolio approach (60% stocks/40% bonds) via backtesting and summarizes results as lower returns but reduced volatility and drawdowns compared to 100% stocks. Finally, it introduces the “Sell in May and go away” seasonal strategy and a related “Investing only in Winter” backtest, which did not perform as expected and included discussion of shortcomings.

The passage advises Galaxy Fold users to unfold their phones or use full-screen view to optimize their experience. It states that some offers are provided by companies that compensate The Motley Fool, which may affect how products are displayed, though product ratings are not influenced by compensation and not all offers are included. It then describes credit card offers, including the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card (unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 welcome bonus after $500 in purchases in 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, $0 annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection with a $25 deductible, with approval most likely for credit scores of 670+). It also references the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card (unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% cash back on certain travel booked through Capital One Travel, a limited-time welcome offer, $0 annual fee and no foreign transaction fees, and 0% intro APR for 15 months with a variable APR afterward, along with related terms). The passage includes standard approval disclaimers, recommended credit score ranges, and general information about Motley Fool Money’s purpose and editorial independence, plus mentions advertising partners.

The passage describes a patent application continuation, incorporating related applications by reference, and discloses muscle targeting compositions and systems using recombinant AAV vectors. It explains background limitations of conventional rAAV capsids, which often target liver and require large doses that can cause liver toxicity and pose manufacturing challenges. The summary portion describes engineered compositions that include a targeting moiety with an n-mer motif (including RGD or non-RGD motifs) associated with a cargo. Example embodiments specify possible n-mer motifs (by SEQ ID ranges), targeting moiety types (including viral capsid proteins), and insertion positions within AAV capsid proteins (e.g., AAV9 and analogous positions in multiple AAV serotypes). The cargo can treat or prevent muscle diseases/disorders such as autoimmune disease, cancers, muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, viral and progeroid diseases, and glycogen storage diseases, and can include gene-modifying cargos such as morpholinos, antisense oligonucleotides, CRISPR-Cas components, or mini-/micro-dystrophin genes with listed repeat structures and optional domains. The passage also outlines vector systems encoding the targeting motifs and optionally cargo, and describes producing polypeptides and viral particles with muscle-specific tropism. It includes additional claims relating to cells, pharmaceutical formulations, and methods of administering the compositions to a subject with a muscle disease/disorder, and provides an extensive overview and brief description of drawings showing AAV transduction mechanisms, selection experiments, and comparisons of engineered variants across tissues and species.

European stocks rose on Monday, led largely by gains in banks, though trading volumes were expected to be thin due to New Year’s holidays. The Stoxx Europe 600 index rose 0.5% to 363.26 after closing 1.2% lower for 2016, and the Stoxx Europe 600 Bank sector rose 0.7% in early trade. Italian banks gained following reports that Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena will issue €15 billion of debt in 2017 as part of a government taxpayer-backed rescue plan; Jens Weidmann cautioned the bank must be put on sound footing without breaching EU state aid rules. National indexes rose, including Italy’s FTSE MIB and Germany’s DAX. Eurozone manufacturing PMI data were set for release Monday, with eurozone inflation later in the week.

The passage describes a study assessing whether circulating indole 3-acetate (3-IAA) predicts chemotherapy response and overall survival in 124 people with borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from the NORPACT2 cohort. 3-IAA was measured in blood before chemotherapy, using targeted LC-MS/MS. The study reported that pre-treatment serum 3-IAA was positively correlated with age but not with tumor diameter or CA19-9, and there were no statistically significant differences in 3-IAA by CT response or CA19-9 decline. Although 3-IAA was numerically higher in some subgroups, it was not significantly associated with one-year survival or overall survival in Kaplan-Meier or Cox models, including after adjustment for age, ECOG performance status, CA19-9, and tumor classification. The authors conclude that serum 3-IAA was not associated with chemotherapy response or overall survival in this non-metastatic PDAC population, suggesting prior findings in metastatic PDAC may not extend here.

The passage is from Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 31, 2020. It includes the index and financial statements (income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, cash flows, and stockholders’ equity) and summarizes results for the three and six months ended December 31, 2020 and 2019, including revenue, net income, and earnings per share. It also provides notes describing accounting policies, earnings per share calculations, other income (expense), investments and fair value measurement, derivatives and hedging, inventories, business combinations (including the planned acquisition of ZeniMax Media Inc.), goodwill and intangible assets, debt, income taxes, unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, accumulated other comprehensive income, share repurchases and dividends, and segment information and geographic data. The report includes an independent registered public accounting firm review opinion and management’s discussion and analysis, which provides an overview, discusses forward-looking statements, segment reporting, and highlights and trends for the second quarter of fiscal year 2021 compared with fiscal year 2020.

A Michigan family in Dearborn Heights says their five-year-old son reported that two teachers repeatedly taped his mouth shut and threw out his lunch, preventing him from eating as many as 10 times. The child has not returned to Highview Elementary since the latest incident on March 26. The parents filed a police report and plan to sue the school district. The family’s lawyer said one teacher has been removed and a substitute teaching assistant was also removed the day of the last incident. The superintendent said the district has “no knowledge of” other times the boy’s mouth was taped and that the district disputes that abuse occurred before March 26; police are investigating. The mother said her son will not return until the other accused teacher is fired.

Researchers at McGill University and the University of Toronto propose a new model of gaslighting as a learning process involving brain prediction and surprise, rather than an outdated psychodynamic explanation. The model suggests manipulators exploit trust and close relationships by repeatedly undermining a target’s expectations, using surprise to influence learning, and suggesting that the target’s surprise reflects a poor “grasp on reality.” The researchers say anyone could be affected if they trust the wrong person, though future work may examine whether factors like attachment styles or trauma history influence susceptibility and help validate parts of the model. The work was authored by Willis Klein, Suzanne Wood, and Jennifer A. Bartz.

The passage describes foreign policy advisory materials prepared for the Reagan transition. It notes that Tab I of Richard Allen’s binder was prepared in advance of the Board’s first meeting on November 21, 1980, with an agenda, press release, and additional attached but unprinted tabs, and that no meeting minutes were found. An October 25 Reagan-Bush Committee news release announced an interim foreign policy advisory committee to monitor international developments through January 20, 1981, listing its members. It also summarizes a December 22, 1980 Department of State national security final report volume setup, the establishment of an Office of Executive Branch Management headed by William Timmons before the inauguration, and the Department of State transition team membership. Finally, it includes an editorial note on Ronald Reagan’s November 20, 1975 statement announcing his 1976 presidential candidacy and his views on leadership, government, and foreign policy.

Builder Eric Woodward has started work on a pop-up public park for a vacant Fort Langley lot he owns, after canceling development plans due to a dispute with the Township. Woodward says the park will include community gathering spaces and family play areas such as an outdoor lounge, picnic areas, and outdoor ping pong, with major items expected to be completed by early July. Planned changes include re-turfing the site, removing concrete barriers, and moving temporary construction fencing closer to boarded-up buildings at Glover Road and Mary Avenue, previously the site of a canceled project that would have included a boutique hotel. Woodward says the park responds to complaints and criticism about the site’s long-term appearance, and notes a prior action involving painting an unoccupied Mary Avenue house bright pink and later repainting it grey. In March, Township council voted 6-2 against allowing Woodward to present his concerns at a special session.

The passage describes the use of transfer learning to address domain shift in neuroimaging, where brain scan acquisition is costly, datasets are small, and differences in imaging protocols, scanner hardware, and subject populations cause models trained on one dataset to perform poorly on another. The authors propose using deep neural network feature re-use across datasets via a pipeline based on simple fully connected neural networks (SFCNs), where models are pre-trained on UK Biobank (UKB) data and then adapted to target datasets (OASIS-3, ABIDE, IXI) through classifier training and optionally fine-tuning the feature extractor. They focus on age and sex prediction from structural MRI, define the training, loss functions, data preprocessing, and dataset splits, and report that transfer learning improves performance over direct transfer and over classical elastic net regression, particularly in small-data settings. The results also show features are task-specific, that transfer learning can outperform training from scratch and does so via feature re-use rather than mere parameter scaling, and that transfer learning can speed up convergence during training.

Teuvo Teravainen and Antoine Vermette discuss their mindset and performance leading up to and during a competitive playoff game. They emphasize staying calm, bringing their “A game,” facing adversity, and persevering in key moments. Teravainen says Finland’s supporters were excited after he scored, and he credits hard work and trusting himself, including improving skating and skills. Vermette notes the team’s need to compete with a fast, skilled opponent by focusing on puck possession, pressure, speed, positioning, and skating, and he describes Teravainen as an effective, smart player with good puck-handling and an active stick.

The NPD Group reports that Rare’s Sea of Thieves is selling faster in its first month than any other Rare game since NPD began tracking in 1995. NPD analyst Mat Piscatella says it was the second best-selling game of March and the eighth best-selling game of 2018 year-to-date, with the highest launch-month sales for any Rare title since tracking began. NPD’s figures include only retail and digital purchases, excluding Game Pass downloads. Based on dollar sales, Sea of Thieves is No. 8 for 2018 so far and is the highest platform exclusive on the list at the time. The April NPD report will include PlayStation 4’s God of War.

The passage describes how to enable and use daisy-chain mode for ADCs via the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register, including SPI frame timing for register writes and reads across N ADCs. It explains that daisy-chain length is the number of ADCs excluding ADC1, gives examples (e.g., DAISY_CHAIN_LEN = 3 in a chain of four ADCs), and outlines steps for register reads using SPI_RD_EN and specific SPI frame patterns. The passage also includes additional information about register field meanings and general device/application details for the ADS9803, such as its accuracy basis (TUE), bandwidth modes, power supplies, and board layout/power decoupling recommendations.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as 10-year Treasury yields reached 3 percent for the first time in four years, raising concerns about higher borrowing costs and as quarterly results did not provide positive outlooks. The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq declined, with technology and industrial stocks weighing, including Alphabet, Facebook, 3M and Caterpillar. Companies cited included Alphabet, which fell after rising expenses and shrinking margins; Caterpillar, down on fears of higher steel prices despite beating earnings; and 3M, down after inline profits and a lowered 2018 earnings forecast. Apple fell amid worries about softening high-end smartphone demand, while Lockheed Martin declined despite better-than-expected earnings. Economic data showed consumer confidence rebounded in April. Oil rose above $75 a barrel before easing after U.S. and French leaders pledged to try to resolve differences on Iran. Decliners outnumbered advancers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, and trading volume was 7.22 billion shares.

The passage describes a study that develops an artificial intelligence model to classify citation intents in Turkish academic texts. It notes that traditional citation metrics ignore the context and purpose of citations and aims to fill a gap in Turkish citation intent classification by creating the first large-scale, publicly available dataset for this task in Computer Science, containing 2,650 annotated citation sentences extracted from 723 articles. The study uses a five-category intent scheme (Background, Basis, Support, Differ, Discuss), a human annotation process with AI-assisted labeling, and benchmarking with large language models (GPT-4o and Gemini) using In-Context Learning (ICL). It improves performance through automated prompt optimization with DSPy (reaching 86.5% accuracy) and then increases robustness using a stacked ensemble meta-model (XGBoost), achieving 91.3% accuracy. The results discuss challenges including class imbalance, difficulty distinguishing semantically close categories, and inconsistent model outputs, and it outlines future directions such as addressing imbalance, augmenting rare classes, and adding more contextual features.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 27, 2018. The company entered into an amended and restated credit agreement with Bank of America, N.A. and other lenders, increasing its unsecured revolving credit facility borrowing capacity from $3.0 billion to $7.0 billion and extending the agreement’s term to April 27, 2021. Borrowings are to be used for general corporate purposes, including backstopping notes issued under the company’s Commercial Paper Program. On the same date, the company established the Commercial Paper Program allowing issuance of unsecured commercial paper notes up to a maximum outstanding amount of $7.0 billion, with maturities not exceeding 397 days, and with amounts able to be reborrowed. Exhibit 10.1 is the amended and restated credit agreement dated April 27, 2018.

The passage discusses preparing for a critical hockey game, emphasizing the importance of rest, warmups, and being mentally and emotionally ready. It describes the challenge of closing out a Stanley Cup Finals series, noting that every outcome can change immediately and that teams with “no tomorrow” are harder to play. It also addresses uncertainty about a player’s skating and the decision not to worry about his availability if he cannot play effectively. The speakers stress staying even-keeled, maintaining a businesslike attitude, and focusing on the task of winning the game rather than speculating about future outcomes, while also contrasting pressure and atmosphere between playing at home and on the road.

Prof. Ross Levine and co-authors report that easier business borrowing encourages environmental responsibility. In an NBER paper, they find that when lending conditions ease—through greater credit supply and lower interest rates—businesses invest more in pollution-reducing projects, including for benefits to fines, worker health and productivity, and public reputation. Using fracking-related deposit windfalls to isolate credit effects, they examine emissions in non-gas-producing counties and find benzene levels fell 26% where credit availability increased via banks receiving fracking funds, alongside similar declines in other pollutants. They also analyze company-level EPA records and find borrowers with main lenders that received shale windfalls reduced toxic emissions more than comparable firms, and received higher environmental group ratings. Levine emphasizes the study does not assess fracking’s environmental effects directly, using fracking only to study the impact of easier credit.

The passage says Ryan Malone, a 37-year-old forward and 2010 Vancouver silver medalist, signed a 25-game tryout with the Iowa Wild to remain eligible for PyeongChang and is trying to make another Olympic team. The U.S. Olympic Committee also announced Brian Gionta, a 38-year-old forward who led the 2006 Olympic team in goals, as the lone men’s hockey player at a 100-day countdown event in Times Square on Nov. 1. It notes that Malone and Gionta have more than 1,500 NHL games between them, that Malone returned from a two-year retirement and later joined an AHL club, and that Gionta did not attend an NHL training camp but had an exploratory meeting with an AHL club. The final U.S. Olympic team of 25 players will be named around Jan. 1.

The passage discusses expectations that David Ellison, backed by his father Larry Ellison, may bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery after the Ellisons acquired Paramount earlier in the year. David Ellison declined to comment on his plans at a Bloomberg event, and the article outlines questions about how a Paramount–WBD merger could work and why it might be pursued. It suggests the combined companies could merge streaming, studios, film/TV assets, sports rights, and back-office functions, and notes that antitrust concerns might be eased by the Ellisons’ political connections. It also cites WBD’s valuation and debt and speculates that Larry Ellison and potential partners like Apollo could provide financing. The article adds that insiders expect CEO David Zaslav to try to keep WBD independent, while Ellison says he would want to “make more, not less.”

Shauna Sinfield, a single Calgary mother with multiple sclerosis on a fixed income, says her son Caden’s hockey gear was stolen in an auto theft. She estimates the missing equipment will cost $1,500 to $2,000 to replace and also needs to replace her 1998 Toyota Corolla (licence plate BLJ 2687). Police confirmed they are investigating and told her the chance of recovering the car or gear is slim, with the thieves likely having pawned or sold most of it. A GoFundMe page for her has raised $685 toward a $3,000 goal.

The passage introduces edit distance (Levenshtein distance) and its development for comparing strings, trees, and, more recently, Reeb graphs and objects in persistent homology. It then discusses the interleaving distance in topological data analysis, defining persistence modules over posets and the interleaving distance via \(\varepsilon\)-interleavings (and its equivalence to the bottleneck distance in a specific 1D setting). Building on this, the work investigates connections between edit distances and interleaving distances.

The passage defines two categories of constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules and introduces an edit distance \(d^{E}_{Ed}\) based on allowable morphisms and their distortion. It also establishes that the path components of the resulting metric space correspond to free modules \(F_d^n\). The main result stated is that for \(E \in \{JS_d,(1D)^d\}\) and constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules \(M,N\), the interleaving distance equals the edit distance: \(d_I(M,N)=d^{E}_{Ed}(M,N)\). The passage further derives consequences showing that stability under interleaving is equivalent to stability under edit distance, and compares this connection to earlier work using Galois connections.

The passage discusses a playoff series in which the games have become tougher. It emphasizes adjusting to officiating early in games, working through difficult stretches, keeping up efforts through shifts and penalty killing, and sticking to the team’s game plan. It notes that Detroit is playing well and that success depends on strong defense. The speaker also expresses strong confidence and enjoyment playing at home, highlighting the energy of the fans, and mentions relying on good defensive play through periods when bounces do not go the team’s way.

The passage describes how the CS_ILIM pin is driven by a signal representing transformer primary-side current for peak current mode PWM control. It explains that COMP pin voltage sets the reference peak current, that primary signals are switched on by an internal clock and turned off when sensed peak current reaches COMP/2 (with a 150 mV offset in the PWM comparator), and that CS_ILIM is also used to configure current limit via a sense resistor connected to AVSS. It further details hiccup mode operation: when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting occurs and a CHICC capacitor timing delay determines how long switching is delayed; switching then stops until restart based on HICC voltage thresholds. The passage also covers external FAULT protection behavior, including fault shutdown when FAULT exceeds 0.6 V for a specified pulse width, a delay period after the fault clears, and restarting if the threshold is exceeded during the delay. Finally, it discusses slope compensation for stability in peak current mode control, including minimum and recommended slope compensation values and how to set it with the RSC pin, as well as related compensation selection considerations.

The speaker says the team had opportunities in the third period and played well late in the game, but a mediocre second period with lapses cost them the game. They note the referees allowed play and that both goaltenders played well, keeping their teams competitive. They say they need to be consistent for sixty minutes, work harder to create scoring chances, and bear down more strongly on the net. The team is going home after a tough playoff game but intends to stay encouraged and build on recent home performance for the next game.

The passage highlights five top posts celebrating open source, including a look at DomTerm’s browser-engine-based terminal features, an article on how an MIT print jam fix influenced software development models, an explanation of what container runtimes mean, and a history of how Christine Peterson coined the term “open source software” in 1998 and its reception. It also describes an Ontario middle school teacher’s Tech Stewardship program that, using Linux and open source, has kept more than 200 old computers running, and thanks community members for supporting Opensource.com.

A 4th-grade student in Grand Haven, Michigan, Lexi Bergeron, sells handmade “stretchy straw fidgeters” to help classmates get hot lunches. Inspired by reports about students unable to afford lunches, she learned some classmates only received cheese sandwiches due to lunch account debt. Lexi began making fidget strings for $1 and earned $11 in her first week. Her mother created a GoFundMe page aiming to raise $188 to pay off Ferry Elementary’s lunch debt; the effort exceeded expectations, and they now hope to raise $2,200 by the end of December to wipe out all lunch debts in the district.

The paper advocates a sociocultural, ecological perspective on foreign language education policy and practice in Asia, focusing on discrepancies between policy intentions and educational outcomes where English is compulsory. It argues that learning cannot be understood separately from the social worlds learners and teachers inhabit, including classrooms, schools, and broader social and cultural contexts. The article discusses research and examples showing how sociocultural factors shape English learning, including inequality of achievement and constraints on teachers’ ability to implement communicative approaches under mandated curricula. It reviews policy targets based on CEFR frameworks in Malaysia and Thailand, teachers’ English proficiency concerns, and classroom-level challenges reported by teachers, such as large classes, limited resources, and tensions between English use and societal language identities. The conclusion argues that unrealistic proficiency targets are self-defeating in contexts where English is not part of learners’ everyday sociolinguistic reality, and that policymakers should align curriculum outcomes with system capacity by taking contextual realities into account.

Researchers reported that bacteria naturally found on grape plant leaves can degrade guaiacol, a volatile phenol responsible for smoke taint in wine. The team collected leaves from chardonnay and cabernet sauvignon vines, identified two bacterial strains that degraded guaiacol in guaiacol-only conditions, and found that removing the gene responsible prevented degradation. While current mitigation methods like activated charcoal can remove desirable wine components, the microbial approach may be more specific. The researchers cautioned that guaiacol is only one of several compounds that cause smoke taint, and additional work is needed to explore the grape plant microbiome for other volatile phenols.

The passage describes why *Plasmodium vivax* and *P. ovale* can relapse after lying dormant in liver cells as hypnozoites, and notes that preventing relapse requires 8-aminoquinoline “radical cure,” which can be harmful in G6PD deficiency. It states that hypnozoite activation biology is not well understood and that relapse timing varies between short-latency (“tropical”) and long-latency (“temperate”) *P. vivax* types, potentially driven by intrinsic and/or external triggers. A mathematical “exponential clock” model is presented as a base model where each hypnozoite activates independently at a constant rate with no external triggers, leading to an exponentially distributed time to relapse. The work derives analytical likelihoods for this model, fits it to longitudinal vivax infection data from the SPf66 falciparum vaccine trial in Thailand (1344 children followed daily for 21 months), and finds that the model captures recurrent vivax infection patterns and supports features compatible with external triggering. The passage then outlines how, in the exponential clock model, relapse rate relates linearly to hypnozoite burden and how model components incorporate variability in biting, sporozoite inoculum size, and infection “destiny,” as well as age-dependent immunity masking symptomatic disease. It reports fitted estimates for hypnozoite activation rate, hypnozoite carriage half-life, sporozoite inoculum sizes, and the relapse-to-primary ratio in the cohort.

A school safety conference by the Department of Education this month will address concerns including drugs, violence, suicide, bullying, harassment, and sexual identity. The goal is to support school personnel with strategies and workshops for safe school practices. The DOE deputy superintendent said safety issues, especially drugs and alcohol, have been increasing, citing 352 cases of illegal drug use or possession on school campuses in 2015-2016 and noting last year’s data is still being compiled. The department has shifted toward treatment for drug offenses, including group therapy, and the conference will focus on law enforcement impact, legal issues, building a positive school climate, reducing drugs and alcohol use, and responding to crisis and mental health. The event begins June 26 at Okkodo High School with about 400 support staff; more information is available by calling 300-1623.

The passage says investors are speculating that the Czech National Bank may scrap the cap keeping the euro above 27 Czech crowns after the bank ended its weak-crown commitment. It warns a sharp currency spike could have major economic fallout, though the meeting is not scheduled for monetary policy. In Britain, the ONS is assessing how to determine recession earlier, noting past underestimation of the 2008 downturn despite generally unrevised growth data since the 2016 Brexit vote. It also reports markets saw sharp intraday swings, influenced by rising oil prices, U.S. jobs data, Fed meeting minutes about high valuations and balance sheet reduction, concerns over U.S. tax reform timing, and caution ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. Wall St ended slightly lower, Treasury yields and the dollar fell, and European markets were expected to open lower with attention on German industrial orders and upcoming ECB speakers, including Mario Draghi.

Jack Wilshere has reportedly met West Ham United boss Manuel Pellegrini to discuss a possible move to West Ham after announcing he will leave Arsenal this summer due to a limited role under Unai Emery. West Ham are considered leading the race for Wilshere, though other clubs, including Fenerbahce, are also reported to be interested with a large offer. It is understood West Ham may not be able to match the money, but Wilshere’s family is settled in London and he may value remaining in the Premier League to stay in Gareth Southgate’s plans for England. The report says Wilshere is deciding on his next move, with his future still unclear.

The passage is largely composed of NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q materials for the quarterly period ended October 27, 2019, including financial statements and notes. It provides condensed consolidated income, comprehensive income, balance sheets, statements of shareholders’ equity, and cash flows for three and nine months ended October 27, 2019 and October 28, 2018. Key figures include revenue of $3,014 million (three months ended October 27, 2019) and $7,813 million (nine months ended October 27, 2019), net income of $899 million and $1,845 million, and total assets of $15,810 million as of October 27, 2019. Notes describe significant accounting policies, lease accounting adoption and lease obligations, stock-based compensation, net income per share, income taxes, marketable securities and fair value disclosures, derivative financial instruments, debt terms and credit facilities, commitments and contingencies (including litigation), shareholders’ equity and capital return program, and segment information for the GPU and Tegra Processor businesses. The document also includes management’s discussion of financial results, liquidity and capital resources, and forward-looking statements, along with a discussion of the Mellanox acquisition and related developments.

Higher education leaders, advocates, and officials said they left the Education Department’s first round of talks on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with cautious optimism, despite the government shutdown. Negotiations over new student loan repayment plans and which programs qualify for higher loan caps concluded Friday and will resume in November as part of negotiated rule making, with many provisions taking effect July 1, 2026.

The most contentious issue was defining which postbaccalaureate programs qualify as “professional.” Initially, department officials said the definition would include only 10 programs listed in the Higher Education Act, but after committee members raised concerns, ED proposed a one-year expansion (July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027) that would include programs meeting specified standards if the college had designated them as professional before July 4, 2025. Committee members remained divided and no unanimous agreement was reached; ED plans another round of talks Nov. 3 to Nov. 7, and if consensus is not reached, the department may proceed with its own proposal subject to public comment.

Because of the shutdown, the department’s website did not post updates to the public, with officials saying documents could not be provided until the government reopened and communications staff were furloughed. The other major topic for November will be repayment plans, including changes under OBBBA that end most income-driven plans as of July 1, 2026, while detailing remaining transition questions for existing borrowers, particularly Parent PLUS borrowers facing a potentially complex process to be grandfathered into Income-Based Repayment.

In a UK Biobank cohort of 451,355 participants stratified by ethnicity-specific BMI categories (normal, overweight, obese) and diabetes mellitus (DM) status, the study assessed cardiovascular biomarkers (carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiac contractility index) and incident cardiovascular events and mortality. About 5% of participants had DM. In participants without DM, higher BMI was associated with worse cardiovascular biomarker profiles, but these BMI–biomarker relationships were diminished in the DM group. Within BMI categories, DM was associated with an adverse cardiovascular phenotype, particularly among those with normal BMI. Over 5.3 million person-years of follow-up, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and cardiovascular mortality increased across BMI categories in both DM and non-DM groups. However, normal-weight DM had higher cardiovascular mortality than obese non-DM (IRR 2.81 vs IRR 1.84). The authors conclude that obesity and DM additively relate to adverse cardiovascular biomarkers and mortality, and that adiposity metrics correlate more with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes-oriented metrics, while both correlate weakly.

The defendant is charged in a 13-count indictment with extortion-related offenses from six incidents over two months at three Chinese restaurants. The defense moves to sever counts by incident, arguing joinder is proper only under CPL 200.20 (2)(c), while the People argue joinder is proper under CPL 200.20 (2)(b). The court explains joinder standards under CPL 200.20 and discusses relevant principles from People v. Molineux, including common scheme or plan, identity, and intent. The incidents are grouped as Group A (December 14, 16, 20), Group B (January 24), and Group C (February 7, 12). The court finds that the offenses are properly joinable under CPL 200.20 (2)(b) based on evidence relating to common modus operandi and intent, and that severance will not lie. The motion to sever is denied.

The speaker advises becoming more patient and resuming their style of play in “simple hockey” by getting the puck deep, minimizing opponents’ speed through the neutral zone, and finding ways to get the puck past a player. They note shot-blocking totals and say opponents are blocking pucks and taking away shooting lanes, so the team needs to execute properly to push the puck through and create chances. They mention opponents collapse defensively, clogging the middle, and that the team should get away in the shooting lanes to reach the net and create confrontation with the defense to get the puck through. They also say they could have played better in front of him, note frustration affected their game, and hope to rebound in the next game.

Chronic kidney dysfunction is linked to increased cardiovascular mortality, and arterial stiffening—measured by pulse wave velocity (PWV)—is a marker of vascular aging. Prior studies on the relationship between arterial stiffness and kidney function have been inconsistent, and the evidence lacks bidirectional and temporal analysis. This study uses cross-sectional and longitudinal data from 67,060 general adults in China to examine associations between arterial stiffness (baPWV) and renal function decline (eGFR, microalbuminuria). In cross-sectional analyses, baPWV was negatively associated with eGFR. Longitudinally, higher baPWV predicted incident CKD, and lower eGFR was associated with higher arterial stiffness risk. Cross-lagged analysis suggested that eGFR decline preceded changes in baPWV. The authors conclude that arterial stiffness is associated with CKD and that decreasing eGFR appears to precede increased baPWV.

The passage describes a case study in one woman with a unilateral transtibial amputation in which lateral spinal cord stimulation (SCS) delivered as somatosensory feedback during overground walking was used to study muscle activity and functional outcomes. It notes that loss of somatosensory feedback contributes to impaired postural stability and increased fall risk, and that SCS can evoke sensations in missing limbs and improve balance and gait in prior work. In this study, after multiple weeks of in-lab SCS use, electromyography showed reduced co-contractions of knee antagonist muscles (vastus lateralis and biceps femoris) and increased activation of the tensor fasciae latae (TFL). Gait kinematics showed increased pelvic obliquity range-of-motion and increased pelvic drop, indicating functional improvements in hip motion and reduced knee/pelvis compensations. The authors conclude that SCS restored missing-limb sensation and, through changes in residual-limb muscle activation, improved walking-related function, with a specific pattern of reduced knee antagonist co-contraction and increased TFL activity.

Adventurer Bear Grylls criticised schools for not being fully equipped to prepare children for adult life, saying they should “empower” young people more than focus on exam scores. He argued that success often comes from determination rather than top grades, noting that he was not “very brilliant” or the sportiest at school, but could control his determination. He said his time at Eton was forward-thinking and gave him strong memories, and he described proving his determination during SAS selection. Grylls also commented on Donald Trump, saying he hopes Trump is “too busy” to join him on an adventure, and contrasted Trump’s desire to be “king” with the lesson that “you’re never the king” in the wild.

Thunderstorms with hail occurred across North Texas last weekend, but the severe weather season has started slowly. Only a few tornadoes have been reported statewide, including four in North Texas. April typically averages seven tornadoes statewide, with a high of 41 in 1994. Oklahoma, which usually averages about 12 tornadoes in April and 56 annually, has recorded zero tornadoes in 2018, with the last similar late-season situation occurring on April 26, 1962. Kansas has also had zero tornadoes so far. The passage says a slow start does not ensure the season will remain quiet, noting that tornado activity often increases in May across Oklahoma and Texas.

Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) commonly leads to permanent neurological deficits. Although MRI can provide information about injury level and quantitative lesion biomarkers (lesion length and volume), automatic identification methods for T2 hyperintense lesions are still limited, often relying on time-consuming manual segmentation with variability across raters. This study introduced SCIseg, a deep learning method that automatically segments the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in volumetric SCI MRI and produces lesion biomarkers correlated with clinical scores. The method is presented as the first open-source 3D approach for simultaneous spinal cord and lesion segmentation, reported to generalize across treatment strategies, lesion etiologies, sites, scanners, and image resolutions, and to perform for non-traumatic degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM). A retrospective cohort of 191 patients (231 scans) from three sites was used, with training performed in three phases including a human-in-the-loop active learning strategy. Models were evaluated on independent test sets from site 1 and site 2 using Dice coefficient, relative volume error, and lesion-related metrics, and compared against open-source spinal cord toolbox methods and a 2D SCIseg variant. SCIseg 3D reported stable spinal cord segmentation and improved lesion segmentation versus the 2D version, with higher performance on site 2 than site 1. Correlation analyses between discharge clinical scores and MRI-derived biomarkers showed no statistically significant differences (P > 0.05) between biomarkers computed from manual ground-truth lesion masks and those computed from SCIseg predictions.

Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said on April 17 that the Russian economy is on a positive development path, citing government estimates and confirmation from analytical agencies. He said the economy has entered a growth stage, with industrial output growing 1.3 percent at the end of last year, indicating industry recovery. Medvedev also reported positive agricultural developments, including 5 percent growth over the last year, a result of government work, and noted agriculture’s export potential. He added that agribusiness growth is producing synergetic effects, with agricultural machine-building developing and agricultural machinery production (including harvesters and tractors) rising by 60 percent.

Army & Air Force Exchange Service shopping privileges are limited to Soldiers, Airmen and their families, but anyone can dine in Exchange restaurants or pick up grab-and-go fare from Express locations. Army Regulation 215-8/Air Force Instruction 34-211 (I) allows anyone, including visitors, contractors and Department of Defense civilians, to dine in more than 1,600 Exchange restaurants worldwide. The regulation also allows anyone to buy grab-and-go food and beverages from 300-plus Express locations for consumption on the installation. Guidelines for authorized users are prescribed by Army Regulation 215-8/Air Force Instruction 34-211 (I) and the Armed Services Exchange Regulations, Department of Defense Instruction 1330.21. Those seeking full Exchange benefits should contact their local Exchange manager, and store contact information is available at shopmyexchange.com/exchange-stores/.

The passage describes a calm group mindset and an emphasis on maintaining a consistent game plan, especially in clinching games and while wearing teams down during a series. It states they will not change their routine, are mentally tough, and will move on by focusing on what they can control. The team aims to start better at home on Sunday, responding to an opponent’s strong start. It also highlights a player’s impressive performance, especially limiting second opportunities and rebounds, and notes strong collective defensive efforts, particularly on the penalty kill and against tough lines. The passage concludes by saying the opponent has been dangerous throughout the playoffs and that the team has been aggressive and forced them into unwanted plays.

The passage is an Amazon.com, Inc. Form 8-K dated July 25, 2019. It reports that Amazon announced its second quarter 2019 financial results on July 25, 2019. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1, and Exhibit 99.2 provides additional information regarding the inclusion of non-GAAP financial measures in related public disclosures. The report is signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Athletes Unlimited (AU) is described as an innovative women’s professional sports startup co-founded by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros, built around player empowerment and a new league structure. After meeting with invited softball players in 2019, the founders developed plans for a league with no team owners, a single game location, a new competition format and scoring system, and a player-led organizational structure including a player-run Player Executive Committee. AU launched its first women’s professional softball league in August 2020 and later expanded to volleyball, lacrosse, and basketball, reaching more than 200 athletes and securing broadcast and streaming partnerships with multiple networks. 

The passage explains challenges historically faced by women’s pro team sports, including underinvestment, limited media exposure, and unstable business models, and contrasts these with AU’s mission as a public benefit corporation focused on empowering athletes as leaders and change makers. AU’s model includes a Mission Equity capital structure, player decision-making on many league and team matters, player governance with no coaches but facilitators, and a leaderboard ranking individual performances to determine weekly captains and overall champions. It also describes AU’s emphasis on broadcasting and storytelling, including digital content and initiatives like “Power in My Voice,” and notes that as of early 2023 AU’s progress raised questions about future growth strategy and economic sustainability.

The passage describes a continuation patent application related to allocating resource units in wireless networks, particularly for multiple BSSID (multiple basic service set identifier) WLANs. It explains that access points (APs) in a multiple BSSID set may broadcast management frames and that stations are associated with specific BSSs, including a transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) and non-transmitted BSSIDs (non-Tx BSSIDs). The disclosure focuses on allocating random access resources for stations in a multiple BSSID set using association identifier (AID) values derived from a group AID mapping in a partial virtual bitmap of a TIM element, and sending trigger frames indicating the number of AID values. Depending on implementation, the trigger frame uses AID values (e.g., corresponding to specific BSSID indexes, zero, or 2045) to allocate random resource units (RUs) for uplink transmissions to selected BSSs, the Tx BSSID, all unassociated stations, or analogous configurations when sent from a non-Tx BSSID. The passage also discusses management frame elements (such as a multiple BSSID element and RAPS element) and provides supporting background on WLAN components, OFDMA resource unit allocation, and examples of trigger frames for dedicated versus random RU allocation.

The passage states that Grupo Supervielle S.A. published a slideshow for an event at Latin Securities Argentina in London. It also includes a note about Seeking Alpha’s transcripts team, which develops transcript-related projects and publishes thousands of quarterly earnings calls per quarter, continuing to expand coverage. The passage lists several article titles and describes a chart with one X axis for time (from 2025-09-29 09:30:00 to 2025-10-03 16:00:00) and one Y axis for values (ranging from 4.61 to 5.53).

The “Look Good … Feel Better” nonprofit aims to prevent loss of self-confidence among women receiving cancer treatment. On May 8, beauty professionals will volunteer at Dignity Health Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital Diagnostic Imaging to provide support. The program offers skincare and makeup techniques and information for coping with hair loss, including eyebrows and eyelashes, and is designed to create a supportive environment. It is free for women undergoing cancer treatment; more information is available at lookgoodfeelbetter.org, and local event registration can be done by calling 1-800-227-2345.

The CAT offense is described as a simple but successful half- and full-court strategy for attacking defenses that trap or double team, including zone presses. It uses a 2-1-2 spread alignment and sharp, accurate passing, with the middle/post position as the key spot for a highly skilled triple-threat player. Key rules include baseline back cuts when the ball is passed to the middle, post roll actions when the ball goes to baseline or corners (with caution that the post should not receive the ball turned to the basket), and an optional post interchange during a post roll. The opposite corner rule instructs skip passes to the opposite corner when a corner is trapped or when players receive double teams. Dribble penetration is recommended sparingly to get out of trouble, emphasizing drive-and-kick, keeping the ball and clock moving, and avoiding fouls.

The passage says tight ends remain an important part of football because they create major matchup problems for defenses. It describes the tight end’s responsibilities as running short-to-medium routes, providing blocking in run and pass games, serving as a red-zone target for 1-on-1 matchups, and lining up next to offensive linemen (or as an H-back). It explains that the position name comes from historical lineup terminology (“ends,” “split end,” and “tight end”). It lists typical skills (strong hands, athleticism, speed, blocking, route running, physicality) and a general body type estimate (6’3–6’8, 240–270 pounds, strong and athletic). It names Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe as among the best tight ends, and concludes that tight ends are important because they diversify offensive schemes and combine receiver-like pass-catching with size and strength.

Guangdong Province in southern China is experiencing its worst-ever chikungunya outbreak, with more than 4,000 confirmed cases reported since late July. Most infections are in Shunde District (over 3,600 cases), with additional cases in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. Chikungunya spreads through bites from Aedes mosquitoes, which also transmit dengue and Zika, and does not pass directly between people; reducing mosquito populations is presented as the most effective prevention. Local authorities are encouraging residents to eliminate standing water to reduce mosquito breeding, and the editorial links the spread to climate change, urbanization, and increased international travel. The World Health Organization is described as issuing new clinical guidelines and strengthening its Global Arbovirus Initiative to improve monitoring, prevention, and international coordination, with emphasis on expanded genomic surveillance and global collaboration. The passage also notes there is no specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine for chikungunya, and care focuses on relieving symptoms.

The passage explains how genetic contribution to phenotypes (h2SNP) and shared genetic effects (rg) can be quantified using variance components linear mixed models, but notes that simple univariate and multivariate models may be misspecified because cis-SNPs tend to have stronger effects than trans-SNPs and genetic correlation can differ across SNP sets. It states that ML/REML estimation in more general multivariate variance components models is numerically and computationally challenging, and that existing methods are limited. To address this, the authors implemented a minorization-maximization (MM) algorithm for ML and REML estimation in multivariate variance components linear mixed models in Julia, citing advantages including numerical stability, fast convergence, and adaptation to positive semidefiniteness constraints. The method is demonstrated using isoform expression in the PsychENCODE dataset, partitioning genetic variance and covariance among cis- and trans-SNPs, and finding sparse but large local effects, collectively large distal effects, substantial shared cis-SNP influences, and more genetic signals from isoform-level than gene-level analyses. Some isoform-specific signals are reported to be associated with increased risk for psychiatric disorders such as autism spectrum disorder, suggesting isoform-resolution analyses may uncover novel disease genes and aid GWAS interpretation.

Officials from the Coalition for Tobacco Control–Pakistan (CTC-Pak) urged people to prioritize health over business during World No Tobacco Day awareness activities nationwide. They said tobacco contributes to 16% of non-communicable disease (NCD) deaths, with cardiovascular diseases including heart attacks accounting for 19% of total deaths, and that other NCD deaths are largely linked to cancer and chronic respiratory diseases. They cited WHO reports that tobacco use disproportionately harms vulnerable populations, with over 80% of the world’s smokers in low- and middle-income countries, and that tobacco use costs countries $1.4 trillion per year due to health care costs and lost productivity. They also stated the tobacco epidemic kills more than seven million people annually, including 108,800 tobacco-associated deaths in Pakistan, and that tobacco is a major cause of heart attacks or strokes. The officials called for strict enforcement of Pakistan’s tobacco control laws, immediate implementation of 85% pictorial health warnings on cigarette packs, and increased tobacco taxes, criticizing delayed warning implementation and continued lower taxation tiers that they said have increased consumption and made cigarettes cheaper and more accessible to children and youth. They noted Pakistan ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) in 2004 and said stronger policies are still needed to meet international obligations. CTC-Pak is described as a coalition of more than 250 civil society organizations working to strengthen tobacco control policy development and implementation in Pakistan.

The passage is an edition of “True Orange” covering Texas recruiting and sports news. It discusses the Dec. 15–17 Longhorn recruiting weekend centered on the annual football banquet, listing 10 remaining serious recruits and noting several top targets and possible visits, along with a list of 19 early football commitments. It then addresses the bowl outlook if Texas defeats or loses Texas A&M, summarizes a UT women’s basketball WNIT win over Tulane and upcoming semifinal hosting scenarios, and provides recruiting/signing updates for UT baseball, women’s basketball, men’s basketball, volleyball, and softball, including player highlights and prior achievements. Additional sections include football and sports “notes,” subscription and gift subscription information, and a note that the next issue will be emailed Nov. 27.

The passage argues that common molecular representations do not adequately capture structures and properties needed for modelling tasks, particularly for unseen or niche chemistry. As an example, it addresses solvent representation in the Catechol Benchmark, which highlights a need for better solvent representations because solvent choice affects many reactions and because many solvents are harmful VOCs. The authors present Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings (SoDaDE), a transformer-based data-driven solvent fingerprint trained on a selected solvent-property dataset (Spange et al., 2021) using data augmentation via shuffled “solvent sequences” and masked-value prediction, with handling for missing values and causal attention. Model evaluation includes a pre-training solvent property prediction task (SoDaDE compared with GP, random forest, and averaged baselines) and performance on the Catechol Benchmark, where SoDaDE outperforms prior representations on both full-data and single-solvent tasks, with stronger results on full data suggesting better representation for solvent mixtures. The conclusion states that SoDaDE improves over tested methods, general solvent features are captured without relying on fine-tuning, and the approach can be replicated using provided data and code.

The lecture introduces causality and stability for discrete-time systems and explains how, for linear shift-invariant (LSI) systems, stability is equivalent to the unit sample response being absolutely summable, while causality is equivalent to the unit sample response being zero for negative indices. It then discusses linear constant coefficient difference equations as a class of LSI systems and notes that the difference equation alone does not uniquely specify the system without boundary/initial conditions; different boundary conditions can yield causal or non-causal—and stable or unstable—unit sample responses. Finally, the lecture presents an alternative representation of LSI systems using frequency response, based on the fact that complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of such systems, and derives the frequency response for a first-order causal case, including its magnitude/phase behavior and the periodicity of the frequency response with period \(2\pi\), concluding with a preview of the Fourier transform in the next lecture.

The passage says Nintendo Switch consoles are difficult to find unless buying a bundle, but starting Tuesday, August 15, GameStop will ship at least five Nintendo Switch consoles to each of its 4,400+ U.S. stores, with units available to sell no later than Wednesday, August 16. It also notes this is the first time since Switch launched that all GameStop stores will have the system in stock simultaneously. The consoles are available in-store only, not online, and buyers may need to call ahead or stand in line. It adds that Target and some product-tracking services have occasionally shown limited availability.

The speaker says their transition play and puck movement were good in the first period, spending time in the opponent’s end, with one defensive mistake in the neutral zone that led to the puck in their net. After the opponent scored a second goal, they played more defensively and lost some north-south and transition play, resulting in a loss. They will prepare for the next home game with fans, aiming to build on their strong home performance. The speaker credits the opponent for shutting them down offensively over the last two games and notes the opponent’s goalie is among the league’s best. They say they need more pucks to the net, more people getting to the net, screens, and better execution to address goals being allowed. They also discuss the opponent’s style and a situation involving initiating contact in relation to rules, saying the league has been contacted and clarification was provided. They conclude that they will address areas needing improvement and expect to play better in the next game.

The passage describes the need for data-driven precision medicine approaches for highly individualized rare disorders and introduces “MMFP-Tableau,” a bioinformatics platform created at CHOP within the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program. MMFP-Tableau is presented as a centralized data warehousing framework that extracts, unifies, cleans, and integrates clinical and research data from siloed sources (including CHOP’s EPIC/Clarity EMR, REDCap, and spreadsheets), models and visualizes the integrated data in a secure web environment, and provides role-based access for clinicians and researchers. The system supports real-time, interactive dashboards and queries at both individual and cohort levels, including views for clinical cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility determination, genotype-phenotype mapping, medication trends, and risk factor delineation. The platform was developed using tools such as Alteryx and Tableau, an ETL workflow to maintain data integrity while reducing duplication/loss, and HPO and ICD10/SNOMED mappings to improve phenotyping and interoperability. The authors report that MMFP-Tableau integrates data from over 2,000 individuals and outline limitations such as inability to access some non-discretized EMR data and certain imaging/PDF content, challenges with automating extraction from external institutions, and potential server slowdowns due to live data volume.

The passage describes Blackwell ninth-generation NVENC improvements, including 5% higher BD-BR PSNR quality for AV1 and HEVC, added support for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding, and an AV1 Ultra High Quality (UHQ) mode that increases best-quality performance by an additional 5% (at the cost of extra time). It also discusses encoder-generation gains and speed and decoding improvements, including a faster sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 decode support. The passage then covers Blackwell power-efficiency features under the Max-Q philosophy, including advanced power gating, new clock gating and memory power management, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep states, with claimed power savings examples. It also outlines DLSS 4 features such as Multi Frame Generation and transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, plus neural shaders and related technologies (e.g., Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces). Finally, it provides high-level Blackwell GPU architecture details and product/speciation references for GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, 5070, and associated GB202/GB203/GB205 chips, followed by NVIDIA legal and warranty disclaimers.

The lecture begins a new topic on radiation (self-emission) from plasmas as a diagnostic tool, noting that all objects emit electromagnetic radiation and that hotter objects emit higher-energy photons. Plasmas can emit radiation across a wide range of wavelengths, requiring different conceptual frameworks (wave vs ray treatments). Radiation has two key consequences: it can cool plasmas and it provides information through the radiation spectrum, spatial distribution, and temporal variation. 

It then discusses radiation transport, describing how emitted radiation can be absorbed elsewhere, locally heating the plasma, and then re-emitted, making transport complex and often non-local. Because the full transport problem is difficult, radiation transport is often approximated as diffusive, though this may not always be valid. To model transport, the lecture introduces the spectral radiance \(I\) along a path \(s\), defines emissivity \(j\) and opacity \(\alpha\) (as frequency-dependent), and presents the radiation transport equation in terms of \(dI/ds\). The equation is treated as independent for each frequency by neglecting processes such as fluorescence. 

The lecture introduces optical depth \(\tau\) as an integral of opacity along the path and rewrites the transport equation to solve for \(I\) at an exit point. It presents optically thin (\(\tau \ll 1\)) and optically thick (\(\tau \gg 1\)) limits, explaining that optically thin radiation retains the initial intensity, while optically thick radiation approaches \(J/\alpha\), related to blackbody radiation and Kirchhoff’s law. A discussion follows comparing optically thick absorption to plasma cutoffs where refractive index becomes less than zero, emphasizing they are different processes (gradual absorption vs sudden behavior at a critical surface). 

Finally, the lecture begins the topic of radiation from free charges, using the Poynting flux to explain that stationary and constant-velocity charges do not radiate in the far-field sense, while accelerated charges do; it sketches near-field and far-field contributions and states that radiating particles in plasmas will require solving particle equations of motion and integrating over particle distributions to obtain measurable emission (steps the lecture says it will skip).

The passage says that the Trump administration backed off from 100% pharma tariffs that were threatened to start on that day. The administration had promised to enact the tariffs on Oct. 1 unless companies agreed to build infrastructure in the U.S. A White House official later told STAT that the tariffs had not gone into effect and that the administration would begin preparing tariffs for branded drugs on companies that do not build in the U.S. or do not make a drug pricing agreement. The postponement is described as possibly intended to leverage more actions such as U.S. investment and deals to lower drug prices.

House Of Fraser reported higher full-year pre-tax profits, rising from £1.3 million to £3.4 million for the year to January 28, while revenues were flat at £1.3 billion. Online delivered a 16.1% sales increase and now makes up over a fifth of total sales; like-for-like sales rose 0.9%. The company warned that trading volatility continued into 2017, noting February was subdued but March improved. It said five under-performing brands will be discontinued this year. House Of Fraser also opened its first standalone shop in China in Nanjing, at Sanpower Plaza, as part of plans to build its brand.

The passage describes the head and shoulders chart pattern used in technical analysis to indicate a potential trend reversal. A typical head and shoulders pattern has three price swing highs (left shoulder, head, right shoulder) and two swing lows, forming a neckline from the swing lows; it is completed when price breaks below the neckline. In an uptrend, it is considered a bearish reversal signal, suggesting the uptrend may turn into a downtrend, with traders often taking short positions or closing long positions. The inverted head and shoulders pattern (“head and shoulders bottom”) is described as the opposite: it has three swing lows and two swing highs, a neckline from the swing highs, and is completed when price breaks above the neckline, indicating a bullish reversal.

The passage notes that the authors could not fully quantify head and shoulders rules for backtesting, so they rely on Thomas Bulkowski’s research from the late 1990s. Bulkowski’s survey is said to show a 93% success rate for the head and shoulders formation (with false signals defined as cases where the stock fell less than five percent below the neckline and then rose). It also reports that most formations occurred after an upswing, with an average price drop up to 23%, and that volume and neckline direction were not considered decisive for success. The passage also summarizes Bulkowski’s findings for the inverted pattern, including few false signals and an expectation of 20–30% returns within 73 days, along with guidance on stop-loss placement. It adds that the Federal Reserve found technical analysis (including head and shoulders strategy) generated statistically significant profits in a 1995 report, while the authors urge caution because Bulkowski used after-the-fact analysis.

Around 125 people attended sessions to give views on drafting a masterplan for the centre of Newtongrange. The sessions were organised by LDA and held at The Mining Museum on Friday, September 1, and at Newbattle Parish Church on Saturday, September 2. Councillor Russell Imrie thanked contributors, noting the views of local people were extremely helpful and that there was lively debate toward making Newtongrange thrive and be more attractive. The masterplan team will now consider the information gathered and develop the design with the council and Blueprint Partnership, with further community engagement later in the year.

The passage explains defensive challenges against the Base Cross offense, especially when it uses “Big” screens against a “Little” post and when quick ball reversal occurs down screens. It outlines defensive fundamentals and three phases for a base cross show-and-recover approach: (1) showing to force the point guard to middle and pressure passes to the post while weakside defenders help, (2) recovering and matching up after the screen with pack-in weakside help and possible yo-yo movement, and (3) final matchups with ball pressure on the point guard and pushing the post off the block. It also describes “All Out SOS” disruption by trapping the ball handler on the wing before an entry pass, using a “Hi-Lo Switch” depending on whether the post goes baseline or over the top, and then continuing rotations after trap passes to prevent ball reversal.

Calvin Alexander, a seventh grader from Caddo Middle Magnet, won the Northwest Louisiana regional spelling bee for the second consecutive year. His winning word was “nectarivorous,” and the competition had 22 spellers from 28 regions over 20 rounds. Alexander defeated Rosetta Schultz in the final four rounds after she faltered on “horotelic.” The event took place March 17 on the LSUS campus, with Dr. Thomas Du Bose serving as pronouncer and a team of judges verifying spelling accuracy. Alexander studied the 2018 School Spelling Bee Study List and Spell It!, advanced to the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee in the Washington, D.C. area, and is set to receive prizes including a 2018 United States Mint Proof Set, Britannica Online Premium, and the Merriam-Webster Unabridged Online.

The speaker expresses honor at being invited to Amherst and discusses the limited powers of the Presidency, saying the President must respond when asked by the Disarmament Advisory Committee. He notes Amherst alumni in public service and argues that colleges should serve a national purpose by placing graduates’ privilege within a duty to serve the public interest. He cites social and economic inequality, inherited wealth and poverty, and stresses that educated citizens are needed to address major domestic and international challenges, including employment, governance across many countries, and racial harmony. Reflecting on Robert Frost’s memory, the speaker presents Frost as both an artist and an American whose questioning of power strengthens national life, and emphasizes art as truth rather than propaganda. He concludes with hopes for a future America that balances strength with moral restraint, supports arts and cultural opportunities, protects beauty and the environment, and earns respect for both strength and civilization.

The OECD warned that the Irish economy is showing signs of overheating, citing a sharp rise in new mortgage loans and loans to small firms, largely linked to construction activity. It said Central Bank loan-to-value and loan-to-income caps may need to be extended to slow credit growth, and it raised the risk of another property bubble if annual house-price growth (about 13%) continues. The OECD also noted that nearly 4% of mortgages taken out before the crash could default in a financial shock, though these loans are not currently in default. The warning comes alongside concern over EU debt sustainability amid political turmoil in Italy, while the NTMA head said Irish government bonds have held steady as investors “reclassified” Ireland’s creditworthiness. The OECD forecast robust near-term growth but said the Government should improve its fiscal position to buffer future shocks, especially Brexit. European Commission officials added that persistent housing supply shortages are driving price increases and that reduced government investment has affected housing availability.

The DuBard School for Language Disorders at the University of Southern Mississippi received recognition from IMSLEC as one of four U.S. schools committed to student achievement through multisensory structured language education.
