Zillow reports 66.1% of homes sold in the past year had air conditioning, and in very hot markets it was nearly universal (99.1% in Las Vegas and 97.9% in Phoenix). Renters also paid more for air conditioning, with typical rentals with central air renting for 2.8% more (about $40 per month). The passage includes metro-level shares and premiums for both for-sale and rental listings.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program to train school administrators in school security. The program allows administrators in schools without a school resource officer to have a firearm on campus in a secured safe to respond to an active shooter, but participants must complete training and receive approval from the local superintendent, school board, and county sheriff. Participating sentries must store firearms in a secured weapon system and obtain approved weapon and ammunition, as well as a specially designed bullet-proof vest. Alabama Secretary of Law Enforcement Hal Taylor and Superintendent of Education Dr. Eric Mackey joined the announcement, citing increased school security and faster threat identification.

The passage describes a system and method for tracing money flow in cryptocurrency transactions to support regulatory compliance (AML/CFT) and investigative needs. It addresses difficulty in tracing transaction origins and destinations on decentralized blockchains and proposes using intelligence labels with known behavioral characteristics plus user-defined tracing parameters to auto-trace suspicious asset paths. The method receives blockchain transaction data (addresses, transaction IDs, timestamps, and digital assets) into a transaction database, receives intelligence labels from a blockchain ecosystem intelligence database, applies labels to source, intermediate, and destination account addresses, and uses an artificial intelligence graph search algorithm (based on constraints such as direction, time bounds, and transaction filters) to determine an auto-traced path and generate reports with tracing statistics and suspicious addresses. If suspicious addresses are found, it can alert users, warn about illicit transactions, and suspend transactions. The passage further describes components such as ETL for blockchain data, a machine-learning-based behavior/risk labeling pipeline, risk scoring and policy engines, optional address clustering, interactive journey boards, and visualization/reporting for tracing results.

The Bank of England warned that the rally in AI-related stocks may be unsustainable, saying AI valuations are starting to resemble those from the dot-com bubble and that investors’ optimism about near-term profitability is excessive. It cautioned that concentrated gains among a few major U.S. tech firms could increase systemic vulnerabilities and that a loss of confidence could spread through global markets via capital outflows and equity repricing, including affecting the UK. The BoE also cited potential constraints from power supply, semiconductor capacity, and data infrastructure that could limit AI expansion priced into markets. While the UK system is described as broadly stable, the BoE said an AI-driven sell-off could cause cross-border volatility due to the UK’s openness to shocks from U.S. equities, and it urged investor caution given risks of a swift, severe correction.

Plum School District officials plan to begin 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday to help avoid a third consecutive tax increase. Board president Kevin Dowdell said the discussions are preliminary, and finance committee chair Michelle Stepnick said budgeting should be an ongoing conversation. The district’s 2017-18 budget is $66 million with a 0.866-mill property tax hike and no program cuts, and it has started the year more than $4 million in debt. In June, the board approved a 12-year, $5.6 million bond and increased property taxes for 2016-17. For 2018-19, the district plans to recruit Chinese students on a tuition basis; visa applications and a recruitment trip for Superintendent Tim Glasspool in September are listed on Tuesday’s workshop agenda. Other agenda items include elementary construction, consolidation and redistricting, and the process for closing Regency Park Elementary School, which requires state notification and public hearings. The workshop will follow a special voting meeting at 6 p.m., though the special meeting agenda has not been posted.

A survey by Infosys Finacle of 100 financial services professionals found that more than 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020, and over half of financial institutions plan to invest in it this year. The average investment in blockchain projects this year is expected to be about $1 million, with 4% spending more than $10 million. Half of banks are working with fintech start-ups or technology companies to enhance blockchain capabilities. Blockchain rollouts will be prioritized for areas improving transparency, automating processes across enterprises, and reducing settlement and transaction time. Expected production use cases include cross-border payments, digital identity management, clearing and settlement, letter of credit processing, and loan syndication. Most banks (69%) prefer private blockchains with tightly controlled access; 20% prefer hybrid/consortium blockchains, and 10% prefer public, fully decentralized blockchains.

Pump and dump strategies are described as scams that are mostly illegal (and also immoral), benefiting only a few promoters and early investors while those who join later face significant losses. The passage defines a pump and dump as a promoter acquiring shares (often penny stocks) and artificially increasing the price by spreading false or misleading information; as the price rises, the promoter sells to latecomers, causing the price to drop. It notes that pump and dump schemes are likelier in the OTC and crypto markets, where many coins have low volume and are unregulated, and where FOMO can drive rapid price increases followed by declines. The passage cites a study reporting that investing in pump-and-dump schemes is fairly common among sample German bank customers and that tout investments produced considerable losses. It concludes by advising people to stay away from suspected schemes, be cautious—especially in the OTC market—and consider systematic or long-term, ethical approaches instead.

The passage describes wireless paging information transmission methods, apparatus, and systems for new generation wireless communication systems that use high-frequency carrier transmission and beamforming. It addresses the problem that applying an LTE-like discontinuous reception (DRX) paging approach is difficult because a user equipment (UE) in an IDLE state cannot predict how paging beams/ports are scheduled across timeslots.

The proposed approach defines a paging occasion (PO) that includes a group of paging resources for transmitting paging information on preset beams or ports. A first communication node calculates a time-domain position of a PO for a second communication node and transmits paging information (paging downlink control information and/or a paging message) within that PO. The second communication node also calculates its PO time-domain position and receives the paging information within that PO.

The passage further describes PO determination using parameters such as the DRX cycle, paging transmission interval, number of paging transmissions, a device identifier (Device_ID), and a PO offset. It also discusses transmitting indication information related to a quasi-co-location relationship between paging-related signals and other sweeping signals/channels to help the second node determine paging message resources. PO may correspond to a synchronous signal burst set or other sweeping resources rather than a single LTE subframe. The disclosure includes related apparatus implementations, a system with first and second communication nodes, and mentions computer-readable storage and program products, including base station and terminal devices.

Orbital ATK reported fiscal Q2 2017 results on Aug. 3, with sales of $1.12 billion slightly above estimates and adjusted pro forma earnings of $1.56 per share ahead of expectations, but GAAP profits were down 3% to $1.51 per share due to a decline in operating profit margin to 12.2%. Free cash flow was negative at $55.8 million versus positive $107.2 million a year earlier. Management remained optimistic for 2017, citing performance and plans to accelerate revenue and earnings growth in H2 2017 alongside “significant free cash flow,” supported by new firm and option orders that produced an estimated book-to-bill ratio of about 1.45. Orbital raised full-year sales guidance to $4.6–$4.65 billion and earnings to $5.95–$6.25 per share while keeping free cash flow guidance at $250–$300 million. Argus Research upgraded the stock from hold to buy, setting a $120 price target and expecting cash-flow growth through milestones and benefits from increased defense spending. The passage also argues the stock’s valuation is stretched, concluding it is too expensive to justify a buy rating despite recent stock performance.

Shepard Fairey was arrested outside the Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) on February 9, 2009, after failing to appear in court on a vandalism charge. Despite the disruption, Fairey’s exhibition attracted about 130,000 attendees by its August closing. The passage describes how the ICA, transformed under Director Jill Medvedow, evolved from a small, underfunded museum in a former police station to a new waterfront institution. It outlines Medvedow’s efforts to reposition the museum, expand outreach and audience, secure funding, and obtain land for a new building on Fan Pier Parcel J, including presentations to the public and the selection of architect Diller + Scofidio. It also notes delays and setbacks during construction, and reports that the new ICA opened in December 2006 to more than 8,000 visitors, later sustaining high attendance in 2008 and 2009.
The case “Pink C. JENKINS v. UNITED STATES of America” (No. 10902) in the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals was appealed and then dismissed on motion of the appellee with the consent of the appellant.

The passage describes a qualitative study proposing the “whole human pedagogy” framework for education abroad, grounded in decolonial theory and literature on experiential learning and alternative pedagogies. The framework centers four tenets—embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming—to approach students as integrated human beings with bodily, emotional, relational, and meaning-making knowledge, and to include diverse knowledge sources in academic spaces. Using purposive and snowball sampling, the study interviewed 17 education abroad practitioners in Fall 2023, analyzing responses in NVivo. Findings indicate practitioners commonly understand whole human pedagogy as central to their work and explore all four tenets, with embodiment emphasized through physical and sensory learning; emotions linked to culture shock and reflective learning; belonging focused on communal, reciprocal relationships and trust; and becoming centered on student transformation, self-knowledge, and self-sufficiency. The discussion frames the approach as a general educational posture promoting collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing, aiming to challenge dominant Euro-U.S. epistemological values and to support program development and future research.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. The sentence followed his July conviction under the Mann Act; he was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges. The judge said Combs had the resources to keep the conduct going and “because you weren’t caught.” Combs apologized to his family and said he was sorry for actions he called “disgusting” and “shameful,” including domestic violence he said he would carry for life. During the trial, accusers testified that Combs beat, threatened, sexually assaulted, and blackmailed them, and that he ordered sex with strangers and pressured male workers during drug-fueled “hotel nights.” His daughters Chance and D’Lila also spoke in court, and D’Lila said she feared losing her father and asked for a chance for the family to heal.

Amazon announced new hardware at its fall event, including new Echo devices with Alexa+ and new Ring camera models, plus three new Kindle Scribe tablets (including a color-screen “Kindle Scribe Colorsoft”). Amazon’s Alexa+ is powered by a large language model, with features like conversational interaction and faster responses, and it is free for Prime subscribers but $20/month for others. The new Echo devices use Amazon’s AZ3 or AZ3 Pro chips and include Omnisense technology. Amazon also introduced new Fire TVs and a new Fire TV Stick model, with a new TV operating system called Vega for the first time on these devices. Ring’s new cameras use Amazon’s “Retinal 2K” and “Retinal 4K” image processing for improved low-light performance and include features such as Familiar Faces, Alexa+ Greetings, and Search Party. Preorders for many of the announced devices are available, and Ring and Alexa+ features are rolling out over coming months.

The passage discusses how container patterns can extend legacy or standardize functionality in cloud-native environments. It describes using a sidecar container to add HTTPS termination to an HTTP-only legacy service via an nginx container sharing a network namespace with the legacy app, and to manage dynamic configuration by sharing a filesystem and synchronizing configuration through an API. It also covers other sidecar uses such as modular introspection (topz), building a simple PaaS using a git-synchronizing sidecar, and principles for designing reusable sidecars through parameterization, a stable API surface, and documentation.

It then introduces the ambassador pattern for brokering communication between application containers and external services. Examples include sharding integration (using an ambassador proxy to route requests to the correct storage shard while the app connects to localhost) and request splitting/experimentation (using nginx as an ambassador that routes a fraction of traffic to an experimental service). The passage also introduces the adapter pattern, which provides consistent monitoring/logging/health-check interfaces by transforming heterogeneous application interfaces into a common format; examples include Prometheus monitoring via an exporter adapter and log normalization via fluentd.

Finally, the passage transitions to multi-node patterns for microservices and scaling, including replicated load-balanced stateless services with readiness probes, session-tracked services, and application-level replicated caching and SSL termination. It continues into sharded services and sharded caching concepts, including routing via sharding functions, selecting keys, consistent hashing to reduce remapping on shard count changes, replicated sharded caches for shard resilience, and hot sharding via autoscaling.

A confidential March 8, 1892 communication by Mr. Stevens reports revolutionary plans in Hawaii that could be checked solely by the presence of a U.S. naval vessel, hostility toward the “half English” heir educated in England, and a growing inclination among all classes toward U.S. annexation. Stevens’s later dispatches describe ongoing dissatisfaction over the queen’s influence by a half-caste Tahitian named Wilson and marshal of the Kingdom, and widespread revolutionary schemes throughout 1892. In late August or early September the cabinet was voted out, followed by a deadlock between the queen and the legislature; a vote of want of confidence was not secured until October 17. Stevens’s October 19 impression is that the queen and her faction would have to yield to avoid long delay of a possible overthrow of the monarchy. In a November 20 statement, he outlines two proposed options for Hawaii: bold annexation measures or a “customs union” with an ocean cable, Pearl Harbor ceded to the U.S., and an implied American protectorate. Reports to the Secretary of the Navy corroborated Stevens’s accounts and forecasts until January 28, 1893, when telegraphic news reported a peaceful revolution at Honolulu and the dethronement of the queen. The report also states that U.S. policy toward the Hawaiian Islands from 1820 to 1893 was close friendship and protection aimed at the islands’ welfare and autonomy and preserving American rights and territory, with distrust of foreign intervention and consideration of annexation under apprehended foreign encroachment. The appendix explains it provides a general view of events and copies of relevant papers, notes that private claims were not addressed, and mentions unperfected treaties (1849, 1855, 1867) and additional correspondence in Navy Department archives.

Seven months after the Trump administration’s Department of Government Efficiency cut the U.S. Department of Education’s research and evaluation activities, researchers and experts described some developments as “cautiously optimistic.” The department planned to reinstate 20 research contracts after lawsuits and to give a reprieve tied to another legal action, and it asked the public for guidance on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES). Some experts cited updates to National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) surveys and administrative data collections, and said IES’s rating on a 1–10 scale had risen from 1 to about 3 or 4. However, many said severe staff shortages threaten data quality and research progress, and NAEP and other functions may face reporting and operational limitations amid cuts. The passage also discusses possible reinstatement of closed regional education labs and broader concerns about rebuilding education research infrastructure and maintaining data quality.

Theratechnologies Inc. announced an agreement with a syndicate of underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to offer US$50,000,000 aggregate principal amount of convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30, 2023, with an option to purchase up to an additional US$7,500,000 for over-allotments. The notes will pay 5.75% interest semi-annually, be convertible at US$14.85 per common share, and be non-redeemable by the company prior to June 30, 2021, with potential redemption thereafter subject to conditions. Net proceeds are intended to fund payments under an EMD Serono termination agreement, approval and commercialization of Trogarzo™ in Europe and other jurisdictions, other general corporate purposes, and potential acquisitions. The offering is expected to close around June 19, 2018, subject to required regulatory approvals, and the notes and underlying common shares have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933.

The passage describes NASA/ESA Hubble’s image of the dwarf galaxy NGC 5949, located about 44 million light-years from Earth. With a mass around one-hundredth that of the Milky Way, it is classified as a dwarf due to its small number of stars and as a barred spiral because its loosely bound spiral arms form a structure that is only faintly visible as a bright, ill-defined pinwheel. Its proximity allows its light to be observed with relatively small telescopes, leading to its discovery by William Herschel in 1801. The passage also notes ongoing issues in studying dwarf galaxies, including the “cuspy halo” problem regarding dark matter distribution and the “missing satellites” problem related to simulations predicting more dwarf galaxies than are observed.

The Supreme Court dismissed a plea by Pradyuman’s father, Varun Thakur, seeking cancellation of interim bail granted to the Pinto family, owners of Ryan International School, in connection with Pradyuman’s murder. Thakur had challenged the Punjab and Haryana High Court’s decision to grant anticipatory bail, which also barred the family from leaving the country without permission and required their cooperation in the investigation. Pradyuman was found with his throat slit on September 8, leading to the Gurugram Police arresting bus conductor Ashok, but the CBI later gave him a clean chit and blamed a class 11 student. Pradyuman’s family alleges the Pinto family’s involvement.

The passage describes the ultimate oscillator (UO), a momentum indicator designed to measure an asset’s price momentum across three timeframes using periods 7, 14, and 28, combined into a weighted average (with the shortest timeframe weighted most). It calculates buying pressure (BP) and true range (TR) using true high/true low concepts, then derives UO values scaled from 0 to 100. The indicator is intended to reduce issues seen in single-timeframe momentum oscillators, such as early overbought signals and bearish divergence during strong advances. It is credited to Larry Williams (developed in 1976 and later popularized after 1985). Trading signals in the passage are generated only when there is divergence between price and the indicator: bullish divergence criteria are given for buy signals (starting from below 30 and rising above the divergence high), with opposite conditions for sell signals. Backtests discussed in the passage report that the default-parameter strategy (buy when crossing below 40, sell when crossing above 50) performs poorly, while strategy optimization of indicator settings produces better results, including profit factors mostly above 2, with an example showing 355 trades, 0.77% average gain per trade, 78% win rate, and 25% maximum drawdown, described as consistent and stable across different settings and as a mean reversion indicator.

The passage says automation could eliminate many jobs, including truck driving, as autonomous vehicles and AI technologies advance. It describes examples of autonomous trucking and other automated roles, and cites the World Economic Forum’s estimate that over five million jobs could be eliminated in five years. It argues humans may need “augmentation” to stay competitive, highlighting brain augmentation concepts such as a “neural lace” discussed by Elon Musk and related research by Harvard nanotechnologists. It also covers body augmentation through exosuits being developed for paraplegics, laborers, and soldiers, noting reductions in effort and potential applications in factories and package delivery. The passage then presents advice from Tom Davenport and Julia Kirby on improving employability by standing out with skills like creativity and understanding machines, while suggesting some jobs may be harder to transition than others and that “all bets are off” if artificial general intelligence arises.

President Trump pushed back on a New York Times article, saying in a Twitter post that he does not watch four to eight hours of television each day. The Times article had described his typical day as including at least four hours of television, sometimes twice that amount, usually starting with CNN or MSNBC. The Times spokeswoman, Danielle Rhodes Ha, rejected the claim that the article was false, saying the reporting was based on interviews with 60 advisers, associates, friends, and members of Congress. Trump’s comments followed a weekend of his Twitter posts attacking other outlets as publishing “fake news.”

A fast-moving lava flow from Hawaii’s Kilauea crossed Highway 132, taking out power lines and destroying 71 homes, with more structures such as outhouses and sheds also damaged. The lava knocked out power to the Vacationland and Kapoho Beach Lots neighborhoods and knocked out the utility’s equipment on the highway; Hawaii Electric Light Co. said it could not finalize a power restoration plan until the area is stable. The U.S. Geological Survey reported the flow advanced 800 yards over 80 minutes before slowing as of Wednesday morning. Authorities issued evacuation and isolation warnings for parts of Kapoho, and reported that molten rock trapped at least one person who was later rescued. The eruption has lasted nearly a month, displaced thousands, opened a new fissure bringing lava-emitting cracks to 24 since May 3, and covered two wells at a geothermal plant, which officials said were stable and monitored.

Meb Faber’s tactical asset allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach that uses market timing to allocate across four asset classes: stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities. These are divided into five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. The strategy is designed so investors do not have to be in the market 100% of the time; positions are entered on entry signals and exited on exit signals, and if there is no signal for an asset in a month, the allocation goes to cash. It can be implemented using five diversified index ETFs rather than picking individual securities. The article discusses backtesting results over 16 years, stating that the active timing strategy produced a smaller drawdown of -13.24% compared with passive approaches that had drawdowns of 40%, -50%, and higher. It also describes the roles of stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities in diversification and correlation.

Richard Berg appealed a trial court’s amended judgment increasing child support. The case involved a 1981 divorce in which Nancy Berg received custody of three children; the oldest child Denise is now over 18, Scott (the middle child) is mentally retarded, and support was originally set at $145 per month per child until age 18. In 1985, Nancy moved to increase support to guideline levels, continue support for Denise until high school graduation, and continue support for Scott past age 18; the court granted the guideline increase but denied continued support for Denise and the motion concerning Scott was withdrawn. The trial court found appellant’s net income increased from $1,246 to $1,721 per month and increased appellant’s child support to $516 per month, reducing to $430 when Scott becomes emancipated and continuing until Steven becomes emancipated. The Court of Appeals held the modification was within the trial court’s discretion but remanded for inadequate findings, requiring specific reasons for increasing child support under Moylan v. Moylan.

The passage is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017. It includes the company’s table of contents and consolidated financial statements, including statements of cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, and balance sheets, with figures for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2017 (and prior-year comparisons). It also describes accounting policies and estimates, recently adopted and not-yet-adopted accounting pronouncements (including effects related to inventory, stock-based compensation, revenue recognition, leases, income taxes, and restricted cash), cash and marketable securities valuation and fair value hierarchy, commitments and contingencies (including pledged assets and legal proceedings), acquisitions and goodwill activity during 2017, long-term debt details, stockholders’ equity items (repurchases and stock-based compensation), income tax provisions and contingencies, and segment information across North America, International, and AWS. The management discussion outlines liquidity and capital resources and provides explanations of net sales, operating income, and operating expense drivers for the periods presented.

Rapid7, Inc. (NASDAQ:RPD) was upgraded by BidaskClub from a “hold” to a “buy” rating. Other analyst actions cited include KeyCorp reissuing “buy” with a $25.00 target, Zacks cutting from “hold” to “sell,” Susquehanna Bancshares and UBS AG raising from “neutral” to “positive” with $20.00 targets, and Northland Securities reissuing “buy” with a $23.00 target. The passage reports two sell ratings, one hold, and eight buy ratings, with an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $20.19. It also provides company trading and performance details, including opening at $18.47, market cap of $796.26 million, one-year range of $10.63 to $18.65, and quarterly results on August 7 that included EPS of ($0.26) versus ($0.30) expected and revenue of $47.44 million versus $46.31 million expected.

The Canadian dollar was little changed at C$1.2857 per U.S. dollar (77.78 U.S. cents) on Monday, trading in a narrow range, after falling 1.3% last week when the Bank of Canada took a more dovish tone and kept its benchmark rate at 1%. Investors were focused on a Federal Reserve interest rate decision and a speech by Bank of Canada Governor Stephen Poloz on Thursday. Speculators reduced bullish bets on the Canadian dollar, while oil prices edged higher. Canadian government bond prices were slightly higher across a flatter yield curve, with the two-year yield at 1.498% and the 10-year yield at 1.849%.

A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards are ready to prevent regional oil exports if the United States bans Iranian oil sales. The commander, Qassem Soleimani, praised President Hassan Rouhani’s remarks about disrupting oil shipments from neighboring countries if Washington forces them to stop buying Iranian oil, and said he would implement such a policy if needed.

The University of Agriculture Faisalabad approved non-development statement of accounts worth Rs3.28 billion for 2015-16 during its 44th Senate meeting chaired by VC Dr Iqrar Ahmad. The VC said the university launched 48 new degree programs, student enrollment has exceeded 25,000, and its financial assistance program for rural and underprivileged students has surpassed Rs700 million. He highlighted research achievements, urged greater government investment in agricultural research, discussed irrigation methods for wheat due to water scarcity, and stated that malnutrition affects 40% of the population. He also said post-harvest losses account for 40% of total losses and that modern handling, storage, processing, transportation, and value addition could save agricultural produce worth billions of rupees.

The passage describes photographer Richard Mosse’s project “Heat Maps,” which documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East using a military-grade thermal camera on a robotic arm. It portrays displaced people in a visually unsettling way that strips identities into troubling statistics, while Mosse aims to make viewers feel uneasy about their own complicity and government roles. The work combines surveillance-like technology with aesthetic ambiguity, built from many small frames sewn into large panoramas, and includes moments where camera glitches remain visible. The project’s logistics were difficult, involving volunteers, border access challenges, and complex equipment, and Mosse also discusses the camera’s potential misuse for targeting while describing his intent to subvert its purpose.

India has demanded that the UN secretariat disclose information on crimes and misconduct by UN staff, including immunity invoked against prosecutions. Yedla Umasankar, India’s legal advisor to the UN Mission, criticized the UN for not vigorously following up allegations against personnel who have diplomatic immunity and said the reluctance to waive immunity may prevent host governments from prosecuting serious misconduct. He urged the secretariat to provide statistics on recorded misconduct cases, instances where immunity was refused, and related consultations and requests regarding waiver. He also said the UN has not publicly released a complete roster of all allegations and proven misconduct across the organization, and that accountability remains elusive due to legal complexities involving sovereignty and jurisdiction, operational immunities, and countries’ ability or willingness to investigate and prosecute. He noted the UN cannot make criminal prosecutions and called for countries to implement laws to address crimes committed abroad by their citizens.

President Donald Trump said the United States will impose a new 100% tariff on imports from China starting Nov. 1, “over and above” any tariffs China is already paying. He also said that on the same date the U.S. will impose export controls on “any and all critical software.” The announcement was made hours after Trump threatened a “massive increase” in tariffs in retaliation for new Chinese export controls on rare earths minerals. About 70% of the global supply of rare earths comes from China, and the minerals are described as essential for high-tech industries including automobiles, defense, and semiconductors.

The passage describes the double bottom chart pattern as a bullish reversal formation in a downtrend, consisting of two swing lows at about the same level and a swing high between them. The swing lows form an established support level, and the line connecting the swing high levels defines the neckline resistance, with the pattern considered complete only when price breaks above the neckline. It explains profit targeting by measuring pattern size and projecting upward from the neckline, and mentions stop-loss placement typically in the middle of the pattern for a 2:1 reward/risk ratio. An example outlines price declines to support, formation of the second low, and a subsequent move through the neckline after a retest. Trading approaches include aggressive entries during the second low based on reversal signals, and conservative entries after a confirmed close above the neckline with increased volume. The passage also notes the difficulty of coding and backtesting the pattern, and references research by Thomas Bulkowski indicating 68% of double bottom formations reach their target.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature classifies emperor penguins as “near-threatened,” and conservationists warn rising global temperatures could further reduce their numbers, including a 2014 Nature Climate Change study projecting a 19% population decline by 2100. A monitoring system described in a May 2 Journal of Applied Physics paper uses an inexpensive time-lapse camera on the ice and matches photos taken every minute with weather data to provide online, remote access to penguin foraging behavior. The system has shown that penguins huddle to stay warm even when it is warmer, suggesting potential trouble finding enough fish, though some experts say commercial fishing could also contribute. Others praised the system as cost-effective for research in Antarctica’s difficult conditions.

The passage includes the sentencing of defendant Pomeroy and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company, each for six offenses or crimes, with specified total fines. It then criticizes the practice of setting aside judgments on technical grounds unrelated to the case merits and proposes a law limiting when new trials or judgment reversals can occur, requiring an affirmative showing that errors resulted in a miscarriage of justice. The passage discusses injunctions, arguing against abolishing them entirely while warning that they can be severely abused; it emphasizes careful, fair use in labor disputes to prevent irreparable wrong and criticizes careless granting of preliminary injunctions that may lead to calls for abolition. It also argues that judges should act boldly and fairly despite public sentiment and should not be shielded from criticism, noting that a judge’s power has limited review and is ultimately subject to public opinion.

Mark Palmer tells Jason Leopold to forward the complaint as an attachment. The forwarded complaint describes a California class action by Pamela R. Gordon against multiple electricity generators and traders, alleging they unlawfully manipulated the California wholesale electricity market during spring and summer 2000 through misuse of confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, “parking” power with affiliates, scheduling outages and congestion to game market outcomes, and related actions. The complaint states these practices allegedly caused unjust and unreasonable wholesale prices, including overcharges of more than $4 billion to customers supplied through the California Power Exchange, and seeks class certification, damages (including treble damages), injunctive relief, and disgorgement/restitution, along with claims under California antitrust and related unfair trade and consumer protection statutes.

The passage describes a CRC corruption issue occurring during UDMA write operations after an IDE device terminates the transaction. When termination happens, the ATAC passes a CRC for the completed portion and should start a new CRC for the next portion, but generally continues from the last CRC, causing the next portion’s CRC to be in error. The first device termination is handled correctly, and the CRC can restart correctly if a host-initiated IDE I/O occurs before UDMA resumes, such as after a host termination following device termination, though this is rare and not dependable. The root cause is corruption resulting from a host termination during a preceding UDMA read (host_pio_term set). The implication is that UDMA writes cannot generally be used due to CRC errors, and the resolution is to use the UDMA I/O blocking feature associated with bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The passage describes hepatic encephalopathy (HE), a common complication of advanced liver disease, and the role of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), which can improve outcomes but also increases HE risk. It outlines an untargeted metabolomics study of blood samples from patients undergoing TIPS to identify metabolite changes that may predict worsening HE.  

Among 22 participants, metabolomic shifts after TIPS were most pronounced in peripheral vein samples before discharge, with bile acids accounting for major contributors. Bile acids dropped immediately after shunt placement in peripheral blood but returned to pre-TIPS levels by discharge. Greater within-participant changes in hepatic vein metabolomes after TIPS were associated with later HE severity, suggesting differences in intrahepatic shunting. Participants who developed more severe HE showed decreased post-shunt levels of bile acids and glycerophosphocholine, and three specific conjugated hydroxylated bile acids in peripheral blood were inversely correlated with HE grade. In two patients readmitted for HE, these bile acids decreased immediately after TIPS and increased after HE treatment.  

The study also used chemical proportionality to infer potential biochemical transformations, highlighting changes related to glycerophosphocholine and bilirubin clusters, including patterns consistent with biliverdin oxidation-reduction. The discussion concludes that bile acid changes may help distinguish patients at risk for post-TIPS HE and that further work is needed to validate findings and explore underlying mechanisms.

The passage describes how interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry can overcome limitations in characterizing large-area crystalline quality in chemical vapor deposition (CVD)-grown hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). It explains that conventional methods (e.g., TEM, STM, LEED, and Raman) are limited by sampling area, sample preparation, inability to distinguish antiparallel domains, or lack of orientational polarity metrics—especially because hBN’s deep-UV photoluminescence complicates optical characterization. The authors show that interferometric SHG resolves antiparallel domains and their boundaries, which form because hBN has lower threefold rotational symmetry and can nucleate in two antiparallel orientations on high-symmetry substrates; merging domains leads to grain boundaries that can compromise properties. They report that SHG intensity varies up to three orders of magnitude across different CVD growth methods and that this variation correlates with Raman intensity, Raman linewidth, and orientational disorder. Numerical simulations indicate that the large SHG intensity changes arise from destructive interference between antiparallel domains, scaling with antiparallel domain fraction and size. The work establishes quantitative optical quality metrics—Raman intensity and linewidth plus SHG intensity and orientational spread—and concludes that the approach is scalable and broadly applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D materials.

Sea Breeze Salt, Inc. and Innofood, S.A. de C.V. sued Mitsubishi Corporation and Mitsubishi International Corporation, among others, alleging antitrust and related claims based on ESSA’s alleged decision to distribute Mexico’s solar sea salt exclusively through Mitsubishi. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit held the suit is barred by the act of state doctrine because it fundamentally challenges acts of the Mexican government concerning exploitation of Mexico’s natural resources, performed in Mexico, and the requested relief would require a U.S. court to invalidate those sovereign decisions. The court affirmed the district court’s dismissal. The court also addressed Sea Breeze’s corporate tax suspension and noted it had been normalized, so dismissal of the appeal was not required.

Wall Street gained on Thursday, led by financial shares, after data showed U.S. economic growth was stronger than previously reported in the prior quarter due to robust consumer spending. The passage explains how adapter and container patterns enable monitoring, logging, and health checks by exposing consistent interfaces. It describes using Prometheus for container metrics via an adapter container (e.g., a Redis exporter), and normalizing heterogeneous logging formats using adapter containers with fluentd and plugins (e.g., Redis slow queries and Apache Storm). It then covers adding richer health monitoring by using separate adapter containers that run scripts or queries (including a MySQL example with an HTTP health-check adapter), emphasizing modularity and reuse rather than modifying vendor-provided containers. The passage continues with distributed systems patterns: it introduces microservices and their benefits and drawbacks, then details replicated load-balanced stateless services with readiness probes and Kubernetes deployment examples, including session-tracked services and caching layers using Varnish plus SSL termination using nginx. It further discusses sharded services and sharded caching, how shard keys and hashing functions work (including consistent hashing), replicated sharded caches, and scatter/gather patterns for parallel request processing, including considerations like overhead and the straggler problem and approaches to improve reliability via replicated shards. Finally, it introduces function-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven processing, outlining benefits, challenges, and when it is a poor fit, and presents FaaS design patterns such as decorators for request/response transformation and event-based pipelines, with examples like request defaulting, two-factor authentication, and new-user signup flows.

James T. Hodgkinson, the gunman who shot House Majority Whip Steve Scalise during an early morning baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, was killed by police. Authorities said Hodgkinson had been living out of a white cargo van in northern Virginia since March and was frequently seen at a nearby YMCA where he often kept to himself while using a computer. Officials said they are still determining his motive. Investigators are tracing his weapons, and the FBI is asking for public help to piece together his whereabouts and activities in Alexandria. Representatives reported that an aide, Zack Barth, was shot and expected to recover, while other injuries were minor and a former congressional aide was hospitalized. Witnesses described Hodgkinson as calm and withdrawn, and a bartender said he drank alone. His brother said Hodgkinson was upset about Trump’s election and had gone to Washington to protest. The passage also describes Hodgkinson’s prior home-inspection business in southern Illinois, his online political interest, past arrests, and an earlier incident in March involving rifle shots into a cornfield near his home.

Perplexity AI announced that its AI-powered web browser, Comet, is available worldwide and will be free to users. The passage transmits to Congress a letter from the governor of Texas dated June 14 and the answer the author prepared. It describes Texas’s intent to extend civil jurisdiction over specific unorganized counties (El Paso, Worth, Presidio, and Santa Fe) and to establish a separate state government east of the Rio Grande, despite those areas having been regarded as part of New Mexico and formerly governed by Mexico until separated by U.S. conquest. The author argues that Texas’s authority is limited to its own boundaries, so Texas actions outside Texas would make its forces trespassers, requiring the President to enforce federal laws under constitutional and statutory provisions. The passage then examines whether New Mexico, as a U.S. territory, is subject to treaty obligations, citing the Constitution’s “supreme law of the land” rule and the treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which includes protections for Mexicans residing in those territories (including rights to liberty, property, and religion). The author states that executive power is limited to executing laws and maintaining treaties, not creating civil or military governments in the territory. Finally, the passage urges Congress to promptly settle the Texas–New Mexico boundary question, arguing Congress should establish the line (with Texas assent) to avoid delays, disputes, and potential collisions, and suggests Congress could offer indemnity to Texas if needed.

James D. Rone sued Boncar Construction Company for negligence after he was injured at a sewer construction site in Hobart, Indiana. Rone, employed by Dan Raymond Construction Company, directed the back hoe operator to stop because the machine could not clear a telephone wire. While Rone was on the gantry lifting the wires, he later fell out of the operator’s vision, grasped a moving cable to steady himself, and severed fingers due to the cable moving through a sheave. The operator testified there was no system of communication signals and did not move the relevant hand lever.

The trial court struck Rone’s count I alleging a violation of the Illinois Structural Work Act, and the case proceeded to trial on counts II and III. A jury verdict found for Boncar, and the judgment was affirmed on appeal. The appellate court held that issues of negligence, contributory negligence, and whether any alleged lack of signals was the proximate cause were properly submitted to the jury, that contributory negligence under the Indiana Employers Liability Act was not decided as a matter of law, and that refusal of Rone’s proposed instructions on agency and multiple parties being at fault was not error.

The passage reports apixaban initiation timing, exposure, interruption, dosing, and compliance across study groups. Mean time to apixaban initiation was about 1.6–1.8 days, and total exposure and interruption up to 24 weeks were comparable between groups. Compliance (percentage of prescribed drug taken) was high and similar across groups (>95% at weeks 4, 12, and 24; >94% at week 48). The primary efficacy endpoint showed mean adherence at 24 weeks of about 91.6–91.9% with no significant difference between the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups; adherence also appeared comparable across multiple time intervals and study groups, with some within-group decreases over specific periods. Persistence and fully adherent subject proportions were likewise reported as similar between certain groups. Logit models for non-adherence predictors indicated significant associations in the Primary SOC group (and not in the Additional Educational Program group for 24 weeks), with some effects involving MMSE, alcohol/technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, age, VKA-naïve status, and permanent atrial fibrillation depending on the time point and group. Subgroup analyses generally showed no significant interaction, except for adherence from week 24 to 48 with interactions by atrial fibrillation type and sex. Safety results indicated overall similar safety endpoints between groups, including comparable AE rates, discontinuations, and bleeding events, with a fatal bleeding event reported in one subject in the Additional Educational Program group before 24 weeks. The conclusion states that the AEGEAN study showed high adherence and persistence through 48 weeks and that a proactive educational program did not add adherence or persistence benefits.

Stockholm and other parts of Sweden had their warmest New Year’s Eve temperatures in at least 157 years in 2013, according to SMHI official data. Temperatures reached 10.4C in central Swedish towns Eskilstuna and Adelsö on December 31, surpassing Sweden’s previous record set in Duved in 1972 by 0.1 degrees. Stockholm recorded 10.3C on December 31, exceeding its prior record of 8.4C in 1975. SMHI measured temperatures between 7pm on January 30 and 7pm on January 31, and meteorologist Lisa Frost said the old record was broken by a wide margin. Frost also said temperatures would drop below freezing across the country on Monday.

The passage discusses opening range breakout (ORB) trading strategies and reports backtests showing that, without added filters, ORB strategies “don’t work very well anymore,” particularly on the S&P 500 futures. It concludes that ORB strategies are less relevant now and recommends adding daily filters while avoiding overfitting, and suggests using strategy optimization to develop robust strategies.

A Utah prosecutor ruled that police were legally justified in the August fatal shooting of Patrick Harmon, a black man whose death was recorded on body camera video released this week. Slowed-down video described by Salt Lake County District Attorney Sim Gill shows Harmon pivoting toward officers with a knife, and Officer Clinton Fox said Harmon threatened to stab him before Fox fired at close range. African American leaders and anti-police brutality groups said the community is outraged and want the district attorney to resign, and about 50 protesters rallied in Salt Lake City demanding footage release. The ruling came amid broader national debate on race and policing, including a prior Utah case involving Darrien Hunt. Gill said his office will decide whether to file charges by weighing whether the officer could reasonably fear serious injury or death.

He notes that some discarded books may now cost over $1,000 used, but says he already acted. He disposes of the books in a blue recycle bin while keeping one volume as a reading stand. He also shares that he later closed his law office and continued humor writing and speaking.

The passage describes a study using VHA COVID-19 Observational Research Collaborative (CORC) data to evaluate whether SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with suicide attempts and self-directed violence among Veterans. Over 100 million people in the U.S. have been infected with SARS-CoV-2, and the effects of infection and the pandemic on mental health are noted as important to distinguish for suicide prevention. The study included 199,474 Veterans with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and 992,036 matched uninfected comparators, followed through one year after the index date. Suicide attempts and self-directed violence were identified from VHA Suicide Behavior and Overdose Report (SBOR) and Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluation (CSRE) data curated by PERC, with suicide deaths not validated and reported as unvalidated PERC data.  

Results showed that within one year after infection, 0.258% had at least one suicide attempt and 0.242% had at least one self-directed violence. Unadjusted event rates were higher in the infected group than in comparators across all follow-up durations, with highest rates in the first 30 days. Cox regression (intent to treat) found higher hazards for suicide attempts (short-term HR=2.54; long-term HR=1.30; one-year HR=1.41) and self-directed violence (short-term HR=1.94; long-term HR=1.32; one-year HR=1.38) in the infected group versus comparators. The study reports largely similar sensitivity findings, and concludes that Veterans infected with SARS-CoV-2 have increased risk of suicide attempts and self-directed violence, especially early after infection, and emphasizes early assessment to support prevention efforts.

The passage describes momentum trading and a momentum strategy for the S&P 500, which aims to buy strong stocks based on historical performance and rebalance periodically. It cites the momentum hypothesis (correlation between 3–12 months historical and future returns) and discusses research suggesting most stocks contribute little to overall market gains. The passage presents a backtest of a simple monthly moving-average crossover strategy on the S&P 500 cash index (1960–February 2023), showing an ending value of 5.575 million from 100,000 (6.6% annual return vs. 7% buy and hold). It notes the strategy is invested 69% of the time and has smaller drawdowns (26% vs. 55%), and claims a higher risk-adjusted return of 9.5%. It also mentions testing both simple and exponential moving averages, with the simple moving average performing best, and references the S&P 500 Momentum Index (SP500MUP) as an index measuring relative strength.

An ADP report said September saw a loss of 32,000 private nonfarm jobs, the largest since June 2020. The six-month moving average was 23,000, the lowest since the aftermath of the 2020 pandemic. Education & Health Services rose by 33,000 jobs, while Leisure & Hospitality fell by 19,000.
