It then discusses microservices as loosely coupled architectures made of components communicating via defined APIs, highlighting benefits like reliability, agility, and independent scaling, and noting disadvantages such as harder debugging and more complex design. The text further covers replicated load-balanced and stateless services, including readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers (and their interaction with session tracking), rate limiting, and SSL termination, with examples for deploying in Kubernetes. It contrasts replicated with sharded services for state scaling, introduces sharded caching and the impact of cache hit rate and latency, and describes replicated, sharded caches. Later sections cover sharding functions (determinism, uniformity, modulo), consistent hashing, scatter/gather patterns for parallelizing request processing, and the challenges of straggler overhead. Finally, it introduces function-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven processing, describing benefits for developers, operational challenges, and example patterns like request/response decorators and event pipelines, before transitioning to distributed ownership and master election considerations.

A Colorado panel voted to limit what health plans in the state will pay for a costly arthritis treatment. The passage also describes European officials nearing agreement on a major overhaul of EU pharmaceutical policy, including provisions affecting medicine rollout, drugmaker investment, and issues such as drug shortages, antimicrobial resistance, compounding, environmental impacts, and the “hospital exemption.” It further explains that U.S. telehealth has shifted from helping patients access doctors to helping companies sell drugs, with on-demand telehealth prescriptions increasingly promoted through consumer ads and partnerships for branded and compounded drug offerings.

The first meeting of the Pakistan-Afghanistan Joint Working Group will be held in Kabul today. A top Pakistani delegation led by Foreign Secretary Tehmina Janjua arrived earlier today to attend. The Foreign Office spokesperson Dr Mohammad Faisal said Pakistan proposed five joint working groups covering countering terrorism, intelligence sharing, military, economy/trade and transit interaction, refugee repatriation, and connectivity, and reiterated that there is no military solution and only an Afghan-led peace process can ensure peace. He said Pakistan will continue supporting peace efforts, but that the Afghan government needs to reach a settlement with different Afghan groups. An Afghan high-level delegation visited Pakistan earlier this week, and Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Khawaja Asif emphasized resolving issues bilaterally and supporting Afghan brothers amid recent attacks in Kabul. Pakistan’s Ambassador to the United States Aizaz Ahmad Chaudhry said Pakistan does not want violence or terrorism in Afghanistan and rejected blaming, adding that Pakistan and the United States have worked together for decades based on mutual respect and trust.

The passage describes oscillator, output, rectifier, timing, fault, and control-related features of TPS7H500x-SP controllers, along with summary guidance and an example space-grade converter design. It explains internal oscillator mode (RT sets frequency; SYNC outputs a clock at twice switching frequency), external synchronization mode (RT floating; clock applied to SYNC at twice the desired switching frequency), and primary-secondary mode using SYNC for synchronization between two controllers. It then outlines primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB), synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB), dead time and leading edge blank time programmability (via PS/SP/LEB pins and external resistors), pulse skipping behavior, duty cycle programmability (via DCL), current sensing and PWM generation (CS_ILIM and COMP/2 comparator), and hiccup-mode operation (via CHICC and HICC pin thresholds). Additional sections cover external fault protection (FAULT pin behavior), slope compensation setup (RSC and compensation options), thermal shutdown thresholds, controller functional principles, and application/design guidance including layout recommendations, input bypassing, and a detailed push-pull converter example with selected component values.

Israel and Myanmar signed an education cooperation agreement to develop school programs teaching the Holocaust and its lessons about intolerance, racism, anti-Semitism, and xenophobia. The agreement also includes “mutually verify school textbooks,” with each state able to edit passages about its own history in the other state’s textbooks where needed. The passage claims Israel has killed more than 100 Palestinian protesters since late March and cites allegations that Myanmar is engaging in ethnic cleansing against Rohingya Muslims. It also says the project will include Israeli and Jewish studies in Myanmar and Myanmar studies in Israel, with joint education initiatives from preschool through postgraduate levels.

The passage describes a disclosure related to a diabetes management partner interface for wireless communication of analyte (e.g., glucose) data collected by an analyte sensor system. It outlines background on diabetes, limitations of conventional blood glucose monitoring, and the development of sensors that transmit data to remote display devices, while noting interoperability and synchronization challenges across devices from different manufacturers. The disclosure’s summary includes methods, systems, and devices for authorizing partner devices to access and modify configuration parameters via the interface, where modifications are made according to partner-specific system requirements (such as connectivity, access control, calibration/data parameters, accuracy, battery capacity, protocols, regulatory requirements, and operational time). It further describes controlling wireless communication paths and access levels between the sensor system, display devices, and partner devices, including whitelist management, advertisement structure/slots, remote-server-based operations, and operating modes for different partner classes (e.g., medicament delivery devices). Additional aspects cover configuring connection models (intermittent vs. continuous), managing alerts, exchanging pairing/analyte dosage data, and monitoring medicament delivery device operability status. The passage also includes figure descriptions and notes that the detailed description and figures illustrate example embodiments.

William C. Smith, 42, of Trotwood, appeared in Miami County Municipal Court and was arraigned on a charge of murder of Willard Higgins Jr. Smith pleaded not guilty and had bond set at $500,000. Police said Higgins, 40, died at Kettering Hospital after an altercation with Smith on Walnut Street around 12:30 p.m. Friday. Smith was detained later Friday by Washington Courthouse police, incarcerated on drug charges in Fayette County Jail, and transferred to Miami County over the weekend. Higgins allegedly had difficulty breathing and requested blood pressure medication; his girlfriend called 911 and he was taken to Upper Valley Medical Center, where he was apparently put on a breathing machine and later suffered a heart attack. He also had a brain bleed and was transported by CareFlight to Kettering Hospital, where he died. Witnesses said Smith made a comment about Higgins’ girlfriend that sparked the altercation. An autopsy is underway at the Montgomery County Crime Lab, and a pre-trial hearing was set for Dec. 19.

A 2015 survey by the University of Hong Kong and Fiji’s Ministry of Fisheries found that known breeding sites for kawakawa and donu had either declined or disappeared in 70% of cases, and grouper catches had declined by 70%. The survey also reported that 18% of breeding sites were labelled dead and close to 9% were labelled healthy, and it said there was a need to raise awareness about the species’ reality. Scott Radway of cChange Fiji reported that 95% of those surveyed in the Suva area would be very willing to stop eating kawakawa and donu during peak breeding season after learning it could help recovery from overfishing. The 4FJ campaign asks people to pledge not to eat, buy, or sell kawakawa and donu from June through September, and says it is supported by partnerships across private sector, research institutions, government departments, NGOs, and communities.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on July 22, 2020. The report states that on July 22, 2020, Tesla released its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2020 by posting its Second Quarter 2020 Update on its website. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated by reference. The filing includes Item 9.01(d) identifying Exhibit 99.1 as the Second Quarter 2020 Update dated July 22, 2020, and is signed by Zachary J. Kirkhorn, Chief Financial Officer, on July 22, 2020.

VentureWire (Wednesday, November 15, 2000) is a daily newsletter of private company business news published by Technologic Partners. It lists top stories about Advanced Technology Ventures raising an $800 million fund, Qualcomm forming Qualcomm Ventures with $500 million, IP Communications receiving $312 million in a second round, and Foodbuy.com ending California operations and cutting about 22% of staff. The issue also provides extensive “New Money,” “Bad News,” “New Products,” “New Deals,” “M&A,” leadership changes, funding/personnel updates, and “VW Corrections,” along with subscription and distribution information.

The passage describes features of NVIDIA’s Blackwell RTX architecture, including hardware ray intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0, and the AI Management Processor (AMP) for faster GPU context scheduling on the GPU. It also outlines new video/display capabilities such as 4:2:2 chroma video encode/decode, ninth-generation NVENC/NVDEC improvements, and DisplayPort 2.1b bandwidth. Additional sections cover Blackwell Max-Q power efficiency improvements (advanced power gating and accelerated frequency switching) and DLSS 4, which includes Multi Frame Generation and transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. The passage further discusses the move toward neural shaders and related technologies like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces, and provides specifications and product positioning for GPUs including GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070).

The plaintiff appealed an order requiring her to serve a further bill of particulars after her initial failure to provide one led to an uncontested conditional order of preclusion. Although she argued the order was improvidently granted because the defendants did not seek further relief within 10 days or allege special circumstances, the court held that the plaintiff’s delays could not excuse the defendants’ own delay. The court also noted the appeal further delayed pretrial proceedings. The order was reversed and the motion denied without costs.

The passage states that the Imperial Russian Government accepted that the seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon was unjustifiable and that indemnity was due, but repudiated the claim’s principal item related to loss of services, equipment, and crew during detention, while not submitting detailed accounts of minor expenses at the time; these expenses are now submitted in a bill for damages. On January 27 (February 8), 1899, the U.S. Chargé d’Affaires offered $42,000 as a compromise to settle damages, stating it would not prejudice claimants’ rights to seek full recovery by arbitration or negotiation if rejected. The Imperial Russian Government rejected the compromise in a note dated March 13 (old style), March 25 (new style), 1899, and offered $2,500 indemnity again. The passage also describes the Okhotsk Sea as a large arm of the North Pacific separated by the Kuril Islands and argues it is a common resort for whalers based on affidavits. It notes sworn affidavits that, at the time of seizure, the commander of the arresting Russian vessel declared the Okhotsk Sea was closed and that he had orders to seize all vessels taking whales there. The passage further cites treaty language from the 1824 U.S.-Russia treaty stating citizens or subjects of the high contracting powers should not be disturbed or restrained in navigation or fishing in parts of the Pacific Ocean or South Sea not already occupied.

The lecture reviews coherent (collective) Thomson scattering in plasmas, focusing on scattering where the scattering wavelength associated with the wavevector difference \(k = k_s - k_i\) is larger than the Debye length. On these scales, the wavelength samples collective plasma motion, with relevant low-frequency plasma modes including ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves, each with given dispersion relations. The lecture explains that these waves exist as continual plasma fluctuations and that scattering transfers energy and momentum to them, producing peaks in the measured frequency spectrum at low and higher \(\omega\) values (ion acoustic and electron plasma wave features). It also discusses how detector placement determines which wavevector components are sampled, leading to broadening from thermal effects and finite angular collection.  

The derivation proceeds in two steps: (1) expressing scattered power in terms of density fluctuations via a spectral density function \(S(k,\omega)\), and (2) evaluating density fluctuations using a test particle approach that accounts for shielding (Debye clouds) and Landau damping. Using a Klimontovich distribution, the lecture quotes that the scattered power depends on \(S(k,\omega)\), which is related to electron and ion contributions through susceptibilities and velocity distribution functions. Peaks in \(S(k,\omega)\) occur when the dielectric function \(\epsilon(k,\omega)\) approaches zero, corresponding to plasma normal modes. Finally, the lecture outlines the warm-plasma (Maxwellian) treatment, where susceptibilities involve the Landau prescription and the Wolf–Z (plasma dispersion) function, typically evaluated numerically for the required dimensionless phase-velocity parameter.

Blue Bird (BLBD) reported record Q3 sales with margin strength, supported by strong bus volumes, higher pricing, and resilient demand despite tariff headwinds. Its backlog remains robust at 3,900 units, supporting continued topline growth into FY25 despite near-term order softness tied to tariff uncertainty. The company is investing in new facilities, product innovation, and federal EV funding for long-term growth and market share gains. The passage maintains a Buy rating due to attractive valuation, healthy demand, margin expansion, and a positive long-term outlook despite short-term EV risks.

On Friday, the stock market fell sharply, with the Dow dropping more than 600 points—the biggest single-day decline since Brexit—and major weekly declines over the last two years. The downturn affected stocks, bonds, and commodities, and major indices including the Standard & Poor’s and NASDAQ also fell about 2% (the Dow closer to 2.5%). The passage attributes the drop to investor panic over higher interest rates after the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ jobs report showed January average wages rose the most since 2009. Although analysts largely do not expect the move to indicate broader economic trouble, they view the correction as overdue and as a return to more normal growth patterns that may involve more volatility.

In June 2009, Massachusetts General Hospital’s Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA) task force met because PATA had long struggled with inefficiencies and patient wait times, despite efforts to address them. A letter to the hospital president described a visit where the patient and mother spent nearly four hours at PATA, with only about 1½ hours of face time with providers. The passage explains that PATA performs required pre-admission work-ups for outpatients and that its capacity constraints and scheduling practices affected patient experiences and OR operations. It outlines PATA’s staffing model, clinic layout, appointment scheduling, check-in and vitals/EKG steps, roles of the charge nurse, RNs, and anesthesiologists, and how variability and manual processes contributed to long appointment lengths and uneven clinic flow. The task force formed in 2008 aimed to focus on changes internal to PATA, and by May 2009 an MBA intern conducted a time study and current-state assessment to evaluate process performance and potential efficiency improvements.

The passage describes the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) and how guest and hypervisor communicate via Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). SEV-ES/SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state so the hypervisor cannot directly access it, while NAE events allow the guest to selectively expose required register state through the GHCB. The document’s purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area and the required NAE events and guest state for interoperability across hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. It defines the GHCB size (4 KB), GHCB/VMGEXIT protocol negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement (bitmap limited to 52 bits), and the GHCB MSR protocol including registering/unregistering the GHCB GPA. It also covers NAE handling requirements such as resetting and using VALID_BITMAP, supported NAE events, error reporting via SW_EXITINFO fields, and examples for GHCB negotiation and GHCB/VMGEXIT. Further sections discuss SEV-SNP secrets page reserved area format changes, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, and SNP guest request events, including SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request, where the extended event returns certificate data identified by GUID with specific paging and table layout requirements.

Stimulant medication such as methylphenidate is widely used to treat ADHD, but long-term effects on the developing human brain are not well understood. The study used a naturalistic 4-year follow-up of participants from a prior randomized controlled trial (ePOD-methylphenidate) and assessed dopamine-reactivity using non-invasive pharmacological MRI, measuring resting cerebral blood flow (CBF) and CBF response to an acute methylphenidate challenge at baseline and after four years. The final sample included 32 adolescents and 24 adults at follow-up.

The study found no evidence that stimulant medication use was associated with long-term changes over time in resting CBF or in CBF response to methylphenidate in any of the predefined regions of interest. However, stimulant medication use showed age-dependent associations: thalamic resting rCBF and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) CBF response to the challenge were linked to the extent of stimulant exposure during follow-up in an age-dependent manner. These associations were not related to changes in ADHD symptom severity. Exploratory analyses found whole-brain CBF response was associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution, but not with dopamine transporter or dopamine receptor distributions.

The authors conclude there is no evidence of long-lasting effects on dopamine system development, but an age-dependent association exists between mPFC dopamine-reactivity estimates and extent of stimulant treatment, suggesting potential predictive value for medication use after ADHD diagnosis.

The passage says the team’s goal is to play well on Saturday night to earn an opportunity to play another game. It describes the team as healthy, rested, and energetic, except for Dwayne being hurt in the series. It highlights a player’s impact on physical play and offense, especially forechecking, and says the team will use the same approach by staying confident in their game plan, executing it, and expecting a favorable result if they play well.

A linguistics expert, Martin O’Leary, describes how seemingly unrelated words share roots traced back to Proto-Indo-European (PIE), proposed as a “mother tongue” spoken between about 4,500 and 2,500 BC. He links examples such as “architect” and “dachshund” to PIE “teks” (“to weave”), and explains that such shared derivations are called cognates. The passage also outlines how PIE words evolved through branches into modern languages, gives additional word pairings (including “blue,” “phlegm,” and “flamingo” from PIE “bhel,” and “sh*t” and “science” from PIE “sek”), and notes that O’Leary posted charts on Twitter that received many retweets and comments.

The passage describes health literacy as a key determinant of health associated with negative outcomes, and notes that WHO and governments have incorporated it to address health inequities. It defines health literacy as involving everyday management of health information and communication, and presents two components—personal health literacy and the health literacy environment—based on ACSQHC. It reports that studies have often focused on adults’ personal health literacy, neglecting the school health literacy environment, especially for children and adolescents and the professionals involved, such as teachers. Teachers are positioned to deliver health education and influence children’s health literacy. The study described uses a cross-sectional design to survey 7,264 teaching staff from 11 schools in Zhengzhou, Henan, China, collecting data on sociodemographics, personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes (health status, health-compromising behaviours, health service use, and healthcare cost). Findings show that 56.9% of teachers had inadequate or problematic personal health literacy and 31.0% perceived their schools as having a supportive health literacy environment. Lower personal health literacy and less supportive school health literacy environment were associated with poorer health status, more health-compromising behaviours, more health service use, and higher healthcare costs. The authors conclude that both individual and organizational approaches to improving health literacy may benefit teachers’ health outcomes and help reduce health disparities.

Former music teacher Robert Pickell, who died in July after falling through his roof, was honored at Webster Elementary with the dedication of two recycled buddy benches. More than a hundred staff, students, friends, and family members gathered, and students wrote goodbye messages for Pickell. Current music teacher Tricia Witmen said the benches are meant to provide a friend to whoever sits on them, reflecting Pickell’s teaching, and staff and students also planted a tree next to the building for a plaque once it is ready.

When the ADS7828 enters hold mode, it captures the voltage on the selected CHx analog input pin on its internal capacitor array. During sampling, the source charges an internal sampling capacitor (typically 25 pF), and once fully charged no further input current flows; the transferred charge depends on the device conversion rate. The ADS7828 can use either an internal 2.5 V reference or an external reference, and the LSB size equals the reference voltage divided by 4096, with lower reference increasing the impact of offset/gain and internal noise. Internal noise is typically 0.32 LSB peak-to-peak with a 2.5 V reference and 16 LSBs with a 50 mV external reference, and it can be reduced by averaging conversions. The device communicates over I2C as a slave, supporting standard (100 kHz), fast (400 kHz), and high-speed (3.4 MHz) modes, with defined START/STOP and data validity rules, byte-wise transfers, and acknowledge behavior. Data reading depends on mode: in F/S mode, conversion data can be read after initiating conversions, while in HS mode the clock is stretched to wait for conversion completion; repeated START is used to maintain bus operation. The internal reference defaults off at power-on and requires proper command-byte control and settling time for 12-bit accuracy when turned on. For layout, the SAR architecture is sensitive to glitches, requiring clean, well-bypassed power and proper ground connection, and external reference noise/ripple can appear directly in digital results.

An engineering firm, Vert Rotors, has developed a scaled-up version of its patented small-compressor technology for industrial use. The VERT.500 is described as oil-free, offering clean air, energy efficiency, and low noise, and was developed with Scotland’s Advanced Manufacturing and Automation Centre. The firm says it can reduce costs for noise protection, lower electricity bills, and cut CO2 emissions for users such as hospitals, food businesses, and electronics manufacturers. Vert Rotors, founded in 2013 and based in Lancashire, previously produced ultra-compact gas compressors and has announced a new “super-compressor” for Scotland’s emerging space industry.

The passage reports several market headlines and provides commentary on market performance and outlook. It says the S&P 500 closed at its lowest level since early July, fell 2.36% last week, and may be consolidating though a deeper correction is possible. It notes the VIX rose to 21.90, its highest since June 23, and discusses that VIX direction can relate to market reversal probabilities. It also covers oil falling after tariff uncertainty and OPEC+ announcements, including a planned September production increase and concerns about demand due to softer jobs and weak PMI data. The outlook suggests the S&P 500 may open higher, either as a short-term bounce within consolidation or as part of a broader downtrend, with this week’s focus on earnings.

The passage discusses relying on trusted people for comfort and guidance, emphasizing communication as an early step. It also highlights putting in effort, trusting initial steps, working hard, and aiming to keep up speed and pace. The speaker mentions leadership experience, control over effort but not outcomes, and keeping a key player involved despite the challenges, noting that the player made a sacrifice for the team.

The passage describes interfacial mobility as a coarse-grained parameter that strongly influences microstructural evolution and material behavior, and explains challenges in connecting atomistic mobility data to coarse-grained models, especially for solute–interface interactions involving solute-drag. It notes that interface mobility results from a hierarchy of atomic sub-processes with various mechanisms depending on conditions, and that mobility is commonly extracted from molecular dynamics using either capillary fluctuation (equilibrium fluctuations) or linear-response (driven steady-state velocity). However, these methods assume Markovian, memory-free interfacial motion, while the passage states that relaxation-time hierarchies create memory effects that can cause transient sub-diffusion and complicate mobility extraction over MD-accessible times. It says non-Markovian memory makes the standard overdamped Langevin description inadequate, and that generalized memory-aware approaches from biochemistry can extract memory kernels and extrapolate to long-time diffusion. The authors then state they adapt these ideas using a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model to study coupling among solute, interface migration, and memory, demonstrating inconsistency with the capillary fluctuation method and proposing alternative mobility extraction and a time-convolutionless approach.

Intel is expected to mark the 40th anniversary of its 8086 processor by releasing the Core i7-8086K. Online retailer listings reported by Videocardz suggest a maximum clock speed of 5GHz, with six cores and 12 threads, and an L3 cache of 12MB, matching the Core i7-8700K (4.7GHz). The K-series chip would be overclockable and, if it is a speed-binned “cherry-picked” version of the i7-8700K, it may offer more overclocking headroom. The passage notes that speed-binned CPUs are already listed by retailers and cites examples. The 8086 launched in 1978 and influenced the x86 architecture. The i7-8086K is described as having near-identical specifications to the i7-8700K, but could still offer performance gains, with an expected price about $100 more than the i7-8700K (around $480).

The passage discusses female genital mutilation (FGM) and Canada’s connection to it, in response to claims that such “barbaric practices” do not occur in North America. It cites U.S. allegations against Detroit doctor Jumana Nagarwala for illegal genital mutilation of two seven-year-old girls and possible additional cases. It notes that the Ontario Human Rights Commission says reliable statistics are unavailable but there is evidence FGM is practiced in Ontario and across Canada, including instances where families send daughters out of Canada for the procedure. It describes FGM as an ancient cultural practice performed worldwide, especially in Africa, and mentions that some related procedures may occur later in life in Canada. The passage also references infibulation and reported cases involving reinfibulation requests, and includes statements from Canadian medical professionals arguing caregivers should not permit genital mutilation without clinical necessity. It concludes that FGM is not a Canadian value and advocates screening would-be citizens.

The memorandum examines the context of an inquiry after creating a skeleton organization, describing expectations for postwar developments. It predicts increasing German peace propaganda to lure Allied Left groups with minimal, formula-based concessions and claims German proposals are aimed at weak points in the Allied alliance. It cites effects of the Reichstag resolution and the Stockholm conference plan on Russia and Western nations, and notes parallel tensions in Central Europe that strain the Allies and pull forces in Germany. It says Germany’s offensive is countered by suppressing responsive opinions and by the President’s reply to the Pope, which it portrays as unifying the Allies through broadly acceptable purposes. The passage also states that Allied governments may not have replied to the Pope due to tense domestic political situations, and argues that resistance to “peace terms” comes from concern that focusing on territory would damage morale and split the coalition.

The speaker says the team has to keep a focused mindset by reminding players to avoid distractions, especially in Calgary, which they expect to be “crazy.” They describe tonight as a hard-fought battle that they “chipped away” in, with Olie performing strongly. The speaker adds that success comes from sticking to the game plan, and the team will refocus and be ready after going back and preparing tomorrow, noting that many players have been on the same page all year and during the playoffs.

The passage describes an epidemiological modeling study of the first COVID-19 wave in the Netherlands, motivated by the uneven spatial and temporal distribution of infections and healthcare burden. It argues that subnational, municipality-level non-pharmaceutical interventions could reduce unnecessary societal burden and potentially improve resource use, economic outcomes, and reduce adherence fatigue, but highlights challenges in separating epidemiological dynamics from heterogeneous human behavior and requires rich, high-resolution data.

Using Netherlands data on demography, mobility, mixing, hospitalization, and seroprevalence, the authors develop a municipality-level, hour-resolved agent-based framework that builds a dynamic proxy contact network from demographic stratification, mobility flows, and mixing patterns, then simulates transmission using an SEIR model with interventions represented in four wave phases. The wave runs from February 27 to June 1, 2020, divided into phases with progressively stricter measures and then gradual lifting.

The model is calibrated to national hospital admissions using four transmission parameters (one per phase) and validated by reproducing observed demographic and geographic patterns. Results suggest mobility reductions contributed most to epidemic control; behavioral changes had a smaller but notable impact, while school closure had little impact in their analysis due to relatively late closure timing.

The study then evaluates subnational implementation of municipality-level interventions using prevalence thresholds (3%, 1%, 0.33%, 0.1%) for initiating lockdown when local infectious prevalence exceeds the threshold. It finds higher thresholds lead to more cumulative hospital admissions but fewer municipalities undergoing interventions, and lower thresholds yield hospital admissions closer to a national lockdown with more municipalities later initiating interventions. The authors conclude that, with appropriate local infection monitoring, subnational strategies could lower societal burden while maintaining comparable health outcomes, and discuss limitations and potential extensions of their framework.

On February 7, 2013, the MIT Sloan Women in Management (SWIM) leadership team faced a decision whether to cancel, modify, or proceed with its 3rd annual conference amid uncertain winter-storm forecasts. The conference planning involved co-presidents Rachel, Lea, and Tarini, and conference directors Janet and Merrill, along with committees for speaker recruitment, marketing, operations, and sponsorship. Despite earlier setbacks in speaker recruitment and a key director’s departure to a start-up, all 15 speakers were confirmed, ticket sales reached 500, and $38,000 in sponsorship funds was raised. As weather predictions worsened in the days leading up to the event, attendee questions and sponsor concerns increased, and MIT closure remained a possibility. At 1:30–2:00 PM on February 7, the team met with an SLO facilitator to weigh options, including canceling before vendors set up, holding a half-day conference, or waiting for more information. The passage ends with the team discussing the potential impacts of each choice as the decision approached.

Scientists studied 105 pet dogs to test how strongly they were motivated by toys such as balls, plush toys, and tug toys. In experiments where toys were inaccessible or placed in closed boxes, researchers measured dogs’ reactions and how quickly they calmed down after toy removal. Using a scoring system, 33 dogs showed signs described as “addictive-like” toy-play behavior, with the drive linked to the play itself rather than the toy. This intense motivation was more common in terriers and shepherds, and an unpublished survey of about 1,600 dogs suggested only about 3% would be classified as having addictive-like behavior toward toys. The researcher cautioned against equating human and dog behavioral addictions, but said the findings highlight the value of play for the dog-human relationship.

The passage explains that baking powder and baking soda are not interchangeable, even though both help batter and dough rise. It states that baking powder contains baking soda plus additional ingredients that cause it to react differently, while baking soda is a base that bubbles when mixed with acids. It notes substitution ratios: 2–3 tsp baking powder for 1 tsp baking soda, or 1 tsp baking powder plus 1 tsp vinegar or lemon juice for 1/2 tsp baking soda. It also gives shelf-life information: baking powder lasts 3–12 months and expires faster in humid climates, and can be tested by adding water to see if it bubbles. Baking soda is said to last longer if sealed and kept cool, has no expiration date, and can be tested by adding vinegar to see if it bubbles.

In September, Federal Reserve officials were strongly inclined to lower interest rates, with the main disagreement over whether there would be two or three total cuts by the end of 2025. Minutes released Wednesday said almost all participants noted the central bank should cut due to labor market weakness, but most judged it would be appropriate to ease further over the remainder of the year. The “dot plot” showed a 10-9 split, with the slim majority expecting two more cuts before year-end. While the full FOMC voted 11-1 to lower the benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point, officials differed on how aggressive easing should be for the rest of 2025 and later years. The minutes also noted concerns about a weakening labor market and that downside risks to employment had increased while upside inflation risks had diminished or not increased. The discussion included tariffs, and policymakers’ views on rates matched a Fed survey of primary dealers. The passage also mentions that a government shutdown could disrupt data collection, potentially affecting decisions if it lasts until the Oct. 28-29 meeting.

The passage introduces LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method for distinguishing large reasoning models (LRMs) by their reasoning patterns using only their outputs. LOT builds a human-readable set of distinguishing reasoning features through three stages—feature proposal from paired reasoning traces, annotation of features in new traces via natural-language definitions with PoR/BoR vector encodings, and training a logistic classifier—while iteratively expanding features when classification fails. Applied to 12 open-source LRMs across five datasets, LOT achieves 80–100% classification accuracy when models differ substantially and outperforms few-shot prompting, VML, and a fixed human-defined taxonomy, while also providing interpretable explanations of reasoning differences. The authors find systematic effects of parameter scale, base model family, and task-domain fine-tuning on reasoning habits, and link these differences to performance gaps via correlation and test-time intervention. In a case study, modifying smaller Qwen3 models’ reasoning behaviors improves their GPQA-Diamond accuracy by 3.3–5.7%.

Brokerages covering Comcast Corporation (NASDAQ: CMCSA) have a consensus rating of “Buy,” with 22 analysts giving buy recommendations and one giving a strong buy. The average twelve-month target price is $79.31. Several firms raised price targets and/or upgraded ratings, including Jefferies (to $86), Deutsche Bank (to $88), Instinet (to $85), Macquarie (to $77), and RBC Capital Markets (to $80). Recent insider sales were reported by EVP Arthur R. Block and EVP Neil Smit. In the last quarter, insiders sold 229,839 shares valued at $17,165,153, while company insiders own 1.27% and institutional investors own 82.03%. Comcast opened at $75.71 and has a market cap of $179.87 billion; it reported $0.89 EPS for the quarter and revenue of $21 billion. A quarterly dividend of $0.1575 per share is scheduled to be paid April 26 to shareholders of record April 5. The company also announced a 2-for-1 stock split payable after the closing bell on February 17, with the split scheduled for February 20.

The lecture discusses policy motivated by behavioral economics, focusing on “internalities,” which arise when people do not fully account for the costs or benefits they impose on their future self. It defines paternalism as attempts to influence or control conduct for people’s own good, and explains when such intervention may be warranted, including issues like self-control problems, inconsistent preferences, limited attention, and learning failures, while noting that motivated beliefs and preference-based choices may not justify intervention. It distinguishes hard paternalism (forcing choices or significantly changing prices through bans, taxes, and mandates) from soft paternalism, including libertarian paternalism (nudges that preserve choice) and asymmetric paternalism (helping those who make mistakes while minimally affecting those who optimize). The lecture outlines arguments against paternalism, such as government information and knowledge limits, heterogeneity, regulatory capture/corruption concerns, and respect for freedom of choice, and also lists arguments in favor, including that people make mistakes and may not want to make complex choices themselves, and that soft paternalism may allow opt-out options. It reviews examples of popular paternalistic policies (e.g., Social Security, Medicare, retirement menu restrictions, safety regulations, mandatory education, cigarette taxes, and mask mandates) and describes why some policies are unpopular (e.g., helmets/seatbelts) and others may be contentious due to externalities. It presents the Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) plan as a successful libertarian-paternalism approach to increase 401(k) savings by using voluntary opt-in, defaults that increase contributions after pay raises, and mechanisms related to present bias and loss aversion. It also examines limits of market solutions for self-control problems and argues that markets can both help and exploit consumers, leading to the role of regulation and disclosure (e.g., Consumer Financial Protection Bureau). The lecture concludes by noting that nudges can help but may also backfire, some people dislike being nudged and should be allowed to opt out, the market does not solve everything, and reducing “sludges” (bad nudges that hinder good choice) can be important, emphasizing that psychological considerations matter for economic behavior and policy design.

A new study on catching cold or flu germs during air travel found that sitting in a window seat and not moving until the flight ends is likely to reduce exposure. Researchers tested cabin surfaces and air on 10 flights, observing only one coughing person and finding none of 18 cold and flu viruses tested for, which they said may reflect luck. The study involved modeling and simulations of a hypothetical infectious aisle passenger and concluded that, on average, about one of roughly 150 passengers would be infected. The researchers also reported that 38% of passengers never left their seats, 38% left once, 13% left twice, and 11% left more than twice; movement was highest among aisle seat passengers. The highest risk was for the 11 people closest to an infected passenger. Outside experts said the small study would be difficult to generalize to broader disease risks, but noted its novelty for airplanes.

Amazon has updated its Alexa assistant to add support for Outlook.com calendars. Outlook users can add their calendars in the iOS Alexa app under Settings -> Calendar, enabling connected Alexa-powered devices to let users ask Alexa about upcoming events or add events via voice commands. Amazon still does not officially support Apple Calendar, but a basic skill on Github can read upcoming events from the native Apple app. Separately, Amazon added hands-free Alexa support to its Tap portable speakers via an over-the-air update, allowing Alexa to be invoked by voice without pressing a button, while maintaining about eight hours of battery life and allowing listening mode to be slept with the power button. Tap speakers also support “echo spatial perception” to route commands to the closest Alexa device.

The passage argues that modern basketball has made defense more important, and it presents SOS pressure defense as a strategy that coaches can adopt regardless of their preferred defensive system. It says successful teams will increasingly use pressure strategies to replace or reinforce past containment defenses. The teaching approach includes a logical progression of individual to team pressure fundamentals, consistent S-O-S key words to trigger on- and off-ball actions, and “operation checkpoint” pressure that directs opponents away from areas at least 18 feet from the hoop. It also encourages two-on-two switching against screens, emphasizes starting break prevention in the backcourt immediately after a rebound, and assigns each defender a clear pressure role so the five players execute together to limit offensive options, create turnovers, and force opponents away from high-percentage scoring.

The passage discusses players’ performances and team leadership during the playoffs, emphasizing one player’s commitment to hard, gritty play and forechecking. It highlights how, as the team faces elimination, players and captains supply their own energy, and coaches reflect on what the team wants to change. It also notes the importance of playing with energy and discipline in early minutes, staying motivated to keep playing hockey, and taking advantage of breaks gained through matchups. The passage references experience handling endurance and overtime situations, strong competition between goaltenders, and overall determination from both teams. It concludes by praising specific contributions, including goalie performance, the impact of returning player Langenbrunner, and Brett Hull’s “little” and gritty work.

A University of Calgary–co-authored study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Science examined dinosaur egg incubation by analyzing fossilized embryos of Protoceratops from Mongolia and Hypacrosaurus from Alberta. By counting daily growth lines in developing teeth, researchers estimated incubation times of nearly three months for Protoceratops and six months for Hypacrosaurus. The findings suggest dinosaur incubation was more similar to primitive reptiles than to birds, indicating birds evolved faster incubation after branching from other dinosaurs. The study also links longer dinosaur incubation and the time and resources needed to reach adult size to disadvantages during the end-Cretaceous extinction, when non-avian dinosaurs went extinct but birds survived. The paper’s authors include Gregory Erickson, Darla Zelenitsky, Mark Norell, and David Kay.

The passage describes how challenges to President Trump’s order ending birthright citizenship, which guarantees citizenship to those born in the United States, moved back to the Supreme Court. After the order was issued on Jan. 20, federal courts issued nationwide and classwide injunctions. The Supreme Court, in a 6-3 decision, repudiated universal nationwide injunctions, holding that such authority depended on historical precedent, and otherwise left narrower-injunction questions to lower courts. Subsequent rulings by district courts and the 1st and 9th Circuits upheld injunctions or found the executive order likely or plainly invalid under the Fourteenth Amendment. The Trump administration signaled it would seek Supreme Court review and ultimately petitioned for review, with Solicitor General D. John Sauer urging the Court to take up the 9th Circuit and New Hampshire decisions. The passage also notes likely timelines for oral argument in 2026 and a decision in the following term, if four justices vote to take the case.

Andrew Anton Sabo appeals his conviction after pleading guilty to possessing cocaine with intent to deliver (a second or subsequent offense) and being a felon in possession of firearms. He argues that evidence seized during a no-knock search of his residence should have been suppressed because the search-warrant affidavit lacked probable cause, failed to support a Franks-Mann hearing for alleged false statements, and supported denial of his motion to disclose the informant’s identity. The passage describes how a citizen informant reported that Sabo possessed firearms and processed and packaged cocaine, and how Officer Ayala corroborated details through independent investigation and surveillance. The trial court found the informant reliable, denied suppression, declined to hold a Franks-Mann hearing, and denied disclosure of the informant’s identity. The appellate court reviews probable cause and credibility issues, concludes the trial court’s findings were reasonable and not clearly erroneous, and affirms the judgment.

The passage describes background on distributed systems, CDNs/overlay networks, WANs, and MPLS, and explains an approach to use Internet-based overlay routing for secure, optimized WAN delivery, including IPsec traffic. It then presents techniques for selecting an overlay network ingress edge region using DNS-based hostname mapping and IKEv2. A customer router resolves a service hostname via an authoritative DNS to establish an outer IPsec tunnel to an initial overlay edge; the edge performs a secondary DNS lookup to determine if it is the appropriate ingress region and, if not, issues an IKEv2 redirect to redirect the router to a better edge. Additional periodic checks can lead the edge to drop liveness probes so the customer router initiates another service hostname lookup and reconnects. The passage also outlines related CDN/overlay infrastructure, an overlay IP (OIP) routing mechanism, and how NEdge regions support IPsec tunnel entry using overlay routing capabilities and liveness probing/failover.

The passage explains shock- and fan-forming behavior of inviscid Burgers’ equation and introduces related nonlinear PDEs, including the Korteweg–de Vries (KDV) equation and Hamilton–Jacobi–type equations. It focuses on solving Burgers’ equation starting from a delta-function (point source) by reasoning that the solution should consist of a fan followed by a shock. An exact formula involving minimization is presented as producing the solution for general initial data, and the shock position is determined using conservation of total mass, leading to a shock location \(X=\sqrt{2t}\). The proposed solution is checked against the shock jump condition and the entropy condition. The passage also derives the exact solution formula via Burgers’ equation with viscosity, using variable changes that convert it into the heat equation and then take the limit as viscosity goes to zero. Finally, it discusses why KDV is famous for being integrable, describing numerical observations of soliton interactions that preserve wave shapes and noting other integrable nonlinear equations, while contrasting them with the unsolved global-existence question for Navier–Stokes equations in 3D.

The passage describes how PMC operational clock writes differ from DD Local bus timing and use a shadow register technique to transfer 32-bit write data. Because byte lane information is not used when updating operational registers, updates occur at 32-bit granularity regardless of write size, and the inactive byte lane retains previous data, allowing corruption of future writes. Corruption can be local (same register on a future write) or cross (an unrelated register). It notes that while the ACPI specification allows WORD and BYTE accesses to specific ACPI registers (PM1_STS, PM1_EN, PM1_CNT, and PM2_CNT), such byte accesses cause the described corruption, whereas proprietary non-ACPI registers are restricted to DWORD only. As a resolution, an SMI I/O trap can be set up for the ACPI defined registers to control accesses and prevent the issue.

AfriForum said forensic scientist Dr David Klatzow has begun investigating the possible cause of the Knysna fires and will first gather relevant information. He will meet with role-players for their inputs and flew over the disaster area to assess the fire’s extent and whether wind could spread it. The public is invited to send information to reint@afriforum.co.za.

Mercedes team chief Toto Wolff said that “stress,” “tension,” and “disruption” between drivers may be necessary to extend Mercedes’ dominance. He contrasted the issue-free partnership of Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas with the prior bitter Rosberg–Hamilton rivalry, which still coincided with Mercedes success in drivers’ and constructors’ championships. After Rosberg’s retirement, Wolff noted the Hamilton–Bottas pairing worked well, and he suggested Bottas should challenge Hamilton next season to raise their performance. Wolff argued the team does not aim to “build a new family” but to be effective, and success requires a balance of stress and calmness.

Astronomers observed a rogue planet, Cha 1170-7626, about 600 light-years away, undergoing the fastest growth rate ever recorded for any planet, increasing by sucking up surrounding gas and dust at up to 6 billion metric tons per second. Using ultraviolet, visible, and infrared observations from the Very Large Telescope and later data from the James Webb Space Telescope, researchers found that between late June and August the planet rapidly accreted material up to eight times faster than a few months earlier. During this period the planet and surrounding disk became hotter and brighter, and the disk showed signs of water vapor. The long, star-like growth spurt and hints of regular binging suggest a starlike origin for free-floating planets, and the team plans to observe again later this year and search for more rogue planets during similar gluttonous periods.

A June 29, 2001 email from Miyung Buster to Ann Schmidt and many others shares links to multiple news articles about California and U.S. energy issues. The included articles describe: a California Senate committee voting to hold Enron and Mirant in contempt for refusing to turn over thousands of pages of documents; Southern California Edison’s parent obtaining $1.19 billion in financing to help meet debts; state regulators exempting oil refineries from rolling blackouts to prevent gasoline shortages; criticism and debate over Bush energy proposals and the pace of congressional action; and federal regulators approving temporary electricity price controls for New York while expressing concerns about limiting legitimate high prices. Other included pieces discuss conservation funding, energy market reporting and analyses, efforts to reduce power peaks via internet-based demand exchange programs, and additional stories on natural gas price cuts and energy conservation measures.

A 36-year-old man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, was arrested at the Coachella festival in Indio, California, on suspicion of stealing over 100 mobile phones. Police said festival-goers used the “Find My Phone” function to trace missing devices and that Henao was detained by security before officers arrived. Officers allegedly found a backpack containing over 100 stolen phones; some were returned to their owners and the rest were turned in to lost and found. Henao was charged with grand theft and receiving stolen property, and was released after posting $10,000 bail. The passage also lists performances and highlights from Coachella weekend one.

Amarin Corp Ads (NASDAQ:AMRN) shares rose 1.33% in the most recent session. The passage argues that Baker Mayfield is the best quarterback prospect in Thursday’s NFL draft, despite widespread debate fueled by off-field and personal narratives. It cites Pro Football Focus analytics, including unified grading this year, and claims Mayfield ranked top in passer rating against pressure over three seasons and was PFF’s most accurate quarterback in the class across all throw depths. It compares his deep-ball performance favorably with Josh Allen, noting similar measured arm velocity, and says Mayfield excels at intermediate throws. The passage also mentions concerns such as his height (under 6-foot-1 at the combine), unnecessary sacks, and potential hesitation over his college Air Raid offense, along with reports that teams either strongly like or dislike him. It concludes that Mayfield is likely to be drafted in the top five.

Thruxton’s 50th anniversary meeting will feature historic races, high-speed demonstrations, and the opening of the new £2million Thruxton Centre. The weekend includes a demonstration run by Karun Chandhok in an ex-Keke Rosberg Cosworth DFV-powered Williams FW08C, with Nigel Mansell and Murray Walker opening the centre on Sunday. Formula 2 events from 1968 to 1984 will be marked by the return of the Formula 2 March 722 driven by Niki Lauda in 1972, along with other period races such as the Woodcote Trophy, Stirling Moss Trophy, Spirit of Thruxton single-seaters, Historic Formula Ford 1600s, and Historic Touring Car Challenge races.

Texas Instruments provides technical and reliability data (including data sheets), design resources (including reference designs), application or other design advice, web tools, safety information, and other resources “as is” with all faults, disclaiming all express and implied warranties, including those of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. The resources are intended for skilled developers, who are responsible for selecting TI products, designing, validating, and testing applications, and ensuring compliance with applicable standards and requirements. The resources may change without notice; permission is granted only to use them for development of an application using the described TI products, with restrictions on reproduction and display.
