TI’s product warranties are governed by its Terms of Sale or applicable terms, and providing resources does not expand or alter warranties or disclaimers. TI rejects any additional or different terms proposed. The notice includes TI’s mailing address and a 2025 copyright.

The passage describes NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end brain-decoding framework that conditions a pre-trained Stable Diffusion latent diffusion model directly on fMRI-derived parcel-wise token embeddings via cross-attention, bypassing intermediate external embedding spaces used in typical two-stage pipelines. It outlines data preprocessing using surface-based fMRI in fsaverage space, Schaefer parcellation into 500 parcels per hemisphere, selection of top k parcels by SNR (reported results for p = 200), and a parcel-wise linear mapping from padded vertex responses to token embeddings. The model is trained by updating only the parcel-wise mapper and cross-attention modules while keeping other Stable Diffusion parameters frozen, using fMRI token dropout and min-SNR loss weighting for training stability. For evaluation, a separate brain encoder selects candidate decoded images by choosing the one with the highest Pearson correlation to measured fMRI activity. The passage also presents IBBI (Image-Brain BI-directional interpretability), which uses cross-attention dynamics across diffusion steps to quantify both parcel contributions over timesteps and ROI attention maps showing where brain ROIs direct attention in the reconstructed images, along with a causal perturbation analysis via ROI masking. Experiments are reported on NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon, using multiple image quality metrics, and the discussion emphasizes improved decoding quality—especially for high-level semantic metrics—plus interpretability insights into the generative process.

Antonio Conte told Chelsea players to focus on getting a result at Huddersfield Town in the Premier League on Tuesday and not think about their February Champions League last-16 tie with Barcelona. After Chelsea’s 1-0 loss to West Ham, Conte said the league is dangerous, challenged the team to change the result, and insisted they must play each game at full strength. He also said Chelsea cannot defend their title and needs to fight for a Champions League place, noting the team’s title chances are unlikely after four losses in 16 games. Chelsea are third in the table, while Huddersfield are 12th.

Theresa May is reported to ask her Cabinet colleagues to back “the softest possible Brexit” at a Brexit summit on Friday at her Chequers country home. According to Robert Peston, May plans a trade deal where the UK continues to obey some EU laws, including product standards for goods and agricultural products, ends freedom of movement for people but makes it easier for EU citizens to live and work in the UK, and involves the UK collecting border tariffs on imports at the EU’s common customs tariff rate. The passage also describes internal Conservative Party conflict, including claims of a possible leadership “coup” and warnings from Phillip Lee and William Hague about leadership challenges and ministers pushing for a clean break.

The speaker says they have been working all their life for the Stanley Cup finals and are focusing on a big game tomorrow night, taking it one game at a time. They discuss calls with the league, respecting the league’s decisions and saying a specific official did a good job. They say they have not yet received information but will likely get it later today, and they emphasize awareness around the net to avoid bumping the goalie, while staying smart to avoid putting their team down a man. They mention that teammates’ different strengths matter, including moving the puck and rush play, going to the net, creating traffic, and playing with poise around the net, particularly referring to three players. They conclude by saying preparing for the next game continues, and outside hockey they focus on family, mentioning managing their baseball fantasy team and joking about another player’s team struggling.

In an original proceeding under C.A.R. 21, petitioners Erin Bond and her siblings sought reversal of a Denver District Court judge’s denial of a protective order. The petitioners, who sued YMCA of the Rockies for negligence after Erin was severely injured, sought to prevent YMCA from obtaining therapists’ notes and records concerning psychological evaluations and treatment. The district judge ruled that the records should be furnished to the defendant, with confidentiality safeguards.

The Colorado Supreme Court held that although physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges were waived because the petitioners placed their mental condition in issue through claims for mental suffering and psychiatric expenses, the district court abused its discretion by denying the protective order without balancing the parties’ interests. The Supreme Court remanded for reconsideration using the correct balancing standard, noting that the trial court may use procedures such as in camera review, in camera inspection of documents, and court-appointed experts, and may employ protective orders under C.R.C.P. 26(c).

AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) announced it will shut down permanently on December 15. AIM, active since 1997 and once a leading U.S. instant messaging service, declined as cell phone text messaging and other social media platforms increased. Michael Albers said AIM was once a major part of users’ lives, including memorable screen names and away messages, and noted that communication has since changed.

The passage says that people who see the August 21 total solar eclipse will be lucky. It explains that Earth’s total eclipses occur because of a “cosmic coincidence”: the moon’s diameter is about 400 times smaller than the sun’s but about 400 times closer to Earth, allowing the moon to fully obscure the sun and reveal its corona. It also notes that over time the moon has been moving away from Earth, making past eclipses look bigger, and that in about 600 million years the moon will no longer completely cover the sun, ending total solar eclipses.

The passage describes a continuation of earlier U.S. patent applications and provides background on data center networking and virtualization. It explains how virtualization enables dynamic creation and sharing of virtual machines and virtual desktop instances, and notes that some service providers shut down resources when a customer disconnects, causing long delays upon reconnection.

It then outlines systems and methods for managing resources for virtual desktop instances in a service provider network. A computing resource instance manager may monitor connections, disconnections, and reconnections, detect explicit disconnections or inactivity, and apply configurable shutdown policies to decide whether and when to shut down underlying virtualized computing resource instances. When shutdown occurs, storage volumes may remain maintained but detached/unmounted, and upon reconnection the instance may restart and the volumes may be reattached/mounted. The manager may also build predictive models based on historical connection patterns and use the information for proactive shutdown/restart decisions and potentially billing-related events. The passage further describes example environments (including provider network components, virtualization services, IP mapping and tunneling, and PES platform concepts) and details mechanisms for detecting active sessions across multiple remote computing protocols.

The passage provides instructions and information for the SanDisk Sansa c200, including how to install or replace its lithium-ion battery, use the Hold switch to disable accidental operation, and record voice using the Record button. It explains connecting the device to a computer via a USB 2.0 port, transferring media (including using Sansa Media Converter for photos), supported still image formats, and deleting or synchronizing files, plus how to safely remove the device in MTP or MSC modes. It also covers basic usage (power on/off), navigating menus to play music, set repeat/shuffle and equalizer options, manage GoList favorites, view photos and run slideshows, use FM radio (including presets and radio recording), and configure display backlight/contrast and auto power off/sleep. The document includes an FAQ about copying and supported media formats, troubleshooting metadata and playback rights, and updating firmware, along with technical support and a 1-year limited warranty. It further includes intellectual property/protection notices, an end user license agreement describing software licensing terms, restrictions, warranty disclaimers, liability limitations, and disposal instructions.

Doctors determined that Erik’s healing process is probably complete after recent examinations, including a consult with Dr. Richardson, so one last consult occurred today. The team said they skated poorly in the game, lacked their usual legs, moved as individuals rather than a unit, and failed to get pucks through or create traffic; they took undisciplined penalties. Coach Laviolette said the opponents outskated them in all three zones, and that the team must win without excuses. The team noted they have veteran players experienced in big games and expect to be ready for the Stanley Cup final game in their building. They also said Doug would be missed, and they expect a big performance from Joe despite a recent knee surgery and ongoing hobbled limp. The coach emphasized that, once the puck drops, it is about hockey—effort, execution, and specialty teams—while acknowledging fan support and atmosphere.

The passage defines artificial intelligence (AI) and describes it as a branch of computer science that relies on data to produce insights and support decisions. It notes that AI in education (AIEd) is an emerging field with both opportunities and challenges, and it includes machine learning and deep learning as subsets. It outlines an implementation strategy for higher education institutions, including setting objectives, investing in infrastructure, preparing faculty and staff, starting with pilots, ensuring ethical and responsible use, promoting personalized learning, using predictive analytics, collaborating with EdTech providers, monitoring impact, and involving students. It emphasizes benefits of AI in higher education such as personalized learning, immersive experiences, engagement, intelligent tutoring, continuous evaluation, improved quality, efficiency, cost effectiveness, and data-driven decision-making. It also lists limitations and risks including high implementation costs, faculty training and acceptance issues, ethical concerns (bias, discrimination, transparency), data privacy concerns, dependence on technology, lack of human touch, cheating risks, and potential teacher job displacement. The passage recommends careful planning, teacher training, good infrastructure, measurable goals, evaluation, ethical safeguards, and data privacy. It concludes that AI can transform higher education if adopted responsibly, while also stressing the need for specific policies and guidelines to prevent misuse and address biases.

The passage includes elements of Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 24, 2022, including references to accounting tags and a large portion of the filing’s text. It describes Apple’s business and product lines (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Wearables, Home and Accessories), its services (such as AppleCare, cloud services, digital content platforms, and payment services), and its markets and distribution channels, along with competition and supply of components. It also discusses forward-looking statements and detailed risk factors covering macroeconomic and industry risks, the COVID-19 pandemic, competition, supply chain and component sourcing, product quality and defects, intellectual property, third-party software and digital content, human capital, technology and cybersecurity risks, legal and regulatory compliance risks, financial risks including foreign currency and credit risk, and stock price volatility. The passage further provides legal proceedings information (including Epic Games litigation), properties information (Apple headquarters in Cupertino, California), and some stockholder data as of October 14, 2022.

Zendaya spoke at the 2017 Teen Choice Awards after earlier speaking out against the Charlottesville protests. In her acceptance speech for Choice Summer Movie Actress, she urged young people to be educated, pay attention, and stand up for what they believe is right. She said they have a voice to use when something bad is happening and that they should not let others dictate what they should feel, emphasizing they are future leaders who will make the world better.

InfoWorld provides PR and usage guidelines for companies that won the InfoWorld Technology of the Year awards. It states that named winners may be referenced in press outreach, and that InfoWorld won’t disclose proprietary corporate information but may highlight information included in the original awards content. Physical awards and reprints can be ordered through the YGS Group. Winners can purchase a license to use the Technology of the Year logo, and must follow rules for proper, unaltered logo use, including spacing requirements; questions should be directed to IDG Enterprise Marketing. The passage also includes approved quote usage from an InfoWorld spokesperson, rules for referencing InfoWorld and the awards in communications (including specific naming and style conventions), and approved descriptions and boilerplate text about InfoWorld and IDG Enterprise.

The passage describes the Put-Call ratio (PCR) as a popular sentiment indicator used to gauge market conditions by measuring put open interest or volume relative to call open interest or volume for a given asset class or instrument on a daily basis. It explains that calls give the right to buy shares at a predetermined price, while puts give the right to sell shares at a predetermined price, and that puts are often likened to insurance against market drops. The passage notes that extreme PCR readings are often used contrarily to signal panic and possible market turning points, but it presents backtest-related remarks stating the Put-Call ratio has not been among the best sentiment indicators and that the authors have not used it for their trading strategies, citing their preference for other tools such as the VIX indicator. It also discusses differences between volume and open interest, the idea that different markets may require different interpretations of “good” or “bad” readings, where PCR can be found (many trading/investing websites, exchanges’ daily ratios, and self-calculation using options data), and that free downloadable sources may be hard to find. The passage concludes by giving an example backtest approach and asserting that their results suggest PCR is inferior to similar sentiment indicators.

The passage describes a UN Chronicle article by Ramu Damodaran on World Water Day, discussing how UN entities address water needs in different countries. It notes UN General Assembly “exclusive rights” over subsoil water as a metaphor for the rights of “we the peoples,” then gives examples: UNMISS improves water access in South Sudan via a hydrosystem; UNICEF Tap Project in Vietnam funds tap water for children; the National University of Singapore, via WIPO Green, develops drainage blocks for water harvesting; and UNHCR in Kyrgyzstan helps refurbish a village water project, installing 12 standpipes for about 800 people after a funding gap. The passage also references a General Assembly decision to hold an ad hoc working-level dialogue on coordinating UN water-related sustainable development goals and includes remarks by Miroslav Lajčák urging that water be treated properly to prevent conflict.

The passage describes the 2018 Chevrolet Equinox’s available 1.6L turbo-diesel engine and claims it will lead its segment in highway fuel efficiency with a 6.0 L/100km rating for the FWD model, citing lower consumption than the 2017 Toyota RAV4 hybrid and Nissan Rogue hybrid. It says the turbo-diesel is part of three all-turbocharged propulsion systems, is SAE-certified at 240 lb-ft (325 Nm), uses a variable-geometry turbocharger, includes stop/start technology, and is compatible with B20 bio-diesel. It also provides details on DEF emissions treatment, where system design and integration were done, and describes the all-new Equinox’s features and pricing, including starting prices of $27,145 and $35,645 for the turbo-diesel engine.

The LakeSmart Team returns for summer to deliver the Dock Talk program, providing cottagers with information on maintaining a healthy ecosystem on Lake of the Woods and nearby lakes. The team will answer questions and share resources at the Matiowki Farmer’s Market at the Whitecap Pavilion every Wednesday in July and August. The three-member team includes Krista Robertson, Reed Cupeiro, and Myles King, who are university students focused on environmental education; Robertson and Cupeiro are in their second year with the program. LakeSmart, an initiative of the Lake of the Woods and District Property Owners Association, is supported by sponsors. The team plans to share practical topics including healthy shorelines, a septic system checklist, invasive species prevention, safe boating practices, and the Clean, Drain and Dry program, and will also participate in presentations and IISD Experimental Lakes Area tours. Presentations can be requested through the LOWDPOA at 807-543-4287.

The passage describes AI-based image encoding and decoding using deep neural networks (DNNs). In encoding, an AI down-scaling apparatus determines whether to down-scale an original high-resolution image using a first DNN, then encodes the resulting first image and transmits image data plus AI data indicating whether down-scaling was performed and related information (e.g., target up-scaling information). In decoding, an AI decoding apparatus reconstructs a second image by decoding the received image data, determines whether AI up-scaling should be performed using the AI data, and, if enabled and available, generates and outputs a third image using an up-scaling DNN. If AI up-scaling is not performed (e.g., AI data absent, down-scaling not indicated, or the up-scaling DNN not available), the second image is output, potentially with legacy up-scaling by non-DNN scaling or via a display apparatus. The passage also outlines apparatus components, transmission formats (bitstream, or separate AI data), and DNN configuration/selection mechanisms using DNN setting information mapped to factors like resolution, bitrate, codec type, and encoding parameters.

The passage describes artificial reality/near-eye display systems that present content close to a user’s eyes and use one or more light sources driven to output different luminance levels. It proposes determining a maximum luminance location in the display based on the eye’s field of view (including the fovea or center of the field of view) and driving multiple light sources according to their locations relative to that maximum. For a given input display value, a light source closer to the maximum luminance location is driven to a higher luminance than another source farther away; related embodiments also include zone-based luminance relationships, possible limits on luminance differences, driving based on distance to the maximum location, and use of OLED or micro-LED light sources. Systems may include a display controller, an eye-tracking subsystem for determining gaze direction/eye position, and machine-readable storage medium instructions implementing the method. The passage also provides background on eye sensitivity outside the fovea and includes detailed discussion of near-eye display hardware and eye-tracking components, calibration, and controller functions.

The lecture explains the large \(N\) expansion in gauge theory as having the same mathematical structure as a string worldsheet expansion: correlation functions of gauge-invariant operators correspond to string scattering amplitudes when \(g_{\text{string}}\) is identified with \(1/N\), and external glueball (single-trace) states correspond to string states. The correspondence is framed as a topological expansion over worldsheet and Feynman diagram topologies, with higher-genus contributions related to quantum corrections to a classical string picture. The discussion notes practical difficulties in matching gauge-theory Feynman diagrams (products of propagators integrated over spacetime) to a unique string theory because one must determine the appropriate string action and because Feynman diagrams correspond to a discrete version of the continuum geometry that emerges only at strong coupling. The lecture then generalizes the idea to include quarks (fundamental fields), leading to surfaces with boundaries and a string theory description that includes open strings. It continues to discuss attempts to match four-dimensional QCD to string theory and explains why simple choices lead to conflicts (e.g., involving massless spin-2 states and dimensional consistency), motivating alternative setups such as higher uncompactified dimensions. Finally, it outlines how conformal (scale-invariant) large \(N\) gauge theories can require the dual string theory to live in anti-de Sitter space by imposing scaling symmetry on a metric ansatz, yielding an AdS metric form, and it gives a brief historical account of how these ideas developed.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted Wednesday on rape and criminal sex act charges by Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus R. Vance Jr., the first criminal case from a series of sexual misconduct allegations. Weinstein’s lawyers said he would decline to testify before the grand jury due to lack of preparation time and “political pressure,” and a statement from Weinstein’s camp said he learned of the charges and accusers’ identities only after turning himself in Friday; his request for more time was denied. Vance said attacks on survivors and the legal process were predictable and that a jury would reject them. Weinstein was charged Friday with raping one woman and compelling oral sex from another, while a grand jury continued hearing evidence. He had been freed on $1 million bail and electronic monitoring, with a court date set for July 30. The indictment follows accusations involving other women, whom Weinstein has denied, and relates to prior public pressure on Vance after he declined to prosecute in 2015; Gov. Andrew Cuomo ordered a state investigation into how that matter was handled.

Touch Football Australia and the NRL announced an “NRL Touch Premiership” to begin on May 18 as a curtain raiser to NRL matches. The competition will select male and female touch players from elite domestic and international levels, aligning teams with six NRL clubs, and will include two 30-minute games (men’s and women’s) played for seven rounds. The games will be broadcast nationally using a mix of live and delayed broadcasts. Ipswich Jillaroos star Ali Brigginshaw said the NRL/TFA partnership could boost touch football’s profile and provide publicity and a pathway between touch and rugby league, noting her own use of touch to maintain fitness. She said her Jillaroos contract likely prevents her from participating in the inaugural competition. Ipswich touch players Jake Notley, Jake Hooper, and Tayla Rosin are also mentioned as having an opportunity to play to a nationally televised audience.

The passage provides instructions for swapping a current HDD with a new SanDisk SSD. It says to shut down the computer, disconnect the power cable, and remove the battery for notebooks. It then separates steps for desktop and notebook installations: for notebooks, it notes differences from desktops and includes steps to remove and transfer brackets/adapters, align and connect the SSD to the SATA pins, replace the drive bay, reinstall the battery and power cable, and power on. For desktops, it instructs powering off and disconnecting the power cable, opening the case, removing the existing HDD by unplugging SATA data and power cables, installing the new SSD and reconnecting those cables, closing the case, plugging in, and powering on. It also mentions that a boot screen may indicate the upgrade is complete, and suggests keeping the old HDD as a backup drive, with an additional note about using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter in most desktop computers.

Leapfrog’s new Hospital Safety Grades report that many hospitals have made significant patient safety improvements, with five “A” hospitals earning the grade for the first time and a total of 46 “A” hospitals having achieved an “A” for the first time since the Safety Grade began six years ago. States with strong improvement include Rhode Island, Hawaii, Wisconsin, and Idaho, as well as Maryland and the Washington, D.C. metro area. Maryland moved out of the bottom five and now has three “A” hospitals, and Washington, D.C. saw its first “A” hospital, Sibley Memorial Hospital, since spring 2013. Overall, among about 2,500 hospitals graded, 30% earned “A,” 28% “B,” 35% “C,” 6% “D,” and 1% “F,” with no “A” hospitals in Alaska, Delaware, or North Dakota. Leapfrog also announced planned methodology updates for the Fall 2018 grading cycle and said the Safety Grade is updated every six months.

The PGA848 input circuitry has a linear operating input voltage range extending within 3V (maximum) of either power supply and maintains excellent common-mode rejection across this range at all temperatures. The valid common-mode range for valid output at no load is shown in Figures 8-4 to 8-1, and depends on input common-mode voltage, input differential voltage, gain, and reference input voltage. A typical application is provided for driving a single-ended input SAR ADC (ADS8860), including a circuit that uses separate input and output power supplies (±15V for the input stage and 5.3V for the output stage), reference components (REF6250 and an OPA192 buffer), and multiple filters to manage EMI/RFI, bandwidth, charge reservoir behavior, settling, distortion, and stability. Power supply recommendations state nominal performance with ±15V supplies and that supply voltages higher than 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines emphasize matched input paths, local bypassing, minimizing parasitic coupling and leakage at DA_IN+ and DA_IN– pins, and reducing leakage/capacitance through careful PCB practices.

The Boathouse at City Point will open on Hopewell’s riverfront on June 17. The restaurant will have 6,000 square feet of interior space, a 1,257-square-foot patio, and 2,450 square feet of event space with a tent pad for weddings, parties, and other occasions. It will be the fourth Boathouse restaurant in Central Virginia, located at 701 West Randolph Street in Hopewell. Owned by the HOUSEpitality Family restaurant group, it is described as a cornerstone of Hopewell riverfront revitalization, with similar menus to other locations using coastal elements and locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant will also offer a chef’s table for group reservations and will open daily for lunch and dinner, plus brunch on Sundays.

Madison Realty Capital provided a $137 million construction loan to JDS Development Group for Monad Terrace in South Beach, Miami. The project will be fully capitalized and includes 59 individually designed waterfront residences by architect Jean Nouvel, with private elevator access, custom kitchens and bathrooms, and outdoor terraces with lagoon and ocean views. The building will be elevated 11.5 feet for environmental responsibility and climate resilience; foundation work is nearly complete, with vertical construction expected in Spring 2018 and an estimated completion in Fall 2019. Sales are averaging nearly $2,000 per square foot, and a penthouse is under contract for $2,700 per foot, a neighborhood record. Douglas Elliman Development Marketing manages sales and marketing.

The passage says that Glibc 2.28 is nearing completion with changes building up after a release, and that it will build and run cleanly on GNU/Hurd without out-of-tree patches. It also notes many Hurd-related commits over the past month. The passage then discusses an attempt to install GNU Guix on Android devices, stating that GNU Guix can be made to run on Android smartphones/tablets but requires many steps, and that a blog post will provide knowledge and commands for installation.
