Tuberculosis is the leading infectious cause of death worldwide, and undernutrition is identified as a leading risk factor for TB and as associated with higher death, treatment failure, and relapse among people diagnosed with TB. The RATIONS study in eastern India randomized over 10,000 household contacts of persons with TB to routine TB care alone or to a 6-month food basket providing macronutrient and micronutrient support costing $13 per month. Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a 40% reduction in TB incidence over two years, and people with TB receiving nutritional support had about a 35% reduction in mortality. 

The study described here developed a Markov model to assess cost-effectiveness in India of a RATIONS-style nutritional intervention for HIV-negative household contacts of people with TB from the perspective of the central government and from a societal perspective. The model compared usual care with an intervention where household contacts received a food basket for 6 months and TB progressors received additional nutritional supplementation during TB treatment. Outcomes included TB incidence, TB deaths, DALYs, and costs over the lifetime of a simulated cohort of 100,000 contacts. 

Base case results estimated lower lifetime TB incidence and mortality with the intervention, along with fewer DALYs averted and higher total costs. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from the healthcare perspective and $184 per DALY averted from the societal perspective, both below a willingness-to-pay threshold of $550 per DALY averted. Sensitivity and probabilistic analyses found the intervention cost-effective over wide ranges, and the authors conclude that a RATIONS-style program could reduce TB incidence and mortality among household contacts while being cost-effective in settings with high TB and undernutrition burdens.

A baby girl born to a family that practices faith-healing died shortly after birth in Oregon City, and the Clackamas County Medical Examiner said she died from “complications of prematurity.” The examiner said she could have survived with immediate medical attention, and that her twin sister survived after receiving medical attention. Deputies are investigating because no one in the home called 911; a church elder contacted the medical examiner, who contacted authorities. No one has been charged, and deputies urged parents to seek professional care when crews arrived. The passage also notes that in 2011 another couple from the same church was convicted of manslaughter for refusing medical care in the death of their newborn son, and Shannon and Dale Hickman are serving six years in prison.

The lecture discusses the problem of dynamic optimality for binary search tree (BST) algorithms, asking whether there exists a single BST that is at least as good as all others for any access sequence. It defines a BST model with pointer navigation (constant-time pointer following) and rotations, and focuses on search-only operations with successful searches and no insertions/deletions.

It explains that balanced BSTs give worst-case order log n time, but dynamic optimality aims to match the offline optimal cost up to a constant factor while using online algorithms that do not know future accesses. The lecture reviews several access-dependent performance properties, including sequential access, dynamic finger, entropy, working set, and the unified property; it notes that no BST is known to achieve the unified property, and that the best known BST achieves it with an added log log n term.

A geometric framework is then introduced: map an access sequence to points with space as the x-axis and time as the y-axis, and represent a BST execution by the set of nodes “touched” during searches. The lecture states a characterization of valid BST executions in terms of an “arboral satisfaction” property on point sets. This leads to an interpretation of dynamic optimality as minimizing the number of points added to satisfy this property, though the exact optimization problem is not known to be solvable efficiently.

Finally, it describes a greedy algorithm for constructing a satisfying point set, and a way to convert the resulting offline structure into an online BST using “split trees,” supporting searches by lazily rearranging touched nodes. The lecture concludes by noting that future discussion will cover lower bounds and whether the greedy approach is nearly optimal.

Faviola Dadis said at a Los Angeles news conference that Steven Seagal sexually assaulted her in 2002 during a supposed casting session in a Beverly Hills hotel room. She alleged that during the audition, Seagal grabbed her nipples and genitals, leading her to end the audition and leave “horrified and totally violated.” Dadis said she later reported the incident to police and that Los Angeles prosecutors are reviewing her case. Seagal’s attorney did not immediately comment. Dadis said she waited to report earlier out of fear of being blacklisted, and her statement was prompted by recent allegations of sexual misconduct in the entertainment industry, including Portia de Rossi’s account. Another woman, Regina Simons, said Seagal assaulted her in 1995, and Jenny McCarthy said Seagal harassed her in 1995. Seagal denied the allegations on Facebook, and Lisa Bloom said there are no immediate plans for lawsuits.

The passage explains the AdS/CFT description of finite-temperature boundary theories on flat space and on a sphere. For a thermal CFT on flat space, the gravity dual is a black hole with a planar horizon whose topology matches the boundary. On the sphere, the physics becomes richer because the only controlling dimensionless parameter is \(rT\), leading to more intricate behavior at low and high temperatures.

The discussion then focuses on gravity solutions in global and thermal AdS, including thermal AdS (a well-defined Euclidean metric) and two black hole solutions for the same temperature: a large black hole and a small black hole. The black hole temperature has a minimum temperature, meaning the black hole solutions exist only above this threshold, and for a given temperature above the minimum there are two possible black holes. The small black hole is argued to have features like negative specific heat and is not the stable phase.

The stable phase is determined by comparing free energies (equivalently, Euclidean actions) among thermal AdS and black hole solutions using saddle-point arguments, concluding that thermal AdS dominates below a critical temperature \(T_c\), while the large black hole dominates above \(T_c\). This is identified as a first-order Hawking–Page transition, with the transition occurring when the free energies match at \(T_c\), while their derivatives differ. Finally, the passage sketches a field-theory interpretation using a toy model of \(N^2\) harmonic oscillators with an \(SU(N)\) singlet condition, relating the transition to the competition between thermal suppression and the exponential growth of the density of states at energies of order \(N^2\).

Matt Baier said the Blue Ox aimed to return to last year’s level and stayed on pace as the team entered the Region 10C tournament as the top seed and won the region title after Saturday’s championship. Bemidji had already clinched a state tournament berth, while Crookston earned its berth by beating Moorhead Miners 3-2 in extra innings. In the championship, Bemidji took a 5-0 lead, but Crookston later scored in the ninth inning to reduce the deficit; the Blue Ox won. Baier credited pitching, including Ben Thoma’s seven-inning win, and noted Crookston scored seven runs but left many runners on base. As region champion, Crookston received a first-round bye in the 48-team state tournament, while Bemidji was set to play its first game Sunday, Aug. 27. The tournament begins Friday, Aug. 18, with the state championship game on Sept. 4.

As Halloween approaches, Dale Capstick of Coxheath says she and her husband have endured nightly visits from large spiders. She reports seeing about three dozen giant house spiders since August, and after searching online learned they are Eratigena atrica. Charles Andrews captured one alive in a jar; it later died and shrank. A Nova Scotia Museum biologist, Calum Ewing, examined a photo and confirmed the species as Eratigena atrica (European house spider). Ewing says the spiders are harmless but startling, live in parts of Canada and the northwestern U.S., and were first seen in Nova Scotia in the mid-1990s. He notes they are often found in sinks or bathtubs due to smooth surfaces, build funnel-shaped webs, and likely appear because of an insect population; once prey is gone, they die of starvation or leave. Capstick hopes the spiders have vacated because she has not seen any for a few days.

Meizu’s Pro 7 and Pro 7 Plus, launched in July with starting prices of 2,880 Yuan and 3,580 Yuan, have received a price cut in China, with new prices set to start at 1,999 Yuan starting 12 December. The Pro 7 has a 5.2-inch Super AMOLED display with a secondary Super AMOLED display and two configurations with 4GB RAM plus either 64GB eMMC 5.1 (Helio P25) or 128GB storage (Helio X30). The Pro 7 Plus has a 5.7-inch Super AMOLED display with a secondary screen, two configurations with 6GB RAM and either 64GB or 128GB UFS 2.1 storage, both powered by Helio X30. Both include dual 12-megapixel rear cameras with monochrome + RGB sensors and a 16-megapixel front camera, run Flyme OS 6 based on Android Nougat, and use 3,000mAh (mCharge 3.0) and 3,500mAh (mCharge 4.0) batteries respectively, with mCharge 4.0 charging 0% to 67% in 30 minutes at 5V 5A (25W).

Rushin Shah, former head of Natural Language Understanding on Apple’s Siri team, left Apple after five years to work at Facebook’s Menlo Park headquarters. He helped launch key Siri features, including voice recognition, casual conversation and “banter” classification mechanisms, and natural language interpretation of user intentions. At Facebook, he will work on natural language and dialogue understanding, though his new role is not detailed. His departure comes as Siri faces increased competition and is viewed as less accomplished than Amazon’s Alexa and the Google Assistant. Apple has expanded Siri with recent iOS updates and a Siri-based smart speaker with far-field voice recognition, and it has not been announced who will replace Shah at Apple.

The Canadian Couch Potato podcast episode discusses the trade-off between cost and complexity in investment plans, arguing that investors should find their own balance. It features John Robertson, author of *The Value of Simple* (revised second edition), who explains options for starting with indexing, including robo-advisors and a tool called AutoInvest.ca for comparing all-in costs. The host also highlights Robertson’s course, *Practical Index Investing for Canadians*, which includes step-by-step videos for opening accounts and building portfolios at Tangerine, TD Direct Investing, and Questrade. In the “Ask the Spud” segment, the host examines Vanguard’s newly launched asset allocation ETFs, noting their low 0.22% management fee but emphasizing trade-offs such as portfolio size, regular contributions (automation available with index mutual funds and robo-advisors but not ETFs), ETF trading experience, account complexity, and target asset mix. The episode states that Vanguard’s ETFs are best for investors targeting 60% or 80% equities and that other target mixes may not be available.

HPE is introducing the HPE Edgeline Services Platform along with the Edgeline Data Aggregation App and Edgeline Address Translation App to help customers manage expanding IoT device inventories. Unveiled at Discover 2017, these offerings aim to connect IT systems with Operational Technology (OT) functions, building on HPE’s prior Edgeline Converged Edge systems that combine IT and OT with smaller footprints and simpler management. HPE describes the new platform and apps as “Software Defined OT,” enabling IoT applications outside traditional data centers or cloud so customers can run functions where equipment is located. The Data Aggregation App ingests and combines data from OT devices such as PLCs and SCADA into a single collection, while the Address Translation App collects network address translations from a larger network and delivers them to subset networks using software-defined configuration that can be managed remotely. An analyst quoted in the passage says customers face difficulty due to many new technologies and variables and that HPE’s single-vendor approach is meant to address this concern.

ESA inaugurated a new 35-meter deep space antenna, “New Norcia 3,” at its New Norcia site in Western Australia, part of Estrack and intended to boost Europe’s deep space communications and data download capacity. The cryogenically cooled, high-power antenna is scheduled to enter service in 2026 and will support current missions including Juice, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, Mars Express, Hera, and others, and upcoming missions such as Plato and Envision. The antenna can also provide cross-support for other space agencies and commercial missions. The project, delivered on schedule, has an estimated construction cost of EUR 62.3 million, with a contribution of EUR 3 million from the Australian Space Agency, and it is operated locally by CSIRO.

A UCL and Imperial College London research team used high-resolution imaging and biochemical experiments to show how polymyxins, last-resort antibiotics against Gram-negative bacteria, disrupt bacterial outer armor. The study found that polymyxins caused surface protrusions, rapid production and shedding of the outer armor, and cell death only when bacteria were active; dormant bacteria were not killed. In lab tests, previously dormant cells became vulnerable only after sugar was present and they resumed armor production, with a delay of about 15 minutes. The researchers suggest these findings may help explain recurring infections and guide strategies to improve treatment effectiveness by considering the bacterial state during antibiotic use.

The case involves certified questions to the Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia regarding whether a private employer’s termination of “at will” employees for refusing to take a polygraph test violated West Virginia public policy. The plaintiffs, Deborah J. Cordle, Brenda G. Billings, and Brenda L. Hall, were hired by General Hugh Mercer Corporation as cleaning maids and were terminable at will. After signing agreements in January 1981 to take a polygraph test when required, they were notified in June 1982 that polygraph testing would begin and their employment was terminated in October 1982 after they refused to take the test. The Circuit Court of Mercer County denied the employer’s motion to dismiss and certified questions, including whether the existence of public policy is a question of law or fact for a jury.

The majority held that determining public policy is a question of law and affirmed the circuit court’s ruling that termination for refusal to submit to a polygraph test violated West Virginia public policy. The majority reasoned that while employees’ rights are not absolute, West Virginia’s policy against such testing is grounded in the recognition of an individual privacy interest. The court remanded the case for further proceedings.

Justice Miller, with Justice Neely joining, dissented, arguing that at the time of termination there was no established public policy prohibiting discharge of at-will employees for refusing polygraph tests because the relevant statute became effective after the termination, and contended that privacy-related cases cited by the majority did not support the outcome.

After bus activation, the host performs SD card initialization and identification. It starts with ACMD41 (SD_SEND_OP_COND), setting operational conditions and the HCS bit in the OCR; HCS=1 indicates SDHC/SDXC support, while HCS=0 indicates neither. CMD8 is received to expand ACMD41 using HCS in the argument and CCS in the response, and if the card returns no CMD8 response the host should set HCS to 0. The host repeatedly issues ACMD41 until the card sets the busy bit in OCR to 1, completing initialization within 1 second from the first ACMD41, and only CMD0 may be issued during repetitions. When the card responds to CMD8, ACMD41 includes CCS: CCS=0 indicates SDSC and CCS=1 indicates SDHC/SDXC. The host then identifies each card by sending CMD2 to obtain the CID, transitioning through identification states, and using CMD3 (SEND_RELATIVE_ADDR) to publish and retrieve an RCA used for future data transfers; the host repeats CMD2/CMD3 for all cards. SDXC initialization is identical to SDHC, with SDXC user area capacity specified by C_SIZE and required to be at least 32GB. After identification, the host issues CMD9 (SEND_CSD), optionally uses CMD4 (SET_DSR), and uses CMD7 to place one card into Transfer State at a time. The passage also describes related behavior for UHS-I voltage switching, CMD6 function switching, high-speed mode, APP_CMD (CMD55) command extension behavior, and differences between SDSC and SDHC/SDXC memory access (including block addressing and fixed 512-byte block length for SDHC/SDXC).

Bishop Hassan Kukah of the Catholic Diocese of Sokoto urged politicians to provide quality governance and not take the military’s patience for democracy for granted. He said that had Nigeria experienced its current frustrations in earlier years, multiple coups might have occurred, but he warned politicians to “clean up” so soldiers stay in the barracks. Kukah criticized worsening governance that leaves Nigeria unable to meet basic needs despite resources, condemned the use of religious sentiment to cover misgovernance, and called on Nigerians to question leaders’ promises and show greater courage. He said issues from the last elections remain, with Nigeria more divided than before 2015, and urged government tolerance of opposing views. He also announced a leadership forum by the Kukah Centre and said Ghanaian President Nana Akufo-Addo would deliver a lecture in Nigeria on sustaining democracy later in the month.

The passage discusses a hockey game in which one team made key saves and both teams played well. Austin Police Chief Brian Manley made a public plea to whoever carried out an 11-day bombing campaign, saying authorities want the person to reach out before more injuries or deaths occur. He said three package bombings earlier this month killed two people and injured two others, and that the violence drew worldwide attention. Manley asked for understanding of what led the bomber(s) to act and requested calls to 911 or contact through the police website. Draylen Mason and Anthony Stephan House died; a 75-year-old woman and another woman in her 40s survived, with one in critical condition. Authorities are investigating possible hate crime involvement, and the reward for information has been increased to $100,000, on top of a $15,000 state reward. Manley reported federal assistance, numerous suspicious packages reported, interviews logged, leads checked, and that lab analysis of bomb components had improved investigators’ understanding.

UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves said she would not rule out tax increases ahead of November’s budget, while reiterating commitment to fiscal discipline and warning that market credibility would collapse if spending were not tightly controlled. She cited geopolitical instability, new U.S. tariffs, and rising borrowing costs as factors reshaping the economy. Although some commitments, such as avoiding VAT increases, remain policy for now, she declined to give rigid guarantees and Darren Jones also declined to dismiss breaking manifesto tax caps. The ambiguity leaves businesses and households uncertain and suggests the government is prioritising credibility and flexibility, as analysts discuss potential need to raise taxes to address a forecast fiscal shortfall.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated January 29, 2020. The passage includes excerpts dated May 9, 2001, and related coverage. It reports that Questia, an online college library and research firm, laid off about half its workforce to reduce costs and slow its pace of adding books, while citing difficulties raising additional cash and noting increased subscriber growth. It also describes mixed Wall Street trading ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting, with the Dow falling and the Nasdaq rising, and discusses lower productivity and bond yield movements. Several items focus on Enron and power market issues, including Enron’s comments that Japan’s newly deregulated power market lacks competition and needs an independent regulator, plans for Williams to expand in Europe’s deregulating gas and power markets, and ongoing disputes involving Enron’s Dabhol Power Company in India, including family relocations, MSEB’s positions regarding capacity and costs, arbitration arrangements, and demands for probes.

The passage describes the ADS868xW ADC transfer function, alarm features, and device functional and programming modes. It explains that the ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar or unipolar ranges and outputs straight-binary format; full-scale range and LSB size depend on the difference between positive and negative full-scale input voltages. The alarm features include an active-high ALARM output with user-programmable input high/low thresholds and an AVDD alarm with fixed 4.7 V low and 5.3 V high thresholds, plus behavior of active and tripped alarm flags. The device uses a multiSPI interface, with data transfer frames beginning at CONVST/CS falling edge and ending before conversions start; it supports multiple SPI/SRC protocols and configurations including single-device, standard SPI, and daisy-chain topologies. It also outlines operational states (RESET, ACQ, CONV), reset behavior, data write/read command handling, output data word formatting with optional appended flags and parity, and relevant configuration registers and register-map details.

The case concerns whether the mother may obtain custody of her son, Edward, against the father. After the mother took Edward to Nevada in 1946, the Nevada divorce purported to award custody of Edward to the father, and it is undisputed the father had exclusive actual custody from August 1946 until June 1949, when the father left Edward with the mother for a visit. The mother then filed for custody; she retained physical custody until August 14, 1950, when the court ordered her to return Edward to the father pending trial. After a February 8, 1951 trial, the court denied the mother’s custody request and confirmed the father’s custody.

On appeal, the mother argued it was an abuse of discretion to award custody of a boy of tender years to the father under Civil Code section 138. The court held that the trial court properly focused on the child’s best interests, including Edward’s established mode of living with his father from ages 2 to 6, and that stability and avoiding abrupt changes were important factors. The court also stated that trial judge remarks cannot be used to impeach the final judgment. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage explains the role of extended enterprise (EE) and digital business process modeling, focusing on Business Process Modeling (BPM) and the increasing need for model validity and reasoning. It presents an MDA-driven business process model made up of a static domain model, a workflow model, and a value model. It discusses business rules (BR) modeling using controlled natural languages and translation into logic frameworks, including considerations of closed-world vs. open-world reasoning and hybrid reasoning over different inference paradigms. It also covers modal interpretation of business rules (alethic and deontic), limitations of existing languages and reasoners, and approaches to process flow representation and validation using declarative methods (e.g., temporal logic and consistency checking). The passage then introduces declarative value modeling (graphical and logic-based) and describes relationships between business rules, process flow, and value models via static, semi-dynamic, and dynamic consistency checks. Finally, it concludes that multi-faceted, logic-based representations are needed to enable both priori evaluation and run-time adaptation, highlighting open issues such as critical area detection and representing pragmatics (reasons for actions).

The passage describes education as a fundamental right linked to national and individual development, noting that access to quality education in Africa remains challenging due to factors such as poverty, lack of infrastructure, and conflict. It introduces digital storytelling as a tool for research and education that uses digital media to create personal narratives and can support learning beyond formal contexts. The article outlines research questions about skills promoted by digital storytelling in Africa and the contexts where it is integrated into African higher education, and presents a qualitative document analysis of 15 studies selected from 2000-present African-focused literature. The reviewed studies report benefits including increased student engagement, motivation, peer learning, reflective and higher-order thinking, improved oral performance and map-reading skills, and potential for community building, cultural preservation, and social activism. Challenges noted across the studies include shortages of resources, limited self-confidence, time constraints, and technical barriers such as insufficient equipment and unreliable electricity. The conclusion states that digital storytelling in African higher education promotes empowerment, cultural enrichment, and transformative learning, with varied applications across subjects and teacher training while further research and integration are recommended.

Steve Wynn’s attorneys say he brokered a settlement in December 2006 with a second woman who accused him of sexual misconduct and who recently reported him to the FBI. According to court documents, Wynn and an attorney met with FBI agents to accuse the woman of trying to extort him by threatening to go public with details from the 2006 settlement. The filings do not provide details of the newly revealed settlement. The woman’s attorney, Lisa Bloom, said in an email that her client denies the extortion allegations and that she wanted to speak publicly; the FBI declined to confirm whether it investigated. Wynn resigned as chairman and CEO of Wynn Resorts last month after reporting by The Wall Street Journal; Wynn denied the newspaper’s accusations.

The passage reports that Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who lives in Islington and is MP for Islington North, was seen waiting 40 minutes outside his home on double yellow lines before traveling to Westminster. It says a traffic warden recognized the car and did not issue a ticket. It also claims DVLA records show his diesel car emits 189g of carbon dioxide and falls in a high vehicle tax band, and that its engine averages 36 mpg. The passage quotes Tory MPs accusing Corbyn of “breathtaking hypocrisy,” and notes that Corbyn has commented on air pollution, including calls for phasing out diesel and support for a Clean Air Act with “clean air zones.” It further states that Corbyn was offered a chauffeur-driven Government Car Service car in 2015 but did not confirm whether he would use it.

The passage introduces ordinary differential equation initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), describing how they are written as first-order systems and how numerical solvers generate time-point outputs and corresponding solution values. It explains converting higher-order ODEs to first-order form and emphasizes that numerical methods must approximate the true solution and manage error. It outlines the Forward Euler method as an update rule, compares related numerical integration ideas (rectangle, trapezoid, midpoint) via Taylor-expansion error scaling, and explains how higher-order methods use more accurate update formulas. It then discusses the complication that ODE solvers require approximations when the right-hand side depends on the unknown solution values, leading to Runge-Kutta methods such as second-order and common Runge-Kutta 4/5 schemes. Finally, it analyzes how numerical error can propagate and amplify, defining numerical stability in terms of the norm of a related matrix, and illustrates instability with the scalar example \(dy/dt=-2y\) using Forward Euler, showing conditions on step size for stable versus exploding behavior. The lecture concludes with remarks about studying stability conditions in the textbook and a homework assignment to write an ODE solver, noting that Tuesday will cover implicit solvers.

The lecture introduces AMO (atomic, molecular, and optical) physics and describes how the field is shaped by what AMO researchers do, using atoms or molecules and photons/electromagnetic fields as building blocks. It outlines a historical shift from studying individual particles and collisions to focusing on few-body and many-body physics, including entanglement and overlap with condensed matter physics. The professor explains that AMO physics has progressed through increasing control of nature—moving from internal-state control (including optical pumping) to control of motion (laser cooling and Bose-Einstein condensation), then to single quantum systems, and finally to creating new, controlled complexity in Hilbert space. Technology is identified as a major driver, with examples including advances in lasers, frequency combs, and high-finesse cavities that enable single-photon experiments. The lecture then presents the course structure and syllabus for 8.422, emphasizing light-atom interactions, open-system methods, mechanical forces of light for trapping and cooling, quantum information elements, and many-body physics of quantum gases while excluding certain high-energy and advanced atomic-structure topics. The professor uses atoms in an optical lattice as an “appetizer,” describing how standing-wave potentials arise from light-atom interactions and outlining related phenomena such as Sisyphus cooling, magic wavelengths for atomic clocks, tunneling and Mott-insulator physics, pulsed-lattice diffraction, atom interferometry, and applications to measuring many-body properties.

CPFL Energia SA launched Envo to serve the growing market for solar-powered homes in Brazil by offering services including equipment, installation, grid connection assistance, and selling excess energy. CPFL’s controlling stake was bought by China’s State Grid for 14.2 billion reais in 2015, and Brazil’s 2015 regulation enabled consumer solar projects to connect to the grid. CPFL CEO Andre Dorf said grid-connected solar projects rose from 7,500 at end of 2016 to 10,000 by April and that Envo aims to capture market share. CPFL did not disclose investment amounts and said it would buy solar panels wherever cheaper. Banco Santander Brasil will provide financing, and Envo clients can use a simulation tool on its website.

The passage is a roundup of HBO Max shows, describing multiple series and docuseries and their premises, casts, and seasons. It includes crime dramas and true-crime documentaries, comedy and satire series, period pieces, animated or franchise-related adaptations, and international productions, noting details such as season timing, renewal or cancellation status, awards, and—when provided—main plot points and episode premises.

A toy made in Vietnam by a Chinese company, designed by a Dutch artist in Belgium, inspired by indie toy culture in Hong Kong, and made viral by a Thai K-pop star is described as the biggest Gen-Z cultural trend of 2025, shaping global culture.

Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park is visited by millions, but its geologic structure and fluid pathways have been poorly understood. University of Utah scientists mapped near-surface geology around Old Faithful, identifying the heated-water reservoir that feeds the vent and describing how ground shaking changes between eruptions. The study used a dense network of portable seismographs and new seismic analysis techniques, with results published in *Geophysical Research Letters* and Sin-Mei Wu as first author. The work describes Yellowstone’s hydrothermal features, including explosive geysers, and notes Park Service interest in managing thermal effects near buildings. Using cost-effective small, autonomous seismometers, the team deployed 133 instruments in 2015 and observed recurring tremor patterns: intense shaking bursts around Old Faithful lasted about 60 minutes, followed by roughly 30 minutes of quiet; the eruption was found to occur near the end of peak shaking. Researchers related the tremors to reservoir filling and pressurized bubble dynamics and used ambient vibration data to image subsurface structures, concluding that a hydrothermal reservoir west of Old Faithful affects seismic waves. They estimate the reservoir’s diameter at about 200 meters and its capacity at roughly 300,000 cubic meters of water. Further surveys are planned, including studies of how air temperature may affect subsurface structure and how earthquake waves propagate and reverberate, and similar analysis is planned for Norris Geyser Basin.

Secretary Stettinius commented that governments’ memoranda should be approached with open minds and minimal formal commitments, since formal positions would be harder to change; he said Dumbarton Oaks proposals were meant to be informal and potentially modifiable. The meeting discussed comments on the proposed name of the new international organization amid objections to the “United Nations” name, and reviewed Chapter I, including principles such as respect for international treaties, juridical equality of nations, and territorial integrity. The passage also describes Stettinius’s diary notes from 1944–1945, including efforts to inform Latin American “associated nations” about potential exclusion from an upcoming United Nations conference unless they declared war and qualified as United Nations, and steps to prepare memoranda and conference planning for the Big Three meeting, including voting procedure issues. It notes that the Yalta Conference was the first chief-of-state meeting the Secretary of State was invited to and that security of Crimea notes was emphasized.

Ronald L. Johnson appealed the denial of his habeas corpus petition, challenging the admission of his confession at a trial concluded before Escobedo v. Illinois and Miranda v. Arizona. He had been convicted in January 1964 of first degree murder, armed robbery, and related offenses involving a masked hold-up and the shooting of a Boston police officer, and he is serving a life sentence.  

The court held that applying the voluntariness standard from Procunier v. Atchley, the confession was voluntarily given and the district court’s decision was affirmed. The confession was obtained during an in-custody interrogation about eight and one-half hours after Johnson was apprehended, and the record described his circumstances including injury, lack of sleep, police presence, line-ups, and that he was not advised of his right to consult counsel or given Miranda warnings. The appellate court concluded, after an independent determination under the totality of the circumstances, that Johnson’s will was not overborne and that the confession was not involuntary.

French President Emmanuel Macron named 18 initial winners of his “Make Our Planet Great Again” climate grants, including 13 U.S.-based scientists, at a ceremony in Paris ahead of a climate summit. U.S.-based climate scientist Camille Parmesan said she is elated to spend the next five years in France rather than the United States, citing difficulties with U.S. climate science funding and a psychological impact after Trump’s election. She will work at an experimental ecology station in the Pyrenees. British scientist Benjamin Sanderson said he found France’s encouragement of climate research reassuring, also citing the growing difficulty of getting research funding in the U.S.; he will live in Toulouse, where France’s national meteorological service is based.

The passage describes COVID-19 public health challenges requiring sustained behavior change and highlights the role of testing, including early case detection via isolation, quarantine, and contact tracing. It also presents the Healthy Davis Together (HDT) program in Davis, California (launched September 2020) and its expansion to Yolo County as Healthy Yolo Together (HYT) in July 2021. The program included free saliva-based asymptomatic testing and other interventions such as targeted communication, isolation and exposure protocols, education to reduce misinformation, personal protective equipment distribution, community partnerships to build trust, and local economic support. The study reports 770,165 tests among 89,924 Yolo County residents, summarizes testing across four variant periods (Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, Post-Omicron), and finds that Omicron had the highest daily test participation and highest number of positive cases. It also reports demographic patterns in testing participation and frequent testing, defined as multiple tests within 15 days, with women, ages 19–44, and white participants consistently among the most frequent testers. The discussion emphasizes user retention, changes in participation over time (including a drop after Omicron), and the role of pandemic fatigue and evolving preventive measures such as vaccination and at-home tests.

Worcester police department employees earned more than $4 million in overtime pay in 2017, and some officers received more in overtime or detail pay than their base pay. The city’s fire department and Department of Public Works also received millions in overtime pay that year, with officials saying the overtime costs are not due to understaffing. Police Chief Steven Sargent cited late calls, special projects, coverage of parades and protests, real time crime center operations, training, and grant-related work. Police officer John Towns received the most overtime pay among police at $59,577, and Hermes Rivera received the most overtime among public works employees at $40,122. The city paid $9,326,718 in detail pay to police officers, including George Kelly ($100,384 in detail pay) and others whose detail pay exceeded their regular pay.

The passage says flu season in Indiana is not over yet, with 278 flu-related deaths reported so far this season. It explains that respiratory germs like the flu virus and gastrointestinal viruses such as norovirus can survive on surfaces and spread through contact, including by touching contaminated objects and then touching the face. It describes a handwashing experiment at IU Health Pathology Lab that found bacteria on hands before and after washing, and officials said the results indicate handwashing may need to be done harder and longer. Handwashing tips include using soap, washing for 20–30 seconds (twice the “Happy Birthday” song), scrubbing hands front and back and around fingernails, rinsing thoroughly, and washing at key times such as after using the bathroom, after changing diapers, caring for sick people, and before eating. The lab also tested a cell phone, finding bacteria consistent with normal flora, and officials warned that phones are often brought near the face, increasing risk of pathogen spread.

The passage explains walking as a bodily and sensory interaction with place that shapes identity and is tied to social and cultural structures. In art and art education, walking can become an aesthetic experience: it supports inquiry, reflection, and the rethinking of established perceptions, linking mind, body, and environment. The study described uses walking-oriented, art-based practices to help prospective teachers convert everyday experiences into visual and textual outputs. It is grounded in interpretive/thematic analysis and conducted over 10 weeks in 2023 under online conditions after the 2023 earthquake, with participants adding walking routes to daily routines. Data were collected through visual diaries, course recordings, course texts, and end-of-study interviews, and analyzed using axial coding and thematic mapping with triangulation. Participants’ walking experiences and engagement with art works (including Francis Alÿs’ “The Collector”) led to expanded meanings of walking, greater sensory awareness, and changing perspectives on art, life, and pedagogy. The findings emphasize that walking can connect daily life and art, potentially support social awareness, and serve as a teaching tool for developing multiple perspectives and visual literacy.

The passage says India’s Supreme Court issued an order barring parties from seeking votes in the name of religion, caste, creed, community, and language. It notes uncertainty about the basis for the order because the judgment text and dissent were not seen. The author argues the order is problematic because it assumes identity-based politics is inherently wrong, and claims identity mobilisation arises from discrimination and has helped marginalised communities gain political space through mechanisms like universal adult franchise and reserved seats. It also discusses religion’s role in politics, arguing that communal violence cannot be addressed by a judicial fiat alone and instead requires stronger enforcement of rule of law and democracy’s self-correcting mechanisms, and that Hindutva must be contested politically. The author further says the order is unlikely to be implementable, pointing to ongoing caste, language, and religion appeals in elections nationwide, and concludes that the judiciary should allow electoral democracy to evolve.

The passage describes the #MeToo moment in Canadian politics as quickly leading to multiple high-level resignations following workplace sexual harassment and related impropriety allegations, noting that none of the allegations had been proven in court. It criticizes backlash comparing #MeToo to McCarthyism and argues about fairness, including the need for political figures to be held to higher standards and parties to address alleged misconduct. Indiana is seeking to address middle school reading struggles by hiring private tutoring companies using “outcomes-based contracting,” where pay depends largely on student improvement. Indiana Education Secretary Katie Jenner said the state lacks a successful existing plan and is responding to vendor proposals after reading scores fell last year. The article notes uncertainty about contract structure and whether Indiana will issue a formal request for proposals. Other states and a contracting support center are cited, including concerns about risks such as student attendance and complex goal-setting and compensation. Evidence of effectiveness is described as limited and mixed, with some districts seeing results and others ending the approach after pandemic tutoring contracts. The state will focus on struggling readers, and Jenner also plans to pursue donations and grants to help cover contracts.
